_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Could be a great game but suffers on many fronts. It plays like a XCOM in real time, but unlike XCOM, where you can customise your troops or have options (what/how to deploy), your options here are, at least in the first few hours and where you play primarily "yourself" only,  limited. All speak about the great classes (there are even DLC for more) and options and the game only offers: Assault, Medic, a rifle and a pistole. Yeah. After some hours this is not enough. I prefer hard hitting, slow firing weapons or something like Flamethrowers, but you do not get them. Or rather only later in the game (not till 5 researchs done, I saw my first reasearch for more weapons, weapons the AI uses in mission one. Ok?).At least you get some equipment to toy around in the missions. Of course, all drops on the map are random, so you can get Artillery Support, Turrets, Shields, ... and more normal stuff, like ammo (in all kinds!), grenades and stims. Still, they are 1. random, so you can not count on them and 2. stay on the map, so no "collect the good stuff you could need in the next deployment (which is ok, but could alleviate some issues).On the other hand the bots, especially if commanded, are top. Easily one of the top 10 or even 5 of "coop/partner"-AIs I have seen so far. Sadly they are not enough to turn the mess around.: - I want to check something on the map - oh noes! The dropship flew to this position and now the intended mission can not be reached in time anymore - I want to capture this one specimen and - yeah, killed again from the bots. - Ok, I need to place this marker for the nuke... ok? Is it already coming? CAN I RUN FASTER??? Dead. Message: "The nuke is on its way, you have to move to a safe area." REALLY? The team is already dead EMMA!- Story? Somehow all were prepared for battle/ factions have awesome weapons, but knock them out on their own (Mild Spoiler: They fire a weapon on the first mission, which makes the whole problem (the mutants) like 1000x worse).- Also story, somehow the game/world plays very disconnected to the team/ player. Yes, there is an "urgency meter", but yeah, why should I care? Somehow it seems to do missions (except where you get good intel/ many supplies/ some specialists/ something for YOURSELF) is just a waste of time.- There are allies with more and better weapons from mission 3 onwards, but they can not give them to you (miniguns/chainguns, flamers, vehicles with huge cannons, drop pods, .....).So, if you want to play with nothing (just a rifle and a "sword skill") and random equip for the first few hours, then go, get the game (on sale); but if you want a XCOM like experience or something like the "Hero/Commando Missions" from StarCraft II or other RTS, then this is no game for you. Note: It is said that in Coop/Multiplayer for this game is/could be better, but I do not see this happening without the ability to use different classes or weapons or even to choose the colour of ones suit. Glad I got the game cheap.El Psy Congroo

_childDocuments_.review: They fixed a bunch of stuff i wrote about in my review but there's still a lot that needs to be done to make this reach its potential. At this point though i would argue this is worth getting on sale. I doubt this will ever be the sequel i would've wanted to see personally though.-------------------------OLD REVIEW BELOW-------------------------As far as sequels go this is a real mixed bag. In terms of visuals and production value this game is obviously much more refined than it's predecessor. However there are many mechanical / ui changes that leave me frustrated and toying with the theory that a lot of the decisions made were in favor of getting the game playable on a controller / consoles.The grim tone of the first game seems to be toned down by quite a bit and in general the game and it's presentation on both the visual and sound front seem to be less spooky and horrific. Slowing down time now isn't a toggle and requires holding the command radial, this wouldn't be such a problem if it wasn't for the fact that you aren't able to pan the camera around while the radial is up. Also during slow-motion the sound no longer pitches down, this obviously makes things less satisfying. A lot of things in general are simplified to the point where i feel it's a detriment. The only active skills the player has any say over are those of the player character, the squad leader. Squadmates do have abilities and upgrade trees containing both active and passive abilities. However they seem to trigger at random with no input from the player, i'm sure they've set some sort of intelligent conditions to make the triggering reasonably appropriate but i'd still much prefer being able to decide myself. All of this is just removing depth and choice from the game to the point where it's mostly been reduced to clicking through the map and watching your squad walk around.The new campaign does seem a lot more fleshed out, clearly taking a great deal of inspiration from XCOM 2. It features research and production as well as a global infestation meter to manage a la XCOM 2's avatar project.Perhaps i'm wrong on some of these things, this is all based on the small 2 hour window i played it in. If so please do point it out. This game really isn't bad but for 30 bucks i feel like i'd almost rather just replay the first game instead at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote a negative review for this game due to its bugs and I advised people to wait a few months for the bug fixes.Only 1 week has passed since the game released and the devs have already pushed out a patch which:- fixed pretty much all the bugs which I had encountered (except a minor 1)- did some QoL changes to the multiplayer hub- normalized enemy wavesI still wonder why they couldn't postpone the release a bit to iron out all the bugs and include the missing content (missions, maps, terminator and hellfire classes), but I guess it's something which we'll never know.I feel like the game is in a playable state right now, so I've changed my review from negative to positive.If you are a fan of Red Solstice / NOTD and want to play it asap then go ahead and get it right now, otherwise probably it's still best to wait until they polish the game even more.The missing content which I've talked before will be added later on with free updates anyway.------> ORIGINAL REVIEW <------I was really excited for this game.If you check out my profile you'll see that I play Dota 2, Legion TD 2 and Elemental TD 2. These games and Red Solstice 2 have something in common: they were all originally Warcraft 3 maps.I've played NOTD before and I perfectly knew what to expect gameplay wise.Red Solstice 2 sadly is a bit bugged right now and considering that:1) It's not an early access2) It's not cheapI can't recommend it.The bugs go from small ones to more severe ones.Here's the list of bugs which I encountered in my <4h playthrough:[SMALL BUGS]- Cutscenes don't play (black screen, only audio)- If you have 2+ monitors and unlock the camera, it'll go crazy. Basically it means you either have to disable all monitors but one, or to never unlock the camera- Multiplayer chat is bugged: sometimes it won't show up and the cursor is completely broken.[MEDIUM BUGS]- If the host leaves (even at the end of the match) or disconnects you lose progress.- If you only play skirmish you won't ever be able to properly HOST (campaign won't progress even if you play it)[SEVERE BUGS]- Ready button often doesn't show up for players in a lobby ==> can't start match- Desync/floor swimming (fixed with the first hotfix)- Objectives sometimes spawn outside of boundaries, making them impossible to complete.- Enemy spawner sometimes doesn't work properly (had 1 match where even at difficulty 16 there were only small fries. No, it wasn't on easy).- Invisible walls (dunno if they were fixed with the first hotfix)Let's now talk about the gameplay:Most objectives are essentially a flavor of "reach a point in the map".Need to save some civillians? Just get to this point and stand there for a few seconds.Need to stop an ambush? Just reach this point.Need to find XYZ? First go to point A, then point B, then point C.Need to secure a point? You got it right, go there and stand there for a few seconds.You don't have to do anything in those points to complete the quest, you just have to reach it.The other type of quests I've encountered are "follow the tanks" or "biomass something".Please note that I don't consider this game to be exclusively bad, infact when it works properly it's quite fun and the marine customization is done really well and allows a lot of different build (in theory, at least).So, in conclusion, wait to get this game. Come back later in a few months and check if they've fixed the bugs.And why not, even wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great top down shooter/RPG that has GREAT tactical depth. (I will be clarifying some things touched on in other reviews)There are so many different ways you can build your character and team they can basically all be viable on max difficultly so long as you follow a few simple rules (bring decent amounts of all 3 damage types, healing (doesn't have to be a dedicated medic can be a bunch of scattered skills across the group) and don't have a weak link when it comes to speed (having a few speedy peps who can run ahead/solo can be good but don't have somebody who will be slowing down the main force)). Bringing a source of burning is also nice but if your damage diversity is high enough you don't need it (burn dot is without type so it doesn't care how resistant a target it)I have seen some people complain about the community in other reviews. The discord is very friendly and many people there are very happy to explain things to new players and give advice. That being said jumping into skirmish on anything but easy as your first time playing you will probably either get carried or loose the mission since this game is about planning and decision making far more so than how good your reflexes are and if you don't have the information of what works for what your likely going to flounder. Which is why your supposed to start with the original campaign where you can get introduced to things at a controlled pace. Skirmish is meant for people who have beet the campaign or are joining friends who have done such and will be able to guide them. (Another review touched on this in a negative light because they had started skirmish and so missing the warning the mission control NPC made that there were hunters in the area, which had they played campaign or had a veteran player with them they would have known that they should really have at least one of 3 thing, fire, powerful energy damage, lot of suppression.)Their are two progression systems with some overlap. campaign and skirmish, in both game modes you gain XP/levels to unlock more skill points to spend on unlocking things; the categories that are shared between skirmish and campaign are small stat increases for yourself (small because the main difference between a starting player and veteran is supposed to be skill/knowledge not stats) and moderate stat increases for your AI teammates if your host. Skirmish also uses these skill points to unlock classes, weapons, skills and suit components. In campaign those are unlock via technologies. Rank ups and medals are also shared between the two (though later rank ups and all medals require skirmish but you don't need either for the first campaign)Also a major confusion point for many people, later unlocks are not supposed to be inherently better, they are meant to be more niche or complicated to use properly. For example the minigun. It has massive accuracy issues when you start firing it, yes this intended. It is not meant for taking on isolated small enemies it is meant for attacking bosses or an entire hoard (it has bullet penetration making it great for the second roll because each shot will hit 3-8 targets) the class that generally carries it also has a skill that they start with called shoulder turret that keeps isolated trash mobs from bothering them so they don't even have to fire unless they have a large target worthy of the minigun. Said class also has a skill to massively increase how much ammo they can load into the weapon in a single reload (525 instead of 150 at max rank) they also have another skill that makes them not consume ammo until the skill is canceled (though the energy drain on that skill is potent at first, though onced maxed you can fire for close to a minute straight without consuming ammo). There are also skills and components you can use to reduce its (or anything else's) accuracy issues but I personally don't use those in favor of truly massive damage when I do have a valid target and the shoulder turret to keep small stuff off of me.

_childDocuments_.review: Added a second follow-up for my review hours down the road.I picked it up on sale, so far I have been enjoying my time on vanilla campaign (normal difficulty). I will do a pros/cons. I have not played Skirmish so I cannot speak for that mode yet, I will add that later. I'm neutral on my feelings towards Season Pass, I do not own it, but it is more expensive than the vanilla game...although it does appear to come with quite a load of content. At the time 2/4 of these DLC contents are not released yet, but slated for this year on their roadmap.Top down action shooter RPG, similar to StarCraft's Undead Assault series.Pros:- LOVE that you can change between RTS styled controls or WASD to fit either style of player.- Enjoying the game style/combat, very mindless fun in lower difficulties, but it can get crazier on later waves/difficulties.- Allowing customization of your combat suits to make your load-out match your playstyle (I sometimes play an explosives Demolition for clearing out nests, sometimes a fast paced invis Recon to run through the maps/objectives).- Unlocking other Combat Suits in campaign does not take too long.- You can choose "private, public, or friends only" for campaign, but you can actually change it before each mission along with inviting friends during campaign. I have not tested friend invites because none of mine have the game.- This may be a pro or con depending on the player (for me it is a pro), in campaign there is a resource management system that adds a strategy feel to the game. You will not be able to do every small side mission that becomes available, there are research panels, upgrade panels that allow access to more campaign related items that can assist you before/during the missions. So far, it is not overwhelming.Cons:- Secondary/Optional Missions within missions are extremely repetitive.- No further armor skin customization (not going to count the limited color changes) outside of seasonal event skins and DLC/season pass skins.- There are some lack of explanation on intractable objects in-game, the in-game archives do not even tell you what they do. Some give you a buff, some do nothing (that I have discovered so far), and some call in supply drops/evac locations that probably are more useful in Skirmish.- Getting into an online game is not explained well. You can only actively search for games through the Skirmish option of the main menu even if you are looking to join somebody's campaign mode.- There are some minor bugs, but nothing game-breaking so far. The 2nd mission one of the soldiers would not shoot any infected.EDIT:After playing significantly more hours, I decided to pick up the Season Pass. After playing Skirmish, it fixed the "repetitive" feel of the optional missions I was feeling in the Campaign. If the host has DLC you don't have, you still can play with them and enjoy the other maps/objectives that are past the base game. The extra classes are pretty neat, but you can still get a lot of out of the base classes w/o DLC.None of the classes feel boring, each of them have their use.The biggest frustration is movement. Sometimes if you switch from to WASD from RTS style (movement with W/A/S/D or right click to move while scrolling with W/A/S/D) your character still tries to path where you originally clicked which breaks up the fluidity of switching between styles (Marksman with a snipe requires a bunch of switching between for me).Second complaint on the movement is that you can get clipped/stuck inside of walls/objects. It doesn't happen frequently, but when it does it is frustrating (especially when you die because of it). I still recommend the game though. Player base is lacking, you see reoccurring names for multiplayer, but sometimes that is good if you don't really have friends, you can make some.

_childDocuments_.review: Much more approachable than the first game imo. I have not played Singleplayer campaign, only the Multiplayer Skirmishes so far, but they were easy to pickup and quite fun. Difficulty is easily scaled to suit how you want to play the mission - Very Hard seems about perfect but a full run on a Normal game can actually net you more XP.There are two main components to customizing your soldier. The first is a RPGesque skill tree that unlocks new classes, weapons, items, skills, and passive boosts. Second is the loadout screen where you actually balance your kit and tune it for your playstyle. A balanced squad will do better and there are classes to suit all playstyles - cloaking snipers to scout or kill HVTs, recon classes for vision or expensive support - like artillery and bombing runs, heavy gunners to chew through hordes with temporary infinite ammo, medics to revive you across the map, demolition to magically poop out rocket ammo every minute etc. Weapons are fairly diverse with different damage types and playstyles; energy, ballistic, explosive, piercing. Some are meant for ammo conservation and high damage, others to pump out bullets to suppress bosses so your squad can apply extra damage, while others are more just to let you run around faster or set yourself to overwatch/autoaim. I find the customization quite satisfying and thankfully weapons are not class restricted (although you may need inventory extenders for larger weapons to fit).The harder part about putting this all together, is all skills/boost items are divided between Offense, Defense, and Support categories with each class getting different # of points for each category. So maybe one class you have 3 defense slots, but another you can have 8. Weapons also have a size and each class has a different size limit for their primary and secondary (although there are extenders to allow you to take bigger guns). This is also where it can be fun tweaking a build to try and make it OP, but also very slightly frustrating when you need to unlock the perfect skill still.My main complaint about the game is skills max out at level 5, and you can have 4 skills. So your character can max out at level 20, however you need support items to allow you to get higher than level 13. So most of the time you're either picking 1-2 cheap, garbage skills that you'll put 0-2 points in (like frag or critical hit :D) because the game penalizes you for taking less than 4 skills, or you're trying to stack as many level boosts as you can without completely screwing your energy meaning you're basically forced to use a passive-heavy skill loadout - which while powerful, i do not find as fun as active skill builds. Considering how hard it is to stack level boosts, I think like a level 15ish base max would have been better and keep initial level at 3. I guess they could also work a bit on expanding mission and map variety for multiplayer skirmishes, but its not bad and they did just add some missions in 1.3.

_childDocuments_.review: In itself, the game along with it's gameplay mechanic, it's ideas and everything else is amazing.Graphics are good, the soundtrack and sound effects are good even if not truly memorable.But Red Solstice 2 is such a mess... It's a grindfest with no end.Leveling up just takes forever and there are many many many "skillpoints" to unlock technology, classes and whatnot knowing some unlocks can take 6 points and to reach that unlock, first you have to invest 15 points in the tree. I'm burned out of the game and it's grind.Now, the gameplay is great but you'll quickly be overwhelmed by tons upon tons of monsters rushing at you from just every direction possible... Running for your life is the only thing you can do at some point.And the worst is the capture mechanic which is great on paper but practically, it's just impossible !The game ask you to capture a certain target which will be drowned in the mass of monster, so you place a trap to capture the monster you want but you get to capture another one which stepped first on the trap.The difficulty is just bonkers and your team can easily get wiped out by playing in normal difficulty.The ranking system ask you to complete missions which are annoying and terribly complicated to succeed.I really don't know what went through the devs head... They created a game which isn't a MMO but needs to be grinded like one. If you want to progress, you really have to spend hours upon hours on the game and dedicate your time on it as if you were starting to play a MMO.And missions often takes too much time to complete without any possibility to save and continue later.All this is pretty sad because the game looks great, plays great, has tons of great ideas and makes you want to explore it but is ultimately tarnished by frustrating mechanics and a story which seems to throws new characters at you without introducing them or the faction they belongs to.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm getting way more fun than I anticipated with it.While I am yet to get thru even halfway the first campaign (it has 4 if you got the season pass with a 5th on the way), but this whole thing is really doing it for me. The XCOM-style layer is a thing I always liked, but having real time combat missions instead of turn based affairs has always been on my wishlist. Granted, them being Alien Swarm style constant enemy pressure wouldn't have been my first pick, but now I dig it. Pulling off a narrow escape as a tidal wave of death comes down on you feels damn good.For those unfamiliar it means that during the mission you need to haul ass and push to complete as many objectives ASAP, as enemy waves get stronger. The base campaign starts you off easy, you can survive running out the clock at first, but as it gets incrementally harder to waste time. You have 3 AI teammates that you can give simple commands but somethings can only be done by a player.There is also a few other subjective appealing aspects working for me. The whole Spartan like space marine vs flood/tyranid thing, customizing my character and the AI squadmates loadout and weapons, and having drop in drop out multiplayer for the campaign for up to 8 total players. There is a surprising variety of toys to play with from guns to items to abilities and a lot of stuff in the map to interact with that can give you buffs, activate defenses, lock down buildings, call down artillery, explosives to breach doors or walls (most things seem to be destructible). You can even find some Matrix APU-style walkers during a mission. Next DLC will introduce usable vehicles.You are probably expecting the other shoe to drop and there is one coming. I gather the developer is small, and evidently ambitious. Came across people experiencing bugs though I've only seen one regarding AI loadouts. It is worth menitoning the game does not do a great job of explaining itself and frankly the easiest way when you find something you can't figure out is to just screenshot it and paste it on the official discord asking what is up with that.There is also the whole skirmish mode which are single missions, a weird profile-specific progression system which mainly for skirmish also has buffs that apply to campaign and playing campaign gives you progression in it.Anyway, 25 hours of gametime and I might still be on the honeymoon phase here, so I am gonna just suggest giving it a try if any of this sounds interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 is a prime example of why I don't trust Steam reviews anymore."It's a multiplayer-only game!"-- no it isn't, coming from someone who plays singleplayer only."This isn't a twin stick shooter, liars!"-- read the game's description, literally the first three lines."Only 400 players, game's dead!"-- let's forget about PlanetSide 2 and how it survived on similar numbers for nearly a decade, huh?"It's filled with bugs!"-- I don't have a clue what people are doing as I yet have to find a bug on my end."Greedy devs, milking the community!"-- oh yes, an indie studio that made a game that is bashed for 'small player numbers' is now getting bashed once more! But this time for planting a clear indicator that the game will be supported for the next year or longer, which completely invalidates the previous argument-- how great. Truly a crime, what a bunch of greedy bas*ards they are for wanting to get their bills, employees and licences paid while they support a game with absolutely no in-game microtransactions, nor a AAA publisher to boot! Actual Satans I say.Sarcasm aside, if you're thinking of getting RS2, do it. It's honestly worth it. It starts slow, but gets extremely hectic later on. It's that sort of game where it's a specific sort of experience you won't find anywhere else. Great theme, fluid and almost dynamic campaign against the clock and literal mountains of build customisation.Yeah the game needs better UI, smarter bot AI and a longer soundtrack-- but for a long time now I didn't enjoy myself as much as I do with RS2. Honestly a mega-replayable long-haul blast of a game with a serious gritty character, but some humour sprinkled about. Only thing I'd really suggest to do is create a Sci-Fi ambient horror playlist on Spotify, turn off in-game music, and let it run in the background. Immersion skyrockets ten-folds.But yeah, to close it off-- God, I hate people sometimes, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell, this is exactly the product I wanted, and then there's more in there that I never knew I needed.I'm a fan of NotD: Aftermath on Warcraft 3.  A lot of people posting comments in here have played the map before, and know exactly why they're here.  Lets talk about why everyone else should be here too.This game is a rush.  A tactical, beautiful rush.  It's always been, since NotD, since TRS1, and now this installment.  The skill tree could use work, maybe?  But the real game is when you're down to earth (or Mars in this case.), on the ground level, being the operative.  Do you work with the team?  Is your role scouting and collecting supplies for a good holdout base?  Are you pushing main objectives, or side objectives?There are so many freedoms, while giving you the harsh reality at the same time; you're surrounded, ammo is limited, supplies need to be conserved, rationed, and distributed.  This is all while there's a whole horde dropping around you from all sides.The start of one's foray into this game is simple.  Kick on the Overwatch mode for your marine to auto-target, grab some supplies here and there, and don't die for the love of everything.  Oh, and try to not blow your whole squad up too.  (FRIENDLY FIRE IS ON, BY THE BY.)As you get better at the game, you'll learn to start telling Overwatch to take a hike, and you'll engage targets of opportunity as you see fit.  As you understand damage types and what you can effectively bring down.  What you can bring to your team.That said, this is a holy grail of team games.  If you make good friends, who build good squads together, you're gunna' go far.  That's what I want from this game, and all games like it.  I want that team aspect every time.  All while we're trying to juggle supplies, mission, and our very lives.It's got more learning curve than other games, but if you're used to "One hero" RTS like maps in Starcraft, Warcraft 3, or Starcraft 2, or MOBA like controls (DotA/2, HoN, LoL.) you're going to have a better time getting comfortable.  Turn based top-down's are also okay in this regard, but you'll need to be ready to make quick decisions.So that said, I suggest this game.  I recommend it highly.  It's team has done excellent work keeping a type of game alive that I found so dear, in a setting that's unique and fresh to their IP.

In terms of bugs, i've played AAA titles with more issues on day 1 than this so i'm actually really pleased with this release all things considered. I don't find UI hard to navigate or understand, but i also took more than 10 seconds to figure it out so i suppose i understand how others couldn't be bothered. The balance feels good to me but i also enjoy things like a challenge and cooperative play with team tactics. I think most complaints about the game are people expecting this to tick every box for everyone and no games does that, but this does tick the majority of them for me because i had realistic expectations of a sequel I've been looking forward to for years. Thanks for a great sequel and i hope great things come from future content and / or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game when it first came out. It was a lot of fun, both with friends and with randoms. I thought the game mechanics and the class builds were fun to play around with. But what makes this game a hard no for me is the player base. They single-handedly ruined the game for me.The randoms that I played with were extremely "particular" about who was on their team. If you didn't join their lobby with the exact class and build they wanted you to play they would kick you within five seconds. There wasn't a "hey, would you mind playing 'x' class instead?" Or, "Could you run 'this' build instead of 'that' build?" It was just an instant kick back to lobby. And this was within four or five weeks of the game releasing that I started experiencing this. You almost had to play with friends so they wouldn't kick you quicker than you could change your class/loudout around. In a large AAA title that wouldn't be so much of an issue, but for a very niche game in a very niche community, it boggled my mind how quickly people were to try to get people to not want to play the game. Just now looking at the steam charts and the 30-day average is 25 players doesn't surprise me one bit. The developers made an amazing game but the community drove it into the ground.

_childDocuments_.review: The best 3rd-person-iso-realtime-action-campaign-cooperative-shooter of the last decade in my opinion, very addictive...Pro:- mars colony setting- visit and claim areas on the whole planet (like in XCom visiting continents on earth)- operation ship inspired by Xcom, great adaption of moving on the planet map like in Xcom- Great atmosphere   * very detailed graphics which absolutely support the setting of lost colonies/cities  * music is very good at supporting the pressure, the combat action, the unknown, the hordes of mutants, the darkness...)  * Apart from all the other missions types there are story missions and different NPCs that add to the atmosphere- unbelievable number of:  * different enemy mutant types  * weapons, armor modules, mods and upgrades  * items usable in combat - all make sense, can be gathered during a mission, are crucial for survivalGood replay-value because of:- many different primary mission types, in addition randomly seeded different submissions, random spawning points- Very extended research tree- a lot of different soldier classes which can be upgraded, modded and improved in a lot of different aspectsContra:- some missions can get frustrating because of:  - not being able to reach mission objective in time or before being overrun (especially if high infestation levels or HUNTER) because not having/finding explosives for blast doors and not finding any door switches or power stationsOverall:- runs smooth on both my Pcs (GTX1070, RTX, both have SSDs and modern CPUs - some reviewers are complaining about loading times - well, they probably have no SSD but mechanical HDD...)- graphics and sounds are superb, as well as the weapon effects and the destruction of the environment- no bugs and no crashes so far - even with all graphic and sound configurations set to highest quality on 4k ResolutionI ABSOLUTELY RECOMMEND this game for all who love constant weapon action, exciting science fiction settings (Mars, cities/colonies in darkness, hordes of enemies, challenging missions, choice of cooperative or single player game play, important decisions about the next research branch or usage of (always too low) supplies...I think I stop here, you get the idea :)

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 2024-10-01: The bug affecting the assignment of left and right arrow keys for controls has been fixed. If the game receives an overhaul of its bad game design choices and horrible balance at some point in the future, I will update my review to a positive one accordingly. In the meantime, this one stays up.The devs like to pander to a miniscule super-hardcore-everything-needs-to-be-ultra-hard kind of audience, which only makes up a fraction of any player base. Whenever there's a new update, prepare to read pages upon pages of nerfs in the name of "balance". Fun? Who needs to have fun in a game?Also, quite a bit of content (cosmetic content like colors as well as gameplay content like weapon mods introduced with one of the DLC) is locked behind ranks that you can only achieve by completing challenges that are getting harder and harder to achieve, especially for solo players. And this is ON TOP of a ridiculous grind (XP) requirement.Last but not least, a recent "hotfix" suddenly broke the controls for many players, including myself; my controls have been reset and I have not been able to re-bind the left and right arrow keys for movement ever since. It's been a week now and despite the release of 2 or 3 more hotfixes ever since, this game-breaking issue has not been addressed (or even acknowleedged) yet.I may change my review to a more positive one if 1) the control bug is fixed and 2) the balance is actually changed to be fun (again) instead of constant player nerfs all around.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing I picked up a few friends and randoms in discord and went to town. Had a blast, even though we only won a few times. _childDocuments_.review: After playing for a while now and several patches i have to give a thumbs down.While the core gameplay is enjoyable and the Single player campaign is a vast improvement over the first title, the game has not only still some major bugs but big problems in general game design.First the more important topic, the game design.Red solstice tries to be a real time tactical squad shooter with some Arpg sprinkled in, but doesnt really commit to any of those enough.Especially the TACTICAL part is missing sorely in Singleplayer, your AI teammates are often times dumb as rocks, the tactical wheel to give commands is so bare bones its laughable. Your AI teammates arent clever enough to stand their ground on their own, and your commands are so minimal it doesnt feel like a tactical game at all.Furthermore the late game missions evolve mostly around running somewhere , stand your ground, or go in buildings to retrieve something.Stand your ground is in late campaign on anything above NORMAL difficulty nearly impossible for your squad, they arent only dumb and dont focus fire on priority targets, you also cant command them enough, BUUUUT you pretty much go on the highest wave level in an instant. And then you only get swarmed by the hardest hitting, bullet sponge enemies in the game ON MASS.So your only option is to run and gun, shoot a bit run shoot run, and if you ever get swarmed from both sides, for example if you go into a building or an alley, you will just get pummeled to death.There is no TACTIC no engaging combat, its just try to be faster and get lucky to not get swarmed to death, and later every single mission on Hard or above evolves in this, you can never stay still with AI teammates.And the enemies dont really come in "WAVES" you pretty much max out at wave 16 in a few minutes into the mission and the enemy just keeps spawning nonestop, without any breather, AND dont forget the Mission can easily take 30+ minutes with all the Main objectives alone, and you CANT save mid mission, so you easily can waist 45 minutes and die at the end. This core game design alone , the Missions that evolve always in the same way, nonestop hordes, with bad teammate AI and nearly no Tactical controls is already really bad.But lets go on, while i think the timers on EVERTHING can be motivating, the amount is just absurd, you even got timers on the RESOURCE you use to start missions!If you dont have any left, too bad you cant do missions and infection spreads, or you get a mission on the other side of the planet where you have no direct route too and you can only watch how the mission fails and get higher infection rate.Lets go to some still persistent bugs,AI teammates dont listen to command,AI teammates wont attack targets,AI teammates dont register enemy vehicle as targets, so destroy convoy missions are super cancer,sometimes SHIVA nuclear bombs dont spawn in the mission,Main mission objectives get repeated again and again after completing any mission on the map.I could go on..And Performance, the game runs poorly on several good gaming rigs with latest driver updates.It runs same bad on low settings medium as on cinematic settings, in regularly and it seems without reason get drops from 60 fps to 40 or 30. It is still clearly not optimized!To sum it up, while the Main campaign can be fun and is much better then in the first game, the AI makes it really a bad experience. The design of every mission evolving into an endless nonestop swarm is just boring and annoying. The none existent Tactical options are just baffling in such a game. The performance is regularly bad and the game still has several annoying bugs.The only reason to play this game is if you solely wanna play online with others, because nothing can be worse then a bad AI with no tactical options for the commander. But you still with struggle with the rest of the problems.The game clearly needed more development time, and at least 3 months+ playtesting from a decently sized player base, there are so many flaws that just feel lazy, that make you question if there actually has been play testing and feedback to in game systems at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I have high hopes for this game as I enjoyed the first one on another account. The first game was straight up hard and this seems to lower the barrier of entry for all new players to enjoy before jumping to harder difficulties. The mission hub system reminds me of XCOM and requires some time to get used to since the UI sort of jumps around after selecting missions (but at least you can navigate your current mission selections on the icon dock).Multiplayer seems to have similar shenanigans as before minus some of the friendly fire mechanics that have hilariously enough caused mass extinction events (defuse nuke and then shooting it...). I have not played enough of the current game and hope to see some fun map interactions in the future in both single player and multiplayer campaigns!

_childDocuments_.review: (edited)i change my mind, i was recommending this game but now i DONT reccomend this game. and after i did a lot of reviews this is my first time i dont recommend a game. this is the reason: after i lost in campaign and lost everything i spent time there, i tried skirmish, it gives skill poin and requisition points which can be used to unlock stratagem (i thought of helldivers stratagem, i was wrong), the painful truth is: it gives so little reward! you need 70 points to unlock harv vehicle, and winning on normal gives you +9 points or +13 if you wonderfully win some side mission and able to survive wave 16 long enough. so you will need to do miracles 6x to get this harv vehicle!! (or i thought so), BUT .... after through playing it on my spare times i manage to build it, but the truth is too hard, it turns out the button "build" there (instead of "unlock") literally told everything. YOU CAN ONLY HAVE 1!, and it also has term and conditions applied: YOU NEED TO HAVE THE DLC before. so in my case, the harv wont come out because i havent bought the mercs dlc (im glad i didnt), and my precious 70 points of requisition points gone! i was really wasting my time to grind skirmishes on spare time on my weekend just to get one time use item. (why theres no warning or locked sign that it needs to have dlc first)really, i've never been so frustrated like this with a game before, i was wasting time spent 30 hours trying to win campaign in vain, then another wasting time spent to unlocking stratagem also not worthy. ...........it only 1x use. if theres still anything left that is skill points. but this is also need spent so much time to grind. (sigh) i just dont want to continue this anymore. i just feel the need to warn the others, thats why i update my review to avoid misleading(this is my previous review)i recommend this game, the fight in the field and the job skills and weapons are very satisfying BUT the campaign systems is so confusing and complex and overwhelming:1. too many informations without a hint which one should go first,  yes there're lots of explanation on everythings but if everything are very important while the resource is minimum which one should i prioritize? 2. clicking area's name means going there, also it means wasting precious time (each mission has deadline and punishment when expired). be careful.3. very few deployment points to start a mission with those deadline, and when the mission expired it makes the infestation spread goes up, and when the infestation level going 100% its game over. maybe im missing something but heres what i was facing as a total newbie in this xcom genre: they give you 10/10 deployment point, each mission usually cost 6-9 points (you can increase the difficulty to decrease the deployment point needed, example: 6 into 4) so basically with 10 points you can only do 1 or 2 mission max, then after that nothing to do, only waiting to the resupply day, BUT while waiting and walking around, the more urgent missions coming out but nothing to do until they are expired, so it means global infestation level going up. and it goes looping like that. 4. game over means all the efforts is lost, buildings, the jobs, moduls, weapons, team level, all is gone and you need to restart the campaign all over again. (here goes my 30 hours plays campaign)so once again, for me as a new player in this genre, this game is very confusing, especially the campaign is not fun at all, its kinda a losing war against infestation (you cannot stop the infestation to spread, just delay it) and the research, resource management, and upgrades are all very frustrating on the contrary my recommendation to play this game is playing skirmish, your efforts and time spent wont be lost in there ( i mean unlocking skill tree points, stratagems and team level/experiences are permanent)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty hard if you play solo, you are reliant on an AI that is in need of some serious improvement.Tutorial doesn't teach how to maintain bots ammo, searching containers seems to be the only way to restore depleted ammo. Interacting with field armories also resupplies squad, but those are hard to find.I also encountered a lot of path-finding bugs, squad mates get stuck in random spots which could vary from out in the middle of no where, to getting pushed into a corner. If you order your squad mates to follow you and run into a thin corner (like the corner of a building), one of your bots will most like run head strong through a horde to reach the other side of the corner (my guess, is to remain in the players formation).I heard that some other people were experiencing desync issues with online multiplayer, personally I didn't experience any problems with desyncing.There is a couple other nit picky things but I want to make this brief.The game is still fun, despite its flaws I really like the changes from OG RS. Making the maps procedural and the new X-Com-esque campaign is pretty awesome and completely unexpected.Definitely worth a go if you are a fan of the series or if you want to try something new.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game for nearly 700 hours, it sucks... that I still haven't got that final rank promotion yet. Keep it on "normal" difficulty level for campaign to play story, although you can adjust the difficulty level every single mission if needed anyway. Want to play on Very Hard or Nightmare, prepare to learn what works and what doesn't. A lot of the recent negative reviews are just wrong in my eyes, as I see no P2W or even necessary DLCs. If you're playing the game solo you definitely don't need any DLC, and if you're playing online then it helps but there are plenty of viable classes, skills, and weapons just in the basic version of the game to keep you plenty competitive.Personally I've had a lot of un-serious fun with this, combined with a small group of friends. We don't run 8-man missions, we use bots, we play silly builds, we horse around and get killed a lot, and yes on the hardest difficulties it can be VERY unforgiving... but then don't play that one.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is interesting and deep on paper, but suffers from a sever lack of polishing in many aspects.It's confusing, difficult to read, lack on the action feedback side and not beginner friendly.It feels the devs made the game of their dreams without putting themselves in the shoes of players who are not in their head.- UI can be confusing and a chore (going from character loadout to weapon customization to skill tree to adjust your build can be frustrating as you have to go back and forth between screens a lot to achieve what you want) (having character customization / server browser / wiki on the same screen level can become confusing very fast for a new player).- Some customization option feels like a placeholder: you select "deploy" a vehicle but it does not appear in game and it's not clear how to actually do it? Unclear how to make a bot level up, to use more skills? Can they actually level up?- Lack of information in general: effect of damage type? What does electricity do exactly? What's the stun chance per shot if it stuns? what's the downside of using overwatch rather than manual aiming? What's the difference between "piercing" and "armor breaking"? etc- The game has a lot of potential for build crafting, but the lack of information described above suppress it.- Lack of punch feedback from weapons (sounds and impact is lacking for most weapons)- Some icons on the map are not displayed in the legend- Difficult to read what is happening in the middle of the action (is your character shooting or reloading? At what? What is hitting you or what killed you?)- It feels like a game of numbers overall: you don't feel as you shot a creature, rather than you are applying a certain amount of damage point that are removed from its health pool. This feels strongly with enemies with armor and/or high regen.- As mentioned above, the game actions feels quite flat, contrary of titles like Heldivers for example.I still recommend the game as it is an interesting experience, but this title will require heaps of polishing to be truly engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 is a bleak ordeal, but it’s not without its charms. There’s a real sense of frantic desperation created as the player scrambles desperately from one mission to the next, helplessly watching the global infection meter always climbing. Whether it’s zombie biomass, sinister corporations, or environmental catastrophe, for the entirety of Red Solstice 2′s play time I was sure that we were only ever a hair’s breadth away from extermination — which only served to make fighting against it feel all the more satisfying. If the developers could ease the repetitiveness from their random mission generator, this would be one of the best successors to XCOM’s legacy, but in its current state it’s just an extremely solid squad-based RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has everything I enjoy about a Co-op game. Its reminiscent of the Marine Undead Assault/Survival games from starcraft.  There IS friendly fire so skills are required.  Each of the larger mutations has certain methods you will have to experiment to kill.  The game requires you to be able to think on the move and coordinating with your allies.  There is a Campaign that can be fun for the single player aspect, but most people I know focus on Skirmish.  There is a large skill tree that unlocks additional goodies for each class (some of which can be shared between classes) that makes customizing your marine fun.  I recommend this game, for what it's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW UPDATED TO "POSITIVE", but the issues remain, so I will keep the original review here. Updated comment on "EDIT 3"."dear devs: please raise the limit to AI followers to 7, not 3.you're assuming that the game will do so well that it will be easy to fill up the remaining 4 slots with real players. but it's not. by forcing an AI follower limit of 3 you're making the game artificially harder and less fun, which in turn drives players away, making it harder and harder to fill those empty slots.there are good things about this game, and i can see it doing well, but your..."encouragement" of multiplayer by limiting AI followers as a huge detriment, and is anything but subtle.EDIT 1: played a bunch more. again, still, the campaign is not winnable unless you get your friends to buy the game, too. very manipulative, devs.EDIT 2: so you can see i've played a bunch of this game. again, this game has a ton of promise. but still the devs refuse to budge to make this game a suitable solo experience. if you want the full experience with 7 allies, you need to get your friends to buy the game, which is very anti-consumer."EDIT 3: I wholeheartedly disagree with the idea that 7 AI followers would be too large a detriment to the experience. There are various ways to mitigate the "clumsiness" of 7 followers. Slower time dilation to allow for more precise commands. Color-coded AI markers on the map and on the HUD, color-coded lines to quickly track where they are, as well as distance values and names, color-coded tactical outlines like in the classic Star Wars Republic Commando, enable custom names, etc. Any combination of these will make it manageable. I would argue that 7 AI followers would bring back the "tactical" in this "tactics shooter", cause right now you just run and gun with your 3 followers and hope for the best. 7 AI followers would actually encourage you to place them in strategic positions cause they actually stand a chance with out you in bigger numbers, whereas sending a lone AI follower alone is a death sentence. so yeah. there is room for 7 followers, and there are ways to make it work. Again, I absolutely disagree that this cannot work.^However, I appreciate that the devs are continually patching their game. And I appreciate that they reached out to me. All in all I'm personally done with the game, but a positive review might bring someone else in, cause all in all it's still is an enjoyable game. I understand that being a small dev team is hard, so the support should help.

Still not happy at all about Skirmish mode losing the core feature of AI helpers, because this kills most of the game's replayability for me, which was its main draw, but Story Mode can be enjoyed anyway like that.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the gameplay of this game. Never played Red Solstice 1, but this is a refreshing take on real-time strategic squad elements and killing swarms of enemies. Game really ramps up with higher difficulties and is awesome playing with multiple people. Excited to dive into more of the campaign; my first attempt on Hard difficulty kicked my butt, so am restarting a different runthrough.Gameplay reminds me of Helldivers (the top-down shooting), XCOM (squad classes/strategy, and the campaign system), and MOBAs (for the skillbar, some of the control scheme and in-mission leveling). Combining these has made for a really fun concoction.I will admit some of the interface is initially a little confusing, but the devs are already commenting on the other reviews that they're aware and they're actively updating in the meantime. I'm optimistic about what they're doing. I have not had any crashes yet, game plays like a dream!

_childDocuments_.review: I need to admit I have been playing back in 2022 and have been back to it today and my first observations: Middle button camera rotating has been limited - you can no longer change the free angle - it has been limited to a few angles by scrolling. The free-angle camera was one of the best features in this game. now it feels like a limitation. please change it back. _childDocuments_.review: I loved this mod back in the day on Warcraft 3 but it just doesn't work for me as a standalone game (I hated the first Red Solstice standalone game). I think it's because the experiences before were so small scale. Like I could pop in, play one game that MAYBE would last an hour, but usually 30 min or less, and be done. Don't get me wrong, I love squad based RTS games. Dawn of War 2 being my all-time favorite. I just think this game misses the mark. The graphics are a little brown, the story is thoroughly uninteresting, and the characters are boring space marine archetypes with no character to their aesthetic (like Warhammer 40k space marines or Starcraft), which doesn't help anything either. Controls and moment to moment gameplay were functional and tight, but a bit hollow. I don't think my experience is going to be mirrored by everyone, so feel free to give this game a chance, especially if you are starved for squad based RTS games.I would bet this game is infinitely more fun as a multiplayer ONLY experience. That's where the roots of this game come from and where they should stay. I should've maybe just focused on that, but meh. I'm over it. On to the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was really looking forward to this because I thought it would be Helldivers with far more customization and RPG elements. _childDocuments_.review: RS2 starts out great, and I had a blast for the couple of hours, but the difficulty ramped up ridiculously fast and got out of hand. I'm facing foes that either don't take damage, or regen up the damage I did while my guys reload. Maybe I messed up my tactical overlay gameplay because there's no tutorial for it and I had no clue what what I did for a few hours. Either way, I'm not having fun anymore. So this was a short-lived experience.The action footage you see here on the store page, that's the first hours of the game. Later on it's bulletsponge gallore and everything is just tedious and annoying. I stopped playing RS1 because it was a bit to hard for my taste, so I should have known better. I just thought the devs balanced it out better since RS2 was so fun at first.---Update: The above was written when I played the single player campaign only. Because of the in-game ranking system that requires you to play multiplayer I started to do that and haven't touched the campaign anymore. The community is a bit toxic so multiplayer is a mixed bag depending on the players you get in the team. It can be awesomely fun if the team works together, and other times you're team-killed because you missed a order among a gazillion notifications that all spam the same chat-box. Besides the chat, another issue with multiplayer is that the server browser clearly tells you the difficulty of the game you're joining, but doesn't inform you if the host changes it. I've joined so many Normal games that turned out to be Very Hard when launched. Multiplayer however, gets old fast because there's so few objectives. You're doing the same thing over, over and over again.  The game can be fun but it's also so frustrating, and the frustration is too common. It could be great with a few fixes though, like a campaign tutorial, a ranking system doable in single player, a proper chat that beeps when players send messages and a lobby that updates and shows changes once a host makes them. A bonus would also be if the campaign in multiplayer mode was a bit more engaging for the non-hosts. Let them see the map and the choices the Host makes instead of just waiting in a lobby.---Update 2: I restarted the Single player campaign in v1.5 and you still hit a difficulty wall after a while. Took me longer this time because I now know a bit more about how to play the tactical overlay part of the game, but I've reached a halt again on normal difficulty. This game is not single player friendly at all. You can only use 4 out 8 slots of marines, and the 3 AI buddies joining you can not use necessary skills and equipment like explosives and giving them explosive weapons just results in them killing the whole team. You're simply outgunned and it's no fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend the game, I really do, but it has alot of issues that need to be addressed. The primary issue is that the game offers the most barebones basic tutorials and nothing else really from there after the beginning of the game.  I wasn't even aware I had 9 points to put into my combat suit until I accidentally stumbled into the tab for it. The game doesn't inform you that you need to research, it doesn't let you know how to change your soldiers load outs, your load out, it doesn't tell you what resources are for, it doesn't explain anything at all, and this is a fairly indepth game. There are options to buy stuff and to add stuff to your missions but I have no idea how to do that. I get it, in the age of games "Holding your hand" it's nice when I developer steps back and takes the training wells off, but the game, any game needs an explanation for it's mechanics. Also on my second mission after the tutorial I was completely overran, the enemies kept pouring in from all directions, for no rhyme or reason at all, and not during a wave. Which resulted in a mission loss. Compared to the prior two missions I have no idea what or why it happened. This isn't a "Git Gud" issue either, I'm going to have to spoil the game for myself and watch a 3rd/4th party youtuber teach me how to play the game.IF the game adds a tutorial I think it would be infinitely better.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello,I (solo player) really tried to love this game (as you can also see on my 48 hours playtime in this moment) and started 2 campaigns which I both now quit due to the same issues which prevent me from having any more fun.This game is in itself amazing, the early game is a tad slow but picks up very fast and gets really interesting when you unlocked more classes and start thinkering about your optimal squad composition in order to tackle all the very varied missions you have to do in order to prevent the infection from spreading. This means, from early to mid game this game really shines!Sadly the late game is the part I've quitted this game twice (and this time forever) now.At some point and especially at one of the later missions of the campaign you just get curbstomped beyond beliefs. You might be able to kill all the "standard" mutants with more or less ease (even the heavy mutants are still doable) BUT now you just get big mutants thrown in your face which are almost unkillable. You can burn, freeze, bomb or rocket them as often as you got ammo for these weapons but they are just shrugging it off while debuffing you into the ground so you can't move, see or shoot back anymore while they slowly maul you to death. You managed to kill ONE of them? Cool, now the game throws 2 more of those mutants at you which is more or less your moment you basically give up the mission.These situations are the reason why I can't recommend nor enjoy this game anymore. Sure I maybe did something wrong or I'm just a bad player but I can't even remotely see where my error is or where I'm doing something wrong even after researching possible mistakes in the steam discussions and the internet.So I'm for my self can't recommend this game because of the insane scaling of some of the heavy mutants in the game while you can't do ♥♥♥♥ against them when you're alone. Don't know if those missions are more possible with friends but as a singleplayer I won't touch it ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I like just about everything about it. Sometimes in top-down games the angle is awkward and I have difficulty moving and seeing, but the viewing angles in this game are perfect. I like how the different choices between classes, skills, and weapons allow you to play what you like and still be relatively successful in missions. Single player and co-op are equally fun, so I'm excited to level on my own without my friends. My favorite part is the movement targeting, especially in buildings. I'm not always good at navigating small debris on the field and the game takes care of that for me. The game is also a joy to watch and look at. From the monsters to the tools, the lockers, the players, it's a fun, realistic cartoon version of an apocalyptic nightmare. I especially love the explosions and all the different ways to make them happen. I love setting off a chain reaction and hopefully getting the enemies caught in the middle instead of my teammates. The only criticism is dealing with the camera lock and a few keybindings, but I think the issues have been fixed and I've figured out what works best for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 is in style a strange sort of descendant of single unit RTS maps in its controls. The most notable genre that evolved from that is MOBAs, but Red Solstice's focus is a little different. I wouldn't say that the enemy designs are especially inspired, but the overall big picture gameplay of scavenging through buildings as cool power armor guys (That you can customise the abilities and weapons of HEAVILY) while fighting for your life against various monsters with different characteristics to memorise (Knowing the enemy is quite important to take them down efficiently) is very cool. The campaign overworld mechanics are surprisingly in depth, if poorly explained, and while I at first thought I was dealing with something akin to Star Wars Battlefronts 2's domination it is genuinely comparable to XCOM.This game is impossibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard if you play it solo, even on Easy difficulty, so make sure you have some bros to play it with. In exchange however, you'll find this game supports an unprecedented 8 players in Co-op for every mission. You can split into multiple squads to pursue separate objectives (The objectives system is, I would say, a strength of this game) and still be surrounded by as many buddies as a regular game would offer you, or group up into a veritable army (Considering that there are friendly NPCs as well) fending off a tide of enemies. Pub games are available, but only barely.NGL game is a bit buggy sometimes, but the development cycle is extremely active so you are, at least, unlikely to see the same bugs week to week.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for March 2022. If you are interested in the game and it's before April 5th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Another Real-Time Tactical game Red Solstice didn’t interest me after two missions, they were story-based missions to get players ready for this game and I almost turned off the game due to how boring and lacking these missions were.  I then played another mission, the first randomized mission and I suddenly got it.  This is a game that takes a while to get started, and players will need to stick with this game to get through some rough patches, but when you do, you get a nice randomized multiplayer experience.The game does have traces of X-com where you build out a squad, and can either play with AI or other players.  This is a game people can put hundreds of hours in but I’d probably find something else.   The UI holds back a lot of the game and there are some bizarre choices, like adding WASD keys to move the character around but the game isn’t designed for that type of twin-stick shooter gameplay and it’s obvious.  Oddly enough there’s also barely any music during the missions either.  It’s barren.Pick this up if you want more action than Desperadoes, or have a group to play with.  With 8 players, multiplayer is definitely what this game is designed for, but at the same time, I don’t feel like returning to this game.  If you’re a huge fan of real time tactics, you’ll like it, but almost everything I did resulted in a “hold this position for two minutes. _childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 throws you headfirst into a desperate fight for humanity's survival.  Earth, ravaged by a bio-engineered plague and overrun by grotesque mutant hordes, is your backdrop. As a squad leader of hardened marines, you'll orchestrate tactical battles, manage precious resources, and make split-second decisions in a constant dance with extinction. Buckle up, soldier, because Red Solstice 2 isn't for the faint of heart, but for those who crave a deep and rewarding strategy experience, it's a triumph.Red Solstice 2 masterfully blends real-time strategy elements with intense action.  You'll oversee your squad from a top-down perspective, issuing commands, deploying defensive structures, and managing resources to secure objectives. The action on the ground, however, is where the game truly shines. You can directly control any member of your squad, diving into the thick of battle with a satisfying twin-stick shooter experience. This allows you to experience the desperation and chaos of the fight firsthand, making strategic decisions all the more impactful.Red Solstice 2 throws away the idea of expendable soldiers often found in strategy games. Each marine under your command is a vital asset, with customizable upgrades and unique abilities. Losing a squad member is a significant blow, not just strategically, but emotionally. The game masterfully conveys the weight of each decision, making victories all the sweeter and defeats all the more bitter.Red Solstice 2 truly shines in co-op mode. Coordinating tactics with friends in real-time adds an exhilarating layer of complexity. Teamwork becomes essential as you navigate sprawling maps, strategically deploy outposts, and unleash devastating combined attacks on overwhelming enemy hordes. Sharing the burden of command and the elation of hard-won victories with friends creates a truly unforgettable experience.Beneath the surface of Red Solstice 2 lies a wealth of strategic options. You'll need to manage resources like biomass (harvested from slain enemies) to fuel your squad's abilities and deploy crucial outposts. These outposts provide vital support, allowing you to heal, rearm, and call in reinforcements. Researching new technologies unlocks powerful upgrades for your squad and opens up new strategic possibilities.The mutant hordes in Red Solstice 2 are a relentless and diverse enemy force. From hulking brutes to swarming swarms and ranged attackers, each enemy type requires a different approach.  Learning their strengths and weaknesses, and adapting your tactics on the fly, is key to survival. The boss encounters are particularly epic, demanding precise teamwork and a well-coordinated strategy to overcome.Red Solstice 2's world is a harsh and unforgiving place. The environments, though detailed and atmospheric, are a constant reminder of the struggle humanity faces. Yet, amidst the bleakness, there are glimmers of hope.  The scattered settlements of survivors, the occasional friendly AI drone, and the unwavering determination of your squad all contribute to a narrative that's more about the fight for survival than a grand hero's journey.Red Solstice 2 is a demanding game, but for those who crave a deep and rewarding strategy experience, it's a gem.  The blend of real-time action, squad management, and resource management creates a unique and thrilling gameplay loop.  Whether you choose to fight alone or squad up with friends, Red Solstice 2 offers a brutal yet unforgettable journey through a world on the brink. If you're looking for a strategic challenge that will test your skills and reward your perseverance, then Red Solstice 2 is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you play NOTD? Do you miss the panicked fun of running around in the dark, being pursued by hordes of monsters, while trying to gather items and complete objectives without running out of ammo or killing your teammates (looking at you, demo)? Are you looking for something to play with friends and be challenged?If so, this is the game you've been looking for. To be honest I've barely touched the single player so I can't really speak intelligently about the campaign but what little time I've spent in it seems neat and a good way to get introduced to the game. My friends and I picked this up to relive some of the NOTD fun and it does a great job capturing the experience in a modern system. I never played RS1 and didn't know this was a thing so I was very pleasantly surprised to find this and much happier to see it was a worthy value once I started playing. It is very easy to load up and jump right into a skirmish with friends. The first few games you'll die pretty quickly while learning the basics of how to survive and complete basic objectives. After that the time will just melt away as you try different loadouts and combinations with your team. The skill tree offers a great level of depth to continued play as you can consistently unlock more minor buffs or additional options to enhance your experience. Visuals are good but not perfect. Sound is great and the music does a good job of building tension throughout play. The controls work great and feels natural for the gameplay. Multiplayer with up to eight players total? Heck yeah. Progression system so I'm cleverly tricked into thinking my repeated deaths are adding something to my overall skill development? Excellent, just what I needed. Honestly though the skill tree is pretty well implemented and when I opened it the first time I was surprised at the level of depth and breadth.There are a lot of complaints of bugs in other reviews but I've played this for easily 15 hours so far and have only a few minor issues. The devs have already been releasing patches and hotfixes though and my experience has been exceedingly positive so far. If you are really picky and don't expect to ever run into a bug then I'm not sure why you would play any new game, these days every game has to work out the kinks. The level selection currently is not very significant for multiplayer, but the game just launched so I'll be happy if they keep adding content as some of the maps are much easier and not nearly the same level of challenge even when you configure the difficulty sliders appropriately. Adding a ping system would also be super helpful for trying to coordinate with teammates. If you want a single player game this might be for you. I've had a little fun in SP so far, but honestly it has been overwhelmingly multiplayer for me and I have thoroughly enjoyed it. This is a great co-op experience just jumping into skirmishes and throwing some friends in the mix for some enjoyable chaos.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice is a game that requires some hours put into it dealing with some possible (likely) frustration before really enjoying it and grasping it, or at least that was the case for me. I played Red Solstice 1 and had some difficulty getting into it, but ended up loving it once I understood what was going on. There are definitely some bugs (so far the patches have been pretty good) and at times strange tool-tips/explanations on skills and whatnot, but with time I imagine they'll improve. Currently what is there is pretty enjoyable for a decent amount of time since missions spontaneously spawn/generate and there's a decent amount of them that can occur - pair that with a lot of difficulty options and there's a good amount of stuff to sink into. Class customization is a little strange at first, but there are some fun builds that you can do once you unlock the right skills. Unlocking skills early on is pretty easy and while it does become a bit more difficult later - resetting/respeccing isn't terribly penalizing (1% total xp) in general. It's a tough game and at higher levels requires a decent amount of communication, but I recommend it despite the flaws that are there because the core is great and I think the community is largely very passionate for the series. If you're a fan of Alien Swarm or things like that - I'd highly recommend Red Solstice. Don't be afraid to ask people for help either; there's a lot on the screen at once sometimes and it can be overwhelming. See you in game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not understand the current mixed rating for this game. It rarely crashes but hey, which software is without bugs. Devs have a good cadence in releasing patches so it is not a game that is thrown on the market and then abandoned.You can choose between six different classes and adjust skills and equipment to your liking. Here again teamwork is the key in completing the mission objectives. With XP you advance in rank, unlock classes and skills.Every player can paint paths on the map so for a group leader it is quite easy to give a direction.If you like multiplayer co-op and controling a small sci-fi marine trooper together with other people on a tactical level, this a game is for you.I had and have lot's of fun so can only recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: After completing the campaign I cannot recommend this game. I haven't touched the multiplayer, so from opinions may differ from a pure multiplayer perspective. This review is bases on version 1.3 and 1.2Strategic LayerMechanis are poorly explained ingame and no, I will not watch YT Tutorials or read this up on the Discord. Mechanics have to be explained ingame or have to be self-explaining and RS2 fails to deliver on both aspects. Overall this seems like tacked on and not as an integral part of the game, as opposed to games like X-Com. Tactical MissionsFirst impressions were quite good, but over time things changed to meh and in some cases to bad. In the beginning its feels good to mow down hordes of Strol-Mutants, but this gets repetitive quiet fast, as the regular enemies have low health, run straight at you and show no special tactics or abilities. At least I haven't noticed this. Sooner than later stronger mutants start showing up and if you haven't concentrated on developing stronger classes, weapons and modules they become overwhelming fast. And even if you did many enemies are incredible annoying bullet sponges. Some have unique abilities like ranged attacks, leaping attacks or area attacks, but it mostly boils down to "don't let them get in melee distance and kill them fast". Also the diference between difficulties are very steep. On Normal some missions will leave you very little chances of success while on easy the opposite becomes true. This is further aggravated as enemy types progress without any (perceivable) connection to story / tech progress. Without rushing certain technologies the missions get difficult fast. Speaking of difficulty: The random generation of maps and missions, especially where you start and where you have to go, make some missions swingy. Got lucky random numbers and all is well, but if your unlucky and don't have the right abilities / techs? Tough luck. One mission was especially bad, as I had to reach a certain point in a time limit. Ok, I made the mistake that my Executor was not the fastest but also not incredible slow, but it was impossible to reach it. I could have made a faster built, used certain sprint abilities, etc. but the point is - giving the player a whole lot of options but screw by RNG if not using the right built is poor design for me. Another problem of non-story missions is the renadom generation as I had the impression most maps became quite repetitive and sometimes looked the same. As maps are not different depending in which region the mission takes place, its not even possible to force some variety into the game. Ok, different types of missions used different types of maps, but as you have little control which missions you get and sometimes rewards and infestation levels determine which mission you have to take, this is also no remedy for this problem.Conclusion:This game had/has potential to become a good game and maybe the multiplayer is already a good game, but don't buy it as a singleplayer game. _childDocuments_.review: Updated an earlier review from not recommended to recommended for a few reasons.First thing I want to mention is the devs are really down to Earth and wholesome. They are also really open to feedback and I don't just mean are willing to take feedback and maybe implement it, I mean they actively seek feedback out and are legitimately curious on how they can improve the game. One of the devs added me on Steam after I posted my original review to chat and ask for feedback. Some of the best devs i've come across hands down, and I remember talking to them when they were still developing Red Solstice 1 and they told me they originally made some spinoff maps of Night of the Dead in Warcraft 3 (which I can tell heavily inspired Red Solstice).For one if you intend to play this game co-op with a friend/friends or intent to play skirmish with a group of players, I highly recommend that. Red Solstice 2 is a game that grabs you way more than you would think, which is for a couple of reasons I believe. For one its something different, there's very few games like it, additionally, there's a nostalgia factor here stemming from old Warcraft and Starcraft maps, provided you played them and finally, even though the XCOM style campaign globe is perhaps slightly less indepth as XCOM2, it still adds a lot of depth to the campaign.As for the somewhat downsides of the game, well they come from if you intend to play the campaign solo. The issues currently the game has when solo mostly comes down to problems with AI (they can't use secondary weapons very well) and in my opinion the game is slightly too difficult for a solo player (probably because of what I mentioned before), All this is being improved in a future patch I am told and I expect it will improve because 1.3 already made it less of an issue. If you intend to play solo, I suggest holding off until 1.4 or 1.5 for when these issues are improved, or for the time being suck it up and play on at most normal difficulty ;).Only other issues I have are some things are lacking in the explanation department, but that improved considerably in 1.3, and the capture mechanic is a little difficult to understand and a bit clunky to pull off, but it was one of the pieces of feedback I gave.tldr. Highly recommend the game for co-op and skirmish multiplayer especially if you liked old Warcraft 3 maps like Night of the Dead. If you are playing solo, either hold off till the next patch or two, or play on an easier difficulty.
