_childDocuments_.review: And underrated gem among isometric squad based games. I have been addicted to this game since the time I bought it on a whim hoping for a twinstick shooter along the lines of Alien Swarm or similar games. The great thing is that you can switch from a twin-stick shooter or a tactical control mode and can do so at will while a mission is on going. The gameplay can get a little repetitive and grindy, but there is a lot of variety of builds, classes, skills, weapons, and maps to try out a lot of different tactics on. Finding out you can even mod weapons, use and mod vehicles as well, adds a nice level of customization and replay ability as well. I have not completed the Elysium campaign but It has some replayability as well, especially if you get DLC addons and get no less than five different ones. They all have varying levels of difficulty and provide different challenges as well as unique missions. I don't know if I'm a huge fan of the doomsday counter campaigns but it does make sense in a game where an infestation is destroying the world.If you don't like isometric games, squad based games, or a little rep/grindy stuff you may not like this one. However it you like challenging RTS squad based combat where you can tweak the settings then you will most likely enjoy this one. It can be a little buggy at times and some controls can get a little weird (especially tank feels like driving on ice) but otherwise It's a fun game that can keep you entertained for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: after putting a good amount of time into this game and also being a veteran of the last one I’ll give my honest input of this game.Now I without a doubt enjoyed this game both multiplayer and campaign. The controls and gameplay are great and give me the feeling I am in control of my character. This is a game where it gives the appearance of your typical Turn “auto aim on and kill everything” but if you plan on advancing to higher difficulties you will find out this game has a very high skill ceiling. On top of that with the customization between skills and classes you’ll have a lot of time to experiment. Now the maps you are placed in are pretty generic but add more layers of strategies as well. Do you want to blow up the blast door in your way or bypass it with a skill. Hell you can even just blow through wall. The maps are also littered with vehicles and barrels that you can use to your advantage. Now the monsters that litter this game have a good variety that will keep you alert and offer a number of ways as to which you’ll want to handle it. Now while running and gunning is your go to. You can use skills and proper placement to increase your efficiency on killing enemies and some as you will come to find will require a lot more attention. Now the campaign came a long way from TRS1 and I had a great time playing it. But I will say while the tutorial helps you out in the combat aspect. The way you go about finding missions and researching was a bit of trial and error. I ended up going to the forums a lot. The campaign definitely gives you a sense of impending doom. Your AI are pretty dumb but they follow orders from following you to looting objectives while shooting at anything that moves. The bonus is you can have friends join your campaign which is a huge plus and can alleviate the pain of bots.As for the multiplayer this is the bread and butter of the game. Being able to drop in with seven different players all with different loadouts adds a lot of strategies to the game and so many different ways to customize between loadouts and classes gives this game a great amount of replayability.Now to be fair I will also tell you things I did not enjoy. If you intend to play this game and jump into the campaign I implore you to find guides on the forums and do quite a bit of research before you start because the campaign will mess you up if you do not. The idea of this game is you are trying to kill whatever is spreading the infestation if you do not know the ins and outs of slowing it down the worse the infestation gets along with the difficulty. it gets to the point where you literally can’t do drops anymore and you’ll get a game over. If you are the type of person that wants to play solely campaign missions back and forth you’ll need to learn to slow your pace down you will have to do quite a few randomly generated missions in between. That includes spamming research and ignoring missions do not do that. Another problem I have is your AIs are dumb as dirt with little variety to the classes besides passive abilities. That being said you can complete the campaign with them but all in all they are glorified turrets. Overall I would give this game a 7/10 But basing it on the campaign I would give it a 6/10 while multiplayer is 8/10If you enjoy multiplayer tactical shooters it’s worth the buy. If you only play single player you can buy it at your own risk.Additional review as of 8/17/22I decided to do an additional review for this game with the addition of 4 DLCsThis game has come a long way and has gotten a lot better… A LOT better.First and foremost this game now has WASD controls and I have to say as a helldivers player I absolutely love this and I find myself switching between the two modes. It’s a great addition and was specifically put in from the input of the community. The devs do watch the forums and adjust accordingly which is a godsend. The game has also added customization to your weapons. So you can tailor your weapon to your needs an example would be giving your medic a rocket launcher or lightening the weapon to allow more movement speed and finally give it the proper paint job it deserves! As for the final big point Vehicles have just been added to the game and they feel like real vehicles from the Agility of Your HARV aka scout vehicle to the massive firepower from your tank. In addition to to this you have a total of five campaigns to choose from. This game has come a long way and has found a way to reignite the fire I have for it. I would like to touch on a point for people looking to buy the game. The foundation for this game is solid, and the rollout for the amount of new/upcoming content is really really quick but it does come with a price. The game does have bugs. Not to the point of unplayability but the game does have them. It’s never stopped me from enjoying the game and the team is very quick to address them. They have a response time of a few days. I only mention this because the developers are very keen on listening to their community and looking to constantly improve the game. The game gets updated and with it the chance of encountering new bugs is present. If you are looking for a game that intends to evolve into an even better one I would buy it. If you prefer a bug free game that never intends to improve itself. I would recommend not buying this. For the campaigns I’ll give it a 7.5/10 As for multiplayer I’ll give it a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Supposedly, the campaigns are a bit of a mess with the story pacing being weird and the story itself being kinda meh. Wouldn't know, haven't gotten through one of them yet, and that's not why you're here.You're here to shoot monsters. And there are *a lot* of monsters to shoot. Not just 5 million zombies either - there's an impressive variety of enemies ranging from cannon fodder to moderate threats to bosses and mini bosses to the dreaded Fluffy. Enemies feel unique, strong enemies feel challenging.The variety doesn't end with the enemies - you've got a good number of different classes and weapons. There's also vehicles and weapon modification, but both of those are locked behind DLC, which I'd place firmly in the "get if you enjoy the game" category. Each class feels unique and potent in their own way, from the basic assault and medic, to the hellfire tanking bosses while burning the world, to the recon dropping artillery strikes, to the marksman hiding in the center of the map deleting every big bad that gets within their vision range.Difficulty is heavily customisable, and while you are encouraged to go through higher difficulties to get to higher ranks, nothing's locked behind them. Everything's relatively easy to get to on its own, but there's a lot of stuff so filling out your unlocks will take some time.In short, this game is fun. Give it a shot

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun shooter-brawler zombie survival game that would be a blast to play co-op or solo. With enemy hordes coming in waves that get progressively stronger the longer you are in the field, it can make for some versatile mission runs if you're up for the challenge. Additional secondary objectives that spawn give you a purpose to stick it out and get those extra supplies for your mobile base or rescue civilians to recruit as specialists for your operations, which can be spent like a resource to train combat AI operatives, build engineering items, or perform research in your lab. Each of your AI operatives have their own skill progression and ranking system, a load-out that can be fine-tuned with augments and an expanding arsenal once you get the technological progression going. Though these operatives do have an 'extra lives' system where they can respawn after being defeated in a deployment, your operatives are  immortal. Once they lose all their lives from repeated incapacitation without healing injuries sustained (done by removing your operative from your active squad for some R&R at base for the length of in-game days), they will be gone for good. Pick and choose your missions for the best rewards and greatest threat level and do your best to keep the infection levels low across the planet, all to save Mars from the alien STROL mutant invasion!

_childDocuments_.review: There are some good ideas here, but fundamentally flawed at its core.As a new player, I should be expected to NOT extract alive. The rogue like aspect is what keeps players returning for more. Its also what keeps the game fresh, as the harder it gets, the more players have to utilize different strategies to survive. As it stands I could probably semi afk play this on my phone and be fine.Movement and kiting should be the heart of soul of the genre. Forcing players to move prevents stale turret base defense game play. Forcing players to kite promotes teamwork and should be borne out of necessity. After all the whole point of a horde is that you cant shoot them all. Currently either the dps is too high or horde size too small.If the devs ever read this, please look at starcraft 2s undead assault chronicles for ideas, or its predecessors on warcraft 3 undead assault/swat.

_childDocuments_.review: (I am mostly touching on the Singleplayer since I found it got the most significant improvements overall)As a fan of the first Red Solstice, I have to say that the sequel improves in virtually every way. The singleplayer campaign alone is no longer a preset series of missions, but instead a Xcom style world-map where you tackle objectives in-between the major narratives while also upgrading and leveling your soldiers who can permanently die (although MUCH more forgiving than Xcom as you lose them if they go down in 3 consecutive missions, so simply keeping a roster and rotating the wounded will allow them to recover).Still on the topic of singleplayer. THE A.I. SQUADMATES DO NOT NEED TO BE COMPLETELY MICROMANAGED! HOORAY! Yes! You heard me right! The A.I. squad that follows you around will actually use their abilities whenever they are available, and will largely stick to following your character without any input/command. HOWEVER! By holding down the ALT key, you slow down time and get a small contextual menu that allows you to quickly and easily command your individual teammates when you want to position them or order one to break down a door while you focus on holding off the infected."But wait, what about multiplayer?" you might ask. Well good news everybody! Your friends (or other players if set to open) CAN join your ongoing campaign and serve as a squadmate. What's even better than doing a co-op campaign to cleanse the infected from the surface of Mars? MISSION PARAMETERS! You can tweak the variables of missions to your own preferences, beyond just changing a difficulty setting. Whether you want enemy waves to appear instantly at the start of the game, or prolong the time you have to gather resources. Or perhaps you want "Air Support" which will destroy half (or nearly all) of the buildings on the map and their resources, but in turn have a much weakened enemy presence for the early stages of the map. There are a variety of little tweaks here and there to make every match more varied and adjustable for your skill level. And what's even better? The variables are based on upgrades/facilities you build in the regions during the Campaign. Meaning that a fully upgraded region can be set to EZ mode where you can steamroll objectives to get resources for your campaign efforts. Yet ignoring other regions and not actively doing missions will allow the infestation to spread/thrive and actually make all the missions much harder. Creating that Xcom sense of "Do I play it safe and stockpile resources to try and ramp up my research/upgrades quickly? Or should I take more risks to ensure that the enemy doesn't become too overwhelming?".

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Undead Assault Chronicles (the SC2 custom map) mixed with real-time XCOM.The singleplayer campaign is cool, but the addicting replayability of the game is the "Skirmish" multiplayer mode.  8 actual human-controlled players can do some pretty fun stuff together, and the gameplay loop (explore, , exploit, exterminate) is kept fresh due to the variety of classes, monster types, playstyles, and difficulty settings.  Let me expand on that last one.The difficulty settings are very granular.  "Easy" to "Very Hard" settings make stuff harder to kill.  "Infestation" level (1 to 7) makes  stuff spawn.  "Horde Speed" (Immediate to Glacial) changes  stuff spawns.  Easy/2/normal can be basically soloed.  Normal/2/quick can be completed with some buddies.  Very Hard/3/quick needs 8 people who know what they're doing.  Difficulties above that (more infestation level / speed) basically needs 8 people on comms with specialized builds.  The game's discord is very helpfully placed in the upper right of the actual game itself.  Join it -- find a group and start kickin butt.

_childDocuments_.review: This is both the most fun and most annoying game I'm playing right now. It's like a combination of XCOM and Helldivers. I don't want to put this game down, but sometimes I just have to walk away. There have been a couple of annoying bugs. Once a primary objective was placed completely off the map, forcing me to abort a mission and incur a failure penalty. A few other times AI squad members have gotten stuck in pieces of the environment, causing me to lose them for the rest of the mission. I'm sure these issues will be ironed out in soon-to-come patches. I have also found some things are not very well explained, even if you read all of the fluff material such as the bestiary and the tutorial sections. For instance, one time I beat wave 15 of the horde, and no more enemies spawned. I'm not sure if that was a bug, or a feature for a specific type of mission, because another time I beat wave 15...and then it spawned never ending high level enemies until I died in wave 16. This lack of explanation is really killing the experience for me. It makes it feel like the game just decides arbitrarily it doesn't want me to do well, so it changes the rules to force a negative outcome.I still think the game is good, and I'm going to keep playing it, despite the fact I haven't said much nice about it yet. The combat feels good, it has nice reward and upgrade systems, it's quick to get in to, and it has a layer of tactical aspects that appeal to fans of that genre. I think this game is an absolute buy...after the wiki gets written, because I'm finding it extremely frustrating trying to learn this game through a series of failures. If you're like me, keep it on your wishlist and buy it in a few months. If you don't mind learning the game the old-fashioned way, you can probably buy it now without issue.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to try  keep it as short but still helpful as I can.. the game is a hell of a lot of fun. We spent most of our time playing skirmish, it was a blast (sometimes a bit too literally..). We did encounter a few bugs here and there but we never came across any that were really game play breaking.Then we moved on to playing some campaign. Levels/ranks/skill tree all share between skirmish and campaign for non-hosts (and you will still all earn progress to levels/ranks/skill tree). However, the host has to do a new type of progression in the campaign where only part of his skill tree carry over (rank/level/ partial skill points all share progress between skirmish and campaign for him too).Host has to unlock Weapons/classes/upgrades during the campaign with"research". While at first i didn't like the idea of the host having to unlock his weapons/classes/upgrades again I do think it makes sense with the way the campaign plays, and honestly it didn't take long to be up to blastin!TLDR: if you like outnumbered by a horde type game play with friends, then its worth it even just for skirmish mode IMHO

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game is solely focused around the base campaign. A group of us all picked the game up, because we messed around with the first game, and while we saw the potential, felt it was lackluster at best. After having just completed said campaign, I can say that only get this if you find the core loop of squad combat particularly engrossing. After 40 hours of basically the same map, and only a handful of different mission objectives, it can certainly get rather stale. Additionally so when there felt like there was very minimal individual progression. All progress being tied to modules, with no real growth for individual characters basically means you will find a setup and never find cause to deviate from it. Even some of the classes feel rather weak compared to others. The Engineer has way way too many options to make others feel redundant, and once we obtained a late game story weapon, playing with the flamethrower felt pretty pointless.A huge bug is that you cannot save load outs in campaign without unlocking said type in the profile progression. Nowhere is that explained, and it took trial and error and just blind luck to realize what finally allowed us to save our loadouts in campaign.There's also numerous audio bugs, voice over lines would repeat constantly on some missions, for myself on a certain rescue mission, an NPC stated the same line 9 times, but only for myself, not the host or other 3 people in mission. Additionally, a different NPC would speak doubled up audio of two different voice lines at the same time, but the secondary dialogue was for a character that wouldn't show up in the story for another 20 hours of playing, so it left us all very confused when it occurred.Most of the cut scenes only played for the host, as well as the GUI breaking constantly for anyone that wasn't the host. The story of the campaign is frankly pretty atrocious, and I will speak more specifically to things below, but if you were hoping for an interesting or coherent narrative, then you will want to look elsewhere. NPCs and plot threads pop up as if they had 10 hours of backstory, only to be completely new to the player. I will concede that it might be because we didn't get far in the first game, but to be blunt, knowing more about the individual characters wouldn't save the narrative. I doubt enough people played the first game to warrant not having better introductions to most of the important NPCs.*SPOILERS BELOW FOR CAMPAIGN STORY*The fact that there are Good/Bad endings, and we stumbled over the bad one really really felt awful. The Bad ending is just so turbo bad that it sucked the interest out of the group of us to even want to come back. (Personal Note: Our group despised Vivian, so the fact she's the only one to survive really pissed us all off, which isn't a fault of the game, but just another nail into said coffin.) Reading up on what is needed to do to get the "Good" ending seems arbitrary and conflicting from what we could find, as well as after playing an otherwise pretty perfect game, we lost a single territory, to get the bad end, and it being this utterly convoluted, poorly explained mess meant we all uninstalled and shelved interest in the expansions.

It's pretty solid for the most part. It's the bugs.But pretty much after the first set of missions... I encountered bugs upon bugs upon bugs. And from a tiny bit of research some of these bugs were FIXED at one point but came back! I've had: -My own bot troops getting stuck on nearly everything and I have to wrangle them out via commands- VIPs/NPCs/Allies just not spawn at all for their mission and just fly off out of the map which would sometimes kill them off- Missions just randomly fail despite completing the objective. - Objective markers not even registering me at an objective despite pretty much at LICKING range of the target (this apparently was fixed?) It's not a bad game by any stretch and if you enjoy it then good for you, I dunno what I did wrong but my experience on two attempted runs was just... rough. For that reason I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Drastically different from the first game, heavily inspired from XCOM🟩 Good campaign story (You've to play the first game to fully understand & enjoy it)🟩 Graphics has been massively improved🟩 Skirmish mode provides post game content, more content can be unlocked via DLC🟩 Bots are pretty good (they can teleport which is super cool)🟩 Gameplay is solid with variety of builds possible (although balancing is not that good). 8 player COOP possible which can be really fun but sadly finding that many people is difficult🟩 Can play the game like an RTS or using WASD movement🟥 Performance is rather terrible - not only is the game locked at 60 FPS but the game doesn't fully utilize GPU to hit that 60 frequently🟥 Crash, crach & crash - game can randomly crash and gets worse as you progress more in the campaign. Setting the game at medium setting probably reduces it🟥 Campaign seems to drag on way too much - you've to wait for months (in-game time) for main mission to pop up🟥 Lots of things are blocked behind DLCs🟥 'Failed to create lobby' random error causes you to return to main menu🟥 Blast doors can be a real pain to deal with. Only the Demolitionist class can easily break them (and their skill can deal huge damage) which gives other class a big disadvantage

The love the developers have for this game shows through very clearly.

_childDocuments_.review: Network Failure: Pending Connection Failed, Trying to join the game session, please wait. Failed to join the game lobby. Please try again or find another lobby. The game lobby you are trying to join is full. Please find another lobby or create a game. - sums up the multiplayer side of the game if you can get into a lobby that isn't on the other side of... Mars. Phantom servers will persist on the browser for sometimes beyond 3+hours.Don't do what the host wants @ all times with no slight deviation or accidentally friendly fire can get permanently banned from lobbies... Nice features exist in peer to peer games so do enjoy the potato ping from someones dying computer & router.No incentives to redo medals once you have acquired them (perhaps for bonus xp?) so anyone new has to slug through many hours of grinding to get the bots to General rank before you can even attempt the harder ones let alone the basics. Community is okay with shooting friendlies especially lower rank just to get desired items that you went around the map to collect instead of asking?Unable to be revived bug, whole lobbies crashing to desktop mid-game except the host; leaving them wondering why everyone up & quit, unable to walk onto terrain/running on the spot, rubber-band back to death, graphic walls such as tables or cover will be hit when you're standing up, hovering items you can't collect along with item specific objective & those are the few of my favourite things.*Maps have enough tile-sets to keep it interesting each drop with interesting items found on Wave 12 onward. Classes have plenty of skills & abilities to vary up each play through allowing the freedom of either going the current status quo or forcing your character into a similar play style.Game is its own but is inspired by StarCraft (2 visually minus Protoss... Executor); the invasion & fall of Mars Sara to be specific. Comparing to X-COM doesn't seem accurate but more so WarCraft 3's experiment: The Founding of Durotar campaign, controlling 1 hero with skills & slots you can fill with found in dungeon items.DLCs add content in the form of campaigns & maps whilst giving access to the two strongest crowd controlling classes though one of which gets a mech. The friendly fire only applies to explosives, ordnance based weapons & enviromental so if you were wanting a hardcore experience from the basic pistol misfire then afraid not but it still a grinding persevering ordeal each mission.Steam community is nigh dead, if you want any life you must go to a discord. May as well just tank it further & have voip in-game with mute function. Watch gameplay if you are not sure because if you intend to try it you will most certainly go over the 2 hour refund threshold. Game could be really great just unfortunately it doesn't hit the mark or just yet but hey, it's just a review folks which is really an opinion and no one cares about those :d.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game around ten hours now, and I've only played the Skirmish mode.Solo runs of Skirmish are pretty boring, I recommend playing with others. To my knowledge, you can play with bots in campaign, or with other people. I again recommend you play with other people, although solo campaign is likely better than solo skirmish. That said, build diversity is where this game shines right now. There's a good number of weapons, classes, abilities, etc. Trying to min-max a build centered around the style of play you like is a fun endeavor, and I really love to see that in games. However, the game does seem to lack in mission variety, as it feels like there's only a few different missions.I recommend the game for sure if you have $26.99 (current price) to spare, as I've gotten $3/hour so far or so for my money and I don't intend to stop playing very soon. I'll probably wind up with 30 hours before getting bored and waiting on updates; that's a bright side I see, this game has a LOT of room to grow and feels MUCH better than Alien Swarm did when it was newer.

_childDocuments_.review: So lets get into this, shall we?  Firstly, Played the first one ages ago. Enjoyed it even then. This one?  Some of its kinda... Buggy. Certain enemies can hit you from REALLY far away with melee, its kind of shocking how much range they have. You want to use the cover in the game as well, but some of it seems.. Spotty. Its incredibly important to also be mobile, as it allows you to kite enemies and move around the map. Leveling your soldiers is... Fun. Once you have some max level operators you start realizing how godly they really are and you start investing more into their skills and abilities. Like XCOM. You also play alongside them.  The variety of weapons is... Interesting. Maybe there will be changes that will allow other weapons to do different damage types during the entire operations you do, but so far the only thing i've noticed is certain weapons by nature do certain damage types. However you can also find different ammo types (Plasma, Nitrogen, and Explosive []) which do different things to enemies. Special weapons... Man, they're all different. No two weapons perform the same duty aside from the Automatic Combat Shotgun and the Cerberus, which the Cerberus does more than the afore-mentioned while having a smaller ammo count. 7/10, good enemy variety, good weapon variety, only has some buggy ui and the sound design is good. Would recommend it to people who like a more RTS style XCOM.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2, while there are a few minor headaches and bugs associated with it currently; however what game doesn't now-a-days at launch, is a fun RTS-style shooter that grows more enjoyable if you play with friends; however the multiplayer does require someone to dedicate themselves to the Campaign style unlocks vs unlocking through a skill tree that other players get.Weapons and classes both feel solid, I haven't seen any 'useless' weapons or skills yet, everything has a purpose or use and offer a large amount of variety to suit your preferred playstyle.I have yet to encounter any serious bugs that have made me want to stop playing, and currently am having a blast even on more difficult, panic filled missions with a group of friends.The only thing I'm a bit 'iffy' about is Humanoid enemies that show up in certain missions (Hostile marines and Terminators), They fully take advantage of the fact they usually have 1250HP and rush at you and shoot you with their seemingly infinite ammo guns, it annoys me a bit but they're easy to deal with if you have the right tools or enough explosives.

Me and the boys have had hours of fun just running around and killing xenos as the emperor intended.  Most of your issues can be fixed my returning to main menu. _childDocuments_.review: Game is okay but lacks ALOT of polish.  Ran into a major bug, right from the start, where i couldn't reload save files and had to restart the entire campaign.  Luckily i'd only done a couple of missions.  I've been told there are worse than that, so save often.  Missions are rather lack luster in design, and the maps...are horrible.  You'll come to a building, have to circle around the entire thing to find the ONE entrance, find a power node to open the blast doors, and all the while fighting enemies.  Most of the bonus objectives are pointless anyway, since they only give you crappy consumables for completing them.  There are some nifty map mechanics though like shield generators, flamable gas pipes, strol holes, etc.  but you have to figure those out yourself, game doesn't explain crap.Speaking of items, most of the consumable items you get while playing a map are useless... 3/4 of them are land mines you have to place before a fight even starts.  Some of them are land mines that only work when combod with other explosives.  Oh and there is friendly fire...goes great with the "einstein" ai.  Where the hell are the grenades?  Right, they're ability only.  Glad they didnt charge full price for the game, seems like it needs another year in the oven even for the $30 price tag.  Only 3 hours in so i might change my mind but, so far, seems like a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential. But buying it in the hopes that it will be updated and fully featured in, maybe a year from now, is not what was advertised. It isn't in early access, it says its release, and that's a bit unfair. I was a bit confused that I can't even name my characters, women can't be characters, and characters don't have much in terms of AI tweaking. You also need ranks to change their colors which doesn't make sense to me as the rank doesn't serve much other purpose besides that and multiplayer. Some AI classes will never use their secondary weapons, even when its obviously appropriate or you spec them out for it. So the entire thing is very flat and basically you are supposed to play this multiplayer, otherwise you have to build your squad in a very set way. The fact that single player is limited to a squad of 4, when the game advertises 8, is frankly fraud. But the fact that 4, single player, and 8 co-op, is a feature, not a bug is embarassingly short sighted. My hope is that there will be a mod that can override this, or maybe DLC one day can stop dumbing down the single player--even without squad commands fleshed out, its really annoying that the single player experience is punished for no reason. Its clearly not a performance limitation. Its a design choice.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this from a perspective of caring only about the single player campaign experience.I had a good first impression of the game and tried to like it, but over the campaign progression the feeling switched to a mix of frustration and tedium - and I couldn't bother trying to complete it. The upside is that the developers seems to be pretty actively engaged, so perhaps in a year or so of patches and balance updates this will be enjoyable to play (I played on v1.2).There's a diverse mix of bugs (AI bots pathing resulting in characters permanently stuck, order of equipped skills changed when loading a save, mission load screen reflecting the previous rather than the current mission, some XP progression achievements not being updated, etc..). A lot of the mechanics are unclear or not explained at all, at both the strategic level and the tactical combat one. Spending half the campaign time flying from HQ to missions and back is rather silly. And at some point the missions start throwing at you multiple boss type enemies at once (in addition to the regular waves of trash and medium enemies) which have huge health pools, resistance to at least 2 out of 3 damage types and silly high regeneration - while you have a task to hold some location for a minute or several. Maybe those can be handled with a team of 8 capable human players and diverse weapons and skills, but not a single player with 3 AI bots and limited ability to outfit and control them.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, games been out for quite some time. Final thoughts:Had my fun, but I would not recommend this to anyone unless you have a hardcore gamer mindset that likes grinding. Every time I make a build or someone else makes one that is "too good" it gets nerfed to the ground. Been playing this cat and mouse game for quite some time now and I remembered why I took a long break from this game only to come back and realize why I had left. Also, too many bugs. Every time a major update came out I've avoided it for about a week or 2 and there is always a hotfix. Bugs bugs bugs...Everything that could've been "fun" is met with extreme nerfs or "add some good stats, and add a lot of negative stats". The biggest slap in the my face was when I made some spreadsheets for helping new players and devs made big nerfs using my spreadsheets (received no thanks or mentions). How do I know this? It was way too specific what they nerfed and a few buffs on some classes, like the 2 that needed their max HP increased.Last update they implemented (stratagems) is more grind to the grindfest and I am all grinded out. Not a good system for returning players. Rewards to get the new system up and running are minuscule and easily lost. The "fun" aspect is lost here, which is a bit of a surprise given there are no negatives to taking stratagems. Even had an issue where it didn't save points after exiting game and reset me back to zero. That being said, its not all bad. The potential was there, but the devs want it to be something else. _childDocuments_.review: I snagged The Red Solstice back in March of this year and had a blast despite it's tedious team management system and abysmal team AI. Once I heard about RS2, I knew I was going to pick it up, and so far I'm leaning more towards a positive review than negative. On release there were too many bugs to bother playing, so I waited until a hotfix which came less than 24 hours later. There are still some issues but nothing that I would consider game breaking.What I like:My first impression of the game is mostly positive. I like having AI that actually uses the skills that it's given. I was shocked to see my medic healing and reviving without being prompted. It was also nice seeing the assault class using his frag grenades, etc. I like the new array of toys that are given this time around and I love the XCOM-like campaign that involves building up your arsenal, traveling to different regions, researching, and even capturing specimens. The maps feel just as big, if not bigger than the maps in the original game. Speaking of the map, I love the amount of interactions available when it comes to the map. From blocking doors to opening up gas pipeline access on the street, everything has a purpose and can be used to escape the horde.What I don't like:While I do enjoy much of what I've experienced so far, I do have a number of issues with the game. My biggest issue is the lack luster tutorial interactions. I've pretty much stumbled my way throughout the game so far in terms of learning the game and how to utilize items, weapons, and upgrade my base. I'm still learning but it would be nice if the hints were useful. Next is the game seems too easy compared to the original. Maybe it's because I'm fairly early into the game but the volume of enemies seem underwhelming overall. My next issue is the side mission generation or lack there of. The timing of the side missions is so random that you can literally finish the main mission in less than 5 minutes and escape before you see any opposition. When you do get missions, some of them don't give clear instructions on what you need to do. Specifically the M.E.R.C.S supply mission. Also some missions will bug out and never end, but I'm sure that will be patched out with time.Conclusion: All in all I am enjoying the game and it's much improved from the original game, but there are still some things that the original does better. I'd like to see a few more elements of RS be put into this installment, such as the ambiance sounds, and the boss creature sounds at the beginning of certain waves.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, the game is amazing. I just want to share that first, so now you know my bias. I'll try to explain why I think this game is amazing and why you should try it. I also want to say that it had some bugs at launch, it still has some bugs, but so many of them were fixed just a few hours after launch that I've been playing most of my time not encountering any bugs at all.Firstly, it's easy to learn - hard to master. It has some clunk, but it is not necessarily a clunky game. It is just that it has advanced controls so it takes some time to get into them, but they have vastly improved this over the first one. It feels very smooth and once you get the hang of it, it's not like you're fighting the controls like other games.It also has a very high skill ceiling. You might feel something is impossible, just to see that it is possible with the right tactics/mindset. It's truly a coop game, where you have strong roles in a team, but you don't necessarily get to feel like "the hero" as in other games (but I think this is perfect). Good teamwork comes together with a good flow through a game-session. You'll constantly compliment your teammates that also compliment you. And the game design truly rewards people for playing as a team, and doesn't really work all that well for solos.It has a decent progression system, which you probably will spend a lot of time unlocking.Campaign is like X-COM, but real time and up to 8 player coop. It's pretty nice.But I really want to return to the game design, becuase I think that is a very strong suit for this game, and something that very few games manages in this day and age. It has a strong game design, where everything has a purpose, and the game has a strong Identity. Leveling up, improving your character/build allows you to improve the way you play, and adds to the gameplay instead of taking away from it, like how it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: You guys should really admit these two things are conflict.I played this game with a friend, he hosted the game in campaign mode. After 2 or 3 runs we decided to change the difficulty because we felt it was way too easy. Guess what? You can only change the difficulty by starting a new campaign, which is copied from XCOM 2 and I can understand that, but that means his unlocks will be reset to zero, what's worse, the game has a considerably complicated character build system.It is said this game derives from a map of an RTS game like Starcraft 2 or something alike, therefore WASD to move the camera instead of moving your character is reserved. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Singleplayer support!- Decent eye candy visuals- Fun, fast paced combat with interesting tactical elements- Lots of playtime and decent replayability- Generally compelling story- Variety of classes and builds- XCOM style strategic map- Howell-Barrex DLC adds interesting variety - UBAS looks coolCons:- Vanilla campaign missions incredibly repetitive- Vanilla endgame narrative incoherent, moral choices poorly signposted- Command lag/unresponsive UI on map overlay and radial menu- Glitchy bot AI for squad mates- Sometimes glitchy mission triggers- Unexpected difficulty spikes in Story missions- Tedious frustrating mission design at times- UBAS useless except for extra health- Excessive energy drain usage makes many abilities unviable- Some items too niche to ever be useful (e.g. seismic resonators)So first off, I do really enjoy this game - imagine XCOM but with real time combat! Despite the emphasis on multiplayer, it's perfectly playable in singleplayer once you get used to the bot AI.  The main campaign provides many hours of enjoyment and the first DLC provides a different enough experience to be worth replaying.  The storyline is compelling and there is much fun to be had trying different builds out across a variety of classes with weapons/abilities ranging from the standard conventional ones like assault rifles/shotgun/minigun/etc to shoulder mounted plasma cannons and back mounted rocket pods to calling orbital death rays.  Maps also feature destructable terrain and interesting tactical elements which can be exploited in combat e.g. using explosives to gain entry to areas, booby trapping exposing gas lines for ambushes or loading up artillery to be able to call down fire support later.What is strange however is despite looking the part for a top rate game, there is an inexplicable lack of polish in places.  Some of this is trivial such as potential mis-translations (e.g. using the wrong word/grammar such "evacuation" instead of "excavation", "kill anything that would prevent your failure", etc) and mis-labelling of interactive objects  (e.g. many control terminals are labelled "Dam Control" when they have nothing to do it with).  Others however are a bit more annoying such as when mission events fail to trigger or objectives are confusing/mismatched - one mission springs to mind you are directed to use a launch button which without any discernible warning turns out to be a self-destruct that affects the game ending.When playing singleplayer the bots are best treated as mobile gun turrets as they seem incapable of using many activated abilities sensibility - they will happily periodically trigger AOE abilities with no enemies in sight destroying cover and friendly structures.  Although there is a basic ordering system, it is both laggy when triggered via radial menu and also inconsistent with bots requiring multiple repeat commands to do anything. Sometimes they seem to ignore attack orders especially on biomass targets or only fire a single salvo off, especially with secondary weapons.  At other times however they will happily overkill a single target one with multiple salvos. killing themselves/other members of the team with point blank friendly fire.Some of the longer missions can also be quite tedious and frustrating since saving can only be performed on the strategic map.  If a mission objective glitches out or your squad is killed you have to restart from the beginning which can be quite time consuming.  This is made worse by some story missions where the difficulty can spike unexpectedly - normally difficulty scales with the infestation level both globally and locally, increasing gradually within each mission with each successive enemy wave.  In one particular mission however the player has to retreat back to firebase after tedious waltz round the map destroying dozens of targets - a 4 minute timer suggests there maybe plenty of time yet less than 30 seconds in your allies inexplicably nuke a bridge on your retreat path with no apparent warning or reason (e.g. no enemies nearby).  If reacting in time it's possible to get out of the huge blast radius (just) however the game throws another spanner by spawning multiple boss level creatures 10+ waves early that knockdown/stun your retreating team members causing a wipe and mission restart.  IMO this is poor design seemingly calculated to screw the player over and results in frustration instead of any sense of achievement from a genuine challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Back story: I originally came from NoTD (night of the dead) back when it was a Warcraft III custom game, played TRS 1 and TRS 2 so the *paltry* 500 hours is only part of the time I spent on this game.I think this type of game offers a lot in terms of strategy. planning how to make your character, working with allies to form a cohesive team, and then putting that into action while being swarmed by mutant zombies of death.There are a ton of strategies, ways to win and hundreds of ways to build your various classes. The choices are absolutely meaningful and makes creating a great build all the more worthwhile.Finding a build that works putting it into action and pulling off incredible feats to save your team and the mission feels amazing.Enemies range from trash mobs, to super bosses that will almost certainly ruin your day - and how to beat each enemy can be quite different making team play and individual choices important.There is a bit of a grind to get medals, promotions and skill points - the nice thing is there is no real RNG to it, you know what you want, and how to get there. The introduction of daily and weekly tasks, as well as tiers to the medals has made the grind very reasonable in my opinion.My biggest issue is trying to find people to play with. Make sure to bring friends or become active in discord otherwise it will be difficult to play with real people particularly on the harder difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best squad based games I've ever played, based on the epic Warcraft III map Night of the Dead. You play as a small team of marines tasked with missions of ever increasing complexity while being attacked by swarms of various mutant enemies. The game is well balanced as a top down squad looter shooter with looting vs completing objectives taking varying levels of importance throughout the mission. Lots of different classes and weapons for customizing your marine and a ton of additonal items and weapons you can collect within each mission makes each attempt unique. Would only recommend if you have a group to play with though, also a little janky still at launch, hoping everything gets fixed shortly

_childDocuments_.review: Its hard as nails and demands a whole bunch of patience. Not for the faint of heart. However, if you stick with it, its slowly opens up and reveal just how much of a gem it is.Combining co-op real time action and tactics with an strategic map, where time managment is crucial it realy is a one of a kind. The depth of this game is truely fascinating but its also the depth that makes the game so damn hard and unforgiving. Theres little room for mistakes, both in the tactic mode and in the strategic, but that makes the taste of victory the better once you master it.I only played this with friends but I have a sneaky suspicion it wont be as fun playing solo. In many ways it feels as if you -need- to be at least 3 players to get the most out of the game.I really recomend this game, if you like a challenge.

The campaign is a nice touch for learning the basics, and I'd encourage anyone new to this style of game to try the campaign on easy mode for a bit first just to get the hang of its mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game released in a state not too unfamiliar with modern gaming standards, which isn't great, but when a development team is in touch with its playerbase as closely as this development team is the bugs are handled quickly and suggestions are taken willingly. If you use the game's main menu to join their discord you can simply go to the appropriate channel and describe your bug and a developer will tell you whether or not they were aware of it and if they were already aware of it they will tell you if and when they fix it. That isn't something you see from most modern development teams, the communication is top notch and it shows as a few days after the game released there have been two major updates that tackled a lot of the problems that people reported in the development chat and the suggestions thread that is available is flowing with ideas that are at least being considered and some I know have been implemented or at least have been confirmed as planned.Respect needs to be given and while the non-saved campaign progression may be an off switch for some people, I for one enjoy the fact that I can choose to join people who are playing their own campaign without boosting my characters level or stats so high that my own game becomes a boring, disingenuous version of the one I played with my friends/strangers. And even still, the levels you gain in skirmish mode as they call it, the coop game mode, carries over to your profile which shares similar unlocks with the single player campaign, so it is not as if your time is wasted, you just simply have the choice of investing the multiplayer experience into your multiplayer character, or the shared singleplayer and multiplayer options, which is your Combat Suit and Squad sections.My advice, try the game out, give it a shot and don't think because the objective is simply "go here and do this" that the game is boring. The difficulty of the game isn't the objectives, it is attempting to accomplish said objectives without running into a horde or large swarms of mutations that call for squads to put their heads together and move together, sometimes pushing through the opposition and other times kiting away from them as best as possible while you whittle down the numbers. A simple straight road to an objective has never been so complicated and I applaud the developers for taking such a simple objective system and making it a lot more challenging than most people give credit. It gives this oddly "repetitive" gameplay as I've seen it described play as something that is far from it. Sure, there are the same side missions and main missions in Skirmish mode, an unlimited mission selection would be nigh impossible, but the scant variety we have is complimented by the variety of enemies, variety of player classes, weapons, abilities, builds, strengths, and weaknesses which all lead to every single game being played completely different. Perhaps you have a DPS heavy team that laughs in the face of hordes but lacks the single target damage to combat most of the larger mutations, or perhaps the opposite is true and the hordes of trash mobs will eventually overwhelm the group causing for a panicked scatter from uncoordinated teammates.This is not a game that should be played on easy and then reviewed, the game only gets better with higher difficulties and more challenges. Any reviews that you see that say the game is "too easy" have never played the game on the harder difficulties, which can only be unlocked by getting total victories on the easier difficulties. The game starts you off with three to four difficulties, with the option of unlocking harder ones.I do not recommend games often, but I can't help but feel that people simply hate on a game for a system that they themselves find lacking but don't look at the entire game as a whole and weight it fairly. Should I not recommend Red Solstice 2: Survivors simply because I prefer to play games like D&D and they don't have fireball? No? Obviously, because this game wasn't built with that concept in mind so giving it an F because the criteria you weight it to isn't the vision of the game is spiteful.

_childDocuments_.review: Look it's not a horrible game, they tried to do X-Com in RTS. However, it pales in comparison, the character customizations are virtually non-existent. For the multiplayer, there's a learning curve, not so bad, and it's actually fun to play with people however the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ part that I feel about this game can be summarized in 2 things- No progression at all almost, the tree is so small, you can max out a single specilization in a few games and just play that forever. The only reason to gain points is to open up other types like medic or sniper or whatever, so if you usually just pick one role and stick to it, you'll max it out pretty fast.-The gameplay itself ends up being either too hard or too easy, you can activate overwatch, which is the character's auto-detect and auto-attack enemies while you walk around, usually you start with this on, because you can just kill all the weak monsters without aiming or anything and the penalty doesn't matter. _childDocuments_.review: Completely underrated IMO. People make comparisons to XCom but it's not as deep. It feels heavily inspired from it though. There is depth though, in terms of the customization and the actual strategy during gameplay. It's difficult but very engaging.  You often have to make moves and decisions on the fly, since unlike XCom, you don't have time to sit around and plan things out.I love the numerous control schemes for the game. I tried playing on the Steam Deck but couldn't get it to recognize the controller. Just found that odd. You can play RTS by point and click, or have it play like twin stick with WASD movement. This was something requested and the developers implemented. That's always appreciated. Controller implementation is very jank when it comes to menus. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. But during missions, works well enough. Would love to have the DPad control the camera as they don't do anything outside of pressing down to detonate stuff or holding RB or LB to utilize things. Might I suggest RB+Down detonate?So many classes to choose that all play so differently. Numerous weapons that handle differently too. Vehicles were introduced a few updates ago, which is definitely a nice addition. My gripe is that I wish mechs wouldn't be locked down to one class. Also, vehicles don't seem to work with a controller.Environments are varied, and love the whole aesthetic and structures. Many smaller things I would've loved to see like a more robust campaign where you are able to see what's going on in your ship, see the aesthetics change based on the upgrades you get. That would definitely feel more XCom like. These are just personal wants however.The gameplay is what really makes this so fun. Missions are long and difficult, or at least scale up in difficulty. It's closer to a roguelike than it is to XCom, with various randomness being thrown in. Holing up in a building and defending civilians is always a nailbiter. Enemies are incredibly varied from the usual cannon fodder, to behemoths chasing you down streets, to silent hunters stalking you in every corner. I feel the hunter is inspired from Alien. Many different weapons and bullet types affect the enemies in certain ways. It really does feel like a survival game since you're constantly managing your resources, hoping you have enough ammo left to finish one last mission or extract. And the game throws so many at you that you're never truly prepared, you just do your best to survive.All in all, I hope more people check this game out. And I really hope to see more like it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: With the major bugs now addressed by the day 1 patch, the game is in good condition and quite a bit of fun. If you want to pick it up and try it out before the return window closes, I would recommend multiplayer (skirmish). You won't see the singleplayer mechanics, but find yourself a few full games on a harder difficulty and you'll skip the gentle on-ramp to see some of the variety and challenge from the late game. Be sure to click around and find your character loadout and skill tree. Oh, and if you join a lobby and there's no ready button? Chances are the host is still looking for a mission. The button will show up when they've got one. If you want to ask about it, enter opens the chat.It's hard to describe exactly what this is to someone who hasn't picked it up yet, but battles are the meat of the game and they feel something like a twin-stick shooter with RTS controls. You'll probably recognize a lot of other games in this one; There are flavors of DoTA, Alien Swarm, and Helldivers in the tactical battles, and a lot of XCOM in the strategy layer that ties the singleplayer campaign together. Ironward has mixed all this into a surprisingly coherent experience and added layers of their own interacting mechanics and unique ideas. The equipment system is one example; It's easy to make an okay build but you'll find yourself playing around with the dozens of weapons, abilities, and components trying to get the BEST build. The leveling system is another example; Just shooting things will only get you so far, sometimes you'll need to demonstrate use of some of the more complex game mechanics before you're promoted again.It all comes together quite well and I find that I rather enjoy it. Bonus points in particular to whoever designed that ability for the Heavy class that temporarily gives you infinite ammunition, so that we can use the minigun the way that we all WANT to use the minigun (By holding down the trigger and cackling until everything within visual range has been reduced to a chunky salsa). I would say that the one great flaw of the game is that it doesn't communicate well. Remember when I talked about the ready button in the first paragraph? It's not greyed out or anything. There's no message saying "the host has not started a mission". It simply doesn't exist, leaving the new player to figure out what's going on. The leveling/promotion system will sometimes want you to do things like "stun an enemy", but to get the explanation for how to stun a target you'll need to read the description on a weapon that causes energy damage. The equipment screen is also a prime example of this. There's two types of energy to get mixed up, the way stats interact isn't immediately obvious, and there's a flood of information that you simply can't expect to figure out all at once. And not expecting to figure it out all at once is indeed the approach I would suggest. You'll quickly figure out enough to do just fine, and having been in some of the betas Ironward IS working to make things more comprehensible. If you approach it with some patience, you'll probably find that there's plenty of fun to be had with this mess of systems they've made into a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I really do. I loved Xcom and I loved Helldivers. But this game is neither of those two games. It plays like a bad starcraft 2 custome map. I get that these guys started with that, but come on... This is a stand alone game... You can make all of your stuff outside the bounds of a custom map in Starcraft. Why you would have the same limited inventory system as Starcraft/Warcraft 3 is completely beyond me. There is soooooooo much room for improvement on this game its not even funny. I think the worst part about this game is the extremely steep difficult jump that happens after the first few missions. The AI bot allies you get in single player can't keep up with the higher difficulty mobs. They just get overrun, so what's the point in even having them?  Also, there is literally NO explaination on how to get Black Ops, how to properly use the tactical overlay components of the game, how to build and upgrade outposts, how to reduce Strol infestation, how to use explosives, etc. There is also literally no explanation to the different Strol units. They just kind of appear and you have to guess what they do. In Xcom, new alien variants were explained somewhat when you first come across them so that you have some idea of how to handle the situation. In this game you're expected to go read through the archives AFTER the mission to get an extremely bland idea of what the monster does. Also the trickle of enemies is so boring and mediocre feeling. Jump Pack feels janky and dumb and it should feel fluid and fun. There's a lot of potential here in this game, but I just honestly can't recommend this game to anyone in its current state. Its in such a bad place right now. Needs at least another year of work for them to build proper UI quality of life improvements and better weapon balancing. Currently most of the weapons are completely and utterly useless once you get bigger opponents. Meaning you can't even play your favourite class because most classes have no way of dealing with higher level threats.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who played the Night of the Living Dead Warcraft 3 custom game, who loved it and thought "more of this would be awesome!" Then all you have to do is just buy the game now. I probably don't need to say that as most folks who did love that game bought the first one of those game and probably picked this one up too.For the rest, the game is likely niche and covers with some caveats.Graphics, pretty darn good. The genre that spawned this game is RTS and that's the basis we're comparing right now. The graphics are clear and enjoyable, a vast improvement from the first and many strives have been made in the UI and general scenery to make it clear what's important. It's a shame I haven't found a way to zoom in and stare at the character models closely yet but I'm sure it's either an option missed or something that could be added as a long term nice to have Sound. Combat is visceral and enjoyable, the voice acting is acceptable. There opening scene has a voice that sounds like someone imitating Arnold Schwarzenegger, and that alone gets points from me for hilarity.Gameplay is super enjoyable. Land on map, get a handful of randomly generated objectives, complete them, survive each wave. I'll note that the single player campaign is a little more structured on the missions for each map and there is a research and phase between each mission.Story. Earth was overrun 200 years ago by mutants. A few years back (first game) they started appearing on Mars. Mega companies have power, there are various factions. The game is attempting to build on the narrative of the first and I can respect that Single/Multiplayer.  Single player campaign is okay. I was planning to beat it first but the real joy of the game is multiplayer. Made some new friends last night, had a blast. This game has a small but string foundational community that plays. The first game has been out since 2014 and it's had a small following. If multiplayer isn't your thing and everything I've mentioned has not interested you then it may be safer to steer away if videos of gameplay haven't sold you. Otherwise, this is a really fun game to play.Hey Devs: any chance to add a tutorial or YouTube video that explains the level, rank, and multiplayer skill system? _childDocuments_.review: I believe this is fairly a good game and a huge improvement over the first one. Meanwhile, although it's an improvement it still struggles to make an impact on what it does. Red Solstice 2 is a top-down RTS with a sort of 'management' similar to XCOM. To be fair, the gameplay is almost a twin-stick shooter (at least on easier difficulties) that you run&gun through almost everything. I have not tried harder difficulties or managed to play with other players so I can't put my finger on how strategic and deep can it get and how communication could be a part of it. However playing the solo campaign, especially on easy (I feared that I'd suck hard at first as this is not quite my genre) is pretty straightforward and no-brainer. The game has an infestation system (i.e. Xcom 2's doomsday clock) that you need to manage to slow it down over time, if it reaches 100% you will instantly lose. While it's scary, you can do missions to slow down the infestation, decrease regional infestation (there are multiple regions that you discover and establish your colonies), or directly the global infestation (the clock). Well, if only those missions were not exactly copycats of each other, I might have actually done them. However, besides some target missions (in which you aimed to kill a high-risk tough target and decrease the global infestation bar by around 2 -and that is the far easiest and fastest side mission btw) I never laid my hand on them after doing a few of each. Objectives were bland. Although I understand objectives and the core gameplay loop would repeat itself, the gameplay does not really compensate for them. The game is as deep as Alien Swarm at most and objectives (even the presentations, dialogues etc.) being the exact same does not help me to get into them either. You do these objectives in rather open areas similar to XCOM but since you don't really have a chance to remain hidden or use covers, it does not feel deep and you just loot some containers and do some chores on the map. Also mind that the map is designed horizontally. It is what it is and it's heartbreaking as I strongly believe some vertical design and creating smaller but more focused areas would add a deeper layer to the game.I've managed to come as far as the Fleeting Hope mission. While the enemies themselves were not hard, the last convoy (you need to escort 3 convoys) got busted fairly easily and at that point, I gave up on the game. It'd be painfully boring to re-do a 50-60 min mission cuz aliens can easily swarm the objective, it cannot move and my DPS cannot match their damage over the convoy. Of course, there are some armory and facilities in-game (I wanted to tie that subject to this mechanics) and they prove useful if you do researches and engineer items which you can use in your ops. Well, I was doing it until my infestation clock was doomed so at this point I can't really afford researching & engineering. Luckily, the game introduces a 'Solar' mechanic which is an orbital weapon that enables you to hit any region and reduce the threat of infestation by over %20. But even with that, infestation builds up back rather fast so you might always be on the edge (between 80-100) and only use it so you can rush to the next mission. This is mainly a result of not playing the game in the way the developers intended the player to. They want you to spend time on a region, gain intel, do strike missions and slow the regional infestation and build outposts here and there, Cuz once your intel is lost infestation grows bigger and bigger and when you lose a region you also lose contact there. I get they may want a slow burn game where the player needs to take their time and think 'strategically' about how should they approach their missions and what should they build next or how should maintain the contact between the regions, for me, it's just not fun. Compared to XCOM (I did not finish it either but I'd be more eager to tbh) it does not like an integral part of the game but just some side stuff. Lack of gameplay mechanics based on animations (finishers, vaulting etc.), lack of cutscenes in animations (cutscenes are mostly in an old-fashioned jrpg mindset, they are just powerpoint presentation lmao and the story is being told over the radio talks mostly. Coming from Borderlands 3 to this is a burnout) and the lack of variations in the level/mission design killed my interest in the game rather quickly and made it harder to invest in. I also thought, that while AI was good in general, commanding your teammates is not as deep as I'd expect it to be. If you feel like you'd enjoy doing the same stuff over and over again (no shame in it, just take a look at the screenshots and imagine seeing the same type of missions over 20-30 hours) it can keep you entertained for a while and there is not really a competitor to this game atm. However, I eventually got bored as I feared and dropped the game for now. I liked how they kept releasing patches over the release though (and very usually). Might turn back at a later date and see how it is improved. TLDR: It is decently a competent and polished game. If you don't mind repetitive/grindy stuff give it a shot and you might like it. If you do, you may find yourself in my boots and get bored in approx. 10 hours. Still, given the fact that it was in Humble Choice for a cheap price, getting entertained for 10 hours is not bad at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to leave this after a few hours. I think i can say my piece. So game is good, pretty good. Not really good, not great, just pretty good. So I would probably represent a new demographic. New players entering the franchise for the first time. I've played the first one in a limited capacity. Really liked the idea, so grabbed this. I really liked hell divers so i figured i would enjoy this. Lets get to it.From a pro stance this game is a fantastic MOBA(dioblisc?) style (ish?) Honestly, i cant really accurately pin what this is. Its a tactical game a lot like Alien Swarm but you get to control 1 character. You have 6 classes with unique and shareable abilities across the board. Classes are really well balanced, like REALLY well balanced. Every class is necessary in high level content. Each one has a purpose and squad makeups can decide a win or if u and ur mate get wiped across the surface of mars. Assault and medic are starter classes, you then get a really expansive tree which allows you to unlock guns, abilities, classes, suit passives, squad passives (limited to npc's? not really sure yet), and more battlefield abilities. As a tip, do not forget a flash grenade, makes bosses a lot easier to deal with. Levels and environments a really well designed, and the layout is relatively logically designed. (Supply pad next to a laboratory) Haven't finished campaign yet but the infrastructure building system is a neat idea and they swiped the xcom base building a infrastructure stuff. Its all and all passable. Cons Well there are a few. This game feels like a niche game. New players to the franchise will look at the menu items and not really understand whats what. That could be because the menu isnt all that intuitive. Like Profile is where you character upgrades are. However u need to slot your abilities in your suit under the armory tab. In that same vein understanding what to do in game can be jarring at first. Your class doesn't feel complete until you unlock your modules which can be a little uinituitive. Campaign story feels boring and is hard to get hooked in to. Although xcom had the same problem. The game has  few bugs yet, nothing crazy anymore but missions might glitch if some captures a boss u need to kill. Unlocking points and unlocking rank are separate paths. This is where the little customization comes from. Lastly while not all see this a con but me personally it is. They will be selling skins on the steam store.While ranking up only unlocks colors. I think you should get special armors or ornaments for hitting high ranks.Sorry, i really missed alot but honestly this for me is a very tentative yeah.... if your bored. I think multiplayer should be expanded and would like to see some workshop integrations and map tools. that would make this a hell yeah for me.

name: Exo One
detailed_description: A strange signal... an alien craft... an interplanetary, gravity-defying journey through space and time. On the anniversary of the Jupiter disaster, an alien signal transmits construction blueprints for an alien craft, which humanity builds, called Exo One. Master a truly alien traversal system and move through enigmatic and desolate alien landscapes in ways you've never experienced. Control gravity itself and build momentum to reach colossal speeds and exhilarating heights. Ride thermal updrafts into boiling cloud formations, careen down hillsides and launch off mountain tops, all the time drifting toward the shining blue beam on the horizon. Atmospheric, diffused visuals are merged with otherworldly sound effects and a hypnotic electric guitar soundtrack. Pilot your craft on mankind's first voyage outside the solar system, and go on an interplanetary journey across space and time.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, therapeutic 2-3 hour experience featuring twelve diverse alien landscapes. The game isn't particular difficult, but it does provide enough achievement challenges to incentivise getting proficient at handling the spacecraft. My only gripe with the game would be the occasional issue of the camera acting in an erratic manner and even losing sight of the spacecraft, when moving in certain directions. There are a few levels that may well incite feelings of thalassophobia or acrophobia for some people, but honestly, that makes me enjoy the game even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A short and beautiful game worth every minute. The pacing is perfect, with every level bringing something new while not overstaying its welcome. The controls are easy to pick up but very expressive, with lots of room for mastery. You can play this game slow or fast, exploring every nook and cranny of a level or zooming through them at exhilarating speeds. There's no pressure to complete levels quickly, but if you decide to, the game tracks your time for each run, making it simple to track progress. The presentation is obviously beautiful, with visuals inspired by space probe photography, a dreamy ambient soundtrack, paired with excellent thrumming engine noises from your ship. Game good!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it's breathtaking at times. Controls are easy to understand, take a little time to master (so you don't lose your momentum by crashing at the speed of sound into the ground). But what really caught my attention, was the audio. The lightning strikes hitting your orb are crisp as hell, the wind flying by is done just right, and the best sound is when you hit the sound barrier, it'll leave you wanting to do it again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this title seems to be a great anti-stress game that has a chill vibe and mechanics that can be mastered easily. Well, it turns out unless you play through dozens of times on each map (guessing here, no idea if that is true), that your real experience is rolling around on the ground hoping to catch a hill or some boost to get you back into the groove.It accomplished the exact opposite of what I expected, it ended up increasing stress due to frustration of the map design. What I think they are going for is you simply drop in and follow some kind of path that leads to what you see in the trailers (effortlessly gliding and satisfyingly bobbing through the environment), but if you accidentally go slightly off course you end up blindly seeking out where you "should be" but nearly zero indicators on where that is or even given mechanics to get there AT ALL. A weak double jump leading to a sputtered out glide feels like punishment to me. Like the developer is insinuating "Git gud, newb!"They frustratingly limit your ability to look around, as if they are trying to guide you from going off course, but when you do go off course this makes it waay harder to get your bearings back.I know, there are not any "rules" to this game other than the simple physics and "go to the column of light" but ultimately it falls flat like a ball of lead that doesn't catch the wind stream at the right time and remains on a ground that was never considered to be a bulk of the player's playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, but confusing and frustrating gameplay requiring you to "skip" your craft off the ground to gain temporary altitude as you attempt to maintain the speed necessary to extend your air-time. Unfortunately, it is very difficult if not impossible to plan your dives onto the optimal terrain since you can't really see where you will make contact, and when you get close to the ground the camera decides to whip around at certain angles and kill your momentum. Worse, it disorients you as to which way you were headed, because there is little if anything to clearly indicate if you are going the right way. You can head off in any direction including back the way you came without realizing you are going the wrong way for a long time. There are upgrade items to find, but if you get lost once, good luck getting back on the intended path to locate them.With a little QoL polish, and the tools to empower the player to skillfully pull off the necessary maneuvers to actually play, this could be an interesting and visually stunning journey, but as it is, fun it is not.
