_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one known for eloquence, but here goes: (tl;dr: (Play-through still in progress) relaxing movement and exploration centric game combined with 2001 A Space Odyssey, worth a buy and buying the soundtrack from bandcamp:  ,also: EPILEPSY WARNING (20 HZ FLASHING LIGHTS) )I genuinely forget what caused me to come across Exo One back in 2017, maybe a post in Games on the SomethingAwful Forums? Either way, the concept of exploring alien landscapes with a ball, and the movement mechanics that could come with it, appealed to me. I missed the kickstarter, but was able to preorder it on humble bundle. I then largely forgot about it for the next 4 years, aside from trying out 1 or 2 demos over that period. With kickstarter products, I've found it's best to put them out of your mind until they either show up on your front door, or show up in your email, removing any feelings of frustration and leaving you with pleasant moments of surprise, and sometimes confusion, if you didn't remember ordering something. When this showed up on Steam, I was pleasantly surprised, and went to find my humble key (since humble didn't alert me that it had released). After a quick download I was off to the races.One of the first things that surprised me is that there is some kind of story to it. I guess I should've expected one, but from the demo I was expecting an aimless game of exploring some procedurally generated worlds via some unique movement mechanics. Making your own fun, essentially. And that would've been fine with me, but they've gone with a story that has me curious as I continue to play. When one makes heavy mention of Jupiter and uses visual effects that are a homage to Jupiter and Beyond the Infinite from 2001 A Space Odyssey, I can't help but wonder where it goes. Compared to the earlier demo, the finished game is quite well optimized. Even with my 4-5 year old Titan XP, I can run this game at 4K with max settings and largely play above 60 FPS, usually in the 70s to 80s range, though there are times when it will dip into the 50s but not at a pace where the frame rate would be considered to wildly fluctuate and cause discomfort for the player. Even when it does dip, the frame pacing is still solid, and I feel no jitters. Both combine for a smooth gameplay experience, which one needs in a game all about movement. The graphics are gorgeous. The lighting, shadow, and particle effects are top notch, and the color palette is saturated and warm. These all combine to really set the mood on some levels. I must really tip my hat to the use of blues, especially combined with low intense lighting, it really does give off an air of mystery, and makes you wanna just wallow in it. The transition between worlds sequence, clearly a homage to Douglas Trumbull's Stargate sequence from 2001's Jupiter and Beyond the Infinite, is a worthy homage, but doesn't compare to the beauty of the awe-inspiring original. To be fair though,  nothing really has in the 53 years since.The controls are simple, but take some getting used to. There is no failure state or time limit, so you're free to mess around as much as you want. Once you get the hang of it, you'll be able to move pretty fluidly on land and in air. The levels also so far have different effects that you can take advantage of with your mechanics, allowing for some additional movement options. Sound design is nice and punchy. And the soundtrack is melancholic and reserved, tracks only occasionally play, leaving you largely with the sounds of the exoplanetary elements. I'd say it's worth a pickup, but if you do, don't buy from steam, buy from the artist's bandcamp:  . Nearly all the profits go to the artist, and you can get the soundtrack in any audio format you want, including lossless WAV format. I can't say much about the camera or it's controls, because I largely just go where my ball's movement takes me, but I found it easy enough to turn the camera towards anything I wanted to see. You can also adjust the FOV, but again, I didn't mess around with that, the default worked fine for me.The only downside I can say so far is that like some other reviews have pointed out, is that some of the flashing lights contained within the game can hit that 20 HZ sweet spot for triggering seizures in those that have epilepsy. So those with epilepsy, be warned, this game possibly might not be for you.All in All, so far Exo One is a very pretty looking and sounding relaxing space exploration game with some unique and fun movement mechanics. One that I would say is not only worth picking up, but was worth the 4 year wait. Once I finish the game, if I change my mind about anything, or have anything additional to say, I'll update my review. Thank you to anyone that took the time to read this review. I hope it wasn't too much of a waste of your time. I hope you and your loved ones have a safe and happy holiday season, and a safe and happy rest of 2021.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: Exo One is a physics based movement experience similar to titles like "journey." It's short, atmospheric, but hard for me to recommend at full price.Gameplay: You are a sphere that can control its movement and even partially its shape. You fly from planet to planet focused on reaching the next transport spot that will shoot you off to the next planet. I found the flying/movement to be ok, you were capable of some fun speeds but there's not much variety and I personally didn't care for the movement system. 3/5.Story: It's really just atmospheric with some memory flashes that made me think of Interstellar in terms of what the "story" was trying to tell, but it's very interpretive and not spelled out as to what actually happened or what is going on. You didn't have much more point than just finding the next extraction point to move on to the next level. 2/5.Music: Suitably haunting, and some great atmospheric noises. 5/5.Graphics: It was pretty, but very bland. I wish there had been more variety in each world instead of the same kind of dead landscape stretching on for a long time. Each world is mostly unique, but just not that interesting after the first few minutes. 2/5.Fun-factor: I beat this in under 3 hours, didn't get all the achievements but really was ok not playing more. I would have liked a more engaging movement mechanic and more interesting places to explore. 2/5.Overall: 2.5/5. Only on a cheap sale would I recommend this, it seems more like a proof of concept than a complete game, especially for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is a game where you basically press "W" to get to the end of the worldspace and into the next. It involves a bit more than that, but Exo One is an incredibly simple game. You control a space craft whose speed is dependent on gravity. This means that when you slow down in the air, you must dive to the ground and find a smooth slope curvature to gain speed and launch yourself in the air. This game has a story that you must gather from bits and pieces of clues given as you traverse the various landscapes with your craft. Exo One is a refreshingly relaxing game. With its simple gameplay and simple objectives, you can just sit and enjoy the absolutely stunning environments that you are meant to travel through. It truly is stunning as the developers have crafted some of the most quintessentially sci-fi environments that are able to evoke your imagination and awe to the beauty found in the game. Mix these with the great soundtrack, and Exo One becomes one of those really neat, simple small games that you will be glad to have played by the end.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: You hear, after carving through the sound barrier in your little marble spacecraft. Or is it a big marble? Who knows; you're far from home and won't find any bananas to help scale yourself.What are you doing? Why are you here? What is your purpose?I don't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ know tbh, but it's hella fun to bomb down the alien hillscape and fling yourself towards the nearest galaxy. I'm sure you'll find an 8-hour long video essay on Youtube if you want the ins-and-outs of the lore.Right, onto the nitty gritty pros and cons+ Great learning curve and depth to the movement system.+ SCHBOOSHtastic sound design.+ Great atmosphere and neat variation + innovation across the levels.+ Relaxing and engaging* Very short (1-2h first playthrough, <1h second playthrough)- Didn't care about the narrative If you like schmoovement in games, if you like space, or if you liked rolling marbles as a kid, you'll love this.

_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. I like it for sure, it was a wild journey of an evening. I feel like it could have been more, and the fact it was (I presume) made on a relative budget is fairly evident at times, but at others it really shone and I feel like it shone more than it didn't. Possibly most importantly for a game like this, it plays well. After the first couple of minutes I felt like I had the hang of the basic mechanics and through the game that feeling gradually evolved into something approaching mastery, or at least something that felt like it (I'm sure I'm not actually a master, but I started to believe I was whilst playing). That's not to say the game always feels good, the level that involved a lot of climbing certainly broke up the pacing, but the climbing itself just felt really bad, camera flying all over the place, not exactly being able to tell how far you are bouncing, I finished that one feeling fairly frustrated. But in the back of my head I couldn't help but wonder that maybe that was the point of the level in the first place? Exo One for the most part is a visceral experience that seems to be trying to evoke emotion as much as present a level to fly/roll/bounce through and at times did so very effectively. I won't pretend I fully understand the story, I'm also not sure I was really meant to. This game... yea it's a weird one. I would recommend it if you enjoy stuff that's a bit more experimental, a bit harder to categorise. It isn't one of my favourite games of all time by any means, but I certainly enjoyed the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: As a 911 Dispatcher, after coming home from a long, stressful shift, I have got to say this game has been one of the best destressers I have had. Usually I'll play some FPS or MMO to get my mind off things but this is a completely different experience that I've never had before.The soundtrack has me in awe, the mix of beautiful graphics as well just honestly brings emotion out of me. It's hard to describe and it's certainly not for everyone but I feel this game can be interpreted by the player into whatever experience they want. Don't try to make anything of it, just turn the lights off, put some headphones on, relax and play. See what happens.Also to mention, the cut scenes and dialog often give me chills down my spine, trying to piece together what happens as I continue to play the game. It's quite the experience and I can't wait to unravel what happened.100% recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo version of Exo One a few months ago and have been waiting for the full release ever since, which I got soon after it's launch. It is a great game with amazing visuals and it is definitely worth the full price in my opinion. Exo One is a beautiful game and even though it only has a few levels, it is still great. It's a very chill game to play, with simple, smooth movement. The controls and different mechanics of Exo One are easy to understand, even though some are not explained to you outright. It's fun, chill, and so satisfying when you hit a dune just right coming down and launch off the next rise at extremely high speeds. Exo One is definitely a unique game, unlike any other game I've ever played. It is a good game any way you play it. However, I would recommend using a controller for the best experience, as moving the camera with a mouse can seem somewhat jerky at times. My one problem with the game is the fact that there is no level select. You have to continue at the start of the level you left off on, and once you finish the game you have to start a whole new one just to replay the levels you want to. I consider this a relatively small problem due to the short time it takes to complete the game, but it is still mildly annoying. Overall, I give Exo One a 9/10, and hope to see more levels added in the future, or at least a level select feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games, but this one needed one. I have never played a game with this true sense of grandiose and borderline "megalophobic" scale. The sound design is absolutely incredible and playing with a good pair of headphones creates an extremely immersive experience. The soundtrack is serene, yet has a touch of loneliness. It's the opposite of the game play. You go so fast, that the colors literally distort, yet the soundtrack remains calm and peaceful. It's such a simple game. You control an alien spaceship that can either be in ball form or disk form, and that's it. But the way the game is designed, the environment, special effects, sound design, soundtrack, and story line make it more of an existential and enlightening experience, rather than just a game. Even just the wind sounds alone, can make your heart rate go up. It's a short play through, but it's worth the experience alone. I would say I wish it were longer, but honestly, I think there's not really much more that could have been done with this game. It's a perfect game (experience).

_childDocuments_.review: You know, this would normally be the sort of game I'd be all about. But it didn't land for me at all.The game makes a lot of gestures at having a story or an emotional arc of some kind, but it doesn't. It will act like there's something coming, like all of this will matter in some way, but it doesn't. This is not helped by the baffling choice to play all voice lines in reverse, which robs them of any pathos they might have had.The gameplay itself doesn't do much to help. Flying the titular craft looks fun and exhilarating in the trailers, but in practice it's fidgety and frustrating. Frustration is an interesting emotion to arrive at in a game with no fail state, but here we are anyway.The worst part of all is how, once in a while, the game just abandons its premise of "follow the blue light" and leaves you to navigate environments that have no signposting whatsoever. Wandering around cluelessly, bumping into the invisible walls at the edge of the map- something the game should have taken pains to NEVER let me encounter, because they completely shatter the illusion it builds -forced me to repeatedly ask myself, "What do the devs expect me to do here?" This question is poison to a game like this.And, spoilers I guess? The climax of the game is an almost beat-for-beat copy of the one in Journey (Oh no! You almost made it to the glowing light beam, but the wind sapped your strength and you died in the snow. What's this? A mysterious force resurrected you? Time for a low-difficulty celebratory sky sequence!) but without any of the impact or payoff. This has the unfortunate effect of drawing comparisons that the game ought not to invite. It worked in Journey because, even without any written text, the player is strongly grounded in the world and in their quest. But in Exo One... there's just nothing there.

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is...nothing but pure unadulterated art in game form. It's not the gameplay or the story or even the visuals, despite their awe inspiring beauty, that make you love the game. But Rather, it's the games bleeding, teary eyed, prideful soul. I nearly cried in the intro level, simply because on some level the game struck a chord at my very being. At the time of writing I am likely in one of the most trying and painful times of my life, and on a whim and a sale, I got Exo One, and I don't regret it for a moment. This game isn't long, or difficult, or complex, but it is worth your time if you're at a point in your life where a quiet, sombre game is enough for you. For the first time in a long time, I played a game with nothing but it's own audio, no background noise, no lights, just me, the game, in a dark room, alone together for two hours. It made me reflect on my life, let me think and in some way, I find that it's likely changed my life in some small, but important way. to any who are curious, I beg you, engage the game on it's own terms, and let you and it have a one on one session, no distractions. You'll coem out all the better for it. Exo One will go down in my list of games I play once or twice, but I'll remember forever. and to the devs, thank you. You've made art that could only have existed in game form.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. Exo One is genre-breaking, utterly unique, magnificently immersive and atmospheric, and is alternately relaxing, phobia-inducing, and exhilarating. Not for everyone, but for me it's one of my all-time favorites. Though short, the story takes multiple playthroughs to fully deduce.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~This game is a one-of-a-kind gem. Though a single playthrough takes about 3 hours, it's a game you'll want to come back to on occasion because of how immersive and atmospheric the weather is, as well as the overall minimalist strangeness of the experience - or you'll come back to it to share it with that one friend or family member who is obsessed with ufos. More than any other game I've played, this game gives me the same rush of being on a roller coaster or tower drop ride. It's audio is incredible, and sonic booms truly feel powerful and forceful. Plunging into the depths of the ocean worlds can give a real sense of thalassophobia; the vast expanses give a sense of autophobia; the vast structures - megalophobia, etc. The whole experience is really incredible - speeding through volumetric clouds on a shapeshifting craft charged by lightning on ancient alien worlds with volcanos and magnetic anomalies - this game is truly one that stands out, and I think the price is well worth the experience.I'd recommend ignoring the controls tutorial, as it is given in a very odd order. Instead, hold the W (forward) key, and then experiment with the space (jump) key and mouse (gravity) button. Once you have the hang of using gravity only on descent and releasing on the ascent, the game becomes a beautiful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so, just got done completing this game. I absolutely loved this game. To take a few comments I've seen to task: I never even knew this game existed until after the kickstarter, I did play the free demo and thought it might be interesting enough to grab after it came out (and boy was I not disappointed), and that was the extent of my knowledge of this game before I just played it through to the end.That being said: There is no way I would deter anyone from trying this game out. If you like interesting, unique style/story games, then I say go for it. This was a really great breath of fresh air from the huge basket of the same old selection of standard genre games. Cons: - A couple of places where info flies by so fast it can be difficult to move ahead if you missed something.- Story is a little too abstract until it starts getting pulled together a bit. BUT once you play it, you recognize it's kind of the point, but I think it could have been done better. I dunno.lPros:- EDIT: I take back what I said about replayability. Might not be a do over immediately, but I just replayed it again and loved it as much as the first time I played it. - Intuitive controls once you get used to it. Might take some time, but a lot of fun to donk around with.- Well done environments to enjoy (they do get 'samey' on many of the worlds by the time you get to an end point, but still enjoyable for certain)- Story is really well done by the time you get to the end. See Cons for an exception.- Bang for buck is excellent for what I paid (not sur if it's sale price, I didn't even check)So in the end, don't listen to anybody - if it looks interesting - just play it and enjoy it. If you don't end up liking it, then we've all bought a bust at some point. Merry Christmas / Happy New Year / All that applies!

_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to Kickstart this game so I am a little biased. This is going to be one of the most relaxing games you have ever played. The environments; the ambient sounds; the homage to influential space movies; All of these combine to create an experience that is sublime. Of course there are flaws but keep in mind it was developed by one person who taught themself how to program specifically for us to experience this piece of art. Do not expect a long journey and do not feel the need to rush yourself (Unless you want those achievements).
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: **This game is for people who enjoy puzzle-like games with beautiful scenery and perfect game design along with an ominous story line to give you chills**Blasted my expectations out of the water completely. Beautiful game. Doesn't belong in a game library, deserves nothing short of a museum. With physics based games you often see numerous bugs or very small issues with the game, throughout this entire play I did not see a single mishap of any part of the game.Movement: The movement is unique itself, the gravity manipulation with the glide feature, along with formatting different levels to take away or give energy to allow the user different speeds or take away the ability to move altogether just puts everything together to make this game playable. All of the levels are very easily guided and I did not experience any confusion on "where am I supposed to go?", every 'puzzle' in this game is about "how do I get up there?". Scenery: Absolute best part of this game, every single scene looks like a moving wallpaper. It blows me away how the game is capable of showing such amazing graphic quality while being so stable and bug-free. So many moments playing this game were absolutely jaw-dropping. So many beautifully terrifying scenes, abstract plot and story, fear factor of the unknown, and the ambient soundtrack to bring it all together makes this game one that I would recommend 10 out of 10 times. Gameplay: The movement is smooth and responsive, the levels are all like puzzles, trying to figure out how to get to some spot on the map by manipulating gravity to use the environment around you is very entertaining. The cleverly placed different obstacles aided in different ways to help guide me to spots that I needed to be in. Some levels gave other-worldly attributes to objects that gave a very very ominous feeling to the game in different ways.Overall this game is one I would recommend to anybody who is looking for a puzzle-like game that integrates beautiful scenes and a story to think about, with no bugs or catches, a game perfect for relaxing and staring in 'awe'.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the money if you're looking for a very chill, relaxing game with optional challenging aspects, while you could just take the smooth route from destination to destination. All the maps are beautifully done and totally unique in their properties, and the parkour puzzles can be quite fun! Get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: As a game I would not recommend this at full price.You don't do anything other than fly between points- this can be a good or bad thing depending on what you like. It looks cool and has pretty visual effects, can be meditative similarly to other relaxed games like Flower.However (just like in Flower) the controls don't translate well to any precision and this makes exploring some areas frustrating. But just going fast can be fun for a bit, and no precision is needed for most of it. There's also speedrunning achievements if you like that kind of thing.(3 hours to finish "story", played with controller)
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly short game (took me less than 3 hours to complete), with a story so cryptic, it seems literally no one knows for sure what happens. Even the best guesses I've seen online don't make much sense, and to me that's a bit off-putting. In my opinion, if you're going to create a story, you owe it to customers to make it a coherent one, and this is probably the least coherent story I've ever seen in a video game. That said, the gameplay mechanics and physics are very well done, allowing you to mindlessly roll, dive, or glide across planets, paying little attention to whatever story there is.This game isn't worth anywhere near $17. I got it for about $5, and I didn't feel cheated. Oddly, I think my review would be more positive had there been no story.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: The planetary and atmospheric designs/ effects are just drop dead amazing. Gameplay is very straightforward and plain simple but can be tiresome at times. However, i really enjoyed every minute of it. 8/10PS: If you are a fan of Sir. Arthur C. Clarke's Space Odyssey, then you are in for a treat since this story reminded me of "Dave" Bowman and his interstellar trip to Jupiter which transcends humanity.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to be one of the best game-play experiences I have had in the past 5 years. I've been following the development on Tiktok for the past year and was extremely excited for the game, and it absolutely blew away my expectations. An extremely atmospheric and beautifully flowing experience, and at the cost of a movie ticket i feel like ive completely gotten my moneys worth. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda wish there was more options then just yes and no on the reviews here on steam. This game is a perfect example of why, cus it's not bad and no i don't recommend against it, but on the flip side i can't rly say i would recommend it ether. The pros are that it's beautiful visually and the sound design, other than that they didn't add real distorted voices instead of just, idk blurr, is rly freaking nice. Also the feel to the game is quite nice. The cons tho are that is so unclear what's going on. Ur an astronaut but a ball, that can turn into a disc. It's rly confusing and u have to play through the game at least once to have an ide of what to do and where to go. Yeah there are some blue lights u are suppose to go to but then there are some orange lights as well here and there. Overall I give it like a 4-5 of 10 due to the uncleanness of what to do or where to go. I like the idé of the game and like i said it feel nice to play, with some clearness on what to do i could see this be rly peaceful and a "good for the soul" game to just calm down and chill out with. But sadly its hard, at least for me, to chill when im having to guess what im suppose to do or where to go or what the endpoint of the game rly is.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an enjoyable, truly atmospheric game. it's absolutely beautiful and innovative. It's definitely of the short and sweet variety but I find it very worth it. The sound, story and level design feel truly alien in an utterly engrossing way. Only after taking a break from the game did I really realize how strange the world I was playing in was. The game feels like a dream in the best way possible. It feels like the creator truly was able to bring their imagination to life.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of the early mobile and online-flash "Learn to Fly" games. Incredibly chill soundtrack, nice and relaxed feel. Not overly difficult either. Definitely worth the time and price. (I beat the game already, can theoretically beat it in less time, but highly suggest taking your time and enjoying the environments.)
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about the game randomly through tiktok, and later I needed a game to play so I grabbed it while it was on special.This game is gorgeous, heartwarming and genuinely incredibly fun.  All while keeping that mysterious atmosphere that we love from games like Journey.  Gameplay is addicting, easy to learn and tricky to master.  But once you get the timing down on your jumps, you find that you spend more time than you need to just messing around with the physics and seeing what crazy jumps you can do.Definitely one of the most unique games I've played in a long time, and worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short but enjoyable.You might enjoy the journey more than the destination, as the ending is a bit ambiguous, open to many interpretations. What to disappoint some.The visuals are excellent as is the general atmosphere, very "2001" (like the end).The controls are simple but effective. It's more of an interactive adventure than a game of skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite nice at first. But the game mechanics are working very selective in such a way that you are forced onto the exact path the developers want you to take. That is in itself not wrong, but the means that are used feel unfair: Invisible walls, and a selective turning off of your normal abilities. All of which is acompanied by a flickering effect that is possibly meant to be atmospheric but which is in fact just annoying.If you want to force me on a path, fine. Do so. Build visible walls that i cannot climb, that is totally fine with me. But invisible walls of all sort are just not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a very long experience, and it's not a perfect experience. But it's an experience that will stay with you long after you've shut it down.It manages to combine so many dream-like elements into a single thread. While playing this you'll experience mystery, freedom, beauty, anxiety, loneliness, triumph, terror, and that wonderful feeling of flying in a dream.With the exception of a few instances, this was a thoroughly enjoyable an mesmerising experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I think Exo One does a great job of giving you a glimpse of how hostile, uncaring and alien untouched planets far out of our human reach must feel like, while also portraying how absolutely tiny we are in comparison to the immense universe we exist in.I found the control scheme a bit confusing at first, but was able to grasp it mixed with the game's physics quite well (except for the water planet, maybe) and soon I was soaring through the clouds of unimaginable worlds in outer space.The visuals can be quite breathtaking at times, at least they were for me and the soundtrack does a fantastic job, underlining it all. And while there's not much story to tell, I think the way it's done here fits the style of Exo One.Played through it in about 2.5 hours and is well worth the price tag of 15,99 € it currently has (although there IS a 10% sale on it at the time of writing this review).
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, simple, beautiful, absolutely loved it. It took me a while to get used to the steering mechanic, but it's totally worth it because the atmosphere is honestly something else. The devs did a very good job creating a "beautiful, but lonely and dangerous journey" feel. Also, the contrast between the organic landscape and large metal structures is an awesome design choice, those shapes look so threatening and eldritch. Scale plays into it, too. I think it is hard to realistically show how big planets are, but this game does it perfectly. Plains stretch in front of you, mountains loom over you, it is breathtaking to say the least. Finally, I really appreciate the diversity of the planets and how the devs took advantage of various geological and cosmological traits to make every level unique. Exo One definitely has a special place in my heart<3
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo is beautiful, unique, and super fun as you fly, dive, and hit mega jumps. A little like Marble Madness, but with wings, it lets the player feel one with the physics and free to express themselves. And although It doesn't need to, the game progresses in clever ways to keep the levels feeling fresh and interesting. The amount of satisfying, skill-based gameplay here is really astonishing given the game has but 3 buttons. If you stop reading right now, and just get this game, you'll likely be somewhere between happy and amazed.There are some odd design choices though, mostly relating to the setting, or "story line", if you're generous with your labels. I have no idea what the story line is, and all the strange voice recordings in reverse aren't enough to get me to care about what little plot is there. That said, it's worth the asking price for sure. It's been one of the best games I've experienced in a long time. Bravo, Jay!Jay, you've got an amazing game mechanism here! In the future, I'd love to see:1) a race format and time trials2) downhill levels3) more "planetary/orbital" levels4) caves5) a tribute to Marble Madness
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Short game. Can be done in about 1 hour if you're used to it.I'm not sure if I can call this even a game however, from the demo and trailer it looks like an exploration game, but it's actually a open world disguised as linear path game. There isn't much to do or to explore besides going to point A to B. It's more like an interactive movie.Scenery is wonderful but can get very repetitive. I just wish there was more to it. It lacks content.I'd say price is right. More gaming experience than gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very simple. You're an object that can change between a ball and a disk, using gravity tech to either increase/decrease gravity, making you gain speed very fast very quickly as long as you use slopes smartly as you would in a tony hawk game.Once you get a bit of speed you store energy, that energy gets used to make you into a disk which you can use to fly around with. Depending on your angle you can use it to go even higher, get more speed, fly even faster and get a sense of speed that even Sonic himself could get jealous of. It's all up to you how adrenaline-fueled you want to make your adventure.Besides that the levels and environments you move around in are breathtaking. I am a big fan of digital photography, I even see it as a hobby if you take a look at the pictures I made from this game so far in my couple hours of playtime. I'd even go as far as to say that I would  even more environments as I got rather surprised when I hit the end at the same night I started playing.I wanted and needed more. More colors, more alien environments to take me away on little adventures and treasure hunts leading to mini blackholes (which are items in the game to increase your energy capacity to fly longer with and such) and for me to take even more pictures in. I wish the developers the best as this is a good foundation to have, and I'll be doing another playthrough sometime to hunt for the last couple of achievements I'm missing. But I also hope there will be perhaps mod support for people to creature their own environments in, and for the developers themselves to add more planets (perhaps even optional pathways if that is realistic) to the game. Maybe multiple storylines from different gravity spheres going around the cosmos visiting planets and places go fly and gravity around in. Overall, very recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game for quite some time. Trailers when I was younger, concept art and teasings. It fascinated at the time, and then the demo dropped. I didn't play it over and over, but I gave it a try and it sparked back up that desire. The desire to just explore, to see alien worlds that hubble and telescopes tried to inspire. To make me feel like to was jumping through something vast.Suffice to say, this game had me more emotional that I thought I'd be. There's a story there, if you want to try and pay attention to it, the personal journey of the pilot we play. But it can also just be your journey, and I think its a special game that can make you feel like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Very curious about what this developer has up their sleeve next. I don't really know what to say... Maybe... check it out for yourself?The story aids most in establishing that science fiction vibe/feel to the game. Along with the stellar music. I've seen people harp about the story, but it does make sense. Aliens would never send plans to a anti-gravity space craft to Earth though, that's a big breach in the Prime Directive. I do have 1 gripe I guess. It is a 'zen' like sort of game for the most part. However, that turns into frustration when your ship's abilities are limited severely or completely taken away. I get that its done for story reasons or to make each planet seem different to navigate. Its still frustrating to have control you used to have taken away. There is a speed running community for this game. Pretty ridiculous how quickly they blaze through the game. You can see my play through took 3 hours. The record is 29 minutes. It shows your time on the main menu screen when you finish the game. Weird for this game to have such a skill ceiling while being so simplistic. Then again, Tetris is simple and yet has a ridiculous skill ceiling as well. I suppose 'Exo One' reaches heights many games fail to attain? A testament to good game design?Anyways, the game conveys speed pretty well. You can dive into sonic booms. Reach speeds that make the screen colors invert (I think they call it godspeed?). I was only able to achieve it a few times, but not to the extent the runners were able to do.Surf on clouds. Skip on oceans. Pretty great experience all around.(Steam broke reviews spacing between paragraphs and the line breaks are a workaround. I'm sorry. )
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what is going on, there's no in game tutorial, and all you do is roll around but no border warning when you can't go any further and it feels like your stuck to the ground, if you manage to get air born it's brief and still have zero clue what it I'm supposed to do in this game. 3 Hours with no in game help, no map, no clue, NOTHING. If you're thinking about this game, I would pass and spend money on something actually entertaining and not confusing. All it seems this "game" is, is just rolling around and being confused. It is not worth the time to even play. 0 of 5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to fly through one of those 1990's Trapper Keeper designs for exactly 10 minutes at a time? Well, now you can!"Exo One" is a very odd, surreal space exploration and flight game that put you in the cockpit of a spherical ship that uses gravity to launch itself into the air. You travel from planet to planet learning How to Train Your Space Marble and meet up with some old friends. Easy to pick up, great for a chill out evening. Play with headphones.Pros:- Immaculate vibes, enjoy this for the ride- Smooth, easy to pick up flight mechanics with a lot of emergent "ah ha" moments- Very cool planets to zip around on, some amazing art direction going on- Great for speedrunners, great movement techCons:- Unless you're in the pipe 5 by 5, it can be annoying to get moving again.- Some levels are way more confusing or obnoxious to navigate that they should be.- Feels like there's a lot of mechanics left on the table- Very short, there's even an achievement for beating the game in less than 60 mins
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but for something that looked so free and relaxing to play, it just ended up being frustrating.I felt instead of being rewarded for smooth graceful flying, that the game was trying to go out of its way to punish mistakes instead, or make it difficult to do what you're meant to be doing at the core element. There were other times where it was confusing where I was meant to be going, or if I missed certain boosters / updrafts, then I just had to struggle through to get to the next checkpoint.(Finally, minor comment, why make all the voicelines reversed? I felt that just left me annoyed with the storyline instead of engaging with it :/)
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Jay Weston, as a child, wanted to touch Jupiter.  He dreamed of endless oceans of clouds and storms that raged eternal.  In his mind, he soared with wings that knew no limit.  He dove faster than any falcon, he swam farther than any shark.  Mankind knows no material wings like those of Jay Weston's mind, no psi-steel or graviton-pulse drive; that didn't stop him from bringing his dream to reality. This may be the closest many of us will come in our lifetime to really feeling like we can *ride* the cosmos, to surf the dunes of an ancient world, to skip off cresting waves of forgotten seas just before blasting skyward like the best frisbee throw you've ever made.  The one that hit the stratosphere and never came back.  The one that made you feel you understood the word "Godspeed".  I'm definitely going back in.  Just for the ride.  It's a short one, to be sure, but it will take your breath away.  Don't stop dreaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: There's no other game that makes me feel quite at peace and yet so powerful.It looks, sounds, and feels so damn wonderful to play! This game is breathtakingly beautiful and bewilderingly bliss for me, and my favourite escape from reality.That being said... it won't be for everyone.For starters, this is more like a walking (flying) simulator with some hints at a vague story that really didn't need to be there... but they don't get in the way and may add to the atmosphere (pun intended) for some people, like me. The game is also quite short, especially if you're going to just rush through each world... this game is there for you to experience, explore, and enjoy... like a simulator combined with a piece of art.And though much of the game cleverly (and subtly) guides or steers you towards your goal if you venture off too far, there are some places where level design that is a bit lacking, leaving you unsure of whether you are going the right way. I wasn't sure if I clipped/slipped through the terrain sometimes. And the camera, though usually well behaved, can get a bit stuck/twitchy when your craft is doing some manoeuvres, in particular around .Plus, as gorgeous as this game is, there are some things that stand out such as no contact shadows when on surfaces and dust plumes right up close in geometric shapes like pentagons. There's also an array of little cross-hairs on the screen - not sure if deliberate. But these are just nitpicky things that don't matter. The game usually runs extremely smooth and I didn't even realise I was playing for integrated graphics for a while, though some of the later worlds made even my dedicated GPU chug for a few seconds, so some optimisation is needed there.Whether you're tearing through the atmosphere like a meteor, breaking the sound barrier and tearing what feels like a new valley into the side of a moon... or gently gliding through the clouds, wafting upward on the droplets of moisture that seem to power your craft... it all feels wonderful and looks even better. And the music and sound design is great too - with a serene yet haunting acoustic backtrack to most worlds and high quality ambience and sounds effects that change depending on your environment. All together it's incredibly immersive and emotive.The screenshots and videos don't do justice to just how good it feels to be in control of the Exo One spacecraft. Some have complained about them, or said they just feel like Tiny Wings, but they feel very intuitive to me (I play arcade and simulators alike) and with a third dimension plus analogue controls it is so much more. Rather than a game with a multitude of meager mechanics, this is one mechanic made masterfully.You can tell that a lot of love has gone into making the craft handle just the way you instinctively feel it should, despite nothing being quite like it. And there are times where planets will test you to get creative when something changes, though I won't spoil anything. Just know that at some point For many this game will be an  but I'm SURE everyone would be able to enjoy and at least appreciate it, and for that there is a  to try the first world. But I know I'll be coming back to play this over and over until I'm old and losing my marbles... save for the marble that you pilot in this game.To the Dev(s?): Thank you so much for releasing this finally. It was worth every cent for me, and I look forward to any updates it receives. It does need a little polish but is amazing - and I'm very thankful you'll be working on a planet/level selector so we can enjoy them individually.Visual/Sound: 10/10Control/UI: 8/10Gameplay: 7/10Story/Immersion: 7/10Performance/Fun:9/10A solid 42/50 from me. The meaning of life, the universe, and everything!The answer to my deepest subconscious desires, but room for improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking amazing. Words cannot describe it. It is such a simple game with stunning visuals. I had so much fun playing. It is extremely relaxing and the soundtracks is so mesmerizing. This game goes to show how you can make a good game without complicated story and controls. The whole story is just guiding the ball/disc or whatever that thing is towards the light. The entire game is just a simplified obstacle course. I played this game on Fedora 35 Linux with Steam Proton, and it runs well without issues. Some cutscenes do not show properly, but 95% of the time, The game played well.I liked Journey, Abzu, Thumper and now Exo One joins that list of visually stunning and relaxing games. The playtime is only about 2 to 2:30 hrs, I think. I finished the game in 2 hours and 3 minutes. If you can play well, you can probably finish it much sooner. This game is a must-play for anyone who just wants to kick back and relax for a few hours. A must-buy for sure. Even at full price. Don't wait for the sale to enjoy the beautiful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who loves space/universe, this game is so chill to play. I get to explore the different planets and space. The control is easy to learn and play. Game is pretty simple, you power up and find a teleporter to the next place. There are no enemies or danger, so you get to really explore and enjoy the environment. The atmosphere and music are amazing. It was really fun to fly the spaceship after you get used to the controls, and trying to break sound barriers was satisfying. I love the game, I wish it was longer and the story line was easier to understand. Overall, if you like space and a chill game, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: dude, this game. THIS IS ******* AMAZING, I finished it in just under an hour and 30 mins but everything about this is sheer beauty!!! the graphics are amazing each world is just a joy to look at and fly around in the story is just vague enough for you to piece together some bits but vague enough so you dont have a complete picture, and the ending really threw me off!!. if I could give you guys game of the year I so would. it's amazing for 5 years of work

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is an intergalactic experience made excellent by its high-quality design on all fronts. The movement has an exceptional flow, and the weaving and gliding would be interesting enough on their own. The atmosphere is crafted to aid the movement, and the mysterious story, make this an intergalactic journey not to be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Worst $17 ever spent, even COD skins give more value for money than this (which is a crazy thing to say, ik). It's one interesting gameplay mechanic overused for 2-3hrs. The game should've been 1/3 the price and 1/3 the time because there's nothing to do except repeat the same thing on different skinned planets. 1. Optimisation is horrible, especially since there is barely any content... they still didn't bother to optimise the little there is.2. The flying ball gets boring after a few minutes and then all you have is vague flashes of public domain images from NASA and a lazy VAGUE story delivered in form of text dialogues with random slowed down vocals for SFX. Somehow the story is supposed to be about some Jupiter Astronaut yet there is nothing resembling even a fraction of good storytelling here. It really frustrates me, there is no hook, no reason to care about any of the mumbling text dialogues, no reason to why I'm driving a shape-changing Alien ball ship. 3. I did enjoy the Space Level with comets and the Black Hole segment in the end, these were great ideas yet only a small fraction of the experience. The game never really utilised it's mechanic in an interesting way. Poor Execution overall.This would be a great game if it was free, this would be a sub-par game if it was $5 but dude... This is probably greedier than Ubislop and EA, which is insane coming from an indie studio. I honestly don't know how people aren't mad about this gimmicky game.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Neat momentum-based platformer set in an abstract space story across various planets and environments. If you ever played Tiny Wings on mobile you'll know the basics of the gameplay. You control an experimental spaceship that can roll around in the shape of a ball to gain momentum or flatten out to use the momentum and glide through the air across great distances.The core gameplay is fun, the mechanics worked in Tiny Wings and work here as well, the problem is with level design. It doesn't seem like much thought went into designing the levels other than "theme" so most of the time you don't really have any good ramps to use for momentum. In fact, in some of the levels the game make it part of the gameplay to work with minimum momentum or reduced movement. This results in most of the game feeling like a really bad Tiny Wings run where you don't get any momentum at all and just waste time doing small jump with minimum air time. Combined with lack of details in the environments the levels just drag on and on.There's some fun to be had here, particularly the early levels are really good. I just don't think the concept work for the full game time even when the game is as short as this one was (around 2 hours). Might be worth buying on sale but at full price I really can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be clear, it has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic mechanic. Hands down best feeling game i've ever played on a controller. BUT.... its short as hell. any normal person could beat this and get it refunded. ez. and the levels are like alpha tests. the levels are interesting but after beating this game twice i've thought of a hundred better ways to use the mechanics for levels progression than what is in this game. its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring as ♥♥♥♥ once you think of the possibilities. ♥♥♥♥ the story. this game needs serious level development. but also seriously there is no story, and if there "is" one its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dog water.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot put into words how much I enjoyed my first playthrough of this game, as I was absolutely entranced with the views you see in every level.I also loved the movement system the moment I started playing, as it was so much fun to see how fast/high I could go.This game is the perfect game for when I wanted to relax and enjoy beautiful scenery, and I loved every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person that has said, on more than one occasion, something like "I would rather starve to death than not be able to compose my art", then you may enjoy this game. Exo One is the epitome of abstract art in gameplay. If you're more a meat-and-potatoes kind of guy, someone who enjoys traditional games, looked at the videos of this, the screenshots, and thought it would be more of an interesting and faster-paced flyer with relaxing music...you're going to hate this game. It is slow paced, the story is barely there and supposed to be extracted from..whatever the game is supposed to be giving you with its indirect story-telling style. The music matches the gameplay's lethargic and lilting design. The gameplay itself is boring at best and frustrating at worst - nowhere is that pacing you're waiting for that you saw from the gameplay videos, never found are the spots of simple complexity or skill-based play. Instead you'll find yourself just...waiting for this level to be over so you can proceed to the next one, and onward from there until you can cross the finish line on a game you know has to be short, and you paid for it, so you just want it to be done with.Frankly said - this game is boring. The story is non-existent. It isn't an artistic, relaxing, fun flyer - it's a frustratingly slow-paced (just get to the damn light cannon already, ball..go FASTER), weird, abstruse 'game' that is less 'game' and more of a 'moving painting'. A painting that you regret buying after you get it home because there's no place for it, it doesn't match the rest of your decor, and the money you spent on it you really should've saved for your main hobby.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, I'm glad I didn't pay full price. It's a... "good" game, I'm glad it exists. But honestly....... meh. I beat the game in 2.3 hours, and it was just meh. Some stages were just needlessly tedious with no real sense of purpose. Just endless traveling... just mindlessly heading toward the blue line in the sky telling you where to go. There was one level that was actually very interesting with asteroids and a star and you had to figure out how to hop to the end, but it was the shortest one. Anyway, Meh. I suppose if you love this genre (is this a genre?) I would say go for it on sale. But if you are not into the genre, I'd skip this one, esp at full price. I got this at 50% off, and I still feel that I wouldn't have spent it had I known. I hate to give it a negative review as it's not a BAD game, it's just not really worth it. But, I gotta do it. Unless you are a fanatic for the genre (?), skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing audiovisual experience with no rush, no clear objective, no definitive story. Just fun and awe. Albeit a bit short, I'd love to glide through more planets. But then again, you can easily return and just explore and have fun. If you just want to relax, stare in awe at beautiful vistas and just let your mind go blank, definitely go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a long rambling one, as most of my reviews are. So, grab a large glass of wine and settle in while I try and work my noggin through this one. If I were to condense most of my thoughts on this down to a single concept, it would be that I don't think this is a game. It's a thing that happens, and you're there to witness it and what you get out of it depends on you.I mean that, depending on how attuned you are to what the developers were going for, you may think this is on a spectrum anywhere between "absolute soul resonating masterpiece" and "basically a pretentious version of monkeyball". I'm not at either end of this spectrum but I'll give my thoughts anyhow.Firstly, a disclaimer; I'm agoraphobic AF, so probably a third of this game I got through while I was a bottle of wine in. The whole transport monolith thing really rattled my thought sponge; after four or so levels I found that it affected me so much that getting through it was a challenge. I've played this for 5 hours and I've had nightmares about it, goodness knows what the lunatic who made it slept like.Yeah I'm weak etc, but the takeaway on this is that regardless of my broken brain, I wanted to get to the end.So, I think this uh .. adventure(?) is essentially split into three main chunks, firstly the mechanics then the story and finally the environment. As I'm typing this I'm not sure what order I'm going with so need to have a think...... ok so I'm going with mechanics first then environment and finally story. Why this order? Well, it's probably because I played the demo and on the strength of that alone I knew it was something I wanted to buy. I liked the casual game play of pressing one button on a down slope and another on an up slope, it was pretty chill and the dev has done an incredible job of the environment. Considering the planet was basically some dunes and stuff it was great to traverse and really looked the part.The mechanics are simple but I can imagine that with enough practice a person could become extremely proficient with the ball and pull off some amazing manoeuvres. It goes without saying that I never really got to that stage, but I appreciate it none-the-less.The environment is in the middle, without a doubt it's beautiful and I've no doubt that a large chunk of the five years this apparently took to make was spent on making the worlds look amazing. They are beautiful and work well for the mechanics, oh and there's a sweet haunting desolation to them that really tugs at me.Having said all that, they absolutely aren't in any way "alien" as some reviews would have you believe. Each world is basically a biome that you'd find on earth with lighting from an eclipse (space rock surfing excepted). I don't think it could be any other way until we as a species find another living world, I guess it's like trying to describe a new colour, our brains can't do it. Finally there's the story, I feel this was the weakest part. I wasn't invested in the characters and the repeated flashbacks to the picture of them pre-mission didn't mean anything much. They were there but there was no reason to care either way. Maybe that's the point, no-one cared after the fact apart from one chap who survived, but then I'm playing this chap or his ball or whatever so shouldn't I care?If I was feeling generous I'd say that there's an argument to be made that my lack of feeling was a product of whatever transformation the pilot of the craft had to undergo to make him suitable to complete the mission. That actually makes a lot more sense and if it wasn't unintentional then maybe it should have been more explicit.The game play loop is simple, casually so, and this isn't to it's detriment. Go down, speed up, go up, glide, and repeat. It's simple and means you can spend your time enjoying the environment which as said before is mostly beautiful and quite passive. Having said that, Exo One does often take an opportunity to ramp up the bloom or the clouds to such an extent that you've no clue where you are or what you're looking at, it's extremely possible to get momentarily lost which is odd because I'm pretty sure that progress is very much on rails.You may be tempted to think that how well you play fundamentally matters to the progress through the story but it's an illusion, or at least feels that way. Many times messages popped up saying that I'd picked up some doodar or other that gave me more power and my glide mode has increased but nothing felt any different and it played much the same way as it always had.It's very possible that I was going through this so incompetently that no matter what I did it made no difference, I know I spent a not insignificant amount of time slowly rolling towards my destination, especially on the more barren worlds. Maybe these messages were more important to someone who didn't take five hours to complete what others had done in two. I'm not precious, so what if my power is out I'll continue dribbling to my destination. It's like telling me that the toilet is blocked when I've spent the last two days widdling out the window.I could go on, I'm sorely tempted to but I'm pretty sure no-one has got this far so I'll wrap it up. Do I recommend this game? Yes, goodness yes, a thousand times. If you're tempted to ask why then you've probably (and understandably) mistook my ramblings as criticism, it's not. Everything I've said is just an observation, it's how I've personally felt about it and it's totally subjective. Before I summarise what I think this is, I'll tell you what I know it isn't. This isn't Battlefield 2042, it doesn't have a £50 price tag with in-app purchases and a 20 page long EULA you have to sign up to or DRM that does goodness knows what to your PC. This is the exact opposite of Battlefield 2042 and I appreciate that.I don't think this is a game, it's art and art is a pain in the arse. It can be beautiful and weird and maybe sometimes it's just a bunch of paint splattered on a canvas. It's not always easy to understand or deal with, and yeah sometimes it makes us uncomfortable from time to time or in my case makes me run about my house wailing that the universe is too big and it hurts so much. But you know what? That's what makes it great and now that it's over and I'm pretty sure I'm not going to play this again, I'm so very glad I did.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was enjoyable but not a must play. This is one of the games I mark as like but I wouldn't highly recommend it. If the trailer looks appealing to you then it is worth a shot. Atmospheric, beautiful, relaxing journey of a ball through space. The music and scenes are beautiful, but the playtime is only a couple hours tops. Worth trying from a friend's library or buying it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Good for it is, a walking simulator in a gliding marble with some light physics puzzles in space.  There is a barely existing astronaut mystery drama glued to it but if it was not present, I doubt most would notice the absence.  Pretty enough.  Inoffensive music.  Imagine a sci-fi game that happens to have a rather pretty aerial travel mechanic with a physics system.  Remove the game and leave just the travel bit.  That's Exo One.  I didn't hate it but I was glad when it was over.  Often felt like I wished it was running on 2x speed.  Encountered no glitches to speak of, works fine.  Hm, this sounds very negative... something nice to say... I really liked the stage where they remove most of your controls except for slow forward and get-heavy with a strong wind pushing you around.  You had to git-gud about using temporary increased gravity as a method of propulsion in a surface covered in craters and hills.  Wish it had lasted longer.NOT worth $17.  Get it only on heavy discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun and relaxing game to play. Was really unique and something very different for me to play which was nice! Tired of playing the same kind of game over and over again. The only drawback is that it doesn't take long to beat. I beat it in 2 hours and that was with me taking my time and exploring some areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is a v~i~b~e. It's a  It's "𝓪𝓮𝓼𝓽𝓱𝓮𝓽𝓲𝓬". It's Space Odyssey, Contact, and Interstellar, in a weirdly accurate dream depiction.Exo One won't be for everyone, but consider giving it a chance. Try not to think of it like a video game, it's more of an interactive narrative experience that is all about the light show. For fans of sci-fi, I would recommend it.Have you ever had one of those dreams where you could basically fly, but only like one meter off the ground? Or dreams where you wanted to go really fast but could only manage a snail pace? How about the one with driving a car but the controls barely respond like they should? Exo One captures all of those elements with what I found to be shocking accuracy. My run lasted around 2.5 hours. I know there were at least a couple collectibles I missed that I was gonna go back for after I finished the game, however much like a dream you know you've had but can't remember anymore, after completing the run the load option disappears from the main menu, and there doesn't appear to be a level select either. Note you can save during a run, but it seems after you get to the end you can only start a new game again from scratch. Oh well. I would have loved to fly around that lovely ocean planet again but I don't think I want to replay from the beginning to get there.There's 10 levels, and none of them take longer than 15 minutes tops. Unless you go after collectibles or just wanna hang out and aesthetically vibe to the mood.If you're still on the fence if Exo One is for you, the demo is still available:
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: So you liked Journey, but want more? Perhaps more flying? Maybe you're afraid of people and don't appreciate the social elements of Journey?Well, this should scratch the itch for more relaxing travel just fine. The visuals are pretty to look at and the relaxing atmosphere really carries through. There's also good diversity in terms of landscapes.I might have more to say about the negatives, but they are more nitpicks than anything else.Admittedly, it might be sticking to certain structural aspects of Journey too closely. But... I don't mind that too much. Speaking of negatives, I did get a few crashes, but I guess they might have gotten patched out because I managed to go through a full playthrough. Also, wish the music played more of a role, though that might perhaps end up detrimental.Tl;dr: A relaxing 1-3 hours, easy to learn but a bit harder to master. Worth every penny and every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic way to spend 2 hours. Yes it's short, but well worth full price. Unique, beautiful, terrifying, existential. It's like a walking sim with a destination, but instead of walking you're peacefully gliding over the terrain, or careening through rain clouds at supersonic speeds, or amplifying your gravity to gain momentum and hit that hill for a perfect launch. You can't lose the game, as far as I can tell, but you can miss things if you don't fly just right. Every planet is unique not just in design, but many also have new mechanics or "puzzles" that must be solved. These aren't difficult puzzles, but they add another dimension to the experience without being intrusive or derailing the "flying" experience. On top of this there is a story told in bits and pieces - flashes here and there. The visuals are stunning and often abstract, lending to the otherworldly theme. I am fascinated by the vastness of our universe and this captures that same sense of awe quite well. I will be playing it again, I'm sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A Magnificently atmospheric game.Almost therapeutic, and escapism at it best in my honest opinion, if this game was VR compatible it be even more awesome.This game has been on my wish-list for two years and i am glad i purchased it ,you can tell it was a labor of love by the developers which is conveyed through the musical score, mechanics and very detailed graphics.I could go on and on with heaps of praise, but this is a good game.

From what I have played though this game is immaculate the sounds and music really bring a depth I didn't know was possible. This game brings a new sense of relaxation and tranquility while also keeping you focused on the task at hand. _childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is more of an experience than anything else.  I very much has that 2001: A Space Odyssey/Interstellar vibe to it.  It's very short, but at the same time doesn't overstay its welcome.  With all that being said, the physics of your spaceship is incredible and when you get a slingshot just right, it's very rewarding.  Graphics are great, the music is perfect.  You will definitely spend time just flying around and enjoying the terrain and collecting all the extras, so there is more than just finishing the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: You're a spherical spacecraft that can intensify gravity 10x to gain momentum across about a dozen different alien planets. The craft is powered primarily with friction so you're rolling half the time. The other half you can compress yourself into a pancake to glide using the momentum you've gained from increasing gravity on hillsides and craters the way a skater would use a half-pipe or a vert ramp. It's got a vintage lo-fi feel to it and the ambient soundtrack sounds like it was made entirely using an electric guitar drenched in otherworldly reverb. It sounds like something I would have made when I was younger and it's quite nice. Overall a sweet short little game if you're into minimal space stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice and relaxing game at its core with sweet visuals!But damn, the background "narration" – if you can even call it that – is very poorly made and entirely uninteresting. The purposefully unintelligible voices force you to read subtitles all the time. It doesn't add to the gameplay in any way. It can't be turned off. The game would be a lot better without this.Luckily this downside is mostly constrained to the transitions between worlds and doesn't take too much time, so the overall experience is still good.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: If you'd want to know this games specific genre, I'd say "Journey-like". Visuals and overall aesthetics are somewhat reminiscent of Journey as well, which should be viewed as a compliment in my opinion. Exo One plays differently though, there is a lot of finesse to the controls which take some getting used to, but work very well in almost all cases: you control your own mass and shape - light or heavy; sphere or disc. That is pretty much it - you can use these physics to soar and glide, fall and rise. It does take some learning to get the hang of it, but it's great fun.My playtime is one playthrough - I may not play through it again but don't regret the purchase. What a fun and relaxing, wondrous and weird experience that was. If you like "weird" scifi or games that are very small and scope but great in visuals, this may be for you! Easily recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It's marble platformer, but with Skiing and gliding mechanics borrowed from Tribes series, and a sci-fi plot heavily inspired by some classics like 2001, Contact, Interstellar and others. What I did like: + Very beautiful scenery. Some landscapes are literally jaw-dropping+ Sound design is great, soundtrack is also good. + Great sense of speed, not every platrormer or racing game can compare to Exo One in that regard. What I did not like: -Some levels are designed poorly and may be unintuitive. In some places you can even fall out of bounds, while others are pretty much linear and game will forcibly turn you around if you will wander where you want instead of where game wants you to. -Game's pretty short, you can beat it in less than 3 hours, and if you aren't able to entertain yourself on your own, that will be it. There isn't much replay value if you don't like gameplay in itself. -Some levels on all maxed settings gave my GPU such heat I haven't seen or heard with any Unity game before, and my rig is much beyond recommended settings from the store page. Not every level does that, but a couple of oceanic/cloudy levels are certainly like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely unique!! Very good, but also very...minimalist? Its a good game to get lost in and kind of..not relax with but zone out with? Works great on the STEAM DECK. There were a few times I got a bit lost, but just remember to head towards any light you see. I recommend it. It's cheap enough not to be a waste even if its not for you. Also, its about 4 hours long if you take your time. Still worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool little game. The movement feels super good and it's really enjoyable to learn by feel and intuition. It's short but I think that's a good thing, it would have gotten repetitive had it gone on much longer without some new mechanics shaking things up. Extra points for polish, no technical issues, glitches, crashes, or bugs whatsoever.Also, nice to finally see first-hand what's on the other side of the monolith. I will probably return for a second look. ;-)

You can sit back and relax, and just surf the clouds, or skip across an ocean planet, or dive into a storm and shoot up out of it... Its very relaxing, simple, and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: What if Flower or Journey were a bit more like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, and also nailed the feeling of 2001 or Interstellar? Traverse beautiful alien worlds full of valleys and dunes, and strewn with monolithic alien cubes, ramps and half-pipes. God is an astronaut and also a skateboarder, it seems. This is a stirring experience when you get into the flow of it. Once you get the basics each level has a subtle but clever twist to it. Except the forest level. Worst level, horrible. I completed it the first time in 1hr58min, the second time 1hr26min. The cutscenes don't count towards your time so don't skip them, it's such a good mood piece. (correction: you can't skip them after the first one) I really liked it!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that this is an experience. If you came here expecting riveting gameplay with a deep, complex story, I'd recommend going elsewhere. In Exo One, you play as an extraterrestrial sphere capable of flight. Rolling and flying/gliding will be your main modes of locomotion. The story is incredibly vague and enigmatic. To put it simply, the story is what you make of it. It's so confusing and mysterious that I still have no clue what was even happening lol. Overall, Exo One was a very pleasant experience. Even if it was very brief.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator if, instead of walking, you Tribes'd. There's a very serene flow state that you can enter once you've learned how to control your little marble/pancake.  No real pressures or dangers, just good sights, sounds and game feel.  Good for relaxing down from stress, or with a little weed.

_childDocuments_.review: *Review at bottom*---{Graphics}---[] You forget what reality is[] Beautiful[X] Good[] Decent[] Bad[] Don‘t look too long at it[] Paint.exe---{Gameplay}---[] Very good[X] Good[] It‘s just gameplay[] Mehh[] Staring at walls is better[] Just don‘t---{Audio}---[] Eargasm[] Very good[] Good[X] Not too bad[] Bad[] Earrape---{Audience}---[] Kids[] Teens[] Adults[X] Human[] Lizards---{PC Requirements}---[] Check if you can run paint[] Potato[X] Decent[] Fast[] Ask NASA if they have a spare computer---{Difficulity}---[] Just press ‚A‘[X] Easy[X] Significant brain usage[] Easy to learn / Hard to master[] Difficult[] Dark Souls---{Grind}---[X] Nothing to grind[] Only if you care about leaderboards/ranks[] Isnt necessary to progress[] Average grind level[] Too much grind[] You‘ll need a second live for grinding---{Story}---[] Story?[] Text or Audio floating around[] Average[X] Good[] Lovely[] It‘ll replace your life---{Game Time}---[] Long enough for a cup of coffee[X] Short[] Average[] Long[] To infinity and beyond---{Price}---[] It’s free![X] Worth the price[] Buy on sale[] Not recommended[] You could also just burn your money---{Bugs}---[] Never heard of[X] Minor bugs[] Can get annoying[] ARK: Survival Evolved[] The game itself is a big terrarium for bugsReview:A very interesting yet relaxing approach to a game. When you look at it simply, you are a ball that rolls around different levels with no other objective. But the way the game is set up allows you to imagine your own story of what is actually happening. The story which the author made isn't extremely in depth which was more than likely purposeful. You are able to explore different worlds and create your own story. The game is short, I beat it in just over about 2.5 hours, depending on how much you explore the maps it could take longer or less time.
