_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but while the game rocks and wears its unique "brainpunk" theme on its chest and is enjoyable for the most part, there are some blatantly bad design decisions in this game.Story: The story has a bad habit of dragging plotlines for little plot reason.. It also has no side story other than dates, team-building events and Brain Messages which is just Twitter and they also lost the plot a few freaking times creating loop holes bigger than the Kunad Gate! Gameplay: The meat of the game. The most praise is sang for this part but even this falls flat. First off unlike every other action combat game this game has NO animation cancelling! But... the highest DPS you deal is on your finisher (at the end of your 4-5 hit combo) that takes a whole 2 seconds to execute. Enemies are especially good at dodging this last hit! You also do not have i-frames when doing this, so get ready to get stun-locked by invisible enemies out of sight charging you at the speed of sound. Also.. for a fast-paced action game you constantly have to stop and slowly charge up attacks (special thrown objects, Combo Visions and Brain Field!) so you have to cut your flow short and it does not feel good. You do not have parry but you can counter, unfortunately its two button presses instead of one. Fortunately this game gives you lots of skill combinations called SAS where you augment you move set with your friends' powers. SAS also comes with Visions which are really important to mitigate damage, improve combat flow and break enemies. Unfortunately most trigger Side content: Whoever planned this should be shamed. ALL the side quests are monster subjugation quests and "collect X items" quests. The rewards are NOT worth it. So many of them give consumables that you easily max out because you can only hold 10 of each consumable or they just give plain cosmetics.. they never give stat sticks such as weapons or plug-ins so avoid these entirely. Also, TV missions requires a full team to get A and S rank!Dating Sim/Bonds: The only one of two side content worth doing because it upgrades your SAS, but now you have to slog through hours of visual novel content just to play the game with the tools they promised!!Cosmetics: They have some sick ass cosmetics that's for sure. Gold plated weapons, laser sword for Yuito, school uniforms and the famous Red Battle Gear. I just wish they put this effort into the rest of the game.Does it get better at endgame? Maybe, in fact it becomes easy until you start NG++ but if you hate a game that disrespects your time and keeps piling the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ until the very end, I suggest to skip Scarlet Nexus.

_childDocuments_.review: BLUF: An absolute Bandai Namco standard. That is "Baby's first RPG, made to this year's technical standards". If you've played similar videogames before (roleplaying games, visual novels, third person slashers) you'll ultimately find nothing new or fresh here, merely a collection of most reliable and safe tropes and ideas fused together.The decription seems interesting and the early hours feel fun with a promise of bigger and better things to come, but ultimately it devolves into regurgitating the same themes and mechanics over and over again, most unfortunately.The game is labeled "Brain Punk". The amount of times the word "brain" is mentioned in and out of context is astonishing. It's all about brains. It's always about brains. Even when it's not about brains, brains get mentioned. Some brains can withstand pressure, some brains avre very strong, some are too weak for this or that, and some characters also have brains, which are important for the plot. Did I mention there are brain fields, brain drives, brain messages, a brain crush move, a brain map that you fill with brain points, and a brain-to-brain connection system which is, surprisingly, called a Struggle Arms System?Now that I've mentioned the braindead naming and writing... A few other things.Graphics are... Nice-ish. There's definitely some design work, but overall the game looks like just unsettling and hallucination-like that it's hard to get immersed in (certain areas are just lazy and downright  quirky).Audio is okay. There are voiceovers over comic-like presentation and there's music. The combat sounds are mediocre.The combat system is pretty flat. It looks like it's going to get better eventually as you acquire more powers, but it pretty much stays at X-X-(X/Y-X/Y)-Y-Hold RT-Repeat. You can use certain borrowed abilities but those don't add much variety, only some efficiency. And some abilities are mandatory for certain enemies on a Pavlovian scale - See enemy X, activate ability Y, proceed as before. You can't choose an approach like melee focus, ranged attacks or magic. You just mash everything together randomly and fights end, eventually.The characters are bland. Yes, they seem mysterious and look like they have their own agendas, but they really don't. Everything and everyone is there to service your chosen protagonist, just from a certain trope angle. And the amount of times I asked myself "What the hell are you/he/she/they doing?!" was pretty damn high. The game never bothers to explain the characters' motivations or have some characters question other characters' sanity. Just because!The plot twists and turns and it's really hard to guess what's going to happen. But it's even harder to get invested and keep caring. Stuff just happens, gods come out of machines, mysterious things and actors are revealed and immediately discarded. The world is built on a need-to-know basis entirely.But the biggest sin is how low bar and family-friendly the game is. There is no immediate gore, you fight  only and every idea, plan or motivation gets repeated at least three or four times so that no player would miss it. In between the monsters, the combat and the global plot you get , which can range from silly to stupid but serve an important purpose - improving your combat interactions with a certain character, so they are somewhat obligatory. And these tend to be very wordy and tone-deaf.But don't be discouraged - there are brain fields, brain drives, brain messages, a brain crush move, a brain map that you fill with brain points, and a brain-to-brain connection system which is, surprisingly, called a Struggle Arms System!

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this with the fact that I do like anime.  I don't watch a ton of it but I do catch at least one show per season, so I'm not coming at this game from a "weeb-hater" perspective, but to be frank, this game is everything that's bad about anime, in more ways that you might at first think.But lets start with the positives.  As you may have noticed from trailers and other reviews, the combat is actually really good.  It starts off very simple, but as you gain more team members and tools at your disposal combat feels fluid and enemies are capable of threatening you, so there is a real seat-of-your-pants gameplay that is really enjoyable.  Oh my mistake, I put a plural in positives.  That's it.  I can't really think of anything else truly enjoyable about this game, so lets talk about the negatives.The  and personalities are cookie cutter anime stuff.  If you think "oh this character looks like x from x anime" you can pretty much guarantee that they will act like them too.  The cool out of touch beauty and the friend loving slightly dense male protagonists.  The lazy but actually super smart short girl, the big guy who actually has a sensitive side, the playboy with a dark secret, the nerd who can't catch a break, they are all there.  I won't even go into the big villain and his motivations because dear god are they trite as all hell.  The  is pretty abysmal.  Not only are there relatively few environments, you will revisit all of them at least twice, if not 3 times.  At the start of the game I went to the same 3 areas twice each before finally being shown a cool new snowy mountain area.  AND THEN THEY MADE ME GO THROUGH IT BACKWARDS AGAIN.  And lets not even get me started about the final zone which is literally just a section from every single zone you've been in stretched out and connected end to end.  The town hubs feel like they are utterly empty, talking to people offers virtually no utility, and there are like 3 quests sprinkled through the city.  These things combined made me stop even visiting it unless i had to at all, instead choosing to just sit in my hideout between stages.  The actual levels are super linear but overly spacious.  You can always tell when there are stronger enemies coming up because all of a sudden there are a ton of throwable debris lying around and the formerly narrow corridor opens up into an atrium or something.  The  is as generic as walmart brand white bread.  There was exactly 1 twist that I didn't catch and that was because I couldn't be arsed to actually read all of the relationship conversation stuff with the playboy character.  There is a lot of deus ex machina, handwaving of atrocities, and plot holes.  I physically cringed when the female MC attempts to kill the male MC [i[THREE TIMES[/i] and everyone is like you should have just told us, its fine don't worry about it, we can still be friends (more on this in the relationship section coming up).  Same deal when the [Literal ending Spoiler read at your own risk] .  This entire story wouldn't have happened if ANY of the characters had stopped and thought for a little bit. And now   Oh god relationships.  So first let me explain how it works.  Between the "levels" you have the chance to return to your hideout with your current party and chat with them, go on mini events with them, and give them gifts.  As your relationship grows with them, so does your support system, which unlocks additional support powers and abilities,  So you'd think "Oh that's cool, so you have to choose which people you have to spend your time with and make trade offs as to which ones you want right?"  No, that would be GOOD game design.  And as we ascertained previously, this is BAD game design.  In this mode you can do it with everyone.  Give a gift to all up to 8 party members.  Go on dates with up to 8 party members, chat with up to 8 party members.  And why stop at one gift?  You can give 2, 3, or 4! As long as its something they like.  Or hell what not give them the exact same thing you gave them last time.  It has a similar effect!  Worse, all of these have tediously long cutscenes, with loading screens between them.   Which means that of the 18 or so hours of play time I have on file a solid 6-7 of them are me just mashing through cutscenes as someone confesses that they like someone else, or the big guy talks to me about cooking or gardening, or the shy girl says she doesn't blame me for trying to kill the person she likes or what ever.  Its ATROCIOUS.  And you do need to do them, to at least lvl 4 out of 6.  The power boost you get out of it is so significant that it makes some previously difficult fights far more manageable.   I hate it with a vengeance.   doesn't really exist.  There are like 4 or 5 main types of enemies, with 1 extra type per zone, and a couple of different riffs on the same ones.  For example "Pool" type enemies spit stuff at you from a range, but it could be oil, water, or electricity, or even fire depending on the zone.  But they all act the same and just apply a different type of debuff.  Initially in place of bossess they'll just stick a big healthbar on a stronger enemy and call it a day, but you do have the occasional good boss fight against an OTHER where it has some actual mechanics and you have to play with your various allies abilities to deal damage to it.  Other than OTHER bosses, there are two more types of boss fight, the x v 1 character fight and the x v x character fight.  The x v 1 character fights are pretty boring, because that 1 character will only have 2 main attacks, and then 1 rarer attack that they'll mix in there, and once you know the pattern its just a matter of throwing ♥♥♥♥ at them and stunning them until they die.  The X v X fights on the other had are a lot more interesting.  Since in these fights you'll be fighting the other protagonist and just like you they can use the abilities of their allies as long as they are alive.  So you might fight a guy with extra fire damage and high invulnerability, or fight him again with teleportation and stealth detection or something.  They are more fun because they will trigger two different phases based on how damaged they are that is actually hype as heck and looks very cool from a visual sense.  Shame their AI is absolute trash, making the actual fights trivial once you understand how they work. I hated how later in the game they just started throwing what used to be bosses but are now just stronger mobs at you in packs of 3 or 4 without actually balancing how they deal damage.  The few times I died it was because 2 or 3 of the large diving/beam enemies would juggle me with their beams while I'm focused on something else and I couldn't land and heal in time.  I really disliked how I couldn't get invested in any character because they are so generic and one note.  I was displeased with how empty the world was, and how large the levels were for how empty they were.   I hated how you only have one type of weapon and it just upgraded in a straight line.  I hated how upgrading your allies gear does nearly nothing.  I hated how you have 3 bits of equipment and you always have to run hp armor and damage, because all of the other ones are just worse. In conclusion, its clear this game was released far too early.  They maybe wanted additional levels, or to actually fill in the levels a bit more.  Or worse, I suspect that this was originally going to be an open world styled game and they ran out of funding.  The combat carries the game but its not enough to buy at $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Since this game has anime elements in terms of story, or characters, if any of those elements are something you don't want, then this might not be a good game for you. Considering it was from Bandai Namco, It feels a little like code vein and god eater in some parts. not all, but if you've played either of those games, you might see where/what i meant. (never played tales so I can't say anything about that)→ OP is catchy and although not the same songwriter as God eater, it somewhat reminds me of it because of the rock theme.→ BGM sounds similar to God eater, but mostly Code vein. some combat zone bgm tho sounds like persona for some reason (i.e Mizuhagawa's theme)→ combat-wise, although some enemies might seem repetitive and at some point locks you in for a few waves, having to mix and match the powers of allies can easily negate/counter/deal with them making combat really easy, and not too repetitive (unless you are farming that same spot over and over then yea). I also like having to execute more than 2 enemies in one execute move.→ as for basic moves, Although many people might say having double jump or air dash should be a "normal" thing and not an upgrade, I think this game is trying to say that you start from nothing and are learning everything slowly. At the end of the day, you'll have enough skill points to upgrade the entire skill tree. If you are having difficulties fighting and leveling up on harder difficulties, then start low. no one's forcing you to start at a high difficulty when it's your first time playing. (there is an option to change difficulty anyway. otherwise, you can just play new game + to have your level carried over)→ Characters in this game are at least grounded to the fact that even if they may be fighting "aliens", no one is crazy enough to be smiling in combat like a crazy war freak being. I believe it's because they want to set a dramatic feeling or at least say that this is serious matter. (idk, i just don't like chars smiling crazy when faced in a world that is like an apocalypse. maybe if the setting was like fantasy and not apocalypse, then sure why not)→ Some may also say that the combat moves here is a bit janky or whatever since you can't cancel attacks or something. Like how you can easily be attacked by another enemy cos you're animation-locked fighting another. But the game already has other ways to counter that. → Combat in this game requires you to mix and match the skills of your friends, with your char's own. Sure you can kill with just your own powers (normal, special, psychokinesis) But doing so, restricts you in more cases than one. if you want to go the challenge of not relying on your friends powers all the time, then sure you do you.The only thing i was hoping was for more large monster bosses where you'd do something special (either as QTE or something else). . As well as human enemies where there is something special happening. Overall, it's a decent ARPG. I can't really say i'd recommend this 100% since there are a lot of diff players out there, but on a personal level, if you like anime, action, satisfying sfx in combat, then you can check this game out. there's a demo anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I might add the review with more details after I finish one of the stories. This review will briefly discuss (gameplay, story & character, and OST)Last week I look at this game at a glance and thought it seemed generic. Turns out, I am completely WRONG. Do yourself a favor and check this game beneath its exterior and you will find a very fun gameplay, an interesting sci-fi theme & stories that supports it, and banger sets of OSTs.Gameplay:In short the gameplay is fluid, responsive, and ultimately satisfying. However, the key word to Scarlet Nexus gameplay is "creative".  I've played many hack n slash games in the past (DmC, Nier, Bayonetta, Metal Gear Rising), and I have never seen the concept of various powers be perfected in a hack n slash game until Scarlet Nexus. In this game you will alternate your combos around your basic moveset, object manipulation, perfect evasion (which has a very precise window and very satisfying to execute) and other quirks you borrow from your friends (e.g, pyrokinesis, invisibility, clairvoyance). It gets much more deeper as you progress as assault vision and more combo be available for use. The game does not shy away on challenging you to use every utility that you have, as the enemy AI have certain powers that can be exploited using your friend's quirks. The enemy can do the same to YOU as well, so to play this game in hard mode you will need to have an awareness of the enemy in your surroundings. Unga bunga is not an option.The con would probably be the lack of enemy varieties, a lot of back-tracking, and the skill tree can also be improved but I found it to be fine since there is already enough variation to do gameplay-wise.Story & Characters:I have not finished the main story yet, but I can say that it is enganging and full of unexpected plot points which I thought would be cliches. I played the story with Yuito first and alternate a bit with Kasane so the story makes much more sense compared if I only played just one path. However, it is ultimately up to you to pick which sides first or to play both at the same time because sooner or later you will found out about the unexplained details that is only seen from one side.For the main character, let me say that Yuito is a CHAD. He is not afraid to express his opinions, emotions and be direct compared to other JRPG protagonists. He also has a clear role as a leader within the team and it shows (again compared to other JRPGs). Kasane will be another discussion as I haven't played much of hers.For the side characters, I was a bit skeptical at first but the further you play the bond episodes I can appreciate the various problems which they have (e.g., lack of actual goal, worries of retirement, quirk insecurities). It is grounded and it is clear these problems are meaningful and feels personal only to them, and it is interesting how Yuito or Kasane reacts as we will not only learn more about the characters we bond with but about the MCs as well. People like to compare the bond system to Persona 5 but in my opinion it is closer to FE3H. To get bond episodes you will need to give them a lot of gifts, and usually I found this gift giving system to be boring but in Scarlet Nexus they actually play around with our gifts and displays them. It is very cool, makes it more memorable and I hope more games like this would implement.The con for the story: it can be quite convoluted if you play only one side, so it is recommended to play another side after one or both simultaneously. Up to you. The dialogue can be quite jarring as well with exposition dumps, especially in the introduction section of the game.OST:Most are absolute banger, and most are atmospheric. Do yourself a favor, wear your headset, search for the Scarlet Nexus OST "Grab your power by yourself", and that should be enough proof for the quality of the OST here. Best part, it's only the tutorial section.Another favorite of mine should be "Welcome to the Musubi's", and many more.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. Only 4 hours in and I had to leave a positive review.First off, the soundtrack for this game is amazing. Just roaming through the towns with the chill music going, really makes me feel like I'm playing an old retro SNES or Dreamcast game for some reason. The world building and storytelling is interesting. I really enjoy the almost comic book style that most of the story is told as. Though, what really makes it engaging is when a full on animated cinematic is weaved into the story telling as well. The art style is very appealing, and I love the detail in not only the outfits, but also the environment. I love the feel and the aesthetics  of it all.I started from the male protagonist's perspective of the story, so I am not sure if it is different from the females perspective, but it seems like that may be the case.The combat is a big one for me. It is very engaging. There are lots of combos, and tricks to discover. It's flashy, entertaining, and it doesn't get boring or repetitive. I find myself looking for objects in the environment to interact with for the psychokinesis abilities, and ways to combo status effects with my current teammates. There is a lot to the combat and the game does a great job at teaching new facets, and integrating them into the environment and your teammates that they introduce 1 or 2 at a time so that it never feels overwhelming. The personalities of the characters are rather wide, and though there are a lot of characters in this game it doesn't feel too overwhelming. I am excited to not only enjoy the rpg aspects of this game, but also to explore the story telling and character development that is already an evident focus. It's also cool that you can unlock combat abilities through building relationships with your squad mates. This is a nice take on getting you to explore the story, while also being rewarded with bonus combat mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a groundbreaking addition to the gaming world that effortlessly combines a captivating narrative with innovative gameplay mechanics. This action RPG developed by Bandai Namco sends you on an exciting adventure in a futuristic, psychic-filled world full of horrible ancient monsters, psychological build-ups, and even greater creatures that get you at the edge of your seat.The most obvious thing you will notice upon starting the game is the way the game looks, aesthetically it looks nothing like any other game really. The bright, animated design stands out and is a visual spectacular that showcases the game's more sci-fi imagery. The character designs are very well done, and the small details in the backgrounds and character models make the world feel even more realistic.Scarlet Nexus' narrative is similarly the beating pulse of the game, and it is not at all disappointing. It focuses on a sprawling narrative involving numerous characters, a shadowy government plot, and the secrets behind telekinetic abilities. The storytelling here is incredibly well done, and the story unfolds in a way that keeps you hooked the entire time. The characters are extremely fleshed out, with layered personalities and backgrounds, forming an emotional bond with them becomes trivial.But what really stands out in Scarlet Nexus is its revolutionary fighting style. It has a new feature called the "Struggle Arms System" (SAS), and you can use it to unleash the psychic powers of your teammates in combat. This not only makes the battles feel visually stunning and engaging but also adds layers of strategic depth to combat. The fluid and frenetic mix of telekinesis, mileage-focused hurling, and effortless power-switching keeps the gameplay exciting and full of variety all game long.It also has strong level design, featuring both urban environments and more surreal and otherworldly landscapes. It is also just fun to navigate these environments, more so thanks to the responsive controls and what is likely the most inoffensive camera system I've ever experienced in a videogame.Scarlet Nexus not only is the single-player campaign strong, but it also has great replay value. This also adds depth in terms of replayability, as players can relive the same journey but in the eyes of entirely different characters. The game likewise highlights a New Game Plus mode enabling you to bring over your spare and see the story in an unexpected way.Scarlet Nexus is top-notch in its PC implementation on the technical end. The game is just gorgeous and it runs great as well even on budget-ish machines. Customizable graphics settings ensure players can fine-tune the experience for their hardware.To sum it up, Scarlet Nexus is a win for the action RPG genre. It crafts a compelling story, excellent visuals, and new game-play mechanics into one of the best experiences in gaming. Scarlet Nexus makes it easy to recommend whether you're into anime, action games, or captivating tales. And it delivers not merely on expectations but actually sets a new bar for the entire genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a fantastic game that ties in great combat and gameplay that reminds me of Metal Gear Rising, along with amazing music and a really in depth and lore rich story and world. The story can be hard to swallow at first, as the game will throw a lot of characters and factions at you quickly in the beginning, but it takes its time in explaining everything. The voice acting for both Japanese and English are very well done, and there are plenty of dialogue in the game to flesh out the world and characters in it. The art, gameplay, and music all tie in for a fantastic game with beautiful scenes and a really intriguing story!The game has a few lesser qualities of course, namely the side quests in the game are not necessarily the greatest, most are just "kill this type of enemy by doing this action" which can become repetitive for not the greatest rewards, and there are not as many animated cutscenes as I would like (there are for major events, but most dialogue is done through still frame facial expressions and read-aloud text).All in all, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a really good beat-em-up sword/blade play game with banger music, amazing characters, and a really in depth story!P.S check out the anime on youtube as well once you play :)

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is pretty good as far as hack and slash goes and I'd rate it on par with the DMC series.First and most importantly this game has everything you would expect from a high quality hack and slash game. With these types of games you absolutely need responsive controls and the camera needs to be on it's best behaviour at all times. Scarlet Nexus does this pretty well, the jumping, dashing and attacks are all very responsive. This game adds a layer of strategy which I'll talk about later, but for now the game doesn't let you cancel out of attacks. This is intentional and it actually forces you to stay on your toes and think before committing to an all out assault, which you will definitely need to do.The camera is pretty good at positioning itself in safe areas where you can see what's going on. Unlike the DMC series, this camera wants to be behind you which isn't a problem 90% of the time. The other 10% is nothing to do with the camera controls or positioning, it's to do with the lock on system. 1v1 tactical fights are no problem because you don't need to see everything or change targets but it can be a problem in some situations when you're being swarmed.Fortunately and this is best part, this game loves its PC users. There are tonnes of options to help fine tune the camera and lock on systems so you'll be able to control the fighting a lot easier. These options aren't limited to camera and button input, there are advanced graphical options which a lot of games released for console and PC seem to be lacking.As I mentioned earlier there is a strategic layer to this game and it comes from borrowing the powers of your allies. They're really fun to use and as you level yourself up and unlock the ability to use more at the same time the game really takes off and makes you feel god-like. The strategy layer seamlessly changes the pace of the game from hacking and slashing through groups of weak enemies to having souls-like 1v1 fights against tougher enemies. The enemies are designed to be beaten with the aid of your allies powers but also breaking the enemy down to expose its weakspots. To help you do this allies will call out to you in battle and there is an encyclopedia built into the game with additional info such as item drops.This game has really high quality user-friendly features. Your allies don't just call out if their power would work better, they also call out enemies you encounter and items you need which are part of side-quests you've taken. Once accepted you can look up the quest in the pause menu at any time and if you have the items on you the mission can be completed from the same menu. This means you only have to accept a side-quest once and never need to speak to the NPC again. The game does a good job of lightening the load so you can focus on progression instead of running back and forth to finish up quests.If you haven't noticed from the media on the store page, this is the same engine that was used for Tales of Arise. Make no mistake Scarlet Nexus is completely free-roam and more so than DMC. You don't jump into instances like in ToA. What the engine does bring to the table is the skits and relationship building that you see in the Tales of series. It adds so much depth to the characters by giving them personality, hobbies, interests, backstories etc.Last thing to note is that Scarlet Nexus uses a two-sided story system and you'll be locked into your chosen character until the end of the game. Once cleared you can play as the other character and carry over all your gear and levels. once you complete both stories a merged save will be created that allows you to switch main character at will and retain everything from both playthroughs. If I haven't said it enough, the game is very user friendly. I would recommend the DLC too because they offer some pretty awesome end-game battles.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I was genuinely hype for this game to come out when it was first announced and in a way it delivered. This game excels in terms of combat variety and I felt like I was thriving in a platinum-like combat arena, granted some enemies have way too much health and gimmicks that make you have to reset more than necessary. Now as for the story, it is so tone deaf that it genuinely hurts. I'll try to avoid specifics but imagine a scenario where your best friend disappears for a day and then presumably kills your sister and is 100% making it clear they are trying to kill you alongside one of their allies and then the next day that same person is inviting you to a Starbucks to talk about what kind of girls you like but it's okay because they preface the message with "we're on different sides but let's forget that for a little while". Literally every time I did something where that character was mentioned pissed me off because the happy music in the background and the dopey smiles characters wore in the scenes contradicted the absolute trauma that I should be feeling. It also doesn't help that 90% of this games cutscenes from the action sets to the annoying jrpg coffee meet-ups are just still frames with slightly moving lips that you have to grit your teeth through even if you love story in your games like I do in order to get back to combat experimentation. I bought this on a weekend sale but even this feels like it might not have been worth the $40+ I spent on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a pretty good game. It's by no means perfect - combat can be repetitive, dialogue can feel clunky at times, and sometimes the plot moves in a direction that leaves pressing questions unanswered. The menus also take some getting used to. While there are so many possibilities for visual customization through accessories, the same freedom does not apply to weaponry. That said, there are so many redeeming qualities that, in my opinion, overshadow the flaws. First and foremost, the overall storytelling is phenomenal, presented in a way that constantly left me curious to find out more. The visuals are excellent, and I frequently stopped exploring to simply look around. Every character is fully realized with hopes, dreams, backstories, and do not match the trope they seem to fill at surface level. The music ranges from atmospheric to infectious, and some songs get stuck in my head for days. You are constantly granted new abilities through the skill tree, and intelligent enemy design forces you to utilize your full toolkit well. Bosses are a treat, and are legitimate tests of skill.If you're looking for a game with great storytelling, a captivating world, fascinating characters, and entertaining combat that fulfills every power fantasy, then this is the game for you. Is it my favorite game? Not remotely. But for what it is, I can confidently recommend it to anyone who enjoys this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus. A Game that reminds me of many games I played in the last 10 years. Which is a good thing. What I expected was a game giving off the same vibe as a PS Vita game called Freedom Wars (and a bit of God Eater 3) but what I received was far better. I will keep this review as spoiler free as possible. There is a lot of things I want people to experience for themselves and they are definetly worth itTL;DR: This is definetly worth every cent and I wholeheartedly recommend playing it and if you want to go the extra mile play both sides.Let's start with the gameplay: The gameplay is of course something a lot of people say is the best part of this game. AND IT IS. Phenomenal work of the dev team, the gameplay or rather more specifically the combat feels responsive, really satisfiying and most importantly: It's fun to look at and experiment too. The protagonists' psychokinesis and the ability to use the ability of your party members makes this combat feel really deep and rewarding when you switch back and forth from using one or the other. The types of enemies and bosses are varied and clearly the person behind their art designs knows what they are doing. The enemies called "Others" have that eerie vibe to them, making them stand out and feel like a breath of fresh air in a lot of Action JRPGs, BUT they still feel like standard enemy archetypes. Doesn't mean it's bad or avoidable to make enemies like that for a game like that. Even tho sometimes just getting an enemy that is just the one you fought before but now they have fire instead of ice is kinda disappointing but you will not be completely annoyed by it.The Story, i will keep short: Expect an anime-like story where you choose between one campaign (be it Anime BOY or Anime GIRL. jk they both have an personality and importance to the plot at hand). With the same characters you would see in some "standard" anime JRPGs (please bear in mind I specifically put "standard" in quotation marks as your standard for that may vary from mine). You have characters like a goody two shoe, a old man, an fun loving mischeavious man or shy girl, but 90% of them are written very well so they are not that two-dimensional. The story may feel at some points is losing track OR that it is taking longer than it should but that may have it's reasons (my theory is the upcoming anime adaptation for it which I feel is counter-productive cuz the anime seems to follow the story beat by beat, making the game or more rather the show feel redundant. Still there is only one episode out on some channels on yt and you should look into it if you are interested in it.) The Presentation: This game's art direction is superb. It feels unique with it's "Brainpunk" aesthetic and monster design. The game's graphics itself is what you would expect from an anime game and effects and lighting are pleasant to look at. The music is REALLY REALLY GOOD. I didn't expect that kind of soundtrack from the game and it to be that memorable. Sure it's not like a Persona 5 Soundtrack of memorable or something in that tier of OSTs but it still keeps an identity and I think you will always recognize where it's from when listening to them without a hint of the title. It's electronica soundtrack and the opening song "Dream in Drive" by THE ORAL CIGARETTES are something I will always catch myself listening to in my down time.In conclusion: This game didn't disappoint in any shape or form. The Story and Combat kept me going for all those hours I now have put into it as of this date (27.6.2021 Playtime around 21 hours) and as I said in my TL;DR it is really worth every price it has. Do you need the DLC? Not really, if you have enough money and want to have cosmetics go for it. I got the pre order bonus outfits but I saw that I never really used them that much because the normal outfits already look amazing. So yeah, great game i give it a uhhhh very good out of ten idk I don't really dig the grading of games cuz it don't really represent the quality of a game in my opinion. Anyway I really recommend Scarlet Nexus and I hope to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'm definitely glad I played this, and I'm really hoping it gets a sequel so they can build upon what they've made here. It's brimming with potential. The combat is fun, the SAS system is awesome and adds a unique layer to fights, the character customisation and bond/gift system that decorates your HQ as you play adds a lot of character to your party, etc. Hands down though it's strongest element is it's visuals and presentation. The enemy designs are so rad, the animations and poses are fantastic, the brain-punk aesthetic is killer and combat really pops with colour thanks to the effects on the SAS system attacks, the whole thing looks great. Love to see modern games with distinctive and colourful character designs and effects rather than trying to be photorealistic.(Before getting into the negatives, let me just say I totally recommend picking this up if it's on sale. The first 20 or so hours are well worth it.)HOWEVER It also definitely has its fair share of problems, namely the severely limited number of UNIQUE enemies (I guess that's the trade-off for each of their designs being so cool). There's probably less than 10 fully unique enemy types (not including bosses), as most of the enemy variety comes from a handful of variations to each one of their enemy archetypes (for example a bird-like enemy has a speed variant, a fire variant, and a lightning variant). If this game was half the length, that would be more than enough for most encounters to feel fresh, but the later you get into the game, the more of a problem it becomes. Especially because you'll be revisiting maps you've already been to multiple times throughout the main story. In my opinion this games length is its single greatest weakness. I like long games, but there's just not enough content variety here to stretch over a 30-35 hour experience. Towards the end of the game you're fighting the same enemies you've been fighting all game for 15 minutes straight because they lack the variety to organically increase the challenge, so instead they just throw greater numbers of those same enemies at you with stupidly high health bars. I played the first half of the game on hard mode and loved it, but by the last 1/3rd of the game I dropped it down to normal just to get these fights over with faster. It really feels like they ran out of funds and just dragged themselves across the finish line with padding. These complaints are exactly why I hope it gets a sequel though, because what IS here is really, REALLY good. It's just spread too thin. Now that they've built up the assets, mechanics, world building, visual style, characters, models, voice cast, etc. I'd love to see where this IP can go.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Tales of, .hack, and Persona having a baby. That baby would look a lot like SCARLET NEXUS. I kid you not. This game looks and feels very old school. From the first moments of loading into Suoh City, I was overwhelmed with a sense of nostalgia. Make sure to bring the music volume up - the soundtrack is delicious! Yes, you will be listening to A LOT of dialogue, and yes, there will be A LOT of static cutscenes, but I promise you, a couple of hours in you will get so absorbed into it, you will stop noticing that most cutscenes were in fact static. The animated sequences are gorgeous and the fights are dynamic and fun - using SAS (switching to companion abilities) is seamless and adds a lot of flavour to your fights. You might find your character movements a little awkward initially at level 1, but once you begin levelling, you will see a massive improvement. The combat flows pretty smooth once you're familiar with your buttons - I would recommend remapping a few keybinds if playing with keyboard and mouse (e.g. the keys for switching locked targets - I changed mine to tab and tilde as I found the default J and L quite awkward). The interface is very similar to games from the Tales of series, which can be a little quirky - when it doubt, read prompts and descriptions. The game is generally fairly good at explaining things. I won't comment on the story just yet as I am not far enough into it, however, all in all my first impression of the game is pretty damn positive. The game isn't without issues, of course. In the first half hour of play, I got stuck in one of the menus and had to reload the game. The good news is, I haven't seen neither that nor any other bug since then. I trust Bandai will support the game now that it's been released and they will follow up with more fixes when needed. Give SCARLET NEXUS a chance. Who knows, it might just grow on you a lot more than you would have expected. ----As a side note, I would like to add a few more words regarding dodging and the lock on system. The lock on button will be your best friend - get used to locking on and off continuously. If you are not familiar with circle-strafing, dodge when you are not locked on to a target - trust me, this will make it so much easier for you. Personally, I have had no issues with the lock on system so far - I found it pretty intuitive and my attacks were connecting fairly well. To players who feel their attacks are not landing as intended, I would suggest paying more attention to their character placement and distance from target. Edit after 50+hours: Overall, pretty happy with the game. Really hope there's a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme try this again. I wrote a review about this game but I felt like I needed to give it a second chance... and here I am to tell you not to buy this, now with better words. SCARLET NEXUS tries to be a lot of things and fun isn't one of them. The combat is the only thing that tries to shine but when the game explicitly doesn't want you to have fun, it simply fails miserably.What do I mean? Oh, it's probably the worst decision I've ever seen in a game where high octane combat is the main selling point - dodging is awful. You can't cancel your attacks and if you get knocked down, if not dodging, your character takes their sweet ass time, close to 6 seconds to get up.Also, 80% of the enemies are designed for you to use your allies powers but if they weren't in such an annoying cooldown, things would've been better. You can't unleash your combos because the enemy saw you, hid inside their pants and if you continue to attack, you will deal no damage to them and guess what? You have to turn invisible to hit them and now you're allowed to inflict little to no damage! Yay!The damage your character does is laughable, even at higher levels. It's beyond infuriating how these enemies negate your attacks, it's like playing Yu-Gi-Oh! and every card you play gets Ash Blossom'd. Plus, these enemies get recycled a LOT and the bosses are just some anime people. There's no secret bosses, no extra dungeons or anything of the sorts either. The last boss is just... meh. The big statue part is cool but everything else is lame since you fight this dude named Karen multiple times during the game as well. Yes, his name is Karen and no, he isn't interesting nor wants to speak to any managers because he doesn't have enough charisma for that.Talking about the unvaried anime people, oh gods... I've played as Kasane and I've never seen a more unlikeable main character. She has her personal issues and stuff and never lets anyone gets close but... the bonding system requires the character to be at least friendly, and it feels so forced to see the other characters saying "oh thank you so much for being my friend!" when she's doing the absolute bare minimum a friend should do, and still feels she doesn't feel like she cares. Think of her as an even more emotional unavailable Lightning from FF13.Everyone else is plain as a door, including the other main character Yuito. Dude is incredibly boring and I'm not gonna lie, I've skipped almost everything story related because I couldn't handle how uninteresting the setting was... well, except for Tsugumi because I found her cute. Waifus, am I right?Oh yea, to increase your allies abilities you need to BOND with them. It's such, but such a slog; it feels like playing a freemium game but the currency you spend is time, the only thing you don't get back.There's a crafting system but it's as barebones as one could get. Just... whatever, who cares.With that said, I needed to justify my purchase and powered through this dull excuse of a game with a trainer. Sue me, alright? I wanted my money's worth and joke's on me because I still feel ripped off, even playing with no cooldowns, overleved characters and not getting hit. Yes, the game still feels like a drag even with cheats. It's absolutely ridiculous how many unnecessary hurdles the game creates. Ice level? Oh there's some ice barriers for no f**king reason for you to spend time hitting and ruin the pacing of the action, or lack thereof.Whatever, this game sucks. There are better options out there for much cheaper so stay away from this dumpster fi-- actually the game is so boring that even a dumpster fire is more entertaining than this.

_childDocuments_.review: ※ review based on personal opinion i picked this up during a sale and tried the story demo, starting with kasane's story. really liked the first two phases from the story demo so i bought the game. i've completed both kasane's and yuito's stories and am currently playing the DLCs in the season pass. note that i started with kasane's story first, before doing yuito's and i played with keyboard and mouse… : fun gameplay, decent story done well with great graphics and cutscenes; no harm playing the story demo before deciding whether to buy the game + dual perspective storylines. this was what caught my attention initially and got me interested in the game. we get to play from two perspectives, and the overarching plot is the same. it provided more insights into each platoon's own dynamics and their POV of the events of the story. they have some shared cutscenes, especially near the end, but largely, they have their own path and story-related happenings.+ the two protagonists grow and develop throughout the game. i prefer to play characters with their own personality and motivations (instead of a blank slate protagonist i.e., us), so this is a plus for me, although i understand that this isn't for everyone + while the main plot twists could be predictable to some, it was executed well enough as i enjoyed the story. the details of a few of the twists, while not super novel, they were not something i could accurately predict.+ i really liked how both protagonists are connected and get to interact (i.e., they have bond stories with each other). it was refreshing to see them interacting and how they often cross paths at the start and as the story progresses. + it's fully voiced (at least the one i played in i.e., JP is) - every spoken lines and character's thoughts in the main game, not just in cutscenes. +/- game has no romance (i.e., romance-able characters), which is a plus for me. sorry if you're expecting any. + combat mechanics are not difficult to understand -- it was not complex which is something i prefer. even someone like me who's terrible at action-related games that require decent hand coordination skills could play this and find the combat quite smooth and enjoyable. + there's a variety of powers and abilities to play with/ use and you'll eventually get the hang of it as you fight the different enemies and bosses (i.e., some skills specifically help you damage certain types of enemies).+ plenty of save points in the game; it also served as a hint if a boss fight or new area is coming up. + there are 12 phases for each character, and in between each phase, there's a standby phase where you can chill at your hideout and do whatever you want to do (e.g., explore, side quests, missions, prep, interact with the characters, give them gifts). there's no time limit. once you're ready, you can go back to your hideout to continue on to the next phase. this helped me to pace myself at good stopping points throughout the game.+ this game is heavily story and plot-based (which is my cup of tea), so plenty of cutscenes are to be expected. bond episodes/stories with characters are necessary to increase their bond level and hence their SAS abilities which you will have to use during fights. if you don't like reading or don't care for the characters/plot at all, this game isn't for you. - a few of the maps are rather long…  the maps might also feel a bit repetitive if you play the two routes one after another as the maps' layout/interior remained the same- i do not understand why i can only hold 10 battle items each in my inventory… let me collect as many green cubes as possible. let me hoard !  - unable to buy all materials from the shop besides the S materials?? gotta grind to get some of the mats needed- there is no actually quantifiable gauge for bond links so i was unable to tell how much more gifts i would need to gift the characters (it only tells us the level) or if i had reached the max for the current phase (is that even a thing?) +/- i spent around 30 hours for my first playthrough with kasane, without skipping any cutscenes. +/- you can buy outfits and add wearable items/ cosmetics onto each character (i.e., visuals such as sunglasses, cat ears, mask) and it shows up in cutscenes as well. there aren't a great variety of visuals that are particularly outstanding but it's passable. if you want more, there are more outfits and weapons in the DLCs +/- not much exploration to do as it's not an open-world game; the city isn't super big but it's sufficiently big enough for its purpose, and you will end up visiting the rest of the maps (some a couple of times) during the story anyway. +/- side quests are something you can ignore and not do as it's non-consequential to the entire plot and there's no story or anything behind them. it felt more like challenges to me so i didn't really felt like pursuing them. i wish side quests had more meaning or at least we get to see how normal citizens live their lives in such an interesting world. felt like it was a wasted opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is underrated. There is so much to like here that it makes the few small gripes I have not matter much.Art style and general aesthetic is top tier. Everything is very colorful and flashy, all of the different powers and abilities are great to look at.The story is crazy and dramatic. Every plot twist and new reveal was more ridiculous than the last, and I was fully invested the entire time.Characters are all unique and fun. I looked forward to getting to know each one better in between chapters through a gift-giving bonding system and unlocking new abilities and combos to use.The combat is where the game really shines. Each member of your party has a unique power that you can borrow at any time during fights and use to string together into your own moves for a huge variety of combos. With some upgrades, you can activate multiple of these at the same time.My gripes are only with the menu navigation and some of the command inputs being a bit awkward.Definitely pick this one up any time it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The newest game after  from Bandai Namco's own studio, following the success of it's predecessor while going into it's own direction - Scarlet Nexus is a normal Semi-Open World JRPG in a Brainpunk setting where you rather fight with lots of psionic abilities and their combinations than weapons.Or in other words, since our protagonists have the power of Psychokinesis, throwing every piece of junk and debris you can find in your surrounding into your opponents face until they die.That said, the combat system is the biggest feature of Scarlet Nexus. You have normal and heavy attack moves/combos, both grounded and aerial, and up to 9 different psionic ability skills from your companions of which you can have up to 4 active at a time, skill like (they use up energy that you refill with melee attacks) psychokinesis attacks and special attacks featuring "quick" time events to deal massive damage, companion-combos and even some sort of "limit break" mode and ultimate attack.Unlocking all those moves and abilities takes time, as you unlock general abilities throughout the story and have to unlock special moves and enhanced combos/effects through leveling and skilling your way through the large skilltree, alongside raising companion affinity to unlock combo moves and raise their combat effectiveness. Which gives you enough time to learn how to use all your new moves.Challenging enemies alongside special bosses with their own finisher moves and attack patterns offer variety throughout the entire game. All of those can come with special abilities countered by specific abilities of your own arsenal, and enemies can have armour you need to break and weak points you need to attack to deal notable amounts of damage and enable finisher moves.And funny special objects can be used to gradually ease your fights - how about surfing on a psychokinesis propelled bus and runnin over hordes of enemies?Once again, just like in Code Vein, health and healing is a thing of concern. If you die, you have to restart at the last checkpoint. Which can, if you feel too greedy, be 3 rooms full of strong multi-wave enemies back.To let that not happen you can use healing items and other consumables for you and your team (which have a cooldown which can be shortened via unlockable skills), there are some passive healing skills - and your companions can help you out.Stressing out "CAN" here. You can set a prioritized combat behaviour for them, from "go all out attacking" to "keep a distance and focus on supporting/healing". Though if they actually heal , block attacks for you, offer special attack combos or even revive you when you go down, is up to your level of affinity with them and the gods of randomness. Having a full affinity level 6 team can make fights quite easy, though you can still go down for good first try in any combat and then be frustrated.As a rule of thumb: If you go down and a companion screems at you with glitching out text - you will see "Game over" soon. If not, someone will be kind to enough to help you up.Scarlet Nexus offers a solid story with highs, lows and plottwists told from the two perspectives of your two protagonists respectively. Even though it is a linear story with only one ending that always involves both of them at any given point - playing both "routes" to unveil the entire truth behind the story is highly recommended. Furthermore both protagonists gather their own cast of companions, having different combat styles and different companion event side stories to enjoy.Considering one playthrough takes roughly 30h (depending on how much you care for the companion events and growingly challenging/tedious side quests), in the end you can expect around the usual 60h of content.Of course one can keep playing after the end to max out their character, or start a New Game+ with the other one (difficulty stays the same though) to finish both routes, and unlock more endgame content after that.The game looks really great with an overall solid design, lots of cool animations and cutscenes and a befitting soundtrack.The characters each have a destinct personality and well developed background story that can be gradually explored with time - and except for one or another overbearing stereotype they are all very much likeable and have character development.Sadly though, they made a really weird decision when it comes to storytelling. Even though the game looks really great and the story consists of roughly 30-40% high quality cutscenes, the other 60-70% are made of Pseudo-3D-Visual-Novel style dialogue, where you have still images of the background (even though they change often enough in some situations to be considered a slideshow movie) with still character faces moving their mouth of the talking characters like some 2008 retro game.The smooth and enjoyable combat gameplay which grows in available options alongside your skill using them is a motivating factor to keep you playing, and the amount of unlockable skills keeping you busy up to level 70-ish offers enough variety even into the late game.There will always be another challenging enemy you have to figure out how to counter and defeat.I haven't bought it, so I can't really judge - but apparently the only available bonus content  consists of the art book, soundtrack and unnecessary extra outfits. Which is included in the Deluxe Edition for a cheaper price, containing even more unnecessary extra consumables.The soundtrack is nice, and generally bonus stuff like an art book or other behind the scenes bonus content like this is a worthy investment, so it might be worth giving it a shot - but that is up to you to decide.Is this game worth it?Sure. If you like combat focused JRPGs with a solid story and challenging mechanics and bosses, are a fan of Brainpunk settings or just generally enjoyed Bandai Namcos housemade works so far, Scarlet Nexus is a good choice to spend some money and a couple dozen hours of your time on.And also, there is always another Steam sale to grab a copy.

_childDocuments_.review: The genre of “Action-RPG” is a big umbrella that covers everything from soulslikes to first-person stealth-action games like Deus Ex to isometric RPGs like Diablo, and many more. But even within that wide spectrum, there’s nothing quite like Scarlet Nexus – a game that combines inspirations from fast-paced character-action games of the Devil May Cry and Bayonetta school with epic JRPGs the likes of the Persona and “Tales of” series. It’s a surprisingly ambitious undertaking, and perhaps even more surprising is that Scarlet Nexus hits far more often than it misses.So when I say that Scarlet Nexus is an action RPG, calling it that doesn’t really paint the full picture of what it’s about. Its moment-to-moment gameplay is a straight-up action game, through and through, like something you’d expect out of Platinum Games – its completely linear levels are structured so that you’re basically just moving from one closed-off battle to another while combat is fast, flashy, and reflex-driven.But the key difference between this and Platinum’s style is that Scarlet Nexus is just as focused on its story, worldbuilding, and character development as it is on combat; perhaps even more so in some regards. First off, it’s split up into two separate 20-hour campaigns that each follow the story of one of the two main characters: Yuito and Kasane. While their journeys do overlap from time to time these are, for all intents and purposes, two distinct and equally essential campaigns that you can play in either order, and completing them both is required to get a full understanding of Scarlet Nexus’s story.And it’s a story worth experiencing – one which takes place in a fascinating world where the vast majority of the population are gifted with powers of the mind. City streets are colored with augmented-reality advertisements, people are able to send messages directly to each others’ brains, and those with exceptional combat abilities are drafted into a Special Forces-like organization called the OSF (Others Suppression Force) to do battle against otherworldly monstrosities known as “Others.”Both Yuito and Kasane begin as newly minted members of the OSF and are placed onto two different platoons, each with their own squadmates and leaders; from that starting point, their journeys branch out in ways that have each character experiencing one side of a dense and complex plot full of conspiracies, ulterior motives, and surprising twists. Bandai Namco does an outstanding job of posing questions in one character’s playthrough and then answering them in the other by providing added context that better explains what led to certain events in ways that lead to some really satisfying pay-offs.While the overarching story is great, what really makes Scarlet Nexus special is the amount of care taken to develop its large supporting cast of eight characters who join Yuito and Kasane’s parties. After most big missions, you’re brought back to your hideout for a “stand-by phase” that gives you an opportunity to converse with your teammates, give them gifts (which they amusingly occasionally play with,) and trigger “bond episodes” that allow you to increase your bond level with each one. This is nothing super new to fans of the Mass Effect or Persona series, but what’s interesting about the way it’s handled here in Scarlet Nexus is that the bond episodes are very often tied to what’s happening in the main story, are entirely different depending on which campaign you’re playing, and are not always about improving a relationship. Sometimes the interactions in these bond episodes are outright hostile, but the important thing is that you always learn something about the character and why they act the way they do, or something that better explains the actions they just took in the main story.Even though most of the characters in Scarlet Nexus do fall into very tropey anime archetypes (the childhood friend/romantic interest, the snooty elitist brat, the shy and soft-spoken girl, and so on) these bond episodes do a wonderful job of developing them, to a point where they wind up becoming more than just their tropes. By the end, even the ones that I rolled my eyes at initially – like the aforementioned snooty elitist prick, Shiden – became characters that I grew to really care about.While these scenes are rewards unto themselves, increasing your bond with a party member will also improve their special powers and open up more opportunities for them to help you in battle. That’s a nice extra incentive that also ties into the idea that your relationships with these characters are growing stronger.The story is also helped by wonderful performances in both English and Japanese, with the ability to choose whichever one strikes your fancy from the main menu. While it would’ve been nice to have more animated cutscenes as opposed to the static storyboard animatics, it’s an understandable compromise considering the sheer mountain of dialogue there is in Scarlet Nexus.It’s understandable to take a look at Scarlet Nexus and write it off as “just another anime game,” but doing so would be a big mistake. This is an ambitious undertaking from Bandai Namco, one that attempts to blend the two disparate genres of character-action game and large-scale JRPG, and achieves an impressive level of success. Its combat and thin enemy variety don’t hold up all the way to the end of the combined 40 hours of its dual campaigns, but its story and characters absolutely do, and make for a surprise breakout hit of 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a story driven action jrpg which you can experience through two different point of views: Yuito and Kasane. If you're planning to only play through one side, I'd suggest Kasane, due to certain story elements and to keep Yuito for the EX NG playthrough, if you end up still being interested in the game. I found the combat mechanics to be pretty interesting. However, depending on the difficulty you play on, it can feel like a chore(only affects health and crush gauge). I'd suggest grabbing "Brain Crush SAS Restore" and at least one "Concurrent SAS Activation" somewhat early on. These 2 Brain Map Support nodes makes combat so much better, it's unbelievable.I've seen some people complain about the Mouse and Keyboard controls, but they are perfectly fine, if not better than most action jrpgs with mouse support. The only thing you would really have to rebind is target change for Lock On, which is not even needed to complete the game(I just relocked on if needed). Keep in mind that you can scroll through items with Mouse Wheel, as well as using them with a Mouse Wheel Press.As this is a story driven game, the game will feel very linear. There isn't much to explore. Side Quests can also be quite a pain to complete, but their rewards aren't that great, unless you're going for achievements, then all you really need is 30 of them. There are more of challenges, than anything else.Overall, the game was enjoyable. However, I'd probably suggest waiting for a sale, unless you have spare money or want to support the makers. While your first playthrough may be around 15 to 30 hours, the second one will much shorter, unless you want to get all of the achievements, and likely less interesting, as you will only be missing minor details that is exclusive to a character's path.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I have yet to finish Yuito's Campaign. This game is extremely likable. The story feels very cringe but what it consists of is nothing short of wild when you start paying attention to it. Combat in this game feels very "odd" to say the least, combos are the greatest adrenaline boost I never knew I needed and finishing them ON THE TARGET is the most cathartic thing I've experienced. However, if you aren't paying attention, you may miss your target entirely and look like an idiot. The music is phenomenal, and the map designs are amazing to play in even if they are on the empty side. Relationships with your characters are incredible and I can't believe I feel so committed to some of the squad characters. If you like Anime, Tech Fantasy, and Electronic Music then buy this game you will probably be able to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth playing. Characters are entertaining and the bond system is enjoyable, it's nice how the events that happen in them are sometimes reflected in the dialogue in the story. The story is enjoyable and not as confusing as most of the reviews say but the pacing is pretty poor sometimes as you will finish a chapter and then have like 2 hours worth of bonding. The soundtrack is surprisingly good. Combat is very fun most of the time, but there are some issues with it. The lock-on system can be very frustrating at times as the camera doesn't really track the locked on enemy very well and while dealing with this you will also be getting attacked by enemies that are off screen which leads to you dying without having a chance to react.The auto save system is also very annoying because it barely happens and there are a couple drawn out sections of the game where if you die it makes you restart the whole section because it didn't auto save and there were no manual save points. Would've just preferred if there were checkpoints all the time as it would've saved some frustration.Using your group's abilities can be very satisfying and it works well most of the time after you get used to the awkward controls when you finally get all the abilities. Unfortunately there are a few fights where you can't use this feature and these are terrible because the combat is clearly designed for the use of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a game that is right on the line for me, one that i've enjoyed for my 13 hours or so, but I think might over stay it's welcome before I beat it it.  The game play is generally good, with over the top visuals, crazy powers, and all the other stuff that you would expect, and the story actually has a number of wtf twists and turns that keep it pretty interesting.  Unfortunately, like a lot of other current anime-heavy JRPGs of late, it including a pace killing relationship side 'quest' system, which is basically you buying presents for team members and then going through long dialog sequences that make sure to go through every cliche JRPG-set-with-high-schoolers cliche trope.  It doesn't kill the game, and you can largely skip the sequences and just collect the exp to level up your relationship, but the sudden pace shifts tend to break my engagement to the point of it usually ending my play session.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels so good!It might be not your cup of tea because: you are the cliche protagonist, loved-by-everyone; anime style is overflowing; locations are reused; there is not too much of style/character build - you just increase your power level and repertoire; you can buy million DLCs with cosmetics; yada yada...But who cares! _childDocuments_.review: I really hope you like getting knocked around! There is exactly zero animation cancelling in this game for some godforsaken reason, which means any time you press the attack button or wind up a long-ass psychokinesis you are absolutely helpless until the animation is done. Honestly I have no idea why an entire face button is assigned to dodge: it's not like you can ever use it if you're playing offensively. I love everything else about it. It's got that Jrpg cheesiness I love, it's got a great concept for the combat, the characters are pretty engaging if somewhat generic... but I just can't stand getting smacked because I pressed "attack" one picosecond before an enemy started winding up to hit me and now I have to wait approximately 7 years till the animation ends and I can dodge out of the way. That's a joke by the way, you don't get to dodge in that situation! You see the attack coming well in time, you press "dodge" to get out of the way of it... and your character totally ignores you because they're 2 seconds into a 4 second psychokinesis animation and you're sent flying. Insult to injury it also cancels the attack you were in the middle of animating!Pro tip: IMMEDIATELY get the Rebound skill, or ASAP anyway. You're gonna get hit a lot, and without rebound you spend several seconds lying on the floor EVERY SINGLE TIME you get hit.

_childDocuments_.review: I could write a lot about this game, but instead, I'm going to try to keep it brief. This game is for those who like anime-flavored action combat. The combat is good and really opens up when you get the ability to chain multiple psychic powers together. Playing as both Yuito and Kasane feels good despite their different playstyles, and Bandai Namco has improved their grasp on action combat since CODE VEIN. The music is excellent from start to finish, and the general aesthetic and environment designs are fantastic. Not to mention the enemies, which have the most unique designs I've seen to date. Performance is great, no frame drops or crashes, and it's ultimately fun from start to finish.HOWEVER, if you're looking for a good story here, be prepared to put up with some time loop shenanigans. In my opinion, a large amount of the content in this story could have been cut and the main conflict would have remained unscathed. I had to write down a list of questions I had as they came up because so many mechanics and plot devices were introduced and then swiftly forgotten. Playing through both storylines is important, but really, once you get about halfway through either Yuito or Kasane's storylines, they become pretty similar. Despite this, there are still some good moments and the ending sequence is fun to watch and experience. The writers did a good job with the characters and their motivations (even if some of them are a little trope-y), so if you can handle some complicated (and ultimately useless) plot mechanics, the story is passable.TL;DR, play Scarlet Nexus for the gameplay and design first, and the story second.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game for around 34 hours and honestly I can say it is a great game. Because of the free weekend play, I went into it, and I was very satisfied in some aspects. I highly recommend this game to fans of hack and slash games.The visuals and the music are top-notch, and the locations range from breathtaking to merely so-so. You can usually explore them in a linear fashion, but there are some bonus items scattered around. The game saves itself automatically but you can also do it manually in certain places. Enemies can be farmed, and there are side missions that test your skills but feel rather scripted at times. On the negative side, you're constantly bombarded by tips that cannot be turned off, plus irritating offers and reminders from NPCs that deliver all too familiar information.Choosing between the two protagonists at the start of the game is far from insignificant; each has their own storyline, journey, team and enemies - intersecting in some cases. Yuito is more melee-focused while Kasane favors ranged combat, yet to get the full story players will want to experience both. Fortunately, New Game Plus helps so you don't have to restart your progress after your first cycle. Luckily it's an easy game anyway.The characters of Scarlet Nexus are one of its most valuable assets. There's almost two dozen of them, each one interesting and half of which can be called in to join your party at any time. When taking a break from the story, you can chat with them in their Hideout, give them gifts and deepen the bond between you, which will pay dividends during fights - if the bond is strong enough, they'll save your skin more often, perform additional attacks and make your skills last longer. Interactions between characters are often funny, providing some much-needed levity against the heavy atmosphere of the main storyline. The cutscenes may put some people off with their comic book-style presentation, but I had no problem with it whatsoever.Fights are a joy in this game. Despite being simple at first, they become even lighter and more rewarding with increasing time and skill. Enemies have lives and shields which, if taken to zero before health, can be executed with a fantastic short animation on the press of a button. Crafting also allows you to upgrade weapons to newer levels. Apart from that, accessories, both functional and aesthetic, are also available. And once you unlock the ability tree in the skill tree, up to 4 abilities can be used at once for intense combat results. In addition to this, characters in your party can bring up to nine abilities into a duel situation which makes beating enemies satisfyingly fun. With the ability to throw objects at enemies or take them out by riding on top of a bus full of them - no wonder it's so delicious! The design of these foes is incredible, although there aren't many varieties and species (as some modified versions tend to repeat). But it's enjoyable watching them die as each killing animation looks great!The fun doesn't end there. The Brain Drive allows you to accrue bonuses when dispatching your adversaries and then, of course, there's the Brain Field. As soon as you fill up the second indicator, you can trigger it and be transported in style to a stunning environment with slightly different rules than what you're used to. Your character is suddenly crazed feeling with wild laughter let out as he wreaks havoc on his foes. You'll need to get out of this place fast, or risk damaging your brain by overstaying your welcome, but thanks to the ability tree some god-like power can be yours; double your time, maximize your attack power - all while enjoying a good chuckle!The fights and the styling of Scarlet Nexus are among the best in the world. There are some lapses in the story, but you'll be happy to skip them because the gameplay is so addicting.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a game that made you think this is why I love games? Have you ever watched an anime that made you realize why you love anime? This game does both of these things for me. Closest thing to anime/game genre bend that works so well. Maybe I've been starved for a great game, sure (been playing Lost Ark a ton b4 this). But still, would really really recommend. Super super fun and great story beats and pacing throughout so far.UPDATE 2023: Still think about this game and must say it's safely in my top 5 (behind Persona 5, PM & the Thousand Year Door and BOTW, in no particular order). The only issue I have is that I have no motive to play the second storyline, as a lot of the events that happen in the other plot feel explained to the other perspective exposition-style. It's not completely lost, but still worth noting considering the advertising of playing 2 perspectives to gain a full synopsis. Still, the 1 storyline I played through was really memorable and had some really beautiful and thrilling moments.When reading other reviews on the game, a lot of people seem to think the latter half of the game is a bit meh. I disagree, as sometimes even the best shows have stellar first halfs with more subdued ends. While SN's second half isn't "subdued", it is a bit less hectic with more and more of the mystery unraveling.And, the gameplay is stellar! Some JRPGs forget about gameplay, but I feel the combat loop is one of the best I've experienced from the genre (experience with Tales, Persona, Nier and Astral Chain, of which I'd rank SN somewhere in the middle of these games/franchises).With all that said, I think this game is worth the price. Note: I got this game from humble bundle, so I did not pay this exact value. But, if I had known more about this game beforehand, I would say a retail value is worth it. Plus, it's on sale a fair amount so anything over 50% off is a major boon. If you like anime and can put away a hyper-critical lens on plot, then this is gold.
