_childDocuments_.review: : It’s a world in which every single person’s brain is connected to a cyber network, and most people have, at least, a little bit of psionic capabilities. Those with outstanding psionic powers are recruited into the OSF (Other Suppression Force) in order to battle monstrosities called Others. The story follows both Kasane and Yuito, two people of different paths and pasts that come together, bound by red strings of fate.     • Play female protagonist’s (Kasane) or male protagonist’s (Yuito) point of view for one playthrough, then the other. Both are needed to see the full story.    • New Game+ carries over items, equipment, BP, levels, challenges progression, and enemy compendium progression.     • Battle system is complex and utilizes many different means of attacking. Might be a bit much for those new to JRPGs.     • Develop bonds with party members for additional story/dialogue and improved skills when in battle together. No romance.     • It states “partial controller support” for some reason, but . If there is something in the game that only the mouse can access, I never needed to use it and I’m not aware of it.     • Great English voice acting.    • Fitting, interesting soundtrack. Opening anime song was decent.    • Complex, but fun battle system. It’s satisfying to pull off various combinations of skills.     • Likable female protagonist. Straightforward and truthful. A no-nonsense kind of woman. One might even interpret her as autistic, as she often doesn’t understand people.    • Likable male protagonist. Kind-hearted and friendly. No stoicism or edgelord BS found. No toxic masculinity.    • Decent character development.    • Gifts given and received show up in the group’s hideout as decorations. Sometimes characters are even shown interacting with them.     • Amusing moments that genuinely had me snickering or chuckling.    • Photo Mode is helpful for screenshots, which I take often.     • “Brain punk” is not a thing. You can’t just add “punk” to something that vaguely describes an element or environment in a game.     • Lots of cash grab DLC content.     • The first boss fight with the other protagonist is intended for the player to lose. I hate that sh!t in JRPGs. Like, what is the point of that? Why not just have a cutscene where they fight and the protagonist loses? I don’t even understand the significance of this for the story. It’s during a training exercise. Why would they want the player to lose so badly for that? It’s not even important.     • An unacceptable amount of typos for a AAA game. They’ve got the money to hire people to proofread.    • No diversity, as per usual for a Japanese game.    • Platitudes about death written by people who clearly have never experienced grief on a deep enough personal level that it changed their life. It would, instead, be nice if media  acknowledged how painful and tragic death is rather than denying those feelings by trying to cover them up with faux words of wisdom and sh!t.     • The story is very convoluted. (Not, like, Blazblue level of convoluted. F*ck no, I couldn’t get through another game of that caliber of confusing sh!t.) This game answers most of the major questions people will have while playing the game, but there are definitely some smaller things that I feel the writers were just hoping people would forget about or not think too hard about. There are definitely some plot points that were all too convenient too, that felt like lazy writing.     • Some really WTF writing for a particular scene. Non-spoiler version: Character A asks Character B if Plan X (which involves something sad happening) is the only way to accomplish saving the world and Character B says “Yes, Plan X is the only way,” goes quiet for a moment for Character A to look devastated,  reveals there’s actually another way. So, actually, Character B should’ve said, “No, we don’t need to do Plan X, we can do Plan Y which doesn’t involve the super sad thing.” But they had Character B say “yes” at first solely to momentarily shock the player. WHAT THE ACTUAL F*CK?! What is this writing?! Spoiler version: It’s a mixed bag, for sure. A convoluted story with questionable writing at times, but really fun gameplay and likable characters. I felt it was worth my time and I’m glad I played it. If you’re not so sure, it does go on sale a lot. I recommend it to JRPG fans with experience in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like anime and dark, sci-fi dystopias, even if the plot is a plenty convoluted, crazy, and, well, anime?Do you like Devil May Cry or Platinum Game like combat, just as flashy, not quite as refined and finely tuned, but with a great deal of options for most every encounter?Do you want to make bonds with a band of anime stereotypes, making strong friendships, and then using that friendship to murder the ever loving ♥♥♥♥ out of horrific monsters from beyond reality and the odd humanoid enemy?If you answer "Yes" to at least 2 of those, then I highly suggest you get this game.I'm especially all for the combat. It's not the "perfection" of DMC, Bayonetta, or even a relatively slower game like Astral Chain with how it has dedicated frames, you can't dodge cancel, and reaction times and dodge windows aren't down to the millisecond. It also has its flaws with how the camera can work against you, powers and groups can get convoluted, and you need to give the game time to build up and open more options and upgrades to you.But when it finally clicks, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if isn't flashy, fun, and badass. It's made all the better as I've got a squad of waifus with me and good friends that offer their own supermoves and destructive powers, I can watch those health bars and armor bars drop before the enemies either disappear or I can execute them brutally, like DOOM (2016).I will admit I'm biased: I love these developers and their works, from Code Vein to God Eater 3, along with having low standards for anime beat 'em ups. It doesn't have to be perfect for me to justify dropping the money and the good review.But it's fun for me, and I'm sure a lot of you will also find it fun as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a neat idea, but fails to grab me. I like psychic powers being the focus, there's a nice array of characters, the two stories fitting together to give a more complete picture, levelling up is less of a grind thanks to an upgrade you get at the beginning of the game... there's quite a lot to enjoy from what little I've been able to play over the weekend it was free.What I don't like is how repetitive the gameplay is. Instead of using psychic powers in an interesting way or the more mobile combat style of , it all boils down to: Stab, bash with scenery, stab and bash again; electrocute / enflame your weapon and then stab and bash; turn invisible, sneak attack, then stab and bash... you get the idea. Dodging can be useful, but if you're using telekinesis to bash an enemy, you're rooted to the spot with no way to dodge. Every battle is a slog with cut-and-paste enemy types with different elemental effects.Then there's the two different super modes. The first is similar to 's Devil Trigger, where you build up the meter by fighting.  DMC, you can't activate or deactivate it when you want, just wait for it to activate when you've cleared 90% of an area. The second super mode is one you can activate whenever (but can't keep going for too long unless you want to die, a mechanic I'm fine with), but it makes you slow and powerful with little in the way of defence or health regeneration. Both super modes need to have upgrades unlocked before you can apply those much-needed bonuses.Then there's the story. Having two different player characters experience different events or even the same ones from different points of view can work well if done right. Unfortunately, Scarlet Nexus is too much like , where one story gets minimal depth compared to the other, and feels like filler than an integral arc. Character side-stories can help flesh out the cast, but it is somewhat shallow with some characters. Not to mention how jarring it is how the cast act all buddy-buddy like nothing happened after the two different parties .Overall, there's a lot left wanting from what I've played. I'm not sure if my tune would change if I played through the whole thing, but I certainly would be annoyed in the process of 100%-ing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A largely entertaining action game with JRPG elements. Aside from across the board stupid names for everything, the story and characters are largely decently written and keep things moving pretty well ("Others" and "Struggle-Arms-System" stand out for stupidity-- I'll defend "Major Other", which may be so stupid it wraps around again). Nothing ground-breaking in originality, but enough twists and turns and decent character plots to entertain. They largely threaded the needle with having a overarching "movie" plot but combining it with the trivialities, subplots and character development you get in a TV series, without getting too short or too bogged down. The combat is good, fun, flexible, and has some depth with combinations. At no point does running over enemies with subway cars or tossing trash cans at them get old, and combining this basically enjoyable constant with the variety of adding fire or hyperspeed or armor (so nothing can interrupt you) keeps you engaged. I am not sure if it is intentional or not, but I want to mention that it seems one of the potential protagonists (Kasane) is likely autistic. I found this memorable and engaging due to personal connections with ASD. There are flaws for sure -- quests are rote trash (recommend to largely ignore them unless it's convenient), long conversation/cutscenes are sometimes sprung on you without being telegraphed, and like many JRPG style games they insist you grind the same content a bunch in order to level up. The two main characters seem to invite playing it twice to get both perspectives, but they probably should have done more to allow you to streamline (and greatly shorten) the second play through. I'm also not sure what "Brain punk" is supposed to mean -- yet another meaningless "-punk" naming appendage.  .Bottom line: it's a fun game with an entertaining story and some good characters (and also Shiden, whom regrettably is never treated to a cask of amontillado). Flew under the radar for me, but glad I gave it a shot and well worth picking up (especially on sale -- some of the DLC stuff will ease the grind early, but note most of it is obsolete end game).

_childDocuments_.review: Learn to let goI've heard a lot of complaints about this game and I wanted to give it a shot for myself.The story of the game was good, I wouldn't say it was great and I wouldn't say it was terrible. You definitely have to play through the whole game to get the whole picture which was fine.The game play was pretty fun and what made me want to play in the first place. You get to choose different abilities during game play and there are multiple types of combo's that pop up depending on the enemy. The implementation of bonding with your teammates in the game is a lot more significant then I've seen in most other games which made me more interested in maxing them out. The bonding quest/missions were interesting enough and probably my favorite part of the game. You do get a bit of a different perspective depending on the character you choose, as you can choose either Yuito or Kasane when you play(I chose only to pursue one storyline though which I personally am ok with.)The audio was pretty sharp during battles, hearing my attacks hit were really satisfying. The music in each area was really nice too. I normally find myself muting the music in most games or lowering it but I ended up cranking to the max. In the beginning the audio reminded me a lot of the persona games and I dare say I think I may have enjoyed this soundtrack a smidgen more.Graphics were pretty. There are cut scenes to the game but they're mostly screenshot type cutscene's and the colors and lighting made them nice eye candy. The world you explore is very linear but there are a good amount of maps which brings me to side missions. The game does have them but they don't really feel like side missions, more like side challenges. They don't send you to an area to clear out monsters, more so to challenge you to use your teammates skills to kill monsters and you get a material reward. This game feels like its trying to send a message or teach something(that I don't want to get in depth about, play the game and find out.)As for whether I would recommend this game to someone, I would say yes. It has solid gameplay, an "interesting" storyline(depending on your taste), heartwarming character moments, and pretty sick audio cues.Overall Rating 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: nice, another anime game from Bandai Namco with sick aesthetic and badass character design. After sinking about 10 hours into the game, without finishing it, here's my reviewThis game is the example of perfectly balanced, for every thing it gets right, it has to do 1 stupid thing to balance it out,The good:+ Cool design+ Pretty nice and satisfying combat animation+ A pretty good storyWhen it started and tells you to pick between 2 characters, one guy one girl, I was thinking it's just about the gender and the playstyle, because each character has a different weapon. Nope, it's actually 2 separate characters with their own stories happen simultaneously. Great! That's good replay value, we can get a look at the story from a different view!Now the bad- It constantly shove tutorials in your face, even in the middle of combat, pausing your game to show you how to do X thing- Even after that, it keeps reminding you 'hey, you can do X thing here'. Do they think people playing this game are 5 year old kids with inability to focus and remember things?- The minimap is locked to North, nice, but then the area map is not locked when you open it up, and it has no indication where is North?! So whenever you open it up you spend a good minute lining things up to see which way you're facing and where you need to go- Enemies with one specific way to defeat them. WHY. I'm all for enemies with specific mechanic and tricks to defeat them easier, but Scarlet Nexus' monsters, the ones with specific mechanics and gimmicks, are near impossible to defeat without the right companion NPC in your team. So if you run into them without those NPC with you? Good luck.- You're constantly faced with groups of monsters that you have to fight against, you will be outnumbered a lot, which is fine. But then you realize even the ones outside of your camera view can whack your ♥♥♥♥ up, which lead to your combo constantly interrupted by attacks that you can't see coming, The camera view is not very big btw, and this just make for a frustrating combat experience.- The lock on feature doesn't move your camera until the locked-on monster moves out of view. I have countless time unable to find the monster that i'm locked onto, only to see it hovering the edge of my screen.edit: and i think the dodge move in this game doesn't have i-frame either. So you have to time your dodge perfectly to get a perfect dodge, or early to get the hell out of the way, or you will 100% get whacked in the middle of a dodgeWith a lot more little things that frustrate me to no end.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings on this one. The gameplay is really fun, fast-paced, flashy, and the system to use powers is pretty unique. The problem is that the way to level up those powers is by going to "hangouts" with your partner, which are essentially visual novel segments which sometimes have a gameplay element for a minute or two. It's nice to get a little backstory on some characters, and these do a good job on developing some relationships (although some are no more deep than your standard "tsundere admits you're a cool dude"). This is all well and good, but it can take up a significant amount of your total playthrough. You can skip the cutscenes, so it could be worse, but there are certain cutscenes which can't be skipped that make the process a bit more tedious (e.g. giving someone a gift plays a 30 second long animation for them to say some variant of "thanks" with a black screen transition to and from this scene). A heavy element of this game's marketing was that you can play as one of two characters, a guy whose melee is stronger than his psychokinesis, and a girl who is the opposite. Their stories deviate at a few key moments, but towards the final 1/3rd of the game, they reconvene and tell each other what happened in their deviations. There is no "true ending" for playing through as both characters, so to me there's not really any reason to do a second playthrough unless you really loved the game (which also means redoing all the VN stuff again). Additionally, almost all of the cutscenes are in a "freeze frame with dialogue over it" style, which is a little disappointing personally.The sound design and soundtrack are both great, nothing too exciting to add there.All in all, it's a good anime action RPG with a middling visual novel attached. Worth it on a sale, but the DLC can be pretty safely ignored unless you're itching for a lot more VN segments.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game. The combat is intricate and fast-paced (the movement is in general), so I rarely if ever found myself getting bored of it. The characters tend to have neat little dynamics with each-other, so you can observe a steady progression in their interactions over time, especially if you invest in the bond mechanic. I also appreciate the tertiary information you can access in the menu about the characters and "Others"; having things like a bestiary or compendium adds much to worldbuilding. The only issue I have with this is the translation. I don't mind the rare and expected grammatical error, but occasionally you'll come across stupid and jarring meme lingo like "simp" and "based" in some of the optional scenes that is obviously inaccurate and detrimental to immersion. I think Bandai Namco should be a bit more scrutinising when hiring for localisation.You can customise your appearance in this to an extent I've rarely seen in other games, so it's useful if you want to look cooler or something. I done Yuito's route first and then followed with Kasane's route, as both are distinct enough in story and mechanics to justify a second playthrough. That said, if you're only doing one route, then I highly recommend that you do Yuito's route. His route has one more area than Kasane's route, and I think the pacing is better, beyond Yuito seeming more like a proper protagonist in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent the last seven hours playing this game and so far it is fricking awesome.  Some of the fights can take a little long if you're a casual-skill player like me but that's what difficulty settings are for. I love the fusion of action game and kinetic novel, which gives you equal parts killing monsters and talking with your companions.  The cutscene design is unique and engaging despite their reliance on still images for most of them.I will note that while the game touts itself as an 'RPG' there are no choices to be had, that I've seen so far, and the story is very linear - thankfully, the two character routes are very different and you have to play them both to finish the game, so that means you'll get to see a lot of your first playthrough recontextualized the second time around.  These differences will be significant, too.  While I haven't played the girl, yet, it feels like the boy is the best character to start with. I've seen a few people complain that the game isn't what they wanted and I always agree that a demo is a good idea, but I am really enjoying it and would recommend it to fans of anime action games and interesting stories. (Edit: A bit of advice, you should play both characters to get the full story and start with Yuito so as not to spoil his character's mystery.)

New abilities are granted to the player well into the later stages of the game, and the skill tree expands almost with every chapter.It is my recommendation to favor this game over the animated series, as one ultimately finds themselves in possession of a far more complete and polished work.I bestow upon the game a distinguished rating of 8 out of 10, whereas the anime earns a mere 3 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: SO, how do I explain this game. If Code Vein is Bandai Namco dark souls, Then this game is Bandai Namco Nier Automata. with that being said, I will be comparing to Nier. When i started, I felt the game's combat felt a bit sluggish and the controls felt off, like locking onto target and switching targets was a pain in comparison to most other game with this mechanic. The ability to pick up objects and throw them at enemies is appealing on paper but it didn't blend into the flow of combat. Instead it felt like a needed interruption. Nier's combat flows very nicely with an amazing mix of weapons and combos. The game's UI and menus even look like Nier, so its not attempting to be super unique. The story may be unique, and i find the story to be interesting but it's not worth playing this when i found Nier Automata to be better in nearly every way. Not saying don't buy the game, but I do want these thoughts to be considered.

_childDocuments_.review: In a single-minded attempt to be "flashy", "cool" and "cinematic", they forgot to include a fun game.  The psychokinesis gimmick is flashy, the psycho-punk setting is cool, and all of the systems *look* so good.  But the gameplay is a wild swing between "can probably do it with my eyes closed" to "repeatedly die from god knows what killed me".The normal mobs become incredibly boring after the 5 hours unless you are on a new map with new environmental attacks, and the boss fights range from decently-fun large monsters to ridiculously random enemy humans.  Oh, and did I mention many of the human fights are not meant to be won?  But rather meet some obscure ending condition?  Sometimes you can simply lose, other times you need to stall for time.  Just keep trying and dying until you get lucky and pass!Well, at least they included an Easy mode and an Invincibility item ("Story Mode").  My suggestion if you decide to take the plunge: just equip the invincibility item and enjoy the game in story mode (even if they lean *way* too heavily on the "We need to fight because I refuse to explain anything to you" plot device).  The "gameplay" just isn't worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A boring, repetitive and generic slog, Scarlet Nexus is a game that after the first few promising hours, enters this downward spiral of mediocrity that makes you wish you were doing literally anything else than interacting with the game. The story and the characters that inhabit it are your generic anime fair with a few whacky twists and turns you'll stop thinking and caring about after they've been revealed. The combat is repetitive and has some of the cooler stuff locked behind late game upgrades, and you'll mostly be fighting the same few enemy types over, and over, and over again. Buy something else like The Tales games, Nier games or literally any other competent action-JRPG if you want to experience whatever the hell Scarlet Nexus does well.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:-World setting is cool and has lots of potential-Combat is a bit too simple but overall fun-OST is pretty nice -Performance is great, most settings max with AA off even on a 1050ti-Not too long of a game which I think can be a plus-Voice acting is great (played the game in JP text and voice, cant comment on EN)The bad:-Lots of wasted potential with the story telling. First half was great but the latter half.. not so much. A bit too contrived -The best way to experience the story for the first time is to actually create two saves - one for Yuito and one for Kasane and alternate after each chapter. My personal suggestion is to start with Kasane's side. However, this is not ideal if you are looking to unlock all achievements and 100% the content (everything should be done on a single save in that case) -Because of the repetitive nature of having to play 2 mc's, I can't help but feel like they should have done something like nier automata where it is purposefully designed to alternate. Lots of the story can be trimmed and characters removed and really nothing of value would be lost. It really could and should be a more streamlined, tighter story.-The bond scenes with party members are pretty disappointing, some ideas are great but they don't really fit in timing wise with the main story. You kinda have to do it though to unlock better abilities-Cut-scenes are mostly stills, think like a visual novel. Honestly not great and all should ideally be replaced with animation (which they do have in a small number of places) Overall i think I can give it a  7/10. Worth it for the ~$15 I got on sale. Would still be interested if there's ever an expansion of the universe/sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gameplay:Lets smash buttons and characters go brrrrrr... In a word "Clunky" you can kill almost anything without a strategy, the game tells you to search for the enemy weakspot yet you have almost no control to where you hit, or how you hit... so the main strategy is hitting it until it falls, to start doing combos or gain "access abilities" you have to go into the skill tree and unlock it... the thing is if you don't plan ahead and save your points or expend them thinking, you are bound to just press the "square" button till the enemy is dead.The Animation:Hahahah you were expecting animations... well think again, the game has almost no animation, it is replaced by some kind of "comic/manga Panel" that shows you what is happening, to then return you to the "action".The Art:In my Opinion the Strong point of the game, A stylized 3D anime with Triple A quality graphics, similar to other games from the company like Code Vain or God Eater.The Music:Save from the Intro that I had catch in my head for almost a week after ending the game, I don't remember the BGM or OST of the game, yet I don't remember ether being mad about them so is more like a neutral zone where the BGM or OST cover the situations yet it doesn't stay in your memory.The Characters:Bland characters following a childish mindset I mean i am not against immature characters yet when their personality is bland and superficial things go wrong, .The Plot:The plot is bland as its characters The Miscelaneous:The Story has a time phase that is confusing at first as the game in the first chapters tries to show off their characters, the time pass faster later when they focus on the real plot.tl;dr: +Art 8/10-Animation non-existent/10-Plot 4/10-Characters 4/10*Music 5/10*Gameplay 5/10Over all a mediocre triple A and yet not a really bad game. Judging by the 1 dollar = 1 hour rule it isn't pricey but the game is so long and so repetitive that it loses the point. So I can't recommend it for you to buy but if a friend has it... well you will not lose anything but time.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a sale with the complete edition, I don't think the complete edition is really necessary as the main story is plenty of content IMO. I can't say much about the story because saying much at all will spoil, but it does a great job at characterizing its MCs, and the supporting characters (If you're into "dating" your supporting character you can do that, and through these you actually do learn more about each one of their motivations); There are multiple hard hitting story moments that will make you question all that you know about the world so far. The gameplay is really what kept me playing all the way through, the team system is built around you playing a single character yet calling upon powers of other character, to change up your damage and move-set. It never once felt clunky (barring getting stun locked in attacks). I would highly recommend this game on a sale if you are looking for a unique action JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you have to play more of to truly understand. It's really slow in the beginning and you don't really have many skills or ways to combo enemies. As you level up you earn more ways to combat foes. Combat is REALLY fun  after leveling up. The first impression seems rough but it's a good way to make you feel weak at the beginning and earn your abilities. Really well optimized game as well. Can't take that for granted after seeing so many poorly unoptimized games come out in the last few years. I'm enjoying my time so far after sinking more time into it. Solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give this game a solid "mid". It'll be enjoyable if you want some gameplay and buy it at steep discount.On the one hand, gameplay is fun hack n slash, asthetics are cool.On the other hand, the plot is just a mess with tons of dangling threads, and you go out for drinks with people who were trying to murder you 5 minutes ago, and will try again in a chapter or two. _childDocuments_.review: It's just not a very good hack'n slash game. The combat looks pretty and flashy but it's so very choppy and slow. There are some design choices that are incredibly weird and awkward, like how you can't cancel animations. All attacks are some sort of committement that can get you thrown around. The dodge mechanic is basically useless, it has no invencibility frames and perfect dodges are 93% of the time accidental. Mobs are either very dull to fight or have some incredibly annoying quirk that nullifies any kind of enjoyment you can get out of a fight, like sprinting up to you and blowing in your face, constantly. Human bosses are just stupid and no fun at all to fight, not with this combat system. Actual cool mechanics are locked behind dozens of level ups and lots of skill tree unlocks, with an affinity system that you will have to go through if you want new cpmpanion moves.Then we have the story; Even if you are the most hardcore anime enjoyer, this story makes so little sense and characters are so easy to forget what other characters have already done that you would asume everyone here is born with severe brain damage. The story could be interesting but it is so very badly executed and the way characters interact with each other is just weird, makes no sense.On the other hand, the art style and aesthetics are not bad, and character design is more or less nice, if you don't mind everyone wearing basically the same thing.I come from heavy hitters like Bayonetta and Astral Chain, so I guess I expected much more. This just doesn't cut it, not gameplay or story wise, and believe me, there is a lot of story and talking and it's just not worth listening to it all.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game.  If possible I would have actually rated it 5/10 instead of simply yes or no.  It's not bad, but it's also not good.Let's start with the good.  The combat is a lot of fun.  Once you get used to it it's highly kinetic and plays with some interesting tropes.The bad is that the writing is pretty bad.  The main story has some good elements and could be really good but its too disjointed and not enough backstory is given to really feel the impact of the ending.  Beyond that the friendship/dating sim elements are simply tacked on to this game with no real rhyme or reason.  They don't seem to flow from the game proper and in fact feel very disjointed with the game.  The rest periods just break up the drama and flow of the game.  Frankly the game would be better with out them or at least it would be better if these elements did not feel completely disconnected from the main plot.  Several times things happen in these downtime periods that directly conflict with the current state of affairs in the game.  It also doesn't help that one of the NPC's is simply insufferable.  It makes these sections really painful to play through or makes them feel like they don't have stakes.  Heck at one point one of the big bad's threatens a puppy one of the PC characters is supposed to feel attached to and frankly we had never seen it and it just made me break out laughing.  It was not consistent with the stakes of the situation and frankly it was just plain stupid.Suffice it to say that the main division in this game is between the combat and the story.  The combat is good, the story has a mess of a main plot and the side stories are terrible.  Fortunately you can skip pretty much all the story elements if you want.So this is why I give it 5/10, its basically half a game.  If you care about story this will likely not be a satisfying game for you.  If you care about the combat then prepare for a lot of fun, but also skip all the cut scenes you are able because they will just make you angry.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay game. I'd say it's a C-Tier Platinum game (if it were one). My biggest problem is the repititiveness of the combat/enemies. There are maybe only 10 enemy types and my last 5 hours felt like a drag. Waves of enemies are just thrown at you, which didn't make it more difficult but tedious instead. I've only finished 1 of the 2 playable characters. I started the other storyline but won't finish it because of that. I recommend this game, if it's on sale for 30-40 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much to say about this game. 1. It is Visually Stunning. The Graphics are top notch and easy to run on most systems (i run it on at I7-7700 and a 1070 8 GB gpu) All the areas, characters and enemies look incredible!2. The Fighting is insane. Combos are everything and so much fun to do, not to mention the teamwork between all the members of your squad! You can hit some nasty chain damage on bosses and Ads (basic enemies)3. The unique Story line. I haven't quite see a game quite  like this one with a story this detailed and good.  An enemy as unique as "Others" which look like a mish-mash of random assorted stuff, makes for an enemy that is first rate amongst any game. Not to mention, You can play throw as Kasane and Yuito. Some people recommend you play through one chapter at a time on two different saves as both characters, but I just straight did Yuito's first. The game has that much replayability.4. The Twists. I wont spoil anything but my oh my, the amount of twists thrown at you. I would Recommend not sleeping on this game. Its for sure one of the best ones out there. I encountered maybe one or two bugs while playing at most. Id also suggest checking out the Anime too (currently on going at the time of this review), Scarlet Nexus the anime follows the game for the most part, however the game has some events that happen differently with the same outcome as the show

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... not very good. The only thing that Scarlet Nexus really has running for it is the fact that its combat is fluid and very satisfying at times, making you feel like an absolute badass. But that's it, and while combat is cool, it can get stale very fast, especially with how irritating it can become when you're trying to execute combos and such and the controls, which are horribly designed for mouse and keyboard, hinder you.The story and characters are awful, which is a trend in in these Bandai Namco games. The story also has this obsession of thinking the player is an idiot and constantly spoonfeeds you exposition which makes the plot way more complicated at times than it should be. Characters also make stupid decisions, some ♥♥♥♥ comes out of left field, and the 'standby' phases completely ruin the already crappy pacing in favour of making you try and get to know the already bland and annoying characters better.I'd personally stay away from this game unless you see it for 80% off or something.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the story as Yuito and it was quite enjoyable, though to get all achievements you need to play the story twice with both characters. And some of the in-game challenges are a bit too challenging (like having to enter brain drive 300 times...)Anime games are not usually my thing since they are mostly fighting (Naruto, One Piece), but Scarlet Nexus has a 'solid' story, action moments, chill moments and storytelling moments. And I liked all of them. Going into details:[++]  There is plenty of music this game has to offer, I didn't dislike any of them particularly. If anything, I loved a few. Some environments have two background music, one plays whle exploring and the other while fightning enemies.[+++]  You get to give gifts to your teammates when you are in the shelter. And these gifts do not only improve your relationship with the members but they also decorate the place you spend most of the time in. And to add to that, they will occasionally use the items they were given, or use the gifts with another team member. This level ot detail did not go unnoticed and I am quite happy gifts had more than one purpose.[++]  Events that happen during the bonding moments with the members of the team are not forgotten as soon as they end. They can be mentioned again in future bonding moments and during small chit chat while fighting enemies or walking around.[+] Basic hints like suggestions to use SAS are always the same, and a few other lines, but the small conversations that take place while you are walking around do not repeat and are always different from the previous ones. It was not worthless to keep listening thanks to this.[+]  I've gone to the place a number of time and I always stopped a bit to listen the music. So does the circus battle music.[++]  The bond system that allows you to get closer to them doesn't drastically change how they perceive you but it just improves which is pretty good. Maybe they can get too cheesy about becoming friends and getting closer.[++]  Good for vibing.[--]  Many plot twists one after another, I found myself often clueless as to what had happened and thought I had missed some important piece or cutscene. They explain this stuff later, but I do not like having the impressions of having missed something. I could have restarted the game. It gets steady after the first plot twists.[-]  It was not really convenient to switch out SAS when you need them.[-] When the shop says there are new items, it doesn't show you which ones are actually new.[-]  Click the trigger twice. You can change it in the settings but due to the lack of better options I left it like that.[---]  That is too bad considering the game is a visual novel for a good part. There are many moments during conversations where both people speaking keep repeating a certain world over and over again making it lose its sense of importance.person: I remember you saved my lifeother person: I don't remember saving your life. So your question was about your life being saved?person: Yes I had a dream of you saving my lifeSee how "Saved my life" keeps being repeated? It could have conveyed the same thing by constructing the sentences in a different way.[--] Due to the previous point, there is a challenge that says to use "Super Armor" to defeat certain targets, but that super armor is nowhere to be seen. Turns out you needed to . And this is a super armor because?[--]  I realised why after finding out about the previous 2 issues. Bad translations. Some quests say that you need to USE a certain game mechanic while defeating an enemy, but in fact it means you need to FINISH OFF enemies using that mechanic. This should be more clear![-] Characters can have interesting conversations while you are in the heat of a battle and you end up missing what they said.[-]  It appears everytime you activate someone's SAS and afaik you can't disable it. While fighting the final boss I am pretty sure I know what to do and how to do it.[-] Sometimes when you walk to a collectible in a certain way you just phase through it without collecting it. I ended up walking away and touching it again to get it.[-]  But you can achieve them with EX clear game save slot I think so that should be easier.[-] When you finish playing as one character you unlock new side quests but you cant bring their reward items with the EX clear save slot because it only contains all the items owned up until it was created so you need to beat the final boss again after completing the extra quests.[---] I have experienced data loss WITHOUT closing the game which is even more weird. The first few times I was just confused and thought I had forgotten to save the game before leaving (but no I always save) and it was crystal clear when I could be sure I didn't close the game, in fact I only had left the Vision Simulator without completing it. I had farmed the revive a member X times in it and quit once done. I had also claimed its rewards. But once I got back to the hideout the challenge was uncompleted... So odd...[-]  Especially with the multiplying Others. You can have the correct enemy in front of you but the lock focuses on something else and you have to keep scrolling all the enemies until the focus latches on the correct one and you can attack it more effectively. This takes time and meanwhile you can get attacked.[-]  where you use random combos to defeat the enemies. Whatever you do, you are always frozen in place while focusing on one enemy so their friends can hit you easily.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a JRPG fan or even just an anime fan, this game will probably have something for you.While not perfect, this game has a lot to offer under the hood. Word around the block is that the story is generic and not a surprise at all, which is really only half true. It isn't anything new in terms of concept. A world where the government is constantly restricting information and lying about the threats being thrust at you. But it is really just the chunks of life through out the story that hold the narrative together. And the cast of characters in those chunks are the glue that holds it all together. One of the more intriguing aspects of the game is how it is something that playing it a second time gives you even more insight into the story. You have the choice of playing between two different characters. Each is doing something different and has different goals, but both characters events are happening at the same time. And while they do interact together, it is the moments that they are apart that you may question what they are currently doing. Well during your second playthrough, as long as you choose the other character, you will get all of those juicy details. It just adds some replayability for those that may want it, but it gives them something new in terms of narrative to enjoy.While not every character gets their fair share of love, the characters that have a decent amount of time on screen are very enjoyable. Your companions will go with you on missions and as you spend time with them, your bond will grow. Which gameplay wise leads to some very powerful abilities that you can use on the field. And then narrative wise you get to learn more about them and about why they may be doing the things that they are doing. Which can completely change how you view each character. Even ones that you may be fighting with will hit you up in your DMs and ask to talk about what is currently going on. Maybe to check up on a friend that they are unfortunately having to fight against. Or maybe just to ask you to go to lunch at the new hip restaraunt to try to fit in with the youth. Each encounter is different and each has something to offer.Gameplay is pretty much your traditional action JRPG gameplay. If I was to compare it to something it would probably be a mix between Nier: Automata and Devil May Cry. It is pretty fluid and satisfying, but it isn't anything new. But that doesn't mean it is bad. If you like games like this, you will probably find the combat pretty fun. Each companion has a different power. It can be anything from basic fire abilities, teleportation or even clairvoyance that allows you to see invisible enemies and easier dodges/parries. And you can have 4 companions to share abilities with at any time. So you can be catching enemies on fire one minute, to teleporting around them and doing hit and run tactics. It allows for some really cool moments that dare I say make you feel like you are in an anime. Each ability is put to use and isn't wasted which is something I appreciate in games like this. And later in the game you can start doing pretty advanced techniques like hacking into the mind of your enemies and taking them into your own world where you are a true force to be feared. Think of Gojou from Jujutsu Kaisen.One of the strongest parts of this game is the soundtrack. While exploring the city/hub, you are greeted with one of the chillest tracks I have heard in awhile. And each area where there isn't combat has a very different, yet equally chill track. Think jazzy lo-fi. Similar to games like Persona. But then once you get into battle, you get down and dirty with some metal/dubstep/trap beats. And then when you go into your stronger form during combat, it gets even filthier. It just adds much needed endorphins into your brain while tearing through enemies. There isn't much else to say other than it is just a fantastic soundtrack that adds a bit of spice to the game. There are things I would definitely change. Such as animating every cut scene rather than sometimes having it be a blend of comic blocks and animation. I loved seeing it when it was animated, so more of that would be great. The world doesn't feel as lively as other games in the genre. While I understand it is a world that is pretty dead and bland for the most part, they could add some more details into the world that would lead to exploration. But the biggest flaw of this game is its lack of originality. It doesn't do anything groundbreaking in terms of gameplay or narrative. But I also don't think it is necessarily a bad thing. It doesn't add a lot, but the things it does do it does well. If you are a fellow weeb, I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: Well. Where do I start? With the obvious, I guess. This game has arguably the best visuals I have ever seen in an anime-style game. I mean the graphics are great and so is the drawing style. Cutscenes are replaced by manga-like images but that's okay too. There's a bit too much of these, though, and they happen a little too frequently for my taste and thus can, like, interrupt your gameplay experience. However, this wouldn't be too bad if the story was great, right? Let's talk about the story then. This game is set in a world, where there's basically two cities, that are under constant threat from Others, monsters that fall from the sky and feed on human brains. To combat these, the so-called OSF was formed. It's members have so-called powers, basically magic abilities. Telepathy for example, or psychokinesis, which the two main characters both have. Powers seem to be an important part of this society as well. They're used to communicate with one another (called Brain Link) and even to read signs. Those who don't posess powers are called "duds" and are treated as some kind of second-class citizens. That's the basic premise of the story. At the start of the game you can choose between Yuito Sumeragi, the male protagonist, and Kasane Randall, the female protagonist, respectively. They both have the same power, which is psychokinesis, as I mentioned.  This means that they can pick up objects and throw them at enemies. In addition to that, they have an additional weapon that they can use. While Yuito fights with a sword and specializes in melee combat, Kasane has throwing-knive like things that she can hurl at enemies from mid-range. Other than that, there's a diverse cast of support characters. Up to two of them can assist you in combat. But basically, they only exist to allow you to borrow their abilities. Spice psychokinesis with pyrokinesis, and suddenly the debris flying in the face of the enemy is burning and incinerates the enemy, inflicting additional damage, But more on combat later. For now, let's continue with the story. Or rather on the question, whom of the characters to choose. The answer is one, or both. Hear me out. If you choose Yuito, the story revolves around...well, him. His past, his actions and the consequences of that. However, you won’t experience the full story if you choose Yuito. Kasanes story, on the contrary, deals with more of the problems that society has. It gives you a more complete overview of the world the game takes place in. So if you want to experience the most story in the shortest amount of time, choose her. If you want the complete picture, choose both. Both storylines don’t diverge too much, however. You visit the same places and in the end you have the same companions and can choose abilities from the same pool. For, like, half the game, the story actually is the same.Right. Now that you’ve chosen a character, what is there to do? Fight, obviously. But let’s save that for the next part. Apart from that, you can roam the two cities and…well. Explore them. There really isn’t much else to do other than roam the streets and talk to NPC. What else can you do? You can interact with your companions. Each one of them has a different personality, ranging from an utter scumbag to somewhat of the mother of the group. Somewhat cliche, but likeable mostly.  Between each chapter there is a so-called standby phase, where you can bond with specific characters. In these bond episodes, you basically get to know them better. Sometimes, they request special missions, where you fight Others with them. With each bond level you unlock more powerful abilities that you can use, when synched with that character. Or passive benefits, like longer skill duration. You can customize their appearance as well, if that’s what you fancy. Characters aren’t the only ones who sometimes request your assistance. Various NPC do so as well. However, their quests usually come down to the same formula. Defeat monster x with method y. Speaking of methods, let’s move on to the meat of this game. Combat. Fighting happens in real time, and involves both mouse buttons. Left button for attacks, right button for telekinesis. Then there is a somewhat special attack on C, a finishing move once the enemy has no armour on G, and the various skills you can borrow. Then there is an ability called Brain Drive that activates involuntarily and gives you a boost on your abilities, and another one called brain field. That one, you need to activate on your own when the gauge becomes full. Inside the brain field, your attacks wield devastating power, but you need to discontinue the field in, like, 30 seconds, or you die. Not mentioning assault vision, where a team member performs a special attack, guard vision and…did I get my point across? It’s far too much to choose from. Especially in such dynamic battles. So. Is it worth it? I think it is. I wouldn’t consider this a hidden gem or the pinnacle of anime games or RPG, but it sure is fun. A bit repetitive, but still fun.

An INCREDIBLE GAME...Unfortunately, it suffers from not knowing what it wants to be a lot...It verges from kid-oriented/friendly game, to dormantly sexually charged dialog (again, hard to describe but it feels there, while the characters are not overly sexualised, they feel like they emit too much sexual tension in how they act/speak, bizarrely enough... Everything from dialog feels as though the characters while not graphically sexualised at all, are sexually charged), and the game has a lot of dark/mature themes that would be a teensy bit heavy for kids... Things like conspiracies, grieving, death, while though to be fair they are not very graphically explicit...Also, yes, combat feels same as above...While extremely fun, hard & fair (adult-like), the constant combat VO repetitions from the commanders assume you have the IQ of a pigeon, or are a 12 year old kid...Stuff akin to something like 'Water will make it harder for you to move... Use electricity attacks on them... Flames cause burning damage over time...' Things like that... Only repeated each & every fight, from mob fights to boss fights... I KID YOU NOT...Game just ultimately feels extremely fun, but bizarre, and will leave you like 'WOT?!?' Even Kasane, while she sounds/feels sultry/sexy, does not feel like game is sure whether she's a damn smexxy adult or some naive schoolgirl...So, yeah, game feels like it has an identity crisis, a LOT...I guess it's mostly at the root of it dealing with occult-like/psionics themes, though, to be fair it IS my cup of tea, and Kasane is bae... it might not be everyone's own...While it is NOT perfect, it oozes a lot of soul, is TONS OF FUN, and from my part, if game develops into a whole series in the coming years... I'd buy any potential sequel/sequels, no questions asked...Original Review Start:CHRIST, IT'S GOOD...HANDS DOWN ONE OF GREATEST ARPG/JRPG ANIME GAMES EVER PLAYED...SLOW BURN, BUT ONCE STARTS BURNING...A FRIGGIN' INFERNO...Everything about it oozes class, attention to detail... While action heavy, it could not be more of a thinking man's game, from Everything down to its title...'SCARLET NEXUS'... Instead of some crassly titled 'PSYCHIC GROUP NEXUS' or something... It attracts a niche, kind of fanbase that knows exactly what it wants, so from that aspect, game did dang right attracting an extremely specific psychic minority of people (Which am one, myself)... Might appear like targeting market 'fail', but the devs got the exact market they aimed for, not b*tches, so from that aspect, MORE POWER TO THEM, and the game got the devs exactly what they wanted from fans... Mostly overwhelming support... One small note though, if you plan to eventually get it:Do NOT buy it, if you do not have at least a minor interest in psionics, psychic abilities (both latent & active), clairvoyance, or at the very least 'The Occult'... If not you'd underappreciate it extremely, like most reviewers that panned it.If you are interested in the above, at least remotely, you'll forgive its mostly nagging, but somewhat unnoticeable flaws...If, you remember Wind Waker, and as a PC player, you envied Gamecube owners for having it...You'll be glad to know the game very much cell-shaded in style, in all except dialogue/cutscene screens.Though, cutscenes are pretty much mostly same in graphical style/quality to in-game graphics (They pretty much use those), hard to explain, but they're a lil less cell-shaded-like...Again, though, some characters are less cell-shaded in style in dialogue/cutscene screens, a bit odd to explain, but you can pretty much notice the difference, some characters are more 'naturally anime-like'.9.4/10*EXTREMELY RECOMMENDED!!!*

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic fast-paced JRPG with the heart in the right place. Scarlet Nexus tells the story of Yuito and Kasane, two young fighters with special powers, that slowly uncover a sinister plot in their fight against the otherworldy "Others".The game mostly centers around its combat. It starts slowly, with your usual weapon attacks and combos, but the more you play the game and form bonds with other characters in your group, the more it opens up. Soon they will be able to block damage for you, perform special attacks in certain combat situations and even lend you their powers over a system called "SAS". This system is the main drive of combat as you use it to borrow someone else's power, perform special combo visions and turn the fight in your favour.Fighting in Scarlet Nexus is pretty damn fun and even on Hard it always felt like a fair challenge. You can play through the game with both Yuito and Kasane, though I am warning you: to get specific achievements and play the game the "intended" way, you have to start the new character on the same savefile that you finished the old one on. Otherwise, the game will not recognize prior accomplishments and certain achievements won't be triggered. I found this out 17 hours into said new savefile. Sad face and it is not very well communicated.Still, I liked Scarlet Nexus so much that I will surely return to it at some point to play through the game a third time after my (almost) two times (EDIT: Did that recently and finally completed the game fully!) Fighting feels great, the voice actors do a good job, the story is interesting, the graphics are appealing and the music is funky. It's an all around fun JRPG that will keep you occupied for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely spectacular. The combat is rather simple execution wise but once you get used to the button presses needed to activate skills the system completely explodes and you're free to craft together some weirdo 90 hit pull-push parallel parking combo that sets the enemy on fire and then you rip their head off. Also I found that the game does a fantastic job of giving you enough time experimenting with abilities and such before easing you into the next mechanic (the beginning of the game can be a bit rough for some because the tutorial is mainly just walls of text that get tucked nicely into some random list of 900 other tips for you to reference later.)The gifting and character relationship systems are a nice touch too and connect the gameplay to the character stories directly. It's not very hard to find or make the right gifts for any of the characters and the reward for doing so is expanded abilities and nice QOL bonuses for combat.And as someone who usually isn't attracted to games because of the story I found the story for this game to be extremely well written. The story and characters are interesting and the time that the game gives you to build the protagonists' relationships is a great choice. I'd bet fans of RPGs or Hack and Slash titles like Devil May Cry can dig into this and have a great time just like I did. Strong recommend from me. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A case of being good, but not excellent. I'm 5 levels from having all achievements and overall, the game does a lot well, but doesn't leave a lasting impression. The primary weakness is that it's a game which is an odd amalgamation of other games, while merely sampling what makes these games good instead of getting the intricacies that made those games good. Many 'pro' reviewers (as we know are generally trash) stated it had a Persona like bond system, it doesn't. It merely has gift giving and character skits. Then there is the claim it is similar DMC... I guess every action game gets compared to it or Zelda. The battle system borrows heavily from Ni No Kuni 2. They've very similar with some slight differences.The good but forgettable:The music to the game is mostly well done. The character development was handled decently. Despite being a hallway simulator, the maps and environments were serviceable. The good:I wouldn't say I'm an anime fan, but the story was handled well. Play Kasane first. (Most of the people complaining the story made no sense likely played Yuito first. His story has literal gaps... by design.) Between the two perspective you get a really nice story about time travel and brain eating monsters. The story isn't great, by any means, but it's better than what I've seen in the past couple of years.The really bad:The lack of variety. There's not much variety in gameplay. Sure you have multiple ways to take on battles, but it's not that much different. Even between Kasane and Yuito you'll find yourself taking on more difficult or annoying enemies with the same tactics. There's under 20 enemy types, which is my largest gripe.Largely it's a 7/10 game that came during a jrpg drought.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really rare that a game gets a hold on me not with gameplay or story but its looks. I really enjoy this game's aestetics. Soundtrack is also one of the most varied collections of audio work I've seen, with it switching between classical, electronic, full on dubstep and rock/metal on a whim.This is not to say that gameplay or story are bad, quite the opposite.Gameplay is quite fast-paced, and becomes almost tactical by the end when you need to juggle and combine 8 different effects of your powers during combat (it's quite intuitive and fun, with game ramping up amount of things you have access to quite gradually). Gameplay also has minor differences between characters, even upgrade-wise, with Kasane having much better air play with double air-dash, while Yuito has a much better charge attack, for example. Story - I have a minor issue with how it is parallel between protagonists up to a point, and after merging the parties everything from other campaign essentially gets spoiled to you. Yuito's story relies more on not knowing what's going on, but his story premise is weaker overall. Also I feel like his story does not set up the endgame as good as Kasane's. I would say that if you want your first runthrough to be the best it can be, pick Kasane (unless you don't like her as a character), but there is value in playing Yuito first (also he has better DLC episodes imho). Structure-wise story really reminds me of Persona games, with it having plot-heavy segments called Phases and spending time with your friend and side-questing in Standby's. I really enjoyed this structure, as it really balances story's more dark tone with moments where characters can be just simple humans with simple everyday activities.All right, I kinda went all over the place, but in general I REALLY liked the game. Every aspect of it was enjoyable. Arashi is best girl, Kagero is best boy. Have fun playing!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through one of the storylines, here is my review:The game takes about 20-25 hours to beat(for one storyline), if you watch the cutscenes and do some side content, which is pretty normal for a storybased game with not too much exploration.The story is actually pretty well written, even though they got some rather clichéd lines in the dialogue and some twists seem a bit old-fashioned, i still enjoyed it. I wont go into detail, since no-one appreciates spoilers.The gameplay itself feels very nice, i've seen people complaining about the Lock-on not working, but it does, it just focuses your camera on the enemy so all you gotta do is move towards the enemy(skills go towards the locked target aswell) , this also gives you the freedom to attack enemies nearby without having to swap targets every time, which is a good point in my opinion.The skill variety and usability of almost all skills is very great, there is only one skill i barely ever used during combat (SAS skills that is) it feels fluid and combining the skills (once you unlocked the ability to use multiple at once) is great. I'm just a bit sad that there is so little monster variety.The Skilltree mainly provides passive boosts to your character like more plugins, longer combos, slightly boosted damage, using multiple SAS at once, and dodging to get back on your feet after getting knocked down (otherwise you just lie on the ground for 3 seconds) and many more.There are about 10-ish(cant check the exact number right now) different monsters with multiple variations each, which have different weaknesses and weakpoints, they also posess different skills and gimmicks which require the use of different SAS abilities to effectively fight them.There arent alot of bosses, but atleast they dont get reused and as far as i could see each storyline has different bosses.I died 3 times (for some reason i didnt die on my first try at the last boss but failed pretty hard on my second when i was 10 lvls higher) So i'd recommend a higher difficulty than normal for anyone that wants a challengeThe AI is pretty bad tho (but they arent there to do the work for you anyways, with the SAS you dont really need them anyways)There is also Character progression, which unlocks more passive boosts to the Character you bonded with, which are super helpful (might make endgame a bit too easy if you go for all characters)The Graphics are fine, nothing astonishing and after turning off TXAA, the afterimages were gone aswell. The only downside is that the holograms look pretty bad and they are everywhere in the hub areas. The skills look nice, the Style for  the cutscenes was actually pretty good after getting used to it, since it allows you to skip dialogue in most cutscenes if you are done reading it. The proper Cutscenes are usually pretty well done and i love that the Visual equipment gets shown at all times and even on the loading screens. Customization is much appreciated, since you cant actually create your own Character, so having a ton of different Accessories and atleast 1 unlockable outfit(which is just a white recolor of the base one) for each character is pretty niceThe music is fine as it is, doesnt distract and fulfills its purpose of creating the right mood most of the time.I didnt pay too much attention to it tbh, but i listened to the soundtrack and i quite enjoyed it.Thats all for my review, the game is worth to check out if you want to experience a full on Story with some DMC style combat that has a twist (i guess).

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Great ARPG with interesting characters and fairly deep combat mechanics. The story has potential but the delivery is somewhat lacking.Scarlet Nexus is a beautiful anime inspired Action JRPG. The immersive brain punk world keeps pulling me back in. Every interaction, every enemy, every object, every piece of architecture has me wondering about the rich history and background that sets the stage for the main story line. Sadly that's never fully explored beyond a handful of anecdotes and a brief explanation of the events leading up to the game. The combat is fluid, but challenging (played on hard) and the mechanics are deep enough to have kept me interested for the last 30 hours. The interaction between basic combat and psionic powers make pulling off combos extremely satisfying. I definitely recommend this to anyone who is a fan of flashy finishing moves and responsive combat. The combat is definitely the main draw here and the main reason why I kept playing despite the story coming to a lull at times.Characters grow throughout the story and as you develop your bonds with them. This also leads to new abilities and passive bonuses. If you've played Persona, its something like that but with less investment in social events. Kasane and Yuito (the two playable characters) are different enough to make things interesting but ultimately they're your typical save-the-world type characters. There's definitely growth but the characters themselves are pretty straight-forward. What you see is what you get and there really ins't any surprises.The story feels somewhat lacking, which may be because its delivered as a series of stills with voice overs. There's potential but the pacing also leaves something to be desired with some phases feeling like a drag and others feeling like too much is happening at once. It also doesn't take the time to build an attachment to the characters themselves so major events which should be emotional end up feeling a little underwhelming. I'd still recommend this to anyone who enjoys ARPGs. The moment-to-moment gameplay is outstanding, just don't expect too much from the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a great game that is definitely worth its price.  not a lot of themThe game is a straightforward action RPG with a linear main story separated into Phases (Acts), but you can return to any location at any time (unless it's temporarely blocked by the story developments). One full playthrough took me about 50+ hours without doing any side quests.You can also decorate your hideout through giving and receiving gifts, each one out of 100+ shows up visually inside your home, so it goes from a barren sterile apartment to being absolutely packed with knickknacks, personal belongings, food and other stuff.Also, DLC Bond Episodes are astoundingly good and will give you tons of warm feelings if you've grown attached to the characters even a little. Each one (10 per DLC) also gives you 4 neat surprises after the end, plus unlocks a new stylish power. Also DLC reward you with a very good looking costume and weapon for each of your 10 characters. So I'd say they are worth the price, especially compared to what *some* games get you for the same price.All in all, it's a very solid game made by people that care, and it has quickly become one of  most favorite games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a fast paced, Anime style Action RPG. It should be noted there is an Anime series of the same name that expands the story as well. The game is set in a futuristic "Brain Punk" world, invaded by bizarre creatures called Others. The combat is where this game shines, as you fight with traditional weapons, enhanced with various telekinetic and elemental powers. Combat isn't overly complicated, but mastering the flow of using different abilities is key, and where the game gets good! You have 2 different characters to play from the start, each with unique style, abilities, and story! Doing melee sword attacks, while following up with smashing your enemies with telekinetically thrown objects, all while setting foes ablaze with flame enhanced attack is just some of what you'll experience! You can further expand your abilities with the skill tree, opening up new possibilities!Only downsides I encountered really, were the story presentation and the voice acting. You do have a choice in spoken language, so you don't have to endure the questionable English voices. They aren't the worst, but I was immediately turned off in the opening cutscenes. The cutscenes themselves was my other issue. They are presented in panels instead of animation (which could be to not take away from the Anime), which could have brought the experience of the game as a whole to another level, If you're on this page, reading this review, you should just go ahead and get this game now!

_childDocuments_.review: This game's combat is pretty good, especially when you abuse Tsugumi's SAS. The best difficulty is Very Hard, and the worst difficulty is also Very Hard. Boss fights against humans: 10/10, Boss fights against others: 4/10. Brain field is kinda boring to use, especially when you get full damage reduction, unless it is against Gunkins, in which case spam it as much as possible to speedrun through that slug of a fight. Luka's ability is mostly useless, and is only useful to run away during brain field or against certain boss attacks, so don't feel so bad about not leveling up his bond, he's already used to the lack of social interactions thanks to his brother. Most of the bond episodes are pretty cute, though some are boring, which brings me to cutscenes. There are over 10 hours of cutscenes in the game, and yet it still has a better game to cutscene ratio than GOW, or any 1st party playstation "cinematic" game. So I hope you like this game's story, speaking of which, it is completely nonsensical, deranged, and has little to no coherency, much like this review. While objectively this game's story isn't very good it is still plenty entertaining, especially when the game is having an emotional scene and the characters all have cat ears, tails, and paws. Overall this game is 8/10, don't buy it full price, buy at discount or with a cdkey.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried both Kasane (ranged, shuriken) and Yuito (melee, sword) into about 3 hours of the story, and I have to admit I am really enjoying the game. The combat is crisp and slightly more difficult than most 'lock on' systems because it is still easy to miss with attacks. The player still has to target manually with weapon attacks, the lock on is for psychokinetic attacks. Team members can share their own power through the game's SAS system, which opens up a strategic battle dimension as the power complements the player, i.e. a monster that is wet can be stunned by using a team member's electrokinesis power. These function similarly to Code Vein's communal gifts. Knowing when to use these is a great benefit. Combos are important, and refilling the PK with weapon attacks makes combos crucial to battle.I've seen a fair few complaints about the story and character development. The game uses both standard cinematics mixed with a visual novel's panels. This is not to cheap out on the story, in my opinion. You will enjoy this method if you like visual novel storytelling, complete with humorous closeups of jealous anime girls and boys! The characters are pretty decent, too. I wouldn't say they are earth shattering, but in the first few hours you'll meet overprotective sisters, naive scions of powerful families, skirt chasers, bigots, and however you might classify Arashi. Characters will communicate with each other using "Brain Talk" which is like an IM in your head. While the idea of responding is neat, it doesn't really add too much and at times it gets confusing as the characters will brain talk despite being 5 feet apart. Add onto that telepathic characters and the computer system, and it gets weird when characters talk to you as if they hear the other conversation. In other words, it's like talking out loud on your cell phone to your spouse about your child and the child will respond on your laptop to what you're saying. The story itself is serviceable, but not overly unique. However, the deuteragonist's (depending on which character you play) story and the player's is intertwined, yet not the same. Gaps in one character's knowledge of events can be filled in with the other character. There is absolutely a reason to play both characters.The RPG elements are light, and half the options are just adjustments to existing abilities like +5% attack, double jump, opening equipment slots. A few are more interesting, especially the ability to use multiple SAS abilities simultaneously. There are also some aesthetic options, if you like your anime girls with bunny ears, etc. I have yet to experience any game breaking bugs or crashes, though I have had a few minor glitches take place.I would recommend Scarlet Nexus if you enjoyed Code Vein or Godeater.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy'd this game. You can choose the difficulty from very easy to very hard. I chose very hard, It makes it very challenging as you can die in two hits but it's more satisfying when you win. The DLC EX boss is probably one of the hardest boss I've ever fought (even more so than dark souls) and near impossible without a specific set up.The game play is great.  The fighting is very smooth and satisfying. Some people may have a problem with not being able to cancel out of attack animations or enemies not getting stunned on hit, but I do not think this is a bad thing.  In fact, it might make the game play better as you can't just mash buttons to victory.  But, the game play itself is actually short, half the time will be spent watching cut scenes and bond episodes.  Personally, I don't mind because I enjoy'd the story and the characters are great.  But there are bonus DLC challenges that does extend the game.I recommend buying the game with DLC because it adds extra content that "completes" the game, especially if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: -Story is filled with generic anime tropes. The cringey bad ones, not the ridiculous cool ones. -Characters are generic anime archetypes with very little development.-Combat seems like it should be fast paced but in actuality the controls are very slow, clunky, and unfun to play. -There is very little character customization and variation. You can only play as the main characters.-You have a skill tree that unlocks a bunch of moves such as double jump, more combos, and counter attacks that feels like they should just be part of your base kit. Even with all your moves unlocked, combat still feels clunky.-The teammate ai are very passive(even on aggressive mode) and useless because you don't even need corresponding ally in party to use their support skills. At most they'll act as distractions and toss you some healing items occasionally.-Very repetitive and spongy enemies with very repetitive map designs.-Bad camera and lock on angles. Lots of attack distancing issues that the game shoves at you automatically, not by your choice.-Visually the game is very stylish and flashy.-Some good music.I bought it hoping it would be fun like God Eater or Code Vein quality, but it was pretty disappointing. Put a bunch of hours into the game because I bought it at full price, but I don't have any motivation to finish it. Only buy during big sales.

_childDocuments_.review: Kasane is definitely on the Autism spectrum.They re-use the maps way too much.  I don't mean "you can go back to the map for side quests", I mean like they will have 12 main quests in a row that only use 3 maps between them.All the cutscenes have a really weird thing where they render the entire 3D scene, but then only show a single "frame" of it with the character jaws going up and down.  It feels very weird, because it's basically the indie "storyboarding" cutscene hack to save budget... but using 3D so not actually saving any budget?This is not like a Bioware RPG where you get meaningless choices during dialog.  The character designs are fixed, and the story is fixed, and your only real story choice is "watch 'character development' cutscene?" (in return for a stat boost).There are only two combat styles, each one tied to a specific player character.  Try the demo to see if you will hate it too much!  Playing the demo also gives you a couple of cosmetics.The crafting and cosmetic menus are badly organized.  There's like 800 elements and you can't even go up/down by 1 page at a time, so scrolling through them takes ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ages.You can put new hairbands and earrings on all ~10 teammates, but it doesn't remove their default accessories.  So it looks kind of stupid.For each character you can choose between 2-4 different outfits, each with ~4 different texture/color/pallette swaps.  They  look like someone feel through an Adidas factory.   expect to build a gothic lolita or OL outfit.The inari (fox demon) accessories look pretty cute, but there's no "auto-remove helmet during cutscenes", so if you equip them, you won't see character expression during cutscenes.It's also a bit frustrating that you can only change outfits of people currently in your team, and people drop in-and-out of your team quite often in Act 1.  So if you decide "OK everyone is in blue outfits now" -- TOO BAD that guy you saw 4 main quests ago is still going to be in the red outfit and look dumb in the cutscene.
