_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review after a 7hr session.OK there's a lot to cover but ill keep it brief.Scarlet Nexus takes place in a tech heavy world where some people posses Psychic ability's.The story is interesting with two main characters who share many moments with each other but also have their own independent story's you must play both to fully understand the story.this is unique and great for world building but makes the story so much more confusing until you play both.the combat feel incredible once you get the hang of it but still feels unbalanced.you either don't ever need to worry about healing or are screwed constantly.it feels forced in a way like a mix between a tales of button mash hack and slash and a hardcore boss battler where every hit counts and timing is key but its SO inconsistent.the levels are short and story dump just to stop all pacing for a "break period" where you can build relationships with the NPCs.it breaks the flow one moment people are dying the next you retreat to "rest" just to have a date like moment or slice of life scene. how can you go from OMG MY BEST FRIEND DIED to hey help me win an eating contest while we talk about out feelings.the game tries to combine to many things and while i like the bond system i feel the game would be better without it and just keeping a heavy story line and great game-play.limited commands for your team often mean just not caring about there stats and just using them as bait or for revives.they usually get themselves killed so fast anyways.almost no progression weapon wise but i am only 7 hrs in and did get strong DlC weapons but they still feel weak.Auto tracking on incoming attacks makes them feel impossible to dodge unless playing very slowly with the dash drawing out fights due to low damage output.All in all if you are interested in the story check it out on sale as much as i can complain its still decently fun but not worth any high praise.nothing stands out to me its just another game if you want play it and enjoy whats here but don't expect anything incredible.if you're bored sure pick it up otherwise i can name many other similar games that are more fun to play and have equal if not better story NOT TO MENTION BETTER PACING OF SAID STORY they flesh out every character so well just for them all to seem inhuman and incapable of emotions death doesn't phase anyone like at all.not even for any good reason besides "well this happens in the line of work oh well".these are more notes then a review still i hope it helps someone not get baited by the few good things shown and the promise of a "Must see story and world" they combined to many ideas and it ruins the rest of them in a game like this i could do with more story and less useless idle chatter or quests that break pacing also WHY SO MANY BRAIN MESSAGES ALL THE TIME WHEN THE PERSON IS RIGHT BESIDE YOU. LAST MAJOR COMMENT MUST READ.I know its because my connection is bad but if your Controller disconnects for any reason (mine being a bad cable) the game does not auto pause you will stand there like an idiot and just get dead. also i know what you are thinking "Just play on Keyboard" but trust me for the sick combos and stun locks you can get id HIGHLY recommend a controller as it just feels more natural.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but could not bring myself to do so. The combat is extremely repetitive and most boss fights later in the game turn into spam healing and psychokinesis until the boss dies. The combat system is supposed to be deep, with your character being able to wield their weapon, their own individual psychokinesis attacks, and 2 different sets of your allies' abilities all at once, but it fails because these systems do not flow well together, breaking up the fluidity of the fighting and making it hard to utilise all your skills effectively. The story is a stereotypical Shōnen story that is very predictable and the characters feel bland and uninspired. It reminds me a lot of the problem Biomutant had where it has a good concept but poor execution. What also sucks about it is in the last quarter of the game, there is a massive difficulty spike where your enemies become very overpowered and your character's abilities and damage output do not scale accordingly to match the difficulty spike. This always leaves you at a big disadvantage when fighting groups of enemies and an even bigger disadvantage when you fight bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, and to be honest, there are some parts it does right. The art direction is fairly solid, the soundtrack is interesting and the fundamentals of its combat are sharp. However, its bogged down by an incredibly shallow story, relatively bland and predictable character archetypes and development arcs, limited enemy variety, and a lack of more in-depth combat in the late game made playing this game a chore, especially in the later half. The unsatisfying ending also leaves a bad taste in your mouth. I feel as though this game could have been so much more if the publishers had let the developers play around with the combat mechanics a bit more. Playing the game makes you feel like a badass, but after the same crunchy combat animation plays for the 20th time, it gets stale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite release of the year. The story has a couple areas that feel a little off, but they're minor and I understand the reasoning for the issues I have. Regardless of those tho it remains very engaging throughout and even can pull at the emotion strings. The characters and their interactions are fantastic and I loved getting to know each of them. Combat is an absolute blast, with a good amount of depth. There's lots of synergy between abilities and the game will continue to introduce interesting mechanics even when nearing the end of the game. Environments are pretty and have lots of useful tools for combat. You'll also have reasons to return to some of the areas after obtaining tools you need to get to blocked off rooms, etc. Enemies also have a good amount of variety, all having their own strengths and weaknesses and interesting mechanics. This game has kept me wanting to return to it for it's satisfying gameplay loop and interesting story. You should probably give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good action RPG with some unique elements.  5 different difficulty settings that can be changed at any time.  A light equipment and progression system helps to keep you engaged and feeling stronger when leveling up.  As well as a wacky but interesting story make this a game that's at least worth playing if not beating at least once.  There are two characters with varying stories, so you can beat it twice with two different POV.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet nexus was one of the few games that I’ve actually followed from when it was announced. In which I had built up quite the excitement for the eventual release. Upon booting the game up for the first time I played for a straight 6 hours and I can tell you that Bandai Namco have done an amazing job with Scarlet nexus.So, what makes Scarlet nexus so amazing? what makes it unique and why should you buy it. I can break this down into two major aspects of the game. The visuals and the combat system.First the visuals. Scarlet nexus on the surface looks very similar to code vein. But there are many ways in which Scarlet nexus differs. It takes the code vein look and propels it into the future with holograms blocking you from walking into the road, and more amazon delivery drones then you know what to do with. I myself want to compare the main city in the game to the one you see in cyberpunk 2077. Visually it’s basically that but in anime form. I consider myself a perfectionist so when I play games, I am always looking at those fine details. That being whether the legs and feet conform to walking up a set of stairs (which they don’t) or how the light reflects of surfaces. Scarlet nexus uses an underrated colour combination that being purple and red. The red is often used as an accent for characters or the environment while purple is used in the combat and abilities. It adds some well needed separation as games like code vein I feel everything blends together.Moving onto the cut scenes. This is where scarlet nexus really begins to become unique. It has some of the most fluid and beautiful cut scenes I’ve seen in a game for a long time. The cut scenes that are animated are stunning they make you feel immersed in the gameplay, but they are not what provide the uniqueness as lots of games have stunning animated cut scenes. The “cut scenes” I’m on about are usually where the characters are seen standing facing each other like they’re having a staring contest. There are no emotion just blank faces. This really breaks the immersion in most games for me. But in scarlet nexus they are made into little 2.0 visuals novels. They keep me immersed as each character is showing their emotions. It carries the tension from gameplay.Finally, the part that makes Scarlet nexus unique is the combat system. The way that Bandai Namco have done a psychic based combat system is amazing. The controls are a little weird to begin with as pressing X and A at the same time on a controller feels odd. (If you not playing with a controller which I highly advise, good luck). The game does a great job at making you feel powerful but not at the level as that you’re a god conquering the galaxy. Scarlet nexus also places a huge incentive on chain attacks or combos, this can be started from you giving the enemy a good slap or throwing a bus at the them. You are basically a jedi with the power of the force. Without spoiling the beginning to much you can then borrow your teammates abilities and use them in combination with your own. Overall, the different attacks that you can do with the different psychic abilities visually look amazing and feel amazing.Inconclusion Scarlet nexus is beginning to become my favourite game that has come out of 2021. I highly suggest anyone who loves anime style games like code vein or the SAO series to give this game a try. You will not be disappointed. Hopefully. For those of you who are concerned if you can run this game. I am currently playing on a GTX 1650, i5 9300h, 32GB ram and running smoothly on highest settings.Thanks for reading my review of scarlet nexus and I hope you enjoyed it as much as I enjoyed writing it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst gaming experiences I've ever had in recent memory, and a testament to how a lone, single factor can ruin the whole product.For starters, the main gameplay is actually pretty decent, with a pretty fun combat system. This is unfortunately marred by the game's incredibly dull and barebones side quest and equipment system, which have no reason to exists in its current state. There's also a noticeable lack in enemy variety, so combat can get a little tedious later on, especially since there's a lack in gameplay variation.But the worst offenders that tainted my entire experience is the game's absolutely horrendous story and it's piss poor execution and pacing. Calling the writing tone-deaf is an absolute understatement, and completely ruins any level of fun I might have. Plotlines are constantly introduced and casted aside at a drop of a hat, without any regard for tone and timing.Characters that are painfully generic yet tolerable end up being detestable and just obnoxious because of the way the narrative is handled, and I end up having nothing but disdain even for my player character.I started this game intending to finish both playthroughs for the 2 protagonists - Yuito and Kasane, but now I couldn't even bring myself to finish my first playthrough. That's how much I hate the writing of this game.Maybe there's still something for people who can enjoy a game for just it's gameplay without caring about the story and whatnot, but if a dog leave a steaming pile of ♥♥♥♥ on my rice bowl, I would throw the whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bowl away.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: The story is...bare bones to say the least. Hey, there's a rebellion, and that's about as much build up as the game gave it too. Suddenly half the squad just wants to kill you for reasons.The combat itself is ok. It's meant to be sort of a spectacle fighter, but it just isn't there. The perfect dodge is also a right pain in the rump since it almost seems like there aren't iframes unless you actually get the perfect dodge so you can "dodge" at what should be the right time and still tank a brick to the face. This is especially annoying on the Kasane fights, or really any of the ones where the random team wants to kill you because, "We can't talk about it, we have to fight."There's also the joy of the crafting system where you have to grind for items in different fights to slowly upgrade weapons or grind your squad's relationship level.Overall, its a pretty generic anime experience. Buy it at a steep discount or just watch a let's play.

_childDocuments_.review: Assume the role of Yuito Sumeragi, a new recruit to the OSF aiming to become an elite psionic like the one who saved him as a child. Armed with a talent in psycho-kinesis, explore the futuristic city of New Himuka and uncover the mysteries of a Brain Punk future caught between technology and psychic abilities in SCARLET NEXUS. Using psycho-kinetic abilities, the world around you becomes your greatest weapon. Lift, break and throw pieces of your environment to build your attack combos and lay waste to your enemies. Deranged mutants that descended from the sky, highly resistant to conventional attack methods and defenses. Tormented by the constant pain of their mutation, they seek brains of living organisms to calm their madness. Explore and protect a futuristic Japanese landscape that combines inspirations from classic anime and western science fiction. Dive into a complex story of bonds, courage and heroism crafted by minds behind the iconic Tales of Vesperia.

name: ITTA
detailed_description: ITTA is a bullet-hell adventure set in a world filled with monstrous bosses. When Itta wakes up and finds herself surrounded by her dead family, her only guide is a strange spirit that takes the form of the family cat who gifts her a glowing revolver for protection. As Itta, players must seek out the powerful beings locked away beneath this seemingly peaceful world and go toe-to-toe against them in harrowing battles. From hulking ancient golems to toothy horrors, Itta’s journey will push both you and her past their limits. Luckily, you can change up your combat style by finding weapons with unique attack styles, and if the going gets too tough, toggle on invincibility or player damage multipliers at any time. ITTA is a game inspired by themes of personal struggle. If there is light, there must be darkness. The important thing is to keep going… no matter what you endure along the way. Features Topple 18 deadly bosses in tight, twin-stick, bullet-hell combat Wield an arsenal of power spirit weapons to fight in new ways Unlock the mystery of a bizarre, crumbling world and its cryptic inhabitants Explore a beautiful, pixel-art world backed by a haunting and eclectic musical score. Never hit a wall; freely toggle damage multipliers or invincibility Glass Revolver is the studio of developer, Jacob Williams. Inspired by everything from manga to Italian gardens, His aim is to deliver eclectic games that are uncompromising in their bizarre vision. Kyle Lisenby is a self taught multi-instrumentalist and composer who cut his teeth in post-rock bands Red Cloud at Sundown and Siren. He has been releasing compositions under the name Invisible Monsters since 2007 and feels most at home in uncharted waters.

short_description: Test your limits in ITTA, a bullet-hell, boss-rush style adventure. Armed with her father’s revolver and guided by a strange ghostly cat, a displaced girl must battle her way through impossible trials in search of answers… and peace.

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a twin-stick, boss-rush style game with a total of eighteen bosses to fight against. The first four bosses that I fought weren't so hard and I thought to myself that the game would be a cakewalk, but I spoke too soon. The next bosses were far more difficult and the game just does not hold back anymore, as the arena just literally becomes "bullet-hell".✔️ Beautiful pixel graphic game✔️ Great and intense boss fights✔️ Exploration with hidden secrets✔️ Combat feels satisfying with a good variety of weapons to use✔️ Captivating story with interesting side-characters✔️ This game is quite literally "bullet-hell"❌ Annoying bugs❌ Soundtrack is a mixed bagYou play as a girl named Itta, and the first thing you see when you wake up is your father, brother and family cat lying on the ground dead. A few moments later a spirit appears, taking the form of your cat, and it will be your guide throughout the game to find your lost mother. This spirit gives you a glowing revolver as your starting weapon and your journey begins. The locations are vast and beautiful to look at due to the gorgeous pixel-art style, from waterfalls to lights rays in caves. In this world, there are hidden secrets and interesting characters that tell more about the lore of this world and its bosses. Another great detail is that there are a few time when you die you will get a short cutscene which tells you more about Itta and her inner thoughts. The story is subtle and very well done, and it will keep you engaged until the end.This game is a mix of  and ; it is a two stick shooter game and your only enemies are the bosses. You have a mix of weapons with infinite ammo that range from a revolver to heavy machine gun. You can also dodge to avoid projectiles or when you are in a tight situation. You also have a health bar, which is upgradeable when you progress through the game. At some point in the game during exploration, you will find a power up which makes you invincible and more powerful (higher damage) for a short period of time, so I recommend finding that power up as soon as possible. Overall, the combat feels smooth and the weapons are satisfying to use. It is also good to note that you can play this game with a PS4 controller, but I recommend keyboard and mouse for better aim and accuracy.The bosses in this game are unique from one another and tough to say the least, as they have their own arena and use different styles of combat, from sword wielding knight to projectile-spitting statue head. There are no checkpoints or a specific area to spawn in everytime you die from a boss, as one of the interesting features about this game is when you die you respawn right next to the boss arena that you died in. I have encountered a few annoying bugs during my playthrough;  I get randomly damaged out of nowhere during a boss fight, which makes the fights frustrating since this game depends on precision and well timed hits and dodges. Also there are a few time where you don't get a visual indicator when you get hit. At certain times during boss fights the camera would move away from the player. When you get hit, the game would make you invincible for a few second until you find your bearings, but it doesn't always work as intended and you would get hit several times in less than a second, which makes the fight more infuriating. Another bug I encountered was that whenever I try to enter a boss arena I would end up going back outside for some reason, so I have to enter the arena again. Hopefully a patch would be released soon, that will fix the bugs this game has.The soundtrack is somewhat of a mixed bag; the music outside of boss fights is just relaxing, with nature sounds that makes you feel like walking in the forest, while some of the boss fights songs are just bombastic and all over the place, they were annoying at times and the contrast was very disorienting.If I want one improvement, aside from fixing the bugs and better boss fight music, it would be adding weapon shortcuts instead of cycling through the weapons mid battle. ITTA is a great game with beautiful pixel art style, captivating story and interesting bosses that would give you huge adrenaline rush.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful the controls are tight. Switching guns is a little very little hassle but other than that, I enjoy the game. I wish it was more than just a boss rush game, but beyond that, this game is really worth the price. The combat isn't arduous or even painful, the game is fairly balanced and works well with keyboard and mouse. To end on a last and a positive note; nothing feels better than wish listing a game on steam that lives up to expectations. If you like 3rd person shooters like Nuclear Throne and Enter the Gungeon, but you are there just for the epic confrontations like Fury. ITTA is a game worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a fast paced, boss rush style game about a girl trapped in a world she doesn't quite understand.  Personally I'm not a huge fan of bullet hell games, but something about ITTA's approach to the bullet hell style really clicked with me.  There's a multitude of guns, and even though I'm not especially far in my playthrough yet, I'm surprised how many of the guns have utility against specific bosses.  Personally I've found the cannon to be my favorite weapon, but I have no doubt that will change.PROS:-Interesting world-Great pixel art-Tight twin-stick bullet hell combat, guns feel good to shoot, dodge roll is effectiveCONS:  -Difficulty is pretty high (but fair), so come in prepared to rumbleITTA also has a very interesting mood associated with it.  Something about the way the music plays with the lonely, but rich environments makes me feel... something.  It's interesting.Overall this game is solid!  I'd recommend it in a heartbeat, even if you aren't typically a fan of bullet hell games.  UPDATE after completing the game:This game satisfies all the way through.  The difficulty was pretty high, but I honestly came to enjoy and look forward to the challenge.  I had a couple moments where I was one hit away from death and I achieved this absolute laser focus zen state, and I don't get that in very many games.  All I can say is I absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't what I would define as just a game, but rather a form of art. Not only are the VISUALS absolutely outstanding, the MUSIC for every area of the game, every boss, every bit of scenery, it is wonderful and a blessing to listen to time and time again. The MECHANICS are something else as well. Dodgerolls are clean and flawless, providing I-frames in-between rolls for hectic scenarios which there are plenty of.. believe me. Since a lot of these boss fights can have very high bullet density, the variety in DPS and play style that each of the different guns provide is stellar. There is most definitely a difficulty spike, so this isn't a bullet hell to rest easy with unlike others in the genre. Even though I've put nearly 10,000 hours into bullet hell games in general, I've died a few times to some of these bosses not even from the bullet density, but with how agile the bosses are sometimes. ALWAYS gotta be moving around.Bullet Hells are my favorite video game genre, and what this man has done with creating this game, he has created both modern bullet hell as well as a literal form of art. This art isn't just with the visuals, but additionally the story and lore hidden around the animated world.Overall, if you love bullet hell, this game is a perfect mash of leniency with plenty of bullet density to even give the Touhou series a run for its money. If you love art in general, this game does the job at really taking what engine it was built in to its limits. Even after completing the game, I find myself simply strolling, pondering around the world from its peaceful ambiance. That is something special.Thank you, ITTA, for providing us with beauty, bullets, and lots more bullets <3
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, but not good. If you're looking at this, but haven't played hyperlight drifter or titan souls I would give both of those games a try before this one.Game's too short, and there's no replayability like in a more arcadey experience. I would say that about an hour of my three hour playtime was spent hunting for explodable walls and trying to collect cats. Most of the game was trivial, especially after unlocking the . Seems like a lot of work went into making cool bullet hell patterns, but then spamming dodge roll seems to invalidate a lot of it.Hitbox feels really weird. I got hit by stuff I didn't think I'd get hit by, and stuff didn't hit me that really should have. Oh well.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous visuals and beautiful, calming music contrasted by gameplay that isn't afraid to crank the crazy up to 11 at a moments notice. Thus far the bosses do a great job of appearing threatening and frantic while still being fair and approachable fights. Controls are also very tight, with all the essential mechanics of swapping weapons and dodge rolling accessible with only mouse input.This is a carefully crafted game that I'm so glad to finally see get released. Totally recommend for anyone seeking some bombastic gameplay that's accompanied by a stunning atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Great pixel animation and amazing soundtrack. Many will compare ITTA with Titan Souls, but unlike the puzzle-like nature of the bosses in TS, ITTA's bosses are just straight up bullet hell gun-'em-ups; there's also a heck of a lot more lore/plot. The hit boxes are quite forgiving and I beat about a third of the bosses on the first try. For a bullet hell/boss rush game, I'd say this is actually a relatively easy one despite first impressions. There are also accessibility options to turn on invincibility and damage modifiers if you just want to experience the game's story and not hit a wall with the boss fights. A few minor glitches and polish issues (also, why are all the NPCs smiling gleefully while they are telling you really sad tales, especially when they also have sad expressions later on?), but overall, a great run and definitely a recommended experience. Took 3-4 hours to finish for me, a novice at boss rush games.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 3/5Notes: The game has great art, great soundtrack, very interesting world/dialogue/characters, and generally a decent feel to the combat.Unfortunately none of the bosses are really that intereresting to fight. While they all look unique, there are a lot of recycled mechanics and bullet patterns and they are mostly fought in the exact same way. Also after about the half way mark of the game it actually gets much easier because you have so much health you can basically zerg down the bosses without even really caring about dodging most things. Dodge rolling is also a bit too overpowered and spammable with no cooldown. I believe there are 18 bosses in total and I think I only died maybe 8 times total. Almost all of those deaths being within the first 2 hours. I would recommend Hyper Light Drifter and Titan Souls over this game if you haven't played them for a similiar but arguably better overall gameplay experience. And if you are into roguelites you should also check out Enter the Gungeon and Monolith. This was still a fairly enjoyable game I would recommend picking up and trying out at some point though, because while the combat is a bit dissapointing, its still decent, and everything outside of combat is great.If this game had the exact same setting,story, visuals, etc. But with the combat feel and boss mechanics/patterns of Enter the Gungeon it would be a 10/10. Unfortunately almost any boss in enter the gungeon is more interesting and satisfying to fight than any boss in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to titan souls in the sense that the gameplay is just fighting bosses but the boss fights are more focused on being a bullet hell type game than one with unique mechanics for each boss. I'd say half of them play the same and the difficulty can vary. If you like boss fights and have played a lot of them or even played games like Enter the Gungeon or other bullet hell's, you wont have much trouble with this game. especially if you go get all the upgrades which you can find most of them by the halfway point which makes it a breeze at that point.there's a variety of weapons to choose from and all of them seem to have similar dps but there's a few that still shine above the rest so there's no real best weapon, its more personal preference.art style and soundtrack are both great and the visuals are done pretty perfect. Projectiles are bright red, the player is a solid blue and most boss arenas and bosses themselves are usually black and grey so there's no trouble seeing where everything is which a lot of games mess up so i appreciate how little of an eyesore this was. the games also very generous with iframes with the dodge as you can almost spam dodge and not take damage ever.There's no new game plus or hard mode yet which i think the game would benefit from, even just an option that increases boss health by 1.5x maybe right off the bat would help seeing i did a lot of the fights, especially the earlier ones, very quickly and a lot of them on my first attempt.On special i'd say the games worth it, its not to long either, maybe 2-3 hours depending on if you do all bosses or not and then maybe 4-5 hours to get all the achievements if your into that. I also had no issues with bugs, crashes or my fps throughout my time.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW : YESNow that I finished the game, I might point some hitbox issue with one of the world boss who can push you with a bigger hitbox than his actual sprite, cancelling your dodge and making you get hit in the process. Some spawning bugs when you respawn and go into a boss room, sometimes it loads the room twice.Apart from that, the game was fun and the story was pretty cool. I might still have issues with some of the music, but I guess that's part of the universe the devs wanted to create.ITTA is a boss rush bullet hell featuring more than 15 bosses. Every boss has his own patterns and there is a lot of work put into them. The weapons are very well crafted and the gameplay is as smooth as it is in a game like Enter the gungeon.While my old review still applies, the game is pretty good and in all honesty, i recommend it without a doubt. Not perfect, but still a great title ! OLD REVIEW : I still recommend the game but it's kinda a mix bag actually.The aesthestic is cool although a bit classic (kinda reminds me or a mix of Titan Souls and Hyper Light Drifter) but the sprites are pretty well animated.The gameplay is fine and easy to use, although you need to know something : Playing with a gamepad is tiring as hell.I'm always playing bullet hells with my keyboard but since it's not a shmup (more like the gameplay of Gungeon), you need to use your mouse to aim. And after trying out the gameplay, I've found that Keyboard/mouse is the easiest way to beat the game, I found that the dodge gives you enough window to evade most of the bullets without any issue. If you add that to the simplicity of aiming and shooting with the mouse, you'll clear the game without issue.But gameplay is another story, you constantly have your thumb on the right stick and it hurts the hand A LOT.There are some spawning bugs here and there but the game in general is smooth and plays fine.Will probably write a final review when i'll finish this.Finally, the important point, at least to me :The ambient sounds and music are pretty calm and top quality, but the boss music....I don't really know if I like it (because your ears KNOW something is dangerous in the room, it adds some stressful / horrific experiences), or if I dislike, because there is so much going on musically that it loses what makes a good music : melody.I'm sorry if I sound really harsh on this (sorry Mr. dev!) but as cool as ITTA can look, it won't please everyone because of theses points.I'm still enjoying it for the most part.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it; I quite liked it, it's a nice little game with great pixel art.Still, I'm a little disappointed by some things: 1) the length, I really took my time to explore everything, and still, already over. 3 hours (After finishing, I even went through everything again and looked, if I had missed something, but after a while, I lost interest to find the last weapons etc.), this is the length, I expect from a mainstream point and click adventure filled with animations, jokes etc. Here you have a little bit of story and lots of boss fights. I think there could have been much more interactions with different characters at the different locations of the game; a little bit of a wasted opportunity not to think of more dialogue and place two or three npcs more. 2) some of the boss fights feel pretty similiar in many ways. 3) the music really is annoying, in the boss fights, it's not really a soundtrack, i mean it doesn't feel like one, it feels like fighting noise, some kind of effect, without depth; it feels like from a cheaper kind of game, not matching the visual and the music while traveling around.Nonetheless, I suggest, you grab this game, when it's on a sale. If you can't wait, I hope, you like it as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game, but I also recommend getting it on sale. It's a 3-6 hour game, and if you use a guide for just the secret bomb-able walls, you'll be quite close to 3 hrs to 100% a save file. It's a giant killer oops all bossfight bullet hell game, and a well done one, but there are only 15 fights (+ final boss who was easier than some of the others) that take 5 minutes max. No second healthbars or checkpoints or anything. I guess it's a pretty good intro to proper bullet hell games, with simpler controls and bullet types.If you find all the HP upgrades, you will have 12 hit points. I honestly died more in the first half of the game, when I had less health points to spare. The other reason the last area feels "easier" is that the scythe weapon is completely overpowered and will melt boss HP at about twice the speed of other weapons. I love it.  There's also basically no dash cooldown, meaning that you can often completely avoid being hit by dodging constantly. This isn't super useful because if you do that, you don't deal any damage. Fun fact! the game never tells you you can dodge roll (it's right click). There are a couple bugs but the game saves so frequently that it barely matters. One boss had an attack that appeared to ignore invincibility frames, immediatley killing you, and I ran into a couple control / visual bugs as well. Nothing super game breaking, and hitting escape and reloading the file will fix 'em.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and sweet little game. Not overly hard if youre well versed in souls-likes or bullet-hells, but fun to play, with GORGEOUS visuals and esoteric environmental design. I almost wish it were longer considering how little we know about the world despite how interesting it looks, but it taking only a few hours to play while still being a challenge (though maybe a little too easy) was a large part of the charm.If you want a lovely and tough little game you can finish in just 1-2 sittings then I highly recommend it(ta)
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I am partly disabled (damaged cartillage and tendon in my hands/wrists) and not a fan of bullet hell games in particular, but I AM a big fan of ITTA.  The controls are not impossible to master, even with chronic wrist pain, which I really appreciate.  The challenges change in type, which ramps up the complexity rather than simply increasing speed, concentration and damage.  But what I really love about ITTA is the art and style.  I've been fan-following the development based purely on how gorgeous the screenshots and clips have been and how cool the developer is, but now that I've gotten to play I'm also seeing a really intriguing story unfold.  This reminds me of the best game ever made: Super Metroid, in terms of its styling, ambiance, exploration and progression (if not directly the mechanics), with a flavor of Undertale.  So happy to finally get to play!
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: The more of the following questions you answer 'yes' to, the more you will love ITTA: Did you like Titan Souls (TS)? Or wish you had liked TS but couldn't because of one-hit deaths/kills, lack of weapon variety, and having to retread your way to the boss every single time you died? Wish TS had other 'beings' to talk to and text/story/lore to find?  Did you love the beauty and mystery of the environments in TS?  Also, did you love the mysterious/haunting music you heard while exploring, and the intense music during the boss battles? Did you like the shooting, weapon switching and dodge-rolling/dash mechanics in Enter the Gungeon, Nucleaer Throne or Monolith? - - - TL;DR- Feels and looks like Titan Souls (general surreal/haunting vibe, trapped in a mysterious place, defeat 10 bosses to escape). Unlike Titan souls though, you have 2 or more hearts, and you spawn just outside the boss room if you die (no retreading your steps every time!)- Plays like Enter the Gungeon/Nuclear Throne/Monolith (shooting, weapon switching on the fly, dodge rolling, bullet-hell bosses). But is not a rogue-lite.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a great game that mixes exploration with bullet hell boss battles. It has some beautiful pixel art visuals with nice pastel tones that are easy on the eye and has a pretty good soundtrack too. The story is engaging from start to finish and leaves some room for interpretation. It’s a pretty short game, I managed to finish it in 4 hours, but it certainly worth your time. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, love the pixel art graphics. Good gameplay, dodging bullets while shooting (or throwing a scythe) is very fun, bosses are unique and show personality. However, I find this game pretty short, would've been better if there was even more content in it and maybe more backstory on the bosses we know nothing about.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun.But too easy because of the roll : if you spam roll, you are invincible the whole time.Also, it could be interesting for players to put away weapons during fight, to walk faster.Rage power is too stong I think (you already are invincible, and last blast makes too much damages versus bosses, so op)
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a great and short bullet-hell, twin-stick-shooter, boss-"rush" (there is frankly no rush, you fight one after another) game, where you play a hooded girl in some kind of mysterious limbo/purgatory plane.The gameplay mixes the dense tension of super tight boss-fights with some melanchollically relaxing exploration and puzzling. The fights are tough but fair and failing never felt cheap.The design is as bright as it is moody, the pixel-art is top quality, the enemies and NPCs look good.Definetly check this out, if you like the genre in the slightest.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and accessible bullet hell shooter / boss rush game! Tons of weapon variety and lovely pixel-art! Sometimes it feels like there is a bit too much going on and therefore the dodge is a bit too overpowered. By lowering the amount of stuff on the screen you could make the dodging feel more "earned by also nerfing the invisibility frames.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Soundtrack is a bit lacking. Controls are not tight enough for me, aim stick should shoot. Not have another button that you need to press (obviously just my opinion). Heavily story driven with long lows outside of the boss fights. In boss fights/combat, dodge in a circle and hold down the fire button to hit the boss. No weak points, little in the way of mechanics outside bullet hell. Which I do like, Enter the Gungeon, Jamestown, Monolith are all some of my favs. Was really hoping for more. I just can't get into it. I also understand there is a character progression aspect and you gain abilities. However the 3 bosses I killed, during the fight I just found myself not wanting to do it. Not wanting to play, no fun being had. I'd love to play through the game, I wish the combat was more interesting.Don't get me wrong, there's a lot right going on here. The game is beautiful, so far has a cool story, incredibly animated. I like cats, character progression and boss rush. It's just not for me. Honestly this game is my wish for Titan Souls minus the actual combat, which I much more enjoyed in Titan Souls. Oof.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, definitely worth the experience.The level and boss design looks good enough to leave you craving for more map.Music is a very strong plus in this game. Especially one track always gives me that Zelda vibe.My only complaint would be the length of the game.About 1 or two areas more and it'd be perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the game and found myself replaying it over and over again on two accounts kept testing myself to finish the game under 45 mins which I did after my first own speedrun I have so much fun on this game and enjoyed every single boss fight my favorite would have to be with the the dog one thats what I call it he has red swords in his room I really liked that one the most out of them all I know this is like two years later but I had it since the start and hope you make more games in the future this was wonderful the art is very stunning and I thought it was one of the best I have seen I loved seeing everything in this game I found it to be utterly beautiful
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: So to start things off, let's get to the point.I give the game a 9/10.Why? Lets dive down. Gameplay:Of course, the controls are better suited for mouse and keyboard. But I ain't about all that. I love my controller, and this game doesn't fail to deliver. I personally love the control schematic for this game, and it isn't a high learning curve. Get beat down a few times and you will be fine. That being said, you have to aim before you shoot, and depending on the weapon you have (there are a lot of them, you just have to find them) you can fight bosses with difficulty or ease. Sword guy giving you a hard time? It doesn't matter what weapon you have, you just have to get good.Music:What can I say? It hits you in the feel and hypes you up when needed. I give it a solid 8/10, mainly because sometimes its too peaceful, and takes away from the severity of what you're actually doing. But then again, that adds to the scare factor..so 9.2/10.Overall thoughts:It may be short, but you will actually enjoy the game. Steep learning curve but hey, if it was too easy it wouldn't be worth a dime.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: So I saw this game and wishlisted it because it looked interesting. So far, it has surpassed every expectation I have had. The gameplay is smoother, the story more engaging, the dialogue more interesting, the setting more surreal, than I could have possibly imagined. I may have skipped this, too worried that it would be a mediocre experience. I want to scream at my past self for even letting that thought cross my mind. The game is worth every penny of its cost and unless something gamebreaking happens, I will not let up on that view. The developer seems intimately engaged with the game itself and the community. These are all hallmarks of games that I find myself intensely in love with. I see Itta in the same way. A review I saw on the Store Page before delving in myself likened Itta to a work of art, something that transcends the title of 'game' and I cannot help but echo that selfsame sentiment.Itta is worth your money, and worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: The boss fights are amazing.The ray tracing is amazing.The meat and potatoes of this game is rushing bosses, and rushing bosses is what you very well can do. The boss fights have a lot of character in their designs as well as the way they act, each feeling like it tells its own stories without words. The different "flavors" of projectiles is a nice touch. With the attention to detail in the overworld map and bosses you can tell a lot of love went into crafting this game. Each boss feels like it has its own rhythms and patterns, and with a wide array of weapons you really get to tool around with which strategy works best against which boss. What's more they are really difficult which is great! I love a challenge, and if you don't love a challenge you can explore the map and find some hidden items to strengthen yourself for future fights.To be a little nit picky and this is a minor gripe. I felt like there could have been some button press prompts during the opening scenes. Kinda had to click around the keyboard a bit to find the right buttons to interact.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've played through the game and I liked what I played. I also beat all of the content to be found in this game in about 4 hours. The game is beautiful, the visuals border on serene and horror inducing (in a good way) and the design of a majority of the bosses are really good. It plays like Enter the Gungeon and is smooth in control to boot.Your mileage may vary depending on how good you are at bullethells. If you like bullethells and beautiful visuals, get this game. If you're discouraged from playing the game due to its short game length, I suggest waiting for a sale. This game at least deserves your time and attention with how much love the developer has placed into it.This is a labor of love. Treat it as such.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: : Itta is a one of the best bullet hell/boss rush games I've played. It's basically Titan Souls mushed with Enter The Gungeon. If you liked either/both you'll like this.Full Review:: Itta is a boss rush game where you fight cool bosses one after another. It's also a bullet hell, so all bosses basically fill up the screen with bullets of all shapes and sizes. All 18 bosses are interesting with unique designs, and their attacks are varied and fun though there are some similarities. There are lots of weapons you can pick up too, and they vary in range/speed/attack type etc. They're all fun to use, though you may end up just using one or two you're comfortable with. Which is a little disappointing, I would've loved  it if some weapons were better against specific bosses so you'd have to use them all.: the story is quite simple but the world is filled with cool and expressive characters to support it. There are short books that add some lore too. Overall the story could use some more love, but it's still cool and fun enough to hold the game together.: I feel the game is more on the easy side, keeping in mind that I played lots of similar games. The increase of difficulty between bosses is a bit wonky. Some later bosses can be much easier than the first ones, though this may be because you'll pick up some good weapons, add health, etc as you progress. One cool thing is that there's an option to be invincible and/or increase your damage rate, in case you just want to experience the game without any frustration.: your sidekick is a spirit kitty, and all around the world you find statues that let you change how your cat looks, which is quite fun. The music is wonderful. It doesn't particularly standout  among other games', but it's still fun. Lastly, the dev has been quite receptive and positive and was quick to respond and fix any issues. I really appreciate that.: at the time of writing, here are some missing stuff that I hope the dev would add:-More accessibility options: It's nice that the game gives options to reduce difficulty, and it would be nice if we could have more: for example changing the speed, number, and/or size of the bullets-Boss rush mode: after finishing the game, add a mode where you can fight the bosses again with all the weapons/upgrades you acquired. It could be a fight against all of them in one go and/or choosing individually. Perhaps adding some changes or increasing difficulty.-Allow changing your cat's looks on the go.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice little experience overall! I would rate it 7/10+ The art is sweet+ The gameplay is simple yet effective+ The atmosphere is great!- Some bosses pattern are unpredictable and can be a bit frustrating- The weapon balancing- I'm a bit frustrated to have discovered some weapons only after finishing every boss of the game, so i could not even try them! ^^Good job anyway!
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is a ton of fun. Titan Souls mixed with enter the gungeon style bullet hell gameplay. If you want your twitch skills tested, give it a shot. That first major boss's teleport is some ol doodoo tho. Also, no bomb only run possibility makes me so sad.*Edit, King boss works like it should now! Also i've actually beaten it so i can talk about the whole game. This game was exactly what I wanted.  It takes from other games and in doing so makes something wholly unique. The story was beautiful and engaging even if it was brief. I can't wait to see this game busted open with speed runs.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA has some of the most brilliant environments I've ever seen in an indie game, especially in terms of pixel art. The animations are brilliant, and Itta feels perfectly responsive to your inputs. I'm not a massive fan of difficulty in games, so I used the accessibility settings here and there. Even still, I want to get better at this style of gameplay. Congratulations Jacob on this wonderful game. I love spending time in the gardens.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a true gem and I think every type of player can find enjoyment in this game! If you like bullet-hell you have an incredible array of challenging bosses to take on. If you are more in it for the story, you have an incredible world to explore.With the accessibility options, Itta can be enjoyed in the hands of any level of player in the way they most enjoy. I loved the lore and mythology interwoven into the world - it was a very unique experience that I will definitely be going back to again and again. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: A game reminiscent of Titan Souls because of it's chilled exploration, (better than Titan Souls), suited to a cute stylish graphic with relaxing colours, matched to challenging boss fights in bullet hell style.The story is CRUEL...the poor Itta finds herself into a sort of world in between in need to find a way back. Deaths are a constant of the story, there's a sort of "mourning" atmosphere in all the game.However there's is the "accessibility" option to turn on invincibility or 2x damage, so you won't struggle too much on the fights if you really want to follow the story till the end....I like those type of games but personally i'm doing it at 2x multiplied damage to suite my gameplay, as i'm enjoing it so far...I don't wish to replay it too many times, i'd just like to consume this charming product till the end...at the moment i killed 9 bosses approximately so i guess i'm at half way...Reccomended.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this game is fantastic!!! The game looks beautiful and the game characters look cool. Fighting the first four bosses is easy enough but when you get to the "Sword King" the game starts to get a little unfair. By that I mean he's hella hard and most of his attacks are almost impossible to dodge. Overall the game is fantastic and I would absolutely love to read more of the lore. This game deserves more players and I think this game is up there.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a very good, if somewhat flawed game. I beat it in about 8 hours on my first playthrough, during which I beat all but one of the bosses, a decent number of the collectible cat appearances, all of the health upgrades (I think), but somehow only three of the guns. It was a bit too easy for me overall, but for a lot of people it may be unbearably hard, depending entirely on how well-versed in shmups and bullet hell games you are. The story is great, and that's all I want to say about it because I don't want to spoil any of it, as it loses some impact if you already know what's coming. If nothing else, ITTA is a lot of fun once you get a hang of it, and for $15 it's a steal. I'm excited to see what else Glass Revolver puts out.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a beautiful, fun game with a great music sound track there's a lot to find in the world and the boss fights are all unique and fun, there are some minor flaws, like getting  teleported out of the boss rooms sometimes when you enter it, and some bosses having to many invincibility frames but all this stuff can be fixed easily with a few patches.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: very cool boss fights, also really liked the combat except it kind of seemed like some weapons were just better than the rest, making other ones oblivious. The pattern the game takes may also seem repetitive to some; fight 3 bosses, fight harder boss, go to next area, find cool stuff in between, repeat. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game with one weird design choice. when you beat the game and when you have destroyed all bosses you can beat the final boss a second time. Their wil be a ? mark on the map, kill the last boss right away! dont be like me and get distracted and see if you missed something on the map because the boss will rest and you cant enter the room anymore, for some reason?So yeah i was kinda salty after that ! bosses are fun to fight an the game has a cool dark story to follow. snake power up with charge meter is a bit overpowered made some of the fights to easy .

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game in just 4 hours and there isn't much replay ability. Sure I can start a new game and run through the bosses again, but why? The art is amazing, the story is interesting, and the boss rush format is a nice change from the normal bullet hell experience. The game just seems way to short and too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I've only faced a few bosses so far, but it's a decent challenge simialr to titan souls ( only you dont die in one hit ) and the controls are closer to nuclear throne, dual stick shooting, a dodge roll - multiple weps in this game as well.you find real weps, and need to make them spiritual so you can use em, neat so far.not entirely difficult to a seasoned player of this style of game, but a good challenge nonetheless.Also, it's highly cute, and has a story with some meaning behind it.I only have a lil time on this, I'll be playing more and updating this as i see fit.The game seems to be 10 major bosses to defeat, and maybe it opens up to be more liek Titan souls does, I'll find out!recommending this as it's charming, and maybe bc I've been following it for 5 years.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel there's something wrong with difficulty curve in this game, it's generally getting easier as you progress (with occasional difficulty spikes) and leads to last boss which was easiest for me. But despite this, it's awesome and very climatic experience, I had this little "I wonder what will be next" thrill the whole time. And it didn't feel like mere Gungeon clone after all.

_childDocuments_.review: itta is a simple and to the point bullet hell game entirely focused on bosses which I really like since they're the coolest part of any schmup game, most of them are really fun though i think the dodge roll actually hurts my enjoyment of the game, sometimes it trivializes boss fights and other times it feels like bosses spam so much ♥♥♥♥ becauses the game is trying to compesate for the dodge keeping you way too safe making some patterns look like real bullet vomit (like the mob psycho middle schooler looking dude in the ruins, jeez does he throw a lot of ♥♥♥♥ while being invulnerable for not being a region boss.).
