_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game,amazing artstyle, challenging but fun bosses, decent story and music.Only downpoint would be the difficulty curve on some bosses (a boss would suddenly become 5x harder at 33% HP), but you'll pull through eventuallyGame is rather short with playtime highly depending on the players skill-level
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a game only consisting of bullet hell boss fights. It took a bit to grow on me, but I did enjoy myself more as I played further into it. I found the attack patterns to rely far too much on spawning bullets near the player going in random directions, which made some of the early bosses a bit tough without any health upgrades.The game itself has very nice visuals, detailed pixel art and all. ITTA has a large focus on death and spirits, which it never goes too far into, but the story is decent for what is there.For a few hours, I recommend getting ITTA, although $20 might be a bit on the pricey side.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a fun one to play if you're into bullet hell, boss rush and/or Zelda-style exploration. I can't say I really cared about the story and some of the bosses are a little repetitive with attacks, but this game manages to make a great impression in the 3-4 hours it'll likely take most moderately skilled gamers to complete. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are good, everything else isn't.The isometric camera might give the impression that enemies and bullets have some height to them, but in reality everything is on a 2D plane just with really bad hitboxes.On top of that, it's not rare for bullets to be hidden by the environment, the bosses, or even other projectiles: this is especially common towards the bottom of the screen due to the way the camera is set up.To compensate for these problems, the game gives you an incredibly overpowered dodge roll you can spam freely, but that just removes any semblance of challenge.The story is nothing special, and neither is the map: 2 or 3 hours, and you'll have seen everything the game has to offer .
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: A well-made and peculiar game that makes you feel worse the better you get at it and the more you complete it.The bullet-hell gameplay is good but it kind of runs out of possible patterns by the end, and as the bosses get into later phases, it can get overwhelming and you can't figure out where you are on the screen.Art style excellent, soundtrack good. A well-rounded package for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: A bullet-hell boss-rush set in a melancholy ‘deepest lore’ world. The pixel art and animation is stellar, the music less so. I love the design of the environments, but the backtracking through them so often felt a tad unnecessary. Overall, it's pretty intense and enjoyable with a level of difficulty that’s just right, but the game does slow down when it's unclear how to proceed between bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent bullet hell shooter with a very unique, almost somber atmosphere and story. The music, sounds and pixel art are great and make even just walking through the map a pleasant experience (and you will need to walk a lot if you're looking for all the secrets).The fights were, while hectic and obviously full of bullets, always fair and never felt frustrating. And you can beat the game from start to finish in one evening, how cool is that?
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: A small masterpiece. Normally, I am not a fan of bullet hell games, but this game is special. Not only the story, the controls, combat, and art style are amazing but more than anything the impressively deep world building ties everything together. Well worth the prize, and can't wait to play the developer next game.Things to consider improving: The only things that could be improve about this game are making the change of weapons easily (using numbers on your keyboard for each weapon like in Doom would be great), and the difficulty/progression. Even for me, someone that's notoriously not great at bullet-hell (but I do enjoy difficult games), found the game pretty easy. I think the difficulty could be cranked up or at least have a more difficult mode, I defeated many bosses on my first try. Also, a stamina bar similar to Tunic to stop you from spamming the roll would help with the difficulty problem. I often found myself spamming roll which completely trivialized some of the bosses cool mechanics. Apart from that this game is gorgeous and just amazing, big congratulations to the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a boss rush game, with no rogue lite upgrades. The upgrades in the game are zelda like. There are some hp up and some beast upgrades. Beast is a bar that fills up as you have close dodges with bullets-when it fills up you enter beast mode, which increases dmg and gives invincibility.There are also a number of weapons you can find and unlock which grant different options for fighting. I've unlocked the shotgun, cannon, bombs, and greatsword (in addition to the starting pistol). Edit: two of the weapons are basically useless in boss fights; the greatsword, which moves you closer and has a tendency to get you killed fast, and the bombs (obviously). With that being said, the others are all useful and provide a little bit of different playstyle.I haven't found any of the bosses extremely difficult so far. I've died 4 times between two bosses, but the music and the game play are really great. Edit: The last boss of Sky Gardens is probably the hardest of all of them, but I didn't die to them either time.Also, if you're like me and get stuck after the first boss, look to the left after you walk through the unlocked tunnel after beating him.As far as the deathless run, that's hard, but you only need to kill 2 bosses before you can get all of the weapons, health ups and beast ups. For the harder bosses wait until your beast meter is half or almost full so you get two uses for that boss.As far as how many runs, technically only one run is required, but I doubt you'd be able to do the only run without dying the first time. The three secret achievements can be done in your first/second run (although the last secret trophy makes a deathless run harder, as you have to use a particular weapon against a particular boss...granted that boss is not particularly difficult).Once you finish your one/two/three runs though there is no replayability.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great birthday gift because it was recommended to the gifter and if you enjoy bullet hell games then this is a game you should play. Would I buy it? no, but if you get it for free like me you should give it a goBut if you're looking for a proper bullet hell game or want to try one out by reading the statement above, type in: ENTER THE GUNGEON to the search bar and give that game a go. So much of me only wanted to play this game because of that one and even found myself playing ETG again after ITTA and thought: "Yeah, that last game was pretty but, it's not this game"I'd say ITTA is like a Celeste (highly recommend, own on console) bullet hell turned on easy that nobody asked for but is still enjoyable enough to play.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great, may it be short game. It can satisfy the itch of a rogue likes ( where you will need to restart a boss when you die) and bullet hell fans, and Boss-Rush fans too. cute style and art is awesome, plus you have a cute cat companion, who wouldn't want that ( you can also find different skins for the cat ).
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game! It's one of the first times I've seen a beginner bullet hell with high accessibility and the focus on telling a short story. Sprite work and boss patterns are absolutely filled to the brim with love and care from the creator, resulting in an intimately crafted world that feels teeming with life, in spite of the fact that well... no spoilers! You can beat it in 3 or so hours and that experience is pretty fun! I died several times but definitely would say the game errs on the side of being pretty understandable in terms of bullet hell style games. Dodge roll gives you plenty of wiggle room, exploration is heavily rewarded with lots of upgrades, and pretty much any one weapon can carry you through the entire game if you focus on the patterns. I can see how some would want a longer game but personally, I'm perfectly happy with games that are fair in price, reasonable in scope, and represents a unique approach to the genre from an amazing developer. Which by the way, if you're reading this, loved your updates on twitter! I followed it from concept to release (it just took me awhile to finally finish it). Def suggest you pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game last year ago. I was casually browsing through my games and I remembered how good this game was, so I of course went back to the game. Just completed all and the hardest achievement (no deaths), the game was better than I ever remembered. The story, gameplay, mechanics, and overall just feels so smooth and nice. I'd definitely replay the game someday as it's just truly amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: It is super fun, has an interesting story, and it was just a great experience of a game, I just finished the final boss, and it was worth the five hours. The progression of the game, the difficulty of the fights, and the new strategies you try after every death make the game fun to play. I'll probably play through it again just because it was such a great game.I highly recommend it, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a game about little girl who finds herself in a weird world and explores it trying to escape together with a cute ghostly cat. Game is HEAVILY inspired by Hyper Light Drifter. ITTA has a little different atmosphere, less futuristic and more fairytale-like, but if you played HLD before you gonna have a lot of deja-vu moments. These doors look the same, these switches look the same, hey, even your cat friend is very similar to that robot companion thing from HLD.Similarly to Hyper Light Drifter your main goal is to explore the world and search for new areas, new items, upgrades and so on. There are some NPC’s as well, talking to them gives you some lore that is (expectably) very vague and hard to understand.There are no minor enemies in ITTA. Instead the world is full of bosses that you must find and defeat, I think there are like 20 bosses totally, but some of them are optional and you can skip them. You will spend most of your time fighting bosses and unfortunately these fights are not very well made and left me unsatisfied. Bosses in ITTA are all bullet-hell based, they spam a lot of projectiles for you to avoid and dodge. I actually like bullet hell stuff but every single boss spams more and more bullets as his HP drop and eventually every fight ends with arena being completely swarmed with bullets moving in every possible direction making any strategical approach and pattern learning impossible.Scared? No need to. Chances that at least one of these hundreds of bullets hit you are very low. Your character has super tiny hitbox and you must literally run into a bullet to take damage. It is common in ITTA to casually walk into a clusterf@k of bullets and walk out safely as if you are in godmode.  Add to this a very strong dodge roll and surprisingly high tankiness of our little girl (you start at two HP but you can easily get to 12) and suddenly all these bullet-hell bosses become a bunch of pushovers. In fact I beat more than 50% bosses in a game at the first try and that was actually easy. I am not saying that every game must be hard as hell but I definitely expected more challenge from a boss-focused game.It is hard to rate ITTA either positive or negative, it deserves something in the middle. Guess positive fits better, there is clear effort there and I do not regret playing it but boss fights are just  underwhelming.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingly pretty, all the animations, all the enemies and especially the map.I love the first major "boss" of this game, unfortunately i ruined my first playthrough by exploring ahead and finding a bunch of secrets and upgrades. still incredibly cool to fight all the chamber dudes even if the difficulty sorta decreases as you play due to how overwhelm works.sword is op with the overwhelm mechanic unlocked, makes things retardedly easy.the final boss was the most anticlimatic and dissapointing final fight i've experinced in awhile and traversing the map the same exact way throughout the entirety of the game gets borring and makes me mad, should have gotten more ways to traverse the map as you progress, or have a way to fast travel.Over all, solid 8.5 out of ten, a must grab if it's ever on sale again.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Cute lil game with a cute lil story and cute lil characters--also your family is dead.Lovely characters with fun gameplay, doesn't take too long to finish but this game is far from unsatisfying. If you're not a fan of boss rushes, this game might not be for you, but if you're anyone else you should probably get this game because its cute and fun as ♥♥♥♥Very Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10While I do recommend this game, a few quick notes:-It is a boss rush game-Its a pretty short game (It took be 3 hours to get through the whole story +the extra boss)-For 3 hours of content, $15 feels a tad bit much for me ($10 feels more accurate)Pros:-It feels solid-All of the weapons are viable-None of the fights feel too hard, I didn't experience any difficulty spikes-Very pretty-Different looking cat familiars, all being pretty cuteCons:-The music is just serviceable & sometimes gets too loud-While it is a solid game, it does not have any unique/interesting mechanics or characters (save for ITTA, but that may be a bit of a stretch)7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, the sound design of the weapons is kinda poor, and actually the whole design of the weapons (the 3 first weapons at least, the ones I saw) is kinda poor generally speaking - I mean, the one that feels the best using is the 1st one, allegedly the weakest. Decent, a bit pricey imho.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Short, fun little boss rush.The best part is obviously the bosses, and how they feel - the developers of ITTA did a great job with a lot of them and how they jump, how they look, etc. I'm not sure how to describe it with how they jump up close to the screen like an artistic fourth-wall-breaking, but it's very very cool and like nothing I've seen before. I never felt like a boss was impossible once I got comfortable with the controls, but I also never felt like it was too easy or repetitive. The story is good, the visuals are good, but where this game really shines is it's gameplay. Whenever you'd die to a boss, it almost felt like the music didn't realize you were dead yet and kept going, and then would come to an abrupt stop when you came back to life. Sound effects also sounded very glitchy sometimes, especially when bosses started spinning and hit a wall, stuff like that made a grinding noise that didn't go away for a while. Overall, of course I recommend this. It's not a perfect game, but it doesn't have to be one. I waited somewhere around a year for this game's release and I was not disappointed. That's all I needed.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: It feels a lot like Hyperlight Drifter which, if you haven't played that, is a more robust experience. ITTA feels like HLD-light, but that's a good thing. It has solid mechanics and fun, arcade-y bosses. The story/world is surreal. I have no real complaints for this 3-4hr game. My biggest negative is that the bullets have height to them which often makes it unclear whether they should collide with your hitbox.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is really enjoyable for what it is. It's a bit rough around the edges but the product, overall, reaches the point where I feel comfortable suggesting it to other people (maybe when it's on sale, given the rather short time to finish it and low replayability). I believe that people that enjoyed either Hyper Light Drifter or Titan Souls should give this game a try. The enviorments are amazing and definatly an highlight of the game. The story is interesting enough to make you want to keep playing. The combat is rather hit or miss in terms of difficulty (I found the game getting progressively easier instead of harder but it very much could have been intentional, given the themes that the game tries to convey, or maybe i'm reading too much into it), also the hitboxes feel a bit off. The soudtrack is a mixed bag, some songs are great, to the point of wanting to listen to them again after i was done with the game, but others feel more like "noise". I'd say that this game deserves more recognition that it apparently has, it's a little, even if unpolished, gem
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Its an okay game if you like bullet hells and you're fine with the game being super short.Personally, took me around 2 hours plus running around for 1.5 hours to get all the missed upgrades.Game mechanic is like enter the gungeon with the iframe roll. Has a bullet graze mechanic to do this OP power move which needs to be balanced. Abusing it can make bosses very easy waiting right before the last form to trigger it and instantly kill the boss.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed ITTA. Its main draw is without a doubt its beautiful pixel art and animation. The gameplay itself is good, but not exceptional in any way. It's a top down shooter boss gauntlet divided up by a semi-open world. The writing was interesting throughout, and I'll leave it at that because I did find it to be pretty unique lore-wise. The music was ok overall with some outliers, a couple tracks felt like an assault on the ears and a couple others I really enjoyed. Most faded into the background though, as was probably intended. I'd definitely recommend ITTA. It's not the next coming of indie christ, but it is definitely a fun time, and is priced appropriately.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a great bullet hell game that feels a lot like a mix of Enter the Gungeon's gameplay, and Hyper Light Drifter's environments. It has a short. dark, and somewhat cute story, with some good characters to boot. The collectables were challenging to find, but not total BS. Some of the bosses were a cool homage to other games and anime. I wish there were more to the game, but at the same time I feel like the story was packaged up neatly and it didn't overstay its welcome. Personally, I think the challenge could've been amp'd up a bit in the later parts of the game, but overall it's a really good game. Also if it's your first time playing a bullet hell, this is a great entry to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Itta is a flawed gem. I came to Itta for the boss fights, since I'm a massive fan of games like Furi. However, most of the boss fights in Itta aren't all that great. A good boss fight needs to tell a strong story through the fight and boss arena, Furi accomplished this by walking the player through the boss's lair before the fight. These sequences were long and detailed providing context to the player and telling a meaningful story. In Itta each boss room is more or less the same, I got no hint as to why the boss was there or what they had done. The combat is also mixed, I found myself relying on activation of the "beast mode" which makes the player invincible and more powerful for an absurd amount of time. The guns weren't great either, I relied mostly on the machine gun once I got it for ease of use and none of them really stand out. Parts of the game are mediocre or don't feel as if they fit together properly. Some of the bosses felt really easy while others felt unfair. Maybe further play-testing could have improved this.For me, all these flaws were made up for by the story and lore. I'm a sucker for a good depressing post apocalypse story and Itta scratched that itch for me. The setting is beautiful and what is going on in that world is horrible and I love it. Some of the characters really grew on me especially the architect and Itta. I don't want to spoil the story but I finished it feeling satisfied.I'd recommend it to those who want a unique indie experience that clearly had a lot of heart put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun! I found the world to be quite engaging and the game has this depressing end-of-the-world atmosphere that I love so that was a nice surprise. It's a little short unfortunately, and I feel that's important because I think the story and characters would've had a bit more impact had we spent more time in this world to become more connected to it. However, since it appears this game was mostly created by one guy, I can completely understand why this isn't the case. If anything, I'm incredibly impressed how good this game is considering the one-man team behind it. Games like this are absolutely worth supporting, and I really hope Glass Revolver continue to make games in the future because there's a lot of potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Dark Souls? Do you like Top-Down rougelites, or a little bullet hell mixed in? Do you like being able to dodgeroll out of danger like a boss and never feel like you stopped trying to also attack? Do you like simple and clean mechanics with some high difficulty curve? If you said yes three or more times this game is short and sweet, but it's worth it's price. This is no slow bullet hell, Binding Of Issac or Enter The Gungeon kind of copy cat- no. This is a beast of it's own with a haunting story. Little spoiler: NPC's but no enemies- only boss doors and the boss behind it.Good luck.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Titan Souls, you should really enjoy Itta. The exploration is a little less puzzle-heavy when compared to TS, but the weapon variety makes Itta the better game. The art style is really neat, and the story, while fairly basic, sets up the world and the events well. It is a bit on the short side, but it doesn't wear out its welcome either. A great Saturday afternoon game.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell if my absurd amount of time I've spent playing Enter The Gungeon has made me too good at this type of game, or if it was just an easy game. 100%-ed all bosses, the map, weapons, and collectibles in just about 3 and a half hours with minimal trouble. I barely ever died, only facing about 3 deaths in my total playtime, never had to try a boss more than twice before I got them down. I even beat the final boss on my first go. The enemy and world design was interesting though. I liked all the boss fights and they all had unique bullet patterns so no two bosses felt exactly the same. Short and easy game for those experienced in the genre of bullet hell/shmup games, but a fun play all the same. Could provide decent challenge to someone new to the genre and could work as a good starter game.7/10. Lacks enough challenge for my liking, but a fun game nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting experience from beginning to end. Personally, I would have loved to see a fast travel, sprint, or something similar that would allow faster travel throughout the map. A legend icon for the starting cave would be a nice quality of life, as well. One of the most frustrating things for me personally was the lack of an audio/visual feedback from hitting the boss; there were a few instances in boss fights when I was completely unaware of whether or not I was doing damage, or whether or not a hostile mob on the field takes damage. Gauging the bosses health via the health bar is very inconsistent. There a moments when you are shaving blocks from the health bar every second, and there are other times where it seems to not move at all for long stretches of time. Switches weapons during battle isn't the greatest either; slowing the game down momentarily would fix that issue. All in all, despite the minor criticisms, I enjoyed the experience and found the challenge satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit different from the rest, some find the music awful, it is great to my ears, yet no idea what you're doing, where you are, but you still do what you need to. It is an experience releasing how far you've come from beginning to end, seeing all the puzzle pieces fit together from nothing. This game isn't for everyone, but if you do find yourself playing it, try and find everything.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, albeit short, twinstick boss rush shooter. Think Touhou mixed with Titan Souls, with a Dark Souls roll. The story, world, and characters are all extremely interesting, and the lore is left up to your interpretation. The game doesn't spoon-feed you information, so it's up to you to digest it as you see fit. I thought the difficulty was a bit low, especially after getting all the health upgrades, although this seems intentional so as to make the game as accessible to all as possible. Overall, if you enjoy short, boss-rush games, this one will definitely be up your alley. Support indie devs, buy the game!
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a wonderful example of how to make a Bullet Hell Game fun but not frustrating.  The bosses are set up in such a way that you can chuck yourself at them ad nauseum until you're finally able to scrape together a victory.   Nothing beats the sense of accomplishment when you finally learn the pattern and beat one without taking a hit.  And even when you do die, there's a chance that the death will show you a glimpse at the story, which is a wonderful way to make you want to keep trying to win!Now the game isn't without its flaws, camera feels a bit wonky, indication of whether or not you hit the boss / it hit you doesn't always click, and whether or not you have I-Frames, well, your guess is as good as mine- though honestly these can be considered personal gripes rather than legitimate issues.That being said, the artwork is fantastic, the music sets the tone wonderfully, and the story is given to you in little bits- even after deaths, which really helps to ease the frustration that can come with losing to a boss mere moments from victory.If you're new and interested and bullet hells or a veteran Touhou player, the game is accessible to you.  100% recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of Bullets: CheckDodge Roll: CheckThe main concept of the two bullet types is simple but effective. One you can shoot through, the other you can shoot down. It becomes a joy to dodge through the sea of bullets. However I knew that the hitbox for the the player is the center of the scarf only from an earlier development post, but why is there no mention of this rather important information within the game? The weapons are really diverse and cool, but I can't even do anything with weapons I found after beating the game... I want to replay all the bosses and use all my new weapons on every boss.The difficulty curve is also a bit whack, since as you gain health and weapons it naturally becomes easier again. There were like three bosses where I died a lot (and I mean a lot), and the rest I beat on my first (or second) try, including the final boss. But that's of course very subjective too.I'm also no fan of the large empty overworld, there are like 2 puzzles and a bit of exploring. It's pretty to look at, yes. It is nice for worldbuilding, yes. However I guess I'm not the type to enjoy the contemplative walks and NPC banter between boss chambers, I would rather have the overworld be filled with interactibles or not there at all. There are cases of new weapons opening up new paths to uncover, but that's the exception.Having said all this, if the game gets some update adding some post-game content (like new game+, boss rush mode, speedrun timer, hardcore mode...) this is an easy recommendation. I want to replay bosses, want to see if I can do better. In it's current form, it just falls a bit short.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good job for a solo developer. Things like that inspires me to learn that stuff or at least to try it :D Anyway, this game is really nice, but too short :( I wish, as it was told, we could repeat boss fights. Maybe some ideas you could think about:- make some option to teleport to the specific areas, at least 1 or 2 in the map so if I want to explore just single sections, I dont have to run that long.- it would be usefull, to chose weapons via 1,2, 3 buttons. Maybe you could use like 3-4 slots for your favourites? And put them there. On some bosses I just died bcs of switching weapons. I had to focus on the wheel, to see what weapon is selected and bcs of that, I lost my view on the field of millions particles flying around :D- Dunno why, but I wished some monsters beeing in the levels while running to the bosses. I know its a boss-rush style game, but the mechanic, movement and the vibe of this game is so good, that this kind of option could make this game more fun. Anyway, good job on this. Hope to see new updates or even ITTA 2?
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with one caveat - it's short. I love the story and atmosphere. The combat is of medium difficulty - it's all boss rush and is pretty forgiving both with the dodge mechanic and with how it places you right outside the boss room on death. But my biggest asterisk is that the game is very short. I just wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ProsBosses are fair and balanced. I found most of the bosses to be thrilling. Learning the bullet pattern of each boss and their changes in each phase they have. They all had a pattern that you could learn and strategize against.The hub world’s atmosphere strange and depressing and I love it. I find the hub world’s music coupled with the art design of world and its characters are done well.ConThe game is difficult. I’m not saying you have to be some bullet hell god or even a veteran of this genre to play this game, but this game will ♥♥♥♥ you… hard… no courtesy spit.I recommend this game, but when you play don’t use the god mode function to get past the bosses… Git gud.Video Review:
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a beautiful, fun little labour of love. If you enjoy yourself a good bullet hell with a Titan Souls kinda vibe, a batch of odd, depressed NPC's and some serious, "Gyah!" moments then you might as well take the plunge.Folks of experience and a level of adept in the genre won't find much in the way of challenge or length but if you're like me you will have fun and if you're less adept and just want to experience the world that's been crafted for us then there are significant difficulty modifiers to get you through the day.Loved it. Will 100% it. Looking forward to any future work that may come our way.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: interesting little game. the boss fights are all rather interesting, though in a lot scenarios, it boils down to near constant dodging. With the exception of a bugged out boss fight (in the players favor), and a few gripes that you can't roll through certain movement attacks, I overall enjoyed the experience (though the graphic imagery is a little jarring at times)
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. Challenging, but fun. Exactly what I was expecting and hoping for. It has a charming and surreal environment. I have not quite finished it yet, but so far while the premise is a little sad it is quite enjoyable and there is an air of hope. I suspect the only issue I may have is that it will be short. Fingers crossed for new content.----After finishing:The game is only several hours long, even with meticulous exploration for its handful of small secrets. But I loved every second of it, the style, the story, the mechanics, the challenge, everything.I only wish it had more content. And to a lesser extent I would have liked getting a little more explanation on a few things, but that is not a complaint either. It takes the darksouls approach of having the story being both open to interpretation and needing to do some searching for all the parts. It remains rather dark and ominous the whole way through, but is not off putting, just a good time all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: ITTA is a lot of fun, and I'm glad I gave it a chance. The game is clearly a labor of love. The challenge feels pretty well balanced, I never felt too frustrated.I was expecting no story, but what's there is really intriguing, but a little dark. It reminded me of a cross between Titan Souls and Hyper Light DrifterThere's a couple boss songs with music that's a bit discordant, which is the only real complaint I can think of at the moment.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game that I've had on my wish-list since March 2018!! Can't believe it's been 2 years already since I first saw it.Amazing game that I KNOW I'm going to get many, MANY hours out of.I've also recommended it to my gaming group of 16k people, so hopefully some of them will purchase it as I know there's a lot of love for the bullet-hell genrethank you for ITTA!
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

_childDocuments_.review: Test your limits in ITTA, a bullet-hell, boss-rush style adventure where you play as a young girl armed with her father’s revolver and guided by a strange ghostly cat. ITTA is a bullet-hell adventure set in a world filled with monstrous bosses. When Itta wakes up and finds herself surrounded by her dead family, her only guide is a strange spirit that takes the form of the family cat who gifts her a glowing revolver for protection. As Itta, players must seek out the powerful beings locked away beneath this seemingly peaceful world and go toe-to-toe against them in harrowing battles. From hulking ancient golems to toothy horrors, Itta’s journey will push both you and her past their limits. Luckily, you can change up your combat style by finding weapons with unique attack styles, and if the going gets too tough, toggle on invincibility or player damage multipliers at any time.
_childDocuments_.name: ITTA

name: Okinawa Rush
detailed_description: FEATURES: • Custom-made fighting engine with unique moves for each character. • Fight with swords, nunchakus, and bo staffs. • Engaging story told with carefully crafted pixel-art cut-scenes. • Dramatic electro soundtrack by Brassica and the Miller bros. • Many different enemies, each with their own moveset and weapons. • Intense boss battles. • Arcade mode for those who want to jump straight into the action. • Parry any attacks, projectiles, and traps! • Upload your high scores and compete globally with other players! • Discover many secrets and hidden areas! • Play together in a local co-op mode , and heal each other to achieve victory! SUMMARY: The Black Mantis clan has come to Okinawa... Take on the role of the martial arts master Hiro, Meilin, or Shin as they face off in a desperate fight for their lives against the Black Mantis clan. DOUBLE THE MAYHEM: Bring a friend and battle against ninjas, demons, and more in the 2-player local co-op mode of this action-adventure platformer set in a mystical, fantasy version of Okinawa. The fast, fluid combat system brings with it many moves, combos, juggles, and an intuitive parrying system. Fight to gain the top spot on our online scoreboard! 🎮🕹️ Controls disclaimer: 🕹️🎮 1 Player: keyboard (not mappable) or pad (you can change controls) 2 Players: controllers recommended! No support for two players on same keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: A superb game absolutely filled with all kinds of in-depth and satisfying content, both with the core fighting gameplay and elaborate stages that have a tremendous amount of secrets to find, as well as the rpg aspects where you train your character in all kinds of alternate modes and mini games and develop your dojo with items you purchase.The game can be enjoyed both on a more casual level with the incredible pixel art and fun combat throughout, or at a much higher level where you can crank the difficulty up with over a dozen choices with each progressive difficulty allowing for higher scores.The game has the odd bug here and there, but the core game content is incredible and filled with tremendous enthusiasm and quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Warning! If you buy this game to play couch co-op, know that it's full of bugs and completely broken. The second player will teleport constantly off screen, be locked into place, won't be able to perform certain actions, or lose all health for no reason.The single player experience works fine as far as I got but I was discouraged to continue as I bought this to play with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes some actual practice, as going out there and just punching dudes is sure to result in you getting your face smashed. But once you learn the ropes and start parrying, everything falls into place. The punches, the music, the sound design, everything comes together into one absolute BRUTAL beatdown. Can thoroughly recommend this, so long as you take some time to actually learn the gameplay systems to do cool stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: When my small daughter caught me playing this game, she immediatelly want to play with me too.The most beautiful tutorial offers playing with Ayumi as mother of 2 childrens, know as herbalist in this game she is living in traditional japanese culture and this was the most favourite stage for my child. She winned all tasks of tutorial without problem all alone. She have only 4 years and she know how to play this game.The most fun about it is that she don t know how to spell name of game but when she comes to me, she say ´´i want to play this ...´´  and she start to do in kitchen fighting moves looking like ...  ´´Right punch  Left punch´´  doing  EH  EH  and finishing with ´´kick in air.´´      I immediatelly know what she want to playWe played many times 2P mode and we beated nearly whole game to the final boss. _childDocuments_.review: Visuals and sound are on point. Everything relating to gameplay, however, is completely sloppy.A dozen spazzing enemies will be layered on top of each other which often makes parrying a crapshoot. Enemies can instantly transition from hitstun to being right in the middle of a deadly attack. Doing an attack yourself might make you face backward for some reason. You may find yourself grabbing open air because, let alone the player, the game's code can't even make sense of the chaos with enemies and yourself shifting and teleporting without warning. Most of the special inputs I could do consistently, but weirdly the simple Red Red Green double punch thing was a 50/50.Nothing feels like it moves as it should. Nothing seems to be getting hit quite like it should. It's like you're fighting against nonstop laggy rollback with 50 dudes at once. Other than the sax on stage 3, I can't describe any aspect of this game as smooth.
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is very satisfying for a side-scrolling 2D action game. You not only can punch and kick, you can also grab and throw enemies, kick them upwards, piledrive them. There are so many moves I haven't remembered all yet. You can also pick up weapons, save villagers, collect coins and use items. It's like street fighter + Street of Rage with platforming.Satisfying combat ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Trill of beating ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Nostalgic graphic ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What a cool game!I plan on updating my review once I play more, but wanted to get it out in time for launch day to help the devs.I don't think I've ever played a game quite like this. It's a bit reminiscent of that old arcade game Karate Champ (minus the clunkiness) mixed with a beatem up style game like Bad Dudes (because everything takes place on the same 2d plane).I bring up Karate Champ (if anyone even still remembers this) because performing the various martial arts moves is kind of the same. You press and hold a direction plus the attack button and depending upon the direction you're holding, you'll do a different move. There's also a rage meter than when built up lets you do more fantastic stuff and a couple special moves that are performed more like how they would be in a standard fighting game.Either way, you should give this a try. I'm having a blast!

Did you also have a love for Metroidvainias, Easy to pick up hard to master Combos and a ABSOLUTE BANGER of a soundtrack look no further. This game is a love letter and FULL of soul and content. You'll want to explore and get highscores and hone your combo flows.... This ones HEAVY in my rotation for Streaming. The Dev is also a Great Chap and Super active on socials so send Pixel heart some LOVE!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks awesome, but the UI is very janky and unresponsive (sometimes I can't even go back to previous menu). _childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I really, really like it.But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it isn't hard. Thankfully it does it a fun way that while frustrating at times, still makes you want to learn to be better and to get to the end. I've mostly played the story mode, which does allow you change the difficulty, but to those who really want to challenge themselves there's the Arcade mode which - from what I've learnt - is supposed to be the HARD-mode. But I must stress, this genuinely hard. So be aware of this.Game Play - the game play mechanics in this game are superb in my opinion - for a game of this genre, which is platforming beat'em up with a lot (and I do mean a lot) of depth. I've yet to come across game of this type which would have had more than half of the depth this game has in terms of game play, but I'd be delighted if someone could point out some for me if they happen to read this review.The fighting in this game is unbelievably satisfying. Parrying, which seems to be the most important mechanic in this game, allows you to deliver some really wonderfully visceral take-downs against your enemies and some of the weapons - the sword especially - can make your opposition to fall into pieces in rather creative ways. But worry not, if you happen to be one of those queasy types, you can turn off the blood if you so wish. You have variety of normal and special moves in this game, and I highly recommend you go into the story mode and use the dojo to familiarize yourself with them before venturing forward.Music - oh the music. In addition to the graphics, this game really hits down hard when it comes to people like me who were born in the early '80s and had the opportunity to put hours upon hours into playing our Amiga 500 games. Yes, while similar to what we used to hear in the time period where Amiga reigned supreme, the music in this game has its clearly modern spin on it - which, again, is question of taste on whether or not you will like it. I did, so I give my thumbs up for it!Sound & Voice acting - the sounds in this game are straight from the Amiga era and I love it! The dialogues in this game are at par with your '80s action flicks from Hollywood, with wonderfully cheesy voice acting - especially the bosses. I love how snooty and almost British the first ninja-boss you meet sounds like - I really had a laughing out loud moment there.Story - Not much to say here, as I've yet to complete the game (as of writing this piece), but from what I've seen so far, the story does seem to be your typical revenge plot straight from the '80s Hollywood - along with the cheesy one-liners and everything. Even the cut-scenes are somewhat reminiscent to what you used to see in top-tier Amiga games during the platform's golden era of early '90s.All in all, I heartily recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a challenging platforming beat'em up - they don't get much better than this.And to anyone reading this, if you buy this game, please leave a review for it - this game needs more publicity. The only reason I happened to discover this game was because YouTube algorithm decided to randomly put a video about this game into my recommendations list - and this was well over a year after the game was released!

_childDocuments_.review: Okinawa Rush~~~~~~~~~~~~Okinawa Rush is a 2D side-scrolling beat ‘em up, that focuses on feudal Japan with era-appropriate themes and conflicts. This is another game that wants to get into the new gold rush that is Arcade gaming on PCs and Consoles. Trying to bring an authentic arcade combat experience, Okinawa Rush did a bang on job at it.But it failed immensely on some other parts, where they should’ve focused a bit more; I’ll get to that later. Plot: You get to play as three different characters’ martial arts master Hiro, Meilin, or Shin and you will be going against The Black Mantis clan. Each character gets their own stories which are revealed in stages, and they all have endings. Although short, and a bit messy, they’re still better than nothing. Hiro: As Black Mantis Clan entered Okinawa, Hiro was out of his home. Having known that the clan attacked and murdered his family, Hiro is now out for vengeance. Shin: Our second character, Shin, is a monk, who went after the Black Mantis Clan after he found out that the clan attacked and left a mark on his student. Meilin: Last is Meilin, in search of her father. She ran into the clan and from that, her conflict with them began.Gameplay: Okay, so first of all let’s get the worst part out of the way.  The game wants to be an Arcade game; good.  It wants to use some Arcady controls and UI; also good. But while doing all that, the devs seem to have forgetten about the part of user-friendly UI, controls, and everything else! It took me 10 minutes every time for the first few times I tried to play, just trying to figure out the game.Nothing worked; not Space, Enter, ESC, Mouse Left! Then I tried Mouse Right and the game crashed! Tried again and again, and this happened every time.Turns out they put exit on the mouse right without marking it or putting any indication on the screen, and most of the menu is something like this. Luckily the gameplay itself was pretty decent, I mean the combat part of it. Pretty well justified and balanced in terms of an arcade-like experience. The game itself is very difficult even for an arcade game, those who love some challenge might find this aspect interesting. Combat: As short bits of your back story are revealed during combat, you become more enraged and engaged in combat, nothing can stop you! Unless you forgot to remap the controls. Although Okinawa Rush’s combat is mostly a two-button deal with movement coordination and jumps, you are not gonna do well unless you change it up to something you’re comfy with. The game lets you buy items for your DOJO, which in turn will bump up your stats. Which is all good, until I found out while trying to shuffle through them that my items were removed, and I had no way of getting them back. Or I just couldn’t find any!There’s a lot more going on in the game; some things are really cool and some got a bit messy due to poor execution, which am hoping will get patched soon.World Design: Visually I think Okinawa Rush is stunning, from its lighting to art to its level design. It was supposed to be based around Feudal Japan, but it more or less turned into an enhanced parody scenario, which is good as well, I guess. Music and sound effects: Impactful and rich sound effects, I honestly wasn’t expecting this to be so good. Hey, I’ll come back for more of this. The same can be said for its retro-ish music, just awesome. Positives: + Decent Plots+ Three endings+ Three rich characters+ Interesting villains+ Fun combat + Great artwork+ Loved the music and sound effectsNegatives: - UI needs a lot of work- Got lost in the UI menu, which I thought was impossible! - Crashed on me a few times- Needs more content and quality of life improvements Three awesome characters with an awesome beat ‘em up experience. 6/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: There's just something about certain games that are just special. The passion and love poured into the game really shines through in every way. _childDocuments_.review: There has probably never been such an intense platform fighting game before. Everything fits together here. Great gameplay, great music, sound, cool graphics, and combat system. This last aspect, especially, is amazing. You can perform amazing actions, even though the game uses... only two buttons plus directions. Plus melee weapons. Cool thing. The game encourages you to explore the levels because it has many secret locations. A nice thing is training, during which we improve the hero and can practice kata, our own dojo, and shopkeeper. For the collected decorations, we can buy amulets that improve character statistics, or items for the dojo. There are also different colors of kimono. Oh, the game has 9 different endings, a two-player mode, and encourages replaying. A lot of this content, really. I heartily recommend it, it is unique

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. I went in thinking it was going to be a fairly standard platform fighter, boy was I wrong.There's a complex and sharp system to this game. Combat is tough, but manageable. You can muddle through mashing buttons a little at the start but you do need to learn fast. The real star is the parry system though; combining the rapid directional changes required to parry with the massive array of different moves has you blasting ninja all over the place!The story so far as I've played is decent. It has so far balanced that fine line between too cheesy and too serious.Graphically it's incredibly well drawn. I like the option to turn the CRT setting on or off (I prefer on). Everything is silky smooth, with zero problems on screen.The music is perfect for the setting and the voice acting is clear (albeit a little wooden for my taste).One big downside to the game is the UI though. The menu is very janky and difficult to navigate. At times it has been completely unresponsive (this was very prevalent when trying to edit my dojo). I think polishing that up and maybe adding in more text hints on the menus would be great.Overall I recommend this for anyone who likes challenging platform style games.NOW FOR MY PERSONAL FAVOURITE BIT OF THE GAMEI'm a karateka, I live and breath martial arts. This game had a feature I was not expecting to see. KATA! A fun little minigame where you need to time button presses as your character completes a kata. Now you might be thinking what's so great about that? ATTENTION TO DETAIL! They are all amazingly well done, I personally did Seiunchin about 10 times in a row because I wnated to double check just how close they got it. It's spot on! I hope you add more kata in future guys, hell I'll personally send you vids if you want em.If you're a karate buff then get this game.If you like 80s martial arts action then get this game.If you like deep combat systems then get this game.Get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's...ok. I'd give a neutral review if I could.First of all, the menus are terrible; I usually end up mashing through menu screens by accident. If you select arcade mode, the game will default to this from now on, and you actually need to know to select back on the title screen. Why is this a problem? Well, arcade mode is actually HARD mode! The fact that the game gives you no warning about this is inexcusable.As for the game itself, it is an OK beat em up. I like the visual style, and it feels good to hit things. This game was advertised as rewarding methodical play over button mashing, but I find that this simply isn't the case. Everything simply happens too fast, and projectile attacks are too small, that I often find mashing to be the only way to progress. There are a lot of special moves which I often end up triggering by accident. The UI icons that tell you if your meters are full are simply too small, and there is no time to check in the heat of battle. Oftentimes I find that I've lost a bunch of health with no idea why. Sometimes a hazard comes out of nowhere and kills me in one hit. It's possible to progress, but also very frustrating.I've also noticed some bugs: enemies get stuck in walls, and hazards that I've bypassed will magnetize me toward them and kill me anyway. Sometimes boss cutscenes will trigger, sometimes they won't. It's still playable, mind you. Levels are big, and there's a lot of content. Taken as a whole though, it is somewhat disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Full livestream video of full game review at  watch?v=gxFyTkLETeMTLDR: If you grew up as a kid with Way of the Exploding Fist 2, Shinobi, Turrican and.. err.. Dark Souls? Yeah well that's pretty much what you get here.The GOOD: Awesome visuals. Fluid animations show the amount of time taken to get the feel of each character just right, and the scenery, while detailed, isn't overpowering that you lose track of the game characters - an issue in many other pixelart games.Combat is hard to master and sufficiently satisfying to play. Piledriving a ninja never gets old.Tons of secrets and rewarding hidden items.The IFFYVoice acting is.. yeah it'll do! Main guy sounds like an angry Mr Worf (actually not a bad thing!)Controls can be a little sensitive - I was using a dualshock 4 - D-Pad seems to be the way to go here.The MEHWhen you first load up, it isn't immediately apparent what to actually do. Oh, top tip - I would advise against playing Arcade mode first unless you enjoy being humbled in 2 minutes...The first screen you see is the dojo screen - and I don't yet know precisely what this does in terms of playing the game. I can see it increases stats, but I'm not sure if these directly relate to story mode.Difficulty seems also to be given as an option AFTER you play in mad ninja mode - after suffering badly, you can then choose your belt colour - essentially how difficult the game is. I chose green - middle difficulty and this seemed to feel about right.Some aspects of the game are not always apparent - I'll avoid spoilers but check your suroundings for anything relevant to your situation. (I think that's fair!)Bottom Line:Buy it if you like old school fighting, appreciate great retro style graphics, and want something challenging. Oh and it has 2 player co-op which I imagine would be a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Metal Slug & Martial Arts this game is a ton of fun, beautiful and varied levels, awesome music, cheesy voice acting and impactful combat that lets you do piledrivers on samurai into announcer tables and giant swings on ogres, as well as use your accumulated score to buy alternate colors from the shop, decorations for your dojo shelf and stat boosting amulets. Tons of difficulty range for both accessibility (it uses a traditional belt system, going from white belt to black belt, then 1-8th dan, then Grandmaster and one special difficulty beyond that) and replayability through the higher difficulties that add more and more enemies. as well as 3 endings for all 3 characters, two brothers who are quite similar but have different key moves, and one girl who has a cool kung fu moveset that's entirely different from the other two (you can do wing chun chain punch in this game). Lots of secrets to find, and a unique take on a game when martial arts seems so under appreciated in video games nowadays. it is good. buy two copies
_childDocuments_.name: Okinawa Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game.Now for the my more complex thoughts. Its a cool little platformer/ beat em up indie that fills the checkboxes for an insanely violent piece of machismo. It also fills a small niche of actual martial arts (like being able to do katas and such.) Not to say the game is realistic by any means but martial arts otaku will be able to appreciate the touches.It has small rpg elements where you do training and buy items to increase your attributes. Most games that include these elements also have extra skills to unlock but this game pretty much has them all from the get-go which I appreciate for a game of this nature and length. This is the kind of game where the tutorials don't teach you everything, but you'll absorb all a lot of the small aspects of the gameplay in very little time. Especially if you're the experimental type.I also like how they don't hide their appreciation for fighting games and FGC lingo. There are quite a lot of useful moves to choose from, even the meter-less ones.This game is pretty short but has a lot of things to go back to making the initial price worth it.For cons, it can get a little unstable. No crashes or anything, thankfully, but I've encountered plenty gameplay oddities. Something about the how the game feels, like jumping/juggling, seems a bit too erratic.Many times I get punished for mashing during crowds but a lot of the time I get by just fine by mashing.So yeah. This is a pretty nice game if you want a crazy fast brawler with plenty of post-game content. I really do feel Sokaikan can do a lot better for a sequel or something similar in the future being their first game and all. I'll definitely be making some revisits for this one until that arrives

name: Gloomhaven
detailed_description: Whether you are drawn to the lands of Gloomhaven by the call of adventure or an avid desire for the glimmer of gold in the dark, your fate will surely be the same… Lead your band of mercenaries through this unforgiving place, where every choice is crucial. Carve your way through terrifying dungeons, dreadful forests and dark caves filled with horrific monsters to reap your rewards… or die trying. Sell your sword to anyone who can afford it, may they be city officials or corrupt cultists. You are paid to get results and not ask questions. Where will you draw the line? Gloomhaven is a tactical RPG and a digital adaptation of the ultimate strategy board game by Isaac Childres (the highest-rated board game of all time on  ). Set in a unique medieval dark fantasy universe, Gloomhaven rewards strategic planning and problem solving.  Face this dark world alone or in online co-op for up to 4 players! Explore the world in a band of 2 to 4 mercenaries. Each of the 17 unique characters comes with their own skills and more than 1,000 different abilities to master! Prepare your deck of ability cards before setting out to explore the dark caves and dreadful forest of Gloomhaven through quests and events. Once inside a dungeon, engage in tactical turn-based combat by selecting two cards for each mercenary on every turn. You can only use the top half of one and the bottom half of another, so plan accordingly! Move up your hired blades on the hex grid terrain to take advantage of the dungeon’s environment. Set up deadly combos and unleash devastating powers but be wary of the cost. Cards are a resource as scarce and crucial as your life points, so watch out for exhaustion. Every choice has life or death consequences. Hone your abilities during the game with enhancements and perks, while your power increases with level ups and new equipment. You need every advantage you can to survive here. So, gear up your band of mercenaries, chase powerful artifacts, buy the favor of the Great Oak, and never let your guard down. Adapted from the original Gloomhaven Board Game, this branching campaign of 95 story missions pits your greed against your morality. Many powerful opponents are vying for control over the city of Gloomhaven while others are looking for ancient crypts and forgotten artefacts. You could always side with the inhabitants, but it may not pay well… Whatever your path may be, it will be paved with difficult choices. Created in collaboration with the community during the early access , the Guildmaster adventure has more than 160 exclusive digital missions that allow you to experience another facet of Gloomhaven with new storylines, quests, map and NPCs. Lead your guild of mercenaries in a region overrun by unspeakable things, far worse than simple bandits. Choose the best combination of mercenaries for each fight and follow their character stories in this deadly new territory.

_childDocuments_.review: I have the tabletop game, that I intend to play with family and friends this Christmas. It took an age to put it all together (o.k, it was only about a week) and an entire weekend to comprehend the rules and start a game. So pretty hardcore for a casual gamer of any kind and even though the kids enjoyed the assembly the game itself was overwhelming to the youngest member of the family and a little bit for the rest of us as well. There is a lot to take in regarding the rule system especially with "Used" versus the "Burnt" abilities on each card. Two cards each round with one choice from two options on both cards. You can choose an ability to burn (and therefore use) or choose an ability to just exhaust and claim back in  a turn or two. Then you can save those high powered burn abilities for later. Once you burn a card it is lost for the remainder of that scenario (with one or 2 rare exceptions were you can claim them back). Making sure you have enough cards for movement, healing, damaging or boosting abilities during a scenario is a logistical challenge, even in the early scenarios!If you like turned based D&D, an element of RnG but mainly tactical game-play, character & skill progression, a backstory to each along with a personal story-line quest for them as well, then you will lap this up. I wish I had this PC version to start with, Now that I have fully grasped the initial rules after a few dungeon crawls I can fill up a few Christmas holidays with the table top among friends and family and the evenings honing my tactics and knowledge playing the PC version. At 34 hours I feel like I have only scratched the surface, (having only leveled up one character to 3rd level with the rest at 2nd and 1st) I still feel like there are many hours ahead. Not to mention Multiplayer as an option and (for me at least) multiple play-throughs.Can be frustrating at first but stick with it and you will be rewarded.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, bugs fixed I can change to positive :-) 240 h in the game.This is a great game. It's great because it's not for everyone. Exactly like a tabletop version, this is a game designed to be best-in-class experience, with no compromises to attract wider audience. * It requires some patience, especially at the beginning. Unique mechanics and design choices may discourage you, but give it some time and they really shine. * This is a dungeon crawler-puzzle game, quests are interesting, but for most time you will be figuring out how to best build your characters, team and traverse dungeons.* This is  a game where you embrace randomness. It's part of the game. Pushing your luck gives these extra sweet moment of heroic achievements. * This is a game you need to learn and explore. Learning and exploration are part of the game. It pushes you out of your comfort zone. * This game is meant to be actively played. It does not entertain you, it's a tool you can use to entertain yourself. Don't blame the tool if you suck at using it ;)By these traits the game delivers exceptional value and hundreds of hours of fun.------ First review -------192.8h on the clock. I love Gloomhaven, both digital and tabletop. Very good games. But the latest update broke it in so many places that it's almost unplayable. I can get use to UI changes (like swapping buttons locations) or some unnecessary changes that gives no value added (sounds maybe? some graphic update? I can't tell for sure. Nothing that would improve my experience).But still - test your game before releasing it!

_childDocuments_.review: [Update (2/3/23): The UI has improved slightly but none of the innate problems have been addressed. People who can looks past its core problems will enjoy this game, but it is clunky and obtuse by design and it would seem they have no intention of changing that. I have put a lot of hours into the game and it does feel rewarding once you master it, but that climb will be obnoxious for all but the most dedicated player. Because of that I would hesitate to recommend this game to anyone, even those who generally like grid based strategies.]TLDR: The game needs serious polish but has a lot of potential if it gets said polish.First things first, the game functions fine. If there are any bugs, I have not run into them and as near as I can tell all the features of the game are based around the actual tabletop version. (which I have not played for the record) In fact, the core systems of the game are really interesting. Each turn you have to choose two cards for each of your characters which determine their initiative as well as what actions they have access to once their initiative comes up. You can use each action in one of three ways generally speaking which typically amounts to: some sort of offensive/defensive action, some sort of movement/utility option, or if neither is something you want then you can use any card as a generic attack or move. At it's core this system is deep and interesting, if a bit complex for something you have to do every turn, but overall I like it in concept.The main issue I have with the game arises from a system that is core to the functionality of the game: burning cards. In Gloomhaven, you generally start each match with ten cards (this may change as you progress through the game but at this point I do not see a way to increase this limit) and each round you use two of them for your turn. Eventually you run out of options to play and you have to take either a short or long rest to refresh your card pool for that character, but in order to do that you have to "burn" one of your cards which permanently removes it from your options. (until you leave that area) If at any point you no longer have enough cards left to play a turn or rest then that character instantly collapses. (I guess from exhaustion?) In principle that is fine, but in practice it is CRAZY annoying because of how it is implemented, particularly because the game gives you loads of incentives to make numerous small movements. There are loads of offenders here but to give a few examples most enemies drop gold on death and that would be perfectly fine if moving across that gold picked it up. Nope, you have to burn two cards whether or not you are in combat to go stand on some gold and pick it up, assuming you are within single move range which is far from guaranteed. This leads to some truly amazingly unsatisfying deaths where you die essentially from bending over too many times to pick up loot. Essentially you have to choose between actually getting the rewards you have earned by killing the enemies or risking death and losing the whole run each time you decide to pick something up.Believe it or not though, it actually gets worse. Remember how I said before that there is a somewhat complex decision you have to make each turn to decide what actions you take? Well, there is no "out of combat" mode in this game so even once all the enemies are dead you still have to be making those decisions and planning super hard for what's beyond the next door while your goal is..... take one step and pick up some gold. And remember how you get a somewhat active action and a somewhat movement/utility action each turn? Well, you don't stop having to choose those just because nothing is happening leading to the baffling outcome of having to meticulously plan out actions that you are willing to throw in the garbage just so you can take a single step to the left. It is truly extraordinary how clunky this feels and any hint of actual tabletop RPGs that the game is striving to emulate just gets sucked right out during these insane moments of fiddly micromanagement. This could all be solved, I think very easily, by having an out of combat mode that allows you to move using both actions (perhaps just turning the generic attack into a generic movement for the top half) and allowing stuff on the floor to be picked up as part of movement rather than requiring you to end your turn on each individual thing. That would radically reduce the amount of tedious planning required for out of combat movement. (the stuff that really has no business impacting your chances of survival in the first place) This mode would activate once there are no living enemies in any active rooms and phase out seamlessly the moment you open a door.I have several other issues with the burn system (I would genuinely throw it out and make the main focus of the game life if I was the game dev but *shrug*) but for the sake of brevity I'm just going to talk about what I view as the most significant among them. I've touched on the fact that each card has two functions now multiple times in this review but it is important for this to understand that the different effects of even a single card are wildly different depending on which piece of each card you decide to use. As a fictitious example of a card you might expect to see, you could have a top effect that causes you to attack three tiles ahead of you with the bottom option being jump three spaces and then push an adjacent enemy away. Every card also has an initiative value, generally speaking basic and/or weaker cards tend to have low initiative (meaning you go earlier) while more elaborate or powerful cards have a higher initiative. (meaning you go later) In total, this means that each card that you select requires that you analyze at least three points of information (almost always more) in order to decide whether it is the right option or not for the current situation. This very frequently results in choice paralysis, particularly since the card effects are often not great at staying in their lane.Now, this in and of itself is a bit clunky feeling but in isolation is probably not enough to be a huge problem. The real meaty issue is introduced when you add in the fact that a good chunk (probably a third or more) of the cards in the game have at least one of their options result in the card being immediately burned without being used for a rest. As we have already established, this is incredibly bad because you only have a maximum of 48 actions (24 turns) for each character before they run out of cards to burn and tap out in the best case scenario. What this effectively means is that any card effect that ends in "burn this card" essentially translates to "never use this function unless you are in the last room and comfortably winning." Even then I probably still wouldn't be burning cards willy nilly because the treasure chests cannot be looted if your objective is met before you get to it. (I guess your character is just too tired from slaying monsters and bending over to pick up gold to bother looting the treasure they fought so hard for) This could once again easily be solved by simply allowing the player to decide when to leave rather than automatically forcing them out once the objective is completed and I really hope they make that change prior to launch if nothing else.I know that the tone of this review is very pessimistic but please do not take it as me just bashing this game. I really think there is a diamond buried here and I hope that the devs manage to dig that diamond out of this rough. This game could truly be something special if it is given the polish that it really needs to shine. They just need to stop emphasizing the worst parts of 2E and make the focus of the experience the actual combat (which is quite good) and deck building. (which may or may not be in the game at this point, if it is I have not reached it)

_childDocuments_.review: Love the board game. Played this; got a refund. I'm fine with an Early Access game lacking polish but having most of its content, or lacking most of its content but having a polished system, but Gloomhaven has neither. When I played, in addition to having very bare-bones content (no card upgrades, items didn't work right, only 4 classes had been implemented), there were a ton of bugs, way more than there should have been for what is ultimately just a digital board game.Granted, this was in 2019, and they've been steadily adding content since then, but things were so buggy at the time I'm going to wait at least another year to give it a second shot.
