_childDocuments_.review: The Rift Breaker is a good game brought down by a lack of automation.The basic gameplay loop is good fun with some nice simplification from a game like Factorio or Mindustry. You will spend most of your time in a loop of finding resources, expanding, researching, and then be directed to finding different resources so you can start the cycle over again. It's a fun if somewhat common game loop. I would consider this to be a solid 7/10 however it's innovations bring that score up to an 8/10. For example, the game simplifies the annoyance of having to cart around numerous resources through having everything connected through wormholes that connect all of your physical resources to each other. Strangely, you still need to build a bunch of pipe and power lines to connect things to each other but resources that you mine or gather are automatically transported around for you.Having said all of that, this game ends up at as a 6/10. At this point the game quickly becomes annoying to play due to several design decisions that detract from what is otherwise a fun experience. The following are the biggest gripes I have with the game as it stands at time of review.1. The game is missing automation when it comes to upgrading things. For example you'll manually run around back and forth upgrading a turret here, a solar panel there, or mine over there. This is okay but rapidly becomes annoying as you have multiple bases, a large interconnected network, or thousands of power plants and turrets that needs manual upgrading. For the love of God, please just let me set a minimum amount of resources to maintain and then let me prioritize automatic upgrading by building type. 2. Depleated buildings should really scrap themselves. Currently, the game will happily tell you that a Carbonium mine is depleted and wait for you to manually run over and scrap the thing. This is annoying as your base grows larger and larger. Most of the time I can't find the individual mine that's depleted or be bothered to truck halfway across the map to scrap an individual mine. Instead, the game just continues to alert me that a mine has depleted when it's been depleted for hours and hours in game. This leaves me thinking "I'm aware it's depleted and I don't CARE!". 3. The resource names are straight up silly. Carbonium? Ironium? You're playing a character from Earth you can just grab actual elements off the periodic table and use them. No need to invent names like this... You know, since you've kept using Uranium and the like.4. I never found a need to change out tower types. You can easily just stick to the basic turret and upgrade it all the way. Adding in hundreds of turrets is as effective as having 10 of the ones the game belives you should be using. There are other issues but those are the top 4 I have at  the moment. In closing this game is fun but at 16 hours played I've beaten it on the hardest difficulty setting, found it easy, and I'm probably done with this game forever unless they add something new to the gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: On lesser difficulties, this is a decent resource management game that involves combat PVE style while also strategizing how to a accomplish the goals.  On higher difficulties, it becomes a survival management game as you are rushed by hordes strong enough to wipeout nascent outposts and keep them gone until you get strong enough to get the breathing room to rebuild, hoping you have enough resources and time to do so.  Having played at the initial release and after some time when the DLCs became available, I am very pleased with the interface evolution that has occurred, making the game more accessable in a time management crisis environment.My largest critique since the publishing of the DLCs is that certain core mechanics (building counts and resource cultivation) have not been tweaked appropriately to take into account the newer material.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Interesting idea but the game is way too repetitive - most of the game mechanics are there only to prolong the game loop.  those are almost meaningless, you get so much so fast you stop caring about it before you even know it You can go out to kill monsters – to get more resources you don´t care about – or you can try go out to find a boss, a hive, or some special location, that has a chance to drop something more than just resources - but most of the time, resources is all you get felt like it was there only to make the game loop longer – as you have to wait for hours to make something done - which creates a lot of waiting, doing nothing periods – just because you are waiting for research to get finished and there is nothing else to do in meantime (esp early game) combined with lack of ability to repair buildings makes it annoying – a player has to repair buildings one by one – making it painfully tedious, especially in the early game – once auto-repair buildings are researched it gets better – making events pointless in the process felt boring – AI, if we can even call it like that, is something programmer of 1st year of any IT university could manage to come up with – get close to target and use attack, repeat – making it easy for players to kite all enemies, even in front of an endless wall of towers. Once again, making every wave of enemies feel exactly the same. felt disconnected from the game – a player jumps to a new map to set up a new base – then he can return back to the main base at any point – action is happening only on the active map, meaning, extra-base provides a passive supply of resources without the need to worry about it – also, becomes repetitive really fast

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Supreme Commander, this is somewhat similar but it's PvE as opposed to PvAI or PvP and your mech can be rebuilt, just don't lose your HQ. One notable difference is that the missions don't last the usual 30-90 minutes like SupCom, it's more of a continuous play.Whereas games like SupCom and Starcraft are a campaign based mission where you go from location to location with a problem to deal with each time, this is a challenge where you are attempting to explore and take over a whole planet while the native wildlife tries to kill you.The game does have some UX issues around being able to unlock things before it actually explains how to use. If you follow the guidance/recommendations of your mech suit in the first few hours, things are explained as you go rather than having to figure it out for yourself. Google helps if you get stuck anywhere though.Some things just aren't explained at all well, particularly around upgrading your mech suit. They aren't too hard though and a little trial and error gets you what you want fairly quickly with minimal loss.Performance is good, autosave often causes game stuttering but otherwise it's very good on a high end system. 2080 ti also seems to have enough grunt to be able to enable the raytracing features while still maintaining a high frame rate.

_childDocuments_.review: Riftbreaker is, in short, amazing.You got all of these element of base building, ressource finding and exploration that mix together perfectly.Event to keep you on your toes without being too distruptive, a decent variety of ennemy type, and a good array of weaponry. It will keep you hook for hours, always striving for something more that is coming.The base building is the most prominent element with all the option, and the defense phase are exciting and require planning.Develloper did a good job of varying wave and the direction of attack. You cannont simply turtle a fixed point and be safe. But you dont need to run everywhere to defend your base, it's a very good balance of the feeling of involvement in a defense phase without being too overwhelmed.The story is good and servicable and they put alot of effort of the interection between the two main character, (the scientist and the robot) Even if at the end , the way the main protagonist Ashley dialogue feel a bit weird in comparison to what you are doing (She's keen on preserving the ecosystem of the planet, but you burn through ressource so fast you need to cleanse alot of the biome)So, get it, it's amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so...maybe it was just RNGesus having fun with me but my second play through so far hasn't had the issues with not enough spawns to complete the scanning mission in the volcano area.So I've updated my review to a thumbs up because who doesn't get excited when you hear "a massive invasion is incoming!" I grab some popcorn and proceed to watch Rift's rendition of fireworks but with alien bits, globs of goo and all the chunks any Rifter could ask for. Artillery cannons, laser cannons, rail guns, plasma beams, and mini guns. Oh sure there's been a few close calls. I even had to re-spawn once because I tried to dance with a rock monster that stepped on me. Between spore colonies growing out of control, lava golems throwing bits of what I hope is them and not their buddies, and nature trying it's hardest to make life difficult with meteor showers, lava bombs from volcanoes, acid rain, face melting temperatures, nuclear radiation...there's so many ways to die!10/10 would melt in lava anytime.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal is the best first person shooter i have played since the original F.E.A.R, in fact i might like it even more because of the replay value i feel like i will get from this game. The gameplay is pretty much perfect, the constant weapons and upgrades you get keep the game from ever getting repetitive. In fact it just keeps getting better as you go along, i had more fun the more i played which is very rare because it's usually the opposite for most games. Towards the end of the game where you have your whole arsenal at your disposal, it's some of the most fun I've had playing a game ever. They improved the gameplay so much that i don't think i can go back to 2016 Doom again.Just like 2016 Doom, a huge reason i enjoyed this game so much was the soundtrack. I made sure to keep the music at max volume while turning down all the other audio options to 30% just so i enjoy the soundtrack as much as possible. It accompany's the gameplay perfectly. Graphically the game looks great and runs great too with the framerate being locked at 144fps with max settings at 1440p. One big reason the game never felt repetitive was the great level design and a huge variety of locations keeping the game from being stale visually. The story was only serviceable which is the one flaw i can think of. It's one of the best games I've ever played and it's a must play for any fan of shooters. 10/10 (Masterpiece)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by and far one of the best shooters I have ever played the guns feel meaty, the combat requires you to think and prioritize which demons you shoot first and with what weapon. The soundtrack in this game is also perfectly suited for what the game shows. The games atmosphere is also unlike any game that i have played before making you feel as if you are in hell with the fire, blood and corpses. The only downside that i can think of is the multiplayer and even then its enjoyable for small bursts but does not work in long sessions.overall the game is a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is not nearly as good as Doom 2016. This is arguably better than Doom 3, though. Arguably. Here's what to hate:1. Most enemies have 1-2 correct ways to kill them, and the game punishes you for not doing this. I get that you want to encourage all weapons and abilities, but this genre is supposed to be about shooting things until they're dead, not memorizing arbitrary weapon selections. 2. bethesda account needed for single player. No. Bad developer. We don't want that, no matter how much money you get selling our data (or whatever lie you've found to hide the fact that you're collecting data you don't need).3. Way too many cutscenes. I want to play and shoot things, not watch my viewpoint slowly walk to a window to make sure I don't miss the expensive setpiece. If you really must have a plot, then tell it in a way that doesn't constantly interrupt my exploring and shooting things. 4. Annoying environments. A purple goo that doesn't let you jump is an interesting puzzle gimmick, and wall fireballs are a staple of gaming, but at least have the enemies be affected by it so it's a strategic choice and not an annoying obstacle. 4. Too many invisible walls. Sure, Doom 2016 was exploitable, but this doesn't mean you should have an invisible wall anywhere you don't want the player going. 5. _childDocuments_.review: Positives:Beats Doom (2016) by a landslide. Amazing movement, even faster paced action and a multiplayer that is completely Overpowered for the demons and that's just the way i like it. Fixed almost all of the problems from the first game including the useless pistol, and many others. Good long game with a fun story and many interesting bosses to fight, with a new "weakness" system to demons so that the game isnt just a shoot till they're dead game. ive seen alot of complaints about low ammo, and i experienced this problem maybe twice. Your equipped with a chainsaw which gives you ♥♥♥♥ tons of ammo, with enemies who can be chainsawed littered around every fight with a delay between uses of maybe 6 seconds. If you are a fan of strategy and learning the best way to defeat your enemy than this is your game, each demons have a specific weakness that can be exploited to easily destroy your enemies. Pinky from Doom (2016) was near impossible to deal with, and now his weak spot is his tail! The game is much more manageable and you feel like you are actually the doom slayer, completely destroying the demons methodically and easily. Negatives:The story doesn't quite go anywhere. there a good streamline idea but Doom (2016) had the story down a lot more, the arcadey aspects of Eternal don't appeal to me, but OG doom fans will be pleased with all the references to the old games. The navigation system in this game is awful, the best way i can describe it is if you needed directions and google pointed you in the compass direction to the very last turn. I never got to finish the last level because my save file became corrupted, so that wasnt very impressive. The "Multiplayer" is COMPLETELY broken. Not only do the demons have an insane advantage over the Doom Slayer, its a client side connection and rubberbanding does wonders, as either the demons or the slayer will freeze inplace because the Client cant keep up and you CAN STILL TAKE DAMAGE WHEN FROZEN. This means that anyone on a bad connection can essentially hit you through walls. I believe this will be fixed in time, so im not too dissapointed with this one. Coming back to the story, unless all answers are at the very end of the game (which they arent) the things it trys to hint at and tell in the story NEVER go anywhere nor give any definitive answsers which leads me to believe that all of the story elements are jammed into readable packet stories which you can pickup, which is great for youtubers who want to spend 300 hours making a lore video but not for people playing the game. At the end of the day id still say its better than Doom (2016), as it is super fun and Mick Gordon shredded even more tracks, with a return of BFG Division. Extremely fun all around.

_childDocuments_.review: 22 hours into the game, played on Hurt Me Plenty. Read almost all the complaints and I'll advocate for both sides. But I'm mostly on the side of not particularly liking the changes.I think Doom Eternal is by no means a bad game. Not at all! But... there are so many small changes the game could do to make it go from good to great. Let's talk about those issues people have. Keep in mind these gripes are very much subjective, you'll either hate or love them but those haters can and should arguably learn to adapt beyond 2 hours of the game. 6 hours +, not enjoying it? Completely understandable.The great chainsaw ammo economy:Major hint: Chainsaws regenerate 1 bar all the time.Yeap. That's a thing. Where other games have reloads with individual weapons your chainsaw is your reload.  After playing the only available master level over 4 times, clearing up and collecting half the missions again and adding up my ammo capacity it does feel like a problem that gets mitigated over time. What doesn't however is the fact that I need to use the chainsaw now, instead of complementing my combat flow it's just something that I HAVE to integrate into my combat flow. No, I can't just use it when I want since non fodder require 3 bars to use it up but I guarantee you my ammo will run out before I can fully utilize all the ammo that the larger enemies can give. So the gripe I have with the chainsaw is that I can't just use it when I feel like I wanna do something badass or end off my fight with a shabang because I will most likely not have the chainsaw fuel (x3 bars) to kill off said large enemies.Weapon variety and versatility:On my first whole playthrough of HMP outside of the cacodemons I thought "eh, screw enemy weaknesses, if I get em. I get em. who cares". I'd occasionally try to burst a revenant's jetpack every once in a while but 7/10 of the times I'd just ya know, brute force my way down to his HP.However after trying the whole weakness system I found it being too effective. Enemies that were major threats to your HP like Mancubus, arachnotrons quite literally get there threat levels down by 80% I wish I was exaggerating but everytime they spawned you can easily decrease there threat with 2 placed Precision bolt rounds. That 7/10 of the times went from 10/10 times for every revenant, mancubus, arachnotron. This just gives off that feeling where some weapons are far more effective than others in almost every situation. If I were to give a good example of making you choose different weapons without completely overshadowing others it'd be the Doom Hunter. He's really weak to plasma weapons but he's not completely useless when you exploit his weakness either, he can still pose a threat until he's dead. Can't say the same for Mancubus', Revenants or arachnotrons. Map design and "linear" design:Another critique that people have of Eternal is that it feels more linear or straight foward compared to 16. Which... I might agree with. MIGHT. I haven't played 16" since 2 years ago so I'm going based off my memory. But I do recall that I could deal with certain maps like the Foundry in ways that I wanted to deal with first, do I deal with the gore nest here first or the one over there. Or maybe get a key card way over there. It was mostly up to me. With Eternal sure the maps are bigger but they're not always better, you go slightly off the path, invisible wall, wanna jump over to that section that has something you can land on? oh no no my friend lose HP, get back and spawn where you just started, or spawn back up even further back. In a game where it encourages you to go off the beaten path it also feels like you're being hand held by another person in that regard. "Try exploring over there b-but wait! that's too dangerous, come back here right now young man!" is what I felt like most of Doom Eternal's exploration is like. However, the actual polish and look of the maps is 10/10. Each place looks varied with myriads of scenery, gothic castle areas, Warframe's void like towers, hell on earth. A lot's there in terms of map variety so you don't get the samey feel of the orange mars and orange hell in 16".I brought most of these critiques up since I completely understand both sides, while I like the game, I really do, I just can't bring myself to enjoy it as much as I did 2016. Overall a 7-8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this review with a quick anecdote:Back when I was a kid, I was somewhat of a DooM fan. I had never actually played any of the games; at the time, the only PC gaming I did was on Adobe Flash. But, as with many shooter fans, I was aware of the enemies, guns, iconic levels, etc.. Thus, when I found a DooM novel ("Infernal Sky," for those curious) at a used bookstore buying it was a no-brainer. The premise of slaying  demons not with sword and sorcery, but with 12 gauge and rage, is obviously too good to pass up. Since DooM's story is somewhat sparse, I was always curious to know more about the metal album madness that is the DooM universe, and how our collective boy Doomguy fits in with the greater world(s). Suffice it to say, I was disappointed. For those brave, mad souls who actually want to read it, I'll tag it: . And so, I remained waiting, hoping, for a wider DooM universe of Demon flesh and Hell-forged steel, taken in new directions beyond the classic games we know and love.And ID Software delivered. Oh  did they deliver.Before I get into the beauty that is this game's worldbuilding and lore, I  talk about this title's stellar gameplay. DooM Eternal has proven itself to be an amazing FPS experience that, like Titanfall 2 and DooM 2016, is one I know will be an instant classic. It is an absolutely, unwaveringly demanding experience. Nothing but skill will get you past the waves of Hell's legions that ravage the Earth and beyond. As the last game put it, "Hell devours the indolent," and so movement, as always, remains a core pillar of the game. Verticality is even more important than it was in 2016, as the "monkey bars" and air-dashing mean that airtime, in conjunction with regular running, is a important tactic to master, should you wish to stay alive. Once you get the hang of it, you'll find yourself effortlessly swinging, Blood-Punching, and weaving between demons like an Argent-fueled Mike Tyson (sans pigeons and ear-biting, probably). And you'll need to get the hang of it, as Eternal's demonic hordes are especially brutal and without mercy this time around. On my Ultra-Violence playthrough, even a few zombie strikes and/or Imp fireballs are the difference between being full on health and desperately needing it. Even the weakest of fodder demons can  kill you, should you allow them. To say nothing of the Heavies and Super-Heavies, who will lay waste to any prospective Slayer ballsy (or reckless) enough to not take them seriously. An Arachnotron, if its turret is not disabled, will  in a matter of seconds (I learned this lesson pretty quick in the first level). Of course, you're by no means powerless, as Eternal gives you every tool in 2016's book and then some (except for crouching and , but that's such a non-issue it's actually funny).  And of course, Mick Gordon’s soundtrack speaks for itself.Glory Kills, Chainsaws, and the good ol' BFG all make their appearance here, and are as awesome as ever (my only nitpick is that you can no longer disembowel mancubi with the chainsaw, but again, non-issue). Compounding your toolset are Dashing, "Monkey Bars," and the Equipment Launcher, as well as some new Mods, putting a new spin on 2016's mechanic. The Equipment Launcher completes a sort of trifecta between it, Glory Kills, and Chainsaws. Where the latter two replenish health and ammo, respectively, the Launcher's Flame Belch gives back armor. This is vital, as Eternal is, as we all know by now, lighter on pickups than 2016. Like before, full armors can be found before boss encounters, and in various nooks and crannies of the level. The lighter pickups (which form a good bulk of your armor in DooM games) are much more sparse, as is the case with health and ammo. This paucity of gun food and gamer fuel means that getting “gud” requires mastering this “unholy trinity.” The Launcher's other modes, Ice Bomb and Frag Grenade, help with this. I often find myself Ice Bombing enemies (giving me a quick break in the mayhem), then Flame Belching and fragging them to get armor while saving ammo. You'll also need to be mindful of demon staggering, as non-Blood punches do little to no damage, so properly timing glory kills isn't just stylish, it's necessary; thankfully, the new Destructible Demons mechanic facilitates this a good bit, as you can now see how close a demon is to getting game-ended. Making sure that you yourself avoid this fate requires mastering Eternal's mobility. Due to Eternal's abundance of platforming, you'll find yourself quickly understanding the distance each jump and dash can take you. This is important, as a single botched ledge grab can get you ghetto-stomped by the demons in short order. If you've played the Shadow Warrior reboot, you'll likely already be familiar with the dashing mechanics. Funnily enough, having just finished 2016 before starting Eternal, I actually found myself  to dash during the first level. I no longer forget to dash.Many reviewers have noted how much more intense DooM Eternal is compared to 2016 and previous entries. They are correct. While these games are still heart-pumping FPS Titans, DooM Eternal is actually strenuous. Let me put it to you this way: DooM Eternal and Animal Crossing had the same release date . After finishing this game, I wanted nothing more than a relief, even if it meant paying a talking raccoon's mortgage for hours on end. I played System Shock instead, but you get the idea. I imagine trying to beat this game on Ultra-Nightmare would be akin to playing the Halo Series on LASO. Meaning I'll probably try to do it because I'm an insane person. DooM Eternal is a shooter so intense, it will make even a stubborn, impatient action junkie like myself truly appreciate stealth and quiet. Hydrate and take breaks whilst you Rip and Tear; you'll need to.Now that we've gone over gameplay, let's finally get to that lore stuff I was crowing about earlier. Since this is obviously replete with spoilers, I'm leaving it down here at the bottom. For those understandably not wishing to spoil the story, I can say this: DooM Eternal's story is great. It is so great, that it not only makes this game good, but it retroactively . This is what I was waiting for, what I was hoping for, as I closed that novel in disappointment. DooM 2016 showed me that ID had understood both the lore and the spirit of the DooM series. Eternal showed me that ID has . .The worldbuilding and lore in this game so clearly has thought and passion put into it. Lore entries will not only reference events alluded to in 2016, they'll drop in meta-jokes and references that just go the extra mile. Even so, the story of the game is still strong without reading it, never bogged down by needless drama and other trappings of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ storytelling. While DooM 2016 was almost completely confined to a first person view, Eternal now makes use of full third-person cutscenes, which bothers people who think story and text in DooM is like bacon-wrapped shrimp at a Bar Mitzvah. While I can't tell you why these people have such a deep-seated blood feud with the written word, I  tell you that the cutscenes are skippable, unlike 2016's. Also, classic DooM literally told most of its story in text, so a reading-heavy DooM is far from unprecedented. If you like DooM's premise and lore, you will  this game's story.TL;DR: 666/10, buy Animal Crossing

_childDocuments_.review: I can't overstate on how much the Doom franchise is important to me. I play it since my childhood and just by thinking on how much it grew and evolved brings me joy. Doom really is a long-lived iconic classic with diverse styles in its various games, some titles being horror focused (such as Doom 3, Doom 64 and Doom PSX) and some titles being heavy packed with unrelenting action.   Doom Eternal obviously carries the flag of the latter mentioned style and does it very well with its elaborate combat system with a defined weapon variety, enemy variety and count, strategic resource management, advanced movement mechanics and a kickass soundtrack. Doom Eternal, while being arguably a hard game, its a very accessible one with its difficulty variety, while also being very lenient with different playstyles, combined to weapons mods that gives your well-diversed weapons a secondary fire to accompany your playstyle.  And last but not least the atmosphere with its beauty and diversification is jaw dropping. Travelling from dimensions beyond is astoundingly varied. From the very depths of hell and to the very ruined realms of a decaying and dwindling extra-dimensional race, to the acidic bog of tortured souls of the Blood Swamps, you travel and fight with one objective in mind: To kill and murder every single demon you face. In revenge for what you've lost and to protect what remained. This franchise made history back in the 90s, delivered numerous titles and even after 25+ years of existence it keeps delivering the most fun I've ever had in any videogame title out there. Can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: 7.8/10, too much purple sludge.Being serious, it's a bit tough to recommend this game to just anyone. It's not as easy as just saying "If you liked the previous Doom games, you'll enjoy Eternal." It is fairly different from previous entries in a lot of regards. These changes, such as the extremely fast and aggressive ai, the low ammo capacities, and the new suit gimmicks are going to feel awkward at first. After a few hours of dedicated playing, the game should eventually click for you and will start to get really, really good.That being said, it's still not a game for everyone. If the sound of combat that is so hopelessly chaotic at first that you can hardly keep up sounds repulsive to you, perhaps Eternal just isn't for you. There's no shame in that, in the same way you shouldn't feel ashamed for not liking turn based combat for being too slow.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanna say this game is great. This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastically done. Everything about screams wanting to be perfect.Yet there are these tiny flaws that most people overlook and I just find it like.. All too rear up its ugly Titan head.Gameplay feels slower, with dashes feeling really clunky when it doesn't wanna work, getting stuck between demons when you really want to get the heck out of there. Enemy AI is there, it works, but holy heck, why do all the enemy attacks track even while you're mid-dodge? Movement speed feels slower too, the wall grabbing half-works, monkey bars are break the pacing when they're in the arenas.. It's all those little things that feel like they don't agree with me. We also got the new drop system, with ammo coming from chainsawing fodder. Which honestly sucks. You're just given so little ammo to work with in spare, it hurts. Why am I able to super shotgun 12 times only? How come I only get 10 rockets? It feels so little and the chainsaw kills get old pretty fast with how long they take, sometimes even getting you killed as the demons suddenly swarm up on you.Guns.. Those guns man, do they just feel like.. I don't know, it doesn't feel like they do much. As insane as it is for me to say it, the guns in this game just don't feel like they do much in comparison to 2016. The Ballista just feels like a far weaker Gauss Cannon, the mods all feel very meh, with the precision ones giving you the best results just because of the weakpoint system, which I mean, sure cool? But that goes back with the gameplay being slower with the system set up to reward hanging back a bit more and taking precise shots more versus those that run in, shotgun blazing, and can still get out without taking too much damage.Marauders. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Marauders. What is this enemy and why does it exist. Why do I have to deal with a demon that blocks EVERY SINGLE ATTACK at range, chunk you for a ton of damage, DASH, summon a wolf that chips away your HP if you forget about it cause you're dealing with adds, and takes a ton of punishment. No really, why does the enemy have a patience way of defeating it? Every single enemy can be killed in less then a second if you're really good with your fingers and know your weapon match-ups. Why do Marauders SLOW down the gameplay more then it should be? Why are they so tedious to fight against? C'mon idSoftware, this enemy is cool in concept, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the execution of this enemy just outright horrid. At least they make you fight them one at a time in the base campaign.Other nitpicks include not moving during examination animations when you pick up a secret! Secrets in general feeling a bit less, especially since there is no hidden levels. Initial replayability since as of this review we only have campaign, master levels, and battle mode, which is the PvP of this game, not interested in it to be honest.At the time of this writing, I have completed the campaign on Ultra-Violence. The level design is great. The soundtrack is outstanding. The overarching gameplay is fast and action-filled. All the levels and details are fantastic, but there are some little things that really crawl up under my skin. I will eventually do a Nightmare run as well as do the Mastery levels, but for now, I need a break from Marauders. Good grief.Updated to finally go through the Nightmare levels. Just going to be brief.Coming back to it with a fresh mindset helps. Optional encounters are painful on Nightmare, but at least they're optional. Do I still recommend this? If you haven't played 2016, play this. If you have played 2016 fresh, give it a bit before jumping into this one.I'd love to switch to a neutral stance for this game, but Steam reviews only has yes and no.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're old enough to remember when ID used to outsource their expansion packs for quake etc. Thats exactly what this game feels like. All in all, its pretty amazing how much stuff they screwed up from the first game, but it ended up still being pretty fun. I dont know bethesdas current inner workings, but if I had to guess, they are like most greedy game studios and probably fire people a lot. So if you're one of the original doom2016 devs, rest well knowing this game is worse. This game takes a while to ramp up and get good. Part of that might just be me having to unlearn how I previously played 2016, and adopt the new chainsawing fodder demons, and other mandatory mechanics. Basically everything I was worried about from the trailers ended up being true: You spend half the game tracking down this sword, which is basically just the old chainsaw you got for free in the first game. The graphics were made to look more like original doom I guess because 2 people on twitter cried. The story is ♥♥♥♥, especially in the beginning.You would think adding a ton of new abilities and mechanics would open up the game play, but it actually just makes it more restrictive. Its a 100% requirement to chainsaw fodder demons for ammo, and you basically just grapple around the map using the SSG 90% of the time until there is a mechanic that requires X weapon to be used. Its not so far removed from console games that are just a series of "Press Y to perform action" scenarios.The game gets significantly easier once you get enough upgrades to get tankier, mostly because the devs idea of a challenge is to just spawn demons literally on top of you that instantly deal damage with 0 counter play. Once you get tanky enough to eat a few of the cheesy hits, the game gets much easier. Go figure. Furthermore, I'd say a good portion of the deaths were a result of running into some invisible wall or obstruction of some kind that stops you dead in you tracks to get instagibbed. Similarly, when fighting the marauders, if they're on some type of uneven terrain, they will instantly clip into you making it impossible to dodge or parry. This makes half the challenge of fighting them making sure they arent going to instantly clip through objects to kill you with no counter play.I could probably write an entire review on how bad the story, and more importantly the story telling is in this version compared to the original, but I'll just sum it up by comparing the contrast of a few things.. In the first doom, you, rather than using a terminal or taking commands from an operator via coms, you just punch the terminal and continue on your conquest. -- In this version, you have a nagging operator for a better part of the game, and you literally have your own spaceship, with your own bedroom, and a personal computer.  The closest comparison of the 1st games storytelling is half-life style, or even the original doom. This version felt more like destiny, or even mass effect.The only interesting bit of the story this time, was showing that ardent energy is literally harvested from souls in hell. Really makes firing the BFG that much more metal. xd

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review with stating this is an excellent game. The genre of FPS has been kind of stale and has slowly shifted from Survival/FPS/Battle Royale into a "tactical" shooter experience. This is a defiant example of what great people can do with long standing franchises when given proper care.The gameplay is a 100% improvement from the previous reboot of the DOOM series (DOOM 2016). There are more things to manage, more gameplay opportunities and a significant increase of rewarding skill based gameplay. The game is definitely more overwhelming than the previous game, which can be considered a good or bad thing, depending on your engagement and the focus.The length and pacing of the game is a little different from the previous game. While some people are arguing that a certain enemy type breaks the flow of the game and that there is an annoying slow goo, it's much better than the first. The game keeps you much more engaged until the end and progresses just fast enough to keep it interesting, but not so fast that it expects you to master skills within seconds (unless you run the game on Nightmare for the first time, which I do not recommend).The music is a complete step up from the first game. It's a total shame it will be the last album from Mick Gordon and I am not sure if the game will ever be the same without him. Speaking of which, I was a little disappointed to find out they only had the soundtrack for Collector editions month after the fact, instead of with Digital Deluxe editions (which costed $40 for basically 3 skins that aren't in game, 1 that is available in game and a weapon sound pack on launch. Pretty meager if you ask me and I was almost certain they said the soundtrack was included, but I wasn't going to pay the $250 CAD for it, that's a little much for what you only really want is the game).The optimisation of this game is stellar. Not once did I fall  under 144 FPS which is something you don't really say from triple A titles these days. I could even push over 300 FPS if I tweaked some settings. The graphics though, well, that's a different story. There are some textures that are clearly 10 years old and I am not joking when I say this. There are some textures that remind me of Fallout 3. There are also lots of mirrored textures which was done to save on download size for the game. Which is nice for people with slower internet, but I don't think it would be that much bigger for even 512x512 resolution textures in this area.Well it seems you've made it this far and have been wondering "well why is this a negative  review?" It's simple. There are more gamebreaking bugs that have been adding into  the game recently than there had been on launch. There is a bug where if I press shift very quickly while mid air and switching weapons, the game crashes. This is unacceptable, because I was playing a master level which does not let you load from checkpoints. What's even worse is that I play on Nightmare, so master levels aren't exactly a walk through the park. Hell, I would even argue that a master level on ultra violence is close to being harder than most slayer gates on Nightmare. Regardless, this crash happened to me twice. I disabled the overlay effect in the options menu and tried  to replicate the bug, but it seemed to have been fine... until I crashed on the first level of the game on One Life Mode Nightmare. It's a shame, because this is one of my top games of all time.There is now a new bug that I have been encountering where the sticky bomb mod for the shotgun would not properly damage enemies and the arachnotron turrets. This is very frustrating and I have lost many lives and lost many Ultra-Nightmare runs because of this.   Denuvo didn't really impact my performance, but that's probably because of my system. I can't really notice a difference of 320 ish FPS increased from 300 ish FPS when it was removed, especially when my monitor is only 144HZ. It's nice they removed it but it seems the cheaters are rampant in Battlemode so I won't be playing it soon™.There is a game breaking bug with the cyber mancubus dealing practically infinite damage (caps out around 900-1000) that has ruined my ability to go through ultra-nightmare runs. I now don't really want to play the game anymore because of bugs that just ruin the run.Please fix this bug, otherwise this is easily one of the most important games of the 8th console generation.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: A bigger, badder and more intense sequel to Doom 2016. It does play very different, and the game is based on managing your health/armor/ammo based on glory kills/flamethrowing/chainsawing respectively. The micromanaging of resources is initially annoying but once you hit the 3rd level, Doom Eternal really hits it's stride.Pros- Excellent and addictive gameplay. Doom Eternal features a greater variety of enemy encounters and the levels are also extremely varied.- Meaty campaign. It took me roughly 20 hours to beat the game. The game is more difficult than Doom 2016 to expect to retry many segments over and over again. The boss fights are extremely challenging but fortunately there is an option for a one off 'sentinel armor' should you really get stuck.- Delves deeper in the Doom 2016 universe/lore (which some may not be a fan of - if you haven't played Doom 2016, the Doom Eternal story will make no sense)- Slayer gates. These optional arenas are an awesome addition to the game and most certainly increase replayability.- Great level design and map system. There is also the introduction of platforming which helps break the flow of combat, but this may be deemed as a con if you just prefer out and out action.Cons- Marauder. Would have been fine as a one off boss, but the enemy design pure sucks IMO. Can only take damage if his eyes flash green, which only occurs at a certain range.- Buff totems. Demons are powered up until you find and destroy these items in an arena. I'm not a fan, as the game already throws relentless amount of enemies at you. It's extremely difficult to hunt these in the midst of fighting hordes of demons.- Poor art direction compared to Doom 2016. Doom Eternal looks garish and cartoon-like in comparison to it's predecessor.- Very limited ammo count. This becomes more of an issue later in the game, especially when you face waves of tough foes. Chainsawing enemies also seems to take an eternity.- Arena hazards. Too much sticky purple goo or fire when fighting hordes of demons.- Ugly UI. I have no idea how they could conjure such an ugly HUD after the beautiful UI of Doom 2016. I also hate the bright colours of the ammo.Overall I would consider this game one of the best FPS games I have played in recent times. It's a step-up from Doom 2016 - which is no mean feat - but I can see why some hardcore 2016 fans may not like DE. I think as an overall package Doom Eternal is the superior game, but there are some things Doom 2016 does better. Though it's honestly a case of comparing apples to oranges - both games are very different experiences. Nevertheless, I'll give DE a solid 9.5/10. I have no doubt it will remain my favourite game of 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played it on release, I bounced off. I wasn't a fan of how most demons have a specific weakness you have to exploit or they get bullet spongy. Most combats felt like paint-by-numbers, you see a spider dude and blow up the top turret. You see a cacodemon and throw a grenade down its throat. Some people told me that's only the case in the first few hours but I still didn't feel like playing it.A few years later I decided to finally beat it... and it's pretty much the same throughout the whole game. Plenty of enemies have very specific ways to kill them or they'll take up a ton of ammo. The chainsaw mitigates this somewhat, but even that just feels kinda bad. Out of ammo? Press the ammo button.A few people told me to turn off the gameplay tips so it feels more organic to find the weaknesses (and granted, most of them are pretty obvious). But that doesn't really make sense as there are multiple enemies that literally cannot be damaged except in a specific way, so it seems the devs intended the first playthrough to have tips turned on.Eternal adds a bunch of other extra weapons and gadgets, a lot of which seemed superfluous. You get a sword which is more or less just a stronger chainsaw. It doesn't replace the chainsaw, you just have another button to keep track of. It also adds freeze grenades and a flamethrower. The flamethrower doesn't actually do damage, by the way, it gives you armor.They also made melee attacks a lot worse. The regular punch does literally no damage, you can't even kill the weakest, most basic zombie with punches. You get a Blood Punch ability which you can charge up by doing glory kills, and then you get a single punch that actually does a bunch of damage in a large AoE... except you often don't want to use it because A) you want to save it to punch the dudes who are weak to it, and B) it can kill a bunch of trash enemies, depriving you of glory kill health or chainsaw ammo.It's been awhile since I played the last game, but Eternal feels a lot more samey to me. A lot of combat arenas feel the same, especially near the end of the game.There's purple good that slows you and prevents you from jumping or dashing. No idea how they thought that was a good idea to add to a game know for fast, frantic combat. Apparently the devs agreed because it only shows up near the beginning, but why not just remove it entirely? It adds nothing but frustration.There's a lot of platforming, another thing that doesn't feel like Doom. It's not hard but platforming has never felt right in shooters. Eternal is no exception.And finally, the non-gameplay stuff. it feels weird to have a story and lore and charcters and other Doom Slayers and whatnot. It was cooler when Doomguy was just here to kill demons instead of all this other story stuff. Instead of throwing grenades, you have a dinky little Inspector Gadget arm with the grenades and flamethrower on it. You collect batteries to power up your ship in between missions. Instead of ignoring the talking heads so you can focus on killing demons and closing the portal, you just follow everything they tell you. _childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, I really do.  For the things I love, this game is hands down beautiful.  The scenes portrayed feel like something horrifying and crazy is happening, yet are painstakingly beautiful.  You can see that much work went into the graphics system and they knocked it straight out of the park.  The game engine runs smoothly and I did not have any types of stuttering or lag while playing where other games, even including Doom 2016, I had stutter in places that could kill you in game.  The music feels truly appropriate for each location you hear and it can make what would be a small uninteresting place enjoyable just from it alone.  The creativity of the creatures and scenarios you find yourself in also enhances this game in amazing ways.  Hell, even the multiplayer is a fun experience that even with the Demons being the more likely ones to win, playing as the Slayer is still enjoyable.  However, the actual combat mechanics, and to a much lesser extent, the story KILL all these experiences.  Let’s start with the combat as they’ll probably be some spoilers in the story line of this.  If you enjoy Doom 2016 and are coming straight from it, your experience of the game will almost certainly be harsh at best.  I understand that many people enjoy hard games and even I have enjoyed harder games such as Dark Souls on my consoles.  But I can say this coming from Doom 2016 myself and that is the difficulty spike between the two is absolutely absurd.  This is a game in which you are the Doom Guy, but within a life-based system around a large damage income and low health and shield recovery.  It ultimately will leave you feeling like some random guy who put on the Doom Guy armor and it’s the only reason you are even surviving rather then being the full-on Doom Guy who the demons of Hell fear so much.  You are expected to use every single alternate ability to it’s fullest and if you are not fast enough or familiar enough with these abilities, you will die quickly even on the lower difficulties.  This incentivizes you to have some of the highest reflexes I have ever seen required for a video game and can be very harsh on someone who is not quick on the draw.  Weapons of the game feel a bit down trodden.  The punch mechanic of the game is nerfed to be almost completely useless taking 10-20 punches to kill even a basic zombie that a single gunshot could remove unless you have a blood punch charged up.  In addition, there is no pistol so the two fall back weapons of previous Doom games are completely removed by these actions.  Your selections of weapons come back to some well-known Doom weapons, but their ammo reserves are so incredibly low that after a few shots you will find yourself running on empty and being unable to fight.  For best example, if you fully max out the ammo increase in this game your Shotgun ammo still does not even reach the first ammo upgrade in Doom 2016 for the shotgun.  In order to combat this, you are expected to make full use the chainsaw on small enemies which will then drop ammo.  It quickly becomes apparent that this is a painfully bad game technique as you are required to quickly kill the larger enemies while leaving the small ones alone. Any enemy in this game can deal serious damage to you so if you leave too many of the small ones around you will be over run as they keep spawning until the large enemies are dead.  However, if you kill too many you will find yourself out of ammo and most likely dying to larger enemies while hoping a small one spawns for a new ammo cache.  Enemies are enjoyable for the most part.  Some of the new additions such as Whiplash and Gargoyles are annoying as Hell itself, but they feel like good additions and fit well into the system.  Marauders though DO NOT and they ruin the experience of the enemies.  This here is a creature that does not fit into any rhyme or reason within the gameplay.  If you are too close, it shoots you with a super shotgun.  If you are two far it blasts you with energy.  If you are standing the perfect distance from it, it will attack you with an energy axe.  If this was all the Marauder did, it would be a strong enemy and a unique one to the game.  Nope, they decided to give it a shield that it can bring up and negate all damage at any time.  Think you’ll one hit kill it with a BFG or Crucible attack, nope it’s immune to both of these one hit kills.  So you have a very attack driven and defensible enemy now.  What more to give it?  How about a large amount of health requiring several shots to kill when you are able to hit it?  How about a summoned dog that spawns and attacks if too much damage is dealt to the Marauders shield by you or by other enemies.  This enemy felt like it should have been a boss fight and for one of the stages it is, but then they just throw it in as a casual enemy in locations with several others in a wave spawn.  There was no reason for this other than to artificially create a difficulty that could have been obtained without this enemy and still felt fair and normal in the game.  At last, the story.  If you do not want any potential spoilers, please end your reading here.  TLDR of this, the story went off the rails like a freight train having a head on collision with another train.  Starting this game, I loved the story.  It seemed as though it was following up from Doom 2016.  There were a lot of questions such as who really are these priests, who are the Makyrs, what exactly are the sentinels, etc.  This game started explaining and answer these questions, you got to see how the Priests behaved, what had happened to the Sentinels homelands, even explained the downfall of the Sentinels.  The story was going great.  Then you get towards the end of the game and you have to rescue Hayden.  Here, the story shifts from an interesting story to “wtf, you threw out everything you just setup”.  Hayden seems to know everything that happened to Doom Guy.  He knows the machine that was used to give him incredible powers, he stole Father to make Vega, he knows the prophecies of the Makyrs from all I can see and find in game were never wrote down or shared with the Sentinels or Demons.  Everything in this game points to him being the rogue Makyr that created Doom Guy, but yet we know from everything in Doom 2016, Hayden was born a human, made the robot suit which others helped work on, and transferred himself into it so he could be a deadly disease.  How is in Doom Eternal this robot is now something that no one has ever seen the technology for and they cannot access it? There are so many questions here that I can’t even begin listing them all as it makes so many contradictions to the Doom 2016 and most of the Doom Eternal storyline when it gets to the end.  Maybe if there was something more clean to this I wouldn’t have issues as I do with the story and all problems would be solely with the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Nah Nah Nah. I'm telling you right now that DOOM: Eternal is by far a sequel done right and pumped up by 1000x notches. You thought DOOM (2016) was great? Well, then you haven't played DOOM: Eternal yet. All these people complaining about how the game is no longer DOOM or how they are forced to play a certain style have literally no idea what they are talking about and are just chatting nonsense. Because Eternal does everything that DOOM (2016) did right and increases it. You get new demons to fight. You get MORE demons to fight. You get new weapons and killing machines to play with. You get a classic DOOM experience in modern gameplay.  DOOM: Eternal is set two years after the events of DOOM. (2016) The armies of Hell had begun their conquest of Earth and are slowly overruning Earth's Military powers. On the first day, 60% of the human population had been wiped out. The UAC from the previous game has now become a technological cult that worships the powers of Hell. (Traitors to mankind) But unknowingly to them. The DOOM Slayer has been watching from his flying fortress in outer space, he is now ready to kill some old and new demons once again. ● Stunning graphics● Steam Achievements● Steam trading cards● Collectibles and Secrets● Very well optimized ● Gameplay on crack ● New demons ● Classic Demon design ● More brutal glory kills ● Impressive gore ● Classic weapon design ● Plentiful of gameplay options ● Super Shotgun improvement ● More chainsaw action ● More demons per encounter ● Master levels ● Arch-Vile solid spawns ● Shotgun ammo ● Steam overlay ● Soundtrack If you're looking for an action-packed game that will get your testosterone up and running then this is the game for you. I see a lot of people complaining about how the game forces you to play a certain style but honestly it doesn't. A common complaint was that you need certain weapons to kill certain enemies. The shielded enemy for an example. That was also a thing in DOOM. (2016) You can easily use a single weapon throughout the entire game. You're not forced to use weapons you don't want. The same applies to the glory kills, shoulder-mounted flamethrower, and grenade launcher. They are all optional. People say that the game is slower. I got no idea what they are smoking. Eternal is 10x faster than DOOM (2016) with the addition of all of the new movement fluidity options. Some people will say the game is harder and it might be at first but once you start using everything given to you. You will feel like a God. The DOOM Hunter? More like a waste of metal. The Mauruder? What a p*ssy, he drops faster than the Greek economy. This is a sequel done right by passionate developers. Buy it now and feel what it is like to be the DOOM Slayer!

_childDocuments_.review: - Sly_Tater (me)DOOM (2016) when it was released showcased some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing visuals. DOOM Eternal turns that up to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 11. Ever single level has it's own unique look. The skyboxes are worthy of gawking at. The lighting is incredible. The textures are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ orgasmic. Overall amazing visuals if your PC can push it.  Nothing short of fantastic. I have not dipped below 100fps on my RTX 2060 and i5 9400f.DOOM has never been about the story. But DOOM Eternal comes in with a pretty damn good one. The plot has no contradictions, it's interesting and overall offers alot to people interested in the overarching lore of DOOM. Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥. The best part of DOOM Eternal. You feel like a force of nature. Each mechanic balanced working off of each-other. The parkour is surprisingly good and offers well needed down time between areas. The boss fights are very fun and rewarding to complete. The guns feel hefty, you feel like you are wielding powerful tools of destruction.  The level design is incredible. Nothing short of incredible. The pacing is quick but not to quick. Parkour and light-puzzle sections offer needed downtime between areas. Enemy placement was fantastic. The visuals as touched on earlier are fantastic. Your slayers abilities (grenade, flamethrower, freeze grenade, crucible, chainsaw) are all important and I found myself using all of them during combat. Also ammo is drastically lower in your weapons than DOOM (2016) meaning you'll need to pay more attention to ammo.The enemy design is quite amazing. I know people are complaining about the Marauder enemy type. I can see why. They are annoying as ♥♥♥♥ and difficult to beat. I understand their position in the enemy roster though. Aside from the controversial Marauder all the other standard enemies are quite easy to beat alone, but when buffed or thrown in herds at you present a fair challenge. They also have weak areas which your slayer can target. The bosses are all amazing. Each boss fight has it's own little dynamic. The soundtrack by Mick Gordon is amazing. It follows the player just like in the 2016 DOOM. The soundtrack on it's own is even still incredible. It goes hand in hand with the gameplay and assists the fast paced feeling of the gameplay.The sound design is good. The gunshots sound hefty and weight. Enemy attack ques are noticeable. It's good, not what I would call amazing though. Overall DOOM Eternal is one of the best FPS games I have played at all. It does have a controversial enemy and sometimes it can get cluttered with all the mechanics to keep track of. But as a final verdict, I give DOOM Eternal a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing shooter in its own right. There's one thing that defines whether you're gonna like it or not - if combat flow, dance, rhythm clicks for you, if you and the game speak the same language - you won't go back to 2016, it will seem too boring. Eternal is very intense, fast, agile and most importantly - responsive. When you need something, there are ways to get what you need and they consistently and reliably work. All resources are there, you only have to manage them.You know how the first thing many people jump to criticize this game for is low ammo reserves? Low ammo is there so you don't forget you have 8 weapons (9 if you count Unmaykr) and don't try beating the game with only the supershotgun. You also find most of the weapons in first 3 maps, and while on first you have only two, game teaches you to always use chainsaw and not waste ammo on wrong targets. There's an "unmodded run" achievement to complete the game with 1 upgrade (health or armor or ammo) and 1 suit token and I've beaten it with only armor and fast weapon swap on Ultra-Violence. Trust me, there's enough ammo if you shoot all weapons at once.Never stop thinking, keep moving, shoot at peak of reflexes, be always aware of surroundings. And always chainsaw the last guy in the room (can't believe how useful this advice is).One last thought: the soundtrack is perfect. It sounds awesome and badass, and has so many references to older Doom OSTs that newcomers will enjoy it and oldfa(n)s will cry tears of joy, hearing Sinister, Dark Halls, Sign of Evil, Into Sandy's City, Opening to Hell (Icon of Sin) and even Doom 3 Intro. Also listening to how Mick Gordon speaks about his work in Doom 2016 and Eternal, makes you notice little details like that chainsaw in Hellwalker and that lawn mower in The Only Thing They Fear Is You. Just wow.

The gameplay, consisting of fast action with many different weapons, mechanics and enemies, is one of the smoothest i have ever played in an egoshooter. They also hit the perfect sweetspot between brutal modern reality and arcade-style shooter like Doom 1 and 2. I especially had fun with the many unlockable weapon mods, challenges, cheats and soundtracks which felt like a few thousands! Only the story leaves a bit to be desired, but lets be honest, who plays Doom for the story anyway? :D Still, the backgroundstory and anecdotes we got fill the great world of the "new" Doom universe really well.The multiplayer is way better than the Quakecopy from the 2016 franchise release as it's build around a new "one Slayer vs. two Demons" gamemode, which works quite well. Yet is still recommend this game exclusively for the great singleplayer!9/10

Everything is just so well balanced and the experience overall is just unlike any other shooter you will play.I've been seeing a lot of people complaining about the lack of ammo and my answer to that is very simple. USE. THE. CHAINSAW. And if you are playing on Ultra Violence or Nightmare you need to be aware of what demons are in the fight and what weapons can weaken them and using he various ways you can traverse the environments can get the upper hand in a fight! The challenge is something I absolutely love! It keeps you on your toes. For the more casual player theres nothing wrong with playing it on a slightly lower difficulty and slowly working your way up? And the boss fights are just out of this world! I really hope the DLC's that are being released to us will have fights that are just as if not even more challenging than what I had to face.The Story isn't anything amazing but I'm so glad they attempted to add context and reason behind the Doom Slayers intentions. And diving into his past and hearing the stories and reading the journals was fasinating and I hope for the DLC's and maybe even a 3rd game they further add to it.Although I have ran into a few minor bugs here theres nothing gamebreaking at all. The experience from start to finish was nothing but incredible.Optimization is for the most part top notch. plenty of graphics options to play around with. Running everything on High-Ultra keeping above 60fps on my RTX 2060 Super. However some moments the fps did dip under a little bit but I barely noticed it as I was so immersed.Changing the HUD colors to suit you was such a nice addition especially as I am someone who didn't really like the color scheme of the new HUD.Battlemode is surprisingly a very solid and fun mode and I really hope they continue to develop and expand upon it.To wrap this review up like I stated at the beginning. This game is certainly the greatest shooter I have played. It delivers on its high intensity gameplay, its smart and fun level design helps the game flow so perfectly. and the sound design and music is something that other developers only dream of accomplishing. I honestly believe this game exceeds expectations and more10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 4.5/5Doom Eternal improves upon it's predecessor in almost every way. Plays even faster, every gun is amazing, more demons, bigger levels and another excellent soundtrack from Mick Gordon. Doom Eternal has a much bigger emphasis on resource management than 2016, with a bunch of new mechanics that ensure the player will always have ways of restocking their health, armour and ammo. Demons are much stronger and more aggressive, and the game does not hold back in throwing every type possible at you in its various combat arenas. All your weapons have different strengths and weaknesses against the various enemies in the game requiring you to constantly swap between your various guns and mods in order to effectively take out tougher enemies. All of this adds to a much faster, more refined and at times more punishing game than Doom 2016.Pros:+ New mechanics like the dash, blood punch, flame belch, ice grenade and meathook add so much depth and strategy to the games combat.+ Plenty of weapon variety, every weapon is effective and unique from each other. + Levels are bigger and have plenty of collectables and secret combat encounters.+ Narrative is by no means superbly written, it is Doom after all, but it is still a very entertaining, dumb, b-movie style adventure.Cons:- Multiplayer isn't bad, but it's certainly mediocre. Currently the only gametype is 'Battlemode' which pits two player controlled demons against a fully armed slayer. It can get rather boring after a while, and matches often boil down to either the slayer being insanely good and wiping out the demons, or the complete opposite with the demons tearing the slayer apart in no time at all. Multiplayer in general is just lacking in content with only Battlemode at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game is alright, but you have to let go of thinking that this is more of Doom 2016, and accept that you have to play it the way developers want you to.So the previous point still stands, this game seems to be built to frustrate the hell out of you.Here is how this manifests:-- Control is rather frequently taken from you, I'm talking mostly about cutscenes like "hey, look at this door that just opened", but arguably glory kills (and you have to do them a lot) also take away control for a couple of seconds-- There are a LOT of invisible walls. This is compounded by the heavy focus on platforming, putting the game in the uncomfortable territory of "we want you to explore and do cool stuff, but don't  you dare stray off the beaten path". And if you misjudge whether an area is real or decorative, you will fall down and lose some hp-- As a mix of the previous two points, there are areas covered in the purple sludge which blocks your jumping and dashing. I have no idea how they came up with this in a game heavily focused on the movement-- You will be constantly running out of ammo. Max capacity of shotgun is 24 (down from 60 in D16), max BFG ammo is 2 (down from 3). This is offset by chainsaw having a mixed cooldown/charge system, meaning that you will always be able to get ammo as long as you don't die-- Enemies  spawn behind your back and  ready their shots to hit you right as you exit a glory kill animation. All the time. And even the cannon fodder does substantial damage-- I was super skeptical about people who said "dude this is way too colorful, this isn't doom" before release, but I have to admit, they did go overboard. I think it would look great when playing on console with a screen two meters away, but when all this color and explosions are right in front of your eyes, it really wears you down. I got a headache by the time the second level was doneNow, why would you ever play this game (or update the review, for that matter)? Well, because not everything is so dire. If the aforementioned flaws are a dealbreaker for you, then don't bother. However, if you can live with them, here is the other side of the coin:-- Visuals are good. Detailed environments. Demon damage system (with chunks flying off the demons when you shoot them). Skyboxes are neat. There are actually different environments instead of "well there is a factory and there is hell"-- Performance is ridiculous. I do get some drops on 1440p, but it's kind of expected even from a very performant game. Load times are stupidly fast, in general a load takes 3-5 seconds (on an NVMe SSD)-- The combat is . If you are looking for a fast FPS, this is THE game to play. When you "get" how it is supposed to work (which includes giving up playing it the way you played the previous game) everything becomes much more fun-- There is more content. More monsters, more bosses, more levels, more collectibles. There is less multiplayer, though. Most people don't care, but I liked it :(In other words, it is a nice game. It's just not a direct continuation of the previous game, and that really skewed my first impressions. They shifted focus to some things that were not front and center (glory kills and chainsaw), and whether it's a good thing or not, you will have to decide for yourself.And as my final trick, I will quickly go over the "neutral" things, which are just kinda meh:-- With the heavy emphasis on the weapon switching (because you always have no ammo) default keybindings don't do the job. You can't constantly reach for "7" and then back for "1" without compromising your movement-- The story is hot garbage. The game doesn't even start where the previous game left off for god's sake. And they decided to go full speed on cheese, and I'm not a very big fan. But to each their own-- Pretty much the only way to play, esp. on higher difficulties, is the way Mr. Martin intended, there is no real room for different playstyles-- Level design in general is kinda hit and miss. The levels look nice, but they went heavily into the "gamey" territory (they did say that it was the goal to be fair), and you will always be reminded that you are in a theme park with random monkey bars and jump pads scattered around. They also went with the "shortcuts that loop back to the same area" approach, and this is great, but with the abundance of secrets you will always doubt whether you should move on and will organically get to a secret later, or whether you need to comb the area in search of a little switch-- I will beat the dead horse and mention the Marauder here. In the game where you have to go fast and rip through demons, having to wait for an enemy to attack you, because he is invulnerable at any other time, is unbelievably dumb. This mechanic would suit a boss encounter, but not a regular enemy. And if you manage to single him out by clearing the area, he will just summon his stupid dog which will bit you in the ass relentlesslyThank you for reading. I hope that you found this review useful.

But you'll have to sweat for them, learn the weakpoints of the ennemies to save ammunition, spread your fingers as far as you can for that quick emergency button that is the BFG, understand that it's ok to rush into several imps to a quick rumble of chainsaw to refresh your life, armor and capacity to kill the bigger ones on your tail.There's always a lot going on onto the screen, but it's above all very easy to understand. _childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr I think it's an evolution upon DOOM 2016 on most of the aspects, and overall an amazingly entertaining game.I waited to finish the game once before posting this, so I can be as fair as possible with ID Software's work. Every game mechanic was required in order to rip and tear properly, but I feel the gunplay has reached an optimized flow on all the difficulties - my run was on ultra-violence and it felt challenging but still fun.I find it more fun, more violent, more aggressive and more polished than the previous installment. The level design is opened and enlarged, the environments are beautiful. The music is as good as our headphones allow. The story is much developed and I found myself interested in the lore codex. The mechanics may require attention at first but you will find you need every bit of armor and ammo you can muster :) The animations are smooth and fast, even the wall grab feels good. Mobility has been upgraded via double dash combined with double jump, dash recharge, swings and even a meat hook!Doom Eternal allows for aggressive or passive style of gameplay, since every gun has 2 different upgrade paths and a mastery perk. There are a lot of secrets throughout the game; you will find some personal customization in your homebase and even an old school PC :)P.S. I am glad to see the continued support in content, from the dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: What blows me away is that the game starts with story exposition right off the bat. The last one made it very clear from the onset that it was a game first and dealt with story with indifference. If you wanted to, you could stand by and listen or just plow right thru with glee as you painted the walls with demon. Now, however, it makes the point that there's a story to this world. Which again is perfectly valid, but instead of feeling optional the game makes it clear that it's now an integral piece to the experience.Fine! I can deal with that, no problem. At least it wouldn't be if the pacing didn't feel like it suffered from both it and other issues. The entire tutorial level uses every bit of bad game design to halt you in your tracks, which is ironic in a game with no walk, sprint, or reload buttons.Now, maybe I just suck but I felt like I ran out of ammo an infuriating amount of times while murdering demons. Part of me suspects it's because the game starts you off with just a shotgun, which I immediately started using on everything including the really basic shuffling enemies. Like the previous game, there are ammo boxes laid out across the levels, but your main refill comes from using the chainsaw. And when you're completely empty, the game automatically switches you to it, without warning.It's fun to get those up close kill animations as you slice a demon in half, that is if you have the fuel to do so. Regular enemies take one fuel but the larger enemies –that the game throws at you from the start– take all your fuel. I can deal with the paltry amount of ammo the game gives for each chainsaw kill a sit adds to the strategy of the game loop, the bigger the enemy the more ammo you get. But it's incredibly jarring to run out of ammo and then instantly teleport to 15 feet away. Even more odd is that my decision to run past those shuffling zombies instead of killing them comes down to the fact that they're immune to melee damage... They should drop with one punch, two tops! You can leave them alive as it seems they still don't count towards progressing to the next area. It's as if they were designed to just waste your ammo even quicker.Maybe it's just me, but there were a number of times that the level design felt somehow off. There were many times I'd go thru an area that had few enemies in it to suddenly an entire battle happening before me. And this stood out more when I got the first map download and saw that now there are areas that are discreetly marked as battle locations, even before you get to them. Sure, I could chalk them up to an in universe explanation that the random AI helper, VEGA, marked them ahead of time. But that doesn't stop it from feeling odd.In Doom, you knew that every area you went to was going to have enemies spawn all over the place, it was part of the fun. Often, more would spawn the further you progressed thru an area to always keep you on your toes. It made each encounter in each area feel carefully planned out by the developer to always keep a focus on the action. Likewise, the times where there weren't enemies in an area, served as breathers for you as you navigated around the world.In Doom Eternal, I just feel like I'm moving toward one direction, even if it occasionally snakes around itself. It's not like it shows me something I may have missed when I see the area I just came from, rather it confirms I've definitely moved forward.It all just serves to break the pacing that was established in the last game. Run forward, shoot, kill, repeat. Run forward shoot, melee kill, repeat. Now it's run forward, get halted by an on screen pop-up that tells you what to do, shoot, kill, run out of ammo, throw up from telekill, lose health while locked in kill animation, get a little of it back after the kill, repeat until you're out of ammo, you die, or everything else has stopped moving.To be clear, it's not as messy as that, there were many times where I could run around and clear an area the good ol' fashioned way. But the times where I got interrupted just seemed to persist. I don't need a hard cut to show me a door opening after I've cleared the enemies in an area. Especially not if there's an objective marker always on the screen! I don't need to be halted do the game can tell that the colored item I just picked up opens same colored door a few feet away from it.Sure, a lot of this could be forgiven and looked past as just standard player on-boarding. Eventually the game will drop the training wheels and let you go off to scrape your knuckles on your own. The game looks great and runs just as solid as the previous iteration. But that's where I think the heart of the problem stems from. This is a sequel to a fantastic game and it feels like many of the issues come from sequelitis. There's this feeling of an unquenchable desire from this game that it needs to be bigger and better than everything from the last one.I had hoped the game would take the approach of the last game and have a moment where it taunted you with new and complex mechanics before Doomguy gives it the finger and rushes off to stick his shotgun up a demon's butt. Instead it just keeps constantly stuffing your screen with objective markers and blips while pausing the momentum for some random cutscene or needless tutorial box.
