_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016’s reinvention of the franchise was a success story no was really expecting, reviving old school shooting mechanics with modern technology to create an intense and invigorating shooter. Doom Eternal expands on every aspect 2016 revitalised, bringing a bigger yet more refined shooter that excels in every category. Eternal is a textbook example of the ideal sequel, building upon all of the ideas its predecessor introduced without invalidating the experience of the original  game.The star of Eternal is its extremely fast and intense gunplay, creating a perfect sense of flow unmatched by most shooters. Eternal immediately emphasises movement, evidenced by dashing and very open environments littered with climbing equipment. Doom wants you moving at all times, which creates a constant chaotic tension as you need to route your way through environments while under attack to avoid death. Thankfully, the game also provides plenty of resources to help combat enemy threats. Plenty of lifeline equipment is available at all times to provide the player with health, armour, ammo or even just a quick escape from a hairy situation like the blood punch and ice grenades. This means mistakes aren’t overly punishing, as there's always a way to easily return to the fast paced shooting antics and their constant availability regardless of your equipped weapon makes them extremely useful throughout the game.The equipment systems work great with your impressive arsenal. All weapons return from 2016 but are improved with various new upgrades that are dotted out across the campaign, meaning you’re constantly finding new powers to play with and building a memorable experience as you slowly power up. Every weapon brings a unique joy to the table, and the limited ammo encourages constant experimentation as you are forced to switch up your playstyle. All of these elements make Eternal’s gameplay an absolute treat as you have to manage a constant barrage of offense and defence, forcing a frantic amount of energy from the player. Boss fights unfortunately stagger at times, usually becoming serviceable at best and tedious at their worst, but the larger demonic horde battles were endlessly enjoyable as Eternal trusts you with fighting more and more powerful groups of foes.It would’ve been nice to have more reasons to return to the game, master levels was a neat idea that hasn’t been played with enough and some extra mechanics like a ranking system would've been fun to play with. Eternal’s gunplay is refined to near perfection, with more than enough variety and potential experimentation provided, the game remains enjoyable for as long as you need it to be.Eternal’s fights can get very intense, so it’s great that quiet time is also handled superbly. Fights are broken up by traversing each level, giving the player time to hunt for secrets or just explore the environments, and what beautiful levels these are. 2016 focused on drab ruined facilities with the occasional dip into hell, which made for some awesome levels, but it could feel a tad repetitive. Thankfully, Eternal’s levels feel far more diverse, there's a huge variety in environments through colour and geography, as well as some amazing background detail that sells the scale of the demonic invasion.The secrets are really well implemented too, they’re just the right amount of hidden and the player is free to search for them uninterrupted. There’s important gameplay buffs found hidden in each level as well as challenge rooms to test the player, but I loved finding the secret collectables that take fun forms, such as the vinyl songs or floppy disk cheat codes. They play into a solid retro feel that Eternal braces, often paying homage to the old games with the classic health pickups and modern interpretations of classic enemies.Visually, Eternal is a treat. Environments and models are richly detailed, but it never takes a hit on performance, allowing the game to look and feel deadly without compromising on performance. Demon designs too are brilliantly detailed, all looking beautifully unique from another, but all maintain a deadly and threatening aura. The animations especially are finely crafted, glory kills are quick and brutal, which sells the power of the Doom Slayer without interrupting gameplay. Demon animations too, all have very clear sells of what attacks they’re about to use, conveying vital information to the player. Eternal stands as a good game with it’s shooting mechanics, but the outstanding quality of the world that surrounds the combat is what makes the game greatDoom’s never needed a story to justify rampaging across hell, but I really appreciate the extra effort these modern entries take into crafting one, even if it doesn’t always pay off. The delivery of the story really synergises with Doomguy’s attitude within the narrative, Cutscenes are brief and always get to the point immediately. You can ignore the story as much as he does and just be treated to cutscenes that are crafted with such care, the voice acting and writing resulting in many memorable lines.Yet for those who want to get invested, the expansion of Doom’s world feels pretty well crafted. It’s nothing revolutionary, embracing a classic good vs evil narrative, but it does an amazing job of setting up massive stakes against you. There’s plenty of codex pages to flesh out the world and learn more about each new interaction that seemingly appears from nowhere, but there’s also a lot of fun found in embracing Doomguy’s role as revenge-ridden rampager. I don’t think I’ve ever seen a silent protagonist justified so well, it's always cool seeing exposition or villainous plotting being rebutted  with a cold glare and a shotgun ♥♥♥♥.However there are times where I think the plot can get too detailed. I think a lot of Doom didn’t need to be justified, it’s why Doomguy is so fun to embrace as a protagonist, but Eternal feels insistent on telling more than it should. While I like the introduction of the Makyrs and Night Sentinels, I feel like at times we delved far too deep into them, making the factions just seem a tad generic at times. The worst example is Other elements of the plot set up in the previous game also feel completely ignored. I wish we’d gotten to focus on humans a bit more in this entry, 2016 had a good dynamic with how Hell’s Argent Energy was being used by humans and placing them in danger, but they’ve mostly just taken a back seat in the conflict this time. Samuel Hayden particularly, was such a disappointment. He was such a  great opposition for the player in 2016, being set up fantastically, so to end as such a useless expository character was a real shame. Eternal’s story still allows for plenty of good moments, but I think it could’ve been taken further in keeping the world consistent from 2016.Doom Eternal is an incredible FPS that does an outstanding job dedicating itself to a particular style by refining every element of the game. It’s absolutely worth playing if you want to enjoy a shooter that pushes the boundaries, but more than that, it’s just really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal is good. But I was expecting it to surpass DOOM 2016, and in that regard, I've been disappointed.In the first 30 seconds of DOOM 2016, you are already fighting enemies. In the first 30 seconds of DOOM Eternal, you get interrupted by a modal pop-up window, which then teleports you to a tutorial gray-box room.Eternal isn't a bad game. It's nice! But DOOM 2016 was such a masterpiece that anything less than that was going to seem weak in comparison. 2016 didn't just know which notes to play; it hit them perfectly. Eternal is more of a loud cacophony. There's a lot more of everything, but it's not all good.The foundations of 2016's gameplay are back, but there are a lot of systems slapped on top. I think it's meant to add tactical depth or choices or something along those lines, but it feels more like a cumbersome layer of micro-management. DOOM 2016 got you into this great "flow state", but Eternal is more like "don't forget about all those different ability cooldowns and those weak spots you need to use!" It feels a lot more exhausting and overwhelming than in the first game. And the way it rail-roads you into these new systems feels cheap; for example, it forces you to use all your weapons by placing severe restrictions on ammo capacity. (You start with a maximum of 15 shotgun shells! 15!)Some of the other gameplay changes feel like big steps backwards on 2016's design. You move slower now, but you have two dashes. So that you could have air dashes for platforming section. I don't like how the tradeoff feels.I'm also not a huge fan of the hub level. I could take it or leave it. It makes the campaign feel much less like a cohesive journey.The new user interface is cluttered, has a frankly terrible color scheme (the alternative ones aren't that much better), and it feels much less well-organized. The new font should've really been a buttons-only or headings-only thing. Why would you write so much neat codex text to then put it under this very unpleasant-to-read font? Seriously, compare the codex in 2016 to the new one. It's day and night. Don't fix what ain't broken.There's a lot of story that comes out of left field in Eternal. It doesn't feel like there's continuity with the ending of the first game. I like the cutscenes, but I wish I didn't spend 80% of my time watching them confused, thinking, "wait, did we see this in the first game? I don't remember something about the King of whatever, or some Sentinels?" 2016 knew exactly what to tell, how to tell it, and just how much to say to strike the right balance between conveying information, how many blanks the player should be left for the player to fill, and how much time the narrative segments should take. Eternal makes me feel like that one time I tried to play Destiny II (that is to say, it's more about sounding cool than clear). A lot of things feel very arcade-y. Weapons and items are now floating pickups instead of being elements grounded into the world. (In 2016, you picked keycards off of the necks of dead UAC staff.) The map tells you about combat encounters ahead of time. You get reminded of "weekly challenges" (?!?) meta-progression stuff in the campaign. I know this doesn't matter to some people, but to me, it feels immersion-breaking. With this and the modal pop-up tutorials that teleport you to a bland gray-box room, it's like the game doesn't care about the atmosphere it's trying to establish.I would also like to add that I've had no issues with performance, and I like all the new places and visual direction stuff. Again, I know it all sounds really negative, but I still am enjoying my time with the game. It's just that it's really disappointing compared to how perfect the first game was. Where DOOM 2016 showed us what it found lackluster in other FPS games, Eternal can sometimes feel like it became the thing it despised.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a typical shooter. It deviates from the norm even more than doom 2016 did, but it's an excellent game nonetheless. Feels almost like a character action game like that of Devil May Cry or Metal Gear Rising, in that you have so many unique weapons and abilities and actual mastery of the game comes from understanding and being able to weave between them at a moments notice.EDIT: Game completed, and I think my favourite thing from it all was the set pieces and level design it had me run through. Lots of tiny secrets here and there. There's some set up for the DLC story campaigns which is kind of disappointing, I was hoping they'd be proper optional content as opposed to potentially extremely important story details, but we'll have to wait and see on that front. The game definitely gets easier at the halfway mark, and its lowest points are those first few levels where you don't quite know how to stay in the gameplay loop. Just remember, the Chainsaw button refills at least 1 pip all the time. Don't ever hang onto that pip unless you're intentionally collecting fuel to one-shot a heavy demon. It's a free ammo button. USE IT.

_childDocuments_.review: I think that this game is one of, if not the best shooter ever made. After mastering the game and beating it a bunch of times in UN (Ultra Nightmare) I'm confident enough to write this review. First of all, the demons are going to kill you if you're not careful, they are deadly and smart but weakpoints can help deal with them, even if some people think it's mandatory to use weakpoints, in reality you can just skip over them and just kill the demons by shooting any gun at them.It runs like a dream, this is one of the best optimized games I've seen in a while and even with my PC (which is not too good but not too bad) downloading a file and Google Chrome open with the game running at a stable 60+ fps (I lower res to get 100+ but if I put it at 1080p it still runs really good).This game also pushes you to use every single thing in your arsenal, all of the things you have are useful in some way and it allows for you to use any playstyle and play at your rythm. I even did the last 2 missions with only the plasma rifle and nothing else.Chainsaw is a complaint I hear a lot, and although I think it's fine as is, if you don't like it, it could get tiring. I just look at it as a reload animation like in any other shooter, just that it requieres a fodder demon and 1 chainsaw fuel tank which recharges really fast. And if you're smart enough with your ammo management, you can save 3 tanks of fuel to 1 shot any heavy demon which could be giving you a lot of trouble at the moment.Quickswapping is something that is not completely necessary to play, but makes things much more fun and easier, the only exception to this would be Master Levels which are just amped up campaign levels to 11 and do requiere you to quickswap in higher dificulties (if you want to kill demons at a reasonable pace).The game is so fast paced that a lot of people at first might not understand what's even happening, but when you get the hang of it, you can't go to any other shooter without feeling like it's so slow and even boring sometimes, including Doom 2016 for me which shocked me because that game had been my favorite game for 2 years before Doom Eternal came out.Platforming is smooth and responsive, if you learn the meathook and ballista boosting, it becomes so much fun to swing around the levels and it's a pretty nice breaker between combat.Game is so replayable, I always go back to it and replay the same levels and try new things and it never gets old (Although more content would be nice).There's not official mod support but you can go to the Doom modding discord and download some mods to give the game a bit more of life.Story can be nice but if you don't like it you can skip it and not read any codex entry which is a nice way to handle it tbh.The negatives I can think of are these:If you don't like the chainsaw animations or using it you probably won't like this game because you need to chainsaw pretty often.Levels can be too hard for a first time playthrough because of how much the game demands for you to use all of your tools (this is more so the case for TAG 1 and 2).Platforming and puzzles can be a big negative if you don't like it because they're in between almost all arenas of the game either one or the other and sometimes both.When you master the game it can go from too hard to pretty easy, because you're using every tool and demon's proyectiles are a bit too slow for some, eventually you can dodge a lot of attacks and regain too much health too quickly. And if you're downloading mods like I do, you can find that in some hard mods the game goes from easy to unfairly hard, which makes it impossible for good players to find a good challenge that is not completely unfair. This however, doesn't contradict what I said about the demons, because they are smart and deadly but some of them don't deal enough damage or the proyectiles are a bit too slow and the damage they manage to deal is cancelled by how easy it is to regain health if you're glory killing and using flame belch/mastered SSG. This could be improved if some of the demons had faster proyectiles and a bit more damage or if they added a way to change damage, proyectile speed and health drop multipliers when you're replaying a level.The multiplayer doesn't feel as good to play as the campaign, because there's no air mobility for either the slayer or the demons so meathooking off a fodder actually feels punishing sometimes because I then fly in a trayectory that I don't control and I might end up in a worse spot from where I'm running away because of the lack of control (same with the demons). Although this only applies to multiplayer so if you don't care about that it won't be a big deal.Overall I think this game is amazing and I'll be replaying it for a long time, specially with the 2 new master levels and horde mode on the way, even with some of it's flaws, I think that this is the best shooter I've ever played. I'll be looking forward for the next game ID software makes and specially, for the sequel of this masterpiece of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: THEY REMOVED DENUVO FOR SINGLE PLAYER!  This is a huge win and solidifies Doom Eternal as GotY in my eyes - but it's worth remembering mistakes.  Forgive but don't forget and all that, so for posterity I leave this rather scathing review up to serve as a reminder that anti-consumer behaviour should not and will not be tolerated by many players.  Having said that, thank you iD for an incredible game that I will look back on for years as an defining moment in my history with gaming.This game was GotY material in my eyes, and judged as a piece of art it still is.  But with Denuvo DRM tacked on in a hasty post-launch update with the intention of sneaking it by the community past the window in which they can refund it is quite possibly one of the most blatantly scummy, money-grabbing, anti-consumer moves I have seen in a very, very long time.  That goes without mentioning the fact that it tanks performance on a vast percentage of users systems, crashes the entire computer on others and in the case of Linux breaks compatibility almost entirely.  I will be testing it on Linux in the coming days and if it crashes I will be attempting a refund - note "attempting" because of the disgusting practice of pushing it on us post launch when everyone has sunk hours into it already.  If there's another group that I feel sorry for, its the developers.  To see something they spent years pouring their heart and soul into being slammed by the very people they made it for is, without doubt, absolutely crushing.  But simply put we as consumers we can't allow this behaviour to continue.  Denuvo is objectively terrible - and as a multi-billion pound industry there either needs to be a better solution or the suits need to take note of games like the Witcher 3 that operated on a trust system and saw very little piracy.  I don't buy games often (nor do I pirate them) because I can't afford to so when I spend £50 on a game it's because I can see myself getting hours of enjoyment out of it, but, if this is what happens when you pay for something, I don't blame consumers for going the route of piracy instead.  Forcing Denuvo on people will only increase rates of piracy and spur the creation of tools to facilitate it further.  To the people who forced this through - I implore you to reverse it before the damage is permanent and the image of DOOM is marred in the eyes of its fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great game.Eternal keeps what worked in 2016 and expands it, and sheds what didn't (which was nothing really).The enemy variety is on par with this games basis - Doom 2. Joining the existing ranks of demons from the first reboot, Eternal brings in Pain Elementals, Dreadknights, Cyberdemons (Tyrants), Arachnotrons and everyone's favorite - damned Archviles. If that weren't enough, the sequel also adds in some  unique enemies - Doom Hunters, Cueballs, Marauders, Gargoyles, Prowlers (which were only in multiplayer before). Most of them maintain their iconic appearances from the early 90s, as well  as the same behaviors. Demon infighting is back, too. You will frequently find demons fighting each other, from the beginning to the end."A Ballet with Bullets" or "Chess" are both great descriptors of the combat flow in Eternal. Every arena is a meticulously crafted playground with monkeybars, crucial item pickups and jump-boost placements. Each fight feels rewarding and makes you feel good for knowing which weapons and weapon modes, which runes, which mechanics to use when and how to use them best. Mick Gordon's Eternal soundtrack is much more nuanced than the 2016 soundtrack and contains many, many throwbacks not just to Doom 1 and Doom 2, but also other games from id, before and after Zenimax acquired them - like Quake, Quake 2, Quake 3, Commander Keen, Prey, Rage, Wolfenstein and more. Have no fear, BFG Division is included and plays at the best time.Surprisingly enough, the story in Doom Eternal is much better  and expanded upon compared to the first reboot, too. A lot of plot details are overlooked but are eventually explained out of order, so by the end of the game the story is actually far better than expected. I really was not a huge fan of Doom 2016 but I can't recommend Eternal enough, it is a fine game. The multiplayer is absolute, unbalanced trash though - I wouldn't play it. Ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, now that I finished my (mostly blind) Nightmare run, I think a review is in order. Overall, I'd give this game a solid 8/10. Very good and far-far above average which modern gaming industry likes to produce. It is, however, a somewhat cautious thumbs-up for other players because there are a few rough edges which are, as they say, an acquired taste so to speak. Some might like them, and others will probably hate them.One thing is for sure, however. Higher difficulties sure bring out all the flaws to the front and make them way more apparent since you have to closely interact with the game mechanics provided. Doom Eternal stood up to the test IMO but not without a few hitches.The good stuff:- Moving and shooting is fun. You get plenty of mobility and places to use it to your advantage. Grapling hook on SSG brings out some interesting ways of playing.- Extremely solid core mechanics. The way you and enemies interact is mostly crisp and clear. There seems to be sort of "healthgate" at roughly 5HP though. Probably to give you a fighting chance after an unlucky hit.- Agressive monsters with a wide variety of attacks and weaknesses for you to learn and exploit.- Guns are decent. With the exception of heavy cannon (assault rifle) which feels odd and plasmagun which is a pale shadow of its classic self, but it breaks shields.- Very good graphics. The environments are varied like never before and are sure pretty to look at. The enemy visuals are done just right IMO. They even suffer visible damage as you shoot them which is quite a novelty.- Runs smoothly on high even while streaming on my GTX1080.- Mostly great music. A few tracks seem to be repetetive though and dead-set on pounding your skull into a headache. Take it from a person who actually enjoys a very big chunk of different types of metal music. But overall, it's enjoyable and fitting.- Reasonable load times.- Quick travel system at the end of the level which allows you to grab everything you might've missed. A very sweet QoL.- You can replay any mission you've cleared previously with all of your current upgrades and weapons. There is also a "master" variation for every level.The neutral stuff. As in the "Didn't hate it. Didn't like it. Wouldn't miss it if it was gone/changed but you should be aware of them" category:- Platforming. Platforming for days. Certain people hate it quite a lot. Obvious inspirations from Mario games with those spinning flame chains are obvious.- Way-way more arcadey than Doom 4 (2016). Weapons you find are now floating glowing models instead of being proper part of the scenery, not unlike in Quake 3. Secrets are now just floating glowing question marks or paper sheets.- The story. Was never the point of Doom games. The lore is okay and doesn't detract from the experience.- Third-person cutscenes.- Getting out of the dev-established game loop will likely result in you having a bad time.- Some glory kill animations are eh. "Not great, not terrible."- Flamethrower. Makes enemies drop armor for some reason. *Shrug*- Two types of grenade you can use are fine. But why do we need a button to switch grenade types when only two of them even exist in the first place? Shouldn't it be just 2 keys for 2 grenade types?- Marauders. Fun enemies on paper. Kinda pushovers once you learn how they work. They feel like they belong to a different game though.- Checkpoints (and 1-ups) instead of hard saves and quicksave/quickload. I'm just old.- Ammo confetti on each chainsaw kill. 2016 at least had the decency to make them all orange instead of the rainbow-gasm. Yes, you can reduce their brightness. No, it doesn't help. Why can't they directly transfer ammo to your inventory on chainsaw kill and skip the multi-color mess is beyond me.- Final boss. Just meh. Looks very imposing, I'll give it that. Attacks are reasonably telegraphed. Killed me through walls in an unclear way a couple of times. It also walked around and attacked me for about 20-30 seconds after I killed it making me wonder if there was something else I needed to do. Nope. Just script bugs.- Progression mechanics. They are here. They are complex. And I have no strong feelings about their existence one way or another. They are ok I guess.- Tons of tools on cooldowns. Feems more like an MMO or a MOBA mechanic rather than a shooter. Kinda nice to have them but they tend to fall victim to being forgotten about ever now and then.- Level design works. It's very linear and arcadey, and secrets are barely secret but it works.- Skins, XP, online components and other bells and whistles. They exist. Yay?The bad and the ugly. Unfortunately.- Bugz. Not a lot but still a quite few, including enemies not spawning at the arena forcing me to restart the checkpoint. Or pain elementals just having AI issues with their lost souls.- Ammo economy is screwed seven days from Sunday. Infinite free refills on cooldown combined with infinitely respawning low fodder beg the question of why on-map pick-ups even exist. On the other hand, the ammo pool you can carry is very-very low (and I mean it) which forces you to break the engagement and look for fodder to chainsaw.- Glory kills, chainsaw kills and such are basically mandatory if you want to stay alive. No simple run and gun here. At least demons would politely wait until you are done with your glory kill / chainsaw animation. How nice of them.- Directly tied to the adove, those same-y chainsaw animations got old pretty damn fast. You are gonna be seeing them a lot and they feel a little uninspired both for the small and big guys.- Some of the damage zones don't match up with their visual representation. Mostly the problem of flamethrower weapons and "the floor is now lava" attacks. Sometimes you can be inside the flame and take no DMG. Sometimes you take DMG without touching anything you shouldn't be touching. Weird.- The purple goop slowing you down to a crawl and preventing jumping/dashing. Urgh.- Doom 4 had many unique death animations for the player depending on what killed them. Here, you either fall over in a generic way or explode into gibs.- Talking Doomguy in the flashbacks is quoting those cringe-inducing comics from the 90s. Plz no.- Botched quick melee. You saw that cool wrist blade you have now? Well, it's only for glory kills. Your punches can break walls, send 3x3x3m metal cubes sliding for dozens of meters and flip over several tons heavy objects but they wouldn't hurt even a basic zombie unless you have a special "magic" punch charged up.Stuff I haven't touched:- Multiplayer. There is only one variation of it - battlemode. 2 demons vs 1 doomguy. Some people say it's unbalanced. Idk.So, do I recommend Doom Eternal? Of course. It's fun, it's fast and it gives you a good shot of adrenaline. Wouldn't call it better than Doom 4 but certainly not worse either. It's different. Those changes, however, might drive away some of 2016 fans as well as ones who prefer classics. And to those of you who liked Doom 3, Eternal is almost a polar opposite of that. So take it as you wish.But is Doom Eternal as perfect as some claim? Not really. The flaws are there, and to ignore them would be a disservice to the future Doom games. Because of course they'll make more, duh. And I'll be looking forward to play them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's painful to not be able to recommend this game. Certainly the shooting demons is fun. That's the best part of the game, and it's a decent chunk of it. Everything around it, though, was painful to the point of overwhelming frustration. Exploration is linear with a coat of non-linear paint thrown overtop, and the level geometry is occasionally confusing in a way that leaves you sitting around feeling as though you've missed a giant obvious arrow that should be pointing you in the correct direction. All of the secrets felt like "finally, I found where they wanted me to go" instead of "oh boy I found something cool exploring on my own". And by the end of the game none of the navigational 'challenges' were fun or interesting; just binary timing gates that didn't really amount to 'skill' as much as glorified quicktime events. The final two bosses are an uninspiring slog through bullet sponges, and the narrative is interesting in a vague way while never rewarding you with enough direct nostalgia or intrigue to string along a nuanced plot. Doomslayer/Doomguy can be funny, but he often isn't, and it's a bummer that the game doesn't seem to understand how to tell a good joke.Again: yes, shooting guys is fun. It is super fun. But whenever I go back to this game, I'm always infuriated by some random design oversight that's somehow significantly impacting my gameplay. If it's not a progress-halting bug that prevents an elevator from moving, it's a level unlocking fast-travel only to lock you into the end of the mission within several steps. Eventually running of cool things to give you and just dumping more tokens into the mix. Always blocking you with an invisible wall atop an otherwise climbable-looking piece of level geometry. Dead ends and ammo crates instead of cool secret paths. And maybe even too many guns; certainly more than a few I don't end up using by the end.I still think if you are absolutely in LOVE with shooters, especially so-called 'boomer shooters'/this brand of adrenaline-filled shooty shooty move-and-smashy, you should at least give this game a look; but for us, the experience went downhill two minutes into the first level when we realized the game was only going to let us explore in exactly the way it wanted and intended us to. And when it randomly teleported us to a test chamber for introducing the chainsaw instead of just letting us saw a dude. And... you know what, let's just stop.Doom: a Turtle is still kinda fun, but it also makes me mad. Rip & tear in pieces. </3

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal has a new dance, and many have voiced their dislikes. Players are pushed to fast weapon switch, as demons have weapon based weaknesses, and your ammo pool has grown scarce. I am reminded of Final Fantasy 8's draw system. Though many had concluded the concept was poorly designed, I can respect their bravery to try new things.In Doom Eternal's case, I love the new combat loop. ByteMe's speedrun had shown me the light. By the time of Eternal's release, I was already a weapon switcher, so the transition went smoothly. Flame Belch for armor, and Chainsaw for ammo. Once mastered, you have earned the right to enter a flow state that is ever so sweet.Many players despise being forced to use a certain weapon to nail a demon's weakspot. I find it a joy to use all of your resources. Plus, by mid-game, you can slay demons in other viable ways. With the Cacodemon, for instance, you can lob a Sticky Bomb in its mouth for the Glory Kill. Also, you can fire a single Arbalest for an even faster finish.Many demons now sport a fatal move. Again, with the Cacodemon, they can fire a projectile barrage that can end your Ultra Nightmare (1 life) run instantly. These demons have grown deadlier and more complex. Deeper chess pieces. More to study. New chances to earn your dominance.Next, your arsenal. Whoever invented the Meat Hook deserves a raise. Many weapons support multiple "verbs". The Flame Hook can be used for armor (when upgraded). It can also be deployed to approach a demon, for puzzles, to reposition yourself, or to gain an aerial advantage. How about the Heat Blast? Use it for crowd control, sure. But, with just one charge, you can also falter demons. Microwave Beam? Cook demons, or tap that beam to keep your foes stun locked.At first, I was concerned about the Energy Shield. "The Slayer would never hide behind cover!" Well, the shield means designers can put you in spots that ought to be deemed unfair. Cornered by demons? Pop up the shield and escape. You can also dash into demons with that shield, causing them to falter. Or, pull the shield up, then safely Blood Punch a demon.The demons and your arsenal are multi-layered. How will you juggle these elements to secure victory? This is your freedom. Express your style. Your way of slaying.Is the combat dance perfect? At the time of writing, no. Chainsaw attempts often give you a "no target" even with a demon in your grill. Blood Punches often fail to register. On an Ultra Nightmare run where one mistake can end it all, these are scary. Hugo Martin, the game director, promised these will be addressed first thing in 2021. Doom 2016 had proven me wrong in terms of design philosophies. Eternal had opened my eyes again. By now, I have faith in these guys more than I believe in myself.So far, I have 548 hours clocked in Doom Eternal. I never imagined around half of those would be spent in multiplayer. Battlemode, a 2 v 1 demons vs Slayer bloodbath, is rather unique. After hundreds of hours, I still find new things to learn. More ways to improve, just like in the campaign.Demons do feel OP at first. I thought that on day one, too. But once you have played enough, you will meet the god-tier Slayers. Not great Slayers. The gods. Demons should be about positioning? Cool. Good luck outrunning the Slayer's framerate based meat hook that borderline teleports him across the map. Locked at 120 frames at the time of writing, but still. Plus, with Ballista boosts, there is no escape. Mancubus is deadly up close? Nice, but still melts under a Slayer's godspeed weapon switch. I cannot fathom how the mode can be balanced for players who have reached such a maniacal skill level.Most of the time, it is indeed strategy versus skill. When you meet these guys, it is mortal against gods. Hundreds of hours later, after improving day by day, I am at a loss. A conclusion drawn after 6-8 months of grinding. For now, I have returned to 2016's multiplayer for those last achievements. Let's see how this mode progresses.That aside, Invasion Mode is said to be on the way. Plus, classic deathmatch and the like would be neat, too. Perhaps they do not wish for Eternal to compete with Quake Champions, however, so there may be no hope.When I run Eternal, it is not a journey to beat the game, but to improve as a Slayer. My Ultra Nightmare run taught me about nerves and having cold blooded focus. It taught me about myself. Showed me things I can take into real life. I participate in community events not because I need those points, but because I wish to be a part of this group. It reminds me of my street basketball days. Hangout with fellow hoopers on the sidelines, then hop on runs to hone our skills. This is a lifestyle.The Ultimate Doom will always be my all time favorite game. I wear those nostalgia glasses with pride. Still, even with that bias, I believe Eternal is the best FPS designed to date. id Software saluted me for beating Quake I. Today, I salute them.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 proved that Doom wasn't done and did so by practically redefining the standards of quality for the genre. Doom Eternal looked in the mirror, felt the sort of rage territorial predators get when they see one another and set out to hit the next level all over again.Doom is about a (Doom) Guy who hates demons. They're invading Earth now, the cads. Time to shoot them. If you're familiar with 2016 and classic Doom games you know the drill: use an arsenal of cool guns to murder demons with an iconic, timeless roster of metal album cover monsters. Have a rock solid gameplay loop of shooting and resource management, make the player and game feel smooth as silk, add excellent exploration and creative map design, good soundtrack and season to taste. Eternal changes things up significantly from 2016. Everything is faster, more intense. Literally. You get a short-range Dash you can use frequently and combine with your Double Jump. You need to move constantly or you'll be cornered, flanked, sniped, die horribly. Demon aggression has been raised to the absolute limits of good taste. On higher difficulties Eternal can be a game that you can't relax in because you need to move, move fast, move with a plan, fight valiantly all the time. New things trickle in frequently, though ultimately amounting to the building blocks of the new resource management gameplay. Set enemies on fire to restore Armor. Glory Kill enemies to get Blood Punches, which work fine as emergency panic buttons or offensive tactical nukes. Chainsaw to get ammo. Probably the biggest new change and for some reason a much divided one. All I can say is: if you wish to complete the game, get used to it. Hit C every so often when you see a Zombie, Soldier or Imp. You've also got the Glory Kills themselves as a vital resource ala Doom 2016, where the period of invulnerability, removal of a threat from the fight and health restoration can be pivotal.Eternal favors arena combat much more, most encounters being prolonged battles against spawning in waves of heavy enemies where you can use infinitely respawning fodder enemies to replenish your resources. The challenge is to identify targets and destroy them while avoiding being run down. Many FPS games pull their punches with regards to "dangerous" enemies, Doom Eternal makes practically everything dangerous. Some are just a bit more than others. You'll die to eating Imp fireballs as well as you would being stomped by Mancubi or Barons. The early stages can be a bit rough as the game really works best when you have all your options. And really, the options can be a bit overwhelming at first but aren't strictly mandatory. Chainsaw fodder every so often, use the flamethrower before a glory kill, frost grenade to get breathing room, dash frequently. That covers most of the game even into Ultra Violence. Where Eternal really takes off is the room to keep pushing that skill ceiling, to kill things faster, navigate the arenas better and so on. Weaving in grenades, quick-shifting weapons, using the best weapon at the right time. The expanded enemy roster with the return of Cyberdemons, Archviles, Pain Elementals and new additions that round out the roster in great ways. Carcass is a magnificent bastard of an obstacle maker, Whiplash is a flanking nightmare and Marauder. Oh, Marauder. If your game has 20+ enemies, having one that pushes back against everything by forcing you to slow down... works well! Like the move from Doom 1 to Doom 2 the expanded enemy roster really lets the game blossom into perfection, each combat scenario having loads of room to be different.So "killing demons" is good, what about the rest? Well, that's simple enough. Graphics are gorgeous, music is great, levels are huge and loaded with tons of secrets to find, interesting nooks and crannies, level paths have good ways of having you come back through previous areas to access new parts of the level and so on. Like classic Doom levels there's a lot of care put into just how every arena and hall is placed. There is a story element to discuss, and while Eternal has a good story, I think the greatest difference is that 2016 had what many saw as a perfect tone and story. So changing that was bound to be a bit rough no matter how it was done.*Spoilers* The story is a bit of an outlier. Eternal doesn't have a bad story but it does have a different one. I guess the biggest difference is that 2016 ended on a fantastic cliffhanger and Eternal starts... well, who has time for that? Here's your cool ship, here's your Hell invasion, Samuel who? Things come together and it flows decently by the end but a bit of a confusing and rough shift mid-journey for sure.It's a big, meaty game. It's a strong evolution of what was already a siren song of return to form for Doom. Eternal can easily take 10+ hours to beat first time blind and then you've got the extra difficulties and getting everything. The quality is sky high and while I did feel at first that maybe things were a little too different, Eternal clearly won me over. For all the changes Eternal makes I can think that they're not bad ideas, they're just different from 2016. It helps that Eternal ends on a perfect reimagining of a classic boss fight.A rare game worth $60 up front, though it's been long enough to hope for a sale. An easy 9/10 and a contender for 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be a heretic and post a negative review. Objectively this is not a bad game, but I feel like it is a step backwards from Doom 2016. The main thing I dislike is that in this game, you spend a lot more time dodging/running than you do shooting. If you're the type of person that likes bullet hell games (Binding of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, etc) and would like a great fps version of that then this is a great game for you; crank up the difficulty and have a blast in hell lol. However, to me the dodging and running around can get tedious because most of the time you are running around to find health and ammo to fight back. In this game every ammo type is shared by 2 guns, so you effectively you have half the ammo compared to Doom 2016 and way more things to shoot. Even when you've upgraded your ammo capacity to the max you feel like you're constantly fighting to not run out of ammo. Additionally, the chainsaw is capped to 3 fuel the entire game. In Doom 2016 you could save up fuel and use the chainsaw strategically either for ammo in long fights or for taking out certain key enemies, but in this game it's basically a 'press-C-next-to-fodder-enemies-for-ammo' button. This makes the gameplay essentially boil down to 1. Shoot for 30 seconds 2. Look for fodder enemy to get ammo 3. Repeat over and over again. There are plenty of new mechanics in this game but most of them feel half baked: the flamethrower is basically a press button for armor mechanic that you will forget to ever use. The melee weapon you get (no spoilers) is super cool and could've been a really cool mechanic but it turns out to just act like a more ammo-efficient chainsaw. The runes and weapon mods are significantly more balanced but as a result are less interesting to use. The runes in 2016 could be stacked in certain ways to create some really broken stuff like infinite ammo towards the end of the game; here they're just little bonus perks. Towards the end of the game you actually encounter a certain enemy that encourages you to actively switch weapons and weapon mods mid-combat which made the game a lot more fun for that whole level, but then you no longer encounter that enemy and return to the same tedious loop which shows that these mechanics really could've been much better with some more thought put in. This game is far grander than Doom 2016, the levels are gorgeous, and the enemies you encounter are far more numerous and diverse. However, perhaps due to this grander scope, the progression and game mechanics feel far less thought out to me and make the game tedious towards the end, even though the essential aspects of the game like the controls, shooting, and movement are fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal has been by far one of the best single-player FPS experiences I had a chance to engage with.Frantic murder-fest with surprising amount of depth and strategy to it. The game required me to, pardon the phrasing, "git gud" to a degree where I had to shed some of the bad habits that other FPSes allowed me to get away with (like still selecting the weapons from weapon wheel), and yet it never felt unfair - every death was due to my oversight and complacency.The multi-player part, I can't comment on, as for me it's been completely broken since release - I could not connect to any matches, matchmaking kept hanging indefinitely, and the like.I should specify here, I use Linux as my main operating system, and I don't dual-boot, thus I can't say how much of that is due to my OS of choice, and how much of that is multi-player being broken. If you're looking at titles to play with others, there are likely better titles out there, but I personally didn't lament it that much; my interest was strictly in single-player portion.A word of caution:With Update 1, id Software has snuck an invasive kernel-level anti-cheat into the game, but has done so in such manner that none of the Linux users were able to access the game at all - not just the multiplayer component, but .Update 1.1 has removed the anti-cheat following feedback, but keep in mind it  happen again, and if you've non-standard machine, or play on Linux, or if you just don't want invasive software with unlimited permissions snooping on your system, you might not be able to play the game any more.As for now, if you're looking for good single-player shooter experience that will push you and your skills to improve, I can recommend DOOM Eternal wholeheartedly. If you're more of a casual shooter player, or are going for multiplayer scene, you might want to look to other titles.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: this is an artistically streamlined game that has a well formed goal in mind, and it achieves it in the best way possible. Watch the store video and you'll know what this kind of game is. If fast paced FPS dismemberment is your thing, you'll love it.There's a lot of complaints that it isn't Doom 2016, which I have to agree with, but only in the sense that Eternal is more refined. The gameplay in 2016 is focused on walking into a room, get locked in, kill doods, move to next room. Secrets are hard to find and broke immersion. It got repetitive very fast. The story was bare and merely mentioned as a backdrop. But hey, that's Doom so you can't complain.Doom Eternal is an upgraded version in all regards. There's everything from before but just a little bit more that makes it perfect. The gameplay is more varied because it breaks the boring grind by adding a bit more platforming, optional fights, and a lot more scenery. Weapons, Abilities, and Movement is tight, responsive, and open to unique play styles. Low ammo is never actually an issue unless you have very bad accuracy (at that point you should lower the difficulty since this is a game purely based on fast paced accuracy). The story is on the forefront and the places you go to have purpose. Everything is beautifully intertwined and given purpose on many levels.One thing that people haven't seemed to mention enough is the level of detail in world and environment design. It's simply phenomenal that every square foot was given attention and high quality rendering. Take some time and walk the halls and you'll find little writings. Zoom in on the papers and they have text. It's pretty derpy, but when I saw that there were potato chip bags I just had to look at them all. Steamed Broccoli Flavor is my favorite.When I say streamlined at the start of this review I mean that the game subtly hints at what you should do in ways you don't think about. Green lights mean go here. Extra lives are given in difficult locations so you don't get stuck in a level replay loop, but you will still feel the panic when you fail. You don't need to hunt for health and ammo because it comes to you. Missed a secret? Teleport back after you finished the level and try again. What's more, you can replay that level any time frustration free to help get everything you missed with freely given cheat modes and stop playing that level the second you find it. This is a game that does not punish you. It's a game about you punishing demons.I can't find any real faults that matter enough to say it's not worth the price. There are some glitches that happen with frequency: a specific fast flying enemy will quite often get stuck in the ground and perma lock you forcing a restart. You can get stuck in the ground from physics. Abilities might just get weird and stop working. I had a critical item not spawn in the world and had to restart. The game crashed to desktop about 10 times during my first 30 hours, but most of that is my fault pushing the graphics too far. Due to the streamlining mentioned above I didn't get all that angry when this happened. Maybe 5-10 minutes lost at worst. These are fixable issues so they could be already patched by the time you read this review.So with all of that said, understanding that this is a game built for gameplay and is focused all on you as the player. It's worth it. Run fast, shoot demons, and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I played Doom Eternal when it launched on my Xbox One. Back then when I beat the game I hated it. I found it tough to manage my resources and I couldn't achieve the high accuracy needed to play Doom Eternal well on a controller. Upon revisiting Eternal on PC I was sure to remind myself of a couple tips I picked up on while in the Doom subreddit; use all your tools, keep moving around the entire arena, switch to weapons based on how effective they are at killing demons(could be for weak points like with the Cacodemons or just a general weakness like with the Hell Knights), and the combo of weapon switching to ignore long reloads when dealing with tougher demons. Finally after changing my play style and mindset... I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. I definitely think the better accuracy of mouse and keyboard played a big role in why I did so well on my return but now that the game has clicked with me I understand why Eternal is so loved. Fights are fast, you're constantly on the move trying to quickly figure out new priority targets as you take out big demons only for new more threatening ones to enter the arena. Most demons are fought differently so you're constantly adapting your play style to fit dodging a variety of projectiles and focusing down whatever enemy you deem to be the highest priority. The game requires constant resource management through use of your tools and even use of your entire arsenal, but when you find that sweet spot in combat where you're on the move, gathering health, armour, ammo, whatever you need, taking down Arch-viles and Mancubie without dipping into low health, armour, or ammo... That's when Doom Eternal makes you the Doom Slayer. Every fight makes your blood rush as you seek out more and more combat to improve your skills. The gun play is unlike any other shooter I've played. Where in most games your choice of weapon often boils down to what has the highest ammo and whether you're dealing with squishier or tougher enemies, Doom Eternal will have you using your entire aresenal in bigger fights, never having to concern yourself with ammo because even if you do run out, you know there's fodder running around the arena anyways. _childDocuments_.review: Even with its few flaws this is EASILY the greatest FPS game I have ever played. All of its systems and music and flawless performance coming together to create an experience completely unique to Eternal that just blows anything else out of the water. Eternal is a direct improvement over 2016 in every possible way, and once I was used to the low ammo it never bothered me. In 2016, I loved using the super shotgun but an issue I had was if you wanted to get a glory kill to regain health you couldn't use it because you would just obliterate any target you hit. I was initially worried that was carried over here but once you get the flaming meathook that all changes. Suddenly it becomes the single greatest weapon in your arsenal and an armor farming machine. This gun becomes the backbone to the rest of the games combat, at least for me. That is the great thing about the combat here though, each weapon has so many different uses that you can approach a situation in a countless number of ways. This has been talked about to hell and back so I wont go on long, but I personally did not like the marauders. They just slow down the combat and make you wait for a little flash to be able to do anything. I like that they encourage you to quick swap to deal with them faster, but they still are a net negative in my opinion. Thankfully they are never really used enough for me to really care, and besides the final regular encounter they are easy enough to isolate and deal with. Besides that, a few bosses were not the most interesting. My problem with bosses is they force you to play one very specific way to beat them, which disregards the absolute freedom and creativity you are awarded from the regular encounters. This game really throws a lot at you, and it can feel overwhelming at first. Especially on nightmare. But once you fully learn the combat and you can just enter a flow state this is where the game shines the brightest. I get the same rare feeling of focus from competitive multiplayer games, 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is an absolute improvement to the excellent 2016 Doom in every way. The game is more violent, the enemies are more varied and harder, the game is faster, your arsenal is larger, and the Doom Slayer has never felt more deadly. The music of Doom Eternal is also great and it retains the same amount of metal and hellish sounds from before and often times outdoing the previous game's soundtrack.There is a lot of platforming in this one so keep that in mind if you are not a fan of that, but personally I found the platforming enjoyable. Certain timed challenges in the game seem outright impossible but perhaps with time, I'll get good enough to beat them. The game is more narrative focused as before but this helps the game rather than hurt it. The story is what is allowing us to go to these crazy new areas and kill crazy new enemies.Everything else I didn't mention in this review might as well be flawless. I really only had issues with certain timed in-game challenges, and the game has tutorials set to "On" by default but I would recommend you to turn them off before starting. Many of the tutorials spoil who you are going to fight or how to win and figuring that out by yourself is doable and much more gratifying. SO Yeah, if you liked 2016's Doom, I can guarantee you will be ripping and tearing through the approximately 15-18hr campaign with a smile on your face or adrenaline in your system.HIGHLY RECOMMEND

_childDocuments_.review: I tried so hard to like this game after loving DOOM 2016, I really tried.What I liked:The Soundtrack - jesus christ, that main menu music is just so goodOptimisation - the game ran buttery smooth on my 1070 Ti and my 2080 TiCombat - when it works, it's great and visually the game looks pretty good tooWhat I didn't like:Progression - DOOM 2016 felt like every combat encounter was a sandbox, you had a solid dripfeed of weapons and tools through the game but were presented with arenas that you could complete to your own strategy. Instead, Eternal feels like it wants you to play in a very certain way throughout the early stages of the game, it felt way too rigid and ammo scarcity felt limiting when DOOM 2016 felt more about the liberation and freedom.Tutorialisation - Every few minutes there's a new menu, a new tutorial, a new crystal shard thing that affects abilities a certain way and it just feels overly complex and ironically less accessible. DOOM 2016 introduced new gameplay mechanics gradually, for example, here's a chainsaw, how cool is that? Try it out and see what it does. Bam. Done. How about some runes? Complete fun challenges to level up your rune and mix n' match them to tune your combat style. I get that you can turn them off apparently but man, the flow and pacing of 2016 is just not there in Eternal.Visuals - I know it's a weird thing to get stuck on, it's petty and very PCMR of me but the visual style of the game just feels so... inconsistent. You'll have this breathtaking hellscape on Earth but then the interior of your spaceship looks so off, I can't quite put my finger on it. Also Earth looks weird in the opening cutscene, a bit too Quake 4 for me.Story - So where'd I get this giant space castle thing? Near as I can tell the cliffhanger from DOOM 2016 is never resolved, there's just a big gap in the timeline. Weird. DOOM 2016 also presented the story in a very Half-Life, never leave the first-person perspective but DOOM Eternal feels like it's edgy younger brother with cutscenes of Doom Slayer throwing around heads, strutting around and casting badass looks back over his shoulder. IMO 2016 worked as a blending of modern and old, extremely well-designed combat encounters, simplistic narrative with teases of something bigger but it never went full "This is your destiny prophesy you are the chosen one, I have the high ground you betrayed me and I'm pregnant" levels of melodrama. I don't think I'm the only one who feels this way but man, Eternal just felt overwhelming. If you liked 2016, give it a try but it's just not for me Chief.EDIT: I played it way more on Xbox so if the 1.4 hours I have here makes you think "bUt u qUiT b4 iT gEtS gUd!!" maybe you should ask why I didn't want to keep playing until it gets good. The answer is above.Update: So I bought it again during the summer sale and pushed through the rest of the game. Despite some spectacle and an improvement to the story later on, I still feel the combat is overall far too restrictive, the Plasma Rifle is a crutch, you run out of ammo far too often (Only 20 shells for the Super Shotgun? For real?) and overall it feels like the game wants you to play in very specific ways instead of navigating combat encounters with any kind of individual strategic thinking (though 2016 sometimes lacked this as well)Overall I enjoyed it a little more, but it still feels and looks far too arcadey. DOOM 2016 left me looking forward to the next combat encounter and setpiece, DOOM Eternal just fatigued me. I look forward to seeing what they do with the next DOOM and I'll be playing with some mods next time I choose to install this.

_childDocuments_.review: With it's visual spectacle, visceral soundtrack, a wide-variety of over 25 demons, and an explosively adrenaline pumping gameplay experience DOOM Eternal can impress even the most avid game enthusiasts.  DOOM Eternal takes the existing groundwork of DOOM (2016) and offers a multitude of additions that improves the formula and stays true to the focus of constant action/violence and fast movement that calls back to but stays unique from the original 1990s games.  For brevity's sake I'll refer to DOOM (2016) as '2016 and DOOM Eternal as Eternal, please refer to the invader zim DOOM song if you feel any DOOM withdrawal.I played the campaign on Ultra-violence difficulty and found that it required my complete concentration on each enemy and my resources while staying balanced throughout the experience.  During each fight (save for the "parry" demons) there is little to no downtime as you swap between ammo / weapon types to take out each demon.  While you're well-equipped to handle another demon infestation with dashing and many weapons to deal massive damage, enemies are much faster and heavier demons are tankier.  Like in '2016, there's great fun in swapping weapons quickly with the numerical keys where each one applies to each demon type.  You also have two swappable modifications to each weapon (excluding the super shotgun) to fit your playstyle, in my experience I only swapped in the beginning where you lack weapons.  Performance, controls, and pacing all worked flawlessly and I hadn't noticed any areas of dropped framerate / inputs, or too few encounters / too many encounters. Ammo is more scarce and limited unlike in '2016 where you have a chance to gain ammo on kills.  I noticed in my playthrough that I burnt through and ran out of ammo several times on each level which heavily incentivizes the use of the chainsaw. In the previous game where I'd use the chainsaw to both clear heavy demons and get ammo back only once, rarely twice each fight I'd use the chainsaw more often in Eternal and only on smaller demons for the ammo.  You can hold a max of 6 fuel pips in '2016, in Eternal you can only hold a max of 3 but can slowly recover a single fuel pip automatically if you have none.  It's up to your discretion on which game did it better but in my opinion I preferred how '2016 incentivized you to use it both for the ammo and cleaving through large demons whereas Eternal punishes you for using it.  If used against a large demon the player is obligated to wait until they get their free fuel pip before picking up any other fuel canisters, in this regard you lose a significant amount of potential ammo to only kill a single enemy and it oftentimes takes you a significant amount of time before you find another canister as there are far fewer fuel/ammo pickups in Eternal (I spent most of my time on one fuel pip).  In addition Eternal lacks the dramatic death animations from '2016, I'd speculate this was removed in order to retain the focus on the power of the DOOM slayer and constant flow of gameplay provided by the extra lives pickups.  As-of launch the game's multiplayer "Battlemode" feels lacking in both balance and gameplay depth.  It's a 1v2 with a slayer versus two player-controlled demons with 5 to choose from.  I quickly learned that using lock-on burst in conjunction with the super shotgun quickly kills demons with little to no counterplay on the receiving end. I hope to see better balance of the rocket launcher in the game's future.  With the current lack of gamemodes '2016s base multiplayer experience was much more appealing and balanced in my opinion.  ID software has done a good job with some of the recent patches which nerfs the slayers effectiveness but still retains a balance for both sides.  However there are several fundamental strategies that the slayer can use with no counterplay options from the demons. Slayers can spend most of the match in the air with jump pads that have no cooldown and offer no counterplay.  The majority of demons are at a disadvantage when a slayer uses a jump pad as the slayer is too high to receive damage from most high-damaging attacks which can be abused indefinitely since jump-pads do not de-activate.  (some maps have jump pads that lead directly onto another jump pad) The Chaingun shield can solo a mancubus at point blank range and the only counter is using hazard zone whose cooldown is far greater than the shield (7/13/2020 EDIT: The chaingun shield now properly doesn't shield the player from behind in battlemode and while it no longer de-activates the shield when the slayer is in a hazard zone it still deals damage as it did before leaving some room for counter-play)The speed of quick-swapping weapons could use some tweaking, slayers can kill player-controlled demons in only 5 seconds.Overall, the fun I had GREATLY outweighed some of the missteps in this incredible game, can't wait to see what new content ID software has in-mind for the game.  RIP AND TEAR!

_childDocuments_.review: I really thought the initial press surrounding Eternal's quake-con reveal was hysterical. The "mortally challenged" and "melting pot of the universe"  SURE DID TRIG THOSE LIBS,..several weeks later, when launching Doom 2016, I had to agree to a new Bethesda EULA with a point to prevent offense given to *special groups of people. Go figure..The fact that you need a bethesda account to play aside, the game felt off.  The game started with a cutscene (skippable) which felt against the spirit of the old game of "smash screens and screw your exposition". This scene was not in first-person but instead a third person view. In Doom 2016, you never actually saw yourself, just your arms and legs when you were breaking stuff. You are no longer doom guy...you're a simp who takes control of doom guy.This complaint comes from the unpopular opinion that I hated weapon mods in Doom 2016. The super shotgun grappling hook was being shown at quake-con and I was just sitting and hoping its optional.  Weapon mods were completely optional in Doom 2016 and only one armor mod was required to proceed. In Eternal, a door early on is locked until you take a shotgun attachment. I didn't play far enough in Eternal to get to the grappling hook before I refunded it, but given the verticality of the maps early on, I wouldn't be shocked if it was also a mandatory mod.Even pettier gripes include the call of duty style hit markers, the bright cartoonish hud, pickups, and menu interfaces. The headshot sound (literally just sounds like a coconut being opened) gets annoying really fast. If someone wanted a recommendation, I would say 2016 or Brutal Doom mod for base games.

_childDocuments_.review: TDLR version: Eternal isn't nearly as good as the 2016 DOOM due to a lot of highly questionable design choices. It has moments of being really good, but it has a tendency to get dragged down by various small things. A lot of deaths feel like your got screwed instead of you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. If you have held off this long, continue to hold off until it is on sale or reduced.It comes down to this: In the previous DOOM, I rarely felt like my death was to the games fault, be it from a glitch, unresponsive controls, BS enemies, etc. I felt like I was in control, that if I died, I could have done better to avoid it. In Eternal, I get frustrated by deaths that I couldn't avoid. The chainsaw not locking on when the enemy it just a bit off the center of my screen, so you get melee'd to death instead. Not grabbing onto ledges despite having a lot of platforming sections (which themselves are annoying and stop the pace), so you fall and lose a bit of health. Your dashes stopping if you so much as graze an enemy, instead of sliding around them or bouncing off a bit. Weapons running out of ammo and auto switching to awkward weapons, for instance: Super shotgun often switches to rocket launcher. Because obviously when I was using a point blank weapon, the next closest weapon I want is a rocket launcher that will kill me with self-damage. Which brings up the ammo problem, except for the BFG, don't bother saving ammo. You are expected to constantly be switching weapons as they run out of ammo, when you run out, to go find a small zombie that they spawn in fights, chainsaw him for a shower of ammo, and continue. It is an annoyance, a chore. Then several enemies are incredibly frustrating to deal with. Prowlers (Teleporting Imps) are incredibly annoying, since they can teleport right next to you and instantly melee. Not much damage, but every time it happens, it takes me out of the game in frustration. Bonus points for when they spawn behind you while you are backpedaling away from an enemy, so when you try to dash, surprise, you get glued to them and your back gets clawed while that hell brute comes up to have a word with you.Then you have marauders, which are the most frustrating enemy I've encountered so far. It is like whoever designed the Hell Guard (the worms in the stone golems) from DOOM was allowed to make a semi-common enemy in the last half of the fight. You basically have to wait for them to attack you (flashing green eyes is the tell) when in sort of medium range and then do a burst of damage. Repeat several times. If you are too close, he will shotgun you in the face, too far, he will just throw projectiles. Attack him when he hasn't given the tell and he will just block your shot, including the BFG. He can also spawn a ghost dog that will ♥♥♥♥ you up if it gets too close and if you happen to get the super shotgun swapping to the rocket launcher automatically... well you are probably going to lose a lot of health. Meanwhile he can dash around rapidly at times, including right into your face and pull out the instant shotgun for some BS damage on you. Basically, it is an aggravating enemy to fight at worst, a chore to fight at best. I don't feel satisfaction on defeating them, I feel relief that I can move on to a different fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the majority of negative comments are due to people not being able to learn to play this game, forgetting that DOOM in it's core, is a power fantasy but not a free one, it requires mastery and some built up anger and determination which is what makes beating an arena so satisfying. The base game is very fair and when you die it's TYPICALLY your fault. The DLC on the other hand is a bit of a different story but I like for the most part nevertheless. People also seem to have this idea that this game needs to be similar to DOOM 2016 which is just wrong. Doom Eternal rewards the player for learning to deal with certain enemies, master weapons and use them in fitting scenarios and manage your "economy" of armor, ammo and health. That said. Most of it is pretty easy to manage once you get the hang of it - especially on the easier difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 the previous game was an unexpected return to the classic "boomer" shooter formula that despite minimal expectations actually rocked. Sure it kept enemy counts lower than classics, but it felt dynamic. Doom Eternal is simultaneously an extremely strong divergence from classic boomer shooter formula and a very natural feeling continuation of it.Since the meat of this game is gameplay, here's an explainer of what makes it cool: Developers went out of their way to make it as dynamic as possible. There's dashes, double jumps, levels are full of speed boosting platforms and bats you can use to jump further, and mobility matters a lot since arena you fight in have the ammo and other pickups scattered. Moreover, you get little ammo, it runs out fast, and different enemies have different vulnerabilities or advantages that make it ill-advised or favorable to use specific weapons against them - say, plasma cannon can destroy plasma shields making them explode, but projectiles are pretty easily dodgeable, so called Ballista cannon is easy to miss and is slow to reload, but it's shots stun some quite annoying enemies upon hit, which all ultimately leads to need to always switch guns to best. Third thing is that while there are arena shooter-style health and ammo pickups, you'll mostly get health and armor by performing glory kill executions onto enemies, or dousing them with flamethrower and having them spill out some armor bit by bit as they burn, these things are very inconvenient to get used to but are really fun once you get the hang of it as you can make pretty dramatic comebacks mid-battle on a regular basis. Also enemy design is interesting, while some are Doom classics like cacos, archevilles or pinkies, the new enemy types interact with player's abilities in some interesting ways, one way or another.Another real interesting thing is how it's probably the first AAA game where I genuinely wanted to explore all secrets and collectibles, instead of giving you generic logs (you'll find those here too but they're usually some of easier secrets) you get a variety of both cosmetic nice cute things and beneficial upgrades. And, well, most of secrets are well-telegraphed, and you can comeback to different checkpoints to re-collect them using fast travel before ending the level, and the rewards are always interesting, so, yeah, good job guys you sold me on collecting virtual funko pops, amazing how you made that fun!Now, the story? It's a bit of an excuse plot to take you trough all sorts of locales and seems half of it is received in DLCs I neglected to buy over reviews, but where Doom 2016 was like you deal with some corporate scifi bastard's screwup and take on a cult, here it's more like... Ancient aliens conspiracy-grade grand fight against both heaven and hell because apparently someone figured out a perpetual motion engine can be powered by blood? Ok.I recommend this if you like action games that keep the pace up and demand some exploration. Don't expect a traditional boomer shooter experience, but nonetheless a real challenging and satisfying one.

_childDocuments_.review: Played DOOM/DOOM II in 1993/4 when I was the target demographic (which I figure is 12 year olds). Also HERETIC, HEXEN, QUAKE, and other FPSes of the era. I murder children in Fortnite because kids haven't been playing these games for 30 years. DOOM III was alright but went in a different direction with survival horror. DOOM IV (the 2016 game was called that in development, fight me) was pretty cool, a real return to form, even more of a gorefest than this one (which I will be calling DOOM V), but took only about 14 hours to finish on ULTRA VIOLENCE (AKA hard mode). This one, DOOM V, is something special. It took 50 hours with the ANCIENT GODS expansions, which you absolutely must play. It has plot! Imagine that! The graphics are a little more cartoony than IV, but still enough to be gross and horrifying, which is the point of them. DOOM as a game has a lot of atmosphere the way a tattoo parlor with bars on the windows and a particle board "door" and motorcycles parked in the front has atmosphere. Calling it a "FPS" is fine but it forgets the feelings it nurtures while you play. You should feel sick to your stomach, with nausea at the disgusting things on screen, but also fear, both constant and acute, and also angry, to propel yourself to commit shocking acts of gratuitous violence, and weary, because all the focus it takes to play should tire you. After turning it off you should be twitchy for an hour.Look, what do you want in a DOOM game? It's got it. You explore a half-dozen different planets. You see amazing things, and shoot them. There are puzzles and keycards. It's got some non-traditional stuff in there too, like a plot, which is someone's swing-for-the-fences epic-scale deeply-personal space-opera where at the end you kill the personification of the author's depression, platforming (which is functional most of the time), the chainsaw and horrifying melee kills are part of the core gameplay loop now, you get another melee weapon or two, you can doubledash and doublejump and will need to for basic survival. It works (except for the platforming, sometimes, which I did enjoy, except when it didn't work). There's even "progression" in the core campaign, which is... fine, mostly because you're given all the things in the expansions, and so undoes any mistakes you make in your progression and/or doesn't require you to have found literally every secret.If I could change anything it would be the game's overreliance on structured fights. You walk into a big, open room with complex architecture, jump pads, and power-ups, you know something is going to go down, and it does. Wave after wave of complex combinations of heavy and superheavy demons whose infernal powers complement each other. OG DOOM had some of that, but what it reminds me more of is QUAKE multiplayer. Which is fine, and fun, but at a certain point the game becomes just one of these after another after another, and your goal is to memorize the waves and figure which demons to kill in what order with what weapons (I recommend saving the BFG for Arch-Viles). Between these arenas there's some light exploration and platforming. In the OG game, demons were a constant presence. On NIGHTMARE mode they spawned perpetually everywhere. It kept up the pressure. You were never safe. You were always low on ammo. It was hard to explore and find secrets because your brain was never able to just sit and think. Also, the secrets usually had demons in them! That would be cool, but because demons are a source of health/armor/ammo in this game, it's not really possible to have that dynamic with this core gameplay loop. You'd be at max health/armor/ammo every time you walked into an arena. It's fine, I accept it.Should you play this game? Yes of course. Did you listen to bitter veteran gamers nitpick every aspect of DOOM V and you're not sure anymore? Don't listen to those guys, listen to me. Fun allowed. You'll have a good time. It beats playing the original and it's 16-bit graphics all over again and again. Wade through an ocean of gore, listen to it squelch beneath your boots, brace yourself for the horrors that will emerge from it, then rip and tear until it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal, with its current situation goes like this....You saw a commercial about car X, you liked the design, the specifications were great and you were extremely excited. This particular car manufacturer had a history of delivering the best of the best vehicles and had a track record of making best in class cars.You asked yourself, "why not?". You went ahead and purchase car X pre-release. The day eventually came and car X was ready for pickup. You went to the dealership to retrieve your car. First impression, this vehicle drove like a dream and you would go as far as to say, this is the best car you have driven in your entire life.A month later...like any other day, you attempted to start the engine of car X and only this time, on the dashboard of the car, it asked you "activate in-car dash camera?". You select "no" and the car wouldnt start. You are not comfortable activating such a feature as this wasnt listed in the specification of the car when you made the purchase initially. Secondly, and most importantly, you have huge privacy and security concerns over such a feature installed in your car without your consent.You called up the manufacturer and the manufacturer responded with "This is part of a system upgrade to all Car X owners to monitor all on-going activities within the car during Uber and Lyft pickups. This is a measure to protect our Car X drivers against criminal activities when picking up passengers". You explained that you are not an Uber nor Lyft driver and such measure isnt needed. Unfortunately, this system update is an all or nothing where you must accept this feature to continue driving the vehicle.My car is currently sitting in the garage and hasnt moved since the system update.1 month and 2 weeks later...Our trusted car manufacturer has made a u-turn on their decision to revert their update and through honest communication, they get my thumbs up again.Keep it up!
