_childDocuments_.review: 2016 DOOM was a dark stylish shooter with fun combat that didn't force you to do anything.This one is something that struck me with very different vibes (in a bad way) right from the menu - you'll notice interface is screaming "CASUAL" and so does the rest of the game. I'm not saying it's easy. It can be hard, but in a bad way. You'll simply run out of ammo every fight and be forced to "farm" the special "farming" zombies for ammo with a chainsaw. They even put a hint in the codex about them: "these are weak enemies, use them to farm resources" - sorry, what? DOOM 2016's codex was explaining the lore and story behind each enemy, gun or artifact, this one gives you hints on how it wants you to play it. The other enemies have "weak spots" to be hit with a special gun, unless you do it you can waste all your ammo on them as if they're bosses.Game got x5 more vertical than the previous one and it feels that there's more platforming than shooting now. Is this Mario?The interface is all shiny and cluttered, hard to read.The powerups/health/ammo items are all shiny and cartoony.DOOM 2016 had guns held by dead soldiers or stuck in enemies, they contributed to the atmosphere of catastrophic events that went by while you were sleeping in your tomb.DOOM Eternal has guns as shining floating bonuses as if this is Quake:Arena. _childDocuments_.review: I loved FPSes back in the early days.  Wolfenstein, Doom, Quake, Unreal -- those games were my jam.  I don't like modern FPSes that much, though, and so I was blown away when Doom 2016 game out and recaptured what I loved about those older games.  It was a blast and left me on the edge of my seat with anticipation for Doom Eternal.Unfortunately, Doom Eternal has forgotten what made 2016 great and has decided that other modern shooters had the right ideas.Did you like being able to pick your favorite firearm and use it to run through alien facilities, slaughtering demons?  Well, hold up -- DE has a "gameplay loop" now.  Ammo is a scarce resource, and you have to carefully watch your ammo levels for every firearm, cycling between them and using all of them in the middle of a fight, then running away from larger demons when you run out of ammo so you can chainsaw a smaller one.  Did 2016's Gore Nests, which locked you in a room until you had defeated multiple waves of enemies, annoy you?  Well, *every* room is like that now -- every stage is just a set of big killboxes connected by hallways, and you can tell as soon as you enter a room that you're going to get locked in there until you've killed everything.  Did you enjoy 2016's simple but effective story that was told mostly through narration and the environment, rarely taking control away from you for extended periods of time?  Well, DE has decided that was a mistake.  Get ready to sit back for some long cutscenes with dialogue, but if you actually want to piece together what's happening, you'll also need to hunt down codexes and interrupt gameplay to read pages and pages of lore.  Apparently between games, the story stopped being about a lone human fighting back the forces  of hell, and is now about an ancient group of interdimensional warriors fighting against monsters from another dimension?  And you're a part of that organization and have some super space fortress to serve as your base?  This isn't the Doom I signed up for.Anyway, I've put several hours into this game trying to enjoy Doom Eternal, but it has just thrown away everything I liked about Doom 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the game, the story, its obscenely fun to play. Fast-paced action and gore, a long campaign, lots of unlockables.However, I can not recommend it to anyone. After release a very invasive anti-cheat system was added which essentially gives access to everything on your PC. This has contributed to stability issues on mine and the systems of many others, as well as serving as a very tempting attack vector for anyone hoping to compromise your PC.The addition of this was detrimental, and if Steam was capable of refunding me at this point, I would take it. Had I known that this rubbish would be added weeks after release, I never would have purchased the game in the first place. Its unfortunate that so much of the developers hard work has to be ignored due to the idea to use an invasive 0-circle OS Kernel level anti-cheat.

Nah... i would rather they do Sonic Mayhem style Quake music on Doom than the EDM Mick Gordon serviceable but certainly overrated score... whatevs atleast the shooty game has guitars i guess.Update3: The Doom 3 theme is the best Tool song because is not made by them and is actually good lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Overall: 9/10Campaign: 10/10TAG1: 9.5/10TAG2: 8/10Battlemode: 7/10My rambling review: This game was so much fun from start to finish, everything from the soundtrack and graphics to gameplay and level design is just fantastic, you can get so immersed in being the DOOM SLAYER - especially when you get to grips with the mechanics and balance of Chainsaw - Flamethrower - Execute to restore your ammo, armour and health respectively. I got all but one collectable because the last one was a right pain, so probs add on about 3 hours in secret hunting and level replays - maybe another hour because i got stuck at a few points and boom a 20 hour or so campaign with lots of lore if you want it but can skip over if you don't. Absolutely fantastic.edit1: I played TAG1 the first week of March 2021 to give you an idea, as I know some things changed with certain updates. I think TAG1 was a fantastic addition to the series, the difficulty increased with the addition of turrets and whiplash spectres was great, and the blood makyrs were a pain the arse - a cross between the drones and the khan makyrs. The level designs were fantastic, a real difference from main campaign, especially the swamps. There's the addition of spirits as well, which possess other demons and make them super-powered - they're definitely ones to prioritise, i found them more difficult than a buff token, demons are faster and stronger and chase you relentlessly, the possessed marauder was a lot of fun, can't believe I didn't die on that.Once you kill the possessed demon the spirit is exposed and you have to microwave them with the plasma rifle, finally making that mod useful.The final boss for TAG1 is pretty difficult, because you have to take out 2 spirit possessed demons before you do damage to him, i didn't struggle with the first round but the dread knight + pain elemental was difficult.TAG2 was fantastic conclusion, i enjoyed the pacing and even more challenges - it built upon mini scenarios that it introduced in TAG1 where it'll spawn in like 30 of 1 type of demon, but with the ammo type that perfectly counters them. My favourite was walking into a room of like 50 boxes of shotgun ammo thinking OOO ITS ABOUT TO GET REAL and it spawned in loads of stone imps which you have to kill with auto shotgun, you don't even have to take your finger off the trigger for the whole encounter just run around picking up more ammo and keep smashing those imps.Speaking of stone imps, they're 1 of three new enemies, others are cursed prowler - if it hits you you get 'cursed' can't dash and take damage over time, only way to break the curse is to blood punch the cursed prowler, a real challenge in the middle of a fight. Also armoured baron, break armour immediately when mace flashes green or gradually with plasma rifle then just shoot him til he dead before the armour regenerates.There's also riot shield guys, they're easy, just soldiers who's shields don't break, shoot a rocket or grenade behind them and don't even blink twice. Last of all there's screechers, ambient zombies but if you kill them they empower all demons around them for like 20 or 30 seconds or something, AVOID, they're designed to throw you a curve ball of 'hey actually maybe don't shoot everything in front of you'. I love it.I was a little disappointed with the dark lord's design, i didn't find him particularly imposing or intimidating, and the boss fight i thought was really easy for what is meant to be the real big bad - i struggled more on the icon of sin.After all the original game and both DLCs I'll give it 9/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought doom eternal as soon as it came out for PS4 as, at the time, i had a PC which wouldn't have been able to run it. It's miles better than 2016 and has a bunch more replayability due to the challenging combat situations that force you to think as appose to solving everything with a super shotgun blast to the face.I can see why some people dislike the change though, as you actually have to think this time. It's not just a mindless adventure, not that there was anything wrong with that.Now having tried the game on PC, I can honestly say I love it even more. 10/10 without a doubt. _childDocuments_.review: DO NOT GET THIS!!!   Due to the first update, it has Denuvo anti-cheat.  For those of you that do not know what Denuvo anti-cheat is, i will simplify it for you.  It is an anti-cheat system that uses your cpu, when you install it, you are giving amazon servers access to a whole lot of your pc.  Just imagine what would happen if somebody found a way to use that to gain control of all of the pc's connected to the servers.  All they would have to do is hack the servers and they would be able to take control of your pc.       The game was very fun,  i LOVED playing it.   It is depressing that it has come to this.  If it was not for Denuvo anti-cheat, i would currently be recommending this game to all of you.  I like what they did with the story and the multiplayer.     I have always been a huge doom fan,  HUGE,  and i never thought these words would be coming out of my mouth.  BUT. If Bethesda continues to use Denuvo anti-cheat in doom eternal, any future doom games.  I will not get another one of their games again.  It is very sad to have to do this but i heavily do not recommend getting doom eternal if you care about your pc.  If Denuvo does not worry you, go ahead and get doom eternal.  But now this, in my oppinion, the fun is not worth the risk.  If i would have known this would get put in the game when i pre-ordered it, i would never have bought it.Will change review if Denuvo anti-cheat is removed*UPDATE*   Denuvo anti-cheat was removed, so as long as they keep it out, i would recommend.  Still curious what what made them think adding Denuvo anti-cheat was a good idea.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal has anything you could wish for in an FPS game. The gameplay is fast-paced (to say the least), the graphics are good (the framerate is stable, which is crucial for playing), the atmosphere and soundtrack are straight up awesome.For whatever reason, there is a storyline and some characters in this game - it is meh, but better than nothing, I guess. The game is centered around concept of player-friendly interface: everything from combat and movement to exploration and collectibles is created in this "easy to figure, hard to master" style. Controls are super responsive, you'll never find Doomguy doing not what you wanted him to do.Oh, you're hardcore and want yourself a challenge? Yeah, DOOM Eternal has it. A lot of it. All of it.10\10

_childDocuments_.review: extremely fun, challenging and rewarding, i recommend. soundtrack is incredible, mick gordon is a legend. super gore nest is my favourite base game track. amazing level design throughout pretty much every level with a few spots feeling a tad bit wonky. awesome visuals, the demons look fantastic and i like the arcade-like feel the game has. horde mode is fun, battlemode is okay. a fun multiplayer mode would've been co-op, tackling new levels as maybe arc resistance members. dlcs are overpriced so buy on sale. tag1 is really fun, even harder than base game and the soundtrack is amazing, andrew hulshult stepped up and did not disappoint. blood swamps being my favourite dlc track. the level design for the first level felt too all over the place in the beginning but it gets better. i hope you like marauders as much as i do cause they're everywhere in this dlc (rip game journalists). the blood swamps is such an awesome mission, definitely one of my favourites in the whole game. the holt is a beautiful level and its a new area of urdak which is one of the coolest places in all of doom. i definitely recommend getting this dlc if you've mastered base game and seek a challenge to further your skills. slightly overpriced though so buy on sale!tag2 is a bit of a let down, the maps seem to lose all their verticality, the new demons feel boring execpt the armored baron hes cute and can stay. the meathook grapple points are awesome but the dlc felt too short for them to be memorable. the soundtrack is good for pt 2 however i feel like the soundtrack in pt 1 was more natural and flowed better with the gameplay. the new weapon the sentinel hammer is cool i don't have too many complaints other than it feels out of place, and not earned. base game 9.2/10tag1: 8/10tag2: 4.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: as a massive Doom fan, and a person who played the OG Dooms as a 4 year old on his daddy's desktop when he first learned to use a PC, i am ASTOUNDED at how long it has taken me to say that i dislike Doom Eternal. i  REALLY WANT to love this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, but as a religious Ultra Violence player on literally every other Doom, this one REALLY breaks my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heart and soul to try and play.i really can't list every little thing i find wrong with Eternal's combat loop. it feels very specific, like it wants a coldly specific loop out of me in every single fight, and until i figure that out it's just game over after game over. there's no actually WINNING a fight, there's no feeling of real understanding, the combat never clicks for me with how much i have to both keep track of and do at the same time. it's not some fun run n gun like older Dooms. it's not the Doom i grew up with and it's not the Doom i wanted more of after 2016. i gave it a solid shot, and due to my dumbass need to satisfy my purchase, i'm going to be forcing myself to get through this game some more. but know that this game WILL NOT satisfy long time Doom fans in particular unless they happen to also be a part of this specific kind of "puzzle combat" group. if you're a part of the niche that likes this convoluted stuff, ignore my review. this isn't for you, go enjoy the game, it's made for you.i'll be suffering while i wait for another good Doom game that respects my time.

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest FPS I've played to date. DOOM 2016 was really good, loved the combat in that game a lot but DOOM Eternal fixes a lot of the crutches players fell back on in this game and perfected the concept of becoming resource generating machine. All weapon mods feel useful in this game and encourage different playstyles unlike 2016 where there was a clear winner in what weapon mod was better than the other. Each level feels like they took their time and knew exactly how to teach the player in the game how to deal with certain enemies and traverse the environment without beating you over the head with it. Each Boss fight feels incredible to play and is always exhilarating  to go through (especially on Ultra-Violence difficulty and above). The base game is an absolute masterpiece and it is my game of the year for 2020. The Ancient Gods DLC is also amazing as well but be prepared to get your butt kicked. It does not mess around at all, it throws everything at you plus a bunch more of stage hazards and new enemies. I died more times in this expansion than i did in the base game. Still, great stuff and you should experience all of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This takes the resource elements of DOOM 2016 and makes it its core gameplay element. This means you need to switch weapons and equipments (flamethrowers, grenaders, glory kills, etc) in order to fuel your fight and regenerate yourself. That was exactly why I put off playing for years: the previous game's combat felt epic, but I also I'm too slow to really make it shine. Surprinsinly or not, Eternal's combat just flows better, I can't pinpoint why. The plot/lore is surprisingly engaging, though I'm a bit lost about the details. Not that it matters.The 1st DLC has some fights that seem to go on a little too long for their own good and there are a few times in the platforming puzzles it's not clear where exactly you're meant to go. This was much improved in the 2nd DLC, which is pretty epic, except for the final boss. Basically if you keep making mistakes and can't consistently bait him, you're looking at an endless battle - or at least a very long one. After almost 30 minutes I just gave up and watched the ending on YouTube. But that's just me not being gud enough I suppose. A shame, a little balancing and it would have been my favorite boss fight of this new DOOM era.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was freaking awesome... until update 1, where Bethesda decided to force the installation of a kernel-mode multiplayer anti-cheat driver.  Absolute lunacy.  I don't even play multiplayer, yet I'm still forced to install this security threat if I want to continue playing.  Not a chance.  They say you can uninstall it afterwards, but I hear the game will not launch if you do that.  In any case, I'm certainly not going to install such a dangerous piece of software on my machine in the first place, especially considering how unreliable uninstall processes are.  I'm going to give Bethesda a little more time to roll out a patch that doesn't require installation of this garbage.  If they don't do it soon, I'm going to get a refund.  So sad.  Doom is the whole reason I got into computers back in the 90s.  Bethesda seems to really be trying to ruin that legacy for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I had pause when iD/Bethesda wanted to install a ring-0 driver for what was, for me, a single-player experience.Given that installation, I didn't opt to partake in a review bomb, but withheld giving one at all.Kudos to the developers for listening to the community in approaching the need for Denuvo and removing it accordingly. I think putting a ring-0 driver in in the first place should be considered something of a ding. I understand the need for anti-cheat, but in a game like this at least give the option of avoiding it altogether by making MP and SP separate executables/experiences. I understand that other games use similar methods, but I don't play those other games, either.Now that Denuvo has been removed, I can confidently say that Doom Eternal is possibly the best single-player shooter experience I've had in a long, long time. The challenge of ultra nightmare keeps me coming back, and the visuals, controls, and overall feel of the platforming are superb.If you're looking for hectic action, plenty of demon gore, and enough lore to keep you interested, get into Doom Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE NOTE, even though I have left comments on, I am not interested in you telling me that I should put 4000 hours into a game I don't enjoy so I can "git gud", and then I would like it. That is a stupid argument. Don't be stupid. Skill is not indicative of enjoyment, and I have better things to do than bash my head on what I personally feel are bad / mediocre games on the off chance I could maybe like them one day. I have a life and don't play games in order to develop Stockholm syndrome.I played in 4k. I am using a 3080 & 5800X processor with all current drivers and patches manually installed on Windows 10 x64. All settings were set to Ultra except AA and motion blur which were off.I played with a mouse and own all of the gameplay DLC.I will update this review if I continue to play and have more to add and will leave comments on.PROS:- No crashes during my time with it.- It runs VERY well; it's obviously incredibly well optimised.- Great music that suits the world.NEUTRAL:- The hub is a cool idea, but doesn't really go anywhere. You're done with it well before the end of the game.- Some fun collectables that are cleverly hidden if you're into that sort of thing.CONS:- They pulled a Wolfenstein: New Blood; it's like they learned all the wrong lessons from the first game and made the gameplay ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. Every time I stopped playing, I did not want to come back and there was really no reward at the end. I actively regret supporting this game. The most damning thing I can say is that I own the DLC, played it for about 10 minutes, and decided I didn't want to subject myself to more of this garbage. I could actively play more that I paid for, and am choosing not to. It feels like work.- The items and terrible gameplay loop don't make any damn sense in the world provided and don't even abide by their own rules. Demons flash to show you they can be glory killed? Visual representation of what they character perceives. Yes, that makes sense. Ammo being bright neon colours? Ditto. Why can some enemy shields be taken down with plasma and some cant? Dunno. Why are some enemies immune to the BFG? Dunno. Why do some enemies take three gas  charges to take down with the chainsaw and some use one (despite running the item the same amount of time)? Dunno. Why are some immune to it completely? *SHRUG* How do I tell which is which? Memorise them all I guess. Why do Slayer weapons operate the way they do when it doesn't make sense in the context of things they've set up? Well, it's just about the only thing in the game NOT exhaustively explained to you in menu text. It makes no sense since it's in service to their awful "combat puzzle" and has no other reason to exist and is poorly signposted.- Since there's so much to keep track of, their combat loop causes you to stop dead in order to think of which of the multiple mechanics you are being forced to switch to before you may continue. If you got it wrong? Well, you're so laughably weak that you'd die and have to repeat the section.- Speaking of weak, don't bother to scour for health and armour as it was all essentially worthless. You can be reduced from full of both to dead in an instant. The almighty Doom Slayer feels like he is made from paper mache and the amount they expect you to be moving continually made the game feel more like a aerial dogfighting game than an FPS.- Know what people always love in their FPS games? Exacting platforming! Do you like dodging fire while platforming? No? Too bad!- Most of the environments are completely visually uninteresting unless you LOVE office buildings, statues, or floating combat platforms.- There were too many sub-items you constantly had to swap back and forth for, some of which I forgot existed between plays of the game and had no purpose outside of very specific individual use cases that were made just for the item. Did anyone actually use the ice grenades? The sword? If the "combat puzzle" didn't FORCE you to use them, I wouldn't have used the flamethrower either. There was just so much cruft that didn't need to be there.- The shield & dog "wait for the green flash" enemy is one of the most annoying enemies I have faced in any game in over 35 years of gaming.- In the same vein, the final level was one of the worst levels I have played through in a AAA game. A large uninteresting tower with a hundred thousand demons? Starved for ammo? Repeating large swaths of levels? No thank you.- The story is awful and instead of glossing over it tongue-in-cheek style like they did the first game, they just put MORE story in. Everywhere. Hey, know what you want to do in a Doom game? If you said "Pause the game every 5 minutes to read what the hell is going on" then you'll love this! Remember the awesome moments from the first game where the main character would smash terminals instead of letting them spew awful exposition? It's the exact opposite of that.- Still multiple bugs, even this far after release. I got stuck in the floor on a save and had to find a workaround, stuck on the geometry multiple times, one demon was just immune to damage for some reason and wouldn't let me progress until I died...- The multiplayer is just one terrible mode. I tried it once and didn't bother again.CONCLUSION:One of my biggest disappointments of the year. How did you screw this game up up this badly? I am mystified as to why this game is so popular.

_childDocuments_.review: "Many Demons.Such Brutal Glory Kills.Very DOOM.10/10 Doom Eternal is the sequel to Doom 2016, and it absolutely knocks it right outta the park with this one. The graphics are awesome, the gameplay is fast and fluid the glory kills are amazing and the story is great. The game throws you right into the action with no boring monologues or unnecessary waiting times. Also lets not forget the Heavy Metal music by Mick Gordon who is a legend at this stuff, it really gets you in the mood to just RipNTear Demons apart.The campaign is awesome and its definitely worth your time to go through it and just shred some demons, it contains twice amount of demons from 2016 and each with unique abilities and counters that you will need to learn. The Doom Slayer feels like a tank who just destroys anything in his path and you will be able to acquire new weapons to help you on your path of destruction to save humanity. There are many secrets in each level and do take your time to try and find them because they are worth it. During your play-through you will have challenges to complete which will award you XP in order for you to unlock cosmetics for Doom Guy and the playable characters within BattleMode.Speaking of BattleMode, its fun, addicting, fast paced and very strategic. 2 Demons against 1 Fully Loaded Slayer with a whole carnage and chaos from either side.If you enjoyed Doom 2016 and want to continue on your blood thirsty rampage then I highly recommend Doom Eternal to everyone. I just can't look back at Doom 2016 after playing this masterpiece of a game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I've never played a DOOM game before this, so take that as what you will.THIS GAME IS SO AWESOME.The story is rich with tons of lore and detail, the music makes you feel like a god, and the gameplay is so finely tuned and well made that it was the most fun shooter I'd played in a WHILE. Yes, it's challenging. Yes, it can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Yes, it can stick it up your ass before it even takes you out to dinner. But you overcome. You use your knowledge and tools and experience to push through more and more. You utilize movement, aim, weapons, abilities, and even the demons themselves to help you succeed. And this is just the singleplayer campaign. Did I mention this game has ONLINE MULTIPLAYER AS WELL?It's unique in every way, and fun in a hundred more. You will rage. You will yell. You will want to rip and tear your computer from that one combat arena or one boss you just can't beat. But while the challenge is always present, DOOM Slayer (you!) will always come out on top in the end. Death is temporary, but DOOM is Eternal. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is an amazing game, and in my opinion it's even better than Doom 2016. _childDocuments_.review: To be honest; I have mixed feelings about this game. I do feel, though, that the positives effectively outweigh this game's negatives. I'll list the aspects that I consider to be both positive and negative so you can look at each detail and decide whether or not you would enjoy such a thing.+ Each weapon has an effective use, encouraging weapon diversity through unique demon weaknesses.+ Mobility is much more in depth and detailed. Utilizing meat hooks, dashes, and specific armor upgrades, you can dance through the air dodging all kinds of attacks. It fits this game's arcade-esque style, and it's extremely fun.+ The Chainsaw, Flame Belch, and Glory kill mechanics all serve as stylish ways to keep you in the fight. The constant need for more ammo, armor, and health keeps you on your toes, and adds a new kind of challenging complexity to Doom's combat, in a fun way.+ The story is satisfying and captivating with a hint of legitimately funny dark humor.+ Level design is amazing. The world is immersive, and I for one actually like the tidbits of platforming this game has to offer.+ The music fits the carnage of encounters perfectly; sometimes I feel like I'm playing the trailer.+ The game has many things for you to do after you beat the game, from challenging remixes of normal levels, to collectibles and Battlemode.- Some of the enemies in this game are extremely challenging, and often times unfair on higher difficulties.- Some bosses tend to bug out, causing them not to use this game's signature "green eye" reaction time mechanic, resulting in a lot of deaths caused by random attacks you never even had the hope of dodging.- Some encounters in this game feel like abundant enemy placement for the hopes of establishing an elevated challenge, but it just comes off as annoying and needlessly tedious. One of my main examples of this issue is on an encounter I fought through on Nightmare difficulty, where three Tyrant's spawned subsequently in unique waves. After fighting the first two waves, and the first two Tyrants, the last Tyrant spawned with no fodder demons, two Cyber Mancubi, and an Arachnotron; leaving me with no way to recover my ammo and fight.Doom Eternal is, in my opinion, better than its predecessor due to its various improvements in Combat design, player mobility, and world and level design. While the game presents new challenges, it does so in a satisfying way (most of the time), leading to a unique and unmatched experience that I haven't seen many games offer in terms of comparison. If you have the money and time, I'd definitely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Though there are many changes that some might say make this the "Bionic Commando Rearmed 2" of DOOM sequels, they'd be wrong.DOOM Eternal is an evolution of the frenetically designed action FPS gameplay that fans of DOOM 2016 will recognize immediately.Instead of merely re-hashing the excellent design mechanic of encouraging the player to get in the demons' faces through glory kills restoring health and ammo directly together, DOOM Eternal breaks that mechanic apart into a bunch of other choices wherein the player has to not just go balls to the wall when low on health / ammo, but needs to strategically think as to which way their play style needs to "lean" to make the demons response suit their current needs.Need ammo? Just like before, the chainsaw is the best way to immediately refill ammo..Need health? Glory kills will get you back on your feet... but they don't replenish ammo or armor this time. Need armor? Well, you're going to have to "toast" the demon before you kill it so they bleed out armor for you.This combined with a new "weakpoint" system along with vastly improved maneuverability thanks to the double jump now being accompanied by double dashing (not the Mario Kart variety), and a wall climbing / spring-jump off platforming makes DOOM Eternal as much fun as an environmental puzzle platformer as it is an FPS.I have not finished DOOM Eternal just yet, but I will definitely be doing so. I can also say confidently, that once again, the talented folks at iD outdid themselves.It may be less of an overall surprise this time around compared to how initial anxiety surrounded the contentious pre-release period leading up to the unexpected massive success of DOOM 2016, but DOOM Eternal is nonetheless a spectacular sequel that improves upon nearly everything its direct predecessor brought to the FPS genre table.I give this masterpiece follow-up to the incredible DOOM 2016 :🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟5 Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of trouble when I started Doom Eternal, compared to playing 2016. But it felt highly polished, like maybe it was a really good game but wasn't working for me personally. I stuck with it, and by the end of the main game I could confidently say, Doom Eternal is probably good game, it's just a very bad Doom game.I persevered, and dug into the DLC, determined to see everything it had to offer. I've kept considering my complaints, reviewing the level design and combat loop, and I've reevaluated my position. Doom Eternal is just a bad game.It wants to do too many things, all the time, every time, and if you can't handle every one of them the right way and fast enough, you'll fail. That's not an FPS game, that's DDR. Doom Eternal is Simon Says played at insane speed, where if you press the wrong button or miss a prompt you get an electric shock and start over from the last checkpoint. Grenades, ice bombs, flame belch, blood punch, everything is on a timer and has to be used every time it's up, in the right way against the right enemy. Every demon has a weakness, if you use the wrong gun you'll be out of ammo and taking too much damage because you're taking too long. Always juggling guns, always slamming cooldowns like you're in an MMO raid.I remember 2016's designers specifically talking about "combat fatigue", where you need to pace things out and not run every fight at max performance, or the player will burn out and get bored no matter how many lights are flashing. Eternal feels specifically designed in the opposite direction; no reprieve, max challenge every encounter, nonstop major encounters. I started out frustrated, now I'm just tired.Lots of people seem to like that, they get a huge rush from the nonstop flash, but it's no surprise to me how DT has become the divisive marmite of the series; you either love it and rave about it, or it leaves a nauseating taste in your mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: Started out with the game requiring you to make a Bethesda-Account and no obvious way to skip it. Though this is definitely not great, I can live with it and made an account.But the update today adds  to the game. It requires you to install a kernel mode driver, which is a piece of software that runs with basically . It then collects low-level information about what is happening on your system and sends that information to an Amazon-server which analyses the data and decides whether you are allowed to play the game. It is not clear what kind of data exactly is collected. Denuvo claims that it is benign data collection, but there is no way for you or me to verify this claim. The most problematic part is that  not just the multiplayer, which is entirely unnecessary. This is actually my main complaint. I could accept this, if it was just required for playing multiplayer, which I don't care about. But needing to run such an intrusive data collection system on your machine just to play a single player game is a deal-breaker for me.If you are thinking about buying this game, then please take a moment to consider if you are okay with this. If you are not, then don't buy it until the singleplayer campaign is playable without it. Unfortunately it is too late for me to get a refund, but I hope that this causes enough noise for Bethesda to reconsider and only require the DRM for the multiplayer portion of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: gave it another 12 hours and that's it; uninstallingGreat graphics; my complaint is with the design decisions. The glory kill mechanism (which in itself is gory and a lot of fun) is made mandatory by the paucity of ammo, the relative weakness of the weapons, and the confined spaces. But this moves the dynamic of the game away from the classic DOOM model.We all want to recapture the feeling of the original DOOM: of being so scared that you bum-rush a ton of monsters in a killing frenzy. But in the original DOOM you could always MOVE; fear led to movement which led to combat, which led to victory or death. Here many encounters are simply impossible until you lose enough that the game scales back the difficulty. Unable to run &out of ammo, you just give up, respawn and try again. Once or twice builds excitement, but thereafter the game becomes a chore.Similarly, the jumping puzzles are inane momentum killers -- this is DOOM, not Tomb Raider. The maps are unintuitive and (oddly) uninspired. The levels are beautifully detailed, but because the gameplay dictates such close combat, it's impossible to get a sense of their space. Quite often you do nothing more than move away from the present danger. You are not going *there* to do *that*. The sense of one's agency as an ass-kicker is thereby greatly diminished.The RPG/character improvement elements are pointless but harmless. And the backstory is tl;dr but similarly optional. But here's a minor complaint about the narrative. In the original DOOM, I was actually frightened that _maybe_ my computer had actually travelled to hell. Here, the forces of hell are revealed to be just another kind of alien invader, like the Strogg. Abandoning the supernatural removes an unsettling and nostalgic frisson of evil-ness. This is hell like the Battle of Falluja was hell, not like the cover art for Reign in Blood.For a game this expensive and for a company that's had ~30 years to get it right, it's a little depressing. I really want to love this game, but I don't.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of stuff has been said about Doom Eternal both by hardcore fans and by the whole crowd of people preferring Doom 2016 and it is important to understand where both arguments come from. Doom Eternal is closer to a character action game like Devil May Cry than to regular FPS and actually it was this way in Doom 2016. Doom 2016 attempted to promote combos of weapons and equipment and utilizing mobility and verticality in its arenas. Overall fighting demons in the last game was a rather complex technical process involving both tactical thinking and reflexes. While Doom 2016 allowed people to just bang their heads to heavy metal, blasting demons with double-barreled shotgun or gauss gun, it still was a game with much higher requirements to player's skill than the majority of FPS game of that time and as a sequel, this is the aspect Doom Eternal doubles down on, not mindless violent fun the series is known for.This is the reason a lot of people don't like this game - it has a set of rules players have to abide by and for those who don't understand those rules ... well, the game can be enjoyable, but not on Doom 2016 level. And I'm not saying they're wrong, I'm saying they come with a perspective that they shouldn't be forced to intimately learn the game they're playing and that for them this kind of stricter rules are a sign of bad game design, they feel that a game punishing them for playing it wrong limits their agency and I wholeheartedly think that it is a valid perspective.I also disagree with it completely.Once a player learns the rules of the game, once he understands the interplay between weapons, abilities, and enemies Doom Eternal becomes vastly more enjoyable than Doom 2016. It's so much more complex, dynamic, fast, and filled with adrenaline that in harder arenas you feel like an action movie hero despite - and even because of - the fact that you're usually one mistake away from death. Limitations inherent to game's rules (being it stricter ammo limit and bigger emphasise on cooldown-based abilities and mobility) actually promote creativity and technical skill of using different tools and weapons - if you don't believe me, compare videos of how the game was played at release and how it's played now, how less popular mods and weapons caught second wind when players start experimenting with them. Honestly despite being more punishing Doom Eternal has much more variety in combat than 2016. But it all takes learning and getting used to, player has to suffer for some time to overcome the entrance barrier and get into a mindset and skillset where the game becomes incredibly fun and some people just don't want to put time into the game to get there, which is completely their right.And no, despite being a huge fan, I don't think the game is flawless. It stumbles a lot, has some questionable level- and encounter design decisions both in the vanilla game and its DLC. Platfroming is mostly fine apart from some parts of some levels. The storyline is pretty much a mix between Warhammer 40k fanfiction and silly anime at this point and bosses were mediocre at best, but all of it didn't ruin the game for me at all.Overall the "Am I going to enjoy Doom Eternal?" question boils down to "What kind of a sequel to Doom 2016 do you want to play?". The one where you can bang your head even harder to even louder industrial metal and rip even bigger demons while tearing their even bigger guts without almost any thought about cooldowns, ammo counts, and specific algorithms for killing specific enemies? Eh, turn the difficulty down and go ahead, the game is still fun and actually EXTREMELY accessible on lower difficulties, so much that even a new FPS player can beat it no problem. Just be prepared that some parts will be frustrating or even downright infuriating.The one which expands the last game's combat system and puts you into the environment where you HAVE to use your every move, manage every ability with its cooldown, every weapon with its limited ammo count, the one that makes killing enemies even more of a technical process? Are you one of those who caught the DMC-Esque vibe from Doom 2016 but found it a bit too surface-level to become really great? Well, this is a game for you. It certainly was for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal delivers stunning graphics, bone-rattling sound design, a headbanging soundtrack, and gloriously gory combat.  It's a demanding game that rewards skill and strategic thinking; hardcore fans will find a nearly limitless skill ceiling. However, casual players like myself will find that even the easiest difficulties demand adherence to a rigid, resource-focused combat loop. This contrasts with DOOM 2016's freer, more arena-shooter style where you could blast away with your favorite gun.While I concede Eternal's design likely gives it greater replayability, I missed simply having a blast with an overflowing chaingun.I played through the entire campaign and expansions on the  launcher including a good chunk on Nightmare difficulty on my first run before giving up when the Tyrant's started appearing and switching to Easy. Ultimately, it just didn't feel like the DOOM I grew up with (my first experience was Final DOOM on PS1). I expected more freedom in how I chose to tackle the demon hordes.Eternal is objectively an outstanding game, a masterpiece of its genre. But for long-time DOOM fans, the more tactical approach might not scratch the same itch. As a high-level gaming experience, it's a 10/10. However, for nostalgic DOOM fans, it's closer to a 6/10. If there was a "boomer" mode this might be one of the best games I'd ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is one of the most addicting games that came out within the last years.Like most games from id Software it focuses on the fighting mechanics and it absolutely excels at that. The resource management system forces the player to think while battling the hellish hordes: incinerate enemies for armor, glory-kill demons for health and use the chainsaw on them for ammo - it keeps every fight intense and yes, this system suits Doom well and refines the Doom-dance to its maximum level.The controls are precise and every time the Slayer dies, the player knows exactly what went wrong. The first three levels can be a bit uninspiring at first since the Slayer does only have a very little part of his arsenal at his disposal yet and thus, the gameplay does not unfold its full potential at that time.The infamous Jump & Run passages are annoying, yes - but not that bad, once you get the hang of it and that is going to happen quite early on.Doom Eternal brings a very interesting lore to the table which adds a lot of depth to its world. While it is completely optional to read, well... you have to read it - and read a lot. The happenings during the cutscenes only make sense when you know the whole background of what happened so far. But it is almost unbearable to read every lore page right away because that breaks the flow. But as soon as it is read, it fulfils a Doom-fan's wishes and all the happenings and confrontations suddenly become more intense.The multiplayer mode is a nice addition to the superb campaign but clearly stands in its shadow. The idea behind the asymmetric battle is easy to learn and each match is a rather short one. It is quite fun to play, but not the main reason for buying Doom Eternal in the first place.So why is it an addictive game, like written above? Because of its campaign, its gameplay and challenges. I finished the campaign multiple times so far with a lot more runs to come. And I can't wait for the two announced DLC episodes and I still hope for mod support, because I want MORE!Thank you for making this game, id Software! You exceled yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best first-person shooter I have ever played. hands. down. To why I say this is multiple reasons from the amazing level design to the thrash worthy music and the heart-thumping combat.(btw this is a sizeable review so fair warning)combatFirst and foremost the most important part of the equation that makes doom so thoroughly enjoyable is the combat. Someone at ID software must have gotten the gift of God himself as I’ve never seen combat flow so well, be so mechanically deep, and be so easy to understand. To put into perspective games like COD or Wolfenstein have much simpler run and gun mechanics where one weapon may do X amount of damage or do a set amount of damage but all do virtually the same thing, and that’s what they are, just weapons, but in doom, every weapon you get is a tool that has its specific use to help amplify the efficiency of your slaughter. An example of this is the super shotgun with its meat hook and powerful damage, this gun can allow you so much versatility as you grapple to demons and swing around the arena all the while doing massive damage, then you could switch to your ballista and kill three imps while mid-air and then lock on with a rocket launcher and clear the room. every gun has its use and they all exploit a demon’s particular weakness and it would be a pain staking to name every single one. This brings me to another point however as every demon is as carefully designed as Doom guy’s weapons all with their unique animations, look, attacks, and weak points that you can use to your advantage. This is just scratching the surface to doom depth, but how does the combat feel? well, one word, BADASS. dooms fast-paced and gory flow keeps you engaged at all times, as said before every gadget and thing you have at your disposable has a crucial purpose like the flame belch giving armor, glory kills giving health, and chainsaw giving ammo, all to help manage resources all the while animations play of you splitting apart demons with your bare hands. Another thing to mention is how gamey Doom plays, instead of fixating on hyper-realism and story like most modern AAA games, Doom Eternal shows respect to its routes in the original installments back in the ‘90s with classic power-ups and in your face humor and the complete suspension of belief. Maps and progressionWhere doom excels in amazingly deep combat and mechanics, it wouldn’t be anywhere without this game’s stellar map design. Every level and every nook and cranny is lovingly and painstakingly designed to fit every facet of the game. Dooms levels act as the support for the game as these are what carry you through the game, every level has secrets and collectible around every corner like little toy versions of the various demons to gameplay aiding enhancements. These collectibles aren’t tedious to retrieve though, they sometimes require small puzzles that only require a little outside of the box thinking and are rewarding to hunt after, usually I’m the kind of player that skips optional side objectives for the main course, but there is so much content here that it feels like a second full course meal that I wanted to devour, so in lamens terms, this is the first game I’ve felt compelled to 100%. Now the side objectives are nice and all but IDs designing of combat arenas is immaculate, every phase of the arenas exudes the opportunity to constantly outsmart and outmaneuver your enemies.musicHOLY F***K THIS IS THE BEST GAME SOUNDTRACK EVER PRODUCED. mhm let me compose myself, to put it simply, Mick Gordon is a genius, his heavy metal synths mixed with chainsaws and 8 string guitars just wows me, how someone can put together such a fitting track and make it good on its own deserves a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grammy, like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This is the only game soundtrack that I unironically turn on to headbang or workout to, its such a hype soundtrack that it does more than just be good music, it sucks you into the experience. When the only thing they fear is you kick in your entire body will immediately feel like you just got a lethal dose of steroids and you immediately decimate everyone. I also tend to credit this soundtrack to raising my sit-up and push-up count from being 10 at a time to being over 200, I will unironically credit this soundtrack for getting me in shape.conclusionsthere is only so much you can fit into a steam review, but the case and point this game is a must-buy for anyone ever, it disheartens me that this game didn’t win the game of the year where I feel ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game journalism favoring mediocre experiences like the last of us 2 caused this game not to be held as high as I believe it could’ve been. this game has problems, yes, but are they enough to mention? no, not at all. to call this game perfect would be an understatement, it is extraordinary, only does a game like this come around once in the gaming generation and I feel everyone should experience this title, now excuse me while I stab myself full of audio steroids and do intense workouts.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fresh migrant from the Bethesda Launcher, I feel it’s my job to add yet another review to the pile and let everyone know my feelings about Doom Eternal. I obviously had high expectations when I bought the Collector’s Edition to get a cool helmet that doesn’t fit my head and a cassette tape of weird monster sounds, but at least now I don’t have to look at the Bethesda Launcher anymore.However, to light things up and get them nice and controversial, let me begin by saying – I think Doom Eternal is better than Doom 2016. Doom Eternal is Better Than Doom 2016: That’s a lot to say because I loved Doom 2016 for its ability to revive the franchise and deliver the feel of the classic raucous and visceral experience while still bringing something entirely new to the table. It’s a game that made the Doom Guy into the Doom Slayer and didn’t even stop to let you ask why. Doom Eternal didn’t have to build that transition though. The developers could have just taken the template they established in 2016 and slapped more content on it and few would have complained. Yet, they chose to craft a game that demanded more interaction, rewarded skill and practice, and paid off by capturing the vicious excellence of the previous game while giving dedicated players the challenge they always wanted.Doom Eternal expands on the skills of the Doom Slayer by giving him tools like the flamethrower and the blood punch – while also adding weak points to the familiar set of enemies. They also created level design with much more verticality and gave the Slayer a significant increase in maneuverability. These features let the player learn to use these tools skillfully to create a much richer gameplay experience. On top of that, the combination of an expanding base/hub that steadily unlocks with your success and an exploration of a still relatively small but interesting story made the game addictive almost immediately. Even with its overwhelming assault on the senses and significantly increased challenge, it was hard to put down.Of course, since my initial rampage through the campaign and subsequent cooling over the past two years, I haven’t explored recent changes as thoroughly. My early experiences with Battlemode were enjoyable and gave me quite a few additional hours in the game, but overall, it was clunky and involved an unexpected amount of lead-in time for only three players. It almost seemed as though you’d spend as much time picking characters, loading, watching intros, and waiting to start as you would in the actual match. Sometimes the inactive parts were even longer if one side was particularly skilled (or unskilled) – which was fairly common. “Best of Five” would usually just be a three-match sweep that might not even make it that far with rage-quits.Playing Battlemode more recently, they have taken some steps to improve the flow, like eliminating the “vote” section for rematch or shuffle which rarely ever resulted in an additional match. However, time is almost always the enemy of a healthy multiplayer population and that means longer waits for matches, a higher chance of mismatched skill levels, and sometimes matchmaking giving you nothing at all. Even with the additional Demon class and tons of balancing changes, it’s still a dice roll whether you’ll get a competitive match with shifting tactics or a demoralizing stomp.Luckily though, id Software added more than just some updates to their sole multiplayer mode. They’ve also tossed in a few more extremely challenging master levels as well as a new “Horde Mode.” This was the replacement for the “Invasion” mode which would have worked like the familiar Dark Souls invasion where a player would show up in your game to try to kick your ass – except this time with Demons. The Horde Mode, however, sort of works vaguely similar to Doom 2016’s Arcade mode, but is more focused on ‘arena’ fights and a limited variety of events like platforming, coin collecting, and demon blasting under some unique circumstances. You’re also required to progress through this mode with limited weapons that unlock as you go. All of your actions in this have point values with the goal of achieving a worthwhile final score – though given my score’s placement on the leaderboards, I definitely need some practice.  However, this provides a unique challenge for those that have become intimately familiar with the campaign and master levels.With these noteworthy changes, the already robust core game, the two story-centric DLCs released, and of course, a soul-melting soundtrack, Doom Eternal went from GOTY level of quality to something truly legendary. It’s great to see a sequel that breaks new ground rather than safely iterates to prevent shocking their playerbase. Even though it lost some of the gritty feel from the original, it gained so much gameplay variety and overall breadth that it was a worthy tradeoff. My only hope is that id Software continues to be unafraid of the scrutiny that comes with change and builds the future of this franchise with as much of a focus on powerful enthralling gameplay. Until then, we can all continue to enjoy the rich game that Doom Eternal has become.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a very good FPS here somewhere. Unfortunately, it is buried under layer upon layer of useless upgrades and skill trees, forced platforming, and worst of all, the ever-present resource management: ammo, health, and armor are intentionally scarce, and you are forced to use special attacks to refill. To some that may be fun, to me it just makes the whole experience feel incredibly clunky and unnatural, interrupting the flow of the game rather than adding to it. While we are on the subject, the number of special attacks is excessive: chainsaw, flamethrower, glory kills, blood punch... keep it simple will you? It's a Doom game, I came here to blast demons away with a double barreled shotgun, I don't want to have to memorize half a dozen key bindings. Then there's the platforming: I like the idea of double jumps, climbing, dashing, somersaulting. Those are all things which, in moderation, would have been a great addition to the game, but sadly they got carried away, and often you find yourself spending more time jumping than shooting - again, this is a Doom game, I came here to fry hordes of demons with a BFG, not to re-enact Nadia Comaneci's perfect 10 at the Montreal Olympics. Probably as a consequence of this forced platforming, the levels also feel very linear.The story is also a significant let down: they turned the tech-occult theme of previous Doom games into a sort of dark fantasy mishmash with kings, priests, gothic churches, and similar elements which might have been great in another game, but which simply do not blend at all with the Doom lore. The main character himself is disappointing: in Doom 2016, through some excellent use of environmental storytelling and brief cutscenes of the Slayer punching and smashing his surroundings, you felt like fury incarnate. Here... meh. The storytelling is also subpar: in 2016 you knew who the main villain was within minutes of starting the game, here, I've played the game for seven hours and I'm still not sure who or what I'm trying to find - something to do with some priests?Overall, Doom Eternal feels bloated and clunky. That said, it is not a terrible game. It is a major step back in the series, and it is also a major disappointment, given how much potential was wasted due to poor game mechanics, but it is definitely not all bad. There are some enjoyable moments here and there: when the fighting picks up and you don't immediately run out of ammo, it can be entertaining. Just don't buy it at full price.---Addendum: I forced myself to finish the game. I only did the campaign because I don't care for multiplayer. I stand by what I wrote: when you are in the thick of the fight it can be entertaining, and once you get the hang of it you even stop running out of ammo (protip: dash, dash, chainsaw), but the glaring issues I saw in my first hours of play only got worse.The platforming and puzzles became so annoying I almost quit several times. I do not know how much time overall I spent jumping around like a frog, or frustratedly looking in every direction, searching for a climbing wall or a horizontal bar that might get me to the next cluster of demons, but it definitely felt like hours, and it probably was. All that time spent not shooting anything and engaged in activities which would have been better suited to a Mario game, was time in which Doom Eternal was failing utterly at its main purpose: being a first person .Then there's the whole "you must only play the way we want" attitude. This was already evident in the forced chainsaw-flamethrower-ice bomb mechanics, but it became even more annoying with the marauders: they're really not that difficult to kill, they're just... boring: there is a certain distance you have to keep, and there is only a specific time window during which they are vulnerable to your attacks. There is absolutely no room for doing things any way other than what the developers decided. And don't even get me started on the Khan Maykr. Once again, the experience feels incredibly mechanical and artificial.The story and the atmosphere... eh. More priests, more fantasy environments, some clichés about . It's all a convoluted mess. Where Doom 2016 was almost lovecraftian in hinting at the unseen and the unspeakable ("They promised me so much"), this was in-your-face and comic book-ish, and I cringed every time the UAC hologram talked. Even the "evil priests" sound petulant rather than scary, definitely not something you would expect from literal Hell. All this nonsense is canon in the same way that midichlorians are canon: it simply does not fit with the rest of the story, it severely hinders suspension of disbelief, and I hope it will be quietly ignored in future games. Speaking of disbelief: what's with "empowered demons" who "killed another player"? This is a single player game, I don't want to know about other players, this has to be the most immersion-killing thing I've seen in a game! What were they thinking?To conclude: several times while playing Doom Eternal I had the distinct feeling that, in some posh executive's office at id/Bethesda, some of the suits decided that rather than improving upon the previous game, the surest way to sell more copies would be to expand the target market by including gameplay elements which may attract people new to the franchise or even to the genre. Unfortunately, the end result is a Frankenstein monster of a game which tries to be too many things at once, and fails to deliver the kind of experience a lot of older fans have come to expect. There are still moments of absolute brilliance, namely when you are given lots of guns and lots of very angry, very mobile targets, but that just adds to my disappointment, because if this game had just tried to be Doom, instead of Doom Raider or Assassin's Doom, it could have been really good.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay has changed up a little bit from its predecessor with a couple of new features.1.  It now has a minimum of 1 gas that is always regenerated. This encourages the use of the chainsaw on smaller enemies throughout the game to gainammo back, especially with lack of ammo compared to 2016, which I personally liked a lot. 2.   The dash feature adds a new level of maneuverability to the game where you can get out of a sticky situation very quickly,or use it to your advantage in some of the various platforming sections in the game. I found myself using this feature a lot in the fighting sections of the game. Another movementrelated change that was added was the hook on the super shotgun, with this feature you can hook to enemies from certain distances away and use that to swing around the arena to gainanother tactical advantage. This feature was so cool to use as you were flying around the map with your dash, and double jump. 3.  one of my personal favorite features in the game is the utilization for EVERY weapon in your arsenal. In Doom 2016 I found myself resortingto the Super Shotgun and not using anything else in my arsenal, unless I ran out of ammo. In Doom Eternal I constantly was switching weapons, utilizing every weapon for certainsituations and I absolutely loved it. I felt variety and its great. Especially with how enemies now have weak points you can destroy to your advantage. ranging from the rockets on the revenants,the cannons on the mancubus, and even the plasma shields on the demon soldiers. A very welcome feature to me.  Does it live up to the hype Doom 2016s soundtrack gave us? The music in Doom Eternal is something I’ve been anticipating since Doom 2016s soundtrack mesmerized me. This soundtrack, in my opinion, is even better than its predecessor. And that is saying a lot, because Doom 2016s soundtrack was my favorite videogame soundtrack.With the haunting screams from the Metal choir ringing in the background, To the glitchy, ear deafening Djenty guitars that Blair over your demonic carnage. Mick Gordon has somehow outdone himself and it is insane. This soundtrack is something I will be blasting constantly once I’m able to get my hands on a physical or streaming copy.  I’m not going to get too much into the story, but I thought it would be good to at least say something about it. Hell has now invaded earth, Doom guy must stop it. That’s the gist of what I’m going to go into the story itself. It was cool to hear some more voice acting, and even see the Doom slayer himself in some cutscenes but overall, I don’t think a lot of people come to Doom for the story which is fine, because for what it is, it’s not bad! And the most important thing is it doesn’t take anything away from the gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to break the standard love or hate of this game and say that it is an acquired taste. You need to give it a lot of effort for the real fun to actually shine through. Doom 2016 was the ultimate instant gratification shooter, and honestly much more of a power fantasy than Eternal. Eternal's satisfaction comes from its ability to make you absolutely HATE its enemies, which then makes killing them that much more satisfying. I'm looking at you, Marauder. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ piece of ♥♥♥♥.Eternal is unlike any shooter I have ever played, including Doom 2016. It throws everything it possibly can at you, and forces you to follow its rhythm or be immediately and brutally punished (at least on higher difficulties). It doesn't matter if you're normally good at shooters, Eternal requires you to learn its rhythm and utilize every resource possible to succeed.  When you're playing, you may think to yourself, "they wouldn't do that to me, would they?" and then they do. And then they do more.  By the end of the game, you're fighting so many enemies that your BFG won't work as a get out of jail free card anymore. You have to depend purely on skill to muscle your way through every fight, or die.The sheer amount of abilities and utilities to keep track of requires excellent muscle memory, because you need it all.  Where my comment about Eternal being an acquired taste comes in, is that I really genuinely don't think the game was that fun until I really started pulling everything together into one fluid system of battle. Initially, fights felt like a chore, there was way too much to keep track of, and all of the enemies felt like bullet sponges. But once I got the hang of actually using blood punch, grenades, and eventually quick switching, it was a whole different ballgame. You start to pick up on the little sounds your suit makes when your chainsaw and grenades refill. You start to be able to discern when to pick off weak enemies, and when to use power weapons to take down high-priority targets. Your movement becomes more purposely and fluid. And after you figure it out and beat the game, you immediately want to go back and give it another try on higher difficulty.In regards to platforming, I think it was mostly fun, and a nice change of pace. There are some parts that get somewhat tedious, but once you've played through once, you'll be able to blaze through them. Yes, the underwater parts are trash, but 5 minutes of trash for a 12-15 hour solo campaign isn't enough to bother me. My opinion of Battlemode may be a little controversial... but it my genuine opinion that most people who don't like it, don't like it because they're bad. It's fun as hell, give it a REAL chance (it took me 10 games to really see what it was all about) and you will absolutely fall in love. Just be prepared to have your ass handed to you for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal wasn't exactly what I was expecting and is a lot different than Doom 2016.  Initially I was really disappointed in the first few hours because I was still clinging on to old ideas instead of trying to embrace the new stuff and take the time to fully understand each demon's weaknesses along with making full use of all the tools given to me.  Once I got a better understanding of the game's systems, the fun really multiplied as Eternal is much more challenging than 2016 and you have to play faster and smarter than in the previous game in order to win.  Eternal is a good followup game if you are part of the hardcore crowd that gets their jollies playing Nightmare mode and you think 2016's Nightmare mode was too easy.  You can no longer overly rely on one weapon for an entire fight due to lower ammo pools and you have to use your chainsaw more to stay on top of ammo reserves.  This change along with adding weaknesses to enemies makes a world of change, where some might have preferred the more simple system of Doom 2016, here it has changed the game radically and there is more setplay involved with making sure you use x ammo for y enemy.  You really have to drop most of your Doom 2016 knowledge and be ready to jump in to a harder game, maybe get kicked around a bit before things start to click.  If you wanted a harder more challenging game than Doom 2016, you should pick this game up.  If you liked the more simple style of 2016, approach with caution and MAYBE wait for a sale or watch some videos to see if it's something you want to get if you were mainly an easy/normal difficulty type of player in Doom 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review of the single player campaign.In doom eternal you will traverse between gorgeous levels and kill demons while moving. About five times per level you will enter an arena where you have to kill all the demons that spawn in order to advance. In practically every level there are a few secret encounters and collectibles, if you don't mind slowing the pace of the game in order to look for them.I found the gameplay to be extremely fun. There are many mechanics at play and it can get confusing at first, maybe even frustrating, but once you get the hang of things and have all your equipment, you will find the combination of weapons (and weapon mods) that suit your style and use them to destroy demons. You are forced to use at least some of your arsenal because of the low ammo count on weapons and the methods of refilling being tied to a cooldown or finding ammo scattered in the world.The game also has a dash mechanic which I feel not many mention but it's a welcome addition that makes the combat feel even more frenetic and highlights that your positioning is key: you have to keep moving. Being static for more that a few seconds is a death sentence.If you are new to doom games, or shooters in general, you'll find yourself dying a lot on normal mode at the start. But persevering, and maybe even increasing the difficulty when you feel comfortable, makes finishing each encounter a rewarding experience. On the second highest difficulty you have to master all the mechanics of the game, be able to cycle trough your weapons on demand and exploit the weakness of your enemies in order to succeed, and succeeding is extremely satisfying. If you didn't beat the game on nightmare, I highly recommend replaying it on that difficulty.The greatest downside of the game, for me at least, is that you need a bethesda account in order to play the game, even single player. The only workaround I found is to start steam offline and play the game that way, but you are locked out of multiplayer and of steam cards.Overall doom eternal is a fun, fast paced, adrenaline filled experience with a great soundtrack and game mechanics that make you use great part of your arsenal in order to be victorious. If the low ammo count and need of a bethesda account didn't turn you off (it certainly did for me until I knew how to circumvent it), then it should be a no brainer to play. If you are still indecisive, at least consider getting it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly the best example of what a sequel should be.They could have easily made another DOOM 2016, but instead they looked at what they had done and sought out to improve everything that was wrong and further improve what was right.No more long hallways filled with nothing, here's a platforming segment to keep you engaged.No more using the same weapon, ammo has been restricted and you MUST swap to keep going.Chainsaw is more predominant simply due to the fact it refills on its own, easing the tighter ammo.Each and every level stands out far more than they did in 2016, rather than have everything be varying shades brown and red, you see a much wider variety of colors and environments.All of the bosses stand out, with some even joining the enemy pool later in the game. Remember the Hell Guards in 2016? Of course you don't.Even the music is far more varied than 2016, as good as it all was all of the tracks blended into each other.All of the weapon mods are far more useful than in 2016, with each feeling like a valid option. The good ones from 2016 stayed and were improved while the useless ones were replaced with a more viable option.The story is there for those who care, and as someone who does care, I personally think it's great and I can't wait to see what happens next in the upcoming DLCs.While I haven't played too much of Battlemode, I can say it's much better than what 2016 had and always has me catching my breath whenever I play.I thoroughly enjoyed DOOM 2016 and to see the devs take everything they learned from it and make the best game they could is honestly something more game companies should do nowadays.10/10, please buy.

_childDocuments_.review: In my time in hell as Doomguy, I've seen my fair share of demons and battles. But let me tell you, DOOM Eternal has taken things to a whole new level.From the moment I started playing, I knew this game was going to be epic. The graphics were top notch, with stunning visuals and animations that made the action feel even more intense. The sound design was equally impressive, with heart-pounding music and sound effects that added to the overall sense of chaos and destruction.But what really sets DOOM Eternal apart is the gameplay. The combat is both fast and brutal. You have a wide range of weapons and abilities at your disposal. The addition of new enemies and mechanics keeps things fresh and challenging, and the level design is some of the best I've seen in a first-person shooter. Each level is a meticulously crafted labyrinth of secrets and hidden areas, and the platforming elements add an extra layer of depth to the gameplay.And let's not forget the story. While DOOM Eternal may be all about the action, the story is surprisingly engaging and well written. It takes the lore of the previous games and expands on it in a meaningful way. It makes the player feel like they are part of something much bigger than just a simple demon-slaying rampage.All in all, DOOM Eternal is a must for any fan of first-person shooters or action games. It's a true masterpiece that pushes the boundaries of what's possible in gaming, and as Doomguy, I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been meaning to review this game for a while now, so here we go. DOOM Eternal has become one of my all-time favourites for a number of reasons. So, let's get to them.  As far as AAA games go, this is quite possibly the most well-optimised one I've ever played. I'd only get one instance of stutter once every 4 sessions or so. So props to the devs for making the game as stable as they could.  I didn't know how I'd feel about a more frantic and difficult experience, after playing DOOM (2016), but I ended up loving it. The combat is extremely fine-tuned, with every weapon being useful for the entirety of the game. Yeah, the slot 1 weapon stays relevant for the entire game. And the demons? They all have weaknesses to exploit. Cacodemons? Lob a grenade or shotgun sticky bomb into their mouth. Revenants, Arachnotrons and Mancubi? Shotgun sticky bomb and heavy rifle precision bolt will destroy their cannons instantly. Pinkies? Blood punch instantly kills, and if not, shoot them in the back. Hell Knights, Dread Knights and Barons? Chaingun staggers their approach. Pain Elementals? Ballista does extra damage to flying enemies. Shielded Zombies and Carcasses? Plasma gun overloads their shields, causing them to explode. And so on, and so forth. And the movement? Insanely fun. From the double jump you start with, to the double dash you get later, to the super shotgun meat hook; you get all the tools you need to zoom across the battlefield. Overall, the gameplay is visceral, and I love it.  Absolute banger! Mick Gordon has outdone himself this time, creating what's quite possibly my favourite video game soundtrack of all time. I swear, if "The Only Thing They Fear Is You" doesn't play during my funeral, I'll be a very angry future dead man. Shame Mick Gordon didn't do the soundtrack for the DLCs. The man is a national treasure.  More than a decade ago, I started losing interest in FPS games, due to almost everyone following the Call of Duty, Battlefield and Halo standard. But I feel like the release of DOOM (2016) has opened everyone's eyes on how to really make a fun FPS experience. In 2018 we got Dusk, another absolute banger of an FPS game, and Amid Evil a bit later on. And after the release of DOOM Eternal? The games just didn't stop coming. Turbo Overkill and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun released in 2023, with Turbo Overkill having very similar gameplay to Eternal, especially with the movement, and Boltgun being similar to DOOM (2016), with Ultrakill in the process of hopefully leaving early access. While I don't think the recent DOOM games are the sole reason why we've had a resurgence of fast-paced, retro-themed FPS games, I'd like to think they were a big influence.Of course, there are some things I also didn't like, or just didn't bother with...  I'll be honest, I didn't like the Ancient Gods as much as the main game, due to some new additions that contradict things the main game has taught you. For example, the Spirits. They possess enemies to make them stronger and faster. That's fine. What isn't fine is removing those demons' weaknesses. And the Spirit lacks any weaknesses itself. You're forced to use the plasma gun microwave mod to kill it, which ruins your mobility. I feel like both of those things are contradictions. I've only played both Ancient Gods DLCs once, so I won't be including them in the overall review of the game.  Never played it. Didn't care for it. Who the hell plays DOOM games for the multiplayer? Hell if I know, but it sure ain't me.Overall, DOOM Eternal is still insanely fun. I just recently beat it on Nightmare, and I had a blast. Perfect 10/10; easily my favourite FPS game of all time.

No pay to win micro-transactions, either. This is how you create a game to please newcomers and all-time fans alike. You won't regret this purchase.
