_childDocuments_.review: I want to clarify something to anyone looking at this particular review;This game is a very very different beast to any previous entry in the franchise, even Doom 2016.It has very different resource mechanics, it has a different feel to the gunplay, you prioritize things far differently, you do things differently in every regard.If you come into this trying to play it like Doom 2016 you will die. If you come into this trying to play it like any other Doom game you will die.The only things that really carry over are as follows: Chainsaw = Ammo geyser, Glory Kill = Health geyser, SSG good, Archvile mean, Mobile Sentry mod on the chaingun is extremely fun, weapon mods, grenades, don't stop moving or you'll die.The game tried new things and personally I think it succeeded at making them work.There was plenty of forewarning that this game was NOT going to be like Doom 2016, a decent sized lot of these negative reviews are from people who somehow failed to get that memo and unfortunately got the feeling that they'd been burnt as a result.It's not for everyone but the sheer speed at which this game goes is unprecedented for an FPS game, really.If you play on Nightmare a single slip-up could be a death easily, whether it be failing to keep on top of your resource juggling or simply clipping a wall at the worst possible moment.To me, it feels insanely gratifying and satisfying to play and conquer each battle, each new demon, figure out how to most effectively and efficiently use each weapon and on what demons, etc.Please, do yourself a favor and look into this game if you're thinking about grabbing it, and if you like what you see then absolutely grab it.If you don't get rock hard watching gameplay of it, then I think you'd hate what the game has to offer as a result, I'm pretty sure this is one of those games with no middle ground. Love it or hate it.Just keep this in mind while looking at other reviews, keep all the information you can get your hands on in mind and try to make as informed a purchase as you can on this one.Fully recommend it if you like what it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Doom Eternal is finally out and, while a lot of fans of original Doom 2016 have preordered it long ago, some are concerned about it’s differences from the predecessor, and for them I’m writing this review. I won’t really do a deep analysis on the game and its gameplay, because it’s not really needed, and instead will tell you about new features of Doom Eternal, point out some clear drawbacks, which came with them, and also tell my own thoughts in the end. So let’s get started:New features:1) Movement and “vertical gameplay”.The developers decided to greatly expand movement in the new title and made a semi-Quake out of new Doom. Now, except usual running and double-jumping (which we by the way now have by default), a dash and double dash were added, with the addition of wall climbing and bars to jump from on the levels.This greatly increases both movement and tactical field making the gameplay very active and intense. 2) Expanded arsenal Now apart from usual Doom weapons we have grenades, fire-thrower and crucible (and please, don’t accuse me of spoilering, everyone knew, we are gonna wield this big red sword in the new game). Though you kinda forget about them at some point, the pressure and difficulty of the game make you to use them to survive.3) New enemies, weapons and modsI’m not gonna go through all of them, I made this section just to point out that this game is not Doom 2016 with new decorations, it has it’s own new enemies and reworked weapons and their mods, and most of them will be useful throughout the game.Drawbacks:1) Battlemode only multiplayer Developers decided to remove all other mp modes because “they don’t make you feel like a Doom Slayer” and left only 1 player-controlled slayer vs 2 player-controlled demons mode. Does it serve its purpose? Mostly, but the problem is that after some hours of multiplayer, when you get the tactics for all demons, you understand that match outcome heavily depends on the Slayer skill, and the player who successfully beats the game on hard difficulties will have no problems with overcoming any demons. So, though classical deathmatch and flag capture are very old modes, they still would be nice to see in Eternal, because without them the multiplayer is gonna die out completely in several months or even weeks.2) LoreWell, developers decided to greatly expand the lore of the universe. It’s a great thing by itself, because the times of story in games compared to story in porn movies are long gone, and it’s good to see that one of the oldest shooter is finally leaving this cannon behind, but the main issue here is execution. Developers made a deep story that starts nearly at the birth of the universe but the problem is that 99% of it is neither played through levels, nor told through cutsences. It’s all written in manuscripts that are collected on the levels and then can be read in codex menu. Is anybody gonna read this? - No, most will just skip and forget about those few characters and cliffhangers they met during the actual game. And, in the end, though you become really interested in game lore, you just cant “consume” it because of boring delivery of it.My own thoughts:Well, though the game has a lot of good points and has improved since its predecessor, I didn’t really like it and... I don’t really know why.The only thing I can say for sure that the game was very irritating for me because of cut max ammo amount which has to be replenished nearly every 5 minutes and overpowered mobs like marauder, which has only 0.5 second window to be attacked and all other time they are hiding behind shield (oh and they can’t even be killed with BFG). In addition to it, the game was very difficult for me. I can’t say for sure whether the game itself became harder or I lost my shooter skills in 4 years, but the fact is that I mostly played Doom 2016 on ultra-violence without having much trouble, but I decently sucked even on hurt me plenty in Doom Eternal. And the icing on the cake were bugs, lots of them. I dunno whether the game is poorly optimized or I am very lucky, but I've got like 3 crashes, 3 falls under textures and countless enemies stuck in the walls, and though it was not critical, it has still quite affecting my game experience.  All in all, if you are fan of Doom 2016 and not against adding some features of Quake, I think you will like the new title. Just remember to set an appropriate difficulty, so the game is both not too hard and not too easy for you.

_childDocuments_.review: What is Doom Eternal? Short answer. Pure unadulterated badass demon slaying action!Long Answer. A well executed spin on the shooter genre, that aims to teach both new comers and veterans a different and unique way of approaching encounters, not only in this game, but all FPS out there. It excels at everything the 2016 Doom introduced and pushes that to a highly more adrenaline fuel rush than anything you've experienced before. It's faster, it's bigger and it's more Doom. It's a true blast to play! There is far more to unravel in Eternal than just "here is gun, make demons go boom". The game requires strategy and reflexes. When you hear that heavy metal music, it's time to fight like hell with both brains and brawn.At first glance you might think the combat is chaotic and all over the place, and truthfully that is how it's going to feel at first because you are just starting to learn "The Doom Dance". Allow me to explain. The combat in Eternal is a rhythm of satisfying executed weapon swapping, dashing, jumping and kills that puts the player in a coordinated mindset to always be on the move, shooting and managing ammo, health and armour. And this dance will be learned and understood the more you play. Don't let yourself be discouraged. You will get the hang of the visceral nature of Doom Eternal. It may at first feel the game is forcing you into a certain play style, it's actually teaching you to better manage and control the situations you are faced with.Until something finally clicks. It's going to happen. And when it does, you will be are aware of every demon, every weak point, and every weapon. You are going to be fully immersed and be completely addicted to the combat. This masterpiece of violence is going to be all you're thinking of when you are finally ready to use every tactic you've learned along the way. It's a grand spectacle of fantastic audiovisual communication to the player. The idea that no matter how much you replay it, the game challenges you to invest the time and experiment and use different methods of clearing each arena, proving how well the new formula works where you want to perfect these mechanics because they reward the player and feel accomplished for their effort. Very good game design on all fronts, and the soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fire!One of my favorite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I'm writing this, because I really thought this would be incredible, especially after the masterpiece that 2016 was. Basically, 2016 Doom was my favorite shooter of all time, and instead of addressing that games few flaws, which let's be honest, were really just nitpicks, they took a sledgehammer instead of a scalpel to the operating table.First, in addressing the Super Shotgun spam from the first game, they basically over penalize the use of any one weapon, to the point where certain weapons are basically useless against certain enemies. Then, they provide such low ammo levels (even with upgrades)  that near constant Glory Kill and Chainsaw spam are required to even maintain baseline levels of ammo. Essentially, you are forced into the play pattern that the devs want you in, not one you actually want for yourself. I can completely understand incentivizing certain weapons against certain enemies, but you are penalized to the point of uselessness. I actually like the idea of GK and CS alternating to replenish, but it is required nonstop to the point of annoyance. To be honest, it feels like the devs are saying "we know better than you, so you're going to play this way or else."Second, the platforming is completely ridiculous and overdone. The first game had too many arenas, so instead of slight tweaks to the layouts, they went full on Super Mario insane with confusing maps and overly elaborate platforming sequences. And they are EVERYWHERE. Had they been once in a blue moon, I could have tolerated it, but it seems like they way overdid the criticism of the original. Third, It somehow looks worse. Far more cartoony and less visceral than 2016. In all fairness the performance is liquid smooth, but everything just looks less sharp and brutal. The cheese is ramped up to 10, instead of the grit. Make no mistake, this is a good game, and I appreciate what Hugo and his team were going for, but in doing so completely overcompensated in addressing the concerns from the first game. 2016 didn't need a complete heart transplant, it only needed a couple stitches and bandaids. In all honesty, this might be one of the most disappointing games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man...To be honest, this game would be better if they cut it straight in half. Let me explain:The first few levels are like any start to any video game. They give you more weapons, more tools more upgrade capabilities and everything feels fresh and new and fun. They add new monster types and whatnot and it's just a normal beginning to a video game... But it isn't, this is DOOM Eternal and they want you to know that. This game does NOT start slow, it starts right where most twitch shooters end.And that's my whole critique at this game: It has to keep escalating, because it has to keep you hooked somehow. They get so desperate to escalate the gameplay, that it becomes quite overbearing and simply not fun.- There are upgrades for the suit that makes explosive barrels not hurt you, drop ammo on destruction and they respawn once. The problem is, the second half of the game barely has ANY barrels, making all these upgrades worthless and robbing you of valuable options to deal with the hordes of demons.- DOOM Eternal has a lot of "fodder" enemies, meaning they are not strong but there are tons of them. They can be a nice addition to a fight but if I got sometimes around 20-30 enemies on my screen at once, it's just too much, since you have not many weapons that deal reliable amounts of AOE damage. THis makes a lot of fights simply frustrating because you get swarmed by smaller enemies and can't concentrate on the big ones.- Enemies are fast in this game. To be honest, most of them are faster than your normal running speed. To combat this, you have to be constantly dashing and jumping. This is fun for a while until it becomes REALLY annoying. You are CONSTANTLY in the air and dashing around. You will NEVER be walking and shooting, you will ALWAYS be jumping and dashing. I can't stress this enough, this ♥♥♥♥ is ANNOYING AS ♥♥♥♥.- After you see the normal stock of DOOM mobs (zombies, hell knights, imps), they add a couple of new enemy-types. Each and every one of them has a gimmick, which quickly makes them really tedious to fight. There is a bigger version of the mancubus, called a cyber-mancubus, which you have to hit with a special attack, before you can kill him in a reasonable amount of time. There are weird snake creatures which are super fast and super nimble, you practically have to freeze them with your ice grenades. There are marauders WHICH ARE THE MOST ANNOYING PIECES OF ♥♥♥♥ EVER DESIGNED. Whenever a marauder appears, the speed and flow of the game INSTANTLY GOES DOWN TO ZERO. Antoher point I can't stress enough... WHY DESIGN AN ENEMY THAT INSTANTLY KILLS ALL FLOW OF BATTLE, WHEN YOU MAKE SUCH AN ENTRANCING GAME, WTF??!??! Anyway, the marauder is INVINCIBLE, except right before he attacks you. So you have to focus on him, SOLELY on him. And there is only one effective weapon against him, the super shotgun. He is IMMUNE TO THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BFG. So you make this weird dance that takes AGES to kill him. It's not even hard, it's just annoying.- The later levels get really hard, even on a lower difficulty. In the first levels, you encounter these things called "slayer-gates", which are supposed to be an extraordinary challenge. Well, they aren't. They are just a representation of the gameplay in the later levels. The last levels are just frustrating and I just kept playing to finish the game. I very nearly just stopped playing.- The sound design is fantastic, except for some sounds, which were made to be hysterically out of place by design. Yes, very funny plob sounds for headshotting enemies and pulling the eye out of a cacodemon. This might be up to taste, but I hated these sounds. Here I was, this demon slaughtering badass, hearing "*plop*" all around me,... ridiculous.- The ending is laughable, but again, this is up to taste.And my biggest gripe:The game gives you so many tools (chainsaw, grenade launcher, freeze grenade launcher, flamethrower) which you all HAVE to use. You can't *choose* to use them, you HAVE to use them. There is no room for interpretation. Do what the game tells you, EXACTLY what the game tells  you. They even tell you about the weakpoints of every bigger monster, because there is a DESIGNED way to take them out. You are constantly switching weapons for each demon type, because you NEED to. You can't play the game the way you want to, you can only play it the way it was exactly designed to be played.Overall, I'm gonna go back to Ultimate Doom with the Brutal Doom mod, I'm almost guaranteed to have a better time there. Plus, with the "Oblige" level generator, you have an infinite amount of content.I can not recommend DOOM Eternal. It's forced nature in everything is endearing for the first two hours, after that it's simply annoying and frustrating.If you absolutely have to play it, stop to play after you encounter the first marauder. It only goes downhill from there, and boy does it go down quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: One thing I have to say about DOOM ETERNAL, is that its positively draining experience. Relentless Action, gory Glorykills and odd uneven parts that kinda weaken the overall positive impression the game makes. Its very arcade-like, even more so than the original 2016 incarnation. What happened in the time inbetween is explained only in bits and pieces, especially the role of Samuel Hayden and his characterization seems odd at first, considering his betrayal in the previous game. Mind you, I only played 7 hours so far, so  there might be some good answers to my questions.   One thing I immediately dislike, is the excessive amount of Platforming and acrobatic interludes, which seem very alien to DOOM. Imagine playing a  grim bloody FPS, and then the game says: "Now its time for some CIRCUS! Bring out the clowns! Ah there he is, the doomguy, our resident clown-acrobat"  It seriously feels like frustrating padding of the game. I can't tell how many times I died in these sequences.  Its not motivating and  certainly not good for my keyboard, which was punished with hard hits and almost spitting at the screen. I felt during these times, that the level-designers needed some...eh..."deconstructive heavy-handed criticism" as well, that's how much anger welled up in me during these times.  These frustrating moments  were paired with glorious violent action scenes and lots of kills and gore, just how Doom is supposed to be.  Its not supposed to be Super Mario Bros. or Metroid. Definetly NOT.  I would still recommend DOOM-Eternal, but th excessive use of platforming and gaudy, super-colorful level assets + FX make it a somewhat uneven entry in the series. I was very close to not recommending this, but yeah...its mostly good and polished. Just very frustrating.   One word about the art-style and level-design. The 2016 entry felt much more like a real environment, while the 2020 levels sometimes seem very illogical. Nobody would build structures and architecture like this,the levels feel more like multiplayer-Arenas and less like real worlds you can explore. its essentially a super-gory Jump-N-Run Land with slapped-together architecture which  is just there for the gameplay, and not how a credible world would look like. This may seem like a weird thing to say, because its a game after all, but looking at Games like BIOSHOCK or DEUS EX, you get a way more "This world/reality truly exists" feeling.  You will get it when you play it for a longer time.  Its an enjoyable, good-looking but sometimes irritating and INFURIATING experience. Proceed with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing, seriously. It's everything I loved about DOOM 2016 multiplied several thousand times. I won't try to praise the game further, since plenty have already done that better then I could, I instead want to discuss some of the critiques I've been seeing from certain negative reviews.1. "The tutorial messages are annoying!" Well, you can turn off the tutorials and pop-up messages in the options. It's mind blowing to me personally that people pay so much for a PC game and never check the options. Admittedly, the tutorial messages are not great, and are very intrusive. But again, just turn them off.2. "I don't like the cutscenes!" Just skip them. If you don't like the new style of third-person cutscenes and a little bit more emphasis on story then I don't blame you, it's preference. But I personally really like what I've seen so far. Regardless, I don't see why anyone would want to give the game a negative review over cutscenes which have nothing to do with the gameplay, unless you just want attention or something.3. "It's too hard!" Yeah it's really hard, but there are several difficulty settings and there's no shame in lowering it. This is not an insult to anyone nor am I trying to make myself seem like a super experienced pro or whatever, because I'm not, but still I have over 100 hours on DOOM 2016 and thousands of hours on Counter-Strike and other similar twitchy shooters so Nightmare difficulty feels perfect for me. Games like this take a LOT of practice, but again just start on one of the lower difficulties and work your way up. And it's not like I didn't died dozens and dozens of times just on the first few levels, but the combat is so intense and rewarding that I seriously don't care if I have to restart a fight several times over to finally get it. I like that kind of thing and I feel like that's how the game was meant to be enjoyed. Now some have said that they can't find that "perfect" difficulty for them, and that DOOM 2016 felt more balanced, again I can't argue against that, it's one of those things that come down to preference. All I can say is keep practicing, if you can't get the hang of it and aren't having fun then I don't blame you. I'm loving the Nightmare difficulty so far.4. "I don't like the arcade style pickups, and I don't like the HUD!" This one is complicated and again mostly comes down to preference. DOOM 2016 had a more realistic style with it's pickups and a less colorful HUD. You can change the HUD colors in the options but I understand that some people might not be satisfied either way. It's just a little puzzling because there has been gameplay footage and trailers for DOOM Eternal for well over a year now if I'm not mistaken, and every bit of gameplay we've seen since has shown off the colorful HUD and pickups, so I don't know why it's a surprise to so many. I'm not a big fan of the HUD either, not the colors but just the general style of it but it doesn't bother me, I'm not staring at the HUD when I'm playing I'm focused on the combat. As for the pickups, whenever you light an enemy on fire and then chainsaw them, you receive both armor and ammo in the form of brightly colored pickups, and apparently people find this annoying. I think it's super satisfying but whatever, this is just a visual thing and I understand that some people don't like it. Don't understand why it warrants a negative review for the entire product though.5. "It's too gimmicky!" This is for the people who think the monkey bars, climbing mechanics and dashing are stupid tacked on ideas that add nothing to the gameplay. I have absolutely no idea why somebody wouldn't enjoy these new features. In DOOM 2016, and pretty much every DOOM game, I absolutely hate the down time between fights. You'd have a great fight, then spend the next five or ten minutes running around alone looking for keycards like an idiot. The dashing, monkey bars and climbing make everything so much more interesting and engaging, and when mixed in with the combat it's just incredible and makes for what I believe is the best combat I've ever felt in an FPS.There are other complaints people have but you get the idea. Not all, but most of these negative reviews I've seen don't even have an hour played and it just makes no sense to me. I understand that not everyone is going to love the game like I do. It's very different from DOOM 2016 and you can't just use the super shotgun the entire game with almost unlimited ammo. It's far more skill based and I think a lot of people just can't wrap their head around the more strict resource management. And as for the Bethesda log-in, yeah it's stupid as hell. But it was also confirmed to be a thing before launch and in my opinion, shouldn't reflect the product itself. It's a stupid log-in tacked on by the publisher, not the developers. Also I should mention I was having some issues with the game when I first started. It would crash on the first loading screen after beginning a campaign and after some research it turned out I had to reinstall some Vulkan drivers. If you're having technical issues please be patient and do some research first, there are a lot of people willing to help online.My whole point is, the games amazing and I seriously disagree with most of the critiques I've been seeing here.

_childDocuments_.review: completely ignoring the totally tonedeaf and on-brand for Bethesda Denuvo incident I can honestly not recommend this game in the least.tl;dr: in terms of content quality AND quantity it's just not a 60 dollar game, its barely a 30 dollar game.Apart from the killer soundtrack by Mick Gordon everything about this game feels second rate. From the hyper-linear and very stale map design to the horrendous flow-breaking platforming that feels like it was grafted on like a gorilla arm to a three legged giraffe. The same recycled weapon spread clashes horribly with the vomit of new and reworked game mechanics, all of which feel halfway realized. The most egregious system to me are the Runes, not only are three of the nine objectively better in fights but they space out the first 3 rune pickups throughout the first several levels and proceed to dump the other 6 on you in the next 45 minutes of gameplay. The graphics aren't bad but are totally uninspired, older Serious Sam games from over a decade ago on ultra quality stood out to me far more. The interesting story is one of the elements that really cemented Doom 2016 as a solid return to the spotlight for the series, and they've thrown it completely out the window in Eternal with a gonzo 'chosen one' style main plot dumbed down completely from the first game, avant-garde filmy plot/cutscene jumps and fades-to-black, and a smattering of cringe-worthy Gearbox style flavor text throughout (ha ha they're the mortally challenged don't forget). Took just under 13 hours to beat start to finish on Ultra-Violence with about 80% collectables, it just simply wasn't worth sticker price.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good, evolves on all the things that made Doom 2016 great, and adds more. Along with all the standard challenges of the FPS run and gun genre (constant movement and evasion, accuracy and quick responses and all of those skills), you'll also need to be good at weapon swapping, familiar with your entire toolkit (you WILL need every weapon in your arsenal), and good at resource management. Ammo is not rare, but it is limited, and being able to juggle ranged attacks with the chainsaw (which drops ammo), the flame belch (which drops armor) and glory kills (which refill health), is crucial. Map awareness is super important too. All in all, just a really good game. It is a shame what ID did to Mick Gordon. Never forget.

_childDocuments_.review: The pinnacle of FPS design. This is what 20+ years of FPS games have led to. If you're coming from Doom 2016 expecting it to be the same, you'll be disappointed. Doom Eternal isn't here to impress you, you're here to impress it. You'll have to Git Gud and use all the new mechanics to the max. Prioritise enemies, use the flame belch for armor, use to freeze bomb to gain distance, and use the chainsaw for ammo. Once it's firing on all cylinders, there is no other FPS like it.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant sequel to Doom 2016 that is only let down by a wet fart of a final boss. Absolutely worth your time and money if you have any love for shooters.The game more or less plays like Doom 2016. It's fast, precise and oh, so very violent. That being said there are a number of important changes from 2016. First, your powerful weapons (like the super shotgun and Gauss cannon/Ballista) now consume much more ammo, meaning they'll be something you switch to to deal with a big demon rather than using them as your main weapons like you could in 2016. This seems to have annoyed a lot of people and I sort of get why; you no longer have that care-free anti-demon rampage the previous game was praised for, since the devs wanted to make this game harder. That being said, it encourages and rewards people who are willing to put the time in to learn how the game is meant to be played. Getting stuck on an encounter for a while can be frustrating but it makes it so much more rewarding and satisfying when you actually do complete it. You feel like you have accomplished something and your skills have improved (and if you want to play with as little interruption as possible that's what the easy difficulty is for). Ammo is also reduced overall, but your ammo-generating chainsaw now recharges on its own and the game goes out of its way to spawn trash-mobs for you to chainsaw when you run low on supplies, so it balances out the difficulty as long as you can count (or at least can see the colour red). The second big change is the addition of platforming. Now, a lot of people seem to be complaining about this and I personally don't see the issue. Sure, it's not Mario 64, but it's really not bad at all. It's perfectly serviceable and there really isn't that much of it. It's more of a way to mix up the gameplay between combat encounters as opposed to the corridor walks of 2016. You'll be jumping, dashing, swinging on monkey bars and climbing occasional walls to get from place to place. It's all very easy for the most part, but a few secrets require more precise timing of jumps and dashes. They're hardly frame perfect requirements, though. The game knows that's not what you're there for, so it keeps them brief and (usually) very forgiving, with big platforms and short distances between them. Sometimes there will be a light puzzle accompanying the platforming but it's never more complex than "push button then platform then punch box to reach new area then platform more."Lastly, there is more story focus this time around. Gone is the unbroken first person perspective of 2016. There are now many more traditional cutscenes. The story itself is on the same level as 2016. Doom Slayer needs an excuse to go to the next place he can kill demons, so a maguffin or bad guy is placed in a level so Doom Slayer can go after it. Not terribly complex but there is a bit more story to sink your teeth into should you want it this time around, mostly revolving around worldbuilding and telling us more about the slayer itself. It can all be ignored if that's really not your thing.Traditional PvP is gone and has been replaced with Battlemode. It's a 2v1 mode with two players controlling some of the powerful demons from the campaign trying to take down one Slayer with a full arsenal. And the Slayer is still at advantage. I haven't played much of this mode but I have enjoyed what I have tried. It requires coordination from the demons and the Slayer has to be on their toes. It's fun and tense and doesn't seem to have any OP ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so far.If you liked 2016 you'll probably like this. In my opinion it's a much better game than 2016 and I so hope we get another one after the story DLCs are out

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible shooter with amazing shooting mechanics and lots of cool features. Using stagger, the chainsaw and the flame weapon to make enemies drop health, munition and armor works really, really well. The level design is also excellent, with  great set pieces, plenty of different enemies, good platforming and lots of secrets to discover.The most significant thing I didn't like is that enemies are bullet sponges if you don't kill them in a certain way with a specific weapon. Let me kill them with my weapon of choice, and use the stagger only when I'm in need of more health. I also don't like enemies spawning out of thin air behind me, especially with so many big enemies that require tons of bullets to kill.But despite these issues, Doom Eternal is an excellent game that makes your adrenaline rise to unseen levels. Well done id Software!

_childDocuments_.review: When the recent update hit with the new anti cheat, I was not very pleased to put it lightly. I think I share the sentiment with a lot of others that I do not want kernel level anti cheat software on my computer. Combined with the performance drops and Bethesda's track record I truly thought this game that had a great launch was being put to rest after a single month.Boy am I glad I was wrong with the recent patch fixing most if not all performance issues and the anti cheat being removed.In my opinion, this game is close to if not GOTY for me. While some of the story elements can be seen as a bit lackluster and some of the lines are in all fairness quite cheesy having been taken from the comics, I don't play Doom for the story. I play Doom for the gameplay, and it certainly delivers. Fast paced and fluid with some strategy involved, it feels awesome everytime I step into an arena. Combined with Mick Gordon's insane music, the combat is truly amazing. However, there is one small thing with the gameplay and mechanics I am not very fond of: the purple goo. I don't want to stick on the goo as it only appears in a few small sections of the game, so I won't. The platforming for me was very nice to see. I have seen criticism to the platforming and it being simple and out of place but I enjoy it because in Doom 2016, traversing the environment was just walking. The platforming makes the more relaxed bits of the game less boring for me, giving me something to do. Another problem I found with 2016 was that in the last third of the game, things became somewhat repetitive as there were no new enemies apart from the boss fights and I found you really didn't need to swap off of the super shotty and gauss cannon. This game changes that by having different weapons being effective against different enemies and continues to introduce enemies right up until the final boss fight. All of this combined makes this game less run and gun, and more run, think, then gun. And I like that. I like that using certain weapons and abilities against certain enemies gives you an advantage. I have not played the multiplayer and do not intend to so I won't touch on it.Doom Eternal is not Doom 2016. Doom 2016 has a much different... feel to it, I guess. Some weapons in 2016 are incredibly powerful while others are left behind and due to 2016 not having as many movement options such as the monkey bars or dashing I felt as if I was somewhat restricted. Also the art style in 2016 was more dark and brutish while Eternal seemed to be somewhat more arcade like. Not to say Doom 2016 or Doom Eternal are bad games, they just excel in their own ways and for me at least, Doom Eternal excels in the areas I like more so that Doom 2016. To wrap up, Doom Eternal is definitely worth your time. I got this game on sale but I would still be very happy with my purchase if I bought full price.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Doom - a game series with ups and downs for 30 years now and there aren't that many games that can look back on such a long history.With Doom Eternal and the two expansions The Ancient Goods Parts 1 and 2, the story also finds its (“worthy”) end for the time being.Yes indeed. However, this wasn't even thought about until Doom 2016, and it's even more complex than many people might think. Anyone who has carefully followed the monologue in Doom (2016) and read all the codex entries already knows this story and has enough background information to be able to enjoy Doom Eternal to the fullest.Anyone who hasn't played the predecessor should definitely do so before Eternal and anyone who is willing to absorb the information provided in the game will then know the story.For those who are interested, I posted a summary of the story in the comments due to its length.Eternal begins shortly after the events of Doom (2016). However, this time difference is not precisely defined. The Slayer has moved into the Fortress of Doom in space, which serves as his main base. How this happened remains as much a mystery as what happened in the meantime. With the support of the AI VEGA from the predecessor, the Slayer is now hunting the hell priests who are the masterminds of the demon invasion on earth. But that won't be the only thing that will keep the Slayer busy on his way because as the game progresses he will repeatedly be confronted with his past as well as his first battle in which the Doom Marine became the Slayer we know and the famous sentence “Rip and Tear, until it is done” comes from.In addition, Eternal, unlike its predecessor, relies on more cutscenes in which the Slayer himself is actively staged and the principle of an active story telling is applied. This reveals more background information about the actions of the demons and the circumstances and the player is confronted with stories and explanations that primarily serve to give the whole thing a framework for the actions that are about to take place. There is also a lot to read. For those who have no real interest in the story and don't want to read every codex entry, you will find out the most important things in the various cutscenes and the messages from the characters.In this game, the formula of its predecessor has been expanded again. The double jump is available from the start and the Slayer also receives a dash that is not just intended for reaching secrets or game passages. This will become a good friend and offer even more mobility in battle. In addition, the Glory Kill mechanics and the chainsaw continue to celebrate many broken bones on the battlefield.Especially when it comes to the double jump and the dash, there is an incredible, unique and fluid combat feeling in which long-range fire and brutal close combat alternate. Covering or retreating is completely pointless here. If something like ammunition or armor is missing, there is only one right path: moving forward inexorably.Thanks to the new movements and swinging on poles, the arenas now offer significantly more vertical action because the fighting areas are often crossed by high platforms or take place on a large cliff where you fight your way from top to bottom. Many of these elements can be used to outmaneuver the demons and attack them from the side, behind or above. What's pretty cool is that there are several runes that either improve movement in the air or slow everything down when you press the alternative fire button, which leads to really spectacular slow-motion maneuvers when jumping.The range of facets of the carnage are almost endless thanks to explosive or frost grenades and the alternative fire modes that are unlocked as upgrade boxes in the areas and can be swapped out at the touch of a button, adding to the already great weapons.But not only the challenging combat but also the level design and the variety can score even more here compared to its predecessor. The locations are just visually great and really offer something to look at in a wide variety of settings. The game isn't dark, in fact it's brightly colored, which is really great because it covers the same grey-brown soup with colors that don't harm the hellish design in any way.The Fortress of Doom is also fantastically designed and, in addition to storing the unlocked secrets, also offers enough excitement to explore. You can also use the collected Sentinel batteries to unlock upgrades for weapons and the Preator suit, and there are skins for the suit like the super cool outfit of the Marine from Doom (1993)A big difference to Doom (2016), which was missing towards the end, is the variation in the gameplay. While in the predecessor you ran from arena to arena, Eternal also requires more skill. Since you can climb special walls here and the double jump and dash are ideal for overcoming large abysses, there are sections in which the game plays almost like a classic action adventure. Boxes have to be moved, switches have to be activated, simple environmental puzzles have to be solved and tricky jumping passages have to be completed. And that's damn cool, but unfortunately in some cases it's sometimes too much of a good thing. At least for my taste because in some passages you don't know how to jump until you get to the next platform, which then - oh wonder - falls into the lava after a while. But when what feels like the hundredth jump-and-run passage comes along, then at some point it's enough.But this slows down the quick arena shooting a bit, giving you time to breathe and concentrate on finding secrets. In addition to collecting items, soundtracks or cheat codes, there are also valuable upgrade points or crystals for the suit, the locations of which are automatically displayed on the clear and freely rotatable map so that you can easily return to the secrets you have not found.Whether you think Doom is good or bad. The games all have one thing in common. They always run perfectly, the controls are precise and the weapons feel really good. And here, if you belong to the Slayers Club, you will be rewarded with various things for playing. The Slayer, the Hud and everything that has to do with it can be adapted to your own wishes and you will literally be showered with free cosmetics. When it comes to this, some other game developers could take a good look at this, because everything is available here at no additional cost. In addition, the game is always up to date and work is constantly being done on it and that is more than just exemplary.For me, Doom Eternal is one of the best shooters of this generation with a unique flow in combat, great arenas, extensive weapons, numerous and different enemies, impressive locations and a brutal soundtrack, which takes arena shooters to a new level.✔ great level and monster design✔ great soundtrack✔ smooth and uncompromising gameplay✔ clever AI✔ precise controls✔ Effective weapon modes and upgrades✔ interesting mythology✔ lots of humor✔ extensive campaign✔ many hidden secrets✔ many customization options✔ Photo mode✔ tactical and quick battles✔ optional time trials and battle arenas✘ Story is told weakly✘ partly monotonous corridors✘ too many acrobaticsRevised and reposted: January 15, 2024

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This game managed to improve the well established fps formula born with Doom and Quake by creating one of the best fps ever made. This game literally leaves you BREATHLESS with its extreme and intense gameplay, especially at the highest difficulties. The difference with the previous 2016 entry is night and day, as Doom 2016 looks plain and simple in comparison. It's true that the first moments here will be painful and ragequitting inducing (I hated it first), but after you start grasping the finesse and intricacies of the "game loop" this is a blast to play, a work of art in the shooting genre, making all the other old school-ish, arena like fps boring and basic. When you feel you've become the doom slayer master by conquering each level with ease, here comes the dlc, which is basically the brutal version of the main game and as such totally recommended. Multiplayer is there as well, this time offering a new twist in the asymmetrical pvp with 1 player as the doom slayer vs 2 players as demons. If you like fast paced fps this is a must. Endure the first levels as a man, and you will be able to enjoy the definitive, new version of the old school shooters.Rip and tear!*If the game hangs while starting, or when loading levels, try to alt-tab or ctrl-alt-canc, then reopen the game. It's weird, but it works.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal has spoiled my experiences for First Person Shooters forever! something about it just feels right, from the well balanced difficulty, to mastering the extremely challenging but satisfying loop of managing the Doom Guy's arsenals aka his fists and flamethrower, Doom Eternal just oozes with polish and attention to game design. It is a detachment from Doom 2016 to be sure, with a more casual approach to the game, making pickups float and glow like an arcade game which may cause some people to question as to why ID Software did that. All I know is it just works, for me at least, I believe the departure from the more serious tone allows Doom Eternal to have more fast paced fun intense encounters. With the introduction of Dash and the way the encounter areas are designed, the game does encourage you  to utilize EVERYTHING in your arsenal to stay alive! I found myself constantly bobbing and weaving about, zipping around the area sending demons back to whence they came, rotating from grenades, flamethrower and glory kills....its a rush, and there is some strategic layer to it if you are playing on harder difficulties. Not only that, since power ups are just floaty pieces in the world, picking it up mid-fight while still maintaining the rapid flow of battle is just easy and feels satisfactory when you nail it, which contributes to how fun and exciting the encounters in Doom Eternal are.Overall, i think the game does a lot of things right in what a sequel should be. A lot of games seem to make a sequel yet the only thing that changed is the narrative, they don't add anything new to make the gameplay loop feel much better or improved in any sense, but with Doom a lot of adjustments and fine tweaking has been made to the gameplay to make it feel like its own game rather than JUST a part 2 of the story. Speaking of which, the story is surprisingly rich and deep with a ton of lore for you to explore! so its nothing like Doom 2016's "i'm mad, kill demons" story. Really good stuff!Of course its not perfect in any way, I don't particularly like the platforming sections. But that's probably just me.  Overall, I really liked the game and I am definitely getting the DLC when its on sale! Can't wait to see what ID Software cooks up next! Wait is temporary but Doom is Eternal! (I finally get to join this trend)

_childDocuments_.review: MINOR SPOILERS: Enemy & weapon names. NO secrets, major story events nor major fights.	The follow-up to 2016’s DOOM is one of the sequels I have most been looking forward to in 2020. And although not quite what I expected, what we did get was something that feels unique without throwing away the style and tone set by its predecessor.	Continuing the story of 2016, Eternal is very much a re-imagining of DOOM II: Hell On Earth, you once again Rip ‘n’ Tear through the hordes of Hell, arguably as the slightly less angry but more focused (yet no less sadistic) Doomslayer. This time in the hopes of saving Earth from the Makyrs - who seem to kind of be Angels, but still demons?	On a surface level it does seem that very little has changed, the arsenal is mostly the same, you seem to have the same moveset and Glory Kills are still the most fun/cruel thing you can do with a single button in games. But, it won’t take long before you start unlocking so many movement and offensive abilities that you’ll almost feel lost with the options set out before you at any one time.	Yet this is where Eternal really puts 2016 to shame, those moment-to-moment, split second decisions you make in the heat of battle. No game has scratched my itch for aggressive high speed action since 2016’s entry, and I am not surprised Eternal has surpassed it in this respect. At any one time in an arena you can grapple hook a Hell Knight with the new Super Shotgun, chainsaw an Imp for extra ammo (now much more of a frequent event than in 2016), set fire to a crowd of Zombies with your shoulder mounted flamethrower or whip out the Ballista (the Gauss Cannon replacement) and go after the Mancubus launching rockets at you from afar.	However, this constant action is where the only sticking point for Eternal appeared to me. There is virtually ZERO downtime. The rooms are filled with enemies. The corridors between them are filled with enemies. The platforming sections will throw Cacodemons and Pain Elementals at you. It just exhausted me physically. Especially when a certain hyper-aggressive enemy becomes commonplace, the in-joke in my friends group was you stop every session when you get stuck on it - and begin every session by beating it.	My recommendation for you if this becomes a problem is to search for secrets every chance you get - essentially making your own downtime. All of the other new and returning additions are all welcome and blend very well in to the macho mythology id software started creating in the previous game.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal engulfs you entirely, plunging you into demonic chaos. Battles are a mesmerizing dance of twists, jumps, and brutal assaults. The game, reminiscent of its predecessor, now introduces the Super Shotgun with a grappling hook, adding new dimensions to the carnage.From the fiery intro on Earth to navigating through arctic fortresses and space, the journey is unforgettable. Every glory kill fuels your health, encouraging relentless aggression. The addition of a flamethrower and the Plasma Rifle's mods elevate combat to new heights. Upgrades for weapons, along with runes and the Super Shotgun's grappling hook, offer a symphony of destruction.Movement is key, with fast runs, dashes, and double-jumps. Every failure feels like a strategic lesson, pushing you to be constantly on the offensive. While minor issues like hidden collectibles and frustrating puzzles exist, they hardly detract from the overall experience.Doom Eternal excels in making combat feel fluid and engaging. It's a blood-soaked ballet of carnage, demanding your complete focus and attention. The multiplayer mode promises intriguing player-orchestrated arenas.In summary, Doom Eternal is a relentless, blood-soaked symphony that surpasses its predecessor in every aspect. It's a heavenly experience, so take a seat and enjoy the carnage!

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is the perfect FPS. (This is a statement and it's not up for debate)I thought that it was nearly impossible to improve doom 2016's formula, well... they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did it!Doom eternal is not just a doom game, it let's you go into the doom universe for the first time and goes even beyond, making some fan theories true and adding new incredible enemies for the slayer.It's really a different game from its predecessor, it's more cartoony and more colorful; the gameplay loop is masterfully designed to be fun and engaging at any time, with new brutal ways to glory kill demons and new incredible sounding weapons; your ammo is really scarse and you have to rely to your chainsaw to refill your weapons, this makes it a lot of fun to combine all the different things into the "combat puzzle" that is doom eternal, your chainsaw also refills itself after some time so you always have a mean to get ammo, as long as there are demons to cut up in half; it also adds some platforming which i find to be a nice way to explore and catch breath between fights.Unlike doom 2016, where the super shotgun was the only weapon of choice for 1/3 of the game, weapons have their strengths and weaknesses for every demon type making them all useful and requiring to switch between all of them to overcome the demon horde.Oh and yeah... the music from Mick Gordon is back and better than ever!For having incredible looking and detailed environments this game runs beautifully, with a gtx 1080 in 1440p max settings i was going 90 to 100 fps with minor stutters during some intense battles.I just have two complaints: the boss fights are not really good compared to 2016's boss fights and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Marauders...

_childDocuments_.review: First off I will say it's not a "bad game", just as much as I wanted to like the game I don't enjoy it much. I powered all the way through to the ending in hopes I might start liking it more, but it was honestly a chore. Half my playtime was spent with the game paused while I did other things.The devs' design approach to this has a very narrow concept of how the gameplay loop should work and anything outside of said loop doesn't work. So you either love it and find it a blast to play, or you just don't. It's not a difficulty problem it's a design philosophy one. Everything is designed around pushing the player to handle things in one specific way from the way the ammo is handled, to the way tools are handled, and all the way to how maps are handled with invisible walls being everywhere. You do it the "right way" or you don't do it at all. It's a love it or hate it experience all in all. If you're looking for something closer to an old school FPS where the only thing you have to do is navigate the levels and keep an eye on ammo while slaughtering enemies... This probably isn't the game for you. If you're looking for a follow up to 2016 that is more of the same this probably isn't for you. And if you want immersion this definitely isn't for you. HOWEVER if you want a fast frenetic almost "arcadey" shooter with a focus on "rip & tear" style play and a gameplay loop that revolves around you chaining all the various tools at your disposal.. you'll probably have a blast with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom is re-inventing the FPS genre (which is appropriate since it created it in the first place in 1993). You can't just shoot what's in front of you, you have to have total situational awareness. You need to know where the trash mobs are to farm from ammo and health, and you need to watch your gauges so you know when your chainsaw (ammo) and flamethrower (shields) are ready. You also need to be careful not to damage the demons too much because if you kill them outright you can't glory-kill them for health.It's like an intensely stressful multitasking puzzle on top of a FPS with tight controls and gory action. Is it frustrating? Yes. Is it unfair sometimes? Oh hell yes. Will you be engaged? Absolutely. Can you go back to playing normal FPS games after this? That's the real question.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 was one of the best fps games of the last decade, and an excellent re-invention of the franchise. It was fast, fluid, looked beautiful, had great combat and a near perfect balance between corridor shooting and arena encounters. It also had a decent, unobtrusive story that was well presented. Doom Eternal has almost none of that. Yes it's fast, but just about everything else about it is significantly worse. The combat has been significantly changed - there's now virtually no corridor shooting, with almost every encounter being a succession of arena combats. Furthermore, the difficulty level has been ramped up to almost comical levels. The Doom Slayer has gone from being a demon killing badass into a one hit kill mobile punching bag. The number of enemies on screen at once has been significantly increased, but so has the level of demon. Rather than facing a gradually increasing hierarchy of demons over the course of the game, almost from the get go you'll be swamped by imps, arachnotrons, cacodemons, mancubi, hell knights and god knows what else - all in the same fight, often with more than one of each and several at the same time. To top this off, your ammo levels have been drastically reduced (in the first game you start off with 20 shotgun shells, and each upgrade gives 10 more. Here you start off with 16 and each upgrade gives you TWO(!) more), and armour and health disappear almost immediately. This means every fight becomes a desperate encounter for survival in which you're constantly running out of ammo and down to 1 health with no armour, and the only way to survive is to use the correct take downs to add just enough to keep going for a few shots more. On top of the stressful and frustrating combat, level design is generally greatly simplified save for the completely weird addition of endless environmental puzzles and platforming. These feel completely out of place in an fps and again it's difficult to understand why anyone at ID thought this was a good idea. Other letdowns include the graphics and general design - for some reason textures are significantly worse than in 2016, and several graphics options have been removed. Furthermore, the cool immersive storytelling from the first game (e.g. physically ripping the shotgun out of someone's dead hands,) has gone, with all items and power-ups now looking like poorly modelled icons. I kid you not, secret items are now just large, yellow floating question marks - I genuinely thought someone had left placeholder art in the game by mistake the first time I saw one. The levels themselves look for the most part like large, empty rooms. You start off coming to Earth and fighting through a ruined city. This amounts to a few simple, remarkably clean and tidy office buildings. Where is all the blood? Where are the dead bodies that littered the floor like in the first one? Finally, the story. 2016 had a fairly straightforward story with a limited number of characters, and some interesting back story hidden in codexes if you wanted to seek it out and learn more.  Eternal doesn't pick up directly after the first game, instead seeming to skip ahead an unspecified amount of time. Earth has now been almost entirely overrun by hell when the Doom Slayer suddenly arrives in orbit in some kind of weird flying castle. Where did this come from? Why does it have Vega on board?  Other than this strange disconnect, the game hamfistedly introduces a huge amount of back story - apparently the Doom Slayer is now part of some ancient group, serves a ghost King of some kind (and yet completely ignores a direct command from him), is part of a prophecy, plus there are now multiple alien/godlike groups introduced all with different aims and interconnected relationships. To have any idea as to what is going on you have to read pages and pages of codex entries. Oh, and I haven't even mentioned the god-awful tutorials which keep popping up every five minutes, either covering over most of the game screen with windows of text or worse, literally transporting you to some kind of test room to explain how to use whatever you've just picked up. Overall, for me, if it wasn't obvious from the above, the game has been a massive disappointment. I know a lot of people absolutely love it and consider it one of the best FPS's around, and that's fine, but for me, there are just too many changes to the first game and almost none of them are for the better. I'm trying to persevere to finish it as I've spent the money on it and can't refund it, but at this point I'm not sure I'll ever get that far. I've already re-installed 2016 and re-started playing it from the beginning, and frankly it's a lot more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never write reviews for games, but I have to make an exception for Doom Eternal.Note that this review was written after the Dunovo removal update, I did not feel like playing the game during this time but now it has been removed I am going back to ripping and tearing.It is a rare thing that a AAA game with such funding still turns out as a game that seems to come from the heart.This game has so much personality, and does something unique to the Doom series. I have almost never pre-purchased a game because why pay 60 euros on a game that you only play once? Doom Eternal was worth it, however.While this game seems to be mindless killing at first, as many other people have pointed out before me, it really feels like a combat puzzle. Instead of just blasting through monster using your super shotgun, the limited amount of ammo forces you to feel creative at every moment. If you lose your focus for 2 seconds you can get destroyed by a Demon that you didn't see coming.The limited ammo amount, forced chainsawing and weak punch will feel abnormal at first, but once you get how Doom Eternal wants you to play, every level feels like a roller-coaster ride. Switching a lot of weapons, taking out enemy weak points and dashing around will keep you on your toes constantly.Rarely have I felt so exhilarated so often after each play session, somehow I always beat a map by the skin of my teeth. Sometimes the first Dark Souls game comes to mind.Yes Doom Eternal is different from Doom 2016.Why release the same game twice. _childDocuments_.review: is a first-person shooter that mixes fast-paced combat with an ever-increasing difficulty steep and platforming to navigate the terrain. The game's main idea appears to be always to keep moving and is an action title that features a crazy amount of weapon and weak points to exploit in your enemies. There is a lot of detail to appreciate in its gameplay and is one of the best first-person shooters. If you are interested in slaying demons at high speed and enjoy crazy good shooting, keep reading!In  enemies have weak points that can be exploited to either make them easier to kill or disable a capacity in them, such as long-range weaponry. The attention to detail here is astounding, as you keep searching for these during combat and start to learn their weaknesses. Targeting a weak point is the difference between killing a demon with few bullets or an entire magazine! It is satisfactory, too, as you get to hear a "bing" sound every time you hit a weak point.This mixed with the game's high-speed pace makes it like an adrenaline-filled experience in which you must shoot lots of demons while also trying to search for windows to exploit their weak points. The maps are filled with pickups to obtain and platforming so you can navigate around while in combat. It is so fast that at first, it was hard for me to keep up, but you eventually get used to it and start to become better while playing, so it has a steep learning curve and just went it starts to become comfortable, it adds new enemies or mechanics to keep you in your toes.I wouldn't say I liked the system for weapon switching as I found it to be quite awkward in my opinion, you can only go back between the last two weapons you selected previously. Besides, you have to open a wheel to select any of the other guns, and while time does slow down during it, my take on it is like navigating a menu mid-combat. Since there are many tools to use, I would have preferred a more intuitive and straightforward system to select them.Speaking of the different weapons, one of the things that impressed me the most is an absolute bonkers number of upgrades and mods! There were so many that I did not know what to choose at times and are very useful! You can turn a shotgun into an automatic terror that keeps going until it is dry or add grenade launchers so demons can chew on them while you kill them. There are also upgrades to the suit, which can help you locate things in your map or lower your abilities recharge.The campaign is replayable, and there are many reasons to play it again, from collecting all collectibles to getting all upgrades. They also added twists to make it more attractive on a second run, such as cheat codes that can influence the gameplay or different modes such as arcade with lives.It can be exhausting to play at times, as I did suffer a bit of fatigue, with some missions being able to last 20-40 minutes. During my time with the title, I would usually play sessions of 1-2 tasks and then pause to make this more tolerable; I don't mind them being long, however. Also, I don't particularly appreciate that platforming seems to be implemented oddly in some sections, like having to break a wall. Simultaneously, it can sometimes lead to falling off, or some jumping platforms can make you lose momentum if you dash.The strong point of  is that it is a first-person shooter with tons of things to discover. There are many challenges, secrets, and exploration to do, and should you do; Then you can be rewarded with upgrades or weapons to add to your arsenal! It adds an extra layer to shooters with the addition of chainsaw enemies to recover armor and have to pay attention to details to come victorious in its vicious combat! Executions have gore visuals into them, and with the high-speed chaotic formula, it doesn't get dull at any moment save some platforming bits.The weak point of this title is that there is no incentive to try the more formidable difficulties. During my playthrough, I choose the one after what would be considered normal, but there was no reason to go beyond that. There are no achievements or significant rewards for beating the game at the max difficulty, and I think this can take some of that replayability I mentioned before. The story did not impress me either, as it boils down to you, killing demons while higher demons tell you to stop, and you ignore them. It could have been more interesting if we had a more interactive main cast, perhaps.It was tested on an RTX 2070 S, during my experience as of this review; there were no crashes. I would have loved if the chainsaw ran out of fuel as you use it rather than being an automatic cleave, as that could make it more gore like while adding skill to using it! There are tactics the game doesn't tell you as burning a demon before executing it still gives you armor to pick up or that you can hook to a monster, and instead of shooting it, chainsaw him to get ammo while traveling long distances. Ammunition being colorful in contrast to the blood theme of the world of  is amusing and looks sick, so I appreciate that detail! is an outstanding title with one of the best shooting I have experienced in gaming, It is a superb title with almost no flaws and adds diverse layers to an established genre. There is a lot to do while exploring the levels it features, and its gameplay is always filled with adrenaline and the exhibition of how good you can be while playing it. I had a great time with it as I went from being scare of demons to punching them out of existence! If you like this review, give it a thumbs up! If you want to add your own opinion or share something informative, do it below in the comments!

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM: ETERNAL.What a hell of a game.10/10. The gameplay is rock solid. The shooting feels fantastic. The animations are smooth, the sound design for the weapons is excellent, and everything about it just oozes quality. Enemies fall to pieces and you can easily get a sense of how damaged they are without ever seeing a healthbar. If you are a fan of shooters, you owe it to yourself to play this game. This is what a good shooter should be, at least to me. It's fast, it's unrelenting, my adrenaline gland has never felt so engorged. There is no cowardly running behind a chest high wall to suck your thumb until the cherry jelly disappears from your vision. If you want to live, then you fight.Strangely, a lot of people had trouble with the Marauder and the Slayer Gates. I thought the Marauder was fairly easy to deal with, just time consuming (I played on Ultra-Violence). Stay mobile and shoot him with the supershotgun when the green lights flash. In 4 of the 6 Slayer Gates, I didn't even die on my first attempt, and I got all of them without having to back track. What I found far more difficult were some of the boss fights (the last two specifically) and the timed challenges - I wasted far more lives on those than I did fighting Marauders or Slayer Gates. Also, I lost a lot of my lives in really dumb ways, not even in arenas. Which is sort of bizarre.I could write an endless song of praises for this game. But that would take forever. So instead, I'll list a few minor critcisms. Warning, below this are spoilers.- The glory kills feel like a bit more of a mixed bag. They're all good, but I think a fair number of them feel "floaty." There isn't as much weight in them compared to most of the glory kills from DOOM 2016. Really, the only way to add that feeling of weightiness would be to slow them down a bit and make pause at the apex or zenith of different movements, and slowing them down like that impacts gameplay. So, I can understand why they made that call.- Punching demons and having it do next to nothing doesn't make you feel very powerful, and sort of runs contrary to the constant power rush you get. But if they went down too easily from melee, then that wouldn't be good either. I think there's a happy medium.- In some areas, it feels like there isn't enough fodder, where in other areas, you're almost drowning in it.- ETERNAL as a sequel to DOOM 2016 is sort of jarring. The tone of 2016 was a bit darker and created more of an epic feeling. The humor was present, but darker. The cutscenes were entirely in first person, and I think they actually managed to make doomguy more expressive in 2016 *despite* only being in first person. Just using hand gestures alone, they conveyed a lot of character. The hesitation made in the VEGA scene, or the anger with which he smashes the elevator panel in the opening scene for 2016, the anger with which he opened doors and stuff - that was really nice. It was kinda funny, actually. I would say doomguy feels a bit too gentle with machinery in this one. I also feel like doomguy is better off as a silent protagonist. I would say that the iceberg storytelling in 2016 was actually really solid and its kind of a shame they did away with it. The power of mystery is extremely, well, powerful. DOOM: ETERNAL lost some of the epic feeling that 2016 had to it by revealing so much, so directly, and not through very telling fragments of a story delivered by a spooky demonic voice. Another downgrade from 2016 is the platforming - not that what appears in ETERNAL is bad, but in 2016, the platforming was much more neatly integrated into the level design. It was flush. The approach to the Argent Tower is my preferred example. Where in ETERNAL you have random floating platforms, in 2016 you had something that felt like it belonged, like you were actually navigating a real structure. Basically, it feels like they borrowed a lot more from the original DOOM, not just 2016. And that leaves for a jarring transition when you examine it purely as a sequel, without that additional context. On its own, it's a fantastic game, but as a sequel, I wish it had carried over more of the thematic and stylistic elements of its immediate predecessor. Instead it takes more stylistic cues from the OG DOOM, and refines the gameplay of 2016. And the style isn't bad, it's just a different flavor than what I was expecting. And I should have expected it, because Hugo said that it was intended to be like a "saturday morning cartoon." And that's what it was. They accomplished their design goal, so any criticism is really more of aesthetic than technique.- I preferred how the lore was delivered in 2016. I liked the more in depth logs that all seemed like in universe documents. Some logs in ETERNAL have this in universe quality, others don't.- In some of the levels, there was an obnoxious amount of prop clutter. One of the biggest things that got me killed was actually getting stuck on some piece of geometry and frozen in place for a second or two, surrounded by demons. In one case on the final level, a BFG round I fired got destroyed by an overturned chair in front of me - it was out of my field of view. That was actually infuriating. I also think that it would be nice if the corners were beveled, so you'd slide off of them. I'd find myself getting caught on them more often than I expected. Maybe that one's on me, but I don't know. This is really the only critique I have of something that directly negatively impacts gameplay.- There were some minor bugs that resulted in me and the corpses of enemies getting slingshotted around. In one a case, a platform wouldn't rise back up out of some lava, so I had to restart from a checkpoint. Besides that, it the performance was fantastic and the game had no real gamebreaking bugs. Solid launch overall.In short, 10/10 game. It's unironically revolutionary, taking all the gameplay elements that made DOOM 2016 interesting and really perfecting them. The only things I can criticize are the aesthetic window dressing and a single aspect of the design of some levels.

_childDocuments_.review: This is why I dislike the very binary "yes or no" rating system of Steam. While obviously I lean on the "yes" side, I definitely have a lot of criticisms of this one, especially when compared to how everyone hyped/hypes this up.First off, I feel like the whole "le epic Doomslayer" thing is a little overplayed here. How can I put this... if the OG Doom is 4chan, DOOM Eternal is Reddit. I'm sure that comparison will make sense to some.The gameplay relies a little too much into the complexities of the combat. I played it on Ultra-Violence and often felt like if I used the wrong weapon or ability at the wrong moment, I might as well let myself die and start again. I was constantly thinking about how I would get more ammo (the ammo pool feels a little low), health or armor, which often took away from the fun of things. It feels sort of like trying to complete a puzzle in zero gravity with all the pieces flying around and you're constantly being attacked from all angles. Sure, there are moments where it's satisfying to pull off the right moves at the right time, but the only time I felt fully in control was when I played this game after smoking a joint. So smoke some weed if you wanna properly lock in. Reddit game indeed.Difficulty wise, I couldn't imagine playing on Nightmare, and usually I have a lot of fun beating old boomer shooters like the OG Doom or Quake. I found Ultra-Violence to be quite grating at times, and the difficulty fluctuates majorly. For example, I died in the final boss battle like once, but multiple times to an earlier boss. It's very uneven to say the least, often making things less than fun.Obviously it's fun, but I think it's a bit overrated. I'm tempted to say that I preferred Doom 2016, but it's been a while since I played that, so I can't say that definitively. Buy when on sale. Took me about 15 hours to beat, not including the Master Levels (which honestly I'm leaving until the next time I get the urge re-install and play this). I also have almost zero interest in the DLCs (unless I got them for free somehow) considering the reviews seem to imply it's even more unnecessarily punishing than the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this a 'No', but it feels like too much of a departure from the feel of Doom. I loved Doom 2016, I wanted a sequel to Doom 2016. Extra lives are a thing to collect and fight difficulty even at Hurt Me Plenty is tuned to make you use them, Glory Kills are now something you must do if you want to keep your health up, chainsaw kills are required to gain ammo due to extreme ammo scarcity for even the basic weapons, switching weapon types to match monster 'weaknesses' is required to not run out of ammo trying to just gun them down, and worst of all (imo) is the introduction of a monster type that requires fighting at a specific range and timing your attacks as counter attacks. I'm sure some people will enjoy the new feel of the fights and the new art style, but it isn't for me. As I approach the end of the single player game I find the fights more frustrating than fun. If another Doom sequel is made in this same style I'll definitely pass on it.On the plus side, the technical execution of things has been fantastic. I've run into no major bugs or crashes.EDIT: I guess Bethesda now replies to negative reviews? You guys doing ok over there? Thanks for telling me my reasons for not digging the game style are invalid because you wanted to make the game more challenging, but in the words of The Dude "Yeah? _childDocuments_.review: All I see when I close my eyes and when I sleep now are the glory kill highlight, chainsaws, weapon combos and demons.Please helpDo not let the appearance of the game deceive you. Doom Eternal is a resource management strategy game in the skin of an FPS. If you are going in from Doom 2016, or another FPS, prepare for a different experience. Doom Eternal ditches the typical FPS formula and builds you from the ground up. Other FPS's (incl. Doom 2016) allow you to win the game with any basic play style or any weapon. Doom Eternal requires you to learn a specific set of rules in order to survive. Your arsenal is a giant tool box used for different situations, which you need to assess and react to really fast. No weapon is useless, or becomes defunct as the game progresses.The main philosophy of this game is: Every encounter, every weapon and every monster are either here to teach you, or to challenge you.The early game experience differs from the late game experience. You are started off with only a single gun, and get taught vital resource management skills. Afterwards, the game grows in size and complexity, and you are encouraged to experiment and formulate tactics using all tools you've obtained in order to succeed. Every encounter is either to introduce a new concept you will need to survive, or to test your knowledge of what you have obtained thus far. If you didn't learn something properly, or didn't execute it properly, that is why you die.By the end of the game, you will formulate weapon combos, using all of the 7 main weapons, and mastering the game's tool box rewards you with fast kill times. Use the right tools for the enemy to succeed. Does this sound similar? Yes, this is literally the same game loop and progression as a Real Time Strategy game.The exploration aspect of the game is often under looked by the people who are just in the game for the combat loop. I feel the exploration of Doom Eternal is dialled in just right. There are enough collectibles and upgrades for exploration to feel satisfying and rewarding without taking out from the main experience.The upgrades are different from typical FPS games. In other FPS games, upgrades allow you to become min-maxed, and obsolete the game challenge. In Doom Eternal, the max upgraded player is just the full tool box, and you need to unlock upgrades to obtain those tools in order to succeed.The story of Doom Eternal is simple, and not a cinematic masterpiece, but doesn't need to be. It is unserious, often times humorous. I can't give a full review on the game's lore because I never really took the time to read all of it. I don't usually take game lore seriously in general anyways. The games story is simple enough to drive the arcade action into play, and is satisfying enough.In conclusion: Doom Eternal is a satisfying Resource Management Strategy Game which takes a fresh spin on the FPS genre. It is not a game of click the bad guy to win. You have a diverse tool set needed to be learnt and mastered in order to simply survive and make it to the next challenge. It is ironic that at a distance, the game appears to be mindless. The digital manifestation of violence (which it still is). Yet as the player, it is an extremely strategic and calculated arcade type game, which is extremely satisfying once you have learnt how to operate within the game's structure.

Thankfully ID (the developers of the game, Bethesda only publish Doom), listened to the backlash and removed it. For that I am recommending this game as you don't have to worry about an unwanted root kit in your system anymore. I still do have other negative and positives with this game that I detail below but other that I do recommend to buy this. Let's get the positive out of the way first:Doom Eternal is an amazing game that I love and ID software are one of my favourite developers. They are are making brilliant games. The story of the game is absolutely TERRIBLE. It made no sense to me because it continues from a story in a novel I haven't read since I only play the games and just makes you lost and from what I do understand of the story, its just bloated.
