_childDocuments_.review: Edit - 29 March:I have changed my review to positive after playing DE for about 10 more hours and highly recommend this game to Doom 2016 fans. I gave a sour review of this game at first because I expected a Doom 2016 style game with different levels and the exact same type of combat and gameplay. Doom Eternal is not like that, the combat and gameplay were when I first tried the game in my opinion foreign, strange and boring; the reason I perceived it to be so was because I just wasn't used to it new style of gameplay and combat that DE delivers and didn't expect there to be a difference than 2016.DE has a much higher learning curve than Doom and it takes several hours to master. You have to juggle many different gadgets each with their own recharge meters, constantly analyze the arena to adapt your approach, manage ammo much more closely and master new mobility techniques. It will seem convoluted, overly-complicated and tedious at first because all these new mechanics are dropped on you when none of them were present in Doom, but learning to use all these new mechanics with finesse eventually offer you a more engaging, nuanced and thrilling combat experience than Doom. Now, I prefer DE over Doom by a large stretch.The new mechanics you have to master are:-Flame belch, shoulder grenades, ice grenades, blood punch-Enemy types and variations have increased significantly; they have weaknesses to certain weapons, hit harder, are harder to kill and have weak points-A self replenishing chainsaw for acquiring ammo designed to be used more frequently than in Doom. Instead of using all your charges for an easy hell knight kill you will be spreading them out to kill multiple imps and soldiers.-In Doom your only movement options were double jump and normal running. In DE, you move slower than in Doom, but start the game with double jump, can double boost in any direction, swing around with the Super shotgun chain(it sounds lame but it is fun and cool as hell) and have poles you can swing from to soar in the air. Pickups also regenerate.DE has a different gameplay tone than Doom, it has taken a different direction the its predecessor and in my opinion was the right way to take this game. You die faster, have less ammo, enemies are stronger, your guns hit harder(especially the super shotgun), you a much larger arsenal of weapons and movement options, weapons have less overall ammo, enemies drop more resources(health, armor, ammo) and there are several different ways to obtain them that require creativity. Combat has become art and action in DE. It is a more chaotic game than Doom; you are bombarded with more enemies and have to smartly and efficiently utilizethe plethora of tools the game gives you to survive fights, I have never enjoyed Doom this much because of the added variety and nuance to combat DE provides. It encourages constant procurement of all three resources(health, armor, ammo) so you are balancing your efforts to restore player resources and engage in combat(sometimes you can do both). Doom's combat became monotonous at times, once I learned to use the new mechanics in DE combat never felt boring because I had many new ways to approach a battle and have the additional considerations of: ammo management, resource procurement, enemy type weaknesses and strengths, planning your approach more methodically and mini bosses. Weapon mods are different and IMO fit DE more than doom making them more interesting to play with.The new art style fits the new tone of the game.The glory kills are vast and better.The art is less realistic/gory and but really livens up the aesthetics while being grounded in reality.The platforming element of the game is nothing short of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun.You move slower but combat is much more nuanced and action packed than Doom(You have to get proficient to understand)Secrets are easier to find but there are moreI had to do some things to really enjoy DE and make the transition from Doom smoother:-I changed the control scheme(melee, interact and chainsaw) to resemble that from Doom-Replay early sections of the game to learn and practice the new mechanics in an easy setting-Spent my first few suit upgrades on ammo capacity to increase my ammo count-Unlocked the 2016 Praetor armor(yes you can unlock armor skins)-Unlocked the second chance(or second throw I can't remember the name) rune that slows down time just as you are about to dieEdit - 22 March:I have decided not to refund the game despite my dislike of many new features in Doom Eternal. It is the only franchise I am interested in at the moment and having something Doom related to play beats not having anything to play:)20 March:Sadly I am refunding this game even though I had high expectations from Id Software and cherished the previous entry Doom(2016). My review for this game is based entirely upon my comparison to it and Doom(2016). I expected this to be a sequel to Doom, and by sequel I meant a game that holds on to what made the prequel good and builds upon it by improving existing characteristics and adding new ones. Doom:Eternal does no such thing and takes the game in quite a different direction that made Doom great while drastically changing the tone of a Doom game to fit the younger(childish) audience.Pros compared to Doom(2016):-Strong emphasis on campaign story elements-Larger variety and diversity of enemy demons-More player movement options-Level design has complex and aesthetic puzzles-CutscenesCons compared to Doom(2016):-No weapon pickup animations-Glory kill animations are jagged, unnatural instead of being smooth and brutal-All pickups have been replaced with cartoonish, brightly coloured icons instead of realistic 3D models-Art style(Weapons, skins, levels, HUD, menu) has become cartoonish and doesn't even look like it takes itself seriously-Less gore and blood almost to the point where there isn't any-Regular melee attacks do No damage and are only for glory kills and blood punches-Hayden and Vega have minimal roles in the story and only have flat and boring lines, other than narrative exposition.-Combat gameplay does not feel anything at all like Doom's-Weird gameplay design choice of decreasing ammo capacity to the point where you frequently run out of ammo and have to rely on the chainsaw(it has unlimited fuel now which recharges over time) to replenish ammo.-Enemy AI seems to react slower and has less complex actions-Level design is more linear and has less exploration-Character upgrade progression is basically given to you and makes the system seem meaningless

_childDocuments_.review: You can't just shoot a hole in Mars. I am DOOM.Fast paced, looks great, gory and excessively violent, with a great soundtrack that makes you feel like a demon slaying unstoppable force, this is DOOM. But then you run out of ammo. And you run around trying to grub pieces off the ground but there's nothing there. Annoying. I read the other reviews before i got this, and I thought great, i'm going to kick ass, and i almost quit after the first mission because i ran out of ammo and couldn't kill the last monsters! Looks amazing, the settings and atmosphere, with a pretty cool story. You smash and slash and slice open demons with your chainsaw and out pours blood and.... colourful arcade-ish ammo and health icons. Completely breaks the immersion. So much to like about this game, but i'd much prefer if I wasn't ammo starved and the amazing landscapes weren't sprinkled with glowing pickups. But you have to adapt to the flow of the game, harvest the ammo and health, and use all the tools at your disposal. Is it DOOM as we know it? Not really. I shouldn't have to worry about running out of ammo in a frantic demon killing spree.However, after you've crept carefully through the missions (by this i mean conserving your ammo), you can easily unlock the perks and cheat codes. You start off weak because they want you to keep playing and level up, but let's face it, you're not going to invest hundreds of hours in to this game and at times I feel Bethesda were caught in two minds about what this game should be - not all games need to have a grind, you get the power step ups with the weapon unlocks. It's fun when you have the cheat codes and then don't have to worry about ammo and blast through to get the remaining perks and achievements. But once you've done that, there's nothing left to play for, as you wont want to have to conserve ammo on another play through. It gets a thumbs up, but get it on sale, it's enjoyable, but not that repeatable.

_childDocuments_.review: * Most Satisfying Doom Ever Made *I'm a Doom fan. Doom was one of my first every games I've played on PC. _childDocuments_.review: The game itself is okay, about on the level of DOOM 2016, although it grows stale in the second part of the single-player campaign.However, the 1.1 update has introduced Denuvo Anti-Cheat (further referred to as DAC) software (different from Denuvo Anti-Tamper, which is commonly referred to as "Denuvo) that operates on ring-0, kernel-level access. That means it has complete, unrestricted access to anything your operating system does, and has full access to your machine. This goes against all norms of information security, and this piece of software is essentially a malware. For instance, having kernel-level access means that DAC can interfere with the normal operation of the OS, causing errors and leading to the famous blue screen of death; it can collect information on EVERYTHING that happens in your operating system and transmit it to anyone without your knowledge, and you only have the word of DAC's creators that it does not do anything of the sort; it also presents CRITICAL security risks, as finding an exploit in DAC would allow hackers complete, unrestricted access to a user's machine. Additionally, there is no guarantee that DAC's information collection policy will not change in the future towards more aggressive data collection, and since it has complete access to OS kernel, it can be updated in any manner without notifying the user.Additionally, it has already lead to various problems with the game - after the update, me and many other users have run into various problems, including (but not limited to) random crashes and frame drops. What's worse, it's activated even when you play single-player campaign, despite being an online anti-cheat, so all those problems arise regardless of the mode you're playing.It's worth mentioning that it has been added in the first update, and the users had no prior warning to the addition of this extremely intrusive piece of software. For one, I would not have bought this if there was any information available about the addition of DAC.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, exclude all the whining of the "DOOM 2016 is better because more ammo, bla bla bla" and the mas-... sorry, I mean "MASSIVE" performance issue and info steal that they introduced with Denuvo (big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deal honestly), this game is best way they could've improved the previous title.Every weapon and every mod has it's purpose. Snipe weak spots with Shotgun's sticky frags or Machinegun's scope shot. Air? Ballista's arbalest. Mobile enemies? Freeze them. Or just kill them all with BFG, because yes.Super shotgun. Simple design upgrade of a close range weapon. Why not, MAKE IT EVEN MORE OVERPOWERED? GIVE IT A TARGET SEEKING CHAIN TO PULL YOURSELF TO THE ENEMY AND SMASH THEM UP CLOSE. PUT THEM ON FIRE AND WATCH THEM SLOWLY BURN WHILIST THEY LOOK HOPELESSLY TO YOU APPROACHING THEM. How just a simple thing can be such a fun gamechanger and for the better. In-depth upgrading system, with a large variety of different paths to choose from makes every game you play unique.Not to forget about the impressive level design, better than having almost every level inside a mars factory but on different planets, dimensions and whatnot. Every 90° is a picture in itself, combining into an immersive world of graphical success - Art. The music, eargasm (The god Mick Gordon - Exudia's Hell Knight encounter had me creamed). The *pop* whenever you get a headshot. Recreating the beloved enemies of the original DOOM, along with a lot of different ones as well, really puts your mind at work, thinking strategies and finding counters.Last but not least, the best aspect that I personally love about the game. The extremely big change in the playstyle of the game. The combat became mobile and fast-paced, every second is a decision to make, every action could lead to an easy fight or an easy death. The dash, the meat-hooked Super Shotgun, monkey-bars, help the game expand into something that it never was and it did it well.I'm undoubtely happy with how the game turned out. The game could very much top the leaderboard for game of the decade and it will especially stay that way for years to come.Rip and Tear/10

_childDocuments_.review: A refinement of the formula established in 2016, while also adding in many new elements that sets it apart. Don't go in expecting to play the game exactly as played 2016, as the new systems completely change the flow of the game (for the better, in my opinion). All weapons and mods have a specific purpose now and equipment items are far more useful here than in the previous game. Ammo is a lot more scarce, promoting the use of the chainsaw, which now regenerates up to 1 point of fuel. It also adds the flame belch, which is primarily used to gain armor. While these changes can be overwhelming for many at the beginning, it really isn't so bad once you adjust your mindset and adapt to the new mechanics. In fact, I find it makes the flow of combat much more intense, challenging, and enjoyable. Also, the music kicks ASS. Mick Gordon is the GOAT. Everything here comes together to make this one of the best first person shooters ever made, if not THE best.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first age, in the first battle, when the shadows first lengthened, one stood. Burned by the embers of Armageddon, his soul blistered by the fires of Hell and tainted beyond ascension, he chose the path of perpetual torment.In his ravenous hatred he found no peace, and with boiling blood he scoured the Umbral Plains seeking vengeance against the dark lords who had wronged him.He wore the crown of the Night Sentinels, and those that tasted the bite of his sword named him... the Doom Slayer.___Tempered by the fires of Hell, his iron will remained steadfast through the passage that preys upon the weak. For alone he was the Hell Walker, the Unchained Predator, who sought retribution in all quarters, dark and light, fire and ice, in the beginning and the end, and he hunted the slaves of Doom with barbarous cruelty; for he passed through the divide as none but demon had before.___And in his conquest against the blackened souls of the doomed, his prowess was shown. In his crusade, the seraphim bestowed upon him terrible power and speed, and with his might he crushed the obsidian pillars of the Blood Temples.He set forth without pity upon the beasts of the nine circles. Unbreakable, incorruptible, unyielding, the Doom Slayer, sought to end the dominion of the dark realm._The age of his reckoning was uncounted. The scribes carved his name deep in the tablets of Hell across eons, and each battle etched terror in the hearts of the demons.They knew he would come, just as he always had, as he always will, to feast on the blood of the wicked. For he alone could draw strength from his fallen foes, and ever his power grew, swift and unrelenting.___None could stand before the horde but the Doom Slayer. Despair spread before him like a plague, striking fear into the shadow dwellers, driving them into deeper and darker pits. But from the depths of the abyss rose The Great One, a champion mightier than all who had come before. The Titan, of immeasurable power and ferocity. He strode upon the plain and faced the Doom Slayer, and a mighty battle was fought on the desolate plains. The Titan fought with the fury of the countless that had fallen at the Doom Slayer's hand, but there fell the Titan, and in his defeat the shadow horde were routed. __And in his terrible rancor between worlds and through time, the Hell Walker found the wretch who shall not be named, but in his heresy was loyal to his evil cause. The wretch adorned the Doom Slayer in a mighy armor, wrought in the forges of Hell, impenetrable and unyielding.With sword and shield of adamantine strength, the Doom Slayer set to banishing all that was left unbroken by his savagery to the void._Yet as the mighty Titan fell and dread engulfed the armies of Doom, the demon priests of the Blood Temples laid a trap to capture this scourge of Hell.Insatiable, even by the vanquishing of the Great One, the Hell Walker sought prey in the tombs of the Blood Keep and blinded by his fervor, the lure drew him in.The priests brought down the temple upon the Doom Slayer, and in his defeat entombed him in the cursed sarcophagus.The mark of the Doom Slayer was burned upon his crypt, a warning to all of Hell that the terror within must never be freed. There he lies still, and ever more, in silent suffering.__So you walk eternally through the shadow realms, staning against evil where all others falter. May your thirst for retribution never quench, may the blood on your sword never dry, and may we never need you again. Corrax entry 7:17They are rage, brutal, without mercy. But you. You will be worse. Rip and tear, until it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like 'Ninja Gaiden' meets 'DOOM' meets the later 'Castlevania' games (specifically "Lords of Shadow").And to add to the "later 'Castlevania'" reference: its more about finding secrets and earning permanent powerups than it is just killing stuff. It occasionally has a 'Resident Evil' vibe to it, because you're always seemingly tight on ammo. Survival Horror isn't bad, and it fits perfectly, but jeez- even if I had decent ammo in original 'DOOM', I still had the capacity to stock up a little- not run out at MAX ammo during a fight with 50 boxes of shells behind me, then be forced to run back and collect them.Great game overall so far, and I'm really enjoying the lore.That brings me to another point, though. They're painting "Doomguy" to be some sort of a godly superhero- which is cool and explains a lot- but I liked it better and admired him more when it was just like, "LOCAL MAN LITERALLY TOO ANGRY TO DIE" and you just defended yourself with whatever you had at hand to brutal effect. That put you on par with the hero and made me root for him as some do with the underdog. Now he just feels harder to relate to, and fights require this 'finesse' that takes you from growling and slogging through guts- to being like, "Okay, I need this to counter act that" ad nauseam.These are just my complaints, though. Everything else is bomb ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥. Top notch.

Short bursts of fun- Story completely forgettable but really who cares, its DOOM 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is great. It takes everything that you loved about Doom 2016 and turns it up to 11. The way the developers designed the game really makes you think before you rip and tear, but still manages to keep the fast paced over-the-top feel that we love.... for the most part that is (I elaborate later in the review.) It offers more of a challenge than Doom 2016 as well as better more fluid traversal. The only thing I dislike is the moments that halt the fast paced demon slaying gameplay Doom is known for. These moments include the purple goop which slows you down and takes away your jump and dash abilities (which are essential to combat.) Under water traversal which has poisoned water and for some reason is difficult to jump out of. Lastly we have the Marauders. In a game that prides itself on its fast paced over-the-top combat they throw in an enemy that completely slows the combat down, making you wait for an opening to attack him. How this enemy type got past play testers is beyond. They are by far the worst thing about this game. Other than that the rest of the game is phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Wow I do not keep track of this stuff. As of July 2020 iD has removed DAC from the game and is now good to go. Enjoy the game everyone. I am leaving the body of this review unchanged. While iD did do the right thing and remove DAC from the game we should never forget that it was added to the game in the first place. We let corpos get away with too much. I really like this game so it hurts to have to do this, but, as of this writing, I can not recommend this game. As of the latest update, on May 17th, Doom Eternal now requires Denuvo Anti-Cheat to be installed. Denuvo Anti-Tamper is bad enough on its own, causing stability and performance problems. Denuvo Anti-Cheat requires itself to be running at all times and runs at Kernel level (it has as many permissions as Windows itself) introducing numerous and serious security vulnerabilities on top of Denuvo's usual list of problems. It is unacceptable that Bethesda and id ask their customers to accept this security risk in order to play a game they already own and to introduce that vulnerability unannounced months after the launch of the game. Sadly, I have had to uninstall the game for my own safety and will not reinstall it until after DAC has been removed from the game.As for the game itself, it's a fantastic game. The combat is thrilling, intense, and tight, the world is beautiful, and the game runs wonderfully even on an old system like my own. The platforming is... well implemented for the most part. I'm not overly fond of platforming, let alone first person platforming, but I never got tilted at Doom Eternal's platforming.Unfortunately I can not recommend the game in its current state. Not while a kernel level DRM and AC system is in use in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters of all time. I didn't think it was possible to top Doom 2016, but here we are. Everything is improved: Gameplay is much more strategic (you cant rely on just one weapon). The story and lore is expanded (especially if you dig deep into the readables).The graphics are beautiful, and gorgeous with HDR.You can now see the Slayer's biceps. Anyone complaining about more story emphasis can just simply skip the cutscenes and not look at the readables.Anyone complaining about the new strategic gameplay needs to get good.I do have three minor gripes: 1. You can't punch enemies and do damage anymore regularly. I understand they want you to wait for blood punch but really, the muscled up slayer should do SOME damage with regular punches.2. While the new arcade like design is great, having weapons and secret items not be found naturally in a level and instead just be a floating icon is disappointing and feels lazy.3. I also think that the crucible and the bfg could have been done better ammo wise. Theres no fun in only having a select few ammo to find for the crucible in the last levels and it makes it so you will practically never use the thing. The bfg is similar but you do find more of this ammo type and in most levels. Also there are barely any powerups compared to 2016.Update: Just replayed the whole game, both DLC, and all Master Levels on Ultra-Violence.What a great challenge and still a 10/10 Main Campaign. Ancient Gods 1 is a 10/10, and Ancient Gods 2 is a solid 8/10 (Too much open space in the maps, and the ending is a bit of a letdown). Every Master Level is great and a worthy challenge except Arc Complex which doesn't have a lot going on. Horde Mode is a 5/10Also I never touched multiplayer in my original review. It's alright as long as you're not fighting a pro slayer who weapon swaps and kills you instantly.It's nice that the events recycle yearly to allow all players a chance to get all the paid cosmetics for free. I wish I did not have to play MP just to get their exclusive season rewards though.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard that DOOM (2016) is getting a sequel, I was quite excited since that game was amazing in pretty much every respect. I waited a long time for the DRM to be patched out of DOOM: Eternal, and honestly the wait wasn't worth it. This game is terrible.The good:-the graphics (aside the enemies) and sound design are pretty much at least as good as those in DOOM (2016)-the Fortress of DOOM is a fun hub area, especially the music platesThe neutral:-unlockable graphic assets are a thing but only if you have a Bethesda account to log in toThe bad:-the presentation is a massive step back from the more realistic and believable approach of the former title--the enemies look a lot worse (this is especially the case for Mancubi)--remember when the Doom Slayer ripped a massive gun off its turret in 2016 to have a new toy... yeah that's not a thing here, you just find stuff in completely random places--literal 1-Ups are a mechanic-the gameplay is awful, especially the ludicrous difficulty, the dearth of ammo, and don't get me started on Marauders grinding the gameplay to a halt every time one appears with their ridiculous shield-that-blocks-everything mechanic-it's also just not fun to play since for the most part it's either arenas full of enemies even on the lowest possible difficulty, or a ton of pointless jumping puzzles; exploration is mostly pointless, see next point-the game is so overloaded with secrets, at some point it's no longer fun to have found a secret and you just tick another piece off the checklistThe ugly:-the aforementioned difficulty is pointlessly high; I finished DOOM (2016) on Ultra-Violence and yet here I had to go to the lowest because even Hurt Me Plenty was too insane; it's infuriating and not in a "holy wrath" kinda way-the final boss fight of the main story is just insane and really shows how broken the "chainsaw enemies to get ammo" mechanic really is when there are barely any enemies TO chainsaw (unless you have a full 3 fuels which is very difficult to do here) while you're swarmed by much tougher enemies WHILE you're fighting a titanic boss that unloads a lot of attacks both melee and ranged at you--did I mention you have to break all of the boss's body parts (8) off TWICE due to the boss having a second phase for a total of 16, and even the supposedly OP Unmaykr deals not that much damage because the boss just has that much HP per body part?--the boss itself is just... kinda there, and throws titanic punches or shoots lasers and big energy balls, but it doesn't really feel interesting since you're pretty much just fighting a mobile building rather than an actual boss that you have to go under, climb up, or ANY OTHER MECHANIC that would have been more interesting than "aim at the thing's parts until something no longer flashes red, then do the next"I will not bother with the Ancient Gods 1 and 2 DLCs because I genuinely fail to see the point. This game is a great step backwards and just doesn't feel worth my time any longer. In fact, had I not streamed it, I probably wouldn't even have done the final boss fight. And that's a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know where to start with this game beyond it being bonkers with its gameplay and producing such a sweaty adrenaline rush sometimes as you just get in the zone and feel like an absolute GOD as you go through the game.I mostly have high praise for this game. It's got all sorts of demons to spice up the gameplay, the levels are interesting, secrets galore, difficulty levels and challenges for all flavors, a crazy story, and tons of replayability if you're into the game. The gameplay really drives the game. The combat is enthralling and keeps you on your toes. Whenever you're introduced to a new system, the game explicitly tells you how to use it and what it's best for, and it's up to you to get used to it. Much of it really sticks with you, too. You quickly remember what weapons are best for what demons, and it's easy to jump back into even after a few months (which is almost never the case for me with video games). The game's got multiple difficulties and accessibility options for all kinds of players. There are rewards for all manner of achievements, and cheats for getting things done quick if you so wish. All of this helps players get a grasp on the combat even quicker, and I'm glad it's all there.The story feels like something that's there just to serve the rule of cool and throw the player into tons of interesting levels. It's not really something you'll spend your days thinking about in terms of some higher meaning or something, but you'll always remember shooting a hole into the center of Mars. It's great.My one gripe for the game is the multiplayer part of it. In multiplayer you get to play either as the Slayer vs two demons, or as one of two demons vs a Slayer. To say the learning curve is steep as a demon feels like a bit of an understatement. It's been extremely rough playing as a demon, even while being in call with your second demon. Most of the Slayers I go up against in multiplayer are WAY higher in skill than me, and it often times ends up producing what feels like completely unfair fights. You've got the entire game to hone your skills as a Slayer, but there's little way to hone your skills as a demon aside from going up against what feels like players with 50 times the hours I have. It's difficult to jump into just for a few games, especially as someone who enjoys playing demon but has no choice but to go up against 2-5+ star Slayers. And don't get me wrong, it's still FUN, just a bit disheartening sometimes, feeling like wins are really outside your control with somewhat unfair match-ups. But that's just the experience I've had, others may of course feel like their match-ups have been fairer.If you want a really fast-paced game that makes you feel like you're really improving as you fuel that god complex of yours? This is for you. It's fun, it's funny, it's bloody, and really bloody beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to the excellent Doom 2016.The good:ID Tech 7 is an incredible engineDemons can be torn apart as you fight themVariety of very different looking locationsSuper responsive fast-paced combatThe bad:Sound mixing is poor, following one of the best sounding games of all timeArt style of 2016 has been traded for a more cartoon based lookCartoon sound effects cannot be turned off unless you change all gun soundsEnemies are spongier, the new "shooting chunks off Demons" feature only exists to try and and make hitting enemies still feel responsiveThe ugly:The game is far sillier than DOOM 2016The focus of the game has shifted from blasting demons to managing several cooldownsThoughts:This is a sequel where nearly every aspect of the game was attempted to be improved, but changing things that already work as well as DOOM 2016 did is just an crazy idea.Lets talk about the presentation.  The engine upgrade allows far more polygon pushing and better lighting.  Unfortunately you will only notice the polygon pushing, the better lighting feels wasted because the art style of Eternal has a colorful brightly lit cartoony style.  Though the engine is capable of far better lighting than DOOM 2016, I thought that 2016 consistently looked better.The music rarely (if ever) fits the locations you are fighting in, and if you look up what the composer has to say about the game then you will know that is exactly what happened - id had him try to make music before there were any finalized level concepts and even told him they weren't going to use the music he gave them.  On top of that, the sound mixing is weak.  Comparing individual sounds to their DOOM counterparts has them comparing favorably, but in actual gameplay nothing is balanced properly.  The music is less than half as loud as in 2016 (of course you can fix this in the settings, and you should!), sound effects sound tiny and pathetic compared to the enemies, you have essentially gone from a rocking power fantasy to a weaker impression of it.The gameplay loop of DOOM 2016 has completely been replaced.  No longer are you simply staying mobile and trying eliminate large numbers of demons as quickly as possible (though it may look like that at first).  In Eternal you are actually avoiding killing all weaker enemies until one of your several cooldowns to turn them into health/ammo/armor is up.  Weaker enemies seem to have less health than before to facilitate this, but this just further hurts the new loop - nearly all of your weapons are too strong on them, and you will kill them rather than staggering them for glory kills (you cannot melee them like in DOOM 2016, your melee does no damage at all unless you have a cooldown up).You are given new mobility options (dodging, leaping off trapeze bars) so that you can go airborne and escape large groups of demons easily (mainly to facilitate this "deliberately leaving enemies alive" mechanic).  Because your new traversal options are so fast, they drastically lowered your running speed.Larger enemies are all intended to be killed with a few specific methods.  This is not like DOOM 2016 where you weapon swapped to deal damage at different ranges, or because you needed AOE - the game expects you to weapon swap with every large enemy you face, and efficient combat actually requires weapon switching after firing a single shot to avoid recharge/reload animations.  Being "efficient" is more important than in 2016, as Eternal limits your ammo to less than half what you had in the first game.  On top of all of this the strongest enemies in the game are all traffic lights - you cannot damage them except for in the half second after they flash green, meaning you have to kite them around avoiding weak enemies while not even shooting.  In Doom 2016 when a powerful enemy came into the arena I always was pumped to take them on, but in Eternal I struggle to think of an enemy I actually enjoyed fighting.  It feels terrible to constantly flee weak enemies because you need to save them for pickups, the exact opposite of the power trip 2016 was.I have seen the new loop described as "combat chess."  I don't agree at all.  This is more like that game children play when they learn their shapes, putting different cut pieces of wood into a box with cutouts on the lid.  You may be able to put a piece in the box through the wrong hole, but it would have been easier if you just used the right one.  You may be able to kill a demon with a weapon the devs did not intend, but you should have just used the ones they wanted you to.I have seen people claim that there is a rhythm to the new cooldown based system, but there isn't, the core mechanics of the game actually prevent it from being in a rhythm.  The cooldowns are there to give you armor, ammo, and health.  Only armor does not quickly despawn, meaning that the only cooldown you can use "in rhythm" is the one that gives you armor back (but if you want to use the armor gaining CD in a rhythm, you actually need to avoid getting an ability that will pick up armor at full armor and apply it towards another cooldown).  You are not always going to get hit, using your health gaining CDs in rhythm will get you killed.  Using your ammo gaining cooldown in rhythm means that you will use it too early, and be unable to refill your heavier hitting weapons when the game spawns in multiple heavy demons that require the same types of ammo at once (which this game does often).The end result feels less like a DOOM game than I hoped.  Your survival revolves around managing your cooldowns and avoiding weak enemies.  When I play it I just wish I was playing 2016 instead.  I really preferred it when DOOM felt like a celebration of the simple core mechanics that FPS games used to be all about.All these absurd issues combined with the terrible new story/lore feel like extreme whiplash.  Doom Eternal is exactly the kind of game Doom 2016 was making fun of.  It makes no sense to see it here advertised with the same name as its predecessor when it is ruining everything the earlier title stood for.To put everything as nicely as possible:  I remember several individual encounters with enemies in DOOM 2016, and even how I approached them.  Despite Eternal having more variety in setting, I cannot remember a single non-boss encounter.  All fights muddle together feeling the same - you avoid packs of weaker enemies, use whatever weapons meet the weakpoints of the heavy enemies spawned, then farm ammo armor and health out of the weak ones.  Though the game is more than competent in every aspect, it is less than the sum of its parts, and I disagree with so many of the changes made.Verdict:  I think I would have enjoyed this a lot more if this were not the sequel to DOOM 2016.  I hate that this has turned into just another game where you spam your dodge button and manage cooldowns.  Some people may like that.

Doom 2 was my previous favorite Doom game, now my favorite is Doom Eternal! Oh yearh the game also runs SUPER well and looks amazing. The pacing is great to, always something new to see or use and always lots of great fights and platforming. The soundtrack in the first game was good but it sounded like it was structured more as an album, with some awesome songs,etc.. but Doom Eternal is on another level with the audio, the soundtrack this time feels like a movie soundtrack, it paces the games soo well along with the game play. As someone into audio most my life to, I must bow down to this man, frigging amazing work on this sountrack, so much variety to and how it reacts to what you are doing on the screen is fantastic ***Doom 2016 was a great revival of the Doom series, Doom Eternal has added more speed, upgrades, better visuals, fantastic performance and more vicious fights. If you liked Doom 2016 pick this up ASAP, this is a better version of that game so far. Oh yeah and let's not forget another fantastic soundtrack.So many bodies and enemies flying all over the place, wonderful carnage! _childDocuments_.review: Oh, boi. I loved Doom 2016. But this game is a total different breed. Not in a good way.First, the positives.- Awesome graphics- Total banger soundtrackThe negatives include the fact that a lot of things that made D2016 great are missing.  I, personally, find this more colorful approach unfitting to doom. D2016 had a dark and gritty tone.The gameplay has a lot of platforming sections. It even rivals Super Mario Odyssey. I am not kidding. If you, like me, want to play a fun shooter and just kill things, then the amount of stupid platforming puzzles will annoy the hell out of you. If I would like to play a platformer, then, well... I would just play a platformer game and not doom.The gameplay has also undergone some changing. Mostly, it became very strict. In D2016 you could rip and tear with the weapon you liked the most. In Eternal, however, the game basically forces you to use X, Y weapon, or else you will just end up wasting your ammo. Overall, Eternal is not a bad game. Not even a bad Doom game. It's simply just not Doom. If you want to have a real Doom experience, then I can't recommend the game. But if you just want to play a kinda restrictive, platforming shooter, then go for it, you will enjoy it.

name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries
detailed_description: BE YOUR OWN WEAPON OF WAR Welcome to the year 3015! It’s a hell of a time to be alive. Humanity has colonized thousands of star systems spanning a vast region of space known as the Inner Sphere. The golden age of cooperation and advancement is now a distant memory, and humanity has once again splintered into disparate factions all vying for supremacy. In the midst of these Succession Wars, power hungry Mercenaries like yourself are in a privileged position to capitalize big time. It’s dangerous work but that’s why you’re here, right? If you’ve got an itch to blast, wreck, stomp and go all out ballistic, step inside and become your own weapon of war! STORY As the inheritor of a once-prominent Mercenary company, reborn in the flames of its near destruction at the hands of conspiring factions, your quest for glory and revenge will stretch light-years as you chase threads of interstellar intrigue along your journey to becoming an elite MechWarrior and mercenary commander. THE INNER SPHERE Home to thousands of star systems and an array of stunning biomes, the Inner Sphere is alive with activity, purpose, consequence, and variety. Systems will be captured and reclaimed, major events will unfold, and new technologies will come to light. The rigors of war will be seen with each passing week as your relationships with the various factions fluctuate according to the relentless Succession Wars and your choices as the leader of a Mercenary outfit. GAMEPLAY The battlefields of the future are dominated by BattleMechs, hulking machines of war capable of leveling entire cities. As a BattleMech pilot you’ll rain havoc upon enemy ‘Mechs and targets, including tanks, ground vehicles, aircraft, advanced defenses, and reinforced bases. Few things can withstand the power of a ‘Mech for long, and the worlds of the Inner Sphere are veritable playgrounds of destruction awaiting your shielding defense or crushing devastation. BATTLEMECHS 'With over 50 unique ‘Mech chassis and hundreds of sub-variants, all fully-realized with high-fidelity models, damage states, and equipment, no two ‘Mechs are the same! Whether acquired from scouring the markets of the Inner Sphere for rare and valuable chassis and equipment, or salvaging directly from the wreckage of your annihilated enemies and the spoils of war, the maintenance and operation of your BattleMechs will be vital to your success both as a MechWarrior and a Mercenary outfit commander.' THE MERC LIFE Off the battlefield, as the leader of a Mercenary company you will need to manage all the key components of running a unit. You’ll need to maintain and acquire ‘Mechs and equipment, hire and field MechWarriors from throughout the Inner Sphere to join you on the battlefield, and manage your relationships with the Great Houses of the Inner Sphere, all of whom are vying for your contribution to their staggering war efforts. Of course, with each Contract comes negotiation, and with each victory comes consequence. OTHER FEATURES With the vast scope of the Inner Sphere and its complex system of world generation providing huge variety and replayability, the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries experience offers no end. Outside the campaign, a fully-featured Instant Action system will allow you to customize and kick off isolated missions at any time, free from campaign restrictions. With four-player co-op supported both within the campaign and the Instant Action system, you can experience the full breadth of the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries universe alongside your friends. Mods extend your game even further! Unlock the boundless creativity of the community to alter and expand the game in amazing ways. With a full editor and interface supporting gameplay mods out of the box your creativity will know no limits.

STORY As the inheritor of a once-prominent Mercenary company, reborn in the flames of its near destruction at the hands of conspiring factions, your quest for glory and revenge will stretch light-years as you chase threads of interstellar intrigue along your journey to becoming an elite MechWarrior and mercenary commander. THE INNER SPHERE Home to thousands of star systems and an array of stunning biomes, the Inner Sphere is alive with activity, purpose, consequence, and variety. Systems will be captured and reclaimed, major events will unfold, and new technologies will come to light. The rigors of war will be seen with each passing week as your relationships with the various factions fluctuate according to the relentless Succession Wars and your choices as the leader of a Mercenary outfit. GAMEPLAY The battlefields of the future are dominated by BattleMechs, hulking machines of war capable of leveling entire cities. As a BattleMech pilot you’ll rain havoc upon enemy ‘Mechs and targets, including tanks, ground vehicles, aircraft, advanced defenses, and reinforced bases. Few things can withstand the power of a ‘Mech for long, and the worlds of the Inner Sphere are veritable playgrounds of destruction awaiting your shielding defense or crushing devastation. BATTLEMECHS 'With over 50 unique ‘Mech chassis and hundreds of sub-variants, all fully-realized with high-fidelity models, damage states, and equipment, no two ‘Mechs are the same! Whether acquired from scouring the markets of the Inner Sphere for rare and valuable chassis and equipment, or salvaging directly from the wreckage of your annihilated enemies and the spoils of war, the maintenance and operation of your BattleMechs will be vital to your success both as a MechWarrior and a Mercenary outfit commander.' THE MERC LIFE Off the battlefield, as the leader of a Mercenary company you will need to manage all the key components of running a unit. You’ll need to maintain and acquire ‘Mechs and equipment, hire and field MechWarriors from throughout the Inner Sphere to join you on the battlefield, and manage your relationships with the Great Houses of the Inner Sphere, all of whom are vying for your contribution to their staggering war efforts. Of course, with each Contract comes negotiation, and with each victory comes consequence. OTHER FEATURES With the vast scope of the Inner Sphere and its complex system of world generation providing huge variety and replayability, the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries experience offers no end. Outside the campaign, a fully-featured Instant Action system will allow you to customize and kick off isolated missions at any time, free from campaign restrictions. With four-player co-op supported both within the campaign and the Instant Action system, you can experience the full breadth of the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries universe alongside your friends. Mods extend your game even further! Unlock the boundless creativity of the community to alter and expand the game in amazing ways. With a full editor and interface supporting gameplay mods out of the box your creativity will know no limits.
short_description: The year is 3015. The battlefields are dominated by war machines known as BattleMechs. Level entire cities and decimate the enemy in your BattleMech. Follow a quest for glory and revenge. Manage an expanding mercenary company. Fight alongside your friends with a four-player PvE co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: INCREDIBLE GAME...WITH MODSHad to get that out of the way. I've been a MechWarrior/Battletech fan since I was 5 years old, sitting on my dad's lap watching him play MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat. That game was *so* good. The visuals, the music, the AI assistant who chirped at you when you took a critical hit, all of it was so compelling and inventive. I've played every single entry in the series, as well as the MechCommander and Battletech games. I have some perspective behind my opinion on MechWarrior 5!I, like many, waited awhile for MW5 to hit Steam. As far as I'm concerned, the poor folks at the EGS were beta testers. Early iterations of MW5 were plagued with bugs, terrible enemy spawns, and a general lack of polish and variety. The base game experience now on Steam in 2022 is *much* improved. Don't get me wrong, there are some head scratching design decisions and omissions here, but that's what mods are for and oh man, there are some good ones on offer.Here are the ones I heartily recommend:- Advanced zoom (for that MechWarrior 3/4 style 4x popup zoom window)- Better lighting hangar, which restores the original PC lighting in the hangar that was removed for the console releases- Better crates, so you actually get useful items from salvage crates you randomly encounter on missions- Better spawns, because spawns are still borked in the base game. You WILL encounter magically appearing enemies within 100m of your mech without this mod. I don't mean turrets popping out of turret ports, I mean tanks and mechs appearing out of thin air. Absolutely unacceptable, this is a must-have mod- Coyote's Missions, adds much needed mission variety to procedurally generated contracts- Dropship Recolour, I like black- Expanded Logos, for more mercenary company banners- Fahad's animation tweaks, to make him less...uncanny- PGI Infantry, an official mod that adds enemy infantry. Great for MW3 immersion- Infantry tweaks, to make infantry not glow like Power Rangers- Infantry outline, see above- Max Tonnage, so you can take a legitimate lance with you on missions and not be arbitrarily restricted- Mech Shader, to make damaged mechs look less plastic- Missile Trails, so LRMs leave beautiful black smoke trails. The battlefield comes alive with this one!- Mod Options, so you can adjust certain mods and their parameters- More Enemy Mechs, so you can fight something other than Firestarters and Locust- MW2 Betty, so your audio assitant has some personality and variety! So good for immersion- MW5 Compatibility, forgot what this one does but it is useful- No dialog HUD, so you don't have crudely drawn pictures pop up constantly when the enemy are ♥♥♥♥ talking you- Paint Schemes of the Inner Sphere, adds hundreds of quality paint jobs and patterns to the mechbay- Pilot Overhaul, allows you to rename, customize, and promote pilots. Adds a ton of depth to your hired hands!- Purchase Salvage, so you can pay the difference in C-Bills between the 28 salvage shares you were alotted, and the Atlas that costs 30 shares.- QOL Upgrades, lots of nice tweaks like a repair all button for the mech bay- Repair Bays, adds repair bays to large garrisons on missions. Adds immersion and a useful tactical option- Salvage Percent, so you can actually salvage that Warhammer you legged, instead of it being absent from the salvage screen- Scary Tanks, adds variety to enemy ground vehicles including new types and variants of existing types. Also makes them more resilient as in Tabletop- Smooth Lasers, beautiful new laser FX- TS Music Mod, adds in Timothy Seals soundtrack. MUST HAVE MOD, the base game's music is so generic and completely lacks soul. Timothy's covers of classic tracks add a ton to immersion, especially Gotterdammerung-TRulez AI mod, MUST HAVE MOD. Adds more lancemate command options and makes them less stupid- Ultra Visual and Weather, makes the game look more modern- Unlock hidden colour schems, like Paint Schemes of the Inner Sphere- Dropship weapon rebalance, makes your dropship useful in combat- vonBiomes, MUST HAVE MOD. Adds numerous, quality biomes to the random contact missions.- WAR FX, MUST HAVE MOD if your system can take the heat. Adds a ton of great particle effects and turns battles into legitimate chaos- Weapons Shader, pretty- XenoPax Optimize, greatly enhanced my rig's performance (I9-9900k, 2080ti, 3440x1440p)With those items installed, I love this game. Without them, the game lacked variety and lacked the heart of what made MW2 and MW3 so good. Base game is slick, no doubt about it, but these mods really add so much to the immersion and fine detail that the Battletech universe has. I would highly recommend this game with that fat disclaimer!

_childDocuments_.review: Moving onto the singleplayer review:Have spent a decent amount of time playing this game on a competing game service:[Deleted link in case it hid my review, it was a screenshot, but I have 3d, 16h, 26m and 9s clocked in on said service]MW5 is not a perfect game. MW5 has a bunch of drama surrounding it. MW5 won't cure cancer, but neither is it the embodiment of Satan. MW5 is decidedly...  Worth 30 bucks? Frankly, yes, I'd say so, even if you knew nothing about the Battletech universe. Easily worth that if you do and you'll recognize all the mechs, weapons, and factions in the game.It lacks an engrossing narrative campaign like in Mechwarriors 2 (and expansions), 3, or 4, though there is... some body of one there. But it serves little purpose other than to give you additional motive to pump up your company and not just sit in the initial low-level area. While on that note, MW5 is very focused on that aspect of the game, with mixed results. If you aren't a fan of running a bunch of procedurally-generated missions to incrementally upgrade your arsenal and mech roster to take on incrementally harder missions with more and deadlier opponents, awesome, go ahead and leave this game behind. If you thrive in a sandbox environment, don't go away just yet.You fly around the Inner Sphere, doing procgen missions for the 5 Great Houses of the Inner Sphere. If this means nothing to you because you don't know the lore, all you need to know is it's basically like a 5-way civil war where everyone's stabbing everyone else in the back. You're a flagless mercenary commander who signs up for whoever has jobs. You can keep doing jobs for the same faction for loyalty perks (more “negotiation points”), but that's about the extent of that. Said negotiation points are used when taking mission to select bonuses for your pay, salvage rights, or insurance for damage taken (higher rate than points for base pay, but you ONLY get money for damage your 'mechs sustained). Salvaging mechs requires an all-or-nothing value of points, you can't bank parts like in HBS's Battletech, but as you gain loyalty and/or select the right (i.e. multi-mission) contracts, it will give you ample points to afford the heavy cost of mech salvage. Otherwise, weapons and gear take one or more points, with a 'tier' system giving subtle bonuses between weapons of the same type (i.e. a Tier 5 Medium Laser is functionally identical to a Tier 4 one, but has slightly better range, damage, lower heat generation, and so on).There's a healthy amount of debate about MW5 “dumbing down” the customization from previous titles, about its canonicity, people pointing at the tabletop manuals and arguing about random excerpts... look, the long and short of it is, MW5 has a different paradigm from the previous games, even 4 which was a departure from the TechManual. Where 2 and 3 had the really generous reading of “if it fits crits, it sits” rules from the TT experience and you could shove a bunch of lasers into the legs or something if it made you happy, MW5 opts for a more fluff-oriented approach of battlemechs having a set role. 'Mechs will have, say, 3 "Large" Missile slots, which can each fit up to an LRM-20, or any smaller size of the same family (an LRM-15, 10, or 5, or any size SRM). It's a one-to-one hardpoint swap -- you don't "double up" on smaller sized weapons. A slot's a slot, fitting one and only one weapon; it just has a maximum size that'll fit.I preferred MW4's system, myself, as it made weapons a bit more abstracted in size (wasn't just small-medium-large, but different numbers of 'sockets' taken per weapon, and components having a number of 'open' sockets that you could fit accordingly), but either way I personally consider it better than MW2 and 3; you may not, and your opinion is perfectly valid, too. My take on it is, if a 'mech is meant to be a missile boat, it's a missile boat – you can't just arbitrarily decide it now carries twin AC/20s. This means that you're forced to prioritize salvaging or purchasing 'mechs (or variants thereof) specific to the roles you want them to serve, rather than the old way of 'mechs basically being “choose your favorite-looking/most-meta-hitbox'ed one” and only using that. I prefer it that way. You may not. But, weapons aside -- No Ferro-Fibrous nor Endo-Steel. If you know what this means, you know, and there's much gnashing of teeth and wailing of women at this. Again, call me a shill, but I equivocate it with the lore: At this point in the timeline, FF and ES are both Lostech. And, funnily enough,  Similarly, engines can't be changed in rating, nor can you mount Light/XL engines (Again, something something lore something something Lostech). Again, again, some variants actually have XL engines, 'hidden' from you seeing them on the interface. They even take crits.The game is set roughly in the 30ish years prior to the Clan invasion. What does this mean? Well, if you have passing familiarity with the BT franchise and consider yourself a salty veteran because you played MechAssault once or twice, this means you won't see Timberwolves (“Mad Cats”), Stormcrows (“Ryokens”), Mad Dogs (“Vultures”), or any of the other Clan-designed 'mechs, nor will you see any of the Inner Sphere Clantech-derived designs that have been 'poster mechs' like the Bushwacker or Uziel. The game does feature a subtle time progression mechanism, such that as you play the game (and progress in the timeline), 'mechs with more powerful weaponry, or later variants (with different weapon slots) will begin spawning as opponents and in shops.The game, at least at a surface glance for the purposes of this review, DOES appear to just... FEEL better than the pre-patch version. There are a bunch of UI tweaks that clean up a lot of what you're looking at, and a bunch of subtle immersion stuff like character lipsyncing has been added. Dumb, I know, but have to say it because there's a committed force of trolls ranting and raving about how it's literally the same since day 1. I've been playing on and off since day 1. It's not.I return to my first rhetorical, do you like sandboxes? If you don't, then you probably won't like this game, but that doesn't really mean the game is objectively bad, it just means you don't like sandboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: Without mods this game is aggressively "meh". PGI needs a swift kick up the arse. They got very complacent because nobody else is making Mechwarrior games, so what are you gonna do, not play? If you're not going to mod this, or are getting this on a console, get it at a deep sale.THAT SAID, with mods this becomes so, SO much better, it's not even funny. My main recommendation would be either YAML (haven't personally tried that one out) or MercTech (the one I'm running rn). They add so much customizability and potential to the otherwise slim base game.Want to drop the engine down from a 340 to a 320 on your Victor? Sure. Or maybe you want to slap in a 380 clan XL into your Banshee and give it a pair of hatchets? Go nuts! New weapon calibers, new equipment, unlocked customization, slap in the TTRulez AI mod and give your lancemates battle roles! Change your mech's cooling to double! Give it Ferro-fibrous armor! The possibilities are, uh, not exactly endless, but it sure beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of whatever the base game is doing.The game itself is, like I said, pretty mid. The story is uninspired, more or less just there to have an excuse for things to happen. The gameplay is really good though. There's nothing quite like sitting into a 100 ton avatar of death and destruction, accompanied by 3 other 100 ton avatars, and beating the snot out of other 25 - 100 ton goons. Weapons sound and feel good (and could sound and feel even better with mods, cough cough), the mechs feel good to pilot, having enough of the signature weight and inertia to really make you  like Batman. Piloting a mech.One major downside of the game is the braindead AI. Mods make it tolerable, but it's still pretty bad. In vanilla though, your lancemates will sniff fuel and eat glue while the enemy pilots are divinely inspired marksmen that have trained since their inception to land a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gauss slug in between the asscheeks of a mosquito at 1000 meters away. BLINDFOLDED. It is so frustrating to watch your team do the poopshuffle in place while you're getting dismantled by omega cracked enemy AI. To be honest, if there was no mod support, I'd flat out not recommend this game solely for that reason.At the end of the day, there are much worse games out there. And if you want Mechwarrior, it's either this, Online, or trying to fiddle with getting the older games to work. Beggars can't be choosers I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yeah I'd recommend this.. but not vanilla. As great as the foundation laid out by PGI is, the base game is just too barren and missing that bit of OOMPH to really make it shine. Enter; MODDERS. Once again, another game greatly amplified and extended and improved upon by the homebrew community. These are not just outstanding mods, but I would say they are close to as essential as you can get. Each one offers massive, yet balanced, additions and changes to the game and turns it from an okay 'Mech shooter into a sprawling, in-depth, strategy-laced, supreme RPG -- taking you right the way into the Clan Invasion! It's a fantastic game, truly engrossing, the 'Mech construction and kitting out is so enjoyable, the missions varied (though with only 6 or 7 archetypes they can get more than a little stale towards the end of the 100+ hour playthrough), and the overall story is enjoyable enough to keep your attention.Sadly the performance leaves a lot to be desire, it's truly wretched more often than not, regardless of how powerful your machine is - the engine just buckles and it can't seem to handle its own weight. It's not uncommon to see framerates dropping to the low teens during heavy fights, yet CPU and GPU usage remain frustratingly low. Still, if you can put up with that (and if I can, you can!) you're in for one hell of a 'Mech stompy adventure. Just, again, don't play vanilla.. get those mods (or the likes of YAML and TTRulez AI) to truly experience what this game can offer.

_childDocuments_.review: The game at its core is absolutely worth buying. This is what AAA games ought to strive for. Right out of the box, you have decent Mech customization and the Singleplayer story is very much worthwhile. I appreciate the fact that you can get people to join your Singleplayer game by loading the file in the multiplayer menu. The music is wonderful and I'd love to get a copy of the soundtrack to listen to on occasion.The single player story is wonderful and ties in well to the lore, which I recommend delving into while playing, especially if you're not doing something story critical. YouTube channels I highly recommend for lore dives: Big Red 40 Tech (for technical delves into individual mechs, some lore, and even exposure to the TTG) and Sven van der Plank (for raw lore). The lore of this franchise is rich and certainly worthwhile.Pay attention to the news crawl on the bottom of the screen when playing or in mission selection.While the game is wonderful on its own, it's best with mods, especially the ones in the Yet Another series. YAML (Yet Another MechLab) is an absolute must as it drastically improves the customization of your Mechs. Armor Green and Colorized Heat Gauge will make it easier to track the status of Mechs (yours and your targets). Mod Options to have a tighter control over how the mods behave, MechAssault Mechs will bring in the heavy metal found in that spinoff. Finally, Yet Another Clan Invasion to add Clan Era mechs, the Clan faction and some absolutely worthwhile parts; this particular one is not only large (2GB download at time of writing), but is practically its own DLC. No Vortex required, you can mix Workshop mods and Nexus mods and it's easy to mod the game. Furthermore, the devs do a wonderful job supporting their modding community. When Rise of Rasalhauge dropped, most of the big mods (especially of the Yet Another series) had updates within 48 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: (WAFFLING, SEE-SAWING HAND GESTURE)This is a pretty good game......It is NOT, however, a very good MECHWARRIOR game.I would recommend almost any other mainline Mechwarrior game before this one. Every one of them has: better AI, better AI MANAGEMENT, WAY better mechlabs, better map layouts, better sense of scale, MORE THAN 3 FRIGGIN' LANCEMATES, ACTUALLY varied objectives, stories that ACTUALLY make sense, better selection and variety of mechs, (sigh)... I could go on.What MW5 DOES have is: it looks good, it sounds good, it runs on modern hardware, the few missions that ARE unique tend to be decent and.... Uhhh.... Well, that's about it, really.--And YES, before all the pedants come stampeding in; there lots of mods that fix lots of these issues. I even started a second playthrough just so that I could mod it up to what it should have been in the first place. BUT, MW5 itself (and PGI, more importantly) deserve ZERO credit for a bunch of mods being practically required to make their game a proper Mechwarrior game. ALSO, a lot of the mods aren't even use-able anymore, usually because they got sick of PGI breaking them all the time.I'd say this is a SOFT recommend, especially on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Don't let the people with rose-tinted glasses or the disgruntled MWO players fool you. This game  is a serious contender on my list for probably being one of the best MechWarrior/BattleTech universe games in the franchise I've played as a long-time fan. Yes, that includes MechWarrior 2, 3, 4, and all the expansions that came with them. (2 Mercs, 3 Pirate's Moon, 4 Black Knight, Mercs, etc.)Here's why.Let's start off with the elephant in the room:  There isn't a wide range of options for mech customization compared to other games: the mechlab is overly simplified, the storyline and mission design feel less interesting than those in the previous MechWarrior entries, the base AI is pretty bad (then again, friendly AI always seemed terrible in MW games that included them), there's no official Clan content yet as of writing this review, no Elementals, no pilotable vehicles, no championship arena, I could go on. But, with mods, I can easily say that MW5: Mercs has the most in-depth mechlab customization and amount of fun I've experienced in any MechWarrior game.I'm a real stickler for more options. Yet Another Mechlab and its associated mods deserve some special recognition here, as it gives you the same amount of options for mechlab customization as MW3's or MWO's (such as the choice of installing Ferro-Fibrous armor, Endo-Steel internal structures, XL engines, double heat sinks, Clan versions of weapons/equipment, and so on) but now with current-gen graphics and a MWO-style UI all in a singleplayer package. I could even argue that the amount of possible Mech customization rivals or exceeds what you could do in MW3 or MW4: Mercs. The customization doesn't simply extend to mechs alone. There are mods that improve the AI (both friendly & enemy) to play reasonably well and you'll find your teammates holding their own in a fight quite often, even occasionally rivaling the damage output a human player could achieve. Another mod can add repair bays to maps based on the context of the mission, like the ones you could find in MW4's campaigns. Others can change your HUD to a 3D version for more immersion, change the soundscape to make weapon reports and projectile impacts feel far more visceral, add such an insane amount of extra particle effects and smoke to make mech combat & map destruction become an incredibly cinematic spectacle at the cost of eating your GPU. It's hard to put into words just how many options are at your disposal to fine tune for an optimal MechWarrior experience.Best of all,  It's been an absolute blast playing through the base game's campaign with friends, something I always wished was possible in previous MechWarrior games.I'd like to finish off this review with admitting that I'm generally biased against most newer entries in beloved franchises. I understand that many fans of a franchise, including myself, often have valid criticisms for what they see as "downgrades" over previous entries. Sometimes, we do get blinded by nostalgia factor alone in spite of the improvements.And here I am telling you that MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries is absolutely worthy of being called a real MechWarrior game. Is MW5: Mercs objectively better than MW2-4? Probably not. But, with the right mods, it just might be.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a flawed, flawed, seriously flawed game. But... it is pretty fun. So positives and negatives, negatives first, because there's more of them:Negatives:The story is beyond terrible. So bland and uninteresting it actually brings the experience down a bit. Luckily it's something you can pretty much ignore as it is a sandbox style game.Voice Acting is pretty bad - ties in with the terrible story.Mech lab is clunky and limited. The upgrades you can do to mechs is surprisingly limited - and the way repairs and changes work is unnecessarily clunky. Battletech and MWO are far superior in pretty much all aspects here.Your AI lance hover between idiotic and MWO pubs. In fact, I have a sneaky suspicion that PGI based the AI on MWO pub matches, as they tend to act in a similar fashion - stepping directly in front of you, stomping through and destroying defensive positions, ignoring targeting orders to hide on the backline...Mission variety isn't great. Probably because of the sandbox nature preventing crafted missions, it does all blend together after a while.Positives:It's fun. Walking around in a stompy mech and shooting other stompy mechs is fun. The core gameplay loop is enjoyable, and to be honest, that covers a lot of sins.The 'gotta catch em all' is strong - building up a stable of bigger and stronger mechs and equipment is a fun driver that has had me play 20 odd hours in the last week. Conclusion:It's good. Not great, not bad, but good. Mods will probably help, future patches will probably help - but the game is decent now.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a simple answer to "should you play MW5". If you love BattleTech universe and spent your childhood piloting virtual mechs, its an absolute Yes.MechWarrior games were never examples of the best game craft, having technical issues, poor plots, changing mechanics throughout the years. But MW series were always a staple in a genre it helped create and almost single handedly promoted. There were some good games insipred by MW, the likes of Heavy Gear, StarSiege, G-Nome, but MechWarrior was always the pinnacle, and given the lack of MW-clones now, it is the only game that helps satiate the hunger for piloting a giant steel robot shining with firing guns like a christmas tree. The more precious this game is to me, as it brings a full single player campaign to the franchise that previously was available only in online format, Enter MechWarrior Online, from which MW5 takes design, art and mechanics.The solo campaign is your typical mercenary story, too similar to what we experienced in recent BattleTech game, and at times it feels as I am playing that same campaign, albeit not commanding the Mechs, but piloting one of them directly. There are your story missions, side missions chained together in small stories that revolve around Succession Wars, and one-off missions that you do if you need extra C-bills, or try to salvage a ceratin Mech before you progress the sotry. It could be better, but at least it's a serviceable package to wrap the mech piloting in. I wish, the next thing the devs do is the Clan invasion, which will hopefully bring not only the iconic Onmi Mechs (ah, Timber Wolf, i miss you so much), but also better campaign that would not require you to roam the Inner Sphere and instead take part in Invasion campaign (and i can only hope, we would be able to choose sides).Gameplay-wise, it's the same good old MechWarrior game with the physics and mechanics from MWO, which were polished during the online game's life. Mechs feel good to control, you feel the weight of the machines on the field. Combat missions are diverse, you have your typical protect the settlement, destroy the settlement, survive the assault, and raid a zone (destroy several key targets scattered on the map). Nothing too fancy, but it allows you to choose from what you want to do and forego what you dont want to.However, the one thing to spoil the fun is you team mates' AI. They are dumb. An AI pilot can wreck his 100 tons mech if they solo rush an enemy squad, and they do that a lot. They pay no attention to damaged parts, and keep on pushing the enemy even if they are one shot way from death. One thing I found that somehow counteracts the AI behaviour is not giving them close range weapons (SRM first and foremost), as the AI seemingly chooses the weapon with highest DPS and prioritizes its usage over anything else (so if an enemy is not in range, they simply rush them).The enemies also prefer suicidal runs. Is breaks immersion, as you know that if there is an enemy medium Mech with an AC10 it will do its best to close the distance, do as much damage as possible and die. They in no way behave like pilots, who want to survive the encounter.But even these setbacks are not enough to prevent a fan from playing this game and having immense fun with it. In part, this is due to that sensation of piloting a Mech, which is as strong in my late 30-s as it was in my teens. In other part, this is due lack of any meaningful competition in the genre, There are no Heavy Gear, Star Siege, or anytheing else alike. At times I even wish that From Soft take a long pause with Soulsborne and give us another Armored Core game, nevermind how strong I like soulsborne series.A quick note on the game's performance. It's not AAA graphics, but it looks solid enough with no visaul glithces to break immersion during comabt missions. One thing to note is poor ray tracing. On my RTX 2070 (playing in 1080p), RT drops framerate to 20-30 FPS with DLSS, while with RT off, I play at 120-140 FPS easily on high settings. Doom Eternal runs at fixed 144 FPS on  high setting with RT on, and Cyberpunk 2077 play steadily above 60 FPS with RT on as well. Since RT does not bring anything noteworty to MW5, i'd suggest keeping it off and enjoy the highest framerate.

_childDocuments_.review: --If it's on a discount, you might as well just buy everything. Otherwise, at least get the Heroes of the Inner Sphere DLC for career mode. Rasalhague adds other mercenary companies. Call to Arms adds a lot of melee weapons (which, speaking as a newcomer to Battletech, are surprisingly lethal).--Without mods, it's serviceable. Stomping and shooting in the vanilla game is fun, but mech customization is pretty shallow compared to what you can do with just the Mechlab mod on the workshop, and the mission variety can feel a bit stale after a while if you aren't actively planning and testing out builds. A full-price purchase is not recommended if you do not intend to mod the game.--With mods, it's one of the best giant robot games on the market, especially if you're into PvE content. Other than Mechlab, I personally recommend 'vonBiomes' on Steam Workshop and 'Coyote's Mission Mod' on Nexus. Those three mods alone turn the game into a sandbox where even the lightest mechs can be turned into monstrosities of engineering with enough C-bills, some lucky salvage, and a little bit of creativity.--For the love of god, and the sake of your own sanity, download the the 'jumpship animation skip' mod. I didn't think it would bother me until the first time I checked every stop in an industrial hub.--Modded co-op with friends is possible, but not flawless. I strongly advise running similar mod lists to minimize jank. Only the host can use the starmap, initiate and negotiate contracts, view the shop and mech market, and skip forward on the timeline. Story/Career progression is saved only for the host. Jumping to a different system will cancel all changes in progress if one of the other players is customizing a mech.--Make sure to keep your weapon groups simple for any mech you're giving to friendly AI.
