_childDocuments_.review: The Dread Mediocrity of Mechwarrior 5In shortMechwarrior 5 is mech shooter and mercenary management game. If you approach it with a games journalist mentality and expectations, and little to no prior knowledge of the battletech, then it can be an adequate game. It certainly can be fun at times, it certainly can give a dose of mech for the craving. It is a decent game. It’s certainly a step in a more mechy direction from Mechwarrior Online. But is it a good game? Not by any means. I don’t say that as a hater, I very much wanted this game to be good. It just particularly isn’t. It’s not horrible, it’s far from horrible. But it’s just a little bit lazy.How it playsThe game consists of three key parts. There’s the mech shooter part, where you stomp out with your lance of stompy boys. There’s the mech building part, where you decide your armaments and armor. And there’s the company management part, where you buy new equipment, undertake missions, and hire new pilots. Each part of the game is flawed in several ways.The shooter partMechs and their sensorsThe sensor systems on the mechs work in some arcane fashion. Sometimes it appears you are able to share sensor data with the team, other times you round a corner to face an enemy your lancemate is staring at, and you never saw it on your sensors at all. Information sharing is one of the most crucial and basic technologies to incorporate in any modern to futuristic setting, and it has been a staple of every mechwarrior game to date. Having it now work in such a finicky and degraded fashion is just baffling and immersion breaking.	Additionally, newly spawned enemies are on emergence displayed with their red target rectangles. Then they vanish, because they are usually out of your sensor range. This is just weird and gamey.‘The level curve’MW5 tracks pilot skills both for the player and any NPC pilots hired by the player. There are skills for different weapon types, for damage resistance, heat management, and for evasion. Weapon skills directly increase the damage you do with said weapons, damage resistance reduces incoming damage, and evasion increases the enemies’ odds of missing you. It is acceptable to track AI pilot skills like this to try to reflect their rising skill level; the AI will never improve its actual piloting, so an artificial approximation of the effects of skill is adequate. But needless to say, tracking player skills like this makes for some absolutely stupid gameplay in what is supposed to be a tactical shooter. 	Essentially, every mission has a challenge level that determines the skill levels of enemy pilots. If you go into a mission over leveled, you will deal great damage, destroy everything with ease, and the enemies will often be missing point blank shots at you, even when you’re plodding around at no speed at all. This gets to the point of ridiculous. Conversely, if you go into a mission under leveled, then enemy mechs will often seem unexpectedly tough, even when you’re nailing your shots. Likewise their damage output against you will be far greater than you’d expect, and their ability to concertedly focus fire on your most important weapon systems becomes almost preternatural.	This makes for some abysmal gameplay. The player’s actual piloting barely matters in resolving the outcome of the mission, your pilot skills ranks are just that significant. On the same note, the system encourages cheesy play, where you farm boring no-challenge missions to rank up your pilots, because if you don’t, you will be liable to lose at minimum some expensive weapon systems every time you deploy.Animation effects on gameplayIt’s sad to say, but Mechwarrior 4 did mech animations way better than MW5 does. MW5 animations are often stompy, janky, and they simply do not look like natural motion. The worst offenders are the limping animations of mechs that have had one leg shot out from underneath them, the jump jet flight and landing animations, and the ragdoll destruction animations.	The limping animations are a problem. It is often difficult to tell which of a mech’s legs is ‘destroyed’ and which is not, so in a chaotic situation, especially in bad lighting conditions, you’re frequently forced to consult your sensors to determine which of the legs you need to be shooting at to finish the mech off. This is of course ludicrous. If a leg is not working, it should be readily apparent from the motion.	The jump jet animations, or their lack thereof, is also annoying. Mechs do not animate in any way to suggest a balancing act while airborne, they just begin rising up, lifted by several miniscule sized jets. It gets worse when they land; there is no landing animation, and the flying momentum of the mech is not accounted for in any fashion. A mech that was flying full speed in one direction can INSTANTLY be darting full speed the other way as soon as its feet touch the ground, with no animation to translate the shift in motion, and no pause or slow down for acceleration.	The occasionally malfunction destruction ragdolls are not such a particularly large problem, but it’s a little shortcoming regardless. Warmachines weighting dozens of tons should not ragdoll in the first place, and it looks twice as awkward when they jolt around with some fairly frequent regular old physics malfunction.Dumb ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AIOne of the worst detractors from the general play experience is the quality of the enemy AI. Regardless of their weapon systems, especially non-mech enemies will happily oblige and close distance with you to make for a hectic and utterly stupid and non-tactical shooter experience. Heavy helicopters mounting autocannons with one of the longest effective ranges in the whole game will happily swoop right overhead and get shot down by short range missiles. LRM carrier vehicles especially suffer, as the game does not apparently allow sensor sharing, so the long range indirect fire support platforms must push in close to gain their own LoS and target lock, making what should be one of the game’s hardest nuisance units into an absolute pushover.Company managementPilot managementOne of the game’s most baffling and egregious errors comes in the management of your roster of AI pilots. The skill levels of the pilots that you hire are capped. A pilots development is hamstrung by their own personal skill caps. Early game, while you are a nobody from nowhere, you can only hire pilots whose skill cap is very low, and whose starting skills are very low. Later on, once you’re a famed big shot, you’ll be able to regularly find pilots with nearly maxed out skillcaps in everything, and possibly maxed out skill ratings everywhere as well, right from the start.This is nearly the exact opposite of what a management game should do. The FUN of managing a mercenary company is in seeing your stable of talentless hacks slowly grow and develop into a formidable force. In MW5, this will simply never happen because of the individual skillcaps. The pilots you hire early will inevitably become useless already by

_childDocuments_.review: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries. A game developed by Piranha Games and Published by Sold Out.I'm far from a veteran of this series, most of the memories i have of the franchise actually have been as a spectator, rather than a player. Until i played a turn based strategy game called BATTLETECH. Set in the same universe, with the same mech designations and a more commandeering viewpoint, i fell in love with the gameplay. So obviously without hesitation i jumped into MW5. But was it worth both the wait and the money?!Remember how i had mentioned BATTLETECH above, essentially the starting premise of that game is almost identical to MW5. Now that's not a terrible thing, but it does leave much to desired in terms of a story you want to back. The vengeance for a long lost mentor is obviously tragic and clearly a strong motivator in any situation. However having already experienced that it felt more like a recycled tribute. "BATTLETECH Lite" i heard people call it. The story doesn't seem to really branch out from there, you follow the same patterns almost entirely, you have to start a new mercenary squad from scratch and earn your reputation till you can call yourself a Hero and finally get vengeance for your loss. Mech Warrior as opposed to Mech Commander always did one fundamental extremely well, The combat. This is definitely no exception, even in the slightest. Combat feels heavy and impactful when you get hit by a shell you know you got hit, when you strike an enemy it feels amazing! Like your every hit is going to be hurting your foe. I love that about this game. It's hard to make a game like this where you are controlling giant robots, its hard to make them feel controllable, it's hard to make them seem real and even harder to make them feel manoeuvrable, While its not seamless here it's definitely realistic. Heavier mechs will go slower, will be harder to steer and overall will just have a harder time navigating landscapes, while lighter mechs will be the opposite, extremely fast, easier access to different locations and able to float around the battlefield like a bee. It's no secret that the Mech Warrior universe has an exorbitant amount of mechs to choose from and to fight against. Which certainly makes combat entertaining. Finding out what type of mech is coming towards you is always a strategic call, closing the distance might do you more harm that anticipated. Keeping far away the same. I like that this is still a concern even in MW5 as it makes combat far more entertaining and overall far more gratifying when you get it right. I have to remark on the fact that i love the battlefields in these games, i love how destructible they are, i love how massive they can be in scope, I love the hills and the cliffs. I like pinpointing a mech amongst a forest and ripping it apart in that split second it becomes visible. The battlefields makes these games great, and MW5 has a huge diversity of them. Oh dear god. The AI...if you really want to or even CAN call it that. The AI is about the most stupid i've ever had the punishment of witnessing. The worst part is that it's so actually stupid it will often ignore direct commands from their commander *YOU!!*. On numerous occasions in my relatively short game time i've had orders completely disregarded, and friendly makes run off into trouble unknown, just to get killed in action and lose the mech in the process. This game would have been a far more worthwhile experience if it was made to be solo instead of squad based. While i'm not against difficulty in these games, actually i seek it to be harder the more i play. The difficulty of MW5 comes from it's unfair and seemingly broken game mechanics. Encounters aren't "hard" if you had some sort of scouting being completed for you. If the people who have radars in the sky could tell me what is coming and where from. But even this is made almost impossible for them as enemy mechs will quite often spawn right up behind you, allowing them to critically strike your core and bringing your career to a very abrupt ending. This is certainly not made easier by the above point i made regarding the AI being actually stupid. One aspect of these games or at least this genre that seemingly always captivates my attention even if the core is terrible, is the customisation. I love to customise my mechs, i love to choose loadouts and min/max my builds. I love to contemplate the potential usage of different builds on different sized mechs. You can still do a lot of this in MW5 but your capabilities are significantly nullified. A lot of the customisations feel like they are just tacked on rather than actually useful. I believe you may be able to patch over this with a mod but you shouldn't really have to.MechWarrior 5 does a lot really well and a lot really terribly, this unfortunately isn't exempted by it's visuals. While the game is exceptionally beautiful for the most part, it does suffer from a significantly large amount of graphical issues, such as tearing, graphical glitches and overall under textured world design. It becomes almost immediately apparent the game is designed to be stunning, and on some parts of the mechs just seem to be lazily textured and others almost entirely devoid of textures at all. I would also like to make mention here that the game is horribly unoptimised, On ultra settings the game was running extremely high resource usage which is fairly standard for games of this scope, I had dropped the quality to test the drop and despite the fall in overall visual acuity the game still seemingly ran high resource usage. It held steady at 60 FPS however with frames locked and never seemed to fall from that despite its resource hunger (See profile for build specs)One thing i find extremely hard to fault in this game is the audio quality as a whole. From the expertly designed soundtrack of music that seemingly keeps every encounter upbeat and full of intensity. To the insane amount of detail relating to the actual mechs themselves which really bring a tremendous amount of realism to the game. The mechs sound heavy, the sound of the engines roaring as you run as full speed through a forest, trees collapsing around you as you break them apart. The heavy thud of shells hitting you as every footfall of yours collides with the hard earth beneath you. This game is an auditory wonderland and it was a truly amazing experience to witness. No audio issues were detected beyond a few recorded dialogues that sounded like they had white noise in the background that wasn't nullified.MechWarrior 5 isn't going to astound you a whole lot. If you're a fan of the series you would have experienced a lot of what is wrong with this game in both MW4 and MWO. If you're new to the series entirely you may find it quite appealing until you hit the difficulty spikes due to the unfair bugs. If you're a BattleTech veteran coming here to continue the story and enjoy the world of MechWarrior you might be disappointed by the significant lack of content compared to BattleTech. Overall this isn't a bad game, and it can't be called that by an stretch. However it is lack luster in a significant portion of its design. If you are still determined to give this game a shot, i'd recommend it at a discount because the full price is a steep climb (with the DLC) for a game that feels like a beta test."Reactor online, sensors online, weapons online. All systems nominal"

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much exactly what you'd expect when you say "A single-player campaign, from the people who made the online multiplayer."  It has some good ideas and cool little details, but it ultimately fails to improve in any meaningful way over Mechwarrior 4 (with the exception of draw distance).  Piranha understands the numerical aspects of a Mechwarrior game (tonnage, heat, weapon recycle speed, etc.), which they ought to after a decade of developing Mechwarrior Online, but they clearly fail to grasp the higher-level stuff like map and encounter design, as well as which 'Mechs are actually fun to pilot.  They start you in a Centurion, which is a pretty boring 'Mech.  It's very sturdy, but painfully slow to get around the battlefield, making it a sitting duck in the hands of novice pilots. And unfortunately, because the salvage system is rigged against you -- 'Mech wrecks have a low chance of appearing in the salvage list and, when they do, are often worth more than the maximum salvage value you could negotiate for -- you're stuck with the Centurion until you do a lot of grinding and get lucky.With mods like Yet Another Mechlab, this game becomes passable if played a mission or two at a time, but ultimately it lacks the charm and care of design that makes Mechwarrior 4 so beloved.  It has the unfortunate position of being unfavorably compared to not only its 20-year-old predecessor, but its contemporary in Harebrained Schemes' Battletech.  Piranha doesn't leverage the Battletech setting nearly as well as HBS or FASA before it, and that leaves the game feeling hollow, because there is nothing to soften the grind, nothing to look forward to but another template mission on another template map.Not worth buying unless (like me), you were *desperate* for some visceral 'Mech carnage and couldn't get Mechwarrior 4 to work for the life of you.  Get Battletech instead.  Also, the HOTAS support is basically non-existent, which is just inexcusable.  The community has assembled a document detailing how to add support for your specific HOTAS, but that's not the point. Even when you add the support yourself, the control binding UI is godawful, especially for the joysticks. Piranha does MechWarrior Online, they know the kind of person that is an Mechwarrior enthusiast.  I appreciate their effort to lower the barrier to entry and making it more comfortable for newcomers by supporting standard gamepads, but MechWarrior's gameplay was designed for a joystick and they should know that.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick update for the new DLC:It adds one terrible mech that explodes on contact to I guess make Jaegermech pilots feel better.It finally adds more Active Bay slots so you can properly deal with needing different mechs of different weight to deal with tonnage limits.Sub Pilot Level 40 - Your AI will just turn whatever mech you give them into scrap metal.This led to me soft locking/game over the new DLC when all my pilots/mechs were damaged and there wasn't enough allowed time to repair to complete the final mission.Meaning you need player mods to reduce repair/healing costs and times you need the stars to allign to complete a fresh start of the Rasal faction.Downsides of the Expansion: The rental fees on the new active bay slots are hella expensive and can drain your resources quickly.Upside - There are other Merc Factions now that can interact with you.  I haven't had too many interactions with them yet as most of them occupy space with no missions to take.  But it seems neat.======================== Old Review ====================================For what the game offers, it's not worth full asking price.  Unfortunately there is only yes or no when recommending something.  It's a fun mech dakka dakka stompie stompie experience with not much else going for it.This is basically MechWarrior Online with AI.  Or another way to put it, it's a straw. Stiff rigid outsides with a hollow inside that is used to suck what little fun there is out of the game.Story: Dumb.  In what amounts to a revenge tale told in one of the worst ways possible your character on patrol watches an entire city get destroyed and decides to rob a bank.  I mean, no need to defend the planet from the invaders or worry about all those now deceased people.... money.  In doing so, your father tags along and you get ambushed by the invading army..... who could of known they would be there after invading right?So, now you set off in whats left of your unit for revenge and profits.  The Merc Mode skips the intro and joins at this point and everything beyond is one in the same.So we get to experience the first shallow event... your ship and crew.  Outside of naming your Company and picking their logo that is all you get to do in terms of customizing your character/ship/staff.  You can hire/fire pilots to suit your needs but you are only ever allowed 4 mech's in a fight and you cannot expand your business.Get used to running back and forth to talk between Ryana and Farrod even though you are the boss and have a comlink.... no one will ever come to you..... the freaking boss.Okay, time to set off and make money.... how does that work?Well, you get to fly to any star system you want across the entire inner sphere map.... awesome right?  Sorta.  There is only so far you can auto travel across the map.  Why? Don't know.  F U for asking.  Even if you have piles of money to pay your bills on time... it just won't let the game calculate that far ahead.Areas are broken up into reputation indicators to help guide the player into areas they can handle but you are not restricted from going into any mission.  There is a difficulty indicator.... it's more of a suggestion.  So you pick your mission and then you get to select your contract options.  The higher the faction rep, the more units you can select.  If say you are hated you get 3 points to put into fields like C-Bill's, Salvage, Damage Insurance, Airstrikes, if you are Hero status you get like 20.  So you select your points and you move to the next phase, pick your mech's and pilots.  You "somehow" have a ship that has 4 mech bays, 8 additional spaces for selectable or "active" mechs and an infinate space for storage.  Where is all this stuff stored?  The dev's didn't care....... Sometimes the games let you repair before mission after you select the contract and other times they don't and you need to take damaged or switch out the mechs...... there is no indication before hand.... so repair before you take a mission.  Also on multi-missions, repair after the 1st mission and by the time the 3rd mission comes around your 1st mission mechs should be repaired.In one of the dumbest decisions ever, you are forced into tonnage limits on missions.  Why?  Don't know.   Isn't this YOUR mech company? The game wants you to think that.  You can't even say it's an issue with ground density and sinking as the enemy will drop in far more and far heavier mechs.  You get punished if your salvage if you go over or won't be allowed to start.  Why? Again... F U!  Even if you take 4 Atlas's in on a scounting mission... the punishment is repairing the damage of expensive mechs to how little the payout is.... not the contractor punishing you.  Why would you accept this mission for them then?  Logic.... don't look for it here!Next glaring issue is there is no IPB which in short means Intel Prep of the Battlefield.  So you don't get to see a map, select a drop/pickup zone, or what mechs might be in the area..... you get to be semper Gumbi - Always Flexible.  Rayna, your XO on the other hand.... knows a lot and just decided not to tell you.Combat - It's tuned to MWO standards.... so a lot of weapons do not work as they should, or at all.  Saves you time trying to figure out a load out...  Melee is a thing, and should be of last resort as you will probably come off worse for wear.  Your AI is okay at the best of times, something for the enemy to shoot at most of the time.Mechs come pre-configured.  There isn't much freedom of choice here.  You do not get a blank mech and depending how you decide to load it that's what variant it falls into.  So you cannot take a Catapult with an LRM 15 launcher and put 2 SRM6's in one slot.  You can only swap 1 for 1.  So this makes a ton of mech's useless.  You also don't get much room to play with... so strip jump jets for armor because missions are long and there are no checkpoints or repair bays. Blowing up enemies doesn't really matter... leg them or core them, salvage comes out to be about the same.Overworld.So, once again Rep determines your shopping and your contract points... and nothing else.  If you are hated, you can still take missions.  Also, I found that Contractors I have never interacted with hated me for no real reason..... maybe they just hate mercs, but they are the employer....There is a passive upgrade system.  By doing Cantina missions you unlock passive abilities you can equip on each of your mechs to customize their stats.... this is a must!  When you use them the game really turns towards your favor.That's about it.There is nothing else to do in the game..... No Solaris Battle Arena, nothing really happening.  The map will change to reflect major events in the timeline but to you, you have to travel somewhere to turn in a quest and that's it.  It feels like you are walking around a large empty mall with no one around.There are mods that make some improvements to the game... so there is that.  Stomping around in mechs is also enjoyable....  but at the end of the day... this feels like a copy and paste of MWO and not a lived in universe.Pick it up on sale and play with friends for a much better experience.  I don't hate this game, it's passable.  I just feel it's a bit hollow for my taste.  The game is in a far better playable state than when it launched and had only one crash and it was probably my fault of alt-tabbing while loading.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - If you have no experience with prior Mechwarrior titles, and like stompy robots blowing things up with beautiful lasers, then this game is probably for you. If you have played previous Mechwarrior or Battletech games, you probably will dislike a lot of aspects of this game. With a little effort you can enjoy blowing stuff up with friends, but on a technical level this game is a real mess with regard to design decisions related to the mechlab, AI in general, and the progression of the career mode. I don't recommend it, because I don't like giving studios money for poorly implemented systems that are actually a straight down-grade from prior titles in the series.Breakdown:The campaign story is bland, uninteresting, poorly written and ultimately makes little sense. The voice acting ranges from okay-ish to absolutely terrible, to the point that I found myself telling the game to shut the heck up after hearing the "TAG" line EVERY SINGLE TIME the AI fired a particular weapon. The "interactive" space where you can walk around the mech bay is sometimes praised by parts of the community for being immersive, but honestly everything is just an un-interactable wall, and the characters inside are annoying at best.Career mode has no real feeling of progression compared to other mechwarrior games. The player can easily get their hands on heavy or assault mechs within 30 minutes of starting a new career, rendering the entire light and medium mech "phase" irrelevant. The player doesn't feel like they are a small company growing into a more and more powerful mercenary when they can literally get their hands on 100 ton mechs in 15 minutes, and the missions don't exactly reward light or medium mech playstyles either (more on that later). The interface is rather silly, you can see that there are missions available, or that "rare mechs" or parts are for sale in places, but you cannot see WHO is the hiring faction for the missions, and you can't see "what special part/mech" is for sale unless you physically travel somewhere (which makes no sense since space travel is specifically supposed to be both expensive and time consuming, so you really should be able to see who you are working for or what mech specifically is so special before traveling somewhere). The mechlab is a severe disappointment, so much so that I requested a refund on epic games and waited for steam release to have improvements, those improvements did not come. On a fundamental level, a good portion of the fun of mechwarrior games is designing the mech and being able to make intelligent decisions about weapon loadouts and heat management to suit your playstyle. This game has the worst mechlab I have ever seen in a mechwarrior title, with the default view hiding the display of everything that isn't a weapon slot (which is very telling about the mindset of the devs), and vague info blocks for weapons, innacurate details and misleading graphical information. Basically the player doesn't have useful info they would have had in any other mechwarrior game. Combat is very pretty, but also very shallow. The enemy can spawn literally right in front of the player, just pop into existence. Most maps have enemy tanks or helicopters constantly spawning behind the player to get free shots in the back, endlessly hounding them and preventing the use of light mechs or flanking tactics because you will simply take too much damage to weak armor. The missions get repetitive, and I have had multiple "soft lock" scenarios where an enemy I have to kill before I can move on has flown off somewhere or gotten stuck in the terrain and I cannot kill them. All of this leads to a game that is kind of fun for a short while as you are struck by the shiny lasers and exposions, but gets repetitive and tedious as you progress.The AI is a joke, both friendly and enemy. Friendly AI do not even target enemies, they literally "detect something within range, begin pointing the mech at the enemy, and fire weapon groups on their mech at random". What this means is that if an enemy spawns to your right side, all the AI will detect the enemy, IMMEDIATELY fire their weapons straight ahead, and start turning toward the enemy. So they often shoot the ground, nearby buildings, each other, you, anything nearby that ISN'T that enemy they detected. This wastes ammo, heat, sends weapons into reload cycles, and very often leads to friendly team damage. You also cannot give them useful commands like earlier mechwarrior games, they can be told to sit perfectly still, to follow you, or to attack whatever you currently have as a target (though this is also flawed because it isn't an order to "keep attacking target X, while I do something else", no, they will immediately switch to attack new targets if you change yours after giving them this order). Multiplayer is also implemented poorly. Netcode issues cause disconnects fairly frequently, which drops a player from battle and they have to wait to rejoin after. Friends cannot even interact with the mechlab or mission screens without some heavy modding, they just have to wait for the host to design everything for them (without being able to see what they are doing) and get assigned the mech the host chooses so they can fight. Also, you can't even play multiplayer right away with the base game, you have to go through at least an hour worth of prologue content solo before you can invite friends, you have to buy the first DLC to be able to join a multiplayer game immediately after it starts (which the devs havent decided to fix or backport to the base game, so pretty much everyone is forced to buy the DLC if they want fun multiplayer without "hoops to jump through").Basically, it's a pretty game with a lot of baffling stupid design choices and poor implementation of AI. I do not recommend purchasing it unless you plan to mod the heck out of it with the workshop, or if you are waiting for the "mechwarrior living legends" crew to tear it apart and use the engine to make their game. I don't condone giving money to a studio that ignores the lessons from 5 prior mechwarrior titles and makes a game with this many glaring design problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so torn on how to review this game. It is, like almost every single MechWarrior game, so very close to be exceptional.But literally, and I cannot stress this enough, the AI does not work. Don't get me wrong, some of the older maps are fine but the newer DLC? Even some of the older DLC? I literally have AI friendlies requiring extensive micro to properly target and shoot any enemy mech, let alone any vehicle you need to destroy, oh and better yet -- good luck trying to destroy any building.This is after an exhaustive search on the Steam Workshop and Mod Nexus to hopefully remedy the AI problem, and admittedly, some of them have made some pretty great improvements here and there. But, these improvements are on the scale of comatose to vegetable. Lights are on; nobody's home sorta gig. Anyways, the real skinny here and what I honestly think you should ask yourself before buying this game:How much do you really love MechWarrior?Do you have a dedicated group of 3 other friends who also really love MechWarrior? (From personal experience, this pool is fairly small/borderline non-existent)Are you comfortable altering files and installing mods?If you are unsure or lukewarm at best on any of those three points above, this game is going to be a tough sale. There's going to be great moments of exhilaration and great fun followed --almost immediately -- by frustrating realization as you're the only one doing anything.If you're however, a die hard BattleTech fan and have a love for customizing your mechs, then this is the closest experience we have to a truly Modern MechWarrior game divorced from a toxic Pay-to-Win system. And if you're a die hard fan, you know the curse each one of these games bear, they are often so close to greatness and fall so very far. Despite the negative review, I will be begrudgingly still playing this damn game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not, in the past, given much thought to the mechwarrior/battletech franchises. I don't really care about big robots or mecha stuff. My co-op group picked this up so I gave it a whirl. At first I was just enjoying it as something like an FPS with a different skin, just give me a robot and let me at 'em, that kind of thing.The real meat though is in the modification of the Mechs which kind of turns this game into a RPG merc company sim where you marry brains (pilots) and bodies (mechs) to make 4 combatants on the field. Pilots have basic skills they improve through use. Mechs are super customizable, and there are also scores of them, with some clearly better than others. You will no doubt spend a lot of time trying to acquire the best Mechs and the best equipment for those Mechs. The pilots are basically just a collection of voiced lines with skill numbers, so don't expect cool dialogue trees or companion quests.There is a campaign, which serves as an excuse for you to wander the galaxy taking contracts with a plot leading you along. The career mode is basically campaign mode, but it jettisons the plot entirely and you are free to roam the galaxy and take up missions however you desire. Most missions on the map are procedurally generated, but there are still plenty that have been hand-crafted by the designers, and those usually come with mini-storylines.Turns out I like RPG merc company sims, so I ended up liking this game a lot. The FPS thing turns out to be a nice touch, a good way to punch way above your (literal) weight and headshot mech after mech in a fight you would, on paper, have no business winning. The expansions provide a ton of extra content, so if you find yourself into the game you can buy them for more things to do and acquire - two of them give you campaign-style mission chains that come with FMVs and voice acting.This game also has co-op, and I am a firm believer in co-op making everything better. This is no exception. The only drawback to co-op is that the host is the actual leader of the mercenary company, so they are the only ones that can shop, hire new pilots, fly the ship, and pick up missions. The other players can of course pilot Mechs in battle, but they can also still tinker with the Mechs the same way you could in your game, so they have things to do during downtime. The co-op is very robust - if you are playing a co-op game, your friends can just drop right in even if you are mid-mission, and people can come and go all the time without the game being affected at all.I feel like this franchise has a big fan base. The following three points get mentioned a lot in their reviews:- Bad AI. I did not find the AI so mind numbingly awful as some of the other reviewers - mechs will get stuck on terrain on  occasion, but you can always go back and order them off of it, or take control of them in a pinch to maneuver them yourself. They fight other mechs just fine, especially if you pick them a target.- Need to love Battletech. I was actively disinterested in this franchise before I picked this game up so I straight up don't agree with that. This was my entry point into the series and I think it's a good one since they have apparently rebooted the timeline and this is the very beginning. The game will give you a lot of lore about this time period if you care to read the events that pop up during your career.- Required mods. Have never used a single mod. Obviously I thought it was very good without them. Perfectly playable and tons of fun. Did I mention the xpacs were great?So yes, overall, all the thumbs up, highly recommended. One of those games I have been very surprised to enjoy as much as I have. Maybe that'll happen to you too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just annoying.  I'm a huge battletech/mechwarrior fan and this game lost me.  The customization that you are afforded is extremely limiting, not even up to the standards of Mechwarrior Online.  The arbitrary drop tonnage is perplexing for a single player game.  The allied AI is stupid and your ability to give them orders is so limited you pretty much shouldn't bother.   The enemy AI, however, will target you, call in artillery strikes on your position no matter where you are even if by the game's own targeting logic, they shouldn't know where you are.   The bonus is that you can can destroy the artillery, but there's no way to order anyone in your lance to do so, so you have to go across the entire map to stop getting constantly shelled, while your team mates just follow along instead of doing useful things like destroying an objective or fighting enemy mechs.I would not buy this game.  I can see why Piranha Games took the Epic store exclusive deal a year ago, cause I feel like people would have returned this game en masse.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I am a fan of Battletech, played tabletop, love the lore. And since ever I liked all those silly games where you can pilot a mech, no matter how little sense there is to it.. from TerraNowa, to G-Nome, MW2 to MW4. Yes, I am old.Now the review: this is not a good game. This not a good Battletech/Mechwarrior game, nor a good mech game, nor a good action game, nor a good management game. Main reason - the mechanics which is done so badly that it takes away the simple fun and joy, the main reason to play games. This is one of those games which gives you a feeling that dev teama tried really hard to screw you over. Difficulty and spawning of enemies - there is no difficulty settings, for some players this may be simply too hard game (for wrong reasons). Artificially spawning over and over hordes of enemies (purely quantity over quality) is just tiresome. Feels like a chore to keep shooting all those Locusts, Firestarters, Blackjacks, hellis, tanks. Over and over the same, just scaling up with your reputation. Enemy AI is rudimentary - there is no much strategy here. What is worse, the spawning is just illogical, with enemies appearing literary out of nowhere, including just right behind your back at worse. Mod "BetterSpawns" helps (when it does not crash the game... ).Lance AI is just atrocious. You can pack them with LRMs and AC/2, the long range stuff.. AI pilots will happily press head on. Tactics in this game is all about workarounding the game, not the battle field situation. Mod "TTRulez_AIMod2" help, when it works.Mission contracts and salvage allocation points. Who in the dev team thought it is a good idea to show the player all items they can't get anyway? Even by allocating full salvage, you may still not get by lacking 1-2 points. So what is the point of doing it? Salvage makes sense in multi-mission opps with very friendly faction, otherwise it is always better to take money and buy the mech you actually want. Apparently mod "Renegotiate" helps here but could not make it work with latest Steam version, always crashing the game.Most mission are randomly generated, and that is fine as it is all a one big fantasy after all. But come on ... after a while it is just a grind with no sparks, zero, nada, nothing. I spent over 400h in Battletech and felt less grind with all those generated mission than here after 20h... Mod "Coyotes mission" helps, although not sure if due to bugs in it or a combination with other mods - something spawned enemies are just borderline ludicrous (... a patrol mission with reinforcements of 30+ hellis at once + Assult mechs - pretty impression to be honest to see it).Music/graphics - no comment, everyone has their own unique taste, gfx feels good enough, sounds okeish, music - don't care, can always put on own playlist in the background. Mod "vonBiomes" is great, brings new and diversified landscapes, a truly impressive work. Concluding my rambling, this is the game which without modding is simply no fun. Which is sad since if you like Battletech then you have not so much of a choice... Modding helps to address many issues (assuming you get to a working state and not crashing game), but what game deserves a positive review if without modding it is just not a good game?

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I have a couple hundred hours in on this game on Epic.Welcome home, Mechwarrior 5. Finally on the platform it needs/deserves to be on. Yes I purchased it again, I dislike the Epic platform quite a bit from a technical standpoint.On to business! What is Mechwarrior 5: Mercenaries? Well it's a big stompy robot smasher game where you pilot giant battlemechs and attempt to turn other 'mechs into scrap metal for profit. It's a simple premise and the storyline in the main campaign is tired and has been done to death. BUT finally we have a career mode. Now that is what this game needed from the get-go and I'm glad they finally released it with some new content to boot. So now we can fly around the Inner Sphere to our hearts content and not have to do random story missions with some haphazard dialogue. Some is good, some is bad, it's hit and miss.How does it play? It's a Mechwarrior game, and it's done right. Mouse and keyboard are excellently supported, it's not as fleshed out as say Mechwarrior 3 was or as flexible as Mechwarrior 4, but it's done well and I can't complain. The mechs each have their own niches to fill, but aside from speed the overall handling doesn't change much mech to mech until you start to jump back and forth between the Assaults and Mediums, your turning speed and acceleration are two notable things you'll feel for instance. The Mech Bay is not as well done as MW3 or 4, it lacks the ability to do things like swap engines or structure components (mods add this in, it is divine) but you can still have some fun playing with loadouts and designing your own death-dealing combos.*EDIT* I forgot to mention the AI. Enemy AI and pathing is acceptable, they do a little circle-strafing now and then and usually don't just charge into your face. Sometimes they do though. Friendly AI is terrible most of the time, especially when you are trying to keep a base together and they run head first into every building they can. So you'll often end up babysitting them.Weapons are punchy and the selection is ever-improving with the new DLC adding some new tech. Mods can be used to add Clanner tech (cue squeals and giggles) but I'm hoping the dev team listens to reason and makes a Clan DLC pack, 'cause I'll buy that in a heartbeat. Mech selection is excellent however some of my favourites are missing (Bushwacker :'( for instance) but who knows what the future will bring.The management of your mercenary company is simple. It's not deep but it's serviceable. I noticed with the new career mode there are now unlockable perks to improve things and make your company more powerful, that's cool, I like the idea of it and I'll see how it plays out. I also noticed a lot of improvements to the mechbay like being able to change your weapon grouping without having to rework the 'mech now, that's nice.Mission variety? Eh it's got assassinations, base defence, base assault, horde mode and so on. There's a good variety but it CAN get a little stale. Mind you that was after a hundred hours in I think, and the maps are different enough that you won't play the same one twice in a row which is nice. There's a good assortment of biomes that match the planet environment you have travelled to, which is excellent. I have not noticed if they've finally added environmental effects in yet, like better heat sinking in cold weather, but if they have that is a huge step up. I'll investigate and update this when I figure that out.How's it look? Ok, I've seen a lot of complaints in this area and honestly I'm not sure why. The game is about giant, blocky metallic robots bristling with guns, this isn't Metro. It looks damn good with or without raytracing, and it runs very well on different hardware, I can honestly say that as I have tested this game on three different systems (I'll list them at the end) and it runs great on all of them, maybe with a little sacrificing here and there for the weaker ones. Terrain in the various maps and biomes is generic, trees look like trees and rocks look particularly rock-like. It's not a work of art, but it's serviceable and honestly you'll be dodging missles and gunfire more than you're going to be stopping to admire the foliage.Sound and music are good, weapons are suitably loud and fun. Soundtrack is good enough to get you going in the heat of battle. Voice acting is so-so, but whatever I don't play this for the talking, I've got other games for that.Overall this is an excellent Mechwarrior game hampered by some flaws and nitpicking. It's not especially deep, this is no Mass Effect, but it's got the destruction and mayhem of the 31st (or 32nd if you play long enough) Century. I enjoy it for what it is and I think Piranha Games has done a decent job here. As long as they keep pumping out new and improved content and don't abandon the game, I'll be a happy pilot.*Systems*Alienware Area 51M R1: 9700K, RTX 2080 (4K and 1080p @ 240Hz, Max settings, RTX On)Asus TUF15: i5 9300H, GTX 1650 (1080p, Medium-High)MSI GT780DXR: i7 2670QM, GTX 970M 3GB (1080p, Medium-Low) *Sandy Bridge is showing it's age on this one*

_childDocuments_.review: If you have never played the Mech Warrior series then here is a primer.The year is 30XX and the galaxy is at war. Humans have attained interstellar travel and hosted themselves among many stars. Broiled in coup attempts and failed negotiations the leaders no longer seek peace, but revenge or glory.After your father dies, you take command of Nik's Cavaliers and charge of a Leopard Dropship. An embattled system will be searching for worth while mercenaries and you can profit from this desire.Complete varied missions, build up your mech battalion and become a feared legend amidst the InnerSphere. There are no aliens, no Immaterium, no magic. Just grounded human stories that i could actually picture happening. Its less lore and more history book. The date in this franchise determines what tech you can use. Lots of equipment will not be invented till you pass time in game and reach the year it was developed. I really like this feature and is a very clever way to keep engagement while promoting balance.Each mech has different weapons it can field and a tonnage limit that must be respected. Each mech has armor laid around the body. Each part has separate hit points and must be broken before you can do damage to its structure. With tonnage in mind, you can ferry more armor, weapons, jump jets or heavier engines depending on your mech and play style. This leads to a near unlimited amount of choice when it comes to loadouts. Which IMO is what Mechwarrior is all about. I love gearing out my mechs and specializing them for certain mission types. It saves me a lot of C-Bills in the long run and helps keep repair costs at a minimum, albeit exacerbates storage costs.You must hire pilots and manage your company to keep it afloat. Each month you have to pay your crew, maintain your dropship and field your mechs. This can be as easy or difficult as you want depending on settings and if you want mods to customize it further. I like having a lot of action on the field and use mods to force extra mechs to spawn. This can kind of be a big deal late game when things start to become really easy. Like, when you finally get a King Crab.Overall, its a slower paced game. You jump star to star looking for contracts to earn more C-Bills. Much of your time will be consumed by altering mech loadouts and jumping around trying to fulfill those contracts.The rest of it is testing those loadouts and blowing up everything you see. Which is really satisfying when you can start landing Alpha Strike (firing all weapons) kills.This is the best rendition of MechWarrior to date, however i will say that MechWarrior online does many things better. From the weapons being reflected on your mechs, firing solutions, all the way to runtime.The worst thing about MW5 is its optimization and DLC. But, fortunately for all of us theres a mod for that (list at bottom)!Without the DLC or mods, this can get pretty monotonous and boring after about 10-40 hours depending on what you enjoy. There are not enough maps, mechs or weapons in the base game. Many of the weapons i used in other Mechwarrior titles are implemented by mods (some of the mods unlock DLC stuff without owning it.) There are tons of mechs i wish were in game, like the Adder and the Bushwhacker to name a couple. (There are over 150 mechs in the Battletech tabletop... lol)I refuse to play the game without YAML, a mod which adds more mech variants, weapons and equipment. Most importantly it adds another layer to your mech customization.I just bought all the DLC and finished most of it under 10 hours or so. A lot of the DLC content is maps and stories. They add a couple mechs and weapons but mostly lacking IMO. Heroes of the Inner Sphere and Solaris Showdown i think are my favorite.These devs need to stop making DLC and actually fix the runtime. Stutters and frame rates are really bad. Xenopax' mods only change a couple of assets and fixes 90% of the issue. Its unacceptible that modders are able to do this yet the devs sit on their hands. They might have a good reason, but it doesnt matter. Dont be Bethesda. If it wasnt for this glaring issue i would happily say this is the best MechWarrior game to date. But sadly MWO is giving it a run for its money with this in mind, even if the MMO has a hell of a lot less content.I still like it, and the mods make it infinitely better. Ill be putting a lot more hours into it. At least until the next MW title comes out.Here are some of the mods i highly suggest. Maybe try the runtime ones first if your new to the series.You can find them all in the Steam Workshop.Runtime mods:Xenopax Art Optimizer (ignore conflicts)Xenopax Optmize (ignore conflicts)MW5 Compatability PackContent mods:Yet Another MechLab + misc YAML packsKh0rns SoundmodBattleGrid OrdersArena Control (if you get Solaris Showdown)SpawnControlWARFXTTRulezAIMod2Planetary ConditionsMod Options

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Plays good, feels good, and is easily modded. It's a pretty good translation of TT rules to a real-time vidyagame, and makes it a proper MechWarrior title. Mechanics are easy to understand and straightforward, which makes it easy to jump in to. It's everything MWO should have been, but wasn't.EDIT: I forgot the most important part: Get AI mods ASAP. Otherwise the enemy, and more importantly your lancemates, are actually braindead. I'm talking starched, dry cleaned, zero wrinkle brains. Get the most updated version of TTRulez AI mod, and the XenoAI mod (which just overwrites some of TTRulez's mod to make it even better). It's far from perfect, but it's a LOT better than it is vanilla.A 'Mech in MW5 is tough but not indestructible. Smaller vehicles can and will ruin your day if left unchecked. Heavy Tanks and the larger VTOLs are genuine threats, as they were in TT. Armor is a precious resource, and taking internal damage is something to be avoided if possible. Every point of damage you take is money out of your pocket and time in the 'Mech Bay. Repairs get extremely expensive and time-consuming the worse the damage is, with limbs costing hundreds of thousands of C-Bills and weeks of work to replace. Armor levels are also deflated back down to TT numbers, which allows singular weapons to be scary again. A second advantage of lower armor is that smaller weapons also have value again, unlike in MWO, as a pair of Small Lasers or an SRM-2 are extremely viable backup weapons. Being able to boat weapons is generally irrelevant in MW5, where it was the only thing that mattered in MWO. You'll still bring a pair or quartet of Medium Lasers though, because they're still THE workhorse weapon of BT, even moreso with normal armor levels.Which brings us to 'Mech outfitting. It's not unlimited. Variants now have value beyond "mUh sLoTs", as sized hardpoints make a return. While it does mean you can't do many meme builds, it is much healthier for the game in general. Now you have to actually think about what variants you want and where you have to go to get them. It makes 'Mechs like the Urbie are particularly useful, as they're one of the first 'Mechs you'll find that can bring an AC/20, and the Large Ballistic slot it has as a result. There is a very good mod that loosens the slot restrictions to be in-line with TT, which makes it so a Small Hardpoint can hold Small and Medium weapons, Medium Hardpoints can hold all sized, and Large Hardpoints can hold Mediums and Smalls. I personally run it as it doesn't invalidate variants but does expand build options.Here we get to the actual meat of your build: Weapons and Equipment. This is where MW5 throws MWO out of the window, very much for the better. Everything you put on a 'Mech can be PERMANENTLY destroyed. If you lose a part of your 'Mech, it takes everything mounted there with it. If you take damage to your internals, it can and will damage the equipment and/or weapons mounted there. And if those things take enough damage, they're gone. You don't get them back, destroyed is destroyed. Beefier equipment like Autocannons can generally take a fairly significant beating, but fragile weapons like Lasers, PPCs, or Gauss Rifles will pop like balloons. Ammunition placement is even more vital now, as ammo cookoffs are both fairly common and extremely devastating. You'll be lucky to still have that part attached, let alone have intact equipment or weapons in there.Now as to why that's such a big deal, weapons and equipment are not freely available. You can't go to the magical ubershop and by whatever you want willy-nilly like in MWO. You have to either travel to Industrial Hubs to buy things, or scavenge it off the battlefields. As well, this game is set in 3025, you're lucky you still have normal Autocannons, Lasers, and Missiles. ER Lasers, Ultra ACs, Artemis LRMs, Streak SRMs, Double Heatsinks, it's all LosTech. Finding a  DHS is like finding a solid gold bar, let alone something like an ER Laser. SLDF-era 'Mechs, equipped with this tech as standard-issue, are even more rare.That also ties in to the Weapon tier system. Weapons are not built equally, and manufacturer matters. The bargain-bin Parti-Kill PPC you bought with a coupon you found in the back of a Sunday comic? Yeah, that hunk of ♥♥♥♥ doesn't hold a candle to a genuine Magna Hellstar PPC (T3). Literally, the Parti-Kill PPC is the T0 PPC, it doesn't get worse than that. Equipment isn't tiered, but it's generally rare. Superchargers are the most common thing you'll find, but MASC, ECM, and Active Probes are also LosTech. On top of that, only special variants of certain 'Mechs can mount them.Mechanically speaking, T0 weapons are the TT baseline, their stats are exactly what you'd read in the rules. T1 through T5 gradually increase those stats, and a T5 weapon is vastly superior to its T0 counterparts. Weight and ammo expenditure are the only stats that don't get touched, for obvious reasons.Using those PPCs as an example:T0 PPC - 10 Damage, 10 RPM, 9.6 Heat, 736m Range, 832m/s Projectile SpeedT3 PPC - 11.4 Damage, 12.3 RPM, 7.2 Heat, 1012m Range, 1144m/s Projectile SpeedAs you can see, the T3 is a dramatic upgrade from the T0. But... you can find that T0 PPC just about anywhere. That T3 PPC? Good luck. T4 or T5 weapons are even harder to find. LosTech weapons are just about impossible to get ahold of until late-game. MWO had zero consequences and was simply a game of "hee hee big number gooder", so you slap the best of everything on to every 'Mech. Blindly slapping weapons and equipment on to 'Mech in MW5 is a quick way to lose all of your good equipment and empty your bank account.To sum it up, if you've made it through this wall of text, MW5 is an honest-to-God MechWarrior title. Of course some crusty grognard will ♥♥♥♥♥ and nitpick about it because it's not their nostalgia-fueled memories of MW4, but they're stupid, and should generally be ignored. PGI managed not to ♥♥♥♥ the bed with this one, which is honestly surprising with how their previous titles have gone.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the combat can be fun (aside from the incompetent enemy and friendly AI), but everything else that surrounds it makes the game bland, grindy, and plain embarrassing.The missions are repetitive and unimaginative - even different types feel identical, and the procedural terrain generation creates completely forgettable maps. That applies to the campaign missions too, which are just a variation on the basic types with more enemies. There is no reason to use lighter mechs once heavies/assaults have been acquired, as mission objectives and setup almost always push the gameplay towards "kill everything".The gameplay overall is a complete grind, every task - such as finding a mech or a weapon other than the basic set available in industrial hubs - feels tailored to take as much time as possible. It's pretty infuriating to fully explore an industrial hub every planet has to be visited and its mech/equipment market examined individually - there is no gameplay in that aside from watching the loading animation a bunch of times and losing money.The story itself is a generic and completely forgettable revenge quest that never really tries to fit with the mercenaries theme - the protagonist and supporting exposition characters are 'good guys' who basically take on contracts out of the goodness of their hearts. There is essentially no characterization or anything of the sort - NPCs exist to blandly deliver exposition and that's about it,
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries

_childDocuments_.review: After hours of modding this game to try to make it better, I've come to a horrible realization: it's fundamentally broken. The AI is trash and they've done nothing to fix it, even when they added a DLC (Solaris) that should have required an overhaul for the AI. There was mods for the Solaris arena before, and seeing the complaints of those be the same for the DLC that the actual company who made the original game put out is just... something's wrong there, right? A free for all arena should not mean that everyone targets you the second your DPS hits higher than anyone else (which it will, pretty much regardless of what you're in.) There are AI overhaul mods out there, and they sorta fix the problem, sorta, but it's just another mod that you will need to get the full experience out of this mess.My next huge complaint is that save files get corrupted, fairly often, and for seemingly multiple reasons. It's not as noticeable in solo runs but in co-op, especially with mods (which you are GOING to want) a campaign can just suddenly die because the save file decides, nope, your friends don't get to play any more.Next is Co-op in general. What's one of the best parts of battletech/mechwarrior? Being able to design your own loadouts for mechs, right? Well guess what buck-o the only one who can ever do that (without mods) is the host. Fun, right? This extends to being able to buy things from the market, being able to train pilots, take missions and side quests, ect ect. Point is, there is a whole other suite of mods you will NEED if you want to make this game actually fun for other people in your co-op campaigns. TL'DR: you will NEED mods to bring this game up to anything more than a tedious mess, and even then there's no guarantee that you'll even be able to see all the content you want without it breaking, and if anything those mods you are gonna want and need are just going to bring that inevitability along faster.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries

_childDocuments_.review: Reactor Online, Sensors Online, Weapons Online, this game is a fun trip back to my memories.Mechwarrior 5 feels like the original idea that PGI really wanted to do when they had to settle for Mechwarrior Online. This game harkens back to a time where the storyline was simple, like the original Mechwarrior game for the PC. No not Mechwarrior 2, that was a Clan game. This game is set in the early 31st century before even 3025.The storyline won't be much, just your standard "Family died, now you're in charge of the Mercenary Unit" kind of thing you've played through before. The career mode is fun for me because you're given four Mechs, a sum of C-Bills, and that's about it. Work alongside a certain faction long enough and you'll make great friends and powerful enemies. Work with everyone and you might not get benefits like a loyalist would, but at least you won't starve. So long as there's two people in the Inner Sphere, someone will want the other dead after all.Be warned though, this is NOT the Battletech game from Hairbrained Schemes. That Battletech game plays more like the board game where you see all four of your warriors on a map and play out scenarios like a commanding officer overlooking the lance. This is Mechwarrior, you're in the seat of your Mech and blasting away at things. Be warned also that this is Mechs. Not Mecha, not Meks, not Armored Core, not insert your whatever mecha title here. This is one of the original properties that brought the genre to the USA and as such there's some things you need to remember.Your weapons do have cool downs. You can overheat. You can eat through ammunition. There's no energy shields. There's no going at Mach 10 while slicing the enemies down. You're in a walking tank and you move your torso independently from your feet. So you may be looking off to one side, but your feet are going in another direction. This is a game where you keep track of your Mech's damage, need to learn to cut your losses, and also target parts of your enemy. Center mass kills a guy, but it also really degrades the salvage.So if that sounds like a decent primer for you, then this game is worth a ride. I won't go into the background of the Universe itself here because that would take forever. Consult whatever forums and fan sites you can find or seek Catalyst Game Lab's novels for the bigger story. the TLDR is this: It's Game of Thrones with walking tanks.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries

_childDocuments_.review: I played Mechwarrior Online from 2015 to 2019. I quit that game mostly for it's pay to win and horrible grind. Coming into MW5 knowing it's single player like the older games I expected a well rounded and action packed experience. Well it certainly is action packed but it lacks Clan content, advanced zoom, and many weapon or engine variants. The Mechlab is also extremely over-simplified. This is where community made mods bridge the gaps. Vanilla MW5 is pretty boring. I don't recommend it at all. Play this game with mods however and it's one of the best MW games to ever exist. Steam workshop contains all necessary mods to bring in the extra weapons, mechs, gear. You will need mods for AI thinking too. The Vanilla AI are brain dead wastes of space. There is a mod to remove the tonnage limit too. All mods appear to just instantly work in CO-OP if all players install and enable them. Only the host has to configure anything.The CO-OP runs off the save file of the host. So they can play singleplayer then seamlessly swap it to CO-OP.This is a great feature. The players can edit mechs but can't directly purchase gear themselves. So your buddies can't burn all the c-bills.Career Mode is the best way to play the game. Just start a mercenary group and see what happens. You can save scum and reload to previous states if you mess up but the best way to play is "hardcore". Just discipline yourself to not reload when you make a mistake. The game becomes much more rewarding and skill based.Controls are identical to Mechwarrior Online which makes picking up this title on mouse and keyboard easy. I was worried at first I might need a HOTAS to get a good experience like with the old games but that's not the case. Everything controls smooth and free of jank. The game unfortunately eats graphics cards and CPUs for breakfast. You need a NASA PC to run this game on ULTRA settings in big fights. If you set the game to lower / medium settings it can still dip bellow 60fps in large fights.For reference I tested this on a i7 8700k + 1080ti & i5 11500 + 3060 (laptop gpu) & i9 11900k + 3080 ti. All systems have m.2 ssd.All 3 rigs ride the struggle bus on large fights with high settings at 1440p. The i9 & 3080 ti handles it better but still does have stuttering issues. I don't think it's possible to really get a constant 60FPS in this game if you have 50+ enemy fights. This game isn't a twitch shooter for the most part though so the frame stutters and dips don't really make any difference in the combat, it's just something that can annoy you.Overall, this is one of the best games to co-op with friends in. I'd prefer co-op to singleplayer just because how dumb the AI team mates are but other people don't mind. To each their own. 11/10 game.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries

_childDocuments_.review: The feeling of being in a big stompy mech is there, and it feels great, but there are some massive flaws that stop this from being a recommendation.The biggest one is the mech customising; The old style from MW4 was perfectly fine - each weapon took a number of slots - bigger weapons took more slots. This is gone; there's only one slot for any weapons of that type.This means that a Machine Gun takes up the same amount of space on your mech as an AC20... There's no deciding between a heavy hitting AC20 vs 3 long range rapid fire AC5s; it's just a downgrade.The other problem is that the story is pants.The graphics and sound are okay, though.
_childDocuments_.name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries

_childDocuments_.review: First of all... I love the Battletech franchise: I've read almost every book available, grow up playing Merchwarrior 2, 3 and 4, Mechcommander, I paint the minis... all the stuff.I feel very disappointed with this new delivery. Graphicaly, yes, is impressive. Like all the eyecandy, the effects, however, it does shows some cracks in between: repeating textures, minor glitches, weird ragdolls mechanics that makes the mechs do weird things.Menus UI/UX is awful. Configuration doesn't save and I've to keep changing the controls every time I reload. Content sometimes is shown outside of the display boundaries so you can't read anything. Small little annoying details that hinders your experience. Gameplay is repetitive at the point that after 10 hours you've seen all (Never forget this mantra: The "proceduraly generated mission" statement is the salesman approach to "lack of content"). Mechlab is at stupid level simplified, taking out all the cool things you could do before. I guess its the current times, where games have to be dumbed down at the point of absurdity and lameness. Controls are basic, options are few and UI/UX is awful and unable to modify...Worst thing is that it seems almost abandoned by its creators. _childDocuments_.review: I would not play this game unmodded nor recommend to anyone to buy this game only to play it unmodded.If you want a feel for what this game plays similarly to, try Mech Warrior Online, it's free to play and PvP so if you're good at that you'll slay here. That said, MW5 allows you to have fun and do ♥♥♥♥ that isn't meta where in MWO that can backfire. Also, bring back armor. Some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Warthunder player in a tank will spawn 2km behind you and nail you in the back and suddenly, you lost a side torso. Also, no clan mechs to be found here. So that's sad.Kind of like Fallout, this game is carried by mods...specifically mods that bring back basic customization that was in MWO (YAML/Yet Another Mech Lab) or add more weapons. Bring friends. 3 of em. The friendly AI is at best a bullet sponge.Gameplay? Pretty fun. You shoot ♥♥♥♥ in giant robots. There's a variety of giant robots and poor bastards not in giant robots to shoot at and get shot by. However you'll basically do all of the missions there are to do within 2 hours of career. I've exclusively played career mode. Kind of like all shooters, this gets repetitive and the only thing that'll bring variety to spice ♥♥♥♥ up is how you choose to play said missions. There's guns. There's lasers. There's missiles. No like, hammer of God giant beam cannons type ♥♥♥♥ you see from anime though.The most complicated the combat gets is heat management if you're boring and use lasers, less so if you use kinetics. That, and shielding using certain parts of your mech by turning the parts you want to shield with towards the enemy to say, protect your torso with your gun in it by shielding with your arm. Battle mechs are not similar to the infinitely cooler Gundams or Armored Cores. You are piloting a big, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow clunky machine of war designed to be shot at. It will be shot at. Mitigate what gets shot at the most by having other things get shot at. Oh, and melee is fun (with mods that actually let you change your engine, because a 48km/h assault mech isn't going to get to melee anything 99% of the time. At the same time, you get masc and a supercharger, suddenly your assault mech is going 150 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ km/h and you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ destroy everything because melee does a metric ♥♥♥♥ ton of damage. I guess it's a balancing feature so this is up to you)The AI? Well the enemy AI works, your friendly AI lancemates and any friendly AI for that matter have an IQ rating somewhere between ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and ♥♥♥♥ all. Do not put your lancemates into a mech you aren't willing to lose and spend millions repairing because they're going to lose it, or all of the damn weapons on it. The enemy AI can sometimes absolutely fold the ♥♥♥♥ out of you by hyper-focusing specific parts of your mech, or instead shoot whatever and do no significant damage. It's incredibly inconsistent and can be very obnoxious.There's a story mode but I've never played it, I play career. Battletech has a been around for a while and does have a pretty badass established universe like WH40K and what not, so it's definitely worth looking up lore videos or the sarna wiki if you want to get into that.The graphics? The game looks good. Environments are cool. The weather even affects gameplay like sensors and heat management (don't bring a mainly laser weapon mech to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ volcanic world unless you want to suffer).Ok now I'm just gonna start talking ♥♥♥♥ about the game (ignoring mods as I think I've said everything that needs to be said.)Your operator is impressively useless. Enemies are in the area? Reinforcements are approaching? Where? What ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ direction? To my south? North maybe? Not gonna tell me? Why the ♥♥♥♥ would you tell me only enemies in the area and not a general direction? I've talked so much ♥♥♥♥ about the operator being useless I don't actually have any idea if its because of lore or not.This games spawn system is appallingly retarded. Behold, lance of 4 slow ass assault mechs. Giant map. Guess where the dropship drops you? On the opposite side of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ map. _childDocuments_.review: You can’t pick up chicks in a tank. But you can pick them up with gaint mechs… …unfortunately they’re only after one thing. Your sweet ferro-fibrous armor plates.It's weird, played old MechWarrior when I was a kid and now I am a dad!Now I have a Bright Pink 90 ton mech that shoots lasers, rockets and shells. It also blasts electric guitar riffs for everyone in the immediate area to hear whenever I kill someone. I paid like $30 for thething. Worth it.Mechwarrior 3 was the first game I got when I was 8 and we had just bought a Windows 98 PC. I was allowed to choose 3 games, and because l'd read a review of this in PC Gamer that gave it like 9/10 or something I went for it. It's pretty much all I played that year. 35 years old now and just treated myself to a new PC just to play this!I've been playing PC games since the early 90s and there's something about this game that takes me back to the late 90s/early 2000s era of PC gaming. It's hard to really define it, but there was something about the art styles, themes, and UIs of that time that few other games are able to capture.MW5 is awesome full stop. If you know anything about mechs, mercs and the size of lasers you could say MW5 is gold plated awesome. I’m thinking of turning my PC around so when the action heats up it blows hot GPU air on me to help simulate the heat buildup in the cockpit.Mechwarrior 5 has that charm that most modern games are missing. More importantly, it has robots and pew pew. Not to mention the kabooms. I love the way the explosions sound. When you 'core a mech, it feels like you just let the whole countryside know that you mean business.The sound design is one of my favorite things about the game. Listening to AC10 round whistling past your cockpit is the coolest thing ever. Or playing in cockpit view and getting blasted by a volley of missiles or lasers to the face… I just love the feeling of melancholy when my favourite pilot gets themselves killed due to my overconfidence.Overall, I still like Mech 2 and Mech 4 better, but Mech 5 has matured into a really nice game. Mech 2 is better written, and Mech 4 has better campaigns. But Mech 5 is the first game to really nail the FEELING of being a Mech pilot as described in the lore.The waves of light tanks and choppers that you mow down, and the buildings you easily smash, give a real feeling of power to even the smallest Mech. In Mech 5 it feels like one Mech showing up to the fight, even a small one, can swing the balance of power. Obviously the enemy mechs don't feel that way, and would probably frustrate players if they did, but I feel more like a juggernaut in 5 than the prior games. The mechs also feel like they have a sense of mass and are a bit lumbering. Which Mech 4 was a little too smooth to really nail.It delivers on the big stompy robot fantasy better than the prior titles, and I enjoy that. Now the Earth-shattering Kabooms are great, but don’t forget the war crimes. Never forget the war crimes.8/10
