_childDocuments_.review: With  I've finally found the perfect Steam Deck game, the perfect time killer, and ultimately it's the most fun I've had with a "nothing" game. By flipping the sport on its head, Triband has created the best kinda-sorta-not golf(ish) game I could ever hope for. Trading the long, meticulous bore of real golf for bite-sized minigame-type levels based on simple hooks and references to past decade indie and AAA greats like . This game is a lot of things, fun is one of them, but it also feels very much like a love letter to the wild and wacky world of video games. The only gameplay constant is your aim and power bar necessary to hit your "ball", but after that, this game stops resembling anything that its namesake might suggest. I  had fun with this one, and I'll keep coming back for whatever the hell this is (especially when its unantiquated sequel drops on September 9th!).Drop your phone and your endless doom-scrolling and let golf save you, trust me on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s very simple to make a silly game that does many things and pokes fun at different genres and mechanics. It’s very hard to make it consistently great. Luckily, WHAT THE GOLF? almost never misses.I suppose, you could call this game a physics-based parody game and evoke comparisons with something like Goat Simulator or Amazing Frog, but in reality What the Golf is much more than that. This game doesn’t simply take the basic mechanic of golfing, so often found in countless golf video games (aim and set power of the swing), and apply it to other genres. It does it in a way, where the results are surprisingly fun on their own. Racing games, stealth, FPS, precision platformer, physics-based puzzle game – there are so many unexpected mixes in this title and almost all of them actually work.Every next set of levels is a surprise. And so very often more surprises hide inside the sets. The game isn’t shy about how silly and full of dumb puns it is, it shows what it’s all about at the very beginning, where it teaches you how to play. Put the ball in the hole? Nice, now put the golfer in the hole. Now put the hole on the flag. Now ride a horse while shooting exploding barrels. Yes, you’re still playing the same game, keep playing.It’s also great that the main progress of the game is nicely balanced with never an annoying or dull moment. To complete the game itself, all you have to do is to finish each level once to finish the set and move on to the next one. But each level flag has two additional challenges you can complete, which are presented as harder versions of what you’ve played in the main level, but in reality are often completely different levels and experiences altogether. Completing those gives you additional rewards, but it’s completely optional and if you feel like some of the levels aren’t fun for you, don’t feel like you’re missing out on something.Sadly, some of those optional levels are really unfun and in all those very rare occasions it’s because the game tries to turn its chaotic random gameplay into a challenge. Most of the time, it’s done in a way that’s still entertaining and is sometimes even easier than the original level. But in a few bizarre moments the game requires impossible precision with its own imprecise mechanics. And strangest of all, in all of those cases the level could be turned into a fun experience by just tweaking the “challenge” numbers and adding one or two additional tries, or tweaking the timings a tiny bit.Those moments are also tied to the least fun sets of levels and that’s another point worth mentioning. There are quite a few genuinely amazing mixes of gameplay ideas in the game, yet most of the truly fun ones are easy and quick to complete. Yet, some of the really unfun ones are unreasonably long (the cars segment just kept on going, for example). Perhaps, some of those really fun sets will be revisited in the future as an update or a DLC, since the game now has an extra mini-campaign based around sport, which wasn’t there at the start.Either way, WHAT THE GOLF? is one of the most enjoyable and entertaining games I’ve played in a while. It’s really fun, really funny and consistently surprising. And I would highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I know a game like this tends to be filled with joke and meme reviews, but I really wanted to try and write a somewhat serious review because honestly, this game is great, and it deserves the praise it gets.I feel like this and Untitled Goose Game fill the same general, I don't know if you'd call it a genre per se, but maybe a  "space"? Games that are casual, full of humour, don't take themselves too seriously, but at the same time, are well made and fun to play.WHAT THE GOLF? is essentially a collection of mini-games centered around a common control scheme and a vague sense of golf. The controls are the same for all the games: you click and drag to aim and adjust "swing" power. What ultimately happens though is dependant on the level itself. I don't want to spoil anything, but all the levels have themes. A lot of them are video game themed and a lot have a more broad theme (like "music"). The levels and challenges are mostly well designed (there's one or two levels which are kind of poor). While some levels can be frustrating, I don't think any of them are so extreme that they're impossible.Overall, I would definitely recommend WHAT THE GOLF? if you're looking for a casual, absurd, and mildly puzzle-y type game. It has some of the most creative levels I've ever seen in a video game and I actually found myself saying "What the f***?" on more than one occasion.

_childDocuments_.review: It's well made and has a lot of content. Maybe too much content to be honest as some levels and ideas start repeating themselves and doing 100% felt a bit tedious at times. I found it as a nice game to jump into for very short 30-60 minute gaming stints just to switch brain off. Most levels are simple to clear, some might take skill, others more luck focused. It's not uncommon to blow through some levels in mere seconds, but the additional challenges help bring more skill to the table. There was some funny ideas in there and it works best when it catches you off guard with your first shot and flips the script on what item is actually being used for the level. I could see the younger audience having a lot of fun with it and the bizarre levels and ideas it throws around.

_childDocuments_.review: (My playtime on Steam is not indicative of my time with the game. I played it when it released on Epic a year ago)What the Golf is an incredibly silly game. Every level does a great job at taking your expectations, and throwing them out the window. Within the first 5 minutes, you will puck a man, a house, and try to score into a moving hole. Some levels are parodies of famous games like Angry Birds, and others will have you navigate the gravitational pull of a planet.The main campaign is a lot of fun, and most of the times it does a great job and changing up the gimmicks. Every level can be replayed in a few alternative modes. Sometimes they will have you do the same thing with only a specific number of hits allowed, while others will strap a rocket to your ball and tell you to destroy hot dog stands. It can be pretty crazy.You can be sure that the game will have you constantly giggling. And that's where my enjoyment comes from. The game isn't exceptionally hard, but can get tricky at times.The new Steam features are welcome. A silly local multiplayer mode, a pretty intuitive level editor etc. The game has a bunch of nice features to fill it out.There isn't really much more to say.It's golf, but funny.Despite the silly premise, the game is actually very well done. You can tell a lot of love went into every aspect. The music is fun, the aesthetic is charming, and the physics work very well with the ideas.If you like golf (or maybe not?), check out the game!  I think it's a very relaxing and funny game overall!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A goofy golf game with cute visuals, silly gameplay and plenty of fun content. The game revolves around the concept of golf obviously, though from this it plays from regular kind of golf, putting the ball, various objects or even yourself towards the hole/flag, to playing different parodies of games like mario, donkey kong and flappy bird. Various genres are also found such as platforming and racing, which does further give a mixture of gameplay to this physics element oriented game. Along with the many, many levels to go through, there are also a bunch of different game modes that can be played, from local co op, daily challenges as well as a level editor which is in progress. Create your own as well as play ones that others have made. Having included the feature of steam remote play is also a nice addition, as it then allows the option to play with friends online. The humour in the game is a highlight of the game, with the puns, weird gameplay and the dopey visuals. Several kinds of environments are also played in too, with suitable visual backgrounds and music. Playing in the winter snow or playing in big arenas are quite fun as you explore the campaign and adventure modes. Overall, it is a great and funny game with a lot of charm to it.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GOLF? is not exactly the golf game one would expect. It is instead a bag full of absurdist mini levels that often revolve around a hilarious pun. For example, a level called ‘Hole in 1’ would have you toss a literal hole from the ground into a gape that is shaped like the Hindu-Arabic numeral 1.My personal favourite levels are the ones based on SUPERHOT. Fully functional bullet-time with the pun being SUPERPUTT. Levels are also based on many other games such as Portal, Metal Gear, Mario, Guitar Hero, Flappy Bird & Angry Birds.The insane amount of variety in humour and gameplay is commendable and the game still has more episodes on the way. There are plenty of challenge levels that escalate well towards mastery and completion. Secrets are always well-hidden; never too obscure to access.This game will constantly churn a chuckle out of you. If you are tired of games that make you sweat, try this one that makes you laugh!

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't care about achievements, this game is awesome and you should buy it. But as an achievement enthusiast, this game is a pain in the ass. They have a habit of adding achievements years later, but then the achievements have issues. It's already annoying enough to come back to finish the game again when the new achievements are added, but for those achievements to be unobtainable without ridiculous workarounds? I have to give this game a negative review out of principle.The first time was when they added Thanksgiving levels and achievements for getting them. The problem was that they were only available for a limited time around Thanksgiving time, and I found out about a week after the levels were removed. I had to wait a year to go back and finish the game again. Now they added a new achievement about a secret in the main campaign, but you can't get it if you already finished the campaign! The only way to get it is to replay the game to this point again (which is like 70% through). Yes, I could download a save, but I shouldn't have to."You're really giving the game a negative review over achievements?" I'm giving the game a negative review for not respecting my time on multiple occasions. Either don't add new achievements, or if you do, make sure they work. And if they don't work, let your community know you're fixing them. Why would I ever buy another game from this dev after this precedent they've set? If they actually fix the glitches with the achievements, I'll be happy to change this to a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: At first looks like an innocent simple golf game, but after playing it for the first few minutes you can easily see what is really happening here. Gameplay is consisting of powering up a shot and aiming the same shot, but that's the only thing that makes the game similar to other golf games. There is a "campaign" mode in a golf game where you play as the ball. You go through different sections with different themes where for each section there are 15+ different levels (and each level has minimum 3 sections). And each of the levels contain a gimmick. In regular golf games, the level design changes from level to level, there are new obstacles etc. But here for example instead of shooting a ball to the hole, you sometimes shoot the "hole" in to a hole that has a shape of "ONE" and when you successfully finish that level, you get a success message saying, drum roll..... Hole in One. I think that this explains so much about this game. Besides the gameplay, soundtrack was fitting and fun. My only non-positive comment is that you can't get one achievement naturally, you need to download an older version and do some stuff. So a fix to that problem can result in a perfect game for its price

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf? is listed on Wikipedia as a game in the "Sports" genre. On one hand, that can't be further from the truth, but on the other, I can't blame the wiki editors because it's hard to pin down great comparisons for this wholly unique experience. The closest game to this in spirit that I can think of is WarioWare; it doesn't have the timed element of WarioWare but it does have the humor, wackiness, and constant improvisation. Indeed, the greatest strength of the game is all the curveballs it throws (golfs?) at you. You really never know what crazy idea they've cooked up next.But man is it FUN. I can't remember the last game that made me laugh out loud this many times. I was just so happy my entire playthrough; everything is so silly and insane that you can't help but incredulously think: "this is so ridiculous" as it throws you from one absurd minigame to the next. I want to list notable examples of its comedy in my review but I don't want to spoil the magic; a big part of the fun is seeing the zany concepts for yourself.One thing that jumps out the screen is how much fun the developers must have had making this game. So much fun, in fact, that they've released a bunch of (very high quality!) free DLCs post-release. Some of these DLCs are actually the most polished levels in the entire game so make sure to check them out. The amount of content overall is stunning, honestly. Not only is the main playthrough quite lengthy, but there's a Vs. mode (which is pretty fun!), multiple DLCs, a level editor, and daily challenges. An impressive package; they didn't have to do this much and they did.As for difficulty, the game is appropriately easy. There are a handful of tricky stages that you might need to replay a few times, but the vast majority you'll beat on your first or second try. Losing is just as much fun as winning in this one though; sometimes you lose in the funniest ways imaginable so you can't help but laugh either way.Presentation is appropriately hilarious. The art is as dumb and funny as it ought to be; I love it. The music is similarly absurd; with various riffs of the same overarching theme. Great stuff.As for flaws, there aren't many. This game is really good. But, at least for me, 3 of the minigames are broken. Like, they simply don't work. There are hundreds of minigames, so it's not a big deal in the grand scheme of things, but it's kind of a bummer that my completion is stuck at 99.9%. I think you could also complain that the physics and controls aren't quite as sharp as they could be, but the game's relative ease makes that a pretty minor concern. Sometimes the wonky physics make it all that much funnier, in fact. You can cheese your way through a ton of the stages if you understand some of its finer mechanics (Soccer levels are pretty guilty of this; you can just spam shots and zoom across the stage), but again, because the game's focus is on zaniness, all in all this doesn't really make the game any worse. Finding a funny way to break a minigame is part of the charm, if anything.Overall, I'd give this game a high, high recommendation. I also think it'd be a great game to give to someone who is new to or unfamiliar with video games. So much of what is here validates what makes video games as a medium so special to begin with. Tons of fun; please support this game! Love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Only get this game on a 50% or more discount if you want to try it. This game's rating is obviously pushed by a fan base living in another world. What should be a fun little "party" game with references to other games turns out to be a physics and buggy frustration getting worse as you play. Sometimes you get a good laugh at what some levels offer but later on the game chooses difficulty over those fun little moments. Simply getting around the map becomes a struggle as the mechanics behind hitting objects in the game rely on position of the object and your mouse cursor not just your mouse. Control requires time to practice and slows down the game quickly such as gravity effecting your ball in different directions.It only took about 5 hours to see this game could be so much more but is plagued by the mess injected into it. A lot of it is good then the bad parts come in the worst way ruining the experience. The levels with "Par" challenges can be overly frustrating due to RNG and the physics choosing whether your object will roll one way or bounce another. In fact, some levels are just constantly trying to get the good RNG for a set up at finishing the level. All the while the same music and sound effects happen over and over until it's near too much.As of writing this I have 29/50 achievements and will try to finish all of them. There's some good things going on in the game so it's worth looking at some more. However, there's gotta be something better our there for you to spend $20 on if you're looking for a great gaming experience.Edit: Wanted to add one more thing. The reason I even wrote this review is the car levels. The  car controls horribly as it will turn left or right for no reason. When it hits something sure but send it a direction then watch it veer left or right. The devs should know better. Good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really enjoyable not-golf game.   The only connections to golf games this has are 1) some levels do in fact have golf balls and holes and 2) you control your "swing" by pulling away from "X" (where X can be a golf ball, but also literally anything else that's not a golf ball).   More accurately, the game is 90% puzzles and closer resembles a Warioware game.  If you have not figured out from the videos and screen shots, you are rarely actually golfing, and each stage does a pretty good job at subverting your expectations for how the level is supposed to work.  More often than not the simplest solution is usually the correct one, but not always the most obvious one.  The game is pretty forgiving and let's you experiment as much as you want.  The only exception to this is during challenge levels, where you may be limited by time or the number of actions you have per turn.  The game has a pretty lengthy main campaign if you are completing all levels and challenges.  I'm 6hrs in and at 70% completion.  It's a nice casual pick up and play game, and I'd highly recommend for something off the ordinary to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I once read on a reddit post recently "How can we make golf fun again? Add defense!"This game is exactly like that, but in a fun, original, clever way. The controls are easy, just point, click, hold back for how much power you're hitting your 'ball' and repeat until you reach your destination. The concept is clever with a touch of goofiness, you really won't expect what will happen next! The visuals are vibrant and fun, sometimes I will pause and just look around to get a good chuckle, such as the satire'd versions of Mario, Floppy Bird, & Angry Birds.So far I have had no issues with the PC port, this game really POPS out from your monitor. Definitely the best experience I've had playing 'WHAT THE GOLF'.This game is made for you if you're looking for something chill, challenging, and relaxing. A perfect nightcap game where you can visit daily to climb the daily leaderboards.P.s: Please make an album! The music is the icing on the cake!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't aware golf needed to be fixed but this game has convinced me. If you're expecting just some silly golf jokes, you're in for a little more of a treat. It's a level of humor you'd be familiar with if you like Katamari Damacy. There's no plot but there's a lot of homages to some of your favorite games that'll make you feel pretty old.It'll also make you feel like a little kid. I've somewhat fantasized about throwing the golfer rather than the golf ball so this is a pretty imaginative game that tickles my fancy.Other than offering a good party game aspect, there's also a main game that isn't boring or impossible to play without your buddies. You can sink into that golf zen when you want. Another huge draw is a level builder. I haven't done too well tinkering in it myself, but the temptation to create levels is a huge one. Allowing for a game like this to have our custom content be playable by others is very alluring.Of course there are some drawbacks. I found the soccer- sorry, football levels to be somewhat buggy. Sometimes the hit box on the ball was overly sensitive and exploded with a touch I didn't even see. That's okay, I guess I overestimated things...but that didn't seem so sensitive in other levels. Anything involving those evil little cultists- I mean delightful children enjoying youth sports seems to be cursed somehow. It's probably just me. I probably just suck at that.This also seems to be best played in bite-sized amounts. Sure you could just binge the whole solo part of the game, but there's three parts of a single hole to conquer so you can get a little crown and prove you are worthy of wandering around this spiffy lab...and possibly wrecking the joint with your superior golf powers. Take it easy so you don't go into golf rage. Unless this is your sort of thing. I'm not gonna tell you how to enjoy your not-golf-golf.

Each different "world" here has a unique theme and often sub-themes, many of which pay tribute to mechanics from other games (SUPERHOT, for example). The game has a very cute artistic direction which I think fits it just right. I think there is a good game here, I just feel this is a subpar platform for it. So again, I would recommend you get it on mobile if you are interested.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I actually have to say "I want to like this game, but can't." It is an interesting concept and a lot of (large) parts of the game are actually very fun. It references a lot of popular games, from multiple time periods, from indie games to Valve or even Nintendo. BUT: Every level-flag has 3 different challenges. And you can tell it was just forced and out of principle in some places. A lot of twisty challenges just aren't fun anymore, they are just some Par number that can only be achieved if every mouse movement is 100% perfected, with perfect timing or some random limitation like "pacifist" in a SUPERHOT-themed level (a shooter game) where there are perfect-aim-enemies standing around everywhere and you just have to "figure it out".But maybe you're fine with just skipping about a third of the content because it is ridiculous, or you think "I like to grind, I can do that". OK. I would normally consider myself one of those people as well. But there's another factor that makes it harder. In those places where the gameplay is extremely difficult, you generally have to make fast and precisely timed movements. But the game's controls almost literally backstab you. If you pull your mouse to far up to go backwards ("down"), it just flips around to forwards again - the literal opposite of what you wanted to achieve.I don't know why this is, but it feels like something someone would have had to think "Hmm, that's a good idea" and intentionally implement. It is not a good idea. It is confusing, almost always unexpected and makes those already extremely hard, forced twist challenges even harder.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another golf game. But What The Golf? is unlike any golf game you know. It’s golf, and at the same time it’s not. What do I even mean? Read on!Even if you do not know the rules of golf, if you’re a regular gamer then it’s likely you have at one time in your life played a round of virtual golf. Realistic or arcade-y, it doesn’t matter: get the ball into the hole in as few swings as you can, we all know that. Easy.What The Golf? does this as well, but with some fun and surprising twists and takes on the sport. Neither the course, the ball or the club are what they seem. The only thing that’s pretty much consistent throughout the game are the physics. Yes, logically you could say, but also because of the many crazy ideas the game throws at you. Naturally you should be able to get the ball, or whatever in this case, into the hole with precision and therefore it’s of such importance that the physics all work as they should, even if the game doesn’t seem to take itself seriously. Imagine instead of swinging the club you’re actually swinging the person holding the club. It becomes a whole different ballgame (pun intended); it’s completely crazy. Welcome to What The Golf?. And that’s just one idea.The game has you play as a golf ball that can be swung into any direction, with any force and with complete precision by using the mouse. As a golf ball you’ll navigate through some sort of overworld first where you can find and enter many courses. The overworld also has many different areas with different themes and although the game is pretty short it stays fun and fresh all the way through because of these different takes on the sport. Despite the overworld having different kinds of areas you only get to play in these settings with those kinds of zany ideas and physics when you enter the level itself. Some fun examples would be having to play in space or play from a 2D game perspective like Flappy Bird or Super Mario. And there are many, many more ideas just like this, almost all of them fun to play. But many of these areas and levels are locked until you complete a specific amount of levels so you can’t just go to the parts that sound or look more interesting to you.Levels are usually completed in a matter of minutes. But you can try to beat the par score afterwards to unlock another level. Finishing that level will ultimately award you with a crown, letting you know you’ve done everything you can in that specific level. Now, the game isn’t hard per se - with the exception of a few levels - but beating the par scores can sometimes get really frustrating. It’s better to skip it for a little while then and get back to it later. Somehow - for me at least - you can always get it done when you’re not trying so hard and just let it come naturally.There are hundreds of levels and unlike the Apple Arcade version the Steam version comes with an included level editor, providing even more hours of fun. Completing the game should take most us around four hours, but to do everything you can easily double that number, or at least make it to seven hours.And even with the crazy amount of levels, physics and ideas I never ran into any technical problems.Visually the game is quite pretty, with a mix of colorful 2D art as well as 3D models that look okay-ish. The 3D models aren’t very detailed, but they’re clear enough to make them out just fine. Just don’t expect anything amazing on that front. The 2D graphics are a whole lot better, however. The animations and physics are all excellent.There’s no voice acting since there’s no actual story. The sounds effects are all great, though. And the music isn’t brilliant or anything, but is still perfectly fine.It’s ridiculous, it’s frustrating, it’s fun, it’s dumb and it’s insane. The game manages to evoke quite some emotions during your time with it. If you don’t think it’s funny - or fun - the first 30 minutes you play this then it’s probably not for you. If you want something else in your golf game, however, it doesn’t get any better than this. What The Golf? is golf game that *does* reinvent the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun singleplayer experience, the game is somewhat enjoyable if you only do the bare minimum number of mostly optional challenge missions. However, it's also extremely short lived for its price and a lot of the gimmicks are going to run really, really dry really, really quick.The floaty, imprecise and inconsistent physics it presents though, make any of the challenge missions (especially the more tedious ones) insanely frustrating, unrewarding and generally unfun. Like trying to enter the grand prix in a unicycle falling apart, you feel cheated because you're losing an uphill battle. These challenge missions can sometimes scream precision or speed in environments where you're provided little to none, making an extremely poorly designed and awful experience.If you still intend to go through with some of these, avoid any of the par missions... They're usually AWFUL and suck all fun out of the game.Though if you do manage to get the optional challenge missions done, what do you get? Some extremely boring figures in a museum that you'll never see again and get no use out of. Terrible rewards to go with terrible challenges.If you're just going in this for the singleplayer then avoid this game outright. Even if it was 75% off, it's not worth it as you're getting an extremely short set of base challenges and if you ever go for the optional ones they're going to be so frustratingly awful that you'll wonder why you ever bought the game.So what about the multiplayer experience?Well, it's actually really great. With some extremely big caveats.First of all there's no online multiplayer. At all. For a game of this price tag, during a global pandemic, that is outright unacceptable. You'll be stuck with Steam Remote Play which, for this game the quality of my remote play sessions (just for this game, generally i've had no issue with remote play before) have been pretty garbage.However the 1v1 multiplayer itself has been really enjoyable and presents a nice amount of variety. Maybe they'll consider using that Apple Arcade money to actually put some online multiplayer in?It's also limited to just the two players. For... Well, i've honestly not found a reason. Why there's no 4 way PvP i'll never know, but it's also a huge negative to the game.So if you're interested in multiplayer, should you pick it up? Yes... At a heavy discount, because it's sure as hell not worth the price tag it's asking for. Maybe wait for a sale, though i'd dip no lower than 60% off on this one unless you're REALLY desperate and none of your friends own it.Overall I can't recommend unless it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: In 1988, the ultimate anti-golf game was released. It was simply titled "Will Harvey's Zany Golf" and the game was so much fun because each hole and each thing you had to do was completely unpredictable. You had to adopt a new strategy for each of the 9 holes and if you made it to the secret 10th hole, Mystery, you knew you had accomplished a great feat. (until I found out you could shoot the mouse's eyes on the 9th hole when they turned red and you would go automatically to the 10th hole). 32 years later, we have a worthy but try-too-hard sequel, in WHAT THE GOLF? I see this as having a lot of potential with a slight caveat: Play more to people who hate golf, like me. "I'm hitting a cat!" "I'm hitting a vase!" "I'm hitting a TV with a VCR!" is cute but it doesn't really strike me as funny after the 10th time I do this. I've heard people say that certain other genres like role-playing games and FPS's will be lampooned and one reason I like this game is that it took on a trope of Super Meat Boy. That is genuinely fun and I like what I'm seeing. That said, I'm thumbing this one up for what it could be, rather than what it is. Simply focus on the parody aspect. You don't need to hit a couch to be funny. You've got this, so make it happen.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game about "golf." And by "golf" I mean whatever was going on in this game. The game has plenty of creative levels using the ideas of golf and hitting the ball in the hole. The game has a great charm with the cheery upbeat demeanor and funny scenarios of most levels. The music added immensely to the experience especially the tracks that singers sing "what the golf" constantly. It doesn't take long to 100% the game but you'll enjoy it the whole time.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf is inherently a boring, degenerate sport. What the Golf? seeks to remedy those two inherent crippling aspects of the game, and does so in pretty much the best possible way: by embracing absurdity. I have rarely had as much pure fun playing a game as I have with What the Golf?, despite the escalating challenge of the late game curve. You play Ball, a golf ball who's been putted into the Golf Lab, a weird place run by a series of linked AIs, all doing their best to figure out how to make golf, which again is inherently boring, fun. pitches start off more of less normal, but get weirder and weirder as you go along, and though the ball is usually on the screen, it's not always what you're hitting toward the hole; other objects include remote controls, TVs, couches, the golfer himself, cars, bicycles, and at least one type of livestock. It's nonsensical comedy sports gaming done right, very much in the style of Katamari Damacy (which I would be very surprised to learn was not among the inspirations for this game), and very much a breath of fresh air. Give What the Golf? a try and if you don't enjoy yourself, then you clearly should seek medical help as you appear to have been born without a soul.

The rug in the bowling levels (which is a clear reference to the Big Lebowski) was so funny. The space levels were amazing (along with many other amazing stuff). _childDocuments_.review: Generally a really fun game about "golf" with tons of dumb and crazy ideas spread out in 11 areas. It's filled with many refrences, way too many puns about golf. It's really hard to get bored of this game, since gameplay is almost always different. Sometimes you are a flying explosive barrel trying to knock down the pins and sometimes you are playing with time and outmanoeuvering your enemies in "Super Putt".Not everything can be perfect, since the biggest problem comes from level variations. So each level has 3 variations and those quality can vary. Sometime there is a new gimmick added to a level which completely changes how it's played or it can be a brand new level with new mechanics never to be seen anywhere else in the game. Other times it can be pretty much the same level again or just a restriction of how many moves you can do. Games like this should always be pretty easy, that's because they are about different ideas, experiences, jokes and gimmicks devolopers came up with. Which this game for the most part is, you can beat like 95% of levels withing first attempt and that's great! Unfortunately there is still that 5%, most of them aren't a problem they just require a bit more attempts and some of them are Incredibly frustrating. There are levels which require pretty much pixel perfect shots or INCREDIBLE LUCK, those levels really put you out of this fun experience. For no reason at all there is a big con for achievement hunters, because of the achievement that requires you to beat 18 daily mission's. In a game that you beat in 1-3 sittings you have to play everyday for 18 days. What's even bigger downside are the daily missions themself, because they are really lazy. It's literaly just 5 random levels from main story connected together.Overally it's a good game and it's worth playing, if you can get it for cheap you get 3-7 hours of joy.Just remember to be carefull with level variations and be patient if you want all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute joy. Endlessly creative, profoundly funny, and on the main very finely crafted. I don't want to say too much for fear of spoiling the fun, except to say that this game is well worth the money. I expected five hours of entertainment; I'm five hours in streaming to my friends and we've got several hours to go yet.What a riot.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I must say...it certainly is Golf-like...but that's where it throws everything else (and the kitchen sink) not just out the window, but at the HOLES!If you're looking for something fun, mindless, and just-challenging-enough, along with just enough extra stuff (like trophies, hidden commentary, cats...CATS!) then this is for you. The physics is good for this type of animated game, you never really count any strokes (unless completing "challenge versions" of holes to get crowns on your way to trophies), and more than anything else, it's just FUN. Oh, and if you have a sense of humour, and have played the odd other video game here-and-there, you will DEFINITELY enjoy the "homage" levels (Portal, anyone?) strewn throughout the game, and the pop-culture nods distributed throughout.Overall, lots of fun, and I recommend it highly!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game from start to finish. From the very start it's fun and kind of addicting and doesn't lose this momentum it gains at the beginning. I absolutely recommend this game, however I do have a few gripes with it.The positive:- Fun and addicting gameplay from start to finish (as I've said above)- The game doesn't overstay its welcome. The campaign doesn't feel drawn out and keeps innovating throughout itself to keep things interesting- The hub worlds are cool- The themes of most of the sub-areas are cool- The extra episodes are great- Some puzzles can be solved in multiple ways- The humor and references are good- Easy to 100%- Simple but effective art direction- Runs wellThe neutral:- The "boss fights" were fine. They got the job done but they could've been more of a challenge i think- Some challenges were really fun and difficult in a fair way, some were just either a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or completely luck based and some were just kinda whatever- The daily challenges are okay but I don't know what purpose they serve other than to pad out the game time for achievement hunters- The gimicks can get rather predictible- LGBT flags randomly appear in some maps. Thought this was worth a mention for some people, I don't care about this tbhThe negative:- I don't think the game is worth it at full price. Buy it on sale- There are advertisements for the studios newer game in this game- I don't like date specific achievements, soI wasn't fond of the daily quest and thanksgiving related ones. Thankfully these can be completed any time if you change the date on your computer.- The soundtrack gets very boringI think this is a good game overall and the main campaign deserves a playthrough at least once.

Controls are muddy, plus they've managed to choose the most dissatisfying amount of friction on every level. _childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 54-year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my son, who is now 14. My son recently started playing this game. This was terrible for me because it was already hard enough for me to spend time with my son because he was always out with his friends or watching YouTube. So I decided to make a Steam account to play with my son. I started playing, but this was my first time playing a video game since the 90's, so I was quite lost. I asked my son for help, and together we spent some hours playing this game. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my son since my wife had died. _childDocuments_.review: You might say that this is just a golf game, but it's much more. It's a view on society. We might say we hate golf, but we play a game entirely based on it. "What The Golf?" is a reflection on our culture. You could show this to an alien, and they would understand everything about humans to the point where they could perfectly blend into society. The computers in the game can be argued to be one's problems, and destroying them would mean overcoming these problems which is what we all strive for. Even though you might think that with such a simple concept of golf that there would not be any kind of creativity, but you would be mistaken. Just like the caveman first discovering fire, and then finding many other uses for it, "What The Golf?" expands upon golf in ways that barely resemble golf, but at the same time feeling just like it. _childDocuments_.review: This game can't decide what it is. Is it a party game? Not really, the campaign is far more singleplayer oriented. Is it a singleplayer game? Yes, but the quick holes that service a punchline at the end would be more enjoyable if the game were more party oriented.Is this challenging? Not really. The majority of holes are over suuuuuper fast, and the ramped up versions of the holes aren't usually even the same level. Most levels are either too simple to be fun, or too frustrating to make finishing them enjoyable because the physics are annoying. Strangest of all, most holes don't even have a par challenge. You just kind of finish them, read the 'joke' and move on. Even the ramped up versions usually are just "this isn't hard....just really slow or really long".The overworld map is also annoying. Each hole has, usually, one hole, then you're back to putting to the next hole in a map with tons of items strewn about that prevent you from smoothly navigating to the next level. It sounds like a challenge all its own, but it's just another annoyance.This isn't really golf. It's just a large series of toys, only sometimes serving any pressure or challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is right on the cusp of 'recommend', but I'm going with 'no' for one simple reason.But before I explain that, I'll say first that the overall reviews for 'What the Golf' are spot on. The graphics are winsome, sound design is pleasant, and the humor is like a Mel Brooks film: when you pump out a dozen gags per minute, some will land and some will fall flat. No harm there.The developers invest admirable effort--there are no heights too high, no depths too low--in levels that last barely ten seconds and serve no purpose other than to deliver a terrible pun. Truly, you have no idea what will be thrown at you next.As others have pointed out, if you are a completionist or an achievement hound, you are in for a rough ride. While you can skim the levels and finish the game with little trouble, some of the 'par' and 'crown' levels are absolute trash, difficult primarily because they are awful. Another gamer gave wise advice: you'll have the best experience if you try the extended levels once or twice and then walk away from the rubbish ones. That's what I did.And I had a good time. A few laughs, a bit of fun. The game was on sale for under $7, which is about the right price. More than that is too much for the goods on offer.Why the thumbs down then? I discovered this game because the developer's new game, 'What the Car', showed up in my recommendations and looked interesting, so I took at look at their (small) catalog and ended up buying 'What the Golf'. And after playing 'What the Golf' I can say I have no interest in playing other games from this team.The actual gameplay is so thin, as shallow as a birdbath, the variety ultimately superficial, the novelty spent, that it's most fun when, through imitation, it reminds you how fun other games can be, and that you should probably play those games instead. And so you should.There's value in reminding us of great games, but not enough for a recommendation, as it is also a reminder of what this game is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again Steam's review system fails to offer the necessary nuance for a great-but-flawed game.What the Golf? is equal parts fun, joyful, surprising, tedious, frustrating, and hateful.For every level where it surprises you with a unique or brain-twisting idea, there is another where the twitchy controls or excessively harsh requirements cause acute anger. Every giggle of surprise is matched by a sigh of weariness.Panic and frustration can be great when competing against other players. Everyone has to deal with the same randomness and silly controls and arbitrary goals. But when playing solo it makes you curse the developer for not tightening up the puzzles a little.It settles into a routine. First part of a stage is quirky, 2nd part oscillates between strict and extremely unfair, and the 3rd part is silly. But over time, the 2nd parts start to taint the other two. So I fully recommend about 82% of this game. But the other infuriating 18% make me think I should never play it.

_childDocuments_.review: A golf game for people that don't like golf games.The premise of this game is rather simple: It is a joke game that is a parody on golf games with unexpected twists.The thing is: it's not fun. The jokes are by far the biggest selling point of the game, but thing is: They just aren't that funny. One type of jokes are the puns that appear when you put the ball/hit the goal of the level. Sometimes good for a small chuckle, but most of the times on the level of 'can I haz cheesburger'/meeminess. The cheesiness is off the charts. And then I'm talking about the original ones that appear in only one or two levels, if the makers couldn't think of something, it's something like 'parfect'. Maybe it's someones cup of tea, but this level of cheesiness just isn't mine.Besides the puns, the other type of jokiness is the unexpectedness of what you're supposed to do. The archetype: You see a guy about to hit the ball, you fill the meter, release to hit and suddenly, the ball stays still but the guy ragdolls towards the flag. Again, this is sometimes good for a chuckle, but such a huge part of the jokiness of this game is build on this one premise, that it soons becomes old. Time and time again the game throws this joke at you: 'Oh you thought this would happen? Ha ha! Another thing would happen.' I'm all for unexpected humor, but here it becomes predictable that something entirely unpredictable happens. And even worse, all the jokes are repeated like 3-6 times each, so maybe it was kinda funny the first time, but the last time, it certainly isn't anymore.The worst thing is, these jokes are such a big part of the game, that each joke is dragged out just a few more times to really make you feel: 'See how funny we are. Right? Right?' Some jokes are good for a chuckle, but the rest of the game (which is 90% if I'm being generous) you're still playing some lame golf game while the game is all over your face desperately trying to be funny. And that is a lot of time that I see myself in the reflection of my screen, just sitting there, going from one lame joke to another.The game is not unlike an annoying 12 year old on your aunts birthday party where you were forced to go to who is showing you all the memes he and his friends thoroughly enjoy. Sure, one or two of these memes aren't all that bad and maybe one is rather funny, but you're still spending your saturday afternoon with an annoying 12 year old while you could be doing all these more enjoyable things, like taking a nap.I have refunded the game. I see two possible audiences for this game: people that really really love incredible and repeated cheesiness and young teenagers (the annoying 12 year olds I talked earlier about). Maybe they would like it, I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of religious missionaries always knocking on your door? Well, for $20 and about 8 hours of their time, you can fix that! Just make them play this game, and then ask them what merciful god would allow it to have been made. But actually, $20 is lowballing it - you might want to put aside a few extra grand or so for potential therapy costs, anger management courses, and a new computer monitor, not necessarily in that order. So yeah, it might be more cost-effective to just tell the missionaries to go away.Alright, now that that's out of my system, onto the actual review.First, the positive, which I can fit into a single paragraph: Some of the levels are actually pretty innovative and clever. The idea of "Golf, but it's a different game entirely" had a lot of potential, and if you're not trying to 100% the game, it might be a fun way to kill a few hours.But... if you are the type who tends to go for 100% when playing games, you will want to keep reading, that you may save yourself.The developers were very proud of the title they came up with for this game. It's in the store description, it's in the background music, it's in the lyrics of the sing-a-long level, and sometimes when you go out of bounds, you'll hear voices going "WHAAAAAT" like this game invented the word "what" because it's so random xdddzs. I actually had to turn sound effects off for one level because that voice was grating on my nerves so much.Speaking of failing levels, let's talk about that. The hit detection is awful. You'll be playing a hole with a par of the exact same number of shots it took you to clear it the first time, but you're inexplicably unable to make it in that number of shots again, often times because you'll miss the hole by half a pixel on your last shot. Oh, but the exploding barrels that usually send you right out of bounds, THOSE you can hit from two feet away! And when you fail to make the par, it doesn't say "You Failed" or "Failure" or anything like that, it just says "Fail", like a little kid who just discovered memes and watched you miss the trash can while throwing away a paper towel. I get that it's a troll game and it's meant to be annoying, but there's a limit, especially at the asking price of $20.And if the extra objective on a hole isn't a par, it's usually something that will make you wish it was. Like a monkey paw but for every finger that curls, two more sprout in its place. And don't even get me started on the damn sheep. Instead of "What the Golf?", this game should have been called "If I See That ♥♥♥♥ing Sheep One More Time...".So, yeah. It might be worth grabbing on sale for a quick laugh, but I'm very glad I didn't pay full price, because then I'd probably be even more angry.

_childDocuments_.review: My main complaint with the game is that it very often relies on "subverting your expectations" in ways that aren't really fair. Like the hole that moves the minute you hit the golf ball. There's no way for me to know it's going to move before I play so it feels a bit unfair. It's not a huge deal to have this experience once or twice in a game but it feels like half of the levels rely on this sort of gameplay. You're basically expected to just try hitting your ball/object for a bit, see what happens, and then restart the level and actually try. It gets really old really fast.A few other nit-picks: The game relies a LOT of references to other games/sports and often sacrifices fun and engaging gameplay just to make a joke. Your shot power is dependant on the distance between your mouse and the controlled object which sometimes backfires when the controlled object rotates around something besides it's center with a feedback loop that makes it nearly impossible to aim the way you want since move the mouse by a few pixels starts to swing the object widely in a different direction. It also causes problems when the object doesn't stay fixed on the screen like if the object is moving fast the view smoothing often causes you to be unable to fine tune adjust your power because the location of the object on screen is rapidly changing. The ending of the main campaign was really weird in my opinion. I'm not sure if there is a proper "story" that I am missing out on but I definitely felt like the ending was entirely random and not very fun either.

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of found it disappointing overall. To be fair, the game made golf less boring but not by much. Each level you play “golf” which either boils down to you using an unusual item as a golf ball or you playing the gimmick of a different game that’s referenced. The former gets boring after a while since the joke only really works once and the latter is just playing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ version of the game which is referenced. Speaking of references, man some of these are old and really not funny. It’s not cringy but none of the humor really landed and the maximum I got was a chuckle off of the puns at the end screen. I really thought this would be an over the top pun filled linear joke fest but it’s just a golf game with gimmicks.Each level is replayable and I do like that some levels don’t have the 100% completion requirement as just “Get it under a certain amount of strokes” but half the levels do and it’s kinda boring. The gimmicks are varied and do hold an interest for a little while but the levels just go on and on. Also, the main overarching plotline with the computer and the frog is just… never brought up or explained. Which is fine but there isn’t even a pay off for finishing the game other than completion. I thought the trophies you collected would be playable and you could unlock certain levels with them but it’s just literally completion tracking.I was super excited about this game because I thought it would be a funny game with golf as the premise. In reality, it’s just a meh golf game with writing that doesn’t land for me. Not horrible (the art style is great!) but just a game that happened. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Levels are short and give instant satisfaction upon completing them, making this game incredibly difficult to put down for too long. 3. Map creator built in along with daily achievements4. The game never dwells on one gimmick for too long, so if you do not enjoy certain maps they tend to be over before you know it. This does however have the downside that really fun gimmicks like SUPER PUTT are also short lived. However, I'd say there is a lot more good than bad and it all evens out into something positive. Cons:1. This is only really only relevant if you're looking to 100% the campaign. The game has a lot of janky mechanics which while often fun, sometimes in the extra levels, the difficulty is ramped up to a point where the cracks in the game really start to show, the horse and crab levels come to mind in particular. There are good reasons why most people do not think "Getting Over It" is a worth while game outside of torture and while I never got stuck for more than 10-20 minuets on a single level I feel I have to make a point that objectively bad movement options + difficulty only lead to frustration, not fun. 2. Many of the extra levels are simply getting par on the exact same course you've just gone through, which feels a bit like padding. Sometimes I would get the Par in my first try only to have to do the exact same thing again. This is the only part of the game where I felt it stagnated. Honestly it's a very fun game and the two cons above never fully interfered with my enjoyment of the game. The reason I have to give this a thumbs down is due to 1 set of levels in the space zone, where you're in an inverted planet that's spinning and you're trying to kick some balls into a goal. This level on purposely attempts to make the players feel physically sick with the spinning screen and judging by the coy message at the end of the third level, the developers know this. I have no other way to interpret this than as malicious intent by the developers. While I was mostly fine with it, many people suffer from motion sickness and trying to induce it on people playing your game is frankly a d*** move and a slap in the face of the people who unwittingly paid money for it.I honestly feel that this level should be taken out and the developers should apologise.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I had some fun with this game, mostly because of the subversions to typical golfing, as you may see in several of the videos and pictures surrounding this game. However, its charm fell apart when I accidentally stumbled upon the "Crown" levels. These levels, while "optional" (in the sense you don't actually need to complete them to progress through the "main" part of the adventure mode), were questionable in their ability to be fun.Now, to some extent, due to the optional-ness of the "Crown" levels, they could be seen as a challenge of sorts. The unfortunate reality is that they're either "fun and easy" or "the worst thing ever multiplied by cancer". The fun ones were like the normal holes you had to do normally, and were no big deal. The  ones were nowhere near the same idea as the fun ones. Their design had little direction, and little control, or had constricting mechanics, sometimes combined with all three and then some. If you want to make a "challenge" you don't make it a deplorable or frustrating experience on the player. Specific "Crown" levels that could be rightly called torture:"Par" levels. (Probably makes up 50% of "Crown" levels) Levels where either the object or screen move to exploit the clunky controls, resulting in either unintended and/or frustrating movement. (There is at least one of these, and that already should be grounds for capital punishment)"Fragile" levels ie: If you touch something or anything you start over; barrel or vase levels to a major extent, or "Super Putt" levels to a minor extent. (These are interesting in theory, but the controls make it abhorrable)Some other minor tidbits:Why does a resume button exist on the pause menu if clicking the background does the same thing?Why are some of the floor plans to get  a level a frustrating experience? The space section does not count, and was actually interesting in that regard.Why does the pause menu not have easy access to the options? I have to back all the way out to the main menu to even try to adjust something as simple as  Not to mention the option menu for such things isn't immediately available upon first starting the game.tldr: Game is fun at a glance, but if you want to utterly complete it, you'll hate it before it's even done.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GOLF? is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  This mobile app is a different kind of spin on the general slingshot flinging game, Angry Birds.  The slingshot mechanic is at the core of this mobile app, but instead of birds and pigs, it's loosely golf themed as you fling a ball (or club, person, clubhouse etc) towards the goal, with unusual interactions on each puzzle level with various objects like cats, cars etc.The amusement factor of the "Oh, that was unexpected" is certainly "there", but you could get that from watching someone play it on their iPhone on Youtube, so we can disregard that.  And taking that out of the equation you just have an (admittedly well polished) low poly Angry Birds ripoff.  Yes, I know it's golf themed, so how can it be an Angry Birds ripofff?  Because just like Angry Birds, 100% of the game is still putting your finger on your iPhone screen, dragging it back just enough, choosing just the right angle, and letting it go.  Angry Birds is not what I spent almost 5 figures on buying a bleeding edge gaming rig for. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The mobile app features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the mobile app (although the requirement for this to run on low end mobile phones is a factor), and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is an eye watering $20 USD (TWENTY BUCKS FOR A MOBILE APP), on app stores, it's about $7 USD. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay MORE THAN TWICE THE PRICE premium for a simple kids mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this is a mobile app, is priced to insult and gouge PC gamers, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.Just who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a Monty Python-esque absurdist comedy show about golf - that is 'What The Golf?' in a nutshell. You may start out putting a ball into a hole, but you will soon be putting the hole into the ball, a cow into a shed, a bike-rider cross country into a flag, and bombs into bowling pins. Then it gets deeply weird.What The Golf? is filled with bad puns, insane moments and complete absurdity from start to finish. The soundtrack is entirely a cappella, the graphics minimalist, and the game play is not merely off the wall, you will be putting the wall, trying to golf with a detached wall, or a house, or any object you can imagine. The game will take you through references as wide as Katamari Damashi all the way to bowling and The Olympics - frankly, there is almost no end to the inventiveness on display. This game is absolutely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).What the golf is a mix between a golf game and a sandbox physics game, with a lot of variation between levels: the objectives and objects used for the “club” and for the “ball” are frequently not what you’re expecting. The game has a lot of short levels divided into chapters in the main game but also several different modes/content that you also have to complete.The graphics are very simple and low budget, but the level and randomness and creativity present in the levels ends up making up for it. Despite the poor graphics, the physics engine seems solid, with objects behaving more or less in a realistic way.Completing the levels is rather simple most of the time but the goal of the game is more about being surprised and having a laugh than really completing it. From all the levels and their two different extra challenges, I only found one to be hard to complete in the sports level pack, as it requires dexterity and good timing and is very easy to fail shooting in the right direction in the required time window.It also has a local multiplayer mode where two player compete against on another that is even more fun than playing alone, but has less variety when it comes to levels available.   63 Achievements. Around 15 hours, with a little help or the more obscure achievements. This time needs to be spread around 18 days for you to complete 18 daily challenges. Easy, all the main levels are easy to complete.  Easy, but there is a harder level that will require some practice and several tries, unlike the rest of the game. Some of the hidden achievements will require a guide too. What the golf is a goofy golf/physics game that is fun to play in small doses and will often surprise you with its randomness and creativity. The levels vary a lot and are very different from each other, even more so in the extra level packs.b]Join and follow my group  for more suggestions and reviews of enjoyable indie games to get all the achievements.[/b]

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and clever casual game that features several laugh out loud moments as you start a challenge for the first time and only by trying it discover what it's all about.  For example, you may have a man with a golf club standing over a ball, and when you draw your mouse back, a power arrow appears behind them to indicate how hard you will swing.  But when you let go of the left mouse button, it might be the ball, the club, the man, or even the power arrow that goes flying (or tumbling) down the course.  Or it might be a couch, an office chair on wheels, a house... it's unpredictable and hilarious and a lot of fun.  The challenges are easy enough to be casual, but sometimes you may have to retry them quite a few times until you're successful, so there's enough of an occasional challenge to keep things interesting.Fun references to Nintendo properties abound, from the Wii Golf-inspired soundtrack to obvious nods to Mario and Donkey Kong in some of the early challenges.  To keep things fresh, there are daily challenges that are every bit as silly and fun as the "campaign" mode.All in all this one gets a solid thumbs up.  It's even stream-worthy because it's almost as much fun to watch as to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Yup, it's crazy but it's really fun! Very very few levels depend on pure luck and you can manage everything even if you are TIger Woods!The music is awesome and many levels have different types well suited to the levels.It's really tough to speak highly of this game without spoiling some of the awesome ideas that the devs implemented in this game (and barely linked it to golf). It's really crazy but they managed to add a lot and it shows they really had a lot of imagination and didn't limit themselves when making this game!I highly recommend this game to anyone with a few minutes every day (but you can also sink many hours in a row). _childDocuments_.review: What the golf is a welcome satire that has an very rich pool of references to pull from. The levels are fun, and while some are tad repetitive, they find ways to change the mold almost every time. The only knock I have against the game is that playing with a controller is actually a disadvantage on timed levels. Playing with a touch screen or M&K can get through most of the timed levels easily meanwhile a controller will struggle immensely if not outright be impossible do to the slower "draw" time per shot that is used so controller players have more control over how hard they shoot (This was my experience on the steam deck at least). Aside from that though, the game was a very fun experience and would recommend it highly to anyone that isn't expecting a PGA tour clone.As far as what to expect on the levels, the most simple answer is that you will be surprised almost every time. If something was decently popular in the last ten years, there is probably a reference to it in here, and the game play itself is easy to understand, aside from a few levels where the puzzle itself is to figure out how to score.Calling the levels puzzles is probably the most accurate description. Sometimes its a race, a puzzle, sometimes just a normal golf hole, etc. Saying too much beyond gets into spoiler territory, its worth experiencing for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GOLF? Is such a cute indie game from Triband, and is spun as, "The golf game for people who hate golf." It lives up to that title in the most unique way. You play as various objects in short levels, putting yourself to the goal, each level having a unique spin on the oft generic formula of golfing, whether it is sneaking through a box past beacons of light a-la Metal Gear Solid, or launching yourself via toaster to a goalpost. The achievements of this game can be quite aggravating to achieve, especially the Thanksgiving achievement, which can only be accomplished on or near the date in question. Overall this game is a great romp and a fun one to dust off every now and again.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What if golf but [blank] was the question, and these people went all AdLib on it. There's some classic golf gameplay, spliced in with lots of interesting weird ideas (also the greatest popular game references). I pretty much fully finished everything without rushing in 6 hours-ish, as the game has additional "adventures" when you finish the main story. There's even some hidden lore in there believe it or not.Apparently there's some trouble with 100%ing the game but if that's not a problem for you and all the things above sound good, I'd strongly recommend getting it.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Collection of physics based minigames. Stretches the definition of "golf" to unrecognizability (in a good way). The joy of the game comes from seeing what kind of crazy new thing is going to happen in the next level - you truly never know what you'll get. Minigames run the gamut from jokes/puns to a few genuine challenges that take many attempts to get right. There are stretches of easy minigames that blend together and can become tedious (though few are completely trivial). Difficulty curve is fairly flat and resets on each world, so even late-game you won't be challenged (but arguably challenge isn't really the point of the game). The definition of a "casual" (in a good way) game. A relaxing experience that asks very little from the player and will feed you a constant stream of surprise and delight.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you're overwhelmed and are in need of some silliness to get you through. Always new variations of old jokes, always new gameplay getting added. It's great. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: - Cute and cartoonish graphics abound. I like how the 2D and 3D portions of the game feel distinct but still cohesive throughout- The music is pretty catchy too. Nothing that'll get stuck in your head for a long time, but it's still pretty good- There's sort of a story there about beating evil computers for some reason. I don't really remember because it had nothing to do with the golfing- And that's probably okay. I don't think like my enjoyment of of a parody golf game was deeply impacted by the lack of a rich narrative- It's a fun, goofy, casual game- It's putatively golf in that the goal of every level involves moving an object to a specific location, but it's a fairly loose interpretation of golf- Each level has 3 variants that typically feature increasing difficulty surrounding a central mechanic or theme. These increases in difficulty may involve things like adding additional obstacles or a par restriction- I don't know if I can think of a reason to replay any levels after completing them. I don't plan on revisiting the game until the Thanksgiving achievement is unlockable again. Sure there's daily levels and stuff, but there's not much point in playing them until it's possible to 100% the game again- This title definitely fulfilled my desire to play a completely unserious casual game. No stakes, only "golf"- Ran very well on the Steam Deck; no issues whatsoever- . Don't expect anything deeper than a silly, casual time. It's a high-quality silly, casual game, though, so it's pretty easy to recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the game's lighthearted graphics, it is much deeper than it appears.The game begins with a simple question: "What is golf?" What follows is a profound adventure through many of life's most complex and pressing issues. From gun violence to the housing market, and even virtual reality, "What The Golf?" has something to teach us about every one of life's experiences.You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll develop complex feelings on one of literature's most common themes "Horse vs. Sheep."I originally waited to get it on sale, but after playing through only the main campaign (and there is so much more content beyond that), I can confidently say it's worth every penny at full price. Go on, buy the game and discover for yourself what a complex and enlightening game golf can truly be.

_childDocuments_.review: WTG (What the Golf) is a great indie game. It doesn't reinvent the wheel but it just throws a lot of cool little ideas at you without much downtime. Its fun and provides a play experience that is relatively rare. If you personally aren't a big fan of golf games this should still be entertaining. It feels more like a WarioWare style mini game bundle rather then a golf game.The game offers a single player campaign that I beat 100 % within about 7 to 8 hours. There are also some extra game modes which I decided not to get into for now as well as community levels. Overall this game is absolutely worth it for its price tag. The game isn't overly hard but if you go for 100 % it can throw some nasty levels at you from time to time. It can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. It can get repetitive, especially if you are going for 100 % but if you do everything at your own pace or come back to it from time to time it should still be a really great experience.One last thing I wanted to note is that my kid loved watching me play the game and try out some of the easier levels. Its a pretty family friendly game in that aspect.Overall What the golf exceeded by expectations and I highly recommend it to almost anyone to buy it even at its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game vaguely reminded me of taking care of someone’s pet cat. It’s cute and clever in some little ways, but it’s often more irritating than you'd expect. Put simply, What The Golf was much more enjoyable when I was b-lining to new stages and basically treating the game as a one-button WarioWare affair. Expecting precise gameplay from the player during the optional tasks doesn't work so well within a funny physics comedy context.The game’s humor is far more energetic than it is competent. Think around the same level as a “hip” diner that uses manufactured dad puns for all their menu’s items’ names. To that end, bootlegging a recognizable game mechanic and writing 'tactless reference' across the screen upon completing the level might be the most video-gamey way to repeat a punchline. (Although in fairness, many of the “inspired” gameplay twists are executed very smoothly.)I think the all-caps implied exclamation of the game’s awkward title nicely summarizes its predictable personality and frantic attempts to get your attention back with a weird new mechanic. Even though nearly all the novelty of wacky golf wears off shortly after the fantastic introduction finishes, What The Golf spits out such a volume of moderately interesting bits that it’s easy to get lost in all the putting. Not a personal favorite, but I’m always eager to jump on the “golf sux” bandwagon.

_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games that are constantly trying to reinvent themselves and only just barely find any sort of connecting formula, you'll probably love this. It's ostensibly about getting a "golf ball" to a "hole", but even the structure of that sentence is up for grabs. Some of the levels are terribly frustrating, some are incredibly fun but only last seconds... It's an absolute grab bag. But the fun is less in the specific challenges and more in the experience of bouncing around all the different ways it can be creative. If you like being surprised, you'll probably love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Very silly game, good for all ages. Though many of the references will work better on older millennials, I could see a young kid being way in to the goofy and novel gags which this game has in spades. It is quite easy to blaze through the levels in a couple of hours, with a few more tacked on if you want to take on the optional harder challenges. Some of these are quite frustrating in their difficulty though, so completionists might find the game to wear out its welcome. However, it is worth playing through everything at least once to see all the creative ways the team has subverted the idea of "golf." It kind of reminds me of a WariorWare game actually, with a very short completion time on each game and a goofy, anarchic sense of humor to compliment each vignette. Lots of puns too, if thats your kind of thing. 7/10: once you've played it there isn't much reason to ever go back, but the creativity on display here is hard to be mad at.
