_childDocuments_.review: While it looks like a very meme-y game (and on some level it definitely is), this game is beyond amazing. Most games have at least some core identity, but What the Golf? manages to cycle through new ideas over and over so quickly, it's almost disorienting. Highly recommended, especially if you're into fun physics, silly humor, acapella soundtracks and everything that isn't golf. Not recommended if you want to play golf.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really smooth game - a highly interactive hub world and a seriously large amount of inventive content with a small palette. I really enjoyed it and completed the main story to 100% over two sessions, totalling just under 6hrs.There are many extensions to the main campaign that I am sure I will enjoy (there seems to be a smaller, second world to explore!)I must admit I was getting a bit burnt out on the 100% completion grind - every level is effectively 3 levels with some permutation - but if I spaced it out I think I would have enjoyed it more. That's just a testament to how addictive the gameplay is!9/10 for me when considering this was a small team's passion project.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I almost wouldn't even consider What The Golf? to be a golf game, because it manages to play with and stretch the limits of the simple stroke and power bar mechanics as far they can possibly be taken unlike anything I've seen. It's also both a celebration of and love letter to all different kinds of games, as it's numerous level and mechanic designs draw direct inspiration from so many others.On top of all that, this game absolutely oozes with charm in nearly every aspect from the music/sound design, to the level design, art, and of course, puns! What this game masters, though, is the art of expectation subversion. Many, many times over the rug was pulled out from under me in the most clever and laughable ways, and I audibly cackled every time.Just breezing through the levels, the difficulty is more on the casual side. If you are going for 100%, some of the levels get ridiculously frustrating, mainly any involving ragdoll physics combined with par time or par shots. But the more aggravating ones are far and few between.9/10  I'm begging you, PLEASE play through all the bonus adventure levels!

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A silly and funny physics game of "golf".This is really the kind of game that is better experienced without knowing as little of it as possible, but the best description I can give about the game is that it's a game of golf where you're rarely just trying to hit a ball into a small hole, as the object you're hitting (or the goal you're aiming for) are different on each level, along with whatever else is happening in each level as well.The game obviously has a lot of focus on the use of physics: balls will roll, but a person will wobble on the ground, a chair with wheels will slide along the ground, etc. Hitting something will also cause an impact that affect the trajectory of the object you're hitting and/or cause the object you've hit to move, fall over, etc.But the game's chair relies on how silly it is. It never takes itself seriously and it's constantly doing something new, very often catching the player unprepared for what happens next, and it's just a really funny experience all around. And while it's not a specially long game, it still has quite a bit of content with 2 challenges for each level besides the "base" level itself (and challenges can be quite different from what the level is), in addition to extra campaigns, multiplayer, daily challenges and a level editor (though the level editor is currently on early access).I had a blast with the game for the most part, with the exception of a few challenges that were pretty frustrating to complete, but hardly anything that turned me off from the game.Easy recommendation, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun little time waster if you are looking for something fast and casual. It got a few laughs out of me and some of the mechanics were pretty creative and were entertaining to toy around with.It did feel at times that some of the levels got a bit repetitive, where it felt like they existed purely to pad playtime. It was fine since it is hard to expect consistent quality throughout games like these, but I wish developers would stray away from the ideology that you NEED to have a long game in order for the customer to warrant the purchase. I would rather have 5 hours of great gameplay than 5 hours of great gameplay AND 5 hours of filler (not to say that this game didn't have 5 hours of filler because it doesn't, just an example.) Still, the ideas and mechanics it presented made for a few relaxing evenings of fun, so I would give the game big ups for that overall.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I love how this game is golf... but not really golf. Hahaha...if that makes sense? If you're a lover of indie/variety games, this game has the most random rounds that bring nostalgia. You have the main storyline and you have plenty more to do if you're a completionist. They seem to have added many other courses too, so I guess the $20 may be well worth it. I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of games like Donut County and Untitled Goose Game. It's just pure humor and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining for the first couple of hours but it gets boring pretty quickly. Most of the levels are mid, but some of them are outright unfun to play and feel as if they were never playtested. The music gets tiring pretty quickly too, with some tracks that are as annoying as the levels themselves. Overall would not recommend outside of a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf? cares very little about rules of golf and is lot wackier game because of that. You better expect the unexpected as there's no way to know for sure what happens after the first strike. Rules are bent so far that sometimes what you're playing is not really golf.Luckily rules are easy to figure out. Just expect to fail hilariously at first.I won't spoil what kind of things to expect as it's fun to get surprised. Levels are short, getting back to where you failed doesn't take too long. Hardest levels might require quite many retries, but game is fun enough that you still want to try just one more time. I have managed to finish the "story" of the game, so most likely you can too. 100% completion needs bit more effort I suppose.On top of everything else, expansions are free. No need to think if season pass is worth it. It's so fun to play despite of some of the frustrating parts (bowling especially). Give this game a chance and try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice game.It has the right balance of fun and frustrating. I lost track of time several times, like I thought I played for about 20 minutes when it was actually 2 hours. The parodies of other games are extremely funny and you'll find extremely low amounts of cringe - which is always good. I laughed audibly several times.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf is a super fun game with lots and lots of references and super funny jokes. I really love the fact that there's a multiplayer option with multiple maps, characters and many levels. I also like how it has so many different features and how each side campaign is built on a different feature, yet contains elements of the different ones as well. This game plays super well and runs smoothly. It also has super unpredictable jokes and gameplay mechanics that will for sure make you laugh. However, I dislike how the game sometimes updates spontaneously and may remove really weird stuff about certain levels. For example, a level where pots were brown changed to white or sometimes speed changes as well. These are very minor changes and rarely affect your experience. That is my only complaint. In summary, I highly recommend this game on Steam due to its easy controls and smooth gameplay, as well as its hilarious and unexpected jokes and refences.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cute physics game that resembles what you might get if you fused Warioware with mini golf. The developers have consistently supported the game with new content and events. I tried to 100% it but found a handful of challenges too frustrating, but going through casually and completing each hole once will give you plenty to do with lots of varied game play.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically pleasing to the eye and soul. I would laugh randomly (and sometimes loudly) at this game, the joy was immeasurable. Very satisfying game play, and a world of fun. Would definitely recommend if you're a fan of a little puzzling and some comedy. Not to mention the soundtrack is *chef's kiss* (in my humble opinion).
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: In my years of playing video games I have found that comedy games give off a fun first impression, but soon after I find myself getting bored with them, especially if they are single player. However, What the Golf is not only funny, but creative in almost every level. The levels aren't very long so it makes you want to beat just one more to see what weird stuff they do in the next one. I will say the final boss is very lack luster and a little disappointing for me compared to the wild originality of all the levels that came before it. I can easily recommend this game when it goes on sale. Give it a shot, or maybe a stroke.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly impressive how a golf game can be anything but golf.That's what made the game the so enjoyable to me, knowing each level was going to try and throw me off made a fun game of if i can guess the the gimmick.There are loads of level to begin with in the base game as well as little secrets to find and explore, the game loves to reference other things In the form of levels, surroundings or the little phrases you get upon completing a level.If you've beaten the base game maybe to 100% completion there are other games modes and little adventures that can keep you entertained for a little longer.The only complaint is the achievement for playing for 10+ hours now, I have played for this long now and still haven't gotten the achievement. However I do plan on playing a little bit longer thanks to the daily challenges so this problem might fix itself.Thought this might be worth mentioning anyway.If you do end up buying the game, enjoy, its definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a weird game. If you're expecting an experience that is in any way related to golf, you are barking up the wrong tree. It started good, but quickly grew tedious and annoying. By the end, you're relying more on luck than skill. There's an old saying i'll paraphrase; Games are fun when you're wasting your time, not when your time is being wasted. This game starts at one end of this spectrum and almost reaches the other by the time you complete the main campaign. Make of that what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: When I started up What the golf I had no idea what to expect and a few hours after starting that feeling stayed. What the Golf is an absolute gold mine of clever fun, inventive levels and genuine humor. This deceivingly simple golf game had me absolutely hooked on every new area and each new mechanic. From putting around a makeshift Mario level to catapulting your ball across space, What the Golf offers a variety of absurd challenges moment after moment. If you want to play a golf game this may not be the one. if you  just want to have fun then definitely give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really nice and relaxing game with lots of creative and funny levels. The developers also updated the game regularly adding lots of new maps. All in all, the game is worth your time and your money.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It would feel wrong to give a negative review to a game with this much loving effort put into it, but just know that this praise is qualified.I didn't like the inconsistent physics, wonky controls and the immovable camera which combined to give many of the challenges a frustrating and unfulfilling feeling.With that out of the way, the game design is great, constantly introducing new concepts and fleshing them out enough, while not having them overstay their welcome. The humor is hit and miss for me, but i appreciate that they don't linger on a joke for too long. The fast pace in both the game and humor gives it an addicting feel, and despite my frustrations, I did want to see what came next, and I didn't have to wait long to  see that.I 100% the campaign in ~6 hours, and while I had fun, I'm not itching to hop back in. A fun distraction that is worth experiencing at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the most creative and lovely games that I've ever played. The simple graphics are very cute and fit the game very good and the music is funny as hell, with those people singing the name of the game :DThe stages are always doable, well some of them are quite challenging, some even had my hands break sweat, but they are never unfair in any way.WHAT THE GOLF? is the kind of game which let's you feel how much fun the developers had in the making.10/10: Get this game ASAP!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Usually i'm not one to give a review 'cause of laziness, but this game was too much of a fun wild ride to pass up not leaving a good-ass review! To anyone out there looking for a wacky 9-10 hours of fun, and possibly more with the side stuff, and the custom maker that's coming soon. Then this is the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Makes fun, viarity of the levels insane, super many references which concepts are implemented. E.g. Superhot, Portal, Mario, Flappy Bird and many more. 3 Campaignes, daily challenges and Level replayability. _childDocuments_.review: 🟊☆☆ - In the end credits there's text that reads, "Different team members worked on different parts" -- I wouldn't condemn the game for this, it just makes it incredibly uneven. The first two levels had me grinning from ear to ear, but the middle game is kind of broken. There are levels that are the definition of casual fun and amusement, and there are levels that are agonizingly stilted.Fortunately, the levels are structured like this:  -- The Fun are the only ones required, so you can reach the end without much grinding your teeth.But the challenges range from naturally expected to, "ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!" So I gave up on getting 100% almost immediately: I have to worry about my blood pressure. And the real shame of that is that I'm never going to see a lot of the "weird" parts. There's a lot of puzzles that are just straight up luck because of the physics engine. All of these could be fixed by adding just one or two strokes to the par. For the hundredth time, None the less, I had a lot of fun. I think if you can grab this one on sale, it would be a lot of fun for the first time player. It's the kind of game where you'll hand the controller to a friend who "Doesn't play games" just to see their reactions. But, you'll want to take the controller away after the first few levels.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun time, especially when taking turns with a friend. The gameplay is always changing. The game is a little short, though. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with a warning. What the Golf is funny, has nice physics, and has several gaming references that will hit home for a lot of people. Yet the game is quite empty. The vast majority of What the Golf is using the simple vector and power mechanic to get one object to reach another, filled with a plethora of puns and wacky situations in between. Each level has three versions of varying challenge, but I felt challenged only once briefly throughout the game. There are a few exceptions that were refreshing to see outside of this mechanic such as first person shooting, and odes to angry birds, flappy bird, mario, superhot, portal, and the like, but not enough to make it feel varied often.That being said, if you are in this for the jokes/parodies I would say go for it on sale. Otherwise you might be disappointed. For a better game with one golf mechanic try Golf Story. For a better mini or microgame collection try WarioWare.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a funny indie game I happened to see on Youtube one day and I'm so glad I did because it is a treat! WTG will make you question what golf truly is as you go from simply playing golf to playing many different genres of games in a golf setting.The complete charm of this game is the randomness of it and how when you really think about it, everything is golf. The first few levels will have you simply hitting the ball to the flag. Then it will be hitting a person into a flag, or a house, or a turtle. Next thing you'll be playing golf as a platformer, or a race, or even an FPS (no, I'm not joking). The sheer amount of different ways the creators made for you to play is phenomenal and hilarious at the same time.The main story mode will have you exploring a facility where then are different "zones" and levels for you to play. Each level has 3 sets of challenges for you to complete in order to 100% it. The first one will be a simple, "get to the flag" challenge. The second one usually consists of "get to the flag with X amount of strokes" or a time limit. The third challenge tends to be a weird zany one. This game has the Super Meat Boy feel in which some of these challenges are hard and infuriating, but hey aren't too bad to the point to where you want to give up. I finished the game with 98% as there were only two challenges I couldn't finish, which is pretty impressive for me. On top of that, the creators have 2 more campaigns, and you can even make your own levels to play and share with others. You can even go to the workshop to see what other's have created and try out their levels. I could say my gripes are that some of the levels are super infuriatingly tough, but it's only for if you want to go for the 100% run. I never found too many of the levels to be crazy. There is a hint of RNG since the game is physics based, but that's also what makes it funny too. Just know if you're going for a 100% run, there's gonna be pain...Final verdict? Check this game out if you want a silly golf game to play. I think the creators did a fantastic job of exploring every possible avenue they could with golf and there are so many gaming easter eggs and call outs that will make you smile. I think one of the ending computer terminals said it best, "Maybe life is golf..." Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Claimed to be made by people who know nothing about golf.FALSE.The devs CLEARLY know EVERYTHING about golf. This is just a tribute.Every level brings something new to the table, quickly replaced by something else on the table, quickly replaced by something else on the table, quickly replaced by... the table. Wait, now it's a car - nope, it's a rocket now.In all honestly, every bit of this is an absolute delight. You can already tell that it leans hard into absurdist territory. If that tickles your fancy in any way, it's definitely a must-play. 100%-ing the campaign will take about 6 hrs, but there is plenty of side content that is just as engaging - and that's not even including workshop content or future updates the devs have planned.So the next time you golf a horse, just remember the most important rule in golf:WHAT?

_childDocuments_.review: This is the gaming equivalent of   recommended for people who play enough video games to appreciate the references. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely hilarious series of golf-themed minigames. _childDocuments_.review: Do you consider yourself a connoisseur of the activity commonly referred to as golf?Me neither.Which is why I would highly recommend this game. Triband asked themselves how they could make golf enjoyable and decided that the best course of action would be to craft a 5-hour game (with 5 hours of free bonus content at the time of this review) where they turn the very notion of golf on its head.The only downside to the game is the somewhat shoddy physics making certain challenges a pain, but it works fine most of the time.Great fun, and definitely worth the price. _childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT? This is not golf! This is better. This is fun. This is funny!This is a golf game where you are not actually playing any golf. Not really. Instead you are playing a parody of golf in the style of everything not golf. The creativity in this is insane and it never gets boring. This is actually a game where I will likely go back and spend time to achieve the "best" "scores" on each "course", as the variations are as creative as the courses themselves.The final boss (yes, really) is as much a parody of video game tropes as the rest of the game and it's absolutely delightful. Highly, highly recommended for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: What the golf is actually a great representation of life. _childDocuments_.review: This review has been completely changed from my old, sucky, and unhelpful review.You start with the Main Campaign, which starts off relatively simple. You read the Golf Notes, you destroy the computers, you play the levels... but then things start to change.In 03 (I think), a wreckage blocks everything off. The Golf Notes are more cryptic. You eventually get to 01. And you beat it. And then...Meat juice stuff everywhere. You finally get to the hole. And you beat the Frog King.You did it! You beat the game... right?Let's start with Sporty Sports. The only other campaign with Crown Levels so far.It's really fun, but can get tough. Especially the rhythm ones.Then there's It's Snowtime.A nice fun snowy one, with a story of two Turtles trying to get pizza. And you deliver the slices.Lastly, so far is A Hole New World.It has holes, and a Final Boss. Not as crazy as the Frog King though.And then Party Mode, for 2 Players.It hasn't been updated with new levels (yet), but is still fun.This mode was first introduced on Nintendo Switch.Ok, after Campaigns is Challenge Me, and Daily Challenge.Challenge Me is always the same I think... Daily Challenge is where the fun is.You have to try to beat the given levels in as few shots as possible to get in first place.Now, that's practically it for this game on every other platform for now... Except Steam.Because it's Early Access, it's a Steam Exclusive for now. In this mode, you can create your own levels! This hasn't been updated in a while as well, but it's still fun.In earlier versions, you could glitch out the camera as well, and have really odd ball placements. But that's patched now sadly. I have a few levels that feature these glitches, like A Topdown Experience.There's also a demo, so you can see what the game will be like. You get to play through the first chapter of the Main Campaign, and create levels too! The only thing is you can't save them.That concludes my review of WHAT THE GOLF. You can decide whether to get it or not now.And for people who already have the game, keep not golfing!And to the devs, thank for making this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I don't think it is worth the cost. It is very fun, though I would recommend to get it only if it were on sale. The game feels repetitive in some points, and a couple of the challenges (specifically the par-ones) can be incredibly frustrating. Overall though, the game is creative, fun, and leaves you wanting more. The developers really made a fun golf game for people who hate golf, and I hope to see more in this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Cheery and cheesy, it's a refreshing take on a few classic game mechanics used throughout. Some levels are deceptively difficult where others are fairly easy. It's a mixed bag of mini-games wrapped around a loose concept of golf with extra silliness sprinkled on top. If you're looking for a game to not take too seriously and practice your quick-click mouse skills, this might just be the game to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What The Golf is a perfect game to play while having a podcast in the background and relaxing.  Each new section of the map adds a unique mechanic that doesn't wear itself out; platforming, first-person shooting, SUPERHOT timestop, etc. Each level includes 3 objectives, the first is always simply getting the ball (or other random object) to hit the flag pole, the second is usually a par challenge where you complete the level within a certain number of hits, but there are sometimes different challenges instead of par, and the third challenge is something so random and vastly different than the other two that it always keeps you guessing. What the Golf has a wonderful sense of humor and plenty of things to do. My only criticism is that it can sometimes get a little tiring after long play sessions, but that just means this game is best enjoyed in bite-sizes. A delightfully silly and relaxing golf game, and my favourite golf video game ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is the work of the GODS!! It's a great game and leaves you wondering whats coming in the next level! _childDocuments_.review: On May 29, 2017, Tiger Woods was arrested near his Jupiter Island, Florida, home by the Jupiter Police Department at about 3:00 am. EDT for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. He was asleep in his car, which was stationary in a traffic lane with its engine running. He later stated that he had taken prescription drugs and did not realize how they might interact together. On July 3, 2017, Woods tweeted that he had completed an out-of-state intensive program to tackle an unspecified issue. At his August 9, 2017 arraignment, Woods had his attorney Douglas Duncan submit a not guilty plea for him and agreed to take part in a first-time DUI offender program and attend another arraignment on October 25.

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf? is like a golf version of Warioware. It's just a ton of mini games all with different spins on them. _childDocuments_.review: I'm only 1/2 way through the main campaign, and I've had only the briefest of looks at the other content. 'Other content' here includes daily challenge/leaderboard, party mode (local 2 player vs mode), extra campaigns, editor, and workshop/community levels so far. This is still a very easy recommended, though. It's just dripping with style, great sound track (in the Katamari style) inventiveness, surprises, nods to other genres/games, humour and most of all, Some of the (optional) 'extra' stages have, most definitely, driven me to shouting out loud (words that would definitely be censored here) in sheer frustration. But for some reason I'm determined to 100% this one. And after a dozen goes on even the 'stupidest' levels, they gradually become not only possible but actually pretty straightforward. It's quite rewarding when you finally complete a level which seemed impossible (or at least not worth the effort) at the start. And actually, as the levels are mostly quite short (so far) this really doesn't take long. It just seems like it sometimes.It also seems to be a very 'active' game, with new content appearing from time to time and community support.So it's definitely recommended to people who like games which don't take themselves too seriously, and yet still offer decent gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review:
The golf game for people who hate golf!

A silly physics-based golf parody where every golf course is a new surprising type of golf, some brilliant or hilarious, others so absurd they will make you go: WHAT THE GOLF?

Golf a house, a horse or car!

Features:
- More surprising new golf mechanics than you can imagine
- Epic golf boss fights
- Made by people who know nothing about golf
- First (and hopefully the last) game that let you golf a horse
- Will NOT make you a better golf player
- Surprises!

name: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos
detailed_description: A dark evil stirs beneath the once peaceful land of Tasos… Deep within the four Great Dungeons, the ancient seals that hold the Titans at bay are gravely weakened and their minions have unleashed terror upon the world. The Goddesses who forged the seals long ago have made a desperate plea for a band of heroes to come forth and save the people from a terrible fate… You are one of the heroes tasked with saving the realm of Tasos from the terrifying Titans. Whether you choose to take on your mission solo, or with up to three friends is your decision to make. Do you have what it takes to save Tasos? Key Features 4-Play Rogue-lite Adventure: Play solo or in co-op with up to 4 players to take down the Titans! Remember that death is not the end; rise again, upgrade your hero and venture out once more, stronger than before! Tackle Procedural Dungeons: With its procedural engine, no two runs are the same! Each room has hand designed layouts, traps, puzzles and enemies all with randomised configurations, making every run feel fresh and different. Classic Weapons: Rogue Heroes features classic top-down swordplay with a large range of tools, spells, and weapons to use as you explore Tasos and tackle the Great Dungeons. Locate classic weapons like a Bow, Boomerang and Grappling Hook to use at your disposal. Rebuild your Town for Upgrades: Spend your hard-earned loot on new buildings for your village of Intori. From Weapons Smiths to fisheries, each can add new ways of adding to your abilities and arm you with the tools to return to the fight. Multiple Classes: Each with their own unique abilities, find which character suits your style of play and take back Tasos!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Fun little ZoL-esque game with a large world, class system and coop mode! Nice change of pace with more casual gameplay, but difficult enough to be a challenge to where you can't just go in guns blazing.Cons:Some of the attack skills like bullet deflection or just the shield are kinda janky with the enemy shot going through your attack at times even if you time it right. Also there is no way to remap the controls on a controller from what I could tell. Adding on to that, there have been times where my friend or I have tried to remap the buttons and immediately get kicked out of our session.Overall 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: TONS of glitches. Just had to save and quit because we were stuck.The biggest issue is in multiplayer, the other player cannot interact with objects sometimes. Like, he can't cut grass, pick up stones, cut a path, etc. But it also doesn't allow him to go through when I cut through. So I have to pull him through to the next area in order to move on. What happened was he got blocked and I was trying to get to the next area and died. We were in the deep swamp, so he couldn't go back, but he couldn't kill the flowers to move forward. Other smaller glitches: His can has an almost indefinite amount of water, mine has to be refilled after 4 plants. After respawning, his screen showed night and mine showed day. In a dungeon, I walked close to an alter and the dialog popped up on his screen and he wasn't able to do anything until we died because the dialog wouldn't go away. When you swing your sword, things across the screen explode. Enemies/animations not showing up well on other screen (partially covered in main issue above).I seriously hope they fix this, it would be an awesome game but it has some work to do... I understand it's an Indy game but I just assumed it would be a little smoother, given the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is hands down one of the best Co-op roguelites I have ever played. It takes dungeon crawling, Zelda-like gameplay and mixes it with modern roguelite elements like an amazing progression system and awesome combat.And so how the game works is that you create your save, pick your class, and then go into dungeons. There is a story that kind of brings you to the first dungeon and explains the game and from there you go through these elaborate dungeons to try to get to the end, and gain a ton of gems for out of game progression.And the dungeons are easily one of the best parts about this game. Each room can be filled with enemies that pose serious threats. And the combat in this game is really great. It feels super smooth and responsive which is what you want. Sometimes you will accidentally touch an enemy which can hurt you but the better you get the less you tend to do that.There are items you can find in the game like bows, magic wands, grappling hooks, and more. Some of them use your mana and some use their own separate ammo like the bow and arrows. On top of that each dungeon is filled with traps like pressure plates that trigger arrow traps, or bombs falling from the sky, and sometimes good things like giving you a ton of other gems.There are also a ton of secrets you can find and one thing this game does that is really cool is that every room in the dungeon can be cleared. And that's mainly just means like killing all the enemies and discovering any secrets. So you might have to light all the torches in a room which will spawn a chest or press on certain pressure plates in a room.When you’ve cleared a room it changes color on the map and you get a notification which turns every room into an entire objective as you want to make sure you get all the awesome loot and find all the hidden secrets instead of just running as fast as you can from room to room.And like I said earlier the dungeon crawling in the game is so fun especially if you are playing co-op. And all of my experience with the game so far has been with me and one other friend online and local. The dungeons appear like they can be completed perfectly fine solo but they are also designed in a way that subtly promote cooperation between all the players.And if one of you dies you drop your skull and if your friend brings it carefully to a sacrificial altar you can get revived. But that is way easier said than done.Overall the game is very challenging. I have played for several hours and I am not even going to lie, we haven’t even scratched the surface of everything the game has which is a good thing. I can tell there is so much this game has to offer and you could play this game for hundreds of hours. And the main reason why is the progression.The progression in this game is fantastic. So all throughout the dungeons you are collecting tons of gems. And these gems are the main currency for all the out of game progression. So you keep respawning in this little town and you can actually build up the town with your gems. So you create a nurse building to gain health upgrades, a blacksmith to get damage upgrades, a gym to increase stamina, a clothing store thing to unlock new classes you find cloth for, and a ton more buildings. And there is so many things you can focus on progression. There are like 10 different buildings all with several simple but deep perk trees that you can subtly improve your character with. There are also several buildings that are really unique like a fishing dock or a place to brew potions, or a farm to grow crops. The progression system is baked into a simplistic town management idea which makes the progression feel natural and grounded in the world instead of random characters giving you random upgrades like in other roguelites. So overall I don’t have a ton to say about the game mainly because I am still exploring it as we speak. It is so awesome because you can play the co-op local multiplayer or online even with Steam remote play if you have a good enough internet connection. So the fact that I now have a roguelite game I can just pop on when friends come over where we all have our own progression yet we are all on a team makes me so happy. And I touched on it a tiny bit but the way the game handles progression with multiple players is great. So when anyone finds gems in the dungeon everyone gets the same amount for the most part but how you spend your gems is however you want. So my friend could use his versions of the gems he got to upgrade his damage a ton and go to a thief class to do a ton of damage while I could go a mage class and focus on upgrading my magic and getting wands and stuff.And I have to say this is one of the best local multiplayer roguelites I think I have ever played and I am so happy to continue playing it constantly. So I would highly recommend this game if you have some people to play with whether online, local co-op, or steam share, but also I do think this game can be enjoyed a ton as a solo experience. You might be at a slight disadvantage but I think its still doable and enjoyable.And if you love Roguelites as much as me then  for more reviews and videos about them :)

_childDocuments_.review: At best its a fun little game, but it has too many problems for me to recommend.If all you want is a mindless little hack and slash to play with friends then go for it, maybe wait for it to be a little cheaper but keep in mind the following.Classes are pointless, they work mostly the same as each other with a few buffs and debuffs, the specials all work similarly and fill the same roll with only slight mechanical differences.Playing anything other than melee is going to have you underpowered. I played a mage, and maxed everything out i could and had low defense. Because i had to depend on mp, my resources were limited and my damage output was barely a fraction of my melee co-op partner. Playing anything other than melee also means that you are going to have to swap to your main tool and that brings me to the next major point.Inventory management sucks. it starts off okay, but soon your toolbar is so bloated cycling to anything, especially in the heat of combat takes forever. You can pause, navigate to the equip window, select the item, unpause. and honestly that's fine in single player but ruins the flow in multiplayer and can get annoying for who you are playing with as they cant even access there own pause menu while you are in yours. There is a quickwheel but.. is only for emotes, not that it works consistantly in the first place. So soon your inventory will be full of things like a seed bag, and a watering can that are only used in the farming part of the game that honestly can be entirely ignored more so in multiplayer, it feels really tacked on. Exploring feels kinda pointless, as while i have found a few neat things for the most part i seem to end up in dead ends and have no reward. There are power spheres to collect but they nothing/so little as to not be worth it. Several times my progress has been hindered by bugs, in fact in one area i couldn't progress because of a bug, but another bug made me warp right past where i needed to go, so i was lucky but what it amounts to is that there are too many bugs.If the game is going to be updated some of the improvements i would like to see are.Make the classes more distinct, maybe replace the sword with a unique attack that works for the class.Add more spells, give users the ability to target what they want instead of a bat, the other side of the room behind 5 obsticals... that it seems to want to do right now.Make the inventory managable. either add in an item wheel for quick select or just allow users to hide items from the rotation.The game is okay, but I was hoping for more especially when it came to classes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game for a little while since it seemed to have all of the elements I was looking for in a multiplayer experience, and I can say definitively that it did not disappoint. It isn't without a fair share of bugs and glitches, but based on the competency of the development team (who, to my understanding is just two dudes) within the rest of the game, I cannot imagine that it'd stay that way. It's chock full of stuff to do/see/find/farm/grind. It's almost exactly what you think, too. It's basically LttP but with multiplayer and randomly generated dungeons. Almost every item has a skill tree which really makes it to where you can play however you want. Classes could use a bit more definition regarding what they bring to the table, but that's a pretty minor complaint.The multiplayer, though honestly rife with glitches and desync issues, has been a blast with my friends. We've had a couple of instances where two of us would get kicked if the third party member equipped a new class. We've had occasions where someone spending gems at the health store spent all of their gems regardless of price. But, even though they're frustrating, they're not enough to remove from the overall experience.Exploration is exciting and fun, and you don't just get new items via dungeons. We'd completely forgotten about areas only to go back through and find a super useful main-stay secondary item in a cave that seemed fairly inconspicuous. That, and a bunch of collectible stuff gives you a great incentive to get out there and really get into the world.Combat is pretty basic, but fairly punishing until you figure out how to get into the groove. Dungeons are riddled with all kinds of traps and puzzles that are doing their best to kill you, and a lot of times you'll find yourself fighting enemies while also trying to navigate a floor-spike puzzle. It's fun.

Regarding quests, follow each step in order, I tried to get to a nearby village after a wayward villager told me I needed a special item, but I had to do a step in the quest chain first that was the opposite way to the town.April 14th review: Yep, the game is buggy all the way to the end, not enough to ruin the enjoyment, but enough to frustrate me. In fact, beyond the end of the game seems to have its bugs too, one of the developers seems to have a typo in one of the two places they are credited towards the start of the credits, and afterwards I gained an unexplained new ability that doesn't work with any consistency. Farming seems a wonky add-on, and the upgrade guy calls out that he can upgrade your watering can, bu there's no spot for it among the upgrades. I would advise skipping it, don't invest in it early and don't rely on it as a source of gold. Gold is really only useful for purchasing health potions within a dungeon and maybe getting some of the treasure boxes if you're absolutely loaded with gold. Yes, I still recommend Rogue Heroes, but it still has the feel of a game that belongs in early access. The most glaring bug for the intrepid swimmer is the climb-out point that launches you clear to the next zone north, pretty much every time without fail. I'd report everything in full detail, but I'd need to get a QA credit and a paid invoice because QA is a job for me, not a hobby. And don't mind not getting the fishing rod completed, there's an enemy that appears in the 3rd boss dungeon that drops the part you probably don't have yet. Likewise, I think it was the same area where you get the parts to finally complete the bow. _childDocuments_.review: I've played a bit of the free demo, liked it, and played a bit more of the game, and I Like it!And I recorded my progress with Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos, please watch if you prefer a more audio/visual format, or just want to get a Feel for the controls and Gameplay: It Feels Good. 👍 Note: The video starts off in the demo, but that is fine, because progress unlocked in the demo is kept going into the main game! OMG! Such an incredible feature that I hope other games emulate.Rogue Heroes is already leading the way in innovation and player focused design! No wasted time here!Anyway, Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is an Indie, 2D, Action RogueLite all about bringing back the bright SNES Glow of Action RPGs, only this time, with Multiplayer, even Local Multiplayer!Yep, Rogue Heroes is offering both Local and Online Co-op, with up to 4 players; though you can always just go solo if you wish. There are Massive The Legend of Zelda: A Link to The Past vibes to Rogue Heroes visually,  though gameplay wise, the influence is more The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords. These are 2 Very Good Influences to Have! And The Retro Glow of the old age is present here as well, presented in Pixel Graphics with a Beautiful Bright pallet that takes you right back to the early 90s era of console gaming goodness. I deem Rogue Heroes a Zelda-Like! It is Decided!A Zelda-Like with Procedurally Generated Dungeons and Meta-Progression, with Class unlocks and Village upgrades. Cool.Speaking of Meta Progression: It is in the form of gems, which you collect in the Dungeons, whether from beating down enemies, finding them in pots and bushes, or as loot in treasure chests. These gems are used to build structures to upgrade your village, and unlock the ability to upgrade your stats, like HP and Magic at the Clinic, Sword Attack improvements like damage, attack speed, or crit chance at the Forge, or to boost up your tools at the Tool Shed; stuff like that.Make sure to use most of your Gems after you die, as much like Cheron in a different Highly Influential Rogue Lite Action RPG, the Dungeon consumes all your gems when you enter, Rogue Legacy style!Interesting. But Why? I Bet there's a story there.Maybe the Dungeon, as both the original earthly Prison of the evil Titan, and now the Corrupted Seat of its Power, is somehow able to reabsorb the Gems on your person?After all, you did take them from the dungeon, and like, knows like. Perhaps the gems are the shattered, fragmented remains of the monsters of the Titan, which are of it, or at least, controlled by it. Maybe, as it regains Gems, it grows Stronger, retaking the Power it once invested into its minions. I'm Imagining T-1000 style re-absorption of separated parts here.Maybe, if it gets strong enough, it breaks free, rampages across the island, and eats your village!And now you must make haste to rescue the shattered souls of the consumed villagers before they too are consumed by the vile Titan's Fury! All while avoiding the Giant Awakened Beast! OMG! 🤯Speculations as to the final destination of the Gems aside, there is even more to like about Rogue Heroes beyond its Retro Pixel Art Beauty, and Meta Progression Its Gameplay is Great. The land itself is an Open World, letting you Adventure around, Exploring, Fighting enemies and discovering Secrets. Fun. In Contrast to the overworld, the layout and contents of the Dungeons is Procedurally Generated, and Changes every run, think different monster locations, different rooms and connections, different loot, traps, stuff like that.Combat-wise: The combat is Fast and Fun.Stick and move, manage your stamina, block with your shield if you like, and use your character's special ability, the default "Hero" ability is a charge. I also recommend using the tools you find in the Dungeon, like the Grappling Hook to hit from a distance, the Boomerang to Stun, The Wand to quickly Burn Em down from a Distance, and the Bomb Bags to bring the BOOM!I really like its intuitive Stamina system: how it shows visually on your character how exhausted they are as they fight for their life. YES! Display information on the character, Dead Space style, not stuffed way up in the upper Left corner. My eyes are on my character and their immediate environment, so don't pull my eyes from that. Excellent UI decision, though I wish they did the same thing with the Hp as well. Perhaps they will at some point. Anyway, in addition to all that Old School Goodness, and Great RogueLite Gameplay,  Rogue Heroes has Full Controller Support, with support for Mouse and Keyboard control if you wish, and will be released on the Switch as well! In short, if you are looking for a Fun, RogueLite, ZeldaLike Action RPG with Co-op, Fun ARPG Gameplay with a bit of challenge, you have found your game. Give the video a Glance to be sure?

_childDocuments_.review: Don't believe the fake reviews.  This is one of the most broken and buggy games on the entire steam platform.This abomination is why developers should spend at least an hour or two QA testing their games before releasing them. Going to list just a handful of them that I encountered in the past two sessions playing it:*Since everyones camera angle is tied together, if one person lags a bit when going through a transition point all players will get stuck repeatedly going back and forth between the two points.  The same applies for houses and shops.*Enemies positions are client side and will occasionally desync between players, thus people will be fighting entirely different enemies or nothing will show up at all for others.*Some transition points are completely broken, for example there is a cave near the waterfalls that you need to go through to get the power gloves, yet it sends one player through normally (and makes their screen black till they alt+f4 out) and the rest of the party all the way across the map to the snow biome where they get murdered from the Tier 4 enemies.*Spells and projectiles do not cast towards the mouse, but rather where the player is facing, and even then not where the player is facing all the time.  For example, casting a firebolt to the left trying to hit a zombie yet it decides mid flight to go straight up.  Same issues when using the controller. *Players all share one camera, so if someone goes afk it stretches the camera out all the way to where the rest of the team cannot see one foot infront of them, in a game where things generally kill you in three hits, this is not ideal. Ghosts also pull the camera where they move, so if a player is just dead and bored it makes the game hell for the rest of the team.*All players are forced to be in the same room, even though we have encountered bugs where we were able to explore separate rooms on our own.  The bug proves that it's unnecessary and also is frustrating, this is similar to issue #1 except in dungeons, occasionally you will break off from the rest of the party and just be going your own way.  This seems to happen if someone alt tabs out or is in a menu when transitioning.*Bosses are unbalanced and stupidly inconsistent with the dungeon theme .  For example, in the graveyard is an 8000 HP boss and all he does is just a weak easily avoidable fireball attack, then lets the players hit him, and repeats till he dies.  His HP implies he's suppose to be tough, but he is simply just a time waster.  Dungeon 2 hints throughout the entire thing that the boss is going to be a two headed snake or something but instead is just a dancing mushroom that takes 2-4 damage per hit for seemingly no reason, and is just a damage sponge for the sake of being a damage sponge.  Dungeon 1's beetle was fine, but the entire dungeon hinted at it being a tentacle monster of a sort.*Players will DC out mid dungeon fairly often just because of how broken the game is, and they cannot rejoin until the host goes all the way back to lobby,  and their gems are not saved on disconnection.  So the rest of the party will have the full dungeon loot yet the person who DCed will come back with 0.*Trap damage is very inconsistent.  In one floor arrows will hit for 50, another will hit for 200.*Early-mid game every class other than just straight up melee is totally useless.  For example in our play I was hitting for 200x3 dmg three hit combos with the thief while the mage was hitting for like 25-50 and the ranger was around 150, running out of arrows after ten shots.*I really cannot express just how much absolute cancer the shared camera is, it's really bad, especially since it only gives about half a squares worth of vision to players who are near the borders, and enemies will occasionally run off screen and attack from out of viewable distance even though they're only like 10-20 feet away.I am glad I got this game for free, because I would have absolutely hated this if I had to pay full price.  And I honestly feel sorry for those who did have to pay for this garbage.  Literally a $5 game in my opinion, a few dollars more than what they spent on Q&A testing.Also just a fun thing, so in this situation I had four enemies to my right, as well as a bat over there too.  To the south of me, on the other side of the room behind like three walls was another bat.I was facing right, towards the skeletons and instead I shoot STRAIGHT down towards the bat on the other side of the room, which is literally offscreen at the moment.And the rest of my shots ALL went to the wall trying to shoot the bat over there.And in this situationI had an enemy I wanted to shoot on my right and another enemy behind me. I was facing right and I shot to the left.  This happens waaay too often.Amazing.  Truly.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, there are definitely some things that need tweaking though.  I found the bosses of dungeons to be remarkably easy compared to the dungeons themselves, in fact the only reason I failed to defeat a boss the first time was lack of knowledge of a floor break mechanic on the first one.  It didn't take long to sus out the location of the legendary fish for the final thread I needed at the end of the game.  I feel like the knight thread is vastly overpowered granting far increased defense and attack at the cost of some movement speed which is easily overlooked by it's ability.  I'd like to see more challenge in the endgame.  After just over 30 hours of play, I'm short a mere seven achievements that are more tedious labor than anything else; marking some things in the beastiary, collecting the power spheres, getting the rest of the fish, getting the rest of the shortcuts, hitting 25 in the endless abyss, and a couple others.  At the end of the day, the game is great, don't get me wrong here, but it could be more, there are many rogue-lites out there that continue to offer challenge even well past the end game, I think that this has potential, especially with the Link to the Past vibes that this game gives off.  Mechanically, I found no issues with the single or multiplayer, however I have heard of some synching issues in multiplayer that cause problems for others.  I enjoyed the game, I just find that it was too easy for me to power through it in just a couple of days.  Hopefully the skull dungeon DLC will add some difficult content that will give the challenge I'm looking for.Now the pros and consPros:Puzzles are fun, most offer challenge without being hatefulThe early game is difficult but not so much that it's discouragingI love the building mechanicI love that there are multiple classesThe retro, Link to the Past style gameplay is fantasticThe story is solidCons:Mid to late game is too easyClasses need more diversity to set them apart, why does every class have the same sword mechanic?The Endless Abyss could offer far more challenge being a post game dungeonSpeaking of the Endless Abyss, adding a prompt to enter the final boss fight there would be nice, I've found myself walking into that fight multiple times now accidentally having not done as much as I wanted in thereI've heard that fishing is difficult, I find it to be the opposite, I didn't even realize the rod could be upgraded before I had caught the legendary fishOnline multiplayer could do without sharing the same screen spaceI feel like some of the tools have 'one off' usesOverall I would rate this game a solid 7/10 right now, it definitely needs work, it stands as a solid introduction to the rogue-lite genre and I would definitely see the younger crowd enjoying the play, but in order to keep the generation that looks at this and says "Link to the Past style Rogue-Lite?  Sign me up!" entertained, it needs to have more challenge and be just a little more hateful to the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put about seven hours into this game (all single player) and I think I'm done. There are so many minor annoyances that I can't continue.There are so many cheap ways to die. It makes me think of Spelunky, where you can be going along just fine and then a combination of things can kill you really quickly. In that game, you can always see how/why it happened and learn from it. In this game, rather than being a learning experience, it's just frustrating. Get poisoned? It happens easily, and you'll die quickly. Your health will drain away while you can do nothing. The rooms may not be randomly generated, but you do see the same rooms over and over. In the second dungeon, I'd clear one room, advance a couple rooms over, and be faced with the same room as before, with the same annoying puzzle to repeat again.In the overworld, the map is designed poorly. When I'm in the upper-left corner of the map, trying to find my way around this swamp, I want to look at the map continuously. But each time you close the map and reopen it, it resets itself to the middle of the overworld, not remembering what zoom level you had it at. Each time you have to zoom in again, and manually move the map to where you want to see. It sounds minor but it's really annoying.Why is there no music? At all? Enemies are hard to see, your health drains quickly (despite me upgrading it quite a bit), stamina drains quickly. It all makes you feel really weak, and each upgrade is so minimal that it doesn't feel like it makes much of a difference.The game's saving grace, and the only reason I didn't quit it much earlier, is that you get to keep all your currency on death so that you can spend it all on upgrades. So there's no real penalty for death, other than annoyance and wasted time.I played this game exclusively on Deck. I got it on sale for $7.50, which for seven hours I guess is okay. I had some fun with it but I think I'm done. It runs really well on Dekc. But, it hangs every time I exit it, and I have to then manually close it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game will let players relive their A Link to the Past nostalgic childhood experience, I thoroughly enjoyed it for the most part. The Endless Abyss dungeon teleport pad in the centre of every floor transition room will end the run instantly with no confirmation message and is easy to accidentally activate. Losing a several hour run for the achievement feels bad.   The equipment selection menu sometimes continues to scroll after exiting the menu.      The farming system is broken, when trees die all tiles used by the 3x3 crop become unusable for several in game days or until exiting the game, except for the single tile which the tree seed was planted on.     The beastiary progression for monsters will randomly stop working for some reason.    Several instances of enemies warping through walls.    Monsters becoming immune to all damage, specifically fish monster in swamp dungeon will become immune when stunned and damaged until after the stun ends.     Player unable to attack or receive damage from monsters. Picking up a world space item like grass or stone fixed this.     Audio (overworld, dungeon, and boss music) stops working. A fragment of the boss intro music kept working then abruptly stop which was arguably worse than if it were just silent.   Unable to track specific power sphere collection progress to know which area of the map to search, This should be added to the menu display.

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing are the dungeons.I have 30 hours in this game, and it is horribly unbalanced to the point that the only class worth playing is the Knight.The second area cannot be accessed at ALL without the knight, because there is a stretch of mud that is barely too long for any other class to jump across. There is no lore. No conversations with NPCs in the town you've built, and the town itself has some bugs. If you built the farm and didn't get a watering can, too bad. Same for the fisherman - you might have the items, but he won't give you the rod.There's also way, way too little direction. You need a compass for a new area? It'll tell you that, but that's it. Guess where it is? On the complete opposite side of the map somewhere you've probably never passed by, and no NPC has information to help you at all throughout the entire game. You built a town, but they only stand around. If you're stuck, you better be okay with watching the singular play-through online that doesn't explain anything, and plays as a knight. For a game that is trying to take notes from Zelda-like series, it is unbelievably lackluster in the lore/NPC interaction department. There is nothing to do, and no tips or aid from any NPC.And if you want to play it for the dungeons, it is rather fun. But don't get your hopes up about the bosses. The final boss doesn't even have music, and its arena is unbelievably tiny. It's genuinely not worth your time. This game is NOT finished, it had no business being released like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 5/10TL;DR - Town building and world exploring is fun, but combat is primitive, frustrating, and without balance due to several reasonsThe Good:- Town building is fun! Making houses and buildings to progress your power feels rewarding- Exploring the world is fun and can feel very rewarding to find hidden pathways and solve puzzles for passagesThe Bad:- Upgrades are too easy to max turning basic weapons into artifacts of legends. A basic wand can turn from 8 dmg to 154 dmg after spending money from one single dungeon run. The Ugly:- Combat (which makes up at least 50% of the game) is honestly frustrating.  - Contact damage is an old school form of damage that should not be present in current games in my opinion. Enemies with spikes dealing contact damage makes 100% sense, but an enemy with no weapons and make of just bones bumping into me dealing 50% of my life makes 0% sense.  - Enemies run wildly and unpredictably making "learning" a strategy nearly impossible for most enemies  - Ranged weapons are either snipers fired with pin point precision or a blunderbuss where the target can stand in front of you and not be hit. I have fired a wand from point blank range only to watch *both* projectiles stray to the left and right of the target.-Coop is glitched very often. I find myself fighting opponents that are invisible to my coop partner.Overall, this game suffers from the idea that difficulty = fun. The artificial difficulty of unpredictable enemies and contact damage make playing 50% of the game frustrating. Great idea, poor execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think the game is a notably entry for what it tries to do, and is perfectly enjoyable in its own right. The world is complete and mostly fun to explore, the secrets are tantalising and often rewarding, and the freedom to build differently or play with friends is great. I just can't help but feel like the game fell short of its full potential and stumbled with polishing the final product.If you know Zelda: Link to the Past, this game is a love letter to that game and  inspired by it. But, it takes a new approach with its town-building progression and randomised elements and classes, and offers a fresh experience with a slightly different combat system and challenges, and ability to play solo or co-op.If you don't know Zelda: Link to the Past, it's a top-down action-adventure game with a combination of overworld exploration and dungeon-crawling. The overworld and some dungeons are hand-crafted, while some dungeons are procedurally generated. There are some puzzles to solve and secrets to find, and plenty of action combat to be had. You'll be collecting gems from dungons to upgrade you character and build up the central town, which serves as a path of progression parallel to your finding of new tools with which to overcome new obstacles.While I recommend this game to fans of action-adventure games, I have to comment that the game doesn't represent a flawless entry. The bugs are infrequent and never really broke the game, but they do exist, most of them related to the movement system in the game. Ice physics sometimes have a weird memory of your momentum, and I've jumped to a space seemingly between the upper and lower layers where I couldn't interact with anything until I jumped back out. The balance of the game also seems to jump around a bit. It feels like the bosses from dungeons added later in development are on an entirely different difficulty curve than the bosses in the main dungeons. These issues don't ruin the game, but leave it feeling incomplete at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really do love the game; it's an excellent roguelike and Zelda combo that genuinely satisfies both,  has great multiplayer. But the horror stories about the bugs in it are real. Apparently since the start of the year, many players found an issue where after a certain amount of time they just weren't able to launch the game past the loading screen anymore, effectively bricking the game on their devices. In my case, it happened on the Steam Deck, and in theirs it was on Windows or other operating systems. All this after it was working fine for a very long time. As far as I can tell, no effort is being made to fix this issue, and until it is, I cannot recommend anybody get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Design decisions work against eachother resulting in clunky & unintuitive gameplay.Poorly optimized, and constantly stutters on a 32G RAM & 5.3 Ghz Computer.You have tiny melee range, and just barely more than enemies, which isn't a problem until you realize that the sword will thrust you forward into enemies and damage you. Back peddling and micro-spacing every rat and skeleton is not fun nor rewarding gameplay.Traps are just darkened tiles on the floor and will almost always hit you when you trip them. They're easy enough to avoid, but are virtually invisible in darkened rooms.The point I'm getting at, is that Rogue Heroes doesn't provide instant deaths like a lot of modern "Hardcore" Roguelikes, but will whittle down on you with chip damage from many unavoidable sources, and will instead frustrate you until you'll want to just throw yourself into a trap to end the run prematurely. Generally a frustrating, tedious and unrewarding experience. I'm sure the Developers have learned their lesson from this game, considering they've went on to make the Blasphemous series.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 (Long story short) Rogue Heroes: Ruins Of Tasos is a great multiplayer/singleplayer adventure Zelda like game where you go through dungeons and upgrade your hero to go deeper through the ruins.My takeaway: I had so much fun playing Rogue Heroes: Ruins Of Tasos that I completely lost track of time playing it with my friends. The premise of the game is simple- you have a hero you can customize and in which you can choose and change from multiple different classes, you go through the ruins that consists of multiple dungeons, level layouts, and puzzles, you collect in game currency to upgrade the hero, and you keep going this way until you finish the game and discover all of the ruins. There’s multiple sidequests and a few things you can do to kill time like simplified farming, selling, collecting, getting monster data, and power stones. I never had a dull moment playing this title and never ran out of things to do until I eventually did.That being said- the game isn’t without faults. Multiplayer can be glitchy and would periodically kick my party out resulting in having to go back and restart from the main menu. Sometimes my friends would have to restart with no progress saved on their character which would be very frustrating. The game doesn’t hold your hand when it comes to the monsters and puzzles so you’ll have to figure out a lot of the combat and mechanisms by yourself. You also have a long list of tools that they don’t make it easy to switch between; I’ve spent a lot of time either having to pause the game for everyone or keep switching between different tools. I also really like farming and this game does it in a way that is simple and entertaining but the reward for the work just isn’t there and it serves as more of a time waster.Overall the game is great for what it is in its current state- an adventure dungeon game. It’s pretty clear it wanted to be more but in its current state it’s very difficult to care for the characters or even know why everything around you is going on. For what it is, it is well worth the time and I’d recommend it to anyone who isn’t expecting the sun and moon from the title.To see more reviews like this one come support me and follow this curating page! I’d really appreciate it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is to 2D Zelda what 20XX is to Megaman XIt's a fun indie approach to an old classic franchise and I LOVE IT!!!This game is basically 2D Zelda in all but name, there are a lot of staples from that franchise here and they work more or less the same as they would in a 2D Zelda game. The big change is the temples, because this is a Rouge-like game the temples don't have a set format, they change every time you enter them and that is really where the challenge lies in this game.The game may only have four temples, but trust me it's going to take you awhile to beat the first one. You're going to have to try a few times and probably die a lot in the process. But each time you die you take the gems you earned and you upgrade yourself getting stronger. Eventually you'll beat that first temple and move on to the others, taking what you've learned and applying it to the future.Between the temples there are side quests to do just like in Zelda and those side quests tend to have useful rewards for completing them. The over-world map is fun to explore especially once you start getting upgrades that let you start entering new areas. The enemies come in many different varieties and some will require thinking outside the box to beat them. This game has taken a lot of the elements from 2D Zelda and added some of its own allowing for a nice indie game that shines on its own.Some of those new elements include the class system. You can swap out different classes at your house and try them out to see which one you like. For me I enjoy using the knight as his higher defense makes completing the temples easier. The thief is also a good choice for exploring the overworld due to his fast movement. Another new element is the fact that you can upgrade your town. That's something you'll want to do as soon as you can, as upgrading the town gives you more options to upgrade yourself. I like how you can choose what buildings go where and that each building grants some sort of benefit to you.I don't know what else to say other than if you are a fan of Zelda buy this game! I think you will enjoy it for sure and definitely get your moneys worth!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.  Gets lots of the aspects from Zelda.Rogue-like, you play as long as you can until you die.  When you die you get gems to upgrade your character. After the first dungeon you'll find yourself going through the game very quickly.  I beat the second dungeon on my second run through, and I beat the third, fourth, and final dungeons without dying.There's a few fetch quests, travel back and forth looking for specific items to unlock areas of the game and equipment, but now that I've beaten it the only thing left to do is see how far I can make it in the endless dungeon.There are a few bugs in the game, specifically collectibles that you can't pick up, as well as some areas you can't reach because they aren't finished.  Hopefully the developer releases an update soon because it's been almost a year since the last patch notes, and there's three remaining areas on the map I'm itching to get to.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy puzzles, dungeons, combat-heavy class systems,town-building, and farming? Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos has a healthy footing with all of these.Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a 1-4 co-op rogue-lite RPG adventure game with farming simulator elements that was developed by Heliocentric Studios. Although this two-person team worked on smaller projects for Xbox Live, in the past three years they have released two of their own games together on Steam. Rogue Heroes is their most significant project. Joshua Grump is the programmer and sound designer, and Brandon Weatherbee is the artist and level designer.GRAPHICS 8.2/10Rogue Heroes’ 16-bit pixel graphics look fantastic. Each class has distinguishing features and each jump dash and blink is exceptionally animated. The world gives off “Link to the Past” vibes and features frozen mountains, boggy swamps (that you can drown in if you aren’t carefully paying attention), and my favorite area, a volcanic region (which made me nostalgic for “The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons”). The overworld submerses you into a well-tied-together atmosphere. Each area has its unique type of terrain, enemies, and plant life. Abilities and spells appear nicely as well. Rogue Heroes’ dungeons are exciting at first but slowly become monotonous as the art style doesn’t change from the first dungeon to the last.SOUND QUALITY 8.8/10Sound quality is one of Rogue Heroes’ best features. The immersive music and sounds made me feel completely engaged in each area. Everything has a specific sound. Each primary weapon has its own slashing sound whether you hit brush, boxes, enemies, or anything else. Enemies have their distinctive cry. Traps in dungeons have a neat sound. Every arrow shot, every bomb dropped, and every gem and pot falling from the sky all make stepping on a trap button worth it. Completing a dungeon was my favorite because of the mini techno beat during the victory screen. The score and sound effects are never disappointing.GAMEPLAY 9/10In Rogue Heroes, you aren’t merely a dungeon diver. There are eight different classes to choose from and each class-tree gives you a different play style. Rather than simply hacking at the enemy (even though that seemed to work best), there are some challenging runs for the more difficult and engaging classes. The mage and ranger have very low defense but are more agile. I did this playthrough as the knight which gave me maximum protection and maximum damage (a "quality build," if you will). As a knight, I could eat everything the enemies, traps, and bosses had to offer. Aside from classes, there is also a level-up system that provides additional abilities. You are also able to switch classes at your leisure. The main currency in the game is gems that are only obtainable by delving through replayable dungeons. Gold is another currency, but it’s only for opening locked chests. Gems give you the ability to build your town which is required to level up damage, health, stamina, tool damage, and buy other classes. There is a great deal of content packed into this game and it makes you want to max out everything so you can through the infinity dungeon with unlimited floors.CHARACTERS 7/10The characters felt reasonably simple without story character building; most side character missions are completed early on and don’t seem to change anything. Most NPCs are shop and store owners, giving you goods, upgrades for gems, and unlocking threads for classes. As the main hero, you do not speak and there is no story for how you came to be. Each area had a seemingly important NPC, but they mean nothing after completing the dungeon as you progress. Each new location has an NPC that gives you an idea of what’s to come or what you need to do to provide headway into each area. NPCs fit their role and include the region that you are currently in.STORY 6.7/10Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos' lowest point is the immersion of the story. The tale is rudimentary and uncomplicated. You are the hero of this quest, and you must defeat each boss in the dungeon to collect coins to unlock the final dungeon. You can altogether skip to the final dungeon due to a teleport pad that takes you directly to the final boss. I was disappointed because I expected challenging puzzles and dynamically powerful enemies inside the last dungeon leading up to the final boss. Yet the final dungeon is simply an infinite dungeon, and I understand why it’s crafted this way. The are sidequest fillers are in this game to progress further in each region, but you can complete them without doing certain overworld side quests. I never felt like I was saving anything or anyone, and it eemed like no one was ever worried about the looming evil of the final boss. The main story is relatively short and can be completed in only 7-8 hours.OVERALL 7.9/10If you want something focused mainly on dungeons, puzzles, and combat, this is the game for you. The sound is perfect and the gameplay is fantastic. I completed the game by only maxing out my damage. I was unstoppable. The characters don’t include much lore, and the story is a bit watered down. However, Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos will hook you with its combat system and you will stay for the never-ending dungeon. Although dungeons are the focus of this game and the farming is minuscule, I was impressed by this game’s extraordinary ability to implement this niche mechanic without making it the only thing to do in the game. Replaying this game solo doesn’t necessarily appeal to me, but I can see myself having a great time playing this game again with up to 3 friends and spelunking through the final dungeon.  All-in-all, this is a great game to play with friends and is an excellent dungeon crawler rogue-lite.
