_childDocuments_.review: On paper, the base concept of the game is good, having a hero (or two with coop), several classes, a rogue system, and some puzzles to go through various dungeon.If fun at first, you quickly realise that the game is pretty much grind til the end because it fall short on several aspects :- The classes are not good. The differences lies in passive damage changes depending on the class, and on a difference in the type of dash you have. That's pretty much it. And there's only so much type of dash you can do, and at the end of a day, a dash is a dash, making the classes not really unique (even the Druid the supposedly new class is just dash fever fest 2000).- The UI is correct at best, and awful for some things. At the end of the game you have a lot of "tools", and having to go through them over and over again to switch from using that one or this one is really annoying. You have shortcut but they still require heaving handling of the controller, making it hard to switch from one thing to another. It's even more a shame that most of the tool are useless in most situation and could have been put on a "separated list", you need 3 to 4 tool in quick access no more.- The game loop is a totally repetitive : get gems, upgrade, rince, repeat (fun fact : we did a run near the endgame where we gain almost as much gems that the entirety of our playthrough). And the rest also falls a bit short. The exploration is always to go through convulated ways to get from A to B, and the puzzle offer very little variation in the dungeon. The dungeons are mostly easy, and once you have the patterns, the boss never provides any real challenge (worst being the final boss that we completely destroyed).All in all in terms of roguelike, even with the coop aspect that could have been fun, I wouldn't really recommend this game as a first pick, but more in sale, and if you already played the others of the genre. I, for one, wouldn't really play that one solo (since there are serious contenders like Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy, Hades, etc...)

_childDocuments_.review: "Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos" is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  It's a mediocre ripoff of Legend of Zelda (but not really, it's markedly different in a lot of ways apart from ripping off the idea) where you just run through procgen pixelcrap "dungeons" doing top down console-esque brawling.  There's some lightweight RPG elements, but this is a true RPG as much as I'd be a Jeep Cherokee if I had wheels. On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.To make matters worse, while lazy, low quality pixel "art" has been used, making the game look bad, many elements of the game aren't done with pixelcrap... which accomplishes a couple of things.  First, it shows the developers perhaps could have done better and they knew it, so that's a major screwup.Secondly, it destroys any hopes the developer had of creating a "retro aesthetic" as their excuse for the lazy pixelart compromise... It looks completely inauthentic from a retro gaming perspective.  Visually, this is a hamfisted mess, a dogs breakfast of bad visuals, and this kind of laziness and poor quality should never be foisted on gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the video game library/engine, Monogame.  It's rarely used, because it's arguably worse than construction kits like GameMaker Studio, RPGMaker and Clickteam Fusion, but it's also much harder to work with.  Despite this, Monogame has very limited capabilities, which go some way to explaining the poor quality of the game.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos" has the preposterous price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Monster Hunter World", "Wolfenstein - The New Order" or "Kingdom Come Deliverance".  No pixelcrap is worth $20. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really like Rogue games but this one gets me.When you die, the dungeons are the only thing that reset. The progress, leveling, and items you got, stays on you. Some items you get in dungeons are made of glass, and break when you die, or leave, but you can make them permanent if you farm enough mats to make them.Leveling is not that hard, not too long and rewarding.Combat and movement, are really satisfying. It's fast, really easy to get from the start, no headaches.I play with a DS4 controller. The game recognized it and put PS icons instead of Xbox. That's not much, but it's honest work.The game seems to be long for the price. I just finished the first dungeon, and halfway through the second. Took me 3 hours to do so. Didn't get the chance to try the Druid class yet. Classes need to be bought, then you level each one of them (I think).There's also an endgame (I think) that when you finish the main story, you get an "infinite dungeon", which is nice.I didn't tried multiplayer yet, but what I saw from videos seems to be fun as hell.Bottom line, I recommend buying this game, on sale or full price. It's a Zelda-Like, kinda game. The story is nice so far, not too deep, not too boring. It's "kill all evil" kinda type, pretty straight forward. There's no "take you by the hand" because it's find the next path to follow. For the rest, there's always a wiki for that.Maybe more DLCs in the future? Would be nice too... Team17 and Ellocentric, hats off to you guys, you did a great job on this one!

_childDocuments_.review: THE ONLINE IS NOT TERRIBLEI'm only writing this early in playtime to counter everyone that says the online experience is horrendous. I almost didn't purchase the game because of it, and online has been totally fine barring one or two disconnects towards the beginning of the launch, so I don't want anyone to be put off by those comments. There are still small inconveniences like hopping into the item menu for one player pauses the game for everyone (which could maybe be fixed by hopping everyone into the menu at once?), however with the quick swap hotkeys (LB/RB on controller) I feel like it's not too problematic. Overall though, me and my friends have very much enjoyed playing this together so far. PS. I might extend this review once I've played the game further.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I'd recommend, hesitantly, though. See, the game itself is a decent little Zelda wannabe. The art style is pleasant. The music isn't anything special, but it's not bad. It's... Just kinda there. And that's the biggest problem I have with the game. There's a lot of really half-baked ideas that are just... There. Not sure if this was a kickstarter game, but the game reeks of someone lazily including promised features in the most bare-bones way possible. There are several classes with very minor differences, they all play essentially the same. There's a weather system and day/night cycle that doesn't seem to actually affect anything. None of the NPCs even acknowledge it. There's a farming system which is extremely generic (rainy weather doesn't even water your crops!) and it's pretty much a waste of time, as all you get for doing it is gold, which has almost no uses. There's a fishing system, but really nothing to do with the fish you catch aside from put them in a fish tank. The potion makers interface seems to hint that there was a system to brew potions from different ingredients, but you have all the recipes from the beginning and it doesn't let you experiment. There are odd and unique rocks spread around the overworld. There's also someone in town who is clearly into rocks, as his whole house is covered in them. I *thought* there might be a connection between the two, so I bring one of the special rocks to him. He doesn't care. There's a tavern that just kinda sits there. The tavern owner acts like he might give you quests. He doesn't. There are 2 currencies, gold, which is ONLY used for opening chests and buying a couple items from a random vendor in dungeons, and gems, which buy all your upgrades. You can only find gems in dungeons, so exploring the overworld feels like a waste of time. For some reason, the game takes away all your gems when you enter a dungeon. The only real collectible item are these 100 orbs that let you keep a small percentage of your gems when you enter a dungeon, which is practically useless, as the amount they let you keep is negligible even if you collect all of them, and you're probably spending all your gems on upgrades before you enter, anyhow. So it's not a bad game, really, it's just frustrating to see all these half-assed features that clearly didn't get the time, thought, and effort they needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I got this game in the Humble Choice.Main takeaway:There are positives and negatives. I think the positives probably outweigh the negatives. But for $20, this could use a little more polish and bug fixing. It's a bit hard to recommend at $20, but maybe on sale this can be a pretty fun little co-op game to play with a friend. While I believe it supports 4 players coop, I don't think it's actually practical due to the choice of 1 locked, shared camera.Things I liked:The graphics, music, world design, level design, and procedurally generated dungeons are all excellent. In a lot of good ways, this feels like a modern take on the familiar SNES Zelda formula. I'm pretty impressed by the procedurally generated dungeons because we never encountered a "soft lock" due to finding keys out of order or anything, which is sometimes a problem in 16-bit games from that era. I liked the money system. Being able to keep money you earn even if your run fails is kinda nice so you don't feel like you lost all your progress. I like the perks. I like that almost all the tools and weapons had some kind of upgrade path. I like that each class has a skill/perk tree you can invest in.I like how the town works. You get to purchase new buildings with different uses. For example, one building is for upgrading your stamina skill tree. Another is for upgrading weapons, or classes, etc. And you get to manually choose where each building goes, so you get to customize the layout of your town. I really enjoyed this design choice and it made me feel like my decisions for my town mattered.Things I'm a bit neutral on:There are like 8 or so different classes. I like this, in theory. However, magic does not seem to be a viable path. And neither does ranged combat. So basically, my coop partner and I each chose different classes (Knight for me, Ranger for him) but both of us ended up using only the sword as our weapon because the skill/perk upgrades for the sword are SO MUCH better than the ones for bow or magic that anything besides sword simply wasn't viable.Lots of "tools." But too many tools. There are several tools which are redundant and should just upgrade to from base model, to +1, then +2 with increasingly improved effects. For example, there's a hammer for hitting rocks. But there's also a boxing glove for hitting rocks. And all the tools live in 1 tool bar, in which you can only access 1 tool at a time. So by late game, when you have 15 tools, you have to cycle through them all in order to find the one you need. And as you get new tools, the tool order changes, so you can never really memorize the distance between different tools in the toolbar menu.Things I did not like:The toolbar hot menu does not function correctly on gamepad. I was able to set up tools on the different hot menu locations, but trying to cycle between them in-game didn't work.What is the point of farming? We tried this a little bit but it really felt like an afterthought and didn't actually ever earn us enough  currency to feel necessary vs simply farming dungeons.Sharing 1 locked screen is super bad. Especially because if 1 player opens a menu, the other player gets stuck looking at the menu and can't move until the first person closes the menu. Does not feel good in a modern game. 2 player coop felt kinda bad with this, but 3+ players felt really awful. Our 3rd friend quit after about 20 minutes because this was so poorly implemented and annoying to share one screen all the time.The bugs. Early game there weren't really any. But by mid game we were experiencing some bugs, and by later/end game we were experiencing constant bugs. One of the most egregious was in the endless dungeon in the main town that you finally access in late game. There was 1 level in this dungeon that we kept encountering that had a broken staircase. The stairway was textured into the game, but it was not modeled correctly so you couldn't take it up to the other area of the room, which meant you literally could not complete the room to progress. Every time we encountered that room (at least 3 times), we just had to quit out and end our run, which was frustrating.Another weird bug that comes to mind: while both of us were swimming, something glitched out when switching between screens and my character was able to walk on water. Which was slightly amusing at first, but obviously wrong and I wasn't able to fix it without quitting the run.--I would say this game starts out feeling like a 7.5/10. By mid game, with increasing bugs, this probably drops to a 6.5. By end game, I think it's a solid 6/10. I was pretty excited to just end the game and be done by the time we beat the final boss. I'm still going to give this a recommend, because I think they did some cool stuff with familiar genera, but hopefully this dev can do more bug testing and fixing on future titles so their games are more enjoyable to play throughout, instead of mostly in the first 1/3.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing almost 40 hours, I recommend Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos for gamers that love and miss the top down Zelda classics such as A Link to the Past or Link's Awakening. However, it is a rogue lite game, so don't expect the heavy puzzles of a Zelda game as this game is mostly a fight-a-thon with all of the main villains' minions and monsters.PROS:There's a large overworld to explore that contains your typical forest, mountain, frozen tundra, volcano, beach, swamp land, graveyard, and lake areas, etc, similar to a Hyrule adventure. As I said, this game's strength is in appealing to the Zelda fan and it would not be amiss to call this rogue lite a Zelda clone. We have a sword and shield, the hookshot, boomerang, a flute that summons a riding animal, the lantern, the hammer, the fishing rod, bombs and the bomb bag, the wand that shoots ice or fire, spells to quell storms or change the time of day, etc. New or original items might include the punching glove and the extremely underused time wand that shows what the area looked like centuries past and allows our "not Link" player character to interact with the environment as it was in the distant past. The bestiary book is technically new, even though games like Breath of the Wild had one, because this bestiary book is a usable item: you close monsters up into it like you would dried flowers in order to add them to your bestiary. If you add the monsters enough times, you master that monster, however I fail to see how this is beneficial as it seems to not add any extra information or give you any perks, other than getting you one step away from completing the entire bestiary and getting a Steam achievement for it. Cracked walls can be bombed to show hidden caves and passage ways, as we've had in Zelda ever since the first game in the series (well, minus the cracks which didn't come until A Link to the Past). Torches can be lit with the lantern to solve puzzles and reveal hidden chests. One good upgrade on our Zelda lantern is that we can now use it to start brush fires or burn down obstacles in our path. At a certain point in the game you earn a masterful sword of sorts that will shoot out a long range projectile beam of light at enemies if your health is at full. In other words, if you're a Zelda fan, there's plenty to love and be comfortable with here, with a couple new additions or changes. Like in Breath of the Wild, we are given an exhaustion meter that can be upgraded to allow us to do more for longer later in the game. This is important as you don't want to get tired of swinging your sword and get overwhelmed by enemies or drown while swimming. Collectibles and monster drops exist in the game but, except for a couple of side quests or so and making potions, I haven't found any use for the monster drops. The lone collectible comes in the form of power spheres that allow you to keep a certain amount of gems when reentering a new dungeon. The game, unlike Zelda, has two forms of currency: the Rupee like gems and the standard medieval RPG gold coins. You'll need both the progress without hindrance. Gems can only be found in the dungeons, where as gold coins are found everywhere. You'd think the village NPC's would accept gold coins more often but unfortunately it's all gems for the most part. You'll need gold coins to pay to unlock certain treasure chests holding gems as well as the dungeon merchant that offers health potions and whatnot while you're deep in the dungeons. Dungeons cannot be left unless you die, in which case you awaken back at your home in the town, your earned gems in tow to help you upgrade before you face the dungeon yet again. As a rogue lite, puzzles do exist, but it's mostly about fighting your way through until you die or become strong enough to defeat the dungeon. In other words, dungeons are not meant to be beaten on the first try, so expect to die. A lot. Dungeons are generated randomly so that every dungeon attempt is different. There are currently 6 dungeons, although more dungeons may come in the future; we'll get back to this later. The village is an interesting aspect of this Zelda clone because you can use your gems in order to build not only your house, but also vacant houses thereby attracting NPC characters to come live in your village. You also can build a fishing pier and house, a bar, a witch's potion shop, a science lab, a gymn, a hospital, a general store, a sword smith work shop, an tool shop, a thread shop, and a personal farm. The farm gives light Harvest Moon chores as the vegetables can be sold in the market town square for gold coins needed for the dungeons. Vegetable seeds can be found while out exploring the overworld, which cannot be fully explored until you earn and upgrade your typical Zelda tools from the dungeons or the science lab or the tool shop, just as you would expect from a Zelda clone. Some higher end vegetable seeds can also be purchased using gems at the general store. Gold coins can be used mostly in town to buy furnishings for your house. Some of these are functional, but most are cosmetic. You start off with two functioning pieces of furniture, the bed and the wardrobe. The bed passes a day, possibly heals you (I'm not sure, I never tried this), whereas the wardrobe allows you to change your player character class, something definitely not from the Zelda franchise. I have not explored using these classes yet, but more classes can be purchased from the thread shop. They help in multiplayer, I'm sure, but I was not able to do any multiplayer, despite attempting it several times. Multiplayer is both online or split screen local. I stuck to the basic starting player character class as it is the Link-clone standard. Other classes have different changes in offense, defense, and speed and offer a different running move or other ability. The standard "Link" wardrobe offers the Pegasus boot move from A Link to the Past, whereas other classes have invisibility, teleportation, skull rolling, flying via witch's broom or a parrot, a bomb jump, etc. Speaking of jumping, the Roc Feather is sadly missing from this game. The basic premise of the game is to kill the four dungeon bosses in order to gain their 4 coins and add them to the final dungeon ala "Super Mario Land 2: The 6 Golden Coins" in order to access the final dungeon and boss and thus free the land from the villains' curse so the villagers can colonize the continent safely. You are quested, not by the villagers, but by four goddesses who have been imprisoned by the monstrous villains. Side quests will help fill in gaps in story telling, but we'll get to this later. The game's over world features random transitions to night and random thunder storms. Certain stores in the village are closed during night and storms. Sleeping in the bed or using magic spells can change the time or weather and are needed for certain over world puzzle solving. During your exploration of the over world, you'll find abandoned villages, farms, and other human (?) inhabitants who have chosen to live outside of your central village. Some of these characters can be recruited to live in your village to fill one of the vacant houses. The music in the game isn't Zelda tune catchy or upbeat fast, but it is good enough and does it's job. The game feels mostly quiet and I don't feel much need to cut the volume off or wear headphones as to not distract the wife while she's sleeping or working, etc. Sound effects are definitely present even though the music seems calm and quiet at times.CONS:The game is unfortunately unfinished and unpolished as of 8/06/21. There are areas that can be seen but not reached, some underground collectibles cannot be dug up due to bug or error, invisible buildings and objects around the inaccessible mine dungeon, an out of place construction sign for the inaccessible beach dungeon. Fully built town feels empty of residents. Bar does nothing. Bugs. Still, I loved this RL Zelda clone.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's so much fun and I've been having an absolute blast. However, there are so many game breaking bugs that happen in both singleplayer and co-op that I just can't bring myself to recommend this game to anyone. My game constantly crashes, my partner frequently gets black screens where he can't see anything at all where my game is fine, the ability wheel gets stuck on the screen and appears in random places permanently, some of the later quests and areas are so bugged that it's just not worth it to play. I want to play the game. Please fix the insane amount of bugs and I will play the crap out of this game.Edit 3/31/22: I finished the game in singleplayer and it was very enjoyable. There are far less bugs in the singleplayer game than in co-op. My partner and I tried playing co-op again after the update that released today and there are still a ton of game breaking bugs. If you just want to play this solo, it's a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I had friends to play this with. Seems it would be amazing with friends!I just solo-completed the story yesterday and through my playthrough, I thoroughly explored everything I could and, got most of it knocked out of the park, so there were very few things to backtrack to or to get some help with a guide.I am down just to the last achievement now, which weirdly enough, ain't even the rarest.The story is simple enough and honestly, wasn't what kept me hooked to the game.It totally was the Link to the Past throwback with enhancements, so my thumbs up.Played through the whole experience on Hard mode (Normal felt like it would be too easy and I didn't feel up to Brutal) and it is a fair challenge until you upgrade damage enough and cut through everything like paper, although for the endless dungeon and the Catacombs the enemies get stronger and spongy as you go deeper.I thoroughly enjoyed the "A Link to the Past" throwback, and while a few things felt like an improvement (Several classes to choose from (although I just played Hero), the many upgrades available, the way you can just swin and much more), another few felt like a total rip-off (bushes, maze rooms in the dark, lamp/torch, rats snakes and bats, and other stuff).I love/hate the Stamina factor. It is a good balance to not have you just mindlessly whacking everything on the spot like you would in ALttP.Rogue Heroes does lack the depth that ALttP would put into dungeon design (for example, how when you get the bow you use it to complete the dungeon and fight the boss, when you get the hammer etc).All of the 4 main dungeons feel somewhat short, while the seem-optional dungeons feel a little bit more thought through or a bit dragged even.I guess some of this is compensated in the fact that the 4 main dungeons appear to be procedurally generated and you get the item at the end of the dungeon (also true for seem-optional dungeon) and it allows you to further navigate the world (as ALttP did), other than that, you get glass items within a dungeon (lose it when you die) to assist you through the dungeon while you don't have the real thing.You don't really lose anything when you die: coin, gems, items (only glass, but you get the real thing as you progress through the game), but you are forced to give up your gems when entering a dungeon, so be sure to spend them real good on your upgrades.Word of advice on this:- Coins are barely used in the game, it is used within the dungeons to unlock chests (which contain gems) and other assists within the dungeon. Coins are easily gathered outside of dungeons rather than within them.- Gems are the other way around: easily gathered within dungeons (no gather outside) and used a lot for your upgrades and unlocking stuff mainly outside of the dungeons.Tavern seems useless in single player.Bosses aren't really complex, I found overall dungeoning and areas putting me through more of a hard time than the bosses did. Boss OST kicks ass though.Talking OST, I SIMPLY LOVE the fact that they used the a couple of free license songs, such as the one in the beach, which is the same for the desert area in Exiled Kingdoms and the one in the fields which is used in some area in Doom & Destiny.In-game bestiary is always a plus, but I don't agree much with their implementation of it, having to smack monsters on a killing blow to get 1st entry of that monster, and again after some kills to "Master" a monster. It is never explained what "Mastering" a monster actually does, so feels like a moot task. You just need 1 kill with the book for each monster entry and to unlock achievement btw - Bosses don't register.I do hate the fishing in this game (controller, didn't try keyboard). It has to be the worst fishing mechanic I have seen to date (and OMG, I played BoF IV, Graveyard Keeper, old school Harvest Moon SNES/PSX, SDV). The only purpose for fishing is unlocking a class and an achievement, and nothing else. You can't eat the fish, you don't use them in recipes, you don't sell them, nothing, nada - actually, just rememberred you can expose them in fish tanks, but really? - Unlocking the class requires 3 different species of 5-star legendary fish, which have better chances in specific spots, which by the way, I got many more of the 5-star legendary fish whatnot than a couple of the species of 3 or 4 star fish I needed for the achievement completion, so that is weird huh.Even with a few of these negatives that I pointed out, I still enjoyed this game pretty much.The asking price is too expensive in my coin (BRL 105,00) and I got a good deal at 90% off, so would advise for the promo.It also features Remote Play Together, which may help to get a coop play going and softening the blow on that price.I guess I may keep this one around after completing achievements and try for a full Brutal playthrough with different classes or as I unlock them and/or try to get a friend onboard on Remote Play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unfinished, and a lot of mechanisms were left half-baked, to where I believe this should still be marked as early-access, and I'm annoyed it just got pushed out the door.Just a few of the things:- Tools are half-baked. There's a punching glove and a hammer that both do the similar function of smashing open new areas. The punching glove is barely ever used. Why??- There's stuff like buying furniture for houses that's a half-baked afterthought. I never even figured out how to add furniture or when heroes move into town and to what purpose...and why??- There's an 'under construction' area in the southwest of the map and some other dead ends and invisible walls...are they even planning on finishing this stuff?- Bugs like floors that are incompletable- Fishing and farming also feels like an afterthought. You end up with more than enough money to spend in dungeons, so there's not much point.I think they had big ambitions to mashup Zelda with Animal Cross and Stardew. The base game is fun - building your character, exploring, unlocking new levels...it all just abruptly accumulates to a point where you've unlocked all these things and realize they go nowhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game quite a bit. I'd like to cover some concerns right off the bat that other users have brought up before. As of the time I write this review, online co-op and multiplayer modes are  Local Co-op (or remote play) works as intended from my experience. Remote play works quite well, not much latency if any at all, however trap switches/ tiles become a bit difficult to see at times due to stream video quality fluctuation. YMMV. Online multiplayer works now, however there are currently some shortcut/ progression issues that can occur. For instance, if one user has certain areas unlocked, they can become unlocked if playing together. These small bugs aside- I would recommend buying the game for it's co-op experience currently.I've only recently discovered this game, but to my knowledge it has been around for a few years. Some users are upset and claim the game is "mislabeled" in regards to it's state of development. I have been around many EA and Indie games and rarely does a title grab my attention like this one has. I think it has a lot of potential to grow, regardless of how the game is "labeled". I try to look at these things at face value, considering some AAA games have been released in the past few years in abysmal fashion. Over the past few weeks the developers seem to be addressing everyone's concerns- and actually promptly implementing said features/ fixes. At the moment, some classes fall a bit short in terms of gameplay, but these are being adjusted as well, and some classes have already seen drastic changes. I would like to see alternate hairstyles and beards, or other braids. Different colored/ tiered (stronger) shields, or have them change shade along with your save badge color. The ability to deconstruct buildings would be nice, perhaps a small % return on gems instead of just deleting the building outright? Also, for multiplayer since the hero's home is replaced by the "hub", a new building like a club house, or a complete redesign of the "hub" would be nice. It is unfortunate you cannot customize your house while playing co-op. The dungeon's difficulty scaling with more players could use an increase, as it becomes a bit easy on some floors with 2+ players. Some puzzles sometimes get repetitive, I hope for more map layouts in the future. Talks of a potential map editor and steam workshop integration seem promising. I am still in the beginning stages of the game, but I am satisfied with the amount of content that I have to explore, give or take a few locations. I am happy there are more areas that will become accessible later on.I was actually on the fence about purchasing this game, with concerns of broken co-op and a unfinished game. What I got was a pleasant surprise, and it will definitely have me coming back for more. The developers swiftly crush bugs and have been working on balancing the game, and that's really nice to see happen so quickly. The game is a lot of fun, but you could potentially get lonely if you play by yourself. At the end of the day, I would rate this game positively, and recommend picking it up- especially if you can nab it on sale.tdlr: Co-op/ multiplayer works, some progression bugs, game is good. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  I love the idea of a co-op Zelda-ish game.  But the game is miserable and grindy to play.  It's difficult in the least satisfying way possible.  If you play slowly and carefully it's generally pretty easy.  So yeah, you play methodically and chip enemies down in a slow, dirgelike rhythym... as the joy of life slowly fades from your body.  But eventually you get bored.  This is inevitable: the enemies have tons of HP (at least with your starting sword) and it's a roguelike so you have to do the same rooms again and again.  And when you get bored you'll try to hurry - try to get an extra hit in on a boring bloody rat who is absolutely uninteresting to fight.  And when you hurry a bit, you'll find that the boring bloody rat's hitbox is a little larger than it seems, or sometimes he won't be knocked back the same way, or the "exhaustion" mechanic means your sword won't swing - and the dumb rat will hit you for a huge chunk of your starter HP.  And so you'll be frustrated and careful for a while, until you get bored again.  Then you'll not properly scan the room for tiles that are one shade darker, and eat another chunk of health to a stupid trap.  Or you'll try to get across one more section of spikes than is safe because you don't want to sit there for another cycle, and the partner you're playing with definitely doesn't want to stand there for another cycle... And then you'll die and realize you have to grind through all that again.Or or or or you'll quit playing and you'll just be saving yourself sadness, because whoever designed this game wants something very different out of a game than I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent 2D Zelda clone that is heavily inspired by the series and more specifically the Four Swords games.  Roguelite elements are also included in the games dungeons with plenty of permanent progression to increase your power and durability as you progress.I currently offer a lite recommendation for the game as it could use some bug patches and content updates/changes to be worth the full price.  Primary issues are listed below.- Online coop desync/bugs- Encountering the same rooms in the randomly generated dungeons too often.  One time i had a dungeon which literally had four of the same large rooms on a floor.- The game is far too easy, especially once you start obtaining a lot of upgrades.- Endgame endless dungeon isn't very enjoyable as it lacks boss encounters and has too many repeated rooms and limited challenge.  It might pick up if you can get extremely far in, but it takes far too long and there are no checkpoints.- The different classes don't feel different enough since at the end of the day the sword is your primary and most powerful reusable tool, which makes whatever class has the most sword damage seemingly the best choice.If the online coop is patched up, then at the very least it will be a fun Zelda-like experience for a group of friends that would be an easy recommendation.  Even if the dungeons can sometimes be a let down with repeating rooms, the game also has a handcrafted overworld to explore and enjoy.  Extra activities like farming and fishing help too, even if they are simple tacked on features.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes Ruins of Tasos will no doubt be a controversial game. Doing something different isn't always going to be clean cut and creating a roguelite game that surrounds itself in Legend of Zelda (specifically A Link to the Past) design mechanics is no easy task. There are going to be plenty of people that will adore it for its charm and creative design as well as its polished fundamentals. Other people will harp on the cosmetic bugs, broken online multiplayer, and under delivering on some of the games features. The game does have its charm, and it is far from a disaster, but the truth is that it could have used more time both in bug cleanup before launch, but also is design. Many of the features feel like they were tacked on as after thoughts and were not well thought through on how they would impact other elements of the game. In the end the game feels like two games in one, and both of them are decent.Overall, I think this game won't be for everyone, but personally, I enjoyed it and recommend this toad for anyone that understands its warts. Sure there are things in this game aren't spectacular, but it was fun to play none-the-less, and succeeded in keeping my attention for the many hours I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best games I've played in a long time. However, keep in mind that I'm an age old Zelda fan and A Link To The Past is one of my favorites, in which this game was largely inspired. The pixel art is awesome, the story is simple but great, the other characters all serve a significant role and most importantly this game perfectly blends the methods of a Zelda game with the Rogue-lite formula. This game in some cases may be even better than many Zelda games because it has very fun and unique puzzles that are extremely creative. Plus, the replay value is off the charts. Starting as a regular swordsman but eventually unlocking several more classes, items, and abilities which will keep it fresh for a long time. Also this game has somethings that are not randomly generated, like the over-world, meanwhile inside each dungeon its randomly generated meaning each time you die, you have to redo the dungeon or parts of it but its never the same one twice. This game is fun alone, but really thrives with at least one other friend. Finally, the boss fights are fantastic. Many games have over scripted bosses or they're super easy and just have giant health bars. This game doesn't waste your time with scripted bosses, they're classic. They come at your with their attack patterns and only hold back with just enough time for you to hit it after it wreaks havoc on you. They're crazy funAll that in mind, if you don't like rogue lites, RPGs, or Zelda games. This may not be for you. I'd suggets being a fan of at least 2/3 of those. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: We got the game on sale for a few bucks, so by default I think I got my moneys worth out of it. However it felt like I experienced the two polar opposite ends of the spectrum with this game: some really fun multiplayer shenanigans with my friend that pushed us to keep playing AND THEN frustration from the game continuously glitching out to the point where we had to edit our save data to recover all the spheres that magically disappeared from the inventories. The base game has a lot of potential but it's obvious the developers stretched themselves too thin just because the amount of half-baked ideas. Yeah technically the game has farming, but it super barebones and provides no real benefit besides money which gets obsolete later in the game. Classes don't feel balanced at all, some movement abilities are clearly better than others, plus the small stats don't make too much sense. This game could really benefit from some QoL changes like a minimap that updates over time with new areas and collectibles you've already collected. Unfortunately while looking up stuff on the Steam forums, it's pretty apparent this game is dead as there have been no updates or even communication from the developers on the state of the game. For the sale price, I think it's worth a quick look with friends since a 2D Zelda roguelite with multiplayer sounds fun, but for $20 you can find better singleplayer/multiplayer experiences. Very conflicted with this review, because I think I can recommend it since we ended up finishing it, but your miles will absolutely vary.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a whole bunch of great and miserable aspects combined. Sadly, there is too much frustrating stuff, which ultimately leads me to this review.Let's start with the great:- you have the option to change classes at will and are not bound to one after choosing. the classes are not too different (often the only changes are speed, attack and magic as well as a small ability)- the dungeons are a lot of fun, the bosses are cool too- exploration is amazing. you unlock different things along the way that make it possible to get into new areas. going back to a biome you've explored before often still ends in new findings- both palyers end up with the same amount of loot from dungeons, no matter if or when then die- when purchasing something that is for all palyers, everyone can chip in, which is a nice idea imo- leveling up is great, you have many many skill trees to upgrade and can freely choose what you want to put your money in- there are quite a number of side quests to doWhile this all sounds pretty good, it's put into perspective by all of the game's flaws:- if you play with controller, your characer will often still follow the comands when you are in the inventory, which is a HUGE annoyance- the map is sometimes weirdly split into screens and you keep jumping between two "frames" because this slip is so awkward- the game is a BUGGY MESS in general- it happened to us that after a "frame" switch, we suddenly were not able to interact with anything. we were able to walk through anything, couldn't deal nor take damage- we were often teleported to a completely different part of the map when we exited a cave for some reason. this happeend more than once. because we were not supposed to be in that biome, we were not able to exit naturally and had to restart the game in order to  keep playing- quite often, you don't really know what to do or how to do it. you are given tools and have to learn by accident what you can use them for. or you have to go somewhere, finally make it after solving an environmental puzzple of sorts, only to realise that you can still not continue.The bugs are honestly what annoy me most. some of them make the whole gaming experience and especially the multiplayer very frustrating. as a game that is pretty much meant to be played as a multiplayer, that is disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of underwhelming experience of game. To preface this, I have not played any sort of legend of zelda topdown games but have watched gameplay of them. The exploration part of the game in the over world is really dull and there's hardly any interesting npcs that you meet or puzzles to do other than shoveling for treasures. The puzzles in the dungeon were definitely designed to be played with 2 or more people as it will take forever to complete by yourself, even though you will get the 1 player version of them. Further in the game in dungeon 3 and 4, there were puzzles where it was clearly impossible to complete solo showing lack of polish in this game. To further this issue on the game's polish, I got locked after defeating the second boss because he was underground and not in enrage form before he died. After beating the final boss, the game rewarded me with absolutely nothing useful other than an amusing bug where the NPCs dialogue didnt trigger properly and gave me a weird message after interacting them from behind. It fixed itself after I reentered there area. I've included a picture of the encounter here. The game gives you too many tools that are straight up clogging up the usefuls ones you need, taking forever to swap to the one you need if you dont use the menu. If the dev's actually play tested this fully they should really have made a function to remove useless tools that are not needed currently in the swap bar. The only tools i found useful outside of their interaction for puzzles were the fireball wand because of its fire debuff DOT and range. You get spells like magic missile and frostbolt but those are just garbage spells you find in the overworld. The other tools than the wand just take too much gems to be good when you need to pump a lot of gems into your sword which is your main damage dealer.The other classes are absolutely useless other than the knight with his ridiculous stats, apparently their fixing this in a later patch to make the classes gimmick's actually work. You dont really unlock any cool techniques like I've seen in zelda game like the spin move or having ranged slashes at max health. _childDocuments_.review: With the time I've spent on this game. I think I'm able to give my point of view on it. I've completed the game (as far as defeating the last boss currently available) and may delve into some optional content.Although I'm currently recommending this game, it is not without its many, many issues. Please don't take my words as a personal swing; that is not my intention. I just want people to know what to expect if purchasing this game.I'll start with the cons first then follow with the pros:1. The desyncs. I didn't have it terribly bad but I've heard some bad scenarios. The worst I got was that I was forced to run the first dungeon three times cause my friend kept glitching through the door right at the end. Other than that, most of our desyncs have been in the overworld; mainly he wasn't able to destroy the bushes so he was stuck while I almost had to go off camera every time just to get to the next zone. I put this at number 1 because it is a major issue, though with word that it's being addressed, it likely won't be a thing soon.2. This is a very dumb-downed look-a-like of Legend of Zelda. Everything feels cheap and not really unique. I'm honestly convinced that the "Procedural" Dungeons actually harmed the game way more than it helped it. Too many rooms, enemies and puzzles are recycled from dungeon to dungeon. I've seen the same areas likely over ten times in my playthrough. Hell, I've faced the same skeleton mobs in all four major dungeons (haven't touched the Endless Abyss yet). My personal recommendation was for the dungeons to be static and be unique to their themes. The Procedural bit could've been an Extra after beating the game or just tied to the Endless Abyss.3. Nothing was a challenge. My buddy and I decided to not pick up any health upgrades at all to even give ourselves some possibility of dying. The second we did though, nothing could even come close to killing us. The most difficult boss, simply because we had nothing at that time, was the first boss.  I feel that the upgrade system kind of made this game too easy since every dungeon seems to be geared towards if you don't have many upgrades at all. Even when we beat the final boss, I literally said to him "That's it?". It just doesn't feel satisfying at all.4. The puzzles were a joke. I don't consider myself smart, but some of these "puzzles" are just simply: Go stand here and there. I'll give some credit, some puzzles had me think for over five seconds, but those were the rooms where the entire thing was a puzzle. Those were the ones where I felt the most rewarded, and that's not a good sign.5. The Overworld was a wasted opportunity. Not only was it even easier than the dungeons, but apart from doing specific quests and exploring for the sake of "hey! what's over here?" It's almost completely pointless. Every time a dungeon was finished, I could not wait to get to the next one and once more, the same bit was recycled again (You can't proceed cause you need X item, go find it in this remote part of the area or talk to a fella, then come back and now you can do it). Honestly the swamp area felt the most unique of the four.6. And the bugs, by jolly, the bugs. Most of it I imagine I can contribute it to the desyncs, but I've encountered issues such as getting stuck randomly on objects, clipping through walls and, without even trying to glitch the system, walking on water. That's not a good sign when one part of the world basically just transforms you into Jesus and the only way to save yourself is to run against a specific cliff.Boy that was a lot of negatives, so why am I even recommending this? Well...Pros:1. Despite all the failings and missed opportunities, I enjoyed the ride with my buddy and may play again with others in the future. It is a good game to play with your friend(s), mainly to hang out and laugh, love and live. It's nothing that's going to make you sweat as failing means you can come back even stronger so you can relax while playing this one.2. For 20$? There's little that you can go wrong here. I've got 9ish hours at the time of this review and that's with me beating the base game and doing I'd imagine most of the optional content.3. Maybe I'm a fool, but I have a soft-spot for these kinds of games and the fact that these fellas even attempted something like this makes me happy. I've always enjoyed games like A Link to the Past and more-so Four Swords Adventure. I guess I could call this one of my guilty pleasures.4. Most of the major issues I've mentioned (such as the desyncs and bugs), are being addressed so I imagine in due time, they will be fixed and the game will be far more stable. Anything about the difficulty or gameplay I've mentioned honestly can be more opinion-based. Your experiences will differ from mine; you may like what I didn't.That is my review! Good luck to the team behind this and I hope for the best of them.-Wigglezz

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes is a criminally overlooked indie title, and it's easily one that deserves more active players and continued support. Building off the foundation laid down by Link to the Past decades earlier, this game improves on LttP's gameplay elements in every way. Fluid movement, wide and aimable attacks, useful tools (in both traversal *and* combat), varied class abilities, and more! The overworld is also designed around these elements, with tons of secrets and extra items scattered around its many environmental areas. Add in some engaging randomized dungeons and much-needed skill tree options, and you have an indie game that will satisfy adventure fans for a long time to come. My issues with Rogue Heroes are mostly nitpicks, so I'll list them below rather that include them in the review proper, but I will mention that the music leaned more atmospheric than memorable. It's not bad by any means, but I'd be hard pressed to remember much of anything outside of the main village theme. Regardless, this is a must-play for any roguelite fans or Zelda-style adventure-game enthusiasts, *especially* if you're looking for the perfect co-op game (multiplayer, whether local or online, makes this game 150% better). Now, I think I should provide some constructive criticism on some nitpicks I have with this title. As of early January 2023, I'm still waiting on an update to fix these issues (and I hope the developers will stick with Rogue Heroes long enough to see it perfected):- No controller configuration is a HUGE oversight. The default controller configuration is pretty good, but not having *any* kind of customization for that is a significant fault on the part of the developers.- There is also a lack of Quality of Life features, although not with the core gameplay as much as the unique content. Little annoyances like a severe lack of Power Stone markers on the map (once you've obtained each stone), the map not updating with in-game terrain changes, not being able to move houses or clear unused land in the village. This little things add up over a complete playthrough, and can be more than a bother if you're going for 100% completion.- I was additionally disappointed to find out that completing the Fishing Log, Farming Quest, and mastering the Bestiary only rewards you with an achievement, instead of a useful in-game item or ability.  - The online multiplayer has some glitchy bugs, especially when players don't have the strongest connection possible. I've run into some serious warping and screen-blackout issues on occasion, when playing with friends.- There are a handful of rooms that have some needlessly complicated or time-strict puzzles that should not gatekeep progression in the dungeons. Rooms in Fyrotek Castle and the (optional) fish dungeon come to mind.- This is a reach, but there is (sadly) no risk/reward mechanics for the tavern minigames, which makes them nearly useless (beyond an initial run of each minigame).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving Rogue Heroes a thumbs up because there is a lot to like about the game, and I want it to succeed. But the game has its flaws, and it still feels like early access.Pros:- Large overworld that's fun to explore and full of secrets.- Engaging gameplay loop of dungeon crawling and upgrading in town.- Strong Legend of Zelda: a Link to the Past vibes with a roguelite and co-op twist.- Online co-op lets you explore with friends.- Active developers who listen to the community, fix bugs, and make the game better.Cons:- Feels like early access.- Some items are almost never used and feel pointless.- Meta progression easily gets out of hand and takes away the challenge.- Bosses, puzzles, and dungeons feel too simple.- The story and the NPCs are completely uninteresting.- Playable character classes all feel the same.- A few soft locks and one crash to desktop over 18 hours of play. (Reported to devs, who seem good about fixing bugs.)The randomized dungeon layouts are a major design choice that I feel is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it keeps things fresh as you replay a dungeon, which is part of the roguelite experience. On the other hand, it means that every room is self-contained and can be fully understood and solved in isolation. The rooms never work together, for example having to enter a room from different sides to solve it, or activating a switch in one room to affect another. The result is dungeons that feel simple and random rather than interesting.I really want to love this game. There is a lot to like, such as the overworld, where I had many hours of fun exploring. However, I'm hesitant to recommend the game in its current state. If you want to enjoy some of the Link to the Past nostalgia, or go dungeon crawling with friends for a bit, this game is fine. Nothing amazing, but you can get 10-15 hours of enjoyment out of it, which to me is worth the price.If you're looking for outstanding dungeon and puzzle design you'd be better off with an RPG like Cross Code. For outstanding roguelite co-op combat, I'd just go play Children of Morta again, where the bosses are challenging and all the characters feel very different to play.

_childDocuments_.review: What you expect in the best ways possible.---Going in, I was concerned that the game would be too simple and too much of a Zelda clone, and while it does have those hallmarks - looking at you, hookshot - Rogue Heroes has me enamored. The randomized dungeons haven't gotten old after 10+ hours and the natural progression of the game allows you to pursue other things if a particular venture is boring you. That simple Zelda styled feeling of reward when you explore, discover, and ultimately return to areas with new abilities and knowledge to unlock things you missed previously are all here. Is it cheap and easy? Yes. Does it work every time? Yes.Playing solo is plenty of fun, and I never felt like I was missing out on anything by not having party members. That being said, I could totally see this being a go-to couch co-op staple; the party dynamic and dungeon crawling is very reminiscent of Gauntlet, and I'm quite tempted to rope some friends into this one.Some of the life-sim elements are fairly underwhelming, however, and really prevent the game from having that ultimate RPG feel. Farming is dirt simple (get it?), home decorating is tacked on, and the inability to customize your character's appearance beyond skin tone, hair colour, and cloak colour is quite disappointing - especially for a game with 4 potential friends' personalities running around on the screen at once.The story is completely forgettable, but to the game's credit, it is not at all the focus here, and thankfully, any mention of the story is kept short, so you and your potential party members won't be stuck reading paragraphs when you'd rather be dungeon delving. Just the standard fare of something evil corrupting the land, and you, the chosen hero(es) are here to restore things to pleasantry; it's all just an excuse to set up the exploration-action-adventure you came here for.Far and away my favourite idea the game has is to force the players to lose their gems in order to enter a dungeon. At first, you will recoil at the notion of losing your loot, but this subtle requirement creates a fantastic pace to the game and its progression by incentivising you to spend your wealth on upgrades or buildings rather than horde it. After all, the few gems you'll be unable to spend that get lost to enter a dungeon are made back after clearing a room or two, so once again, the players are encouraged to attempt long, deep runs through the dungeons in order to maximize the profits.Overall, this is a well thought-out game that captures that nostalgic feeling of when games were complete on release, polished, co-op, and simple fun. Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos doesn't break the mold much on the classic old-school Nintendo RPG format, but it doesn't really have to when the formula is as tried and true as this. Despite this game deriving obvious inspiration from the pixel Zelda games, I - a not so huge Zelda fan - find myself struggling not to spend all of my free time playing this game. I'm just over 10 hours in and there feels to be around 20+ more hours of content, making the price here an easy purchase.If you dare to give it a try, I doubt you'll regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've absolutely loved playing this game in multiplayer, however there are quite a few desync bugs that have made my friends and I have to re-do puzzles or restart the game entirely. Solo-play is pretty fun, but a lot of the puzzle elements are dumbed-down so that a single player can solve them, making the dungeon crawling a little less interesting. I have always loved endless-upgrades style games and Zelda games so this is really scratching an itch for me, but the bugginess of multiplayer has been making it harder and harder to enjoy. The developers are not addressing the multiplayer bug issues at all and I wouldn't expect them to be fixed in the future. I do hope they prove me wrong on that because this game has great potential, but in its current state I can't really recommend it unless it's on a really big discount. Even then, expect to run into issues where you may have to re-do puzzles or quit and relaunch the game. There's even bugs where if you progress too far before trying to finish a quest the quest isn't complete-able (I'm lookin' at you, farmer dude).

_childDocuments_.review: Not a functional game, very fun gameplay but horribly broken.You will encounter bugs all the time, specially as you progress further. Bugs which either softlock you or force you to reopen the game and lose progress.Here's some of the many bugs me and my co-op partner met during our 12h play session:* Game has constant issues with desync during co-op. * Game will constantly and randomly warp you to lategame areas where you have no way of leaving, forcing you to restart the game to respawn at the bed. Easily reproduceable if either player plays Thief, for some reason the game breaks whenever you play that fast class.* Druid is also unplayable on co-op. If co-op player attacks while Druid is shapeshifted, the Druid also attacks. It WILL get you killed because Squirrel has a lunge attack, and you will be forcefully lunged at enemies.* Game aiming with magic is broken, focusing targets far away and ignoring targets in front of you. No way to turn off.* Game will desync badly if both of you try building something at the same time.* Game dungeon puzzles can softlock you, forcing you to restart the game not to complete the puzzle, but to leave the puzzle room itself.* Aside from the 4 main dungeons, all optional dungeons have no revives for co-op. Hilarious because the Reaper class is a co-op focused class and one of its upgrades is to make it easier to be revived.* Game will desync badly for no reason randomly.Now if that wasn't annoying enough, you WILL get warped to random locations every 30 minutes when leaving a cave. It just happens more consistently with fast moving classes but happens regardless. Exploring a new area but found a cave? Pray it doesn't lead to you being thrown on a glitchy ocean forcing you to restart your game and having to backtrack all the way from where you left off.The game is just barely playable on co-op. I'm sure it works better on single player but co-op is just broken in all sorts of ways. Really cute graphics and really fun to play, but the sheer amount of bugs you will encounter make it too frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun to play with friends.  It's a great LoZ experience with multiplayer aspects that makes the game challenging and fun.  The puzzles aren't too difficult but remain fun to solve with the presence of enemies to interrupt your problem solving attempts.  The world is interesting and fun to explore with a plethora of upgrades for your gear.  A nice QoL that make the game even better is that it tracks quest progress for everyone in the session.  You don't have to worry about repeating missions in your own game (unless a bug pops up which I'll get into shortly).  All in all, a fun game worth the price tag.  Though the game is great, there are a few things that still need to be ironed out and hopefully soon.See, despite all of that good stuff, it's still pretty rough around the edges with its multiplayer.  My friends and I have encountered a couple funny glitches and that's all fine and dandy, but the worst offender of a bug is when the game decides not to auto save quest rewards.  If you suddenly have connection issues or have to drop from the game without being able to select "save and quit", chances are high you will lose out on the reward and it's happened a couple of times to date.  Now, the game keeps track of quest progress for ALL members regardless of who's hosting as I mentioned.  However, in my case I lost out of a quest reward and cannot repeat the quest (because Comcast is awful).  It was a pretty significant item but won't mention it in this review.  If you can get over the hurdle of risking your quest rewards online, I wholeheartedly recommend this game to fans of LoZ, and those that want to get into this kind of game.  Take care and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a charming yet imbalanced action-adventure game that leans heavily on its dungeon-crawling roots. The difficulty curve feels uneven, starting out challenging but becoming easier as you accumulate damage upgrades, which eventually mitigate many of the threats you'll face. This progression can make the game feel less rewarding as you become overpowered fairly quickly.The game offers five main dungeons, each with a boss at the end, alongside an endless dungeon for players seeking additional content. The overworld includes puzzles and quests that unlock new character classes. However, I found this to be the weakest part of the experience, as I was more interested in jumping straight into dungeon action with friends than solving overworld puzzles.That said, Rogue Heroes truly shines when played with friends. The cooperative multiplayer elevates the experience, and if you enjoy teaming up to tackle dungeons, it's easy to recommend. For solo players, there’s still value if you find the core gameplay in the demo enjoyable, but the experience is undoubtedly more engaging with a group.All in all, Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos has some pacing issues but offers a fun co-op experience, especially for fans of dungeon-crawling action.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Fun game that can be played with friends both online and locally but DO NOT spend more than a couple bucks on it, either wait for a 90% discount here on Steam (that's how I got it and I suspect it gets discounted regularly) or get a key from the usual key dealers. It's unfinished, full of bugs (some inconvenient, some gamebreaking) and apparently abandoned, if the price gets lowered to around 5€ this could've possibly been a positive review but I just cannot reccomend it for 20€I won't point out all the negatives simply beacause there's so many that I just can't remember all of them, just know that there's issues with pacing and clunkiness and a lot of bugs, this is essentially an early access title with some unfinished content that never got added/fixed for some reason, you can still get 100% completion thoughI never tried out co-op personally, only single player, so my thoughts are mostly relevant for single playerSome of the most problematic bugs and design issues:-The randomly generated dungeons can bug out and softlock you, either by spawning chests that block your movement or by failing to generate doors to other rooms (happened to me in te 4th one), both prevent you from progressing and force you to abandon the run (=the same as dying and respawning) from the main menu-Sometimes you can't get out of the water, the docks simply don't work and you are forced to wait for your stamina to run out and die. Water exploration is unclear and sketchy even when it works, could use some more guidance-Ranged combat is very unpolished and underdeveloped, you can't aim precisely and the projectiles fly all over the place, it's just not worth the effort and basically never needed, it's not unusable by any means but unless you want to challenge yourself on purpose there's no reason to ever use your bow or wand for anything other than dealing minor chip damage when your enemy is too far for your sword to reach-Some things are just never explained or explained incorrectly and cannot be figured out unless you stumble upon them randomly or specifically look for guides online, I'm mostly referring to I liked most of the secondary, non-randomly-generated dungeons and some of the bosses, especially the , the general mechanics and gameplay loop are fun which makes sense considering it's essentially the exact same as the classic 2D Zelda games

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start of by saying i WANT to leave a Thumbs up.. But i can't.Let's start with the good! The graphics are cute, and animations are beautiful. This gives HUGE Legeng Of Zelda: Link To The Past vibes and it's so much fun to play. It has some pretty simple mechanics, but the retro style of gameplay actually keeps the game Semi challenging.. mainly because i'm an idiot and i like to run into enemies..The village building aspect of it is cute, and i like the idea of being able to build up your town with new NPC's who can sell different items to help you along your adventure. I like the idea that you only gain gems and currency AFTER you have been killed in a dungeon.. but.. this leads to a problem which i will talk about later in the review.Multiplayer is so much fun! Playing this game with friends adds some more depth to the game, as it increases the dungeons difficulty, depending on how many people are playing. Also, throwing things at eachother is so much fun to do. Because the other player automatically catches the item, it's fun to catch them off guard! though that being said.. Throwing a bomb when it is 1 second away from blowing up and your friend catching it is... well.. it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny. When a player dies they have the ability to float around as a ghost and posses items that they can throw at enemies once they get close enough, and the resurrection aspect of the game is great, giving players a chance to redeem themselves! But.. don't play catch with their skulls too much.. if you throw their skull.. it can break.. leaving your friend a moaning, floaty ghost forever! It's pretty fun.. But.. this is only when the Multiplayer works..Now.. the bad..The De-Sync and Disconnection issues in this game are absolutely unforgivable. And i know, everyone and their dog is complaining about this. It wouldn't be SO bad.. if you didn't lose EVERYTHING when you get disconnected. If you've just collected a total of 1400+ gems in a dungeon and you get disconnected.. yeah, say goodbye to those gems. THAT'S the most infuriating part of it.  This is also the reason i haven't had a chance to defeat any bosses. I don't want to play this game on my own, i want to play it with friends.. But i can't even reach the boss without being disconnected.Opening your inventory forces the game to pause for everyone else.. Why? I literally do not understand this design choice. it's annoying, and it makes you feel like you can't check your inventory, or the bestiary to read about enemies without the risk of annoying whoever you are playing with. It just seems very counter productive. This also goes hand in hand with talking to NPC's. As this too, will stop the game for everyone else, and actually is one of the main causes of the game Soft Locking, causing everyone to need to restart and rejoin he game. And this NPC is right at the very beginning of the game.. Not something that should be present in an early access game.. let alone a full release.As soon as these connection issues and De-Sync issues are fixed, this game will be perfect and i'll absolutely change my review.i would like to say.. The fact this game was made by two people is astounding. I do not want to discredit the work they have done so far, it's amazing.. But these issues NEED to be addressed, as i'm sure they will be in future. It's just a shame i bought this game on day 1 release, and can't play it as much as i really want to.Also, There is a discord for this game. Don't dare go in there and tell them of the problem.. because they will defend the fact they got given a broken game, and then they will kick you :) Pretty dope place.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good faith recommend this to anyone. TLDR: Game is very short on content and the content that is there is bland and uninspired.There's very little content in pretty much all aspects of the game. Also the class system was clearly an afterthought and adds nothing since every class still uses a sword and you play at a huge disadvantage if you pick one of the classes with low sword damage since it's still stronger than your magic. It's also impossible to reasonably switch to a melee class since you've already invested points into the lamest skill tree I've seen in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Online co-op's got sooooo many bugs! I even unlocked the winter zone after exiting a cave even if we were soooo behind in the story. We've also lost progress so many times due to the game glitching out of nothing. As much as I've enjoyed the first few hours of the game, I never could bring myself to feel ''safe'' after hardcore grinding since I never knew when it would be the next time we'd glitch again. It felt like there'd be no reward at the end of the tunnel (literally).The only away I could say I enjoyed my time spent here was because I was playing it with my friends. Otherwise it'd be a HUGE NOPE for me. I wouldn't even have bothered to buy it in the first place, if it wasn't for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 4/3/22: I waited over a year before revisiting this game and I must say, I'm so glad I gave it another shot! My friend and I had no issues in online co-op. We had an absolute blast playing and still have so much content to get through! Overall I'm very happy with the game and definitely can recommend it now!As it is, I can't recommend it. Especially if, like me, you were wanting to play it with friends. The co-op is so broken. We played roughly an hour and in that time it broke twice to the point of having to exit out of the game and restart. If you're looking to play this single player it may be fine but I can't say for sure since this isn't a game I personally want to play alone. All in all it seems fun and like it has a good amount of content. I really hope the devs will fix the multiplayer issues and I will definitely update my review if/when they do!

_childDocuments_.review: The multiplayer is horrible since everytime anyone pauses the entire game pauses for everyone. You also have to stay on the same screen at all times. The online coop feels like you're playing coop and is not taking advantage of the fact that everyone is running this on their own machine.But even with these flaws this is such a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little Zelda-like Rogue-like game.  I enjoyed the gameplay, exploration, and advancement aspects of it. It isn't really deep or difficult like most Rogue-likes which eventually made it grow stale a little quicker than I would have expected.Pros: Zelda style gameplay, co-op mode, feeling of progression and lots of options of how to grow stronger.Cons: Endless dungeon is buggy as all get out.  I had one floor that I needed a key and there was none to be found (likely enemy drop that fell to narnia). I had another floor where I seemed to get put underneath the layer of where the objects I needed to interact with were. After 2 runs that ended with me having to suicide to leave the dungeon, I just stopped trying.I do think this game is worth getting on sale. I enjoyed my time with it...the bugs were only one part of the game that wasn't necessary for enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good game to play with a friend (or up to three friends), an interesting set of puzzles in multiple procedurally generated dungeons (adapts to the number of players), large variety of enemies to fight plus bosses which will surely kill you on your first attempt (at least!). There are several zones across the world map (your typical grass/snow/lava/jungle etc), as well as a home hub which is your main source of progression by constructing buildings for different NPCs in order to acquire new quests, new classes and to level your stats and equipment.If it's on deal and you're in the market for a new co-op that's easy to jump in, definitely grab it - you'll get a good number of hours play and all of which will be great co-op fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this one and look forward to them finishing the remaining areas because I'd like to play more of this game.I purchased this on sale along with the Bomber DLC class. It plays similar to "The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past" but the right stick attacks in the pressed direction allowing you to attack while you retreat. I used the Bomber DLC class, which can also kick bombs like "Bomberman," until I replaced it with Knight and later, my favorite, Reaper. Total playtime at time writing is just over 26 hours, local co-op with my son plays well but the screen expands too slowly leaving you vulnerable at screen edge and we had issues with quest progress since we didn't start from scratch together. Even when his character was P1 and we were using his town my progress threw some events off.The game appears to have been made by a two person dev team and right now feels like it was finished just enough to release, but it lacks polish. There are four areas that are locked out on the map, or are only partially accessible, that appear to be for future expansions, but the Kezar Fist could just be replaced by the hammer and Mastery of the Book of Beasts doesn't feel rewarding yet, for example.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure that this type of game appeals to certain people, but I am not one of them. The gameplay grew repetitive and rote fairly quickly, and was a mix between very easy and very difficult rooms. The city management and roguelike aspects could have been fun, but they were fairly simplistic filler between different dungeon runs.  The exploration was nothing to write home about, and the different characters had little discernible differences between them. There are many other games in the genre that you should go to before this one.
