_childDocuments_.review: If I have to be honest... the game is honestly not the best. I've been playing this with some friends of mine, and even though all 3 of us have fairly good PC's, one of them seems to keep getting stuck between doors repeatedly to the point where he had to basically stop playing with us. As for me and the one friend, we have managed to get soft-locked in ridiculous situations a total of 2 times....The idea of the dungeons is cool and all, but some of the weapons end up being completely worthless to use, to the point the only real weapons to kind of use is Sword, Grappling Hook, and Wand. The music isn't anything to write about. at least the boss music is decent, and the Froggy music is probably the best theme in the entire game.... and It's only played in that one Mud part of the game. Oh... and I almost forgot... there is no cross platforming so if you have a friend on a PS4- PS5, or a Nintendo Switch, or any console related game, you will not be able to play with them. Overall, this game is absolutely meh... I'd give it a 5/10 or a solid C grade. the soft-locks are just random and kind of funny at the same time... but I'd say... play it with friends. It's more fun if everyone enjoys the random stuff the game has to offer you.

_childDocuments_.review: I played solo. Its a nice little distraction for a few hours, a mix of classic zelda with the breath of the wild stamina system. Though it is short if your decent at the game. Theres 4 dungeons to conquer and then a final boss fight. Currently there are 3 dungeons that have not been released yet but those are optional. Its not a really deep game and if your looking for a crafting system look elsewhere. Its possible to grind one of the additional dungeons for fast gems and max all stats making the game much eaiser. I did not have the DLC bomber class to rate that however all classes have their own stats and one special move which is usually a charge/dash of some sort. Id advise against the bomber class even though I didnt play it on the grounds of classes being almost the same and the base ranger class being more then enough to beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Multiplayer Zelda (but the puzzles are easy) and it's pretty buggy. Also make sure to play with friendsI got this at a deep discount, and I probably would not have paid full price if I knew nothing. After playing through juuust about the whole game and DLC, I'd recommend it for the full price (and I'm a cheapskate!). For the skeptics, let's start with the cons.Cons:It's buggy. Very. There will be game breaking stuff, there will be funny ones, take that as you will. It only detracted from my playing experience once or twice, and the rest of the time it was funny to me and my friends.Difficulty is wack, and so is balance. Certainly feels as though some classes (and upgrades) are a better choice, but it doesn't detract from the gameplay imo. This game is at its most fun when you're playing it casually, and trolling your friends a little. I think we played it on the difficulty above base, and it felt like a healthy challenge.UI is also a lil wack, but with some practice it's managable. Devs if you're reading this, I think this is a pretty simple fix. Maybe be a little more transparent about what the book does as well? I wasn't able to find an answer online on the benefit of "mastering". Generally, be more transparent with stats and all the like, gamers will love it. I understand it's difficult to toe the line of simplistic design and informative HUDS, but maybe add some hover effects :^)Pros:THE IDEA ITSELF! Multiplayer roguelike zelda is an excellent gimmick. Super fun with a full lobby of friends, but I can't imagine it'd be too much fun singleplayer.An adorable art style I love. We had a player who had no mic, and the expressiveness of the characters and emotes were enough to send us reeling. The soundtrack is pretty good, but nothing to write home about. Sound effect design, and the overall satisfying bits of the game really give the aesthetic its pop and make you feel rewarded when you pick up good stuff.Some humorous moments, albeit rarely from the story. There are some goofy mechanics you'll love if you aren't taking the game *too* seriously. Frog flute is the pinnacle of game design. You will laugh playing this game if you have the right people. Troll your friends a little, this game makes it soooooo easy.A playpace that knows exactly how to toe the line of exploration and progression. It's easy enough you'll probably always know what to do next, but the game rewards you a lot for exploring the massive open world, and it's an awesome break from when you're tired of the main quest. It's also got achievements and collectibles that will entertain the collectathon fan/achievement hunter for hours more than the game itself. You don't have to be grindy, but you certainly can be.Overall, a great game! PLAY WITH FRIENDS!

_childDocuments_.review: Game just does not work for multiplayer.  Constant lagging, glitchy camera, etc.  At one point one of my friends got slightly desynced from the rest of us and had us constantly warping 3 rooms back where he was unable to move any longer.  Honestly, even if it weren't for this the game is kinda meh.  Classes have practically no point to them beyond slight stat changes and a movement ability that I honestly never found a use for.  Dungeons are randomly generated and run on a rougelite system of upgrades, but none of the upgrades is in the slightest bit interesting.  Pretty much just minor stat boosts.  Movement is to fast and slippery so you end up running into enemies when you don't mean too.  I payed 2 bucks for this on sale and I kind of feel like even that was a rip off.

_childDocuments_.review: I heavily recommend this game. It truly feels like a 2D Zelda game in the style of A Link to the Past. Combat feels great, progression feels great, and the world has a lot of personality. Music, graphics, and level design work together well to create the world. The Rogue-lite elements are used really well without making things too repetitive. A sort-of Stardew Valley style town-building system keeps you motivated to collect more and more gems.

_childDocuments_.review: Can I give it two thumbs up? One does not seem like enough! I wish I payed full price for this game I enjoyed it that much. I guess I will settle for buying copies for friends on sale to spread the love for this game! It has so many things I enjoy in a game such as class changes, town building, an expansive, fun world to explore, fishing and farming, though optional as well as having a Zelda like approach to dungeons and landscapes but still feeling like it's own world. It is funny though I did not learn about certain aspects of the classes till near end of the game. I didn't know the reaper can roll and be immune to spikes and such using his movement ability. Man all the spike deaths I could have been spared! Or that the witch could fly over them with her broom or the pirate can do so as well with his bird. So many class aspects I overlooked but now that I have completed the main part of the game it makes me want to go in and do the other dungeons I didn't finish with different classes. See how far I can get with a class out of my comfort zone. You can die in a dopey way at times but  it has this great Hades feel to where even if you die you progress because you keep gems to buy abilities and such. I started this game playing in an online group and that was fun as well. It can make the dungeon's more challenging puzzle wise but also can make you laugh as you lug your dead friends head back to a raise point. This is a a game I know I am going to keep going back to over time. Heck I am fighting the urge to get back into it now because I am writing this! I have beaten it and yet still have much left to do if I want to and I actually want to! There is one thing I will say that I did kind of blunder. After you get to a point where you can go into an endless dungeon. I thought I had to go through at least 25 levels to get to the last boss because I saw the achievement for 25 levels... well I got to 26 and no go... thankfully I looked it up after and found out all I had to do was walk into the statue at the start of the endless abyss and you get to the last boss... derrrp. On the 26th floor after getting the achievement I just went to the entrance of that floor walked into the statue and beat that sob! Well least I got an achievement! ^_^ I will definitely try to get 100 for this game as an excuse to get back in and to display it on my profile page.   Do not miss out on this adventure. Also expansions have come out for it already with additonal classes and areas so its an ever expanding world. You can't lose with this one in my opinion. Do yourself a favor and give Rogue Heroes a try! P.S if you are going to fish I looked up a video on it and doing it with a keyboard even though I played the game with a controller was a lot easier for anyone getting frustrated with it. Good luck and enjoy the game!  Remember when games were fun? This is one of those kinda games! ^_~

_childDocuments_.review: A heavily inspired Zelda-like, rpg-lite, puzzle-dungeon, rogue-lite adventure with its own unique twists that successfully make it stand on its own. It is charming, fun, very addictive and surprisingly casual for the amount of deaths you will encounter. Some slight grinding is required, but does not feel like work! Dying forces you to spend your collected gems and gems equal upgrades! Upgrades mean less dying, therefore the fun lasts longer! Lots to do and explore and the forced world progress keeps things locked away just out of reach to make the gameplay loop bring you back for more to make yourself more powerful at every step of the way.Quite lengthy if you really allow yourself to explore every nook and cranny of this delightful journey.

_childDocuments_.review: The price is why I recommend this game. The story was pretty fun to follow along with and the dungeons were pretty good. While the bosses were a bit lack luster, I would still say this game was worth the money. Me and my buddy put ~20 hours in and we both had a really fun time leveling up and progressing through the game. The only thing is, once this game is over, the game is over. Which I don't mind, but don't expect this to be a farming simulator to max your entire profile out. I lost interest once the story/dungeons were over.

_childDocuments_.review: All bugs aside, it's a fun game. The music is great, the art style is very nice, the combat is a bit challenging at times, and there is a bit of grinding to do but nothing too intense; all things that I personally enjoy the most. The issues are a bit odd and mainly arise in online co-op, things such as the teleportation circle breaking if anyone other than the host uses it, and some of the keys not working, but nothing that a quick restart won't fix. Like most multiplayer games, it is always better with friends, but it is still really fun playing solo too. 10/10 recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: We bought this game 5 days after it was released and played it for 4 hours. Here are some things to note, and things that I came to understand:1. Game is very Buggy in online co-op, our friend walked up an invisible bridge as an example, another one of our friends took out 2 wooden archer towers on his side, whilst they were up for the 3 of us and we were unable to take them down.2. The Class system is unbalanced, the only differences between the classes are stats and 1 ability which is either a dash or a jump, classes do not get unique weapons.3. Menu system sucks on online co-op as well as going to a different area or tile.4. When increasing mana or health, the bar would go outside of the bar's area for a bit then reset5. Sometimes we were randomly soft locked, luckily one of our friends went to the door and reset the area for usThe great things about this game however far outweigh the problems listed above.1. Great Experience and is fun with friends2. Interesting system with upgrades and town progression3. Cute visuals as well as very detailed areas4. Randomized dungeons and different layouts make it daring and exciting5. Only for 20$ not too shabbyFor all new players who are interested in looking and playing through this game, although it may be buggy now i'm sure the developers are looking towards fixing and bettering the game. I found this to be a great game with friends as listed above with a lot of stupid and funny moments, obviously this would be great solo as well as it feels similar to Zelda: Link to the Past but with its own twists and progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Great coop Zelda game! I have mainly played it in Local Mode, over Parsec (so, remote local). I did not see any bugs.The game does summon a lot of the Zelda A Link to the Past nostalgia. Now, I would not play it alone though. The game does lack a compelling story, and I don't believe the game is meant to be played single player. Also, the dungeons are semi-generated every time you enter them. So if you die in a dungeon, and go back to that same dungeon, it will, in fact, not be the exact same dungeon. In that regard, it is not like ALTTP for example.If you are looking for a game in ALTTP style, but with more story, then I can suggest Blossom Tales.But for a coop Zelda, I don't know a better game! It can truly be fun. And with at least 2 players, this works well! The way the game works, this is a little bit of a "you will have to die a few times before you can start to win" kind of game. But it's all in good fun. In fact, when you die, you can get stronger (you can to train more skills). While there are not a lot of puzzles that truly require a ton of cooperation, completing dungeons in coop can be a lot of fun. And playing as a group starts to make more sense once you can change classes.

_childDocuments_.review: Only grab right now if you're willing to deal with potential bugs.Fun, but buggy, especially for multiplayer. Even in singleplayer there ARE a couple puzzles you won't be able to solve yourself, if RNG isn't kind to you. Luckily the devs have been both rolling out patches and been in contact with the players, including problem-shooting.Plays like older Zelda titles with rogue-like upgrade skill/tool trees via a minor town building system. The game has a pleasant visual and audio aesthetic, so it shouldn't be taxing on wired-potato systems. There's several different classes that have slight to major play differences, but sword & board is the prevalent mechanic. There's a very, very minor 'farming' system, but it lacks impact on actual gameplay. Story is run-of-the-mill adventure game in a monster-troubled world that the 'hero'(PC) must save. Along with updates and patches, the devs have mentioned rolling out new content, including the cut/inaccessible areas and quests; along with possible DLCs and classes down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: I've got this game for the Zelda-ish aspect and the light rogue like gameplay, me and my friends have been enjoying it so far.i would definitely recommend this game, Yes it is a rogue like but it is very light and enjoyable.As of note here are the bugs or things i have noticed.Slight desync but does fix it self overtime.Had a situation we're missing a key to continu the dungeon so we had to end the run ( we suspect a key fell down a hole when a player died)We Had one instance the Moving block puzzle was only playable by host but our second encounter with the puzzle , everyone was able to interact with it.We never got the quest to find Nik even after defeating the first dungeon and building multiple structures.Most of the time, the gem counts of other player is not updating correctly. The player itself see his own count accurately but not the others.Some Puzzle is painful to complete due to camera limitation. _childDocuments_.review: When i first played this game i was confused why it was only at 78% positive reviews on steam. After a little more time with the game i understand but will still cautiously recommend this game. The first 6-8 hours of gameplay in this game are really good. It is retro zelda gameplay, with a big overworld and dungeons to explore. After a death (or victory) in the dungeon you get to upgrade your town and yourself. There are new characters and tools to be acquired and a bunch of sidequests and secrets to hunt down if you are tired of the dungeon gameplay. And it even has multiplayer, what is there not to like?Well the game is extremly shallow at times and feels kinda unfinished.After a while the dungeons get really boring because neither the puzzles nor the fights provide a real challenge.The differences between the character classes are too small for them to be considered character classes.A lot of items and tools are used only a couple times, almost as if the developers forgot about them.Gardening and fishing really serves no purpose as there is no depth to it.There are plenty of softlocks and out-of-bounds glitches all over the game.One achievement is currently impossible to complete and is glitched since May of last year.Neither keyboard and mouse nor playing with a controller feels very good, selecting items is a hassle as there are just too many and the quick-select options are mediocre at best.Despite all that the game is just fun to play, you go into a dungeon and mindlessly kill a bunch of enemies and solve some puzzles for an hour and it is a good time.At the time of this review the developers are working on a big patch that should solve a lot of the issues the game currently has. (at the moment you can play a test-version of the upcoming patch)

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a rogue-lite adventure that's starting as a fun game and ends quite dead. It's buggy, lacks variations in classes, has unfinished content and is overall unrewarding. Halfway through you come to a point where you either ditch the game or finish it because you feel like you've wasted your time already so just might do it till the end. neat, classic old-style adventure type. Just exactly what you would expect from the genre. it's there but it's also easily forgotten after. Nothing special, but at least it's not annoying. not deep or unique, common for the genre. lacks content (as-in, there are dull placeholders for cut out or unreleased content). There are places you can't go and things you can't do yet the game is not an Early Access title (experimental patch 1.7 at the time of this review). I don't think there was a way to change the difficulty unless I totally missed it. As it was, it's unbalanced from my point of view. Starting curve was good: you lose, you grind for upgrades, you progress. About 40% into the game you become too powerful with some classes making you nearly invincible while you keep on getting tons of resources for further upgrades. Turns the second half of the game into a walk in a park. bad. Lots of tools without easy navigation through them. You have to scroll through them without any way to rearrange them or access specific tools quicker. And those are not optional, you have to use them often. You can't get some information about the game elements through UI (spell descriptions after you've acquired them, for example). there are collectibles hidden around the game world which are utterly useless except for achievement hunters. There are game breaking bugs that make you abandon your run and start dungeon over. buggy game that's either unfinished (you can finish the story line but there are lots of placeholders still lying around) or implies that there would be paid content for what's missing (if it's free, see p1.). Fun level drops too fast, can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready for nostalgic joy!!! Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is retro top-down SNES "Zelda: A Link To The Past" goodness with MORE features and an art style that's perfect for the experience.This game does an incredible job of paying homage to "Link To The Past" while adding things you never even realized you wanted to increase re-playablity. With rogue-like elements such as procedural dungeon generation and buff collection exclusive to individual runs, no 2 dungeon dives are quite the same.Spend the gems you earn in each dungeon to customize your character's strengths via health, magic, weapon, and tool upgrades and more. Collect special items to unlock different classes with special abilities (not all features of this are active just yet), and brew potions using items from monsters you've slain.If re-playable dungeons and character customization weren't enough, there's also building of your town, upgrading and decorating your house, gardening and selling crops, fishing (a must for a Zelda style game), and more. There are also additional "mini-dungeons" and of course plenty of puzzles and quests.This game can also be a multiplayer experience, which I have not tried yet.  It is my understanding that there are currently some issues with multi-player that are being ironed out as quickly as possible; we've already had the first patch just 2 days post launch and the next is on the way.Free updates are planned per comments from the developers. Currently there are at least 2 areas of the map that are not even explorable yet, so there's still more to discover and conquer in the future! It's my hope that the developers will continue to expand this game and satisfy my never-ending itch for top-down pixel art adventures. There are so many great things they have implemented that I can't wait to see expanded upon.Lastly, I'd like to give a shout-out to their team for their caring and responsiveness - I experienced something I thought might have been a bug and their support team responded to me with a solution in just a couple of hours ON launch day. It turned out to be a very easy fix through file repair in Steam, so it wasn't even something that was their fault, but they helped me solve it anyway and in record time!TLDR: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a blast to play (and re-play) and has more content on the way! Rejoice in the satisfaction of a "never-ending" retro style action puzzle adventure! Praise the developers for having the insight (that Nintendo apparently doesn't) to give us the throwback we wanted and needed with expanded features and the genius addition of rogue-like elements!As for the negative reviews regarding multiplayer issues, etc. - keep in mind that this is an indie game that just launched, and the developers are incredibly responsive and resolving issues as quickly as they can. They are also implementing player suggestions for improvement coming as soon as the next patch/update. I genuinely think we can count on them to continue to refine and make this game as great as possible!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about 90% of the way to being a classic. The gameplay is good, the exploration is rewarding, the items work as you'd expect and the enemy variety is perfectly acceptable. I love the upgrade system - there's a lot to like about the game.However, I have a caveats to that.Firstly is the art. Yes, it's a style - but let's be honest here, if 16 bit tiles looked *better* in the 80s than your current gen ones, you should probably consider altering the game's art style. It is, by design, more or less flat - but that does not IMPROVE the game. It doesn't make it worse, but it doesn't add anything - and a charming aesthetic could certainly accomplish that. You already have all the tilesets and such programmed. Why not change the style to something that will be more eye catching, and less forgettable?Secondly, characters. IE, there are *none*. You don't care about anyone in this game, because they have no character, and have no actual distinct appearance. Yes, yes I know they *technically* are different - but they're not different enough to matter. Writing alone couldn't fix this, either, because the characters just don't look distinctive enough to really lodge in your brain. It's bad enough that it even makes it a little tricky to remember who upgrades what, early on. If the characters were more distinct, had more unique behaviors - maybe had more dialog - and had a look that stuck with you, it would go SO FAR towards improving the game.Third - item favorites. You need an item favorites system. There are WAY too many items if you want to scroll through them all without opening your menu. Implement a favorites system where you favorite four things from your inventory, and have those be all that scrolls with L and R. Do that, and the gameplay would be *rock* solid.Overall I still highly recommend this game, but actually caring about the characters in it would work wonders. I want to care about those four goddesses, and see a unique appeal in each of them that's WORTH fighting to release!

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks beautiful at a glance, and if I'm not paying much attention to detail, it's truly a game that grabs my attention(I love the art style). But, there is such wonky things that will ultimately keep me from coming back.Going up stairs... Why is it so slow... And the character going up the stairs left and right just looks horrible lol, he walks off the edge of the stairs, yet the character is centered, just move him up a few pixels so he's not centered on the stair sprite.F is the default to continue speech... Really? Couldn't use something easier? space, click, or even E would be better.What's with the GLASS equipment. They couldn't just explain that you lose equipment on death? They had to go all out saying it was glass and shatters on death? A glass bomb bag lol....There is frame drops through the game that get worse as you play (memory leaks?), I'm assuming it's because of AI in far off distance performing actions when player isn't around, because the longer you run around, the more bogged down it gets. I have a fairly good PC set up too. Played for a little over and hour, and it seems like 15ish minutes is where the laggy framerates start to happen, dying solves the problem, but dying to frame rate drops is pretty sad, and annoying. Roguelite games are where you want to die due to skill, not lag.There is also confusing things, some NPC's will ALWAYS have an exclamation mark above their heads, even without a current quest, making me think I'm missing something, when in fact, there is nothing.There is no way to skip NPC dialogue. When they yammer on and on and on, and the only way to continue their dialogue is F, which is also the key to TALK with them again, if you press it one too many times, you get back in their loop, which is soooooooo annoying.Throwing the boomerang uses mana, but using a bow doesn't? Using the lantern to light stuff costs mana, but if you equip the lantern and bump into the stuff, it will light without mana cost...The first class which I admittedly didn't play for long (I switched to the thief/hunter class pretty early on...) has a WIND-UP to his class skill, the other characters don't (I played the mage for a bit too). There's a good 1-2 second delay before he dashes, and it would be useful if you go in a straight line a lot, but you don't. The dungeon was twisty and turny, and once you get the teleport locations, there is no use for the first classes skill, which is kind of dumb since a lot of players will probably stick with that instead of rushing to another class like I did.Losing all your "gems"(rupees) upon entering the dungeon is pretty ridiculous seeing as most of the time you'll only lose 10-100ish (adds up over time) and really only annoys me that you're making me re-earn them when I shouldn't lose them in the first place.Also, gems, AND coins? Why would you make it complicated like that, ditch one for the other, and WHY are coins permanent when gems aren't? They're only ever used in the dungeon, if ANYTHING, it should be the other way around for losing them on death. Because they're used in the dungeon... And most of the time, they're used to open chests that give gems, why the hell is that even a thing?Honestly, this game just put me off within the first hour of playing it due to clunky gameplay, and bad game design(purposefully?)It looks beautiful, and for the most part, there is some really cool things in the game. I may try it again in a few years to see if anything has changed, but I really doubt that anything will.Thanks for reading my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally play RPGs like this, but When I used Parsec on a friend's PC, this was a must-buy for me. I LOVE this game. Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a dungeon-crawling multiplayer roguelite, heavily inspired by the top-down Legend of Zelda titles. You can play this game either by yourself, or with up to 4 players locally, or online with Co-op.Gameplay: 7.5/10Game feels extremely solid in terms of movement, combat, and usage of powerups and abilities. Super well done. I've never played Four Swords like other people have, but I HAVE played LTTP, and this feels 1-1 with it. You have access to 1 class as you start, and you can unlock 7 other classes (1 of which is DLC, but it's worth it.) in-game. Each class gives you special abilities based on who you pick, like Hero having a charge attack, Bomber having bomb jumps, Pirates having a parrot companion to save you from traps, Witches with potion specialisation, etc. Not only do you possess different abilities, but to balance out the game better, each class has different stats, which let you mix and match upgrades of your choosing, like weapons, tools, potions, stamina, health, etc. The upgrade selection is very proficient and nicely done. Being able to increase your attack speed, reach, strength and stamina consumption goes a long way. The game lets you build villages and other buildings that service different purposes, Like gym's for Stamina, Hospitals for Health, Shops for resources, etc.My other issue is how the camera gives you fairly little room for being able to see with multiple players on screen, whether it's co-op local or online. If each player got their own screen, that'd be amazing. But for now, it's kind of a big problem to me. Although I understand why they went this route.Graphics: 8/10Very cutesy and adorable, centred around small pixel art-based characters, environments, objects and enemies. Fairly simple yet effective.Story: 5/10 The game tries to centre the game around you, the main character, and your journey to saving Tasos. Nothing insane to write here in terms of plot. Just your standard "save the world" cliche. No princesses to save, so that's a refresher.Online: 7/10 This game has a pretty good functional online system. It plays great, and it's fun with friends. My only reason I'm giving it a 7 our of 10 is cause this game does have a couple of issues with regards to online. First one, which does hinder progress sometimes, forcing you to abandon your run: Getting teleported in random places. So me and my group of friends decided to grab the Kezar Glove to go to the barn and grab a watering can. As soon as we got into the dungeon, we teleported to the top left of the map (The Arctic) and got lost. This does hinder progress as we walked all the way up to the Kezar caves, for our friend who didn't have the glove yet. This has also happened on a couple of different occasions, but for the most part, the glitch has been consistent. Even though the online is there, take it lightly with a pinch of salt when I say: This is the only Early Access part of the game that should've put the game back into it's EA state. There may be a couple of bugs that hinder the experience a fair amount, but i feel like in due time, this will be addressed. Hopefully.Final Score: 7.5/10Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a Zelda-inspired roguelike with multiplayer elements and a healthy amount of content for its price-tag. From its solid gameplay to fairly decent multiplayer, i'd encourage you to buy this on sale, simply from the bugs I've encountered online. Otherwise, if you look past it, Rogue Heroes is a really fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I completed everything in 30 hours and I rate the game 6/10. Fun little game to play with friends. Game is most definitely balanced around multiplayer rather than single player. What I mean by this is that bosses and such have the same amount of health and do the same amount of damage, regardless if you're solo or with 4 players.I have some gripes that just really ruined a few things for me, but doesn't drag down the entire game. So here they are:1) Honestly too many 'Equipment' things to have on the scroll wheel, and the 'Favorite' wheel is clunky.2) Don't bother with Thief as a class - You can't crit bosses, and you take 1.5x damage for no benefit.3) Don't bother with Mage as a class - The wand picks a random monster to attack, not caring about aim.4) Don't bother with Ranger as a class - The bow requires more upgrades to matter, and the sword is always better, with less cost.5) Don't bother with Witch as a class - The entire shtick is potion effectiveness, so unless you're going with a group of 4 and want them to be fairly worthless except giving you stronger potions, I'd avoid it.6) Circling back to points 1 and 3, specifically the Equipment:a) The Boomerang is entirely worthless. The grappling hook does everything it does, at no cost, and is your traversal tool.b) The Lamp is just annoying, because you always set yourself on fire too. Just instead make it have an interaction function on items that require it, like the wood blockades.c) The Book of Beasts is just a monster tracker, and if you farm enough with it, tells you what they drop...but you already know that when you kill them.d) The Temporal Scope is an item you'll never use outside of leaving the dungeon you get it, and to 100% the game. It has a total use of 4 times, and that's me counting a room in the Endless dungeon generation.e) Bombs are fun, but entirely 100% optional unless you want to 100% complete the game.f) Hammer and Kezar Fist should've just been the same item to reduce clutter. Same as lamp, just make it have an interaction instead of an actual thing to scroll through.I know the list is long, but they were serious downers for me. There are some other little nitpicks here and there, but the above list is what I truly wish would've been fixed before the game lost update support. I still recommend the game for a group of friends, especially if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. This is a cute multiplayer copy of the older Zelda games, and honestly exactly what I would want if it weren't for the game breaking bugs, specifically, one MAJOR bug. Unfortunately, this bug make it a chore to play and after over a year I've lost hope they will ever fix it.I will preface by saying I have only played this game in multiplayer, so I don't know if this bug exist in singleplayer. However, I bought this game purely for its multiplayer function, since well, I could just play The Legend of Zelda if I wanted a singleplayer game like this.Now onto the actual bug:At multiple locations where you exit a room back into the overworld (ex. exiting a cave), you get teleported to the corner of the map. This softlocks you since you end up either walking on the water out of bounds or in the snow biome, where you don't have the necessary gear to get out of said biome because you weren't supposed to be there yet. I'm astonished this has not been fixed since it is completely game breaking and you will encounter this bug even if you are just going through the main story line - i.e. no exploring hidden paths, no checking the cracks etc.I waited over a year to buy it hoping they would fix this bug. Alas, I am greatly disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop is what truly kept me engaged. You’re actively encouraged to gather gems, becoming stronger and getting access to unlockables in the process. And although this feelings of progression eventually wears off due to having maxed out everything, the road of getting there is what matters. What could be improved upon is the world-building itself. It feels empty and lifeless. I feel as if there should be more side content to flesh out the setting of this game.A few bothersome things are certain elements that really shouldn’t have been in the game. Having a bunch of essential collectibles scattered through the world is a bit tedious given the world’s maze-like layout. Even if not for the achievement, these collectibles are necessary for improving your class perks. Having progression locked behind collectibles in a game like this is rather questionable. At the very least they should have given the player Something that did tire me out throughout this game were the block puzzles and everything revolving around them. They were fine at first, but given the repetitive nature of this game, you will encounter the same handful of block-related obstacles over and over again. There was one instance where I would actually softlock myself because I couldn’t reset nor move the block from the exit, trapping myself in a small space.Despite the fun factor, I would suggest getting this game with a discount. It certainly will keep you entertained, but I still think there should be more to it. There is definitely potential here to rival games like Stardew Valley.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the other reviews and was, like, okay, how bad could it be? And yeah, it’s about a little south of “meh” right now. This is not a “finished” game and it should be considered early access. The story (or lack there of), the dungeon levels, the RPG progression, and the “Stardew Valley”-esque elements are so half-baked and forced together it is almost confusion. When playing, you want the game to make sense but it doesn’t. Why does it take so long to get the fishing rod and what is the point of that and farming? Why use any other tool when the grappling hook is clearly the best item in the game? (uses no stamina and no ammo) What is the point of building all these generic homes for the generic townspeople in the bland land of Blands-ville?Wait, so there are only like ~20 different enemies the game? For a $20 game? I’ve gotten better value from a free mobile game. Why the artificial difficulty spikes? The most punishing thing in the game is when you bump into an enemy or trap. The dungeons are waaaay more difficult than the “bosses”. I literally stood still and grappling hooked my way through most boss fights. And and and yeah more. All that said, I played through solo and I know that’s not the intended experience. I wanted to test the game out before recommending my girlfriend and I play it and I just ended up hate-finishing while hoping it would get better and it did not. I feel like I saved my girlfriend from this experience. My verdict: I’ll come back when there is an update or when it’s more polished but I’ll burn all of Tasos to the ground if it’s paid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Having fun with it thus far.  I get Link to the Past x Binding of Isaac vibes with some persistent upgrade elements thrown in.  Definitely on the lighter side of roguelite.  Good enemy variety, interesting exploration and abilities/items that enable further exploration.  If it's too hard you can grind a bit and buff up your dude with some upgrades.  Nice art direction and dungeons have puzzles that are on par with Link to the Past - nothing too difficult but might take a minute to figure out.  Nice little town building mechanic with light farming elements as well.  Couple different currency types that are used for different things.Some notes for improvement:- Limited variation between classes- Exploration - once the waypoints are unlocked it would be much more convenient to be able to teleport between them whenever you want vs the current system of only being able to access the waypoint system when you are at a waypoint.- Item selection needs to be streamlined, maybe something like hold down a key/bumper to open a radial menu for item selection.  As it stands scrolling one-by-one or opening the main menu to select an item is too cumbersome as they begin to accumulate.- Dungeon rooms - The algorithm needs to be adjusted, on multiple occasions I have left one dungeon room only to go to exactly the same dungeon room.  I find it's not uncommon to see the same room multiple times in a single dungeon run.- Town building - Would like this to be expanded, I had everything in the town built before I even accessed the second dungeon and there are still a bunch of empty lots.  This would also serve as a gem sink for later in the game once you are pretty much maxed out on persistent upgrades.  Let me relocate buildings, further customize my house, and maybe some options for purely cosmetic items/decorations and buildings that can be placed in empty lots.- Also, when moving on ice I experienced some instances of inability to move.  I thought my controller was running low on battery but it seems when sliding into a wall sometimes it will freeze your movement for a second.Overall have enjoyed the game.  Can't comment on the multiplayer as I've only played solo.

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie love letter to the  franchise. Equal parts  and , this RPG integrates some roguelike mechanics into its dungeons to make a product that balances the retro gameplay with modern mechanics nicely. It suffers from a severe lack of polish and a litany of bugs (some game-breaking), but if you can look past some of these quality issues you'll find a fun, casual RPG.You play as a nameless denizen of the continent of Tasos, which is beset by monsters summoned by four invading demons. With the blessing of the goddess in tow, you must go on to fulfill your destiny by clearing out four procedurally-generated dungeons. Invest the loot you earn from dungeon crawling in a variety of upgrades to power your character up and improve your chance of success. With town customization, minigames, sidequests, bonus dungeons, a class system, collectibles and more,  has a lot to experience.Perhaps the game's most unique feature is its optional co-op.  offers both a campaign playable in singleplayer or up to four-player local or online co-op. The game does a pretty good job at straddling the line between being small enough to suit one player and large enough to fit four; dungeon maps, for instance, have enough space to allow multiple players to distinctively move around, but players are mobile enough that traversal never feels like a grind. The level balance is loose, since there are too many permutations of playersThe roguelike elements are more of a mixed bag. While it is true that dungeons are procedurally generated, there is a very limited amount of rooms for each dungeon that the game pulls from. Thus a player of average skill who takes maybe 3-4 trips to finally complete a dungeon will likely encounter almost every single room from a dungeon's pool, just in different orders. Beyond making repeat runs feel samey, the level design can rarely introduce a game-breaking bug: since players can enter a room in any direction, you may get stuck in a room that can only be unlocked by defeating an enemy which you can't reach. As there's no room reset option upon saving/exiting standard to other roguelikes like , you always risk losing a bunch of progress anytime you attempt a dungeon.Speaking of bugs - this game has a lot of them. Twice the game broke during dungeon attempts due to level design flaws (the aforementioned unbeatable enemy, and once my character got stuck behind a level prop). The game also frequently allows the player to walk through breakable objects. Music would cut out until the game was reset. Certain enemy hitboxes were inconsistent. Some additional QA would've gone a lot further to give the impression that this game was made as well as possible.The other major selling points are mostly irrelevant. The minigames are easy to miss entirely, the farming element progresses far too slowly and there is little incentive to complete it, the character classes all play too similarly to offer replay value, town customization is limited to placing buildings on a grid, and the collectibles are frustrating to keep track of because the game never erases the clues for where to find them after they're collected, forcing players to waste tons of time backtracking or to remember each of the hundreds of locations they've already visited. In short, if you're playing , you're doing it for the core RPG gameplay. makes a valiant effort to capture the spirit of  and the gameplay of  fused with roguelike gameplay and other modern types of side content, all to a mixed-positive result. The core RPG gameplay is impressively adaptive to the standard singleplayer experience as to the zany chaos of multiplayer co-op, though the roguelike feature is underdeveloped and exposes the game to some serious bugs. Temper your expectation a bit when comparing this game to the inspiring  classics, and an enjoyable adventure will await.  gets a B-.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play many roguelites because they often are stupid fustrating hard. Rogue Heroes doesn't really have that problem.At first, the first dungeon is ridiculously hard, since you are a squishy nobody that is whacking away with a stick. Traps pretty much 1 hit you, you are getting battered around by skellies, etc. But once you beat the first dungeon....the rest of the game goes downhill. Each of the 4 dungeons are 3 floors. Roughly take 45 minutes to clear a dungeon (depending on level) while solving all puzzles, and clearing every room. After I beat the first dungeon, I was able to beat each next one within one full try. It took about 3 hours to beat the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and final boss. You are just way overpowered and get so many gems that its just now about how fast you can clear it, not being careful anymore because it doesn't matter anymore. If the first dungeon was a little easier, and the rest of the game was a bit harder, this would've kept up with the increase in your power as well. Unfortunately, it doesn't and you end up being a one-man army really quickly. Also, there are several classes but I don't know why you would use them? I chose Knight, because looking at the shop, it has the most upgrades available. More upgrades = more power. Also, the bow and staff is really annoying to aim. Some of the enemies move too fast to be able to use them effectively. And the auto-aim thing is a bit wacky. I only used the staff and bow when I had to for traps/puzzles. Don't get me wrong, this game is fun, but there is just such a disconnection between challenge and reward.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun and I do recommend it. The combat can be satisfying if you like hack and slash combat. Some of the classes are viable, others show up way too late to care for. The game can be rather easy in the dungeons and gems are given away so frequently, you would hardly have to grind after your first few attempts at the first dungeon. The puzzles are very similar to A Link To The Past and it makes me want to go back and play Attp and A Link Between Worlds. The problem is, the game is hardly a rogue-lite. It's more a dungeon-pillaging puzzle-adventure game with some rare stat modifiers and 2D Zelda. Everything else is pre-planned. No luck involved. If you die, it is likely your fault and has very little to do with what your build becomes in a dungeon. But it is incredibly easy to overcome by pumping more gems into your combat and health with some rare circumstances where you need to buff a certain tool (eg. bow and grappling hook). The second half of the game is pretty disappointing. You get some really great dungeons early on but after main dungeon 2, you get some puzzle dungeons with challenging bosses (losing in these dungeons is awful since you have to do all the puzzles again) and your standard dungeons which are easy to breeze through. You also get a lot of the tools around the 2nd dungeon. The reward for the 3rd dungeon is completely useless and there is no reward for the 4th major dungeon. My recommendation to the developers if they decide to release an update is to add something that will be useful for shortcuts . For example, how about an axe to cut through annoying trees or maybe something to climb up mountains to speed up the exploration process and last-minute side quest cleanup. Yes there is bugs. I've had to restart my game a couple of times due to soft-locks. They do not destroy the experience but it does break up the game's flow. Still, I recommend it because it can be fun. I mention the negatives because you should know what you are getting yourself into and temper your expectations. Either expect a super easy "rogue-lite" or a Zelda clone where you could power up your character using standard RPG levelling mechanics. Also, the frogs are awesome and I wish they were used more.

_childDocuments_.review: The basic game loop is fun! Explore the overworld, find a dungeon, try to beat it. Fail to beat it? Go back to town, upgrade your stats, and try again! Eventually beat the dungeon, which unlocks a new item, which you can then use to explore farther on the overworld, eventually reaching a new dungeon.The graphics are cute and fitting. Nothing felt out of place. The sound effects were generally good as well.The overworld itself was fun to explore. There were lots of varied locations, and even though the secrets were generally obvious to find, it was still satisfying to hunt them down and get the rewards from them.There were a ton of different things to upgrade, and the different upgrade trees were cute to look at and explore.Some of the game mechanics felt superfluous. The game had a town building minigame, which mostly involved placing various buildings in various slots around the town. It was cute, but placing a building one place instead of another was just thematic. It was weird placing down a building in a random spot, not understanding what the building was going to be when placed. Several times after placing a structure, I had wished I had placed it somewhere more convenient, but didn't know until it was placed that it would be some building I want to visit often. Ultimately it just made walking back and forth to places in the town slower than it had to be for no real benefit.There was a whole planting / farming mini-game thing that felt entirely useless. My 2 friends and I played through literally the  game without a single crop growing. It seems more designed around singleplayer, where time might pass more often whenever you sleep, which it didn't in co-op.And on that note, there were several other things that didn't quite work so hot in co-op.- Pickups being individual meant we needed for farm 3x as many things to complete the varied "collect stuff" quests (Almost every single 'quest' ended up just being "I need 20 slime balls" or "I want 30 fangs")- Screen transitions were slightly awkward in co-op. If any one player walked off the edge of the screen, it would teleport all players to the new screen. Understandable, but very often jarring. Someone might accidentally walk off the edge of the screen, for example. Or it was purposeful, but then someone else immediately walks back to the previous screen because they were pressing the wrong direction. There was no delay or warning for these transitions, so it caught us off guard several times.The difficulty curve of the game was very poor. We beat the first dungeon after perhaps 5-6 attempts. It was fun, challenging, and the boss was mechanically interesting and relevant. We beat the second dungeon after only 2 attempts, the first attempt ending prematurely because of bugs. The dungeon was a breeze, and the boss's mechanics were irrelevant and we just ignored them. We then proceeded to beat the 3rd, 4th and final dungeons on our first try without even a hint of effort expended. They were just too easy. Or, perhaps we were too strong. Two sides of the same coin. It got really boring near the end because we were just so incredibly overpowered compared to the enemies.The balance of the different upgrades and things were really off as well. My friends went for a sword-based build. I went for a grappling-hook based build. For exactly the first dungeon, I felt like my damage was relevant. I maxxed out the entire upgrade path and never did any relevant damage again, because the sword upgrade tree was much deeper than the grappling hook upgrade tree. Understandable, I suppose. So for the next 2 dungeons, I 100% maxxed out my wand & magic pool. My friends were nearing the top of the sword tree at this point. For comparison, they would deal around 300 damage a hit, 3 times a second, with a 50% chance to crit and hit for 800 or so. Worked out to be around 1000 dps. With every single possible upgrade spent to improve my magic, I could deal around... 30 damage a second. For some later enemies, I could literally expend my entire magic pool on a single enemy over 20 seconds and it wouldn't die. My friends would one-shot them with a sword. This was WITH me using the mage class with it's assorted magical bonuses. Repeat this same process when I tried to level up bombs instead. They just didn't hold a candle to the basic sword weapon in any regard. But, on the plus side, they did self-damage so I died a lot when using them! A fitting end to the saga of "trying to make anything that isn't swords work in any capacity."Also, co-op was exceptionally buggy. It would work great for half an hour, or maybe even 2 hours, but then it would desync. And once it desynced, it was not likely to recover to a playable state, so we had to restart the session to have all of us be able to play again. Additionally, even when it didn't desync, it handled latency / lag very poorly. I know that lag isn't the game's fault, but I feelt like an acceptable outcome for a poor connection is to, say, pause the game until it recovers. Or have the lagging player sit on a wait screen. It's not really an acceptable outcome to have someone lagging be able to pick up a crystal pickup on the ground 500 times because they are lagging, and suddenly get +80,000  gems. Or, like, to be unable to kill anything in the entire dungeon, because while the host sees ever enemy dead, the client doesn't, and they just die to invisible unkillable enemies. Or like... when a screen transition happens during lag, the lagging player (or maybe everyone) appears inside a lake and drowns. Or inside a wall and is stuck. Or the screen transition never happens, and the game is softlocked. It wasn't unplayable, and obviously wouldn't be an issue in solo play, but it was a huge factor in my enjoyment of this game.It's a fun game, and I would recommend it for fans of games in this genre. However, if you plan to play online multiplayer and have low tolerance for constantly restarting your game, or other random bugs, then steer clear. The difficulty curve is not smooth in the least, but it didn't ruin my enjoyment of the game as a whole. Despite the bugs, it still seems more enjoyable with friends than on your own.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, making games is a difficult endeavor. I considered (and re-considered) this fact many times during my hours spent with Rogue Heroes.Quick lead-in before I give a litany of criticism: It's a nice pick-up-and-play, 4-5 session game to jam through with a group of friends. Many pieces of the game are wonky or outright multiplayer-hostile, but there's a special kind of bonding that can occur when you support each during times of adversity.If you have a group of friends that are looking for a fairly casual, low-commitment game to play (the folks you'll have a good time with no matter what you're doing) this is a good pick. Perfect for the off-season of an MMO raid team, for example.Now, to get into the chunkier feedback:It's got a lot of rough edges. It's almost always clear what the game's going for (since it's so clearly built in the vein of classic Zelda games) but there are a lot of little details that got missed in the process. Like how blocks don't get pushed in discrete, 1-unit chunks, there's no the subtle magnetism that vacuums you to be even with bushes / pots / blocks you interact with, the (lack of) readability of which ledges you can (and should) leap off of, that kind of stuff.There are also new, exciting issues unique to this game with no parallels to classic Zelda. A lot of these are situations where the game mechanics are a bit self-sabotaging, especially in multiplayer play. Things like:The game's not all negatives, though (I'm even giving this a positive review!) so here are some good points:It's definitely an odd one, but I enjoyed the block of time I spent with my friends in this game. Enough to give it a slight thumbs up. Grab it on sale, and have a good time!And, you know, I get it. Making games is hard, and they got this one across the finish line. That's an achievement few can claim, so don't be afraid to take some pride in that.

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the negative reviews of this game are completely false. In regards to co-op bugs, I can't speak to, I play solo. But I almost didn't buy this game from some of the complaining about solo aspects of the game: i.e. puzzles can't be completed, unpolished dungeons, unbeatable situations, etc.... But most of these reviews also call the game easy. Clearly not that easy. Look, if you're looking for some souls-like super punishing hardmode game - this isn't it. If you want a fun, Link to the Past (if you're like me and grew up playing Zelda on repeat, you'll love this), semi-challenging but not too punishing (anything too difficult - gems are easy to farm, you can easily scale yourself up past each dungeon and easy mode them) puzzle game: this is very worth it.I love that it's pretty casual, I have found a couple of minor bugs in terms of being able to climb something I shouldn't be able to, or jumping and suddenly landing in a different spot not quite where you should be. None are game breaking. None have stopped any of my runs. And the stuff people are saying about solo mode bugs - totally false. There are some genuinely challenging puzzles but I'm in the 4th dungeon now and haven't run across any puzzle I couldn't do solo - though admittedly some are very frustrating and time consuming (one especially in dungeon 3, but I'm convinced there's any easier way I haven't thought of yet).Bugs about co-op - sure, maybe, I dunno, everything else people are whining about... well, guess the game isn't as easy as they thought if they couldn't complete the puzzles on solo. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes feels a lot like the old top down Zelda games, though it is more fast paced. We also experienced some glitching of the UI, with HP bars getting locked at lower values than they should be, but those glitches never stuck for long.Edit: After finishing the game, I have to say, the end of the game felt rushed and bugs became more common. _childDocuments_.review: very fun game if you are a fan of old school zelda. upgrading inventory is a great mechanic, though the sword will dwarf all the other items in terms of damage. enemies don't really get complicated, they just kinda get tankier and dish out more damage. personally I think the trap damage got ridiculous but that was about it. Stamina system I don't mind except that the sword just doesn't let you attack once you hit half stam. having the class ability be separate for the stamina bar was a really good choice though. Maybe if there was an easier way to switch between magics I would have used it more. you have to go into the inventory menu to change with spell you are casting. but was still really fun to sword and board the game. Ranger to me felt like the best class. It has a high base speed and the dash ability gives you iframes and recharges very fast. I didn't even bother with the bow mechanics. it was honestly fun enough to dash into enemies and slice them up instead. the aiming for the bow and the spells can be wonky at times. it will target enemies that are not close to you when you have enemies coming right at you.Grappling hook was my go to side arm. Not only does it help traverse the world, but it doesn't have to target enemies it just moves in a straight line. not much damage just like the rest of the items but it felt more consistent if i wanted to attack at range.I like that the main dungeons were more roguelite. _childDocuments_.review: This game is basically "what if the Zelda franchise was public domain and someone re-made Four Swords but also fallen into the trap of traditional RPGs and quantifying every possible stat while putting the focus into traversing randomized dungeons". And it's fairly decent.Having completed the main portion of the game and still having some collectables to look for, my general opinion is that this is a serviceable "Link to the Past clone" for the most part. There are some obtuse things you're supposed to intuit along the game and (currently) it's possible to sequence-break yourself into softlocks, meaning that you'll make that save game impossible to complete. This is avoidable if you don't go too deep into the upgrades to unlock something which will make you sequence break (like swimming stamina) or just focus on doing the main quest as a priority; I'm just saying it so you can prevent yourself from losing your time investment.The main focus, as I stated in the beginning, is clearing dungeons. There isn't that much in the way of difficulty beyond learning enemy attack patterns and finding the class you're most comfortable playing as, since each plays slightly different from each other with the active "movement skill" and percentual distribution of damage (to them and to enemies) as well as movement speed. Keep in mind that faster classes are generally frailer but easier to use when dealing with some timed traps and dungeon room objectives.One of the main gimmicks, the multiplayer component, is something I haven't experienced at all. Sufice to say that at worst you're going to get desynchronized with other players, but at best you're getting the full experience. Dungeon puzzles take into account how many players are in the game and it should be obviously much more interesting when another human being is controlling your progress by being cooperative. There's a local multiplayer mode, but haven't got anyone I could test that with either.The negatives? Personally, I hate the fast cycled sub-items for a specific reason: in dungeons, you can technically select items that you will NEVER have a purpose to use (such as crop seeds). If I'm cycling from the hammer to the hookshot, why would I ever want to pass through the seeds...? One less item to cycle in dungeons would also mean faster swapping and encouraging usage of all your resources more. The game also has a few bugs here and there, but nothing major aside from the sequence-breaking softlocks, in my experience.I'm going to recommend Rogue Heroes because I'm all for someone else taking a shot at classic Zelda titles with multiplayer, since the official source refuses to make them. It's a flawed game but possibly a shiny gem in the genre. No idea how updates will change the game in the future (currently I do see potential to do a bit more with what there is, but again: I haven't completed 100% yet, so no clue), but it's still a good game and significantly better than a few that burned me in the past.

_childDocuments_.review: You start off by exploring the map for the first dungeon. Once you get there, you proceed through a random collection of rooms to get to the boss. There are three floors per dungeon and four dungeons total, but there is a lot more to explore in the world outside of the dungeons. Within the dungeons themselves you can obtain temporary tools (glass) that you will lose when you die or finish the dungeon. You also find gems which are exclusive to dungeons that can be used to "buy" more shops in town which are then used to buy upgrades for your character such as increased health, magic, attack power, attack speed, character classes, permanent tools (not glass), etc.Beating each dungeon will also give you another permanent tool like the hook shot or bombs which are used both in dungeons and in the overworld to get more treasure. Other character classes can be unlocked which give different offensive, defensive, and speed stats. Each class also has their own secondary ability. The basic class uses the Zelda-like pegasus boots charge. The thief class can turn invisible and run fast and so on.The game can be played completely solo or with up to four players. I played mostly two-player with my brother. The game supports both local and online. We played online with two copies of the game on two separate computers in two separate rooms in the same house. The game ran fine online most of the time. There were a couple times where the game desynced and dropped one of us from the game.If one of you dies, the other player can pick up your skull and take it to a revival statue (multiple found in each dungeon). All gems that are picked up by either player are given out equally among all players. This is great because it avoids the problem of fighting over rewards like in Zelda Four Swords Adventures. Also great is that spending gems back in town is done on an individual basis. Each player chooses how they want to spend their gems. The shops purchased for developing the town can be bought with pooled gems. Each player will volunteer how many gems they want to create these new buildings. Playing with my brother, there weren't any problems splitting the cost of these. Note that only the host player will advance the town in their game. Guest players will get to keep all the upgrades they buy for their character, but will not see any of the town developments if they load up their file solo afterwards. This is not a problem because they will be powered up enough to take on dungeons on their own if they want. All player will still earn achievements for beating dungeons at the same time, and will earn personal achievements like defeating X number of enemies separately.As of March 31st the game has been updated to fill the entire world map. There are three new optional dungeons that end with their own unique bosses. However, these dungeons are not randomized like all the other dungeons. these are more traditional top-down Zelda-like dungeons with unique puzzles. They are only one floor each, not multiple floors like all the others, which makes them much shorter experiences.This is a very fun Zelda-like action adventure game with great multiplayer. There is also a free demo, so go try it before you buy!Please watch this for further demonstration of my review points and about the community experimental build.

_childDocuments_.review: The game basically feels like a 2D Zelda in terms of control/abilities, but it turns out deliberate level design is an important part of what makes those Zelda games work. The "rogue-lite" aspects of the game just don't serve the Zelda gameplay well. In a proper roguelike, the game stays compelling because each run has the opportunity to be unique. In Rogue Heroes, dungeon runs aren't interesting because the player's set of abilities is too static. You might pick up some buffs to your stats, but you won't acquire anything that would cause you to adopt a different strategy. The level design of a Zelda game doesn't mesh well with the roguelike format either. Many rooms in a dungeon will feature puzzles. The puzzles in Rogue Heroes are fine, but you're going to encounter the same puzzles multiple times if you run a dungeon more than once. Repeatedly solving the same puzzle isn't a fun experience.Aside from these fundamental structural problems, the game isn't finished. It shouldn't have been released as a 1.0 in the state it was in. The character class descriptions suggest the classes have abilities that they simply didn't have at launch. At least some of it has been updated since I finished playing, but it was pretty frustrating to play as a Mage and find that my magic wand wasn't anymore effective than it was when I played as the base class. There are also large areas of the map that are pointless, but the game doesn't tell you they're pointless, and in at least one case it actively leads you to believe that there should be something more happening:-There was a sidequest to find a lady's husband-I found the dude-I was rewarded with a key to some kind of crab dungeon-After beating the final boss of the game, I went to the crab dungeon. The key opened the door-Inside the crab dungeon was a small room with another door-I couldn't figure out how to open the door. I thought there must be something I'm missing. Obviously this door has to open somehow. -I scoured the world trying to find whatever other ability or key I must have missed that would allow me to progress.  I resisted the urge to look anything up because I assumed it was some kind of puzzle and I wanted to solve it myself.-After probably an hour of this I give up and check the discussion board on Steam. It turns out there's currently no way to open that door. Ok, sometimes games have cut content or they have areas that are plants for future DLC, that's fine. What's not fine is leaving that sidequest in the game. Block off the area of the map until the content is done! Don't give me a key to a nonexistent place! That's ridiculous. So yeah, that really soured my experience. Even if I put that aside, I wouldn't recommend this game. It's not terrible, I had a mostly ok time with it, but you can do a lot better than mostly ok.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this one.  This is not super far from being a "do not recommend", but if it's pass/fail, I give it a pass.  If it's cheap, get it.  Link to the Past mechanics cloned (and barely altered), turned into a pretty shallow but cute rogue-like.  They do puzzles well.  They do upgrades ok.  They do NPC's poorly.  A lot of the quests in town felt like the devs assumed they'd be fun just because they were there.  A lot of them weren't, they felt forced, although they did make the town feel more fleshed out.  Your character moves fast, which is fun for exploring, but makes combat feel unfair at first, until you get used to the fact that it's just jarringly quick.  Other than those god-awful dive-bombing birds with impossible to read movement patterns, combat is something that you can work with and get good at (seriously devs, take that enemy out of the game or fix it, it sucks)The different classes basically all feel the same.  I think this game would have been better with fewer classes with more meaningful differences.  As far as I'm concerned, the only three classes in the game are Hero (balanced), Thief (fast and weak), and Knight (slow and strong).  Using the other classes felt like being punished by having to invent my own reasons to use them, and not being able to find them.I think the devs had a pretty strong priority of getting the player right into the exploration, combat, and dungeoneering as fast as possible, and they did a good job with that.  They handle death really well.  It's enough of a setback that it feels like it matters, but you can boomerang back in really effectively.  It felt like they were working from a checklist of "things a good game should have", and just dumped a whole bucket of that stuff in without consideration for fleshing it out, tying it in to the rest of the game, or making it feel like any of it mattered.  Despite that, I still had fun, but not as much as it feels like I could have had.  I can't bring myself to call it good, bad, or forgettable.  It's more fun than it should be for how hollow and perfunctory it is.  Go in with mild standards and you'll have a fun little romp.

_childDocuments_.review: 29.5h (100% achievement, finished the game)  No (some might be grindy depending on your playstyle). Yes (34 achievements). No. is a top-down action-adventure game that can be played by up to 4 players in both local co-op and online co-op. It offers 4 main dungeons and several smaller ones, with the main dungeons being randomly generated each run. That being said, the game is completely playable solo, and this review will be based on that.- 4+ dungeons, with the main dungeons being randomly generated each run- Infinite dungeons for those who want to keep on playing after finishing all contents- A lot of things to do: side quests, secret areas, and others- Grinding might be needed to progress at the beginning- Exiting the game equals dying; your last location won't be saved- Unable to zoom the map fullyIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 uses pixelated visuals in a top-down view. The layout looks similar to  games with their rocky cliffs, square-shaped dungeon interiors with bricks, and other objects such as bushes, pots, and rocks, although it still tries to make them look different. The map size is bigger, for example, with more bushes that you can swipe in between. Moreover, the tileset is also changed based on the terrain, modifying all of the objects to match it. The enemies also try to follow suit with their recolor versions despite being treated as the same enemies.The story is only told at the beginning. However, it can be hard to follow since the game auto-advances the dialogues. Luckily, it only serves as a premise to the game - you won't miss anything if you don't know about it, especially since there is nothing more to the story even after you finished the game. is an action-adventure game at its core. You have an overworld that you can explore with your trusty sword, which you can use to kill the enemies. Killed enemies won't respawn until you reenter the area, making it easy to mark explored spots. The game is pretty much linear - you might have some optional areas to explore, but most areas are only accessible until you progress the game.Enemies have different attack patterns, and it's your job to figure out how to beat them. Learning how to kill some enemies without taking damage might seem tough at first, but most of them will be easy to beat once you know what to do. If you are still having trouble, you can upgrade your stats to kill most of them in 1 hit.Upgrades need to be purchased. Unlike Zelda-like games that allow you to power up by finding items, you need to have enough gems to purchase a stat increase instead. This forces you to grind if you are not good enough, although this also means that you can cheese most bosses as long as you are willing to grind. On the other hand, I like seeing the town getting upgraded after you purchased some building upgrades.As I said before, the main dungeons are randomly generated. Both layout and traps changed each run, and puzzles might need to be solved differently based on your starting location. Moreover, there are a lot of rooms available in the mix, making each run feel different. You need to redo each dungeon several times just to find all rooms that the dungeon has to offer, and playing the game after knowing all rooms isn't going to bore you out since there are still some slight randomizations in the rooms, whether it's from the enemies or the exploration to search for the area exit.The game seems to not know how many keys you need. Clearing a room will net you some reward, which often has a key that can be used to unlock a door. However, I always find myself having more keys that I can use. This might seem to be done as a precaution in case people can't solve some of the puzzles that have the keys as a reward, but I just find it weird that you don't have to explore every room to finish the dungeon because of the spare keys.You need to restart the dungeon from the beginning if you die. Since dungeons are randomized, it's obvious that you can't pick up from where you left off. However, dying in a dungeon will allow you to keep your gems, which can be used to purchase upgrades to make you stronger. The same gems can also be kept if you manage to finish the dungeon, although it might be hard to do without investing a few upgrades beforehand.You won't be able to keep your earned gems if you enter the dungeon. This seems to be one of the "roguelike" aspects that the game has. You need to use them all before you enter each dungeon, or risk losing them. To be honest, I find this feature to be useless - it just forces you to use all gems before entering a dungeon. Losing 400 gems won't matter if you can get 10k gems afterward.I finished the game in 29.5h. The game can be finished faster if you just rushed both dungeons and enemies. It also has a lot of things that you can do: there are side quests to complete, secret areas to explore, bestiary to finish, and many more. As for the difficulty, the game isn't hard as long as you are willing to grind. Some puzzles in the dungeons might take some time to figure out, but most of them are simple enough. If you are stuck on some, there are a lot of spare keys that you can use - you are not forced to complete every room in the dungeon to finish it.I got soft-locked when I tried to do the endless dungeon, forcing me to abandon my run to exit from the area. Moreover, you can't save inside the dungeon. Loading your save will also respawn you to your home, which makes it feel as if you are dying. This prevents people from playing the game in short sessions. Lastly, the map still looks blurry when zoomed to the max, making it hard to figure out everything.Despite its roguelike tag,  doesn't feel like a roguelike at all. All it takes from that genre is the randomly generated dungeon with some upgrades in between. Your currency might be reset upon entering a dungeon, but you can always use them before entering. You might have to reset the dungeon from the beginning, but the game offers a shortcut to go directly to both the second and third floors once you manage to reach and unlock them. The game will try to make everything accessible no matter what, allowing you to finish the game as long as you don't mind grinding if you suck at it.The game feels more like a solid Zelda-like game with some additional features. You can fish, expand your village, plant crops - there are a lot of optional elements, which don't take time to finish. You only need to spend a few minutes at most, allowing you to focus on the action-adventure elements. Exploration might feel unrewarding since it will only offer you collectibles that don't help much with the game, but it's still fun to do if you like to explore everything to its fullest. If you enjoy Zelda-like games and don't mind having to focus on upgrades instead of finding secret collectibles, make sure to buy this game.
