_childDocuments_.review: TLDR version: Fun but buggy; wait for a sale or until the bugs are fixed.I had a lot of fun playing this in co-op online.  There's a lot to explore and several dungeons (monsters & puzzles) to complete.  The first dungeon was seemingly the hardest from starting out.  The bosses at the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and endless were easier due to upgrades unlocked.  (You get the upgrades from gems; the gems you get from completing the dungeons.  It's easy enough once you've completed the first dungeon once to run back through it and just farm for more gems for better upgrades.  Once in endless I got to floor 25 and stopped (got the achievement and it was getting late so I stopped playing).  One thing I did notice was that the levels of the monsters in endless mode on the floors stayed the same (at 120).  The only levels that continued to increase were those of the snakes in the pots (did increase each level).The classes behave in a similar attacking manner - you'll be using your sword for most of attacking purposes.  All the classes do have a different jump/rush ability for fast travel (goes on cooldown for a short bit afterwards).  There are a lot of tools to switch between.  I do like that there is the option of selecting which 8 you use the most and programming that to a button for easier access.  Some of the tools are zone dependent and I wish there was the option to hide them from the tools you'd scroll through in zones they aren't used in at all.One minor annoyance is that when one person opens their menu it will not let you continue playing if you are in co-op mode.  It will just tell you that another person has the menu open.  It's great if you just want to pause the game, but you need to open the menu to check for things.  Having it pop up each time can hinder game play.While playing in online co-op we encountered a lot of bugs.  Some were pretty amusing, others kinda annoying.  Below are some of the bugs encountered:-Entered/exited a cave and came out in a different (unvisited) zone.  (Not a big deal, able to get back to where I was at.)-Walked on water instead of climbing up to an area that should have been accessible to climb up to while swimming.  (Game breaking - was unable to continue in the current state aside from just running around on water.  It was amusing to watch but ultimately had to quit the game and re-enter from town to fix the issue.)-Glitched into what seemed like a different layer of the dungeon floor (was running around in areas I should not have been able to access; since it was online co-op the other player was able to go into another room and pull me into that room.  It's not game breaking in co-op but would be in single player).-The shovel will not work on certain areas of the map in the current state.  There are areas marked where you should be able to dig, but the shovel just makes the noise that you cannot dig there.  (Game breaking in the sense that you cannot get all of the achievements to 100% this game.  If you don't care about the achievements, then this isn't of concern, as it does not affect being able to beat the dungeons or final boss.)Ultimately since I did have fun with it I would still recommend it, but with all the bugs in its current state I don't believe it is worth full price (half off, sure).

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, but my recommendation comes with a condition/warning attached. There is a steep difficulty curve, because game resembles classical ones and combat requires precise positioning and stamina management.There are 2 permanent upgrades and unlocks in the game that make consecutive runs easier.As you play you get stat upgrades, unlock secondary weapons (incl. ranged weapons) and classes.Upgrades are unlocked by playing the game and "upgrading" the world/village, which I thought was a very nice touch. I don't dislike the generic "get a magical mcguffin to unlock upgrade menu and then select a trait you want to learn" type of design, but working to hire a blacksmith and buying weapon upgrades from them just feels more organic.There's some open-world exploration in game and (at least early on) the world feels sizable, but it's mostly gated behind dungeons (so far only feature in game that feels very artificial). Sadly I found nothing of value in areas I had access to, which is disappointing. With that said, there IS a place you can go at the start of the game where you will get your butt kicked by super high level monsters. Kudos for that! I hope more games do it.You get access to basic attack (same for all classes), block, special action (class specific) and secondary weapons, which makes most classes feel similar. Special action does make a bit of a difference, but it's hard to use most of them with precision the game requires, so special actions often end up being niche utility skills, rather than a combat skill that changes core gameplay loop.Combat feels like that of a classical game, where position and precision matters as much as knowing enemy patterns. I felt it required a little too much precision early on. What I mean by that is you will take some time to adjust fighting against basic enemies, and once you do they are not a real threat, BUT it's still very easy to screw up with more than 1 enemy around. Combat rarely feels unfair, but when it does, it's because there are multiple enemies to fight and they don't leave much of a window to fight back (especially early on). Attacking one roots the character in place for a brief moment, which leaves them open to damage. This issue gets better later in game, when ranged secondary weapons become available AND character upgrades reduce the difficulty.Just to be clear, I didn't play this co-op, so I will not rate it, but I did buy it with co-op feature in mind. This game is definitely not designed to be a co-op experience. Game is mostly split between exploration and combat. A lot of gameplay is exploration and some of it is combat. Exploration of similar game in co-op just doesn't work, apart from few puzzles, unless everyone is following one player. Combat is outright bad for co-op, as most monsters get knocked backwards AND have contact damage, so 2 players can't reliably hit from same side and they can't surround it. You can't both fight the same enemy, unless both of you are ranged or want to chase it after every hit.Despite being released this game is still in development(at the time of review). There are a couple of bugs in game (they break achievements) that have only been fixed in beta version. The problem here is that you need some technical knowledge to transfer your save back from beta to main game. As of this review the bugs are at least 4 months old. Also there are few areas in game that are clearly meant to have content, but are instead blocked off, which is supposedly for future update content. Game being developed further is a huge positive, but it's only a pure positive to people who play it AFTER it's finished, and a small negative to people playing it now.To summarize I am having fun with the game, and I certainly see the audience for it, but it's a niche game and I think most people will not like it.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is not a finished product by any stretch. The fact that it's not listed in 'Early Access' when there is an in-game dungeon with a sign out front that literally reads 'Under Construction' is frankly deplorable.I wanted to recommend it—it's a generally fun game and the combat feels good, but there is just so much left to be desired, and this game doesn't even come close to competing with its competitors.In fairness, the concept of a roguelike open-world RPG is very well executed. Venturing into a dungeon becomes a procedurally-generated roguelike experience, while the overworld remains a traditional 'Legend of Zelda' or 'Metroid'-like experience, with all the trappings of such a game, for better or worse.The art and graphics are also fantastic, even if somewhat cliché in their genre. It looks, at face-value, like a high-quality game.Unfortunately, a number of very core features feel tacked on and meaningless, like shallow gestures with no substance. This includes the "story," which is so generic and tacked-on, it honestly feels like an afterthought.But the classes are the worst example—the game advertises a great number of distinct and varied classes to play, but they are anything but. Each 'class' is just the same generic swordfighter with slightly different stats and a different dash/leap.This is exacerbated by the fact that the secondary items like the bow and magic wand feel absolutely terrible to use. You can aim them freely around you, but there is no targeting reticule, making it extremely difficult to aim the weapons and use them precisely.So even if the Ranger and Mage get bonus damage with said items, it's rarely worth the effort, and just using the sword is going to be the default experience no matter the class.There are a number of other shallow, tacked-on features too. The farming mechanic is almost completely useless, offering nothing but a way to earn a currency which is very rarely used.The fishing mechanic is unlocked more than halfway through the game and does absolutely nothing to the wider game—no experience, no currency, no NPC favour, just a single achievement.The town-building mechanic is almost entirely pointless too. The NPCs that move into town may have a quest here and there, but there's no relationship or faction system, no dialogue besides a single generic line for each character, and no real incentive to actually invite NPCs to join the town at all.In fact, the game is so clearly unfinished that even after buying every building you can, and inviting every NPC into the town that you can, there are still empty, vacant plots of land that you can't do anything with, which just feels cheap, and a little bit frustrating, since it would seem, when you first start the game, that every single plot will eventually be filled.Regarding the actual dungeons, the core element of the gameplay loop, the bosses are dramatically and almost absurdly easier than the rest of the dungeons.There are also not enough varied rooms for the procedural generation, and you will constantly run into the same rooms over and over, even two or three times within a single dungeon.Extremely important mechanics and interactions, like the ability to cut down shortcuts with the sword, burn piles of wood with the lantern, and throw pots at switches in dungeons, are never explained, and can leave the player feeling extremely frustrated and confused at their seeming inability to progress further.And finally, and possibly most frustratingly at all, because the game is unfinished, it's very hard to tell which parts of the game are inaccessible at the current point in the story and which parts are actually not done, and can't be explored.Ultimately, this game needs a lot of work. In it's current state, it feels like half a game, and it should have never been published outside of Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun and I recommend buying it. It scratches the itch for top down zelda action. It has a bunch of heroes, great puzzles, and a grind mechanic that keeps you gathering and unlocking. But it's not perfect. 1. You save up gems to unlock something, and then have to find something before you can use it. Which feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Examples: I keep finding a place to brew potions in the dungeon, ok here's a shop that makes elixirs I'll save up the gems to build that...oh they make potions, but they don't sell any bottles. I have to save up and UNLOCK a dfferent shop first, then save up and buy the bottle, then brew the potion. AND this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ train of unlocking X things to get 1 thing happens all the time. I have a fully upgraded farm, that's probably really useful early game to make $ I bet, but I've never found the watering pail. So why let me unlock a farm and hide the tool I need? Why not just give me the F$%$!^! tool and let me find a better tool! Sorry it's just really frustrating design. 2. Tools feel really weak, you have to spend a lot of gems to upgrade the damage/speed/rate of your tools, but you could have just spent those gems on your sword damage. Which uses no ammo and you always have, so if you love the feeling and power of the bow/bomb/boomerang in Zelda sorry it's not going to feel as good here. 3. You can't really access the dungeons in any order. You have to get the tool from 1 dungeon to even get to the area around the next dungeon. I mean that's Zeldaish, but there's only 1 dungeon you can access (afaik) at the beginning. And so you will GRIND and grind that dungeon to level up your stats for a long time, and it's gets boring fighting the same enemies and solving the same room puzzles (in a different order, but the puzzle is always the same). If they fixed those points above, make the game more openy less locky it would be amazing. But they combined 2 unlock mechanics (gem spending and tool finding) in a way that clashes rather than improves the experience. So in short how to avoid this in the future:1: Give access to more than 1 dungeon the player can experience and beat from the beginning. 2. Give the weak tools quicker and easier. (especially if it's tied to a building you can buy like elixir and farm)2b. Be careful with nesting unlocks behind unlocks, done wrong it can kill the feeling of reward. 3. Hide and let the player find upgraded powerful tools (which you could also apply the gem upgrades to).FInally:The controls feel greet! The hero abilities are fun and different. I wish each hero had 2 abilities instead of 1 but their great. And whoever did the map design, dungeon designs, and puzzle designs did a really great job!

_childDocuments_.review: If you would like to play a Link to the Past ripoff but with really terrible tweaks and simply not fun mechanics, this game is for you. This game boasts of its random procedural generation, when it is really the same 12 tilesets but in a random order each time you enter the dungeon. The bosses were not a challenge at all.  Almost everywhere an enemy is able to get stuck on a different layer, making it impossible to kill them.  In the span of 12 hours, my game got soft-locked 4 times, due to lack of design effort on the dungeons. There are only about 8 items, and all of them are literally from the Zelda series, but are made to look like they aren't. The soundtrack consists of three songs that play regardless of where you are at, and sound just like - you guessed it - ZELDA. The hit registration in this game, is just awful. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, 16bit Zelda combined with Roguelite sounds great and in general, the game captures the oldschool feel quite well. Especially the combat and visual style are spot on and will take you back instantly. However, if you play online coop, the camera system ruins it because all players share the same screen and the camera only zooms out so far when players are spaced out. If you wander off just a little bit, everyone else will get stuck on the edge of the screen and hate you for that. Not so great in a game where most of the fun comes from exploration... Also, if one player enters a house like a shop or another room inside a dungeon, everyone else has to follow and gets teleported there instantly, no matter what they were doing at the time. This also means that if one player interacts with a shopkeeper and another player leaves the shop, the purchase of the first player gets cancelled and he's being teleported outside as well. I understand that a system like this was all you had back on retro consoles, but I don't understand why this is neccessary in a modern online coop where everyone could just have their own screens.If you are a die hard fan of oldschool Zelda and/or Rogeulites and not planning to play coop, this might be for you. Everyone else, be warned...

This is more of an opinion but it would be nice to see different attack patterns and harder to dodge attacks.The only time I perished to a boss was due to bug that rooted me to the floor.Audio.I appreciate this isn't a selling point for many but I have to give the audio a really low score.Every sound or piece of music has been used or heard in some form or another, having no sound at all as the credits roll was also a bit jarring.Gameplay.While not necessarily a bad or good thing if you titled this under another Zelda game you may not know the difference, especially with the level design, items, weapons and some of the sound effects.Was a little on the nose in places.With these points being said there is a lot of fun to be had here.The procedural dungeons up the replay value, multiplayer adds another layer of watching your friends die to a trap you've just set off, and having it be a more roguelike zelda style game isn't a bad thing, just needs that little more polish!With a small team of 2 I think Heliocentric Studios have made something entertaining and fun, even with my gripes I would still recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is WAY BETTER than it has any right to be. This takes Link to the past, Stardew valley, and Crosscode, then drops them into a blender and forces them to make love as they splash into a beautiful new amalgamation. Is it a triple A game? Nope. Is it smooth and responsive? Yes! Is it a roguelike? Barely-- Its closer to an rpg that has respawns than a rogue IMO.Has:Combat-Magic (Find spell "runes" while exploring to equip a new spell and spend mana)-Swords (Everyone gets one! fast and consumes active stamina)-Bows (Bows are chunky, slow, and satisfying!)-Hookshot, hit-them-with-a-book, punch them with gloves, etc.Exploration-Zelda style overworld-Quests and puzzles-Nooks and Crannies-Tons of environmental challenges-Swim around inside frog mouth!Village-Farming-Fishing-NPC quests-Pay the carpenter to build houses, workshops, etc-Minigames!Progression-Dungeon currency (gems) is used for upgrades, which you get from going into a dungeon. You drop all gems when you enter a new dungeon, so try to spend em all.-Gold is used for consumables as you unlock things.-Exploration will earn you things like the power gloves and farmtools, but unlocking most things is a quest or dungeon reward. While in a dungeon, you can get temporary versions of things.Doesn't have:MicrotransactionsRomanceEasy difficulty (Only normal, hard, and extreme IIRC)Overall, while still a teensy bit janky and derpy, its a loving homage to Link to The Past and is honestly fantastic. 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes is a otherwise very solid Zelda/Rogue-lite mashup marred by several technical and design issues. So, first thing first, be aware of what your getting with this game. The state the game is currently in, is not what should be considered a finished state. There are a number of quite severe bugs in both single and multiplayer that somewhat ruin the experience. Many of the bugs that existed at launch have already been fixed (1 week after launch) which gives me hope the remaining issues will also be fixed, and this recommendation is based on that.The core gameplay in Rogue Heroes is solid. It's fun, and the controls, audio, and graphics are all very satisfying. The challenge is fair, and the grind isn't too terrible, so it's easy to simply level your way past any obstacle that your skills can't handle (which is the lite part of rogue-lite). Playing in the overworld or any of the dungeons brings back memories of the best of the 16-bit era of Zelda games. So, with that out of the way, lets dive into the issues that still need to be addressed.On the technical side the worst unaddressed problem currently (at time of this review) is a network de-sync problem that makes the online co-op mode at best a frustrating experience, and at worst unplayable. Slightly less breaking but equally annoying when using steams play together feature to stream local co-op the audio is often horribly distorted and very loud leading to a physically painful experience until the remote players mute the games audio.On the design side, there are a few choices that are going to be much harder to fix as they'll require some re-evaluation of core gameplay. First, there are the power spheres. These are effectively collectibles, and finding all of them currently represents the primary end game activity in the game. The problem with them design wise, is they're utterly pointless. As you collect them, they allow you to retain an ever increasing amount of gems when you enter a dungeon (where normally you lose all unspent gems), but that's an utterly pointless effect. By the time you have enough power stones to where the effect is noticeable as more than a rounding error you don't actually have a use for gems anymore. Considering you'll likely have "beaten" the game by the time you have even a quarter of the power spheres (unless you've been going out of your way to specifically hunt them down), and also likely have purchased literally everything you can buy using gems, being able to retain more gems is utterly and completely useless.Secondly, there's the lack of end game content. There are 5 dungeons, and a final endless dungeon in the game (the devs are working on adding more dungeons though). Beating the 4 of the 5 dungeons (the 5th is optional and unlocks one of the classes) unlocks the final endless dungeon which is effectively the end of the game. Beating those 4 dungeons will take somewhere in the ballpark of 10 hours or so the first time. Once you know what you're doing it's probably doable in as little as 5 or 6 hours for most people. The endless dungeon is, honestly rather pointless. Yes you can keep pushing deeper and deeper into it, but there's very little point to doing so. Aside from an achievement at level 25, you get nothing by going deeper, and the dungeon doesn't really change much either. It's just the exact same thing over and over again against slightly stronger enemies for resources you have no use for. Rather than an endless dungeon, a new game+ mode that increased the difficulty of the original 4 dungeons probably would have been a better design.

name: Neon Abyss
detailed_description: Combining furious run ‘n’ gun action and deep, roguelike mechanics, Neon Abyss pits you as a member of ‘Grim Squad’ – a task force set-up by Hades himself to infiltrate the Abyss and defeat the New Gods. Death is not the end as every time you die, you’ll find yourself more empowered than before. As you progress through each dungeon, random item drops will be key in helping you infiltrate the Abyss and these passive effects can stack between every item. With no limit to how many can apply; a wide variety of combinations will make each run unique. With each run, you will be able to unlock new rooms, items, bosses, special rules and even new endings! This means each dungeon is unique and expandable, being tailored to your own specific playstyle. Hatch and Evolve Pets If you need some company on your journey into the depths of the abyss, or just some additional firepower or assistance, eggs can be found which will turn into a random pet that has a special ability and will evolve the longer you survive. Mini-Games Take a short break from slaying minions and take part in random mini-games that will also bag you some loot! Jump into Piano Performances, Meditation Challenge, Dance Competitions, and more – staying alive just got a lot more interesting!

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, I really enjoy this game a lot. There's times I've found myself letting time go out the window and end up going for "just one more run" and wind up playing for several more hours.As someone who's played a lot similar styles of games, I was pleasantly surprised with Neon Abyss. The gameplay, the music, the replay-ability all hit's the right notes. It's really easy to just get lost and keep playing. I really wish I had discovered it sooner. If you like other games such as Streets of Rogue, Dead Cells, Fury Unleashed and other similar rogue-likes, you'll find a good home here.The amount of combinations with weapons and items can be absurdly OP. What I enjoy most is that no two playthrough is ever alike. Item drops are randomized and there's plenty of variety.One thing I would like to see maybe implemented, is a way to remove an item you might get in a run. There's been a fair few runs where I'll find something and if you're not playing as Amir or have an ability to see what you're picking up, you can completely break a build. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, and is an excellent take on the side-scrolling twin-stick shooter, something there's not a whole lot of. The intra-run progression is great; while there are different guns you can find that vary in strength, there's also a plethora of Binding of Isaac-style upgrades that integrate into whatever gun you do have, adding things like damage, rate of fire, extra projectile range, extra bullets per shot, and more. This means that, even if RNG doesn't bless you with a good weapon, you'll scale up over the course of the run no matter what and end up with a fun weapon - the first run I won was actually just using my starter weapon, souped up with upgrades. There's an egg hatching system, too, which adds a fun Pokemon-type vibe to your progression, unlocking fun pets with a variety of effects as you play. There's also a persistent skill tree between runs to unlock new items, characters, and dungeon features. All in all, this is a very solid roguelite for any fan of the genre (or run-and-gun games in general).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly a breath of fresh air. I'm surprised I don't see more people talking about this game. It seems the developers saw what most other roguelikes do, and tried to alleviate the most annoying aspects of them.Pros:Most items I have encountered don't have downsides, direct upgrades to your build are truly and factually direct upgrades in most cases. This is such a refreshing change of pace. There are a few items that can hurt your run, but these are just a result of strange mechanics interactions, and may be funny at first.Items seem to be designed to synergize and create really fun builds, sometimes I'll get a whole string of items in a run that seem to complement my build very well. It makes me wonder if there is a hidden mechanic to favor spawning items for specific builds per-run, which would actually be really neat!One thing that is honestly in my opinion a genius design is relegating most "followers/familiars/babies" into a unique type of floor pickup. (in the same category as hearts, coins, etc) You gain them through "mystery eggs" that hatch into followers with cool effects, they can even upgrade themselves. Relegating these followers into a unique pick-up rather than dedicating full items to each one is such a clever way to mitigate bloating the item pool with mediocre effects.The game doesn't seem lock anything behind the difficulty modes, aside from unlocking an even harder difficulty mode through hard mode. It's nice to see this game going against the trend of locking vital content and progression behind its hardest modes. In my opinion, difficulty modes should just be a means of which for the player to modify the experience to be more fun and engaging if they so choose.Guns can be upgraded by your builds, and there's no ammo management in this game.The game lets you disable items, enemies, and other content, but with a caveat: disabling enough items and enemies will disable achievements and progression. However, it gives you enough breathing room to remove a handful of stuff from the game and still continue. This allows you to pick and choose what your want your game experience to be, disable items you personally do not like or have bad experiences with, etc. This is such a cool idea, and really puts control in the hands of the player! Think an item ruins your run too much? Think an item is useless? Just disable it! You can also choose to disable any and everything you have unlocked, with no downside.Cons:You can't see what items do before you pick them up, and for a few items even after, making certain mechanics unclear and forcing the player to consult the wiki sometimes, if the wiki was updated that is. There are characters who CAN see this info before hand, but have a major downside. This is somewhat disappointing, especially after having played games like Slay the Spire which is very clear about what items do, letting you see what they do on mouse-over. I don't find hiding info from the player very engaging to the experience, just annoying and a memory exercise.There is a type of door and chest in the game that is possibly the most annoying thing ever. They require coins to open. Upon paying, they have a random chance to open. I have spent lots of money to open a chest or door before, and it's so frustrating. I feel like the door is the worst instance of this, because you could end up paying 25 coins to open a door to a crane game, which costs another sum just to activate.Everything is a currency for unlocking doors and containers, pretty much. While not necessarily bad, it does limit the niche of keys.Overall:Get this game. It's such a good take on this genre and doesn't actively make you hate yourself for playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Binding of Issac with guns. A few enemies are pretty much the same and a few power-ups and familiars as well. (Not the right terms but still.) That's it. A daily challenge and some single player challenges would make such a big difference and make me more likely to keep coming back. I haven't unlocked all the characters yet but I feel like there isn't really a reason to. I beat the game just fine with the basic characters. Bosses need way more health too. They die way too fast so there isn't much reason to learn the attack patterns. Button remapping is crap. I can't rebind anything to any key that isn't a letter on the keyboard (no ctrl, alt, shift) I can't rebind the melee button. Hope you like F as melee cause that's all you get. Oh you like F as the interact key well guess you gonna be stabbing, dropping mines, etc on a lot of doors instead of opening them.No controller support is a weird choice. This would be a fantastic game to get nice and toasty and just recline and look at the pretty lights.Overall I would say I got my moneys worth. (I had more fun with this than I would at an arcade for the same amount of money) This just has the potential to be a MUCH better game with very small tweaks. Idk maybe these complaints are known and it's harder than it seems. I'm no game developer what do I know.

_childDocuments_.review: There's things I like in this game, but I don't like this game. Overall, it's an okay rogue-lite shoot 'em up in the vein of Binding of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, or Undermine. That said, I feel like those games do what they do much better than Neon Abyss, and the mixing of mechanics doesn't do much to elevate NA.Pros:++The soundtrack is fun, upbeat, and fits well with the tone of the game+The visuals, while nothing extraordinary, look good, and readability is solid on projectiles, enemies, etc.+The basic gameplay is smooth enough, providing good feedback and the controls are responsiveCons:--The bugs. Oh man, I have lost multiple runs to enemies dropping through the floor, getting locked out of rooms for no reason or softlocked in them to name the worst of them.--While the basic gameplay is solid, the lack of enemy (and boss) variety will start to wear down the fun of it, and makes the game really easy after you learn the enemy's patterns.--Permanent upgrades are available, but are locked behind a grindy system that doesn't feel rewarding to progress in. I do like that the upgrades add things to the environment or possible extra rooms, but it's too little too late by the time you get them. Good idea, terrible implementation.TL;DR. Neon Abyss is a solid rogue-lite, but similar games in the genre (BoI, EtG) came along years ago and stole what thunder it would have to add.Score: A one-shot-only gun range/10

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelikes live and die depending on the addictiveness and enjoyability of their core gameplay loop and Neon Abyss simply fails to capture the "magic" of its contemporaries.I am usually not a fan of judging a game by comparing it to others. But Neon Abyss takes such heavy inspiration from games such as The Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon, that comparisons are unavoidable and I am sad to say that Neon Abyss falls short of its forefathers in almost every way. Lets get into the good things first: The game is beautiful and the Soundtrack is fitting and quite catchy, though it gets repetitive quickly.   The Gameplay has the potential to be up there with the best that a Roguelike could possibly offer. Shooting is very satisfying and the movement feels fluid.I'll get into how the game doesn't utilize this promising framework further on.My very first run was very enjoyable, the music had me bopping my head and the bossfights seemed very interesting.But the scepticism set in when I beat the first "final boss" on my very first run. I am not here to show off, I am in fact not very good at all at 2D games, it took me many hours to not have my ass handed to me in Cuphead for example. The game is simply that stupidly easy. The "challenge" comes in the form of grinding.The gameplay loop consists of getting a useless run, either dying or painstakingly finishing it over the course of way too much time once or at most twice and then getting an op run. So while you will have an entirely unrewarding and slow experience two thirds of the time, the remaining third consists of equally unrewarding runs, where nothing even remotely poses a threat. The only thing stopping you from playing through the entire game on the first good run that you get, is an arbitrary barrier to your progress, in that a run unavoidably ends once you beat a "final boss" that you haven't defeated before. Once you reach the fourth "Manager" or so you may only unlock further bosses by spending a very scarce resource that you only get by defeating previous bosses. And so the grind begins. This resource is the only way to permanently "progress" in the game, by granting you the ability to unlock Upgrades, Features and even characters and it is incredibly time-intensive to come by. This grind doesn't get any more exciting considering that I got bored of the repetitive enemies on only my second run. The "variety" in the form of bosses seemingly fleshes out the game, but they are all so incredibly unthreatening and boring in terms of their attack patterns and defensive options that they quickly melt into the colorless mass.Finishing a run usually takes a little less than an hour for which you are handsomely rewarded with around 20 points, which equates to maybe 2 permanent upgrades in the very beginning. To reach these permanent upgrades you will have to spend half your points on single use "Trial Items" though, so permanent progress isn't even guaranteed. Through these you'll often be left with the prospect of getting even less of a challenge on your next run aswell as not being able to afford anything permanent such as characters or straight up upgrades. So you play for around an hour, upon which your run is forcefully ended only to progress by about 1% in a skill tree to make the game even easier, although it is already basically impossible to fail. This is what this game considers its gameplay loop and it isn't really a loop, but moreso a straight line. I know what you're thinking, but let me assure you that simple damage and health rebalancing wouldn't fix the issue, because the system is inherently flawed. The game is not designed in a way that will ever allow you to feel like you "get it" and know how to reliably avoid all damage. Not receiving any damage is moreso a product of killing everything and anything the game throws at you immdiately. Even on my very first run the fights were usually resolved by immediately clearing out every room and basically facetanking the bosses, since the game absolutely drowns you in health and shield drops. Neon Abyss copied the entirety of BOI's framework without realizing or emulating what made it satisfying in the first place. The inherent difficulty and rewarding nature of the gameplay loop, perhaps even the obtuse story that creates intrigue. Neon Abyss has none of this and it feels like you are dripfed progress simply by breathing. Let me clarify that I didn't go into this expecting a game that would be able to surpass the likes of BOI. However,  having played and greatly enjoyed Undermine among other (obviously BOI inspired) roguelikes, I expected to get my moneys worth in the form of a satisfying, well rounded first "playthrough".Instead I received a promising first impression and the feeling of complete and utter emptiness after every completed run.I somewhat enjoyed my time with the game and I may even play it again, however I can't help but feel like I'm wasting my time whenever I play it.If you simply want to experience what the game has to offer and you enjoy leaning back and not really thinking about what you're doing you might still enjoy this. I didn't though.The game didn't offend me in any way, and aside from a few nitpicks there aren't many things that will immediately stick out as bad or annoying, but I simply cannot recommend a game that fails to motivate me to play it further even in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game in it's current state, although it is a decent timewaster for what it currently is. The game feels and plays really smoothly, has pretty aesthetics and all, but aside from that, it's very bland at it's current state. Neon Abyss tries to use wacky weapons and 'infinite' item combinations as a selling point, but in reality just about all the guns are worse than the stock one, and the items are generally just slightly faster firing rate or more damage. There isn't a whole lot of enemy variance, as you go down the levels in each run all that changes is that they start doing contact damage and just get more HP. There isn't a whole lot of enemy variety either, and changing the difficulty of the game just makes enemies take a little longer to kill. One of the biggest issues is the upgrade system they use, you get multiple pages of skills to unlock that cost these boss token things, and you only get one per boss takedown. The prices of the later upgrades are so exorbitant that it would take multiple full game clears just to get a few on a page filled with many, so it becomes a grindfest (not even a fun one at that either). I'm gonna try to stay optimistic for the future of the game though since it just released, hopefully they will listen to people's complaints and address them to improve on the many issues currently present in it. All in all, I really can't recommend this right now, wait for a sale or after some future updates hit that fix things if you really wanna bite the bullet 💜

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame I have to leave a negative review, because Neon Abyss is a game I really wanted to like. Right out of the gate, though, it feels slow, quiet, and uninspired. I found a lot of QoL issues in the demo, but figured that build's about 8 months old, so that's not really too much of an issue- but save for one, they're all still present in the base game.Within 40 minutes of playing, I found the following problems:The trailers will have you believe this is a fast paced, Gungeon-esque game, and I was hoping this would scratch the Gungeon itch, but instead it just makes that itch worse. Instead of taking the positives of Gungeon (its humor, polish, core gameplay loop, balance) it seems to take the negatives (visually busy design, pacing, pre-update slow backtracking) while offering almost nothing new to the table. Babies are a neat concept, but even they aren't completely polished, and that's the game's only standout factor- I had a baby that split into about 10 zombie babies, and it was never explained why- I had to go to the pause menu to figure it out. I never saw the actual health of the zombie babies either, and the item text implies it would just continually split itself, which I figured wasn't right, and sure enough they all died a few seconds later.I feel like Neon Abyss doesn't know what it wants to be. It wants to be Isaac, it wants to be Enter the Gungeon, but what it lacks from those two games is staying power. I put this in the same category as Steredenn and Wizard of Legend, where they're games I really wanted to like, but out of the gate i saw pacing and polish issues that I just can't overlook. I'm willing to overlook problems with a game if it's fun, because no game is perfect, but Neon Abyss... isn't fun.A game being derivative is okay and expected in today's industry. Monolith, for example, is one of my favorite roguelites, and it's just about one of the most derivative roguelites you're going to find. This is derivative for the wrong reasons. Where Monolith takes existing ideas, iterates on them, and seamlessly integrates them together into a cohesive experience, Neon Abyss feels like it's taking existing ideas, throwing them in, and praying it works, and the way I see it, it doesn't work.I think this game has the potential to be good, but it's going to take a lot of changes. The game, overall, needs faster pacing (at the very least optional like in Gungeon) and needs to be able to stand by itself, as well as a lot of quality of life iteration. If i found this many gripes in 40 minutes, that tells me there's probably a lot of others, too.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Buy Binding of Isaac instead.The game has a good art style and a decent idea of what the game should be. But there are also a ton of design choices that become annoying and frustrating the longer you go in the game.And a lot of the time, I just think back to the Binding of Isaac, and how much I wish the devs had just straight up copied some of the design philosophies from it.For example, you can see what minion/follower/companion you're getting before acquiring it in Binding of Isaac, and you almost always remain in control of it. In Neon Abyss, it's ALWAYS random. You can get a minion/follower/companion that may be very detrimental to your run, which just leaves you wishing for the little bastard to just die already. And not only that, you have actually no control of them. You need a health pick up? Race your little buddy to it or they'll grab it to try and give you shields. Need money? Grab it before Mini Trump snatches it up before you. Need to hold your fire in order to not corrupt a crystal chest? No worries, your lil' buddy managed to land a shot on it through the power of chaos theory.In my opinion, never pick up eggs at the start of a run, they're a big part of the game but not worth the hassle.A lot of the pick-ups are what I'd consider borderline useless. And even worse still, is the sheer number of them. So plenty of pick-ups to choose from, but very little of value to be had. And the good pick-ups are all basically the same. Extra jump or the ability to fly along with weapon damage, fire rate and bullet/projectile count. In over 30 hours of playing, never once have I been happy or found it useful to get an item that either increases my melee damage or gives me a chance to get a crystal/heart/shield or whatever when I manage to get a melee kill. The melee is bad, and none of the upgrades address it or fix it.The game leaves me wishing they would have carried over more of the good ideas from Binding of Isaac. "Angel rooms" in Neon Abyss are the only ones really worth it as it can be obtained for free. Meanwhile, the "Devil room" in Neon Abyss, is absolutely atrociously bad. You MUST take damage consistently to obtain it. You MUST sacrifice a heart container to even be able to see which items are on offer. Items that aren't even necessarily exclusive to the "Devil room". It's just not worth it unless you NEED to go and defeat Ares.Meanwhile the devil rooms in Binding of Isaac has you able to see all the items on offer before you make a purchase with the exception of a rare floor curse. Devil rooms in Binding of Isaac are also less costly to get to to begin with, in  Neon Abyss it dictates that you HAVE to take repeated instances of damage to fill up the meter, no devil room until it's full. In Binding of Isaac you work with less guarantees due to it being based on a percentage chance of getting one, but you can influence that percentage, and doing so is also way less costly in terms of health & play style. In Neon Abyss it's frustrating how easily it can be to accidentally turn towards Devil rooms despite trying to avoid it, and reversing it towards Angel Rooms is an uphill struggle at best. If you're unfortunate and collide with an 'evil' crystal chest, door or whatever.. you could be half-way to an Angel room and it'd reverse your work to the point you'd be half-way to a Devil room now, but doing the reverse of using a 'good' crystal item, does nowhere near that much, meaning pure RNG can almost block you into a Devil room, where it'd straight up be faster to just work on obtaining the Devil room to clear the bar, rather than trying to slowly reverse the damage. It's not fun, just frustrating. And you don't feel like you're in control of the circumstances leading to it a lot of the times.I don't know if this is something the Devs eventually patched in or I unlocked from progressing in the game, but the starting levels of the game got harder enemies in it now. Normally I don't mind a challenge, but they all seem to come in a variety of long lasting invincibility where you then get a small time frame to deal damage before going back to being impossible to kill. They're not really a challenge, they're just slow and tedious to deal with.The game does have a large unlock tree, but one so large and costly that in order to see it to the end of it, you'll likely be driven to stop playing due to the shortcomings of the game. In Binding of Isaac, you'd have some fun and interesting though of course also sometimes annoying and tedious tasks to complete in order to unlock some things, but it at least gave you something to do and some variety, a tangible goal to work towards. Only thing left to do in Neon Abyss is to just play the game some more as the unlock tree works with currency obtained from defeating bosses.Did Binding of Isaac ever make areas impossible to get to unless you had some special mobility items? Yes.Does Neon Abyss do it a lot more often than Binding of Isaac for less reward? Yes.Biggest advice I can give a new player is to keep your browser open with the game wiki's full item list. Because even when you get the item pick-up that actually lets you read what an item does in-game, it doesn't work in the shop where you have to buy it first, for some god awful reason.The game does have good potential, but it needs a lot of work to get to that potential.

There's also some story, it's not as infuriating blowing yourself up every 2 seconds (though most of my upgrades were reset so maybe it still happens?  Some runs though are crap, You can say it's RNG if you want, sure. It might very well be, though I'd love if there was more cross-play between the items. The items are very unique and well thought out there are times though where your pick-ups are worthless. Or could be amazing, but only if you get a different or upgraded gun that never comes.  Now I know the game is supposed to be a bit rogue-like (or so it seems) and i've cruised through all the bosses (great designs) but I dont want to grind.  suggestions: Constructive criticism. Two untouched rooms should activate the Wisdom bar rather than a chance of not finding a purple chest/door until last room (if then).  Make an option where both bars activate simultaneously, but you can only choose one of them as reward. Wisdom/Athena bars get penalized still (maybe?) but let the damage stack for Ares.  Or, make it a transition rule. If you get hit in a room, Ares will fill Next room hit in, if you don't get hit Wisdom/Athena gets filled next time you aren't hit through a room.  Generates a skill style that seems to already be there but doesn't cause a negative, sliding back on a bar/skill/gameplay is such a game breaker.My 2 cents, take it or leave it.----------------------------No Review--Go ahead and read below if you want my original "positive review" I have to change it, new items new unlocks etc etc all focus on that same mechanic that is infuriating bombs, chained negatives and teeny tiny tweaks wherein the game gets worse the more you unlock. _childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a fast-paced action platformer game developed by Veewo Games and published by Team17. The game features a neon-colored world filled with enemies, power-ups, and unlockable characters.Players take on the role of a member of the Grim Squad, tasked with descending through a procedurally generated dungeon to defeat the New Gods. The game's fast-paced gameplay is enhanced by a variety of weapons, items, and abilities that can be collected and upgraded.The game's pixel art graphics are vibrant and engaging, with a unique visual style that adds to the game's overall charm. The soundtrack is also well-designed, with upbeat electronic music that complements the game's frenetic pace.One of the game's standout features is its replayability, with randomly generated levels that offer a new experience with each playthrough. The game also includes multiple endings and secrets to discover, adding to its longevity.However, the game's difficulty can be a drawback, as it can be challenging even for experienced gamers. The game's randomly generated levels can also be frustrating, as they can sometimes result in unfair or imbalanced encounters.Overall, Neon Abyss is a fun and addictive action platformer game with a unique visual style and great replayability. Its challenging gameplay and engaging visuals make it a must-play for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Free: gifted to me by a friend. Edit: I have since unlocked everything on the "skill trees" and beat all the bosses, and had fun doing it!  Recently (Jan, 2022) there was another free content update with some new bosses, so I paid to buy the DLCs.  The extra characters are....meh....but I think they deserve some money out of me for all the fun I've had.  Have not reached the new bosses yet but I'm working on it!  Original review follows:Roguelite platformer/shooter with zillions of items and guns, and quite a few pets too. Shoot the badguys, and don't get hit by their shots.  It's nice that many enemies don't damage you on-contact, just from their actual attacks.  At the end of each stage there's a boss fight, and after several stages, there's a big boss called a manager.  So far I only beat the first one. 5 types of 'currency' in the game:-HP, which you can sometimes pay directly or indirectly to buy things or access new areas. Restore them by picking up full/half hearts. Moldy hearts may heal or harm you. -coins. Gain them as copper(1)/silver(5)/gold(10)/larger-keys-grenades / explosions, there are plenty of obstacles that will only disappear/open from explosions. -crystals, which you can think of as MP. They are used to power your RMB special ability. Some doors/chests can be opened for 3/2 crystals, or you can shoot them to turn them into a 'spiked' version that instead costs 0.5HP to open. On a run you can find big yellow coins, which go towards unlocking things on a skill tree including new characters.  Some of the skill-trees end in a one-time-use bonus that seems pretty dumb...the longest skill tree ends in double-jump (one-time-use), though you can sometimes get that, or even flight, from RNGesus during regular gameplay. There are several characters you can unlock in-gme (and more you can buy as DLC), they vary in health/shields/keys/grenades and their special abilities.  I like the black guy (default version) that lays landmines.  At the risk of hurting yourself, you effectively have infinite explosions.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a Maybe option for recommendations. This game is a visual and audible treat, but the mechanics are not. Like straight up reach out and jab you in the eye not enjoyable.Some examples:- there is an item that give the chance of shooting an explosive rocket, sounds sweet right? No its a trap and you'll end up hurting yourself as you try to shoot boxes because you were one pixel away and didn't melee (not to mention trying to shoot enemies that rush you)- Synergies in general. they just feel really lackluster, like really really pointless for the most part. In Isaac when you get a tear upgrade it can completely change a run in Neon Abyss not so much. Extra fire rate based on coins, faster fire rate with more pets, bigger bullets. All good things yes but all very bland as well.- Melee. You have a melee weapon, there is no keybind for it, but don't worry the game will choose for you if you get close enough... because removing player control from their character is always a good idea.- Pets. In the game there are a few rooms that are set up so that you have to use barrels to break open blocks to access things. As the enemy can cause them to explode sometimes you must prioritize getting to them before the room is clear, normally not a problem EXCEPT pets will auto shoot at enemies even if they don't have line of sight. Which means boom you no longer get access to those chests/items.- Athena/Ares. For every room you don't take damage you build up progress to Athena if you take damage you build to Ares. This is a nice reward for skillful play and salve if you get dunked on for a few rooms. But there are also crystal items that can be used and reward progress towards the Athena/Ares meter. All your hard work for the past few rooms can be removed by simply TOUCHING one thats "turned" (in addition to doing damage). Your pets will screw you here as well by turning them as they try to shoot and enemiesTLDR: Ok game that shoots itself in the foot with mechanics. Isaac punishes the player for doing stupid stuff this game just does it randomly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential and I really hope the dev team keeps pushing updates to reach that potential. In no general order this would be my wish list.- Weapons need to be buffed. Most of the time it feels better to keep the default gun. Charge and laser weapons feel pointless when most enemies go down in a few shots. Particularly when the most overpowered I've felt has been when carrying a default gun with a lot of damage increase, fission, and ricocheting bullets.- More enemies. The enemy variety is okay is on par with most rougelikes. But when weapons are not all that interesting that leads to stale gameplay over time.- Allow us to see what items/weapons do before picking them up. The game even acknowledges this is a benefit as there is a character who can preview them. Some of the items genuinely hurt gameplay, making picking them up a gamble when you can't drop them. Picking up the "drop mines whenever you jump" item ruined one of my runs, when your explosions can damage you this is a horrible ability. Now I just look up every item/gun on the wiki before I pick it up. Many roguelikes do this and it's a bad design choice. - Fix bugs. For being a released game there are quite a few bugs. Mostly harmless and visual. But at times game breaking. - The melee/shooting logic is really bad. Why do I sometime shoot boxes/enemies when I'm standing right next to or even on top of them? This makes melee a mechanic that is better to just ignore.- Please have the character move their gun when moving the cursor while no enemies are present. This may seem really minor, but it feels weird to see your character running around always pointing their gun forward. It almost makes entering a room with enemies feel jarring.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nicely made game. The challenge is appropriate for a roguelike and offers great replayability via all the unlockable items and guns. If you're experienced with these games, the best I can offer as a description is the gameplay from rogue legacy, isaac, and gungeon all mixed together in the setting from hades with an artstyle that is uniquely its own. Movement is responsive and clean, I always get what I expect on the screen when moving around and the movement in general feels fluid. The game is tough but offers a lot of opportunity to solve small puzzles for items and consumables if you're careful not to obliterate everything in sight when entering/clearing a room. I have not felt supremely underpowered on any run that I've done in my 40 hours so far; you will find yourself stuck without keys, frags, money, or crystals occasionally, but usually not all at the same time.I like the pet system from the game which can reward good play by pets surviving longer, evolving, and giving better benefits. These kinds of variety are what keep the game interesting and replayable. I do hope that they add more pets in the future.All that being said, the game's animation and artstyle are amazing. I love the unique take: Cyberpunk Hell.........Where else are you going to see that? The music compliments the game fantastically and the DLC is all reasonably priced and adds actual variance to the game. Overall, I would give this game a 9/10 with definite room to grow to a 10 with updates or significant DLC. That being said, very glad I found this gem of a game, I'm sure 40 hours is just the beginning!

_childDocuments_.review: To be completely honest, this game feels like it was made by someone who has never played a rougelike in their life. Everything in this game just feels bad, and there's no flow in the game play. This game is quite literally this: lets fill the screen with as much ♥♥♥♥ as possible. The vast majority of the mechanics just feel like they're missing something.Positives: you want to see big number, here you go! This is a pretty mindless game, so it's good for when you don't really want to focus or pay attention. The artstyle is nice too, and the progression system is fine. If you want an easy game, here you go.My absolute #1 complaint is the fact that in the later parts of the run, you're literally not able to see anything because of all the flashing gun lights and whatnot, making it impossible to actually try and dodge bullets. This bothers me so much- there's no option to reduce the amount of effects on screen or highlight enemy bullets- THIS NEEDS TO BE A FEATURE YOU ARE LITERALLY UNABLE TO PLAY THE GAME. LITERALLY EVERY RUN I CANT SEE ANYTHING BY THE END OF IT IT'S NOT FUN. The game is quite literally is unplayable at this stage.There seems to be little to no skilled game play as well, pretty much every run boils down to this: get as much damage as possible. Very braindead gameplay.Another negative is that all the characters practically feel the same. Just in general all the runs tend to feel like a repeat of the previous, it's just an endless cycle of the same exact run. Who wants to play the exact same run over and over and over? Whenever I play this game I feel like I'm slamming my head into the wall over and over and over.And more than anything- the game just isn't fun. When I get hit instead of feeling like oh I could've dodged that or I could've outplayed it, I often feel cheesed and just annoyed.Honestly there are so many better rougelikes to play. This is the most watered down baby rougelike thats not fun or skillfull. I honestly don't know why this is so highly reviewed, if you're an actual rougelike player stay away from this game. I'm a real hardcore rougelike player and my opinion is that this is a bottom of the barrel tier rougelike. Don't waste your time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it, and a lot that doesn't. By far are the biggest issue with it in general in my opinion is the general room design (primarily that it leads to a lot of unavoidable damage rooms). There are a few specific rooms and combos that cause particular grief. Any room with a bomb wall that requires you to throw the bomb while falling (usually next to a jump pad) is extremely frustrating, because of how little control you have over bombs. They throw out horizontally at a specific angle and it can be extremely easy to waste bombs in these rooms or damage yourself. The other is any room with a staircase that spawns the enemies that fire two bullets downwards then split and move horizontally. Visually, it seems like standing on the lower level of the staircase would make this pass over you - it does not, and you will get hit.Rooms also tend to pen you into one corner with the monster spawn locations instantly. A lot of the design decisions of this game are more or less taken from top-down roguelite games, but because this is 2d with gravity to contend with many of these decisions do not work well.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a crazy, frantic, action-packed roguelite which I feel will grow even better with time as the developers seem to actively engage with the community for feedback. I'll go ahead and summarize some of the positives and negatives of the game from my experience so far.+ Fluid movement and shooting mechanics+ Vibrant colours+ Plethora of room designs+ Lots of different enemies that increase with progression+ Great pixel-graphics+ Plenty of pop-culture references+ Interesting and diverse synergies+ Solid soundtrack + Learning curve that isn't too steep+ Progression based rewards (items, characters etc.)+ Unique experiences across runs+ Decision making is incredibly important (investigating room layouts, usage of keys and grenades)+ Strategy is equal to mechanics and skill+ Addictive gameplay-loop- Some rooms are incredibly goofy and seemingly impossible not to take damage in- Luck proves to be a major part in progression at times (critical on hard and abyssal)- Hatched eggs prove much more detrimental than beneficial regularly- Small bugs occur from time to time (etc. Ghost enemy stuck outside of screen view, almost ended a great run)- Portal network isn't available in every room of a level- Bosses can be a little too similar at times (etc. Johnny + Kimmy)In conclusion the positives outweigh the negatives pretty heavily so I would definitely recommend neon abyss to anyone looking for a new adventure in the roguelite scene.

The starting options are a dude who starts with 1 grenade, or a girl who starts with a knife AND an extra tank of health.-Unlocks that add nothing to the enjoyment of the game, just more randomization.If any of that sounds fun to you then maybe you'll enjoy this but it wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by stating that I did enjoy the game while it lasted, however I have no desire to play it any further. This review is also going to mention The Binding of Isaac (henceforth referred to as TBOI) a good number of times, so it'll be clearest if you've played that. This review is based upon the game without the DLC.The gameplay is pretty straightforward when you look at the tags. It's a 2D roguelite shooter, you move through levels consisting of non-randomized rooms placed randomly next to each other in a grid system. When you reach the last level (up to nine) the run is over and you're reset back to the starting hub. Every level has 1 boss room, 1 item room containing an item, 1 shop room and 1 duel room which rewards the player with another item. To get stronger the player collects these items, which give the player various bonuses ranging from straight up more damage to making it so bullets bounce off of walls or explode. The game uses 6 types of resources, hearts and shields, which are the players' health, bombs and keys which can unlock areas and chests, coins which are used to buy items in the shop, and lastly crystals which can be used to use your weapon's active ability (if it has one) or use certain purple objects.The game obviously took inspiration from TBOI, which also has the rooms listed above, coins, bombs, keys, hearts, shields (soul hearts in TBOI). However, I would never call this game an isaac clone, as the gameplay is too different from TBOI.The crystals are part of the game's most interesting feature: Wisdom vs Violence, this game's version of TBOI's angel vs devil system.Throughout the game you will find various purple doors, chests and crystals. Shoot them and they will turn red and spiky. While purple, you can use crystals to activate the object and start the wisdom meter. Activate more purple objects or finish rooms without getting hit to fill up the meter. While red (and spiky) you can touch the object, which will hurt the player and initialize the Violence meter. Fill it up by activating red objects or getting hurt in rooms (once per room). Once full, you can teleport to another room not connected to the rest of the map. If you went for Wisdom, you can choose between 2 items and get one for free, for violence the player will have to sacrifice a heart container and get to choose between 3 items (up to 5 later in the game). The game also has an egg/pet system, which evolves TBOI's 'babies' (which are mostly pretty useless) and turns them into an integral gameplay feature. Eggs can be found throughout the run and can later 'hatch', which will either result in "hatch failed", which gives the player nothing or it can hatch into a random pet which can do anything from just shooting at enemies to picking up coins and dropping random pickups. Okay, so you're playing the game, you've reached the final level a couple times, what do you get? Neon Abyss uses a system a lot of roguelikes use in the form of a currency (Faith Gems, in this case) earned throughout each run and are the only thing not lost upon the end of the run. Faith Gems are gained upon defeating a boss and are used to unlock new items, characters or dungeon upgrades.This is the second biggest issue the game has that limits its replayability. In TBOI item unlocks all have different requirements, like "Beat X Boss with Y Character" or "Finish level X without getting hit". In Neon Abyss, everything is unlocked using the same currency, gained in the same way.This is pretty personal, so take it with a grain of salt. At time of writing, I've played the game for exactly 8 hours. In this time I've beaten every administrator including Ares and Athena. I have only gained enough Faith Gems to unlock 1 of the 6 unlockable characters, meaning progression is very slow, not to mention that later upgrades get more expensive. Slow progression is fine, but not when it's so linear and uninteresting. I've already mentioned that a lot of rooms can be cleared by standing in the entrance, this problem is magnified if you have a weapon with long range, as you can kill most enemies without them even being able to hit you. This is also true for hard mode. I did like the game for my time with it, learning the (limited amount of) rooms, (limited amount of) bosses and (less limited amount of) guns but it simply lacks the replayability of a game like The Binding of Isaac because of its boring items and progression system. I also want to mention here  that you can't rebind actions to buttons like 'Mouse4', 'Mouse5' or the 'Shift' key for some reason, a truly baffling decision. Not recommended for it's current price or even half off. I would pick it up if it ever drops to 5$ or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Because Steam doesn't let users post reviews in terms of score, I'm forced to give a not recommend because the gameplay is just not that good, though it's still at the least a 6/10.  After defeating a boss, you can pick up upgrades, but these mostly affect either your DPS or health and not radically alter gameplay like Enter the Gungeon -  a game that serves as obvious inspiration to this game.  While this ensures that all boss drops are useful  to an extent, it reduces the replay value of the game, a poison for roguelikes.  The guns all have infinite ammo, so that's one less aspect of resource management for those seeking them out.  The massive downside is that you can only ever hold one gun at a time. This makes combos non-existent and the game very unengaging. In fact, there is a character who can specifically combine two weapons into one as a bandaid solution for this very problem, but the way the combination works is just so lazy and unimaginative it's not worth mentioning - just a combination of those two gun sprites shooting both types of bullets at once.In terms of quality of life, the game actually does most its job well, with remappable everything and difficulty selection anytime in the hub area with no penalty, you can also customize the weapons and passives to disable the garbage you accidentally unlock, so no more Dead Cell BS here.  The one biggest gripe I have, however, is the translation quality. Without mincing words, it's honestly atrocious, combining broken syntax with wrong grammar. While this is mostly limited to the character selection and not item description from what I've seen, it's still grating to see them in-game.Edit: I have maxed out my gears and unlock all characters by modifying my saves, just to see if the game does increase in variety in the late game as some have said. That is unfortunately not the case for what I described above. Of course, apparently I'm just a guy complaining about the translation quality of another language IN ENGLISH, and not the language that I intend my criticism to reflect, take it with a grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a fun little Rogue-Lite Run and Gun Shooter. It draws heavily from Isaac in places, like having  permanent health and temporary health, angel rooms and Devil Deals (essentially, although you do have a bit more control over which one you trigger). It's a fun experience none the less, once you've gotten to grips with the controls, which are a little different from most platformers (Jump is mapped to up on the D-Pad by default) you'll soon be filling the screen with ridicuous amounts of bullet hell and beam spam. The default difficulty level is probably a bit too low however, as once you've got a half decent gun and leveled it up or added more bullets to your shots, it's almost trivial to lay waste to most of what you'll encounter. By the time you get to the final two bosses the screens are often so chaotic that the only really viable tactic that you need is to tank their damage and blast them to hell. It's not a subtle game.On the base difficulty, it's only taken me 17 hours of play to unlock and beat all of the bosses. I'd probably recommend playing on Hard Difficulty for more experienced players. There is more playtime available if you want to unlock all of the items and characters, but I think I am very close to seeing all that this game has to offer. It's been a fun time, but I can't help but wish for a little more depth, or variety of enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game, it has too many issues at the present which I’ll outline below. – The whole game is repetitive and a grind. To advance the game, you have to defeat ‘managers’ which are the final level bosses. The first manager is found at the end of level five. After you beat it, an additional level with another manager is unlocked. But you don’t get to advance to the next level straight away, you are forced back to the beginning, and now you have to beat six levels to unlock the next manager. Rinse and repeat until there are eight levels.After that, you still have to run through all the same levels, but now you have to get to a special room to find a token that drops randomly so that you can access the next two managers. This wouldn’t be so bad if these were optional bosses, but it is necessary to beat them to advance the game.I’m sorry, but who thought that this was good game design? You play well enough to get to the room, but no token? Guess what? You might as well start a new run grinding through the same levels that you have already played multiple times at this point. Like I said, repetitive.  – For the first couple of runs, the music is ok. But OMG, after several runs it becomes repetitive and grating. For the love of God, please add some more variety to the music! After several runs, I got burnt out on the soundtrack. Anyone who says the music is great should reevaluate after 10-15 hours of play. I can almost guarantee that they will change their opinion of the music. Come back after 15 hours and see if you still think the music  is good. – Often times there is so much on the screen it is difficult to make out what is damaging you. Not only do you have your own bullets flying around the screen, (often flying in multiple directions at once), you can also have multiple pets that follow you around attacking enemies and firing their own projectiles. (I’m not sure how many pets you can get, but I have had several runs where I have had 20 or more.) At the same time you have multiple enemies and their projectiles, not to mention the background which often has flashing elements. In between you, your pets, the enemies, all of the projectiles and flashing background elements, it can become very difficult to see what the hell is damaging you. The overall game feels like they made the game and weren’t really sure what direction to take it, so they just started to add stuff to it. They even have an in-game joke about this.There are other frustrating elements to this game which I won’t go into. But I will say that most of this game's faults become very apparent around the 10-15 hour mark. I think that most of the positive reviews that have less than 15 hours playtime should reevaluate and see if they feel the same way once they hit 15 hours of playtime. Due to the game being repetitive and a grind, among other issues, I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game at all, i don't recommend it but i don't don't recommend it either, the problem is Steam doesn't propose another choice so i put a thumb down because, as a rogue like (and considering the other rogue likes on the market), this one is frustrating.Frustrating because it has a great potential. There's a lot of bosses in the game. They're all pretty neat, nice mechanics, sometimes hard and not very fair but still fun because the core gameplay itself is very nice. Running, jumping, shooting: it all feels great. Grenades are pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up tho, but after some time you'll get it. Visually, well, it's well made but not very diverse. It gets boring after a few runs only. Not a lot of environnements AT ALL but there's a lot of "secret or bonus rooms", and they're very funny sometimes, pretty creatives. Soundtrack is boring, sadly. Not a lot of diversity in terms of ennemies either but i don't know if it's a big problem because it's already hard to understand what's happening in game. Lot of ennemies per rooms, A DAMN LOT OF PROJECTILES so you reeeaaally need to pay attention to everything. It's fun. Not easy, but fun.So yeah. Great gameplay, pretty creative and original game when it comes to all the bonus rooms, secret rooms, bosses...But there a problem. A very big one in my opinion and the reason why i give the game a thumb down instead of a recommendation. Items. They are awfully boring, the very vast majority of them. Sure, there's many different weapons. Most of them plays the same BUT they are kinda still different and some of them are very unique. They can change the gameplay a bit. But the items... IMO, items in a rogue-like like this are very important. In this game, they almost NEVER change the gameplay. What's fun about Binding of Isaac for exemple, is that there's always this excitation when you're about to get a new items. What is it gonna be ? How is it gonna affect my gameplay ?Sure, in Enter the Gungeon for exemple, only the weapons are really gonna be big changes but all of them are incredibly unique so they don't need to spice it up with gamechanging items. Weapons aren't like this in Neon Abyss, so you need items to make everything more diverse. But they don't. 90% of them are something like "get hit by [insert something] and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]", "kill ennemies and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]", "use [insert drop like bomb or key] and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]". THAT IS SO BORING.Items are either like this or like that -> "get one more heart" or "drop more something". I mean, yeah items like that are also in Isaac but they are not 90% of what you are gonna get, in Neon Abyss it is waaaaaayy too much, way way too much. It's very rare to get something a bit fun like an item that will add a projectile to your weapon or making your projectiles bigger. Very, very, very rare. I mean sure it's fun when it's happens but waow it almost never does.And it makes the game honestly boring, most runs are just the same, the gameplay rarely changes. Except, it's the point of rogue-likes like this. So, thumb down for that because the game has the potential, it's just sad that it fails in the one essential category.Oh, and i forgot about eggs. Yeah but you know what, you'll forget about them too. Eggs sometimes get you familiars, but you will never really see them. I mean, they do stuff, they hit ennemies, they shoot ennemies, but there's already so much happening on screen that you won't pay attention to your little familiars at all.So yeah, the game isn't bad, but, when you can play Gungeon, Isaac and such, i don't see why you would spend time on Neon. So far, it's not competiting. But it might soon, because they make updates, so keep an eye on this one, the potential is there.
