_childDocuments_.review: While I have enjoyed some of this game and would prefer to give it a neutral review, I'm skewed towards the negative.This game is very much like Binding of Isaac, sharing many of the positives and all of the negatives.It also tries to put its own spin on a lot of it, ultimately coming out all the worse for it.Take the 2D perspective for example, while it has been shown to work by plenty of other roguelikes, Neon Abyss' characters limited mobility, bad level design and unfair enemy placement/types make it significantly less fun. It takes many elements of all of these things directly from BoI without really considering how well it works in 2D, resulting in an overall frustrating experience.Run variety, one of the most important factors of a roguelike and something that BoI in particular excels at, is also abysmal in Neon Abyss. The reasons for this are the lack of item variety and Neon Abyss trying to reinvent the wheel with new systems.Guns in particular significantly limit variety, where in BoI you just had basic tear projectiles to start with, you had a wide variety of items that completely transformed how they work and look, in Neon Abyss that is mostly achieved with guns.There are many different guns that all work somewhat differently, however they have very little synergy with items.You can get items that increase damage, projectiles, range, firing speed or add a chance to shoot additional projectiles with different properties, however your gun will still fire the same mechanically.For some this is a positive as you can always just switch your gun out for a different one mid-run, but ultimately this significantly limits item variety as none of them can fundamentally change how you fire each gun.Another thing Neon Abyss takes and ruins from BoI is the familiar system. In Binding of Isaac there was a category of items that granted you a (most of the time) invulnurable familiar that followed you and helped you in various ways, like shooting enemies or dropping items for you.Neon Abyss instead has the egg system, where you can pick up egg pickups that over the course of a couple of cleared rooms have a chance to become a familiar. these familiars work in much the same as BoI aside from one key difference: they can be killed. Whether it be by enemies, projectiles or traps, if your familiar takes enough damage it will die and that's that. This feels like a complete downgrade from the familar system in the most frustrating ways. Eggs more often than not fail to hatch, and even when they do, chances are the familiar you get isn't any good anyways, and even on the off chance that they are, if you aren't particularly careful and having a great run, they'll get killed anyways.Finally a third feature that I feel is a straight up worse version of something in BoI is the faith system.Where in BoI you had Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms, special post-boss rooms that rewarded you for not taking any damage per floor with great items, Neon Abyss exchanges that for a faith system.Now you have to rely on crystal items (chests, doors, etc.) to get the process going, where you activate said item with crystals that you pick up to fill up the "angel" side of the bar, or damage it and let it deal damage to you to fill up the "devil" side of the bar.You can then also fill up said bar by either not taking any damage for each cleared room for the angel side, or taking damage each room for the devil side. This would not be an issue at all save for one important detail, only one side of the bar can exist at a time.As you might strive for angel rooms as those align with not wanting to take damage anyway, you might happen to accidentally damage a crystal item, either by shooting it mid-fight with enemies or having your familiars shoot it with no input from you. This results in your faith bar instead getting changed to the devil side with a lot less of the bar filled up, essentially wasting all your effort and forcing you to either abandon that mechanic until you find another crystal and start over or force yourself to keep taking damage for devil rooms.This is one of the most frustrating aspects of the game.As you keep trying to do no damage runs for extra items, which is already frustrating enough with the level design and enemies in this game, now you also have to contend with crystals being obstacles in every other stage where your already flawed and fragile familiars are now an active threat to your run.This is a major issue in a game like this that heavily relies on items to make it fun and exciting, when the vast majority of the ones you get being nearly useless or incredibly situational, every chance at an additional item is crucial for having a good time and saving a run.This could have very well been a great game but the devs insisted on trying to change mechanics that already worked incredibly well in their main inspiration for significantly worse versions of themselves, making this game a lot more frustrating than it is fun.If you don't mind bashing your head against the wall for that one god run where you destroy everything then this might be for you, otherwise save yourself the trouble and find another roguelike.

The soundtrack are pretty awesome and I like the high randomness of this game (every run through feels special and funny, even if you can only beat the first bosses).The random factor is pretty high because of all the artifacts, weapons and pets you earn during your round. Some of them maybe useless in your run but it feels so nice if you got lucky and can build around those mostly "useless" things and see them become valuable.Also there are alot of easter eggs to most every kind of game/movie/TV-Series, e.g. from several Animes, Marvel universe, and many more.And the developers are very active. I think in the last 4-6 month, they added 3 new bosses. But it's probably recommended to run this game in experimantal mode to get always the newest features. The game is pretty bug free even with all the ♥♥♥♥ that is going on (even in experimental branch) :) So I would really recommend this game, it's very lovely designed and fun to play!

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is overall a really fun new roguelite. It has a really awesome visual style and really awesome music and the gameplay is a mix between Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon.You can find different weapons and passive items that make you even stronger and the items synergize together really well. You can make some crazy gun combinations just like in Binding of Isaac.The movement is a little stiff but I got used to it after awhile.There is a really cool gimmick with finding eggs that hatch into pets, the only problem is that late game they can actually be harmful so it kind of defeats the purpose of them.My biggest complaint with the game is that the progression is obnoxiously grindy. It takes like 5-6 hours of just beating the same bosses over and over and over again to unlock new characters and it makes it feel like you aren't actually making much progress. Also there is day 1 DLC which is super scummy in my opinion.Overall this game is fun if you only expect to have a max of like 25ish hours of playtime. This does not have the replayability of say, Binding Of Isaac that could keep you playing for thousands of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Underneath a bunch of annoyances and the occasional bug is exactly 50% of a really fun game.They made a solid basic combat, but the enemies get tedious by the 5th run. _childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a roguelike shooter that combines a modern cyberpunk aesthetic with an environmental setting inspired by Greek mythology. You start of at the Cerberus bar where you can unlock new gameplay mechanics and characters, browse through your unlocked items and pets, select your character and do some other nifty things (like dancing).Runs are started by jumping down into the abyss, where you will face randomized rooms filled with various enemies, treasures, shops and puzzles throughout multiple levels in a classic rougelike manner. Every level also features a boss fight, which needs to be defeated to access the next level. As you continue playing you unlock new levels and bosses, as well as cursed forms of previous bosses that require following certain paths to be accessed. When it comes to gameplay mechanics, Neon Abyss doesn't reinvent the wheel, but that isn't a requirement for an enjoyable roguelike in my opinion. You collect keys which are used to open locks and bombs which are used to blow stuff up.Health comes in the forms of heart containers as well as shields, with shields being used up first. An interesting mechanic are pets, which players can hatch from eggs found across the levels. These eggs hatch after clearing a few rooms but might fail to hatch as well. Pets come in various forms, from protective pets to offensive pets and also in the form of pets that collect certain pickups and drop other stuff in exchange. These pets can also level up and become stronger throughout the run, however they also come with their own health and therefore can die.Killing bosses drops a badge that cycles through various upgrades and boosts your stats in certain ways depending on the badge you end up grabbing.There are hundreds of different items to be founds and a fair amount of guns as well, however many of the guns exist in multiple forms which end up being the exact same gun but with different active effects. I found quite a few of the guns to be very annoying to use because of strange bullets patterns and because every gun exists in multiple forms you ultimately end up with not thaaat many different guns for a shooter roguelike. When killing bosses you unlock faith gems which are used to unlock new gameplay mechanics, rooms, secrets and characters in the aforementioned bar. Each character comes with 2 different "costumes" (if you own the respective DLC) that also grant them different abilities and i found the character variety to be pretty neat, some of them come with very unique playstyles.However, the part where Neon Abyss falls pretty short is the end game in my opinion. Some of the late game content seems a little rushed and most of the cursed bosses are just different forms of former bosses that feel like bullet sponges in most runs. To get to these cursed bosses you also need to rely on RNG to some degree since you need to follow specific requirements in every run that can easily be messed up. There also are no achievements for killing any of the end game bosses which once again reinforces the feeling of rushed end game content. Also, the screen tends to become very cluttered towards the end of runs as you find many items and pets which can make dodging very hard since you need to stop shooting to even see whats going on.Neon Abyss also has its fair share of clunky mechanics and bugs (you can't rebind all keys, weapon upgrades cycle in an annoying and unpredictable pattern, elemental effects overwrite each other, the minimap doesn't show all objects, occasional crashes when entering a new level, errors in the English translations and so on). From what I can tell the game is no longer developed and while I wouldn't call it "abandoned" it still could use quite a bit of polishing in its current state.At the end of the day this is one of those games that make me wish steam had a "mixed feelings" option besides recommending or not recommending a game. Overall I still enjoyed most of my time in the abyss and if you are a roguelike fan then you will probably find some joy in it as well. I would definitely recommend playing all the other top tier roguelikes first (such as Isaac, Spelunky & Gungeon) and if your rougelike itch still isn't satisfied then you can't go wrong with picking up Neon Abyss, although I would recommend doing so during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this for long, so these are my absolute first thoughts.I usually don't play these kind of games, got it in a bundle, was bored, and figured.. why not try it out.And I am so glad I did, it is a fun game with a ton of different weapons, gadgets, companions that help you, and so on.I am gonna be honest, had close to no idea what was going on, just that I was shooting stuff and avoiding stuff, and it was a mess and it was fun.I feel that it is a game that you can easily play more than one playthrough, if not for just like fun and try different playstyles or a different difficulty, there's always the achievements for the people that like to 100%.I would say that this game is definitely worth it, even at full price (though it is steam so there are sales all the time, or check something like GG.Deals for the cheapest place atm for a key or something.)Loads of weapons and upgrades that keep the game interesting and make you try new playstyles.But to all good things there are some negatives.There are some trophy rooms in the game and some shops for each map, where you can in the trophy room, choose between 2 items. And the store is.. well.. a store.. buy stuff with coins you collected by killing mobs. The only downside that I found was that unless you have played before and memorized what that item or weapon does.. It doesn't say at all untill you have picked it up, which in the trophy room where you can only choose 1, is more like.. well.. This looks cool, meanwhile the other item could have been better, but you will never know untill next time.I am currently enjoying my time in this game and would recommend it to almost everyone, if you can find it anywhere cheap, pick it up, like I said, this is usually not what I play but it surprised me.There is some nice music, cool weapons, and actually nice graphics even though it is pixelated.10/10 - With the experience I have now from it, would even buy it had I not got it in the bundle, thanks Humble Choice for being so diverse with games.

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, let's review this one...So, this is a roguelite that aims to step up to Isaac, Gungeon and similar gems.Is it fun to play? Well, kind of, but it has some flaws.TL;DR: 2D shooting Roguelite with unlocks & some questionable mechanics.Good stuff:1. A lot of guns and items to alter your run. Some items really change the playstyle, some - just don't.2. Controls are pretty good and you sorta feel every press of your buttons, which is nice.3. Unlocks. The more you play (& defeat bosses) - the more you are able to unlock. Which is ok just in scope of this game.4. Wisdom (?)/Rage(?) - mechanics. There are some elements, that let you get extra bonus if you a) don't get damage b) get damage. And by bonus I mean extra items. That's quite interesting, though I have some questions. And I guess that's pretty much it. Questionable stuff:1. When and how you obtain the items? Comparing to Isaac, where every item has it's own logic to obtain - here you embrace chaos. You can get item by defeating a random enemy or breaking a random crate. Or you can NOT get an item after a boss fight. It's completely random. I can't say it's bad, though it's confusing at times.2. Eggs. You will obtain eggs. After couple of rooms they will hatch (or not) into little friends to help you out. And they can evolve to more powerful versions! Cool, huh? But wait, they can die. How? No idea? By being hit by enemy bullets? Maybe. There are some sidekicks that suppose to block bullets while orbiting around you. Do they act like temporal shields? I don't know and after 30+ runs, I can't say for sure.3. Randomness in general. In Gungeon/Isaac/etc your strategy was based on understanding of WHAT you could achieve during your run (you are sure that you can get this here and that there, if you have a key). In Neon Abyss - this logic won't work. You may or may not gain a gun in a level. You may or may not get an extra item, Again - not a flaw, but rather some confusing stuff.And here come the breaking points1. The combat (even with good controls) feels bland and non-satisfying. You don't understand how much damage you do to enemies. Enemies are trying really hard to be diverse, but in the end - from level 1 to 7 you're fighting same creeps all over again.2. Some guns should never exist. They are obviously fillers that don't bring anything fun, but are there to promote the "We have a 2000+ guns" line in commercials.3. So are the items. Yes, there are synergies, but some items are clearly created from the "top of my dome" just to fill in the list.4. Grenade tossing and accuracy... Oh God... No comment.5. Bosses and "bullet hell". It's a joke. Seriously. Bosses are cardboard dummies. You will easily overcome any boss up to Argus with a base gun and no powerups. 6. Grenade tossing. YES! Again. This is THAT bad.There's probably some more stuff, I'm missing to state, but hey - New Year is over the corner! (So, Happy New 2021 everyone).Anyways, I can't say this game is bad or that I wouldn't recommend it. It's fair in it's own rules, though those rules are pretty unclear and no one bothers to explain them, You should definitely give it a try when the game is on -50% discount, as I won't grant you'll get satisfied at any higher price. I'm having my part of fun here, but I can't say it's the game you must play. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, obviously if you are interested in this kind of game then certainly play Binding of Isaac before this, but if you're tired of Isaac then this is a good alternative to scratch that itch.A glaring issue is the use button is also a melee attack. Alone that's not a big deal but in this game they have a mechanic where you can either use or attack a crystal to increase a paragon or sin bar, unlocking powerful items in a run. _childDocuments_.review: I have a number of issues with this game, but I will start with the pros to maintain good faith. The TL;DR, however, is that I wouldn't buy this for any more than 10 dollars, because the controls feel off and the chests that require explosions to open are more challenging than most enemies.Pros:+Good initial concept, the idea of cyberpunk'd Greek gods was what got me to buy the game in the first place+At the beginning of every run, you are able to fully customize difficulty, RNG seed, what items are banned from spawning, and even which enemies are able to spawn, though setting a seed manually or making too many changes to item/enemy spawning will disable achievements+The rocket launcher (or at least the only one I found in my playtime) doesn't explode when it hits walls, only enemies, which is a nice QOL thing.Cons:-I honestly did not have fun playing. I am a fan of rougelikes and roguelites in general, but the movement and gunplay in this one felt wrong. You have to pay 10 of the "floor bosses drop 2 each" currency that many of these games have to unlock the only character with a dodge ability.-The game is very easy on the Normal difficulty. The primary challenges I ran into were trying to open awkwardly placed stone chests without getting hit by my own grenades, finding out my bullets now explode and dying in the next room due to every bullet I shoot damaging me, and the occasional "You wanted to open this chest with crystals? Too bad, it's spiky now!"-The ratio of eggs that hatch to eggs that don't is very low, and when you actually manage to get a pet from the eggs, it dies in 3 or 4 hits (whether it's bullets that hit me, or bullets that hit my pet, I can't tell). Even if they were beefier, there's no way to have cute floating pets killable that doesn't feel crummy.-The final straw was when I ran into a third floor boss that was a recoloration of a first floor boss. A slightly more difficult bullet pattern, but aside from that he was just a sunburnt version of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is great, i love the aesthetic and is pretty fun, plus also some humor and references on the side is a nice touch. I only have 2 criticism for the game:1.- On the later half of any given run the chaos on the screen becomes.. too much and is hard to distinguish enemy projectiles and it becomes a bit overbearing to dodge everything, deal damage and distinguish my bullets from the enemy's, which is only made worst when you have the occasional enemy that can shot through walls so yeah.. Ideally i would like to see a better contrast from the background and the color of the enemy bullets so its easier to read the screen and react in time.2.- At the time of the review i just finished a run killing Athena (dont know if this is related) and one stage before getting to the final stage, a mistery stage appeared, so alright pretty cool, like surprises. However this was something called "chaos room" or the like, in which basically is.. f0ck any of your decisions you made through your run, you are stripped of all your power ups (except health, shields and pets) and now you have to fight any the first bosses 4 times every 3 rooms, each room you will get a random upgrade, make it through you get to a room which maybe you expect based on the sign at the start you get all your items back plus get to keep all the new ones.. no... you get a bundle of upgrades and thats it, so you have to pray the final build (which is COMPLETELY RANDOM) is equal or better in power than whatever you been building so far. WHY? WHY!? i had a disgusting awesome build, my weapon was basically a minigun of death that i tried my best to build up to the few times i got choices and then out of nowhere the little agency i could have is stripped away from me and forced to comform to whatever random roll of the dice coocked for me??WTF.. if i made it so far as to the final stage chances are im pretty happý with my build or proficent enough to have a chance at winning my run, whats this senseless idea of throwing everything out the window and force me to use whatever when i might have adopted a particular strategy early on to sustain my build up to that point and had to do sacrifices in the middle? Dont get me wrong im not salty because i lost, actually i won my run (tho it was a bit on the edge) but the sheer feeling of betrayal and sourness in my mouth completely killed off the run for me. So now i have to go into every game hoping either A) if this happens again i get a better build or B) this doesnt happen at all. So great, getting a 50% chance (allegedly) of not knowing if my knowledge of the game becomes useless around the end or god forbid, i somehow craft something weird but fun and want to try its viability towards the end game and the suddenly be like: "hahahahahaha NO"..I do recommend the game, but i honestly wish they changed this 2 main grips i have with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Every feels copy and pasted. Same enemy design with slight variations. Same level design with slight variations. Some variation with the guns but most of them are stinkers and some are down right terrible. Half the upgrades are functional useless. You also have no idea what an item does unless you have item that tells you what other items do, A character who does the same or a really good memory. Unless you happen to find a gun that does melee damage, then you are still SOL because that next upgrade you picked up wreck the idea of a "build" you were going for. You also collect 2 resources. Keys which are used to open doors and treasures chest and bombs that are used to open doors and treasure chests and. Sure you can toss those bombs at enemies, but that's just a waste of resources. And to be fair opening up a treasure chest that requires a key or a bomb feels worthless about 50% of the time. I've gotten better stuff from blowing up destructables in the environment. _childDocuments_.review: Game seems fun at first, but once you're over the honeymoon phase, you're hit with the realization that the game was barely QA'd. The things that are meant to appeal to you end up working against you and 80% of the time, you're being punished for things outside your control. The other 10% is your skill and the final 10% is the game being nice to you. Reading the top negative reviews will give you a detailed insight of why this game works against you as a roguelite. Not worth full price and potentially never until they change certain game mechanics (probably won't happen).Edit: It's been nearly 2 months since I left this review. Not much has been done on making the game more fun. The update seems to mainly focus on fine tuning the RNG elements of the game to just be right on the middle of being tolerant, or not fun. That's it. I don't like to throw accusations around but the devs seems to be so heavily invested in keeping their RNG mechanics over making the game have any semblance of enjoyable replayability. Whenever I try to pick this game back up and try to enjoy it, I'm frustrated right on the first level, and it doesn't get better. Killing bosses, beating runs, have barely any satisfaction in them. Only a masochist will play this game. If you like playing roguelites where you absolutely have no control over your run, go for it. What I wouldn't give to purge this game from my game list.

_childDocuments_.review: The fortunate upshot of systematically going through the exhaustive list of titles that I have on Steam and reviewing them is that I keep coming across questionable titles from unknown sources that either amaze me in their design or profoundly irritate me to no end.  does neither, really. I'm not even sure I'm going to remember this title outside of reflecting over my reviews and wondering if I did enough justice in conveying my opinion of it. is by no means a terrible title so much as it's... well, it's there. It has the unfortunate position of being played after I completed , which is infinitely a better title. Which reminds me, this title actively compares itself to  as a sort of meta-commentary within the actual game, and that in an of itself makes me want to cast aggressive criticism toward it. But I'm getting ahead of myself here.To keep it relatively brief,  is a roguelike platformer bullet-hell mash-up where you, the player, continuously progress further into the depths of some sort of dungeon to defeat the "New Gods", which are a cyber-punk mess of pun concepts realized in pixel graphics. From the outside, this concept works effectively enough, to a fault. I want to say this title feels a bit half-baked, like the developers just through things at a wall and worked with whatever stuck. The controls aren't exactly functional, and some of the menus don't react properly to pressing down without pressing up first, which seems like something that should have been fixed early on. The artistic choice works to a point, but it also becomes incredibly difficult to discern what's going on when you're trying to dodge a hail of projectiles while there's a stream of eggs following you around like the end of Snake.That is by no means the only fault that this title suffers from. The RNG that the title employs is a bit broken. You can have a dozen attempts through the dungeon where every buff is completely useless before you get a single run where you're practically set up to be completely indestructible before you complete the second floor. For instance, I had a run where the shop continuously reset, taking damage dropped money, killing things dropped more money, and explosions made money. By the end of that run, I looked like Liberace fell into a vat of technicolor acid, became supersized and ate steroids for breakfast while rainbows literally spewed out of my anus. I won't apologize for the bizarre image that might plague you from that description.With all that being said, I didn't hate the experience. I'd call it bland before I would claim that I enjoyed myself, but there were some positive aspects to the title. The music, for example, is quite well orchestrated. The weird minigames in the form of secret rooms were a pleasant change of pace from "bounce and shoot". Even with the scenery becoming an indiscernible blob of bright flashy colors and literal Easter eggs, the bosses aren't so difficult as to detract from the experience. Mind you, getting beyond the first eight bosses or so is more grind than its worth, but still.I don't really know where to put this title. I didn't hate it, but I didn't enjoy it enough to warrant a recommendation on my part. As a sale purchase it would seem fine, I suppose, but it doesn't really deserve much in terms of commendation at all when there are other titles out there that do the exact same thing but slightly better. Perhaps this title would have done better with more development time or a bit less whimsy on the developer's part.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to rate this negatively, because it has so much potential and I did enjoy it, but this game feels very incomplete. It should have released in early access, perhaps. There's been major balance issues, a lot of frustrating design decisions around negative pets and items, extremely grindy skill tree which includes unlocking other characters and not just abilities, and including temporary buffs/items in the skill tree? That feels like a major waste of an already scarce reward.But then I reached the end of the game, defeated the boss......... and there's nothing. This game has no real ending, nothing rewarding or providing a feeling of completeness once you've 'won'. All that's left is grinding to unlock other characters and rooms, and I'm not interested.Why does the Office exist above the bar? I had assumed all along that would be part of the ending or post-completion reward, but it does nothing?It just feels incomplete.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Rogue-lite with an Cyberpunkish graphics, tons of unlocks, weapons and passives, it gets better as you go on.It gives you this adrenaline rush when you're trying not to die dodging bullets and avoiding traps, there's few difficulty levels which you can change whenever. Replayability is amazingEvery fan of rogue-lites should give it a try, especially when they're bored of fantasy settingThere's tons of upgrades that you can buy with currency that drops from bossesAlso there's a lot of easter eggs, even in the item descriptions! Apart from that there's great egg hatching system which is fun and random, every time you get an egg you have a chance to hatch it by completing the enemies rooms and the sprites that hatches from them give you bonuses. Game is a blast, it was in bundles before, get it and you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: How can't I recommend this game? Awesome soundtracks, really nice platform gameplay, not too punishing(look for punishment? See Enter The Gungeon and break some peripherals :)), lots of items, guns, possibilities, art is fantastic, Saya is amazing(I really like her), bosses' designs are nice. Nearly everything about this game is good and better than expected. Some bugs and glitches are present but, bugs are a part of developing and you cannot expect a product without any bug at all. I really recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I have to give this one a negative review, because the game just feels like it doesn't like the player at a few too many corners. Don't get me wrong, the overall gameplay could be a lot of fun, and maybe it will be in the future, but compared to some others in the genre this one just makes me feel like it actively wants me to not be happy. This ranges from room with 5 enemies immediately rushing you without space to dogdge and important systems like grenades, egg familiars and the violence/wisdom thing being infuriatingly designed, to actual situations where a boss seems to take no damage at all, for no apparent reason whatsoever.As it is, for this game, I just don't ever get the 'just one more run' feeling, instead I'm kinda just thinking 'I'm good for now...', and that's really strange for a roguelite.However as a positive note, the devs have started experimenting with changes in the right direction already, so I'm hopeful for the future and will change my review if the game manages to win me over again. Sadly, that day seems to be well in the future at best...
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a 10/10 rogue-alike, neon-colored, side-scrolling platformer version of Binding of Isaac.All of BoI's mechanics & features are translated directly to the side-scrolling platformer genre and in a good way:From a locked golden door with a free item on every level to hidden rooms that need to be bombed, keys & grenades, being locked in a room until you kill all the baddies, many pick-ups & mods for your weapons that change you visually & the effects of your weapons, pre-fab rooms with proc-gen placement in the map & proc-gen filled with baddies, each level ending in a boss room, bosses aren't bullet-hell-frustrating (*ahem* Enter the Gungeon, ugh), several unlockable characters, optional use of seeds, and...The most important feeling for a rougealike to generate: that  instead of anguish when you die.Neon Abyss also goes farther than BoI and adds good features such as difficulty settings, some rooms having a minor puzzle in how you move & blow up barrels to get to extra treasure, the ability to ban items or monster types for runs, an upgrade/"skill" path to unlock features with tokens you get from boss kills all to suit your gameplay preferences.(These bits remind me of the customizations that Streets of Rogue allow, which I love.)The other important thing to mention is that movement, platforming, jumping, and aiming with the mouse all feel good. You're not too slow, you're not sluggish, the speed of everything you do/control is appropriate.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: A fun roguelite at first, but the gameplay loop quickly becomes repetitive and boring.The game also suffers from gated progression, bad RNG mechanics, and questionable design choices.I'd recommend Binding of Isaac, Risk of Rain, Enter the Gungeon, Dead Cells, or Gunfire Reborn to name a few alternatives.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Great rogue shooter. Plenty of weapons and pets to collect, mini games are great too. The game can get a bit repetitive at times as you'll notice the same room layouts and enemies. It can be hard in the early stages to manage the resources as you can spend valuable coins on a weapon that is terrible as there's no indication of what it does beforehand. The RNG can be brutal too with low key/nade runs, this results in a lot of running back and fourth trying to find the best way to use the utility which makes an already bad run drag on too long. Overall worth a go if you like rogue style games and can pick it up in the humble bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a side-scrolling rogue-like platformer that shamelessly rips off The Binding of Isaac. And that's exactly what makes it worth playing. It has similar itemization, similar room types, floor layouts, health system, followers, pickups, and characters. Unfortunately, it's not executed as well as Isaac. It does a poor job at rewarding the player's game knowledge, some questionably useful items, poor transformations, and less variety in room layouts, floor types, enemies, bosses, and characters. All that said, I still recommend this to fans of rogue-likes. Don't expect anything ground breaking and enjoy the cyberpunk atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty addicting 2D roguelike shooter. I managed to beat most of the regular bosses after a few tries and experimenting with weapon + item setups. I found Ares difficult to defeat at first because of his shield and the fact that you had to sacrifice hearts in the first place to reach him. But, with all the weapons, items, sprites, and ways you can spend your tokens to randomize and customize each dungeon run, this isn't the kind of game that gets tiring after a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me start by saying I love this game so far. It has a great aesthetic and manages to capture that feeling that made Binding of Isaac such a great game. That said, It has one glaring bug that makes it all but unplayable for anyone playing with a mouse on a duel screen PC. If you're frantically clicking away shooting at enemies and you click off your screen the whole game minimizes. There's no option for non-windowed full screen, either. So you can't bind your mouse to stay just in the game window. Fighting bosses was incredibly frustrating as in the panic and excitement your screen would just seemingly minimize out of nowhere, completely ruining the experience. If they get this glaring UI oversight fixed I'll happily change my review to recommend this game.** Update ** Despite this having been reported by many people and the assurances of the devs (such as the one on my review here) a week has gone by and there's still no patch.This should have been something that was hot-patched a day or two after launch. Since the game is unplayable in its current state I am requesting a refund and will never know if they ever actually fix this issue so the review stays.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a fantastic rogue-like, bullet-hell metroidvania.While you may occasionally run into a bug or two, and there is a *lot* of RNG involved in how successful you are in finding good loot for completing a run, the fun far outweighs the small annoyances.The memes and jokes are fresh and relevant. It's even making fun of games in development while this game was in development. The artwork is slick and well suited to the atmosphere. The music is poppin.But the thing that really sells this game is the  available. I've pumped nearly 50 hours into the game as of this review, and I've still only found about 2/3 of all the available weapons and items. The potential for varied gameplay and experimentation is nearly unparalleled. While it's easy to draw comparisons to Hades (even the game itself makes some tongue-in-cheek meta commentary on its similarities), Neon Abyss more than stands on its own legs as rogue-like with a ton of replay value and between-run progress.If you're looking for a fast-paced rogue-like you can really sink your teeth into, don't sleep on Neon Abyss!

_childDocuments_.review: This is less a review and more of a disclaimer. This game is NOT 2d Enter the Gungeon. I thought that was what this game was and was disappointed at first, until I realized that this game is actually 2d Binding of Isaac. Gungeon is all about amassing a giant stockpile of weapons and destroying everything in your path. Isaac is all about making yourself into a being of absolute hyperdeath. This game is much more like Isaac in the sense that you get tons of upgrades that make you insanely op. It just seems to be trying to pass itself off as Gungeon. If you're looking for more Gungeon, look somewhere else, but if you want some Isaac insanity, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike ‎Neon Abyss from Veewo Games is an innovative roguelike that combines elements from traditional dungeon crawlers with modern aesthetics. Unlike other roguelikes, Neon Abyss offers a colorful pixel art design and a stunning soundtrack crafted by 2-time BAFTA Award winner Danny Baranowsky and an impressive selection of special abilities, weapons, and items that offer an extra layer of depth to the action. Players can explore dungeons filled with enemies, bosses, and loot while ascending each level with progressively more powerful gear and abilities. Fans of the genre will be delighted to find that Neon Abyss also employs challenging roguelike elements such as permadeath and randomly generated levels.Neon Abyss is an excellent example of a God-tier roguelike. The colorful art style and original soundtrack combine to create an exciting atmosphere that immerses players in the game’s procedurally generated world. With plenty of secrets and new content to discover, it’s a great game for fans of the genre. The roguelike elements work harmoniously together, rewarding skilled players for their strategies and providing an engaging experience for newcomers and veterans alike. Neon Abyss is an excellent roguelike experience that is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Art direction, having a ridiculous build is fun and almost guaranteed, reasonable amount of content.Cons:One of the easier roguelikes out there, if you're new to the genre/bullethell in general I might recommend it. The main problem is the difficulty fails to pace with the content, you have to use currency from runs to purchase the ability for certain rooms to appear, and I managed to reach the credits without having unlocked many types of rooms, and those that I did unlock often proved inferior to the rooms I already had, and left me wishing I just hadn't bought them. The main way you'll die in this game is getting a gun/build so ridiculous that its shots fill your screen and you have trouble dodging enemy bullets, which IS fun, but the issue is that the variety of items is such that almost every one is just flat increase to stat(s), goofy or double edged sword items are few and far between.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play many games like this, and I'm not one to put in 900 hours into a game, but I played this game every day before work and rather enjoyed it. Loved the randomness of the builds, tho some items feel more like trolls. Don't think I could beat this game on hard tho lol. There are multiple characters but IMO the only one that actually has a bonus is the guy that can dodge roll. HUGE advantage besides the android.Runs great, lots of diversity in playthroughs, lots to unlock. Nice colors and music (would have liked more variety in music). Not enough level variety, dislike that they take flight from you for certain bosses. Final boss is tedious. Def recommend at its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen such utter lack of originality in an otherwise pretty well-made game. Yeah, I've played Binding of Isaac too, dear Veewo Games, you could be more subtle about lifting almost EVERYTHING from it. Hearts, keys, bombs, similar enemies, crates, casino machines, rooms that you can only enter by taking damage, secret rooms you need to blow up walls to see, the whole map, the power-ups system — all that is straight up stolen from Isaac. And developers haven't added anything from themselves, no new ideas, no new style, nothing. Story is laughably basic and boring, graphics are generic pixelart with a few good backgrounds, artstyle is a mess — game want to be cyberpunk-ish, but forgets about it 5 minutes into first level.Other than that, the game works perfectly fine, it is moderately fun, gameplay loop is nice. Upgrades are random, wacky and interesting. Guns all feel unique, but not all feel usable. On the later stages the screen becomes really cluttered with all the effects, projectiles and enemies. Bosses are too easy (played on Normal). Default control scheme is bizarre (left trigger to jump - really?).Overall — there is nothing really wrong with Neon Abyss, it is just so painfully average and generic. I see no real reason to play it over dozens of other amazing roguelikes out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend you get it on a sale if you're just dying for a roguelite. You can definitely have overpowered runs, but instead of wacky unique item combinations it basically comes down to "did I get a lot of +weapon upgrade pickups?". Runs felt like they dragged on whether you're overpowered or barely making it through because of how "samey" everything is. Could use some biome diversity and maybe more varied music.It's a fine enough game, but with how many great roguelites there are out there, you have better options.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: it's unnecessarily grindy and not that fun.  You have a bunch of characters, and *each* of them are supposed to kill all bosses, which is like 70+ runs. That's fine if the game is good, but it's strangely not. The characters's classes feels more annoying than useful, like one character can lift things... what can you lift and why you lift them? Can't tell. Another character can revive pets by hurting yourself... except they died very easily and the game itself rewards you for NOT TAKING DMG. Which means that character is useless for a no dmg run by default.  And then there the upgrades... some of them are good, others are very situational and some downright breaks your build. Also I feel that either you are dominating or you feel weak, not much in between. Also mobility is king but it's rare to get those items.  The enemy rngs can also get bad, like enemies that explore on death and you are in a small room fun of them... And the environment traps are more pointless than challenging, especially your pets can died to trap dmg as you try not to take dmg.The entire game is full of these weird design choices, it's almost like the devs don't want you to have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all : No Dodge roll. I don't understand this game. If the game didn't stop your run, i think than you could finish it in one run. When you are lucky in drop, you just roll over every boss easily. When you are unlucky, you just die trying. The unlock tree is just there to force you to play again. All the run are mostly the same, only the mobs are changing sometimes. If you stack a lot of items, your are mostly invincible quickly. There is no really skills needed to play, just to have luck.I do not recommand it. Another game who hide you his lack of content by stopping you playing arbitrary (just because you have reach the boss to kill, but, surprise ! for the next target, it's just the same path of boss with one boss more ! On the same RNG map, mostly similar to what you played). This is really disappointing.Most of the weapons are similar, some are just more crap than other, only the effect of shooting is changing. There is ton of items, but they have mostly the same effect, so what's the point ?! The treasure rewarding is really bad. _childDocuments_.review: It's fine. Main reason I stopped playing was more because the music was getting annoying than anything else. There's a solid roguelite here with all the usual features and plenty of weapons and items to discover over the course of countless playthroughs. The feel of the game is a bit off though. It's weird to have 360° aim on one stick and 8-way movement on the other with no analogue sensitivity for movement speed. Jumping with the left trigger always feels weird too (though admittedly I'm not sure what to map it to considering your right thumb should be on the right stick almost constantly). All and all it's still a fun game, so I recommend it if you're bored of your other roguelites. But if you haven't played Hades, Dead Cells, or The Binding of Isaac yet, definitely get to all of those first.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to others who like roguelike 2d shooters, however this game has some obvious flaws as well. The most glaring flaw is that the screen can become very messy as your character spams a bunch of projectiles and bosses/enemy projectiles aren't always distinct enough to make them clear in all the mess. They should really have a brighter red outline like gungeon on most enemy attacks to make it clear what is going on, for instance the second end boss has some attack that drop stars or something that is almost impossible to see through all the clutter. It doesn't help that you can have an army of pets adding to the clutter.Also not having the ability to dismiss pets, at least not as I have found, is rather annoying and can lead to very cheap deaths. I was low on hearts, entered a room with hearths but I had to clear an obstacle to get to them. One of my pets just rushed over and ate the hearts turning multiple hearts into half a shield. This happened multiple times.I also ended up having pets that spammed bombs that kept getting me hurt because they knocked me around, I ended up having to spend as much time dodging my own pet's bombs as enemy projectiles.Overall good game but could benefit from some improvements, in particular more clarity on what projectiles will damage you and what won't

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is  a fun little rogue-lite romp through a handful of copy-paste-randomized levels. The difficulty is very low on Easy and Normal so this may be a good game to hop into if you're new to the genre, or even to side scrolling shooters on PC. The item pool only has a handful of what I would consider "never use" items, and most of the time I find myself feeling very powerful, which is nice. The progression of bosses feels a bit out of order, with it being much easier to reach the "final" boss than it is to reach the boss just before it, but that's a non-issue after it's been done one time. I would recommend this game to anyone  who is a fan of games like Bleed, Binding of Isaac, or Enter the Gungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun games with tons of weapons, characters, items, enemies and more.Honestly this game is fun to play and replay lots of times, there are lots of things to unlock and lots of different characters, most with their own unique playstyle (and another variant which alters their playstyle if you have the Alter Ego dlc).This game sadly does become quite repetitive if you play it too much. There are too many gun/health upgrades instead of new items that alter gameplay, there are lots of items that are literally useless on their own because they change the way eggs or sprites (little fire attack things) or other stuff like that works and the backgrounds, while they look great, can get very repetitive.I still think this game is worth getting, preferably on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I will divide this review in the following categories :- Game atmosphere- Actual Gameplay- What I believe that should be prioritized in the upcoming updates- My personal suggestions to the devs- Final ReviewGAME ATMOSPHERE   When you begin the game, you're sitting besides what seems to be a pixel Keanu Reeves, who will introduce himself as Hades and tell you that a bunch of guys killed your family before offering you a drink. Next moment, you're in a strange bar ready to jump into the Abyss to kill a god...Or perphaps just to take a pause and enjoy the music of a rave as your character rocks the dancefloor.    And that's pretty much Neon Abyss, as you explore the dungeon, you won't be able to forget that rave feeling as your weapons turn into a light show the more you pump it up and you might have a taste of American Gods as you defeat the final bosses, while the ones that come before them are funny sketches of consumism and critics to modernity (ex. god of pills, god of mobile videos...).ACTUAL GAMEPLAY   I believe anyone that had a past experience with roguelike games will be familiar with most aspects of Neon Abyss and might find it pretty casual. It consists of getting through many rooms, collecting coins, bombs, and keys to open special rooms and chests ( sounds familiar? ) in order to get items and weapons that will make your character stronger.   So, what makes this game different? It has has two unique systems that you'll be able to encounter early in game : collectable pets which can fight on your side and a " faith " system which allows you to get more items by being damaged or killing enemies while avoiding damage ( I know it sounds confusing when put like this, but just take my word for now that it's pretty cool and experiment by yourself )   Aside from that, you'll find a tech tree in the game which allows you to unlock special rooms such as mini-games or more ways to spend your in-game resources, characters and items. Which means that there is always a reason to do "just one more run",UPCOMING UPDATES PRIORITIES   I think that the features and changes that were shown to be tested in the experimental branch fill pretty much any gameplay demand I could have with my experience so far. Good work devs!PERSONAL SUGGESTIONS   These are mostly about character customization : the game has awesome looking items, and I wish there was a way we could control which items are actually being displayed over our characters or not, since we can collect so many of them. So maybe displayed items could have special frames in our inventory and we could scroll through them in order to select and unselect what masks, hats and weapon mods we have currently on.   The second suggestion would be adding some kind of wardrobe in the bar where we could change special skins collected by defeating the game bosses. We would be able to firstly unlock skins of the used character and, if we had all of his unlockables skins so far, we would start getting skins for other characters.FINAL REVIEW   This game has been released 6 days ago at the time of this review. It has bugs, it could use some changes - and the developers are already showing that they will work for these changes. The game has a refreshing amount of items and weapons, 10 characters, and all the unlockables and side-content keep making each run a new surprise everytime you play. I definitely reccomend and believe that this game could be a great introduction to anyone who is curious or want to get into the roguelike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo, i never wrote any reviews, but after playing this game i felt strong need to do it.This review  is specificly l for roguelike fans like me.So first - game is great. It has awesome style, tons of items, interactions, overall i like it and enjoy playing, but there's not a few, but quite a lot of but's. So i played pretty much every decent roguelike out there, and after this experience i feel that this game is have a LOT of very frustrating things in its core mechanics, movement and some interactions.1) - your character does not follow your crosshair with gun - and this feels very off, especially because when you fire - your gun points in the direction of fire. this is confusing sometimes2) this game is not easy and it doesn't offer you a lot of mechanics to dodge- you can dodge only by your movement and jumps. This is not so bad, but it's bad very often, because of few next things. For example, in bullet hell like enter the gungeon, you always have your i-frames during rolls3) characters throw grenades only in the direction they facing, which creates a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up moments - this is super confusing, because your character doesn't face the direction of your crosshair. I played 4 hours in the time of writing, and i missed 90% of my grenade throws because of this very unnatural and inconvinient mechanic. Maked grenades almost useless in battle, and hard to use for other things.4)Because game can be messy in the matters of blood, explosions, other particles - the fact that you don't have any tool (besides one character or special items) to dodge in the core mechanics - it can be very frustrating. Just doesn't feel right.And that's just 4 things i encounter in every run, without spoiling some things i can't tell you more, but i counted 11 things overall which are quite irritating or straight up bad in this game.Honestly, if this game was in early acces (and it feels like early access :c ) - i would not complain a thing, i would just write bug reports and feedback to the developers, but the fact that it released with such unpolished gameplay and core mechanics... Anyways, overall game is fun to play, great roguelike, but o wouldn't put it on one shelf with something like enter the gungeon, or isaac for sure. I really hope developers will eventually polish a lot of things here.Sorry for grammar mistakes, english is not my native language.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well made game with some really annoying design decisions that made it not recommended to any kind of casual player. I wish I could give it a middle thumb. As you can see, the art is great, controls etc are on point. However, there are a plethora of items and they choose not to tell you what they are. So either you can take the time to memorise (or note) what they all do, while taking risks on an item that *only* has a picture and a name, no description. Or you can just play it with the wiki open. All seem suboptimal. Also RNG, there is a lot of RNG, from chests that may or may not open if you put money in, to what items do (because if you haven't memorised it and don't use a wiki, then it's RNG basically. On top of that it is pretty punishing in terms of HP. Sure, that's ok, but if you finally get deep into a run, they suddenly ramp up the damage that *everything* does. Suddenly any source of damage will do twice what it did. Overall this is a great game if you're willing to invest the time to memorise everything and get ultra sharp reflexes. Otherwise it's probably best to just pass and find a more forgiving game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a 2d platformer twinstick-shooter roguelike, it's one of very few that I haven't uninstalled as it feels good to do individual plays through with. However the considerable lack of variability with each run, other than tied to character, certainly hold me back from reviewing this as an absolute must.I've got a lot of close friends that are major rogue-like/lite fans, me personally I've been a fan of only a handful but probably more than the general populous, this doesn't make me a resident pro or anything and I want to make that clear (I'm not paid to play games, I just love gaming as a means of downtime) however for all the pros of this game I feel the random aspect almost wears this game thinner than it should feel. Yes I'm aware of what the genre entails but for all the good aspects this game is weighed down by the negatives of the rogue-lite.Yes come at me if you think Rogue-like and Rogue-lite are appropriately different genre's because to me they are evidently different. Roguelikes should be completable on run one f you're good enough and the RNG is in your favour, rogue-lite's generally favour an approach that it's far less likely to achieve first run through and they provide universal upgrades between runs.Hate me on my views, but please I'd rather a discussion on what the genre differences are.Again simply put, I really do like this game but my positive review comes with a tonne of caveats and the concerns that I don't feel this is as a fun a game as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: What starts off as a fun and engaging roguelike becomes a rather frustrating and dull experience. I wish it were just game play mechanics but the problems just seem to boil down to bugs and lack of attention to detail.The first thing that stood out to me is there is no aim assist for controller, so you spend a great deal of time hunting down enemies which should be easy targets. There is also the matter of hit detection, often times obvious hits just go right through enemies as they play out their animations - not to mention you can't hit enemies as they are spawning in and they have invincibility frames so easy room clears turn into you taking guaranteed damage more often than it should. There are also some unpleasant bugs. Some of the prize rooms are insanely difficult. The crane room will outright break on you and not pick up items at all, the dance room demands impossible reflexes from the player with no rhythm involved. Why design a gimmick like that? I spent 1000 coins in the room only to earn two items. The timing really is that unforgiving. Weapons have a lot of repetitive attributes. There are something like five guns with the same special. None of the gun attributes really feel useful or unique, and I almost never find a reason to switch from starter weapons in the run. There is a sawblade gun that doesn't do enough damage, the projectile disappears when it hits a wall (otherwise it boomerangs back at you) and because of invincibility frames on enemies you can't kill anything close range with it at all. And the list of complaints just goes on. You need a wiki open just to look up the item descriptions as you play. Not to mention the item graphics aren't really descriptive, you mostly just guess what an item does based on its graphics and you are often guessing wrong. The only way to disambiguate items is to use a certain character or pay meta coins for a starting item (when you really are just looking them up on a wiki anyway.) And this game just lacks charm, there is no story, after thirty hours I really have no idea what any of this game is about. It just lacks the character of something like Binding of Isaac.Anyway it not a actually a bad game, it has the potential to be pretty good but as it stands there is just nothing special about it. It will waste your time and you'll have some fun but on the same note you'll forget about it pretty quickly.

I tried the demo they put out a long time ago, liked it a lot, and bought the game fairly quickly when it was finally released on STEAM and I am quite happy with my decision. The devs also give DLC away for free for a week, so that's fairly cool of them if you own it and are paying attention. _childDocuments_.review: Ah, Neon Abyss, or as I call it, "What the Hell Just Hit Me?" Its not that it isnt a fun game, Ive only played like 20 hours, and will probably still play more, but its not really all that satisfying to play. The visual design is great, and I like the style a lot, but the gameplay is meh at the best times. The controls just feel...off somehow. Its responsive enough, but it feels floaty or something, especially when you get a powerup that makes you fly. Controls are always hard to explain when they dont feel right, and I wish I could explain it better. The big issue, like other people have said, is that your bullets take visual priority over the baddies, and that makes it literally, not figuratively, impossible to see where the baddies are shooting. You know how Enter the Gungeon makes it very clear where the bullets are coming from? This a total 180, and its annoying. It doesnt even make much of a difference in how you play because most runs give you boatloads of hearts and shields, so it just turns into tanking every room and boss because youre legit blind the moment you start shooting. None of this is enough to ruin the experience totally, it just makes for an experience thats predominantly annoying when it could be just over the top fun. Buy it if you like the style and those things arent deal breakers, there is some fun to be had, but Im glad I got it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun mechanics and potential to be a great roguelike game, but it's horribly imbalanced. Resources, similar to the Binding of Isaac's bombs and keys, are extremely scarce while the road blocks require a lot of them while often giving little payout. 90% of the weapons seem to be gimmicky or joke weapons, often being useless. I would expect a game that utilizes guns have more straightforward firing mechanics with different rate of fires, damage, etc., but most guns shoot bullets that loop, rubberband back at you after a short distance, or are just dumb in general. Passive items and pets are often detrimental or useless, such as getting a lot of melee related items IN A GAME WHERE GUNS ARE YOUR PRIMARY ATTACK, or pets that literally make it harder for you (pet that blocks bullets, but you picked up an item that randomly shoots missiles which can collide with your orbiting pet and hurt you. Randomly.) There's a lot more issues I won't go in depth with, but as it is, game is unfun. It has potential, but unless the devs swiftly patch the imbalances and frustrating parts of the game, it will soon be forgotten. Games are meant to be enjoyed, not cause frustration with the player. I thought this didn't have to be said, but indie devs seem to have forgotten this key aspect of video games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit torn on this one.  I have 30 hours in the game, so it must be at least somewhat worth it.  But honestly, it's just not that fun for me.I have thousands of hours in various roguelikes.  Isaac, Dead Cells, Undermine, etc.  This seems like it would be right up my alley.  Unlock-a-thon, upgrading to become super OP, etc.  But after the initial honeymoon period of getting to know the game, it rapidly starts to feel like a chore.  Every run feels too samey to me.  Despite the huge number of guns, they almost all fall into a couple of different categories, and they don't feel that different to use.  Most just have some kind of gimmick that turns out to not actually be all that useful.While the game has melee attacks, it can be annoying and unreliable to perform them (on mouse and keyboard) - it really needs a dedicated melee attack button.  While there are items that give you some incentive to kill with melee (extra chance of loot dropping, etc), i still never felt the trade off of being exposed was counter acted.  This is made more annoying by the fact that such a huge number of items are related to melee - it means that many runs are punctuated by a lot of eye rolls when i find the fourth straight melee related item that i didn't want.I also have a variety of little nitpicks - i think the way grenades work is annoying, getting to the late-game bosses feels tedious, and all of the ways the game slows down the action (little slot machines that take coins to open doors or chests, and the mini games sprinkled around each map, for example) just start to wear on you.Overall, it's not  a bad game - graphically pretty, sounds good, controls fine.  But the combat isn't interesting, the unlocks aren't all that rewarding, and the annoyances stack up to make me not have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss has fantastic visuals and responsive controls but fails to remain compelling beyond the first few hours of gameplay. I would not recommend this game unless you can get it for a very steep discount.Overall, the gameplay feels very sluggish and individual runs take a loonnngggg time to complete. The gameplay loop is as follows:1.) You'll clear a handful of stages (each having multiple branching rooms) and then fight a 'mini-boss' at the end of the stage. You'll spend considerable time backtracking through each stage to gather coins, items, unlock chests/rooms etc. 2.) After defeating the handful of stages, you'll fight a 'boss.' 3.) After that, you're forced to start over from 'step 1' - the only difference being that you now have access to a 2nd big boss. *Rinse and repeat to add each new additional boss.The forced grind thrust upon the player to unlock all of the in-game bosses is a shallow (and annoying) way to elongate play-time. By the time I had beaten the 3rd unlockable 'boss,' I had essentially experienced everything the gameplay loop had to offer.Although there are certainly enough relics and guns to potentially maintain some replayability, Neon Abyss shoots itself in the foot by making the details of relics and weapons unknown until the player commits to the selection. It's all too common to pick up a relic that's either completely useless or one that otherwise craps on your existing synergies. You cannot drop/remove acquired relics which means you're permanently screwed for the remainder of the run if you lose this needless game of chance. It's quite unintuitive to think that the average player is going to memorize the details of such a large assortment of relics/weapons with only name and visual sprite as a reference. Forcing the player to rely on blind trial-and-error, excessive memorization, or external references in order to effectively build up their character during a run is poor game design and mars what could have otherwise been a standout entry in the genre.

Then they introduce a sudden wall of grind tho progress and unlock more progression and the story....The moment the NPCs start to talk, the game is dead. lines after lines of META developer  humor about not finishing a game and creating a filler content for it..........At least they have self awareness.This literally destroy the small amount of charm that was entirely contained in the visual identity of the pixelart and the retrowave mood.After the grind part, the next two bosses require you to chance upon an item. _childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Bear in mind about half of my time played here is from leaving this running overnight. Sadly, I'm a very torn on this one. Its a fun little roguelite platformer with a ton of different weapons, passive bonuses with interesting combinations, and lets you stack as many as you can find like BOI. The first 5 hours or so are good fun, and there's lots of stuff to unlock which unlocks more stuff in each zone, increasing the complexity, giving you more control, applying more random luck, etc. It's a great package on first glance.But, it won't take long before you reach the point where your weapon becomes your own worst enemy. There are lots of upgrades which increase the number of projectiles you fire, the size of your projectiles, add secondary effects (explosions, leaves fire, shoots lightning, etc.) and before you know it, you go from a professional bullet dodger to trying to dodge invisible enemy projectiles in a screen FILLED with absolute particle effect nonsense. You can reach the final level with as much health and armor as you can acquire, with as many 'chance to dodge' powerups as you like, and still reach the final boss with only a couple of hits left, because you have to clear a ton of rooms filled with enemies and projectiles you just can't ****in' see! Its very frustrating that your own character power, which you can't fully control, and which you want to be as strong as possible, ends up being the only thing that actually kills you. It really doesn't matter what weapon you use, as every upgrade is ambivalent of your weapon choice. They can all become killing machines and screen-wide particle effect disaster areas through things that aren't fully in your control.You can go from feeling like a king, to feeling like a moron in seconds, and for that I have to give it a negative review. It's the kind of game that I'd absolutely love to get invested in more, but regularly failing through events that aren't even my own fault isn't a game anymore. There's nothing more to learn when the game doesn't give me any visibility. I have absolutely no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea what the bosses after level 5 do, even though I've killed 3 more bosses after that, because I just cannot see jack ****. I'm just trying to kill them before they kill me and hope I dont get hit as a blind man trying to walk through the gauntlet in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.They desperately need to improve the particle effect soup problem and make it clearer where your character is, and where the enemy's/projectiles are. Fix that and this game would be top tier awesomeness I'd pick up and play regularly. Without it, its just another disappointment in a sea of Roguelites that always seem to excel in the first few hours, and then drop the ball, having missed the point of the 'power fantasy' entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why I only see the dev replying to English comments despite I know the game is from a Chinese dev... So I am writing this in English.First off, I like this game: great visual and overall fun to play. It is rare to see a game has the ambition to become the binding of issac.However, after the first couples of hours, I feel this game can hardly live up to the ambition and the game is somewhat boring and even annoying. Here is a (non exhaustive) list of why:Why boring:- repetitive levels: ETG and issac does not give me that- repetitive items: the items just look different, they are largely the same. Both ETG and Issac have lots of game mech changing items. Maybe I have not unlocked them but unlocking needs grinding. Types of guns are repetitive as well.- repetitive soundtrack- repetitive enemies: part of why I feel the combat boring. ETG has more engaging combat.Why annoying:- unnecessary platforming: I do not feel the landscapes are properly designed. They don't add anything to the combat, but rather I have to climb up the ladder to go to the next room- change of angel and devil room. Lots of people said that - a mindless attack makes all effort in vain- the female character's melee and interact share the Rb button! _childDocuments_.review: Stunning visuals, amazing music, and the exact gameplay loop you want from these types of games. There are many different builds you can end up on in a run, and the most powerful ones are absolutely ludicrous. Get the right items, and the game becomes a neon explosion. A persistent upgrade tree makes every run feel rewarding, even if you lose.My only criticism is that the game encourages you to brute-force through bosses. A lot of them become trivial when you have a really powerful build going, leading to me not actually fully understanding some of the encounters because I always seem to melt them before I have to pay attention to mechanics. That can be offset by increasing to a harder difficulty, or just by enjoying the sheer chaos of feeling unstoppable.Great game, I recommend it to any roguelike and roguelite fan out there.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 MUST BUY- ESPECIALLY IF ON SALE!Everything about this game is RNG based. But that's what makes it FUN. You use what you find to progress to the next floor. Its NOT all about finding/getting the most OP gear and easily running through floors. Though you can upgrade every weapon you find making stronger such as multiple projectiles and faster shooting speed. Theirs TONS of unique weapons items cosmetics and pets that you can find all of which can be upgraded as well to help you fight and progress through the dungeon and all also have their own unique perks. There's so many different unique items with so many different unique perks and ability's. and that's what keeps the game fun. There's no grind at all and every single dungeon run you do will be different from the last do to vast majority of RNG that takes place.CON- it is pretty visually intense with so much happening on screen at times so it is easy to lose track of your character sometimes. but if you like bullet hells and bright LEDs this is the game for you. lol
