_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten all the bosses in the game so I an essentially finished.The good: -Guns: lots of guns to choose from, ranging from borderline useless to straight god tier. Gun finds rarely tend to stop a run tho unless you get extremely bad luck. -Combat: fast paced almost bullet hell type combat. On normal it feels like a good mixture of difficult and fun. -Items: some really awesome items that can make you ridiculously overpowered. This is what will have the largest affect on you runs and how far they go.-Bosses: are challenging but fair and if you are good at seeing patterns/learning game mechanics are not too difficult to take no damage from. Also they evolve every time you beat a final boss to become more difficult.-The colour scheme they use is right up my alley. Lots of bright flashy colours, Neon is in the name for a reason. The Bad:-Eggs/Pets: These things tend to be either just bullet sponges that don't help much to things that can downright just impede your progress. I have only found 1 actually useful so far and that's the little blue guy that gives you shields when he picks up hearts. (hopefully devs fix these guys are they are integral to the game in many ways)-Skill tree: Only a few actually good options and they are usually hidden behind less good options. Also with how long it takes to beat the game the upgrades cost too much. -Melee attack button and the use button need to be able to be bound separately to avoid accidentally melee attacking certain objects -The enemies that are only vulnerable when they change colour to attack often have slightly too small of windows in which to damage them, specifically the smaller ones. The Neutral:The Faith System: I like how the system works and the risk/reward component to it. What I don't like is the placement of some of the objects needed to interact with to further your faith build up. It can pull you right out of a run in the later stages where you need a certain amount of purple or red bars filled.Overall Neon Abyss is a fun action-platformer roguelite with some downright excellent gameplay that is held back slightly by some of the games systems.  I am recommending it with the caveat that it can get frustrating at times (like any game in the genre tbh). I would give the game a 7 /10 imo and if the devs polished up just a few small things it would be easily a 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: While this review is indeed still positive; Neon abyss is a mediocre game at best.To keep things short I would say only buy this game at a heavy discount and if you are a real roguelike/lite fan.There are some things the game certainly does well such as adding a neat feature to disable a small amount of enemies from future runs, or being able to collect small lore cards troughout your runs. Furthermore a lot of weapons are pretty cool or have cool effects going on.The general gameplay and artwork is decent as well, the story is kinda neat too.But this is pretty much where all the positives end, everything else in the game is just mediocre or downright frustrating.I got all major unlocks in the game and have almost all achievements, meanwhile I also took notes of most issues I found.So lets list them all in a wall of misery!- The game has decent music, issue is that it often feels like there are only 3 songs most of the time- A bunch of bosses suddenly spawn in bossrooms and have a high chance to telefrag you when they spawn in, getting a free hit unless you memorise where each boss spawns.- Very low enemy variety, most are just previous versions of themselves but they fire an extra projectile or something as an example.- Some of the lowest variety between floors I've seen in a roguelike/lite, almost feels like recolors at times.- Certain endgame special bosses have annoying requirements to reach them, making getting certain endings you may want to get on a run often impossible.- You can upgrade your weapons 8 times with items, these items upgrade all your weapons you have and pick up in the future, yet these items keep dropping after reaching weapon level 8. These upgrades replace other rare item drops and thus can screw you over in the long run if unlucky.- Probably the biggest problem in the game is that while a lot of the player weapons look pretty awesome at times, many weapons absolutely FILL the screen with their projectiles/beams etc. to an extent that most of all hits you take in the entire game are from enemy projectiles turning invisible because your own projectiles just completely overlap everything. - There are a bunch of difficulty settings which is neat, sadly the actual difference between all difficulties is quite minor.- The majority of enemy visual design is just goofy at best and uninspired at most.All things said and done, Neon Abyss is very mediocre but I guess it is still good enough to warrant a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: There are better roguelikes out there.Neon Abyss starts off as a really fun game. For the first ten hours or so, I loved what I was playing. As the game went on though, the flaws became very apparent and ruined my enjoyment of the game.Gameplay:Running and shooting enemies is fun for the most part. Attacks make sense, and every enemy attack pattern can be learned. Melee weapons on the other hand, are effectively worthless on anything but the weakest of enemies. Hitboxes on melee weapons never felt like they worked correctly, and these weapons rarely did enough extra damage to be worth it.Getting Stronger:The fun of every roguelike comes from the crazy items and synergies built up over a run. Neon Abyss has a very respectable 400 items to play around with. However, acquiring the items is just as important as the items themselves, and this is where the game falls apart completely for me. Typically, each floor has an item room with a choice between two items, a shop which sells one gun and one item, a boss room that drops a stat boosting item, an arena which may pay out with an item, and minigames that pay out with items. Oh, the minigames...The minigames destroy the balance of the game entirely. These games are all timing based and have nothing to do with the core gameplay of Neon Abyss. This would be fine as a distraction, but these minigames pay out with items on every victory. Some of these minigames can be played over three times per floor, allowing for insane amounts of items in one run.Characters:Every single character felt the same to me. Each character has a slightly different starting weapon as well as a unique ability. Outside of the character who could carry two guns, I never found these unique abilities to be particularly useful and was more successful when I just ignored them completely. I fail to see the purpose of alternate characters if they don't have anything substantial to differentiate themselves from the default.I want to like this game, but I find it really hard to enjoy it when it feels like every run comes down to blind luck and hoping I don't botch the super hard timing minigames to get items. Maybe it's just a skill issue on my part, but this game felt like it leaned too far in the luck based direction for my liking.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what I don't like about this game.Artstyle is absolutely amazing, music is good, controls are tight. _childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I was so close to giving Neon Abyss a thumbs-up. Not because it's a standout roguelite in a field dominated by giants, but because it was a fun diversion that cribbed a lot of mechanics from other, better known titles in the genre and combined them to make something that was decent. Not mind-blowing, not terribly difficult, but if you scored it on sale, worth the money.I was digging my time with Neon Abyss -- not as many hours sunk as Steam says I have, because I have an infant to feed between naps, but a decent amount -- and after I puzzled out the Wisdom/Violence system (the only original thing this title brings to the party), I went after those last three bosses. I won't detail the Wisdom/Violence system here, but the path to the last bosses basically boils down to this: You build up a gauge, which lets you visit a special room with loot. Sometimes -- and ONLY sometimes -- you will also get a special Boss Token in addition to that loot. This token lets you visit that boss's level at the end of your run. Didn't get a token? No extra boss for you. But let's say you DID get that token, and you beat that boss. Guess what? Now you have to beat the Cursed version of that boss, because that's the only way you're going to get to the final boss of the game. So just do that all over again, hoping you get that Token that appears sometimes and not others, but this time you have to then build that same gauge up to max again while in the level in question. Now, you can build that gauge up and get a chance at that Boss Token multiple times per run. I'm no great player, and it's not hard to build the gauge up a few times before you hit the end of a standard run. I went through this rigmarole enough to beat one Cursed Boss and faltered on the final. Tried to do it all over again with the other Cursed one, and let me tell you, from experience, that you can build that bar up three times in a run, get zero Boss Tokens, and then do it all over again next run, three times, zero boss tokens.So after two fantastic runs where the only thing keeping me from finishing the game was – a dice roll? coin flips? -- keeping even the possibility of attempting the final two bosses outside my grasp, I said no. You can give me a bad loadout because of RNG, you can give me sub-par resource availability because of RNG, but to just arbitrarily lock off the last, hardest part of the game due to RNG?  I don't want to be the That's Bad Game Design Guy, but . . . *gestures wildly*.It's unnecessary padding. It's a bad implementation of RNG. It needs to go, but it's still here. There are roguelites out there that will punish you while respecting your time. Play those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: In short:PRO:- Plays great with a controller (there's currently a bug in the menu, you can't press down without pressing up first)- Great music and you even have a dance feature in the bar- Many rooms, and even secret levels that look pretty cool- Lots of guns, power-ups and pets- Pretty easy to learn and get decent atCON:- Using certain game mechanics will disable your achievements- RNG is absolutely awful, from 10 runs, you're lucky if you get 4 decent ones- Some level design is just bad and you cannot reach certain areas, and you also don't get power-ups that will help you get to them in those particular runs.- Devs try to enforce people to have fun a certain way that doesn't appeal to many- There are no accessibility issues for people with various impairments, except for an aim assist that i don't think it works in the first placeLong detailed review:First, i am not a good roguelike player, hell, i had to ask my good friend to give me a breakdown of this genre because there are many confusing aspects to it, and it's more confusing because many indie titles just throw that term around everywhere.I figured i would jump in this, because i loved how the game looked, and i liked the presentation overall.Second, i really love the gameplay, there are lots of weapons, power-ups and pets that give you a hand in various ways, the levels are beautifully crafted (visually), effects are cool, music is very delightful. And yet, i am not really having fun, and you might ask yourself why.1. I know people complain about RNG in many games, but i think, in this case, it's very different. It seems like the devs generally (not just with the RNG) went an extra mile just to prevent you, the player/customer to have fun.2. You get some eggs that you can hatch, but you can end up getting pets that actually harm you. As you progress through the game, instead of unlocking more interesting stuff, you unlock... a transmog system? And a "cheat code" system that actually punishes you if you use it.Most of my complaints are tied to the achievement system (Which some of you don't care about, and probably are repeating in your heads, "hurr durr achievements are pointless", but tough luck, some people like this system for different reasons, and it contributes to your overall experience with each indiviual game).1. You finally hit the jackpot and manage to have some good RNG after dying 6 times in a row? Would you like to play with that RNG again? Great, you can, but the achievements are disabled.2. You'd like to replace some of the monsters? You can, but if you do it too much, achievements will be disabled?3. You just unlocked the "cheat code" system, which are not even cheat codes, you first have to find cheats (they cost some neon coins you get, and you buy them from a vending machine that either gives you some wiki-like items, either cheat codes, it's random), they cost crystals that you open the doors, and really aren't doing anything too crazy, plus they have a limit on how many you can use. You want to use them? Fine! But guess what... You're bloody right! For using our mechanic we worked so hard, we'll blap you in the face.For some reason, the devs thought it's a good idea to force people to have fun the developers' way, without even considering that people might want to play their own way, and this is not a multiplayer game, it doesn't even have local co-op or anything. Plus achievements really don't grant people anything, besides a nice pleasant dopamine hit in the brain that lasts few minutes.Some achievements are probably literally impossible to obtain, and whoever says otherwise, i will just assume they used an achievement unlocker (For example, there's an achievement that requires you to complete a run (whole game), without ever getting damaged. In a bullet hell game...Hotline Miami is easier in this regard. Hell, Quake 1 on Nightmare difficulty is easier than what these achievements are requiring from players.Achievements mean different things for different people, and they don't have any sort of value, why are they even giving so much ♥♥♥♥ about them in the first place? Let alone punish you if you use the actual game's mechanics.Okay, apart from the achievements what else is wrong with the game?Lack of any accessibility options. There's only an aim assist option that isn't doing almost anything (I can't see any difference if i toggle it on or off). In my case i need to work 4 times harder due to some neurological issues i have. Sometimes rooms and chest spawn in places you cannot get to unless you have wings power-ups (in 20 hours of playtime i only got them twice), there are also other power-ups that help, but yea, it's not really a good mechanic.You cannot progress unless RNG. I've defeated the previous unlocked boss for about 5 times already, unlocked the next one, but guess what, RNG didn't give me the option to fight the next one, so i am basically doing the same thing over and over hoping i will get the chance to fight the next boss.Bottom line, devs tend to have an annoying sadistic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ personality. I don't want the game to be easier, i want it to be more fair, there needs to be more balance, and the game should appeal to multiple groups of people, and people should be able to have fun their own way, the way they see fit.Game overall is good and you most likely will have fun in it, but that fun is strongly limited by the developers' faulty logic and lack of consideration.These issues for me, personally, and to many others are bumming, and remove the pleasure of actually playing the game.I would've seen myself play this for 300-400 hours easily if it wasn't for these issues, but i am about 20 hours in, and i doubt i will make past 30.If you don't care about accessibility options and are a healthy fella, if you don't care about the achievements, and if you generally are a tough try-hard with a humilation fetish, you will really love this.If not, you will still have fun, because the game is awesome overall, but you might not get your money worth entirely.This game is a palm's length away from being really great, but i am really skeptical devs will come out and say "Hey, we improved the RNG system a bit, you no longer will be screwed by your own pets, and hey, we decided you should have fun your own way, just enjoy yourself and don't worry about anything else".

_childDocuments_.review: While well made and interesting in it's own way, there's some glaringly obvious issues. The main of which is visual clutter, like the title implies there's a lot of neon in this game, yours and enemy projectiles brightly glow, which makes it really hard to tell what you're supposed to dodge. This is especially bad on later levels with more enemies and your upgraded guns firing more projectiles. One of the other flaws is with the "karma" system; you have "Wisdom" and "Violence" bars, the problem is that any time you shoot or blow up a chest or a door that consumes one of the currencies, crystals, it locks that chest or door to a "Violence" path, which requires HP instead. There's no way to revert the change, so any accidental shots could potentially lock you out. I don't know why they left it that way, it just seems such an obvious oversight. A bigger issue is the promised variety of items, now admittedly I haven't played much, but every run so far I've had at least 3-4 different items that do almost exactly the same thing, which is pretty much just stat upgrades. All that being said, I think this game has some neat ideas, like all the different pet eggs, or being able to "ban" some enemies and items from appearing. It's just a shame that it's biggest problem is the visual mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a roguelite that combines fast-paced action with an addictive, randomly generated gameplay. You'll start each new playthrough with nothing but your fists and your wits, with a multitude of weapons, items, and abilities to discover and collect along the way. The dungeons are filled with enemies and traps, but with enough skill and luck, you might just be able to face the final boss and take your place at the top of the leaderboard. Neon Abyss is a game that will engage you for hours on end, and it's perfect for anyone who loves a challenge and the thrill of discovering something new with every playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: basically a worse version of enter the gungeon.lots of needless visual noise, the music is not as a good as advertised in the shop screen.The fight system is shut-your-brain-off stupid simple, you just hold fire down fire and that's practically it, no dodge rolls, no ammo management, no reliable secondary sources of damage (bombs are kinda useless in combat), there are no interesting combos or mechanics, on top of that you get those egg critters that are there to basically passively aid you and add nothing else but more visual noise.I can see how this game's music and cartoonish/mobile-ish graphics can be appealing to younger kids but i just don't think genre vets can find it appealing or challenging.I will say though, that this game is very well optimized and runs incredibly smoothly, I love the art and I cannot wait to see a future title from this team.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite fun for a while. It has a lot of weapon customization/synergy aspects that are promising and fun. I like the aesthetics and the distant bass of the club in the bgm. It has pretty solid platforming and weapons feel pretty weighty. Hit boxes and clipping can be a bit jank but otherwise core gameplay is pretty tight. My biggest complaint with the game is that crazy weapon combos is very gun base rather than modifier base. It was a lot less insane than I was hoping for but it is still a solid roguelike.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: So I've just beaten the last boss of Neon Abyss and... Yeah okay this game is an Early Access that just isn't called Early Access. There is no conclusion to the story, no "true final boss" (both bosses are branch possibilities). I still have barely unlocked anything but three characters because unlike other games where you start with multiple characters (EtG) or unlock them through achievements (TBoI), NA is just... yeah, grind more. *You just grind to get money, and then spend said money on upgrades. The "synergies" are honestly rare, more often than not you just want + damage and + bullets. Some of the guns are flat out overpowered, I just had a run where I took no damage. Not because I'm good, but because I had a gun that protected me with Guardian Sprites all the friggin time.The levels just... mesh together. To compare it to the other two games I've cited above, when you're in a level in The Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon, it looks like THAT level, and not any other. In Neon Abyss, the four first look a lot alike, and even afterwards... There's not much difference. I'll blame the enemy design for that as well, as it feels like you face the same enemies over and over again. The low amount of bosses you can face, and the fact that half of them are just harder versions of the first level bosses doesn't help in that feeling of progressing through the levels. The Managers are nice, though, even if it kinda feels like the hardest ones were put first (the final boss before the optional ones feels easier than the one before him).Flight breaks this game, as usual. Most bosses can be cheesed by flying over them, so if you can fly... yeap, you just won. Except the devs must have realized that because you can't fly when you face one of the optional bosses at the end of your run (haven't confirmed with the other boss yet).All in all, if you like Rogue-Lites... Yeah, pass Neon Abyss for now. It's not ready yet and it FEELS like itThat being said, in a year, maybe, when the game has a lot of patches to add an actual ending to the story, more bosses, more enemies to feel like we're actually progressing through harder levels, I think it'll be a good game. _childDocuments_.review: Don’t mistake my hours spent. I actually played this game extensively before it came out, as I was working on a review for my YouTube channel. I felt obligated to leave a review here because the game is ‘mixed’ in recent reviews. Please don’t get the idea that this game isn’t fun, because it is, a lot, but it can also be very frustrating. It’s a wiki game, which are the opposite of relaxing, and this is no exception.My video for the game never got made due to health issues. But I played the full game, recorded all the footage, wrote and recorded the script - it just never got edited. I’ve done my research though and overall strongly recommended the game.HOWEVER, it is not an infinite game. It’s not Gungeon, Risk of Rain or Binding of Isaac. It’s a game you should put down once you’re done with it, usually once you’ve exhausted the content (which to be fair: there is a lot of!)It truly captures the essence of what we love about these games, in all their broken glory. However that does also come at the cost of very poor visibility, and *a lot* of frustrating deaths. You’ve just got to build around knowing you’re going to take hits, and for once, that is not a skill issue.The synergies between upgrades are glorious. My first run on the PC version gave me a homing rocket launcher, an upgrade which duplicated my bullets, then another upgrade which made my explosives leave trails of fire. I was wiping rooms with ease.Within that same run, I changed up my build, and found a gun that let me turn my hearts into gold, alongside an upgrade which increased my rate of fire when I got hurt, which now I could trigger whenever I wanted and got rich for it. I was buying out every store, including something which made my rate of fire even hire the more keys I had, and I could afford plenty.If *those parts* appeal to you, rather than a balanced or challenging game, then give it a chance. It’s currently in a Team17 Humble Bundle with all the DLC, Trepang2 and some other good games. That’s why I decided to support the makers and buy a second copy for myself. I’m sure you’ll enjoy at least most of your time, if you can push through the rough.Overall a solid 7 out of 10. Despite what the internet believes: that’s better than the average, and is still worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while it had potential, has a number of flaws. I can't recommend it in its current state.First off, it seems to be missing a few features present in other roguelikes that seem kind of obvious. You can't see the descriptions of items without picking them up (Although, there is one item, and a passive benefit for a *DLC* character that changes this), you can't drop items (Which is an issue, if you pick up something it turns out you didn't like), when looking at items in a shop, you can't even see the name of them, just the price and appearance. Furthermore, there's no equivalent to the Ammonomicon (At least, one at the point I'm at.). This means you can't what an item does and so forth easily. Unless you the wiki. (It also means there's not really any established lore for items, which just kinda makes me sad. I like that sort of thing) Furthermore, it's hard to tell what items are unlocked, or even if items can be locked. I'm still not sure. I don't think they are, I've not killed a boss and had it told me "X is unlocked!" even with some of the more endgame ones.The pet system is cool, but kinda flawed. You can find eggs, which, eventually, will turn into familiars. They have a limited amount a health, but can be useful. However, I'd say there are probably 3 that are actively detrimental - Peter (Turns hearts in to moldy hearts), Grabber (Takes your money, gives you pickups), and Vibrant Ball (Blocks shots, explodes on death). However, these are all annoying because: Moldy hearts can hurt you, and it can essentially serve as a roadblock, as there's no way to remove it (Except the pet that turns hearts to shields, I guess), and you can pick it up at full health, meaning it could just hurt you. The economy for grabber is weird, it seems to be more based off of a chance to drop something upon picking up money, rather than trading money for pickups. I've had him pick up 50 valued coins, and drop nothing. Vibrant ball blocks *your* shots as well, meaning if you've got explosive bullets, it can just outright kill you (And it has, for me). Add this to the fact you can't drop these or determine what pet you get, and it's pretty annoying.There's also some items which are kinda detrimental (Or useless), and, since you can't see item descriptions before picking stuff up, you might grab something you didn't want and end up stuck with it. For example, the Matchbox, a seemingly useful item that lets you blow up rock by having your eggs touch them. However, it's fairly unwieldy, and if you have enough eggs, they'll just blow up on pretty much anything in the room. Plus, due to the way explosives are calculated on things like the doors that take 2 bombs to destroy, you can have a bunch of eggs hit it, and it only be affected by one.The Wisdom and Violence mechanic is cool. But, like a lot of things, it's flawed. You get Wisdom by putting crystals in things and then clearing rooms without getting hurt, and violence by attacking things you might put crystals in and running into them, as well as just taking damage. The more annoying thing about this is that any damage turns wisdom objects into Violence ones, even damage from enemies, pets, or things largely out of your control. Then they can just get in your way, like the moldy hearts. Plus, Violence seems to outweigh Wisdom, in terms of progression.Playthrough to playthrough progression is slow and grindy. You get 8-9 coins max per run, and, even just on the second page of things, that's enough for one item. Other things: Some of the items seem useless. There's not many different bosses. Some of the weapons seem useless. There's not much variety in the music, and it gets really tiring after awhile. There's not much in terms of discernible lore for this game (Aside for, say, the stuff on the steam page). Pickups are either extremely scarce, or you have more than you'll ever need. The minigame rooms are fun and interesting, but rare, and hard to unlock. There don't seem to be any challenges for unlocks. Some items are useless without other items to pair with them (Popcorn (Bullets explode) in later parts of the game and Dangerous Mine (Drop a mine when you jump) are pretty much useless without Big Daddy (Immune to explosions). The game starts to feel very repetitive very quickly. Some of the enemies aren't fair to fight. And so forth.The game's got issues. It's also got potential.I'd say add a compendium for items and lore, fix some of the items, implement the ability to drop items and pets, lower the price, add more music, make it so you can at the very least see the names of items in shops, add more bosses, add more room variation, and then the game might be better.I can't recommend it as is.

_childDocuments_.review: is a twin-stick roguelite platformer with a ton of outside references, much like  and  In this game, you choose from the available characters and take a dive into the Abyss, which becomes progressively deeper (more levels) as you beat the game multiple times in its permanent progression. Killing bosses also drops credits that you can use to unlock new things for future runs or to instill a permanent rule change for future runs. What stands out about this game is the large amount of power-ups and loot that you get during any lasting run that makes the game seem overwhelmingly silly, but still fun.Starting up this game, you get automatically a sense of the bright colors and flashing lights you can expect to see in playing. The pixel artwork is really pretty to look at. The sprite, objects, explosions, bullets, etc. animations are all done with plenty of detail to make the action/reaction gameplay very enjoyable to look at.After a short tutorial and a boss fight that you cannot lose, you are then tossed into your first run, so good luck! The game is very responsive playing on the keyboard + mouse or with a controller, so you will be able to take your pick and dive in. As with any such roguelite games where you will be expected to die a lot and then improve over time. The most important aspect of playing these games is the knowledge about the game's mechanics that you cannot get except by repeated exposure.So your task is to go from room to room, clear out all of the enemies and loot what you can, then move on. The doors lock up after you enter and trigger the enemies to spawn, so you have to clear them out to move on. Some rooms will not have enemies but may have items, consumables, or chests/destructible rocks, etc. There are a number of different resources to manage in this game, including the expected coins, keys, and bombs, but also purple crystals, which are important for opening some doors, chests, or for active skills attached to many weapons that will use these up as well.And then there are followers, a lot of followers. When you see an egg on the ground, you can pick it up and it will have a potential to hatch into a follower or upgrade one you already have. These followers each have their own abilities and traits, and to balance the fact that you can get so many in each run, they all have their respective HP and if they take too many hits, they will die. Many of them have an associated death effect, so there are definitely times when there are plenty of fireworks on the screen.The bosses are randomized from a pool, so even if you have trouble making it past the first couple of levels for a while, you will still be seeing different bosses from run to run. This is the case for the non-final boss floors. The game starts being 5 levels. After beating it once, it becomes 7 levels, then 8 after the next time you beat it, with a couple more extending progressions after that. These pre-set "final" levels always have the same bosses within.After the very first run, you will be able to change the difficulty of your next run, choose your starting character, and also pay up some credits at the bar to do some permanent unlocking for future runs. If you are unhappy about the way you handled a particular situation or part of a run, you can always write down the seed number that is displayed upon death and you can enter it again for a repeat of the same Abyss set up. Using a seeded run will stop you from getting achievements, but will definitely teach you how to get better from your own mistakes.I find that any run that lasts for a reasonable length of time leads to the playing character becoming rather over-powered, in a rather fun and also messy way. Your bullets will increase in size as your weapon becomes more powerful. You may have increased number of bullets, etc. It becomes a little bit more difficult to see enemy fire if you get to this point. But more often than not, it becomes much easier to deal with the enemies also. But there are some teleporting enemies, or enemies whose bullets break into smaller ones, that when you are filling up the screen with your own awesome firepower, they can be a bit difficult to spot. Example here where all of the on-screen bullets are my own:I think that there is definitely room for improvement, many of these areas are being addressed and tested in an experimental branch. They are actively working on bug fixes, but still have some that need to be addressed. It's really nice to see that the developers are paying attention to the players' feedback and concerns. I am not really sure how many bosses there are total, but after a few runs, you starting getting used to many of the bosses, each with its movement/attacking patterns. Twin-stick roguelite platformer with a lot of items to loot each run, with their own synergies that make the game rather fun. KB+M works fine, controller works great. You can rebind your keys inside the game.Nice pixel artwork and animations.Sound effects are good and seem to fit the game well. Music can get repetitive after a few hours though, so you may want to listen to something else after a while.Base price is $19.99, pretty reasonable for what the game has to offer. I wish the game wouldn't have the DLC already on launch that's going to incur an extra cost for people who buy after the first week post-release. I have only unlocked one more character so far beyond the starting ones, and by the looks of it, there will be a few more. is quite a lot of fun. Its permanent progression system with unlocks, Abyss increase in size, new enemies/bosses makes it fun to keep going back for more, no matter whether your last run ended in success or failure. These developers definitely listen to the users and have been implementing/trying plenty of changes in the experimental branch that anyone can access. There are still bugs to be fixed and some areas that need polish, hopefully everything gets taken care of sooner than later.There's a seeming adaptation that the game takes to the player, in terms of difficulty, even within the same preset difficult of Easy, Normal, or Hard. From what I understand, there's an even more difficult setting waiting to be unlocked. I wish the DLC given to players during the first week after launch would have been just worked into the game as part of the game instead of having to pay for two additional characters if you happen to buy the game after the first week. While the price isn't unreasonable for this game,  and  do offer more content and more replayability than what's present here.I would still absolutely recommend this game, because of the enjoyment contained within.

_childDocuments_.review: If it was possible to make a "neutral" review on Steam I would for this one...it's certainly not a bad game but it mostly just feels kind of "Eh..."It can be decently fun I guess but for some reason it just feels lacking overall...I'd definitely agree with what I saw another review say that the game feels pretty lacking in personality, which is a shame since I feel like that's an important thing for...well any genre of game really, but for some reason in roguelikes it feels especially so. The art is pretty good at least as far as the boss sprites go, but the players and regular enemies are kind of boring...All at least serviceable though...Something I specifically found myself thinking is that the items tend to seem kind of random in their theming compared to what they do (basketball jersey that makes you take less damage?? I mean I guess...) and neither their theming or effects are very memorable, so unlike a game like Binding of Isaac, I don't remember what any of the items do and have to look them up every time. And then a lot of items have really niche and kind of lame effects like "get a coin when your angry sprites die"...which you get when you don't even have any angry sprites or way to get them in the first place, and maybe you don't even know what an angry sprite is and have never seen one before because you never got an item that spawned them. Unlike what the store page says, none of the items really have interesting synergies that I could find other than "You might need this other item for this item you just picked up to really do anything at all" which...is not exactly the most exciting combination...The progression with the game getting exactly one level and boss fight longer every time you clear it also feels a bit tiresome, though eventually you reach a point where it seems to stop doing that (not 100% sure though)...This is another thing that is kind of like Binding of Isaac which also has a thing where the game gets longer as you clear it repeatedly, but for some reason here it feels more like just going through a checklist...The game also seemed a bit easy, though admittedly I've only played on normal difficulty. Maybe it'd be a bit more interesting if I went up to hard but I haven't bothered with that yet.Being able to turn off the permanent upgrades (just the ones that add new rooms or whatever to the level generation, you can't like...un-unlock characters) seems like kind of an interesting feature though, for if you wanted the game to be less "roguelite"-y, but I'm not sure how unusual a feature it actually is.I dunno, it's not nearly bad enough for me to actually say "No I don't recommend this game" because that seems like it would be too harsh but I think maybe only get it if it's like, on sale or something...and you really don't have any other more interesting game you'd rather get with that money...Not very exciting but if you just want to press buttons for a bit I guess it's fine.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game. On one hand, it appears to completely rip off existing games (notably The Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon),  but the simple change into a platformer instead of a top-down game makes it a unique and fun experience. Even if most of its ideas are directly copied over, I can't say that it isn't fun to have wacky item synergies and cool guns in this new perspective. This feels to me like what Exit the Gungeon should have been - a dungeon exploring platforming roguelike. And though most of the ideas are stolen they are implemented well.My main gripes for the game have to do with the art direction. The core visuals of the dungeon are great, and there are some excellent visuals on the backgrounds and the water and all that. But my problem is that every area looks... basically the same. There are only slight tileset variations but each new level you descend into feels exactly the same as the last. I found this rather disappointing, since in roguelikes part of the excitement comes from reaching completely new areas. I also find the character sprites to be underwhelming. They look like something a young teenager just getting into game dev and pixel art would make. They have little texturing/shading and just look... wrong. I hope they remake these sprites. I'd also like to see more original ideas in the game. Ultimately, though it is fun, I'd rather go play The Binding of Isaac instead. The only reason i'm not is because I burned myself out from that game putting more than 1000 hours into it and I'm waiting for the big update. If they can implement more original ideas into this game and more distinct areas, this could become something special. As it is right now it's still fun and worth the purchase, but will likely not be remembered as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes a game.This game takes all those frustrating elements of other rogue-likes and fills the game with what I call "Sometimes Items." These items that you get, only sometimes, do something. From the help you get from eggs that SOMETIMES hatch, to the items that give you a cool effect SOMETIMES. Wouldnt it be nice to get extra grenades when you pick one up? Sure. What about if it only happens SOMETIMES? Instead of getting an item that gives you an advantage, you get one that SOMETIMES helps. This is further exasperated since there are straight up upgrade items. Items that give you another jump, or just more damage. But those are so rare, you will have entire runs where you have 30+ items, and only two or three are actual upgrades, the rest are SOMETIMES items.

_childDocuments_.review: Previously this review was complaining on a couple of pets, Jack, Vibrant Ball and Blue Doctor. As of right now, the first two, as well as Peter (pet that turns hearts moldy, giving a 50/50 chance for it to deal dmg or heal double, effectively reducing healing to 0 on average.) are removed from the game until a pet update. Blue Doctor and Grabber can be quite annoying as well but, they have their uses. Is it worth the money now? Eeeeeeh, maybe, it isn't too innovative and progression is pretty slow. You get about 8 crests or so every run (if it's completed start to finish). There are multiple upgrade branches, each having 15-20 upgrades or so, ranging in cost from 5 to 10 to 15. Which is...fine I guess, but, say, in gungeon there was way more content after you've actually beaten the game. Try the secret floors, try new bosses, try each character's past, which kept the game fresh. In here, after beating both final bosses in the first 12 hours or so of the game, as opposed to like, first 50 hours or so of gungeon, it really feels like the game is done and theres nothing left to do. Maybe once the game has alternative goals outside of extra unlocks?

_childDocuments_.review: I've ONLY played about half an hour and... I dunno, I just can't get into it. And I love roguelikes and have played a good amount of them. Maybe I'll give it a little more time and if I change my mind, I'll edit the review but for now my opinion is that it's kinda meh? Maybe this is a nitpick but the platforming is not that great. The jumping feels like ♥♥♥♥ because there are some platforms that you just can't jump to. The game tells you not to destroy EVERY destroyable item because you might need them to get to an inaccessible area, so yeah, that's fine I guess? (Even though I think being able to destroy ♥♥♥♥ is fun and telling players not to destroy ♥♥♥♥ is kinda lame but I digress) Anyway, NORMAL platforming to get from one side to another just feels like ♥♥♥♥! It just feels like there isn't any love into the environmental design and it's just a victim to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ code to randomly generate a room. You tell yourself, "Oh I can jump to that platform." BZZZT nope! Gotta jump to THIS platform first by going BACKWARDS and THEN you can go forward. Huh??Another thing: for a platformer AND a bullet hell, there's no built-in dash or a way to clear bullets with bullets that move WAY too fast and have like 0 telegraphing from the enemies. Even top-down games (e.g. Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Isaac, Hades), which gives you even more movement to begin with, usually come with bullet clearing and/or dodgerolls/dash or better telegraphing or slower bullets... platformers limit your movement a lot because gravity so this just feels even worse not to have any I-frames, a way to clear bullets, and barely any telegraphing.... Just feels like I have a rock tied to my ankle with bullets slapping me around. Even learning what the enemy attack patterns are doesn't help much imo.I have no opinion on the item/gun versatility since I really haven't played for that long. The basic thought I had was: the guns are fun, items are not that memorable. The random passives you get through "eggs" is honestly a stupid mechanic alsdkfjasdf why couldn't they just be random items you just FIND in the game rather than just having an RNG-fest? xD That's right, the eggs themselves are RNG. They may hatch and they may not. And when they hatch, it's another randomizer to decide what passive you get. I expect RNG in a game like this but omg this is a stupid way to do it xD Idk, it's not an AWFUL game but I think it's not for me!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The visuals are charming, the music is nice, and the boss fights are enjoyable with few exceptions. Then, a bunch of minor things happen which get in the war and mar the experience so much that it stops being fun. While the visuals are good, it's extremely cluttered, making it difficult to see projectiles, view boss tells, and generally avoid taking damage. Some boss attacks can spawn inside of you, causing unavoidable damage. Projectiles linger after a room is cleared, including enemy death effects which might last for several seconds, meaning you have to be wary even after combat is over. For some guns, like the death ray, the audio has a bit of desync with the mechanics of the weapon, making them oddly hard to use.None of these individually make this a bad game, and even together I don't think I would call this game , but it's too frustrating to play for very long and certainly not good enough to recommend when there's better games in the genre. Go play Dungreed instead if you want a game in this genre which is just better.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, listen up you little monkeys. Neon Abyss, yeah, it really nails that roguelite addiction, doesn't it? Proper gets its grubby mitts into that part of your brain that just wants to have another go. The whole shambolic mess of getting new doodads that completely change how you spread led across the walls. It's brilliant!But...and there's always a 'but' innit? The visibility is absolutely dog ♥♥♥♥♥. You're getting slapped around like a redheaded stepchild just trying to see what's coming at you next. Loads of annoying deaths, I'm telling you.But that's just part of the charm, isn't it? You miserable lot know what you signed up for. Gotta build yourself up, learn to take those hits on the chin. It's not you being total pants at it for once.Now the real star of the show, the glorious synergies between all the upgrades and doodads you can nab. On one run, I got meself a homing rocket launcher that was raining pure hellfire. Duplicate bullets, leaving trails of fire like the devil's skidmarks everywhere I looked. Clearing rooms like it was going out of style.Then I found this neat little gun that turned my hearts into gold any time I got smacked. ﻿Coupled that with an upgrade that increased my fire rate when hurt, so I'm just pummeling myself to get stinking rich and buying up the entire shop. Even got something that made me fire faster with more keys I had. I was rolling in it, telling you!It captures that roguelite chaos beautifully. If you haven't played it yet and you're a fan of that sort of nonsense, maybe give it a go? Just don't blame me when you're hurling your controller through the wall after the millionth cheap death, alright?

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a unique and slightly awkwardly positioned Roguelike indie game. You can see the imitation and blend of many famous Roguelike gameplay but also will experience a rather strange sense of déjà vu in the game.The game has a fun and sophisticated pixel art style, different props and weapons, a variety of game mechanics and level design, and a novel pet system. Neon Abyss certainly has its characteristics and allows players to experience a different Roguelike game experience. The game allows players to make highly customizable choices for their routes, allowing players with different playing styles to flexibly choose their strategies.But this work is not satisfactory. Whether it's the lack of introduction to the game's mechanics and equipment, the repetitive and long-playing game design, or the unbalanced and overly dependent on luck prop design, these really easy to stimulate the player's sense of boredom and displeasure. For players using the handle, the game using the right stick aiming and shooting operation may take a long time to adapt, and the production team focused on the free Neon Abyss: Infinite mobile version of the decision is also quite unfavorable to the PC players to get a good gaming experience. In addition to weapons, props, and modes, even the mobile version has been added to the multiplayer online play mode. Players who paid for the PC version seem to be treated like outcasts - at least for now.I only recommend Neon Abyss to those who have not played too many Roguelike games. Most of the players with more exposure to Roguelike games have strong opinions about this game, and the game itself is not overly innovative in terms of gameplay. Given that the game's mobile version is free, has more fully updated content, and has a multiplayer mode, I really can't think of any advantages of the PC version at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more stingy than Enter the Gungeon at its worst.You'll go an entire level without getting any of the resources you need, either coins, hearts, shields or bombs. The store items cost at minimum 15, and 50 for a weapon, 70 for a passive item. I went 3 floors without getting to even 20, let alone 70. The game seems to have a fundamental hatred of its player when it'll set up so many rooms in a row that require bombs but none of them give you anything worthwhile, several item placements require you to be able to fly or take damage to get to a chest, which will inevitably also be worthless.I had one run where there were several rooms that required them and I didn't have a single bomb on me, the one I did have from starting the run was used to remove some rocks that had a chest behind them and the chest had a SINGLE COIN. After several runs I've decided I can't justify paying $20 for something that so actively disrespects a player's time and effort and I'm refunding it. It doesn't matter how good you play either, I went damageless for an entire floor and I wasn't rewarded for it where even Enter the Gungeon gave you something, and that's the stingiest rogue-like of all time.I don't know if I'm unlucky, or if it's the game being weird but at a time where money's tough to come by I'm not wasting it on a game that has such utter contempt for its player.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 (right now at least)SO! I loved the game initially, but as the previous negative review said, the balancing needs a LOT of work. The game has a decent amount of weapons and a lovely amount of items many of which(just like BoI or EtG) do the same things. The synergistic action going on is much better than many other RL's out there right now, but not quite enough: they feel like fancy veneers. Much of the crazy stuff you see going on is simply power+ pickups and bullets+ pickups, which are both common, and uninteresting after quite a few hours. Most guns suck, a few actually... help.... Items almost universally add power/firerate/bullets which makes them much less unique than say, EtG's item set. The items that don't (I.e. # of enemies killed/items picked up after picking up this item boosts power/firerate, tending to be useless because you get these items MOSTLY AFTER CLEARING THE ROOM >:/) tend to just suck. Why add an item to shoot bullets from a grenade when they're insanely hard to target ANYTHING and you need to save them for opening several different types of doors/rocks?The eggs/pets... are interesting. I don't hate them, but I hate the lack of a way to get rid of certain pets. One steals ALL of the money you find to give you maybe a key or two, one steals ALL of the hearts in the room to give you maybe... 2 shields all together? One orbital pet blocks your shots, which with any explosive guns/popcorn instantly ruins your run. One steals your hearts to give you a 50/50 damaging heart. WHY ARE THESE BENEFICIAL IN ANY WAY? C'mon devs, I know you could've found a way to make these synergistic in ANY way.The difficulty is weird; it's not that hard of a game, but many of the enemies feel cheap. There are several "popup" enemies that have no tells aside from just showing up with maybe .5 seconds to react, IF they're not contact damage. The bosses are far easier than any of the standard rooms, especially as you take 1 full damage from any source after lvl 5. Why not invest the time to make different and more difficult enemies that STILL do .5 damage instead of reskinning the same enemies and just giving them contact damage? Being on easy makes no difference, you still die very cheap, stupid deaths due to enemies either shooting through your bullets(which you can't see), popping up being you with contact damage or being stuck on a side of the room where you can't move. Oh, and they attack as soon as they spawn.Lastly the wisdom/violence system is neat, but broken. I can see how the risk/reward thing was applied, but when an enemy spawns right above your wisdom crystal thing that you need to touch before you even start on the wisdom thing shoots and immediately corrupts it, I feel like the devs could've set SOME safeguards in place. I understand if YOU shoot it, it becomes corrupt; if an enemy shoots it, they're just following pathing logic and often set them off in the process of trying to shoot YOU. Why not reward the player for simply not shooting it? It feels stupid cheap when these things happen. In addition, the meter, once started in either direction, doesn't really want to change. Take damage? Violence. C'mon now...Overall, very well made game, with a similar love and touch that EtG and BiO had, but I feel like they were borrowing too many mechanics that made those games work, changing one or two things about them, and kinda ruining the genius that made those mechanics work for those games. Change doesn't mean better. I may try to finish the game on easy, but with the endless grind that doesn't really add all that much, I don't know if I even care to finish the game. Very disappointing considering I was very excited for the game initially. Would I recommend? I suppose, but only until the devs figure out the balance in this game; weapons/pets suck most of the time, the enemies are often very cheap and hard to read and the wisdom/violence system is broken. I'd like to love this game, but they tried too much without making sure it all fit together. I hope they take community critique into consideration because this game is sooooo close to being amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: After initially being impressed by the conglomeration of overlapping mechanics, shiny things, and cute little buddies following me around, I had a good first experience with this game. I even won my first run without dying, which was swell.My subsequent runs were not a similar experience.Having played a vast litany of roguelikes through the years, there are some things you can sort of 'smell', for lack of a better word, in terms of basic gamesense and playability. There become commonalities across the genre that start to become not style choices but purely functional usability issues. Things like allowing map teleports with or without 'teleport/portal checkpoints', how you allow the player to handle loot they don't want, whether or not rerolls are a part of your system, etc. etc. etc.. To a certain degree, any or all of these can be sealed behind an unlock system and still be acceptable, but if your initial experience with a game is lacking any of these core functionalities at the start, it sets a worrying precedent for how seamless your ongoing experience will be. In my mind, it also says a lot about how much your time is given value versus another experience.My case in point for this involves a necessary comparison. In Enter the Gungeon, a game primarily about getting cool guns, whenever you do NOT have a cool gun, you are probably not having a very fun time. Dodging bullets and shooting enemies w/ your basic firearm is all well and good to an extent, but the default weapons are programmed to be sort of clunky and underpowered, encouraging you to replace them and begin rotating superweapons as soon as possible.The problem with this setup, at least in my experience, is that whenever you begin a run, and, for whatever reason, do not run into the necessary resources to secure yourself some kind of upgrade (keys, coins, whatever meta currency allows you to unlock systems, etc.), the run is abhorrently unfun, and will continue to be so until RNG decides to fix it.In some long term versus short term projections, this isn't that big of an issue. How patient are your players, and how big are your rooms? How satisfying is the core shooting mechanic, and how well have you integrated the physical environment into your encounters? In all of these aspects, Neon Abyss seems to grind its gears rather than attempt to excel. Teleport stones are fine, but not when reaching them or adjacent rooms requires fifteen additional seconds of platforming just to search out a new route or pick up a power-up you missed. This is, again, a pure usability issue. I'm probably  not a particularly patient person, so I can see this as somewhat of a pet peeve--but even then, from a design perspective, I cannot understand why, when presented with the two options, "allow the player to instantly backtrack anywhere and reach a resource or path they need" vs. "force the player to jump/move/wait for 5-15 seconds in order to traverse a room no matter how many times they go through it", you would for any reason pick the latter.Plodding around with the default gun in this game did not feel fun to us. The unlock tree and buddy system felt great, but after 3 or 4 restarted runs in a row, going entire floors without a key or sufficient gold to buy our way out of the hole, it seemed a precedent had been set in motion before we even began. This will surely level out towards the mid-game—the law of averages dictates that EVENTUALLY I'm going to get a key, or access to a gun, or SOMETHING. But going through two floors keyless and watching sods of loot pass by just because I couldn't double jump, or didn't have a grenade, etc. etc. etc.. it just sucked. And I didn't want to do it again any amount of times. I can point to countless examples of other games in this genre and parallel genres that let you 'have cool thing' right from the get go. And, at the risk of pre-empting possible counter-critique, if you 'start with good stuff after you unlock it', then you do not START with good stuff, in the true sense of the word. If I just bought this game, which I had, and I want to boot it up and 'do cool thing', I did not feel I had a fair enough opportunity to do that. It is, overall, a fairly entitled perspective. But it's one I have, whether I'm just spoiled in the genre now, or my standards are too high, or whatever.I suspect Binding of Isaac fans would quite like this game, but even Isaac gives you a free initial item that you can restart for to a degree. The boss encounters were admittedly very fun, and the bullet patterns are unabashed in their Touhou referencing. Some of the other guns felt fun to use too, IDK. I'm sorry I didn't end up liking this. So it goes.Oh, and as a final nitpick, the single instance of a female player character bummed me out. Feeling like someone I want to be when I play a game is important to me, and I'll often pick characters based on how they feel to me as opposed to their in game abilities. Only one girl made me sad. Maybe it's dumb. But it was my experience.EDIT: I'm editing this review after giving the game more of a chance. Subsequent runs have seem less key-starved, but still had problems with other resources. The platforming puzzles are incredibly binary and punishing. Every single character other than the default one feels less fun to play. So many of the items feel completely useless. I don't want to use melee, I don't want to get perks for my melee, I don't want something completely arbitrary like 'DO MORE MELEE DAMAGE WHEN IN THE AIR', and there is absolutely no interplay of 'when to pick what item' or 'which item do I pick', because you don't get to pick. Whatever the game hands you is what your build is, and pretending that you can 'aim' for certain items is stupid, because you have absolutely no influence over anything you get. The two redeeming qualities this game has are that 1) getting overpowered generally feels good, as it does in any game where you can get 'overpowered', and 2) there is the purple laser beam from Raiden. That second one alone almost made me change my review, but after starting yet another run as the default character, realizing none of the unlocks I would be getting will save me from the hell I'm in, having done three runs in a row in which I kept the first gun I found because it was flatly better than every subsequent gun I encountered, and finding a loot item that is completely worthless to my ideal build and playstyle, I quit out with an intense urge to never play this game again. I will probably give it one more chance. I am not even yet cresting the litany of complaints this game has generated for me, and it is by the grace of god that I even bothered to type this as feedback in the hopes that maybe some future soul will be warned away from being as infuriated as I was.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I had decided this was worth changing to a thumbs up review a while back. The game has received several updates since my initial review, and I've definitely gotten enough enjoyment out of it to warrant a positive review. Old review:Wow, I can't believe I'm giving this a thumbs down!  It's fun!  I really like it.  If this were Early Access I would be giving it an overwhelming thumbs up!But it's not, and it should be.  There are lots of bugs and a few things that just need a little bit of polish. I guess everyone has their own opinions about games being released for $20 that are Early Access and stay that way for years.  I've seen some really great ones, like Dead Cell that were solid games to begin with that eventually released out of Early Access.  Then I see games made in 2013 that are still priced over $20 that never left Early Access and clearly have been abandoned.This feels like good Early Access game.  The style and gameplay really scratches that Dead Cell/Enter the Gungeon itch.  Some of the items are a bit less original than Gungeon.  A lot seem to do the same sort of stuff like give you an extra jump or simply increase damage/fire rate/speed/jump height ect.  But building lots of items in a playthrough gets pretty crazy and satisfying.  This reminds me a lot of Risk of Rain, which I loved. It advertises "unlimited synergies"  I guess that's true, but it's not really the same as Gungeon where if you get two matching items they do something completely different than what they do on their own.  But that's not really crucial to having a bunch of items stack to make unique abilities and gameplay.  It's just what I had sort of come to expect the term "synergies" to mean in a game like this.The levels are a little redundant. I often see exact rooms repeated, possibly even on the same run.  This makes me concerned that even with plenty of content still left to unlock, it could easily end up feeling grindy and monotonous.  This is the main area that seems like it needs a bit of polish to me.  I'm happy to stay that it has remained challenging so far.  Even if you get super stacked to the point where you feel almost invincible, some of those stacked abilities can work against you.  I just defeated the final boss for a run and was randomly shooting my weapon a few more times since I knew all my stacked abilities would be gone once I went through the portal.  Well my 'chance to fire a rocket' ability apparently hit one of the familiars floating around me and the explosion took the last half a heart of life I had left.  *facepalm*I went to check which was the current main boss I was working on to see if I still got credit for defeating the one I just killed, but I couldn't actually confirm whether I did just yet because the game glitched and none of my commands ended up working.  I was just stuck on the boss screen.  I had to exit the window and shut the game down through Steam. That's exactly the kind of thing that I have no problem looking past in an Early Access game.  Even with the price tag, for this game, the fun is there.  The style and artwork is there.  The continued development seems to be there, but so are the bugs. TLDR:  This game is a lot of fun and has a great style to it.  But with this many bugs and a few areas that still need a little polish, it should really be in Early Access. That opinion is the only reason I am not giving the game an enthusiastic thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a great game oozing with potential. With the feedback being heard and tackled by the developers quickly, I have no worry that this game will meet its potential.Neon Abyss is a game that was made by developers that clearly enjoy the genre and shows very evident inspiration from The binding of Isaac. But the great aspects of other games is also clearly here. If you love the genre, I see no reason why you wouldnt love this. I feel it really scratches many itches often missed by other games.Ive seen a few other reviews talking about bugs, poor design or just bad mechanics and claiming that the game should be considered early access. While I cant say whether or not it should be EA still, because yes there are bugs and some annoyances with balance: The devs have acknowledged people feedback and have pushed fixes for most of these things into the experimental branch. A big, BIG issue I had was instantly shooting/attacking enemies when they spawn in right on top of you, enemy bullets being too hard to track, and general balance issues on items. Reading the latest patch notes shows that, enemy bullets now are above yours, enemies take a while to spawn in with a portal ALA enter the gungeon, and items are consistently being reworked. Perhaps then, it should be EA still. However, I wouldnt say to not play the game because of this. As most of the issues in these reviews have been worked on already.The only real cons aside from occasional bugginess (I have however only experienced one bad bug so far, and its been smooth otherwise) is that the whole "Infinite synergies" seems a little misleading. I love the genre but I hate when games dont have synergies. Its the best part of Isaac. This game has them, but, most items are actually quite generic. "Damage up / Range Up / Rate of fire Up / Velocity Up"... Its mostly Isaacs stat ups. There are a lot of items that do work together, but not many that make a run-defining gameplay change to you or your gun. But then, I havent unlocked the tech tree yet.Theres also a lack of a real dodge and... I just dont feel that. One character has a roll, and a certain gun lets you roll as an active ability, but, I think people would love a simple "Hold down to duck" or something.Your hitbox is wildly unfair to you. If you fly over a pit of spikes to pick that one coin up thats visually higher than the spikes, you cant get it without damage. Your feet either arent hitboxes, or, the coin doesnt visually match its own. Same with a coin up high on a ledge. If your head passes into it, you wont collect it either, so your head isnt a hitbox.But enemy bullets going over your head or under your feet will hit you. In fact, some bullets can hit you while visually missing you and that bothers me so much. A game like this should use precise hitboxes. This is why ducking would be welcome.As for the tech tree, its pretty neat. Unlike Isaac where upgrades and unlocks seem random, with mechanics just popping up after 20 hours. Here you have a tech tree to spend special currency from bosses on permanent unlocks as well as dungeon altering upgrades. I feel this really pushes the playability factor and the addiction factors. You WANT to play again to unlock a new kind of secret room, or explosive bullets. And YOU get to pick what to unlock and when. You also get unlocked items as a freebie for your next run, so crafty players can start with a god run on the cards.Other games like, immortal redneck, Gunfire Reborn, Skul and the like have upgrade trees, but they often are little stat changes like +5% HP, +3% damage.... thats fine, it helps, but it doenst keep me coming back. Unlocking new items like in gungeon, or even new kinds of rooms really sell the game for me.Speaking of rooms, lets talk design. Its a nice theme, quite reminds me of Black Future '88, very neon punk. Its pleasing, the music is great. But the variety does lack a little. Every floor looks almost the same and the room design does too. I hope the developers differentiate a little more going forwards, perhaps after the managers.Managers? Yes, take on your inner Karen because the big baddies are managers. So lets talk boss and enemies.Bosses are fine, their HP seems fair enough. I dont find myself tediously piddling away at a massive HP bar unlike a lot of games while at the same time, im fighting a long enough time for there to be challenge.BIG PLUS: The bosses scale the further you are in to the game when they show up. In Isaac, getting bloat on a floor 1 boss is a nightmare chore. Here, that bloat would be weaker and easier to fight on floor 1, but, fight him on floor 4 and he will have a new design, new attacks, more HP and so on. THANK you. Your starting gun is enough for these guys early on without taking gungeon's 20 minutes to kill.Some enemies are total BS but it looks like its getting fixed quickly. There are a lot of cases of walking into a room and instantly being shot from above by a squiddy boy, or the little red teleporting melee guys which always seem impossible to avoid. But the patch notes show they are working on smoothing these things out. (again, try the experimental branch if you want the changes now)Replayability factor is high enough to keep you wanting more. Every run I have had success in was quite definitive. From homing, splitting, piercing arrows. Bouncing lazer beams, and a gatling gun that shoots 5 bullets per shot that explode... I felt like a classic homing brimstone power level of god. The upgrade tree was reworked to be less grindy. Now, if you have a good run. Chances are, you are getting a new upgrade.The guns are, unfortunately, hit or miss. I find that, some are POWERFUL, some are weaksauce and dont seem to do much over your starter, not much in between. Personally, I would love to see some gungeon variety... or hey, go get inspired from ratchet and clank or something. There is potential here (Yet to see even a shotgun?)Some sounds could use more OOMPH too, lasers and rockets dont feel too satisfying.The wisdom/violence mechanics are great. Its like Angel/devil from Isaac, but more consistent. Spend crystals to enable wisdom, then spend more crystals or flawless rooms to fill a bar. Once full, unlock a room with a choice of one of two gifts of decent power.Or, Take damage in rooms and spend health on red crystals to up the violence meter. Unlock a room with the ability to give up a heart container for a powerful item.Red crystals are activated by shooting the purple ones, this counts doors and chests too, so there is a lot of consideration at work each run on how you want to move forwards.TLDR: Neon Abyss is fantastic. Well recommended. While it has bugs and flaws, you can opt for the experimental or wait for a main update to alleviate a lot of them. This game has potential, and the devs are active. Pick it up if you love Isaac or gungeon or just roguelikes in general. Its a lot of fun, and £15 is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: God, I've really tried with this one. And I'm gonna play a little bit more than I have currently. But already it's easy to tell I can't recommend this one. One of my absolute favourite parts of roguelikes is when all or nearly all of the damage feels avoidable. Through repetition you learn the enemy patterns, traps etc and the feedback loop of learning and overcoming is incredible. However this game just feels like a kid with ADHD wanted to see as many things on the screen as possible, regardless of whether that inhibits you from seeing the things that matter, like enemies and enemy bullets. So often damage upgrades come in the form of additional projectiles, and some guns have multiple projectiles, or projectiles that explode at the end of your projectiles, or bouncing projectiles etc... Paired with the dozens of eggs/pets you can amass often firing their own projectiles, this can VERY QUICKLY make for your screen being covered in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that looks like someone just dropped a match into a giant box of fireworks. While as a spectacle it can be cool, in a combat setting it can severely detract from the readability of a game. Another point of negativity I felt goes a little bit back into the review about how it feels like so many of the upgrades end up being just adding projectiles or direct damage to your weapons. It just gets repetitive and boring pretty fast. It has good bones, and plenty of people do and will like it. There's just so many other roguelikes out there that accomplish what this one tries, and in my opinion, fails to accomplish.
