_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far one of the most RNG dependent luck fests I have ever played, much to the game's detriment. It also has some odd mechanics, lacks item synergy, and punishes the player in weird ways. Where to begin?You have three consumable resources: grenades, keys, and coins. Coins will come naturally and generally aren't a problem. Grenades and keys, on the other hand, drop when they feel like it. For a game dependent on exploring and power up, this is a problem. You will go entire levels without getting either, thus not being able to enter some rooms/open some chests. It's frustrating. I tried to make sure there wasn't any confirmation bias here, but I can legitimately say over 10 hours of playing this game that sometimes the game will just decide not to let you in any rooms due to a lack of keys and grenades. On top of that, expending these resources occasionally leads to getting LESS of a return back. Opening a locked chest or blowing open a stone door just to find a couple coins is a uniquely aggravating experience.Speaking of money and doors... slot machine doors. Some doors you need to pay to enter. You pay 5 coins and the game plays a little slot machine. Each time you fail, you get more likely to succeed. No big deal, I guess... except for the fact that occasionally the door will take your money and explode, becoming inoperable and PERMANENTLY locking you out of the next room(s). Once again, this is totally RNG based (though often seemed to happen to me on the 3rd or 4th spin). On top of that, these rooms can suffer from the same problem as above, where the reward is worth less than you put into the slot.Of course, it's not just slot machine doors that can break. Any of the minigame consoles can break too! They take 15 coins to play and will occasionally just explode DEALING YOU DAMAGE and disabling the mini game. Why? What in the world is the point of this mechanic?On top of all of this, the game goes with a Binding of Isaac style "items do random things and you can't even begin to figure it out until you pick it up." Luckily, most of them are not detrimental or horribly playstyle changing (see below about synergy, or lack thereof, for why that also doesn't work).Finally, touching again upon area accessibility, levels will often spawn areas you can only get to by having flight or multi-jump. Haven't gotten lucky enough to get one of those? Too bad! You'll be missing those chests/items!Not much to the gameplay. You move, jump, shoot. Some characters have a unique ability. I actually recommend playing this game on keyboard and mouse. It lets you aim more accurately and just feels better, to me. You get items that generally buff your guns but sometimes give you something unique. Here is where my main issue with the mechanics and synergy crops up.There are a TON of items in the game that buff melee. To my knowledge, only three characters have a dedicated melee button and of those three, one is a DLC character. Now, don't get me wrong, every character CAN melee. When you get close to an enemy and press fire, sometimes a little knife flicks out instead of shooting. Sometimes. It seems to me to be very inconsistent. On top of that, melee in this game can be very dangerous, as you can imagine.There are also a lot of items that interact with jumping, as in when you jump a thing happens. These are always janky, short lived, and weak in my experience and are COMPLETELY negated if you get an item that allows you to fly so... good design there.Finally, the other awkward synergy is with grenades. For some reason, the devs seem to think you're going to use grenades in combat instead of saving them for doors and chests and as such a number of items make your grenades explode differently or do something related to them exploding. Why, again, is this a thing when on an average run you'll get maybe 10 to 20 grenades total (if lucky) and need to use those on doors and chests?While I'm discussing this topic, I want to say that the "game feel" is kind of off. Despite what the screenshots and vids show, the game feels kinda slow. Projectiles are slow, enemies are slow, you're slow. It lacks the kind of high octane movement and quick attacks and dodges that something like Hades, Risk of Rain, or Dead Cells thrives on and makes the game a bit of a slog. Not to mention that you frequently need to backtrack. It's honestly not even really a bullet-hell.Finally, the game is just kind of easy. The bosses are pushovers (with the exception, so far, of  who generally manages to get some good damage on me) and with a bit of RNG on your side you'll likely end up with a build that can just crush most rooms. This makes the game feel even worse, as when your RNG is bad, you know you're dying not because of your skill, or lack thereof, but instead because the game just... doesn't want you to win.The music is fine. Electronic EDM kinda stuff, I guess. Fits the theme. I'm not really hip and with it. It's mostly forgettable, however, and I wouldn't buy the soundtrack.The characters aren't balanced well at all. In my opinion Anna, one of the starting characters, is the best of the characters I've used and from what I've read she and one of the DLC characters are the best characters in the game (imagine that). One character has an ability that straight up has a chance to just blow him up and deal him damage. Great.The story is essentially non-existent, at least as far as I got. I like the idea of merging neon-punk with greco-roman stylings but I feel like they put in the BARE minimum effort. Plus, with Hades absolutely crushing its theme, throwing out a half-assed Greek theme feels kind of lame.Finally, while this may just bother me, I found a lot of the item names and descriptions to be completely divorced from the mechanics of the item. It feels like the devs wanted to reference a ton of things without caring about if it made sense. Like they had the item mechanics figured out and then decided to throw a dart at a dartboard of names. For example, the item "Big Daddy" is a diver's helmet and a clear reference to Bioshock. It makes you immune to explosion damage. What? Why doesn't it buff your melee (bouncer) or ranged (rosie) (or even your explosive damage like the ones that threw bombs in Bioshock 2)? Out of ALL the items in the game that buff your melee, why not the one referencing the game that prominently features ON THE BOX a big daddy with a gigantic drill? Not to mention that in every game explosives were the best way to deal with big daddies so immunity makes no sense. Then there is the "Garand Clip"... which has the art of a STANAG magazine (super nit-picky, I know lol).If you've read this far, bless. I really needed to rant about this game. I finally gave in after I unlocked the ability to fight . Turns out, you can only fight him by RNGing up a specific violence room and then making it to the end. Great. Fun. To progress I need to rely on RNG AND hurt myself AND reduce my max hearts. That's awesome. I presume there is an equivalent for wisdom rooms (which luckily don't hurt you) but holy crap that is tedious.There IS a fun game here. I played it for 10 hours before it finally crushed me into submission. If the devs just tweaked the RNG a little bit and made the progression feel natural and not tied to RNG, I would totally play this game again. (And hey, throw in a balancing pass and take a look at your weird anti-synergy too, why not.) As it is, I just can't be bothered to put more time into the game. Ya know what? Pick it up when it's on sale for like 5 bucks. I wouldn't pay more than that for it, but 5 bucks is fair.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wish I could give this a neutral review. But I can't so here's a cliche pros and cons list.Rogue-likes and lites alike have a huge influence from RNG, sometimes you're just going to have unlucky runs. But in Neon Abyss you frequently do not get enough grenades\keys to get into various rooms. This can cause a run to die simply because you get 5-6 levels in and just don't have the items to keep up. This also doesn't take into account that you can have a battle room that costs 2 keys or 2 grenades to get into and then it gives you a chest with 2 coins (a grenade or key from the shop costs 30 coins). This sort of bum room is expected and would be a good "crap" set back if keys and grenades weren't such a scarce resource. There are a number of items that just don't do much. This honestly may be the fault of the devs for not having an indepth item list in existence yet (one with stats so we can see how much more damage an items gives for example). But due to the overwhelming number of items (294 not including weapons, note the original binding of isaac had less than 200 items) I think there really ought to be less items that only work in a combo or are simply the same items but slightly different (ie an item that reveals all secrets, another reveals all room types, and another reveals the whole map layout).On the subject of overwhelming large amount of items, you don't get them often enough or enough choices in order to actually make a "build" and you're stuck relying on the RNG Gods to grant you items that go together. Just for example, there are item upgrades that require you to get 4 of the same theme of item and you'll get an extra per, like being immune to explosions, in my 8.8 hours of playing (at the time of writing this) I have never been able to get more than 1 of a single type of item collected, let alone all 4 of them. Not to mention some of these items pose a mild threat to you until you get all 4 of them. If Neon Abyss is going to have this large of a collection of items there needs to be a better way to obtain more/different items, ie. every item room has two choices and you get one. Or Wisdom rooms letting you take both items if you want. That being said, if the item collection itself was improved the game could be made hard and should be made harder. Honestly you can be bad and roguelikes and just bash your head into the wall for 3 or 4 runs before just getting a godlike combo out of pure luck and killing everything in any room almost immediately. That's not to say that absolutely destroying enemies isn't fun, but it certainly feels empty when you can't particularly control your build. I would equate it to playing Slay the Spire but the deck is pre-built and random every time you play. All that said, I'm gonna keep playing. Neon Abyss is fun, it just makes me wanna bang my head against my desk and play Binding of Isaac instead every few runs, and honestly I think when I start getting runs like that, I'm just going to be quitting because I know this game doesn't lend itself to being able to dig yourself out of a dead run.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all i got every single item and achievement like most of roguelikes i play...the game was pretty fun at first, decent difficulty, fun mechanics, cool graphics, but there are way too many 'details' that made me dislike this game more and more, for example:-XBOX prompts on dance/fishing minigames while using PS controller -W button is hard coded-can't shoot straight up with the weapon "Song of Joy" and "Passenger"-turning the Wisdom gauge to Violence gauge goes 1:1, but the other way around 2:1, Why?-Enemies and pets' attacks turns crystal devices to spike devices, i can tolerate why that happens with pets, since they're your allies, but why enemies?-Only 'attacking' a crystal device turns your wisdom gauge to violence, why not when you actually get hurt by it?-Goblin Unlocker Skill (from Meteor Weapon) explosion damages you even with Big Daddy-Ming's characteristics says that you can cancel the egg hatching with circle when you really cancel it with X (with PS Controller)-Items stacking on top of each other makes them wacky to get, if you walk straight forward to the stack and you want the lower one, you can get it unless you jump or move the items somehow-Items goes out of bounds way too often, even if you can't see them in the room, the map shows it, and its frustrating to go to the room just to realize that the item was unreachable-Doesn't show any stats besides health/shield and weapon level-The 'Lore' of the game is pretty much unnecesary/useless. _childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss ReviewGAMEPLAY-	GeneralThe game plays very smoothly and it doesn’t take long before you get the feel for the flow of the game. As you play through the game you unlock new characters, ways to obtain items and rooms. This helps break up the game, which would otherwise be quite monotonous. The diversity of the weapons helps create a run that is unique every time. The items on the other hand are a major complaint from me. Whilst there are plenty of items in the game, very few of them actually drastically change the way you play. Some just level your weapon, others slightly increase your movement speed and others still just add a heart. Compared to other games in the genre this is where Neon Abyss is quite lacking. Also, a minor nitpick, the game felt a little short to me. It wasn’t a glaring issue, but once I was finished all I could think was ‘oh, that’s it’.-	Enemies and bossesThe regular enemies are not that great. Designwise they are relatively bland and they don’t feel fitting within the neon-drenched hallways of the abyss. On top of that, their A.I. isn’t that great either, which makes fighting against them quite boring. Once you get a few levels on your weapons, you’ll most likely not even be looking for their attack patterns, as you’ll just melt through them in a second anyways.The bosses are the best part of the game for me. Their designs are amazing. Most bosses feel like they belong in the world and have attacks that match their visual design. The first four floors the bosses are randomized, meaning you won’t know which one you’ll be up against until you’re standing in the boss room. After that you get set bosses unfortunately. These bosses are well designed, but once you learn their patterns you’ll be doing the same in every single run.SOUND AND GRAPHICS-	The sound designUpbeat dance tracks follow you throughout the experience. None of them stood out to me, but I remember enjoying the tracks whilst I was playing, so can’t really complain.-	GraphicsIt’s quite simple, but the neon pixel aesthetic fits very well within this game. Even with loads of effects on the screen you can still see where you are going just fine (and my framerate wasn’t impacted at all, surprisingly)MISC-	Never played a game that ran this smoothly despite all the things happening on the screen.-	Did not experience a single bug or glitch during the hours that I played.CLOSING STATEMENTNeon Abyss is a good introduction to the genre for anyone wanting to get into these types of games, but feeling like they’d be overwhelmed by the sheer amount of customization. If you are looking for a very deep procedural roguelike, you may want to skip this, unless the aesthetic particularly grabs you. All in all, not a bad game

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This used to be a positive review, but at the end of the day and after all this time in EA, this game just isn't good. The items are bad, the enemies are bad, the guns are bad - there's a huge lack of design foresight, it's like no one ever asked themselves how these pieces should all fit together when the game was done.There are essentially 5 or 6 different 'synergy' types for items (e.g. items that enhance pets, or items that enhance grenades, or items that enhance jumping) but there's no way to focus on any of them, so you always end up with a lot of half-functional synergies and broken builds. Guns are both rare and not exciting or interesting, they lean heavily into "why would I use this over my starting pistol?" gimmicks. The vast majority of items in the game are simple stat buffs - gain a heart container, your gun does more damage, gain a crystal container. The items that try to do more are still very boring - when a pet dies, you have a chance to get a grenade. When using a grenade, you have a chance to get a pet.The enemies are either offensively threatless or just annoying to fight because of limited windows where you can attack them. Many of them have attack patterns that open them up to literally just standing in their face blasting.Boss fights are a few seconds long and just feel like larger regular enemies despite being intended to be more - they have very simple attack patterns that are heavily telegraphed every time and mindless to ignore. Most bosses have platforms in their room that you can stand on or jump between where their attacks literally cannot hit.You have to commit scarce resources like bombs, keys and even hearts to open chests or unlock side-rooms, but the majority of these chests/rooms have either no reward, reward you with exactly what you spent to unlock them, or reward a single coin (or something less valuable than what you spent to unlock them).Over the last week I tried to play this game 4 separate times, and I wasn't able to make it past the third stage without alt-F4ing in disgust at how poorly all of these moving parts fit together(I beat the game multiple times back when it first launched in EA, so it's not like I'm missing out on fun content that comes in later stages - I know it doesn't get any better than this)

_childDocuments_.review: Eh. It's just...kind of okay.It's very pretty and the controls are mostly crisp. There's little overtly wrong at first glance, but once you scratch the surface there isn't a whole lot there. This is clearly a game that wants to be Enter the Gungeon, but it's nowhere near as good.* The balance is really poor - the items and pets are mostly meaningless. Just get one of a handful of overpowered guns and stack badges, instant win. Given the choice between an item and a badge, you always choose the badge, and I've yet to encounter a non-gun/badge item that "made the run". There's no real sense of progression between "sucky starting gun" and "steamrolling everything with a good gun". There's a whole melee system that is mostly rendered meaningless by the ranged options being vastly superior and the lack of any real damage avoidance mechanic beyond "stay away from things". Most of the time, when you spend a resource (bomb/key), you get one back, plus some extra items. There aren't really any decisions to be made other than "collect everything".* There's basically nothing in the way of a narrative, and the problems in translations end up being pretty jarring. Not that these sorts of games need too much narrative, but even a little bit helps. It *seems* like there should be some narrative, but you're just dumped into it without even so much of an explanation of who you are or why you're there.* Systems aren't explained particularly well - the "pets", for example, are just collected and upgraded over time without any real obvious mechanic, but you don't make any decisions or have any input in what pets you get or how they upgrade. They can apparently die, but you don't have any means to heal them, keep them out of danger, or otherwise manage them. They end up being more of a visual distraction than anything else. You can't carry more than one weapon at a time, but all your upgrades carry over to whatever you're carrying, so you just pick a good one and roll with it. At one point, you're asked to collect "abyss gems", but at no point is it explained what they are or how you get them. Completing even full runs doesn't appear to give you any. There's no accounting of how many you have or how you get them.* Characters don't feel particularly well-differentiated (I ended up just playing on "random" after a couple of runs for the extra starting item). There's not really anything unique about any of the bosses.* The game mostly feels like a wrapper around a "grind for gems to complete your upgrade tree", except you'll be clearing the entire run quickly without needing any upgrades to do so, so there's very little compelling reason to grind it out. Most persistent upgrade mechanisms reward your improved finesse at the game with a more and more powerful loadout - in Neon Abyss, it mostly just feels like it's there to give you checkboxes to grind for.It's not a bad game, but it's nowhere as good as it could be, and if you're expecting something on par with Enter the Gungeon or Dead Cells, you're going to be sorely disappointed. It's worth a few bucks on sale but you're not gonna get the hundreds of hours out of it that you will out of its competitors.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic roguelike that will keep you coming back. Neon Abyss is filled with colorful and great looking scenery, characters, items, and weapons. A lot to unlock so you'll be spending time trying to get everything if you enjoy that.The bosses at the end of each level are the New Gods. There are sub bosses and then there are the managers. So your first run will go through four sub bosses and then you'll do a fifth level and fight a manager. Once you beat the first manager the run will end and you will rinse and repeat but then get to go further and fight the next manager and so on. After the third manager then you have a challenge to complete which gives you a key to fight the next manager.  When the game first launched there were only 5 managers but with updates they added three more and the now final one is a challenge.When you beat and of the gods you will get tokens to unlock new characters, items, perks, and changes to your runs. Like new challenge rooms or barrels to break that can give you hearts, shields, or money. There are now a total of about 425 items to unlock. There are also cheat codes you can unlock and lore cards now that you buy with a small token you can randomly find. When you turn on the cheats though the achievements will lock.Another cool thing in the game are eggs. You find eggs in the levels that will float behind you and possibly hatch into little pets. Sometimes the hatching does fail. Pets can also level up the longer they stay alive. They all have different perks like one that picks up hearts and turns them into shields, or the one that looks like trump and picks up money. When the pets that pick up items die they will drop a bunch of the item they collected.The devs have been putting out some great content updates that have added some cool features to the game and make it even better. They also just recently release a character pack for $2. I highly recommend it because the character Saya in it is pretty dope IMO. The game is definitely worth the full price as I have sunk almost 50 hours into myself. If you like action games or roguelikes I highly recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun...when it's working right. A bullet hell rouge-like in the vein of Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Isaac, etc. 2D style, fun/unique loot, and fun bosses. The problem is that is game also has its share of bugs: sometime you can't spend the currency to unlock new upgrades because the game just won't let you do it. Most annoyingly, sometimes the game just starts to slowly break down as you play it.I was on a run, completed the first floor. When I got to the second, the music stopped. I thought "Whatever," and kept going. The third floor, sounds effects were gone. The fourth, the game would lag every time you or your pets picked up an item; ANY item (coins, loot, hearts, etc). The fifth floor, the game lagged every time a bullet was shot by you or the enemy and every time you entered or exited a room. As you could assume, I quit out at that point. It doesn't happen too often, but it is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ when you're on a good run. I digress, the game is great so long as you have patience. Hopefully the devs will iron out the kinks. If they do, this will be a formidable game of its genre. If they don't, it's a novelty at best.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not that bad, but when there are alternatives like death must die or enter the gungeon, why would you play this?It feels (and plays) like a cheap, mediocre copy of enter the gungeon with some new elements.Diffuculty is pretty low. Whenever you are picking up items or guns, you always gamble. Why? Because they don't tell you about anything. You only find out about the details of an item AFTER you pick it up, which is just annoying. This is probably the biggest diffuculty of the game.Gameplay is easy and simple, bosses are easy to beat, mobs are pretty much all the same stuff with different flavors.Guns are mostly the same. Couldn't see any fun variety. Some guns have "active" abilities. But all the active abilites I saw were just economy abilities. I would expect an active gun ability to, you know, help me in battle. Do something interesting. Maybe shoot a bigger bullet. Maybe shoot something else. Among the abilities, 2 of them gave you money in exchange with your energy, 1 of them gave you random pickable (like hp and shield) for energy, one of them gave you an egg, for money and energy. None of them were interesting, fun or added anything to the gameplay. When I upgraded my weapon for the first time, I thought something interesting would happen. No again. It just increases your bullet numbers. I used to shoot 2 bullets, now I shoot 3... Yey, so fun. There are already pickable upgrades that increase your bullet volume, so why even bother with this? There is so much platforming, but it is done sooo poorly that it stops being challenging and starts being just annoying. There are lots of empty rooms with just teleportation crystals for some reason? Probably around 10-20% of my gametime was spent on pointless, boring things. Jumping up and down, backtracking etc...It's  a 6/10.You could play it. You could enjoy it. But why?? There are so many better alternatives, why would you spend your time with this instead?Also, if you check out the dlc's, they just look like things they should have added to the main game. Kind of scummy imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Art can really fool people into thinking a game is good. I was really hyped about this game only to be dissapointed. The game at best is average. There is very little enemy variation between the levels and even after beating the first main boss the enemies remain consistent. Bland boring level design with many grey walls to see, some different colors, but all still radically the same design. Throwing the grenade is a pain, I don't know why you can't just aim it. Guns in this game sound crisp and satisfying to defeat enemies which is good, so the sound effects are great. However, ironically the level music for this game is really dry and boring, sounds like I am in a elevator at a club or something. Bosses in this game is one of strongest attributes of this game, and are slightly above average and I had some fun with them, but because this is a rogue-like game you'll maybe tire of them. Pets in this game are okay, it drives a skinner box satisfaction when they hatch which increases addiction in some people. Many of the items that you think are new after defeating a boss is just a reskinned heart container which is not fooling me. To end this review, guns and bosses are the best parts of this game. Overall I give this game a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game because it is beautiful but many questionable design decisions such as:- Game gives you eggs, which hatch after a certain number of cleared rooms and contain a familiar that helps in combat. You get these almost constantly and really they're just extra. There are epic chests however that also contain eggs. Why? I have to use a key to open it and all I get is a egg? I already have like 10 of them- There are chests littered all over the map but you will likely only open like 20% of them because you dont get enough keys in a level. Why put all these chests if I can't get them?? There was one room that had 3 chests, then a locked door, then another 3 chests, another door, and then some epic chests. It cost like 4 keys to just reach the end and I didnt have enough keys to unlock everything, and when I opened one of the chests all it had was half a heart.... why...? There are also chests hidden behind a roulette. Yes, a literal slots machine. You pay some coins and eventually you may get access to these awesome chests that contain more eggs and hearts. So useless.- I really noticed there were useless decisions when I saw there is a robot character, RX-9, who starts with 4 shield instead of heart and has a key and grenade. The starter character has a key and grenade and 3 hearts. RX-9 cannot pick up hearts. Why the hell would I ever use RX-9? What is the point of picking a character that is worse than the starter? Is having 1 extra shield really worth not being able to pick up hearts?- The shop costs crystals, which you need for opening epic chests and also using your active ability. Then you need to spend gold to buy things in the shop. Why?? You can also shoot the door to the shop to make it take half a heart instead. Why am I paying to enter a shop??? "The items are OP of course", right? Wrong. The items in the shop are almost always useless, like keys. Lmao why would waste scarce coins on a key that will likely only get me a half heart chest when I can just wait for a heart room or a common chest to drop a half heart? The guns are also pointless because upgrades carry across weapons so theres no reason to buy a new gun.This is just what I remember but honestly so many pointless and unfun decisions keep me from enjoying this

_childDocuments_.review: It looks great. I love the pixel neon aesthetic and the game itself feels great, but it's WAY to repetitive and grindy. After a while, it just gets boring to kill the exact same bosses over and over to get the crystal thingies you need to unlock stuff. Also, the levels are too samey. You can basically have a black background and all levels would be exactly the same. In my opinion, it simply does not have a fun gameplay loop in the long run and unique synergies you would find in for example Binding of Isaac. And sometimes there's so much clutter on the screen and bullets everywhere that it's almost impossible to see wtf is going on, and this is especially annoying in challenge rooms where you don't want to be hit! It's not a bad game per se, but since I can't rate it neutral or mixed on Steam, it will be a thumbs down for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to preface this by saying that the game is still subject to a lot of changes, and I personally haven't finished all the content, but there are many core mechanics I find extremely frustrating and that kind of ruin the entire game for me.1 - Pets:"but they're making the bad ones optional!!" so what? pets are garbage the way they are right now. You get WAY too many, they clutter up the screen and are annoying af no matter what.2 - Not being able to drop items:Sometimes some items will ruin your entire composition and there's nothing you can do to prevent it other than remembering every single item or googling them so you can be sure that they won't have a ridiculously dumb effect.3 - The purple / red bar thing:Purple bars are ridiculously easy to fill up and have basically no downside since you're completely showered with crystals all the time, but they have the ANNOYANCE that you can ruin it so easy and lock yourself out of entire rooms if you shoot a bullet in the wrong place. What the ♥♥♥♥? why? Red bars need you to sacrifice a ton of health to fill up the bar (but at least you're kind of guaranteed not to get frustrated over ruining it since once objects turn red they won't turn back) and then they need you to sacrifice an entire heart slot so you can get basically the same thing as purple but with one more option....pretty insignificant considering how much more difficult to get they are.4 - Grenades: Grenades are partially the problem, and another part is how many chests and bits of content are locked out by stones. It's seriously annoying how sometimes 70% of the chests can be locked out by rocks and there's nothing you can do about it since these grenades are rare for some reason, so you end up unable to destroy these rocks, and completely locked out with nothing to do about it.And in the other hand, if you get some form of explosive item, grenades are completely useless trash that you're going to stockpile and never use since they're made extremely annoying and frustrating to use in the first place with purposefully scuffed unidimensional aiming mechanics. There's no way to aim them other than look to the left or right and jump and time it with your current height (why?????)This, combined with other miscellaneous aspects of the game that are equally frustrating (like for example the extremely difficult and punishing piano event) make up for an overall pretty ♥♥♥♥ experience.All of that being said, the game is well made when it comes to fluidity, gameplay and visuals. It feels good to play the game itself, but the game design is very lackluster in the things I mentioned before. The experimental branch makes me realise that the devs are aware of the current state of the game, and are working towards fixes. But the game remains to be frustrating and many of the core concepts are honestly stupid and will probably never go away 100% or get reworked which is a pity. TLDR: Don't buy, at least as of yet. Core concepts need to be redesigned to be less frustrating and stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss has been an utter disappointment. It contains some items of merit (companions, fun minigames, interesting club/greek theme, fun unlocks), but these are all greatly outweighed by its flaws.The game is riddled with bugs, so much so that it feels like an early access game yet in reality it is already on update 1.25.Most of the bugs are just annoying, but you will experience at least a couple during each run. So far I have only come across one game breaking bug.The game starts off with a promising theme and some really pretty visuals. However, the visuals and enemies quickly become repetitive. Most of the enemies are very generic and don't fit with the theme at all. The visuals also are quite bland after the initial stage. I wish they embraced it more because the game could look a lot better!The difficulty is quite easy, and even on hard doesn't really challenge. Also, beating the game doesn't provide you with any sort of reward. It's just endless grind for achievements and unlocks. Also, most upgrades during a run don't do anything interesting. Upgrades mostly just increase weapon speed, increase jump height, increase movement speed, etc. More upgrades is always better until you are ridiculously OP. The game just lavishes you with item drops.Also, the strategy is always the same: stand in a corner, blast your enemies, jump over an attack every once in a while. There is even a boss where you can just stand there while it throws free money at you, and you are never in danger of getting hit. Yikes!I bought this game because a reviewer had compared it favorably, likening it to Enter The Gungeon. Besides a couple of artificial similarities, I find that the two games are not comparable as they are just totally different. I am shocked that any professional reviewer would ever recommend this game.If you are looking for a game that itches your action roguelite itch, maybe try Rogue Legacy? Or Gungeon if you want a bullet hell type game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game. The style is great. Tons of replayability. Lots of weapons and characters and things to unlock. It's really the kind of game I enjoy, yet I'm finding myself enjoying less than half the runs I'm on. That's concerning.It's unfair, a lot. Moreso than the usual roguelite. Compare it to games like Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Issac, Rogue Legacy, those games really leave it up to you to make mistakes. Neon Abyss will just slap you out of nowhere or stack mechanics on mechanics to force you to take hits. I've got the 100% achievement in TBOI, playing hard games isn't a big deal. Playing unfair games on the other hand just feels worse when you know you're getting better and don't have a choice but to lose because the game puts you in impossible situations.Currently at 12 hours with most of the mainline unlocks, and beat most of the standard bosses, but those wins came from being lucky, not good. You will eventually get some overpowered combinations of items that will carry you through the bosses. This game will also shut down a run whether you like it or not. There's only so much skill and practice can overcome. Here's a couple examples.Enemies will teleport on top of you with a pretty minor telegraph that appears behind you, and they'll spawn in on the other side of a room that you can't see when you initially enter. If you have any amount of busy bullet effects, it's almost impossible to see before taking a hit.Enemies will inconsistently fire through walls, and again, will fire at you off-screen before you know they exist. There's a little more time to react, but not much, and when you're not expecting it while dealing with the first half of the room, getting hit is not unusual.Large rooms will occasionally will have enemies that pop up on the wall, fire, and then burrow back into the wall again. Frequently you will not be able to track them down and fire back within range before they dig away again. Combine this with any room that has a laser trap to take damage either while dodging the laser and getting popped up on, or trying to chase down the enemy and catching a laser from bad positioning.Almost every boss will ignore damage and still be allowed to throw attacks at you. It's annoying and unfair design because ~nuuuu you're not allowed to beat my cool boss without seeing all his attacks nuuuu~ reasoning I assume. If players get lucky and end up with a good combination of weapons and items, just let them roll over the boss. Making your boss cheese through fights without taking damage is unfair.Looting the boss leaves you trying to catch a quickly flickering upgrade with no rhyme or reason what it will end up on. It rotates between a health container, attack speed upgrade, and damage upgrade. Naturally if you're already good on health you want the damage or attack speed (which both cap so you might want one specifically) but the random roll means 66% of the time you're not getting what you thought you selected. Also, why is it in the background when the room is clear? Put the items in the foreground if the room is clear. There's no reason I have to try and manuevuer my conga line of followers around to try and see what's going on aside from being annoying making the player feel like they messed up trying to select the buff they actually want.The egg system... You pickup eggs and followers hatch, sometimes. Or you get a nothing. The followers are entirely random, and about 60% of them are useful. 10% are useless, and 30% are actively trying to screw you by stealing money, health, turning health into risky health, dropping bombs on environmental explosives, etc. Keep the hatch/fail mechanic, but make them an optional pickup with the name of the follower so the player can elect to pass if the mechanic doesn't fit the current run.To be fair to Neon Abyss, they've made some changes since early access. You can technically blacklist the items, weapons, enemies, and followers if they annoy you in particular, which I've tried my best to cut out the most egregious offenders. However it's pretty strictly limited to a very small proportion of the overall sheer amount to pick from it's really an illusion of choice to try and mitigate the annoyances. This, in and of itself, is an annoyance. Giving just enough to call it a feature while still inevitably being unable to effectively make the game fair to play.Anyway, I want to like the game more than I do. I wouldn't recommend it to most people, only if you're really into having a game beat you rather than beating the game. I'll probably keep playing it anyway.

name: World of Warplanes
detailed_description: World of Warplanes is an aerial combat MMO action game set in the Golden Age of military aviation. Throwing players into a never-ending battle for dominance of the skies, the game allows aircraft enthusiasts to pursue full-scale careers as virtual pilots, earning their wings in intense 12-vs-12 battles where supremacy in the air depends on not only a fast trigger finger, but also coordinated teamwork. Five Aircraft types Learn air combat skills with five different aircraft types, each of which is unique in its configuration, role, and behavior in battle. Aircraft of different nations Choose any aircraft you like from seven different nations—U.S.S.R., Germany, U.S.A., U.K., France, China, or Japan—and enter a battle. Aircraft configurations Upgrade your aircraft with various weapons, engines, equipment, and consumables. Maps and layouts In World of Warplanes, battles unfold at picturesque in-game locations. Although most of them are original, the maps are based on real landscape types that can be found in different corners of the planet.

_childDocuments_.review: While the core mechanics aren't terrible, WarGaming has a bad reputation as a developer for a reason. They're highly focused on forcing you to follow their exact method of gameplay, and will punish you for deviating in the slightest. Pros:   -- The matches are pretty quick, so if you only have a few minutes here and there, you can still participate fully in most of the game. Good for people with real world schedules and casual gamers.   -- Not as grindy as other WG products. You get rewards fairly frequently. Weekly chests and reasonably frequent events mean that you can get Premium status, gold, premium planes, and other rewards without having to sell your soul to the game.   -- The background scenery looks pretty good and does a good job of immersing you in the gameplay.   -- The hangar interface isn't as complicated as other WG products. It's relatively simple to see event mission requirements and track your progress on daily missions.   -- Tokens can be earned without paying for them, and can be used to expand your hangar, allowing you to eventually unlock as many hangar slots as you want without paying a small fortune to WG.Cons:   -- Small player base. There aren't a lot of people in this game, which leads to the incredibly annoying scenario of being stuck with some of the worst bots in gaming history as teammates.   -- Matchmaking. This is a WarGaming product, so by definition, the matchmaking is horrendous. You'll constantly be stuck with opponents who are either incredibly good or incredibly bad. I would estimate no more than 20% of matches could be described as close matches with reasonably equal skill levels and equipment (i.e. planes, pilots, mounted items, etc.). You either win big, or lose big.   -- Forced win rates. WarGaming has a policy of keeping as many of their players at approximately a 50% win rate as they can. They accomplish this largely by tweaking the matchmaking system to stack the game either for or against you. If you are losing too much, they'll give you better bots and human teammates with better win records. If you're winning too much, you get worse bots and human teammates that couldn't pour water out of a boot with instructions on the heel.   -- Scoring. Bizarrely enough, attacking and killing planes will only help you win if you are doing so over a capture zone. While a reasonable argument could be made for giving a bonus to killing an opponent over a cap zone, it makes absolutely no sense to give no reward whatsoever for defeating an opponent outside of the designated areas. You win by scoring points, and points are only generated by cap zones, so each game is basically a glorified king of the hill match.    -- The bots. The AI is incredibly clunky. For example, the bots in the games will always, always spread out. Despite the obvious fact that focusing on just one or two zones (especially at the beginning of a match) is much more useful, the bots will spread out no matter how many times you give them commands to go to specific zones. This is largely accomplished by the fact that you are only able to give commands to a very, very limited selection of bots, and the bot is chosen almost at random, with no thought given to which would actually be the most helpful.   -- Slow release of new planes. I haven't seen a single new plane be added to the game since I started playing. WarGaming, while they haven't quite abandoned this title, are clearly not interested in making any progress in it.   -- Ground attack gameplay. If you are playing a bomber or a ground attack plane, you actually don't want your team to do too well in the match. If your team manages to capture all or most of the zones, you have almost nothing that you can do. GA's and bombers are technically capable of shooting down other planes, but it's risky and tends not to go well. Actively incentivizing you to want to have a mediocre team if you are in 40% of the plane types is just absurd.--Unstable platform. The game will occasionally crash for no discernible reason and you will be unable to get back in. Your only recourse is to log out of the game, wait for the match to end, and then try to log back in.Final Conclusion/TLDR:The game has some good points, and isn't terrible if you're a casual gamer who likes planes and is not concerned with winning a lot. But WG's policies and lack of attention to this game definitely make it only F2P worthy. Don't spend any money on this unless they seriously overhaul a lot of the cons.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, yes, the one game in Wargaming's roster that seems to be treated like an unwanted stepchild. All I constantly see is everyone complaining and whining over small little details, so as someone who can see this from an objective perspective, allow me to show you why this game has a lot hidden under its surface.PROS:One of the first things that caught my attention when I first got into this game was the controls. I recall a period in time when the controls were horrendously complicated or sometimes unresponsive; however, that time has now passed. I am greatly impressed by how simple things have become, regardless of what role you play. Whether it's looking down the sight lines of your bomb sights, or zooming around holding W to get your plane to go faster, the ability to use your plane is so simple it lets you actually focus on the other dynamics this game has to offer.Speaking of roles, the five roles to choose from (Fighter, Heavy Fighter, Bomber, Close Air Support, and Multirole) do seem simple; however, there is such a wide array to choose from depending on which nation you choose, and each one offers a different dynamic. I personally found that the United States and Germany had the widest array of aircraft, and it was something that made me fall in love with the game coming from someone who's used to playing bombers in War Thunder. It's an experience that I've also shared with friends, which is amazing.CONS:When I first load up most games, I tend to open up Task Manager on my second monitor to watch its performance throughout the game's duration. When in battle, I have tended to notice that the game has a minor RAM bleed, but this seems to go away once you return to your hangar; however, this RAM bleed is similar to that of the size of Discord's similar faults, so it's not something that is dangerous in the short-term. You will, however, see some performance loss if you're not playing on a good rig.Aside from this, the only other con I see is that there's not a lot of players playing the game from what I remember when the big update happened a few years ago. Naturally, most games on the lower tiers are riddled with bots, and these bots have relatively predictable, albeit dynamic flight patterns, so if you're playing an interceptor craft, it won't take long to take down smaller fighters.All in all, I'll rate this game 7/10. I believe aside from needing performance tweaks, adding more planes available to all nations (looking at the UK, France, and Italy in particular), and finding a way to populate the game a bit more (even if it's just a better bot AI), I believe this game is currently in its best state and I look forward to when Wargaming is able to devote more resources into improving a game I've enjoyed for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my personal opinion and review for world of Warplanes! (or Wowp for short) Let's begin!The good stuff: 1. Fun gameplay!2. Beautiful map design!3. Killing enemies is pretty satisfying!4. Nice level of customization!5. Upgrades often change the look of your plane which is really cool!6. Multi-role fighters are very fun to play and are pretty much the most OP class in the game due to their versatility! (though it's arguable because i heard people saying that heavy fighters are the best so idk)7. Some paint jobs look pretty cool!8. Wide selection of aircraft to choose from!9. Hangar is very detailed!10. Opening cinematic looks incredible!11. The music is quite nice! 12. Controls are easy to learn!13. Matches are quite fast!14. It's easy to become king of the match even with the starting planes making it less stressful to play as them!-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The bad stuff: (Which actually comprises most of this review)1. Horrible unfair matchmaking! (you will often be thrown in with the crappiest AI ever)2. You will mostly lose regardless of how good or powerful you are!3. Enemy AI is incredibly annoying as they will take advantage when you leave an important capture point behind!4. For some reason wargaming thought it was a good idea to let them decide who wins instead of the players!5. Once the game decides who wins it will rig the AI in the team that is selected to win giving them unbelievable levels of firepower and agility! 6. Enemy AI is WAY too aggressive!8. Matches are incredibly unbalanced! For example, while your team is out there crashing into mountains and paying no attention to capturing sectors, the enemy AI team will be out there obliterating your teammates and capturing sectors like savages.9. Playing as a bomber is incredibly stressful as you will always have packs of fighters on your tail relentlessly shooting at you trying to take you out of the skies! 10. Game actually can change its mind on who wins in the middle of a game! For example, you could be winning a match thinking you'll finally have a sweet victory after all those years of losing matches, but then all of a sudden the enemy team just "climbs out of the gutter" and starts obliterating you and your teammates.11. You will often be killed by the same person twice or more in a match!12. Out of all of wargaming's creations this one has the slowest progression system in my opinion! 13. Why does almost everything require gold if it's not even the main currency!?14. The premium shop is incredibly expensive for what it's selling! (most items will cost over 50 dollars despite having about the importance of a few dust grains)15. There is almost no way to collect a nice amount of gold without purchasing it in the premium shop!16. Don't even bother with the in game events unless there are not just more premium deals in disguise!17. The missions for the "free" aircraft are way too difficult and they require tokens to complete which makes it even worse!(unless of course your somehow loaded with tokens)18. Wargaming almost never properly updates their game unless it's to introduce more ripoff deals or make a few bug fixes!19. For a game powered by a company called "Bigworld technology" the maps are quite small for a combat flight simulator!20. Maps can look quite lazily designed at times! (for example trees are just flat digital cutouts and while the landscape can look pretty good at a distance when you get close to it you can see that it's all just flat textures and effects)21. I also noticed while playing a match there were all these low budget fake airplane shadows! (idk why they added this)22. There are not enough countries to play on for it to be realistic!23. The game has WAY too many limitations during matches for it to be realistic at all! (For example you can't go too far off the map, you can't go too fast, you can't go too slow, you can't go too high, you can't go too low, etc)24. Some of the nose art is very provocative!25. Chat system is really confusing!26. There is no tutorial at all!-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The Overall review:While this game is quite decent, it's good sides are absolutely avalanched by it's bad sides.The AI is trash, the graphics are good in some places, bad in others, and the overall game feels like it's in early access because of how hollow it is. I hope Wargaming will read this review and learn from their mistakes and find where to improve upon this game because this game has a LOT of potential. To reach that potential, wargaming will have to put in a lot more work then they currently are with this game. _childDocuments_.review: Built on the same principles and engine as World of Tanks, this game fails to impress in any positive way. The game engine is called “Bigworld”, probably ironically, as the maps are way too small for a game with airplanes. Map variety is almost as limited as the map size. The hit points system is very uninspired because part of the beauty of dogfights is to feel how you take apart the enemy airplanes, and to see and feel how the damage affects the planes, but this experience is very limited in this game. The physics are very restrictive as in, you can't go too fast, you can't go too far, you can't go too high, and you can't do too much damage too fast.UPDATE 2020-Oct: The game is a still a huge money grab and most “players” are bots. _childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, is World of Warplanes a fun game? Of course it is. Compared to War Thunder, it is much more arcade-like in its flight model and is more straight forward so you can just jump in and play without the hassle of learning various air combat sciences and procedures such as climbing to altitude for a few minutes. However, that right there is EXACTLY THE POINT. It's designed for anyone to play and just shoot stuff up in their favorite warbird. War Thunder is for those who want their air combat to be replicated more to real life and WoWP is for those who just want to shoot up stuff and make things go boom in your favorite plane.PROS:-Very easy to learn but of course, hard to master. You can jump right in and have a blast, but learning the game and understanding air combat can give you an edge, there's a casual and competitive side to this.-A great arsenal of aircraft to unlock and upgrade, and each of them fulfill a certain role that can apply to your playstyle, Bombing from high altitude? You can do that. Turning and Burning dogfighting? Of course you can.-Great aircraft customization, you can make your bird really stand out, and the game utilizes a 'Specialist" configuration of your plane that you can unlock after fully upgrading the plane. Once you unlock the 'Specialist" configuration, you can mount further upgrades to the plane to get the most out of it. Of course, there are plenty of paint schemes, nose art, and emblems to decorate your warbird with.-One game mode, Conquest, but it's quite good. Sure, you can argue that only one game mode is bad, but it's quite fun to play. Your team captures various strategic points that give your team advantages such as spawn points, bombing runs, rocket attacks on enemy objectives, etc. To capture a point, everyone does their part, fighters engage defense aircraft to clear the skies for attackers to hit the ground targets. Maps also have various configurations that will have different objectives to capture so you'll have to play it differently from the previous configuration.-Not as grindy as World of Tanks or War Thunder, In two days id you dedicate the time you can have yourself a Tier 5 aircraft which is usually along the lines of the P-40, Bf-109, FW-190, Spitfire, etc. Not to mention that in battle, each class of aircraft has their own objectives to complete and as a result, gives you more EXP and credits. For example, fighters have objectives based around engaging enemy aircraft and defending/attacking objectives, completing these milestones will give you affinity ribbons that increase in value as you complete your objectives more often, thus resulting in more EXP and credits.-Various combat missions for you to complete, and be rewarded for doing so.CONS:Low playerbase, and most players you will run into are veterans with Specialist configured planes that fancy seal clubbing noobs, just steer clear of them and feast off the AI so you can focus on leveling up.Pretty bad optimization since it's on an outdated engine, my PC can run a game like War Thunder at high settings at 70fps yet it struggles 50fps here. AI can be a bit flunky, one second they're giving you easy kills then they're all over your tail chipping at your health.No tutorial of any kind, however the game has easy controls and in game hints that kinda walk you through your first few games, and theres some beginner combat missions to introduce you to the game.Overall, this game is worth checking out for your arcade air combat needs. Comparing it to War Thunder is like comparing Mario Kart to rFactor or Assetto Corsa. It's just pointless as these games are in categories of their own and simply can't be compared. Don't listen to the people complaining about "unrealisitc aircraft handling" as in this game, though it's still arcade, you still feel like you're flying an aircraft. Something like a Beaufighter won't be able to throw itself around the sky like a Spitfire can. Certainly a fun arcade flight game

_childDocuments_.review: World of Warplanes presents an intriguing premise with its aerial combat theme and a diverse range of historical aircraft. However, the execution falls short in several aspects. The game's mechanics often feel clunky and unrefined, leading to a less-than-smooth game play experience. Controlling the planes can be overly challenging, especially for newcomers, resulting in a frustrating learning curve that detracts from the overall enjoyment.Moreover, the game suffers from imbalanced matchmaking, frequently pitting players against vastly superior opponents or mismatched teams, leading to one-sided and unsatisfying battles. This imbalance can make progress feel arbitrary and leaves little room for skill development or fair competition.While the graphics and attention to detail in aircraft design are pretty good, other technical aspects, such as server stability and occasional glitches, hinder the immersive experience.                                        In essence, World of Warplanes has potential but is marred by game play issues, unbalanced matches, technical flaws, and a less-than-ideal community atmosphere, making it a less recommended choice for those seeking a polished and consistently enjoyable gaming experience.

World of Warplanes lets me hop into a match, blow some stuff up in my favorite plane, and go back to my studies. It's perfect for my busy lifestyle. _childDocuments_.review: Not really first time playing on steam, back then I did touched a bit on this game via Wargaming Launcher with my Logitech Extreme 3D Pro Flight stick for fun (Flight stick felt even worst than mouse & keyboard)World of Warplanes, around 10 years since its release date as of writing of this review, is basically a "Arcade Dogfight" for casuals that was made like a mobile game. Before I answer "why you said its like a mobile game?", let me put out the goods that I found playing this game:First of all, its simple and fun, the mechanics in the game are absolutely basic to minimum, you lead your crosshair to the enemy plane's direction and fire. No weapon bloom, its just you putting holes to the enemy plane until their health pool's gone, capture and protect sectors, destroy some ground targets, and score to win. And the economic system is basically same as any other Wargaming games does (World of Tanks & World of Warships), which is play to earn plane XP and some money, buy parts, ammunition, upgrades and progress through tech tree, rinse and repeat.Aaaand here's are the obvious flaw it has: (And its still plague since the first time I've played 3 years ago)The game is , like seriously, it's nearly to the point of chasing a plane and shooting it down. Like it has some basic strategy of "theoretically" what you should do in a dogfight; YES you can dodge by steering away or braking your plane to let tailing enemy fall infront of you, YES you can try to shoot individual parts to  its effectiveness (not disabling it) and YES, thats all. It seriously doesn't have anything else you can perform during these fight, you are just trying to grind enemy's health before yours. (And no, short controlled burst doesn't affect your accuracy, it only reduce the gun overheat/jamming issues)And second thing, its Economy. It's still has the old "World of Tanks early days Bulls**t" where you know...  And the total amount of nation planes are small as well, especially the Europe and China, they are just stuffed with . Balancing wise, as many players in the review already stated, YES, its just unbalance. The heavy fighter class is just too good to use, large health pool, fine damage with rear gunner that auto shoot anyone tailing, and ATG unguided bombs with only the trade is maneuverability. But don't let the maneuverability fool you, that rear gunner is what it'll keep most of the tailing risky. Plus, you won't even able to grind its health down before it reacts and chase you back.Last but not least, the matchmaking is pretty much dead here. Mostly you'll just match with bots and get easy kills.So all in all, this game isn't bad, its has simple gameplay that other game developers that has perfected it already, and yet itself doesn't even wanna improve from the core mechanic. Pretty much a waste of effort.My only suggestion for this game is to make all the modules destroy-able, like World of Tank's ammo rack module where it reaches zero, the tank immediately killed. Except for planes, make the pilot killable/breakable parts/detonatable undeployed air-to-ground bomb or anything, like seriously, you guys already decided to make player respawn unrestricted already, so why not make the combat more brutally rewarding like World of Tanks or World of Warships than "fly around and trying to put as many holes on enemy before you" game.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my wind down game lately. If you've never played a Wargames game, they are multiplayer battles between faithfully recreated world war 2 vehicles. Starting with planes from the end of the first world war, you fight battles and earn experience to unlock new modules and planes.World of Warplanes is very different from its sisters. For a start, you can respawn to a point. I never liked Call of Duty's Search and Destroy gametype as I'd die right at the start from some gameplay exploit and have to spend the rest of the game watching other people having fun. For the first 5 minutes of this game you can die as much as you like and join back in. Eventually the squall line appears and stops the respawns but by then its near the end of the match like the game is hurrying me along to the next one. But I don't mind this because it means the final moments of the game progress towards an intense and exciting climax.You can't do the slow crawl you do in tanks or ships because if you're not hurtling across the sky at 100kph then you stall and drop embarrassingly into the ground and so the gameplay is very different. As usual, there are different classes of planes. Fighters are the weakest lacking armour or firepower but they can out manoeuvre all the other classes and, most planes lacking a powerful rear-firing gun, can bite the heavier classes in the arse without repercussions. Heavy fighters are almost the opposite. They have speed, armour and firepower on their side and are great for taking out the heavier targets and strafing slower ones. Attack planes have weapons geared towards flying low and destroying ground targets and bombers reach great heights to rain bombs safe from enemy fire.There are a couple of different deployments for each map but all the games boil down to capturing areas. You can do this by shooting down enemy planes and destroying ground targets in the area. The areas are also split into area types, each one geared towards a different class of plane. For example, airfields contain more defence planes and few ground targets making it great for fighter classes whereas plants have heavily armoured ground targets and few defence planes ideal for bombers and attack planes. Capturing them has a gameplay benefit too. An airfield controlled by your team, for example, serves as a second respawn point to get you back in the fight faster and the military base launches rockets at adjacent areas to help capture them.Progression in this game follows a similar route as it's sisters. You play and earn experience with a plane to unlock its upgraded modules and the next tier plane and collecting all of this will give the plane elite status. What is different, and what I think should be rolled out to the other games, is that each plane has a specialist rank above elite that can be earned by completing challenges. Unlocking this allows you to upgrade your modules with bonus stats and means each plane plays subtly different.I enjoy working towards unlocking all the planes and leveling them up to specialist. It's an extremely grindy game and is going to require a large time commitment to get even half way up the tech tree. There are also limited starting hanger spaces for your planes but these can be expanded through micropurchases. You can also use tokens to buy hanger slots (something I'm pretty certain can't be done in the other games) that you earn by achieving the rarer medals and complete daily challenges, but you will need a tier 8 plane for that.So I would recommend Warplanes. I've preferred it to its sisters and found it hits the right balance of exciting dogfights and trackable gameplay and it scratches my collector's itch.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for kids who are interested in planes and plane combat to play, and maybe for people who would not be good at flight sims and want a more arcade flying game.But it is very very arcade-esque. You don't control your turns by banking and diving your plane, instead you just move the mouse to the direction you want to fly in and the plane automatically turns for you. You can't really control your throttle/speed. You stay at a set speed and have an option to either reduce your speed by 65% with the "brakes" or boost it for a few seconds to go faster than the standard speed. But that's it for speed options.It's very very much an arcade game. If you want more of a simulation experience, where you actually control the plane's finer realistic details, then maybe look for something like Ace Combat or War Thunder or DCS. P.S. Some players have trouble with the game crashing shortly after a match starts. You should/may be able to fix this issue by launching the game directly via the executable. Instead of pressing play on the game within Steam, try navigating to this spot with your file explorer:C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\World of Warplanes\Then find the application/executable for the game and double click that file to open the game. Fixed the crashing issue for me. Good luck!

The base game isn't good but I am genuinely amazed at how unfinished it is. Even just adding a trifling amount of PVE content and allowing players to collect planes and just buy currency, points, and planes would make this game far better. Don't waste your time on this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. As far as a plane simulator, it is not half bad. It can be fun to play, the game mechanic is based on advancing through different technological levels, acquiring experience to research new planes and new parts for the planes you own, and acquiring an in-game currency, by fighting, to buy it. This game needs several significant changes before I recommend it: -  It needs to have a tutoring game mechanic that teaches the aspects/mechanics of the game(including the monetary system). -  It needs to add more parts to each plane for more customization instead of having the current complex technology tree, which involves literally dozens of planes for each country.-  The Flak game mechanic needs to be significantly nerfed/reworked:       -It needs to be proportional to the enemy bombers in range.        -It needs to only attack bombers and not fighters, although collateral damage to fighters should be possible.       -It needs to be far less accurate but with far more damage possible per explosion.       -It needs to stop aiming at a player-controled plane if it is within 100 meters of a neutral plane.-  It needs to add a microphone speak/listen portion so that players can strategize. From my experience the game as a whole is free-for-all, it needs something that adds structure to the gameplay:       -This could be accomplised with a patrol/dogfight option where fighters engage over neutral ground and a bomber escort/open battle portion which is what is offered now (with points awarded for properly escorting bombers).-  It needs to be purchased to support the game development. There is a way of buying in-game currency; but, this is quite expensive, and just makes you advance faster(detracting from the purpose of the current game mechanics). It would make more sense to make this a paid game.

_childDocuments_.review: A failed project best worth avoiding.Lots of egregious pay-to-win gimmicks that directly determine who will win any given dogfight harmed the game's player-retention. Wargaming have gotten increasingly greedy with P2Win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in their other games; but this game is mobile-games levels of cynical pay-to-win ♥♥♥♥ in terms of how fundamentally upgraded equipment impacts each and every fight.This is exacerbated by the upgrade path featuring lots of RNG slot-machine mechanics to further frustrate you into paying for an advantage.Depending on the time of day, day of the week, and season, the vast majority of players in any given match will be bots - turning a 12-vs-12 format into a 3-vs-3 at best. And bad luck if your teammate is flying one of the PVE planes, as you're going to get ganked again and again and again by the three human players on the opposite team.Unlike WoWS and WoT, the game is cynical enough to disguise the bots names, and make the bots speak in chat channel, to deceive people into thinking the population levels are healthier than they are.Because of the chronic mishandling of the game, and the consequent lack of popularity, the game has been treated as an afterthought by Wargaming - which means truly diabolical servers, and terrible support.Which means ridiculous desyncing and consequently abysmal hit-detection - you'll often see planes warping around (there's literally a visual effect you'll see when they rubber-band into position) as the game tries to resync the action.On top of this, the login server constantly fails to return you to the hangar after battles - resulting in frequent timeouts, and having to relog.The game suffers significant framerate issues, despite being on a dated engine with completely unspectacular visuals.It's a substandard product, with a very high premium, and it's not particularly well executed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 20 hours in after a few days of playing. The game is fun and doesn't concentrate on real world physics but rather playability making combat enjoyable. To me this is a good thing because physics can be a bummer when it comes to combat situations as tends to draw out boring time in between. This keeps you engaged. It can be heart pounding at times when you know there are a few enemies near and you have to plan out your dog fight and not get killed in the process. There can be plenty of skill applied to each situation, aircraft and requirement. Every aircraft has it's own physics, load out, etc. You may love a light fighter but hate a heavy fighter. But, the game a has a ways to go, I think the dev lost sight of "early access" and jumped in the deep end working on pay content when there are still a number of things to address. There are a few German Heavy fighters that are far too powerful and are used to simply ram an enemy to destroy them and no harm to them. Sometimes the physics on a plane go cross eyed and the plane just ends up flipping direction or becoming unpredictable.  lastly "services" and "upgrades" can be confusing. I have a service with a ! next to it with nothing for me to do, no clue if it's working or not because there is no feedback. There are "player points" which are just experience point but they don't show now many you have and can only see how much more you need in order to "research" something. It's just kind of annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun concept killed by lack of other players.  At it's core, World of Warplanes has very satisfying dogfighting mechanics that would be elevated if you could actually play against other players.  Maybe you're kept out of matches with more players until you reach a certain tier or something, but you're lucking if you solo queue into a match with more than one other person. A fun distraction for a few hours, and extremely fun if you yourself are a history buff or have interest in aviation history; but otherwise a game that quickly loses its appeal.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.  People will compare it to War Thunder and they are both fine games but for simple FUN I much prefer World of Warplanes.  Flying with the mouse is very easy. The Tier system starts easy at Tier 1 and gets significantly harder once past Tier 4.  It is very easy to progress Tiers up to around Tier 7 onwards where you may need to grind to earn the experience for the next plane.   The variety of planes is large with significant performance variations so there should be a "good" plane for everyone.  The games are reasonably quick.  The waiting times for a match - reasonable.  Probably the best thing about the game is that I believe the Game Producers are generous with giveaways and rewards. I have now played around 150 hours over two months and have received 3 Premium planes and two others, multiple hanger slots and other equipment including experienced crew simply for playing regular missions that they provide.  I hope that you try the game and enjoy it - Good luck Pilots and have Fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, yes, the one game in Wargaming's roster that seems to be treated like an unwanted stepchild. All I constantly see is everyone complaining and whining over small little details, so as someone who can see this from an objective perspective, allow me to show you why this game has a lot hidden under its surface.PROS:One of the first things that caught my attention when I first got into this game was the controls. I recall a period in time when the controls were horrendously complicated or sometimes unresponsive; however, that time has now passed. I am greatly impressed by how simple things have become, regardless of what role you play. Whether it's looking down the sight lines of your bomb sights, or zooming around holding W to get your plane to go faster, the ability to use your plane is so simple it lets you actually focus on the other dynamics this game has to offer.Speaking of roles, the five roles to choose from (Fighter, Heavy Fighter, Bomber, Close Air Support, and Multirole) do seem simple; however, there is such a wide array to choose from depending on which nation you choose, and each one offers a different dynamic. I personally found that the United States and Germany had the widest array of aircraft, and it was something that made me fall in love with the game coming from someone who's used to playing bombers in War Thunder. It's an experience that I've also shared with friends, which is amazing.CONS:When I first load up most games, I tend to open up Task Manager on my second monitor to watch its performance throughout the game's duration. When in battle, I have tended to notice that the game has a minor RAM bleed, but this seems to go away once you return to your hangar; however, this RAM bleed is similar to that of the size of Discord's similar faults, so it's not something that is dangerous in the short-term. You will, however, see some performance loss if you're not playing on a good rig.Aside from this, the only other con I see is that there's not a lot of players playing the game from what I remember when the big update happened a few years ago. Naturally, most games on the lower tiers are riddled with bots, and these bots have relatively predictable, albeit dynamic flight patterns, so if you're playing an interceptor craft, it won't take long to take down smaller fighters.All in all, I'll rate this game 7/10. I believe aside from needing performance tweaks, adding more planes available to all nations (looking at the UK, France, and Italy in particular), and finding a way to populate the game a bit more (even if it's just a better bot AI), I believe this game is currently in its best state and I look forward to when Wargaming is able to devote more resources into improving a game I've enjoyed for a long time.
