_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a fantastic game for those who enjoy a more relaxed, yet engaging gaming experience. It didn’t take long for me to get completely hooked—what started as a casual session quickly turned into hours of addictive gameplay. The game brilliantly balances strategy and management, placing you in the shoes of an emergency services dispatcher responsible for saving lives.The gameplay is simple to grasp but offers enough depth to keep you invested. Managing resources, prioritizing calls, and responding to emergencies in real-time create a unique sense of responsibility and immersion. It’s the kind of game where you can lose track of time as you get absorbed in making critical decisions and seeing the consequences play out.What makes "112 Operator" stand out is its ability to be both challenging and chill at the same time. You can approach it at your own pace, making it perfect for when you want to unwind but still feel mentally stimulated. Whether you’re handling routine incidents or sudden large-scale disasters, the game keeps you on your toes in the most enjoyable way.Overall, "112 Operator" is a gem for anyone looking for a fun and relaxing game that still offers plenty of excitement. It’s easy to get hooked, and before you know it, hours will have flown by as you manage your virtual city’s emergencies. Definitely a must-try for fans of strategy and management games!

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, it offers a very unique experience, but I will warn anyone that is looking to buy - this game gets out of control very quickly, and it is deceptively difficult. You will almost certainly find yourself extremely taxed as incidents pop up constantly, never giving you any reprieve. If you can handle that kind of exhausting workload, or you just... enjoy feeling extremely stressed while playing video games, then this is probably a good buy for you. My biggest compliments are that it is occasionally a very emotionally resonant game, and there are a good few incidents that are interesting to deal with, but my biggest complaints are how tedious a lot of the micromanagement can be, (especially with fire units constantly running out of water as if their truck tank is the size of a water bottle..) and the aforementioned overwhelming flood of incidents even when playing on lower difficulties. I don't think anything above normal is physically possible to win. The feature of expanding your district control out is interesting, but once you reach those larger and larger and larger areas, it starts to get nearly impossible to keep track of everything, your dozens of units with unique squads, even with the AI dispatchers doing some of the work for you. I really, really wish I could opt to play on the scale of 911 operator, because the entire city areas available in this game is just.. it's just too much.It's come a long way since 911 operator, just prepare yourself for war, because as soon as a building catches on fire, or there's an armed robbery, or any other actually serious incident... every single person in the city will immediately descend onto bike-stealing, jaywalking, and every other petty, time-wasting use of resources possible to ensure your reputation tanks since you'll never ever be able to stop them all.Rewarding and good, but often tedious, inane, and overwhelmingly stressful. Just uh, like the real job I suppose. So good..? Work..?

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: Very fun, interesting, challenging, rewarding and emotional. Long story:I've played the 911 version before this and was immediantly hooked to this style of gameplay. When 112 was released, I thought it would be similar to the previous game but with larger maps and new vehicles. However, the developing team has surprised me with a series of surprises. For example, allowing you to witness the process of each mission by displaying it with icons at the info page (similar to chess), this actually made me felt like the incident was really happening and not just one bold spot on my screen. There’s also a mail box which gives you information that foreshadows the events that might occur in your next duty. You might receive treats, compliments, game tips and possible events.The idea of adding man hunts and wildfires just spices up the taste of the game. Of course, along with this feature comes with a reasonable wheatear forecast that might determine the spread of the fire. The new mission system gives you an additional goal that you might want to achieve while playing. The game includes kits instead of individual items, allowing the player to equip their team with different kits that performs differ jobs, making it more convenient and requires more considerations. Fire trucks now have a water storage, if the storage runs out, the fire won’t be extinguished. You need to send another team to the site in order to put the fire off.As usual, the calls are very intriguing and realistic, it requires you to think calmly while there are multiple on-going incidences. This really challenges the player, despite of the fact there are different difficulties and levels throughout your campaign. Additionally, there are also calls that just makes the situation worse, (spoils alert) an example of such will be a certain huge explosion in a building with people inside. No matter how well you have assisted the situation, it’s going to happen. This just makes you feel guilty on the other side of the phone hearing the explosion, which adds more emotion to this game. The vehicles in this game is very well thought of. It has all its advantages and disadvantages, you as a player needs to figure out how to organize your units in order to cope with the demands. For example, motorcycles are fast and can resolve a traffic jam easily, but they cannot carry any suspects. A police truck can hold four suspects with 4 officers, however they cost a lot. There are so many other features that I haven’t experienced yet, but this game is super worth it and I cannot resist myself writing this review!

_childDocuments_.review: When I reviewed 911 Operator, this game's predecessor, I felt quite ambivalent about it. It was fun, had some great voice acting but didn't necessarily grip me. Well, in many ways 112 Operator is quite similar. It has the same kind of gameplay, a somewhat basic management layout, and it keeps the strengths of the past with strong voice acting and good scenarios. And yet, something was gnawing at the back of my head when playing this game. So I decided to give it a bit more of a chance this time around, because there is something here that is worth actually examining. If you want a TLDR, then what I stated above should give you an idea of what the game is; I recommend it, you should try it out.What does this game do well? Well, most of what's in there is good, but what really stands out is the calls themselves. In normal gameplay, you will get random prompts that are displayed as symbols on the map and that's it; pair the right vehicle to the right symbol, you're good. Calls are more complex. Firstly, you have sort of a CYOA component, where you need to choose the right dialogue options in order to get information and/or direct the person on the other side. Secondly, you have to use that info to determine what services to send, or to ignore the call altogether. Sometimes they're used as a part of bigger events, like storms or wildfires, as well, which require their own responses.All of this is great. The events feel dynamic, they require good judgement and splits your focus from the normal gameplay, raising the challenge of the game. What really make them pop though is the voice acting and the writing. Many times, these calls are their own little stories and the acting makes them feel real. Calling the emergency number is not a normal event, and people won't sound fully clear or rational sometimes. That's captured in these games and it pairs up beautifully with some really dramatic situations. It's not fully consistent, but when it hits, it hits hard.You might think I should be finished here. The gameplay is good, the story is great, so... great game right? Here's where we get to a problem, that might not be a problem depending on your sensibilities. It's time to talk about police. In this game, the cops are, much like the ambulances and the fire fighters, an unproblematic entity. A symbol comes up, you send the police. Sometimes people die, but they're just squares on the screen, so it's fine, right? Sending the police always means that the police is the right entity for the job. The thing is, there are some assumptions shining through. Both police and criminals are static in their behaviour; police are always seen as a solution to a problem, while criminals are the source of violence. It doesn't matter if you show up with two cops or ten, the drug dealers are going to fight either way. And after sending police to case after case, where more cops always lead to better outcomes, I started to really think about it. Should police really be sent after someone walking naked on the street? Am I causing more violence than I'm stopping? And when you're tasked to send police to a peaceful demonstration, which predictably starts producing rioting... well, it felt off to me. The fact that arming the police, any and all of them, with military equipment is seen as a pure gameplay upgrade with no downsides? It doesn't help.On top of that, in the game's storylines, your calls are rarely wrong nor punished. If you give the wrong instructions, bad things might happen, but it doesn't touch you nor follow you through the game. What does haunt you has nothing to do with your calls. Instead, you're blamed for things you didn't do. I think that's a shame. Instead of someone being hurt because of events out of your control, wouldn't it have been better to actually make you guilty? To base it off a call you made, a standard event spiraling out of control because of your actions? "Maybe I shouldn't have sent those cops" or "Did I just send those fire fighters to their deaths" – those kinds of doubts would have been easy to create with the systems already in place. If there is something that doesn't work in the call sequences, it's just that: Consequences, or the lack of them.Maybe it's unfair of me to judge the game off of this. But I think that 112 Operator could have been something really, really special and it annoys me when a slight change in perspective is all it would take. Adding a  critical eye to the systems portrayed would have been enough. As it is, the game is still good, but the drama feels a bit hollow to me. I wish it was different. With that said, the game is still worth playing. Other people might (probably, let's be honest) have a different view than me and end up loving what this game provides. It's more than just your usual management game, and for that I do appreciate it. Give it a look. You probably won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Same game as the brilliant first game, but with severe balance issues because the core gameplay systems does not work when you increase the map size and incidents like the sequel. Just buy the better balanced first game (911 Operator) right now. This experiment in  adding a district macro game completely fails by turning a good micro game into an overwhelming micro game.------------Loved the first game but as of writing, there are huge balancing issues in the sequel here. It's largely the same core gameplay, except the map size and incidents has been scaled up tremendously, whilst your resources simply does not scale in line with the extra demands. Even if you do theoretically somehow have enough resources available, there are way too many incidents, and the developer's idea is that you hire AI to do it for you in districts, basically to automate the actual gameplay away.  The scaling system of the first game which worked well before, completely collapses when you increase the map size and the number of incidents like this. There are also features such as blizzards and storms, which disables your already severely lacking fleet. It's good on paper and would've worked in the first game, but it only compounds the existing problems of this current one. Also doesn't help that you have bugs such as units getting stuck in snow during blizzards, forgetting their original orders once they dig themselves out. There is just not the same satisfaction that you get like in the first game anymore because every shift becomes an exercise in frustration. The original 911 Operator was a good micromanagement game, but by simply scaling everything up with minimal adjustments, it has turned into an unmanageable chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Only played 7 hours on free play mode and already expanded to more regions of a city than one person can effectively manage while having fun. It's just chaos... in an annoying way. Your units are constantly shouting over each other so you can't listen to what they need. You don't have enough units that early on to effectively cover the map. Of course, your fast response bikes and medi-helicopter are grounded because of bad weather... not that they would be of any use anyway because you still need a dozen more land ambulances than you have. A half dozen units are stacked at their base and you can't easily see who and what is there and it's not easy to select the one you want quickly. It's hard to understand what your units are currently doing by the icons that are supposed to show what they're doing. There is no fast way to see which units are 'free' and where they are. It would be MUCH better if when I select an incident that requires an additional unit that I see a list on-screen of free units and distances, maybe allowing me to double click on one of them to direct them to the selected incident - instead I have to fly round the map looking for what I need, select it, then re-select the incident to move the screen to it so I can click on it AGAIN to direct the unit to it. All while a dozen units are shouting stupid useless stuff and more incidents are popping up. I found myself constantly just pausing the game simply to pause new incidents while I hunt for units. It's just manic and not at all fun. I enjoyed 911 Operator much more!

_childDocuments_.review: A modest, but solid evolution from 911 Operator. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 2nd, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Handling the emergency services for towns, including your own. 112 Operator is a sequel to 911 Operator with similar gameplay based on the European system rather than the American.  You’ll control different cities, such as Berlin, and have to route emergency services to different events as well as handle calls yourself.  This sounds like it’s simple but it’s quite intense. The calls are rather entertaining, with many of them being well-acted, or at least done well enough to keep my attention.  A nice new feature is the ability to base the game around where you live.  This game was able to detect where I lived, and sure enough, put events in the city and surrounding locations from my home.  It pulls real street information too. That's kind of interesting. Pick this up if you want a strange game.  I never thought I wanted to be a 911 or 112 operator but after playing this game I was entertained enough that I’m going to return and play more of my game, and the campaign.  This isn’t an action game or a AAA bonanza but 112 Operator was well done and does feel like it’ll work towards overwhelming the player with the number of different tasks they’ll have to juggle. _childDocuments_.review: In 112 Operator you play as a... 112 Operator. You must receive calls and dispatch units to solve incidents that occur. The game makes attempts to have you question your morality and decisions and has loads of unique ideas, but ends up being a frustrating repetitive mess.DLC?Don't know, don't care. If you like the base game then pick up the DLC rated higher than a mixed and you should be fine.Game's Story - 2/10The story is basically none existent. They try to stuff a story into this game, but it ends up being very weak. An incident at the start links to an incident all the way at the end of the game but that's it.In the game, you have a daughter but you only ever interact with her once or twice. The game should've made it so you interact with her more often for more character development. There are more reoccurring characters, but they come up so infrequently it doesn't even matter.They try to have you question your morality and decisions but do it in a very poor way. You'll have people call or email you saying "Thank you" or "F*** you!" but it just didn't phase me because I felt so disconnected from all the events happening on the ground even during emergency calls. DEFCON did a better job at morality by acknowledging that you are disconnected from what is happening and using it to its advantage rather than trying to work around it.Overall, there is a lack of character development when it was awfully needed to make this game's tiny story work. As well as failed attempts to make you question your decisions.Visuals - 2/5The visuals aren't impressive. The UI is alright and I like the artwork for the different vehicles and people and whatnot, but other than that it is really basic.It is possible to zoom in and get 3D buildings, but you have to zoom in so far (and it causes lag spikes) that it just becomes impractical which sucks because that was a large selling feature of the sequel.Audio - 6/10SFX - 4/5Credit where credit is due. The sound effects are really good. The voice acting is alright. Something else I really like is that you can hear stuff happen around you in the world. If it is raining, you can hear it. If there is a riot, you can hear it. Concert? You betcha. Your character can even comment on it at times which is cool. You will hear other operators calls in the backgrounds and your squad cars will respond when you click on them. However, I do wish there were one or two more voice lines for when you click on units and send them off to an incident. As well as many more voice lines in general.Music - 2/5The music is pretty basic in my opinion, it is enough to get by but is not very revolutionary or interesting.Gameplay - 3/10There are a lot of good things and a lot of bad things. It is fun to manage your units and send them off to different places, and this game provides so many new QOL features compared to 911 Operator. However, there are a lot more bad things to talk about which just ruined my experience and ruined the gameplay for me.First, the gameplay ends up getting boring and repetitive. With special events happening rarely and being underwhelming at best you stuck with almost the exact same gameplay for several hours with varying levels of difficulty. At one point I had a tornado come and I was getting ready with all my units, and then it went across the city and nothing happened. No unique phone calls or incidents, nothing. What the hell? There are also other special incidents like one where you just get rid of 6 of your ambulances (which I just found you could ignore and get the reputation back throughout the mission anyway).  Some special incidents just give you zero time to react to or take your units 6000 years to fix. I don't know whether I want consistency or what but the special incidents are what should make or break this game, and they smashed it up with a hammer.Second, sometimes you have hidden "special objectives" you must complete to succeed a shift. Unfortunately, it won't tell you these "special objectives". Sometimes, it won't even mission fail you until the very end of the shift forcing you to playthrough the entire shift again just to move on. On the last shift, I was solving the last incident and was happy to be done with this game and then it popped up in red with text saying "You failed to save the VIP" even though that happened at the very start of the shift which made me fall in despair. I had to do the shift all over again. Also, the very end of the game sees you having to make a high stakes phone call but after you fail the phone call (which you will), you immediately fail your shift being forced to play for 5 minutes to get back there. After the time all intensity is removed, it turns into a frustrating trial and error section where you hope you picked the right options. I got so peeved off I just looked up the answer on the third attempt.Third, just small annoying things. Such as how if multiple units are in the same spot it becomes really hard to pick between individual units and there was another thing as well but I forget (it's late).Fourth, the game advertises to you when you open and close the game. It just puts a big list of DLC and other game's they have made. Which is annoying. I will cut them some slack because: A they are indie and B other devs do this, but it doesn't make it acceptable.Fifth, they take away the best part of the game. The best part of the game are the 112 emergency phone calls you get to respond to, however about halfway(?) through the campaign you get promoted to a higher position where you literally don't take 112 phone calls anymore. What! Not to mention that even then there just a lack of 112 phone calls in general, I wish there were at least double the emergency calls and a few extra for freeplay, because if you ever play freeplay you will be unsurprised to learn that there are no unique phone calls and you will just hear the same crap over and over again.Sixth, you get to hire other operators to play the game for you. However, I'd just rather have less incidents and a smaller map than just hoping that the operator can solve it on it's own.There probably more issues I could ramble on about, or I could find several things to nitpick about like not being able to have a squad composed entirely of dogs but it is late and I just wanna finish this review so I can go to sleep and forget about this game forever.Value For Money - 6/10Played for 13.2 hours, but wish I had just stopped halfway through.Other - 2/5Performance - 1/2This games runs really poorly. Long load times (to be fair I had this game installed on a HDD), lag when loading in 3D buildings (making it useless) and just random lag spikes near the end of the campaign when you have lots of vehicles and a large map loaded in. I HAD LESS FRAME DROPS WITH DOOM (2016)!Bugs - 1/2Found a few things, that seem bad but nothing game breaking fortunately.Community - 0/1Dead. No community. Apart from one person/ a group of people who just made a large pack of workshop mods which completely change the game. Maybe that will make it better, who knows? I'm sure as hell not going to find out.Overall - 42/100This game has a lot of unique concepts and a lot of unique ideas. I had fun playing this game at times, especially at the beginning. However, as time went on I got more and more frustrated and more and more annoyed with the game. With lots of large issues with this game I just can't recommend it. You would be better suited playing other simulation management games.The best part was when I ordered all my units (other 40) to go to a single incident, they kept spamming the voice line "Out of space" when there were too many there which was funny.

_childDocuments_.review: This review might seem a bit harsh, but let me be clear, I absolutely give credit to the developers for creating (for me at least) a stable game, with a much better UI than 911 Operator, giving a discount to those who owned it, updating the game often, but most important to me, actually lurking in the discussions area and responding. That's great. Also happy to finally see an option to sell units from the garage!So as I mention the UI in this game has massively improved, among other great stuff, but unfortunately for me I cannot recommended it quite yet. But this isn't a game you should turn away from, but rather wishlist it and return in a month or two. Sorry if I sound overly negative but some of these things are just ugh.- There are too many incidents! This feeling is shared a lot on the discussions area. Even in easy mode, the calls keep popping up especially as you get deeper in to the game. I absolutely get that it's unrealistic to get every unit to every call before it expires, because a lot of the time, at least in my country, units/resources are stretched, but this is pushing it a bit. You can get several incidents one after the other and you're not making enough money to upgrade your units quickly enough to cope with the increased demand and significant amount of more area you have to cover. Easy should at least be relaxing!- The tutorial is reasonable but it seems to miss quite a few things, like it didn't tell me I could shift click an order to queue it, that I could double click on the map for a unit to go there with sirens on, and the tutorial came up telling me that I can hire additional dispatchers around the 8th or so day, but apparently the feature isn't available to use until around the 15th, making me look around the interface wondering how to do it, then coming to the forums to discover it isn't possible yet.- I find it annoying that the difficulty modes for freeplay are locked. I can't play hard until the 15th mission or so and I can't play the top difficulty until I've completed the ENTIRE campaign. That will take ages! Why this silly lock? - The time to respond to incidents on bigger maps is too small especially without the money to buy more units. It's a shame there's no realism with vehicle speed either, would be good if they could speed up a bit on long straight roads but that's just a minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥. :P- This is by far my most fustrating experience. This game has not improved on the 112 calls from the 911 Operator game. The calls are extremely repetitive, often getting the same calls from the previous mission. I'm only 9 days in and I can already recite most of the calls, knowing exactly what they will say and what options I shall pick. It feels like I am rotating between the same 10 calls. I made a discussion thread on this and several others feel the same way. Both because of this, and not, I would like to see a setting to disable the public's incoming calls entirely so I can just play the game as a dispatcher. In my country, the call hander and the dispatcher are seperate people away, so the option would be a realistic one.- There are a few UI ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, like if I sort my units by police, then open the new units menu, the filter I just set for my units will reset to show everything. That isn't what I wanted, it should stay as I filtered it. Some sort of 'compact' view to see all of my units without scrolling too much would also be valued. The lack of facility to re-order units or sort/group them by anything other than district is also a bit fustrating. - As suggested in discussions, in some circumstances, like the police being at an incident and taking a prisoner, if I have the unit queued up to attend another incident, the vehicle will cancel the queue and will go to the police station. The vehicle should go direct to the queued event unless the vehicle is full of prisoner, and I think most others would expect this behaviour. If the vehicle did go back because it was full, that order should only go in between and the vehicle should continue with the queue once they stop the suspects off at the station.- Some information, maybe on the tutorial, on how staff members skill increase (or don't they?) would be nice.- The messages that appear in green at the top of the screen like when a fire engine runs out of water or police need backup, should disappear once the problem no longer applies. I.e. if a fire engine runs out of water, as soon as that fire engine leaves the scene to fill up or the incident becomes complete, the message should be removed. Sometimes I get multiple messages come through at once and I have to click each one to understand which are relevant and which have passed. This is a great game and I have hope that many of these changes will come with the active development team, so I'm not refunding personally... but for now I cannot recommend purchasing this game. I will watch the development closely and will absolutely amend this review as appropriate, mainly after the balance and public 112 call problems are resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was received free for review purposes.On the surface of it, this game might seem just like a slight polish of 911 Operator, its predecessor. However, after playing it for a fair few hours, I do have to say two things:- It's as fun as ever, especially when you get an abundance of things to do and have to juggle your units around- They've added special events, storylines, weather, e-mail feedback, promotions within the call center (you get to hire dispatchers under your command, etc.) and so onThe voiced 911 calls in the previous game were fun and, arguably, the highlight of each duty you took. However, the quality of the voice acting (apart from the operator who has an excellent voice and was apparently a real dispatcher) was all over the place and often somewhat silly. What's worse is that the calls started repeating fairly quickly. Not a huge deal but you knew what to expect and what to answer.This has changed in 112 Operator for the better. There are two reasons for this. I feel like the frequencey of voiced calls are lower each duty now. A bit of a shame but I'd rather have that than repeating calls every few minutes. The second reason is that there is now a MUCH larger variety of voiced calls. They also give you many more options on how to respond (correclty and incorrectly, with consequences). The quality of the voice acting is on a much higher level and more consistent. You have panicking people, people in distress, those that wish to stay anonymous, people that will argue with you, prank calls, etc. A lot of them now not only start an emergency you have to send units to respond to, but also begin new mechanics like a search for missing persons, manhunts, etc.Speaking of new mechanics, the weather now changes and presents a new challenge. A huge storm? Expect lightning strikes, your motorcycle units out of commission, children getting lost... A heat wave? Get the already stretched firefighters to set up sprinklers and respond to huge wildfires which now spread through regions and have to be dealt with immediately. Firefighting units now have a certain amount of water in their vehicles and need to replenish those.As each emergency unit arrives at a location, you get a much better visual overview of what's going on. The game will represent a top-down view of pretty much everything quite accurately. A broken pipe spewing water, a damaged road sign, a collission between a motorcycle and a car, a stadium with a concert, etc.To top it all off, there are now minor stories involved in your duties, like a manhunt for a serial killer over several days, an arsonist and so on. You also get to read e-mails from survivors, your dispatchers and your supervisor.As a negative, when there are a lot of units going everywhere, it's sometimes difficult to quickly gauge what's available and what isn't or where a unit is heading. A simple solution would be to turn the path of a selected unit red instead of just highlight it a slightly brighter white.All in all, very much a surprising sequel. I honestly thought it would be a fun rehash of the original but would present nothing new. I was mistaken. If you liked 911 Operator, you will absolutely enjoy 112 Operator even more.Let's Play of 112 Operator:

It is stressful, and some of the content could be disturbing to you (suicide, bombs, murders, rape gets mentioned, some other stuff like that) but if those things aren't an issue then you should totally try this. _childDocuments_.name: 112 Operator

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for any kind of strategy or depth, look elsewhere. This game is fundamentally just a click-fest that involves sending the nearest vehicle icon of a colour (blue/white/red) to flashing incidents that match those colours. And given the multitude of problems (listed below) with the clunky UI, most of this quickly becomes an exercise in sheer frustration.I really don't understand a lot of the design choices here:- At any given time you are controlling dozens(!) of units and reacting to incidents that spawn every few seconds across a map that is often so large you have to scroll around to see where half of them are. Think about that for a moment, because you'll also want to read each incident so that you can allocate an appropriate unit. Except you simply do not have the time, so you just have to send the nearest. Fast. Because six more incidents just popped up...- You are meant to fail. This is by design. But the problem with this game is that you will fail even harder if you try to use strategy. You have to use speed only.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game, but can't recommend it. There are literally NO quality of life features for managing the later stages of the game. For those who don't know, you start the game as a junior dispatcher managing one single district with only a handful of units. This is fine, relaxing and enjoyable. But as you progress, you have to manage more districts and units. Once you get to 20+ districts or so, the game starts to become an unmanageable mess. Let's try to break it down.Dispatchers:Once you reach day 16, you unlock AI controlled dispatchers. You can assign them to districts to manage them for you and help take some of your load off. The more districts you have, the more incidents you get, and the more units you need to have, so you cannot manage large numbers of districts without them. The problem is that you have to assign each dispatcher to each district, ONE BY ONE. This is fine when you have less than 10 districts. The problem becomes more apparent when you start to expand. You see, to assign a dispatcher to a district, you first need to click on the district, then click on the "assign dispatcher" button, then finally click which dispatcher you want to assign. It doesn't take a math genius to see that this adds up to TONS of clicking very quickly. Once you unlock the full map, you often have 50+ districts to manage, in some cases over 100. This means that if you want to assign dispatchers to ALL your districts (which you MUST DO, otherwise the game becomes impossible to play) it takes between 150 and 300 clicks! CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK! You spend more time clicking than playing the actual game! This become EXTREMELY frustrating, VERY quickly! And if you ever hire a better dispatcher and want to replace one of your existing dispatchers, guess what? MORE CLICKING! You have to re-assign the new dispatcher to every single district, one by one. There is a very simply way to reduce this clicking by at least 99%: simply add the ability to shift-select multiple districts from the district list and assign one dispatcher to all of them. Problem solved. I don't understand why this wasn't in the game from the start.Spreading out units over the map:Incidents occur randomly over the whole map, so you can't just have them in one area and call it a day. You have to evenly spread them out over the whole map to be able to solve incidents in time. Again, as with dispatchers, this isn't a problem when you have a few districts and a handful of units. But when you have tens, or even hundreds of units? I made the mistake of once multi selecting all my units and sending them to one spot on the map. This reminds me, why can you multi-select units, but not districts? Anyway, once i did, i now had the pleasure of having to MANUALLY spread them out over the whole map again. How do i do that? If you guessed MORE CLICKING, you were correct. I now have to click EVERY SINGLE ONE of my 100+ units and click somewhere on the map for them to go. Another 200 clicks! Yes, so much fun! A simple "spread out all units evenly across the map" button would solve this.Assigning equipment to staff:In this game you can assign different levels of equipment to your medics, firefighters and cops, which you definitely want to do unless you want a ton of dead cops and firefighters. Once you unlock vests for your officers, and heavy fire suits for your firefighters you need to assign them to everyone so they don't die as often. But since each unit has at least 2 people, and you can only assign equipment ONE BY ONE to each staff member, guess what? MORE CLICKING! Let's say you have 20 police units and 20 fire units (which isn't even that many) and you want to give everyone in those units better equipment? You now have to click a minimum of 160 times! First you click on each staff member, then click on the equipment to give them. That's 2 clicks per staff. And each Unit has AT LEAST 2 people. So that's 4 clicks per unit, minimum. Times 40 units. Some of them even have up to 4 people, so that's 8 clicks per unit. Why can't you just SHIFT select multiple units and assign the same equipment to ALL people in those units? Then you can manually tweak it if you want some specialist equipment for some units. And while we're on the subject? Why can't you save unit templates with specific equipment and vehicles to the list of predetermined units so you can buy them quickly?TL;DR: They should rename this game 112 clicker. Which is a real shame, since i love the game but there is simply TOO MUCH CLICKING! It's just too frustrating to manage large numbers of units, dispatchers, and districts. Simply adding a "spread out units" button and being able to SHIFT select districts and units to quickly assign equipment and dispatchers would solve 99% of the issues i have with this game. I want to recommend it, but until the devs fix these issues, i can't. A real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is much improved over 911 operator. Here are some pros and cons that I can give with 6 hours of play -PROSVoice Acting The voice acting is 100% better in 112 then 911. It actually makes me feel like i'm talking to a real person. In 911, it was easy to get information out of people and they seemed to have no emotion. In 112, voice actors will fight with you and will sometimes refuse to give location, details and etc. If the person doesn't like what you did or said, they will audibly disagree with you. This makes what you choose to say to them is very important. Consequences and RewardsChoosing the wrong voice options and giving bad advice has worse consequences now. When you tell someone to scream instead of running, they could end up dead. Rewards are also more shown. Deploying units quickly and gathering evidence from the calls you take will help you with the 'events' that happen in game.Map sizeThe maps are HUGE. I thought the 911 operator maps were small and easily beaten. In 112, the maps are almost double or triple the size. This means placing your units in right areas is even more key.Story drivenThere is more of a campaign / story mode in 112. While the story still isn't perfect, you can actually get promoted which means unlocking more responsibilities and even assigning other dispatchers to work for you. You will get updated on your progress from your supervisor and will eventually become that supervisor.Greatly improved management mode screenInstead of just modifying your units in this screen, you can now check your email and see many more stats. You can see which region has what type of calls more frequently then others, the weather and much more. If you piss someone off, you will get an angry email and threats. Co-workers will email you asking questions or giving you props or might tell you to get your ♥♥♥♥ together.CONSDifficultyI started this game on normal, as it said normal was the right difficulty for people who played 911 operator. But damn man, this game is actually way harder. You will constantly have to ignore calls because you simply don't have the units. With the map being so big, it was bound to happen. You earn WAY less money in this game. You will really have to decide which calls are more important then others. The amount of incidents you get is INSANE. This isn't really a con but, even on normal, I feel like I'm playing on hard or expert. - Units still get bunched up together and it's hard to determine if they are available or not.- A couple times some incidents spawned on the same location (or very close to) and I could not select units to go to the different incidents.- Playing on Berlin, there is literally NO police station on the East side of the map. Police units must go all the way back to the West or South to take suspects back.There is so much more I could write and I will try to update this when I gain more hours in the game. If you liked 911 operator or are new to the series, I definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy 911 Operator?Then this is a worthy successor with a good share of quality of life updates.You can see the status of your units on the map and redirect them without checking the menu (I found this out in the 2nd last campaign duty!)You can queue a few tasks for your overworked units and give them more time critical tasks then less important tasks later. E.g. Robbery then parking violation Both  911 and 112 operator can get a bit repetitive as in the end it's a simulator of a real job. However the developers tried to make 112 more fun in general with some more interesting phone calls and problems to deal with. They've also allow you to send in backup units from neighbouring cities, hire dispatchers to help you and have a wider variety of content.Did you not enjoy 911 operator?Perhaps give this one a miss as the basic premise is still the same. You're still a emergency services dispatcher BUT there is a nice variety of content to keep you interested in the campaign mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that challenges your resource management capabilities and snapy decision making skills.Unlike its predecessor 911 operator, it has added tonnes of content and significantly increase the detail on how you micro manage your squad's load out, allowing you to min-max if you so choose to.From the game poster you would have figured out by now that you are managing and dispatching 3 uniform services to complete "Emergency" task in a timely fashion.You get rewarded for mitigating emergencies and punished for failing it. Note that it is sometimes worth it to ignore excess emergencies at the end of the day as overtime penalties can easily ruin your ability for expansion and handling increasing cases in future.-You no longer micro manage what the squad does on site-You are no longer given accurate information of the situation, i.e. an armed robbery can be a single felon that you can handle with one cop and likewise an assault could be a gang of 8 armed men that takes out your entire Swat team.-Greatly increase in load-outs for your personal and giving you the capability to customise and create new loadouts.-An evolving control sector, as you progress the area you manage also expands and that itself increase the difficulty of the game since you will need to redistribute your assets to keep up with the expanding map.-You now have the ability to build bases ontop of the existing ones on the map.-As your area of control grows to a certain size you can hire assistants to manage districts for you, though they are much less capable than you are.-Human resource are much more limited, thus ensuring the safety of your crew has become more important.-Weather can adversely effect some squads ability to operate so plan your squads accordingly.-There is no quick and easy way of sorting squad on the drop down UI, thus making it a nightmare to look for a specific unit when you misplaced it on the map.-When your squad gets wipe, the vehicle gets sends to the garage and you need to redo the process of placing the vehicle and customising the squad all over. This is especially annoying in late game as you lost track of the optimal position of that particular vehicle. It would be better off if they left the vehicle on the map and warn you that it is missing crew members to keep it operational, allowing you to hire replacements or shuffle crew from other squads into it.-The ability to create presets for personals but not squad units makes it a hassle to manually hire, equip loadouts for squads. Its a nuisance at the beginning however it grows increasingly tedious as the game progress, compounding the fact that you need to do this when you squad gets wipe, it is definitely not a fun aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has no replayability in the campaign. I started with the first city on the list thinking that as I continued to other cities there would be some sort of progression or difference between the cities plot-wise. NOPE. The story is recycled no matter what city you play in. This is a missed opportunity to tell different stories relating to each city-maybe even with story connections to other cities, or an overarching plot line?Don't show me ads every time I: 1) Open the game. 2) Finish a scenario and go back to the menu. 3) Exit the gameSeriously folks, just don't do it. That move by itself is an incentive to thumbs down. As it is the gameplay-which feels like a watered down rts-(with advantage for memorizing/knowing the first aid tips that appear in loading screens) does not carry the game.The scenarios are decent, although the calls repeat enough that a knowledge of which calls are fake-or non-emergency is a primary skill to beat some of them on hard.The inclusion of workshop is great-I haven't tried anything from there, but even if the workshop stuff is spectacular, my opinion is set. There is potential here. Much of it is unrealized. It's ok for a bundled game, but $25 for this game-really anything over like $4- is laughable.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very great management game that places you as an 112 or 911 operator in control of medics, firefighters, and police to take care of various real-life incidents.Pros:-Can play in  (Real-life data)-Customize your units' gear and vehicles-Not all incidents are the same   -Weather can affect incidents-Hire other operators to do work for you-Unique calls with easter eggs, references, and mini-stories-Deal with natural disasters-Can adjust your difficulty level-Has a difficulty curve as wellCons:-Money (i'm bad at managing it)-Call options aren't very descriptive (I asked a man how high up he was and he jumped off and broke his leg)-Gameplay loop-You need to buy the Facilities DLC if your city has ♥♥♥♥ placement of existing facilitiesOverall this game has a lot of pros and cons. It may be your cup of tea, or it may be an absolute dumpster fire for you. You should try it if you wanna, or don't.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't honestly recommend this game.  It is fun at first while you have a small area to cover and take the various calls/etc, being able to cover everything most of the time except when something like a natural disaster happens then you're real buggered for a bit which makes sense.However when you get to the latter stages where you're covering the whole city the fun is completely gone.  You are just utterly overwhelmed by everything, all I hear is 'beep beep beep' every second of the time to announce more incidents occurring and its just headache inducing.  You hire dispatchers to help you cover the city but that is not really the problem as you can pause the game if needed.Issue is you never have enough of anything.  Things progress too quickly to save up properly as you repeatedly get promoted over and over again and each new section of a city you are given comes woefully equipped.  It turns the game into a stressful mess and saps away all the fun very fast.I can see myself playing this for the first 2 or 3 sections of the game but when it gets to the latter parts I will undoubtedly stop and start it again somewhere else.  It doesn't feel like anyone tested this fully for the back parts of the campaign, I'd expect it to be a mess during a natural disaster when a tornado comes through/etc, but even just days where nothing special is happening I at best can cover 90% of the incidents.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The Devs have taken the old reviews into account and the latest update really solves the majority of the problems I initially had with this game. They did a truly fantastic job tweaking the balance so that you earn a bit more money easier, the volume of responses needed on the map feels much more in line with what I was expecting in the first place. Its a lot more fun now and I can't stop playing.This game throws you into the deep end of the pool and doesn’t even ask if you can swim first.Compared to the 1st game 911 Operator this game has gone a few layers deeper in some areas, and come up very shallow in other areas. For example, in the first game you would get a lot of calls every shift to handle, many of them not requiring too much. In 112 almost every call you get is an insanely dire emergency And you get a lot less of them. Maybe even as few as just 1 call in the whole shift. Meanwhile the map is going absolutely bonkers with more crimes and medical needs and insane amounts of fires that it’s impossible to keep up. You don’t earn nearly enough money to even purchase the new units you need to be able to handle the volume of responses needed. The first game handled all of that so much better than this. 112 just feels like a constant game of whack a mole and it takes all the fun out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, it can be a really overwhelming game when about 10 jobs pop up all at once and you have to prioritise them, but it's all a part of the game. It's a massive upgrade from 911 Operator, good job guys! There's a few things that I'm not a huge fan of;1) District Operations - I'm not sure if it's just me but they don't seem to actually help as much as what they could. I understand the levels of the operators but as you seem to personally rank up you just end up having more and more jobs to assign to teams, whereas the operators in each district should be reacting a lot quicker to incoming jobs and assigning them to teams.Something I'd love to see added into this section is possibly for you to actually manage the team of each district? Possibly assign them tasks like what you were given when you first began the career mode. (ie. respond to all pickpocket calls as a priority to bring the statistics down in that area etc.) 2) Assign units to districts - although this is already a thing at the beginning, if you need to take a unit from a different district to help out can they not automatically go back to their original district instead of congregating at the nearest base after finishing a job? The same goes for Police Patrols too, I have some units that just like to go on patrol throughout all districts instead of staying in the area they were assigned to.3) In 911 Operator before your duty began it would show you exactly where a concert, protest or event would be so you could assign units to them and then move around other units to help cover the entire map. This seems to not be the case in 112 and you have to wait for the job to be called in before you can send units - can this be reintroduced?4) When changing equipment of your teams is there a way that process can be more efficient? When you have 50 individual police officers it's so timely to have to click each gun icon to change the equipment. A button to change all would be super helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and will still play for much longer but I think there should be another update that adds some game changing quality of life stuff. The Developers had an anniversary update for year 2, so maybe a year 4 could add some improvements? Although I think the game is pretty much abandoned since they are focusing on new projects.The Main point I want to get across is, I don't think the game is "Finished" yet, as there is still minor bugs and improvements that can be made. In the current state, it is still a game with a cool concept and is still worth checking out, especially the Last Duty DLC which I enjoyed a lot.I dread the prep screen before the Duty starts. Simply because there is no multi-select for the Team Members. I feel like I NEED to swap things around pretty frequently, because I am a micro manager. Since I swap people and the gear around so much its almost annoying and kinda makes me not want to play anymore because its a lot of work when you have 20 swat vans. Being able to remove multiple people on and off units and the ability to swap all their gear at once would be AMAZING! Instead, currently, you have to individually click on each Team Member to change their gear or remove them from the unit. It would be cool if I could just select 10 Team Members that were all police and be able to click on purchase "Swat Gear (Rifle)" with a pop-up saying "Are you sure you want to buy 10 Swat Gear (Rifle) and equip?" with a yes or no button and maybe show a picture of each person you are buying the gear for, and maybe even what unit they are in."Add a Predefined Unit" should have some more customization. It would be cool to make our own presets for purchase, for example if I clicked on the Bicycle Patrol Unit, a Menu would pop up or stretch out and show like a plus button so we could craft our own presets.I think the feature should also be expanded to the already purchased units so we can have some form of Auto Equip.When you buy a Team Member they always come with the Unedited Default Gear. If the Default Gear was edited it will not carry over to when you buy a new person, this is somewhat related to the customization I was referring to earlier. It causes duplicates and is annoying. I think locking the Default Gear so it cant be deleted or edited could be one way to fix it, but making it so we could update the gear would be more of a step in customization.It would be nice to have a new slider in the Audio tab for the Radio Chatter. The Audio slider that the Radio Chatter is affected by is the "Background" Slider. The radio chatter gets repetitively annoying so I turn it way down. But in doing so you also turn down the music. Maybe since the Slider is already named "Background" make a new slider called "Music" instead.Also those adverts would get less hate if they were more discrete/discreet. With maybe just a giant tab at the bottom of the main menu saying "More from us" that you have to hover over to see the other games.I am highly doubtful that this game will be updated, which is why i'm giving a thumbs down, but from what I gathered from the developer responses, they are looking for ways to improve features in their new games, hopefully this is helpful to them!

_childDocuments_.review: This would be fine as a mobile game or if you pick it up in a Humble Bundle or similar but I'd struggle to agree with it having a "campaign" or for picking it up for full price. The comments you can make to influence the story or conversations are limited and you can effectively resolve situations before saying something relating to an earlier response in the conversation and have it all blow up in your face. The dispatchers are less than useless despite them being an objective to recruit and I found myself monitoring and managing each emergency myself anyway, and it's not easy to identify which unit has which gear and therefore who is best suited to each emergency. The "major incidents" seem a bit like they've just been dumped onto the map as well, i.e. a tornado tearing it's way through London is not massively realistic - it would've made more sense to have something that could relate to London (e.g. a tube crash) and every police officer being armed is also a bit off. Also, ACAB, and stop making me send police to deal with loud parties or kettle protestors to provoke incidents. If the campaign was a bit shorter this might have been a positive review but it felt so dragged out by the end of it I was just waiting for it to be over.

_childDocuments_.review: At one level this game is whackamole with consequences. It is however delightfully realised, gives the player tremendous control, allows a level of planning and strategy then hammers you with concurrent urgent tasks that will stretch your resources and eventually force some difficult decisions.That's true of its predecessor, 911 Operator, but here you get to work in multiple European cities, each with familiar layouts and different challenges. Objectives and emails add story elements to the game, campaign objectives are credible, the calls you answer are credible (and at times nasty) and the game is just well designed. There are new top-down scene displays as your emergency services reach an incident. These add a little information that helps determine whether to dispatch more units but primarily add flavour.Overall it's not a style of game I prefer (as I play games to avoid stress, not have it imposed on me) but it's very well done and I am enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Before buying this game, I was a little worried that I would either find it repetitive and boring after a while, or that it become too stressful and frustrating. However, after completing the campaign, I can happily say that it was neither of these things. I found the duties to be neither too long or too short, and the incidents that occurred had an impressive variety. Like many people, I particularly enjoyed the calls that the player handles - the voice acting was superb and believable, and I felt that the decisions I made were really having an impact, even though at the end of the day all it meant was that I got a better Reputation! My only criticism with the calls was that after getting further into the campaign, I no longer answered very many of them as other operators began to handle them instead. The occasional call I did get often didn't seem quite as exciting, as it was usually from another operator providing me with information about some event that was happening instead of the person who called 112 in the first place. I'm yet to try Free Mode, so I'm not sure if this also happens there.The game does a good job of making you feel like you're under pressure whilst still allowing you the ability to pause and work out how to handle things, meaning it caters to a good number of play styles. It's also surprisingly immersive, and I found myself sitting with baited breath as I watched the tactical view more than a few times!My only real criticism of the game is that while the storyline is alright, I think it's maybe lacking just a little bit. There's already an email system built into the game, but I would like to see the player receive messages not only informing them of upcoming events and things to watch out for, but also more that are relevant to various elements of the story. I felt that on occasion, my choices seemed to be forgotten pretty much the day after I made them, so fleshing the story out just a bit more would make it a little more believable.  Following on from this, the game's cutscenes are great (though I've found that they tend to cause my game to freeze for anywhere up to a minute), and so maybe they could be used to explore the player's home life?Aside from that, however, this is - at least in my opinion - an excellent game that I've thoroughly enjoyed so far. The gameplay is engaging and often tense, and the ability to invest in new and different types of units and equipment adds even more strategy to it. Overall, I'd highly recommend this to anyone who's considering getting it (even if you're worried that it might get repetitive after a while, as like I said at the start of this review, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it doesn't!), and I'm excited to see what future updates bring!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the tags for the game is "RTS," and that's an interesting way to put how this game works. The game occurs in stages, with the player being able to use resources to purchase units and equipment, as well as determine their initial location. After that, you are given a map on which problems arise, some of which are just map pop-ups, some of which come in as dialogue trees that you need to navigate to determine the nature of the problem. The latter calls are the the heart of the game, requiring you to be efficient in how you interact with people. These calls are the most interesting part of the game and they're generally quite good, but they're not without their problems. Your options to respond to callers are in 2-4 word summaries, which I found were completely fine for ~80% of the length of the game, but after that some of the time they wouldn't always be what I assumed they were in terms of tone or content. This is especially egregious in a late-game event that has a harsh failure state that you can arrive at in unintuitive ways, but isn't otherwise a major issue. Regardless of call type, you need to send police, fire, and/or medical units to the location, which take time, in order to solve the issues before they become unresolvable. There's a large variety of units and equipment with which to solve these issues, but at least in the campaign I played the variety felt a little empty. I rarely felt like I had sufficient coverage and time to purchase and send specialized units to solve problems, as when I started to get to that point, I gained a larger region to control and had to spread them back out. It'd likely be more interesting in a free play game, or maybe on a harder difficulty, but on normal it felt like specialized units would've been impossible to use effectively. Overall, I enjoyed the experience. The game could get a bit frantic at times, but had a nice flow that I enjoyed. Solid recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great, but suffers heavily from one bad design concept, maps are simply too big. Game is most enjoyable when you play first few hours of campaign. You have small district and quite small respond force, but as the game progresses you equip your men with better equipment, learn the pattern which units belong where and pick most fitting units for the job. But when you start to control the chaos... BAM your district doubles when your forces almost stay the same size. So you have to learn, adapt, equip and reinforce your units. _childDocuments_.review: I would give 112 Operator a mixed/neutral option if possible, but I do think the good outweighs the bad.The core gameplay is fun. You direct police, medics, and firefighters to various emergencies on the map. Sometimes you have to make dispatches while answering a phone call, which is stressful in a good way. The calls are fun and can be educational too, but there aren't very many of them.My biggest complaint is the lack of replay value. There are endless map options, but since the gameplay is the same, it isn't enough to feel fresh for me. There are 8 scenarios, but each is only 2 days long so they're over quickly. The campaign is the biggest disappointment- it seems they're identical, just with different map layouts. 31 days per campaign is also way too long imo.For comparison, in Delivery Inc, each city has its own storyline- Paris with restaurants, Moscow with crime/drug smuggling, etc. Delivery Inc is newer so I assume they refined the formula over time, but that gives players little reason to go back and try their older games.Also, I like the concept of becoming a supervisor and hiring your own dispatchers, but in my campaign on normal difficulty, they were too expensive to be worthwhile. A good idea with poor execution.I think I saw the vast majority of the game after 10 hours, which is rather low. At full price, 112 Operator is definitely not worth it. I think there's enough worthwhile content when it gets a heavy discount. But if you only have enough time for one game, Delivery Inc is far superior.

But the voice acting is good, the visuals and audio are good and the gameplay is easy to pick up. However, it can get tedious very quickly and boring if it's played too often. If it's under $10 I'd say it's a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: **Update 12/17/21:I decided to repurchase the game and give it another shot due to the positive reviews people are posting and the developer's suggestion. After playing 24 hours worth of game at 31 duties at the time of this writing, I suggest everyone play on EASY MODE for the CAMPAIGN MODE even if you have 911 operator experience on expert. Additionally, SLOW the game down or even pause it. It allows you to have almost 100% efficiency to the point where you will dispatch even before the auto-dispatch kicks in (you don't even need those dispatchers). It makes the game more manageable. Another tip is that add as much vehicles as you can before every duty. Max it out (with cheat codes for money). That makes a big difference in the game. I found out that 112 operator is much more enjoyable on EASY mode after 911 operator but I wouldn't play 112 operator before 911 operator. The diffrence being is that the districts are constantly added in the campaign mode and so, if you are not used to it, it can get overwhelming quick! The developers did release a major update to balance the calls with having fun in the game but even then, it takes an hour for me to finish each duty, but I found myself having more fun than in 911 operator. --------------------------------------------Did not like this game after playing 911 Operator (60+ hours on 911 operator). It was simple enough at the beginning where you respond to unique calls. I like how it automatically pairs the strongest driver automatically in each car. Also drones that can scan 4 squares at once is cool. HOWEVER, after 2 hours of playing the campaign, the map gets progressively bigger and bigger as you advance, to the point where it was not fun anymore and you're not even focused on the calls but just dispatching mindlessly. _childDocuments_.review: Great sequel to 911 Operator that I played just before playing this one. It improved everything in every way except a few. 1) For the campaign, you're only allowed to play on one map. Unlike 911 where you get a varied selection of maps, keeping this interesting and new. Instead, you slowly unlock "districts" in the city you select. It makes the maps much bigger than the previous game, but for better or worse is up to you. The campaign is also 32 days long, so spending that long on the same map got boring imo. Personally, I prefer the smaller, sectioned maps of 911. 2) Since it's a bigger map, I think the devs decided to up the spawn of incidents. Given that you can buy an unlimited amount of units to place on the map. However, in later campaign days, the incidents go crazy. Almost literally 1 incident per second. I understand they wanted to go for realism and not being able to do EVERYTHING all at once and to ignore the smaller offences like drivers going past red lights or speeding etc, but you get negative reputation if you do ignore them. All-in-all, it made the later game very frustrating.3) Speaking of the later game, I think the game was too long as well. And you can kind of tell they padded it out a bit as the actual 112 calls you get almost cease to exist after a certain point. For the last 10-15 days of 32 day campaign, you're only responding to incidents and calls from your superiors. Or maybe the devs figured since you were promoted and can hire other operators that you were too-high in position to answer every 112 call that wasn't immediately urgent? Either way, the 112 calls are basically the biggest draw of the game to me. There should've been lots more imo.  I had a good time. At least in the early game. I got annoyed and was waiting for it to be over in the later half of the game. If I ever find the itch to play one of these games again, I think I'll stick to 911 operator. As after playing both, it's my preferred one. But this one is still worth checking out and despite my grievances above, like I mentioned in the first sentence, it did improve on everything else. Graphics, unit variances (despite A LOT of them being useless), controls etc.

No, it doesn't crash all the time, but you are still stuck with managing with far fewer resources than you actually need to handle 2/3 of the problems.First few days are fine, but soon you will find yourself wishing you have another couple of units, then a few more, then you'll realize you need another 15 to 20 units just to not miss half the calls.Add to this you're -forced- to expand your play are every successful day, and the problems magnify fast.I started in southern New Hampshire with one town.   Soon I was trying to manage the entire southwestern state (25 towns) with the emergency resources of two towns. That impacts your income significantly, meaning you don't have enough money to buy the two or three police cars you need, and that's often a mission goal too, so next day you'll miss even more calls because you're spread out even more with even fewer resources.The entire thing is a mismanagement nightmare.   Jutsu, maybe bring the income levels up to more than 13k a day?   Until the income to cost ratio is balanced better, 1/5 stars only because i can't give you negative stars.Like you keep docking my pay for reasons you caused.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Much more control. The first game, 911 Operator, had a simple premise, you get given a city to take calls from and then dispatch Police, Fire or Medic units (or no one) in response, now you not only do that, but you also assign other dispatchers to districts and expand your control to larger areas as you progress, being in control of all the emergency services in a place like Berlin or London is a daunting but thrilling task.- More focused campaign. The campaign of 911 Operator was simple, there was a list of cities and you had to complete an in-game day or two running the services in each one before moving on to the next, now the campaign is set in a single major city (you can pick which one out of a choice of many) which you run for around 30 in-game days, starting you off in a relatively small area then gradually expanding your control to neighbouring districts until you’re an incident manager for everything, being invested in a single city allows you to develop its services more and makes the campaign feel more committed, and there are also several storylines and objective sets that develop across multiple days to give a greater sense of continuity.- Great calls. The calls you as an operator receive are varied and often intense, with lots of different choices to make that can leave people coming out of the incident alive or in a body bag depending on your advice, they feel a lot more engaging than those in 911 Operator.- On site visualisation. When you send units to an incident, you now can access an “on site” tab where you can see what your first responders are doing in the moment (removing debris, rescuing victims, getting involved in shootouts, etc etc), down to being able to see all the individual names of the responders, the people they interact with and the actions taken, this makes incidents feel much more believable and adds to immersion.- Greater challenge. The gameplay’s ever increasing scale makes it much more challenging than 911 Operator, as you manage more and more units and territory and have to face more incidents at once, with potential for things to tumble out of control and to end up with more incidents than units to address them, making for tough choices on who to save and stop and who to abandon.Cons- Voice acting. The voice acting isn’t bad, for the most part its well done, but the problem is it isn’t region specific, your dispatcher and most callers will be Americans despite the focus of the game being European cities, whether you are in charge of Berlin, London, Moscow or Paris your population will be American, of course this being a crowdfunded indie game there are understandably limitations on how diverse of a voice cast there can be, but it is kind of immersion breaking to see given the game’s European focus.- Weather events can be excessive. The game loves to throw curveballs and one of them is weather events that disrupt gameplay and complicate unit management, this is a great fun element, but one part of it that is implemented poorly is snow, if there’s a lot of snow on a given day you can run into situations where any unit you send to an incident will end up getting stuck in the snow and unable to respond, over and over and over again, leading to a string of failures that aren’t the player’s fault, there’s no problem with throwing this curveball a bunch of times, but when it’s so often it makes gameplay unfun that can be an issue.Imagine 911 Operator but made with a bigger budget and more polished design, that’s this game, the campaign feels a lot more thought out than the first game, there’s more detail, experimentation with your role (going from humble dispatcher to the incident manager for an entire city) and more variety in the units you can call in, very well done game worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: is a riveting and highly engaging emergency management simulation developed by  and published by . This sequel to the acclaimed 911 Operator expands on its predecessor by offering a larger scale, more detailed emergencies, and a global reach.After spending 65.4 hours with 112 Operator, I can confidently say that it offers one of the most immersive experiences in the genre. The game places you in the role of an emergency dispatcher, where you must manage resources, respond to a variety of incidents, and make critical decisions that can save lives. The strategic depth of the game is impressive, requiring you to allocate your units effectively, manage resources, and respond to an escalating series of emergencies.The UI provides a comprehensive overview of your assigned district, showing the locations of police stations, hospitals, and firehouses. You can pre-position your units to ensure maximum coverage, which helps mitigate the chaos as your shift progresses. With over 60 new types of emergencies, the game keeps you on your toes, dealing with everything from minor accidents to major disasters.One of the standout features of 112 Operator is its realistic and often emotionally charged scenarios. The voice acting and sound effects enhance the immersion, making each call feel urgent and real. I vividly remember handling a call from someone stuck on a railway track with an oncoming train, the panic in the caller's voice, and the sound of the train's horn growing louder was incredibly tense. Such moments are plentiful and add a significant emotional weight to the game.The game’s difficulty curve is well-balanced, offering a steady increase in complexity that keeps you engaged. Managing multiple districts with various ongoing incidents requires not only quick reflexes but also strategic foresight. The game's ability to simulate the high-pressure environment of an emergency dispatcher is commendable. Each decision you make has consequences, which are detailed in the post-shift report, providing valuable feedback and areas for improvement.Despite its many strengths, 112 Operator is not without its flaws. The visibility of units can sometimes be an issue, making it difficult to track which resources are available and which are not. Additionally, the game can become quite stressful, especially during prolonged sessions, which might not appeal to everyone. The interface, while streamlined, can still feel overwhelming due to the sheer volume of information and decisions you need to make., 112 Operator is an excellent game for those who enjoy management simulations and high-stakes decision-making. Its realistic scenarios, strategic depth, and immersive gameplay make it a standout title in the simulation genre. If you are ready to take on the intense and rewarding challenge of managing emergency services, this game is well worth your time.For more details, check out the game's .

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator: A Real-Time Strategy ChallengeRating: 4/5112 Operator is a unique simulation game that puts you in the role of an emergency services dispatcher. The gameplay is immersive and stressful, accurately reflecting the pressures of real-life emergency management. The voice acting adds to the realism, making each call feel urgent and important.However, the game has its flaws. It can become repetitive with a consistent cycle of calls, and the map can feel crowded, making it somewhat challenging to navigate. Despite this, the added control features for directing units offer a level of finesse and strategy that keeps the game engaging.The game also introduces weather conditions and day-night cycles, adding an extra layer of challenge and unpredictability. These features make each playthrough unique, ensuring that no two games are the same.In conclusion, while 112 Operator has its shortcomings, its unique premise and engaging gameplay make it a worthy addition to the library of any simulation or strategy game enthusiast. Despite some repetition, it offers a compelling and rewarding experience that is hard to put down.

There are dozens of vehicle types, each supposedly with their own specialists, different worker types with different ratings for different activities and different cities with different regions.  Sadly very few of these differences make a blind bit of difference to game play.One fire truck is more or less as good as any other for 95% of incidents, some police vehicles are slightly faster than others but only just, same with medical units.  Sure bike do not having capacity to carry arrested or injured parties (so why bother buying them) and large police wagons are handy when you get to shoot outs (but are slow and require redundant officers any other time) but they are so situational as to not really matter.In terms of the map, there is the promise of different zones being different as the stats to view past crimes per zone is there but they bear no relation to what future crime is like so are useless, and finally in terms of actual incidents they play out very similar in each game so even replay-ability is low.Take the idea, make the differences bigger, make the stakes higher and you would have something worth the effort, sadly this isn't there.
