_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you played 911 Operator, 112 Operator will basically be a more in-depth version for you. If you haven't, I would suggest doing increased research before buying this game, because 112 is a lot to handle sometimes, and I would suggest playing the first game first, AND THEN playing 112 when you think you've gotten the hang of everything.112 Operator is a pretty good game, a definite four stars. The UI is clean and the gameplay is fun, and pretty much free of any large (and even small!) noticeable glitches and bugs. However, there is still one overwhelming thing about this game that I don't like: the amount of side tasks to complete. If you played the first game (911 Operator), you'd know that you'll get calls, and side tasks that pop up at the bottom of the screen that you simply just assign units to, and would be done with. While that does still exist in 112, they OVERLOAD you with side tasks, so many that the game is REALLY HARD to play (even for an experienced player like myself!) on a sped up setting. It's crazy, and makes features like the 3D Modeling of situations that are unfolding basically redundant, because by the time that you've finished watching, you'll have 50 other side tasks that you'll have to complete. This is a big problem, and kind of makes the game 20% less fun. Nevertheless, I still really enjoy 112 Operator, and will surely keep playing, as well as would recommend this game to a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game! It's not something I play all the time, but a game I quite often come back to. Yes there are bugs and frustrations sometimes, but nothing major (except the dispatchers issue). It's definitely worth the price, and the DLC's are normally worth downloading to enhance the experience. Things that need to be improved:-Return Fire resources to their assigned base location immediately after an incident. I try to work on a realistic framework of wanting fire appliances to return to their base fire station once an incident has been concluded, however, despite the fact this has been input for police returning to their original patrol route, this hasn't been done for fire and ambulance, which for me, is more important than the police one. -BETTER dispatchers, this is my biggest frustration! I have found consistently that I am better off having one low level dispatcher covering the entire city area, than trying to have 4 high-level dispatchers to assist with tasks. The mechanics of the game do not seem to like multiple dispatchers, which takes away the point of having the ability to split your city districts to different dispatchers. Their number of tasks per minute seems pointless with this issue. And a few things I would like to see, personally,-Being able to combine districts in your city for easier assigning of dispatchers to areas, and assigning of resources. I understand the way some of the areas have been split, but where the dispatchers search within these boundaries first for an incident, it takes too long for them to recognise a resource who is closer, but just outside of the boundary of the incident, despite being controlled by the same dispatcher. If you could merge districts, this would make assigning dispatchers far easier, rather than having to go through each individual district one by one to assign. Or at least an easier way to assign a dispatcher to multiple districts.-On the above, I'd like to have colour co-ordination available as an overlay whilst in game mode, to show the district areas, so that it can be easily visualised who has control of areas, whilst sill seeing available resources, as this would really help to visualise the area, and who has control of what, whilst seeing where your units are that they have control of, and type of unit available. -Ability to focus on one emergency service, rather than all 3 - Most European control rooms only deal with one service. Or at least more control over which service incidents appear more often, so that the tri-service incidents can still appear. -More editing capabilities built into the actual game for call modifications, rather than relying on people knowing how to edit files. There's lots of things that might be realistic in other countries, but are very rare in places like the UK. for example; It would be nice to be able to turn off guns being spawned or reduce the gun spawn rate, without having to trawl through the files for hours editing. And also change who takes responsibility for certain calls, for example, in the UK, a vehicle blocking a roadway is not a fire service issue, but a police one. -Stop sending firetrucks to search incidents. I really can't figure out the mechanics behind this. I've tried turning off the search radius and ability of fire resources, and increasing them on police, but for some reason, fire units get sent to search for wanted criminals. This is not realistic. The search parameters need to be based only on what service takes responsibility for the outcome. If it's the "fire seen" incident, then fire units should be dispatched to it. If it's a missing person, then it's police, if its an alzheimers patient, it's ambulance, etc etc, rather than constantly sending fire engines to incidents that they then shout "Need police assistance", for an armed person.-Easier way to set the call spawn rate, without having to input a cheat code. This would allow people to find their ideal call rate for the number of units they have. Those are the things I would like to see, but even though there's a few frustrations in their, the game is still playable and enjoyable, as shown by my 153hours current play time (which will be going up today to trial the new water incidents DLC).Just, please, don't stop working on this game and keep improving it and throwing more DLC out there!Definitely a 8/10 (with potential only to go up with minor improvements), and would recommend to anyone who likes emergency services, and management style game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked 911 operator you will love this game, simple as that. There are major upgrades to the UI, the difficulty scales through the campaign as you gain more districts, and the game likes to throw challenges at you in the form of special events like concerts or tornadoes.With that being said I do have a few bits of feedback that I am going to mention because the developer is very active on Steam and I hope they see them. This is a common thread through a lot of reviews and whilst I appreciate the developer seems to have done this on purpose to force you prioritise, it's just too much. There are times when you are bombarded with incidents that you just can't deal with and it ruins the fun of the game reducing the amount of time I feel comfortable playing. It makes it not fun, there is a difference between pushing players and overwhelming them so I would say this needs a little bit of balancing. once you get to a certain point you can hire dispatchers to run regions for you, you can even assign them to multiple regions and have them manage whole sections of the city for you. Meaning you only have to deal with the major incidents. For me the system was poorly explained and just didn't do anything. Assigning dispatchers over multiple territories is difficult and tedious and I didn't notice a drop in my work load. Maybe if this worked better it would make my first point moot. In-game units warn you of problems by speaking to you, these pop-up as text on the map so that you can see what needs to be sorted. I constantly got these when they weren't required. "Medical unit needed" from the ambulance picking up the casualties, things like that (and no they didn't need extra capacity). This again just makes the game feel less fun as you are constantly being harangued by your own units and again just feels overwhelming at times.As I said at the start if you love 911 operator (as I did) you will love this. And with a few tweaks and updates this would be a perfect game but it does have a few small teething problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in to this game with high hopes, because the the concept of being an emergency dispatcher in a video game sounded great on paper.  In practice, not so much.  Like other reviewers have pointed out, there are two major flaws with this game.First, it forces you to unlock new zones whether you're ready for them or not.  I was surprised to see this in the sandbox/freeplay mode where I just wanted to play a single zone to get the hang of the game and the mechanics, but as I'm trying to learn, it's forcing more zones and therefore more incidents and calls to deal with while I'm still trying to figure out the gear system or what units to place and where.Second, it becomes repetitive immediately.  It's built in to the core concept of the game...you're an emergency dispatcher.  You're doing the same thing over and over.  This would be a hard concept to pull off in a video game, and 112 doesn't quite accomplish that.One other complaint I had about this game was that it's not very clear on what units to place where, or how to do things like change out your personnel gear.  I didn't figure out the gear until about 3 hours in.  By then I was just about bored with the game already.  As for unit type and placement, I basically just bought the regular cop cars, ambulances, and firetrucks and put them everywhere and that covered 99% of my needs, I wouldn't buy the specialty units unless an objective popped up for it.  At one point I kept getting blocked from buying more predefined units because I didn't have enough personnel, never did figure out how to address that because by this point I was 5-6 hours in to the game and had lost all interest in continuing because I was just burning through calls, finish that stage, load next stage, get forced to take on more zones, burn through more calls, repeat...over and over again.  There's nothing else to it.Had this game not been given to me by a buddy, I would have refunded it in the first 2 hours at 25 bucks.  No depth, repetitive right from the start, and apart from occasional AI emails telling you "good job!" it's really not all that rewarding as you progress.  I couldn't recommend this game for more than a couple dollars, to be used as filler/time killer in between other more fulfilling games.

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a fantastic game for those who enjoy a more relaxed, yet engaging gaming experience. It didn’t take long for me to get completely hooked—what started as a casual session quickly turned into hours of addictive gameplay. The game brilliantly balances strategy and management, placing you in the shoes of an emergency services dispatcher responsible for saving lives.The gameplay is simple to grasp but offers enough depth to keep you invested. Managing resources, prioritizing calls, and responding to emergencies in real-time create a unique sense of responsibility and immersion. It’s the kind of game where you can lose track of time as you get absorbed in making critical decisions and seeing the consequences play out.What makes "112 Operator" stand out is its ability to be both challenging and chill at the same time. You can approach it at your own pace, making it perfect for when you want to unwind but still feel mentally stimulated. Whether you’re handling routine incidents or sudden large-scale disasters, the game keeps you on your toes in the most enjoyable way.Overall, "112 Operator" is a gem for anyone looking for a fun and relaxing game that still offers plenty of excitement. It’s easy to get hooked, and before you know it, hours will have flown by as you manage your virtual city’s emergencies. Definitely a must-try for fans of strategy and management games!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first game a lot but thought it was perhaps a little too short so I bought the sequel full of excitement and got a mixed reaction. Positives: - Definitely longer than the first game- More things to do- Creative features- More interesting storyline overallNegatives:- Unless you have a supercomputer the game will lag and crash in later levels. My computer is older and the later levels are almost completely unplayable due to crashing/lagging- The sequel is perhaps a little overambitious adding cutscenes and a LOT more units to control. Again that doesnt help the crashing/lagging problem- The 3D models of buildings once again don't help the lagging/crashing problemOverall I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoyed the first game and want more 911 operator content (also if you have a great computer) but I'm disappointed that I probably won't be able to complete it due to technical issues. For the price I feel like I got half a game due to the crashing/lagging. I'm disappointed but the part that I actually WAS able to play was very good. 3/5

_childDocuments_.review: If you thoroughly enjoyed playing 911 Operator and are contemplating whether to purchase 112 Operator, I wholeheartedly recommend it. After pondering for a few years, I finally took the plunge and have no regrets. The interface has undergone significant improvements since 911 Operator, and the game mechanics now offer a wealth of additional content.One notable enhancement is the inclusion of a weather forecast feature, which adds an extra layer of strategy as you anticipate the necessary forces for the next day. The interaction system has been streamlined, making it both easier and more engaging. Personally, I'm delighted that I can now easily discern the driver of a car, as the member with the highest driving skill is indicated with a special marker.However, I'm currently grappling with one minor challenge: I haven't yet discovered if there are shortcuts for changing the game speed. It would be fantastic if keys 1-3 could be utilized for this purpose. It's worth noting that I may not have explored all the features in the game, so there's a possibility that shortcuts exist and I simply haven't found them yet.Overall, if you enjoyed the predecessor, 112 Operator is a worthy investment with its enhanced interface, expanded content, and improved gameplay mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I played previous 911 operator, I enjoyed it a lot. But somehow this feels like a worse version of the original.Problems:- it doesnt seem to be so different from previous game, more like dlc - core gameplay is identical, its just bigger now and with few new disasters (that of course rarely appears)- there is still no easy way to compare detailed statistics of staff. Why? And why is it in decimal? Nobody wants to hover mouse over individual staff and compare 7 decimal numbers. Why not to use 5 stars rating?- number of incidents is too high (playing on Normal). I would expect Normal difficulty should be ok for most of players, especially 911 veterans. But its not. The struggle with not having enough money/staff is worse here than in 911. Whats the point of having warning emails about upcoming problems, when I am broke and cant prepare anyway?- mostly cant use top tier stuff: usually games present you with new stuff that you can try NOW. Here I get notification about a new 200 000$ helicopter, while I have 20 000. And since I am always low on staff/vehicles, I am forced to spend it on low tier vehicles, so I will never make enough money to have cool stuff. I am so glad save files are just a JSON files, so I can balance it myself.- stacked units. Its bigger now, More units, Map zoomed out more. Why doesnt a grid or something appear when I hover over stacked units, so I could see what is there?- lack of UI elements: its big now, I need to be able to filter and order units by vehicle type, I want to have filter to see idle units, units of certain vehicle type, highlight units (its routes) sent to incident with a distinctive color when clicking on a incident (not a bold white line/borderline, something more visible)- sometimes not getting info on a incident report page what could be done better (why only 7 out of 10 points etc)New features- new feature: dispatcher. So you make a bigger map (more work) and then allow players to delegate work to dispatchers (less work)? But why... that cancels each other.- new feature: bigger map. You get more and more districts as you play, so you struggle with money/staff shortage and as a "reward" for your career it gets even worse? Well, thanks.- new feature: districts and its statistics. Really? Clicking one by one to see one very detailed district statistics (when I have 20)? With numbers and percentage? Please reduce risk chance to 5 stars system, remove frequency, I want to have fun, not do math. Possibly add graphs to easily compare districts.

You'll pull out your hair with how many calls you get, but it's hard to actually lose with how forgiving the game is and how many reputation points you get. That said, it's a great successor to 911 Operator. My biggest gripe is there isn't a true 'free mode' There should be a mode where you get 10 million dollars to build up your emergency forces how you please and choose disasters to go against just to test it.

_childDocuments_.review: During the Civil Protection course, both the firefighters and Paramedics that trained us, said that they value our assistance to keep the situation under control until their arrival. And in this game you can clearly see why, there are no unlimited resources to answer every single call, and sometimes even real emergencies end up in queue for several minutes or even hours due to the long distance or just priorities. I guess I value this game because it encourage us to be more prepared to handle all types of emergencies, not to be the heroes or anything, but to give the real professionals that bit of extra time to come and handle the situation.
_childDocuments_.name: 112 Operator

_childDocuments_.review: The basic principle is okay and exciting - you assign emergency personnel to different incidents and take calls on the side. The calls are quite interesting at first, since you also have to give instructions from the 1st aid. In the end, however, the dialogs repeat themselves constantly and you just click more or less blindly and annoyed on the answer options and hope that the conversation finally ends, so that you can devote yourself to the rest again - send fire department, police, emergency service to their missions.At the beginning, the whole thing is still clear, but later it's just a huge chaos. It feels like every second three more missions pop up on a huge map. However, all of the emergency services are on the way or far away - in principle, you have no chance to cope with everything. The difficulty levels hardly make a difference. On "easy" you only get to this point later, while on "hard" you basically already start like this.The game is also not really clearly arranged. The further you get, the more vehicles are on the road. Sometimes they pile up on top of each other and it is impossible to see who is doing what and who is currently free. You can zoom into the map, but then you miss the thousand new cases that appear somewhere else every second.The predecessor of this game is supposed to be more balanced. Maybe it's worth taking a look at it.I found this review here and I really agreee with it so I copy&paste it here in english.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game but I give it a big recommend! I think it's a good improvement from the previous game (even though I liked that one too) From reading some of the reviews I noticed a few things that got brought up a lot and figured I'd put down my own opinion on them, in no particular order: -Bad performance/Stuttering Did not experience this at all, I have a middle ground pc and usually have some demanding stuff open in the background (I'm an artist so things like photoshop, CSP or even video editing software is usually open) Maybe this is something that has been patched and improved on. -Repeating callsHaven't had a single repeating on but I'm also not that many hours in the game (will update should this change) -Not enough resources/too many incidents While I do agree that It's hard to expand your police/ambulance/firefighter force I wouldn't put down that as a negative(once again take it with a grain of salt considering I only have 7 ish hours) but there are times in the work day there you get bombarded with incidents but I've never had too hard of a time missing/timing out too many of them, maybe 1-2 a day. Been able to add about 1 new squad/unit per day and I seem to have pretty decent coverage. Don't have that much more too say than that

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was quite excited about this game, as someone who has lots of playtime hours on 911 Operator, i was looking forward to this game, as the trailers promised a lot of variety and fun.Well, that was partly the case.We'll start of with the good aspects:The new Special cases and Wildfires are a really cool addition to the game, and (assuming you play on easy difficulty, which I'll get to later) the game is a partly brain demanding, but still fun game. ...For the first 2 hours or so.When you see the Interface for the first time letting you choose all these different cities of all around europe, you get really excited, hoping to play all of them and learning while you go, as cities get harder and harder. That is not the case. Throughout the first playthrough, this game is a blast, having to deal with all different kinds of emergencys and really thrilling special events. The E-Mail system is great, too. But when you get to the second city, you realise that ALL cases and special ceses are exactly the same. ALL cities have the same old boring cases and the same old special cases from the ones before. You realise that the cities only differenciate from the map they are structured on.Well, you say to yourself "this isnt so bad though, there are still many more difficulties i can try". And then you realise that increasing your difficulty doesnt make the case harder, it just gives you more of them. Instead of that broken Hydrant requiring longer time for your fire team, and them requiring further units, you just end up with 5 other simple cases, the old boring ones, in that matter. You get the point.So then you say "well the game is a bit difficult, but there are still all these scenarios"aaaaaaaaaaand you realise the scenarios are just special cases from the campaign broken up into different maps and games. And again, the difficulty increase just gives you more incidents to worry about.So you are left with two options: Cry in the corner and never touch this game again, or buy DLCAnd there is a LOT of DLC for this game, especially considering there will probably be more in the future.So you better get on buying that, or you will be stuck with us, paying for a 20€ game and only really receiving 15-20h of playtime after it just gets plain boring.Conclusion: Exciting at first, but just gets boring as its the same missions over and over again. Not worth the money. Play 911 Operator, I'ts cheaper and more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it was both funny and realistic how water cannons give a boost for extinguishing fires, and the story lines told through the calls (and occasionally the ones in the emails) can be engaging or at least interesting, i thought it was more humanizing to the player character when i got to skip a duty because my player character's actual daughter called 112 to talk to him because she was sick. that's about all the good things i have to say about this game. there are glitches to be found when trying to manage equipment and the game feels very unfinished. the riots, protests, forest fires, and water incidents are not as interactive or fleshed-out as they deserve to be, and in real life you can't extinguish every area fire in one day. some decisions were questionable at best. also this game deserves officer transport busses (for riots) and they should bring back prison transports cars with 6 seats for criminals. helicopters can't land on the water in real life. Police horses should be able to be strategically redeployed with pickup truck trailers, as they are in real life. police horses should give a boost to pacification, as they do in real life. the operators you hire are more often making your life more difficult than making it easy (unless i'm just stupid). they cancelled my order to send support to neighboring cities at least 10 times, causing me to lose reputation every time. this game took my expectations of a better "911 Operator" and crushed them. also sometimes it takes way too long to calculate the entire city's roads, and sometimes when expanding your city, certain waterways may just disappear. I hope in the future they take this criticism into account and create a truly wonderful game called something like "999 operator" or whatever. Ultimately this is a half-baked game.This is not an exhaustive list of my criticisms of this game.By the time you're reading this, if there's another sequel yet, skip this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "112 Operator" is a simulation game developed by Jutsu Games that puts players in the shoes of an emergency services dispatcher. Building upon its predecessor, "911 Operator," this title offers a more extensive and refined experience, allowing players to manage emergency calls and resources across various cities around the world.Realistic Emergency Dispatch Simulation (4/5):"112 Operator" excels at creating a realistic experience. Players are tasked with managing a wide range of emergency situations, from medical emergencies and fires to criminal incidents and natural disasters. The game does an impressive job of immersing players in the high-pressure world of emergency services. It requires quick thinking, resource allocation, and multitasking skills as you juggle multiple ongoing crises.Varied Gameplay and Challenges (4/5):The game presents a diverse range of scenarios, each with its own set of challenges. From coordinating fire and police responses to guiding paramedics through life-saving procedures over the phone, "112 Operator" keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging. The addition of day-night cycles and dynamic weather further adds to the complexity and realism of each situation.Global Locations (4/5):One of the notable improvements over its predecessor is the inclusion of various international cities, each with its unique characteristics and challenges. This diversity adds depth to the gameplay, as different cities require different strategies and approaches to effectively manage emergencies. It also provides an educational aspect, as players learn about the geographical and cultural nuances of each location.Learning Curve (3/5):"112 Operator" can be quite challenging, especially for newcomers. The game's mechanics, while realistic, may overwhelm players initially. The learning curve can be steep, and it may take some time to become proficient at efficiently handling emergencies and deploying resources. However, for players who enjoy a steep challenge, this can be a rewarding aspect of the game.Graphics and Presentation (3/5):While the game's graphics are functional, they don't stand out as particularly impressive. The user interface is informative but could benefit from a bit more polish. However, the focus of "112 Operator" is on gameplay and simulation, and the visuals serve their purpose adequately.Conclusion:"112 Operator" is an engaging and realistic emergency services simulation game that offers players a taste of the high-pressure world of dispatchers. It successfully builds upon the foundation laid by its predecessor, providing a more extensive and diverse experience. While the learning curve may be a bit steep for newcomers, those who appreciate challenging simulations and want to experience the complexity of coordinating emergency responses will find "112 Operator" to be a rewarding and immersive experience. It's a game that offers a unique perspective on the vital work of emergency services personnel.

_childDocuments_.review: Blimey, the maps are HUGE and there are lots of them! You start with a small district and after a few promotions you're serving an entire city (with a help of a bit dimwitted assistants). Although the maps' sizes are very impressive, other aspects could use more attention.   The units' pathfinding is, unfortunately, quite jerky and sometimes results in a situations where your police car instead of chasing an offender, goes "180" about 6-10 times before actually deciding to complete their pursue. In other situations they just have issues finding the shortest route and it results in a really long detour (during which they might fail some of the calls).  The background chatter is pretty good, alas, it could use a little more diversity. Hearing a report about a church fire 6 times in 2 minutes is a little too much (there is an option to decrease the background audio, but i really enjoy listening to it sometimes and having more than 5 reports would be really awesome).  Nonetheless, the game is really impressive and is a proper sequel to the 911 operator. There're new vehicles, new gear and, most importantly, — new incidents! Really worth the money, especially with the sweat -33% discount that's active until 9th of July.P.S. "I neeeed somebody, not just aanybodyy"

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wondering whether this game is worth the price, it is.I've played a lot of 911 operator and I really enjoyed the game. This is the sequel and it is a big step forward, building on the original and adding improved and new gameplay elements.As always there are really interesting calls to take where you have to manage tense situations under pressure.In addition, there is a really engaging career mode where you start out with one district and work your way up the ladder to become the head of operators. As part of this process, you'll receive specific objectives which will lead to promotions down the line.The career mode also features emails, weather information, events, etc. which makes 112 feel more immersive compared to 911 and really gets you invested in the experience.As you advance, you'll be given the responsibility to manage more districts and unlock more units. As with 911 operator, you have to spend your budget wisely. This includes purchasing a range of vehicles, hiring personnel, and outfitting them with equipment.One thing that I love is the new information overlays that you can enable, and among other things you can label your teams. That means you can create your own specialist units and give them specific names to keep track of where they are.In general there is a lot more information available, and the game makes it clear what the consequences of doing or not doing something was.In addition to the improvements mentioned above there are loads of quality of life improvements. This includes lots of little improvements compared to 911 which you'll discover as you play the game.  I would highly recommend buying 112 operator, both for players that played the original and for newcomers to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had potential to be excellent. Unfortunately, this was a case of taking a great thing and rather than improving on it, making it so large and heavy it no longer has positive returns but rather takes away from the things that make the game good. Districts are a great idea on paper, but in practice, my map is approximately 350 square kilometers of region to handle. In freemode, there's no way to disable this (unless you play on child's mode that takes away much of the fun of the game). I think one of the best summaries of what this game is like comes from the game itself: I have to send a fire crew to repair fire hydrants, but I have to send the fire trucks back to the station to refill water when they run out of water on the truck. That is an absolutely perfect analogy. The balance is bad, the execution falls flat. It can be fixed in the future and I hope it is, but the multitude of patches since release have done little to make the game worth buying for anyone besides hardcore fans of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: It makes a lot of fun and has a good challenge to it. Especially the ability to change the level of difficulty helps getting a good entry into the game and advancing the difficulty  together with your  abilities without having trouble of being stuck at a point where one difficulty is to easy whilst the next is to hard like with some games. There are some annoying factors though. For instance some playthroughs not only start in a storm but stick in a storm for, what would be 4 or 5 days in game where you are unable to use certain units, and whilst in the mid to end game this isn't as much of a problem, in the early game the given bike units are quite usefull and are, depending on the situation, hard to impossible to replace without calling in reinforcements for the shift. Also, there is the naming of 112/911 calls. Sometimes it just doesn't take the name entered and there is no need nor time to enter a description. Furthermore it is not uncommon, that you have units right arround the corner and therefore no time to even name it without switching to the situation overview whilst typing. Somehow I managed to cancel calls that way because it switched mid typing and I hit some button that just aborted the call without all the units needed even ariving at the scene. _childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a truly unique and engaging simulation game that I absolutely love. It offers an immersive experience where you take on the role of an emergency dispatcher, managing calls and coordinating first responders to various incidents. The game’s focus on supporting first responders and highlighting their crucial work is both educational and deeply engaging.One of the standout features of 112 Operator is its realism and attention to detail. The game accurately simulates the challenges faced by emergency services, from dealing with everyday incidents to handling large-scale emergencies. The variety of scenarios keeps the gameplay fresh and challenging, requiring quick thinking and efficient resource management.I particularly appreciate the game's global scope, allowing you to play in cities around the world, each with unique challenges and emergencies. The ability to manage different types of incidents, from medical emergencies to crime and natural disasters, adds depth to the experience.112 Operator is not only entertaining but also offers a meaningful look into the important work of emergency services. It’s a game that fills a niche and does so exceptionally well, making it a standout in the simulation genre. I wish there were more games like this that shine a light on the vital roles of first responders. If you're looking for a unique and rewarding simulation game, 112 Operator is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I found It really fun and novel at first. The small little story lines of crimes you get like the crossbow killer and the school gas leak add nice flavor to experience as well and I enjoyed the small scale that allows you to get more invested in each case you are sending officers into and taking calls for. It'd  all make for a good 2 or 3 small little game. The problem is it isn't only 2 or 3 hours. As the campaign progresses you get the feeling oh they are going to make it more interesting by gradually introducing more types of disasters with unique was of handling them with instances like the tornados and large fires which I liked however that's all they introduce in vanilla at least. No the the main method of ramping it up they actually use is spamming you with small scale scenarios and shootouts which quickly become tedious and annoying souring the entire experience making the game feel more like a chore of pause click pause click pause click over and over again till the day finishes with no time to actually care about any of it. Overall pick it up on sale its a good 2 hours experience but I cannot recommend it full price as the full experience past the begging is just eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeehhhhhhhhhhhhhh and quickly outwears its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator caught me by surprise. Some of the calls get pretty intense and have me thinking, "I can't believe they are allowed to put this in a video game." The RTS gameplay is also fun. Especially in the beginning.This game doesn't scale well, though. As you get further into the game, the spawn rates of call increase while at the same time you also unlock more districts that you have to manage. On the other hand, you income grows rather slowly and is almost constant compared to the growth of calls. This means that you will exponentially gain more calls while your force increases linearly by just a few cars each day.To offset this growth, the game offers you the ability to use AI dispatchers that send units to calls. That sounds cool in principle, but it is completely useless in-game. The AI doesn't take into consideration of the vehicle or gear of your units. This means that you  have SWAT teams pulling people over while patrol car after patrol car is massacred attempting to stop a street gang. In the end, you will never use the dispatcher.Overall, much of the gear is useless in the game too. But you wouldn't know this because the game doesn't explain how any of the stats work. I spent maybe close to 4 hours of my game time just browsing the discussion in the Steam overlay trying to figure out what everything does. The only useless guide is written by a dev (or an associate of the developers), but that guide is a sugar-coated copy of the in-game explanations.To further my point at how basic this game truly is, the legitimate strategy recommended by 911 Operator veterans is to spam patrol cars, fire pickup trucks, and the largest ambulance. Volume.It's all about the volume of your force. Meticulously doing things only works in the early-game of your run.Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: You’re an operator at an emergency center, dispatching units to incidents in the districts you manage. As you progress, you earn money and “career points.” You can spend money to deploy more units and career points to unlock/manage more districts. The incidents you can encounter range from non-emergency calls and broken hydrants to armed robberies and serial killers.
_childDocuments_.name: 112 Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is very well done. It looks nice, the interface is easy to use, there's a reasonable amount of variety in the content.  One facet that's pretty cool is how you can play this in your own town, or pretty much anywhere around the world.  My biggest complaint is how utterly difficult the game gets very quickly. I'm playing on normal and it's overwhelming already (partially through the first - Berlin - campaign). There's two other difficulty levels above normal, I can't even imagine playing those.  I get frustrated when incidents pop up all over the map so quickly and I don't have enough servicemen to get to, let alone complete the incident. My second (smaller) complaint is how monotonous the incident & response game play loop is.  The 112 calls help a lot but they fizzle out after a while (I've had days where none come in), and the "click, send servicemen, wait for completion" mechanic is boring after a few hours of game play.  Don't get me wrong, the developers have created a well put-together game and I'm certain lots of people will really really enjoy this title.  I just don't like games where I'm overwhelmed by things I have no means to properly play through (in this case too much happening at once).

_childDocuments_.review: I did not play a lot yet but I come from 911 and there are some differences. It is not just the same game with more units or something, the interface and possibilities changed and some are good and some you need to get used to. The gameplay itself is simple, but - depending on the difficulty you chose - not really easy.You stare at a map, problems occur and you send units there to solve them.You get calls and have to ask questions and if you behave incorrectly people die. Sometime people die even if you do everything correctly but the game does not punish you for such a thing. Your behavior is judged, not the result, which is really, really good.If you look at an event you see how many units are already directed there and can see what status the handling is at.Firetrucks need water and if the fire is large enough they need to go and get some. But they only leave for this if another fire truck is at the current location (not sure about this).If there is a problem where you send police to it, motor cycles are faster than cars. But if they have to bring back prisoners to the police station then motor cycles are useless. But they can still handle the case and wait for a car with space for prisoners.Same principle for medics. A motor bike can go there fast, but if you need to deliver a patient to the hospital, good luck.Then there is the planning phase, before the real time commanding phase (with pausing, slowing down or accelerating the time). Here you can buy vehicles and personal (yeah, they are yours, buy them, but you have to pay them too, so not really slaves) and equipment.The interface is worse than in 911 but there is ONE big advantage: you can rename the units.The after action report is bad. Really, really bad. I just checked just for this, no, this is NOT Early Access but the really important after action report feels like it.Very often you can't read the whole description of a task because you can't scroll down far enough. Or the text is missing? Don't know, I don't see it.Then, the worst: you have no idea what you did wrong sometimes.You only see that you got minus points or no points for a task, you see the dialog during the task, you see the actions you took, some in color some not. But you have NO idea what went wrong. I checked the forum, others have the same problem, the answers were always something along the line that the errors and correct behaviors are recognizable because of the color of the text in the task description. Which is NOT true.I really tried to find out what went wrong but you do NOT see it.A good thing is that the vehicle list during the command phase is sortable. This was needed so much compared to 911.So... if you have 911 and are happy with it, this is not a successor in my opinion but a slightly different game which can be fun too and can make you mad. If you don't care about the money, try it. If you care about the money, don't try it. It is not really so much better or different than 911 that you have to get it.I currently don't remember any bugs in 911, only a lot of missing features like sortable vehicle list or information about incoming vehicles for events. So.. playing 911 is more relaxing which is a very sad thing for me :-(-----Update:I will go back to 911.112 has too many features I don't want and behavior I don't need.Weather reports, emails, missions, larger and larger area.911 is simple and easy and fun. They should have just made that one better instead of creating a slightly different game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyed this as a laid back game. Haven't found any issues thus far - one thing I'd suggest is to ensure you look through the loading screens. They provide some good advice for when you're handling calls around treating different injuries.The UI of the game is average - I think this is the area it could improve the most. At times, it's a bit clunky. I've also got the DLC, which adds COVID to the career mode. Having to go through and give my staff protective equipment against it was painfully slow, you have to do it individually, there is no way to mass edit.Pros: - Pressure feels real to get to each incident. You'll find your units stretched and pulled all over the place, it's up to you to decide how to handle this. I enjoyed the strategy aspect of this. - Difficulty level is a good curve - it does get harder in career, but you can usually work out if you've made a mistake - DLCs did enhance the career a lot for me. I do think it's worth getting themCons: - The UI is a little clunky. Requires too much clicking when you're doing the same thing over and over - Handlers seem to miss incidents that they claim occasionally. I've got rid of my handlers nowOverall, I give the game 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game was exactly what I expected, but I've really enjoyed playing it. I've played both in free mode in my hometown (getting to play in your location is one of the best parts of the game) and in London in campaign mode. The good bits:-I enjoyed both the crossbow killer storyline and the international summit one, I think it's neat that they continue over several days. -I liked the ability to buy the vehicles and staff myself.-The game is easy to pick up, even without an extensive tutorial.-It's cool to see the character interact with the 112 office every once in a while.The not so good bits:-The storylines repeat when you enter new campaigns and locations, so it gets repetitive.-The daughter storyline was underdeveloped (minor point).-The background noise of other operators is constantly repeating and it seems quite random but specific too (something about a jellyfish? a bit odd). But honestly the negative points are mostly me being harsh, it's a great game and I do recommend it. I did buy it on sale though, and I doubt I'd have bought it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game will stress you out a lot and really make you feel like an emergency dispatcher. The calls in this game are much improved over the first game. I don't believe I have heard the same phone call twice yet but of course I also do not have many  hours in the game. The campaign feels much more realistic over the first game as your dispatcher is assigned more and more districts to cover in a variety of major/capital European cities such as Berlin, Paris, Moscow, Istanbul, etc... There is also a free mode which basically allows you to search for really any major or minor city in the world so you can even simulate playing as an emergency dispatcher in your own home town! This game is really fun and on top of that very educational. I recommend it to anyone interested in RTS games or anything to do with emergency services.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is very engaging and can be fun, the lack of community relations and clarity of how Open Street Maps is tied to 112 Operator and when (if ever) the game will be updated with the changes made by users to properly reflect local police stations, fire houses, and hospitals. One of the main selling points of 112 Operator is that you can dispatch in your local community, But 112 Operator fails to mention that while most of the roads are marked correctly in your community, most if not all of the stations/ hospitals are missing or are out of place. While it is clear that 112 Operator pulled from what was at one point the most up to date version, that version has quickly gone out of date. Developers, on the rare occasion that they engage with the community, have given several different answers that contradict each other as to why 112 Operator has not been updated to appropriately reflect updated versions of Open Street Maps and if an update will ever occur.I have spent hours updating my local community's OSM by adding over 50 fire stations and dozens of police stations and hospitals. Then a month later, 112 Operator announced the Facilities DLC. To me, This can only be seen as a money grab and a band-aid for a much larger issue. Sorry Jutsu Games, But I am not going to add in another 45 fire stations.Because of this lack of clarity and community relations, I am inclined to leave a negative review of 112 Operator.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game where you can jump into an authentic role as a 911/112 Operator, or tailor the experience to be as close to that as possible, you're in the wrong place. The geographic issues are abundant and lack of customization options to fix those issues make this game frustrating and unplayable, for me at least. Very few of the facilities in the area where I'd like to play are authentic, and many of which are on back roads in the middle of nowhere. This game would like to convince me that there is a medical facility in Pattersonville, and in the middle of the woodlands on Kunkles Hill Road, as well as a police station in the middle of someone's rural driveway on Old Mill Road, miles from that municipality's actual police station. Sheppton's fire company is at the cemetery in the village, none of Shenandoah's fire companies are represented, and the Shenandoah police station is at the post office. There are so many facilities either misplaced, or in the literal middle of nowhere. Add insult to injury, none of the county's four hospitals are accurately represented, but the one defunct hospital is, somehow. I have been waiting for months upon months for the options to rectify these issues and cultivate an accurate experience for my area, to no avail. I purchased the Facilities DLC in hopes of finding those options, to no avail. Though the experience in 112 Operator is improved from 911 Operator, specificially in that I can actually cover my hometown, I cannot overlook these glaring issues, and, while I cannot expect the developer to fix them, I can and do expect to have the options and ability for the user to fix them on their own.

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a continuation/improvement on 911 operator. It's technically European focused, but functionally, it just expands on the locations, scenarios, and tools that you can play with. This means if you have North American locations you'd be interested in playing, they're still available.It's a relatively simple and repetitive concept, and so it won't appeal to everyone, but I'd consider it a softcore mix of grand and tactical strategy games. While it can get tense, it ultimately is fairly lax and low stakes, with linear campaign or level progression.I can't recommend buying it at full price, I just don't think there's quite enough there for the price point, but if it's ever on sale for more than 20% off (and it often is) then it's worth grabbing.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic continuation from 911 Operator. The basis of the game is for incidents to appear on your screen, either randomly or from calls that you take (more on that shortly). You then decide the best team to attend the incident to solve it in the best, or worst, way possible. Controlling Police Services, Medical Services and Fire Services allows for a good range of incidents. After a few hours, they can get a little repetitive if you do not read the in depth descriptions of the incident and go on just the title. This is unavoidable when you have multiple incidents appearing at the same time. Answering an incoming call instantly slows the game down to half speed, regardless of what speed you had the game at previously, which helps. Although the incidents do not stop appearing, having it at half speed allows you to focus more on the call. The voice acting on the majority of the calls is superb and allows for you to really get involved and engrossed in the moment. Although, same as with the incidents, the calls can get a little repetitive and you learn what the calls will be from the first few lines. The Devs have done a good job with having some variations on some calls but not all of them. As with the incidents, these do change and get more demanding as you progress but, in my opinion, not quickly enough to keep the game completely fresh. The controls are easy to pick up and can be operated with just the mouse, fantastic for anyone with disabilities that prevent two handed playing. The game gives a good amount of options and the varying game speed timers can help the player get the experience that they want from the game. As stated before, the difficulty progresses at a steady pace and both free play and campaign mode allow for good progression. The varying officers and vehicles available means that you can build a specialist service or one that is average across the board. The money that you get for each completed shift allows for a steady growth of your troops, as does the free units that you get with the expansion of your area of operations, but it makes it difficult to get the more specialised units as they seem a bit expensive compared to the income. The maps are very detailed and the Devs have done an amazing job at creating the real locations that they allow you to play. The amount of areas is also very pleasing. I would like to note, I have played the facilities update and it gives a good few units that compliment the existing game and add some needed functionality, I have not played the Water Services DLC yet. Overall, this is a fantastic game and allows a massive rush of adrenaline when things start getting busy. After the first few hours, it then becomes more of a game that you jump on for a "shift" or two when you would like to kill some time as there is very little downtime within the shift after the first few shifts.

_childDocuments_.review: In 112 Operator you take the role of a dispatcher to manage incidents, distribute assets accordingly and deal with incoming calls that can range from serious accidents to trivial callers. You can play in campaign or just free play which comes with a list of cities with the option to search and find cities if your hoping to play a particular one you like. Before it starts you will be given the option to equip your current assets, hire people or buy equipment and vehicles, these are split between fire, police and ambulance as you do your best to best prepare for unpredictable situations which range from quiet to suddenly stretching your assets to breaking point.For those that are new to this type of game it can be a lot to take in but for those that have played 911 Operator before it won't take long to get to grips with 112 Operator but there is new features that still give the game a fresh feel. Zooming into the map will show buildings and particular landmarks, police patrolling is now optional also with sending paramedics to hospital and firetrucks to refill water. Maps are now split into districts and once you unlock enough you can even assign people to manage the districts leaving critical calls to you. Traffic jams and weather will hinder you units ability to respond to calls or sideline them completely. One addition which makes things much easier is now equipment comes in bundles which makes equipping you crew much easier as each bundle serves a particular role.So if you've enjoyed 911 Operator and hoping for more then 112 Operator will do very nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to its predecessor, 911 Operator, this game puts you in the emergency call operator's seat again and puts you in the work shift to handle incoming calls and dispatch personnel to handle various incidents. Do it right and in time and it will favour your career and the future circumstances you'll handle. The campaign mode allows you to choose one of the select capital cities for the career you want to build on. There are story cases that come and go but a few that will last over days and builds some intrigue over what's happening in the city. However, once I've finished the campaign in one city, I've seen most of it all. The neat feature that graced 911 was the map generator using actual GPS data to generate a city of your choice, even the city/town/village you're living in. I also enjoy this sober atmosphere that's relevant to the situations and treatment handling done in the real life, which is in fact educational. In the end, 112 is sort of a 911 rehash with some new case variations and global-focused instead of being in the USA. I enjoyed it while it lasted but players new to the franchise are well-recommended to give this strategy simulator a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent, but it has the potential to be a lot more. I would only recommend this game if you're someone that is interested in a management sim. As you progress through the game you handle less calls and need to micro more units in a larger area with dispatchers that are supposed to help but are actually completely useless.Issues with the game:1) Overused voice lines that you keep hearing while playing and random background noise that you hear that has nothing to do with the gameplay.2) Lack of calls to answer. Which is strange as this is seemingly the most advertised part of the game while being a minimal part of the experience.3) It can be hard to tell if a unit is busy or just going back to base/patrolling.4) It is hard to tell if another dispatcher is using the unit.5) Units “patrolling” are actually completely useless as they will never respond to incidents themselves anyway.In conclusion the game is “not terrible”, but it could have been so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game I only got it 2 days ago and I've played for over 12 hours now. Not going to lie though this is probably one of the most stressful games you will come across, having like 1000 people trying to talk at once and spreading out your units. But yeah if you haven't played 911 operator it's going to be stressful for you but it is very fun. The campaign is a decent bit bigger than 911 operator, and I love how they added weather to the game it's annoying but realistic and cool. Also, there are missing person searches and VIP escorts, as well as large fires. These challenges are when the real stress from the game can be felt, as you will need to disperse all of your units correctly and make split-second decisions like should I send an ambulance to this person having a stroke or this gang fight that is going on. Also, there is a tornado in this game that is quite devastating to your fire and medical units and overall makes you plan accordingly. All in all, I really recommend this game it's a great sequel to 911 operator and the developers seem to be very passionate in their work and making continual updates to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: 112 Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel to 911 Operator and I really love it, even with playing it for just a little while. The career mode can be finished fast, but it's much more engaging and exciting than the previous game. They also added new scenarios as well, which are basically a single day of duty, but with a major unique event that you have to solve to achieve good results. The graphics are much more improved than the prequel and there are also some small cutscenes that break the monotonicity of the regular duties. The map is now also 3D, however not every city is available to play yet. The fun part about freeplay that the police stations, hospitals, etc. are actually at the real locations, I tried out playing at my own city and it was interesting! I believe they use OpenStreetMaps data to do this.Speaking of freeplay, it's somewhat simplified compared to 911 Operator, because the units don't seem to use all the small streets available and the districts are very broad especially when it comes to small, densely populated towns. However, this is just a minor issue and the overall experience was really great so far, even with just a couple of hours in. I would definitely come back for more gameplay and if you're interested in this theme I'd recommend trying out both games. Keep in mind that 911 Operator is considered finished and is not going to receive any updates.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well made game that expands on 911 Operator. You are REQUIRED to buy not just one, but however many districts will hit that magic number of career points. In campaign, I can sort of understand this decision. But in free mode? _childDocuments_.review: Although I will return to this game a few more times I fully expect this will not hit the '10 hour mark' in my list due to a lack of replayability and its apparent repetitiveness over multiple playthroughs. For that reason I can't recommend this game on anything less than a 10 euro pricetag in its current state.-Calls seem to be in the same order, so I've heared some calls multiple times now even answering the wrong questions because of boredom/wanting to get it over with.-I fear for replayability. Lets do the exact same thing with American voices in 8 different cities, that have been made unrecognizable in the current maps. IRL I have been to Berlin and Paris and I could not tell what part of the city was where. I would really suggest adding life to the city campaigns by at least giving the cities more character rather than the blue wasteland I'm looking at. It seems money was spent on a fancy intro movie that adds nothing or little to the actual immersiveness  of the campaign, yet I couldn't tell you which city I was operating in by looking at the map.-Some material (horses, cops on bikes) seem useless. They don't seem to have the incentives they might have in real life. They just do the same thing a regular cop car does, but very slow.-I unlock new weapons/armour etc. but so what? I'm confused by what gear my guys already have, and I don't know why I would add to their current loadout.-People in my team promote. So what?I like playing around in my own area, but I then seem to get the exact same progression (mainly talking about the calls) as the campaign. No sandbox mode, just a campaign-lite I guess?I think there are some concepts mentioned above that have been added to the game as leftover from the brainstorm phase of development, then have been left alone to never reach their full potential.I will play this some more the coming days, and I will most likely revisit it on a Friday night in the future when I've had a few beers. I hope the devs will keep improving and that I will like it better in a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: Take calls and try to prioritize which units get sent where. The fact it uses OpenStreetMap to generate the playing map is neat, but it can't tell the difference between sea, ocean, or shallow lake, and that causes some annoying issues where it'll give you a ton of boats when you really need more land vehicles.The concept is okay, but it quickly becomes repetitive. More annoyingly, after a few hours it begins to freeze for several second every few minutes, and the freezes only becomes longer each time the map is expanded, so the game quickly ends up being unplayable.It also completely lacks regional awareness, so when you for instance pick a city in Denmark, it still gives you police units that are illegal here (and thus don't exist) along with smugglers in our tiny lakes, and a lot of gunfights that would never happen here.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game.  Saw it on YouTube, and decided to give it a try.  The 112 calls are the real star here.  They're complex and interesting.  Unfortunately, most of the game is dispatching, and as someone who has worked as a dispatcher before, real dispatch is more fun than it is in this game.  I wish the focus was more on routing trucks efficiently from one call to the next and less on finding a way to use all the less-than-effective vehicle types (motorcycles) they insist on giving you while keeping up with emergencies.  The fact that you can literally load up any town in the world to play a free game in, though, is really cool.  I enjoyed getting to dispatch the actual town where I lived.

_childDocuments_.review: A good strategy game that also helps you understand how emergency services works. The one downside to the game is that some content and achievements are hidden behind DLC. Compared to 911 operator, this has better graphics, content, and unit controls. You can now queue actions, return units to their starting positions, group units together, and tell units to wait for backup. New scenarios include tornadoes, spreading forest fires, and neighboring city requests. The UI has been improved are easier to understand. Different units and vehicles have been added to be more suited for certain scenarios.

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is ALMOST a good game.  I really wanted to enjoy the experience of dispatching emergency services all over various cities, but I didn't.  I anticipated different units providing unique benefits or at least forcing me to deal with some limitations, but the only difference seems to be whether you can carry criminals/patients in the vehicle or not - vehicles that do not allow for transport seem almost useless. The calls aren't very compelling and the dialogue options send you down one of two very clear paths - provide support or be a total jerk.  Even the noise in the background is recycled every 45 seconds or so; you will hear the same repeated phrases coming from the "operators" around you throughout the entire campaign.  It got annoying.This is essentially a point-and-click time-management game masquerading as an emergency operator.  I played through the entire campaign, collecting achievements and hoping it would get better, but it didn't.  Don't waste your time like I did!

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a really good game, I've never tried any of the games by Games Operator yet, but I saw an ad for "911 Operator" and my friend bought me the "112 Operator" because it was newer. The UI is actually quite nice.The funniest calls I've received have to be a Slenderman attack, a lady called "Karen Gessler" who didn't get the response from the manager she wanted and a man who got a lightbulb stuck in his "behind"The more serious calls are a gas leak in a high rise building, a 15 year old child who was abducted and the man stuck in the train line, I like how the "preventable" deaths actually get you worried, I can't imagine how stressful it must be to be a real operator.The only things that could be improved is the repetitive background noise "sting ray attack" etc, and some noticeable spelling mistakes (on some of the achievements, and some of the responses when you receive an emergency call) I've only played 4 hours of this game so far, but it's definitely worth playing and I'll be definitely interested in buying more games by Games Operator!

_childDocuments_.review: - 112 operator 19hrs finished in 8.5 hrs on 5-8-2022:            6/10Far better than its predecessor, 112 operator improves almost all aspects of 911 operator, the UI is much better, units are faster and resolve incidents faster as well and its easy for you to see their progress, calls are more varied and interesting, the unit screen is more organized and you can filter them, you can name and number your units and set them to control groups among many other improvements.There are some annoying things that stuck around like the callers making muffled sounds when describing addresses which takes you out of the immersion, and the units are still not easy enough to click and sometimes you unknowingly cancel a unit’s destination thinking you’ve selected someone else. I liked the overall campaign and some of the overarching stories which go from duty to duty, all of them were unique and interesting, and some even hurt you if you failed. The game’s length is also just right since if it was longer it would’ve bordered on repetitive and boring. While there are many things the DEVs can improve on this game (Items and gear are still somewhat useless, unit selection and responsiveness, even better UI design, better controls, more music to put you in the mood etc.) the game is still very much recommended.TLDR;Pros:- Improvement over predecessor- Faster gameplay- Better stories- Great real-life info to have- Short and SweetCons:- No music during gameplay, the best music is the end credits- Unit controls need improvement sometimes clicking them doesn’t work first time- Voice acted address lines even if they’re imaginary places, otherwise it momentarily breaks immersion- Gameplay eventually doesn’t go too deep and is more click and sendOverall score 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It may be "just" a map on which you send around tiny police, paramedic and firefighter icons, but it's extremely well-made and very immersive; it really makes you feel like you're doing important work, even when you're obviously just playing a video game. Add to that the fact that you can save people in your own hometown (and an ever-growing radius around it to increase difficulty), and you've got yourself an A1 emergency simulator. _childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a game I think many people will play as it ends up being the first alphabetical entry in their library.In practice, I think it's fine. The calls themselves tend to be more engaging than the management of units, which tends over the course of several in-game days to be largely reactive in terms of purchase/placement (the player doesn't need to consider incident trends in any real depth and where a trend will exist this will be very bluntly brought to the player's notice via their in-game emails, which means that most of the decision-making involves identifying areas which were more problematic in the previous session and investing to address them.My biggest bugbear is how distinctly American all of it feels when the purpose in contrast to 911 Operator (which I don't intend to play) is to simulate European cities rather than American ones. It's particularly jarring when every voice actor is ostensibly American, and when standard scripting used when answering the phone isn't even adapted to local norms.With that being said, it's a fine management sim game which will occupy a few hours of your time. Consider buying in a sale.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a more fleshed out version of 911. Story wise it is more engaging as the better you do the quicker the rank up and the more districts you have to manage. The flip side is 112 operator has a lot more hands one work and can be way more stressful compared to 911, this does allow it to be way more interesting though.The core gameplay is still the same, answer calls, send patrols to events etc. There are more dual events and the calls are more engaging as well. One key difference I noticed is the equipment and different events. For example, fires can now be MAJOR fires like Australian bushfire level of fires. This means you will need to make sure you have water supplies nearby and you can micromanage where the fire engines focus their efforts, controlling the fire to some degree.If you like 911 then I would recommend 112, it is also pretty fun if you are into the idea of being a dispatcher.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, if you liked 911 Operator, you'll love this game. I've been playing for a few hours now, and I'll definitely be playing more. For sure, you have to prioritize certain things and ignore others, but I feel that's a fun part of the challenge of this game. It's meant to make you think like that.I really do recommend this game if you're looking for a bit of organized chaos and fun. I really have enjoyed it so far, and I'm sure I will continue loving it as I keep playing. :)

The game barely gives you 1 fire, 1 ambo and 1-2 police.  Making this game, even on Normal Difficulty, extremely difficult.  This game is a must play and will be streaming it when I can!

_childDocuments_.review: So there I am, quarantined because I have Coronavirus and this bad boy drops. It's like a better version of 911 operator and I love that game. Those who read my review for that will recall that I am an Emergency Services Worker and will recall I stated there are few things sadder than those who play at their job on a video game at home. It's got to be the definition of being job-p*ssed and I am unrepentant.I get a massive adrenaline kick every time I hear emergency sirens start up, because it makes me think I'm about to start running to a call. I've had three bloody weeks off trying not to die and I crave it and in a small way this game is helping.Yes, I'm covering the area where I work and yes I've also given the units I have call signs appropriate to that area. I love it! The scope is bigger and the only thing I hope for (at this point I've less than an hour in) is that there are more units and equipment, for example Area Cars, Q Cars, Dog Vans, Helicopters, Paramedic Response Cars and so on. They did a great job with this and I'm excited to keep playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the game's core issues are already starting to be addressed, but I one main problem, and it's about career points. One of the main appeals of 911 Operator, this game's predecessor, was the fact that you could play on any city in the world. This was awesome because you could play in your hometown, or some of the biggest cities around the globe. Now, 112 Operator has changed that.112 Operator has much larger maps, which I honestly think is a great feature. Each city has multiple districts which ensures a variety of gameplay. The only problem with this? The majority of districts are locked behind these things called career points. So rather than playing in the city you want and in the district you want, you now have to grind out these career points on other cities or districts. Once you've done this, you're finally able to play where you want, until you want to change maps, in which case the grind starts over again. This gets down to the main problem with 112 Operator, it's trying to fit linear progression into a sandbox style game. 911 Operator knew that it was a sandbox game, and gameplay followed suit. 112 Operator does the opposite. Through restrictions like career points, locked operator levels until you've completed a certain number of duties (or the campaign for the last level), and forced buying of districts (which the devs are addressing), the game forces you to play how it wants you to play. This in my opinion is the biggest failure of 112 Operator, the fact that so many of the best features are locked behind a wall of progression.Cheat codes in the game enable you to circumvent some issues, but not all of them. Hence, there are two recommendations I would make to the devs to better facilitate the sandbox elements of the game, and to improve gameplay in general. 1. Remove career points.2. Eliminate the requirement for a certain number of duties and campaign to be completed before unlocking higher operator tiers.I hope the devs take this feedback into consideration, and if they do update the game for the better, I will change my review to reflect that.**Edit**The devs did address the above mentioned issues. The game has improved in the sandbox element, and while cheat codes still are required to enable some of those features, I can now feel confident recommending this.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the casual tag on this game, it's a massive lie, I managed to play the previous game even on harder difficulties, but this one can easily overwhelm most of us even on normal.The good parts:- The slides giving tips are as informative as I expected;- There's more ways to customize your characters than in the previous;- The phone calls are still a pretty strong point here;- The email feature feels like a nice touch, even if it is unrealistic in some parts (like people actually thanking the operator);- The weather is used well in order to create new situations you must overcome;- Progression is much more evident (giving more districts to manage);- As far as I've seen the character names make sense for the most part (I haven't seen english names in my home country, nor the other way around);- There's instruments to help you, like cctv to see how scene look before you send teams there or drones to help with your search.The not so good parts:- It tries to make the operator's family relevant to the plot, but it usually feels too forced to actually make impact;- It's way harder than it's predecessor;- In the later game, you stop receiving emergency phone calls and they are replaced by reports or other districts asking for support, by that point duties become pretty dull compared to the chaotic charm of the starting ones;- The dispatchers that are supposed to help manage your team in the late game feel dumber than they should and most of the time you'll be confused why an ambulance is chasing a speeding car;- The campaign feels too long.How I would rate it: 6/10 because I didn't have as much fun as I had with 911 operatoror 9/10 for people that like management games (I'm not one of them, but I can see these people liking it much more than I did).

_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator' is in my eyes a worthy successor to the previous '911 Operator'. Especially the "calls" have been improved. Not only that there are new calls, the soundscape is more detailed and realistic. In addition, there are a few new functions for dispatching units: for example, the possibility of a unit waiting for reinforcements, the stringing together of emergency calls that are dispatched and the like. Also, dispatchers have been added, which you can set in the different districts and which will then dispatch units automatically (even if it proves to be difficult at times). Nevertheless, '112 Operator' is and remains a very cool game with an interesting campaign and several scenarios. If you are not an extreme fan or collector you should wait for a discount until the game costs around 10 to 15€/$.[Translated with  (free version)]

Glad I gave it a try -  I think it's really fun! _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game but do have some critiques of it. On the whole it's a great game and I am in love with the message it delivers and how it can educate on real situations. Giving real life saving advice as a background tot he game. Wonderful to see and congratulations on integrating it in smoothly.I'd love to have had the option on first launching to pick the voice of my operator. To get a more feminine voice. Even only having two options would open the game immersion up a little. The other issue I found was the guns and the tanks. It was just a bit ridiculous while playing in London to see standard issue equipment being guns. Some localisation would be amazing and less focus on a gun at the scene means a cop needs a gun. It just doesn't work that way everywhere. One last thing I think could be improved is the background chatter. It gets very repetitive very quickly. More variety there would really help I think.Really though I think on the whole these are minor issues and maybe ones the modding community has already come together to solve. The variety of units, the variety of incidents and how it slows down when a call comes in. Love it. Really made the game feel like there's always a lot going on but it's not just so overwhelming you can't keep up.
