_childDocuments_.review: 112 Operator is a great representation of Emergency Management. If you're into games in which there is strategy and decision making then you will find 112 Operator is the perfect game for you. In some instances, you will find yourself dispatching medics and police officers to "Gang Wars" then all of a sudden you get a call for a cardiac arrest, but all of your medics are dispatched to the Gang War! This game will most certainly sharpen your resource management skills while you're having a fun, interactive environment to play with.What this game does lack is that it does get a little repetitive and redundant. It gets boring after awhile. Well- maybe not "boring" but it is very easy to get burnt out in this game and click off to do something else. What I like to do is play this game while I am on a call with someone else, watching a movie, or listening to music. A second stimulus [at least for me] is a must for playing this game for hours and hours on end. Other than that, if you're bored between classes or something along those lines, give 112 Operator a try!

I heard the same "stung by a stingray" "me and my partner took care of that earlier today" "may i advise..." far too many times-E-mails are just entirely non-functional, you won't get warning for events, or sometimes you'll recieve them a day after? _childDocuments_.review: If we ignore the whole police bad thing for a moment, the game has promise as an emergency services management sim, where you have to prioritise calls over others when busy to maximise earning points. I don't like that the game calls it reputation, but I can't think of a better suggestion other than just "points". Gameplay wise you have to click on incidents as they come in, assign appropriate services to respond to them (your vehicles just sort of amble around the map until you task them), and occasionally respond to phone calls from citizens who need help. In the latter, you click through menu options to attempt to say the right thing and get the information you need to dispatch the correct team. These calls are fine, except that sometimes the caller just isn't helpful. One woman in the first mission calls because she's being stalked home by (in her own words) "a man with no face". The woman later admits in the conversation that she has taken drugs at a party, I tell her she'll be safe inside and if she's worried about the man she should hide. The phonecall abruptly ends with the sound of breaking glass as it turns out he was real, so I sent the pig patrol to go and arrest him. Case closed.The first screen you see when you launch the game is a menu of links to go to the steam store and buy their other DLC. Low effort. The DLCs include a coronavirus themed one (low hanging fruit), what appears to be a zombie apocalypse scenario (lower hanging fruit), and a 100% proceeds to charity DLC that replaces all the little character portraits with ones wearing masks (admirable).There are only US English voice lines despite being able to play in a variety of cities around the world, and I don't like the idea of the Americans having privatised my emergency services. I picked London, and all of the in-game calls I received were also Americans, so maybe this is a paid for service for US citizens in foreign countries? Not sure about that one.The visuals are fine, it does feel like a mobile game that was ported to the PC though. The game revolves around a section of a map (of your chosen city) which is nicely displayed, and the vehicles get a blue glowing route line ahead of them to indicate where they're going and what path they're taking to get there.Upon exiting the game, I get the same DLC ad screen, which is just rubbish.Play if you like:- 911 Operator board game- Low stakes management simsDon't play if you want:- Engaging dialog and story- To abolish the police

_childDocuments_.review: It's obvious what you have to do, but I can't quite explain there is something extremely addictive about this game. As well as saving people, answering phone calls and upgrading/kitting out the rescue teams with the money gained, there is a real feeling of satisfaction. At the end of each day there is a review showing your performance and if you missed or failed any incidents. Its quite frustrating to think you've had a good day and then see you've missed several phone calls (or more). However this doesn't effect your money too much and you can continue the game. There are no levels that you will get completely stuck on and can just keep going, which I like, there's nothing more frustrating than getting stuck on a level and eventually giving up a game because of it but this game isn't like that thankfully. You can also slow down time to make the rate of calls coming in slower which is also a good idea especially as you may find yourself prioritising calls due to lack of resources. There are basic management games and complicated management games and I think this one is somewhere in between. I like that. Well done.Windows 10Intel core i5Predator HeliosNvidia GTX1060

_childDocuments_.review: I retyped the review  so it should make a bit more sense! But if you’re here from the older game (911 operator), this one is better in many ways! Even without DLC.  ^Though, remember this, there is  with a lot of units or districts(?) to the point where I sometimes wish the game did crash, so keep an eye on that.   Overall it’s best to have these two together. A virus breaks out and if one of your units gets infected, they’re out of commission. It’s overall pretty fun and adds some challenge since you have to think out where to have your units stationed or your facilities(DLC). Speaking of facilities, they allow extra places for your units to go (transport suspects, remote hospitals, water refill stations, etc). There are a few extras with police (speed cameras/cameras in general and whatnot). But overall it doesn’t provide too much of a difference in the game. You have access to boats now! There are a few new calls/responses you can take so I won’t spoil them too much for you. They can get very annoying if you only had a few boats (like I did), but it is enjoyable if you want to have extra calls to respond to. And finally, a sort of zombie apocalypse! You do get a bit of a warning from a call you respond to that something is coming (if you look at the attacker they should show ‘infected’), so you must prepare pretty early. It ramps up later on and overall is pretty stressful if you don’t know what you’re doing. Make sure to have a bunch of units! ^And IIRC, it goes till you have no units left? Though I got tired of it so I didn’t get that far. >The graphics themselves are 3D compared to the older one. But that might tank older machines(?) if you don’t adjust the graphics when you boot it up.>It has a pretty good balance between the stress of not having enough units or too many situations, and the fun overall. Though of course, later in the game it's abnormally stressful, especially if you don't have a lot of units!

_childDocuments_.review: Im gonna start this review with a warning: The positive reviews are overrating this game in an absurd way. It is a decent game and the concept of it is very interesting. However, it has a lot flaws. I would love to have the maybe option here, because that would be the most fair way to rate it. If you're into time management games, you're gonna love this. If you're not, you won't. That simple. There is a bit of micro-management to it. You can use the money you gain as you progress through the game to buy new equipment to your workers and more vehicles to distribute around the city... and that's it. It's not a very complex game. The number of options you get as you progress in terms of new equipments and vehicles is decent. The calls you answer and the procedure you gotta memorize for each situation gives a bit more of a challenge to it but nothing extraordinary in terms of difficulty, which is ok.There are flaws though. The UI could be a little better presented. Sometimes it's difficult to spot exactly where your vehicles are going or if an emergency appears too close to another it gets tricky to send units to each one of them. Also, game is very repetitive.  There were some improvements in comparsion to 911 operator but they are minor. It's pretty much the same game.Good points: + The music and voice acting are very well done.+ It's a realistic game. You take control and answers calls as a real 911 operator.+ Very easy to learn. Game does a good job explaining the basics on how your vehicles, equipment and procedure works.+ The DLCs add some cool features to the game.Bad Points:- The UI could be better.- It is very repetitive. Also, specialists and work types makes little diference to the game. If a vehicle matches the color of the incident, just send it. Works out anyway.- No replay value. - Without the DLCs, the game lacks a lot of depth.- Very similar to the previous game, 911 Operator. Almost the same game in fact.- Not very difficult after you get the hang of it. Put some effort on it and you can easily cover every single call and event.Score: 5/10 Worth Buying: Even though this review says yes, in fact, it's a maybe. If you're into time management games, do it  but only if you get the DLCs as well. Otherwise, the game will bore you very quickly. I suggest staying tuned for sales discounts!

_childDocuments_.review:
112 Operator allows you to manage emergency services in any city in the world! Dispatch units, take calls and face situations caused by weather, traffic or changing seasons. Help the city survive escalating events like riots, organized crime, terrorist attacks, cataclysms, natural disasters and many more!

Help on a scale bigger than ever before. The sequel of the award-winning 911 Operator lets you act on many, completely different levels -- from taking care of a single neighborhood, to coordinating several operators' work in the world's biggest metropolises. Full 3D visualisation will give you the inside view of your units' actions. Choose from over 100 000 areas, such as districts, municipalities, and tens of thousands of real cities from all over the world.

Face the dynamic weather, based on authentic, historical data. Watch the incidents change as day or night comes, traffic increases and seasons pass. Watch out for extreme conditions that may lead to cataclysms and natural disasters. Try to tame big wildfires spreading across the map. Weather isn't your only problem though -- be careful when dealing with terrorist attacks and gang wars.

detailed_description: Feature List • Retro-styled visual wonderland with a psychedelic color explosion by award-winning Canadian cartoonist, Jesse Jacobs • A fine-tuned platformer with tight controls to dash, dodge, and jump off surfaces to survive against neon spiders, massive rainbow worms, and bomb-dropping moondogs • Plunge into the psychedelia of unique worlds ranging from neon plains, to experimental tanks, to frozen icelands, all the way to outerspace! • Face off against kaleidoscopic bosses and shoot them down with your babies as ammunition • Inviting and replayable for everyone; a speedrunning challenge for the insane • Soundtrack by famed Canadian artist, James Kirkpatrick, featuring compositions written on modified Gameboys and circuit-bent, hand-made instruments. About the Game Enter into a world thick with bubbling psychedelia. Descend deep into a new ecology teeming with multiple pathways, luminous levels, and complex obstacles. Transcend the material realm and assume your true form as Spinch, a hyper-agile organism consumed by the quest to rescue its litter of missing offspring from an endless invasion of misshapen and malformed offbeats and oddities. Bringing back old school difficulty, Spinch will have you replaying sections until you master your timing and reflexes. Dash, dodge, climb, swim, jump, and even shoot your own babies as you take on six enigmatic bosses in six vibrant worlds. Collect items to give you the upperhand while searching for your missing babies. Be on the lookout for your cousin - he's babysitting some of your relatives, but he's a little weird. With only a ticking clock and quick restarts - no lives or game overs - the game is welcoming to players of all experiences, but a formidable challenge to even the most capable of speedrunners. The world of Spinch has been crafted and brought to life by talented award-winning Canadian cartoonist, Jesse Jacobs, known for his precise and detailed line work in combination with bold and simple color palettes. His works contain an affiliation with psychedelia, spirituality, alternate realities, and a blending of nature with technology. James Kirkpatrick, well known for his participation in the early Canadian graffiti movement and as avant-garde hip-hop artist, Thesis Sahib, created the audio landscape of retro soundbites and electronic sounds found within Spinch.

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who plays a lot of plat-formers, I can say that this game is a real treat to look at and play. The game play starts really simple in world 1, but gradually amps it up nicely the more you play. My only complaint is that most of the underwater levels are not fun to play simply because its really slow to move. Also I would like it if it would display the boss's health so I would know how close I am from beating it.*Keep in mind that here are a few bugs lingering around because this game just came out. If you really want a bug-free experience, then just wait until the game receives a few bug patches.*
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: The Game starts off pretty great! The movement feels very tight and rewarding, like it should in a platformer, but i've never seen a game throw out so much quality in such a short time span which is really a shame because i was really enjoying it.As i've said, the beginning is absolutely fine (World 1-3) but everything after that just feels off, especially the water levels because they basically get rid of the tight movement and leave you with something that feels very clunky. The level design also gets worse and worse to the point where it just feels like a chore to complete the levels in question.Im actually sad to give this game a bad review because the art direction and sound design is so on point, but the gameplay is abyssmal... i personally could'nt enjoy it that much :(

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:  DO NOT BUY THIS DEAD GAME. If they ever put in the little amount of work it takes to fix it THEN you can reward them with your money. They are selling a broken game for $15.Loved this game.  I used to speedrun it.  I have most of the WRs in the first few worlds.  It's unfortunate that the developers have abandoned it as a very broken game.  It actually has more issues than when it first was released.  Here are the issues.Before we start.  Game has been reinstalled several times to try and fix it.-Hz of monitor never used to matter.  Now I have to lock my monitor to 60hz or else the game will slow down.-Best times after world 4 are completely broken.  They never save correctly.  One level my record is around 1:20 but it says 13 minutes instead.  Times are broken for the whole global leaderboard.  The biggest gameplay strength this game had was speedrunning. These issues make that impossible.-No QOL changes like better world and stage select.  No ability to replay bosses for better times.-Many instances of achievements not working.  I have no personal issue with this because I don't achievement hunt but many people seem to have this issue so I will amplify their concerns here.-Devs were unresponsive in the discord when we were all concerned about bugs that needed to be fixed.  I was personally contacted about my issues but no patches have been put out since.  The Akupara Games discord no longer lists Spinch as one of their games in the "Our Games" channel list.  The game is essentially dead for them.It is a shame because the art of Jesse Jacobs and the music of James Kirkpatrick rule.  Those are some cool dudes who make incredible art who deserve at least a working polished game for their work to be presented in.  This game should not be sold in the condition it is in.  It doesn't even need much, just some bug fixes.  DO NOT BUY THIS DEAD GAME.  If they ever put in the little amount of work it takes to fix it THEN you can reward them with your money.  What a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: after reading other reviews of glitched achievements and janky controlls, i thought you know what, its a small studio, people might be expecting too much from it, lets give it a shot! What a frustrating mess of a gamePro's : the art style is unique and eye catching, its vibrant and each level looks like a lot of effort and care went in to the design. The Story is easy to understand with no in game dialog needed. The mechanics of collecting something in a level, to then use it later on in a boss, is a fun concept i enjoy'd. This gave a lot of value to bonus levels where you could only attempt it once, but the reward made it worth it. The soundtrack in this game had my head bobbing along to every level, the sound effects were pleasant and not annoying. The over world looks so amazing in this game.Cons : This game feels like it was made by someone who never playd through every level completely, but was learning how to make a game. The begging levels are extremely basic for difficulty and mechanics. By the time you hit the first world boss. its just a cannon and shooting the collectables you found. By the final boss, its a 4 stage boss, with parkour in between the buttons, pixel perfect jumps, tight timing, and rng of where bullets are being shot. This goes for the level 6-1 as well. It took over 30 minutes to complete, where any other level took under 10 minutes to 100%. I thought the deathless achievements in this game would be a fun challenge to aim for, doing world 1 was beyond easy. But once you hit later on worlds you realise each section of the map was only done once to see if it was do-able. If each level was fully tested from start to finish, i think it would be obvious how silly the achievements are. Enemys AI that chase you is made to catch up to the player no matter what, there speed increases the more distance they are away from you until they are 10 pixels behind you then they go back to being a snails pace. This is unfair if you as a player are running fast trying to find secrets and need to back track, only to have the thing chasing you be right behind you already. I found my character to get stuck on random invisible pixels during the maze level. This again shows things werent tested too much, just attempted until it was do-able then put in.  The achievements in this game are still bugged. Anything related to world 5 unlocks for world 4 and vice versa. If simple fixes like these are missed, it just seems like the game was made and sent out. There have been multiple people complaining about issues with the game and nothing has gotten fixed. I can only reccomend this game for the ascetics. Nothing about the gameplay after world 3 made me want to continue playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Jesse Jacobs' work, I was very excited to check out a game based in his world of psychedelic colours and shapes. Unfortunately the game feels half baked and amatuerish at times.The platforming is ok, but doesn't have the feel of a Super Meatboy or Celeste. The dash adds some variety to the gameplay but can be frustrating to use sometimes. This is on top of occasional frustrating bugs, like platforms not resetting when respawning at checkpoints, being killed instantly as there is no respawn invulnerability, or dashing through the world geometry and getting stuck in walls.The art is of course the main draw for some people and it was pleasant to be inside a world created by Jacbobs, as well as see it all animate in strange ways. It does feel like the game was rushed though as there are a lot of reused assets, bossfights that are progressions of the previous, and bonus levels that are the same mechanic with one more obstacle than last time.The music and sound design did absolutely nothing for me (this is a personal thing ofc), I found the sound effects annoying and poorly mixed, such as the sound for killing an enemy with your 'star power' being so so much louder than everything else. The sound design overall felt kinda cheap.I really really wanted to like this game being a fan of Jacobs' work, but didn't find it entertaining enough to persevere and see it through. Could have been I wasn't in the right headspace for this game at the time, but I feel there are better indie-2d-platformers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: You think you like the game because of its simple, fun platforming and beautifully weird aesthetics/music, but, then you get to the "Water World." My God... the developers took the most hated aspect of platforming, being underwater, and somehow found a way to make it more annoying and un-fun (these were also the longest levels to play compared to the other levels before them). When you enter water, your speed warps down to a crawl, and even though you have a dash button, using the dash button constantly screws you due to the incredibly long amount of time it takes to stop your momentum and change directions. The worst was when one of the water levels constantly forces you into vertical hallways and turns into an auto-scroll, dodge the spikes mini-game. The sluggish direction shifting in those areas made me question whether or not I should uninstall the game. You can also alter the speed you're moving during these auto-scroll moments, which there are something like 6 of them, to either be moving quickly or slug-like slow. In order to make yourself shift to slow speed, you have to hold the direction button in the opposite direction of the auto-scroll. This is more annoying than it may seem, because if your thumb leaves that direction button for even a split second, which happened all the time to me because of the constant need to dodge spikes, your character shoots forward with a high risk of you dying because of it. All of my negativity is focus on the water world, because it truly was that horrifying of an experience. This is more of a "meh" game rather than a "don't buy" game. It's not original in any way except for it's look and sound, but you'll still have some fun outside of the water world.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels great movement wise and the first few levels really start off good but as soon as the game decides to switch things up and add new mechanics it starts to gets kinda annoying to play.The reason for this is that the further into the game they introduce more and more things that slow you down and forces you to either wait for or gently float along with gaps between enemies.I wouldn't mind if there was levels like this every once in a while but after the first world it really just turns into "wait for cycles the game" where every single challenge that shows up in your path really is just a to challenge your patience lol.I ended up playing through like 5 worlds hoping that the one i was on just had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gimmick to it. I still kept playing though, thinking that i might as well finish it since it seemed to be like max 5 hours long but then I ran into the water world and JESUS CHRIST IT'S BAD.I generally think that people are too hard to water levels in video games cause the change of pace in the middle can be nice sometimes. But considering this game has been forcing you to slow down the entire time until this point it really didn't provide this feeling.Instead it introduced these awful water controls that has so much inertia you just run into spikes or enemies if you ever try to speed up since slowing down to a stop takes a good ~3 seconds.And to add some salt to the injury the last 2 levels in the water world have these tight spiky environments which really don't function for these kind of controls at all so the difficulty just spikes super hard for these sections.It feels like the water controls were either changed after the levels were made or that the levels just weren't tested.At this point I decided to stop playing and just not bother.Anyways, bad game lole xd
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: A fine example of why Steam needs a "Maybe" recommendation. I was intrigued by the description and striking visuals, which in game are indeed very cool and interesting to look at. But I have a hard time truly recommending this after playing through the first couple worlds. The controls are tight as claimed, but traversing the levels just doesn't feel all that interesting and that's what let the whole thing down. Maybe this improves in later worlds but I really shouldn't have to put up with boring level design to get there. I'm a proponent of the idea that games should be fun from the start, not at some arbitrary X-hours-in. If I had noticed there was a demo I probably would've saved myself some time by trying that first, so I suggest doing so if you're on the fence.The interesting visuals, weird ideas and cool music can't carry the milquetoast gameplay for me. But if you're a total platformer junkie then you'll probably want to check this out. So a firm "Maybe" from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch's psychedelic visuals might draw your interest at first, but you will quickly find that the gameplay does not live up to the same expectations. It's sad, because I really wanted to like this game, as the platformer genre is one of my favorites. I've played many ruthlessly difficult platformers such as Celeste, so I know from experience that for the difficulty to feel "fair," the core game mechanics need to be polished to a sheen.Spinch, however, is a farcry from that level of perfection. From getting softlocked at the end of the final level from a broken checkpoint, to getting stuck on flat terrain in the middle of an intense chase sequence to a dash that sometimes gives you a little extra height and sometimes it doesn't. My initial enjoyment of the game quickly became frustration as I trudged my way through the game to get all achievements.By the way, numerous achievements are bugged out and although this has been known for a long time, it doesn't look like they're going to be fixed anytime soon. It sucks to see such clear passion and innovation in a game, and still be unable to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: An infuriating but fun psychedelic platformer that has great ART to it (make sure to check out the 'Trading Cards' artworks), a fitting soundtrack, and fluctuating difficulty. It goes berserk at one point and then there's no going back. There is a great learning curve tho but none of it matters if you don't figure out the timing. Get your kaleidoscope ready and play this game if you love trippy challenging platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Difficulty: This is a hard game. Most of the time it is hard because it feels like you cannot control your character. Sometimes there are things off screen that you are supposed to time correctly but you can't because they are off screen. There is also a glitch where you randomly get stuck in the floor and you lose all your momentum. Some platforms make you lose momentum when you get to the edge of them.Some sections the game are pretty much impossible to not to get hit by something.Gameplay: The level design is not that good. throughout the entire game you will get dejavu because you will see things that you have already seen before. This is because the sections repeat themselves throughout each level with only a few things changed.The checkpoints are poorly placed. sometimes you will get two checkpoints almost back to back during a fast and easy section then there will be no checkpoints during a long and hard section.There is very little focus on killing enemies. Most of the time it's just better to avoid them. About half the enemies you find will be invincible anyway so it's better to not even try. Enemies just feel like moving obstacles rather than enemies.The bosses are boring. Every boss is very similar to eachother.The game is short, There are only four levels in each world and then a boss level. The bonus levels aren't even levels they're just garbage minigames.There are not that many secret passages. Most of the spinch babies are in plain sight and there are no other collectibles.  There is no incentive to collect the cubes because they only provide a short period of invincibility after collecting 50 which most of the time will be at a random and non beneficial time.Story: there just isn't much story. You are a spinch and you save the babies.Music: The composition of the chip tune music is very good. However, the pieces of music are short and repetitive which can get annoying when you are playing a level for 20+ minutes.My experience:I had some fun during the first three worlds and the fifth world. The fourth world was complete garbage. I stopped playing in the sixth world.I got this game on sale in a pack of three games. It's not worth $15. Don't buy this art project if it's more than $3.00.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really digging this game so far. The controls are snappy and the music and art direction are on point. The first world eases you in to a lot of the gameplay skills you'll need, but the difficulty starts to ramp up in the second world. So far I'd say I would definitely recommend this game to people who like challenging, fast-paced platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Was more or less vibing with this game until World 6, at which point an enemy is introduced that requires near perfect movement to avoid in some sequences. However, the player character physics aren't exactly consistent here, from losing wall bounce momentum randomly to suddenly stopping on flat surfaces for no reason. It single-handedly diminished any interest I had in completing the game. I just don't care anymore.Oh yeah, the horizontal acceleration in the water levels is horrible too.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game at the first glance, but it turned out my first impressions were wrong. Yes, it is colorful. Yes it looks happy. But only looks.A good platformer must have good level design, but this game doesn't have any level design better than corridors with timings. Levels look stylish, but feel empty when you play them. The game would be alright if only levels were a bad thing though. Spinch lacks polish. There are a ton of bugs here and there, to the point that you can get softlocked and forced to restart a level if a weird collision happens. Some levels do not feel quite balanced, difficulty curve is weird. All bonus levels are the same level with different aesthetics. At least the bosses are different lol.Overall, it was a dull and a bit annoying playthrough. I don't even want to to any of the post-game stuff. Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: -One of the first games where I actually hated the OST and sound effects. Every noise in this game sounds terrible.-The Aesthetic is cool, but it is not nearly enough to carry the game.-Level design from start to finish is incredibly repetitive and boring.-Player movement is solid but pretty simplistic.I made it to about half way through the 4th world before throwing in the towel on this one. A lot of people in reviews mention that the game starts off great and gets bad after world 3, I would disagree. I would say the game starts off slightly below average and then never really improves. Only reason I quit at world 4 was out of boredom and knowing that there is slim to no chance the next 2 worlds were gonna improve substantially enough for me to care.Even at a massive discount I would not recommend this to anyone looking for a platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: I like the visual styling of the game, and the level design for the first few worlds is pretty good. It's fun up until world 4 which is almost entirely underwater based. The under water controls are extremely slow unless you dash, but the dash gives a lot of momentum, which is very hard to control while underwater. It's also worth mentioning that every boss fight functions the same. The music is also lack luster. If you're looking for a simple platformer to waste a few hours on, this is an alright choice, but it really doesn't do much that you can't find done elsewhere better.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: As a wannabe speedrunner and someone who loves a palm-sweat inducing platformer, Spinch is a perfect choice. It's a high-challenge, precision platformer set in a super psychedelic and colorful world full of wonderfully weird obstacles. Each level prepares you for the next set of obstacles or mechanics, but none of the levels lets you off easy! The game also retains a high replay value, encouraging for us completionists. I'd also add that the soundtrack is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Quick heads up, if you're using a 144hz monitor (or anything other than 60hz), you'll need to go into your OS's display settings and manually set the screen refresh rate to 60hz for the game to run smoothly. I feel like this should be warned on the store page since apparently it's something the devs cannot fix. Anyway...I want to recommend this game, I really do! I love the visuals and the music/SFX, but man, the gameplay and lack of polish is pretty rough. Controls are a bit too slippery to feel satisfying and can make some deaths feel out of your control. World 4 in particular is a really frustrating example of this - lots of water levels that feel like you're swimming in molasses (slowing the game down to a crawl) with longer gaps between checkpoints, it was a gut punch after going through the previous three worlds. The level design can feel amateur in places and quality of life is sorely needed for the pause and level select screens. (...this isn't particularly important but the final boss was almost great! just get rid of that blue bullet attack it does, that thing is pure RNG on most phases and it sucks getting sniped by it offscreen with 0 time to react!)I think this game deserves to be looked over again by the devs and fixed up. It's such a rad concept seemingly left to rot and that's such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some delightful visuals and some impressive music. It has tight controls, with just two buttons, but there's more to it than just jumping and dashing. _childDocuments_.review: One of most mediocre and (gameplay-wise) uninspired 2D platformers i have played for a long time.+ Good art (though it lacks variation)+ Sometimes good music (but half of the tracks are more on the annoying side, especially due to their extremely repeditive nature- Very limited movement options (running, jumping and dashing) that are not very fun to play. Underwater movement might be the worst i have ever encountered in a 2D platformer- Uninspired and mediocre level design:    - Hardly any original ideas, very few ideas in general. More than a third of the game is simply a "run away from instant-death enemy" challenge, with very boring and basic obstacles along the way    - Repetitive inside a single level (some sections seem to be copy-pasted) as well as during the whole game (later levels recycle themes and concepts from earlier levels) - Bad, unbalanced difficulty: Despite some difficulty spikes, single sections are merly really difficult on their one; but it gets very frustrating if you have to repeat a long section of easy challenges over and over again, since checkpoints are multiple minutes apart in the later levels.- Pretty buggy (position warps/glitches, achievements were'nt triggered, wrong times for level playtimes, stutters with framerates > 60 fps)

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch is is an easy to pick up platformer, where you play a happy little white blob, trying to rescue your babies from a multi-colored menagerie of menacing monsters. The game combines solid platformer controls and interesting level designs, with rainbow psychedelia pixel art provided by Jesse Jacobs and a great "bleeps and bloops" old style video game soundtrack as composed by James Kirkpatrick.The platforming is equal parts frustrating and rewarding. Frustrating in the sense that there will often be times where you know exactly what has to get done to move past an area, but your timing is off. Which makes the rewarding dopamine hit when you get it right all the better. Some levels even include button/switch-based puzzles to solve, which make for a nice break in the "move/jump/dash" platformer format.I hate to use the phrase "headtrip" to describe the visuals of Spinch, but I can't think of a better term. It reminds me a lot of some of the pixel art commercials that occasionally get played on Adult Swim. It's certainly a hell of a visual feast, and sometimes you just want to let the level timer run while you take it all in.Speaking of the timer, it's a bigger enemy than what you face in game. You bust your back to finish a level in 5 minutes, and you feel good about it. Then you look up the leaderboards and find out people have cleared it in under 2... How?! And that's when the hook sets. Now your hands are getting gnarled, you slam your desk every time you die, and the Nintendo Thumb injury you picked up when you were 6 is flaring up, but you know you can find a way to improve your best time.Next thing you know, it's 3am, you have work in 5 hours, and all you dream about is running from Moondogs and trying to catch the children your pink cousin is throwing at you. Why, cousin, WHY?!
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch puts the fun back into platforming games that many modern games no longer have. I love the art style and music.The game itself is just fun to play! Will be my go-to single-player game to unwind the stressful day.I personally have not experienced any crashes or frame rate drops that other players have been experiencing, and I'm at 2160p as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: The demo alone sold me on this game.  Very tight controls and some lovely precision platforming mixed with a touch of exploration. Obviously the visuals are fantastic and burn into your retina (in a good way). Haven't quite figured out what the purpose of collecting the sugar cubes is and was a little disappointed that you couldn't replay the bonus stages (although I understand the decision). Overall a solid platformer that I'm enjoying very much.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the true definition of visual candy. 11/10 artstyle and ideas everywhere you look. The levels are interesting, the platforming is nice and the movement is feeling good. The difficulty curve is also well managed and has some nice linear scaling to it as you progress. I'd literally buy this game just to look at it a be totally mesmerized, so the fact that I can actually play it is a nice bonus and I absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: This is, in its essence, a short to medium length 2D platformer with obviously tons of colors, and awesome animations. Music is alright most of the times, but does get annoying/repetitive, especially within the longer stages. As far as the controls go, they are a tad unusual for the genre (definitely more floaty than what you'd expect), but simple enough to get used to quickly. The quality of the level design varies tremendously. The first three worlds work well in general, albeit there is some tediousness to be found as many of the challenges are just repeated multiple times in a row. There is also a lot of downtime in general (having to wait for obstacles to align in certain ways), which feels weird in a game with a timer in every level encouraging you to go as fast as you can. Anyway, I like what the woke worms and rolling logs (forgot the latter's real name) brought to the levels.Don't have much to say about world 5, it was fine.On the other hand, world 4 (water world) is possibly one of the slowest, most boring platforming experience I've had in recent memory. It's not even that hard, with only a few cheap traps here and there. But everything moves so slowly and again, is repeated excessively. And then world 6, while I don't necessarily disapprove the very sudden and extreme ramp up in difficulty, gets difficult for the wrong reasons: the checkpoints are grossly far apart, the only non-boss level is way too long and repetitive (and a maze, cause why not, right?), and some problems in the controls get more visible, like how I would sometimes get stuck on the floor until I jumped, for no apparent reason.Finally, there are some bugs. Apart from getting stuck to the floor, I remember at least 2 achievements being mixed up, as well as the game somehow taking my best times for world 4 levels and registering them in world 5 instead. At least, none broke the game.I'm disappointed I can't recommend the game, because it did start showing much promise and originality, but the later parts just aren't very fun to play.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch is a Psychadelic 2D platformer, and although I’m giving it a thumbs down, its honestly not a bad game and there is definite appeal for players who like these types of games. It’s just that the movement controls made me want to throw my controller out the window.Pros:-2D platformer with precise controls, I hate the movement drift but it does give you a lot of freedom and versatility. Besides getting briefly stuck on random corners I never felt like the controls were inaccurate.-Unique visuals-Checkpoints with infinite lives so at least you don’t have to start levels all over again.-Level designs are ok. Nothing really wowed me, but it is fun to look at with all the bright colors and weight architecture.Cons:-The controls have a lot of momentum and drift. This can be tough to get used to but its manageable for most levels. And then I got to the water levels and wanted to kill myself. The drift is multiplied by like 10 and its super frustrating to have to account for. A game where you have to be super accurate but also drift this much is just a recipe for frustration.-Checkpoints are sometimes abundant, and sometimes scarce. Can be frustrating having to repeat sections over and over because you get tripped up at one part thats way past where a checkpoint would normally be.-The music can be fun, but its such a high tempo that when you get frustrated it makes the experience worse and it can be hard to calm down and focus.Overall it’s a decent 2D platformer that I can see more hardcore fans of the genre enjoying a lot. I just felt that certain elements of the gameplay and design felt too frustrating when combining precision with drift. Some people will enjoy that challenge though.Rating: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch is colorful, beautiful, solid, fun, and brutally punishing.It's been out a year and only 90 reviews? What gives? I'd describe this as a 90s throwback with crazy psychedelic art. Each enemy, boss, nearly every part of the level is some part rainbow and flashing. It's super psychedelic, the animations are fantastic, the whole game is a feast for the eyes. If you have epilepsy, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. Despite being so colorful, isometric, and somewhat busy, the levels are easily navigable and you never feel lost or that you aren't hitting the right part of the "3D" object or determining background/foreground. Love the enemies and the art style, each level brings a new environment and themes challenges to fit. These levels are hand crafted and each one has a new piece of rainbow art to add to this strange world.The music was probably the weakest part of this game, it's fitting but very forgettable and lackluster, nothing I would listen to outside of the game, and even gets a bit repetitive depending on the level.The gameplay is very simple yet addicting due to how well it controls, wall jumping and dashing feel like second nature. The platforming is straight out of the 90s. Very few glitches, but there were some involving movement that were hard to replicate. There was one glitch that almost made me quit, the checkpoints on 6-1 if you alt tab will occasionally lock up and force you to restart the level, this wouldn't be a big problem if this wasn't the LONGEST LEVEL IN THE GAME. It happened 3 times to me, and I had to essentially beat the 15+minute level 3 times in a row.Game loop is simple: you play as a cute little ball guy, go through levels, collect squares which eventually turn you temporarily invincible, collect your babies in secret areas which you use to shoot at the boss, and go to the next level. Unlike a 90s game, you have infinite lives and there's an interesting health system that may or may not be accidental. If you collect a heart while already having the maximum number, you get n+1 hearts every time you spawn even after you die, if you have less than the max, it just heals you. The babies mechanic is really interesting since it gives you an optional way to progress and make the bosses easier. The more babies you collect in a world, the more you'll be able to shoot the boss before reloading. The babies are hidden in various areas throughout the level but are very fairly placed, except ONE on 6-1. There's also the option to get bombs as ammo with bonus stages, these were okay and brought an additional challenge to break up the platforming monopoly. The bosses almost remind me of cuphead, there is very few random elements and while they are difficult, it is all about learning the patterns and mastering them. What's interesting is that the bosses don't really go out of there way to attack you usually, you're just having to dodge them to get to the gun to shoot them and load the babies again. Despite this, I messed up and died too many times from this false sense of urgency the environment provides.Yes, some of the water levels suck because you move slow, some of it was ridiculously hard and I had to save up hearts and take hits for certain parts, but that's part of the hardness of this game. The checkpoints are not generous just like games back then and sometimes you'll go back seemingly half the level, but it just forces you to get better and master it. I don't mind the difficulty, it really ramps up after world 2 but it's not unfair, just very hard. It says I beat the game in 347 deaths to give an idea. I also tested this on a 3rd party controller and it worked fantastic.There is some very obvious faults of this game most of which are recognized by the developer and will hopefully be fixed soon. The world map isn't easily navigable, you can only try the bonus levels ONCE and if you fail, too bad. You can't go back and fight old bosses again after defeating them. There's some QOL stuff like having markers to show if you've no-hitted a level or not and no restart level button.Overall just a great and challenging art game with extremely solid platforming that I'd recommend to anyone who likes the art books of the artist, Jesse Jacobs, and a good challenge without being a full on speedrunning game like Celeste. I found it a joy to play and was really impressed at how well of a game it was, despite appearing that most of the work went into the artwork. This game deserves more love!

_childDocuments_.review: At only .5 hours in, I've found myself immersed in the perfect blend of retro psychedelic visuals and wonderfully complementing music.The simple controls are best played on a gamepad and the beginning levels allow you to get a feel for your bearings. Difficulty quickly ramps with less forgiving obstacles and monster encounters but, with a little time and dedication, that rewarding feeling you get on completion is totally worth it! There are plenty of side areas to explore for the adventurous types, while still allowing a speedrun opportunity.The seamless mesh between music and visuals within level design takes things above and beyond just a simple side-scroller and I look forward to discovering what puzzles lie ahead!10/10 would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch is a definite must play for the platformer enthusiast. It's a psychedelic journey with just the right amount of punishment. The graphics are simple and clean, making the colorful experience pop. The soundtrack is well composed and I found myself humming the tunes outside of game play. The controls take some getting used to and a controller is a must (though you can suffer through the game with a keyboard just fine!!!) but once you learn them the motion of the game becomes a little more liquid. There are some minor bugs in the game that can be irritating at times but nothing that can’t be overcome with a little time and maneuvering. Overall this game is worth the coin.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: Genre: -Precision PlatformerFit for me:-Perfect, my fav genrePros:-One of the best looking platformers I've ever played.  The visuals, the animations, the unique characters and environments are all top notch.  World 3 is one of my favorite looking world of any platformer that I've ever played.-Well designed bosses that compliment the platforming sections really well.  You don't see too many solid bosses in precision platformers, but the bosses in Spinch are the exception.  They are all great to look at, and challenge you in a different unique way.-Great use of collectibles, by using the babies that you can find in the game as ammunition against the bosses.  There is even a secret level every world that can be unlocked, and if you beat that secret level, you gain a bomb as ammunition.-Very responsive, and runs quite smoothly at 60 fps.Cons:-The water levels in world 4 were very frustrating, but more importantly, they felt out of place.  You will never be in the water again, and so it feels that you have to complete an extremely tedious and challenging set of underwater platforming sections for no reason other than to add more content to the game.  I found these levels to be the least fun as well.-Artificial difficulty by way of excessive chase sections where you can be one hit killed, and extremely far away checkpoint between checkpoint 2 and the end of the level.  I think the devs could have found more creative ways to increase the difficulty.-Every time you turn off the game, you have to rebind the keys which is a small thing but should be noted.  The default dash is set to L which is a strange choice for a dash key binding.-Doesn't live up to the bar set by the best platformers in the genre w/ regards to platforming sections, fundamental mechanics, and teaching players how to become proficient at the game.Thoughts:-This is a tough one to review.  I'm happy w/ my purchase and had a good time overall, but the few problems that I ran into near the end of the game really dragged down my overall experience.  It's really important in platformers, that every level feels necessary to the player.  I like playing tough levels that challenge me, b/c as I develop new skills for the game, it makes me a better player.  But I don't like having to do a long set of challenging sections that don't really offer any intrinsic reward, other than moving on to more levels.  The best games in the genre are able to achieve both goals at the same time.  The incredibly creative aesthetic and interesting environments were enough to win me over, but the platforming sections left a lot to be desired.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This is an average platformer, but an absolutely gorgeous visual achievement.  If you like the aesthetic, and can get past some of the artificial difficulty issues; Spinch is worth a try.  It's colorful, cute, creative, and much more challenging than you would expect.  This is an easy recommendation when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Spinch has clever mechanics, fun levels, strong challenge, great music, and a very unique look. It's frustrating, but not hopelessly so. It seems to really ride that edge of "Okay, if I don't make it this time, I'm quitting forever" and then boom -- just as you're about to give up, you  make it. _childDocuments_.review: Jesse Jacobs and James Kirkpatrick produce a delightful combination of art and sound for Spinch.While the game itself is a very basic (but very tough) platformer, this creative combo is the reason to play.During my experience with the game, there were several very frustrating bugs and hard crashes.Many of these have been resolved as of the most recent patch, but plenty still remain.You will absolutely get stuck on some very difficult levels, and it will challenge you a lot.The final boss alone took me at least 8 hours to finally complete.If that sounds like fun to you, then enjoy Spinch.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review: This is Mescaline the the platform game. The game play is inspired by platforming classics like Mario and Sonic. The speed of movement is also some where between those two. This is very much a psychedelic platforming game experience. The art and colors are lush and the there is a color/rainbow theme throughout both the art and story. Its like the drugged out love child of Mario, Adventure time, and Super Jail. I've only made it to world 2 so far but the game is allot of fun and the difficulty has been increasing steadily with each level. The level design have been varied as well so you don't know what to expect when you go to a new stage. I bought this game on a whim because the it looked really trippy. I was not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Spinch

_childDocuments_.review:
Transcend the material realm and assume your true form as Spinch, a hyper-agile organism consumed by the quest to rescue a litter of its missing offspring. Enter into a world thick with bubbling psychedelia, swelling with an endless population of misshapen and malformed enemies. Disrupt your psychic architecture and be absorbed into the world, teeming with multiple pathways, luminous levels, and complex obstacles.

Our hero Spinch can dash, dodge, jump off walls, and shoot his own children as ammunition. Platform your way through side-scrolling levels collecting items to give you the upperhand while searching for your missing babies. Be on the lookout for your cousin - he's babysitting some of your baby cousins, but he's a little weird. Bringing back old school difficulty, Spinch will have you replaying sections until you master your timing and reflexes. The ramping difficulty will see Spinch swim through experiment water tanks, chased by hordes of weird creatures, and traverse backward and inverted environments. With only a ticking clock and quick restarts - no lives or game overs here - the game is welcoming to players of all experiences, but a formidable challenge to a speedrunner.

name: The Sojourn
detailed_description: THE SOJOURN - GOLD BUNDLE About the Game A tale of light, darkness, and the nature of reality Traverse a thought-provoking puzzle game and its immersive colour-drenched world of light and shadow. In The Sojourn you arrive in a mysterious land, where lights guide you forward. It’s not long until the world reveals itself to be full of challenges. Now, you must overcome these intricate and ever more demanding obstacles to uncover the nature of reality. KEY FEATURES Dozens-upon-dozens of challenging puzzles Delve into four beautifully crafted chapters, each with their own distinct style and atmosphere Banish the darkness in order to reveal the obstacles The Sojourn has prepared for you Unravel a captivating tale of light, darkness, and the nature of reality

short_description: The Sojourn is a first-person puzzle game set in an immersive colour-drenched world of light and darkness. Think your way through dozens of puzzles as you traverse parallel worlds, awaken mysterious artifacts and overcome challenging obstacles on an unforgettable journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I enjoy a mental challenge, The Soujourn has finally worn me out. Gameplay can be summarized as 'solve puzzle' and then 'move to next puzzle.'  Although the scenery is lovely and the sound track enjoyable, the repetitive nature of the challenges is exhausting. This is compounded by the fact that there is no reward for solving a puzzle. Instead, you just move along to the next one. The story begins with following beings of light into an environment that unfolds before you. At first, it is delightful and I had a real sense of discovery and wonder. Each area has an average of 5 puzzles. 5 'scroll challenges' are added to these as you enter the second phase. From this point, each area then has around 10 puzzles. Multiply this by numerous areas and the number of conundrums is a bit daunting.Puzzles consist of managing light and dark to power devices that direct energy, swap positions, and open bridges. Some have gates that turn light/dark on/off as you pass through. Others have barriers that change according to whether you are in light or dark mode. Lastly, many have a stationary or movable power source. Solutions are a mix of physics and resource management to create a path from each start to finish. Although there are multiple scenes with statues, there is no narrative and no real story to follow (other than what can be inferred from the statues). Each scroll has a philosophical quote but these do not tie to any theme that I could follow.At this point, I have over 26 hours invested and am approaching the completion of the third (out of four) major sections. I do not regret buying the game and have gotten my money's worth. But, I am not inclined to continue. While it is possible that 'all will be revealed' in the end, I don't have the stamina to complete this marathon.This is not a bad game and I experienced no bugs or issues. However, I would recommend it with a major caveat. If you are a gamer who enjoys puzzles for the sake of puzzles, then The Soujourn may be right for you. If you prefer an adventure with a sense of forward motion or discovery, then you may want to look elsewhere.Update: As noted in the comments, after a 10 month break, I circled back to The Sojourn and played to 100% completion. The fourth (an final) section of the game was easier but my original thoughts remain the same.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts with fifteen levels that are almost entirely logical combination puzzles. Then switches to one of those exasperating just-in-time challenges that require you to clickthenturnthenclickthenmovethenturnandrunlikeHell in tenth-of-a-second windows. I know there are lots of people who like those games. But getting fifteen levels in without needing any of the necessary reflexes and other skills, only to find the game has become unplayable without them, is utterly maddening. See, we just can't do those things. No problem with people who can and who like those games. But why design a game around a particular style of play, let your player get used to it and feel like they're settling in, only to add a needless time-limit feature that calls for precise action? This wasn't an action game for the first fifteen levels. All of a sudden, you can't proceed without being a Ninja.Just an awful let-down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to say much about The Sojourn as it's a puzzle game without actual storytelling and it doesn't show us anything that we haven't seen in other games before.It's that type of game where you can't say anything bad about it but at the same time it's rather tedious - it's very unlikely that you'd want to complete it in one play session. It has nice visuals, it's polished and there's pleasant music most of the time. However, there are better alternatives like The Witness that was available for many years, or great puzzlers with more entertaining gameplay like Lightmatter, or dozens of minimalistic puzzlers that may provide a similar level of challenge with simpler but smoother gameplay.All in all, it's a decent game with good puzzles, nice visuals/atmosphere and slightly outdated game design/presentation so I'd recommend it to people who enjoy puzzle adventures with walking simulator mechanics and looking for more games of this genre. An easy skip or purchase with a solid discount for everyone else. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: What would otherwise have been a truly fascinating "almost entirely pure puzzle" game, with mechanics that bend your mind in all sorts of fascinating ways, is COMPLETELY RUINED for me because -- just every once in a while -- you need to do something with split-second precision timing.WHY do developers do this?  For the vast majority of the game, you have time to sit back, think, listen to relaxing music, move around, figure out just how you're gonna manage to get from point A to point B while leaving statue C in position D, and then WHOOPS -- YOU HAVE EXACTLY SIX SECONDS TO SPIN AROUND SOMEWHAT AND MOVE AND TURN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT DIRECTION AND MOVE AGAIN or else you have to either reset the puzzle, or at the very least repeat several actions in order to get everything positioned properly again.Here's what is NOT my idea of fun:  Twisting my brain around the light/dark mechanics, figuring out what I need to do in order to progress through the level, and then having to pause the game, activate a CPU throttler, play through the STUPID time-sensitive portion at one-quarter speed, then re-enable normal speed, and continue.The reason this is ESPECIALLY frustrating is that they have ALREADY incorporated a mechanic in the game where a certain "quality" is only depleted while you travel a certain DISTANCE.  Yup, you have plenty of time to think about where you need to go, and the timer only goes down when you move.  So, why couldn't they have implemented the same mechanic for the other thing, instead of having the timer go down in real time, so that you need to react very quickly in real time?If only they had implemented the other timer in exactly the same way as the first one - decreasing ONLY as you move, not decreasing in real time even if you stand still, this would have been a totally awesome game.As it stands, I'm pretty sure that I wasted my money, and I won't be finishing this -- too frustrating, not only because of the way it is, but also because it DIDN'T HAVE TO BE the way that it is...I like the way that, towards the beginning, I was gradually introduced to new items, and how they functioned.  But then there was a LONG LONG set of levels (all the way to the end???  I may never know) where it was just "OMG, I have YET ANOTHER combination of a handful of these exact same things??!!?".After a while, I didn't even try any more.  "Crap, I've gotta solve SIX of these things before the elevator will let me access five or six MORE of these things??!!  I'll just watch a video and play along; I don't even care any more".  This is, for me (maybe I'm just too stupid?) a case of "increased complexity removes all the fun".Imagine you're doing a series of jigsaw puzzles.  You do a couple with just a few pieces, and you feel rewarded and clever.  Then you do a few moderate-sized ones, and they take more time, and more effort, but eventually you finish and feel rewarded and clever.  THEN somebody dumps a million jigsaw puzzle pieces out of the box, and says "Ok, this is what the next several levels are gonna be like - better get to it!".Or, like doing 9x9 Sudoku puzzles are fun.  I've even done a few hexadecimal ones (0123456789ABCDEF).  But the puzzles in this game start out with a difficulty similar to, maybe, 4x4 or 5x5 Sudoku puzzles, but the later ones are so intricate and convoluted it's like doing maybe a 25x25 Sudoku puzzle.  Sure, I know how they work, and if I'm patient enough I can gradually get things placed in the proper locations and orientations, but by then it is a chore, and nothing more.Countless back and forth trips, altering the paths of "dark" beams, picking up relics, placing relics, going through archways, teleporting with statues, making all sorts of minute adjustments to directions and carefully re-locating statues requiring numerous little steps - it just isn't fun after a while.MIGHT have been fun if they had allowed a "top-down" mode -- where you see all of the "pieces" on a grid, like a chessboard, and could easily see where each of the towers and beam generators were, and could simply pick up pieces with a mouse and move them, rather than having to walk around pathways (with no railings??? why not???) and trying to keep the "grand picture" in your mind.(p.s.  Also, couldn't they have made little railings along the sides of the pathways?  I didn't fall off very often, but considering you re-spawn exactly where you fell, it just seems like a way of needlessly requiring the player to be more precise with actual movements, when the main focus of the game is thinking about how to progress -- would have been much more enjoyable if there was no stupid "oops you fell off -- wait a few seconds before you can continue" mechanic...)Finally, and this is NOT a deal-breaker by any means, but still - what is with the blindfolded statues?  Am I supposed to be smart enough to string all of them together to form a coherent story, or something?  If so, I must not be smart enough - and since they are quite far apart in real time, whenever I encounter a group of them, I've already forgotten what the previous group was doing (and is there supposed to be ANY relevance to the gameplay??)

_childDocuments_.review: The Sojourn, a high quality puzzle game with some interesting and well made mechanics that just feels off somehow.The positive:I love the mechanics, the dark world, the introduction of new elements is very fair and slow to get you used to it before hitting you with harder stuff. There's about 5 core ones and all are original, any more than the amount they have would be too much for my mind to handle.The ability to cheese puzzles is great in this, and both a blessing and a curse. Because the mechanics are not as "solid" as other games, you get a chance to pull some stuff the developer did not intend to solve the puzzle. How often this happened I'm not sure, but some puzzles I definitely felt that I had skipped some things via this. I do not want to call them glitches since they are so uncommon and they do fall within the rules of the game, but they are common enough to break the monotony of the levels. There's a lot of places you can just barely squeeze some of the visual based mechanics through, some of it is intentional, some definitely isn't but it feels fair. This reminds me of the Talos Principle in that way, and it's definitely a good thing. The only real complaint about this is that during the first time playing, it could lead you to believe that some of the objects are red herrings, how many or if any actually are, I still don't know.(POSSIBLE GAMEPLAY SPOILER)For example when you fall/jump off a ledge, you respawn where you first fell off, but what I figured out on accident, is that if you start a harp playing before falling, it will still be playing when you respawn -2 seconds. So you could use a dark mirror beam over a pit by hopping into it and using that split second to activate the harp, respawning with it still playing and cross the bridge. Please do not fix this devs, it's only really useful in a handful of levels. (END SPOILER)A Beautiful World, it's almost similar to Monkey Ball where the levels are the same, but when you look around nearly every level has a beautiful semi-cartoonish environment filled with buildings, castles, mountains, It really makes me want to jump out and start exploring that instead of the actual game.Actually challenging! It's hard to find a puzzle game that's this challenging but fair and you'll get levels and levels (and levels) of this. Some are easier than others, even nearing the end you get hit with some real brain teasers and some softballs to follow them to help you not feel like you're stuck. Another page taken from the Talos book, BONUS PUZZLES. You can skip these and come back to them after you beat the game which is a plus. Some levels are criminally easy, and once you've mastered them, new sections open up with new objects and a new goal, increasing the difficulty of what you've already mastered. These are where the game shines in its creativity.Soundtrack does its job and I barely noticed it aside from a few ambient noises.Both a positive and negative is the content, there are so many puzzles in this game, I thought it was going to end 2 or 3 times and it just kept going.The Negative:Beautiful and well made game, there's a lot to be desired when it comes to keeping the player on board.There is little to no sense of progress, you complete an area, go back to the hub, unlock new area in the hub, go to new area, repeat. For how beautiful the game is, there isn't much to do between puzzles besides walk at an absurdly slow pace and look at things.You just get ~80 puzzle marathon of one after another, there is some sort of story told by various statues throughout the hub, but I failed to find it compelling and didn't bother with it for the most part. There is a section of the hub where I travel the same looking hallway over and over, the second I get enough levels to unlock a new area, another of the same hallway. It was really discouraging, even some sort of mountain or tower where you can look back to see how far you've come would've alleviated this.Backtracking, this is especially bad with bonus puzzles, there are many situations where you know what you need to do, it's just a matter of taking the 2 minutes to backtrack through the puzzle to get to where you need to change it. Worse, what ate up too much time for me was when I had clicked something and immediately messed up the puzzle, forcing an essential restart and with the ungodly slow walking speed, it was truly frustrating. A simple undo button would have been nice, or at least some sort of sprint. By the end I really started to fell like the slow speed wasn't to keep you from exploits, but to pad the game time.These issues wouldn't be as big a problem if there was more to the game than just puzzles, think marathoning a comedy show like I've done with stuff like Curb Your Enthusiasm, it stops being funny when you see the bigger picture and clear patterns arise and ruin some of the magic.The puzzles started to boil down to a simple logic problem, yes there's a bunch of different mechanics but they all boil down to you needed to be somewhere, swapping something else for yourself, and having the right variables when you arrive at your destination. This isn't a bad thing as it's the bread and butter of most games like this but the monotony makes it weigh on you more. The more I played the more it felt like I was playing dozens of the same variation of the Seven Bridges of Königsberg problem especially due to how the game works mechanically.This feels like a good quality game and there is a certain amount of fun the average person will get out of it, but I doubt it will be able to keep interest past a few hours, since you've basically seen all there is to see by then.I hate to not reccomend this game, but there's really only a few people I would give this the go ahead to, and those people would probably give a similar list of issues despite the polish and initial quality of the game. I really enjoyed the first 1/3 of the game, the last bit began to felt like a chore, and that's really not what you want from a game.

_childDocuments_.review: The opinion of this game depends solely on what exactly the player is trying to find. The puzzles here are the most important component around which the plot revolves ... I would like to say that the plot revolves around them, but here it is so vague and non-obvious that at some point you stop paying attention to it. Puzzles for the sake of puzzles is the best definition that can be given to what is happening, and as for me, it turned out quite well. Riddles focus on light manipulation, teleportation, thinking speed and planning. The toolbox expands as the action progresses, so even at the end of the game, solving puzzles is fun and exciting. If we talk about complexity, then it deliberately varies on different scales, and it does not correlate at all with what stage of the game you are at. Only one or two riddles left a feeling of deliberate complexity, in terms of ease of understanding the mechanisms of solving the game designers did a very cool job. All this is accompanied by pleasant music and good visuals that set you up for a peaceful exploration of the world. The scale of the game is impressive, there are really many puzzles and a lot of time will have to be spent on them, although by the end of the game it seemed to me that the creators would drag out the final a little. As a result, we can say that the term "puzzle game" can be applied to this game as honestly as possible, because it offers a huge number of them. Pleasant and competent work that deserves the attention of puzzle lovers.

_childDocuments_.review: So... I got this on sale and I am a huge nerd for puzzles of all kinds. BUT, I cannot say this game is a thing to recommend to just anybody. If you want to know the experience this game gives you just do some real puzzles and instead of lore or story or anything that has to do with the actual game, just open a fortune cookie that is most of the time poorly worded. That's this game. It's art is wonderful and the story could be great [if they had more than ~20 seconds of it] The music is nice [if they played it more than once every half hour] it's like it has the basis of greatness without the extra bits that make other games thrive. I did like this game and beat it last night, but I did not feel a sense of gratification. the puzzles were sadly more of a time waster than an enlightening or gratifying experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like it. Puzzles were good, visuals fine, mechanics and whatnot. Good "A-Ha!" moments too. There's not really any story, which is fine. The Witness is in the same boat, and I enjoyed that as well.What this game so  needs is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RUN BUTTON. The walking is UNBEARABLE. Whenever I have get stuck and finally strike that "A-Ha!" moment, I want to RUN to fix it because I am EXCITED that I figured it out! Instead, I jump small heights in fruitless attempts to bunnyhop. It makes the pace at solving the puzzles so sluggish and it's disappointing. I know it's a minor thing, but in the long run, time really adds up.  I hate not recommending games under Iceberg too. Sorry, Shifting Tides. Sorry, Iceberg. :(Edit: I have realized that adding a run option would break how some puzzles are solved. _childDocuments_.review: An extremely linear first-person puzzler.As mentioned by others, this game is almost purely puzzles. There's no exploration at all. There's also barely any story, aside from some statues shown once every few puzzles.  There's no narration, no books filled with philosophical meanderings, and no characters aside from the aforementioned statues.So what  there?Puzzles. Lots of puzzles. At the end of each puzzle is a door, which leads to the next puzzle. Later on there are some hub areas, which consist solely of doors leading to puzzles.The puzzle mechanics work like this: there is a light-world and a dark-world. In the dark-world, you can interact with certain puzzle elements, such as a statue you can teleport with, or a harp that creates platforms.  In the light-world you cannot.  There are platforms that bring you into the dark world, but you only stay there for a certain number of steps, so the puzzles usually involve teleporting the statues in specific ways to leave you with enough dark-world steps in the right places. You also obtain a way to interact with things in the light-world in later puzzles.If these sound like good puzzles to you - great, buy the game! For me, I thought they were just alright. I ended up refunding the game because after an hour the puzzles still felt easy and all felt kinda same-y, and there's literally nothing to keep you here besides the puzzles.Everything about the art and sound-design is well-done. This game is wonderful to look at. I didn't beat the game, but the Internet claims there's about 5-7 hours of content.Overall, if you like pure puzzle games that aren't insanely difficult, this is a good one to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzles and interesting visuals. Not much story, but what there is is interesting.My biggest complaint is that the game doesn't tell you when you will advance to the next section and not let you come back to complete optional puzzles. So, if you want to complete everything, make sure to do it before moving on or you will not be able to do it later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: The Sojourn gives me a mixed feeling It looks beautiful, but the puzzles and rules are sometimes questionable, especially the time part with the harps. Some puzzles can be solved by breaking the rules and not by logic. This for me is a dealbreaker and somewhat ruins the gameSome puzzles are well designed, but then others are beyond insane with too many steps and backtracking.They added a "story" but it has no purpose, no meaning en no explanation. it's just there to make the game look more mysterious than it really is. At the end of the day, the Sojourn is simple puzzle game wrapped in a beautiful packaging5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Sojourn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm grudgingly giving this a thumbs up. The puzzle design is unique and absolutely brilliant. So why grudgingly? The rest of the experience frequently ruined it for me. The blindfolded statues clearly indicate there's supposed to be a story, but it's not remotely clear what it's supposed to be. Then there's the random enigmatic sayings that would make a fortune cookie jealous (or, frequently, confused). These started out as a bit odd, but quickly became annoying. I did like the ending though.Pros:- Unique puzzle mechanics that are added at a good pace to keep things interesting- Great level design- Good difficulty balance - frequently challenging but rarely difficult enough to be frustrating, resulting in a feeling of accomplishment upon figuring it out. - Most levels contain optional scrolls for an added challenge- Great music- Gorgeous visualsCons:- There's no running. This isn't a big problem during puzzles, but is often frustrating between levels when you're slowly walking through experiencing whatever the story is supposed to be- The statues and achievements make it clear there's a story, but it's as clear as mud. It doesn't seem to be a case of 'up to interpretation' either.- So what about the scrolls? Surely they tell you something about what's going on right? Nope, just more vaguely wise-sounding word salad that I found often ruined any sense of accomplishment at solving the puzzle. To be fair, a lot of these were quite nice, and I really liked the final one if you collect them all. It really felt like they were reaching for a lot of them though, like they needed a certain number of wise sayings to put on the scrolls but ran out half way through.Verdict: 7/10
