_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever thought, "Hmm, I love FF Tactics and MCR, how can I blend these into an interactive story experience?", Othercide is your answer. This game does a good job of telling a lovely and emotional story interwoven with interesting gameplay. The choices of playable classes for your characters is a bit limited, but you can pretty quickly build a good roster and change team compositions to suit the particular mission requirements.The combat mechanics benefit from player choices with character skill customization and items, which gives each player a way to tailor the synergy of their teams to suit their taste in play-style. One thing I did enjoy was the inclusion of the combat timeline, a HUD feature that shows you when your character will be able to act if you take certain actions, when delayed attacks will trigger, when enemies will move or take actions, etc. At first blush the content might seem a bit shallow. I think there are 35 - 40 "days" to play through, but each "day" has multiple missions to play unless it is a boss mission. You are probably not going to get through the full game on your first playthrough though, and the game is designed with that in mind. All told, I clocked around 67 hours to get most of the achievements and beat the final boss, which was a satisfying amount of playtime for me.I would give this game overall a 7.8/10, and definitely recommend to anyone looking for a tactics-style game.** DISCLAIMER **- I got this game at a significant discount during a sale (picked it up for just under $10), but having now played the game through to completion, I assure you that the price point has zero influence on my recommendation. -** SECOND DISCLAIMER **- I am not going to hide the fact that the overall aesthetic of this game is going to bias my opinion significantly. I love the art style, the atmosphere, character design, and soundtrack of this game. Deal with it. -

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide was a diamond in the rough for me. It took me a bit to... "get it", so to speak. Once I did, I absolutely loved it.The game is a slow roguelite, so I didn't really get what it was going for for the first run, I still enjoyed the turn based tactical combat and the aesthetic (visuals, sound design, music and voice acting are all top notch from the get-go) but gameplay wise it wasn't really clicking for me. With only 3 character classes and only 3 abilities each, the variety in the combat was a bit limited, and there were enough mission types to keep me going but not to have me feeling hooked.It wasn't until I got utterly destroyed by the new enemy types that appear after beating the second boss that I started to understand the gameplay loop of the game. After losing (or choosing to start a new Recollection), you are given the option to activate "Remembrances", which are passive buffs or bonuses that make your next recollection easier and more dynamic, while allowing you to start the game at a later stage, to not have to play the early levels over and over again (which I still did because I wanted my Daughters to level up and be a little OP to face the bosses, cause they can kick your ass pretty quickly if you aren't well prepared).Once I got my Daughters to level up and unlock new abilities I started realizing the cool combinations you could create to control the tide of battle (especially by equipping Daughters with Memories, which improve their base abilities with a variety of cool bonuses), and the game completely clicked for me after Recollection 3, which I had to start after the third boss  (which was cool because I got to start again with the coolest surprise the game throws at you, ).I absolutely recommend this game, even if the start may be a bit slow and confusing. The whole vibe of the game is wonderful, the main story is pretty cool and the side story that you unlock as you play got me in the feels, really well written stuff. I loved the game and will probably play it again on Nightmare mode one day (yes, I played on Dream because I like my games to be fun, fight me).

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a frustrating UI, this game blends a unique atmosphere with a complex and interesting tactical game. I especially enjoy the fact that each mission takes very little time, which is golden if your'e a busy gamer.One big caveat is that you will NOT enjoy this game if you are the type of player who hordes his potions or always reloads when someone dies in XCOM. In this game you will constantly have to gamble with the lives of your troops, and sacrificing them is a core mechanic. You are sending soldiers to the meat grinder, not building up an elite troupe of your favorites. So if that bothers you, absolutely steer clear of this game.I only have two big complaints about the game. The UI in between missions is very tedious to sift through and was obviously designed with controllers in mind, leaving PC players with too much unnecessary clicking. _childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a grim, stylish, turn-based strategy game (a la XCOM, but smaller) with roguelite elements seamlessly baked in - I specify that it's seamless because the roguelite portion, which forces you to sort of lose in a forward direction and gain bonuses from your failures, fits so well tonally with the presented story.The story itself is simple but satisfying, and a bit esoteric, as it is primarily told through codex entries, limited dialogue, and to a lesser extent, the environment itself. It never feels forced on the player, but it (like the rest of the game) wins on the style front.As for the combat gameplay, it primarily revolves around managing the timeline, which is an action-economy initiative order shown at the bottom of the screen while in-mission. You plan your moves according to who is on the battlefield, and while the initial learning curve can be sort of brutal if you're not cautious, the play smooths out relatively quickly. For the most part, it plays how one might expect - you attack enemies by spending your action points to use various abilities, and try to avoid attacks from enemies. Enemy movesets are available to you in-match and in the codex, though at times their descriptions feel incomplete. There were a few instances during the game when I had to open the wiki to confirm something after an enemy seemed to break a rule previously stated by the game, but this was uncommon enough not to be too bothersome. Overall the gameplay was satisfying, and I enjoyed setting up combos between my units using their reactions and such. Pulling off a slick play in Othercide feels really good.That said, the game started to drag a bit for me at the end as repetition took its toll. Luckily it didn't overstay its welcome, as a full clear (campaign completion (on the intended "nightmare" difficulty) + 100% achievements) for me took between 30 and 40 hours - hard to give an exact amount because I left it open a few times when running to a store or making food. Oops. I'll also say that perception of Othercide's difficulty seems to vary person-to-person as the other reviews I've read speak about the challenge in inconsistent ways, but I found the difficulty to be comfortable. It was tough at times, but never insurmountably so.Current full price is $30, and I don't know if I'd have bought it for that (I picked it up on sale), but I would've felt comfortable spending $20 on this game. I really enjoyed it, I'm just picky about my cost-to-playtime ratio.My overall takeaway is this: Othercide is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. If you like turn-based strategy and the visuals doesn't seem too fatiguing for you, I'd definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another hard game to judge. Purely on tactical combat it's decent. My MAJOR ISSUE is that it was a drag towards the end. Also don't look at my play time, I was alt tabbed playing league of legends most of the time on this game, which is a testament to how i felt about it at the end. If you enjoy SRPGs, tactical combat, progression systems that make you feel stronger, and moderately difficult game-play then this game is an instant buy. But, and BIG BUTTS ARE HERE, it gets a little repetitive at the end and the challenge evaporates. There is no narrative what so ever to keep you interested (this is no fire emblem) and the customization is bare bones but what is there has meaningful decisions to be made. The core of it is this -  the rougelite elements detract from the game utterly. The randomized levels don't do much to elevate the game but rather hurt it. These drab samey levels with similar enemy placement. The game is also a very player phase oriented with powerful abilities reserved for limited use on enemy phase.  Overall really a decent SRPG with decent style. I wish i could give a mediocre review, but I'll thumbs up because i think it was a good effort. But I will ultimately forget this game in a few months. It has nothing memorable - nothing that others in the genre haven't done. No story or characters to remember.

_childDocuments_.review: HelloThis is personally for me one of my favourite games to date. The art style and environment of the game is something that appealed to me straight away. Its dark, gloomy and really portrays the concept of little hope. The game itself is a tactical turn-based game. Roguelite only if you fail but considering the game can be completed in a single remembrance according to the hidden achievement. This would make it just tactical turned based if you can achieve it. The Daughters are each unique in how they should be used and the combos you can pull off are satisfying when you get it just right. The main complaints for this game as that is what should be important to comment on. I wish there was more than 4 Classes, but it was Ok. The maps do get repetitive with some maps only used a handful of times. More maps, more enemies, more classes, more skills. Just more of everything and id love the game to 10/10. As it stands the repetition does begin to show itself. Important points i think should be mentioned. Game is separated into 4 Era's (Sections). When you complete one, then if and when you fail you don't have to start from the beginning. You can select a remembrance in game to start at the beginning of the Era you failed with stronger daughters. Your second run will be Recollection 2. Things by design are harsh, first encounters will sometimes end badly and sometimes you just have clearly the wrong build for the mission you entered. An example one of the bosses loves its armour, if you enter without a means to shred it, it will be quite difficult. While other bosses have no armour at all, then it’s pointless to take armour shredding. Don't be afraid especially if you failed once already to just start boss fights earlier. The game by design each fail you come back a lot stronger. I’d say 1st Recollection Brutal. 2nd Recollection is Hard. 3rd Recollection is Normal to Easy. (In fact, I found it too disappointing at Recollection 3. It really was way to easy). I strongly believe only if your going for the single recollection run, then skipping nothing matters. Maybe i will attempt this in the coming days. Kind Regards

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I bought it in a sale and despite only having it played for 10 hours for now I will get back again and again to it. The game got my interest at first because its amazing style and because it is not so easy to find good turn based strategy games. Games like Fire Emblem, FF Tactics and such classics are totally my jam but I have to admit I was a bit sceptical because of the rougelike aspect at first. Then after giving it a try this game totally took over me because of its substance. I admit I got a grasp of the systems on hard difficulty quite quickly and almost finshed two bosses in my second run already, but still this game is dope and keeps on giving me things that I really like. What I really like besides the style is the voice acting, the general atmosphere and how you build relatively thought out characters that can be used for different kinds of missions. There are some things the game could improve upon, but for me most are non issues because it is not a hugely expensive game. Don't expect a story like that of a Final Fantasy or a Fire Emblem in this genre and look at it for what it is. The whole kinda Lovecraftian theme is also cool. What I would appreciate would be maybe more classes, more character models, maybe more different types of missions and maps. So a bit more content basically, but just because I can't get enough from this game. This game is well worth your money already, more content would just be icing on the cake for me. Only thing that really needs a bit of tweaking is the AI sometimes and a couple of convenience features like sorting selecting favourite daughters so that you can revive/find them more easily or something. Obviously I wouldn't pick favourites, all my daughters are worth the same. Who am I kidding, ofc I love Melody more then Peach ;D Oh and one thing I would imagine to be fun would be some place to appreciate daughters that I sacrificed or where I can show how many atrocities they killed or something. Call me weird or whatever but I feel cold hearted for sacrificing my daughters regularly, especially those that I create only to sacrifice them again. A shrine or something could be interesting, but I mean, it is fine as is since every daughter can be revived.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games i have ever played, especially considering the price tag of merely 30, with a possibilty of a sale.-Not only is it visually very appealing to me because im a fan of black/white colors, but the red tones gives it a very elegant flavor.-The audio is very, very awesome, for the most part even better than most triple A games for a price tag around 60.-I like its gameplayelements as well, IF you like the idea of going in, reaching your limits, die and then restart all over again with stronger abilities and characters, while also having more experience with certain enemies and bosses yourself - until you eventually reach the endBut even if the system is not for you, there is a more relaxed gamemode, which is still a challenge to beat (also those 2 difficulties dont affect achievements at all)-Character design is very good, each class has its clear, own strengths (Blademaster has very hard hitting strikes, lots of mobility, and stances you can build around to synergize with other classes)(Shieldmasters main purpose is to delay enemy actions and to soak up boss damage, also deal quite underrated damage)(The Gunslingers is by far the most versatile class in my opinion, since you can build them around damage or utility in form of buffing allies or armor breaking, they re ranged by default, can interrupt actions and stack damage with other gunslingers)(4th class (to not spoiler) is very utility sided, can remove armor very quickly very easily, has multiple damage buffs and stances similar to the blademaster, and trades off a little bit of damage and mobility for range and AoE attacks)-Enemies are fair designed, especially bosses (except for the final boss, im not happy with that one sadly),most of them bosses have very unique mechanics you have to play around and they re not just a super spongy megaenemy like in other games-Lore is very complex and not fully available at the start of the game, for both antragonist but also protagonists story you have to unlock their memories first, a cool sytem, and i really love both of their stories, inthe end i think it has a lot of depth to itI thank you, Lightbulb Crew, for creating such an awesome game, and i really hope i get to see more of you guys  :)

_childDocuments_.review: A quick little review, initial impressions, take this how you will if you chose to disregard it. I picked it up cause I like FOcus Interactive and loved the art style so I gave it a gamble for 30 bucks.  got about 2 hours or so in if. Sprang for the artbook and soundtrack for as well. Overall I'm happy with my purchase. The art style is really what sells the game, commanding some ninja cuties is it's big appeal.First off - I wouldn't say Im blown away - but I had fun in the hour or so. The story is a bit baffling. Im not sure why im commanding ninja blood cuties or what the rules of the world are. Like, who is the Mother and who are The Others? Why is she guarding the veil? Is this earth? I guess this is elaborated further in but a little bit more expose for us to care about the world woulda been nice. Even if it's just some text and pictures since they had a small budget.Gameplay wise nothing too crazy. Not sure how deep the tactics really go, but surface level it looks good and I thought about my moves in the first few levels. There is no save scumming here, if one of your blood cuties dies, they die forever.  So bascially one bad move and that character can be gone instantly. Though you can resurrect them with tokens you get but not instantly, and memories you gained with them live on. It's a little confusing to take in, but basically there is perma death. I do wish there were more variety in your blood cuties, more ways to customize them. I mean that's really why Xcom sold well, you could create your own little RPG characters and command them. Woulda been nice to see more variety in looks and outfits off the bat, I'm sure later on additional options will open up, but doubt it's the customization of Xcom. Some more classes initially woulda been nice too, Im sure budget constraints prevented that though. Overall it's solid what you get and all the model assets are cool.Overall a pretty solid game, def worth 30 bucks if you're a fan of Tactics Games.I know this is pretty irrelevant but for me good art, attractive women and models is basically not existent in games nowadays so i have to support something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: interesting project, with dark theme and tactical combat. there will be plaguebearers\doctors, spirits and all other kinds of monstrosities, the enemy design is rather gruesome, stuff for nightmarescombat is turn based, one misstep may cost you a unit or a big hunk of unit HP, so you have to get used to enemy AI patterns for optimal play and understand your own strenghts and weaknesses.progression goes by Eras, each Era lasts 7 days. each day has a set of available battle encounters for which you can participate, each encounter after success locks out particiapting units until next day. you unlock boss encounter midweek which you can do anytime to progress to next Era or wait till 7th day where you'll haveno choice but to confront boss.progression system suggests that you are expected to lose over and over, starting over from the beginning (and if you managed to kill some bosses - skip some Eras that you alrady played through). basically, Game Over is not exactly that, but rather a New Beginning. you get special resources (Shards) that are accumulated from encounters you cleared and which can be used only after starting new Recollection, which is caused either by Game Over or by player deciding that enough is enough. in new Recollection you get to spend Shards to use unlocked Era skips and various power ups to support your progress3 unit types at the start (more unlocked further as you progress). Tank unit, Melee unit and Ranged unit. all have their pros and cons and skill development. Most encounters have 3 units max lockout, but some will have you take max 2 or max 4+. game suggests synergy between units, so its good if you can learn how to do combos (e.g. one unit pushes enemy close to another unit that used interrupt ability which causes them to automatically do damage when enemy enters melee range with them)what game really lacks is narrative. it is there, but it isn't at the same time. nightmarish setting probably suggests for mistery, it doesn't feel like a mistery, rather "♥♥♥♥ happens, we are not telling you why and to what end, just bear with us"overall, good game. totally recommend

_childDocuments_.review: The weakest possible recommendation.It's by no means a bad game, but it feels very same-y after a few hours.  I think some increased variety in the classes - either additional skill selections, even a whole new class - would go a long way.As it stands, every few levels you get one of two predetermined abilities for your three classes, meaning there's not much room for experimentation, seeing what works, what doesn't, high-rolling a particular set of skills, every Daughter feels equally useful but none of them feel particularly interesting or challenging.  Also, basic attacks need to just have their damage raised, you shouldn't have to equip the "Give this ability +x damage" memories on them to make them usable.Also, making the mission difficulties "Challenging", "Hard", and "Impossible" as opposed to "Easy", "Medium", "Endless enemies"... I get what they're going for but it isn't intuitive for new players, and that breaks the immersion they're going for the descriptions.  If I see a mission is described as "Impossible", my thoughts aren't "This is perfectly achievable, I just need to play it smart and I'll be fine", they're "The game is telling me I don't have the numbers to win this mission", I avoided the first survival mission until the day the Surgeon attacked because I thought I needed more levels for it, only to realize when my Daughters were level four that no, that was just telling me it wasn't possible to kill all enemies.I don't dislike it, it's a decently-executed game if X-Com-type games are your thing, but I'm just bored with it.  I only played three hours and cleared the first boss, but there was never a point where winning felt like I was truly getting one over on the game as opposed to just tediously chopping through enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Crunchy XCOM-like tactical combat without the annoying base management. Many missions can be played perfectly with smart play and the right combination of caution and aggression. Pulling that off feels great. Unit skill options support different playstyles, and I often wish I had a different skill, no matter which one I chose (they're all situationally useful).Cons: Feels like the limited map and enemy pool should result in repetitive game play, but the combat loop is so good it doesn't. A few glitches (like double-voice-triggers playing audio over itself) are annoying, and some can detract from the gameplay until you learn to account for them (mostly related to boss AOE ground indicators getting out of sync with where the effect will actually land).???s: The setting leans hard into the tropes, and plays it straight. Probably not for everyone. Art style is similarly polarizing, though the scarves turning gray is a nice touch. The unit customization allows for a lot of unique setups, but there's no characterization; they all feel replaceable. Having same-class units with different skills can get confusing ("oh, shoot, they don't have the teleport I built the plan around..." etc.).One of my favorite games in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Noir Claymore with a Lovecraftian twist.'Othercide' is an ingenious name for this game. Not only is it more obviously a play on 'Otherside', representing the Lovecraftian dimension of Unreality the 'Others' hail from, but it is also a play on 'cide'. Homicide, infanticide.. Othercide. 'Others' being this game's enemies. Gameplay is brutal initially and seems unfair since you cannot heal any of your daughters without sacrificing another (she has to be the same level or better to be sacrificed), but it gets easier as you learn the mechanics and your daughters level up. All daughters and classes are well designed and the definition of chic.Soundtrack is phenomenal and you will keep coming back to it.Story is obscure and revealed through memories you retrieve whilst in a Synapse (missions). Once you have all memories you can piece the story together and it is a 𝘨𝘰𝘰𝘥 read. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just... WOW! Such an incredible gem! First of all the art direction is astonishing (especially if you like the macabre theme). The black and white setting with splashes of red makes for a very authentic world. Those visuals are supported by more than commendable audio (shrieks, whispers and VO). The whole package is a real audiovisual treat.Secondly, and of course more importantly, this game is just a blast to play. Lovely turn based tactics and combat, where you can pull off some splendid tricks. I literally finished levels with one mouse-click (bring your Scythedancer to level 15 and you'll understand). Perhaps the gameplay isn't as unique as the art but it's rock solid nevertheless. Where the game really shone for me was the initiative order and recollection system. No Xcom-alike heroes first and enemies second setup, but a combined initiative order which can be manipulated (you feel so smart doing that). The recollection system grants you extra options and possibilities once you have to start over. It's a lovely system that balances the game for you no matter your skill level.Lastly, I really liked the 'point of view' the game has on (the) main characters. You're playing with a team of Daughters so no masculine, pumped up, brainless machos here. It felt like a fresh wind of air. Because you're Daughters all look like very fragile schoolgirls, it was even more impressive when they sliced some monstrosity in half. :)The only downside of the game is its size. There aren't that many levels, so there is an element of repetition involved (didn't bother me that much because I just luuuv it). So, devs, make my day and create some DLC!!!

They really need a tutorial for all those intricacies.Boss is super hard. I died from a boss & it restarts & my daughters are reset to starting level. Only recollection buffs remain. Either that or I don't understand the interruption system.Also, it doesn't really say how many daughters you need. & there doesn't seem to be much info about how sacrificing one does anything useful. _childDocuments_.review: A few weeks ago I lost my biological mother to covid.  This hit me pretty hard emotionally but my step-mother (the woman who raised me) was there to soften the blow that would have otherwise been disastrous. This coincided with the steam summer sale, and at that time I made the decision to pick up this game on a rather generous discount.I installed this game and right off the bat, waves of depression and grief overcame me as this game deals with the loss of someone important to the story.  After what I thought was going to just be a tutorial on how to play the game, I was never presented with a means in which to customize my 'daughters'.As an AR.NB.IOC (Aromantic Non-Binary Individual Of Color) I find it rather upsetting that I was not able to change the skin color of the units, nor was I able to update the gender pronouns of the 'sisters'.  In that respect I would give this a 2/10 stars as it does not take into consideration the mental state of the player.In comparison to a game that is much better, XCOM2, I was able to customize my units, name them, and change their skin color and I played the heck out of that game.  I guess you could say this is somewhat similar in the sense that it is isometric and turn based combat, but if you cannot customize your units you can never really feel attached to them so I didn't feel bad when my first "Blademaster" died.Overall I would say that it is a mediocre entry into the strategy genre, and would pick it up on sale for <15$ but if you really want to play a turn base strategy game you could probably just play XCOM and XCOM2.

_childDocuments_.review: So I may not have played this game for the longest time, but I absolutely love it. It is just my niche of weird and creepy, while still being really fun and engaging on the strategy game front. First I'll start with what attracted me to the game: the art style. Now obviously this will be subjective due to the nature of it being so stylised, but oh my god I love it. I didn't even know this was an art style I loved until I saw it! If it was just the monochrome black and white I wouldn't care so much, but just that splash of red does so much to bring out everything and make it as visually appealing as it is. While I'm on the superficial stuff, there's a particular song that's made its way into a couple of my playlists, and some of the VA is chilling. I'll admit, lines can get repetitive sometimes, but there's a few voices (the Deacon is coming to mind) where the delivery of those lines are just... disturbing in the best of ways. Now let's get to the meaty bits: mechanics! At a surface level it all seems rather simple. You control 3-4 units (called Daughters... did I mention this game gets weird?) each having one of three classes. The Blademaster, the damage dealer of the three, just don't let it get hit.The Shieldbearer, the tankiest of the three as well as the one most capable of controlling crowds. Mobility is on the low end though.And the Soulslinger, dual wielding pistols to provide ranged support to her sisters.Every Daughter and active enemy unit on the map gets placed on a timeline, which dictates when they get to act. Each Daughter has an amount of action points, you spend them to move and use abilities, end turn to move down on the timeline. Use up only half your action points, and you go halfway down the timeline, use up over half your points however and you end up all the way at the end of the timeline. Seems simple enough, but it's one of those systems that's easy to learn but has plenty of depth to master. How well you can manipulate and manoeuvre yourself around the timeline will dictate how successful you'll be. Though there is one thing I have yet to mention: health. What could be so special about that you ask? I'm glad you did! Your Daughters will have access to certain skills that, rather than having an action point cost, have a health cost to activate. Now you may be thinking "oh that's not too bad, you can just heal them right?" to which I'd respond with "you poor naive fool." Y'see, you can't just regain health in Othercide. If you want to heal your Daughters, you have to sacrifice another one. The health of your Daughters will not be regained in any other way. (IMPORTANT NOTE: There is an optional difficulty setting where Daughters will regain a portion of health each day. There is no shame being on this setting! It's the one I play on after all)So that then begs the question: what happens if you do lose all your Daughters? The answer is easy: you try again. Armed with the knowledge of what you now know, as well as your choosing of buffs that you can apply to your next run to give you more of a fighting chance, you keep fighting. Again. And again. Just because you have been defeated doesn't mean all is lost. The veil has been torn, time has ceased to work, reality has been fractured, so what's a few more attempts to conquer Suffering between a mother and her daughters?I am aware that last sentence probably made no sense... did I mention this game gets weird?To summarise, the foundation of this game is a solid turn based strategy game that's easy to learn with plenty of depth to master. The decoration is an absolute treat to the eyes, the story is all sorts of weird and fascinating, even if a few of the voicelines won't leave my head. Just don't be discouraged if you fail, it's almost encouraged to fail at least once!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I would recommend this game if you like XCOM and Darkest Dungeon. As for tactics games, it adds a cool initiative timeline system with the concept of taking a half turn. Also, you can never heal your units between battles without sacrificing others. You will lose units, you will lose and have to start over, it is brutal just like Darkest Dungeon.The good:Excellent art style! The scarves that your daughters wear are also HP bars. They lose their red the closer they are to dying.The timeline, with delayed moves and windups this makes initiative more than a roll.Not being able to heal units, Sounds bad, but makes HP a limited resource. It also adds strategy between fights.Boss fights are hard, and if you fail you have to start a whole new game. High stakes!The bad:Unfortunately, it gets a bit repetitive quickly.Not a large array of maps.High stakes game, just like Darkest Dungeon. If you don't like Darkest Dungeon you won't like this.Only 3 different units.The ugly:Nothing!Wrap up:If you like Darkest Dungeon and you like XCOM, you will like this. _childDocuments_.review: A very cool idea misguided by an artistic direction that tried a bit too many things at the same time making the gameplay suffer because of it.The game is good, at least the concept of it, I like the "bloodborne-ish" setting, the very vague explainations of the victorian setting and how the timeline works, both in combat but also in the overall managment of the game. Unfortunately the gameplay is barebone to say the least. I think the developers don't understand what makes these strategy game such as X-Com work, and I think it's the fact that the player has to navigate an enviroment and move forward on the map. All missions I've played so far are the opposite in this game. You just sit in the middle of the map and defend from swarms of enemies that come to you, which devolves very rapidly into "camping the center" and waiting for them to be close enough to be attacked but not close enough to attack you, by moving your units so that they are just 1 square away from the enemy, so that when they approach they can't attack. And that's literally it when it comes to gameplay. Thow your characters at the game till you have strong enough characters so you can revive them in the next run and start advantaged so you can progress further, but there is absolutely NO skill in how the game is played, it's incredibly boring.The art direction, while cool, also is boring. The black and white style looks nice for 1 hour, then the brain starts begging for colors and VFX which are nowhere to be found. I like the short cutscenes that play sometimes during combat, but they are very repetitive as the amount of em is limited and gets old quickly.One thing that I really, really dislike is the Darkest Dungeon rip-off Narrator. They just hired a lady to spout a couple of "cool" phrases, very much like DD Narretor does. The problem here is that these phrases aren't cool and the language isn't interesting, they sound flat and uninspired. The fact that they are very few makes it even worse. You'll costantly hear the same 3-4 phrases repeated over and over and over during gameplay.Overall, I strongly suggest NOT to buy the game, not even on discount, as the core gameplay is boring, repetitive and grindy. They attempted to create a mix of darkest dungeon and roguelite with x com elements in it, which is amazing on paper, but entirely failed to understand what made these games great.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, it's a masterpiece. This game sets the tone to be challenging and imaginative all while pulling you into the world it's made. It creatively explores fundamentals about turn-based fighting and team synergy. For certain, it re-invents how you look at initiative and turn order. As forewarning, the game isn't kidding; you will lose teammates, and keeping a healing teammates is a struggle, if not a luxury, but the game rewards you for being resilient and adaptive, as it gets easier and easier every time you recollect and start over.To unpack a little, Othercide is a story of suffering and sacrifice. In a place where the veil between reality and unreality has been torn, you raise and guide daughters bored from the blood of a mysterious but loving woman called "The Mother" to slice, bash and shoot your your way through thralls of twisted nightmares in hopes to reach a haunted child at its center and close this rift.The art magnificent from the painterly character designs to the stylized choice of only using one color among the blacks, whites and greys. The soundtrack combines haunting violins and cellos with a kick of rock whenever the battles get tense. The story is a glass menagerie you find more hidden depth to the more you piece together by finding memories and defeating bosses. The mechanics of strategy for both you and your enemies with all this smashed together births a captivating game that challenges and presses you to dive deeper and deeper into darkness to find a way out.I'm not one for turn-based games, but I got this game at full price and stand by my word that it's worth every penny. It's an underrated hidden gem, so give it a go, especially if it's on sale! This game is original in every way I can think of, and if the developers ever choose to expand further on the vast world they've created, either by opening it up for mod creation or adding additional gameplay content, there's no telling where Othercide could go!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. I've finished the game. The reviews on this game are all over the place. So I'll try to clarify the main points on most of the reviews : 1) IS THIS GAME HARD ? Yes and no. There is a lot of whining about the difficulty of this game. READ THE IN-GAME CODEX. Every monsters is explained after you have fought it. Every monster got an IA and in THE CODEX IT IS EXPLAINED HOW EVERY MONSTERS ACT. Some monsters attack the closer daughter, some the one with most HP, some the one attacked by other monsters, etc. You could actually predict every single monsters next move, every fight could be kinda like chess. This game it is hard if you usually play super-easy-game that require no brain, just clicking to kill. I'll say that this game it is a MEDIUM difficulty game. You have all the data to make the best move in every fight. If you make a mistake, it is YOUR FAULT, not the game fault.2) IS THIS GAME A GRIND-FEST ? No. You unlock remembrances by the achivement of several objectives (Kill a boss, doing a certain amount of damages, and so on), and with those "remembrances" you could start from a certain "age" (=Stage), or with your daughters on level 5 or 7 etc instead of level 1, and so on. So you could reduce the grind by A LOT if you want.3) YOU SHOULD KILL YOUR DAUGHTERS TO HEAL YOUR DAUGHTERS !!!Not necessarly. There are two difficulties that you could choose at the beginning of the game : Dream or Nightmare. In dream your daughers heal after each day, in nightmare not, so you should "kill" your daughters to heal another daughter. This is one of the main and most peculiar mechanincs in this game AND I REALLY LIKED IT. Let me explain better this point : (a) There are "resurrection sigils" that you could unlock by doing specific missions, so you lose the girls but you could also resurrect them during a run (b) If you use a daughter to heal another one, the healed one TAKE THE ESSENCE OF THE ONE YOU HAVE SACRIFICED (=lot of bonus). More, to kill the most advanced boss you should use this mechanics not to heal but to exchange the essences between your strongest daughters, to make them killing-machines. I really loved this mechanic.4) BUT THE IA IS STUPID, SOMETIMES ATTACK, SOMETIMES NOT, AND... (Whining whining whining, excuses excuses excuses) Not. Every monsters like I've already told you, got a pre-programmed IA, that you could find in the CODEX. The monsters DO NOT ATTACK (usually) on the turn that they spawn not because they are stupid or for a "bug", but because it is an in-game rule. And NO, the monsters do not attack you from the spawn point (the exception it is if your daughters....).5) THERE ARE NOT ENOUGH MONSTERS !!!!I think there are around 20 types of monsters. Enough for a 20-30 hours game. And yes some of them are an upgraded version of the weakest one, and that it is ok. Even just 10 monsters with different kind of IA and attacks are enough for this game. 6) THE BOSSES ARE UNFAIR, AND FOR THE LAST ONE YOU SHOULD GRIND A LOT !!!Boys and girls. This is a turn-combat game with RPG elements. Do you whine when in your rpg you couldn't kill monsters above your level ? I do not think so. You just go to some secondary quest, or you go farm monsters. Same here. Yes, you should probably do a couple of run just to farm "resurrection sigils" and exchange the essences between your strongest daughters, but THAT'S IT. And btw, again, in every run you unlock stuffs, so it is never wasted times. And btw, you could resurrect daughters from another run with the "resurrection sigils". So you never lose "forever" your favourite daughters. 7) THE STORY IS NOT EXPLAINED, IT DOES NOT MAKE SENSE ! Blame dark souls. There is a lore explained in a souls-like way, and there is a main plot. I would say that there is an ATMOSPHERE more than a story in this game. And that's ok. Do not play this game for story or characters, play this game for the gameplay and the art....That's said, this game got an amazing soundtrack, and an amazing atmosphere. The art is very peculiar, and I really loved it. I loved that this game was trying to do something different from others games, with an indie budget. I would love to see this game evolve in-to an actually souls-like game, or something similar, but not everyone are the from-software, or got enough money to do so.FINAL QUESTION : Is this a 30 dollars game ? Not sure about it, but if you find it under 10 bucks, you like the genre and grim atmospheres, you could buy this one. I would give that a 7 out of 10. Buy especially if like me you love to just listen to some courses, or youtuber, or whatever, while playing something for the gameplay...this game is perfect for that.

_childDocuments_.review: is a turn-based strategy involving some future event, and the need to produce daughters to circumvent this event that seems to be at some point in the future or past, during the opening of the game. Gameplay involves a good bit of grinding at its core concept. You can gain points to invest into direct abilities, and unlock things in each zone as you go along. Losing a few times is actually not such a bad thing in this game near the beginning, since you will accumulate more to spend on some of your unlocks, which you can then use to give you a slight edge.I want to make one thing fairly clear though. The game itself is not actually extremely difficult. I do not consider this roguelike either. Permadeath is there for your current run, but it doesn’t really fit many other qualifications for the genre. I would say the difficulty is in a sort of , meaning it’s grindy, and time-consuming to raise your daughters, of which there are several classes with varying abilities. The learning curve is the only problem, then it becomes somewhat clockwork in nature. Some of the daughters were unbalanced when I played last. The big issue with the way the grind system is set up is that inherited traits of classes are the same for each class type, and you only get one, which is in red on your skills for the daughter that received the benefit from a daughter of a higher level, where the lower level will inherit the said trait. This is why the game is so grindy. You can also pick up random debuffs/buffs to stats that can be permanent, or practically permanent based on things your characters do while in battle. Another thing upon leveling is you gain extra usable battle skills. You can choose one or the other and it can vary depending on which you want to keep, given the situation.There were several types of situations one might end up in, ranging from surviving all waves, to reaching a goal, or escorting missions and some other various types. You may choose to skip right to bosses, bypass bosses altogether, or do other things depending on how far along you are in the game. I thought some of the bosses were hard, but once you learn what they do in each phase, you can find ways to take certain counter-measures. Most are not too hard to figure out, but there was a bit of randomness and trial and error for me. Supplementing with a guide for ideas on how to effectively play is useful, since the game didn’t really explain it too well at the time I played, in my opinion.Pretty graphics, with a noir and red style of background. The daughters reminded me a little bit of 2B or something similar, and the music paired well with the game’s overall feel and mood. The setting and plot are hard to understand much about, but things get revealed to you as you go, and there are sections to examine for unlocks, extra enemy information (which I cannot stress the importance of enough, as it reveals attack patterns, weaknesses and strengths to take advantage of), and other such things, which can be viewed in the menu any time once you’ve unlocked them.You can gain other abilities which can be applied manually to your daughters when you meet the right conditions. They are usually chance-based, but if a condition meets all unlock requirements, it’s possible to get these orbs which can be later added. They are removed after a game ends. Your daughters you lose can be resurrected as well later on as you open up more abilities, so a complete wipe isn’t necessarily a bad thing in many cases in this game. Early on you probably won’t really  be worried about specific daughters, and may instead try to get a few with some good overall stats, since these can vary.While I think the game is good, I also think there is a lot of untapped potential in what is possible with this system and the way it was done during the time I played this game.Lots of customization is possible. More is possible with further optimization and unlocks, further adding to possibilities.Nice graphics, and the gameplay is fun early on, as I got introduced to the game. It can get a little bit repetitive, due to only a few classes of daughters to choose from, thus limiting your movesets.I liked the counter-attack system, and the attack time grid at the bottom of the screen. This could be somewhat exploited early on, but as far as I’m aware, most instances of this have been hit with the nerfbat.Decent amount of variations, and different ways to play, based on how you choose to set up your party. Good to strategize, since you can only fight once per day and need a rest with daughters. There is an easier mode where resting gains life. I never tried the other mode as of yet though.The game could use more enemy types, varied attacks, and different characters and encounters. While the game is fun, it is still tedious and a bit predictable at certain points, depending on how familiar you get to creature habits and how to move your daughters efficiently to get the most out of them.The roguelite elements are only having to do with earning extra currency to buy more skills as you unlock them with progression. This value only decreases in the current game, and you continue to gain more as you fail.Very grindy when I played. This is what ultimately made me take a break from playing. I still don’t really feel like finishing this yet, but I do believe it will be enjoyable to jump back into playing again sometime and see how it is now compared to when I played it in October or November.The battle speed was a bit slow too. Even speeding things up, it was a bit of an annoyance to wait on everything to finish turns.Just felt inefficient and unbalanced having to grind and keep levels close, so I could then add stats in sacrifices.Good foundation here, but I see a lot that could be built upon. I personally felt that this game should have been in Early Access or beta still when I played.Way too expensive for the amount of material in the game, however it still feels like a higher quality game than many out there, most likely thanks to publishing and development making polished and crisp graphics a big priority. The scenes and action bits are quite nice in presentation, so I did enjoy some of the cutscenes.Some of the voicing would mess up, be silent, or overlap. Not sure if this was corrected or not.  It’s also a bit repetitive since there are not a huge amount of phrases.No 9S in this game. Why can’t there be some dudes around?! I’m probably out of room now, but this one is tough for me to swing one way or the other. Paired with the expensive price, I recommend this but with some caution. It’s not a game for everybody, and the tags are a bit misleading. Buyer beware! Still a nice game overall, but I hope there have been some improvements since I last played. I’ll update if I decide to finish the game and go for all the achievements! All in all this one is worth a go, but do not run into it with majorly high expectations!Game curator review made possible thanks to  for allowing me to review this, courtesy of

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions:TL;DR:Othercide is a blend of genres that isn't seen very often,but works surprisingly well. On the one hand there is the Turn-Based combat that can almost rival XCOM in terms of depth. It's easy to learn but hard to master. Making full use of all the options given will require lots of strategic thinking. This paired with the punishing difficulty makes prevailing here hugely satisfying.And while it is certainly hard, it doesn't feel unfair. Looking back at a turn, you can almost always identify something that you could've done differently to prevent a characters death, due to the large amount of options the game gives you, in terms of skills, movement and special character traits.On the other hand you have a lot of Roguelite elements sprinkled in there, that will allow you to make progress and get stronger even if you fail. And you will fail - but like any good Roguelite, Othercide mixes things up from run to runby having a degree of randomization, as well as allowing the player to shape the outset of a run.Add to all of that the unique, dark aesthetic and you have yourself a recipe for greatness.An experience that I recommend to anyone that even remotely enjoys turn-based combat games!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? This game was hard to get into. The fact that it became repetitive after 2 hours due to the lack of variety in the maps made it feel weird. However this game grew on me the more I played it. Don't get me wrong it does feel repetitive at times HOWEVER the gameplay is what carries this game along with the unique artstyle that accompanies this game. This game is less intense compared to XCOM. I would say this game is comparable to a game of chess. Every unit u control and move must have a move planned ahead of time to ensure success in missions. The mechanic of using AP which decides what u can do per turn helps elevate the feeling of playing chess across this game and it's what got me hooked despite it being repetitive. The gameplay mechanic of having your daughters heal only when you sacrifice another daughter adds a layer of depth that I didn't think was possible. Do you heal the lower level daughter to invest into her development? Or do you keep the high level daughter despite her having low health. Such questions are asked while you are playing the game. Trust me you are meant to die but through each death you adapt your tactics, get more powerful daughters, get more powerful relics to start each run. Each run that you do in this game has a purpose and certain elements are carried onto the next run. This is a very good roguelike game worth your money. Yes it will get repetitive but the feeling of killing your first boss after multiple runs is so satisfying I would compare it to dark souls. This game is harsh, annoying, anger inducing but man I am having one hell of a time with this game and the atmosphere and lore behind it

_childDocuments_.review: It was hard to click "no" on this one because it's such a mixed bag for me.  I love, love, LOVE the style of this.  The aesthetic to it, the music, the voice acting... it's all just so freakin' cool.  I want the Warhammer people to see this and give this developer a license to do fifty Sisters of Battle games, they've nailed how that should look, feel, and sound.Ultimately, though, it pains me to admit that this just quickly becomes not that fun a game.  I'm a big fan of tactical turn based squad games but this one becomes both repetitive and convoluted very quickly.  I was impressed by how novel the whole system was of pushing units around on the initiative line, but it wasn't meaningful enough to be all that useful.  And the interaction and complicated chain of events that could be set up between all the units and enemies interacting, especially in the boss battles... well it could have made for a chess match but instead it just gets so weird and convoluted that I feel like I need to put my data analytics training to work and build a machine learning algorithm just to figure out how to take my turn.  Information can be difficult to dig out of the interface (I'm still not sure if there's a way to view individual unit trait effects during a battle and that can be important) so you end up either having to remember or keep notes.  And I found myself having to do entirely too much math in my head to figure out what kind of combos I might be able to pull off.  What could have been cool if the information was presented effectively just became a chore.One little change to the whole RPG combat trope that I thought was great was how hit points don't regenerate between battles.  You can win the battle and still lose the war, I thought that added and interesting element to it.  Unfortunately that's coupled to a grind that's designed for you to fail.  You play a bunch of missions, you fail but win some bonuses, and then you try the same thing again.  That doesn't make for a satisfying game loop, because you don't feel like you won.  You just come away feeling like you persevered long enough that the game eventually felt sorry for you and gave you enough bonuses so you could proceed.I liked the haunting nature of the story but that suffers from obfuscation and complication as well.  I'm sure it all ends up being some kind of deep metaphorical look at mental trauma or something like that, but it's presented all abstract and weird so you spend more time trying to guess what's going on than you do enjoying it.  Maybe it all makes sense in the end but the journey purposely just leaves you a little too lost and confused for my taste.I love this as a collection of novel ideas.  I adore it as a piece of art and style.  I wish I could say I liked it as a game, but I just don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to the XCOM franchise, this is a turn based strategy game. Due to it being an Indie game, it has not been advertised widely. But it is a hidden gem of a game.The game has a medieval horror setting, but it is not overdone. The in-game animation, art and soundtracks are done perfectly. Especially, the use of only three colours throughout the game (black, white and red), which perfectly conveys the desolate and unforgiving vibe in the game.The game expects you to lose, you cannot finish the game in a single run. But it rewards your run by progressively unlocking more powers and levels on your daughters (the heros that you control) in your subsequent runs. I recommend the 2nd difficulty mode for getting the true experience( there are two difficulty modes - 1st one heals your daughters for 10% hp at the end of each day, while the other doesn't). In the 2nd difficulty, the damage taken by your daughters are carried forward to the subsequent missions. The only way you can heal is by sacrificing other daughters of a similar or higher level. Even some of your stronger skills in mission require you to sacrifice hp to perform. So you have to weigh the cost/benefits. The monsters are also well designed and the boss fights are epic. You also can't abuse the save option as the game auto-saves and doesn't allow you do do manual saves.The in-game story and lore are also engaging and keeps you hooked. If you are a fan of the turn based strategy genre, definitely give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good.Replayable. I thought it would get boring, but it really does not.Innovative unit level-up mechanics too.You are forced to 'blend' your units into more powerful combinations to progress deeper into the game. Its pretty cool. Starting squads will all die, you cant beat bosses with starting units. But what game forces you to do, is take your starting squads, get them killed, and combine survivors into more and more powerful characters... And so it goes. And as you get deeper, you collect trinkets that let you skip the level grind of fresh characters. After boss 1, your units start at level 4. After boss 2, units start at level 7. And so on. And you can skip bosses as well on your subsequent runs. Clever.Combat forces you to think for once. its not a steamroll at higher levels. Key abilities like overwatch, stuns and interrupts cost health, not action points. And there is no healing in the game (other then blending in the character management screen). And you can only blend units of equal level. So yeah, your characters have a shelf life, they are NOT expendable, and it forces you to think which unit to take into battle, because you have to keep multiple copies of toons roughly in equal levels - spares are used in healing/blending. No powerlevelling for U, in other words.Anyways, its a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide combines compelling tactical RPG combat, a la Final Fantasy Tactics, XCOM, or Fire Emblem, with Dark Souls style unforgiving play, all done in an art style that is a masterful blend of beauty and discomfort. Othercide has changed my mind about its entire genre.To respond to some of the criticisms I've seen in other reviews, the indie studio that developed this clearly didn't have the budget to implement--and balance--procedural stage generation. What they did do is create a few different maps for each era for each of a few different mission types and ensure that combat was dynamic enough to feel fresh even on subsequent playthroughs of same or similar missions.The other thing I want to address is the lack of healing--mistakes having permanent costs are a core part of the game. While most other games allow us to slowly recover from mistakes over time, this one does not--our mistakes build up until ultimately we're either able to succeed despite them or decide to try again. The Recollections system, whereby players can customize subsequent playthroughs, is the payoff--if you had particular trouble against Scavengers, you can activate the anti-Nightmare Recollection for extra damage against those targets. If your Daughters were too squishy, there are Recollections for boosting their maximum health, and there are even Recollections for giving us resurrection tokens with every run.GAME MECHANIC SPOILERS BELOW:Resurrection tokens can be used to fully heal two Daughters of any level by sacrificing one of them to heal the other, then resurrecting the sacrificed Daughter. This not only fully heals them both but also grants the receiving Daughter a permanent boon based on the sacrificed Daughter's class and stats. Imo the game doesn't make this option clear enough--I personally couldn't see myself pushing far with any single run without using it, so I'm sharing it here for others who need it but might have missed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with what the game does very well, and that's its style. It has incredible visuals and music, my tense battle against a boss where both sides were being beaten down and it could absolutely go either way, was far more epic than anything I encountered in X-com or x-com 2. In that regard it's amazing. Unfortunately, and this is why I don't recommend the game, the actual overall gameplay is designed really poorly. Not the tactical part of battles which are decent though not amazing, but the overall strategic layer ruins the whole game.The only way you have to heal any of your characters from the damage they take in battle is to sacrifice another character of the same level as that character. Which has a few consequences, you need to grind up throwaway characters so they're a high enough level to use to heal your good team, you are penalized for using many of your abilities that pay with health to use in battle, receiving any damage at all in battle is catastrophic. In my case I had an amazing fight with a boss, lost one of my team and the other two barely survived. That battle was an amazing experience... unfortunately trying to continue the game after that was futile, new characters were not high enough level to survive missions to grind up to heal my good characters who were on death's door. Even if I managed to level them up enough, I would just be putting all that time and effort in just to throw those characters away, it just all feels so pointless and a huge waste of time.There is some mechanic in the game that I didn't use, as it feels like cheating. You're able to restart the game but you get extra bonuses at the start, the effect being that you're essentially able to use cheat codes of increasing power every time you start the game over again. This again feels pointless, because if you do that your success in the game is determined only by how long you play and not how well you play, eventually you will just have enough bonuses to win.It's a shame because the visuals, music and atmosphere could make an amazing game if the core gameplay was any good

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a decent game that I would say have lots of pros and cons. The game is a tactical turn based gothic based game. I have been playing this game for 11 hours thus far and I have noticed some really annoying elements in the game. Some are hits and some are misses. Then some are just awful. There are only so many variety amount of missions. Hunt, Rescue, Ritual, Survival, Penance Mission. There are also tons of enemy differences and as you progress in the game, the enemies become harder of course. But your Sisters you have, as they level up or rank up, should be able to deal with the coming enemies. I give this game a 7.5/10. I would rent this game or wait for it to go on sale. I have only beaten the first and second boss and will probably beat the third soon. Yes I plan on beating the entire game. Pros- Art style, amazing- Soundtrack- Graphics - Customization- Healing system (sacrificing your sisters)- Traits system- Shard system- Vitae system- Resurrection - Boss design (amazing boss design)- Memory System- Random Events- Move set list of enemy.Okay- Steep Learning Curve Per Level- Mistakes are super punishing- You have to think ahead - 3 classes, with 2 skills per mastery . LVL (1,3,5,10,15) - Understanding  the difficulties. ( Hard, Challenging, Impossible)- - Understanding the AI. Each enemy has its own personality. Some will literally bum rush the first sister it sees. Others will move away once you get close. Sometimes an enemy will move literally HALF THE MAP, and still get a swipe at you. Like WHAT?. Even through careful positioning and planning, you have to learn the AI. This can be a little frustrating as you progress to new areas. Cons- Burst system (not a big fan of)- RNG (Every hit matters and you will most rarely dodge) - The lack of feeling of an accomplishment.  (Very minimal)Awful- Enemy can sometimes spawn on top of you because there is no control where they spawn which can lead you to getting smacked on their first turn which idk why they included that in the system. Especially the Infected which can even buff their allies. - Some of the enemy types are just insane such as that Larvas or Infected. When they root or pair up with other enemies that can move fast they can really catch you by surprise and you may not do any damage to them due to shields.- Most Enemies take more than 1 hit to kill and the burst system makes you have to prioritize which enemies are dangerous, but can you leave your sisters opened to other possibilities of attack if you decide to use your entire stamina bar. Most of the time you are surrounded by enemies and you will take damage. ESPECIALLY SINCE THERE IS NO TRUE HEALING SYSTEM. Yes, you are expected to fail or take massive amounts of damage, but why spawn so many enemies on top of me or why have them hit across the ENTIRE MAP. - There is a delayed action queue on the timeline, but why does it not show how long buffs last. You never know when a 680 shield or a 150 shield from an enemy runs out in a fight and you don't even know when your buff runs out. - Under leveled sisters. After you beat a boss, you can have 1 or 2 or all sisters alive, but your sisters will most likely have taken a big chunk of damage especially if you are fighting the boss for the first time. You are forced to go into the next area, but you want to use your sisters that might be of lower rank to accomplish the mission. You are most likely going to have a hard time clearing the level or you might lose those sisters. _childDocuments_.review: The game is enjoyable but I disagree when others compare it to Darkest Dungeon.This game doesn't feel crisp, it lacks some major polish making some parts of it feel rather clunky.- The camera feels really bad, selecting a unit to read about it/see it's range will force lock it on the target for a few seconds. The enemy range also extends when you're 1 tile away? But they can't actually hit you despite the game showing you they can. - Occasionally a melee enemy (the little crawler guys) will attack me from a range? _childDocuments_.review: I actually had to switch my review from down to up, I can own up to speaking too soon.I originally thought that the game loop revolved around one boss (the one at "7 days"), and it would seem pretty repetitive/pointless to keep having to replay just those 7 days to kill it and be done. I was wrong, there was several bosses after him (each 7 days after you beat one boss), and for every step different enemies and maps open up.I loved the style and some of the improvement over your conventional tactical turn-based approach (you can do more each turn, but it will cost you "initiative" which means the next turn for that character will came later), but there is one: One, the interface is very poor, you never really know what things mean, or even what traits are active. Sometimes one of your characters have an "aura", but ... which character? what aura? you have to find out moving around. It is somewhat complicated, I think a small icon for each aura/passive skill on the character bar would be a huge improvement.The game is somewhat repetitive but each play is different in the way that you will have to build up your "daugthers" again, and there is a lot of random traits and skill you get along the way. You can revive "daugthers" from previous runs, but it is kind of costly so you will probably do it with only one or two.In the end, other than the interface lacking some information value, since this is a game where every bit of information is important, is a little distracting, but it just makes you the more focused on thinking your moves thorugh.

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a game, pun intended. The game is a mixture of atmosphere of Bloodborne/Thr Order, the turn-based combat system of shadowrun, and the  rogue-like gameplay of Darkness Dungeon. After the short intro, the game stops holding your hand and leaves you to figure out the game for yourself. A lot of trial and error involved in this game, and it tests your aversion limit to failure; invested time spent on upgrading characters or progressing in a certain match could be over with a wrong move or with a wrong team composition. The replayability of the game stems from failure as the player has to start all over again, but the game is bit forgiving as it accumulate tokens from previous game to spend on future game. On topic of New Game +, game can get repetitive when you know the mechanics and have farmed enough tokens to overpower new game +. Overall it is a very stylish and fun game that respects the players intelligence and rewards risk taking. Well worth the money I spend on Othercide.

_childDocuments_.review: So I don't often write reviews for games, but I feel for this one I really should try to inform people who are looking to buy the game...I see a lot of the negativity around this game based on the fact it's a bad Rogue-lite game. Let me make this super, super clear. This isn't a Rogue-lite. No where in it's marketing does it call itself a rogue-lite, no where on it's website or Steampage does it call itself a Rogue-lite, it's just the community who has slapped that title on the game. The confusion around this comes from the fact the game plays off of a Time-loop where if you reach a game over, you go back to the start of the game to try again with a new unit roster and a new chance to approach challenges that might of cost you a lot previously with new strategies. For example, if you find in a stage a monster has thorns and melee units get hurt by attacking him, you might want to build a more solid ranged team to overcome that on your next run. The game isn't perfect, but I think it's a really solid Tactics game, and a lot of the critisism I see against it is really misplaced and silly. Complaining that this game is a bad Rogue-lite is about as useful as complaining that Ocarina of time is a bad FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: So you go out with this chick. She is great, intelligent, hot, a real catch. You're even considering marrying her already. But by the end of the night you discover she has a ♥♥♥♥ and it's bigger than yours. So if you want to know why*, before you buy it lets keep this in mind:Pros:* Art concept is awesome.* Core game mechanic is fine. Not super complicated, but not dumb either, but**...* Base classes are ok. You can be strategical or extremely overpowered.* Presentation is souls-like. Very subjective and you have to piece things together.* All bosses are fine, but ***.* It is challenging, but ***.Cons:* UI could use an improvement with the revive/forget Daughters. It is too prone to f'ing up.* The recollection loop is dumb just because you have to re-select your remembrances over and over again. What a tedious f!* AI is simplistic to a point of being unfair. See **.* There is no good end game loop.* ** The game core mechanic relies on initiative push/pull. This is not a problem if it wasn't unbounded. This means that some mobs can decrease their initiative and go before your daughters artificially creating a infinite loop. I had this happening with the four-legged-wobbling-worm-thing that buffs def where they were acting 3 times per daughter before I had a chance to play while also buffing their defense. I quit the fight because both had 3000+ def. Oh my see **** *** This is the sole reason why this game is a cluster ♥♥♥♥ of bad game design choices put in a cauldron of big ♥♥♥♥♥. Last boss abuses the initiative push/pull to a point that is unfair. From what I've seen the boss is also heavily bugged with most of its description being wrong. Not only that as it change phases the fight gets exponentially harder to a point it will be 1 shooting your Daughters. This boss took me 6~8 hours of seeing the boss auto attacking me with long f'ing animations while I was watching Becker.An in all the game is not bad, but the last boss experience is why the thumbs down. I can't possibly allow another human being to have the same experience. I was thinking to myself "She is a great girl! I really like her! ♥♥♥♥! But she has a ♥♥♥♥! And double ♥♥♥♥ its bigger than mine too!". And yeah I went all the way and I felt relief finishing it. Puns aside I hope they balance not only the final game, but the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Reason i'm not recommending it is because its niche and does not cover Roguelite tag (which i personally picked up because it had one) it's misleading.Each tl;dr will have more detailed explanation down below, but my current statement is that this game is worth only half the price of it's original. It looks polished, but when you play you notice its design is scaled in a fashion that forces you to rebirth with additional boons that help you scale accordingly. Lacks actual rogue style elements and strongest impressions it gives are first couple of hours, each boss and the ending. It has very little to no replay value.TL;DR what's wrong, what's right ?The right stuff,Theme (world end, last hope of humanity, apocalypse, the last stand) with stylistic presentation, music, ui, character models, animations and even map designs (details that go beyond boundaries of play field) all of it is fresh, unique and well made.I absolutely adore xcom unit treatment system. No matter how much you invest in a unit, he's not immortal. All it takes is couple of slips and you're caught in regret of investing so much in one character. Each character with minimal characteristic differences grow differently and you get attached to them, maybe you start playing "doll house" and imagine them interacting with each other or bonding as they go trough missions and handle hardships. Them being veterans they soon  lead team of newcomers just to form new bonds as mistakes become memorable events that change dynamics and fill pages of story that entail them all. Emotional gymnastics and biased decisions i make as i'm being tormented by difficult decisions is what i love. Being emotional masochist this game caters to my needs.Most memorable, memory,  being first boss fight, all daughters in range of a deadly aoe attack. Only one daughter can move before it goes down, she can move boss, but only in 2 directions. Either she dies, or other sisters. Being my favorite and grown attached to her i made my decision with a heavy heart, it was a calculated and best one i could have taken ... is what i kept telling to myself. Just as memorable were equal level veterans sacrificing themselves to squeeze out more progress out of a run.The wrong stuff,While not excessively, everything else. Replayability, for average player getting trough whole story takes 40-50hours. Once you are done, you are. There are no roguelike random elements aside from 1 measly buff for that days missions (which is called an "Event"). Skill enchant system (memories) drop from specific mobs at certain percentage chance, traits (that give characters minimal boosts) are condition based with chance percentage once meeting conditions. Maps are hand tailored (assuming as i've done several new saves and noticed a lot of repeats) mob spawn locations are also handpicked. Mission types differ minimally between each type. It's the same thing every time, go to a mission, clap some naughty sister cheeks without getting hit and you're done. Repeat.Also bugs, convoluted/unclear inspection system with half predictive stats making first 20 hours very "shot in the dark" experienceDespite this game having so many rewards and good reviews i'm pretty sure they were given on same basis as i sung praise for this game in earlier stages of the game. I got hooked up on it, but as i slept on it soon this impression dissipated. Visual style is done right, theme and premise, story, additional lore is done in concise simple, but also captivating way. Few music tracks, like mainscreen "Soulswap" , first boss phase switch is absolutely on point and immersive. It feels like a proper masterpiece, but it falls short in progression, depth and clarity aspect gameplay wise.As you progress you meet enemies, after reaching certain milestone you meet next tier version of said enemies that coincidentally have (on average) twice that stats previous tier had and once you get to the next one, same thing applies. Thus restarting shortly after every milestone is unavoidable as you can't keep up with the numbers. Missions from each other differ in their completion objective, but overall will feel just like any typical Hunting mission.I'm not exactly sure where the randomness comes in that's attributed as key feature for rogue genre. Maps are hand crafted and so are spawn locations. At times in predictable patterns. Scaling, gearing, improving system. Each character upon its creation has different starting stats. (Minimal difference, but because of slow rate of growth, could be significant in order to min/max) As one levels up they gain skill at certain levels. They have a choice between 2 every time and a slot which can boost stats by equipping "memory". Which most of the time doesn't show how they interact with it. Or that this skill is being affected by the boost or have one to begin with, there are no indications when you are on about in the battle. You have no idea, unless you document it. Outside of memories and skills there is trait system. Minor buffs which are obtained by completing certain conditions you are not told (wiki has all documented), some of them despite meeting conditions still have percentage chance. Couple more desired traits have counterintuative conditions. Aside from this there is Remembrance system. Boons you obtain by fulfilling conditions. These conditions are mentioned in the journal. To acquire them you need to finish missions which give a currency and you have to rebirth to redeem the said currency. This is effectively is a catchup mechanic, giving ridiculously strong boons. Both stat and mechanic wise. From which (damage percentage boons) are not displayed into calculation until the moment you strike the enemy.Ui and clarity. It's awful as mentioned before some memories don't display their stat effects when hovering over the skill. Neither do the boons from remembrance system. Worse is when timeline in battle doesn't show duration of the buffs, debuffs of your units or enemy, but wait, it gets worse. You have the ability to click on the enemy in battle and review their skills, range which most of the time (the range) doesn't show up or is misaligned. Enemies in journal have tips about their behavior, but some of them change between different tiers making it convoluted.  Now the fun part, the bugs.I didn't experience any bugs or issues for first 20 hours, then they started popping in or i just started to notice them. In a boss battle i lost the ability to move my map around with wasd. This lead my battle against the boss significantly harder as enemy behind it (which was my desired target) could not be targeted as i hovered over it, boss stat information window would popup and hide it behind it ... Another instance, or more like recurring one is when enemy units sprawl over intersections of the fields. Meaning. Unless i however over the right quadrant, i don't know which one is he on visually. I've also had a bug where enemy would grow 4 times it's size in the background as my unit attacks something in the foreground and stays like that blocking half the map behind it. And making it virtually impossible to see attack range of the enemies behind it. In other news, i've had a instance where enemy spawns in without character model, being invisible. (I failed that battle and redid it with another group) This time, literally the same culprit as before would spawn in (note when enemies spawn in, if they are ranged they can only move, if they are melee and spawn next to someone they can attack, but generally move if there is at least one square inbetween without attacking) popup behind a unit thats over 20 squares away, perform a backstab attack of over 1k and return to his spawning location.All these reasons add up to me not recommending this game, but honestly, for me at least, it's worth the experience. I feel problem to me is that once im done with it ... it's just going to sit in my library as a ... memory
