_childDocuments_.review: Few games have blown my mind as often as this one has. I was often left genuinely surprised by audio cues, certain story elements, when I passed a particularly difficult stage, when a Daughter miraculously survives or when an already 'trait-heavy' Daughter gains a new trait making them even stronger. Game felt very satisfying (if tedious at times) and I am very interested to see which direction any sequels will take, should there ever be any. Interesting Great (probably even better with an OLED display) Fantastic. Very atmospheric and complemented boss fights and certain situations very well Challenging and enjoyable, although repetitive towards the end As described, however a certain skill from a certain class trivialises the difficulty (but that's not until the very end game, so it's ok) A few, but nothing game-breaking.- Turn timeline can get a bit messed up sometimes- Found a wall I could stand in on one map- Found one exploit where I could extend the range of an attack under certain conditions- Story is an interesting concept, however you need to 'unlock' the backstory to get the full context. I managed unlock it all in one or two full playthroughs so it's not that hard to do. - Art style was pretty good too and I really liked the use of language in some parts as well. - Despite all being clones, there is enough variety in the Daughters to tell them apart. - Good variety of skills to accommodate different play styles and situations.I found the language questionable in parts with odd grammar and phrasing.Daughters sounded a little too identical and often indistinguishable from the Mother.A lot of memories were either identical in effect to other memories or were otherwise superfluous.I felt the need to take a long break from the game due to it getting tedious at one point.

_childDocuments_.review: On the onset, the twists on the X-Com format Othercide takes I thought were pretty engaging and unique. And they ARE unique. But, as I played on, restarted the campaign a few time (which is a built-in mechanic), the mechanics that set Othercide apart, for me, quickly grew tedious.Personally, the biggest appeal  for the turn-based, squad oriented tactics games is taking a rag-tag group of soldiers and watching them grow and become attached as they become powerhouses, losing some soldiers here and there. X-com excels particularly well at this - it's what creates the battle to battle drama and tension.Herein lies I think the main problem with Othercide, while at the same time I acknowledge it as probably what  they intended to be their defining and most unique gameplay feature. See, due to the mechanics of failure and progression, your soldiers ("daughters") are largely expendable. In order to heal a soldier after each encounter, you have to sacrifice (kill) another one. Granted, killed daughters aren't gone forever. They go to the cemetery, which carries over to each playthrough. But each new playthrough you get 3 new daughters, which, again, you will grind to level up and inevitably have to sacrifice to heal others in order to have a healthy team for boss encounters. Now, there are mechanics that allow you resurrect dead daughters, who retain their stats, traits, etc. That, in essence, is how you go about creating a "powerhouse" team, through a long cycle of sacrificing and resurrecting your soldiers across many restarted campaigns. But, though an interesting mechanic, I think its a mechanic that is ultimately off-putting. You can see how this then becomes a tedious cycle of grinding cannon fodder, until they are leveled up enough to be able to be sacrificed to heal your actual priority daughters - that's how it actually ends up being played out - and it just takes away the attachment and tension X-com creates while making the game (at least the first 15 hours or so) kind of a bore. There are unlocks and such as you play that alleviate a bit of this, but it never got to a point where the actual slog was all that circumvented..The traits system is fun and done well (sacrificed daughter imparting traits onto the ones they heal) and of course, its got a well done aesthetic and visual style. The 'timeline' turn order mechanic I think is interesting and good take on the typical 'turn-based' gameplay, allowing for some fun decision making. Ultimately, I just think the cyclical nature of the game brings it down too much for me to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a turn based tactical roguelite with an interesting setting and an excellent visual style. While the monochrome art with red highlights might be off putting to some, I found it to fit the setting very well and the artists have done a good job of balancing the contrast by focusing on darker colors, while white & red are used for details and highlights which makes it a lot easier on the eyes.Gameplay consists of a grid based tactical combat, but some of the core mechanics are a little different from most of the other games in the genre. Every turn you're given a base AP of 100, but if your AP drops below 50 you enter a burst state that consumes your next turn - in a way this could be seen as a chance to use 2 turns in a row if the situation calls for it, which adds a nice layer of strategy to the combat.AP is consumed by moving and casting abilities, although some special abilities such interrupts etc. use a % based value of characters HP instead. Which brings me to the 2nd twist mechanics wise, the only way to heal your characters in the game is to sacrifice another character of an equal or higher level. While this sounds rather harsh, it adds an element of risk to the game - although later on you're able to mitigate this a little by being able to resurrect a certain number of characters upon restarting a run.Due to being a roguelite, failing your run is something to be expected and often you've unlocked some new things to start out with during your current run. Which in turn allows you to have a stronger start and eventually you're able to maintain a team of characters you carry through your runs.While the visual presentation is great, the audio side has some issues in particular with the repetition of voice lines over the course of the gameplay. Music of the game is pretty good, but often a little too muted in the background. Sound effects do their job but do not really stand out in any way and while the voice overs are delivered well enough, the game has an unfortunate amount of repetition when it comes to in combat commentary - after hearing "They collect pieces of broken souls" and other melodramatic lines for hundreds of times, they get really annoying.And speaking about issues with the game in general:- While the setting of the game is great, the overall story is abysmally boring and bland.- Repetition: There isn't a whole lot of enemy variety in the game, environments are repeated often and the roguelite aspect of the game introduces some amount of grind that further highlights how repetitive some elements of the game are.- Very little replay value: Due to the grind and the repetition, there isn't a whole lot of incentive to do additional runs.- Balancing of the game is badly affected by the roguelite aspect of the game, this starts to be particularly noticeable around the end of the 3rd recollection and is especially highlighted in the 4th & 5th recollections where the difficulty spikes up a lot until you unlock specific things to mitigate it a bit.- Skill design often clashes with the mechanics, in particular with the boss battles where some skills are practically useless due to bosses having hard counters to them. Which is a shame as it punishes you for choosing specific skills.- Grind used as a padding to extend the game length- Final boss of the game is horribly designedOthercide is one of those unfortunate cases where the game starts up as a fun and enjoyable experience, but ultimately ends up having enough issues to sour the experience - in this particular case some additional QoL features and better balancing would already go a long way. For now though, I wouldn't recommend buying the game - instead wait for a sale and see if the developers patch some of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even half-way through the game, yet, but it has been great so far and ticks a lot of boxes for me, personally.The Nightmare difficulty (the game's recommended default) is rather brutal early level and you WILL end up wiping and restarting, but that leads to increased power and steady progression through the Remembrance system which grants passive bonuses through subsequent Recollections (runs). Not being able to regenerate health through normal means adds a good level of difficulty and decision making, as the tough choice to sacrifice valuable Daughters in order to overcome the next difficult fight and progress further makes each success rewarding. Sacrifices also provide excellent power boosts to the recipient Daughters and you can always bring back your favorite ones later.That said, the grind to progress may not be for everyone. I'd still recommend trying the game on Nightmare first and then, if you still find it too difficult or frustrating, try the Dream difficulty which adds passive healing (50% recovery) for Daughters each new day and a free Resurrection Token at the start.The combat mechanics are fairly intricate and can take some getting used to in order to get the most out of your skills and the dynamic timeline, but it feels really good when you manage to set up and pull off devastating combos that turn the tide. The boss battles can be absolutely brutal and a single mistake or miscalculation can lead to defeat. Bosses can feel overpowered or downright unfair at first, but once your own power grows and you learn their mechanics and what to watch out for they aren't too bad.There are only 5 Eras, but with the difficulty and rogue-lite death loop there is enough content to fill quite a few hours. As far as the Synapses go, there are a couple really difficult ones that can be costly and tedious to undertake if you aren't properly prepared. I'm looking at you Rescue mission... Others, such as Hunts are typically simple and straight-forward. My only real gripe is that there are a fairly limited number of Synapse maps which can get a little stale after a while. It would be nice if there was a greater variety of maps as well as more initial random spawn locations on each. It would also be nice if we could choose the formation of our Daughters when spawning into a map, to allow for more tactical positioning at the start. It seems like every boss fight my Shieldbearer starts way in the back, so I have to spend a turn or two simply moving them into range, which can be a bit more painful with certain Traits like Ethereal Flame which lowers movement range.The art style and aesthetic is perfect for the bleakness of the world and the character designs are amazing and quite polished. While there may not be a huge number of enemy types, I feel that the number isn't lacking. There seems to be a good mix of different types (melee, ranged, elites, etc) with their own skill sets and mechanics that add a good amount of complexity to battles. I've seen many reviews stating that the story is lacking, but it is actually unlocked through progression. This makes a lot of sense when you think about how the game is based around unlocking memories through recollections and remembering events. The lore is unlocked in bits and pieces, like a puzzle that takes time to unravel. The story that I have unlocked so far is actually quite intriguing.The soundtrack is absolutely amazing. When I first started the game, I found myself sitting in the menu just listening to the music for a while and checking the credits to listen to that song for a while longer. The music for the first boss was excellent and the transition into phase 3 of the fight fit so perfectly. Truly well thought out and executed.All in all, I am really enjoying this game and I wish I would have found it sooner than I did. A very solid 9 out of 10 for me and highly recommended to anyone who likes dark fantasy, souls-like difficulty, rogue-lite progression and tactical turn-based RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite good. Given more resources, I feel Lightbulb Crew could unseat XCOM as the undisputed best within the genre.I enjoy the aesthetic, although it does feel a little try-hard and troublesome at times. They were going for melancholy/Lovecraftian, but I don't think you have to go 90% grey scale to do it. Sometimes the environments, enemies, and animations feel washed out in the grey on grey on grey palette. This is a shame because it sells the artistry a bit short in what appears to be a ham-handed way to achieve the feel they wanted. In the end it's very unique, especially within the genre. The artists who worked on Othercide are fantastic, but I believe the nuances of their work would be more appreciated if the grey scale dial went from an 11 to maybe a 9.I suppose you could call this game "unforgiving" or "not newbie friendly", and you wouldn't be wrong. There isn't a lengthy tutorial. Some of the more complicated mechanics are left for you to get experienced with mostly on your own. It's a game you will need to lose in order to win, if that makes sense. I'm not sure if this is a positive or a negative. I view it as mostly positive, but I could see it turning some new players off. I thought the design of the UI was intuitive enough to not need a full lecture on how to do everything. If a turn-based tactics game isn't just a disgustingly brutal emotional curb stomp, then I personally am not interested, but maybe I'm just a filthy masochist.My only other complaint I don't even really feel is all that valid because I don't think it would be there if this game had more of a budget behind it, but I'll mention it anyway:I just wanted more. More customization, more weapons, more attacks, and so on.That short list contains all the negative things I could say. Fundamentally all the things you need from an enjoyable TBT game are there. I couldn't help but feel that even if these developers don't choose to pursue the genre and expand on this universe, eventually they are going to create something special and genre-defining. Othercide isn't quite that IMO, but it is a damn fine game that got remarkably close while still being indie. Worth every penny and every bit of time you put into it. I'm excited to see what the future holds from Lightbulb Crew. They've made a fan out of me.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it fair to write a review based off 67 minutes of gameplay?  Probably not.I've never refunded a game on Steam before Othercide.  Just a lot of things irked me a little bit. -Only three character classes, which doesn't have to be a bad thing, but then each level up gives you a choice of two skills, which didn't seem like enough variation.  -Pretty shallow, repetitive fights.-Clunky interface.-I know it's very minor, but it bothers me when HP and damage values are in the hundreds at the start of the game.  Why does my level 1 daughter do 917 damage?  It's an artificial inflation of power.-The "creepy" things being said between fights were so not creepy they made me laugh.And then on top of that is the grind that other reviews complain about that I didn't have the patience to get myself to.I like the concept of the game.  It checks all the right boxes for me.  The Gothic Horror setting.  The FFT/XCOM style battles.  The reintroduction of timed actions in a grid based strategy games hasn't been seen since the original Final Fantasy Tactics.  I was very excited, but ultimately, it felt like a shallow homage to greater inspirations.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on sale for $12 and love the genre. Have been pretty disappointed so far after being excited to play this one for awhile.This game suffers from moderate design issues and severe, experience killing UX/UI issues.A roguelite's biggest hurdle is not making things feel grindy - each run should feel distinctly different, even if slightly. So far this game hasn't offered me that at all. Upgrades are largely passive bonuses (+dmg%, +hp%, etc.) and so each run just feels like you're a little stronger - you hit harder, you can eat a little more dmg, etc. - but the core gameplay mechanics, interactions, skills, etc. have hardly changed at all for being 6+ hours in so far. Beyond that, there are lots of little things that drive me insane. For example, the game shows tiles when new bad guys are going to spawn in and where. Fine so far. But you don't know what KIND of bad guy is going to spawn in. Beyond that they get to move and attack the same turn they spawn. So you basically have to just stay miles away from any new spawns or risk getting bad RNG. In an unforgiving roguelite with permadeath, that sort of mechanic is just insanely frustrating and adds nothing to my experience. There's no strategy for the player to relate to the mechanic.That's whatever though, I can enjoy a game with those flaws. The killer for me is that WITH that design approach of lots of character improvement via passives or skill augments (e.g. teleport to a square is the base skill +add armor when landing on the square is the bonus), the game communicates these things extremely poorly. Nothing in the UI is clearly communicating which skills have perks and bonuses. Character armor is not visually represented on health bars, but only appears on the character/enemy pop-up card. The art direction is cool, but I'm constantly having to read the name of my character to figure out whose turn it is. The menus for managing your squad are cumbersome and require too much clicking. Again, the visual style causes extra energy to be spent trying to identify the characters you care about and those that don't. I really appreciate the attempt here and wish I could recommend the game, but if you're a fan of the genre you'll find constant small annoyances that will wear you out.

_childDocuments_.review: Two hours in and my number one thing that I want to make note of is that this is not XCOM and I think any comparison to XCOM is doing Othercide a huge disservice. Think of it more like a mix between a typical rogue-like single story that you learn over multiple playthroughs combined with a more JRPG-style tactical system. Visuals: Great. Sound: Great. Gameplay: Fun. Going into this thinking you'll have an XCOM-style tactical experience really won't bode well for you in the end because while Othercide is a tactical-based game, the primary game loop is very different from XCOM's. For me, Othercide is a lot of fun and I'm eager to complete it. For anyone who likes board games, this feels very Kingdom Death: Monster, especially when you get to the bosses. I like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this is a temporary thumbs down, as there's quite a lot I like with this game but at this moment there's one big flaw.Let's get the theme and artwork related stuff out of the way: I really dig the horror setting of this game (it's NOT a horror game but a strategy game in a horror setting), love the visual style and enjoy the soundtrack. I'm not someone who's into such stuff normally but in this case they really add to my motivation to play and enjoyment.I also really like most of the design decisions in the game, most certainly including the idea of healing as well as how skill synergies work. I like that instead of having a long and linear campaign, it's designed to be replayable (though not evergreen, there's not much randomization and once you solve the system you are done with this game. Do not expect a Militia 2 or Auro here but rather Crying Suns).So what's the problem? Balance (of the initial segment). The game is split into parts that correspond to different enemy types and a final boss. The huge balance problem that exists in the game as it is now is that the initial "normal" missions are extremely easy. And you NEED to do about 10-12 of those before you can fight the boss battle, which at least in the beginning looks quite hard. So in essence, the game poses a very interesting tactical problem with that boss but then asks you to grind about 2-2,5 hours of very easy missions. And you have to do that every time you lose after the boss battle. Now after your loss, you might think "this is impossible" but then realise some interesting tactical possibilities that might actually beat it. But to try that idea the game asks you to go through hours of drudgery. Absolutely unacceptable. And also absolutely fixable, so I hope the devs do a balance pass to make the early parts of the game similarly as exciting as that first boss battle. Until then, I don't intend to do drudgery for something I paid to entertain me.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/5. Great atmosphere, utterly game breaking final boss fight. The game dives headlong into the grimdark, and nails the aesthetic. It’s too light on lore, even from a ‘hidden lore’ angle; it’s just too obtuse.The tutorial does an excellent job setting you up for the entire game, it really is a necessity. When you have a grasp on the mechanics, the game becomes a wonderful puzzle to figure out. It’s stressful yet rewarding, because when you click you can utterly devour bosses on your first try if you’re careful enough. That all come crashing to the ground when you get to the final form of the final boss.I’m not sure if this is a glitch of some kind, or the game is “working as intended,” the final boss fight is a 15-minute interactive cut scene of watching your girls die. The final boss can stun-lock your girls. All of them. All the time. Fortunately, you can unlock upgrades that make your girls immune to stun-locks.The boss stun-locks you regardless. It doesn’t care if you’ve buffed your girls out to be 200% immune to stun-locks, it doesn’t care if you have abilities that move them up the turn-based time line, the final boss will lock you out and take back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back turns until you’re dead. Who play tested this? It feels like nobody did. They just threw together a boss, said “how can we make this too difficult?” and then broke every single game mechanic they had.This used to be a fun game. I thought I had ways to prepare my team against the final boss, and it didn’t matter. This isn’t pulling the rug out from under you, it’s pulling the entire foundation of the house out from under you. If this is a bug, it needs to be fixed. If this *isn’t* a bug, the balance team and the play tester need to be drawn and quartered.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Game with an intriguing art style and great strategic options. Atmospherically pleasing and intense at the same time it does have basically everything you'd want for a game of this genre. The only downside for someone like myself is that, even if you think everything through 15 steps ahead of time, you will still be faced with a certain sense of sacrifice at times. And yes you get benefits to unlock by means of shards, which in turn make additional runs easier to go through but for someone like me who really wants to have the full experience in one of the initial runs, it becomes very hard a few era's down the road (mainly era 4 and 5). They really expect you to fail a couple of times and passively power up via Remembrances to make it through all the way in one good run. Other than that however i can barely fault the game. Perhaps a few more classes and such would have been nice given how nice the combat feels, and seeing how much of the move sets can be intertwined and combined with one another.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide isn't bad but it's quite bare-bones game-play wise. Don't buy if you dislike the painful experiences of games such as Darkest Dungeon or Don't Starve. You'll be spending time each run building your elite team and then starting over when it goes wrong.If you want to try the game, by all means, play it on "easy".Playing in the "normal" recommended difficulty is a pain. Like most roguelites, you'll be repeating dozens of times the same run with a handful of random missions and maps as you struggle to earn the generic "points" that unlock upgrades for your next runs. The difficulty lying in the fact that your characters remain dead until you either spend special rare coins to revive them or you decide to level up new characters which would be a waste of time in the end. By the 10th run, the cemetery will be a long list of names that you'll have to clear. It's a slow grind that makes the overall game boring and repetitive.Yes, you can sacrifice one character to heal another but only if they're of a similar level meaning you'll still have to grind for hours to use that possibility in later stages. It's just not worth it.I didn't expect the game to be that hard unless the RNG is broken or i missed something. I saw some players manage to go further but I was suspicious of the damage and luck they had on some hits. It can't just be due to the upgrades and the memory system...After dying yet again at the first boss I gave up and started a new run on the easier difficulty. It's sad it's not the default one as it seemed better balanced and actually encouraged you to use more of the blood related skills. How about something in-between ?While I was exited at first by the design and game-play, especially since the devs were talking about patching up some of the issues, now I'm slowly loosing interest.Overall, not a terrible game. It's challenging and the small number of variables help you maintain some control over what's happening, still, the overall RNG and enemy spawns can get you good even if you're paying attention.On a side note, the one single thing that bothers me the most is the UI and by extension UX. This game was meant to be played with a controller by the fact it displays the button (keyboard keys) names on screen at all time. It’s not necessary, even for console players but it still does. I wish there was an option to hide those. KB and mice users have been used to shortcuts for decades and basic stuff like closing a screen with the back key or bringing up a main menu with "escape" is basic PC UX. If anything, having letters or key names like "[space] Activate" on screen at all times is annoying and takes precious screen real estate for no reason, not even accessibility.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide takes a bit of getting used to even for fans of rogue-like-ish games.First is the healing mechanic which isn't really a healing mechanic in the usual sense but part of your long term strategy. Healing one daughter requires sacrificing another of equal or higher level. The kneejerk reaction here is "this is stupid and wrong". The thing is that sacrificing one daughter permanently empowers the healed one and as you play you'll receive permanent unlocks that allow your fresh daughters to come with a higher level and to resurrect dead ones. This makes it easier to "feed" sacrificial lambs while also grooming your "champions" in the long term even if they die.The above is all connected to basic gameplay where you need to maximize efficiency in combat to lose as little health as possible while also wisely using your hp draining abilities for maximum effect and doing your best to prepare your "A-Team" for the boss battle so they go into it as healthy as possible. The first paragraph of enemy entries in the Codex describes their movement and attack patterns, reading these is very helpful for predicting and exploting enemy behavior. The game seems a bit sadistic when you first start but things come together after you get the first few unlocks, higher starting level, resurrection, more hp for all daughters, etc. It's an interesting system you don't see often that takes a bit of time to wrap your head around.The UI could be better in some cases. For example, once in combat you can't see which memories (ability enhancements) your have equipped so if you have multiple daughters with the same class it's very easy to forget who has what equipped.   It's a rogue-like with meta progression so obviously there's grind involved though not as much as you'd think from the first impression (thanks to unlocks). Whether it's too much or not is up to you. The game does have an option to speed up combat animations and such. Othercide doesn't have the complexity and sheer variety of something like Iratus but the combat and progression mechanics are solid and fairly unique and the aesthetics are quite stylish in a dark, edgy, French anime-ish kind of way.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay for the most part, but there are too many issues that bring it down.-I appreciate trying a different art style, but the color scheme is hard on my eyes sometimes, and I frequently can't tell the difference between some of the characters, or between the types of terrain.-The dialogue in missions gets repeated so frequently I wish there was a way to turn it off.-Sometimes your abilities get locked out of use for no reason, you have to fiddle with the controls to regain access to them, and sometimes that doesn't work.-The between mission interface is f**king abysmal. There is a codex for characters, lore, upgrades etc. and each of these pages is just one long-ass list that you have to slowly scroll through, so whenever something new is added, you have to spend forever to get to it. You can upgrade abilities using items called memories, and it has the same problem. There is a huge number of memories, and you have to scroll through one smallish window to access them. They also are named in a very unintuitive fashion. Everything is called things like "purpose" and "mercy" but the names don't correlate to their function. Additionally, a memory that gives say +50 to damage is called something completely different from another memory that gives +55 to damage. So there is no way to infer a natural progression of memories, you just have to scroll through them one by one. It's stupid. When you start a new run, you can turn on bonuses called remembrances, and every run you have to turn on every single remembrance individually, and there are dozens of remembrances. I don't understand how they didn't think to let them stay on between runs.The biggest issue is the balance. Classes are not particularly well balanced with each other, and skills within classes have very clear superior choices. There really is no need to have a well rounded group of characters; once you learn the best choices for each class, there is no need to deviate. Additionally, the enemies are just plain unfair at times. Sometimes the enemies will push your character's turn back, allowing other enemies to go before you get a chance to respond. If multiple enemies with this ability target the same character, you get stuck watching your character die without being able to do anything. There is no real way to stop this; it's just sh**ty and not fun. Most of the bosses have a mechanic like this too, where if you do enough damage, they immediately get to skip to their turn, then they can do multiple actions in a row. Having one boss with this would be fine, but every single boss fight having this mechanic sucks.If something between thumbs up and thumbs down existed, that's what I would rate Othercide. I like some parts of the game like the theme and (some of) the combat, but there are too many frustrating/lazy elements for me to fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. The timeline mechanic is amazing. The art style is beautiful. The enemy design is so horrific that it's gorgeous. The fact that some moves require you to use health instead of action points is just .I really want to love this game.But, I don't think I can say that I do. Maybe I'm just not a big fan of the roguelite mechanics. For those unaware, a roguelite is a game where every time you lose, you get upgrades that make the next run easier. This game in particular can have . Maybe, since there are only three classes, I find it too easy to forget which character is which. Maybe what annoys me is the fact that resurrection tokens not only respawn your heroes, but can be used on characters from other runs. This means that every time you restart the game, you never truly feel like it's a clean slate, and you don't ever feel like you lose too much. "Oh no, my favorite character just died. Now I'll just have to wait until my next restart where I get a free resurrection and I'll just get 'em back." I want to love this game so much; that's why I sunk 10 hours into it. But I can't say I enjoyed those 10 hours. I liked the first few. Maybe one day I'll come back to it and realize how wrong I was. But until then, I can't say I'd recommend it. Which sucks because there are so many things I love about this game: the enemies are so diverse, with each one having a different way it decides which character to attack; the art style, again; the little things like how the character's scarves show their health; and even the combos you can make by pushing one enemy into anthers attack that you charged up last turn.

_childDocuments_.review: Okey, here we go. Just pros and cons.Pros:- Great artstyle. Cool and simple. Really, it`s just a piece of art. - Nice music on boss fights. Moments when the music changes following the boss stages can touch your very soul.- Cute girls. Maybe too cute for a warriors but great anyway. I`ll be honest, they’re the only reason I made it through this game.- Iniciative based combat mechanics. This "timeline" stuff plays pretty fun.- Pretty hardcore. I don’t remember another game where the price of a mistake was so high.Cons:- Most of gameplay. Someone told the developers "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love rogue-lites" and they made "rogue-lite" mechanics. Yeah. But unfortunately none of them understood what it meant and they did not bother to find out. So gameplay is just a repetitive grind. No randomness at all. Same maps (there are very few of them), same enemies, same enemy placements, same girls, same skills, over and over HUNDRED of times and tens of hours. And then you meet a boss with counter-intuitive mechanics, wiping you out on the second turn and guess what? Yeah, grinding again. And thats not all. The icing on the cake - most of cool skills wasting your HP, but you can`t heal your girls in this game, so you can only afford to use them on bosses. What it means for you? Yeah, grinding via two skills. You can move and you can chop, thats your gameplay here.- Bosses. Maybe I'm too dumb, but I haven't found a tactic for any of the bosses. They have different skills, different stages and... i have no idea how to counter them or play with it. So It`s all about abusing reaction attacks and interruptions no matter wich boss and what it`s going to do. Same tactics for everyone, everytime.- Ambient sounds. I mean these random voiced lines. They are good, they create the atmosphere, but why do they come out SO OFTEN? "Memories hurt... memories hurt.... memories hurt..." - continuous annoying spam dozens of times in a row. I’m sure ì`ll hear them again in my nightmares. Her lips...her legs...her lips...her legs...her lips.... Aaarrggh! Overall: This game is great as a piece of art and mediocre as a game. So if you don`t mind of some tactical grinding enjoying the dark atmosphere and cute warmaidens - this game is just for you. But if you are looking for good rogue-lite.... go look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an masterpiece!Othercide is an turn based game. You command an Army of daughters (1-5 per match) against the forces of darkness. There are 4 classes of daughters. Every few levels they learn an new ability and they also get traits and you can upgrade them with memories which are dropped from enemy monsters.It features an unique artdesign, mostly white/black/red which fits realy well with the setting.This game is like Xcom, set in a creepy "all is lost" world. The game starts of to be very challenging. The chances are high that the first boss will Rip off your Face and you gona post "NERF IT" on the forum, just to realise a few runs later, that the boss is completly harmless if you play it right.The game is crafted in such a way, that the more you play, the stronger you get. If you lose the game, you keep your earned shards which are used to enable different buffs. And these buffs are crazy....like +80% Total Hitpoints for every daugher you have.If you play long enougth, its completly possible to make a new run and one shoot the first boss. Talk about revenge! Because of the buffs, you can also customize your run. Currently im playing a new run with lvl 1 daughters, with no ressurects allowed, but they all get +50% exp (buff) to level up realy fast and have lots of hp + damage (again buffs).This leads to a classic "Xcom" like gameplay. Another example: i could start a new run, ressurect my strongest daugther and try to finish the wohle game with her alone.There are two things which make the game go from "Its ok" to "HOLY MOTHER OF HELL!"1. Is the Soundtrack. its creepy, haunting, with an apocalyptic feel.2. The boss fights. Seriously, i played LOTS of games but these bosses.....bloody hell, i want to meet the guy who designed them. Overall i rate it 8/10 because it can get a bit repetive, cos there are no random generated maps and only a few maps per "Era".

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful crafted game, weird and atmospheric, makes one think and feel, very few games out there that do that. That said, game is somewhat short and the ending lacks closure, hints to a part 2 or dlc. Overall this game you should get . ( better with a discount ). However, word to the wise, you will cry for your daughters. On the gameplay side, imho this game cant be compared to xcom or wasteland 3, because of the hiting chance. While the enemy can and will dodge your atk sometimes its no big deal, as most basic atks are 3 in 1 ( soulslinger ), and each char has a generous ap pool wich can be further enlarged with traits. I recommend for the end game team 2 soulslingers, 1 blademaster, 1scythebearer. For the last boss just add another soulslinger. There are other viable builds but i found this one to be the most forgiving in terms of mistakes. Prolly a pro gamer ( wich im not ) will finish the game in less than 30 hours. In my opinion worth the money aslong as you pay max 20 euros. There is also some replay value here, as you cant complete all missions in one given chapter, not even with 2 viable teams, wich anyway you cant build sooner than closer to the end of the game. Anyway thats my 2 cents, cheers, may your favourite daughters survive, and if not, ressurect them :)

_childDocuments_.review: Brutal and unforgiving, Othercide teaches players a strong lesson in permanence; failure is not just expected, but an opportunity to grow. Darkly atmospheric reminiscent of every Linkin Park album cover and dipped wholly in Evanescence, the game offers a fun challenge for veterans of other roguelikes while offering up the style and substance newer players have come to expect.It's good to look at. It's good to listen to. It's good to play, though a lack in variety is probably the strongest weakness of an otherwise good game; you'll be seeing the same enemies a lot, with beefier versions later in the game.The bosses offer up a decent challenge to push your playstyle to its limits, and you'll often be faced with the hard decision of letting one of your dear daughters go before a fight is over as things go on, but that's okay; you can bring them back or pass their skills on to another, if you'd like. In fact, game overs give you a chance to play around with the many, many bonuses you unlock for progression to use at your liesure.Is it good? Yes.Is it fun? For a few hours every now and then.Is it good for a few playthroughs? You'll be doing a lot of them.All in all, I look forward to seeing more. DLC, sequels, spin-offs, whatever; Othercide offers an edgy, grim-dark universe that begs for exploration.A solid 8 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetic is cool, but unfortunately my short time with the game was riddled with what I can only assume are bugs. 3 separate occasions a plague guard, which is a melee enemy, uses a basic attack on a daughter 7 or 8 spaces away when their attack range is supposed to be melee range only. They didn't use a skill or anything, it was a basic attack. Not sure if anyone else has had anything similar happen, but in a game as punishing as this is supposed to be, the last thing anyone needs is random BS that isn't supposed to be possible ruining an already challenging game. Cool soundtrack and art, but I wouldn't recommend a rogue like game that has such serious bugs in it. Really a shame

_childDocuments_.review: Two months after original review:The developers have released one major update since launch alongside several hotfixes designed to address bugs. The Dream update included a new difficulty setting as well as some more traits that can be obtained by your characters. Some skills and traits have been re-balanced. For the time being, I would consider this to be final state of the game.The game itself has excellent art and story direction. I think the atmosphere, music, and art style are all excellent additions to the game. Some of the voice acting is out of place (especially end-of-game buddy voice overs), some of the lines trigger much too often, but I can honestly say that I'm impressed with how much effort they went through to get the music and art for this kind of story.Gameplay-wise, there is potential that the game ultimately falls short of delivering. The developers tried to balance the game around losing and seem to have looked at producing a rogue-like experience where your characters can gather different traits each playthrough (most like Darkest Dungeon). Characters can choose different skills as they level up. There are game-altering options that you can purchase upon losing / starting a new playthrough that change how the game plays. Unfortunately, that's where it stops. The skills are mostly one-sided or redundant for most of the characters. The playthrough modifiers mostly just make the game universally easier - instead of changing how the game plays, it's just a difficulty slider that increases your characters' health, increases damage to enemies, increases experience gain, or skips chapters. With how the game is balanced, you go from playing a game where any damage is lethal, to one where characters can just walk through enemies. Instead of offering new ways to succeed at the game, it just lets you play dumber. There's not much fun in replaying this.While unintended, the game still has a number of unacceptable bugs for a $35 game. Especially as an iron mode game, where the game constantly saves automatically, save data loss of corruption is unacceptable. This is still a frequent phenomenon according to the discord channel, that plagues players and wipes hours of play (from a game that is already designed to make you restart). Beyond that - the save state compromises, in that quitting to menu in the middle of a map will reset the entire map. This is very easily abused, but even if you have no intent of abusing this design decision, if the game crashes (which is not uncommon) then you will reset any decisions you may have made on the level. Melee range enemies can occasionally hit you from across the map. The recent update added a new bug where damage calculations are universally higher than actual damage output. With that said, I would not recommend purchase at full price. I would be happy playing this as an indie developer game with all its bugs and design flaws for $15-20, but at $35 the expectations for a fully fleshed out game are higher. Original review:Othercide is an extraordinarily atmospheric game with excellent writing, design, and soundtracks. The first few hours in the game were excellent. Having said that, I cannot recommend it to anyone else, . There are substantial game-breaking performance issues with the game. I'm using an Intel i7 laptop with a GTX1080Ti eGPU. It can run XCOM2, Fallout 4, modded Skyrim, Sekiro, etc. at over 40 fps. When Othercide runs, it runs at a stable 60fps at maximum resolution and settings - but periodically the game freezes (about once every 45 minutes). Sometimes the game will chug through like nothing happens, other times it hard freezes the computer - not CTD, no task manager interrupt. Worse, on two occasions it has corrupted saves with >15 hours of play. I've played with the settings to try and mitigate this, but it seems that I've only been able to lower the frequency of these crashes - low shadows, VSync off, no AA.Besides the game-breaking crashes, Othercide has a surprising amount of polish in some areas, and lack thereof in others. The soundtrack, atmosphere, codex, and lore are rich and entirely different from the waifu simulator some have jokingly called it. The noire, pseudo-Eldritch story is excellent. The entire game revolve around sacrifice and loss. The game is balanced around defeat. However combat UI, enemy behavior, and boss battles are all bugged: enemy delayed actions don't properly display if the enemy has changed position; some AoE delayed attacks don't display correctly regardless; killing an enemy next to another blows their model out of wack; starting turn doesn't allow actions if your character has negative initiative; one boss's cutscene can bug out and soft-lock the game... these are only some of the ones I've experienced. Ultimately this turns a difficult but rewarding combat system into what feels like an unfair slog of repetition, especially when the game freezes.I'm putting the game on the shelf for a month or two in hopes that the developers will address these bugs. It has a lot of promise, but I would advise waiting some time for the game to develop.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. It's hard, but once you master all the pieces: enemy movement, timeline, bursting, skill combos, and more it just comes together as an amazing feeling of just dominating each mission.The difficulty is high, but the rogue-like system the game employs is rewarding while not simply handing you the win with boosts and power-ups after so many runs.The soundtrack is amazing, fits perfectly and has some great surprises on important battles. _childDocuments_.review: Very cool strategy game. I love the visuals. The color pallet is awesome. The game plays really well. Its invigorating when you out smart your opponents with a timed combo. I did run into a few glitches where the enemy would hit your character straight from spawn even when they are out of range but that was about it. On the upside: Gameplay is fun. Having interrupts and a timeline adds a whole other dynamic to the game that make it interesting especially when you find that perfect counter or you out play the AI into taking a lethal backstab. I have 2 downsides to this game: (Spoiler alert. The last boss doesn't give you time to play your moves as it always uses skills to make sure it goes first on the timeline. There is certain skills that you can unlock on a daughter that counteract it. But that means it forces you to build your daughters in a certain way in order to complete the game. Considering how long it takes you to level a daughter, and that you start the game again if you fail, it makes the end boss frustrating. I would like more versitility). The second thing I don't like is that when the game was released, you couldnt customize your daughter. I liked the fact that you couldn't because it gives the daughter personality and makes the game feel like you not cultivating their personality. (Just my opinion). On a whole its worth the price if you suck at the game and you need to do many recollections. I would say worth it at 25% off.

_childDocuments_.review: It looked like cool game, turns out it's x-com with even less depth. the 'timeline' system that gets talked about is literally just a basic initiative system from games like FFT. there is no customization of your characters aside from some 'choices' of skills at some level ups, but like x-com at each level for each class there seems to be an obvious pick and a wonky ability, so there is no real choice. _childDocuments_.review: Well, I must say I don't like the idea of having a cemetery of Daughters or sacrifice them one for another to upgrade the survivor because I get attached to the characters, especially when I give them names. I can see that this was the developers' idea from the start, but instead of teaching me a lesson about life fragility it just made the gameplay repulsive and overall experience unpleasant.I found the core mechanic repetitive and dull. I can tell I'm not good in this genre, so it took me almost 4 hours to get through the first round. When all my Daughters were on the cemetery and I had to start over, I just quit. I'm probably not the core audience of the genre and the game was difficult for me; I wish there was a some kind of a "beginner" difficulty. But I played turn-based before, it was not as frustrating as Othercide.Some skills and game mechanics were not self-explanatory at all. So when I did something in the game thinking that I can predict the result, something completely different happen and it led me to the loss. Like Corroded Scissors Remembrance with the description "You may resurrect a fallen Daughter" - no clue how it works, because I have Daughters in my cemetery and I'm still offered to resurrect them for a token.I wish I never bought this game because I'm IN LOVE with the aesthetics, and the lore, and the visual part, it's absolutely amazing, but the core gameplay is either for true fans of genre and the hardcore or... Ugh, I don't even know. The disappointment is just tormenting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing, short (25-ish hour) game that I would recommend for anybody who likes turn-based, squad RPGs like XCOM.This game doesn't have quite the same amount of gameplay choices and strategic depth as XCOM, and the map variety gets kind of stale due to the way the game is played. However, the story in the game is very well done, the themes and tone are relayed extremely well, and there are a lot of satisfying emotional beats as you discover the story of the Mother and the Child. The music in this game is particularly outstanding, and I often play the tracks to the boss fights when playing other games.The game is absolutely gorgeous despite not having the best graphics, in part to the wonderful aesthetic that is put into it. The designs of the Daughters and Monsters are really well done, and the sound design is on point.The boss fights are amazing, tense, and difficult the first time you do them. I finished the game in 4 recollections, though. I would imagine as you get more remembrances, the game gets a lot easier. I think I one-shot the first boss during my final recollection. The aforementioned amazing music and design only heightens the amount of fun you have playing.Overall, I really really loved this game. Even though the gameplay itself isn't as special as say, XCOM or even Troubleshooter: Abandoned Children, the atmosphere, story, music, and boss fights were unique and scratched an itch that I really needed in gaming.EDIT: Forgot to mention that I did recieve this on sale for around $22. Looking at the current price, it is a bit much for the amount and quality of gameplay, so I would wait to get on sale. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: IGN commented that this is one of the best strategy game of the year it was released. I don't know whether I would praise so highly of the game, but it is, without a doubt, an outstanding game. In case you don't know, it combines strategy with rough-lite mechanism, which means on the third "rebirth," the game becomes easier to play. Nonetheless, the difficulty scaling is done well and there is always some degrees of challenge to entertain players. Its graphic, battle, and UI design deserve praises. The color scheme of black, white, grey, and red create an unique atmosphere that fits the gloomy vibe the game tries to deliver. The creature designs (and animations of all creatures) are charming and scary. Battle is consistently engaging and does not have the common flaw of slow pacing that plagues so many turn-based strategy games. UI is just easy to navigate and understand. It could be further simplified, but is already a good example of what UI should be. The only flaw, or comparative short-link of the game, is its story. I haven't beaten the game yet, so my judgment here should certainly be taken with a grain of salt. Nonetheless, my impression so far is that the game takes itself a bit too seriously without offering a matching story to justify that seriousness. The story and overall setup of the game yearn for that mystic vibe, which gets in the way of making it clear what exactly the story is about. I have no good clue about what makes the enemy evil except that I play the good side and so the enemy must be bad. This is to say that the story is not clear logic to it. Part of it is due to the rogue-lite setting: telling a story where the character bizarrely restarts from the beginning repeatedly is simply hard. So I am fine with the story being vague and unclear.Overall, I recommend this game to anyone who likes turn-based strategy game. If you like rogue-lite, this would be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a beautiful looking turn-based RPG games with heavy rougelite elements. This game has heavy x-com vibes as well....With that said there are a few key issues that you must be aware of: 1) The difficulty on "Original" and "Dream" are VASTLY two different mindsets; Nightmare difficulty will push even the veteran turn-base gamers to their limit, as the game will throw everything at you. Dream mode however is essentially a walk in the park; basically a traditional turn-based RPG game; i recommend playing it on Dream mode to better understand the game first before playing it on original2) Group size missions must be definitive and not just "Okay, one mission is 3, and another 4" because, yes while it may be a game design choice or cheese; on original mode the game is extremely hard and will insist that you clear the 7 days before the boss attacks. And guess what? If you die, then the current run will end -- yeah no. 3) During combat there is no instant click. So like for example there are "overwatch" type abilities that will watch for enemy patterns - here's the thing though, You have to CONSTANTLY click on the soulslinger; it's not just a one click type of deal which is an odd design choiceAudio & visually it's a breathtaking game, and I recommend the soundtrack.As I mentioned, it's a sale game; however, if you really want more Turn-based games in your library at this current moment then this is a full buy right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the grim dark aesthetic is amazing, concept is original and the gameplay is generally sound.Easy mode can be challenging but I enjoyed my experience in Original more, while it might sound masochistic xd.I felt that every time I lost, afterwards I found that organising the Daughters and understanding enemy types became far easier.Heres pros and cons.Pros:Story! I love the lore in this game, the abhorrent enemies, the sick and twisted bosses and gradually uncovering the truth of the past. The game also feels original, which is a breath of fresh air in this age of sterile media.CombatFast and brutal, for both enemies and Daughters.AestheticFlawless, there is nothing in this area in my opinion that needs to be changed.ConsStory... I know its in my pros, but I found some aspects hard to understand, especially the Memories. Also I'm still confused as to what the Chosen One truly means, what the Suffering is and what Others are. Combatyes its also in my pros xd, but I ve found it can be frustrating for no reason. For example, on many occasions, ive had plague butchers and plague guard strike Daughters from across the map, which I assume is a bug. In addition, Infected spawn and immediately shoot a daughter, which due to the fact they can do it across the map, frustrates me. However, I think the worst experience Ive had are the Painslingers, simply because of Corrupted Haste. It wouldnt be a problem if they only used it once, but when there are a pair of them, they use it on each other and have 4 turns before you get to a Daughter's. Unless you re capable of killing one as soon as they spawn (Which can be difficult considering they have 3000+ health), it can completely overrun the mission.In addition, actions that can counter interruptions would be great for both enemies and Daughters, as I feel that any action or ability in a strategy game needs a counter to feel immersive.DaughtersI think this has been repeated a lot in the reviews, but more customisation would be nice. Memories are one thing, but I do get attached to the Daughters ive had for several Recollections. Moreover, Shieldbearers don't work in Nightmare, at least they feel like the worst class. This is due to several reasons, one they can't aggro enemies, they can t generate armour without using hp, they do less damage than every other class (Yes even Soulslinger because they get Shadow Round.) which wouldnt be a problem if they could soak up damage like an actual tank. The biggest problem is healing, they need a way to regain health during missions, perhaps as an attack so you couldnt do it every turn. Having a big hp pool is useless if you cant use it. More classes would also be amazing, I'd love to have one with an axe or maybe a musket to have another ranged class.RepetitionI have autism, which results in me finding games like Warframe and FF14 enjoyable to play, even after hundreds of hours of gameplay. I would say for Othercide though, having more items to collect would be a boon.Voicelines.After hearing 'Give life to our Daughters' and 'A clean cut.' a million times, some more voice lines would be great, and help with the repetition.ConclusionI love this game and I am intent on buying any content that comes out for it. Despite some problems here and there, I find myself enjoying Othercide immensely. I am looking forward to it's future.

_childDocuments_.review: A tedious, unfair game built on infuriating mechanics, making it a repetitive mess.Visually the game seems pleasing, but after a while the monochromatic with red accents seems overdone.The soundtrack is great for an indie game, the voice acting as well at times, underwhelming other times.The story is skippable as it adds nothing to the game.The UI isn't very helpful:-There isn't any indication on how long an effect lasts; i have been rooted seemingly infinitely with 3 characters while the "maggot" that cast root, was long time dead already, creating a slow wipe for my team.This cast was from across the battlefield, leaving no way to defend myself.-skill explanations of enemies seem lacking clear information.-Stats aren't clear during battle, enemies have 150 block for example, i have 300 damage, i attack, 0 damage every time.. how does the calculation actually work?-The same goes for dodge: scavenger has 15% dodge, i do a total of 15 attacks, 3 hit, he dodges everything else.-buffs aren't very clear which are active and what the effects are.-The enemy stat screen overlaps part of the battlefield making you pan to select the target. Add to this that after an action the camera pans back so if you want to attack a second time, you have to pan again, quite annoying.The mechanics are somewhat unique, yet make the game overly grindy in an absolutely tedious manner:-"daughters" get attacked, don't ever heal automatically and the only way to heal them is to sacrifice higher or equal level units. Start grinding to possibly heal decent units.-add to this that any decent "combo-worthy skill" what the game tries to promote costs actual health percentage, makes this mechanic insufferable.-once skills are set, they are permanent. Want to replace skill on a decent unit? wipe it, start a new grind.The game feels unfair, especially during rescue missions, mostly at chapter 4 and up.-infinite spawns that trigger when reaching a point are acceptable, except when adding trashy enemies with OP mechanics like "maggot" with its root ability, making you rush towards it, creating 10 to 15 spawns at once, basically wiping your team, since it's impossible to survive this, not by fighting or by rushing to the exit.Hunt and ritual are acceptable missions, but survival depends on rng where and what spawns, including the exit.Boss fight entirely depend on cheesing by abusing certain game mechanics and feel like chores.They also have several Ridiculously OP moves that once performed wipe in 1 to 2 turns.Now the wipes wouldn't be necessarily bad if the resurrect mechanic was good.When getting wiped during a boss, the game resets, all your daughters die, your set memories are all wiped.This way you barely will know what u did wrong, being it a wrong skill on a unit, having to regrind a unit to hope that next time she will be what you need for the fight or being it a wrong set of units. I didn't even finish the game, i just quit during recollection 3, chapter 5.I didn't even lose the last battle i played, i haven't tried the 5th boss which was reachable for me at this time, but i just had enough of the bland, monotonous, frustrating  grindfest that is the core of this game.After chapter 3 you've experienced all there's to experience, only a grindy, tedious gameplay loop remains.The looks, the sound at first pleasing, exciting became what i eventually hated about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Did they send me daughtersWhen I askedFor sons?They did! And these daughters totally rule! Othercide is a tough as nails tactics-game that immediately jumps at you with its distinct visual presentation. The main hook of the game is your squad of Daughters, heroes and warriors who will battle the demons for and with you. They come in various classes which fulfill your standard rock-paper-scissors role but with an interesting spin to it. At certain levels you will choose between two abilities, although I must say that one choice seemed superior more often than not.During battle the order of actions is determined by a clever mechanism of initiative. Each daughter has action points and using half of them means she can act again in a certain amount of time. Using all the action points means you can move further or attack more often but comes at the heavy price of your next turn taking twice as long to come around and so the game has you planning those crucial turns and weighing the decision of having one Daughter stranded after going on a rampage. Even moreso because later enemies will not take as long until their next turn!Should your Daughters take damage in battle, you will find yourself faced with Othercide's next defining trait: Its healing system. When playing on Nightmare difficulty, which is the standard difficulty, your daughters do not automatically heal after combat but only if you sacrifice, yes kill, a Daughter of equal or higher level. A part of her stays with her comrade in the form of a permanent buff, but the game will still force some heavy decisions upon you this way. You can resurrect some of your team, but only at the price of rare tokens, so that decision becomes equally tough!SIDENOTE: The game offers a second mode in which each Daughter heals 50% of her health after each overworld turn and since each Daughter can only go on one mission per such turn, most of them will usually be at full health. I imagine the game would be no less punishing inside the missions but I played it using the standard mode. Just an fyi.The bosses in the game provide interesting combat puzzles although the community has come up with some ways to absolutely bully them. I would still recommend going in blind on your first try and failing miserably! It's a learning experience!Should you fail a boss mission or if you choose to do so between missions, you end your run and bank the metaprogression currency of shards, which are used to activate buffing trophies, Remembrances. These will give you all sorts of benefits from your Daughters having more health or starting at a higher level to outright skipping one or more of the game's five stages. While some of the Remembrances felt very strong, none of them seem mandatory to beat the game, so the game does not feel grindy in that way.All in all I would highly recommend Othercide for any fan of tactics games. It's a real nailbiter at times but feels highly rewarding when you bring a boss down. And while the story seems a bit cryptic and to be happening on a meta or possibly psyche level, it provides an engaging backdrop which gives your Daughters their reason to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played only a few Xcom-like games, and this has so far been one of my favorites. The enemy variety switches things up with each new era you progress through, and you can easily get attached to certain daughters and there's thankfully a way to always bring her back if an untimely death comes her way. I've yet to get to the end game, but so far I haven't felt the need to grind. Many powerful and permanent bonuses can be unlocked to make new resets much easier. However, I've noticed that if you are an above average player, you can easily unlock nearly all the important upgrades after only 2 or so resets. Once you've done that, the only thing left to do is to try and get as many traits as possible onto every daughter. And if you end up not being good at the game, that is when the grinding will likely finally show its face.The class variety is sadly low though, and many skills just aren't as good as others. You may find yourself making tons of the same daughter rather than unique ones.There have been a few bugs however. Tooltips and the codex don't always line up. Some enemy logs say they do X, but in reality they do Y. Sometimes the movement phase of characters can be visually buggy, requiring you to swap between all their actions until it correctly shows where you can actually travel. Red danger zones on the ground seem to stick around for longer than they should, which can get confusing when an entire area is nothing but red and you're unsure of what's actually safe.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first things this game does is admit that this game is flawed. The game genuinely says be prepared to lose your favorite characters because they will die to B.S. They're right.The game is hilariously unfair, even with the easier difficulty mode. Get used to your girls dying in just two hits because every single enemy is overpowered. You'll have 700 HP at the start of the game with one girl for example and a hit from an enemy is 350 hp. How is that good game design? Why do you want our characters that you want us to build up and keep die so ridiculously quickly? Horrible game design. The BIGGEST PROBLEM with this game is it's AP system. You are only allowed to use FIFTY of your one hundred AP points. If you use more than fifty you are PUNISHED. THAT IS SO INCREDIBLY STUPID AND A TERRIBLE GAME MECHANIC. Moving takes so much AP so moving to an enemy usually uses your first 50 and then you're screwed if you use anymore because if you go above 50, the game punishes you by pretty much forcing your character to wait double the amount of turns before you can do anything again. On top of that attacks cost 25+ AP so combat is a terrible chore that isn't fun. Does this even sound like good game design? No, it doesn't. It is flawed and horrible and yet they decided to keep this garbage in the game.Game also allows enemies to pretty much outnumber you every mission but you're only allowed to bring up to 3 girls, sometimes 4. This is the worst, especially during rescue missions when the enemy amount is doubled. No, that's not fair. Stop restricting us with poor game mechanics and decisions and let us have fun. _childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this strongly enough. It has some flaws, but it's an unforgettable experience. I didn't pick it up until it was on sale, but having played it, it is absolutely worth buying at full price.As a tactical RPG roguelite, you're going to find yourself in very similar encounters every run, but the game punishes you harshly if you don't get everything *perfect* considering how hard it is to heal or revive so the level of challenge keeps it interesting. The atmosphere is wonderful and the black/white/red art style suits it perfectly, complemented by an amazing sound track. Your Daughters don't have any voiced lines, but they gain traits under certain conditions (and possibly with certain probabilities attached?) which can make you pretty attached to the ones that you keep using. Between that and Mother's lines praising them, you get truly attached to your girls... and the healing mechanic means you eventually have to either sacrifice them or let them die. I don't think I've ever apologized to a video game character before, but I felt so awful each time I had to do it.My only complaint is that it felt a little too easy on Nightmare difficulty, especially the boss fights; I was able to finish it on my 4th run, clearing both the fourth and fifth bosses on my first try, with my blademaster able to skip entire phases and she also made it to the final boss completely unhurt. Looking at community posts, it does seem I had an easier time than most, however.It didn't quite scratch my itch for the truly punishing game I was expecting, but it was still a wonderful experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that go around unnoticed, but deserve a bit more love and recognition.-Gameplay: The obvious comparison would be to XCOM, but here you won't have any cover (in fact, any and all environment obstacles will be issues against you, never to your advantage). and there is a time unit system that allows for a more fluid combat. Your units have 100 or more action points, and as long as they leave 50 points remaining, have a resting time of 50 time units, with the option of using those points too, with the steep cost of waiting 100 time units.The main idea is alpha striking the enemy as much as possible, allowing the enemy to act will end in wounds, what may not sound like a lot, but unless the player has picked the not recommended dream mode, those wounds can only be healed through the sacrifice of a similarly leveled daughter, a very punishing option, obviously.Another factor is HP skills, those skills do not cost action points, and can be massively devastating, but said skills cost a percentage of the daughter's HP, so the player will be constantly having to balance the satefy of strong skills that interrupt the enemy, or bring damage extreme enough to clear bosses effortlessly, with the slow but constant drain of HP, what may end in casualties.Othercide is hard, no other way around it, the game punishes mistakes ruthlessly and moving through the campaign is an effort of balancing risk and reward and being able to say no when you're clearly outmatched.This game has metaprogression, rather easy to unlock, since as early as the second run I managed to unlock almost all the options. Every cleared mission gives 25 shards, those add to a permanent count that you can use to activate advantages. Some are very standard, like money income, or exp gain, but others heavily help to reduce the chore of retrying the game, like reviving some of your previous run's daughters, or being able to skip parts of the game, a nice touch to maintain the roguelite aspect while also allowing the players to move forward as fast as possible if they want.-Sound and Music: A hit and miss, the boss themes are  and something to be enjoyed, on the other hand, the rest of the time you will be hearing ambient music that could pass for dull, a bit of a more intense combat music, at least facing elite enemies would've been appreciated.I would send a bit of a negative point about voice acting, while the voice acting of the red mother and the child are ok (if the red mother sounds a bit weepy for a hardened fighter that lived for centuries) other voices, like the maid's were rather uninspired and wooden.-Story: A story about eldritch entities encroaching onto reality and making a small child suffer in the process, tragic and dark, it follows a narrative style offering all the lore in the codex, units and memories' descriptions. The story is clearly not the game's main point, but it's still ok.Final thoughts: An enjoyable roguelite with heavy strategic elements, it doesn't overstay its welcome and doesn't try to bog the player thanks to the metaprogression, but still offering the option for those who want the full challenge to get the base experience and do their best.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!So many games of this genre just feel like XCOM with a new skin. Not this one.I love XCOM, however, its impossible not to feel so mift when some RNG decides that a shotgun will miss from 1 tile away with 99% hit chance. This game still has RNG in form of dodge, but it feels far less one sided. Both sides get a fair dodge chance that can be built up, you dont feel like that 99% hit chance youre told about is actually a 50% hit chance.The AP system, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yes. The combos you can create are amazing, no more of the usual: move up, shoot and enter quick shot mode. Or move up, miss shot and stand there like a idiot that will now die next turn. You can get so creative, do you keep 50+ AP so that your characters turn occurs sooner at the cost of you maybe doing less for this turn. Or maybe you move up next to an enemy, shoot the ground whilst flying to a square 6 tiles away to then shoot once more, now with no AP you use 5% of you HP to enter a vanguard mode allowing you to interrupt the enemies next turn if he tries to attack an ally. HONESTLY, WTF IS THIS BADASSERY I NEED MORE OF IT IN MY LIFE. The way you have to throw away this idea of getting attached to a character is amazing too. No more grinding your favourites to the top, some have to be sacraficed to keep others alive, whether in battle or after to heal another character. Eventually some become too high level that it gets too hard to keep them at full HP as you have to grind another to the same level in order to do the healing. So you sometimes have to sacrafice the higher leveled character to help heal the lower leveled but easier to keep full HP characters.The art style and soundtrack are just perfect. Already praised to death in the reviews thus far so I shall leave it at this, i never buy soundtracks or art books anymore...but this one has made me break that long streak ;) Really would love it if the main menu theme was in the battles too but hey it means it feels even more enjoyable booting the game up and seeing/hearing that menu screen.Only cons I can think of is that the UI and button presses can be buggy, sometimes dont work and will need you to back out and try again. Thats literally it, just a minor pain that doesnt change the experience whatsoever.9.8/10please add that main music theme even if its for a DLC boss or whatever, JUST GIVE ME IT!

_childDocuments_.review: I think Othercide is a creative and ambitious title that overstays its welcome.First, let's list Othercide's pros:*Stylish and unique art style, especially with the bosses*The levels you fight on are darkly beautiful & imaginative*Solid tactics-style gameplay with a deep focus on initiative...*...leading to new & different mechanics compared to XCOM*Interesting (if overly artistic) world, lore, and backstory*Super cool boss fights & themes (#3 in particular)However - and I cannot stress this enough - Othercide gets boring after a while-Your characters all look the same. Not a little similar, they are carbon copies of each other.-You have 3 classes for the first half of the game. That's it (although 1 unlocks ~15 hours in)-Classes have 4 abilities each in the first ~2 hours and get 2 more over the next *30* hours-Monsters are visually interesting but mechanically similar to each other, so levels feel repetitive-No randomness to maps means you are playing on the EXACT same maps over and over again...-... and since the game is black-and-white with red accents, it can get really old after a while-Finally, voice lines are cool but JUST. KEEP. REPEATING. "Stop. Stop. Memories hurt" - gets old.Ultimately, I put down Othercide after making it through two-thirds of the game. I've enjoyed my time with it (and I may end up going back to finish it), but for now I'm just bored thinking of all the missions I have to clear to get to the ending.Is it worth checking out? Almost certainly if you are a fan of tactics games... but I would recommend waiting for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus. Has it really been only an hour? That was the longest hour of my life, and not in a good way. This game knows its aesthetics. It has good sound, visuals, colors, and theme. It reminds me a lot of the harshness of DMC 3's higher difficulties, and the red/white/black palette is incredibly slick. The idea of a roguelite tactical is nice, but it definitely didn't carry out well here. The whole things feels... disjointed. Everything looks slick and fast, but feels so slow.I think the way the tactical RPG elements were implemented took away the most important emotional aspects of games like these, and that's a connection to the characters. I don't need a lot to get attached. If you give me the ability to name them, I'll get attached. But so quickly you learn that these characters are resources. And that's fine. But the way the game's story encourages your attachment, and the way it seems the story is trying to get you invested in lore, makes this so incredibly jarring that it's an off-putting emotional whiplash. The controls aren't great either. The UI makes it seems like it would be good to play on a controller, but the controls aren't formatted for it. So you use the keyboards, but the gameplay loop and UI isn't formatted for that either. When I look at a similar Tactical game like like XCOM or TROUBLESHOOTER - the latter of which is doing 10x more stuff with half the controls - getting into any rhythm is difficult and janky. And while it gives you the illusion of customisability, a lot of that is smoke. Customising your daughters aren't rewarding because they will likely die. Customising your skills aren't great, because it's just a multiple-choice, and again, very quickly, you realize there is an "optimal" choice. And that optimal choice means this souls-like game is definitely not balanced to play. The difficulty doesn't scale well either. You don't get stronger opponents. You just get more opponents, or get an opponent that does more. So when you lose, you don't feel challenged. You just feel overwhelmed. When you win, you don't feel successful. You feel lucky or confused, because there's not enough inter-connected mechanics to make planning mean anything. The only people I think who would enjoy this game are some level of sadist or masochist. And as a gaming masochist myself, I don't feel any satisfaction from the release of suffering, just more suffering.
