_childDocuments_.review: MINOR THEMATIC SPOILER WARNING:i wont go into detail about the specifics of the plot, character or anything else but i will talk about other media with similar themes, if you want absolutely no spoilers, i think the gameplay is good if you like designing and fine tuning RPG builds, or if your into fantasy or philosophy manga/anime. entirely worth the $20 asking pricethe gameplay is solid, reminds me of terrarias calamity mod quite a bit in terms of flow and attack patterns. Some bosses have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ last stand immunity/bullet hell phases but even on the hardest difficulty every time i ran into one of these bosses i was able to make my build so stupidly broken in one aspect or another be it damage or surviability that ii could cheese the BS phase. as someone who enjoys making interesting and varied highly tuned builds it was thoroughly enjoyable.im not an art guy but i think it looks good, and if you like cronenberg or lovecraft your gonna be right at homeBefore talking about the plot i feel the need to establish some credentials, im a massive weeb, in fact im such a weeb that I do volunteer work for 2  manga translation groups. so ive read/am caught up on a few  manga.with that established, this games plot is incredibly good. I wasnt expecting anything going in after looking at anime memes in the featured screenshots but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ i was blown away. Without talking about any details, it reminds me a lot of girls last tour if it were written by HP lovecraft, and i mean that in the best possible way. there is some tonal whiplash going from discussion of super serious metaphysical topics, then within the same dialogue finding out that an antagonists name is a dumb pun on a late 90s childrens show. Its not uncommon for manga/anime to have that kind of tonal whiplash but that doesnt make it any better, this isnt the worst case of it ive seen but it could definitely do better.as for other misc complaints: - there are some typos and grammatical errors in a few of the lines of dialogue (not many ~10 from what i remember) - some weapon descriptions have exact damage numbers, some dont, for no reason     > adding on to that, if a weapon has a special attack or charge attack only the basic attack damage will be listed, and sometimes not even that - there are some terrain assets that go a bit farther than they should and makes it look goofy/unprofessional in a few places - 2 achievements just didn't unlock for me despite me doing what they require, woulda had 100% completion if they did too (100% took me ~18 hours at a fairly casual pace) -       >

_childDocuments_.review: Defeat enemies, collect and cook various ingredients that drop from them, eat them to gain permanent new abilities and "passives". That is Dungeon Munchies in a nutshell.The idea has potential. Experimenting with ability and weapon combinations are fun, the player can equip a total of 7 abilities (or passives) and 2 weapons before heading out for combat. Players can switch or mix up their style at certain cooking stations, a meal (ability) needs to be cooked only once, then it can be eaten/equipped countless times. (For some reason you don't have to cook it again, which doesn't make much sense). Weapons are crafted and are not acquired through eating. Not sure what the need for a crafting mechanic was, since both the cooking and eating mechanic are pretty much the same thing within the game.In order to craft or cook stuff, you need to use experience points. Defeating enemies or making progress on the main story grants you XP. Most of the stuff grants so much XP that the XP-cost mechanic itself becomes questionable pretty quickly.Combat and movement feel unpolished, some of the abilities like "climbing" are janky.Pacing is mostly off, sometimes combats are a breeze, and sometimes fights take too long.The level design feels stiff and uninspired, something a platformer must have been extra careful about.Characters are cute and dialogues are fun, some facial expressions feel like a bug than a joke though.All in all, Dungeon Munchies is ok. Cool idea but lacks "polish". I am sure the devs are working on them but I can't really recommend the game at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Nickel is a chemical element with symbol Ni and atomic number 28. It is a silvery-white lustrous metal with a slight golden tinge. Nickel is a hard and ductile transition metal. Pure nickel is chemically reactive but large pieces are slow to react with air under standard conditions because a passivation layer of nickel oxide forms on the surface that prevents further corrosion. Even so, pure native nickel is found in Earth's crust only in tiny amounts, usually in ultramafic rocks, and in the interiors of larger nickel–iron meteorites that were not exposed to oxygen when outside Earth's atmosphere.Use of nickel has been traced as far back as 3500 BC. Nickel was first isolated and classified as an element in 1751 by Axel Fredrik Cronstedt, who initially mistook the ore for a copper mineral, in the cobalt mines of Los, Hälsingland, Sweden. The element's name comes from a mischievous sprite of German miner mythology, Nickel, who personified the fact that copper-nickel ores resisted refinement into copper. An economically important source of nickel is the iron ore limonite, which is often 1–2% nickel. Other important nickel ore minerals include pentlandite and a mix of Ni-rich natural silicates known as garnierite.Because nickel ores are easily mistaken for ores of silver and copper, understanding of this metal and its use, is relatively recent. But unintentional use of nickel is ancient, and can be traced back as far as 3500 BC. Bronzes from what is now Syria have been found to contain as much as 2% nickel. Some ancient Chinese manuscripts suggest that "white copper" or cupronickel, was used there in 1700-1400 BC. This white copper was exported to Britain as early as the 17th century, but the nickel content of this alloy was not discovered until 1822. Coins of nickel-copper alloy were minted by Bactrian kings Agathocles, Euthydemus II, and Pantaleon in the 2nd century BC, possibly out of the Chinese cupronickel.In medieval Germany, a metallic yellow mineral was found in the Erzgebirge that resembled copper ore. But when miners were unable to get any copper from it, they blamed a mischievous sprite of German mythology, Nickel , for besetting the copper. They called this ore Kupfernickel from German Kupfer 'copper'. This ore is now known as the mineral nickeline, a nickel arsenide. In 1751, Baron Axel Fredrik Cronstedt tried to extract copper from kupfernickel at a cobalt mine in the village of Los, Sweden, and instead produced a white metal that he named nickel after the spirit that had given its name to the mineral. In modern German, Kupfernickel or Kupfer-Nickel designates the alloy cupronickel.Originally, the only source for nickel was the rare Kupfernickel. Beginning in 1824, nickel was obtained as a byproduct of cobalt blue production. The first large-scale smelting of nickel began in Norway in 1848 from nickel-rich pyrrhotite. The introduction of nickel in steel production in 1889 increased the demand for nickel; the nickel deposits of New Caledonia, discovered in 1865, provided most of the world's supply between 1875 and 1915. The discovery of the large deposits in the Sudbury Basin, Canada in 1883, in Norilsk-Talnakh, Russia in 1920, and in the Merensky Reef, South Africa in 1924, made large-scale nickel production possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Shoddy and ramshackle in both its gameplay and production, which the screenshots do quite well at hiding. Plays like an extensive student project that also costs money.The talksprites along with some of the animation and pixel art appear fine, but a significant amount of the sprites and environmental design are cheap and inconsistent looking. Enemies randomly jitter, float, slide and wobble around as if the developers couldn't even bother with programming them to believably navigate the terrain. Players attack with lazy looking limb swinging animations to awkwardly beat enemies back, haphazardly platforming away from swarms and overwhelming attacks as they desperately try to pick away at the enemy health bars whenever possible. The platforming is extremely simple yet the few mechanics that it has are sloppy and temperamental. The locations don't inspire any immersion while being so basically structured that it literally feels like a game, not a world.Some of the story elements are interesting but a lot of them are flat and arbitrary. Everything seems so random and mashed together it's almost like a fever dream. Perhaps it's meant to be silly and whimsical but it doesn't feel like either of those at all, just amateurish and unconvincing.This game has perhaps the worst sound design I've ever heard before. Some things that would have sounds, have sounds. But other things that would have sounds just don't have sounds. A lot of the sounds are distinctly quiet and underwhelming compared to others, while the music is so inconsistent as to be forgettable. At least one sound is extremely loud compared to everything else for absolutely no reason at all. It legitimately seems broken; it's so ramshackle between the varying volumes, absences and intensities that it straight up seems busted.The game tries to have this whole resource gathering and item equipping thing but it's not very compelling. Enemies drop materials, new things are made with those materials, sometimes the player has to grind a little to get certain materials; and the new gear they create steadily gets stronger and stronger as the game progresses. It's not very creative and borderline not very necessary either. It's just a slightly alternative way of drip feeding new gameplay options to the player while gradually making the older ones obsolete. This whole system could easily just not be here and the game wouldn't feel much different, just less time spent in menus toggling weapons and passives that don't really make up for the awkward combat. Even on the hardest difficult the game doesn't seem very difficult or engaging as combat just revolves around the player aggressively smacking enemies before moving away or dodging their attacks. It doesn't flow together at all and generally doesn't feel like combat either. Things are relatively easy until the game abruptly decides to be difficult, now suddenly there's a boss that flies around the room filling it with unstructured flurries of projectiles that blanket the screen until avoiding damage becomes physically impossible. If the player survives that stage the boss becomes invincible and just keeps filling the room with more projectiles until the player gets knocked out. I really don't know what the player is supposed to do past that point and honestly I just don't care. This game already felt like a chore to play even before the developers decided to make a boss that shoots two sets of projectiles with the same attack so the player can't dodge through one without randomly getting hit by the other. If I'm going to obsessively memorize every single mechanic on a boss just for it to be beatable then I'll go do that in a better game.Cobbled together assets that look like they were ripped from different store bought packs, sloppy combat that doesn't flow or have any sense of impact, monotonous platforming that randomly won't even cooperate with itself, low effort looking terrain that is completely boring to navigate, superficial progression mechanics that could easily not even be there and nonsensically shallow world design that reads like it was created by a randomizer. The production quality of this game is extremely reminiscent of multiple erotic action platformer games I've seen before. The difference is that this game doesn't reward players with erotic content after they suffer through all the shoddy gameplay. The reward is just more shoddy gameplay and sometimes tolerable character dialogue, over and over until it ends.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

It gets interesting halfway through or so, but then drags its feet through plot points. At the end, I just wanted it to be over.- Gameplay is generally unimpressive and unrefined. _childDocuments_.review: I was inattentive and thought this game was in a genre I like more (management games). Then I thought it was just in a genre I like less but still enjoy sometimes (action RPG-platformers). Then I realized it was also in a genre I've never been able to enjoy (bullet hells). Even when I thought it was an action RPG-platformer, though, I was only having the bare minimum of enjoyment to keep playing. Needs a lot more work than just adding story or balancing existing content to live up to its potential.I honestly thought this was one of those hybrid management game, like Recettear or arguably Stardew Valley, but when it turned out to be an action RPG-platformer (...) well, I figured that was my fault for assuming, and that such a highly-rated game at least deserves a chance (especially since I rather enjoyed Hollow Knight). There were some problems immediately apparent; just off the top of my head I recall that the GUI is basic to the point of being a turn-off, there are some graphics that would be fine for internet memes but come off as cringy in the context of this game, there was at least one typo I spotted in the tutorial, the jumping and movement felt off, many core mechanics felt disappointingly underused to the point of being gimmicky-- but at the time I felt all of those could be overlooked for one reason or another.Indeed, fast forward to around an hour or so later, and I was kind of getting into it-- still didn't really like the controls, and the humor was mildly amusing at best, but it was charming enough in its own way. Then as I was about to beat the second boss, it suddenly turned into a bullet hell-- an unpleasant surprise for me, since I find bullet hells too overwhelming to enjoy (except arguably Enter the Gungeon, and I still haven't gotten past either of its first bosses). I gave it a fair shot anyway, and shortly enough I was able to get to the bullet hell section pronto. Unfortunately, getting past that was like hitting my face on a brick wall over and over, and I just could not bring myself to care enough to put in the effort anymore.I hesitated to give this game a thumbs down, as many of my problems are rooted in mistaken expectations that could have been very easily corrected before I bought this game. Ultimately, though, one thing led me to post this review anyway: even setting aside that I'm not the game's intended audience, I feel that it lacks the well-honed basic experience I'd expect of any game that has an overwhelmingly positive rating. Perhaps I just didn't give it long enough for it to come into its own, but even when I thought it was just an action RPG, I was only minimally engaged-- it was fine enough to play in the moment, but I don't think I would have felt compelled to go back to it on either a gameplay or story basis.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly enjoyable game that was swept under my radar. I was hesitant about picking this up because I thought it'd be a bit weeby and tacky. I was wrong. A lot happens, and by the end of it all, there are so many feels going on that it just makes you sad that it's over. In terms of combat, it's pretty fluid and there's a bunch of upgrades you can mess around with to make some ridiculous builds. I enjoyed experimenting and hunting for new recipes (abilities). While it wasn't a particularly long game, I loved almost every moment of it. Big ups to the devs and I hope they make more games in the future with a similar style of writing. On a side note, there are some iconic Taiwanese details in the game that anyone who has been to or lived in Taiwan would immediately recognise. I wonder if there were some subtle jokes about Taiwan that went over my head? One last thing, don't reduce the difficulty if you want some kind of challenge. I got ♥♥♥♥♥ up by a boss and reduced the difficulty to see how I could beat it. The game does warn you that it's irreversible, but I thought at some point I could change the difficulty again, like in New Game +. _childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a game that starts off lighthearted and gradually transitions into a dramatic and dark narrative, sprinkled with slightly cringe-inducing yet humorously charming moments to balance it out. The characters within the game exhibit depth and character development, which adds to the overall experience.In the game, you assume the role of a zombie in search of sustenance, obtained by slaying monsters to create new dishes and weapons that grant you enhanced abilities. The gameplay is both enjoyable and straightforward, and on the highest difficulty level, you'll encounter challenging bosses that keep you engaged.As you progress, you'll come across Simmer and Grill, two characters who play pivotal roles in your journey. The story takes you deeper into a peculiar and gory underground city, concealing a mysterious secret that explains the absence of humans.Dungeon Munchies is a fantastic game with a compelling story that takes you on an emotional rollercoaster. However, it does have some noticeable bugs that remain unpatched. Notably, the lack of right stick controller support for aiming and menu navigation, which can reset your language settings and hotkeys upon interaction.Despite these issues, I was able to overlook them because it's one of the best story-driven games I've ever encountered. It made me laugh, brought tears to my eyes, and provided plenty of fun, leaving me yearning for more. The only downside is that Chapter 3 feels a bit rushed, and some aspects of the story are left unexplored, resulting in an open-ended conclusion. I would have appreciated some cinematic sequences or a more conclusive ending.For me, Dungeon Munchies deserves a solid 9/10 (10/10 without bugs), and I eagerly look forward to any future projects from Majaja. It's a hidden gem, and it's unfortunate that it's not more popular, as I'd love to purchase merchandise to show my support. <3<3<3

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a wild ride. Honestly I was losing interest in the beginning but I'm glad I powered through because I would've missed out on an utterly bizarre story full of captivating characters and intriguing world building. The gameplay can be frustrating at times with enemies that are super easy but bosses that are artificially super difficult. What I mean by this is the bosses die just as easy as anything else, but at certain hp checkpoints they just become nigh invincible and turn the game into a bullet hell by spamming projectile attacks that cover the entire screen; this lasts for 1-2 minutes probably but can feel like an eternity. Halfway through the game you start being able to pull off weapon and perk combos that just completely break the game, but even with that I still needed a few tries on certain bosses. This was probably done to maintain a semblance of challenge in the game, whether that's a good thing or not with this type of game is up to you but ultimately I didn't mind it too much. Speaking of the game breaking combo stuff, it's honestly pretty fun and allows for a lot of custom builds. All in all, the whole experience was pleasantly surprising, would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a charming Platformer RPG, reminiscent of Cave Story.  I thought it was going to be a roguelite metroidvania with monster hunter elements of upgrading your gear through fighting enemies, but it turned out to be a perma unlock crafting system.  You can come up with all kinds of builds and such with different weapon types!The strongest part of the game is the story - it's really good at capturing a heartful story interspersed with dark humor and very likable characters.  When the gameplay slowed down a bit what kept me going was wanting to explore all the little lore bits and read the rest of the story!  They do a great job with the callbacks, especially what I thought was a throwaway joke ending up becoming super integral to the plot!The core gameplay consists of fighting your way through a level, picking up the monster materials, and then finding recipes sometimes to craft new gear.  Then you equip combinations of food and weapons to take on the next stage.  There's definitely a lot of fun to be had fiddling around with the different archetypes and combinations, whereas my favorite was the summoning type.  As for the general combat feel, it's pretty solid but it does feel slightly stiff compared to a game like Dead Cells, which is my golden standard.  Sometimes there's swarms of enemies where it gets kind of mosh-y, and other times you get sniped by a laser from a faraway enemy.  Some of the stage designs are kind of annoying, especially later on when there's a bunch of diagonal slopes which act kind of weird with the game physics.  Sometimes the jumps seem kind of weird since you'll just bounce off a platform when you're trying to ascend.  On the topic of difficulty, the curve seems pretty weird.  Expect to die a lot as you figure out how the enemies work, especially the bosses with their bullet hell attacks.  The clarity could also be a bit better - with how crowded it gets in some stages it's hard to tell if i'm getting hit or avoiding the attacks.  Expect to get swarmed and die a few times in some places.  Overall though, between the generous checkpoints and flexible weapon-changing, it shouldn't be too bad to figure out how to beat bosses.  I wouldn't call it extremely difficult, but there are times where it seems like it's difficult not to die.On the whole, I really enjoyed the game despite a few bugs (i.e. pausing with enemies around doesn't stop their movements).  Definitely worth trying out!  Play past chapter 1 before really making a decision - that's where it really kicks off!

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a little bit of an acquired taste, but once you do, it's a good experience.Gameplay:Completely middle-of-the-road action-platformer combat play is propped up immensely by the meal/weapon combination system. It doesn't really elevate it to a higher state of play, but it's fun. Probably best played with keyboard and mouse, as the aiming was wonky as ♥♥♥♥ with a controller. The simplicity of the gameplay makes this much more acceptable than it would otherwise be. You can be precise and get through things without taking a single hit, certainly... but there's a fair bit of wiggle room. The cursor and controller would get into messy arguments about who was in charge, frequently requiring a game restart or switching program focus to something else, then back to the game.If the controls were silky smooth with everything else being the same, and if there weren't the seemingly random conflicts of input when I'm not even touching the mouse, there'd be no real complaints. A simple game that controls really well gets more points than a simple game that controls okay. Sometimes, due to the stickiness of the selection, I'd wind up spending a lot of resources upgrading something I had no intent of ever using. This additional layer of required deliberation contributed to the overall Kinda Clumsy™ feeling the game had.Story:Ramps up kind of slowly, but once it got its hooks in I pretty much had to finish the game. Arguably the best part of the game. Characters were all quite delightful.Aesthetics:Passable-to-good. Some visual glitching in the appearance of the Zombie Chef protagonist, especially when it comes to attack frames and meals that change facial expressions. Some memey and Crude Humour™, mostly pertaining to things like whacking the stiff logs off the front of trees, etcetera. It's a weirdly horny game, or at least I found it to be.Music was generally kind of forgettable until Ch2 onward, but that might be on me. Sound effects do their job - though it seemed like enemy sounds could get "stuck" in certain areas, and sometimes they were annoying sounds, so my playthrough was just perpetually periodically haunted by the horrid squealing death rattles of various things.So I guess, out of 5, we'd say... Gameplay 2.5 (Mid), Story 4.5 (Great), Aesthetics 3 (Fine). This seems to be the dev's first game or at least their first released game, and I'm keeping an eye out for anything from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting a typical Metroidvania experience but ended up getting so much more than that. I have absolutely no complaints about the game other than not having more content to play. This review was written by someone who aims to get 100% completion in these types of games, and plays on the hardest difficulty. Not that it really matters but I felt like including it for my perspective on the bosses.For starters, the amount of customization that is available is absolutely insane. There are over 100 different dishes to make with each having their own unique effects that change how you play the game. Not to mention that they also change the appearance of your character, which to me made me feel like my build and character were unique to me. There's definitely something for every style of play, so you'll have to do your own experimenting to see what you like and what feels good to you. There are also over 100 different weapons to choose from. These are a bit more copy and paste with improved stats as you progress through the game, but most still have their own unique strengths, weaknesses, and effects. I will say without spoiling anything that the weapons you unlock near the end of the game are completely bonkers in terms of visual effects and fun value.The bosses are all unique and fun to fight as well, with not being a single re-skin of a previous boss in the game to be found. Some bosses are definitely harder than others and have a learning curve to them, but none felt like they were hard just for the sake of being hard. One thing I will say is that I think most of the bosses have "survival/desperation" attacks, where you can't do any damage to the boss and are forced to dodge and survive until the attack ends. There are two fights from my memory that are harder than others due to this and you will most likely die to them your first time(s) around, but don't let that turn you off of the game, it truly is a great experience!The story and the characters are definitely what surprised me the most. I don't want to spoil anything for anyone who hasn't played it, but this games story goes so much deeper than just cooking different food dishes for different effects. You'll have to play it to find out what that entails to though! The characters are all immediately lovable with each one feeling unique and being a stand out when compared to the rest. At no point did it feel like a character was introduced just for the sake of their introduction. The writing for all of the characters is done extremely well too. They know when to be goofy and go for laughs, and they know when to be serious. I think there needs to be a fine balance between these two and they nailed it on the head for sure. I even found myself getting (slightly) emotional at points if that tells you how good the story is, from a game you think is just about making food.There IS postgame content, but I haven't gone that deep into it and am unsure if I will or not. From what I can tell it's pretty much like every other New Game+ in games where you keep everything you found in your previous playthrough, and go through the same game again with significantly harder enemies. There's a cherry on top giving you incentive to play it again, but like other New Game+ playthroughs, it's simply to provide minor power boosts to your character.In conclusion I'll keep it short. If the game looks like something you're interested in, it more than likely is. There's a reason this game has overwhelmingly positive reviews. It's a relatively short game, as you could probably complete it in under 10 hours if you don't want to get 100% completion, but I genuinely think you're missing part of the fun if you don't 100% the game. Definitely a recommend from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Wow I really knew nothing about this game when I went in. I just saw it has cooking and some interesting looking combat. I will say it did not disappoint! So much stuff to experiment with in combat and a fun quirky story! I'm only about half way through right now and when I started I thought this was going to be a much shorter game. If you can, I'd recommend going in blind and trying it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because it looked interesting, and I played it all the way to the end due to its lovable cast and genuinely splendid writing that comedically mocks many aspects of our postmodern society. The game feels like one massive sh!tpost (in a good way) with its endless jokes, but it knows when to be serious too. Just for the characters and story alone, you should play this game, 100%.In terms of game play, if the trailer and previews intrigue you, then it'll be your type of game.The soundtrack isn't really something to write home about, but it's not bad either.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: To not give it a deserved review the truth is that this game made me give a new opportunity to the metroidvania and indies, I did not give much hope to the genre but after playing Dungeon Munchies I realized how much fun they are.a little synopsis:you are a zombie who just woke up without knowing very well who you are or what is happening, as you progress you meet a ghost who loves to cook and your goal is to help her accomplish her goal while you discover the events that were happening in the world while you meet other characters that will help you in some way in the story, the game has its own humor and a very catching plot as you progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: When I first launched the game, I thought it was a steaming hot pile of garbage. Only the cute anime waifu kept my interest. But I guess that during the time the game was in early access, the developers sharpened their skills quite a bit. By the time I got to the point where the second waifu with the huge honkers shows up, I was completely engrossed in both the gameplay and the story. Dungeon Munchies is a fun game that isn't about difficulty and overcoming challenges, but rather about the player's creativity in making a build that will humiliate and wipe to dust anything that moves on the level. Of course, the challenge is still present, because the bosses have mechanics that won't allow you to just roll your face on the keyboard and win. The way the developers twisted the story after the first chapter is commendable. Together with the soundtrack, it creates very memorable moments, especially when the feeling of loneliness or sadness sets in. Frankly, the soundtrack was one of the best parts of the whole experience for me. Not everything is perfect, of course; some of the dialogue was too cheesy, and some of the allegories were too in-your-face. Like, completely unaware of who the developers were or where they were from, I managed to precisely determine at one point in the game that they were from Taiwan. Nothing against that, of course, just an interesting observation. In short, the game is great and deserves its rating on Steam. But to be honest, I still can't decide between Simmer and Grill. Both are top-tier waifus. In the end, it all depends on whether you preach flat is justice or enjoy being dominated and called a mommy's boy. As for me, I just want a hug.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies may not be a cooking game, but the joy Simmer takes in the expression and experimentation of the art is something you get to participate in by cooking up... character builds!No, but seriously: in this game there's no faffing about with stats or whatever. Your build is determined entirely by your gear (two weapons and seven dishes), making it a breeze to tinker with or completely swap playstyles whenever you feel like it. One (pleasant) shock was that you don't even consume ingredients to cook or craft, making the grind practically nonexixtent!The story was a pleasant surprise, too. It keeps a tight focus on its cast that gives their personalities, relationships, and history plenty of room to breathe, elevating the story beyond its surreal and ♥♥♥♥-posty tone. I found the pacing to falter a little at the third act, as it felt like I was being yanked away from the finish line to repeat some themes and wrap up a B-plot, but the general quality of the presentation and the inherent fun of spin-2-winning my way through everything softened the blow quite a bit, and the finale was definitely worth the trouble.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game! From the nods to mega man, to the dark as sin story.Boy does the story gets dark... but some how the devs manage to find humour in it and builds all the characters so well. Action is also really spot on too.I don't really have anything bad to say about this game. For it's price it's definitely worth it. Some of the subtle jokes are related to the culture in Taiwan, but none of it hurts the story. Here's hoping more people will get to play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I am so happy I found this game.This is a gem. Truly fun and enjoyable every step of the way through. Tons of items to collect, many different builds to make. The best part is that all the upgrades are really meaningful and they don't require ANY grinding, unless you want to make multiple builds (which the games lets you have later on). The story is the perfect blend of goofy yet heartfelt, and it really ramps up at the end. I am always going to remember the story of Simmer and Grill. This game is 100% worth the full price, but if it ever goes on sale BUY IT. Super fun, and you can easily make it much more difficult with higher difficulty settings and NG+. For collectors, there are plenty of hidden items to find. In terms of replayability, I'd say its pretty decent as the combat is fun enough and varies enough with each build that every playthrough could feel different enough to not get old. Music is also very good. Theres a few minor bugs in the settings menu, but other than that everything worked very well technically, only frame drops during quicksave spots, never crashed.It's been so long since a game truly made me smile while playing it, I needed this. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon munchies, it was a really fun game for me. Though it is something that the best way you can describe it is "It's an indie game." Some dishes are just outright superior to others, so are some weapons, and then upgrades get involved and sometimes enemies get irritating.But it wasn't bad. I really loved the characters, especially the three waifus. My only real complaints are that at points the plot felt a little repetitively preachy in the message that it was trying to get across, there was also the issue that is the finnickiness of your summoned companions. I had a ton towards the end and they seemed pretty reluctant to attack if they were range based like the drones, so I had to basically get in the face of the enemy. But overall I had a fun time. It isn't long, the plot isn't the most complex, and I imagine new game+ is just a fun romp with all your OP gear.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly great action platformer. The pixel art is great, the RPG mechanics are satisfying to engage with, the soundtrack is incredible, and the story is actually worth paying attention to without taking itself too seriously. This game came out of nowhere for me, but was so good I played through the entire thing in one day. Easy recommend even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a unique and entertaining game that combines cooking and combat in a fun way. The game's graphics are beautiful and well-designed, with a cute and colorful pixel art style.You play as a zombie who must explore a dungeon, gather ingredients, and cook meals to gain new abilities and progress through the game. You can experiment with different combinations of ingredients to create the perfect build for each stage/boss.Combat in the game is fast-paced and challenging, with a variety of enemies and bosses to fight. Overall, Dungeon Munchies a fun and challenging game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This is not your average dungeon crawler. Packed with funny dialogue, personable characters, and increasingly ridiculous recipes Dungeon Munchies offers hours of entertainment (and frustration). While the endless combinations of weapons, fighting styles, and power ups add much replay-ability to the game, I personally fell in love with the goofy spectral chefs and their skeletal collaborators, and was quite surprised to find myself scouring levels for any morsels  of lore I could find, and holding my breath every time the story progressed. While sometimes the movement mechanics feel a bit undercooked, overall DM offers great writing, great pacing, and above all great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I usually dont get emotional over games but this. This got me emotional. I got this game ages ago and finally decided to play it. Its got that whole doki doki situation going on as the first chapter is kinda just wholesome while the second chapter(and end of first) has some pretty good body horror. All the bosses are dope but the coolest ones have to be the fleshy abominations.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: The absolute goofiest and zaniest dungeon crawler I have ever played. Fight every urge to skip the text, and do yourself a favor and just read some of it from time to time. The story and side quests are just bonkers. The combat is really intuitive. There is a priority to progression but skill is king. If you can dodge and have decent coordination then you don't really have to rely on gear and talents that much. The dungeons are fun and imaginatively planned and designed. Doesn't really get boring either, it just increases the intensity as you progress enough that you don't lose yourself and you also just can't put it down. Just loads of fun and potential to just play it over and over.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Ive gotten past the Lord PRotector so far. Heres my criticism on it however:I think the ups and downs of difficulty make it really hard to play through. 5 goats is harder then the hypes up boss.It should have a class guide so you know what foods to get if your a mage or melee or ranger.It doesnt have to much playtime it seemsBut other then that, id say its worth the price for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just perfect to me. the combat flows well and you can create your own play-style with the various combinations of food and weapons, the music is amazing, humor is on point, and the visuals are great! I recommend to take your time with this game in just take it in for what it is. The only thing i do wish for is an actual cookbook (please make it happen).
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing Metroidvania which to me checks all the right marks in the right spots.The platforming is fun and interesting with hazards not being randomly slapped everywhere but fairly placed and if you actually try to avoid the traps you probably won't die to them. (Also no instant kill garbage, i.e Blasphemous)There's a large variant of Enemies that puts most of the Metroidvania Genre to shame and nearly all unique with what they do and how they try to clobber your undead posterior.The Music is fitting and generally pretty good, it won't leave you hanging.The character design is amazing and probably the best part of the game.The story is very engaging and even if it has memes or jokes written into it which they interchange between serious and joking though it's mostly serious stuff later on.The variety of weapons and upgrades the game offers is incredible compared to many of the Metroidvania clones out there and I would even dare say comes close to what the original concept wanted to have.Considering this is the developers first game, this game should get all the support it needs because I can only see a shining light at the end of the tunnel for what awaits us after this game.I'd give this an honest 9.0-9.5/10 just for a little bit of the glitches that the game might have, (i.e Simmer showing up twice in a place for some reason and the light axe not working properly.)
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: So, the hype and the criticisms are real.  What a wild ride it was.  The only regret you will have with Dungeon Munchies is not being able to experience it all again for the first time, but rest assured a thing of beauty will never fade away, thorns and all.If you end up vibing with this experience, rest assured your time and dime will be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful experience. Tons of fun to play and it's hard to stop once you start playing. I love trying out new weapons and builds and the concept of cooking to get stronger is interesting as well. The characters and art are lovely and the conversations are great too. They managed to bring home a deep message to the players while you have fun and laugh with the characters. Super fun and worthwhile. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game, and i only just beated the game once! I still have to try out the new game plus and hardest difficulty!The characters are on point and hilarious, and there are multiple ways you can play this game! Even thought you can trivialize some fights with the schyte weapons in normal difficulty, but then the solution is to use another weapon and try to learn that. I highly recomend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging yet simple game. The large variety of abilities and weapons in the game will allow you to create different kinds equipment and ability sets to the point that you can get pretty damn OP. The story is more than it seems at first and is paced out well. The same can't be said for the power ups you get though. Most of the power ups will be shoved in you halfway into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the concept and reviews for the game and needed to try it. I was so hooked I played through it in 3 days. You need to play this. There is so little on this game on the internet but I adored every minute. Existential dread, fun cooking and friends, Terraria meets Risk of Rain combat almost, min maxing and so many ways to switch up your build.  Spooky twists and lore that made me want to find out more. I can't say the entire game was unique, but its definitely a memorable experience worth trying.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems like a cute one. It subverts that expectation. It is not just cute. It's got decent controls, a wonderfully interesting story (ahh the joys of existentialism, arguments about meaning itself, labor and the weight of being a ruler) and some fun gameplay mechanics; an excellent all rounder and a great use of your time. A few of the memes are really good deep cuts and the humor made me smile plenty. Fun little achievements too. Greatly recommended. It is not a hard game and rewards both exploration and changing your build to suit your problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of the side scroller genre. If this is also your reason for not giving Dungeon Munchies a try, I don't blame you. It took me 4 full months to finally consider making an exception, and that's because this game was on sale.And now I am begging you to buy this masterpiece so that I may play another game from this studio as soon as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very fun! Still worth the price! I bought it on sale.Pros:Action combat is very fluid, with multiple jumps, air dashes, timed dodges, choice between melee and ranged weapons and shieldsGreat dialogue, fun charactersEnvironment looks great (for an indie studio) and very fitting to the storyline (occult horror)Cons (depending on your viewpoint):Very linear, no sidequests or meaningful choicesNot memorable music, in my opinion
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game.  I don't know exactly what I was expecting when I came in, but this blew me away.  Really, really good.  The gameplay is one element; you have a ton of freedom in customization that allows you to change up your build very quickly and easily.  Bosses often ask you to try multiple different builds until you figure out what works for you, so have fun with that.  The music was great, and I'll be listening to it for a while. However, the best part of this game was absolutely the story.  The characters are all fantastic, and I enjoyed every moment I got to speak with the cast.  Cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, loved the story. Gameplay might get a bit repetitive but it's still serviceable and fun, finding the best food combo that you like is definitely addictive.The story's REALLY GOOD. Dialogue writing is full of internet culture but doesn't lean into the memey-side to make some very funny jokes.Absolutely recommend it if you enjoy cleverly written characters and an interesting story.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the store page for Dungeon Munchie, I didn't take it to serious, I thought it a funny meme game but I was wrong. This game writing is exceptional and the narrative is very engrossing with very causal cute/funny moment as well as very dark and unsettling moment. A perfect blend. Gameplay:The game play like stated is a 2D platformer metrovania which has some customization on load out where you can focus on ranged, physical, magic, as well as food buff you can apply to make it more build defining. You can create buff  by cooking monster you defeat as you travel from zone to zone. There also hidden recipe you can find, if you go off the pathway into hidden corridor. The combat in my opinion is probably the weakest part of the game. it can feel very repetitive and boring.  Game play length is actually quite longer then I expected, Averaging around around 8-12 hours for main story.The Story:The story is well written and quite enjoyable and definitely the best part of this game. It is deliver in a visual novel style format which work well enough. The story start out very lighthearted and goofy as your MC is a zombie who eventually become a apprentice to this professional cook name Simmer who happen to be the very powerful necromancer spirit. As you play through the story, the game start to shift to a much darker story hidden in the background but it still keep it lighthearted and comedic dialogue to balance it out. I wont go much into the main narrative but it story that has to with existential crises, depression, sadness, loss of hope and bit of horror.Music:The music choice is quite good. Composer rAye create a blend of atmospheric, EDM and progressive rock that has this very chill almost lofi feel to it that bring the world alive. Each well crafted to bring out different emotion depending on the scene.Final thought:I guess don't judge a game on first appearances. There more to Dungeon Munchie then just cooking monster. Underneath it colorful cast of characters/world, hide something much more sinister and darker in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that feels like a complete package; good front to back.  No single part drags down the experience, and no matter what part of the game youre engaging with, whether that be the combat, story, or build-crafting, its all a good time.  Its a little rough around the edges, as even four months out from last playing the game, I can remember some bugs or awkward features, which glancing at the updates appear not to have been fixed.  That being said, Id be hard pressed to recommend a better game I played this year.  Well, maybe not that hard pressed, but this ones still a winner.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out silly and a bit too easy, and ends with full on bullet hell style bosses in a story more fit for a cosmic horror title. There are many weapons and buff combinations to keep game play fresh, and the characters are likable enough that you feel for them when you see how messed up the situation actually is.My only real complaint is that it was too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game just does  good. The story - engaging and interesting; what first seems to be a lighthearted cooking game, quickly progresses into way darker tones. The bosses - I've never had to fight a literal vegetable Gundam mecha, a muscular vegetable vine and a literal nightmarish Eldritch Abomination from other universe, all in one game. The music - banger. It fits the scenery perfectly - sometimes it's soothing, sometimes it's sad, sometimes it's sinister and dark. Summing it up - I came for the ghost waifu, I stayed for everything else. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, short and sweet game, just like the dishes you cook up (i think)I had actually bought the game a couple years ago since i had the money at the time and it seemed pretty cool, but i wanted to wait until it was fully released to actually play it, and boy, am I glad I let it finish baking before having a bite. (I'll see myself out.)To elaborate a bit, the game only took me about ten hours to get 100% completion, but I was enamored the whole time, and I think that's more than worth it. The bosses are rad, the soundtrack is a bop, the story is great for reasons I cant elaborate on, and the best part is there's so much to work with that how I've gotten through the game with my combinations of weapons and food probably isn't gonna be the exact same way you handle your playthrough.All in all, game's great. Pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game, man. I'm not gonna go into details on the story, because this game should be experienced blind. There's so much more than just another "Quirky Retro Platformer" here. This story is good, and the game's much longer than you'd expect.As for the gameplay... It's also very good. The HUGE number of weapons and powerups you can get in this game undoubtedly has a ton of fun builds you can do. Wanna be a summoner? Go ahead, pick up a scythe. Wanna rely on Damage over time? Grab yourself a dagger and some debuff items. Ranged? Grab a bow or some magic. The game does still typically build around your weapon choice, but it gives you plenty of options.The boss fights are where this game shines, though. While the early game as a whole is weak (the story doesn't hook you right away, the gameplay is simplistic, etc.) the late game bosses are, I kid you not, on some touhou stuff. Straight up, between phases bosses will have their CG pop up in the background, and they'll just go full bullet hell on you. Some of these patterns look right at home in a touhou game.Overall, I suggest you get this game. If you have any worries you aren't getting you money's worth, don't worry. The game's like 10 hours long, and TONS of fun, with a cast of characters I've grown to adore.9/10, I'd say. It's not a perfect game. Animations could use some work, and some weapons are clearly better than others in certain points in the game, but the story, world, characters, and even the quirky bits of humor were absolutely endearing.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, the combat is good, its cool that you have all those different playstyles to choose from,the level design is cool and lots of different locations but the real gem is the story.Its just so good. Its starts out with this cute fun story and gets real serious the second half of the game.Would like to experience it again without knowing anything ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I will let Clifford tell you my first impressions on this game.Clifford: Arf Arf!That's right Clifford, couldn't have said it better! This game is a hidden gem on Steam; it has great gameplay, amazing music and satisfying boss fights.Also a funny yet serious story that will subvert your expectations all the time.Clifford: Arf!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a bit of a sleeper hit. The main weaknesses are that the pacing at the start is a bit slow and the music is pretty whatever for the most part, but it really builds on itself with a well put together story and combat that gives you enough freedom to try out different things and see what sticks. Different builds are definitely encouraged for different situations, and while there is some power disparity in different areas, it doesn't ever feel like it really takes away from the feel of the game. The humor can be fairly hit or miss, but never borders on being unbearable. Overall a fun, unexpected experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This is what happens when you mix the gameplay of Terarria with the atmosphere of Made in Abyss. Really interesting story with a good sense of humor. The cooking mechanic and weapon crafting allows you to experiment with a lot of really fun different builds. Amazing game that deserves more attention!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes you feel like an actual friend. It's hard to not find yourself caring for the characters.the game itself is pretty straight forward, kill things and use things to make more things to kill things and to it's credit it has a lot of different buffs and weapons but I have found myself far more drawn to the story and the people of the game than the combat. And I love bullet hell combat
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much everything about this game is amazing.I loved the story and the wild ride it took me on.The comedy is fantastic.The combat is a bit simplistic, but build diversity is pretty large. The soundtrack is full of legit bangers.It's overall just a really fun time.Do yourself a favour and experience this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty meme-y, fairly linear, metroidvania-ish game about being a zombie that gains powers from eating "food."This game is shockingly good and weirdly hard.There are three difficulty settings and you can lower the difficulty if you hit a point in the game that you just aren't good enough to get pasts anymore. Unfortunately, you can't re-raise the difficulty once you get past that point, but the game is still fun either way.The story itself is good enough to keep me reading the dialogue and the characters were engaging enough that I cared about them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game. some of the builds you can do are fun as hell, with a pretty wide variety of weaponry and buffs I was still experimenting at the end of the game. The story was surprisingly good, i was expecting it to just be there to push the game play but to my surprise it turned out to be well written. In all i'd say buy it if you enjoy 2D action games. only complaint is that weapons fall off at the end of the game, unlike the power-ups provided by the food. it would be nice to be able to upgrade the weapons to still be usable.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my new favorite honestly.Gameplay seems weird at first but as you go through it starts to click and become very fun to mess with.Art and Graphics are fantastic too, you'll definitely feel immersed into the world.Story is actually really good, at first I was skeptical but my opinion quickly shifted the more I played the game. This game is a 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Initially checked out the game because a friend showed me the funny stretchy face lady in the preview, finished it because the game is just so delightfully goofy with wonderful characters and a fun premise. It has a very nice variety of weapons to choose from that you can mix and match to your heart's content. Swords, spears, shields, axes, guns, lasers, bows, daggers, throwing weapons, grappling hooks, various spells, and a few others I can't remember, a whole smorgasbord to pick from and customise with all the ability granting munchies you can shove down your gullet,  though personally I probably went for the most "boring" build of dual axe blender sustain, I still had a blast doing so anyways.Music was quiet nice and surprisingly varied, though some of the sound effects for various elements were rather lacking but not in any way that it detracted from my experience.The story also kept my interest and rather large in scope which is something I wasn't expecting. Not wanting to give anything away but when it ramps up it ramps up fast. As for the game's art, man oh man did it take me by surprise at just the variety of enemies and the amazing backgrounds it has going on, and that's not even mentioning all the character portraits, be they goofy veggies or stretchy ghosts. (Shout out to Captain DUI)Though I will say the game does have quite a few bugs going on still. The one I've encountered the most was when I was scrolling through my recipe list, the selected box would jump over and highlight one of the ingredients on an unfinished recipe which was annoying at times. There was another which I'm not sure how it happened, but I managed to glitch out the menus and had different and never before seen UI elements pop up and cover the screen as they refused to close. The last bug that I can recall was during the final boss. Essentially I had swap my build out on the fly because something wasn't working as intended and caused the fight to be a crapshoot on whether or not I'd die instantly from getting hit. But all in all, for twenty bucks this game is an absolute gem. Fun game, great art, good music, and fantastic characters. Definitely recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that Chapter 3 which I assume is the last chapter of this game is out, I feel like I can write a review now, so here goes. My apologies for the long review, TLDR; at the bottomBefore I talk about the pros and the cons I need to talk about something else for a bit. It doesn't really fit into neither the pros or the cons in my opinion so I kinda want to get it out of the way first. Bite sized length: This point, in my opinion can be seen as a bad thing or a good thing depends on the person, this is because this game is very short at the time of this writing I spent 15 hours and I already completed the game. And while I enjoyed my time with it other people might expected this game to have more contents to offer considering the price, but outside of beating up monsters through out the game, reaching the final boss, and new game+. This game doesn't really have much contents to offer which, depends on the person. can either be a good thing or a bad thing.Cons:The translations: From what I can see, it seems like this game's main language is chinese. And because of that there are bound to be some translation errors due to the language barrier. And while I'm not entirely sure, this might applies to the other language options in the game as well.The Final Chapter: It's almost like the chapter has been rushed, and it's a bit disappointing. For the final chapter of a game, it's really short and while the final boss's gimmick is rather interesting, it's still a letdown for me.And now, let's look at the pros. There's not much to talk about due to the simplicity and the rather short length of the game, but it doesn't mean that these aren't great.Pros:Fun game play: you build your character by collecting a large variety of ingredients(which there is A LOT of, I'm sure you'll be very surprised) and cook them into various foods which then you can eat (aka equip them). These foods will grants you various buffs ranging from generic buff for your character to outright granting new attacks and play styles, these new attacks and play styles are linked to the various weapons and equipments you can use though, so it's a bit limited but the variety makes up for it in my opinion. And there are permanent upgrade you get by simply progress through the game as well.Story: Easily the best part of the game, you started out a bit slow(to some it might feels confusing but I have no problem however), but the story continues to improve as more and more mysteries and new plot point reveals itself, then suddenly you'll quickly realize that there's more to this game than meets the eyes, the store page alone might get you interested since it does contains a bit of spoilers in it. And not to mention the comedy, which I personally really loved it. It contains jokes that references the world we lived in and it happened from time to time in the story which I think is a really nice addition to the story as a whole.The art: Cute and charming yet . If you're someone who enjoys the anime art styles, I think you'll love it.TLDR; A fun little adventure game that you can complete in about 2 days or even 1 day if you're really good at bullet hell, the price might makes you skip the game however, but if any of the things I mentioned or the premises of the game caught your attention. Then at least I recommended that you get the game once it's on sales.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't terribly impressed for the first hour or so of this game; it seems to focus primarily on meme centric, cheesy dialogue initially. This slowly evolves through chapter one, ending with a dark turn and instilling in you the impression that you're no longer playing a silly, lighthearted game. You're not left entirely in the dark thankfully, as the slapstick, off the wall humor persists throughout the whole experience, offsetting the dark tone of an inevitable disaster slowly approaching.Customization is king here, and much appreciated. Builds are easy to plan and a sound strategy for whomping enemies and bosses comes fairly naturally. I sort of just stumbled into a scythe build with soul explosions, coupled with a dps secondary and it worked like a charm. Every recipe and ingredient has a clever bit of lore with it along with well made sprites. Combat is not terribly challenging, as long as you have a proper build to champion your way. Bosses don't feel unduly difficult and are each unique, bringing new mechanics to each fight.I cannot emphasize enough the depth of the story experience here; while the game starts off silly, it quickly progresses and sinks you deep into a world filled with strife, sadness, and peril. Dialogue interactions can become very heartfelt quickly, cutting through any lighthearted tone set just minutes before. Characters are unique and interesting, each with their own piece of the overall puzzle to add, making for convincing interactions. There's just an absolute grab bag of references, philosophy, and rationale to mull over when viewing some of these scenes. While the absurd character designs can be a bit distracting, pulling you out of the moment and asking such questions as "why the hell am I listening to a living pineapple ponder the meaning of it's place in society and have an existential meltdown while being slowly crushed under the tyrannical rule of a living ice cream cone?" I've found those moments only serve to enhance the charm of the game.If you like DEEP story combined with fast paced, satisfying combat, platforming, and build customization, it's the perfect game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of inconsistencies to this game. Most of the time I enjoy my time playing this game, however I think it's still important to highlight the parts that I think can make or break the enjoyment of playing this game.First, the story. It started with plenty of jokes and light-hearted moments, but then the story gets too serious it ruins the pacing and immersion. Right now I'm 2/3 done with Chapter 2, and I don't know if the plot will get better once I finish it. Second, the movement. This game isn't advertised for platforming, so I expect the game not to be too punishing if I get the jumps wrong. However, the movement is pretty janky; I expect to be able to double jump after hugging a wall, but the game sometimes only let me do one jump. Because of this I took damage in places where I shouldn't, and it's really annoying.Third, the difficulty. I'm playing on normal difficulty but I feel like it's too easy. In first chapter I died a few times because of the builds aren't that great, however once you transition to mid-game, the builds decimate enemies in seconds you barely take damage. Boss fights can be trivialized too, I barely get to see the boss does normal attacks as I shred their HP too quickly, I only had to react to their bullet-hell moments where they are immune to any damage until they are done with it.Maybe grab the game during a sale, because $20 doesn't seem to be worth it considering the game isn't that long and with the problems mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast and a half to play! I haven't had this much fun in awhile, I highly recommend this, especially for the 20$ price tag (or even better if it's on sale).The gameplay is fun, chaotic, fast paced at times, and the difficulty progresses at a reasonable pace so you don't feel like you're hitting random difficulty spikes that ruin your momentum. You start off as a lowly zombie, slowly making your way through the games story and world while collecting different items and weapons to make yourself more powerful. You also walk and move around on this 2D plane but as you progress you gain tons of freedom for movement throughout the game, which is something I liked a ton! You go from walking around to basically flying everywhere across the screen.The weapon and item varieties are very fun and allow plenty of different play styles, whether you like ranged or melee or even magical weapons. I found myself mostly playing with the spears, guns, and magic the most because of all the fun passives that work with them from the items you can craft. The passives you can get from items modify your gameplay a lot as well, whether giving yourself new attacks with weapons, more mobility, more damage/effects, and other useful passives.The characters are also very well done, with everyone you run into having their own distinguishable personality even if they're a random side character. The humor with NPCs and Item/Weapon descriptions throughout the game is also top notch, I was stuck laughing a good bit at many different times, just to screenshot something someone said and show a friend because it was that good. My personal favorite being Captain DUI, a real american hero. It never feels over the top or too forced as well, the story in the game has a good mix of its being silly and being more serious moments too. I usually am a dialogue skipper but I found myself not doing that for this game, and actually going along with the characters and reading what they had to say, and it was definitely worth it. I'm even going back and trying to earn all the achievements because I enjoyed it that much.

_childDocuments_.review: So some thoughts now that this is done.Overall:- Highly interesting build design. Not only is there a lot of ways you could viably play, but often times weapons that you would typically forget about from earlier in the game have the potential to become build enabling hyper-competitive weapons again upon unlocking a new ability. Most notably, you can hotswap your builds at any time so when you get stonewalled by something you experiment to get past it.- Charming world.This is one of those games where I found myself trying to find *all* dialogue I could, simply because it was enjoyable.- Rough early game.The first chapter has very little audio, and less polished fights then the rest of the game. The first two hours give a highly negative impression compared to the rest of the game.- Rough audio balancing.Sometimes enemy audio can be too quiet or too loud by impressive amounts, key story moments do have decent audio usually though. There may be some bugs here, since some weapons I used in the beta had sounds but were silent in my current playthrough.- Interesting boss mechanics.Bosses have spell cards where for a time they do dramatically more interesting and character appropriate new attack patterns while upping their damage resistance, even if your build has massively overblown damage bosses can still take advantage of yourprobably lacking survivability to stay challenging. Sometimes you need to adapt your build to address the difficult of these.Mind you, they are never damage immune and hitting them still helps. Overall, it keeps the game fun when minmaxing is done, and is far better then any other implementation I have seen of this. No straight immunity phases that you have to fight through.- Solid story.Its a little rough, but this story actually has a point, is well connected/planned, has good velocity, and keeps total control over its tone at all times even if the developers regularly shock you with how rapidly the tone shifts._______________________To the developers.If you ever plan on patching this game more, I highly recommend polishing the first two bossfights to be closer to the standards of the later bosses. This isn't that I want them to be more intense, but rather I would like it if their animations and sounds actually matched what they were doing better since the lack of audio for these fights is borderline jarring compared to later. One common bug with the first one is that they face the wrong way when doing attacks directed at you.Something similar could be said to all the audio-less act one weapons and enemies. The later parts of the game are impressive, but the beginning being this raw compared to the rest is likely going to result in a lot of new people being confused as to why anyone likes this game.

_childDocuments_.review: After having finished the final chapter just now I can definitively say that this was a great experience all the way through.The characters are cute, unique and interesting.The story is interesting all throughout an develops nicely with multiple twists and turns and no matter how serious it gets the devs always found a way to throw in a pun or two.The visuals are stunning, one of the best pixel art I've seen in a long time, the backgrounds are the icing on the cake. The characters are well drawn and designed with fitting and funny expressions.The combat can feel a bit whacky at times but overall fits the feel of the game nicely and doesn't get in the way of trying to beat anything. Plus with the update that introduces the final chapter, they have improved the way the character moves and feels which helps greatly when exploring and fighting enemies.The difficulty feels nicely balanced, based on which overall level you decide to play, nothing seems too far out of reach at any given point. The boss fights are well designed, very unique from one another and offer enough of a challenge not to be overly aggrovating or acting as a complete hard-lock nor are they too easy to just steam-roll through (mainly due to their timed-sections).The grinding for materials to craft and cook each individual weapon and recipe feels just enough to be neither annoying nor tedious, yet still satisfactory.The level designs are interesting and bring several new mechanics, enemies and secrets to the table with each new area. It makes for a damn good feel when trying to find every recipe and resource there is.The soundtrack adds a nice touch to each area and boss fight, it's an amalgamation of several different music genres that combine into one... "experience" let's call it.All-in-all Dungeons Munchies is money well spent in my opinion.It is a rather short game, even when farming for every unlockable but offers enough content to not feel like a rip-off. Plus, if anything, the experience is what counts and I personally enjoyed my time with the game.I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, even to people who may not be a fan of manga or anime as, aside from the character designs, it has little to do with anything "anime-y".

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a very entertaining game. The first and second chapter are very well written and executed. The third and final chapter is a little unsatisfying in comparison. Overall a very good game. The Lickspittle theme was my favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid game, well worth the price tag, especially on sale. This game will probably take between 5-7 hours to complete. Maybe like 8-10 hours if you wanna collect all the secrets and make all the foods and weapons. (there are currently 2 chapters, at the time of this review)tldr: would recommend 8/10. Has great potential.story:The lore is suprisingly deep and the story is actually quite good. I went in expecting a cutetsy anime girl cooking game, but its much more of a hack and slash platformer with an actually fairly dark story. The games writing is also very good, its entertaining and I read every line, didnt skip a single one. This game actually made me do some deep thinking, which is not what I expected going in.Art:the hand drawn art is definitely much better than the pixel art. the pixel art isnt bad but it isnt like exceptional either. The animations are kinda strange and once you start having many foods equipped at once, you start looking like an absolute abomination, kinda like the binding of isaac. I wish the background characters had some sort of idle animation or something, they just stand absolutely still and its not very immersive.Gameplay:Its basically like a hack and slash platformer where you equip different weapons and foods with different effects. I found making synergies between different foods and weapons very fun.Difficulty:The games not that hard if you spec out a build with good synergies its relatively easy, you can kinda faceroll most of the enemies if you build for it. there were a couple hard bosses that took me a few tries but thats it. I died like 20 times throughout the course of both chapters. The combat in this game isnt very hard. It is pretty satisfying though.Music:The music in chapter 1 isnt that great, I barely noticed it, but the music in chapter 2 slaps, I liked it.Bugs.Due to this being an early access game and a game translated to english from chinese, theres some strange working and translation errors it seems. The translation in the story seems professionally done and is overall very good, but the item and food effect description translations seem a bit weird. I couldnt really tell what they exactly did by reading them and had to go test them out. Also there are some bugs, like theres this item that says you take 10% increased damage but you actually take 100% increased damage. pretty big difference. Just from the description the item is op, but in reality its really bad. So theres just a few small things like this, I didnt encounter anything game breaking though.The only thing I really wish they did differently was explain who tf the character you played was. Throughout the whole game I had no idea who the character I played was, I was mainly just watched the other characters develop and killing ♥♥♥♥ for them. You play a zombie so you have no personality, you also have no idea who you are except for like one 5 line flashback.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little gem! This game is surprisingly good quality in every area. The graphics are adorable and fun! Its story is charming and shifts between being lighthearted and tragic. The gameplay involves killing enemies for ingredients and inspiration which you use to cook buffs that fill slots and craft primary and secondary weapons. There are several synergies and they all have cosmetic effects which make your character look like they're a crazy cosplayer. While the soundtrack is not near the calibre of Christopher Larkin or Jeremy Soule, it has some fairly catchy jingles that are consistent with the tone of the story.My singular critique is that many of the weapons and food buffs are poorly balanced. There are too few defensive buffs (inc regen) and some weapons (swords) get much more love than others (hooks, spears and magic); the former enjoying MANY more buffing foods and interesting combos than the latter.

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses are difficult but they're not too difficult, you can usually find a pattern or a blind spot pretty easily. Now I'm saying that it's hard because I went through the 2nd chapter only using the foods from the first chapter so I don't know if it should be easier than it already is. Explosion staff + Chili gun = big dpsGameplay-wise, it's fun, me being the casual player with next to no iq points to put in the complicated combos. I got carried thorugh the game with a shield-spear combo. After that, I used the rgp+chili gun combo. They send you the new enemies by themselves most of the time and they're tanky enough for them to exhibit all their attacks, if there's a large quantity of one enemy you've never seen before, then you can expect them to be the cannon fodder of the bunch. There may be major jumps in difficulty in certain areas though. Art is also a major highlight.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. At the current price it's a bit steep given the relatively short length. You can blaze through what I guess counts as the first chapter in 3 hours. I like the combat though it feels like it could be... snappier somehow. Localisation is solid with a high quality translation which I was a bit worried about initially, unjustly as it turns out. I spotted maybe three typos in the script throughout but the language and humour are excellent. Makes me wonder if the original script is in English even, so no worries there. And the art, it almost goes without saying, is amazing.Devs appear to be a three man team who are providing reasonable updates and while there have been some delays it seems a big update is coming soon. So happy to have purchased this and recommend others do as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a fun little platformer with a lot of customization for weapons and skills, despite being a shorter game.
