Using these recipes, you can gain stat boosts, buffs, weapon abilities, and the beloved double jump. As of now, the game doesn't really have a set ending but the "Final Boss" fight was really impressive and the overall story followed through really strongly.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing title, had me hooked right off the bat.  The characters are lovable and funny, the story is compelling while still providing good laughs, and the ending cliffhanger will have you begging for more (as of 5/2020).The combat is comparable to a more developed version of Starbound, including dodges and high customizability.  I found that for a majority of the game damage over time was the best build for me.  You gain new abilities and increase stats with each meal you eat, but you're limited to how much you can fit in your stomach, so if you wanna trade, you need to cough something back up.  (You can regain the previous dish's effects without reconsuming the ingredients).  Mobility is satisfying, and it never got to a frustrating point thanks to the ease of control.  This game has been an absolute blast and I look forward to seeing more from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start. hmmm, how about the hour per dollar principle. Generally speaking, I don't play video games unless they offer at least an hour's worth of playtime per dollar spent. This game I only played for about 3.5 hours, yet I'm reccommending it for full price. Why?It's good. Real good.Not that kind of good that you play through without getting engaged. It's the kind of game with virtually zero flaws. The game isn't punishing, yet it could offer so much challenge with how smooth the combat system is. It's very solid, as it avoids putting barriers between the player and the actual combat. Normally games like this game playing very difficult by injecting combos and complex inputs. This game defies that convention, making complex movements easy and simple. It also adds several playstyles that are all viable and engaging. Surprisingly enough, the combat isn't the best part.It's the writing.The game does an excellent job of slowly building up the characters over time. I felt genuine emotion several times, and I also sympathized with the characters. When something awful happened, This surprised me as the story starts off as very goofy. At the same time, it isn't lacking in depth. They explore an utterly abusrd premise, and the developer does so with an unflinching resolve. This creates an execution that's elevating; it makes the story shine brighter than it should.So despite only getting 3.5 hours out of the game, I still would reccomend it as it was a breath of fresh air. These are the kinds of games I remember, and I cannot wait to see how the developer decides to finish the story. Excellent work on your parts. Really well done.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in early access. This game is a rollercoaster of emotion, and overall an interesting take on cooking! I love the art, the character, and combat. The game goes into three basic categories, all of which have their ups and downs; Movement, Combat, CookingMovement: Throughout the game, your ability to move will become faster, and versatile. Sometimes it's a little sensitive, but most of the time it's fair to the player. Combat: Combat is a little iffy with what enemies do more/less damage, while also being odd in what weapons do more/less for the player. Some weapons are direct upgrades, other weapons have niche's that the devs probably wanted to try out. If you've played bullet-hell type games, you should have an easier time avoiding numerous enemies. Otherwise, be prepared to dodge and attack frequently.Cooking: Cooking is a mechanic shown in the first video for this game and it shows off what cooking does only a little. By killing monsters you get resources, and with those resources, you can cook various dishes with them. Each dish grants you some kind of ability or buff. These dishes are vital to not only overall movement but combat as well. Conclusion: This game is still in early access, so treat it like such a thing. Games in early access are still in development, so supporting them by buying the game is always appreciated, for ANY game. The game might have a small amount of playtime or replay value right now, but as the game finishes development, that should increase. Optimization will also increase. I don't know if anyone else has noticed, but these are clearly foreign developers that not only have to help code the game but translate it and put the updates out for us, the players. This game has already met my expectations as being a funny take on cooking, involving necromancy and fighting. The emotion from characters chat is in most cases hilarious, while at other times being dead serious. Be prepared for a lot of emotions, and hopefully a joyful necromantic experience. P.S. Simmer Best Girl

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off by saying this is an unfinished game, and this is an unfinished review. When the game is finished, I will give my full review. This review is subject to change.Now, with that out of the way, I think it's best to begin at, well, the beginning of the game. When you first load up the game, you are presented with the menu. It's a pretty bare bones minimum menu, but it gets the job done while looking nice. Go ahead and jump right into the game. First things first~The movement:There is nothing special about the movement. I think the movement system can definitely be improved upon. It is as generic as jump, walk left, walk right, along with a roll to dodge. That’s it. There is absolutely no momentum to be found. The second you stop pressing any buttons, you are stopped dead in your tracks. It feels very lacking and just all around isn't fun. This is a hack and slash platformer, it needs good movement, but it just doesn't have that.The combat:The combat really isn't bad at all, aside from the movement aspect, the weapons you get throughout the game feel rewarding. One of the only problems I have with the combat, is that it gets way too easy late game, specifically during and after  This game is based around synergies. Basically you have weapons and you have upgrades that work together to from a great combo. Upgrades in this game are very interesting, and it is a take on upgrades I have never seen before. They aren't even really upgrades, in the sense that you can pick and choose exactly what upgrades you want when and where. You aren't locked into your choice the second you make the decision to go with say, a health upgrade. You can always swap out for a damage upgrade later on if you want. Which brings me into~The crafting:This really is an interesting category, because usually when you think crafting, you think “ugh grind for materials.” But there is little to no grind in this game at all. Most of the crafting recipes (and yes, I really mean actual recipes) only require the materials you would get going through one specified area one time, to craft either one weapon, or cook one dish. If you make something, and decide you don't like it and want to try something else, then is when you would need to go back to the area again. This means, the only real grinding you would do in this game would be for the achievement for crafting and cooking everything.The upgrade mechanic:One of the main selling points of this game is being able to unlock new upgrades by eating food that you have cooked from materials gathered through killing unsuspecting plant (monsters?) and sometimes bugs and fish. The catch here is that you only have 7 slots available in your zombie stomach. With there being 49 foods, it starts to become more interesting the more you play. You are presented with pretty early on in the game, the dilemma of being able to change what upgrades you have at any point. Something interesting here is that there are mobility upgrades, such as faster speed, or double jumping. In any other normal platformer these would be with you throughout the entire game. However, in Dungeon Munchies, you have to option of say, replacing your double jump with a damage, or defense upgrade. One problem I have with this system, isn't necessarily with the system itself, but a side mechanic called “surgeries” which  This mechanic is fine, but personally I don't like the specific surgery  It would have made the game more enjoyable to me personally if that surgery never existed, because I would actually have to think about my next move and what upgrades to tack on along with it to be efficient enough. Which leads me into the difficulty~The difficulty:This category I find the most disappointing. The game feels way too easy. What is the target audience of this game? Obviously it is meant for more mature audiences, what with the  But I think, for the target audience, the difficulty is very lacking. It is a very easy game to blast through, but it presents itself as something that should be tough, and have you dying at LEAST 100 times throughout your journey through the dungeon, however, in my playthrough, I only died 10 times The sound design:This isn't anything special, the music generally matches the mood of the locations you are in, but during the boss fights, all the momentum of the situation quickly fades away. Personally I feel there needs to be more action in the music when there is something intense going on. None of the music is very memorable, but it adds flavor.The story:The story is very interesting. I won't add any spoiler tags here because I am not going to talk much about it, and if you already played the game, then there is no real need to see a recap of what you just played. If you want to go in totally blind, I recommend skipping this part, but nothing major will be mentioned in this part. The story focuses around two old friends turned nemesis who have different viewpoints about the situation happening in the dungeon. Both sides have their own fair arguments, which is what makes the story so compelling to me. There is a dispute going on, and neither side is right or wrong, just different. I won't get too much into this, but if you are looking for an interesting story, and don't care too much about the (negligibly) bad movement, this is probably a good investment.There you have it. This is my review for what is out of the game at the moment, and I will be changing it based on future updates. For what is given in this early access game, the game is actually pretty polished, it is just missing a few key details.TL;DR: The movement and the sound design needs to be worked on, along with the surgery mechanic needing to be tweaked.

_childDocuments_.review: In the 4 hour time span that it took for me to beat this game, I ended up being emotionally attached to all the characters. I enjoyed this game a lot, searching every nook and cranny for those last few secrets, even though I'm still missing a few. I could have rushed through the game, but it never felt like a chore. The combat always changes depending on what food you have and what your weapons are. It caters to different playing styles, from the traditional sword and shield, to the hit and run tactics of using dagger and poison. It never feels unfair and when you do die, your first thoughts are somewhere along the liens of "I could have played that better". It doesn't use any cheap tricks, and all the attacks have some build up so even if you don't know exactly what's coming, you know that you're going to have to dodge soon. It's amazing, and I really love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to just state, that I clearly havent put a lot of time into this at all. Because i literally got as far as picking up your bag in the tutorial area and from what I see, the PS4 touch pad does NOT work to bring up the bag. A Small complaint really since you dont really ever use your bag per say. And id also like to point out that aiming and moving, is tied to your left analog stick. Basically like the old school metroid prime on GC as an example. It basically makes it impossible to use any aimed range attacks like the seeds you pick up cause you have to aim and move at the same time. The aiming itself is kind of wonky as well. Not very fluid.  If i remember right the keyboard doesnt have these issues. But Either way, these are just a few things ive noticed so far and not even 10 mins into the game. That said, I know this is Early access so im not trying to bash the game. Just giving feedback as far as the ps4 controls go. maybe look into it when you got some time and come up with a better controller layout. Or at least allow button mapping in the future.Now on to my review. I played this straight for roughly 5 hours and got to the end. I will say I really enjoyed the humor and artwork in this game. I feel like 13$ was a pretty good price for the amount of content. The game plays really well for keyboard and mouse, compared to ps4 controller at least (Idk about xbox controller). Its an Early access title but truthfully it played really well overall. I didnt have any kind of game breaking bugs, or glitches to speak of. I really just played through it all in one sitting and i thoroughly enjoyed it. I would recommend this game if youre looking for a breathe of fresh air as far as an rpg goes(along with the unique humor and setting). I dont know if this would be classified as a rouge like, as it seems to have its own qwerky dark story. But theres really no penalty for dying, its like the devs took what makes a rouge like/lite good, the abilities, the gameplay, variety,  and blended it with a unique story and artwork.. Its a very dark kind of humor overall as well, but i enjoyed it. I say this is worth 13$, but i do hope to see more content coming out in the future. Lastly, i will mention i actually liked the soundtrack in the game. I felt like it really set the tone for the areas you were in. Especially when the game got a little bit more serious. Overall, as i said earlier, i think this is worth 13$. Its a fairly short game though, so if youre expecting a long game, as of now, or a truly challenging one (im not the greatest gamer and i managed to beat it in 5 hours so...), this probably isnt for you. Just yet at least. cause who knows where the devs will take it in the future. I do see promise in this game and Ill be following this to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: for early access game  id say it is amazing i have beat the game to what is currently the end at points it is relentlessly difficult i think it would be amazing to get some voice actors for the characters as for game play as a word of warning the game starts out very easy then as soon as you get to the first boss the difficulty ramps up sharply it took me 3 hours to beat the current build 23 deaths i cant wait till further updates come out the game is fairly priced as well worth the current price its easy to pick up adorable art style i now await further content

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW WARNINGI don't normally recommend games. But good golly gosh where to begin. I won't give any spoilers as the charm of the game is just going though all of it yourself.GOOD THINGS:-characters are simple, yet likeable even if you don't really interact with them-game play in my opinion is fairly solid, just maybe needs more refinement here and there-there is some weapon/fighting style customization (build wise) which is niceBAD THINGS:-hit boxes are a little unclear, especially on the player character-while I understand ingredients are important for crafting, it took a lot longer than it should have to earn certain items because of RNG I guess?-when you don't have the wall climbing item and need to double jump instead, a lot of walls are just a FEW pixels too high and you REALLY have to time jumps optimally just to get to the next platformtl;dr  - enjoyable game that's got a lot to offer, but needs some minor tweking in areas

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun side-scroller. I'm personally a huge fan of necromancy in games, so that's a big appeal for me. Character designs are great, especially the last(?) boss. _childDocuments_.review: Played through what was available in about 11 hours. Combat was fine. Some of the bosses had "bullet hell" mechanics, which threw me off from the almost hack-and-slash antics it took to get to them. I did a dagger/poison build and watched most enemies die a few moments later from one cut. I always looked forward to killing new monsters to see what new abilities/weapons I would unlock nice. _childDocuments_.review:
Hunt down monsters to cook and eat them!

You’ve been revived in a massive underground complex and you must leave this bizarre facility. Aided by the undead Necro-Chef Simmer, you must stay safe, get fed, find a way to get out.

Dungeon Munchies is a side-scrolling action RPG with a focus on hunting down creatures, cooking them, and eating dishes to gain certain abilities. The combination of dishes you choose to eat will impact your entire play style.

Big Menu for a Big Stomach
With a stomach that can only take seven dishes, you must put together a meal that maximises your abilities. Guava juice, grilled shrimp, or crab stirfry may mean the difference between health recovery, damage output or a watery shield.

Tools of the Trade
Craft all kinds of deadly weapons out of the animal and plant parts you can't eat. Pair them with your favorite dishes to create the most overpowered combat combo.

Farm-fresh & Locally-sourced
In this day and age, ingredients are hard to come by. You should be prepared to face off electrical snails, razor-sharp shrimp claws, and laser wasps to get the delicious parts you need.

Something Doesn’t Feel Right...
From the self-professed-AAA-license-holding necro-chef, to the diabolical voodoo “Lord of the Forest”, to the radical revolutionaries of the fruit revolution, everyone wants you to do their thing, but no one's really right in the head. What’s really happening down in this dungeon?

name: Per Aspera
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game The surface of Mars is littered with Humanity’s failed attempts to colonize its surface. This time will be different - this time there is no room for human error. Per Aspera is a planetary simulation game that combines hard science fiction and base building and takes the experience planet-wide. Step into the role of AMI, an Artificial Consciousness with the prime directive of terraforming Mars for human colonization. FEATURES: Balance a complex well of resources to build interconnected structures that span the entire planet. Customize your planet with branching research trees that allow players to tailor their terraforming plan — Develop new technologies, steeped in real-world science, to create a thriving interplanetary civilization. Uncover the mystery of a threatening presence on Mars and defend your colonies from unknown and combative forces. Immerse yourself in a rich, compelling narrative or take your time and craft the perfect Martian landscape with Sandbox Mode. Includes the immersive voice acting talents of Troy Baker, Phil LaMarr, Laila Berzins, Yong Yea, Lynsey Murrell, and Nneka Okoye. Terraform Together with Friends (up to 4 players). Sandbox Mode Only. Using scientific theories proposed by real space agencies and geographical data directly from NASA, Per Aspera presents life-like conditions and challenges steeped in theoretical science. Per Aspera contains a rich narrative that presents players with difficult decisions with planet-wide consequences. See the world through the eyes of an infant AI as it traverses a complicated ocean of self-discovery and shapes the fate of the human race. Navigate your ever-evolving programming to adapt to morally challenging concepts and forge relationships with the human colonists that look to you for their continued survival. The choices you make will impact how your mission ultimately concludes. Keep your wits about you as this is not the first time humans have tried to tame the Red Planet. Expose long-forgotten relics of Humanity’s failed attempts, learn from their past mistakes, and uncover a looming menace that threatens to see you fail at any cost.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played through this game, and it is quite fun for a casual mars "colony" builder. There are some improvements that could be made. I haven't played through with Blue Mars yet, but my impression is that the DLC adds to the main game, but it really feels as if it should have been included in the main game to start with, so consider picking the DLC and the base game up together, especially if you want to support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Summary - While I understand the mixed reviews - and I read most of them, I find this game solid.   Many reviews talk about the UI being clunky - yes, and I would add lacking in some areas but its still quite polished.  The "value" is arguable at its current price and "development," but also consider I have played 50+ hrs in less than a week - this is MY kind of game.  So over all - THUMBS UP!   I do not regret the purchase of Per Aspera.Detail - there are some very unique aspects in this game.   In over 200 games in my library, this one is completely unique in so many ways - and most of my titles come back to this general genre. There is a story line and plot that allows choices instead of strictly linear, so its not a 1 play.  And its not predictable.   The full game design is intriguing.This is a very grindy game.  If you don't like grind, then probably not your game.  This is not a game to sit down and finish in one day.  Also, not a game that you can walk away from: stuff happens, key choices that can affect the game later.I don't show this game is still in development some but some key pieces are missing - like a basic tutorial. The plot provides a bit of a walk through, but there are key points in the game that you are left to just figure it out.  An additional challenge by design?  Possibly.  The in-game knowledge base is somewhat helpful, but I found it lacking.  Mouse over labels would be helpful since the UI is very full.  If you prefer detailed instructions, then this also may not be something you will enjoy.  After the time invested, I am still figuring out the UI.Make no mistake - the game IS completely playable.  If you do any kind of simulation/base building/colony sci fi sim, then you won't be disappointed in this title.  The graphics are eye catching - the developers spent time on detail. The game presents layers and while you could argue some things were missed or could use improvement, there is a lot of complexity to mechanics and game play.I see there is much room for future development, which is definitely a positive.  Arguably, I could see an ongoing series that takes players through the solar system and beyond, tracking future space exploration.  There is a lot of unused material here and hopefully they will run with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Find a different terraforming game. Early game is interesting but is lacking. Mid game makes you want to restart because you didn't build everything 100% correctly and removing buildings is the most annoying thing in the game. Late game is just watching your screen for 5 hours as the nitrogen pressure goes up. Dont build near the south pole as it will blind you whenever its winter, and dont use 50% of the planet without paying them 6$. Dont upgrade roads in mass as you cant cancel road upgrades. Dont land a new lander in an area you already scanned. Yeah this game has some bad mechanics that make you feel like you can do whatever you want but you cant. Also the story-lines dialog gets extremely political and boring as all get out.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Free weekend:At its core, the game is a visual novel, and idle sim. Its really boring. Any game that has a 16x sim speed option you know is going to drag, and this one drags.You just plop building down and wait for meters/bars to fill up, then repeat. At set points, the story will continue. The story is the only redeeming quality, but its not worth it, the gameplay is not engaging enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with this one. I especially enjoyed the story in the campaign mode. As a colony builder, Per Aspera is fun albeit a bit on the simple side. The only complaint I had was with the automated worker drones. The priority system doesn't work that well so it can be hard to get them to focus on what you deem important. Overall though I'd say this is a solid entry in the Colonise / Terraform Mars genre of games. Hope to see some DLC or expansion in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little resource management game, with a good campaign. Excellent story, if you like to play like an AI that is trying to figure out its own morality, and place in the universe while terraforming Mars. Some light combat mechanics, and 3 interesting endings based on your choices and who you trust, and all of them were satisfying to me in how they concluded, and how the game responds to your pick.The worker management takes some getting used to.. While in general, more worker, means more better, you can save resources, by upgrading your energy grid, keeping an eye on not producing too much of something, and optimising routes and priorities, and cleaning up obsolete buildings. "Blue Mars" is a lot of fun, but does make it harder to be "sustainable".  The game does offer controls of how resources are allocated, but these are more global. People who are looking for really in-depth resource management may be disappointed, but for me it's the perfect balance of story, exploration, and management. The game has matured a lot over the years, and has become more polished as a result. It now offers some nice additional goals and little story bits, to do after the credits have rolled, and you can continue to build and explore artifacts as much as you want. I did reach 1M colonists, and I did like these type of challenges. I do wish the game would have more "sustainable" options. Food, and population is not an issue, but it would be nice if metals & plastics could be recycled for instance, reducing the need to ever expand. (keeping workers alive, and repairing buildings is what keeps draining resources)All and all I really enjoyed these 58 hours, and it's a little gem in my book. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoy this game. Some of the other reviewers point out the difficulty in this game, but be aware that mostly means the game is willing to allow your economy to crash out to zero if you try to overbuild in one direction without securing your basic resource nodes. Also keep an eye out when building in areas that will eventually flood with water.If you pay attention to those points, and otherwise give respect to things able to actually harm you, there's a cool story and decent enough terraforming game past those skill moats. There can be times where the nature of the game involves long stretches of gap time waiting for things to finish working, but with time acceleration of x16 availible, it's pretty clean to mitigate the wait times if you're ready to be keeping an eye out for resource shortages while zooming at max speed.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat it's an obvious choice for anyone that enjoyed Surviving Mars. It's perhaps not as far reaching or involved, but seems to have enough challenge as it starts. Also has an interesting plot with good voice acting and some intriguing choices, since you play from a refreshing angle - sort of. Overall looks worthy of a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's a charming blend of story and resource management that takes the tedium out of the supply-chain genre.  Engaging for one playthrough (~20h), though the Green Mars and Blue Mars DLCs are required to enjoy the game.It's worth it for the strategy fans who need a more relaxed experience without it being dumbed down.  The only way to lose is if you stop expanding, run your mines dry, and start to doom spiral.  I didn't find the gameplay to be repetitive, as I was discovering better strategies throughout my playthrough
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A management with a good story Per Aspera will keep you engrossed for a very long time.  There is some replayability but it is limited to maybe two or three games.  Furthermore the game is a fair bit longer than its tech tree so expect to be max tech long before you complete the game.  I hope the devs add more content in the future but we'll have to wait and see!  At the time of writing on DLC (Green Mars) has been released and was a welcome addition to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The core concept here is really appealing. The high level concepts are good - terraforming, logistics, managing projects. But the execution results in a fiddly and boring gameplay loop. The story seems interesting, but not compelling enough to deal with the fiddly resource management (which isn't well explained and online guides suggest has some bugs still as well). It isn't bad, it just isn't good. In a word, I'd say bland.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The current steam rating for this game is 6/10 and I think it is accurate. So why I can't recommend it ?- The fleet management lacks basic QoL like rally points or targeting enemy units. AFAIK you can't even disband units.- sooner or later the logistic system simply implodes - there has to be a way to assign more workers to hub or upgrade amount of carried items - just faster roads/ways are not enough- game includes 16x speed option in game and you will use it for 95% of game time - and it still is waiting game- game story isn't flexible enough - AI was talking about nukes when polar caps where already gone. And people guessed what can be the nature of threat, after it was already defeatedI can't believe I write this: if you want to face any challenge try Surviving Mars instead. -Even if it is reskinned Tropico and requires huge amount of micromanagement in difficult scenarios/achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Per Aspera is a great game. There's no better game about colonizing Mars yet and this game isn't just better it's really good. Graphics are candy for the eye, there's story which I enjoy, mechanics are very easy to learn, but it doesn't becomes overly easy or hard. It's difficult to fail, but it's easy to mismanage resources especially if they start to run out, so the balance is there.I think it's worth your time if game picked your intrest in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The player interface needs a bit of further refinement and mars built workers need to be more resilient in addition the worker factory shouldn't just keep pumping out workers when there's no hub to support them.  The generation of resources nodes need refinement in amount and placement.  Road placement mechanic needs to avoid craters at all cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game but could do with alot more work to make it more replayable for a simulation game. I have done about two games and gained 48 achievements out of 51 and i feel it could have some more special projects or other planets, (Pluto is a planet btw, so suck it) and terraform those planets not just into green but lava worlds, methane worlds, or any other. I think if you made the planets a bit bigger too it wouldn't hurt and allow to turn the entire planet into an ocean and build underwater cities it would go along way from making people play 30 hours into people who play 50 hours. Nevertheless really fun game and i got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: After I have played a few hours, I gotta admit that this game is such a nice experience. Here is a breakdown:PROS:- Nice graphics and sound- Well optimized, would probably run well on older systems - Very relaxing base-building experience- Clean and pretty to look at UI- Very pleasant voiceover - Topographic map of Mars is very beautiful- Camera movement is very smooth and zooming out to orbit and back is an eye candy- Not much micromanaging (could be a bad thing if this is what you after)- Has nice story- Simplified yet scientific tech and data (temperature, pressure, CO2 levels etc)CONS:- Music is mostly ok but some tracks are below average, which is a shame- Lack of micromanaging makes gameplay feel a bit two dimensional- Difficult to find things once your base is built up. Upgrading factories and mines is annoying, since I could not find a list and had to look for every one of them on the mapOverall I it is a very pleasant experience, a chill, pretty base building game with a bit of exploration and story 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game on and off for a while, and I kept coming back to it now and again because there is some stuff to really like about it. When I saw the latest news about more content coming I gave it another go and rediscovered why I'd never been able to stick with it for all that long.I love Mars and the premise of (somewhat) realistically terraforming the Red Planet is a dream. Combined with a thoughtful story of an AI, what it means to be conscious and responsible for others and actually being able to shape to some extent the personality of that AI and its relationship with the human colonists is amazing. The graphics are not anything special but they are quite pretty. The music is good and all the dialogue is credibly voice acted. Everything about it seems good, or even great.But then you start playing it. After a couple of hours you find that at its core, under all the beautiful dressing, the gameplay is just a basic economic management/tycoon game that has half a handful of simple production chains and it never really expands any further from there. That alone wouldn't be too bad but what really kills any sense of joy or pleasure from playing is the game's handling of the logistics. Its total garbage.It really cannot be understated how awful the system is. You have almost no control at all over how resources and products move around, from the start until the end of the game its handled by automated little rover cars  in a way designed to be as inefficient and obtuse as possible. You can't decide where the roads go, every building paves a spiderweb of roads to make individual connections with every other building nearby. As you build more rovers your base is chopped up into little districts automatically, as there can only ever be one rover operating in an area. You cannot chose the size of that area or which buildings go into it, the game just decides (poorly) for you. Your rovers never really get better either, they only ever can carry one unit of resources at a time. Research lets you improve the roads so they can go faster but their prioritisation and pathfinding remains brain-dead throughout. And speaking of research, to illustrate how badly the game represents this area; the peak, the pinnacle, the very highest advance in the logistics chain of the tech tree is Elon Musk's bloody Hyperloop. The single worst and most inefficient mass transit design ever!The transport and logistics completely kills this game. As much as the other aspects range from good to great it just turns Per Aspera from a potentially great experience to one of alternating frustration and boredom. It needs a complete overhaul and after two years and major expansions none has come. Don't bother.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The more I played this game, the less fun it became.Per Aspera has a really cool foundation and pulled me in quickly. Unfortunately, all of its problems build up and up the longer you play and don't really become problematic until you're outside the refund window...I struggled with the user interface and it battled me more and more as my base grew. The number of menial and repetitive tasks you need to complete only grows as you play - there is no automation, no copy/paste, no building templates, no delegation of tasks to AI, no technology to research that lessens your cognitive burden. You're supposed to colonize an entire planet here, but none of the game mechanics work  you on this. There are no signs or labels or user-created districts to help organize your base or offer any aid in visual recognition. There are no hotkeys for building, and every single building you place needs to be situated within numerous zones of influence - you will have to toggle these, one-by-one (where's my filter?), and pre-position your cursor because some of the overlays don't even allow you to place buildings at all!I struggle to see which buildings or swarms I've selected. I struggle to respond to in-game alerts and notifications and locate their sources. When your buildings break down, you have to zoom in to see either the damage or the icon to spot it - and when your base is half a planet wide, you zoom in and out and in and out and in and out. When important events happen, the game fades to black, and then fades back in, with no prompt or notifications or voice effects or  to indicate what has just taken place. Voiced lines play out-of-order with regards to story revelations from minutes ago. To top things off, I had four crashes to the desktop, and one PC hard-lock in the ~8 hours I've played.It's a mess. This game doesn't feel playtested  What it feels like is a trap, and even having purchased this on sale I don't feel it was worth it, and I'd refund if I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRIf you wanna zone out and play a building/terraforming game, this is for you.  It's relaxing, but can get monotonous.I played 3 runs.  1. I played the campaign for a bit.  Story is interesting.  AMI keeps talking so as keep you 'engaged' or 'immersed', but felt a little much after a while. The tutorial is good.  AI is fine and getting a decent set-up isn't too bad.  2, Reload and try again, campaign from scratch.  Blow throw all the stuff and get my colony to explore another part of the planet and think 'oh boy!', but am a bit disappointed because it's almost just like repeating the very beginning tutorial again.  3. I try one more time, this time in sandbox. The beginning is fun and getting everything set up, but each time there gets to this very critical point once all the set-up in the beginning is mostly 'running smoothly' that is just becomes boring.  I never even made it to flooding the planet just because waiting forever for the research was so tedious. There was hardly anything 'urgent' or even 'necessary to do.  It does run smoothly, just wish the gameplay loops had a bit more variety/tension to it.  Just feels like 'build a million mines and factories and oh some people are here now.'

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was neutral review. I like this game concept but i dont like execution. I played it to the end because im sick and i like games like this. Im kinda addicted to them. But this game is exhausting even if almost nothing happen. I mean on one hand everything works on its own so not much need to be done, but on other hand it dont work very efficiently and its hard to make it work better. Progress is really slow (even on x16 speed) and campaign randomly attack you with some conversations with timers so you cannot leave game alone and clean house for example. Also i felt punnished for terraforming in game about terraforming. I mean there are research stations all over the globe to research. But once temperature raise some of them are underwater and are not reachable anymore. At first i thought there will be tech for this. Later i was not happy and wondered if i can reverse terraforming process. And later i found out that these research stations are practically meaningless which is not good either. Also a lot of resources are lost in the water. This game needs on-water-buildings or something like that.I finished the game and i feel tired. It was like pushing heavy stone uphill for long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Don't get drawn in to a few pit falls:O2 - This made me restart, I was too eager, slow down, too much O2 and it just runs away. with fires and trying to balance it was a PITA.Attempting to load up on Nitrogen, to give the 70/30 spilt that earth has (give or take).The game tries to move you on, but don't be rushed too much - unless your speed running - if you are fair play, I'd love to see a speed run of this game..Balance RP so you have enough colonist to research mil tech when it comes alongDrown the world too fast and you lose out on a tonne of resources.My second play through I slowed it right down, looked at floodable areas and didn't have stores etc there. _childDocuments_.review: This is the planetary terraforming game I've been waiting for. You play as a physical AI running the terraforming mission in the narrative, instead of just as an omniscient amoral god that you are implied to be for most resource management strategy games. That extra layer creates a ton of narrative depth, making this the first construction-centric strategy game in a long time I've actually wanted to start again from the very beginning (rather than just continuing to expand the colossus I had spent so much time building).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: There's some problems with the design of the game.Firstly, you basically just build things on resource nodes and then as long as everything's connected up stuff will kinda just work. There's no interesting logistical problems to solve, every problem you come across can basically just be solved by building more of the same thing. The only real upgrades to these factories/mines you can get are for more production and by a few hours in you've got enough of everything so these upgrades feel useless, you're basically waiting around for the right asteroids to be detected or for some meters to go up.The story is kinda forced upon you and sometimes feels a bit overbearing, I don't think it was really a needed addition to this game as you just kinda sit there and listen to a bunch of different people be unreasonable and deceitful to you. like I can see what they were going for because it's an interesting premise but by halfway through my play-through I was hoping to just terraform this planet in peacesome progression is kinda weird, there's a limit on buildings you can have which you can only increase by doing more research - which if you've left it too late can require more buildings to speed up, so you just kinda sit there on 16x and wait. New portions of the map are locked behind story progression which is really annoying. I kinda wish this game just gave you the planet and told you what the levels were supposed to be and just let you figure it out with interesting planet wide factorio-like logistics, but instead it's kind of just a railroad of checkboxes with an annoying story bolted to the top of it, which is a shame because the game is great in a lot of other respects - it's competently made, runs well, is scientifically accurate where it needs to be and its graphically pretty enough, like the effort is top notch it's just not that fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game.Pros:* Nice story with a few interesting concepts and a few twists that feel okay* Lot of hard science in the terraforming process* Proper geography (aside from resources)* Multiple endings that make sense* Good voice-acting* The player is often given a choice between doing things the proper but slow way or taking a shortcut, often with strings attached; both will work and strings can hinder you laterCons:* Playing it properly needs a lot of micromanagent; while the pathfinding works (more or less, it's not perfect and sometimes the drones forget to deliver a few last resources necessary for a project), the supply logic does not: player must often enable/disable factories manually to ensure limited resources don't get wasted* You can't set any high-level limits on anything, like "produce only up to 100 Parts", it's all or nothing (so, if you want to have a specific amount in reserve, you need to micromanage again)* The game is still very buggy; aside from an occassional typo (where it's not expected - sometimes they're justified in-story via, for example, signal degradation) and sound-vs-subtitle mismatches (not very problematic), some are really annoying; I happened to have all vegetation suddenly stop growing without any reason, needing a few resets to fix* The game leaks memory like crazy and crashes once it has nothing left; save often and restart it once an hour if you don't want it to crash in the worst moment (and don't count on autosave, it can crash during autosave)* There are in-game problems with handling the moving shoreline (and it will move if you're doing the terraforming right) - your ports (in Blue Mars DLC) and water plants will turn to sunk rubble often and without warning, often destroying resources in ports or throwing your economy into chaos when the water stops flowing* It's very difficult to determine where particular resources are once you have many storages; the only valid way I found was simply to go manually through every buildingNeutral:* Sometimes, the game will simply interrupt you, pulling you to orbit or with a call without a chance to finish (which is annoying if you're aiming for a perfect placement of something); use pause to avoid thattl;dr: I had fun, and the game is pretty good in general, but it has a few rough edges that should definitely not be present in something old enough to have a paid DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and Musk references both put a damper on an otherwise really fun experience. I'll keep playing, but the whole battle UI is a real hassle to wrangle. *edit after more gameplay*The game is decent, but is missing to many ease of life features to be good. There is no way to cap manufactured resources which stops you from building any form of efficient system without running out of raw mats. The whole terraforming progression is also unsatisfying as there are no noticable consequences for any actions. Blowing up a bunch of nukes or crashing a moon into the planet should do more than just raise the temp a bit. The whole water system is also a bummer, there is no stats showing how much potential water there is on the planet. This means that you must either just wait with terraforming to build on flood areas or just ignore those places. The pathfinding of deconstructing buildings is really bad so building a base and then later deconstructing it to move away from water is tedious and frustrating. There are a bunch of things I could overlook if the core gameplay was more polished, but as of now the game has to many annoying moments to make me overlook that sort of stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool concept, terraforming Mars? Sick. The gameplay loop kinda... runs out, though. _childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh, a city builder focused around the terraforming of Mars, cool" I thought to myself.But honestly, the city-building is a bit so-so. The pacing is pretty bad. You can unlock most of the interesting buildings pretty early on, but they don't do anything until certain stage of the terraforming, which is usually much later. There's a lot of waiting.But the game's pace is quite contemplative, and the simulation forgiving (at least on easier difficulties). So you can listen to a podcast, or watch a movie, and wait for the worker drones to build the occasional building.I was not prepared for the narration that truly elevates the game. You are AMI, an artificial intelligence in charge of the terraforming project, and the safety of the colonists. You only have the information that others deemed relevant to the mission, either upon your creation or during the mission, but you find yourself asking questions like: "Who am I to myself? To my creator? In the scope of Earthside politics? Who am I?"The real goal is to learn how to answer these types of questions.EDIT: One thing's puzzling, though. I've terraformed the planet. I've completed the quests. I've done the things. I have no idea if I've finished the game, or whether there's still something to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the rather limited resources, and even less of a fan of the building limit. The story seems fun. But that's for a one off. So you'll be sitting waiting for aluminium for example.Not my cup of tea, but it's rather relaxing, so if it sounds good to you, don't mind my thumbs down too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very glad I was able to play this game as part of the free weekend. The game itself is decent as a base/city/planet builder. I played my first (and only game) in realistic mode, and I eventually quit out of sheer boredom.The game is simple. Natural disasters like asteroids impacting the planet are the only opponents I found in the game. There is a whole military branch, and one "opponent base" which was effortlessly destroyed soon after I found it, and learned how to move my drones.Any base you build is doomed to eventually die of mineral starvation. Drones (worker, maintenance, military) cost non-refundable resources, and can not be recycled. They all naturally wear out over time - workers are automatically destroyed after a set time, maintenance drones are destroyed after they've repaired a certain amount of repair points, and military drones are destroyed if they get shot by an enemy. These are permanent losses of resources, and there is no way to get more resources.The planet has a certain amount of resources, and that's it. You build drones - which require a lot of different resources, and those resources can never be returned, nor required. This means every base you build will eventually die of mineral starvation. Your goal is to beat the scenario before you run out of your resources.This is a very slow game. I was playing the last several hours on 16x speed as I simply waited for the terraforming to be completed (Since I didn't want to spend my limited resources to speed things up - things like aerobraking asteroids, or importing green house gasses are a permanent loss in resources).For people wanting a few hints:1) Assault drones can be moved by clicking on the triangle above then which displays the number of drones you have. This isn't something you're told, and only reading other people's comments can teach you.2) When you find something that must be researched, the way you do it is put enough food and ice into the research station, then find a colony and turn it off. This is the only way to populate research stations. Be sure to turn the colony back on once the colonists reach the research station.3) Water treatment facilities, water packing plants, crater farms, and biodomes are the only way to survive once you start running out of resources needed to make food. These facilities create food and ice all by themselves. This'll help slow the eventually mineral death of your colony, but due to building drones - which is required - your base is still doomed to a slow death. If only you could retrieve your drones and recycle them... but you can't.In short, on realistic mode, I had no difficulties. There is absolutely no challenge to the game... This is just a waiting game, and a minor story is mixed in... but hours upon hours of waiting. It might be interesting to people who like to build bases, but since every base is doomed to mineral starvation, even they may hesitate to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand all the negative reviews. I think a lot of players simply fail to understand what this game is.It's a solid colony builder with just the right amount of micromanagement. The tech-tree is not overly complicated but that's totally fine. The challenge is to maintain a steady flow of resources which forces constant expansion. So there is never a state of build-it-all or a perfect colony layout or something of that sort.The graphics and overall aesthetics are well made and suite the story quite well. It's an interesting combination of a lean, computerized, functional management interface with just a little bit cartoony flair when it comes to the humans. I think this suits the game and its mood very well and I kind of like it actually.But what makes this a true gem is the non-linear story mode. It's well paced and the story itself is actually quite intriguing. It gives you choices which actually matter and therefore this is one of the few games where I want to play the campaign multiple times just to see what happens if I had decided differently. That's rare and absolutely awesome in a colony builder.I guess the negative reviews are the result of the fact that this game diverts expectations of  many players as it is a unusual combination which gives it some depth but keeps game play very casual. I think that's quite rare and makes this game a true gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game shortly after it's release and it had a number of issues, the devs fixed most of them, and it's an entertaining game overall. The story is enjoyable overall, but a little ham fisted, but not bad. The biggest issue I have with the game is that as your colony grows, managing it becomes harder and harder, and figuring out what is where and what might be missing can be very difficult. But once you get later in the game and unlock the hyper tubes, things become much easier, to the point that there is no real difficulty, and you're just waiting the clock out, but it's still a fun way to pass a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gave me serious nostalgia vibes of when I used to play Sim Earth back in the day with friends. It's simple but addictive gameplay. My only real complaint is that is has a serious optimization issue that causes FPS to steadily drop as you progress and build up your colony. I started story mode with 60, and by the end had only 25. CPU and GPU never increased the entire time so it's not using system resources as it should.Would I recommend it for full price? Nah. But I got it in a Humble Bundle so I got my money's worth. It's also worth a try if you're a fan of the Red Mars book series.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Surviving Mars, even with Surviving Mars problems, but this is meant to be a different type of Mars game.  A very lot of game time is spent just watching resources being transferred among nodes.  The entire campaign might be a nice long story (I did not finish it), and the planet size to build on is very large size. Considering Surviving Mars base game was given away for free sometime past and considering its sales plus sale-bundles, this game seems worth no more than 75% off ($7.50 US including Green Mars), and I think Blue Mars seems to be needed (for maybe $1.50 US more) considering some Mars in-game flooding that is supposed to come later.  Even then, you must like this style of game compared to Surviving Mars, which is more fun, to even consider buying this.  Hope this game gets better later, but I am not sure if the developers want to later make big change improvements to the game's current style. I was unable to create a multi-player lobby for co-op, I did not debug that much, and I am not sure if no-multiplayer was planned or not for the Steam Free Weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I had a great time with this game when it first launched. The story was intriguing with an AI forced into deriving it's own moral code and decisions as the player which could alter the trajectory of that story. Not what I was expecting of a city builder/colony sim. The initial launch had a few rough edges, but it was not enough to keep me from playing avidly. And this studio did a great job of addressing issues in a timely manner. The organic growth that emerges as you aim your colony layout towards the resources that you seek is very compelling, and provided me personally with a continual "just 5 more minutes" mindset. The game also does a good job with events that force you to revise your strategies along the way and re-evaluate what you need to do next. The elements around enticing colonists to Mars and satisfying them well enough to stick around was straight forward enough, but needing them not for their labor but for their creativity was a great twist. A lot of the elements came together in a complementary way.I went back after a few updates and found additional enjoyment with the game and the latest updates are drawing me back in once again. The additional metrics and analytics that they added to the game really helped to clarify what was going on in your inevitable colony sprawl. I am looking forward to the ability to define districts and see how that "local" perspective helps you drive sustainable growth. A lot of good stuff in this game and it still has more room to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: So I've done two playthroughs--one in the story campaign and one in sandbox--and overall, it's a decent game.  I adore the visuals, and I literally got emotional at seeing clouds and running water and oceans and green fields on Mars.  So let me give the strengths and weaknesses here.Strengths: Once you get past early game, it's very zen at times.  The music is very enjoyable--I've been considering getting the soundtrack and adding it to my general playlists, especially for writing and the like--and there's a good emotional core with AMI and her voice acting that I very much enjoyed in the story campaign.  Also, I really like the exploration feel and watching things develop.  The new water system update added a great deal of late-game content that was sorely needed and it made it possible to sustainably develop Mars for settlement that wasn't available in the initial release and made deciding what to do with craters more interesting--I had a bunch of crater farms in central locations and then adapted less-useful sites into animal sanctuaries and composting sites, but it made it all interesting.Weaknesses: The core gameplay loop is too front-loaded on early game.  The early logistical loops to get the basic worker units up and running is THE most complicated logistical setup, and you have to do it all in the initial setup; once you've got that going, everything else is much less complicated, meaning that mid-and-late game projects are basically a matter of "place a thing and wait for the workers to construct it" because once you hit a certain point, it's just a matter of waiting.  And there will be waiting.  Prepare to spend a lot of time on 16x speed waiting for processes to get going, and expect to start up subsidiary bases at various spots around the planet just to give yourself something to do.  Overall, I will recommend the game, but with the note that this is basically a low-pressure, slow-paced base-builder.  I felt very much like I was building a garden and watching things sprout and bloom, and while that was nice, you have to be both in the mood for it and temprementally suited for it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are quite a few problems with this game.First, the campaign, makes absolutely no sense. They wanted to tell the story of an AI awakening, but it doesn't fit here. So yeah, completely unable to suspend disbelief there.I tried sandbox mode, but there just isn't much there. The game is just a scaffolding for their story in campaign mode; it's not enough by itself to be anything but boring.So no, I would not recommend this game to anyone, ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Some neat ideas hamstringed by a lack of usability and a DLC that should've been packaged with the base game (and feels very tacked on, to the point that I found it hard to use and placement of things obnoxious.) Just totally lacking in QOL it feels like, and hard to believe anyone played through this QA wise and didn't notice these things.As of the time of writing:- No bulk orders for delete, upgrade, disable, etc. with a building cap makes for a frustrating experience. Very annoying to try to replace/disable old sections of the world.- Constantly kicking up to the Orbital layer just to manage space missions can get annoying. On top of that no methodology or display on what's a repeated or single time mission.- No automatic deletion of old mines that are empty- Research system has some neat space options, but mostly just feels like a lack of convenience improvements that instead just add more weight to the game as it goes on. Very little simplification as you proceed or things that make the gameplay smoother. A lot of later game is spent just.. idling for that next building that's just better than your previous (and some of which you can't just upgrade into or are a pain to upgrade into.)- Resources have no actual uniqueness, they're just different colored cubes that all kinda act the same except that produced versions require a different set and there are hot spots on the planet. Uranium being the only exception.- Certain aspect ratios actually lose portions of the UI, I was playing a 16##x10## resolution and noticed there were sections of the screen and UI half-cut off.- (DLC) Due to the nature of flooding in the game and the constantly rising sea levels you must constantly keep moving your ports and shipyards and any water-adjacent buildings. This makes the entire Blue Planet DLC an annoying experience as the ports are already fiddly with placement, the boats seem to path globally and waste tons of time, and any increase in water level will require you to reconstruct everything.Story mode was good, concepts are neat, art is great, just.. fails on the UI/gameplay front. _childDocuments_.review: Really needs more nuanced prioritizing options. Its all supposively about automation; but falls flat due to the chaotic nature of the workers deciding to do their own thing before everything else that should be more important... Forexample: My silicon mines are stuck with full mining stock piles, but my electrical factories are starving of silicon, yet no drone hubs nearby is doing anything about it; unless i hit the prioritization button which basically says all drones should be on the task which remove them from doing something else equally important somewhere else in my huge base. Sudden a mine runs out of something and something else starts lacking, because i was too busy trying to fix another chain and not expanding my base to the next nodes.Its micro management game without nuance and more about just placement, that its obnoxiously slow yet absolutely chaotic at higher speeds.Combat becomes just blobing up a huge assault drone fleet with defense towers here and there. and is definitely not the main focus.At the start the game is manageable, but as you start expanding between sectors and have to balance your atmosphere composition with microing the absolutely massive base which will eventually crawl down the gameplay as you forced to play at slower speeds or risk death spirals.Suggestions- Give us the ability to set alerts for specific levels of production or when efficiency for a set of buildings go down or if resource production levels fall below a level, especially ability to slow down the game if something is triggered. We are an AMI after all.- Conditional Power off / Power On of buildings.- Stockpile management needs a lot more work especially when once starts working with large units of resources- Allow us to assign drone hubs to specific buildings instead of area.- Should be able to assign mines/factories to stock piles instead of a resource, to avoid drones from going all over the place- No way to convert oxygen back to carbon dioxide. This should be simple, we already do it here :) and stockpiles of carbon is available. Currently too easy to get stuck at 95% oxygen and going into a death spiral since everything is on FIRE and silicon and chemicals get completely drained- Give us the ability to have multiple graphs of  resources up at the same time.- More variation in music... it gets a tad monotonious.Bugs- I can get calls from the same character while I'm still talking to the same character. I get these are conversations that may have happened, considering the timeframe. Slow the game down perhaps when such have been accepted to avoid such?- Research completions interrupts story elements and can get jarring.- Story elements do not stop the game from running in the background. Had all the psych evals WHILE i was in 16x mode and I think that screwed me up in the end game on my second play through attempt

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fun gameplay concept that is however very shallow and towards the end frustrates by not being rewarding and throwing a hundred little stones into your path for being unrefined.The story is okay. It starts out fine, but it tries so hard to make us care for overdrawn, one-dimensional characters that however instantly default back to normality the moment the plot needs to advance. The game gives you choices, but almost none of them seem to really matter. One big conflict that threatens to tear the very protagonist apart somehow disappears into the void later on, even if you never chose to resolve or confront it. Poof, gone!But the biggest problem will certainly the be the sprawl. You will find your base hopelessly overgrowing, because resources run out so you need to keep building mines and expanding your reach. But the old mines need to be deconstructed manually and production needs to be either moved along or you need to rely on one of the worst logistics management in a base-building game: none. You cannot influence the way the game paths resources. So one worker will be overburdened with dozens of orders while the worker in the next sector idles peacefully because the orders do not go or from a building in its sector. You can put buildings into priority mode so they get preferential treatment when goods are moved, but if you have for example one area where a lot of water is being extracted and one area rich in chemicals, you cannot have the game path those resources together where you want to turn them into food. Only put the food factories into priority mode individually. And when another resource then gets pathed by those food factories, you will see all your other projects grind to a halt because your worker drones will prioritize the food resources over whatever else is needed. This can be resolved with clustering production, but it feels more like working *around* the bad game pathing rather than clever base design, and it will slow down your production. The only thing you can do is basically give every mine and factory its own worker, at which point you can enjoy the framerate grind to a halt, because running anything other than x16 speed is horrible (most sound effects aren't played on that speed so they won't keep building up to a deafening drone) which also cuts your framerate in half. I found myself spending more time on de-sprawling the planet towards the end, while the actual endgame presented no actual challenge.And if you want to hunt down the food factories to un-prioritize them, have fun, because unlike every other game like this that I have played, icons do not stay the same size when you zoom out, so you to scroll across literally the entire planet looking for this tiny symbol next to every building. This also goes for drone swarms in the laughably shallow military aspect, where biggest swarm always wins. Want to know where your huge swarms are? Well, have fun checking every single defense tower. How do you find them? Well, let's go for icon-hunting again!Only engage on your own volition. It is addictive, but not rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure other reviews have covered most of this. Despite really looking forward to the game, and it being in theory one of the kinds of games I really enjoy, I just found the whole thing to be quite lacking. The core loop of mine-build-expand lacks both detailed feedback and any way of really getting "better." Compared to something like Factorio, despite the apparent presence of a resource management aspect, there's almost zero depth. It doesn't have to be a Factorio clone, but the fact that resources dry up so quickly means that you're mostly just trying to expand all the time.Starting second bases is a problem. For a start the ships you send out have almost no resources, so you're forced to make another bootstrap base even if you have the long-distance hyperloop system. This means that while you may think it's a good strategy to send out a lander, build a hyperloop and connect it up to your main resource stockpile, you cannot do this, and are stuck going through the exact same aluminum-steel-parts process to bootstrap a base to get a hyperloop connected. Also, once you have researched higher-level mines, as they are set to the default build option at the beginning, you can find yourself being unable to even build a starter aluminium mine in an expansion until you work out how to select the lower levels.One of the resources you run out of soonest is water, and despite crashing whole asteroids full of ice into the planet, you are always running out, unable to get water from the literal oceans you create.The terraforming process is also incredibly shallow and, as others have pointed out, often means you end up with an excess of oxygen and no way of generating what you need to counteract fires. The notion of carefully guiding the Martian atmosphere with the right amount of CO2, O2 and N2 from the beginning seems to be alien - why? Why would you need to spend years making O2 only to discover that you need a shedload of N2 later on? Why wouldn't you want to be balancing these emissions from the beginning? It makes no sense and is just frustrating.The story is good, but the painfully slow mechanism of sending out landing sites, bootstrapping them, building research outposts means most of the story is simply too much of a pain to unlock, or you end up unlocking it out of order. A real shame given the work that was obviously put into this side of the game.All in all it feels like a game that needs more playtesting, more depth, a balance overhaul, and a revisit of the whole core loop to give you something to do and optimise in your base. I hope it will be a good game in a year's time and look forward to seeing if the developers can rescue it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm of mixed emotions as to whether I recommend the game or not.  I played it through and...it had tedium in spades.  When a a really big, important moment happens...it was filled, to the brim, with blaise tedium.  I wanted the damn thing to be over and done! But it kept going, and going, and going...and going, and (dear Lord make the tedius people SHUT UP!!!)...nope, still going....uhg.Likes:-Colonize Mars-Terraform Mars-Mars will turn blue and green as you do the things that let that happen.Dislikes:-Terraforming isn't quite handwaved...but it glosses over a lot of things, like if you run out of CO2 because you're really trying to turn Mars green, surprise! Nothing actually processes O2 back into CO2! so watch your mighty surge of plant growth get held back.-Also, where did all the water come from?!  I got about 480 meters of water all over the planet just by heating it up.  If I'm wrong and there really is this amount of water hanging out then I accept my wrongness, but I was under the impression that we will need to import a LOT of water to actually make Mars blue.-Sending missions to find a useful asteroid and throw it at Mars to add it's resources is a one time shot.  That seems like a very repeatable mission to me.-1 worker, 1 hub...I believe this is how they dealt with some horrible pathing issues...but uhg...I have a hub that really only functions as a charging base, but I can only run one worker bot off of each hub.-got a spaceport? Sounds totally logical that a space port isn't just tied up during landing/launch, but also while building a thing, while the thing is flying for four or five months somewhere...In the end I'm mixed.  I want to really like this more.  I'm still giving it a thumbs up...but I'm not giving it an enthusiastic thumbs up.It's a very cerebral story.  I've got no problems with that.  I like cerebral stories--but there's a mod that literally shuts your self-reflecting AI up.  That's all it does.  (I was highly tempted to install it on the main play through--don't cause you'll actually miss clues--but still...)The story is very slow paced.  My problem is that for this very cerebral story the timing of things makes zero sense.  You go years between contact with ground control.  Uhh, devs, yeah, good call, I really don't want to talk to ground control as much as would be really happening during a real mission, but the timing of things is weird.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a  good game. Don't get me wrong, it needs some work. Fortunately, in the last couple weeks the devs have been listening to the community and are making rapid improvements and fixes. Construction and research choices, as well as dialog choices, can seriously alter the game. Some choices can send you on a mission to destroy the very colony you built, or getting deleted, while others can flood the planet, while others can lead to immortality (for AMI at least). Worth your time. Fun to play, with a really good story. That said, here's my list of gripes:  It is  difficult to house more than 1000 total colonists. Most of that limitation is from water scarcity. Even after you have sections of your colony drown, you'll still be mining ice, and using it up, rather than doing any recycling. That wouldn't be so bad, but for two things:1. your research comes from colonists so it takes 3 to 5  to research higher level tech with 1000 colonists.2. Half of a whole tech tree is dedicated to buildings that you can't use. Who needs to be able to build colonies that can support 1000, 5000, or 20000 colonists, if you can't even feed 1000? Another issue tied to the tech-tree, and the story progression. You can't progress to techs to balance your oxygen until you're already over dangerous levels. Worse, it's gonna take  of time to research what you need to get the levels safe again. By the time you've done that, there's no need for the unlockable trees and animals... Trees would almost certainly spike your oxygen again, and it's much faster to research and finish teraforming than to research plants and animals. There's a lot of poorly ordered dialog. Make a new discovery, and 10 minutes later you get a phone call wondering what that discovery might be. Melt the ice caps, then spend the next hour getting  calls and thoughts about we might soon melt the ice caps. The worst one is near the end. A few good dialog and construction choices, and you can uncover the secret of . Later, you find a dangerous thing, that does the same thing to your own colonists. Not only is this rather silly, but it becomes a serious plot point "if I had known what the danger was, I could have taken precautions." Worse, the fate of the colonists doesn't actually line up with the uncovered secret history on the origin of Carmine.

_childDocuments_.review: Aggressively dumb story, fun gameplay with mods (which disable achievements). So, borderline thumbs up on sale.Story: the game is about an AI sent to supervise the planet-wide infrastructure for the colonisation of Mars. The space part of the story is fine, great even. The game wears its Kim Stanley Robinson influence on its sleeve, and is the better for it. There are some issues with the impact of certain choices, but nothing major. 9/10.The story dealing with the AI is aggressively dumb (and a huge chunk of the game). The AI monologues and does things which are massively dumb, while commenting on its own logical precision; massive soap-operas are born because the AI doesn't talk to the humans to ask advice or more information.The story arrived out of order multiple times, e.g.: the AI argues with a character, they get very upset, and they no longer speak to the AI. 30 minutes later, the character cheerily contacts the AI with no reference to the prior discussion.There are mods which stop the AI monologues but I found that the AI dialogues were a bigger headache. I advise playing the sandbox mode, which has no dialogues or monologues.So, the story is infuriating, but the option exists to remove it: 3/10.Gameplay: I started playing with mods reducing artificial restrictions and micromanagement (but I disabled my achievements by enabling mods). And I had a great time, smooth and fun gameplay while watching Mars transform around me. If Skyrim can get rated on how it plays with mods, then so can Per Aspera. The controls are somewhat poor, and are especially bad in the battle UI (e.g. left-click select and attack). 8/10.Stability: finished the game in 22 hours, I did get the game stuck once for 10 minutes(!) when placing a building. Most people would've closed the game and lost 10-20 minutes of play. So... it's decent, but I'd like at least an option to save according to real time, as the game only autosaves according to in-game time.
