_childDocuments_.review: This is a horrible game..Good things about the game: The graphical design is very well done, it is impressive and they obviously did an amazing job on it. The sound design is also so well put together that it fits seemlessly into the game, nice work.Bad things about the game:1: Limited basic resources like iron, coal and silicon... There are mines on earth that has been in use since the bronze age and geologists estimate that many of those mines will be exploitable for several thousand years into the future even with modern mining methods... Now we look at Mars that has never been exploited before. Mars has several craters on it's surface and most asteroids contain a boatload of minerals, the game however does not let the player exploit the craters but instead ignores them for stupid gameplay reasons (artificial difficulty). In real life there are so many basic resources on Mars that you could run fully modernized mining operations there for thousands of years and there would be barely any end to the amount of resources that would be exploitable.This kills the immersion, this absolutely destroys the atmosphere of the game. The whole story becomes nonsensical. It's like the AI (PLAYER CHARACTER) is so dumb that it doesn't exploit the near endless amount of resources on the actual surface of Mars. The game only lets you have like a few mines here and there WITH LIMITED AMOUNTS OF MINABLE RESOURCES IN THEM. THIS IS RIDICULOUS. There is enough iron within one of those asteroid craters to fuel the whole earth's iron industry for several decades. But somehow it's not enough to fuel a few little drone industries with drones that fly around and move things/repair things.. Are you kidding me? This is absolutely idiotic game design.2: Absolutely idiotic gameplay when it comes to your worker drones: So the drones which repair your buildings cannot be recycled and break after a few months, they are completely useless but costs a fortune of VERY LIMITED resources to construct. You need them to repair your buildings because if you don't your buildings break. But they barely get the job done and then they break. The game does not even let you recycle them, it doesn't even give you a chance to re-use those resources that were lost with the drone. When you have STUPIDLY LIMITED RESOURCES for the most idiotic gamey reasons these drones quickly become a huge thorn in your side. You have to produce massive amounts of them over and over again whilst you are forced to build a million other buildings and transport drones. You will be forced to micro-manage several dussins of factories eventually because of the limited resources, you have to individually turn them on and off at the right times in order to not waste resources which becomes EXTREMELY tedious after just a short while.3: The game pretends to be sandboxy but there is a time limit in the game. The time limit has been converted into STUPIDLY LIMITED RESOURCES. Because you have to build production chains you need specific resources for different production chains but since the base resources are STUPIDLY LIMITED you will eventually run into a dead end where you run out of that specific resource. Which soft-locks you from the rest of the game. Sandbox huh? More like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.This is some of the most stupid game design that I have ever seen. Don't get me wrong, the sound design and the graphical design is great, well done. But holy smokes.. The gameplay is horrendously bad and completely nonsensical. The game claims that you play on the surface of Mars, but on the surface of Mars you would have near limitless amounts of minerals. THE WHOLE REASON AS TO WHY THE PLANET MARS IS RED IS BECAUSE THE WHOLE DAMN SURFACE IS FILLED WITH IRON DUST.... OMG HOW THE HELL IS IRON A LIMITED RESOURCE, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?This game made me sperg out completely regarding realism. This game does not play out on Mars, it does not play out in anything that we could even compare to the real world. Most if not all fictional universes has simple laws and rules that makes those universes relatable to us. But this game just ♥♥♥♥♥ on your face and tells you "NO, THERE IS NO RESOURCES ON MARS, YOU WILL HAVE TO SCRATCH THE SURFACE IN DIRE HOPES OF FINDING A SINGLE GRAIN OF IRON, SILICON OR COAL."I will never play this game again, refunded. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, it makes no sense what so ever, the gameplay is stupid, the game is stupid. Don't buy it. Unless of course you are just looking for a mediocre challenge with some really dumb logic to it, maybe then this game will fit you. Whatever entertains you is up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Most people quit before getting through 1/10 of the game, solid DO NOT BUY! The early game is intriguing with interesting characters, a story that is told in through a unique perspective and unfolds with the choices you make throughout. The game is admittedly slow but it can't be that way all the time right? That assumption was oh so wrong. I have 20 hours in and many problems are technical but the majority, the vast majority, is the padding. Let's start with the resources, they are randomly found, generally far away and creates a burden to get them constantly. I played on normal and the resource veins were a lack luster pittance but everything and I mean EVERYTHING is expensive not just in materials, but power to. This probably padded out 14 hours of my play time. This has been a problem from the get go and it's obvious it isn't fixed which is a major problem in my eyes but the biggest technical bug is one you do not notice when things are on micro scale and that is the worker drones. The worker drones AI are still bugged, just check the forums to see the problems with that and again it's a problem that's been there since release. This only become glaringly apparent when you go to the macro scale of the city management and it only gets worse the more you do. Such as I would set a priority build and my drones wouldn't work on it cause if I had something else building that needed the same resources but it wasn't a priority. The AI couldn't figure out where to put the items and so worker drones would shuffle them around like a paid by the hour worker with no over sight and were just trying to run out the clock to the end of it's shift. Frustratingly the clock is your time and this caused my economy to tank so I had to use a cheat engine to increase the yield of the ore veins. That worked to fix the supply issue and let me continue play but the overall issue of the AI of not working only made me wait longer and longer to get things done and that is not acceptable. That problem was probably the next 5 hours of game play so that leaves the last hour to story. Yep, 20 hours and maybe an hour of story. I also got achievements that only 34 some odd percent of the player base has gotten and this has been out since December 2020 with a mostly positive? How?!? The game had 4k player in December 2020 (steam spy btw) but it hasn't broke 300 since Feb 2021. That along with the low achievement's given out means that this game is abandoned long before I quit playing. I am the exception not the rule and it isn't hard to see why. There was something interesting here at first but the dev's are either too focused on their vision to keep the game interesting, flowing smoothly and unwilling to compromise the padding or they're too inexperienced to know any better. Either way the game lacks vision, lacks engagement beyond the first couple of hours, doesn't respect the players time and they lack the technical expertise to fix what is broken. Period. Do not buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a version of Surviving Mars where each drone hub can control one and only one drone.  And building more hubs only shrinks the area of control of the hubs around it.  And drones won't cross over other hubs to help out in busy hubs.  In this colony builder/resource management game you're often trying to play around the strange and somewhat broken AI of the worker bots, and the resource management system in general (if you upgrade the roads between buildigs A and B so workers move faster between buildings, then you build a new building C between A and B those upgraded roads disappear entirely.  There's no way to hook new building C into the existing road network.  Don't ask me why this was left in or seen as a good idea.)The tech tree is unbalanced and backwards.  For example, you can unlock wind farms early on, but they won't help you until you get on with the terraforming, and by then you should have access to nuclear fission power plants anyway.  Meanwhile building hyperloops basically is a complete game changer and should absolutely be rushed.The RTS elements are poorly executed.  I wasn't sure what the purpose of drone hives is, since my swarms seemed to gravitate to worker hubs just as often after combat and the drone swarms seemed to be able to operate far away from hives with no loss of capabilities.  If the Drone Hives are only spawn points, why include a Drone Factory building as well?  Also the control system for the RTS elements were annoying and that whole element was poorly balanced (I was able to crush enemy bases with little effort and hadn't even researched half the military tech tree, while playing on the hardest difficulty setting).Also, the main game mechanic is at odds with the other mechanics.  When you terraform the planet you lose access to a lot of resources and research sites that disappear under the ocean.  You won't get much benefit from terraforming (no open-air farms like Surviving Mars) so I didn't see any point in rushing it.  I wasn't sure what half the bio techs were doing (yay now the colonists can have animals on Mars.  How does that help me out?)  The bio tech tree seems really unbalanced with the broken resource-gathering mechanic.  Researching the bio tech tree allows you to have massive colonies of a hundred thousand inhabitants, but I couldn't swing a colony of more than a few thousand due to the limits of the worker bots in moving resources from mines to factories to colony sites.Finally there's not much in the way of replay value.  The Campaign seems to unfold the same way upon subsequent playthroughs and your choices don't seem to have much impact.  For example Carmine will still appear even if you use the most peaceful ways of terraforming the planet.

_childDocuments_.review: Per Aspera is an interesting take on the 'city builder' strategy/simulation genre. It's not a perfect game, but if you're willing to overcome some of the difficulties, there is some fun to be had playing it. The highlight of the game is the story, which is all voice acted with a pretty good cast that puts a lot of feeling and emotion into it. The story is definetely what got me through the game over the actual gameplay. The gameplay itself is not BAD, but it's kind of weirdly designed and there's several things I would have done differently. One of the biggest differences between this game and others is the fact that 'worker hubs' only have one singular worker. This means you have to be strategic about worker hub placement and not have one hub servicing a dozen different buildings. Planning out your logistics is the most crucial part of the game, and you can't brute force it with sheer numbers.However, I will say that the game is somewhat unclear about a few crucial aspects of the game. Here's a list that new players might want to know before playing:* Resource nodes do eventually run out, so you will have to be constantly expanding. * If a resource node runs out, the building on it will automatically turn off. You can scrap it if you want, but it might be better to leave it for a path. * Solar power is pretty constant, while wind power goes up and down a LOT. I avoid wind power entirely because of this. * Just because you put a bio dome somewhere doesn't mean plants will start growing. Check your biome map to see where plants/lichen will grow. If you need more of the map to be fertile, you might need to import more water. * On a related note, plants will more or less spread automatically. Bio domes get the process started, but once the plants start spreading you can turn it off. * Once you have all the technology, the best expansion plan is to place a hyperloop hub as far away as possible, then an advanced landing site next to it to build it.* Lastly, you can right click to de-select whatever you've selected. This is particularly helpful when controlling your combat drones.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I love it.  It's ambitious and well worth it.  You def want the blue Mars DLC.  It's been a while since a game sucked me into it this much.  I'm near the end (I think) of my first playthrough.  Base game is a colony management / terraform Mars sim.  It's fairly epic in scope; this isn't just "drop off a terraforming package and watch it green up." It takes time to build your base(s), develop tech, and build your tech that has an impact (pun intended) on the planet.  On top of that is story mode where you have conversational choices to make, people count on you, secrets are gradually revealed, loyalties shift, and *things* happen.  There's even a little bit of "combat."  Along the way we explore several ideas such as the nature of consciousness and personhood and a few others, but that's easily skipped/skimmed if you'd rather.   I'm looking forward to finishing up story mode, though I love it, so I can also try other modes.I don't have a lot of nits to pick.  Foremost in mind is the tech tree structure strikes me as a little strange, but that's not much of a problem beyond suspension of disbelief.  Another is that some story event triggers also sometimes seem to happen at odd (late?) points but again not a dealbreaker.  I could wish that it was easier to find a particular building on the map, like maybe a search function with filters - late game you can have a lot of buildings (*EDIT - nm, found the building list! Helpful.).   And that's about it.  Graphics are pretty and detailed, story engaging, and the UI and mechanics make sense.  Voice acting is well done.If you read the description and think you'll like the game, you probably will.   Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Have to thumb this down sadly. A cool game certainly, with some original ideas in there, however its got some major flaws which I would argue mean its not worth a buy. I've done one entire play through on the second highest difficulty. I mostly enjoyed it however that is the most I will get out of the game. The story I thought was really cool, until the ending. Could've had some epic in game implications that were lazily not implemented.-Firstly, and most glaringly obvious. Combat?!?!?! Why does this game about terraforming Mars have combat? I like a good space fight as much as anyone else but the execution of combat was absolutely ♥♥♥♥, a total add on/afterthought that did not feel tacked onto the plot/game at all. Incredibly boring, incredibly simple. You can easily win the game by only researching 1 military tech, the rest r unnecessary (for context there is like 30). The enemy AI will always have a pitifully weak army that is easily destroyed. Cool idea, IF implemented wayyyyyyyyyyy better. Bit of a joke.-Game felt poorly designed. Hard to optimise your production lines at all, robot workers take resources wherever instead of where their needed. You cannot streamline/optimise properly, the no.1 best tactic to win fast is just expand constantly and rapidly, throw efficiency to the wind and just build ♥♥♥♥ until the planet is covered with your mines and factories. Feels lazy, and gets very repetitive.-The actual terraforming process is bugged and weird. Might have just been my play through, but the planet terroforming process constantly felt strange, I was pulling wayyy ahead meeting certian targets while lagging behind on others. You could say Im bad, and your probably right, the the terrible UI descriptions led me researching and investing in tehcs that did nothing or where the opposite of what I needed at the time. Story and voice acting were cool, though at time the story confused the hell out of me. This AI intellegnce (the player) is given enormous and total control over terraforming and ultimately controlling mars. Felt very odd with how little oversight the characters gave me, felt like Mars was an afterthought for them. For e.g. the mars colony was quite literally under attack, with humans dying, annndddd.... nothing. I repaired the damage and then a call came in months later that mentioned the attack as a bit of a side note. Like what??? Aliens/whatever/something just attacked humanity on Mars and I am not instantly contacted about wtf is going on? seems odd. this dev team had a cool vision I can see, and with a rating of 88% most players r clearly enjoying it. I certainly did at times, however felt like the game has way to many enormous flaws, oversights and plain poor design to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it again and changed my mind. It's a pretty relaxing city builder, with a boring story tacked onto it. All the voice actors suck and I hope I never have to hear their annoying voices again. At least you can turn off the voice volume so you don't have to hear their inane highschool drama wittering on as you place your factories in a neat row. No face pyramid in Cydonia, 0/10"Ancient Mysteries" Means building a research colony to get some fluff text that offers no tangible benefit nor does it say anything interesting. There's no mystery either, and the big reveal at the end, eh, ok. Why does story telling have to be so flimsy and full of logical plot holes you could fly a starship through? it's worth it in a sale, which is why I got it. Pretty fun city builder, nice and streamlined.But it's let down by the story tacked onto it. There are better games and stories that deal with the issue of AI than this, and all the false dilemmas and drama was anti climatic. At the end of the game you're presented with a false choice. Likewise, I'd like to ignore all the messages because I find the story telling and voice acting atrociously bad. But no, if you ignore it it'll just play messages with a delay. There was even a false choice I was presented where I declined to hear what the "leader of the colonists" said but the project still presented itself. I think I'll go back to surviving mars. At least that game had some real mystery.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it on Friday, finished on Sunday. Perfect game for "need something to do in the week-end".Gameplay: 8/10Graphics: 7/10Audio: 10/10Replayability: 6/10Innovation: 9/10Value for money: 8/10Overall: 80%... and it was just enough length in the game to keep me interested. The feeling of really making a difference on an entire planet, made this game stand out. The storyline was just long enough, and did end just in time before I felt it became a chore. The difficulty for the normal storyline was pretty easy. There might be some replayability in trying other ways of completing the storyline. But I doubt this is a game I will play more than a couple of times. There is no base design in this game, as you just plop down mine after mine, and try to set the factories not too far away from the required mines. So it just boils down to making sure you have power-, repair- and worker coverage for everything. It is not a game you play for min/maxing. Just do tasks and enjoy the story.Graphics is functional, but the gui had some annoyances. Some elements was hidden behind other elements, and it could be a bit difficult to understand what was where and how to access certain features. The audio on the other hand is spot on. Nice music. The voice acting is very good for a game like this. I had expected some cheesy stuff, but some of the characters are really believable.So would I recommend it? Hands down, yes. The theme terraforming mars has been used in other games, as well as the well as board games. But I feel this game really is spot on, combining science with a fictional story, and good voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: If the developers want me to take this game as anything other than a dystopia simulator, they should add the ability to recycle materials. Not just taking material back from deleted buildings, I mean a circular economy with recycling plants and water filtration etc. None of the techs seem to enable that, though plety are made to let me bring _more_ things from farther away/mine faster, I'm watching my colony bleed mineral deposits dry and the detailed reports on the amount of CO2 and GHGs in the air show no sign of where they all go. I could import GHGs from Earth because, according to the game, there's a surplus...It's only a matter of time before I wouldn't be able to sustain the colonists in real life and another planet will be ruined. A game for the throw away/ship it somewhere else generation.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I usually don't play games like the sort and decided to give it a go after I watched gameplay on youtube.I must say that I was surprised for the best.It did took me many tries to understand the way I like to play and that can work, and without spoilers there are so many reasons you can fail that makes this game awsome.I guess there is better optimised ways to do what you are tasked with in the game but the fun part for me was to learn from my mistakes and to find the way that I believe is best and to make it work.If you like to take a go on your own and enjoy the ride the ride is well worth it.Also I recommand to go for the Per Aspera difficulty, "realistic" hardest one, it makes the ride much more interesting and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with binary choice. I don't hate it but can't say I would actively recommend it. On the positive side, the scale of the game is quite impressive - allowing the entire planet to be unlocked and worked on. I also appreciate just how grounded in science the developers tried to make the game. There's a lot of useful tidbits of general knowledge and might even recommend it in an educational setting. That brings the other side of the coin. It has some serious pacing issues. It seems to be a direct consequence of both the subject matter (terraforming is not a quick job) and just how "scientific" the game is meant to be but for a colony management type game, there are some lethally boring segments - especially in sandbox mode, where the decent story and acting is nowhere to be found. A little dynamism and random surprises would go a long way in that regard but perhaps will be put in at a later date. Actual colony mechanics are a little shallow as well with production chains not needing much thought to manage and your biggest challenge will likely come from not noticing that one of your extractors ran dry and scrambling to put things back in order. Even that carries little risk though (unless you run out of aluminium, which is used for absolutely everything... including an aluminium mine),The closest comparable game would be Surviving Mars and I couldn't necessarily say Per Aspera outshines it in many regards other than letting you work with the entire planet as opposed to just a small piece as in Surviving Mars. For some reason, it's also made me want to play Rimworld more - likely due to me absolutely starved for some dynamic events apart from a falling meteor or twister here and there.There's a (slightly unfair) dichotomy between educational games and traditional games with the former often being seen as boring or non-engaging. Per Aspera helps show that there is in fact a spectrum of games in between and games can teach as well as engage. This particular game just doesn't do enough of the latter for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Terraforming mars scratches my itch :), in all honesty the game has some shortfalls in efficiency of delivering bots mid to late, + a constant strive for resources that I personally skipped by editing ^^ ,  however the story is solid and I like the concepts and the characters :)Great game!, I wish there were more to do!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is right up my alley in terms of genre.  I love space sim/colony/builder/survival type games.  I started playing the game yesterday and all of a sudden it was 3am... this is exactly the effect a decent game should have on me.  I love how the tutorial is woven into the campaign story, and everything about this game is unobtrusive.  The voice acting is good and not over the top or cheesy like you get from a lot of games, it's all very professional sounding.  The background music is good, and I say good because I didnt even notice the game HAD background music until about 4 hours into play.  That's what I like... not having to immediately go into settings and adjust audio volumes.  I also really LOVE playing as the perspective of the AI.  I'm excited to see how my choices affect my game later down the road.  I'm hoping HOPING that this can be a sort of Black & White type thing where I can be a benevolent AI, or I can be an evil domineering AI overlord.The game mechanics are not too complicated if you've played games like this before.  There is no "hand holding teach you to move, shove info down your throat" type tutorial, and that's OK because the game is simple enough to figure out on your own.  The UI is not busy and in my opinion is well organized.  I can already see that this is going to be a game that winds up with hundreds of hours of gameplay.To the devs, great job!Feature requests:-Add a technology to maybe increase the worker drones per worker hub from one to two.  Late game and I'm having some load issues despite cramming in new hubs everywhere.  This load issue is even after I rebuilt half my base to keep resource chains in close proximity in an effort to be efficient.-Some of the AI "reflections" seem a bit repetitive.  I was already building up atmospheric pressure and was almost at 300mb and the AI was STILL rambling on about the microsuns.-I like talking to Houston and the Commander.  Can maybe add in a feature where I could initiate communications with them at will instead of them just randomly calling me only when there's some event?-Allow me to set the transfer colonist task at the spaceport to auto-expire instead of having to sit and stare at the progress bar waiting for it to get back on Earth and only then can you cancel it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: After a long deliberation, I unfortunately cannot recommend the game. I was on the fence, but progressing further in the game you see more and more janky features. Cancelling roads is impossible, if some road decided to put over your prospective mine, bad luck - you cannot build a mine anymore.Resource distribution with workers is made complex busywork, you need 30-50% of buildings to be workers... Mines are somewhat odd - there are few at start, and later there are deeper mines, but they are clustered together in "resource villages". Also resources are finite and depending on your luck, you will always be low on one resource. Repair is another micromanagement stuff, you have to put a lot of repair buildings. And in some building views you do not see if there is resource spot where you are putting your building. You sometimes find it out after placing a building and have to press cancel building quickly.Scanning is a bit of busywork too, which goes very slowly even with 10 built towers.Game is okay, 6/10. Maybe get on sale when you have finished rest of strategies.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: First off: This is a great game!Look out that at higher drone densities it can get laggy while still not using every hardware asset (so there is place for multithread improvements).Please note that the endgame travel hyperloop building does not automatically connect to each other, you have to do that manually and spend a bunch of extra resources on it.Same with road improvements, they need to be done manually and cost extra, every single level of it.The mars terraforming is an extremely neat feature, with all the atmosphere balancing and other aspects.Per Aspera also has a decent storyline, and really catchy music too!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The workers are frankly broken. They're basically uncontrollable. While the game nominally allows you to assign a prioritization for tasks, the worker drones seem to love just completely ignoring that. I'm sitting here watching my Martian civilization die a slow death, because despite the fact that I've allocated literally every possible task to a lower priority than the "make more workers in the worker factory", they're all running around doing basically anything other than moving the damned gears that need to get from the warehouse to the factory that's right bloody next door. Meanwhile, these mindless drones are slowly dying off, and none of them seem to be willing or able to do a damned thing to replace themselves. Oh now it's been five minutes, not only are they not moving the gears from the warehouse to the factory, some of them have gone and taken the gears from the factory and moved it elsewhere. Why? Who the hell knows. No, of course you can't manually control them when it's important, that would be *insane*. Who would want to be able to actually fix a problem? The game doesn't even let you reassign the area where you want your workers to be focusing on. You just need to kinda build these "hubs" and hope what workers you have pick the right ones to move to and to start doing the jobs you've actually assigned as high priority. Instead of, I dunno, stockpiling 1000 units of polymers just for the hell of it. Very important.

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the base builder, stayed for the story! While I can nitpick a couple improvements I would've like to have seen like being able to run water pipes from the treatment plant or an easier way to filter by buildings that were empty or destroyed, all-in it was a great base builder. But the real story here was the story, I loved that I was an AI running things with options that lead me down various paths. I found the storyline quite engaging and didn't want it to stop. I won't say any more to avoid spoilers, but this gets an easy 2 thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing a play through on the hardest difficulty, I have to say: This is not a colony builder, this is not an rts. This is a resource management-RPG. Everything is a resource, the aluminium, the iron, the colonists. What is important is to find more and more, while developing your character, literally. You are an infant AI, learning to be a grown-up. Everything in this game serves that agenda. If you approach it as a colony builder, you won't like it.  You have to approach this game from the perspective of story telling and making a character. If you do that I'm sure you'll have fun, deciding whether to be the arbiter of peace, or the genocidal villain, is what the game is about. Both having direct routes, each decision having a logical path that you discover as you play.The end game can get pretty slow, so don't worry about slowing down your mission for the sake of the story too much, like I did. You have plenty of time to get everything you want done. It can get pretty boring after you finish with the story aspect otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Well made (mars model especially), seamless execution and interesting story are strong points of the...ha, it is hard to call it game as it is more some sort of simulation. and this is where it might disappoint  as it can be boring (as terraforming can be a long process). one run is good and worth your time but then not much to do after.Despite this I'm giving a thumbs up for the game mainly to recognize the efforts of the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I am unsure why this game has such a low score. I beat the campaign, but honestly prefer sandbox. Stripping the low ocean areas of resources while build efficient methods for shipping and travel so that I can begin terraforming just have really appealed to me. You don't have to strip mine the future ocean areas, but until they introduce aquatic units and buildings, I cannot stand to see all those wasted resources haha. Anyways, mostly making this post because I don't agree with this games rating. I would personally put this game between 80-86% personally. 80% at full price and 86% when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Game is addicting.Gameplay is all about juggling resources and efficiency, all in the name of that huge goal -- terraform mars. I love how the planet changes dynamically to how you influence it. Once you get an atmosphere, wind will blow across the martian surface and you'll see the blue glow from your orbital perspective.It has an immersive quality that I love. You are an AI in mars orbit and that's why you see everything the way that you do. There is a worldbuild behind it too, one that you'll really only get into if you seek it out. The story is a feature that I adored and was a perfect change of pace to the regular base building.If you are one of those people who spent a ton of time with cities skylines or satisfactory, I'd really recommend this one.Very good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... so, bear with me ;) This is awesome, I love city sims and the like and this ticked all the boxes,but where this game shines is how it makes that a new thing... RTS!I wasn't overly sold at the idea and from the advertising it felt more like the 'battles' were a pure senario event thing... but it's the most of the game!Granted I haven't actually progressed that far through the story, but my first experience of it was plodding through the early game, taking my time, speeding up time... you know, city sim. But out of the Fog-O-War there pops up a swarm of hostile blinks on the screen. I suddenly realise I've miss managed mt time and within the first strike my whole economy was ruined. Was gagging for round two with actual defences this time, despite the grind through the tutorial for the fourth time. A word of warning for those who read this far, the auto save if few and far between and doesn't seem to have a way to make it more often. Save, save often.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game. People complaint about resources being scarce and logistics are a problem but... This game a resource management game guys... I am on my 20th hour in the game and this is still my first play through. I am playing on the realistic difficulty and never ever thought the logistics are being a problem or had a headache from resources. It is really fun to see the red planet become green slowly.My only complaint about the game is the lack of tutorials/explanations about drone attack ranges, hyperloop connectivity, road upgrades. I thought that hyperloops connect by themselves about an hour :D
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review 06th December 2020 :I initially provided a positive review for the title, unfortunately the current state of the game requires that I leave a negative review highlighting the issues i'm seeing : 1) Road construction AI : There needs to be a way to control how roads are built to create a more linear transport network. See point 22) Worker transport AI : As a result of the bugs with the road network the drones will commonly go into a death loop, getting perpetually stuck between two buildings. Drones are the lifeblood of yr planetary network, there inefficiency, coupled with long construction times results in most of your production buildings grinding to a halt due to full storage capacity3) Despite well placed worker hubs and storage depots, the workers will dump random resources at production buildings. 4) No way to store resources for an emergency or specific future project. 5) Maintenance Hubs : The drones are consumed upon doing the repair works. This is a redundant game design choice. Why would a sentient advanced machine produce expensive drones that comsume themselves? Rather use resources that create nanites that the repairs drones consume. we can then have a supply of nanites close at hand to supply these hubs.. Or build this into the Hubs functionality. 6) Resource pocket quanities. The recent update increased the spawn rate but there will need to be a buff to overall resource quantities per node. 7) In general the game is not forthcoming with info letting you know when you have issues with production.Summary : The AI is the worst part of this game right now and as the player taking control of a sentient AI machine, you cant fall in love with the system because you constantly faced with the glaring errors of the drone AI network. There needs to be far more control for yr drones. I see no other way than to allow the player to create their own road networks so the drones are forced into set paths to achieve efficient logistics systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: -- The Good -- Early game is quite satisfying as a Mars terraforming simulator.  Setting up that first logistics network is great.  The story progresses nicely.  Speaking of which, the story is excellent!  I think it is the strongest part of the game.--- The Bad ---The story being the best part of the game in a base building game should indicate that the base building portion is weak.  After the first few nodes in the logistics network it becomes a mess to try to control.  There is no manual way to adjust the road networks.  The storage facilities aren't prioritized higher than mines, so you cannot set up a storage facility near a factory as a buffer to ensure factories are running at full capacity.  There's minimal ways to throttle production other than outright turning off factories, so you end up with thousands of items you just don't need stuffing up your storage facilities.  And without a way to manually assign worker hub zones, trying to keep them balanced is just frustration incarnate.Speaking of the story.  It unfolds so, so slowly after the first burst of activity.--- The Ugly ---Lichen and Trees cannot hop road networks.  You have a choice, make breaks in the network, or portions of Mars remain barren.Blue Mars was introduced as a way to access research facilities and resources under water.  Unfortunately, as water raises you are constantly moving ports, shipyards and water purification stations backwards.  On top of that, the boats are beyond dumb.  I watched my entire fleet decide to move goods from one port to another, ignoring all of the resource nodes on the water.  The two ports were hooked up via a much faster Worker-Hub-and-Hyperloop network.  Another time I watched 4 boats take 4 aluminium from a wind farm, to a port, then carry them back to the wind farm, back to the port...Personally, I'm glad I bought it and played it once for the story.  But there is no chance this would become a Mars terraforming staple that I play repeatedly as the years go by.  Surviving Mars and Terraformers are both far better games with exceptional replayability.  Per Aspera is not.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good conscience recommend this game. The sound is buggy, the story is stupid, and the game's constant need to wrench control away from you at all times is a right pain in the ass. Additionally, there's no quick way to sort through all buildings of the same type planet-wide, the atmospheric handling is fiddly as hell in a way that it really doesn't need to be, and it's just not very good. Make a better game next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS WARNING!!!This game has a very steep learning curve so prepare for that! I really enjoyed the first 10 hours of constant challenge but the last 4 hours I just sat and clicked a single button and waited for the ships to be built.I found the story was good with a few nice twists thrown in. If you are after a challenge terraforming your own world, I definitely recommend this game, In the end give yourself some other goals to tide you over though.This game could use with some more development on balancing and resource availability, there was a quite a few times I had to deconstruct key buildings in order to progress which was annoying at worst. The worker bots are broken and do make logical decisions at all. They will travel halfway around Mars to pick up a resource that is literally right next to them.Art style is clean and informative using standard topographical lines to show elavation as well as the 3D is very nice. The way the planet physically changes as you progress is awesome! I loved watching the oceans slowly rise.All things considered I would rate this game a 6.5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game started a first playthrough saw some things i wanted to change restarted it played until 6am went to sleep got up at midday played more.Played 23 hours total finished the story once with full freedom for me and i have to say it is a great experience with the story and the game but there are quite a few things that can be changed and prob will in time.Currently id say late game pace is a bit off next to that no control over road building leads to spider webs of a mess that will in giant bases(think 1000+ buildings) lead to slowdowns even on high end machinesSome of the story events are forced and will lead to you having to go down a route even when you dont want toBesides gameplay elements though the game is stable no actual bugs that cause me to have to restart or crashes or anything which is a nice refreshing thing to see from any game now days ;)My rating for this gameGameplay 7/10Story 8/10Visuals 6/10Visuals like terrain and such can be made to be a bit more diverse in later stages of terraforming and some of the drones when zoomed in really do not look good but overall it is a pleasing game to look at thoughOne suggestion id make of all the things in my list, Make drones have a tech that you can research so that they can carry more then 1 item at a time please
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this is a game that's disappointing to dislike.I'm a pretty avid city builder/strategy nerd.  I appreciate very heavy games like what Paradox produces, lighter games that are well executed like Banished, and everything in between.  This one just isn't good unfortunately, well below my low bar.The good:The voice acting is very good, and the story is somewhat intriguing.The bad:The game play is really poor.  Honestly it reminded me of an idle game I might play on my phone, except I had to watch it the whole time.You land on Mars and immediately are interacting with 95% of the available resource types within 5 minutes of the game starting... and those interactions are going to remain virtually unchanged for the next 20-30 hours.  This might be forgivable if it went somewhere... but it does not.  Initially you will feel like it might be going places: there are little prompts with temperature and oxygen levels and when you hit a couple of different milestones the planet undergoes a neat little transformation.  But after that... the game virtually stops.  There are a few more parameters to tweak but not only is it mechanically very tedious it doesn't *feel* like you are effecting the planet anymore.  I got the "congratulations mars is terraformed!" message when the planet was -1.8 degrees C, the water level was still well inside what was obviously supposed to be the ocean boundary, and the planet was still entirely red and dead looking.  There are endgame techs you think might be cool that are literally pointless, like open air cities.  The whole game just provides none of the mechanical joy I would expect out of a game of this genre, and none of the wonder that you might get out of a building game like Cities Skylines... It just isn't very good as a game.  There is a light combat aspect in the game that is also largely pointless, which ties to a plot element I wont spoil.  I suspect that system pulled a lot of attention away from the rest of the game, which would have been far improved by a more linear game play loop with a focus on the headline mechanic of terraforming.  Kind of a classic example of not knowing what your focus in development is.Very rarely do I leave poor reviews, but this is a thumbs down.  I wouldn't even pick it up on sale honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Whole game's premise was nice at the start until you progress slowly to terraforming mars.The tech tree was somewhat lacking:- only one worker per hub- you can convert water to ice, but can't convert ice to water, very weird limitation- you can't build anything on water bodies despite with all the 'techs' to terraform mars- hyperloop terminal didn't carry any power from one to another- worker hub  only handles at their own sector/district - paths has to be upgraded manually, upgrading all at once hampers your logistics greatly- pumping water from north to south is a pain job to do for crater buildingsThis also one of those constantly 'searching for resources' kind of game depending on your game settings. The game is also a long duration once you reached stage 3 of terraforming
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. Has some good ideas, but the end result is "fine".Don't worry about how your cities look. It will always form a blob of buildings and streets running all over the place. Looks awful, and resources reach where they should eventually anyway. It has some combat, just make a blob bigger than your enemies and throw it at them.Transport of stuff is a serious problem in this game. Because this is ThE fUtUrE, you can't have a train, truck or any reasonable medium of transportation. You have pods. Each pod can transport ONE resource through ONE road, so resource transport is slow and bottlenecks are frequent. Just add more pods to the blob until flow of resources resumes, so not a terrible thing. The problem is the hyperloops. They are ALSO pods, just faster, so they suck and are usually a bottleneck. Put normal roads on top of the hyperloop, and normal pods will transport resources that the hyperloop going and coming full speed trasnporting ONE RESOURCE EACH TIME just can't. The Blob keeps growing. If you ever wondered why we don't have hyperloops, play this game.Besides that, there's some cool ideas here, but the core of the game is... fine. It's fun for a while.Oh, also, the plot. It's also fine. Promises a lot, but I feel it doesn't do a lot and it kinda ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty fun, wish it had a speed quicker than 16x though as at times you are only waiting for a tech that might take 2 years and especially in the end as you are waiting for the terraforming goal to slowly tick away, there is not much else to do except wait. I tried to optimize the base more in the end (replacing obsolete but functional structure with new, optimize the paths etc) but that was just to pass the time, it didn't really affect anything. Something more after the initial human breatahable/walkable terraforming phase would be fun too, whats the next step? Could I get a score depending on how quickly and well I terraformed (how many people died as a minus for example due to mismanagement). No score right now as far as I can see.I played this through during 2+ days in the free weekend, so I guess I do reccomend it, not sure about full price though (a playthrough is 20-30h I guess and at this point I don't see a lot of replayability).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I would really love to give this game a thumbs up, it is visually very appealing and all the little lore bits to find are very interesting.But the current resource balance is just too frustrating.I understand the resource scarcity is meant to force the player to expand their base and research like none other, but with low tire materials seemly the most scarce, it's a bit of a farce.Personally I would like the game to do away with specific mining points, and just have a "heat map" or the like, where here you can extract 500 units, but over there a 1000.Anyway, not a bad game if you don't mind endless waiting.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea for a game but unfortunately rather poor implementation. Too much focus was put on the "story" aspects, such as the game asking me how I feel about decisions...every decision... It is obvious that the game doesn't include QoL features seen in Factorio or Dyson Sphere Program. Some examples of poor QOL I experienced in just a handful of hours:- Every building in the game you want to build must be clicked on. There is no hotbar, no "smart key" to build a building you are hovering over, etc.- There is no way to run an electrical, repair, or worker hub network. You cannot click and drag to place multiple of these spaced neatly apart at maximum range like you can power poles in Factorio / DSP.- There is no way to mass upgrade road networks, it is an absolutely painful process.- The view which gives you details about traffic on your road network CANNOT be viewed while upgrading roads. This made me feel like the devs don't play their own game honestly.I tried to play past the lack of QoL just to get through my first play through but after having no challenges presented to me with the game running on max speed it felt like a waiting game. I would spam click buildings to expand as fast as I wanted and just wait... Got bored. May return just to see what Mars looks like terraformed but besides that this game is a pass from someone looking for Factorio / DSP on Mars!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it was a nice game with a nice story behind it, but I'm 60-40 to recommending it.Cons: - the performance is horrendous in late game to the point I couldn't get more than 15-20fps on a 5700 XT with a 2700x at 1440p on High/Medium - the DLC should be part of the main game and for one I haven't bought it - the workers hub holding only one worker is dumb - the combat is a jokePros: - the game tries to be as realistic as possible - the progression is extremely slow, as it should be, you are transforming a damn planet, you won't fill 4,200,000,000 cubic kilometers of empty space with oxygen and nitrogen in a couple of days. - the story is interesting - the building system is nice, although it would be amazing if the worker hub had more workers
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: 2 major issues I don't know why they exists:1-Why no on map building filters, just why.2-Why I can't see where a product is stockpiled, I have around 1,5k ice stockpiled but can't see where and colonies lack ice unless prioritized, which I shouldn't have to unless there's traffic in sector.These just ruin the game for me as I look at the map %50 of the time and can't find anything unless I go into buildings screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: So at 11 hours I feel pretty comfortable and ready to actually try to take on Mars. It's a surprisingly crowded niche with 2 near peer competitors with the Paradox's one and the new early access one. This feels meaty and well crafted though. While I did enjoy the paradox version, this one has some passionate developers and doesn't feel as chained to the paradox dlc model. I have not tried the new early access one yet but I'm going to let it bake a bit longer while I get into this game. I feel like at 11 hours I'm scratching the surface as it is a very slow burner but with the improvements to UI I'm seeing the depth better, but just one small nitpick. Games should allow you to play peacefully if we so desire (Minecraft and Factario come to mind), sometimes after kids have destroyed your freshly cleaned kitchen you want to just chill and build with out anything kicking over the castle but the tide or the sunrise in the windows.  I look forward to where this game goes and the plans the devs have in store for post launch support.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game for 40 minutes so far so here's my thoughts:The idea of an AI made specifically to terraform Mars and one that is sentient and has some existential crises is a great idea in my opinion.However, sometimes it DOES get stale but when something happens, its good. This game is also very ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pc friendly, as I have one and it usually maxes around 40-50 FPS8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: For an indie game, yes it was pretty good. I really liked the story and the characters - it was in fact the best part of it......but the meat of it was quite thin once you had achieved self reliance. I kept on expecting more of a challenge, and then it never came. I prepared anally for something that never happened. Ending was quite disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very impressive and addicting game, great time killer. You've got the entire Mars on a birds eye view topographical map.As the game progresses, more and more areas open up to you and allow you to slowly cover the planet in buildings and trees.I find a lot of the mechanics of the game to be fun and creative, some areas being flood zones and having the danger of being out of reach to explore the rovers, artifacts is a good addition, and the orbital view for projects looks dope, but it does definitely has its lackings.Farms' food production pales in comparison to the food factories. The game does not create bridges over the rivers when water levels start to rise, which looks strange at best. As such, some buildings definitely need a buff or work up.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you WILL be sucked into if you like basebuilding/citybuilding games. There are threats, and there are disasters, and you will want to punch your monitor when an asteroid lands RIGHT WHERE IT KNOCKS OUT ALL THE MAIN POINTS OF INFRASTRUCTURE RIGHT AS THE GAME AUTOSAVES.... But it makes me feel like I am running a Mars Terraforming effort, and that is DAMN impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun. Nothing super complex like Factorio, but just a chill little game where you build out Mars' infrastructure as you watch the story unfold and the planet slowly getting terraformed. The story is the main plus point in this game I think. The voice acting especially is really good.I was turned away by the mixed reviews previously. I ended up getting it at 50% off, and can say that it was well worth it. I ended up getting 100% of the achievements in about 22 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The game as it is now would be acceptable if it released into Early Access. I think the story glitched in my play through since I seem to be getting dialogue happening out of order. The gameplay needs a lot more playtesting to have the rough edges pulled out of it. I'd like some way to turn off the icon noise so I can find where new mineral patches are for putting down new miner.I don't know what the district or travel overlay does for me, or why it's unlocked first. It's entirely AI managed, and you have no influence over it until much later in the game when you unlock faster roads, but you have to individually upgrade individual roads, which isn't worthwhile because the AI will always path around your upgraded roads, so you have to upgrade everything.And speaking of the AI, your playthrough can crash and burn because the AI won't transport items from one location to another. Even if you have plenty of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking awsome, once you get the nuts and bolts of it. It took me a while to get to the point where mars actually turns green but I did it in the final hour of my first playthough. The biggest con' is that some of the mechanics (road upgrade, i'm looking at you) are not explained at all. The story is fun, with the multiple endings and all :)
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Could this be?  Finally, a worthy successor to Outpost 1 and Moonbase??  No.  No it is not.  For the first few hours, emotionally, this fit all the positives I felt as a child playing space colonizers for the first time.  But after that, the gameplay gets so boring and repetitive that I couldn't keep playing.  Cool narrative but I'd rather read it as a novella.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the free weekend.The game is ok. Resource management and city building are right up my alley. The campaign could use some work. You're building everything up and then an objective comes up, 'go explore the other side of the planet' and you've barely built out 1/4 of your first sector. It kind of pressures you into building really big, really fast.Then, after a bit of an initial build-up you just kinda hoard resources by playing on 16x speed before your next big push into base development. The game quickly turned into, base-build for 10 minutes then do nothing at 16x speed for 5-10 minutes.Edit: I wrote this and discovered that an additional landing zone could be created. I've been sucked into this game. It's great. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I tried it out during the free weekend, and I was very pleasantly surprised at how complex this game actually was. A really good Colony Sim if you don't want to control the colonists in a more in-depth field of way! Highly recommend this title for anyone looking to get into Colony Sim and might find the other titles to daunting.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline is excellent. 11/10, if you enjoy the idea of terraforming games but they leave you feeling unfulfilled then this is the game for you. My biggest, and almost only, critique is aimed at the Devs. The HUD. Having to scour the globe for every single factory you've ever made looking for a single one to turn off or on is just plain silly and hard on the eyes. There are plenty of great examples of industry control HUDs out there. I just want to know how many steel factories I have and if theyre having supply chain issues ect. I have the same critique for power/water. The left side display just shows planetwide, whereas a small drop down with a district breakdown would be considerably more user friendly. I spent a lot of time trying to look around small icons that blended together that would have been better spent enjoying the gameplay experience or plotting my next move.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A good idea but a bad implementation. I am kinda used to play this type of games but the way it's made make it more of a headache that an enjoyment. The AI which is manipulating the resources it's flawed, after 6 hours the AI stop producing workers due to the fact that it was missing an item even though in the storage AI had 300 pcs of certain item. Even though i started to prioritize that item it would still not go in the worker production facility even though it was prioritized( i still had 18 workers).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I noticed this game as it looked fun after a review and a letsplay. However, it has massive shortcomings when it comes to resource management which is this games core. Since you can not transfer Resources between Bases (Districts) and the Resources being limited plus you initially do not know where which resources are, running out even one of them means the entire base is doomed to fail, hindering your progress. Progress is also mostly waiting for research which seems to be artifically slow. I spend way to much time just watching youtube waiting the game to progress on max. speed while keeping an occasionally glance to check if resource levels are stable.The game is also very short on notifying you if problems arise. If a Mine runs out of Ressources, it will simply power down, its upon you to keep an eye out for that little symbol and hope you have additional nodes you could exploit. If not... well see above. It is a shame because i love the premise of this game and it could have been great, however it forces you on a terrible mix of trial & error coupled with a large chunk of luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I've got this game on the 'free weekend' and I must admit, I was very close to buy it, if I wouldn't have finished the main campain for ca. 20 hours. But it definitely worth the time spent. The main campain has an astonishing detective plot that keeps you on toes throughout all the game, which you rarely find in colony-builders. However, after completing the main campain, as an experienced gamer, you quickly realize, that there is nothing much left to do in the game. So I can only wish adding more stories, planets and new campains. But for the beginners and fans of the genre, I definitely recommend to have a look on this product, you won't be disappointed (probably lol).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I cant exactly pin down why I love this game so much. The peaceful cheerful sounds as the little robots deliver their goods to their destination. Logistics is handled by the game and you just build things and just give it time and it will build. I like that expanding harms the growth bacteria and trees. You don't necessarily want to build everywhere as that prevents growth. Nitrogen is your main concern. Trucking it it from Titan seems like the only way possible. I like how there are many cool sci-fi ideas on how to terraform mars that made me google and ask questions.Storyline: This was clearly written by different people at different points. It isn't cohesive and the characters aren't very believable. In one breath the AI doesn't like the idea of ISA using mars as a mining station and in the next is willing to rape and pillage Titan for its resources.(Titan is one of the only planets with liquid oceans of methane and might actually have life that is very different from Earth, a slim chance but still worth probing) There are 1000 inconsistencies or just stupid dialogue that makes no sense but suspending that the game is really enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mix of a citybuilder and a visual novel. The story of your AI is quite interesting and takes some fun twists and turns, and there are several different endings. The only problem I have is that the final step towards colonization is pretty... slow. You're basically just waiting for the plants you put everywhere to transform all the CO2 into oxygen, which for me took 10 years of ingame (total duration 73 years) during which I had the entire story pretty much wrapped up (just waiting for the final "yay, you did it" part) and five years before I finished terraforming I had the entire tech tree maxed out.Still, it was a fun game, and there's definitely some replay value if you want to see the other endings (though I personally don't really feel the need to.)
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Very nearly beat the game, was on the last stage of terraforming to create a magnetic field, but the late game lag and breakdown softlocked the entire system and lack of management tools meant I couldn't fight it.Full of tedium, horrible management, you have a single "priority" order on a per-building basis, breaks down late game into a laggy, buggy mess and workers fail to deliver produced resources to necessary buildings. The whole "flooding" system is ridiculous too, if you want to interact with the water mechanics at all before you have fully flooded the planet, be prepared to rebuild stuff over and over as water rises because you CANNOT build water pumps inland. It started out so strong with an interesting story but the game just fell apart underneath me late game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: really fun and the story is great. Gameplay is very much managing your production and consumption and continuing to expand as resource nodes deplete. Only suggestion for the developers is to increase the built limit and if possible, increase performance as near the mid point all the buildings do take a hit in the frame rate. Great job and great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: At first I loved this game but I became more and more frustrated the more time I spent with it.Logistics become a nightmare. The game is based on scaling your base on a planet wide scale but the games system and algorithms simply don'T allow for that. At some points I had 1000s of ressources and production buildings and omes that complained about missing ressources.The pacing of the story is completely wonky. _childDocuments_.review: There's a decent game in here somewhere but the catastrophically bad way of how it currently handles logistics makes the experience insufferable. No matter how many hubs you spam down, 90% of the time, mining and production buildings will be at a stand-still due to being filled to capacity. Here's an example:4-5 worker hubs with fully upgraded roads outside miners leading to both factories and supply depos are halted.. "Uhh, just rearrange the roads and stuff". I'd love to, but the game doesn't let you. Everything is hard-locked to being automatically attached to each-other via circles which right out of the gates creates a minimal spacial inefficiency of 11-60% on-top of looking like spiderweb diarrhea and the AI also has a tendency to not take the best routes. This becomes particularly annoying because once mines are depleted, you're encouraged to scrap buildings.... Which disconnects the roads.In a similar brain-dead fashion, power generation & maintenance is also restricted to circles with buildings also requiring constant maintenance so every single time you want to reach out to get resources somewhere, the project goes from being a single building with a road (maybe a cargo hub) like other actual good management games to:Once you put a few hours into the game, you also realize just how incredibly simple it is. No complexity, only occasional "threats" that randomly destroy stuff and the obligatory "research" element that involves you waiting for 10 hours before getting another toy to play with.Disappointing mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in its present state. I had voice over lines cut short, I had missions that fired randomly or not at all. The logistics/building part of the game is slow and extremely tedious, and the bots that carry stuff around can rarely be counted on to do their job efficiently. The research tree is rather dull, with only the hyperloop being an actual game changer. Running out of minerals and resources is frustrating as you have to make longer and longer "tentacles" of droid bases into the unknown for just one or two resource nodes. I spent most of the time playing at maximum speed, and it still felt like the game was absolutely crawling. The soundtrack is also extremely repetitive which I shouldn't have noticed having only played the game for 4 hours, but just sitting and staring at the bots moving steel plates from one side of the base to the other leaves nothing but the soundtrack to appreciate, and I didn't appreciate it. I thought the story was weird and incomprehensible at times, but that might just because the game randomly cut short dialogue or skipped entire conversations on me. Ultimately what you spend a lot of time on in this game is staring at your base and waiting for resources to either be made or moved without any satisfaction. It's not like Factorio where you get that cool moment of making something really efficient or you get to the next research tier. There is just nothing to look forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Never have I felt so insulted and wasteful of my time as I did playing Per Aspera.This is a game that has polish, an attractive GUI and an interesting premise, but it all falls apart at the seams.  It was the worst experience I've ever had with a colony sim on a mechanical level.Sure looks pretty though.GAMPLAYThe campaign is INCREDIBLY uneven in both pacing and difficulty.  There is a scripted crisis early in the storyline that hits with no warning that can be brutal to recover from if you aren't massively overprepared.... then it's trivial.Speaking of pacing, some sections I was triggering dialogue events one after the other, almost on top of each other, at other stages, I was waiting for several HOURS of IRL time (at maximum speedup) for the next milestone to trigger.  Normally, in other games this could involve micromanaging things to speed up production, or planning for the next step, or restructuring things to use resources more efficiently, but you are railroaded so hard that you will take about the same amount of time to finish regardless of what you do, so I was forced to idle through several sections of the game, since I slammed into the brick wall of the game's speed limit.I won't spoil anything here, but several mechanics aren't fleshed out well and the base building looks way deeper than it actually is.  Basically you just tile the same ratio of everything across the planet like a blob and spam worker hubs everywhere as you go.  There's literally only downsides to keeping things adjacent and trying to design anything like specialized districts once you understand everywhere needs a little of everything (Workers, power, maintenance, and eventually waterr).Did I mention how SLOW this game is? Even at the fastest 16x speed setting, the game is barely tolerable.  I only slowed things down for about 20 minutes total during my entire playthrough to troubleshoot an issue or two. (Also I researched literally the entire tech tree while I waited for stuff to finish, so it's not from lack of having resources)Having remote bases were another annoyance in the campaign.  At several points you establish remote outposts for story reasons, but developing these bases is hardly practical and ultimately you should just build up your core base more so you have everything on the same logistics network.  If you could shuttle resources back and forth to other base hubs, there'd be an incentive to actually grown the outposts and mine resources locally, but instead, I just jammed everything in my main base and absorbed the closer outposts/abandoned the remote ones.STORYThis has the veneer of hard sci-fi, but the simulation of the planet is incredibly primitive.  Consequences of things you just give you a few points here or there towards whatever stat.  Nothing like rain shadows, ocean currents, weather, orbits etc. is modeled in any way.  Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri from the 90s did a better job at making you feel like you were actually terraforming a planet.The story itself feel very railroaded.  I refuse to play through again, but several dialogue choices seemed to be obvious non-branching paths with no real impact on the outcome of anything.  Additionally, several optional objectives encountered in the story didn't seem to provide any benefit and only further slowed the glacial pacing of the game.There's also some ludonarrative dissonance in several sections of the story (which the game has taking place over basically 100 years).  Several of the more dramatic events in the story that the writers seemed to want to have happening over the course of days were actually happening over the course of YEARS in game time.  Yet, other scenes try to account for the passage of time.... you meet new characters, and children are born and grow up.  It's just wildly inconsistent.  At least Civilization just rolls with immortal world leaders magically staying the same age.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim expecting a simple terraforming game where I could just watch the gradual transformation of Mars into a paradise. I wasn't expecting anything major out of it, just a few hours of entertainment and logistical planning while doing other things. Color me surprised when I came into a rather indepth and cleverly written story ruminating on concepts such as AI agency, independence, and the nature of what it means to be sentient.While the core loop is simple, it's engaging enough to keep you going to put you through the rather interesting story and the mystery at the core of the game. _childDocuments_.review: To sum it up in a single sentence: This game is conceptually fantastic but mechanically infuriating.The idea of Per Aspera is very appealing. Watching Mar slowly gain an atmosphere, watch surface water slowly begin to spread and even greenery begin to blossom is incredibly satisfying. It is obvious that a great deal of care and attention has gone into recreating Mars and there's a lot of fun to be had just rotating the big red ball and admiring all the craters and canyons.But as a game, Per Aspera is infuriating. For a game primarily about base management, I feel I have very little control over how my base is run. So much of core gameplay is left to the whims of the AI and frankly it isn't up to the challenge. It becomes difficult to focus on further terraforming when basic things like keeping Drone Factories working, Maintenance Hubs and Colonies can fall apart if you look away for too long. I would kill for a little more micromanagement. Just the ability to tell a worker "Your job is to take food from this factory to this colony and nothing else." Especially with resource placement being so random that you've got no guarantee that the resources you need will be anywhere near each other. Considering the story is suppose to revolve around an AI fully in control of the terraforming mission, you can often feel helpless watching your workers skirt around at random.I'd be lying if I said I didn't have fun playing Per Aspera, but at the end of 20 hours of playing my frustration with the mechanics quickly began to outweigh my enjoyment. This is an impressively ambitious game, and the story seems to suggest an amount of replay-ability, but the mechanics need a lot of work before I'd consider playing it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game my autistic a.ss. always wanted. You are set with the task of making Mars liveable. To do so you build a sprawling mass of roads, mines, colonies, and the facilities to run it all. You then have some research trees which the colonists can put their minds to work on. It's all very satisfying to watch your progress over the years in game and see the little projects you've completed along the way become part of the unique layout for your colonies. WARNING: Flood zones flood! Now, you can build there but make sure you are ready to leave. The sea takes all and you cannot stop it once you start the terraforming process.I wish the building limit was higher (or just gone tbh with a warning about it being unstable). Game ran pretty well for me, unmodded that is. However the longer you play the lower the fps gets. It will be stable but it will sink.Overall, if you like the idea of being in charge of bringing life to Mars, and making a massive blob of buildings and roads, then I'd recommend it. The game is slow and your first two hours are pretty much like the rest. Watching your base and the Martian landscape slowly change. That's the selling point for me, especially on sale.TL:DR - Game good, take forever though so put a few days aside.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a tough call, but after some deliberation went for a positive review, simply because the game has kept me nicely entertained for 15 hours.In the game's current state, if there was a 'neutral' review option I would have gone for that.As above, the game is entertaining, but there are some issues:- some things don't seem to be explained well (new landing sites, how to choose)- some UI issues (building population versus 'real' researched population limit)- some bugs (weird negative research values and some others that I can't tell if bugs or lack of explanation)Positives:- some of the best voice acting I've heard in a video game- graphics are very nice and you can really see the planet changing- runs well on my system (Ryzen 7 3700x with GTX 1070)- interesting story line and concept- good core game play - has the 'just a few more minutes' vibe...At this point, I will likely try and finish current game then mothball the game until patched further in 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Per Aspera for what is it trying to achieve, but I hesitate to recommend this game at full price. I'm giving it a thumbs up because I had fun and wanted to keep playing, but the game did feel like a chore at times. The user interface needs a complete re-do, and there's a lot of missing features that other citybuilders have that I could consider core. Things that filter what you see on screen so you can find certain buildings easier. That was the most frustrating thing for me.I would be very keen to play this again if an overhaul update comes out that improves a lot of the friction in the endgame when your city is huge. The story was quite good and I was always intrigued by the characters and plot. At endgame, the performance did suffer a bit, but being such a slow-paced game, it was completely fine to play at 30fps. I think the simulation was tanking the performance more than the graphics at that scale. If I completely populated every inch of Mars, I am sure it would be completely unmanageable and the simulation would cripple my computer.Despite that, it's actually a good game, and I got my money's worth. I hope to get more if the game gets any improvements down the line. If you're looking for a citybuilder that doesn't have a lot of micromanagement, but has an engaging story that ties in with your progression, you'll probably enjoy this. I did, even though I recognise its shortcomings.
