_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, it really made me feel like I was back in the PS2 era. I only have 1 minor problem, the game is too easy to 100% and there's not a whole lot to do after beating every side challenge and story mission. Then again the price tag was $30 so I can't complain. I hope these developers use the money earned from this to make a true modern Destroy All Humans game with more of everything that was in this game.Graphics 8/10: This game looks surprisingly good and not just in comparison to the original. Explosion effects look really good, and everything isn't realistic but just detailed enough to give off that feeling. The only mixed part is the human characters. The only 2 alien characters look so nice and fit in but the human character models look like exaggerated caricatures where as the original had a more realistic look. Either you love it or hate it, I personally love it because the dialogue is intentionally exaggerated so now the look matches the tone.Story 7/10: (Not much spoilers, everything I'm saying here you find out in the opening sequence so please look away if you atleast want to jump in not knowing a single detail)--The story I really like, it's pretty simple and straight to the point since the mindless destruction is the main course. The story is from the perspective of 2 aliens known as Furons looking to invade earth. The protagonist being Crypto-137. The story starts with Crypto's clone 136  being captured by humans on a scouting mission. They have found a way to become immortal through cloning but their DNA is degrading over time so they're looking into Earth because humans have an ancient Furon gene deep in their DNA. (This implies they made humans long ago to farm them, it's kind of dark and funny when you think about it). The rest of the game is what the title implies. Starting slow with throwing comes to finding yourself at war with the US Government.Audio, 8/10: The audio has been remastered for weapons, explosions, but the dialogue wasn't touched at all. They left that untouched. I think it's because the other alien named Pox was voiced by Richard Horvitz which if you don't know was the same person who voiced Zim in Invader Zim. Once you know this it is very hard to not hear Zim's voice when Pox talks. He's a top rated actor and I think they chose not to chanage the dialogue because there's no replacing him. But that does come at a minor cost. See the audio is very slow paced, fits in with a PS2 game but in this they made cutscenes try to match up with the audio. So you'll have awkward cutscenes where there's action. 1 quick example so you know what I'm talking about, there's a scene where Crypto gets knocked onto his butt, he makes a snazzy insult at some soldiers and the sound effect of him picking up his gun is like 10-15 seconds after that insult so he's animated to awkwardly look at the soldiers and he casually walks to his gun with no one shooting at him with such a big window to do so. This happens a lot, and keep in mind the first game came out when Metal Gear 3 was barely setting a new standard for video game filmography but like the human designs you either like it or don't. It feels very old school so you'll appreciate that if you're into that. Gameplay 9/10: This is the bread and butter of why people love this series. It's a 3rd person shooter where destruction is the only point of playing. I wish there were more games like this because the last total destruction game I remember playing was Prototype. You start with almost nothing and the game slowly gives you new abilities, upgrades, and weapons as you progress. You have telekinetic abilities, throw people around, throw a cow at a human, crush them with a car too. You can make people's heads explode to harvest their brains. You get a jetpack for more mobility. You have 4 weapons and a flying saucer that can crush cities.The big improvements they made I love. They changed a lot. You now have a dash ability and with the right upgrade you have access to S.K.A.T.E which is just hover boots to move faster and feel fun to use in combat. You can mix telekenisis with skate and weapons. In the original skate wasn't a thing and you can only do 1 thing at a time. If you fly with your jetpack you couldn't shoot, if you were lifting something with your telekenisis you couldn't fly or shoot. In the remake you can do multiple of these giving you more ways to approach enemies. They also added minor things like picking up rockets and grenades mid air to throw them back. The saucer had a button that works like a parry, pressed at the right time can send missles right back to whoever shot it. Boss battles were revamped and built from the ground up to work with these new features and mechanics too. They don't have the same attacks as before. They also got very creative with the boss fights like the final boss. Before the final boss you did fight a 50 foot robot and the same robot's remains are on the final boss arena. During this fight the giant robot uses his chest blast to scortch the entire area so you have to take cover to avoid damage. I loved that detail and it was never in the original game. The final boss in the original didn't have a lot of complex attacks because of limitations like player mobility so they went all in with this boss jumping around the arena, using cover, it was so fast past compared to the original. My biggest problem with gameplay is because this is a remake they didn't add in as much as they could have, they only added in what the devs couldn't at the time because of limitations with the tech. There's only 4 guns, so although they added what they could to make it feel like a proper remake it still feels like there isn't as much as there could have been. At the same time after beating the story it is so easy to go back and 100% the game. I'm not saying the game is lacking in content, it has plently for a $30 game but I am saying it feels like they could have done so much more. But what it does have I would recommend this game if you just want to switch off your brain and have mindless fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original game. Dev's, to there credit, did a great job of remaking it for modern systems, but they've also made a few radical changes and pretty much every update, change or improvement they made was either poorly executed, or unbalanced the game in some way. For instance, let's start with character models. When they updated to graphics, the devs decided to go for a more cartoonish look for the human NPCs, and I actually agree that this was the right move. Destroy all Humans is a silly game, and going for photo realistic look just wouldn't work. Problem is, they took it a bit too far. NPCs don't look cartoonish, they look like characteratures of cartoons, and bottom line, they're just really ugly. The rest of the world is gorgeous, just not the NPCsAnother example is the grinding.  In the original game, every so often, you would have grind for brain stems (basically the games currency) to continue the plot. This was a determent to the original game so I happy they removed it. Problem is, the grinding served a purpose. You didn't turn in those brain stems, you got to keep them to spend on upgrades. The brain stem grind was there to make sure you were properly prepared for the next level. You still have to grind for upgrades, in fact you have to grind more because the dev's added a bunch of NEW upgrades.  The only difference is that you decide when it's time to grindSpeaking of those upgrade. let's talk about the dash ability, and more specifically, the zero friction upgrade. This at first glance is a great QOL upgrade. One of the week game play points of the original game was how long it took to get from one point to another. even with the jetpack, the game really suffered without a dash or sprint ability. The Dash and slide upgrades are a great improvement, but the Problem is, the zero friction upgrade lets you run literal circles around enemies. With a bit of practice, you're pretty much unhitable, and since you can use your weapons and powers freely while sliding, you can mow through wave's of soldiers and majestic agent like they are nothing.But even without the zero friction upgrade, the game's just too easy now. NPCs with guns attacks are slower and easier to dodge. They took away the psychic majestic agent's ability to nullify you own psychic powers. Tanks can now be thrown via telekinesis just as easily as cars, which pretty much negates any threat they would have posed to you.  I'll admit, the original game could be frustrating at times, but the challenge was enjoyable for the most part. the remake has no challenge whatsoever, and no challenge, for me at least, means no replayability Overall, the games a good remake, but It just isn't as good as the original. I'm hoping take the mistakes they made to heart with Destroy All Humans 2. They really did try

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans takes place in an alternate universe where the practical medical uses for opium were never discovered, therefore many drugs such as morphine were never conceived. Because of this discovery... or lack thereof, war casualties were much higher than they are in our timeline but more importantly, the famous Romanian actor known for his role as Dracula, Bela Lugosi, never had an opportunity to become dependent on the drug morphine. Of course his sciatica neuritis would give him pain until the day he died, but it would not however kill him... unlike the morphine did.The timelines seem to be pretty similar, with Bela making many of the same mistakes he would have in our timeline, like turning down the role of Frankenstein's monster for the film Frankenstein adapted from the famous Mary Shelley novel Frankenstein, and Boris Karloff would still become immensely famous for the role of Frankenstein's monster in Frankenstein. This would leave Bela fading away into obscurity, until he would later meet up with the one, the only, Edward D. Wood.For those unaware, Ed Wood is known to be one of the worst film directors of all time, directing such anti-classics as "Glen or Glenda", "Bride of the Monster", and most famously of all; "Plan 9 From Outer Space". They are films to be enjoyed with your friends drunk on your ass on weekends, and for that Mr. Wood, I am grateful. Mr. Lugosi would star in all of these films, but as we know in our own reality, he unfortunately passed away during the filming of Plan 9. But in this alternate reality, Lugosi lives and stars as the antagonist of Plan 9, splitting our timelines in two, forever. You might think that in this alternate reality that Plan 9 is a good movie, yes? No... it's just as bad, in fact, it's even worse. But people saw the movie, and noticed the man they knew from Dracula, and people loved it. Loved it so much in fact, that they wanted a sequel. Ed Wood got to filming the sequel right away, and when it released it was also a hit. So they made more sequels, and more, and more and more and more. And each was worse than the last. Eventually there were 33 Plans from outer space, leaving us with the latest entry in Ed Wood's (s)hit franchise, "Plan 42 From Outer Space".And that's where our story as Crypto-137 begins. The Furons noticed all these horrendous works of film and wanted to put to a stop to it. How would they do it? Well, by destroying all humans of course. They could not for the lives of them bare to see a "Plan 43 From Outer Space" be excreted out into the universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much spent my entire time playing trying very hard to convince myself that this was good. I desperately wanted this game to be good, this and the second game were some of my favourite games growing up and still are. Biggest problem- the upgrade system. The original game had one, but in what I'm guessing is an attempt to "modernize" the game, the remake has expanded on it drastically. Every single weapon and ability has 3-4 upgrade tier, with some of them having two upgrade tree, with 3-4 each tree. As a result, ALL your weapons and abilities start out garbage. So you play for a while, upgrading what you can, until VERY quickly the upgrades are costing easily 7000 DNA an upgrade. The problem being, side quests, at minimum, give you 200, and at best 1000. Main quests now have tacked on side objectives, and even if you complete them all perfectly, you get maybe 2500. And remember, your grinding to upgrade about a dozen trees, who's cap stones are 7000, let alone the early upgrade to even unlock the capstone. So you streamline your play for the most DNA possible, you only play using methods that can extract the most DNA while doing the missions (some side quests leave you unable to collect DNA, like destroying the buildings in the saucer, which has it's own issue= you can't complete the armageddon missions until you upgrade your saucer to a level that you physically HAVE the firepower to not just fail the mission, and when you do, I hope you enjoy another mission you can grind over and over again for a grand total of 200 DNA. Long story short- While it is easy to become overpowered, side quests, main missions, hell, even just running around extracting people DNA, does nothing to help you collecting DNA faster, it becomes an absolute slog and it stops being fun very quickly. Another problem is focusing. In the original (or the second one when they introduced transmoging objects to turn into ammo), you had to focus specifically on something to transmog it, the same with scanning, TKing and extracting DNA from people. In this remake, both are tied to the same button with no need to focus, and hopefully it targets the thing you want it to. Example being- your up against a group of soldiers and you try to DNA extract one to help solve the problem, the game gets confused and starts transmoging a hitherto unknown piece of wood on the floor, and you get killed. Yes, there is a lock-on button for enemies, but that's different. When the new engine contains extra bits that can now be transmoged for ammo, it's not helpful if the game doesn't necessarily target what you're looking at.Aiming itself seems to be a problem in some regards- the chain lighting gun can branch off of one target to another to another so on and so fourth. Many times i would aim at someone, only for the beam to curve completely around them and hit something else entire that wasn't the problem i was trying to deal with.In trying to recreate the power fantasy of the original, the developers of the remake have made you both over powered (in the original getting the max wanted level when majestic came to play was very quickly a death sentence, whereas now they're more of an annoyance to your latest brain harvesting spree you've been forced to go on), as well as under rewarded, with low amounts of DNA points given and overly expensive upgrade.Side note- I'm pretty sure in the original, when it came to extracting DNA/Brains, you had a random chance of getting extra DNA, IE most people would give 25, some would give 50, majestic agents would give usually 75 and the psychic soldiers would ALWAYS give 100 DNA, which is why they were so tough to fight. I may be mis-remembering, but in the remake, every one give 25 and the psychic lads give 50. I think the devs definitely  need look at the balancing for the upgrade system VS the mission reward system.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! is a really great sandbox action game and a game that lovingly captures the feel of classic 50 sci-fi movies, now to tell you the truth I've never played the original game so I don't know how this game compares to the original other than the change in graphics, so I won't really talk about if this remake is better than the original. So the story.The Furon Empire are a supreme intergalactic conquerors with Incredible psychic powers that have been conquering worlds for centuries, but at a cost. Reckless use of atomic weaponry had completely destroyed their ability to procreate, the only thing that saved their species from extinction was their cloning technology, but now even cloning has become incredibly unstable. But luckily they've discovered that long ago their ancestors went to a little planet called Earth and mingled with the primitive human life forms to the point that now deep within the human brain is a small uncorrupted piece of Furon DNA, it is now up to Crypto to go to Earth and harvest brains in order to save his species and continue the glorious Furon Empire.Now the likes, the gameplay is really good with a mixture of combat, exploration and stealth, all the while using a good variety of psychic powers and weapons as well as a spaceship with a variety of destructive powers. I mean getting to go around killing humans, removing their brains or flying around with your spaceship and destroying buildings is quite enjoyable, there is also plenty of upgrades for your character and your ship giving you access to more destructive power. Also the gameplay does have some variety so not to get repetitive with stealth missions and destroying certain objects and when you completely clear a level there are plenty of little challenges and collectibles you can do that allow you to unlock artwork which was a nice incentive to keep playing the game. The powers and weapons that you use are good the powers like reading minds and lifting up objects or even taking on human form were fun to use, especially the levitation powers making enemies and cars go up in the air and use them as projectiles was fun as hell. The weapons you have were cool and fun to use especially when upgraded to their maximum, like your classic disintegrator ray and the more unique weapon the Alien Probe that allows you to rip brains out of people's butts.The story is really good very well written with a great balance of comedy, satire and badassness as you play this evil alien and if you're a fan or have some knowledge of classic Sci-fi b movies then there's plenty of references you'll get to see. The characters are very good and very well written even some of the side characters were very good, I especially enjoyed the two agents that you see in some parts of the game I loved their banter, I also especially loved the banter between Crypto and Pox they both played off of each other really well one being a sarcastic Mastermind and the other being a sarcastic killing machine.The graphics are really good, incredibly colorful with amazing scenery and an atmosphere that really captures the feel of an exaggerated fifties. The levels are very good quite detailed and diverse from a farm land, to a small town to even the capital, it was all really good and quite interesting to look at and explore finding all the little details that makes the world feel alive.The voice acting is really good with some voice actors you're definitely going to recognize from previous works; even the NPCs have good voice acting you can tell all them really brought their a game. The comedy was quite good while it wasn't laugh out loud, it was quite chuckle worthy, the humor mostly steming from the writing and satire with some use of using of visual gags and playing with classic B movie tropes. The music was very good and fitted well with the whole sci-fi B movie feel of the game.Now the dislikes, the game could have used some more bosses instead of the three we got to fight, they're also should have been two more achievements for the game, one achievement for collecting all the little probes throughout each of the levels and an achievement for 100% each of the levels. I also would have liked the remake to include the original game as an unlockable, also I wish the game had controller mapping.Okay with that said Destroy All Humans! is a really great sandbox action game and a game that lovingly captures the feel of classic 50 sci-fi movies, with a lot to love from the really good gameplay, really good story and very good characters.So if you're looking for a game that lets you play as a villain and if you like good satire and enjoyable gameplay I highly recommend getting this game, I also like to thank my friend for getting me this game you rock.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans (2020) is a from-the-ground-up remake of the PS2-era cult classic of the same name. This is a relatively ‘safe’ remake, meaning the developers have changed as little as possible from the original, though cut content has been added where appropriate. While its age may show with its simplicity and certain design choices, this third-person alien chaos simulator still manages to be a ton of fun, helped by its light-hearted tone, a great variety of destructive tools, and its quality over quantity approach to content. Breaking from the tradition of most save-the-world-type experiences we see today where you play as the saviour of Earth, Destroy All Humans places you in the shoes of Crypto-137, an alien seeking revenge on the inhabitants of Earth for capturing his brother. Think John Wick except the guy they just annoyed has zero sympathy for the entire race that wronged him. This simple goal gives your chaos a purpose, and even though this sounds like a setup for an alien invasion film you’ve seen before, it feels surprisingly unique as a video game since there are not too many linear experiences where you play as the undisputed bad guy. The writing is surprisingly funny, portraying Crypto as a spiteful force to be reckoned with, and conversely presenting the humans as incredibly gullible creatures who believe communism is responsible for Crypto’s existence. Further context is delivered through a series of mostly enjoyable, short and sweet cutscenes that occur within and between some of the levels. However, the transitions to these certainly show this game’s age, as they sometimes occurred without warning after you’ve reached an objective, which I found to break the momentum of the experience, especially as the narrative mostly takes a backseat here. Combat is split into two modes: on-foot playing as Crypto, and in the air flying a UFO. You’ll be on the ground most of the time, using Crypto’s array of weapons and telekinetic abilities to achieve the goal set out by the game’s title. You can chain shock multiple humans using a lightning gun, disintegrate them with a jacked-up ray gun, and fire incredibly volatile projectiles which can be thrown to create devastating explosions. Crypto can also throw any living organism and object in the environment, and both this and his weapons can be used almost simultaneously for maximum effect. There’s not much variety here, but what is on offer creates a very fun and gratifying power fantasy, helped by satisfying audio feedback from the weapons, and the hilarious reactions of your victims. Crypto can also move about by jetpacking, and can perform an endless skating manoeuvre which is equal parts a useful, fun, and unique method of traversing each environment. All of the above and your UFO can be upgraded by collecting currency from completing missions and killing humans by affecting them with an ability which primes their brains to be consumed. UFO combat is similarly basic but still plenty of fun. You’ve got your standard destruction beam, a powerful sonic boom attack, and the ability to drop mini-nukes onto the world below. The enemies, combat vehicles, and surface-to-air missiles that stand in your way don’t pose much of a threat until later on, so it is pretty easy most of the time, but this isn’t necessarily a bad thing. Not every game has to be super challenging to be fun, and Destroy All Humans smartly recognized that disrupting its power fantasy by weakening your destructive capabilities would have been a poor move. The campaign takes place across 23 missions which are launched from a mothership-themed menu. These are split between six open environments, all of which have a simple but distinct theme ranging from a farm to a classified alien research facility, and the objectives you have to complete are typically focused on a small part of one of these areas. After finishing your first mission in each zone, you are able to freely roam that world to complete some exclusive activities, or simply destroy as much of the area as you’d like to. There’s good variety here; you’re not just causing carnage throughout all of them, as you’ll sometimes be required to kidnap a target stealthily or infiltrate a guarded facility to gain some important information for Crypto’s quest. You’ll make use of the ‘holobob’ ability in a few of these assignments; this allows you to take on the appearance of any human on the map and walk around without raising suspicion. Whilst this does slow the game down significantly, I liked the change of pace that these offered most of the time. However, tedium set in during a couple of missions where the holobob ability was required whilst following a slow-walking human, as these don’t give you much to do while waiting. I also found it a bit frustrating that completing an objective’s requirements would sometimes cause the mission to instantly end, even during the middle of chaotic battles for no good reason. This could have been fixed by asking you to exfiltrate the area by reaching your UFO, and the small size of the maps means this wouldn’t have become repetitive for me.There are four types of hub-area activities, each focusing on a particular element of the game, and reward you with one to three stars based on your performance. Races require the fully upgraded SKATE ability and ask you to follow a probe to collect dropped resources from it as quickly as possible. Armageddon activities give you more opportunities to be rewarded for destroying the environment with your UFO. Both of these follow an identical format per hub-world, but remain consistently enjoyable as a result of their low quantity. Abduction activities require you to pick up a particular category of object and throw them into the tractor beam, ranging from humans to household objects, and Rampages ask you to kill lots of organisms as fast as possible, ranging from civilians to special agents, and even cows in one instance. These are all really simple, but absolutely feel worth checking out after you finish the campaign if you’re looking for more to do. It took me around seven hours to complete the campaign, completing all of the bonus objectives per mission along the way, and an additional two hours to clear up the remaining achievements. There are a series of collectable probes hidden throughout each of the maps, but obtaining all of these is not required to collect the achievements, only rewarding a bit of upgrade currency and some concept art for seeking them out. This made completing the game incredibly pleasant, as there were no annoying or repetitive activities that stood in the way of completion, and so the 100% experience is highly recommended. Performance-wise, the game ran at a buttery-smooth 60fps on high settings on my main machine (GTX 1660Ti, Ryzen 7 3700X, 16GB RAM). The ultra settings did not increase visual fidelity to the point where the performance decrease was justified for me. While I never played the original Destroy All Humans, I can easily see why it developed a cult-following as there are not too many mindless experiences that have quite the same setup as this game does. I’d highly recommend it if you’re looking for a straightforward third-person action experience that focuses on gameplay, and provides you with the freedom to endlessly level entire towns and their inhabitants without requiring much effort.Click  for more details about what my review scores mean!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is a great remake of the original and worth the purchase for old fans, but also a great experience for newcomers. The biggest amount of effort has clearly gone into the overhaul of the graphics which are now in a stylised from but this works with the setting and tone of the game and has been done very well, the best evidence of this being the unlockable concept art that shows the original asset from the first game and the redesign next to each other. This effort has not gone to waste and the game's environments and effects look great in-game, simultaneously looking new but not changing things to be unrecognisable compared to the first game. The other main addition are new gameplay mechanics that while not significantly altering the gameplay loop from the original game, are a nice addition for returning players and brings the game up to what modern games are expected to have, like optional objectives, the dash/skate ability, Skins and the Repulse-O-Tron etc. Also worth mentioning is the good support for both controllers and MK+B with the ability to seamlessly switch between the two just by pushing a button on either, which also immediately updates the HUD and prompts. Personally I find the controller the best given that's how I played the original, but both are useable.There are downsides of course. In technical terms the cutscenes are a bit lacklustre with an often noticeable lack of ambient sound or score that makes things awkward, and the lipsyncing  in these scenes can sometimes appear off? I'm quite paranoid about audio and video being out of sync, so this may just be me. While no means bad, the audio effects in gameplay also seem a little less punchy than they should be, but this is very minor. Also annoying is the saucer gameplay in the new game. Mainly, the most noticeable issue is the rather low ceiling for the saucer which was obviously present in the original as well, but because the graphics are much more detailed and there are no technical limitations to justify it, it becomes more noticeable. The Repulse-O-Tron I also found difficult given the relatively small size of maps and the ability to lose the prompts in the chaos of destruction which pairs badly with the introduction of the drain mechanic for recharging the saucer's shields into the remake. Also, as far as I can tell the extras from the original game have been dropped which is a shame but hardly a turn off for the game.Ultimately the development team deserves as much kudos for what it hasn't done for what they have done. Namely, they have NOT dropped any of the dialogue or altered the tone at all and deserve praise for this decision. The game's tone and parody of 1950s America is undoubtedly the best aspect of the game and soul of its experience, and being able to experience it as an adult and actually UNDERSTAND the references and jokes is honestly one of the best parts of the remake. They have also amplified this tone by writing the Furon Handbook entries in the same tone and style.In conclusion, this game is a fantastic remake and should be upheld as an example for future remakes: A complete technical remastering that extends far beyond just updating particle effects and raising texture resolutions, the maintenance of the original's creative content, and the addition of just enough extra mechanics to create a unique experience compared to the original. It has been executed with care and passion, and I heartily recommend it to both old and new players

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Pros:+ 50s setting is awesome+ Bright and colorful graphics+ Enjoyable story mode+ Voice acting is over the top and very enjoyable+ Plenty of upgradesCons:- Repetitive gameplay- Drags a bit towards the end"Long" version: is a third-person action game developed by Black Forest Games and Pandemic Studios and published by THQ Nordic. You follow the adventure of Cryptosporidium-137 in his quest to gather human DNA to save his dying race from extinction, as years of cloning started degrading its DNA.The story does not take itself seriously and is very silly, which I really enjoyed. Crypto is an okay protagonist, as he is unashamedly cold and apathetic towards humans, but his demeanor is a bit one-note, as it never really changes. It does work for the story, however. The other characters are just caricatures of real life political figures or stereotypes of 50s tropes, like the bimbo blonde with an exaggerated accent, the dimwitted farmer that mistakes the protagonist for an ugly wild animal or the idiotic FBI agents/army men that are terrible at their job. It does not come across as mean-spirited, however – more like self-deprecating humor.I felt like the story had a strong start but slowly lost steam, especially towards the end of the campaign.Gameplay shines in .You have two different types of gameplay – on foot, where you use Crypto, and you can also use your spaceship to fly around.Crypto controls well, as you have a wide array of deadly weapons and movement abilities. Each weapon has strengths and weaknesses and it was enjoyable to scroll through all of them and dispose of humansby the hundreds. Your abilities provide much needed versatility to your arsenal, as you will be able to fly around with your jetpack, slide across the map at high speed and lift enemies up with telekinesis and yeet them across the environment and against each other, for example. There are also several abilities that allow you to engage in a bit of stealth gameplay, which is nice.The flying saucer controls are okay, but I felt the game did not offer much in terms of variety when it came to spaceship missions. You usually just have to destroy everything – enemy forces and buildings – and cause as much mayhem as possible. While not necessarily bad, it did grow boring.You can upgrade your arsenal with a considerable number of upgrades, but most of them felt like basic stat boosts that did not change my approach to gameplay.My main problem with the gameplay only came up later, near the last third of the story - it grew repetitive. Pair that up with the story’s lack of focus I mentioned above and everything starts feeling same-y and uninspired.Graphically,  looks awesome.The color palette is vibrant, character models look silly (definitely intentional) and you get to explore different areas of the US with diverse biomes, citizens and enemies. Even the loading screens have a lot of personality and charm, which I really appreciated.Both the soundtrack and the sound effects are great. The voice acting is a lot of fun, as it leans into the cheesiness of the premise and makes fun of the humans.While I did not care much for the last third of the campaign and the side content (mission challenges) was very repetitive, I did enjoy . Overall, I think it is a fine game. It embodies the best aspects of early 2000s games, though it occasionally shows some of their flaws. It provides 10-15 hours of pulpy fun. While I feel like its base asking price is a bit steep, I totally recommend getting it on sale. The game plays well, has a strong art direction and does not take itself seriously.Final score: 8 out of 10.If you enjoyed this review, please consider following my .

_childDocuments_.review: Maxed this on Xbox and there are a lot of welcomed changes but there are some unwelcomed ones too. First off, the insta-death from touching water from the original game has been addressed here, you now get a chance to get out of the water before you die, thank you! Secondly, I love the jetpack changes, it's more versatile which I love. The cut content from the very original because of the space problem back in the days of PS2 like the missing 'independence day' like death Ray from the underside of your UFO is welcomed and the missing mission that had to be cut too. Healing your saucer by using humans and vehicles for their health is a great idea they took from the OG Destroy all Humans 2 idea of 'transmogging' if I'm not mistaken. Now, to the unwelcomed things I didn't like starting with the style of the graphics. Although back in the day there were limitations on the graphics, they still tried their best to resemble realism with their towns, people and vehicles but with this remaster they've gone down a more silly and goofy look to match the story and goofy gameplay but I'm just not a fan of it. Some line's and conversations along with animations aren't quite in line with how they were presented in the original and it's a little off putting and weird. Moving back to the visuals, the blood from the cows has been removed and the brains from humans that you collect are now glowing with green radiation or something which I don't like as well as the DNA points you get being the same amount whether the humans are dead or alive when you remove the brain which in the original, the brain was worth more when the victim was alive and halved when they're dead. I'm also not a fan of the telekinesis, it was done a lot better back in the day and it was fun throwing people up in the air to watch them fall to their death and hear the bones crack. I might have missed some things or forgotten some things, good and bad but they're just a few. Anyway, I love the work THQ has done here and keeping the original voice lines front he original and used them here is an absolute brilliant move by them, thank you so much for that. I highly recommend this game if you played the old one and to new players, you'd probably fall in love with this version. A definite ne 8 out of 10 for me!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like how they made a remake of just the first one, it wasn't even the best one compared to others. It would have been better just to make a new entry to the series with new weapons and everything. But since they didn't do that, I'd be almost expectant of them to remake the others too.The graphics also kinda suck. Everything is super saturated with bloom and god rays (which I turned off later in the .ini files) and the new models for characters are kinda sucky. Crypto himself looks more like a celebrity recast with a facelift, which might be a good bit of irony, but he still had way more character on the PS2 because the jagged angles complemented his iconic evil smile, while here you can't even tell what he's thinking with that glossed over glare. The other humans were given a more cartoony caricature look too, which I think they did later on to make them fit into the higher resolution environment. They might have overdone it a bit though. The animation in cutscenes sucks, a lot of it was smoothed over to try to make it feel more 'natural' I guess but everyone just moves at the same speed no matter what emotion is being portrayed. In the PS2 version, you actually see Crypto have an angry breakdown in front of pox in the intro cutscene. Here, he just turns his head like he's pacing and the camera cuts a lot to make you think he's moving. One last final bit, a lot of audio was just taken out of the original game, so that also hurts the cruddy animation a bit, but they also had to bring Invader Zim himself back for more bonus mission dialogue, so you'll have some weird shifts in fidelity. He also sounds a bit old or tired to be doing the iconic voice anymore, so sometimes he'd do the flamboyant emphasis but squeak it out and it just made me feel kinda bad for him and want to give him a break. No disrespect to his career of course, he still did a decent job.So in terms of graphics, it's a pretty bad remake, but with gameplay, it's actually a pretty good upgrade from the original. Moving Crypto around in PS2 Land was like dragging around a garbage bag while drunk, and you could only ever fire your weapon and move at the most. Here Crypto gets to do all the cool dynamic movement and jumping he really deserved, and you can pick up a guy with TK and toss him at a tank while firing and ridding your jetpack through the air all at once and it's amazing, as it should be. A lot of weapons were reworked to be better but worse in parts though. The Zap-o-matic gets a huge upgrade, but it's now the only weapon I'd use half the time as it just became a DPS lazer with infinite ammo, and the Disintegrator ray just became this thing that shot heat seeking fireballs (how even) as opposed to the cool plasma gun from Doom 16 type thing it was. The Probe should have been removed all together, that's all. I think the Ion Detonator got nerfed, but I can't remember what it was originally like. Now it's this weird charge up distance thing that only goes half as far as it did, but you can still manually detonate it so that's cool. The saucer weapons are worse. The death ray is pretty much just the Zap-o-matic taped to the front of the Saucer, so it ends up being more flashy than it is an actual DEATH RAY. Neither the death ray or the Sonic Boom can take down a building any quicker than like 10 seconds, even with full upgrades, so you can't level half the town anymore in a few minutes like you could on the PS2. There's also way more stuff that attacks you in the saucer, like missiles which are nearly impossible to reflect in time given the game's default crappy FOV. I also don't get why they didn't add in the cloak for your saucer, just to give you a break from all the missiles.Either way, it's still a fun game. Go kill em all!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first remaster in a while where I actually played the game growing up, so I was excited to see how much justice this remaster does to the original. Thankfully it does one hell of a job. This game is notorious for its humour, and the devs didn't hold back by censoring content. There's a warning at the start, describing that times were different but they wanted to keep the old content in which is highly respectable because a lot of snowflakes will probably cry about it. The newspaper transitions are especially brilliant, the headlines are always hilarious. Something I didn't experience as a kid was the ending of the game as I never beat it growing up.  Something I noticed in the intro cutscene was that Crypto's voice is way different, I'm not sure if it's a matter of original audio vs remastered or if the voice actor put on an accent and then scrapped it. Either way the intro cutscene plays out completely differently to the rest of the narration which is a little strange. One of my biggest annoyances with this remaster is that there's no restart checkpoint feature. There's only the option to restart the whole mission which is pretty useless. When doing the optional challenges I found myself just suiciding in order to restart, and this could have been easily streamlined with a restart checkpoint button on the menu. Speaking of optional challenges, I completed them all just to realise that the relevant achievements are bugged and won't unlock which was quite disappointing. Seems like a fix is nowhere to be found. + humour (newspaper transitions)+ didn't censor the original+ boss fights - checkpoint system- bugged achievements Rating - 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: There's challenges, side-missions, equipment-upgrades to grind for, and a campaign. But that campaign is just extremely basic and cliché, and doesn't really offer much of anything... Honestly, all you do the entire game is play around with your gear and kill humans/buildings. That's why Destroy All Humans is best described as a Sandbox. This gameplay can be fun at times, but will get very repetitive. The campy nature of the game did give me a few chuckles here and there, though at the same time it can get  cringy as well. Overall, the entertainment is just too short-lived, campy and limited. I feel like there isn't much reason to keep playing. Well, except for maybe finishing the campaign and achievements if you're a completionist (like I did).I also want to note 2 other flaws I came across. NPC's are just copied and pasted way too much, causing you to come across the exact same farmer/wife/whatever and their quips hundreds of times in the same mission. Also, I found the psychokinesis ability to be rather finicky and non-reliable. When I want to throw a target into another, it often just drops it mid-air like a limp ragdoll, hardcore face-slams it into the ground, or just plain yeets it off far into the distance.So even though Destroy All Humans can offer some fun moments and has decent gameplay, the game's basic and repetitive nature, extremely campy campaign and real lack of purpose keeps me from recommending it.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! is a remake of 2005 game and it's very close to original in many aspects. At the same time game looks amazing and (almost) perfectly polished.We play as an evil alien named Crypto-137 in 1950's USA (with all essential stereotypes included). Each mission takes place in a half-open location and is conventionally non-linear in most cases, but there is no great freedom of action either. There's a lot of hilarious cinematics that are mixed with gameplay sequences - humor is definitely the strongest part of the game. Unreal Engine 4 works great here and I've encountered only one issue with performance on one of the last bosses (RoboPres) where I had to reduce graphic setting to low to avoid weird lagspikes on phase 2-3 (definitely not a PC FPS issue). Every other technical aspect of the game was just great.It took me 6,5 hours to complete campaign with a majority of achievements and I suppose it would take another 3 hours to complete all the rest. There's next to no replayability beside completing achievements and a couple of additional challenges.  gameplay is a little bit awkward in some moments, because it kept most of original mechanics and I constantly had a nostalgic feeling that I'm playing an old game (not exactly 2005's original but old game in general). It was a good feeling most of the times but some mechanics looked too outdated and some actions that are supposed to be fun were kinda generic/boring.All in all,  is a great remake of a hilarious game that definitely won't disappoint people who played original game and wanted to experience it again while it could also entertain new players. 8/10

I think I remembered this game so fondly was because I was a young babby child and it was one of the only few games I had. Idk, you should get this if you're feeling nostalgic. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's amazing to see how much was redone and for it to still have the soul of the original. For $30, no doubt it's something you should pick up.I normally play through the first or second games each year. This is a whole-hearted, great recreation of the first game.Most the missions and all the cutscences are exactly the way they were, some had more level and objectives added.The new mission that didn't make it into the original, Mission 13.5, Yes. The audio is from the PS2 era, but it is serviceable for how great the actors are in their performances.Now the gameplay, the real meat here. The PK is an improvement over the focus meter but not having the full control over the object/person in terms of distance, height, and flailing of the people is kind of a let down. Now they are full on projectiles. It losses some of the levitation charm for more usefulness in the offensive.Zap-O-Matic - With the really nice upgrade system that was added, this will be one of your mains in cutting down the masses in how powerful it gets.Disintegrator-Ray - More of a single target weapon that can take them out in a few shots.Probe - Instead of having a charge up or ammo in the second game, it uses timing. Still unlimited like in the first, but faster. Ion Detonator - Fires a fat ball that explodes in a bigger, more satisfying boom and can now be PK'ed in a direction. I recommend not getting one of the upgrades that slows time, it's not good at all and just disrupts the action.The saucer also got some major improvements including: smother flight control, drastically better way of replenishing ammo as well as shields, and not having a load time between on-foot to air assault.Ending thoughtsCan't wait to see what's to come if there is a complete rendition of the second title.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect demonstration of what a $30 game should provide. I have a bit of history with the Destroy All Humans games. I played a bit of the first game, and then played the hell out of the sequels. That said it's been so long I barely remember the series. To that end, I want to review the experience of what I just played, rather than the quality of the remaking process. Simply put, the game was satisfying in all aspects. Interacting with the various weapons, the saucer combat, the numerous upgrades, the free-roam options, the game works and it's hella fun. The story is also great! Since this was a game made in 2005, it reflects the mindset of the people that time. At the same time, it was also before the current period of taboos and sacred cows. It is genuinely satisfying to play a game this engaging, that truly does not care about your offense. Sometimes I want a game that cares about social implications and historic strife. Other times I want all caution to the wind. I'd like to be in a world where both options are freely taken, and no one option is socially mandated to be the norm. Also whatever option the game devs feel is the most fun to create- and I 100% believe the folks who made this game had a blast! The ultimate meter to measure the game is on the price tag. Models are constantly reused. The guns, while varied, are few. You are going to hear many lines repeated ad nauseam. Plus you're absolutely going to encounter bugs, or the occasional difficult spike. $40+ or higher would be absurd for such an experience. I believe $30 is right on the nose, but maybe wait for any sale. I hope to see Destroy All Humans! come back as a modern series with new entries. There's many new gameplay options that can be attacked, and a whole new world to mock.So long as the Devs have courage and never bend the knee.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely faithful to the original, which was so good on its own, I had to buy this game when it came out.  I was not sure what to expect but from the vary first scenes of the game, I was blown away by the graphics.  After first landing in the woods next to the farm, I just could not stop myself from focusing on the graphics around me.  With the trees covering the area in shade, the rustling grass, and the sheer vibrancy of the scene was just something I could not get past.Far from being realistic, the art style matches perfectly with the graphics of the game.  Stunning landscapes stretch way into the distance, making you wonder how far you can go.  The game makers gave it a great depth of scale, enticing you to explore far and wide but also usually showing you clearly where you do not want to explore.  The vast landscape is a great way to not have true "walls" while still containing the player to the main areas of the levels.I get so caught up by the graphics, that I keep forgetting the game-play.  Flying around with a jetpack, shooting people with lightning guns, sending them flying through the air, using your mind to pick people up and use them as a floating human shield, there is a huge amount of opportunities to combine your special abilities for some really fun situations.  One of my favorites, that I discovered really late in the game, with the skating ability.  I don't know how I missed this but it just added a whole new depth of hilarious ways to Destroy All Humans!Great game, with lots of funny jokes, some witty dialogue, and a unique take on 1950's era/present day era culture mashed together.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I didn’t care much for the original in 2005. I think I played it for an hour or so before abandoning it. It just didn’t resonate with me. 17 years later I got this one in a bundle and decided to give it another try. And to my surprise it is a solid and to this day pretty unique game. The mix between 3rd-person-shooting, stealth missions, all-out-rampage UFO-action and kinda funny cutscenes was good enough to make me finish the ~8 hours long campaign. In six hub-worlds across the USA consisting of backwater areas, several cities and secret military bases you go to war with all of humanity.The 23 main missions are linear with fixed objectives, still leaving some room for creativity with an interesting pool of weapons and skills at your hand that can be upgraded between missions. For example you can disguise as humans, control them to a certain degree or use telekinesis to manipulate matter. All in all the mission design is varied, but I didn’t enjoy the stealth missions as much as the action mission. Blowing up stuff is certainly the most fun you will have in this game. Gladly most of the game is about that. During the course of the game you will also unlock side missions in the hub worlds that add further challenge and volume to the game. Just don’t expect some cutting edge action game. Everything feels a bit unpolished and janky, but never too much to get in the way of the fun. It’s a good remake, especially the graphics and controls got a huge overhaul to make this feel like a modern game. This also runs pretty okay on the Steam Deck after fiddling around with some settings. But even on my PC the performance wasn’t always that great with some stuttering and frame drops here and there (ultra-settings @1440p on RTX 2070 Super). Still, I am actually surprised how much effort they put into this remake instead of just releasing an upscaled remaster. Some other publishers should take note.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Destroy All Humans was one of my favourite games of the 6th console generation, it was a stupid amount of fun, with so many memorable moments and with an engaging atmosphere.However I won't lie when I say it's dated compared to Modern Third Person Shooters from today, it's still a lot of fun, however I was looking forward to this remake a lot, wow it delivered big time.This review isn't going into much as the game as it's own, but more on the fact it's one of if not the best remake I've ever played.New controls for Crypto and the saucer, allowing for more intense gameplay since you can now use PK and your weaponry together, and the saucer can now swap weapons quickly for fast mayhem.Game looks fantastic, the new visuals and new details the devs added are great, like when the Farmer's wife comes out to find the Farmer on the first mission, only to see a grey smug face looking at her with her husband under his feet are very welcome.Has the classic music and voice acting from the original game, they haven't been replaced.Has a new Dash and Skate ability for Crypto, a very welcome power up, giving new mobility options for in and out of combat.The added cut mission is fun as well and fits into the game perfectly, if you told a new player it was originally not in the first game, it would shock them.Has a new skin system which allows you to customize CryptoNew side challenges during missions for extra DNA and special skins.The grind is nowhere as bad as the original game.Doesn't replace the original, I don't like it when remakes make their original games near or completely obsolete, like the Crash N-Sane Trilogy and CTR Nitro Fuelled, since there's no reason to go back to the original games for the average Joe since the remakes are just better in nearly every way, however the way this game controls compared to the original is night and day and offers a different gameplay style from each other because of it, which makes me very happy, since I have a reason to play the original besides just for nostalgia's sake.No skins for Saucer or the weapons, which is a massive shame, weapons weren't to be expected anyway, but with Black Forest adding skins for Crypto, a feature from Big Willy Unleashed and Path of the Furon, I was hoping at least the Saucer would get some too, but alas, nope, hopefully a DLC or something down the line gets added.I don't know if it's just me since I know the original game like the back of my hand or the new controls or whatever, but this game was very easy, I remember the original being a lot more harder.While bugs and glitches are rare, I've had the following...1. During the Mission Duck and Cover, I accidentally let a Radioactive cow destroy the escort, when it restarted, I got stuck where the mission would start from the checkpoint, only to be blown up by a cow within seconds, I had to restart.2. On the new/cut mission, there's a part where you need to find 3 officers, 2 are labeled/hinted on the map, the 3rd one isn't and is hiding in a corner with some soldiers.3. I spawned in Rockwell one time and just saw a car fly by, it wasn't stuck, it was flying like it was driving as normal until it touched the floor, then drove of... ok cool...4. During missions where I'm in disguise, stay in stealth and need to talk to a soldier or something, the game would randomly transmog an object BEHIND the person instead, leading me to fail the mission.5. A few texture glitches on some maps where you can see under the map, but these are rare and often nearby the boundaries.I've played many remakes, I've played remakes of many of my favourite games, and i can easily say, without a doubt, this is the best remake I have played, bravo Black Forest Games and THQNordic, hopefully another Destroy All Humans game or Remake is on it's way.

_childDocuments_.review: In essence you run around to "Destroy all humans" in a fantastical universe set in the 50s. You have different "cities" you invade which considering this is a remaster of a game from many years ago that's not super surprising but it helps give a nice open world feel to it, which you didn't get a lot back then. The "loading" time between each area is kind of annoying but that loading time will be more based on your computer than it will be the game itself.In essence you "learn" about the humans along the way by doing various things and studying to slowly work your way to end-game plot, at which you fight what I would define as a "broken" last boss due to the fact the game forces you to actually go back to some places to play the "challenges" and/or you have to buy very specific upgrades to make it tolerable and not boring and repetitive. Outside of that one gripe, basically you run around and blast stuff with various weapons, and of course a saucer. The graphics were updated so the explosions and stuff are cooler but does look like they took some fun elements out from the OG, but for the most part still plays like the original. Is it worth it at full price? No. Is it worth it on a 75% or more sale? Most definitely. $30 for an equivalent remaster with less than 15 hrs of gameplay(20 or so if you want all the achievements) isn't really worth it.TLDR: Mini challenges to play, short storyline that's a bit funny and good voice acting, and fulfilling ending after last end-game boss that's broken. Hint. If you do end up getting it, focus on SAUCER upgrades especially on the reflecting ones. So, a little bit of replayability if you're into that kind of thing but it gets boring kinda' quick. Personally not going to sink 5+ more hrs into this just to 100% the game as it requires you to do very time sensitive challenges and it's just not that worthwhile and fulfilling.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans is a fantastic game which I played for the very first time recently.This game was gifted to me by a very good friend and I am glad that they gifted it to me! I actually never even knew that this game existed when I was younger.Everything about Destroy All Humans is perfect; The story is perfect, the gameplay is spotless - no gimmicks, no micro-transactions, no boring grindy repetitive quests.This is a 3rd person game. You play the role of an alien clone created to basically gather information on the humans in order to eventually subjugate them!As you progress through the game, you start to encounter much more difficult enemies. The end boss fight is like a cherry on top.I especially love the little snippets of newpaper articles that reflect on the carnage caused by you as you progress through the game - they make it seem like it's all an accident or some top secret military experiment gone wrong or something.Destroy All Humans isn't really that long, I was able to get through this game + do all the side quests and extra missions in under 20 hours.This game is totally worth it, if you are a fan of great narrative driven single player games. _childDocuments_.review: A faithful recreation of original game from our childhoods, this game is as fun as it was back then with new stunning visuals.I have to say, I'm not typically a fan of remasters as most seem to be shameless cash grabs on our beloved franchises. However, this one has surprised me with just how much love and work has been done to craft a faithful yet fresh-feeling recreation of a beloved game.The gameplay is the soul and heart of this game. Throw everything else out the window, because you will be here to enjoy the fun and wacky combat, the body snatching stealth mechanics, and the UFO saucer combat. This does unfortunately mean that the story suffers quite a bit, with Crypto himself (the protagonist) being the central point of the entire game. Thankfully, Crypto himself is a fun character, hellbent on the destruction of the human race and the harvesting of their genetic DNA. He makes some dated but still funny one-liners but aside from that- don't expect much in the way of character development or story. Pros: - Amazing overhaul of the visuals both with textures and effects.- Very stable on PC having never crashed while playing to 100% completion.- A vast array of maiming humans with weaponry, telekinetic powers, and Crypto's UFO.- Everything is destructible. - Great enemy variety if a little stale towards the end of the game as you melt everything with your overpowered arsenal.Cons:- Story is very basic.- Very short.- Side activities can demand quite alot.- Maps are small as a consequence of the original game's age.If you're a fan of the old game, you would enjoy this one at full price. If not, wait for a sale and try it out. You wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Lately I've been kind of bored of video games, but Destroy All Humans really got me motivated because of how fun it is. I didn't know until later that it was a remake, but I'm so glad they decided to do this and I hope they remake the 3rd one as well (because the 2nd one has already been announced with a trailer recently).What's great about the game is the small maps make it easy to run, so you don't need and insane $3000 rig just to get 100fps. Along with the hilarious jokes and dialogue that makes fun of typical American stereotypes and somehow always bring up communism every 5 minutes. There's also some adult jokes included as well, and it's still relevant and funny after 16 years. It's so great how when you zap the humans or run by then they make noises and comments such as "Midget Commie!" and "They're trying to steal our way of life" *but extremely exaggerated to make it sound goofy.Along with the game already being so entertaining it's also very satisfying. You're able to glide or hover around really smoothly and quickly, as you could be electrocuting humans at the same time or even anal probing them (you'll find out what that is later if you haven't played the game yet ;) ). Being able to go into the flying saucer is really cool too, as you just get to destroy civilization and innocent people's homes just because you're angry and it's fun.If I had any complaints at all it might be the interesting controls for the saucer, because you can't move your mouse or joystick and up down, you can only aim side-to-side and you have to move fowards or backwards if you can't meet your target. But I'm sure there's good reasons why that's a thing, I just found it a little annoying while playing. But other than that it's definitely worth the money, and if you have a sense of humour + love to reek havoc to let your frustrations out or just for fun I highly recommend this game. There's other cool features like disguising as another humans beings too which is a really cool feature, but yeah it's a sick game just buy it if you haven't already stop reading this review lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: Even tough I recommend this game, I personally have mixed feelings about it. I am a massive fan of the original game, and used to play it all the time on Xbox, so I was really excited when I heard that a remake was being made. I bought the game and, like I said, I have mixed feelings. Here are some of the things I liked, I love the fact that the kept all of the voice acting from the original game, they even put in some unused dialogue and alternate unused takes which is cool. Flying the saucer around is and blowing stuff up is even funner than it was in the original game, its very faithful the the original game, and I think the extra costumes for Crypto are neat. Here are some of the things that kind of disappointed me, first, the graphics, I am aware that, even back when the original game was released, the graphics were not the best, but the cartoonish look, particularly of the human characters in this game, I personally don't care for. Second, some of the mechanics I think are not as fun as the ones from the original game. Personally I prefer the original game, but, despite the problems I have with this remake, it is a good game, so I do recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally games have you fight off aliens to defend humanity, this game is the complete opposite. Now YOU are an alien trying to take over humanity, what's more this is a recreation of the original "destroy all humans"!Pros:- Very nice Graphics, they pretty much hold up to today's standards.- Very nice voice acting (they even had the voice of Tank Dempsy in here, holy crap)- Fun gameplay mechanics, if you're in a mission there's several ways to play it, if not you can literally do whatever you want. Go crazy and go on a rampage! Or blend in and observe the humans.- Interesting story, the narrative wasn't too hard to understand and I felt it was an interesting plot (considering we're taking over the world)- Funny jokes (until you've heard them several times, covered in cons)Cons:- The voice lines sound a little choppy, the acting is fantastic but the audio quality from the voice lines aren't perfect. You can tell they've brought them in directly from the old version.- A bit of repetition especially in the stealth segments. You hear the same lines over and over, it gets a little stale. Eventually the repetition catches up and you just keep hearing the same lines even in combat.- The game isn't too long, and compared with the price tag I'd say wait for a sale. (I completed the game in 6 hours, the extra hour was from idling)- It's not been out long so there's a bit of an issue with optimization, especially at the end. I struggled with the second last boss simply because of the game freezing long enough for me to get spun about and run into hazards.Overall I'd say this is a very fun experience, something you should try out if you didn't play the original "Destroy All Humans!". Though, wait for a sale. It's not worth the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans Remake was a nice addition to my collection, but the gameplay itself left a sour taste in my mouth after playing it for several minutes. Here is my list of nitpicks that I've noticed so far.- Using any of Crypto's telepathic abilities (besides Corvex Scanning) can interrupt and expose Crypto's current disguise. In comparison to the original game, you were allowed to use your telekinesis, brain extractions without having to deal with your disguise automatically failing, but you still had to scan to maintain the disguise. This change was one of the biggest flaws IMO that really limits the gameplay, enjoyment and adds more challenge over the fun aspect (especially during exploring mode which is one of the best replay value options you can have in this game}.  - Ragdoll physics from this remake looks a nicer upgrade, but there is no flailing when you levitate someone in the air. They just stand up like a stiff board (dead or alive). One cool addition would be the hats and guns falling off than it super glued onto their hands/head. On a side note, compared to the original Destroy All Humans, the bodies were remained in whatever pose they were and it would have some weight while in the air. Plus I think the ragdoll joints were better overall in the original than the remake because the legs were hard to spread apart and usually stayed close to one another. It felt like I play moving around jello.- Telekinesis in this remake has a better visual, but the control of objects felt weightless (there was barely any delay of air movement when moving them left , right, up, down). Another flaw was the ability to target and throw the levitated object at an NPC or NPC to NPC. In the remake, you can do it, but often it's impossible and usually it would miss the target that you're trying to aim at.- Personally, I didn't dig the cartoony scheme of it all. I liked the one from the orginal more, some of the humans look uglier, but they definitely got THICC-er and that would be one of the good ones, but also bad since there wasn't a lot of variety besides the same clothes with different patterns.

You do feel every upgrade, and it is tiered to ensure you use every version of every weapon.I do have some technical issues (AMD 8350 Asus 1080 FE 16GB RAM) which lead me to needing to apply some tweaks within my system software. I still have audio issues, and no matter if I choose single/dual channels, and no matter the frequency, when things get crazy the audio gets choppy. I can live with it, but for some this may be a turn off. I hope they patch it, and will be more than willing to submit an error report if anyone knows how to. The game is fun. I bought it and a copy for my brother. Despite being single player we're still able to talk about the funnier moments of the game as we were playing through.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original Destroy All Humans! back in the day, this 2020 remake is like revisiting an old favorite, but with way better graphics and smoother controls. It's got all the same charm, goofy humor, and destruction, just with a fresh coat of paint.Visually Updated, Same Good VibesThe game looks awesome. They really nailed the cartoony 1950s vibe with all the alien tech and small-town America stuff. Blowing up buildings and zapping humans never looked so good. The destruction physics make tearing up the world even more satisfying.Upgrades Make You Feel PowerfulOne of the coolest things is the upgrades. They really mix up the gameplay and keep things from getting stale. I found myself wanting to fight way more because the upgrades make you feel like an unstoppable alien powerhouse. Honestly, being stealthy just felt boring after a while, even if it meant missing out on some extras.But Oh Man, the Loading Screens...Now, the worst part—THE LOADING SCREENS. Holy hell, they take forever, and I have no idea why. The game even froze on me during one of these long loading sequences, which happened after my first death (on the final mission, of course). It only happened once, but still, it was annoying.It's Got That 2005 EdgeLook, this game has some humor and themes that probably wouldn’t fly in 2024, and honestly, that makes me like it even more. It’s got that cheeky, irreverent vibe that games used to have before everyone got super serious.Short but SweetThe game is pretty short—like 8-9 hours max—which was pretty standard for games back then. If you’re into 100% completion, it’ll probably take you around double that (I’m working on it now, and by the time you read this, I might already be done).100% Worth It for the PriceHere’s the kicker: I got this for like $5 on CD Keys, and for that price? This game is a no-brainer. It’s absolutely worth it if you want a fun, quick romp as an alien causing chaos.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All humans is like X-com but in reverse.You play as Cryptosporidium-137, a member of an alien race known as the Furon. The Furon have a genetic mutation where they don’t got no ♥♥♥♥, so they have to find fresh DNA samples to keep their cloned race going without running out of the good stuff and going extinct.So you go to Earth, or the United States to be specific. The only place on Earth that MATTERS, and you start anally probing people for [s]fun[/s] brain stems. Originally released in 2005 for the PS2 and Xbox, Destroy All Humans only recently saw its way to the PC in the form of this remake. Graphics have been modernized, controls changed, and framerate improved, but how does it actually play? For the most part, Kill All Boomers is a third person shooter with some vehicle segments thrown in-between. Crypto has a handful of weapons to play with, including an Arc gun, a plasma gun, the MEGA GRENADE, and butt plug. For the most part, you'll be fighting some form of government agent if you're not just eating the delicious DNA of random civilians, although in some maps, random citizens will also be carrying weapons. Every weapon seems to have a purpose, and they're all fairly fun to use and easy to control. Though its easy to see that the game was originally made with a controller in mind, considering how I can just kind of wipe out entire divisions of US soldiers in a few seconds. Movement controls actually remind me of this game called “Outwars” from 1998. Please don't tell anyone I'm old.You have a full range of movement as well as a jump-pack option and a dash that you can upgrade to basically be permanent. Considering some of the enemies like to play bullet hell-lite, its kind of welcomed to be able to change direction in mid air or dash from left to right quickly. Every now and then, the mission calls for you to get into your saucer and just blow stuff up.  There isn't much to say outside of you're going to draw a ♥♥♥♥ in the ground. The game is shorter than I remember, with the main story clocking in at about 5 or 6 hours. There's extra stuff to do like challenges and drone collection, but once that's done, you're done. The game also asks you to perform certain things during the main quest for extra DNA and 100% completion. Destroy all Humans was fun to play. $20 is a fair price for the game but I would still wait for a sale if you're iffy on the game time. From what I've been told its incredibly easy to 100%, so if you're looking for an easy 100% for your steam profile, hey here you go. Fight all Monkeys gets 7 inbred aliens out of 10. A Wood Frog can hold its urine for up to eight months. Special thanks to Abdul Alhazred  for sending me this game. Please put your tentacles back in your robe.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake.This remake is absolutely true to the source material in every single way, they have changed some things but these changes are entirely for the better, such as removing the DNA requirement to unlock missions. It's one of the few games I took the time to 100%.The gameplay has been cleaned up and streamlined, so it plays much more fluidly. The graphics are incredible all things considered, the only criticism I would have would be the lack of variety in character models, there's probably less than 10 from what I could see. The more cartoonish style is hit or miss, I'm not a fan but I don't think it's necessarily a bad thing.Any real criticisms of this game that I have stem from issues with its original design for 2005, so I can't blame Black Forest. Some elements are very antiquated but you know what you're getting with a remake of a 15 year old game. After a few missions and upgrades the shallowness of the gameplay does start to come through a bit. The combat isn't the best, movement isn't the best, interaction with the world isn't the best and there's a poor variety of mission types. Whether or not you will like this game depends on whether or not the concept of it is appealing to you, there's nothing ground breaking here, no big gimmicks or anything. If you like the idea of being an alien probing people and destroying buildings then honestly that's all you need to be able to enjoy this game.I really hope THQNordic go ahead and let Black Forest work on a remake of DAH2 as it improves upon the original in a lot of ways.
