_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I highly anticipated this game. I remember back in the day, I saw a Game Informer issue where this was the cover story, and I was instantly transfixed with the idea of being a little alien running around and blowing everything up. I was not disappointed when I finally got it, even if the game's crass humor got me in trouble with my parents for a bit. So I have a lot of nostalgia for the series. But how does the remake hold up?The good news is that the gameplay here is totally revamped. Crypto feels more mobile and more powerful than ever before. You can skate around levels thanks to a new ability, allowing you to effortlessly dodge enemy projectiles. You can chain together several of your abilities now; In the original if you wanted to use your psychic abilities you needed to remain grounded, whereas here you can pick up a tank, fly through the air, and then shoot at a soldier while you throw the tank at another tank all at the same time. Your psychic energy meter is now totally gone, meaning you can use all of your abilities at will for however long you want. The power of all of your abilities is also greatly enhanced; The brain extraction power, for instance, was something you used rarely in the original, but is now a bread-and-butter tool in your arsenal for providing powerful crowd control utility. It can now be upgraded to spread on use, and victims under its influence will fight for you for a short time before their heads explode!The weapons are also a lot more powerful. The Zap-O-Matic is never truly outclassed like it was before. The Anal Probe also remains a very useful utility through the end of a game, instead of being something you use exclusively for farming DNA for upgrades in between missions. The only minor problem I have with the arsenal is that the final upgrade for the Ion Detonator, which is your grenade launcher, isn't all that useful and actually harms the pace of the game. The time slowing mechanic cannot be cancelled as far as I can tell, and only serves to annoy. It's the last upgrade in the tree, so you can just skip it, but once it's installed it's installed for good.The saucer combat sees fewer changes, but does have some nice updates. As before, your weaponry is vastly more powerful. The updates they make also means that you will be utilizing your entire arsenal frequently. You are actively encouraged to switch between weapons to maximize your destruction thanks to clever upgrades, meaning that you will deploy your Quantum Deconstructor frequently instead of just for special occasions.In short, gameplay when you're fighting is what this game does best. It's a very video-gamey video-game. It's non-stop fun just going into sandbox and blowing away humans because the core gameplay loop in the combat is executed fantastically. There are a few control misgivings, such as the auto-targeting sometimes not picking the thing you want, and the context-sensitive pop-ups sometimes misfiring meaning you might pop someone's head instead of implanting a command, failing the mission. But for the most part it works well.Where the game doesn't hold up as well is the structure itself. The early 2000s stealth mechanics just aren't as fun in 2020. The actual missions and activities and collectables definitely feel 2000s as well, the product of an older school of game design. They hold up decently but it definitely holds the whole game back. The humor hasn't aged as well as I would have hoped, but it still gave me a few chuckles. The story itself is perfectly serviceable, leaning heavily into cheesy 50s b-movie territory which is totally fine.So what do I want to see out of Destroy All Humans going forward? A lot of people want to see a remake of Destroy All Humans 2, but I actually disagree. The game is at its strongest when it's leaning into the stuff they could modernize, meaning the actual gameplay and combat mechanics, and how Crypto interacts with the world. The game is at its weakest when it comes to the overall dated structure. This structure also means the game is quite short, as I was able to 100% this game in just under 16 hours.What I want them to do next is make a totally original game out of the IP. Take the fantastic foundation they laid for this game and disconnect it from the stuff that doesn't quite hold up in 2020. I think there's a lot of stuff that they can explore that they started to hint at in the side objectives you can do, such as neat Hitman-esque assassinations you can do in one mission, but they couldn't really flesh out fully due to the constraints of the story they had to adhere to. I think a fully modernized Destroy All Humans experience would do much better than another remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All HumansSo this is an entertaining remake of a (mid-2000s?) game for PS2/Xbox, modernising it.An action/adventure game where you play as an alien invader intent on, well destroying all humans (give or take), fairly self-explanatory.So, good points:The graphical style lends itself to not ageing badly, and while work has been done, nothing is spectacular.I was also very much a fan of the voice acting, the story is fairly cliche, but the audio brings it to life.There is plenty of little things to chuckle at as well, this is a game that doesn't take itself too seriously at all. There wasnt really a lot though for the price, and there isnt a whole lot of replayability.The gameplay is decent, but there are some problems:#1 - ControlsYou cannot remap the controller buttons in-game on PC. This is simply NOT ACCEPTABLE in modern titles. Get it together.#2 - CameraGenerally this wasnt too bad, but the times it was made me hate it. The field of view was too narrow for my liking (and no option to change), and a lot of the gameplay required holding down/mashing buttons. This means you cant use the associated analog stick to move your camera, creating a problem when you want to do both at the same time. Cameras will never be perfect in 3rd person modes, but in cases like this a camera needs to be more adaptive to support the player.#3 - TargetingLeading nicely in here. There are a lot of objects to interact with in numerous different ways. Ostensibly this is good, however, if you're on a timed challenge and you cant.get.the.thing.you.want because there's dozens of - at that point - irrelevant objects in the way it is immensely frustrating, and breaks immersion. I get staying true to the original, but these are the kinds of things to work on in a remake (adjustable/context sensitive priority filters perhaps?)#4 Other little thingsHaving to rewatch the same little fly-to-earth scene when starting a mission. Its fine once, but adds nothing after that, stop wasting my time. Or having to wait for a countdown and listen to the same intro on restarting a challenge...every...time (just have a go-button for the player, not difficult). Again, time wasting and annoying. Minimap has too much content and not enough info. All more stuff that shouldn't be in a remake (I think these were like this in the original).One final problem I encountered was framerate drops/sound stuttering. Most noticeable late-game when the screen gets busy. May just be my setup but I saw other reports of this on forums.Overall, the negatives outweighed the positives, and there just isnt a good enough reason for them to give this a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: While not entirely bad, you can tell this game comes from another time. It's short, a bit shallow and totally lack substance regarding its gameplay elements. Could have been a nice destruction sandbox type of game, unfortunately you'll only have time to mess with 2 or 3 civilians before getting swarmed by endless waves of law enforcement units.You can fight back, of course, but at this point, it's just the most basic and repetitive 3rd person shooter gameplay. Weapons and abilities are fine, but it would have been great to have a dozen more, and most important, to add some spice to it. Like I don't know, an inflatable gun to make people explode, a gun that transforms people into animals, a big magnet gun to disarm all your opponents... the possibilities are endless with this setup and it could have provided real combat options and combos potential.In the end, it's so down to earth you can even ask yourself why playing an Alien after all If it's to have so many limitations during gameplay. In any case, either you're curious or nostalgic, I would not recommend paying full price for this game. Paid it 10€ during sale, and it felt more than enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans does some things right, but other parts can be very frustrating.DAH is at its best as sort of a mayhem simulator letting you run wild, pop heads, and blow things up. The weapons and abilities are good, and movement is solid and intuitive. There's very little that is as satisfying as grouping up a bunch of humans and starting a chain reaction of heads popping. About half of the missions are fun. The optional objectives add some extra nuance without generally being a pain to go the extra mile.Unfortunately, DAH is also frequently aggravating. For a non-stealth game, sneaking around is not the worst I've ever seen, but its still generally pretty bad. Protect missions are mostly painful. The targets are brittle, and enemies/obstacles are frequently overwhelming and unpredictable (and not in an interesting way).And then there's the insta-fail mechanics. LOTS of them. Don't do something precisely the way the game wants you to, the mission is instantly failed, and you restart the mission or checkpoint. I hope you enjoy certain dialogues because the same ones play every time. Insult on top of injury.The final boss is kinda outrageous. While the combat difficulty of this game is generally fairly mild the last boss was pulled straight out of a Dark Souls game. Its a 15 minute long bullet sponge slogfest, and the boss can instantly remove your entire shields in one hit.TLDR: Decent game brought down a fair bit by restrictive objectives and a few really poor design choices. C+

_childDocuments_.review: Games from the PlayStation 2 era have a very recognizable feel to them. Even when they look significantly better, like in this situation, the gameplay limitations of the time always leak through. Destroy All Humans exemplifies the concept of being a “product of its time,” but whether or not that’s a good thing is up to you.Abbreviated Reviews: Destroy All Humans looks as solid as you could expect from a remake/remaster. It doesn’t necessarily look amazing, but the improvements in textures, lighting, shadows, and resolution are obvious side by side. There’s always a limit of how far you can go with remaking a game before you’re just making a whole new game (see Final Fantasy 7). While I’m sure some areas could have been better, what has been done is impressive given the source material.While the graphics shine, it’s hard to find as much appreciation for any improvements made to the voice work or gameplay overall. It’s too much to expect re-recording the main voice lines, but there are parts where they’re noticeably crunchy sounding and it can be a little annoying. The AI for enemies isn’t anything spectacular here either. Everyone will beeline toward you shooting whatever weapons they hold and unarmed people will do the same in the opposite direction. The predictability of the experience limits the challenge up to the point where the only time I’d die is doing something ridiculous, at least for most of the game.Destroy All Humans is best when you’re blasting through waves of enemies, especially in the latter half of the game when more join the fight. The “power fantasy” genre was at its peak around this time. Games where you mow down your opponents by the dozens were the standard and this game delivered that. While you only have four main weapons, they provide distinct mechanics and each has its uses. In addition to those, your psychic powers come in handy just as much if not more than the guns. Crypto’s telekinetic throw is what I used more than anything just to get people out of the way.The saucer portions of the game, while fairly limited, are even more fun from that perspective. Torching tanks with the death ray or blasting down buildings with the sonic boom was always fun. I always wanted more of it, but it was generally the final mission in the series for each of the zones, and there are only around five or six of those across the 23 missions. These saucer missions usually don’t require much outside of blowing things up though, so maybe they didn’t want to spread that too thin.Things get a little less enjoyable in Destroy All Humans when you’re doing the stealth portions. These require you to take the form of a human and sneak into areas to collect information, items, or sometimes people. They can have their moments, but the missions feel thoroughly one dimensional as you simply dodge things that can detect you and pointlessly refresh your disguise. The interactivity is limited and the frustration the main character shares with not being able to destroy things is exactly what the player is feeling.There are parts of Destroy All Humans that rise above and fall below the typical missions. For instance, out of nowhere, there may be a multiple-choice dialogue section. These can be mildly funny but are as dated as the rest of the dialogue. Then there will be escort and follow missions and we all know how messed up those can be. In 2005, they were still pretty common, and mediocre AI didn’t help that at all. On the other hand, defense missions presented the solid combat mechanics with some new goals that made them even better. It could be a mixed bag at times.There were also some more fundamental issues like failing missions due to venturing a bit too far out of the designated play area. I feel like that’s a relic of gaming that you rarely see these days. However, by far the biggest issue I had with the game is the ridiculous spike in difficulty for the final mission and boss fights. It’s several times harder than anything before it. Unless you made some good choices with upgrades, it almost requires you to go back to play the challenge missions to gain bonus DNA. Luckily, most of these can be pretty fun and even provide unique gameplay like the abduction missions.Overall, Destroy All Humans is a reasonably fun time if you can tolerate the issues common for games of that era. For me, it was a step back in time. For some, it might be an era they’d like to forget. The majority of the game felt well designed and, while dated, some of the comedy still lands. I just cannot figure out why they felt the need to have that final mission be so devastating. Regardless, if you can get it cheap enough, it’s worth giving a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah. Destroy All Humans! A gem of a bygone era of PS2s and Xboxs. The game about a little gray man from outer space with one objective, of taking over earth that most of us fondly remember. The original on PS2 hasn't aged very well. It's mechanics are clunky, all the towns look gloomy and its technical achievements are dated. So how does this remake hold up against modern standards for gaming?It actually holds up surprisingly well when compared against a modern standard for gaming, in spite of its limitations. Now most of you must be thinking "Why is this any good? There's a lot of remakes/remasters/reboots out there that are sleazy nostalgia money grabs with little to offer and often worse than the originals!" And I thought so at first when I saw this, however, this is far from just being a shortcut to our wallets by way of our hearts.The game has been essentialy rebuilt from the ground up with the unreal 4 engine, as obviously, just slapping on some high quality textures on the PS2 original would not do. The art direction is superb, buildings and props look pretty great, though the NPCs look a little bit weird, a few of them make you wonder if the creator was going for something akin to porcelain dolls. It is forgiveable  though, the art is on point for the game and the setting of 1950's America. Speaking of the setting, it is what you'd expect of a game about an alien attacking 1950's earth, most, if not all tropes are there, such as mind reading, mind controlling, desintegrator guns, flying saucers throwing things around. Even the music is a throwback to cheesy science fiction movies, and I must say, it is on point for what you'd expect. This brings me to the second portion of the setting, which is... arguably not so good. Though the game was ladden with humor and it was quite something back in the day, some of the jokes and the humor don't hold up nearly as well as they did back then. It is excuseable, though. My only other big complaint is the aptly named "death ray" on the flying saucer not desintegrating NPCs, just leaving them in a ragdoll state.Other than quality sound, a great art direction and great ambience overall the game also features several quality of life improvements over the original, such as being able to use weapons, PK and also fly around with the jetpack at the same time. If you remember playing the original, you'll remember how much of a pain it was to choose inbetween all three of those. The game also has added side missions, which are basically abducting people/objects, racing after a runaway drone and trying to collect the DNA it spews out, a rampage mission where you must murder enough of a certain NPC, and armageddon which is basically seeing how much destruction you can dish out in a certain amount of time. "Rampage" is much like "Armageddon" but on a smaller and much more focused scale, and from all side missions, the racing ones were the hardest to get all 3 stars on and arguably, the least enjoyable. Other than that, Crypto also boasts a whopping 60 something upgrades for his powers, saucer and weapons! Better try to maximize your brain harvesting!Not all is roses however, as the game's main shortcoming is it's lenght. It is very short, like the original, if you were to just blast through the main story missions you'd be done in a few hours, especially since most missions are fairly easy, on top of being of short duration. The second great shortcoming is the lack of co-op. You'd expect this game to have co-op, especially since the sequel on PS2 had co-op and it was a huge blast to play with your friends. Sadly, perhaps, in their efforts to remain as faithful to the original with a little bit of wiggle room, the developers made a mistake by not adding co-op. What could be more fun than exterminating humanity with an anal probe and the company of your best friend? The game also has your standard collectible hunt in the form of furon probes, and well, it is very satisfying to fly around the saucer destroying everything inbetween missions, but the game just lacks things to do when you're done with missions and side missions. It's still fun reading NPC's thoughts but... it doesn't remain super entertaining forever. Something else that bothered me was that a lot of times while playing this I just felt like I wanted to play the sequel, on PS2 more. Not that it had a lot of things more to offer, but the setting wasn't confined to 1950's America, but it was set on the 1960s and you had missions in San Francisco, London, Tokyo, Siberia and The Moon! Not to mention, Crypto's arsenal was much more robust. The side missions were also far more interesting and varied than in this.This is by no means a bad game, it is fun and if you played the original and remember it fondly, this is definitely a worthy purchase IF on sale. On full price, well, you are going to get your money's worth out of it, but after hunting all the achievements (also another missed opportunity, why not have one for destroying all buildings in a map? Or hunting down all probes? Or probing X amount of humans?), destroying the same city over and over and over and reading the minds of NPCs for the 10th time, it gets stale and sadly, there isn't much else you can do. The only DLC is a skin pack for crypto, which was given free of charge for people who preordered. The skins are quirky, but it's pricing is a bit steep and nothing of value is lost by not purchasing it.Is this a good remake? Yes, yes it is. Hopefully this will be enough of a commercial success to warrant a remake of the sequel, which as most people who played both games remember, had a lot more to offer and was a lot more fun, despite being more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I need to say that this game was part of my childhood, so my review might be a bit biased. That being said, this game does what the original 2006 release set out to do, and dare I say, for once the remake does it better.The goal for you and your protagonist is very simple: conquer the Earth (not "Destroy All Humans", contrary to the name).  is very average — perfect for a game like this. Missions tend to be repetitive if you strip them down, but the changing setting makes (almost) every mission interesting. The stupid jokes during the cutscenes and the gameplay made me snort a few times. The game makes light fun of 1950's communist-fearing, suburban-loving, burger-eating America, so there are some low-hanging fruit but I personally like the style. However, I would argue the story is not the main point of the game, armageddon-style shooting and blowing things up is.The  feels very smooth and satisfying. You are running, gliding, flying and skating through the cities and farms. You zap, burn, smash, explode not to mention probe through the citizens, who seem to beg for it with their moronic and obnoxious voice lines. And that is only when you are on foot — get in your saucer, and your powers triple. Crypto's arsenal isn't amazing, but you have all you need for some Grade A carnage. The game has simplified some mechanics from the original game, but added some new stuff too (I love SKATE!!!). I have to say, after completing the game there isn't much else to do than tormenting those virtual citizens in free roam.The game feels very polished, no game-breaking glitches or bugs to be seen. Definitely some minor funny business when using SKATE, but it didn't really bother me. The devs really did a good job on this one and didn't just release the game half-done to be beta-tested buy the consumers.There are three boss battles, which felt quite anti-climactic and too easy. Especially the last one was just shooting and running, no special gimmicks to mention, just shoot the thing until it's dead, and oh, here're some minions. This is where I should mention the game, staying true to the early gaming era, has no . If you are looking for a challenge, you might not find it here. And this is coming from someone who got frustrated by Dark Souls III in the first few hours and quit. That being said, had I been using a controller, the game would've probably been harder.The  are very nice. Overall there is a cartoonish draw style. I think it fits nicely to the game, reminding the player not to take it too seriously. But that doesn't mean it isn't well made: be it buildings exploding with a nice bass and disappearing into a ball of fire or a Private's head making a gratifying PLOP sound when his brains jump out, It all adds to the satisfaction you get from destroying everything. Everything in this game is crafted to make it a perfect virtual power fantasy.Aside from the story and its optional objectives, there are 4 challenges and some collectibles (drones) in each of the 6 areas of the game. It took me 15 hours to complete every achievement, of which the story took about 7 hours. And I had to replay most missions to to complete the optional objectives. I'd say the playtime for 100% completion is around 10-20 hours for the average gamer. There is practically no replay value, since it's a strictly linear game.

_childDocuments_.review: A humorous game about invading earth and using a variety of weapons to - well - destroy all humans.The game puts you in the boots of Crypto, an alien on a mission to essentially take over the earth by force. The core gameplay thus consists of roaming decently large open levels on foot and using weapons such as an electricity gun or an anal probing device to dispose of people and destroy their property. In addition, Crypto can enter his space ship in order to unleash even grander weapons on the civilisation below, flattening buildings with laser beams and sound blasts among others.To get around the levels while on foot, Crypto is equipped with hover skates and a jet pack, giving him great mobility that feels quite good to use. Crypto also has a few mind tricks up his sleeve, being able to telekinetically move and throw objects as well as reading, controlling and extracting people’s minds. He may also transform into people he encounters, which is mostly used for basic and not very fun stealth sections.The main content of Destroy All Humans! Is made up of a string of missions strung along by a light story of Crypto moving through the United States on his quest to conquer them. These are rather varied given the basic gameplay features and certainly kept me interested throughout the game’s runtime. Each mission features some optional bonus objective, which increase the game’s challenge and can add some light replay value. Either way, Destroy All Humans! Isn’t a particularly difficult game, being more focussed on letting players have fun.As the game progresses, it introduces different enemy types, ranging from everyday humans to army personal and government agents equipped with ever escalating equipment. To counter this, your weaponry is similarly expanded every couple of missions, which goes a long way in keeping things fresh. You can also upgrade your weapons along with Crypto’s abilities using points mainly gained by extracting humans’ brains.In between missions, you can enter the locations you’ve already been to, allowing you to mess around in a sandbox environment and fully explore the maps. To encourage the later, each stage contains a number of collectibles you can gather to gain more upgrade points, which makes for a fun if tedious side activity. For some more collectibles, there are also a bunch of concept art pieces you’ll unlock with each mission beat as well as cosmetic skins for Crypto obtainable by completing quite varied tasks, like completing all bonus objectives in certain missions, successfully completing bonus missions etc.There are also various bonus missions of a couple of different types spread throughout the sandbox levels, tasking you with e.g. collecting certain objects in your ship’s tractor beam or completing obstacle courses using your mobility gadgets. All of these bonus missions are timed, challenging you with reaching certain point thresholds in order to unlock bigger rewards in the form of upgrade points. Fully completing these missions can be quite a challenge, with some of the later ones in particular tipping over into being quite frustrating to max out.The narrative in the center of Destroy All Humans! is predictably basic, essentially serving as a way to get you from mission to mission. It does however also play a big part in one of the game’s stronger aspects, being the humour woven throughout. Cutscenes as well as in-mission dialogue mostly serve to have Crypto mock humanity and its culture while also showcasing his lack of understanding of various human concepts. Adding to this is Pox, your more serious supervisor, who instructs Crypto, often leading to the two bantering, with their contrasting personalities making for some great chemistry. Personally, I found the humorous tone and the ever-present ridicule of the 1950s United States decently entertaining, even if it mostly managed smiles instead of laughs.As for the game’s presentation, the original look has been beautifully updated into a fittingly cartoonish yet detailed art style. The visuals are further enhanced with some rather nice-looking lighting and particle effects. Blowing up buildings in particular makes for a rather enjoyable spectacle, with crisp explosions and a neat if a bit simplistic collapsing effect.While the overall style works well, I found some of the game’s animations to feel rather stiff and its sound design to be lacking at times, mainly during cutscenes. The pacing of Destroy All Humans! also felt off at times, with some areas being noticeably underutilized and story beats being stretched out to fit in more missions.With all that said, I had a good time with Destroy All Humans! and do recommend it for some straight casual fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Always played the demo of this game back on PS2 or Xbox. The nostalgic bug finally got to me recently with Bikini Bottom Rehydrated, and I do not know why I've put this one off for so long. DAH! is a wonderful remake, with it's on the nose satire of American culture, and delightfully absurd mechanics. It's all about messing with humanity, making them fodder in comedic, yet sort of twisted ways, and infiltrating their ranks to make buffoons out of the humans. The devs have just done a damn good job bringing the art-style of the original into the modern era. I am looking forward to Reprobed. I know that is one many back in the day raved about. So glad that absurd game concepts like this exist. Also runs pretty decently on the Steam Deck, I ran most things at Normal settings, with Texture details set to the highest, and I was getting around 35-55fps. One can lock the refresh rate to around that golden 40/45HZ on the Deck and have a very pleasant experience with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Again, I play another remake with nostalgia goggles and remember when fifteen year old me was glued to the TV playing it. it brings back a lot of memories and is a nice time capsule game that captures what open world gaming was like prior to Oblivion and Skyrim. With that comes some much needed life in the gaming world and a reminder of what we’ve overcome and have yet to shake off from the past.The Good- Open world. One can play the story mode and revisit to collect brainstems, explore, laugh at the puny humans, find lost probes, and now there are missions. Lots of replay value!- Perfect blend of 1950’s humor and science fiction. Some of the dialogue escaped me back in the day but I have a new love for it now that I’m older.- Lots of a methods to destroy all the puny humans. Many of the old school ways of doing so are available. Although I’m very fond of being boring and just making brains explode.-The old dialogue, music,  and sound effects are still in effect, just remastered for our modern ears.- Crypto can dash to evade some enemy fire and hover for a little bit, making long travel less tedious. This was a very nice addition to the game!The Meh- Challenges are a new feature (if they were in the old game I must’ve forgotten about them) and give you more to do in your free time but many require a perk upgrade or two before you get three star ranking. Rampage, Race, and Abduction can be complete with relative ease but I haven’t even gotten one star in Armageddon yet since I don’t have my saucer upgraded.- The humans look very cartoony. Like the old game there’s’ only about ten character models for humans and they all look very fake compared to how Crypto got upgraded. Not a biggie, just weird.- Crypto can transmog everyday items into ammo for his guns, which sounds nice on paper… but it randomly determines the ammo type, making it more likely you’ll get disintegration rounds when you really want more ion grenades. A great idea on paper.The Bad- Like early GTA games the enemy will be on alert pretty quickly and hiding only evades patrols for so long. You can go from no alerts to having Majestic patrols around every corner pretty early on in the story mode.- Until fully upgraded both Crypto and his saucer are pretty susceptible to enemy fire. When the games turns into bullet hell it becomes bit of a pain. I used cheats back in the day but they are absent from the PC version.- The story mode difficulty only gets harder as it progresses. Once robots start showing I u just remember using cheats just to be able to play the game. Haven’t made it there again yet, but let’s hope fifteen years later I learned a thing or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All HumansFor me this was a childhood classic. something i loved playing growing up and also on Ps now just a few months ago. After that, this remake was announced and i won't lie, i threw my wallet at my screen.So if you've played the original you'll know what a fantastic game it was, there was so much fun to be had, but if you're playing this for the first time, you're in for a fun ride.GAMEPLAYSo let's get straight into the gameplay, so much has been improved on by Black Forest Games, for one, it's a tonne smoother, gliding through the air on your jetpack whilst shooting puny humans and blowing up everything in sight has never been easier and felt so smooth. Controls are very simple, easy to access which gun you want to use, using the jetpack, PK abilities, holobob and more!The missions are near exact to the originals with some slight tweaks here or there with added cutscenes to improve an already brilliant game.During the Rockwell mission, you holobob the mayor and answer questions to keep the crowd happy, there was also more of this introduced in later missions which were very welcome.The ufo is very easy to control, just glide around as you'd expect, smoothly and turning just as well, you get all the weapons in the original but to Crypto and the saucer, there are so many more upgrades to get making popping people's heads even more worth it!GRAPHICSSo graphically this game imo is beautiful, compare it to the original and you can easily see the level of detail has been put into the graphics to really make this game blast forward into 2020. Now, is it the best graphical game of this generation? probably not but it doesn't take away from the fact that it's a beautiful game with great lighting, textures, ray tracing and overall fantastic detail.As most games, it's not without it's bugs, i came across a few cars casually driving in mid air up the street and a random person morphing with a building but nothing more since. In the original, when destroying building they would simply just collapse and weren't as destructive as you'd expect BUT in this remake, blowing building up, hearing the explosions and seeing it crumble to bits really makes you feel like the terror has just begun.CHARACTERSWe obviously return with Crypto and the classic Pox in this remake, these two miscreants still have their entertaining banter and witty remarks they throw at eachother which makes them a treat to watch during cutscenes and even during the missions. The npc's have also been recreated from the ground up with a more cartoonish look but the style and design is unique and fits perfectly rather than realistic people.    There are still the main characters from the game such as the general, president and more (no spoilers)LEVELSThankfully, even the levels are near exact the same as the original, as expected, some tweaks here or there for great improvements but the layouts are exactly the same with greater details. Turnipseed Farm, Rockwell, Santa Modesta, Area 42, Union Town, Capitol City SOUNDThe sound in Destroy All Humans Remake, has been greatly improved on. In some instances you will hear original audio from the original game but with a greater quality and no recaptured which i find to be a really nice touch. Other improvements are levels such as Turnipseed farm, you can hear birds chirping very nicely in such a rural environment, obviously busier towns take away a little bit from this and focus more on the surroundings such as more people talking, the Rockwell fair and even the squeaking of cars where people.....well you know the rest.The weapon sounds have also been greatly improved with the Zap-o-matic sounding alot more like a big Taser and not a faulty plug hanging off the wall, shooting fireballs has never felt so good as it sounds as you'd expect, like a ball of fire being shot although i'm not sure how we'd really expect that to sound lolThis goes for the weapons on the saucer aswell, Shooting the death ray sounds like you could very well shoot through the building and leave a smoldering crater in the earth and don't even get me started on how much i love the quantum de-constructer.Overall the sound quality in this has been greatly improved and really adds to the gameplay and enjoyment.CONCLUSIONIn conclusion, after playing this as a youngster i am extremely happy with this remake, it takes me back to being a 13 year old that purely wanted to destroy the human race or use the PK ability to hold someone in mid air and drop them onto a car to hear the thud....i was a sick kidGameplay for me is brilliant, fun to play, easy to use and i could just sit around demolishing the cities all day, not to mention the probe collectables you can get on every level!There is plenty to do, missions are very fun, optional mission objectives makes the missions even more fun and there is challenges to complete on each town which get more difficult as you go onVery fun, Very Smooth, sounds great and an experience for everyone to enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: One small weapon test for man, one giant leap on mankind!Cryptosporidium is on a mission to destroy humanity for the glory of the Furon Empire! Explore, exploit, exterminate your way through six locations across the United States, crushing their pathetic army, laying waste to their urban settlements and eradicating their stubborn leadership, from General Armquist to the President ending with the mysterious leader of the even mysterious organization Majestic.Summary:*This is a fairly short game, you can finish it in about seven hours. The challenges and collectibles add a few extra hours. *The game is humorous. I committed the occasional nose exhale and had a few chuckles now and then.*Graphics are pretty with a style.*The banter between Pox and Crypto is golden.*Camera controls are VERY clunky. The Saucer takes some getting used to.*Arsenal consists of four weapons. Three good ones and a anal probe, which you can, coincidentally, shove up your ass,   because it's more of a gadget than a gun. *Game stutters every now and then. It's not incredibly annoying. 7/10, it's fun. Get it on sale. There is not enough content for the 30 euro pricetag in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: 16 hours and I've done 100% of the content this game offers. I've collected every collectable, purchased every upgrade, aced every challenge, done every side mission and I've got all 40 achievements. In all fairness I drew it out as long as I could by doing some mindless destruction, mundane grinding, frustrating searches for the collectables, experimenting with how many heads I could pop in one chain, etc. etc. All in all there is about 10 hours worth of content here, but what you get is worth it. The graphics are highly stylised and every caricature looks to be plucked directly from a 50's billboard. The story is as cheesy as you can imagine and the humour is almost as if it was written 15 years ago. The same voice-lines over and over again gets old quick, though. Quicker than the 10 hours it takes to complete this game. My opinion is that it's worth the money. You can spend £5 to enter a rollercoaster ride that's done in under 5 minutes, by that logic it's £1 for a 1 minute of fun. This is £25 for 600 minutes of fun. A great deal in terms of entertainment, if you ask me. Especially if you hate rollercoaster rides like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as Crypto-137 on a mission to extract Furon DNA from humans to kickstart the cloning of the Furons and kill all humans. The character design is very different from the original game, the characters were designed to look more stereotypical/wacky looking than the original. The attention to detail is amazing, the interiors to building like diners and gas stations are fully 3d while the houses only have a picture of a room inside which you won't notice while playing. I kid you not even the female NPCs panties are fully detailed, with some of them being see-through.. Now the gameplay is just like the original but they made Crypto's movements so much smoother and with way better destruction. The debris from destroyed buildings plus the trail marks from your laser beam doesn't render out so you can basically destroy the entire town with nothing respawning or rendering out. They've also changed the sounds of all the weapons and added more ambient sounds to the area Crypto's in. All in all, if you like a game where you can play as a bloodthirsty alien anal probing and laser beaming every human on sight while collecting scrumptious human brains then this is the game for you.Edit: I beat the game and got 40/40 achievements in only 20 hours, I forgot to mention there are 30 story missions, 20 challenges,  6 unique areas to explore, and 100+ probes to find scattered in the various maps. I noticed some glitches with the physics like flying cars and humans that you fling can clip into objects but it makes the game even funnier and more ridiculous. This was the most fun I've had in a while inside a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept (no wonder, since this is a remake of a legendary classic) with a solid execution... and yet, there are some problems. On paper it's great, but in practice there are too many frustrating moments. There are some serious difficulty spikes in the campaign, but on the other hand, most of the missions are easy and even relaxing. And then there are challenges which are sort of optional, but without them you will have a hard time dealing with these difficulty spikes. And then, these challenges.. they surely _are_ challenging, to the point where they can be very frustrating.This could have been a very fun game, but I think that the above-average difficulty ruins it. The game presents itself as a comedy and something cheerful which seems very welcoming, but then it hits you pretty hard, so better be prepared for that.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wanting to experience the mid-aughts era of open-world gameplay, this is probably one of the prettier games you could do it with. The remastered graphics look fantastic, and run almost flawlessly. The humor is certainly of its time; most of it was middling to mediocre even then and hasn't aged any better (though parts of the NPC dialogue, especially those voiced by Steve Blum, have a few good bits - it's a shame they didn't subtitle these to make them more accessible).Still, this remake was competently done, the VO performances are still phenomenal, and it's a decent enough way to spend ten bucks and ten hours to 100%. _childDocuments_.review: **Review: *Destroy All Humans! (2020 Remake)***  *Destroy All Humans!*, the 2020 remake of the 2005 cult classic, is a nostalgic revival that manages to capture the quirky essence of the original while offering a polished, modernized gaming experience. Developed by Black Forest Games and published by THQ Nordic, the game puts players back in the shoes—or, rather, alien boots—of Crypto-137, an extraterrestrial invader tasked with harvesting human DNA and wreaking havoc on 1950s America.  ### Visual and Audio Overhaul The most immediate and noticeable improvement in the 2020 remake is the graphical overhaul. The original *Destroy All Humans!* was built on mid-2000s technology, and the remake updates this with vibrant, cartoony visuals that are perfectly suited to the game’s whimsical tone. The environments are more detailed, the characters more expressive, and the lighting effects add a dynamic layer to the chaotic destruction Crypto brings to Earth. While it’s not aiming for photorealism, the visual upgrades significantly enhance the playful satire that the game thrives on. The audio, too, has been remastered, with the original voice acting intact—a big plus given the stellar performance of Richard Steven Horvitz as the snarky, irreverent Crypto. His sardonic commentary, alongside the bombastic declarations of his superior, Orthopox (voiced by the iconic J. Grant Albrecht), add a lot of charm to the experience. The sound design complements the on-screen mayhem with satisfying laser blasts, explosions, and the occasional sound of terrified humans fleeing in panic.  ### Gameplay: A Faithful Remaster with Quality-of-Life Improvements In terms of gameplay, *Destroy All Humans! (2020)* sticks closely to the formula that made the original a hit, for better or worse. It’s an open-world action game with mission-based objectives, allowing players to use a variety of alien weapons and psychic powers to wreak havoc on humanity. Crypto’s arsenal includes a Zap-O-Matic for electrifying enemies, a Disintegrator Ray for turning humans into ash, and the infamous Anal Probe for, well, you get the idea. These weapons feel as fun as they did 15 years ago, with the remake enhancing their responsiveness and visual effects. There are also some minor quality-of-life improvements that make the game feel less dated. Crypto’s ability to use multiple powers in tandem has been streamlined, and the controls feel smoother. New mechanics, like the ability to use your jetpack more fluidly, make movement easier and combat more engaging. However, it’s worth noting that some aspects of the gameplay still feel a bit archaic. Enemy AI can be erratic, often charging directly into your line of fire, and some mission structures are repetitive by modern standards. ### Story and Humour The story of *Destroy All Humans!* is purposefully absurd, centering on Crypto’s mission to harvest human DNA and infiltrate the United States government—all while delivering a satirical take on 1950s Cold War paranoia, B-movie alien invasions, and conspiracy theories. It’s lighthearted and doesn’t take itself seriously, which works in its favor. The humor, often dark and filled with innuendo, still holds up remarkably well, especially with today’s lens of satirizing paranoia, government overreach, and societal norms. The game’s writing is laced with snark, and its parody of the ‘50s setting, complete with exaggerated accents and cultural tropes, offers plenty of chuckles. However, some jokes that played well in 2005 may feel a bit dated or tonally off in today’s more socially aware environment. Still, the over-the-top humour, when taken for what it is, contributes to the game’s charm and identity. ### The Downsides:Aged Mechanics While the remake does a good job of bringing the original up to modern standards, it can’t entirely mask some of its aged design. The mission structure, for example, often boils down to basic fetch quests or simply obliterating waves of enemies, which can become repetitive. The game is also fairly short by today’s standards, with most players able to finish the story in about 8 to 10 hours. There are side activities and collectibles to pad out the runtime, but they don’t offer much in terms of variety. Another downside is the difficulty curve. *Destroy All Humans!* doesn’t have much of a challenge, and enemy variety is limited, meaning that combat encounters can start to feel monotonous after a few hours. Although Crypto's weapons and abilities are fun to use, the lack of meaningful progression or complex enemies means that the novelty can wear off sooner than expected.  ### Verdict: A Fun, If Flawed, Trip Down Memory Lane *Destroy All Humans! (2020)* is a love letter to fans of the original game, offering a visually impressive and faithful remake that captures the spirit of its predecessor. It’s a fun, chaotic experience filled with irreverent humor, creative destruction, and a lighthearted tone that sets it apart from more serious, modern titles. However, beneath the shiny new coat of paint, the game’s age still shows in its repetitive missions and simplistic gameplay. For newcomers, it may not have the depth or sophistication expected from today’s open-world games, but for fans of the original, it’s a nostalgic romp worth revisiting. Despite its flaws, it’s hard to deny the simple joy of being a wise-cracking alien wreaking havoc on an unsuspecting human population. After all, who wouldn’t want to destroy all humans—at least for a little while?  **Score: 7.5/10** A solid remake that stays true to the original’s quirky charm, but some dated mechanics keep it from being truly out of this world.

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of having some mixed feelings about this remake, overall I really do love the remake.  Most changes and additions have been for the better, a few for the worse and overall its still the same game I have been in love with since I first played the original.  The improved graphics are absolutely awesome while remaining true to the original which is always a worry with a remake and most of the changes to the controls and gameplay are welcome.The only real gripe I have is with how PK works.  First of all, the controls have been greatly simplified.  While this makes it easier to use in combat, it also greatly limits how it can be used.  My friends and I would spend hours finding creative uses the PK ability to kill our subjects in the most hilarious ways possible.  We would use cars to block tank rounds, slam people around in hilarious ways or even pick up a truck and slam it on top of people over and over.  The updates to PK however make all of that impossible as now all you can really do is grab things and throw them.  What's more, while they are grabbed they seem immune to physics.  Attempting to use the new SKATE feature to ram someone I grabbed into a tree for instance caused no damage at all.  For some this may be a minor gripe but for me, half the fun of the game was playing with this ability.A minor gripe is how the physics works in this game.  Its not a dealbreaker but its really odd to throw a tank at a human victim only to watch the tank bounce of the human's head instead of bowling the subject over and continuing it's trajectory.  What I find more puzzling is that humans thrown at each other seem to behave just fine, but throw a car and suddenly the physics seem to break down.Those gripes aside, I still recommend this game.  It is highly a entertaining satire of McCarthy era America and highly entertaining mindless destruction fest.  Will it offer as many hours of mindless fun as the original for me?  probably not, but for the price, it is def worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, great throwback, and lots of fun.  Any one who played the original and loved it, or even wants a throw back to when games were just simpler, i would strongly suggest this game to them.  This is a great remake of a classic, but it is of course not a carbon copy of the original some things have changed so going in keep that in mind.What Stayed the same:-Story-Voice Lines-Cut scenes-Feel and play of the gameWhat changed:-weapon upgrades are different now this includes your ship-abilities flow a bit nicer now, and can use PK while your jet pack is running-so abilities and weapons work different all together now, for example in the old game your abduction beam from your ship would grab waht was below you, now it grabs your target in front of you, things like that.The cartoon graphics fit really well with the overall silly story, the game itself looks wonderful, of course going back to the game taht came out in, what, 2005? its kinda funny to see the dated level designs and the limitation that were put on the game back then, such as fairly small levels.All in all, the game has great charm, holds true to the original for about 99% of the game, save for like i guess one line in the earth girls are easy quest due to something something politically incorrect something something, but other then that its an amazing game for anyone wanting to replay a great classic.

_childDocuments_.review: A cult-classic, loved by its fans during its time in 2005, Destroy All Humans! is one of those games that just wants you to enjoy your time behind the monitor. I remember perfectly when I was playing the game way back in 2005 on my PS2, I always wake up in the middle of the night, past my curfew just to play the game. I had to turn down the volume so my parents wouldn't hear me playing.This remake lives up to its original formula, adding content that fans will definitely love -- skins, a much better progression tree, improved controls, and of course, eye-candy visuals -- while keeping the same, good old cheesy dialogue that takes a shot at political and current social issues. In short, it has a satire narrative, and it's very solid.The methodology lives up to its title, and Crypto-137, your anti-hero alien, is there to bust heads and exterminate humans -- destroying all humans, per se. You have your arsenal of alien weaponry and a spaceship that shoots death rays (the Saucer) to bring down enemies and structures. It's mayhem, and it's hilariously delightful.Forget about compelling and twisting narratives, forget about intricate gameplay mechanics, Destroy All Humans! is all about having fun, keeping it simple, and when you're done you still have challenges to keep it everything engaging; to unlock other skins and artworks.8.5/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Every single thing in the archives, from objectives to tutorials, has a paragraph of communication from the Furon's point of view, along with a funny quote from the archivist, Gastro-999. The humor is good, the graphics are really good, and the gameplay is amazing. Feels like a game from 2005, would shill for free.

_childDocuments_.review: But that doesn't change the fact that the game's content isn't really special or even outstanding, and the remake won't change that either. Sure, don't forget that the last 15 years have also left their mark on Crypto, but I've had great fun kidnapping cows, blowing up the White House or exploring the mind of the average American in the 50s.But that's exactly why the Furoners have a really big problem.Due to the constant use of atomic bombs, all of them have become sterile over time. Although the Furons got the problem with excessive cloning under control, this presupposes that new, fresh genetic material keeps coming.So this time it's the blue planet's turn and Crypto can kill two birds with one stone.On the one hand he can suck off the necessary genetic material from humanity and on top of that he can save his brother, who crashed with his spaceship in Roswell at the time...The Destroy all Humans Remake is probably more aimed at fans or connoisseurs of the game.But ✅ graphically revised remake✅ good light and particle effects✅ successful change between action and stealth✅ improved UFO controls✅ Boss fights better✅ Challenges and unlockables❌ annoying shortage of ammunition❌ low tension narrative❌ little to discover❌ partly short missions❌ sudden respawns from people❌ a lot of copy pasta

_childDocuments_.review: So... Destroy All Humans! Remake. For those who don't know, this game is back from Xbox and Playstation 2 days. It plays kind of like Saints Row 3 and 4, more or less 4 because you can fly and do crazy amounts of damage. All things considered, I'd rather play a DAH game over a modern Saints Row game. This series has a huge cult following and for good reason, it's one of the funnier games out there. A lot of the jokes in these games would never be allowed in today's clown world. Just know that this genre of game is a bit dated and dying because of horrible flops like Agents of Mayhem or Crackdown 3. The whole game can be completed in just a few hours and 100%'d in less than a dozen hours. So for old players, how is it?This team did a great job remaking this game overall. They made several changes to fix issues the game had in the original version. The best improvement was the addition of the mission select menu. In this remake, you're able to play any mission in the game with all of the upgrades you could have had unlocked at that part of the campaign. If you remember, that was a huge issue with DAH and games like it. It's one of those old games where you get the best stuff in the last 10% of the game and then have no time to actually enjoy it because the game is over and there's no missions left. They also streamlined and simplified a lot of the controls and mechanics which helped and hurt the game in a lot of ways.This remake has a handful of glaring issues. For one they've oversimplified some of the mechanics. If you recall in the original game, each NPC type had a different value of Furon DNA (upgrade currency) in their brains. I believe civilians were 10? Cops were 25, soldiers were either 25 or 50, majestic was either 25 or 50, and then scientists were 100. In this version of the game, all brains are worth 25. This means the whole mechanic of trying to salvage the brain of a living NPC goes out the window. In the original game you got the most points possible if you extracted the brain of a living NPC. If you killed them, it devalued their brain. This was a mechanic because of the Furon mind ability to make heads explode and the probe gun. They were harder and riskier to use on live targets, because they left you open to taking damage. Therefore, in this game it doesn't matter if you save or kill them, making the probe gun virtually useless until its maxed out due to it's slow firerate.Additional issues with the game include balance and performance. The performance of this game is pretty solid for the most part, but it does have occasional stutters or lag spikes during hectic fights or on bigger maps like Capital City. The race challenge in particular is more difficult on Capital City due to these freezes. Others have reported they had trouble with the final boss due to stutters. As for the balance, I don't know what's wrong. I don't know if it's because I haven't played these games since I was about 10-12 years old and I got better, or if I'm getting DAH 1 and 2 confused, OR this remake has somehow changed mechanics. Overall, I never died and I only had my shields pop for the first time in the entire game during the final missions. I think in the original you had to use the abduction beam to harvest brains from people in the UFO, but in this game you can just mash a button from down the street and have their brains fly to you. This greatly decreased the grinding time in this version which I guess is a nice quality of life feature.On a final note, there are more positives than negatives with this game. I was actually quite surprised to see this is one of the better remakes/remasters in the last few years. I would put it up there with Resident Evil 2 Remake. They do a great job staying with the old game, making it look decent, and even fixed the whole upgrade/NG+ thing. I think the $30 price is worth it just because this is a good game, but new-gen players will be upset with the amount of content for the price. All of that being said, I hope to god these guys get THQ Nordic to hire them for a DAH 2 Remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgic for about two minutes, but the controls are unforgivable and a game-breaking bug/issue is preventing me from proceeding anyway.The flying saucer controls are true to the original, but completely baffling for a 2020 PC game: WASD to move in the XY-axes, but MOUSE forward/back to move vertically, and NO pitch (up and down) camera control, so the ship view is constantly locked at a downwards angle that prevents you from seeing the horizon and targets not in your immediate vicinity. The ship's ray doesn't have a lock-on, it's floaty, and between the overbearing UI and the effects, you can never see what you're aiming at, so burning targets on the ground just turns into waving the ray back and forth until the cursor highlight goes away.The original's stealth was already dubious thanks to the wide-open, densely populated levels without any real paths or cover, but now it just feels unbearable. The existing issue -the utter lack of cover or other visibility mechanics- means that stealth means using trial-and-error to find weird corners/objects to hide behind that put you inside the tiny range within which you can use abilities on humans (or, more often, just flying over everything and cheesing from a rooftop). Worst of all though, the main stealth ability 'holobob' stops working without warning as human targets (or your link to them?) somehow severs or despawns at comically short distances, canceling your disguise and instantly failing the mission. There are threads of people complaining about this, but evidently the problem still exists.

_childDocuments_.review: A remake of an Xbox/PS2 Classic that delivers on all fronts. The models are faithfully re-created to fit the cheesey and parody-esque aesthetic of the 1960s. From blocky faced, chiseled chinned G-Men to poofy, curly haired Dames. Same easily goes for the weapons, Saucer & Mothership. As well our beloved Pox & Crypto. Gameplay wise, it definitely feels updated and more slick compared to the Classic. With the glide/skating system being a big improvement to help you move thriugh the levels at a faster pace. Especially when collecting Drones or trying to get to challenges.Easily recommend this if you want to revisit an old classic.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to praise this game on two fronts:What a fantastic transition to the PC architecture. After poor past experiences with nostalgic older titles being remade and re-released on Steam, Destroy All Humans sets an exemplary standard for how this is done right. Buttery smooth performance on top of high quality textures, models, and effects, none of which drag FPS below 60 on moderate hardware. Although it would be a luxury feature to see the framerate be unlocked above 60, I wouldn't find it necessary with how comfortable it is to run this game as-is. Well done.Now I'm not sure if some game mechanics were actually changed here; it's been over a decade since paying the original, but from vague memory it seems like some abilities have been adjusted to better fit the flow of gameplay. Transmogrifying props into ammo is an ability I don't fully recall, but it's addition gives you a nice way to keep magazines full for maximum human obliteration. This and a few other tweaks allow Destroy All Humans to realize the full potential of what it has to offer.Thank you to THQ and devs for showing the industry how it's done, and packaging it all at a modest $30 price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! is a faithful remake of the 2005 cult classic. Some people might view that as a negative but I found the game to be good, dumb fun. Barring the final boss fight, the game doesn't offer much challenge and you'll be able to get through its 8-10 hour duration with little effort. That said, sometimes you just want to play something laid back and DAH fits the bill. It offers a small set of large, sandbox levels and a bunch of missions within each one. The mission design is reminiscent of last-gen open-world games so if you're expecting intricate or complex stuff, you'll be disappointed. The missions are basically just excuses to use your arsenal of over-the-top weapons and gadgets and that part remains consistently enjoyable. Whether you're obliterating a town with your UFO or sneaking around military bases, there's a good mix of stealth and combat to keep things interesting.  After unlocking each level, you can also go into free roam mode, find collectibles and complete challenges. That gives the game some nice replayability. In terms of writing, the story is predictable and not all that interesting. I definitely wouldn't consider it a story-driven game. However, the comedic elements are pretty solid and offer a satirical take of 50's Americana. Communist paranoia? Check. Nationalistic propaganda? Check. Antiquated gender roles and stereotypes? Check. The humor is hit and miss but I found myself chuckling more often than not. If you're looking for a 50's alien power fantasy that'll make you laugh, Destroy All Humans! is worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: When someone tells me that a game has been remastered and re-released, I think oh, yeah, that is cool. Probably supports all kinds of controls now, fits the screen better, maybe even looks a little better too. Some extra content maybe. Nice.This blew all of my expectations right out of the water. This is not a remastered game, this game was remade. Every asset has been updated, every piece of art has been improved. They kept the fantastic voice acting (that makes me want to go an re-watch Invader Zim) which made me super happy. It is crisp and clear. The game plays like a dream. Often times when I buy a game like this from my youth, I can really feel how old and dated it is. This felt like a brand new game, like it had just come out in the last five years. I couldn't believe it.Obviously, the game play and story-line remain the same, which does kind of date the game. There is only so much havoc and chaos you can spread. I can see how when I was super young, how this game would have held my attention for hours and hours and hours, but now you can speed through it decently quick.However, I got it on sale for extremely cheap, something like 80%-90% off. It was so cheap it once again boggled my mind. As it is, full price, I don't think it is worth it. On sale for like, $3 CAD? It is a steal. Buy it when a sale comes around, whether you have played it before or not. It is a hilariously fun game that, if you have played it before, you should come back to experience the glory; and if you haven't played it before, you need to play it and try it. Just ofr the voice acting!Highly recommended, when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of the best remakes I think I've ever played ever. It's literally the PS2 game untouched with all of the old stuff except it feels better, with SEVERAL quality of life improvements to the gameplay to make it feel more fast paced and fair. For example: You can shoot your death ray straight down this time, draining lets you shoot and drain at the same time if that wasn't in the original, you can not only dodge but you can just do straight up hoverboarding, and there's more I can't account for. Now again I love the original but it's been years since I touched the original game on PS2, so if I'm wrong about anything then feel free to discard that. But at the same time it again keeps the original cast, keeps everything that made it special but it even added content cut from the original (mainly one mission called "The Mutant Menace"). And the amount more extra detail they put into each of the levels is astounding! The only things I could say that maybe could mess with people is the art style? That's subjective for me because I think the art style lends to the whole 50's parody aesthetic, though I think having everyone not look like warped cartoonish versions of themselves would've been ok too. Also holy s h i t that final boss fight in the remake feels WAY harder than the one in the original. Other than that I don't know, I can't really say too much except I hope these guys remake the second and ESPECIALLY the third then continue on with the franchise from there.Pros:Pretty much everything is back but betterUpdated environmentAdded extra contentCons:It's subjective but some have been mixed on the art style? I don't get itStill feels like the old ps2 game in some degreesOverall fantastic 15 hour experience I say anyone who is fans of the original should DEFINITELY try out

_childDocuments_.review: These are my first impressions of the game, remaster and the PC port. This is not a review.Destroy All Humans is a series that has evaded PC. Given the work done with this remaster, I'd say it's a crime we never got these games sooner. This is a game that plays like a dream for what it sets out to do. Controls in the remaster are fluid, environments are great and gameplay is varied and fun. The voice acting and general writing is very notable and the overall "fun factor" is just up there. While the franchise hit its stride with Destroy All Humans 2. The first game, especially with this remaster. Is very much worth checking out!Basically, you're an anti-hero type alien (Furon) named Crypto that sounds like Jack Nicholson. You run around and harvest humans for their strains of Furon DNA that has been apart of the human DNA strain for centuries. Furons can't reproduce except for cloning themselves but the strain weakens after each cloning. It gets so bad that it effects intelligence, and even a clone of Crypto was captured back on Earth because of it. So now you must harvest humans for their stored Furon DNA and rescue the Crypto clone all the while you control the human populace and make sure they aren't alerted to your presence. This is while government agents are trying to stop you during the games wonderful missions which have you using all kinds of abilities and tools such as anal probes, lightning guns, flying saucer death rays, body cloning, brain harvesting. Good stuff. Great dialogue and voice acting backs it up too with some intentionally strange and eccentric performances from the cast.There are some problems. Voice audio sounds a bit muffled in the cutscenes. Sound bytes also repeats often within the game when you're zapping humans and they yell the same things over and over again when they spot you. The game has its share of glitches in the press pre-release copy. I've seen the same trucks in the same spot spawn in hovering 3 feet off the ground. There are some performance hitches when starting a level too. There's also the issue regarding the art style. It generally looks nice but the character models vary. They look a bit too much like plastic dolls sometimes and their jawlines would make Chad Thundercock blush. There's also the obligatory, awful-looking Unreal Engine 4 particle physics that look like blinding neon lights. They look awful and I don't know why every game has this problem in this engine.From what I've played, this is an excellent remaster despite flaws in the original release and the remaster itself as it improves the original significantly from what it was. Destroy All Humans 2 is still a much better game and I really can't wait for Black Forrest Games to get that one out as it improves so much upon the original. If you haven't touched the series, I'd definitely give this version a look but you might be better off waiting for a sale or the sequel as it's just that much of a better game. If you liked the original, absolutely pick this up as soon as possible. You won't be disappointed (except maybe with the character models, then again the original was pretty hideous too).Thanks for reading! I have a full video right here if you want to check it out:We also have a curator page if you want some more recommendations: Have a good one!

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a game that I played for dozens of hours on the PS2. Or was it the PS3? It turns the usual sci fi trope upside down. Instead of defending against an invading alien force, you are the invading alien force. An army of one. Using your psionic powers and your superior technology you will conquer earth through a series of missions. Some of the missions are easy. Many of them are hard. A few are frustrating. Surprisingly the game looks pretty good. Kind of like a clay-mation cartoon. The voice acting is top notch, especially the voice actor for the main character. Rich Little couldn't have done a better Jack Nicholson impersonation. And the game is funny as well as fun. If I had one complaint it would be the save system. Instead of allowing to save anywhere and anywhen, the game saves at checkpoints. When the missions are easy, this isn't much of a problem. As the game gets harder, it becomes a big problem. You land up playing the same 5 minutes over and over again.
