_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game when it came out, but I waited for a really good deal on it because I've become accustomed to disappointments.  Anyways, this was not a disappointment!  I was really happy to genuinely feel nostalgia as I remembered some fun parts of one of my favorite games growing up!I remember the gameplay being awesome, and that's how this game is too.  There were a couple missions where the difficulty spiked unexpectedly but not a huge deal.  Just had to hit retry and lean forward.  I'm only 8 hours in, and it's really great so far.Well done with this one.I don't really remember the old game enough to comment on improvements or depredations.  I can only say I've only encountered one bug and it is extremely minor.This works very well on controller too.  The lockon mechanic works very well.I also noticed some lines in this game referencing other stuff, but I don't remember if they were lines from the original game (and hence other media is referencing this game) or if they were created as references to other media in this game.1. Rick's recipe for "dark matter" appears in one of the newspaper articles!2. "Don't get mad, get sadistic", which I recognized as a voice line for Viegar in LoLI'm sure there's even more I'm not picking up on.  (If anyone's curious, I got this in a humble bundle; $14 for this game and a handful of others.  It's probably worth the $30 price tag but things go on sale so often, why not wait a bit?)

name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead
detailed_description: Special Edition JOIN OUR DISCORD COMMUNITY About the Game In Iratus you find yourself fighting for the forces of darkness in the role of the titular necromancer—Iratus, recently freed from his millennia-long imprisonment. You control an obedient army of the living dead, with skeletons, zombies, banshees and many other unliving warriors. Create your soldiers the only way a necromancer knows how: from the body parts of your slain enemies! Expand and improve your underground lair. Strengthen your servants by researching secret rituals. Explore the twisted corridors and underground catacombs, and battle against lobotomized miners, greedy dwarves and corrupt mercenaries. Aid Iratus in his quest to recapture and eclipse his former power. Lead him to conquer the forces of good and unleash an eternal kingdom of death upon the world! The sheer variety of tactical and strategic options makes Iratus a true treat for any ardent fans of the roguelike genre. Play on the side of evil, embodied by the necromancer Iratus! Expand and improve your underground lair. 19 types of obedient servants: zombies, vampires, skeletons, mummies, banshees and many more! Craft minions from the body parts of your conquered enemies. Advanced combat system: to win you need to know both the strengths and weaknesses of your troops and enemies. Iratus can kill his enemies not only by magic or claw but also by draining their sanity! Each minion has six unique abilities for a total of nearly one-hundred abilities for you to command. Four talent trees that alter the way you play: Alchemy, Magic, Ire and Destruction. Roguelike elements: minions that die are gone for good and the game saves automatically, making each choice irreversible. Detailed 2D graphics and a gloomy atmosphere of dark fantasy. Various difficulty levels, satisfying every type of player from novice to hardcore. Iratus himself is voiced by the voice-acting legend Stefan Weyte, famous for his performance as Caleb in the cult game series 'Blood'!

_childDocuments_.review: You absolutely need to compare this game to Darkest Dungeons, and unfortunately it's worse in just about every way. The narrator voice is annoying, the combat is repetitive, the abilities are boring.____________Months later I decided to give Iratus another shake, and though the atmosphere still kinda annoys me (the narrator lines are bleh) - the combat and strategy is actually very good.This game plays out quite differently from darkest, with each fight being a strategic puzzle with different abilities and threats that can be addressed by changing your team composition. The difficulty of each fight is way higher and losses are way more frequent, so (at least on higher difficulty) you really need to plan each fight.It's actually quite a bit more strategic than darkest. The abilities and enemies are really well designed.I wish they didn't make it look like a darkest clone, since the gameplay itself is different and really solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Trash balance mixed with poor game choices.I bought the support pack of the game when it was on early access because at the time it wasn't as bad. idk what i missed when they decided to kill the part system of the game, where instead of being able to customize each minion you know just have a bland and boring leveling system, sane level of blandness as the items and later game enemies. Whomever tought of the design of the 4th level has issues, having enemies like the Living Armor that kill entire playstyles and make one of the most important parts of the game, the magic system, help the enemy more than it helps you is utter garabe, and im not even talking about enemies like the Sword Mistress, that one-shoted one of my minions the first time i encountered her, without any imput or play around from my part, just an 85 crit to the face.You may think all of this can be fixed by making a new team or trying to use a different strategy, and you would be extremely wrong. I used an stress party for the first 3 levels, it wasn't a cake wall, but i could win battles. All of this changed of course on level 4, because i built Iratus to be very magic centric, but it just happens that i can no longer use magic because Living Armors will get upwards of 123-135 damage neither am i able to use the full potential of an stress build because no magic and because Living Armors have no stress bar, i tried to build a pure damage build, but it just happens that they have 30 flat armor (another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and bland mechanic on the game) which makes it literally impossible to kill them as my minion are only able to pull 2-3 points of damage each time, and even when i tried to build headhunters with full stats put into damage, there is always a healer that can regenerate more health than i can chip trough. And then of course, i ran out of brains, making it impossible to experiment or try new builds, because thats just how the game operates, you have 1 team, and you stick to that team for the whole game, and if you happen to build a "bad team" its pretty much game over or having to ultra cheese the game to the point its no longer enjoyable.The game is not "Horrible" but it is one of the few games i've seen somehow become worse after release, i do not advice buying this game when there are far better and more balance/polished choices like Darkest Dungeon.Unless the devs do something to make the game actually fun to play, this review will not changeBtw, announcing a DLC that includes the ending of the game after release is a pretty ♥♥♥♥ move, very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sketchy

_childDocuments_.review: It makes the Dead Lord itself unjustice, but that's what happens when you take the idea after something. Both of these games are incredibly similar but DD is way more harder. Something worth to mention is that battles here involves our Dead Lord. Even though he is not present in the battles, you may use him to throw curses and buffs at your disposal. Combat is also easier because you cannot stress the undeads, you dont have to pay them to heal their wounds. Well thats true for undeads, but these 2 things are making the game incredibly easy once you begin rolling with your starting army, collecting bones for further troops and upgrading older units.I never lost a battle and only one unit here, meanwhile in DD my crew usualy takes weekly breaks from progressing further into harder catacombs. I don't dislike Lord of the Dead being easy, it is keeping flow and it is still challenging to adapt into new enemies. Creating your crew demands destroying your enemies and you cannot grind that. Just so you know you would rather want to be extremely careful. For example unlocking Vampire demands from you putting specific curse on enemy unit and this unit needs to flee from battle. That demands your troops to stress enemies and RNG to trigger that mind break. Ideas like that are cool because game demands more from you than just a "win" in few situations.There is still a bit of work needed to be done on this one, mainly on difficulty setting but the idea is nice, this is as close as you will get if you liked DD combat but hated it for to much grind around resources. Game is looking good has good mechanics, skillset and units. It is all coming together in a style, just missing something more to worry about, more unexpected events to play around. I am eagerly waiting for more, but please make difficulty more interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun dungeon-crawling roguelite with several interesting leveling systems. The combat is very enjoyable and is very similar to Darkest Dungeon. The game has a lot of moving parts regarding its crafting and leveling systems, which makes the meta-game an enjoyable aspect as you manage your undead army. The art and animation is good and the game is an overall fun package. I would recommend this game! However, I can't help but feel like some of the gameplay aspects are too "phone game like." It's definitely not justified to compare Iratus: Lord of the Dead to a mobile auto-battler, but a combination of small details gives off that vibe. Overall though, I would say that this game is well worth it, especially on sale. It's an enjoyable strategy game with a fun premise that lends to the purpose of its well thought out systems. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fun to play actively, also fun to load up and play a couple rounds here and there while working.  Run in a smaller window and alt-tab between meetings, etc.  Graphics are great, voice acting is solid, good depth in the various minions.  The map path choices start to be more important as you increase in difficulty.  I've been playing on both Windows and MacOS.  Super stable and performant on either platform.  Zero crashes.My play time is a bit skewed as I idle quite a bit, but I've played through 3 times, each on increasing difficulty.  The hardest difficulty, which I'm at now, actually has me thinking about restarting and hoping for better fight outcomes and random drops.  The previous difficulty was challenging, but I never really felt in danger of having to restart.  Recommend continuing on after the tutorial on easy mode just to get a sense of the game and easily explore the various team comps to see which you enjoy most.Comparing it to Darkest Dungeon:  Less grind, less negative RNG (no character insanity, for example).  I can get a bit more attached and reliably spec out the minions.  Some might find Iratus a bit less gritty and challenging than DD, but, thinking back on the two, I think part of the challenge of DD is simply tolerating the RNG frustration.  I find Iratus more fun and enjoyable.Cons?  at least up until the last difficulty, I feel once you hit a certain tipping point, you're pretty much unstoppable unless you consciously screw up.  This can make the large maps somewhat unnecessary.  Would prefer a more noticeable scaling during each level.  Course, then again, I'm getting my ass kicked on the first run of the hardest difficulty, so maybe I should calm down on that scaling idea.Overall:  Great asynch, lightweight gameplay that scratches that RPG character building dungeon crawler itch.  Recommend.

Customizing your squad after getting the idea of who sort of works with who is fairly minimal and uninspired. The item variety is... there isn't any, it's basic stat boosts, same stuff you get from upgrading the materials out of which you create the monsters. Doesn't feel very rewarding to add +6% magic damage taken. Needs something fun for higher level items and monster upgrades. Something to really set out that level 7 Skeleton with purple everything from the level 3 one except the first one has Slightly better stats, but is still just as prone to getting oneshotted. Same for the skills, as fun as they are to learn, you quite quickly get the grasp (at least for myself) which are the optimal choices for most of the early level skills and just level up each monster type the same way. Gets a bit boring after a run or two unfortunately.Great base game, length wise should be fine with 3 "stages" done and 2 more apparently to come. Lacks deeper gameplay choices and customization that I'd personally love to see more in the form of skills, items and special things to make Skeleton #7 different from skeletons number 1-6. 7/10 good value off a 20% sale. _childDocuments_.review: Overall: 7.8/10Very solid but not astounding. I'd recommend it if you're in love with turn based strategy the likes of Darkest Dungeon (hereafter referred to as DD). Consider waiting for a minor sale if you don't enjoy this kind of gameplay with a bit of difficulty.Gameplay: 7.5/10Kill the enemy squad. That's 90% of the experience. A colossal proportion of the smaller features and mechanics at play here directly influence your ability to kill the other squad. If you're taking advantage of Steam's refund policy and trying this game for 1 hour and 59 minutes, make sure you're enjoying this.Outside of combat, there's some sort of economy to grow and manage, roughly similar to XCOM's basebuilding, where you invest resources gathered from combat to improve your combat performance. For better or for worse, it's not too deep, though.When your units level up you are able to upgrade their abilities, but this system is surprisingly lacking. You have two options for each ability, and 90% of these total options will either upgrade the Primary effect of the ability (doing damage, doing stress damage, healing, etc.) or it will upgrade the Secondary effect (buffs, debuffs, effect duration, etc.). There are few times you're going to find an upgrade that opens a ton of new strategies. You can also freely upgrade your units' stats when they level up. However, I found that increasing their damage resistance was overwhelmingly effective, as it mitigated the effects of enemies getting lucky with crits many times in a row. I'm sure after playing this game more, I'll find some more interesting stat distributions, but it seems that minmaxxing your units to serve 1-2 specialized jobs is Extremely strong.Between combat, you move through the map similarly to Slay The Spire, where you choose a path that will grant you the kinds of encounters you're looking for before you reach the boss.Graphics: 8/10(?)The character models themselves are very impressive to me, but some of the animations aren't the best. Sometimes, characters will move in such a way that you can clearly see the joints on the puppets in action. On the other hand, some of the animations are simply incredible. At worst, these are Serviceable, and it only goes up from there. Although, it can look pretty goofy when a character who moves like they're in the game Barotrauma is casting a spell.Story: 3/10There's none. You're a necromancer trying to take over the world. That's about it. I didn't buy this game for the plot and neither should you. I didn't factor this into my final score, but it was worth mentioning. Despite the lack of story, the tone of the game is very consistent. Iratus narrates your experience the same way The Ancestor does in Darkest Dungeon. It adds some character to your quest.Sound: 7/10The music does its job well, both in combat and out, but it's not winning any awards. As I write this, I can't call to mind any song from the game, except the battle music of two of the worlds you travel through. After about ten hours of playing, I had switched the music off to listen to a playlist instead.The sound effects aren't super consistent with the in-game source. It's very strange. The "Dark Knight" character has one specific sound when receiving damage that makes him sound like a whiny zombie that's tripped on a ladder and fallen over. The same character has a different pain sound that makes him sound like a demon laughing menacingly when he's struck. The "Miner" enemy's primary attack sounds like he's aggressively zipping shut a zipper, while he swings a pickaxe at you. I've used these two examples because you start with a Dark Knight, and you will fight a Miner very early on. These examples will be easy to find for someone looking to experience this game and still be able to return it if they like. I'd say about 15% of the sound effects are strange like these.Overall, Iratus is a decent game, but I doubt I would ever put more than 200 hours into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game fervently, it takes a lot of the elements of Darkest Dungeon and really stands on its own feet. I can see myself investing countless hours into this game, but unfortunately the game suffers from incredibly skewed boss fights. Not, "Git gud" fight, but instead incredibly random RNG fights. An example I can recall very vividly is that of the inventor, and his 10% luck that crit 9 times of the about 12 times he used his 4 tile electrocute. Not only does the RNG seem so aggregiously skewed, but the fight doesn't seem to have been playtested either (this is an early access I'm aware) as whenever  I've put a fair amount of time into this game already and plan to put in more, but it is painful to literally throw wave after wave of perfect parties that should handle the physical damage/soak rush that this fight requires just to have the Inventor spit on my corpses. I'm not a game developer, but I can tell from the countless corpses thrown at this guy that he is incredibly overtuned, and even the streamers that I watch that are Darkest Dungeon veterans have stated that they believe the boss "wasn't playtested" or is "overtuned." I want this game to do well, and will continue trying to beat him, but I only have a surplus of so many corpses before the Inventor will have drained the last of my will out of me. TL;DR I recommend the game, but to those looking for a more casual experience with a Darkesst Dungeon feel, this is not that. The game will beat you down and keep you down. If you like a challenge, with bosses that have unique mechanics, this may be your cup of tea, but this game won't hold back. I have a fair amount of time in this, and Darkest Dungeon and believe this to be a solid entry, if a little skewed toward the RNG.EDIT: It is worth noting that the Devs have now released a balancing patch that is designed to address some of the issues with the game. When I have the time I will be attempting the boss again to determine if the changes have made a big enough impact!EDIT2: I have faced the second boss, and even with just level 1 Lost soul, Dark knight (x2) and a Skeleton, I was able to defeat the boss with only losing the Skele and Lost Soul. The change has definitely made this boss less of a headache! .

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus - A Delving Dungeon Crawler similar to Darkest Dungeon but great in it's own rightI purchased Iratus in the hopes it would be similar to Darkest Dungeon in terms of being a challenging, sometimes morbid dungeon crawler and strategy based tactic game. I was not let down. You get to play as the minions of Iratus, a dark and evil necromancer who wants to wipe the planet of anyone in his way. And let's be honest, who doesn't think it's cool to play the bad guys every so often? Iratus is challenging, and while it's in Early Access, the Devs are responsive and constantly churning out balances and fixes. They listen to the feedback of the community, and that is truly a refreshing thing when dealing with an EA title with not only tons of potential, but also a future. I've just scratched the surface in playtime thus far, and I have thoroughly enjoyed every minute of it. It's engaging, challenging, and it makes you think in terms of strategy for your teams. I enjoy it thoroughly. The only caveats that I think could use some tweaking is obviously some balance issues with the Zombie early on. He can be extremely powerful (albeit I am playing on the Normal mode). That said, each minion has it's strengths and weaknesses. I do wish the Tutorial was a little more indepth as far as upgraded "body parts" for creating your minions, I kind of had to figure that out on my own, with trial and error. Also, it is a bit confusing as to what the items are for and the artifacts also. That said, those are only minor things, and with it indeed being Early Access, I am positive the tutorial will be more in depth as time goes on. The only major gripe I have is not towards the game itself or the developers, mainly the publisher. I absolutely loathe the "advertising" of other games in the title screen. I think it's cheap, tacky, and completely takes away from the immersive experience every dungeon crawler should have. I highly recommend you pick this game up if you like rogue like dungeon crawlers. It's fun, challenging and unique. Enjoy and kill all the humans!Edit: While I understand that the publishers advertising is just "new projects", I still find it intrusive, annoying, and ultimately tacky. I don't want to see advertisements or "suggestions" of other games from a publisher when I am starting an immersive game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Ignore reviews that say this game is unbalanced. Give it a shot!So I've been watching this game for a while now, and finally bought it on sale. I'd seen a lot of reviews go into detail about things that need to be fixed, or keep it from being fun long-term. So buying this was a bit of a risk. However! I love this game! I know there's a disclaimer at the beginning that says this game will be super difficult, but that entirely depends on the difficulty setting you choose. At easier levels, it is possible to play this game casually, but don't expect to not give your moves any thought. One of the things I saw people complain about the most was running out of minions, crafting goods, and other resources late into the game, and feeling like you wasted an entire playthrough. Given the complexity of the resource system - everything forces you to make a choice - I don't see how this is possible. If you consistently ignore the importance of certain resources, you will probably reach a point where you can't continue, but the game is well-balanced and does a good job of sending you clues that you need to be working on things that will keep your undead army balanced. As far as other aspects go, the aesthetic design is wonderful. The voice acting sounds perfect for the genre, and the art style embodies its slightly-irreverent tone. Enemies and minions are varied, and no one of them is exactly like another. Between the minions and enemies, there are no "mirrors" or characters that are just faction copies of each other.

_childDocuments_.review: Be a necromancer. Command a horde of stupid undead and ghosts, smash puny mortals with a rain of fire and expoding skulls.Gather their parts to build even more undead...It is a great game! Huge potential! Very well exectued mixture of Darkest Dungeon (Combat / Building) / Slay the Spire (Progression). I realy enjoyed my first two runs. It might be difficult though. Make your enemies go insane and attack each other, skip turns or run away.Graphics, interface, sounds, music, voice acting, animations, characters, ...  Lots of usefull spells, sadly some are utterly useless, overpriced or a waste of skillpointsI like the idea behind it, but right now it lacks the depth that the other featues have, could be improved, but nevertheless I like the direction. Maybe implement crafting of items for Lord Iratus. There is an abundance of items to gather!They just pile up and I dont know what to do with them. Build everything I could / needed and still had an abundance of them flying around... maybe let the player spend them on something - shops or convert into ressources?And this one building that creates more architect souls... it's not needed at all. _childDocuments_.review: Overall i think this game is really greatThe art style great and i love it and the gameplay is really fun and keeps you hooked, you get to play the bad guy and theres lots of nice game mechanics that give the game a good feel and make it challenging but keep it enjoyable. It keeps you coming back for more even at this early stage.  Whilst it is like darkest dungeon in reverse you playing the bad guys, the game does have its unique mechanics and ways of play. Alchemy plays a big part in making sure you succeed as you progress, again im wondering how many people have actually paid attention to this game mechanic before giving up and writing a negative review. As well as this your  undead minions can curse and stress enemies , you remember how many times your dudes died of heart attacks in darkest dungeon well you can make your enemies die of stress in this game and its a great fun way to defeat tougher foes , instead of knocking down thier health you can turn them insane and even cause some to betray each other. Its little things like this and using your minions correctly and thier abilities that make the game more fun. I think some of the negative reviews just havent given the game chance or explored some of these mechanics enough.Once you learn the game its a lot of fun and you unlock more powereful minions as you progress im enjoying my run at the moment, im part way through the second tunnels after beating the first boss, im close to unlocking the bone golem and bwhich sounds grusoemly ace,  im about halfway through the dwarven tunnels and yes i have lost a few squads but have been able to rebuild. this is simmilar to darkest dungeon.  I have been able to keep my best critters alive though and have 2 high levels so this as kinda what i expected from the game. Yes the game does need some balancing as some enemies do hit high crits and this can be a bit odd, but as i already pointed out at the start this is on the roadmap and im confident the devs will pick this up and balance the game out more its very ealry days and the games still in its early release. but as i already said this is on the roadmap.  I think the game deserves the credit its due its a lot of fun to play and keeps you hooked theres a lot of depth to it that the creators have obviously put time and effort into making Iratus a unique game. I dont think it deserves a mixed response its in its early stages still and when you look at the roadmap i wonder how many people reveiwing the game have seen that the  constant balance changes are something that are on the roadmap for the games development. Overall brilliant game and good challening fun, great in depth mechanics , learn it and it will pay off worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Dead'uns and Deadbeats, Clappy here. Today, I am reviewing Iratus: Lord of the Dead and Dank, a turn based roguelike dungeon crawler set in an alternate timeline where Mortis worshippers from Disciples were never banned from magic schools and the Empire was...well, still the Empire but with more heretic burning. StoryYou take on the role as Iratus, a necromancer who, attempting to fulfil his perfectly reasonable childhood dream of being hailed as a supreme master over the known world, but being misunderstood by his fellow man to be 'overstepping moral boundaries' of starting wars with other people for personal benefit, sent 'heroes' (haters) who killed him just as he was about to decimate humanity. Normally in fairy tales, this is where the story ends and the heroes throw a party to celebrate, game over. However, Iratus had a trick up his sleeve: he had achieved relative immortality and so was imprisoned far beneath the earth to stew in eternal hatred at how close he was to making Mama and Daddy proud. But then, in a stroke of luck, braindead human and the boyz break into his chamber, overturned his grave and tried to rob him, a necromancer with hundreds of years of experience, blind of riches. Jokes on them, they get reminded of their lowborn place in fantasy society, and now Iratus can restart his anti-human revolution against the government to revoke their right to live and breathe ever again.In my opinion, the story is simple and to the point which I like in such a game and the in-game texts to explain the dungeons and characters are interesting though I felt they could do more with Iratus' background, so I give it 7/10 on that.Gameplay Let me clarify, though the gameplay plays similar to Darkest Dungeon, there are differences that make Iratus its own game. For one, your meat shields won't stress out, panic and sabotage your dungeon experience forcing you to waste your money buying supplies because some idiot in a level 1 dungeon decided it was time to snack FOR THE THIRD ♥♥♥♥♥ TIME IN A SINGLE HAL-*ahem*. In this game, you are the menace fighting humanity, undead don't need morale!! They just need targets inflicting damage on your foes either by  blunt force trauma until they stop spilling blood (Physical), or cause debuffs and heart attacks (Stress) like forcing a weeb to watch badly dubbed anime and skipping openings (but be careful, like in Darkest Dungeon your enemies can sometimes become 'virtuous' or in this game's case Inspired with buffs for themselves or the whole party not just around healing stress and health). You as a necromancer have access to Mana, you're not hiding behind mercenaries relying on their abilities and survivability when you can personally throw bones from the sky or help your stress build by inflicting Stress damage yourself if your minions are acting incompetent. Wrath is another mechanic that lets your units perform their 'ultimates' to turn a fight in your favour or gain an early advantage, each minion has one that can go from position traps to outright killing an enemy instantly if certain conditions are met.You are fighting from the bowels of the earth to the surface, dead corpses are your fuel for the war machine creating new minions, potions if you have the DLC using body parts which you can find by simply fighting enemy parties that stand in your way and cutting them down. There is a hub, the Cemetary where Iratus can use his own minions to upgrade buildings (non-refundable) that give benefits like base mana you start combat with, healing your units and increasing Iratus' experience ( Spellpower ) which means you can use Spells with less Mana and skillpoints to spend in his own unique skill trees for more powerful abilities in and out of the battlefield. The dungeon boss doesn't need x missions completed to show themselves, they're at the end of the dungeon waiting behind their meat shields cowering until you come to them. However, the size of the dungeons will test your resource and minion management and quest battles, though this is alleviated by other events in between fights such as quests having the option for you to not involve yourself sparing your team further pain, health and mana founts to heal your units or Iratus' mana pool and artefacts/items which you can equip to Iratus and/or minions giving them unique bonuses. The minion roster isn't completely unlocked for you, no you start with a set few unlocked while the rest have conditions to fulfil through multiple playthroughs that you must complete to earn them, but when you do you get options to expand your playstyle and how to weaken your enemies.I have a lot of fun with this personally, as there is replayable value for me and I enjoy testing out new teams on the living. Though I felt tension going through the dungeon and considering my odds in fights, careful planning and playing with comps aided me through the stages even when they on the rare occasion gave me glass cannon teams to stack odds against me. I felt the hub wasn't too complicated and the UI was user-friendly to me. Solid 9/10.Overall my thoughts are that Iratus is a great experience, and if you want to feel like a bad guy underdog trying to fulfil his hopes and reasonable dream of world domination weaving spells and making minions powerful to enforce your desires while enjoying a reasonable difficulty curve, it is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, yes it is a bit hard and unforgiving, but that is the point of it, once you learn about the units it is way easier to progress in a stable fashion. Shortly after release there were plenty of negative reviews and complaints about the difficulty, people couldn't kill the first boss etc. I myself fully wiped on the second boss. But if you actually spend more than a few hours playing you will learn what synergies work between your units and what you need for certain enemies (especially bosses). Guess what? Now the forums is full of different setups that all can beat these bosses, who would have known you would just need to read the abilities, think, and learn about the enemies in order to beat them? Some people seem to expect to beat the game with a rag tag team of misfits without any thought behind the composition.I made sure to try all the new units, once I got the Lost Soul my favorite comp was set: Mummy, Lost Soul, and two Dark Knights, they took me from the start to the end of the current game (beating the third boss finished the current state of EA) without any real issues.Things that should be addressed: One major downside is the retreat option, especially when it kills your entire team if the game crashes. It would be better to just restore the save. Punishing accidents is way worse than allowing people to abuse the save system by alt-f4:ing, especially considering that they can probably just backup the saves if they really wanted to.Add a casual difficulty: where a full wipe isn't necessary, maybe return the materials for units, or let the user farm back materials in other fights. Just disable all achievements in this mode. My partner would love to play this game but she can't stand the frustration of losing all her progress so she stays away from roguelike games. :/I'll be back when more content releases! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on the Darkest Dungeons formula with a pinch of Slay the Spire level design that lets you play as the bad guy for a change.Graphics and Artwork are nicely done and fitting the theme, Resource Management is pretty extensive and working well (you can spend the resources you loot from defeated enemies on creating new minions, refilling your mana, healing your troops, combining them to gain items to equip your troops with... so you always can do something with your loot instead of just "saving up gold"). The ability to equip and level the Alter Ego of the player and have him cast spells in the battles is a nice addition.There is some variety in both enemies and own minions as well so you can experiment with different groups and strategies quite a bit.Overall a work well done and good value. Looking forward to future releases from the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Visually pleasing and very challenging. I had to delete my first run of the game because I failed to kill the first boss and didn't have the resources to continue on. Then I made a few test runs, googled a bit and then I beat the game.Pros: - Cool concept and very cool art style.- Many characters to unlock with much interplay and different tactics you can do. Unlocking characters is game-wide, not specific to that run.- Similar to Darkest Dungeon in a good way.Cons / suggestions: - The game isn't that long as of yet and more dungeons is needed. I beat it in 12h which includes being AFK and doing test runs. I'm going to replay it on the harder difficulty and unlock the remaining characters though.- Needs more paths to take when walking around the dungeon, I'd like it to be more similar to darkest dungeon in that sense. When you take a turn in the dungeon, you are locked to it and need to follow it until the next cross section. When you have reached the boss you cannot go back and explore. This is what results in you needing to restart the game if you can't beat the boss and run out of resources. You need a way to recover after a total loss, such as being able to go back and fight a few battles to get some resources in order to take on the boss again.- Needs a retreat button, it sucks having to loose all characters if you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and didn't bring the right composition for the fight, and then potentially having to restart the game because of it.- Narrator should read quest texts and stuff!- Save is deleted when you kill the last boss, needs to be changed ASAP. I didn't mind though.Overall I enjoyed the experience enough to recommend the game, and I'm sure they will fix many of the issues in the near future!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this entire game (Necromancer bundle + skin sets) for 17 dollars, lesser than the cost of some other roguelite base games. But I like this game for the very reason I like DMing in 5e; the monsters are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. The variations in the monster designs really bring this game to life,. from werewolves, to mummies, to flesh abominations, and the fact that you craft them out of the body parts of your enemies. In fact, most things are made from the parts of your enemies., and there's even a uncommon/rare part system to variate their stats. Brains allow you to level up characters you just created (in which their level is their only in the tiniest amount of flavor text). The combat system has more in common with Darkest Dungeon than say Slay the Spire or Legend of Keepers, and the game seems pretty fair so far. I highly recommend this game to people who like different character playstyles (examples being the werewolf's ability to set a trap, the abomination's ability to shield their friends while attacking the enemy), while keeping a base fundamental between them as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great, satisfying itch for a game similar to DD. Animations, art, narration, music are all spectacular. Each unit has multiple abilities with 1-2 ultimate abilities that require a special resource from Iratus. I actually like this concept as it makes each play more strategic. Some of the units though are completely not worth playing, I'm looking at you Lost Soul.  She is actually really neat but the negative effects on the enemies do not even get close to out-weighing (or just making even) the positive effects she applies to the enemies as well. However, that's what early access is for and i'm certain things will get balanced out. My biggest complaint is the progression cycle. It gets old FAST.  Take DD, you had multiple options to progress and the paths weren't so linear. With Iratus:LotD, you only have one path, and if you fail its back to the very beginning for you. Now you do get to keep all the creatures that you've unlocked, BUTTT the cost to create them, level them and upgrade their parts completely destroys your run. When I reached the first boss, I had about 5 armed and level units, I beat the boss and lost all of them but 1. got enough materials to make a few new units they start at level 1 too, always. On the first battle of the second floor I lost my whole crew, and couldn't progress because you can't upgrade or obtain materials without WINNING battles. That is what kills it for me. In DD it hurt to loose your top units BUT you had ways to get them back up without having to start over. You had to grind and grind but you could get back and kick their ass.  In Iratus you don't, if you loose any of your top Units you are done, you'll slowly drain out until you have to start over. Once those level 5 units with Epic or Legendary parts that took ALL your materials on the whole first floor die you are screwed, and its not like you can go back and reload. DD punished you for mistakes but gave you time to learn and try again. Iratus Lord of the Dead, Punishes you, shoves you to the floor, kicks you in the balls/boobs. When you try to get back up it it jumps on you and cuts your head off. GAME OVER.Having such a major problem can ruin this game quickly, however there are several ways they could fix this that would be quite simple. I'm recommending because, it has huge potential, its the first day of early access and I want to give the team time to read the feedback and see what they adjust.  I don't want to have to change my recommendation to a thumbs down and I hope they truly listen to the feedback and make the appropriate changes. They have a great thing here and it would shame to see it crash.

_childDocuments_.review: After a Dev response I decided to reword my review into a more constructive and accurate one. First playthrough is really fun (+-6-8h), characters are many, animations are nice and I like the setup.Things I really dislike: The second difficlty starts out great but after a couple of matches the cheapshots start. Not being attentive one second and you will suddenly get struck with 10.000 more damage then your character really has. I mean, Just let the action do 50 percent or 80 percent damage but not this. It feels like a cheap way to ramp up difficulty, and it is supersudden instead of gradual.Then my biggest complaint atm , and the second reason why i wouldn't recommend this at the time is how u follow one path and one path only. You can at no point backtrack or take a big rong road. You are stuck to one path basicallly, left or right. _childDocuments_.review: Iratus Lord of the Dead takes Darkest Dungeon, turns it around and end result is better game in overall. Being in receiving end of dread and insanity is not as fun as inflicting them. Though Darkest Dungeon is still worth it as an experience, just finishing it might feel like a chore after playing Iratus. What both share is the line based combat. Both sides have their characters in a line and abilities are based on the position. So positioning the minions right really matters. Layout most likely won't static during the fight as some minions have abilities that move them around. Which might prevent other minions of using their most useful abilities as they might end up in wrong place. There's also multiple damage types, which means that knowing the enemy helps as you know their weaknesses and abilities even before the fight starts. Which means you can plan ahead better. There's humarium that you can use to look that information up. It won't be filled up right away though, you have to collect randomly awarded tokens, which means that in order to unlock the whole thing, you have play the game multiple times.Despite of what the game states of minions not being expendable, it's still somewhat forgiving. Minions will get experience and raise their level, but levels are mostly based on the brain (quality of parts being the other factor). Plug in high level brain to fresh minion and you'll get quite many levels and access to customizing abilities right away. So if you lose a minion, you should be able to create something close to the previous one if you don't lose too many of your minions. Good stuff will eventually run out and only thing left is parts for cannon fodder. Keep losing even more and you'll run out of even the bad parts.Between the fights you have multiple ways of improving things like using alchemy and artifacts to get and edge on next fight. If you have the Wrath of the Necromancer DLC, you can also brew potions. Most of the things will consume your stock of parts, so you have to balance things a bit in order to keep current minions alive or have enough parts to create new ones. Different minions are constructed from different combination of parts, so having stock of everything helps. You might also have to heal your minions in mortuary, so they will unavailable for next fight. Which in turn might mean that you have to rethink your tactics and come up with new potential synergies. Unless you have spare of same kind minion of course.As Iratus is kind of reverse dungeon crawler (you are climbing up from a dungeon instead climbing down) there's a dungeon that you have to traverse. Implementation resembles Slay the Spire as you choose paths from already revealed map. So choices do matter as you can plan your route beforehand. You can only change your direction in intersections, so once you commit to a hallway, you'll have to go through it. You'll also have to move always forwards toward your goal, so exploring whole dungeon is not an option.Sound and graphics deserve special mention. They really make it extra satisfaction of lashing out dread and damage to the opponents. Low health is really visible on the opponents (unless the damage is inside). Add over the top narrator to the mix and it gets even better.Minion types are unlocked via multiple ways, but the unlocks are permanent. So there's few new minions maybe for three playthroughs. Especially because few minions are unlocked by finishing the game with certain difficulty. It doesn't matter if you have played these line based battlers (there must be proper term, but I haven't seen any), Iratus is better to the competition by large enough margin. If you totally disliked Darkest Dungeon, you probably won't like this one either as main mechanics are so similar. But in all other cases, Iratus is worthy addition to your collection.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of strategy games and rougelikes, Iratus feels like dream come true. It takes existing rougelike styles and takes an approach that ramps up the level of strategy and makes resource management a real component of the game. I managed to complete what currently exists of the game on my first run, but the allure of many minion types to play around with and the many build styles that come with that, along with higher difficulties to conquer, makes it likely I'll be sinking many many more hours into the game. The game is certainly difficult, but for the most part not unfairly so. And while the game needs balancing, the devs have been putting out balance patches on a fast pace and that is what early access is for. This game has plenty of content as is, and the roadmap the devs laid out for early access is promising even more minion types to try, more enemy variety, more dungeon levels, and just overall more variety to most aspects of the game that will further extend it's replayability. So far this is certainly early access done right.

_childDocuments_.review: So I want to open by saying that this game is a lot of fun. Minions are entertaining, artwork is grand, and you can blow through hours fine-tuning your teams to be the ultimate hero-killers. I love Iratus, and have been waiting on it ever since it was first announced. But there are a few serious issues with it in Early Access that may or may not be dealbreakers for some people who enjoyed Darkest Dungeon. I do hope that some of these issues will be fixed in future, but as they are now, they add unnecessary problems to the gameplay.----------------Stress. In Darkest Dungeon, Stress worked as an extra statistic that forced you to attend to the mental health of your party.If you didn't take care of it, characters that you had worked on for days and days could just keel over dead, making the player panic and rush to fix severe mental scarring in a hurry. In Iratus, Stress amounts to little more than an extra health bar that MOST enemies have, that claims to give debuffs and insanities to enemies, but seems to have a negligible impact outside of the occasional backstab done on its own teammate, and the damage done is so low that I might as well have just done the damage myself. Also, Battles are random, certainly, but there are minions that ONLY affect the stress bar, but enemies that don't have one at all that can just appear out of nowhere. So if you have a couple Stress minions, and a couple physical minions, half your Alpha team just went into the crapper as soon as a golem or elemental shows up. I sincerely hope that this is fixed in a future patch, and that sanity becomes a MUCH more important feature, but as of right now it has little to no point outside of adding padded time to an already drawn out combat.Story.Why is it that every time a game claims "Embrace evil. Be the bad guy!" they always feel the need to make the 'heroes' just as bad, or comically bent? I'm an ancient, forgotten evil on a pissed-off rampage. The first thing I see? Mind controlled slaves, villainous taskmasters and corrupt dwarves. If I'm to be evil, stop giving me 'good guys' that are written to be just as bad! Greedy diggers cracking open my tomb is one thing, but after 30 fights with corpse-robbers, insane mages, drugged slaves and malicious mercenaries, I'm seriously starting to wonder if I'm actually the bad guy here.Iratus himself.Holy crap the guy yaps like an old woman on a long distance phone call. Every spell, attack, ability, and so on, he has something to add, and it's usually something he's added a gajillion times already. There's only one line of dialogue per spell that you can cast, and he belts out the same line for each spell, over and over like a busted phonograph. I've heard the words "How about a little tingle up your spine?" so many times that the captions are burned into my eyelids. He seriously either needs to ease up, or some more lines of dialogue should be added to give him some variety.The backpack.Explain to me why we need a bar at the top that counts our resources, but also need to see every single non-stackable instance of those resources in a bag when we're trying to find a single piece of gear? I have pages and pages of skulls, but one single Etched Bone. We don't really need all that clutter, do we?The Dungeon.Darkest Dungeon was a good game, with custom heroes that you could work from rags to riches under your own power. Iratus tries to have the same, but lacks a key feature that we desperately need. The random dungeon. If we can't go to grind materials and levels, what is the point of having these minions level at all? Without the ability to go back and grind, necessary resources become harder to get, and thus, if you have one bad run or glitch, it can essentially outright end a game. I don't mean we need some procedural generator for content or anything, but the ability to go back and travel the paths we didn't walk down in the existing dungeon might be nice, rather than having several paths on a procedural map be locked off forever, meaning that the game put in all that work for nothing at all and might as well have just given us a linear corridor for all the good the randomized design does..To the creators of Iratus, I want you to know that this list of complaints really is a love letter, and that I have already burned through several hours of gameplay with the intent to play a lot more. I want it to do well, as it really is a stellar Early Access game. It's fun to lay traps, set up combos, murder dudes with zombie cannoneers and evil spells. But some aspects of the game are just... not as fun. I hope you don't take upset at this review and I look forward to the day when I can flip around and say "BEST GAME EVAR!".Love,A Huge Fan

Easy mode is very easy so far.  A couple times I sent in a rookie team against a big fight to scout it out and they win anyway.  I had to retreat out of the fight before it ended in order to make sure my big boys got the xp from the boss fights. _childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wish I could give a neutral rating. It's not a bad game, but it's not that great either. There's a ton of tedium between each fight. The enemy diversity tries to encourage different builds, but almost any strategy is going to work. The only enemy that forced me to change strategy was the monks.The game isn't long, but the time I spent getting through every floor felt long because nothing really different happens. The most interesting nodes you can interact with are the mini-quests, but even those boil down to "Have a specific minion you wouldn't know to bring" or "Do an extra optional fight for rewards". It's a ton of choices with lots of micromanagement, and not enough pizazz. You even have to re-select the group you've made every time you open the map. It's a ton of constant small choices, and nothing feels like a significant choice.The strengths the game has is actually the fact that you can make almost anything work. It's fun making a Boiling Blood Werewolf or Lich and having it solo the world. This is fun enough to carry the game pretty far, but not enough to totally save it.Overall it's extremely mediocre. It's a ton of constant tiny decision making without any impact, but at least the massive number of choices means you can play around with tons of builds.

_childDocuments_.review: I fell out of love with Darkest Dungeon and Iratus solved many of my complaints.One of my biggest ones is how DD encourages overly cautious play. You want to delay turns for extra vestal heals, spend extra turns removing stress, and err on the side of overpreparedness since failure means goodbye to many hours of progression. This makes an already long game longer, and I do not find "maximize combat length without the game noticing" to be fun. Iratus just lets me focus on having fun tactical battles. I also appreciate that because each battle is broken up, you can mix up teams much more frequently and combats can be harder in general.It is probably unlikely Iratus will ever fully get out of Darkest Dungeon's shadow, but for me it is a game I like to play whereas Darkest Dungeon is just a game I like the IDEA of playing (until I remember having to juggle stun locks and heals at the end of every combat).

_childDocuments_.review: So Iratus is an interesting game. I came into it thinking it would be a game similar to Darkest Dungeon and played it as such...which led me to not enjoy the game at all! Once I realized I had to approach the game completely different from DD, i.e. not getting attached to characters AT ALL, in fact there is a minion with a super strong heal built around sacrificing your other minions, I started having a ton of fun.The game is HARD, borderline cheap in some cases but if you persevere there is a rewarding and challenging game that awaits you. Contrary to what many people say every minion is viable, not sure about the Ghoul as I haven't unlocked it yet. Not every minion is as good as the next but I think that is what makes the game interesting. I found a lot of enjoyment in figuring out OP, in my opinion, combos or going all in on good body part rolls. The former gave me a lot of strategizing through multiple playthroughs and the latter let me come up with strategies on the fly (and let me try minions I wouldn't normally use).Enemies are HARD, harder than DD in my opinion. They are unforgiving and can feel cheap at times, however, if you approach the game from a Necromancer's point of view, i.e. minions are expendable, you will have a lot more fun. Once I embraced this mindset I enjoyed overwhelming my enemies with numbers rather than super elite units (which you can still get, it just requires sacrifice of other units to get there, for me anyway).The TLDR is to approach this game with an open mind and devote time to master it. If you do you will have a great time!My only annoyances so far are the following:1. I want more ways to effect enemy stats/actions (not just stress)2. The Ghoul is WAY harder to unlock than the other minions (if not explicitly trying to unlock it)3. More ways of retaining your high level parts after a minion dies would be nice and help when a party wipes. I get the game is supposed to be hard, but it should just end the game at some point when you lose enough parts because it feels like an exercise in futility to use base part minions to try and get past the super hard fight you just lost to.Additionally, I really love the art direction of the game! I'm really looking forward to the new levels and enemy/minion content!I only mention my 1st point because I enjoy debuffing more than I enjoy doing direct damage. But the design for synergies is really fun. I particularly like Wraith, Shade, Banshee, Vampire as a party ^.^. I really like how much insanity effects the game. It gives interesting mechanics as well as just flat debuffs. Very well implemented in my opinion!Overall I think this game is great and a welcome addition to the genre! Definitely going to keep following this game and looking forward to updates!

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT REVIEWThis review is for the Wrath of the Necromancer Edition which includes the DLCs as I bought it as a bundle.  The comparisons to Darkest Dungeon are unavoidable but don't think of this as just a Darkest Dungeon clone, it is actually a much better game than Darkest Dungeon.PLOT:  The plot is pretty standard fantasy fare.  An evil necromancer has awoken from his imprisonment in an underground complex and is sending forth hordes of undead to destroy the world and the forces of good must rally together to defeat him.  The twist with this game is that you are playing the evil necromancer.COMBAT:  Its a 4 vs 4 tactical combat game.GRAPHICS & SOUND:  The graphics and sound are very good but where this game really excels is the voice acting for Iratus himself which is absolutely superb and really sets the game apart from many others.REPLAY VALUE:  Very Good.  Its a roguelike with 4 difficulty settings ranging from Cakewalk (Easy) to Eternal Harvest (Very Hard).ISSUES AND BUGS: The game runs “straight out of the box” and appears to be bug free.ACHIEVEMENTS AND TRADING CARDS:  Full integration with the Steam platform.VALUE FOR MONEY:  Average at full price.  However, it's definitely one to put it in the “wait for a discount” category.  Its not an old game (only just over 2 years old at the time of writing) but even so it comes round on offer regularly and with a big discount at which point I rate it as excellent.  (It was 80% off in the Steam 2022 Summer sale and was on a similar discount about a month before the sale and again a month after the sale.)LONG REVIEWWhen reviewing Iratus Lord of the Dead it is impossible to do so without making comparisons to Darkest Dungeon but it should not be thought of as purely a Darkest Dungeon clone.  At the highest level it is darkest dungeon in reverse with you playing the bad guys and making the heroes go insane.The gameplay is more streamlined than Darkest Dungeon with much less micro management involved.  Effectively items/trinkets are a one time allocation (once they are assigned that cannot be unassigned although they can be overwritten).. There is no “equipping your party” and no “inventory management” involved so the level of micro management required is significantly reduced.The elements of grind and randomness that plague Darkest Dungeon have also been removed.  In Iratus you probably need to develop 2 parties (you can do it with 1 but probably need some back-ups) as opposed to the 4 required in Darkest Dungeon and the brains offer a way to bring new minions in at higher level without having to grind them up from the start.  It also feels a lot less random that Darkest Dungeon.  Darkest Dungeon suffers from a “there is nothing you could do about that, the RNG just hates you” feeling.  I'm sure Iratus has an RNG in the background somewhere but its far less intrusive.Iratus also has 4 difficulty settings as opposed to 3 in Darkest Dungeon  I would say the game is easier than Darkest Dungeon as effectively the 4th difficulty setting (Cakewalk) is at the lower end of the scale.  This addresses the biggest problem with Darkest Dungeon and that is that the game is just too ****ing hard!All in all Iratus Lord of the Dead is not just a Darkest Dungeon clone, it is actually a much better game than Darkest Dungeon.Generally I'm not a fan of DLCs (they are often just a blatant cash grab) but the ones for this game aren't too bad as they actually and contain a reasonable amount of content.  The additional skin sets strike me as rather pointless and are probably best avoided.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who plays a lot of Darkest Dungeon on my Switch and some on the PC I am a huge fan of the genre.  I have had my eye on Iratus: Lord of the Dead since it was first announced on Steam and so happy that it is now released to Early Access.The big stuff out of the way first: 1) While it shares a lot in common with Darkest Dungeon it does make plenty of changes that set it part and improve on the formula.   Normally I am not a fan of playing the bad guy but this game certainly makes playing the bad guy, "good".   Some people will think that the only difference between DD and Iratus is you are playing the Antagonist however that is really one of the minor difference.  So if that is your concern you can reset easy, it isn't just a reskin of Darkest Dungeon.  2) That game was completely stable during my 90+ minutes of playtime so far.  No crashes or bugs that I could tell.  I also didn't notice any mechanic bugs, however as I am still getting the hang of the game it could just be that I wasn't aware of them.The fun factor is there as is the, just one more turn factor.   The artwork is nice and the voice acting is good too and has plenty of humor.   Combat is pretty straightforward if you are used to Darkest Dungeon.  Like Darkest Dungeon if you go straight for the enemies health you may be sitting yourself up for failure.  The game is all about strategy and getting to learn your enemy.   Even after a few run-ins against the Doomsayer I still make a lot of mistakes against that particular character/class/enemy that would have had me pulling my hair out, if I had any.I am a firm believer in posting an initial review and then coming back after I have a fair number of hours under my belt and reviewing.  That said if my gaming time continues to be as fun as it has been so far then I feel that this is a game well worth the asking price and can't wait to see where the developers take it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, we're all here hoping to get some more of that Darkest Dungeon fix, don't deny it. This review will probably contain many references to DD, but the developers pretty much brought it on themselves.The Premise is pretty much exactly what I'd want out of this kind of game - You're the big bad ascending from his tomb after 1,000 years to wreak havoc and go for World Domination attempt 2, Electric Boogaloo. You build up your army from bits and bobs taken from your slain foes, nice Necromancy delivering all you need for your minions. A feature I particularly like is that these parts (Bones, armor, flesh, ectoplasm, etc.) come in many levels of powerful, and slapping them on a minion means they get more stat points. So you can start a level 1 minion with some really decent stats if you save up, or upgrade some of your longer-standing ones further. More on leveling later.The Minions themselves are quite varied, certainly visually. Werewolves, many types of Ghosts, all flavors of flesh amalgamations, some magical constructs, and more. Having a look at the trailers will tell you the sort of beasties at your disposal. Unlocking new ones feels rewarding because not only do you have more options, you *want* to play around with this cool new monster. The designs are fantastic and it makes me very happy to see the Developers didn't cheap out and make things a reskin. It really makes you feel like the Big Bad Evil Guy with his horde of nightmare creatures.Their abilities fit with their themes and usually have fun names to boot. All of their abilities are unlocked from the start and are only restricted by unit positioning, unlike in DD where you could only equip 4 but also had to worry about positioning. I'd say that this is primarily because combat has a lot more shuffle - your minions and the enemies are often moving positions of their own volition and in response to attacks. Having limited ability slots would mean you'd either have to choose one ability to work for each spot or just be screwed if the shuffle puts you in a tight spot. Though in DD you could have a character move instead of using an ability, in Iratus you have to use a spell to move someone 1 space, and you can only cast 1 spell per round of combat, and there's a dozen better things you could be doing with that spell instead of moving so it feels like an odd decision from Unfrozen.Let's get into combat a bit more. Your minions are slaughtering people, and people generally have two bars - Health and Sanity. They also have varying kinds of resistances to physical, sanity, and mental damage. In addition, there are Shields and Wards, which will tank any 1 hit from their corresponding source (Wards pull double-duty for magic and sanity damage). These can make the first rounds of combat something of a slog as you put out attacks just to wear down their blocks unless your minions have abilities to bypass them. Now, your minions can get these too, which levels the playing field somewhat, but it still feels slow from it.Stress damage is a nice addition to the combat instead of restricting things to mere health damage. It make sense thematically - we're the BBEG after all, and our minions have no such concerns for sanity, but all the squishy mortals do. Rather than trying to stab a particularly tough opponent to death, you could stress him to the point of having a heart attack, drive them insane, make them flee in terror, or just turn on their allies. However, like in DD, there's a chance that they may become inspired under the pressure and become a bigger threat. Higher difficulties increases this chance of Inspiration, but certain trinkets can negate this entirely and guarantee they'll never become so.Trinkets are part of your Loadout. Iratus himself can be equipped with artifacts in certain slots that grant bonuses of varying quality. Like a sickle that boosts minions if their combined party is low-level, or a cloak that permanently increases minion damage if they land killing blows on enemies. There's also that trinket I mentioned which disables enemy Inspiration, which makes dealing Stress Damage a really effective option for dealing with multiple enemies - just let them weigh each other down and it'll all go smoother. There's also Minion artifacts - they have 2 slots and you can't pull them out - once it's spent on a minion, it's stuck there. Some combinations of equipment and minions can feel quite unbalanced, like ones that deal percentage damage to health and sanity of enemies every time that minion uses an ability. I like to slap it on my riposte minions to whittle down the whole enemy squad.On the topic of unbalanced are Spells, but first comes Leveling. Iratus' minions level up from combat while Iratus levels up all the time. As minions level, you can boost some of their stats like damage, evasion, adding wards or shields, so on. Iratus has some standard RPG trees in 4 disciplines that basically boil down to Resources, Buffs, Curses, and Damage spells. When you level up, you get a point, as well as some boosts to your Rage and Spellpower. Spellpower does what it says on the tin while Rage allows minions to execute special moves in combat. For some spells, Spellpower means more damage or boosting, but for others it means cheaper casting. There's a spell called "Fate" which guarantees the next attack from a minion will be a critical. This is very powerful and useful for your hard-hitting minions like the Werewolf or the Zombie. And then there's the Bride who has a dedicated attack that does way more crit damage than normal, so you just hit her with it and let her chomp healthbars by half.This all may sound like the game gets easy once you learn the tricks, really it's more that you HAVE to learn the tricks to stand more of a fighting chance, especially on the harder difficulties. You have 16 minion slots in your squad bar, and it's because you should expect your minions to be getting pretty well hammered or killed. Now, this is to be expected - they're your minions, dying is in the job description. It also sort of forces you to try out squad variations and new minions you acquire. You have to really learn your enemies' attacks and skills to help keep your minions un-alive. Some enemies can utterly wreck your squishier dudes if you don't negate stances or take out certain foes first. Playing intelligently and planning your turns out will keep you going, but remember that you're still going to take losses. Keep at it, and crush the mortals beneath your feet.The final thing I'll touch on is the "Story" not that there really is much, and that's a problem for me. Darkest Dungeon's story was all-pervading; it was in the descriptions of characters and buildings, the explanation of bosses, the state of the manor and hamlet, and the foes you faced. The Ancestor's narration constantly gave more insight and meaning to everything you did, and by the end you felt like you understood everything that had happened. "In time, you will know the tragic depths of my failings..." he says. Buuuuuuuuuut that's not here.Iratus' goal is to rise from the underground and try to take over the world. The most "story" you get outside of that is 2 cutscenes near the end and some brief boss text walls. Iratus still narrates like the Ancestor does - in combat and as you expand your base and create minions, but it lacks the same depth. What I mean is Iratus just sort of talks smack or gives a comment on his thoughts. He never expounds on how mortals have changed and advanced, memories of some of the areas, allusions to these battles you're fighting being like ones of old, none of it. There's no sense of discovery or wonder to it, of getting to know the narrator and his story. It just feels lacking. His voice acting and lines are good, very good, but just lacking.Overall, this is a fun and interesting game with mechanics hard to find elsewhere. Support Unfrozen - they did good work and I want to see more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: When thinking about Iratus, I always compare and contrast it with Darkest Dungeon.  They're very similar games in some ways but in others they're quite different.  In Darkest Dungeon, you play as someone who has returned to their ancestral home/estate to try and deal with the evil there.  You recruit a bunch of expendable adventurers, build/upgrade buildings with various effects, purchase items for each mission, and then send said adventurers off on various missions.  You keep this up till you're able to tackle the Darkest Dungeon.  That's a basic summary of Darkest Dungeon.In comparison, there's a bit of a role reversal in Iratus.  Here, you ARE the big bad, who's once again free to wage war on the "good guys."  The gameplay loop in Darkest Dungeon is largely the same in Iratus.  Instead of recruiting adventurers, you build minions from the pieces of slaughtered foes, you construct/upgrade buildings, unlock talents for Iratus, equip artifacts, and then venture through various areas as you attempt to  kill everything in your way.  So in essence, while there are a number of differences between the two games, if you like one you're likely to like the other.  That said, I'll now talk more about the differences between the two.One of the more obvious differences between the games and one I'm rather fond of, is the sanity system in Iratus.  In Darkest Dungeon, your adventurers have a sanity bar that slowly decreases from various things, like moving through a dungeon, being hit by a sanity attack, suffering a crit, interacting with a curio, and so on.  Iratus uses a very similar sanity system but instead of watching your adventurers go insane, you're the one inflicting madness on your foes.  Just like in Darkest Dungeon, it's possible for someone to get a negative or positive effect when stressed out.  Some effects, like Berserk, can go either way according to the situation.  In the case of Berserk, an enemy with this effect deals increased damage but also takes increased damage.  The sanity system in Iratus is handled pretty well in my opinion.  Some enemies are completely invulnerable to sanity/stress damage, others are designed to make use of a loss of sanity, like dwarven berserkers who always gain Berserk when stressed enough.  At the same time, there are some enemies who are very dangerous if you try to kill them through normal attacks but are much more manageable when fought using stress/sanity attacks.  While it feels like you're encouraged to change the composition of your party to match the enemies you'll face in each battle, you're not forced to rely on regular attacks or sanity attacks most of the time.  I say most of the time mainly because I've never tried to beat any of the boss fights with sanity/stress attacks.  I'm pretty sure you can, I just haven't gotten around to it yet.Anyway, I've already spent 30 minutes on this review and I haven't come close to mentioning everything I'd like to about Iratus but in conclusion, I think if you like Darkest Dungeon you'll also like Iratus.  Also, I personally like Iratus more than Darkest Dungeon.  I hope just as Iratus improved on elements from Darkest Dungeon, Darkest Dungeon 2 will do the same thing.  Fingers crossed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game.  Very similar to Darkest Dungeon though a little less character specific.  Building a new minion after one dies is easy if you have brains (may not be plentiful all the time though).  It is also in early access so it isn't the complete game yet however it is fun.  Pros:  -Good fights that don't drag forever but represent a challenge-Meaningful choices to make on what to upgrade first, both in base building and on unit level -Meta Goals to achieve to unlock additional unit types-Great variety in unit types, allowing for multiple victory conditions (stripping sanity, stripping health, fleeing etc) -Clean interface, super important to me I hate playing games that aren't intuitive or have ugly IF Cons:-Early Access so not all content is available, when I ended one run with victory after floor 3 the file is gone so no picking it back up when the full release takes place.  Not sure why that was done this way -Depending on your tastes, a single minion dying has a lot less impact compared to Darkest Dungeon or X-com type games -Would have liked a bit more story, it creates a cool atmosphere but this isn't a game you buy for story.All in all 9/10, bloody fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: When i opened this game, i saw a familiar message, one claiming this game to be brutal, with many setbacks, and an extremely brutal campaign. A mantra held high by the likeness of Darkest Dungeon, a truly brutal game that took me 100+ hours and did indeed cause me to recoil in horror as i lost my team many MANY times.This isn't anything like that, in fact this might be one of the easiest games I ever played.I spammed reaper scythe attack to get past all the levels easily without fail, up until the 3rd boss who had an AoE attack. After that i lost a monster every now and then but i could immediately get  a new one buy putting a brain into the same type of monster.Resources where so plentiful i basically got to have everything right at the beginning, which really hurt this game roguelike feel.At 30$ its really pricey.Theres an option to turn off "cliche voicelines".... the voicelines are like the least cliche thing about this game, the characters look like they are from a shoddy mobile game. + The plot is actually good, like really good, not as good as Darkest Dungeons which is the exact same concept and price, and just WAY better, but its good.This game has some really neat cutscenes, but again, not as good as darkest dungeon.Basically what im saying is this is an overpriced game that has a pretty direct competitor that is actually worth your money. If your on the fence about this game, just do yourself a favor, get Darkest Dungeon. Its ACTUALLY hard, way better designed, way more fun, better animated, has non cliche voice lines, and as a bonus, you dont spend most of your time allocating stat points.yeah i should have mentioned that, i spent MORE time spam allocating stat points than i did playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I love this game and will play it for a long time to come. If you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, then you will likely also enjoy this game. Both games are great and they both shine as great games in this genre, but if you want to be the villain instead of the hero, then buy this game and slaughter all who stand in the way of the One True Necromancer. I'm someone who plays extremely quickly and I had a VERY good team on the EASIEST difficulty and the animation settings were to 5x with talking disabled and it took me my current playtime to beat it. Thats entirely too long for a single run. The worst part was after the first floor it really didn't change at all. There's four floors with maybe 50 rooms per floor or something insane like that. If the artifacts were way more interesting and the runs were about 1/4 the length of the current runs then maybe it would work.
