_childDocuments_.review: First things first, you play as an ancient necromancer that hates the livings because their heroes defeated and sealed you until some jackass decided to unseal your tomb in the name of capitalism. After killing the jackasses who unsealed you, you decided to harvest each and every organs of those poor souls and make some undead from it to be your personal minions. For some reason, your tomb was built like a castle with lots of convenient stuffs in it, so you decided to make it your base. is mediocre at best. The only complaint that i have is Iratus's voice acting in narrating stuffs throughout the game. Sometimes the narration just feels unnecessary and out of tone, and his voice just doesn't match his looks at all. BUT that just my nitpicking. plays out very similarly to Dankest Dungeon so i'll compare stuffs to it. Iratus: Lord of the Dead tried to be unique from DD, which in some aspects works and kinda don't. In Iratus, you unlock and make your own minions instead of hiring mercenaries. The more living beings you killed, the more your army of undead will grow. However, your minions will die and get sacrificed A LOT. In higher difficulty, it'll be much harder to get resources to create them. So you need to play it smart, reserve some resources in case something happens. And when you get to see a sacrificial altar, make sure to use it by sacrificing a minion and hopes that you'll get some good items in return. If you didn't get anything good, well... you can always sacrifice more later, because they're just... your minions after all... expendable minions...Increasing your minion stats is not done by equipping good gears, instead you'll need stat points for stats and skill points for enhancing skills accordingly to your playstyle, almost everything is inherent you see. Finding a good skill set for your party is hard, you'll have to experiment with it a lot..... Or you can just find some good builds on youtube or something.You can equip your minions with up to two items that you can craft through alchemy, or by finding them from the dungeon. These items don't necessarily increases their stats (some does, under some conditions however), but they can also be game-changing later on.There's no  (although skip turn/DoT debuffs is still there). Instead, you'll be relying on Evasion to evade or Block/Ward to negate physical/magic attacks. However, some units doesn't have inherent block/ward stats so you'll have to rely on their defense stats (Armor for physical, Resistance for magic). Evasion sucks, trust me, unless you're playing on Cakewalk difficulty. I forgot to mention that the further you are in the dungeon, the more DoTs is in play. So investing for higher hp pools early on is never a bad idea.And now, . My only complaint for this game is that, as far as i can tell, there's no end-game content. Unlike DD, this game also borrows the 'rouge' element from games like Slay The Spire. Similar to STS, Iratus has 5 linear dungeons for you to conquer. Completing different difficulties also unlocks more higher difficulties, unlocked minions and enemies's codex will also be carried over (NOT the units). However in STS, re-decking your deck in different runs and difficulties does works wonderfully. But for a rougelike team-building game..... It just doesn't really mixes that well IMO.All in all, this is a pretty good game. Just keep in mind to not invest too much time in your minions, because in the end, they're just your sacrificial pawns. However, if those pawns were to be led by a wise one, they can turn into hideous and powerful undead, nightmares for the livings.7/10

Having long been a fan of games like Darkest Dungeon and the Dungeon Keeper series (and a lot of games with the word "Dungeon" in the title) I was pleasantly surprised to find that this game blended not only the aesthetics of both of those titles, but much of what was fun about them as well. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a difficult one for me. I really do enjoy almost every part of the game I have played so far but one thing I just can't enjoy are the really unfun instant kill mechanics on some enemies. Regardless of your stance on difficulty and difficulty is something I am quite fine with, having an enemy instantly kill one of your minions from full health isn't really about the difficulty, it's about how fun the game feels to play. When you've put the time and effort into improving your minions, an instant death ability from any enemy is just a slap in the face that kills all of my motivation to continue playing. Instant kill mechanics are not fun and really aren't difficult, just frustrating and really unenjoyable, especially to a new player who doesn't know the enemies to enable them to counter them yet.TL;DR Instant kill abilities are very anti-fun and unenjoyable and are easily replaced by similar difficulty abilities that are less frustrating.Update: Since I first Reviewed this game there has been a lot of work on it and my main gripe with the instant kill enemy has been resolve with an ability that mere does a decent chunk of damage instead. With Iratus' full release the game has more features than it did when I last played and all of them have seemed to only improve the game from my initial experience. I can now very enthusiastically say you should buy this game, it's great, it's enjoyable and quick and easy to get into.

_childDocuments_.review: Since it's clear from the outset that this is a Darkest Dungeon clone what most of you will be asking is whether or not it's as GOOD as Darkest Dungeon. Initial impressions will lead you to believe that whilst Iratus is certainly a very good realisation of the style of game that it's slightly lacking somewhere that you just can't put your finger on. I would urge you to at least complete the first two difficulty levels before reaching this conclusion as it improves as you progress along its learning curve. My current feeling is that it IS, in fact, as good as DD and has the potential to become better than it. Even as it is it is an absolutely worthy purchase and there's not really a lot more to say about it than that as, if you are looking at it at all, you have a fairly good idea of the kind of turn based tactical game that it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay and great ideas. Some of the worst balance I've ever encountered in a game. You routinely run into enemies that can kill you in 2-4 hits while it can take you upwards of 10-15 to kill them. Couple that with how abundant healing is for your enemies, and how non existent it is for you, makes for some real BS fights.I get it, your minions are disposable. But having them 2 shot when they are level 5, losing all the materials from making them and then basically losing the other 3 minions as well, since once you are down 1 party member, you are almost guaranteed to lose the fight.They say "strategy" is required, but when you have no idea if you are going to be facing enemies that buff tons, are immune to stress, have high def and every other form of advantage, strategy is impossible. The fight previews show you  enemy out of the 4 you fight meaning you can prep for that 1 enemy that is weak vs stress attack, build your party with that in mind, and then find out the other 3 are immune to stress damage.Virtually every single fight contains enemies that easily strip you of any and all buffs, meanwhile you have or 2 minions tops that can do the same. Meanwhile in these same fights, an enemy can strip you of all buffs, debuff you, and hit you for 1/3 of your hp all in one attack/action. And this same enemy can the next round give itself, block charges(immune to attacks besides crits) and buff it's crit% and attack damage again, all in one action. No big deal right. Oh yeah, practically every single enemy buff/debuff  in this game stacks. So if you try and wipe those clean, you are spending the entire fight doing that and not damaging anything, or you just don't have a minion who can cleanse those buffs/debuffs and you just die in a few hits.This game has a phenomenal approach, and a real unique mechanic. But, holy hell is it poorly executed. The enemies are overpowered, your minions are incredibly weak, your magic spells are either weak and take too much mana, or they provide buffs to the enemies when you use them. Your only support character than can reliably heal your characters is unlocked after a considerable amount of time in game, and heals you for x-y damage, and then the next turn it damages you for the same.RNG can be a PITA some times but, in most roguelike games you can work around it. In this the game is specifically designed to make it as unfair as possible. Difficulty is meant to feel challenging, not cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good clone of Darkest dungeon as those go. I played on the highest difficulty the game allows you to for your first run and was thoroughly bored before it ended. The game is about making compositions of undead that compliment each-other. I found out fairly early if I used one character who would punish stress damage with more stress damage and 3 that do group wide stress damage that I could trivialise almost any encounter. This game offers you no incentive to change compositions and in fact with the levelling system actively discourages it. Due to this after around the third floor of six the game felt like a chore to finish, today I finally got around to finishing it and received an okay cut-scene for my efforts. I wouldn't recommend you buy this game at all unless you really like turn based games and you have around 20 hours to waste away. Even then if you don't get it on sale for less than £12, you overpaid.

So one more fight. Cool, got 'em again. Let's do one more fight. And one more and one more. :DEverything is quite selfexplanatory, though sometimes it is a little anoying that once you made a decision (for example when leveleing the talents) you can't correct it, if you think you took the wrong decision.Anyway, that's not a gamebreaker for me.Also, I read that some people are annoyed that their minions are, well, "dead" when retreating. I personally do not regard that as an issue, even if some of the minions were already leveled. It is not about the minions - it is about the Lord of the Dead himself, it is about Iratus, who needs to get stronger and better to acchieve his goals. And all those nice little minions are nothing more than what would be "consumables" in other games.Cynical? Nah, just seeing the world through the eyes of a necro. :D

_childDocuments_.review: I put more than 100 hours into this game and got all the achievements. I should probably review it.This is a fun little game that can be boiled down to "Darkest Dungeon but you play the bad guys." It's not actually that simple as there are a good number of differences, but if you want a one-line sales pitch, there you go.If you've never played Darkest Dungeon and somehow ended up on this page, here's a quick summary: you play as a necromancer controlling a party of undead warriors. They fight successive parties of heroes in difficult turn-based combat. The flow of the game has roguelike elements, where it autosaves frequently and you're expected to struggle and suffer losses along the way.It's not without its problems. I can think of two major ones.First, the game is unforgiving of complete failure. In Darkest Dungeon, if your best team gets wiped, you can just hire more characters and send them into lower level dungeons to slowly progress back to where you were. You're set back, but you don't have to abandon your save file. In Iratus, if your best minions get pulverized by a boss, you may actually have to reset the whole run because there is only one very limited way of replacing high-level minions, and low-level minions probably aren't going to overcome what your best ones couldn't.Second, the achievements are boring. There is nothing creative about any of them, it's all just stuff you'll end up doing in the game normally - that is, except the last few "kill X enemies", which are just a tedious grind. I was probably at 40 or 50 hours in when I had most of the achievements, and the final few dozen hours were spent grinding out Humanitorium tokens and kill counts.But as I said, the game is fun. There are lots of team compositions, and the minions are actually pretty well balanced despite the large number of them - I can only think of one that I didn't have any use for, and one other that was so good it felt wrong not to use it. The game also doesn't feel as plodding as Darkest Dungeon, as you're always moving forward at a brisk pace.So if you're looking for a game like Darkest Dungeon and don't mind that you probably won't get all the achievements, give Iratus a go.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is mediocre at best. But it isn't all bad. Iratus: Lord of the Death has a fitting soundtrack, good artwork and decent gameplay. But it's not worth 30,- €, not even for genre fans. The 60,-€ for the game with all DLC is ludicrous. For genre fans, I would recommend it at 70% off. Everyone else is better served to spend their hard-earned money elsewhere.Edit: I have been giving the game a more extensive look. The balancing and the ability to choose different play styles to win is surprisingly good at the difficulty level, "good always wins". On higher difficulties the player is railroaded to exploits, and on lower difficulties almost everything works. But on "good always wins" it can be fun to try out new strategies, if that's your thing.I still think the game is a bit overpriced. 35,- € for the game with the supporter's DLC are fair in my opinion. That's the reason I recommend it for genre fans, that are primarily interested in the gameplay, at 20% off.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 1000% worth it. The time I've gotten as of now (without finishing one, let alone the three difficulties) is crazy. The game is a constant dripfeed of resources and there's always a new creature being unlocked, slowly but surely. It's that progression and evil tone that gets this games hooks in FAST. I'd gotten 9 hours in before I realised I should farm insanity off of my enemies to unlock X character. Then I can collect X to unlock X character and so on and so on. You're always grinding, it feels great. The two complaints I have, which is rare given my tendency to dislike things, is that their needs to be more creatures, that are variety. A lot of the mobs unlocked are good, and unique with how they attack, but are relegated to "not as good as X" or "doesn't fit this slot" (Looking at you third party position, seriously where are the DPS?) there are a few good unique characters that play like no other such as The Mummy and The Headless Hunter, with the first focusing on curses and making opponents 'unlucky' and the second with pisspoor accuracy (tends to happen when you're lacking a head) but good damage and stun chances, I just wish there were more characters like that in the game. The combat is juicy and there's no BS hit chances to sully your fun, if my character had good enough accuracy I was always hitting my shots asides the aforementioned Headless Horseman. Battles constantly feel fun and the variety of enemies means you have to shake up your team comps a ton which is great, it leads to a lot of natural gameplay and testing of what works and what works for something else. Some enemies have a lot of armour, so heavy hitters or magic that dispells or negates armour is great, while others have physical wards, which can take three galatic explosions before they break meaning you need a stress composition. Then there's mental resistance which stops said stress attacks, and requires a mix of multi attack moves and good AOE. Overall an amazing game, I bought the supporter pack and Necromancer DLC as well, simply cause it's so fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up playing through the core game on the easiest difficulty, no DLC and only utilizing the new free unit given to everyone: The Werewolf. I intend to play through on the next difficulty. If it's your first run, I highly suggest you finish the lowest difficulty first in order to unlock new units and gain the most important thing for future runs: information on the enemies as learning their effective counters can be very important.Overall, the core game play loop is risk/reward and forward progress only. You will always and constantly be trading one path for another and which forced battles you will take part in and how difficult they can be. Some RNG is expected, especially when it comes to the artifacts you can equip to Iratus and some are more exceptional than others -- like the shackles that prevent enemies from being inspired and escaping. I actually much prefer this game and how it approaches things better than Darkest Dungeon which is arguably where most of these types of games have copied the battle format from most. Unlike it's counterpart, Iratus attempts to add it's own spin to the formula by removing the RNG in your "hired" heroes. This affords you much more control over the encounters by allowing you to come into a battle with a party synergy ready to go. Granted, you'll only really be pressing forward with two teams at most depending on the damage type you're focusing on (HP or Morale damage). There are some pretty big difficulty spikes when you move from one floor to the next of the five-floor dungeon you're up-crawling from while leading your undead horde (more like 3-12 minions, not so much a horde). These difficulty changes seem very much geared towards ensuring you can't continue unless you understand the core mechanics, but the game doesn't really say those words exactly -- it just expects you to figure it out. Not the best way to present this to your players, but if you don't pick up on nuances of each enemy unit you encounter, you will die pretty quickly.The game offers on the two lower difficulties quick save/load features and you can even restart the floor you're on in the event things go horribly, horribly wrong. On the two higher difficulties the quick save/load is removed and the enemies start getting a bit more unfair advantages against you. Clearing the normal difficulty does net you two new units and it's the only difficulty that has unlocks associated with clearing it. The other unlockable units require you to perform various in-game tasks such as gathering enough Bones or turning units into vampires. These unlocks are required to fully upgrade certain things in your crypt which creates this sort of strange gating of progress in some aspects which is why I suggest finishing the game on the easiest difficulty first or even throwing your first game to unlock some units. It's sub-optimal, but not outright horrible.The biggest crime this game has is the fact that the excellent voice talent of Stefan Weyte is unfortunately not given enough chance to deliver story or more background on Iratus. Iratus himself, as a character, is somewhere between downright evil and comically evil which overall leads to a rather enjoyable protagonist. It's just a shame that the format of this game doesn't lend itself to better story telling for Iratus or the events of his past. A few people have spoken about the ending being rather unfinished or not tying up loose ends, all I will say without much spoilers is that I feel that the ending is meant to be open to your interpretation as to what Iratus ends up doing after the climax.The TL;DR -- Good fun, some questionable design choices, but better than Darkest Dungeon in my opinion. Great for quick burst play sessions while you're busy with something else. Amazing voice talent by Stefan Weyte and worth hearing him as Iratus. Definitely recommend if you enjoy the rogue-lite/rogue-like elements and planning out decisions well in advance. Finish the easiest mode first and unlock minions and information on  enemies before a harder run.Edits: Grammer/spelling.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 hours, I still cannot recommend this game.  It looks like darkest dungeon at the first impression, but the feel is very different when you are deeper into the game.  Unlike the heroes in DD, the minions in this game are very expendable.  With the right material, you can create an identical minion instantly.  The minions also have no attributes such as perks to make them unique.  I guess that's why I don't feel much when losing a long serving minion, which is pathetic. Difficulty is another problem.  The game has so many difficulty levels without meaningful differences, and learning from the outdated Diablo 3 doesn't do any good.  The first two difficulty levels are so easy that make the first two runs very boring.  It's a huge waste as the first run is most important to player's overall experience.Achievements are also designed with very low effort.  Most of the achievements are designed to kill X number of enemy in a level which are basically unnecessary grind.  To kill 1000 enemy in each level requires you to play about 12 runs and I probably only enjoy 3 or 4 runs at most.After all, the game actually has some potential but not best implemented in many details.  I wish the developers can put more thoughts into these areas and do better in the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I have only played for 1.5 hours up till now, but I have serious issues with the art design of the game. The idea is good, and I want to like the game; but it feels like a flat, boring, unpolished Darkest Dungeon and HoMM2-Necromancer-town rip-off. Iratus' graveyard is a cheap copy of the Necromancer town in Heroes of Might and Magic 2. The colors of the game are too bright, and thus feel contrary to the atmosphere that is trying to be built. There is a total lack of unique atmosphere & story & suspense. The music is generic and boring. Even the fonts are boring!! I cannot really tell which font it is, but it is really disturbing to see Arial fonts hovering over minions in a battle. (Check out the alchemy table in the promotional images as a case in point.) The heavily-muscled necromancer looks more like a dead Conan, and not like a terrifying necromancer. I will probably play and finish this game, but it is really hard to get past the poor quality of art direction. The developers seem to have spent more time in developing mechanics than the actual content, and even then it is basically a DD rip-off! I would normally see no problem in a game focused mostly on the mechanics. (take FTL and Into the Breach as brilliant examples of this. Still they have a certain color palette, and style that feels unique.) What made Darkest Dungeon work was not just the brilliant idea behind it, but also superior voice acting, writing and art design all of which contributed to the great atmosphere of the game. Really sorry to say this, but Iratus is a terrible sore in the eyes... It feels as if there is no effort behind the game, and as if the developers wanted to make a quick buck from rogue-like and DD fans. PS: And please, please, please, please stop calling every game with a skill tree a RPG! RPG does not mean "a game that implements skill trees."

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A bit lacking in the setting and atmosphere of Darkest Dungeon, but manages to capture the essence of its gameplay.  Long: I'm finding the slog of this game is getting a little tedious since reaching the final floor. However, the journey was mostly enjoyable. This game makes no attempt to shade its homage to Darkest Dungeon, but the copy is rather shallow. The puzzle-like combat is there, but the dark atmosphere has been replaced by 80's villain cheese. Iratus is boring, and his recurrent quips in the non-battle screen quickly grow tiresome. When your ancestor talked in Darkest Dungeon, even when it was a repeat, it contributed to the overall sense of doom and foreboding. The art style in DD also helped with this.The heroes looked heroic but also pained, especially when they took damage. It always felt like you were sending in a squad of ill-prepared adventurers when they trotted off into the dungeons. Iratus's style of undead minions lack soul and are in some cases weirdly inappropriate. Big-titted vampires, really? I mean, I guess it would help them attract unwitting victims, but then why big-titted ghosts? The levels all start to feel the same, too. The combat changes as each floor has a different theme, but enemies aside, the atmosphere never changes. The same is true of Iratus's base. In DD, upgrading the town showed visible changes. In Iratus, you only see one change, from no building to a building. After that, the buildings never grow or evolve in appearance, which is a shame. As for the combat, it mostly captures the punishing difficulty of DD. Your minions will die, sometimes often. However, you can usually figure out the way forward. There are some weird exceptions with the bosses and a few particular encounters (wardens) that seem to require one specific strategy, but for the most part, you do have the freedom to craft teams that can handle a variety of encounters. You only start off with 8 minions, but you start unlocking new ones right away. I have mixed feelings about how they are unlocked. Some are relatively straightforward and easy (upgrade this building, deal X damage, make Y enemies insane). Others seem easy but end up being longer than seems necessary (bone golems). I do wish they HAD copied DD here and simply allowed you to start recruiting anything right out of the gate. One game probably won't take very long to complete. I'm on the final floor of a Good Always Wins game, and it took me about 20 hours (minus the 30 minutes or so of the mandatory tutorial). Overall, if you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, I would say this is worth a discount purchase. I picked it up for $15.00, and it seems worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Conceptually this is right up my alley: a dark (but funny) take on the Darkest Dungeon model. After playing through the tutorial and a bit of a normal run, I had to refund. TL;DR I wish I could give it a thumbs up but I can't. If you're a DD fan, maybe wait for a sale or give it a shot now if you're really hankering for something similar. Fans of Darkest Dungeon might find things to love here, but it lacks the polish of its inspiration. It makes up for that with its own character but its systems can't quite take it over the finish line. Definitely worth picking up on a sale, or after a few updates perhaps, but I can't recommend it in its current state. The combat is a bit slow compared to DD, and didn't pick up at all during my time playing. Minions are interesting, but upgrading them feels somewhat shallow / not very meaningful. In the end, your choices are mostly which stats (even in the abilities tree, which just increases stats and the attack's power type) and don't feel very meaningful. The expendable nature of minions lack the engaging character of DD--I always tried to keep my veterans alive and had a sentimental attachment to more than a few of those poor souls--whereas these minions are truly expendable with no meaningful differences between the next one you raise / sacrifice. This is a minor complaint, but: the voice acting for Iratus is REALLY awesome, love whoever they hired for it. That said I don't feel like I'm Iratus--or that I'm even supposed to feel that way! Who am I as the player? That might be a weird criticism, but I felt divorced from what story was there because of it. I wanted to see more but I wasn't willing to slog through the combat to get there.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, this game is hands down a superior Darkest Dungeon, or at least WILL be if Workshop is added in the future.To continue onward, while the game is fairly balanced in some aspects, there are a few things that need buffs and de-buffs.Mainly these two factors (from as far as I've played) are the Body Part upgrades and the Elite Squads.Elite Squads are meant to the the elite of the elite, hard to kill, and rewarding. And having had my share of them, the Dwarves seem to have an Extreamlay overpowered combination with the Oracle, Hammerer, Marksmen, and Geomancer. Being mainly that the Oracle just spams Mark and Defence boots for her teammates to make them near impossible to dent without throwing 3-4 whole batches of your own units at them. As in 3-4 squads. At 3-5 level, but this is just a sight from early on as I have only just begun to start.Being that, I have encountred some difficult combos, but nothing like that. that one squad managed to wipe out my entire tomb before I could kill Just the Marksmen.However, as I don't have many unlocked characters, prahaps that will change the tide of things once I get to that level.Though the main issue that ties into that, is that you tend to yield less resources then you lose units once you get to the dwarven zone. Making a sturdy assault on such a high tier Full Elite team with such high end units, very hard early game.Though, I will come to admit I might have just got the short end of the straw.Next topic, is the Body parts and Items.Considering that they really only give you 3-10 HP at best when you start leveling up your units mushy flesh bindings.It makes sense when you look at Initiative, evasion, Guards, Resistances, and accuracy, but less so when you look at ATK and HP. This is because when your level 6 Dark Knight is going up against some real heavy fire power like the Hammerer mixed with a Marksmen, He's not going to thank you for the +5 hp that the Blue Tier body part gave him. In simple, Speciffically the ATK and HP boosts from any upgrades are highly underwhelming. The damage output is all the same as your enemy starts getting higher and higher in defence, especially when captain rattle me bones starts only doing 3 damage per hit to a 115HP unit.So my solution to that (while no one needs to listen) would be to make it so that with every tier (colour) higher then Basic (white) add lets say, a range of 5 damage max. adding a 5 range to every rarity boost. 5-10-15-20 etc. but that's just thinking of ATK.As for HP, do 7-9 boost per.That's my only gripe with the current upgrading system, because honestly I don't even upgrade my units for that since the numbers are so low, I only do it for Wards or other Defensive purposes.---Other then those slight balance issues, there is nothing else I can seem to find a problem with other then my usual hunger for more content.In all, This game has so far surpassed my expectations and been quite addicting to play.And as said before, I'd hope they add Steam Workshop once the game reaches it's final stage. So that it may outlive its intentional life span.Also, Side note (compleatly ignorable). A Unit Idea: Wight - A type of Unit that is modeled like a Grim Reaper, having a scythe and Cloaked body, but is more about Stress damage, having one kind of physical attack that can leech/heal allies.Since at the time, I need healing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I dont write alot of reviews but since this is in beta I thought id give it a try. This part is without spoilers, and ima put a spoiler section further down for everyone who wants to read it. My initial thought of the game is it is pretty much a a blend of darkest dungeon and slay the spire, you have RNG , events, theory crafting, and you base your minions off your talents and artifacts to try and be as strong as possible. I like it even though its missing a few things for me, but I wont get into specifics on what exactly i like and dont until the spoiler section. The talents need improvement, the bugs iv found with the AI, and the debuffs staying on my character from certain enemies and doing nothing to me ( get into that into the spoilers) and sometimes the game doesnt register that you met certain requirements for minions. Over all for a beta game its fun, and it keeps you engaged at all times. For the price as is its not a 25 dollar game, but im hoping with the addition to new content itll be worth the investment. Money isnt everything though and as long as you have fun with it , it doesnt matter if its not the most optimal purchase. {{{{spoilers below.}}}}}}Ok so to begin with lets start with difficulty. Difficulty: the game is not worth playing on easy as it looses its engagement immediately on easy as you dont even have to pay attention 90% of the time. Totally play on normal on your first play through as it actually challenges you in the middle and endgame. Which on easy feels alot easier due to the talent system and materials you have amassed. Minions: The minions feel strong, some have their uses and niche comps as any game usually has generally strong minions like the bride, wraith, dark knight, and some that just feel mehhh/niche comps like the zombie, banshee, skeleton, shade. I do have a complaint on some of them as it said it needed to amass certain amounts of materials for the bone golem for example, and it told me during a entire play through i only amassed 25 bones, and I counted i had over 35 in my inventory alone. So ether i dont understand if its just from enemies, or the docks, or whatever but it doesnt feel good. Some required me to get 3 of a certain minion, and i never once encountered a vampire, and one i had three sitting on my bench and it didnt register that i got them at all. Talents: in my playthrough i rushed Alchemy tree, and i had little problems in the middle and late game to which i transitioned into destruction to just pop mobs i didnt like, and i got a ton of mats to upgrade.I do not like the fact i have to grind and invest 10-12 points into a tree, just to have my big money talents be restricted on RNG scrolls. I just tells me they are worthless without the scrolls and id rather have passives up all the time, or destruction spells that i can use reliably. So i would say to balance them to make them playable without the scrolls so i feel like a ultimate ability isnt restricted to a RNG item. I had finger or death and the skulls from destruction and i never got to use them once because of the scroll restriction. Over all i think they work well, with alil imbalancing that takes away the hype of spending all of your points into something and not getting to use it. Some others might find 10-15 scrolls on a play through and to that i say cheers, but when u dont you just feel bad not taking a ability that could just really make a elite fight alil easier. Also i think the building resource talent should be replaced with a talent that gives you percentage chance to salvaged dead minion parts, as the building resource is to easy to get. Buildings: some minions requirements on buildings i totally understand but i think that the cost for them need to go up. The build resource by the end of the game was sooo easy to farm, by the end of it i had over 300 with nothing to spend it on because i didnt own the minions to upgrade them and i just got 20-30 a turn because reasons. There was no decision making involved and every minion that i had upgraded all the buildings before the end of act 2 , and i just sat on a ever growing resource pile i couldnt spend. By the end of it the only building i cared about was the healing hut, and arena to switch out minions i needed xp on. Everything else became forgettable. With the alchemy tree giving you so many materials i wouldnt say no to more minions needed to upgrade or level of minion requirements, just 2 per slot is alil easy when i can pop a skele into it at level 1 at little resource cost to get wrath, mana, xp to my main dude Iratus, or even just more building resource early to build my base easily. Game-play : Game play was fun , and should be the reason you stick with a game. It had replay ability since RNG can give some nutty items to go stress build, or crit builds depending on what you pull. I do have a visual bug to report tho , as the mages on act 3 , when they did the ice slide ability , the notification for it got bugged on my minions and never went away. So i never knew when/if i was going to slide. You basically have 3 ways to play , crit builds, self damage to heal builds, and stress builds. Some work better in some fights then others, i just hate loosing my squad because i walked into a fight with the wrong party. (but it does add realism) Ending : If this is all we get for the game , i would be so disappointed as the goal was rule the world, and we just escaped at the end. I totally wanna act 4, where we fight elite heros ina main city , unseen servents providing aid ina ambush on the other side expanding the battle field to a pincer attack. All leading up to fighting a mage/ priest of the light ina epic final show down that determines the fate of the world. It just leaves so much unsaid to leave it as is, and im so excited to see what the game creaters have in mind. Again im not the best with reviews but those are my thoughts so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always loved these kinds of Roguelike RPGs, but almost all of them force you to play as the "good guys", which for aspiring supervillains (and misanthropes like me) is stale and bland. It seems like Darkest Dungeon's the only one who got that right for me... So that's why I recommend Iratus, as it's a great twist on story and gameplay! I just wish it was either a little bit longer or allowed for workshop mods- some of my favorite things to do in Darkest Dungeon are using the many workshop characters available, and I'd love to use other types of undead minions here!!

_childDocuments_.review: Really good for an early access, but there needs to be fixes and additions to make this game outstanding. At this point its short, but replayability value is high. I would like more than 2 extra zones upon release tho.They are updating games balance often so what I say after might not be relevant at this current stage.Long rant about mechanics below:More pain difficulty (medium) felt good, I managed to complete the content from current early access without a party wipe, yet losing around 12 minions in total. Skills felt impactful and useful. fights fun, many different build composisions seems viable. boss fights, well sort of similar, very similar (between each other).Now I tryed the hardest difficulty (good always wins) and for me it felt like a mess. The biggest problem is the numbers game. Numbers in this game are lieing to u. Typically like in XCOM u will miss with 95% accuracy like every third attack and enemies with 60% attack chance will hit u every time. This is really appearant on hardest difficulty because you face really buffed enemies. So if debuffs like accuracy decrease feels like a waste of turn. some insanities which debuff enemies with luck or accuracy is also a waste. Best example is Mummies ultimate ability which deals sanity damage and then extra damage for every minus luck enemies have. But on this difficulty its basicly impossible to make enemies have minus luck, therefore this synergy is useless. The feel of trying to control the battle slowly with debuffs, stances and buffs is gone and most of the time you just hope to burn enemies faster than they burn you which takes away form the gameplay. Basicly feels like high difficulty level of Civilization game (emperor, deity) where you can only win via domination strategy and most game flavour is gone. Enemies completely hate some types of minions more than others so sometimes it doesnt matter how u possision your party it just means that your banshee and headless dude gets focused to hell. I would like to see more interesting enemie party compossisions, synergies and strategy from enemie and not just typical +20 to atack,dodge,crit and call it higher difficulty.Next, items, buildings and other upgrade mechanics:I find obelisk completely useless. You have to pay currency and sacrifise minions to get the same currency back over time... sure it might accumulate, to a bit more, but there are more important things to build in graveyard and once u finish them u feel less obligated to invest into obelisk. This may change with more acts available upon release because u will spend more time playing the game - so more payoff. There are not Enough artifacts currently available and items for minions are booring. It would be awesome if items alter some skills minions use, for example change from stress damage into vitality damage etc. yet most of the time its a stat increase with a flavour of u get more X stat if u take damage, be at possision 2 etc... All in all good promise for an outstanding game if devs put a lot more content in it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game a lot. As a lot of other reviews say, it's very similar to Darkest Dungeon and if you like that game, you'll probably have a good time with Iratus.  It has a LOT of potential to be brilliant and it's definitely a beautiful gem to stumble upon, I'm hoping the best for the developers and as I write this review, I've already gone and bought the supporter pack not for the pretty goodies it comes with, but in hopes of giving them the funds they deserve to make an amazing game.All in all, everything's reversed in Iratus. You're the supreme bad guy, the necromancer, the big bad evil dude that wants to spread horror and mayhem everywhere. It's not just 'Darkest Dungeon but evil' though. There are plenty unique mechanics that you can get into that turn the game interesting; you craft your minions from parts instead, meaning you can control what you get, and each minion has a lot more unique abilities they can utilize, with various playstyles I'm discovering. Stances also apply a lot of interesting stuff to the game. If I had any critique whatsoever, then it'd basically just be anything you'd expect to hear for an early access game. Namely the difficulty. I have to play CAKEWALK to get any progress, and even then, I get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ destroyed in some playthroughs. Thank god the devs havent made corpses a thing. (though id find it interesting if they did, since well, you're a necromancer.)

_childDocuments_.review: Necromancy? Darkest Dungeon style mechanics? Slay the spire esque aspects? SOLD!There's a LOT of potential here for a solid game. The good: - It's sort of reverse darkest dungeon only without all the overt "f**k you" mechanics being tossed at you endlessly save for a few elites it has "f**k you" moments but those seem mostly like teething issues of early access.- No corpses... I cannot state how awful that change to DD was. Simply awful. If you like DD but hate corpses this is for you.- In an inversion of Darkest Dungeon, you get to "stress out" enemies and have them flat out die or go insane and attack their own guys. But some enemies WANT you to stress them out and gain bonuses from being insane. Great fun! nice to be inflicting the stress for a change :P- It's aesthetically pleasing, if you like all the edgelord stuff and I do so +1 from me ;) - The devs are active on the discord and folks are on there talking strategy and being chill so nice playerbase. -  Insane potential with it's premise and marrying of two different sets of game mechanics that we all know and love/hate. It's early and needs work but it's fun as heck.- No needlessly censored and understated/hyper realistic female clothing. The monsters are monsters and the female form monsters are not bound by the "You need to have realistic armor!!!11!!!one" nonsense. They're reanimated corpses and bound spirits. It's fantasy and that's that. So it's artistically chosen to go with classical fantasy tropes in clothing. I missed this stuff.The bad:  - It's overtuned a little and "cakewalk" is not the cakewalk it states xD but it's still fun if you consider that normal mode. - The unlocks are a tiny bit grindy, stuff like damage your own minions or kill x amount of people. They're nice to have but they seem like an afterthought in some cases and in others teach you mechanics on how to use the minions better. I love the latter and dislike the former. I see what they were doing and it worked mostly but it's also annoying given a few of the starting minions are a little under-tuned or too fragile. In time that might be less of an issue. I'm used to terrible unlock systems and grind it's just irksome to see them done in a way that's not as interesting as they should be. Might change in future though.- The talent system is kinda full of fluff. You could remove half of the talents and no one would notice. Some being amazing, others feeling like they're in the way to something you could use. A ton of the talents should be baseline tbh, it would free up a lot of strategies early on and give a better range of options in how to use the earlier out of the box unlocked minions. - It seems to not know if it wants you to callously sacrifice your minions for victory or build them up for more competent strategies because of the permanence of death of minions. This is going to be difficult to balance and design around and I'm surprised it works this well already. Mainly because you can get "brains" which can be placed into minions in order to instantly level them up. But this is tied in with the iffy talent system and naturally this is sort of dichotomous with the item system, spending a ton of resources which are used to create new backup minions to create items only to lose them to a string of crits, leaves youwith the impression that items are for the most part pointless. Powerful but pointless. In short                                                                "Brains op. Equip items poop" - Me, just now.- The city building part is good but half baked at the moment. This is probably because there's no endless mode and only three of five floors released as it stands. You gain points on wins (altered again with... talents ugh) which allow you to sacrifice a minion and some points to gain long term bonuses, it could be that it's only three floors that this effect is hampered but... it's great, it's just not implemented as well as it could be. For one you have to sacrifice the minion AND then use another one to staff the building, whichever minions you use to staff doesn't matter. Only that you throw them in there and in a game where resources are tight until about the mid point of act 2 IF you build right. I can see some folks resenting the +10-50% chance increases to gains and the huge costs that if you neglect at all from the beginning. Are pretty pointless. Yet at times seem mandatory. I just wish it was implemented differently although it's NOT that terrible a system.  - There's a few small crashes here and there nothing major. This wouldn't be an issue only, if you crash out of an encounter just as you surrender out of one, you lose all minions deployed in the fight. So crashing + losing team entirely + scarcity of resources to make more + no brains (heh) = scrubbed run if you crash. Ah, early access. Think it's running on unity too, this is the RIGHT type of game for unity but unity will ALWAYS suck. Horribly suck. - There's a lot of "figure out out as you go along" and while I don't like handholding and enjoy finding out things. Being told what the mechanics of the sacrifice encounter tiles would help a ton. Knowing that each specific minion sacrificed will give you items that match the rarity if their parts AND a specific artifact which Iratus equips for entire run boosts. - Some of those artifact boosts don't work or don't work as expected... You might think it's for lich summon spam and sacrifice play which takes some set up to even get going for it's "every 3 minions that die grants you max mana" on one set of robes for example. Only it seems to either only work once per fight or... not at all on summoned minions dying. Tooltips need a massive going over. Artifacts have massive potential for fun and build complimenting but as it stands they're barebones. Heh, get it?- The alchemy system is pants, it compounds other issues or suffers as a result of them. It needs an overhaul but it's a nifty idea, just needs iteration and for the love of bob. A few "combine all of X" or "combine all to highest" so you don't have to spam clicks.This is all I can think of for now, bear in mind I adore this game and haven't stopped playing it since I got it. Not bad for a few Ruskies with a kickstarter :P Just pick it up, it's great fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. You'll hear people say things like "If you like Darkest Dungeon, you'll love this". I would go one step further and say that Iratus is like a less depressing version of Darkest Dungeon. I'm also the type of person that has a hard time concentrating on games for a longer period of time. My career is in software, so sometimes I need a game that will allow me to kinda turn off my brain and just let me have fun. Which means spinning up Prodeus or something that doesn't take too much cognitive energy. Iratus is actually not too taxing on your mental resources. I'm only 2.8hrs in, but I've had a blast since I bought this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. It's constantly being compared to Darkest Dungeon. While it is a similar style game, I actually enjoy playing this from the Necromancer perspective a lot more. It's much more fun to drive others mad than to be the one driven mad. This game is difficult, but also quite enjoyable to play. I'm almost finished the game on More Pain mode, which is the second highest difficulty. Once this mode is complete, you have access to the highest difficulty. Unfortunately you don't unlock all the minions at the start, you have to earn them by completing the game on the more pain difficulty. I'm still missing 4 minions that will unlock once I beat the final stage and get a few more bones as drops. So far I've found quite a few strategies are very viable to win. For the first half of my run I focused on driving my enemies insane and giving them heart attacks with stress attacks. The main purpose of this was to unlock 2 minions; the vampire, by causing enemies to flee, and the wraith, by driving enough enemies insane. After this, I found a minion I enjoyed and built a team around buffing them. This was also very successful and I could often wipe out a full enemy team in two shots.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game that plays well on Steam Deck.It's a tactical game where you control 4 minions against groups enemies.You can create several loadouts from a variety of minions and can upgrade them.It's almost like a card game meets tabletop, with Iratus having a great voice over that fits the character very well.There is something about this being a fairly easy game to get into, being simple and intuitive, but the tactical gameplay definitely requires you to use your brain.I could not put this down.

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus: Lord of the Dead is a challenging game that is still in early access as of my review. I wanted to put some hours into not just it but the community before I decided on my recommendation.I recommend this game to people who:Enjoy a challenge and learning from your mistakes.Like having many choices in group composition and enjoy searching for that "perfect" team.Want play the bad guy and send your minions to DESTROY!Have fun with games that have some micromanagment of buildings and unit upgrades.I don't recommend this game to people who:Want full sessions that finishes fast. (The levels can be somewhat long but you can leave and come back from a non battle screen without penalty.)Like to steamroll content.Have no patience for losing.Are looking for a fully finished and polished game.Yes, there are unbalanced parts (It's still in Early Access) but the Devs have been great so far on patching out bugs and balancing gameplay as we play and give them information to work on. They have been active on the Discord where they listen and have commented on suggestions and bug-reports or just popped into chat to say hello.There's still content to add and the roadmap (currently visible on the news page here on Steam) shows just how much more content they're working to add to the game.The Discord community has been a helpful and relaxed bunch who are more than willing to answer questions and often brag about their favorite team compositions.This game has kept me playing from the start with it's darker tone and challenging rogue-like gameplay and it's only getting better as time goes on.I recommend you give this one a look.

_childDocuments_.review: i've played darkest dungeon and i've played this game and honestly i like this game a lot better.  i'm a very casual gamer and this game feels a lot more user-friendly and less demanding.  it's much easier than darkest dungeon so if you liked darkest dungeon but thought it was too hard, this is the game for you.  the biggest difference is that in iratus you don't have to play through an entire dungeon in one shot, you can do one battle and then return to base and regroup and send out a different squad of monsters for the next battle.  plus the character of iratus can cast spells in combat to help the monsters.  the art style is very cool, there's lots of options in combat, all the monsters all have clever animations, there's plenty of upgrades and management to do in between battles, and the overall story is pretty cool as well.  the repetitive dialogue and corny one-liners get old real fast though.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting game and thoroughly enjoyable if you like Darkest Dungeon or Tactical RPG/Rougelike games. The battle setup is obviously similar to DD and there are some light town management aspects here, but Iratus brings quite a few things to the table on its own. Mainly I felt there was more control over your minions and actions than in DD where sometimes bad stuff happened and you were just really screwed. There is less of that here. In DD you had to worry about stress but now the enemy has to worry about it and YOU get to inflict mental damage, which is a big change here. You can choose between physical, stress, or magic damage while mixing several different minion types to experiment. The addition of Iratus as a character that can be equipped with items and cast spells to benefit your party is really cool and another neat aspect that makes this game feel unique. The dungeon maps are sprawling with lots of events. My one playthrough took me just over 30 hours and I still have things that I would like to go back and get, so the replayability is nice. The game is difficult, especially in the later levels. If you have played games like this one before I would try it out on the second-highest difficulty and see how you feel first.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I've wrote an in-depth review so bare with me if you can. If you played Darkest Dungeon and wanna play as the other side then this is the game for you. You play as a necromancer with his unique army of minions that allow for different playstyles. Wanna get rid of some enemies quickly in the next turn? Shred them apart with a werewolf before they can even breath. Wanna spread fire and mayhem on the entire battlefield? Get a lich and blast everyone (this can include your minions) into ashes  with overwhelming firepower. Prefer a subtler approach? Pick any one of the more ghost-like minions (Banshee, Wraith, Shade) to terrify the enemy into submission and watch their sanity and fighting spirit crumble apart from the pressure.The examples above illustrate the 3 main damage types. Physical, Magic and Sanity. Physical is the most common and is the most direct way of dealing enemies. This is usually mitigated by heavily armored foes .Magic is another form of damage that is not mitigated by armor, this time instead by resistance which are often only possessed by other mages in the opposition. Use this to cut through most armored foes on the front without much resistance. Last and the most exquisite is Sanity. If you played Darkest dungeon it's another form of life bar that directly bypasses armor and resistance to instead attack the opponent's psyche. Once it reaches a critical threshold, the enemy then goes through a check to determine whether he'll get inspired and get his hero moment or be heavily crippled with a debuff that drastically lowers his fighting efficiency, sometimes even getting him to turn on his fellows (a personal favorite of mine was getting a slavedriver, even the act boss himself, to get torn apart by his own deranged workforce. Quite the poetic justice if I might say). Once it reaches full there's a chance that the next stress attack the enemy will die of a heart attack. Stress attacks also increase the chance the enemy unit will rout in their next turn so you wouldn't have to fight them. This is countered by some enemies not having any sanity such as golems or automatons that can only be destroyed physically. There's also another form of defense layer in the form of blocks and wards. Blocks are removed whenever you or an enemy take physical damage while wards are removed whenever magic damage, stress damage or a debuff/spell is used against an enemy. Lastly you have a resource called wrath that builds up whenever you damage or take damage from an enemy. It builds much faster when minions take damage. This allows access to to minion ults that allow a minion to peform a special move whenever you have enough to cast it.For the basebuilding aspect, every fight you get resource in the form of body parts and souls. Body parts enable you to literally build your army of minions. Not all minions are unlocked at the start and some require a specific condition. Each of them are unique and synergize well with each other if you ever want to mix and match lethality and terror. Be aware that parts do run out as not all body parts are recovered if a minion is ever destoyed in battle so you can actually be defeated if you've run out of parts for replacements. Parts also have a rarity and the more uncommon the more stats you can give to your minion. The digger souls allow the buildings to be built which you would then need to build a specific minion to enshrine in order to increase its efficiency. I'd say the main difference in gameplay is that Iratus himself can directly participate in the form of spells and potions. Spellcasting costs mana and allow you to buff your minions or damage/debuff the enemy to control the flow of the battlefield much better. The efficiency is determined by your spellpower which is Iratus's current level that can also be increased by certain minion abilities. Potions do the same thing but instead of mana being used you use body parts to create a one-time use consumable that can individually buff or debuff the opponent either for a few turns or entire duration of the battle. Not all recipe potions are unlocked and you have to individually create a mix to get the recipe. Iratus can also equip artifacts that can further augment either his minions, his spellcasting, or increase the resources he gets after a battle. His voice acting also provides some much needed roleplay and personality since most of your minions lack one.Enemy variety is quite rich and ranges from the drug addled mining workforce with their slavedrivers, the resilient and stocky dwarves, pesky heroes/mercenaries and their standard D&D comps, the militarized religious arm along with their priests and priestesses. There's one more but let's keep that one as a surprise for later.Level design is randomly generated and is designed so you can choose a route that enables what kind of rewards you get. Either artifacts for Iratus, general or minion-specific items, xp for either Iratus or his minions, and there's also a special type of encounter called quests that provides benefits in the short term in the form of resources or provide long-term minor buffs that will carry on until the end. The caveat is these quests often require a specific minion to be accomplished more easily, there's a challenging fight or simply succeed or fail due to rng. In terms of difficulty the first few ones offer a surprising amount of challenge without being too unfair while the latter ones provide a much needed hardcore experience that will test your knowledge and resource management. Overall, I'd say give this a go if you love a grimdark, turn-based, resource management challenge like Darkest Dungeon. This is very much an improvement to that existing formula. Now go forth and slay your enemies to your heart's content.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - While my vampire used her own blood to debuffed the wannabe heroes, I lost my ♥♥♥♥ when my goul chick simply ate the poor damaged bastards! While the ladies did the killing, my ghost dude simply floated there, buffing himself up to become unhitable... (is that a word?) Great game, highly recommend!May 2021 - I've followed this game since it early days, waited for the right time to approach it. Saw it on sale and bought the core game to try it out... 27 game hours later, the campaign is finished and I'm back to get the DLC and Supporter Pack. This is the kind of game and developer I'd like to support. You start the game on easy and get though a basic tutorial, once finished you get to continue on easy or start new and choose difficulty. I chose the middle way, normal difficulty and while there were some tough fights none of them felt unbalanced or unfair. The bosses were really fun and provided a different type of challenge than the ordinary level-fights, which in themselves also never felt tedious or boring since the constant mix of enemies brought different need of tactics.Your own creations/minions combined with the gear you find (loooooot baby!) gives possiblity to create optimal gear+minion+magic-tactics, but there was no need for that on normal difficulty. I simply played with the latest monster I unlocked, changed when they were low on life and made new ones or got new ones though the levels. You get plenty of material to make new monsters/minions should they die, but that happend very rarily.Progression felt OK as well, never too far away to unlock your next thing (on my first play through) will try again on difficult and see how the replayability is. And then there's the DLC for the additional level, and ending.Great game, have fun scaring the life out those poor puny heroes. Moahahahaha!

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this, but the end result is a game that lacks flavour beyond it's initial appeal. There's a lot of potential, but it just falls a bit short on depth compared to its competitors. There is very little variety after your first playthrough. While each minion is interesting as a base, there is really nothing that builds off that. They have no unique traits, so they all feel generic. The items are very samey and plain so growth feels stagnant. The parts mechanic could have been an interesting way to cobble together unique minions from spare parts, but instead they're merely flat stat points. You can experience everything the game has to offer in one run, easily unlocking nearly all the classes, and it unfortunately doesn't hold much for you after that. If they added more personality and depth it would be an easy recommend for me. If minions had traits or growth that separated them from others of the same class. If items were unique and build defining. If parts made a minion instead of feeling tacked on. If events were events instead of fights with a minor temporary buff if you win. If there were more unlocks or unique minions past the initial few. if. if. if.The setting is neat, the voice acting is great (notably the main voice actor), being the bad guy is cathartic, the mechanics *would* be appealing if they has substance. But all in all it just doesn't feel fleshed (heh) out. It could be worth it on a deep deep sale for a playthrough or two, but other than that I unfortunately can't recommend it when the competition is so stiff.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming into this purely for the "more darkest dungeon" angle, you will probably be disappointed. The game has similar elements to Darkest Dungeon but plays very differently. I played on the "More Pain!" difficulty, and I found some challenge but it was mostly inconvenience, if you lose a unit the narrator says "I'll just make another one" and that is actually what you do, the losses impact the game minimal at this difficulty. And to tell you the truth I didn't mind that so much, what I minded was the somewhat mindless way of playing the game. Pick the enemy that will cause you the most problems, rush them down with either damage or sanity attacks. Rinse and repeat. When a character died it was more a "Sigh, now I have to make a new one. Give them a brain, set up their talents and distribute their stats again." which got really old on the last stage. And reading whats different between two upgrades can sometimes be difficult cause every ability is described in a text, not listed off in an easily readable way. This is what made me decide not to keep playing into the harder difficulties cause having to do this more on a harder difficulty would just be beyond frustrating. All that being said, the game has a lot of interesting ideas, I particularly liked the process of making vampires.There are also a lot of references to other games and media ranging from hidden to bordering on plagiarism. So should you get Iratus? If you want more Darkest Dungeon content: Absolutely not. If you are interested in the game for it's own sake: Get it on sale. Overall: It's not a terrible game. It has a lot of cool ideas, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired. So I do not recommend anyone buy this game unless you are really really interested in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game so far. So far, i'd say its harder than Darkest Dungeon and the difficulty curve can be erratic sometimes. However, they've already done 2 balance patches since i've been playing, so they are actively tweaking it to make it enjoyable, difficult but not necessarily unfair (at least on purpose). With that being said, it still going to be hard and certain enemies are a handful and need to primaried quickly for your group to survive.Don't get attached to your minions, they will die. The minion crafting mechanic is interesting and provides more depth than darkest dungeon's equipment mechanic. Getting a lot of parts to combine and improve your minions can be a time sink but helps you square away the perfect build. Then, like Darkest Dungeon you get the "equipment" mechanic through items as each minion has 2 slots for special items to further build up your minions. You also have the Necromancer Iratus that can be upgraded through experience and artifacts, which allows special buffs/effects during fights and gives you fairly large list of magic/destruction skills to use to help swing the battle in your favor.Keep in mind, while the game doesn't explicitly state it, you'll want to start on the easy mode first "Cakewalk" to help get a grasp of the game/mechanics, but also to start unlocking a few of the other minions (which will carry over to any play through). The starting minions vary from good (dark knight) to meh (Skeleton) and while they'll get you through the beginning fights, you'll want to get some of the other minions on harder difficulties to start with. Keep in mind, even though its called "Cakewalk", don't expect it to be super easy on your first play-through.There is also the Graveyard mechanic, which functions similarly as Darkest Dungeon's City, but goes a bit deeper with ways to augment your Necromancer's abilities after fights (recharge mana, extra experience gained or rage during fights). You also have the building to heal your minions after fights (good to have multiples of the same minion in case they die or need to be rotated out). Then you have the excavation building which is helpful to gather more parts, which is crucial for maintaining an abundance of parts to keep building and upgrading your minions. So, while it compares to Darkest Dungeon's city mechanic, there are some differences to just it being a place to restore health and to upgrade. Speaking of which, upgrading minions is all free and they don't need to be placed in a building. This comes at the cost of them being easier to kill as compared to Darkest Dungeon. However, even with your minions being easier to kill, the game does provide some help so you don't have to grind them back up in the form of "Brains". Periodically, after a fight you'll gain a brain (30,40,50 IQ), which correlates to instantly upgrading your minion to Level 3 (30 IQ), Level 4 (40 IQ) and Level 5 (50 IQ) immediately when using the brain. This helps prevent grinding a minion back up at a key point. As mentioned, don't get too attached to your minions, or be aggravated when one dies, as they can quickly be replaced. You are a necromancer after all, you aren't supposed to be bro's with all your characters, they are merely fodder.Overall i'd recommend the game even as early access. The Dev's have already shown they're open to feedback and made some very quick balance changes to help with some unfair mechanics and smooth out the difficulty curve. Worth the money in my opinion if you enjoy a difficult Roguelike pulling from Darkest Dungeon's mechanics but with its own unique twists.

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely pretty good.It is, by design, sort of a simplified Darkest Dungeon where you play as the villains. Simplifying the formula doesn't add anything new and interesting to it, and it makes the game quite a lot easier (apart from a couple of wild difficulty spikes at certain bosses), but it's sort of fun to just cruise through, wrecking encounters on normal.There's a sanity mechanic, and you can use it against enemies (although you often need to build a whole team around this, and there are some enemies that are immune to sanity loss).Units are easy to create, promote, and swap into and out of your team.Upgrades are easy to come by, and mostly involve waiting to unlock the right type of unit to use as their foundation material.Units have a decent variety of directions you can build them in, and don't cost much to improve.Basically, if you bounced off Darkest Dungeon because of the difficulty, or you want something that's a bit more generic fantasy (although with some decent gothic notes), this should mostly hit the mark. It doesn't have a lot of plot, but the writing is decent and the voice actor for Iratus deserves a medal.This is a solid purchase on sale for most rpg fans---although Iratus is pretty blandly evil, and if you don't enjoy that, playing as him may put you off a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Darkest Dungeon is a great game for many reasons, and Iratus: Lord of the Dead does a tremendous job of highlighting those in its own way while also improving on the formula in several ways that makes this feel like a Definitive Edition of sorts for the genre. The production value is obviously slightly lower, but if you don't get hung up on some of the awkward voice acting/writing/sets, it really just hits the right gameplay loop out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: A rather poorly inspired attempt to show the other side of the Darkest Dungeon's mechanics. You will quickly find yourself in a defeat spiral because you are not allowed to backtrack, farm, and approach fights tactically. If you want to play a game where you will end up in an utterly untenable position and be forced into restarting the whole campaign because of one bad fight - even if you tried to scout the fight out and come up with a plan - this is the one for you. It's a grind monkey festival, albeit a short one, which is another thing not in the game's favor. Don't bother trying to play at higher difficulties at the start since the base building mechanic is tied to being a grind monkey and killing enemies in special ways to unlock the units you need to expend to achieve higher tier buildings.There's a lot of good in the game, but it is overshadowed by the misguided attempts to force replay value into a short campaign which boasts as its main difficulty point "bad loot RNG." Play Darkest Dungeon until the game is finished and if it is better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an example of Early Access done right. I first played mid-way through the EA phase, then came back for the full release. The differences are significant - not mere rebalancing, but fundamental changes to mechanics - yet it all works cohesively thanks to the devs' attention to feedback and detail.The game itself is an excellent example of the roguelike tactics genre. It was rewarding to find effective combos of minions, and challenging to have those combos negated by a different set of enemies which functioned in a very different way.Despite the wide variety of minions and enemies, the game does a fine job of keeping that variety within readily understood mechanics. While new enemies might throw out my old strategy, I understood how they did so, which allowed me to work on new counters to them.It's a well-presented, well-balanced, carefully designed game with plenty of content - well worth a go.

_childDocuments_.review: You like Darkest Dungeon?This game's better than Darkest Dungeon. It takes what's fun about the Darkest Dungeon formula and makes so many dungeons that you never knew made sense for this type of game.Example: This game does away with the grind of Darkest Dungeon and instead replaces it with an unforgiving rogue-like dungeon progression system that forces you to manage your resources for both short and long term.Other Example: You see the enemies that you will face before you pick your group to face them in Iratus. These enemies are more specialized and more unforgiving than you'd find in Darkest Dungeon, so you have to consider how to counter play the teams you will go up against. As a result, you cannot lean on the same tried-and-true party compositions in Iratus, you have to learn how to play many different styles to succeed.Make no mistake, this game isn't just a cheap Darkest Dungeon knock-off. It's aiming to be a full-blown competitor with fresh new ideas. Fresh new ideas that work.(To be fair, this game does lag behind Darkest Dungeon in art, but then again, Darkest Dungeon is a prettier game than most others out there.)
