_childDocuments_.review: So as of now, the game has just gone into public Early Access, and is still very much a beta. I expect plenty of numbers to be changed as it develops.Traps are a neat mechanic that makes you value movement skills so much more. Sanity damage is fun to build around, and seeing you're enemies flee in terror or have a heart attack and die goes great with the atmosphere of the game.The ability to string together your army from the corpses of enemies is a great idea, as well as just slotting in a brain to make your units level up quickly. In fact everything to do with flavor is already amazingly on point and it makes the game much easier to get invested in.That said, this is definitely a beta, and there are lots of balance issues, the most glaring of which are golems and bosses.Golems have no sanity meter, and hit like a truck. When they are too far away to hit you, their move that pushes them up boosts their accuracy, So if you build with stress in mind, the regular golems are often harder than elite fights.Bosses are naturally quite strong, and are where you really notice the game's lack of healing. In a battle that lasts many many rounds chip damage and crits add up quickly. The first boss could be fine with some minor changes, but the second boss needs major changes.At this point anything extra would be rambling, So I will just end by saying that I do really enjoy this game, and am excited to see where it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Darkest Dungeon you will enjoy this. Its similar but with some tweaks. You will have more characters customization and a less forgiving experience when things goes bad and you lose your minions. Unless you screwed it very badly, you can recover with a fresh one of similar level immediately, at least a couple times. The fact that you as the Necromancer can  gear yourself and cast spells in battle damaging the enemies or buffing your minions adds for an intesreting option. That, with the mentioned characters customization and the fact that you can't remove the items (trinkets) once you give them to your minions, makes the game separate from Darkest Dungeon. Also combat involves more moving around and stances.And you also will have insane difficulty levels if you like to push your limits. Darkest Dungeon was an easy game (even on the hardest setup) once you know the mechanics and play properly, I think the hardest difficulty in this game will be more like a challenge, probably with a little bit of min/max needed here and there.On the only bad side, I find the game not as polished as Darkest Dungeon, which remains the superior one for this genre. The city management system was also superior in the DD game; here it is very simplistic.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people compare it to darkest dungeon, but outside of the combat system it is a completely diffetent game. For an early access it offers a lot, 3 levels, with 4 difficulties, a great amount of minions to create, a ♥♥♥♥ ton of abilities and a big variety of enemies. Right now there are only 3 bosses and the game isnt long enought to take advantage of completely inproving your base (even less outside of the easiest difficulty since apparently you get less materials, so you have to decide if you spent them in your base or in your army) but once they add more levels that will be better.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage and overall bizarre design choices, starting from the premise of the game that contradicts itself : - the game overly emphasizes how your troops are expendable and just as easy to replace, and yet, if you lose one guy, there's an high chance you'll lose the items that you invested on that dude, not a 100% guarantee that occurs, but, its possible. To the odd and downright unfair boss designs that are designed around trial and error : - if Boss 1 gets attacked, all their henchmen gets a free attack on you- Boss 2 just attacks 5 times each turn, decimating your troops ... basically for free, also have 1K HP each. Very shallow gameplay loop that, if you fail too much and burn your resources too quickly, you ultimately fail the campaign because you can't progress in any other way but retry the same fight :- did you get RNG'd on that last bossfight ? lost all your good dudes have no good monsters to replace them ? well ♥♥♥♥ you gotta start the game again from the start.The combat is okay, but the progression is just just ... you'll be stuck with a handful of monsters, +2 if you buy the DLC, the rest are unlockable, a good numbers of those are only available very late into the game, and a few, only after you complete one run for whatever reason ... that is just dumb. The artstyle is okay, nothing to write home about, the animation are bad and Caleb is a good narrator, overall, i think it lacks all the charm of Darkest dungeon but, eh, what can you do. I could only recommend it to someone who truly loves the DD formula type of game, otherwise, hardskip.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Love games like this, but nearly all of them make you play boring good guys. You constantly deal with so many pesky things when your a good guy, this game on the other hand makes you the other side and damn is it fun and refreshing. There is so much joy in making all the enemy go mad from your undead minions and then to see them croak from a heart attack is just a delight. If you enjoy being a bastard and downright villain this is a great game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not for everyone with average level and it may be very difficult for players that into this roguelite game. For example, it requires a big intuition when you had to utilize into any characters that available every floors and once a character died, you'd have to either create another one or dupe in order to level them up again. The only quick way to level them up is to boost them up with a special "item" (I won't spoil it for you, but you have to play it out for yourself). I only stopped at the 5th floor where it ended up at last floor with insufficient lvl45-40 and I couldn't be further anymore. I should have invest more into those characters but that's where I crossed the line. On the plus side, I was actually had so much fun with it, and pretty addictive! I would highly recommend for players with err....high IQ. >_> You *could* try it out if you want but tbh, I wouldn't be recommend it if I were you.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best games I've played in the past few years.  It fixes the issues that Darkest Dungeon has, and actually made them fun.  Great team combos, but no cheese.  It still had RNG aspects that can be frustrating at times, but it never seems unfair.Also, even if you wipe, it give you plenty of opportunity to rebuild your teams.  You get to build the way you want to build and artifacts really make a difference in your team comp.  Wonderful art, music and narration.  Normal difficulty is challenging and fun, with higher levels for those asking for more of a challenge.  Hats off to the devs on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion it's better than Darkest Dungeon, the later updates leaned way too heavily into puzzle type combat. This game is far more straightforward, all creature types have skills for various combat positions, although they'll be way less effective if knocked out of a spot it's not as much of a disaster as DD.Also, lots of undead waifus, with one being a literal undead waifu and another basically being Lizbeth Covenant from Clive Barker's Undying.Some of the minion balancing is kind of terrible at the moment, however. One of the starter minions is a perfect tank but doesn't actually have a taunting skill, while the backup glass cannon melee skeleton for some reason does?
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Good for first impressions. It's not difficult in an annoying sense, it's more difficult in the sense that you have to learn what moves combo with which other moves. _childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I too got stiffed with 'load last checkpoint' at the end of the second floor. Just 3 battles away from the final boss of level 2 after pouring quite a few hours into the game and getting the hang of things, I decided to experiment with mixing rare parts to see what that was about. Quickly found out it was a gamble not worth taking so clicked the button that in any other game would be a 'load in last checkpoint' button... as in the end/start of the previous battle... and... back to the... start...OF THE ENTIRE FLOOR...ERGH!!Now yes I agree it did say what would happen and I checked afterwards and it was my mistake admittedly. However, in an adrenaline filled moment as excitement was brewing for the final battle and the next floor was inching closer, it just feels a bit like the carpet has been swept out and I am now totally deflated about this game. My reaction is to now to take a break from the game with a sour taste as my final memory before I decide whether or not to repeat the same 4-5 hours of gameplay to get to the same point.. that prospect really doesn't sound fun at all. Solution: Make a clearer warning message pop up. The gravity of this decision is so far and beyond all the other little message pop ups that the game kind of gets you in the habit of dismissing. ALT Solution: Get rid of this macho 'our game is hard' 'it has tough consequences' BS and make saving and reloading an OPTION for those players who don't like having the frustration of repeating 4-5 hours of the same gameplay for an error.

_childDocuments_.review: Very decent, challenging game that twists the Darkest Dungeon aspect over! While I enjoy being the bad guy and being able to dish out sanity to my enemies, there's a few points that bring the game to a crashing halt.1) Economy: This was my number one grievance while playing in the difficulties above "Cakewalk." If I lost my minions enough times, there was essentially no way for me to gain them back. While I appreciate that these enemies I've died to don't regenerate their health and such, if it's a boss, the player is left quite screwed.2) Minions: I liked that there were some which you only gained gradually as you progressed, what I didn't like was how overtly stronger some were compared to others. Skeletons and Zombies by nature make great cannon fodder and since they're starter minions, this was understandable. However, the synergy with Lich and/or Ghoul (a very overpowered minion) shouldn't be a deciding factor in my team compositions when there are numerous other minions to choose from. This could just be my lack in forethought how the other minions work, but I DO know for a fact none of my other minions do nearly as much damage as that Ghoul, not even the Dhampir/Bone Golem.3) Quests: I actually found myself planning my paths based on how many of these popped up. Lots of them were actually really cool, while others after effects weren't clear. For example, I received extra Vigor to Zombies, which appeared in upgrades for them. On the other hand I'd receive a debuff for -XX Vigor to enemies for my next two fights, but at the start of the battle it didn't seem all that apparent they took any hit to their Vigor. Another point to bring up is the lack of information on risk/reward for specific options chosen. The most regrettable one I made being to "Parley" with a group of mages only to have a decently worked on minion die for it. 4) Artifacts: This was implemented really well, there were quite a few combinations that really helped the player decide a playstyle. I didn't care for the two or three I'd get all with different names that did the exact same thing though. There's a particular one that gives 10% chance of extra body parts, and then another two or so that give the same effect, BUT go in the exact same slot. So what's the point? It also didn't help that depending on the random artifacts you start a game with, those felt as though they would push you to play a specific way. 5) Buildings: I feel this one is more of a "Wait-and-See" than any of the others, some buildings were mandatory (but only depending on your chosen playstyle). If you intended to do a lot of spell-slinging, there was a building for that. If you wanted to use ultimate attacks in rapid succession, there was a building for that. If you wanted to MAYBE get a few extra parts for WHEN not IF you lose some minions/waste your time MAYBE getting an extra minion item, there were buildings for that. Having an infirmary was a moot point, didn't feel like upgrading that whatsover. Aside from those buildings, I don't see the point of building something that allows me to build more buildings, when fighting enemies gives me the currency I already need to make that happen. Same could be said for the training grounds, there's an item that bumps my lvl 1 to a lvl 3-5 in an instant should I be willing to spend the EXP to Alchemy to more frequently attain said item. Tip for those reading this, the vampire spell made it easier to find "grunt workers" for your numerous buildings. All in all, great concept, but there's a lot of traffic jams that frustratingly cause players to need to start over if they distributed their resources incorrectly. For that reason, I can't say I'd recommend it to someone unless they're a glutton for the kind of punishment Dark Souls and Darkest Dungeon didn't explore...Start Over.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as the Anti-hero Iratus, the idea is world domination but how does one achieve this?You craft minions out of body parts dropped after combat wins and loses(to recoup some of what is lost).The minions make up to teams of 4:Some teams do damage to enemies and sometimes this is the only path to victory.Other teams can be based on stress damage which can chain kill enemies and give them massive debuffs and sometimes crushing buffs- to the enemies.Other more niche teams focus on spellpower and allow you Iratus to pump the damage or party-wide buffs for a time.Minions can use class trinkets which only they can use these are often focused on what they are intended to do like do more damage in DoTs form or to gain stacking buffs to endure more pain.Minions can have up to 2 items equipped and they are whatever you like so you want tanks like Bone Golems to have defensive items and Brides to have damage buffs.The minions grow in strength by both leveling the stat page or by gaining one of two skills and this adds lots of depth to the game and sometimes completely defines builds.You can name the minions and change their skins for fun!Sometimes bosses are better fought with one minion and certain items, YOLO SOLO build.You can gear Iratus and invest into his skill trees and every run is different as items drop randomly and levels are even random.There is also a special vault where you spend diggers souls to upgrade called the graveyard giving you buffs in and outside of battle.You can craft potions which are made of the same parts as your minions and they grant massive boons and even allow for boss cheesing but you have to figure out how if you want to- I don't.The enemies grow in complexity as you go further and they often cause people who don't use proper teams game over moments. The depth of item uses, potions, trinket, gear, spells, minion comps, enemy comps, etc. will really press you in EH3-5 EH5 being the hardest difficulty. Every battle is a puzzle and you can win if you try out new stuff and plan ahead. The gameplay when you really dig into it is 10/10, it's the nuance on tweeking builds and being able to go all in too that really shows that they made a lowkey masterpiece.The artwork is great and the soundtrack is lowkey worthy of praise not sure how the team pulled the game off but 10/10 for art and sound design.The games difficulty goes from a cakewalk yes it's called that to blindfolded Elden Ring underwater.I am biased because I was the first to beat the hardest mode after it was updated to the games last build version. I have 569 hours on this game. I play the game now in a modded state with rebalanced stats and the Next Floor Mod but even in Vanilla this game is 10/10. I also mod the game and have my own balance patch. ; )You can easily spend hours theory crafting if you want to min/max the game but even played as a casual people love the feeling of dispensing Iratus(Wrath in Latin) upon the hapless peons you will face. Good luck in beating the game, so you have chosen death!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfrozen's 2020 creation and Daedalic's publishing lead have learned from Darkest Dungeon, but in my fast look. What can I add in its negatives and positives not touched on. Let's get to it.What I liked:The Switch: Well obviously you are evil here, were DD you are the tragic heroes. They don't hide that its a clone, but not having the pressure of saving the world is a nice twist. Here destroy the world. Nice change.Graveyard: Here your focusing on key units and not having to watch in horror as you keep hiring units to fill the endless graveyard of DD. It has a fun level unit system without the worry of torches, and endless potions to match in game traps all day. Graphics: Everything complements one another in color, scheme, and easy layout functions where you not searching for something. The effects are spot on, and the game has great mod potential. They learned from DD and thought it through. A plusSound: Wondeful voice overs and sounds that bring the atmosphere to lifeAilments: Some may miss the DD stress systems, and some may find relief in never dealing with those negative effects again. Masochist anyone??!!!Controls: Super easy to manageWhat I feel needs to improve:The Base: A nice base start here with simple 'upgrade" systems that move up in one direction, but games miss the idea of mutations and having both functions for a player to use. Not just upgrading that castle one way, but mutating it another. You will upgrade that Skeleton, but miss the opportunity of making into something else with diverse mutating and upgrading systems. A miss for me.The Expert player: They may find the game itself, too easy, especially if they are DD masters. The Buildings: Though gorgeous in the HOMM style and everything does compliment the game mechanics, they lack creativeness and don't bring anything new to the genre. DLC expense: Another long line of games that gain income for DLCs that could have been included. Final Take:I liked a lot of Iratus, with wonderful potential of expansion and modding, but turn base genre games must grow and be more creative in there implementations to compete since the genre is flooded with these types of games. Whether isometric, first person or old style left to right dungeon crawlers. Iratus is a nice addition and if you love Darkest Dungeons, you will enjoy Iratus for what it is. See the game play in videos above the discussion tab before you buy. A nice start to destroying the world. My score: 3.7 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: is a turn-based dungeon roguelike RPG that looks and plays quite similar to another popular game called Darkest Dungeon. -there are four difficulties to choose from, and the first two difficulties are seriously noob friendly.-quicksave is available in the first two difficulties (no more stupid backing up saves by hand manoeuvre )-for the higher difficulties where quicksave is unavailable, there is the retreat from battle option to save the day(could fail)-you control 4 units max, and explore 6 dungeons , each of your unit has 6 skills that can be upgraded and augmented with items.-collect gold to build up your small base to become more powerful, and collect items for your units to make the fights more interesting.-you are represented by the main character Iratus, an undead necromancer who wants to take over the world. He is the narrator of the game just like the one in Darkest Dungeon. While not participating in combat directly, he has mana and can use magic spells just like the hero in Heroes of Might and Magic 3.-a lot of units to choose from(some require unlocking), to form your dream team!This game is developed by Unfrozen studio, a small studio from a country called Republic of Cyprus (first time I heard of this country), their company staff came from games such as Disciples series and Pathologic 2 . The most straightforward way to describe this game, is that it is a better and noob-friendlier Darkest Dungeon in almost all aspects. Better looking even, with more details to every units. I hated Darkest Dungeon's gut. No matter how prepared you are in Darkest Dungeon, the enemies would wipe you out 2+ times in a row on easy missions. Darkest Dungeon is also full of stupid micromanagement such as stress damage that you have to deal with after battle, food, torches, shovels, and other stupid time wasting mechanics. Unfrozen studio did nothing of the sort to this game thank god! Darkest Dungeon's only saving grace is its workshop mods(and maybe its extremely talented narrator ).If you've ever feel screwed by the unfairness of Darkest Dungeon, I highly recommend getting this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Iratus: Lord of the Dead" is a turn-based strategy game developed by Unfrozen Studios. The player takes on the role of Iratus, an evil necromancer who creates an army of undead after being freed from his dungeon.One of the game's unique features is that players take on the role of villains instead of heroes, adding a new and interesting twist to the genre. The game is full of black humor and macabre elements that bring it to life.However, "Iratus" also has some weaknesses. It can be challenging and requires a lot of strategy and patience. The upgrade system can also be confusing due to the many abilities and equipment items available.Overall, "Iratus: Lord of the Dead" is a captivating and entertaining game. The characters are interesting and full of personality, the graphics are dark and detailed, and the music is atmospheric and fitting for the game.if you are looking for a challenging game with black humor and macabre elements that provides a fresh perspective on the strategy genre, "Iratus: Lord of the Dead" is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is a lot less stressful to play than Darkest Dungeon, that's for sure. But is it a good game? Yes, I think it is - it's got pretty much all the best parts of DD, team building and graveyard improvements and adds another layer to the tactical combat: Iratus, yourself, can cast spells during a minion's turn for the cost of some mana with various effects.You can also build any minion you have unlocked through repeated gameplay from the outset as long as you have the 'parts' to create them so there's no random element to who becomes available. I'm playing the game with all the DLC so I have more options at the start. But the werewolf is a must-have and he's a freebie. get one asaap - it's a fun addition to the game.Otherwise, you get to play as the bad guy and stress the enemy out causing them to go insane and to have hearts attacks. You don't have to worry about your favourite minions getting afflictions requiring a lot of gold to remove.The voice acting is not as good as DD's but it is still entertaining. While more stylised, DD's artwork is probably better but this looks mopre realistic and you have several skin options  to customise your minions.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Original review from early access is below, I've tried playing the game again since release and found the developers did a great job creating methods to rebuild your units up to fighting strength. Among other aspects, the ability to retreat in a battle going south, getting minions at comparable levels to your current party during certain map events, and the fact unit training building actually lets minions gain experience faster than map battles, all allow you sufficient wiggle room that even a spat of bad luck won't prematurely end a campaign.Game has enjoyable setting and has fun combat mechanics with enough units to make finding new synergies rewarding.OLD REVIEW:The game has a lot of potential, but it seems to be suffering from two competing design strategies taken from Darkest Dungeon and Slay the Spire.The former game, Darkest Dungeon, emphasizes the expendability of your units. Making defeat a constant spectre of any dungeon run depending on how strong your units are. This isn't problematic however, as the game is setup such that you can return to old dungeons with fresh units in case a string of defeats has set you back to nearly square one. You're never railroaded into continuously more difficult encounters in case you've had a bad string of luck.The latter game, Slay the Spire, emphasizes the indispensability of your unit. You have to achieve victory in every single combat up to the final boss lest you need to restart the game entirely. This isn't problematic either, because there's not much setup or time invested into any one run. The game is also balanced such that with a little luck and enough knowledge of game mechanics you can put together card combos that make defeat nigh impossible.The problem with Iratus then is that it tries to emphasize the expendable and replaceable nature of your units in a game setting where defeat is very unforgiving.I want to recommend the game, and again: the game has a lot of potential, but I think the developers need to figure out a way balance the gameplay design such that a string of defeats won't leave you resentful of the fact you're being forced to progress in a losing scenario. Where quitting and restarting the game is actually the more viable strategy compared to seeing things out until the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Very playable in the current state, though if balance issues bug you, you should definitely wait for the full release.  Still, I see a lot of potential here.  I like the artstyle, Iratus himself is fun to listen to, and there's the makings of a pretty interesting resource management system. I will say that if you're coming to this after Darkest Dungeon, you should know you'll need to take a bit better care of your minions.  Your primary means of making minions is killing the living for parts, meaning if you ever get to a point you can't make more, you're screwed.  This isn't a complaint, mind you-- it helps with the feeling that Iratus really is desperately clawing his way back to power, and that this is a challenge even for an ancient necromancer.  But you will need to unlearn the "Well I can always get a new mook off the carriage" mindset.  That's kind of a delightful reversal, when you think about it: In Darkest Dungeon, life is cheap.  In Iratus, corpses are dear.Thumbs up.  I had misgivings about getting this game on early access, but I don't regret it at all.  If you don't mind dealing with the odd bug or balance issue, I'd say this is worth the money.  Can't wait to see the finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: I started and finished the game. Worth every penny when on sale ($5~6). I beat the game in about 10 hours, from tutorial to end credits. I beat it on an easy mode. It was not a hard game in easy mode at all, I lost two minions the entire game in boss fights. Overall enjoyable game similar to Darkest Dungeon (which I found to be way more difficult frankly) and really its even more like Legend of the Keepers with the moral/stress mechanic (which I enjoyed but it too was difficult at times). I'm not a fan of "rogue-anything" games where you play and die and start over so I wanted to just play through it and beat the game and be good with that. The art is great. The audio is great. There's really no story or any lore, it's a straight forward game play type game. I didn't use all the minions and i unlocked half of them (headless was my last and didn't unlock any others for half the game). I beat the game mostly using the werewolf, bride, zombie and skeleton. Each area has different enemies and so you need different ways to deal with them. You can't beat the game with just stress, you will not get anywhere with just stress. If they flee you don't get the parts they would drop and you run out of crafting material fast. The zombie, skeleton and werewolf were my favorites. Zombie brings AOE with magic damage (which was a bid deal on the Cathedral level with all the high armors). Skeleton is a multi-do-all minion that can tank well, guard well, stun, ignore armor, can't be debuffed (this is huge, makes him immune to lots of bad things all game). Werewolf is not great but I used him as a front line assassin because in that position he gets a single nuke attack first round on the enemy rear line (which is always a caster type) which meant I always took out 1 enemy first round with him immediately (I used destruction magic to remove any shield/ward on the target first). Made every fight automatically easier. My final fights were mostly two Zombies (both with magic AOE stance attacks constantly and both in back row), skeleton (guarding werewolf) and werewolf up front (for the first round nuke attack). They were in the low level 50's when I beat the game.Enjoyable to level up minions and choose their upgrade paths for what you need and equip them with items according to what you want them to do. Lots of prep strategy there. Example, I focused on defense on the skeleton and gave him items that game him damage reduction and dealt magic damage when something attacked him. Magic damage tank in that setup and very tough.For Iratus himself, I focused on Alchemy (all of it is very useful, early and late game, way more useful than nearly anything else) to get more materials to craft. Magic is another good tree, if nothing else just to get dispel (hugely useful late game). Ire is my 3rd tree to get minion supporting passives (the actives are not great). And I put the rest into a little destruction to get a few final spells that were very useful (obelisk is enormously useful, magic damage and stun, it wins fights on its own). Starting out, do alchemy rapidly so you always have mats.Would I play it again? Maybe. Not right now. A year from now maybe? And play through with different strategy, maybe harder? I don't like difficult games, that's not fun for me. But I wouldn't mind playing through again one day differently.Looking back, I would have easily been able to beat the game with Zombie, Zombie, Skeleton, Dark Knight. You could sub Dark Knight for any other minion with defensive abilities or even just a 2nd Skeleton. 2 zombies 2 skeletons could beat this game on easier modes for sure with massive tanking and lots of magic AOE damage.I have no DLC. I couldn't unlock the other minions without it, and I won't bother with that. The base game itself is worth the $5 or so on sale. Not sure I would buy all the DLC because I just wouldn't play through this multiple times over and over (rogue like type approach). The DLC costs more than the game it seems.

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason, I really enjoyed the difficulty and insane ramping damage. I played a good amount and has played on the hardest difficulty. I do think a lot of the bosses are absolutely overtuned and numbers are way too high, but there is so many things to enjoy about the game that I highly recommend, especially with the sale! It's like Darkest Dungeon but with a different look, you play as evil monsters defending a dungeon, and you decide to push back. So you start to storm through the human(?) areas down a navigation path similar to Slay the Spire. You pick up items, new allies, and encounter enemies. Each end has a boss. You have a certain amount of floors to go through until you break free of your tomb.  Each floor has new enemies and items to get it, while at the same time building your minions from pieces of dead bodies you have killed. It's a pretty fun system and trying out combinations to unlock classes is interesting. You can also equip items to your main guy, Iratus. He holds a number of abilities and passives you can unlock by leveling him up. There is a few different builds to go, but towards the end you'll be using around the same "meta stack" of what you believe to be the strongest stack. But that is why there is difficulty changes! It's really fun if you just wanna chill and look at cool animations and unlock stuff, it's worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game as far as it has gotten.   Was really bummed that they don't have more completed.  Good strategy and resource management.  Fun commentary. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but I struggled to come up with enough redeeming factors to outweigh the negatives currently facing the game.  Of course it's extremely similar to Darkest Dungeon, but where DD was somewhat elegant in the overall simplicity, this game seems to add some unncessary fluff mechanics to make up for the refinement of it's core gameplay.The result is core gameplay that still needs some balance tweaks and a lot of other features that feel lackluster or cobbled together.  Gameplay-wise, there are many similarities between DD and this game.  Besides the setting, the big difference is that you can actively damage enemy stress versus going  after health, and just like DD, if you stress-out an enemy enough, they will break and get debuffed (or in some cases, HEAVILY buffed).  Combine this health / stress mechanic with a two part armor system: There's physical armor and magical armor.  So now you're presented with the option of dealing normal damage, magic damage, or stress.  The game will throw various combinations of enemies at you that are (usually) good at resisting at least one of these things, so it's often you'll see enemies strong against magic who are weak to physical, or enemies strong against physical attacks who aren't strong against stress abilities.  Therefore your own party composition will generally need to alter from fight-to-fight so you don't get straight up counter-comped.  After all, it's pretty hard to be effective going in with a team focused on heaping on debuffs or stress when the enemy team is packing a member that will constantly heal stress and clear your debuffs as fast as they are applied.This emphasizes knowing the next fight and managing your troops accordingly.  It's hard to say if these troops are truly meant to be expendable or not.   There's not a HUGE difference between a level 1 minion and a level 5-6 (max) minion, although the game does emphasize leveling up a few teams and using them properly.  This becomes more difficult as very few minions can effectively heal, and so it's fairly difficult to preserve your forces.  They're not THAT difficult to replace, but unlike DD, it does appear this game has a final fail state once you run out of body parts to replace minions.  There's no "farming" or going back on old fights - you just go one way through the dungeon.This non-stop ramping up of difficulty then means losses to your A-Team or upgraded minions is extremely punishing.  Since there's no going back to farm anything back up, unless you already have a backup lined up, it's permanently going to set you back as you replace that minion with either something not suited to the composition, or simply something lower level (and thus more likely to die again).  Again, DD of course functionally has no fail state, but this just seems it's too easy to get painted into a corner from which there's no return.Lastly beyond minion creation, there's little upgrade equipment you stick on your minions, then upgrades you stick on the necromancer himself (but some of these are one-shot on the next fight only) so then you get to go back and re-equip necro after every fight.  Then there's this whole building / garrison mechanic, but your troops aren't doing stuff like relieving stress or learning abilities, some of them get healed, some level up, some do research for you, some dig up body parts, and so on.  This is ok BUT there's no summary screen like DD that shows what everyone is doing, or what their level is - so you get to click around to all of these UI elements to see if you accidentally parked your level 5 Skelly at the mortuary.Between the necro and the minions and the buildings and the lack of most any summary UI to see wtf is happening between all these little systems combined, it's definitely a game in Early Access.  A few improved UI elements and a balance pass or two would go a long way.   Most notably:  A summary screen to see what ALL minions are doing, and second, something that will display the potential next fight(s) so you can tailor your team accordingly.  Stress attacks too seem very random at times as to what they'll do or if they're going to be that effective.  It often seems easier to just club through armor and kill, even if someone is warded.Whether or not there's any change on going back to "farm" stuff or having that ability.  I dunno.  It seems there's a certain roguelike element to this that doesn't exist in DD.  In any case, for now I'd say wait until more changes go in to buy.  It's hard to tell exactly how this game will turn out.

_childDocuments_.review: I found Darkest Dungeon too hard. Losing a high-level character puts you back to square one and you have to start all over again (or be constantly grooming a very large group of characters, which takes a lot of time). I found Iratus to be nearly a clone of Darkest Dungeon with the exception of the "brain" mechanic. While I'm sure this mechanic was intended to ease the pain caused by the brutality of losing characters in DD, unfortunately it swings too far the other way and makes Iratus too easy. In DD, you are back to level 1 after death but in Iratus you can use a brain to basically lose no levels at all after death. I found this made the game almost trivial. I give it a thumbs up because it is well implemented and fun to play, but if you've played DD, there is nothing really new here. Hopefully there will be eventually a game that threads the needle between being too hard (DD) and too easy (Iratus).

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be dissuaded by the "Early Access", the game has a lot of fun, content and replayability already available and I have not run into any bugs. I heartily recommend the game even now in Early Access and am really looking forward to seeing what the full game is like. Gameplay seemed fairly balanced on easy and normal difficulty so far; maybe on later difficulties there is more unbalance.An update for re-balance and a new character comes out tomorrow, so this review is for the game as I played it for a week or so before the this update.So - obviously, this games takes inspiration from Darkest Dungeon, but playing as forces of evil against heroes instead. It's interesting and allows for some pretty neat classes and designs to select from for your party. While the comparisons to DD are fair, I think Iratus does a great job at establishing it's own identity. Instead of a long and grueling campaign with slow progression like in Darkest Dungeon, you instead have a short campaign through some dungeons where you can make a lot of progress and build up quickly.  Fail or pass, the available minions you unlocked carry over to the next run. Thus, there is huge replayability in trying out new minion compositions, ascending to higher difficulty for challenges, or just playing for fun because the core gameplay loop is addicting fun. Since the campaigns are short (my last campaign shows 39 battles played, and I deliberately took some longer roundabout paths to fight more battles), it's easy to play and complete one in just a weekend.In Early Access, there are 3 dungeons to conquer, with what looks like at least two more to be available in the full game. 18 minions (characters to form battle parties) are available with a 19th being added tomorrow. There are tons of items to find and utilize as well as spells/skills for Iratus to choose from. The minions themselves can gain up to 7 levels and with each level they can choose to upgrade a skill in one of two directions which have different side effects (i.e. maybe less damage than the other upgrade but now is able to stun targets) and also different stats. So even if you don't plan to use the skill for a build it may be useful for the stat boost. Then instead of equipment, minions can be enhanced by adding items to 2 item slots, or by crafting them (or replacing existing parts) with rarer parts that have stat boosts built into them.Iratus is a necromancer, so instead of getting free party members like in Darkest Dungeon, you must find parts in order to craft your party. You can use alchemy to transform parts into different kinds. Extra parts can become mana to use for spells instead. You find parts at the end of each battle and can boost the chances with some items you may find along the way as well. Like Darkest Dungeon, there are also upgradeable buildings to enhance the experience. These do not carry over through playthroughs though. The different benefits you can get from the buildings are:More exp for IratusMana regen for IratusWrath boost for Iratus at start of battle (Wrath is sort of like mana but for minions to use their more powerful skills. It renews in battle through damage taken and received or skills that directly give wrath)An arena to train up to 4 minions 2 exp at a timeA health regen facility to restore health up to 4 minions  left in the buildingAn item finding facilityA part finding facilityAnd lastly a building that boosts the currency used to make these buildings in the first place.A typical gameplay loop will be as follows:You start with one item, and 4 minions and some parts. You start at the hub where you can choose to upgrade Iratus (if have talent points from leveling up), upgrade the minions, move minions around to rearrange parties, place minions in buildings, make the buildings, craft new minions, craft parts through alchemy, etc.. From this hub, you can also select a map which has you enter the dungeons.The dungeons is an overhead view of a map where you can see what the next battle encounter is and plan your party accordingly. If you see you're fighting a golem for example, a stress party is not going to be helpful as golems don't have fear. At some points in the dungeon there will be a fork and you have to choose with path to go to. You can look ahead and see what is coming, but battle encounter more than one movement away will only reveal one enemy type. Also note there is no random encounters or replaying battles. There is no going back.Only forward or to the side. Not all paths are equal. Some can be longer and more rounadabout if want to grind for exp/items/parts, but this may also be risky and can lose your best minion before the boss. The boss will always be the final encounter on each dungeon/ Once you've played the boss once and seen how it works, it probably won't be too challenging in the future. Maybe this will be addressed in future updates.Battles are fairly similar to darkest dungeon. It is turn based 4 vs 4 system with  a health bar for yourself and a health and stress bar for the enemies. You have three different attack types: physical, magic, and stress. Fire also exists as a status and there are all sorts of buffs, stances, stuns and so on to fine-tune some strategy. Stress can lead to insanity and debuffs or possibly inspired and buffs which may ruin your day. So it can be risky, but in some cases, some enemies are dealt with easier via heart attack of too much stress or scaring them into fleeing. Anyways, after each battle, you are rewarded in parts and exp for both Iratus and the minions along with any bonuses from the buildings constructed. You are also returned to the hub. Thus between each battle encounter you can swap your party, send your hurt minions to heal over the next battle etc. So the game isn't quite like Darkest Dungeon where you need 1 party to survive many encounters. Instead, you can swap your party around and tune it to each encounter. However, the drawback is healing is pretty scarce, especially in the early game before unlocking later minions. Most of the difficulty comes from this. I had a really rough time in my jump from easy to normal difficulty because I was missing some key party members that make great self-healing tanks. I think my next run will go a lot smoother now that I've unlocked such.That said - the easy difficulty is indeed easy. If you were turned off from Darkest Dungeon by its difficulty you may still like this game on the easier difficulty.  If you like the challenge, this game definitely gets more challenging as you go up in difficulty. You can also impose your own challenge through your choice in party members. That said, no party member seems useless. They all have been pretty fun. But as hinted by the above, some do seem more crucial in alleviating the difficulty than others. Definitely recommend this game, especially to any RPG or dungeon crawler fans. It gets really addicting unlocking all the minions and I would recommend to try out each one at least once. On paper some may seem lackluster, but then when you combine them with another minion something clicks. For example, marking your allies to provoke them to be attacked more, then sending that ally into a counterattack/defensive/healing stance. The game stands out from Darkest Dungeon for the following:IMO, it is more accessible and easier to learn and get into, mostly due to the next pointShorter campaigns and easier to restart and play through in a weekendYou can cast spells to interfere with the battles at any point in your turn (once per cycle of all your minions)While Darkest Dungeon characters may be more iconic and memorable I actually really like the designs of the monsters. Especially love the Unfrozen, Damphir and Lich.  The aesthetic in this game is awesome, love the art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an acquired taste. If you're really into dungeon crawling and you like Darkest Dungeon type combat, get it. Which is a shame, because the art is nice and the setting has a pretty cool vibe to it. It's all just very shallow and it didn't feel inviting to me to explore further. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a perfect roguelite experience, but pretty good overall.+Lots of different minions with lots of different abilities, items, artefacts and talents. No run need to be exactly same.+Feeling of permanent progress when you unlock new minions to use and enemy entries in humonarium.+Fights are a comfortable challenge, if you know what you're doing.-Some things are too good, even on higher difficulties (Looking at you, Finger of Death). Instead of modifying strategy against specific enemies, you'll end up spamming the one tactic that works everytime. Then you have to resolve not to use it at all in the next run simply for the sake of keeping things a challenge.-With lots of things being too good, lots of other things are too bad. Many useless abilities can be upgraded to include handy effects, like moving an enemy or removing all blocks and wards, but too many damage abilities simply have "increase x damage" or "increase y damage". -Runs tend to get a little boring on 4th floor and upwards.Did you know you can upgrade a part inside a minion with digger souls? I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game. Decent replayability due to increasing level of challenge. Story is basically nonexistent if you care about such things. Its similar to Darkest Dungeon in that you have 4 characters with different abilities vs 4 other enemies with different abilities determined  by class. Its one long dungeon crawl as opposed to quick jaunts into dungeons. In Iratus, you are crawling out of a dungeon.There is far less RNG in Iratus, which i like. Yes you still miss key attacks, or roll low on damage, or fail the roll to make the item to upgrade your duder. However, the decision you make are far more impactful. You decide what your team is. You don't have have to wait for lich to show up in a wagon, you just make him. Also there is far more customization of your characters than in DD. You can turn your lich in crowd killing, he even kills your guys, power house or can make him into a stress dealer. You can make one minion into a solo duder with upgrades and items, forget bringing in 3 others.Overall, I like this game more. The pacing is solid, a campaign won't last for eternity but around 10 - 20 hours depending on how fast you take it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Darkest Dungeon I always was on a lookout for any similiar games in an interesting for me setting. In general I really like the possibility to take a "bad guy" cape in video games (almost all of them only give you an option to be a boring boy-scout which gets tiresome at some point). And when I played DD I thought "I wish there was an ability to play the monsters or at least use them somehow" (and there was that possibility, with the help of some mods of course).I also love the idea of necromancy in games: controlling hordes of the undead, slaying everything in their path, only growing stronger with every battle and consuming all like a disease. That's the reason why I always try to build pet-oriented characters or at least employ some form of dark magic in games.And then I saw a trailer for this game and, o boy, it really seemed like a perfect fit for me. I patiently waited for its release and here we are - I finally got to play it (it's only an early access release, but oh well).What can I say right now? I like it. When you first play it, it certainly feels harder than Darkest Dungeon in some aspects, but when you get used to it and start to see a bigger picture, then it gets easier to enjoy the gameplay. Just gotta learn those enemy abilities, try on bosses and make up a fitting build to counter them. Not everything works though and the balance in this game is certainly in need of attention from the developers (and it looks like they're right on it - devs are active in the forums, they listen to feedback and rollout updates to change things up).The variety of available minions is to my liking (and there will be more), there are enough possible ways to create and use different builds and the progression is decent enough (not too grindy, not too fast).I like the art style, the music isn't too distracting and I find myself enjoying some of the Iratuse's remarks. What I would like to see added to this game: mod support, as mods really boost the game's life and improve the game in many aspects: players can add new content or improve the existing one and they can also change the balance how they like.I also would like a possibility to make it less linear in some way, for instance it would be interesting to have a way of exploring the whole map or be capable of backtracking to gather as many resources as possible to prepare for a boss fight. tl;dr: You probably will like this game if you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon and want to try something new with a different approach as there are enough gameplay changes that make this game less of a copycat and more of a DD inspired creation.

_childDocuments_.review: So far after a few hours I can tell this game should continue to appeal to my hardcore sadistic Darkest Dungeon rouge-like/lite mindset, but if that doesn't describe your style of play then it might be more frustration generating than fun.The key word here is "balance", and given the dev's quick response to player's concerns I assume there will eventually be a hardcore sweet spot along the road map.For now there may be rage quitting aplenty, especially with players being unfamiliar with some of the more extreme mob traits; for instance, in my last run there was a mob that didn't seem too threatening, that is until I saw that after a few turns it got a buff which couldn't be canceled that stated , and since I hadn't bothered to focus fire it from the first turn, I couldn't kill it in time, it was a total wipe, wiping away all of my characters' development to that point, and since I had decided to focus the majority of my resources on that now defunct squad, it was the end of my patience for this evening's Iratus session. Now given my affinity to the genre there wasn't any anger, but I just didn't feel like spending more time to get back to a similar point for the evening.So know yourself, and if you like the genre, this offering has enough activities outside of battle to develop your characters/avatar (including research trees), crafting, gear grinding, and travel map branch choices, to provide excellent replay value for the tactical squad focused micromanager gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a worthy waste of your time ;)If you like Darkest Dungeon, but always wanted to play the bad guys, then this might be of interest to you.The core mechanics are pretty similar:You create a team of up to 4 evil minions, unlocking more and more the more you play. Each minion has a prerequisite to unlock it throughout all playthroughs.And each minion has different stats and skills, some being tanks, some buffers or debuffers, some damage dealers, etc.Many minions you unlock later can fulfill similar roles, so you can perhaps swap them out, but still play the same kind of combo.There are 3 different kinds of attack: physical, magical and mental.The first 2 are self-explanatory and mitigated by armor or magic resistance values. The latter is where the game starts to become fun, since stress attacks target the heroes' sanity (just like in Darkest Dungeon, only you are the one dealing stress ... and the attacks are much more devastating). I found this to be the superior strategy early on, since enemies tend to have a much lower stress bar than health bar ... and your minions generally deal more stress damage as well. With a few tweaks, stress attacks can induce "panic" very easily, which gives the enemy a nasty debuff of some sort.The more I moved through the levels though I found that a strong physical team is less fragile and more consistent, albeit a lot less fun. Which is imho the first real problem I've encountered with the game: It's a bit unbalanced. At least on easy (I imagine it's just getting worse on higher difficulties).My final team consisted of a werewolf, a ghoul, a reaper and a bride. I could have used a vampire for the bride instead, would have been good as well. A "shuffle-heal" team. The Reaper healed all allies after every kill. The werewolf healed automatically before every turn. The ghoul can also almost constantly heal and the vampire has an ultimate skill that lets her heal with every attack. Combined with some actual armor upgrades and this team was simply unbeatable.Around floor 4 I got bored with the game due to that reason. I "could" have tried out other combos more (I did try all minions at least), but I felt, why bother?Unlike Darkest Dungeon Iratus is a strictly linear game. You will inevitably advance towards your goal, unless you reset the entire floor. This is one of the main drawbacks compared with DD. DD is an "endless" game. You can just play a quick dungeon with whatever units you have available ... but you also risk it all. You have random encounters, secret bosses appearing, pitch black runs for more loot, challenging bosses to tackle, just vastly different arsenals and interplays, different biomes, different enemy compositions, etc.In comparison Iratus is just rather "boring". It's alright for one playthrough, maybe two if you really like, but it doesn't offer that same level of just "playing one more dungeon". Darkest Dungeon has the hamlet as an additional progression system, Iratus has, well Iratus. You can upgrade the necromancer in various ways, but most upgrades are spells ... which you can only use 1 or 2 times during a battle usually, unless you have a minion that gives you back mana. The items Iratus can wield are also rather limited. And at least I had him fully upgraded until the end, but actually didn't want 90% of the upgrades.The graveyard upgrade is another comparison to the hamlet, but also just stat boosts, I've had it fully upgraded almost by about the middle of the game. Then I didn't know what to do with my over 1,000 souls ...If they'd ever make a sequel I'd wish they'd invested more into actually making the gameplay more fun in the long term. Going from battle to battle got boring rather quickly, especially since enemy compositions were often the same. Animations are "alright", but nothing to write home about. Models are really nice though as well as backgrounds. The weird round shadows are unnecessary though. I'd like a deeper progression system (unit progression is fine) and a better alchemy system. I didn't bother using potions.And the unit roster UI needs improving. You "can" have 1 unit of each type, technically, but 6 or 7 will always have to be either in a healing or XP building in the graveyard to make room for the others (you can only ever have 16 minions present).It's definitely worth playing for, even if it's just to listen to Iratus' great voice actor! I just wish the game had more ... "theme"? In Darkest Dungeon every enemy is a masterpiece (and actually dangerous), here, most enemies just seem so bland, especially in the last floor, which lacks complete cohesion (though there is an in-game explanation for this).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great mix of Darkest Dungeon and other similar indie rogue-like games. It's niche is you are the bad guy this time, no sanity required.The grind has been pretty much completely removed as you progress in one big dungeon with a boss at the end of each floor with multiple paths without the ability to change paths or go "back" or any way of farming outside taking paths with more enemies than others.It has a lot of characters, it's voiced by the guy from Blood. Pros:*Lots of Characters, good level of tactics and different approaches*Nicely streamlined between moving units from working in your buildings, raising more units and progressing*RPGesque Talent system and ability to use Magic and actively helping your undead party is sweet*Fun, expansive. Great visual design with an awesome evil vibe.Cons:*Bugs, like multi-thousand critical strikes, Armor, Block & Ward calculations going wonky at times. The ability to lose resources by backing out of transmuting them/putting another item ontop of them.*Balance is needing a bit of a fix, but for early access is pretty awesome. The sanity battles need a bit of work tho'*The voice acting work while good, isn't varied enough. There needs to be more voice acted lines with Iratus speaking, and I really feel the writing in a lot of spots/the takes don't represent how great of a voice the actor has, also makes it feel very early access. I hope the devs got the budget for more voice acting. More lines, more jokes, much more variance is needed.Conclusion is that there is the makings of one of the best, friendly Roguelikes to come out. It's a streamlined, annoyance-removed, grind-removed tactical roguelike with a really neat vibe and potentially with more updates, extremely expansive and varied.Current state is a 6.5/10. But everything for a 10/10 is in the works. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a lot more time in the Oven.There is a lot to say here, so i will try to organize this into sections:General balance:First of all, though, this game is NOT darkest dungeon and is not supposed to be similar to it or compared to.They share the same format (2D- 4 team vs 4 team) and that's about it, they have completely different mechanics in all aspects.Comparing Iratus to DD is like comparing apples to oranges (for the most part).Just a bit of background: I completed the game countless of times on "More pain!" which is the medium difficulty and one time on max difficulty ( although i had many attempts on max diffculty with other line ups).I'm going to list the features that bother me the most and prevent me from further playing this game.The overall balance in this game, and the balance patches the developers release feels like one huge roller-coaster.Minions are either nerfed or buffed to oblivion in every patch. In this game minions have 6 skills each and there are some, like Lich for example that are only used for just 1 skill, the rest are completely useless, this is a flawed design that requires overhaul.Other times there are RNG-based minions that, like Blood phantasm that can either be decent or completely worthless depends on how the dice roll, this diminish strategic thinking  and only promote frustration.You would expect that a minion will have a strong side and a weak side, but there are some got either everything or nothing.For example, Head hunter is durable physical damage dealer. However, he has extremely low base accuracy AND extremely large gap between minimum and maximum damage. this means that he is practically un-usable as a damage dealer and can only serve as a damage sponge.Speaking about RNG, the way the game makes you lose feels cheap, frustrating and leaves a bad taste in the mouth.This comes in two forms:1) RNG plays dominant role in the form of critical hits and misses2) Un-imaginative design - mostly regarding the bosses in the game.I will elaborate:Critical strikes in this game bypass any form of defense or strategy you can field, because they ignore all defenses.There are a good chunk of enemies that has very high base damage and very high crit chance (in the hardest difficulty it can go up to 60-75% chance to crit).Whats more, the game has little tools for you play with in order to stop those crits from destroying your party.Generally, the way to deal with this is through CC, namely either stuns or "turn skips", the former is very scarce (only banshee has a reliable CC) and the latter is non existent as minions skills.Even if you build around controlling your enemies with debuffs and whatever CC you can muster, you have "hit chance" to overcome.Generally that's rarely a thing that makes you lose, but in this game there is black magic that i can't explain.You have a minion with 95% hit chance misses 3 times in a row against an enemy that has 0% evasion.When that miss is a crucial stun, the result is a crit in your face.Those crits are generally out of scale, as an example, a swordsman in the FIRST level, on the first turn can double crit you for TWICE 30+ damage, if he misses he gets a damage and accuracy buff, and he is usually paired with an ally that buffs hes damage even further.You, as a logical decision, attempt to debuff him or stun him ouf this, but he also has 30% evasion to boot. you miss the stun/debuff, he plays and double crits one of your minions two times, each 42 damage , essentially a one shot.Considering how long battles take in the game, more so in hard difficulties, it can generally spiral out of control and you lose.How do you think it feels, when you thought the scenario through, you brought the right tools, had the right plan in mind and lost to random odds that overcame all sense of strategy.RNG is OK to include in a game, but it should NEVER be the dominant factor that decides if you lose or win (unless your just a bad player).Generally i'm a person with a lot of patience but even I eventually raise my hands up at some point, say "screw that BS" and go play something else.Finally, whats even worse is that said enemies, like the swordsman are abundant in the very first level of the game, there are more enemies that have double attack + high base damage an good crit chance or a combination of 2 out of the 3 (notice the pattern?): Miners, assassins, berserkers (2nd floor). But it gets worse, against certain combinations of enemies it feels like you play a lottery rather than playing a strategic "chess game".For example, remember the swordsman? well, how about 2 of them in the front and 2 support enemies in the back line.What does the support do? buff their damage of course, because that's the most creative thing you can come up with.By how much? 30%, and it STACKS. if the swordsman misses with at least one of hes DOUBLE attacks he gets another +30% buff AND accuracy buff (and remember that they also have high evasion).What does this mean? this means that if you somehow don't find a way to debuff them or stun them (assuming you brought the right tools to do that........) one of your minions have a good chance to get vaporized in a single strike, doesn't matter if you stacked armor or block on it.But there are two swordsmen, and they are ALSO protected by blocks and wards (forgot to tell you that as well), which you need to break in order to CC/damage them.There are also elite variant of said enemies, with more stats, more crit chance, more evasion...more of the good stuff.Again, the most horrible fact is that the players need to face such "challenges" at the very start of the game, where your minions are fairly low in level and you have limited tools/spells to play.That's how fun the strategic depth of this game is, and this is but one example, I could write an entire article about other scenarios like this.Bosses:This is where i will compare to DD because what it looks like is the devs took the necromancer boss from DD, copy pasted it 3 times and slapped it in all 3 levels.When done with next to no thought, adds in boss fights serve nothing but creating artificial difficulty.And generally you don't spam them, like in this game.Overall the boss fights are terrible and boring, revolving around going through minions in order to get through the boss, but some of them are worse  than the others:-First bossRNG shows its ugly face once again in this fight, since he can summon dangerous enemies, sometimes 3 at once (WTF? why can't he summon one a time?), after you bothered clearing them, and if you got unlucky, you can get some things like 2x miners (double attack + high base damage, sounds familiar?), the boss, of-course also have an AOE nuke on your entire party to make things even more interesting and a single target weak attack that he uses once in a blue moon.-2nd boss.This fight is actually fairly fair, you just need to bring the right tools for the job (buff removals) (oh, there are also adds).-3rd bossNothing special, again adds, this time they explode in your face and the boss does nothing interesting except casting generic damage spells.The bosses are just bland, they have no interesting mechanics or niches and honestly, sorry for the insult but they feel like they were design by in-experienced minds.In DD, all bosses are completely unique and sport different mechanics and skills.Finally, I'm going to finish with Position control and shuffling:This is another comparison I will make to DD because the same should share the same concept.In Iratus, nearly every enemy has good means to kill you no matter what position he is at, attempting to employ strategy through position shuffling, against the vast majority of enemies is pointless. (I ran out of room to continue this review).Anyway those are the glaring issues for me, i'm going to shelf this game for now until it will get in a proper shape.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a Kickstarter backer for this project so when it was first announced I thought, 'Hey cool, a Darkest Dungeon style game and you play the bad guy.  I'll take a shot.'  So the game comes out of early access and I was expecting a Darkest Dungeon Clone but a fun experience.  As I started the game it actually seemed the game had some really unique ideas as well, with monster creation and how you could get better stats with better parts and so on.  So my expectation of a better game increased.  But as I began to play I noticed  there seemed to be some big issues with how some of the enemies were balanced to the point of it seeming the devs made the enemies to not be challenging but to outright kill your party no matter how hard you try to strategically play your moves.      I will give one example,  In the third level, there is the Crossbow enemy, a ranged combatant.   Their primary position is the back two slots of their party for their primary attack.  So as a player, I would want to try to get him to the front row.  As you do this he has a secondary attack, some kind of flash bomb, that he can throw to reposition him to the back.  This is fine, except as a secondary attack it can also hit your characters pretty hard and not only can it do good damages it hits EVERYONE in your party and can also critical.  And this is his secondary attack.  As a cross reference, I will use Darkest Dungeon when you are fighting the brigand with a rifle.  You can get him to the front ranks and while he can attack in the front,  his attack is much weaker, not as accurate and if I remember correctly doesn't hit everyone or if it can it is very very weak..the whole move is to get him to the back of the line again.      This is not the only enemy like this where the secondary attacks can be almost just as devastating as the enemies primary attacks.  There is the elf swordsman if you move him out of the front ranks he has a move that hits,,,again all your team with a pretty hard attack to get him back to the front ranks.     Also there are issues with how percentages work as well and abilities of the enemies, there is a normal swordsman who has an evade of 30 but you will miss him constantly,  instead of a 1 in 3 chance to miss ,you will miss him 2 out of 3 times on a consistent basis.  I can even predict when the game is going to make me miss so it will keep an enemy alive so it can get another attack.     Enemies can also go into stances and the game allows them to remain in those stances throughout the battle and still attack without having the enemy use an action to reset the stance.  Your characters on the other hand have to reset their stance every turn and it uses an action.    To me, the game is unbalanced with how it implements the abilities of the enemies.  Especially with the enemies secondary abilities.  I have played Darkest Dungeon a TON and have even beat that game.  And while there are times Darkest Dungeon can pull a fast one on you it is overall a fun fair game.  Iratus however I feel is not and the Devs have added in all these special abilities of enemies they want to attack you with and almost break the game to showcase those abilities.  In other words..it likes to push in cheap hits.     I have went back several times to play as well just in case I felt I was missing something or doing something wrong and I wanted to be fair in what I wrote. But I feel overall that my experience with the game is pretty much on target.     I'm not sure if the devs plan on doing any updates or balancing of the game but I hope so as I would like to play the game more and it be more enjoyable but as of right now it is a pass.EDITED FOR GRAMMAR

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to take on the role of the Necropolis faction from Heroes of Might and Magic games but with the combat system of Darkest Dungeon? Then look no further. We play on the side of evil here, as the necromancer Iratus, and on our path to conquer the world, we have a few scores to settle with the mortal heroes. This is a simple yet fun premise that helps to service the tactical gameplay.The combat is very similar to games like Darkest Dungeon, with our team having up to 4 minions and the enemy team also having up to 4 fighters. The positioning of the characters matters, as some abilities can only be done from certain positions and target specific positions on the enemy side.The number of possible minions we can have is really good and there's a great variety in them. They all fit the theme of undead monsters, such as skeletons, vampires, wraiths, banshees, mummies, and so on. They all have their own unique abilities and can be levelled up throughout the course of the campaign. At first we have only 6 minion types unlocked, but over the course of the game we unlock the others, and these become available forever, for any new games you'd start after this one. This is a nice way to introduce each minion so not to overwhelm the player with too much at once while also keeping our curiosity piqued each time we unlock a new minion.There is a wealth of different combat mechanics here. Aside from simply dealing damage to the enemy HP, we can also drive them insane with stress attacks, as well as lay traps at specific positions that affect any enemy that moves into the positions where they're located. There's also a blocks and wards system. These allow the character to fully resist an attack regardless of how strong it is (blocks for physical attacks, wards for magic and stress). These can be used to buff our own minions, however, the enemies will also make use of them, and the game provides many ways to get rid of these.We craft our minions out of body parts that drop from slain enemies. Each minion requires a specific combo of body parts. There is also a brain body part that can drop, which can raise any minion to a specific level, and hence this allows us to bypass grinding.The dungeons we access on a map screen and can decide which paths to take. There's no backtracking, so we can't go back to grind for items or experience. But since we can see all paths ahead, we can plan our route and decide what points of interest we'd like to interact with. In this sense, the dungeon crawling aspect differs a lot from Darkest Dungeon, because we don't do individual dungeon runs, but rather just go through one giant dungeon and recoup in our lair in between battles with enemy troops.We also have the 'Graveyard' area where we can construct buildings. These have different functions, such as healing minions in between battles or improving the amount of experience that Iratus gains, and so on. In addition to this, we can equip Iratus with various artifacts, and also level him up too and get him to learn new skills, some are passives, and others are spells to be used in battle to aid our minions. The game has 4 difficulty modes, so it can appeal to a wide range of players who enjoy tactics-based games. The game has a nice level of presentation. The environments are crafted beautifully. The minions all look impressive and have fun battle animations. Voice acting for Iratus is also nice and adds some flavour during battles. The music is a little generic and doesn't stand out too much, but it does its job well and fits the theme of the game.I've found myself really addicted to the game and have already played through it twice (on the first two difficulty modes). It has a tonne of strategic depth and a lot of potential to experiment with various team combinations of minions. The amount of enemies is quite large too, so you'd always be facing fresh challenge with interesting battle mechanics that will keep you on your toes. The game's style and combat mechanics resemble Darkest Dungeon a lot, so it often gets compared to it. For the most part, both games have some similarities and some differences, but both offer a deep tactical gameplay to last you many hours. And although there are some people who liked one but not the other, I'd say if you've enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, it's highly likely that you'd enjoy Iratus too.For a more in-depth review and a gameplay video, check here:

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game is great, but I had no idea it even existed. I loved Darkest Dungeon so when I had a recommendation for this in Steam, I had to try it. Honestly, it's just as good gameplay-wise, lot of meta to explore and strategy to delve into. The game is hard but feels more "fair" and has more quality-of-life aspects than Darkest Dungeon - it's also really cool to play as the villain, driving the "heroes" you encounter insane and terrorizing the humans/dwarves in the quest events. It's also funny in a dark humor sort of way with Iratus himself narrating the situation (his 1000yr return after being defeated and disdain for mortals), and the minion/enemy descriptions fleshing out the world-lore with irony. My only gripe is that the soundtrack is too quiet/soft for a game that comes off as metal af. Other than that, it's amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus thoughts. Note that I lean more towards mixed than negative on this title. It's just alright. But after 8 hours, the more the game kinda reveals that it's a long, long burn. Which, I mean if you want a less frustrating, less challenging Darkest Dungeon, go for it. But what you're left with is a very repetitive TBS game that doesn't honest elicit any sort of reaction out of me. So, there are 5 levels to the main campaign and cross a single level at best takes a couple of hours. And until then it's just a slow campaign. I like the general theme of being this super powerful necromancer and you get a decent display of that here, but the spells are fairly boring (or bad). The minions, while varied, have zero personality in combat. So, I feel little attachment or interest in them. They mostly just become disposable corpses. While the game also tries to make you invest into them. Which is just....a really weird design choice. Honestly I think the pacing is just extremely too slow. There should have been quests or missions or just something to break it up but it just goes combat -> get X thing -> combat -> get X thing -> elite combat -> get X thing and repeat till you get to the boss. I don't mind that it has a slower pace but it needs something to break up the pace and add excitement. I may have played on too easy a mode but I'm also not excited about doing a harder version of it. Cause failing that means resetting a level alllllllllllllllllllllll the way back to the beginning and I'd rather not. Enjoyed the theme, enjoyed the narrator and the aesthetic works. But I have no compulsion to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Darkest Dungeon, you'll probably like this game. It's slightly easier than Darkest Dungeon, but the point of Darkest Dungeon was you and your band of heroes facing impossible, lovecraftian foes that you could just barely defeat.This game is a lot more forgiving, and that only makes sense, since in this game you're playing the bad guy, that the heros have to overcome. That being said, this game is not easy, as the achievement data shows, lol.At the time of this review, only 10% of players have beaten the bosses of the second floor/area in the game.The art is great, simple but not overly so, with plenty of detail in the units and enemies you face, along with the backgrounds for the areas you travel through.If you want a version of Darkest Dungeon where you were the big bad, reveling in your sheer evilness while the MC quips out one-liners and cheeky commentary the whole time, this game is for you.
