_childDocuments_.review: I daresay that I felt this is at least as good as if not a better game than Darkest Dungeon. I got it on sale, super cheap less than 5 bucks I think. It was amazing for the value. A number of negative reviews mention that buffs aren't clearly explained. It's true that the tutorial leaves out the glaring fact of the "feature" buffs when you start the game. Once you take that in it became fairly easy to figure out how to min/max accordingly. The characters scale nicely as you play, and pair well with one another. The game also seems much more fair, in that very few battles (if any) are unbeatable with the cast of characters you may bring. I beat it each progressive difficulty setting, I didn't die or fail on any of them, but the last one was definitely challenging. I used a playthrough that was stress based and physical damage based, each one had their pluses and minuses. Overall a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid little dungeon crawler rouge-like that borrows as much from the CRPGs of the 1980s as it does from more modern games like Darkest Dungeon. It's basically the premise (and some of the game play) of Wizardry 4: The Return of Werdna but with a much more forgiving game to play. That's not to say Iratus is a cakewalk, it's a decent challenge. Wizardry 4 was just very hard. It's got a pretty addictive game play loop. The dungeon is big and there's a variety of ways you can use your very VERY expendable minions to get ahead. The difficulty scales well as far as I've seen. Worth a shot if you are looking for a good time sink.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I was hesitant to give this studio my money because of the way they handled a different release of theirs. A friend's review of this game convinced me to give it a shot, but I was prepared to ask for a refund real quick. That said, the game hooked me quickly. I have made it through the campaign on lowest difficulty and am happy with the purchase. Please bear that perspective in mind when reading my review, because it may be totally invalid as viewed at higher difficulty settings. Pacing of city development seems a little off- you want souls at the beginning, then get stuck and don't care about it much anymore midway through. The Talent system could use tweaks- passive minion buffs are peppered throughout, and ended up largely being what I chased in each tree. The spell system seems oddly balanced too- I didn't end up wanting to use many of the spells and don't know that I would have used some of them anyway (eg minion buffs instead of just dealing direct damage that would far outpace the dps buff). There was a lot to like, and as I get better at the game and progress further, I am confident that I will squeak out better strategies and point allocations than were required for an easy run.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game art and mechanics! Mix of Darkest Dungeon, Monster Train, Slay Spire, etc. Would love to see the modder community grow for this game! Only issue I had with this game is around dungeon 2 I just kept the same characters till end game doing the same moves over and over and over again, which helped me win, but it just felt like the same tactics.Also what would be great to set this game aside from others is maybe introduce a 5 character floor, all these rouge/dungeon strategies have 4 character floors. Would also love to see a mutation/variant occur during the battle. Not a lot of games have it where a character transforms mid battle. Since this is a new game and has so much potential to set itself apart from other I think maybe like an event can occur on the battle field whether that be weather/dark/light/meteor interactive with the stage/arena, just something that sets it apart from what other games are doing. Would be cool to get pushed into another arena during a battle or have like titans/stage monsters that are part of the level that effect the battle. Just SOMETHING DIFFERENT that doesn't play it safe.

It's directly carried by how good Darkest Dungeon was and people looking for games like it, but also directly carried by a lack of supervillain games out there to play. 3/10.If someone said they were looking for a supervillain perspective game that's like Darkest Dungeon and could I recommend one, I'd say "No, I imagine someone's probably working on one though. _childDocuments_.review: I -- DO NOT -- recommend this game because- It crashes pretty often --although these did not corrupt or delete my saves--- No mods so the problems the game has can't be fixed other than by devs- Seems to be abandoned by devs, last thing they did was a blog 6 months ago- Don't see the replayability and the first run is not good enough to recommend - Bought it at 80% off (5 bucks) and highly recommend u don't buy it any higherStill giving thumbs up because- more of these types of games is a good thing and I want to inspire devs who are deciding what to make next- kept me entertained for 16 hours and for 5 bucks that's not bad- less BS than Darkest Dungeon and for a clone that's an acheivement - could have been a lot worse. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this just isn't much fun. It's an interesting design-flip on Darkest Dungeon - be the bad guy, drive the good guys insane instead. But you soon come upon enemies that can one-hit-kill your minions unless you do very specific things - it feels less like "play" and more like "instant punishment." It's also a bit grindy/churney. I kept pushing until frustration overcame me - a slow and insidious killer of my motivation.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I've put 45+ hours into the game and it's not even finished yet (3 of 5 floors are available right now until 4/23 when all floors will be available with the official launch).I've unlocked all 19 minions and so far I've only found 2 teams that can kill fast and survive multiple battles. When the full game is released, I want to explore more teams because it's either the case that some minions just aren't really useful or I'm not smart enough to figure out how to use them.What I hated about Darkest Dungeon was that I was forced to switch out units when they got infected with some random status or ran away, etc. This doesn't happen in Iratus so you can focus more on battle tactics than on taking care of your units.I like the first two modes of difficulty for Iratus but the first team I came up with so good that they never needed to be switched out. They just killed every enemy and every boss in like 3-4 turns. So I went to the 3rd level of difficulty which did force me to change teams, but the boss for the 2nd level was overpowered. He kept freezing my chars which left them unable to attack, so I either need to rethink my team or his ability to paralyze was just broken.If it helps, here are games I've enjoyed: Darkest Dungeon, Final Fantasy Tactics, Fire Emblem, Persona, & Banner Saga
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: The hardest difficulty of the game is simply not balanced. Generally the hardest difficulty of any game is the "endgame" it's where you go after you've mastered the game, built the "ultimate" squad, and are ready for a challenge. Sadly, the hardest difficulty in this game can't be beaten by skill, it's entirely RNG based and it's very likely you will lose, because some of the enemies attacks are higher than you can even get most of your minions HP, IE 1-shot. On the easiest of difficulties you can basically not know what you are doing at all and just breeze through. On the middle-tier difficulties you might have to have some knowledge and have a decent squad but it's still pretty easy. So, that's the kind of game this is. Once you figure everything out the game is ridiculously easy or it just 1-shots you. However, I suppose figuring that out is fun for a masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all its a good game, and for the asking price worth it.I wouldnt recommend it, if it was any more expensive.Its rather short and the fact that I have to BEAT the game once to get a lot of the characters (and others you only get towards the end) leaves a very bad taste in my mouth, especially paired with the fact that this game is boring to replay.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game following the playstyle of darkest dungeon. I really like the minion designs, the skills and magical abilities are well developed and there are quite a few combos appearing to work in several occasions. The game is still in development so there are many additional features to appear but I believe the devs are heading the right way. I also like the addition of difficulty levels from noob to expert which is a very good element of the game. Finally I would like to see minions with healing abilities as the ones I have unlocked so far have offensive, defensive and supporting abilities (with the exception of vampires). I do not know if anyone of the locked minions can heal but if not, I would like to see this addition. Finally, as rng is rather important in this game especially in higher difficulties, I would like to see the choice to replay dungeons or at least complete the paths neglected in the first run. If you cannot rerun completed dungeons then I think that sometime in the final levels (or sooner) there may be a dead-end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a "Darkest Dungeon" clone which in my opinion does not add anything valuable.Pros:- You are the evil guy which is fun- You can craft and upgrade a lot of stuffCons:- Story and atmosphere is less interesting than in Darkest Dungeons- All that crafting and upgrading seems to be pretty useless, since combats are repetitive- I am basically still on my very first tactic and just click through all the fights in same manner- I got this game on sale for 15 €. _childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I really hate the fact that I need to choose the recommend or not recommend, instead of just providing an opinion on why I didn't like it. Because this is a game that clearly is recommended if you did like Darkest Dungeon game, and almost as clearly not recommended if you didn't.To be honest, I was hugely disappointed to find this is in core form a sort of reskin of darkest dungeon game, but let's say with the viewpoint from the other side (you are the evil one, your minions attacks can generate stress and health damage)., but decided to give this one a go anyway.I personally got bored of grinding through the DD after 30 hours or so, and never bothered to come back to that, but in this case I got tired of the game much quicker. Yes there are significant changes:The town got replaced with graveyard and I think the overall handling of building and upgrades are a bit of an improvement, the heroes do not come randomly to be recruited, but rather you make your minions from the spare parts. But still it seems to be geared towards incremental "grind grind grind" solution to unlock new upgrades. In the end you will spend a wast majority doing the combat encounters, and these do play exactly like in DD. I mean it uses the same cheap old tricks as DD to impose how "dark" and "difficult" it is, when in fact once you deal with the fact that your minions die on regular basics and cope with that, it becomes a boring issue of micro-managing your resources. While you seem to have some control on "exploring" the dungeon, you basically follow some generated paths of more or less random encounters, and the final result is the same as there would be no path and no choices.The final verdict - I guess the choice is simple - If you like the Darkest Dungeon - you will like this one as well. If you don't care - then you most likely will not care.

name: REVEIL
detailed_description: More Horror from Pixelsplit Funhouse Edition In addition to REVEIL, the Funhouse Edition contains the following DLCs: REVEIL Original Soundtrack: 14 original compositions, beautiful and haunting. Digital Artbook: A look behind the scenes of the game, featuring concept art and inspirations. Black and White Camera Filter: Use this in game for vintage horror atmosphere. Audio Plays: A selection of audio plays recorded with the game's voice actors, more bits and pieces from the world of REVEIL. Developer Commentary: Commentary by the developers to be found in-game, for even more background insights. About the Game A unique, visually appealing, mentally challenging story. Versatile puzzles, unanswered questions, confusing clues and a disturbing psyche demand a lot from both the player and the protagonist, Walter Thompson. Can you manage to make sense of it all? Should you persevere, there is a chance to find answers to your questions. You wake up. You're disoriented. Your head hurts. Things seem surreal, yet familiar. Your wife Martha and your daughter Dorie are not there. Why? Looking for answers, you explore your environment and fragments of memories. On your journey you are repeatedly confronted with riddling tasks, driven by the desire to find out what's going on. What happened last night? Why can't you think of any other thing aside from your days as a stage builder at the circus? As things get crazier and more bizarre, the lines between reality, memory, and imagination become more and more blurred and you realize: there is no going back. You have to do whatever it takes to bring this story to an end, no matter at what cost... 'The feeling of safety is an elusive one. It's not over yet.' In REVEIL, the player is immersed into a world, designed with attention to detail, where the boundaries between reality and illusion become blurred. The setting is an authentically orchestrated environment inspired by the circus of the 60s, which soon takes on surreal features. Get a glimpse into the psyche and the past of Walter Thompson: The impressions become darker, more mysterious, more enigmatic the further you advance. Once caught in the maelstrom of deceptive impressions, memory fragments and mysterious visions, your only option is to dive deeper - in the hope of finding answers to your perplexing situation and condition, even if this hope is slowly fading. The only thing that keeps you from giving up is the will to find Martha and Dorie. Do not shut your eyes to the hints left by the two, but keep them wide open and ... try to not lose your mind. A deeply psychological experience that will keep you questioning everything. Five playable acts in different, carefully designed environments. First-person narrative experience including: Various puzzles and riddles Beautiful and immersive visual experience #madewithunity Multi-layered narrative with psychedelic, biographical and disturbing elements Atmospheric paintings, posters, writings referring to the circus era of the 60s.

short_description: REVEIL is a narrative first-person psycho-thriller game that focuses on story, puzzles and exploration. Find out what’s going on inside Walter Thompson and what his dark past at the Nelson Bros Circus has to do with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was great in the first couple of hours, then it turned into avoid the monster/entity and retrieve object horror game play which I shouldn't have to be doing in a walking simulator. I was looking more for a story driven and interaction/solving puzzles but not so much getting caught by monsters and having to start things over without any explanation why this is happening. Not the kind of game I thought it would be. I thought this would be more Layers of Fear type of horror, but I guess I was wrong. I think they threw this in just so people would not complain that there's no game play.
_childDocuments_.name: REVEIL

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Falls short of being great (for me) for these reasons:- Poor final puzzles. After some of the earlier ones, doing the modules at the finale felt like a chore. They weren't difficult or interesting, and didn't match the quality of puzzles found throughout the rest of the game. - Mandatory stealth sections. They don't add much, don't fit with the flow of the game, and the crouching speed is honestly much too slow. - Some unclear plot points. - Ends with no real resolution. The mysteries are wrapped up nicely enough, but it seriously just sort of ends without any flair. You solve a few lacklustre puzzles, open a door and the credits roll. It felt quite rushed and unimaginative.All in all, a strong game with some rough edges. It's not scary, but the set pieces, imagery and storytelling were all very good, as were the vast majority of puzzles. I would love more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: REVEIL

_childDocuments_.review: Visually gorgeous, excellent sound design and a story (with multiple endings) that will keep you on the edge guessing until the very end.I was fortunate enough to be given a pre-release key to review this game so thank you very much to the developers for this. The game is a very good entry into this genre. The story escalates with each chapter building towards the final chapter climax. In my opinion, often these kind of narrative games don't know how to make the ending tie the story together leaving me feel confused and underwhelmed. However, in the case of Reveil I think the developers did an excellent job.The puzzles were quite lightweight, nothing too challenging but enough to keep me engaged. The horror is more focused on atmosphere and pacing, not cheap jump-scares! This is a major positive for the game personally but if you are looking for a jump-scare per minute then this isn't the game you're looking for.  Overall, I would recommend this. Give it a go if you like narrative driven horror games with puzzle elements. I bet you won't be able to guess what is really happening before you reach the end...
_childDocuments_.name: REVEIL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very lucky to have played REVEIL already and I can absolutely recommend this game.I don't want to spoil the story but I can say the following:The story is gripping from the start and its narrative simply forces you to keep playing! :D I couldn't bear not knowing what is going on. The feeling of "Just one more chapter" is omnispresent!The narrative is cleverly set up and all its twists and turns fit in well into Walter's story. There is SO MUCH to unearth. The logo of the game includes the Penrose triangle and we can find it in many places of this world. The premise of the Penrose triangle is: it is an impossible figure that cannot exist in a three-dimensional world... thus it is but an illusion. Whilst exploring the story, one realizes quickly that things are not what they appear to be - they are illusionary. Walter is an unreliable narrator from the get-go and WE have to find out what really happened in the Nelson Bros Circus. The game is very much story-driven yet contains a handful of well-placed puzzles. The difficulty is balanced in so far as riddles can be challenging, yet they do not frustrate. Visually the game is pleasing. I am a huge fan of the lighting and the uncanny feeling that the player is surrounded by. This uncanny feeling is also supported by a great soundtrack. "The circus" is a theme that was used in horror games, films and literature before, and in REVEIL this set-up also does not disappoint. If I had to describe the setting in two words, I would say "playfully gruesome". I mean this in the most positive sense, I felt truly immersed in this world.Is the game scary? Hell yea. I've had many eerie, jumpscare moments that are again well-placed. You can tell that the devs have a very good understanding of placing them at the right time and have been inspired by games such as Layers of Fear. I was scared, yet I didn't feel the frustration of getting jumped at all the time. The balance was again just right!A lot of times the fear was entirely in my own mind - and that felt eeriely good. The game manages to confuse the players and thus make them feel just as overwhelmed as Walter is feeling.If you like psychological horror games, REVEIL is a great one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting classic puzzle game with a fresh modern coat that could have been a lot more immersive had the intentional flaws been fixed. * The puzzles within the game are very nostalgic as they are akin to the puzzles that games have had for the last 20 years. Very classic escape room style puzzles. * Immersion is broken because the game keeps taking control of your camera and forces the narrators speech into to your ears every few minutes. * Game is a little short and does in fact feel very indie and for that I would say its consumer price should be $9.99 rather than what it is currently for sale for. Similar to: Layers of Fear mixed in with a vintage 2005 puzzle solver game. Verdict: Give it a go but maybe when the price has dropped a little.

_childDocuments_.review: Reveil is a first-person psychological horror game that mostly takes place inside the mind of protagonist Walter. He suddenly awakes after having a nightmare only to find that both his wife Martha and his daughter have disappeared. Unable to remember what happened, he needs to discover the mystery behind his family’s disappearance. Soon enough, Walter starts questioning his reality and the environments take the shape of his imagination, bringing him into a dark circus filled with unsettling attractions and hostile monstrosities. As you can imagine, this is the classic formula for horror narrative-driven waking sims. For the record, I enjoyed  - although I don’t include it amongst the best horror gaming experiences I’ve had - but I have grown tired of horror games that use the same narrative clichés (amnesia, surrealism, hallucinations, trivial psychology). It was cool when  was the only one doing it, but now it’s getting way too abused in my opinion. That said, if you loved LoF you will likely enjoy this one too, but probably less so.The game is divided into five acts and really doesn’t take long to complete. It took me about 5 hours, including reading notes and looking in every corner for collectibles (there are quite a lot).  But someone who just wants to follow the story might complete it in four hours or less. I can’t talk about the story too much because this is the entire game, but what I can say for sure is that the protagonist talks too much and doesn’t allow you to interpret the story in your own way or to just feel the environment. The voice acting isn’t good either; it felt like the actor knew the lines but not the context of where the action happens (either that or he didn’t care too much). The house sections were great and immediately reminded me of  and . The other (mostly surreal) environments were more linear and less interesting. There are twists here and there throughout the story, but none that really shocked me. The multiple endings depend only on a choice that you can make at the end, so there isn’t any replayability. The one I got was short and felt like a rushed epilogue, and the others that I saw online were no more satisfying than mine. I don’t understand the idea of making multiple short endings rather than one solid ending (especially considering that the game is extremely linear). Why give a choice at the end when there were none throughout the entire game?Being a story-driven game, all you have to do is explore each new location you are thrown into and solve puzzles while trying not to be seen by hostile monstrosities. Some puzzles are a bit more creative, but most of them require that you find a key item and bring it to another place in order to progress (that’s not really difficult even when playing hide-and-seek with the monster). In-between the story you do get some cheap jumpscares and parts where you are being chased by a monster. Again, typical scenarios for a horror game that no longer provide any tension or surprise to someone who eats horror games for breakfast.Now the graphics are really beautiful at max settings. Each location is created in great detail and provides some very good atmospheric moments, also thanks to the great lighting in both external and internal locations. The game performance is also good, only few frame drops here and there, but this is not the kind of game where you need 60 fps or more all the time. I think that Reveil is a game that maybe takes too much from other games from the same genre (particularly ) while not adding anything new or different to the gameplay and narrative structure. Not only is the game short (especially considering the price) and without any replay value, but it lacks tension and except for a few atmospheric moments, doesn’t engage you in the protagonist’s story. It might be worth trying if only for the beautiful graphics and locations (especially if you like the circus), but it certainly won’t be a memorable horror experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was a fantastic psychological horror walking simulator.+ The graphics, art style and atmosphere are amazing. + The Funhouse in the circus section was well designed and super fun.+ The puzzles are original and well balanced in difficulty+ A few parts of the game were genuinely creepy and got under my skin- I could not turn the subtitles off or the big white crosshair dot in the middle of the screen, very annoying and ruins a bit of the atmosphere when playing.The story was interesting to me and I enjoyed it.  However there is a big twist at the end, and I think some people will not actually like the twist.  I got all 5 endings in 4.5 hours, the first playthrough took me 3.5 hours for reference.9.5/10 from me!Very polished and well made.

A very good story and well worth a second playthrough to see everything from a different perspective.  No custom saves but no worries, All the important saves are in the proper places.  You even get the advantages of a new game+ right from the get go, making achievement hunting the pleasure it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautifully crafted game. There are different scenes in this game that never feel overused as it mixes them up a lot. I particularly enjoyed the circus setting. There's a chapter that has, what other have said, a Layers of Fear-esque vibe but personally I think it does it much better and doesn't over play those mechanics to the point of being bored unlike LOF. It's cleverly written and the abundance of assets in this game is a testament to how much detail and love was put into this project. There's a big twist towards the end and I only wished the last chapter lasted longer as I felt the game was getting better and better. The game messes with your head a bit and maybe in that sense it's unlike traditional horror games, apart from the 'avoid the monster' sections. The enemies overall were easy enough to evade and the puzzles weren't too taxing. There was quite a bit of note reading in the last scene as the story completely unfolds. I missed most of the collectables even though I took my time. Although I did start the game past the demo section, so I would of missed a lot in chapter 1. 9/10

I'm so glad I didn't give up. I loved watching the story unfold. This game is super intense, scary, and made me scream a couple times. You couldn't ask for a better game. Everything was perfect! No crashes or bugs it ran beautifully! I can't wait to play more and get all the achievements. Thank you Dev!!

All will make sense when you reach a certain point in this game and believe me its not a simple game. Sip and enjoy it slowly, as I kinda rushed it near the end because of the text below.I kinda pulled an all nighter to finish this one, again its a habit of mine, but its worth it, I'd recommend finishing the game in one sitting, as at times it may seem like you know where this game is going, but at one point it does a cool 180 and at those moments its an instant recommended from me.Story: 8/10Graphics: 7.5/10Soundtrack: 10/10Gameplay: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is worth the money, and worth the experience if you are a horror games fan. And so, If you are a casual player looking for or expecting an epic psychological horror atmosphere, very well done dark visuals, an interesting unexpected twist in the story with multiple endings kind of vibe, that you can finish in 3-4 Hrs, then this is a PERFECT choice for you. and It could be rated 8/10 on that Scale. _childDocuments_.review: I will keep it spoiler free up here, a bit later there will be some spoilers when it comes to the story, but I will leave a new warning before that.-Headphones strongly recommended when playing-First up: How scary is it?If you are sensitive to circus stuff, than it's either gonna be not for you, or incredibly scary.If not, then I would say somewhere between beginner and early intermediate.It has some jump scares, but they are pretty mild in my opinion and tasteful, so your ears are not gonna bleed!The atmosphere and sound design do most of the heavy lifting.+ Pros• Visual art style is fantastic. Especially when the film grain is turned off the atmosphere gets really immersive.• Textures look believable, are not too repetitive and high quality.• The lighting is super smooth and looks amazing. Fantastic work!• Level design is heavily inspired by a few older titles (I think) at times, but I think this is a pro. Well executed and it looks great!• Sound design is fantastic. Music, sound effects (the sound effects are incredibly good btw) and spoken lines are super well mixed, super high quality and elevates the atmosphere up by a TON. I can't get over the sound, it's really really good!• Voice actors do (mostly) a good job. The grunting can sound pretty funny, but otherwise the lines are well spoken.• Story keeps you engaged to keep playing.• Runs very smooth on my weird system. 4080 but the bottleneck (ryzen 7 3700x) doesn't hurt the performance here. Runs well!• FOV SLIDER. As a person who gets motion sick or headaches when the FOV is too low, I greatly appreciate this!- cons• Puzzle difficulty varies a lot between very easy and intermediate. No puzzle is really hard here and there's no option for a separate high puzzle difficulty or similar.• The camera often locks to "interesting things". Only a minor thing, but it feels like taking away control. I hear that stuff is happening, If I would be able to rotate the camera myself it would be way more immersive.• The protagonist talks too much. If you're fast it even overlaps or the voice lines come way too late.• Not really a spoiler, but man the protagonist is not the brightest, let's put it that way.• Some models can have a bit lower quality then the rest, makes it look a bit off. I especially mean the merry-go-round horses, they do look a bit.... edgy? It doesn't have a lot of polygons.• (already got addressed) The tooltips (press c to crouch and stuff) come all the time at certain scenes and there's no way to turn them off....yet. Devs already said on discord that it gets added to the list. Appreciate it!I will type some stuff about the story all the way below, so for anyone who does not wanna get spoiled I do put my final words here already:I highly recommend playing this game if you're looking for a good entry into the horror genre, or if you wanna solve some puzzles in a dark atmosphere and have a story with it.The price quite low. You can about 4–6 hours of playtime, depending on how fast you are.I strongly recommend it. It is really fun to play through, easy to get into and easy to get lost in.Fantastic work Pixelsplit, not only are you fantastic people to chat with, but also devs that seem to keep a good balance between feedback + your own vision.I'm proud to have the fun house edition in my library, as well as the supporter edition of Indoorlands from you. You deserve the support and I hope this game is getting known more.---THIS IS MILD SPOILER TERRITORY---The story:It got advertised to me as a "mindfu**" which is probably accurate for most people. If you're an "old timer" who has a lot of experience, you can piece some things together. The ending is not what I expected, but honestly probably due to the wrong reasons. I was thinking way outside the box here and got misled, the story is way more logical than I hoped. The extra notes in game are not that necessary to get the full pictureThis is only me speaking though. It does present itself as a perfect story for horror beginners though. I liked the story, but it's not reinventing the wheel or adds anything truly unique into it. Still, I really enjoyed it. It was money well spent, and I recommend to pretty much every one of you to pick it up. Great product for a good price!

_childDocuments_.review: As far as short, sweet indie-horror titles go, this is honestly one of the best I've played in years. There's so much to love about what Pixelsplit have created here, it's almost impossible to know where to start.The attention to detail is the first thing which struck me. Everything has been so lovingly crafted, from the puzzles right down to feel and flow of the environments. The use of lighting and color is particularly stunning, and if you have a HDR display, you're in for an absolute treat. The sound design deserves equal praise - from the ambient elements to the soundtrack itself, the immersion was pretty much flawless. And there's some genuine creativity in the mix once you start to understand the broader context of the game world.I did initially have some misgivings about the voice acting. Not because of it's quality, but rather the tonality in the context of the protagonist's experiences. Without spoiling anything, this too has it's place - and the latter parts of the game took some turns I genuinely wasn't expecting.On the performance side of things, I ran this at 4K / max settings on a 3080 Ti and only experienced the occasional hitch when entering a new area. Reveil does have some very brief loading screens between chapters, so while the odd stutter was disappointing, they were so infrequent that it's almost not worth mentioning.In short, the love for what this small team has crafted here just oozes out of every corner of the game. If you're looking for a palette cleanser or just feel like a bite-sized trip down a psychedelic horror rabbit hole, I honestly can't recommend this enough. I really hope this finds the audience it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got incredible storytelling; moderate scares with lots of tension before and after; and lots of foreshadowing.However, it feels too cliche towards the end and it left me really disappointed despite everything else. _childDocuments_.review: The beautifully realistic graphics pulled me into Reveil, but I stayed and even endured some motion sickness for the emotional quest of the main character to find his missing loved ones, the nightmarish locales and the nifty puzzles, capped off by an exhilarating final chapter that truly succeeds in turning everything upside down. I know jump scares are often a main attraction in horror games, but I’m personally not a fan of them so I’m glad they didn’t go overboard with them here. Although there were just enough to make me instinctively curse out loud on occasion, something I’m usually not known to do! I certainly don’t regret getting a ticket to this crazy circus adventure. It may not be the greatest show on earth with only a four-hour funhouse ride, but it makes for a captivating exploration through its protagonist’s twisted dreams and tortured memories.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like it, the story/experience was shallow as hell. As a walking sim it doesn't offer any special puzzles or lore, the storytelling is clumsy and slow and clichéd, and the scary scenes are just QTE or running away from monsters. The story isn't developed enough to provide the kind of existential dread you would get after playing SOMA, or the revealing of an underlying horror in The Signifier. What's worse, all of the plot's tropes sound forced and unnatural. I'd tell the team to focus more on the plot and gameplay instead of focusing only on how it looks, cause looks dont sell a game. Soma or The Signifier are intellectually compelling, while MADiSON or Visage are way better horror experiences. Reveil is a second tier indie game. I'd recommend playing Don't be afraid instead. It doesn't look as gorgeous as Reveil, but the puzzles are demanding, there's plenty of secrets and lore and, most importantly, a real crescendo in intensity and fear. _childDocuments_.review: I can see the SOMA influences all over this game. It's worth picking up for sure but there are some points where it could have done a lot better:Even the more challenging ones () could't puzzle my brain enough as it was quickly (made) obvious what i should be doing (protagonist's commentary also serves as passive hint system). This game feels more like it belongs to the so called "walking sim" genre rather the "adventure" genre which is alright, but be ready for that.  Subjectively speaking it's not really scary, only sports jumpscares in one bit, thank god, with the excpection of a couple of truly scary sequences (). Unfortunately, it always become predictable to me what transpired in the backstory before each reveal, i frequently found answering my questions with certainty before important plot turns. That has a negative effect to the  "phychological horror" as it doens't allow the story to feel more affective.In the contrary, when it comes to graphics and sound desing, i do believe they are responsible for carrying more of the horror moments.The underlying idea is just great! But certain parts feel weird:a. b.  c. d. ...which duh, it's the nature of the genre, but it is felt way too much most of the times feeling i have to walk from A to B, very little exploration or illusion of openess even, just a narrow walkway forward is how this game felt to me. Compare it to how SOMA or The Vanishing of Ethan Carter or other similar games structured their adventure lines.The 1st stealth sequence felt off mechanicly they just don't add up but also  The 2nd stealth sequence was plain bad. In conclusion this game would have benefited from more solid puzzles, a much better ending and more attention to story. This should also help to bring the overall duration up a bit, 5 hours is on the short side for me and i spent most of it looking at the graphics and taking screenshots.This is not a "poetic licence" kind of game by any means, it's a game about 'wow' story moments and I didn't quite get that. This company is on the right track with this one, especially on the art direction department, im sure if they improve upon this formula the next game is going to be a banger.

_childDocuments_.review: The story on this one finally won me over, but only as I was nearing the finish line. Reveil is a great looking game but it's also one you've likely played before.  As a walking sim goes it "plays the hits" but its kind of a bummer to hear that every hit it plays is just a pale cover of the original.  It's a creepy walking sim with an unreliable reality a la "Layers of Fear." It's a reminiscing story like a dozen games I could name. It has a couple of additional gameplay elements. Logic puzzles being one (pretty decent!) and the other is creeping around without being caught by the scary thing while you hunt for 3 props (my least favorite!). That's it really. It hadn't offered me anything new and just felt like another drop in the bucket walking sim that I spent most of my gameplay planning to ultimately not recommend it.  But then it subverted my expectations in the end. I'll leave it at that as not to spoil things. It's still a mostly rehashing of leftovers but it really did surprise me and left a pleasant taste in my mouth and I kinda of love it now so if you venture in, but sure to stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Reveil," is a first-person psychological thriller that immerses players in a surreal circus environment. The game follows Walter Thompson as he searches for his missing wife and daughter, unraveling a narrative filled with psychological horror elements.Pros:- Engaging Narrative: "Reveil" presents a compelling story that delves into themes of memory and reality, keeping players invested throughout the experience. - Atmospheric Design: The game's visuals and sound design effectively create a haunting circus atmosphere, enhancing the psychological horror elements. - Challenging Puzzles: Players encounter a variety of puzzles that are well-integrated into the narrative, offering a satisfying challenge without disrupting the story's flow. Cons:- Limited Scare Factor: Some players may find that the game leans more towards a psychological thriller than outright horror, potentially lacking in traditional scare elements. - Voice Acting Inconsistencies: The protagonist's voice acting has been noted as occasionally lacking emotional depth, which can detract from the immersive experience. - Short Playtime: With a runtime of approximately five hours, some players might feel the experience is brief, especially given the game's engaging narrative. In conclusion, "Reveil" offers a captivating psychological thriller experience with its engaging narrative and atmospheric design. While it may not deliver traditional horror scares and has a relatively short playtime, it stands out as a noteworthy addition to the genre.Score: 9 out of 10 circus tents—A thrilling ride through a mind-bending big top.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Beautiful 3d visuals with detailed models, atmospheric lighting conditions and cool optical effects like volume lights and flares.- Decent horror atmosphere with some immersive moments, yet without managing to be really scary.- Well designed world with various places to visit and some surreal sceneries although most of them are based to cliché horror scenes you've seen before.- Despite the overall shallow gameplay it offers two or three interesting puzzles that have some creativity and need a little bit of thought.- Good audio design. It's pretty simple but offers some convincing environmental sounds and many creepy others.- There is a certain point with a twist that saves the story. Although it's a little bit rushed with mediocre build up it manages to give new interest to the game. Some pieces are coming together and the story parts ways from worn horror elements.The bad- Maybe it's intentional, but during its first two thirds the game is pretty boring based on cliché horror concepts like small girls, bloody walls, objects that are moving by themselves and more. Most of its mechanisms are worn too. Deformed places, labyrinths, rooms that change shape behind you after reaching a dead end. We've seen all these several times before.-  The first two thirds of the story is a combination of random events and cryptic symbols without particular coherence, like it just tries to impress the player. Storytelling is also poor with memories and voices at certain points revealing parts of the plot. The final third is more interesting but it needed some better build up.- Gameplay is shallow. You mostly move into a linear path watching horror tricks and a few silly jump scares.- Voice acting performances are not convincing and fail to catch the vibes or the emotions of each moment.

_childDocuments_.review: as a horror game fan. REVEIL, I can confidently say it's a game that truly immerses you in a psychological rollercoaster. As you navigate through a world where the boundaries between reality and illusion blur, REVEIL presents a series of cryptic puzzles and unsettling clues that test both your intellect and your sanity.The game's narrative unfolds in five distinct acts, each set in meticulously designed environments that draw inspiration from the circus era of the 1960s. From the faded grandeur of circus tents to the eerie corridors of Walter's mind, every location is rendered with stunning detail and immersive atmosphere, pulling players deeper into the unraveling mystery.What truly sets REVEIL apart is its multi-layered narrative, which seamlessly weaves together elements of psychedelia, biography, and horror to create a story that is as compelling as it is disturbing. As you delve deeper into Walter's psyche, you'll uncover dark secrets and hidden truths that challenge your perceptions of reality, leaving you questioning everything you thought you knew.But perhaps the most impressive aspect of REVEIL is its ability to keep players on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its cleverly crafted puzzles, visually stunning environments, and spine-tingling atmosphere, the game offers a truly immersive horror experience that is guaranteed to keep you hooked until the very end.In conclusion, REVEIL is a masterpiece of psychological horror that deserves a place in the library of any horror game fan. With its compelling narrative, immersive atmosphere, and challenging game-play, it offers an experience that is as thrilling as it is thought-provoking. If you're looking for a game that will keep you guessing until the very end, look no further than REVEIL. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Full gameplay: Like some of the other users mentioned, this game is very similar to Layers Of Fear game, if you like those type of psychological narrative games without many horror elements I think you might like this game. Game has good visuals with an interesting story, but unfortunately the gameplay is not engaging even with few good puzzles. You basically just walk from point A to B to progress like many other horror games, although I am not sure if this game considered as horror game or not because there weren't many scary elements in this game. I was able to finish the game after about 3 hours and I think for $20 asking price this amount of gameplay is little short, however there are multiple endings and some replayability. So if you are OK with this price and game style I'd recommend it. Otherwise wait for discount. I liked overall visuals and art style, these type of games like Layers Of Fear have a good and creative way of presenting their story, there are lots of unique visual elements and presentation in the game that I liked. Overall graphics are good but it didn't wow me. One of the negative points for me was lack of body for character, in these games I think having animation for character body adds a lot to immersion. The gameplay as I said is very basic, walking from A to B, solve some puzzles in between, read documents and interact with objects to understand what the story is and progress. You've seen these type of gameplays in most of horror games so don't expect something new. Some of the puzzles I think were fun to solve and I liked them but some were unusually simple. There are some chapters in the game that you need to hide from enemies to survive, the positive side of their design is that if you fail and die you'll get back to a very close point without losing a lot of progress, it feels like it was part of the story and you don't have to start from beginning of checkpoint. Overall game speed felt little slow even with running option, I wish the running was little faster but it's not game breaking. I think story is best part of this game, although it started very slow and felt very boring in the beginning, after 30-45 minutes of my gameplay it got a little more interesting, you start to feel something is not right and become more curious about what has happened to the antagonist. Some of the areas of the game like the bedroom felt repetitive, from story stand point it made total sense to visit it multiple times but from gameplay standpoint it was a little on boring side. There were some other areas that you visit for multiple times and I wish there were more variety to the environment that you visit in game. I think story was good and interesting, however there were some questions that I didn't get the answers for but there are multiple endings while some of them were very underwhelming. Overall I enjoyed the sound effects and specially some of music track were really good. I played on max quality with DLSS on quality mode and was getting more than 200fps. There were some hiccups when entering new areas and also alot of ghosting probably because of DLSS, but overall the performance was really good and game run very smoothly and didn't encounter any bugs during my gameplay. I also have to thank devs for including this save system, although it's not manual save but for this game I think it's good enough, you have list of chapters and within each chapter you can select the checkpoint to start.There are some replayability in this game, as I said there are multiple endings and also there are some collectible in each chapter if you are interested in these stuff.CPU: Intel Core i9-12900KMB: MSI Z690 Edge WiFi DDR4RAM: GSkill 32Gb DDR4 3600MhzGPU: Asus GeForce RTX 3090 StrixMonitor: Samsung Odyssey G7 32" 1440P 240Hz

_childDocuments_.review: Look, if you want to help a small, pretty much one-man-band indie developer, buy the game.  I understand as a dev there's a point where you ask yourself, "Well... do I polish this, and work on detail for the next two years, or just release it at a bargain rate and get noticed by a big time developer with a small game like this in my portfolio?"  He's not wrong, by the way - but the game is far from finished.  It is also far from entertaining.  Here me out:Early into Chapter 1 I fell through the floor at one point in a hallway, and didn't die.  After no clipping, and the screen going black but still having the reticle, I found I was able to run/walk, so I thought it was part of the game, (since you have multiple and sudden psychedelic moments).  Nope.  Just didn't hit a death barrier, and was essentially under the map with no reference in any direction I ran and heard my footsteps.  Time to restart and avoid that spot on the floor while running down the hallway.  There's several more instances not unlike this, where I thought, "Why in God's name am I still bothering to play this?"  Then I would have to restart again, and avoid that spot, or attempt to open the object again hoping it didn't glitch.  It might be petty, but another notable nuisance is movement in general.  The only time you *actually* run in the game, is a forest scene with a Baba Yaga of sorts, otherwise "running" is a derpy, awkward, shuffle forward.  There IS no "running."  The majority of the game you walk VERY slowly, (to extend the very short storyline I presume - as much as a viewer can stand, yet still play regardless).  I cannot emphasize this enough.  You move so slowly throughout the game, it put me to sleep in Chapter one looking for the up-teenth item to leave the area the first time I attempted playthrough.  There are THREE puzzles in the game.  Yes you read that correctly.  One is using a clever little Crytography versus symbology with a laser to unlock a box, the second is opening a puzzle box, and lastly the final puzzle is fumbling at a machine with different modules to get the coding correct for an interface sequence.  The rest of the ENTIRE GAME is TREASURE HUNTING for parts/pieces/objects to escape, (if you like that sort of thing).  Some jump scares, and again poor programming for interactions in my opinion, (at least with an Xbox controller).  This game pulls out ideas from successful stories like Vanilla Sky and Total Recall.  I saw nothing truly original, nor remarkable.  Sprinkle in some Groundhog Day, and voilà! you have Reveil.  I bought the bundle, so I'll have to play through it's semi-sequel Shift 87, but quite honestly: I think this dev paid some YouTubers to "review" and play the Reveil game, then hoped to make a million bucks after working hard on it , (EDIT: Dev replied 5 years)  That's what it feels like, that's how it played, and that's the level of engagement I got from it.  Although, with  (EDIT: Dev replied no AI used) the ability to simply pull all these assets directly from an game engine without having to design any of it now from scratch,  At the end of the day I don't mind paying.  After all, it was as I said, reasonably priced ($24 for both in a bundle).  If you're not 43 years old, and a film studies major, you'll likely enjoy this game and it's twists.  I had a great experience myself with Backrooms: Lost Tape, Pools, or Superliminal - extraordinary games that didn't pull from typical Hollywood tropes; also very reasonable price points that were in my opinion more frightening, or in the case of Superliminal, highly puzzle driven.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR |   REVEIL is a decently crafted horror indie game that focuses on puzzles and some mind messing to create some fun jump scares and a few creepy areas.  At 20 bucks i feel the game sits at the edge of worth it price.  When on sale it is a  well worth it buy if you like horror games with puzzles that won't tax your mind to much and can be beat in one sitting.Full Review. REVEIL is a short horror game that sit's it self on the edge of a Walking simulator with a few minor threats.  A bit like Layers of Fear in that regard.  Though with alot less "death chance " moments.  The story it self is unique with a some fun twists that did honestly have me smiling by the end of the game.  Though it did give me a few good jump scares here and there. Sadly they where to few and far apart. The game focuses more so on the story and events of Walter Thompson. but out side of that i did not find the game overall that scary 90 percent of the time.  The game also has no real threat through most of the game.  The few times you have a threat, it is very easy to avoid. Luck is not really a factor at all with them. The game does also use the "motion interaction" method that Frictional Games (amnesia, Soma) use in their game.  Though i do feel it's not as well implemented in this game.  I had a more than a few moments where it was hard to understand exactly what and how it wanted me to move my mouse. Thus causing things to be more frustrating than immersive overall. Length of the game is also not that long.  A single play session of 3 to 4 hours will beat this game.  It dose have a little bit of a replay value once you beat it to get the endings.  Thankfully once beat you have access to well place Chapter select options so you don't have to PLAY the entire game all over again just to make one little choice to change things up. Overall I give this game a 7/10.  If you like games that mess with your mind a bit like Evil Within, Layers of Fear. And want some Puzzles that where part of old school horror games from the ps1 days.   I feel you will enjoy this game and the story it has.    If your  looking for hardcore horror and jumps cares though like that of OUTLAST style games, This is not it.  It is here to tell you a story and go BOO a few times.   A bit of a hard sale at 20 bucks, but when on sale a worth grab to add.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of horror games, I'm always on the lookout for experiences that truly push the boundaries of the genre. REVEIL, developed by Pixelsplit, stands out as a shining example of what a narrative-driven psycho-thriller should be.From the moment I stepped into the shoes of Walter Thompson, I was engulfed in a world of mystery and terror. The attention to detail in both storytelling and gameplay mechanics is simply astounding. Every corner of the Nelson Bros Circus, with its dark history and hidden secrets, kept me on the edge of my seat as I unraveled the twisted tale that awaited.What sets REVEIL apart is its seamless integration of story, puzzles, and exploration. Each element complements the other, creating a cohesive and immersive experience that is as satisfying as it is chilling. The puzzles are cleverly crafted, requiring both wit and courage to solve, while the exploration rewards curiosity with haunting discoveries.Pixelsplit has once again proven their prowess as developers with REVEIL. Their previous title, Virtual Rides 3, showcased their talent for creating immersive experiences, and REVEIL takes it to a whole new level. The atmosphere they've crafted is palpable, drawing players deeper into the darkness with each passing moment.But perhaps the true highlight of REVEIL is its narrative. As Walter's past intertwines with the horrors of the present, the story unfolds in ways that are both shocking and thought-provoking. It's a testament to the skill of the writers and the dedication of the development team to deliver a tale that lingers long after the credits roll.In conclusion, REVEIL is a masterpiece of horror gaming that deserves a place among the greats. With its gripping story, clever puzzles, and atmospheric world, it's an experience that will haunt players long after they've put down the controller. If you're a fan of psychological thrillers, do yourself a favor and dive into the darkness of REVEIL. You won't be disappointed.And for those interested in witnessing the terror firsthand, check out my live stream of REVEIL at Rays Sim's YouTube Channel . Join me as we brave the nightmares together!

name: Jupiter Hell
detailed_description: Do you miss the good old days when games weren't holding your hand? Then you're in the perfect place. In Jupiter Hell - Action follows your every move. When you act, your enemies act. But when you die. You die for good. Jupiter Hell lets you become a hero in a classic 90s-flavored sci-fi universe. It's you and your trusty shotgun (or chaingun, railgun or even a chainsaw) against hordes of demonic and alien motherfu***. All to the shine of CRT monitors. Just like in the good old days. But the graphics are much better. Unlock new perks, test out new builds and try to live through the hell you have ended up in. Every run is different, thanks to the procedurally generated levels. Earn new perks. Build your character to endure what lurks around the corner. If you manage to survive the Jupiter Hell - you can unlock new challenges. It's not gonna get any easier. Quite the contrary. it's gonna make you suffer. Does 20+ years of experience making top-down, cosmic-hell roguelikes sound like a recipe for a hell of a good turn-based roguelike? ChaosForge team, the developer of Jupiter Hell, gained recognition for creating Doom, the Roguelike (known also as DRL.) They built the Jupiter Hell as a spiritual successor to DRL.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just great! Really easy to fire it up and get killing, none of the usual roguelike faffing (though of course there's a time and a place for that). It's shot through with a sense of fun and exuberance. Though I haven't quite plumbed the depths of it yet, I can see that there is also a lot of depth to it with regards to customising your run too. Also  on the run where I got the furthest, my character was ludicrously overpowered, until he wasn't and an enemy one shotted me! But it always feels fair when you die, and the loop of getting you back into play is so fast it doesn't matter! Dev seems super nice too and always v responsive to feedback and bugs etc. If you're hesitating, get it! It's totally worth it. It's a great entry level roguelike too - the immediacy of it reminds me of Brogue, which is one of the very best games ever made. Can't wait to explore this one a hell a lot more!

I known the dev team is small, but I hope they update the heck out of this game because of how flippin awesome it is!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A 5-6/10 that's just okay, at the moment. IMHO.I hate to say this. Normally people don't genuinely mean that, but I do.Unless significant changes are made, this just isn't worth (near) full price.Is it a bad game? I wouldn't say that.Whether you played DRL or not, this game seems a bit... average.Not bad, but not very good. It's an okay game.Graphically, everything is far too muddy and dark.Perhaps it's for atmosphere, but it just went too far with it.The core gameplay was... functional. However, it became repetitive far quicker than expected.For me, everything became very stale around floor 4.It's possible that mid/late-game mix things up, but I'm not so sure.Sounds are not great. Certain weapons, like shotguns, sound weak.Music is generic, at best, and fails to get the blood pumping.The player character became annoying very quickly. He rarely speaks, but was annoying when he did.I can't think of a better description for the player character than "edgy tryhard ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."This gimmick can work, and can be entertaining.Something is off about the execution here, though.It wasn't doing anything for me.I won't speak on difficulty, or weapon and enemy balance.As I haven't really played enough to comfortably gauge that.However, I had no issues there. At least on medium difficulty.The inability to unload weapons is a minor annoyance, but nothing beyond that.I must say, however, something stands out with character balance.The marine, as far as I know, is the only class that can't increase inventory size, or number of weapons.This is a massive drawback, that I don't think his improved health regeneration makes up for.If I'm completely blind, and somehow missed the option, then ignore this point.I still can't say this is an objectively bad game.But I just can't call it good.It plays everything too safe, and just ends up being very average.As a result, I can't score it higher than a 5/10.If there was ever a need for a "neutral" review option, it's here.I hope the devs can improve the game, and make it the great game it deserves to be.

_childDocuments_.review: GAME DESIGN:The game has a grid-based, turned-based movement system. You can usually move only in 4 directions. There are three character classes. Each class provides different tools to beat the game. Most of the tools however are available in some way to all the classes which makes the classes not that unique. Nevertheless, I think the game has a well-thought-out and well-balanced character development system.AI:Enemies are very often stupid, which makes some sense because all of them are zombies, monsters, or robots. In a lot of cases you just hide behind the cover and enemies willingly walk out of their covers to be easily shot. Enemies seem to walk towards you when they hear you but when they lose you from sight they weirdly retreat. The AI ​​in this game to me feels quite artificial. I would like it if an enemy could consciously (not accidentally) shoot the explosive barrel when I'm standing next to it.GRAPHICS AND CHARACTER ANIMATION:The graphics are ok however, I would like to point out that:- The lighting is not quite polished in some parts of the game. For example in Europa cave levels light is so strong that you can barely see the items on the floor.- When you for example press the up button and the right button at once it seems that the character is moving diagonally. In the tutorial, they explain that actually, you can move only in 4 directions, and moving diagonally is only a side effect of the animation system and that they're two consecutive moves. I think the graphics should match and accentuate the game design.THE MOOD:The graphical style and the music are inspired by DOOM.In my opinion, the music lives up to the original DOOM score.SUMMARY:Jupiter Hell is a very good classical rogue-like.I have played it for 25 hours and I'm still not bored.The game is still a bit unpolished but it's understandable. It's a very complicated game and it has been developed in a very small team for the last 13 years.It is still in active development and a lot of things will eventually get polished.The game is definitely worth trying out.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great spiritual rogue-like successor of DoomRL which improved upon its formula and removed some really annoying mechanics (destroying items, giftdropping, unloading weapons...). Now it is its own thing with great variety of difficulties and modes to play at. Biggest improvements are cover/dodge mechanics, more much clearer rules and less RNG depended playthroughs. Also its 3D but that is not really important for game like this (but its nicer to look at at least :) ).Like before each class and individual master traits provide different enough playstyles that can give enough playtime for hundreds of hours. Variety of weapons, items, traits, uniques, monsters and levels is in the sweet spot where there is enough but it is not too much where I know what to expect but it is still variable enough.Majority of times I die (and that can happen a lot) I know perfectly well what I did wrong and how I could have prevented it (usually by hoarding healing items and refusing to use them until it is too late). For me that is most important trait of good rogue-like - I hate when I lose purely to RNG.Highly recommend for fans of tactical games, rogue-likes or DoomRL fans.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic and addictive, but be warned. As fun as it is - and I do not throw this around lightly as it is a stereotype of whiny gamerz lol - this game is *so cheap*. Prepare to die in the most absolutely unfair ways. In a sense, I understand this as it is very common for rogue likes to have huge difficulty spikes (and this game's theme is for it to literally be hell). However, there are times where the game just absolutely bends you  over and there is no recourse. It can be so frustrating, especially after a great hours long run, just for it to end on rng for an enemy spawn, or for a random massive spike of damage from one bullet that flukes and hits you. With that said, this game again is so addictive, and so easy to just pour time into. Diverse character builds, interesting and challenging enemies, a variety of cool locations to explore and loot, and of course the fantastic angry space man voice acting of none other than our "favourite spaceman on the citadel" Mark Meer. If you can stomach the rough patches of difficulty, you will have an absolute blast playing this game, it's a diamond in the rough that is well worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: Many moons ago there was a free fan made game called Doom RL, it was the perfect blend of the Doom universe and the genre that has come to be known as "rogue" or "rogue like" it was a passion project made by a single developer and the combination of the Doom universe and the rogue like game play meant it was an amazing game that I personally sank over 200 hours into. With many different strategies to try and a sadistically beautiful quality of game play that lead to that "one more go" mentality, it was truly a gem of an indie game... however, the developer was brought low by a cease and desist forcing them to remove the game from their website, a true tragedy for the indie game scene as it became lost to the ether. When I updated my computer, sadly it was one of the files that slipped through the cracks in the process and alas I was unable to track it down again, even though memories of playing it stuck with me for many years.Jupiter Hell is the spiritual successor to that long lost game, a lot of the same game play mechanics are there from Doom RL, the game plays exactly how I remember Doom RL playing, even down to the weapons and armour upgrades, the class system, the special harder levels with bigger rewards, and the character development system. If you like Rogue likes and you like SciFi demon killing, then this is the game for you.TL:DR It's Doom RL remade without the Doom branding due to copy right, and it has been given a lot of love.Buy it. NOW

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating game marred by questionable design decisions.First things first; it's fun and interesting. The 80's zeerust aesthetic is excellent, and multiple types of enemies are difficult yet engaging insofar as finding ways to overcome them. The upgrade system is, perhaps, a touch more bare bones than I would like such a game, but understandable regarding game balance.The bad; those questionable design decisions reveal just how skin-deep certain strategic decisions actually are. Consider the following:You are in the early game and are using a weapon kit that involves, say, a grenade launcher, a shotgun, and maybe a autorifle, and are getting ready to go down to the next floor. The floor you are currently on has had a horrendous number of enemies who used grenade launchers, and you spent a great deal of time weaving around trying to avoid getting splattered. Congrats! You've successfully not died to a potential early game killer; however, you spent so long trying to avoid dying that the enemies, now dead, had managed to reload their weapons.And you can't unload them to get that rare-for-that-point-in-the-game ammo. Unlike other options in roguelikes, where a decision is made with a limited carry-weight or pack-size in consideration, the game has artificially restricted your available options. You can't move/drop relics, either, because they break on drop. To put it another way, certain complications on weaponry and relics exist solely to complicate their usage, and in certain situations simply mean that I am borderline forced to use a mediocre copy of the weapon I already possess simply to conserve ammo, since it is irretrievable once loaded.Progression is almost purely linear; there are branching paths on each planet, and each route may have a 'special' floor that you can return back to the route from, but those are exceptions. This, inherently, isn't a problem, but it makes the decision to break relics on drop even more baffling.So, yeah. There are the bones of a stellar, 10/10 game here. But there are a number of moment by moment decisions that turn an interesting experience into an aggravating one, and an aggravating one into an angry one. I gave the game 20 hours and I got to Dante, so I know enough to know that there were design decisions that broke this experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely amazing tactical, atmospheric, heavy metal, 90s action movie roguelike! One of the complaints of roguelike haters is RNG. However, this game brilliantly balances probability with binary (yes/no) tactical decisions. For example, a shotgun that has 33% accuracy on an enemy will inflict 33% of its max damage on that enemy (guaranteed). On the other hand, a single projectile weapon like a sniper rifle will hit with the given accuracy. For automatic weapons, a 33% chance to hit is applied to EACH bullet in the burst, so if your gun shoots 3 bullets you will hit with 1 bullet.200+ hours into the game and I keep coming back to it. There are so many variables for level branching, combined with a rich set of skills to customize and experiment with, add in mod-able proceduraly generated loot and weapons and baddies galore.In summary, this game has not reached a fraction of the popularity it deserves yet. I hope the developers keep working on it.That said, every game could be improved a bit. Some of my hopes for improvements follow:1) More diverse set of skills that help to differentiate play-styles for each character type.2) Better balancing and more testing to ensure that each build is viable all the way to the end boss. Currently, some builds make it near impossible to defeat the end boss. An example is Gun Kata master skill. It's super fun to shoot 2 pistols simultaneously with each move. However, you run out of ammo stupidly fast and it would not even be viable with the number of baddies on Hard difficulty. This is even true when getting skills that allow you to convert ammo types to equipped weapon. Also, Gun Kata will auto-shoot at the nearest enemy. In the final boss battle, minions are spawning every turn around the boss, but you cannot direct your fire to finish off the boss, so there is no hope of winning with this build. Additionally, a sniper build is not viable on Hard due to the shear number of enemies that are constantly rushing you and you cannot waste a turn aiming at a target to enhance damage. A lot of work can be done to test and improve balance.3) More information on the enemies would be extremely helpful. After 200 hours, I still cannot understand in what scenario the Medusa can reduce my HP max. And I have no clue what the white HP overlay is on the enemies (armor??). You can also suddenly be reduced to a pile of ashes without any warning because several enemies were prepping a simultaneous attack on you, or one enemy is targeting you for a special attack. So, some UI information on the estimated damage you will take on a given round could be nice. Or, perhaps this is a mod option on a combat visor that gives you a prediction of damage received on the next turn!Best of luck to the developers, I hope your game receives the popularity and recognition it so deserves!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible fun. I was on the fence because I'm a baby, and I wanted a metaprogression system, but that would be a very silly reason not to get this game. _childDocuments_.review: Way back at PAX East 2018, I had an opportunity to demo this turn-based action game. It had this dark space setting with heavy metal vibes, and all in all, looked really cool. Now, I am a huge Doom fan, and not just the recent games. I grew up with them. Doom was one of the first FPS games I experienced. Anyway, back to the above game. It’s clear this game draws a lot of inspiration from Doom. I chatted up one of the devs at the show and he gave me a business card with the game’s name on it: Jupiter Hell. I am actually kind of annoyed at myself for not following Jupiter Hell after PAX (I did not have a gaming PC at the time so anything I enjoyed at the show that was slated for PC release was kind of forgotten). Connections to Doom aside, I just have to say: this game is a wild time.Developed by Chaosforge, Jupiter Hell “is a roguelike set in a 90s sci-fi universe.” You play as a lone space marine against hordes of demons on the moons of Jupiter. Wearing its influences on it’s sleeve like a tattoo on its forehead, this is a fast-paced (well, as fast-paced as turn-based can possibly be), in your face, hardcore, thrill ride.You actually can play as a lone marine, scout, or technician. I mean, you are still alone but you do not have to just play as a marine.The objective remains the same regardless of the class you choose: survive the hordes of demons and guards and mechs and drones and get to the next floor and the next floor and so on and so forth. Each of the three classes plays the same way with the exception of special abilities. The marine has a fury resource. He gains fury by killing, which can be used to activate adrenaline which allows him to heal a bit and ignore the pain for a few seconds. Scouts utilize stealth for short periods of time, which can help get to a better position for combat. And technicians have access to smoke bombs that break line of sight with enemies, which in turn allows for better positioning or easier escaping.Upon taking control of your character, you learn that you can only move in the cardinal directions: up, down, left, and right. Diagonal movement is done via two separate movements quickly like up and left or down and right. I said turn-based earlier, but it’s not as simple as games like Final Fantasy Tactics where there is a clear distinction between each side’s turns. If you have ever played Superhot, you will see some similarities. When you move, they move. You can choose to wait, which serves as a “turn,” and then they will move. Waiting is usually used to take cover and open fire once the enemy makes its move. The game shows your chance to hit so you can decide whether rushing in or waiting is the better option.There were a few times that I entered a room to loot a chest and could see four enemies approach. By waiting in the corner, I picked them off as they came into range. There is also an option to manually target, which comes in handy with the numerous explosive barrels throughout the levels.Your objective is to find the elevator to advance and get off each planet. Levels are completely randomized, but sometimes, you find the elevator almost immediately, while other times, you need to uncover every square inch first. You are free to leave right away, but exploration may be in your best interest. For one, this is how you improve your arsenal. You only start with one weapon, but you can find combat knives, pipe wrenches, shotguns, and even miniguns to name just a few. There is also armor pieces (head and chest), grenades, and multi-tools which have several uses.Throughout the levels, you come across terminals. These terminals do a number of things including revealing the map, marking enemies, providing weapon upgrades, health upgrades, and even disabling some enemies all at the cost of multi-tools. Exploration also helps you earn experience. With enough experience, you level up and gain access to perks. The perks are displayed in list format but they behave similarly to talent trees in other games with perks locked until previous perks are picked up.Perks range from health increases to dual-wielding to life leech, but their names are the best part. Names like Son of a Gun and Angry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, or, my favorite: Rip and Tear (gee, wonder where they got that one from).What is funny is that Angry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can also describe the marine almost to a tee. For example, if you press the button to pick up and there is nothing to pick up, he will say, “There’s nothing here.” Keep pressing that button and he raises his voice to say, “I told you, there’s nothing here.” When you run out of ammo, you may hear, “Reload dammit!” or “There’s no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ammo!”Guess who also might get angry? YOU. This game is a roguelike. This is more like Rogue than it is like the roguelikes that have been released in the past two years or so. How so? When you die here, you die. Game over. There is no level-up screen to show what you earned to make the next run or the run after easier. You do see how you performed compared to your other tries, but that is it. The next run starts right from the beginning just like it did when you first started the game. If it is any consolation, you can save and quit to prolong the inevitable but every run is a brand new run.Replayability is extremely high in this game. In campaign mode, you choose your difficulty and then have to make it to the end. Levels have branching paths which make no run exactly the same. If the campaign is not your thing, try a challenge run or a trial. Challenge runs set parameters like limited inventory but increased movement speed or only grant rocket launchers as weapons. Trials change everything from removing all branching paths to playing forever/until you die, or even having every level available with the ability to choose where to go (you normally have to find either exit).Jupiter Hell combines one of the most popular genres of late and one of the longest-running and best-known series, and somehow, it just works. In fact, it works really well. Permadeath and that “one more run” feeling with the in-your-face and heavy metal vibes of Doom combined with turn-based, tactical gameplay make for an extremely enjoyable and fun as hell (PUN INTENDED) game. Side note: if you want all of the above-described action but without the foul language and cheesy 90s style, you can actually turn it all off!
