_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is an awesome game and I honestly think everyone should play it at least once. I'll try to quickly describe various parts of the game; sorry if it gets messy.The game is a roguelike by all means, but focused on long-range combat. You'll find all the pillars of a roguelike: RPG elements, turn-based gameplay, grid-based levels, procedurally generated levels and, the hallmark of the genre,  permadeath.Infinite replayability, because all levels are randomly generated, aside from the special levels, which have the same general layout, but small parts of them are still random. There's a branching system, which allows you to take different paths to make the game a little more varied; the different branches are sort-of parallel and meet at one point.The trait system is great. Kornel (game author) said that no trait should be seen as "lesser" and all traits are actually useful. This statement holds, as I find myself experimenting with different trait combinations and when I'm choosing my next trait, I feel like a kid in a candy store. The variety of traits and their combinations extends the replayablity by a whole lot, too. And if you combine the right traits and inventory together, you can pull off some really amazing runs that make you feel like you're on fire!You can choose from 3 character classes, each with a different set of traits (some are common, some are unique to the class) to play with. There are 5 "master" traits which offer a massive advantage, but you may choose only one master trait. The master traits require some traits to be already required, and they're designed to fit your playing style (eg. if you already have traits that help with automatic weapons, the unlocked master traits will also fit that style).On paper, 3 classes with 5 master traits each should give you 15 different approaches to the game. In reality, there are more ways than that to play the game, because you can use different trait combinations, use different equipment, choose different branches etc.Whatever mood I'm in when I start a new run, the game has means to suit that mood. I never feel limited by the game's mechanics, there's always something to help me with experimenting. I honestly lost count of how many unique approaches I've tried out and it always felt like the game was made for each and every one of them.The inventory system is a nice balance between DRL and AliensRL. It only allows a limited number of weapons and wearable gear, which works great against hoarding.The cover mechanics are nice and intuitive and really add a strategical aspect to shooting things up.Modding equipment is done by having 3 kinds of mod packs and each mod pack will let you choose between several options of modification, letting you personalize every modification you make. There's a trait that lets you get more options and stack more mod packs onto the same equipment.Stylistically, the game is everything I love. It's a 90s themed game and brings all the tropes I personally loved about that era. If you're not into that, it's still configurable, so you don't have to hear the one-liners. Fowl language can be turned off, too.The graphics are pleasant and even though I'm an ASCII freak, I wouldn't play JH without the graphical mode anymore.The soundtrack is metal AF. I especially like the track that plays on Europa.One of the things I really appreciate is no microtransactions. You buy the game once and it's all yours. You cannot purchase progress, everything you get is through pure gameplay. There's no meta-progression either, aside from unlocking challenge modes where you can make it harder on yourself.Overall, playing the game is a blast. Even if you lose, you still feel very satisfied, because you had so much fun doing it. The game is challenging, but plays fair - no cheap deaths, you know it's you who sucks.And for those of you coming from DRL: it feels like home, but actually better! You will have to let go of some DRL mechanics (diagonal movement, assemblies, ...), but I promise you won't miss any of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A great example of old-school being touched up and made into a nice neat package. The gameplay loop is strange at first, but like most of these types of games you get used to it. A great game to experiment with builds. Leveling up is fair and the randomness of the game isn't too challenging at normal difficulty. Curveballs and risk/reward is diverse enough to have you guessing what punches to roll with. The cover mechanic is brilliant and the classes are pretty cool despite only being three currently.Easy to learn and quick to pick up. The main marine is very reminiscent of old school shooters, with Duke Nukem-esque quips and violent gunplay. Surprisingly these can be turned down or tuned up to taste, but because I grew up in the early 90s I enjoy having an Evil Dead like protagonist so everything is turned up to max.I enjoy how each weapon is unique with its own use instead of it being a one-size fits all approach. The shotgun in doom was probably the mainstay and made all other guns look paltry in comparison. In this, the shotgun being one shot before reload is a great mechanic as you use it more as a room clearing spray rather than a multi-tool of destruction. Juggling three weapons is fun and brings a new level to tacticality. With each turn being used for reloads, consumables and actions itself. Each engagement feels like making a choice to mitigate as much risk as possible while the level design gives you fun ways to set traps and use the environment to your benefit/or detriment. Which is what I feel a lot of top downs miss the mark on.Really the only thing that is missing is more gore and violent death scenes, perhaps executions on close enemies that are low in health, which would really make the game feel finished at least to me.[9/10] with a Workshop already added that can easily turn to 10/10 as long as the modding community is active.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Preserves quite a lot of what made its predecessor (DoomRL) such a tremendously entertaining short-form roguelike. While the jump from ASCI to tilesets to, now, full 3D graphics (admittedly used basically like a tileset), might rankle some purists, under the hood it's still 100% grid-based, turn-based, ever-descending dungeon crawling goodness, albeit with the same atypical emphasis on ranged combat that helped differentiate the original game from its kin. The additional costs in terms of sound and graphics assets, not to mention the extra copyright law focus a commercial release garners, does mean it loses some of that delightfully bonkers smorgasbord of equipment straight up lifted from other media. But it remains a really solid, strategically engaging, and immensely replayable experience that consistently rewards experimentation and thoughtful planning. It's short, and it's flashy, but it still bears the torch of meaty, engaging challenge passed on by traditional roguelikes all the way back to the originals.I do have to unfortunately admit the cover mechanic really dictates a lot of how the game plays. As in any traditional roguelike, risk mitigation is king. But that means the optimal strategy is often protracted games of peek-a-boo with enemies as you stick to corners and exploit line-of-sight. It can get repetitive, and for a game based on a game based on Doom, that does mean it's a little short on that cathartic space marine rip-and-tear feeling. Even the most heavily armored monster of a player character still has to play cautiously. That in and of itself isn't unusual for a traditional roguelike, granted, but it can sometimes get wearisome.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite appearances, a very traditional rogue-like - turn based, grid movement, resource management and punishing difficulty - but with guns.  Well executed, if you like that sort of thing.I've been pleased to see the developer has been regularly putting out substantial content updates, even though the game is 'complete' (no longer early access).Don't be baited by the difficulty settings into playing on 'hard'.  'Medium' is plenty hard enough to get your first win, even if you've played a fair amount of traditional rogue-likes before.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't a ton of depth to the mechanics, honestly, and that's a major problem in a roguelike. Yeah, there are lots of ways to approach things, but most everything amounts to "get into cover, shoot, etc". It's okay enough, but it gets old after a few hours. There are a few areas that are almost instant kills unless you're lucky. The music isn't bad, but gets old after hearing the same few tracks again and again. If the game was 8-10 hours, I would be more forgiving, but sadly this outstays its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: While Jupiter Hell doesn't have the incredible depth that D***RL has, it's very well put together and presented. The lack of meta progression compels you to learn as you go (or keep the Wiki open for quick reference) and while you can build your character the same way run after run, the random drops and sub-areas will prevent things from getting too stale. A very good "proper" roguelike, one that I hope will continue to get new content and updates for a good while.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is mainly for people who didn't play classic roguelites like DOOMRL. Jupiter Hell is a classic roguelite turn-based shooter. It's visually similar to very old arcade games with the UI resembling the screens of old arcade machines as well as the font looking like it is straight from the 90s. Gameplaywise it luckily feels like a modern game. With a top-down view, you're looking on the battlefield, controlling your soldier going from one level into another, killing other soldiers and monsters, getting new weapons, pieces of armor, and leveling him up. Your goal is to find a new spaceship to flee with, or is it? Younger folks maybe won't know this but this being a classic Roguelite also means there isn't a meta progression like you know it from some newer games. You won't really unlock new things to make future runs easier. However, you can unlock new difficulties, challenge mode, and trials (like a faster experience of the game, etc. - mostly modifiers to the settings). The whole game is turn-based even if you're not in a fight. You're playing with Keyboard only (or Controller) and there is no way to play with a mouse. This also makes it possible for you to have a faster experience. You move one step after another and carefully lookout for enemies and stuff. Whenever you press and hold a key to move faster, the game will stop you from moving for a short amount of time when an enemy comes nearby. This is a nice addition because sometimes you would probably oversee them.You have an inventory with up to three weapons, ammunition, and items such as medkits, grenades, tools, and more. Aside from headgear and armor, there isn't much to find to make you more resistant to enemies attacks.There aren't different attacks like in XCOM or other TBS games - just shoot with one of your weapons. It's pretty rudimentary but still tactical to some extend. They are procedurally generated and change from time to time. You can find chests with weapons and items in them, go to a PC to hack robots (which WILL shoot you if you don't deactivate them or something), and more. At each level, you need to find an elevator to progress further. Sometimes there is more than one, sometimes you need to activate something first before using the elevator. Maps look mostly the same with some small differences like snow, etc.    Jupiter Hell is a fun little roguelite turn-based shooter. It's based on a classic game and evolves some of what was offered back then to make it more attractive for newer folks. Personally, I think they could easily add a few more elements to go with the flow of newer roguelites. I can see why they don't and I respect that but because of this, Jupiter Hell couldn't suck me in. It is enjoyable to some extent but I easily lost interest. Still, if you're looking for a hardcore turn-based shooter and don't need any form of meta progression, this is a solid game and you should get it on sale.If you're looking for a tactical turn-based strategy game - don't buy it. This probably won't satisfy you.

_childDocuments_.review: Badly balanced but it doesn't hit just how bad it is until you're over halfway through.  My first run died in zone 3 because I got hit by poison that did more damage per tick than any enemy attack did in outright damage, and suddenly 20 damage, 19 damage, 18 damage, 17 damage, 16 damage.  Even attempting to heal did nothing for me because I didn't have the "remove poison" heal.  There was zero chance of surviving thanks to a single hit wiping out several times my full life bar.Bad RNG out the ass but then got to zone 3 with a bunch of extra heals and... burned them all on a boss that was hitting for 50+ damage per turn.  I healed with a medkit and ended up with less HP than before I healed.If I was playing in one of the super-hard difficulties, I'd accept: yeah that's probably balanced for it.  But playing on NORMAL?  It's bad.If you don't pick an exact build that can counter the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ somehow, you are going to go from doing really damn good to instant death.  Can't recommend until they figure out what balance is.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As a DoomRL enthusiast, it took me way too long to buy this game.It is DoomRL, with extra lovely modes, and the best gamepad support of any roguelike game I ever played - yes, even better than the Shiren games, thanks to less complex mechanics.My only complain so far is that the 3D view is superfluous, and even detrimental to some readability: while the guns and loot are easily identified on the floor thanks to near ASCII iconography, foes are troublesome to distinguish from each others to my aging eyes, and some very important elements, such as which barrels have been detonated and which haven't, I am unable to tell without inspecting each element with the keyboard cursor.I really hope for an ASCII mode, or even better, that an icon mode shaped around the ones of the loot is implemented someday. Given the continuous support, I expect this to happen eventually, when the developers will start experiencing old eye issues!In any case, what a wonderful, satisfying little blast of a roguelike.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game's seriously hard to put down. It's a very traditional roguelike with the personality of finely aged 90s era cheese (read: awful, but fondly nostalgic), but with a modern coat of paint on the visuals, and with a focus on ranged weapons. Boy, do the weapons feel damn good to fire, though. There's not THAT much loot compared to what we're used to, but because of the turn based combat system each upgrade and variation feels meaningful, and substantial. There are many of fun builds you can do, from a hacker that can turn all sentries and mechs against its enemies, and my personal favorite: an axe murderer that none of the enemies are capable of hitting because his Dodge skill is so high he sprints through bullets, grenades, and other explosions like it was dust, and I just keep coming back to try more.Oh, and, this game is hard. Like, REALLY hard. Don't let Easy mode fool you.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this game a lot of praise.It's been so long since a roguelike has hooked me like Jupiter Hell has! In it's Early Access debut, it already had a lot to offer with various classes, weapons, enemy types and level paths.  Now that it has fully released, the game is true roguelike gem. Where the game truly shines is in it's mechanics. It uses an easy to understand cover mechanic that, along with enemy knowledge and experience, can really be used to your advantage to put you in control of how to approach each room and situation.This roguelike also does a fantastic job at walking a fine line between accessibility and depth.  This roguelike is not bloated with a ton of obscure commands and systems, but has plenty of fun variety and tactical decisions in each playthrough.  I think both newcomers AND veterans of this genre will absolutely enjoy this game.If you are a roguelike fan, or even mildly interested in a turn-based, Doom-like tactical game, then you owe it to yourself to give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great roguelike game and a proper successor of DoomRL which is my favorite game in the genre. Glad that ChaosForge finally released a commercial product and I'm really happy to support their work.Jupiter Hell is simple enough to just pick up and play, no requirement of memorizing a huge amount of shortcuts(game plays great even on controller), systems and mechanics are self explanatory. Build possibilities are diverse and offer different playstyles giving you varied expirience every run. Challenge modes are fun and completing the badges(which is in my opinion one of the coolest features of Jupiter and DoomRL even though it can be compared to regular achievments) for bragging rights will keep you replaying the game for a long time.Hopefully devs will keep up with releasing new updates and deliver on their roadmap promises.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent! This game instantly became my No.1 'go to game'. Sometimes I just want a quick game of something that isn't heavily immersive graphically. Being Rogue-like, when you're dead you're dead but this game makes me launch in again as fast as I can. The rogue-like map randomisation keeps every moment fresh so there's no running over the same old ground. The graphics are visually rewarding without being intrusive or distracting which is what you want when you're in play mode. I'm giving this 10/10 because HELL! What do want for under $10! Nice!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I knew when the DoomRL folks announced this as their retake, it would be a very solid take.So far, 22 hours in, ive managed a few wins, but they've taken what was a good rogue style game, and turned it into a very good one I enjoy despite the crud they had.JH is hard, even on easy. It will kick you down the stairs. But it fairly does so. (Outside Medusa's, those Bleepers can eat a BFG.)The game very heavily focuses on cover and tactical positioning. Its easy to pick up, hard to master, and the game feels so very satisfying when you pull it off. Every main area has its core area, or you can diverse off a side path for certain rewards. (And they cater to certain styles in each split.) Then recenter back on things.You have melee, rocket launchers, pistols, smgs, shotguns, rifles, automatics, and more. Its a testament to the design that rather than there being one clear 'you get this' in a run, theres always options and trade-offs for something.  An example: An advanced variant may have some strong specials, but you lose out of needed slots for other boosts. You may get a rare item, and need to level it up, but at the cost of it being temporarily weaker now where you got it. I heartily recommend this game. Its fun. Im bad at it, and 97% of the time, my deaths are 'ah well, i can do better next time.' and my wins are either 'holy bleep, i won?' and 'That was a superb run.' The variance changes each time in a good way.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I just entered Europa (which I think is like..chapter 2?)  absolutely a riot of a game.  Hillarious Doom and Duke3D memes, Excellent voice actor.  Wish the music would cycle around the playlist more.  If I'm complaining about the soundtrack cycle rather than the soundtrack itself, that tells you everything you need to know about this awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: In many roguelikes, a hefty amount of the combat amounts to mashing your face against the rank and file enemies, reducing it to little more than a gear/build check for non-elite fights. In Jupiter Hell, there's not an endless volume of foes, but health and resources are scarce enough that every grunt matters, and every shot must be taken strategically.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when he was just a little tiny DoomRL . . . My baby has finally grown up!Winning a melee only run was the best fun I've had this year!Gamepad controls make sense and are easy to remember, skill system is flexible and easy to get the hang of, getting unique equipment actually makes you feel like a badass most of the time, heavy metal soundtrack, graphics are pretty detailed for a rogue-like, and whenever I've had my ass handed to me, I knew it was my fault . . . and that makes the wins even sweeter . . . and so much more.Kudos to the team, very well done!11/10, would "Clean-up on aisle f**kface!" again
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game you really want to like. The engine is smooth, the graphics solid and it plays really well on a controller. But the more more you play, the more you realize that as talented as the dev team is, they really need a game designer just as talented. There is so much wasted potential here. Uninteresting classes with tons of useless choices, cookie cutter weapons, no interesting items opening up alternative tactics, etc.Every game follows the same anticlimactic path - you slowly ramp up power, hoping that rng smiles and gives you one weapon worth a ♥♥♥♥. Defense is quickly outpaced by monster progression, so finding a decent weapon is really the only thing that matters. But mostly it's just cheap stupid deaths and when you do win, you realize it was so totally about dumb luck that even that feels cheap.In the hands of someone that really understands how to create meaningful choices and build interesting progression, this could be an amazing game. As it is, it's more like fast food - addictive and pleasing in the moment, but ultimately unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Loads of fun.  I backed this via Kickstarter and I've been waiting for it to be released.  It's in early release now and it's pretty solid.  Played a few levels and I've had no issues thus far.  Great soundtrack, graphics are awesome, and the gameplay is addictive.  I love rogue likes and strategy games, and this game has both.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a Classic Roguelike (top down, turn based, tile based, no meta) heavilly inspired by the old DOOM games.Its focus lies mostly on ranged combat and positioning. The ammount of active abilities you have is limited, the game focuses more on weapon selection and passive skill choice on level ups, though there is the ocasional active ability you can aquire.It has 3 character classes, with each having a mriad of way of being built and combined with all the weapon types in the game, there's plenty of variety in how you build your character.The path throught the game is mostly linear, with the possibility of taking different branches as you go through the game. There is no backtracking and no time/hunger mechanic.In addition to the main gamemode the game also features a TON of challenge and trial runs which change the rules of how you play the game. (Wanna main the rocket launcher? There's a run for that. Shotguns only run? Yep, there's one). These are unlocked by earning medal for reaching certain milestones in the game.Its is overall an excelent game for those who like Classic Roguelikes. Its is plenty hard, so even those people should probably start on normal difficulty until they get the gist of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the tightest, cleanest, most elegant rogue-likes ever. Maybe the best cover mechanics of any game ever? UI is wonderfully simple. A good selection of build archetypes centered around "master level" skills and a wide array of other skills and customizations for gear mean you can really create almost any play style you want. Great value for the money here.

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical turn based rogue-like in a Doom universe.They managed to give it a nice top down shooter feel. The real challenge is in positioning and finding the right skill build that will allow you to access the end boss which is, on max difficulty, quite a challenge - especially the mob are plenty and incredibly hurtful on the last levels.The single negative I found was chapter 1 who gets really repetitive, is quite long and doesn't have gear you will stick with. Actually, you can skip it once some of the numerous new modes unlocked but I really felt I needed all the leveling I could get.That put aside it really feels good to launch a run. You can play it casual or tryhard (difficulty settings are well made, with a great difficulty progression inside each one), it has plenty of options and even 3 classes with really different playstyles. I've spent 43 hours with this and I only sticked with the Marine (others are Scout and Tech). It is full of content, yet really polished. Bravo!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A turn-based tactical shooter roguelike is not something I expected to understand right away, but Jupiter Hell's welcoming learning curve makes accessible to anyone looking for a nice change of pace in the genre.  There are a multitude of different strategical approaches to each floor that lead to victory.  A bangin' rock soundtrack set to a dark and leering atmosphere create a familiar tone found in more popular titles, but in an exciting new way.  It rocks!  I stink at it, and I love it!!

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a modern kickstarted sci-fi spin on the old Hack/Rogue genre of games.  You play a sci-fi 90's action hero diving through "dungeons" in space killing various enemies, looting, and seeing how far you can go before you die.  Just like Hack in the 1980's.  It's not the 1980's anymore. And this is a difficult review to write.  It's easy to write a review when it's obvious the product is unnaceptable, doesn't work or is just woefully bad quality.  It's much harder to tell gamers not to bother with something for less objective reasons.  From a technical basis, while some of the game assets aren't exactly award winning, it gets a pass, with 4K graphics, polished visuals (but really ugly pixel menus), smooth controls, the game "works" from a "can this be played?" perspective.Another important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a key design defect (as I see it) that makes this too difficult to recommend.By design, this game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.While that's the intent of the game design, as you do repetitive "runs" through the samey procgen levels again and again, this adds less value to the experience than the developer doing their job and creating a completable narrative, even as an addon/game mode to the game.  Because this is absent, the overall experience with the game becomes shallow very quickly.  I know that was the intention of the game, but I feel like it's a bad idea, and subjectively of me, I think that if they had made this into a content driven game instead of relying on procgen to do their jobs for them, this could have easily been a AAA tier smash hit. So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Jupiter Hell has the cash grab price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Lethal Company", "Project Zomboid" or "Kingdom Come Deliverance".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: It would be reductive to call Jupiter Hell simply a modernized version of DoomRL. I think it started out that way (and it's generally the same folks that made that excellent roguelike adaptation of Doom). Plus, calling it that was a smart move for a pretty successful kickstarter campaign and run in Early Access. I've put hundreds of hours into DoomRL over the years. It may not be my favourite roguelike, but it's easily in the top 10. I did back this on Kickstarter but mostly to support the devs. I've dipped in and out of Jupiter Hell over the years, but I'd say the bulk of my time with the game has been spent after the recent Abbatoir update. At this point, I think this game has probably well surpassed what DoomRL could ever hope to accomplish.DoomRL was a tremendous distillation of the ~vibe~ of Doom in roguelike form. That's not to say you're running and gunning everywhere (though you are generally shooting a lot of people, places, and things). It was a deeply tactical and tactile affair. Having to manually reload the shotgun after every shot felt like the right move for a roguelike audience. Every action had a heft to it. Every firefight required at least a bit of careful thought. Eventually you'd get enough gear to start steamrolling through most trash mobs only to over-extend and get smoked by an ambush or cyberdemon. As the game was using ASCII graphics, everything was super destructible, too. With enough rockets, you could solve a lot of problems.Jupiter Hell mostly carried that forward, but moving into a 3D space, you couldn't just demolish every wall. They also added barks and one-liners to the protagonist (something you can turn off in the settings - which I did, very quickly). Environments in Early Access felt a little samey to start with. There are three different classes (Marine, Scout, and Technician) you can choose from, each with their own skill trees. I feel like a lot of work has been done building out the range of items that can be found in the game and the options for tinkering with your gear. Figuring out how to build a nearly-invincible-when-in-cover technician or an almost-unkillable melee-focused marine has been deeply satisfying. There's a greater variety of enemies and environments that have been added over time. All of this adds some much-needed variation - especially for the early stages of the game.There's just more to chew on than what I encountered in early access: more interesting decisions, more interesting loadouts, it absolutely has its hooks in the sicko theorycrafting part of my brain and unlike some other roguelikes, the runway from conceptualizing to actual execution is much shorter. Half the time, my harebrained schemes are damn near viable from the jump and only require an extra run or two to get a little further than before. The true test will be when I stop messing around and actually try to press deeper into the dungeon (instead of just stress testing where the limits are) but even in the tinkering phase, I'm having a great time. Runs well on the deck, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays fast to the point you forget it's turn-based. Nice throwback to over-the-top action hero tropes from old school games like Duke Nukem. There were a few moments I ran back down a hallway for cover while being chased + fired upon, and due to distance from enemies which = dodge % the whole thing felt surprisingly cinematic. Pretty engaging overall. Lost an hour and a half on one run and didn't even notice until I died. $10 for this? Great deal. Only negative thing is the music. While I've not gotten too far, the beginning soundtrack is always the same. You'll notice it sooner than later in a genre where repetition is a core feature. More music variety would go FAR.

_childDocuments_.review: Was a big fan of DoomRL but never terribly good at it, and didn't care to get good at it beyond a certain point - found I took to Jupiter Hell much better and completed the standard difficulty on my first or second run - hard mode was then appropriately challenging enough that it took a good dozen+ tries to get a win on, and felt satisfying to do so.Already in a pretty good state for EA and didn't run into any bugs that I can recall, and had fun trying out the variety of skills to work out how I liked to play (akimbo revolvers 4coolness points) - that was before the recent updates that have added the berserker and the new master skills - so will no doubt be sinking another 20 hours in the future to play around with those.One thing that I highly recommend this for: I can play it from in bed with a gamepad, and in fact prefer to use gamepad over M+KB, which is always a big plus for me in roguelikes - that and the fact that it's easy to jump into for a quick run, with most wins only taking 1-1.5 hrs tops.A bit niche of a title, but a tight package to those it will appeal to.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best games I ever played. Jupiter Hell manages to strike the perfect balance between accessibility and complexity. Presentation is stellar, combat is fun from the get go, but you will have to learn the mechanics if you want to be successful.Replayability is great, your first win is just the beginning of the journey. Each game poses a new challenge. Levels are procedually generated, there are mutually exclusive side quests, a huge variety of unique items only a small selection of will be possible to get in any run, three character classes with multiple master traits.All too often your undoing is forgetting that this is a turn based game. Jupiter Hell can feel like an action game, triggering "Fight or Flight" reflexes. More than once I died with an inventory filled with stuff that could easily have saved me if I had kept a cool head.Jupiter Hell has a metagame too. There are a lot of different challenges and trials, many of them requiring mastering a particular aspect of the game. Completing challenges earns you military ranks. Some of the harder challenges are tied to a specific rank.Currently Jupiter Hell is my second most played game on steam and I still haven't explored many of the possible playstyles.By the way, the game is still being worked upon and is getting regular updates. I think the developers are trying to make this the best game they possibly can.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's somewhat bare bones but the core gameplay is polished, graphics are nice, guns sound chunky and environments varied. The enemies are faithfully 'inspired' by doom and satisfying to blow away.it's also good having different (more risky) routes for rarer drops and to add some variety for runs.I don't necessarily agree with the developer that adding some form of permanent progression is a 'grindgate' they wanted to avoid, as roguelikes have unavoidable grind built into them due to learning the game, the RNG or bad luck.Hopefully more is added to the game in time as it's definitely worth supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you every feel a void in your chest? The desperate and irresistible need to be absolutely trounced by demons and zombies in some strange RPG-rogue-like-space-chess? It's a good thing we've got Jupiter Hell to scratch that particular itch!Become Earth's last hope and defense while you desperately attempt to hold on to your sanity. In Juptier Hell you'll take on the role of a space soldier, collecting guns and ammo, killing baddies, and leveling up. Procedurally-generated levels will encourage you to develop situational tactics and keep you guessing as the baddies get smarter every level. Differing paths, structures, and sections add a flavor of diversity which can make each run feel like a different base. With a spectrum of classes and difficulty levels there's even more variety for each players individual play style and needs.Each update the Devs are making both visual and behind-the-scene's improvements.Get this in your inventory  and run with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is an absolutely amazing "rogue-like" game. It is said to be a successor of DRL in 3d graphics, so I expected it to be very much like DRL. The idea and game spirit is that of DRL indeed. However, to my pleasant surprize, the gameplay is different. The game mechanics is very well thought through. Enemy encounters are not reduced to just blasting your way through, they are about constantly assessing the battlefield and making tactical decisions using available weapons/items, environment, and enemy behavior patterns against them. The game is hard and unforgiving, it takes some time to learn the tricks. But it immensely satisfying to get the first win. And this only the start -- even at this early access stage where lots of features are still to be added,  the replayability is great. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: i don't get it.  aside from not being very fun, this game tries to ride the nostalgia wave a little too hard.  keyboard aiming?  WHY?  there are a few reasons for the first 90s FPSes not using mice (not everyone had a mouse since windows had not become popular, the shooters were not 3D, etc) and none of them apply and adding an inconvenience as flavor seems silly; I might have not gotten a refund had this game allowed mouse control.  Running this game on a laptop makes control annoying since laptop keys are small and shallow; this is not a demanding game, therefore, you can't make the excuse that folks would be playing on desktops anyway.    The curved screen look?  WHY?  Curved monitors were a bad thing, the curve distorted the image and made it difficult to see the corners if sitting close.  Pseudographics for health/energy bars?  I mean there are graphics in the game, this showy retro thing is shallow and annoying.  Beyond that, it's difficult to see what's happening, the first levels are too easy (making replay a chore) and it's just... i don't know... not fun at all.  i played doom in the early nineties and it was a hell of a lot more fun than this.  with such a variety of tactical shooters available, i don't see why anyone would pick this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a game that requires a little introduction. First of all, this is a turn-based roguelike that follows very closely in the footsteps of the original Rogue. The map, the inventory, the combat, the random generation, and the fact that you carry over *zero* progression between runs is the way Jupiter Hell rolls. Personally I don’t have a chip on my shoulder about all the recent “roguelites” that are flooding storefronts, but I am having a hell of a time with Jupiter Hell. The quality on display here is no surprise as developer Kornel Kisielewicz has essentially been making this game since 2002.The story, level, and enemy design is heavily influenced by DOOM. You are a space marine (or a scout or an engineer) trapped in a space facility where ♥♥♥♥♥ gone awry. With little introduction you just have to start blasting your way through the facility trying to survive. At first glance Jupiter Hell may look like another isometric shooter, but it’s actually turn based. Enemies don’t move or attack unless you move giving you time to assess every situation. When you are just clearing rooms, however, the animation is so smooth that it almost looks like you’re moving in real time.There’s a cover system that let’s you shoot around corners while staying safe, which makes combat more strategic. The loot varies from armor pick ups, tons of weapons, grenades, and other various supplies. Enemies range from melee demons, fire throwing demons, and other solider who have gone rogue. Plus each starting class has their own list of perks and abilities. It’s quite a complete package if you’re itching for some authentic roguelike action or you want to spray, and rock out to, some heavy metal.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Doom back in the day, and also a fan of turn based roguelike games, I was really excited to try this out. Unfortunately I just couldn’t get into it. It took me a while to figure out why.When I think of Doom I think of demons right up in your face being carved apart with a chainsaw. I think about frantic paced exciting action, running away from fights at low health only to come back again and kick some A. While this game makes a valiant attempt to recapture that feeling, I think it ultimately fails in what it is trying to achieve.Where this game succeeds is in the voice acting and in the music. However where it fails hard is in the presentation. The game screen is so zoomed out you feel completely detached from what is happening on screen. Everything is dark and underwhelming. Your character looks the same as all the enemies. The camera never moves from a fixed perspective.As a result of this, the game fails to take advantage of the rag doll physics, lighting effects, giblet effects etc that have been built into the game. When you fire a shotgun into a demon at point blank range and see it explode, it should be exciting. Instead it just feels underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good - I like audiovisuals, atmosphere, design and gameplay. Solid roguelike with three distinct classes each offering multiple valid builds. The loot is interesting too. Props for authors for balancing the game well enough, so it offers good level of challenge - the game can get very difficult especially on Hard and onwards. Medium is much more forgiving, but still changing.There are various modes, but I personally enjoyed main campaign on Hard/Medium and 'Endless dungeon' - I hope the authors give some polish to the latter in the future, because I think there is some potential there. Content wrapped as Sci-Fi on a distant planet filled with demonic presence which needs to taken care of.I rank the title as 8+/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is great, thinky fun, yet still retains its brutal roots in DOOM theme. There's lots of great tactical decision making about what class, upgrades, and guns you choose depending on your playstyle and objectives for a run. I always keep coming back for more to experiment with and there's always something new to experience here.The graphics are amazing for a traditional roguelike and you can really tell the amount of optimization and coding effort that went into the game. JH sets the standard for other traditional roguelikes to follow from an artistic standpoint and it stands heads and shoulders above the rest in its part of the rogue-game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I uh, I gave it a shot. I know I haven't played enough to warrant a full review, but at least I can leave my reason for my refund request here.On my second try after getting killed due to being overzealous with my medpacks, I finished the first level, and took the elevator to the next map.Right outside the second level's start, I found myself on a T intersection with enemies pouring out of every single door. I shot a few with the two weapons I had with me, all the while running trying to find a little cover. There were demons in every direction I ran to, catching me in an alley with enemies just going to town on me from both ends. I used all I had on me, but unfortunately, it was a losing situation. I doubt there would have been anything that I, now or 50 game hours from now, would have been able to do to salvage that encounter. Now imagine this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ happening at the tail end of a run.The reason I purchased Jupiter Hell was because I wanted to play a turn based roguelike game that isn't banking on being extremely difficult and unfair. This is the reason I tried this one and not The Pit, Quasimorph, Qud, or any of the alternatives, and well, I guess this game just tries as hard to be "hardcore" as them, because I am absolutely not going to give my time to a game that on the very second level has demonstrated to have this little interest in respecting it. _childDocuments_.review: Good Rogue-like (no real cross run progression), that is set in a doom type universe. There are 3 "classes" each with a different perk tree with a few cross over perks between them. Mechanics in the Jupiter Hell are typical for an over the top tactical game with cover and line of sight implemented well. Weapons and armor have set values depending on type and then have a random rarity that goes from common to unique, additionally there are two gear slots that can also contain things to help build your character. Difficulty on normal seems appropriate though some builds seem to be vastly more powerful than others. That being said I feel like there should be more perks available for each class, which would allow for more builds. Overall I give it a 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review games but..As a spawn of the 80's and a person with a discerning budget adequate for indie games I quickly fell in love with Kisielewicz's interpretation of DOOM as a Roguelike, and have been following his work ever since. I've been a lurking supporter of ChaosForge since the early days of the beta on ITCH.IO and payed for this game twice on ITCH.IO and steam and  I tell you, it was worth every penny to be a part of such an amazing game and would do it again because this game is so well done for the price. This game is punishing yet enjoyable, to a degree you will loose time and burn food on the stove as if it wasn't an auto-pause style game. If you enjoy challenges and a fan of tactical top-down shooters with a DOOM style aesthetic, you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: DoomRL/A Doom themed roguelikeOne completion on Easy, 1 Angel of Shotgunnery completion on Normal, 1 Angel of Vampirism completion on Normal, one Haste Trial completion on normal, 128 deaths to those 4 wins.- Great classic roguelike gameplay, complete with no meta progression, punishing overconfidence, and needing to learn to actually progress, with a bit of RNG that occasionally lets you do more than you normally could. (I definitely would have died in my Vampirism run if I hadn't gotten a Wavesplitter early).- Ingame supported ways to not go for the same build every time: Random/Fated has been really nice for keeping me from just trying to go Gun Kata Scout every run. If this option wasn't there, sure I could just generate some random numbers somehow and try to follow that, but I know myself well enough that I know I wouldn't do that.- You can just quit out of a run at any time and resume it later.- Unless you're saving your run summaries somewhere, there's no way (currently that I know of) to see what equipment and skill build you went on your runs. You also can't seem to tell if you were doing some challenge on the run.- The slightly tilted camera angle is a bit awkward for me, and I would really prefer it to be head on.- It's difficult to tell exactly how much cover is doing for you/you can't see how high of a chance the enemy has to hit you. I think the developer has said they're looking into this, so fingers crossed.- The game once told me to stop watching porn when I alt-tabbed for a while.- ASCII mode is a real blast from the pastI love this game even though I'm terrible at it. Even though there's only 3 classes and no real story to speak of, it doesn't feel stale.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely satisfying Turn Based with some roguelike elements. The fluidity of the controls seamlessly blends TBS combat with exploration and movement. Controls are exactly how you would want them, akin to your traditional TBS. Re-bound my half-keyboard to have all the actions on it so I can play 1 handed FeelsGoodMan (new keybinds should be shown in UI, quick fix). The brutal feel of combat where boxes scatter or limbs fly gives a Crusader: No Regret vibes where you (or your enemies) inflict massive damage to each other and the environment. Graphics and theme are extremely polished and the theme definitely has some strong Doom vibes. Re-playability seems extremely high and there's numerous biomes to keep the areas fresh. The random encounters, tasks, and sidenotes actually give you mini-missions that could improve your run. Chest loot is exciting to find, always looking for that next piece of loot. Strongly recommend the game in it's current state. IMO, can only get better from here with more seeds, biomes, loot, classes and other procedural generation. Will update as I get a better feel, but I will definitely be logging some hours into this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phantastic modern incarnation of a traditional Roguelike. It plays so well with a controller, which is a refreshing way to play such a game from a comfortable position further away from the screen. The size of the HUD elements and the adjustable map zoom accomodate this well. The aesthetics of the interface hits all the the right tastebuds for me, as a kid from of the 80's and 90's. I remember curved CRT screens and that very font from old textfiles. If you like old-school Quake and Doom, you will appreciate some content referencing those games, such as keycards, armor and health orbs. The gameplay heavily emphasizes tactics and positioning. The mechanic of cover is most important. Bits of lore is fed to the player via e-mail messages exchanged between staff members of the bases on Jupiter's moons. However the content of these messages are so vague, that I mostly can't make out much sense about what they are trying to tell me. From what I understand, they hint at good loot that can be found in branches, which can enable advanced players to aim for a certain exploration path and character build. The turn based nature allows for relaxing and cautious play. The animation of the turns is so fluid, allowing for faster play in less dangerous situations. You can get into a real rush of killing sprees! Gibbing the enemies feels so satisfying, as well as all the weapon sounds of shooting and reloading. The game is brutally hard, but the typical audience expects that and I like a real challenge. It took me over 30 hours to get my first win on Easy difficulty, even though I have many years of experience with Roguelikes. The game has no metaprogression system unlike several modern Roguelikes, but this adheres more to a traditional Roguelike. The graphics and the lighting are pure eyecandy with highest quality settings on a 4K monitor. Tough I am a passionate Metalhead, I play with the music muted, because the metal soundtrack is too repetitive and generic for my taste. Instead I use quiet playback of some Dark Ambient from outside the game, as this enables me to better hear the enemy noises and I also find it more atmospheric like that. The official Discord community is very friendly and helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this several months after it entered early access, was very dissatisfied with how dumbed down it was compared to it's predecessor, and my complaints were generally dismissed as elitist and premature. If it were any other devloper I would have gotten a refund but I'm a huge fan of DoomRL so I figured I'd leave it on the shelf and hope it got better. It has, but not in the ways it needed to.Go play DoomRL instead. It's so much better, honestly. It's full of unique enemies, weapons, and easter eggs. There's alternate fire modes for weapons and destructible terrain. The gameplay flows more smoothly because you don't have to wait or move one turn at a time and check for enemies, the game lets you move a long distance and only interrupts you if you spot an enemy. It has more interesting achievements that aren't just doing all the challenges on a given difficulty. The special levels are far more interesting with solid themes. It has a better UI that shows your character stats like movement speed and resistances properly. It has better combat balance, instead of limiting your sight range to significantly less than the effective range of half your weapons.The only things this game really has going for it are the graphics. It makes a lot of sacrifices so that it looks nice and can be played more easily with a gamepad. And while the game is pretty for a roguelike, there are better genres to sate that appetite.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Roguelike, keeps the core gameplay simple for a faster paced sort of play, but comes with plenty of build options for the 3 main classes, a variety of gear with different modifiers, and a crafting and modification system to really customise your pew pew to your playstyle. An isometric 3D perspective with explosions and lighting effects should also make it quite approachable for those who like Roguelikes, but dislike ASCII art.A worthy spiritual followup to DoomRL.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: With modern crappy business practices and overall tasteless designs in video games, roguelike genre is at least worth to try, offering endless replayability and a ton of memorable moments with no strings attached. Jupiter Hell is, in my opinion, probably the best way to introduce new players to this amazing genre. Set in the 90's sci-fi fictional universe heavily influenced by original DOOM, Jupiter Hell is quite easy to learn, but is very tricky to fully master with its tactical gameplay and constant decision-making: you have limited inventory slots, you have limited weapon slots, you can take different paths and use different builds on different characters, and all of this , always keeping you on your toes. Luckily, with average  run time of nearly two hours (compare this to my ~60 hours for a golden  ending), you can always start over and try a different approach.The game is visually appealing, with blood splats everywhere, barrels exploding, dead monsters falling off cliffs, and that's accompanied by heavy metal soundtrack. It even has a plot (), what else are you looking for?On the negative side, with such relatively simple graphics, you'll probably expect that this game can be played on low-end video cards (e.g. Intel), but as of March 2020, this is not the case.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun and I would totally get it perhaps if it were on sale.For me, after winning one run, on easy . . .  I was sort of done with this game. And the reason is, you will die often. And, you do learn from your mistakes, but sometimes you don't, like when an enemy hits you for half of your health and your run ends unexpectedly. A run, played carefully for me, takes about 4 hours. There is no metaprogression, and there is no saving, so dying in 2 hours after playing a very well thought out and maximized run just feels completely awful. This genre is super fascinating and fun to play. There is a lot going on, with item use and management. Planning for upgrades and there are quite a few routes to take within each of the 4 biomes to give you very diverse runs. Right now skills feel very specifically tailored to certain guns. I am not encouraged to take rifles or guns that use 7.62 ammo it feels. As someone pointed out, this game really forces you to play defensively. and that can often slow game play down. With that said, there are certain situations where things go downhill quick. for example, using a medkit takes an actiion. and while it is almost always a bad idea to use it during battle, it intuitively feels like the right thing to do even though I have died that way many times.

_childDocuments_.review: So here we finally are, full 1.0 release. It's a hell of a roguelike, combat focused and stripped of a lot of the tedium you'd find in most classic roguelikes. The game looks great, runs great (minus making half the map explode from barrels) and has a ♥♥♥♥ ton of replayability. Which is good cause this game is also balls hard, it took me a good while to beat it on Ultra, but man did it ever feel good. The devs are great, open to communication, and were open to balance suggestions as well as bug fixing throughout early access. If you want a combat focused roguelike with extensive class based skill trees and Diablo like loot dropping look no further.As a side note, and touching on sound design a bit, the hero is voiced by none other than Mark Meer (Commander Shepard) and he is absolutely chewing the scene with his VO as a pseudo Doom Guy. Some might find it cringey, but I love it in the Doom comic sort of cheese-fest it is. It can be safely disabled though if wanted. Music is appropriate and mildly catchy but nothing to write home about, I've swapped it out a few times for a synthwave playlist. Jupiter Hell is a game I picked up a while back on a whim and has become one of my favorite roguelikes of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's Doom the Roguelike. In 3D. That's all it is so far and that's all we ever really needed.It's a roguelike (generated levels with permadeath), with firearms and cover tactics, where you shoot zombies and demons in space. The tactics keep it challenging and the challenge modes and rank progression give you a reason to keep playing it over and over and over.The graphics are great: the "CRT" GUI and general presentation is wonderful, if a bit dark and oddly GPU intensive for a top-down game.The soundtrack is nice: unlike some other reviewers, I really like it especially towards the end.The gameplay is perfect, it plays like a more streamlined DRL, but all the tactical choices are more obviously visible.Clearly, there needs to be some more content added. It's missing some skills (I first beat DRL with a Marine shotgun build, which really isn't possible now with the current skill progressions), there's no levers/traps, it could use some more level branches, the special weapon builds aren't implemented yet (and they better be!), but the core is there enough to completely replace DoomRL as my roguelike of choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Managed my first medium win after about 12 hours I'd say.I really like the different classes and the "ultimate" skills you can work towards with each of them. The game gets brutally hard, but you get a lot stronger throughout the run to tackle the ever increasing difficulty. Loot is not entirely random as some locations drop loot based on your prefered weapon on the run.My #1 tip for progressing further: Running for cover is good! You get a juicy dodge bonus as you run and most enemies don't have excellent ranges so their hit changes as you get distance become noticeably worse.One trick is to not open doors manually but instead destroying them by shooting them from a safer spot. Even the wall right next to a door is better than being exposed and taking a turn to duck into cover. Also getting any of the movement speed skills can allow you to easily kite enemies as long as you have the space. It really helps to be faster if you are walking down a hallway and there is suddenly 6 guys coming your way.It's basically DOOM as a roguelike.The game is hard even on Medium difficulty. You'll die fast if you fight in the open.Note that there's no progression. If you die, you start all over from the beginning with nothing to unlock.I know it's basically DoomRL in a shiny wrapping, but it's a good wrapping.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell got me breaking down psychological barriers about the essence of gaming itself... We must play by the rules of a game, within the designed framework. If you're hesitant to learn new rules, you're hesitant to play a new game. It limits you to only playing games that are very similar to what you already know. If you wanna play games that are interesting and different, you're gonna have to learn new rules, and experiment with different or unfamiliar gameplay elements, and have the mindfulness to know you're not gonna know how to play the game instantly without investing some more time and attention to the experience.Any time and attention you invest in Jupiter Hell, you get rewarded for. There are multiple plateaus of game-knowledge. Every time you break through it's a satisfying confidence boost. But then almost instantly you get to see the next level of the plateau, and have a clear idea of how to get there. There are lots of options that seem overwhelming at first, but just reading through and playing, it all comes together quickly. If that cycle of mastery of mechanics appeals to you, this is a top, top-tier game for that experience. How I see it, Jupiter Hell is more than a game, it's like a toolbox. You are given full control over so many aspects of how you want to play- you can choose your own class, spec, guns, gear, route, and more- all huge varieties- and can build any type of run you want around the playstyle you're feeling for that session. The possibilities have my head spinning, even after 80+ hours played. I've never played anything like it. What's old is new again. If you're into roguelites and strategy games as a whole, and are looking for something fresh, IMMERSIVE and engaging, this is where you wanna start to get a taste of what a traditional roguelike can offer. You just have to be willing to maybe play by some new rules.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent roguelike! Easy to understand with short, yet informative tutorial. Pretty much what turn-based Doom would've been like.I'm honestly struggling to come up with much to say about Jupiter Hell. It's just a solid game all the way through. I have no complaints about much of anything. And all my questions and issues (had a bit of trouble running it in Vulkan) were answered by the developers on Steam forums. I've spent 16 hours in the past 3 days alone playing Jupiter Hell. If you like roguelikes and blasting monsters with a shotgun, then definitely give this game a try! Jupiter Hell is well worth of your time!

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, spooky and tense as hell, this is the game that Doom 3 wanted to be. Every step taken and every door opened could be your last but it never feels unfair, just a chance to try again. Music is appropriate to the setting and will give you the one-more-turns long after you should've gone to bed. The weapons are all satisfying to use and the enemies are interesting and varied. The gibbing effect in particular is glorious.Game is not easy, so if you're new to roguelikes, maybe try DoomRL first as it's free and this game builds on that foundation. It would be nice if you could rename your character ingame but that's a minor gripe.Would rinse and repeat again.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving this game. Normally I would not play games with unforgiving difficulty and perma death, but Jupiter Hell does a good job of ramping things up slowing and starting the game on the easier side. The gradual introduction of enemies and gives you some freedom to see what works and does not work, the perma death keeps you from getting stuck based on earlier mistakes (such as squandering resources early in the game). I was able to beat the game after 30 hours, with my 1st winning play through taking 4 hours. Upping the difficulty adds more enemies with better weapons, and I feel beating the game on easy, felt like it helped a lot for playing medium, and hard.There area a bunch of other games modes to switch things up. At first these are locked, but you can do a play through with only shotguns, do one with only grenade launchers and rocket launchers, as well as a large number of other. These also change the game slightly such as giving you the weapon to start with, and allowing you to convert ammo. There is also an endless more where random levels are generated endlessly, and a area mode where you are in a smaller area and waves of enemies spawn, you get rewards, and move to another area, repeat.Overall the game is pretty tight, allowing a lot of approaches worth trying, and making the focus much more on adapting to the evolving situation. While standing in cover and shooting some lightly armed guards is easy and simple, that changes if some demons hear you and come from the other direction, or maybe the guards have a friend with a grenade launcher who was out of sight. Higher levels have much more going on, with more issues to address.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting one. I'm generally a big roguelike fan, and a HUGE XCOM fan. Somehow, though, this game got old fast.There are a LOT of builds that you can try and what seems like infinite different weapons. At 13 hours, I still feel like I haven't scratched the surface of what's possible in the game (and I haven't beaten it, although I started on hard mode.) But despite that, the core gameplay loop and the graphics just seem to create a boring game. Encounter enemies (or what you think are enemies, based on poor lighting conditions and retro graphics), run behind cover, wait for them to step into the open and shoot them.Overall, I think this game is probably good, but just not for me. There may be a lot of choices in terms of itemization and perks, but the combat feels so straightforward that it makes it much less enjoyable. If you know that going in, I say go for it, but if you're looking for a deep combat experience or good visuals, go elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell might well be my favourite roguelike, but my recommendation* comes with a caveat.What the game offers is a deeply tactical and strategic experience, impeccably balanced and trusting of the player. You are a lone soldier in the familiar theme of 'all hell (literally) has broken loose, in space', but this time on the moons of Jupiter as opposed to, say, the clouds of Venus.The gameplay appears simple at first glance - it is turn-based, you can move in the four cardinal directions (seems limiting at first, but it works), and shoot at zombies, robots and demons. After killing a few of them, you level up and can select a perk. Level up a  times and you can select a 'Master' perk - and this is where things start to get interesting.Each moon has 5 possible paths through it - straight down the middle, or the option of one of three of four side-branches. Every branch has a special objective to discover, and you're rewarded for accomplishing it. Furthermore, weapons and armour found in a side branch have unique bonuses, which at first appear to be only minor, but in combination with perks and the ability to customise weapons and armour through 'modpacks', can become incredibly powerful. In addition to that, exotic and unique items can impart unusual and powerful abilities, if you're lucky enough to find them.But you are  at the mercy of RNG.Even the most overpowered build with the most astonishing luck, a few wrong moves and you're toast. It may be through attrition (you really failed 3 levels ago but didn't realise it), or a moment of hubris leading to a speedy demise; nearly every win or loss can be attributed to the player, and the decisions they make.You will lose a lot. Almost every run. No, you don't unlock a new weapon or gain some permanent bonus,  the permanent bonus of knowledge. As familiarity with the game increases, you learn to exploit its mechanics, how to leverage the RNG to produce an item you need, what the best way to fight a particular type of enemy is. As long as you don't fall to complacency, a win is possible.* So why the caveat? It's addictive. Not in an exploitative way - quite the opposite, but if you have a lot of stuff to do and are easily swayed into  doing it, Jupiter Hell could be that demon in your ear convincing you that it's .

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't look like much on the surface, but once you start playing you come to realise this is an extremely well-designed roguelike. It's hard, certainly, but it's generally fair (at least until you get into the difficulties that are intended to be unfair). It has an absurdly deep strategy pool and steep learning curve for such a seemingly straightforward game, and it has enough game variants and challenge modes to keep things fresh.I should also heap a big helping of praise on the little things, the small design decisions that show the developer really knows their stuff. The tiniest details, things you might not even consciously think of as design choices, are all geared to keep the game flowing and avoid micromanagement.I strongly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a roguelike turn-based strategy game with procedurally generated levels and permadeath. The game is still in Early Access so expect some changes depending on when you are reading this review. The game is fully playable as it is right now according to the developers, which is nice.You start by choosing from three different classes, each with its own buffs. So from the beginning you have a slight selection for the type of gameplay that suits you.Like in may tactical turn-based games, you and the enemies will both be able to take cover behind objects. All of the fighting in this game is done from a distance, because you are firing guns at each other. You have to remember to reload your weapons too, and that's something I forgot often.You will have a limited amount to carry, so you have to decide what to loot from the drops of enemies, usually guns and ammo.There are also spawned items on each floor. There are not many, so you have to use them judiciously. These include med kits, armor, grenades, etc.I have no idea how many levels there are, because I keep dying in all of my attempts so far, even on Easy mode. I am still have a great time though.The game does come with a very good interactive tutorial, which is always appreciated.Currently there are two game modes and four difficulty levels. The game modes are Regular and Challenge. I think there are two more that are currently locked, and will likely unlock with updates in Early Access. Of the four difficulties, I played on Easy, and even that has been a challenge for me. The most difficult setting is locked until you meet certain requirements. Difficulty does not bother me because this is a true roguelike. is the spiritual successor of .This is especially notable for a roguelike, it is so very good. Everything is top-down in view. Some levels are a bit dark and can be hard to see at times.The music is not my cup of tea as it is very repetitive. The sound effects are good, though there's a lot of mature language. So be warned, do not play this game on loud from work, especially in the presence of little children.The game can be fully played with a controller or a keyboard.A little more than 10 minutes of sample gameplay can be found here:The price in Early Access at launch is $25 USD, in my opinion that is a bit too steep. Most roguelikes will cost a lot less. Though the game is quite fun and looks fantastic, so if the price is not a hindrance for you, definitely get it. Otherwise waiting for a sale is a reasonable thing to do as well. is a really good game, even though it's in Early Access. The launch price is a bit high, but I would still recommend it at this high price. It is always nice in these turn-based shooters to be able to take cover, and I really enjoy seeing that here. The gameplay combines the turn-based roguelike and the shooter genres. It is just a lot of fun. Like most other roguelikes, you may have to play and replay to get better. For me this is enjoyable, but for others, I know this can get frustrating.Overall it is a very good game with plenty of replayability.Leaving the price out, I would give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Duum the Roguelike, 3D edition. Did you like the 2D version? I did. This is more of the same. The protagonist isn't as likable as the Dome Marine, and the camera really needs to be made rotatable, but the first is a matter of taste and the second may well end up changed.Overall this is one of the most original and well-made roguelikes so far, and the developer has a clear vision of what the game is meant to be and is laser-focused on getting the job done.
