_childDocuments_.review: With this game nearing release, I figure it's about time I do a review here.  This has come a long way... for context, I was one of the backers on this one.  Normally I avoid Kickstarters like the plague, but I made a very special exception for this.  I'm glad I did, though it has been a LONG wait for it to reach this point.If you're not aware, this is essentially a spiritual sequel to DoomRL.  Like that game, it is very fast paced, and goes far, far away from many traditional roguelike concepts (thankfully, as I hate most of those).  No endless bump combat, no unnecessarily gigantic blob of skills/spells that you'll always cycle through in exactly the same order, and biggest of all (at least for me) no godawful unidentified item garbage.  It's that last bit that originally attracted me to DoomRL in the first place.  Well, that and it was based on Doom.  Duh.What I'm saying here is, if you've played more "traditional" roguelikes and found them to be overly convoluted, irritating, or just bloody stupid in some ways, this might be the one for you. Though it does have its issues nonetheless, but we'll get to that.Like DoomRL, combat is all about positioning, movement, timing, and cover.  As I said above, there's no brainless bump crap here.  If you're not considering all 4 of those concepts there, you're going to get smeared all over the wall.  It's fun, it's exciting, and it's fast paced, and it's a huge part of what makes this game what it is.And considering this game's lineage, it's all about GUNS.  The unusual emphasis on ranged attacks makes the game feel very darned unique when compared to basically any other roguelike out there, barring DoomRL itself, and it's a very nice breath of fresh air.   There are many, MANY weapons to pick from, and they are all good at different things.What's more, as the early access process has progressed, these weapons have become far more interesting.  If you'd seen the game in one of its earlier versions, you probably would have seen that most guns tended to be almost identical.  But not so now.  You'll find all sorts of screwball traits/abilities that your weapons can have, and this makes finding new ones extra exciting.  You'll love finding those glorious purple chests that signify a new and interesting way to obliterate demons.  You can hold only a couple at a time, so deciding what to carry at any given time is important, particularly as new enemies appear later in the game.  Some guns just arent good against some things.  If you've reached that one branch area full of CRI bots (big mech things), well, you better hope you have something that works darned well against armor, or you're in big trouble.  All of these things go for your armor as well, as that too has all sorts of unique traits.What's more, you're going to find all sorts of other items (grenades for instance), and lots of machines to interact with that can do different things, but are limited in how many things they can do at once.  Do you use that construction machine to build an advanced weapon in a particular class, hoping to get some good traits?  Or do you use it to make armor, or maybe a weapon mod?  Choices like this appear frequently, and with the game's very fast pace, there's never much downtime between interesting or exciting moments.There's lots of enemy types as well, though they can seem a little samey in some cases.  It might be neat to see some that have genuine unique abilities, as right now its mostly about their primary attack method, health, possible armor, and so on.  Then again, maybe that's all it needs, I dunno.  One way or another, you still definitely need to get a handle on what each horrid demon/robot/whatever can do.Lots of variety in the levels, too.  There are many floors, and a boatload of branch areas and special zones (which are optional).  Deciding just where to go whenever a choice is given to you is very, very important.  Like that CRI lab I mentioned earlier;  if you go there, you arent getting back out until you've gone all the way through, and that means LOTS of horrible robot things.  Think carefully about your current build before entering.  Same with any other optional zone.  Levels have interesting design too, making them more fun to explore... something I wish a lot of roguelikes would learn to pull off.  Look, I'm tired of the usual "random ultra thin corridors and equally random blocky rooms".  These levels are generated much better than that, and I love that.Also, the game is a visual treat.  Most of the time, I prefer ASCII for roguelikes.  And the reason is twofold:  First, I just like ASCII, but even moreso, most roguelike tilesets are butt-ugly.  Not so here.  Great visuals and overall aesthetic here, fitting the overall theme wonderfully and adding to the satisfaction of the combat, with things flying all over the place when blasted and stuff like that.Where the variety does falter a bit is that there are very few overall classes to pick from. Only a couple, really.  Each one has a great many traits to choose from when levelling up, but still.... it's definitely a weak point in the game.  And the Marine in particular could do with a change... his active skill, Adrenaline, is easily the most boring (low grade heal, and a short term buff).  The others are definitely more interesting, but... yeah, there's very little choice here.  At least each class has tons of build variety within itself.The other thing I'm not too fond of is the way that it handles ammo.  Perhaps you're having a run where you've got a focus on shotguns, right?  You've built one up with some mods, you've chosen skills that support it, and so on.  Well.... too bad the game doesnt tell you that shotgun ammo almost entirely stops spawning once you get past a certain point.  Why?  I have no bloody idea.  Look, I get that the game doesnt want you to just stick with the same couple of guns the whole way, but switching out a weapon for what is often a much WORSE weapon because "oh that type of ammo isnt on these floors, you WILL run out for good, better not use that weapon class anymore" is not exactly satisfying.  It can make progression feel outright backwards at times.  Surely there's a better way to encourage the player to change things up.  This aspect just feels unnecessarily forced.  It's been the #1 thing I dislike about this game from the very start.  It can also make weapons not feel quite as exciting to get as they COULD be.  Sure, that new gun you just got as a reward for beating that special zone is great and all, but... it sure isnt quite as satisfying when you know that its ammo type will stop appearing 3 floors down the line.But hey, that's just one issue, and maybe it wont irritate you as much as it does me.  And the rest of the gameplay more than makes up for it.  Super fast paced yet very tactical, exciting combat that never feels tedious, lots of interesting and tough choices to be made, huge variety in builds, weapons, areas, everything... also did I mention the frequent level-ups and the awesome "master traits"?  Yeah, that's pretty great too.Also, this is FAR more accessible than most turn-based roguelikes.  It isnt permanently set to "nigh impossible" as its only difficulty level.  Like Doom, there are quite a few to pick from.  And the controls/UI ARENT FREAKING TERRIBLE.  Certain OTHER games could learn from that!  You can even play with a controller (and boy am I glad for that one).  Which works wonderfully.  If you're a fan of Doom, if you like fast-paced and tactical games, and if you want something that actually dares to change up the roguelike formula instead of trying to be the 350969034742397th Nethack clone... yeah, get this one.  It's good.  And as of this review, it's nearly done... just a couple of months from full release.  What better time to give it a go?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic roguelike. The core game has you picking one of three classes, each with their own skill tree.  You gain perk points for each level up, and can work towards one 'master' perk that defines your playstyle on that run and requires investment in multiple prior skills.  So far I have had successful runs with a dual wielding pistol and SMG build that fires extra bullets for each shot, and also with a shotgun based build that allowed my shots to pierce and work at a far greater range than you would expect.The base game mode is a relatively lengthy campaign that I would estimate lasts around 4 hours on average, although far quicker times are possible.  Each of the four main zones that you pass through consecutively have a number of alternative paths with their own themes, enemies and drops, and terminals dotted throughout the levels give you hints regarding what you are likely to find if you decide to go down one of the alternative paths.  This, once you get familiar with the possible routes, allows you to influence the rng and find the equipment that you actually need.  There is also a system in place where, by using, for example, a pistol extensively during your run, you make it more likely that you will get better pistols going forward.As you play, you unlock medals and ranks, and these unlock further difficulties, challenges and trials.  Challenges restrict your character in some way, for example giving you access to only 4 inventory slots.  Trials alter the game substantially; the Haste trial greatly reduces the number of floors that you need to pass through and alters the drop tables and XP to compensate,  Arena makes you face waves of respawning enemies, etc.  This all means that replayability is very high, and as the core experience is both satisfying and challenging, I can see myself playing the game for a long time to come.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Frickin' good time. Evokes memories of playing Doom back in the day and all the tension and discoveries in there... Really dig the advancement system and the badges/promotions you can complete over multiple playthroughs.  Soundtrack slaps, more heavy music reminiscent of those days... And maybe most importantly the devs haven't left it so you have a self-destruct key adjacent to your movement that can perma-kill you any time if you misclick.  I will recommend virtually anything that hasn't wasted ten years leaving Windows key enabled when it leads to an instant loss, so bonus. Project Zomboid devs could learn from these guys.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the plans and development for this game from even before the Kickstarter (and consequently, from before the moment Zenimax/Bethesda were required by law to protect their trademarks), and it has evolved into something so much more than just "Trademark-Friendly D**m The Roguelike" over that time. The story, told through emails left on long-forgotten access terminals strewn across the various satellites of Jupiter, is exactly as invasive as it needs to be: not at all. And that suits Jupiter Hell as a game down to the last, since everybody on this page likely remembers the slow crawls of text that the original D**m series would paste to the screen at the end of each episode. The gameplay is as fast or as slow as you need it to be. You can surge forward recklessly, dashing from cover to cover as you frantically search for an access terminal to lift a Lockdown. You can hunker down and enjoy a nice hot cup of coffee as you plan how to get past a squadron of high-powered security robots with only a crowbar, ten health, and a single red keycard.All in all, this game truly is the successor to "D**m, The Roguelike" that it always set out to be. Now if you don't mind, I've gotta find a way to Europa...

_childDocuments_.review: When I first got this game, I was reluctant.This was awhile ago, when the reviews were kind of mixed as they suggested "it's good, but basically just a graphically improved DRL which is free."I tried DRL, I liked it, but the screenshots here still showed a bit more and figured what the hell, give Chaos Forge some money to help them out, I've already sunk an unhealthy amount of hours into DCSS (another of their free classics).Since then, Jupiter Hell has with each new update become bigger and more amazing. Far more diversified weapons and enemies than D**M ever did, and in a way that feels more balanced too. Honestly one of the best of these kinds of roguelikes I've played, and the only one that scratches a certain kind of itch for a sci-fi shooty roguelike that games like Cogmind left unsatisfied. If you wanted something that is kind of like doom, but more of an rpg (you level up and get skills and all that jazz) and turn based, buy this. It's great, I'm sure it won't get worse, and we all know games tend to go up in price when they leave early access ;)

_childDocuments_.review: ** A letter of love for both DOOM and the true classic Roguelike genre **The game might sound like something unbelievable : taking a universe like DOOM, nervous, aggressive, fast-paced, and applying to it a turn-based gameplay implying strategy to avoid an unforgiving permadeath. These devs did it, and they did it well :Jupiter Hell offers the action and the bloody massacre someone would expect from a game like doom as its gameplay, visuals and also musics are immersive enough to get in action and take quick decisions.At first, you would obviously die, like a lot. Since like any traditional rogue-like, Jupiter Hell is not an easy game. Though unlike most of roguelike, the choice of difficulty can offer you the choice to just have fun running around and shooting as in lowest difficulty, the game would allow you to make mistakes in your decisions and choices.The game also offers three classes which are well balanced with their own resource to manage, activable powers and passive abilities. - Marine, focused on direct attack- Scout, focused on backstab and escape- Technician, focused on bulky stratsAlso, since we're playing a rpg, you'll have a system of leveling to unlock new traits to spice up the gameplay with new passive or activable abilities, combined with an important point of the gameplay : the gear.Maybe it's the only moment of the game in which the pacing might slow down but for the good sake as it would often occur after the gunfight when the area is cleared and all the time required to explore, think and relax is available, to be ready until the next level.And when the classic gameplay might feel too much, you can still enjoy the game with other original way of playing with the challenges or trials the game offers.Cherry on the top : if despite all the points mentionned, you are still not doubtful about the game or its content, you can still embrace the community which is active, fair, welcoming in addition to the dev team whose always listening at their players and modders.AND YES, I said modders : the game also provides a workshop with mods so you could add your own content in the game both in its gameplay and visual.In conclusion, Jupiter Hell is pleasant experience, a game which worth its price and deserves to be known and tried. If you love DOOM and love Classic Rogue-like games, this is for me a must play for the hommage it represents and the content it offers. And if you're a novice in rogue-like, this game is fair enough for a good introduction to the genre.Enjoy !

_childDocuments_.review: I've played quite a few rougelikes in my day. This has to be one of the best ones to come out this year. Great soundtrack. Great play style. The way the game is set up and controls makes you critically think about your position and where you want to be. It's DOOM with out the running and gunning. It's DOOM with critical thinking behind it...oh what am I saying it's DOOMrl and AliensRl's little love child!

_childDocuments_.review: Update:  So, after a hiatus, I jumped back in on Steam Deck.  There are still some issues, but they aren't too terrible. Chalk it up to me not remembering the problems or there were some improvements with steam/game software--I'll list the Steam Deck issues below.Upon saving, the game will freeze (either a salt and pepper screen or just freeze what was on screen, audio will still play). Don't fret!  Just hit the "Steam" button and exit game, load back up and continue. I did this 4 times yesterday and it always loaded up where I left off. Not perfect, but not a huge issue.When you complete a world (Callisto, Europa, Io, Dante), the game will go to black screen and act like it is frozen but audio still plays. As soon as I hit the "Steam" button, my character would say something then I would load in on the screen.  Minor issue.An issue that I had previously that I did not test was when the Steam Deck goes to sleep while the game is running or the game is manually closed while the game is running. I am going to assume this is a still a problem, I play plugged in and my settings give me a good 20 minutes so I never organically tested this and was on a rip, so I didn't take a break.  I'll recommend saving and manually exiting the game if you plan on walking away for bit, don't manually put your Deck to sleep while the game is running.I believe there is now a disclaimer on this title for the issues described above, which is good. Still 100% like this game as a title for Deck as the issues are completely avoidable, but they are absolutely devastating if you aren't aware of them and lose your progress because of those issues, so that said, I keep by the motto of save often.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original:  Bought for Steam Deck, mostly play on desktop.It plays very nicely on Steam Deck but when saving, the screen goes grey. Sometimes it will become unplayable if the screen gets turned off/back on or goes to sleep.So, if you play on Steam Deck, save and exit often.  You'll have to force quit the game and reload save, but its better than losing progress.  If this issue gets resolved, I'd be ecstatic, because its truly a great Steam Deck title and I'd rather play this in bed vs at my desktop.

_childDocuments_.review: It does what's advertised very well, the cover-based combat actually works, nothing is unbalanced, it flows very quickly, it's hard enough and the gameplay styles are pretty different. Possible cons are that it's attrition-based (you never get free heals after combat), isn't consumable-focused like classic roguelikes But that's mostly preference, and I prefer it this way, and I heard a year of content is on the way. Also doesn't have as many build choices as DCSS or StS, but  more than GKH.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is essentially if DOOM was a traditional rogue-like, it's a very approachable modern rogue-like and so far I only have two issues which are noted below.  Aside from these minor issues I'm really enjoying the game and I look forward to beating it eventually.1) PLEASE make it to where the numpad and enter on the numpad can be used to navigate all menus, I remapped the UI controls to be able to use the numpad to navigate menus but I can't rebind it to where I can use the enter key on the numpad so I have to awkwardly move from the numpad to my keyboard enter key when I want to select something.  This should be a very easy fix and I hope it comes soon, being able to use your arrow keys OR numpad should be standard in all rogue-likes.2) The game has really good graphics for a rogue-like considering ASCII was the standard for a long time and I really do appreciate the effort that went into it, but I would appreciate some mode to help make it easier to look at for people with substandard vision, whether that means introducing an ASCII mode or adding some kind of slight highlight to make it quick and easy to spot and differentiate your character and enemies.  While the graphics are nice, sometimes I find it hard to spot my character, especially when playing on a laptop, it's almost unplayable for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the reviews already hit this on the head.It's a good game.It's an enjoyable game.But is it not a great game.Visually great, writing does the job it set out to do.It is a top down Doom without the complexity or skill cap of Doom.There isn't a lot of variance and a lot of the game relies on RNG.Which means on higher difficulties RNG begins to drain away from player agency.The result is a very shallow strategy game. Is there strategy? Sure.Is it complex or a major part of the game? No.I'd say this is a good get at $10-$15, but beyond that you really have to have a love for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For every thing Jupiter Hell does right, it does three things wrong... And yet, you want to play as this egocentric manly man in quest of uncovering the truth behind what happened to his ship, this guy that will not stop spewing obscenities and dropping the F bomb whenever he feels like it lol.This is a tactical roguelike RPG, and if I say Roguelike, you'd think: "I'm gonna die a lot, huh?"... But no, actually the game is only PART-roguelike. Let me explain; when you die it's permanent, however unlike roguelikes you usually play, your progression DOESN'T carry over! This in part (I think?) is balanced out by the fact that the game is very extremely easy, even on Hard mode. You play as a nameless rambo whose ship collided with another, and upon inspecting it, he finds himself fighting hordes of undead, Doom demons, parasite-infested marines and *insert any other sci fi horror creature you can think of*. He climbs up elevators to reach new areas and before doing that, he'd have to fight a boss for each area. The game follows a "crypt of the necrodancer" paradigm, in which every time you move to a direction (or perform any action really), the enemy AI also does the same thing and that's the tactical side of it. Don't worry, however, because the AI controlled unit are such trash that you will breeze through the game like it's nothing. All you have to do is carry around healthkits and prioritize getting Keycards; now these give you an edge on the map because they allows you access to unique upgrades available if you could hack into terminals! Then it's a matter of getting into cover, and waiting for an opportunity to empty up your machine gun unto the oblivious creatures that come through the corridor... It's very fun to see that happen. When you level up, prioritize grabbing upgrades that directly affect your "damage in a row" counter and you're good to go. Although the game is easy, the challenges are NOT! And although doing them over and over again might sound addicting, it's the graphics of the game and the annoying looping soundtrack that actually pose a problem. The graphics are very dated for a modern game, and the main character's movements seem forced and abnormal. The creatures are also badly designed and at some point you won't be able to distinguish between who's the enemy that poisons you and who'd just straight out shoot you... Jupiter Hell is a  experience to only go through once and never again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough, especially to roguelike lovers - after all this time we finally have a breeze of fresh air in a genre. At first it was quite hard for me to get used to it, as I was comparing it to the previous product of ChaosForge - DRL, but now it feels really awesome to me.I deeply appreciate that the game works stable, despite being in EA and using the custom engine. The graphic part is very neat, and the soundtrack is just what would you expect from this sort of game! It also gives you a perfect feeling of simultaneous turns (which is hard to explain actually, you just have to try it).Now about the roguelike part. It's a bit less deep in tactical sense than DRL: you can't open doors manually, firing with shotgun in the darkness almost never works, diagonal movement is absent (which makes dodging more tricky), there are no melee weapons (at least I didn't find any yet), and finally you can't run. Despite this it adds few useful things, like a visualized covers system and various grenades, both can be a game changer in certain situations. Like in DRL there are many possible builds for your character and in-game achievements unlock new game modes.Now on the things I would like to be changed:1. Though adding realism, pain mechanics feels very annoying, especially when you're almost dead. I would prefer to make less damage than not doing it at all because of misses.2. In DRL I had a lack of medboxes only in the endgame, and here I have to hunt for them starting from Valhalla Terminal. Would be very nice if their spawning rate increased, at least on Easy level.3. There's no speech on double shotgun pickup, which feels very unnatural especially as character is quite talkative in all other situations :) Overall - nice work, keep going! Hopefully the game will become even better on full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent successor to the awesome DoomRL from back in the day. A very tactical rogue-like where positioning is crucial to making it through each level, particularly on the harder difficulty settings. I've been playing this since it was greenlit for open beta and have seen the game grow and develop to meet its potential as a contender for being the best tactical rogue-like ever.PROS* Addictive and highly replayable* Three distinct classes with many builds available within each classes' skill trees* Lots of fun loot that can be further customised* Multiple game modes with various challenge settings to add to replayability* Fun Doomesque setting with a 90s feel to the music and atmosphereCONS* Slightly janky FPS, at least on my ultra widescreen monitor* Melee builds are difficult to succeed with on higher difficulty settings. Maybe I just need to 'git gud.' :p* Needs more enemy types with distinct strengths and weaknesses. This can be easily remedied with additional content, howeverThis game from an indie developer ticks all the boxes for what makes an engrossing tactical rogue-like for me and thus earns a well-deserved recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I have regularly played a turn-based Rogue inspired game. I just didn't connect with any and was sticking to real-time Rogue games instead. This game has changed that and has shot up to the top of my play list. I foresee many many hours spent fighting the Forces of Hell on the Jupiter moons.The UI, dialog, music, gear and enemies all combine to set an excellent gaming experience with a point of view. There is a lot of swearing by default but you can turn that off. Also, for Roguelike purists, my understanding is you can go into the config files and remove the progression unlocking everything right away.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to DoomRL- aesthetically, it's Doom 3 to Doom 3 to DoomRL's Doom 2, but in every other sense it's actually a gameplay refinement. There's room for improvement, and it's not what I'd call up to the level that was just YET- but the improvements are tangible and it's easy to see it getting further improved from here!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game for new players of the traditional roguelike genre, which is also very satisfying to veteran players.  Jupiter Hell is a no-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ no-tedium streamlined traditional roguelike (turn-based, grid-based, permadeath, etc.) with 3D graphics, animations and a physics engine, making it truly unique and one of the more stunning titles in the genre to look at.  The game is primarily ranged combat and has a great tactical feel to positioning and movement due to its use of line of sight, terrain, and cover mechanics.  It has a skill tree (I'm a sucker for these) with each skill having a big impact, and a balance of loot and inventory space to make the experience one of the player making fewer but very important decisions, contrasted with other games in the genre that have the player constantly making small decisions with minor impact for cumulative gains.  Overall very satisfied with the game so far and it is well worth a look if you want a truly unique traditional roguelike experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I should start out with a disclaimer, I put many many hours into DoomRL, absolutely loved it, and still play it. I also think the developer is great, and I've loved everything he's put out that I've tried. That said, I just can't recommend this game and I really really hate to say that, especially since the list of things I don't like about Jupiter Hell is so short.This may be the only roguelike I've played that I think handled the transition from ASCII to visual well. The graphics are great and I'm glad to hear that an ASCII mode will be included at some point. I also think the small changes to the story/lore/etc were handled very well. The thing that completely kills it for me though, and I know it's a tiny detail, is the lack of diagonal movement. I wish I could get over it and adjust, it truly bothers me that I can't. There are a few other minor things, like not being able to carry extra equipment or unload guns, but the movement is the only real dealbreaker.I'm not planning on giving up on it, but every time I try to play it I just get so frustrated by that little detail that I have to put it aside for a while and go back to the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Unique and refreshing combination of Doom-ish themes and classic strategic roguelike gameplay. At first it can seem like some encounters can practically instakill you if you're not careful, but with a bit of experience you'll get a good sense of when you need to use some consumables or just GTFO of a bad situation. Your class and build can really change how the game "feels." Survivor Marine can dig in and take a lot of hits, the Scout variants can either focus on stealth, sniping, or extreme mobility, and Wizard tech can kick back and let the bots do the work. Really good game.Worth a try for fans of roguelikes, Doom and/or turn based strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with Doom and Doom 2, and sometimes I still play a modded Doom version In a roguelike way: launch a map generator to create a few random levels: if I die, then I quit and delete the .WAD.Jupiter Hell feels like Doom like no other game, in a roguelike fashion. - It's a roguelike: not a rogueliTe. No metagame bonuses carried over to the next run, every game you start over. It wouldn't feel like Doom if it wasn't this way, where every new game welcomed you with a pistol and the E1M1 map.- The atmosphere is very "Doomlike": nowadays roguelikes tend to have cartoonish or pixel graphics and simple music. That's ok, but as a Doom fan I would reject a tribute-game with such features. Jupiter Hell delivers realistic, dark colours with very nice light effects and shadows like every demon-slaughterer would expect. I don't like the "old LCT monitor" effect, but that can be desabled. And please let me praise the composer that created that masterpiece of a soundtrack. Notes and riffs are meshed together to create tracks that are not merely clones of the Doom ones, but instead they deeply share their soul (more with Doom 2, since it's metal, while Doom 1 had a more unsettling soundtrack). The composer really understood the spirit of the game and delivered accordingly. Download the free DoomMetal tracks, then listen to this game's songs and judge for yourselves.- All the characters of all my runs have been, are, and will be called "Doomguy"Let's move on to other aspects.Jupiter Hell is a turn based roguelike. Time ticks only when you move, but the devs made an incredible job about movement. If moving fast enough the game looks and feels like real time! Never seen such a smooth movement in a roguelike. You can choose your hero from three archetypes: the tank, the rogue, and the tinkerer, everyone with his own skill set, special ability and general gameplay. The levels' layout is procedural and consistent: no strange rooms or useless corridors. It's random but looks like handmade (premade chunks randomly arranged? or maybe "style rules" for the generation algorithm to follow?).Combat is ranged only, although melee will soon be introduced. I bet they'll add the chainsaw, can't wait for that! Overall it is satisfying, and the cover system introduces that little bit of strategy which is required in every roguelike, but not too much... it's an action game we're talking about! I like it. And I do because it's simple. Not too many weapons, not too many items. Every run I want to kill demons in Jupiter Hell, instead of spending dozens of minutes comparing stats and numbers. When I want deeper strategy or variety I play other wonderful games (like Synthetik) that cover those needs.The UI is clear, you know when you're in cover and when enemies are; items drop always in the nearest free floor tile available and are clearly distinguishable. There are a lot of destructible items: crates, barrels (which can explode and deal different kinds of damage, like fire, cold or acid). Enemies are different enough and unlike most other roguelikes (when they simply disappear or turn into a "corpse" sprite) they ragdoll nicely when they die. New mechanics are constantly added like hacking (enemy bots or terminals to open vaults, turn turrets to your side, or discover the entire map of the level): those add depth to the game, yet are not too complex.In conclusion: Jupiter Hell succeds to transfer the feel of action in the inherently static gameplay of a roguelike, with an atmosphere which will please for sure all Doom fans, but is not enchained by that bigger and more famous franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It started life as an AliensRL / DoomRL amalgamation. It has grown *so much* since then. Today, Jupiter Hell is an action packed, easy-to-play, hard-to-master roguelike with tons of options for replayability. It's games are between 30-60 minutes for a decent player, so it fits a nice timeslot for a "coffee-break" roguelike.Only, compared to DRL, this has TONS more content.Graphics are great, voice acting is hilarious (Thanks Mark Meer!), music is good and gameplay is top notch.I'm not gonna lie though...it's hard as balls. Do I recommend Jupiter Hell? HELL YES.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this at the kickstarter as I was big fan of their previous Ascii rogue like DRL, which provided a tactically interesting fast paced addictive rogue like and I have followed it through it's time in EA.It takes all the things that make rogue-likes good, cuts some of the cruft that can make them feel like work and then wraps it in a setting, sound track and visual design that makes it feel fast paced and tense, or slow paced and tense depending on your playstyle and your current situation.I highly recommend giving this a go
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Doom as a Roguelike.Pros:-Feels like I'm playing turn-based Doom-Difficult and Challenging-Each class have different skill trees to encourage multiple builds and different ways of playing the game-Each level have multiple routes to choose from. You can view the messages in the terminals that give hints as to what rewards / hazards each route possesses so you can manage risk vs rewardCons:-Exalted / Elite mobs are a bit too powerful-Too many times you turn a corner, find yourself staring face to face with a group of exalted mobs, and that's the end of the run if you don't have any proper defensive items-Your character can't outrun melee so if you get swarmed it just becomes a slugfest-Last two areas are deliberately over-turned to deal with powerful builds. Enemies deals an enormous amount of damage in comparison to the previous levels.-Final boss swarms you with an endless number of summoned mobs while also spamming attacks on you.Don't get me wrong, Jupiter Hell is a great game and I honestly had a good time with it. But with runs being 2hr+ long, runs consistently ending due to rounding the corner into a pack of elite mobs and promptly dying along with the over-tuned final areas makes the game just too frustrating to deal with and ultimately feels like I'm wasting my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the smoothest turn-based games I have ever played, if you were to watch someone play quickly, you may not even realize it is a turn-based game! Solid mechanics through and through, if you like traditional roguelike games, I can't think of anything to say other than well worth the money, quite obviously a labor of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: D**mRL and AliensRL are some of the top roguelikes, immensely playable and replayable. I’ve been enjoying them for years and backed JH on Kickstarter. JH is a cross-over and a further development of these, with controls simplified but not dumbed down. 3D graphics, music and speech only make the game better.Whole-heartedly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly hesitant positive review at the moment. It's strategically somewhat unique for a roguelike with its cover system, movement-dodge mechanic and its heavy focus on gunplay. The game certainly can be interesting when you reach tense moments. So far however, it feels like the vast majority of the time I'm just using rinse-repeat strategies on helpless basic enemies which is far snappier in a game without cover mechanics. I find myself taking damage simply because I don't want to run away to cover and wait for enemies to catch up eight times per floor. This game also definitely lacks the item management and variety of something like Dungeon Crawl or Infra Arcana. You're pretty much just managing your life bar, ammo and a few grenades here and there, while you hope for a good, mostly generic gun that suits the build you've locked yourself into.I intend to update this review after a bit more playtime, but I'm not particularly looking forward to replaying the first 10 or so floors before more difficult enemies start spawning on hard mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat this game on MEDIUM after six hours. I had 5% HP left. And my heart was pounding through the entire endgame.Jupiter Hell takes a well-established genre—the roguelike, with its pedigree in console-based games of the 20th century—and spruces it up with graphics, guns, and a gosh-darn brilliant soundtrack. No, this isn't the FTL kind of roguelike; it's right down to the basics of the genre, with turn-based grid combat, permanent death, randomization, and punishing difficulty.Roguelikes of that sort have a reputation for being unforgiving. But Jupiter Hell does a great job of easing you in, with eye-popping three-dimensional graphics and a stripped-down core. This is what some call a "coffeebreak roguelike": short enough to play on a (very long) coffee break, but still meaty enough to sink your teeth into. The interface is at first slightly impenetrable, but you eventually learn to interpret what you need and remember the critical keystrokes—which are more expansive than simpler titles, like Brogue, but not so numerous that you're constantly pulling up a help menu. I was able to master the interface in the few hours my first win required.Jupiter Hell also eschews the melee focus of most roguelikes in favor of ranged combat, with mechanics that are simple to understand yet thought-provoking enough to drive the gameplay. Positioning is everything, as is weapon choice. It's a lot more interesting than the combat in some other roguelikes, which is simple enough that some games even automate it!Inventory space is also limited, so you're forced to choose weapons and other items to maximize your effectiveness. The items can get same-y after a while, but the game tries to mitigate this with occasional rare item drops with randomized traits. There are also multiple viable weapon builds, so you can get replay value out of maining a chaingun one run and a rocket launcher the next.The replay value comes from a large set of achievements and challenges, as well as a difficulty scale. For instance, one challenge mode requires you to use rocket launchers the whole game! And if MEDIUM is too easy, there's always ULTRAVIOLENT. It's more than enough to keep me coming back after my first win.A couple of complaints: The graphics aren't optimized, so I can only get about 10 fps on my integrated Intel chip even on low settings, while I can easily get 60 if I switch to my Nvidia discrete card. Jupiter Hell isn't a twitch shooter and the graphics are all eye candy, so it would be nice if the developers added a low-performance mode. Also, while opaqueness is a part of the genre to an extent, there are some spots where it seems pointless—for instance, why can't you see what kind of ammo a weapon uses until you equip it?Still, an excellent title; even after my first win, I'll be coming back for more. Jupiter Hell was highly anticipated in the roguelike community, and it has surely lived up to expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game regularly for the past 2 years and it doesn't get old. Essentially this is a sort of remake or spiritual successor to DoomRL with 3d graphics and commander Shepard's voice actor Mark Meer playing a one liner in human form (the amount of references in this game will make any 80s movie fan happy).Like any roguelike, dying and learning what you did wrong for the next run is part of the gameplay. If this is your first foray into the genre, don't get too attached to any of your runs and don't worry too much about "losing". Even a successful run will last about an hour and a half on average, so its a game where you'll keep playing over and over. Gameplay can change quite a bit depending on the class you picked and what build you went for, so replay value is pretty much a given.Overall if you like roguelikes you'll like this. If you like roguelikes and Doom, you'll love this. If you only like Doom, you might like it, so give it a shot.Pretty much the only thing i dislike here is that every armor is just a recolor of the old doomguy belly shirt, even the armors that are said to be a huge suit of combat armor in the description look like this. I'm hoping this changes somewhere down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a couple of hours of content. It is possible to blow through the main game on Easy because the Easy mode does not require any more than the most basic of tactics. After reading the negative reviews, I feel that the posters had a couple of hours of fun, and ran into a brick wall. The basic tactics that got them that far or into a particular situation stopped working, and it caused them to stop playing. Other times they phrase it as "I've seen everything" with less than 5 hours clocked in. It could be they had a really good RNG run and completed a run on Easy pretty quick. This can happen in any roguelike albeit rare.This game is not for everyone. Also, it is labeled as a "traditional" roguelike, and won't have FTL style rewards for making it halfway through. So this could be the cause of some of the negative reviews, and that is understandable. Worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: More then 5 hours in Beta, but Steam does not count them.Excellent TURN BASED Rouge Like. And I am talking here about true Rouge Like. From the same Guy who made DOOM RL before Bethesda tore down the game. Jupiter Hell gives you a highly tactical Rouge Like set in a SciFi setting where you fight Demons and Rouge AI drones in branching Levels. It looks good and feels good. Every action counts in combat. Shoot em, stab em, hack em, depending on your class and skill choices. Grab the epic shooty or better two hand guns? Charge into melee or use cover to you advantage. Misstakes can be deadly.Enjoy features like Trial mode and a profanity setting (Seriously, set it to max and hear Commander Shepard Dub Mark Meer do his best 90s Action Hero impressions). It is really well made, by a small studio that cares. And it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In This Episode we rip and tear on the red planet with Jupiter Hell of the Magister by new developer Chaos Forge.  Jupiter Hell is an Action PRG combining a Sci-Fi horror setting with turn based combat as well as roguelike progression. The player takes the role of a soldier with the task of investigating a colony on the planet Jupiter, which has suddenly ceased communication with earth. The colony is under seige from demonic forces destroying the colonists and threatening to spread to earthIn order to succeed you will need to master the Turn Based Combat system, utilising the environment and weapons to even the odds against superior numbers. This game takes heavy inspiration from the doom games and I highly recommend it for fans of doom and also strategy game enthusiastsPlease note my opinions are my own. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It took a minute to get used to. For the first hour or two, you won't like the controls and think it's missing features (what? no analog stick?), but once you get the hang of things, you realize why they're not there. They went out of their way to ensure that there is nothing tedious at the cost of a few reasonable limitations.I've never played a game quite like it. It's turn based, but once you take action, the turn lasts just a split second. The pace is entirely up to you at every move. You can always stop to think about it, or you can finish a whole encounter in a second. There is NEVER anything time sensitive in either direction. No rush, and no delay.I always _want_ to like turn based combat games, but so often the menus and animation sequences just make it a chore. None of that here.A small thing, but you can save & quit anywhere, as well. I like when a game doesn't try to control my time.I do hope they add more camera control, though. I would love to be able to zoom in and out.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on kickstarter and after a bit of a play of this early access version I'm already very happy. It's EA so obviously some things are missing (that's what an early access release is for), but the foundation is already solid and as is, it's a great modern roguelike, modern as in the good bits of classic RL design (the tension, buckets of it) mixed with much-needed ease-of-use improvements (slim UI, readability, fast-playing if you want to, no grind, you can play a complete run without sacrificing your night).TL;DR: great shooty bang-bang demon-blasting turn-based fun, pick up and play, tactically deep, and it's probably going to get even better as early access progresses.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I like it. Never played DoomRL, so this is coming from someone with nothing to compare it to. Has an old school feel, like doom and an old ascii roguelike had a child. The level up perks have a decent amount of variety so I feel like I can mess with different builds to an extent every time I die. Looking forward to seeing what improvements come down the pipeline.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: the best introduction to the genre. heavy focus on good positioning and decisionmaking. if you suck at roguelikes, just try this. it will teach you all the basics you need. and it's extremely replayable and balanced, with lots of nuanced mechanics and different playstyles. oldschool fun with modern ui and pacing. it's so much more than turn-based doom
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell has gradually over the last year become my favourite game. It has been amazing seeing it grow over the early access period, patch by patch, from a clone of its predecessor DoomRL into a separate game of its own. It has incredible depth, with many game modes to choose from, and many styles of play which feel noticeably different. After 280 hours, I still feel I am learning new things which will help me do better on future runs.It is a traditional roguelike in the sense of being a turn based, grid based, pseudo-rpg with procedurally generated levels and permadeath. What it does better than any other traditional roguelike I have played is making highly tactical ranged combat seem smooth.Tactically, it reminds me of XCOM games with cover, accuracy and positioning often being more important than raw damage per turn output. However what sets it apart is the streamlined play allowing it to played at action game pace (if you choose). As someone who would usually play a roguelike with mouse, I was wary of hearing it was pure keyboard, but once I got used to it I think its control system is what make the combat side of things so enjoyable.Thematically, it is hard to miss the influence of Doom: Hunting zombies and demons across the moons of  Jupiter. The soundtrack is brilliant, fitting the feel well and not getting annoying even when playing for long periods of time. The voice acting is pretty memorable also.The item and crafting system and inventory management fall under the "easy to learn, hard to master" category, as does the skill system.My few complaints (lack of modding support, some information that can't be found in game so need to check the wiki for it, some of the newest systems to be added have a bit fiddly interfaces) are all on the Devs to-do list and I can't wait to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very solid. I've always liked both doom and roguelikes and this is a really nice take on the turn based genre, focusing on tactical ranged combat. It is simple and quick to pick up, but really makes you think during later levels how to approach each area of the map to have optimal coverage and escape routes in case things to south.The most fun things about the game are the trait system when you level up, and finding better weapons with randomly generated mods on them. I feel like your run depends heavily on them though, so if don't find anything great the demons will get you.The art direction of the game is great and the sound track is OK.I beat the game on medium on my third run, but there's still 3 difficulty levels to beat, and different challenge/trial modes. I don't know if there's a huge amount of replayability (for me), but at least some. For the price I think it's a good buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly an amazing unique roguelike that is simplified to be welcoming to beginners but has some depth to make it interesting to keep playing.My concern so far from what ive seen is two-fold1) Balance - I've finished a game as Marine - Survivor on normal on my 3rd run but felt that it would have been impossible to win without some sort of self-sustaining ability (Survivor negates death by one shot, and also allows passive regeneration. Functions similiarly to Guts from Monster Hunter series)Ive tried a few other builds so far, namely Scout - Ghost and Marine - Onslaught and i find that while cool, it might not be viable late game. With better understanding of the systems i hope it wont be a big issue.2) Variety - From what i've seen so far: There are a fixed amount of levels per region, with 4 regions in total. Each map has 1-3 special regions.There are also several weapon types with 1-3 specials per type.There are maybe 5-7 distinct enemy types i can remember. So far its still interesting but i suspect it will end up being kind of mundane in the long run. Adding in more content in the future would definitely be great. The only one i probably dont have issue with so far is the builds you can make (Though to a certain extent only Master builds modify your playstyle by a large margin)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Being someone that played Doom on Sega many many years ago, just seeing people compare Jupiter Hell to it, I had to see what was going on. If Doom was made as a turn-based rogue-like: this... is... it... Jupiter Hell is an absolute blast that feeds my turn based strategy passion while keeping things moving with sudden enemies ripping my soldier apart with chain guns and fireballs. Not to mention all the random references to movies and other games: Warhammer 40K... Evil Dead... Equilibrium... The Easter eggs are aplenty. Grab this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Your point of view is a bit too far from the character who looks tiny on screen. The keyboard and mouse control is horrendous but if you are looking to play games from PC stoneage it's alright i guess plus it's turn based but gets really choatic with big waves coming at you agressively and during these times you really don't want to click on the wrong button using a controller so that might be another reason. Yet I still prefer to play it with a controller which feels bit weird for a PC culture rooted game, why can't we just use our mouse? For that alone I want to thumb down. The achievements list is made for the real completionnist, not for fun, not for me. The music is nice, cheery Doom-like, the gameplay is really neat, melee is brutal, the shotgun wipes floor, the sniper is death touch, so far so good. And there's lots of good quality loots where guns get their own twist and surprises, also last mention for the depth put into characters builds. Jupiter Hell is not an outlier, it's not the best either, but overall it's a good effort, I wished for more cinematics though, I liked the animation during the intro.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't meant to be a harsh review. I just didn't really enjoy the game. It's turn based by virtue of each action (a step, a shot, a reload, etc) is a turn. Example, as you take a step, the enemy takes a step at the same time. This isn't you move, you action, and then finish your turn and it swaps to the enemies. The gameplay, at least in the 40 minutes I played, was moving around darkened spaces, spamming the fire key whenever an enemy came in sight. To be honest, ammunition was so plentiful there wasn't any challenge. It was just boring. I didn't really like the interface, and the 'curved screen' effect on menus is just a bit off putting. I just found it a bit too boring to persist with.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun game, so much strategy and replayability. Combining different traits with different inventory-style preferences, stat enhancing armors, techno-chips, and demon bodyparts (so metal) will never get old. Not much in the way of story or conceptual reflection though -- beyond an incessant recognition by the game that life in an isolated military facility is even more hellish than slaughtering demons. Sometimes I wonder about whether these soldier or scientist-turned zombies ought to be afforded some respect after death, like a space-burial, but my shotgun doesn't seem to understand that I don't want to blow them to bits. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's metal. The systems are complex enough to make each run and build interesting and challenging, while not so deep as to make it difficult to learn. A really nice touch is you can learn how the mechanics work by default when looking at your level perks. They often describe how it works without the perk giving you clues into the deeper mechanics of the game and builds. The game runs beautifully and definitely offers a challenge, though you can quickly learn what works for you. The class options are another level of customization it offers for taking on another run. It's still in early access, but it's got me hooked wanting to explore. Do you enjoy randomized levels, path options? You get to choose your loadouts as you choose and can mod your guns to suit your play. Or try to get personal with melee.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: So.I'm twenty-one hours in, according to steam, and I can feel that I'm just scratching the surface.Frankly I'm only leaving a review in the hopes that it boosts whatever numbers steam uses to recommend games. Because if you know what Rogue, ADOM, AliensRL, ToME and the likes are, you know what this game is and isn't - It's a (worthy, and superior) successor to DOOM RL, it isn't a trad high fantasy roguelike...It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥' good game is what it is. With a exellent soundtrack - my biggest gripe is that there isn't enough tracks. 21 Hrs is too short to cover the gameplay - I'm a slow learner, so I'm still experimenting with different builds and whatnot, still haven't got a win on my belt... But gods dammed it I'm having fun. This game has a setting to decide how much profanity there'll be in the mc's quips.This game will let you decimate roomfulls of demons with a shotgun.This game will crush you mercilessly because you spammed the "wait" key in the wrong place at the wrong time.And, frankly, this game needs more exposure, reviews, wishlisting and whatever else. So here I am. I'm not trying to get you to buy the game - I believe that if you've heard of it, you know whether you'll like it or not - I'm here to convince you to give it the publicity it needs to succeed. We are a (relatively) small playerbase, with a (relatively) few games to play, and this kind of competent, awesome, clearely loved game needs all the promotion it can get.So please. Leave it a review. Even if it's a negative one. Wishlist it if you're interested. Stream it if you do that kind of thing. Just give this labor of damned love the recognition it deserves - give the devellopers the means to not only bring this project to completion, but also the next.It's a good-looking, addictive, meaty, bloody, metal as all hells roguelike for the ages. And If that tickles your fancy, don't stop at playing it.The game can bring you joy. We can bring it success.Please, please do so.We both know it deserves it.

It's intuitive, strategic, and well-designed. The classes, skills, and weapons are very different, and many different weapon/skill builds and styles of play are feasible. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest problems with most roguelikes is that ranged weapons often feel like they lack impact. This game takes care of that by letting me gib a room of enemies with a single shotgun blast. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'm having the kind of fun in the first two hours that I wouldn't normally feel until I've become super powerful in most other titles. Another element that really sets the game apart from other roguelikes is the cover system. Very simple stuff you've probably seen dozens of times in games like xcom, but for a genre that traditionally REQUIRES you to hold a choke point at the end of a hallway in order to kill dozens of enemies single file, it is a remarkable breath of fresh air!I anticipate many more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell hits all the beats that I loved about DRL. Everything is obviously prettier - DRL runs infinitely better on my tablet, sadly - but the style lends well to the gameplay. Nothing feels too weird despite the turn-based timing, and everything feels mechanically tighter... and so much tougher than I remember DRL being. It does it well, though!I mentioned my tablet, which can only run this game at 1024x768x30 if I'm lucky. I'd love if this had a 2D tiled mode one day 🥺

_childDocuments_.review: Hellishly good fun, also very refreshing, smart gameplay... the each action advances the clock system is really cool and lets you play as fast or as slow as you like without losing any sense of tension or bogging things down.  Of course if you are like me you get overconfident and start playing like its real time and then get yourself killed but it's pretty much always your own fault. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those on the fence games. It is not bad, but I can't really recommend it. I have put 22 hours into the game, and will likely revisit it again sometime. It is deeper than some reviewers have complained about, but the branching system doesn't really make that much difference to the repetitive feel. It is very dark. The player and enemy models are small. The character classes do operate a bit differently and the skill system can tailor them a bit to taste, but they look and feel the same. It would be nice to have different models, voices, and flavor dialog for each. A female model and voice would be great as well.Gameplay-wise each level is most difficult at the start where there is a significant danger of getting mobbed. Once you overcome the early danger, it is generally a good bet you'll make it to the next level. This is a problem in other games as well, but it is worth mentioning.The number of ammo and weapon types is a bit overly complicated. I also don't like the use of 20th Century standards. It is hard to imagine a future colony system around Jupiter using 44-caliber or 12-gauge weaponry. No bugs or crashes encountered. Performance was not issue on a Mac Studio.It is a small thing to mention, but it felt great that the default keys are convenient for a touch-typist. I'm used to having to switch the usual WASD layout to ESDF so that my left hand sits properly over the home row. 'F' for fire, 'g' for get, 'r' for reload, etc. The default for movement is to have your right hand on the arrow keys (the game is not mouse-driven).Overall, it is no FTL or Dungeon of the Endless, which I continue to play (currently over 400 hours each). I'll say 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; What if a Roguelike removed all the tedious bits, and left behind only the intense bits?A successful run is relatively short, but more intense.  It's basically a heavily distilled essence of rogue.  There is no grind, no backtracking, no excessive detours - just alternate paths forward.In exchange for being shorter, each engagement is much more involved.  ALL enemies benefit from cover, some of which is destructible.  Half of the enemies will take advantage of cover to attack at range, while the other half rush you.  Between that and the limited hearing of non-robot enemies, even the simplist fights are more complicated than "whack enemy with a stick."  It feels very similar to XCOM in terms of positioning and scouting.Resource management is very involved.  You have precious few inventory slots to share with ammo, grenades, upgrade ingredients, healing kits, and special items.  Depending on RNG, you could hit a famine of any or all of those resources - so you have to choose what to stock up on.  You can only carry 3 weapons by default, but there are ~4 damage types (regular, anti-unarmored, anti-armor, anti-armor & robot), ~4 effective weapon ranges (melee, close range, mid range, long range), ~4 ways of dealing damage (high damage single target, low damage * multiple shots, multitarget, explosion radius), ~6 ammo types... you get the idea.  You will always have at least one weakness.Compare this to Nethack.  Excessive backtracking through dozens of levels, 90% of fights are zero risk, passive healing makes chip damage irrelevant, positioning is as simple as standing in a hall or doorway, and enough inventory space for 50+ items BEFORE getting a bag(s) of holding.  Other roguelikes vary in the specifics, but they all have a similar formula of 85% tedium, 10% risk of death by attrition, 5% risk of instant death.  This game is 90% death by attrition, 10% chance of a instant death.---If you ever feel like you've "mastered" the game (50 hours on medium difficulty got me my first win), there are a few dozen unique trials and challenge modes (including "you can't reload weapons, you have to pick up a new one" and "pacifist, lose max hp each time you kill an enemy"), all of which can be played on four difficulties (with the hardest being "deliberately unfair").  After that, there are personal challenges: 3 very different classes, with 5 subclasses each.  A handy and exhaustive list of medals is there to remind you of what you haven't mastered.
