_childDocuments_.review: A *real* classic rogue-like, the kind of games I like and Steam needs more!If you enjoy games like Tales of Maj'Eyal, Dungeon Of Dreadmore, Cogmind, Cave Of Quod but want or don't mind mind simpler mechanics/systems (usually called "coffee-break roguelikes"), this is going to be perfect for you!ChaosForge (and it's main dev) have been creating roguelikes for almost 2 decades. they know their ♥♥♥♥.It's already a good game, and I'm excited to see future content and features! These devs deserves support.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this expecting it to play like DRL and was ready to drop it after two runs, but I'm glad I gave it another shot.Jupiter Hell requires a more deliberate playstile where you carefully have to plan your approach vector and your eventual escape route should things get a bit hairy as it very much relies on a cover system. You should generally try to never be caught in the open as opposed to DRL where you can just weave through enemy shots.The game offers a very good amount of build variety, multiple difficulties and several challenge modes. I feel like it's still a little bit lacking in replayability as of now, I'd really like to see more memorable side areas and a couple of cool boss encounters - the final boss also was a bit of a letdown and seems more like a placeholder.I think the price tag might be a little bit steep for what Jupiter Hell brings to the table right now, but I'm nonetheless looking forward to get back into it when the next content update releases. The core gameplay is rock-solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's the best game I've played for a few years. The AI is much deeper and complicated than appears at first glance. I used to complain that I wasn't doing well, but I have content for the next 400 hours of trying to overcome at the various difficulty levels. Also the developer puts out free updates continuously? I played for free for 100 hours,  I saw the new update and thought, "It's not like I don't like the game..." This game is this year's version of This Land Is My Land or Battle Brothers, at least for me. Highly, highly recommend, but I would warn that it will destroy your social life. Call it creative destruction.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A weird, wonderful gem. I wasn't sure how much I liked the keyboard (or gamepad) controls and old-school CRT effects.. But, the tight tactical gameplay quickly won me over.In short, it's a bold, turn-based tactics game done really really well. Great music, great theme, great tutorial, and highly satisfying character progression. Every upgrade feels punchy and the gameplay is just buttery smooth - over just the first hour or two you'll go from bumbling around each room and item drop, taking  10-15 minutes to clear a floor, to tearing through an entire floor in 3 minutes.There are only a few classes that each sound a bit unimpressive from the selection screen.. But they have their own deceptively large, unique skill trees that will have you coming back for more.Tips:Open up the settings while you're playing through the tutorial and tweak them to your liking. I zoomed my camera in, enlarged the mini-map, and removed the CRT effects.. You'll almost certainly want to lower the camera distance some. Made a world of difference.You can also remove or reduce foul language and turn off being shouted at for being idle :)If you're on the fence, you can easily complete the tutorial and a run or two to decide if you like it within the 2 hour refund period.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Really good roguelike. Lots of build varieties and challenging gameplay. My only caveat is that there is a significant jump in difficulty from the main game to the final boss. I can get to the final boss pretty easily with most build combinations but usually die before I can kill it. The difficulty should be consistent across the game for each of the difficulty levels IMO. I would recommend a Scout Sniper as a good first build that will get you through the game and give you a fighting chance with the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: As of  August 9th the developers are still silent about how they acted towards negative reviews. For now I would wait until Jupiter Hell launches before giving them any money due to how badly they took negative criticism. Chances are that not a lot of people are going to look at this and give much of a damn, but if anyone needs proof of how they behaved, other reviewers and I documented the majority of what they had said before they edited/deleted comments.I'll update this review near the end of its early access or when it launches, going more indepth with other aspects my review didn't mention and updating others with how they changed at the end of EA.The camera perspective is terrible, since it's too zoomed out to tell similar enemies apart (is he carrying a shotgun or an autorifle? That not-imp looks a lot like that other not-imp..oh it moved twice in one turn and is murdering me in melee and  throwing fireballs) and zooming in means you can't see the geography up ahead and plan your movement. The worst part is the default zoom level doesn't zoom out far enough to see your max view distance, though at that point good luck trying to tell what is actively trying to murder you. This wouldn't be so bad, but the command for zooming in/out isn't listed in the controls section and also requires you to use the mouse as well, which can add up in time spent.To me this is a fundamental flaw that should have been squashed early on since being able to identify enemies accurately is a big part of roguelikes in general. Focusing on making enemies and their armament distinguishable from a distance (via enlarging the models or otherwise) should be prioritised, though I'm not sure how to go about it without redoing large chunks of the ingame models which may not be an option at this point for the developers.The UI looks out of place, considering the graphical style of the game, using ascii text. This isn't a huge issue in of itself, mind you. The mapping system however is terrible, since it's usually obscured by lit objects forcing you to squint to make it out, not to mention its placement means it's hard to glance at it in the corner of your eye to quickly check where you have/haven't been.Finally, one pet peeve I have currently is that it's very hard to bait the a.i into following you anywhere it seems. This makes it hard to utilise the cover system not to mention giving enemies free shots at you if you want to try to clear them out. Oh, also add onto it that you can't see the the cone of fire for shotguns.I enjoyed the hell out of D**MRL and was hoping for something that'd be it and more with this, but so far it's just an exercise in frustration and absent quality of life actions (unloading weapons you find on the ground for their ammunition as one example). It's still in early access (or just launched as early access rather), so things are subject to change and I can only hope a lot of these issues are addressed over time. For now though, I would say wait and see before purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great rogue-like with a ton of depth. There are tons of weapons, armor, and perks to insure that no two runs will ever play quite the same. The game is initially quite accessible, with an in-game tutorial, but you'll need to consult the wiki if you want to get OP and maximize the damage you do on each run into hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not an expert in roguelikes, but it's a genre i'm well accustomed to and familiar with the more accessible choices, such as ToME or DCSS or ADOM .... Jupiter Hell came out as a very fun and fresh experience without straying too far from the classic formula, getting into it was easy and quick enough thanks to a functional and helpful tutorial that helps you with the basics but leaves out some few key details that certainly could've helped me more if i knew early, but, nothing too crazy that warrants yelling at the devs. There's not much for me to warn about for potential grievances, there's good enemy variety and an insane amount of juicy items and variants that spice up every run, 3 backgrounds and a lot of perks to choose from, there's a lot of options in terms of character progression. Jupiter Hell for me is an easy recommendation, easy to get into, fun and satisfying to play from start to finish, lots of variety in terms of game modes and challenges and a good team behind it that support the title with juicy updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Although I haven't been able to beat any of my runs, I am hooked. This is a great rouguelike. Can be tense even if it's turnbased action. Heavy metal soundtrack is great, graphics are suitable for this kind of game. Any PC-potato will probably manage it. I encoutered no technical problems or bugs. Randomness of the loot can kick you in the ass but it goes well the theme. A well deserved thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Yeah!I'm an old-time hand who grew up with Doom and Doom II as my childhood fond memories. This is TOTALLY up my alley, and heartily recommend it to any fans of the genre.  A friend roped me into the developer's early Roguelike version of Doom, now known as DRL and which I still play during the off hours at work. I'm very much enjoying the current iteration of Jupiter Hell and looking forward to everything else coming down the pipe!What, you're still standing there? Shut up and give them your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it for Mark Meer's Voiceover.   Stayed for the fun game.   First off, the Developers are supporting the hell out of this title, and it just keeps getting better with every patch.   I enjoyed it immensely at the start, and am still enjoying it, especially with the new flavors for the various areas that they're working on.    This is Gauntlet meets Doom.   All that's missing is Mark muttering... "I need heals... badly..."  as such, it's a blending of two incredible old school flavors that go together in an olive oil and salsa kinda way.  Surprisingly tastier than you'd think.   This is a game for when you've got an hour or so and just want to blast away at the bad guys without thinking too hard about it.   Yeah there's a lot of fun strategems to explore, and they keep getting more interesting with every patch, but the catharsis of blowing away demons to obvious old-school Metallica (Before they cut their hair and sold out)  is a retro moment that those that missed the 90's are sure to enjoy. Plus you know...  Mark Meer.  If you like him here, I highly recommend you also Check out "Tiny Plastic Men", an Awesome Canadian TV show that was one of the first victims of cancel culture.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A quick impressions review at less than 2hrs play.... a lot simpler and less interesting than I hoped. No traditional roguelike depth or emergent gameplay. No real chaos spirals or creative loadouts. Perk progression is slow and unexciting, lacking imagination.Just monsters running down corridors toward me. Very little tactical involvement. Comments re: 'Doom as Chess' feel misplaced when you're often simply sitting in cover trying to maximise DPS. AI is simple, aim system is simple, damage variation is simple. Shooting explosive barrels is the only tactical wrinkle in the first few hours, it seems.Visuals are adequate but unexciting. Kills aren't visually satisfying like those of - for example - XCOM2. Environments are dull. Writing sometimes aims for humour but usually misses. It usually presents the most generic scifi blather, at a bare minimum to contextualise tips for hidden loot.Perhaps far further into the game the depth expands, but I'm not sure I want to lose my refund opportunity on that gamble.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's very whatever. "Whatever" is the most i can say about this title. It's fine. The promise of rogue-like elements did not occur in my few sessions i went through. No unlocks, no changes, no customizations. I have to assume this may change later on, but I didn't encounter anything that would fall under the "rogue-like/lite" style of game.It is a poorly designed game. The UI is the least friendly UI that I have seen in quite a long time, and required multiple trips to google to figure some things out. The gameplay itself is as follows - take a generic twin-stick isometric shooter, then make it turn-based. Thats it.The rogue-like genre is packed with amazing titles, and this doesn't hold a candle to most of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Old skool gamer here. Game totally nailed it the spirit of the 90s Doom generation. the soundtrack is sick! Its all about plain "kick ass and chew bubblegum" fun, though i wish the protagonist referenced that in the game! sorry, but I laughed at the clean version language as an option.It actually push your skills to play, and the reason its roguelike because at each restart you'll find sometimes your quadshotgun you found never turns up and u have to change playstyle throughout. enemies might be puny this time, next restart suddenly they swamp you with grenade launcher. yeah sure you can argue to play safe, probably  its time to stop being a wuss and go in guns blazing! its really fun. its fun to get your ass handed to you by denizens of powerful enemies, then next round you obliterate them with you supershotgun! The levels arent repetitive, felt it probably because you die and restart alot at first, each place has a different feel, some small corridors, plenty of shotgun opportunity, suddenly next stage long corridors and very little cover provided. the random gun drop really get you to change gun tactics, one playthrough you plough through enemies, next they swamp you with you having only your tiny 9mm, next no ammo drop from enemies, next swamped by OP exhalted fiends, next swamped by bots, next hack the bots to attack everything on sight  - wait for the explosions to die down then BANG you've leveled up from standing still. yippekaiyay mofos! Theres a lot of variety in gameplay!I havent finished the game and already I hope to see more content, a sequel and more of them brutal heavy metal tracks! Well done ChaosForge!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Great game, absolutely worth it.Pros:Simple control scheme. Easy to get muscle memory, gets faster the faster you play. Great feeling/powerful tech trees. Thought I had maybe 3 hours in it when I realized it was actually 12.Highly reccommend, runs well on Ubuntu 20.04 + Proton, therefore will make a GREAT steamdeck gameCons: Many things endorse melee, but the whole structure seems to punish melee strongly compared to cover-fire....just like real life I suppose.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The control scheme is from the early 1980's, pre-mouse era, as is the font.I'm not digging the 1990s CRT monitor look ( the developer copied a flickering, non-interlaced monitor, complete with curved distortion - who even bought more than one of those? Usually the first non-interlaced purchase was an accident, due to a smooth-talking salesman, and complete ignorance about computers ). The flickering was hard on the eyes and gave some people headaches. The developer is clearly trying to blind people. I turned it off in the display settings.The aesthetics were all over the place. The game combined a great opening, anime-esque cut scene intro, with a 1980's keyboard-only menu and tutorial ( I had flashbacks to using the "VI editor" on a Unix mainframe - fun times ) with hard rock music, that I instantly wanted to turn off. The font was ugly as ♥♥♥♥.You have to have some serious nostalgia goggles to think that this is a "good look".Me: How high were you, when you made this game?Developer: Yes. Me: How much of the purple juice did you drink as a kid? It was methylated spirits... methanol. You can go blind from drinking that stuff...Developer: Um...I wanted to uninstall and refund the game after seeing the 20 minute tutorial. The trailer was fake - this is a turn-based game. It's hard to see the game's appeal. This game might have been amazing in 1983.You can enable mouse control in the settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: REVISION: full release definitely follows through on the promise of the earlier work. I started following Jupiter Hell as a fan of DoomRL... it is truly a worthy successor, a “pure” roguelike in an era where the term has been used and abused to the point of meaninglessness...But for people unfamiliar with classic roguelikes, it is definitely closer to "chess with shotguns." You can move as fast or as slow as you like-- and speedrunners can go VERY fast-- but the world and the monsters in it react only when you yourself move, sort of a more discrete, turn-based version of Superhot.There's a ton of replayability already, and the dev has proven he is dedicated to constantly updating and improving the game... DoomRL still gets updates more than a decade after release!BONUS: extremely profane vocal quips from Mark "Commander Shepard" Meer
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have not returned many Steam games, but I did return this one!First of all, it crashed my PC during the training!!  In fact, it did more than that - it shut my PC off!  I have never had a game do that on my current PC or my previous PC!Second, I have no idea why reviewers here have said how great they think the graphics are!  Do they get better during the actual game play??  I think they are mediocre as best.  Certainly not on par with Desperado's 3 or even X-Com.Third, the interface is like an old DOS game.  The controls are set up to use the arrow keys.  I did not want to remap them to use the traditional WASD, and other keys.  Maybe mouse support isn't necessary for this game but I would have certainly appreciated it if I could use a mouse to move around and access key commands.I might have given it a longer chance if it didn't shut down my PC (which is more than enough to play a game like this!).And this is the first time I have posted a review of any game that I have purchased via Steam or anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not have meta progression. Each run is started from square zero, and all progress is lost when you die.Your "build" in this game is mostly dependent on gaining experience, leveling up, and choosing talents tied to your class.There are RNG elements to this game, such as weapon perks or floor layout, so on and so forth but they aren't as heavy as Binding of Isaac or Risk of Rain, to name a couple popular roguelikes.This is still a fantastic game, super immersive and the game play feels great and there is quite a bit of replayability. Highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Ugly controls, ugly inventory system, no way to save the game.If you want to play as marine smashing aliens - don't play this.This game is about doing 3 things:1. Press "skip turn" button n-times until you see an enemy coming2. Press "fire" button n-times while you character auto-aims 3. If there are still enemies at the level - move to the next room and repeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game on easy and I haven't had this much fun with a roguelike in a long time. I must admit the graphics aren't really my thing, and the Duke Nukem style one liners don't really do it for me either. Also the music really gets on my nerves, I muted it before I even finished the tutorial. Despite all that, I am having a blast with Jupiter Hell. It really strikes the perfect balance between a fast paced, action packed role-playing experience, and a true to the core traditional roguelike. This is a roguelike with meaningful character progression, fantastic item variety, exciting loot, excellent sound design, and most importantly, very slick controls. I played keyboard-only and it was super easy and intuitive. I don't really have much else to say, apart from that I think this is an incredibly well crafted game and an absolute must-have for every fan of the genre. Also, if you're intrigued by the idea of playing a traditional roguelike, but intimidated by the extreme complexity of games like Nethack, this might very well be your perfect introduction to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly fun and very faithful to DoomRL but there is very little variety throughout the first levels where you will be spending a lot of time as you try to get good. Something else to do besides shoot demons and open boxes would be nice. The moments I find one of those "unlock vault" terminals are a great reprieve for example.I am quite unhappy with the soundtrack - while the music itself is perfectly serviceable metal, it isn't used well - it's basically being blasted constantly which puts you into a mood where you want to go through the level as fast as possible, it's basically the main cause of my deaths. There should also be some more atmospheric tracks playing when there are no or few enemies around, so players feel comfortable taking their time - leave the high intensity stuff for high intensity encounters.The core gameplay is very good though, would recommend. Not sure if the price is worth it at this stage of development but I'm considering my purchase as payment for the free fun I have had with DoomRL in the past so it's fine for me
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Its too hard.This game has multiple difficulty levels... but even on easy its too hard.  Wipe the Dorito dust off your fingers all you like and abuse me with "get gud scrub"... but if a game has a mode called "easy"...... I expect it to be easy!  If the difficulties were called "Hard", "Very Hard", "Insane", and "Hell on Earth"... I would not complain.  This game is great for the niche market of people who like VERY HARD games that explain nothing and expect you to die and die as you slowly learn the game.  It lacks polish and i don't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty bland and repetetive while being uninteresting mechanically.  For a rogulike - less than mediocre, even in terms of early access. My two main advices would be to expand on grid mechanics and enemies interaction with it to make the game less repetative and rework the ost into something memorable. Often, a good or bad ost can make a game a lot better even if otherwise it's mediocre.Since it is an early access game, I can't say anything on how it will turn out later, but at the moment I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a fantastic game and I really enjoy it. It's a turn-based, roguelike homage to Doom-style one-marine-against-the-hordes-of-hell, sci-fi horror. The game is lovingly-crafted, atmospheric and marvellously challenging, packed full of satisfyingly chewy heavy metal and carnage, well done sounds, visuals & many little details done right. I particularly like the keyboard control scheme and responsiveness and speed of the game experience - you can go as fast or as slow as you like.This kind of game isn't for everyone, but if - like me - you enjoy conquering punishingly difficult skill ramps, this game is one of the most satisfying I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of roguelites for their sense of accomplishment and replayability, I have to say that as a genuine RogueLIKE this game was a complete blast of fresh air and an absolute joy to play. _childDocuments_.review: Your patrol ship was suddenly shot down by your homebase’s own defense grid and you barely made it out of the battered wreck alive, only to find the hangar even worse for wear. Corpses pile up across the floor, demonic markings painted in blood cover the walls and your previous comrades snarl like wild beasts as they turn their guns at you. Does this setup sound familiar? The action may take place on Jupiter, but simply watching through the game’s introductory cutscene removes shadow of a doubt as to where it takes its inspiration from. It is only natural given that Jupiter Hell is a spiritual successor to DRL – Doom, the Rougelike.While many among you will immediately have an idea what to except in terms of setting, enemy design and interior decor – the gameplay is an entirely different beast. Jupiter Hell is first and foremost turn-based title presented from a top-down perspective. Every single action performed by the player takes a turn: moving a tile, shooting, reloading, using a medkit. Some among you may now argue that turn-based combat is an antithesis to fast-paced gunning mayhem of Doom, to this I retort – not in the slightest, outlandish as it may seem.The kicker is that all of the aforementioned actions may be performed in a blink of an eye, allowing the player to blast through a level in 2 minutes while also shredding all of the enemies on your way to the exit. A 20 minutes-long session can easily translate to several thousand turns and motion is fluid enough to make you forget that you have all the time in the world before acting.  Frankly, the game almost taunts the player to recklessly rip and tear until suddenly the protagonist is done, much to your disbelief, as the endgame screen delivers impassionate breakdown of damage from 6 hits at once you ate while rushing into the open.Satisfying as the fast-paced slaughter may be, it will come as no surprise that such angle of approach won’t get you far in Jupiter Hell. This title offers unique gameplay which takes patience and perseverance to even get started, let alone explore the depths which the game is able to offer to its veterans. For now, take my word for it – you really don’t want to skip the tutorial.Staying true to the rougelike genre, Jupiter Hell relies on repetition to extend its playtime. Why some rougelikes encourage the player to repeatedly beat the game in an increasingly extravagant manner, the title of the day induces repetition by beating... the player, to death and repeatedly at that. Bluntly put, Jupiter Hell is punishingly difficult – to the point where the first boss will likely seem ridiculously overpowered as you make your acquaintance. Those among you familiar with this type of games will also anticipate that the same boss barely makes for a speedbump once you learn the ropes.That’s where the perseverance comes into play. To make proper progress through the game, the player must engage in an extended period of “trial and error”, during which one will gradually familiarize themselves with myriad of different mechanics Jupiter Hell has to offer. There’s a lot to unpack too, weapons come in different calibres, optimal firing ranges and with an extensive modifiers system. Especially the latter deserves a separate mention. Upgrades may include anything ranging from mundane faster reload or increased range, through additional elemental damage, and rounding up with unique modifires operating vastly different from their ordinary counterparts (say, a self-charging rocket launcher shooting fireballs).No less complex are the levels themselves. At face value, each one is a small dungeon complete with loot, batch of enemies and usually some optional additional risk, which may yield greater rewards in return. It will come as no surprise that hellspawn-marked corridors of Jupiter base are best enjoyed in a leisurely stroll once all enemies nap peacefully in the dirt. However, the only condition mandatory for further progress is finding the exit elevator, giving the player a possibility of sneaking out of tough level mostly undetected. It doesn’t take long to find out that each biome has limited building blocks available. To remedy this, every chapter of the game includes randomized side branch of levels. They all come with a unique twist and offer best rewards if the player handles the extra challenge. You can probably see the pattern emerging by now, namely Jupiter Hell is a chain of risk vs reward calculations, where player needs to continuously brave ever greater dangers to keep racking up even better rewards. Overestimate your prowess though and the chain breaks.I hope the multi-layered wrapping of the game doesn’t come off as overwhelming as we are not quite done yet. The game offers 3 classes, each with unique active skill and dedicated set of abilities. Every class can offer a refreshing new twist on the gameplay and may open your eyes to an approach you didn’t previously take into account. However, not all abilities are equally powerful and in title like this one, consistency is the key. Take my word for it, in a game primarily about slaying demons, you might want to stick with combat-oriented Marine until you beat the game at least once.Let’s assume you’ve done just that – picked your best guns, found a favourite build and discovered branch levels which yield rewards fitting your playstyle. At long last, the game-over screen sums up performance not of a freshly baked corpse, but that of a victor. You might take notice that victory screen is followed by list of completed challenges and how you barely seen the tip of that particular iceberg. Once you have mastered the game enough to be able to beat it, there is a room for further ascendance which can easily fill hundreds of hours with whacky achievement runs, higher difficulty settings or challenge modes. Sky is the limit.More than deserving of separate mention is the overall 90’s touch to Jupiter’s aesthetic. Visuals are slightly curved at the edge of the screen as to imitate CRT monitor (or “brick” as some may call it) and the protagonist fills the time with cheesy quips often referencing action films (profanity filter is an option, however to my ears it would be a disservice). To yours truly, this is just the right corny touch which evokes adventurous spirit of both 90’s cinematography and games.Jupiter Hell is a tremendous game, nonetheless no matter how enthusiastically I would spin it – this title is definitely not for everyone, far from it. The steep learning curve will turn away all but the most patient players and not even the rougelike genre veterans are guaranteed to find purchase during the climb. Despite this, resilient enough to make it to the top will find an entire mountain range, offering countless hours of top quality gameplay. It takes time and intimate knowledge to truly appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new addiction. Very similar to the dev's previous work, DRL (free to download), but still growing with content additions. Turn-based and keyboard only, but with 3D graphics and an engine that can play very fast - the mouse would slow things down. There are a few minor UI issues that can cause confusion and annoyance, but all together I'm adding to my GOAT list.Jupiter Hell is a true Roguelike with no "real" metaprogression; you do unlock new modes as you play the game, but in theory you have access to everything in the main game mode from the very beginning.  Actually encountering everything the game has to offer - let alone surviving it - requires many, many attempts, though... so not having metaprogression isn't really a downside.If you're interested in Jupiter Hell, I recommend trying DRL first.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still bad at it, managed to reach Io a few times and get destroyed, got to the Beyond once (on Medium).That said, I really like this roguelike, snappy, action-packed but tactical nonetheless, the developer said more than once that he hates adding stuff that bogs down the gameplay with repetitive, grindy actions, the main one being unloading ammo from weapons on the ground for example.In a sense, when you look at other classic roguelikes, it's a bit of a streamlined experience, but there's no shortage of impactful decisions you make every game you start, ranging from what path you take, how you engage enemies, what to fill your inventory with, in other words, it doesn't detract from the experience at all, but enhances it. Also it looks gorgeous for what it is, get that ASCII out of my face.In short, it's tactical, but also fun, fast and satisfying, with an awesome soundtrack to boot.This is clearly a passion project and as such I'm happy to support it, it's a great game even though it's tough, try it out.EDIT: Just won my first game on Medium!

_childDocuments_.review: Original review 2021-10-21: The game is fun. The spooky, isolated atmosphere, and fun gunplay, and great audio is really cool.That said, it does feel "not quite done yet" : 1.Some of the levels are cool and fun, but many have a very similar "square with rooms" feel with very similar colors. More variety would be good - and devs are working on this.2. The classes feel very similar at the start of the game and don't start to feel really different until you get the Master Traits at around level 10. The master traits might be called "active skills" in other games. Generally for much of your first dozens of runs you will be doing "wait at corner, aim, shoot" until you get a Master Trait that you can use for fun.3. For some reason it's prohibitively difficult to play a melee character from the start. I think the idea is this is because the game is gun themed? Which is fine, but just feels a little odd that you get good at a skill you are not practicing and can only start it at level 10.Once you get into the swing of things, though, the game is indeed fun. The devs seem like good guys and are working hard to add content to the game.Edit, 2023-11-06: There's a little more variety in rooms and treasures now, but I still feel the main problem is that all characters play generally exactly the same until they get a unique skill near the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Remember DooM? The feeling of alternating panic at hordes of demons coming at you and the power trip of shoving a double barelled shotgun in their faces and blasting them off?Remember DooM RogueLike, which captured that essense perfectly in ASCII-art top-down roguelike random-generated number-crunch-fest goodness?This is what you get when you debrand DoomRL. No, this is not Mars and its moons, this is Jupiter and its moons. No, you cannot copyright rocket launchers, demons, pentagrams or heavy metal, but just in case, everything looks and sounds legally distinct.It's still Kitchen Ace (tm).It retains most mechanics from DoomRL, including the challenge modes (Angel of Carnage, here I come), trick shots based off manual targeting, bajillions of gun mods and grenade types and, of course, the various skill trees. It also adds distinct classes patterned after Doom RPG's ones, probably, its own soundtrack (don't worry, it still sounds like the best fusion of Doom's 3D0 and PSX soundtracks one can hope for) and even an animated intro sequence!It's still the same amazing time-consuming game as before, except now it has spiffy graphics, and I am eternally glad I backed that Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. This is basically a more polished version of Doom RL in most ways, but there are certainly a few differences. At least tonally, DRL is Doom I and II and Jupiter Hell is Doom 3. However, the tone of the game is very silly and feels right out of an 80s sci-fi action film. There are plenty of weapons and variants of them, but not too many to be lost and forget about them. The three classes are fun to play and make you feel pretty cool. The controls are very intuitive (mouse free too!) and clear. You can certainly play as quickly or slowly as you desire, but playing fast and loose is a good way to die instantly. Overall, this is a wonderful game for fans of quick and strategic combat or the Doom franchise. While this is a roguelike, there isn't a crippling amount of RNG at play, and it's fairly easy to remember the item pool. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fairly difficult (I am playing on easy and still die regularly). That said, it is fun and there are 3 diff classes (with different upgrade perks) and each class plays differently. Despite being difficult however, this game is actually fun (something I could not say for games like dark souls and their ilk generally).  Although it looks like it is real time, it is not...it is 1 for 1 movement (i.e. you do a move and then enemy does immediately after). It is easy to get overwhelmed so do not rush in, upgrade your guns etc. and my advice would be to just head to the different worlds (don't go to the special levels until you are more experienced in the game). For a few negative points i will say that the hacking tools seem useless...when you get to a terminal you need way too many of them to make them useful in the majority of cases (especially since you have limited inventory). Yes you can upgrade a skill to lower the hacking cost..but you need dmg/crit/health upgrades way more than some perk that requires heavy investment for a terminal that may only show up every few levels and even then may only have a small benefit in using it (which i don't believe is offset by the inventory space it takes up). My other gripe would have to be with the game itself when it comes to the different paths...normal paths (i.e. normal elevators, specialty elevators and then things like the anomaly elevator (anomaly is very hard but you can go there on after a few levels on the first world...game should warn you the enemies are much harder there (and unless you have some mad skills you are just going to get murdered). Despite those two negative points, this is a fun game, is generally well made and the community in the game is very helpful and willing to provide tips/advice on how to do progress in the game. Dev also participates as well, so I think they deserve your money...buy the game and see for yourself! you won't be disappointed :)

_childDocuments_.review: Bounced off this game initially but gave it another shot once a buddy had gotten into it and could correct misconceptions and answer questions.  Ended up apparently playing for 46 hours and beating the normal difficulty with all three classes.A turn-based version of a Doom-similar (but just distinct enough to not get sued over) world where you're going to die a bunch of times learning how to play.  The controls are simple but do a lot based on context.  Moving, interacting with items, and even waiting all give the world a chance to react.  A lot of the talents at least early on don't seem like they do anything.  The thing I didn't get was that you level up quickly, and a lot of the mechanics in this game are designed to work together, so you quickly rapidly ascend in power.Once I learned how cover worked, how defense worked, and the basics of the level progression, I was hooked and I never looked back.  Dunno how much more I'll get out of this for now, but I've enjoyed the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: roguelike-lite game with demons and guns. Recommended? 80% yes, 20% no.I think the comparison with DoomRL is inevitable. Lets see what changed and how it effects the gameplay. -- it is more claustrophobic, more packed, the vision and the range is smaller. The first and foremost impression that it is not as good as DRL was. If you don't opt for a kind of enemy sense or if you don't have allies on the map you tend to get into ♥♥♥♥♥♥ situations while opening doors. You can shoot them, true, but half of my deaths came from door related things. Apart from that, most of the tilesets are look great while the rest are okayish. The map have their variations, although I think this is an area for improvement. Several maps tend to be too much packed (cave and Europa maps mostly) or you are struck with 1 corridors. Corridors are another kind of pain as usually you don't have cover, you have to open certain doors and if you don't have a smoke/gas grenade or a high dps you can get into trouble. (Turrets, high tier enemies, etc.) -- A mixed bag honestly. The AI is stupid if not in "Hunt" mode, moving in random directions if activated. Several enemies will seek out you if they hear you, but most of the time pulling them into a good position is a pain. In DoomRL you had blind fire (radar shooting) and gift dropping for pulls works, here you are mostly using the wait keys and maneuvering around the map and hoping for the AI to stay put. Enemy variation is okay, although I feel that several enemies are too powerful or designed to burn through your medpacks. ((Arch)Medusas for example). The mechanical-beast-demon-human balance is okay, monster infighting is fun. If you take the pulling into consideration I think DRL was better, without that, both games are fine and very good in this regard. Apart from a few difficulty spikes, balance is okayish. Certain builds will have trouble in certain places (ammo, armor, enemies...) but it is part being of a roguelike/lite game. -- Another mixed bag. JH has certainly a better itemization in my opinion as random weapon and armor traits allow for greater freedom. I still miss the crafting element of DRL thou. Exotics are more powerful and maybe a bit more plentiful, but a single rifle with 2-3 mods can get you very far in the game in JH. In DRL certain strategies were built upon a weapon, in JH weapons tend to change and rotate as you progress through the game. I think this is a positive thing. Skills? Quite similar to DRL, some are quite op (looking at you techie gas, wizard, remote hacking), some are lackluster (mostly marine ones). The classes are distinct enough, have different paths, so you have your options. It is different from DRL but I don't think it is strictly better. -- I play with music turned off as it is not my kind of music, so no idea how good is that. The ambient and weapon sounds are great, they create a good athmosphere for the game. Enemies has distinct sounds you can recognize and prepare for them. The graphical presentation is very good and detailed, whatever you do ingame will be seen on the monitor. (Dash, cover, etc.) The GUI effects are not my style, I found the CRT and the noise effect annoying (turned it off, you have several options for them), the camera handling is... well... annoying. The fine camera movement looks good on paper, but it looks awful with detailed/anisotropic textures ending up in moire patterns after you've moved. Fortunately you have the option to use a fixed camera mode that solves this. The GUI itself is a bit chunky by design I reckon, nothing fancy but utilitarian.So as a summary, if you loved DRL you most likely will love JH. If you are new to the genre, it might work for you. I think the transition to 3d removed some of the charm of DRL (Derek Yu's exceptional tiles), but JH has some merits of its own. The devs are good people, they listen to feedback so overall I am more likely to recommend the game for you. As a demo you can always try DRL, as it is free and runs on just about every PC/MAC of today. Beside these, JH is so much better in price/gametime ratio than most of games that it also tilts the scale... Don't get me wrong, JH is a quality game (rare nowadays), it might just not be perfect for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Another review likened this game to a cross between Doom and Rogue, with a splash of XCOM thrown in. I find nothing to argue with as far as that goes, and I feel it adequately captures the soul of Jupiter Hell.Jupiter Hell, like DoomRL before it, is a turn-based roguelike in which you set the pace: the flow of action and reaction goes exactly and only as fast as you want it to go. Whether you want to meticulously plan your moves like George Clooney and Matt Damon in Ocean's Eleven, or go all-in like Doomguy himself, you can tailor Jupiter Hell to your preferred playstyle with an expansive perk tree and enough weapons to make a Kentucky gun nut blush.Make no mistake, though: this is a rogue-like with a 'K.' There's no meta-progression, no chain of unlocks making the game easier as you go. You start the game from a clean slate every time, and it ends one of two ways: victory over your final enemy, or with your blood splattered across one of Jupiter's moons.This game is playable with either keyboard or controller; in this writer's opinion, it feels right at home on the controller. The buttons are laid out very intelligently and are (almost) completely re-bindable using the in-game menu. (The dev has mentioned at some point adding mouse support as an accessibility option; however, it will not be the recommended playstyle.) The game should never surprise you with an input that doesn't work like it "ought to."Graphically speaking, looking at JH you might immediately think that it was written in Unity or Unreal. Nope: Jupiter Hell uses an engine that was written from the ground up for this game. It includes dynamic lighting and shadow, partial ragdoll simulation and hard-body physics for you madmen who can't leave any bench unbroken. It supports both OpenGL and Vulkan rendering pipelines, and overall it looks as good as you'd expect to see from a commercial game engine.On the sound front, this game features a bespoke soundtrack that evokes the thumping soundtrack of its namesake -- or, rather, what it could have been had it not been limited by the hardware of its day. The mood of the soundscape changes as you transition between levels, and is never inappropriate to the act, no matter what you're doing.In perhaps an oddity for roguelikes, the main character has a voice: none other than Mark Meer. Taking a leaf out of the Duke's book, he is foul-mouthed, sarcastic, and incredibly 1990s. It isn't necessarily something you would notice as missing if it weren't present, but its inclusion serves the game exceptionally well.In closing, I won't try to assign a numerical score to this game, as I feel it cheapens matters to do so. I hesitate to even assign a "value" or a "recommended price point," as even that can feel awfully subjective. Setting aside as much bias as is possible for a person to do, though, this game is absolutely worth the $25 it asks of you.

_childDocuments_.review: Fight zombies, robots, and hellish demons in this Doom-inspired turn-based Roguelike.  It features a huge variety of weapons, equipment, and skills to upgrade, which allows for a huge variety of playstyles, as you level up your character to be able to face tougher and tougher foes.  The maps are randomly generated, so no two playthroughs are the same, with difficulty settings and challenge modes to provide something for players of any skill level.  Also features gorgeous visuals with smoothly animated monsters, and it's all set to a heavy metal soundtrack, with a wise-cracking protagonist who sounds like he could have come out of an 80's action movie.I've personally sunk hundreds of hours into the early access version of this game, and it just keeps getting better and better, with endless replay value, so I can highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays like old-school rogue-likes which is refreshing in the world of meta-oriented rogue-lites.Your meta progression is you _knowing_ the game better.Tactical layer isn't too deep, but its solid enough. "Take it slow", "choose your own fights" and "don't be afraid to run away" are the paradigms that surprisingly still found their way in a gun-based game.Strategy layer consists of managing inventory space, picking a skill build and managing weapons and armor.This is where it gets a bit hairy.Having access to all skills in every run and being forced to pick your build-defining Master perk somewhat early means that you'll probably stick to something that works for you and it cuts down heavily on replay-ability.Inventory space is always lacking and annoying to deal with and only good thing I can say about ammo management is that it organically forces you to slowly migrate from 9mm to 7.62 to plasma as the game goes on, because of the loot tables the mobs have.Armor doesn't get access to your damage reduction perks and with how scarce repair stations are, you not being able to field-repair it and armor effectiveness going down as it gets damaged, investing in something apparently made of paper that still manages to impede your dodge chance doesn't feel good.You can mod the weapons and armor mid-game, but it doesn't feel like it affects the game too much as by the end of it you'll find some unique weapons that are both unmoddable and much stronger than any of the stuff you can make as long as they are at least somewhat relevant to your build.Still, its fun to play and well worth the price tag and I haven't even touched the atmosphere, voice acting and memes.Go forth and slay the demon hordes!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough to fans of turn-based action. One of the few early-access titles that has been worth my investment. It's also had regular major updates since it came out; it's had one of the most consistent development cycles I've seen in an early-access game. The developers have been continuously refining the product into a truly worthy successor to Doom : The Roguelike. Similar to its predecessor, it takes place in a sci-fi horror setting, populated by zombies, robots and all types of vicious demons. Games are approximately two to three hours in length, accommodating a wide variety of difficulty levels. The action is brutal and violent, emphasizing intelligent, tactical gameplay. Careful use of your resources is vital to success, and the game provides a massive arsenal of interesting weapons and items that can radically alter how you approach your run. It's extremely satisfying to chance upon an advanced energy weapon that can take you from barely surviving to massacring the enemy with relative impunity.There are three character classes and numerous difficulty levels ranging from simple to virtually impossible. Each character gets his own skill tree, the skills you choose will determine the way you'll approach the game.  There are a generous helping of additional challenge modes help extend the playtime of this game. I've already put over 200 hours into it myself. If you're a fan of the turn-based tactical genre, you'll want to check this one out!

There are many game modes and challenge modes that keep things fresh, although I haven't played them as much, as there is enough depth in the normal game to put in hundreds of hours.I played half my time about a year+ ago, came back to it again and found new boss, new branches, new enemies. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, and I have barely scratched the surface at 2 hours in. Its inspired by many games, from Doom, Dead Space to System Shock (and I'm sure there's more), but it never leans on them for help. Its truly unique in game-play, and is more tactical than it appears, leaving you room to breath and learn, but also punishing you for being bold. You're all alone, and you can get help, but it will cost a lot, and you're forced to make tough choices like whether to access a floor, or hack security for drones to kill the enemies+themselves in the process. This mixed with data logs giving you clues to future floors and items makes for a good gaming experience where you want to keep diving. I haven't even cleared the first floors, yet have been enjoying it thoroughly, and really look forward to the branching routes you can take. This game could be described as a Doom-like game, but its far more interesting and slow paced, not to mention way harder.
