_childDocuments_.review: edit2: Or so I thought; there's a lot of content to this game in terms of choices you can make during a run. No doubt that what I said in the first edit sort of stands, the base weaponry and combinations are what they are - but there's new modifiers now, as well as a ton of unique items and secrets to discover. =Make no mistake, the game itself is solid - I sunk ~10 hours into it before getting bored, where it was feeling 'samey'; but now I've just played 20 hours - and am hankering for more. The updates really did a wonder on replayability and making it all more interesting/decision based across the board.Recommended it when it first released, and definitely recommending it even more with all the updates it's had - with more to come on the horizon! <3edit: After about 5 hours, you discover all the game has - and while it's cool, the content and play (mechanically) is extremely limited at the moment. I think it's a very well produced game, and certainly fun for a while - and even past that - but, I have to acknowledge that things do hit a point where they feel repetitive; no matter what you do. The three different classes help keep it fresh, but the weapons and items always being the same (with minor random modifications if you're lucky - but even then, they don't feel different - just slightly "better"), things feel same-ish. :shrug:This game is a love letter to the Doom franchise, as well as turn-based combat/board games.It's simple(y) fun....and now I'm trying to decide; another run, or sleep? It's hard to want to put this one down for the night. The game is not only great mechanically, but plays extremely smooth and quickly - but if you think there's no decision making, or depth of play here - you're sorely mistaken.There's tons of choices to be made along the way, and they all feel valid. One wrong step, one poor choice - and you're going to be in for a world of hurt. However, the same can be said for your enemies - there's a real planning and execution, to how you approach each different room; and potential position of enemies.The music is spot on too, every step of the way.+ It's a labor of love, and it shows in each and every element.+ It doesn't get bogged down in overwhelming amounts of information or variables; and all the relevant information you need is on the screen as you play. [Sure, learning what augments do on the equipment you found takes opening the inventory once or twice - but, they all make sense - and they're easy to remember].+ If Doom were a turn-based combat game, this would be it.What more do you need?Oh, and knife/melee-based builds are not only possible, they're viable.Rip and tear baby, rip and tear. <3

_childDocuments_.review: edit: The majority of my concerns are being addressed with an upcoming update, and I am switching this to a Yes. Leaving the original up though as it's a reflection of the current state of the game.Another instance where steams yes/no reviews aren't good enough. I'm going to leave this on a No to hopefully bring more attention to some massive UI issues in hopes they get fixed. But I'll likely continue to bash my head against learning the game, as I'm enjoying everything else about it.---An improvement to DoomRL in a lot of ways, streamlining a lot of tedious and awful mechanics, but it's currently plagued with some absolutely awful UI decisions, and a lot of descriptions are sorely unclear about mechanics.In my 9 hours of playtime, I've thoroughly enjoyed experimenting with the variety of classes and traits, it feels like there's a lot more cool things to work with compared to DoomRL mostly being passive buffs. But while trying to learn the game, I'm frequently running into new things that just aren't explained anywhere. This leads to some frustration as I'm forced to basically die and see what effect this unexplained mechanic is just so I can learn it and be more prepared next time. Primarily seeing this from a new enemy just added, the Warlocks, which have an aura and a status effect they put on you. They don't even exist in the games wiki site yet. The existence of these UI quirks makes sense as this was for the longest time an early access game in a niche genre, but with a proper release they desperately need to be addressed for the sake of new players trying to pick it up.A simple ingame database detailing every enemy, their stats, mechanics, status effects would ease a lot of these concerns.---In my short time playing, my personal list of grievances so far is;If you get enough mods on your armor, their descriptions take up the entire info panel, and there is no way to scroll it down to see the stats of your armor. Surely there's plenty of input space available even for controllers (hold the minimap button to modify dpad up/down to scroll?)There is no info screen detailing your stats like movement speed, dodge while moving, etc.Trait descriptions like Assassination say your dodge is maxed after using it, which can be inferred as 100% dodge but you'll frequently eat an attack from the target you use it on so the only assumption you can make is that it's taking your movement dodge %, unless there's a dodge cap that isn't explained? I'm genuinely confused on this one.Terminals that offer to repair armor say they'll repair your armor and boots, but boots aren't an armor slot in this game, helmets are, which do thankfully get repaired.Bladedancer's description says it's a master trait, but it's not and you're not locked out of picking another master trait, and it's even a requirement for one.Some enemies have two health bars, some are colored yellow, some are grey, some entities like doors have two health bars, and none of them are explained anywhere.Status effects like Chilled and Frozen aren't explained anywhere. Are they penalties to movement speed, entire action time?Late game enemies get status effects and auras that you have no way of reading what they do. Receive a new status effect? You have no information as to what it does. Enemy has an aura? You have no information as to what it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem that is frequently updated and tweaked, and for some reason somewhat overlooked.ChaosForge weren't kidding about JH being almost like chess, because this bad boy requires you to think-- and a lot at that.Jupiter Hell is essentially the most puritan rogue-like there is, with a gorgeous aesthetic and an absolute s**t-tonne of replay value. Unlike games like BoI, in JH tactics are key and adapting your build and inventory to changes during runs is absolutely essential.If you want to rush and play something fast paced, this isn't for you-- you will be slapped about and spat upon by everything you come across if you run about without any strategy or thinking behind your movements. But at the same time if you want a casual strategy experience, then this isn't for you either as you'll soon find yourself wanting to rip your hair out due to how high-octane JH can get. It perfectly blends a thinking game with 'WTF is going on' moments that I only really experienced in FPS games such as PlanetSide 2 and RTS games such as Supreme Commander 2. In short, be prepared to be swarmed from every angle, with it being your job to save yourself and beat the foes while dodging literal walls of lead flying straight at you.Again, replay value is mad. I played for around 6 hours straight after work and not only I got so immersed that when I looked at my watch it turned for 4pm, to nearly 10, but also not a single time did I get the same experience. With each run having a different layout, different weapon drops, different elevator destinations, etc. At first I didn't understand how some people have 300 hours in this game already, but I get it now. There is A LOT of content in this one, and set up in such a way that if feels even vaster than what it really is-- which is brilliant, as it means when ChaosForge will keep releasing content, it will nicely blend in adding to the whole experience. There are dozens of weapons all acting in different ways, with dozens of different mods that can be applied, with dozens of different rarities along with unique variants-- which also applies to armour pieces, relics and AMPs (augmentations). All that on top of an RPG-like perk system which one tweak and your play style can drastically change. I also love the retro Doom-like take on the world as well, with everything from the UI to special effects and colour palette reflecting that overall vibe. Huge plus in my eyes as I'm not a huge fan of the newer 'make everything blindingly blue and orange' bandwagon aesthetics that Bethesda pumped out in the past few years with their reboots.Jupiter Hell is an masterpiece at what it strove to become-- an extremely well made rogue-like, with a massive array of content, vast opportunities for replay and a sick art style to boot. Absolute must buy for anyone into rogue-likes, Sci-Fi and strategy titles. Don't get me wrong it's not for everyone, but if you think 'rouge-like with a tonne of guns, near infinite replay value set in an 1979 Alien-like universe killing the possessed and demons' sounds awesome-- get it. For 20 quid, it's an absolute no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: This one has more depth than at first glance. The further you go, the more enemy and loot variety you'll come across, including item rarities, effects, mods, and even "levelable" special weapons (though don't expect this to be a turn based Diablo degree of loot or anything). Gun sound effects could use more punch, imo, and the shotgun effect looks more like spraying water than a gun blast. Mouse functionality is a nice, if currently experimental, addition. Enemy pathfinding gets wonky sometimes, I occasionally see enemies "bumping" into obstacles as if they're trying to move through them rather than going around or making some other logical action. And there's a decent selection of skills to choose from.Overall I've found myself really digging it more than I thought I would. Definitely a solid recommend if you're a traditional roguelike fan, and even more so if you enjoy the Doom-like aesthetic and cheesy action movie one-liners. (One recommendation is to turn on "Entity Outline" in the options, otherwise it's easy to confuse enemies on the screen, especially on a smaller screen like on a laptop.)

_childDocuments_.review: Glad to finally be playing the first game I ever backed on Kickstarter.Jupiter Hell is what Doom (2016) could have been if it was:a) a rogue-like, andb) a good gameAnd ignore the devs responding to reviews drama - for a game to be this polished in Early Access, they can be as salty as they wanna be.Personally, I cannot wait to see future iterations of this shiny successor to the one true D**M.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Devs did a great job. It's obvious how much effort and love was put into this game.Game designers on the other hand failed miserably - they managed to make a classic turn based rogue-like boring as hell (no pun intended). Looks like they were trying to make it appealing to to both audiences: people who never played any old-school ASCII games and those whose nostalgia can be monetized. To me they failed in both. The key feeling of "just one another turn" isn't there, because turns don't mean anything in this game, you can think about it as an action rpg shooter with auto-pause after every shot. Just imagine this: 3rd person doom game which pauses after every single shot. That would be it. Can't stress this enough: no strategy is required (or even welcome), you don't see enemy health and you just spam shoot button until everything dies.  You can imagine how boring that becomes after the first 100 turns. It would have been WAY better as a generic action shooter (which it already is) without any turn-based mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: A well done,  turn-based, pure combat roguelike. No meta progression by design, and I'm ok with that. It's a streamlined version of DoomRL. However, if you stick with it to Europa and other levels, try different classes and master traits, and read those emails, you'll find quite a bit of depth in the gameplay. The A.I. can seem a bit simplistic but this is DOOM after all!

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game while looking for the game DoomRL, And while I don't think it's as good a game as DoomRL I still rate it quite highly. Unlike DoomRL this game can be played with a controller, but also unlike DoomRL you cannot move diagonally. Another thing that's different is the cover system, You'll have to get used to picking your position carefully or else you'll take lots of damage while doing very little in return.I just completed it on the easiest difficulty after about 34 hours of trying and there's still quite a way for me to go with this game. I feel the player characters comments are a little annoying, he likes to swear a lot for no apparent reason but other than that the sound is top notch.Overall I'd say 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: While rogue-lites have provided a fascinating bridge between the methodical rogue-likes of old and the seat-of-your-pants reactivity of contemporary games, they nevertheless lose something in that from the ways of rogue-likes. Jupiter Hell, on the other hand, takes a different approach. Instead of removing the turn-based methodical elements of rogue-likes, it removes the tedium and abstractness of it all by never keeping you waiting to perform your next action, while still having a gorgeous and fully-realized visual representation of everything that's happening in the game world. Of course, the game itself is wonderfully engaging to boot, and borrows heavily from shooters, namely in that almost all fighting is done at range, leading to an approach much more dependent on clever use of positioning and cover to stay alive...or you can spec yourself out to feed on the blood of your enemies as you hack them apart limb-from-limb with a chainsaw. It is an RPG, after all.This has become my favourite rogue-like, and I would strongly recommend it to anyone.If you like rogue-likes, or the idea of rogue-likes, but always wanted something a bit more up-to-date in design, and without the focus on melee combat, Jupiter Hell is for you. If you like rogue-lites and are curious about their genre forebears, Jupiter Hell is for you. If you just like the idea of acting out the fight scenes from Equilibrium on the rogue's gallery of Doom, Jupiter Hell is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until I had beaten this game at least once (even if it was on easy), so that I could give a fair review.  I would have played a bit more, but I think this is a critical time where there are a lot of eyes on this game since it just came out.Long story short: I really like this game and I have high hopes for its future.Long Story:I've been checking this game out for a year since I first heard of it.  The prospect of playing a doom inspired roguelike had me giddy.  I waited and waited until the 1st of August rolled around and then I eagerly jumped on steam to check it out.  The price tag of over twenty dollars had me go "oof" and I stalled for a few days trying to make a purchasing decision.  I read the reviews on here and as you can see for yourself, most of them are positive (and deservedly so), but it was not enough for a cynic like me.  I browsed around the web and I found an interview where the developer said that there will be more content in the future.  I don't know why, but it just clicked with me.  This is obviously a passion project and I want to support that; even if the price seemed steep they will be adding stuff in the future right?I bought it and got hooked right away.  *The soundtrack by Roland La Goy is awesome and I sometimes just idle in a mission to enjoy the tunes*Mark Meer is the marine's VA so that's obviously awesome!*The graphics and aesthetic are very pleasing to the eye and rumble a nostalgic feeling in meBut the gameplay is the most important part since this is a game after all and I think that they nailed it.  I've gotten hours of enjoyment from experimenting with different weapons, learning the ropes, adjusting tactics, playing with different perks, and I've only played on one of the three classes so far.If I could think of a criticism it would be how annoying it can be with the protagonist constantly shouting cheesy one liners,  but guess what?  You can adjust the profanity filter and how often the marine talks.  So my only gripe that I can think of is null.The game is exactly what I expected and I believe it is totally worth the asking price.  I look forward to future updates and kicking more demon ass!   PS: The developers are very active on the Jupiter Hell subreddit and on steam.  So if you have any questions they are totally available and I find that really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice roguelike. I remember playing ADOM back in the oughts, and this reminds me of it, just with (better) graphics, doom atmosphere, and much more streamlined gameplay. These days, having way way less time to play, I don't miss a bajillion little things and skills from traditional roguelikes (bridgebuilding, sigh..). Special shoutout for amazing voice lines, that's exactly what a doom guy would say! As for negatives: - I'd say three classes is too few. I want to try more different playstyles.- Some descriptions are really nondescript, like a pistol Death that says that the thing you shoot will die. It certainly will, of old age if nothing else, but some details would be appreciated. My build was not pistol-oriented at all, and enemies were dangerous enough not to fool around and find what happens, so I skipped it.- Story is kinda murky. E.g. what exactly is Dante station? Who opened the portal to hell again, and why? Sure it's doom, so run and shoot, but I can't help wanting to know more.Still, very much worth a try for anyone who likes turn-based roguelikes and doesn't have time for old-school stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a refinement of a previous game by the same team, and after playing it for a bit (and playing the original a lot) I can say it's a really darn good one. The ranged-combat-focused roguelike creates a unique gameplay feel that you won't get from anything else, and it's one that they refined to a mirror finish. The 90s-shooter aesthetic still works well. The dodge system has been simplified (to the player's benefit) and in its place is a cover system which works quite well.There's a huge variety weapons and a huge variety of character builds (each of the 3 classes has half a dozen mutually exclusive "master traits" you can steer towards, which favor different weapons or playstyles).There's also still a wide, wide variety of challenge modes, and an acheivement system. If it's anything like its predecessor those acheivements will keep scaling up to provide challenges beyond the capabilities of most human beings if you're looking for them.Overall, roguelike fans should not miss this one.

_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: In the same way that DoomRL unexpectedly won my heart from ADOM, Jupiter Hell delivers an experience that you can't expect to be as addictive and fulfilling as it is... but once you let this demon into your life you and give it a chance to grow you too will find satisfaction in the well-calculated nuance of slaying your way through a techno-organic space apocalypse with nothing to lose and so much to gain.However this game is a difficult beast to master, with many options to explore mechanically and tactically. If you cannot bear the die and repeat learning of a true roguelike, you will suffer more than your Jupiter Guy. If you're still here, buy this game, it's a diamond for those who like it rough.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the spiritual precursor to this game and was excited to see the news of Jupiter Hell coming years ago.  It did not disappoint.  I believe that this game appeals to both newcomers to the Rougelike genre who don't like a heavy burden of knowledge and also long-time veterans of the genre.  Of particular interest are the ways that you can customize your difficulty to get the experience that you want.  Do you want to win most of the time?  No problem, play on easy.  Do you want more challenge?  Keep walking up the difficulty or use challenge modes until you feel the struggle.I am also looking forward to the future game planned by the developers to make something similar that takes inspiration from the Alien movies.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of playing Jupiter Hell, You could spend hundreds of hours on cookie clickers as well. But there's a definite difference of intensity and meaning behind those hours.Basically Jupiter Hell Guy is a marine who thought that waiting for other's turns on XCOM was wasting his life, and started his own private alien slaughtering business on his own terms. While the game is turn/cover based firearms fighting, the game eats and animates commands so quickly and smoothly, that you could think JH is real time action.Mix in three different character background selections with numerous unique perks and builds, random generated maps, tough but fair difficulty, huge amount of weapon types, armours, modding capabilities threats and challenges on a very painstakingly balanced. Once you get the hang of it, this game starts to drain hours and hours.This game takes the legacy of DoomRL and rocketjumps it to my personal hall of fame.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game.  The new update has made it even better.   Worth every penny.  If you play other roguelikes you know how frustrating it can be to get deep into the game and have to start over.  With Jupiter Hell your average run is only going to take 30 minutes to an hour so it's a lot easier to swallow when you die.  This game is not about being so complex as a game like DCSS or Nethack.  That said there is a lot more going on than is apparent at 1st and the game does have depth and strong tactical decisions to be made.  I think it would make a great 1st game for a player interested in the genre or an old pro.  Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Old-school rogue-like mechanics with DOOM-style violence and story. Graphics are gorgeous, a good amount of variety of builds between the three difference classes - each class with various ultimate arch-types. A lot to like here for those into that stuff. Would love to see what's next from this dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: . I am what you might call a professional reviewer. Jupiter Hell is a turn-based shooter from the depths of cosmic hell and I hope I can give you some insight into why this is one of the most original (and not to mention best looking) releases I've played in years.Much like in what other games have called "nightmares" and "drifting planes of nothingness" I spend much of the first few hours of Jupiter Hell playing this game entirely alone, and it's strange how time seems to fly by when you are enjoying yourself. Jupiter Hell is nothing like any game I've ever played and that's something that I'm really appreciating.Let me just say this from the get-go: Jupiter Hell is a masterpiece, and it's very hard to describe how brilliant it is, but if I were you, I'd at least drop everything you're doing to check out a demo. Just try it once. You won't regret it.***Do you hear what I hear? One of my favorite composers in gaming, Koji Kondo, has composed the score for Jupiter Hell, and I can confirm that it's nothing short of incredible. All the music in the game is a showcase for the genius that is Kondo. Even the background music is fittingly moody, creepy and tense. It's just all so incredibly stunning.It may not have been intended, but the music in Jupiter Hell perfectly compliments the gameplay. I was going to describe some of the themes in the game in this review, but there are simply too many to write about all at once. But I will say this: there is a track called "Prayer for Light" that will take your breath away. It has a truly haunting theme with some heavy bass and powerful drums.Anyway, this is game is what you would call a "rogue lite," meaning it is annoying to play if you want to make progress or not. The enemies come out in waves and they're pretty weak so you just do what the green-haired, shirtless demon hands you. In fact, much of what you need to know to win this game is already in the game, if you look hard enough, so I'll try to summarize some of the elements of the gameplay.The controls are fairly simple, but not nearly as simple as anything out there. You move and aim with the D-pad. Your basic movement direction changes when you take cover behind something, but the placement of cover makes movement in multiple directions a bit more.Part two of my review coming soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Just giving a heads up first that controller support does work. When I launched the game, it did not detect my controller at first. I turned off Steam Input and then it works fine. I guess the game probably has native controller support that doesn't play nice with Steam Input. My entire playtime is with an Xbox controller.I've never played DRL before, but I have tons of experience with other Roguelikes or Roguelites. As far as turn based games go, Jupiter Hell is very fast paced. What I mean is that you don't need to navigate menus for most of your actions be it moving or shooting - you perform them instantly with a press of a button (or combination of buttons). You also don't need to wait for your enemies' turn, since everyone moves simultaneously at the same time. This removes the tedium of waiting in turn based games, and it feels super refreshing to be constantly in the thick of things.As a roguelike, there is no progression and successful runs only rewards you with higher difficulties and unlocks challenges. Your only progression is your deeper knowledge of the game. It took me around 6 hours (including failed runs) for my first completion on the easiest difficulty, and it was a blast. There are also other classes to choose from, and many different weapons and perks to try out so the replayability is there.The atmosphere is great and I especially love the BGM. I never tire of it even when it's played on a loop. Jupiter Hell makes me feel like I'm playing a stop motion version of Doom. This is a real gem and I highly recommended it, even for the "modern" players who think turn based games are slow and tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I really had high hopes for this game, but I'd really just recommend anyone who is interested play DRL instead.I find myself missing many of the things that made DRL special like, destructible terrain, alternate fire modes, assemblies, hazardous terrains, and the ability to carry around gear in inventory.  It feels really samey with all of that stuff stripped out.  This game still has stuff to offer, I like the changes to Traits and the utility slots, DRL had problems but this trade off doesn't feel worth it.I'm definitely not a fan of the new inventory stuff, it seems too cramped, like I can't carry around a lot of the more fun consumables without being at risk of running low on ammo, which leads to me just using the same weapon or two for every encounter, which is a shame cause a lot of the new consumables are really fun.This is more subjective, but I really wish things were more distinct sometimes, a lot of the humanoid enemies look similar but the different weapons they can sport can really screw you up, something that was never a problem with the distinct colorful sprites in DRL.  This game feels best when played at a higher speed, but the visuals are often too dark and muddled to make out clearly (even after you turn off the screen effects).  I also think that the item floor icons would benefit from some borders and heightened contrast.  On brighter floors they can blend into the floor and be harder to make out.I hope this game continues to improve, maybe one day I'll come back to it and be pleasantly surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea behind this but far too much falls into RNG. Every attack (except for a couple of explosives) are hitscan. Taken from its boomer-shooter roots, enemy shots should be projectiles so you at least can dodge them and be presented a choice: stand and shoot or move the character to dodge? Instead it's just a couple of dice rolls until someone falls. It just doesn't feel fun. Heck, even dodging is only accomplished by moving the character where you only receive a dodge percentage and another RNG opportunity. There really isn't a trade off between moving to dodge since the enemy is just going to shoot again.It's a hardcore rogue-like so, in theory, the runs should probably last a couple of levels and you die or reach the end in maybe half an hour. But in reality it's something like 18 levels and my game winning run on easy took something like 3 hours to complete, and since it took about +2 hours to just reach the 12th level, the game will just wipe your save and you need to restart.Rogue-likes usually will have some sort of mechanic that, through playing the game, you improve your initial start with better stats, better unlocked gear, or starting later in the dungeon trek (reach level 10 to unlock level 8 start and a basic loadout). Instead it's just level 1 again with a pistol.It's very disappointing overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like roguelikes? Do you like making meaningful decisions at almost every step you take? Then this is the game for you.Jupiter Hell does what many other games (even some of the greats of the genre) lack: it presents you with a number of options and expects you to (almost) always pick the best one to succeed. This might sound stressful, but believe me, it isn't. The way the game flows and how the gameplay loop (shoot, duck behind cover, move carefully) works, guarantees that the precise decision making expected of you to win a run will lead to a plethora of adrenaline packed situations which play out in seconds and - even though the game is turnbased - will feel like an action movie.There are 3 classes, each of them with a number of skills and "master traits", which basically function like subclasses as you can only pick one on each character and they significantly change how your run will play out. There's also a good variety of guns, melee weapons (although keep in mind that ranged combat is the focus of the game!), relics, exotics and special levels to find and explore.I could go on about how there's also terminals to hack, mods for your weapons, trials and challenges etc. but others have done that in great detail already.If you're a fan of roguelikes (no unlocks in this one that make your character stronger, only additional difficulty levels, trials and challenges) you definitely need to try this. I never thought I could love a game as much as I loved ADOM back in the good old days, but Jupiter Hell might be a strong contester for my personal #1 in the genre.Buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, 1.0.286.9 hrs on record doesn't include the hundreds of hours I spent on the beta test branches, trying out every new feature as soon as I possibly could.This is my favorite roguelike. This is quite possibly my favorite video game of all time.The controls are clean and intuitive, allowing you to focus on the sharp-- and unforgiving-- tactical combat. The guns, especially the big guns, are meaty and satisfying. I *love* plasma. The enemies are varied and plentiful. Between all of the different character builds, all of the different types of weapon and armor, and all of the gameplay modes, Jupiter Hell has more than enough replayability to last the hardcore, dedicated player for the rest of their lives.If you're a roguelike fan, I cannot recommend this game to you strongly enough. And if you are not a roguelike fan, yet, I cannot think of a better game to make you one.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 40+ hours, and the game was fun. This is the most Rogue-like game I have played in a while, and I mean that in the purist terms: this game is a lot like the classic game Rogue (just sci-fi instead of fantasy dungeons.)Most importantly for me, I feel each playthrough is different regarding what gear is found and the gear can be make or break. Combined with the different builds of character, including a blade character that rocks, and you get a varied game. When this is done right in a game, you get a masterpiece like Doom or Rogue, but when done wrong, you get a game where the RNG kills you, and you hate it for only requiring LUCK. While I do die a lot, for most of my 40 hours I have been quick and eager to jump back in. At 40-something years old, this is a rarity in a game nowadays, to play for hours. At my old age, I don't have the gaming patience I once did, back when I was 12 and playing Zelda 2 all night, living off of root beer and microwaved hot dogs. Egads, all those hot dogs.I guess I would call this a true Rogue-like that is a mixture of Doom and a Fallout 1/2 overhead isometric view. (So for isometric fans, this game should be a real winner as well! This is one of the best isometric games I have played in a while, and the gaming world has been full of isometrics the past two years!)WARNING: If you do not like rogue-likes, then do not buy this game, and here is why: Any Doom, even Doom 3, I can beat. Most Dooms I can also beat on real hard levels. Far Cry, on hardest. Darkwood, on hardest. This game? I can barely beat easy, and medium wins are luck-based. I can get a few levels away from beating hard, but for me, there is not enough skill perhaps, even though I tried so many builds...maybe there is too much RNG/luck, and my luck is poor.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: great, addictive game... am struggling to get a win on the "medium" difficulty, so it's no walk in the park. Music score fits to the eerie atmosphere, lots of enemies & weapons and plus mods available to pimp your gear. Since there's three characters with many different "career paths" to choose from, you won't get bored. Did I mention I'm struggling to get a win, yet can't stop trying... damn game caused me another sleepless night  :(
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A cool roguelike implementation of Doom™. At first I wasn't completely sold on the idea and gameplay, because as opposed to more traditional RL's this one is almost exclusively focused on ranged combat. So initially this type of gameplay felt off but I gave it some time and it grew on me. I tried different builds and approaches and finally understood this: while positioning is often very important in traditional RL's, here it is utterlly vital.The presentation is fine overall. The CRT effects are off-puting for me but thankfully they can be disabled entirely. The music is some generic-to-decent metal but I don't think it fits all too well ironically enough. Sometimes you're just sneaking around or exploring and this full on metal blasting on becomes de-tached from reality. This game would greatly benefit from dynamic music. So for now I just mute it. SFX are fine as well for the most part, but it feel like it's lacking some "meaty" effects for when bullets hit a target.Ultimatelly I can easily recommend this to both veterans of RL and newcomers alike, althoug the price seems a bit "steep" (relativelly speaking) for a RL, which I assume is mostly de to the 3D graphics production, which if we're honest is the least concern when it comes to RL, so maybe wait for a sale for the best value. This RL is on the category of "coffe break" RL with shorter runs (my 1st win took less than 5 hours and I took my sweet time) after all. But overall yes it is a fun one, no doubt about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Has promise but the execution is poor.The concept is great, and reminiscent of Orcs & Elves and related spinoff games for mobile a few years back (which I really enjoyed). There's a variety in terms of playing style, old school Doom humour and probably a decent amount of depth, but it ends up grating because it just fails in simple areas like UX/UI and explaining to the player what's going on.This begins with a tutorial which essentially front-loads a lot of information in a short period of time which you are expected to remember, but continues into the actual game where just knowing basic facts like how much damage I'm doing, what the effect of armour is, how different ammo types interact with different enemies etc. is frustratingly difficult and this ruins an otherwise awesome concept. The developers have gone for a retro roguelike vibe but they've done it at the expense of making the game understandable. Watch videos of the UX to see what I mean.It's a shame because with a little extra help, new players would be willing to readily engage with what seems to all intents and purposes like a fun and strategic game. But in its current form, I'd say it's just not worth the bother.Perhaps I'll return to it in future if I feel like making the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to DoomRL, Jupiter Hell succeeds in its focus towards action-heavy roguelike gameplay while maintaining enough item and skill variety to mix up playthroughs and consistently challenges the player as they get more and more skilled at the game with a well-balanced array of difficulties. Would definitely recommend to roguelike aficionados, as well as people who want to get into roguelikes through a visceral and fast-paced experience with solid feedback!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have been supporting this endeavor from the start of early access. Jupiter hell is a great roguelike that does what it does best - allow you to kill the demons and their army by the dozens, while being smart about it. In the nutshell, it is a deep enough experience to warrant learning the ropes and mechanics in play, but it is also a roguelike that allows rng sometimes stack the cards for or against you, making each playthrough unique even when you learn the main mechanics and settle on what is your favorite build. then Challenges come.In short - rip and tear, my friend, rip and tear.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The cover aspect, destructible barricades, gun accuracy, feels like all it does new in the roguelike genre. But without spells I can't really figure out a way to add depth to the gameplay either.  I guess it isn't necessarily the developers fault, but combining FPS with roguelike seems to result in a worse bastardization of both worlds.  Forgive me, as I haven't fully completely the game, but it just seems like optimizations of the same trivial gameplay mechanics, over and over. I guess maybe in place of spells there probably should of been more types of guns besides just 'rootie tootie shooties' though it may be beyond the scope of the developer to program, but there could of been portal guns, acid guns, drone pets, electric guns that arc to enemies, etc... Probably should of been different types of enemies too besides things that just run at you or shoot you.If you enjoy the barebones aspects of roguelikes, of just mindlessly cheesing and clearing enemies in narrow hallways, I guess this is for you. A solid 6/10 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As mostly a turn based strategy player with crappy reflexes, this is the closest thing to a shooter I'll be able to play proficiently.Well, as proficient as you can get with a CRI bot sawing your limbs off.Jokes aside, this is a pretty neat Doom themed Rogue like. Shooting demons over a nice cup o coffee. Active and responsive devs, variety in runs has increased tremendously since EA.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a fantastic effort, polished from start to finish. There are a wide variety of possible builds, a ton of weapons, levels, and enemies, and a significant number of ways to play. The game is turn based but turns can play so quickly that it feels much smoother than many rogue-likes. Different types of enemies offer different sound cues, which rewards experience as you learn to distinguish them before they are ever in line of sight.I particularly like how no two runs ever feel the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enjoyable rogue-like game heavily inspired by Doom. At first, you wouldn't think it would feel so fast paced since its a turn-based game but once you play it for more than a few minutes you quickly realize that you will be mashing keys and playing at almost real-time. The skills you unlock as you play each class feel like they lend to some distinct play-styles and the various challenges and paths for each area adds a lot of variety to every given run. I'd almost call this game "Doom-lite" for when you want to slay demons but want to give your wrist a break from a twitch shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing I'm missing is more characters/classes. However, since all the classes currently available have so many different master traits, resulting in very varied builds, it's not like there's content lacking. I just want more.I call shotgun.---Edit after 40 hours. Finally beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of the final boss on medium. Game's great. I knew, at my initial review 7.3 hours in, that this would be a blast.You should buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This action roguelike plays fast yet has a decent degree of tactics and planning necessary to do well. The visuals are nice and the gameplay & environment exploration rewarding.It may lack the full nostalgic appeal of DoomRL, having its own Doom3-ish theme which doesn't lean heavily on nostalgia for appeal, but instead provides its own setting which is as worthy of the Doom name as any other recent iteration (perhaps even moreso *cough cough Doom Eternal sucks*).The primary strategy involves managing your inventory + your stat choices, so don't expect Nethack-level complexity. This one is meant to be played just shy of realtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like I have been waiting my entire life for a game such as Jupiter Hell to come along. It successfully combines the intense moment-to-moment tactics of an authentic trad roguelike with visceral, fast-paced combat. The result is unlike anything else on the market.Even at this early stage the game impresses. The detailed animation, punchy sound design, and moody atmosphere lend satisfying weight to all of the chaos. Balance seems to be tight and the difficulty fair, which is to be expected from veterans of the genre like ChaosForge. It must be said that the controller support is flawless and downright fun.The devs are super active on the game's Steam community discussion forum, which made the purchase decision easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say this is one of the best EA's I have bought into in recent years.  During my 16+ hours of playing since going EA I have had zero bugs/crashes/etc.  Game stability appears to be quite rock solid thus far.  I still play the predecessor DoomRL/AliensRL and had some concerns with some decision changes to game mechanics etc.  These concerns were quickly washed away as I found myself totally sucked into the game.  Before I knew it hours had passed and a game hasn't done this for me for some time.  I could definitely see this ported to many platforms due to the fact of it's simplicity in design.  The dev's are all very involved with the community and take feedback to heart which is a great thing to see.  I imagine this one becoming one of those gems I play for many many years to come.  I honestly can't recommend Jupiter Hell enough and look forward to things to come.  Money well spent :)UPDATE post 1.0The hours got blown up by leaving game running quite a few times, however, I have still played close to around 800+ actual gameplay hours by now.  Its the main game I play when I have time to play.  Been with it since the EA dropped and has been an amazing experience all the way.  This game is definitely one I will be playing for a long time. Money well spent and looking foward to more games by this dev team.  They take feedback to heart and have worked with their player base to create something really special.  Congrats ChaosForge on 1.0!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Besides the core gameplay being really fun, there are two features of the game that keep me coming back from an accessibility standpoint.- You can exit a run at any point and load back up to the exact same point.- Controller support is amazing. It says partial but it's basically full (you can boot up and play without ever touching the key board).It made it real easy to hop in and out of the game for me.The game itself took me a couple hours before I really got into it. But once I started to figure out how some of the game mechanics work, it really hooked me.Here are a couple tips to help with your first few runs of the game:- The name of the level is in the upper left. When it's blue, you've killed every enemy in the level.- Multitools can be used to repair your armor/helmet.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game since Early Access. It's a worthy successor to DRL, wrapping the same concept in a more modern and superior implementation. To me, it's about the perfect version of the "coffee-break roguelike", with fast-paced turn-based gameplay and lots of tense situations.The game has 3 classes and lots of build possibilities for each class, along with a system of medals and challenges, which makes each run different than the last, and adds lots of additional play value even if you manage to beat the game. Cause make no mistake, you will die plenty of times - most of the time because you made a mistake, sometimes because of bad luck. Should you hit a roadblock, you can always switch to another challenge or medal, or just chill out on an easier difficulty and feel like a badass.Add some hilarious and at times outrageous voice acting from Mark Meer (Male Shepard from Mass Effect, for those that were wondering where they recognized the voice from), a musical score which fits perfectly, and you've got a very engaging cocktail that can keep you entertained for hours. It sure worked for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on Kickstarter, and it's amazing to see it reach Early Access now. It's pure Doom/DoomRL feeling - one HELL of a game.If you liked DoomRL, you will definitely like this one. The best thing about it is that you can play it at your own pace. It's still turn-based, but everything adapts to your speed, which is perfect for different play styles. Sometimes I just want to rush through, go berserk and see how far I can get (and yes, it can be a really hard game!), and sometimes I try to think more, and take it step by step.Looking forward to seeing more content being added to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Steam game review ever.After 800 hours of playing, today I decided to delete the game because of "questionable design decisions."Here are some of the things that recent upgrades brought in that I absolutely hate:1. It is harder to find cover on the new maps. Many rooms have too many doors that mobs could come in at the same time. Why on earth would someone design rooms like that?2. Mobs no longer seem to be randomly scattered on the map; instead, they ambush players in masses. Sometimes in a map, there are only two spots where I ever exchange fire with them, and together with 1) and those watcher f*ckers, consumables are used a lot quicker.3. Some new enemies are too strong. WTF is the ADAPTIVE attribute? I was playing as a gunslinger/sniper, but I could not take down one of these after 20 rounds, and this is INSANE. I remember in earlier versions this build was meant to be a glass cannon that could almost one-shot everything.The creator of the game may argue, "it is for the better balance of the game." However, most players do not care about game balance. Look at Binding of Isaac; it has no game balance whatsoever, but it is one of the most loved roguelites by people. Sometimes we just want to have one hour of fun, but the creator decides to make it harder with every update.I still remember playing Nethack, I die a lot, YASD (yet another stupid death). No big deal, my fault and I could do better next time. For this game, recent deaths make me feel played.It is still a fine game, but not as fun anymore, at least at UV which I usually go with.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game when it first came out on my older Steam account and absolutely loved it. Something about the gritty atmosphere, the sound design and the tactical choices all combine to create what I think is one of the best modern roguelikes on the market. Took a year off of PC gaming and this was one of the first games I repurchased when I returned. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: That old Doom feeling in a roguelike wrapper... Decent enough to try, good enough to keep playing.Caveat: I haven't tried it on anything but normal difficulty, I've only played a single run, and I compulsively swapped the movement controls to WSAD ("drop" key from D to E, "equipment" from E to O) and turned off the CRT geometry effect before event trying it on stock settings. Knee-jerk habits.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't have assumed that permadeath turn-based and "90s carnage shooter" were a good mix until I played this game. And the lead developer is active on youtube/discord and already confirmed that there will be ongoing development (so the game is only going to get better and more expansive)Easily the best game I've purchased this year, utterly addictive. If you like turn based games at all, don't pass up on this one. for people with specific roguelike questions: 1) yes, there's a config file to bypass all the 'progression' unlocks. 2) the game has a large number of conducts built-in, great for replayability.3) there are a lot of unique branches, and the item variety is great. 4) like many other modern roguelikes there is (almost) no backtracking.5) I see an 'ascii' mode switch in the config, but I think this feature is not yet functional on all platforms. 6) a typical ascension takes about 1-2 hours, speedruns have this under 10 minutes already.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is the ultimate evolution of DoomRL.An incredibly fun and fast paced ACTUAL roguelike about shooting demons.And yes, real roguelike, hard as titanium steel, savage like jupiter demons, with a dungeon that has several floors to explore and die in, with random loot and layouts, dangerous enemies and resource management.No long term bonuses, complete wipe on death.Survive and kill while listening to an incredible metal as heck soundtrack, let it energize you.Oh, and the UI is pretty... pretty, slick and in hellish colors.I played demos for a while, and the full version is even better.Definitely gonna waste several tens of hours on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I never really got into DRL, but this spiritual successor to it had me thoroughly gripped for a long, long time. It's got a lot of traditional roguelike DNA in it, but the turn-based gunplay feels very fresh and unique. There are a lot of different ways to build out the three starting classes, and the inclusion of 'challenge' runs with specific restrictions is a great way to explore the strengths of those different builds. Mastering the systems and figuring out how to become an unstoppable demon blender is deeply satisfying.The one caveat I have is that I really recommend you turn off the main character's little voiced quips—which, fortunately, the game anticipates you might want to do. They're not offensive or anything, just... boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review for the latest patch - Master Traits.Master Traits are out, and they are fantastic. They ramp up the power level and offer various ways to play all classes. Favorites so far are GHOST (greatly improves the invisibility skill), ASSASSINATE (teleport from enemy to enemy & murder them), GUN KATA (fire your pistols automatically while moving) and ARMY OF DARKNESS (makes shotguns spew death and destruction).The game also has gotten a rebalance, to even out the increased power level of all 3 classes.I would say that now is a great time to pick up the game if you were hesitant before.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I really like roguelikes and turnbased combat.  I found this game really boring though.  I will give it another few chances,  but it just feels like walk around, stand in place and press f until everything walking towards you is dead.  If I could get a refund to buy another game I might actually enjoy I would defs swap it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Highly addictive classic roguelike gameplay.  Everything seems simple enough when you first start, you will probably worry it is too simple to sustain interest.  However, the more you play the more you it dawns on you how granular the moment to moment decision making is.  Simple changes in approach such as which side of a door to hide on can make run ending differences.  The more you invest in learning the minutiae, the more rewarding and satisfying the experience.  It is very much not a game for everyone, but one of the best games I've played in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A Doom inspired roguelike with ranged combat mechanics. You fight your way through space stations and weird dig sites and fight demons and other creatures. There's a lot of replayability with different difficulty levels and challenges, and the different builds you can make vary up the gameplay quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great modern take on the traditional roguelike formula. The streamlining of gameplay was done beautifully allowing a quicker pace of playing while retaining many aspects core to a traditional roguelike. Graphics are also modernised vastly increasing approachability for a first time player of the genre, which seem like a major hurdle when talking to others about ascii or even tilebased traditional roguelikes.Geniuinely can not, at the time of writing, think off a facet of the game i would like executed differently, exepte maybe changing the difficult curve of using a melee weapon as it feels heavily frontloaded to the first part of a run.For someone who plays traditional roguelikes frequently, The fact that the games focuses on ranged combat in the form of guns is, somewhat refreshing as most other games in the genre either focus on ranged magics or bows/spears/sling for non melee based combat interactions. All in all amazing for both new and returning players to the genre, a steal at the current prize and a must buy during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of bugs with level generation.  Also crashes quite often.  Content is fairly lacking and not even up to the quantity that was available in the free game that this was based on.  Game has many serious balance issues and runs often end due to random absurd spikes in difficulty.  Every update makes things worse, with the latest 1.4.0 patch introducing far more crashes and making the game balance even worse.Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: First i have to say that I'm strongly into the rogue-like genre and I was excited about this game, due to gorgeous visuals and animations. I watched some game-play videos/streams and it seemed pretty cool.But sadly, I didn't play it much before i asked a refund, because after only 3 runs i got already bored about the lack of enemies and weapons variety. Sure the floors layouts are proceduraly generated, but that's all. The first 5-6 floors (didn't go more far) are always filled with same enemies and i was always using the same weapons, only changing it for the same ones with an upgrade.About gameplay? The concept is cool but once you figured it out you always do the same pattern: spot enemies, hide behind a wall, shoot until it dies, repeat. Got bored pretty fast from that, honestly i was expecting more. It would have been ok if we had more enemies/weapons variety, but the combination of both really reduce the replayability by a lot to me, wich is a shame for a classic rogue-like. Also the class system (3 classes) make some slights differences but the gameplay stays overall the same from what i saw (i might be wrong as i didn't go far), unlike other classic rogue-likes where changing class makes it a completely different experience.This game also has other issues in my opinion:-Can't use the mouse at all, even when navigating in the UI, or for aiming. I understand that most classic rogue-likes players are used to use keyboard only, but guys, these games are from the 90's, and we are in 2020. There are classic rogue-likes like TOME, Cogmind or even recently StoneShard that have full mouse integration, as it should be. No mouse at all feels like a big step back for a game that has a modern visual design.-The zoom: by default the game is zoomed in a way that you can't see details like which weapons enemies are using, you can zoom in FROM THE MENU as a setting but not directly in-game, wich looks like a very bad game design choice. Also even with the default zoom (maxed out), the camera angles makes it so sometimes you don't see enemies from south that are in range to shoot you.Jupiter Hell may become better in the future, since it's still in early-access and has potential, afterall almost everything i complain about can be improved. Also i have to admit that admins seems commited to the game and you can feel some love into it, so i might change my review if it become good enoughin a few patches/release. But as it is now, i can't recommand it for it's price, particularly if you expect a great replayability like in other classic rogue-likes.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's an acquired taste... aka have to be a masochist...ridiculously repetitive, I mean more than usual rogue like games and absolutely underwhelming in terms of character/player growth. You're skills mean nothing almost compared to a decent/good gun drop... overall, don't buy unless there's a massive discount on it
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a roguelike/light player for a over decade now. Some personal favorites include DCSS, Synthetik, Cogmind, ♥♥♥, DOOMRL etc. Jupiter Hell absolutely has what it takes to satisfy many hours of dungeon diving. With my first run, I had the impression that there was not as much depth in the gameplay as I like. I was definitely wrong in making this judgement. JH is just very easy to get into. Accessible enough that on an easier difficulty you can just blow through enemies and grab whichever guns look neato.However, after a handful of runs on harder difficulties and reaching the more difficult content it becomes clear that building a character with clear synergies is absolutely necessary. I've had my most success with a hyper-ammo-efficient-dual-wielding-pistol-crit-machine marine and a hacker technician who uses blankets of smoke and stolen mechs for mayhem. Reaching the network terminal as a hacker and turning all the bots friendly is a riot. All around you in rooms you can't see there are suddenly gunfights and explosions as those turrets the soldiers thought were protecting them suddenly become hostile.I've been playing with a controller and they've figured out a very nice scheme allowing easy play. Really the only gripe I have is with the UI. I feel like the inventory and various interface screens could be a little more user friendly. When I'm applying a mod to a gun and my choices are optimal range+1 or maximum range +1, I have to back out of the menu entirely, go into my inventory to see those stats on each gun, then reopen the mod pack and remember which gun I wish to apply the mod to. It'd be nice if the mod window showed the gun/armor etc stats and exactly how they would change. Concerning graphics, they're great for what Jupiter Hell is. I did turn off the CRT bend effect and black frame effect. If that turns you off, know there are many options in the menu to fine tune the setting or just turn it all the way off.Each death so far has felt fair and I'm just excited to start a new run. Very happy with my purchase and I foresee playing JH for many more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. A wonderful mix of classic turn based rogue-likes and DOOM. Your class choices and combinations are all cool and have meaningful impact on the way you play the game. The guns feel cool, and the difficulty curve is spot-on-  allowing you to feel like the Doomslayer carving through minions one moment and then slamming your head into an elite or boss.Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best and most balanced traditional roguelikes in existence.  Systems are in depth enough to be interesting without being cumbersome.  Challenging without being unbalanced.Particularly nice as it's the only traditional roguelike I've ever played with well made and easy to use controller controls.A+++ would buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I'd held off on buying this game to wait for some features to be added for increased build diversity, but I picked it up recently and am glad I did. If you're a genre newcomer, this is a great place to start. If you're a veteran, it's worth your time too.The controls are easy to learn and simple enough that you can reasonably play the game with a controller. This is  common in a genre where many classics manage to use an entire keyboard (or more!) worth of commands. Jupiter Hell manages this through tightly focused turn-based tactical gameplay - both combat and exploration.Overall the game feels a bit on the easy side for the genre, but that doesn't mean it's easy. If you think it is, there are several challenge runs available to make the game harder. Based on the official forums, some of these have never been completed on higher difficulties - there's no record of AoNY have ever been completed on Hard, let alone on the top difficulty "Ultraviolence." The dev team only manged it once and on easy. Good luck.Verdict: ----Launch edit: AoNY has gotten a bit easier and Ultraviolence is no longer the hardest difficulty. Still recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent traditional roguelike with modern sensibilities, making it a nice introduction to the genre. Still expect to die a lot.  Runs great on the deck, and has mouse support.I didn't spend much time with this when I first got it, but the devs keep pushing new content, and this last update pulled me back in.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a traditional roguelike currently under development in Early Access, set on a futuristic moon station that you might recognize from the golden era of ‘90s gaming.  You play as a Totally-Not-Doom-Guy fighting for desperate survival against swarms of demons and zombie soldiers armed to the teeth.  Along the way you’ll find plenty of pistols, shotguns, grenades, medkits, and BFGs to fend off the hordes of hades.  Sound familiar?Roguelike games are best described as a turn-based WEGO version of the original Diablo on hardcore mode.  You start at the first level of a procedurally generated dungeon and fight petty enemies and work your way down to the deadly bosses and beasts at the bottom.  Anything can permakill you fast if you’re not careful.  The action takes place on a grid and all units’ moves are calculated simultaneously, usually with speed stats to determine who moves first.  Thus, you can sometimes squeeze in “extra” turns if your speed is higher than the enemies.These games typically have medieval fantasy settings, and they require you to use nuanced tactical thinking to properly utilize a staggering variety of spells and magic scrolls available.  It’s common for newbies and experienced players alike to die with inventories full of situationally life-saving equipment.  Jupiter Hell stands apart from the genre by offering a meaty, no-nonsense guns-n-grenades tactical turn-based combat experience instead of magic and swords.  Anybody who has played classics like X-Com and Shrapnel’s 101st Airborne in Normandy should feel right at home – only instead of a squad of poor schmucks tottering into the dark, it’s just you and your gun.You start Jupiter Hell by creating a player character.  You choose between three classes – Marine, Scout, and Technician – each with their own starting equipment and special abilities.  The Marine starts with a medkit and has some self-heal abilities, making him an ideal first-timer class.  The Scout starts with a .44 revolver, has a stealthy cloaking ability, and begins every floor with the exit locations mapped out for quicker access.  The Technician starts with a few multitools, which are used to open doors or hack consoles to gain map data, track enemies via radar, or even command security bots to kill everything on the floor.  Technicians can also use consumables faster than most, and can throw down a smoke screen in a pinch.Each of these classes use different forms of “mana” to power their special abilities: Fury, Energy, and Power, respectively.  These are earned by killing enemies, opening chests, and picking up orbs from dead enemies – again, respectively.  Once you’ve accumulated enough “mana,” you can activate your ability to use a quick flourish that might save your life.  This is one of the newer systems introduced to Jupiter Hell, adding to the legacy of the free downloadable DoomRL and making the game just a bit more accessible to newcomers.In addition to pretty graphics and nice voice acting, this retail release enhances the combat by adding a bit more tactical depth.  The biggest improvement is the cover system: Walls and obstacles add to-hit maluses against targets in cover, with higher maluses for better cover, making it advantageous to maneuver into cover or around an enemy’s flank.  Additionally, you can “hunker” by spending a turn paused behind cover, gaining a temporary bonus to defense and your next shot.  This is a welcome addition to other features carried over from the free version, such as pain from wounds incurring penalties to your to-hit rating.The inventory management is streamlined from the original free roguelike, which is a benefit for newcomers to the genre.  You have a backpack limited to ammo and consumables.  You also have several weapon slots which can be used for anything from firearms to melee weapons, and you have slots for armor (helmet, chest, boots), but you can’t store any spare firearms or armor in your inventory as they must be equipped or dropped.  This feels like a bit of a drawback compared to the original where you could store spare armor and weapons, but this may have been done in an effort to balance new features that give the player an edge.  Overall I don’t find this change distracting as a fan of the original free game.Another apparent drawback is that you can only have one character at a time, which is an odd choice.  Hopefully they decide to implement multiple character files before the full release.  In the true spirit of a roguelike, I’ve yet to survive far into the labyrinths of Jupiter’s moon before being blown up, shot dead, or eaten alive.  My first impression of the game is very strong, though it’s clear that there’s still work to be done in Early Access.  I strongly recommend this game to fans of the roguelike genre, and cautiously recommend it for interested newcomers.  The free DoomRL delivers another awesome tactical turn-based gunfighting experience, along with similar free games like AliensRL (set in the James Cameron movie), Cataclysm DDA (zombie apocalypse), and Infra Arcana (Lovecraftian 1920s).  However, these games lack proper 3D graphics and mostly rely on either community-made sprite packs or ASCII symbols that take time to interpret on the fly.  As such, Jupiter Hell is a fine entry point into the genre.So if you always wanted to play Doom but lacked the reflexes, Jupiter Hell is a fantastic tactical challenge that will demand a lot for you to succeed.  Look up those keybindings, be patient with your moves, and prepare to die a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game and ADOM are 2 of the best rougelikes in existence.  Have you heard rougelike and rougelite thrown around for just about every game nowadays?  Get this game and experience what those games are supposed to be like.  Now if you've ever struggled through the ANSCII version of dwarf fortress you may know that graphics can be a boon to rougelikes.  This game is beautifully rendered, with lighting and fog effects, sometimes the ambiance is darn spooky.  The turn based gameplay can feel turn based in complicated situations, but can feel fluid once you get the hang of things.  Personally I enjoyed shooting an i or a h and seeing it splattered against the ..#+###^.... and its a wonder to see this project come to fruition.   The traits system and items are also very well done, I'm sure there will still be some tweaks to them, but these systems have been pretty well polished over 15 years or so.  The player record is also excellent, even counting creature kills and kill types.  I haven't had a chance yet to see if item mod patterns have made it into this one, but even if they didn't there is a rich weapon and item arsenal to hope you're lucky enough to find.  One thing I'm enjoying is the exotic(?) item experience level, where you find a super rare powerful item, and then as you gain experience it gains levels too, I found a helmet that disabled security robots on sight : o I would recommend getting this game even if you put thousands of hours into the previous projects, because now everyone can see the steam achievements ^_^I have been a longtime fan of doomrl, I played it before it got the graphical overlay with mouse.   I even managed to get a pacifist win nuking the cybermind on hard in one of the later ANSCII versions.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better "true" contemporary roguelikes even in Early Access. Fans of it's spiritual predecessor (DoomRL) may find it's systems lacking, but comparisons are mostly unfair as this is a new game made by the same developer and not simply a graphical version of DoomRL. The simplifications make the game less tedious and the player less dependent on monotony for advantage. However, this is still a hardcore and unforgiving roguelike. It's graphics and simple controls make it a great intro to roguelikes, and full gamepad support allows you to kick back and strategize. This game also works great played via Steam Link on a Smartphone or whatever.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm curious to see how this game develops, but for now its not fun.The basic of mechanics and look/feel of the game seem pretty solid, but there is a real lack of things to do.  I enjoy rogue-likes for their itemization and complexity that requires numerous failed play through to learn how to be successful at the game.  There are very few items and game play is pretty straight forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of positive reviews for this product and I see most people talking about all the good things this game has to offer, but there's one thing nobody mentions: this game has the perfect retro UI. Incredibly attractive rendering with screen curvature, bloom, jitter, static noise, glow lines, flickering, horizontal sync, -- I mean they are really capturing the feel of P3 phosphor CRTs in these menus (devs add some burn-in please for the full Wyse experience). Incredibly cozy and nostalgic, like everything else about this game. This thing is mechanically lacking and sadly very short. I wish they would do a lot more with it, but in terms of aesthetics this is the perfect roguelike experience. If you play roguelikes, you have to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: To say it in the words of the hero: Looks good – feels good!The game is extremely fun and addictive and strikes the perfect balance between hard challenges and success. And while it is turn based, it's all handled so efficiently it still feels so fast paced and action packed that sometimes you get carried away in a fight (Warning: Usually doesn't end well).There is plenty of variety to explore in classes, builds, game modes etc., and the areas where some might want to see a little more diversity are now actively worked on by the dev with the post release updates.So, if you like an atmosphere uncannily similar to Doom presented with beautiful gfx engine this is a definite recommendation.If you excuse me now, I got a few more demons to kill. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a true roguelike - turn based, top-down, permanent death. It is difficult, it is often unfair, and it is very rewarding once you start understanding the systems in place. You will need to play defensively and use chokepoints to survive. Being caught in the open is a death sentence. Every death is a learning experience and is mostly avoidable with correct play. A worthy successor to DoomRL. Blowing up demons with a shotgun never gets old.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really loving this game! It's super fun and interesting, good balance of complexity and approachability. The developer seems great, I really love all the updates we've been getting so far. Looking forward to the extra music coming soon!If I had to come up with a downside: it's surpisingly heavy on your GPU.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most bad-ass fast-paced action-turn-based game I've ever played. Don't let "turn-based" turn you off. Slick interface and key interactions make this game incredibly fast to play (if you want to). It's more like simulturn. Or instaturn. Love the spicy humor, too (you can adjust profanity levels in the settings). Strongly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of D**mRL, it was only natural that I'll be interested in its spiritual successor.So, I've got this game as soon as it had hit open Early Access on Steam. Truth be told, I was somewhat disappointed initially.The game was lacking several vital features of its predecessor and didn't provide enough to compensate for that.However, while that was the case before, I don't think this is true now.Over time, the game had evolved considerably, gaining more and more features of its own, becoming more robust and engaging.So, aside from a possibly negative initial impression of Jupiter Hell simply not being more of the same, it otherwise does a great job of adapting and expanding most of the core elements that made D**mRL a great game.All in all, Jupiter Hell is a great modern roguelike well worth trying out.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A Spiritual successor of DRL, finley crafted hellish mayhem in a sauce of rouge-like genre. Fancy crafted graphics, DOZENS of loot, mass of enemies, gibs, lore-bits and turn-based-shooting and walking. Pick your classic rougelike, dress it in clad-cool marine armor, give it a gun, blade, and load of enemies and you will have Jupiter Hell. Incredibly robust and stylish game that make me angry  time to time but death and restart is always typical for rougelikes. Make me want return for more and reach another medal of Carrnage, or try different build with different set of skills and weapons. After good dozen of updates it have contet enough for couple of such games so Chaosforge made a lot of nice work to make this game trully a gem.So if you seasoned DooM-fan, rouge-like-enthusiast or even both - this game is nice time and money investment. PRO - It's freaking DOOM-Themed Rougelike - that enough reason for me to play! :D. _childDocuments_.review: Best roguelike I've played in a long time.The ranged based combat means you're always seeking out cover and thinking things through, even on the easier levels. The common problems with roguelikes, inventory management and food, don't exist here. The amount of stuff you can carry is just right with no encumbrance and there is no stupid food mechanic which constantly pits you against the clock. The combat is tense enough that it doesn't need it.The music is very good and the graphics are what you'd expect from a roguelike which are functional, nothing special.Difficulty-wise, I'm playing on I think medium and I'm pretty far in without having been killed yet. That said I've been smacked around a few times and don't feel like I'm unkillable or don't have to pay attention. I don't see even a beginner to roguelikes getting frustrated by this unless they're playing on easy.I got this on a 20% sale. Full price I think is a bit pricey for a roguelike, even a good one, but I wouldn't be upset if I had paid full price.

name: ANIMAL WELL
detailed_description: Hatch from your flower and spelunk through the beautiful and sometimes haunting world of Animal Well, a pixelated wonder rendered in intricate audio and visual detail. Encounter lively creatures small and large, helpful and ominous as you discover unconventional upgrades and unravel the well’s secrets. This is a truly unique experience that can make you laugh in fear, surprise, or delight. Dense atmospheric puzzle box world with tons of secrets Light candles for safety and gradually fill out your map Nonlinear -- explore and collect items in whatever order you choose Enemies, environment, and items interact in surprising and systemic ways All items have multiple uses Learn how innocuous details can become meaningful The main game is just the beginning. Players will be discovering hidden puzzles for years Assess for yourself what is safe and dangerous Focus on tension and suspense rather than action You are disempowered, but can make clever use of your environment and items
