_childDocuments_.review: EDIT Post 100% completion of the game: I would say, for the first layer of the game, 100% of the puzzles do not require a guide, are reasonably thought through, and reward thinking outside the box on completing some of them with one of the best items in any puzzle game, period. However, after the first layer, and you've beaten the game, and you achievement hunt, I think you'll find it less and less likely you'll be able to do it all alone, even keeping a keen eye some of the layer 2/layer 3 puzzles were solved as a consorted group effort of minds, and not something a majority of individuals will accomplish solo. And if you value your time, and still seek 100% of achievements, I'd say, give the map your best comb over a couple times post game completion, and whatever else you can't find, bust a guide out, it gets pretty esoteric towards the end and I can't in good conscience say it's something to be tackled blindly. Still a fantastic game, I enjoyed every hour of it even as the frustration piled on, the satisfaction was always worth it.I can't tell if I've managed to break the game with one of the items I've acquired or if it's designed for me to subvert puzzles with it. Either way it's amazing while still challenging to pull off.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to this year's Fez-alike. This is a great platformer, with some novel movement mechanics and a gorgeous visual aesthetic. It is fun to explore and fun to obsessively try to find all the hidden objects. It has a bit of the meta, but thankfully never fully breaks the fourth wall. There isn't much narrative so much as a vibe, so don't go in expecting the next Ori or Hollow Knight. There is no combat, which works extremely well and makes the game a bit more mellow and approachable. It is a relatively pleasant way to spend 15-20 hours. A bit of criticism:The early-to-mid-game is much better than the late game. Congrats to Mr Basso, looking forward to more interesting things to come!

_childDocuments_.review: In 2022 I finished Elden Ring. In 2023 I got to the final boss of Baldur's Gate 3 but didn't finish it because I did not want the game to be over. I can confidently say that this is my GOTY so far, and it may even stay that way for the rest of 2024.The art, the sound, the ambiance, the puzzles that respect my intelligence, the extremely tight platforming, and just the way I  playing this game are all so completely joyous together. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An inspired retro-style experience. Best gone into blind, this beautiful indie gem is absolutely worth your time, especially if you enjoy combing through a game for secrets.I wanted to play this sooner, but waited for a slight sale to justify adding it to my already massive backlog. Animal Well is the first game for both its developer and publisher, and they unquestionably hit a grand slam. It's hard to define the genre here, but if you like search action (Metroidvanias), puzzle platformers, or just exploring idiosyncratic games with one hell of a vibe, buy this now.The story is surreal and barely present until you really start grinding out post-game secrets, so I won't go into detail. You are a little plant-born blob thingy guy, and you set out to find four flames. Along the way you'll collect a variety of literal toys which will enable you to overcome new challenges and explore an unsettling, gorgeous underground world. Along the way you'll meet both helpful and antagonistic ghosts, animals, and ghost animals.The runtime is short, only requiring about 6-8 hours to roll credits, but in that time you'll only scratch the surface of what is on offer; namely secrets galore. While the map can be a little overwhelming, it's pretty well-designed for hunting every pixel of every room for cryptic collectable eggs and other puzzles. I personally found about forty of the sixty-four eggs, and there are still a few big riddles for me to run down when I feel like picking this title back up in the future.Animal Well was an obvious labor of love, and it's an absolute treat to experience. It's gorgeous, dreamlike, and ingenious. I'm so glad there is a market for niche art like this, and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys indie gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The decency of the puzzles does not justify how much this game willfully ♥♥♥♥♥ on your time. This is not a metroidvania, this is a needle in a haystack simulator that you get mildly improved tools to search with over time. If you enjoy having your time wasted by pointlessly ignoring all the quality of life changes games have made in the past 30 years, this is for you. Now the puzzles can be good. At best, small g good. The general basic puzzles starting off are cool, you get tools to help you do them, and they can be solved in multiple ways (which is the neatest part). As you get more tools you can break puzzles more and more to the point that they stop being interesting. At that point the puzzles start to get very large and meta-y. But throughout all of this the game ♥♥♥♥♥ on your time with a deliberateness that is reminiscent of the "getting over it" and "only up" genres. You don't fully lose your progress, but the checkpoint system is straight out of the 90s and often failing an attempt at a puzzle will throw you way back in nowhere so you have to re-traverse stuff just to get back to the platforming puzzle you were attempting. If you want puzzle platforming, just go pick up Celeste, it is far better and respects your time. Then there's the absurd amount of stuff that is hidden behind random walls you have to try and break. Again, straight out of the SNES/super metroid days, it's not a fun mechanic it just wastes your time. Then you get a late game unlock and have to go reexplore the ENTIRE map to see if it happens to do anything anywhere. There is no indication on the map of whether or not you've fully found everything in that room, again, games have known how to do better than this for 20 years now. Again, JUST WASTING TIME. Give this game a few quality of life changes and it becomes REALLY neat. Better checkpoints when you fail a puzzle. A map that has some indication of whether or not a room is cleared so you don't have to re-check literally THE ENTIRE MAP when you get some powerups. Until then, just watch a streamer play it. This kind of disrespect for the players time is good for them, it means more content.

(get ready for a rant)Even though this is a 2024 published game: ⁃ the mouse is disabled ⁃ it's not possible to rebind keys ⁃ the keyboard controls are hard-coded for the US keyboard layout ⁃ continue/interact and cancel/back are the same key… except when they are not When the f*ck are we? the 2010s?Look I get that this game is supposed to be played with a controller but some people (like myself) prefer mouse & keyboard and In addition, not everyone uses a US keyboard layout.And please just let me use my mouse to click on menu items. Especially in the map I'm constantly struggling pressing the correct keys because the controls are just not intuitive.I'm loving the game so far and less-than-ideal controls are not anywhere near enough to make me not enjoy the game.It's just something that is really starting to piss me off in platforming games.A barely functioning keyboard support is slapped on to at least have something, but you're almost always handicapping yourself if you do decide to use it.I appreciate that it's in at all, I guess, but I can't help but feel like the devs (or whoever is in charge of it) don't give a sh*t about me as a mouse & keyboard user. _childDocuments_.review: animal well is an amazing experience. I have never played any game that comes close to the mood and style of this game, and don't even get me started on the puzzles. I myself solved 8 secret bunnies on my own, and the rest as I've seen I either overlooked or were simply very very out of my playing field.the technical aspect:this game is insanely large and complex for a game smaller than the steam artwork of it, or a 3 minute speedrun of it. there's a huge map to explore, and no room is innocent. the remarkable size of this game compared to the features and content of the game, seems like wizardry, but is simply born from the genius of the creator billy basso, who took it upon himself to code up his own engine in C or C++, using opengl I believe. games made in opengl are usually rather simple due to the limited scope of opengl only giving you very simple shader control to draw images to the screen (correct me if I'm wrong about billy using opengl). an empty unity project is larger than the entire game.additionally, the art direction of the game, is amazing, including, on top of the gorgeous pixel art in many places; navier stokes fluid simulations which interact with the environment in real time, a great lighting system which gives such a unique moody and dark feeling to the environments and more.the gameplay:animal well is a puzzle platformer metroivania in all senses of the term. it's a metroidvania; going from room to room you are bound to see in almost any room you pass a dark corner that doesn't seem like a solid wall, too high up to reach, behind spikes, behind a locked door, and more. eventually, you'll be meeted with a toy, an item that can be used in a way similar to their real life counterparts, each one with its own unique behavior. seeing the slinky for the first time, you can't really think of much to do with it, but the game manages to condition you to start looking for stairs automatically and you are bound to eventually find a secret, or a puzzle you had no clue how to solve. you will see many of these, like the disc, the bubble wand, the top, the bouncy ball, all of these seemingly innocent objects all have several hidden uses, which you will either never find or find on accident, which will make you think of where they are applicable, and consequently find a lot more animal well to explore and ponder upon.the platforming, even if it's a puzzle game, that doesn't mean there's no platforming. the controls are extremely responsive, having your character starting to accelerate on the very next frame after you push an input with very short acceleration, making for a very precise to control character, which feels very good to control, akin to madeline from celeste, or the knight from hollow knight. and that fun movement isn't wasted on simple jumps from one platform to another, there's plenty of challenging platforming you can take on, not forced upon you but indeed rewarding, with almost any place you can think of that would be cool to hide something does have something to hide, however hard it is to get there. unfortunately you won't find any path of pain level challenges, but it's completely fine for what this game wants to be.and now, for the crown jewel; the puzzles.I can never completely describe the puzzles of this game, prized endlessly for its innovative puzzle design. anything I would say about the more complex puzzles would spoil them, so read on with caution, the 2 people who will read this. this game's secrets and puzzles are split into 3 (technically 4) "layers" as the creator billy basso puts it.the layers are described as:layer 1: the secrets and puzzles that most players solve in their playthrough, not terribly difficult, but can be sometimes stumping without paying too much mind to it.layer 2: the eggs. the eggs are collectibles scattered around the well, usually involving either solving a puzzle to get them, finding a secret location in which they lie, or finding a secret location in which a puzzle is that guards that egg. these are not terribly difficult to find but most players won't find more than about 10 of them if they don't look for them.layer 3: the bunnies. the bunnies are unique puzzles, not very abundant in the well, with only 16 existing in the game. every bunny is extremely obscure and hard to solve, at least most of them are, but all of them are unique. here comes the spoilery part: my favorite bunny that I found myself, was one which to solve its puzzle, you needed to take a screenshot of some grass in some room, make it black and white in some editing software, brighten the highlights and darken the shadows, crop it, and voila, you've got a barcode, which you need to scan to get a code of 8 digits from 1-8, which correspond to directions you need to play the flute in, while in that room, to open a path to the secret bunny.I cannot describe how deep this game goes. there have been multiple args for it, even before launch, with great puzzles involving background objects from a video of an interview with billy basso the creator. there's not a single thing I don't like about this game, I myself have not yet completed it fully, but I'm getting close. unfortunately I've been spoiled as to how to get the rest of the bunnies and other stuff I was missing, so perhaps I'll never fully solve this game myself, but damn do I recommend you to play it.final thoughts:animal well is a game, so well thought out, I think of potential puzzles and tinfoil theories for it in my sleep. the graphics are insane, there's no computer that can't handle it, it's smaller than a picture in byte size, and contains so so so much to do and explore and ponder about and solve. the only other game I've played that is even close to the puzzles of this game is Tunic, which is a critically acclaimed game for its ingenuity and style, and animal well's puzzles blow it out of the water. (tunic is one of my favorite games play it too)it's a must play; and it certainly is worth the money, even if it's somewhat pricey. billy deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game with one really big problem: there's no rebinding support. This is an absurd thing for a 2024 release, people should not have to resort to third party applications to rebind keyboard controls. If you're going to be lazy and demand that people use a controller, don't even build in keyboard controls.A second, much less big problem is that the puzzle design in this game -- even along the main path -- can sometimes be *intensely* obscure, to the point that there's at least one puzzle that basically needs you to backtrack through the entire game looking at random ♥♥♥♥ until you remember that a specific item exists, if you didn't remember that immediately when seeing the puzzle. While I generally love obscure puzzle games, I think a little more playtesting would reveal a couple trouble spots that could use some very gentle signposting.I am still really enjoying the game despite these problems, and if the keybinding issue is resolved I will absolutely change this to a positive review, with the caveat that this game is very definitively a puzzle game first and a platformer/metroidvania second, and as such is definitely not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the good: * The game has a cool style and looks great as an art style goes. * It is a metroidvania game, and mostly plays like one. * The music during the save areas is pretty cool.The bad: * The sounds, while they may match the gritty pixel art, are mostly grating and terrible. * The graphics themselves are pretty messy and it's frequently hard to see what's part of the environment vs part of the actual map. I would say the game looks good but the actual game suffers greatly due to the art/graphics. * There's a lot of terrible perfect pixel and/or perfect time puzzles that are just lame, annoying and stupid. * The cat boss is one of the worst boss fights in the history of man. * There is a lot of bad and confusing level design. * Overall, the map is kind of terrible and hard to read and use.All in all, I would say skip this, unless it's on sale for $5.While it has a pretty damn high score on Steam, it seems like very few people have actually played this game all the way through, and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Iz good. Vary big mode.So it's a very cool, cute, little game about solving puzzles, and those puzzles are really satisfying to solve.The art style is obviously peak brilliance.Tremendously, this game kind of taught me about how to make a boss more terrifying than pretty much all other bosses. There was a moment in the game where I could choose to overcome the boss (and likely fail), or I could run away and maybe come back later or find another way around. The game didn't force me to either fight (like most games) or run away (like most scary games). It gave me a choice, and as soon as I saw the boss, I literally noped out of the arena.I think there must be something going on psychologically where if a person chooses to flee from danger when they have the option to fight, it's way more impactful and visceral. Like fight-or-flight is going off, and my brain is feeling something sincere as if it's real danger. I need to think about that more. I think there's something to that.A lot of AAA games focus on breadth rather than depth. Like you have dozens of hours to do the exact same stuff again and again and again, and a lot of content is copy-pasted throughout the world or levels.It's awesome how many unique moments in this game had me go, "Oh, wow. Look at that." Or, "OMG. WHAT IS GOING ON?"There are so many rooms the character walks into where something completely novel is taking place or a unique challenge that must be overcome.My biggest complaint is kind of just that at about the last 15% of the game, I wasn't entirely sure what to do. Like I'd explored most of the map, and in some cases, there was a place I had to revisit, because (when I first went through that area) I didn't have the right tool to go down a particular route, and then once I got the right tool at a later point in the game, I had to go back and revisit those places, and that can kind of be easy to miss.There's also a Lastly, a puzzle is satisfying to solve. There were really only 3 or 4 puzzles I needed help solving. The game also implements a lot of backtracking where I'm having to resolve puzzles I already solved in order to get to a certain area. If the game implemented more one-way doors and shortcuts and ladders that can appear, then players won't have to expend their patience re-solving puzzles they already solved. I don't really get satisfaction solving the same puzzle a second or third time.Great game. Lots of fun. Can be frustrating at times. However, ultimately very satisfying and left me with a smile on my face at the end.Great job.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure there's a witty Dunkey-related comment to be made here, but this is too good to really put into words. Best game of the year thus far - and anything looking to dethrone that position has its work cut out. _childDocuments_.review: As much as I don't want to admit it, Animal Well proved that I get caught up in the chatter surrounding gaming more than enjoying the medium itself. This game is an excellent puzzle platformer Metroidvania where every room has multiple purposes and all your upgrades are multimodal. What's more, secrets are placed throughout the world map with increasing levels of obscurity. Once you uncover the secondary use of a tool, it makes you curios enough to poke and prod at other locations to see what else the game has in store. Granted, the amount of secrets can be a little overwhelming, especially if you go into the game with no goal in mind. But even then this game has multiple stopping points that will leave players of different skill levels satisfied. While it's not wholly unique, Animal Well is the most consistently good puzzle platformer Metroidvania I've played in a long while (if ever).

_childDocuments_.review: First off just to describe the game. It's a 2D puzzle platformer where you play as a little meatball exploring your environment and finding secrets. The game introduces many mechanics and tools which include a bubble-wand, a Yo-Yo and a few others; those two were my favourites however. Using these tools you are meant to explore your surroundings to uncover more of the map and what it has to offer. (Mainly just finding a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ collectibles).Now on to why I think it's ♥♥♥♥:First off, the puzzles are either really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy or impossible without a guide or just absolute brute force. There was absolutely no inbetween when it came to the puzzle elements in Animal well. I can't even really describe most of them because of how not memorable they were either. There's no moment where I go "oh wow that was fun and satisfying to solve! I feel so smart now!" or whatever - something like that which you would get from other puzzle games. I compare this to something like The Talos Principle or Baba is You where when you finish a puzzle you feel the sweet satisfying feeling of beating a challenge. But that doesn't exist in this game. I just moved on instantly because it took no effort and finished it instantly.Then there was the second type of puzzle where I bashed my head against the wall trying to figure out what stupid solution the developer had in mind when designing this absurdly difficult puzzle where you have to do the most specific thing ever with absolutely no indication that that was the solution. My mind especially comes to the spinning top puzzles in the late game. The spinning top mechanic is introduced somewhere in the middle of the game and it makes it clear that it is used to break a certain type of brittle surface which can be clearly indicated and marked out by how it looks and its difference in appearance to the environment. So evidently all you need to do is just keep an eye out for these surfaces and then use the spinning top when you find them right?  For some reason in the game, the developer decided to make some breakable surfaces which just look the exact same as non-breakable surfaces and I guess you're meant to find out through just trying to use this thing on literally every surface in the game?!?!?!? I don't know. But anyway yea the puzzles are ♥♥♥♥.The exploration is actually decently fun at first. You're just kinda looking around and vibing, seeing what the place has to offer. But then after like 1 or 2 hours of gameplay it just gets boring. There's a bunch of rooms that you can go into but at a certain point it just feels pointless. Other exploration based games such as Outer Wilds as an example, you actually have a purpose to what you're doing and where you are going. "Yes I want to go to this planet to find out more about the Nomai" or whatever. But that doesn't exist in this game. You're just wandering about randomly not really doing anything or trying to achieve a greater purpose. You're just some meatball on a hike. All my curiosity and excitement in this game just disappeared after the first one or two hours and then I just asked myself why am I still playing this game. There's nothing to find or discover. "Oh what's this way?" Another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ room.But actually there are things to be looking for in this game. Namely eggs and Fires. The fires are used to complete the game which are shown on the map where they are. And the eggs are just random collectibles where if you collect them all you can unlock the secret ending or whatever some random stuff - I didn't really give a ♥♥♥♥. I just found it incredibly unsatisfying to play this game and wander around just to find some random eggs and whatnot. As I said in the TL;DR - If you like trying to 100% games by finding all collectibles and stuff then this is the game for you. But I hated it.The platforming is really easy with only a few times that it took me a few attempts and a bit of effort. Which is a real shame because I found the tools in the inventory to be really interesting and I think there could have been so much more done with them. But unfortunately it was all just really basic and undercooked. And to add insult to injury some of the tools just let you straight up cheese and bypass entire rooms and segments.Using the bubble gun to just fly anywhere you wanted or the frisbee if you preferred a challenge. But other than that, with tools like the slinky and the yo-yo I really thought there would be more interesting puzzles or things to do. Like maybe being able to have a bit more control of the yo-yo and letting it go further or something to do some wacky button hitting. I don't know but what's in the game is just really basic.Overall the game is just far too easy and simple, and just incredibly boring. I 100%ed the game just to see if there were any worthwhile secrets or if there was any payoff to all the trouble that the meatball went through but there isn't. You get to the end and it's just roll credits. I can safely say I would not recommend this game to others at all and I really hope that the developer improves on these faults in their future games.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many great things about Animal Well. The puzzles are challenging and just the right level of difficulty to still be fun. _childDocuments_.review: And it's a no at the price point. It's not a terrible game.I've had better quality experiences at a lower price point. I've played enough to give a judgement on what I've experienced, and nothing has really drawn me in. I purchased it 100% on hype through reviews, and a personal recommendation. And after having hit a frustrating spot where a pixel perfect jump is causing me to try again, and again, and again, I took a step back, thought for a second, "do I even want to keep playing?....". I decided, no, I don't.The art style is unique, given I haven't seen a lot of games replicate the older PC graphic style, that part was alluring to me. The fact that it's a simple and familiar sidescrolling platformer made it an easier purchase. And the overwhelmingly positive steam review status made it an easy purchase, usually that's a sign of obvious greatness.But pixel perfect jumps for the sake of making something "hard" is a cheap gimmick. And that is what unfortunately made me realize I wasn't experiencing anything charming or groundbreaking. And for $22 on sale.I find a lot of metroidvanias create the illusion of something bigger or more vast by making you backtrack again and again. And when not done right, makes it frustrating when you're not sure where to go next. Which happened a few times in the hour and a half I played. Feels like cheap filler.The puzzling can be "neat", and is ultimately imo what this game does best. But just being "neat" isn't worth what I paid imo.After having closed the game, I haven't once had the urge to step back in the game. I've been on the fence on refunding the game, which I most likely will. That $22 could get me an experience that I would want to jump back into. At a lower price point for what I've experienced, I probably wouldn't bother with a refund. So my recommendation is to wait on this one for a heavier sale if anything I've described resonates with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a wonderful little gem, coming to us from designer Billy Basso. I had a great time exploring this dense world, solving so many interesting and unique puzzles, and admiring the beautiful visual and audio experience.You play as a little blob in a deep, dark well full of animals. Hence, Animal Well. Your job is to get four flames and banish darkness or something.You're given this very sparse context and set free which I loved because the depth then came from the atmosphere and interactions with the game world itself. The game is open ended from the start, allowing you to go pretty much any direction with some limitations based on tools and abilities you don't yet have of course. I found myself just wandering around solving what I could and grabbing the flames in whatever order seemed to make sense with what i found. Funny enough, it turns out one particular tool is one I could've gotten way earlier and would've probably completely changed the order in which I explored the world. I love this, as it hints at what could be wildly different playthroughs for individual players.As you go through the maze of Animal Well, you'll encounter puzzles and dangerous enemies that you can't quite fight back against but can only defend. It's up to you to use the tools given and your own ingenuity to pass each test. The game does a wonderful job of teaching you how to use each item, but each one also has some hidden uses and techniques that I loved discovering on my own. When I used one of theses hidden techniques to accomplish something, I truly felt like I had used the power of my own brain to find success. Throughout, there's plenty of hidden nooks, crannies, and even whole areas as well that reward you with optional tools and eggs. Collecting eggs unlocks further abilities, tools, and rewards. While I haven't found all of them, it's tempting to go back and complete that portion of the game, if not all of the crazy endgame quests you're given.All of this is wrapped up in a beautiful presentation package. The pixel art combined with retro scanlines pops beautifully with the added modern lighting techniques. The music is ethereal and haunting, and the sound design on top of the brings this dark but charming world to life.Honestly, my only complaints are some frustrations at certain parts. The game asks you to pull of some challenging platforming and maneuvering both for optional rewards and for the main quest. I definitely got pretty heated during a particular mandatory chase that seems to have challenged a lot of players. Regardless, with a clear head I can see the game was never quite unfair, but wow there are definitely some spikes here and there.Overall, Animal Well is another shining example of the beauty, wonder, and challenge the indie community can bring to gaming. It's unique in so many different ways and executes so much of its vision too. Highly recommend everyone give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Not my usual type of game, but I enjoyed it anyway. It's clear that the developer put a lot of thought and effort into it. The puzzles are well-designed and the secrets are fun, but some of them can be a little too difficult for my smooth brain. Got stuck multiple times, but I managed to get through with some guides.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a top tier exploration focused, puzzle-platformer and metroidvania game. There will be plenty of moments where you feel lost and see no direction to move to and then in the corner of the mini-map you spot , ooh I've not been there yet eventually until you think you've seen the whole map.And even when you are done, there are secret rooms upon secret rooms upon not so secret rooms that you wonder how you missed it. You will definitely find these looking for collectables. With a lot of incentive for people who think "Hmm, can I go there ?" the answer is yes you probably can and you probably find something as you get there. while having its peak moments in discovering new things and the boring moments in backtracking to the bland rooms, this game presents a standard gameplay loop in a fresh manner, with innovative power-ups. Give it a try !Overall a 8.5/10, not worth full price for everyone perhaps , but at 20% off or more it is a steal !!

_childDocuments_.review: As a big Metrovania fan....I didn't enjoy this game....tbh, the game is pretty good. Puzzles are very clever, artstyle are unique, secrets well hidden, until you hit the unavoidable backtracking plateau, as the nature of a metrovania game.And naturally, when you hit a plateau, you open the map try to figure out where you haven't been in such game. But the amount of puzzles.... almost every single room has a puzzle, and a lot of them are well hidden. This made the backtracking extremely tedious.Usually, in a metrovania game's backtracking, you got to use all these new abilities dashing through the old stages, this offsets a lot of the tediousness and gives you a sense of progression.But not in animal well, your new abilities rarely have any effect on your traversal, and unreached path/puzzles are in every corner of the map. My speed of traversing literally have 0 improvement even tho I unlocked most of the items.For people who has a lot of time and energy to invest, this is probably a god tier game just based on sheer number of well hidden puzzles.But for me...I just can't take it man. I don't want walk the whole map 10th time on the same speed of game start.And the thing is, I don't even consider myself a "casual gamer".... I 100% every single metrodvania game I have played, except Hollow Knight cuz it involves speed running.Or maybe I'm just getting old...
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Hey this game is pretty good!This game is like a platform puzzler in a large open map where you use the various items you find to open up new paths (i.e Metroidvania). Whats so great about this game is that it doesn't treat the player like a child. Many of the items have alternate uses left for you to discover. A friend of my discovered a tech, early on in our playthroughs, which let us skip tons of early game puzzles and it turned out was necessary for the end game puzzles. After you beat the game you will find that there are many more puzzles after beating the game and many of them will require some deep thought to solve.I recommend playing the game through once and then only returning to solve the harder puzzles at a later date on a new file. Personally I found it a bit easier to remember where I had been now that I knew what to look for.If you enjoy solving simple puzzles and exploring a mysterious world without the designer telling you what to do every 10 seconds then this is an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say this because I really want to like this game, but this feels more like a chore than a game, and I was just duped into paying $25 to do a chore. More often than not I find myself endlessly backtracking through areas I've already been through and/or struggle with to get back to the same puzzle that will kill me immediately if I don't solve it correctly. Most of the time the puzzles are either trivial, or so ridiculously annoying, (I say annoying, not hard) that I'm pulling my hair out. I don't feel any satisfaction from solving the puzzles, only relief that it's finally over.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A unique metroidvania, blending exploration, puzzles and multifaceted visuals in a brilliant way.Enter the Well, a mysterious place inhabited by animals, sometimes cute but not always friendly, where each corner could conceal a secret nook and many screens present layers of hints for you to uncover and unravel. In this journey, an inquisitive mind and an attentive eye will your most trusted allies which will allow you to proceed, find strange objects and discover all their applications. For each puzzle, its cleverness is equal to the joy of having solved it, and there will be plenty of them here! Often a room you thought you explored completely hides more spaces, to be unlocked in a creative way.Even if you are not the sharpest secret hunter, the base path required to reach your home is feasible by most players and still gives a rewarding satisfaction. Do not give up on this game, because you fear you cannot finish it without a guide, but instead play it savouring each accomplishment it can gift you.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well invites you into a deep, labyrinthine world of exploration, where an ever-expanding toybox of tools helps you navigate its intricate secrets. There’s no combat; instead, the tools you find assist you in further exploration and help you avoid danger. While it may appear on the surface to be a simple puzzle-platformer, the deeper you delve into its mysteries, the more layers there are to uncover.With its stunning pixel art, the game is a delight to explore. Even after completing the main story, Animal Well offers plenty to do, revealing its true depth. Its densely packed with secrets that remain consistently engaging...just when you think you’ve uncovered everything the game surprises you with yet another layer. If you’re like me and craving a new FEZ-like experience, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game constantly lets you get to a point where you think you know what's going on, and then you learn that Billy built this game on a pile of rugs and he's gonna pull each of them out from under you, sell them to you, and then make you go find them again, and you're gonna love it. Great game, totally worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really well-thought out game. The atmosphere here created is uncanny, exploration benefits from it. Admirable that power-ups given are not run of the mill, but either make an impact on puzzle solving part of the game or traversal. They are also not one trick pony, being useful in variety of situations thru out the world.  The game is very beautiful and levels are staged in a impeccable manner, making for an extremely enjoyable time. Even if one is not going to spend a lot of time for trying to get all the puzzles, it is still a fantastic burst of fun and the first hours of discovering this world a joy.The only negative, that is hard to see a solution for, is how the world loses its luster and mystique, when made to be meticulously combed thru in way of finding all the secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game of the year so far.The density of map, puzzles, and content is beyond amazing. Exploration is the driver of this game.Soundtrack is minimalistic and ambient, serves to the atmosphere very well.Mind blowing experience after the first ending. And the last but not least, amazing one-of-a-kind abilities that you find during the playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania with mostly open-ended exploration and lots of secrets for those with a nose for them. The items you get are interesting and rather-creatively used in puzzles that allow further progression while also opening shortcuts to allow for faster/easier traversal between areas you previously visited. I am reminded of La-Mulana 1&2 and Tunic in that regard, albeit with more focus on puzzles, exploration, and feeling out secrets.Wonderful pixelated style yields some fantastic scenery. Extremely impressive compact file size in spite of an age of increasingly inexpensive & higher capacity storage. Not too much in terms of a soundtrack, but the game does well to fill the air with ambiance.Finding everything on your own is a challenge, but indeed doable. I will admit I found all but five eggs on my own, but upon looking up their locations I can see how I could've organically found them without outside help-- especially with a particular late-game item. The last couple of achievements were things I probably never would've figured out on my own (Sneak, Best Ending), but I was happy to see the core game is pretty self-isolated. Though there is a bonus collectible objective that sometimes spills into a borderline mixed/augmented reality game with a couple solutions that apparently involve personalized origami printouts and a 50+ person collaboration, but those are extras not accounted for in the Achievements. 2meta4me, but thankfully unnecessary outside of personal completionism.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the only games I have gathered all achievements for (save for one..) just out of spite. This game is absolutely fantastic. A genuine work of art. It will lull you to sleep and slap the **** out of you in one sitting. You have to use at least 73% of your brain power to even think you've finished it, and you haven't.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I got into this game with a lot of expectations, I must admit. Unfortunately the base game wasn't really that interesting. With zero dialogue and no story the game doesn't have a story to keep you hooked or to motivate you to explore the world more. The puzzles themselves are mostly uninteresting, with only a few of them being more engaging or clever. It seems the main appeal of this game is the "true" end game, which is at one point near impossible to work out on your own, which takes a lot of the fun out of the game. Even then, I didn't feel any motivation to try to grind further into the game as I didn't really have an incentive to do so, other than the promise that I was going to get something amazing in the end.I definitely think I ruined my game experience by reading too much about the game and reading reviews about this and I probably wouldn't have bothered to write a review if I just planned on playing a 6 hour metroidvania with no additional content.In conclusion, I'd get the game on sale but if you're a completionist you might end up ripping your hair out.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: frustrating. frustrating, frustrating. frustrating, frustrating, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The first half of the game is a fun albeit flawed little puzzle-focused metroidvania that I truly enjoyed!However, the latter half of the game is just a snore-fest of pure pixel-sniffing, resulting in rubbing all your tools across the game's world like multiple weird metal detectors, one pixel at a time, ending in abstract trial and error that would make even 80s adventure game developers blush and ♥♥♥.Some might call that , but I call it .Really, at about the halfway point the game just falls apart into abstract ARG trial and error puzzles, so you are craved to rely on others online who have already solved it for you.These ranging from having a printer plugged to your computer to coordinating 250 other players in a singleplayer game. Pure tedium. It makes the game feel "post-game" before even hitting the first end credits.It doesn't help that most of the puzzles are tied to background decorations, so now you're just going around trying to find meaning where there is none. By the time I grabbed a guide and found out it would have been impossible without one anyways, I was already tired of the game. So I just stopped. I already reached the credits once, I don't want to bother with this game anymore.The game has a lot really cute and awesome details and mechanics that was fun to play around with for the first half. But after the developer fell into their "ARG and egg collectathon" ballpit it became increasingly harder to push myself to the end credits.Doesn't help the end credits are behind an end boss-fight with zero build-up or emotional establishment... Really such an underwhelming and unsatisfying ending.And a forced frame cap + no rebinds truly is the fecal-covered cherry on top. This was outdated technology even 20 years ago.I'd rate it with a 'mixed' recommendation score if I could instead.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: ANIMAL WELL is more than just a game. It's a beautiful work of art in both audio and visuals departments with fun and thought provoking gameplay that just doesn't get boring. I love the dedication and attention to details that was so clearly put into this game. It's easily my favourite game of this year and one of my all time favourites as well. _childDocuments_.review: i was skeptical of this game at first, because everybody said it was extraordinarily good without saying why. after playing it for 22 hours, i am no closer to understanding why this game is good. 10/10. i would say it's a thousand little genius moments of game design. all those dark souls/metroidvania level design moments where you're just in awe of how compact everything is. why spend all this time on gimmicks or complicated combat systems, when you could just spend all of it on the level design. and it's not just the level design, it's the items you get, it's the way you use the environment. they use every part of the beast and i eat that ♥♥♥♥ up. but even then, i feel like i'm not doing it justice. there's some extra secret sauce in this game. let's just say it has unspoken rizz.

_childDocuments_.review: The animals are puzzles, the platforming is a bunch of puzzles, your movement options and upgrades are all puzzles. You could even say the well is a puzzle.The game does a fantastic job of making you feel not like a protagonist but just a visitor in a busy ecosystem. You're there, but it's not about you. Each animal you meet has its own bite-size behavior, so you get to have a little moment of discovery every time you meet a new guy. It's not really clear if they're going to help or hurt you at first glance. In this way, the game gets you to engage with your environment and try to use everything around you to get to the goal, which feels really great in a puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first couple hours are fun, art direction and music are fine enough, nothi no super original but impressive for a solo dev. Just… it’s not a metroidvania. It’s a puzzle game with rooms and there’s basically no satisfying pay off for anything. If you’re a conpletionist who loves getting steam achievements this is the game for you, if you’re looking for interesting encounters and various ways to use weapons there’s literally none of that there. Since there’s no combat encounters all objects you get are just used once or twice to solve puzzles. I beat 90 percent of the base game with just the disk. It’s a game that’s made for Nintendo fans and dunky wannabes who love bing bing wahoos and jumping on hats. There’s no story. There’s no characters. Unfortunately this should have been released free on itch to get funding for Billy to make a better game. “But brooooo, layer threeeee, discord puzzles!” That’s the lamest cope I’ve ever heard for having overlooked context clues in the game world itself. I’m not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on Billy, good job bro, but dunky and his legion of drones hyping this game up as some genre definifing ten out of ten is pure disingenuity. I’m not gonna waste ten hours of my life for unfulfilling puzzles to find lame eggs just to get the “true” ending. That ♥♥♥♥ was lame with fez and its double lame ten years later

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle design is mostly great, items are unique for the genre, and graphics and atmosphere are unique, charming, and frequently unnerving. Everything in the postgame is a tedious obtuse mess in which the main challenge is not dying of boredom as you scour every single room in the game looking for blocks and background details that you didn't know to take note of on your first pass through. Movement is not interesting enough to make the backtracking engaging and trekking through the same hallways over and over again straining your eyes looking for hidden nooks or offcolor patches of wall sucks.I wouldn't mind this so much as optional content, which it *technically* is, but the Any% ending is so sudden and non-substantive that it leaves the game feeling unfinished; the dev clearly wanted people to play the endgame content to get the full experience. You can have a game with complex community driven puzzles and piles of backtracking, but you need to provide players that don't want to subject themselves to that with an actual satisfying conclusion, which this game was severely lacking.The only situation in which I recommend this game is to buy the game at a price at which you feel a 6 hour metroidvania with clever puzzle design and a lackluster ending is worth it, and to avoid the post-game like the plague unless you suffer from a unique kind of masochism.

_childDocuments_.review: Putting Dunkey and the buzzing around it aside, Animal Well is a great metroidvania focusing on puzzle-solving and discovery. While others in the same genre often put the emphasis on combat, the game relies more on letting the players figure things out. It does not teach you anything. It does not have any context of what's going on, who are you, and why are you here. You are born into this dark, mysterious world. The only force driving you forward is the curiosity to explore. It's quite an experience, and I am glad Animal Well is so well-received.In the same vein of Tunic, Animal Well tosses the player into the cavernous underworld, without guidance, without context. The only thing driving you forward is curiosity. The game presents you four paths to choose from. Each of them contains its own branching routes. You can explore them of your own accord. The game does a great job at handling how far you can go before stopping you with a gating threshold. And speaking of gating, Animal Well also doesn't rely on the usual mobility-enhancing abilities. Rather, it offers you a peculiar range of items: a flying disc, a yo-yo, a slinky, etc. I admit. The first time I received these items I was confused as hell. And that's the point, I think. Discovering what these things do is also a part of the exploration. Everything becomes more interesting when you discover you can ride on the flying disc, that you can bait other animals with the glowing yo-yo, and that you can use the slinky to press buttons for you. Every time you receive an item, the puzzle-platformers you've done can now be done in faster and more creative ways! Take the starting area for example. There's a section which you need to raise the platform out of water to proceed. With the flying disc you can just sit on the disc and wait for it to deliver you to the other side. The more you experiment with these items, the more surprises you will find on your journey. →Well hidden secrets and subtle hints.→The retro art style adds an extra layer of mystery and eeriness.→Save points are scarce and really spread-out.→Instant-kill attacks are really unfun in this game.→Some puzzle-platformers are way too punishing.中文小簡評→這款類銀河系惡魔城非常吃電波，需要玩家喜歡主動探索。→復古像素畫風多了層神祕感及詭異。→專注於活用手中的道具探索解謎。→不同於其他同類型遊戲，這款的關鍵技能並非移動技能，而是一些看似普通的玩具，但是他們功用遠超乎你的想像。→探索未知區域很有趣，發覺手中道具的功用也同樣有趣。→地圖藏有許多秘寶且給足線索，眼尖的玩家特別受祿。→存檔點過於分散。→被秒掉就得重走一大段路....→某些跳台過長又沒有記錄點，失足易成千古恨....

_childDocuments_.review: This is a challenging platformer very reminiscent (to me) of games like Metroid or Hollow Knight, except the focus is around puzzle-solving rather than combat. If that sounds too difficult, however, don't be put off. Although it is hard, it's also really intuitive and I never found it to be so frustrating that I wanted to quit. I'm proud to say I made it almost all the way through the game without any outside help because the main progression clues in-game were so well set out. Ultimately it is a very rewarding experience that makes you feel smart when you solve its mysteries while getting better at the game at every turn; plus it's absolutely loaded with secrets to uncover once you start to get the hang of the mechanics and start recognizing patterns in the terrain.All in all, 10/10. Phenomenal game that everyone should try.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of speechless for once, game of the year for me. The atmosphere is easily the biggest thing I enjoy about it. If you like detail-hunting and puzzles wrapped in a metroidvania style game, then this is the game for you. This game is ''mystery'' personified. The game is surprisingly tense, the visuals for me are beautiful (please keep the scanlines on!!). And there have been so so many ''What is this?!?'' moments it's unbelievable. Even the power ups that you get are often not what they seem at first glance. Wow, easy 10/10 for me.  Do not buy this game if you do not enjoy cryptic puzzles and/or pixel-hunting. The platforming is also sometimes far more precise than I anticipated, which is no problem for anyone familiar with jump and runs.. but a newer player might struggle. It's not just a puzzle game either.Seriously, unbelievably impressive.EDIT: Just adding to this review because I voted it as game of the year. (:

_childDocuments_.review: If you take a look at my profile, you'll see a bunch of  reviews for games that I love. It's because I like to get awards, and people generally don't really read these super long reviews. But forget it, even if no one reads this, I just need to get serious for a moment about Animal Well.I'm going to break this down into a few parts to keep my thoughts organized. But most of all,  for this work of art, .I'm going to borrow from Dunkey here when he said Animal Well is "the lasagna of video games... only once you peel back its layers can you understand why you enjoy it so much".It's a  game in every way, but most of all in its visual presentation and the seemingly hundreds of sounds you can hear at any given time. Every area, every creature, and every pixel is placed with intent, and I could stare at my monitor for eternity in awe of it all. I've spent hours so far just interacting with swinging lights and hanging flora. The Well isn't just an area in a game; it's a Techno-Sylvan world brimming with electrical animals of all sizes and formats. Speaking of the titular critters, let's talk about gameplay!I cannot stress enough how much fun it is to figure out the inner machinations of Animal Well . The decision to not add a tutorial or to offer any sort of help to the player is what makes it so magical. The player will find several objects throughout the game. Though their functionality appears to be very simple at first, you'll quickly realize just how much you can do with these secretly-sophisticated tools. Like when I learned you could  the .But the well runs deeper than that, pun intended. You play as a little blob who must navigate its way through a beautiful but treacherous environment. You may find yourself lost, confused, or even afraid sometimes. But if you just take a second to look around and enjoy the little things around you, you might feel refreshed and ready to take that next step.? Animal Well is a game that reflects life. At the end of the day, we are all really just small blobs of meat that tumble and fall through life. We make our own victories, and the decision to quit means you miss out on what the world has to offer. I cannot believe 34mb of storage on my computer has gotten me to contemplate so many things and compelled me to write this long-winded novel, but I digress.The gameplay is awesome. The puzzles never feel impossible, but you'll have to reach into that empty skull of yours every so often if you want to find all the secrets. Speaking of secrets...The developer has stated on several occasions that this game contains secrets that "may never be found". Excuse me, but ? You are presented very early on with the concept of "secret eggs" that you can find, which are aptly named as they are quite literally eggs that are secret. For most people, the hidden content will end there. But I have this gut feeling that there is so much more to this game than meets the eye. Not just other hidden easter eggs, but a whole world that once was. What's the story anyway? Every frame invites you to look around and guess. There are statues of animals EVERYWHERE, but why am I this little slime guy? Why are there  and ? Did people live in this world? Is the well underneath a whole different ecosystem and environment? Who are those blue ghost square guys? After my relatively short time played, I am left with so many more questions than answers. I cannot wait to keep playing, but more than that, I cannot wait to keep .10/10. I cannot see how anyone could play this and not enjoy it. Thank you again for this absolute gem, and thanks to  for still reading this, for some reason.P.S. thanks to my gf for the awardI STOPPED PLAYING HADES 2 TO PLAY THIS GAME, ENOUGH SAID. SERIOUSLY.

_childDocuments_.review: If lasagna was a video game, it'd be Animal Well. With multiple layers of tasty digital deliciousness, Animal Well with sate your platforming desires. The first layer of this tasty digital lasagna is the visuals. Animal Well boasts a mesmerizing pixelated art style that is sure to please the senses. With moody lighting and surprisingly detailed effects, looking at animal well is like looking at the fine melted cheese covering your delicious lasagna.The next layer of this mouth watering cuisine, is the smooth... creamy... ricotta cheese gameplay baby.  Oooh yeah. You know what time it is. The gameplay is smooth and responsive. The puzzles and tools keep you intrigued.  But what is lasagna without the meat? Animal Well contains a vast array of meat, I mean animals, in a charming subterranean environment. You'll encounter a vast array of animals in your journey. Some will be your ally, some will be your enemy. Finally, the marinara music of Animal Well brings the whole dish together. From the ambient music to the wide variety of animal noises, Animal Well's soundscape takes you to a new world.If you like lasagna, you're gonna love Animal Well.

_childDocuments_.review: ANIMAL WELL is a puzzle-platformer metroidvania developed by Billy Basso and the first published game from popular YouTuber videogamedunkey's company Bigmode. Despite fitting in with other genres, ANIMAL WELL manages to be unique with it's set of puzzles, experimentation, exploration, and atmosphere. I have thoroughly enjoyed my nearly (ongoing) 7 hours of playtime. The fact that this game was solely developed by Basso over the course of around 6 years is astounding.ANIMAL WELL's atmosphere is dreamlike, the scan lines along with the vibrant neon colors make the game's look feel familiar yet refreshing. From exploring many areas throughout the map, you can tell the amount of detail that is put into every nook and cranny. A previous area you might think was added for the sake of it, only to realize as you continue the level of intricate design that all mesh together like clockwork. The tools that are at your disposal are unexpected, but you will find each of them highly useful. The game's minimalist approach on tutorials encourages you to experiment, so tools you might have thought only had one basic use can actually have a variety of ways to use them, rewarding clever thinking and skillful play.For me, it's hard to talk about the impact of ANIMAL WELL's success without talking about the current climate of gaming. We're living in a strange time where we see more and more prominent game companies make highly questionable management practices. Sony breaking the Helldivers 2 playerbase by nearly forcing psn signups to which the game hasn't been relisted in previously delisted countries as of this review, Microsoft's shutdown of multiple studios including Tango Gameworks (creators of Hi-Fi Rush, The Evil Within), Electronic Arts's CEO wanting to use Artifical Intelligence in their games. The growing cynical and depressive nature of the modern gaming industry is almost too prominent to ignore. It's because of this, that it's important for games like ANIMAL WELL need to be brought attention to and praised for, as well as publishers like Bigmode for helping bringing it to life. There's a line near the end of videogamedunkey's video My Indie Game Publishing Company, where the vision for Bigmode is as follows "We're not aiming for bronze medals, we're going for the gold." If this diamond of a game is considered gold, it makes me more excited to what new gems will be published next.

_childDocuments_.review: There are moments where ANIMAL WELL is enjoyable to play and there are moments where you can get stuck and have to look up a guide to progress further. I liked the art style, the music fits the game and immerses you, and most of the puzzles and eggs I felt were easy to understand and complete. Even with that I did not like that for a few puzzles, resetting the room by exiting and re-entering was difficult. The inability to rebind your controls for keyboard in the game is also something that I did not like, as it seems like something that should be extremely easy to implement. Finally the random difficulty spikes for bosses or flames was something that, while I see the point of having, I really disliked as I went into the game thinking it was going to be slow and relaxing (EX: ). Overall the game is fine, but not something crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Packed MEGA dense with incredible mechanics, gorgeous pixel art, wonderful puzzles, vexing secrets, and every single glowing inch of the game oozes with love and charm. _childDocuments_.review: An amazingly fun, engaging and smart puzzle-platformer.It may look simple and "old school" at first but it's actually full of fresh ideas, both in design and in gameplay. The items and thier mechanics are interesting spins on classic metroidvania gear, and can be used in amuzing, surprising ways; every new item you find makes you see the game world with different eyes.The map is quite large, especially considering that it's full of things to do and secrets to find; it's easy and quick to navigate for the most part and that's great because backtracking is heavily featured (mainly if you aim at finding everything, which I recommend).Overall going back and forth trough the map doesn't feel boring because the exploration aspect is so well done: the puzzle and level design are so genuinely stimulating for the brain that every screen has you thinking on ways to reach a chest or a hidden path, which is best thing a game of this type can do.Also tight controls, nice cute graphics and soothing soundtrack.100% recommended: not only this is an incredible work of game and level design, but it also knocks out of the park every single other aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well takes a peculiar approach to the metroidvania genre. There are no combat per say but there are lots of ennemies to defeat, sneak past to, run from or simply outwit. Most of the game revolves arround solving puzzles to unlock new tools and progress further into the world. Those tools are incredibly original and have several clever ways to be used. However nothing is ever directly teached to you. The game does a perfect job of always putting you in a new situation and letting you figure out what to do with your current tools. Everytime you get stuck and think to yourself "Did I just softlock myself ?", you will find a new way to use something you already have and it is tremendously satisfying. The game world is simply gorgeous, it is eerie and hauntingly beautiful. The subtle soundtrack blends perfectly with the visuals and it's a pleasure to explore and discover new areas. The main "questline" last about 7-8h and is well worth getting the game for. However if you're the completionist kind of person and enjoy unravelling all the secrets hidden within a game then you're in for a hell of a ride.Without spoiling, once you finish the game, there are several "obvious" objectives you can challenge yourself to. They will lead you down a deep, deep, deeeeeeeeeeeeeep rabbit hole. People reference Tunic and Fez for good reasons. The game takes direct influence from those game for the scale of their Meta Puzzles and the sheer madness required to unlock everything the game has to offer. This is not my cup of tea but once I finished the game I took great pleasure in looking up guides online and watching people figure stuff out. Well worth checking out.This is a work of love and it shows all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Just a fascinating puzzle/metroidvania game unlike anything else I've ever played. I recommend taking notes while playing though since the mapping system isn't fully sufficient and there is a lot that you'll want to remember/keep track of. It'd be awesome if an update just added a few more different stamp types but even if that never happens, I still fully recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The vibes are immaculate, I enjoyed my time with Animal Well. The pixel art is beautiful and unnerving at the same time - from capybaras resting in a hot spring, to cats that give the Cheshire Cat competition in terms of creepiness. The puzzles were fun too, but felt a bit too easy. Once I understood what my main objective was, the game pretty much fell into place for me. I'm not the sort of person to replay a metroidvania once I finish it, so maybe I'm missing out on some other stuff like the other reviews say. There's a lot to like about this game, but I don't want to spoil. Go play it, support indie devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game. It reminded me of the dungeon crawler-esque puzzle games that I used to play as a kid, and the CRT Filter just adds to that aesthetic. The puzzles are intricate, engaging, and fun. And the way that you can interact with the environment and the things around you is crazy. All in all, the word I would use for this game is "contrast". The game itself is both simple, and yet extremely complex. It's beautiful and innocent at times, and sometimes it's malevolent and it's had my hairs stand on end. Its 8 bit aesthetic contrasts with it's in game effects such as smoke and light. Even the positional movement contrasts with some of what you have to encounter in the game such as enemies and other creatures. It brought out a sense of wonder and fascination that I haven't found in a game for a long time. I would 100% recommend getting this game and trying it out for yourself. It's not too short, but also not too long, and I would say that this was money and time well spent. Thank you so much to the creators for making such a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent game, but I did not enjoy it as much as most. I've only completed the first credit roll and will not go further (I left the game open for a few days--I did not actually play that long).Good:Very flexible items and relatively open-ended puzzles.Incredibly detailed, interactive game world.Interesting take on 8-Bit pixel art.Bad: It's a metroidvania, but traversal is boring. The items are interesting to use in puzzles, but don't make for fun movement. While a fast-travel system can be unlocked it has very few warp locations, all inconveniently located. Lots of tedious backtracking is mandatory.Many puzzles require precise execution and feature long walks-of-shame to retry them. I've played many metroidvanias but am far from speedrunner material. I often had to retry puzzles I had already solved 10+ times to get the jumps and movement correct. It's not uncommon for metroidvanias to have challenging platforming sections, but, as mentioned above, movement in this game is not engaging, so much of the game felt like a chore. The platforming difficulty also means that testing solutions to puzzles is onerous--many puzzles involve time constraints, and it can be hard to tell if you have the solution but aren't executing fast enough or if your approach is wrong and you're wasting your time trying to optimize your movement. In some cases there are clever ways to use your items to make the execution easier than the "intended solution", but in many cases the puzzles carefully foreclose creative use of items to force these difficult platforming skill checks.The rudimentary controls are frustrating in light of the demanding platforming and tedious traversal. For example. basic features like holding down to jump down a ladder are absent--you have to jump up and then fall to jump down a ladder. Death means a return to your last save point, items collected since your last death in tow, but unintuitively does not save the game. This can lead to huge progress loss if you're not close to a save-point but haven't collected anything since your last death and close out the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not that this game needs Yet Another Positive Review, but it really is fantastic.  My advice is that if you like Metroidvania games and enjoy exploring eerie environments positively dripping with atmosphere, pick it up without hesitation, and try not to spoil yourself too much on other reviews or even the official trailer videos.  There's a ton to discover, and you'll have the best time in the game if you discover 'em yourself!One thing I really enjoyed was the twist of having a lack of combat.  You  sometimes directly imperiled by hostile creatures, but in general your tactics boil down to avoidance.  There's a million Metroidvanias out there with combat if that's more what you're after, but the lack of direct combat plus the ambiance/vibes gives this one a really unique feel.  There's a few places in the game where you've got to do platforming under pressure, and one in particular which represents a pretty hefty (and unexpected) difficulty spike, though the game's respawn mechanics mean that you can generally retry those segments easily.It's not a  game -- there's a few very-endgame puzzles which I'd personally consider unfair (as in: requiring outside-game input to complete, or just clues which are nearly impossible to catch on your own).  The few sections of platforming-under-pressure kind of dissipates the vibes in the game a bit, too -- after you've died a few times trying to complete a difficult section, a lot of the atmosphere-derived tension kind of evaporates a bit and it starts to feel like just Yet Another Metroidvania.Still, my nitpicks with the game are quite minor compared to the absolutely delightful bulk of the game.  I'd highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become one of my all time greats, and I still haven't even "finished" it yet. Animal Well scratches an itch that few games do, combining its amazing atmosphere with ingenious puzzles that make you go "ahhhhhhhh," tight platforming, fantastic exploration, exciting items to collect, gorgeous music, excellent worldbuilding, and tons of replayability. The fact this game takes up less space on my computer than a single picture I might take with my phone is mind boggling and a testament to the efficiency of a one man team. Mr. Basso should be so utterly proud of what he has created, in my eyes it is nothing short of a modern masterpiece. Many times I thought to myself playing- "This is a less a game, and more a window into one guy's creative process, ideology, and personal perception of art". _childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is compelling and interesting.  This one is a bit like , ,  (if it was more open and minus the combat),  (If it was deeper) and vaguely reminds me of games like  and  too.Games like these are always intriguing, but very hit and miss for me.  At some point I get annoyed or confused on how to make progress.  While in Animal Well it is very easy to get stuck somewhere (And I did), I managed to complete the main game.  To collect all of the eggs and uncover all of the games secrets would be a lot harder, there appears to be quite a bit of postgame though it may only appeal to the more diehard explorers.Missing chests and items aren't marked on your map, though you can mark your map with pins if you've found the items that allow this (1-2 hour mark was when I found this I think).  You will unlock fast travel to teleport to a main hub at some point but it is mildly cryptic and I suppose potentially missable (Just search online if after hours you haven't worked it out).I want to say they took the ugliest kind of pixel art and made the most out of making it quite pretty and well done.There is very little music, atmosphere relies more heavily on sounds and it does a good job of sucking me into its world.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, it takes about five hours for a regular runthrough, ten for 100% achievements, a little more for total completion using the community's puzzle-solving data.  You can likely see the credits without referencing a guide, but completion is at least a pen-and-paper affair.  You'll also likely want to turn flashing effects off, whether you have a medical reason to or not, because the flashbang effect is just unpleasant.  This game is extremely into backtracking and quadruple-checking every room for secrets, which is by turns charming and laborious.  Some of the rooms really get on your nerves after a couple times through, and it only gets worse if you aren't making detailed notes on your map.  But when you solve the optional puzzles on your own, it really does feel quite good.  I would have preferred more automatic tracking of fully completed rooms and missed-but-seen treasures, especially since the stamps easily overwhelm the small, blurry map.  A lot of care was put into layout and puzzle development, especially to check for softlocks in the highly open-ended exploration.  However, there is no concrete story or character to latch onto, this is a gameplay-first endeavor with an animal theme.  If you do not want to solve puzzles in a metroidvania style world, there is literally nothing else here, so don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Chameleon Twist 2  continues to enchant gamers with its unique mechanics, whimsical world, and endearing characters.From the moment you dive into the colorful and quirky universe, it's clear that this game is something special. The vivid, cartoon-like graphics burst with personality, creating an immersive experience that feels both nostalgic and fresh. Each level is meticulously crafted with an array of imaginative environments, ranging from lush forests to mysterious caverns, all teeming with hidden secrets and clever puzzles.The standout feature is undoubtedly its tongue mechanics. As Davy, the adventurous chameleon, players use his versatile tongue to grapple, swing, and manipulate objects in ways that are both inventive and immensely satisfying. This unique mechanic sets it apart from other platformers of its time, offering a level of creativity and strategy that keeps players engaged and constantly thinking outside the box.Controls in the game are smooth and responsive, making it a joy to navigate through the diverse landscapes and tackle the increasingly challenging obstacles. The learning curve is perfectly balanced, allowing both newcomers and seasoned players to enjoy the experience without frustration. The addition of new moves and abilities as you progress keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting, ensuring that there's always something new to discover.One of the most delightful aspects is its cast of quirky characters and playful narrative. The story, while simple, is filled with humor and charm, making every interaction and cutscene a pleasure to watch. The game's lighthearted tone is complemented by its whimsical soundtrack, which perfectly captures the adventurous spirit of Davy's journey.Replayability is another strong suit. The game encourages exploration and experimentation, with plenty of collectibles and hidden paths to uncover. Whether you're aiming to beat your best time or find every secret, there's always a reason to revisit the enchanting world of Chameleon Twist 2.In conclusion this game is a timeless gem that deserves a place in the pantheon of great platformers. Its innovative gameplay, charming aesthetics, and engaging level design make it a must-play for any fan of the genre. Whether you're a nostalgic gamer or discovering it for the first time, Chameleon Twist 2 offers an adventure that's as delightful as it is unforgettable. ... oh wait I'm messing this up, this review was supposed to be for ANIMAL WELL ... yeah it's pretty good too.

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous and atmospheric non-standard Metroidvania. The gameplay is focused more on exploration and discovery rather than combat. There is no combat! The game is more about traversal and platforming and solving puzzles. And although there's no combat, that doesn't mean there aren't hazards and hostile creatures to avoid along the way (and boss fights!)The game is non-linear in progression and you can tackle any area at any time. You get various items (which would function as "weapons" or "upgrades" in standard Metroidvanias) that allow you different means of interacting with the game world. For example: You get Firecrackers which can light up dark areas and scare off enemies. You get a Disc you can throw to hit far away objects. You get a Yoyo which can knock things down and spin into tight corners to hit switches. You get a Bubble Wand which allows you to create a bubble to jump on. And so much more! Very unusual "upgrades" which are all very fun and unique to use.Because of its non-linearity, the design of the game facilitates a variety of different ways of traversing the game world. Several screens that require some means of using a tool can all be "solved" in different ways. There's a room where there's a gap between exits and a large stretch of water in between; you can't jump into water because you are a lil potato guy who can't swim apparently. So water is off limits. There's a bit of an overpass above you with stalactites hanging down, but it's too high to jump up to. So how do you get across? There's multiple ways! You can use the bubble wand to jump up onto the overpass (or even across the water). You can use the Yoyo to knock the stalactites into the water to hop across. Or, you can throw the disc and jump on it to glide across. Simple design and interactions like that really drew me in. The room itself isn't even a puzzle but I was amazed that such thought was put into allowing multiple means of "solving" it. Speaking of puzzles! Oh boy get your thinking cap on cause there's a lot. You have to use a wide range of all your various items and some good timing to get through the puzzles, and it's very very satisfying when you do. There's even some neat tech stuff you can do with the Bubble Wand. The Bubble Wand is basically this game's version of a double jump (a bubblejump, if you will). You blow a bubble forwards, it rises up, you can jump on it and jump off, and the bubble will pop after doing so. BUT! If you're good enough, you can blow a bubble, jump off, blow another bubble and immediately land on the new one. And if you repeat that, and you master that, you can jump *anywhere*. It's incredibly satisfying to learn and pull off, and it never feels like it's "cheating" or "wrong". In fact, it almost feels like the developer wants you to be able to do these kinds of things. You can clear past some very difficult platforming sections just through bubblejumps alone.There's also S E C R E T S shhhh don't tell anyone(seriously, there's a TON of secrets, the rabbit hole goes DEEP deep deep)Overall a very unique and enjoyable experience and a very different take on the Metroidvania genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a great exploration game with an ethereal feel to it thanks to its art direction and sound design.  While it does have actual puzzles, it's much more focused on exploring the map and finding eggs and secret paths using the items you collect along the way.  Some obstacles require some very clever thinking, but most are fairly straightforward and don't require a ton of time to be spent on them.As for negatives, a few items (Especially the ) don't feel like their primary uses are telegraphed properly when you first acquire them, and after looking up the solutions to the last few eggs I couldn't get on my own, I can definitely say I never would've found them otherwise due to the items needed to get them having very obtuse uses.Some people have said the game is too short, which it probably is if your only goal is to get to the credits as fast as possible and ignore everything else...But after exploring the vast majority of the map and completing all of the achievements, I felt like the length was just right.  Overall, if you're a fan of FEZ, Knytt Underground, and similar exploration-focused games, you'll probably love Animal Well.
