_childDocuments_.review: This is what indie games are all about. It's hard to describe, but you can feel the heart and soul that went into this project. On paper, Animal Well is a fairly typical metroidvania. You wander around a giant map, unlocking new abilities to reach new areas, solve new puzzles, and find new secrets. In practice, while it certainly bears the hallmarks of metroidvania, it's a beautifully immersive and gripping world that had me losing all track of time as I delightedly wandered the map without any particular aim or direction.My issue with most metroidvanias is the constant dread of FOMO, the thought that I might be missing a particular secret or that I have to go in a particular order in order to unlock everything. Animal Well solves that by giving you entirely free rein. Yes, there will be areas that are briefly inaccessible, but the answer is generally contained within a particular area, and the world opens up in just about any order you want it to. The map/level design feeds back on itself brilliantly, the mechanics practically teach themselves (deceptively simple elements combining into a wealth of movement options), and I can't wait to get further into this delightful little gem.TL;DRIt's like Halo 2 and 3 combined

_childDocuments_.review: I was aware of this game because Dunkey promoted it, but purchased it mostly because I saw that the youtuber FuryForged was excited for it 1y+ ago, and I liked the other games he associated with. This is a game that is great because of its simplicity, mechanics, and aesthetics. It takes away tons of the annoying parts of sidescrolling 2D games and replaces them with a well-designed world that has corridors around every corner one may suspect. I also enjoy the slow build up. At first, you look for four easy to find items that are marked directly on the map, then you look for 64 secret items of varying difficulty, then you look for 16 (32? unsure atm) things that are more difficult to find than the previous "quest." This buildup makes the player feel an increasing sense of exploratory mastery, and that feels really good. There is also some movement tech. All I will say without spoilers is that the most useful one is extremely easy, and can be figured out in a few minutes, while other ones are more difficult, but also used much less. The aesthetics are a strong point as well. It is definitely a retro aesthetic, but its lighting and other on-screen effects make it seem modern. The lighting is also used to interact with the world in multiple ways, and the endgame lighting item makes one almost feel like exploring the whole world over again to see it in a new light, in that way, I often forgot it was a pixelated game since I was focusing on random holes in the wall. Overall, this was a game that anyone could probably beat within 15-20 hours, but unlike some games with that distinction, it is mentally stimulating throughout its playtime. I could probably play a game like this for 100h+ if it continuously progressed like this one did.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as you think I've figured Animal Well out, you realize that you really really did NOT at all. Between it's peaceful tranquility, breathtaking environment, immersive world building, and SO SO SO many little animals, there is so much life and adventure hidden behind it's aesthetic CRT filter. Billy Basso completely reshaped my impression of metrodvanias and even the world. I shall now go start smashing holes into my walls, just in case there is any collectible bunnies or secret chests. But, as you progress through the game, the puzzles will get gradually harder and more opaque, and you will need to be more committed to get that feeling again.Unless you're a huge fan of puzzles, your playthrough of this game will range from 6-12 hours. This is a very high quality product, and I believe that its price is well-deserved. However, you're not getting a lot of playtime for what you're paying. _childDocuments_.review: Downvote but more like "meh"I'm a big Metroidvania fan, and while Animal Well was decent, it didn't quite hit the mark for me. Clearly, a lot of effort has been put into it, and I don't want to sound overly dramatic, but the game just didn't live up to the hype.Sure, the game was enjoyable, and there are secrets everywhere with puzzles that can be quite demanding. But the story and progression are very cryptic. There's no real narrative, and the game won't hold your hand at all. If you're not into that kind of experience, this might not be the game for you.The platforming sections range from boring to difficult, with a fair share of tedious and annoying parts. The atmosphere is definitely the main draw here – it's enjoyable, peaceful even, except for the constant backtracking and platforming quirks. Nobody dies (except you), which adds to the serene vibe, but it's disrupted by the gameplay frustrations.One of my biggest gripes is the relentless backtracking. I get that it's a staple in Metroidvanias, but here it's overdone. There are very few fast travel points, and I lost count of how many times I had to retrace my steps for missing just one jump.The respawn points aren't set per room or area, it is very possible that you would respawn in a very different area, forcing to backtrack AGAIN because of the very questionable respawn logic.Overall, after finishing the game once, I felt Animal Well leaned more towards being a platformer than a true Metroidvania. Keep this in mind if you're considering buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Perhaps Very good.Highlights:* Graphics - not even sure how he did it. Internal 3d lighting projected onto 2d? Unsure. But it looks great, and unique. * Sound fx - great. Chiptune-esque while being entirely fitting to the context and the animals in question. I liked the ostrich.* Atmosphere - good. Nice textures, haunting areas in some places. A bit dark and miserable though, but I understand some people like that.* Animals and gameplay - excellent, well-tuned. I think the animal pattern breaks are the best part of the game - like, dogs will chase you, but not down holes, but then one sausage dog does and it's terrifying as ♥♥♥♥.'* Puzzles/inventory - well-stacked. The items have multiple uses that get discovered over time, and as you re-explore old areas you find you can traverse them. Of course, this is the metroidvania ideal but it's done uniquely. Unlike The Witness, the puzzles generally have that 'aha' moment without feeling like you're having to guess a lot or be obsessively observant. At least in the beginning. Having said that it probably helps if you've played a few similar games before, as hidden passages and their calling cards are du jour for this sort of racket.* Performance and quality - the lack of bullcrap on opening the game is refreshing - straight to the menu, then straight into the game within 3 seconds. No hussle, no advertising yourself. Well done. Runs on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ potato. Nice to see nowadays in the age of overbloated game engines catering to every type of game.A few downsides:* Music - "less is more" is actually less here. There's two pieces in the game (not counting the end theme, end boss theme and menu theme), and they both feel low-effort and not immensely atmospheric - although the 'boss' music does it's job. Compare that with Knytt Stories, a similar game from the early 2000's which introduced different (sometimes amazing) music for each section, but didn't replay it so that it wouldn't interfere with the atmosphere or get annoying. This is the biggest downside of the game and really affects the ability to get absorbed into it or connect with it, for me. I've often heard the excuse from devs that they 'want the player to connect with the atmospheric sound fx' well, wind noises never made me feel anything emotionally, so nuts to that. Besides which, music doesn't have to go all the time.* *Some* puzzles - the closer you get to the end game, the less intuitive some of the puzzles become. Mostly the items have good tutorialisation, but at one point you have to use the slinky while also using the yoyo - and there is no indication in the game, before or after, that you can use two items at the same time without releasing one of them - in fact, everything up to that point shows the opposite - that you can't hold two at the same time. I found more of these sorts of things the closer I got to the end. The 'top' is usable to break away ground, but the first place you discover that, the ground disappears so fast you can't tell if there was some visual way of identifying ground which can be broken with the top. The run with the "M.disc", where it doesn't tell you that this is, explicitly, the "Mock disc" from earlier in the game, isn't problem-solving, it just means you have to do a massive run on a hunch and potentially waste your time if you got it wrong. And so on.* (first) End boss - the other bosses were doable, fun even. The end boss just kicks it up to 14, and it's neither enjoyable nor fairly doable, just brutal. And every time you die there you have to do another few minutes of walking. Not fun.* Relying on secrets as the main draw of the game - unlike most of the games I've played where secrets were a fun and mysterious part of it - Cave Story, Fez, Knytt Stories - the secrets in here seem to be the 'whole point' of the game. That's an unfortunate outlook. The reality is that those other games had something else going for them - in Fez, the unique traversal mechanic, music and atmosphere, in Knytt the atmosphere and the music, in Cave Story the plotline, characters and fighting. The secrets were secondary (possibly 1st-equal in Fez). This has just got puzzles and puzzle-solving, but no plot, which is fine. But when only 1/5th of the game is getting to the end, and the other 4/5ths is other supposed layers of deeper and deeper secrets... I'm sorry, you've lost me. You've thrown a perfectly good game on the fire and expected me to warm the cockles of my heart on it, well... not for me. Maybe someone more obsessive. Good game. Maybe very good. Not great. Look to Psychonauts, Fez, Cave Story, even A Short Hike, for that.It's hard to know what amount of the overwhelming hype for this game played into my expectations. But I did love the first 3/4ths of it before the last flame and final (first) boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game with some annoyances.The visuals and audio are really impressive. The game manages an enormous amount of expressiveness within its small tiles and simplistic audio. The world feels vast, mysterious, and unsettling.The map is a mix of wide-open hubs and linear segments that do a good job of looking fairly non-linear. Backtracking is handled through an excellent web of shortcuts that open as you progress. The map also has a large number of hidden nooks that might have you endlessly jumping into walls and crevices to make sure you're not missing anything.Map exploration can be done with a very small number of items. This commitment to "not holding the player's hand" is great in some aspects, but also can be a bit annoying. I frequently found myself uncertain if I was meaningfully moving toward any sort of reward. Some areas are rich with minor rewards, while others are oddly empty.The game's difficulty is generally mild with at least one sharp spike that I wasn't a fan of. The room puzzles were engaging and well varied. I didn't find them to be too difficult. The real difficulty comes from figuring out what the (very unique) items do. They're given to you without explanation and sometimes without anything to verify that you understand them. So be ready to randomly bash new items against every suspicious looking thing on the map.Definitely a solid recommendation for anyone that likes exploration, puzzling, and a bit of platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Animal Well is a good game, but I can only recommend it with some extensive provisos that may give you cause to reconsider whether it is right for you.Essentially the game can be divided into two parts: Part one - exploring an extensive interconnected world and solving challenging platforming puzzles. Here, the game gives you nothing, and I really mean absolutely nothing in terms of plot or direction and asks you to put the pieces together via atmospheric clues. What do the symbols on the map mean? How can you reach  the various biomes? What is the point to any of this? The game gives you zero help and invites you to take the initiative. I found this part to be satisfying and rewarding, but as many have commented on, it's over way too soon. This section can be completed in around 5-7 hours. If you're a slower gamer or completionist it might take you 10. But it's over all too quickly.Now on to part two: The post-game. This is where things soured greatly for me. After getting the first ending you're given the challenge to collect 64 doo-dahs. At this point for a number of reasons it simply stopped being fun and became as enjoyable as pulling teeth. The remaining items are hidden in such a way that looking for them is practically impossible for any single player. They're hidden in such inaccessible or niche ways that you find yourself rubbing your little pixel blob body against every wall and pillar to see if there's a hidden crevice. Nothing is signposted, there are no hints, and no game logic to follow. I found this section to be insulting to the players' time and intelligence. And most critically it just wasn't fun in any way. I got about 40-ish of the 64 collectables before tapping out. I wasn't enjoying it whatsoever. The game shows a disdain for the player - objects are hidden in ways that are, I repeat, impossible to find in 1,000 hours of playthrough. Here I resorted to step-by-step guides and even then it took me hours to find any of these remaining things. I felt angry and ultimately shortchanged. The world lost its charm and became a frustrating slog, and the graphics changed from being beautiful to being ugly blunt force trauma.If you continue with the puzzle solving there are further layers and layers of even more impossible puzzles to solve. If this floats your boat then I'd say go ahead and a buy a copy. But ultimately I find it very hard to recommend the post game section. It's a twisted mess that shows no respect to the player and forces you to use guides to get ahead.If you're willing to buy this for the short main game, it's a well-constructed puzzle box. But I think the majority of players will want to stop there before the fun dramatically cuts out and you find yourself trapped in a dark and miserable well and no closer to the surface.

_childDocuments_.review: "Were you too born in this infinite well?" I asked of the baby chimp before it's mother threw a rock at me for talking to her son.Animal Well is a very well designed metroidvania that puts exploration at the forefront, both in the sense of filling out a map as well as challenging the player in their belief of what can be done. Unlike in similar games that currently hold popularity in the genre, combat is not a focus in this game. "Combat encounters", if they can be called that, are few and far between and the main tool for dealing with them is a consumable resource (the only consumable resource in the game) that is rarely given out except around the proximity of those combat areas and are simply, without skill, thrown on the ground to chip down the lives of the particular enemy you're fighting.What is the focus is exploration and puzzle solving. The world you're dropped into a mysterious one with subdued darker colors displayed in beautiful pixel art reminiscent of the resolution of a CRT television. It's navigated with a detailed map that can be marked up and written on, and that I've pored over in depth, plotting my path to objectives and noting oddities and missing pixels that could suggest pathways I haven't yet been on. Of course, how actually progressing through the world works is with the finding of various upgrades, and the upgrades in this game are truly interesting. Again not being combat, or really even action focused, upgrades in this game aren't a flashy affair. You won't find anything that gives you truly flashy movement like dashes, jumps, or flight. Instead, you'll find your toolbox is a toybox and in prodding at the edges of the world come upon items like frisbees, bubble blowers, and yoyos, to name less than a quarter of what is available. You're left to piece together how these items can be used in a multitude of ways to traverse previously inaccessible routes, remove obstacles completely, and interact with the ever-present and eponymous animals in the well. It's a truly living world, largely in part due to the multitude of animals, some adversarial, many neutral, that are keyed to your presence, and which you need to come to truly understand their behavior of to progress. Yet, the game also has many smaller things that keep it from being stale and static, such as the dynamic behavior of some liquids, grasses, vines, and light sources as you move through and change the world. This all in sum makes playing the game a wonderful experience.I find myself having beat the game (reaching the credits) around the 7 hour mark. I now near finding all the obviously-designated collectibles, and have just about exhausted my interest in the game. However, between starting the game and where I am now, there has been a fantastic journey of prodding at the game's world and systems and finding many secrets that have blown me away in my expectations of what I would be rewarded with finding. For all the lulls that I feel naturally occur when trying to make progress in a game of this genre, there have been many stretches of cascading "aha moments"; writing down clues and notes (the new Steam notes feature has been very useful with this) and running to areas I remembered from before to test a new theory; uncovering a new secret, tool, or piece of info; and repeating. Even now, I am aware that the solo (and this must be emphasized) developer has previously made statements with implications that what would normally be considered 100% completion in another game is still only a scratch of the surface of all the secrets that have been emplaced in this one. It very well could be that what's uncovered with my finding of the last collectible, will have me running around for another 20+ hours, pulling at the remaining itching strings that I still don't have an answer for.Ultimately though, I believe that no matter how deeply you want to engage with the systems in this game, it is one that is very well worth the time and money in playing and experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface this is a really enjoyable short metroidvania game with a very unique vibe and atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is one of those special games that only comes along every once in a while. Filled to the brim with atmosphere and charm all in an incredibly polished package. _childDocuments_.review: Updated review 13.8 hours in After a certain the point the game stops being a puzzle platformer and becomes a precision platformer, less can you find a clever use for a tool to get somewhere more can you do a fiddly thing with a tool multiple precisely timed times in a row to get a secret.Fundamentally the game doesn't respect your time, the first time a new tool or use of a tool makes you go back through the map seeing what it can do is interesting. When you're six tools in a row of the same gimmick, and then you start spotting a pattern in background details which would mean checking every single screen again, including repeating several annoying platforming sections with bad checkpointing it just gets too much. The shortcuts help a bit with this, but there are too many places where the game expects you to repeat a fiddly platforming section just to use a different item at the end.Definitely just start using a guide instead of endless repeatedly tracking through the map. Would give this a neutral review if I could under steam but as you can't have to say don't recommend.Updated review 5.5  hours  Still not recommending because there's no recommend but with big caveats option. The good:- Letting the player discover innovative uses for the items.- Some of the more annoying single screen puzzles use falling in water as the failure case, which means you can retry repeatedly with minimal retracking.The bad:- Death returns you to your last save point with map progression preserved, but removes items for no good reason.- Check pointing is still poor, resulting in far too much backtracking, especially with the number of instant death hazards, some of which you'll only discover are instant death after they kill you the first time.- No consistency in it what is harmless, hurts you and is instant death.- Platforming puzzles that extend across multiple screens, relying on successful leaps into the unknown - made worse by the poor check pointing.- Apparently the interesting part of the game  vno good if the game is too frustrating before then. - A few too many pixel perfect jumps, could have made the distances a bit friendlier to make it less frustrating.Limiting platforming puzzles to single screens would have enabled more generous check pointing and much less frustrations.If you find the platforming annoying with the first two hours, it will only get more frustrating, so refund before then if you aren't committing to finish-- Initial Thoughts after two hours --Good* Generally controls well in character movement * Does a good job of teaching by play without explaining* Provides option to disable scan lines graphics effect in settingsBad* Visually indistinct (particularly in the  meaning some of the discovery is because things aren't always visually legible). Communicates depth poorly in terms if things behind or infront of the character. The scan line effect makes this much worse.*   especially don't stand out well which is a shame given how many puzzles involve them. They are also buggy in collision and randomly let you enter their space without taking harm.* The   controlls abysmally especially if using an analog stick, with no in game help it's hard to know if it's intended or I'm using it wrong.* Checkpoints are too infrequent resulting in a lot of repetition when solving a puzzle/platform challenge divided into parts over multiple screens. Would make more sense if this was more of a metrovania as it's more of a platform puzzler really it quickly becomes annoying redoing solved bits to try the new thing again. Would be fine if the punishment for failure wasn't loss of a limited health stat resulting in death and having to redo it all. Annoying because the failure punishment for falling in water doesn't involve health loss so I'm not sure what health really adds. Is it testing puzzle solving or platforming?* Too many points of no return without any clear signposting whether or not a screen exit will be an unreturnable fall or one that provides the ability to backtrack. Means you may be stuck having to solve a particular platform sequence with no option to explore elsewhere instead when you were just trying to check out potentially routes. Feels at odds with the intent that that's no set order and that your are supposed to experiment.Indifferent:*Apparently there's some  .  I'm not the target audience of ARGs.Fundamentally I suspect that certain routes through the game/orders for acquiring new tools are simply more interesting than others. At least I hope they are, because this will get very irritating otherwise.Not as good a first impression as ratings/hype would suggest. Will play it through to see if this issues are my own skill or a bad early path or fundamental to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game.  It's right up my alley in so many ways!  It's a metroidvania, it's got great a great atmosphere and unique style, it uses sound effectively and with impact, and it doesn't hold your hand, but rather let's you figure things out through exploration and gameplay experimentation.  BUT, where the game get tedious is towards the late game when you have to do A LOT of backtracking, and not being able to zoom in much on the map makes it a little tiring trying to figure out where to go back to.  Yes, there is a fast travel method, but only taking you back to a hub connecting to different parts of the map.  I love being encouraged to explore, but I felt like it was a bit too much towards the end.  I still really like this game and would probably put it in my top 10 favorite metroidvanias I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania-style game. The visuals and sound design are phenomenal. It's absolutely dripping with atmosphere and everything feels cohesive. Animal Well's game progression is highly intuitive - which makes up for the lack of tutorials, an intentional design decision which helps the game's sense of discovery. The "upgrades" are super unique and are well utilized. The world design is also top-notch; it's crazy how well everything wraps back around - making traversing the world a cinch. There's a lot of depth to the progression, but some of it borders on tedious "guide-gaming". It's all optional "post, post-game" content so it's a very small gripe.If you're a capital-G Gamer, pick this up. It's damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a fantastic spin on a classic metroidvania, where moves are replaced with tools that help you traverse the world and solve puzzles. Despite sharing genre conventions with games like Hollow Knight it's a LOT closer to FEZ, where the main "thing" you're doing is solving, not fighting. Much like Tunic there are tons of secrets to explore if you're willing to sit down and think about it, but it's pretty great as a puzzle-platformer as well if note taking doesn't interest you. The graphics, sound design, and world are all amazing and super memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: I never would've thought one could make such a masterful blend of the metroidvania and puzzle game genres yet here we are. Getting 100% completion will most definitely require that you look at a guide unless you're willing to sacrifice your mental sanity, but I'm ok with that being the case and I definitely enjoyed the whole journey - guideless or otherwise.On top of that, this is also a technical masterclass on how to make an optimized game from scratch completely by yourself. You don't really see games being made like this anymore, which is a pity because I've always enjoyed delving into the intricacies and optimizations that old games usually had. While it's not really a necessity nowadays, looking at how the whole game only takes up 33 MB of disk space puts a smile on my face every single time.Beware, though, despite the hardware requirements needed for this game being pretty much null in terms of raw power, it still requires a directX 12 capable GPU in order to work.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty good! I thought the puzzles were really clever in many parts. The items were all really interesting; most of them I've not seen close approximations in any other game like this. Especially the "optional" items you get after layer 1.  The "enemies" you run into on this adventure were truly imposing and unique, utilizing movement and attack mechanics that I've not really seen in other games. The music that played during some of these is truly haunting. Indeed, the ambience of the game in general is beautiful. I loved the atmosphere of the world, hearkening back to Hollow Knight and a little bit of Limbo. I really like the "layers" concept; having totally unique challenges for different kinds of playthroughs, and I ADORE the idea behind the layer 3 puzzles (For what it's worth, I completed layers 1 and 2 as of writing this review.)All this said, the game did have some flaws for me. The biggest was probably the traversal/warp system. It's really annoying that the warp to the center of the map takes you to this out of the way room, from which you need to go through a bunch of hallways to get where you actually wanted to go. I found the warp system insufficient in general; there just weren't enough exit points, and i ended up having to do way too much backtracking to get where I wanted. This is only compounded by the player's slow movement speed, making some parts of the game sluggish to get through. Some important visual components didn't feel distinct enough. One of the optional items you can find allows you to break certain blocks, but those blocks look almost exactly like every other block, so it's hard to get much use out of unless you're switching to another optional item to aid in your search. There's another optional item that flips certain switches, but these switches are really hard to see. Speaking of items, there were a lot of items to cycle through by the end of layer 2. This constant menu-diving/pressing L/R over and over again felt cumbersome by this point, and I wish you could have mapped different items to different controller buttons or something to ameliorate this. All in all, though, it was a good game. It's not often that I feel the need to "100%" a game, and this one reached that point for me. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well gives you that feeling back you had when you started to first play videogames.The amount of times i said "Oh" or "Ah" out loud after finding solutions for something is not countable.Unique approaches to metroidvania itemization and awesome level design keep you asking what's next.The game can be divided into multiple layers which tackle you with more and more absurd puzzles. This recommendation only focuses on layer 1 and 2, since those layers are the only ones you can realistically solve on your own without a guide. Further layers only got solved through advanced community work and are not meant to be solveable as a single person. Getting all achievements is possible without these later layers.Despite Animal Well being a short journey, with layer 1 and 2 taking up about 8 to 15 hours, it is well (pun intended) worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I personally had a great time with this game. Don't be turned away by the horror genre tag, as I generally didn't find this game scary, and this is coming from someone who can't even play the first night of FNAF 1 without getting super paranoid. Unnerving at times, yes, but not terrifying.ANIMAL WELL doesn't have "swing your sword" combat, as it more focuses on innovative puzzles and interesting room designs to make you really think. Pretty much every room has something to do, and it's never too frustrating to figure out (though, if you're like me and *did* get stumped on some puzzles, the community has made several helpful guides to get you on the right track).The atmosphere and music is awesome too. If you're used to how Rain World uses their music tracks to intensify a moment, then its similar here. Less music, more environmental sounds. Very nice and immersive.I'm sure I'm missing things to do, even though I've gotten all achievements and all tools, so this game has loads of content. If you like puzzle games and exploration, with a hint of an unnerving vibe, than this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is an outstanding accomplishment for a solo developer, and a truly memorable ~8 hours or so before hitting the credits. (Though there appears to be much, much more for those dedicated to uncovering every delightful mystery...) The blend of dense, scan-lined pixel art and modern fluid effects gives this such a cool, unique look, spooky and surreal but still colorful and inviting.The sound design is a stand-out, too. If you close your eyes and just listen to this, you'll feel like you're in a subterranean jungle or something. It's so rich, so alive, while remaining understated enough to quietly meditate over... mostly. ;)It's also mechanically unique among Metroidvanias, offering much cleverer puzzles than your typical lock-and-key fare. There isn't really combat, but survival is not guaranteed; you'll have to use your fun array of toys in novel ways to make it through the otherworldly labyrinth. It's all very fresh and very satisfying!Also, your mileage may vary on this, but I gotta give big ups to any game like this that tells you *nothing*. There's no dialogue, no tutorials, no bullsh*t. It's not even clear what kind of little guy you're playing as... nothing whatsoever getting in the way of immediately experimenting and getting lost in the joy of discovery. I love this approach to design and game "storytelling," and Animal Well nails it.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This was an excellent first entry for both Big Mode and Billy Basso. It's been many years since I've had this much fun with a Metroidvania, with the closest example I can think of being Metroid Dread in terms of enjoyment. Animal Well is not too long and the lack of combat is an interesting new twist for the genre. The abilities are unique and bend your brain as you get deeper in the well as you use them to traverse and solve puzzles. Speaking of, the puzzles were fantastic! I was able to solve the first ending and about 58 of the 64 eggs without a guide.  Good luck for whoever tries to 100% this game with no help, especially if you plan to do the true ending. Overall very worth 25$, so buy it (and if you haven't played Metroid Dread yet, go play that first. It's the best the genre has ever had, and Animal Well is a very close second!).

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐️ 10/10 ⭐️Rarely do I ever give a game a perfect score but as I sit here to write a review I can't think of a single negative thing to say other than I wish it was longer which isn't really a bad thing. It's really hard to find anything that surprises me with puzzle games anymore, many of them utilize the same tropes and the same solutions that hardly ever give anything new to the genre. Animal Well is the exception, the puzzles feel *fresh* and the items you pick up along the way are so *unique.* Every time I found something new the pang of excitement I felt was something I kept craving throughout the game, it was thrilling to continue discovering new ways to enter new areas or remember an area where something you picked up can help solve it. I praise the developers for their *ZERO* hand holding and wish I could hug each of them for their very clear effort in execution. The game really drops you in and wishes you luck, my favorite type of adventure. But, they're clever in their helpful hints whether it be background markings or teaching you new ways to move by giving you rooms that provide you with a little more context about how an item works (purposefully being vague here to avoid spoilers). The atmosphere this game builds is spooky but curious, horrific but charming. It's the perfect balance that somehow tells a story without any dialogue. I love that "the end" is not really the end, too. I can't wait to continue to play and really uncover everything it has to offer. Congratulations to the team, y'all really killed it here.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, an excellent metroidvania. Very satisfying progression and mostly logical and well thought out level design.I will note that at times it can be frustratingly difficult and feel disproportionately difficult compared to an area you were just in. But the experience as a whole is really great and personally I'm a big fan of the high contrast dark-neon pixel art. Of course, if backtracking isn't your thing, give the game a miss, it's part of the genre so if you don't like it then don't play. It was great to re-explore with new tools thoughSpoilers ahead (mainly feedback aimed at devs):I love the flute, I love that they weren't afraid to give the player the ability to teleport from anywhere and that there were a few key locations you could warp to.One of the frustratingly difficult things that I refuse to complete is the "Floor is Lava" bunny, I only tried it because I thought one of the achievements would be getting all of the bunnies because on Steam they are secret but I looked up a list and found out that it wasn't. I'm very relieved that it wasn't mandatory for 100% because I wouldn't have gotten it otherwise. Another frustratingly difficult part in my opinion was the first Manticore section, but only up until I realised the lantern was the key to success in that fight, maybe there was a clue I missed about using it in that section but it was an annoying section until I figured out the lantern could buy me time to figure out the puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A triumph. Feels great to play, the world is interconnected and unfolds like an origami rabbit (hehe) as you continue to explore and unlock new items. It looks and sounds absolutely beautiful. The secrets are SO satisfying to solve and well constructed, and there are TONS of them. Bravo Billy Basso!!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Super delightful.  The items, atmosphere, and animations are all supremely charming.  There's not really any combat or punishment for dying which makes trying things out and searching every nook and cranny not too much of a chore.There's so, so many secrets, to be found and I'd say a good 90% of them are very doable on your own if you have a bit of patience.  Making liberal use of the map, stamps, and drawings makes it very rewarding to go back to things once you find the right items to see it all.  All the different areas, animals, and secrets constantly surprised me in a very addicting way.By the end of my experience, I found one or two things to be a little too difficult to solve on my own, but it was still really enjoyable to seek it all out even with the help of a guide for a few things here and there.  I really, really enjoyed this game and got a lot more out of it than I thought I would.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enjoyable and creative game, but seriously over-hyped and overrated. This review is my attempt to bring some balance to the force...The good:The not-so-good:Also you'll hear this game compared to Outer Wilds, but I think this is an unfair comparison. Outer Wilds rewards your perseverance with remarkable plot reveals, incredible locations, and interesting game mechanics, combining narrative, puzzle solving, and world building beautifully. Animal Well doesn't have any of those things; instead it has a series of interesting, challenging, and layered puzzles in an appealing world. Just don't expect to be blown away, unless you are really into the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by its pretty visuals; Animal Well is an intelligent, often unsettling metroidvania and game-of-the-year contender! The ethereal pixellated art style is a visual treat wrapped in tight platforming and elaborate puzzle-solving. The animals in question have the capacity to be cute and novel to nightmare-inducing, sending chills down your spine without needing to jump-scare you. Couple that with the game's immediacy, fun items, and the most obtuse of puzzles, and you have a product you can sink so much more time into even after the credits roll.Bigmode's first published game smashes it out of the park! Animal Well delivers on a Rain World-esque metroidvania with some of the most delightful visuals of 2024!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: lots of exploration and puzzles, as a guy who hates metroidvania's exploring the map of animal well surprisingly fun. The game does nothing to even indicate that there is more hiding within each nook and crannie but the sense of exploration and scale that the map creates makes it fun to search for things on your own.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an interesting metroidvania where you slowly unlock more areas of the map not only by getting new gear, but also by learning new things you can do with your gear.It is also a deep rabbit hole of hidden stuff you can get into even after finishing the game... Kind of wish it was a bit less obtuse in places and helped you complete more of it rather than making you reliant on guides...
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It actually is the first well type game: The puzzles are such that you find yourself getting sucked deeper and deeper into the 'well' so to speak. You decide to do a puzzle and it takes you 20 tries but you know it can be done. Then when you finally do it, the game knows. Deeper and deeper into the 'well' you go. A great example is the bubble level - on the surface you can just cross the stage on the bubbles. Then you wonder whats below and suddenly the bubbles which were easy before are now your only way out and become a whole other game in itself as you must climb up them now. Its constantly twisting and turning and asking you 'what now huh?' but always always there's an answer.Great work Billy Basso
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: If you like platformer games you'll LOVE this game, I have't played one in so long and playing Animal Well has been the most fun I've had playing a platformer ever. There are still so many secrets I haven't gotten yet and I can't wait to sink more hours into it just looking for them10/10 would play again and again and again
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is an unconventional game, but absolutely amazing if you go into it with the right mindset. While technically it's a metroidvania platformer game, it's more of a game about secrets as described by the creator himself. This game is best played without a guide, trying to figure things out for yourself. The game is expertly crafted to give you well designed hints that lead you to a solution without outright telling you. It makes you feel smart. On top of the well designed mechanics, the game is just beautiful, the pixel artstyle and the different particle effects look great. While it might not be for the average player, Animal Well is a great experience that I can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I watch a dude goes by Fury Forged on YT, he usually covers cryptic Noita puzzles and similar niche indie games that make you use your actual brain. So when he said this game was "densely layered, a love letter to video game secrets of old." I had to give it a try.Yeah, the statement provided by Fury is accurate. This game is absolutely charming, moody, spooky, intriguing... and most of all fun to play! At the time of writing I've found 26 eggs, and found 3 out of 4 of the games Macguffins (the colored flames), found a handful of obscure secrets that were VERY obtuse...and yet I feel like I've only scratched the surface. The dev has crafted something special here, and I like the time I spend in the world they've made. Pick this up if it looks interesting AT ALL. and DON'T READ SPOILERS lol.Also I don't know what a Dunkey even is.

I say 'finished' because I'm pretty sure I'm only through one of the several layers of gameplay that exist in the game, but other reviews have covered that thoroughly, so I don't think there's any need for me to rehash it here.I enjoyed my time with this one. _childDocuments_.review: I played the game for over an hour, but I still don't get the hype. It's a good puzzle platformer so far, but nothing that surprised me. Maybe this comes later in the game, but right now I don't have the feeling to play something so special, that it deserves an overwhelming positive rating. With that being said: If you believe in the hype, then I wouldn't recommend the game to you just based on that.p.s I remember playing Tunic for the first time: finding the first few pages of the manual and noticing they are not just some collectables, but fundamental to the game's understanding; that was special! And later, when I figured out the hidden line paths in it, which ultimately let to the golden path puzzle; that was mind blowing.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: You'll love this game if you enjoy incredibly fiddly platforming that requires exact jumps which only land if you do them at the very last minute, while being attacked by things or dealing with things that drop or pop as you stand on them, combined with extremely twitchy and slippery controls, where making a single mistake means you have to repeat an entire frustrating section from the start and the game then starts to make you do this while jumping between screens such that you can't see what you're even aiming for (or if you're even headed to the correct side of the next screen) until you're there, where you inevitably make a mistake (because you didn't GUESS where you'd need to land, and then fall down and have to backtrack for miles just for another attempt).You'll love the game if you like that. But I won't love you, or the game. I hate this game. Which is a shame, as the presentation is great, and it looks like there's a good metroidvania under the hellish moment-to-moment gameplay.This is the kind of game that I'd only play today via an emulator with savestates. It's just too frustrating, and the frustration comes from bad/outdated design, nothing else.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well can be described best as a descent. It's a metroidvania that tells you very little upfront, and tasks you with following your own curiosities to slowly learn more about the game. It's one of those situations where I can't say too much because a lot of the game is centered around secrets and self-discovery. You'll just have to take my word on it.Luckily, Animal Well is still pretty accessible and doesn't ask you to do anything crazy upfront. There are many "stopping points" when it comes to uncovering the secrets of this game. Beating the game up to the credits is not too difficult and is a nice, atmospheric experience with some fun puzzles and tense moments. I only did a little bit secret hunting after this point because I suck at navigation-based collectible hunts, but I got my fill of exploration and puzzles for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I am not very far into this game, but the atmosphere is unparalleled. It reminds me distinctively of Rain World in a magical way. The way the game looks is immaculate; never seen anyone do the things this game does with pixels and lighting effects. It lends the entire world an air of deep mystery and allure that must be similar to what archaeologists feel. Get the game. Do it. BigMode is onto something big.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to let you all in on a secret I found, but don't tell Dunkey you heard from me, alright?If you boot the game up at 3AM, stay on the title screen for 3 minutes and then recite 'Beeg beeg Yoshi. Beeg beeg Yoshi. Beeg beeg Yoshi' into the mic several times. If you did it right, you should get a picture of a big green guy on your screen. _childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprise.The compelling pixel art is the main reason I bought this game. Before playing I've  heard news about hidden secrets and crazy ideas but I try to play blind, and stay out of spoilers, do as much exploration as I can and enjoy a relaxing journey - in fact, I was surprised by how peaceful Animal Well is.Platform seems to exist only for action games, previously popular games including Ori, Messenger and Hollow Knights etc., all are not easy to finish and bring tests on reactions and proficiency, rewarding player satisfaction after each boss. However, enemies in Animal Well won't chase you till the end and there's no mandatory bosses to fight to finish the 1st run. There are, indeed, some enemies but nothing too challenging, overall this game is super friendly to new players of action games, and surprisingly, offers the same level of satisfaction upon finishing.The pixel art is superb, with top-notch map design and mind-blowing multi-use of inventories, I can't praise enough how clever some puzzle designs are. There are some places where I got stuck so I had to check playthroughs to pass: (1) Use bubble gun on fish (2) Use yoyo on mouse (3) use fireworks on chinchillas, and (4) ghost cat chase. With a bit of help, this game is such a pleasure to play.I finished the 1st run in 9 hours with more than 20 eggs. Upon knowing there's more to discover, I earned extra tools and eventually doubled the amount of collectible eggs. I'm never good at finding secrets and not that keen on discovering everything, so after 14 happy hours as I discovered as much area as I could I decided to stop. I'm yet to find the use of that giant ring nor the clock, never seen the time capsule but every minute I've spent in Animal Well is pure joy. I wish in the future there will be new DLCs, and easier ways to reach the other endings, but for now I'm already satisfied with the content I've explored.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game has floored me with its trippy lighting and immersive sound design! The puzzles are tough but don't leave you stumped for too long. Something to note is this is a game with no combat and you have to find peaceful resolutions to the creatures that stand in your way. All in all this is an indie game MUST PLAY. Great work from Billy Basso!!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely creative and delightful. It's clear that so much thought and attention has gone into every aspect of this game. From the unique and vibrant pixel art to the tight controls, everything is so well done. The puzzles are challenging, but intuitive. The platforming is tough, but precise and never feels cheap. I couldn't recommend this game enough. Anyone looking for a fresh puzzle platformer, you've found it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the Dunkey fans mislead you. This game is for real for real an amazing game, it's not just YouTube memes. The sound design in particular blows me away and the gameplay feels so smooth and satisfying. This game has genuinely reminded me why I like playing games. Every mystery I solve gives me so much excitement, and my wife enjoys watching too.This first of it's kind open well game is very unique and I don't want to spoil too much as figuring out the game is part of the games charm. I will say though that this game is BIG, the developer absolutely insane to have done all of this themselves. I'm around 5-6 hours in and have barely scratched the surface of this game. It's WELL worth the 20 bucks.If you like beautiful, atmospheric, and mysterious metroidvania style games this should be an instant favorite for you. Also it plays perfectly on steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is okay, but probably not worth it at full price for any non-collector gamer. Playing this game to the initial "end" is about 5 hours of pretty interesting metroidvania-esque platforming and puzzle solving. There's a bunch of secret collectibles and a really interesting meta easter egg that was fun to watch people figure out , but realistically is not something obtainable for an average gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I love the adventure and the secrets that the game is littered with. As a metroidvania type game, this does really well with it.My only complaint is there is a little too much back and forth and going all over the map 100x times over, which gets a little repetitive, but I still thoroughly enjoyed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are why I roll my eyes when I hear people complain about the quality of games these days. There will always be an overwhelming number of low-quality titles in circulation, but developers like Billy Basso will always be working behind the scenes to deliver something memorable and worthy of passing on to your peers and loved ones.You won't find them yapping on Twitter or YouTube; you'll find them working hard to deliver an experience like the one you'll hopefully purchase after reading this review.'Animal Well' is a unique gem in the platformer/Metroidvania genre, offering a nonviolent gameplay experience peppered with rewarding puzzles. Its ability to balance charm and unease is a testament to Basso's design methodology.When you play this, go in blind, exercise your curiosity, and soak in all the magnificent details it offers.Thankful I purchased this; I hope you do too.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a short game to "beat". It took me about 7 hours to get to the "end", though there are still many secrets to find. If you are only looking to roll credits you'll have a fun time, but you'll probably finish it in 2-3 sittings so keep that in mind before purchasing. As for me, I'm more than happy with that. Animal Well is the type of game that begs you to achieve 100% completion. Secrets and puzzles are perfectly laid out, always rewarding your curiosity in any direction you go. The strange creatures you cross paths with on your adventure give the world such a unique feel, always getting you to wonder just what led this place to be the way it is. Because of its atmosphere and dense map, Animal Well shines in a way few games do. Also I like the silly abilities.This may be a slight spoiler but: The game

If you like metroidvanias where you can just get lost and explore youll enjoy it. _childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Main game is great fun, exploration is open ended and cleverly designed. Tools feel widely useful and I was always excited to get another. Puzzles can be hard but never felt insurmountable. Fun begins to trail off a bit the further you get into secret hunting and the postgame. Later tools feel much more specific in use and some of the puzzles are really only solvable by blindly scouring the whole map or googling the solution. Some puzzles, like the rabbit mural, were probably really awesome while the community was still figuring them out. But now, a while after release, they amount to nothing but a google search. Presentation is brilliant, no complaints here. The various animals milling about are a delight to discover, and there is a fair amount of interactivity with them for exploration and secrets. Overall a great metroidvania, but for the average player, perhaps not worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, there is an option to set controller button layout type which gets a massive + from me. Getting major FEZ, Rain World and Cave Story vibes from this game that's packed into an expansive metroidvania style map. You're spawned in the world with no obvious instructions expected to find your own way and find everything you need (including certain UI elements) along the way. I've already found more items than I expected and am surprised by the variety and honestly just the whimsicality the game has to pull some of them off. The graphics are beautiful (I don't use scan lines). The method used to mimic dynamic pixelated lighting on creatures and the environment is something I don't think I've seen done before. The sound design is minimal but perfectly captures the atmosphere. Also the haptic feedback and audio features of the PS5 controller made for this game are incredible. You actually feel the grass rustling as you move through it and each jump of your character feels light and bouncy in your hands.I heard there's layers of secrets in this game but I've yet to get far enough to confirm how deep it goes. This is the type of game you'll want to go into as blind as possible though I can tell.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game at this point and I honestly don't even know what to say, but I'm going to try. Firstly, there will be no spoilers here! So, as a long time Metroidvania and general retro gaming / indy game fan, it left me with no complaints. I really haven't been so happy with a game in a very long time. It is beautiful, atmospheric, challenging, the world tells so much entirely through seeing. Not a word is uttered and yet you'll feel so many things as you go through the game. I figured from the trailer that I would be into this, but I had no idea I was in for something as deep and passionately made as this. I really don't think I've felt this way about a game since Super Metroid, and let me tell ya, it's been a lot of years waiting. If there was a one time award you could give a game on Steam, I'd have never touched it in all of these years, but today would have been the day I did. Seriously do yourself a service and give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Really digging it so far. Emphasis on exploration and puzzle solving, the art style and visual design of the world is gorgeous and unique. There's no hand holding or tutorials but the game gives you enough visual queues for you to piece together what you need to do, it's very clear that the design of the game is very intentional and considered down to the tiny details.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a mechanically great game, with literally nothing else going for it outside of hype and meta-gaming. It should win 2024 GOTY, but only because it's been an abysmal year for games.It's also incredibly overhyped and a tad overrated. This is an amazing metroidvania, with gorgeous graphics and artistic style. The world building, atmosphere, and platforming are top tier.But it's difficult as hell, esoteric as ♥♥♥♥, and has literally zero story or lore. I wish there was something here, an overarching story, even if it was a simple one. But the game is just a bunch of un-connected, really fun, platformer challenges.Don't get me wrong, there is a GOAL. Get the four flames. But there is no explanation why, nor reason to do anything outside of "to do it."The "end-game" is also incredibly lame. It's frustrating and un-fun, and you would never be able to do any of it on your own without outside knowledge. This is a literal design choice, and I think it's a bad one. There are so many things that are just literally never explained to you, and unless you cheated, you would have no way of knowing about them. It's engagement bait for "lore youtubers".I would give the game an 8/10. It is good, but I personally have to dock points for the complete lack of narrative and some bad design choices.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game and highly recommended for both puzzle and metroidvania fans. You're constantly getting new items and discovering new areas

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting, beautiful side-scrolling and exploration game with novel puzzles and great "gamefeel". Reminds me of Fez and that whole era of indie games that felt like they were stuffed with secrets under the surface. If you told me this was a lost XBLA game from 2007, I'd believe you. 100% worth buying!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Its a really good metroidvania that incorporates more ideas from discovery type games, such as FEZ, TUNIC, and Outer Wilds.In the game you will both receive mechanical upgrades that helps you progress, but these tools have a lot more versatility than meets the eye, and the discovery of these applications is as much of a metroidvanian upgrade as the mechanical ones.My major gripe with the game is that it is very annoying to backtrack and find out what you are missing. You unlock tools to mark off stuff on the map so you can come back later. But this is an upgrade that you dont start with, and by the time you unlock it you've passed so much already that you should've marked off.There are a lot of collectibles, and a large portion of the game is dedicated to these collectibles. I only wish it was easier to see where there is more to discover, such as an icon on a map tile telling you that you have found everything that you can find in that tile.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Its alright.Its has quite unique, charming abilities that i rarely see in a Metroidvania. Theres tons of secrets to find, but it gets tedious in some areas, where you have to runs through 5+ screens just for another attempt. Its short, but has extra content to find after the end. You dont even need all abilities to beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and unique puzzle-focused Metroidvania. The power-ups are unorthodox, and the level and puzzle design are great. Interactions between you and the world feel natural, and the sense of discovery and wanderlust doesn't disappear for all 8~10 hours the "main" game will take you to complete. Animal Well might be the first game in the genre to actually try something very different from the norm to great success - coming from a single developer, that is all the more commendable.The game also has dozens of hours of extra post-game content, with many mysteries and obscure secrets for you to find and solve. I wasn't going to play this anymore, so I took a quick look, and multiple of them seem like completely random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to me; however, I know a lot of people love this kind of thing, and if that is you it's your lucky day.As you might know, Animal Well is the first game published by Dunkey's publisher, BigMode; as a result, a lot of reviews are effectively worthless memes that ignore the developer and the game's merits entirely. Hopefully, this gave you a better idea of what you're getting, although this is an easy recommendation for pretty much anyone since the game is a short, well-polished experience.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. This game gives you a simple toolkit, but man, there are so many creative ways to use your items. It doesn't take very long to get to the first credit roll, but this well goes so much deeper afterwards!This game certainly isn't for everyone, but if you like metroidvanias and/or puzzles, then you will love this.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully made game. The atmosphere is great, interesting and even a bit haunting. A world that's fun to get lost in. The game mechanics and puzzles are fun and very well thought out. For the most part, there's a good gradual pacing of the difficulty of the puzzles with a range of casual to pretty advanced levels of difficulty. It's simply enjoyable and one can tell alot of love went into this. Play it! You'll find that the Well is deep.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like outer wilds if outer wilds was a metroidvania. For the most part, you can go in any direction assuming you know how to solve the problems that are presented to you. If you have the knowledge, you can overcome the problem, much like in outer wilds. Outer wilds is probably my favorite indie game ever so I am all for it. Buy this game. It’s a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It seems fine. Perfectly fine for a puzzle-focused Metroid clone, but not what I was hoping for.While I dig the general atmosphere and ambience, I don't find it as immersive as I thought it was going to be, due to general nitpicks like the arbitrary block-puzzles and floating platforms hanging about, gamifying the areas more than I'd like. While it is petty, I guess I just didn't think it would be going for that with such unsubtle design.Gameplay-wise, its puzzles and simple platforming in a 2D environment. You like flicking three switches by moving stuff around to open a door? You got it. And that kinda feels like what most of the puzzles are going for, at least until you might get the tools to spice up things up with the big overarching problems shown early, but I really don't want to do more switch puzzles to reach them from what the game has presented, I could easily find a hundred or more so puzzle games that just devolve into switch flicking.And some of the threats during gameplay feel a bit easy to deal with, and fairly brute-forceable with simply tanking hits and using the invulnerability frames to ignore them while you get past them. It just feels like you were actually meant to be weary of them in puzzles, but you just run past them anyway.The art is pleasant enough, if maybe a little less detailed than I'd like, and turning on scan-lines make things pop better, but hurts my eyes after a while. Other than that, its not the worst looking pixel-art style I've seen. Not a big fan of the player character though, though I suppose for the art style it might be hard to make something interesting equal to a block in size for puzzles that isn't just a non-descript slime blob creature.I guess overall, I just find it a bit too expensive for what it is, though its not quite to my taste. I even thought about comparing it to La-Mulana or something as I was expecting a bit more of  sort of puzzles, but the puzzles are initially too simple to get read on of the overall product. Maybe it gets better or maybe it doubles down on the door switches, but it isn't worth $30+ to me from what its shown so far.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem. This is a puzzle game, disguised as a platformer/metroidvania.The puzzles have puzzles. Traditional combat doesn't exist, and all the better for it.Front to back could probably clear the 'initial' game in 10~hours. I spent an additional 38 hours combing over every room in the game, coming back days later after having a random thought "But what about this?". Words can't describe how great this is. If you enjoyed games like TUNIC or FEZ, this is an absolute no brainer.Don't read a guide, figure it out as you go, you'll be way happier in the end.TLDR: The next Billy Basso game can't come soon enough. Puzzles have Puzzles, that have Puzzles...that have Puzzles. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I am few hours into the game and found my first flame and the journey to get it was truly magical. Interactions with the animals are the highlights of this game, finding clever ways to get around the animals or use them to get around sometimes never gets old. The tools provided are a work of genius, props to billy basso. The sheer amount of secrets in this game is baffling but finding them is so damn rewarding and shout out to dunkey cause if wasn't for him this game would have gone under the radar for many gamers. Now i know what halo 2 meets halo 3 feels like.(Overall- 4/5)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out very strong, has some good moments and a few really good items that are fun to figure out on your own. Unfortunately it runs into the classic metroidvania problems near the end of having not enough content left, but what is left is obscure and hard to find and you don't know where to look in this now enormous map. A few items are either really annoying to use, or incredibly situational and would've been better having just not been included (looking at you, B Ball).As for the end-game riddles and puzzles, I know some people will really love them and appreciate them, and I myself am that person sometimes. But it all comes really out of nowhere  after a full game of what's a pretty standard metroidvania format (albeit with great art and some really cool ideas). I know some people will say that it doesn't matter because you can still complete the normal ending without doing everything in the game or even finding all the eggs, but for me a game ending like that, showing you there's significantly more here but you just haven't done it or figured it out, spoils the standard ending and I just come away with the experience feeling incredibly incomplete.Had this been a game like Tunic, upfront about its riddles and obscurity throughout the entire game, I'd have no problem with any of this. But just throwing in ridiculously obscure riddles and puzzles and an ARG after a full game's worth of none of that, just makes me feel frustrated. It's the same issue Fez has, it becomes a good game to talk about but not a good game to play. It starts out fun and ends frustrating, souring the whole experience
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art is sometimes gorgeous, sometimes so busy it's hard to see what's actually happening. The music and mood are sublime; the enemies and atmosphere are brilliant and menacing. There are exquisite details the likes of which I haven't seen since Hollow Knight.I cannot stand, and it's enough to ruin the game for me, the pixel perfection demanded without being consistent. Yo-yo not going to the right place? Tough, better hope it scrambles and finds its way to that switch. Not making that jump, but only missing by a pixel or two? Good luck figuring out if you're just missing the jump or altogether lacking an item.There *is* physical momentum, so you have to take running starts, but sometimes basic navigation is hateful. I'm not talking about a challenge room, and not necessarily an overall platform challenge game - it's mostly puzzles with timing elements, with a few tight jumps in and around spikes and traps. Every once in a while, though, there are regular traversals that demand pixel precision. Why? It's not Super Meat Boy.The way it changes screens is often literally, visually sickening and disorienting, where your character is instantly approaching the new screen from the old position, with no cue, clue, or indication how you're going to end up in the new screen. Yet it frequently demands that you know exactly where you needed to be in advance of you even knowing where you're going.It's got atmosphere and style like most games can only wish, but I really don't understand people saying this "redefines metroidvanias." It happens to be one with tons of style and a fantastic, creepy, sinister vibe, like you're bumping into Old (animal) Gods you should never have met. But damn does it suck to play in a bunch of ways. I'm going to try to finish it, but I look forward to putting it away when I do.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit skeptical due to assuming inflated review scores from the Youtube publisher's devoted community. In spite of that, the game is utterly absorbing in both atmosphere and depth of content. The emergent complexity evolves from a pick-up-and-play level of intuitiveness to utterly labyrinthine levels of depth in both its mechanics and secrets to uncover. It straddles the fine line of having virtually zero intrusive tutorials without ever becoming unreasonable to reach the credits without a guide. Fan of the genre (or Dunkey) or not, this is easy to recommend for anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The second I hit install the second it was download and ready to play, I was shocked!Billy Basso has crafted an amazing atmosphere in this game.  The song playing while you're on the menu gives the perfect vibe for the environment you are about to explore.  You will constantly be surprised with how some of the animals react when you use your gadgets around them.   The same applies for how your gadgets work as well.  You may think something has only one purpose, but the more you experiment with them the more you realize there are multiple different ways to meaningfully use each gadget.The puzzles feel very intuitive and satisfying to solve.  You are greatly rewarded for testing out your own ideas and thinking outside of the box to find the solution.  There is also the platforming which can feel like a puzzle in itself at times, but that brings a nice mix to the game.  Mechanics are amazing and well thought out with how it all works together.  Absolutely loved accidentally jumping onto the frisbee and discovering what happens when you land on it, that's all I'll allude too for this review.Once again, Billy Basso has made an amazing game, I hope to see more from him in the future.  Big thanks to him for making it and another thanks to Bigmode/Dunkey for putting so many eyes on the game.  Be sure to recommend Animal Well to your buddies who might not know about Dunkey, the more new faces, the more recognition for both Billy Basso and Bigmode for crafting and publishing such a unique game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Every part of this game is fun. I had so much fun even dying isn't that painful most of the time. If it looks bad to you you will hate it. But if you don't need a photo realistic experience the style explodes across the screen TIME AFTER TIME. This game BLEEDS ascetic out of every pore.My sense of discovery continues and I recommend getting weird. Do stupid stuff, that *shouldn't* work. It often does.You will however be expected to think about the environmental puzzles in order to solve them, but if you aren't going 100% most of the most complex puzzles are optional.Seems expensive for an indie title from a brand new publisher but at full price this game is a steal. This can depend on your personal budget but if you want something to chew on by yourself or with a friend or two sharing stories of exploration I can't recommend it more.This game will almost certainly go down as another masterpiece alongside noita, hollow knight, and super mario brothers 2. Dozens of others will continue to make games inspired by this as love letters for generations to come. I look forward to more WELL type games from Big Mode.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautiful, captivating, and unexpectedly horrifying at times. A wide variety of fun and unique tools to unlock as you traverse puzzles that are difficult but incredibly satisfying to accomplish. A game that could beat Knack as GOTY.I would not be surprised if in the future, the name Billy Basso is household knowledge of the likes of Hideo Kojima, Todd Howard, or Gabe Newell. I can't wait to see what Billy will create next!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put in words how this game made me feel. Animal Well has something for everyone. It feels both difficult and fair, but never easy or punishing. The joy of finding secrets, discovering new ways to explore the well, and solving some of the most fun puzzles is around every single corner, and hidden in every nook and cranny. Controls feel tighter than possibly any game I've played in the last 10 years, every single room is a hand decorated work of art, met with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, topped off with some of the most enjoyable and creative puzzles I've ever solved. Moment after moment after moment of "How did they even come up with this?"
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much more I can say that hasn't been said before, but Animal Well is a master class in show-not-tell gameplay chock full of aha moments and more depth beyond your initial (of which there are many) credit screens than perhaps any other game. There are many stopping points at which players can choose to gracefully bow out of the game, but for those who enjoy increasingly obscure and esoteric mysteries, puzzles, and secrets Animal Well is the deepest I can recall. Some of the post-game puzzles start becoming SO mysterious you should not feel ashamed if you want to declare you've had your fill with Animal Well and move on or look up solutions on the internet, but I think that is a strength of the game and not a weakness; This well is, ironically, as deep as you want it to be. The innovative uses of the tools you find are always fun when you discover a new, unexpected use of something you've already been using for hours, and who knows what percentage of those secrets of the game have yet to be discovered.The style, the sound design, the fact that the entire game is literally only 33MB, you can just go on and on about this game. Suffice it to say, I would recommend every single gamer, whether they are specific fans of metroidvanias or not, to at least try this game at some point. Yes, it is that good.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a metroidvania game heavily focused on puzzles: you'll find yourself in a big world , where each of the obstacles and struggles down your path is treated like an effort in creative thinking (). This game is not an high octane action adventure and you'll may feel disappointed ig that's the experience you're seeking: AW is a slow burn, you're a little thing trying to survive and understand a world much bigger and more complicated than you, the OST and sound effect will both lull and agitate your senses depending on the situation, you'll feel the frustration of getting lost and the satisfaction of discovering new areas.All of this just to say this is not a game for everyone and this leads to my final thought: is this game worth $24.99? To be fair it's subjective. For me 1$/hour of gameplay is a fair compromise for a singleplayer non-rpg game and in my opinion not recommending this game because there are cheaper and better alternatives like Hollow Knight, Blasphemous, Bloodstained or Guacamelee is a dumb and disingenuous argumentation: I'm not recommending this game because it's the best of the best, I'm recommending it beacuse it's something different where you can chill and take your time figuring out your next move. It is not an experience for everyone, but for those who it's adressed to it's a hell of one.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL
