_childDocuments_.review: I can't say anything about Animal Well that hasn't already been said. What Animal Well accomplishes is genuinely extraordinary from both a Technical Standpoint and a Design Standpoint. (I hate calling it this, but it is what it is) Metroid-Vania ESC games have been around for a long time, with varying levels of innovation and deep thought on pushing the genre. Animal Well somehow finds a way to do both in ways that are engaging, interesting, and thought-provoking. On top of that, the game launched at 35+ megabytes in a complete state. If that doesn't impress you in the landscape of Video Games in 2024, I don't know how to help you, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Halo 2 meets Halo 3 but better with less of the first person shooter element and more of the goo ball is stuck in a well filled with animals element.You can tell a lot of passion is going into this game. I've played a lot of Metroidvanias and Roguelikes, but this one has some awesome looking art and unique mechanics. The accompanying sounds are haunting at times and really set the mood. The platforming can be tough at times and the controls are quick and responsive to compensate. Use a controller if you can.So far the puzzles have been unique, but not overly difficult. Enough to give that serotonin release without being too frustrating.The price point is a bit overzealous for an indie game from the first publication of the developer, but an hour in, it seems well worth it.Bottom line is this game is clearly a labor of love, well thought out and will be sure to provide a lot of enjoyment for those who enjoy the Metroidvania genre.Also Slink is Cortana.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! I knew about it due to Dunkey, but didn't really cared about it till its release day.When released I started researching, and soon I stumbled across a comment: "I haven't felt like this since Outer Wilds". At the point I immediately knew that I had to try it because that game was a life changer for me.I haven't played any metroidvanias. Didn't even knew what they were other than seeing a few super metroid clips here and there.I couldn't stop playing! It took me a weekend, or to be exact, 12 hours and some help here and there but reached the credits. I think I was a bit slow, but maybe because I don't really play puzzle nor platformer nor metroidvania games. ^^It was an awesome journey. Maybe I should try other metroidvanias.After I reached the credits I felt a bit empty and I wanted to keep going. And turned out there are tons of more puzzles and this wasn't even the real ending. I mean the credits rolled, but (I guess canonically) the real ending is further ahead. Though for some reason the game felt closed for me with that credits roll... and continuing collecting the remaining stuff, solving more puzzles seemed a bit tedious for me. That's how far my curiosity brought me I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Brainy, tight metroidvania. Went straight into the top echelon of the genre for me. Animal Well drops the traditional combat aspect of the genre for a more heavier focus on puzzles. Puzzles range from easy to brain burning, but you can see the end credits without needing to solve the most hardcore ones. I saw the end credits in around 9h mark, but the game had still much more to offer after that. I had explored maybe 2/3 of the game if even that, at that point. An easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Took me a bit but I've almost 100% the game. But the feeling of wonder and exploration without being handheld was refreshing. Learning things either by mistake or with an idea to see it come true was amazing. There's no combat but a focus on puzzle solving. Overall, I've enjoyed the experience and plan on tackling the next secrets later.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't written a legit steam review for a game in about 10 years and Animal Well was so good I'm changing that. Animal Well is a game with so much love and passion put into it that it's so incredibly hard to put down. Please buy this game; it is one of the best experiences I've had with a Metroid-Vania in a VERY long time.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This a fantastic puzzle metroidvania. It really encourages you to experiment with your platforming and the use of your tools. I think Fez would be a game I would positively compare this to.I especially like how dense the game is. A single puzzle room might have multiple different ways to tackle it, sometimes just allowing for different methods to solve it and sometimes leading to different paths or collectables. Then, that room same might have secret walls or paths layered on separately from the puzzles, allowing for even more progression.Some spoilersI think the area revolving around the disk is the best example of this. It is a gauntlet of several rooms that you tackle several times, and depending on your progression, it changes how you go through them. The first time, you may only be able to address the basics, but there is minimal stress. The second time, there is more stress, but you have a new tool from the same area to solve puzzles and platform differently. The third time, there is even more stress, but you may have several tools from around the game and one of the game's primary goals waits at the end.End spoilersThe graphics are fairly minimal, but do a great job of conveying all of information you need for any given room. I think the various animals standout for their impressive design. The music is atmospheric and fits the setting well.Overall, this game is worth your time. You can dive as deep as you like. It's satisfying to just play and find what you can, but you can dive so deep that you'll be working with other players to solve large-scale ARG puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It is very refreshing to see a game that is so neatly designed under a unified vision. The lack of traditional combat only makes the game more enjoyable as it leans more into its excellent platforming. Its pacing lends itself well to letting the player get “stuck” and then discovering the path forward just before frustration sets in. Take your time with this one, you will be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Unbeatable atmosphere, and exploration. I would also dispute the fact that there is no "combat". Ye sure you never get a sword to swing and kill things but that doesn't mean its a walking simulator, there is plenty of things that can kill you. At its heart this is an atmospheric puzzle metroidvania and I think its worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Just adding a review to the pile of good feels.  Nothing I say here will be any more useful/informative than any of the other positive reviews, in all likelihood....but, I'll still add that even with only 6 hours in, I find myself engaged to try and figure out as much as I can without a guide/spoilers.  That 6 hours DID include "game completion", which seems wack at first for the price, but it's a misleading notion.  The initial clear doesn't even seem like more than halfway through what a dedicated player can achieve (and I'm not even talking about "fanatic" level of dedication); new opportunities are immediately apparent to dummies like me.  That said I DID figure out a critical "bypass" technique very early on, probably since it's more easily performed than similar genre maneuvers, and this allowed me to explore very non-linearly in the early hours...so I'm not really sure how much of the map is left to uncover.It didn't debut in the right era (or with the kind of story/soundtrack) to make the kind of impact indie games like Undertale did, nor is it as action-packed as fellow MV legend Hollow Knight, but by eschewing combat in favor of exploratory reveals it definitely carves its own curiously-engaging niche.  As understated as it can be, it nonetheless ends up being a bombastic debut for the brilliant Billy Basso, and a bigass finger in the face of Bigmode/Dunkey's doubters to boot....something something halo 2 halo 3
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This really gave me strong original Metroid vibes when I played this as a kid (either 7 or 8 years old). While Animal Well has no combat, I felt isolated like in Metroid. It felt a little creepy, like Metroid sometimes could, and it had that same focus on exploration to find items, to then continue exploring. Animal Well has no combat, but has made its name from the exploration, puzzle-solving, and emphasis on finding secrets. I believe I read that the designer of Animal Well says that has 3 layers of deepness within. After looking more into the "post-game," I see that I only really consider myself yo have completed the first layer. As can be seen by my achievements, 16/20 is is most of them. There is so much more to the game. That said, as an older gentleman, I had a feeling that it wouldn't be worth my time investment to engage with these other layers and looked up information about what was missed. Turns out there is a lot there, and was correct that I'm glad I left the game where I did. I think this fist layer could be completed much more quickly than what I put into the game. Despite everything I've said, I personally feel that the first layer was worth the time and money to play through. I think the second layer is what a lot of people would end up striving for and is not unreasonable if you don't mind doing a lot of backtracking to find secrets. The third layer involves at least one challenge that flat-out require multiple people to solve and are, generally, a lot more esoteric.I think anyone that likes games that don't railroad you into exploring a particular direction and games that don't hold your hand in explaining what things "do" will really get a kick out of this. I don't want to really describe much more than this because Animal Well really invites a player into its unique world, but is particularly waiting for those small few that really want to delve deep.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Videogamedunkey chose a really inspired studio to produce the first Big Mode game. I can almost imagine "more dunkwell" each time I open or close the game.Edit: so it's by one single guy, Billy Basso, and it's been in development for years before Bigmode. Anyway, I really like this game. It's got a cool CRT monitor scanline effect, which probably isn't too hard to make happen, but the design of everything in the game is meant to go well with it (which isn't true for all pixel-art games). Reminds me of old flash games I used to play in high school like Tiny Heist and some other game by the same guy (I think Joust), and of course Endeavor. The main difference being that this map is sprawling and can't be finished in a single half-hour sitting. And the music is great for relaxing to, which can't be said for old-Internet flash games.Spoiler for midgame:  Further spoiler for the same spot of the game:

_childDocuments_.review: does an incredible job of introducing and letting you discover how new mechanics work at your own pace and makes you wonder how to apply them across all the areas you've already explored. great sense of mystery that I'm only starting to crack at, many things littered around that feel like they have some reason to them and it's going to be a long time until i figure it all out, excited to keep exploring. highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: A well made and concise metroidvania that deviates from the path of having the powerups do all the work and instead makes the player think. I collected all of the eggs without help in 13 hours, so it's a reasonably sized game, and there are still secrets beyond what i played. The atmosphere is incredible and unnerving, with great sound design and great spritework. Truly is like halo 2 and 3 combined
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of the best games I've ever played, with some of the most interesting secrets and puzzles. Secrets and puzzles that get so specific and complicated that even the smartest people I know could never get to the end of them. I had such an incredible amount of fun working to get all 64 of the secret eggs in this game, and I managed to find 62 of them before I had to perform Google searches. Even after all of that searching and solving, I still had so many unsolved questions about the game. I would absolutely encourage anyone and everyone to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One BIG step for BigmodeOne GIANT step for Billy BassoBeautiful game and I am excited to experience moreSound design is top notch and I love the polish of the puzzlesReminds me of Fire n' Ice for the NES, its not a breeze of a puzzlerCheers to Dunkey and Mr Basso!(Just want to point out how similar Billy Basso sounds to Joey Bonzo)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely metroidvania focusing on exploration, puzzles and some nasty chasing parts. There are bosses, but no fights. You don't have weapons, but quite some handy toys to find. Great pixel art graphics. Nice atmosphere and music. No technical issues on my end (Linux). I'm through but motivated to do the 100%. Total recommendation.PS: If you're one of those who want to do 100% and even more ... there are some very nasty end game puzzles that require perfect(!) timing and/or external tools.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. The dev made the effort to code every animal behaviour and animation system from scratch, as well as the items. So it's a game unlike one you've ever seen because it's very organic. The world is beautiful and while being vey dense, 7 years of playtesting allow the player to browse it seemlessy thanks to its coherence.There is nothing bad about this game. Also stop saying "omg it's 34MB Billy is a wizard", it has stopped being funny. A very advanced program will be short in size if you don't use tons of librairies / engines, which is the dev's philosophy. Nothing too surprising.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect game for those who like scouring the entire map for secrets and collectibles, and with fun platforming and items to boot. When I accidentally figured out you could do *that* with the frisbee, I was hooked. Billy Basso packed so much creative energy into this project and it shows all the way through. My biggest complaint is that most of the puzzles are pretty easy, but the few remaining in the endgame are extremely cryptic or hidden in niche places that I totally forgot about. Animal Well demands that you take notes along the way. Or use a walkthrough, like I did. (No shame!)8/10
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A captivating and unique Metroidvania experience. As someone who doesn’t usually particularly enjoy Metroidvanias, I’m kinda shocked at how engrossed I am with this game. It just oozes atmosphere and begs to be explored, rewarding the player with fascinating puzzles and environments in every corner! There are also tons of secrets it seems like, and I’ve already stumbled into a few.This is just masterful game design. Each room is so well-tailored and designed that there have been a few times I’ve put my Steam Deck down and said, “Wow, well done.” The developer knows what he’s doing.Give it a try even if this isn’t usually your cup of tea! This is a special one.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I am not normally much of a Metroidvania fan.  However, I am a big dunkey fan and def wanted to support his first publishing venture.  This is really unique.  The art style is cool with this CRT scanline style that is such a vibe.  I played about 3 hours so far and each time I got stuck I was able to move to another area to progress.  I am not sure how long I'll play it tbh, but I really appreciate the love and care put into the game.  Especially the fact that it is a one man venture with programming, art, and soundtrack all by Billy Basso.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Nice puzzles (mostly). Some of them are quite hard (but still fun) - Nice ambiance and sound design- Multiple ways of exploring and getting into places, this makes the experience really rewarding once you figure it out- The map is huuge and has A LOT of hidden stuff- You can play it as a normal metroidvania (you will miss 80% of the fun though)Cons:- Some of the collectables are really easy to miss and since the map is really big its a little annoying sometimes - Some of the endgame puzzles are probably impossible to figure out by yourself (I'm not talking about the one that its meant to work this way)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A well made metroidvania at its core. You can explore and even when you are not supposed to you can often access areas with the items you already have. Having no direct power ups (so far) you have to get creative when using your items. The game easily conveys what you need to do (for the most part) and it just takes some critical thinking and some trial and error to get to the solution
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Visually and mechanically inventive, Animal Well is the best kind of puzzle platformer, putting its tools to perfect use in strong challenges while consistently rewarding curiosity & exploration. A lot of folks will talk about the Deep Secrets in here, the Fez-like mysteries that take a village to solve, but even being someone that doesn't find that scale of gaming particularly appealing, there's lots here on a regular, single, short playthrough of the game to love. There's very little filler, instead jumping right to the full potential of the abilities & animals in play for one or two great puzzles before moving on to the next one. No matter how far gaming as a medium progresses, hopping around as a little guy will always be one of its greatest pleasures.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I have ever played. Interesting graphics, game play, and mechanics. Even after beating the game there are still so many things to do, in a different way then most other post game content. This is the first game I have ever 100% and it was more then worth it. I always look forward to finding the next puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: We can jest about spaghetti and meatballs or 38 megabyte file sizes all we want, but let’s not gloss over the face that this quiet, little game exudes brilliance. Billy Basso is a rare gifted specimen with DaVinci-esk qualities, who will leave you wondering how one single person is capable of creating literally everything within such a highly qualitative product. From its mechanics and concepts, to its design and soundtrack, Basso proves himself a modern human universalis by being responsible for all of it. To be able to conjure up such a unique treasure is easily something to be envious of.Animal Well has such a tangible atmosphere where you can almost just taste the cool fresh water of the world. The gameplay is hardly ever frustrating and allows for fun creativity within its own rules. The puzzles are well balanced and savvily executed. There’s always something clever around the corner and there is even room for surprisingly effective pieces of horror. The main game is short and sweet, but for those who dare venture further there remain layers upon layers to be discovered in the realm of Animal Well.Bigmode’s first outing is a massive success and deserves all the support it can get. It’s an overly clear labour of love, talent and ingenuity.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Halo 2 meets Halo 3.But in all seriousness, this game is amazing. The art style brings me back to old gameboy games, the music/ambiance sounds are amazing. At a certain level, there was some gentle yet tense music, then everything goes crazy. I love all the puzzles and secrets in this game and I'm still trying to find more of them.Billy Basso did an amazing job creating such a fun game and props to Bigmode for publishing it. I expect I'll be continuing to put more hours into this game just to try and find all the secrets!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The first few moments were really charming, and the sound design and little details really felt polished. Then I fell into a really awful loop of being stuck and not knowing where to go, and incredibly frustrated that I couldn't teleport to a previous checkpoint. I get that they want you to explore the world and enjoy the ambiance, but that cute animations quickly turned into a monotonous loop of the same few locations. The screen shift also caused me to die way more than I would have if the screen would shift up as you move to the next room, but with it hard cutting you often cannot see the platform you need to reach and die repeatedly for it. It's impressive that this was made by a single person, but this doesn't feel fully baked. The seahorse bubble room gives you no shortcuts after beating it, and maybe I'm trash at platformers but I was stuck there for so long because I couldn't get a chain of bubbles to form the way I needed to. I struggle with metroidvania type games because if backtracking isn't done right, you lose a lot of sense of exploration and momentum. If you want a cool puzzler with amazing sound design and sparse story, Cocoon is out and is a much less frustrating experience at a similar price point.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: An exploration puzzle game that let's you loose in the world and gives you the freedom to go where ever you find progress. There is a main path with objectives, important items to gather and a clear ending, but you're not told where to go next and it does not matter. If you can figure out how to use your items to get to new places, you're bound to make progress. I felt lost in the beginning with several places I could go to, but soon the world started making more sense.The puzzles are great. You have to use items in creative ways to press buttons, climb the level and to open doors. There seem to be a lot of voluntary puzzles that you can pursue after the credits, giving you collectibles and sometimes even optional items. Observing the environment carefully helps with finding a lot of extra loot.There is no combat in the game. There are some enemies, but not so many that you are constantly running away from them. It's a good balance with the more calm exploration parts. You are mostly trying to out-smart or just avoid any hostile creatures you might run into.The sound design is minimalistic. Mostly you'll listen to ambient cave and nature sounds, which give the game a calm feeling, but occasionally the game throws some tense tunes at you to instill a feeling of dread or panic. Similarly the graphics are simple, but work very well. Some special effects specifically look very modern and stand out against the 8-bit look (in a good way).Definitely recommending this to anyone looking for a metroidvania-style game, just be aware that there is no combat. It's not the longest game either, it took me around eight hours to see the credits, but I also spent a couple of hours finding secrets afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer metroidvania is what Animal Well is.Every ability is unique and never seen before. Why unlock double jump when you can just unlock a bubble wand to create bubbles to jump on?I would say there are 2 or 3 tiers of puzzles in this game, level 1 and 2 for tools and eggs. And level 3 for other endgame secrets :) The level 3 puzzles can be very hard to solve, but are not required!Overall a very fun game, no bugs to be found, maybe a little pricey though. I would price it between $15 and $20.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little metroidvania full of mystery, intrigue, exploration and some incredibly fun and addictive puzzles. Easy to beat in a sitting if you're smarter than me, but the egg hunt will continue your explorations even further.I want to highlight the soundscape in particular. Mysterious, ephemeral and haunting are the only words I can use to describe it.So basically like Halo 2 and 3 combined.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with striking and powerful atmosphere. The kind of game that rewards exploration and a willingness to try ideas, even if they're a shot in the dark. A wide variety of puzzles that greatly vary in difficulty but, for the main experience of the game, I wouldn't say they ever get too frustrating. There are plenty of puzzles that have multiple solutions, and some that you may not even need to solve at all if it's out of your grasp, you can always come back to it later. This game encourages players to look around and take whatever path seems the most interesting. If you play through the game and don't want it to end, you're in luck. There's a great great deal of "post completion" things to do! If you do end up wanting to dive into the trickier content, I highly recommend looking up SPOILER FREE guides instead of walkthroughs. The community is amazing and there are plenty of guides that gently coax you towards figuring things out for yourself (or blatantly tell you to look up the answer and save yourself a lot of time and frustration.)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The environment was like if Disneyland's Electric Main Street Parade were transposed to Burning Man, which in turn was being held in a billionaire's penthouse reef-aquarium set-up, then rendered in pixels.  The soundtrack is also pixelated. I have no experience with the Metroidvania genre and was baffled and annoyed, as was my child, who says, "It's stupid, all you do is walk around." So I leave this review as a warning: if you are similarly Metroidblivious, you may not have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Probably in my top 3 of Metroidvania games i like. The "main quest" part of this game reminds me a lot of Super Metroid (which is my n1), although the gameplay itself is completely different. There's still a lot of experimenting with the tools you get, but the combat is basically completely removed (which for this game I like a lot). But the game really shines in the post-game where during my playthrough I started to focus on collecting everything and solving all the puzzles, which was by far my favorite part of the game. It reminded me a lot of playing FEZ. At this point of the year probably my favorite release of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

But this itch was deep down somewhere in my brain where my childhood wonder sleeps. What a beautiful production! What a lovely experience! What a wonderful time to be alive!

Like finding something written on the wall that makes no sense, wandering around doing puzzles and unlocking gadget, hours later finding something on the wall which seems like a decoder of the previous one. Makes you feel big brained!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: 30 something megabytes of cryptic techno sorcery. I get what I expected in my playtime. Very well thought of puzzles and challenges, pleasant movement and mechanics, mystical and beautiful ambiance. While playing, you start to wonder how deep the rabbit hole is. Protip: and deep that is. While I dont care for it that much. Its being there makes it whole better. Some crazy bastards will always go for it and thats fun even for players like us.I have almost forgot the fact about the dev. Yeah, not plural. _childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A bit short, but great otherwise. I have everything in the game that has been discovered thus far (except the time-based things). Very creative and engaging puzzles with only the most secretive things being arguably too obscure (required looking stuff up online), but those aren't part of the main story and are more or less for completionists or people up for a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only metroidvania I've played more than 20 minutes in. I love how the gadgets you collect along the journey are always unexpected and silly; which is great when juxtaposed with the profoundly artful puzzle/level design and how you can often solve puzzles numerous ways, depending on what you have--and what you're good at using.This game is a stunning thing. It's both a return to childlike wonder, and a departure up a mountain of challenge. It will defeat you, but if you persistently return, you will eventually summit.Animal Well is an immensely satisfying, beautiful journey.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is fantastically creative as a Metroidvainia - there's a multitude of unlocks to help you traverse the map in new ways, however not one of them is a dash, double jump, or anything so mundane. You'll be getting new traversal methods all the way through completing the main "story", and the surprise of what new oddball trinket you'll get and puzzling out all the ways to use it is great.The post-game is extensive - and by and large great, though not without flaws. Without treading into ARG territory, there are 64 secret eggs to chase after. Most of these are fine, and I had a lot of fun chasing after them. There's a great puzzle difficulty curve - some of the endgame egg unlocks are combining all of your tools together in pretty satisfying ways.... but. The number of times you'll have to retread the map gets excessive. Really, excessive. Later unlocks become increasingly niche - you go from getting upgrades that can be used in nearly every single room to getting something whose sole purpose is unlocking 3 eggs tucked away in far corners of the map. So you'll end up retreading the entire map 4-5 times in the late game as you're drip-fed these last few upgrades, just spamming your new toy in hopes of finding one of the last few needles in the haystack.Definitely play, but maybe don't be shy to look at a map as you're creeping up to 15, 20 hours. There's an excellent spoiler-free map in the community guides.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I got to 60 eggs and 5 bunnies(found 6) before I had to look anything up.The most spoiler free look ups I could find to still solve ♥♥♥♥ on my own, ya know, look around in this room idiot.- Shoutout 'A Travelers Guide to Animal Well' in the Guides section.But the solutions just became more and more... I'm gonna say 'arbitrary' but I don't think that the word... That I eventually just decided this game wasn't for me to 100% I'll just read along and watch the videos.10\10 enough puzzle solving for ANYONE.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a chill metroidvania with a greater focus on puzzles. A highly atmospheric game with a nice visual style and rainy day vibe, I'd recommend Animal Well to anyone who wants to spend some time doing some deep exploration.I do have to mention however that there were a few moments thoughout the game where I felt that the difficulty spiked or the pacing of the game shifted somewhat dramatically.While this shift in the game isn't an overall bad thing, it was not what I was expecting and probably didn't fit the vibe of what the rest of the game had set as the tone.Regardless, Animal Well is an excellent title and an amazing feat of game design, having come from a solo dev.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a really cool game with lots of interesting mechanics. There are many levels to explore and different puzzles to solve, from easy ones to hard ones. The boss fights are quite easy, and it would be nice if they were more challenging.The game looks great with its pixel art style, and the items you find have cool mechanics that make the game more fun. However, the price is a bit too high. It's definitely a game you should buy when it's on sale.Overall, Animal Well is a good and fun game, and it's worth the time spent playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A must play! It's one of my favourite games of the last few years, and an experience I won't forget anytime soon.Platform/puzzler/metroidvania without combat, incredibly smart design, and lets you figure out the cool stuff on your own. It hits some of the same notes as Outer Wilds, with lots of discovery and "woah, really?" moments. Beautiful graphics too.Anyone can probably beat the game and hit the credits, which is very satisfying, and for those who love headscratchers you can go much further in depth. On this note, I'll go back to look for more secrets...
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with an amazing atmosphere that will leave you lost in its intricate world. Each room seems to have something in it leaving the game feeling fresh throughout its entirety. Even rooms that seem as if they have nothing will later reveal to have deep secrets if you are dedicated enough. Overall, the game is truly something i think is great and one of a kind. Even without any "Boss fights" the game is still action packed with hidden secrets around every corner.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: a solid exploration game with very intuitive puzzles. I've enjoyed every minute so far and expect to invest even more time in the end-end-game. I really love games like Fez and Tunic and Noita, and was hoping Animal Well would scratch that itch. I started to expect it might, judging by the ARG they ran prior to release. Having played through the majority of the game, I can't say the game has really met those unfair expectations. It is, however, a solid exploration game with very intuitive puzzles. I've very much enjoyed my time with it so far. I haven't really felt any part of the game is unfair, or had any of those "Well how was I supposed to figure THAT out?" moments. The game teaches so well, in fact, that I often felt the puzzles and secrets were rather effortless. When I did miss things, being a very curious little explorer who likes poring over my map's blank spots and revisiting areas I hadn't been in some time was usually enough to find just about everything. A healthy dose of attentive curiosity is most of what you need to solve the game. For reference, I've gotten two endings, 6/10 of a certain collectible, and the lowest hanging trophy. I did most of that without any assistance in the first 24 hours after launch, only spoiling myself on 4 eggs. One I guessed correctly how to get it, but a glitch made it seem like I was wrong; two required a mechanic of an item that is very very niche and I feel were very well hidden; and a final egg that requires movement tech so niche I can't imagine being stubborn enough to try to force my way up that jump to learn that you could even do that. So I've done A LOT of what the game has to offer, I think. And basically completely by myself. In the first 24 hours after launch. I've reached "Layer 3", as Basso calls it. I think. I can't help wondering what I'm missing, however, because the game doesn't feel as uncrackable as I had expected. Maybe these last few loose ends on my todo list will provide that. A certain staircase. A certain very long song. A certain light up display. A certain collection of mysterious statues and symbols. They are all, so far, pretty tough nuts to crack. But I have the feeling, like most of the puzzles I've solved so far, that they are just a matter of a shift in perspective, a sudden "Oh! I get it!" and they are as good as solved.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so you've heard the hype because of all the dunkey fans, but is this game actually good? I was hesitant to check it out because I couldn't tell if people were just bandwagoning to meme or if this was an actual gem. And now that I've played it, do I recommend it?Yes. I highly recommend giving it a go because if you like metroidvanias then you'll find something special here. And I also don't want to spoil anything other than to provide some additional context in your decision. From the moment the game starts you're not given much context about anything that's going on and the only thing guiding you is your desire to explore. There's a surprising amount of depth to the design in the game that rewards inquisitive players to try stuff out and see what happens. Secrets are a huge part of this game, but I think most people who play Metroidvanias know to search every corner of the map. But these secrets go deep, like Tunic or Fez deep. And that's all I'll say.(Also, the art style of this game really is quite gorgeous. There's a few change ups in the environment but it mostly has the feel of one biome that is lovingly crafted and had me in awe.)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Meme reviews, reviews committing to the bit and reviews that are repeating what has already been said aside, if you like metroidvanias then Animal Well is a must play. Billy Basso is an incredible game designer, with each room of Animal well (slight exagguration) a mini puzzle that you may not be able to solve on your first visit, but you should keep in the back of your mind. The first puzzle really shows how clever animals well is with its level/puzzle design and what you should expect going forward. It has a kind of Rain World vibe to it - where you are a small blob in a living world that doesn't really care about your quest and will continue to do things as they have. The tools you have are unique and interact with the world in different ways. Movement is quite fun and once you unlock a few items, Animal Well becomes magical.Animal Well is dripping in expert design and mystery. It is a game best played completely blind.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not super far into Animal Well, but HOLY HECK IS IT GOOD. It's not even tagged as a horror game but it has made me flinch from its immaculate atmosphere alone more than any other game I've ever played. The mechanics are simple yet enjoyable, and learning to use them in creative ways is required to make progress. Be warned however, the game seldom tells you anything. I keep a notepad file open to write down any new discoveries I make!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready to be lost for many many many days trying to figure out what the white rabbit means, and why sometimes you can do certain things and find other rabbits. Or why this big roo keeps hopping around and screaming at me before crushing me with its big feet (hot).I have been obsessing over every last little detail in this game. I found every secret egg, but the game just got bigger and more complicated from there. Once you beat the game, you truly have not "beat" the game. Keep exploring, dig deeper - if you look at something and wonder "does that mean somet-" YES, YES IT DOES. Figure out WHAT it means! You got this! Go in absolutely spoiler-free. Don't even watch the trailers. If you enjoy games with deep complex problem solving that takes you beyond the main game, this is a game for you.Things are not all Well in the Animal Well.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, but it is held back from being a great one by overly punishing checkpoints. I get that this game is one person's vision, and maybe it's just because I'm older now and my patience for repeating certain things is more limited now, but IMO this is a thing of the past. I like hard games but when the check point is like a couple of minutes away from the actual area it makes the game tedious in a way it didn't need to be. I also REALLY think the main character of the game needed more to distinguish it from the background. It's just this small brown blob and I often found myself losing where he was on the screen. Mega Man is Blue, Mario is Red, Kirby is pink for these specific reasons.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: What struck me most about this game is its no thrills attitude. No superfluous mechanics, loading times or tutorials that waste your time. Just a stripped down puzzle metroidvania about exploration and discovering secrets. That sort of respect for the player isn't something you see in games a lot these days so I respect when I do rarely see it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The hype for this game is unwarranted imo. Yes the riddles are good and intiutive. The atmosphere and music are also good, but nothing special.One core mechanic of this game is tediousness. You will encounter it time and time again, many of the respawn points are wildly inconvenient. I enjoy mechanical difficulty and am a patient gamer but this game is so unnecessarily frustrating. Yes I will gladly try a boss or a difficult riddle 50 or 100 times, but I dont want to walk 30-60 seconds just to get there and many of the long riddles could easily be split up with a respawn point. If tediousness was only a small part of the game and the developer didn't purposely lean into this concept, I'd have let this slide and just not reviewed it, but I'm certain the vast majority of players will enjoy this game less because it was designed like this.The bosses have very basic designs, which is fine in a non-fighting game, but the wolf boss sucksss man.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I put up some content on the YouTube, URL =  , but short version: I've been testing Animal Well on and off for nearly two years. I've seen how it's evolved. And I've seen teases of puzzles that may take months for the community to figure out. I strongly urge you to get through the first 8-10 hours spoiler-free, because you'll have plenty of excuses to look online for hints and help once you reach the game's first "ending."PC-specific notes:* DualSense works really well, as far as vibrations and second-speaker compatibility. If you own a DualSense, use it.* Ultrawide support doesn't exist, because the game blacks out rooms that you're not in anyway.* Runs great on Steam Deck with all settings maxed out.* I've seen at least one puzzle that seems to be easier to solve on PC than on other platforms. That's all I can say.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in every single definition of the word. Impossibly clever puzzles hide extremely well kept secrets in the most densely packed metroidvanias ever designed.What Billy Basso has showcased here can only be described as a marvel of modern computer science. Get this game right now.

_childDocuments_.review: The New Indie darling everyone is, or was, talking aboutBut should you buy into the hype?Animal well is an excellent game and well worth your time and investment, but if you're looking for a game that will change your life as many in the community may try to convince you it will, you'll likely come out of this experience feeling disappointed.Animal well is a fairly simple metroid-vania game at face value, and you won't really miss out on much if that's all you engage with.  If nothing else, this game does have a fantastic visual style that should make anyone above the age of 30 extremely happy, but I hope some of the younger generations can also appreciate the love that went into the visuals.Upon "finishing" the game, you'll only have engaged with about half of what you're meant to, and there's a lot of extra content to find and engage with, but if you want a game that offers up rewards for your added effort, you'll likely be disappointed as Animal Well doesn't have a story or lore, and the added items you'll find only allow you to engage with more and more esoteric puzzles.Continue further and you'll find that there's even more to do in this game, but it involves an ARG and working with other people in the community.  At this point, all the puzzles have been solved and there's a pretty good guide that will give you the answers to all the puzzles.  But, in the end, completing everything this game has to offer can only offer you a feeling of satisfaction from having completed the game's content.Again, this is a good game, but the discourse surrounding it may have been drawn to the game with too much hype, so go in with tempered expectations and you'll have a good time.  I also recommend ignoring the bunnies.  I went back to complete them and went away pretty annoyed rather than satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that slowly build up and you get into it more and more. At first I didn't know what the hell is the point of the game and why is it supposed to be interesting, but then you start noticing well crafted puzzles, secrets, hidden mechanics that make you want to go further and further. This game has no explicit tutorials, you just figure things out on your own, but it's done in a such nice way that you pick it up really quickly and feel great  about yourself (just like you are supposed to feel when playing good video games).Main MVPs are level design and movement. The author must have spend a lot of time on planning and building. It also has an amazing atmosphere, music and warm graphics while being less than 50 megabytes in size.This is definitely a great game that I can recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is just sort of my thinking out loud to the computer, a jumbled variety of praises sung with no real direction. Sorry! The short of it is that this game is exceptional, and everyone should play it and get lost in it's world. I've been excited about Animal Well for quite some time. This game has been on my radar for  and years, so the hype was definitely building. Billy Basso (the solo developer behind this game) has created something very special here that I think is worthy of praise and discussion. This is a game that was made for me. Billy called me personally and told me "I made this game for you". Now that's a little lie, but he might as well have.Animal Well is, at it's core, a surreal Metroidvania with a major emphasis on smart puzzles, fun and challenging platforming, and an atmosphere so thick you can cut it with a knife. Everything Animal Well attempts to do it does exceedingly well, but I don't want to go too much in depth into what this game does because I think part of why it's so good is just figuring that out for yourself. Animal Well is built on secrets. There is virtually no guidance other than some instructional button prompts and a squirrel you can follow around for the most ideal starting path forward. That's it. I feel like we've seen a lot of this type of thing since Breath of the Wild in 2017. Elden Ring expanded upon this in 2022, and now Animal Well pushes it further with some seriously brain busting puzzles and codes that the community hasn't even cracked yet as of writing this review. Aside from some friendly animals and beautiful plantlife, you are really on your own out here discovering  path forward, and I truly admire that. Without going into too much detail as not to spoil any items or tools right now, we can compare this style of gameplay directly to something like Metroid or Castlevania: go along your own journey, and when you can't go progress, go find something else to do until you can. Every tool is incredibly varied in it's approach to how you solve puzzles, and no tool feels under utilized. Whatever items you  you'll find in the well, you're probably wrong, and that's really cool!The map is just the right size. It's not overly huge with tons of rooms where nothing happens, but it's chalk full of secrets, little extra rooms, detail and so much to take in. Every single room is different and weird. Each "biome" or section(?) has a distinct flavor without being fragmented. I'm hesitant to even label things as sections because they all flow into each other so seamlessly. Nothing feels tacked on or "well we have to have a water level" or anything like that. You live in the well, it's your home now.The visuals and the atmosphere are next level. This is the some of the best atmosphere since Super Metroid. And it's , it's , and I wouldn't have it any other way. You can get absolutely lost in the visuals here, but it's not overwhelming or visual noise. There's just a lot of prettiness to take in if you really look for it. The limited soundscape accompanied by some truly wonderful little melodies puts you right in the mix with the plants, the birds, bunnies, and the the terrifying giant kangaroos. You'll hear the cuckoo clock mark the hours you play into the night, but another hour couldn't hurt.  Technically speaking, nothing is out of place, and I personally haven't experienced any bugs or softlocks or any issues. For a game made alongside the engine it runs on, that's incredibly impressive. This game is jam packed with stuff, but it's so quick and snappy and beautifully optimized. I know bugs  (they have to, they always do) but I haven't encountered any, and it seems like for the most part this is shared amongst the community.  I appreciate the "layers" this game has, allowing anyone with any puzzle solving abilities to play it and enjoy it. But true puzzle-heads and egg hunters can sink their teeth into hours of codes to crack. During my playthrough, I dabbled in the third layer (which includes ) before moving on. That was the perfect amount of puzzling for me, but I appreciate the fact that there is just so so much more.  The only real criticisms I can even give this game are that the endings felt a little abrupt to me, where my brain was expecting a little more breathing room before the credits rolled. But that's seriously a non-issue, and it's really just my personal taste in pacing. Other than that...I mean I guess it would be nice to be able to zoom into the map a little more? Just ignore me, it's a non criticism. This entire game has been made with an overwhelming amount of care and love. So much thought has glazed over every surface here, I can see why it took so long to make. I picked up the physical edition and can't wait to display this game alongside some of my other favorites on the shelf. Literally everyone should play this game, what are you doing? Stop the review!! Go play Animal Well! And to whatever Billy Basso does next whoo boy I'm along for the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically one of the best 2D puzzle games but this negative review is for the lack of checkpoints.You could potentially have to traverse half the map AGAIN if you die.I get it developers want there to be consequences of dying in order to give players a sense of challenge, but don't punish the players who failed with nothing but chores? It's just walking back to where you were, it's not fun.There is a fast travel mechanic but it's not very accessible half the time it requires you traverse a huge amount of terrain to access the fast travel hub.

_childDocuments_.review: Completely unbiased review here. As much as I love Dunkey, I came into this game with skepticism. After I played the entire playthrough in one sitting (14 hours - don't judge me), I can say this game truly is like Halo 2 meets Halo 3. This game absolutely creams my jorts. This game's puzzles are intricate and make you think, the sound design is perfect for the atmospheres Billy Basso was trying to convey. The way you unlock new tools as you go makes exploration worth every second you spend failing skilljumps or having to redo puzzles to get to new places that you didn't even see before. The map is huge, the zones are creative, the enemies are interesting and have movesets that make you think outside the box. I love this game, and can confidently give it a 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic blend of metroidvania, puzzles, and jump-scares. And when I say jump-scares I mean it very literally--unlike a horror game where it might be disturbing or prolonged these jump scares are short, sweet and surprising in a funny way. The retro style feels like the crunchy pixels of Dead Cells put to good use. The music and animals make it feel alive, and the atmosphere is quite chill for the majority of the game.I'd say the biggest allure of this are the secrets. Secret passages, walls, messages, codes, and so on keep you exploring and interested. A must for any retro-enthusiast or any metroidvania fan looking for a refreshing non-combat alternative!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Cryptic Puzzles with out of the box solutions plus lots of endgame contentIf you like La-Mulana, Fez, Tunic, Outer Wilds, Noita, Braid endgame content you will probably like this.Most people won't be able to 100% the content because the end game puzzles are very hard and obscure with what they want, be satisfied with finishing the main game and getting 85% of the second layer collectibles. Specially because the last few will probably have a mechanic that wasn't explained at all and will be hard for you to discover on trial and error.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for games which give the player the freedom to bypass the normal routes provided they're skilled enough, and Animal Well does this much better than the large majority of games I've played.[Light gameplay spoilers ahead]Just about every item in the game has additional uses that might not be obvious at first, or other ways to implement them which go beyond their basic functionality, whether it be chaining bubble jumps, throwing a frisbee at the peak of your jump so you can land on it right as it appears, or even using the notes from the flute as a source of light. Perhaps what the game does best is getting the player to doubt whether or not they're breaking the game in the first place.There was one instance where I chained together bubble jumps to reach a seemingly empty corner of a room, only to then come across a series of pillars covered in spikes which required the full use of mechanics which just a few minutes earlier seemed like a potential oversight. The game demonstrates the clear ability to limit the players options through obstacles that prevent the use of certain items, but instead lets the player experiment with what they have at their disposal, reserving the more elusive secrets for players who utilize the mechanics to the fullest.I normally don't leave reviews with so little time in a game, but the way Animal Well pushes the player to explore through the map in their own unique way is such a nice change of pace from other games I've played which actively try to fight against the player's attempts to make the most of their toolkit.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Metroidvania with a bit of mystery in its setting and well-signposted emergent mechanics. I personally think the media cycle on this one oversold the postgame easter eggs a bit, but it's a highly competent game in a genre that developers often struggle to get right. The focus on puzzle-solving and light platforming over combat is a welcome change of pace.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made, a part of the newly explore "metroid-brainias" along with another favourite of mine: Outer Wilds. There is emphasis on finding items to further your progression sure, but there's also layer upon layer of knowledge you uncover to help you with things that have been staring you in the face the whole time. _childDocuments_.review: I can see why this game would appeal to certain players but I really can't get into it. The traversal is a bit too punishing for me; dying can set you back 5-10 screens and forces you to redo large sections of platforming. _childDocuments_.review: The visuals are absolutely stunning, the game play mechanics are insanely creative, the level design is totally inspired - I could go on and on. This is a game that rewards the player for thinking outside of the box, rather than discouraging them; the map is designed for exploration, and every new area or item found feels like the game giving you a pat on the back for taking the time to look around. The mechanics manage to strike a balance between skillful and forgiving - getting to a hard-to-reach cliff isn't rage-inducing but manages to feel very rewarding anyway. An incredible amount of thought and love was put into this game, and it absolutely shows.

_childDocuments_.review: An exquisite, enveloping game, made with obvious love. Part of its great charm is that it does not really break new ground; it collects old and familiar ideas, but with so much care and polish that they come truly to life. The experience feels fresh simply because of its quality. Meticulous personal attention has been lavished on every pixel on screen and every kilobyte in memory. It's palpable. I think that, as much as anything else, is why this game has inspired such enthusiasm. We want games to come to us already knowing how to be adored. Animal Well knows.Its pixels are REAL, not just a superficial retro affectation. There are exactly 320 of them in every row, always. It looks beautiful.You've probably heard that the game is full of "secrets" and "puzzles" and that some of them are wildly obscure. For now, that stuff needn't concern you. I promise. There is an utterly satisfying, fun, fair ~10 hour game here. After that, if you have the urge to go further (and you will), there are several more hours of only slightly more obsessive things to do, which lead to a splendid second ending. It's well worth it.After that... well, things do break down a bit. There are still interesting things to be done, and some delightful puzzles to be solved, but at this point the designer's fondness for "ARG" type puzzles led him astray, in my opinion. Several of the challenges at this stage (and beyond) are deliberately obtuse, to try to enforce community solving — i.e. designed against solo players rather than for them. But of course true community solving can only happen once, and it's already in the past. Eventually you will find that reading spoilers on a wiki makes more sense than continuing to "play," at which point the game will effectively end with a whimper. How you feel about that will depend on your personality; I found it a rather sour anticlimax. But that didn't happen until after I'd been playing a truly superb game for nearly 20 hours. I'll take it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings because this game is a decent puzzle metroidvania, and if that's all I was expecting going in I wouldn't be disappointed at all, but it's marketed as a super deep meta-game puzzler like Tunic or Fez and I don't think it lives up to that at all. Before the first credits you have a classic puzzle metroidvania where you unlock new abilities that let you do more puzzles etc etc, and the puzzles are pretty fun. Nothing crazy, and I wasn't as mind blown by the abilities as some of the other reviewers, but a perfectly good puzzle game. After the credits I was expecting a whole new meta game to open up like the holy cross and manual in tunic, but there's nothing like that at all. There's a tedious pixel hunt collectible hunt with potentially hours of painful backtracking that unlocks what is basically an ARG. No deeper narrative, no deeper gameplay, just more of the same but all you do is scour the map for collectibles and unlock maybe a few more niche abilities if you rushed through the main game. If you go in knowing that's the case you'll still enjoy the bulk of the experience, but just be aware that any comparisons to Tunic or Fez or Outer Wilds are completely off base

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing GameBilly Basso knocked it out of the park with this one and I can honestly see it joining the greats alongside indie classic, I haven't had this much fun playing a game in a while and it was well worth picking up recently, This game is beautiful and so atmospheric, the art style and humbling ambient sounds really make you feel alone when out exploring in these alien environments, the music is great too but it is used sparingly which heightens moments when it is used, who knew a Sausages Dog would be that terrifying? or finding a telephone and hearing the music come in gives a sense of relief and calm, it reminds me of the serene warm vibe of Firelink Shrine in Dark Souls 1, in a way Animal Well reminds me a lot of the Dark souls series in terms of atmosphere which is a huge plus in my book minus the the difficult enemies trying to kill you, that isn't to say Animal Well doesn't have enemies in it but the difficulty comes in the challenging puzzles littered throughout the world, I love that it doesn't hold your hand as the game just sets you loose to explore, it's the classic Metroidvania game play with tight creative controls, nothing ruins a game for me then terrible floaty controls and the tight platforming of Animal Well feels great to control and deliberate especially with the multiple ways to use items, this game has so many collectables and secrets to find that it's honestly overwhelming, and what's crazy to me is that it's not even a 100 MB in size given the size and content in the game.Don't skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning visuals, no hand holding, variety of challenging but hardly brain numbing puzzles and the emphasis on allowing the player to be creative rank "Animal Well" as the best game I've ever played.The best way to experience this game would be to just jump in with a PS5 controller without watching any gameplay or review footage.

The items are very unique and leads to a lot of fun experimenting and eureka moments with what they allow you to do, all set in a world that is extremely stylish and beautiful and absolutely riddled with fun secrets. Strangely enough, given the cute graphics, the game has made me jump from time to time when predators do something unexpected (*cough* *cough*)I highly recommend it if you enjoy puzzle platforming, but if you're looking for a new Symphony of the Night, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say right now that starting this game I was unaware it was published under videogamedunkey's studio. Despite that, I am a casual fan of his, and I think it's amazing that he can use his platform to boost games like this that may otherwise be cast aside!!Now, onto the actual review -Less than an hour into this game and I am already inspired to write a review, get my thoughts down on a screen. Metroidvania is a very beloved genre of mine. With the release and success of Hollow Knight, it's no surprise that the genre has been thoroughly revived among the indie scene. From what I've seen; it is a very accessible genre for new, indepdent developers to tackle and put a ton of quality into.Metroidvanias are however, very formulaic. Even Hollow Knight is! This is not an indignation whatsoever, in fact Hollow Knight and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night are some of my favorite games of all time. I love metroidvanias so much BECAUSE of their formulaic, curated experience. Nonetheless, it's true that at times it can feel like once you've played one - every title after it you play can feel repetitive in some way.I think this game, however, takes the formulaic element of metroidvanias - and blends it with other elements to craft something I haven't quite seen to this extent yet within metroidvanias. Maybe I just haven't played enough, but I can tell this game is going to evolve into something very unique.One of the biggest elements of metroidvanias are combat. When I first started this game, I was expecting exactly that - lots of fun combat, that's why people must be raving about this!! And, there is indeed combat, but very interestingly it is not treated so much like combat. Enemies exist as well, some of which can even be killed, but they don't feel like random challenges just plopped down to break up the game either.What I am getting at is; every single element of this game has a precise purpose. An exact reason for existing. Because the way this game predominantly progresses is actually through puzzles. Which means the combat and enemies themselves are designed with being a part of these puzzles in mind.So still, Animal Well is a very formulaic experience - but it uses its formula in an unconventional way in terms of metroidvanias. Still, like metroidvanias, the focus is to gain power-ups so that you can traverse throughout all the nooks and crannies of the map. But the entire map itself, nearly every room, nearly every enemy, is a cryptic puzzle waiting to be navigated by the player. I see many people in the reviews jokingly claiming that this could be a new subgenre. Perhaps that is from the video, but it is absolutely true.This review as it exists now is very preliminary. I imagine once I beat the game, and actually watch the video, I will come back to this and write a more thorough review. I haven't even discussed the setting, the plot, all the other elements that synthesized together make this game incredible! But so far I am utterly fascinated by what this game is pulling off, and I absolutely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a very, very good time with this game. An excellent puzzle platformer that lets you look for as much depth in puzzle mechanics and hints as you're willing to look. The gameplay feels great, and all the critical path puzzles are just as difficult as they need to be. The presentation of the graphics and art is also just soooo good. It REALLY feels like you're in a deep abandoned well. I  recommend keeping the CRT filter on as well, it adds a lot.If you like Tunic, Fez, or La-Mulana, this should be directly up your alley. If you like discovering secrets, finding new ways to use your tools, and solving puzzles at all, you should get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone.I am in love with animal well, just today it made me lose track of time and for me, that is quite rare to find these days.I mainly bought the game because I want to support Bigmode as a company, but it just happened to be a game in one of my favourite genres, so I have bit to say.I am no where near completing this but the map is HUGE, it feels like it never ends and at the moment it's honestly feeling kind of overwhelming. Most areas you go to you can't "complete" until you progress further in the game, but because the game is so big it gets hard to remember where you've been and where you haven't. Combine that with the fact that the teleport system is very limited and that checkpoints can be quite harsh, and backtracking through the maze-like map can feel daunting.I do recomment the game to lovers of the genre, but I do not think it's a good first game for people getting introduced to it. My one recomendation is that you USE MAP MARKERS!!! I only found out about them 5 hours into the game and it feels like I could have a tighter grasp on it if I started using them sooner. Also, as soon as you get the pencil, write down why you couldnt' advance in an area, so you know exactly what you unlock when you get new items.I will update this review when I'm finished with the game with my thoughts then.

_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare I play games that provide you impossibly and incredibly useful tools, whilst simultaneously ramping up the environmental puzzles so excellently that you near constantly have to think on your toes. Only about halfway through I believe? An excellent excellent game though, enthralling atmosphere, intoxicating visuals, and an environment that takes on a life of it's own around you.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a metroidvania guy, or at least I wasn't before playing this. I tried Hollow Knight, I tried Ori, and although I loved the visuals and thought the stories and games were interesting, I just couldn't help myself from being bored. I love exploring and going off of the beaten path, but I always felt like when I did that in other games I wasn't doing the right thing and always had to go back to the "right" path. For the first half hour of ANIMAL WELL, I felt the same way. But after a little bit, I realized that there is no right path. There isn't a correct way to go, and going off the beaten path just felt so good. When I treated the game like a puzzle game, just going into a room, doing everything I can, and then doing more, trying to fill up the map, it felt so good. It was pure fun. And of course, the visuals and music are beautiful, the animals are so fun to interact with and watch, and the blob feels good to control. There's tons of secrets, and I enjoyed doing as much as I could (about 3/4 of the eggs!) before looking up the rest. You know the game is good when you even have fun completing the stuff you're looking up. The recording at the end really touched me and I'm so glad you made this game, Billy, and really glad you chose this game to publish, Jason. This game will definitely stick with me and maybe even changed my view on metroidvanias as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Back when video rental stores were still a thing, I would frequently rent NES games over a weekend. These games would rarely come with an instruction manual and, in those days, they were often the only way to know how to actually play the game. I know that seems kind of obvious but consider that most games nowadays start with, like, a two hour tutorial mission. So, firing up an old 8-bit game and figuring out how it works as you play was a common situation back in the day.This is the same kind of experience you get while playing Animal Well. Players are thrown into a pixelated world and expected to basically figure it out on their own. And it's awesome.Animal Well is frustrating, but in all the best ways. It's surprisingly - even shockingly - deep. There are puzzles in here that will, once you solve them, make you feel like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius.Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is more of a puzzle and exploration-oriented metroidvania than the sort of Action RPG or Roguelite types that are more popular now, and it's quite welcome. It reminds me of some classics like Lyle in Cube Sector, VVVVVV, or Environmental Station Alpha. This one is a relatively short game that is not too difficult. Although, it has a fair bit of precision platforming, and even has some deeper tech to master if you're the type. There aren't too many upgrades or movement options, and instead the map is filled with blocked passageways and gates that must be opened by solving switch puzzles. But the overall layout and interconnectedness of the map is executed beautifully, and the puzzles are just challenging enough without ever becoming hopelessly frustrating. And in general, the level design and aesthetic stand out above all else. I'm still working out the end game, where there seems to be a good bit of optional content and easter eggs as well. This is definitely a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Having heard nothing about the game prior to purchasing it, it turned out to be a surprisingly well made metroidvania, with a unique approach to both the setting and mechanics of the game. A lot of really satisfying puzzles & platforming challenges, and as long as you stop after getting all the achievements, doesn't overstay its welcome.Seriously though, after you have the achievements, just watch the rest on youtube - even the dev didn't expect anybody to bother solving the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: My choice for GOTY. Calm puzzling, clever secrets, a hypnotic and droning soundtrack, and a retro art style that  Animal Well pays homage to. It might not be for everyone, but it certainly will be fun for most players. The way that you trip across interactions and find out new techs for older items creates an extremely satisfying gameplay loop of explore, discover, adapt.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A seemingly simple game with a lot of complexity hidden bellow the surface. The basic thechnics are simple. You can jump a short distance. When you get a few items, they each have a simple obvious use that helps you solve puzzles and access traverse more easily.But, each item has several more usages that require experimenting in order to discover, by interacting with various animals, with differemt components of environment, with other items, and with yourself.Aside from the main route which has symbols on the map, there are many, many more side paths and secrets that greatly reward exploration and carful attention to details on the map and on the screen. These paths hide collectibels, some just for swag but some with real uses. I never get tired of trying a challenging platforming section or examining the nooks and cranies of the map to get them.On top of that, the art and sound make a surreal and mysterious atmosphere I really enjoy spending time in and uncover it's secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest metroidvania fan, I normally get burned out playing them, but this maintained my attention the whole way through, can't believe I'm giving a game published by a YouTuber a 9/10 rating! the last section is really damn intense! I'm not going to give any spoilers since I believe it's best if people walk in blind! The puzzles are largely straightforward if you stand still and think about them, but they can have some severe difficulty spikes in certain portions. The only negative aspects I can think of are that the ladder can be awkward to climb at times, and the spikes are difficult to see when doing platform jumping with the bubble! The jumping felt fluid and smooth and the world's colours and animal designs were fantastic. the game rewards discoverability with cool items to progress the map, The boss battles were enjoyable and some were even creepy! This is my favourite game of the year so far, which I was not expecting to say when I started playing it. It makes me want to play other greats of the genre, which is the highest compliment I can give it.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little metroidvania that involves a bit of skilled platforming, exploration, and puzzle solving.  I enjoyed my roughly 8 hours to finish the main story portion.
