_childDocuments_.review: If you're a One Piece fan, get this game. If you're not, well, I suggest watching the show up to a certain point because you're not going to know what is going on, at all. It's NOT for newcomers/gamers.I love Japanese RPGs, and this has the system covered. While it does cover a few stories of One Piece with an original mixed in, it gives it a overall nice twists (I had to come back to edit this that the last half feels kind of rushed? The combat system works (with turn base), but if you're looking for a hardcore challenge or something radical/energetic (especially puzzles, though fun), this is not it (Lots of people b-tching about this in particular...).Honestly, the graphics and writing is simply AMAZING, I cannot stress it. I do not know how many times I had a stupid smile on my face and laughing because the characters are themselves (no hate on the English dub, but these Japanese voice actors are on another level, and I love the cast) and the One Piece humor is there.Easily the best One Piece game that I have ever played. I always hoped for something like this, and the developers were ambitious enough to make this for us and I am super happy to be able to play. When One Piece eventually ends, I'd hope they make another that is just as good, HUGE,  if not better than this for any and all One Piece fans can have to cherish even more. I think the Kingdom Hearts route would be key for this, if they should try with "world" explorations. They definitely had the right idea with this one with visiting the few sagas.I am still playing it, collecting everything because I am a collection freak, but definitely going to put more time into this.Enjoy yourself!!!! I certainly am!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge One Piece fan, started watching back in 2012 and am current in the Anime. So, may be a bit of a bias here!I'm not far into the game, but the intro/tutorial seems to be 1-2 hours long. The game starts off as the Sunny(Strawhat's(the main pirate crew that Luffy(the main character) is the leader of) ship) becomes shipwrecked on a "mysterious island"(that is not part of the show whatsoever) and the crew is separated and then quickly finds each other, but then loses their powers(explained, don't want to give much away). The crew and game seems to be at the same point in the show as the Whole Cake Island Arc or just before it, in case anyone is curious about powers available.The game performs well, however so far I have noticed there is no mouse sensitivity slider and the sensitivity is somehow tied to the framerate of the game? Also there is no FOV slider and you have to use a 3rd party tool(Universal Unreal Engine 4 Unlocker) to give yourself access to the console(~) menu, and then do "fov XXX" to adjust the FOV, but that does change how cutscenes are shown(they will be zoomed out or in depending on your FOV adjustment). Not a huge deal, but does suck when you change FOV due to motion sickness/headaches.I still need to play more, but first impressions are very positive on my side. I believe the overall story is solid so far and fits the theme of the show and the characters are all voiced correctly, are accurate to the show in their mannerisms, and the gameplay is solid as a turn-based RPG. I was able to get this for $20 USD, which I think is a solid price for this game, so far I wouldn't recommend this game if it is over $30 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline of One Piece Odyssey revolves mainly around revisiting past memories, which is an interesting concept, but it is executed somewhat lacklusterly in terms of content. Players are thrown into the climax of the story arc, with previous events quickly summarized in cutscenes. The introduction of two new characters feels too brief. Overall, it's satisfactory for One Piece fans to play through once.The game features a turn-based battle system within confined zones, where your crew is separated at the start of combat, adding dynamism to battles. However, this novelty wears off after a few hours when your characters become overwhelmingly powerful, rendering battles too easy. The addition of an auto-battle feature feels unnecessary, and the lack of difficulty settings diminishes the challenge, making item usage during fights pointless.Exploration suffers from sluggish camera and movement speeds, discouraging thorough exploration. The world lacks enticing loot, with equipment limited to stat-boosting stones easily acquired through battle rewards or shops.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PIECE ODYSSEY

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface by saying that I TRULY wanted to enjoy this game. I am a HUGE One Piece fan, and was extremely excited when I heard about this game being made. However, I was only able to slug through the first 2-3 hours before deciding to shelf the game for good. PROS---------- The graphics are easily the best looking you can get without going into realism, and the uncanny valley. I genuinely think that all One Piece games going forward should look like this, as every character and location was beautifully done in such a respectful way to the source material.- The story and dialogue are great, and I think this game truly shines in this department, however as I will cover in the Cons, this game is an experience best suited for a Youtube video with all the combat parts removed.CONS-------- The combat is a MAJOR part of the game and it is easily the biggest flaw. The combat is extremely boring, and the "Rock, Paper, Scissors" aspect of combat is extremely unengaging. I never felt like I couldn't use a "Paper" attack or ability on a "Scissors" enemy. There is no feeling of danger or urgency in any of the fights, and I never once sensed any outcome that resulted in me failing any combat encounter. - The beautiful locations you are able to "explore" are amazing, and I truly did enjoy exploring them. However, this game is horribly plagued with forced backtracking that is completely alienated from the story, and serves nothing but to halt progression for the means of inflating playtime. Having to run for 5-10 minutes just to pick up one item, and then another 5-10 minutes to return is insanely boring, and ruins the pacing and enjoyment for me. This repetitive backtracking is what ultimately made me quit the game. OVERALL:------------Overall, I would not reccomend this game unless you could get it for under $10-$15 dollars, and even then that might be too much. I appreciate the effort from Oda, and the developers. However, the combat and horrible progression and pacing make this game unbearable to slog through. Even the most dedicated One Piece fans like myself might have trouble finding enjoyment beyond the surface level when it comes to One Piece: Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I'm a HUUUGE One Piece Fan. I watch every new Episode each Sunday, I already have played some other One Piece games and I just love it.BUT: This game seen as a game is just not good in my opinion. I pre-ordered it in like October or November 2022 and was hyped as hell. I barely spoiled myself with any kind of footage or something. I just wanted the whole new experience. I read something like "open world", "round based" and which parts of the OP story you participate in.I don't say, the story, animiations or whatsoever are bad, but the gameplay and the gameplay-mechanics: The combats are suuuper easy - like the enemies deal 50 damage while having like 2.000 HP - except for when there is one special event fight with one buffed standard enemy (one of those 50 damage dealers), who suddenly deals like 1.600 damage! Like... what the f*** is this?! Only these two extremes do exist and it's just way too unconsistent. Apropos special event fights: When normal fights give like 1.000-2.000 Exp, some special events additionally give like 12.000 Exp! Meanwhile some (Mini-)Bosses also give like 10.000 Exp at maximum. Also you can just freely swap characters in combat (except in special event fights sometimes), so you can position them best possible always. Even the characters, who already are in combat. Like what is all that combat-zone system about, when you can just swap them like your underwear?!Another annoying thing for me is the "exploring" of the "open world". Yeah, there are some sideways with loot and sometimes even chests in there, but... all of that is just ♥♥♥♥! Some stupid cooking material or I don't know. Often the chests contain worse stuff then the loot just chilling and blinking on the floor. It just doesn't feel good finding and opening chests. It's just "ah, another soup" or "ah, some other ingredients for some healing/buffing stuff" always.Then there are the skills, attacks and stuff: Yeah, they look pretty cool and nice and there is a lot of them, but... just why? I don't know, why all of zoros (single target-melee-)attacks do the same stuff, except for the damage numbers. I mean yeah of course they have different costs to activate, but... sometimes they're just too similar, even in numbers. Also why do some characters have like 15 attacks, when others have like 5? And the upgrade-cubes: Some characters (preferably those with more attacks) can upgrade more than the others. And the finding-rate of these cubes seems totally random and disproportionate. I believe, I got like 3 of zoros Skills upgraded before the first of Nami or Robin. Just why? Btw: This upgrade system just sucks in my opinion. Finding stuff to upgrade a limited amount of attacks just in numbers. To be fair: The thing with the stat-equpiment-items is kinda cool.**Spoiler-Alert**: The enemies are just super boring and repetetive. In the first real chapter (Alabasta) I hoped to fight against the Baroque-Agents (Mr. 1, Mr. 2...) and their companions, but the only fight like this was with Mr. 2... It was just so disappointing.I played some other One Piece games like Unlimited Adventure and Unlimited Cruise 1 + 2 (all on Wii) and I loved them. They were sooo great. You were able to individually train, buff and level your characters - instead of having no choice which to have in your party and level automatically. The combats were not round-based (not a bad thing per se) and action-loaded. You were rewarded doing combos in combat so you were not spamming the best attack or something like this. You were rewarded exploring and collecting stuff. My thoughts drifted away to those games while playing One Piece Odyssey and I wondered, why I play this and not these games. I really love One Piece, but this game is just so f****** boring. I'm really sorry to say that and I'm also really sorry paying 80,- € for this game (Pre-Order-Stuff).**Spoiler-Alert**: I'm currently at Enies Lobby in the Prison-Area while texting this and I think, I won't continue playing, because this game is just not worth my time... :(

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice and runs well on PC, if you're a fan of One Piece you will most likely enjoy it (as long as you don't mind JRPGs and turn-based combat).Having just finished the first chapter, these are the complaints I have:Vsync doesn't seem to work, even though it's enabled I still see screen tearing from time to timeThe main cutscenes are prerendered and capped at 30 fps. This also means that if you change the outfits of the characters this won't be reflected in the cutscenesFor now, the game is extremely easy, to the point where I have been one-shotting enemies consistently (the upside of this is that all characters - even those not fighting - get the EXP and levelling seems relatively fast; I don't expect much grinding will be needed to complete the game, if any)Traversal is a bit too slow for my liking, but there does seem to be some fast travel mechanism which I have not unlocked yetOverall, I would recommend this to OP fans and JRPG fans alike, although I'd warn you that the game will spoil plenty of One Piece lore (Given the bounties that can be seen in the save screen, the game seems to be set between Whole Cake Island and Wano, so around episode ~900 of the anime and also chapter ~900 of the manga). If you're not interested in either this is most likely a game you can skip, as it doesn't seem to have any groundbreaking gameplay or storytelling (for now).

_childDocuments_.review: Its a one piece turn based fighting game. If you like one piece and/or turn based fighting games, this game is for you. I only really have two issues with the game, first is the way you get exp. Of course, you get it by killing enemies, but every encounter there is a (seemingly) completely random chance that you get a special challenge. Stuff like "Kill the buffed enemy before a crewmate gets knocked out". Completing these challenges gives you extra exp, like a LOT of extra exp. Multiples of what you would normally get. The issue is that leveling up is really really slow without these challenges, so if you're unlucky it can be difficult to get levels. My other issue is that the game is a bit too easy. I can one shot most basic enemies when I have the type advantage, and sometimes even when I don't. I am still in the early game so maybe that's why. (ignore my playtime, i left the game running overnight a couple times on accident.) Aside from those issues though, the game is pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game fails in two main categories, storyline and combat. Copy & Paste destroyed what could have been a great game.The problem with the storyline: it is boring and highly repetitive. Kill one elemental, travel one memory world, do that 3x, some final encounters, The End. Everything is predictable after the first 5 hours. Character development is non-existent; every character starts in the usual "happy leader", "grumpy", "slutty", "lone samurai", etc. clichés and does not move an inch until the credits roll.The problem with combat is that it offends the intelligence of even an 8-year-old child. As a result, there is hardly any motivation to use anything but the most potent available attack.As of today (game version 1.0.0), there is NO setting for any difficulty level. Therefore, everybody is forced to play on what can only be described as "super-easy / story" mode.Stats-boosting food is available in abundance, and should your resources run out, one of the overpowered meals corrects this problem immediately (for all party members) in one action and then repeat the same until any fight is won. Also, there is an endless recycling of enemies and bosses, with almost no new models in later stages of the game, up to the degree that would make even Square "colour swap" Enix jealous.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a One Piece fan, you will likely enjoy this game quite a bit. It has all of the charm of the One Piece universe wrapped up into a neat little JRPG bow. That said, I have played better JRPGs than this before, but I've also played WAYYYYY worse. This game is more than passable, especially if you're invested in this franchise. The writers have managed to maintain the lovable personalities of the beloved Strawhat crew & friends, and even bring back a lot of old jokes and characters that were surprising and welcome to see. (Kung-Fu Dugongs were a large standout)   The combat is a bit too easy on average, but there are a few boss fights throughout that will require a bit more forethought than many of the minion battles. The moves the crew has access to are a delight to use, however. The animations are crisp and it's always a blast to see Usopp's Rubber Band of Doom and to see Nico Robin squish somebody's nuts. The dual zones allow for a tiny bit of additional strategy that helps to spice up battles just enough to keep them interesting. Overall, you can see the inspiration from some of the more successful JRPGs of our era and that's definitely a good thing in this instance.   The story is actually decently interesting and most of the jokes land pretty well. Of course this is all under the assumption that you're already a fan of One Piece. But if you are, I'd argue that this title is a must-have for you. Especially if it ever goes on sale. Give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked One Piece: Worldseeker, but this game blows it out of the water. _childDocuments_.review: Stunning Visuals, and amazing original/revisited story, paired with a very well thought out turn based fight system makes One Piece Odyssey honestly one of the best ONE PIECE games currently on the market.Initially I was sceptic about the turn based JRPG system the game was planning to use, being used to arena fighters, and games where you mash buttons for combo's, I wasn't interested in a game where you press one button, and have to wait to make a move.However being a One Piece fan I just had to get the game, and I was pleasantly surprised at how much I was enjoying both the story, visuals, but also the game play; which I originally thought would be tedious and dull. I have only just beat Crocodile, so I am not too far into the game, but so far the re-telling of the Alabasta arc was very nostalgic, but also refreshing; as a lot of different things happen compared to the anime and manga adaptations e.g. Luffy rescuing Pell from sacrificing himself, by using his devil fruit powers to deflect the massive bomb in the air.The only matter of contention is 90% of the battles so far have felt easy they require no real strategy, and there’s no way to adjust the difficulty. Hopefully later down the line the difficulty increases.It took a long time, but One Piece now has a video game that stays true to the franchise's reputation. One Piece Odyssey is a proper, meaty, witty, powerful Japanese role-player that will please fans of the manga series as well as lovers of the genre in general. It certainly helps if you're already a devoted fan of the series, but this is enjoyable enough that it deserves anybody's consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do like this game, but the only gripe i have is the combat devolves into a slap fight with a punching bag. If you happen to have a single enemy that is important you would think "Ok he's gonna be relatively stronger than the mooks around him" and he is, but not relatively, i'm talking 20x the health and 3x the damage. So you go from a stomp to a brick wall that you just end up doing the same 2 moves and getting hit by the same 2 moves while you spam heal with chopper when someone gets low for 15 mins. Suffice to say the combat has a really cool idea, but ultimately is tacked on to an otherwise decent one piece episode. Honestly could just cut the price in half and sell the cut scenes as their own movie and you'd have a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sad because I had some hope for this game based on what they showed us, but it feels unfinished in too many areas.First, I want to say that I really like the fact that battles are turn-based, it breaks from the usual "Beat them all" formula of One Piece games and since I like tactical RPGs, I am glad that they took a risk and went into that direction.That said, even the battle system feels incomplete. It's too simple and combats feel too repetitive. The first few are fun, but as you progress in the story, I found them boring. There is not enough challenge, and it would have been good to be able to adjust the difficulty to make combats harder and more interesting.The game has a good foundation, but to me, it needed another year (at least) of development. Even menus seem unfinished. There is no in-game button to close the game??? You have to go back to the main menu and then from there you can exit. I agree, it's a little detail and not the worst thing, but it perfectly embodies the problem: not enough time for development.Honestly, I would rather wait another year or two than to have a rushed product.60 bucks for that when there are indie games out there costing a third of the price with incomparable quality and gameplay? What can I add...I am a big One Piece fan and I have played some of the games, but I was always disappointed by the lack of depth and the shallow gaming experience these games offered. This one is no exception then, but I had hoped otherwise.I am sure that if they had taken their time, they could have addressed all these issues. There is nothing more frustrating for a developer than being forced to release an unfinished product.So, my conclusion is that, if you are hesitant to buy this game, then simply don't buy it.  It's not worth its price, not even half of its price.

_childDocuments_.review: "One Piece Odyssey" is a lackluster entry in the world of One Piece games, failing to capture the essence of the beloved anime and manga series.Let's start with the gameplay. While the game promises an epic adventure through the Grand Line, it fails to deliver on this promise with shallow and repetitive gameplay mechanics. Combat feels sluggish and unresponsive, with limited movesets and uninspired combos that quickly grow stale. Exploration is similarly lackluster, with bland environments and generic side quests that offer little in the way of excitement or challenge.The story mode, which should be a highlight of any anime-based game, is equally disappointing. While it attempts to follow the events of the One Piece storyline, it does so in a disjointed and rushed manner. Important plot points are glossed over or omitted entirely, and character development is virtually nonexistent. As a result, the narrative feels shallow and unsatisfying, leaving fans feeling shortchanged.Graphically, the game is a mixed bag. While the character models are well-rendered and faithful to their anime counterparts, the environments are bland and uninspired, lacking the vibrant energy and personality of the One Piece universe. Animations are stiff and awkward, with characters moving in a way that feels unnatural and janky.Even the online multiplayer, which should be a major draw for fans of the series, is plagued by issues. Matchmaking is slow and unreliable, and laggy matches are all too common, leading to a frustrating and unenjoyable experience.In the end, "One Piece Odyssey" is a disappointing addition to the One Piece video game series that fails to live up to its potential. Its clunky gameplay, lackluster story, and uninspired design make it a hard game to recommend to anyone other than the most die-hard One Piece fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscious recommend this game. Odyssey is a turn based JRPG set in the One Piece universe that will last you anywhere between 40-50 hours but I'm dropping this early. Here are my impressions after beating about half the game:PROS+Great graphics that accurately portray the art from the mange/anime+Story is engaging at times even if it's ultimately an inconsequential filler episode+Battle system is unique and fun for a JRPG+Sweet looking special moves+Fun to revisit past events in the anime with the new crew members to gain a different perspective CONS-Excruciatingly slow character movement speed which is a big problem when you spend most of the game running around from place to place-Too many cutscenes to the point I started to skip them and not care about the story-Unskippable cutscenes when the character portraits talk at the bottom of the screen; whomever implemented this should be banned from making video games-Zero difficulty, I haven't lost a single battle in 23 hours so far-Awful, repetitive music I had to turn off-Too much padding of the game length doing pointless tasks -Overly complicated upgrade/skill system that I didn't bother with and it doesn't matter anyway because this game is a cakewalk -Invisible walls everywhere even though this is supposed to be open world -Dumb design decisions in general; for example if I want to turn the music volume off I have to click my mouse button 100 times to get the level from 100 to 0, there is no slider for whatever reason.I wouldn't even recommend this on sale unless the game is on deep, deep discount. Only the most obsessed One Piece fans are going to enjoy Odyssey, everyone else save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen better camera control in phone 1.st person shooter games,There is no auto or quick save features so if you  don't save everytime you pass a save point,  you  are risking hours of progress. Keep in  mind  that you don't always know when battles happen, boss battles included. (you can flee from most battles, but never boss battles or ones bound to story or any side missions)Has some minor spelling/translation  and zone area names mistakes, but nothing that ruins the  gameplay.Collecting in this game is obviously optional but not rewarding unless you're going for 100%.Terrain is simple to move around in, enemies are mostly easy to avoid but whenever you  slingshot yourself over gaps you have to stand  there for a while until the camera movement unlocks. This  also makes auto-running near impossible in many  areas.Story  is good  and we're  introduced to many likeable characters, but my god there is so much unskippable text that  i stopped even looking at the screen while mashing  the button to speed it up. Almost  all cutscenes are skipable, but you need to hold down the button for almost 2 seconds to do it.Combat speed is fine  with the speed up feature, and the auto-battle is nearly perfect.  I just wish we could choose what abilities, attacks and items to be used. Want to use a combo attack? Switch to manual. Want to  use items? Switch to manual. Want to save ability resources?  Yeah back to manual.The world is well sized and luckily there's fast travel points which  you  can access  nearly any time.There are too many lootable items such as sellables only, cooking ingredients, equipment and battle items. You can sell everything except equipment, which, oh my god, piles up into an unending scroll even if you filter them. Yeah any purple equipment you get is stuck in your bags.Voice actors are on point, scenes and humor is just like any non-recap movies.Maps and areas are well made, but there is not a lot of it. Same with villains and their companions. I wish there were  more Arcs included in the game and with  more than 1 or 2 of their respective villains.Some things feels rushed,  but most things don't. It's like there is something cut out, or not included. There are currently 9 of the main characters in the game's time, but you can only play as 7  of them for some reason. They all have their abilities and move set,  even enemies. From smaller NPC's to boss NPC's,  they each have stats, basic attacks, abilities and good animation. I feel like there could be a game mode where we could control them in battles, or customize crews to fight with.Game is overpriced  for what you get unless you only want the story.Story is great.Combat is good.UI, Camera and QoL is pretty bad.Overall  3,5/5 experience.If you like One Piece, you should  get it. If not, you've been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: A few minutes were enough to make me be rather not happy with this game.Don't get me wrong the graphics look nice and about half of the animations i'm happy with cuz they feel like they put effort into making the characters show more expressions.The downside has just more weight to it.- The other half of the animations is really choppy. Static head movements, awkward flow of animations especially while controlling your character. It just feels like they stopped the development of the movement halfway through.- Next thing is the controlls and camera movement... Now this could only be me but i feel like i get cancer every time i see a game where the camera does not follow the character like at all when you jump. It just keeps on floating over the ground at the same height and your character jumps out of scene. The camera movement itself feels rather bad too like when you look around it has this super high sensitivity but when you turn your mouse faster it gets way slower which is also something i always never got why some games do that. Besides that once you aim down, the camera flows through your body into a first person view which is not really a flaw but it couldve been made better. Feels rather unsettling this way.- The next are just some small but still rather weird things i noticed in just a few minutes of gameplay.First is that the game doesnt have a pause option. _childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 31.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game too many times, or play nearly as long as some of you. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely the single best One Piece game made. If you’re a fan of the franchise, it has everything you’ll want and more. The game isn’t perfect. It can be extremely linear at time, there are plenty of sections that intentionally pad out play time, and the puzzles are insanely easy. With that said though, I’ve never been a fan of JRPG’s in general so this might just be something they all share in common. Now it probably sounds like I’m saying all negatives at this point, but those are my only real complaints with the game. Even then, they aren’t as much complaints as critiques. The combat, while appearing daunting, is actually extremely intuitive and fun. The exploration, while kind of basic is expansive and rewarding. The feel, settings, and story though; these are where the game shines. I’ll try not to go into spoilers, but there is a massive shift about an hour in that takes this game from a really well executed One Piece Adventure, to a nostalgia and fanservice trip. Everything works together well. The characters and their dialogue is fantastic, the story itself is engaging and interesting, and I’m constantly stuck waiting to play more whenever I have to stop. If you like One Piece. Buy it. Thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: If you like One Piece or are OK having no clue what's going on, this is a flawed but decent turn-based RPG. I would recommend you at least be familiar with the manga up to and including the Whole Cake arc. Get it on sale for half-off or lower if you can ($30 is a fair price IMO).While I agree with most of the common criticisms of the game, I would like to add a few caveats that helped me not mind as much."Too easy" - I never got a Game Over during the base game, but that doesn't mean I was never challenged. A few fights came VERY close (specifically Rob Lucci, the Ice Colossus, and the Admirals at Marineford) and I feel like I easily could have failed if I'd made missteps. The ability to switch between characters in battle helps a lot. I also like the sudden challenges that pop up in battles, and the fact that they give you a bonus but don't force you to change your strategy if you can't. Conqueror's Haki will help you blast through most regular enemies when you unlock it, but the bosses do require a little more thought. For what it's worth, the Reunion of Memories DLC offers tougher fights with tighter win conditions should you so desire (I have had PLENTY of Game Overs in that)."Too much dialogue/cutscenes are too repetitive" - There are absolutely lots of  unnecessary cutscenes and some annoying backtracking sections in this game, especially at the end. This game's focus is first and foremost on the experience of playing as the Straw Hats and watching their interactions. You can skip the cutscenes and battle dialogue, and while you can't skip the attack animations, you can fast-foward (press c). I did really like all the attention to detail in the writing. The characters will all say different things in fights depending on who you have on your team, what they do, and what happens. That's neat! Everyone feels like themselves, and Sanji and Brook's pervyness is toned down to make them more likeable, at least to me (the camera angles on Nami and Robin are still quite pervy, though). It should go without saying that getting all the anime voice actors is a big plus. You can't skip the dialogue exchanges when you take bounties but none of those are very long."No open world" - The main story is very linear and takes you back and forth between set paths. I was personally disappointed that we didn't get to visit some of the more colorful locations like Skypeia and Fishman Island. You are eventually able to hop between all the different areas, though, and I think  the amount of sidequests helps make up for the lack of levels. One area in particular is only unlocked after you play through it once in the main story and go back. I especially loved the Bond Quests: these each take a random team of the Straw Hats back in time to fix something in the past, kind of like Quantum Leap. I love it when unusual characters are paired up together (Sanji, Brook, and Chopper go on a mission, for example) and your reward is a unique team attack. More of those would have been cool. The bounties are simple but also pretty fun, since they usually tie into the lore in a humorous way (like a team that's ripping off Germa 66 or a guy who's trying to hunt Tontattas)."The beginning is too tedious" - I will 100% understand if people get bored and dip out around or before Alabasta. All I can say is the fights and different character-stuff helped me get through it. I did love being able to walk around as any of the first eight straw hats and the fact that they all have unique animations for walking, climbing, and breaking open boxes (Sanji kicks stuff, Robin creates a ladder out of hands, etc.). The temples were kind of dull for me but never completely overstayed their welcome. "Game ran poorly" - Obviously YMMV: check the specs before buying.  The animation was very smooth for me and the game only stalled a few times and never crashed on my 4+ years old Lenovo Ideapad. "I didn't care about the story" - Again, I would compare this to a playable One Piece movie. It is technically standalone but draws from lots of the lore and background of the world. While I thought it was weirdly paced (we learn something early on that it takes the straw hats FOREVER to figure out themselves), I did enjoy the new characters Lim and Adio. The "Memoria" levels are not just flashbacks: they offer moments for our heroes to reconsider everything they've done so far, and were often quite poignant. The final cutscene is truly epic and satisfying.There are some frustrating issues with the game but I would still recommend it and the Adventure Expansion Pack overall, as long as you go in with the right expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: I legit started soypointing at the screen when they did the Banana Gator conversation, I will never ever forget the name Banana Gator. I hate it but I chuckled when they started doing it. ♥♥♥♥ Banana Gators.Any way if you're a fan of the series you'll love this gameIf you're a fan of JRPGs keep in mind this one is easy to the point you can auto-battle most of the game with little over-leveling.The exploration is cool, you use different characters' abilities to collect stuff, it tries to capture the essence of the show and so far it's been enjoyable. The OST is solid, the dialogue is funny, the story has been aight so far and I dont mind the lack of english dub but I see why some people would be upset at the fact.I also didnt like that it feels extremely restrictive at first, literally hand holding you so you dont stray off from the main quest's path, I have to admit it was quite frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: So I picked the game up for half price a few weeks ago, and I'm thankful I didn't play full price.  I'm only about four hours into the gameplay, and so far it's fun.   So let's go over the pros and cons of the game.PROS-Feels good to play as the Strawhats-Amazing graphics-Voice actors are all the original anime cast-Highly modableCONS-Combat can be monotonous and way too easy-Exploration is extremely limited-Story is kind of original, but also just rehashing old Stawhat adventuresUltimately yes I would recommend the game, but buy it on sale and mod the hell out of it.  The best mod you'll want to get is  from the Nexus Mods website.  They have a lot more mods that you might like, but that's the one that's going to make the game much more enjoyable.  I'm currently using the Hard Difficulty mod and it's made combat much more challenging and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend this game if you are a fan of One Piece and it is on sale. You'll need to have  read/watched up until the end of the Dressrosa arc. The game's story provides a new island called Waford and then gives you flashbacks of old stories in Alabasta, Water Seven, Marineford, and Dressrosa so you see lots of old faces and story parts (nothing is different or can be changed from how it went in the canon story).On the plus side, it is nearly fully voiced by the original Japanese voice actors, which is great.The animations and graphics are great for an anime based game (although Luffy does look a bit weird in 3d, and Nami and Robin's chests are comically large.On the downside, It is an incredibly easy game, I didn't have my party wiped once.  There is no need to grind either, since none of the battles are very challenging. Just equip the best ATK+ items on the characters with moves that target all enemies (namely Nami). The combat is a rock/paper/scissors type thing, that basically just forces you to swap in the character with the right attack type depending on the enemy (or just blasting everything with Nami's Thunderbolt Tempo and Luffy's Conqueror Haki). You can also boost/heal/revive your team with a meal made outside of combat by Sanji to make things go faster, or use Usopp's trick balls to weaken your enemies (only really useful when doing the juiced up power bosses post game).There are fetch quests, which are pretty boring and the rewards aren't usually worth much. And if you want to 100% complete the game you'll have to smash/break every box/barrel/chest in the game, so if you missed one you'll be spending forever looking for one you didn't see while playing through the main story. You'll also need to buy the DCL to get the last 5 achievements.It also seems like there was going to be the ability to purchase additional outfits (currently you can only get them through paid DLC) and weapons, indicated the presence of weapon and clothing stores that you can't buy anything in. It just seems looks like they dropped this feature partway through development.If you don't want to be mind numbed, by how slow the movement is, and how much backtracking there is, get the Movement Speed x 2 mod, and Jiggle Physics mods from nexusmods.

_childDocuments_.review: One piece odyssey could have been a decent game but unfortunately it's wrapped around poorly outdated gameplay mechanics and design choices. It had the potential to be really something great but instead it feels like the devs ran out of budget midway and just tried to rush the game out with that small remaining amount they have. My pros and cons after beating the game.Pros+ The story is good for a one piece game. It tackles past story arcs while also inserting an original story and new characters to it which gives a fresh take of these old familiar arcs.+ Strawhats are as lovable as ever and the game gave them justice. Also cool and familiar villains like croc, don flamingo, and the admirals are in this game.+ Excellent ost and great voice acting.+ Unique battle system. The whole zone system feels fresh and offers a new take on turn based style combat. Also it's always really cool seeing the strawhats hit their signature moves on the enemies. Luffy's gum gum gatling never gets old to me.Cons- Story is very predictable and just falls flat at times. Some of the story just felt rushed and some of the strawhats can get locked in some chapters.- For a game advertised as open world the game is surely linear. Most of the time the game doesn't really allow you to explore and forces you to follow a linear path to progress the story.- Too damn easy and with no difficulty options. The whole rock, paper, scissor approach of power, speed, technique system they've introduced are just very inconsistent and unbalanced. Zone system although fun but also kinda drags and slows down the pace of combat especially if you're facing a lot of enemies per zone. Battles can also get pretty repetitive since you're basically facing the same recycled enemies over and over again.- Insane amount of backtracking and sidemissions are mostly tedious fetch quest. Also some sidemissions are just downright confusing and gives you little to no hints on how to solve them.- Some chapters just felt really rushed.- The equipment system is pretty uninspired and the only way to learn new skills is to progress the story.As a huge one piece fan I still do think it did it's job and I also enjoy it enough to reach the end... so thumbs up. I highly suggest buying it at a discount if possible. This is a 7/10 game for me. It's probably one of the better one piece game out there but unfortunately it's just a very average jrpg game at that.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Odyssey is an absolute gem! The combat system is a delightful throwback to the old times of RPG turn-based battles, evoking a sense of nostalgia that fans of classic games like me will appreciate. It effortlessly captures the essence of those beloved classics while introducing its own unique twist with zonal combat.The combat mechanics truly carry you back to the golden era of RPG gaming. Every move, every decision feels significant and strategic. Game stands tall among the greats. If you're craving that nostalgic RPG experience with a fresh twist, and you love One Piece, this is an absolute must-play. It's a fantastic journey that will transport you back to the golden age of turn-based battles, leaving you with a smile on your face and a heart full of fond memories. And this game has Nami and Nico. What more can you ask for?

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting one I'm a lover of games but I do love me my anime, this was a decent combo of both, if you're looking for a semi? unique One piece story while reliving some of the more major and popular arcs this games a decently fun time, if you're looking for a turn based JRPG it's that and has a lot of great ideas and mechanics but it falls a little short due to some poor balancing and use of the mechanics I mentioned, is it worth a full retail price? Personally I'd say no but it's an okay enough game, especially if you're a one piece fan that I can suggest it dood.Okay onto the meat (imagines Luffy screaming meat at the top of his lungs) of the review, so the story takes place in a unique island called memoria where the strawhat crew crashland as is quickly shown and are now abandoned in, to start you all seem quite overpowered but I'm sure you can all guess what that means XD if you're expecting to use and see all the game has to offer you're gonna have to work for it! Although I cant quite say why due to spoilers, what I can say is this is an odd island with lot's of danger and fun to be had dood!Combat is one of the cooler things in the game and something that I haven't personally seen in a game before, so ya got a rock paper scissors mechanic going on, even got some elemental stuff too, pretty basic right? Only what do they do? they have areas in battles! That's right of the four crew on the field they can be entirely together with a group of enemies, split up against certain enemies or even be in a free space and able to move anywhere they want although the same can go for the bad guys too, adding the fact there are ranged moves and ones that hit multiple or even all enemies at once and it's a super cool concept I can really get behind! sadly for the most part the games a little too easy or then again at times the difficulty jumps crazy high, it really couldn't make up it's mind but you'll never struggle too much even in those situations dood.To continue on that end of the last paragraph as to why, the game also has cooking/food mechanics (as you'd expect with Sanji) as well as debuff tools (as expected of Usopp factory!) between these two things you will never be too weak to beat anything, especially with how crazy powerful some buffs are and yet they do compliment the game and characters themselves...also yes Sanji can't hit women as usual which I adore dood XDYou get the whole strawhat crew! Eventually, sadly that is one thing I wasn't too fond of, you get some of the crew to start but certain circumstances leave you without members until quite frankly way too late in the game for my liking but they are all as awesome and stylish as you'd hope for! all their attacks look great, their facial animations are on point and at times hilarious and what it lacks in the right kinds of difficulties it makes up for with flashy attacks that layer on the fanservice dood!Accessories are another interesting thing, so you get a myriad of them throughout the game, some rare, others normal but here comes the hitch, ya see they have slots, now unless you're super new to JRPG games you should know what these are but let's assume you're not, so you use other accessories to fuse into each other to gain their effects, now here in lies the issues, first you lose those things, like forever, poof! gone although the rare ones can't go away, sure you can buy more but some of the more important ones? gone forever, what does this mean? It means if you use them on a weak accessory you just wasted it, secondly and why most people will feel that way is that each shop holds a super expensive really powerful item, although by the end you will have more than enough money, it still adds up so much that you aren't gonna wanna spend it until late game but well...you also don't need to, got to the literal end game before I fused everything into a super powerful item dood.Paragraph got a bit big there but to continue on the devs really should have made limited pieces altogether and have them easily slot in and out, no one's going to waste money on items that are weak but also that they don't even really need either, it was a clever idea and in fact you can if you're lucky get up to double the stats from the item you fuse but to go to the effort of it all just isn't all that worth it in the end dood.The levels are cool and all recognisable and you can walk around as all the other characters who also have their own unique abilities to help you as you traverse the game but there are two characters you can't and what's worse at least one of them they could have made a running character, especially due to his funny running animations, he'd pull a muscle...but he doesn't have any! yohohoho! (sorry I had to lol) but yeah I say this because the game is reaaaally slow on the movement, even with quick travel just getting to where you need to is a terribly slow time, even in world seeker they had a faster mode of transport, it's not the absolute worst but it's certainly not fun dood.The story was fun and it even had be tear up a little, it also had some nice character progression as time went on for a certain character, keep a close eye on how they act and you can really tell the difference over time, it was nice to see personally speaking, the music was pretty good too, not always amazing but still nice for sure dood!All in all the game is pretty fun, it's a real decent port too, no crashes on my end, even played pretty dang good on the steam deck when I played on there from time to time, I think it's more a game for the fans but it definitely had a lot of potential in the gameplay department if they refined things just a little more a collectable counter and where they are missing to would have been nice for various reasons too, I would have clocked in more game time if that was added in for sure but after meticulously searching everywhere in these huge maps and still missing so many I gave up and just beat the game XD otherwise it's decently solid pay an okay price for it and you won't feel tilted, again especially if you are a fan dood.Thank you for reading my review, I hope it helps make your decision and if ya buy it I hope you all have fun with it dood! ^-^/

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, I'll recommend it, although there are some weird old design choices: walk 5 metres, cut scene, walk another 5 metres, cut scene, walk another 5 metres, cut scene... you get the idea.The game gives you a run down of the controls at the beginning of the game, where you'd expect them to be.  But then, you play through the prologue and do a tonne of fights, then you finish the prologue, and you're treated to a series of pop-up windows telling you the controls again... and then it goes STRAIGHT INTO telling you the controls for a THIRD TIME straight after, but this time as a slightly different set of pop-up windows.The 'player teaching' is all over the place: one minute you'll be chided by a character for stepping 1 centimetre off of the path, then without warning you're allowed to free-roam (with restrictions, but no warning that you can do this), then as soon as you've kind of gotten used to the free exploration for a bit... you're back to being chided for venturing a gnats bawhair in the 'wrong direction' (in a JRPG! Where the key to success in every JRPG ever made ever is that you follow the 'wrong path' to level up and gear up).And how do you quit the game when you're finished? I'm glad you asked because you have to navigate to menu F, sub-section 3, scroll across to menu sub-section T, then scroll-down to option 92e, but be careful you don't accidentally press the button for option 92d, or you'll have to start back from the beginning (of this process, not of the game, thankfully, although I did whizz past the 'Start New Game' screen a couple of times).Haven't Bandai Namco ever made an RPG before? Are they new to this process? I mean, I've never heard of them before, they must be a boutique indie company, right?Thankfully the game is pretty good fun so far: and the party change-on-the-fly mechanic is awesome, the platform swinging is quite cool, and the vibrant art-style we all know and love is always an asset to the One Piece IP.Kinda wish the dodgy design elements had been cycled out during play testing, kinda wish the character could run faster than the sprint mechanic, and kinda wish Luffy could jump down a ladder inside a village... I mean he can jump down a sheer face 3 times the height inside a dungeon, but in a village he has to shuffle down the ladder one rung at a time like a little old man.To quote Mike Stoklasa: 'Bizarre, bizarre, bizarre!!'

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the name fool you. Yes, One Piece Odyssey sure is an odyssey... through emotions and memories.One Piece Odyssey is a turn-based RPG with a rock-paper-scissor-system. One character may or may not be stronger or weaker against certain opponents. Now, I have never been a huge fan of One Piece. I mean I read the first manga and have watched a few short clips of the anime, but I gotta say; I'm impressed to what this game had to offer, and as such, I think I'm a bigger fan of One Piece than I was before. However, this game is only worth its full price if you are a hardcore One Piece fan. I got my copy of a Deluxe edition for cheaper than the base game's regular price.I got into this game almost completely blind. For example, I had no idea who Usopp, Nico Robin, Sanji, Franky or Brook were until I started playing this game. And even characters you get to meet on the odyssey (through emotions and memories).This game has some flaws and minor bugs, but truly, this is all I ever wanted from a turn-based RPG. This game is amazing!Graphics:The graphics are just beautiful. Start to finish. One thing I noticed it that most overworld objects have these weird "scratches" I don't recall them being on objects in the manga or anime, but I guess it was a design choice, after all.9/10Audio:Music and voice acting are spot on. Luffy, Usopp and Adio all have so much character in their voices when executing certain attacks.10/10Controls:Perfect. Just perfect. Both inside and outside of battles.10/10Lifespan:I completed this game in approximately 32,5 hours. This time was spent trying to find as many secrets as possible, having parties and not skipping any cutscenes. A huge game I'm sure will take at least a few hours to get through if you were to speedrun this game.Overall:9.75/10This game is like a dream come true. And for being ILCA's first Steam game I am once again impressed. I will update this review once I'm done with the expansion of the game "Reunion of Memories", so stay tuned!

_childDocuments_.review: Perfomance: I played it on an Msi gtx 1660 ti 6th gen i7 on 1440p max graphics zero issues steady 60 fps (cinematics are locked on 30 fps)Visuals:magnificent both the design of the characters and the Islands are like they are pulled straight from Oda's pages.Same quality you can expect with the voice acting.Story: A decent One Piece story that you could easily find as filler in the anime. Its strength lies in the interaction between the Strawhats which feels like you accompany them in their adventures. The negative points, the flashback segments I foundthem completely unnecessary they offer nothing new and serve as top 10 moments of the arc despite that I found the way the writers fused the two parts quite interesting.Combat:To my suprise turn based combat was a perfect match for One Piece past used action which made the the weak members of the crew like nami and ussop useless. Other than that I found the rest of the combat luckluster they had implemented many mechanics with devil fruits weaknesses buff and debuff but never utilise them fully making the combat really easy and a bit repetitive near the end.Music: The biggest disappointment not for this game only but all One Piece games, I just don't get why they don't use the existing music when they have the copyrights.Overall I will grade it 6,5/10 with a potential to create a series of this style of game if they try to enrich and improve on the current combat system they have built. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge One Piece fan, I would encourage you to buy this game and enjoy it for what it is.  It takes a unique approach to gameplay compared to most OP games that exist with a turn based combat.Worlds are breathtaking and the story (though it is filler) is interesting and keeps you hooked.  There were a few issues I noticed while playing:1) The gameplay could use a few more hints/push toward the side mechanics like bounty hunting.  I accidentally skipped going to the original NPC in Alabasta entirely and was confused for a while where it was.2) There are a few long spots where you cannot travel back and forth to the worlds/islands and are simply stuck with where you are.  A few are story based which makes sense, but I wish they could have limited this even more because exploration was very cool and there's a TON to do. Sadly I didn't get much of a chance/push to do a lot of it or go back and do it until the end of the game which I didn't feel like doing at that point.3) The last island is a bit short and starts around halfway through the climax (for obvious length reasons), but it also cuts out some interesting characters like the Tontatta and battles.  The game started to speed up for me a bit too quick towards the end almost feeling rushed.With all of that said, game is still fantastic and worth the playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! I'm a huge One Piece fan as well as a turn-based RPG fan, so this was a really fun mix of both. It's also been a while since I've watched the anime (I'm WAY behind), and it was nice getting to relive some key plotlines from the story. As a quick summary, this game is its own self-contained story, where the Straw Hat crew land on Waford Island, lose their strength/skills, and have to regain them by revisiting some key plotlines in a memory world called "Memoria". The One Piece plotlines you relive in Memoria are  Each one has a bit of a new "What if?" spin; won't say much more to avoid spoiling too muchThe gameplay was a lot of fun: I found the world fairly fun to explore, and while it wasn't  as open-world as one might think (e.g. you would typically be pushed towards your objective and not allowed to deviate too far from it), I enjoyed the level of freedom they gave: I felt like I had  freedom to explore what I wanted, but not so much that I ever felt too lost. My only gripe with the world exploration was that, even though they introduced a "fast transport" mechanic to instantly jump to parts of the map that you've already explored, they disable it for some quests, and I found it a bit boring at times to just run from Point A to Point B, then to Point C, then back to Point A even though I had already been to all of those places and had already found the "fast transport" things for those locations.The battle system was fun as well: it's turn-based combat where you get 4 "player moves" per turn (you have a party of >4 characters, and you can swap in and out as needed without using a turn), and each player can do a basic attack, use a special attack (which uses the "MP" equivalent), or use an item. There's a bit of a rock-paper-scissors dynamic to the combat: each character (on your team as well as enemies) are one of 3 "types" (Power, Speed, or Technique), where Power is strong against Speed but weak against Technique, Speed is strong against Technique but weak against Power, and Technique is strong against Power but weak against Speed. There's also multiple "zones" on the "battlefield", and each character in the player's party can only attack enemies in their "zone" (but can move to another zone once their zone is empty). It wasn't an overly complex battle system, but complex enough to make it a bit more fun than blindly mashing "Attack" on every enemy, which I enjoyedThe visuals and music were absolutely stunning. It has a 3D visual style that looks faithful to the anime, and I really enjoyed all of the details on the characters, enemies, world, etc. Lots of colors, beautiful rendering of the islands I enjoyed in the manga and anime, excellent orchestral soundtrack I found myself humming even while not playing, etc. My only gripe is that there was a decent amount of stuttering (I think it might have been the "shader compilation stutter" issues that plague Unreal Engine 4 titles), but for the most part, I was playing at a pretty stable 4K 60 FPS on my gaming PC (i7 CPU and 2080 GPU), so not too bad. Another (very minor) gripe was that, even though I was playing at 60 FPS, the cutscenes (even those that didn't seem prerendered FMV) seemed to be locked at 30 FPSOverall, I  recommend this game for One Piece fans! It was an excellent experience

_childDocuments_.review: I am a pretty big fan of the anime and manga, but games based on anime IP(s) in the past have been historically bad. It wasn't until Kakarot that I began to develop any sense of hope that maybe this genre of games would make a resurgence and produce some palatable titles.One Piece Odyssey is a pretty good game, it looks excellent, it feels like it stays close to the source material, they've really managed to capture the heart and soul of the One Piece franchise as a whole.The product's store page has the tag "Open World" on it, but I am unsure if that's an accurate statement. I have been playing for about two hours now and this game has felt insanely linear, to the point the game will literally refuse to let me take other paths, pick me up and put me back on the "right" path. If I have to play more than two hours in to a product in order to be able to get in to the meat and potatoes of it, then they are doing a poor job at designing the game.(Edit as of 3/8/2023: The game isn't open world. I don't know how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cattle paths forcing the players to go where the game wants somehow qualifies as an open world game, but it sure as hell doesn't deserve the tag. Dragon Quest was more open world than this game is. What was advertised on the store page isn't what I was sold and I am really pissed off about it. I am still playing it, but in the future, I am going to seriously reconsider anything else from these developers if they are gonna flat out lie about the game)This game is very dialog intensive, but it makes up for it with plenty of voice acting and wonderful scenes. The game has a bad habit of interrupting you all the time and it really messes with the general flow. This whole cube collecting thing is really bogus in my opinion and is simply a device used to pad out the entirety of the game. I really despise collect-a-thons like this, I would have much rather had a bog standard JRPG with perhaps a few side quests to unlock ultimate techniques or something.The entire world is nothing more than cattle paths connecting to larger open areas that quickly turn back in to cattle paths. The occasional dungeon breaks this up a bit, but even the dungeons aren't much fun. They got you doing a bunch of stuff that simply feels unnecessary and out of place in the game.The quests are terribly mundane and often involve a ton of back tracking. Most of the time I don't feel any interest in completing these quests besides progressing the story. A lot of them are things I simply cannot care about and feel like they don't even belong in the game. They play with this whole mindscape concept and I think it did a lot more bad than good for this game. The characters know they are basically traversing their memories and yet every single NPC with some sort of stupid ass sob story is treated like a life and death situation. It's utterly insane when you take a moment to consider it.They are using this concept as an excuse to revisit the story, while being able to change it and justify those changes because "memories are fuzzy", but honestly I would have rather have had a standard JRPG that started from the beginning and wrapped up in one of the later story arcs instead of the nonsense they are getting away with here.The game looks enough it would have succeed just being a condensed recap of the anime up until the last finished arc. Even with those complaints, I have been having a good enough time and for a lot of that I feel like I am simply watching a episode of One Piece (besides all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥).Kinda wish they would have gotten both English AND Japanese voice actors though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fan-service-game. For what it is, it is a really good rpg-game. The first 10 hours were a bit boring but when it came to the mid-game and especially for the late game i had a very good time. Sidequests:The sidequests arent good. It's always a delivery from A to B (and sometime to C) and a fight. The sidequests-stories are a bit funny but i wouldnt recommend to play those. The rewards for the sidequests arent helpful aswell. Mechanics:Besides the long ways you have to go this game does a lot right. The combat-mechanics are nice. The attacks are awesome (as a fan of One Piece) and the equip-system is great. Story:The story is good and here is were it comes to a fan-service-game. If you don't know about the story of One Piece at least until the end of the dressrosa-arc it will be confusing. This is because there will be a lot of context you have to know to understand what is happening. Bugs:In my experience the game is almost free from bugs. I found a bug where the movement freezes when you jump to a whole a switch to chopper while the character is in the air. I think that the commands are sequentially so that the jump will stay in a loop in the backend. Almost the same bug happened to me when i jumped and switched to zorro to cut a door.If you are a patient person and like the One Piece - franchise then i definitely recommend this game with having in mind that the game will end in a lot of fun after about 10-12 hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't consider myself a JRPG fan by any means and the deepest i have delve into said genre would be only around as deep as the likes of a few of the old Final Fantasy games and the all of the Pokemon games amongst a few stragglers like Earthbound, etc. So if your a hardcore fan of the genre I probably dont have much cred to talk about the genre but here is my takes on this game 23 or so hours into the main story...PROS:------------------As a One Piece fan myself I can wholeheartedly say that the art style captures the world of the anime beautifully, despite being 3D models in place of the 2D drawings which the anime series is known for. The gameplay is similar to the standard JRPG style in the sense that you have a roster of characters in your party which have strengths and weaknesses in the style of a type triangle with one being super effective against another (for example: Power being weak to Technical and that being weak to Speed) and visa versa. It can be a little repetitive at times but I feel that is just the JRPG style of combat so ill call it a pro.The maps/world is also just as incredible as the graphics for the exact same reasons, it encapsulates the anime's hard work at building these immense lands across the ocean of the One Piece world so well at times I found myself just taking in how incredible the landscapes look at times.The Story (so far) is great its just like a story taken straight from the anime but it gives you the control of the characters to truly encapsulate you into the world, so far I haven't found anything that seems out of the ordinary for the One Piece universe and everything falls into place so well it really does feel like you are watching/playing a chapter from the Anime. And its nice to see parts of the world that the anime covered like (Spoilers-->) .CONS:-------------------Some (not all) animations are a little janky or funny to look at (for example, Robins running animation is hilarious i thought) and a few other animations not syncing up like Luffy's running animation is a little fast for hes sprint speed.The combat can be a little repetitive but like I said in the pro section it is more than likely just the JRPG style so it is a pro as well as a con.CONCLUSION:---------------------------The game over all is very solid, enjoyable and is definitely worth playing, I would recommend waiting for a sale as I do feel £50 is a little pricey for any game. However the devs have really shown their love for the series with this game and I cannot recommend it enough as this game has pretty much stolen my free time after work and at weekends, now I am struggling to put it down since becoming completely engrossed in the immense landscapes and worlds of this game, also getting to see one of my favourite Anime people and places the way the game has presented them to me has made this game one of my favourite pieces of media to consume in recent time.OVERALL SCORE 9.5 / 10 :DHONORABLE MENTION:------------------------------The mover crab and the lil' mover's faces still give me the heebie jeebies

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly felt a bit slow and easy in the beginning, but since I paid full price (and because One Piece) I kept playing.I had seen reviews saying that it was just pick the best attack to win, and it genuinely seemed that way at first. However, once I got a little ways into chapter two, it did pick up a little. Nothing hard, and I thought save points were a bit too abundant, but then I had my first fight with the Sandora Dragons. Again, nothing hard, but it was a fun fight where I was thinking and strategizing to make sure none of my crew was ko'ed. And even further down the line, some of the boss/mini boss fights had me invested as well since (while still manageable without much sweat) they posed a threat to keeping the whole crew alive.On top of that, the layers of customizing gear, upgrading moves, and finding the upgrades/items, is something this game does as well as you could ask, even though its nothing new or done amazing. I do love the way you can use Sanji and Usopp to create different dishes or items to use similar to their roles in the Anime, it adds a nice touch.Now on the story side, I can't praise it much if at all. If you watched One Piece, you know whats coming and it does feel forced to a degree, depending on personal opinion, since they have to make a game around it. Like Samus always losing her power-ups at the start of a Metroid game. (Unless you're Metroid Fusion) However, there is one unique feature where you are rewarded with extra xp/items when you stay accurate to the Anime or how the Anime would go in this storyline. An example would be taking out a specific boss (spoiler free) with Sanji since that is how the Anime played out. It does add a fun level of 'challenge' even if its not a 'difficult' one.I have only made it pass the boss of Chapter 2 (I think, I stopped right after, and he was the main antagonist of the arc in the anime.) so there is PLENTY more game to hopefully scratch the rest of the itch that is missing. If the game has a difficulty curve, then it only gets more difficult from here. Maybe I'll update my review later.But at the end of the day, you can crush your enemy's balls as Robin so that demands a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game! It is definitely not for anyone looking to get into One Piece fresh. If you have some knowledge already and want to play through a few of the arcs in a turn-based RPG then it will be pretty enjoyable. If you do NOT want to revisit past arcs and want ONLY original story then this isn't for you.I read a ton of One Piece back when I had an incredibly slow and boring job but haven't kept up in a few years. Even so, all of the arcs that are recapped in this game are ones I read so I went in with some familiarity and it was cool to be reminded of them all. The actual original story stuff is very, very light and I would not be shocked if it only shows up again at the end of the series when threads tie together since it has little bearing on the overall plot as it stands.However, the turn-based gameplay is actually really fun and fast. It's rock-paper-scissors style with different zones your party can be in. You can choose from a wide variety of attacks that hit your zone, zones outside of your current, or all zones and each one has a pretty slick animation to it. By the end of the game it isn't exactly challenging because you become pretty OP just by playing the game normally but it is a fun take.Visually the game is great. The art style is very pretty and mimics some of Oda's linework while the animations themselves are fluid and on point. ILCA does a lot of character/animation work so the fact that the game looks this good isn't surprising.Overall, I'd say out of full-on ILCA projects it's better than BDSP but still not exactly a masterpiece. It's fun, it's not too long, it isn't grindy at all, and it's pretty. Is it worth the price tag? Maybe not. Wait for a sale. I got my copy with a coupon and I'm pretty glad I did. Definitely enjoyed my time but it didn't blow my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty solid JRPG. I enjoyed the game, love how the style kept close to the anime (comical facial expressions, gags, etc.), with a bit of interesting turn based combat mechanics.   I loved how customizable your party is in how you can build their stats and party composition. You can swap party members mid combat on the fly to adjust to enemy weakness or for your own utility (as long as they haven't used their turn yet or are part of a Dramatic encounter). You can even swap characters with each other whether they're in the same zone or not. Battle starts and your Nami spawns with 3 Power enemies in her zone? Just swap her spot with Zoro and he can have advantage against them. Boss just chunked someone with a powerful attack and froze them? Swap in Chopper for a turn to cure both the health and status then swap him back out.   Accessory customization was great as it allowed you to make anyone more focused on damage, tanky, or a some mix. Nami is the first character that got a mapwide attack so I pumped her with all attack forged gear and she wiped regular mobs up in one turn. I had her and Usopp built as glass cannons with 100% crit rate, 13k+ attack, and less than 3k hp. They were safe for 80% of fights being ranged and only got hurt from enemies that had ranged or raidwide moves but Nami solved this with her Mirage Tempo giving anyone a guaranteed dodge. I turned Brook into a tank god with 80% dodge with 100% resistance to all physical types (Power, Speed, Tech) with over 10k hp. He would sit there buffing everyone while being the only one in the boss' zone.   The game does have a few problems but my main issues were the bloat, chapter length, and forced story progression.Overall a fun experience with the Strawhat crew and I enjoyed the trip down memory lane to see some previous arcs and seeing some of the characters from there (I love you Smoker and Tashigi).

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was skeptical about the game with it being a turn-based battle type of game. But I am a fan of the Persona games, and this feels like just that with added elements such as division of enemies in an area, bond attacks, sort of like a limit break. And the game play is smooth. Haven't come across a single bug (or maybe I'm just too entranced with the game that I really can't notice the bugs, but in all the Japanese developed games that I've played, I rarely come across bugs, something that I have always admired with Japanese made games.). Story is a certified nostalgia trip with a twist. This is one of them Japanese developed games that is not too hard to understand and the upgrading and leveling system isn't too convoluted and confusing (for a gamer who isn't really a fan of games developed by the a Japanese company, this is one of those games that I actually liked). I'm not sure if there was a difficulty settings as I don't remember coming across one when I started the game. But the difficulty of this is game is just right (if you are a veteran turn-based battle system player, this game should be a piece of cake for you). Highly recommend this to a One Piece fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently up to Chapter.. 5? Just playing here and there when I have time. (Con at the end)I really enjoy the game as both a fan of One Piece and just someone who likes to play all kinds of video games. I believe I would enjoy this game with no prior knowledge of One Piece. That being said, however, I wouldn't feel the impact of a lot of the little bits that are awesome to come across, which simply makes sense. I also wouldn't get much of the emotional impact of many of the flashbacks. The music is fun, the dialogue hilarious and accurate as well as the quirks of all the crew and all the different attacks that are pretty fun to watch. One of my favourite things is how they've made each character useful in some unique way for exploration. Though, I will say not all these uses are immediately apparent and some take a bit of work to get to. Also makes the completionist in me quite happy that if I explore every nook and cranny, it's not for nothing. The story is fun, and very One Piece-esque. There's a whole lot of reminiscing that is satisfying to play through while not feeling like I'm rewatching the arcs themselves. I will say that sometimes the story locks you onto a certain path, so if you want to explore you'll need to finish that path and come back later. This can be annoying but almost every time that's happened I've had to come back to that area for another reason anyway, so in the end my annoyance was for nothing. No bugs/glitches that I've come across, no awkward gameplay, just slightly different keybinds to get used to and that's it. The game is simple fun. A con I've seen mentioned is that you can just use the same attack over and over again, and if you do that and complain about it, that's on you because you certainly don't HAVE to. Much like many games, you can grind the same thing over and over and get to the end, but that isn't the only way to play and is certainly the most boring. Each character has lots of different moves with different animations that are just fun.The only con I feel holds weight(and is directly related to the above one mentioned) is that the combat is easy. If you want challenging games, sure, this isn't for you but not all games need to have difficulty modes, and maybe they will add one someday(since I read something about an expansion or DLC at some point)? Either way, I enjoy loading up the game and playing it without getting stressed out over a single battle killing me constantly, I have plenty of other games for that.
