_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on the Early Access version and   for the Full Version (In case people read it after the full release).Pros and Cons (A more detailed review is further down):Tags: Retro Platformer, Turn-based, monster collecting. + Good controls+ Decent variety of monsters+ Evolution of monsters (Light/Dark and Evolution are nice options to utilize the various types of monsters in even more different ways.)+ Good music+ Riddles are not too difficult and not too many (Some you can simply skip, if you don't really need the item)+ Balancing is okay, though slightly favoured towards heavy Physical Crit Builds (That was my experience after some hours) - 13h of gameplay (Remember, it is EA. They will add more.)- Economy is pointless. You earn gold but can't really spend it, because it is pretty easy to get the top gear without spending money- Item variety is too smallThis game is a retro style platformer with turn based monster fights. And as such it works pretty well. The platforming part is solid. The controls work well, even for someone like me, who is not used to controller gameplay.The fights are very fun and interesting. You collect various monsters with varying abilities. It is the usual rock, paper, scissors style where you counter your opponent with the specific element or ability to gain the advantage. And in that regard it works pretty good. You don't just have the usual 3 or 4 elements, but instead they are also split into physical and magical attacks. So if you want to make absolutely sure to have the upper hand, you can choose from a variety of 50 Monsters to counter your opponents weaknesses. In this stage of the development, you can play through 6 or 7 areas with are filled with riddles which are sometimes challenging, but definitely doable. I am usually someone who googles riddles quickly, if i spend too much time on them, but this game has found a good balance in difficulty. Of course because the game is still in EA, some things are lacking a little bit, like e.g. the skillsystem needs a bit of balancing. I was able to build a: Healer/Buffer; Magical/Nuker; Physical/Mass Crit Team which carried me through the last 4 hourse by nearly onehitting every enemy team without a sweat. People who want to rely on a core-team will see that it is not advised to just stick to your favourite 3 monster party, but you should always keep at least some monsters up to speed with your main team, in case you run into a fight where you are heavily disadvantaged. The game adds a lot of variety with options to additionally evolve your monsters to either light or dark which opens up further actives skills and passives. Also you can evolve your monsters with certain items, though this is really late in the game and thus not really relevant yet.Also the game offers some challenging Bossfights, as well as a very basic infinity mode. Also PVP seems to be an option, if they ever think about adding Multiplayer. PVP fights against the AI in the game are not really challenging and thus i hope i'll be able to duel with real Players in the future.The games economy is very basic. Your items have preset effects which do not differ to items of the same type. The is no rarity element involved. You got a weapon, it deals certain damage, you can up it +1,+2,+3 and thats it. Money is pointless. I literally didn't need to spend a single gold coin. You can only buy items like gear, potions (which you do not need to use at all, because it is easier to heal with skills and the HP resets after evey fight.) and food. Upgrade materials can be found and not bought, but you find lots of those so no problem there.It would be interesting to see rarity added. You slay a Boss and have the chance to drop some nice weapons. Definitely something i would love to see.Overall i can to recommend this game in its current state. For the price you get at least 12h of gameplay and in the future i can see a lot of content being added which might even double or triple the time. This game as a lot of potential. So if you are into the turn-based fighting and don't mind some platforming in the meantime, this game is a safe bet.

_childDocuments_.review: Pokemon meets Metroidvania. Overall, a fantastic game. Finding good synergies between monsters is key to having a smoother combat experience. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice selection for April and I highly recommend that everyone, Pokémon fan or not, should get it. It has enough going for it to stand on its own without the comparison. Monster Sanctuary is a wonderful blend of creature collecting, TBS, and oh so light amounts of platforming -- just enough to keep an adventurer paying attention. The game has a wonderful story that builds just enough curiosity to make the player wonder why the world is designed the way it is. While finishing the story did leave me feeling a bit confined in the Sanctuary (I want more), it was all because the game did such a great job of giving me such a rich experience within the confines of the world that I was given to explore and the monsters I was able to hatch. I love that you can't just power through all the content with the same team (without experiencing diminishing returns). Combos and team roles (healer/shield/damage/etc) are a thing and slowly become a wall you need to overcome in order to learn how to efficiently win battles without simply using brute force (until you figure out a team that can use said force efficiently).I love that in this game, equipment and food buffs are an actual thing to signify progression instead of just being tacked on. I also experienced a lot of freedom in swapping around monsters for my various teams as I worked my way through the post-game content. The game allows you to invest resources, within reason, towards new monsters so that you can try out various builds without experiencing buyer's remorse. It's a game that wants you to try everything and really think about various builds within each extensive skill tree to make the most of your experience.It was just an awesome experience overall and Monster Sanctuary definitely filled a void created by my disappointment in newer Pokémon games. I'm glad that this game was one of the few I chose to pick up again after a long hiatus from Steam. Money well spent!

_childDocuments_.review: This game proved to be quite a pleasant surprise for me!Basically this is an RPG where you're a monster trainer who runs around in a 2D landscape that looks like a graphically improved Terraria and is laid out in the style of a Metroid style game. You have to figure out various jumping puzzles on each screen, sometimes requiring the use of the monsters you've acquired on your journey to reach tricky treasure chests that were once impossible for you to obtain. As an example, the vaero monster (which looks like a bird) can pick you up and carry you across large gaps. Another monster, the monk, can bash walls on command and sometimes reveal hidden passageways leading to treasure.The assortment of monsters you can collect is where the game really shines. Battles play out in a standard turn-based JRPG fashion with each of your monsters having an elemental strength and weakness, and a plethora of elemental attacks and support skills to use. At the end of any given fight, you may acquire an "egg" that, when hatched, gives you a type of the monster you just defeated. Each monster can be equipped with a weapon and three accessories that are very heavy on stat modifiers, all of which can be upgraded at a blacksmith. All monsters also have skill trees that you can sink points into when you level them up from fighting. The skill trees in this game are super satisfying and allow you to learn stronger versions of existing attacks, brand new abilities, and all sorts of cool passive modifiers that do things like drastically increase your critical hit chance if the selected monster has a buff on it, or leeching hit points whenever the monster deals damage, and these two examples are just the tip of the iceberg.I expected this to just be a cute little game that I'd put a little bit of time into, but I'm approaching 10 hours just over a day after I first played the game. I'm seriously hooked on Monster Sanctuary. There's so much customization, battles are surprisingly strategic, and exploring the various 2D platformer-esque "biomes" of the game's world and finding secret routes and treasures is so much fun.This game is early access, but it genuinely does not feel it at all. Don't let the simplistic and retro look throw you off, this game has a lot of depth and is super polished already. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the long time fans of the Pokemon franchise who is bitter about the decline in the  quality of the games and the whole "Dexit" affair, I'm really glad I stumbled upon Monster Sanctuary. While it is in the same genre as Pokemon, but does a bunch of things that makes it unique and isn't simply trying to ape what Pokemon does. Not only do you have a large cast of monsters to pick from to add to your team, you can customize them all with unique skill trees, food slots and equipment. Each of these bits of customization are meaningful strategic decisions that can drastically alter the way your monster performs in combat. The fact that most battles are 3v3 means that you'll almost always have 3 of your monsters out of the field at once, allowing you to further customize your team by creating synergies within your team to amplify their effectiveness. While still in early access, I have yet to encounter any bugs, glitches, crashes or instances of gross game balance issues. The platforming metroidvania element of the game is probably its weakest point, but even that doesn't really detract from my enjoyment of the game and I can appreciate that the devs are trying to do something unique. Some of the puzzles can be a little frustrating, not because they're hard but because they're fussy. However, the treasure hunting element that this mode brings can be enjoyable as you probe the nooks and crannies for hidden treasure chests. Overall, this game is worth your time and money even at this stage at its development and as it progresses to a 1.0 release will become even more of a good deal. I have no regrets buying it.

Every monster you get gives you abilities you can use outside of combat to find secret areas, unlock doors, and provide new options to traverse the landscape. A wacky combination of previously disparate elements seamlessly blends together into a very enjoyable experience. And though I haven't gotten to it yet, it's got multiplayer!

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, you got some Pokémon in my Metroidvania!What? You got some Metroidvania in my Pokémon!Mmmm... mysteriously delicious!No seriously, this is one of those combos that had never occurred to me before, but now that I've sampled it, I suddenly realize that they go together perfectly. Kind of like 'Disney characters + Final Fantasy' was a joke before Kingdom Hearts became a bestselling blockbuster series.So, you've got a bit ol' Metroidvania-style map to explore, with various biomes that each carry a distinct atmosphere, look, and selection of enemies. But instead of accessing new areas by finding upgrades, you do it by battling and catching monsters who can assist you with new abilities. Instead of finding a grappling-hook in a chest somewhere, you catch a giant spider who can web you to where you need to go. Instead of finding scuba-gear, you catch a giant fish that can pull you swiftly through the water. Instead of finding double-jump boots, you... well, actually, you still find double-jump boots, but frankly, for a Metroidvania, double-jumping is so utterly basic that it'd be silly to tie that to any particular monster.The combat-system, meanwhile, is remarkably deep and varried, featuring a variety of potent buffs and status-ailments that gradually ratchet up the challenge and complexity as you progress through the game. Early on you can get by easily enough just targeting enemies' elemental weaknesses, but carry on doing that, and you'll hit a wall in the late-game, where instead you have to focus on stacking buffs and shields on your own party, while loading the enemies up with crippling ailments and grinding down their own attempts to buff up high. Just don't forget to still keep an eye on the elemental lineups, or your key buffer/healer might just get suddenly one-shot by a heavily-boosted 'Super Effective' attack! There's also an intriguing combo-system that takes some getting used to, and a somewhat arcane 'grade' system that gives you various rewards from each battle based on how well you performed.What I'm getting at is that this game is DEEP, and neither pulls punches nor holds your hand all the way through. You get some mild tutorializing at the start, introducing you to the basic systems, but it's up to YOU to actually figure out how to apply them effectively, and if you fail to keep up, things can get pretty frustrating pretty fast. You have to be ready to revise your approach, switch out your monsters, change your gear, and try new things if you want to make it through the adventure - and, more importantly, hatch 'em all!If I have to give it ONE serious criticism, it's the frustrating way the 'shift' system intersects with this game's version of 'evolutions'. Without going into too much detail, the shift-system is enabled around or past the halfway-point of the game, depending on exactly what kind of path you take, and causes new, more powerful variants of every available monster to start randomly spawning. You can turn regular monsters into shifted variants using an item, but this item has highly limited availability and cannot be bought. Meanwhile, the 'evolution' system allows you to use certain special items to transform a small number of monsters into different, usually more powerful, monsters that invariably can ONLY be obtained in this way. Some of these special items are simply dropped by the 'evolved' form of the monster when encountered in the wild, but others can be obtained only ONCE, in treasure-chests or from NPC's. Additional copies of these evolution-items can only be gained randomly from 'reward-boxes', which means spinning a really big wheel-o-fortune and crossing your fingers. Do you see the problem? By the time you unlock 'shifting', you're liable to have already wasted several semi-unique evolution-items on regular, unshifted versions of those monsters. If you want a shifted version of the evolved monster, you'll thus have to either pray for another evolution-item to drop from a reward-box, or expend an equally rare and valuable 'shifting-stone'. It's really more of a nitpick, but it's something I feel could really have been handled better. Consider it a warning, also, and a reward for having read all the way down here!So yeah, apart from that one niggling annoyance, an excellent game that combines two genres in a remarkably entertaining fashion. Definitely worth recommending!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 100%'d the game aside from NG+, and had a great time.  Two thumbs up. I beat the BBEG and there's more game to play!  I don't know if I have DLC or what, but I'm happy about it.  Been having tons of fun with this game.  Metroidvania with plenty of map-exploration abilities to collect, and a few difficult platforming areas.  The combat is not platforming, it's like a JRPG, 3 vs 3 or 3 vs 1 (boss) or 6 vs 6.  When you finish a fight with a high enough rating, or if you just get lucky, you can get an egg for one of the monsters you killed, and hatch it as your own!  Each monster has a different selection of attacks/skills (many are repeated on multiple monsters) to be unlocked as they level up.  It's up to you to build an effective, synergizing team, and there are lots of things you could focus on!  There are 2 attack types: physical and magicThere are at least 5 damage types: neutral, air/wind, fire, earth, water/iceThere are attacks that only hit 1 monster or AoE all 3There are attacks with different quantities of hits, which affects your combo counter, and whether it got dodged etcThere are healing and shield skillsThere are a ton of buffs / debuffs You can also equip them with a weapon and 3 accessories, which all do different things and can also be upgraded. Lots to play with, especially once you get into the high levels and can fully spec out your monsters.  That has a lot of COOL factor, but it takes a lot of TIME so I tended to build 1 team and use it until I got stuck, then try to build something new.  Currently $23CAD on Steam, but I got it <5 on a Fanatical Bundle, and it's well worth that.  Having a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: Pay little attention to my playtime. I played through this game on Gamepass and decided to buy it with the sale on steam.It's a brilliant game. Once you reach a certain temple tough, things really start to pick up, both in terms of creaturedesign and complexity of combat. Combat itself is quite tactical, but one minor gripe I have with it is that a lot of the ability-upgrades of your monsters are just passive, which still have a big impact on battle, but don't feel as special as entirely different moves in other creature collectors.The metroidvania-elements are also quite nice, having to use the abilitys of your creatures to progress is quite fun and gives you an actual reason to catch them all.Best thing for me personally though is how easy it is to build new teams in the post-game. Every new creature you catch is close to maxlevel and skilling(or re-skilling) is pretty easy to do. No hours of breeding and training specific values required! Really wish every creature-collector would do it like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time playing Monster Sanctuary. It was a nice game to play through and there is definitely a lot there for completionists and people who want a challenge.There are a lot of comparisons to Pokemon. However, unlike Pokemon, the battle system deep and more engaging, and many times you can't just be completely overleveled and expect to roll over story encounters. It feels a little more like Persona or other SMT games in this regard.The game can be strategic and punishing because of it. Encounters can be very difficult if you don't have a lineup that makes sense in terms of roles and elemental affinities. The battles against other NPCs test your strategies very well. However, there are still some very cheap strategies out there that can get you through the game pretty easily (the snail is very strong in most NPC encounters in my experience). One negative is the game feels like it dragged on and became a little tedious. Near the end I felt like I just wanted it to be over with and rushed through most of the last few areas, only fighting monsters that were impossible to get around.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like monster tamers, buy this game.Nearly every other monster tamer relies on the Pokemon formula of 1v1s and one-shots. Monster Sanctuary finally brings monster tamers into the world of modern RPGs, rethinking all of the cliches and conventions to make a game worth more than just sum of your nostalgia. It's simply fun to play.There are no bad monsters. Every monster has a purpose (or multiple), and every monster can be strong in the right party comp. Want to try something different? Reset the skill tree with a common item. Having a hard time with a late-game fight? Hatch a monster at near-max level, and slot it into your party with 0 grind. No other monster tamer is this detailed, this strategic, or this flexible.I've been a fan since the original demo that ended with the Steam Golem fight, and I've been waiting a long time for the full release. There are some things I'd like to see improved, like the writing, and the early areas could be improved by applying the design skills learned from 5 years of development, but I have absolutely no hesitation in recommending this game right now.It's just fun to play, start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Early game is a lot of fun but then it becomes a chore. They've implemented level scaling (very odd scaling based on how many rooms you explored and monsters in rooms set to your strongest current ones, so in theory you could meta-game that if you really want to), a level cap at level 40 (which means enemies set close to your level cap, especially random encounters become a chore as you can't out-level them anymore) and contradictorily core gameplay loops.You have wild encounters and bosses where you fight 3-vs-3 (or 3-vs-1 for most bosses) and you tailor your party usually around that, but then there are party fights of 6-vs-6 (though only 3-vs-3 in the fight, if one of your monsters dies you have to select a replacement from the remaining ones). The party fights are an absolute chore, usually about having the right buffs/debuffs and don't allow much flexibility to overcome. Either you have the right monsters or you're dead.Now, the monsters come in egg form. If you hatch them they usually have a level around what your highest level is, but only the 6 main monsters gain experience from fights. So if you later need one of the other monsters for a specific talent, yeah, you have to grind that up, which happens quite often later in the game. It's really tiresome.All this does is make the early game rather exciting with lots of stuff to explore and get but later due to all the mechanics described fighting becomes more and more tiresome.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. If you like collecting creatures and also like the Maple Story vibe (but don't like actually playing Maple Story), this is the game for you. I'm not normally a platformer person, but this was fairly simple and straight-forward. Since I enjoyed just jumping around places enjoying the vibe, it didn't bother or frustrate me to build up my plaformer skills to get places. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is essentially a Castlevania: SotN metroidvania with Pokemon style monster capture and old school JRPG turned based party combat.    Each creature has a unique skill tree and can be further enhanced by light/dark shifts, upgradable equipment, and perma food buffs.  The game progresses at a nice rate and exploring the map feels natural without too many road bumps.  You will likely need to retool your team several times to focus on intra-monster synergies and opponent weaknesses throughout the course of the game to meet the demands of stronger challenges or boss fights.  Absolutely recommend for the aspects mentioned above as well as the enjoyable drop in game play, great pacing and difficulty ramping, sense of exploration, and the endearing pixel art.  The free DLC "The Forgotten World" adds a new area with additional monsters and challenges that add on to the already great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a monster battler with a metrovania overworld and turn based 3 on 3 battles. I've played through the game 4 times now (once with each starter) at various points through early development and once again when it was released lovingly into the wild (60 hours in the last 2 weeks). And I'm still finding new combinations to try.Do you want a physical based team that smacks down your opponents, you can do it. Do you want to debuff the opposing team to oblivion and watch them helpless die to fire, poison, and ice, this game lets you do it. Do you want a cute frog, adorable fluffy one eyed monster, and a caterpillar facing down the odds, yup, you can do it. The freedom is yours. Each monster has different skill tress you flesh out that lets them do what you want them to. You can be a dedicated healer or a direct damage beast, or an aura sharing support, the flexibility is yours. And every monster is viable. In my current playthrough 1 on the monsters from the first area traveled with me literally to the last zone. It's biggest strength can also be a weakness however. There are 101 monsters each with varying skills and putting together a synergistic team is important. There's a lot to take in and its easy to get overwhelmed. Fortunately, the community is extremely helpful and the dedicated community liaison actually liaison so help is only a discord or forum post away.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: If you like metroidvanias and monster collecting-battler/tactical games, this game is for you. I like the former better, but I also like to get lost in skilltrees, combining creatures, and equip them with stuff that makes them stronger. This game is seriously good, I like it a lot. I don't really go for achievements with steam games, but I unlocked all 34, just for fun. Even if you go through the vast map and storyline, the game still proveides things to do.There are many pros:- I love the pixelart, the animations are not many in frames or types, but the existing ones are made well.- Many retro tunes to listen to- The monsters are cool as hell, some are cute, or funny, some are noble and majestic, some are terifying and horrendous. And there are a LOT of them. You can modify them to light or dark, (upgrades to base stats, and a new skill) tripling the creature number. Some even can be evolved to a new monster.- Interestingly both the platforming and the tactical battling made really well (with small hickups).- The metroidvania part include the monsters too: all creatures have an ability that helps in exploring and progressing on the map.- Worms!There are some cons:- The map is not a big help, it's very basic, not giving any information whatsoever (no ability gates, not even the area names).- If you look for a specific thing (a monster, a crafting material etc) it could take a long time to find it.- To max out everything, you probably have to look for some guides as I did. Some secrets are hard to find (wich is fine, I just mentioning what I used some guides to), most of the champions are hard to defeat to 5 stars. Some of the puzzles are hard to solve (the timered ones especially). To find and build a team for defeating a specific champion could take a long time, as they probably need some equipment you don't have, and maxed out. And the skilltrees, as I mentioned I love to mess around with them, I'm just not good at it. :)But, despite the cons there is so much to love, this game is worth it's cost, and if you are on a budget, wait for a sale, and then buy it, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: quick note: my playtime is inaccurate, add +20 hours to the time of review. I mostly played and beat the game over one weekend I didn't have internet, so it didn't sync playtime. A complex, party-based RPG with a pokemon-like coat of paint and metroidvania world gameplay. Each 'monster' has an extensive skill tree and the name of the game is building synergies with your team. Every action affects your whole team in some way, leading to lots of emergent complexity and synergy. Instead of 1v1 being the standard, battles are 3v3 opening much more possibility for teamplay. But, skill tree resets are very easy to get your hands on, so you don't need to be afraid of investing a dud skill point or going down the wrong path - you can reset and try different things as the monsters unlock new skills, and you rotate in new picks for your team. You can re-skill your entire team after a boss battle to take advantage of a different approach. For me, the real fun in the game comes from optimizing my team so I can beat most battles in 2-3 turns. When wild encounters start lasting more then 3 turns, I know my team isn't keeping up and I need to optimize their skills and equipment. On the other hand, Trainer and Boss battles provide a longer form battle where synergies really shine. Spending 3 turns of set-up and defense to allow your Sweeper to spend the next turn bulldozing an entire team is incredibly satisfying, or setting up a stall + dots team and watching the enemy slowly dots themselves to death.  The great thing is that wild, trainer, and boss battles are all so emergent different. Wild battles, you get the most rewards for beating them fast so you want some good all-out attack to do these quickly.  Bosses are typically incredibly strong but fairly narrow in scope, so you need to build a counter that really focuses on their strengths and weakness in particular.  20% damage reduction against all kinds of damage won't do you much help on a boss buffed itself to 500% fire damage, so you really need to prepare for exactly what you're fighting, after a few failed attacks to scout out their moveset and weaknesses.  Keeper duels are different again, with a 6v6 style that are highly varied where the Keepers have all the same mechanics and options that you do. All these kinds of battles require different approaches so you never get stuck in a routine and are constantly on your toes, thinking about how you can leverage the skills and abilities to you have to build a plan against the enemy infront of you. It is difficult to stress just how important team synergy is in this game. You can't just build each monster individually to fit a predefined role, their role will change fluidly depending on the match-up of allies and enemies. My tank in one battle is my DPS in another is my support in another. All monsters can, and should, do all depending on the situation.  Trying to play most monsters 1-1 matching a role or ignoring synergies with allies (and against enemies) will lead to severe under-performance (and long battles), but the game is very forgiving and you have easy access to re-skills to fix things or just try something new.Built in new game+ and options for randomized and nuzlocke-style  ('Brave') runs with or without permadeath give this lots of replayability that I'll be sure to keep coming back to.

_childDocuments_.review: One may be tempted to say that at first this is a pretty cute-and-dry Pokemonlike, but where it excels it turns the game into a whole new, and much better, form.Here, the monsters you can tame have skill trees, and that makes all the difference. Suddenly, instead of simply having one team that maximizes type coverage, you have a set of builds you can make, and this set is huge. Every monster has many different ways you can stat them out in these trees, and there are many other points of customization as well. This adds incredible, fascinating depth both in and out of combat. It makes combat a dizzying whirl of effects, both active and passive, being applied in a turn, and it really is a joy to experience.It also bills itself as a metroidvania. This is true! Monsters grant out of combat abilities that allow you to access new areas. I was never good at combat in metroidvanias, so replacing action combat with real-time combat is a really genius move, if you ask me. I will say that the original Pokemon has metroidvania elements too, what with HMs and all, so this isn't exactly revolutionary, but I do love platforming and discovering things on the world map in this game.The writing is... Nothing to write home about. A little too inspired by Pokemon in that regard. Another (admittedly weird and minor) gripe I have is that there are no game over screens when you fail a plot-required battle, but instead when you lose, you're instantly and unceremoniously teleported back to before the fight. It breaks my immersion, honestly, and I'd at least like to have a game over screen I need to press "continue" on to get teleported backwards.Overall, do I recommend this game? Absolutely! The actual battles are far and away much better than its inspriation, and the builds I can make will have me thinking for a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have played on Steam. The battle system is well designed, and from my experience in story mode, well balanced. The map layouts are cleverly designed to suit the game progression well.If I have to complain it is that after a while battle may get boring, especially if you want to grind. Having to choose your starting 3 pokemons at the start of each battle because each time the enemies are different can get a little annoying even if you do not grind. Also the game does not run very smoothly all the time on my Mac. But I can live with all of these.

_childDocuments_.review: So if you're looking for a new Pokemon this isn't it. It was mildly fun, but the game keeps freezing on me. At times this makes it unplayable. Adding to that, I recently found out that only a handful of the 101 monsters can evolve. For me, like 60% of the fun in Pokemon was evolving your pokemon. It gave the game a nice progression and made me feel more invested in my team. Well, all of these monsters look like level 1 starter pokemon, and they don't get any better. The skill tree would be cool if there were a greater variety of moves. Half of my monsters share essentially the exact same skill tree, and the other half have another version of the exact same skill tree. So essentially it doesn't matter in the least if I pick one or the other of my grass-type monsters. None of these monsters so far have anything unique or special about them.The level design is confusing and not in a good way. I spent a good deal of time trying to find my way back to a certain part of the map on the first level, and the map was no help at all in trying to do that. It's just nondescript green blocks, and they don't give you really any idea of whether one way is a dead-end or whether it was a soft dead-end that I needed a certain monster's special skill to get through. The level design is also pretty boring so far. Everything looks the same.The monster special abilities would be cool, but they don't really do anything except help you get to chests which have seemingly pretty common/underwhelming items. Would be cooler if you had to use them to get through certain parts of the level, or if there was a better payoff to using them to find treasure. There is not a lot of surprise in this aspect.The story so far also seems weak. I was not invested. You live in a monster sanctuary. You and everyone else hatch and train monsters. That seems to be the extent of it. I really wanted to like this game. I think it has potential, but I would have to see a lot of changes before reconsidering. Including:- (actual) Monster evolution - More interesting level design with better maps- More engaging storyline and characters- More variety in skill tree/monsters have unique abilities that would make me choose them over another monster in battle- Fix the constant freezing (I know this isn't an issue for everyone but I have never run into this issue before on this computer)Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this since the game's early alpha builds before it made it onto Steam and I love it. I first found it on a pokemon fansite, as like pokemon it is a monster collection RPG, but thats where the similarities end. The game takes place in a sort of hidden lost world within our own, one where the culture of the humans inhabiting it remained unchanged since the middle ages (just without the senseless bloodshed). The action starts fairly quickly and each monster has a unique skill tree. And also like pokemon many of these monsters evolve too (though every evolution uses an item and they can be hard to find) My only complaints are in relation to the difficulty curve. I say this because while an RPG does sort of expect one to do some amount of grinding, often you have to go to some pretty far lengths to get the EXP needed to level up and even then  a tough battle can still wipe you out due to the rules of tamer battles not letting you use items (which makes sense, as you can heal/revive with certain monsters all you please) but the real problem comes in when we factor that in each new area the difficulty curve spikes to a level forcing you to grind like mad and at a certain point the EXP gain for the previous area becomes abysmal, forcing you to waste money on items against wild monsters and the item shop doesnt appear to get stronger healing items making it somewhat difficult to get a good handle on progressing unless you are that determined to waste hours training against significantly less EXP yield than what you actually need.Overall I give it a 8/10. If the developers can rectify the issue of how grindy the game is I might rate it higher but for all I know I could be just asking for too much.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a number of games which claim to be Pokemon adjacent or somehow threaten to usurp the Pokemon throne- we all know them! Temtem, Yokai watch, they all generally get tripped up on one or more fronts that really fail to capture what it is that truly makes Pokemon such a beloved franchise! It's not necessarily some epic world-saving quest, it's not necessarily just collecting monsters, it's not necessarily the cute designs- it's a game that somehow manages to be simple to understand but surprisingly deep in the mechanics and capacity for creativity, it's a game that manages to be straightforward but full of mysteries, it's a game that rewards you for however you decide you want to play it. As someone who grew up with Pokemon since I was a kid, I've really wanted to find something that catches that same level of amazement and wonder that I felt back then- and finally, I've found one! Monster sanctuary is incredible in every single way I could think to describe it. I'm more of a Pokemon casual, but a great friend of mine does competitive battling and she's blown past my current progress and rants and raves about the game and its balance, its catering to many different play-styles or strategies, and how it remains a really engaging game all the way into the endgame! In fact, she's already plotting a second, or even third play-through- which should be evidence of just how in-depth the mechanics are for this game!Important to note however, is that these many mechanics are expertly introduced, a slow trickle of complexity that actively gets used and expanded upon over time, without ever becoming too much at once! Unlike Pokemon, as well, the game itself is designed from the ground up to teach you about these mechanics and to encourage you to use them- so what seems like a vast array of potential avenues to explore always feels just one step removed from what you just got comfortable doing- and that slow trickle of interesting, engaging ways to play the game continues well into the end-game!Another incredible thing to note is that none of the Mons end up getting outclassed- no arbitrary tier system because some Mons are just statistically so much better than others- it does a really, really good job of giving a huge variety of valid strategies and making every Monster good in their own way, even the humble monsters you start off with! The sheer diversity of monsters composing the highest ranking teams for the online battling (That's right, online competitive multiplayer!) is baffling to the extreme- and mind you this isn't just because nobody knows what they're doing, these are the truly competitive teams that have fought their way to the top.I feel like I could go on and on, but this is already an extremely long review, so for the sake of brevity! Play it, it's incredible, the graphics are cute, the monsters are amazing, the battling is so well paced and balanced that it boggles the mind, the mechanics are incredibly fun, the story even goes crazy places, this is just some of the most fun I've had with a game in a long time and I simply couldn't recommend it more. Worth every penny!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, although it took a while to really show it. Combat and mechanics are all awesome, with slight nitpicks here and there. No persistent health and not being allowed to switch monsters mid-fight makes having 6 of them somewhat redundant, at least until the game gets hard enough where you have to start abusing type advantages hardcore. These issues don't apply to the master-vs-master battles, though, which are great.The skill trees are awesome in general. Not much else to be said there.I said the game is great, but it took a while to show it. I said this because the game has a lot of issues that oddly get better or stop appearing later on into the game. For one, the aesthetics and level design at the start of the game are pretty poor. Enemies that don't particularly follow or attack you at all, so you can run right past them. Treasure chests strewn about haphazardly. The layout of the level doesn't really make for interesting platform challenges, and there aren't many puzzles or anything to keep you busy. I understand the reason for some of this. You have 6 monsters with 4 equip slots each, so there has to be a boatload of equipment right off the start to fill those slots. That said, it would greatly serve the game to give context to all those items: receive them through puzzles, receive 'starter kits' from an npc, change the sprites to something other than just chests (big red gemstone for red gems, etc.), maybe have some monsters come pre-equipped with an item or two, etc.The start of the game needs a lot of work, and honestly it really gives the wrong impression. Later on chests start appearing mostly behind platforming challenges, puzzles, hidden walls, or unavoidable enemies, and they really don't spam them the way they do at the start.The visuals of the levels later on also improve immensely. It seems like the further you get in the game, the better the levels start looking. The enemies still have fairly passive ai, which I'm not a huge fan of, but they at least start putting them in positions where they're difficult to avoid.Here's a couple more gameplay nitpicks: the player character's physics are honestly pretty bizarre. You rocket up when you jump and can turn instantly, but your max horizontal speed is kind of low, which feels really weird. I also wish there were more applications for the monster overworld skills, and also wish they would be more responsive to use (imagine enemy shoots attack at you, you dodge, then use your monster skill to hit the enemy and get to start the fight with some kind of bonus.)Ultimately the game is more rpg than metroidvania, so it's not the biggest deal in the world, but at the moment the metroidvania half of the game could use a bit of work.The final big issue I have with the game is the music. Similar to the level design, it generally improves over the course of the game. The music in the first couple areas as well as the battle theme are honestly just not very good. I'm not sure if it's the instruments or the mixing, but it's pretty rough. From around the 3rd area or so and onwards, the area music becomes far more bearable. The music in the snow area in particular is fantastic. I don't know what the difference was, but the snow area really nailed it.Main thing is the game could really use different battle themes based on the area. There's only 1 battle theme for the entire game, besides boss fights as far as I can tell, and it gets old pretty quickly. If there were different themes for each area, that would be perfect.It may seem like I'm really bashing on the game, but I actually really do like it. It kind of nails the 'Pokemon, but with skill-trees and also it's 3v3' idea. It just has some work to be done in the aesthetics and metroidvania department. The story isn't anything to write home about, but people don't really play these types of games for the story anyway.I'm just nitpicking it pretty hard since it's early access and all this stuff has a chance to get fixed. I think the game really does have a lot of potential, and that it could be something truly special when it's finished. Even if you want to wait on it a bit, it's definitely worth your time. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: The map progression in the game is somewhat linear. You can explore zones outside the main story to an extent, but as the story advances, new zones with new monsters become available. Each monster has a special skill that can be used outside of combat, such as gliding, breaking blocks, and more.These skills are used to solve the game's puzzles, which are generally quite simple. They also allow you to reach certain areas through platforming. However, platforming isn’t the main focus of the game, as the jumps aren't pixel-perfect or difficult, and there are no hard platforming puzzles.The zones and monsters are beautifully designed, and the monsters are quite unique—you'll likely end up with some personal favorites. Each monster has a unique combination of passive and combat skills, which you unlock as they level up. Some skills are shared between monsters, but since the combination of abilities is different for each one, every monster remains useful in various situations, even if they share some skills with others. Monsters' abilities often revolve around specific themes, such as debuffing, buffing, or dealing damage.The combat is the best part of the game. Damage-dealing attacks are divided between physical and magical types, and each falls into one of five elemental categories. In addition, some attacks come with secondary effects, like buffs or debuffs. The buff/debuff system is extensive and becomes increasingly important as the game progresses.Combat is 3v3, but your team consists of six monsters, allowing you to build a team of your favorites or monsters that complement specific combat strategies, such as a debuff-focused team or a buff-heavy team. This system allows for deep strategy, with a lot of variety and viable setups.Regular enemy encounters are fast-paced and not particularly difficult, but battles against other characters with their own teams of six monsters are much more challenging. There's also an online mode where you can challenge other players.The story isn’t very deep, with a simple "good vs. evil" narrative.In summary, if you enjoy monster-taming, building synergies and strategies in combat, and customization with a bit of challenge, I would recommend this game. However, if you're looking for a deep story or challenging platforming elements, this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really impressed with this game. The sprites are done very well in a style that reminds me of terraria. The game is really more than just a metroidvania/pokemon mash up, which is a refreshing new idea. It has a deeper level of customization. Each animal has a skill tree and weapons can be equipped. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing fun for anyone who likes pokemon or Dragon Warrior Monsters from back in the day. However, it does need a little work. The power curve never feels quite right, so you have to grind a lot to get up to the next tier of abilities (I set a macro to autocomplete battles and set the speed to x4 in cheat engine and it still took 1.5 hours to go from level 25 to 30) A lot of the abilities feel like copies of each other with a different coat of paint.[Abilities]The abilities boil down to:-Do damage (usually one big finishing move or a multi attack chip damage)- Damage over time (fire, poison, chill effects. All pretty much the same)-Heal-Shield (adds a second health bar)-Buffs and debuffs (just change percents on damage or chance to hit)[Combat]The combat is super fun to start out, but once you get into it, you'll realize the best way to win battles is just stacking damage over time effects while healing your own monsters. Damage dealing moves are still relevant, but just don't pack a punch. They usually do (with buffs) about 20-40% of a normal enemy's health and you don't get that same anticipation and reward as say a 3x sword danced pokemon one shotting anything in its path (which I feel is pretty comparable.) [Story]There definitely is a story and it's similar in quality if not better than old monster fighting rpgs like pokemon or DWM. [Final Thoughts]This game is fun. It is very fun for the first several hours, but it desperately needs more variety. Everything begins to feel the same and you find yourself mindlessly completing encounters or skipping them all together. Definitely give it a try if you like similar games.[Note to the Devs]Please, please, please add breeding mechanics to this game. They would make collecting monsters so much more fun, especially if there were powerful monsters you could only obtain through breeding. An online breeding feature would be even more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: i absolutely adore this game and everything about itexcellent visual style, monster mechanics that make you have to think about how to build your team and large build diversity for each monster.also one of the few games i've played where damage over time effects have felt Goodcan't recommend it enough
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: You know how sometimes you hear an elevator pitch for a game and think "this game attacked me personally"?Not only does this game have pet-collecting with cool designs, there is tons of exploration and most importantly a very tactical battle system. The talent trees are huge, and every new pet brings on a ton of new brainstorming for new options.Example: I got a fungus-creature that had an Aura that allowed poison to be stackable an additional 2 times. Immediately I remembered another monster that had that Aura and rushed to put them in a party together to see if I could stack poison up to 5 times. It worked!None of the monsters feel worthless or weak, and different areas required different strategies so I was always changing up my team.It's in Early Access, so the story isn't complete, but I found myself continuing to play even after "finishing" it just getting new sets of monsters to level-cap(36) to try out more combos.10/10 would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I played the demo a long time ago and was instantly captured by the gameplay. Monsters are cleverly designed, battle is simple and easy to grasp but not without strategy, and story (so far) is well developed.The only complaint that I have is with the UI during battles. I wish there was a way to see your monsters stats during the battle such as their physic, magical, defense, mana, etc. I know you can check the stats of your enemies, but being able to also see your stats would be beneficial. Other than that, highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Well ive finished the whole game, got basically every monster, its fun BUT the only thing that I'd have to complain about is that the champion monsters (boss monsters that you can get) suck (except for like. . . 2 or 3 of them), like their absolute garbage, their skills look good on paper but over all the common monsters that you find in the first area with a good set up can just destroy everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I love creature collecting and battling games.This game requires much more strategy to be able to beat some battles.I like that this game is more challenging than most other creature collector games.I like that you have to look at the skills and figure out who will work well together in a team. And not just press the one super move ability all the time to win like other games.Though at times I found it overly difficult.The difficulty is all over the place and not consistant. With Zosimos being harder to beat than the last boss which was very easy compared to him.I like that you don't have to constantly heal your monsters after battle.I like exploring and discovering but the areas are too maze like and boring looking.Not a fan of the  puzzles. It's not fun and more annoying and unecessary content.This game is alright, it's quite a unique game but areas just look boring and uninteresting with not much of a story.The areas and story are a bit of a let down. I'd rate it as a slightly above average game as it has some good stand out things but also things I don't like. I am on the fence about this game as it felt tedious,  boring  and a slog at times and I hated some of the puzzles. But I felt compelled to keep pushing on and was obsessed about collecting all creatures but didn't as it got boring. It's a bit disappointing that only a very few can be evolved and I don't like the game enough to play through it more than once. Don't think I can recommend as I can't stand the thought of playing it again and feel a feeling of relief that the game is finally completed and can try and find something better to play.I'd rate it  6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: In my book this is the best game in the monster collecting sub-genre at the moment. Making the monsters abilities the "keys" that unlock new areas ties in the theme of the game very nicely with the metroidvania style of level design. Where genre leaders stubbornly refuse to innovate, Monster Sanctuary brings in a lot of new ideas and executes them very well for the most part.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is been a very unique take on the monster collector genre.The metroidvania aspect with platforming and exploration gives it a bit of that hunting feel, looking for new frontiers and monsters to add to your own ranks.Combat being fully 3 vs 3 all the way through not only adds a lot of combinations but the skilltrees each monster has also means the specializations really feeds into it, giving things a lot more depth and complexity which I personally tend to look for in the genre.For those interested there is also PVP, though I have not tested that personally.If you enjoy exploring a beautiful world and more complexity in combat this game is an absolute steal at any price.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: DLC was fun, but shorter than expected. I guess it's free so there's nothing to complain about but I sure wish there were more dinosaurs!With the increased level cap I finally managed to complete the base game and become Keeper Master (I suck). It is hard to level new monsters to build teams around some of the end-game and champion fights-- but at some point a patch made it so that leveling your monsters past the cap gave you infinite rare candies instead of just one, which was very helpful.As a monster battler it's great. As a metroidvania it's pretty good. I clocked in 35 hours and I definitely think it was worth it, though I'm not trying to get the remaining 9 achievments.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 This game is amazing. It has so much potential and I love the leveling system, the stacking food effects, items and upgrades. Highly recommend. My only concern is the balance on some monster abilities. You can only enter combat with 3 monsters, and some combos I want to pull off i cant without sacrificing damage or defense. _childDocuments_.review: I honestly wanted to enjoy this game, but it just has a hard time hooking me in any meaningful way. Most of the battles feel like a cycle of healing and slowly chipping enemy health down, or the enemy team just completely wipes out my underleveled monsters. The different strengths and weaknesses don't provide that interesting of gameplay to me as they are very rock-paper-scissors focused instead of something like Transistor where you mix and combine abilities to create unique outcomes to situations. Overall, it's got a decent idea, but just lacks any fun level of unique thinking and finds me mashing buttons to get through battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid turn-based battle system, monsters are varied and interesting, and more importantly, late-game monsters are not automatically stronger than the monsters you found early on; that's not just "you CAN beat the game with a butterfree and a raticate, but it's a dumb idea", that's "You can genuinely make solid endgame teams with early-game monsters".Out-of-battle RNG can be compensated for and overcome; there is no RNG in monster stat distribution, and no items are RNG-only or wholly-missable thanks to various systems in place.Story is forgettable but doesn't get in the way of gameplay and isn't bad.Map exploration is good, use of monsters as metroidvania exploration powers is a fun quirk.Looking forward to NG+ mode soon to be implemented, which will allow you to replay with your full monster collection from lv1, on a higher difficulty. Edit: NG+ mode is as good as expected.Not just a good game, but a game where the devs have put in various anti-frustration features without making the game too easy or exploitable. Solid recommendation if it looks like your kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a LOT OF FUN, but definitely not for the casual gamer even with the "casual" mode option. Once you get about half-way through the game it really pushes you to make proper builds and take the time to understand all the synergies between the monsters. That alone kind of pushes things a bit above casual game-play, then near end-game the difficulty imo gets BROKEN. There is a lot of creative stacks you have to do to actually BEAT the game, this isn't like an optional boss or anything, the last two to three bosses and even leading up to the final boss get exceptionally difficult for the average gamer. I had a lot of fun, but to me it kind of ruined the experience. Game plays basically like a metroidvania game, but you have monsters you collect up and fight other monsters in turn-based combat. The game itself is fun, learning curve majorly ramps up though. Lots of fun optional things you can do. Biggest gripe I think I have with this game is the weird imbalance towards end-game, and the annoyance of getting 100% of achievements requires a lot of tweaking of builds. If you're an achievement seeker though, 100%'ing this game will be REALLY satisfying.In short, worthwhile on sale but be ready for a brutal experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I try to keep abrest of various Pokemon-Alikes on Steam, as a fan of the genre, and that's how I got recommended this one by a friend. This game... I don't know if I'd agree with calling it a Pokemon-alike exactly, but I do like it, and I like it a lot, and I think that willingness to be its own thing with its own identity is a big part of why I like it a lot.The Turn-based combat system seems solid, I'm looking forward to it really kicking my ass as the game does on, because it looks like it's gonna get ready to, and I like the abilities to customise my monsters. I like the idea of having actual builds for my monsters, that's not something I've really seen from the genre, and it's interesting, though this system I do feel like I'm dreading screwing it up more than I'm excited to make something synergistic and fun, but hopefully that's just the early levels where I have fewer choices.I was also not expecting to enjoy the Metroidvania world design as much as I am, but it's neat, and I like exploring for secrets and loot and monsters, and I feel like the best endorsement I can give this game is that in typing that, I just realized a spot on the map where I think I can go back now and find a rare monster to add to my team, and now I'm totally gonna go do that.Game is good, and this being steam, you'll get an opportunity to buy it for cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It may not be perfect, but it's extremely well done. Growing up, two of my favorite games were Super Metroid and the original Pokemon; this is a beautiful marriage of both of those and well worth playing.The combat system is surprisingly robust and the game will definitely challenge you at times. Getting wiped by a boss later on in the game can be a real bummer, as these battles with other trainers get to be very long. But it is so rewarding to come back with a better strategy/lineup and take them down. Really love the battle system here, it's the highlight of the game for sure.The Metroidvania aspect is also pretty well fleshed out. It isn't full on Super Metroid level of exploration(of course,) but it's fun to get the power-up to finally unlock a new area. The idea of your pets giving you these abilities is awesome too and it does call to mind both Pokemon and even Golden Sun as well as the aforementioned Super Metroid. Graphics are great, the game has a lot of charm. I love the visual designs of the levels and areas and most of the monsters also look awesome. The story is respectable and does at least give a fresh take on the formula. It isn't overly dialogue heavy like some similar games tend to be, but there's enough story there to keep you on track and engaged.It isn't perfect though and there are some faults, but I consider them all to be pretty minor. It took me a while to get used to the floaty controls. But the platforming here is pretty tame and you do adapt to it just fine. But there was definitely a period where I had to adjust to it. And while the story is fine, it's certainly a weaker point of the game. But outside of these two things, I can't really complain.With all that said, highly recommend this game and I think if you are the type of person(like me) who sees a preview/trailer for this game and thinks that it looks up their alley. You should totally get it, I feel pretty confident that you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great turn based pet battler game.  Lots of interesting creatures to pick from.  Evolutions, equipment, skill trees, this game has alot of team min-maxing and customizing.  I had alot of fun coming up with strong team compositions.  The musics enjoyable, the scenery is nice.  Interesting enough story that kept me playing. The pacing was fair too - Didn't have to overly grind levels, and when I beat the game, was just about around max level.  Optional side bosses were a solid challenge.  Overall, worth a play thru if you like Pokemon, and don't mind 'metroidvania' platforming.  One complaint.  Found some puzzles VERY annoying and frustrating to do.  But other than that, wonderful game. Glad to have played it.

And once you beat the sun place and get shifted monsters, even more fun.There's duels, bosses, regular mobs, and platformer puzzles.  There's also online play (haven't tried it yet), as well as infinite dungeon (which I also haven't tried.)If you don't like the demo: You won't enjoy the full game.Demo save carries over to full version, effortlessly. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I was so inebriated when I wrote the last review I decided to rewrite it into something comprehensible.This is hands down the best monster catcher game.Every single monster from start to finish serves a unique purpose in combat, there's no monster that's functionally worthless until it evolves and you don't find another monster later that invalidates one you've been using for a while. Rather you will find a monster who trades off a couple of good passives or attacks for a few others and it's all set up specifically so that there's always a scenario where your best choice is your favourite or that a particular support can make a monster that otherwise seems bad into the best for a few particular fights.Combat is actually fun, it's strategy team based combat where you don't win by just playing rock paper scissors which is refreshing for the genre, bosses and rival trainers will regularly flatten your team not because you aren't high enough level or you didn't get the right element on your monster but because they have a strategy that forces a swap. The first rival trainer fight that beat me was spamming buff removal attacks and I was trying to stack defensive buffs at the time.The game regularly rewards you with cool ♥♥♥♥ that changes how you evaluate your monsters for combat. After the first third or so of the game you unlock "shifting" which is shinies. Except that each monster has 2 shiny variants that are functionally different from the base colors with unique stats and abilities. Also you can change the shiny variants you have so no need to grind endlessly, the spawn rate for them is 1/4 so even if you did want to grind it's bearable. There are others as well I won't mention to avoid spoilers for those who don't want to know everything the game has before starting.The campaign of the game genuinely does last about 30 hours and is a ton of fun start to finish with a story that's actually interesting at times, something I can't say about any other catcher game.The only complaint I can even make is that there's two monster designs I don't like. That's pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome, I can safely say this is the best game I own.

Its a me problem, but beside this, this game has a very splid soundtrack and very cool designs. For the more hardcore fans for the genre, this is a game for you.

Each monster has it's own skill tree and equipment so you can easily start mentally deciding what role or strategy its going to fulfill in your team which is really enjoyable.There's not a lot of story and it's fairly stereotypical, I found myself wanting to skip through even what little it had just to get to the gameplay again.Some reviews mention the difficulty ramps up, but it's been challenging but manageable for me so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is an underrated Creature Collector game.I disagree with some negative comments saying the game gets unpredictably hard.Just pay attention to different types of monsters and their gear.The story is okey, the world design is cute and unlocking different areas with new monster dependent travel options is neat.I would recommend the game if you enjoyed any edition of Pokémon or equivalent games.Solid 10/10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fascinating game so far!  You fight and gather monsters, and can use the monsters abilities to reach new places in a large 2D platformer kinda map.  It's like a metroidvania rpg with pokemon!  kinda... It's interesting.  Instead of set abilities for each level there are skill trees where you can mix and match what abilities you'd like.  You could dynamically change the monster based on what you choose.  Make it a healer, an enhancer/support, or a tank with 5 different elemental attacks!  I've only been playing for a few days so there might be more to this... but for now I def think it's worth looking into!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing.The monster classes are exactly the right mix of complexity, depth, and understandable.  you have a lot of very meaningful options, without becoming too bogged down in minutia.  The best combat system in any monster raising game I've ever playedThe exploration is fun with interesting puzzles, without being onerously difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary provides a large world for you to explore, one that both conjures to mind nostalgia as it call upon your adventurous side. With over 101 different monsters you can collect - literally any enemy you face can become a party member, albeit champion monsters become a more balanced version, and each one offering at least 2 different playstyles, this game lets Pokemon meet Metroidvania, while adding some great JRPG flair. Of course, it offers its own dash of originality to the game!If you like both platformers and Tactical RPGs, this title is a must-get, offering at least 40 hours of gameplay if you want to have and see it all - and quite a bit of replay value, in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this one. The animations are nice and movement feels smooth, but the combat feels flat because you'll always know exactly what will happen in advance. The repetitiveness wouldn't be an issue (given the type of game this is) if it wasn't for one thing that made me uninstall very quickly: The music. This is the most haphazard collection of notes I have heard in a while. And while the exploration theme is "just" bad, the combat theme seals the deal as not only do you have to listen to it practically all the time, and it's very short and repetitive, but it's also incredibly obnoxious and just plain incompetently written. You *can* mix major and minor in a song, but you can't just throw in major chords at random. Monotonous repeating string hits don't make a theme feel tense. Of course you could just turn off the music, but at that point why bother? This music sounds like it was generated by AI.You can buy the soundtrack separately if you are in the torturing business.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and a nice mix of different elements from genres that you wouldn't really expect. The platforming stuff is a fun way to break up fights every once in while and some light puzzle elements throw an additional twist. The amount of monsters in the game is great and the Devs are good at keeping us all up to date on what's going on and what changes are planned. I've enjoyed everything I've played and I'll be continuing my play through every update that comes along.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't this much fun with a game for a while - it's well thought out with the monster's balance, enjoyable with its huge variety of monsters which seem to be useful in most of team compositions and the exploration aspect of the game really gets you with that "Ooooh, I need to hatch that" thing. Can't wait for the DLC to come out!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of the best monster battle games I have played. However, and a big, however, the general design of the game needs a ton of rework before launch. I constantly feel while playing the game, that everything is an afterthought. It's like reading a book were the author constantly fills in the backstory as he goes along. The level design is so frustrating it nearly made me quit playing multiple times. A lot of the "difficulty" comes from getting to a point in the story and having the game tell you "Oh you don't have xyz item now go back and get it, return here then after getting that thing you should have had but didn't know you needed until you got here, then and only then can you can proceed"With what I just said and in the insane amount of contradiction between the opening statement and what followed. You you bet that the game must have done something right. It did, the combat, the monsters the exploration, the art. It's nothing short of amazing. It feels like playing pokemon as an adult, on PC, with a fresh new battle system. These things hold the game above the water created by its misgivings. Yes, it is still an amazing game despite the shortcomings that would normally make me uninstall within the first hour of playtime and as of writing this review I have over 40 hours logged because its just so bloody good.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a blast to play, and even to 100%. It has a great stratagy element to it, platforming from the old days, and unlocking new skills and moves makes your mind run with excitement about what you can do next or what your team comp might be now!Playing threw this my main team changed many times as my knowledge of the game grew, and seeing and unlocking more monsters to fight with. Trying to 100% this wasn't hard either,  seeing my Significant other playing this on her switch, she saw how much I was enjoying it and got it for me on Steam, Since I try to 100% games before moving onto the next one. The end game wasn't bad either, and plenty of guides here will help you get 100% if you're aiming for that, just remember where you saw new skill locations to revisit them later to unlock new items and monsters!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is awesome, the only reason it has negative reviews is the late game difficulty but the satisfaction makes it worthwhile.I've never reviewed a game before but this might be a perfect game. When you start the game is super simple and easy to let you start understanding mechanics. The difficulty curve is perfect so that you are constantly pushed to improve but never overwhelmed, until around level 30. The difficult spike is huge & got pretty frustrating trying several strategies before I could continue. Once you find a strategy that works at that level (as a side point, there are A LOT of strategies you can use so it doesn't feel limiting at all) it's extremely rewarding though. The game is also under active development with balance changes & free DLC being released.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredible, much more fun than any of the last Pokemon games. The skill trees for each monster is unique, inventive and unlike any RPG I've played before, a fair warning there is a difficulty curve but there's no penalty for failing thus you can try out new strategies over and over. The variety of combos which each monster team you can make is incredible. Highly recommend this game, especially for RPG lovers looking for something a little different. o3obbb
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on Switch, rebought it years later for my Steam Deck. It's that good.Fantastic pixel art and colors, fun metroidvania puzzles and a great map that lets you place labeled markers. Deep and well-designed mechanics that really encourage tactical play at high levels and allow for lots of great synergistic team-building.My hours are so inflated because I just love building new teams and testing them out. I keep coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and solid game that's brought down by a small number of issues.The game progression (as of writing this review) feels very formulaic as you enter a new biome, catch all monsters, defeat the boss, go to next area. I am currently in the fifth or sixth biome and have uncovered half the map. Due to monster variety, and their exploration skills, comes dyslexia as you wander around the world while carrying several pokeboxes worth of monsters with you (while in Pokemon you would find those boxes in the Pokecenter). This freedom is welcome as you always have all skills with you but you slowly realize that it makes menuing needlessly complex. There are options to leave monster behind or at day care but the UI is visible straining because on that screen you do not know which monster has which skills so you go back and forth from main menu to day care deposit. Overworld battles are dmg over everything and you are motivated into doing the monotonous skill rotation combo until the enemies are defeated. For bosses however, you are punished for not building defensively. So either you have specific boss-only monsters that are permanently benched while on overworld, or you build some weird mix-builds which makes the overworld monsters needlessly hard. Exploration is nice and the metroidvania effect is wonderfully settled in but the platforming is made by platforming experts (sometimes we need pixelperfect jumps and hover application for those chests), and the switch puzzles are merciless and not fun. The minimap needs some more QoL like the ability to place markers. It's hard to keep track if a maptile is fully explored or waiting for a specific monster's exploration ability. Lastly, if your monster is not part of the 6-unit team, they do not earn exp. But only 3 of them are constantly fighting while the other 3 are benched, that's why it's uncommon to really care for equipment for inactive monsters outside of squad battles (6v6, very rare occurence). It becomes apparent that from the vast roster of available monsters, you never actually have a need to switch and just try them out. They need to be skill levelled and they also require equipment, and if you split your exp on too many units, you will be forced to grind to make up for it. Remember specific pokemon from the first generations, the one that you only carry around because they learned HMs? Monster Sanctuary embraced this mindset.In the end, this game feels nice to play and there is always a small excitement of getting new eggs, checking their skill trees and also their exploration skill. Although transparency in regard to monster roster is not well thought out, this game is definitely worth it if you ever see it on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: ep combat system where you have fairly standard stuff like weaknesses and resistances, various attack elements (like fire, air...), attack types (physical, magical), and debuffs (like weakness or poison), but all of this is then juggled on top of a combo system where each hit adds to the next hits effectiveness. There are some Metroidvania elements present; when you collect monsters they can be "equipped" to follow you and each one gives you an extra power like 'break through walls', 'glide', 'burn vines', etc. that allow you to progress to other areas. The world feels large and the zones feel unique. The story is pretty basic and the dialog is weak, but it keeps everything moving along nicely while giving me a reason to catch 'em all. My only gripe is the imbalance of 3-4 of the encounters; they are WAY harder than the rest of the game and end up making the final boss look like a pushover.
