_childDocuments_.review: I've now finished the game and gotten all the achievements, and I felt like this was a really good game so I'm gonna share some of my thoughtsExplorationThe metroidvania aspect of this game is really fun, getting new monsters and getting new abillities to use in the world is a really fun mechanic, as well as just the exploration of all the zones and new creatures. Probably my favorite part.CombatI like how the 3v3 mechanic gives you more flexibility to come up with new strategies, and the fact that all monsters are viable in different compositions is awesome, and means you don't have to abandon one of your favorites as you progress in the game. I also liked the fact that you don't have to heal up your party everytime you fight, due to them being replenished automatically, which makes the pace of the game feel faster. The StoryThe story and the characters were okay, nothing revolutionary. You have the classic archetypes of nerdy friend who helps you, your frustrating rival, you're supportive rival, and the big bad group of people trying to do something devious. It's not the focus of the game and that's okay, it's just there for the progress of the game. The dlc zone has some interesting story, I just wish the characters were fleshed out a bit more, and perhaps a bit more creative liberties with the world.AtmosphereThe artstyle and monsters are super cool and cozy at the same time. It some parts the music was really great, but I felt like there could have been more sound effects and some more soundtracks for different parts of environments. About halfway through the game I felt like I was super outmatched by the npc's, even though I outleveled them, so I took a break. If I'd give some advice to avoid this happening: spend some time choosing some of your favorite monsters and making a team that synergises really well. If you manage to do that you can take down opponents much higher leveled that you, and it's super satisfying seeing all the pieces of your team synergize and dominating battles.Overall I'd give the game an 8/10. It feels like a game fueled by passion, and it excels at the fundamentals, exploration and battle mechanics. Only parts that are lacking in my opinion are the characters, story and sound design in some places.

This is probably the closest thing PC has to pokemon and for some that will be enough to pull them through but really the game feels half-baked in too many ways.Metroidvania seems arbitrarily tacked on as platforming is really bad in this game. The controls are janky with not the most appealing graphics, graphically this game is bland as hell, with uninspiring music, badly written story + characters, it seems virtually everything except the monster battling part of the game is either forced or nowhere near finished / developed enough. A good RPG, especially ones in the JRPG vein, is vastly complimented by far more than simply the battle system. It doesn't feel like art. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Game with very interesting team building. Metroidvenia Aspects are OK (coming from someone who does not like Metroidvenias). _childDocuments_.review: Very promising game.  One of the best Early Access games I've played by far.Simple to understand and play through, but definitely has depth. Has a good story (and even 4 pages of lore for each monster), but not hard to follow.Pretty well balanced.  There isn't really any OP 1 shot champs.  It forces you to play smart to get 5-6 stars.Variety, variety, variety.  Has around 80ish monsters right now and level 38 cap with 6 man teams (3 for pve battles). _childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary. A game developed by Moi Rai Games and published by Team17.I have at the time of this review currently allotted 20 hours into this game, Perhaps enough to give a realistic and fair assessment of the game in its current form.I have always been, for as long as i can remember. A deep and intense lover of monster collector games, Such as Pokemon and Digimon. I've spent many long hours with Tamagotchi's and Virtual Pets, collecting, battling and breeding them. So i like to think of myself as a rather devoted gamer to this genre. Monster Sanctuary scratches this itch for me in many ways and helps improve and reinvent the genre with its own personal twist. Although Monster Sanctuary does indeed have a relatively unique story, In these games it always feels as though it's playing second fiddle to the gameplay. Which makes a lot of sense, the fun here is collecting the monsters and fighting them against each other. Levelling them up and proving you can be the best in the world.Monster Sanctuary provides a story that isn't too deep that you will be distracted from the game itself, but also not shallow enough that you will want to ignore it entirely. You are (Generic Monster Hunter <Insert Name Here>) Battling and Collecting to be the best, but whilst doing so you uncover a horrible secret and events that could threaten all life as you know it. Building your team is now more important than ever to stop the disaster that awaits on the horizon. The dialogue is well written and presented well to you through discussions with both people and monster alike, I would have liked perhaps a few written history lore notes as well to help flesh out the world as i feel there is a lot of room for it. But that is simply a knit pick. As a purely monster collecting game, Monster Sanctuary is a well designed and scripted game, There are (at the moment of this review) 101 monsters to find and collect scattered across the world. Varying in type and element, Vastly multiplying your possible team combinations considerably. While you are exploring this considerably large (Approximately 15 diverse regions) you will eventually get bored of your current surrounding, Personally having spent about 15 hours in the starting area exploring every nook it has hidden, I got bored of the verdant green and hilly landscape and yearned for something more, The following areas, somewhat resembling a brick fortress, almost immediately made me wish i was back outside, but how diverse the landscapes are has stuck with me. Now when i started this review i did promise something that would make this unique in the genre and at last here we are, 1 portion of why this game has stood out to me so far. The items. Monster Sanctuary functions as most would expect any monster collector to function. That your monster is only as powerful as it is. In Monster Sanctuary this isn't the case, You can equip each monster in your team of 6 with 1 weapon (That can be upgraded) and 3 items that also vary in stats and usefulness depending on how you want to build that particular monster. Cool right? So say you want to completely rework a monster, make it function completely differently, That is a complete possibility. Tired of having 3 damage dealers and want a support and healer, Swap some items and bam you now have a functional buffer and healer in your team!  And another excitingly unique aspect to Monster Sanctuary. The skill trees. Yes you heard me right, Monster collector fans. SKILL TREES!!! This completely took the game for me to a whole new level. Not only is there already vast ways to change your monsters individually, you can specifically build them how you want to play, Respec them and try a totally separate style. While i'm not a huge fan of online competition anymore,I do recognise its requirement in the gaming category, So while i don't personally enjoy it, i do enjoy seeing it in games of this type. It adds a lot more replayability and customisation to the game, especially when you have a real person to compete with rather than just an AI. In saying that as well, Monster Sanctuary also provides a considerable amount of in game challenges as well for the hungry monster keepers out there in need of a challenge to sate their appetite. Now i'm not saying that Monster Sanctuary is particularly hard, or that having the game being hard is bad. But by about 10 hours in the game throws some low blows at you that can if you haven't built your monsters smart, can become quite a blockade for you, and might even make you put the game aside. Once you are past this initial hurdle and start acquiring additional skills, this becomes less of a concern but in those early moments it can be quite frustrating. This is probably the only thing that bothered me in this game to this point so far, that has caused the gameplay score to take a dip. The turn queuing, Although it is done well in a purely "on paper" standpoint, it feels as though some aspects of its allocating have been done in the favour of game difficulty rather than enjoyment. This isn't a particular bad thing in most cases, but when you are farming XP, items or gold for hours and you encounter this repeatedly in every fight, It begins to become more and more cumbersome. (Main concern is that enemies will be gifted heals before they receive their debuff damage or you will miss a turn for no particular reason).This was a hard category to detail, as this is a pixel based turn based monster collecting game. There really isn't a lot of graphical power here to offer a standpoint on. The game looks beautiful for its art style and genre. It plays extremely smoothly and has not once dropped below its capped frame rate (Current refresh of 143). My only qualm is that despite it being a pixelated art style the game doesn't have any options to sharpen its edges or provide higher resolution or detail. A touch that would have pushed this ahead in this category in my opinion. (Current PC specs are in my profile)While the visuals weren't much to talk about, The audio has plenty. Monster Sanctuary has a beautiful crafted audio palette, A vast array of recording sound bytes for a number of different skills that make each one feel unique and powerful in its own right, to an overwhelmingly detailed soundtrack that seems to capture the environments subtle details and extend them well past what was visually possible in this art style. The audio here has been lovingly and passionately designed and it shows in every single moment. Lost a point due to its lack of depth though, There isn't much more beyond its monster skills sounds and background music.Monster Sanctuary does an amazing job of holding true to the fundamental game play mechanics of any monster collector game, Although it doesn't reinvent the wheel it certainly revolutionised it and provided its own take on a realistically over saturated game market. The implementation of its skill and inventory options provide a vast amount of customisation to the genre and help flesh out its content considerably more than you would anticipate. Coupled with its bright and colourful art style and wonderfully orchestrated soundtrack, this is a journey you simply have to experience if the style fits your mood.Your journey to becoming a Master Keeper has just begun!

_childDocuments_.review: I've primarily played this on the Switch so my time here's low but I liked it so much I wanted to have it on Steam too!This is a great monster tamer with interesting creature designs and combat much deeper than any other in genre. Builds have a lot of fiddly things that go in to them, which can be either good or bad, but until the very end-game I felt it was at a satisfying spot for someone who likes team synergy but doesn't enjoy optimizing every little thing. I put it down at the end boss because it was too difficult for the teams I had already raised and didn't want to rebuild and reoptimize everything, but I felt the balance was at a good spot other than the very last encounter. The difficulty does jump up quite drastically throughout the game but it's nice to have a difficult game in a genre that's otherwise filled with cakewalks.The metroidvania layout was satisfying to me since I'm a huge fan of exploration but it's not the best example of the genre. I think it adds something nice to break up the combats and monster catching that other collector games tend to lack. Definitely enjoyed it more than I would have a more linear platformer or top-down RPG.The dev's been tweaking things post-launch pretty well and seems great overall. Totally give this a try if you're an RPG/monster collector fan!

_childDocuments_.review: Art Work/Music-9.5/10Story------------6.5/10Game Play------8.5/10Artwork (9.5)The developer clearly put a lot of love into the animations and individual sprite-work and animations. Music was mostly fitting and didn't feel intrusive. Minus half point due to no songs being particularly memorable.Story (6.5)This is just put together enough to be called a solid story with no weird continuity errors. Game play (8.5)-.5 slightly grindy, -.5 minor unrewarded play time, -.5 creativity inhibitorsPart 1 battlingVery solid Monster RPG battler that encourages synergy and thought in team building and didn't feel particularly unfair at any point. This game is punishing if you are unfamiliar with RPG synergy set ups, but is very easily beatable with almost any team with 2-3 tanks/heal tanks on it. The main issues I have are that if you are constantly given a stream of monster and trying to get them to level up to try new team combos is a bit of a pain this could have been circumvented by just having the player gain xp then have the monsters just have skill points equal to your level. Additionally, the moves and items feel a little on the generic side which is semi-forgivable due to the size of the game but does mean that a lot of monsters feel samey until about level 20 at which point you have mostly picked favorites and don’t want to grind up older monsters unless you are a big numbers fan. My biggest gripe with the gameplay is the battle tower bosses as if you are trying to get that 5-star egg drop you can waste literal hours trying to get a perfect score and not get any gold, xp or items to show for it.Part 2 platformingVery solid I never got stuck or locked out anywhere and the timer puzzles were incredibly tight on timing. This did however did lead to me attempting to beat timers that were unbeatable without a mount resulting in about 30-45 minutes of trying to beat timers.Part 3 MetroidvaniaWhile cool in theory using monster abilities for exploring was often a little confusing on which monster I needed to grab to get through a certain puzzle. While this didn’t block story progress as you only need 2 abilities to beat the game it did making exploring less fun. I would recommend either replacing this mechanic with tools received from bosses rather than trying to grind for a specific type of fish egg. Additionally even if you have a monster specifically meant to get into certain rooms the rewards tend to be pretty lackluster often being random crafting materials or foods I would recommend redoing the chests to contain a unique item and perhaps a “trade deal” contract that allows you to buy new things at the base and leave the generic items as monster drops.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic, masterfully done monster tamer that really shows off the genre's potential.Let me get my major issues off first. The story is mostly generic and uninteresting. It's essentially a good vs. evil story with a bunch of doohickeys to collect in between. Every character's dialogue also feels like they're coming from the same mouth. I feel that the dialogue could've been more varied if more characters had distinct speech patterns (like have the shy character stutter more or have my toad partner say "ribbit" every now and then or something) or emote more (either by way of character animations or speech bubbles with emoticons that pop over a character's head). NPC dialogue in general is also mostly explaining some game mechanic, rarely giving any lore or world building text. One of the best parts of Pokémon for me are the NPCs that just talk about hanging out and living in a world with Pokémon, something that this game is really missing. The combination of these issues makes the world hard to connect with overall. They make the world feel like a world that exists in service of the player, rather than a world that exists in spite of the player.I found the metroidvania aspects of the game fine. It's mostly just standard jumping and backtracking, though I do love how you actually use your team's abilities to solve puzzles and clear obstacles. It's a much better mechanic than the HMs in Pokémon. The soundtrack is okay, though not particularly memorable. I think the boss music straight up sucks and doesn't fit a lot of the game's fights.Now, for what the game does great: the gameplay. Right off the bat, this game is not for casual players, despite it having a "Casual" difficulty level. Don't go into this game expecting a Pokémon-like experience where you simply choose your favorite creatures, then overlevel or catch a legendary to complete it. You WILL run into trouble if you play the game this way. At the same time, the game isn't nearly as complex as people in other reviews as stating, as least for me. Most of the combat mechanics in isolation are pretty straightforward. The hardest part of the game is figuring out synergies that would work between your creatures, while still making sure your team has enough damage, healing, shielding, and buffs. It's not uncommon for your entire team to have the singular goal of supporting one creature or mechanic. You find yourself swapping in other creatures or respeccing to handle different enemy teams. This theory crafting and constant team building is the best part of the game, and the game mechanics are smartly designed around this with the hatching and experience catch-up mechanics. Nothing feels better than finally figuring out a team that works and plowing through fights that you previously found tough. With that said, the game does get trivial once you do get your team figured out, but I find that more as your reward for smartly utilizing the game's mechanics.Graphics and pixel work are also super well done, some of the best of any pixel game I've played. Each area has its own color palette, and the monster animations in particular are smooth and give each monster a distinct personality.Great game. It's fairly cheap as well, so it's worth trying out if you're any bit interested.

_childDocuments_.review: Having purchased this game on day one of the Alpha release (8/28/2019), I am deeply impressed by the quality of this game already! As of writing this review, I have only progressed to the Blue Cave (the initial entry), and have not encountered any serious glitches - the only minor glitch I've seen is the occasional seemingly random presence of the Spectral Lion's fire (this being the starting monster I chose), where the lion isn't located. The fire is only present for a second or two before disappearing and doesn't appear to have any actual consequences.        Monster Sanctuary, as of now, has an interesting and fun combat system, an enjoyable exploration system (having a sense of freedom while also clearly providing a direction to progress), and well-designed monsters with interesting lore. All-in-all, I would certainly recommend this game, and can only hope it will get even better as updates are released.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best indie games I've played.It was the whole package for me. The RPG aspect is very deep and addicting. There are endless combinations and builds available to the player. All monsters have potential and it is nice to explore the possibilities. You'll get hooked after a few minutes in.

_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I legit cannot think of a single bad thing to say about this game, it feels like a masterpiece. The monster battling and collecting mechanics are enjoyable & engaging, exploration feels incredibly satisfying, especially the further in you get and the more abilities you acquire, the pixel graphics add such a unique charm to the game and the world building is also really solid, with multiple threads constantly pulling you and pushing you onward. Each of the different zones in the game have their own flare & style, making each one memorable. Hell, even backtracking to older areas with new abilities feels fun, and that's not something I feel every Metroidvania gets right.Whether you're someone who enjoys getting to explore a vast world, someone who likes to collect and fight alongside magical monsters, or just want to experience an interesting, fantastical story, do yourself a service and BUY THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted a monster trainer game where your monsters are like full-on party members? This is it. You name them, equip them, build their move & ability set, and they help you get around the terrain and solve puzzles. The combat is (usually) a 3v3 scenario which rewards team strategies and defensive strategies just as well as it does pure DPS ones.I'm about 10 hours in and still have a LOT to do. tl;dr - Good game. Worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and surprisingly polished monster collecting game. But with more promise than most.Unlike a fair bit of early access titles I've encountered thus far, this game has its primary, secondary, and tertiary gameplay loops down, has attractive animations and creature designs, suberb UI (which is something that I don't often notice) and is chock full of everything that a fan of the genre might be looking for.For full disclosure, it has turn based combat, type matchups, a mana system as opposed to an attack usage limit, evolutions for monsters (although less common than in pokemon), an equipment system, and integration of creature abilities into exploration.The most important thing to an early purchaser is that it is gameworthy even in its current form, and all signs point to it becoming strictly better.More than worth your spare 18 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game unless you  a "challenge"- and by challenge I mean min/maxing. As a person who has grown far beyond the epenor waving contests of his youth, I really just want a gaming experience that  trying to personally ruin my day with unnecessary "challenge." I just want to have fun. Being stonewalled by a scripted event until I craft the right team to beat it isn't fun. It means putting away the team that I enjoy playing to pickup a few monsters that just happen to have the right combination of abilities to abuse the weakness of said boss. And just- no. I hate having to play to enemy weaknesses. It turns the team of monsters that I've been naming and playing with into disposable utility pieces. It makes the game a min/max playthrough experience- and I am not here for that.I bought the game in early access and played it for a few hours before putting it down. I tried picking it back up again, but it's the same game. Nothing's changed. It's still this effort in min/maxing that devalues everything about making a team and going on an adventure. It's not fun. Sure, it has promise, but the devs aren't really interested in making the game more accessible. They say they're making a "casual" mode, but still maintaining the difficulty. Devs, if you're listening, not every gamer finds "challenge" fun- and just because  find min/maxing fun, doesn't mean every gamer does. Some of us just want to build a team, grind them up, and then stomp the endboss while cackling maniacally. If I had known this was the direction the game was going to take, I would have never bought it.Suffice it to say, I can't recommend the game.Edit. Alright, after messing with the defense stat on my monsters in an editor, I've found that a 200-250 range makes the game a hell of a lot more enjoyable. Instead of hitting a brickwall with the scripted duel bosses, they become more of a checkpoint to test whether you have the proper DPS, healing, and condition removal to continue. But, just because I can now enjoy the game, doesn't mean I recommend it. The game's difficulty isn't tuned very well- and battles usually end up as these long debuff/buff wars.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary.. I can't express how much I love this game. I'm not amazing at it, as my team building skills isn't entirely great, but I absolutely love this game. Pokemon feels far too easy these days, as everything feels handed to you to make everything too easy. While there are modes in Monster Sanctuary that lower the difficulty, if you play the game on normal difficulty, you'll be sure to find times where you might be stuck at a fight because of your team comp. It can be discouraging, but you can find new monsters that synergize with others, and make awesome/deadly teams that shred through the enemies. You might have to a couple times.Regardless, the monsters are either badass or just adorable, the amount of metroidvania feels super cool as well, as you'll find yourself going back to earlier areas to access rooms that you couldn't before. It's played out really smoothly, and it doesn't feel like you get an item just for one thing, just for it to be over with in a second (maybe besides the warm underwear, that's only used for one thing lol. But that's not exactly a bigger item like double jumping or upgraded flying, so it doesn't affect it all that much). Everything has it's purpose. There's a lot more stuff to do after the game ends, and while I personally don't think I'll ever become good enough to 5 star each champion monster, or catch each monster in general, I find the post game content to be fun to play. Some of the post game rewards feel a bit underwhelming, but some can actually help create perfect team compositions.So if you like Pokemon, you'll love this game. It packs a good challenge here and there, and there's a lot to love about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually, the game had a pretty good potential. It could be a pokemon-like game that can be enjoyed for a long time. I was hopeful. However, there are so many annoying platform elements in the game... I wanted to deal with my team dynamics, monsters and tactical issues. However, the game turned into an annoying jumping, running, hopping simulation. Unfortunately, for this very reason, the game quickly became unplayable for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good metroidvania game, and a good monster collector. Exploration feels good, although the game would benefit from some way to mark the map. Every monster species has its own skill trees and every monster feels like it could work well with the right team, and monsters give you access to different field abilities to help explore. The difficulty DOES ramp up, and by endgame you will probably have hit the level cap and will be fighting enemies that are also at the level cap (40).  You cannot brute force through fights by grinding levels, you need to pick your team and try to get a good synergy going. If you're into team building and want to optimize your monsters' skill trees, this is definitely the game for you.Edit to add: After some updates, the game is better than ever! There are some new options to make new playthroughs of the game a bit different, and some new monsters have been added that are very fun to teambuild with. There is also now a way to mark the map, making exploration a bit easier for folks like me with bad memories.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was looking for something similar to Pokemon and I can say I was not disappointed.This is a surprisingly deep game. It challenges you throughout your whole playthrough and you will have to adept to different circumstances at all times.One team will hardly be enough, at least it wasn't for me. The Jump and Run aspect of the game was fun enough, even though I am not a big fan of the genre.Graphics are what you can expect from an 8 bit game. There is a lot of content and it took me almost 60 hours to play through the game.I guess you can do it in less time.Enough said.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The story is very much like Pokemon, kinda cheesy and nonsensical but still fun. The 3v3 battles lead you to come up with builds and strategies that can involve monsters you previously disregarded because you ran into another monster that opens up a completely different play style. The music is extremely good. I was vibing with every background and battle OST.My only gripe with it is there exists sudden difficulty cliffs. You could have a team that wipes the previous bosses/trainer fights and suddenly run into a hard counter that decimates yours. It could be very hard to figure out how to proceed and grinding for materials to upgrade equipment can be a chore. When this happens, the path of least resistance is to radically change your play style to accommodate the fight. It's definitely a game that forces you to adapt.Overall, a very satisfying strategy RPG. It reminded me of playing Pokemon as a kid but with infinitely more depth in monster builds.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a great mix of genres. It's both an RPG not unlike Pokemon and a Metroidvania. You are an aspiring monster hunter/collecter who has to find out the mystery of the rising Champion Monsters. Pixel style, turn-based combat, 6 monsters for your team, overworld abilities to reach further areas, and leveling/customization. There's quite a lot of mechanics going on and it's really neat. _childDocuments_.review: I  had this game on my wishlist forever but kept hming and hawing over getting but boy am I happy that I finally did.  I feel like I keep getting burned on triple A games that over promise but under deliver and this game did the exact opposite.  It's a simple concept but with a lot of additional depth.Exploration wise it's a 2D metroidvania game with lite puzzles, but the true meat of the game is the monster collection, team building, and battles.  There are a ton of monsters and you can form a team with and the combinations and strategies are incredibly varied.Don't be afraid to try new monsters and new team set ups either!  Whenever you hatch a new monster it's only a few levels below your max level monster so it makes it pretty friendly to switch out and try new teams.  I found that once you start getting lvl 20 monster skills it opens whole new team synergies and a lot of really cool team setups become available.  And then again when you start getting some of the high rarity equipment more teams open up that wouldn't have seemed possible before.And the devs are still making free new content updates!  Definitely a lot of fun and a lot of stuff to do, highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying my first 5h with this game a lot. The art and animations are adorable, the monsters are charming as heck, there's a neat story, I don't love platforming but it's so forgiving in this game that I didn't mind trying a few times to get the jumps right. But. The difficulty. Is just ungodly. I set it to casual. A game should not be this difficult when set to casual. This isn't Darksouls. Why do all games these days try to emulate Darksouls and hit you over the head with frustrating difficulty? I don't care about optimizing strategy. I just wanted a cute, fun pixel game and collect adorable pets! It's fine if there's a hard mode for people who want it, but why can't easy actually be easy?? After getting absolutely bodied multiple times by two different bosses, I just don't care anymore. I already have a job that makes me cry.It's a real shame because, as I said, up until the Dungeon I was doing fine and having fun. But oh well. If you're like me and you're thinking this will be a fun, relaxed experience - don't even bother.

_childDocuments_.review: The team building in this game is great! Each monster has intricate sets of skill trees to choose from, and passives that make using monsters together produce synergies based on their type (not just element, but whether it's a warrior, or a reptile say). The monster designs are fantastic, and had alot of community input into the final roster (see the discord): There are creatures wielding weapons and armour for instance, and even goblins and trolls! The roster has an overall old-school RPG feel to its designs, and that is a welcome change of pace compared to the overly cutesie designs favoured by other monster catching games (although don't get me wrong, you WILL find your fav cutie in this game tho :3). It reminds me of Digimon or Monster Rancher, more than Pokemon. The combat is AMAZING: Everything hits just right, from the music (of which there is a choice) to the sprite animations to the impacts. It can get incredibly tactical with battles lasting potentially several turns (some bosses depending team could last around 20 turns!). That said, if you manage to build a first-turn-kill team then that can be incredibly rewarding! As can having a shield-heal team that is impenetrable. Essentially, the choice is truly yours in this game. How you use the monsters and when is completely up to you. There is little to no grind, as the HQ has battles that generate infinitely for you which give you XP and items, and monsters are "caught" via hatching egg rewards gained from successful combat - should you require. Hatched monsters spawn at the lowest level in your current party, regardless of the level you fought the monsters at (i.e. if you decide you want to have a monster in your party from a low level zone, and you're high level, it will hatch high level). There is plenty of fun gear to kit your monsters out with (and I mean kit out... I'm talking RPG style character inventory screen, with main weapon and offhands, and even food buffs - for all monsters).The story is just dressing compared to main systems in the game, but it does its job dutifully, with unexpected twists and some endearing characters. If (when) you find yourself being immersed in the Sanctuary's world and lore, then the story is a pleasant motivator to progress and explore. It is completely non-invasive.The soundtrack is FANTASTIC: If you are a fan of chiptune then this is quite frankly beautiful - there are moments in its composition that remind me of SAO for instance, with triumphant and bright melodies, contrasted with heavy and exciting peril tracks (it is available on Spotify if you fancy a listen).The artstyle is solid and faithful entry into the world of pixel art, and the sprites are surprising characterful for their [16x16?] size - the animations are also excellent, really being able to give a sense of speed and motion to the scenes.This game also stands out from other monster catchers in its metroidvania-esque map and exploration (essentially a sidescrolling platformer): There are PLENTY of secrets and treasures to be found, many of which you acquire by using your trusty monsters and their exploration skills (such as cutting down vines, smashing walls, flying, etc). These exploration skills happen in real time, and as your monster companion follows you, seeing them interact with the world at the push of a button (rather than a special interface) is great feedback, and really immersive, giving you the sense that your monsters are living, breathing things.There is little evolution in the game - and I personally like that - though there is some, where it tends to make sense (i.e. for a baby monster with a clear lineage). This is achieved at the players leisure through item and location, and is not even necessarily desired or advisable - the monsters don't get a straight "upgrade" but may have their entire skillsets changed, completely changing how you use the monster. I have atleast one monster that is my go to that I deliberately haven't evolved as for my purposes it would have become worse. This means that a) you really get to spend time with and appreciate all the monsters should you wish, and b) it's not the usual "rush to evolve" seen in other games that makes the previous evolutions utterly pointless, and kinda boring. All in all, no word of a lie, Monster Sanctuary is my new absolute favourite monster catcher game (if not game in general tbh). I'm a long time fan and player of Pokemon, I also play and enjoy Temtem, but Monster Sanctuary REALLY stands out and if you are looking for a unique and rewarding monster catching experience then this is definitely the game for you. Furthermore, it is still receiving regular content updates and the devs really listen to community feedback - there is a thriving if apparently small community and constant fanbase, which are chill af, as well as PvP tournaments and seasons. Just this week I entered the official fanart contest and it has been the most fun I've had with a franchise outside of playing the game quite frankly in years.If you're an aspiring Keeper ready to tame some monsters, then I'll see you in the Sanctuary! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like really hard pokemon mashed with a light metroidvania. You have to REALLY think through your teams synergies to progress through the game, and there is always a secret around the next corner. It is incredible to me how versatile each monsters roster is and how even with overlapping skills between monsters, each ones kit and selection of abilities feels fresh.Some advice for beginners:Damage is completely overrated. Control of debuffs aka removing and placing them, as well as shields will be your best friend. Shields can be equal to your max HP, so if your monster has a ton of HP, this can be a really effective tanking strategy. Also don't forget Safecast. Barrier + Channel + Shields will win you many fights. This reduces damage dealt to you, gives you extra hp to work with (Shields) and ensures you can always cast your best spells. Lastly, Shields over Healing. More HP is always better than healing your HP bar as ideally you don't want the enemy to touch your HP bar at all. Minimal healing is good, but you don't need much more.I will say, there is some amount of disappointment to team building. Mass debuff removal and shields are essentially a must for every team. This does limit team building to some extend. I could also be completely wrong and built it wrong, but damage outside of slow teams using Age stacking felt like they just really could not cut it and output the needed damage. Either way, I could not put this game down from start to finish. So much to love about this game. The art style, music, dungeon designs are all top notch. I love pokemon, this is not pokemon outside of collecting monsters and turn based combat. It is much harder. That said, I love how you have all 3 of your monsters working together and the teamwork between them is lovely. It also makes or breaks the harder fights of the game. I would highly recommend this to anyone who likes hard strategy games and collectables. Easy 9/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game worth playing?If you like the idea of a metroidvania with turn based battles with monsters you can train, then YES!This is what really makes this game shine and worth playing, you'll be hard pressed to find anything else like this.The concept is really well done and work much better that i expected, glad i found this hidden gem.Most fights are 3vs3, so having a monster team that works well together is the key to success, this opens many more strategic options. You'll need to think about what each monster can bring to a team and exploit it as best you can!There's many, many ways to go about this due to each monster having a unique skill tree to play with, so even one monster can have many roles.Combine that with the ability to equip each monsters with a weapon and 3 accessories, this gives you many options for customizing your monsters.If you like to min-max in games, then you'll be right at home here.Other thing i really like is no matter what monster you use, even that little blob/slime monster, can still be a force to be reckoned with in the right team, even late in the game.You might be tempted to use the same monsters over the course of the game, you can do that but you'll missing out on potential synergy and unique skills related to each monsters.The metroidvania aspect come in the form of monster skills you can use outside of battles that can be used to open new areas to explore, find secrets and for puzzles. Nothing challenging mind you, the focus is more on training/customizing monsters rather that the platforming aspect.There's also have a infinite arena to really push your team to it's limits and PvP to get...uhhh destroyed in. (Only for the most dedicated players)That's about it, hopefully you can enjoy the game as much as i did.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really cool combination of a monster tamer and a metroidvania. The combat is the best monster tamer combat I have ever experienced. It starts out simple, early on you might think its just pokemon but triple battles, but it quickly spirals as you learn all the mechanics within skill trees, equipment, feeding, etc. It's also some of the most accessable. All monsters are usable and viable, its not about just finding the OP dragon pokemon, its about how your monsters synergize with each other. The exploration and story are servicable. The story starts out nonexistent but slowly builds up over time, its not crazy complex but it does its job. The exploration is metroid-like as previously stated, there are abilities you get from monsters that you use outside combat to solve puzzles and discover pathways, expect to travel back to early areas when you find some new ability that say lets you hover or double jump.As for my critisicms, I only have a few. The combat can get overwhelming if you don't pay attention, and the game does have a few difficulty spikes that make sure you have a good team and aren't rushing past encounters, but I didn't mind this. My biggest critisicm is that a lot of areas feel overly paletty. What I mean is the areas often have a reused palette that is repeated for an area. There is very little distinguishing between rooms besides layout, which makes it hard  to know where you are without the map. There are exceptions and some areas look quite nice, but don't expect the life that you would find in say hollow knight

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift, but would have purchased it on the Nintendo Switch if I hadn't received it on PC. This game is definitely one of, if not, THE best monster collector's out there and I would easily give it a 9/10, maybe even a 10/10 after the devteam comes through with the stuff planned in the Roadmap. It is a perfect mixture of Metroidvania and Monster Collector, and you can genuinely feel the love that the team behind the game have put in to every part of this game. PROS:-Music-Art style (seriously one of the best pixel art collections in a game to date)-Level design-Monster design-Battle mechanics-Difficulty (finally a monster collector that isn't braindead easy)-Story length (I have played roughly 10+ hours offline on top of the 17 hours at review- and I've JUST finished the main game) -Post game content-Skill trees (although at times overwhelming)-Map interaction and progression-"Shifting" mechanic adds flavour-Simple to understand but complex enough to make PVP very interesting-Diversity (Not as simple as Fire beats Grass beats Water beats Fire, etc.) -Variety (A lot of monsters to play with, but not to the point of being overwhelming)-FUN!!!!! CONS:-Story dialogue (mostly towards the end of the game the dialogue treats you almost like a child or someone with a form of memory disorder by overexplaining stuff you played through)-Addictive for a time (I nearly missed a university class to play this)-Small roster for evolutions (One of my favourite parts of these games) I would say that my biggest issue is that I can't get enough of this gem. Please treat yourself to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game for any monster collecting fan (eg Pokemon). I absolutely love this game!The platforming is responsive and fun, if you mess up no worries, restart where you left off and try again. The puzzles are simple yet engaging and it's very rewarding to solve them and get treasures.The monsters you collect are unique and very well balanced given just how many of them there are to use. Unlocking light and dark variations about half way through the game adds even more variety and strategy options for you to explore. Sure, a couple monsters are stronger than others overall (Catzerker is OP) but that doesn't stop you from wanting to try and perfect strategies for all of you little friends.Combat is a fun 3V3 turn based style that is quick and engaging, trying different combinations of monsters in battle is tons of fun!Being able to carry a seemingly unlimited number of monsters with you at any time also allows customisation of teams on the fly and makes using them to help you explore the platforming world tons of fun!There are a few QOL tweaks that could be made however;Being able to favourite or organise monsters in your inventory based on element or explore ability for easy access to them for team management and exploration would be a huge help.Instead of having only certain monsters gain an improved explore ability, if the player could pick up an item during the story to give all their monsters improved explore abilities that would save a lot of time spent looking for the right monster with the improved ability. Another possible idea along these lines is to be able to find or buy explore ability improvers to give to your favourite monsters in order to improve their explore abilities.I'm sure that there will be lots of balancing of the combat but a couple of suggestions I have would be to give shields and healing a little bit more power in PVP, not %100 of their PVE power but a bit more than they currently have. As it stands, they are close to useless, the only way to go about PVP is to use as many buffs as possible.As I mentioned before, Catzerker is OP. This is the only example of a monster being wayyy to good in my opinion, there are other pretty strong ones but he is a little over the top. Giving him a very small nerf couldn't hurt. A couple of other things that came to mind while playing were;the art in the monster journal and some promotional materials is a bit off putting in my opinion, perhaps it is place holder art but the promo material might turn off potential players which would be incredibly unfortunate. I would like to say that I do however LOVE the pixel art for all the monsters!A dig explore ability might be fun to add and use especially with Molebear or Goblin Miner. If you could walk up to a slightly out of place mound of dirt and dig to find treasure much like finding hidden walls it would be pretty cool.Maybe adding a "shiny" variant of the monsters would be fun too. I love hunting shiny Pokemon and this game seems like a perfect match for a mechanic like that!Once again, I absolutely love this game! For an early access game it is phenomenal! I would recommend it to anyone who asks. Please don't take my critiques as me thinking this is a bad game, the devs are doing a great job of communicating with the player base and seem to really be listening to feedback so I figured I'd give mine.Thank you for taking the time to read all this, have a great day!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying myself quite a bit with this game. Leveling up and making builds with monsters is pretty interesting and can offer a lot of different teams. I'd say the difficulty curve of this game is also pretty smooth. Keeper Duels, those one-on-one duels with NPCs, can be a little difficult, but that makes sense as you're fighting against a person rather than monsters, and couldn't be solved with a little bit of grindingThat being said, there are some issues that while not ruining the experience overall, they do make it irritating, which follows:- The game doesn't show you how many items you have in your inventory when buying the same item in a store- When hovering over your monsters from the menu, it doesn't show what elemental abilities they have or their affinities and weaknesses, so it adds an extra button press when assembling a team and makes it more cumbersome- When viewing the buffs and debuffs in battle, it displays all the ones activated rather than spacing it out to the specific monster, so it just clutters the screen- I wish I could view my monster's skill tree in battle to double check on passive abilities and whatnot- Being a metroidvania game, there will be chests and secrets that you can't access just yet. However, you can't place markers down, and the map doesn't tell you which region is which by name, so you might get lost easilyOverall, I think the game is pretty fun and challenging, despite all the UI issues. People have been complaining about the grinding in the game as well, but that can be alleviated by hatching the monster you're grinding, although that doesn't work for evolved monsters. Either way, give it a go

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game for the first 2/3 of the story, but now I'm forced to give it a negative review before I even get to the end. Here's the tragic saga of my experience.THE GREAT STUFF:You know what I've literally always wanted to play but could never find? A creature collector that played like a more traditional RPG. You know what this game is? Basically a metroidvania with creature collecting, and that premise made me so addicted to it that I sunk over 80 hours without realizing it had been that much. The plot is pretty run-of-the-mill, with a big ancient evil coming back that you have to thwart, but it's built around a pretty diverse and unique world that's (at least at first) fun to explore. What's especially cool about it is that, like most metroidvanias, certain areas are inaccessible without certain upgrades, but instead of gaining new equipment, it's with skills that only certain monsters can use, so you have to "catch 'em all" in order to progress. It was such a fun and neat aspect to the game that made me excited to keep going so I can finally get to areas that had been blocked off. And since certain monsters are required for certain areas, the game allows you to keep as many monsters as you want in your party, though you can only have six "active" members. Another neat variation of the RPG genre is that you constantly find new gear that's also upgradeable, except instead of party members, you equip it to your monsters. There's eventually even "light" and "dark" variations to the monsters that unlocks after a certain amount of progress, which give special perks that standard forms don't have. All the monsters have skill trees, as well, which allows interesting customization that isn't just leveling up to gain new attacks. The map is MASSIVE, too, even to the extent that there's a hidden area late in the game that's entirely missable.HOWEVER.THE INSUFFERABLE STUFF:At a certain point, I found myself getting exhausted playing the game. There are several major flaws, but the first one I want to mention is that the sheer amount of choices and customization ends up being a double-edged sword. There's too MUCH choice. It gets overwhelming, but beyond that, it also starts to get confusing. There isn't a way to check which skills or abilities certain monsters have except for outside of battle, and even then you have to look pretty closely at the skill trees for each monster to determine if they have specific variations of skills. For instance, the chill debuff doesn't normally cause damage, but certain monsters can add a "congeal" variation that can cause massive damage if chill is stacked. Not all monsters can stack debuffs, however, and others can learn the ability to cause chill damage that's NOT congeal, which doesn't do much damage. This all sounds fine until you realize that some monsters have very similar abilities, but not all of them, and some of them can't learn the same abilities until much later in their skill trees, so it's hard to keep track of. My ice slime, for instance, was a juggernaut of chill damage and passive self-healing, but its attacks were weak overall and couldn't heal other party members, so it was useless in drawn-out battles. My penguin, on the other hand, had a variety of powerful attacks that could also apply chill damage, but its chill effects couldn't stack or congeal, making it less useful in other ways. However, both monsters have extensive skill trees that look very similar, and since you can't check anything other than actual move sets in battle, it took a long time for me to figure out when to use which monster. It gets tedious, and I realized that despite having played over 80 hours, I probably spent a collective 5-6 hours just double-checking my monsters' skill trees or spending ten minutes figuring out which new skills pair well with others it knows, or which skills only pair well with skills that a very similar monster has but it doesn't. I lost easily winnable battles because I assumed one of my monsters had a skill set that it didn't. And of course, you also don't know what passive abilities your opponent has, either, so chill effects might be catastrophic or just inconvenient. Another problem that stems from all of this is that some of my monsters were by far more powerful and useful in battle across the board, but in very specific cases would be mostly useless, or monsters with massively powerful passive skills with weak defense or healing abilities, meaning I needed to juggle 8-12 monsters at a time, which slowed down the level up process in such a way that I would either be forced to grind, or end up being several levels weaker than I needed to be once I got to a new area, all of which was compounded by the fact that most locations were only useful in leveling up certain types of monsters, meaning that I had to work overtime to keep all my monsters on-par with each other. The further I got through the game, the more of slog it was, and I grew to hate it with every fiber of my being.One of the most enjoyable games I've played in years, turned sour due to its own virtues. Yikes.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda like the game, i had now 78 Hours into the game because i love to grind and the game give me exactly this, but you dont have to grind to be clear here i am just a grinder thats all,  with the combination of collecting all the monsters out there i liked it a lot so if you are in monster collection game with a lot of fun go for it it´s worth the buy in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Hate Keeper Battles, seriously didn't enjoy at least 3/4 of them.Loved the normal encounters and champion ones. Those were very well balanced and didn't force me to use Buff clear and debuff comps 100% of the time. (looking at you 2nd last fight)Everything else is very well made.The skill trees give you a reason to actively level up your monsters. The skills and passvies are a lot of fun to uncover and use.Secrets are here and there, they are fine as they are. !! A marker on your map would be massively helpful so you can track areas you were previously unable to crossA lot of ways to build your comp. So anyone that has an itch for that will be satisfied. Sadly late game will prohibit you from using most of your wanted monster due to  (or, you know, 7stacks of sidekick :/ )Easy access to new monsters. Just perform well, you'll almost always get the one you want :)The metroidvania aspect. It's fine overall. Again markers would help tremendously here.The OST imo is okay. I didn't "like" it per say. But I most certainly didn't "hate" it either. It was servicable for me. Though this depends on my subjectivity more than if it's actually good or not.Overall this game is a gem. My review may have sounded a bit more negative but that's bc I was a bit picky at times, especially due to being annoyed at the rather poor endgame balancing.For ~6bucks this is an absolute steal and the amount of content will definitely satisfy you.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: this is a great game, generally most encounters you can force your way through with various builds but quite a few boss fights you need to build a certain way or else you will lose so it forces you to change up your strategy, the only complaint i can think of off the top of my head is endgame gets very grindy because you need to kill a lot of things for those final 1-2 levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game but wow, this ending has got to be one of the hardest for ZERO reason.I can't believe you can go through the entire game relatively easily with whatever monster team you want, but get to the end? Nah nah nah, you have to have the PERFECTLY crafted team of PERFECTLY crafted skill sets, synergies, and equipment.It has to be the biggest kick in the face I've ever received, I genuinely had a blast playing through this game, but the ending just makes me want to never revisit, restart, or even try completing the last fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I have only had this game for two weeks (at the time of writing) and I've already completed the story and all the achievements. Pure dedication at its finest.This has to be one of my all-time favorite games now. The graphics are beautiful, and the story feels engaging. What I enjoy most is the concept of the Spectral Familiars and the Sanctuary itself.This game is a mix of adventure and strategy. Each monster has an ability it can use outside of battle. There are some that are required to continue the story.There are dozens of puzzles that may take you forever. Sharpen your reflexes, cause you're gonna need them.Freedom at last! You can set up your monsters for success by choosing their skills, branching out from 3-5 skill paths in their skill trees. This allows players to make their monsters diverse. The only con I have right now regarding skill trees is that one mistake will lead to having to reset the entire skill tree. Would be nice if there was an item that resets a single path.I am glad the game has an option to show different controller buttons. I use my PS4 controller for gaming, and it is a pain to look at xbox symbols instead of the PS4 ones.With that said, I rate it a 10/10! Hoping to start collecting official merch if there's any!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a mixed review I would. I'd recommend you get it on sale.Unfortunately, this game attempts to be many things, but only reaches a mediocre level at all of them. I think it would be lovely as a game for kids if it had a more balanced battle system (edit: I JUST found out this game had three difficulty levels. Still, the rest of the review stands.)As a platformer/metriodvania(??) the level building is samey, not very interesting visually, and REPETITIVE. Most areas have very similar patterns of platforms, where the "puzzle rooms" are located, and even the secret chests. I actually liked the pixel artstyle (and frankly if you saw the trailers you'd already know what to expect in that department) but I disliked the lack of variety. The only zone I liked was the  The puzzles were a pain. Not even that hard, or thought provoking, just annoying obstacles to overcome. I think they had an interesting idea designing them but never reached a satisfactory outcome.I'll add in that the plot and dialogues are terribly simple. Everyone does hamfisted exposition at you, at all times. There is no subtlety to be found. Everything is spoonfed at you in the most direct way possible. I would find that great for a game for kids. But I think kids would get frustrated at this game, so it's no use.As a...  monster collecting, pokemon-like game, it has certain issues that make playing tedious. The game requires you to create teams that work together. Every monster can play different roles depending on which skills you choose. And you also have to take into consideration which weapon and three accessories you're gonna give them in order to make them useful. You can't preview weapons or accessories if another monster is already utilizing them, which is a pain. Those are already some things that force you to think very hard about all the variables and stats so that you can prevent the monster from being complete garbage. Because that is another issue, monsters tend to either 1. Die a lot 2. Fail at killing enemies via direct damage 3. Both. The most reliable way to deal damage in this game, is through debuffs. Debuff based teams are VERY easy to create, monsters with debuff skills are more likely to synergize with other monsters (compared to more direct damage builds) and just make everything easier. Which is its own issue. Once I found out debuffing completely blew everything else out of the park, I began using debuff teams and not stepping out of that comfort zone. When team creation requires A LOT of thought, time, and careful consideration (monsters + skills + accessories + weapon + synergies...) you just stop enjoying it and start looking for the easiest method. Which is debuff spamming.All in all I think this is a nice game, again, I would leave a mixed review if I could. Has some nice ideas but fails to develop them satisfactorily.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it until you reached that last area where the man just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spams debuffs on you and gets infinite buffs on himself.  For some reason, when I get to an area to farm for a monster, the drop rate is significantly decreased for an egg, even though I get a 5 star rating in the battle.  Please for the love of ♥♥♥♥ put in an item that increases the chance of getting an egg so I don't have to test my ♥♥♥♥ luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than Pokemon! I love this game. I got it on a Saturday and I played 20h until I had to stop and work on Monday. I like everything about it, the monsters, the combat system, not having to "fix" the injured monsters outside of combat, and I just LOVE the exploration part of it with areas that need higher skills that you get later and you come back to it. And how you need diff monsters by your side to interact with the world in order to get you to new areas. I think it's much better done than Pokemon.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Pokemon meets metroidvania with a sprinkle of tech tree upgrades and equipment system. It's downside it's not being long enough. It really shows potential for future sequels, there's some uniqueness in the mix of all of this creature collecting rpg features.Between having to capture specific species to access hidden areas to tuning synergy between more than one team, you'll have a blast testing out the combinations.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: We really need more games like this that showcase fascinating additions to the addicting gameplay loop of Pokémon. Monster Sanctuary lets you hatch monsters to build a team of up to six, where three monsters fight at the same time against either other teams of six, wild monsters in groups of three, or single boss monsters. The brilliant thing is that actually acquiring all the monsters and then levelling them is easy enough, and that all the actual game focus is put on finding team synergies that work well against tough opposition in the later half. Going full buff, or full debuff, playing the long match with aging and stacking mechanics or rather build a sweeping team to defeat enemies as fast as possible, mixing elements to have the type advantage or rather focus on single elements to make great use of certain passive bonuses... you know, optimisation, and in such an enjoyable fashion \o/
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect the combination of monster tamer and 3d platformer to work, but wow was I wrong. The monsters unlock parts of the map, and every monster is a viable option. Never felt a grind, as there's plenty of level up items and story to push you forward. The battles are 3v3 and the strategy is deep. Glad I finally convinced myself to give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The level design just get more cancerous after the first two area. It is not necessarily challenging like white palace in Hollow Knight, instead it makes you go through multiple rooms again just by failing some jumps. Plus it is not an optional challenge that you can take but a part that you must go through to continue the game. The developer should have put something like this in the first two area to let player know what they are getting themselves into.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is not a bad game, but it lacks a few things to make it a good game. Partially, it feels unnecessarily slow and while the rock-paper-scissors combat mechanics are okay, they don't feel satisfying to me. Each monster has a set of skills that can be unlocked, but it is hard to focus fully on one specific thing since you will need to waste points on unlocking unrelated things to access stuff you actually want.I think my biggest complaint about Monster Sanctuary is that the monsters feel generic. Really generic. They are so generic, the Catzerker is probably the only memorable monster - not even the four starters are memorable. They lack a unique charm.It's an okay game, but for the money it costs, there are better titles available. Consider buying this on sale, though!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best monster collecting games I've played. Since the fights are 3v3, you need your team to cover a lot of bases, and also be aware of who's the biggest threat in the enemy team. The combo system adds an extra layer of complexity, since you need to chain as much heals, buffs or attacks as you can for the final hit each turn. Evolutions are not a straight up upgrade from their "base" form, but it can change what kind of role the monster fulfills on the team. The addition of monster shifting makes up for the lack of evolved monsters, since each shifted forms covers a different playstyle.An amazing game all around that I absolutely recommend to everyone who wants a good monster collecting game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can describe Monster Sanctuary is that it goes so much harder than it needed to, on every level. From the wonderful monster designs, to the very deep and rewarding combat system, to the joyful experience of just exploring the world, and a great story, everyone who worked on this game clearly poured love and effort into every part of this game. I cannot recommend it enough if you're a fan of Metroidvanias and/or Monster Fighting games.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to recommend a game that have the most unfair difficulty spikes I have ever seen. I could breeze through majority of mobs and battles, but now I'm being obliterated at one of the major story fights. I know I can fine tune my team, change monsters, etc, but I don't want to spend time on mindless grinds just to try other monsters. It's a shame because I had a lot of fun with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful retelling of sorts of pokemon but in a non repetitive way, the monsters are interesting and the story is new enough to be intriguing but bot new enough to be overly complicated as to confuse the player. Either way atleast 30hrs of playtime for story ending maybe 4 more hours for full achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top-tier monster collector-themed game, probably the best on the current market:Pros:--Metroidvanian open world, with each monster presenting a movement ability in the open world. As you collect monsters, you also get movement abilities.--3v3 Battles. This makes sure that team composition is an important aspect.--6v6 Trainer Battles. This adds an additional dimension to 3v3 Battles, with you also having to consider how your bench fits into your team.--Every monster is useful. I'm not kidding. Every single monster can fit into a build. Every monster has a purpose.--Skill Trees instead of linear skill progression. Every monster has at-least 2 or 3 viable builds. A team with the same monsters can have multiple compositions. Neutral:--The battle score system is balanced around you winning in around 2~3 turns and taking little-to-no damage. This is matter of taste. It does ensure that battles are exciting but don't overstay their welcome.--Platforming is challenging and plenty of it feels like you've barely made it. But practise enough, and you'll make it! It is challenging. This is another matter of taste, if it is a pro or a con.Cons:I don't like doing this, but there aren't any cons I can think of, off the top of my head. Maybe this game fits my tastes perfectly. But this and Fell Seal rank as my favourite turn based tactics games. Monster Sanctuary is a top-tier game. I'd say this is my favourite indie title of 2020.It is super cheap for the value it gives, and it also has a demo. Try it! And if you enjoy the demo, buy it. If you like turn based RPGs and platforming, you'll feel right at home.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: When you start to sink a lot of hours in this game, you can see there is lot of content in this game in terms of variety of monsters you can use (with each monster being charming and different enough from the others), in different weapons and gear, making very fun to experiment different strategies and teams to battle. Of all the ways to play, having a debuffer in your team usually makes your team very OP, since debuffs deals a lot of damage, it kinda makes a playthrough without one very difficult (at the end of tha campaign), but I guess other team compositions are still doable.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This intuitive mix of Metroidvania and Monster Tamer is a true joy. It brings a much-needed revival to the Metroidvania genre and some much-needed difficulty and real strategy to the Tamer genre. Unlike games like Pokemon, you can't win without really thinking things through and making a real effort to strategize. Highly recommend to fans of either genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I've yet to review or recommend a game (as far as I remember), but I'll just say this;This game has the most tightly-knit and friendliest community I've ever seen on the official Discord server.That reason alone pushed me to get really into the game and into it's PvP aspects. If you enjoy Pokemon and Temtem but want a more straight-forward and less "messy" approach to it, this game quite easily fits the bill!Fair warning; this IS an early-access title, though, so expect some improvements and more content to be added in the future (hurray!) ! For the time being, though, the game is quite easily worth it's very fair ~$20 CAD price in my opinion. :)

Not a big fan of the story either, but to be fair I didn't get very far before I got bored. Its not for me, but that is my personal opinion. name: Unbound: Worlds Apart
detailed_description: What is Unbound? Unbound: Worlds Apart is a challenging, atmospheric and hand-drawn puzzle-platformer set in a universe where all worlds are connected by portals. You control Soli, a gifted young mage who has the power to open portals and control the unique properties of each world - such as inverse gravity, time manipulation, super strength and more. Using these newfound skills, Soli must journey across dangerous and mysterious worlds, each brimming with secrets and challenges. You must use every skill Soli has to defeat a ruthless evil that is tearing reality apart, while learning the shocking truth behind your world’s collapse. Gameplay Your reflexes and twitch platforming skills will be put to the ultimate test in Unbound: Worlds Apart. As Soli you can explore large worlds full of hidden secrets and unlockable skills that open up even more of the map as you progress. Along the way you will meet many weird, wonderful and devious characters, each with rich backstories and dialogue. By completing their quests or listening to their tales of hope and sorrow, you will learn more about Unbound’s grand universe of worlds and the portals that connect them. Key features: 10 different portals with unique mechanics Vibrant and detailed hand-drawn artwork Twitch platforming with new skills to unlock Challenging puzzles, traps, monsters and bosses A rich narrative, world lore and cast of NPCs Hidden secrets, quests and collectibles

_childDocuments_.review: Well, where do I start? Are you a fan of Ori and the Blind Forest? Is Hollow Knight your favourite game? Well, let me tell you something. This is your lucky day! This game has everything you've been missing: the fascinating, cryptic lore of Hollow Knight? Check. Trying platforming and puzzles like Ori? Check. Charming NPCs? Check. Varied and stunning locations? Check. Honestly, this game really feels like Hollow Knight and Ori’s third long lost sibling. And Soli the protagonist is so adorable!About the gameplay and platforming. It’s honestly what I would call *fair*. The game starts with some kinda easy platforming, but it has a really uphill difficulty curve. It gets from easy to really hard towards the end. And by hard I mean Super Meat Boy hard. The later part of the game will really put you to the test. If you’re one of those gamers that really likes a challenge, then the extra content the game has is definitely for you! *flashback to Hollow Knight's buzzsaw level* I’m not telling you how to get it, so have fun discovering that one on your own!I'd say the game clocks at about 20 hours of content if you explore everything and get all the secrets, so you're getting your money's worth. If you're like me and you're still (im)patiently waiting for Silksong's release date, then this game will scratch your itch. Have fun and thank me later!
