_childDocuments_.review: At first look it’s easy to see that Unbound: Worlds Apart borrows quite a bit from Ori and the Will of the Wisps. The vibrant, hand-drawn art style, the fairy-tale like story telling, and the challenging platforming are all hallmarks of the Ori series. However, once you dive just a little deeper into Unbound: Worlds Apart, you find a side-scroller that relies more on puzzle solving and pure platforming precision than combat, and keeps a wealth of surprises under the hood.In fact, there really isn’t much combat at all in Unbound, which is in stark contrast to Ori and the Will of the Wisps. Soli, the game’s protagonist, must use his portal generating ability to use the environment to solve puzzles and defeat enemies. His jump isn’t very high, he can only take a single hit, and he has no weapons. This portal ability is what truly separates Unbound Worlds apart from other Metroid-style platformers.Each region you visit gives your portal a distinct property. First off in reverse gravity. Activate your portal and Soli will flip upside down and rise to the ceiling. This allows you to avoid dangers, kill unsuspecting enemies, and also float in the air by quickly activating and deactivating the portal. It very quickly takes the lessons you learned in the fairly simple tutorial and literally flips them on their head. And this was just the first area.Soon after solving the puzzles in that region I found myself in a completely dark underground cave. Here my portal acted as a huge bloom of light, allowing me to see obstacles and enemies previously hidden in the darkness. There was a catch though; the faster I walked and more I jumped the smaller the circle of light emanating around Soli got. It didn’t restore to full strength until I stopped and rested. This meant I had to survey the area and do a lot of the platforming my memory in almost complete darkness. It was a totally different mechanic and pace than the previous region, and was indicative of the large variety of mechanics the game offers. Who knew a single button and ability could be so dynamic?It’s that endless possibility that really struck me about Unbound: Worlds Apart. In a landscape of games that borrow, but rarely come up with unique mechanics, Unbound: Worlds Apart had me excited to see more from the very start. Part of why I like video games, especially indie titles, is their ability to experiment and provide new experiences, and Unbound: Worlds Apart is perfect encapsulation of that.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and I'd recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.  The platforming was delightful, the dimension mechanic felt fun and unique, and it controlled really well.  The bosses felt creative and interesting to fight because you didn't any offensive abilities, so you had to figure out how to interact with the boss rather than unload on them.  It's not super long outside of plowing through the story there's still more to do and explore.  Worth the $20 for what you get.Game looks beautiful, and the music really sets the atmosphere.  The world and story is set up well.The main thing that I thought was overkill(but won't matter to some, and others may love, it's up to taste) was how much it autosaves.  It autosaves almost every single obstacle so there is almost no punishment for dying to something, and on average you maybe lose a few seconds with just a couple parts putting you back further.  Even some bosses had autosaves in middle of the fight.  The platforming throughout and nearing the end can get a little difficult in a fair and rewarding way, but the autosaving makes it feel like you're playing through it with save states between every jump.  It'd be awesome if they eventually released a higher difficulty mode that toned it down juuuuust a little on the autosaving.Overall though I loved the experience. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------------------------Unbound: World’s Apart is an old school platformer with modern mechanics and sensibilities. This isn’t a metroidvania although it is obviously inspired it. The graphics are cute and charming with more than a passing resemblance to . However, gameplay-wise, the bulk of Unbound is closer to platform games such as  and  while the timed events and boss fights are indeed, straight out of Ori. The portal mechanic although not new, is utilized intelligently without creating confusion. By the way, there is no combat; there is no attack button, not HP bar, everything (except the bosses) are one shot kills. In this regard, it’s an especially old school platform game a la Super Mario. While not perfect and certainly not original, Unbound as a whole is greater than the sum of it’s parts and for the price, it’s a good game for platform beginners and provides moderate challenge for veterans. Recommended. ---------------------------------------- Each section of the world pass through a gate which will grant you the ability to conjure a portal that changes your immediate environment (think Gateway but without the Gateway Guns). This could be changing gravity, changing your size, changing placement of an obstruction and even change a hostile.  and you won’t get confused by how, where and when to use them. Your power-ups and level design are in fact,  and  this speaks to a clever and considerate game design. . They are tight enough that you can do precision timing and precision platforming. Although I do feel that movement is just slightly heavy but on the whole, movement has an enjoyable flow. . Unbound doesn’t require precision platforming but it does require some precision timing (think Braid). Having said that, it isn’t too difficult nor is it too punishing as provides you with ample respawn areas and teleport points. ----------------------------------------Unbound . From the artwork, to the level design, to the boss fights and the timed events. You could forgive them this since they are a Kickstarter studio with very limited resources which they used to focus on gameplay rather than original graphics. . There is way too much exposition from characters rather than naturally incorporating them in the gameplay. The emotional payoff at the end is also a miss since there wasn’t adequate build-up to give the ending the impact it needed. But again, the money went to make a better gameplay so you can forgive this oversight. ----------------------------------------. Unbound is more akin to an old school platform where you one shot the enemy and the enemy one shots you. There is no attack button and you generally use the environment (some times your powers) to kill hostiles. The boss fights is like Super Mario 1 or 3 where you have to strike the enemy 3 times to kill them and the bosses have elaborate attacks and phases that you have to memorize (think Ori's boss fights). I think there only like 3 or 4 bosses in the game and they are very unique and distinct. On the whole, I think it works and is generally fun, except for the last boss which personally, I find annoying and just long-winded.  though I’m a 30 year gaming veteran and I steamrolled everything. Still, 6 hours is a short game and it may disappoint some people. In Alien Pixel’s defense though, this is their first game and considering the amount of things that they managed to accomplished here as well as the price of the game, I think the short game time is reasonable. Still, buyer beware. ----------------------------------------I really enjoyed this game. For an Indie Kickstarter game, I think Unbound: World’s Apart is a pretty accomplished. If you like platformers, you’ll probably like this. If you’re a beginner, this is a good place to start. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop here is most similar to Celeste in that the gameplay focuses on a lot of short, challenging fine-tuned platforming "levels" even though holistically, the art/story/atmosphere/music/exploration/environment/map is much more similar to Ori and the Blind Forest. If you die on any section you restart on that same spot which is pleasant. IMO the game starts getting challenging after about 1-2 hours in then the difficulty stays pretty consistent after that, comparable difficulty to Celeste A side.The vast majority of the game's difficulty comes from the mechanical/platforming side rather than the puzzle side, definitely there are tons of spots where it will not be immediately obvious what to do and you need to use your brain a bit to figure it out, but very few hard puzzles- IMO there are only 2 villagers on par with the Crystal Hearts in Celeste in terms of puzzle challenge (I kind of feel like anyone who has 100%'d it will know exactly which 2 I am talking about lol). I would have liked to see more sections like  to really amp up the puzzle part of the game but that's just my personal preference.Overall the quality of the game is just great in every aspect, would highly recommend if you enjoy moderately challenging platforming. The monster aesthetics are especially unique which was offputting to me at first but I grew fond of them throughout the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a while now and I'm super happy to finally see it released. Despite the comparisons I didn't feel like I'm playing a different version of Ori or Hollow Knight. Unbound has a strong and unique atmosphere which can easily take you out of your room to the melancholic realm of Vaiya, Sanarya and Umberra.Although the main focus is platforming there is a solid metroidvania-stlye exploration which goes really well with puzzles. The learning curve is well designed. I never really felt like I'm stuck and can't go on. There are some more difficult optional puzzles but you can always leave them and return when you feel you are ready.The controls are fine and the pacing of the new abilities is also great. You always feel like there is something new you can use to face even more deadly traps.Although the base move set doesn't add anything we didn't see before, the portal mechanics really make the game different than anything you played before. Thanks to the mix of different portals and abilities the gameplay is always changing as you go on. You won't have problem with repetition.I really like the art of Unbound. The visuals improved so much over the years. The 3 worlds are really different yet you feel they are somehow connected. Each realm has its own charm which makes you want to explore more.For my taste the presentation of the story could be better. To get a hint of what's going on you need to collect script parts by saving lost villagers. They all tell you a fragment which doesn't really mean anything when you get it. Later you can read the whole story and that makes it more clear. So basically it won't be the story which makes you keep playing. You'll need to work really hard to get the story.The music is really good and supports the mood very well. I feel like there is not enough music though. It fits well so most likely you won't feel like it's repetitive. Still some additional tracks would be nice to have.Out of 10 points I would give 8 to Unbound. I highly recommend it for anyone who likes metroidvanias or puzzle platformers. If you are new to this type of games I would still say it's a good one for starting.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful puzzle jump and run without explicit combat. Doesn't mean it is peaceful. Dodge obstacles or trick them into killing each other. Usually you don't really have a choice, trick-killing enemies is required, especially for bosses. If you aren't doing that, you are talking to some classic 4-lines-NPCs that give you more background. I can't tell if it is the mute protagonist or just good writing, but I enjoy the little tidbits of information or one-sided interaction.For now, my repertoire is limited to walking, jumping and a parallel-world portal. Sounds like a one-trick-pony, but since there are different parallel worlds with different mechanics, it doesn't feel like it. Many one-trick-ponies, maybe?The author did so many little things right:- The game auto-pauses when it loses connection with the controller (pet peeve of mine)- There are checkpoints everywhere. Short of time rewind shenanigans you can't do better- The tutorial mainly makes you figure things out by yourself instead of patronizing you with "push stick to move"Right now it feels easy with a enjoyable amount of challenge for spice. I dread tomorrow when I continue and have to relearn everything.If you want to compare it to other games: Ori (minus the boring combat and as yet without escape sequence)Hue (with more variety and actual graphics)

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the project on Kickstarter back when it first came out and I was pleasantly surprised to receive my copy today! The controls are very smooth and on point and the portals are very responsive. Some puzzles seem harder at first but after you figure out what to do, you only have to time your portals and platforming correctly. I died a couple of times, but Soli always respawns close by so there is not much backtracking.The level areas are moody and awesome, the art style is lovely and the soundtrack lends perfectly to it.  Loving the game so far and can't wait to discover more of it! Awesome job devs!

name: Unholy
detailed_description: Open the doors between your everyday reality and a dark unholy world to unveil the mystery of the disappearance of your child. Explore both worlds to find clues, solve puzzles, decide whether you infiltrate or fight brutal enemies and stand up to an aberrant establishment. Two parallel worlds to explore. The grey and cold reality on a brutalist post-soviet Eastern European town and the creepy and twisted world of Unholy, a grotesque society ruled by a relentless priest caste. An unsettling horror experience driven by an intense narrative with captivating visuals based on the works of reputed dark artist Tomasz Strzałkowski (Duality Games Art director and founder).. A unique gameplay blend that combines meticulous exploration, intriguing puzzle solving, infiltration and stealth with innovative shooting dynamics. A versatile unique weapon. Use four different emotions: anger, fear, sadness and desire to interact with the environment (destroy obstacles, trigger mechanisms, overload circuits, illuminate your way) or to confuse, lure or damage your opponents. Masks! Everybody in the unholy world hides behind a mask and it can be the difference between life or death. Build your own mask to get new skills and improve your abilities or wear other masks to infiltrate, confuse your enemies and impersonate your opponents.

_childDocuments_.review: Unholy is dominantly, a stealth game that features horror aspects and light exploration whilst telling its narrative. Unfortunately, it misses its mark in all facets and became a drudgery to complete. The few redeeming highlights of the game are quickly buried beneath its myriad of troubles. In Unholy’s current stage, particularly at its given price of $AU43.95, I cannot recommend it.The story is set in a post-soviet Eastern European town which is brutally ruled by an oppressive and malevolent religious cult. Players take on the role of Dorothea, a member of this cult-like society and mother to a young boy. Her child is taken from her by the leader of the cult, and the game centres around her mission to single-handedly rescue him, mixing between the real world and an alternate hellish universe.This story felt unimaginative and is something I have seen frequently. It tries to focus on a mother’s love for her child, and her willingness to do whatever it takes for them. The problem with this is…  players were never made to feel anything for either of these two characters, instead, we are met with some of the most cringe-worthy lines of the protagonist shouting “I am NOT just a woman, I am a mother!” Despite the lacking story, it is by far, not Unholy’s weakest component.On the Steam store page, Unholy is described as a blend of genres, with exploration, stealth, combat and puzzles. Exploration is generally rather linear, ammo for your weapon can be found, and minimal collectables, but that is about all. Objects are scattered quite literally in plain sight, thus not requiring any diligent searching. Puzzles are exceptionally simple, typically able to be brute forced by randomly clicking things, or simply looking at the solution that is on the puzzle itself. Examples include matching symbols on a chest (twice) where the answers are right there in front of you. Or turning on power by pulling a lever, then running back to manually adjust the equipment, then running back to pull a lever again. I kept waiting for something I would consider to be an actual puzzle; however, it never came. There are three basic enemy types in the game, with guards, hunters and general infected. Each are the same, in that if they see you, they will chase you. Take two hits and you will die. Hunters can only be seen while using a specific mask, which originally, I found interesting, but eventually becomes a huge hassle. Awkwardly shifting through 4 different masks with frustrating controls is not scary. In fairness, whilst the puzzles were abysmal, I did like the ideas on the method of killing enemies, which could be considered a puzzle. Enemies must be lured to specific electrical objects which can then be shot and will explode on all enemies within that radius, killing them. This was a great idea and allows more thought on how to use the equipment provided to players. The weapon you have is a fancy slingshot, which can be equipped with different ammunition crystals that will all cause different impacts. Ammo is plentiful and can be used to lure enemies to a specific spot, create a fog shield to obscure their vision, or can be used directly on them to stun them. These concepts are interesting, but poorly executed with an overabundance of controls that I will explain later. To add to this, most enemies just get stuck walking into walls, on invisible objects, or are unable to traverse stairs to reach you. When I was being chased, if I just hid in a locker (right in front of the enemy, who is standing behind me), they will function as if they never saw me and walk away.Keeping this brief, but throughout the game players will discover masks to use. Each mask bestows different abilities such as being able to breathe better in toxic gas, or to see Hunters. Each mask gives a different filter to the game, such as a hazy blue or green and made me feel nauseous. They are equipped with numbers 1-4..  but add this to the 4 different ammo types and you will find it extremely awkward, constantly trying to shift through different masks and switch ammo simultaneously, all while being chased.To summarise *some* of the bugs I encountered, I have made a list.Stuttering of lights, missing textures, lag when rotating the camera, unresponsive controls (particularly when trying to quickly equip the slingshot), mouse sensitivity is extremely slow, even when placed on maximum (seemed to only happen when examining things or doing puzzles). Audio issues with the characters weeping/heavy breathing staying on repeat, even when the scene had passed. Enemies continually becoming stuck in walls, 2x crashes during cutscenes, severe FPS drops in later sections (120FPS down to 20-40) and was quite unstable. Falling through almost every elevator only to be randomly transported to the top and become stuck in the floor. Sometimes no toxicity meter would show up in the gas sections, resulting in me having to guess when I would die. Sometimes it randomly reset itself even if I was still in the gas, other times it wouldn’t. The final boss is atrocious. His lightning clips through all objects including stone barriers, automatically killing you. The number of times I had to restart due to this, and have to listen to him call me a worm, actually became entertaining. Overall, the game is exceptionally clunky with some of the worst AI I have seen in Indie’s at this price. For a game relying on its stealth sections, these will irrevocably damage player experience.Most environments were rather impressive, but were letdown by all of the technical issues mentioned above. Characters look very stiff and are badly lip synced.Audio is also a letdown, alongside the aforementioned issues, the voice acting of the protagonist is …bad. I found it to be similar to HOG games I have played, and that is unfortunately not a good comparison. I would have preferred to have played this in the developers’ native language as the result was extremely distracting, over-acted and uncomfortable, at least for me, as a native English speaker. 6-7 hoursUnholy is riddled with bugs and whilst they are not game-breaking, they make it a slog to complete. Combining this with extremely poor AI in a stealth-orientated game just does not make this enjoyable. I wanted to like this game and consider myself somewhat of a connoisseur of Indie horrors on Steam, but I cannot recommend Unholy.

_childDocuments_.review: Adventure, female protagonist, stealth, mystery, exploration, puzzles, dark.PLOTWe are in a post-Soviet Eastern European city, the life of Dorothea Linde, a single mother, is not easy, in her past there is an alcoholic father; the only hope and help he finds is in a form of religion called "The Circle"She decides to be guided by this caste of priests, the idea that her son Gabriel is the chosen one makes her proud, but she doesn't know that she is pushing him into the wrong hands, these cultists want to use the child as a sacrifice to create a path towards a world called "Eternal City"One morning he discovers that Gabriel has been kidnapped and placed on an altar to celebrate a strange rite among masked men. Trying to stop this absurd thing, the unexpected happens, a fire breaks out and the child together with the entire building are destroyed.Dorothea, overcome by grief, does not accept her son's death, tears down the obituaries hanging in the city, and searches for answers at her father's house, thus discovering that her family was hiding secrets, but who was her father really?Confused, desperate and alone she finds herself listening to a strange old woman, in her eyes she appears like a guide, a "Baba Yaga" who invites her to perform a ritual to access a parallel reality where Gabriel is still alive.Armed with great courage, this mother is determined to get her son back, she throws herself into this journey into the unknown, into a disturbing and distorted world of Unholy, a tyrannical society governed by a caste of unscrupulous priests, where slaves live , ordinary citizens or members of the "law enforcement agencies" who do not tolerate any rebellion.Dorothea is willing to make any sacrifice to prevent the "Prophet" from completing his ritual and unmasking his madness!But who is this old woman who drives it?He certainly knows a lot about the sect, he owes him some explanations, because many things have been kept hidden, what is the truth?Will he be able to save Gabriel?And stop this dangerous society?PLAYABILITYThere are 10 chapters where you will find notes that will give an explanation to the plot, after a promising start, the journey will unfortunately take place in places that are well made graphically but sparse, dilapidated, where everything falls to pieces or is burned by fire.You cannot face the guards directly but you have to hide, so don't rush, stop for a moment and see what route they take, walk along small stretches, hide and take down the security cameras where possible.The enemies are slow and stupid so use cunning and have them follow you to lead them to the mines, or armed with your slingshot you will easily deceive them.Arm yourself with good curiosity and look everywhere around you to find and collect all 15 "Memories". They will be very useful to you because they are points to offer on the altar of the "Mother" located around, you can acquire very useful skills.You won't find real puzzles, but there will be machinery to start, or objects to search for.It's called Horror, but it's not scary, there's certainly nothing that will make you jump in your seat, it just creates a bit of tension having to be careful not to get killed by enemies.The difficulty in the game is that you have to understand where you need to go and what the right path is to continue towards the next location.You have no weapons, but only Gabriel's slingshot which is used to shoot Emotions with different characteristics, and masks that will help you see what others don't see or help you with poisoned areas.However, don't give up at the first levels as you progress through the game you will be provided with increasingly valid help.As an experience it was interesting because it's not the usual adventure where you make your way with a sword and off you go! NO!!!!!!! Here you have to use your mind, with cunning and cunning, create a plan to deceive and circumvent your enemies or induce them to eliminate themselves, believe me it gives much more satisfaction!

Just as in all other games - get code, find 3 blobs, set some dices. I think - it's ok.Story? Cultists are bad, they get portal to hell, go get revenge for your beloved rabbit? _childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how to rate this game. It starts off promising, then it became a chore and near the end I started liking the gameplay a bit more. I`ll give it a thumb halfway upGraphics are beautiful and detailed, but they don't do anything very original with all that talent. I was expecting a creatively nightmarish world but it's essentially a dilapidated city with a bit of alien overgrowth. Monster design is uninspired as well.The main problem of the game is that it's simply not that fun to play a lot of the time. It progressively became less enjoyable when stealth came into play. I would often get spotted no matter what I do and that is often fatal. You die in 2 hits, but taking damage makes you unable to run for a short while, so you usually get hit a second time immediately. Eventually you get different slingshot crystals that can create various effects. Those cannot directly kill enemies but you can lure them to traps or blow up stuff. At that point it was more enjoyable to figure out how to dispose of enemies. Individual puzzles are simple, but the real puzzle is to figure out the best way to deal with enemies in an area while you complete the tasks. Overall, it is definitely not as good as other recent indie horror games. Can be worth it for those like me who can`t get enough horror games, but get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would have liked it more if it were to set in the apartment complex the whole time, it had such an eerie and unsettling yet nostalgic homey feel to it, had so much potential. All in all the game has a draggy story with not much of a body. Some segments were hard to follow and didn't make sense. Oh well. I appreciate the effort as it is an indie game. Its definitely better than most but not a game I can recommend to the average player.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing this has going is it's atmosphere with some of the creepiest set designs I've seen. It's very slow paced and not scary by any means but gives you more a sense of pure dread coming your way.You're Dorthea (also vocalist of Windhand HAH) and on a quest to find your son who's been kidnapped by some satan worshipping junkies. Ok, maybe they aren't junkies but they're not in their right mind that's for certain. You follow linear levels and acquire items by puzzles in order to advance the story. Staying stealth and using tactics to an extent are your keys to survival. The game runs decently with some occasional hitches but better than a few other recent titles I've played. But... BUT!! My biggest complaint is the sensitivity. SLLLOOOOWWWW Please for the love of all that's UNHOLY make it faster. It's maxed out and still seems like I'm turning at a turtles pace. Please adjust this devs. There also seems to be a lack of music to add extra intensity to the atmosphere of the game but there are plenty of creeks, and sounds of suffering to give you a slight bit of anxiety.So, If you're a weirdo like me and like the devil and all things occult, you will dig this. I'm an atheist but satanic panic/crazy religioso schtuff is my jam!Infernal hails

_childDocuments_.review: So I want start off by saying that I am a big fan of indie games. Game developers who don't have a big budget behind them or big investors for that matter. This is a game I have been following for some time and had it on my wishlist because the moment I saw the first teaser trailer, I knew this was going to be a good game with a great story. I am also a big fan of psychological horror games. The execution of the game is remarkably amazing, the story is awesome, the gameplay, while clunky, is not a big deal and stuff like that usually gets hotfixed as every game has bugs even the big budget Triple A games. I haven't beat the game yet but based on the playthrough, I am enjoying it very well. The gameplay is very immersive, the story and plot is on point, I can only imagine how more amazing this game could have turned out if it had a larger budget with a bigger team. That said, I don't know how IGN gave this game a 4/10, they clearly don't respect the hard work and dedication it goes into video game development like this especially coming from indie developers but I really enjoy this game and to me it's better than a lot of other Triple A games out there. So I am going to give it a perfect score of 10/10 because that's what this game deserves. I hope in the future the dev's add more story content, perhaps new game modes, survival mode, gauntlet mode, anything to add replayability, perhaps even some dlc content. It's a Thumbs UP from me folks!

_childDocuments_.review: While I was hoping for a great game, it started out feeling like it would be an enjoyable experience. The game quickly felt like it couldn't tell what genre it was, what type of game it was, swapping between overtly simple stealth tactics, to repetitive and simple puzzles, and a story that simply got worse in terms of how it was written the further alone I got at the point I'm at so far with nothing necessarily horrifying within it except for it's story, game play, and apathetically done voice acting. The game visually is beautiful and the music is great, but not so great in any other aspect and I would not recommend it even at it's current sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: Unholy is visually unique in it's depiction of an other worldly vision of horror summoned by a twisted cult in the protagonists home town. Stealth mechanics work great while hiding from the cult members, and there are some nice upgrade options to help empower your player to fight them off as well. Overall the game play, graphics, and mechanics deliver an engaging and approachable horror experience rooted in the horrors of religious zealotry.

_childDocuments_.review: There's an evil masked priestess lady sacrificing your son and....she sounds and talks like a soccer mom. It's kinda hard to take her seriously. All in all it's a decent game with thick atmosphere and great visuals. General gameplay is mostly tactical. _childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: It's an indy game. It has it's issues. I finished it in 11 hours, 21 of 27 achievements and I enjoyed it. It's a little quirky, a little preachy and the whole thing of a female protagonist fighting with her emotions is a little... yeah. But in the end it's complete, no major glitches, didn't have to restart and no one screaming 'the message' in my face every 10 minutes and so by those standards it beats the hell out of 60% of the AAA games released this year. Enjoyable. Good looking. Ran smooth for me. At the indy price, its worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been to the Salt Lake Temple, have done a tour and ask "What happened to the golden pages?" or you're driving in downtown Clearwater and you see groups of 10-15 young Scientology people all wearing white shirts and black pants on several blocks crossing traffic then you can quickly relate to the opening of Unholy.  Once the story unfolds to another world it quickly crumbles apart.  IGN was right to give the game 4/10 which is unfortunate but true.  The graphics are the games strong point but beyond that the AI and mechanics are clunky and gets worse as you progress.  The story is extremely cliche as well.  I didn't find myself enjoying the playthrough.  It felt like a chore to complete.  I think Early Access would have really benefited the release of the game to kill bugs as well as hash out usability testing to find out what improvements could have been made via feedback to improve the gameplay.  As the dev team squashes some bugs it will be a stronger title but even then the story will be disappointing and some gameplay won't be able to be fixed.  Wait and see how much gets improved before buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Full gameplay: I really tried to enjoy this game, based on the trailer it seemed like an interesting idea but unfortunately it was a frustrating experience with a gameplay that felt like a chore after a while instead of being fun and engaging.You are a mother that a cult took your child and trying to get your child back from them and you travel to an alternate reality called Eternal City. You have to get masks to get different abilities and your weapon is something like a slingshot that shoots emotion stones. The visual and the world that you go to is really good and well designed but unfortunately and performance was mostly good but these are the main positives about this game and maybe the story(?) but personally after a while I didn't care about the story and wanted to be done with it.One of the worst part of this game is the AI, I have never seen anything like this AI in a long time, enemies randomly get stuck and block your way, sometimes they attack you and sometime just do nothing and for couple of times guards hit me and I went inside the storage cabinet in from of them to hide and they just ignored me and left the area!!! The UI of the game also has issues, your stones have 4 colors and when you try to shoot you can't see the stone and constantly shoot the wrong stone, on the corner of the screen there is a very slight background color for selected stone that you can't see it since mostly you are in dark area. Every time you interact with something or pickup a stone or put a stone in a device ... your flashlight turns off! Every time!! I have to turn it on after each interaction so annoying. Puzzles in this game are very basic and don't need a lot of effort, find a number or find a correct order of items.I thought the game was supposed to be horror and scary but I never felt that during my whole gameplay. You basically need to hide and avoid enemies or use your stones to kill them.As I said the story started really interesting but it became predictable after a while, specifically the ending was very anticlimactic, I was expecting to see a boss fight or some final fight but there was none. You can finish the game probably in less than 3-4 hours if you don't face any issues with AI or something, I think the game price for this amount of gameplay is not fair.Overall it's a good looking game that has been ruined by bad AI and poor gameplay mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I tried very hard. I was hype for it for a very lomg time waiting for it to come out. And for the price mark its ok... but lets break it down. Possitives: Atomosphere. That is the absolute selling point. The artistic value put into the atmosphere and the ambient sounds are above and beyond. Horrifying and beautiful. Negatives: the character models are stiff, dialog seems forced to me and the premise is a little too cliche. And once you do come across enemies... they too are stiff and cold. There doesnt seem to be a lot of warmth with the characyers at all... no fluidity. The controls felt unbalanced and the "puzzle" aspect of the game was very rudimentary.Final grade: C If you are looking for a Wonderfully horrifying atmposhphere. This is for you. If you are looking for challanging gameplay that makes you question your survivability... maybe not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: The depth of this story is amazing. Graphically it's gorgeous. Game play wise it's extremely fun and keeps you on point. Okay... so there was a lot of talk about this game between a circle of friends of mine (and possibly some others online) about how the game was seemingly "broken". The main factor in their argument being that the guards awareness was way too "OP". However... if you play through the story... it kind of explains all of this away if you just pay attention to certain things that happen through the progression (I'm not going to give anything away... just pay attention). Other than that... the game itself was totally worth every cent I paid for it... and I would eagerly pay for another game made by these guys in the "horror" genre. I like games that focus on story and atmosphere and not so much blood and gore.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks good for its size but is poorly optimized in a number of places, leading to bad frame-rate stutter and control wonkiness.  The developers are responsive and clearly are trying very hard to improve their game and make it as accessible as possible, hence the day 2 patch based entirely on player-feedback.  I appreciate this a lot.That being said, there are a few things that hold this game back from being good.The controls are borderline-broken in several places.  The crouch mechanics are janky as all-get-out and I swear it would not let me UN-crouch in over a dozen places until I started sprinting.The GUI is flawed, making you end up mashing buttons to clear the screen whenever you pick anything up.  This is compounded by the fact that the game does not pause when you do this, so enemies are chasing/looking for you while you are stuck trying to get out of an Item-Grab screen.The story is paced very poorly.  We go from not knowing who certain characters even are to pleading with them to "not leave us!" in a moment's notice despite not earning the attachment.  The motivations of the protagonist are all over the place, and half the time I don't understand why the objectives are what they are.  She goes way out of her way to perform certain symbolic actions despite admittedly not understanding their relevance at that time in the story.  Not to mention her over-willingness to search for her son in the first place, which I would have to give spoilers in order to explain in better detail.The 4 ammo types give an illusion of varied game-play/features that don't really exist.  I only found 2 types of ammo to be relevant while the others just take up inventory space.  These are the red and yellow ammo types.  The rest do virtually nothing, save 1 spot in the entire game where 1 is required to pass a door. You can literally run past everything else in the game.There are several points where they begin employing invisible/stealth enemies directly after taking away your ability to detect them.  They also do this in segments with long and narrow hallways with dead-ends all over the place so you cannot avoid them unless you have played the stage enough to brute-force memorize the layout and enemy-placement, which I did in only a couple of tried each.  It felt like a cheap attempt at jump-scares with no agency of the player to do anything about it.  In short, the game relies on a bunch of "gotcha!" moments, which I cannot stand.  The next would be the bad Controls.  In a good number of places they jam you into a small space with a chest with a red lock that you need to aim down to shoot in over to open the lock.  The issue is that the controls do not allow you to aim down or up very far, making the shot impossible despite being literally at your feet.  This causes you to have to leave the room, open a door, and then shoot it from a distance in order to then return and pick up its contents.  Also, you have to be basically mashing your hitbox into the hit-box of the item in order for the option to pick it up to activate.  It would be a major improvement if they widened this item-pickup radius even slightly. The file size is 30 Gigabytes, which is massive considering the amount of content.  Skyrim, for example, is less than 1/3rd the file size and has over a thousand hours of voice acting alone.  I don't understand how this game is this large seeing as audio is not compressible.The price at $30 is also too high for this kind of release, at this short of a game.  Games I have played at the same price that are in the same category, but are better in more or less every conceivable way are the lies of Madison or Visage.  Smaller in size, better voice acted, better story-told, more to do, better and longer gameplay, better atmosphere and a sense of payoff at the end. This game tried hard, and I want to support the devs.  I hope to come back to this game a month and give it another play-through and have all of these issues fixed, or at the very least addressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Too many problems to name, but mostly the bad controls, the inability to defend yourself properly, bad game mechanics, bad enemies, frustrating camera, and areas where it's so unclear what you should do that it makes me wonder if the people from the different departments even talked to one another.Shame. I was looking forward to playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game!Not scary, but have some scare jump XDA lot of stuff that I wasnt expecting, just happened.If you like horror, mistery and puzzle, just get this game!It took me 11 hours to beat the game, because I was doing some challenges  XD so that was some stuff that I needed to avoid
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Unholy is classical horror genre game, where main protagonist Dorothea is searching the way to rescue her son Gabriel.This is for one side artistical gigantic wave and for other side this is complicated story with short but somehow no wide cause of important messages.The first chapter opens the game in fantastic way, the next are a bit worst but average to the point.The grand final and all execution is worth to expierence beacuse all the time classical horror background is continued and well made.The symbolical vast directions ingame are too deep for the most players. Gameplay is solid and artistical side is masterwork - congratulations and honor for Tomasz Strzałkowski. Altought the mechanics and some levels are too unobvious what made place for few gaps  and errors easly.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game to be well-designed and quite unique compared to other horror titles. Instead of relying on jump scares, it created a few genuinely creepy moments. The storyline was engaging and kept me invested throughout. Initially, I thought it was strange that your only weapon was a slingshot, but it surprisingly fit the game well. The use of masks added an interesting element, and the mechanics were solid; I didn't encounter any bugs that impacted gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: The game features creepy atmosphere with brilliant grotesque designs. It gave me Silent Hill vibes. However, it is a slow burn and loses a lot of tempo during several sections. And the AI isn't great. I'd only recommend this to players who like psychological horror games.I posted the first 90 minutes of the game on my youtube channel. You can check it out if you are interested.Finally... Thank you Duality games, for providing me a review code.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: The visualization of this game is at a very high level. The game is beautiful and captivating because a person automatically returns to the 90s of the last century. After passing the first locations, the game changes beyond recognition because we enter a new world where we will have to fight with opponents. The game has an interesting system of fighting opponents. I definitely recommend UNHOLY!!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Typical polish neighborhood. Spooky people in elevators. Nightmarish basements. Church doing some crazy stuff. People doing very bad life decisions because of minor issues they can't handle. Some mean looking guys want to beat you up because they don't like the way you look at them.The game is nice. Not great but not terrible also. Just a horror walking simulator with some stealth action and magic tricks. Graphic is nice, sound too (play on your headphones, positional sound is great). Some bugs in few places but nothing game breaking. Mobs sometime stuck and can't move but thats it. There are some puzzles but nothing too complicated. Monsters are there too, but they are not lethal threat. Good thing you don't really need to kill anything. You can choose how do you play. Game by default support 21:9 ultra-wide screens and 120 fps if that's important to anyone.edit.Okay, it took me around 8 hours to beat the game. Late chapters and ending are a bit unpolished. Hopefully few patches will fix that.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Unholy is too linear and sometimes I forgot what the story was about. I am also very confused on how to use my weapons as there isn't as much of a guide to anything. However, it is done. I completed it and yay me! - I liked the art and it was fun trying to finish it. You should get this for like around ~$15
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Although gameplay and combat is buggy, I recommend playing for the AMAZING art design, sound quality and story.The dark art direction here is some of the best I have ever seen. Often I had to stop just to check out the paintings, texture details and analyze the environmental sounds. There is a loooot going on, and it really makes this an immersive experience.Unfortunately the gameplay is buggy as hell, interaction keys often do not get triggered, doors open/close with a 1 sec delay, weapon selection system is slow and annoying, weapons itself are well thought out but do not really what intended to the enemies.If you can appreciate a well thought out Indie game that still needs some ironing out to do, I HIGHLY recommend playing UNHOLY.Note: The game looks and sounds scary, but the enemies are rather goofy in behavior, it is a good horror game to get into if you are as jumpy and easy to scare as me, as it never feels too intense.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the story was amazing! But as the game is now, it's hella buggy, and the whole blue balling of the last cut scene sent me into a frenzy. I REALLY hope that they change the ending. I got no satisfaction from finishing this game. I dread having to replay it to get the remaining achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: This is the worst game I have played in years. The controls are sloppy and sluggish. The visual presentation- models, textures, animations- are a joke. The script is a very obvious product of late-development rewrites. The mechanics are low effort stealth with some of the dumbest enemy AI I have ever seen. I expected it to be bad, after the demo, and I was still disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game.  Took me 24 hours to beat while doing a no kill challenge among others.  Was expecting a really scary game with lots of jump scares but this isn't that game.  It's spooky with a great story but not really scary.   If you enjoy story driven spooky games that won't give you a heart attack, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful and clearly well intentioned indie title that wants to be PT and Dishonored at the same time. Lots of puzzles with moon logic tendencies, but the biggest problem is the complete clunkiness of it all, especially if playing with a controller. Interaction prompts often don't work, and puzzles refuse to detect thumbstick movements, so you have to use the mouse anyway. Despite the decent story and truly gorgeous art, this is one of those dime a dozen indie horror/puzzle titles that are always skippable.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and the sound are good for this game. It is a normal linear type of game. If you are looking for horror things, you won't find them in this game, but if you like a creepy story and more creepy environment, you will like this game. It is pretty much a mid-core female protagonist game (which is not made by feminist or extreme lefty developers). The price is not bad if you want to support the developer, but that is up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: A-g-o-n-y - 5 lettersU-n-h-o-l-y - unfortunately 6 letters which ruins the whole set up. But the rest of the joke is they end with y, have an o in in the middle, etc. Look, what I’m trying to say is Unholy reeks of the same problems that made Agony so terrible. It lures you in with a proactive and dangerous spiritual city, gets you extremely excited to explore it, and then punishes you with unskipable cut scenes and awkward save spots. I wish I could recommend this game. I really really do. But at the end of the day I just did not like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game has been totally misjudged. It has a very interesting graphic style, it is simply unique. At the beginning we see a picture of harsh Poland during the communist era, but later more than once I had the impression of being thrown, into some vortex of images, Steampunk occultism created by Zdzislaw Beksinski (PS. The game's play with colors is of great importance). The game itself has a lot of puzzles more difficult or easier, and I myself admit that sometimes I had to think about what to do in it. As for the gamelay itself, a very interesting idea as to the use of emotions as a defensive-warfare mechanic. I will admit playing any probably horror games, I am coming back to this game right now to complete it. Looking at the credits, this is not a game made by a great team, and in my opinion, it really deserves to be appreciated all the more.I briefly recommend this game if you are a fan of horror games with puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: High-level designs and atmospheres with creepy environments that are amazingly detailed. I am a fan both of stealth and psychological horror games so Unholy is exactly my cup of tea. Worth mentioning the surprising gameplay mechanics (the usage of masks and emotions' ammo) and the nice even if sometimes basic puzzles.I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good horror game. I've been looking for a long time for good horror games, like Crimson Butterfly back in the day.the graphics and atmosphere are really good and the POV looks like they are aiming for VR.It is enjoyable although sometimes can be dizzy. I recommend switching on the lights whenever possible.Check the requirements, because it need a GTX 1660 minimum, and it uses it.Overall, I recommend this game if you like horror games with heavy atmosphere. I hope they add content and keep developing it
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: +very moody environment and atmosphere (reminded me a hint of Dishonored)good storygood logical tasksbeautiful art and designretro block of flats-short areas, short missions, short chaptersnot much to explore at locations, lack of interactions, exploration in roomssister-enemy appears only one time :/not much use of smoke-thingnon-sense action key at obviously barricaded and stuck doorsdumb puzzles, obvious codes, no riddles or brainwork really
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: Unholy was a real surprise to me. I had fun from the beginning until the end. The graphics are really nice, the atmosphere and sounds really do work hand in hand to pull you in.I liked the variation between dream and reality phases, the riddles were moderate and what was best for me were the enemys which aren't that ambitious to catch you sometimes. That helped me a lot since I am still not used to horrorgames, although I love them very much. (When the mobs ran in circles/were stuck in some corner, it helped calming a bit and figuring the situation out :D)One thing that bothers me is that now that I finished the game there is no option to choose a chapter or having multiple savegames, which makes it hard to get the missing achievements. If I start again and miss another thing, I have to start all over again and again. But still, awesome game. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Unholy

_childDocuments_.review: UNHOLY...a game which i have on my radar for a long time. it is truely a nice looking and atmospheric game. The gameplay is fine, the intense atmosphere is even better. It comes with fresh ideas! and gets never boring. The little riddles are easy to understand, but sometimes very hard to pass through, which i like. After a while you are be able to understand the mechanics which you are given. And here the game begins to "swallow" you in. I really recommend this to all people who like to plan where to go and how they can do it with the given stuff! Bravo to the devs. Its not for everybody, thats true:) But for me it is brilliant. If you love psychological horror with a well written story, this is for you.For me a 9,5/10, not more, not less.(the -0.5 is, because sometimes only sometimes the "ammo" not hit right, but very little cases)

name: Bloodroots
detailed_description: One-hit kill die-retry murder ballet. Chain deadly combos by improvising your kills with utterly everything you can get your hands on: from carrots to plasma guns. Die and retry until you carve your way to vengeance in this fast-paced one-hit kill beat 'em up. Betrayed and left for dead, Mr. Wolf is hell-bent on finding his killer and enacting revenge - alone, and vastly outnumbered. Thankfully for Mr. Wolf, the world is your weapon in Bloodroots - a relentless action game that unfolds across the sprawling Weird West. You’ll choreograph spectacular, ultra-violent combos by making use of everything around you, from hatchets, to ladders, to...carrots? It’s improvise or die, as Mr. Wolf fights his way to the center of the mystery: why was he betrayed? A world overflowing with makeshift weapons that not only change the way you fight, but how you get around Improvise the most deadly combos and compete for fame on worldwide leaderboards Fight your way through a variety of handcrafted levels, from forests to mountaintops Experience a twisted Western revenge tale with a deranged cast of characters

_childDocuments_.review: Rigid. Very little room for the player to do what they want instead of the presupposed momentum intended (read:expected, demanded) by the developer.The game has style, substance, charm and a good sense of slapstick, violent humor - but it is thoroughly unenjoyable.I'd like to see more from them in the future, though I cannot recommend this at its full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: This game will test your patience, at least as much as it tests your reaction time, but maybe my reaction time is badI went into thinking this game was kind of like Hotline Miami, which I quite liked. However, I felt that by comparison Bloodroots was more punishing, really requiring you to have perfect timing. I died a lot because since the camera is zoomed in so close sometimes I couldn’t react to an enemy running in from off screen in time. And my other source of frustration was the system for picking up new weapons, if there was more than one weapon close to each other if was hard to consistently pick up the weapon you wanted. In such a fast paced game picking up the wrong weapon type, or something with less durability than the weapon you wanted can lead to a lot of deaths. It also doesn’t offer you as much choice and freedom versus Hotline Miami on how you to get through each level so it was kind of repetitive by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun to play, and there's a good difficulty build-up. More and more coordination is required as the amount of enemies(and enemy type) progresses.I like how there is not one predefined way of beating a level. Levels are designed in such a way that allows the player to beat it in many different ways.some of the things I enjoyed the most:- It's an absolute blast to try out all sorts of objects as a weapon!!- The music is simply amazing!!There are enough cut-scenes and story progression so we don't get too bored of grinding levels.No tutorial or explanations at the beginning, so it may be frustrating at first for less experienced gamers. For most people, it's pretty intuitive, so not needed.I definitely recommend, it's a ton of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptionally fun and fluid to play. A large chunk of my fun was derived from trying to full combo each level. Trying to come up with good routes and variable item kills is very enjoyable. The game looks pretty has a nice soundtrack but most of all it plays very well. All the different items are unique and have fun interactions with each other. The game is as hard as you make it. When you get a perfect run it just feels so damn satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: is an extremely inconsistent game. Often times you'll find yourself stuck on scenery or expecting to traverse an area only to find yourself humping some invisible wall. When you're not negotiating the difficult to parse terrain, partly due to the wonky perspective and floaty movement, you'll be struggling with weapons that have unexpected behaviour; some times not even triggering an attack and instead leaving you wide open for an enemy to take you out instead. The presentation is great of course with its stylized visuals and over-the-top cartoony violence but otherwise I much prefer a game like . Arguably more basic but so much more enjoyable because it does exactly what you expect at all times. This is not an outright  game but merely decent at the best of times. The basic mechanics of  were simply too messy for me to appreciate the rest of the package. However, if you're not a purist' and can overlook some of these issues then I imagine you can still find some enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: This game came outta nowhere and is extremely fun to play. The flow of combat, the sheer variety of 'weapons' you can pick up to hit enemies with (yes, you can pick up literal fish, carrots and cabbages to smack enemies in the face with). I've completed 4 levels so far and its been amazingly fun. Every weapon/pick-up works differently and feels awesome. I worry its going to end soon (such games are usually quite short in length/gameplay time) and I'll be left wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game during PAX West 2018. I met the developers - they're awesome. I played the demo - it was awesome. I've got the magnets on my fridge still. I've patiently waited for this game to be released (on steam) for 3.5 years and it has not disappointed so far. The closest game to it is Hotline Miami - but this game is faster paced. The combat is fluid and I love the story so far.FINALLY
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, it's hotline Miami with more gore and much faster gameplay. I like the art style, combat, sound (though there is no memorable track for me), a huge variety of weapons, and verticality in level design! While there are not many boss battles, devs made them entertaining and enjoyable,my favorite boss is owl ladyGood job guys!But there are drawbacks also:while having vertical gameplay in this game, it feels frustrating sometimes to me. What I mean by this - I suggest adding a circle beneath our hero while he in the air. That way we will always know where he'll land. I've got many times where I cant predict where am I going to land and died afterward.I found myself distracting and not able to recognize the enemies on the level because they merge with the environment. Maybe dim the environment or add a little outline for the foeOn jumping pads I can not maintain the momentum like in other platformers where I can fly a little bit far by holding the movement button (Maybe you have done this intentional)And I feel the last few levels are longer than they should
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: What a hidden gem this is, I thought it was great! It's quite hard and you'll have to replay the levels multiple times to get it, you die in one hit, but its so fast paced and fun that it feels like the completely correct design choice. It reminded me a lot of Ghostrunner where you are an absolute machine of mayhem but fragile and die from any damage. The game also features a story which is told in 3 acts, its nothing amazing but did the job quite well and the writing was interesting and funny enough to keep me entertained for the entire game. Would definitely recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably update this review after I get further.Generally a very good game.  The gimmicks are hit-or-miss (cannon good, laser grid bad), but the game has mostly stayed open-ended and interesting.  Remember the accessibility options if an area is too tedious, you can just come back to it later.Tangentially, I love the hats.  It's a good nod to hotline miami because it works even if you have never heard of HM.  It ties into the aesthetics and motifs of the game so perfectly it was only when I saw the equip menu that I noticed they were essentially the same mechanic (in a different genre, admittedly).It's a shame the game has such sparse support, but that doesn't make it a bad purchase.A couple of bugs:The area with all the cannons leading up to the room of nothing but spikes and barrels in Act 1 had an issue where none of the cannons animated properly.  They spun like a gyroscope, clipping through the ground.  They were still perfectly usable, the aim worked fine.  idk if Wolf's hurbox tracked his model flying around in the seat since there were no enemies to test it with.The area in Act 2 right before the room with nothing but two hammer boys and scrolling lasers had some insanely buggy geometry, Wolf kept teleporting around and it was hard to tell why.  I think it was wall geometry, but I'm not 100% sure.Devs, don't be discouraged, you've done some wonderful work and made a bunch of people very happy with it.  I wish you the best of luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: As a playtester for this game's Steam release I can say with confidence that this is a really solid game with amazing gameplay. And not only that, it has a lovely indie team behind it too! Definetly pick this game up .The gameplay feels very smooth when hacking your way through levels, being able to pick up virtually anything around you as a weapon in your fight as Mr. Wolf. Even when dying a lot at points, which can happen quite frequently with the well-executed 1 hit death system, I never felt like giving up or taking a pause. For those who don't like dying much: there is an option in the settings to make yourself invincible so you can really go all-out slashing.While the story isn't the primary focus, it does deliver the drive it has to and especially towards the end it starts to become more and more mysterious. The end left me with a special hard to place yet satisfactory feeling after the remarkably well-done build-up.After the ending you can go back to re-play the levels, improve your score on them and unlock new things, like hats which give you slight benefits while playing. Replaying levels has never bored me at all and it is great to keep improving with all the different weapons. Also there might still be new content coming in the future.Overall a really outstanding game which is great to play and with nice developers who deserve all the sales and positivity.Aaand if you are still not convinced you can try the free demo and then buy the full game!
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: This aesthetic one-hit-one-kill gem has quickly become one of my favorite plug and play games for many reasons:- Gruesome and expressive art style- Challenging yet fair difficulty- Variety of enemies with exploitable weaknesses- Constant trickle of unique weapons- Level design that provokes new ideas instead of written tutorials- Surprisingly ample storytelling with distinctive character personalities- Seemingly infinite ways to approach every level- Collectible hats that give perks such as Double jump + Run faster- AND A BOPPIN SOUNDTRACKIf these features appeal to you, then 20 dollars is a small price to pay for 5+ polished hours of pure adrenaline.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It's identity and the ost are genuinely good. The story isn't that deep, but it is more complex than it initially seems. But the reason I dislike this game is rooted (see what I did there?) in what is arguably the most important aspect of this genre of games... the gameplay sucks. It has a good base, but the level design is extremely linear, which takes away all the fun of trying other strategies because the game makes it very clear what you should use for what. And when you don't, you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ die. Ironically, the best levels are exclusively the first ones. I know it sounds like a skill issue, but trust me, I would still play the game if it was hard in a challenging way, and not in an insufferable way. It is truly a sad case of a game that didn't harness it's full potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: When you're playing a hotlike (that's what I'm calling these, shut up) , precision and responsiveness are everything. Hotline Miami is an eyeblink from death, but movement and aiming are just as instant. Katana Zero has a certain halting rhythm, but your timing and the enemies are easily matched up, and the next action you need to take is always possible. Neon White is so smooth and responsive that it almost feels like you're gliding through fights.And then there's Bloodroots. Everything from which weapon you're picking up (which is important, as they have vastly different movesets), to the enemy you're targeting (which is a bigger issue as a lot of weapons seem to work on Batman rules instead of actual hitboxes) to jump timing during the platforming challenges this game has for some reason. Plus, while the graphics are stylish and charming, they make the edges and locations of objects and enemies very ambiguous, in addition to the top-down 3D perspective making aiming more uncertain than fully 2d or fully 3d games in this genre. It's pretty and the story is cool, but for a genre this unforgiving, I can't forgive the flaws in the combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have too much time on this here on Steam, but I did play it on EGS when it initally launched. I wasn't really feeling it back then, but I decided to double-dip ( I'm a sucker for this style of art ) Anyways - I have some more dedicated time  on Steam ( being familiar with how the game works already ) so I started picking apart each level to get as clean a run as possible, and it's a lot of fun to do so. You basically apply hotline miami rules here; every attack will kill everyone in one hit. And here's hwo the game mixes this up : you can use improvised weaponry all over every level, and sure - it starts out simple; but experiment a little bit - you might find some things work in ways you wouldn't expect.Every weapon has an attack ( and limit to how many kills you perform with, usually 3 ) some weps only stun enemies, some things ; like bails of hay, can be toss through fire to set things ( and pesky guards ) on fire. So why give us a ton of ways to kill? well, because it's fun! And also, because you can string a combo together for a fluid run - meaning, you took out an enemy in a successive pattern - which will count for your grade.but you can't just spam the best, easiest attack over and over - you have to mix it up and add variety ~so each level turns into a delicate ballet of balancing your available weps, the environmental props ( like carts, barrels, spikes, etc ) to your advantage, while also maintaining your combo ( and of course, not dying yourself ) each level area is separated into lil chunks, and your final enemy takedown will have an ultra cinematic flair to it ( it's neat to see, but imo - you should be able to toggle these off as an option ) The graphics are very eye-pleasing, it's running at a peppy 144fps - and did I mention there's hidden stuff, and unlockables ? ;3and a leaderboard? ';3there's a lot of good stuff to be had in this game. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions video: The Hotline Miami games are some of my personal favourites. The brilliant fusion of fast-paced action and puzzle mechanics, combined with high difficulty but pacing that moves so fast, you never have time to get mad before you're right back at it. At the time, there was really nothing like them. Blootroots takes that formula and evolves it several notches into something amazing.Gone is the neon and synthwave, replaced with a cool wilderness cartoon aesthetic, full of strange characters and creatures with some truly impressive bosses. There is a story but it's fairly standard revenge plot faire. That's not really why you're here anyway. It's all about the gameplay and Bloodroots has it in spades.Each mission is a series of crafted levels with enemies that will always be in the same places but can be taken out in a ton of different ways. Every arena is littered with weapons but to take it a step further, almost any object in the environment can also be weilded as one. Every object has a unique type of attack strategy, area of effect and animation and while some objects can only be weapons, some can also double as faster means to get around the environment. Eliminating every enemy is the goal but you have a huge number of ways to do it and with the game's use of a scoring system, online leaderboards and special modifiers you can use on previously completed levels, you're encouraged to replay them to find better and faster ways to finish.This game starts challenging and only gets moreso as you progress. Personally, I find it to be more challenging that Hotline Miami was. I'm actually not normally one for hard games but what always makes these so compelling is how the best ones have an instant restart ability. If you die, you hit a button and you're immediately back at the start of the arena with everything reset and ready to go. If the game makes you wait even a few seconds for a reload, it gives you time to reflect and get frustrated. With an instant restart, you're never given that chance and immediately, you're right back at it. For me, that makes the challenge worth it because if I mess it up, I just get right back into the action again. If Bloodroots didn't have this, it would be a far worse game but Paper Cult knew what they needed to have to nail the flow and feel of a game like this.Control response and performance are also key in games like this and while I have a fairly high-end machine, it runs very well for me. I was in some of the early betas and during those, I felt some noticeable input lag that's not present here. I never felt like I died because "I know I pressed that button in time!" Make no mistake, you'll die in this game a lot but at least in my experience, it was never the game's fault. But hey, there's a demo available so you can always confirm how it runs before you buy.Paper Cult absolutely nailed the formula a game like this requires and I've been having a blast with it. I definitely intend to finish it and that's not something I do with every game I get press code for. If you like tough but satisfying games in the Hotline Miami kind of vein, Bloodroots is not to be missed. This should be getting more attention than it has so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotline Miami on speed. This is a great top down action game, it's fast paced, very fun, a lot of creativity and a very strong level design.  The OST has some really nice bangers as well.There is A LOT of weapons everywhere and your goal is to power through levels by any means necessary. Use a pistol, a scythe, a snowball, a fish, an explosive barrel, a mini gun and others more or less crazy alternatives. It's all about speed, making combo and using different weapons to try to get the highest score possible. You can unlock hats that have various effect by defeating bosses or reaching a certain highscore. The hats have a real Hotline Miami vibe of course, you can tell the devs are fan of that game, you feel their passion throughout the game.The artstyle is quite unique and beautiful, all the different elements of maps are well highlighted, making combat really fluid. There is also a good variety of enemies from your basic John to miniguns, riflemen and big boyz just smashing the ground. Sometime they have protection and are immune to melee or range attacks so you have to find the right type of weapon in the heat of battle.There is also boss fights, which are a combinaison of platforming and combat. They all pretty good and always original. The only issue I could find was that sometimes the perspective will kill you. There is a bit of platforming here and there but  sometimes you don't really see where you are going to land due to the complexe level design and the fixed camera.The game has a correct length for his price, around 15h to 100% for me (there is collectibles, high scores and one speed running cheevo to get for the full achievement, not very hard but very enjoyable)So yes I really recommand this game, very fun and explosive top down action game, very arcade. For the fan of Hotline Miami, Honk Kong Massacre and other of that type,  fan of action games in general and achievement hunters. The price is good, the whole production value is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Hotline Miami but you can kill enemies with rubber ducks and carnivorous fishes not to mention hundreds of other weapons, not to mention it looks like Samurai Jack, not to mention level design is SO good, not to mention it is really fun to play. My only complain is that bossfights are not great, mainly the second boss looks like a dollar store Fury boss wannabe. That was pretty stupid tbh. But that was the only stupid thing in this game. Assuming you don't consider killing a person with a rubber duck "stupid".Recommended. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: This game started out fun and interesting but as soon as you reach Act II it turns so unforgiving it is terrible to play, enemies are too stacked and the amount of weapons with 3 attack charges is scarce, you'll also need to pay attention to several ranged attackers and annoying platformers with terrible camera angles and to top it off your checkpoints are spaced so even if you did manage to pass a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ section on your 10th attempt you might need to redo that because the next section is even worse and you didn't have a checkpoint between them. The game has a really nice concept and mixes the gameplay with different platforming sections such a sidescroller and a bullet hell-esque boss fight (really neat) but these things are overshadowed by the terrible camera angles, bad platforming and annoying as hell enemy composition

_childDocuments_.review: Hyperspeed cartoon Western Hotline-Miami-like with platforming. Grab a weapon, introduce a mook to it, grab the next one, keep the flow going. Knives, axes, harpoon guns, barrels, giant shoes, ladders, snowballs, bits of fence, fish and the titular root vegetables are just some of the murder tools available, and they function in many different ways. Planning and speed are both indispensable here.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super cool game! I discovered it during the steam festival and the demo was giving me high hopes. No deception after buying it. The game is fast and very satisfying. I like to play casually and I'm not chasing the perfect score but there's definitely room for competitiveness, which is good. The movement are very satisfying and you'll love discovering how you can interact with all the obstacles and objects in the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, of course these kinds of games will be shorter, but the story and the game play are definitely worth the price they're asking. It also has amazing replay ability since you always want to do better than your last personal best on a level. Also, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the amount of weapons in this game is absolutely insane!
