If you're thinking about buying this game, I highly recommend you do so as you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: tl;drif you liked Hotline Miami for its gameplay, buy Bloodroots!Devs took few concepts from Hotline Miami and implemented them in a great way.The game revolves around OHOK *one hit one kill* mechanic, in a Western setting with really nice graphics.There are many cut scenes and part of them are hand-drawn animated and the other part is played in a game.Many weapons to choose from — carrot, fish, axe, ladder, barrel, rifle — a few examples and each weapon has it's own perks, e. g. You can jump on the barrel and ride on it, killing the enemies, and then jump off of it and it'll go in the last direction you were steering it at, killing even more enemies!You can set few weapons on fire, and they'll spread fire to enemies and environment.With ladder and other long weapons, you can make big jumps, and they tend to have a great AoE damage.The skill entry level is quite low, it is accessible (you can make changes to the gameplay at menu), but the skill ceiling is quite high, e. g. I finished 1-1 level in around 7 minutes on my 1st playthrough of that level (yes, you can go back and repeat previous level, there is even global leaderboard for points and for time), on 2nd time i finished it in around a minute.You can collect headgears, like in HM and they change the way you play, although these headgears work only on repeated levels (in example there's a regular Mr. Wolf's wolf headgear, there's a bear headgear which strengthens your punches, or a fish headgear which inverts Your movement *gg finishing level in that*).Overall the game's very nice and with 5/10 being a medium game, I'd give Bloodroots 7.5-8/10 as a great game.#editI forgot about music—it's great! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of games like Hotline Miami, Ghostrunner, and pretty much any one-hit-one-kill type games, this is so far up your alley it may as well have made refuge in your home. Just pure adrenaline fueled fast paced brutal decimation. I have been thoroughly enjoying myself, albeit the few times that I've quit and come back later due to an area being particularly difficult; but with the amount of objects in the world and freedom to path out exactly how you want to murder the enemies in the zone, allows for a lot of general tinkering with different scenarios.Also, whoever had the idea to make a kill cinematic for every weapon deserves a medal. There's nothing quite like getting 3/4 of the way through a zone, booty on full tilt, not knowing if this is the run or not; then all of the sudden a quirky animation plays of Mr. Wolf just absolutely dumpstering a dude with a carrot. It's such a satisfying way to dictate the end of a zone and allows for just a general relief whenever you hit the animations. One of the most satisfying experiences I've ever had and I'm only halfway through the game. It's a bloody good time, y'all.
_childDocuments_.name: Bloodroots

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game, a couple of minor quirks aside. Plays kinda similarly to Hotline Miami, with more of an emphasis on using a variety of weapons, and with more enemies that have different conditions that must be met to kill them (No melee, no ranged attacks, etc.) The combat is smooth; not as fast as HM which makes it a bit less chaotic, and very satisfying. My only real issue is that you are at the mercy of the autotargeting at times, and it can be... quirky. I found sometimes that I would go to pick an item off a table, only to pick up the table itself when I wouldn't want to, or throw a vase only for it to fly towards a barrel 45 degrees away from where I wanted it to go. These sort of things are hard to avoid though. What took me by surprise was the quality of the writing. Whilst the story isn't anything groundbreaking, it plays with structure and the method of storytelling more than I'm used to seeing in games. We aren't give exposition dumps, but we instead have compelling characters revealing more about our protagonist through their relations and feelings towards him, which are written evocatively. Overall just a pleasant way to spend a few hours; well worth your time!

name: Hokko Life
detailed_description: Latest Content Additions! Introducing the Desert Islands Distractions Update! Set your sights on a faraway tropical island, brimming with all sorts of new life for you to discover and add to your collection from tropical fish to beautiful butterflies. Grab the brand-new Artefact Detector and become a renowned archaeologist as you uncover hidden artefacts and exquisite gems. About the Game Hokko Life is a cosy, creativity filled community sim game. Step off the train into the town of Hokko and get settled into your new home! This quiet village needs your help to turn it into the charming rural town everyone loves. With hammer and paints in hand it's up to you to design, build and decorate homes for all of your new friends! Busy yourself away in the dusty old workshop and let your creativity flow! Craft materials and combine them in whatever way you desire to create new and wonderful furniture and items for your town. Collect flowers, mix paints and use them to design wallpapers, flooring and even clothing! Will you design an urban-industrial furniture collection or maybe a bright flowery wallpaper set? With all of the workshop at your disposal, you'll have complete freedom to design a town your villagers will absolutely love. Want to share your charming creations with other players? Then upload it to the Hokko Community Store, allowing you to share items, peruse showfloors and download other players' creations with the sharing of a simple code. Join the weekly challenge themes and enter for your chance to be featured! 📐 Design & Paint 🎨 Head into the workshop to put your own spin on items in the game. Use the design table to build your own furniture, combining different shapes and materials in a simple but powerful editor. Get out those brushes and throw some colour down. You can paint furniture, wallpaper, flooring and even clothes! Make your village truly your own. 🏠 Build & Decorate 📦 Enlist the help of the resident builder and start expanding the town. Place buildings wherever you like and get them ready for new villagers to move in. Customize the interior and exterior of any home, choose designs and place furniture to make a home your new friends will love. Tire of the layout of your village, want to spice things up? Then move your houses and buildings at any time, for free! 🎣 Icthyology & Entomology 🦋 Looking for something to do? Then spend a quiet morning at the various fishing spots around the world of Hokko and build your fishing collection. Fish have unique habits, and require different craftable bait, so you'll need to vary your approach from one fishing spot to the next. Then, spend the lazy afternoon in Hokko with a net in hand, catching and collecting the critters fluttering and scuttling about the town! You'll find a whole range of insects for you to catch and build your collection! 🪓 Extra Curricular Activities ⛏️ Looking for something extra to do? Introduce yourself to Hokko’s townsfolk offer a warm welcome, and with varying personalities, they all make for fantastic friends! or push out on resource gathering expeditions as you chop, dig, mine resources to fuel your creative endeavours! and don't forget to take part in the myriad seasonal events, weekly creator challenges and more!

_childDocuments_.review: I only have a bit more then 5 hours so far but I must say its wayyyy better then I expected it to be. You can decorate how you want, even create whole new furniture and download other players creation for free and just use their furniture sets. I have a whole Ghibli town so far mixed with Stardew Valley. Villagers are super cute and the game is really really relaxing. Im positively surprised about this game.If you like Animal Crossing or just a relaxing simulation game this is for you. Maybe you missed out on Animal Crossing because you dont have a Switch or have a child and you look for a cute game, then I also recommend it. Im glad I bought the game after it being forever in my Wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early access review. You fall asleep on the train, miss your stop, seemingly forgetting why you're in a new little town (or you just don't care). Then you end up mooching off of someone's attic space as you start gathering and decorating around the island. The music is nice, the atmosphere is relaxing, the bugs aren't too bad. It does feel a little unfinished (as it should I suppose), but overall it's cute. What I want to see in improvement is mostly the lack of direction. Maybe use some story to string the player along? Honestly when you're like me with the attention span of a squirrel, there's a lot of things that are hard to figure out on your own. I seriously hate the 'furniture design' thing and I wish there would be more pre-made crafting options. For example right now, I'm stuck on a villager's quest who wants a bed. I am then supposed to design a bed on my own using a Bed blueprint you find out you have to purchase - but then what? I spend too long figuring out how to put some planks on it piece by piece and a cushion and call it a bed, the quest says it's ready but the villager keeps saying it's unfinished with no further instructions. Stuff like that just makes me want to instantly quit. Especially when there's no story to follow and you don't know what else to do. It would be helpful if there are instructions for how to do things in the game in general, like a tutorial if you will. Another thing are the settings, if you could reach them as well as the controls in the in-game menu, that would be amazing. The perception is a little wonky as well, I can't tell if the bug is behind or in front of me sometimes, or where the fishing rod will hit. It would be nice if you could have quick slots for tools using say 1-5 or something.I think it has potential but it definitely needs more updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun! You can interact with a lot of villagers and do tasks for them such as building objects to suit their needs when they request it. My favorite part about everything is the ability to freely customize or create furniture/objects. Decorating the inside of houses or outside in the town areas is something I also find exciting to do because you can use those created objects that you created or by somebody else to create the space that you want to be made. Only one developer is actively working on this game and seeing and playing the game from the start of Early Access a lot has been improved and a lot of content has been made. I'm eagerly anticipating more updates and improvements after the game comes out of Early Access.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Its not an Animal Crossing clone. If you take everything from Animal Crossing and make it more Harvest Moon you have this game. No real time no stress no durability no stamina houses build quick the art style is unmatched the music is entrancing 5/5 its also on Xbox and Switch. I love it and best of all not early access. This is a national treasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Just another farming game. You do whatever those NPCs ask you to, generally gathering this and that for them. In this game, the dialogues and conversations with the NPCs are so boring, feels like talking to AI. If you just want to play a chilling game, this is a good one; you can do whatever you want without placing a sequence. You can go planting all day and night or decorating many houses and your farm, it is all up to you. It is better to put it this way. However, we have a ton of these types of games. I am expecting something different.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: It wants to be Animal Crossing really bad, but there's a few reasons it isn't. Attention to detail is a big one - characters won't look at your character when they talk to you, there are no jingles when items are placed, or obtained... there are footsteps but that seems to be the extent of it. I'm not sure how the day night cycle works either. My character had infinite stamina, which definitely can be a problem (no gameplay limitation which allowed me to play too long and not feel I had finished a day to save and continue another real life day). I could keep going ... The game generated this expectation with EVERYTHING that it'd be like Animal Crossing but then it just keeps throwing fetch quests at me. Pick this up, place these things, cut these trees. This is MMORPG game design in a single player "chill" game. Not for me, maybe it is for you?
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Unpolished dev project, can't call it a game. Very unpleasant and slow "gameplay" and uncomfortable keyboard/mouse controls. Unbearable "tutorial". That's where I left it.I'd give a shot, if not the unskippable pacing of the start and awkward camera, and plastic interactions with NPCs... But I admire players who got 100+ (or 500+) hours in this, maybe I'm not the person for this kind of game. I DID want to immerse myself into this cute universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great game. It just seems to keep getting better. There are achieves now, which is nice. The sandbox aspect of this game really adds a nice creative element to the game that keeps you engaged. I really love it. The village people are awesome, the quests are quick and fruitful and the farming/fishing is tons of fun. You should give it a try. You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hyped about this game, but it feels so clunky and rough to start during the beginning but that's not the worst thing about the game. It had so much potential with all the Steam features, like Online features, sell your stuff online or buy from others, meet random other players etc plus this game nearly don't get any support with updates or new content and it feels like the devs quit working on this game. It's a missed opportunity from the devs to create a awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: simply put, i haven't played a animal crossing game since city folk. WHICH WAS 13 YEARS AGO. Its wild how this game "Hokko Life" comes out of nowhere basically recreating those beautiful childhood memories in the matter of minutes. I'm glad i picked it up :)Mind you, i only played animal crossing off and on when i was really bored and just wanted to have a fun time in those days of dial up internet and not having a gaming computer.Do be advised. This is its own thing, Don't expect every aespect from animal crossing to be pushed over to Hokko Life. Its fun its own right and i really enjoy it so i definitely recommend giving it a shot if you've played any animal crossing game in your life. This is going to be the closest thing we'd ever get to animal crossing being ported to PC.I know its also in development but a multiplayer aespect would be a nice touch so you can join your friends worlds too. Just like the old days of animal crossing on the wii/ds
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about the potential about this game, but it's... lacking. It's a mix of Animal Crossing and MySims, and the idea is cute, but that's about it. It's a very slow start, and even after a few after hours of playing I feel like I'm barely making any progress. The camera and movements take a while to get used to since they feel jagged. Everything feels very repetitive and you have to sleep a lot just to progress. Overall, it feels lackluster.Pros:-very kid friendly-nice music-Naruto runningCons:-limited options for character creation and the scales were confusing due to lack of labels-the "what to do" list at the top of the screen is small and it's hard to understand what to do at first-the plot just kind of throws you in without having a character as an introduction (think Rover or Mayor Rosalyn)-you have to wait for things to spawn (which is fine) but you have to sleep a lot for any progress-some grammar mistakes that aren't a big deal but it was offputting
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend! A cute, cozy, farm game with talking animal villagers. Although a little frustrating, I love how you can get creative and make different things in the workshop. You can upload and share your creations with others in your own personal store, I just wish there were more spaces in the store to upload more personal creations.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: If the first few in game days is any indication of what Hokko Life has in store, then prepare yourself for extreme disappointment.  Hokko Life does not stick its landing and, if anything, feels like a void shell of a template rather than an actual game; early access aside, the early steps of this experience were shallow and terribly misdirected.After creating a character and doing some introductory tasks of cutting down a tree, making some benches and later cleaning the beaches of trash... the game just up and vanished.  You're suddenly left to your own devices to do... nothing.  I cut down a few more trees, later planted some trees and flowers at a request, gave someone a fish when asked to do so and... that was it.  I went to bed, found absolutely no new tasks from anyone in the city upon the new day, so I waited hours in game for something new - something different - and was presented with a new potential villager at the Inn.  But still, an entire day wasted with having done nothing, because nothing exists to be done.You get your first axe free and later make a shovel, but you have no fishing rod or bug net so there are no collection tasks you can occupy your time with.  Another sleep, and another day with no one asking for anything, it's as if... I finished the game?  That's surreal and impossible.  I discovered this next day that I could pick up items from my villagers houses, Mei and Tola, and so I stole all their worldly possessions and sold them to Moss in order to buy a pick and a bug net, as well as two bag upgrades, and I still have one thousand paw-coins to spare!  I've now been collecting butterflies and  to catch fish but the minigame is out-of-this-world terrible and I never want to experience that ever again.  In any case, later that night, a realtor arrived to set up shop in the town the next day, so I slept.The next sun arrived and there was no new shop, it's under construction of course, so sighing, I realize I have yet  day of literally nothing to do, because, you guessed it, no one had any tasks for me.  All I can do is catch more butterflies, ignore the stupid fish, maybe cut down and replant new trees (for no reason because I have nothing to craft), and... just wait.Eventually the flowers bloomed and I was able to turn them in, later converting them into potted plants and unlocking the ability to do designs!  So... I made a bridge!  I used the bridge to access previously unattainable areas, only to locate: nothing.This isn't a game, it's a drawn out and mundane preview, at best.  The intro should catch you and encourage you to move on and find what's over the crest of the next hill... but instead we're presented with the makings of a game with no real game at all.  Here's the thing: I had to sell the other townsfolk possessions to have enough money to buy the blueprint for the bridge, the pickaxe and the bug net.  If I didn't do that, I'd  of Hokko Life because the progression would have been .  It's a cute, well written story, so far, but there's literally nothing to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Too many bugs for my taste... Game looks fun, but the whole thing is not fun when you constantly hit a wall (sometimes invisible...). In a few hours I was blocked by an invisible objects, I had to restart my whole character as I didn't get stairs which blocked any further progress, requests I've been making for people which are completed are not actually count towards the goal which is not giving me rewards blocking further progress... And those are not like new issues, some of them were actually reported on steam and dev haven't fixed them :(
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful. It is like if Animal Crossing and old school Harvest Moon had a baby, but with far more design and customization options. From the animal villager aspect all the way to the farming, it is such a wonderful adventure. The game is constantly being tweaked and the developers listen to the fans. You can join the discord and voice your opinion and will be HEARD. For anyone who loves the games listed above, this game will be an amazing addition to your library :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game at all in this current moment, at least due to the one major bug that seems to be happening with the game: Unable to even load into the main menu screen and crashing before can even play. This doesn't seem to be a thing only happening to me, since looked up about the game and this seems to be an issue. And yes, I understand it's early access and I can understand small bugs and glitches when inside the game, but a bug that doesn't even allow to enter the game is a major flaw to me. So unless the developer of the game makes a patch to allow the game to be playable, I can't recommend it. Maybe I will buy it again (currently refunding it) when the game it patched to not crash when trying to simply load it up, but right now, I will wait and see what comes of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and had it on my wishlist for months.  I ultimately decided it is not playable in its current state.  I made it about 9 in-game days in before it just was too boring to continue.  There are a few early quests, one of which (planter quest) requires you to skip multiple in-game days just to move time along to the point that the required items can be collected.  There is not much of a way to get money in the beginning to get houses going for people to move in.  The dialogue trees just stop with the NPCs and they act as though you should know what you need to do next.  One keeps recommending I go fishing with no net and no bait to pass the time, with no indication of how to get those items.  You're told to place items in the town square which are then destroyed as soon as the real estate office gets built.  I waited for a few updates but it seems as if the beginning of the game has not been given any new quests, clearer direction, or anything much at all to do.  My playtime consists of 2 "tutorial" playthroughs as I got softlocked the first time and had to delete my save file and restart.  Perhaps this is the curse of early access games, but sadly there just wasn't enough content in the early game to make me want to keep playing.  They keep adding later game content that I'm too bored to figure out how to get to.  Hopefully they will increase the initial game content to a point that it's more fun and feels more like an Animal Crossing style game instead of an exercise in wandering from building to building only to find that there are no quests available and nothing but a couple of pieces of grass to sell.  I would wait on buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: [Updated] Wow... just Wow... Tried to give it a chance despite inital irritations. That was a bad decision. You know how the game is about designing your own furniture? You can design your own containers to put stuff into, too. You know what happens when you delete the blueprint for an old container design from your workbench because you got a better one and don't want to build it anymore? What happens is, that all containers of the old design get deleted from the world, WITHOUT WARNING AND INCLUDING ALL ITEMS CONTAINED WIHTIN! Say goodbye to everything collected during the entire game. Now i've got the choice to go back to an old save and lose multiple hours of progress, or keep the save and lose everything ever collected. My choice will be to uninstall this mess of a game and keep others from wasting their time on it. The game has some nice ideas, but also some serious game breaking bugs and balancing issues. I can just recommend to stay away to save you from the frustration.TL;DR: Deleting a blueprint can delete all your stored items.PSA: Does not offer ultra-wide resolutions. Can force them by editing config files, but some menus are cropped or awkwardly laid out.Fun fact: The "Exit game" button on the main menu does not work if you have not started a game yet... seriously?

_childDocuments_.review: Tackling some issues other people have brought up:- This game may be similar to AC, but it is not. Very centered on customization possibilities and town expansion. - You unlock infinite sprint after some days and unlocking merit badges- The crafting may be tedious, but the limits are endless (resizing, rotating, etc.). You can literally build ANYTHING if you are willing to put in the time. I got the hang of it pretty quickly.This game has incredible customization opportunities. Furniture and decoration creating, house placement, item placement, and the possibilities are limitless. You don't have to wait days to move a house. You can just do it. Moving furniture with items in them (dressers, wardrobes, tables, refrigerators, etc.), you can just move them. No need to remove all the junk inside. I think this game avoids more of the annoying aspects of animal crossing for me, I do wish the villagers had more variety and were cuter though. You can also evict people immediately, I enjoy that.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I’ve reached seven hours in at the moment, and STILL only in the tutorial. Granted this is due to me not putting down another house till right now, (along with needing eight different original designs; essentially locked out of the next part of the game unless I use the janky custom design feature. I could do eight different low effort designs, but I’m not up for that) When I say that the game has strange balancing that’s what I mean. Another example is that to get to both the axe or pickaxe upgrades you first need to unlock an upgrade that has you fish up about ten treasure boxes. THESE ARE RNG BASED! Not only that, why do you have to fish to get mining or axe upgrades? The whole mayor merit unlock trees just make no sense when thought about as a typical skill system. (Plus, having RNG be necessary to unlock anything makes the grind feel worse unless the person is just that lucky)I can see why people just drop off, because this isn’t slow pacing; this is just a grind fest! If I wanted to waste my time grinding skills I’d go play a rouge like (and it’s not even skill grinding since a lot of the stuff has nothing to do with each other) I thought this was supposed to be a relaxing life sim. Actually, forget what I said about it being worth it at $4, it’s not even worth that much.Also, for the first time I listened to the game’s music and sound since I heard it was a positive point, and I am being fairly harsh. The music is… decent. I’d probably still play without it. As for sounds, they tend to be a little soft (or nonexistent; like I’m fairly certain there aren’t any sounds when talking to Dennis I think the fish npc is when offering new fish types to him, which makes me second guess if I actually did anything) One other positive I’ll give it is it does run off of a micro sd card when playing on Steam Deck fairly well (the loading is probably a couple seconds longer, but otherwise everything else seemed negligible)I’m probably done playing at this point. I gave it a long try, but sadly one of it’s major weak points is it’s biggest selling points. The creation system is just unintuitive to use and the mayor merits are completely unbalanced. I’m not sure if I’ll pick this back up.I bought this on a whim for about $4 from Fanatical, which is about the price I’d suggest buying it at. There’s quite a few issues and glitches that add up to it being nowhere near to a $20 game. This is going to sound odd, but I got this because the graphics had an uncanny feel to them. I’m sure there are people who find the animal designs in this cute; I am not one of those people. They’re not bad, there’s just something off about the look; which can be said about the game as a whole.Looking at the guides, I’m apparently not even out of the tutorial yet. I’m gonna keep updating my review as I go along since none of the reviews here are all that comrehensive.One of the most annoying things is that there’s only one quick slot for items so you have to open the menu to switch the item being used (edit: quick update: there is a quick menu; on controller it’s mapped to up on the d pad. I’m going to chalk up the fact that I missed this on me playing while sick. Further update: the quick menu bugged due to the UI stacking issue. It stuck on screen and stopped working. Welp. Saving and quitting thankfully fixes it)There was also an issue in the character creation where the right stick was mapped to BOTH the rotation of the character and menu scroll. Thankfully, it’s not a long menu, but it’s still annoying. (I was playing on Steam Deck; I didn’t touch the controls, so this is how it’s mapped by default) Textboxes spawn outside the screen (this I understand a bit more than the others, but it’s still annoying)Little less forgivable is that UI occasionally overlaps making things unreadable or certain elements clear quickly due to this (probably another reason why I’ve missed some information)The map (this is an unlock) is poorly implemented for this kind of game. It only shows the current area the player is in. When the game is focused on quests for characters that can move in DIFFERENT AREAS this makes the game annoying. I thought the map would help, it does not.The mine is probably the WORST I’ve ever dealt with (I get limiting players from just going down all the way when there isn’t a stamina system, but having the player stop after three steps and a popup saying “it’s a bit too dark” EVEN with the lamps down makes it tedious to deal with. You only get to one rock before you have to put another lamp down, if you’re lucky. Why hasn’t anyone else brought up how tedious this is? Even having to do this once, I’d rather have a stamina system)There are probably other issues; I know I’m not that far in yet. The story is extremely simplistic, to the point that the player character doesn’t even have a backstory before stepping off the train to this town. It seems to be implied that the player is the mayor now, but I don’t remember anything coming up about that. (Granted, I’m getting over a cold as well, so it’s entirely possible I wasn’t paying attention all that well)NONE of the characters have personality (the designs stand out, but that’s not really a substitute) There are a lot of unnecessary features (like a photo mode, follow mode, emotes?) It makes the balancing seem off since these get unlocked before some important game mechanics. (And don’t seem to have a point?)The game is a very slow burn. It’s the kind of thing that’s not going to interest everyone, though I’ll probably keep playing due to buying through a third party service so I can’t refund.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a game you'll enjoy if you need a plot (spoiler: there isn't one), or a game that can be 'beat', or are looking for challenge rather than a time sink. I kept expecting the game to open up and get interesting, but in the end gave up and turned to a guide to see what unlocks were left. There wasn't anything I felt worth the necessary grinding for. Many of the 'objectives' in this game are basically you verse the random number generator and gave me no more sense of achievement than rolling a double-six with dice. There's no lore in the game and the characters (while graphically distinctive) are functionally interchangeable.Game's unique selling point is the ability to design your own items. This is done to an extent I haven't seen in other games before, allowing you to build up your sofa (bed, chairs, decorations etc) from scalable, rotatable primatives in a basic 3D editor. These can then be uploaded and shared with the community (and you can also download other peoples designs as well).I encountered a game blocking bug in the tutorial after an hour mark. I reported it, and received excellent support.While this game is not for me, I did get 10 hours out of it, experienced excellent technical support, and didn't buy at full price as I got it as part of a Humble Choice subscription.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was on the fence about buying this game for a while, since I saw a lot of negative reviews saying the experience was shallow and that Animal Crossing or Stardew Valley are better. If you are a fence-sitter like I was, then I hope this review helps highlight the strengths and weaknesses of the game better.First of all, no, Hokko Life is not as good of an experience as something like Animal Crossing: New Horizons - but at the same time, it is pretty much 1/4 of the price - and this is reflected in the game itself. Hokko Life is very much like Animal Crossing but scaled down in quality and design, and then balanced out with the unique furniture creation mechanic. I think the best game to compare this to is actually MySims (for those who remember that game.) It's basically a way better version of MySims, and a worse version of Animal Crossing. I think what really makes or breaks this game is the furniture design element, which I was extremely interested in when I saw this game for the first time. I would say it is pretty much the core mechanic of this game, much like it was for MySims as well. If you don't like the idea of designing your own furniture, I will be completely honest, you will probably find this game a bit hollow and lacklustre.If you saw the game online or in the trailer, and thought the furniture creation part of the game looks really good and tempts you to buy it, you will probably enjoy this game a lot. If you are just looking for an experience similar to Animal Crossing, then you might be a little more disappointed as it is a more shallow version of that - and if you are looking for a farming simulator like Stardew Valley then I think you'll be very disappointed because farming really doesn't seem to be a major part of this game, more like an additional activity to fill out the ingame days. I would also like to mention that the game does have a lot of jank, there are definitely areas for improvement in the way the game handles - my main gripe is that it's very difficult to select multiple small objects that are very close together when designing furniture - it would be great to be able to group certain objects together while you're editing just to make it easier. And I have also encountered some minor bugs throughout the game (especially at the start) but so far they have just been annoying at worst. The last game-design element I wanted to mention is probably not something that anybody else cares about but me - but for any insect lovers out there, the bug catching in this game is just butterflies and moths, no beetles or anything like that unfortunately. Which is odd, because the fishing is actually quite diverse. I also would have loved to be able to use the bugs and fish in crafting furniture to make my own aquarium or something. That would be great.Lastly I want to go over the art direction. It's very hit-and-miss in my opinion. Some of the characters are really cute and I've quickly found some favourites just like I did for Animal Crossing, but some of them really don't land at all and come off rather uncanny (the shop-keeper giraffe character is definitely the creepiest) I find the best characters are the ones with more cartoony eyes and unique designs, and the worst are the ones with garish colours or more realistic eyes that twitch around unnervingly. There's also some issues with shadow and lighting I think. When you place things like shelves in your house, even when you have the lights on it can cast shadows on everything on the shelves underneath making them look bleak and boring. All-in-all, Hokko Life is a game mainly about customisation. You can pretty much make anything you want - and this is the game's strongest element. If you buy the game for any feature other than that, you might find this game underwhelming and bland. If you love the idea of making your own furniture and designing your town or house around a very specific idea or theme, you will probably really like this game, warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to begin my review with the fishing, The fishing part was unclear to me but then I got it. This is for Keyboard/Mouse people. When the fish bites, it will ask you to hit the E key. Do that. Then hold down the left mouse button until it starts jerking and gets angry yellow. If it's getting angry yellow, let loose of the mouse. Generally, it will ask you to pull left or right at this point. Pull left = A key. Pull right = D key. Just hold them until the fish is in the middle of the bar.  You may have to re-tap and hold the A or D key. Then left mouse again. I thought you had to repeatedly tap the A or D key but no. Just hold them. It's actually much faster that way. Now on to my actual review and some tips:I was a bit put off by the reviews, at first, but I decided to try it and I have to say I love it so far. It is slow-going at the start, with money and supplies, but now (in Summer of the first year) I have no lack of anything. You quickly realize what plants you'll need going forward and can create massive gardens and forests. Summertime provides ridiculously expensive butterflies so money in Summer is easy.  In the beginning, I just slept through days that were raining to give the trees I'd planted time to grow and there were no adverse affects. I also built houses for ten residents before I built a house for myself. lol  The only thing you get from building a house for yourself is access to four other-people-built-them structures (in the computer in Moss's store). I like building for myself so... having my own house was really nice as far as I can put more storage spaces in it but that's about it. Tips, if you want'em: When villagers ask for Wild Green Plants, there are no such things in the world. You have to buy the Green Plant Seeds from Moss, plant them, and then dig them up. Not simply harvest the tops of them. Watch out for when Moss sells Brown Plant Seeds because those are super important and rare in the world. Plant some asap. Hold on to all the stone and chalk you get early game.  It will help you immensely. Plant conifers early on, as many as you can. You can completely fail orders from villagers and be fine. They're 100% forgiving. I built a bridge when I had access to the blueprint (no one asked for a bridge) and it didn't work when I put it on the river. So I thought I didn't have access to the rest of the world yet. Duh, my bridge was simply too short. It has to be at least 8 spaces long. The designing in this game takes some getting used to, but is pretty cool once you get used to it. I've barely gotten into the paints (I now have one of each because that's how I roll) so I'm looking forward to making floor designs and wallpaper.TL;DR: This game is fun. Otherwise I wouldn't have played nearly 20 hours in the last three days. Far few games these days are actually fun and this is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state I can not recommend this game.I am a big fan of the Animal Crossing games, and there is no 2 ways about this, this is heavily inspired by Animal Crossing, but it does have its own unique charm to help make it a little more its own game. The devs obviously loved Animal Crossing, but wondered "what if" a lot, for example "what if people can make their own furniture", "what if you didn't rely on a real time clock" Sure its pretty good from that stand point there is enough to make this different to Animal Crossing. Which is nice.Now I get that this game is in Early Access so I can forgive some of the bugs and other issues. One of the issues I have mostly is when you use tools, the tool has a "hit highlight" that follows a grid like system, you think you have the tool on the item you want to remove (say a tree stump) but nope, you dig a hole instead, you get away from the location then the item pops up. Again these little teething troubles I can deal with.But this game is broken badly, you get to eventually design your neighbours homes and the like. which is a great feature too.. but what it also lets you do is take items from your neighbours and store them in your backpack. Ok so not a big deal there must be something that stops you taking them out the house right, nope none what so ever, so within the first "day" I was able to rake up a nice 5k "coins" or whatever the currency is here, allowing me to buy a lot of stuff that I shouldn't really be able to buy this early on. I have also found a weird duplication glitch, when planting flowers I had a full inventory went to use one of the items and after planting one item I picked up some clay, this made my inventory full, and I was able to continue planting the flowers (I only had 4 seeds) multiple times - I had dug up a load of holes as I was testing to see what happens if you plant things close together.These bugs aside, which I am sure will get fixed and/or addressed... we also have another problem.This game doesn't feel "alive" it feels dull and boring, the Animals don't seem to have any real emotions behind them, they don't seem to have any goals (and they don't have any furniture now either) The missions plod along slowly, there is a point in the game where you will be skipping time, you are asked to pick some flower petals to continue what I can only assume is the tutorial.. but the flowers take 3 days to plant, so its a case of go to bed, wake up next morning check the shop, buy anything you don't have, then go straight back to bed... Sure you can try to catch bugs/fish to pass the time if you have the right tools, but you want to progress through these missions and hopefully expand the map a bit... Also the NPCs you need to talk too, the one that helps you build homes you are told "they sometimes come here during the evenings" I just thought alright, I will rest up for 6 hours and take a look.. and there they were waiting for me... I know this sounds like I am nitpicking especially after I said how slow these "missions" seem to progress, but I wasn't expecting this person to show up the same evening we got told about them, I was expecting a little longer.As it stands right now, this game needed a little more fleshing out, It feels pretty empty at the moment. Maybe in a few months time? Who knows.. Good luck to the developers I may re-purchase this when it comes out of Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far, the most promising Animal Crossing/Story of Seasons/Stardew Valley/Harvest moon hybrid project on the market. _childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life is a charming little farming/city building sim. I enjoy the various characters and their random conversations. A major bonus to this game over others is there is NO STAMINA REQUIREMENT. This means you can do stuff all day without tiring out. I have yet to play a farming/building sim that had a fishing mechanic that I liked. Unfortunately, Hokko Life hasn't changed the streak. There's nothing wrong with the mechanic, except that catching fish takes too much time in comparison to say, just snagging a bunch of butterflies. Yes, the butterflies aren't worth as much, but I can catch SO MANY of them in the time it takes to catch a fish. Farming, so far, is a lot of work for little payout. I'm imagining that if we get a cooking update, it'll be more worthwhile. So far, a nice, tidy little EA game, with lots of good stuff in the works.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: 89.8h (100% achievement, played until 17th winter) Yes (2+ achievements). Yes (~22 achievements). No.  is a life sim where you have to finish villager's requests, gather resources, and decorate the whole island. It is targeted at artistic people who like to decorate islands and create items, with the possibility to customize almost everything. - Freedom in creating your furniture and design- Decorate the village however you want- Freedom to progress however you want - Unlockables take too long to unlock- Highly repetitive- Punishing for noncasual players - easy to get carpal tunnel if played in long sessions- Lifeless villagers- Resources can be grindy to get Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650    is a life sim at its core. There are a lot of things you can do: plant crops, mine ores, fish, treasure hunt, and forage. On top of that, you also can talk to the villagers to get a quest, which is usually taken from a randomized pool of quests. Some villagers will ask for the same thing, although you might need to make an extra effort to fulfill their request. With time, you'll recruit more villagers, and your number of requests will also grow. However, these requests end up becoming a chore, especially since they are endless - you will just get it again later if you don't finish it now. Moreover, the reward don't seem to be interesting either.  The game seems to reward casual players and punish the rest. There is barely anything that you can do every day, and you might even wrap up and sleep after a few hours. Or you can try to min-max everything, gathering extra resources so that you can finish the quests as soon as possible. The latter one will significantly eat your playtime, forcing you to spend hours each day to get the resources you need.Different plants can be planted on such a huge land and your farm will take minutes to load every time you enter it. And more plants mean more time to plant, water, and harvest, especially since you can only do them one by one at the beginning, which drives me crazy. Couple all that clicking and several hours of playing nonstop, and you'll get carpal tunnel soon enough. Or at least it does to me. I had a slight carpal tunnel syndrome years ago and it got triggered and got worse after playing this game. It's still not fully recovered by now.  Seasonal changes are not that important. There are hardly any changes to the environment from spring to fall. The only change is just the color of some trees in the latter season. Each season only brings new fish and insects to catch, which can be finished in the first few days of the season. Some crops are also plantable at a certain season, but that will take longer only because you need to water them daily until they grow up. You can progress the game however you like. Some features are locked at the beginning, which will only unlock after you continue with the main questline. There aren't any time constraints, and the only thing that would hinder your progress is the unlockables in the mayor merits.The mayor merits do a good job in setting the short-term goal at first. It has small incentives that will help you to unlock more things to do - things to keep you busy. I like this feature at first since the game is pretty empty. However, it soon becomes annoyance since the last few unlockables are hidden behind grind - some even unlock after you spent more than 1 in-game year!  Events are so boring and badly designed. There are only 2 events each season: fishing and bug catching. Both do the same thing: you need to catch a predetermined amount of bugs or fish. While the bugs are easy to catch, the fish can take longer since you need to do a minigame to catch one. However, the game doesn't seem to check the bug or fish spawn time. I once asked to catch a bug that wasn't catchable within the tournament timeframe.Sometimes, you need to be lucky to get on the leaderboard and be registered as participating in the event. Some fish can be rare to find, and the RNG might be so bad that you won't have enough despite catching the whole day. And don't get me started with the leaderboard. You'll hardly see other NPCs doing anything but the leaderboard will show one of them catch as many bugs or fishes as you, forcing you to catch more if you want to stay on top. Moreover, you need to do the catching for hours. Real-time hours.Characters are lifeless. Besides for a few NPCs that sell something to you, they will give a randomized line every time you talk to them. Moreover, all villagers have the same dialogue pool, making them less unique. Sometimes, these dialogues won't match with the current situation - there was one character who praised me for my new hair even though I haven't changed my hairstyle since I started the game. For a casual game, treasure hunting can be quite harsh. The end game forces you to hunt for pristine treasures, which can be harder to find because you need to pass a minigame with very little room for error. You need to press a button when a pointer is on a certain bar, and for someone with myopia like me, the bar is very small.The game becomes boring as you play. It was fun in the first few hours since you have a lot of things to do and unlock, but once you finish them all, all that's left is just grind. I finished most content by the end of the first season, and to get all the achievements, I had to continue playing until early winter.It took me 89h to reach the 17th winter and get all the achievements. It's mainly because I tried to stock up a lot of resources and finish a lot of content, though. You can do it faster if you only care about achievements and don't care much about stocking up. The game is easy - you can let your character not sleep at all, and it's very casual if you don't care about completion or min-maxing. I don't know why, but the game tends to crash. The game only saves when you move between screens and it hurts a lot when it crashes after I spent hours for the fishing tournament.  was fun at first - there were a lot of things to do and it gave you a lot of leeway for everything. However, it becomes boring as you play since you'll be left with grinding. The worst part is watering the crops. You can only water one by one and the unlockables for mass watering are only available in the early fall - meaning two-thirds of the game. It came so late that it gave me carpal tunnel and ate my sanity. To be honest,  is enjoyable if you like to create things - I had fun doing so. However, you also need to grind for materials to freely do that, and the grind is not enjoyable. The game just hates people who are not playing it casually and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Hokko Life for a couple hours and I truly think it is a game with a lot of potential. While it seems inspired by staples in the life sim genre like ACNH or SDV, it's unique and in my opinion, a well-done balance of multiple elements I like about these other games. The fact it isn't locked behind 24hrs clock but still incorporates elements like new villagers instead of a fixed story (like SDV or HM/SoS), while still having tons to do on any given day gives it a lot of potential into becoming a staple in its own turn. The design aspect is particularly innovative and reminds me of MySims. Now, with that said, the game is in Early Access, and it is very buggy. Some bugs are minor, others are game crashing and sometimes even require a restart which, for the casual player, is a bother. It's good these bugs are being squashed NOW because later in game, a restart would definitely turn people off. I will also say the beginning of the game is slow and while the game is supposed to be chill, the first days should allow for more engagement rather than spending a week in-game in tutorial type quests. I also wish the game was more explicit about how to unlock or discover new things. I get the idea is to give the player freedom; but it's important for the beginning to be guided in order to understand how to use that freedom if that makes sense. All in all, I think there's a lot of potential in Hokko Life and I'm excited to continue playing and discovering what the dev has in store! It's nice to see new games in the genre that are wanting to innovate and take risks : )

_childDocuments_.review: Let Me Start by saying i was SOOO excited about this game, I had watched it for months anxiously awaiting its release! Started recording my lets play/review and 14 minutes into the game i experienced a bug. I reported it through the game, on the discord and on steam. I also saw it was posted in there discord as "known Bug" and we were given steps to follow to delete the save file to wipe the world (Instead of giving us the option in the game to start a new world) however those steps did not help this game breaking bug for me or 2 friends that were also playing it. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't gotten all the way through this game yet, but I find myself actively wanting to play it and for long periods at a time sometimes.  It is simple and relaxing yet complex and active if you want it to be and any level of either in between.  Some resources have a finite amount collectible per in-game day and others have no limit so you can gather as much as you want and all day and all night if you want, once you have the tools to do so.  I love a game that allows you to sleep but doesn't force you to, especially when sleeping can allow you to skip some time.  Hokko Life even allows you to choose how long and when you want to sleep.  Double thumbs up for that already.  The game runs smoothly even on my computer and only lags a tiny bit for a tiny time when something spawns near me.  Players with more optimal computer situations may not experience that.  Which leads me to my extreme relief and enjoyment that Hokko Life allows you to rebind every single action in the game to whatever you want or need.  I also like that I am able to interact and utilize tiles along edges because I like to maximize my workspace and I think it is aesthetically pleasing to be able to plant flowers and trees et cetera along edges.  I did find a couple of tiles that had problems: one I planted a tree in an extreme corner that I couldn't chop when it grew and the other I felled a tree to discover I couldn't replace it (mostly only a problem because I loved that tree there) :  but if you push any boundaries in life, you are bound to find them.  :)  Also, I like and appreciate that this game is very forgiving if you get yourself stuck, in location or knowing what to do next.  If you place an item on top of yourself, you can generally wiggle out of it and if not, it is quick and easy to move any moveable objects.  If you don't know what to do next, speaking to the NPCs will generally get you on track -but they aren't pushy if you don't want to do that- or there is a section of the backpack that lists tasks available.  If you are literally lost and don't know where to go, there is a simplified map in your backpack once you unlock it.  Crafting items, gathering resources, propagating plants, and building are some of my favorite things to do so I already love this game And there is still much for me to do.  If you like any of those things or just like a peaceful place to relax while watching butterflies or moths flutter around the trees/flowers/beach/inside your house, then I recommend this game for you.  ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines parts of Animal Crossing with 3D modeling software. It's cute, relaxing, and casual-friendly.You live in a village of little animal people. You do fetch quests for them and/or evict them to move in other, more interesting animal people. They don't pay you rent or taxes, but they do sometimes bring you crafting materials, which is nice. I got my hands on diamonds way earlier than I was supposed to, thanks to those guys.Crafting is a huge part of the game. You can craft items already in the game, but you are also free to create, edit, and place unique items around your house and world, provided you gather the materials. For example, I gathered a ton of wood and then sculpted it into a statue of my own design. Like I said: 3D modeling software. The ability to make and place custom items is probably my favorite part of this game.There's also a system in place to download other players' creations, which I always appreciate. It's great seeing the talent coming out of the community.Aside from that, there's also elements of fishing, fashion, and farming. I didn't get into those as much, but I see the potential.I did get bored after a while, mainly because there's no monsters to fight. That might be a "me" problem... :D If you want a simple game with crafting, farming, mining, fishing, and fetch quests, I say give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko life falls flat in almost all it wanted to do. The game is slow and needlessly grindy. The quests, along with the grind, end up being buggy. The core gameplay is simplistic, mindless and boring, while the loading screens are also irritating. If you are looking for a good Animal Crossing clone, this is not it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: My pros and cons.Pros> Really promising game.> It's cheap, well atleast here in my country the game is only 13 bucks. Animal crossing was like 60 to 70 bucks when it came out here. > Runs technically well for an early access game and I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs.> Beautiful graphics and it doesn't look like a cheaply made game.> Music is great and really sets the theme of the game.> Villagers are cute and beautifully designed.> Crafting is amazing and you can build or design anything to your hearts desire. Crafting is where I would say hokko life has an edge over animal crossing.> Lots of items to build and collect.> It has its own day and night cycle so you will never have to wait in real time or cheat the timer just to finish certain activities.> There's mp integration like being able share your crafted items online while also being able to download other players crafted items and use it in your village .Cons > Map is quite small and it already feels crowded after building a few houses. I also wish the beach/lake area was bigger. > Still a bit buggy and rough around the edges. Characters easily clipped, get stuck, and it also easy to pass through objects. > Some exploitable stuffs that needed to be fixed, like being able to steal villagers belongings and then selling them for easy money.> Some objects/stuffs still has missing pics or texts.> Quests are limited to fetching or delivering items to villagers. Some quest are also a bit annoying like a villager asking you to build stuffs for him/her and would then ask you to put it inside their house after that to complete the quest. (Damn these lazy villagers!)> Game progression can be quite a bit confusing.> Character customization is still lacking and no facial feature options right now. Clothes are also pretty limited.> The villagers kinda feels the same.> Although crafting is amazing it can also be quite overwhelming and complicated for some.> No object interactions like watching tv, opening the ref, turning on the stove, toggling the lights, etc...The things you buy are mostly decorations right now.> Day and night is kinda weird at times. _childDocuments_.review: *UPDATED REVIEW, now with 16hrs of playtime*At the time of this review with the farming & shopping update;Pro's:-Its super cute-Design your own character, make your skin color any color-You can craft simple items like planks in bulk-You can move forward in time just by sleeping-Once you move into a house (build a house and add a bed and light inside) you get the Creator Catalog. You can get free weekly items from this made by other users in the city-Houses can be moved at anytime, as well as the villager-You can change your hair and skin color anytime after unlocking a shop-The city only has 3 shops right now BUT its super neatCon's:-The progression system is not great-Fishing is not worth the time it takes with how little money you get from the fish-Making money in general is slow. Most people are just spamming certain craftable items to make cash-Crafting new items is also a hassle. Most people are just making one item then switching it out with different requests because no one want to spend the time to make these items from scratch EVERY TIME. -Fish move under the groundThe game needs to update its cash system and crafting system if it truly wants to be enjoyable. Fish need to give you more cash if we're going to have to play a long minigame.UPDATE: They have updated it so that you get a little more from bugs and fish. Still don't find fishing to be worth it at all.I feel the crafting system would be better if it gave you a silhouette of the blueprint. This silhouette could be toggleable so if people really want to go solo they can. It can be hard to figure out the right size an object needs to be. Honestly all-in-all, crafting might be better if it took inspiration from My Sims.Progression. Oh gosh the progression in this game. This is what brings the whole game down for me. Its all based on who you have move into your town. If you're not reading a walkthrough for the game, you will have no idea who you need to invite to get stairs, bombs, etc. When i first wrote this review I was stuck because I had no idea this was how it worked and I couldn't get the stairs to get to the top part of the world. It was frustrating. I finally looked it up and got who I needed in town but a game like this should not force you to look at a guide to be able to progress. This will turn many people off who come to this game hoping to have as good as a time as Animal Crossing. If you have bad rng like me and don't know this system, it could take 5-10hrs to get the right villager. Some of the progression is fine, like having to complete oh so many quests for your villagers and have a certain number of houses/villagers. Thats great but most of the game is solely based on having specific villagers and hoping rng puts them in the inn for you to talk to.Also don't expect to get farming early on. After 16hrs I finally unlocked the area with bombs but it turns out you need even more more to get started farming. You need iron. Which requires another villager and a number of quests done and a number of houses built. Why not get you started with copper items for farming? Why does it have you go straight to iron? I was so happy to finally get to the farming area to only be disappointed again by this progression system.If you want to play this game, open the potentially outdated walkthrough on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been loving this game so far. I had an itch for a game similar to Animal Crossing for a while and this game scratches that itch and more. It is very very similar to New Horizons, but also has many things that make it stand apart. I have always loved Animal Crossing, but New Horizons really didn't quite do it for me, and I have been enjoying Hokko Life more than New Horizons. The premise is mostly the same:-Travel to a town-Fix up the town-Build houses-Move in Villagers-Decorate your town-Fish-Catch bugs-etc.However, where the differences come is the best part. You are able to take requests from your villagers, they'll ask you to build them something, repair a piece of furniture, or simply deliver an item to another villager. Very similar to New Leaf when you could actually interact with Villagers, unlike New Horizon. There is also a bit more "exploring" if you want to call it that. Since this game focuses very heavily on crafting, which is also a major difference it has from Animal Crossing, there are many other areas to discover. There is a large mine where you can find different stones and minerals, there is a beach area for sand and fishing, a swampy little pond area for more fishing, a small forest for gathering different kinds of wood, a farm, a CITY center, as well as your own little town center. This adds a lot more to do so you don't have to rely solely on your one little plot of land to try to do everything in one place. You can also use creator codes to view other people's creations. In the City Center, there is a "hotel?" that allows you to visit other player's shops and download their creations from any console. There is also a smaller shop that has rotating items that are all player created items. You can download them and they get sent to your mailbox FOR FREE! Doing this you can essentially decorate your entire little town by spending no coins at all on decorations. If you liked Animal Crossing but were craving something a little bit more, this is the game for you. Out of all the cozy games I have played so far, this one is definitely the closest match to Animal Crossing. The only negative thing I can say currently is that I have been experiencing a bug where there is invisible walls/objects around my town. If I run into it one way, I get trapped, but if I run into it at a different angle, it's like it's not even there... Super weird and they haven't really been updating the game anymore so you would think that bugs like this would have been ironed out long ago, but regardless, I am enjoying the game enough to where it is more so just a minor inconvenience than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: is a cozy game that is often compared to Animal Crossing / Harvest Moon / Stardew Valley. However, even if it fits into the genre through its game design, mechanics and adorable graphics, I dare say that the gameplay is slightly different than what you’d expect from a farming / life sim.  is more of a crafting / building sim than anything else, and because it doesn’t have a story, nor a system of building up relationships with the other characters (nor romance for that matter), the end game goals turn into unlocking as many of the crafting designs possible, amassing as many resources as needed to support the crafting process, and ultimately shaping / decorating the game’s world with the crafted items, according to your desires. It's certainly a fun and very chill game to play for fans of the genre, but it does have its own shortcomings.The game’s main focus is expanding a small town into a thriving community. This is done by building houses, decorating and furnishing them, and then inviting potential characters to move in. In order to craft furniture or clothing items you’ll need raw resources, while building a house also costs coins. As such, most of the time is spent gathering the materials needed for your next objective, which requires various amounts of grinding for resources, depending on what you are trying to build. The stone and minerals respawn daily, while the flowers or trees you harvest take a few days to regrow but you will also be able to plant new ones in order to maximize your throughput. Coins can be obtained by completing requests from the villagers, catching insects / fish and selling them in the town’s shop, or even selling the items you produced. takes crafting to a whole new level. While in similar games the crafting chain consists of 2-3 steps (you create some intermediate products like planks from harvested wood, then a piece of furniture using these planks), in  you will be able to unleash your full creativity by customizing the crafted products (including full buildings) as you see fit. Each of their components can be readjusted, moved, resized, replaced or deleted, you can add new shelves to a bookcase in any position you desire and so on. There are limitless combinations of what you can create in-game. Some of the basic blueprints for these items are unlocked by completing requests from the NPCs, while others are bought with coins. The items created can all be decorated with all sorts of metallic or non-metallic ornaments, and each of their composing elements can also be painted. The creations you make can then be showcased in your own shop back in the main city, which other players can visit in order to download your designs and end products. The community’s creativity is tremendous, and by browsing the stores even briefly using the identity codes posted on the Steam forums or on Discord, you can easily find lots of artistic items that are basically miniature masterpieces.I find that in , some of the features are implemented better than in other similar games. For example, there is no tool durability - it’s refreshing to not have to worry about how many charges you can use a tool before having to replace it. Secondly, there is no energy bar that limits your actions. The in-game time flows rather slowly, and during a whole work day you have plenty of room to engage in a lot of activities. I’ve never felt restricted by what I was able to do during a full day, because I was always able to harvest to my heart’s content (even the entire map, if I so wanted), plus complete a couple of villagers’ requests, hunt for a few insects or fish for some extra pocket money and take part in small competitions - all of these until the day ended, almost on a daily basis.The progress in  is incremental, and gated by so-called “Mayor Merits”. These are sequential challenges that have specific mixed requirements and which unlock a certain perk that makes your gameplay a bit easier later on. The Mayor Merits serve both as a motivation for the player to spread their efforts over multiple types of activities in parallel, but also as a guide on how to best progress through the game. On the downside, you can’t really see what benefits your next unlock will bring you, so you don’t exactly know which of the several possibilities to prioritize, and some of the requirements are not clearly explained. has a lot of positives, but unfortunately several negatives too, apart from various visual and gameplay bugs that persist even after the game exited its early access phase. For starters, there should be better guidance for the player, and not only at the beginning of the game but also whenever a new mechanic is unlocked. Although a tutorial exists and it’s pretty decent, there are some object interactions that are quite unintuitive and these are not covered at all. Aside from that, some UI elements could be slightly improved and made more accessible (for example, it doesn't make sense that you can progress through the dialogue using the keyboard primarily, but selecting dialogue options works only by using the mouse). The fishing minigame is likely the least entertaining activity because the fish don’t always take the bait even if they are in its proximity. The characters are pretty one-sided and have only very few lines; as you unlock more characters you can also see that there are some interactions between them based on their personality type, but these are quite shallow and overall uninteresting.The NPC’s requests are usually a hit or miss. At the beginning of the game they were rather slow to come in, but as I progressed and more people moved into town, my days started to be really busy, filled with plenty of tasks. However, after another few days, they stopped coming altogether, and I had to start manually hunting down every character on a daily basis to see if they actually wanted me to do something for them or not. The notice board - which in theory helps gather requests - also remained sparsely populated (1-2 entries per week). These requests are usually in the form of fetch-quests or fixing some furniture items, thus they can quickly become repetitive for some. I found them rather interesting because they helped me progress through the game by forcing me to unlock new designs. However, the biggest challenge was to find the quest giver (they move around the world and there is no quick way to locate them). After many hours of gaming you can unlock a map, but it’s not extremely useful because it displays the NPCs only in the region you’re currently in and only if they’re roaming outside buildings. It’s funny though that it’s so hard to find them even on a little map as ’s is (there are only 13 areas to explore, and they’re rather contained, each taking a few screens). provides a relaxed, pressure-free experience. Its’ world, with beautiful pastel visuals and slow-paced gameplay, is particularly welcoming, yet the game often felt that it needs more substance for me to consider it truly great, aside from the aforementioned bug fixes and accessibility improvements. In its current state, it’s a decent sim and the negatives aren’t particularly bothersome, but it still has a long way to go. It has huge replayability value, not only because it doesn’t actually have an end game (you just keep building and crafting ad infinitum, plus the map layout is randomly generated for each playthrough).

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a very slow start to it, and there were a few in game days that I just slept to try to get the game moving, but once you get past that the game is very enjoyable. I like how the residents will give you things to do, it makes it worthwhile to talk to them daily. I have had some residents request things that I did not have the means of getting in the required amount of time given, such as requesting iron before I had the mines open. That was little frustrating. The crafting system is a very cool feature. It took me a little time to get used to it, but I like that there is so much creativity you can explore with it. Being able to download other users' designs is also really great. I love seeing what others do, and it helps to get the inspiration flowing for creating your own items. The ability to not only decorate your home and the outside, but also the other resident's homes is really nice. The graphics are nice and clean and very cute, and the music is sweet and very relaxing.The lack of a storage feature is very frustrating, and I'm hoping that this is something added into the game. There's not a ton of pocket space, so filling them up doesn't take too much. I don't feel the pricing for selling fish is super balanced. It takes a decent amount of effort to catch a fish, and a lot of them sell for around the same price as butterflies that are not only pretty abundant throughout the game but very easy to catch. So, instead of fishing, I find myself just running around catching butterflies for money. If fish sold for more money, then I'd spend more time actually fishing.The game still does have a few glitches, which is to be expected in early access mode, but I haven't run into anything game breaking. Overall, I've enjoyed playing this and am looking forward to seeing where this games goes.

I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life oozes charm and a more adult flavor than Animal Crossing, although you can tell it is heavily inspired by it. I was having a conversation with one of the villagers, a rabbit named Benny and he spoke of feeling burnt out and tired and not knowing where to go. The thing with Benny is by chance he ended up in my village. But what's my point? Most adults can related to feeling tired, burnt out, and lost. That's just one way I feel like this game is headed off to a good start. It doesn't necessarily want to dethrone Animal Crossing, but provide an alternative that feels different and familiar at the same time. However, it does have flaws to speak of. This game is in no way perfect in it's current state. You will run into slightly annoying bugs and there's not a ton of in game content at the moment. What you're investing in is the potential this game has and right now it's looking very promising. It's ran by a team of one developer, but if you join the discord you will see Robert is tirelessly working to squash bugs and has already announced a Farming update at the time of writing. He's also had a good amount of experience working on teams for Killzone, Fable, and a few other big games in the industry. To wrap this up if you are patient and a fan of life sims such as Stardew, Harvest Moon, and most importantly Animal Crossing then I would recommend giving this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Fun to play, steep learning curve, has a bit of jank.First the pros, it's a game with a similar calm feeling to Animal crossing, the design tool offers complete creative freedom with almost no restrictions (which others see as a negative as it involves having basic creativity). The seasonal events occur in real time but the game has it's own clock and ability to sleep to the next day, which is great for growing things and skipping to a house being built. This is much more preferable to other life sims that require you to wait 24 hours in real time to reap rewards. All villager houses offer full customisation so you can realise your creative vision, want a villager to have a 50 Shades style Red Room? You can. The customisation extends to the entire village so you are able to place furniture anywhere alongside the free form design tool really allows you to transform the place.The developer is consistent with game updates and posts which does offer reassurance that this game is continually being worked on.The cons include a litany of glitches, the most known one being the design tool  crashes the game and requires a force quit if you have a controller connected, this has been known about for a while and while continued updates to the gameplay itself continues, it seems that some glitches have been left unaddressed other than a "Please unplug controller" post in the community tab. There is no real tutorial for this game within it, to learn to play you are effectively required to spend a lot of time in community posts and guides, unfortunately due to the age of some of the "how to" posts means that the information given can  be obsolete and useless due to a newer update, leading to a few frustrating moments where I was unable to progress the game. The city update is nice but ultimately quite barren.Overall I would still recommend this game despite some setbacks as the creative freedom more than make up for a couple of bumps in the road and I am looking forward to seeing how this game continues to progress.

Customization for the player character is also quite limited, and the player character models seem very low quality compared to the other models in game.I can't truly fault the game since it IS E.A, but I would not advise purchasing at this stage.
