_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat bias review: Not my kind of game. I very much enjoy Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, Drago Noka and the like, but I don't enjoy this game. This game is VERY much animal crossing in all the ways I dislike.The game-play loop of crafting consists mostly of gather resources->build stuff->sell excess->repeat. The issue herein lies in the fact that material gathering is painfully bare-bones, and it doesn't help that the hit detection imo isn't great (I have frequently missed the first hit on an object because I was one step away or facing the wrong direction). Additionally, the variety of things to collect is very limited, and the game doesn't give you agency to progress very well. What I mean by this is that you are painfully held back by the story arbitrarily deciding when to unlock what feature and this railroading in a  mostly sandbox style game is constraining and chokes the experience.The focus of the game isn't crafting, and building, it's wholly set on designing your own town and beautifying your environment. You can design furniture, decals, and outfits, if that's what you're into, but the crafting aspect of the game is limited to 'collect base materials to allow you to customize something'.This is a very casual game I feel would fit on the switch, 3ds, or even a mobile aspect since it's probably best enjoyed in bite sized amounts, but if you're into making efficient farms and watching big numbers get bigger, this isn't the kind of game for you.PS: I have had to sleep through multiple days without doing anything just to progress the story so that I can have something new to do. Quite painful to be frank.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is fairly similar to Animal Crossing New Horizons, This game is need of a few improvements and overall polishing, despite how pretty the game already is.My first critique would be that it takes way too much inspiration from Animal Crossing in regards to Mechanics. The fact that you have to wait for only a few type of items to be available in the shop at a time, was always a poor mechanic of Animal Crossing, and Detracted from the Fun of the Game. The Store should have many more items available at all times. I would recommend revitalizing the store to resemble the general stores that existed in the west during the 19th and 20th centuries, where everything costed a dime and you could always find the supplies you needed. This would be an excellent way to encourage the players to jump right into the customization options. That being Said, I will say Hokko life offers better tools to the player as opposed to Animal Crossing, which was VERY ANNOYING. Tools that break within a week's use of the item, if not a day, Nintendo messed up on this factor of the game, emphasizing a very realistic problem in the home improvement industry regarding cheap tools and supplies. Seeking Hokko life give the player tools they never have to replace was a breath of fresh air. I've known people who've owned tools that they use quite often, of which are almost a century old, so I'm glad this is certainly being considered as a factor in the game, as the cheap tools imply so much about the cheapness of Nintendo's business practices and policies. Tools generally should last as long as the person who uses them. If they break easily, that means longevity was not considered important, and the game would be so much better if this remained the case. It's a pointless mechanic to have the tools break. I'm already running around and gathering materials and waiting a day at a time for them to regenerate to produce more. I see the emphasis on realism, but There should be an option to buy supplies instead, like in Animal Crossing, so that not a lot of time is wasted on the part of the game that wasn't advertised. If you're going to make ads about how exciting it is to customize everything, one would think they'd be doing that right off the bat. This was a rather deceptive way of advertising the game, At least animal crossing showed you were gonna be working to build everything by yourself with tools before you even have the option to customize.The Second Critique is the tutorial. Hokko life's tutorial is unskippable, doesn't provide much player choice, and is ultimately frustrating. Imagine evicting a person who moved into your village against their will. It's very strange how you're not allowed to plan the community until after the game forces you to go through the tutorial.  I don't like the idea of evicting people from homes that I don't want in my community, Don't put me in this position, game developers Make it very obvious that it is skippable.Then there's the all of things that are unlockable. There's so many pointless blocks and obstacles that take away from the experience of enjoying the full game right away. With boundaries hiding the hidden places, we should have the option to think for ourselves to buy tools of all kinds to fix these things.Overall, The Game is very enjoyable, but it leaves a lot to be desired, which I suppose could be said about all games, but there is clearly room for improvement. If there ever is a Hokko Life 2, it should HEAVILY Deviate from immitating Animal Crossing, Talking Animal People Put Aside, and make the game far more unique, as this mimicry is a shell, where something greater lies within this attempt to recreate Animal Crossing but better. I want to see a more original game that inspires and innovates the Life-Sim Farming Sim Game Category. Oh, and there should be open-world travel. Would love to see more places to be traveled to, as the train station with the no destination interface implies that there could be other places to travel to in the game. That, and the days should be far longer. A Day Should be an hour in real time. That would be an excellent thing to add in.Again, It Leaves a LOT to be desired, Please consider adding these things and more to the game, as I would like to see it do better than Animal Crossing.

_childDocuments_.review: A sub 360$ alternative to Animal Crossing. Not as smooth with animations and such, but fundamentally fantastic~Update: Satisfying at face value, ground to a complete halt. There is an item, the bomb, that makes one of the areas of the game accessible. I've repeatedly done the main aspect of this game, the quests. I've tried even looking up guides to get past this and it seems up to chance that you'll ever get this blueprint. This feels like a fault in the game. _childDocuments_.review: Don't know why there's all the hate towards this game, it's probably the most chill game I've played so far.I don't like much animal crossing timegating stuff since my sleep patterns are always messy, so this game is nice for me to enjoy the similar experience without much stress.The game's pretty much like animal crossing, you plant flowers, grow trees, cut three, go fishing, catch bugs, and go mining. There's also farming later in the game (I haven't touched it yet).This game has no penalty afaik, little buggy Yes, but you can always exit the game, and the game is going to reset your character into your own house again, so no biggie( and this game always saves your game whenever you exit via in-game, so it's always nice for me).Time doesn't matter much in here aside from affecting villager routine, some seasonal events, quests, and store open times, other than that, it doesn't affect you one bit.Villager Quest also doesn't give you a penalty for missing out on the timeframe, you can always remove it so no stress is added up for missing out.a little suggestion for the developer I think maybe add a teleport to home button, I feel it's a nice addition since walking back to home is a bit painful. In the end I'm using the lazy's way, exiting the game to the main menu, and the game resets to my own home.Also, a little more optimization would be nice, since the game gets laggier the more plants I put in the world. You might need to check the blur in game too, I keep seeing small stuttering near the teleport in the shop area (around the blurring part)I think the villagers pathfinding needs some work too, they keep bumping and stuck around in some parts. Some characters are also way too similar (like the elephant one, I've already seen three elephant characters in this game so far). And also more variety of dialogue, I feel like some character way of talking also way too similiar.Oh, and also a more balanced villager quest, lots of the quests early in the game are impossible until I gather some stuff, a simple quest would be nice.btw, lots of this game's villager is obsessed with paints 🤣I find it funny lots of quest it always about paints

_childDocuments_.review: Having put six hours into this game already I can say that I’m really enjoying it. There are reviews here that state that they got frustrated or bored after around two hours and I’m here to tell you that you need to actually give this game a chance. The features open up to you slowly. The game doesn’t overwhelm you with tons of different things you can do straight away, it has you ease into things instead. I’m six hours in and I still haven’t unlocked everything the game has to offer. But I’m okay with that since I have plenty to do on my way to more features. This works for a game because you will always have something new to explore as the game progresses, and that’s why not everything unlocks right at the beginning of the game. You need to earn your ability to expand the town and customize everything. I will say that building original designs in the workshop is a bit tedious but you get the hang of it with time. I enjoy working toward unlocking merits and expanding the game. It’s very similar to Animal Crossing but I’ve found that I have gotten more into this game than AC. I recommend it, but as I said, you need to put time into it so you can progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is uh...well it's something?I'm a cozy gamer who enjoys titles such as Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, Story of Seasons / Harvest Moon, and just about every other cozy game under the sun, so when I saw this game I was pretty excited!! The gameplay stills here in the store look like they have detail, the generated characters look cute enough, and it definitely has a softer style like that of Disney Dreamlight Valley or of course, Animal Crossing--but this game is far from being playable or complete.Pros:> nostalgic premise> open world customizing features> good price (WHEN PURCHASED ON SALE)Cons:> little to no starting character customization> animal villagers are HORRIFYING and look like randomized sims> UX/UI is very unpolished and still looks as though it is in beta> dialogue and world comes across as lifelessOVERALL 2 out of 5 STARS--if it's on sale and you're bored, go for it. However, costing $20 US dollars full price is absolutely absurd seeing as this game states that it's in early access and that is definitely visible upon playing. I wish instead of releasing an overpriced and unplayable game the devs would have just put more time in to at least a redesign of the UI and giving players more meaningful interactions with the villagers. At the end of the day, this is clearly an Animal Crossing clone, but it does so unsuccessfully. If you want something that fits the cozy genre and breathes new life into the life sim genre while offering similar mechanics, I would check out Dinkum instead! Maybe if this game gets an overhaul in the future, my view of Hokko Life can become positive.

_childDocuments_.review: I have physical and cognitive disabilities that limit the types of games I can play. My reaction time is very slow, and I'm easily fatigued, so I thought this slow-paced game would be just right for me. It's true that the pace of the game is slow, and it's nice that you can't be killed by monsters (I never encountered any enemies, and I made it to the second-to-last mine level, the silver level). I talked to all the visitors to the island, and asked them all to move in, and they all said they would... but they never did. And then the visitors stopped coming. I had many vacant houses, but they never moved in. Later, I learned that you're supposed to walk up to the house and click on it to make them move in,  but I had to learn that from Google. I never got around to trying it. The main feature of the game is building furniture, which is not something I have the cognitive energy to do. I didn't realize it would be such an integral part of the game. I would only recommend this game if you're interested in building furniture. Farming was a grind. (I didn't get far enough to craft sprinklers). Mining was boring after the first couple times, since there are no enemies. The whole game is about collecting resources, like tufts of grass, to build furniture. The villagers are creepy looking and devoid of personality. And there's no story. No potential for friendship with the villagers (as far as I was able to figure out).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hollow a vapid shell of better attempts at the genre. You can see from woke race and gender flag that use in the trailer that this was going to strip out good game mechanics for destructive politics. Lets start with the fact that you character is a person without a gender. You can make them look more like a girl or boy with the hair options but their body does not change. The game assumes that you are a woman so if you think you made a guy then be prepared to be weirded out ever time another guy calls you dear. Not that it matters to much because there a no relationships of any meaning in the game anyway. The game is a railroaded as you can get with virtually not choice in what you get to do. The area that you get to act in initially is tiny and there is nothing here that would make me play long enough to wait for it to get much bigger. Last the tools are a real pain to switch between and use. For a game that is almost all mouse controls the fact that you can not harvest with the mouse is baffling.This game is not worth playing go play My Time in Portia or Animal Crossing instead.

_childDocuments_.review: On par with a lot of the reviews: lots of promise, needs lots of work.I can do pros of course, but its an early access game prone to change, and the only real pro you can have is this is a pretty decent AC-like life sim with heavy emphasis on designing/creating. I've played around 7 hours and still haven't progressed as far as you currently can so far, so the game concept is there and sorta finished. But it will need a LOT of polish!My suggestions (and I guess this is the cons too):- More bugs/fish/creatures. There's a very limited amount.- Adjust prices. Fish and bugs shouldn't cost around 2g in this game, especially when that's all you can mostly do on a day to day basis for a while. -  I see what they want and it sorta works at first, but the moment you can move people in it all crashes. Bugs and exploits allow you to access further areas you shouldn't be at yet; you can take and sell any villagers items, including the main town shop furniture.There's a big push on villager requests, and the game does a terrible job atm of explaining that you need certain villagers and their quests to unlock certain recipes to help you progress your exploration. That would be fine, but then to move villagers *in* you need to have materials that are at places you shouldn't be accessing until you've already moved X amount of people in. The gameplay loop and the ideal path you're supposed to take to progress is heavily flawed, and also doesn't mesh well with the  sandbox of the game. - Tutorials: game has virtually no good tutorials or organic interactions that help you understand how things work/how to do things/how to progress correctly. You'll progress the "story" but then once you finish the current objective its like you hit a brick wall until you can find out from some other players what you're supposed to do next.- UI: The UI is not very good. Inventory screen is usable but lacks personality and ease of use.- Bugs: I don't need to really include this one. Its early access so it is a given. -  Overall, the game is an exhilarating new step for this genre on PC finally, but the amazement lasts for about an hour or two. Once the gameplay loop does kick in, the devs seemed to have overlooked many of the gameplay flow details which has made my experience confusing and drawn out so far. But even so, when you aren't taking part in the story progression of the game, you see just how less of life and personality this project holds in comparison to its Nintendo IP inspiration. It's early access and I don't mean to sound rude, I do still love what we have here, but it is obviously flawed in a lot of places. There's a strong lack of presence and identity outside of the general ideas they try to develop on. I feel if they get a good budget/community support and more time in the oven, and they reapproach a lot of the core ideas and mechanics, they can turn Hokko Life into a casual PC staple!Besides that, if you like these types of games and REALLY enjoy building and decorating with items, than yes I can recommend this! But only for veterans of this genre itching to try out new things. Elsewise: kindly wait until the game is finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like it.  It all feels pretty hollow.  The thing that got me to finally say 'no' was the designing of items.  The camera is obnoxious to control, there's no snapping to grid lines for item placement so that things are aligned.  There's no 'mirror' duplicate option either so that again, what you have on the right/left side is done to the other.  Rotation should probably have different settings like 30 degree, 45 degree, and then free-form rotation rather than only having one free-form rotation.  It's also not very intuitive on if you have an item selected.  Sometimes it's hard to tell if a button select worked on an item.  I like the idea, but it needs more attention and love and to have more streamline-user friendly customization.  The customize section feels like regular Blender with built in assets, and Blender, while an amazing tool, is not intuitive and user friendly off the get-go. You have to watch tutorial after tutorial.  So the bar of satisfying entry here in Hokko Life is...a bit too high when the general focus of the game seems to be customization.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend holding off on this one, at least for a while. Pros:*Pretty*Nice music*Dev is active in discord, is open to suggestions, and has already released an update addressing some issues*Villagers are super cute with different personalities. *Fishing mechanic is creativeCons:*Controls on keyboard are very clunky, it's difficult to line yourself up to catch bugs or cut trees.  It's probably better with a controller, but I don't have one. *When the game starts, the only ways to make money is to sell flower petals and grasses, which take days to respawn, and does not earn you enough money to buy the bug net.  Your only choices are to steal furniture from your villagers and sell it, or just sleep through multiple days to pass the time until the bear comes to give you the fishing blueprint. *After you get the fishing rod you can sell fish to buy the bug net.  This is the only way I've found to make any money, but it gets boring very fast*Eventually someone comes to town and you can build them a shop, but the shop takes several days to build.  During this time, no one in town asks you to make or do anything, and there's nothing to do but catch bugs and fish, and it gets boring, so I ended up again just sleeping through several days to pass the time*Once that building is made, it unlocks the ability to build homes for more villagers to move in.  Again, it takes several days for that home to be built, again, with nothing to do to pass the time.  Queue sleeping through another three days*Building a home means you need to make furniture for it.  You buy a blueprint for the bed, but that blueprint doesn't tell you what you need to make the bed.  You have to design it yourself from the ground up, and if you are not already creative, it's not easy to figure out what pieces need to be used and how to place it all*While I said above that the fishing mechanic is creative, it is not intuitive to learn, and takes a long time to catch each fish, making it a lot of energy for little reward.  Bug catching is faster, but gets very boring, and it can be very hard to tell where the bug actually is. TL;DR:  $20 is too much to ask for this game as it is right now.  It is in EA, and the game will probably get a lot better, but right now it's not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Uncanny valley vibes.A lot of the reviews make mention of the odd art direction for this game and it's for good reason. This gametook heavy inspiration from Animal Crossing and it shows in the music, villagers, dialogue, and mechanics.This isn't a bad thing as it makes a lot of strides in doing certain things better, but unfortunately all the charm from Animal Crossing is not present here.The villagers are all animal based and meant to be cute, but they are so anthropomorphic that it just comes offas creepy. The dialogue with them is so stiff and their expressions so limited that they all just seem solifeless. Pair this with the fact that the animations reset during conversations and it just becomesunsettling interacting with them.The dialogue for this game is so one sided that even when you are given a choice to answer it's onlyever one answer. Seriously, in the three hours I played they kept asking me a question and prompting a response,but you only ever get one choice. It comes off as lazy and insulting. Why try to prompt the player to respondif you don't really get to decide? It could have been written in a manner that didn't require asking one to answer.Crafting, collecting, and decorating is miles better than Animal Crossing. The amount of customization you haveis absolutely stellar and truly allows you to go all out, but the villagers and NPCs just drag this game so down.There's a reason why the video focuses so little on them.If you like Animal Crossing New Horizon and are fine with the look of the NPCs you'll enjoy the game. If thescreenshots of the game are off putting then take it at face value as it doesn't get any better.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: As of now, the hours I have for this game are inaccurate because I accidentally left it on.Anyway, this game appears to be an Animal Crossing dupe combined with Stardew Valley. The character customization is awful while the rest of the game looks cozy. The walking animation for the character is just terrible as well.I would get this on sale but not for full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wanted to like this game...there's just so many little QoL annoyances that I just can't enjoy it.- I don't actually hate the design of the animals. I think they're kind of cute, in a semi-horrifying way. Sure they have dead zombie eyes with weirdly dilated pupils, but at least they're colorful. I guess.- You can design your own furniture, which on the surface is what I was looking forward to and I still think it's a great idea.. unfortunately the controls to do this are SO fiddly and obnoxious that I almost ragequit the game trying to put legs on a table. Please let me use the arrow keys to nudge objects around by a couple of pixels. Why can I not do this? Why is there not a "snap" option for basic things like PUTTING LEGS ON FURNITUREplease- The mines are a cute idea but the amount of lamps you need to put down so that you're not constantly getting "IT'S TOO DARK PLEASE SAVE ME" messages is obnoxious. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of early access launch I feel in love with the game even though limited to what you do it has so much potential and I happily stayed to watch it grow and develop and I don't regret it one bit! Sure the game has had it's fair share of bugs but it's one single developer and Robert that solo developer is amazing, he speaks with his community and goes out his way to try and deal with these bugs and issues as quickly as he can. The way he always listens to the feedback and suggestions from the official suggestion forms for the game, and more just really shows inside the game itself as it's developed. The old tutorial that was difficult and didn't explain really anything at all have been remade completely, the old one is out the window and a brand new one is near perfect for newer players. The way the tutorials now work I can't help but adore the new tutorial that even gives the characters more life and personality than before as you go through it. The design tool/bench to create your own custom designs, items and furniture is really great, it really is the best feature in the game and now for those who don't like or still practising with the bench/tool can now use pre-built designs (only limited ones so far but have heard more could be coming!) using a brown book icon.  Though with the tutorial you do need to actually read all the prompts and such, I know many don't seem to for some reason haha.Many compare the game to animal crossing, even more so at the launch of early access and back then it was easy to see it that way but since then, will all the major updates like farming, mayor merits, narrative and so many more it really can stand on it's own two feet. This how I strongly feel myself for the game. It has areas where you can relate to animal crossing but at the same time it can also feeling like a different game as you play it yourself compared to seeing gameplay/watching it. With more updates hinted that are yet to come I can't wait to see what else is coming, seeing this game grow since early access until now has just been an amazing experience to really see it become it's own game that can stand on it's own feet if given the chance.Then there's the community. The official discord server is a great place filled with so many amazing and kind people who are willing to help answer questions, help you deal with bugs and to fill out a actual bug report form so that the bug can be dealt with. The steam forms slowly and surely have been growing with more life along side the screenshots and the "artwork" page for the game growing. I personally highly recommend the game if you want a relaxing game with the same genre as animal crossing but has more to it, more to do and a feeling of going somewhere more than it. If you love to get creative the design bench/tool, the art easel for creating clothing, wallpaper and flooring is perfect for you, the tools to express yourself are amazing in the game once you get the hang of the controls and way to do so. BUT I don't recommend the game at its current state to players who don't want to deal with bugs, who refuse to make backups of their saves, who don't want to bother filling out an official bug report form or understand that an early access game isn't complete and still is in the making. Those things can be stressful to people and ruin the game experience for them but sadly it's early access, bugs tend to happen making backups of your saves regularly can massively help you when you encounter a major bug. But the choice is fully up to the person, the feeling of a good game and the game going into a good direction is up to the person, the art style of the characters not everyone may agree or enjoy it can really depend on preference but I like to say give it a try if the genre and creativity are your thing but only do so if you can handle what comes with an early access game.Once past that tutorial stage it can feel slow slightly but once past it you are free to do whatever you'd like. You are have freedom to create, build and control the town to your own design. I happily do giveaways for the game and will always fall in love with it and it's community that love to help each other and share their creations, thoughts and feedback! If have discord please do join the games official server. It honestly is a great place and hub for the community where the solo developer reads feedback and can find the links for bugs reports and suggestion forms, community help and more.

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems fun so far, and we have to keep in mind it is an early access game. Therefore, not recommended *yet*, it will need a lot of work before it can be officially released. Basically what I think it's like early game: In a nutshell, collecting butterflies, cashing them in, growing trees, and designing furniture in the designer tool. Basically its a designer tool with a world surrounding it. Things that make the game suboptimal: - Incentive based gameplay is completely non-existent; there is no notification of quests completed, not even coins visually going into your backpack when getting rewarded, no cheerful reward bells chiming when you turn something in.. No "feel-goods" about achievements or missions finished. - The camera is not movable and your character goes in all directions, there is no third person toggle possible sadly. This means it's hard to see things, or the really be immersed in the game. It can be nauseating when you are used to third person view. - It's early access so on bugs: There are glitches with non-working ramps, bridges and stairs. It's the only design i've tried so I don't know how many other designs bug out. So far ONE design that a certain player made (their tutorial is in the forum) works, but for a game that is all about design, its sad that all other creations seem to float in the air and become unmovable... I had to delete my save and start over again with the river full of floating bridge-designs I had tried. What would be *really* helpful is a way to access the game's Settings while being in the game, not forcing you to quit first to find the settings in the main menu.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A take on Animal Crossing. Hokko Life screams its inspiration.  You have animal characters, arriving in a town on a train, and people just walking up to you and making demands of your time.  But that’s also exactly what Animal Crossing is.  This isn’t trying to create a new genre, it’s taking what is successful and finding its audience, and doing that well enough after a few minutes to get comfortable with the game.Hokko Life is focused on a laid-back style of game, where players build a town for characters, add new citizens to their town, and just have a simple existence.  It gets into the meat of the game quickly but this is a slow raft ride down a lazy river rather than whitewater rafting.  It’s not going to appeal to everyone but it’s a game you can boot up every couple of days and play for thirty minutes just enjoying the atmosphere. Pick this up if you enjoy Animal Crossing.  I stress this because this isn’t attempting to be something completely new, it knows what it wants to deliver to players and does it successfully.  This is the comfortable shoe for players who want to experience Animal Crossing on a different platform, and the fact it’s not tied to a set internal clock means players can play on their schedule.  If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a child running around with their arms outstretched like an airplane, possibly making "vroom-vroom" noises, and then running up to you with a "really cool" bug that they think you'd like to have. Now imagine your town elders getting inebriated one evening and saying, "We're tired of running this dump. Let's let the kid do it!"That's the basic premise of this game (minus the inebriation part - I'm not really sure what their motivation is). If it doesn't make you run away screaming, you'll probably love it! I confess, I wasn't impressed with it when it was first released. I found the muted colors depressing, and there really didn't seem like there was much to do. After a short time, I got bored and uninstalled. But I went back recently and found it much improved. The beginning is still kind of slow. You arrive on the train, having no idea where you came from or why you're there, and you're given free room and board at the hotel in town. Then you're asked to do some simple tasks, but you run out of them quickly. NOW, however, there are a couple of broken down houses in town, and you're asked to fix them up. Then you're allowed to take one for yourself, and the game takes off.It's similar to many of the Harvest Moon-style games, though farming doesn't come into the picture for a long time. Instead, you do chores for people and learn how to build things and collect butterflies and fish, in exchange for cash. The creator wanted it to be similar to Animal Crossing, and it definitely evokes that game. When you catch a butterfly or fish, the camera zooms in and you display your catch. If you've played Animal Crossing, that will be very familiar. So will many other elements, including the animals moving into town. (Fortunately, I don't have to endure them asking for wardrobe changes and strutting around on the runway. Ugh.)It isn't Animal Crossing. It's a similar, but unique game, and after several hours of gameplay, I haven't even come close to running out of things to do. On the contrary, there seems to be more to do, as the game move along. I haven't even opened up some of the areas yet! So it's definitely fun and engrossing. The muted colors are a stylistic choice I don't really agree with, but at least there is a lot of variation in weather and the time of day. I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: After 14 hours and still progressing through the game, I can say I recommend it. I've unlocked a ton of stuff because I tried to optimize my playstyle while still playing at my pace. Please try and set your expectations when you compare it to any other life sim game. Its not a randomized or generated map. It's a static one. Dont just like "animal crossing" or "stardew" or both, think about other games... like MySims. I'm not kidding, my boyfriend mentioned MySims, and that made a lot more sense for the visual feel, how items go flying, the way all the characters individualized designs feel a bit eclectic. But most of all, the crafting system opens itself up slowly but surely into an individualized make just about whatever you might want to. I've seen foodtruck decor pieces, I've seen final fantasy mounts as chairs. The creation contests allow community approved submissions to become canonized objects you can buy from the main stores rather than downloaded. It can be slow rolling at first, and like many games these days there can be a risk of tutorial slog. I dont mind that, as I can still get to doing what I want. And if you're patient, "it doesnt matter which house I choose as mine", yeah because you can move them later, and you can move into a bigger house you build later. I do wish there was an easier way to find other players' creator stores, but we live in an age where the answer to your question is on a discord server. RipperoniI look forward to seeing how this progresses past this stage of early access at July 1st 2023

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle to see who this game is for.  There is not enough farming to call it a farm simulator. There is not enough game play to call it a RPG.   In short the game is about 15 hours of gameplay, and then you realize there is no game.  If you want to have a truly painful and tedious item build scenarios, this is the game for you.  The game is pretty to look at, but that is it.  I kept hoping for more content, but it never came.  The only updates have been hotfixes and window dressing.  Great I can change the flooring again, but what else?
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a neutral review I would. It's okay, it feels like an attempt to create Animal Crossing for PC, but of course it's nowhere near as good and there isn't that much to do. The characters are a bit weird looking, not as cute as I would have liked and they don't have much depth.I enjoyed my first few hours catching bugs, relaxing and fishing but I really hated the crafting. It's pretty complex, especially when it comes to making original designs. I couldn't design anything that didn't look really, really bad. This is an issue as making original items and uploading them to the world is part of the games merit system if you want to complete 100%, I didn't find this cosy or relaxing at all. Another issue is the inventory system. It's just bad, even with max upgrades. Every time you want to craft something you need to take out each crafting material and put them in your backpack, then return them all to storage when you're finished. The storage sucks too, it's huge, and makes your world look really ugly.Hokko life is okay for a few hours, but there's not a great deal to it unless you love crafting.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I know what you’re thinking, Animal Crossing but the animals are emojis. That my sound like criticism but it’s far from that. The truth is that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. And while obviously inspired by AC the game has a charm of its own that make it super fun and worth your while.I love that the concept of the narrative is basically animals who kidnapped you to make their town pretty by holding you hostage in a fever dream.It’s such a wholesome game… trusting a mysterious stranger with unrestricted use of your spare room and giving them an axe. What could go wrong?The game looks great, and although the anatomy of the animals is a bit wonky at times it doesn’t take away from the experience. The truth is I’ve been desperate for a game that combines Animal Crossing and Farm sims, and it has so much potential for improvements. I can’t wait to see how this game evolves.Finally, I absolutely adore how completely British all the characters sound.  That alone makes it a 10/10 experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeously cute but the game feels hollow.You move to a town, for unknown reasons, and meet a bunch of very bland characters who suddenly with no real effort make you build a town. None of the characters are particularly unique. And the conversational always feels fakely nice, like a kids show.  I feel no purpose in the game. I do not connect with any of it. I am just doing, because I am told to do.There are still plenty of game breaking bugs. Within the first _2_ minutes after the initial conversation I was stuck in a wall. I then had to build something, which I ended up building twice -- because the UI didn't update when I built it the first time. Then later I had to do a quest which required wood -- but there wasn't enough because of that mistake and I was not given the tools to replant.It's a shame. Because there's some great features, like building your own furniture, and the art as said is gorgeous. But I cannot recommend this game when so many good Farming Sim/Life Sim games exist. It's a definite No, not even a Maybe from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game but so far it's very.... lacking. The Very Slow start is frustrating and will lead players to getting bored Very quickly. It takes ~4 in game days before you can start fishing or catching bugs, which for a while it seems will be your primary source of income. The crafting system inspired by My Sims is pretty rough around the edges and needs a lot of work. There also seems to be no real tutorials on things so you're left with only really vague ideas on what to do.Slightly less vague if you've played a certain Other life sim involving animals. However where that game succeeds, this game is struggling to find it's footing. In AC you can start making money pretty quickly without any hassle, in this one though? Things you find around the world sell for very low, while items you need like crafting recipes, tools, & backpack upgrades cost Quite A Bit of money. It's just too grindy for its own good.One area of the map seems to be locked off by a Very small height difference you could easily climb or jump...but you can't. So because of that, for the early game you're going to be locked to 3 areas with very little to do in any of them. I'm going to cut this game some slack since it's only a single person developer on top of early access, But as of right now I can't really recommend it. If you're a fan of life sims & animal crossing in particular, maybe keep on eye on this one. But while it certainly has potential, I'd definitely wait awhile before dropping $20 on it
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life is the result of chasing the things that make Animal Crossing the success that it is without having the chops to compete. Lifeless, dull characters with designs ranging from ugly to adequate populate a small town full of tedious tasks. Due in part to attempting to provide 'constant' gameplay a la Stardew Valley and eschewing real-time progression like its inspiration it has a lot of things to do; it's just that none of said things are enjoyable and the characters you do them for are written very poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd really like to recommend this but unfortunately I don't feel like I can. It's definitely a game for the young ones. The perfect way to play this game, would be doing a resource run every morning while waiting for shops to open etc, but time pauses in the mines, once you break those 12 rocks what do you do for the extremely long days due to every 10 minutes in game taking 3-5minutes IRL(or what it feels like), atleast there's the option to sleep for a few hours as well as 'until tomorrow', so you can pretty much skip through-out the day. There's not much to do in general, I know these types of games can be slow to begin with until you unlock this or that, but this game doesn't really have anything like that to unlock, besides a side path in the forest and maybe a clothing shop in the town 10 days down the line. The inventory was probably the most annoying thing, although i really like the little merit addition to unlock things, If the game was bigger in general I don't think locking a Map and Inventory Slots behind those is the right way to go, it does give you something to work towards though. Again there's also not much to have in the inventory so it's not all that bad I guess. The art style is both good and bad, while It's nice to look at and quite modern in a farming sim kind of way, some of the characters are quite terrifying to look at, especially your own character that you create in the beginning, the eyes just look like they're staring into my soul and it was super off putting.While it does give a huge , It's very bland and feels extremely unfinished, but if you're just getting into these kinds of games, or are  I think you'd really enjoy this game. Pros;- Art Style- Easy to learn- Can sleep for a few hours, 6 hours or a night- Merit system - Achievements seem quite easy to grind out( if you were interested in 100%)Cons;- Art Style- Not much content- Nothing challenging about the game (e.g Stamina bar, )- Sprint only lasts 2 seconds. (doesn't make much of a difference, the shrines to teleport to places are easily unlocked, and there's only like 3 places to go anyway)- Time pauses in the mines( I found this to be pointless due to there only being a few levels and around 8-10 rocks on each level, considering you can't get to most of the levels for awhile)- The building/design etc was quite difficult to learn and get used to.- bugs are small(considering the size of everything else, butterflies are barely visible)- lack of inventory slots- Mines only have around 5 levels I personally think an Animal Crossing inspired game quite like this is a great idea, it just needs a little bit more work.

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie version of  without time flow in real time. It recently released into Early Access with core mechanics in place but still needing a lot more work. Despite that, the game is quite fun and I look forward to seeing what the final product will shape up to be. It's a good game to dive into now so that you can hop on the forums and Discord channel in order to give input to somewhat contribute to the further development of this game. Please keep in mind that this game is primarily created by a single developer who is very responsive to suggestions and is working on frequent updates to help fashion the game into a better experience.There's a minimalist story, in which you, the protagonist human character, falls asleep on the train and wakes up in the rural town inhabited by bipedal humanoid animals who you can befriend. (If it's sounding familiar by now, I think it's intentional.) Without a place to stay, the innkeeper offers you a small room to stay and keep some of your belongings, in hopes that you will stay and help make the town better. The game starts with only two neighbors/villagers, and it's up to you to slowly expand and invite more villagers to settle. The gameplay is focused on several different elements, all of which are casual and essentially stress free.1.  play a huge part in this game. You can practically design and create anything you would like, from utility items to decorate pieces, using the crafting materials that can be found in-game. The in-game designer/creator tool doesn't have the best UI so it's hard to see what you are doing at times. Nevertheless, this will get most of the players to spend hours trying to create some cool-looking pieces. You can also create paints and fabric dyes, wallpaper, etc. to fully personalize how the town appears to you inside and out--from interior design in the homes to external decorations and statues.2.  is also something that you carry out bit by bit. Now keeping in mind that this is limited in function at this time, as you can build 4 different houses and each one can only house one resident. The biggest limitation is that the houses cannot be moved once they are built and only face forward at this time.3.  given by the villagers will come along, especially when more of them move into town. This is usually something fairly straight forward, such as giving an item to another individual or obtaining an item that's easy to get to. Other times you will have to provide a quantity of a craftable supply. And from time to time, you will also be asked to design and to place a piece of furniture in their home. This last bit sometimes can get a bit time consuming if you start pouring in creative juices in trying to design the next best thing. These tasks often have a number of days limit attached to them, but there is no penalty for not making the deadline, the quest/task just cycles out and will come back again later. Sometimes you are just unable to get the supplies needed in time, and that's okay.4.  are inevitably linked together, as when you start, your area of movement is very limited and you have to use those resources to explore more and expand the available locations that you can visit. With more regions progressively opening up, you will have more materials and more land to use. Ultimately the resources go back to materials needed for mostly the designs and crafts that you will do.5.  is also to be expected, as you will be fishing for a number of fish and catching insects (butterflies) also. The butterfly catching is easy and effortless, and the fishing is probably the only aspect of the game right now that involves any kind of reflexive button presses in its mini-game format that's fairly easy once you get used to playing it.Easy to use a keyboard and mouse, the controls that you might want to use are displayed on screen when it comes to that, so it's easy to figure out what to do. Controller works well for the most part, including the item design, but there are times when you will need a mouse and keyboard and the game will tell you. I imagine that full controller support will be an eventual goal.The game has adorable design, and you can create almost anything if you put your mind to it and have the resources.Seeing as you will likely end up spending many hours playing, the music can become a bit repetitive. It's not difficult to turn off the music if you so desire and play other music in the background.Almost everyone who is remotely interested should be able to play this game. It's casual and adorable, with a heavy emphasis on personal design.Current Early Access price is $19.99 base, which I think is reasonable for the game overall. Currently it needs some work still, so only buy in if you want to try it now and maybe contribute to the game's on-going development. The core mechanics are there, but the developer is making frequent updates both in planned content and also to fix problems and implement suggestions from players.1. It would be great to be able to generate blueprints to save for the items that you design instead of only being able to copy/edit from created items in the inventory.2. Villager identification for quests/tasks. It is very tedious to run around and talk to each one of them just to see if they have something for you to do that day.3. In addition, a quick map to show where each villager is would be awesome, since they are always wandering around and sometimes are difficult to find to trigger/continue/finish a task.4. Hopefully this comes around soon, but currently the houses that you build are permanent, and when they are put in, they cannot be rotated. So everything in town has the same directional orientation and I had misplaced a couple of houses so as to block off chunks of land that I could otherwise use. It would be great to be able to more customize the housing locations. This is going to be especially important when the planned farming update comes in.5. There's a way to share with other players your designs, and that's in the works. It currently only allows sharing of 5 designs so it would be nice to eventually get Workshop support and people can create and share whatever they wish instead of having the heavy restrictions.6. Craftable storage units or allowing users to maybe put clothing and other supplies away would be so much appreciated. Currently when I don't use something I toss it all over, and fortunately the game saves whatever you toss on the ground, so it's a big deal. The backpack inventory is all you have, and even fully upgraded, is not nearly enough slots for what you might want to hold.My very first play session is recorded here: is an impressive indie game made mostly by one person. It has some rough edges but has enough core mechanics for people to play it as a casual game and also to spend many hours with the designing tool. The game is rather shallow in terms of other content right now but hopefully that will change. Nevertheless, it is fun and will likely only get better from here. Definitely check it out some time!Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: 17 hours. finished it with complete achievements. Actually I want to give this game a side thumb, rather than recommend or not recommend it. In my view, this game is a cozy game that might be more suited to child players. On the positive side, this game has a warm, slightly nostalgic vibe, and a small portion of adventure that can keep someone awake and interested while playing it (e.g. unlocking new area). I also like some of the features, with the added positive value of the art style regarding the buildings and natural settings. But on the negative side, I am less satisfied with the character art style, customization (like seriously i dont like any of the hairstyle), and features which tend to be limited. This game is under-stimulating for teenagers and adults, making it slowly become boring despite the warm vibe it has. I also don't like things that feel pointless in this game, such as having barn even though there is no animal-raising feature. That being said, I think the 2$ price that I got at the discount is still worth it, but I don't think I have any interest in continuing or playing this game anymore. Good work, but still needs a lot of work.

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life is a cute little game, similar to Animal Crossing.It has everything; mining, farming, fishing and foraging! You even have a workshop where you can use little pieces to design furniture that you don't have the blueprint for or you cant find in the shop. The villagers are similar to ones from Animal Crossing but besides their requests, I don't really see much interaction with them.The progression for the game can be quite slow, and it's not always clear on what you need to do to progress further. It's a game where the merits really come into play, forcing you to do the tasks to get the merits in order to progress and unlock items. For example, I didn't realise I needed to unlock the bomb through merits to progress further in the mines and then be able to get to the red forest. Sprinting in the game is quite useless as I think the walk speed is enough and there's areas where you can teleport to from basically anywhere, but sprinting is useful for merits. The sprint speed is quite quick but doesn't last long, making the merits harder and grindier to get. The regrowth of trees is infinite unless you shovel the stumps out of the ground, and they don't take too long to regrow, the flowers and the grass take the same time to regrow. The stones/rocks in the mines spawn back in the next day which makes it easier to grind for stone, coal, etc. The game can be quite misleading when it comes to using emotes (waving at villagers), I looked at the merits and found that I needed to wave at villagers, so I went to the settings and was told the emote wheel was F. I pressed/held F and nothing happened, leading me to believe I just hadn't progressed through the game enough, like how it is in Animal Crossing. I then researched it on google, just to find out the actual key was C.I'd give this game an 8/10, but I wouldn't buy it at full price and rather when it's on a sale between 50-75%. It's not worth the full price, but it is a fun, enjoyable small game nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game with lots of potential. It follows the Animal Crossing formula, new kid in town earning money, decorating homes, and expanding the town.My favorite aspect of the game is the ability to customize craftable furniture. The world is your oyster. If you check out creator's custom content, you'll find amazing things. This is a huge plus in my book.You can decorate your villager's homes manually. You can take out and put in whatever you like, something that took Animal Crossing forever to do.It's not based on a real time system, which is great because I'm not time traveling or stressing about the passage of time. I spend each day how I want and can skip to the next day if I really want to.This game is STILL very buggy. If that's something you're not into or feel skeptical about, then you might want to wait on the game. I could make a list of bugs I've found. Many are benign, but others can be downright frustrating.It's possible for the game to freeze, lose items, and the fish AI make challenges hard.Overall I think it's a good game for creative folks, and it's worth the wait if you hate early access games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big Animal Crossing fan and I have always wished for Animal Crossing, or an Animal Crossing-like game for PC, well here it is. However, this game still has a long way to go before it gets there. I totally understand that it is Early Access and still in development, so I am not going to go off the rails and say that I don't like the game and won't play it, because in good time, I believe that this game will reach my expectations. My biggest complaint with this game currently, is that it lacks direction. There are very few quests that relate to any sort of story progression that are constantly active. There are a few in the tutorial of the game, but then you're on your own. The only quests that do exist, are if you talk to a villager and they ask for you to make them an item. This gets boring and repetitive after awhile. Similarly to Animal Crossing, it would be nice if the villagers grabbed your attention on their own, like displayed something above their head if they have a quest for you. The more villagers there are, the tougher it is to have to talk to everyone and find who needs something. I just need something that points me in any sort of direction with story progression, villager requests, etc.My next big issue is crafting using the blueprints. The blueprints, are hardly blueprints. An actual blueprint would show me exactly what I need to put where and guide me through HOW to build "a bed", or "a dresser", etc. Currently, all the blueprints do is help with size. I'm not that creative, I need a lot more guidance. How about making one general blueprint, like what is already available, for those who are creative and can make furniture from their own brains, and then have an option for those of us who struggle with this type of thing that guides us through how to make something.I also agree with many of the other reviews here that the animal villagers look a bit lanky and weird with the human-like bodies. That's one of the things AC does nicely with their game, is they make the villages cute, short, and chunky, or whatever qualities might relate to that animal. Another thing I would also really like to see is more of the furniture and items be interactive for both my own character, and the villagers. Like, I placed some musical instruments in my town center, but all they do is sit there. It would be cool to see the villagers wandering around sit at the drum set and start playing, or have them interact with the beach balls that I placed on the beach!So, overall, the game is a great start, but it has a ways to go! I would love to see it have these features I just listed, as well as many of the features that other reviewers have suggested. I do plan to stick around and hopefully see them through!

_childDocuments_.review: I would save your money on a better Animal Crossing clone rather than this one. It's boring and there's not much else to do when starting out. _childDocuments_.review: This game is rough and I'm changing my review from positive to negative after investing more time into it.Don't let the cuteness fool you.ISSUES=======- Hit boxes and collision detection is off in the shop. I can walk through counters.- Hit boxes and collision detection is off behind the houses. I get stuck walking.- Hit boxes and collision detection is off at the beach. I can partially walk on boulders.- No clear indicator that you are on a mound near the beach and can't walk off.- You need to unequip and reequip an already equipped item after every dialog.- You need to unequip and reequip an already equipped item after pulling weeds.- Derris does not tell you what fish or bug he is rewarding you for- Derris will reward you for fish or bugs you have already sold- Derris will reward you for a fish when you have caught a bug- Fishing mini-game has you awkwardly positioning fingers (D+E)- Fishing mini-game takes to long to reel in a fish. Like other reviewers said, it's not fun.- No ability to reorganize your backpack.- No sort button on your backpack- No "Sell Max" button on Sell dialog.- No "Craft Max" button on Craft dialog- Hitting right too much on both dialog returns you to 1 instead of clamping it.- No indicator you are at max with the arrow keys. Another reason this should be clamped.- Timed quests for places you can't yet travel to early game. (Ingredients)- Hitting space should progress dialog between characters like most games.- Mouse cursor hides during a dialog temporarily, making you lose track of movement.- Return  to unequip items and way on the other end of the keyboard. (Fitt's Law)The last might sound petty,  but this means a mouse and keyboard user either has to move his hand from the WSAD position, or his hand from the mouse to reach it. This goes to show how much care the developers put into simple input mechanics.CONCLUSION===========Think of this game as the offspring of My Sims and Animal Crossing.... but unpolished. I ask the developers to lookup Nelson's Law of UX. See how other games operate. Users will transfer expectations from one product to another. I understand its early access, but this most of these issues should have not been in its initial release.To make this more concerning, we are getting a farming patch with a few bug fixes inside them. Why introduce new features when other features are clearly broken. How much time was taken to read the reviews when this new game feature was introduced less than a week from early-access launch?What this tells me is that instead of plugging the hole in your boat that's sinking, you added a telescope for the passengers to look out at pretty things. All aboard! Hope you packed your swimsuits!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so much.  There are non-binary characters.  It is charming and the story is actually refreshing, being about getting tired of working constantly and feeling like you have no purpose, only to fall asleep from exhaustion and end up in the country.  On a whim you decide to stay and revitalize a small town.And then I played it.There is basically one or two quests for every in game day.  The pacing in the beginning is so incredibly slow that at one point I had to wait 3 in game days while flowers grew.  At this time I decided to 'beautify' the tiny space of the town.  I picked weeds, moved trees around, planted flowers, made pathways for the villagers.  I was so proud.  Then I sold what I thought was random trash.When the flowers finally grew, I found out what I sold was needed to progress.  And guess what?  It doesn't respawn.But then came bridges!  Surely I can build a bridge and cross to another part of the island and fix this, yes?  No.  I grinded money chopping logs, re-planting, waiting for them to re-grow and then chopping again.  It took hours and then I built a bridge only for it not to work.  The bridge is there!  But I cannot walk across it.  I can only assume that I have to progress further, only I can't because items won't respawn.Oh - and the update yesterday?  It has totally broken the collision of everything I have done so far and deleted half the furniture I made and placed the day before.No thanks.I am way too frustrated with this.  Maybe in a couple years when they actually get this from an Alpha build to something more like a game that works.Asked for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is still early access so I don't want to be too harsh with the recommendation, but I'd like to give some feedback based on a little over  7 hours of play time so far.The Good:-Furniture placement is really nice. Love the option to free rotate or rotate by 90 degrees.-Environmental art and furniture is very beautiful and polished.-Controls are very easy to pick up.-The crafting mechanic is really the star of the game and for the most part it's fairly intuitive. It's also super satisfying to see the villagers sit on chairs or cross bridges that I built from scratch.-I love getting quests from my villagers and really appreciate the extra time to complete them just in case you've depleted your resources for the day.-Fishing is fun! Reminds me of SoT fishing, one of my faves.The Not-So-Good:-The characters seem robotic. They are so close to being cute, but their faces don't emote at all and the dialog is super bland.-I bought a wallpaper in the shop and when I used it in my room it just disappeared. Would have been nice to block the action if you can't use wallpapers in there.-I placed a wall item in my inn room and it got stuck clipping halfway into the ceiling. Again, would have been great to block these actions if you aren't supposed to use those items in there.- Eh, I take it back. Not to hard to rack them up. However, it is hard to earn enough scratch for the net starting out without selling your neighbor's stuff.- Turns out I was a couple days before fishing became possible. Would be great not to get that prompt before I was able to fish... or at least have a clue that it's something I can't do yet. You know, "someone used to fish here quite a bit. I wonder what happened to them?" just a head's up that someone's going to make an appearance soon and let me do that. - Not hearing this issue anymore.-There is just too much dead time in the first 2 hours of gameplay. I found myself sleeping through most of the first several days and almost giving up on the game entirely. Once you can craft it's easy to get lost in the game, so I'm glad I stuck around... but I really feel that crafting should be introduced a little earlier, like day 2 or 3.  The Weird:-Stamina doesn't make sense right now. I burn stamina quickly while jogging, but chopping down trees and digging holes doesn't consume any of it? Seems like a pointless run block if you aren't going to use it on anything else. -I can just yoink items from the villagers' homes and they don't notice or care. I'm all for thievery but it seems a little out of place. I guess I kind of get it, so that I can decorate everyone's rooms, but it just feels weird...-Crafting is the best feature of this game, but it can be really frustrating to see the problem indicator on an item and not have a clue as to why it's showing up. Would be great to be able to click on that and see a reason, such as "object is too tall" "object is not wide enough" etc. I had to watch a few youtube videos to understand what the problems could be and could finally start having fun with it.Again, this is just some feedback based on the current state of the game. I'm sure the game will keep improving as time goes on. Looking forward to new developments!

_childDocuments_.review: This game leaves one wanting. It is clearly an Animal Crossing dupe and it isn't following the top rule of borrowing someone else's idea: they didn't improve it or make it their own at all. This game is thin and surfacey. Hokko Life lacks complexity at every turn. This is made worse by the fact that the devs did not bother to explain roughly 50% of the game principles/mechanics to the player. I believe it is this lack of transparency that makes Hokko Life appear to be more than it truly is, which is not worth more than $10.Gameplay:The pinnacle, #1 problem with this game is that it is one of targeting tiles (to use tools, to farm, to build) and the movement is clunky. The fact you can't change perspective adds to the dilemma. Oftentimes, I will mysteriously look past the next square, and have to walk back two spaces and forward again to target correctly. I don't like that the animations for watering/digging still happen if it is impossible, or you've already done it (in the case of watering). It's difficult to fish when you can't see the rive well, when you can't angle your pole, and catching butterflies can sometimes be vexing. I think it is because of the clunky, unpolished movement that they were kind enough to make your tools infinite. This game would be unplayable if the tools needed replaced after missing the same darn butterfly six times in a row. Since they weren't going to improve the visibility/character movement I guess it was the least they could do!Crafting:Do you like to make cute stuff? Do you check for balloons every 4 minutes? Don't worry, the crafting is completely untenable in this game! You receive maybe a dozen "recipes" and buy the rest, but they are really just ingredients. Then you can toil and suffer through their in-game building system. It does not follow any system I have used before. Every item I made was wonky and unfortunate. In the city, after taking the train, you can download all sorts of items for free. They are free! How cool. If there was not a community, though, this game would be ugly and boring, as the creators made Hokko Life an aesthetics desert.Farming:First off, the flowers. They are ugly. There are 5 kinds that you can grow. There are some one the island, and I dug them up to replant, but they don't spread and it was very tedious. The island plants are the best, but you can't grow them. Unreal. PS, my red flowers have just cropped up all over in one area, as they are spreading? Do I need fences? Why are no other flowers spreading? I hate the weeds. They are everywhere and sometimes you'll stand two squares away before the dialog to pull will appear. Movement, people! Fix this!!Next, the crops. There are so many and watering is OBNOXIOUS. It is so fury inducing I must use CAPITAL LETTERS. Okay? It's so bad! I have a real life garden and it takes the same amount of time to work for real food as it does to get you watering done in Hokko Life. Please tell me how an entire watering can only waters 7 plants? They don't tell you the water must be refilled so make sure you place your garden beside the pond! Or you'll want to drop dead :) Water every other day! Be smarter than me.Now, you may want to know, understandably, why is there farming and fishing etc. if the crafting is undeveloped and sort of nonexistent in the state they left it in? Exactly, I guess there had to be a game somehow, you know? You catch fish to sell them for 10 in game gold that you don't need to buy anything. You can grow them to fulfill food requests from Oma. By the way, did you know you need to keep seeing Oma to move the game forward, like, at all? Explains the otherwise pointless Inn, I suppose.Fishing:I prefer this method to the AC style, as it is very stressfree and easy to have prompts help you along as much as Hokko Life tries to help a fisherwoman out. On the flip side, it has to be this way because the vision/movement issues make it so that you'd really never have any hope of catching a fish without it telling you E! The river and pond are the worst offenders for visibility concerns. The fish are boring, though, and pointless. The challenges are okay. The boots are annoying. The baits matter, not that they explain that at all. Another time that the community made the game playable. In fact, fishing was very unrewarding until I looked it up online: you can get a treasure chest of basic crafting items/money you don't need if you hit E during the orange/blue section of the timer bar. Some fish are available during certain weather events, seasons, and require baits types. This is probably the most developed and nuanced portion of the game, but to no end. There's no clam bake on the books, kids, I fished for steam achievements.The 10 fish in 10 minutes challenge is painful. Getting a boot during a challenge is gutting.The fish Tournaments are a CROCK OF SPIT. Okay?!?!:?! I played for the last 10 hours because I wanted my blue ribbon. My good girl ribbon from Steam for getting all my achievements is not coming. The achievement says "COMPETE" in fishing tournaments. I don't enjoy fishing, really. I don't fish in real life. I don't like fishing and catching boots. I don't like it, Sam I am, and I tried it, alright? So I took part in the fishing tournament and it went quick, I caught enough to get bronze and laughed all the way to the bank. The second tourney I took part in but it was catching river fish and you know how I feel about that, so I caught one and got on the leaderboard. I checked, there I was, with one. The game didn't count it, though, because I guess I didn't get a medal? It isn't 1st, 2nd, 3rd, either- they say you need to catch 10 of the particular fish to get a gold, 8 and 6 for the others, respectively. This is OBSCENE. Compete does not meet place. It does not mean "meet an arbitrary number of fish caught" marker. It means take part, try, show up and give it a go. I am fuming. I told myself I'd stop at 23 achievements. 78% is enough, I thought. Then I was like, no, I'm so close, but I have to go to sleep another 90 times to attempt this achievement. Are you joking? It's not even a game anymore, it's a chore.Outfits/Character:I liked how much I could customize my character, but the outfit options are nonexistent. There is a tailor's knock off shop that has 4-6 unfashionable, plain things in one color each and the shop is only open 8 hours a day, and doesn't open when the day starts. I have been twice. I have gotten clothing as a reward from villagers. I have duplicates. Unreal.Villagers/Town:The villagers are boring and superfluous. I would take or leave them. The houses can be customized, but it's sort of buried in the one shop option a day and the dsigns take different items/money. I just built the same basic house for everyone because all the work for the others didn't make sense for how little I enjoyed the so-called improvements. There's not much to do with them, though the game wants to insist there's stuff to do. I'd say everything about this game is the appearance of substance but it's a cut out.Quests and Challenges:The mayor merits of the game are stupid, okay? I have unlocked whole rows of them but they unlock linearly, so since I haven't built 50 known recipes (50 chairs?) I have half a dozen "locked" things in the game. I'd realize, oh, I need to blah blah, make 20 custom things and then it'd be like UNLOCKED, UNLOCKED, UNLOCKED. How annoying to be held back that way. I have beaten this game and attempted to get 100% completion, and I still have dozens of locked mayor merits. That just doesn't make sense to me. May it also be mentioned that in my attempt to get 100% completion I saw that the most basic achievement is at 56% and most others are less than 10, 5, even 1%. People do not buy this game and play it, full stop.All this to say, nah. Play something  like Polyville Canyon or Kingdom and Castles. Love you, bye!

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't bode well when the achievement completion rate for a game is this low, for the kind of game it is.It is a game heavily inspired by Animal Crossing. It does things better than Animal Crossing, it does things worse. The one thing it gets rid of is having to play the game in real-time to progress. And with that said it's incredibly strange that most players stop playing the game after building their first house which is about a couple hours into the game at most. The progression makes sense for the most part, but certain things are overpowered compared to how you would obtain certain resources otherwise. Fishing gives you a lot of basic resources like wood, stone, and coal. And it even replenishes your bait used for the most part. But having to manually go around an crop trees is quite tedious, but that's a gimmie compared to other games where you harvest trees for resources.It's just that this game gives you a very free way of obtaining wood as well as making money. Money isn't an issue like most other Animal Crossing like games. The main issue I mainly had was storage. As well as placing items being quite honestly annoying because of the different shapes of items, as well as not being able to place items even if there is space to place it, as well as being able to place items when there isn't space to place them. It's very inconsistent and makes creating certain layouts either tedious or impossible. If you want to place an item behind another, most likely you won't be able to because the interaction hitbox is the physical model of said item rather than the tile outline that item occupies for whatever reason. This game very much embraces the psychotic ideologies or theories people sumize about Animal Crossing. You cannot say no to anything. If you are tasked with something you will have to do it. You cannot overfish, you cannot over catch bugs, they are an infinite resource that respawns constantly. You will always be able to get a treasure snag on each cast. You will always be able to catch a butterfly even if you miss the first swing. You can dig holes, and not fall in them. You can magically teleport to each load zone even if the teleporter is literally right next to the load zone you want to go to making it utterly useless. There is a subtle, yet underlying, unhinged quality to this game. Maybe it's the fact you can dye yourself a neon red and stand out like a cherry red tomato as you stand ominously in a bush. Maybe its the fact the villagers don't react to being pushed around or you barging into their house in the dead of night and sleeping in their bed without permission. Maybe it's the fact if you get the angle just right you can shove a villager partway into the floor. Maybe it's the fact you can plant trees clipping into the rock walls enclosing your encampment. There is a lot of liminal qualities that I cannot decide is the result of lack of features or pure intent. The achievements aren't all that difficult either. You just wait three days and harvest minerals to upgrade your tools and then buy more houses. This isn't the most ambitious game, but there is very little to mess up. This is very much a game meant for children.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in custom decorating, 3D modeling or kitbashing, this is the game for you!If you can slog through the first bit of the game and unlock the basics, then this game becomes absolutely worth the price. The high levels of custom creation you can get with this game is insane. You can literally make anything you want as long as you procure the necessary resources. Unlike AC where I had to save tons of bells and wait literal days to be able to get a cute bridge, I was able to fully create my own custom Japanese red bridge exactly how I wanted pretty quickly from scratch with some wood planks and red paint. You can also upload your creations for others to use! Don't want to make your own stuff? Download other people's creations & use it for yourself! The creation UI is very similar to 3D modeling & everything you create is kitbashed from sets you unlock!I was kind of unsure about this game at first because of the early slow burn, but now that I pushed through it, I honestly think this is going to be one of my favorite games.I also recommend joining the discord & taking part in the community there! Share your creations & get inspired by others. The devs also listen to requests and have already acted on some community requests which I absolutely appreciate.Edit: This game is constantly being updated with so many new cool features! Definitely impressed with the dev's dedication & creativity
