_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun life sim, get something else. If you're looking for an unsettling coma theory bait axe murderer story, this is the game for you. The scene of your character riding the train to the village is deeply unsettling, straight out of a horror flick. It doesn't help that you waltz into the inn at an obscene hour in the wind and rain, and everyone is so excited to let you stay the night. It felt very odd, and half the villagers being plushies did not help the setting. Maybe that's the point? The Mayor Merits system is just weird to me. PC is not the mayor, never said anything about being the mayor, and you have to complete them to unlock things like running. And the meh gameplay and clunky controls did not help at all in endearing this mildly creepy game to me. It's a good idea, needs a bit more development time to really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: super cute game and I am sooo happy I bought it. It is kinda like a bootleg ACNH, but at the same time it has features ACtwt is still crying and wishing the "original" would have. It definitely offers it's very own spin and seems like I can actually play it for a few years.POSITIVE+ create your own furniture (feels like modding)+ trees/houses become see-through when you stand behind them + place objects everywhere!+ rotate the objects however you like+ everyone is they/them. you don't need to choose a gender and you can just express it by hairstyle and clothes. all the villagers are genderless, too (in English at least. I played in German for a while and there they used gender pronouns)+ place things in different areas. put a house on top of the mountain, decorate the special farming area, build a fish shop. the possibilities, omg+ the town is kinda small-ish, but because of the different areas you don't have to include a farm in that space which gives more opportunities to create your dream town+ online feature / hokko creator shop: download community items and place them freely around your town.+ move the villagers houses without paying in-game currency. just pick it up and move it (even rotate it)+ decide who moves in and into which house+ you can move into another house as well+ there is so much to do! farm, fish, catch insects, visit the island, mine, decorate, build things, ..... it has so much content! NEUTRAL / HALF-HALFo I know many people think the villagers look creepy and I remember the first look/trailer, but in the final product I honestly don't think they are that creepy? Some of them are weird, but there are some really cute ones too. I love the detail each villager has. Instead of offering hundreds villagers with the same personalities each one has their own story and character, which is really cool.o the town is created newly in each save file and can differ. the first town on switch was not good because the workshop was so far away from the exits. with my pc file, it's almost next to the teleporter AND I have a freaking mini-waterfall in the middle of my town. so cute, didn't know that was possible. If I had known, I would have restarted the game more often until I had gotten the perfect layoutNEGATIVE- sometimes a bit buggy (game flickers while running)- the start is super slow and you basically have to go to sleep at 2 pm to skip for the next day- then, boom. five quests in one day and you feel crazy busy. I wish they would lock some of the things more behind quests and guide the player more.- some things take quite some time to figure out and there could be more explanations from Oma or other characters- I played on the switch first and building mode was basically unusable. It is only for PC. For switch, it is absolute hell- creator shop only allows 8 items on display. there are mind-blowingly amazing objects by the community, but they can't be downloaded anymore because the creator updated their shop- the amount of downloaded and created objects is very limited. I hadn't downloaded much and it still said "limit reached" (AFTER I was trying to save a selfmade creation and it got lost. which sucked)- game often crashes when using the online feature- downloading one creator object multiple times can result in data loss / game destruction Even though I do have some negative points, I think these could be fixed in future updates as the creator is apparently listening to the community well and some bug fixes are already in the works. But, the positive outweighs the negative by sooo much and I am really happy with the game. Heck, I bought it two times already haha. I moved to PC because I want to create my own objects, but I will still play on my switch from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun and cute game.  The crafting and designing is amazing! I'm so bummed though because when I first bought this game, I couldn't get it to start.  It kept giving me error messages.  I looked online in discussions and forums for answers.  I tried to add it to the exceptions on my firewall which didn't work the way the instructions told me to because it wasn't on the list to add and I couldn't add it by selecting files. It was frustrating. I tried restarting, clearing the cache, and restoring files. Then I just kept trying to log onto the game. It would seem to work and then the screen would go dark and close out.  I got a few different error messages each time, but I kept hitting play and trying. Then, suddenly it let me play.  I was able to play for a few other sessions this way, but it always made me try several times before working.  Now this morning I've tried the same as before, but now it's not working at all.  I don't understand the inconsistency.  It doesn't make sense.  I hope others don't have the same issue.  I recommend the game, but want others to know that this could happen to you.  Sad that I can't play, but hoping for a fix.UPDATE: I just decided to uninstall the game and reinstall it and that fixed it! Thought I'd leave the original message in case anyone else needs help.  We'll see if this is a permanent fix, but so far it loads up just fine now.  YAY! Okay, so for my complete review after playing for 19 hours:  I'm so excited for this game to be fully complete because I'm loving the early access game play so much.  It's a vibrantly colorful world with beautiful graphics and so much to do.  If you enjoy Animal Crossing and farming games like Stardew Valley this is going to be such a treat for you.  If you aren't sure what to do at first, talk to the NPCs in your town.  If they don't give you hints or quests you can work on catching butterflies by buying a net from the store and just focus on earning money by selling the butterflies at first and then go to bed and see what the next day offers.  Each day you'll have more things to work on as you unlock more things and get more villagers.  Fishing is a little tricky at first, but follow the prompts on the screen and you'll get it down. The design table can be a bit tricky too, but same as fishing, follow the control guide and you'll eventually get a feel for it with more practice. You can also look for guides (see my suggestion below in the last paragraph)  It's the kind of game that just keeps getting better and better the more deep you get into it.  There are some really great tutorials online if you just google or search on YouTube.  I found a great YouTube channel called Satoshi Gaming and she does some very helpful tutorials and relaxing game play.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this one.  There's too many game breaking bugs in the tutorial that block progression in the game.- You have an item cap in your inventory but nowhere to put down items. - You have a required tutorial quest to fix a chair that you can't do so you drop it in the house to save inventory- Now you can't pick the chair up to finish the tutorial- Tutorial is required to unlock all the features of the game...Its not ready yet guys.  Its kind of embarrassing.  Fix the tutorial, then maybe people can play it.[UPDATE] Most of the progression problem is level design / usability.   You need to progress through several days, get all the way into the back of the mine where the Iron Ore is, make sure there is inventory space in your backpack (which it is not clear where the cap is).  Then locate and make sure at least TWO villagers have moved in (specifically Poa).  None of this is obvious.  It took me 5 hours of beating my head up a wall to get through it before I saw any design features and customization that we were promised.  Only 6.4% of players (at the time of writing this review) actually got this far.  Oh...and i still haven't figured out how I'm supposed to make bait to fish with yet.You could go back to learn Design 101:-Put a bulletin board up for getting / returning quests.-Make a storage solution available right at the start so you have somewhere to put stuff.-Give players the ingredients you need to craft stuff to get through the entire tutorial.-Break tutorials into smaller pieces as you 'discover new areas', don't force it back to back.  -No tutorial event should take place over a day span.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you get it on sale. I was able to purchase it for only $4. I wouldn't purchase it for the full price unless you're a child. I love cozy games but this game felt too simple for an adult. I do like that it's slow paced. You don't feel stressed or rushed by what time or day it is like in most games in this genre. But what is stressful is how wonky movement is. I wish you could turn your camera around to move your character in different angles, instead everything is tiled like a pixel game. Catching bugs is also a pain too. I found myself getting frustrated swinging my net around. There isn't an actual mechanic to it, or a way to know how to catch the butterflies exactly other than by chance.I wish the NPCs had more depth and lore to them. I don't feel compelled to talk to them so in turn I don't feel attached to the world.But I do like the very slow chill paced, and how everything unlocks in time by work and completing merits badges. The furniture and store items look cute too. It could be fun to fully decorate the houses in time. The music is also very relaxing.I might jump back in again in the future to play further along. Definitely not the best game, but not the worst either. I honestly rate this game somewhere between a thumbs up and thumbs down.... but I'll give it a thumbs up because I bought it for so cheap and it's a nice simple game to unwind in...

_childDocuments_.review: IN 4 WORDS: GREAT IDEA, POOR EXECUTION.Where to start?25-28 hours in, I unlocked nearly everything.Was it fun playing those hours? Not really.The game is very slow and tedious.You do upgrade some tools, but the merits You need to finish to get them, makes them useless by the point You finish them. It's very frustrating at times, and while the game seems to be 3D, the camera is fixed. Meaning... if You rotate the building so the side of the house is visible to You, You won't be able to enjoy the beauty of it.While there are many types of houses, I found that there is no need for any fancy ones, as the basic one will do the job, and nobody will complain (didn't see any NPC saying he doesn't like it). I saw about 2 different colours of external walls and roofs, and this is very disappointing because we are in the game where You can craft so many things, make complicated items, make Your own fabrics, rugs, wallpapers and floor, yet a function like use PAINT on external wall, does not exist!To be honest I would be completely happy with a game where I need to buy stuff in order to build something, and make quests to earn money, and just throw away the whole aspect of farming and mining, because I NEVER felt so bored doing these chores.The item builder/editor is a nightmare. Maybe it's more intuitive on Nintendo, but it doesn't work well on PC. It won't snap properly, You can't centre things. It's hard to point stuff, rotate, resize. The whole experience could have been so much better if the devs simply focus on the thing that makes this game UNIQUE - ITEM CREATION. Instead we got some farming, some fishing, some mining, some frustrating bug catching, because of the camera You can't really say how far You are from the bug, and an editor which is so frustrating that if I would have been playing on a console it would fly out of the window a few times.If You don't mind too calm, too slow game, and controls that are not intuitive, then You might try the game, but to be honest, I've seen a lot better games than this one for example: Dinkum.

_childDocuments_.review: A game similar to Animal Crossing, but with farming sim stuff too.    • This game is mostly comparable to Animal Crossing, but additionally, there are farming sim mechanics as well.     • Gameplay includes: placing houses & recruiting villagers, villager quests, planting trees/flowers, foraging, crafting, mining, fishing, bug catching, artifact seeking, collecting, and eventually, farming.     • Initial character customization is choosing hair, eyes, and skin pigment. Your character is, by default, non-binary and characters in the game will use “they/them” pronouns on the rare occasion that they refer to your character.     • Further customizing your character with clothes happens after the game has started. Eventually, a character that runs both a clothing shop and hair salon sets up in the village square. Items that can change appearance are: tops, bottoms, shoes, glasses/masks, and hats.    • Merits Rewards are rewards granted for doing a certain number of tasks. Some rewards unlock objects or functions that make the game easier.     • No combat.     • Several afro-textured hairstyles. Most games have, like, 2 (feminine & masculine) or none at all. Additionally, the player can make their skin pigment whatever they want.    • Rainbow-themed clothes and at least one Trans Pride top.    • A decent amount of areas to unlock and discover.     • It’s fun to choose where houses are built and to decorate the town.     • Fishing and bug catching is fun.     • The controller works well for the most part.     • Tedious crop watering. The watering can only holds enough for watering 6 crops. Watering is one-by-one. There’s only one pond on the farm land, so the crops planted further away are particularly annoying to go back and forth for. It takes a long-a$$ time to unlock sprinklers or the weather device; the prerequisites for unlocking these are things you’d accomplish toward the end of the game. (Btw, why do devs do this sh!t? Why would you make something extremely useful available toward the end of the game when the player is about to be finished with the game? Devs do this way too often in games.)    • I absolutely hate the furniture designer. It’s frustrating regardless of whether I’m using the controller or mouse. The mouse is marginally better, but it takes a lot of patience to actually make a good design. I just don’t have said patience. Sadly, to unlock Merit Rewards, the game requires you to use the furniture designer a lot. Ugh.    • House exterior roofs and siding (to buy) in the real estate office don’t alternate often enough and don’t have nearly enough variety. The whole time I played the game, sidings were only ever yellow, green, and blue. Roofs were only pink and variations of brown.     • Lack of personality. The devs just took a lot of gameplay ideas from Animal Crossing (which is fine), but didn’t really do anything special with them. What makes AC so successful is both gameplay  it’s cute/quirky/upbeat personality.     • Game locked up after the first new resident event. My character was supposed to spawn in front of Rosa and the new resident, but I placed the house near the river, so my character couldn’t spawn in the river and it kept spawning across, where it’d get stuck. Had to restart a few times to get my character to spawn in the right place for it not to lock up, and by right place, I mean right in Rosa and the resident’s faces.     • During a Merit Reward unlock, the game locked up. Couldn’t exit the menu from any tab. Had to shut down and restart. Thanks to autosave, I didn’t lose too much time, but it was still annoying.    • Fish shadows occasionally show up out of water. It doesn’t even come close to being as fun as Animal Crossing,  there was some fun to be had. It’s not as expensive as AC, so if you don’t have a Switch or money for AC, this technically is an alternative. It also often goes on sale, so there’s that too. It’s usually $20, but I got it for $6-something. Ultimately, the game wasn’t anything special, but it was fun  for me to not hate it. If there was a “neutral” option for reviews, this would be in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Someone took the look of Animal Crossing and mixed with My Time at Portia;  Bit of a winner for the kids, and big kids I guess.I like the crafting mechanics in this game. You can literally build anything if you have the resources and the right size blueprint. I wanted to build a bridge over a river to get to the other side and there was a blueprint for it. I took about 10 mintues to craft a pretty simple brige but it still looked good. You have a simplified 3D interface which allows you to drop pre-fabs in to craft the item to your specs (Scale/Rotate/Move are available) . Certainly encourages the creative crafting aspect. You can also buy extra things like paint and fabric materials as well as 'stampy' template textures.Just don't expect to be crafting everything.  You have a very small movement area  which even though its small you don't really want it to be big as your resources rely on rock and wood mainly. Not sure where you are supposed to mine when you have taken all the rocks though. Seems like a good game and wasn't until 3 hours into the game that I discovered I had to meet the fisher dude at the beach before I could craft a fishing rod. The fishing mechaninc is much different from any other fishing mechanic I've used so you'll have to try a couple of times before you catch a fish.  Just need an online presents but for now its a well paced quest line.Note there is no online presence so don't expect an MMO experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Relaxing Music, Good Graphics, Good variety of fantasy skin tones and unlimited energy to catch bugs, fish. Etc.Cons: When it rains its really dark - could use some lights around town or at least ones you can make to place, You cant move the houses that are already down in the town - makes it hard to plan your town, Items sometimes land out of reach when you dig, For diversity purposes there needs to be a better color wheel of sorts to allow for more natural skin tones & finally the game is slow to start, you have to run back and forth a lot the first 3-4 days to different characts, the game could use some small tasks or mini quests would make it a bit more fun and not as "grindy"Overall I think this game is beautiful however some suggestions are: A build menu that allows us to move the already existing townies, homes (within reason of course), A better color wheel for natural skin tons, the rgb sliders are great but they just don't give the vast range of skin tones that people have. An on-screen quest list would be great and finally to make the town more cohesive I think it would be good to have paths that we can move/make and move. Thank you for the super fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes away all of the annoying things about ACNH, retains what people love and expands on that. Sure there is no terraforming, but I personally don't care about that. I'd rather have had the key elements of Animal Crossings of the past just better. This game is developed primarily by one person I believe, and I'm convinced now more than ever that people should have higher expectations of Nintendo. They have the money and a large team, they can do so much more for the $60 they charge. This game is early access and is lacking a bit in polish that you'd find in a AAA game such as NPCs getting stuck behind furniture and items sometimes falling where they shouldn't but for the most part it's been a wonderful experience. If you're like me and often wait for a sale, I'd say just get it at the $20 (I did) it's more than worth it for hours of enjoyment you'd get out of it and I'm happy to support a game where the developer put obvious passion and hard work into.Some minor details that may be helpful to some people, this game has good controller support and works well with remote play (i've been using the Razer Kishi). So basically you can play handheld like Animal Crossing. One tip i'd give is to make sure you never turn in a quest or loot with your inventory full, very rarely you can run into an issue where you can lose the item. Looking forward to the finished product!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Manages to be both boring and fiddly at the same time. I am very impressed by a lot of the user created content, but that's not a good reason to play a game like this, IMO.I was looking for a game that had minimal to no time pressure while still providing something to look forward to as I played. What I got was a game that managed to put its most annoying mechanics front-and-center while what I would have originally thought was the main gameplay zipped by in tiny bursts. I gave this game thirteen hours to impress me, and at the end of that time, I realized all I was actually impressed with was the ingenuity of the community in building custom items.Main game progression is gated behind use of the most normal-sounding and yet most frustrating sprint mechanic I have ever put up with; you sprint with left-shift, but you have to start sprinting after you start moving, which I have never seen before, and your character gets winded very quickly. Have fun sprinting for 400 seconds about three seconds at a time to get the essential unlock, let alone the 1800 for the unlock that seems to be there to celebrate how long you have been thoroughly playing the game.Main game progression is gated behind grinding treasure chests via fishing, which manages to be both easy (hold WAD keys as indicated) and a pain in the rear (you can't control your cast distance other than choosing where to stand, you have to get the hook very close to the fish for them to care, and they move around quite a bit). I got treasure rarely enough that I managed 4/10 treasure despite having caught over 100 fish. This is where I noped out.As far as the character interaction, the visuals are cute, and yes, I would be able to identify specific characters by their dialogue, but that's about it. At least one character is actively obnoxious, and most of them are just meh. The tasks they want you to do are basic and don't seem particularly tied to the character, and none of them are actually endearing.If you, like I, got this from Humble Choice recently, I found Grow: Song of the Evertree to be a much better game. Doesn't have the Animal Crossing vibe quite as strongly, but at least it hasn't left me feeling like I got scammed out of my time and energy.Edit: I decided that so I don't get constant news about the building contests and so on, I am removing this game from my account. I am so sure I will never play it again that I don't even want it languishing in my backlog.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Review UpdateI don't know if Hokko Life will become a different game than it is now, if it will be story rich action packed multiplayer or whatever dreams you might have about it, but in its current state it is A GAME FOR CREATIVE PEOPLE.If you consider yourself not very creative, if you prefer to follow a story told, if you are at a loss what to do because nobody told you, if you find games where nothing happens just boring, if you have no patience with an Early Access, if you want action, goals, entertainment, fun, then Hokko Life is DEFINATELY NOT the right game for you.But if you just need a blank piece of paper to get entertained by your own imagination, if you are into designing things, if you like crafting stuff but don't want a game holding your hand, THEN THIS IS definately THE RIGHT GAME FOR YOU.On top you will meet other creative people who share their creations with each other. Hokko's welcoming community is waiting for you.- - -If you've ever played My Sims on PC then you'll recognize the similarities. I wished for years someone would remake the concept & this dev, Robert Tatnell aka Wonderscope has succeeded in doing so.The game is structured very similarly to what i played as My Sims. One starts in a run down town & the main endevour of the game is to make it attractive enough, so that new people want to settle there. The world is disected in smaller parts, which load on entrance, it is filled with different ressources & those are used to build & create. Oc Hokko Life is not a complete carbon copy of My Sims from then, which drew itself inspiration strongly from another game, Harvest Moon & in the meantime there were similar & very popular games, like Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia & the residents of Hokko are actually fable like animals & thus the game reminds many players of the also very popular game, Animal Crossing. Why i mention My Sims is because it had a very unique ingredient not to be found in any other game afaik, a workshop where players can do more than just rebuild predefined items. Hokko Life contains a very similar workshop, filled with building parts, textures & paints, which are assambled by the player in the workshop with atmost freedom, with the only restriction, the objects must be functional along few points, every other design is up to the player's imagination & skill. Hokko Life is in its current state in Early Access, it is a pretty far developed but not at all finished game. It is unpolished, it has bugs, it has dead ends & is unbalanced. I would still very much recommend it, it is already now a very fine peaceful & charming game & it looks like the dev is quite experienced, dedicated & updates the game often. The game shows a great promiss & i am very excited to see it grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: Game  didn't seem that bad at first, but wow is it a headache... And i'm QUITE patient with early access games.Wasn't expecting much, as I went in with the impression that this game is basically in alpha. I expected bugs, but hoped for none too major. Found my first game breaking bug just now, and it pretty much did me in--my character is stuck in the fence because I was trying to catch a butterfly by the workshop and as I pressed E, the dialogue box to "enter" came in.Big mistake.See, this game has no logical pathing. My character didn't run into an object and immediately script, "oh, I'm stuck. better WALK AROUND THIS SOLID THING IN THE WAY UNTIL NO COLLISION". It didn't even just automatically teleport me in. *sigh*Would have been forgivable if I could manually save without quitting the game, but as far as I can tell, that's not a thing. So I basically am going to lose an in-game week and over 2 hours of progress over this tiny oversight. I'm not sure why the devs even allow you to walk indoors with something equipped. Considering the butterflies clip through and SIT INSIDE the buildings, did they not foresee this issue? Or is it something they just decided to work on later? It's a pretty obvious bug and pretty irritating with no unstuck commands or ways around it (such as reloading). You can't open the menu nor control the character when they are attempting to enter a building, btw. everything on the screen goes away and no button presses work, (except maybe Alt+F4). Other issues are usually simple stuff like you have to be basically directly on a character to talk to them, using MK to play doesn't set the aiming up right--it is very clunky and games like this need a controller, (hardly any support for that atm but there is some, so I'm sure they'll add more later), when talking to characters they slide over to you when turning and, if they are seated, they basically are just floating and sitting in midair. Very Strange. Speaking of interaction distance, the entrance bug was unexpected because the distance in order to enter a building is quite small. It was, (presumably), significantly smaller than the distance i was when trying to catch the butterfly, so that vacuum effect was quite strange.In terms of money, the economy feels fine and well balanced. No complaints there. The fishing is not worth it, however. It is an absolute waste of time and probably the biggest headache in the game. If you have played games like My Time At Portia, the fishing system won't be hard for you to catch hold of (ha). However, casting your line and getting a bite? LOL good luck. Even if you cast and it lands directly in front of their faces, the fish will swim past the bobber and go about their business. It's like you're so unlucky you manage to find the only blind fish in existence. Now, the fishing minigame itself is challenging, I admit that, but what do you expect to catch with a rod made of sticks and grass? It'll likely be easier with upgrades, (logically speaking), In terms of money (again), fishing is a massive waste of time because you'll probably not get anything worth more than 6 coins. Add in the time consumption of spending maybe around a minute+ just trying to get the fish to SEE the line and then another 30-45sec of minigame... Yeah. SUPER not worth it. You could probably catch at least 5 butterflies worth 23 coins each in the time it takes you to catch 1 fish. Don't bother with it. Also, there's some mention of bait, which I'm saving worms for, but we shall see how that develops. Also there isn't  any snapping in placing anything, so you might end up with some furniture ghost floating around that you can't get back down. The "Move" prompt just doesn't show for it. Another bug, but not a huge deal. I'll just be more careful in the future so my future house isn't hideous.That being said, if you have epilepsy or any photosensitivity, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. There is a BIG flash when you catch insects, and I really don't know why they don't give a warning?? That's a huge safety issue, and you could probably get sued over it. Yeah, sure, people don't have to play the game, but what if they don't know there's flashing BECAUSE YOU DON'T TELL THEM and they catch a bug and immediately have a seizure?  Some people are sensitive enough that 1 flash can trigger them, some others are triggered by repetitive flashing. Better safe than sorry, just don't play at all if you're photosensitive. Seriously. The only way to make money for the most part is bug catching. You might be able to get something for the items you craft, but that takes blueprints. Which cost money. So unless you're fishing 24/7, good luck with that. The game will ridiculously grindy, but somewhat possible. It just wouldn't be worth the time as of right now.Speaking of money (again), I think the biggest pro here is designing everyone else's homes. Seriously. 10/10. I sold all of Oleander's stuff for being a bad boi and kept what I wanted from it. Sold the purple elephant's amps because I don't want noisy neighbors. Lots of money, lots of free furniture for me, and bad boi has to sleep on the cold floor in the corner. (Next time he gets the can of pennies.)Overall, in its current state, I would not recommend. I was actually quite disappointed given how long I've been waiting to see this game, but I am grateful to be able to at least play! I'm definitely going to keep playing, but realistically, I would say wait at least a good 6 months from now when they have more updates done, and see if content-wise it's worth playing. Hopefully we'll have a decent amount of bug fixes then as well.Edit: Updating to recommended because this game actually has an autosave feature. Wasn't sure if it did or not because it doesn't tell you, and I don't expect early beta/alpha games to have such a feature. I logged back in and was reset to the bedroom starting point, but it was the same time and I still had my money/items. The game breaking bug was thwarted without my knowledge... Just wary of something different in the futureEdit 2: There's other good stuff to the game I never mentioned, and I feel that's a tad unfair. The first that came to mind was ETHNIC HAIR. YES. You read that correctly!!! They actually have DECENT ethnic hairstyles!!! They have twists and cornrows, and either could really pass for dreads, as well as lovely fluffy ponytails/pigtails! More than just the standard boring Afro for anyone who isn't european or asian. Anyone with curly/kinky hair knows how hard that is to find in a game, let alone having it look decent.Another pro: YOU CAN EVICT RESIDENTS. I didn't like one particular resident, so I gave him the boot. Brought in someone else I convinced and I love my town A LOT more!!! That level of customization I always wanted in Animal Crossing, but they never implemented anything like that. Quite silly, really...I would also say the furniture designing platform is both great and awful. It's hard to understand until you get it right for the first time, and then you get what you're looking at. You can eventually unlock a computer that shares users' creations (current WIP?) and it's looking similar to the workshop in Sims. Basically you can share your creations and use others'. However, the creations they have on there I suspect are just stock creations by the devs, but I could definitely be wrong! There's challenges for furniture themes on there, so it's quite believable that it is indeed creations by other users. Add the fact that the interface and creation scheme is incredibly in-depth, and I'd say I like it more than I hate it now that I've gotten used to it. I will say, however, bring in PLENTY of materials. Seriously. I do it in the hundreds. I never know how much Im gonna need of each material, so i try to bring 200-300 each time i want to be creative on the bench. It would seriously suck to spend hours and then have to start over again because you're short a bit.

Villagers don't seem to have as much personality as in AC, and the UI isn't as friendly. Don't go into this expecting AC and you will be pleasantly surprised. There are enough differences to make it its OWN game in my opinion. I have currently played 15 hours and feel as though I have barely scratched the surface, so I don't understand the reviews that say there isn't much to do. Yes, overall the game is a bit watered down compared to other big name sim games, but there's still enough to keep you busy. There's mining, fishing, bug catching, crafting, etc. Hokko Life draws heavy inspiration from Animal Crossing, but I feel as though it stands on its own and was created with love by a dev who really put their heart into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew it was an early access and I knew what I was getting into. It's not finished or polished and it's made by one person. I knew what this meant and I wanted to support them and try the game. THERE IS A TON TO DO and work towards in the game, I'm never bored. This is an enjoyable and casual game with a very unique and complex crafting/building system. I've been playing for days straight and will continue to. The game has never felt slow and boring yet and I still have a ton of things to unlock.FUN THINGS You Can Do In The Game:- Craft furniture from absolute scratch. Buy paint and a couple square cubes and manipulate shapes into furniture and usable objects. Allows for insane creativity. If you're bad at this, you can download other peoples designed furniture or buy furniture from the shop.- A farming update is coming soon, so says the Dev.- Seasonal changes. Bugs and fish change depending on time and season and location. Collecting!- Unlock new areas. Later in the game you can unlock more locations to find new resources. More locations will be added in the future.- Recruit villagers and decorate their homes. Each evening a new villager will arrive whom you can ask to move in. Make unique furniture for them or buy furniture and decorate their house!- Minority friendly. The single-studio developer goes by he/they pronouns. There are a good chunk of afro hair styles. Once you pick your skin tone, ranging from ivory to deep brown, you can then adjust sliders for undertones.- NO energy drain! We love not passing out at the beach because we wasted all our energy for the day.Once you join the discord or ASK OTHER PLAYERS questions when you're lost, you'll keep playing. If you never seek out solutions, you'll stop playing. The game should provide this help to players, but it doesn't currently which is why most people stop. I just look in the Steam discussions and ask questions in the Discord (for quicker replies) and I'm set.XNEEDS IMPROVING Or Adding: (not gonna touch on bugs because, duh, it's an EA)- A crafting tutorial. It is so hard to do if you're not into model-engineering-stuff and aren't an art major! Even if you are those things, the game doesn't tell you how to do anything it just sort of happens.- A better introduction. You're on a train, wake up, and you're just here. I do not have a problem with this, Animal Crossing is very similar in this respect, but I don't have a problem with people saying they would like more narrative.- The only things you can do at the moment are craft and decorate, but these take up A HUGE amount of your time and resources so I don't see how you can get bored with it, unless you don't like creating artistic pieces and decorating. If so, maybe don't get it YET. I say yet because more content and activities WILL be added in the future.To people who say the game shouldn't have been released in the state that it's in, ... it's an early access. It's kind of like a Kickstarter. Finding interest and supporting the developer(s) (financially and with constructive feedback) allows them to create the finished product they know they can make and that you know you want. With peace and love, if you don't want to play an unfinished game, don't.p.s I've experienced NO game breaking bugs so far. Only one small duplication bug. Im absolutely able to play the game fully with little to no issues. That doesn't mean you won't have any, but thought I'd add that.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, charming little game similar to Animal Crossing. There's farming, crafting, fishing, mining, etc. You get villagers, do requests, etc. pros: you can save anywhere and at anytime. Would like more variety. It can also be a bit fiddly. Like, crafting could be great with a few improvements.watering crops takes way too long. I assume there might eventually be an upgrade. _childDocuments_.review: This game is not a replacement for any possibly related game you might see a resemblance to (ex. Animal Crossing, Harvest Moon/Rune Factory, Stardew, Ooblets or the like). My current recommendation is to play those games if you haven't already. If you need something new and you’re okay with a different animal crossing-like experience(one focused more on design than connections or story advancement), I think Hokko Life mostly delivers. It takes some of what those games have offered and delivers in a semi-unpolished way with a focus on creation. (The unpolished parts of this game lead to a lifeless or unfinished feeling.) For the price offered, I think that's a deal. Even more so at a discount. (I picked it up for 13$ after its post-EA release.) I recommend it if you're looking for a town design simulator with a few extra moving parts.I haven't seen all Hokko Life has to offer, but I plan to spend more time in it. I was really struggling to find a review post-early access with the information I wanted, so wrote this and I will add-on when I have more to say.I'd like to expand on why I think Hokko Life is a good experience, and also on what I feel is missing from this now complete game. Why I like Hokko Life:- the biggest asset the game has is the furniture customization process, so if that isn't interesting for you then the game might fall flat; being able to share these is really great- there are settings for audio, display, and controller/keybind remapping; bonus points for separating the music and sound effects (nintendo pls take notes)- inventory stacking is great! I specifically love that bugs stack which brings me to....- money is easy to get, bugs are quick to catch and easier to sell- the environment looks nice (though I still prefer to use reshade for additional fine-tuning)- the controls are easy to use, tried both, prefer controller for easier bug catching- the loading screens are fast, but there are a few of them between some important tasks (like selling or crafting at first)- the characters have a bit of personality to them, in design and dialogue (though the game maintains a quaint happy-go-lucky village vibe. pro/con)- Mayor Merits are diverse and provide very real buffs (ex. endless watering can, plants growing faster, shopping catalogs, SPRINTING)- the furniture customization is in-depth enough that it feels unique and fun (with multiplayer sharing)- NO TOOL DURABILITY, thank you.- Uses game time instead of real time, so you can progress at your own pace- the ability to freely move and edit housing & furniture (including neighbors)- so far at least one villager wants for something/has a task for me,  which i personally enjoy- biased but fishing is a plus, i love a good fish catalog - havn't used yet but multiple save slots is always a plus- ongrid and offgrid furniture placement with full rotation is lovely!What is missing:- 1440p resolution support at least, widescreen support would be a great bonus (playing on a 3440x1440 monitor)- It locks my mouse in the window and the game freezes when not in focus. (playing in windowed mode)- there are no text display/speed options- character models feel weirdly squashed flat on the sides, most notably on the pigs (Rosa & Poa), and are stylized in ways that make them love/hate; plus their outfits not editable (can't wear your designs)- being dropped into the game without direction or controls (took me a second to figure out which building to enter and how to do so, and then how and where to 'sit' for the intro.) was jarring.- Mayor Merits are too obscure. We need to see what is being unlocked, and some of it should not need to be 'unlocked' in the first place like sprinting. (also sprinting does not need stamina, this is not a survival game)- there should be a basic set of things we learn to build immediately from Sally instead of just a planter box; a storage box should be one of them (you acquire the storage box way too late)- the current player dialogue feels... meaningless. There is no personality in the options, and never an option to refuse or postpone things.- there are currently no hairstyles that I personally think look good in game, nor does the character's face look 'right' to me (I'd love the ability to choose another face type or something.)- in standard directionless fashion for these kinds of games, there is no guidance on unlocking specific tools or buildings which is only made worse by the obscure mayor merits (I don’t want a wiki to play the game please)- not having a space or anything to really show off our ‘collections’ in game feels odd. (bugs/fish)- most of the furniture has no interactions, a tv doesn't turn on a picnic table cannot be sat at. this leaves the world feeling a bit lifeless- for the mine area, a wearable lantern should be the first available option to deal with the darkness, crafting a ton of light posts seems excessive and expensiveA running list of what is NOT in the game for people coming from similar games: multiplayer of any kind, swimming/diving, cooking(?), any sort of combat or enemies, an in-depth story, friend ‘connections’/heart events or gifting, player owned businesses, a museumIn honesty: I think this game is decent. From a one person studio. I'm interested in designing a town stylistically, but returning to or staying with the game long-term is probably off the table.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give Hokko Life... a timid recommend.Don't get me wrong on the timid. It's a great game and I am going to have many more hours in it I'm sure. There are just some things about the game that keep it from being an outstanding game to me.The biggest one is the character designs. I don't know why they seemed less uncanny valley in the trailer, but they did. A lot of the characters are very very strange looking, especially the elephants (other than Paula whose design is great). You also get friendship points with NPC's but thus far I don't see a point to talking to them? Their personalities are pretty bland, a lot of repeated dialogue, and there's (thankfully) no romance option.There's also somehow, at the same time, too much to do and nothing to do. The days are super long which gives you plenty of time to do things and if you do everything you need to in a day you'll likely use up all that time. Go to the mines. Gather seashells. Pick all the flowers. Chop and replant all the trees. Check the shops. Then when you get far enough, water your crops and go to the island. The thing is that once I have done all those things... there's really only so much to DO.That brings us to the coolest part of this game. The creative designing of furniture. You get various shapes to work with that you can resize and reshape to just about anything you want and put together to make pretty much anything your brain can come up with. I built a 90s easy bake oven and a Stanley red standing tool box for storage in Sally's shop. It's honesty so much fun to sit down and build something cool. It does have it's problems though.1) There's not nearly enough prefabricated furniture. Sometimes I want to just be able to build something without having to go into the creator and make it from scratch.2) For as many shapes as there are, there just isn't enough. There's A LOT of things I wish were in the game. A big one? An equalateral triangle piece. The only triangle piece has uneven sides and it's practically impossible to make one. I made a pair of kitty ear headphones for the gaming set up I want to make my character in my game and I had to use the heart piece and flip it upside down to get something anywhere near a cat ear. Also getting a "leg" type piece that is square with round corners would be nice. I have many things that would make this review mostly suggestions for the rest of this review. More things that are fabric. Ability to add water to something. So many.3) Being able to save a design to be used on another design. Like I can save any design I make, but I can add that design to another design. Like if I take the time to make a latch. I'd like to be able to save that as something I can use in another design instead of having to remake the latch on any new design I try to make.4) There's a way to share your designs with other creators and that's so freaking cool. I love it. I just wish that I could go in and search for items by name instead of needing a creator code. Let me search "table" and then if I see a cool one go to that creator's store. Having to have creator codes makes it hard to find stuff you want that you don't want to try to create yourself. There are contests though where you can make themed items and enter them and then there is community voting which is really freaking cool (my easy bake got into the voting for the toy theme and I was stoked).5) The last thing is honestly no fault of the dev.... and that is that if you aren't into the idea of creating items to decorate your town FROM SCRATCH.... you probably won't get much out of this game and I don't recommend it. The creating of stuff is such an important part of the game. Even if you just want to decorate your areas and NPC houses. You will have to either struggle to find specific furniture you want that is community made or struggle to find the furniture you want/need from the general store. The game will be very slow with very little for you to actually do if you aren't going to design your own stuff along with doing the other stuff. So if you don't think you are creative enough to make your own items... you probably won't get much out of this game.Overall. I recommend the game to people who are creative types who enjoyed animal crossing but wished there was more furniture and that you had more creative freedom. Do keep in mind tho that this game is not Animal Crossing. If you disliked the lack of personality in the AC villagers you'll HATE it here. If you want an insane range of creative freedom though in a game that scratches a bit of that AC itch and enjoy life sim games. This is a pretty good one.Edit: I did want to edit to add one additional thought.... ♥♥♥♥... the... net.... There's a learning curve to catching bugs in this game but you will miss a bug FAR more than actually catching it. _childDocuments_.review: **NOTE:** This review is part of my steam curator review and is the extended version. Check my steam curator page at  . Follow appreciated!--- Hokko Life is a rather unique game. While adhering to a farming/sim game, it is obvious that it is somewhat influenced by Animal crossing. Some people claim it to be a full copy,  while some merely believe it got inspired by it. My knowledge on Animal Crossing is minimal, having never played it, but from what I have seen is that yes, there is some influence here and there but the game is also greatly different. It's nowhere to being a copycat. In Hokko Life you wander upon a small village after having fallen asleep on the train. And so our story begins. You slowly start integrating into the society of the village, helping others with their personal tasks and attempts at making the town a better place. Everyone, including you, wants the place to be more lively and get outsiders to come over and visit - perhaps move there too. The game follows a story which helps you get started with the basics but also introduces you to intermediate aspects. Of course you are under no obligation to follow the story - but you kind of have too. Without a story you don't unlock the new stuff and so forth. But it's all worth it, because before you realize it the town is thriving and you can build whatever you like, buy whatever you like. Have your own house designed your way. The possibilities are endless! The game runs on beautiful graphics that even a potato can run. The colouring of the game is perfect. I'm in love with the bright colors, and the characters are amazing too. Talking animals and a talking human. What a twist of events. You could compare the graphics and tone the game sets to Animal crossing. It's the same style. Hence this game is amazing for those that played Animal crossing and want the same type of experience regarding game style. The game is also amazing in not having common in games ‘invisible walls’. You know when there are multiple objects close to each other but there's a gap but you still can't walk into it because the game wont let you? This game has none of that, which impressed me the most. You can walk virtually everywhere, there are no invisible restrictions or alike. Lastly, as I'm sure some will still be hesitant over this game, I'll summarize the above one last time in asking, is it worth it? Is the game worth its price or not? Simply: Yes. It's worth it. The price might be somewhat steep for some who view this as an Animal Crossing copy, but it's not. The game comes with an amazing story, child-friendly of course, that can span on forever it feels like. Above that, the game also comes with endless possibilities for those that love designing their own objects, home or town in general. I can't stress enough on how you can virtually do what you want here. Build a fence to trap the inhabitants? You got it. Design your own house? Go for it. Steal stuff from other houses? Oh yea. However, like all games there will be a problem here or there (which won't mean the games are bad, just some people can be picky). One of them is that some non moveables aren't fully solid. They are in a sense transparent in that you can slightly walk into them or NPCs do. One of these are some chairs in the Inn (the place you start your journey!). Another is that in some areas the game wont let you place an item a certain way despite there being no obstacle. Other than that, I saw no other glitches. Also, the latter rarely happens so don't worry. All in all, having summarized the aspect and feel of the game, including potential issues, I still stand to my opinion that you should go and get the game. It's a perfect game for a calm evening and basically let your imagination do its thing.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting "chill" game that has a big influence of games like "Animal Crossing" and similar ones while adding some extra ideas and it's own touch to the formula with an interesting history that would make you meet some interesting characters.It has A LOT of room to improve as it can seem a little bit flat on the begining as a result of beign an early access that needs to polish and add details that could make the game feel more solid and emphasize it's personality, appart from this you can expect some bugs that won't end up being game breaking at all from what I've seen (but it's normal in an early access like this one, so the game will surely improve in this aspect)Basically if you are looking for a game to play in your free time while chilling and you like games like "Animal Crossing" you might find this one interesting if you can get a discount on it or wait for it to come out of early access as there are some basic things (confing saving, slowdowns when entering a room, etc.) that need  a lot of work at the moment.Here you have some footage of the game:

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little game. I played a tonne of Animal Crossing on Switch, and I've been eagerly awaiting this game for a while. Look, real talk... It's Animal Crossing - there's little that separates it from it's progenitor, even the interface bears resemblance. However, I'm judging this game on its own merits. Overall, I enjoy this game. It's calm, chilled and charming. It's exactly what I want out of an Animal Crossing game, and has some unique little tweaks to make this experience even better. Things like deep customisation on furniture, rotation of objects more than just 90 degrees, and the 'grid' of the game being altogether smaller makes this feel more of a simulation. Despite it being a clone of Animal Crossing, I'm looking forward to seeing what this game brings that's different over time. It feels as though they've built the foundation of the game on Animal Crossing's shoulders, but I hold out hope that from this foundation it'll blossom into its own beast.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to prefix my recommendation with... if you like creating items from scratch. If you like the imagination process of figuring out how to take basic shapes and making something amazing, this game is for you.If you are not into that, if you're looking for more of a life sim game, or more of a farming game, this game is not for you. The game loop is pretty much, gather materials so you can make really cool things and in the process do doing that gain achievements that help you unlock more cool things. I'm not really into creating items, I tend to want to design things as an end game thing when I play games like these. So I don't find this game very compelling, I also don't think unlocks should be hidden behind achievements as a result because like I don't want to design 25 things or 50 things or whatever. But I understand their are people out there who may want that and their wonderful community of creators is proof of that.And the game as it is functions is quite good. Any bugs that may have existed at launch I did not experience. Yes the villagers can be more life like, but frankly as far as dialogue and interaction goes they could be far worse. They were interesting character designs, some I liked more than others. The fact you can put the houses anywhere in the world is lovely. I had wanted to put a cottage in the Red Woods until I decided that I couldn't be bothered to continue the game.So just be aware of what you're asking for when you buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and fun! It has animal crossing vibes and I am all for it aha. As of right now the beginning of the game is quite slow, as in it takes a lot of time to earn money as the only way to earn it is through catching bugs, fish, and selling anything else you collect (most of which is worth between 2 and 10 coins). The fishing is a little hard to do, the mechanic when you actually catch a fish is fun, however trying to get a fish to bite can be difficult. You can cast the line right in front of the fish and it will completely ignore it aha. The building mechanic is fun and easy to navigate (although I'm not that creative and it would be nice to have some pre-built designs where you have to get the resources then you can paint it and stuff). The only issue with the building that I have encountered is that the guide for the size for the object you're building is not very accurate. For example I built a bench to the height the guide recommended and when i put it down my character was much higher above it when she sat. It doesn't matter too much I it's just for decoration though :) Overall it is very fun and I would definitely recommend to anyone whose looking for an animal crossing style game for pc, it is in early access and I can't wait to see the next update! :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's really fun but it has some Quality of Life issues I wish they would re-work.  Such as tools, you can only use one tool at a time.  You have to open your bag, pick a new item and then you can interact with it.  You have to do this with everything, if it is multiple items, such as seeds, then you have to open the bag *every single time* to pick the seeds.  This is obnoxious.  The numbers 1-0 do nothing in the game so there is no reason why you should not be able to work with an entire bar rather then one key for one item.  Once you unlock sprint, it is very fast to deplete.  It's annoying and your character doesn't get very far before you have to stop all together.The textures in the game are beautiful but the UI is horrible to look at.  The buttons look like cheap, glossy plastic.  It looks like a mobile game user interface.  It could be much, *much* more stylized to fit the game.  The logo for the game alone is a great direction to start with, if you were to consider actually designing a real UI for your game, rather then a flat, bad-looking copy & paste UI.Atmospheric sounds should be a setting all on their own.  A big point of these types of craft/farm games is the atmosphere.  Being able to silence the music and turn up the sounds of nature are almost key to any game, but especially in a game where the player is going to be spending so much time just hanging around either while fishing, catching bugs, farming, whatever.  It needs to have a beautiful, natural soundtrack.  Very slow progression for an already slow genre.  You need to wait days, sometimes even up to over a week in-game, for some things to happen such as trees growing.  IMO this is asking too much of the player.  You are already expecting to have a very casual, slower-paced session when you go to play a game like this.  But literally spreading this out over such a huge amount of time while giving the player literally nothing to do other then sleeping the days away (unless you *really* just love walking around catching bugs & fishing all day, every day, while waiting) is not how the average player is wanting to experience the game and I feel like this was somehow a huge oversight in development.  Four days for a tree, trees are finite in the game unless you catch bugs & fish constantly to pay for the seeds to grow trees to cut for logs in order to make planks for crafting.  But you are waiting SO LONG for the trees to grow while you are waiting.  It feels like you are always waiting in the game, something I particularly hate in my day to day interactions, and I despise seeing it in my games. I have a lot of negative things to say but basically, it really is a fun little game.  It doesn't break any new ground.  It isn't going to win awards for changing the genre or anything.  It's incredibly cute, the quests are easy to understand & carry out.  The UI shows everything without being too intrusive.  There are many little interactive piece of furniture you can craft and/or buy.  There's real customization in the game, which is very rare to see still even after all the fuss everyone made when Sims 3 came out.  The animals are charming and easily discernible from one another making them easier to remember.  When you need to talk to a villager you will see a visual effect around that NPC.  This is a super kid friendly game as well as a great way to just have a calm night in with a cup of coffee.  You can even move many of the items in the town as well as picking out exactly where your next villager will build their house & what kind of house they will have.  Later on in the game you can further customize all of the houses.  Merits are things you can earn by completing tasks in your journal such as cutting down a certain number of trees, catching # of bugs/fish, etc. The Golden merits will give you buffs or you will get 100g in the mail for helping finish requests.  Tons of great things about the game.  Nothing game breaking or so annoying that it stops you from wanting to progress.  But things that could definitely be worked on or looked at.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute game. As many others have said, I am also a long-time player of animal crossing. I think there is only one dude working on this game, and it is going to take a little more time than a huge dev. SDV was also clunky in places when it first released, and look where it is now. It is important not to review bomb early access games just because they did not meet your extremely high expectations of the genre.. this is how you stop sales, stop the dev's income and then subsequent good updates and content do not get done. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.The grapics are cute, the music is ambient. The artstyle used on various decor, nature, animals etc etc. are very nice with a ton of details.Character customization is charming, and there are a ton of outfits to collect.But I still find it lacking. The tutorials are either too short or simply not there.The grind to unlock features is massive. I would not mind that so much, if I actually know where I'm going, but I do not.Yes there is a tech tree, that lists things you have to do to get a bigger backpack etc.One achievement says "visited the small wood" - yes sure but where is that forest?I have unlocked the map, and level 2 in the mine, the bronze pickaxe, leveled up fishing, an  island etc etc, have even started farming. But I have still to see that forest, unless I'm looking for a tree or something?...edit... to the above: I have now unlocked that "visit the small wood" - but only because I'm  extremely stubborn AND was willing to again grind massively.I'd love a bigger house for my character. I can build it, but what about customization, other colors etc etc. That I cannot do... yet. I suppose I need more unlocking of features. So ok - what if I build a bigger house with the default settings. How do I move my character to the new house? There is no move house feature. Yes there is an evict button on all houses including my own. So what happens if I click that button? Am I kicked out of the town, or will I be able to grab the new house?On several occations I found, I had once again sold items I need to either complete a quest, or needed to craft X item. Once unable to find X items again, so I deleted the save game and started over.The lack of storage is a massive issue, that quickly becomes an annoyance, until you figure out how to get around it.The character interaction feels hollow.I'm puzzled as to why you cannot interact with the other NPC's if you hold something in you hand.I am normally fairly creative, but the design tool drives me up walls. How some players can create the wonderful art they do, simply evades me. What can I say besides I'm in awe.I have created various items. But once I have used those items, where do I find them again, if I want to create more of X item?If I have to take the train and then go "to my store"... then just NO that needs to be changed.Another example, I had unlocked how to craft a bulb, but no matter what I did I could not figure out how to use said bulb to create an actual lamp.After wasting a ton of raw materials and like close to an hour getting nowhere, I decided it was enough...... edit to the light bulb issue - again after grinding some more, I can now use the bulbs when crafting something.I'm all for heureka moments and like playing games where I have to figure out how everything works. But constantly going blindfolded is not my idea of fun.The game has massive potential, but needs a lot more development before it's something I'll really enjoy to play. As it it now it holds too many frustrating moments.I will continue to spend more hours playing, hoping for more updates. If/when they do I hope I'll be able to change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, but as it is now, it's still lacking in a lot of areas. After a certain amount of progression in the game, you'll find yourself just repeating the same thing again and again until the next thing is unlocked, which was supposed to make your previous chores easier, but at that point it'll be too late for it since you've already finished grinding up the things you desperately needed a while ago. Things that I think could be improved on: - Make requirements for important game mechanics to be unlocked more obvious to the player, mechanics like farming, fishing, cooking, should be unlocked relatively early in the beginning for the game to feel busy, as of now everything is unlocking too slow, which leaves the players feeling bored easily. - Either balance out the rewards for villagers requests, or give a long term goal for actually completing villager's requests. There are crafting, produce or food requests that actually makes the player lose profit if they were to complete them. In fact, there's actually not much reason to complete them besides completing the mayor's merits. - If the main goal is to complete mayor's merits, look, I love to grind in games, but some of the requirements are too ridiculous and slow. Food requests only spawns once per season for me, and you need to complete 20 food requests to unlock all the mayor's merit. Fishing tournaments are super rigged since the fish that are required to be caught either only starts spawning around 5pm, or you'll need fish gut bait to catch them (which in itself is quite troublesome to grind). - The villagers houses are so empty, and it's not worth decorating their interiors with my ugly builds since in the end of the day, the villagers don't care what's being placed in their house.  The first two villager's house was so full of personalities, it would be great if the other villagers get to have requests that asks the players to help decorate their houses based on their own unique personalities. - When a mechanic is designed, usually players would like to do it for a purpose, to unlock better upgrades, to increase skills or relationships. So far a lot of things in this game are just placed there so you could just do it, for funsies : / Maybe it's fun for some folks and I'm not the targeted audience for it, but that's just my own two cents.- Maybe have a different music theme for different seasons? As of now the music is kind of limited, but fixing the pacing of the game should always be prioritized.I can see a lot of potential for this game to be a great cozy game, and I hope to see more from this developer improving in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game like Animal Crossing that isn't Animal Crossing, this is a pretty good pick, but with a few caveats.Hokko Life captures the concept pretty well with cute characters, slow pacing, and low-pressure, repetitive gameplay.  It's the kind of thing you play when you're trying to calm yourself down and lull yourself to sleep.  You're never in a hurry to get anywhere.The unique gimmick here is that instead of the large assortment of collectible furniture in the series it's emulating, Hokko Life offers an object editor that lets you build your very own furniture.  The editor is kind of clunky, but it's flexible.  I'm no artist, but I'm sure someone who is could make something really impressive out of it.  Perhaps the biggest flaw in the editor is that materials are required for each part added and you can't JUST design an object, so I keep getting stuck one piece shy of my artistic vision and having to save, gather 1 piece, then come back to edit.  Weird design decision.On the flip side, the drawback to having a game rely on community content is that if there's no community, there's no content.  In-game discoverability is low and I assume that I'm expected to go dabble in some online forums or discords to find friend codes, but I can't be arsed.  I just want to chill and play home decorator.  Without furniture to browse, I can't do that.It's also worth noting that with the flexibility of user content creation, you give up the interaction that would make furniture really interesting.  I can't put tapes in my tape deck.  I can't pretend to play my SNES knockoff.  I can't play my instruments.If you're looking for an escape from your endless debt to Nook, this might be a good place to find it.  Ultimately though, this just makes me want to dust off my Switch.

You have to be 4 or 5 days into the game before you can really do anything and then when you can you have to use a horrible design interface to make things like bridges, furniture, etc. You need a blueprint to make an item but the blueprint doesn't tell you what pieces you need, where they go, what size they have to be- nothing. It is the least intuitive I've ever seen a design interface within a game and I'm majorly disappointed. I understand it's early access, but can't find any plans for that design interface to change in anything from the creator. It also doesn't have great controller mapping at startup- but it does make it fairly easy to change the controller setup mid game with no lag so that's a positive.

_childDocuments_.review: I never leave reviews but I feel the mixed rating on this game is a shame so Im tossing this out there. Lots of content if youre willing to actually play for a while or if you need to give it another try post-early access to see it more polished (the route I went).Its a gradual upgrade/unlock of features as you play to get to everything, similar to AC as people have mentioned, but it has its own unique elements that make it a standout imo. Freeform item creation is huge (I havent seen such a funky open-ended design element in a game since Amazing Island on the gamecube). As for general gameplay, if youre wondering why you cant do a certain thing....just keep playing (work toward the merit rewards).It has some qol features that not every game in the cozy life/farming/crafting genre has or does well: unlockable fast travel spots, free movement of storage items without having to take everything out, free movement/re-placing of houses once the ability is unlocked, optional snap to grid when placing things (opens up so many creative decorating options when off!), easy tool switching, apparently unlimited item stacking (even the critters. ♥♥♥♥ your non-stackable wildlife AC), plenty of time in the day, etc. Lots of things I have suffered through in other games, this game does really well to get you to the fun part of designing, crafting, and decorating. That said, there are some things that could be tweaked or polished for better user experience (like the sorting of some purchase menus, let me sort the catalog by item type pls), but for me the minor inconveniences are far outweighed by the positives. Again, the ultimate freedom with item creation and then placement without a grid is is the showstopper (and really fun if you're like me and played more sims build mode than the actual game growing up). 4 bucks on sale? 20 bucks full price? Either way I'd say go for it.Fun game, good job to the team that made it!

Either you choose full force cuteness, or you make the contrast over the top and humouristic. Here it's just uncanny. All those cute animals talking to you like your senior neighbours... _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game and am optimistic that the developers will continue to flesh it out into something worthy of your time, but at this time I simply can't.Pros: - the art style. This is of paramount importance for these types of games, and thankfully it's pretty good, but the player character needs more customization options beyond just the hair. The art style makes for very pleasing graphics overall.- the music. It's great. Simple, but relaxing.- the creative freedom. There's a good amount of freedom in customizing things, both in where to place furniture and how to customize the furniture itself.Cons:- the writing. It's bad enough to ruin the entire game for me, but this is something that sticks out more to me than perhaps it will to others so take it with a grain of salt. The characters are very bland and lifeless, and get used to reading "Haha" as its own chat bubble after each sentence every single time you speak with the town NPC's. Every character uses a "they" pronoun as well, which while that may seem heroically inclusive, it paints every interaction in the same shade of gray. It's pedantic and tiring.- the content. This is in Early Access as of this review, so I don't want to harp on this too much as I'm sure that much more is coming. That being said, the gameplay loop is just too flat. The days are very long, which may seem nice at first, but then you realize that the relief that comes when you manage to get that last chore done before the sun goes down is very much a rewarding part of games like this. There is of course a balance, but this game does not even try to find it. Much of the time you've done everything you care to do that day and it's only noon. It makes the experience feel more empty than perhaps it deserves.Overall, for me the initial charm has worn off after 6 hours, and once that's gone you're really not left with much. I believe that, eventually, this will be a game worth your time, but in its current state that is not the case. I wish the developers the best and encourage them to keep at it as it certainly has potential, and I will be looking forward to seeing how far the game comes as it progresses towards full release.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting nearly 14 hours into this game, I can honestly say that it's a drag to play. There's very little to do besides grind away collecting and harvesting resources which isnt much fun, or customizing. At least everything is a single click. Your other option is to spend time designing furniture which is fiddly and extremely frustrating. Which is fine if it's optional, but to advance in the game, you HAVE to do it. I opened up My Time at Sandrock recently and had so much more fun, even the crafting and mining components. Hokko Life is much less fun.However, there are some pros to the game. The fishing mechanic is quite fun, as long as you can cast the rod in the right direction. I appreciate that mining and harvesting is always a single click, and there's no stamina to worry about (besides sprinting). The artwork is very cute and clean and storage is available very early (you can also nest and carry storage units, which is an amusing quirk/bug - infinite storage!)I hate to give it a thumbs down because it was actually fun for a while. It just overstays its welcome and frustrates the player in the requisite design mode.

CAPITALISM.Where in AC I personally focused on getting as much money as possible, this game just isn't focused on that.
