_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I was hoping to get a better feel of this game before writing a review but due to the Steam Community's uncanny ability to burn bridges with game developers working on the Mobile Suit Gundam IP, I guess I oughta give my early impressions on the game, because from what I've played so far, it is  bad enough to warrant telling Artdink to go ♥♥♥♥ themselves. Yes, it's pretty rough on the edges, but I found the game to have some pretty solid foundations.Let's get this out of the way first and foremost: consoles will always have better options for Gundam games, but if your only gaming platform is the home computer, it's probably pointless to compare SD Gundam Battle Alliance against games that will never see the light of day on PC. On another note, it's apparent to me that the more recent efforts with the Gundam brandname seems more focused on PVP titles even on consoles thanks to Gundam Evolution, the Extreme VS series, and Gundam Battle Operation 2 (Gundam Breaker 3 is six years old now, just an FYI). Anyways, my thoughts on the game.Probably the two biggest issues I have with the game right now are the story, and the camera. Story because it's utterly forgettable, though I think the concept of having breaks in history is a good way to justify having mobile suits appearing in timelines where they don't belong is a neat concept, though I feel like the execution could've been a lot better. Camera is workable in most cases, though I kinda feel that certain areas in the game can make the camera controls detrimental for you (biggest example i've seen so far involve narrow canyons)What I DO like about the game is that the basic core mechanics are understandable enough that you can get a decent feel of how most things work, the only time where I felt confused with how things work is the GR symbol on your HUD which never seems to be explained in-game. The game does feel like it takes a while to acquire mobile suits that are more fun to play with and I think the game becomes more a lot more enjoyable once you figure out how to pace yourself. Okay, I've also been half playing this game half writing this review and one gripe I have above the previous "two biggest gripes I have" is that acquiring the Gouf takes a lot more time than I was hoping it'd take, especially considering the technological leap from the Zaku to Gouf. Another minor annoyance I have is that there isn't much point in picking companions other than Gundam pilots, since the non-Gundam mobile suits feel a bit ineffectual unless player-controlledRegarding the game's graphical options, I don't think i'm the most qualified person to talk about this considering that this is a cross-gen/Switch release on consoles, considering my "bragging rights" build . That said, I think more advanced graphical options would be welcome for higher-end users, along with people wanting to squeeze out every bit of performance out of a low-end system. Namely, I think this game would benefit from having a resolution scaling option to help satisfy people on both ends of the PC hardware spectrum, though also being able to choose your resolution would be nice too.So yeah, I think this game is above serviceable for people who only have a PC as their main gaming platform, especially when you consider that we're basically hemorrhaging developers working on the Mobile Suit Gundam brandname.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know about you, but seeing that Artdink was making a new Gundam game amped me up. But this isn't anything like Gundam Battle Universe or anything. This is a repetitive, questionably designed beat 'em up with SD Gundams. You get new mobile suits by collecting blueprints that are dropped by completing certain levels. Sometimes you have to replay a level a few times to get them. As the game goes on, the enemies get stronger and you're expected to level up your mobile suits. But every time you get a new mobile suit, it starts at level one. That means you can't use it in the levels you haven't played yet, as it will absolutely get destroyed or take forever to kill anything. Instead, you have to replay levels to grind for money until you can afford to level them up enough to use them. But it takes a while to do this, which means that a lot of players will just stick to mobile suits they got early on instead of bothering with it. There are three types of mobile suit: melee fighters, ranged fighters, and balanced fighters. Unfortunately, the ranged attacks mostly suck. For your main ranged attack, you get five or six shots before you run out and have to wait for a lengthy reload. There are also skills that operate on another cooldown, but they take so long that you'll predominately be doing damage with your melee attacks, which makes the ranged and all-rounder mobile suits practically worthless next to the melee ones. As for melee, attacks use up your boost gauge, which interrupts the flow of your combos. The combat is okay, but there's a delay on everything that makes it feel like you're queuing up attacks instead of having precise control. The levels are mostly short and boring. You go in, kill some fodder that mostly stands around, and then a boss enemy drops down. The bosses are mostly unflinchable unless you put them in a break state, which means you have to walk up and mash buttons to hurt them. But they have a massive amount of health and, even if your mobile suits are leveled up, they can kill you in a couple of hits. Since your attacks don't flinch them, they can attack you at any time during your combos. You can dodge or guard to mitigate this, but your partners will be hitting them, which creates visual effects that obscure their character models, which makes it borderline impossible to watch what they're doing, so you can mostly forget about using your guard and dodges to get out of the way, as you simply won't usually be able to see through the explosions and beam shots. This game is a massive disappointment. Gundam Battle Universe came out in 2009 and is still notably better. At least the game looks nice, I guess.Update: After getting to Directory 5, things get even more tedious. Some missions have you fight three bosses in one go. If you play this, I really hope you're playing with friends. You have to uncap your suits using materials. After your second uncap, a single stat boost costs 13,000 of your currency. I've been playing with one suit almost exclusively, pumping all of my money into it. I meet the level requirement, but the bosses are tearing me apart on normal. You get pilot skills every couple of levels. I'm level 28 and, every time I get a new skill, my response is, "who the f*ck cares?!" Because they're almost all completely useless. I'd like to try out some new suits, but I've invested over 100,000 of my currency into the Exia and it's still not enough, so that's a pipe dream. I'd also like to change my two assist pilots, but they're also level 28 but still getting routinely wrecked by the bosses. Grinding up new ones would take hours. And y'know what? I probably wouldn't be this hard on the game if all of the above was true but it was fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 30 hours solo and beated the game, not tried the multi-player content yet.In short: Game does not deserve to be mixed.As an Asian kid growing up playing a ton of Gundam games, this game is a true love letter to the fans.The amount of classic lines, the classic BGM, the amount of Gundam scenes, still got me hyped every time even I saw those 100 times in other games.Needless to say, the graphic is rather smooth and beautiful for a Gundam game.If you played Gundam RPG game before, it is likely you have seen a couple of story and know exactly how those true mission gonna go. (Some still got me hyped tho, with the right BGM and everything)Love the break mission on my first play, not knowing which random MS will appear next, and I literally went shouting if I see some of my fav character appears randomly.And the details, oh man, just look at the enemy type, with zaku alone you see a TON of different versions based on generations, not just some lazy Zaku II re-use. Some Gundam not even playable, but they make it anyway just for that one battle scene, like the Impulse Gundam, that was the unit Shinn was on when he fights Destroy Gundam, they didn't just put a lazy Destiny Gundam because it was easy. You can see how much love the dev put on this game.I mean, it is everything you ask for in a Gundam action game. Some solid melee combo, some great gun fight, the melee combo is rather repetitive in some units but that's expected. Blocking could get tricky in time as you have to land a perfect guard to avoid damage, don't like the perfect dodge as I see no purpose of it (e.g. if I failed this I take full damage, why shouldn't I just dodge early or try a perfect guard when I feel risky?)Now comes to the cons list.Capital is rather tight in this game, you have to really focus on leveling one unit instead of trying out all of them.Boss fight can sometimes be very unbalanced (MA, cough cough). There is a particular fight which you have to spend 15 mins fighting mobs until you can get to that boss fight, and lost immediately because how unbalanced that thing was. I attempted that stage like 5 times while I first-time cleared all other stages on the same page. They should really review some of these boss movement, it is just BS to miss a shot on that big thing because it keeps wiggling, then 1 spin to wipe out my whole squad.Don't know if I should put it in the cons list, but I discover the partner level starts with your current pilot level when you obtain the unit, which means if you not play with the partner constantly they will likely be no use later on. My boy Kira and Setsuna sadly still sitting at the dumpster and likely will never be used again. It also stops me from farming some new unit until I reach max level, pretty bad design imo.This is a solid game, just need a bit of polishing.Really sad to see Gundam ain't known to the western or to the new generations, very hard to explain what a masterpiece that was.A majority of people who rate this game bad just simply play the game without knowing some Gundam Lore, which this game is very much based on.

_childDocuments_.review: Been a Gundam fan for a long time, have all the series on Blu Ray (UC timeline, that is) and build a ton of Gunpla. I've been waiting for a Gundam game like this for a long while, and even though I have played roughly an hour it has already exceeded my expectations. Plot is serviceable, and pretty interesting. You're basically Timecop, going back through all of the Gundam universes to fix them and make them historically accurate. However, where the game really shines is it's attention to detail both in the environments and the Mobile Suits themselves. Every suit has unique abilities, and are split up into three types (ranged, melee, balanced) that all feel different and fun to play. The most important aspect however, is that all the Mobile Suits are authentic albeit in SD fashion. GMs utilize ball cannons, Zaku's can whip out their Heat Hawk, ETC. The animation is also true to the series, it will never get old watching the GM and RX78 use their guard mode as the animation looks straight out of the OG 1970's series. Environments are incredibly detailed. You can see sand rise up when your suit stomps down when doing the introductory mission of Operation Odessa. Even the original OG series' soundtrack plays! It's a small thing to praise, but it makes the entire game feel genuine and like the devs really cared about the franchise and what they were making. Combat is pretty straightforward, combos, ranged weaponry, and neat specials that are unique to each Mobile Suit. Think a less complex version of Devil May Cry's combat system. Upgrade system is basic, but forces you to be thoughtful of what you upgrade and how. Upgrading a Mobile Suit you love and ignoring others may be detrimental later on, and trying to spend Capital (the games upgrade points) on too many suits at once limits your ability to develop powerful Suits for difficult missions. While basic in principle, you can't treat this like a brainless upgrade tree. You have to be strategic. I honestly don't get why this is "mixed" on Steam. If you're not a Gundam fan than yes, I can see why this would not necessarily appeal to you. But then I must ask, why purchase this in the first place? However, if you are a fan like myself, this is the RPG Gundam game I think a lot of us have been waiting for.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a neutral rating, rather than Yes/No.Battle Alliance starts off pretty solid for the first several hours! You're unlocking new suits, familiar faces, and reliving major parts of Gundam canon, from OG Mobile Suit Gundam to Iron Blooded Orphans. The tutorials do a reasonable job of teaching you the basics, give you small capital rewards since you don't have a cash grinding setup yet, and things go pretty well!As time goes on, little things start seeping in. The controls are a little wonky and keep you locked on dead enemies, (This is so you can continue attacking them to generate SPA, though I don't know if that's working properly right now, as I've ran into pilot skills that just don't work) or that the fight keeps going while you're using your SPecial Attack and you wind up whiffing, (Looking at YOU Gouf Custom) or losing your target in a giant explosion/beam since they have no outline in combat, you cannot rebind multiple button actions like the Role Action or Chain Break! (This functions like a Burst in Guilty Gear, a crucial "Get off me!" effect)Again, little things that don't really mar the experience too much. Then Directory 4 rears it's ugly head. Mobile Armors are HORRENDOUSLY overtuned, being faster than mobile suits, able to turn on a dime, and having very little attack wind up for some VERY hard hitting attacks (200+ damage if you fail to guard at all, ~60-100 on a standard guard) . At first I figured I just needed to learn the patterns better, improve my suits some more and come back. So I did! (Alex Gundam is a beautiful cash printing machine by the way, clearly Zeon was stealing it to finance the war)I even went back with a friend, and we routinely had our ♥♥♥♥ wrecked on the MAs in Directory 4, overleveled as hell to boot. After about six attempts we cleared a particularly painful Mobile Armor. Then it was on to another Mobile Armor fight which was less hellish, and then onto a more hellish Mobile Armor fight. A pattern emerges here. This is a fun game at it's core, but there are *several* questionable design choices present that make me regret paying full price for it. Get this on sale, as there's probably a thirty or forty dollar game here. Modders will probably be the ones to save this game on it's flaws if the devs don't. Bottom line, If you can overlook some questionable design choices there's a LOT to love here. But god help you if can't. Edit: turning on a time, while a humorous screw-up, doesn't make much sense.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent IBO grunt suit game, trying to be GBU, disguised as a spin-off of SDGO.During the first few days of playing this, I was not really enjoying myself all that much but I figured I should at least finish the story. Towards clearing up all the story missions on Normal, I've come to appreciate the game for what it tried to do, even if it didn't manage to make the game feel especially enjoyable. By the point I've gone through half of Hard, I've come to understand the game and why it is made this way.Combat is less mashy compared to GBU. My highlights of my time playing GBU was missile spamming while running circles on the Ga-zowmn and switching on MEPE on the F91 and being unable to see what's going on. My highlights on playing SDGBA is well timed blocks into a follow up counter on various MS and MA. It's a very big change of pace and it's not one that everyone can make the jump. I went in hoping it would be GBU but by now, I sort of appreciate that it didn't try to be exactly like all the previous games.Attacks felt a little underwhelming early on, with melee being just a small combo string and 3 special melees, all of which is limited by a boost meter. This made melee feel a bit lacking compared to GVG where you had various melee strings based on the direction but it opened up melee to being more than just a one-way direction where you get 3 hits and the enemy falls over. Ranged weapons felt like they took too long to reload and you often end up getting stuck having to use a really awkward 2 combo melee.This 2 issues eventually tie into 2 things, co-op and balance. Unfortunately, it's only something you will reach after at least 20 hours into the game when you finally reach Hard mode. If the game were to be as fast-paced and allowed you to play really aggressively, it could have fallen apart really badly with 3 people just flying around launching missiles all over the place. If you started out really strong, the higher rarity parts would have been really disappointing with small increasing numbers or players would have just gotten so ridiculously out of scale. Both could eventually end in disaster as co-op could eventually be reduced to 1 guy with good parts just nuking bosses to oblivion with rapid reloading missiles, or boss fights just becoming a huge slog to try to match against 3 players.While it's not the the most enjoyable game from the get-go, it eventually get somewhere as a co-op game. No one player is strong enough to rush the rest of the team unless you're significantly past the recommended level. A good melee player would need a lot of practice and effort to block everything perfectly. A good range player can eventually have an unlimited ammo loop but you can't burst down a boss without having to worry about what you're going to do once you have aggro. That's what you eventually get as your final product, not the Gundam game that you wanted, but a Gundam game where it can feel like you're a squad of 3 grunts fighting something a lot stronger.As a Gundam game, I can and can't recommend it. Your mileage on this really relies on what you want from a Gundam game.As a more methodical co-op APRG, I can decently recommend it. It's a slower paced APRG that focuses on a more measured approach on tougher enemies to bring value to co-op.For it's price point, I can't really recommend it. While there is a decent polish and the content time is fairly decent (30 hours currently, I expecting to hit close to 50 before I start running on fumes on what to do), it's hard for me to tell people to spend a good chunk of money to get this, there's just too many things that people will not like and if you can't stomach it till Hard mode, the price value falls apart.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; A lot of good idea executed rather poorly; a very rough first draft that might do better in a sequel if its many shortcomings are addressed.This will not fill the Hole Dynasty Warriors Gundam has left, so go get an Emulator and your 100%.tm Legal copy of DW:Gundam & play that. I'd recommend DW:G Reborn, as it would seem many never got to play the final entry as a result of its unfortunate PS3 exclusivity.So. Where do I begin with SD Gundam: Battle Alliance?The Positive.- A good number of Series are represented with a decent number of suits from each series present.- The Premise. As this turns up in the first 10-30mins of playtime - SDG:BA takes place in a simulated video game like world & while it does not always stick the landing, it uses this premise pretty well throughout.- Haro! It's always fun when Haro gets top billing in the cast & SDG:BA has a Haro Front & Centre & for the most part is a fun addition to the protagonists.The Negative.- No Grunt Suits.Despite including a good number of Series, there are some notable exceptions & poor highlight choices - Esp as a number of "Grunt" suits show up, like the G:Wing Leo, Taurus, that aren't playable despite also turning up in the hands of Ace characters during missions & seemingly having complete animations/move-sets. A real missed opportunity.- Text walls.While the basic premise is a fun romp thru Gundam history, it parses that information VERY poorly. "Exposition Dump" might as well be this games subtitle, not "Battle Alliance".- Level Design.Forgetting the blatant re-use of levels to pad out game time, most level design is just a series of boxes connected by corridors. The set dressing might be interesting in places, but b/c of this basic approach, some levels are just downright annoying. Not helped by the poor base movement & dash speeds of your MS. Also not helped by the often spawn in of enemies up high on ledges you don't have access to & can't get at or worse, the camera freaks out about when you try to lock onto them.- Inch deep Mechanics & moment to moment Gameplay.SDG:BA is a beat'em-up. Call it whatever else you want, but it boils down to that & in that, its not horrible but it is rough. One basic attack button, one Heavy/Launch button, a Jump, a Dash/dodge & two special attacks on bumpers & a ranged attack on your R-trigger. That's the full move set. Now there are Combos & parries and other mechanics, but they're poorly implement & with the visual noise on screen in Ace fights I regularly had problems executing these - Not helped by the fact the Parry is mapped to Jump+Light attack, which often meant then opening myself up to an immediate reprisal when things went wrong.- Finally got to play an MS you just spent an hour+ (as some are gated behind story progression) trying to unlock for 5 Minutes? Great! You've just experienced all the suit has to offer, because there's no mechanical progression!This might not have been as bad as it is, but progression for your individual ms = "Number Go Up", rather than unlocking number abilities as a reward for playing with the same MS. Once you've pressed every move-set button at the start of a mission, just to see what each atack does & how it handles, you've seen 100% of what your MS can do. That's it.- The Upgrade system.SDG:BA in its marketing says its an "Action Adventure RPG". In some ways, that not a lie. If you think "Number go up" is an RPG mechanic. Which unfortunately, is the most your going to get out of the Upgrade systems for your Mobile suits. Bar a few tweaks with "parts" that can alter the base stats of a suit, somewhat.- No English Dub.This is likely not a deal breaker for many & is not for myself, but its a growing trend w/Gundam releases (what few there have been of late). I feel that not having an English dub makes sense, as localising all of SDG:BA + its DLC would have added to Dev costs in a way this arguably Budget title couldn't afford. But is notable by its absence, esp as during missions i'm often too busy fighting to give a damn about whatever the Operators or other characters are jabbering on about.The Truly Bad.- The Controller Layout.I want to find whoever decided the basic controller layout was going to be THIS, and then beat them with a 2x4 for 20+ hrs & see how they like that. The button mapping is so right side heavy I often had to claw my hand over my controller, working the bumper/trigger with my middle finger, so my index could button press while my thumb handled the game obnoxious lock on. All of which could have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FIXED if they'd just added a Camera Centre to the Guard trigger! I just want to see what i'm blindingly flailing at SDG:BA! Same for the Minimap. You have to open the start menu to get a wider view of the ballefield - Just map that to the L3, let me toggle the mini-map in & out!- Ya like boxed in canyons or bunkers? Because your gonna be seeing variations of those two themes in pretty much every level.- The Bully pit.Mobile Armour fights have a little more room to them & seemingly dedicated map spaces in their design, likely a concession to their size, but most Ace (MS or MA) fights take place in a VERY restricted box - even if your in the middle of the damn wide open with all the room in the world to move. Enjoy those invisible walls & the fact the Ace can move in ways & at a speed you can only ever hope for.- Grind.Playing a level a few times to unlock a particular MS is ONE thing. But upgrading it to its fullest potential to use in later missions? Good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck. 1st Batch of upgrades to level up a suit costs 20k in game currency or there about. 2nd batch, more like 200k, 3rd batch, more like just south of 1 Million & w/my current playtime yet to unlock the 4th batch! It wouldn't be so bad, but b/c of the way progression works, this is MANDATORY. Optional grind, esp to play on hard mode or go for late/end game content is not a bad addition to a games design, but this? this is just padding for the sake of it & considering it would seem like Bandai wanted to monetise this feature (this is inferred based on observation & discussion, check out the games DLC that isn't actually DLC!) this just feels Greasy as all hell.- DLC Pricing.While the DLC adds in some Great suits, Moon Gundam & "Graham Gundam"/Exia R4 being personal Favourites & something I loved to see [Seriously, these were a big part of the reason I ended up picking up SDG:BA! I really wanted to play as these suits, see them in motion & hear the voice cast! I was hype for these.], the price of those 2 Mission + 2 or so MS DLC, is just egregious. Which is all the more galling when you consider these DLC often introduce new enemy ACE MS, which have voiced lines & a full animation/move-set that aren't then unlock-able/playable! [To be clear, I get that adding these in as player character MS would be more Dev time, but still!].There's more than all this, like how poor melee feedback is or worse lost in all the visual noise, or how the hitboxes on MA vary wildly. SDG:BA is just a deeply flawed game in my opinion. Great ideas, but poor execution & it is a REAL shame. Because I really WANTED to like SDG:BA. The west has been starved of quality Gundam video games or ANY games until the last 3-5 years & this seemed like it might scratch a very old itch; but it wasn't to be.If you saw the marketing leading up to release & though maybe Bandai were taking a stab a doing a "legally Distinct" Dynasty Warriors beat-em-up, go play DW:G Reborn on your "100% legally acquired" emulator, You'll have a MUCH better time.To conclude:Buy it on Sale or not at all & even then, be aware that much of the criticism found in Steam reviews & elsewhere surrounding SDG:BA is pretty valid, so don't pay more than £10-15 for the base game, as if you want the "100% complete" experience the DLC is EGREGIOUSLY priced for what it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why some people aren't too keen on this game, but I rather enjoy it despite its flaws. It's good chaotic explosive and visual fun imo. My only big gripes are the lack of an ability to turn anything volume related down all the way, no actual pause button, the ungodly grind that I'll be in for, and how units look when all standing still. You could take a screen shot and minus the hud and map it looks the exact same as when you're looking at them in the actual game. It looks a little silly with some stances on units like the phoenix who is just floating there and there's nothing animated showing how they're floating, like their jet pack shooting fire out or something at the least. Other than that, I do think it's a pretty fun time and I would recommend it. I'd say wait for a price drop though. Not a bad game, I enjoy it, but I agree with everyone else. It's not worth full price.P.S. I got the deluxe edition and ALL of the dlc. FML. xD

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the game had some issues on launch, the developers are fixing them one by one delicately based on the feedback players have been providing. Something I cared about most has already been added like 4K support for example. Honestly, this is pretty rare nowadays, I have seen enough arrogant devs who do nothing after the game’s release, leaving so many bugs and issues behind, pretending to be blind and deaf to users’ desperate requests. Recent’s LEGO Star Wars Skywalker Sega is a prime bad example for this. Though I didn’t leave a negative review for it, I swear never buy another LEGO game from TT ever, since they treated PC gamers like none-existence. Back to this game, the developers are doing hot fix for the game means they care about both their game and customers, showing respect to the community and love for their own creation.Now, about the game itself. If you’ve watched any anime of gundam, you will enjoy Battle Alliance I assure you. This game is a celebration show of Gundams. Devs put almost all most recognized Gundams from all Gundam anime in the history into the game, with the campaigns telling you how they’ve appeared. The selection is across all Gundam universe. The story of the game is a twist of all these important events with its own original ideas. If you’re not familiar with the Gundam universe, don’t worry. Each mission also has a separate session with VNs to tell you the background story of each campaign you are in and what are you suppose to do. Everything in such detail, I can’t help to see lots of love and passion from the team of the maker whom delicate their lives to the game. I honestly think they need my support, not the blame for some small flaws which will be fixed anyways.The game’s follows some mechanics that a mobile game usually do which means it is also good for players who is always on the move. The reason I said so because, apart from the story, it basically is a ‘Gundamon’ without hateful Gotta cha system which you frequently see in a mobile game. By completing levels, the enemy Mobile Suits(MS) you’ve defeated will drop some pieces of blueprint of plural of gundams(currently level specific, not random, don’t worry). Once you collected all blueprint of a gundam, you can develop it and add to your base. Then rise it up and go for a fight. There are so many Gundams in the game waiting for you to develop. Each one will need quite some funds to grow while you fighting campaigns to earn. Each level takes from 5-15 minutes to finish. So even if you are out, with a steam deck or switch, you can play a round or two when you have even a little time. Or enjoying it with a 4K screen at home, of course. The game’s more fun with up to 2 friends to play together on CO-OP mode, which I had lots of fun with my friend.The replay value is also high, after beating the whole story once, the game unlocks Hard Mode which is basically a post game that new levels can be earned, new Gundams can be collected, new challenge levels with powerful foes. I’d say the price is worth because developers really want you to stay and spend lots of time on this game if you’re interested in doing so. And they’re making new DLCs on extras for extremely delicate players who have beaten everything and don’t know what else to do.If you like anime, interesting in Gundam, like hack& slash games, this is a good entry for you to Gundam’s universe. 9/10 A must play for Gundam!P.S Hello is the best Gundamon

_childDocuments_.review: It's not everyone's cup of tea for sure.  It's a very very nice game for Gundam fans as it exposes you to the main plot lines of the Gundam series you may not have watched.  Think of it like a director's cut but for all the series combined.  As for gameplay?  It's pretty standard but there's just a part of you if you own or build any Gunpla that feels giddy piloting your favorite one.I think it's a pretty mediocre game, but if you're a fan of Gundam in general, it's a treat.  No revolutionary game play here otherwise.  Pass on it if you're not a Gundam fan.  If you are a fan, it's fun because somehow they got 90% of the Voice Actors (JP) to voice their roles, Stella (Seed Destiny) isn't Stella's OG VA... but then again all she does is scream.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is just a normal, enjoyable action game, with no more or less jank or grind than you'd expect out of bandai. So if you know what that entails, go ahead and ignore the mixed reviews and pick it up. Frankly I'd view it as more of a "Mostly Positive" if it got fair reviews. It does have the usual bandai flaws, like basically still being a console game just thrown on PC, but nothing crazy.EDIT: Just figured out, if you go into Library, you can set the game to check a custom folder, for any MP3 files, and use that as custom music in game, to either replace any of the tracks in the game or play when you use your Super (SPA). This is amazing to mess around with, Rules of Nature now blares whenever I use mine. And this is official too, no modding required, just make a folder and get the MP3sSo first things first: Most negative reviews you'll see on here are people expecting things no one who usually buys bandai games expects. A dub? When's the last time a gundam game had a dub? Would it be nice? Yes. Does it ruin the game to not have one? No, the same way it doesn't ruin half the other bandai anime games that don't have dubs. PvP? Read the description, do you see any in there? Bad Lock-on? A) I haven't had any issues with it, and B) that's nothing new for a bandai third person action game. So if you know the usual jank a bandai game brings, you'll have no issues, just enjoy the game.Pros:Graphics: Game looks great, runs great. Some people say it's unoptimized, I'm running a laptop 3060 and a ryzen 5 5600h (3.3 ghz and 6 cores 12 threads) without a single frame drop so far, at 1440p 60fps.Gameplay: Will elaborate in the cons, but once you *find* the depth the combat has, like all sorts of cancels and combo breakers and extenders, it becomes a lot more fun to play. Ranged is not nearly as useless as others have said, though whether or not it's the meta I have no clue. Boost being consumed for melee isn't really a downside, you'll only run out if you're mashing and you regen it very fast, only a second or two to charge to full.AI: If you've played DB Xenoverse, basically expect it to be as useful as that. So basically just ignore it and maybe sometimes it'll do things. That's a little annoying, but it doesn't ruin the game. You can revive yourself anyways, as long as you have any heals left.Lock-on: People have complained about it, I have had zero issues with the camera or lock-on so I have no clue what they mean. Story: It's like if Xenoverse actually tried. Instead of villains just randomly getting stronger in the past, people and things are getting crisscrossed between time. So characters aren't where they need to be, and you're fighting dangerous enemies they shouldn't need to. Characters actually respond accordingly too, and actually converse about what's occurring instead of glossing over it as Xenoverse did. Yes you have to read the subtitles mid-fight to understand this, but I've never had an issue with stuff like that since I was 8 so, I dunno how that's an issue.Soundtrack: They have several tracks from each series, and you can customize which ones play when you use a super, and they're all bops. I'm quite enjoying it. s: This game definitely understands not everyone will know every gundam story, and explains it as such. But it also doesn't over explain, so as to bore you. As someone that knows lots of surface info of gundam without much in-depth knowledge of any series, this is quite handy.Cons:Poor Tutorial: The first level doesn't actually explain half the game's mechanics, you'll need to do the optional practice tutorials to learn what you actually need to know, like Role Actions, Perfect Guards and Sidesteps, dash and jump cancels, combo breakers and extenders via Chain Breaker. These greatly improve combat, which means if you don't do the optional tutorials, you miss out on them.Money and Blueprint grind: Your big reason to replay missions, is to make more money to level your gundam, and get blueprint drops to make new Gundams. Due to money being fairly tight, you'll have to replay missions several times to level a new gundam up to where it needs to be. But by the point that becomes a real issue, you'll likely need to do so anyways to get all the blueprints from a mission. So if replaying levels several times bores you, then yes this is an issue. As an avid Xenoverse enjoyer, this is just Tuesday.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoy all things Gundam I cannot recommend this game at full price. If you're a Gundam fan but not a fan of beat-em-up style games I'd wait for a significant sale. I personally don't believe this was worth the full price tag.The visuals are beautiful and so great to look at. The game play is okay, fun at times. The big bosses are super annoying and don't feel like they're worth fighting on harder difficulties. The story is what you may expect and quite honestly forgettable, but the characters are fun and have their own anime-esque charm.If you're a super Gundam fan I'd say go for it. The base game is not very long and you'll get into quite the grind fest if you want to unlock everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent Gundam game when it's on sale (80% off or more), but definitely only recommended for Gundam fans. Takes a bit of practice to learn how to break opponents' armor and perform perfect guards/counters/side steps. Once you learn to break armor and guard, it becomes a lot easier. Unlocking all the Gundams and levelling them is a major grind, but it all becomes easy once you get to hard mode. Start by focusing on one or two Gundams, and then you'll be able to max the rest more easily by clearing stages on harder difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Updated after 240+ hours for refinement with more accurate info.Just 5 hours into SD GUNDAM Battle Alliance (SGBA) and here I am writing a review for it. This rarely happens to me unless it's for a game that I'm refunding or I disliked it so much that I'm sure I won't ever want to touch it again. However, this time it's because I'm having so much fun with it that I feel obligated to do this game some justice given its mixed reviews.SGBA is an action game that defines its own brand of action that focuses on visceral yet deliberate combat. You pilot a Mobile Suit (MS) and clear missions. Encounters in the game vary between few to many enemies, and bosses are other MSs or Mobile Armors (MAs) which are huge and have attack patterns and specific weaknesses. What I find interesting about the game is that it doesn't rely on a complicated combat system to deliver a fun and satisfying experience. Instead, it gives you the basic tools which form the basis of how you would approach combat - and I found it to be darn effective.The combat and controls in SGBA are are tight and responsive. The game uses two melee attack buttons for light/heavy attacks found in most action games, and uses long presses for spin (AoE) and launch attacks (for air combos). There are 3 weapon attacks that are known as Main Weapon, Subweapon 1 and Subweapon 2 where the former is always a ranged attack while the other 2 attacks may be ranged or melee depending on the MS you pilot. All weapon attacks use an ammo system which auto-reloads but will incur longer reload time if they fully deplete. For movement options, every unit can jump, sidestep, dash (like running) and air dash (like flying horizontally). For defensive options, there is guard and dodge; you can negate damage or parry a melee attack by doing a perfect guard, and use perfect dodge to evade an attack completely with invincibility - they have tight timing that require skill and reaction. For resource management, other than ammo, there is a boost bar (like stamina) which depletes when performing movement/melee actions. There is a guard meter which gets reduced when taking chip damage while guarding and will leave you wide open if depleted. Combos in this game can utilize every attack, movement and defensive option and is very free-formed. However, not all actions can connect to another and depends on the MS which requires your experimentation. Every MS has a different capacity for doing combos; some shorter, others longer, and a select few can go on indefinitely. Your MS has a skill meter that is charged up as you do and take damage. The skill meter can be used to perform a "get off me" move, reset combos and role action (there are 3 roles and every MS is assigned 1). There's also canceling in the game which (again) vary for every MS. Last but not least, every unit has a special attack (SPA) that will trigger a short cutscene for a flashy move. The great thing about the controls are that they are simple to pick up and has counterplay elements to make combat interesting - which can make a PvP mode viable.Story-wise, it's not great but I didn't find it bad either. The writing and voiceovers are good and the story is presented in Visual Novel style with a mix of imagery and cutscenes. The storytelling may still be confusing for someone entirely new to the Gundam series even though the dialogue does attempt to provide background information. One nice detail about story mode is that the game doesn't assume you are interested in it and will instead unlock lengthier scenes in a library (for later viewing) and not force you to go through it. It's a shame, however, that many popular MSs like most of them in Gundam Wing are not in the game. But this is a constraint that I can understand.Gameplay-wise, SGBA is mission-based. The game loop is about clearing missions, gaining xp and loot, unlocking MSs, upgrading existing MSs and progressing to later missions. Missions are replayable and need to be replayed for earning the blueprints to unlock MSs, farm parts and earning capital (the currency). It's grindy gameplay but surprisingly isn't that bad due to updates to the game. The player unlocks pilot skills (talent abilities) as they level up and caps out at lvl 100. MSs are upgraded with capital to increase stats, which in turn translates to a level based on the amount of points invested, also capped at lvl 100. Invested points on an MS may be re/unallocated but cannot be reverted back into capital. Because leveling uses capital, capital may be earned with one MS to level up another. There are milestone levels where the player needs to uncap the stat limit in order to further level the MS. You can bring 2 AI partners in each mission. Partner levels affect their MSs' stats and there is a friendship level that affects the effectiveness of the buffs they bring to battle. Parts are items that can be slotted into the MSs as enhancement, with each part being able to have 1~3 stat enhancement (like + HP/damage, + guard window, auto guard, etc) which are random. Instead of parts containing beneficial modifiers, they can also contain 1~2 modifiers that reduces stats (like longer reload times, etc) - this makes itemization more interesting. The slots on the MSs increases based on the milestone levels which are at 15, 30, so on so forth.Overall, the presentation of the game is good with attention to detail like making the MSs look battle worn. The textures on them (or the environment), however, aren't hi-res and can be jarring to look at up close. The particle effects look amazing and feel very appropriate. Audio-wise, the sound design is great and with a lot of detail on different MSs. The game includes a lot of music from the Gundam series and even a few arranged tracks. I found the arranged track for Gundam Unicorn to be exceptional, the rest are ok. The cool thing about audio is that music is customizable in the game. Even cooler is that the game has an in-game feature where you can specify a folder containing your .mp3 files which you can use to replace the music in the game. But even cooler is that you can even assign a song to be played when you use your SPA (like in Super Robot Wars series). I love this feature and my personal recommendation is to put "Life Goes On" (from SEED Destiny) there - it's amazing.Performance-wise, I haven't had a crash in my 240+ hours. However, there are instances where there are very noticeable framerate drops, though these are very infrequent. Apart from that, it runs great at 60fps on my GTX 1060 6GB (max settings). Btw, listed specs on the store page is misleading perhaps due to support for raytracing in the game.As for the things I think are not so great with SGBA, here's a few I can think of. The camera can be wonky and takes time getting used to. The telegraphs of MS enemies are hard to read due to the over-the-top particle effects obscuring the enemy unit's actions. AI partners don't survive well and will require additional effort from you to keep them alive. Personally, these are not really major issues and they haven't reduced the fun for me in any major way.I think ARTDINK (the developer) might have stumbled upon a potential winning formula here for a Gundam game series. SGBA is ridiculously fun and can be played both casually or hardcore, with so much to explore and even has online multiplayer. It's a solid action game with solid foundations, full of content, fan-service and has nothing I would want taken away. Nevertheless, I do think that it has too high of an asking price and better to wait out for a sale. In conclusion, I strongly recommend getting the deluxe edition at 50% off as the included DLCs are of good value - better quality and for more efficient late-game farming. It also includes, imo, the best arrangement of outstanding music tracks like Vigilante, XI and car5p3/PENELOPE by Hiroyuki Sawano. I'm very happy with the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Gundam game? Nope. But I enjoy the hell out of this game. There are glaring issues, specifically the camera and the grind. The camera is probably the weakest part of the game. Could've definitely used some polishing up - sometimes, you can't tell what you're doing when you are zoomed in so close to your Gundam's chest or back because you're next to a wall. The grind, not too bad to be honest. But, it does get a bit annoying when you have to play the same stage 4 times to get the needed number of blueprints. And the in game currency grind does get a bit tiresome at the later levels.Now to the best part. The graphics, for what it is, a chibi-Gundam game, is good. Better than what I was expected. My frames are consistently 60fps without any lag, if any. Combat can be a bit clunky with some Gundams at first, but once you get used to the combos and controls, it's so smooth and fluid. It just takes getting used to. There's practice/tutor mode. USE it. Don't skip thinking, "I'll figure it out as we go." It helps with some advance movement to help get 60+ combos if you do it right.  Not needed, but wish I knew about it earlier. There's enough variety of Gundams with their own game style that you can have fun for days. It doesn't have all the fan favorite rosters (i.e. endless waltz) but it has enough to keep the fans happy in my opinion. Hopefully more gets added in the future through DLC. Fingers crossed. Once you find "the one" Gundam that suits your game style, oh man, you just end up playing for hours on end without realizing it. But, again, this game is a grind to get the stuff you want and the needed upgrades. If you don't like the art style, and that's the only reason, then I highly recommend you to try a demo mode, if you can, just to get your feet wet. And if you still don't like it, well, you don't like it and you move on, not spending any money on this game.I personally like it and recommend it to Gundam fans. If you're not a Gundam fan, I would recommend it for the gameplay. It's smooth and not too complicated. It only gets complicated if you want to start going to the "advanced" moves.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does take some of the concepts from SDGO. Mobile suits are sorted into 3 categories, there is backstab damage. And more importantly the artstyle is SD with stage designs reminiscent of the PVE maps from SDGO. If you are expecting this to be the next SDGO however, you might wanna take a closer look at the packaging lest you wanna complain after buying it. If however, you are looking for a fun PVE coop experience, then this is the game for you. Its an ARPG. Expect grinding for levels, parts, mods and blueprints (hunting for materials like any RPG for the matter). Expect rerunning stages to make the max out of things. Grind isn't that bad in multiplayer. Single player is tedious because of the VN style story telling used. You have your standard standing characters yapping away to a still background. And then you have the animated CG and cinematics (recreation of anime events). If you are not a fan of the VN style story, multiplayer might just do it for you. You can still progress story without having to sit through all that VN style plot. For gundam vets especially to those who rewatch gundam series, they tell it like you're 5 so it might get draggy. To sum it up,1. Great action. Fun mechanics. 2. Mindless controller action fun, better in multiplayer mode. 3. Animation is spot on (Kampfer pumps the shotty after each shot, reloading the Zaku MG and you can literally see your boy slapping on a new mag drum)4. Graphics are pleasant to the eye. 5. Fun boss fights (my personal favourite is fighting the legless Zeong)6. Custom soundtracks for your special move (Tunak Tunak Tun Guntank ftw)My personal nitpick :1. Hoping for more playable grunt suits in the future (you already made the asset, make em playable please?)2. Some series lack presentation (Gundam Wing for example)3. Draggy VN style story telling

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in no way worth sixty dollars. Buy it on sale for thirty.There is, deep down, a very fun game here, however as you keep going you don't so much "get used to the jank as part of its charm" as you do "uncover entirely new layers of jank and regret this game's design decisions on part of the developers." The grind is tremendous, the lock-on system is atrocious, the original story can be generously described as a complete non-entity, and the game options can be downright bizarre; this is perhaps the first game I've encountered where the lack of a non-Japanese voice track is a legitimate detriment to my game experience, as trying to parse the ABSOLUTELY CONSTANT barrage of midstage banter while you're in active combat is at best exceptionally distracting.If you absolutely cannot stand Souls/Nioh-style mechanics, this game is 100% not for you. Battle Alliance can be sighted in as an attempt by Bandai to answer Final Fantasy Origin: Stranger of Paradise being a shockingly good gameplay experience, without realizing what actually made it fun or good: the deeper levels of combat are highly based on perfectly-timed guards, counters and evasion, but the timings required for these are very tight, often absurd and in a few cases a shade or two short of impossible to anticipate. MS-to-MS combat can be incredibly fun and feel incredibly rewarding, but when the larger-scale Mobile Armors appear as bosses, the combat begins to crumble under highly-questionable balancing decisions, turning that prior feeling of fun from defeating a boss to "Oh my good lord, FINALLY, I can move on from this fresh nightmare oh cool the next boss is a MA as well."Factor in how you NEED to grind previously-completed stages to not only acquire new MS through a semi-random drop system, to say nothing of bringing new MS you acquire up to speed, but simply to KEEP AFLOAT with your primary progress altogether, with a heavily-punishing level-scaling system stacked entirely against you, and you may be fighting these utterly horrible bosses constantly.Frankly, the first three-ish hours of this game were the best I've had in my ten-hour run. Enemies were tough but had a constant level of telegraphed anticipation to them, and muddling through Mobile Suits to find what clicked for me was a good time. After a certain point, however, I feel locked into my choice of MS as trying to raise multiple at once simply extends the grind to an annoying degree as you're doing the same stage again and again with not much more than a speedrunner mindset of "How can I get this done sooner" to keep you company.Honestly, just wait for a potential balance patch, or for a modding community to grab onto this game, because as it stands you're basically sunk-costing your time.

_childDocuments_.review: The enjoyment of this game all boils down to expectations.Is it grindy? Kinda. But the combat is juuust deep enough for it to be a pretty entertaining grind but each person's tolerance differs. Some of the boss designs are terrible, the camera and lock on system are terrible and Gunbutts outside of one or two have a lack of AoE that makes the farming a bit less satisfying than it could be. There's a limited roster of robutts and though spans a large portion of the Gundam universe, it only offers one or two from each of the series leaving a want for more. (Where's my damn Heavy Arms) Most likely all according to plan for future DLCs.All in all, I enjoyed it but I like both action spectacle games, musou games, robutts, and farming. This just happens to check mark all of those and be pretty decent at most of them. For everyone else, pick it up on a sale and expect the DLCs to cost an arm and a leg.First ramblings, the bad.The camera compounded with the small arenas and targeting issues is frustrating af.Cutscenes. My. Frickin. God. This needs to stop in games. Learn from FF14 who learned from themselves. Interupting the player in the middle of combat constantly for a short boss cut-in scene or special attacks that last more than half a second of taking away camera control/situational awareness needs to frickin stop. It interupts flow and is frustrating as all hell when coupled with the AI being enabled right after a cutscene. The player is orienting themselves after camera control and visibility is taken away from them, let's have the AI immediately combo them right out of a cutscene.Unskippable tutorials need to die. Unskippable tutorials that force you to do EXACTLY what it says and lock everything else needs to be resurrected, then nuked, then beaten with a stick and forced each one of its little particles to go through a forced quick-time event sequence before being buried in a black hole. This is a game, let the player experiment and learn through the interactive medium. The additional optional tutorials are good, the way those optional tutorials play are crap. Tell the player the information on the side and let them try it and whatever else they wish.Bosses. The Gunbutt v Gunbutt fights are great. You learn the patterns and get better building upon the rest of the game's combat system. Dodging, perfect guarding, counters, combo breakers/extenders, bar breaks, back attacks, aerials, all of these systems works in these fights. Then the game decides to throw giant robutt fights where nearly all of these mechanics get thrown out the window outside of trying to time perfect guards while a giant Gunbutt jumps up and down blocking your entire screen. Combo extenders? Get knocked down. Melee fighter trying to combo? Giantbutts have super armor and ignores your puny little hits. Solution? Play a ranged robutt, fire your load, and hide until things are reloaded. What about melee? Don't.The balance of the game skews heavily towards ranged. Yes robutt v robutt fights can be easier on a melee butt, but melee butts get wrecked in giantbutt fights whereas rangedbutts perform slightly less good to meleebutts in butt v butt fights but are by far WAY the hell easier on giantbutt fights. Butts.Some of the missions are also designed in an annoying way forcing the player to backtrack or having really tight corridors coupled with bad cameras and a lot of enemies. It's misery. Boosters should really allow you to move faster when not in combat.The balance of the robutts are terribad. The crater between one extreme and the other is huge. Infighters get the short end of the stick and ranged beams are superior to everything else.What about the story? WHAT? I can't hear you over the mashing of the skip button. Something about time cops and the matrix. Why can't I just hit one button to skip the entirety of the story parts? It should really be optional.Finally the everything else ramblies!The combat is really pretty fun when it's working. Counterattack windows are tight so the player doesn't do them left and right without effort but when pulled off, it's really satisfying. Perfect guards are more lenient and make a huge difference in reducing incoming damage, layered upon that are normal guards which still hurt like hell but allow the player to survive long enough to maybe heal. Getting hit in the face gets increasingly punishing to the point where two full combos would probably floor a player if face tanked on an average robutt at higher difficulty. The balance here is really good.Hit points of enemy robutts is also well balanced. At each point of uncapping a Gundambutt to the next tier (raising the stats cap), there's spike in power if focused on pure offense. But towards the end of that cap and before the next cap raise things don't just die and it emphasizes playing a bit more cautious once more. Outside of a few boss fights, the enemy health bars aren't long enough to be a pure slugfest and coupled with the limited heals per mission results in a nice pressure in combat. The game is balanced in a way that failures will happen and for the most part, it's not impossibly difficult. Just a bit frustrating when the game controls fight you.Farming for new buttsuits is pretty fun too. You see the silhouette of the robutt and can see a list of their skills (though with often terrible descriptions). This is the carrot that swings in front of the player to collect things and is a pretty fun loop (if only the robutts were balanced a bit better). Having Capital be the main resource to be farmed means the player has more freedom to goin around doing what they want while still making progress. The 'parts' system where you can equip a robutt with 'enhancements' adds a loot hunting endgame to further empower/customize butts. Keep getting knocked around and wasting ammo? Superarmor. Keep getting back attacked? Omnidirectional block. Have something that boosts beam damage but all your moves are physical? All attacks become beam modifier. There's enough depth there to create some playstyle changing robutts. It's still not deep enough but looking at the competition of these type of games, it's pretty damn good by comparison.The levels are pretty. There's a lot of variety and love to the source material. The player will naturally have to repeat the levels over and over again so it's good that for the most part, the levels are pretty unique and have little enjoyable details the first 9 out of 100 times you do a level. Some of levels are more annoyingly designed than others and slightly too long to be fun. But there's good with the bad giving a taste of the general feel of each Gundam series. The 1 on 1 or 2 on 1 combat of normal sized robutts is where this game shines. The movesets and targetting is not good enough for the larger battles (both in size and in numbers). Movesets should really include more AoE and for those that do have AoEs, they should really be a bit bigger by default. All in all it's a fun romp seeing new robutts and wanting to get it to try out leading to hours of targetted hunting for parts and experimenting.

_childDocuments_.review: SDGBA, or as I like to call it: Gundam Breaker At Home, might very well be the BEST Gundam game on PC (at least until GB4 drops on August 29th). But seeing as its only active competition is a shoddy port of a PS4 Gacha game (which btw still doesnt have fully functional matchmaking), and New Gundam Breaker (lol lmao), it's not exactly a high bar.That said, don't let the Mixed reviews fool you, this IS a game worth playing if you're a fan of the IP, but it's not necessarily a game worth **paying for.** With its rather lackluster roster, the DLC is basically mandatory to get the full experience out of the game, so paying full price for the whole package is absurd. Get this game and its DLC on SALE, as low as you can get it.The Positives:- The combat has more depth than it lets on, each suit has unique cancel routes for their air combos, and some cancel routes are universal. What's more, the game also has INFINITES. That is, until you run out of subweapon ammo (if you build a certain way, you wont)- The dialogue between partner characters is great fanservice. Thank u Artdink.- CUSTOM BGM. THE POSSIBILITIES ARE ENDLESS.- Multiplayer is an option if you have friends, so you can grind together!- The exclusive remixes for some of the well-known themes go really hard.The Negatives:- It's a Gundam Action RPG, which means it's grindy. But the grind only really gets heavy around endgame anyway so I don't think you have too much to worry about.- You can't turn any of the ingame volume sliders to zero. Artdink why.- This is a very japanese game in that it has a visual novel type of story mode going for it. It's extremely exposition heavy so hold that skip button if you're not into being info dumped every level.- You can't turn off the dialogue that happens during the levels you already cleared once, so you're gonna be hearing the same lines spoken over and over when you grind story missions. Endgame EX missions have no dialogue, so don't worry about those.- Quess Paraya is a DLC boss. Best mute that volume mixer when you fight her, she gets REAL noisy.- Game seems to have stopped support since the WFM DLC, meaning there won't be any more additions to the game and that makes me sad. Given the game's fighting game-styled combat, i would have loved to see suits like the Hygogg, Zeong, or Hydra Gundam playable.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system of the game is rather basic and not too much in depth.It is nothing groundbreaking, but can be rather fun when you manage to pull of a big combo. The Lock-on system is only ever usefull when fighting a boss. When facing multiple small enemies, it will actually get in your way. The lock-on system will cause you to combo enemies that are long dead. To have the best experience, simply turn off Auto lock-on. This will allow you to switch targets mid fight rather frequently, with which agile mobile suits like Barbatos Lupus become very fun. Most gundams work the same way, making it rather easy to learn them. That being said, that does not mean they are identical. The Gundams do in fact feel different enough for me to make a preference. And the items that drop from quests can make a big difference in how you approach a boss, but...It does take a few hours to properly pick up and understand how you are suppose to approach a boss exactly. This seems mostly difficult for most people since the game switches from a general beat em up to a more tactical gameplay upon starting a boss fight. You can not really rush in and instantly combo a boss.Every boss basically has a certain amount of armor you will have to break first. This is best done by using counters, breakers or Special attacks.However, this is where the design of the visuals kinda mess things up. When you have Gundams from the selected mission and your own partners helping you out, you will often have so many effects on your screen that it will make it difficult to predict what the boss is gonna do next. This will cause the boss to charge straight at you from a large dust cloud for example. Additionally, the boss will always target the Mobile Suit that is doing the most damage at the moment, unless another mobile suit attempts to repair someone. In that case it will switch its target to interupt the repairing.This sounds like a fine system at first, but makes the Sharpshooter class of Gundams when playing single player unreliable. It is very difficult surviving the constant pressure of a boss with a gundam that has Limited guard and lower health then any other gundam class. The sharpshooter variant only really makes sense when you have an infighter getting the attention of the boss. Even items and skills that help you interrupt your attacks to counter guard will not work here, since all ranged attack of the sharpshooter are special attacks which can not be canceled. Additionally, since your constant ranged attacks will get the attention of the boss, the boss will proceed to move all the way towards you while you as a sharpshooter will attempt to keep your distance.This will cause your partners to barely get any hits and even miss SPAs.The All rounder class works fine and is the most beginner friendly, as it should be. But the Infighter class simply makes the most sense when playing singleplayer, as it can basically face tank a boss when played correctly. This game will show many famous scenes of different gundam media. This also means that there is an imense amount of lore to pickup, which did cause me to lose track of what is going on exactly multiple times. Especially since you are tasked with ,,fixing,, the story of the shown scenes and make them lore accurate. However, the chance of seeing Mobile Suits from different Gundam series meeting each other is honestly amazing. I love the dialoge they share with each other, including the ones you get when combining different partners. Another important part to the story is that this game likes to often end with cliffhangers. It frequently shows the climax of different anime with a cutscene, but then proceeds to interupt them. THEN the game will proceed to tell you by text what exactly happens after the cutscenes. I very much disliked this at first, but it does make one curios for the series this cutscene originates from which most likely is intended.  The SD Gundam designs do take some getting used to and is definitley not for everyone. But there is something charming about seeing your favourite Mobile Suit as a little chibi. The visual effects sometimes feel over the top. I generally prefer gundams that do not cause too many effects while also not looking too boring during combat. This is especially important when you want to keep track of what a boss is doing. i do recommend this game for Hardcore gundam fans. But if you decide to wait for it to go on sale, you are not really missing out on much. This is a cute and fun game with lots of up and downs and a rather unique entertainment curve.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10 it's fun, The gameplay has more depth than you'd expect but not as much as you'd like. Though occasionally it feels like you're fighting the camera more than the enemy. Safe choice for a sale. Has co-op.DMC-lite, standard moves pretty much every suit has are a basic combo, aoe slash, air launch, and an air spike. You can chain most of this together for some simple combos. Evades and the i-frame perfect evade (which you can increase the window on with equips)Guards with chip damage, perfect guards with no chip damage (which you can increase the window on with equips), and a perfect guard on certain attacks can parry enemies and interrupt them.A burst that can be used offensively to cancel/extend combos, or you can burst when getting hit for a good ole "get off me."The number of hits, range, damage, etc. will vary between suits but that's all pretty much standard.Then each suit will have three unique moves that have charges (basically ammo) that recharge overtime (some actions can refill these ignoring the cooldowns) and then one special move.One of these moves is almost always a normal ranged attack, these can usually be mixed into combos or be used when juggling enemies or to just attack from ranged (who would have guessed?)The other two vary quite a bit from suit to suit but they can usually (but not always) be chained into combos with normal moves or sometimes with eachother, these in combination with normal combos and the burst to cancel/extend combos are what let you make some crazy combos.The special move is usually a big flashy move that does a bunch of damage, for some suits it also powers up the suit for a short time, and then for even fewer suits it just powers up the suit and doesn't have an attack. The ones that power up may change your basic moves for the duration as well. Most specials get i-frames during the activation so if you time it right you can use it to avoid attacks but it has a long cooldown so you won't be able to do that frequently (unless you build for it).There's three "classes" or "roles" that suits have, Sharpshooter, All-Rounder, and Infighter. They also have a specific action based on the suit's role.Sharpshooters shoot, a lot, their unique moves are almost always more shooting, specials are usually shooting as well. Sometimes the basic melee moves are actually also shooting which lets that suit play a bit more flexibly. The role action replenishes charges of the unique moves.All-Rounders are more balanced, they're more about combos and chaining stuff together. The role action makes more moves chain together (faster) for a short time allowing for some better/wackier combos as well as react to the opponent faster with evades/guards mid combo.Infighters are the melee tank, high health/defense and a lot of melee attack, the unique moves (not including the ranged attack) are usually melee, dashes, and/or grapples. The role action prevents enemy attacks from staggering/interrupting you for a short time, you still take damage but you can play out your "you can't stop me" fantasies for a little bit.And then there's pilot skills that unlock based on your pilot level and random loot equips that have random stats. This lets you customize your playstyle closer to your preferences.Each suit needs materials and money to be upgraded and so to upgrade your suit to max or to upgrade multiple suits can be a bit grindy, especially later on when the missions get longer. If you only want to do each mission once you're probably not gonna have more than one suit upgraded by the end of the game. Unlocking other suits can also take multiple mission clears depending on the suit/mission.Once you unlock a suit you can select it as one of your partners, you can have two partners at a time. You don't have to worry about upgrading those suits for your partners.Now I know I've explained quite a bit so it sounds like there's a lot of depth here, and there is, but that's about it, there's a bit more with bosses and specific suits/playstyles but this covers like 90% of it. I'm not explaining how the mission system works cause it's mostly linear. Beat a mission to unlock the next one, unlock hardmode after you beat the game for better loot.It's a good game and I enjoyed it very much. I'd hope that even though this currently sits at mixed reviews (which I think is a bit unfair, 70-80% would be appropriate) that the devs/publishers decide to bring more Gundam games to pc.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I think the game has decent mechanics, if simplistic. I believe the mobile suit collection could also be better, though I am guessing that is what the DLCs are for later. My two major issues are that the third-person camera has serious jank and often has the wrong angles at the worst possible times. This causes problems when trying to complete boss battles in particular. The final issue is that despite verifying my steam install, updating my graphics drivers and opening up a ticket with support, I cannot fix why the FPS keeps going as low as 10 from highs of up to 100. It leads to an abysmal experience. I can only conclude that perhaps this has not been optimized as much as it should have been, which is disappointing considering its price point. If you are on the fence, buy it after a patch or two, and buy it on sale. Full Review:As a lifelong Gundam fan, I was very excited when this was announced. Overall, it turned out to be an okay game, minus the glitches above. But I think there could be some improvements.Firstly, for new players, the tutorial is not detailed enough. I think it should be longer and go into detail about what to do, especially regarding the types of attacks and the strengths/weaknesses of the mobile suits. It only went over this in short detail, so some more detail would help.I noticed a ton of mobile suits missing, many from SEED in particular. It would be nice if they were included as this game is expensive. I am sure the player base will get squeezed through DLC, though.The graphics look stellar; in my opinion, this is much better than Cross Rays, or SRW, that recently came out. The voice work is also excellent and faithful to the lore. I have no complaints overall in this area.My main issue is with what I can assume to be some sort of porting issue. Even with my 3070, I can't hold a steady 60 fps+, and the framerate goes up and down between 10-100FPS. I have tried multiple settings, updating my GPU drivers and verifying the game via steam. None of this has worked. The other issue is how terrible the camera can be. It goes into the worst possible angles, and you have to re-lock on to targets, which puts you at a disadvantage during boss battles. It can range from annoyance to infuriating. I hope this gets fixed.Overall I give this game a 6.5/10; it would be higher, but the technical issues destroy the experience, and the camera issues are unacceptable. For the price point, I expect better. Do not buy unless on sale and after a couple of patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically review games, but playing this and seeing peoples' opinions on it,I think that the current reviews of "Mixed" does it justice. This is my first experience with anything Gundam, and what it does good, it does really good. What it does bad is very jarring to the experience. Breaking it down, all purely from a single-player perspective:The Good:-Beautiful Aethetics-Huge variety of Mobile Suits-"Decent" customization (extremely homogenized in the beginning, but gets a bit better as you progress)-Combat is very fun-Lots of boss diversity-Level layout, while very simple and rarely eye-catching (and I think could have improved drastically in the vertical world-building department) makes the missions flow nice and easily The Bad:-THE VOICES. Holy hell, let me turn them off please. There is no English localization in this game, and while I enjoy very much learning the history and lore behind each Gundam and character as I unlock them, the story doesn't give enough info to make it compelling so instead I'm enjoying the game more through the wiki. The normal cutscenes are fine, nothing to write home about and certainly underwhelming for a $60 game, but I don't mind. But hell's bells, they do not shut up during missions. It's always in Japanese, there's subtitles covering half your screen and I'd rather just listen to explosions and music rather than hear their babbling CONSTANTLY in the middle of the mission. In a 10-minute long mission, it's just constant talking. It drives me up the wall. There needs to be an option to disable this.-Lack of mission variety. Honestly I knew what I was buying, and I don't mind this because at least the boss encounters are very diverse and it doesn't actually feel like the same thing every time. But they could have changed up the formula instead of making basically two mission types, and really one's just a more complex form of the other.-Lack of HUD/menu customization. I feel like this plays in with a lot of other elements people criticize, such as targeting. While that hasn't been an issue for me, menu options to change music, disable voices, adjust FOV, remove subtitles during missions, etc. really should be baseline in a game like this. The Iffy:-Very grindy. Most blueprints to make a MS require multiple runs through a level. Every time you make a new one, it starts at level 1 and you have to restart the grind. I like it personally, but I imagine a lot of people won't like restarting the grind every time they get a new toy. Undoubtedly this will only get more intense the later in the game you get.-No uniqueness through Mobile Suits. Again, something I don't mind but I think others will. I have only received one MS so far that has a unique subweapon that I haven't seen on another MS. Most MS have unique melee movesets, but it appears there's only like ~4 different kinds of subweapons per item slot so far from what I've seen through Directory 3. -Extremely linear missions-----Honestly

_childDocuments_.review: is a Gundam action RPG that I’ve had on my radar since it was first announced some time back. I was very excited to finally play this title but unfortunately was let down on several fronts. I’d like to state that I don’t think this is a bad game, I’d just take caution and read some other reviews and watch some in-depth gameplay to make a better informed decision before purchasing. I  think that there is definitely an audience for this game, but I feel that audience is not me and perhaps I expected too much from it. Here are some points that I’d like to touch on:There are a couple things I’d like to expand on that are mix of pros and cons:It’s first and foremost definitely a Gundam game. All the elements are there. From visuals to sound, any Gundam fan will be tickled pink beam lasers. I think combat can feel clunky and unresponsive. To me, it feels like you are queuing up attacks instead of actively fighting. I think that it is annoying how easily you can be staggered and how enemies can absorb hits. I also think that ranged combat feels lacking, especially when there are classes that are supposed to be able to excel at ranged combat per their combat classification. These issues coupled with a shoddy camera that has some horrendous angles and a screen full of explosive special effects make it hard to keep track of what is going on at the most crucial moments. It’s a shame I didn’t get to play more of it, but after two hours of pushing through, I was simply not having fun. I hate that I have to either give this a thumbs up or thumbs down. I really just want to help people make an informed decision. Ultimately, I was not a fan, so I suppose thumbs down it is.
