_childDocuments_.review: So basically this game is what it would be like if you personally controlled a unit on a battlefield in 3rd person from any of the SD Gundam G Generation series since you get that universe mixing thing going on, but only half the fun.The visuals are very beautiful, even though it make take a second to render some of the textures properly, most noticeable with Liu Bei & Cao Cao eyes and some of the buildings' shadow. It's got that levelling up and unit upgrading that you'd come to expect from any mecha game. Co-op is a nice touch, useful for some of the harder missions since your AI partners are pretty dumb.However, the overall gameplay needs some work. Now even though the controls work for the most part, it's making the mechanics work. So the shield/guarding, this should be your best friend in any given situation, right? Well, it's weak AF, takes 4-5 hits at most before it's durability is lost. It's hard to land a counter/perfect guard since most melee attacks boost at you which will throw your timings off. Also if you manage you land a perfect guard against a large target charging at you, they will still hit you afterwards, I had this twice against Psycho Gundam.I feel that the boss damage scaled up pretty quickly at Directory 4, which honestly wouldn't be a problem if you could actually guard against damage but since there's no defence upgrade to help offset that damage so you keep raising your HP higher do deal with it. The likes of Zeong and Psycho Gundam can down you in 3-4 hits and even if you ress yourself, you're at 1 hit from being downed again unless you heal right away and don't even think about guarding against bosses, a part from the large bosses, the ones same size as you tend to have multi hit attacks that will break your guard and down you anyway, except that you made yourself a sitting duck since you can't move while guarding.And that's just for normal mode, there's still hard and chaos I haven't touched it.Then there's object collision/blocking. Depending on the terrain that you're fighting on, your ranged attacks/specials can miss your target because of uneven ground, debris, buildings etc. There is also the issue of not being able to melee them too if your target passes the barrier outside of the operation area.Also on the subject of specials, as cool as some of the attack animations are, it's very annoying that your target is still able to move while you're doing your special attack, Cao Cao is the prime example of this, I've had Psycho Gundam do a Goku and teleport behind me by the time I was done. Two ways to deal with this, disable it for multiplayer mode and have enemies freeze on the spot for solo play.I dunno if it's just me, but dodging boss attacks seems almost impossible, the enemy AI always seems to have all the perfect timings and firing angles. Maybe my timings are off, but your boost just doesn't feel fast enough to dodge them 80% of the time, they boost towards you and then they gain even more speed for their melee attack. The only saviour to all this is chain breakers but even that is limited in use because of how slow the bar fills up.And for the very last thing; Juno, this character's face and personality has ruined it for me, mind you Hermes is annoying too but not nearly as much as Juno. I'm not even bothering with the story anymore because of her. She's supposed to be this smart techie, with a collective mind but yet no matter how many times she's told that she can't interfere with the timeline and change the outcome, she just can't accept it, gets reminded AGAIN and back to sad awoo face.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont usually write reviews. Which you will notice. i will kinda fall all over the place.But i hope it answears some questions.Its Dragon Ball Xenoverse without the HUB area and character customization.I don't know anything about Gundam but wanted to try this one out after i read alot of negative reviews.I dont want to review the games as a whole, just point out the bad stuff mentioned and reflect on that.While playing it i slowly realized that alot of the bad reviews are either overexaggerated, or people who just havent realized that there is something called "options" It is a neat feature in all games. And alot of the bad reviews played the game for less then 2h just to get the refund and never really got into the game. And like i said. Tried going to options.The complains i read mostly was the lock on issue or the "grinding" for blueprints that when you unlocked them you had to start with the new Gundam at level 1.1. The lock on is something you can adjust in options, even the screen turn speed. I did that before i started playing. Havent felt any issues. I turned auto lock on and switched to manual locking on to the enemy most center of my screen.And then it was just smooth play.2.1. The grinding is SUPER easy compared to the likes of Monster Hunter or Xenoverse.Most blueprints are finished after playing the map ONCE. SOME (not alot) require you to play the map 2-3 times, depening on how many that drops. But IT always gets you atleast one of each IF you defeat the right enemy, which you get information about before starting. Also each map doesnt take long and you do kinda want to grind for money though.2.2. Starting at level 1 everytime you get a new gundam, yes i get the issue. But some reviews stated that you hade to go ALL THE WAY back to the first mission to level up the character. First i never had to do that once and i changed Gundam alot.Second you can just take the best character you have at the moment and do the mission that gives you the most money and then use that money on the Gundam you want. But i barely had to do that. Also if you change the diffuclty on mission you dont get less reward. Which means, grinding goes super quick.If you even want to call that grinding.And third. The newer Gundams have better starting stats then the older once, which mean they dont have to reach the same level as your current one to be almost as powerful".I could do mission with recommended level 20 with a gundam at 12, did it take some extra time? Sure, was it impossible no.The AI does a decent job. And are really good at prioritizing you when you are down. Read that some people experienced that they just died all the time, i havent experienced it like that at all. I never had both em die at the same time. And not alot either.There are 3 classes.Infighter (meele)Sharpshooter (ranged)All- Arounder (mixed)Some reviews i read stated that infighter was the only good one and the rest kinda made no point.I cant speak for all-arounder because i havent tried that one as much, but the issue some had with sharpshooter was that it didnt have much ammo and realoding took time.Once more, i get the issue but i never felt it.All the attacks the sharpshooter has except the normal one which is meele, are otherwise ranged. And by the time i finished using my normal ranged attack i went on to use my skill1 and skill2 and by the time i did that my normal ranged had reloaded. And sometimes you have to go in for some quick meele, but then its right back at being ranged. Also they do alot of damaged. Just like infighter does with meele. I even did a mission at lower level with a sharpshooter and finished it quicker than i did with a higher level infighter.I still prefer infighter though.My real only issue is the special attacks.Because when you do them a small cutscene plays out, the problem is, that the fight still goes on in the background, and by the time the cutscene is over then enemy has moved away so the special attack misses.. Maybe you can turn cutscenes of in options, its not something i have checked. But still i find it kinda bad but not game breaking.Also the bosses cant get staggered only guard breaked, which also seemed like an issue for some. And once more i dont agree. Because if you could stagger the boss with each attack, then where would the challenege be? Then you and your team would just non stop attack the boss and win without even having to try. So no i dont agree that it is a "dumb" choice by the makers. Its the only one that makes sense in this case.You should probably play with a friend though, i think it will help the experience.But its not bad, maybe lower the price a little like 39,99 instead. but still. Its a fun time killing game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a difficult review for me to give because of what kind of game it is and the audience it was meant for.The best way I could put it in words for this game is Baby's first gundam game. It isn't good. It isn't bad. It is meh.It has almost no content, the game difficulty is so low that it would only be fit for children, man babies, or people into gundam that would get this game regardless.There are some pros, some cons, etc.... I will go over the cons.Side note. This game is most likely meant for children. So, some of the cons are undeserved ONLY if that is the case.1. No difficulty. Most missions are about a minute long to 2 minutes long yet you have a 30 minute timer."This does not count for missions with multiple paths like the one where you get the pieces for Zeta Gundam, etc." Not asking for Famicon/NES Ninja Gaiden difficulty "even though I would personally consider that normal or easy" but at the hecking least make the game A.I do something.... Then again, this game is most likely meant for children. Not adults.2. Little content. Technically the gundams are cosmetic. Just err. Very minor differences other than their ultimate whatever and stats. "Already forgot all the names of everything except the hate line..... because how dumb that name is." Your gundam is irrelevant. Three types. Just go for the type you like with the best stat ratio/build with items. This game is so shallow that even PS2 games outdo it in content and much more. Gundam Vs Zeta Gundam PS2 or gamecube... THOUSANDS times better than this... WHY? WHY?  This is a rant but also to make a point. There is no depth to it at all.3. Worthless item collection and currency.  The currency in the game is meaningless. It has no purpose. I don't even know why it is in the game.4. The story is horrible. They knew it was bad which is why they gave the skip option.5.  LOTS of unused or blocked content in the game. WTF? They were planning on a cosmetic edit mechanic but then removed it last minute? Many gundams that are in the game "FULLY FUNCTIONAL" are for future DLCs.... REALLY hate that greedy trash. You can go through the game asset files yourself if you don't believe me. Already people cheating in multiplayer using boss gundams that you can't access or future DLCs that are not currently available. Unused levels, stages, and much more. Though, all that unused content is probably just sitting there waiting for bandia namco to say, it is time to milk our little piggies. Drip drip the content that SHOULD HAVE BEEN IN THE GAME TO BEGIN WITH! And the preorder garbage is just sheer greed. I fell for it.6. The monotonous gameplay was so bad that I just didn't want to bother beating the game. Doing the same missions OVER AND OVER to get the items needed to unlock that gundam. This is to try and add more "replay" value to the game but all it does is let us know Bandai Namco gave us the middle finger and will only release trash gundam  games for PC rather than anything good like Gundam VS Extreme and so on.7. Button smasher and meaningless mechanics.... Yeah, you can dash with invincibility or block cancel out of the same attack over and over to repeat the same attack over and over to built up that meaningless combo..... I don't know if I can say the dynasty gundam games are better than this, but at least they weren't as vile as this. None of the battle mechanics mean anything. You can beat every mission just pushing the exact same button over and over.............8. Games are meant to have fun..... and there was NO fun to be found. I looked everywhere, even in the gundam carburetors.... None. This is subjective.. however, I doubt most people will find pushing one button over and over then moving an analog stick to move a lot of fun....I could write a few more cons but going to stop there. here are some pros.1. A decent variety of gundams are in the game albeit locked behind monotony.....2. The SD style doesn't really take away from the game.  Yeah, some of the mission maps look like early PS2 games if not worse. Battle Assault 3 had better maps in some cases. regardless of that, the art style is fine. It isn't eye gouging or anything. And in some cases adds to the charm.3. No bugs? I am about 75% done with the game or so as of making this review. Had no bugs at all. Rather shocking for a game of this day and age. 4. Optimization. Smooth gameplay. No frame drops, or any issues of the sort.5. Easy controls. Easy for almost anyone except the handicapped.6. It is a gundam game for PC..... Main reason why I got it. Can't really think of much else to say....7. Oh, it has multiplayer but is broken and filled with cheaters. That about does it..... If you want a gundam game to play with your kids. Sure, this could be it. Other than that, I can't..... I just can't recommend this game. And it hurts so darn bad.

_childDocuments_.review: A good, solid albeit flawed Gundam game (but what game isn't flawed?). Simply put, the game is a somewhat simpler, more numbers/stat driven, SD version of the Gundam Vs games but with a more action RPG focus to it's overall approach as opposed to being a 3v3 arena fighting game. This is the easiest way to sum it up.The developers did a pretty good job on it's underlying system where you can play it casually in Normal mode, but to succeed in Hard mode you need to actually learn the system and how to play and combo properly as opposed to simply mashing buttons. Fighting game style staples such as cancelling, rapid cancels, super cancels etc all exist here, which is a good thing if you like these sorts of things but for those wanting a more shooter style game like Battle Operation, this game is NOT for you. This game is a very numbers driven, combo focused game.There are numerous issues, such as unit balance, certain moves being too weak, others being too good, and Mobile Armors overall right now being a bit on the overtuned side. However, nothing that cannot be fixed with some balance patches and going by the content updates that Bamco seem to have planned, there'll at least be a fair amount of support for this game for a bit. Of the 74 odd units currently in the game, every single one plays very distinctly and is unique and have a very distinct move set. There is very little copy and paste in that you're not going to be able to play two units 'identically'. Play them SIMILARLY yes, but not IDENTICALLY. There is a big difference there.All the SD Gundam models are from the SD Gundam G-Generation series, meaning they have a massive back stash of models to recycle so if they really wanted to they could keep simply adding to this game like DBZ Xenoverse 2. Whether or not they actually do this has yet to be seen but personally, I wouldn't mind if they went that route and simply kept adding content.tl;dr if you want a pew pew sort of game, this game is not for you. If you want Gundam Vs, go play Gundam Vs, this game is not for you. If you want Gundam Musou/DW Gundam, go play those, this game is not for you either. This game is it's own beast, with it's own unique system, and a lot of the current negativity surrounding the game is going to be one of 3 things:1) The game isn't <insert other game here>2) I hate the SD style3) I pew pew and can't DPS!!! THIS GAME SUXXXXXX!!If any/all of the above 3 is your gripe, go away, this game is not for you. For anyone else interested in a solid Action-RPG style SD Gundam title with new mechanics to learn, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: HOLY COW, the combat and customization in Armored Core 6 is exactly what I was hoping for in this game. Environment, sound, atmosphere, combat, weapons, etc. are way better (minus the Gundams). Don't ever get this game. Get AC6.TL;DR: This game is absolutely not worth $60. If this was Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, it would be as if every character having half their moves and be able to do one or two combos with little variation. Character models would be stiffer and clunky, there would be no custom move sets, no Mii Fighters, etc. The World of Light map would be bland, items like metal box, bunny ears, and rocket belt would be at 30% effectiveness or wouldn't exist in the first place. The other game modes would be gone or watered down. This is what it feels like going from SD Cross Rays and SRW 30 to this pile of gunk. -The auto-aim is unbearable to play with and -The maps and environment you play in exist. -Dialogue during boss fights fly through your ear when you have to focus on the enemy.-The story is a story.-Attack animations will lock in the initial direction and not follow your camera. What hurts this game the most is the lack of customization. Add-ons, skills, more abilities, more combos — anything to really spice up the combat. There needs to be more than three weapons, three abilities, and one pilot skill. If it  to be done this way then make them really impactful or diverse, but that doesn't appear to be the case.My point of reference is from playing SD Cross Rays and SRW 30, where you could do some crazy optimization to make your mechs/pilots feel OP. I don't see this here at all. The three roles thing going on here seems like a really pointless gimmick. Get rid of it and let us equip weapons from any acquired mechs. The overall experience feels jarring. There's instances where you're forced into a small corridor and the auto-aim messes you up. If I wanted to listen to the dialogue, I would have to run away because the boss is spamming moves and combos. The main menu UI could be improved. Add a team setup tab, where you could preset multiple teams and make adjustments there. Having to go up and down the entire mech list is annoying.This game absolutely could have been a banger.

_childDocuments_.review: Must Read Review. .  Do not buy! Big Gundam Fan BTW.  The game itself doesn't understand how scaling works. The game is fine on Easy and Normal. . However on Hard, the game just becomes unfair and unplayable. #1 Such as Mobile Suits, Gundam's, and Mobile Armor's slaughtering you and your Partners (NPC Teammates) #2 Revive mechanic is soo bad. The Button to heal is Down Button on the D-Pad, to revive your Partner is also Down on the D-Pad. Attempting to revive someone, the game thinks you're using a med kit to heal yourself. (I had to bind the button to something else) Also if your NPC Teammates die, the boss will Aggro on you at all times. Making it next to impossible to revive your team mates. #3 Bosses Spamming their special attacks. This is the case of you have to wait 100 seconds to use your special. Meanwhile any boss you face can use their special as much as they want in rapid succession. #4 Can't pick up additional Med Kits mid mission. On Hard expect to use 2+ Med Kits per boss battle. And at times you'll fight two or more bosses in one run. The game isn't exactly player friendly. It's understandable your playing on hard and it provides a challenge. But to me it's to unforgiving at all. #5 Hashmal = Broken. There is a Boss in the game "Hashmal" it will destroy you it's so broken, how broken? Well you can't shoot at it because it some how has armor that resists any incoming ranged attacks. So the best way to fight it is by using a physical attacker... But here is the catch, Hashmal, jumps, stomps, and jumps, and stomps. Using an "Infighter" means death. Using a Sharp Shooter means death. #6 If you get a "Game Over" you have to redo the entire mission.  It's fine how games do that but at least there are check points or at least a way to load up before you got the game over. There isn't even any 3 attempts then game over.  You mess up just once and get a game over that means you have to redo the mission all over again. #7 The scaling, some missions have a level requirement and that at times you will be 2 to 5 levels above the mission and with a high level mobile suit have the knowledge of how the game works. And STILL you and your team can end up getting destroyed. I am not kidding when I say this but Try harding isn't even the best way to describe it. You'd have to literally sweat and make every single frame by frame decision to take out bosses on Hard, and guess what there are missions where it's 1 level above you and there is no way to grind your character to gain levels because that level is gate keeping you from farming the items required to boost your mobile suit from 80 to 90.  Lets not forget that at times you'll fight two bosses at once. Good luck trying to revive your NPCs with that. #8 a lot of QoL aspects would make the game feel better and flush out it's flaws and even toning the "Hard" Difficulty of the Enemies. It's just one of those games that while it's fun on easy and normal.  On Hard it's too hard. In an unfair way. It's like the game on Hard makes it so you have to play multiplayer with teams on a social media platform to provide call outs and what not. Guess what, only 60 people are playing this game on average in a 24 hour period. How am I suppose to do these missions online. I shouldn't have to rely on 3rd party social platforms or multiplayer alone to progress and jump to the next set of levels 80 - 90. And by the time you reach to Hashmal the first time, you won't be able to return the game because it takes a little over 2 hours to reach to Hashmal the first time.  I'd rate it a 3/10.  Trust me don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sad state of affairs, honestly.I remember the first time that I touched a game console (Playstation Original) and the excitement that followed as I expanded my collection of consoles and titles, as well as deepened my knowledge of the industry that put forth amazing titles like Vanguard Bandits, Crash Bandicoot, Xenogears, and countless others. Now, I just question why do some of you all try? Why waste our time when you run the likelihood of losing reputation, customers, and just showing how you've wasted your life doing something you're not cut-out for. Granted, designing games is not my area of expertise, however, I've researched and deconstructed enough to be able to assess what I and fellow consumers might feel when given a half-baked product.I know enough, where if the opportunity arose, any game I had a measurable hand in developing would at a base minimum cover the following:[] In-depth customization. It's 2022... As a member of the gaming industry, are you seriously unaware of how important it is to release a detailed customization system with games of this genre (most in general), which extends beyond just coloring or weapons?[] You have access to a wealth of inspiration and intriguing titles, which could've played on the "leap through time" concept better than this. It's like you tried to make the Break Decal Arc from build fighters into something its not, and didn't even bother to try and spice up... Must be cheaper to go without a writer?[] Single players or Co-Op Missions. Please, don't tell us you're so down-bad that you need to include basic features into DLCs? Why are there no basic alternative features (i.e. Deathmatch, Rumble, etc.)? [] What was going through your heads with this simplistic leveling system backed by an early 2000's korean-mmo (Archeage) influenced point grind? Who told you that would be a good idea? You have "65" various suits to choose from, so why would you want the player(s) to spend more than 36-48hrs grinding the baseline stats? [] Why do you just have baseline stats? You could've created skill trees for all-rounder, infighter, etc; broken those down further based on semi-broad weapon categories that the players like, and given people a decent range of repeatability.Honestly, you need to be ashamed that you even got on live advertising this product like it was going to be worth the wait or money. It's shameful not business acumen or cunning, because you may not lose a ridiculous amount of money from sales; however, you still do become the mistake to learn from for competitors, regardless of how you try to "bounce back". That said, I hope we never cross paths in this industry when I enter it, as I'll be more than happy to express this to your faces too.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat feels shallow and clunky, with your dodge and guards having to be frame-perfect even though enemy attacks can pop out of nowhere, even with the big boss fights. difficulty spikes kinda weirdly, and the progression system is also really poorly thought out. You'll be replaying the same missions sometimes up to 5 times to collect puzzle pieces for suits. Why? Just feels like lazy padding out of playtime. Grinding out the same missions repeatedly is just not enjoyable. On top of that, upgrading your suits to actually be functional requires a large amount of resources so swapping suits isn't just a matter of unlocking them and playing, you have to then grind out materials to level up that suit to make it usable in higher level missions. Same with your partners, if you unlock them early they stay low level and die very quickly if you decide to play with them again in later levels. I played this to completion purely because I wanted to play *a* Gundam game and without a Playstation and living where I do, this and G Generation Cross Rays are my only two options. I'm sorry, but unless you're desperate or a crazy Gundam fan that just wants to see mobile suits in a game, there's no real way to recommend this. Pick it up for like 10 bucks when it's on sale and you'll at the very least get time for your money.

_childDocuments_.review: SD Gundam Battle Alliance is odd beast. People compare it Dragon Ball Xenoverse and I see why, but it's also misleading claim. First the story. We control a nameless Commander of Gatheroad Squadron in the Universal Century, during Operation Odessa. But During a normal fight we're suddently suck into G-Universe, a amalgation of Gundam Works by Sakura Slash, an AI made to control G-Universe. Together with private Juno Astarte, also from Gatheroad Squadron we have to stop breaking from doing damage to G-Universe. Story isn't great, but i liked. It's competent, even as choices that we have as silent protagonist could be voiced. We prettu much have every anime series, outside of like Seed Stargazer, or more SD Gundams. Sadly it has a problem of Main Character centric. You want GM or Gm Sniper? You're in luck! You want Jesta, Jegan or Strike Dagger? Sorry. There's a lot mobile suits, and that's a plus, but again, no mobile armors. I get it, but in Gundam Dynasty Warriors we could control Destroy or Psycho Gundam. Uch roster rant over. How's the gameplay? It's three person tps with some hack and slash elements. We have 3 classes. Infighter, Sharpshooter and All Rounder. So smash, shoot and both. Pretty much every avaible suit handles the same but the skills are actually very different. My Main was Phoenix Gundam with it's sharpshooter attacks, but I also used a lot of Strike Freedom and 00 Raiser. When it's good, it's good, but there is jankness to it. So i reccomend it, but i bought at lowered price with DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you're a huge Gundam fan. _childDocuments_.review: Gundam game vet of over probably 20 years. We've received some pretty decent ones over the years and some less than stellar ones as well. Sometimes we dont even get certain titles because its assumed that western audiences wouldnt enjoy certain designs in game play, aesthetics, etc. Among all the titles I've played, this is the first one that not only took the SD appearance that I love, but the rich crossover element filled with characters (ALL VOICED!!) and mobile suits from stories we've either enjoyed or have yet to do so, and the easy to learn / hard to master game play of a vibrant hack and slash. There is so much in this game I love that I bought it and beat it not only on Switch, but Im running through it on PC now as well, with later hopes to attempt modding it. The game is so much fun that I was saddened when I not only completed the main story, but blasted through the DLC as well. I admit that the story is so-so, character interactions are limited, the stagger mechanic for enemies is annoying, and I wish they did a bit more in a few areas. But this game makes me greedy, I want more of this, I want more games like this, I want Japan to feel like there is merit to produce and ship more games like this over here. This game may not be perfect by the standards of many gamers, and I wouldnt fault them for feeling that way either. However, I can only see the potential for a game like this to grow into something greater if given the chance. I implore you to try this title out, show them your support, and even if it doesnt replace Red Dead Redemption or The Witcher as one of your favorite games of all time, I guarantee you will have fun with this even if you just beat it and yeet it. But at the very least, the next SD Gundam Battle Aliance type game could come and be even grander than this.If you are a fan of Gundam, I wish you all the best and to have fun!PS: Co op with your friends is awesome too!

_childDocuments_.review: i grew up with Gundam more or lesswouldn't consider myself a hardcore fan, but i saw much of the shows and still (despite staying miles away from anime and co.) kinda sorta keep up with new media releases.as such this game is great, although i'm realy not into the SD art-style.it's kinda a best of a-arpg; does the plot make sense? nope; is the writing great? certainly not. but you get to see many of the core happenings throughout much of the lore and meet (and play along) lots of the most iconic (and not so iconic) characters. for fans it's great. people who don't know the first thing about Gundam: do not buy this game for the story or dialogue, nothing will make sense to you.but here comes the one and most severe negative: there's no english dub. which means mid mission you will be flooded with japanese VO and english dialogue  an a-rpg, with pretty tight nit mission-design. this is by far the worst choice for this kinda setup and english dub should've been mandatory. the gameplay is solidMS and Gundam come in 3 categories: allround, range or melee focus. which basicaly determines their stat-focus. apart from that mechanics are the same: you got a normal and heavy melee, you got 3 "special" weapons (like guns, bazookas, beam rifles, and all the rest) which are on limited ammuniton which inturn replenishes via cooldown.mix in blocking and "dodging", perfect blocks and counters, the ability to air-juggle and you get a solid combat system.there's a lot of the series stable here when it comes to actual suite choice, but you gotta keep in mind that the actual gameplay differences between the models ain't mindbending...it's not Mechwarrior or Battletech.customization and progression are kinda lacking. you level each suit individualy via currency (currencies, aka cash and uncap mats), and you can equip up to 4 special slots for modifications (everything drops in missions). you get a player level which levels via classical exp and allows you to equip up to 3 skills (like faster health-pack use, or more air-juggle damage) and up to 2 companions, which inturn also level classical via exp (and offer passive boni aswell).it's solid, it works and it kinda keeps you motivated.but it ain't great. especialy when you come into the game expecting some Daemon X or mentioned Mechwarrior like customization and progression. it's more like a very light Diablo-Gundam lacking the lootpool and talent-trees. but seeing how most of the core-lore is centered around fixed units similiar to how GW's Spacemarines work like...it's okay. it's not a great arpg, but it's a fun combat focused grinder; nothing to play for 10 hour sessions, but in short bursts it's quite fun. if you are a fan of the franchise you probably got the game anyway ;)

_childDocuments_.review: By far this is not the greatest game. Plain scenarios and very simple controls. Visually it does look adequate for such a small scale game.Nonetheless, this is a very fun game. Gameplay is a reminder of old beat em' up: varied enemies with a very straightforward stage system and small side objectives. It's simplicity does make it fun for a couple rounds, specially with friends. Sound-wise is more than good, less than great. Fully voiced story and remastered tunes and sound effects taken from the anime. The main artwork take on the models could have been an interesting take (SD Gundams with a more realistic texturing), but not missed in game.Overall, fun game. Great for those Gundam fams that have a need for wacking and smacking in short co-op missions, where some of the fun relies on identifying the mechs.A solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: the SD thing will throw you off from taking some of it seriously. . . However.  . .It's not the most complicated game out there, but strangely satisfying, and the story about going through the digital record keeping like world is strangely interestingly done this time. It's not the first time they've done similar, we see it to some kind of effect in Gundam VS, but this time it's really interestingly fleshed out.But on the game play ends, it's satisfying. Things get cut in half, you send some into collapsing buildings, super moves that are charged up go boom, and there's quite a bit of MS to unlock from all kinds of eras.Dodging works, there's some ethics tot he air combo system that can be quite fun at times, and I was pleasantly surprised.Now if they could just do this kind of thing with a non digital world, where people are being ripped through time, or even just changing events int he timeline like the now ancient Gundam vs Zeta Gundam game back on the ye ol PS2. That one still remains my favorite. Changing the timeline to seeing what could happen back then was really fun and a lot of love went into that game.All that said though, this game almost kind of takes me back to that ancient tittle, but unlike then, you can really play some good co op with a couple friends here.Many would say that the full price tag is asking a bit much, and yeah I could very much see the reason for that argument. But any kind of sale, like the one that's going on for 30 percent off, personally I think it's worth it even if just ten bucks lower than the usual, and if you really need a PVE gundam experience that isn't trying to shoe  horn you into PvP and say you can only use melee or shooting, not both, like the very odd design choices of Gundam Evolution does, i'd dare to say it's worth the full price tag.give it enough time, you stop paying as much attention to the fact it's SD style. But bandai would be wise to take everything that's here, even the SD gundam show mechs, and just simply make them more legit scales and not SD. It's really the one thing that chased off a lot of day one buyers.The rest here with game play, and even the story if you have the mind for it, it's a fun ride. I got it for the co op but actually found myself going back through earlier levels again for getting a deeper insight on the story going on, and the game play I honestly was having quite a bit of fun with, even the battle armor matches that seemed like you didn't have a chance, if you play it how to sacrafice a team mate of who's going down and how, and who can revive, there's some deeper stratagy to those battles going on than meet's the eye.Play it smart, and you'd be surprised how fast you can progress, but even when you feel you need to grind a bit elsewhere, it's fun. it really is. Especially when some of that grinding you can do by meeting up with some friends, shoot the poop, talk about your day, and just cut down some MS or blow them to kingdom come at the same time with all three people's specials firing off at the same time.Like Gundam and want something different than the recent past offerings? This is a surprisingly solid option. It's more fun than ya think looking at the cover.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely not for everyone. If you are a Musou fan and you like Gundam then I would give it a try for sure. The game is all about combat and unlocking new Gundam types. I will give the story props for it's interesting approach but like the Gundam anime's it showcases throughout, it's very laborious on dialog that is meant to sound grandiose, but doesn't really mean anything. Especially since the characters are about as A-typical as you can get, both for anime and  Gundam.   Having said that, there is alot of fun to have from the combat in of itself. I was pleasantly surprised to see such nuance and depth. Things that the tutorial doesn't reveal and can only really be figured out after a fair amount of time tinkering. Those things alone I think make the game entertaining enough to warrant a buy, if as I stated before you already enjoy the musou game type. Plus Battle Alliance is packed with Gundams. There is a play style and a Gundam in here for you, for everyone, it's hard not to find one that suits you with the insane amount that they put in the game. I beat it and I'm still unlocking new ones. Eat your heart out Gundam lovers!
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: FIRSTLY, the story is subbed but you can get caught up with cut scenes at your own will. Secondly, some mobile suits are very "zippy showy flashy" so fighting the camera/ knowing what the **** is going on becomes an issue at some parts. Thirdly the combat gets repetitive (spawn, spam/combo, repeat). play a few missions then jump to another game. Positively speaking its an awesome game. The game play is good enough to monkey brain spam combos to victory but also the boss fights can have the timing of a Dark Souls/fighting game. personally i'll unlocked a new MS then watch the anime its from. I loved seeing the mash up of Gundams and mobile suits from different eras fighting each other. If you have watched some of the shows you'll definitely get your "geeky nerd moments" sparked.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty solid game if you are a new or long standing Gundam fan, I enjoyed this game for what it was worth, it's short and simple and can be beaten in about a week or two, mechanics take a bit of time to get use to but after a while you'll have gotten use to it. There's quite a bundle of iconic suits from most of the series, some might be left out unfortunately but you'll more or likely find the suit that you want or one that fits you're playstyle, this game mainly captures iconic events throughout the Gundam timeline as well as mixing things up in terms of story so you get a mix match of interactions amongst Gundam characters.Graphics are as advertised, though with so much going on and particle effects it can be rather confusing as to what is going on, but nothing that can't be tweaked in settings. You cannot pause in this game, but enemies will lock off of you if you do happen to pause and lock onto you're teammates if so you decide to bring any.A lot of this game is basically learning boss's movements and looking out for specific attacks and looking for an opening to launch a counterattack, that and knowing when to dodge and when to rush in, A.I teammates can also launch a special attack that you can coordinate for extra damage.A.I teammates are great to have, however don't expect anything more of them, the most they do is attack and heal, though you can mix and match them, so feel free to find a set-up that works for you, weather it be the Unicorn, Banshee and Phenex or RX-78, Nu-Gundam and RX-0, there's a lot of hidden interactions between them as well that's fun to try and find, or you can fight alone if that suits you better, but it's mainly up to you on what you decide to do.Overall it's a fun little Beat 'em up/Hash and Slash game to play, it can get boring and tedious at times and even feel a little rushed, but it's nothing short of a fun little button masher if that's what you're looking for, with enough Gundams and Mobile Suits to leave the average gundam fan satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, and especially enjoyably with a friend. _childDocuments_.review: I've played this game almost exclusively on the Deck even though it's listed as unsupported. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag, it has a few pros and a few cons. For me personally, I like to spend time grinding if it means I can make progress min/maxing something, and in that vein this game was a total treat for me. I loved trying to find what moves can truly combo into others and how to achieve glass cannon damage numbers. The story is pretty bare bones and is just enough to explain the context of the missions and why they have "breaks" and explain the real canon events. Unlocking late game mobile suits will take multiple tries and you often find yourself getting unlucky. Capitol grinding was always generally slow even when the game came out but the end game DLC gave weirdos like me tons of capitol for playing the same levels over and over again but I do not recommend that unless you genuinely enjoy trying to max things out. Mobile suit selection is also pretty bare bones but I have a few favorites from the SDGO days that are here (such as my Wing Zero and Freedom). I have probably spent more time than most trying to actually derive the damage calculations and what stats are necessary to actually min/max (spoiler generally people are wrong but i don't blame them for certain assumptions). The fact this game is Coop is a really nice element but you will still see a few "meta" units in multiplayer. Overall. this game isn't for everyone but if you love Gundam and you love games where you can tinker and level up then I strongly recommend. If you just want a quick solo Gundam game then this would not be a good pick.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to make this short. This game is fun if you want to collect units. The story is okay and its fun but nothing great. The combat is very clunky, it doesn't feel smooth at all. There will be times you're going to be smashing the attack or heavy attack while waiting for your sub weapons to reload... But in end game content, the bosses have super armor so they don't stagger with normal melee. I think if they added a mode change (like SDGO) where units can have access  to more subweapons, that would be great. If they added passive abilities to the units, it would give every unit a bit more personality. I hope in the next game or sequel, they can do better with the flow of combat... Also balance out the job roles or re-tune it all together. I would give this a 8/10. Fun game but it has its flaws. Don't come in thinking this is the next SDGO.

Price-wise? I don't think I can say. I felt it was worth the cost at full price. That's just me as a player. Others may not. In the age of rising costs of all games, it's getting harder to say what's worth what anymore.Overall verdict: If you're a fan of Gundam, I say go for it. Sale or not. If you're a die-hard Gundam fan/gamer looking to critique every ounce of gameplay, holes in the story, or mechanics to the Nth degree, perhaps wait for a sale or don't play at all. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is casual fun for people to grab a buddy or two and play through major battles in the Gundam franchise. Many spoilers for Gundam shows galore.This game is really fun. It's a near impossible entry for non-Gundam fans who haven't seen a majority of the Gundam shows(mainly those of the Universal Century Timeline, as well as Iron-Blooded Orphans), but for the people who've seen their fair share of Gundam, this game is great! The writing is charming and actually got me to laugh a couple times, the characters are great, and the story is actually not half-bad for an SD game. The main theme behind Juno's character arc is very interesting and I could relate to it quite a lot as someone who enjoys learning about history and war.People who complain about lack of content have not beaten the game, or they have mountains of time on their hands. The main campaign is about 30-35 hours long, and I've only maxed out 2 Gundams, as well as developed less than 20 units in that time. Then there's chaos missions, and the DLC that I still haven't played yet. The combat is simple, but it does enough to give you the illusion that you have every weapon a Gundam would be equipped with. You can hack and slash, then you can also pull out cannons and guns at a range. Many levels towards the end got very difficult for me, so expect a little bit of a challenge. The tutorials will help you. Trust me.My main criticisms of this game stem from the dialogue placement. This game *really* should've been dubbed. The combat is high-speed and fast reaction times are your biggest hope for survival. So having to read subtitles while fighting bosses is not ideal. Neither is reading one spot of dialogue before it abruptly switches to the next conversation after walking a miniscule distance. Not to mention the 30 minute timer for each level that disincentivizes sticking around and listening. The missions lose a lot of character interactions because of this.Overall, I love this game. I feel my money was well spent, and I'm definitely going to achievement hunt this game, since its achievements aren't all that hard. The ending theme is amazing, and was well worth the rage-inducing struggle the final boss gave me. I've listened to the song many times already. Honestly, I don't think this game deserves the hate that it got.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really love this game. It's great for a beat em up. It's not Dynasty Warriors Gundam but it's a good close second. (HINT HINT. RELEASE DYNASTY WARRIORS GUNDAM: REBORN ON STEAM, BANDAI). Great music, and if you ever get sick of it you can put your own music in there, decent collection of mobile suits, and a fun storyline full of easter eggs.My gripes would be the lack of customization for your character. It's just a faceless male who just has the same grunts and voice lines during combat. Would be nice to use different voices and character portraits for your character, but I get it. It's a good cost cutting technique. Also, outside of the Zaku and the GM there are NO Grunt suits available to play, despite a plethora of Grunt suits you're able to bash around in the game. If you're struggling vs Mobile Armors just grind, level up, and experiment with different skill sets. Dont think of it as "I'm going to go full in on this boss". Take it more like a Dark Souls boss. Learn the patterns and you'll be fine. If you're struggling with the aiming system, use a controller.Finally, my only other issue would be the online is practically dead. If you're lucky to find rooms, they're usually in private. Maybe crossplay would fix the issue so we can play with out console comrades? If you're a fan of Gundam and you want fun SDGO style action, go for this gem! I'm begging you, Bandai. Please give me a Gyan :[

_childDocuments_.review: As of this writing, the targeting is whacked out so it is recommended to play with a controller, or adapt your mouselook to keyboard instead (see some temporary fixes suggested by other players).If you come from Gundam Breaker, there is no building your own MS. Customizing is limited to upgrading basic stats and option parts, limit breaking MS levels, and pilot skills that provide situational benefits. If you come from G Generation, there is no large roster of evolving units. The list is sufficient, but not substantial. Large number of key MS are not available (probably as DLC). If you come from Gundam Senki / Target in Sight / Battles, there isn't much to strategy or simulation. Depending on the mission there are different paths. Mobs might change here and there but it's all very straightforward. I have little experience with Gundam Versus type games, but I can say this is not as fast-paced or fluid. Fights can get very draggy. Ammo, while rechargeable, is limited until you can increase them in meager amounts. You are sort of expected to master the dodge and block mechanic. Basically, grind for capital and items to sell. Upgrade your unit. Grind for blueprints, unlock unit. Play the story solo or co-op. Repeat. Each unit will have a certain playstyle but they all conform to the same archetypes. Some are clearly better, and they are in the later parts of the game, so it is recommended you look up a guide, and stick with 1 or 2 until you can grind for your favourite MS. Story wise, it's all over the place, although I think they did OK trying to meld the different "world breaks" together. Character interaction is also fine, sometimes funny. Better than NGB. You can also bring up to 2 partner MS of your choosing.Aside from the occasional crashes, it's mostly alright. Manage your expectations and you'll be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I was torn on recommending the game or not, but after the newsletter went out that Bandai Namco is hearing feedback and plans on addressing it, I am hoping I can continue recommending.Continuing forward.This game is actually a very solid beat-'em up Gundam driving game.The issue comes in the form of how little resource you have to upgrade Gundams, so you can screw yourself into a life of farming if you decide you want to level that Zaku II because, but it overall isn't pulling its weight against the poorly managed Mobile Armors.Encounters against bosses are decent.  The mechanics are there, but...each mobile suit is extremely unbalanced as to how well they do against other boss mobile suits.  Some have sub-weapon attacks that are absolutely amazing for breaking the boss, and making the fight more dynamic....and others...are lucky to even reach a boss before they start slaughtering you again.I guess that is why teams of three exist?Mobile Armors on the other hand...are absolutely horrendous.  Super Armor.  Their weakness isn't always apparent (some are weak to only physical or beam melee...so if you don't have that, have fun.), large, sweeping attacks and extremely aggressive AI, while doing more damage than anything else in a stage all make for a completely *unfun* time.  But they are aware of the problem, so maybe they'll find ways to make those fights less "OMG I JUST WANT TO HIT YOU ONE TIME WITHOUT ABUSING SUPER ARMOR MOVE OR DYING".However, if you can find some friends to play through from front to end, this game is a solid ass choice all the way through.  Playing with my brother has been extremely enjoyable, and we really want a third to help alleviate some of the difficulties of being a duo instead of a trio.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a great game!Graphics - 95/100The graphics are beautiful, very surprised by the detail. _childDocuments_.review: Another game getting a lot of hate it doesn't deserve, mostly due to people not reading or ignoring the SD part of the title or wanting it to be something it isn't.SD Gundam Battle Alliance is a pretty fun beat em up action game that plays more akin to a fighting game where it's best to look for openings to punish and break the balance on boss mobile suits to string together you're combos to ramp up that damage, or punish the mobile armors after their string of attacks get a few hits in and get out.The difficulty is pretty solid requiring a decent amount of skill and attention not found in a lot of games today and depending on your skill level the difficulty might seem to spike every now and then, just know guarding is very important and the auto guard part it gives you at the beginning of the game is a trap that I wouldn't recommend using as it could lead to bad habits during game play and could make some fights harder. Learn how to guard yourself and learn the attack patterns and if you do fail just learn from it.The big negative I have for this game is the lock on switching for keyboard and mouse, as if you are locked on switching lock to another target is moving the mouse and it is "very sensitive" often leaving you missing attacks or turning your back when you don't want to. An easy fix would be to just let us change it to another key, this isn't much of an issue on controller.All an all It's a pretty fun game alone or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love SD Gundam as a whole, then playing this game is worth your while since it consists the core game play of RPG based action and the idea of collecting all Gundams that are yet to be unlocked. The thrill of the game is that it challanges the player to grind and basically develop skills, items, stats,and equipment that may vary on its effect or rarity. As a casual player/gamer this game will not disappoint, yet if you seek the competitive side of things, the game wont cover much on its multiplayer lore. The story and content was well done yet if you are leaning towards the long span of the game, I'm afraid you'd wish there's more added story lines within the SD Gundam franchise. Furthermore on those whom loved watching various gundam anime series, the game is very straight forward in showing the sense of nostalgia along with its music themes that straight came from known series such as the cosmic era of seed, 00 series, UC, etc. It is indeed notable that the developers did their homework in having each series to coexist all in one, while reminiscing familiar classic Gundam franchises together at a deformed chibi sized gundam that most gunpla collectors or fans alike love and enjoy aesthetically. The only disappointing part about the game is that It has lackluster features on multiplayer and missing things you may find known to specific gundam units that lack abilities seen on anime or other similar games you've played in the past. However, the presentation on the graphics design and combat mechanics are superb or should I dare to say very satisfying enough to cover a bit of its flaws. Overall its a solid game that resembles past classic and modern Gundam series with a heartfelt care in developing the game and how it shows passion to show attention to details. Somehow at the end of playing SD battle Alliance, players would probably tend to question additional contents and additional features that may somewhat be seen in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game, held back by odd decisions.The story mode is decent, and serve the premise of the gameplay pretty well. The switch from regular Gundam models to the SD one is honestly top notch. The music choice and the series included are also great. They don't overly focus on a singular timeline, which is something I was worried about, as many Gundam games seem hell bent on focusing on the SEED/Unicorn Timelines. The choice of units that are actually in here, is also really nice, some good suits that I genuinely didn't expect to see as an inclusion (such as the GM Sniper II, The Reginlaze Julietta, etc). However, the game also falters pretty badly in these same areas. While the gameplay is fun, it's grindy at times. And playing as a ranged unit is just hellish at times. Your AI companions are mostly worthless unless you get their friendship to max rating, at which point they become somewhat useful. Mobile Armor bosses are by and far the worst part of the game, fighting the Psycho Gundam, any of the Garbage Space MAs, and even Devil Gundam and the first fight with the Zeong are just ridiculously unfair. You're expected to hit them in their weak points for increased damage, which is almost exclusively their heads. However, that requires flying, which consumes boost and reduces your ability to fight for extended periods without using chain bursts. Flying also reduces your ability to avoid incoming attacks if you're fighting, because again, boost is required.The choice of suits, while I do praise them for including some lesser seen mobile suits, is also baffling. They omitted basically anything from Wing aside from Wing Zero and Epyon. This wouldn't be a huge concern, but you fight Leos, Taurus and Virgos, and you interact with Wings timeline 4 times. Meaning each time you go there, the boss will be one of those two gundams. If they'd added say, Tallgeese or the Mercurius and Vayate, it'd be less repetitive to fight in this time line. Wing isn't the only timeline to suffer from this, as G Fighter also suffers from the same issue, as does CCA. Progressing isn't nearly as difficult as some people make it sound, just play the game on Easy mode, get to mission 7-2b and grind it out once or twice with Alex Gundam, God/Master Gundam, any of the 00 Gundams, or the Lupus Rex, and you'll have more than enough to get a mobile suit up to level 50 (the cap before beating the game), that said, early game it IS a struggle if you want to play a specific suit and don't have it unlocked yet, and since most of the suits are unlocked through either playing a mission or clearing a chaos mission (an additional break in during a mission you've already completed), it makes getting a suit you want, and also leveling it up  before the end game tedious at times.Overall, with how much I've complained here, you might be wondering why I still recommended this game. Frankly, it IS a fun game, especially with friends. The core game play loop is fun and the moments they chose from Gundams 40+ years history really do feel great to play through... when they don't involve Mobile Armors. So yeah, I'd say get the game, preferably on sale, as 60 USD is a bit much for the content we're offered here. If the game DOES eventually get the support that Xenoverse 2 gets, I'd recommend it even more.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I'd give it an 8/10. An above average, excellent game, with only a few downsides, but to get into it...SDGBA is a gundam hack-n-slash game with a fairly wide pool of SD Gundams to choose from, including an SD Gundam which was given a regular Gundam design which was then given a new SD Gundam design based on that... for reasons.Anyways, the pool is a little slanted, with most series only have 1 or 2, and a few series like IBO having 4 or more, so this is definitely a game where you'll want to look up what it has on offer before purchasing.I want to dispel a rumor before going further: THIS GAME HAS  TO DO WITH SD GUNDAM CAPSULE FIGHTER ONLINE. This is part of ARTDINK's series Gundam Battle, which was not released out of Japan until now, hence "Battle" Alliance.As I said, it's a hack-n-slash, but that may have been a bit misleading. The game's difficulty rises quickly as you play through, with several chapters being considered "player filters", which seems almost specifically designed to force you to get good at the game. While you can see for yourself the combos are very simple and nothing in the button layout should be particularly confusing, but this is like saying Dark Souls is a hack-n-slash because its combos are just R1>R1, You'll find as you get further that you either need to strategize, learn how to perfect guard or dodge, or play as a much easier mobile suit (sharpshooters work for many people). While the mooks are easy to kill, the bosses are the meat and potatoes, and they are very well designed. They have a limited moveset, usually 3-4, with a powerup phase that introduces a couple new moves. There's exactly enough to learn and master; there's not too much to become overwhelmed or too little that it becomes simple. There's also a wide variety of bosses and boss types, that play very differently. Unfortunately, all of this means you won't really know if you like the game until you're 10+ hours in and far past the refund limit, so spend cautiously.This is where I get into the negatives, of which there are few and they're mostly nitpicks.My first is there isn't enough of the game. You have the story mode and co-op and that's it. No other modes. No boss rush or timed trials or challenge missions. At most you can say Chaos Missions are a little extra because they add a boss to a level where they don't belong, but that feels like more Story Mission in my opinion.On the note of story missions, I really wish they had translated the dialogue into English, as it stands this is by and away the worst part of the game, and this is the only negative I wouldn't call a nitpick. I can't fight and read the them talking at the same time, and it's frustrating and overwhelming as an autistic person to listen to them speaking a language I don't understand with text boxes in the middle of boss fights. I know there's a mute, but that doesn't fix the text boxes, so short of translating it to English, I wish they'd give the option to turn it off entirely.Next, capital is required to upgrade your gundams, but they don't give you a lot of capital and you get a LOT of gundams, so you're forced to pick 1-3 gundams and focus only on them. What happens if you don't? The game actually has an underlevel mechanic where you deal significantly less damage than you should because your gundam level is too low, so you must keep up to date throughout the story. 1-3 is more or less okay, especially because you CAN drop gundams and move to others by just not upgrading old gundams anymore, but it does take away from the variety until endgame.Additionally, certain gundams do not feel like they were given very much attention, as they have skills which many wouldn't consider important or accurate, such as Arche having ranged funnels. Arche does have these in the show, but many would consider the beam fangs mode to be more appropriate. Additionally, other gundams have a class which doesn't make too much sense to me, such as Dom being In-Fighter, but this issue is much rarer. In both cases, however, a non-gundam fan would never notice or care, so it doesn't matter much.Finally, there are some rare bugs in the game. I had some issue using .mp3's for music. They would start and stop at odd times and occasionally crash, so I removed them. And on one mission a blueprint wouldn't drop for non-host players, which was very annoying, but all-in-all bugs were rare for me.I know I referred to all mobile suits as gundams, and that is not accurate, but I felt it would be the least confusing term for non-gundam fans, as I imagine most gundam fans have already settled on if they like or hate this gameI did not cover music because you can change the music in-game and beyond that you can hear the music for yourself and/or see the song list online. I also did not cover graphics for a similar reason: you have eyes and can see for yourself. I wouldn't want to disrespect your intelligence by implying you can't see or hear if you like something on your own.Finally, I'm a huge gundam fan, and as a result this review is pretty biased, but I sincerely hope it's also informative nonetheless, and I did my best to approach it from a perspective of someone who isn't a gundam fan because I'm confident gundam fans have already made up their mind about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am providing my review of this game now that I've gotten 100% achievements for this game. The game is totally worth its price. This game does have its pros and cons and for all its worth, can be incredibly difficult and frustrating at times but can be well worth it once you figure out the nuances to the game. This is a looter-shooter type game where you enter a stage, experience the story if you wish and gain loot in the form of Parts to enhance aspects of your Mobile Suits/Gundams and blueprints to get expand your pool of usage units. The game feels much like an action-fighting game; you go in and cut things down with your GN sword or duke it out with your beam rifles and guns until you face the Mobile Armors. As with all Gundam games, fighting Mobile Armors is an absolute pain in the ass especially when playing solo. Most mobile armors in this game has I-Fields which you need to break by consistently shooting Beam ranged weapons. Your AI partners are extremely dull when it comes to attacking so you'll need Parts and maybe the Pilot Skill Piercer to deal increased damage vs I-Fields. You can of course opt to use a physical attacker but the game developers made it so that if you are able to take down the I-Field, your beam attacks do increased damage to off-set the time you may have wasted breaking the I-Field. I learned how to Perfect Guard really well with most Mobile Armor enemies. You can Guard and Side Step in this game but Side Stepping isn't really that good because the game's tracking AI is really stupid. Unless you perform a Perfect Side Step which is pressing the button at the correct time, you're going to get smashed so I went with Guarding for most of the time since if you perform a Perfect Guard against enemy melee attacks, you can perform a Counter that destroys their Balance meter allowing you to put in more hits while they're staggered.. That said though, some enemies can be Side Stepped easier than others.The Target Acquisition/Lock on system in this game is a pain in the ass to deal with when playing on Mouse and Keyboard. Using a controller is fine and a lot more manageable. I still don't understand what way to shake my mouse to change the lock on target. The reason for the problem is when fighting bosses, sometimes add spawn and you just want to stick on the boss but you may accidentally move your mouse a bit as you press Mouse 1/2 and game goes, oh you want to target that dood instead and switch off the boss. Then you struggle switching from add to add trying to lock onto the boss again and die miserably. I really enjoyed the dialogue in this game. The overall story is meh but the character interactions in this game is amazing. It's like on the level of Super Robot Wars where some characters actually have lines related to characters from other series. There was one particular mission where Amuro joins as a ally in this mission and there are characters from different series that pop in and Amuro would have some dialogue expressing his thoughts on those people and their timelines. The cutscene animations the game developers placed into the game are also very nice too. That is also to say that the Gundam models and animations in this game are amazing. Using weapons whether it be ranged or melee weapons you can actually see the full animation of the Gundam doing the action including pulling the beam saber out to attack and returning it place after finishing unless you animation cancel. Oh yeah, SDGO players would love to know MCA is in this game although not as easy. Now the one thing I dislike the most in this game are Special Attacks (SPA). Ranged SPA aren't that bad but melee SPAs are absolutely horrendous to the point that it's useless in some situations. Against Mobile Armors you can pretty much kiss your melee SPA good bye because unlike non-Mobile Armor enemies which get stunned if you SPA close enough, Mobile Armors couldn't care any less that you used it and just does whatever they want to do and which is usually jump out of the way. Like I mentioned earlier, non-Mobile Armor enemies get stunned but they are not locked in place which means if someone knocks them out of your way, then your melee SPA is S.O.L. I don't understand this design idea.Ranged SPA also has its fair share of problems. If you lose track of your target when you use your SPA, you would miss the SPA entirely as well. Half the time that both melee and ranged SPA miss is because of the cut-in animation that prompts when you SPA. It's like a whole 2-3 seconds before you actually start attacking and so many things can happen in that time frame. On the subject of SPA, I also don't understand the design concept for some of them. SPA damage can be beam, physical, or both (hybrid) and can be ranged, melee, or both (hybrid). So you build your Sharpshooter with Ranged damage but its SPA is melee like why? Same goes for In-fighters which you build melee but its SPA is ranged. The game definitely has annoying game designs that makes no sense and some artificial difficulty because of said game designs but the game is fun to play. Playing with friends make it more enjoyable of course but there is multiplayer so if you're faced with a difficult mission, just create a room or join a room and play with others. Now I just want more Gundam variety added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say first, that this game is not like SD:GO, and it never claimed to be like it. I'm not sure why people are criticizing it for this.• The graphics are very nice. However the controls are customizable, so I am not sure, how this can be a legitimate criticism, when you can re-bind most of the controls. I recommend using a controller though instead of the keyboard.• I've seen some people complain about the difficulty, who are bizarrely some of the same people, who are whining about the game not being like SD:GO, which is just kind of funny. But some new players might also be caught offguard by the difficulty. I understand, that this might be frustrating to some people. But I don't see, how it is worth a negative review.Anyways I like it, and I've been a fan of Gundam for almost my whole life now: 25+ years.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game, but fair warning, there are hitches along the way.  The plot is nothing to write home about, but many of the character interactions between those who normally wouldn't see eachother are pretty charming.  Music is pretty good, and like most Gundam games it includes a means to introduce your own custom tracks, along with the ability to have it cut in certain songs when you activate your Special Attack.The big thing though is that this game feels INCREDIBLY inspired by an old Gundam F2P game named SD Gundam Capsule Fighter Online(Or SDGO).  Back attacks, movement, sub-weapons, parts, the "trio-category" system for organizing unit playstyles, it's all incredibly familiar, just improved, while also adding their own dash to make the game unique, of course.The game also has a pretty satisfying combat loop against normal-sized bosses:  Bait out attacks, and hit them with your Subweapons while their stamina gauge is lowered to force a "Break", then do your best to rack up a large combo to do as much damage as possible.  It's simple, but intuitive and with a surprising depth that encourages players to figure out how to play the units they like the most.The difficulty can be a bit of an issue.  The best way I've seen it described is that instead of difficulty "spikes", there are moreso difficulty "steps".  Nothing really feels "insurmountable" or like a massive jump, but there are definitely moments where the game gets more difficult, and it feels frustrating until you adjust.The best thing I can recommend is that you get used to guarding.  Perfect Guards will ensure that you take no damage and lose no guard gauge, but even if you're unable to, it's still far preferable to block than eat a hit.  In a game where early units can end up with 500-900 HP, blocking will easily take off over a hundred damage from each hit.The main complaint I really have with the game is how grindy it is.  Not for blueprints to unlock units, that's fine, not even for parts, that's cool too.  But instead, I hate the Capital grind.  You just get too little money for how much the game expects you to have a variety of units.  As an example:  If you focus on a unit that specializes in ranged beam attacks, you're probably going to not be happy when you start fighting enemies with I-Fields.  Not just that, but it really encourages sticking to one unit, and that just feels wasteful in such a great game where all the units feel pretty unique and fun.  Not to mention the stats are already capped by the, well, "Uncap" system, making sure that you stay at a pretty reasonable stat spread for each section of the game.Another small issue is that the AI is..really, REALLY bad.  If you have friends, this isn't a big deal, because you can play with them.  But single player can certainly be a little frustrating with how much these guys get in the way.  But it's not the end of the world, the game is still absolutely playable in single player mode.All in all, I do think the game is a hearty recommend on my part.  I'll admit there's some nostalgia bias on my part because SDGO was how I got into Gundam in the first place, but it's been an incredibly fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle Alliance was a great game to play. It was extremely fun, and up'd it's difficulty as you progressed making it extremely challenging, but rewarding, as you continued. It has been the best 40-ish hours I've ever put into any game. The different MS (Mobile Suits) were very cool, and despite what others have said, I didn't have much trouble upgrading random suits and going into the next available mission that I had. I found myself trying to do so many combos, and move through all enemy attacks with dodge it was funny and fun.In terms of problems, there were a couple. The lock-on system is not that great. At times, it will lock on to an enemy that is behind everyone else for some reason. The system also tends to re-lock on to something that you locked off of. The camera does not move fast enough either to even really count as a lock-on, causing you to have no idea what the enemy is doing or missing attacks on the enemy as a result of not being able to see them. I managed this somewhat by turning off Auto-lock, and quickly locking onto my targets myself, and manually moving my camera to compensate for the slow moving lock-on.Problem two : the AI companions. These things are the dumbest things on earth. Sometimes they will only heal you when the enemy is hitting them (god knows why), preventing them from healing in the first place. Many times, they will just not attack for a good while until you force them to use their ultamites/SPAs. I feel there would be a benefit if you would set options on the AIs such as :  "Heal down'd ally when x. Only heal x ally..." and so on. Being able to set these features and designate roles for these helpers would go a long way, especially for players who are completing the story alone.Tips : Use role-actions and combo cancel/reversal. Role actions give many benefits and help boost stats, attack faster, stop you from being staggered, or allow you to reload and utilize your abilities again. Reversals are very useful when fighting MS bosses that grab you, or put you into a combo that you want to quickly break out of. (can even stagger or lower their shield by a lot). I found that for the MA (mobile armors) that are really annoying (those guys hit hard and it is hard to see their attacks :/), using the "reversal" can help stop damage of one attack that is incoming. Use that info as you will.Now this game is extremely fun, with it's own faults, but I still like it. It has a souls-like feel to it, meaning at some point guarding, perfect guarding, or countering can feel very important, or simply dodging. If you like fast, challenging games (very fun with friends), this is for you. If you just want to sit back and relax, either play on easy mode, or this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouse and Keyboard mapping sucks, does not recognize mouse thumb buttons when attempting to remap. It does not register thumb buttons even after their 'fix' to include thumb buttons and, when it does, they are still unresponsive. Restarting the game or returning to the game after fixing thumb buttons and setting them up doesn't undo the keybindings, but outright refuses to recognize them again. In addition, mouse movements, and non-mouse movements randomly switch lock-on targets. While controlling mouse-and-keyboard, your camera is locked to the enemy you're locked onto, so you end up bouncing around attacking the wrong target wildly to a stomach-churning degree. At least you can remap lock-on to Tab or Q, but it's still useless on mouse and keyboardOverall, not a great port control-wise. At least I have yet to suffer a crash or game-breaking glitch.
