_childDocuments_.review: It seems like "boomer shooters" are a dime-a-dozen these days, but not all of them get the "feel" right. HROT feels good. The weapons feel good. The balance feels good. The pacing feels good. And maybe most importantly the level design is good. They always seem to expertly loop you back around to that locked door after picking up the needed key, which cuts down on the wandering around factor some shooters suffer from. You also have a mini map if you get lost. Yes you have your key hunts and toggle switches. But even though the inevitable enemy spawns that result from these pickups or switch toggles may seem predictable by now, it's a staple of the genre, and HROT gets it right. The ambush arena battles are intense and fun. The boss battles are a little ridiculous, but that's also par for the course in this genre. I love the setting of HROT, taking place in old Soviet Czechoslovakia in the mid 1980's. It's dark, it's bleak, it's... brown. But supposedly that's what it looked like back then. I love all the little Soviet propaganda posters you see everywhere, written in Czeck (you can translate them by pressing "use" on them). It gives the levels a nice atmospheric touch. Additionally, the occasional Geiger counter clicking makes it feel like you're traversing areas you shouldn't be in. It's great. Very Chernobyl-like in some instances. (I love that the end level switches have A3-5 written on them. Which when translated to English letters means AZ-5....which was the Soviet RBMK nuclear reactor shutdown switch. The same one that kicked off the Chernobyl disaster. A nice little touch.)The enemies are varied enough to keep things interesting. And you'll discover which weapons in your varied arsenal are best for dispatching each enemy. Don't forget to hunt for secrets. Health, which comes in the form of strange Soviet styled food pickups, and medpacks seem quite rare. Which may be a nod to the 80's Soviet "Era Of Stagnation" and scarcity. So you'll want to look around for either breakable walls, or strange textured walls to find extra health and ammo pickups. Especially if you're playing on the harder difficulties. Some people call HROT Soviet DUSK, and I think that's a fair description. It is very DUSK-like, and that's ok! DUSK was freakin awesome. Overall If you like boomer shooters like DUSK, Doom and Quake, then you'll love HROT. Bonus points if you appreciate Soviet aesthetics. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed HROT, i hope they add more levels to it eventually. It's brown aesthetic and pixelated graphics are quite charming. This game didn't get enough attention upon it's release in my opinion. A recommend for anyone who loves these kind of games. I'd say it's beginner friendly as well. Pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got my recipe for stroganoff, can't wait for more to be added! Seriously good game tho, if you like the first quake you'll definitely enjoy this. The weapons are a bit more powerful so you kill more quickly than in quake which is really satisfying with the weapon options. The pump shotgun and smg in particular are really enjoyable for what they are. And I just love the setting, colors, and somewhat dry humor the game has. Overall, very epic
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Super strong vibe, great ambience and fitting music. Gameplay's mostly good, though I'd probably slightly increase the supplies found in levels (or make them give more health/ammo), as the resources are pretty scarce for an action shooter like this, it's absolutely do-able, but can prove pretty difficult if things go haywire.Some sound effects are a bit weird, though that might be intentional, some guns (namely the shotgun) don't sound very punchy, crossbow has a funny sound to it too. Enemy variety is great, designs are interesting aswell. The level quality went up as I progressed, so can't wait for future content! So far, it's a pretty short experience, but packed with interesting content and detail, worth the buy and support, especially if you're into this depressing soviet vibe, like me.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the old graphics fool you, the motion of the ocean is very modern, a very unapologetic shooter, comfortable with its own existence and cocksure about its target market, much less than be said by much bigger projects!  Trigger Warning: Communism and Lenin and his bros etc but I think the protagonist might be insane.9/10 good game also this walking meme of a developer wrote this in Pascal, haha.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Looking great so far, deserves much more attention. Whats there is a very polished and atmospheric experience.I really like the enemy variety, there is quite a lot of them, all appropriately creepy. Shooting the baddies is satisfying, but sound effects could use a bit more punch.While the 50 shades of brown aesthetic might not be for everyone, it creates a heavy, oppressive feeling of dread. I love it.I live close to what was previously known as Czechoslovakia and I'm a sucker for this depticion of dystopian Soviet past. Guaranteed extra points from me for that.HROT is surprisingly interactive, with many destructible objects, switches and gibbing enemies. Good stuff, makes the levels a lot of fun to explore.Amazingly HROT is being developed by one developer. Thats very impressive given the results. Keep up the fantastic work Spytihněv.While the game is still far from finished, its definitely on the right track. If you like Quake and Dusk, then HROT is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is indescribable.When it started, I thought it was just some indie-shooter.And though I was right, it was so much more than that.The atmosphere tells the story of sorrow, pestilence, perseverance and humility, a lovingly crafted, if low poly recreation of many Czech landmarks and sights, sprinkled with culture and love.The combat is exhilerating, as to be expected of a boomer-shooter, but with a level of depth that many modern triple-A titles lack. The feeling of discovering that you can kick the Kejdovec's bombs back at them, both disarming them and setting them on fire for a slow but ammo efficient death is a feeling of discovery and joy I haven't felt since I was a child picking up my first controller.And the bossfights. Dear God the bossfights are awesome.There'S at least 1 per level and every single one has a unique design and aesthetic. My only complaint would be that they only have 1 or 2 attacks to their name, which may get tiring over the course of a bossfight, but the spectable these fights present in tandem with their quantity leads to nigh unforgettable experiences in numerous succession each chapter.I am only 28 hours into the game, having just completed episode 3, but this game has suprised, confused, shocked, and intrigued me to my very core. I will return to it again, searching for achievements and exploring the newly added bits of content, hungry for more. And I'd like to thank the developers for making this game as much as a particular friend of mine, who blessed me with its presence.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a genuinely old school FPS with a very strong 'You Are Empty' vibe to it. Not just because of the retro looking graphics either. The gameplay is decidedly yesteryear with secret areas, numerous enemies, labyrinthian levels, and sometimes obscure pathways on maps that can lead to running around in circles until you figure out which grate you didn't break or what turn was the wrong turn in the maze of corridors,HROT's simplicity is what makes the game so engaging and enjoyable. If you really enjoyed this type of run and gun shooter from the late 90's and early 00's you'll likely find yourself wondering where the time went when you sit down to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A humorous boomer shooter that's worth playing only if you're a fan of the genre. What keeps the game interesting in the 3 episodes is the gags and jokes the developers throw at you more so than the actual gameplay or the level design itself. In those aspects of the game it's pretty by the numbers. Because of that i didn't end up having a blast playing it, i was just admiring the uniqueness that it offered, i love the ending in particular. 6/10 (Decent)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Civvie was right, this really didn't need a boost. It's already very good.Despite being in early access, it has a good amount of content behind it. Not only do you have a solid roster of enemies to fight against, you have a solid arsenal of weapons you can utilize. You also have some pretty fun and creative ideas! Like how you can drive the motorcycles and interact with most objects on the map. I especially love the aesthetic and overall mood. It's achieved very well with its brown industrial look. And the fact that a custom game engine has this amount of polish behind it is honestly impressive. I've only came across one bug and that I died during the transition to the next level, and I was put back at the beginning of the previous level. My only major complaint is that there's no Windowed mode (as of writing this). Other than that, it's a very good game that you should definitely check out if you're into retro shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I like to think of myself as something of a shooter connoisseur.  Those of us who love shooters went through a dry spell during the ascendancy of the military CoD clone.  It was like being a wine snob stuck drinking nothing but Night Train out of a dixie cup.  The last five years or so has seen a resurgence of great FPS titles of all budgets, from the pure, white hot brilliance of Doom Eternal, to the janky atmospheric greatness of the Metro series, to the gaggle of fantastic retro/indie titles like Dusk, Amid Evil, Ultrakill, Project Warlock and others.As with any genre renaissance there was soon a bunch of other FPS games that sought to sell copies by copying what works in other games without having a feel for the details that make those games work.  Steam is littered with games that tried to capture what Dusk does but fail.HROT isn't one of those games.  This is a spectacular shooter because it drips with details and mechanics that show the dev loves FPS games.  I'll often judge indie/retro shooters by asking myself this, "What would I think of this game if it had modern graphics and AA production values?  What if this game looked like Metro Last Light or Necromunda Hired Gun?"HROT would be amazing with those production values because it's greatness is in it's combat, it's levels, it's balance, it's exploration, and it's world.  Nothing would please me more than finding out the dev who made this is working on a modern FPS title.Because it released well into the FPS revival HROT has flown under the radar a bit and that's a damn shame.  This is one of the best shooters of the last few years.  It's great not because it's a retro shooter, it's great because it's just a great shooter.If you like FPS games this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant shooter with lots of heart poured into it, extremely atmospheric with everything from the guns to the flavour text of the news clippings matching the ex Soviet block setting that the game nails so effortlessly.Level design is brilliant, with looping levels returning to previously explored areas (usually with a new gimmick or some new enemies added in) and keyhunting that feels just like the good ol' days.Buy it, play it, get addicted to it. From Česko with love.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic and level  design is amazing, but matched by Dusk's - the only thing that's superior about Hrot is its Soviet aesthetic (I love said aesthetic), which is subjective anyway. However, the game-play is so shallow it actually takes away from the aesthetics and level design.This game is certainly over-hyped, and overpriced considering how poor the game-play is.Maybe that's just me and my game-play oriented brain?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Rock Solid Brown Colored Quake-like Boomer Shooter. Lots of Brown Sewers, Brown Castles, Brown Caves, and Brown Corridors. Some Shake ups aesthetically might've been nice. This is the kinda game where all the little details make add up to something special. Like how every level takes direct inspiration a real place in Russia. When Duke Nukem 3D came out, gamers back then loved how levels felt like real places rather than abtract mazes. This is the natural evolution of that.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: They have just released episode 2, so in total it's a good 5 or 6 hours of play (included say half an hour on endless) hence there's already enough content to justify the purchase even if on Early Access. And the content, is spectacular. The level design is great, graphics are good, sound effects and music is top notch, mechanics are super - in my opinion it's one of the best retro shooters since Dusk (from which it borrows quite a bit, and it's not a bad thing).
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the new wave of retro shooter revivals this (and DUSK) stand at the very apex above the rest. From the authentic custom engine with polygon jitter to the impeccable gunplay, this game understands and executes on what made classic shooters from the 90s so great.The level design and combat in this game is fantastic. The varied enemies are dynamic to fight and the weapons are well balanced and a joy to use. It's one of those shooters that just "feels" right to play. While only one episode out of three is playable at the moment, the game shows great promise for what's to come. There has already been an update just a few days after launch that's added two new weapons and some tweaks based on player feedback.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are subjective but I enjoyed the visual style of Hrot very much. Music is good enough that I enjoyed it during the levels but wouldn't just listen to it on it's own. Level design is mostly good but some of the puzzles are impossible to figure out without a guide. The running and gunning is easily the best part of Hrot, the movement feels very similar to quake and the guns are super fun to use. Unfortunately some of the enemies in this game are pure bullet sponges and the combat gets bogged down when you need to land 3-4 direct hit grenades to kill 1 dude. (Wheelchair/Snake enemies on NORMAL) The game teeters between serious and goofy which didn't bother me but I feel compelled to warn you: don't expect a coherent tone or story. My first play-through of the game took me about 7 hours, I probably spent about an hour of that stuck on obscure puzzles. I'd estimate 6-10 hours to beat the game maybe 20-30 hours if you want to hunt down all the secrets and such. Overall I'm happy I picked this game up and I'd recommend it to anyone who likes "boomer shooters".
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is game where you feel comfortable yet weirded out. Gameplay is so responsive you think your character is you, while atmosphere and maps are so interesting and discomforting it keeps you on your toes. But you can see the dev had lots of fun with it. Highly recommend, really fun game. And tons of hours worth of content if you want to hunt achievements, secrets or higher difficulties. Great stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot really grew on me. I came for the boom-shoot, stayed for the Czech.Every level is absolutely stuffed with references to Czech culture and history, and it's wonderful.Gameplay is totally solid and enjoyable, but nothing groundbreaking. The real highlight of the game are the levels. In spite of the depressing color palette there is a big variety of real life locations, enemies, and fun stuff to do. I highly recommend reading up even a little bit of lore on the fandom wiki, it will enrich your experience.Two thumbs up for the music, fits very well. Sound effects are good, some weapons sound anemic, enemies are often funny (Zabít!).Graphics are authentically retro, no Unity plugins here.I will definitely have to visit Czechia one day.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Do You like Quake? Ohh, you’re certainly in luck. HROT got you covered. Brewing a couple of years in Early Access, HROT is a decent retro shooter. Developed by one man, which is an impressive feat. Unfortunately, the final product is pretty uneven. It has its moments, but it never feels consistent. HROT has no story - I guess there was an outline, but dev just abandoned the idea of any storytelling somewhere during Early Access.. This just adds to the feeling you’re just playing a collection of random levels.Gameplay wise, it’s a mixed bag. Most weapons really lack oomph, with Super Shogun saving the whole lineup. Level design is okay, with really strong Episode 2. Beside that? Sewers, lots of them. Standard key hunting, hugging walls to find a secret. Mostly solid experience. Got a few cheap shots in the back from across the map or projectiles passing through textures. Like I said - mostly solid.I had fun with HROT, but I really do love Quake. I think it has a big influence on my perspective. Well, Dusk still reigns as an undisputed king of retro shooters/boomer shooters. HROT is nowhere near, but it’s still fine. Buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT uses a palette of browns and grays and the very industrial/brutalist architecture of late 80's Czechia. In the hands of lesser developers, this would have wound up as a disappointing Chasm: The Rift wannabee, but Spytihněv is an artist and HROT serves to be an incredible FPS, with level design that shows a true understanding of arenas, and an artistic eye that understands how to utilize a 'drab' palette and make a legible, tight, Quake-like.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: So far it does everything I wanted for as retro style fps or boomer shooter. Great smooth movements, great artstyle, good selection of weapons and great level design. Some might be put off the brown look but honestly with the ambient sound it works well and it does not feel like a quake clone as some may say. Would recommend for anyone into this genre of games even if its in early access.Only issue is the horse is nightmare fuel......
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A wholly unique experience among modern retro shooters! From the visuals (don't let the brownness scare you away), to the Czech setting and crazy gimmicks found in every level. It's most reminiscent of those janky but ambitious FPS titles you'd see from Eastern Europe, but infused with so much creativity and clear passion that you just can't help but love it! If you think Quake meets S.T.A.L.K.E.R. turned up to 11 on the goofy-scale sounds fun at all, then I simply can't recommend this enough!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what else to tell you. This is a one man, episodic project (of which only episode 1 has been released so far). Updates, whilst regular, are not huge content drops and episode 2 might take a while yet. Still, the attention to detail in this game is amazing and I'm glad I supported its development by buying early.Edit: I'm glad to announce that as of two days ago, episode 2 is now available in full and a third, final episode is in the works.Edit #2: Full release happened on the 16th of May 2023, a total EA success story.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's only 2 episodes in its development and it just keeps getting better, the recent 2nd episode blows the 1st one out of the water in terms of pacing , fantastic creepy thick atmosphere, great level design and just variety that keeps it from becoming dull.Visually it's like an even more brown Quake 1, yeah that's possible to achieve apparently but it works to set the mood I'd say. The gameplay is not really fully Quak-y and it even has some blood/duke nukem 3d injected into its style too, it has kind of a slower pace to it though and you can't jump all that high as you usually can in most old school shoot games. Ammo is also far more scarce in this game compared to other boom shots, it at times can very much feels more like a horror game almost but it's still more into classic boom shooting old school action than spookiness, granted this recent 2nd episode def. leaned more into horror than the 1st episode and i loved it.Only thing that's lacking in Hrot are a fair share of the gun sound effects I'd say, They're fairly weak sounding and could use improvements, especially the SMG and Pistol sound effects.But yeah give it a go, if you want a more spooky old school shooter it's worth checking this out.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: (Still in early access)Super slick FPS with great controls. Gives you quake vibes but has its own personality. updateJust played latest version as of today... the new weapons are great, and after playing a few other games I forgot how fast and clean this game feels to move around in. It really captures the speed of the old 90s early 2Ks FPS games along with great weapons and fun shooting. The levels are kinda mazes and that is fine, but sometimes everything looking similar can throw off your sense of direction as you can't tell if you have been there before or not. Trouble finding keys and new areas with the backtracking can slow down the combat a little. Maze like level design is also a note taken from the retro FPS and can be interesting.I really like games like this and wish a lot of success to the developer, and hope to see more from them in the future! Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great there are some flaws that are pretty major- The saving system requires you save before any major event at any point, because of that you find yourself playing through having fun and boom! back to the very beginning of the level because you forgot to go into the menu and hit save.- Important things and drops are very hard to differentiate between useless items on the floor making you walk toward things you didn't need to wasting time.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT stands proudly among DUSK, Amid Evil, Ion Fury and CULTIC when it comes to the boomer shooter craze of the past few years. If you want a retro inspired shooter that does not mind to get a little weird, than there should be 0 hesitation and you should play this game. Even though some enemy designs and locations seem very random, most of them are well thought out pieces of culture and/or nods to folklore from the Czech Republic. Apart from that, the game plays like a forgotten game running on the Quake engine during the PS1 era. Which in this case is a very good thing. There's tons of secrets, interesting enemies to fight and cool level gimmicks that keep you guessing about what's up ahead. The depressing atmosphere and haunting music are very well made. Safe to say, I love this game. So if you call yourself a fan of single player FPS games, you should not be reading this. You should be playing HROT.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, old-school FPS with great atmosphere and lots of tongue-in-cheek humour (especially for those of us who grew up in the former Eastern Bloc) practically on par with other retro hits such as Dusk, etc. Levels are complex and fun, the soundtrack is spot on. I'd only like the guns to sound a bit meatier :-) Otherwise, an all-round great early access experience. Can't wait for the next episodes to come. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic addition to the Boomer Shooter niche and beyond weird throughout. As an American, i get very few of these references, but the game is fantastic to play through. It controls super well as a Quake-like and the levels are fantastic. Act 3 is the highlight of the game, but you get the weirdness throughout beforehand as well. If you liked Dusk or things like that, you are going to love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: id give hrot roughly a 7.5/10 from what ive played so far (edit: ive now completed the game up to the end of the second episode which is all that is available at this time) . its still a very fun retro shooter with some unique enemies and a very moody atmosphere that rides the line nicely between all out action and tension. There is also a decent amount of tongue in cheek humor that helps offset the complete lack of narrative (the plot is even more sparse then doom or quake for reference) my biggest complaint and what i think holds it back the most is its overly strict adherence to retro fps dogma. i think it could benefit from distinguishing itself a little more from the likes of quake or dusk. nothing wrong with sticking to a formula that works but i think especially in the weapons department its a bit bland. overall however id recommend picking it up if you enjoy retro shooters, especially if its ever on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Czech yourself before you wreck yourself.Often compared to Quake or Chasm: The Rift, and sometimes referred to as "Slav DUSK", HROT is a retro FPS in the vein of the aforementioned titles, running on a custom engine derived from the archaic Pascal engine for maximum visual crust, and uniquely set in 1986, Soviet-era Czechoslovakia, and rife with historical and cultural nods thereof- some obvious, such as the protagonists' choice of a sickle as melee weapon, others far less so.An unspecified disaster has struck the city of Prague, malevolent, gas-masked goons, attack dogs, hideous mutants and more stalk the streets, and someone has left a lot of bagged semi-skim milk lying around. What is an upstanding armed socialist to do? If you have played any FPS in the last thirty years or at all, you can probably guess.HROT plays exactly like it should, with reasonably speedy movement, no penalties to accuracy from moving, and the only weapon that needs reloading is the pistols, Duke Nukem 3D-style. There are secret areas and keys to find, switches to flick, sequences to complete and doors that open elsewhere- HROT feels familiar but not at all formulaic, and it's overwhelmingly brown color palette is not only in keeping with is inspirations, but also serves to readily evoke the oppressive Eastern Bloc aesthetic. This is complimented by various CSSR-era statuary, propaganda posters and signs, as well as locations based on Czech landmarks, such as the basilica at Fort Vysehrad. All written text is in Czech, but you can simply walk up to them and press Use to have them translated into English via subtitles, and hopefully other languages down the line for other folks. In addition, the soundtrack is minimalist but atmospheric.In addition to the expected steam guides for weapons, secrets and achievements, there is also a guide for this game that explains many of the cultural references for the curious. You can find said guide here: The map design feels similar to DUSK as well, with layouts that make enough sense, flowing from fight to switch and back again, that you rarely get stuck, which was a problem for me back in head-wracking mazes like Descent and DOOM 2. I got stuck maybe once in HROT's first episode, and's only because I forgot to check an obvious spot on the last level for a third valve wheel.Only one episode, "Kiss me Gustav" was initially available when I first wrote this review. Now it is fully released, and I would say that HROT is in the upper tier of retro FPSes. Episode 2, "The Degustation" and Episode 3 "The Gastroscopy" have been added, each featuring new enemies, mechanics and Czech historical and cultural references not seen in the first episode.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Comparisons with Quake, with which HROT’s user reviews apparently abound, are somewhat unfortunate. Outside its surface level visual similarities, or some of its weapons or enemies that evoke their analogues from Quake, this is a somewhat different sort of FPS. One certainly won’t find Quake’s movement or verticality here. Rather, HROT is closer to Chasm: The Rift if latter offered more variations in height within maps. Take away Chasm’s dismemberments and sprinkle the maps with some cute Buildesque interactivity, and you’ll have some image of what HROT is as a game. And as the sort of FPS it is trying to be, it is very good indeed: weapons are satisfying in their functionality and visual feedback (audio leaves something to be desired but this is something the dev is actively working on improving), and most of them play useful roles rather than being gimmicks or feeling obsolete after one finds shinier piece latter on. Enemies are varied in their looks and behaviour, and none of them are bullet-spongey. Maps are well designed, with character, with semi Build-style realistic-locales as opposed to Quake’s abstractions.All this is set in this gray concrete nightmare, the world of Soviet brutalist tenements and industrial spaces, of smoke-covered skies, of deformed life. The world wherefrom everything natural and beautiful is exiled. Such environment is violence on its own so that explosions of orgiastic violence of which game such as this consists can feel only fitting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, like really good. The only reason people stopped playing shooters like this after the 90s is because people stopped making them. I for one am glad they're coming back. HROT has nailed every bit of 90s shooter aesthetic and the custom engine handles it so well. The lighting, textures and sound design are a particular treat. The soundtrack is a great mix of 80s synth/early industrial and really fits well. The enemies are varied and the models are period appropriate and look awesome. The boss battles are on the easy side but the bosses themselves are crazy and often hilarious. If you've played any game inspired by Romero then the weapons will seem familiar and comfortable with no one gun ever truly replacing another, just fitting the situation better.Only episode 1 is available right now with more on the way, it feels like the shareware version before ordering the diskette in the mail. It still has replay-ability in this state though, lots of secrets to find in the levels and an endless wave mode to round it out. The asking price could seem steep for 2-3 hours of current content but I was happy to help get this game realized. I can't wait for episode 2.Edit: Just a reminder that you can nomiate Hrot for categories during The Steam Awards.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game couple of minutes ago and I gotta say...HOLY S**T THIS GAME WAS F*****G AWSOME ! I've had so much fun playing this game and it was a pleasure to play this game. The sound was pretty good, the models were pretty good, the maps were pretty good, everything about this game was awsome.Is it worth buying it? Yes its abso-f*****g-lutely worth buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Good:+ Nice aesthetics+ Ambiance and the music are alright so far+ Interesting enemy designsBad:- Placements for ammo and health don't feel like they were really designed around a pistol start on Hard. It's not uncommon to run out of ammo entirely even with smart management and not missing targets. Compare it to DUSK or Quake for how item placement should work.- Collision doesn't work in a lot of places. Ogres can shoot grenades through floors above you (why) and guard rails don't block you or enemies from walking through them.- Save for two weapons, the sound design and damage of the weapons are mediocre. Direct hitting a popcorn enemy with a rocket would gib them in any other game.- Since there's reloading there should be a button to manually do it, and an indicator for how much is left in the magazine. Why this isn't in to begin with is beyond me.Just play DUSK or Ultrakill honestly, HROT is overhyped. Even for an early access release this has a lot of problems that should have been ironed out before being listed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great, its atmosphere is something else. You of course feel like an unstoppable killing machine that most retro throwbacks make you feel like, but there's certain moments where you begin to doubt this as it just goes into horror . This is just one episode right now and Im so excited to see the others when they get released. If you like quake and dusk, you'll absolutely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Good retro gaming, decent levels, reasonable weapons.Some issues were tight enclosed boss battles with ridiculous numbers of respawning enemies and a lot of strafing.  Seemed a bit repetitive and not challenging as much as it was wearing me down when I happened to die near the end of the battle and had to start it all over again.   I like a challenge but not the same thing over and over.Seemed too easy to find enough ammo and I always seemed to have good health even on the hardest level.  So it seemed skewed a bit too far to "easy" in my opinion.Some secrets seemed to be hidden too well and you had to stop in a room and scan all the bricks to see the ONE that was different from the rest or you had to make sure to touch every wall everywhere to find hidden stashes.  That was more time wasting than satisfying.It was fun to play but I'm not sure it was as good as I wanted it to be.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A 156 MB package of brown minimalismUnder the drab dreary exterior lies an expertly crafted shooter. This could easily have been just simply ugly but the map/art designers tread the needle by making it all just barren and low poly enough that it mimicks any psychos bad indie game map design or the genuine low budget eastern european article and yet theres intent and skill involved. Its quite strange.Beyond that it was just fun to play. It took me ~3 hours to beat with each level maybe lasting 20 minutes but it felt longer and just right at the same time. Good stuff and i hope they can keep this up with the next episodes
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT works for me on two layers. For one, it's a lovingly crafted throwback 90's fps shooter, with fast, fluid and satisfying combat, bonus points for running on a custom engine witten in Pascal. And for two, as a proud slav living in Prague, I can't appreciate enough the attention to detail in regards to the actual locations recreated in the game, as well soviet era signs, statues, appliances, cars etc... Not to mention a lot of little interactive easter eggs.In my opinion, that attention to detail is what separates HROT from other modern "boomer shooters".Can't wait for more updates/episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a "Boomer Shooter" FPS developed by Spytihněv; developed in the vein of older FPS games like Quake and the like. Recently it came out of Early Access, I had it sitting in my library for a while (shout to Sabwones for the game!) but I wanted to wait until it fully came out to truly give it a spin.I'll start with the story since there isn't too much in the way; you're in 1986 (according to the steam page) Soviet Union (specifically the Czech Republic as multiple mentions of Prague were in the game) as you find your socialist country surrounded by invaders. You decide to go out and kill these invaders and that's kind of it that I was able to find  as well as mentions of how  Other than that, for the most part any lore is kind of spread apart, which is fine cause I was mostly focused on the gameplay and atmosphere. The Gameplay was great, more throwback shooter gameplay with secrets, boss battles, and the such. Truth be told, I don't really have much to say here that the likes of DUSK, Quake and other shooters like this haven't already done. What I can tell you are some of the more noticeable things that popped in my mind; some of the levels in the first episode when ramping up can be on the confusing side in terms of layout but the more the episodes go on the better it gets, shift is a giant kick which you can use to both kick enemies and enemy grenades back and when timed right it feels amazing. I think Episode 3 is my favorite just from how insane it really gets, from fighting Salamanders or Otters with giant guns to the ability to save adorable dogs from cages to murder attacking enemies (which was my favorite part of the game, you can indeed pet the dog in this game). Other things to mention is that driving around the motorcycle is a lot of fun running people over, and also to keep an eye on your environment because this game will surprise the hell out of you real quick with enemies (mainly static vehicles coming to life to try to run you over). The double barreled shotgun will be your best friend along with the grenade launcher; and I guess the final note I can throw down is that you can interact your environment like opening cabinets to find ammo and in some levels keys, of which like other old school first person shooters you need to open doors that leads to the end of the level. For the last stage of Episode 3,  Last thing, I tried with everything but no rocket jump that I could find, so unless I'm dumb as s h i t don't even bother to do it cause it won't work.The Atmosphere/Art Design/Everything else for the most part was solid; at first the drab tone kind of got on my nerves a bit, especially with the sewer levels in Episode 1 (titled Kiss Me Gustav) but the more I played (mostly from Episode 2 and 3), the better it got and the more variation it had in it's environments. Keep in mind, I love oppressive atmospheres, It just took a while for me to get adjusted. Graphics look like Quake and other old shooters and as a simp for old throwback games I love it, the enemy designs are great environments whilst samey looking for the most part change up later on. The only criticism I have in this part is that two of the weapons, the Pistol and Machine Gun, feel under powered like a pea shooter; while I understand the pistol is supposed to be a weak weapon you have as a backup I don't really like it as a weapon mainly due to the fact that even if it's weak that it should still pack some sort of feeling. Otherwise, honestly this section is the strongest part of the game; it has it's identity in the sea of browns and blacks and it's not afraid to really get the Soviet aesthetic down.To finish off my thoughts, if you like old school throwback shooters than I feel like most people would like HROT; it's gameplay of finding keys and opening doors, interacting with the environment in small but interesting ways, shooting your way through strange creatures, etc. I enjoyed my time playing HROT, it has a unique personality with it's own inside jokes that I don't totally understand (like getting a recipe for food at the end of each Episode? Strange but made me chuckle) but I appreciate the hell out of, it grew on me the more I played and to me was it's best at Episode 3 . Is it worth your time and money? I thought it was good enough to get my money's worth but I guess 6 hours for 20 dollars depends on what you really find to be worth the price. It's unique and it deserves it's place in the Boomer Shooter pantheon, and a must play for the h o e s like me that love retro stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd use the word "charming" to describe a Quake-inspired FPS but here we are. HROT oozes personality, don't be fooled by the prevalence of the color brown. Sure, environments will start to look samey after a while, but the bestiary, the sound design, and the level design will all keep you on your toes or put a smile on your face. The pacing is fantastic and the game knows when to end the show. Fantastic!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's a weird and ultimately boring Quake. The level design is bland, the enemies suck, the music and sound effects are repetitive and overall just terrible.Dusk is infinitely better, but even then you should play Cultic or something: HROT does not compare whatsoever. In fact, it's plainly mediocre.Also, whatever the f**k is up with the puppies/dogs in the game and their sounds -- the game developer should be put in jail for it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pobaví, postraší (dej si to na Spalovače mrtvol když to hraješ poprvý :D), plno detailů, skvělej oldschool feeling, dobrej pocit ze zbraní, možná by to chtělo výbušnější zvuky u brokády.Hlavně dodělej víc kapitol, máš to skvělý.Žeru i hudbu, atmošku a to surrealistický prostředí. Přijde mi jako bych byl ve snu.Pros:-Great weapon/movement feeling-Action packed-Creative boss design-Scary and funny-Music/atmosphere-Surreal enviroments-Attention to detail-Boomer ShooterCons:-Maybe some weapons have weak sounds-Lack of new enemies but i expect there to be some more/different ones in the next chapters.-Bosses are easy even on hardest difficulty
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT's greatest strengths are its compelling level design, it's frenetic combat, and its oddball charm and humour. Levels are meticulously crafted to nudge the player along while still providing a sense of exploration and creativity. Combat is meaty and satisfying, with a unique arsenal of weapons and a very creative spread of enemies. The game's tone and sense of humour is very eclectic and may not be to everyone's tastes, but I found its political satirization and ridiculous style extremely funny. A fantastic retro FPS that shouldn't be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful!  As someone who played Duke Nuk'em, Doom, and Blood through the '90's, this game is awesome.  I know all the levels on the games I mentioned.  This game plays like the ID engine with levels that at times seem familiar, but are unknown to me.  I could play this for days.There was that point in video games, and fps games that ID lead around the turn of the century.  This period where the graphics weren't great, but the games rocked.  These guys have captured this time in gaming wonderfully.  Congrats!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Quite an interesting game, I liked somethings like the dancing geckos and the game is pretty good about not running around in circles looking for keys. I do wish it went a little harder in any direction. Scarier and more surreal areas and more gags would be nice, I've played a couple boomer shooters and I think this one is worth your time if you enjoy the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This title is a masterpiece. I played the game when it only had one chapter and I already had a weakness for the game back then. But I didn't know what plans the developers had for the game and they brought the game to near perfection. This is a FPS retro shooter set in Czechoslovakia in 1986. The game contains 3 chapters, each chapter ends with a crazy boss fight, and that's not to mention the bonus content, which is also plenty. I can warmly recommend the game.10/10 .
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: i've just finished main quake campaign and started looking for something similar (besides official quake DLC's). stumbled into this thing and instantly loved it. perfect quake-alike retro fps shooter. as a guy from former soviet union counrty i can say that atmosphere is kickass. nailed it.  obviously level design is still kinda raw, i guess it requires more decoration/interior/attention to small details, but all and all, for an early acces game it's great!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Now I know what you're thinking... I thought the same when I first saw this game in the Store."Someone's ripped off Quake again".But this is actually a completely fresh game that has been written using a new engine (apparently in Pascal). While it is very Quake like in appearance and feel, it's actually a completely new story set in Soviet era Czechoslovakia.This game is Early Access, so you may want to wait until the completed game is developed before committing to a purchase, but if you like games like Quake, Half - Life, etc. then this is definitely worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most clear focused games to come out of the retro styled fps wave, everything feels fantastic, the world design is simultaneously beautiful and oppressive. Atmosphere is a highlight: the ambient sounds, lore, music, level design and enemy design all create a cohesive narrative of CSSR post Chernobyl Czech misery and accurately expresses a wide stretch of Czechoslovakian culture -to my knowledge-. Whether you're the type to get lost in a virtual world or just want to blow chunks out of vile creatures with a fantastically satisfying armoury, this game ~will~ be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the first episode. Really excellent retro shooter that feels like Chasm and Quake mixed. The bleak Soviet setting is also really great. Very interesting maps and enemies.The only areas I'd want to see tweaked are:Overall fantastic game that I had a blast playing. Very strongly recommend to fans of boomer shooters. Can't wait for the next episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: For a game in Early Access, this is impressively smooth to play.  Bleak and cheeky in tone, the levels are well-crafted and the gameplay is remarkably balanced between punishing and fair.  The enemy types are all charismatic, particularly the bosses, and the weapons handle exceptionally.  Certainly one of the most focused of the recent glut of retro-shooters, HROT lands firmly between Quake and Blood with the tone of Silent Hill.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pair this up with Cultic and you have a bundle of some genuinely awesome boomer shooters within the past year. Takes a lot of guts to try to design fun water segments in basically every level, and it succeeds on every front. I'm in love with the weird as hell enemies with gas masks that just get progressively weirder.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good old-school shooter in the vein of quake with a very specific (and to me, entertaining) sense of humor. It's not the best of the bunch, but it's solid. The enemy variety is good and keeps things fresh episode to episode (many staple enemies combined with various few level specific ones). The weapon variety is ok; it's perhaps too similar to quake and I wish it had one or two oddball weapons. The level design ranges from great to average in most cases, but a few levels feel like samey mazes. Also the secrets often suck, as while a lot of them are well thought out, equally as many of them feel very "original Wolfenstein" inspired (mash the use button on walls). I will say my time is mainly due to secret hunting and achievements, as otherwise the game isn't too long (though I think the price is appropriate to its length).Overall, if you liked quake or dusk, I don't think you can go wrong with this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: it's a great game with gloomy atmosphere, strange enemies, great music and sounds, smooth controls and satisfying combat. it's a little bit of Quake, a little bit of You are empty, really. what makes it even more amazing, that it was developed in Pascal. never thought that Pascal is capable of anything like this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Great atmosphere. Interesting setting. Simultaneously funny and unsettling bosses.Cons: Lack of variety in enemy patterns leads to unengaging combat. Limited color palette makes levels difficult to navigate. The "puzzles" often involve endlessly walking around the map looking for the item you missed (either a valve, lever, or electrical box). Verdict: I look forward to seeing how the project turns out, and will play other episodes when they are released. With only the first lackluster episode currently available, there's not enough here to warrant a purchase yet.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly executed love letter to the game design and the art of the 90s first-person shooters. However, what sets this game apart, is the brilliant commentary of the Czech history and the fact it features real-life and topically relevant locations (you can visit). Oozing with references in a very idiosyncratic, well-versed, and witty way, HROT's a step above the typical addition into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know much about Czechoslovakia (even though I may be part Czech) but this is Czech DUSK and is just as much fun if not more-so.It is in early access, with its first two chapters available now and a third to come out some time in the future. I hope the final chapter will come alongside some refinements, like the railings that aren't actually real, or the weird paths the enemy likes to take as they approach you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat decent Quake/Dusk/Chasm: The Rift inspired indie shooter, with a bit of potential. Like most early access games, this one's a bit rough and severely lacking the materials of being a full release, alongside with needing to iron out a few issues.The enemies are ok and are fitting for the game's art-style at a certain extent, some of them felt underdeveloped and the boss encounters were rushed and underwhelming. Some of the enemy designs were a bit lazy and are more on the goofy side, than the intimidating end of the spectrum, they took me right out of the game whenever I was getting immersed. Granted a game doesn't have to be too serious, especially when it has slightly cartoon-ish graphics and very janky animations, but from how the game presents itself as being this bleak, lonely and oppressive scenario, sometimes putting in goofy additions like hostile, gas mask-wearing horses to such a world might not work as well as intended. Unless if everything were shown or explained to have been changed through mutation and technological experimentation. Also the snakes can take at least several times the amount of punishment a foot soldier can, for some reason.The music and ambience gets a thumbs up from me, they suit the game's dreary tone and loneliness pretty well, although the overall colour palette could use a little bit more variety - HROT is probably the brownest game in existence. I know it's a style choice to make the game look that way - However seeing nothing but brown environments for hours on end can get very tiring and monotonous.The level design is pretty solid, the secrets are 'well' hidden; if not a bit too convoluted and few and far between and you won't be able to find most of them if you aren't using the map. Most maps have a lot of thought and detail crafted into them, I would also say the same about the placement of their secrets. The issue that I have with these secrets, is that most of them have a tendency to reward far too little and aren't worth searching for most of the time, especially in more desperate scenarios.The game runs well and plays okay. There aren't any bugs that I have encountered so far, except for enemies clipping through grated floors, unless if that was intentional. Drowning can apparently damage your armour and you won't be getting that health back, when it should regenerate after getting damaged by the drowning. There were times that it felt like that the game was trying to be a fast paced shooter like Quake or Dusk, while at the same time, trying to be a Survival Horror; Health items are very scarce and seldom abundant, especially the armour. To some degree, that contradicts with the game's fast-pace oriented action. If the game is going to take the Survival Horror route, then being able to move slower and crouch behind cover would be nice. Enemies are also weird when it comes to trying to avoid their gunfire, it's as though they know where you are at all times and will instantly shoot if they see one pixel of your character out of cover, feels like their aim is tracking you from behind solid walls/cover and is quite cheap and frustrating, rather than challenging. It does add an element of unpredictability for the enemy encounters and happens to make the gameplay more dynamic. Personally I think a bit more fine-tuning may be needed, like enemies being unable to pin-point your exact location, after breaking out of their line of sight for a certain amount of time.My least preferable aspect of the game is the weapons, not only did they feel under-powered, but they also have some of the worst sound design I've heard in a while, even in an indie game. But I did like the shotgun and how satisfying it felt and sounded. The SMG is useless, the pistol being more accurate and useful than the sub-machine gun didn't really make sense to me - Since SMGs are supposed to be pistols on steroids. The only weapon I solely use in the majority of episode 1 is the shotgun (and the grenade launcher and sometimes the pistol), I could just hide behind a door and shoot at every enemy that tries to swagger in. You can get stronger weapons but they appear much later in episode 1, they were probably hidden in some secret I missed, considering how convoluted the said secrets are. The crossbow, of which I'm assuming is the rail gun equivalent of HROT, was pretty bare bones and boring design-wise, including the lightning gun. Like the enemies, I think they need a better introduction to the player and more depth into the game's universe, but that's just me.The game has flaws and I wasn't really impressed by it's dull and janky stature. But to the game's merit, there were a few aspects that I liked, such as the lonely bleak feeling, decent gameplay, music and level design. But beyond that, there's not really much that would make this game stand out from the rest and look less bare-bones than it already is. And I know the game is still in Early Access, but sheesh, this turkey really needs more time to cook in the oven. Lastly, I think the dev needs to present and catalogue his additions and updates to the game in a less subtle manner; I never noticed that these new levels even existed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Seems promising so far. I really enjoyed what there currently is of the campaign. Endless mode is enjoyable too, but everything seems a little barebones given the early access state of course.Some things I'm a little turned off by- Some of the guns feel boring and week. I found myself mainly using the pump-shotgun the entire game because it seems to be the best weapon for good damage and the ammo is everywhere.- Boss fights are pretty dull. They all followed the same pattern of chase, jump around, and shoot at you. - Enemies are very same-y feeling too. There's very little telegraphing from enemy attacks which makes it pretty hard to dodge attacks.- I often found myself low on health in most missions, which wasn't really a problem, but there's a constant heartbeat sound that plays and gets very annoying.I overall really enjoyed the experience, despite how short it was. I wish it was a little cheaper, but as long as more content is planned then I should hopefully change my mind about that bit.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I've had of the recent batch of retro shooters that have been coming out lately. Even though Dusk and the like were excellent, there's just something very satisfying about the game that's hard to put my finger on. The idea alone is brilliant. A late Soviet-era Quake with gasmasked horses and cybernetic Lenin heads as enemies, set against a menacing backdrop of unspecified disaster which seems to have zombified the populace and left a swirling black void in the heavens. It sounds dumb, but it holds together very well, and while the primary mood is one of horror the little touches of humour are really well-integrated and constantly surprising.Of course a game like this lives or dies on its gameplay, and in this regard it doesn't disappoint. The map design is particularly excellent, focusing on tight maze-like environments that double back on themselves at key points to avoid backtracking or aimless wandering. Music is also very highly polished and fits the atmosphere perfectly, transitioning from creepy background synths that set a unsettling mood to more driving pieces that get the blood pumping whenever certain key moments are triggered. Weapons generally feel tight and and enemies and environments are varied enough that you'll find yourself adapting your tactics on the fly. Things aren't perfect in this regard (shotgun ammo is a little too plentiful right now, and a couple of the enemies need tweaking to make them more of a challenge) but hopefully these things will be improved in the final version. At higher difficulties the game can feel challenging but thanks to a lack of hitscan enemies it never feels cheap or unfair. I have no idea what the final two episodes will be like, but if they continue to develop in this vein while developing the nightmarish atmosphere so effectively built up in this first episode we're going to be in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on Hard Difficulty. VERY BROWN in a lot of ways. Has graphics reminiscent of Quake. Runs smooth as silk. Don't even recall ever seeing a hitch. Guns are pretty standard and the pistol and machine gun sound fx aren't punchy at all. Everything else is ok. Gameplay overall is pretty fun and challenging. The few times you find powerups like quad damage or shoot twice as fast, it's pretty fun. Motorcycle is kinda silly but it doesn't hurt the game at all. Story is almost nonexistent and told more through the environment/scenery. Enemies are weird but fun to fight. Bosses are even weirder but still fun.All in all if you're a fan of the retro style shooter craze that's been going on in the past few years, especially from the early 3d era of quake, you'll get a lot of fun out of this. It's maybe a tad short on Hard. I beat it in 8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is both the creepiest and funniest boomer shooter to come out of this seemingly-never ending parade of throwback games. The utter lack of even the slightest CRUMB of story means that every level is completely unpredictable. Fighting a gorilla dual wielding rocket launchers or a possessed pommel horse? Cool. Rocking out with bipedal newts headbanging to trap music? Awesome. Exploring a crypt haunted by someone's dead grandmother? Why the ♥♥♥♥ not, I love it.Through all of that the developer shows this constant simultaneous love and disdain for his country. Some will get more from the social commentary than others, but even knowing very little it made me snort with amusement throughout. And let me just say...American developers? We need more games where every boss is a mutated and or superpowered version of our politicians. It would be very therapeutic to fight Mecha-Trump or Spider-Biden. Anyway, this is 10/10. Now please add workshop support so it can live forever.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, charming and fluid retro shooter game that has quite the appeal especially for Czech audience.+ Fluid, smooth gunplay and movement you would expect from a shooter like this.+ Excellent weapon variety. Not too many but those that are there are all useful.+ Graphics, artstyle and music is excellent.+ The biggest plus for me personally is all the communist Czechoslovakia imagery.+ Game is well priced for what it offers. Decent length, doesnt overstay its welcome.+ Runs very well on everything.+ I liked the interactivity. You can ride a bike, interact with many many things.- I felt like bossfights were all easy. I had more trouble with some enemy groups than with bosses.- Sometimes enemies can nuke you almost unfairly but its nothing major.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Best Orloj Simulator on the market right know. The detail of simulation for the clock is amazing! Intricate animations, switching times, adjusting for moons and of course the most important bit - the apostle procession!  Good thing one can scare the pigeons off before they foul the grand square as well.10/10 clock experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent retro FPS that fans of Quake in particular will love. The game's unique setting and atmosphere is well-crafted, and Episode 2 introduces new locations and enemies yet feels grounded within the same world. The overall quality is consistent across the two episodes currently released, and perhaps even increased in Episode 2. I was initially concerned about the need to collect keys to open doors and progress, as I generally think it's a dated mechanic that needs to die, but it's never excessive here and will never have you lost and wandering aimlessly. Rather, it intelligently guides the player through the superb level design, provides an indication of progress, and keeps gameplay flowing. Enemy design is interesting and the game is excellently balanced. The lore, humour and creative gameplay sequences--such as motorcycle and minecart riding--injected into each level never feels over the top or like a gimmick. I look forward to Episode 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best Quake-like boomer-shooter of recent memory. Edges out Amid Evil for me by a bit, and Dusk doesn't even come close. Visually it it's atmospheric, I'll admit, but I found it a bit dull and suffocating with 99 shades of brown being dominant. However, with the game's unique sense of humour and the unreasonably fun combat, my 15 hours with it went by very fast. If you enjoy Quake 1, this is a must-play and if you don't, you should still give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it from the moment I started playing it. It's tense, bleak, and downright claustrophobic in certain areas, but that's what keeps me coming back for more. Similar games have trouble with enemy placement when it comes to switching between open areas and tight corridors; they'll haphazardly fill a hallway with enemies strictly for the challenge of it while your arsenal is full to bursting. HROT focuses more on keeping you armed, but not comfortably so, sprinkling enough enemies in the appropriate environments to keep you on your toes. Cockiness is costly, especially on higher difficulties. The color palette and gunplay are very Quake-like, but unlike Quake, the world feels like it could actually exist (also, the shotgun is usually a make or break weapon for me when it comes to boomer shooters, and the shotgun in this game absolutely rocks).The only con for me would be the enemy jumping, which can be jarring at times. If an enemy is below you, and there is a platform of any height in front of them, they will continuously try to jump onto it, even if it's five or ten feet above them. Sometimes they make it, sometimes they don't, but either way it can be a little distracting in the middle of a fight.Overall great game. If you're into boomer shooters, this is a fine pick (I'd personally rate this above Wrath).

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is the funniest and most original game that came out within the new retro shooter wave.It constantly throws curve balls at you and adds new elements. _childDocuments_.review: This game is proof you don't need a big budget, a franchise license, a huge team, or a game engine license to make a fun, engaging, and at times hilarious game.  Sure, you've played the original Quake (if you haven't, go play that right now!) but have you played Quake set in 1986 Czechoslovakia? This is a passion project and it shows in the details. I love a game that has a toilet, but one with a working model train set?  Yes please,  This game was built using a custom game engine, and the footprint is only around 250MB!  I did not type that wrong, that's megabytes not gigabytes.  It ran flawlessly with no crashes or slow downs (what big budget studio can say that?).  Sure, you can ramble on about the sound design and the graphics but at the end of the day, that is what the dev wanted and they achieved their vision.  And they achieved their vision in a quarter of a gigabyte.In summary, this game is exactly what it says on the tin.  If you are not interested by the description, move along.  I can't make you like this game.  However, if the premise intrigues you I can promise you this game does not disappoint.  GIve the demo a try first.  I knew within the first 5 minutes of gameplay I wanted to buy this.

Very brown, blocky, and depressing aesthetic that perfectly captures the feel of soviet industrial / government buildings. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, HROT is a good game that should be a blast for anyone into retro shooters. One of the most enjoyable parts of the game for me was the bleak atmosphere and mysterious setting but sad part with that is that for me it doesn't really see a satisfying payoff. There's a lot of interesting and quirky moments in HROT but it never really reaches the heights that DUSK, one of its inspirations does.

_childDocuments_.review: I never knew I needed a moody soviet fps in my life until I played this game. Although the game's color palette is quite brown, it matches the atmosphere perfectly. The music only adds to this and really makes you feel like a stranger in a strange land. You've got some very weird and strange enemies that only add to the mystery of what happened. There are some objects that you can examine to get little bits and pieces of lore, which I can appreciate. You have a great variety of weapons here too, and if I had to gripe about something, the smg sounds like a pea shooter and there's no real 'umph' to it. Besides that, very solid early access, I am excited to see what we'll get once the other episodes released.

_childDocuments_.review: I' m a big fan of retro shooters, especially ones that resemble Quake. But with all the other retro shooters out there, I found myself asking: When will someone make a game that lets me fight a mutated version of ex-leader of Communist Czechoslovakia Klement Gottwald? Well folks, finally, I have an answer to that question- Hrot! Unnerving atmosphere, strong resemblance to the original Quake, iconic Cold War-era Czech weapons, but with a few surprises as well.  One particularly good feature was giving enemies the ability to jump, meaning that they can reach you on ledges. I know it's early access so here are a few suggestions that would make this game perfect:1- Better sound for gunfire and other weapons. The shotgun's not bad but the other weapons need louder sounds. The first time a fired a Vz-52 on a range, some people on the neighboring lane exclaimed: "That Vz sounds like a cannon!" 2- More ammo, maybe balance with more enemies. 3- I'd say do away with reloading for real Quake authenticity. Or if reloading must remain, either have a manual reload key, or just limit reloading to the pistol, kind of like Duke Nukem 3D. Other than that, I'd say this game is really going places and I eagerly await the new episodes.Also if you ever lived in Prague you will catch a lot of cultural references.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend! Wrote this during the production of Episode 3, but the visuals and music are perfectly atmospheric. There's always this claustrophobic feeling when you're in a sewer or a bunker or a mineshaft, unsure what every turn around the corner awaits you. The levels are well designed as well, I didn't get lost once and they never overstay their welcome. There's all these neat little embellishments in every level too that I don't want to spoil in this review. Cool weapons, good enemy variety, and lots of creative moments. If you're a fan of single player fps games do not pass on this, but fair warning, it can be a little spooky from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you think Quake (the first one) is the best old-school FPS, play HROT.If you like shooters that focus on atmosphere and exploration, play HROT.If you think sewers and subways actually make for the best levels, play HROT.If brown isn't your favourite colour, play HROT to change your mind.HROT eschews the recent trends of boomer shooters becoming increasingly complex in the wake of Doom Eternal. There are no alternative fire modes. No upgrades or mods. There is a single move speed, a kick, and a jump. All enemy attacks can be dodged by strafing in and out of cover, or by circling around them.On the surface this might sound like a negative, but this mechanical restraint is part of what makes HROT so great. Old-school shooters weren't all about mowing down waves of enemies with complex movement/weapon combos. They were about exploring a hostile and mysterious environment. Enemies served as a way to make the levels feel alive, as well as a means to instil tension and dread in the player.HROT nails every aspect of this old-school philosophy. Its beautifully brown levels echo real locations in late-communist Czechoslovakia. Environmental storytelling is abundant and enemy designs are both humorous and terrifying. Most importantly, the game keeps you constantly excited (and slightly scared) for what comes next.HROT consists of 24 levels (each around 15 - 30 mins long) spread over three chapters. Each level is set in a distinct location, centred around the game's themes of industry, technology, transport, bureaucracy, and Czech history. Levels loop back on themselves in interesting ways (e.g. sometimes the exit is near the start, but you need a key), but are always well designed enough so that you never get lost (I didn't know there was a map until I finished the game). Most levels have several secrets to discover, and each of the three chapters have a sprinkling of set pieces and Easter eggs.Each level features around 60 to 70 enemies. Most of these are placed in small groups evenly along the level. There are often contextual clues as to when you'll encounter enemies, which is important as the skill in defeating them lies in anticipating (or reacting to) their presence, rather than long fights. Both the enemies and the player are reasonably squishy (even on normal difficulty).Some enemy types move in a slightly unpredictable manner, like they're a bit drunk. This makes them slightly harder to hit, but not frustratingly so (none of them are annoyingly fast).Enemy variety is also good, mostly from an aesthetic perspective, but there's also reasonable mechanical variety: enemy size, movement speed, projectile speed, damage, flying enemies, leaping enemies etc.Most levels also feature one section towards the end with a concentration of enemies in a big arena. If you found a bunch of secrets and didn't take much damage earlier in the level, it's a fun opportunity to use some of your powerful weapons. If you rushed through the rest of the level, it's usually a decent challenge to just scrape through this final wave.Other than one or two surprises, the weapons are all things you've seen before. But they all feel good to use, and each of them excel at dealing with different types of enemies.The brown crunchy graphics are perfection. The music is also excellent and the game does a good job of switching between atmospheric music, uptempo music, and silence depending on the situation.You should play HROT.

Whether it's facing off against hordes of enemies while dodging trains, admiring a fully functional Astronomical Clock or getting the ♥♥♥♥ scared out of you by abruptly appearing snakes, this game has everything you'd want and a whole lot of random nonsense thrown in. It's clearly a passion project and while it is pretty short, it's very much worth checking out if you want a shooter that has a whole lot of heart (and liver dumplings).

_childDocuments_.review: No thanks to David Oshry, I found this game, played the demo, and loved it. While the first episode is fairly short, this is going to be a new all time favorite shooter for me. If you think that possibly 5-6 hours of content isn't for you, then maybe wait for the creator to release more episodes. But for me, this is so fluid and fast and I love that. Cheers to you!8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of retro FPS games for quite a few years now. I'm certainly not the only one as there's been a real renaissance of these types of titles. However, I've grown tired of it due to a huge amount of Unity engine retro FPS games. So I was genuinely surprised when I picked this game up and found myself genuinely enjoying it.HROT is a retro FPS game with an engine made from scratch, as such it avoids feeling too much like other games. The shooting feels great with a solid and orthodox weapon selection. The movement is well implemented and it reminds me a lot of Unreal for the most part. The character has a very weak jump however and relatively slow movement. The levels are well made. They consistently loop around to where you need to go and are in general very easy to navigate without using the game's map system. Plus, there are a lot of well hidden secrets so far. The enemy variety starts off typical but quickly introduces some very unique enemies into its roster.Overall, even if you are tired of retro FPS games, I'd still recommend trying this one. It's quite special and it's been very good so far.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted FPS with the nuance of an expert.  This game is incredibly inspired and proudly wears it's influences yet never compromises it's unique style. Never once does an enemy, weapon, nor level feels like it is wearing down and becoming more of the same, nor does it feel like they overstep the boundary of the game's design. I truly, cannot overstate how much of an accomplishment it is to have this game stay true to style and world while also never feeling like more of the same. And to manage so with an intentionally duller, more laxxed audio and visual design is nothing short of master craft.   I hope all who play this, enjoy it or not, can at least see and appreciate how carefully and meticulously crafted this game is to deliver with a restrained design palette whilst never letting the boundaries of such tax the experience and give way to repetition.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fun boomer shooter. Low poly, somewhat varied enemies. Wish there was more variety in weapons as you only use a few and they are just standard shotgun and submachine gun. The environments are varied, although not super interesting. But its fun, shooting and movement work well. The fact this was made by one guy is pretty awesome. I will say there are a lot of better boomer shooters out there. 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Like Quake coated in Cosmoline, HROT is way smoother and sleeker than it looks. Brown has layers, and they're all delicious.Player movement: responsive, speedy, no crouching because a real Comrade fights on their feet!Weapons: Typical FPS assortment with Czechnological flair, they feel pretty good to use, especially the shotgun.Enemies: Despite everything being seemingly a handful of Soviet Browns, enemy types are easily distinguished and understood, making even large combat encounters feel entirely doable.Maps: Blocky corridors, blocky outdoor areas, but never boring. They gracefully dance that line of lo-fidelity environments based on real places. Cool little memorials and secrets and neat widgets are most everywhere and ass just enough depth to keep the world engaging without cluttering it.Overall: Game, like rifle, is Fine.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really bananas. One episode you're fighting in what looks like military complexes and underground facilities where you fight a communist leader on spider legs. The next you're in some sort of castle and later get to drive a bike on the road and fight a stone faced grandma in a small village. Yes it's mostly brown but so was quake and people loved that game, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little shooter made by a single Czech developer, HROT feels reminiscent of days gone by with its Cold War-era setting, brutal difficulty, and limited graphics created by a custom Pascal-based game engine, but something about it just seems modern all the same, in a way that I just can't do justice. It has plenty of odd humor and interactivity, while counterbalancing that and the action with sprinklings of horror and suspense. I was admittedly hesitant when I first got this game, but it grew on me once I learned to appreciate the subtlety of it all.
