_childDocuments_.review: after the fact note - just found out this isn't some weird implementation of unity and in fact a custom engine written in pascal. this almost nearly excuses the performance but if you have written your own game engine, there is almost certainly room to improve it and add additional features but similar to the end of the review development has basically ceased, so instead of being excited about seeing the development of a custom engine we can just watch it be stretched out like a drum skin and atrophy. original review belowtechnically rotten. the game, as in the assets, weapons, enemies, levels are all competent and enjoyable. the engine or more specifically the utilization of the engine is piss poor. there is no true fullscreen mode. the game completely struggles to maintain over 100 fps despite being arguably simple rendering and logic, compared to dusk or a similar game that is even more advanced both technically and graphically, this game runs awful. there is noticeable mouse input delay that can be slightly improved by hopping around between the experimental gl rot or regular rendering, either way its bad. tons of graphical artifacts when you decide to  "change resolution" an impossibility since the game is just 24/7 borderless windowed aka lag mode. the game likes to do funky frame buffering so that screenshots don't work properly and the steam in game overlay mostly just breaks and restarts itself. visiting the pcgamingwiki for any hopes of a remedy but mostly to discover the dx api level to apply dxvk and hope that does something and here is a quote about running the game above 60 fps "Renders multiple identical frames, making visuals heavily stutter and prevents the game logic from properly functioning." absolutely terrible. on a technical level this game while being inspired by quake resides well below the function of that engine. quake ran at a silky 72fps stock. this game aborts itself over 60. according to pcgaming wiki this game is software rendered only with the experimental opengl support. so i guess some of the awfulness can be excused for going out of their way to not utilize directx. makes it extremely hard to enjoy the game. the lowest fps limit is 120 fps which I can't even maintain so I have to use nvidia control panel or riva tuner to limit the frames to 60. some parts of the game drop so hard the fps goes from 100ish to low 60's and of course development has basically ceased. only play for eastern europe nostalgia porneven further after the fact notes - linux and steam deck users are left to suffer and do some pretty big work arounds just to get a playable experience. these issues ideally would be addressed by the developer if they didn't completely give up
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best boomer shooters you can buy today. Expertly designed, polished to hell, consistently creative with many surprise moments, tough as nails, sometimes even quite scary, funny, and thoroughly unique - from its looks to its setting, lore and design. Also lots of little things and gimmicks here and there that really show how passionate and dedicated this developer is. There simply just isn't anything quite like it out there. I took my time to play it and did each episode a few months apart from each other because I didn't want it to end. 100% recommend, especially if you're into bommer shooters - this is one of the greats.Bonus points for having an actually decent survival mode after beating each chapter!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Game's worth the price for episode 2 alone, the other two thirds of the game are great but the level design on ep2's levels clicked with my monkey brain. The challenging yet fair hard difficulty with an amazing ascetic aesthetic makes it tempting to give this game a perfect rating. Although there are issues such as bosses being samey and weapons that aren't too interesting. Still one of the better ways to spend $20.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A Retro-FPS that manages to captivate both the gothic and industrial aspects of the original Quake and package it into a 1986 Soviet Union setting. Despite the alarming amount of sewers, the game has great usage of Soviet-Bloc architecture mixed in with levels that contain many traditional european buildings like churches and mausoleums. The weapons all handle great, and it feels wonderful once you pick up a 2nd pistol or manage to complete the arsenal, my only complaint is how limited you are when it comes to using some of the power weapons as they tend to leave your hands right as you picked them up. Quite an enjoyable and refreshingly refined experience for a game made by a single person, especially when so many Retro-FPS games fail to capture the feeling of truly older experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a pretty unique retro FPS. Set in the Soviet Union, the game tries to do it's own original thing and if anyone told me this game came out 25 years ago I might even believe them. If I had to pick a classic game that looks similar to this game I probably would have picked Quake combined with a little of Wolfenstein, 'Blood' and a few others. I would not say this is the best retro FPS out there but because it's so weird (you are fighting horses with gasmasks....) it's worth checking out anyways. One thing to note though is that this game currently has 1 finished episode (out of 5 I think...?) and episode 2 which is 50% done. Even though the game may not be abandoned and there's probably only a small team (or 1 person even) working the game, it does not mean you can get away with everything. The normal price of this game is just way too steep, even if all 5 episodes were there (probably) plus the game has been out for over a year and at this rate all 5 episodes would be done in 4-5 years. If you do not care about any of this then give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, I think the game is too short to be worth it currently. The game is still in early access, so when the full thing releases it will probably be worth it. One thing I disliked was how lame jumping felt compared to a game like Quake, which this game is incredibly similar to. I wish there was B-hopping. I liked the new types of enemies that were exclusive to chapter 2, I hope chapter 3 adds some more cool enemies. All of the weapons feel nice to me and have a purpose other than the landmines and the crossbow imo, even the handgun and sickle have more use. Endless mode is fun but feels limited, I think more maps should be added to endless mode. I went to Prague in 2018, nothing like the game, except for the throwing up.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! Enemies do not have hitscan, and as such hit way harder if they DO land a shot on you. Lots of running, lots of shooting, unapologetically brown (though more like Quake than the typical 2010s military shooter game) and you can get li'l rat-catcher dogs! Most of the game's writing is in Czech, but you CAN get English translations if you want some help with directions, plot, perhaps humour too. Does have SOME jumpscares, screen flashes, and spiders (though the game at least lets you convert those spiders into rats)Well worth the money for the time you can get out of it, even if the buffets never seem to be open.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Quake-like retro FPS, if you're coming from the modern Quake mapping scene the level complexity doesn't stack up with the likes of Arcane Dimensions (but then does anything really?) but I would say they're a good step ahead of Quake's original maps, and there are a lot of visual and interactive flourishes as well as the overall CCCP aesthetic. Gameplay wise weapons are distinct and useful, the double barrel is if anything more satisfying than Quake's, the kick mechanic is a nice touch for zoning/clustering enemies for AOE and bouncing back the Hrogre's (heh) grenades. Finally there's an endless mode for going fast and listening to your own music in while you gib Semiks left right and centre. Basically if you like Quake, buy the game.Oh and in case you didn't notice there's a demo so you have no excuse to not at least try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a warning for others considering buying the game: DO NOT play if you suffer from visual-induced motion sickness! 1-2 minutes in and I already felt nauseous and dizzy due to the narrow environment that game starts you off in. This is very unfortunate because I love giving indie games a go ahead of AAA+ games any day of the week!If you really want to give it a go but not too sure if it'll set off your symptoms; download the demo instead to see for yourself. Nothing against the game itself...and (stylistically), it looks fantastic but I hate the fact that I personally can't play due to an affliction 🙄

_childDocuments_.review: There's a very interesting quality to HROT. Despite being at its core a fairly straightforward retro shooter, HROT is simultaneously dedicated to painstaking recreation of even the most mundane things (most of the levels are set in recreations of real life Czechoslovakian locations and there is a lot of effort put into random tiny things, such as a fully working top, model train track or billiards table) and complete absurdism (One of the early bosses is the statue of a gorilla in the middle of a carousel, wielding double rocket launchers. It's not even the weirdest boss of that episode). There isn't really a story, and the game seems to actively defy giving you one, even at places that the games it's referencing would, such as the end of episode text crawls.The result of this is an odd, almost dream-like experience that is at the same time explicitly set during a specific period in a real life place. I can't quite describe how that makes me feel, but it's an extremely unique identity of its own, and I appreciate that a lot in a genre that is, I think, a little bit too eager to abide by the same few tropes.The game itself is quite good, for the record. Similarly to something like DUSK, there is no singular, crazy mechanic that HROT can just use as its main selling point, but everything it does is rock solid, I can't really name any level that was less than good, although I will say that the first episode's are probably the least interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A "pretty good" Quake style game with a really unique vibe and setting.If you're into boomershooters, this is kind of a no-brainer, and one of the better efforts I've played in recent memory. However, I think from a raw gameplay perspective it plays its cards a little too safe to the "Quake" formula - the weapon selection is as you'd expect, and the combat encounters and level design challenges all feel very Quake, which is fine since that's one of the best shooters ever, but really I was hoping for a little of it's own unique flavour and it's own spin on proceedings. On more than one occasion it felt a little too much like Deja Vu for my tastes.One thing that is unique, however, is the setting. The comedy horror soviet vibes felt really original to me and I don't think I've seen this done in the same way anywhere else. It's part scary, part comedy - has a wicked sense of humour but also feels really grim and forboding. I love having to shoot flying lenin heads in a very brown soviet bloc.Overall, I recommend this shooter!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an old-school, fast-paced first-person shooter.It is heavily influenced by the designs of Doom, Quake, or any other similar games. There are also references to other games like Project Warlock, Half-life, etc.There is nothing new as far as gameplay is concerned. It plays like a standard shooter.It is divided into three episodes, each having eight levels (plus a couple of secret levels). The majority of the levels also contain secrets to be found.I liked episodes 1 and 2 more than the third episode. I think they have run out of ideas for the later part of the game (especially episode three).The level design is serviceable. The music and sound are quite good. Some of the soundtracks gave me an eerie feeling.There are five difficulty settings. Very easy, easy, normal, hard, and very hard.Gameplay-wise, there is a theme here. Find a key. Do backtracking. Kill the enemies that spawn at previous locations while backtracking to the door. End the level with some sort of boss fight. There is a major boss fight at the end of each episode. Rinse and repeat. This may sound monotonous. And it is, to some extent. But if you are a fan of such gameplay, then you will have a blast for sure.You will start each episode with a basic weapon (the weapons do not carry forward from the last completed episode) and will get more weapons as you progress. After completing an episode, you have to start a new episode from the select menu. You can also play a specific level from a specific episode from the selection menu.There is enough variety in weapons. But some of the weapons sounds may lack punch. The enemy designs are amazing, bizarre, and funny. I was surprised to see some of the enemies. The enemies' shooting is projectile-based rather than hit-scan, which is a good thing. There are some minigames throughout the campaign. Those were cool additions.Story-wise, there isn't enough explanation, and it is up for interpretation. There is so much written material scattered throughout the levels. These are written in the Czech language. You need to press the "E'  or 'use' button to read them in English. There are no voice-over dialogues. Voice-over is there to make various sounds of enemies. I didn't like some of the messages that were conveyed through the scripts. It could have been better if they had hired some story writers and voiceover artists to streamline the experience. I faced some visual stuttering (or low frame-rate on some occasions); this may be due to some optimisation issues.Each level may take around 15 to 20 minutes to be completed if you are playing for the first time. Some may take less time than that. There are two secret levels that I missed on my first playthrough.I have completed the campaign on normal difficulty (without going out of my way to hunt for the achievements and secrets) in around 7 to 7.5 hours. There is an endless mode. Which contains four maps from the main campaign. This is standard wave-based gameplay. Nothing new. Just try it out if you want to have fun for a bit.Overall. I have played this game in 3–4 sessions. And I've enjoyed my time.But if you decide to play in one sitting, this will become repetitive.I read somewhere that only one person has developed the game. Kudos to the developer (you have done a remarkable job).I'll play this game again to get the remaining achievements and also try out the higher difficulty setting. I'll add more to this review if needed.I'll recommend getting this game when it's available at a light discount or in any bundle if available.My verdict: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: As of posting this, episode three has not yet been released.This game was hard for me to get into initially but once I 'got' it, I was supremely hooked.It's a retro-quakelike, a lot of the secrets are actually hard to find (unlike a certain modern Doom title) and despite it's simplistic mechanics has enough weapon and enemy variety to keep spicing things up. There are tons of little details scattered everywhere, some more symbolic than others, and most of it ties into the setting. All in all, an excellent experience. Looking forward to Episode 3

_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I don't know what kind of nightmares the dev. had, but I love it.Hrot is a a ''boomer shooter'' and a damn good example of one: a quake inspired feeling and gameplay (actually, I believe there are several inspiration - and Dusk would be the main one - but in gameplay, yup it reminded me a lot of ID first full 3D FPS) with the interactivity of a 3D realms 90's shooter, all mixed with an ol'good semi-horror segments.Besides the gameplay, which is the highest feature, settings and story are also worthy of note.... If only made sense! And yet, the game perfectly makes you feel in a country within the URSS's period, with some incredible mixing of realism (the towns and the other location) and horror- fantastical, and I believe this exuberant idea has been implemented so astonishingly by the dev. that alone is worth the ticket.So, basically, a simple (something hard to achieve), easy to play, 90's inspired FPS with some ingenious ideas and spectacular implementation. YES PLEASE! P.S. This game must be played by everyone... the socialist party DEMANDS IT!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot was an interesting game, an engine made by the developer, brown like in Quake, but set in a Soviet country in 1986.I played all of chapter one in about 2.2 hours on the medium difficulty, your mileage may vary.You, as the main character, don't know much, so you grab your pistol and your hammer and sickle, and start shooting anyone, or anything, on sight. There is probably more than what meets the eye.Movement speed is quick in a nice way, I don't go too fast or too slow, guns sound a little bit weak, but for this kind of game is perfectly fine.Gunplay is similar to another throwback shooter that we all are very likely to be familiar with, where the only hitscanner is you, with exception to your rockets, land mines and grenades, that'd be stupid.I haven't fully mastered the travel time of the grenade throw, it does have its dedicated throw button, RMB by default, which does what it does.What is very strange is why the button to reload the pistol is set to 2 by default than just R, not complaining when I can run it akimbo, does have a nice little reload then.Overall I found the gunplay quite good, enemies are relatively quick to kill on the medium difficulty, which is usually what I play at, feel free to try the harder difficulties if you're feeling masochistic.Here's to seeing chapter 2 and 3!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stupid good. It even gives Dusk a run for it's money, and that's really saying something because I love Dusk. It's probably my favorite of the retro-revival FPS games but Hrot is hot on its heels.Hrot revels in its weirdness. On the surface it looks like your average retro shooter, and it definitely is a retro shooter don't get me wrong. All the hallmarks of games like Doom or Quake are here, but there are so many strange things throughout that it never feels like just another Doom clone. I don't want to give any of it away, it's worth experiencing for yourself because there's some crazy things that go down in this game but yeah this definitely worth your time if you're into these sorta games, or if you enjoy the color brown

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a wonderful and very charming FPS shooter hearkening back to the days of DOOM and Quake with an infusion of life set in the cold war era. It manages to faithfully recreate the experience of the classics whilst being true to itself; it affectionately pays homage to what came before without being a duplicate re-textured clone. I love the monotonous dark brown and sad beige colors, they evoke a certain flavor of desperation whilst simultaneously providing a slight amount of hopeful warmth. It's a game that's so simple, it's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The below is a mix of early access review edits. I'm leaving them there for posterity and because it shows passion, which is the foundation to the development of this game. This "review" is rough but I can't get rid of my thoughts from throughout development. I'm not being lazy - it's a time capsule. I'm leaving the edits be as this is my GOTY 2023. Therefore, my thoughts need to be preserved. This is one of the finest FPS games that I've played in years. It is S tier.------This review is out of date, because frankly, the game has moved from "early access" to "early access but it is already ****ing brilliant and I'm already very happy with my purchase." The developer is obviously a perfectionist, not that I'm complaining. He's also obviously a John Carmack level sort of genius, and loves to show off - he implements new achievements just to show off a cool thing he made in his custom engine, haha! Every new update blows me away. At time of writing, this is a very promising early access title inspired by Quake, Wolfenstein and Blood, with a hint of Dusk and Half-Life 1, in that order. Notice that I left Doom out there, although obviously that DNA is everywhere too. The soundtrack is amazing. With each (very regular) patch the game gets more polished and feedback is taken onboard. The developer cares. I cannot say more than that due to the game not being finished, but I encourage anyone who likes the above games to give it a shot. Also, it uses a custom engine written in pascal! That's cool! Super nerd cool! It's mighty impressive too.Edit: Still EA, but updates with some incredibly unique ideas come seemingly almost every week at the moment, and this game is shaping up to be one of the more unique doomer-shooters on the market. I usually avoid playing early access games until they're finished, but I'm enjoying following the evolution of this one.Edit 2 about 6 months later: This is how early access should be done. HROT is the definition of early access done right. Every single update brings quality and content to the game. I am incredibly hyped for the full release and I am honestly struggling to fault what is here. Even though it's only about two-thirds finished, I already consider HROT to be a masterpiece.V1.0 edit: There is a story if you pay attention, but don't take it *too* seriously. To say any more than that would involve spoilers for the ending. Episode 3 is WONDERFUL. The ending is EXTREMELY powerful.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! awesome and weird. There are tons of creative and interesting enemies, several of which made me stop and laugh. Why do the wheelchair guys do so much damage!? lol. The movement and combat are slick, fast, and fun. You have a veritable arsenal at your disposal to gib and massacre the bizarre hoards that fill each and every level. Dual pistols ftw! My one and only complaint stems from the weapons: they sound a little pathetic. C’mon gimmie some oomph. Otherwise this game is top tier.  It’s got so much atmosphere. There aren’t any cheap jumpscares save one, which totally got me. I shouted loud enough to startle my dogs too hahaha. I particularly enjoyed the part in episode 3 w/ the two dog companions. _childDocuments_.review: I had a shorter, more snappier tidbit in place of this review but after replaying it I found I had a lot more to say about it now. This is quickly rising up to be one of my favorite throwback shooters, its got so much great going for it.What really stands out to me though is the level design, not only is it insanely tight and well-composed from a design perspective but its also extremely memorable, throwing new things at you constantly to really keep an old formula fresh. I love exploring in this game and coming across some silly interactable, its amusing everytime. The setpieces are bonkers, its not afraid to mix it up with some absurdity despite the otherwise bleak tone. However, even without those moments the levels themselves are just great to look at and explore, in spite of the bleak color palette. Combined with the great soundtrack, in the moment to moment gameplay it can give a really great atmosphere that makes it all very memorable.The combat itself I'd say is generally standard for this kind of game, Id say there's decent weapon balance overall as I found a use for every weapon, but there's two things that stuck out to me in my playthroughs. Firstly is that the ability to kick enemy's grenades is so much damn fun and adds a nice layer of flair and strategy to a pretty straightforward shooter. Second is the enemy design, the beautiful thing here is that none of the enemies are hitscan, even the ones you'd think would be. Rather, its just very fast projectiles. This really helps encourage aggressive and fast-pace combat which makes the core loop of exploring and combat have a nice contrast to eachother that sometimes is hard to reach in these games. When the action picks up, it reaallly picks up in a great way, even further helped by the great enemy balance that makes you focus in on your target priority since so many are great threats, without it ever feeling unfair or unbalanced.If you're a fan of retro shooters, I feel like this is a no-brainer. Even if its nothing extremely stand out to you personally, what is here is such a tightly designed and solid package that I can't really see you having a bad time at all. If you're not as acquainted to this kind of game, though, I'd say try out some others first, I feel like what makes this game shine will be harder to see without having played the classics it draws a lot of inspiration from.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Quake"esque" shooter that earns the title "brown", in that nearly everything in the game is brown to some degree.Which does not take anything away from the game, as it still is worth the purchase.Gameplay is solid and the array of weapons you get, all have a distinct usage, but the shotgun is 100% the one gun you're going to be using the most. As mentioned before, everything is more or less brown, but there's still variety in the level designs and takes inspiration from eastern european enviroments, specifically the Czech Republic, as iirc it was mentioned a couple of times throughout the game, that makes it so that while the color palette does not change immensly, the designs and variation of the levels do.I highly recommend this for anyone that loves "boomer shooters" or generally loves great shooters.

It's essentially Quake with communist overtones if you want a basic comparison.Gunplay is quick, controls are responsive and enemies drop at a reasonable pace once you start hitting them. _childDocuments_.review: HROT is basically a "mod" for Quake 1.  Remember how iD Software open sourced the Quake engine (aka iDTech 1)?  Most people thought that was a good thing, but they were all of them decieved.  Because it just gets used to make garbage like HROT.   HROT is an abandoned Early Access first person shooter (obviously, it's basically Quake 1).   It's a reskin of Quake 1 with some custom levels and objects... all of which detestably lazy and low poly.  But what do you expect?The game was abandoned roughly 3 months ago, and was in development hell for a lot longer.  While there's still time before the game reaches the developers committed deadline to complete the game, this is just because the developer laughably said it would take them 8 years.  There's no reliable indication the game will ever be completed, which is a reason for gamers to avoid this.  But it does highlight a problem with Valve's failed Early Access program, which was intended to help amateur developers finish their games, but instead it gets used for this... a paid mod, and absolutely a cash grab, and quite possibly a scam.  We'll get into that later.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.  Sure, this is because this is just a reskin of Quake, but... it's 2022.  So gamers deserve better.  The industry has advanced.  The minimum bar for gaming has, too. Unethically, the developer sold keys to this abandoned Early Access game into cheap, nasty game bundles, where they knew it would be advertised and sold as a complete game.  This seems to have been done in an attempt to mislead gamers into buying a knowingly faulty, defective and incomplete product.  When a developer does this for a game they have zero practical intention of completing, this is essentially a scam, an intention to get paid for a broken/unfinished product.  Often this is done as an exit strategy, as the developer takes the money and runs.  No refunds have been given, the developer kept all the money they took from gamers.HROT has a laughable, eye watering price of $20 USD (for a paid mod!!!!), for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games, let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend.  Quake itself is also free, so just play that if you want a solid retro experience.   This cash grab paid mod for Quake is garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic retro FPS. It has a lot in common with DUSK. The developer of DUSK called it "Basically Slavic DUSK", and took it upon himself to promote the game because he personally likes it quite a bit. The movement, shooting and basically complete lack of a story all remind me of DUSK quite a bit. It's as brown as Quake. Shooting is pleasent and your arsenal are classics like shotguns or grenade launcher. Frequent updates keep me coming back; I've noticed there's a great attention given to detail and huge points for enemy uniqueness. There is a satisfaction here, one that keeps getting refreshed with every update; I'll gladly keep playing my way through, impressive throughout. Thumbs waaaaaay up.

_childDocuments_.review: I for one think more games should reward me with cooking recipes for beating them and their levels.That aside, while I don't claim to have ever played Quake and its ilk, nor was I raised in a former Soviet state, so a lot of the references are lost on me, I do love HROT a lot. It's the peak of classic, simple, boomer shooter activity: you run, you gun, you scuttle around the levels looking for new items or creative ways to keep up the running and gunning. _childDocuments_.review: Even though only Episode 1 is complete, this is a completely awesome game. Plenty of references to Dusk and classic FPS games, but it creates a moody, spooky atmosphere that is uniquely its own. Like many of them, the story is minimalist, but after playing through a couple of times, you begin to see where it's heading. The Soviet-era world is convincingly portrayed (at least to these western eyes) with lots of cool unobtrusive details that never feel tacked-on or superfluous. The level design for E1 is very tight, and you will find yourself grabbing a key in proximity to the next point of progression, so it's not difficult to find your way around. Well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I like the aesthetics and cool retro engine but I don't find the levels very interesting and the gameplay rarely manages that sweet spot of being challenging without being too unfair or too easy.Maybe not the right place for this, but I also found the comparisons to Quake 1 of some reviewers to be unfair. Despite some higher poly models in several places, the level design is completely unlike Quake, and the resulting gameplay is more akin to Wolfenstein 3D with the full-3D blockiness and lever hunting of Tomb Raider.I wish I could give this a neutral review, I enjoy it reasonably but it's nothing special. I commend the developer, especially regarding the lovely, crunchy engine.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Game has finally come out of early access as a full release and is an easy recommend for anybody interested in 'boomer shooters'. The setting is very unique and the enemies are weird but memorable. Despite the lack of an actual plot being told, the overall experience makes up for it. Great stuff, I've recommended this since the early days with a single map and it's great to see the finished product.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Memorisation, not skill.Ultra hyper hardcore. Very Hard is unplayable on first walkthrough and it's unfair to saveload all the time. Otherwise it's atmospheric Doom-like shooter. If it's impossible to defeat enemies without knowing their locations and skills beforehand, why play it? It's not hardcore, it's grind and remember. Can't rate this difficulty mess for now. Enemies just hide all the time knowing player exact location and not making any noise. So it's hide and seek except everyone is against you. Enemies can jump much higher than player. Sometimes they just spawn and deal instant damage no matter how much you are bunnyhopping. This is memorisation hide-n-seek seeker simulator with guns... There always will be some surprise attacks that no one can predict and counter(damage is instant against 5 enemies). The only way to beat it is to know everything beforehand. Very often is too easy or too hard. Every wall can hide multiple enemies. I'm an ex-global elite in csgo and this makes me saveload because of not knowing what's ahead. It's impossible to play cautiously, enemies see through walls and will chase you down everywhere. In some cases downing monsters one by one isn't possible and there's no ammo. It feels random very often.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a Quake 1/Chasm styled shooter wrapped up in a decaying USSR Czechoslovakian setting. Despite what the trailers and images suggest, it is not a depressing and moody 6 hours of shooting men and mutants, it is a slightly humorous game with the Quake 1 brown filter over everything that lists out some lovely recipes at the end of every episode. Frankly, this game wasn't what i was expecting it to be at all and I'm partially glad it wasn't. The weapons are fun to use and get plenty of time to shine, there is a MASSIVE cast of enemies to fight across the episodes, the locations have a ton of variety despite being drowned with the Quake 1 brown filter, the music is similar to HBO's "Chernobyl" mini-series with most of it being depressing and almost foreboding, there's tons of secrets to find across the levels, and plenty of challenge to be found in some of the game's arenas.The lesser parts of the game are the weak sounding weapons (especially the sub-machine gun, good god), some enemies being tanky as hell (no, making your COMMON shotgunner enemy eat 4 shells to go down isn't fun or challenging in the slightest), some levels are difficult to finish as the exit and/or way to progress isn't exactly clear (true to the 90's!), and not all that much to look forward to once you beat all three episodes (unless you want the pride of 100%-ing it.)Long story short:If you want something to remind you of Quake 1/Chasm/You Are Empty without actually playing them, or just curious about the game, buy it. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the recent Boomer Shooters, HROT is probably the most authentic feeling one out there at the moment. The custom game engine really nails the feeling of a a long lost slav-jank FPS gem from '98 in the best way possible.Also, you can take a dump in the toilets. Can't wait for episode 3.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an amazing "boomer shooter" made with lots of love, humor and wine. Mixing the styles of Quake, Chasm and Build Engine games like Duke 3D in a Slav-themed world full of gun wielding mad men, horses with gas masks, floating heads and the occasional bear. Definitely one of my new favorites in the retro-modern FPS genre. With a focus on pure fps gameplay, finding secret rooms, interactive props, silly jokes and cute puppers that will be your friend till the end! Just make sure you like the color brown, but that should be obvious based on the store page media.Highly recommend if you want to play a very solid and smooth retro-modern FPS and spend hours looking for that one secret you missed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is another retro-shooter but with its own unique identity and beauty. While the game may look bleak and brown, that is simply its charm, I'm usually not a fan of this aesthetic but in Hrot, it just works, and most importantly, fits! The numerous czechoslovakian references are sure to amuse any czech person playing it and seeing Prague depicted in retro-shooter graphics and level design is something mystical. The game's atmosphere is eerie and so are the enemies in this game, always generating a sense of a creepy ominous group going after you, which is indeed what was happening in Czechoslovakia in the years this game is depicting. Enemies wear creepy communist clothes with gas masks and various protective suits. This all becomes more and more intense until you realize you're fighting an aggressive horse with a WW1 era gas mask jumping at you. Safe to say I absolutely love the enemies in this game, the contrast between normal regulat shooting bad guys to the more bizzare aforementioned communist horse is great!Music and ambience are very good, keeping you on your toes and always reminding you that this game is played out in a gloomy reality while often having a melody that you simply can't help but notice even during an intense fight.The gameplay and movement in Hrot is snappy and responsive and this even surprisingly extends to the rideable motorcycle you can find in some levels, which can run enemies over and even drift to make quick turns to make the movement with it that much more enjoyable.Difficulty options are pretty good although I do feel like the game could be a little harder on the higher difficulties.A big bonus for the game is that, if the game wasn't replayable enough already, it features an option to randomize enemies and items in a run, which is always gonna be fun.I hope Hrot continues being updated frequently and I'm hoping for a potential multiplayer and map editor in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Very competent retro FPS, there's really not much to say other than it's exactly what you think it is. If I had to offer some slightly esoteric praise then I'd say that I often pronounce a lot of films and games as not as smart as they think they are, however HROT is not only as smart as it thinks it is, I would say it's smarter.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is kinda awkward for me. I do love the style of the game, the setting, the enemies.... But it's very basic, the maps aren't decorated much, it feels sterile. Atmospheric sound is okay.I do not recommend this game FOR NOW. If the devs will work hard on the game and deliver regularly updates with content and improvements, I will change my recommendation. But there is still the chance that this game will be a cash grab and stuck in early access forever. The price is too high for what you get.You have been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT stands as embarrassment to the AAA developers. Sure those bloated studios can manufacture titles with high def textures, but they could never make a game that's as GOOD as this. I just bought Zelda TotK because it came out around the same time as HROT, and I find myself repeatedly setting my Switch aside to enjoy another horrifying/hilarious/fantastic ride through the brownscape.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another Retro FPS. You would think I would tire of them, but I only Hunger for more. Game definitely needs some polish, but for the most part is a solid foundation. The atmosphere is great and is essentially 50 shades of brown with a dash of red . Guns are pretty standard, only missing a . Levels currently offer a balanced mix of close quarters, underground and surface areas, with some interiors. HROT currently has 1 Episode, containing 8 missions and 4 bosses. It took me about 4 hours to beat the game on Hard while goofing around and looking for secrets. Bosses are pretty easy and simple. HROT is somewhat of a key and button hunter, but most are located in pretty obvious and not maliciously hidden. My biggest gripe, which is personal preference, I despise monster closets and sudden hot drops of enemies. But when the rest of the game is solid, I cant let a personal preference stop me from playing this. Also, the game is really, really brown.

Only complaint is that, at least on normal difficulty, the game is far too generous with ammo. HROT is at its best at the start of each episode, where resources are scarce and you feel grateful to have nine shotgun shells left.Note for Linux/Steam Deck/Proton users: particle effects make the game chug super hard and AFAIK there's nothing you can really do about it. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real gem for 90's 'boomer shooter' people, with an atmosphere that will let you quickly understand you're lost in Nucular Apocalyptica. It plays and feels a lot like Quake or Chasm: The Rift (in the current stage of development, it's more like the latter), but it has its very own and unique background story, and it plays in our real world, in an alternate reality setting.There are frequent updates with new maps, features and bug-fixes by the game's developer, making for its own satisfying experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT DAMN, this is a good game! (one playthrough on hard)So let's get this out of the way. Yeah, it's brown. Really, really brown. But it's tasefully brown, you know? There are other colors in there to make the brown happen that, when looked at closely, are actually pretty colorful. The textures also have pretty clear differentiation between floors, walls, and ceilings, giving a nice subtle guidance to your eyeballs to make sure that you're never actually lost for what specifically to look at.Gameplay. It's good! Solid shooting, a pretty darn generous spread of weapons for a first episode and nothing that really gets outshone. What I would consider the three power weapons get just enough ammo to make it clear that it's safe to use them, while never keeping you too flush with ways to trivialize encounters. Other weapons do tend to run out maybe just a little bit too quickly; one specific common enemy is a good deal tankier than their comrades, and there just aren't all that many pickups overall. I was never OUT out, but there were one or two places where I was down to a couple handfuls of pistol ammo and nothing else. At least the dual pistols do good damage. Definitely hunt around for the second one, you'll probably need it. As for the sounds, make your own decision, I didn't mind them overall but something just a little punchier would have been nice too.A good variety of enemies, too, and new ones popped up pretty frequently. There's a main selection that shows up in every map, but some of the weirder ones come and go, letting them be a nice surprise when they pop back up. There's some overlap as far as their abilities, but nothing that actually ends up feeling redundant, so that's nice. Oh, and no hitscanners, but the bullet projectiles move pretty fast and are maybe a tiny bit too hard to see.You get four bosses in this first episode, too, which is already twice as many as Quake had for an entire game. They're nothing particularly mechanically complex or interesting - they all generally behave the same what with the jumping around and a projectile attack - but their inclusion is welcome to break up the pacing a little bit and give you a sudden end-of-level surprise.The levels are a bit of a muddier (hah, brown joke) point for me, because while each one does manage to do a lot to feel like it has its own identity, there's only so much it can have based on the limited palette, and not just the colors. You'll see the same set dressings used across just about all of the levels, and they're used well, but there's still only so much that can be done. Each level generally has one specific structure or piece of scenery that the rest of it is building towards, and you'll have a big fight there, but on your way to that big fight there are a lot of hallways and boxy rooms. I wouldn't call it boring level design, not at all, just very utilitarian, which I guess fits the theme. There's a lot being done with the presentation of the game, but maybe there isn't enough there to do much more with? Regardless, they all flow pretty well, and I only got turned around a couple times overall (see again, subtle texturing work, etc etc), so again, make your own decisions while playing.Difficulty-wise, like I listed up top, I played the first episode available once on Hard, and I found it generally pretty manageable. Enemy placement is very 90s but not quite as mean-spirited. Expect a lot of dudes coming out from secret walls or waiting beside a door, but not as many as you'd find in older games. I know the amount of ammo and especially health pickups are a point of contention at the moment, but with careful playing (and just a little bit of savescumming) nothing seems all that unfair. If I had to make a suggestion regarding difficulty, I'd ask for exactly one more +15 health pickup per level, and that's about it.So yeah I'd say this one's pretty good. It's a throwback shooter in maybe the most literal sense we've seen of the recent revival - not really any specific attempts to take a mid-90s shooter and add to the formula with modern tools and design sensibilities, but more something that does quite literally feel like it was taken off a forgotten floppy disk found in someone's closet. I mean that in a good way. It's a celebration, not an elevation. Something that feels at home among the Quake 1s of the day, not looking down at them.That's all I got. I'm excited for the next episodes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand how this game has overwhelmingly positive reviews. I tried it on the steam deck and the frame rate is all over the place. The game can't run at constant 60 fps even if it has this retro graphic which isn't that demanding on the CPU and GPU. I tried multiple proton versions, in one the audio didn't work, in another the inputs didn't work.I don't consider it necessary when I buy a product to debug it until I make it work, especially for a shooter which isn't that resource demanding.Also the steam deck playable status should be changed to unsupported. Yes it is playable, if you like lag, stutter, changing a bunch of settings and hoping that it will run smoothly. I hope the developer works to make it run 60 fps on all platforms because it's a fun game but in this current state unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the first episode and I have to say: It's pretty could! Some improvements could be made but lets bust out the good first.1. The art style is pretty rad. Despite being mostly brown and gray, I can clearly see the enemy and they don't blend in that much.2. Guns are simple but still fun to use.3. Levels are well designed and I rarely found myself getting lost. Levels have a natural flow that lead the players to where they need to go.Some of the flaws:1. Guns sound extremely week. The shotgun, pistol, etc just don't have enough punch to them. It sounds like someone is spitting into the microphone rather than bullets leaving a high powered firearm.2. Pistols and SMG have automatic reloads that you have no control of. A simple manuel reload button would fix this, easy.3. Lack of ammo. Starting levels without any ammo from previous levels feel suprisingly scarce. My favorite gun was the lightning gun but I barely got to use it simply cause I couldn't find any ammo for it. Even the shotgun and pistol have low ammo pickups and made me feel that I had to make every shot count. Which is fine, but it does feel like some ammo drops in secrets or the level were just not there where they should be.4. More intresting guns would be cool. You get this ye old shotgun that works more like a long range sniper or rail gun and I would like to see more guns like this to give the game some more flavor.Overall: This game is good even if it doesn't reinvent the wheel. Can't wait to see the next two episodes!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If I didn't play, Dusk, Ion Maiden, Amid Evil, Quake, DOOM, DOOM 2, DOOM 64, Heretic, Hexen, Hexen 2, Duke Nukem 3D, Shadow Warrior, Unreal, and like a handful of DOOM mods and conversions, then yeah I'd say its worth playing. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best boomer shooters out there.The atmosphere is tight - both thanks to the great ambient soundtrack and well-designed locations (especially further into the game), weapons feel great to shoot and you're always low on ammo - which I see as a plus.HROT may feel a little underwhelming at first, but as you progress, the closer to DUSK-level quality it gets.Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's 1986 and there are far worse things lurking in Czechoslovakia than British stag parties, moustache or pickled veg. A solid indie shooter that combines the muddy brown and black pallette of mid 90's FPS like quake, to a distinctive Central European horror (believe me you will jump at times).Exceptional detail and interactivity:-> press "E" to kiss a photo of the communist leader-> flush toilets-> get a translation of any Czech writing you can see (delightful!)-> authentic Czech weaponry CZ-25 submachine gun, duel wielded CZ-52 pistols, hammer and sickle.Worth price of admission and hopefully much more to come too. Czech yourself before you wreck yourself!

While the gunplay is good, the setting and aesthetic are what help elevate this game above it peers. If you enjoy Chasm or Dusk, this game will be very enjoyable.(Reviewed build as of 2/13/21, Episode 1 available)9/10 currently, would flee from gas mask horse all day
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: So it's over. Finishing good games makes me sadge. HROT is quite something. Most games these days go for the abrasive, colorful look. This game is not afraid to be brown. I'm Polish and although I'm not familar with the history of Czechoslovakia, at times I felt at home. Mad respect for the custom engine written in Pascal - my slow computer appreciates that. All in all, a pleasant boomer shooter full of surprises, great level design, and sense of humor. Looking forward for the next one from the creator - whatever that may be!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot's setting is grounded heavily in socialism era Czechoslovakia. The campaigns are tours of real-world places around Czechia during around 80's. It even makes sense geographically, the way they lead into each other. The castle levels, for instance, are various famous Czech castles. The wagon boss-fight is a callback to Hussite war wagons from the 14th century who resided in the location that level takes place in. The horse legs you fight at the gym are a gymnastics prop you leap over or onto during PE to this day. Bumper cars, carnival rides with swan seats and a random gorilla in the middle, gas mask drills to prepare for American nuclear attacks, the random socialist slogans, the crappy mass produced furniture, milk sold in plastic bags, etc. Every inch of this world is oozing with callbacks to things the previous generation grew up surrounded by.One more cool bit. Apparently the name Hrot means "Spike" in Czech, but it can also be used figuratively as "escalating a situation" or "picking a fight" something akin to "having a bone to pick with someone". I thought that was really neat.★★★★☆ 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "boomer shooters" out there, largely due to having impeccable atmosphere, unnerving ambiance and clever level design. There's nothing else quite like it. Gameplay is somewhere between Quake and Chasm, but don't be fooled by the comparisons - Hrot creates its own identity and offers flattery to its predecessors without blatant imitation. My only critique would be that the firearms aren't as punchy as they are in other games, though they still offer their own charm.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Like Quake and Chasm: The Rift had a mutant baby. The graphics capture the era quite well, and the soundtrack is fantastic so far. I like all the little sounds enemies make, the different interactions with decorative objects - it's like an old friend.11/25/21 - Episode 2 is shaping up to be fantastic as well, the levels more complex and more mechanics to make them interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a one-of-a-kind game that deserves to be played.  It successfully blends its gritty atmosphere with a wacky sense of humor, and it keeps you coming back for more.  I consider this to be a hidden gem in 2023.  In a year with several big-name titles, don't overlook this one!Check out my video review here:

_childDocuments_.review: good and maybe a little ridiculous oldschool fps that gives a lot of quake vibes (very good secret placement btw) but still has a lot of its own unique gameplay features; graphics look pog (especially the design of bosses), destructible environment is life, sound is pog. one thing that still amazes me is endless mode: before update it was a little boring and very hard with kinda no motivation to play, but when it got updated it became more BALANCED, not easier (also it has 2 arenas and each of them is different, game almost settles new gameplay loops inside of them) and also rewards you with some achievements. sometimes i just feel like i want to kill some sharp funny enemies so i go to endless mode.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A friend returning from several months in the Czech Republic liked to do an impression of a dour Czech, delivering an accented, expressionless, "it is okay" when questioned about something's value. That's this shooter. It is okay. It's not that fun and it's not that clever. The theme is fine. Everything is brown. None of the weapons feel good to use. The enemies are sort of funny but mostly kind of dumb. The level design is a so-so retread of actually good shooters from the 90s. I get that it's a passion project. It isn't worth twenty dollars. It is okay.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Did you play Dusk and wanted some more? Well HROT is basically Dusk's little brother. - The music doesn't have that same punch as Dusk does.- The weapons are cool and who doesn't love a super shotgun? But Dusk had more memorable weapons- The levels are okay but a bit repetitive. The scenery isn't as great as Dusk.- The story is barely there. Nothing like Dusk's and you don't get much resolution at the end of the game.- The game play is a bit slower than your standard boomer shooter. Almost like a mix between Serious Sam and Dusk.- The enemies are pretty generic, for the most part, with some standouts here and there.- Not very innovative in its game play except for the kick feature and some easter eggs. I really liked both those . Though, Dusk made me rethink how good a boomer shooter could be. This game merely solidified my love for them.- Difficultly spike between Hard and Very Hard is massive. So be aware of that when you start the game.With all that being said, the game is still a lot of fun. If you liked Dusk then you will probably like this since. I'd only pick it up when its on sale unless you just really want it since $20 is a bit steep for 5-6 hours of game play and a vague story.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is pretty much what it looks like. Quake set in the nightmarish, post apocalyptic, Soviet hellscape that is Prauge. This game is only for based 2nd world doomer chads, no cringe 1st world zoomer soyjacks allowed. 3rd world zooider coomers are welcome but it'll bar you from visiting NATO countries. BTW the closest translation for the name is something like "Sharp prong-like object / Fountain pen nib"It is a no nonsense, fast paced, run and gun, where you gotta find the exit and shoot everything that moves. It is delightfully simple in how it plays, you WASD around the map at ludicrous speed and left click on the bad guys until they take the forever nap. You got a peestol that does some ouchies, a shotgun that makes beeeg ouchies, a submachine gun that does a lot of little ouchies, and some other stuff that really lays the pain on em. My favorite is the symbol of the humble agricultural collective, the sickle, which you use to poke these chunky gas masked dingbats in their precious eyes.Speaking of, there are a menagerie of enemies. Rats, robe dudes, Allahu Ackbar, hazmat suit dudes, what da dog doing, dudes who launch grenades at your booty, feeshy, ARACHNAPHOBIA, and H O R S I E. just to name a few. The environments are kinda what I imagined the socialist / combloc / warsaw pact nations to look like, but made into fun ID style maps. Tightly packed apartments, community centers, displayed infrastructure and civil engineering, Ancient buildings from the Pre-Soviet days either preseved or repurposed, and Government buildings. The environment is almost alien, uncomfortable, oppressive, unwelcoming, and just like the mfkin OG Quake..... B R O W N and I  L O V E  I T. Seriously this game is either Sepia toned or Czechoslovakia couldn't afford any more colors. Also laden with secrets and easter eggs.The score is okay, I suppose. Ominous gothic tones in slow combat, and a bit more up paced banger for when the hovadina hits the vetrak. Buy this game so the devs are encouraged to make more. And maybe learning more about this Velvet Divorce will help me in the inevitable event that my parents marriage dissolves like the USSR.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a perfectly serviceable  old-school FPS who's main appeal is it's slavic-setting-turned-nightmare. HROT doesn't try to evolve the formula like Ultrakill or subtly tell a story like DUSK. Instead, everything - from the choice of weapons, to health and armor pickups, to enemies - are all drenched in whatever stage of Soviet decay Czechoslovakia was in in the late 80s. The levels are all "realistic" locations, much like Duke 3D, but have the Brutalist bent that's signature to the USSR. And much like Duke 3D, interactivity plays a huge part of the novelty of HROT, with an odd assortment of items that can be switched, flipped, or flushed, including Czech signage, which can be interacted with to get an English translation. Other than the very basic premise of some nuclear disaster  going awry, the story might as well not exist - it's an excuse to show increasingly strange enemies and a sense of unease. As a shooter, it's a solid lineup of weapons and enemies with suitably off-beat designs but nothing to exciting game play wise.HROT is sits comfortably in the middle of fun game and weird passion project who's primary audience is, presumably, people who have grown up in Czechoslovakia presumably in the 80s and 90s. It's cool to see that even with a flood of old-school FPS games on the market, developers can still find ways to distinguish them.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is incredibly good, even with just one chapter. Its reminds lot a lot like the old time classic Quake, just set in Soviet sattelite state. The gameplay and level design is well designed.  Also the dark atmosphere and  ambient music give a tense and good experience. Pros:- Decent graphics- Great soundtrack- interesting variety of enemies- Nostalgic/retro FPSCons:- High price tag- Ultra short campaign- Easy boss fights- Simplified puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S OUT OF EARLY ACCESS, BABY!!! And it's better than ever! The last episode is soul-tearing, finger-licking good. All of them are, but these people just can't stop surpassing themselves with every iteration.When mosquitoes get sufficiently bloated with blood and turn into Party leaders, ghastly swamp lights, the stars of Kremlin, appear over the muddy waters. When these corrupt servants of tetanus drag enough gurgling victims down into the mass grave of black sludge, the palace of torture rises from the bog. With its bricks made of porous raw meat, and dark secrets weeping within its premises. The wandering graveyard flagellates the surrounding lands, grimacing on its defiling path. On the bones of the grieving, it feasts, distorting the nature of man, perverting the very concept of good intent, turning spring waters into vinegar to dip people in like dumplings. Rolling in loops of ruthless violation, the breaking wheel was created of rot, yet it never crumbles, only flakes. Nurtured on its mastitis milk, when someone hands you a loaded gun and points in any direction, you ask no questions. Tebe davno pohui.Here's HROT, an uncompromising mockery of the Soviet nomenclature and its exploits, a malicious parody based on disturbing authenticity, an absurdist hyper-reality of all overgrown socialistic establishments. Of their mercantile militarism, totalitarian autocracy, and imperialistic toxicity. Going through the Soviet underbelly guns blazing even just on Hard, not Very Hard, is an enterprise for the brave. I found it challenging yet not entirely masochistic. Time after time, I died in its hellish corpse mounds with a guilty hard-on, sipping on the noxious bile they secrete like it's Heaven's nectar.To highlight a couple of things before we go on, HROT has the coolest multi-layered skyboxes ever, the rest you can see on your own. But I gotta note that there's a world of difference between works that look like crap because an artist is a hack, and HROT, every stroke of brush in which reflects immaculate taste and truly cunningly expressed intent. The latter is the most important thing about art to me, I  don't care for "just pretty". Or "just ugly", for that matter. And however painstaking a vapid creation may be, something as resonant as the game wipes its hairy ass with it. The sounds have the oomph, but there's no music. It was replaced with static, dripping, droning, humming, and every little thing works as potent steroids, force-fed to the Herculean atmosphere of this rust golem.In terms of gameplay, it's a classic. You're a rat of many mazes, looking for doors and keys, oppressed by the resource scarcity... or deficit, to be more authentic. I think there were but a couple of moments since the first level when I had full health for a few seconds, and I could never afford to waste ammo. To fight for every crumb like a homeless man battles a stray dog for a rotten chicken leg is how I like it. This made discovering hidden stashes an alluring prospect, a necessity, not a mere completionist endeavor. And are they challenging to find in this game! Typically, I was able to uncover a third of secrets on any given level, seldom more. Unapparent buttons, fuse boxes in weird places, tricky acrobatics, you name it. HROT's developers come from the oldest of schools, especially when it comes to deviousness.The levels are all familiar places like a gymnasium, palace of culture, mausoleum, or a uranium mine. Try googling the latter, the sights are grim and morbidly fascinating. I keep hearing that something is industrial, was never quite sure what it meant. Now, I can say without a doubt, that I've witnessed the apogee of industrialism in every sense of the word. Even more so than Quake, Dusk, or You Are Empty. The level design reflects the claustrophobia of squeezing through the queues of the enormous Empire of Hostility. It always maintained the same rhetoric, sneeringly proclaiming World Peace through the clenched teeth. So, French-kiss your current Leader's portrait and enter the vile dimension, in which every elevator shaft leads to Hell, the only bar is perpetually out of beer, and where my childhood memories, doubling as my deepest fears, come to life. A life to shoot on sight.The enemies reflect the themes. Soldiers choking on vomit in their gas masks, bulky ogres in riot gear, bears to burn, БЕЗНОГNМ, demon horses, helicopters, ovcharki, homing Indiana Jones' boulders, and more. Spin on a carousel when it's not occupated by an occasional gorilla and watch out for that  in the school gym! Surrealism meets kitchen sink, an angry take on the kind of normalization that gives grotesque a run for its money. What's extremely commendable is that some foes are unique and only appear in certain levels, or are just very rare. You don't see it in your usual AAA titles anymore, where they always make an attempt to milk every asset, going as far as suggesting you push a button not to miss someone's carefully made set piece. HROT is the opposite of that approach, it doesn't care if its effort goes unseen since it's a bloody freight train of unstoppable inspiration.Except for being a gimmick for the pistols, there's no reloading. Finally! Some retro-shooters just get it, reloading was never a necessity in a world of uncanny artistic abstractions. The shotgun is great, the double-barrel is impeccable. Like the game's explosives, it leaves you soaked in clouds of blood and tushonka, drooling. Everything feels just right, just the way a grimy 90s shooter must be made. Like with that vomiting in a gas mask (sorry, no space for descriptions of tortures), there's a little story behind every piece. Take the Bolt Lightning Gun, the local BFG, for example. Bolt Lightning was a Soviet SCP of sorts, and it sure featured some grimdark lore to scare the kids! I remember being fascinated and horrified by tales about it hovering in through the window leaf and frying someone's ass. Some said it looked like a small Sun, some made up even stranger things. To have the legend in my hands, and with this context to boost, felt like bliss.So did this game, at large. Intentionally ugly, brutal, fast-paced, and containing so much raw, uncut emotion within, it presented me with a meaningful, inspiring experience, both in terms of its gameplay and setting. Despite being in Early Access, having 2 out of 3 episodes ready so far, it's a feature-full game. And it isn't janky at all! Not a single bug or glitch bothered me throughout. HROT isn't a mock-up, nor is it a mimicry, and it wasn't over-corrected to fit the present. It could've genuinely been a lost shooter from a bygone era, an actual cult hit in the 90s. But instead, it chose to be that now, when we need it the most. I award it as many medals as its sunken chest can hold.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VIDEO REVIEW:The premier in modern Slavjank FPS games! If you are a fan of the modern renaissance of old school FPS titles this could well be up your ally, but it is absolutely not something for the uninitiated and may well be a little too authentic for the general consumer.While many of the newer throwback FPS titles have tried their best to authentically recreate the feel of 90s shooters, there is an odd analogue to them all where despite their efforts it is somewhat clear that they are generally simplified Unity and Unreal engine titles, with any oddities coming from a lot of purposeful programming to recreate old exploits (strafejumping, physics objects bugs etc…), Hrot goes one further by having its own bespoke engine made in Pascal, an engine that seems to be running software rendering with its honorific ugly textures and weird lighting, plus its tinny, lightweight sounds give the impression the sound driver is badly made. Furthering this feel is the manner in which a lot of the items in game act in an extremely uncanny manner. While on the ground movement is predictable, jumping is odd. Vertical hops feel extremely anaemic, barely going 2 feet in the air, yet horizontally you can seemingly fly long distances, which creates a really odd sense of disconnection between the elements. To further this enemies sometimes do weird things like jump over walls or erratically bounce around, peddling the air as they go, all with very odd looking animations on models that just look so utterly off they would be the uncanny to the already uncanny. In this manner Hrot genuinely could be mistaken for a 1998 budget title that nobody paid any attention to, maybe bar a PC Gamer review that would give it 45% because of how much it lagged behind Quake 2 or Unreal, forever consigned to the budget DVD rack you found in hardware stores that nobody ever bought.This dedication to the warts-and-all feeling of an odd engine may make it sound like Hrot is a bad game. I would however argue against that though as its general combat design and level layouts say otherwise, meaning that it is less a lack of talent and more a pointer to where it’s inspiration lies. While titles like Dusk or Amid Evil were trying to recapture the mood of classics by Id, 3D Realms and Epic titles, Hrot is more an attempt to remake things like Chasm the Rift or capture the mood of Cryostasis: Really odd, slightly broken titles from Eastern Europe that likely did not have the time or budget to achieve their wants and ultimately got pushed out too soon. In this emulation of the feeling of these kinds of titles, Hrot excels without ever sinking into the mire of bad design: its quirky, not awful, and very purposefully so in its admirable dedication to jank. Sure, maybe the developer could have made it in a more powerful engine and ironed out all the oddities, but what is the fun in that?Here however is the issue: for the average consumer this is just a little bit too janky for most. It is well designed and the combat is a lot of fun, plus there are no bugs or badly designed moments where the player suddenly dies because of something cheap, but the dedication to jank will certainly put off many who would likely hope for a title to put Ion Fury through the ringer. If there was one element that seems a bit off it is the level design where it is a little hard to find the way forward from time to time, but those moments are limited to about 3 in the whole of the first chapter, and I cant help but wonder if they are purposefully being obtuse in their emulation of those older, more cult titles.If I could summarise it I would say Hrot is the perfect game for a slavjank fan. It smells so soviet that the game has constant references to the CCCP and the health packs are weird cartons of milk and the delicious sounding tins of “Blood & Fat”. In this if you love your weird European games Hrot is a bucket of fun! If you demand high quality across the board without any oddity to the game itself, be cautious as it may be a little bit too much for you.I am giving this a recommended rating over not recommended as it is good, just a very cautious recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I’m not trying to play every classic FPS of this new wave in the genre revival (especially since a lot of them are not good), I don’t pay attention to many of them as they pop up. HROT, though, had a curious style and a… “vibe”, I guess, that got me curious about the project back in 2021 when it was still in Early Access. Now that the full game is out and I had a chance to shotgun my way through it, I gave it a go and… Yeah, it’s quite odd, but mostly in a good way.While this title seems to draw most inspiration from Quake, there are plenty of identifiable other influences as well. The interactivity on the levels is closer to build engine games (specifically Duke Nukem 3D), there are a couple of Half-Life aspects here and there. But the visual style and overall feel of the combat is indeed closest to the original Quake, which is a great reference to stick with as it still feels great.But the game built on this clearly “influenced by” foundation is very different and… quite odd. In a way, it suffers from the classic shareware FPS issue of the first Episode (of three) being the most cohesive and well done. Not that the two remaining Episodes are bad, but they rather quickly stop giving a damn about any kind of logical connections and visual and “narrative” cohesion and become, at times, completely surreal. It starts as something like You Are EMPTY, but done well – a game with a clear style and theme, rather pure approach to classic level design, refined for the tastes of 2023 audience. But then turns into a mishmash of unfinished ideas, levels that are build as a one giant reference to something, levels that have a weird gimmick, sudden jumpscare-filled horror themed levels and whatever else that came to the developers’ minds. I can’t even begin to describe what state of confusion I was for the majority of Episode 3.It does play quite well most of the time. There are crappier (and usually, but sadly not always, one-off) enemy types, there are levels that get confusing and there are weapons that don’t feel as great as one would expect them to be (or they feel great but rarely get ammo pickups). But most of the time, it is full of fun combat encounters, cool shooting and exciting exploration. And it’s great that most (if not all) levels remain fully backtrackable right until you press a button to finish a level.Quite possibly, a lot of references, jokes and just things will be lost to many players who don’t know much about Czech history or didn’t live in the Eastern Europe when Soviet Union still existed. For me, being a Ukrainian born during that time, I did recognize a lot of things that were same or similar to my own experiences or were related to products or things that were imported from Czechoslovakia. But I also had to look up a lot of things afterwards just to understand what was that all about. Like one of the levels that’s based around a famous Karel Čapek novel that I haven’t read myself, or the nuances of the Hussite movement that I had only superficial knowledge of. It’s odd, honestly, how the game is chock-full of such things, but seemingly more just to have them instead of trying to share a story or give any kind of judgement to the era it references. It’s more about “vibes” and “member berries”. Apart from the bosses, I suppose, though even the game is more bizarre than pointed.HROT is not going to be a title I’d be recommending on the same level as DUSK or even AMID EVIL. It won’t have the same appeal as Prodeus either and, weirdly enough, even Chop Goblins might be easier to recommend because of how approachable and simple that game is. Already mentioned You Are EMPTY, for how poor its design was quite often, is also easier to understand, I feel, without a reference and strangeness overload that HROT might have. But nonetheless, I can easily recommend this game as for all its occasional poor decisions and for how surreal it becomes, not always in a good way, it’s a really fun game that understands the basics of a classic FPS design really well.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very little time played, but I feel like I've played enough to know that this is something special. The way this game pranks you sometimes is very reminiscent of half-life, and I absolutely love it. No BS simple solid fps gameplay. Remembering enemy placement within the level will help you immensely on subsequent attempts.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my absolute favorite singleplayer fps game, if not atleast tied with DUSK.Great mix of horror vibes, great levels, wacky and fun enemy designs, wild story, unforgettable bosses and maps, and some of the best humour in any game I have ever played. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to get an Early Access release for some time now. I see a lot of reviewers comparing this to DUSK which is likely inevitable, but I really think HROT is going to earn it's own respective place in the "boomer shooter" renaissance.I think nostalgia is a very powerful art design technique, and it is masterfully done here. It really does feel like you've just discovered an old unlabeled floppy disc under your bed that is truly haunted and possessed in it's own twisted lo-fi way. Some of these enemies really feel like they are straight out of the nightmarish paintings of Francis Bacon, existential, grisly, and complete abominations of nuclear disaster. Enemies will grunt and snarl from corners close by, background music will occasionally go quiet and you are left to the sound of your pounding heart and dripping (mysterious fluids?) nearby. I love this game. I'm so excited to see how it grows. I for one am glad New Blood isn't getting there paws on this one, I think it will be equally as acclaimed with this new dev team coming up to the spotlight. STRONGLY RECOMMEND.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the campaign in 4 hours, now aim to get all achivements! Great fun, I love retro FPS, Black Mesa, Dusk, Doom1,2....
