_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro boomer shooters out there right now. It's basically Chernobyl Quake, but that's okay because HROT brings it own particular flavor of 90's Drab Brown Textures to the table. It's frantic, visceral, and goofy fun. Highly recommended, a real gem here.Pros:- Crunchy, brutal combat with a variety of well-designed enemies and encounters- Bursting with creative level design, they get a lot out of the 1980's Soviet aesthetic- Amazing soundtrack- Some genuine scares mixed in with fast-paced action, changes up the pace- You can pet the dogs and feed them treats until they barf- Some laugh-out loud gags and achievementsCons: - Lots of "find the key right behind a locked door" type of progression- Stops introducing new enemies after cultists, kind of a bummer- Very punishing difficulty sometimes, you can die to some real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥- Needs a weapon wheel- Bosses are meh
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A throwback FPS that does pretty much everything right (we aren't talking about that last boss though). Doesn't try to reinvent the wheel like most throwback FPS do and because of this, it shines a little brighter in my opinion. Enemy variety is great. They all look well-designed and are fairly well animated. Though there are some...Very strange ones in there that don't make a ton of sense, but I'll leave that for you guys to find if you playthrough the game.  There's quite a few that hit hard on higher difficulties, so they do a feel a bit tedious to fight sometimes, but that's not a bad thing. If anything, it adds that sense of dread that makes you take your time and contributes to the horrible situation you find yourself in. Weapons are nice. They pack a punch, although I only found some of them once or twice in my playthrough. Namely the "super weapons" in the game. That being said, there are quite a few weapons at your disposal and they're all pretty useful in their own ways. Level design is on par with what I expected, given the dev has only ever made 2 other games, neither of which were throwback FPS. It always felt like you knew the path to the next objective since enemies would respawn on the path behind you to lead you back to where you need to be. Though, there are a few, and I mean a FEW, parts where you'll be running around scratching your head. Overall, I think HROT is a must buy if you like retro FPS games. It's not perfect, but it's significantly better than most other games in the same genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: although I was born after the change of regime (1989) and not in Czechoslovakia (but in a Middle-European country close to it), there are countless things in this game, such as the different pickups and items in the gameworld that I instantly recognized, and they are absolutely wonderful, just full of charm and soulIf you are into boomer shooters and/or you are from an ex-communist or eastern bloc country, this game is a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Another amazing throwback fps. Feels great with a soupy atmosphere and a chunky shotgun. Buying it now basically grants access to the game's first episode, and so far I'd say it's worth it. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty dang good. Levels are big and varied with lots of one-time stuff you can interact with. This was made by one guy, on a custom engine he wrote, which is nuts. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of classic doom, with it's own Slavic twist, HROT immerses you into an outlandish world without a plot- which I had only realized around 2/3rds into the game, after fighting the giant leninheads, carousels and horses, and hospital workers, and around the point of the bumper cars, where I realized there was no meaningful cohesion, despite that vague feeling of some sort of underlying idea behind it all. I think that describes part of what makes HROT so unique- absurdism underlying the concept of an idea, though with that addition of fundamental structure set up in its extremely interesting level designs. I never find myself bored with this game, yet there's something that prevents me from wanting to keep on playing it whenever it's turned off. This is perhaps more of an issue with myself, as I have far too many games inflicting with a choice paralysis, but part of me might just be unsure how to think about this game. I suppose thinking about it solely in the perspective as the absurd slavic FPS suddenly makes it a bit indistinguishable from all those other absurd FPS Doom-likes, like the recent Slayers X, Trepang2, or Incision. Despite this, I would say there's just a certain something that does still make HROT stand out. Perhaps intrigue. The fact is that even though the weapons are mostly your standard affair, they still stand out. I remember the mortar launcher much more than I do of any other grenadier weapons, the mines more than I do of Half-Life, the shotgun more than DUSK's, even the pistols too. Perhaps its for the same reasons that this game persists in my mind, despite conceptually being bland. If you haven't played many DOOM-like FPS games, I highly recommend this game. If you have, I still recommend this game, but see if you keep thinking about it when you aren't playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: At the first glance, this is a proper Quake 1 sequel we've been waiting for. But despite having great aesthetics and weapon selection, the game totally falls short in the level design department.John Romero said, "I had a rule for the designers that if they created a room in Quake and it could be replicated in Doom then they had failed". And it describes the problem of level design in HROT perfectly: the game totally ignores verticality and 3D aspect of space, its levels feel flat and boxy, and look like something that could be easily recreated in Doom. Even more, some retro shooters using Doom and Build engines (like Ion Fury and Hedon Bloodrite) have significantly better level design than HROT.I am also not a fan of combat design since almost every monster attacks you with very fast projectiles. This makes constantly strafing around the best tactic, but it quickly becomes boring and dull. It seems like the game creator didn't really think of introducing enemies with various attack patterns and then mixing them in different combinations to create unique fights. So every battle here starts feeling the same in mere minutes, especially when the game keeps spawning enemies at you almost every time you press a switch or take a key.Furthermore, the game just loves locking you up in a large room or an arena (always rectangular!) and spawning mobs around you. And all boss fights also follow the same pattern: you fight one big dude who has tons of HP and spawns adds. You might call it retro, I just call it lazy and bad design. I would rather have one boss fight in Quake over several boss fights in HROT. Seriously, bosses in Wolfenstein 3D were more fun than here. I approve of this decision, but this doesn't make the game good, and I won't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is surreal. Off the rocker. Engaging and highly enjoyable.A very good retro style FPS. Level design is superb. While the game is reminiscent of Quake 1, it keeps subverting expectations. Here's a clever puzzle, here's a curiosity, a surprise, then maybe a jump scare, an inside joke, or something bizarre. It never gets dull. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun shooter game. The level design and the atmosphere were great, and the gunplay was quite ok. _childDocuments_.review: I kinda love it? The atmosphere is easily the best part, each level had me on edge and nervous throughout. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing special, just one of the best "boomer-shooters" of the recent years. On the surface it has great level design with quick and intense gameplay, but below it is so much more. There's loads of enemies and mechanics in the game, it breaks up the simple quake-like gameplay loop constantly with totally unexpected things. It's somewhat scary, but it is much much grotesquely funnier than that. Pummel Horse miniboss? Sure. Boulder that chases you up the stairs? Its just genius. I don't want to give off to much spoilers, this game is very funny, discover it for yourself.Visually its also very distinct, all the levels are very unique, each with its own visual quirks or details. As someone who grew up in Hungary the little details are everything in this game, whether the little cloth on the television, the exact washing machine my grandmother had, or just generally the vibe of a gym. Great stuff all around, I don't think you'll ever find a retro-style fps as unique as this ever again.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A boomer shooter heavily inspired by Quake with a Soviet Czechia theme. Getting the nickname "Soviet Quake".Bit more to it than that though. Has pointless interactivity items found in levels, like a lot of Build Engine games, to add to the immersion. Game was amazingly made by one person!Highly recommend checking it out if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let´s be honest, I first thought that HROT would be just another retro shooter like so many others. But after having played through all three episodes now, I have to state that this is THE BEST Quake-like retro shooter since DUST. It´s even better than Prodeus, Wrath or Ion Fury (have played them all). The gameplay is very fluid and satisfying, the level design is AMAZING and the setting is very atmospharic and kind of fresh. Some people say that this is a spiritual successor to Chasm: The Rift, but believe me, this one is MUCH better than Chasm (which is just a mediocre, overrated shooter from the 90s, in my view). On the technical side, the game runs perfectly well, graphics are amazing (if you like low poly late 90 shooters) and quickloading is very, very fast (which I think is an essential aspect in a good retro shooter). So do not hesitate, this is a MUST BUY for retro shooter fans! Support these devs, because they are able to deliver the quality standards that games came up with in the 90s. Who else does that nowadays?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up in a bundle of boomer shooters because I wanted to play Ion Fury and Dusk. Imagine my surprise when I loaded this unknown game up and enjoyed it more than either of those two.If there's one thing this game has in abundance its atmosphere. It is unsettling, creepy and weird. When you combine that with a well made fast paced shooter your in for a good time.It's a lot of fun and very unique. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: love me some post-Soviet depression AND humor in this very well made FPS. It's just a fun little game where you fight enemies in respirator, horses in respirator, enemies in hood, horses in hood, a gym wooden horse, former secretary general of the Czech communist party, floating Lenin heads (plural). _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR buy this game, is good. Okay, this is the first time I've felt compelled to write a review, and seeing as it's in Early Access and only has been out for a grand total of one day, I just have to recommend this game. If you're on the fence about it, don't be. The gunplay, the music, the tone, all of it pitch perfect. Obviously, there are some issues, specifically regarding framerate drops during some of the mid-Episode 1 levels. However, I fully believe the developer is hard at work solving these issues as they have not only kept releasing updates all day, but also used those updates to add and change secrets for those who've played the demo already. Another thing to consider, this game has been and will continue to see comparisons to Dusk (2018), which is fair. It clearly takes a lot of inspiration from that fantastic gem. However, HROT takes strides to not only distinguish itself, but set it's own form of atmosphere. Whereas the dark humor in Dusk can be, although cute, slightly cringy, HROT's humor is both dark, and oddly quirky. Random things will occur that are only elevated if you have an acute awareness of what it's satirizing especially the historical connections to real life. Sound is also really well designed, with each creature having it's own distinct idle noise for the player to identify and prepare for. The weapons are satisfying, while also reminding you to conserve ammo and to carefully choose how to approach combat scenarios. Overall, I am very excited for the future of HROT, and I eagerly await later episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a game I really, really wanted to like, but feel really short for me. I get the "everything is brown" color scheme is meant to evoke Soviet brutalism, and it does that really well, but it makes for incredibly boring and unengaging levels. The game's tone is very mellow and flat, and while there are elements of horror in it, things like a pommel horse coming to life and firing rockets at you is too silly for the tone the game establishes. All of that can be forgiven, but the game commits the cardinal sin of FPS: The guns just suck. Very little hit feedback, really weak sound effects, and very little animation to convey power.Hrot is absolutely admirable for it's scope and development, but ultimately it ends up being an unenjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: While I like the game, there was one issue that made the experience a lot worse for me. The game simply does not run smooth. Posting this negative review as a warning for others, since it really affected my time with this game. I also tried to contact the developer about the issue, but no response within a month. Here is what I sent to the developer:Hi,I really love HROT and I bought the game on Steam to support you and this awesome game!I want to report an issue that the game is not running smoothly on my beefy PC (AMD 5950X + RTX3080). My monitor is 120Hz and while the framerate counter is showing 120FPS all the time, the actual framerate is definitely lower and fluctuating. I am very sensitive to framerates and it's very easy for me to detect that issue.I tried various things in hope to resolve the issue: changing my desktop resolution to 4k, 1080p, 720p, running the game in a window with even lower resolutions by modifying config.cfg. It's definitely not an issue with rendering performance, I have super stable 120FPS reported all the times.I also tried to switch between raw mouse input on and off, but while that affects sensitivity, the smoothness was not fixed. Also experimented with GL_HROT setting, but smoothness issue is present in both on and off state.I also found a forum post stating that too high polling rate on a mouse could cause issues with HROT running smoothly. I tried lowering mouserate to 125Hz and that did not improve the smoothness, it only introduced a slight, but noticeable latency in responsiveness.Also tried disabling GSync and tried various VSync on/off and framerate cap in the settings to no avail.Running out of ideas on what could be tried next. It does remind me of the latest Amnesia installment which was locked to 60FPS and you could unlock the cap for rendering, but mouse polling was hardcoded to 60FPS in the engine which made the whole experience 60FPS even though I was able to run the game constantly at 120FPS.HROT real framerate is varying between 60 and 100 FPS for me. Again, the FPS counter is showing 120FPS all the time. The only time I could really feel it was 120FPS was right at the beginning of second level. That lasted only for a few seconds as moving forward to the next area made the framerate go down.I hope that you will find the info provided here useful as a bug report. If you want me to try some things, don't hesitate to ask. I am technically inclined, software developer too.  Keep up the good work!Thanks,Damian

_childDocuments_.review: It would be too easy to dismiss HROT as a Soviet themed total conversion of Quake, but the game, however, is so much more. The game and its levels ooze atmosphere, the game dev clearly has a vision they're going for. Almost a must buy for any fan of retro-revival shooters (boomer shooters). As is, the game only has a single chapter available and is in Early Access, but personally I am more than happy to support a single-man project with a vision this strong and a clear drive to make a game that actually has an identity. The game runs fine (the game engine is very light and the title regularly reaches 1,000-1,200 FPS even with a lot of action on the screen) and there are no major game-breaking kinks, some oddities like hostile vehicles bleeding or killed turrets making monster sounds, but all of this can easily be forgiven seeing how stellar the rest of the offering is and how this is the first launch version of the title into Early Access.Personally I can't recommend HROT highly enough to fans of retro-revival FPS'es and will be keeping an eye on future chapters of the story and updates to the title. One of the best titles to launch (into early access) in 2021 thusfar, without a doubt!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a very atmospheric shooter similar to Quake.This game is still unfinished, so I'll provide only an opinion here.Pros:- great atmosphere - the first two levels feel like a horror genre, you don't know what's going on, yet it's scary and wicked enemies show up- good pacing - the pacing of the game is mostly OK, once you know where to go and what to do - you'll breeze through levels- music matches the levels - I mean, it's mostly dark ambient, but suits the game very wellCons:- some levels have convoluted design, but it's oldschool so it's ok- even at later levels one predominantly uses shotgun and the basic pistol, so arguably the item & ammo placement needs some review (for example SMG is only used tactically as to be honest I've never run out of shotgun shells)In general - I like this game and I'll play it more when more episodes are ready.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Calling HROT "Quake but Soviet" is selling it short. It's so smooth. The level design and atmosphere are so good. This is the type of retro FPS that should be supported and celebrated.Funny how another certain retro shooter (one that shall not be named) went into early access 4 years ago, 2 years before HROT. It charged more than HROT, and offered less. That game is still not out and has seen no updates in years unless you get excited seeing biweekly dev updates showcasing those epic upcoming new vase textures whoop-de-doo! (Yeah, you know which game it is. Well done.)Why was all this relevant? Because on the other side of early access... you have good developers who know what they're doing like Gloomwood's, DUSK's, and of course... . (Presumably) One gigathad fueled by nothing but actual player feedback and vodka, pumping out  improvements and level after level on a consistent basis throughout 28 months of early access. When people point to the aforementioned poopy game as a reason why you should never get games in Early Access, HROT is one of the few that prove the opposite by simply saying "Actually, yes it can work".Good on you, Spytihněv. Vashe zdorov'ye.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to recommend a game more highly than HROT. Every bit of it is focused, considered, crafted and honed. It's early access but there's easily enough content here for a dozen hours or more of gameplay if you play through multiple difficulties, collect all secrets and try your hand at the endless mode. The shooting is chunky and satisfying, the weapon selection covers all of your retro FPS basics like a shotgun and grenade launcher with some fun off-kilter additions.The graphics are truly impressive. It looks like a remaster of a 90s FPS game and I mean that in the best possible way. Extreme care has been taken to make sure everything looks convincingly old school, it's a treat to just take in the environments. The oppressive Soviet era atmosphere is so unique and the color palette never gets old because the developer makes level variety a priority. Enemy design is a highlight with some of the most interesting foes ever put into a game. You're never safe and your opposition makes sure to keep you on your toes.I could keep writing rambling sentences because it's hard to express how much I enjoy this game. I know I'll revisit it for years to come and if you're an FPS fan, you owe it to yourself to play this. DUSK has been the apex of the retro shooter genre for years and HROT is easily its peer. Edit for Black Friday: This game is even cheaper, 20% off. Can't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it's dark, monochromatic and unwelcoming atmosphere, Hrot is a blessing of silliness and creativity amongst Boomer Shooters, and easily one of my top 5 of this genre. I have never seen something so creative in the most weird way possible. The developer poured their soul in every corner and every map and I have enjoyed anything that was thrown at me. Simply amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review episode 3 is still in development.I had initially brushed this game off as yet another in a long line of by the numbers retro throwbacks to the days of Quake. In hindsight I wish I would have not judged this book by it's cover as HROT has shaped up to be one of the most enjoyable FPS experiences I have had in ages. Carefully crafted, well balanced and chocked full of secrets this game had surprised me at every turn with it's dedication to innovating it's own wheel. Though coated with drab art direction HROT makes every effort to make you see the beauty in it's browns, greys and beige walls.Episode 2 definitely takes some bold steps forward in terms of it's level design and outside of the box ideas, and I can't wait to see what more is brought to the table in Episode 3 in the coming year.I would strongly recommend this game even in this current state to both fans of the genre and newcomers wanting to dip their toes into the retro FPS sphere. 9/10 Legies
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: : Soviet-era Czechoslovakia and medieval Czechia. Rust, dirt, blood, and a myriad of brown textures worked great to make me feel dread in one level and spook me in another. Jumpscares felt out-of-place, though.: Easy bunnyhopping. High player speed and no hitscanners -- you can do a no-damage run on the highest difficulty. No fall damage for you -- ridiculous fall damage for your enemies. Use the kick button (mouse2) to reposition them, kick Ogres' grenades back, and save ammo, which is scarce in the first few levels of each episode.: HROT is a competent Quake clone, but like with all Quake clones, Level 1 is really similar to Level 30, gameplay-wise, and HROT can't do much to surprise you.

_childDocuments_.review: Delightfully brown. Charmingly low-poly. HROT pretends to be a lo-fi game, but the amount of care for details really surprises. It's small things that make the difference: breakable lights, interactive props.The gameplay is solid and time-proven. No nonsense: shoot bad guys with guns. Pick up health and ammo. Repeat until the end.And, of course, the atmosphere. Everything in HROT looks HROT. It has its very distinctive style.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: HROT is short, simple fun. Set in a strange soviet environment, with a odd sense of humour and doesn't pretend to be anything more. HROT is HROT i recommend.Took under 8 hours to beat the Campaign but it was extremely well paced and I never got bored. I'm certain if you wanted to, and if you don't care for secret and easter egg hunting, you could get through the game in less than half that time. There's also an Endless mode if that floats your boat. 4 difficulty modes and i found Hard to be a decent enough challenge without feeling unfair.Enemy Design was varied and balanced. There were no enemies that seemed cheap or way more annoying than any other enemy. The surprise bulldozer can go straight to hell though. What is important is that even with large groups you can tell each bad guy apart from sight alone and they are fun to blow away with your arsenal of soviet inspired weaponry.The weapons were okay enough but felt unbalanced and inconsistent.  I felt the sub machine gun in particular was barely worth using . It was too inaccurate and very weak. The lack of punchy sound effects didn't help the feeling that it wasn't worth using. The duel pistols are more accurate and powerful even though i only got them first at the end of the 2nd Episode and you'll run out of ammo for both of these weapons quite quickly. The Landmines felt like more of a hazard to myself rather than the enemies too unless you're kiting them through a doorway.Most of the time i was playing was using both of the shotguns or the rocket launcher and those were the only truly reliable weapons with plenty of ammo around. The crossbow is nice enough though and the lightning gun was great to use whenever you have ammo for it. BFG style Lightning gun was awesome but i only found one level in the game where you get to use it. Bottles of Wine felt overpowered since you could just save them all and down a bunch before a big fight or boss fight to get max health. Overall a mixed bag but none of the weapons i hated or avoided using. Just some are far better than others.The real strengths of HROT is not in pure gameplay however. It's sense of humour, the level design's ability to surprise and throw you completely off guard and it's quirky boss fights are where the game shines. It's what kept me invested in seeing the game through because i really had no clue what to expect next. There's plenty of interactivity as well with objects in the environment as well.No spoilers. The final boss in particular is just one of the strangest bosses I've ever encountered let alone how you actually finish the level and get to the epilogue. Just what in the name of all things holy Spytihnev.If you're on the fence i'd recommend waiting for a sale just because of the short length and the gunplay being fun but very typical of an average boomer shooter. It kinda kills replay-ability for me unless i REALLY wanted to beat it on the hardest mode.  However if you're interested in HROT for it's style, humour and trippy design on top of being decent enough boomer shooter then it's an easy recommend.I can safely say there is nothing else exactly like HROT. There are better boomer shooters around sure. Similar ones in style like DUSK (DUSK is far better even). But HROT does it's own thing and i like it just as much for it despite some basic gameplay. HROT is HROT and i liked it warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: I was eagerly anticipating this game and it did not disappoint me.Movement feels great, gunfights have good audiovisual feedback, music is excellent.*THIS IS NOT DOOM* don't expect a power fantasy, you will be near death often and ammo is scarce.Art style is bleak but not bland, comparisons to Quake or Chasm are unavoidable.A lot of people saying the weapons sound weak, it's an intentional aesthetic choice that I think works well. _childDocuments_.review: This Quakelike is great. Inspired by the fps greats and parodying slav jank, this game takes place in 1980s Prague shortly after the Chernobyl incident, fitting the "horrors of Chernobyl" themes well. An unnamed enemy force takes advantage of the situation and invades Czechslovakia, breaking the Orloj in the process(although that plot point doesn't come into play until late episode 3). You must leave the safety and comfort of the fallout bunker, defend the homeland from the invaders, and fix the Orloj before Prague falls. One of this game's strengths is how it handles swings in atmosphere, one minute you're fighting some enemies in a cramped room, the next you walk in on some more enemies, but these, well, these enemies are having a dance party. If you like fps game(and don't have arachnophobia) this game will be worth every penny, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: внимание внимание Comrades! HROT pronounced ha-rot is an amazing Quake like shooter set in Czechoslovakia during the Soviet Union days...Those were the days. In any case things aren't going to well and you have to annihilate the terror before you! The game is filled with European History reference, and filled to the brim with hidden secrets like any old retro styled shooter should. The game also runs on its own engine made in Pascal. If you like Quake like, Doom like games then this is for you. I have no complaints except I want expansions & hopefully MP down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is weird, at least to my own Western sensibilities. Admittedly, a lot of what might be subtle jabs at the communist past of Czechoslovakia is missed by myself. Except for the kiss. The sounds could use some beefing up, save for the shotguns.However, there's no questioning the retro-shooter that Hrot has at its core. It's pretty damn good. The industrial communist locale combined with some pretty great horror elements and solid shooting mechanics make this one nothing revolutionary, but something tried, true, and dependable. It has a good arsenal of weapons that are pretty well balanced and weapon switching to save ammo will be a great way to maintain a leg up.  And yes, the pump action is pumping wrong, no one friggin' cares.Some will may take umbrage with the abundance of brown, but the game is setting a very particular atmosphere. It wants you to feel like you're in an industrial wasteland, with your surroundings feeling both alien and familiar. It does this with aplomb and you learn to love its dreary and washed out aesthetic for this reason. The ambiance is what really completes the experience. What would be otherwise ugly visuals are made appreciable with the music and sound design. It's like salt or vinegar in a video game, here. I've never seen the effect music and sound can have on a game so profoundly demonstrated before. Map design can feel a bit dated at times, but it's never too awful. It makes you want Spytihněv to further flesh out the world and what has happened to make it go so horribly wrong.UPDATE 10-15-2021, The first two levels of the new episode are showing off map design that is really good. Also, credit where it's absolutely due, this dude made an engine that's specifically designed to look like it's being rendered in 1990s software rendering. He has accomplished it and then some.Even MORE props, Spytihněv has a DEMO FOR YOU TO TRY. A demo. In 2021. The fact that he's released a demo in a day and age when developers (read PUBLISHERS) don't want you trying it until after you've parted with your money says a lot. Spytihněv clearly believes in his product and while it doesn't mean Hrot deserves a purchase, it should deserve a look.It's pretty great and it's worth the purchase.Voted GOTY because the industry should be ashamed with the crap it puts out, now.UPDATE: 5-16-2023The game is now finished. Is it worth it? Is it worth it after years of development?YES, IT'S AWESOME. GET IT. The last episode gets even more twisted and weird than the previous entries and it makes for a bizarre but fun time. Perhaps call this Spytihněv's Bizarre Adventure?Either way, it's complete and well worth getting. This is a quality FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Played up to E2M5, the last level at the time of reviewing.HROT nails the Slav Quake vibe right on the head, but isn't perfect. Ambiance is spot-on and the gameplay is a slower pace but still fun. Levels are laid out in really fun and interesting ways that play really smoothly, but I feel like resources are a bit tight. Playing through on Hard, it's not uncommon to be struggling for ammo, health, and armor. Ammo/health economy are great ways of creating tension but in HROT it feels more like walking on a tightrope where you have so little room for error and can make some levels a chore to play. Not only are items really rare but on higher difficulties a single hit from some enemies can deal about a fifth of your HP. I think that with some tweaking to damage numbers and being a bit more lenient on the amount of items will iron out any of the gameplay problems I had. Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic soulfull and funny light horror love letter to OG shooters, has the same asthetics and similar level design as the orignal quake but it's in Czechoslovakia, i highly recommend buying it full price for anyone who enjoys level based shooters, has a couple references to stuff from the 80's and 90's so just mind that.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT truly stands out from other titles in the Boomer-Shooter renaissance. HROT is built on a custom pseudo software-rendering engine that has been tweaked and honed to recreate the PERFECT classic FPS experience. Everything weapon sounds good and feels better to use, with nothing becoming truly irrelevant. The melee weapon is very useful for a specific type of pest enemy, and the starting pistol can become akimbo if you find another. There is a wide variety of fun weapons that are very powerful. While I wish the Ball-Lightning Launcher was in more levels than just E3M1 and Endless, it is still a neat addition. The Wine bottle serving as a portable heal kit AND special grenade is one of the coolest ideas ive seen in retro-FPS as well.HROT has atmosphere, you can really feel the soviet oppression through the whole thing. The level design is truly something else, there are many moments in the game that feel like the level designer is "setting up" the player for a trap, a la John Romero's DOOM levels, and I am here for it! After episode 1, the game suddenly takes itself much less seriously. Once this happens, and the goofy soul of HROT starts to really show itself, the game just becomes a joy to play. I got 100% achievements in under 24 hours playtime with some light usage of guides and playing on Hard difficulty for my main playthrough, so HROT delivers without overstaying it's welcome (something that many other Boomer-Shooters could learn from...). This game is seriously worth your time if you consider yourself a fan of DOOM, the first three Quake entries, DUSK, or if you're just a serious alcoholic and really want to make out with Gorbachev
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a superb, brown game. It's a lot of fun to just tear around in, ripping and tearing, and if the obvious Quake inspiration is all you need to get circlestrafing then you won't be disappointed. The levels are fun, the enemies varied enough to keep the gameplay fresh with new combinations and the movement and shooting feel good. There's also an excellent sense of humour to the whole enterprise that revels in a very Czech-style dry wit combined with joyful surrealism. The episode bosses in particular are a real weird highlight and the final level peaks in the gag department in a series of superb bait-and-switch ploys that I won't spoil. An easy recommend just on the surface level.Going a little deeper, there're some very well-hidden secrets that can become fun to hunt down once you get a flavour of them and what to look for. There are also lots of achievements for odd behaviours and quirky little things unique to each level; having them pop up unexpectedly is a nice surprise and you can have more fun guessing what might trigger them.On the deepest level the game is full of cultural tidbits, hints and references that will provoke a more intellectually curious mind into learning some Czech/Czechoslovak cultural history simply for the sake of understanding some of the more oblique jokes. I know more of the history and also the national character of the Czechs than I did, because I played this game and it evoked a certain mood well enough for me to do a little web-searching. This is entirely parallel to the main experience of the game though: I was bunny-hopping and circlestrafing contentedly for the overwhelming majority of my playthrough and the intellectual stimulation didn't diminish that at all. This is after all a game for which someone somewhere took the time to record a silly noise to simulate the sound of an overfed terrier vomiting so you can imagine the cerebral side is not overpowering.It's a good game, at a good price. I don't regret a minute of my time with it. Big yes from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I can't recommend HROT. I might revise my review if that happens and I find reason to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a wonderfully idiosyncratic sojourn in Československo, or at least some fantasy version of it. HROT wears the trappings of a retro FPS, especially Quake and Chasm: The Rift, but its more than just killing. Like DUSK, you're completely enveloped into a world full of violence, but also many quiet moments of exploration and discovery. Most levels are long, intertwining mazes of corridors, secrets, sewers and exterior sections. A bit reminiscent of Heretic or HeXen. There are many well hidden secrets to be revealed by an inquisitive player. The score, by Sjellos, exponentially enhances the feelings of lurking danger, oppression and confusion evoked by the HROT and its visual identity. HROT is the complete package for those looking for a fun to play and unique FPS experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Just feels like an overall weak experience. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing this game for the most part. It's very satisfying to run through the post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe landscape and the humor is really on point (at least for the first two episodes (for me.)) You play as an unnamed soldier trying to reclaim his country from all sorts of nightmarish abominations. The environments have a lot of objects you can interact with which encourages you to explore. The game has a humorous side as I mentioned before but for the most part it takes a backseat to the horrors you face (until the third episode.) For me the guns are all satisfying to use, although I do prefer the grenade physics of Quake. The best compliment I can give this game is that it feels like a Quake mod, a very good Quake mod.Episode 3 is when the game drops in quality for me. The goofiness gets dialed up to 11 immediately. I won't even spoil the absurd things you encounter as I do think it's worth experiencing for yourself. It honestly turns into a joke .wad at this point. The level design falls off a cliff too with the only two design philosophies for this episode seem to be "haha so random" and "spawn a lot of enemies when you pick up a key or pull a lever." Now don't take this as me crapping on the game because I still love it and recommend it to anyone like me who grew up loving games like Quake, Unreal, and Half-Life. It's worth it even at full price. I would be interested in trying something else from the dev in more of the same vein of Episode 1 and 2 with more of an atmospheric horror theme.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2 is my all time favorite old school shooter. It blended horror, action, mystery, and exploration perfectly. There were times the game was terrifying, keeping you on edge, wondering if that next pickup is a trap (it always is). There were times you were strafe shooting around an arena, dodging fireballs and pumping shotgun shells. There were times you wanted to know what happened here, with the environment telling a story that in game logs never can. And you were rewarded for hunting for secrets, without them being mandatory nor too difficult to find at least a few of them. If all of this sounds amazing, you'll like HROT. It ticks all the same boxes of Doom 2, plus some additional humor thrown in from time to time. It's in early access, but there are a decent number of levels available at the time of this review. Get it, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a retro FPS game made by Spytihněv and takes place in an alternative version of 1986's Czechoslovakia.The game takes obvious cues from Quake, Chasm and even a bit of S.T.A.L.K.E.R, both in terms of art direction, VFX and even sounds, but it's more than that. At first, Brutalist Soviet Czechoslovakia can seem a bit...simplistic, but here's the trick : you take Quake intricate but simple level, and you fill them with so much detail you quickly forget it's a Quake/Chasm-like. The fourth level, Sokol Gymnasium is a brilliant example of that, where you start in a sewer, then go up in an area filled with small businesses and some appartments, then you head to the gymnasium (where you can play football alone like any social-awkward kid that grew up in Europe).And then you have the MEAT, the gameplay. It's tight, precise, fast-paced, and simple yet extremely satisfying. You just shoot and dodge your way through flying sniper heads, pistol-wielding grunts, shotgun-wielding people in hazmat suits, even the grenade launcher fat dudes make a comeback from Quake ! No iron sights, no zoom, you don't even need to crouch, even to enter vents !The weapon models are also pretty nice and you can feel they pack some punch too.Sound wise, it's brilliant, except for weapon sounds that need more basses to sound more...meaty. There isn't too much music, but rather atmospheric pieces that help setting the gloomy tone of the game.Overall, I really look forward to complete the first episode and I really recommend this game, as it's one of the best bang for your buck retro FPS, and shaping to be one of the best !...Civvie's sewer count is going to commit die.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Now at first glance, this game looks like a soviet Quake but its not. It reminds a lot of Quake in how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brown everything is, but it's so much more. This game is awesome, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. Possessed Excavators, cursed horses with gas masks, inanimate objects that shoot rockets as bosses, and the weirdest yet kind of fitting final boss, this game has it all.The weapons are pretty standard, you have you pistol(s), shotgun, machine gun, super shotgun, rocket launcher, and a BFG that is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous and makes the sky thunder when used. Both shotguns have weird and janky animations and are probably the two worst things in the whole game. (After the sewer level...) You'd think that a game this brown would end up being bad but it fits, because the best part of Hrot is its atmosphere. Instead of banging tunes hyping you up as you plough through the levels, you get an eerie atmospheric soundtrack - again, reminiscent of Quake - that is actually really effective. All enemies look cursed as hell with their gas masks and hazmat suits. Especially the horse, don't get me started on that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horse...I can't wait to see what episode 2 holds, so support this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Quake. But fun as hell. Even though quake is great and hrot doesn't have a much different take on the key elements, I'm enjoying it way more. _childDocuments_.review: Brown Eastern European QuakeA really outstanding retro shooter; dark, bleak and gritty, encapsulating the Soviet doomer aesthetic while featuring an outstanding attention to detail, moments of complete hilarity and legitimately amusing jump scares. It's also completely filled to the brim with obscure Czech references that I had no hope of even noticing until I went to the wiki and found the trivia. Chapter 3 ending was a bit mid but oh well.My favourite moment was breaking into someones apartment and finding out there was a working model train set in the back room. My second favourite was desperately running through a cemetery escaping endlessly resurrecting skeletons to get to a shed, only to open the door and immediately be charged by an evil bulldozer. Third is feeding the doggos too much that they barf in a comical fashion.Might not be everyone's cup of tea but I personally love games created by insane eastern European boomers.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely cannot wait for more content in this game. HROT has to be one of the most fun singleplayer games I've touched in a long time and that's saying a lot, with only eight levels and an endless arcade mode at the time of writing. The maps are very Doom-esque, the creator clearly has some knowledge of how the level layouts work, with the masterful backtracking, keys, and secrets. Enemy design is fantastic in every one of them, and while they're all easy to avoid, I like playing on the hardest setting, where their strengths can really shine through. It's fun to die, it's fun to learn a route through a stage, where to best use your equipment, just like running DOOM maps, and I think that's why HROT has so much value.Something unique about HROT is its mode where you can randomize guns and enemies within a level, sometimes making you struggle to make your ammo count work and other times getting overpowered weapons in areas you wouldn't normally. Gunplay is incredibly important to an FPS game (after all, what else are they for?), and HROT nails it. It's not so fast to be a blur on the senses, and not so slow to be outright boring. It hits the perfect pace with the perfect weapon design and every kill feels, *nice*, in some way I just can't put together. Maybe it's the satisfaction of blowing back the big guys with a point-blank shell, how the explosions and grenades act, the way enemies don't attack while on fire, letting you focus smaller threats in a group while the big guys burn up slowly. HROT is really something special and if the quality keeps up through more maps or weapons I could very easily see this being one of the most tight-knit and satisfying singleplayer games I've touched. Already we had a rocket launcher replaced with a crossbow and that new weapon feels amazing. The creator has such a nice formula down and I am YEARNING for more; let me boot it up and run through the campaign for the twentieth time, hang on...
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend playing the demo for this game (it's free, why not?) before you continue reading the reviews. It gives you a good idea of what the gunplay and basic enemies are like that you encounter for most of the game.One thing that this game excels at is easter eggs. There are very, very many of them. In the final game, Vyšehrad (the demo level, but finalized) has eight secrets to find, not including the references. The horse boss you fight, which seems like it came out of nowhere, is actually a reference to a Czech story where a knight escaped Vyšehrad by jumping over the walls with his horse, named Šemík. There is plenty more of this stuff in the game, but I don't want to spoil anything more.The guns are not necessarily the most unique from each other, but that is made up for by the shooting being super good and the controls being responsive. Practically everyone I've seen so far has commented on the guns sounding weak, but I don't really mind (except for the electric beam gun, I think that one needs something more zappy).The enemies are all very unique from each other, the closest, on paper, being the Smaskou, the standard raincoat guy, and Skapuci, the wizard raincoat guy (which are not really all that similar in-game at all). Enemies sometimes don't fire at you for a second or two, which is kind of dumb, but it's not really too much to worry about. I would advise to play on medium difficulty or higher.The graphics are an obvious homage to the shooters of the 1990s, with it's brown color palette. Not much to say about them, except that I think they're pretty good.ultimately, just play the demo then decide if you want it or not (just remember that, at the time of writing, there's about 300 positive reviews and only 3 negative reviews)

I realize now that Hrot is more inspired by Chasm than Quake but I digress, this game is one of the best throwback boomshoot games i've ever played. The attention to detail, the humor, the interact-able set-pieces, the ambushes, everything is handled extremely well and done in a way where you can really see the developers love for the genre. This game has now been fully released and it's worth every penny. Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: (EARLY ACCESS REVIEW FOR 12/07/2022)SYNOPSISHROT is a first-person-shooter set in the wonderfully grim and bleak 1986 Czechoslovakia. You have no name and your only goal is to destroy the hostiles that reside there.GAMEPLAYIt's traditional FPS goodness with some thriller elements thrown in. Run, shoot, find secrets and kill enemies as you explore various locations. Weapons are your usual pistols, shotguns, submachine guns to the explosive grenade launchers and lightning canons. Your enemy variety is quite expansive, from the Soldiers, Mutated Animals, Cultists and a horrific combination of all 3 thrown together. PRESENTATIONDon't be put off by the all brown / grey style, it actually works REALLY well for this kind of game. The feeling of dread, despair and grim shines through in the best way as the feeling of "something horrible happened here" starts to creep in. MISCIf you've finished the story and want more to do, you always have secret hunting, endless levels and of course Steam Achievements to work through.This game also doesn't demand much in terms of hardware. I was able to play the demo relatively smoothly on my laptop without having to alter any settings.Overall I recommend this game if you're in the mood for a suspenseful shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: is an interesting retro shooter game that is set in Czechoslovakia, an eastern european soviet country at the time in an alternative timeline, where the country is filled to the brim with monsters.- Great 90's aesthetic, you can choose the resolution to your own liking to make it as pixelated or as crispy as you'd want.- The atmosphere is gritty and dark- Soundtrack that fits with the atmosphere- Maps are designed well and are fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just finished Hrot ...and that was wild!If you've played Dusk or original Quake this will feel familiar but Hrot is a unique experience totally separate from anything else. The action is twitchy and brisk but not generally frenetic. With fewer monsters than either of the above games, it sometimes feels like a survival horror mixed with a Saw movie.Hrot also maintains an oddball sense of humour, leaning into its Soviet era theme with passionate detail and full of eccentric situational gags....And inanimate things suddenly lunging at you.Hrot is an intense boomer shooter dripping with character. _childDocuments_.review: You'll either love this game, or you'll hate it.Hrot is a love letter to original Quake, but with some of the rougher edges smoothed out and replaced with some Quake II and Duke Nukem 3D style.     It must be remembered that Quakes 1 and 2 were *all over the place* thematically.  They didn't bother you with tonnes of exposition, or cut scenes. They didn't have long procedurally-generated open-world areas. They were tight, focussed action, with an emphasis on keeping the player moving.So, if you like your graphics spangly, and your levels looking like they were rendered on a Cray supercomputer, Hrot isn't for you.  If you want to have lots of high-paced fun in the original Quake style (yes, including the brown-ness), then play this game.  It's not incredibly long, but even on 'normal', it's quite a challenge. You're a little more vulnerable through most of the game than you are in Quake.    Sprinkled throughout the game are loads of funny references to Czech TV shows, little historical events, personalities, authors. There's also amusing setups, and recipes keep popping up.   It's definitely the work of a fevered imagination.  I loved it, but then, I'm an OG Quake fan :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is of course an early access game at the time of my writing this. It's possible the as yet unreleased levels will blow my mind (or suck).Initial impressions? It's good! The atmosphere is dark and compelling. It's definitely a solid Quake+ clone, but that isn't an insult in my book. The guns are from Quake, the monsters are from Quake with some later surprises, and the level design is Doom/Quake-ish.If you are just getting into this particular vein of retro-fps, then I will always recommend you play DUSK first (even before trying the nostalgic originals, DUSK is that good). But if you know what you like, and what you like is classic shooty-bang-bang, you can't go wrong with HROT.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Episode 1 during its launch weekend (and having previously played the demo months ago), this game is already shaping up super well and I'm certainly looking forward to what the developer has in store. As of making this short review two new weapons were added and he has begun addressing one of the few complaints I had prior to the date of this review (namely he is updating the weapon sounds to be punchier, as previously weapons like the shotgun lacked a certain oomph one might expect, at least in the sound department).One of the biggest compliments I can give is the atmosphere alone is already quite stellar, with the game really nailing the oppressive feeling I'd expect from something set in 1980s Eastern Europe, and that air of mystery I got from games like Quake when I played them for the first time (though the levels in HROT are a little closer to something like Duke Nukem 3D in that they're clearly designed to have some level of realism, as opposed to the semi-abstract designs of Quake). Gameplay-wise the game may not deviate too much from what one might expect from a shooter that is following in the footsteps of games like Quake or Chasm: The Rift, but this is hardly a negative as I value fun and intrigue more than originality.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I review the game, here are my relevant biases: I'm a fan of HL but not many other 90's boomer shooters, and I'm not Czech. Hrot is outright the strongest "games-as-art" shooter I've ever played. It's also pretty hard and pulls no punches, mitigated by unlimited saves (at least in the difficulties I've played.) The entire play experience is best described as nightmarish (as in replicating the experience of being in a nightmare), pulling together cues from pop culture, motifs and styles completely alien to most players outside eastern europe, and incredibly strong sound design to create an atmosphere of dread. This spikes to terror when the game throws waves of enemies at you, coinciding with dramatic music and even lightning flashes. It's not clear if you're running away from something or towards something, but the fast-paced gameplay lends the whole experience a frantic vibe. All this is done with minimalist storytelling.Update: I wrote my review during early access. The third chapter is here, and the game is complete. I really can't find anything to nitpick about, since the final chapter is just as polished as the original two chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this one, though it's not without it's drawbacks.Pros:- super tight movement/controls- satisfying gun play- tons of secrets/Build Engine - esque interaction- level design/layout is very well thought out and tightly knit. - Super unique, sometimes funny enemy variety (horse man, bulldozer of death, etc)- immersive and comprehensive atmosphere/tone----------cons:- though it's effective at setting the vibe, frequently similar locations/textures/color schemes makes for a very "samey" experience, level to level. - Level design *is* really clever/solid, but the samey environments make it easier to lose thread of your goals than should otherwise be the case. -----------------------------------If you're looking for something with that Quake-feeling gameplay, this is gonna deliver. _childDocuments_.review: Let's be clear right away in saying HROT is not finished, and buying it now is an investment for the future. My playtime clocks in after a bit of achievement hunting and playing on Hard, so if you play on an easier difficulty and don't care about hunting achievements too then your playtime will probably clock in around the 3-3.5 hour mark right now. If you prefer to have a full game right now instead of a game you'll come back to for major updates, do a rain check on this one. However, if this isn't a bother to you, HROT is worth it, with a few caveats."Slavic DUSK" is a phrase that gets thrown around a lot and whilst it's becoming a cliche, I have to agree. Playing this and DUSK back to back reveals just how many lessons and direct design ideas HROT takes from David Szymanski's seminal work and this isn't a bad thing, generally. For the most part HROT learns all the *right* lessons - boss fights that aren't overbearing nor overly complicated, an arsenal that is varied with one or two creative elements but, for the most part, conventional, and enemies that are challenging but not unfair. Arena design is similar, too, with smaller areas and larger spaces where the combat occurs. The story is, like DUSK, surrealist and more of an excuse plot than anything. Soviet experiments gone wrong mean you, a more or less ordinary citizen, need to go fix things up. Best of luck.I'd say the main places HROT stumbles right now are areas where DUSK excelled, and whilst HROT does innovate a little in terms of its own style, the obvious shortcomings from emulating such a well-rounded title but failing to execute the same ideas as well rear their head. Secrets are plentiful but bloody obscure, even for someone who has played secret-focused shooters for decades. When you do find them, they aren't always worth it - the most bitter example was cracking open a wall with an explosive grenade, only to find a measly small health pickup within. Many secrets are exceptionally tucked away - beyond reasonable levels of finding them yourself, even if you're looking for them - and unfortunately the "shifting walls" secrets that DUSK used to great effect to reward observant players are almost nowhere to be found. Gun feel is also very diminished with unimpactful animations and weak sound design. One or two weapons - the shotgun and grenade launcher - were quite satisfying, but everything else generally felt lame. A lot of weapons that, again, seem here because of lessons learned from DUSK are weaker, less memorable, and less interesting, and I'd argue the only stand-out weapons that were unique were the tesla weapon and the BFG equivalent. Both were exceptionally rare in gameplay and also not terribly satisfying to use.Much of what I've said above can be excused, I believe, because of HROT's early development, and as far as I can tell this is the first time a game like this has been made by this developer. It's a good start, and I enjoyed my time so far. There's a gem to be made here, if enough refinements are made, though right now it's a mixed bag of potential and flawed execution. Give it a go if you're feeling lenient and otherwise keep an eye on where it goes from here.

To be honest there's nothing this game does that's new or original (I mean the enemy design and aesthetics are original, but from a gameplay perspective nothing new). _childDocuments_.review: Well, I don't know what to think lol It's like Quake meets Dusk meets Chasm? It has a lot of references to places, events and people that I'm unfamiliar with. Goes right over my head. I think if you're someone with a familiarity to the history of the Soviet Union you'll be able to appreciate the game even more. But that doesn't really interfere with the core game, which is awesome.The level design here is great. You're unlikely to get lost. You can move so quickly through these levels that I had to make myself stop playing at one point out of fear of finishing it in one sitting. The levels are tight, and have a lot of neat details to find and interact with.I've only played through it once, on normal, and I didn't get nearly all the secrets, and I haven't tried out the endless mode much. That took me ten hours, so there's definitely a good amount of game here because I don't believe I'm done with it.I would recommend going into the options and increase the "color" slider. It's still going to be brown, but it's much more saturated and generally looks better, I think.Overall, I don't have much to say about this game. Not because there isn't a lot to say, but because I think what's good about it is the same as what's good about every retro FPS game: great level design, fun combat encounters, interesting enemy variety, secrets, atmosphere, etc. The bosses range from wacky to insane and definitely got a big reaction out of me several times. If you like the demo, you'll like the game. If you've played a handful of the other retro FPS games and feel like you just can't get enough, this one is definitely worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after pirating it at first, it was back when there was only the first episode. I was filled with the sorrow from the fact that the game made me to fall in love with it whilst having so little, played it several times on several difficulties opening all secrets, admiring quirky map design and great atmosphere, i could feel myself getting pulled into the Czechia, from soviet style apartment complexes to grand churches and castles. I decided to buy it without a slight doubt and never regretted it after. If you like Quake style gameplay with various enemies and weapons for any occasion, good level-design and not overly serious but convincing atmosphere i cannot stress enough how much id recommend this game. Also urge you to play any map with secrets at least twice, once without guides for secrets and other time with guide, secrets can be often tricky to find and to this day i cannot remember all of them. secrets, believe me or not often change the course of how you play the level, see it for yourself.Preferably the game should be played on hard/very hard if you enjoy a challenging game, though if you do not enjoy dying often Normal is completely fine difficulty to play on!I'm very grateful to devs for making this masterpiece, nothin' will ever replace this game, it will truly always stay in my heart as a dear memory that i might pick up from time to time. TLDR:just buy it, now.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent boomer shooter in a Slavic setting. Every minute detail is polished and done very well. Classic old fashioned gunplay is awesome and feel good. Level design is great, every single mission feels different and unique, there is a lot of old-school hidden secrets, so keep your eyes open. This game is odd and weird but in a good and fun way, there is a lot of enjoyable interactions with everything, with enemies, bosses,  secrets, references and just all sudden stuff that can and will happen, you can literally form a dog gang and be their leader and pet them, that is something. Story divided into 3 chapters, there is enough missions, but maybe for someone it could possibly be too short, but it doesn't really matter that much. Last boss is one of a kind, it's a must see. _childDocuments_.review: Have you played Dusk? Did you enjoy it? Good, this game is a lot like Dusk but with Polish history and setting (as accurate to reality as Dusk itself is). It combines a lot of the same high quality of life aspects of Dusk and PS2-ish era of graphics with a polish twist to bring new enjoyable first person shooter challenges and puzzles. With any luck the game will see full release by the end of June, so a lot to look forward to.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A retro shooter in the truest sense. Hrot makes no attempt to modernize the traditional formula unlike its many contemporaries, instead focusing solely on being the greatest soviet love letter to shooters of old it can be and doing so with flying colors. Don't mistake the drab look for a lack of character either; this game oozes atmosphere and is not afraid to get as goofy as it is brown at times. That coupled with excellent level design and enemy variety elevates Hrot well beyond a mere faithful imitation of its 90's inspirations, placing it firmly among them as one of the greats.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good and fun for the most part, but I recommend the hard difficulty or above for more intense fights. It's fast paced and has a variety of guns that are fun to switch around during fights. The pixelated style graphics and atmosphere go so well together, creating a haunting vibe. If you're into Quake, Doom, or Blood then I consider giving this game a chance. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: i know everyone is comparing this game to dusk, but I actually think they make a great contrast representing different ways of doing a modern quake-style FPS. while dusk is open, flowing, and fast, hrot feels considerably more claustrophobic and gritty. ammunition is scarce, health is even scarcer, and the silly big-tent-spooky aesthetic of something like dusk has been effectively replaced with a grim loneliness that gives the game an oppressive and apocalyptic atmosphere. i'm excited to see where this goes in future episodes especially, and what other types of levels feel like with this engine and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "Maybe" button. It's good, well polished and interactive but just not my cup of tea. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, my time with this game has been marred by constant audio issues. Most of the time I have a constant popping sound that I have never had with any other game. Other times I try to boot up the game only to have no audio at all, forcing me to restart. As you can guess, trying to play a game with constant audio crackling in the background is not the optimal experience. It may very well be an issue on my end, but regardless it saps all fun out of playing. As for the game play, that is another area I was disappointed in. Guns don't feel as punchy and satisfying as they should, and movement felt too sluggish and limited. Enemy variety was ok in the short amount of game time I was able to stand. Unlike some other reviewers I actually don't mind the color palette, map design, and aesthetics; I love the soviet sci-fi/ Stalker vibes I get from the game, which is why it's so much more painful to observe it's issues. It all comes down to this--it just doesn't feel good to me. There is something missing from the gunplay and general gameplay loop that leaves me wanting. I do not think Hrot is a bad game, but maybe it just wasn't what I was looking for. Top comments are claiming this game is a communist Dusk, which I find very misleading. For those prepared to purchase Hrot, play the demo first, because it is really nothing like the fast-paced, frenetic boomer shooter you may be expecting. Again, this isn't a bad thing, it just leaves something to be desired in it's presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun shooter with a unique (and weird) premise. Really looking forward to it being completed.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing boomer-shooter with a creepy doom meets soviet union vibe to it. _childDocuments_.review: HROT is a strange, waking nightmare.It's beautiful in that terrifying, liminal way of challenging art. _childDocuments_.review: Hrmm, this one is a bit odd. For full price, I feel like I would've been a bit disappointed since, while it is charming in some ways with its unique aesthetic and odd quirks, the core gameplay and level design was pretty basic and bog-standard. _childDocuments_.review: What a strange game. This is a great game if your are an avid fan of the FPS Genre. It has solid fundamentals but neither the art or gameplay are going to be breathtaking. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I dont understand the hype. The game lacks fun factor, and a clear-cut identity.Shooting mechanics are awkwardly slow paced but not fast-paced arcade goodness. There's no fun movement mechanics either. I say this as somebody who thought DUSK was pretty low-mid tier, but it hardly lives up to DUSK in the raw mechanics department. Health and ammo felt overly scarce as well, and my shotgun felt like it literally just did RNG damage. SMG also felt awful (even when the pistol felt like it did it's job better) but I'm willing to accept that I had scrub aim when I played it. but in total weapons felt like they lacked impact due to poor sound design, scarce ammo, and weird inaccuracies.This game is brown. Like, WAY too brown. This makes levels are extraordinarily bland and boring, they really crave a secondary color like red (which would still thematically support the aesthetic of dilapidating communist eastern europe). The enemy design also confuses me. The grunts are all fine, albiet quake clones (hey, don't fix what aint broke I guess). The bosses are dumb, however. It seems clear to me it's not really going for a "mystical"-type setting, so when objects like bulldozers and a gorilla statue become possessed/alive and start attacking you, it's just awkward. I really like the concept of the grotesque head-type enemies. They're white instead of purely gray which gives them an aesthetic that sticks out. The only issue is that I feel like the game doesn't lean HARD enough into this. I understand this is just episode 1, but give me more subtle storytelling a la HL1 about how and why these things exist and I would be a lot more interested in the game at large. I will at least say there were a few things I genuinly really enjoyed. I liked the translation feature as it really immerses you in the area without making it impossible to read everything. Being able to kiss portraits on the wall was pretty funny, and the cosmonaut part was also funny (you'll see it if you get there). And I think the game's setting has potential.And lastly, if you're genuinly reading this negative review, I want to you to really consider if you *enjoy* this game, or are just getting caught up in the hype circlejerk. If you look at the positive reviews, you'll see people who probably never even touched OG Quake 1 blindly worshiping the game as "le epic communist DUSK." I think this game has its fair share of very overt flaws, which makes it extraordinarily boring, and not worth purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pure joy to play. Each episode is full of creepy, hilarious, and downright bizarre moments. If you are debating the purchase of this game, let me ask you: Have you ever battled a sentient, rocket-shooting gymnastics beam? A gas-mask-wearing horse? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ KING KONG? I mean, you get an achievement for flushing poop down a toilet.Humor aside, the map design is incredible. Each map is a labyrinth of both open and claustrophobic spaces intertwining with one another, along with hidden rooms containing cool gear and weapons. As others have mentioned, games like DUSK have wide open areas with hordes of enemies. In contrast, this game swarms you with enemies in both open and tight space, something very unique within Quake-style games. For example, one of the boss fights takes place in a single small room.I cannot wait to see more episodes added, and highly recommend that you purchase this game if the demo even SLIGHTLY interested you. The demo is great, but I would check out some gameplay videos, as the full game has so much more to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of gameplay, it is like Quake but set in Czechoslovakia and you're under influence of mushrooms and alcohol. Very solid retro-style shooter with good gunplay and decent level variety. Full playthrough should take around 3-4h, add extra hour or two to that if you are checking every corner for secrets and Easter eggs of which there are many.Strong recommendation if you like "boomer-shooters" and don't mind very brown colour palette, this game is absolutely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan already - been following this one for a while (mostly due to other people's connecting it to DUSK, probably my favorite shooter of recent years). Played through the demo a couple days before release, and pretty solidly went through episode one when I could get my hands on it. Most of my issues are relatively small, and carry over from playing the demo: I find certain levels to play much better than others - I certainly found myself lost often, often looking for a single stray powerbox (keep your eyes open, seriously), and the sound needs some work (a lot of the guns lack any real sort of punch, imo). I also, at points, found enemy placement could be a bit frustrating - But these were relatively minor criticisms/problems for me. I am excited to play more. The game is dripping with atmosphere, from the general aesthetic of the locations to the enemy designs, and its hard to not get sucked in and go through the whole chapter immediately. Would recommend a play through the demo - if it seems like it's up your alley, the first episode will not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Yes, this is only one episode, and - being a slow gamer - I spent 4 hours with it. So yes, the price might seem steep to you. But this is Early Access, meaning you pay for what you get and what you will be getting in the future, which is at least two more episodes and we'll see what else will be happening.As for what you can get right now: A good game. Check out the demo first, after that you'll know what you're getting into. It's brown. It's weird. It's also heaps of fun. The dev, who is active on the Steam forums and thankful for constructive criticism, shows great creativity (apart from the color palette) in enemy- and level design, and all this in a new, self-coded engine!Will it remind you of Quake? Sure. Will it feel like Dusk at times? You bet. Did the dev take inspiration from Chasm: The Rift? Most probably.But HROT is a good game all on its own, it's fun as is and shows a lot of promise for its future development.Again: Check out the demo. If you hate it, you will hate the game. If you like it,  get it while it's HROT.
