_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend Hrot, with a few reservations. At it's core, the game is fantastic. The levels are atmospheric, oppressive and appropriately dreary. The enemy roster is distinct, inventive and has clearly defined roles. The guns, after some sound and balance overhauls, are fantastically fun to use. The real star of all of it though is the soundtrack and ambient drone that accompanies all of it. Top notch stuff. The developer is also very responsive to feedback, which is much appreciated. Here comes my reservations though: The game is really, REALLY stingy with ammunition. Which is fine as a balancing element (Especially for the highest difficulty), but rarely did I feel in the first episode were you given a chance to just let loose and not have to count every bullet to get by. I feel like a slightly shift in ammo drops to give you slightly more ammo for weapons introduced in the same level and less correspondingly for other weapons would help a lot to alleviate this and give you more play with the newest unlocked toys. In Episode 1, there's a handful of instances were the way to proceed is to shoot an object in the environment. Every time this occured it felt poorly telegraphed and unintuitive, which was not helped by the general stinginess of ammunition pickups. Making the interactible object pop out from the environment more would help, as would giving you more "cheap" ammunition (Pistol/SMG) close to these objects. Mind, this whole issue might just be me being both blind and stupid. The enemy behaviour when traversing from different elevations and from water is also a bit jerky and weird, but it seems like that is being worked on.While sewer levels are thematically appropriate for being naturally both dreary and brown, they're still not that fun to navigate. So hopefully we'll see less sewers in Episode 2.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice, especially has great "feel" and controls; and clear graphics (in its style of course) and interesting levels with coherent themes. It has little interactive story elements which I like too. Look forward to the third campaign when it's ready!Few suggestions: Some of the secrets are very hidden, might be worth giving a little more in the way of in-game hints/visual nudges. I also never quite got a sense of ammo availability for the various weapons; also don't think I ever actually learned to recognise visually which ammo packs were for which weapon, which might have contributed to that. I'd also have liked a bit more "wind-up" for enemy attack animations, especially melee attacks - they feel instant now. It'd be a tiny bit easier but it didn't feel right to me.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is simple but fun boomer shooter. The atmosphere captures a sad dystopian (Czechoslovakia) close to the USSR. The setting suffers from an unknown radiation insident in 1986. There are enemies like monsters and people in radiation suits that are the result of the radiation insident/fantasy and come in a good amount of variation. The gameplay includes your typical range of weapons, Schyte (melee), Pistol, shotgun, smg, launcher etc. Although the gameplay is easy and staightforward to understand. The main enjoyment of this game is the atmophere and fast paced action. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is clearly one of the top 5 retro-styled / old-school-like first person shooter-games I played in the last years. Don't be afraid of the amount of brown-tones. There is no big variation in the colour palette, but this contributes to the whole atmosphere of the game. What I didn't expect was the amount of humour the developer put into HROT; this lead to a special twist in almost every map. And, dude,
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I feel I need to comment on this game, because of how great this game is. It took me 8 hours to play through it, and I am sure it can be played faster as well as slower. I played to whole game on the second highest difficulty and I very much recommend this difficulty. I absolutely love this game. I love the fast style, the weapons, the enemies, the achievements, the design, the creepy, dark environment, the balanced management of amuntition so that I had to think about using different weapons during combat that better suits the situation. Everything feels perfect. Each chapter gets better and better, and I was constantly surprised and on the edge by developers inventive idea through out the game. I do not want to give anything away, but all I can say is that everyone who decides to play this game will enjoy every minute of the game. Only thing that I have to criticizes is the lack of dialogues from the enemies in Czech, but that is my personal opinion. I would love to hear the enemies have some czech phrases or comments against the player, during the encounter or during their deaths. There are a few such dialogues from a couple of enemies that I can think of, but I would definitely want more.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROTs quality is like, when you want to cook, but have barely any ingridients left in your kitchen and babushka comes over to help you out. With her help it becomes a decent meal. You think to yourself, if babushka had more spices and other ingridientns, it could've been an excellent dish. But before you lies a dish that is "Not great, not terrible" just decent.HROT knows overall what it wants to be as a "boomer"/classic shooter and it does what it has to do.- Gunplay feels nice for majority of the weapons roster (e.g. explosives, shotguns), but for the few other weapons (Pistol and smg), they felt a bit like peashooters and lack responsiveness. - Base mechanics are solid with strafing, kicking objects/Grenades and enemies, but imo it could've a bit more. Jumping and especially nade jumping lacks a bit of verticality and/or speed. I would've also liked it, if you could kick more projectiles of enemies back.- Secrets are hard to find without map and feel sometimes barely rewarding, Example: There are hidden buttons in form of bricks, that are barely noticeable due to the color palette of the entire game. You manage to get it open after 5 minutes of wallhugging and spamming e and what do you get? 5 hp.- The visual style, from its sick mutated, radioactive look of the enemies; and the titbits of the game world create an interesting setting. - Also the crude humor the game has, as what enemies you can encounter, made me first jump out of my chair and then laugh about it. Those oddballs in the enemy roster appear rarely throughout all 3 episodes.- I liked the overall level design, not too long not too short. The campaign structure is btw the typical 3 episodes with x levels in it,If I would rate it out of 10, it would be like a 6,5/10. Like above mentioned "Not great not terrible", there a couple of boomer shooters I played, I had more fun with, but this one is still recommendable.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Quake but if the Ranger was living a Slavic-induced nightmare. One of the best retro shooters I've ever played, some great atmosphere, a nice blend of comedy and horror, fun gameplay with some interesting puzzles and minigames, unique enemy designs, and an Orloj clock, which is the game's hidden story.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, generally the boomer shooter category when approached is either really good or flat out mediocre and this game was pretty great. I loved how over the top some of the enemy designs were and felt like they had pretty unique identities. The final boss was truly a sight to behold and stuck to the theme of being flat out ridiculous, fun, and over the top. This game to me was a title that really stood out to me as far as boomer shooters go and I would love some sort of sequel 8.5/10 I wish it was longer!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If on the fence, feel free to download the demo. As of this review, it showcases most enemies, weapons, what I think is one of the better levels available, and the endless mode which is almost 1:1 with the first episode release. Also keep in mind that this is currently an investment as at least two more episodes are planned plus whatever other additions come.HROT is a very promising oldschool-style shooter that focuses more on the claustrophobia and grittiness you could find in the Quake era, and with its scratch-built engine it's about as authentic as you can get. And it offers some unique customization options such as screenspace weapon placement and scale to tweak what you want out of it aesthetically.The setting is very unique and leads to nice setpieces and plenty of excuse for open arenas. However, my biggest gripe with HROT is its level design and encounters, which I feel don't take enough advantage of its enemies or the unnerving atmosphere that the game can create; the bosses are also somewhat same-y, however they're still quite entertaining, especially the Episode 1 final boss!An exception to my gameplay gripes is the endless mode, whose constant waves of random enemies and items lead into situations of pure chaos and panic, that I really wish would be replicated in the campaign levels. I understand these issues of mine are largely based on taste, and HROT as a whole is an excellent foundation that I'm certain will evolve and be more than worth the asking price. I hope for a level designer in the future.TL;DR, you should try out the demo, and you'll certainly be investing in an evolving product, but I believe the end result will be worth the price and it's a quite unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an acquired tasted.After watching Civvie's video on it, I decided to give it a swing and if you don't have nostalgia for the Quake era of gaming, I can't imagine this game as much to offer you. The gun play is very weak, your guns feel inaccurate and limp. As this game draws on nostalgia from the early 3D boomer shooters, the failure of the gunplay kind of unravels the rest of the game. Shotgun is probably your most impactful weapon but it's damage is inconsistent with the classic gaming shotgun with 5ft range. The grenade launcher is the runner up for impact but that's also lessened by it's really weak blast range and damage, and since you can only carry 30 at a time, unless the enemy numbers significant or packed together enough. You might as well just shotgun them.Secrets are interesting to hunt for, but it seems to be drawing on wolfenstein more than anything since alot of secrets are just press E on a wall, and the best way to find them are with your map so a viable strategy  is just to run around rubbing your face on a wall until you see an opening on the map.The game is kind of dull all round actually, it's so boring on the moment to moment that some of the more outlandish moments are met with a flat "Huh." You encounter a robot monkey or a sentient vaulting horse and it just doesn't electrify like the game seems to expect it will.I plan to push through and finish it, but it's very telling that the only time I really perked up and enjoyed myself in this game is when I found an old handheld on the floor and got the highscore.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is one of the best indie shooters I've played recently. Whether it was the incredible atmosphere or the fun weapons, HROT always managed to be enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: Like others have alluded to, HROT is like DUSK with a Russian twist. I think the comparison is fair, but overlooks the fact that the game engine was built from the ground up supposedly. You can drive a moped in the second level which really activated my almonds. It is super impressive to see how optimized this game is and how much interactivity it allows through the custom engine. It does seem like it borrows inspiration from DUSK with the sickle and the quake-like graphics, but I think it's coincidental considering the soviet atmosphere and that destructible environments aren't uncommon. This game reminds me a lot of quake and the amazing atmosphere reminds me of S.T.A.L.K.E.R., but I think the fact that this game exists is a testament to the fact that there are amazingly talented devs out there with great insight into what makes gamers tic. This game in my opinion is superbly original where it needs to be and for the price at the moment (with the 15% discount) is a freakin' steal. Considering the amount of replayability and upcoming 2 episodes, I think this game deserves to be in the library of any gamer who enjoys oldschool FPS games. I am super excited to continue following the development of this game and in that respect it truly will be like experiencing DUSK again. I've played through the first two episodes so far and was thinking about what fixes or improvements would make this game better, but as I was typing the review, my nitpicks were so small that I forgot. The quality of this game overshadows many of the small issues that are pretty much non-existent, which is rare considering how games launch these days. This is a great use of early access listing and I cannot wait to see the improvements and updates made to the game. I think that there is so much room for this game to be G.O.T.Y. material truly. I would definitely recommend it currently.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing 90's inspired FPS. Its immediately apparent how much love and care went into faithfully recreating the look and feel of a retro shooter, so much so that there were genuine moments that I felt like I was playing something that I somehow missed when I was growing up.From the get-go the game just oozes style. The quake-style low poly art paired with the dour post-apocalyptic setting is a match made in heaven and really goes a long way to evoke an oppressive and haunting feeling while playing. The gameplay is pure old school; you run and gun with no reloading, levels are labyrinthine and filled with enemies, and there are tons of secrets to uncover. There is even a respectable amount of interactivity with the environment, not unlike what you would find in Duke 3D.The game is in early access, but don't let that deter you. What is available to play is incredibly solid with the promise of more to come. With that I give this a high recommendation, if this is your style of game you wont be disappointed in the least.UPDATE: After now finishing the full release, I can say that the developers delivered an amazing experience, with each new episode topping the last. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I don't really like boomer shooters and I've never played Quake, Chasm, STALKER, or Dusk, which it seems like most reviews are drawing a comparison to.But I really like this game.The setup is simple; you're a person on a mission to push a button at the end of the level. To get to that button, you'll need to find a series of hidden keys to pass through a series of doors. And of course there's enemies the whole time that you'll need to shoot. The game doesn't try too hard to push the boundaries of this formula, and instead focuses on creating a tight, quality experience with the few moving parts it has.The level design is interesting, and I was never really lost or confused despite the game being almost completely brown. The puzzles aren't particularly difficult, but solving them while clearing enemies is very satisfying. Weapons can be found in every level that will help you push through the tough parts, and they are placed thoughtfully so that you get them right when you need them.The enemies in this game are also really great. There are maybe 10 different types that are all interesting fun to fight in their own distinct way. The AI is smart enough to jump on things to get to you, and when they shoot at you it feels both challenging and fair.My one nitpick is that the save system is sort of weird. The game allows you to save at any moment, so you could technically just save before and after every major fight and cakewalk through the whole game. It also carries your stats/inventory over from level to level, so if you finish level 1 with 44 health and a grenade launcher you will now enter level 2 with 44 health and a grenade launcher. BUT, it doesn't autosave at that point so if you then quit out and start level 2 later... you're back to square 1 with 100 health and a dinky pistol. After accidentally doing this to myself twice, I just committed to never using the save system and finishing every level in one go with a fresh start. And actually, I liked this much better. Starting with only a pistol forces you to look for better guns, which have been thoughtfully placed around each map seemingly for this very reason. And once you know the rhythm of a level, most of them can be beaten in a few minutes anyways. I just found it a little strange that the levels are all individually loadable and carefully designed to be doable without additional weapons, but then the game also allows you to just savescum and snowball your weapon collection through each level. These two design decisions kind of clash and it made me a bit confused about how exactly the game was intended to be played.All in all though this game is very cool and fun. It took me about 10 hours to beat every currently available level (episode 1 + the first level of episode 2) so I feel like I got my moneys worth already. I can't wait for the rest of episode 2!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start with a confession: I f*****g hate Dusk. I know it is an unpopular opinion, but to me it's one of the ugliest and the most overhyped FPS games I ever seen. The fact that it made a wave in boomer shooter scene says a lot about how desperate people were for some oldschool action. I will never understand how can anyone set the bar so low to just accept that arid level design, lazy texturework and a goatdamn 4-faced sticks as weapons models.Having said that, I do love HROT. It's an answer to the question what could have been if Dusk had a soul. If it was made with a coherent aesthetic style true to the 90's shooters. If it was made by someone with an actual talent, not someone selling mediocrity disguised as retro stylistic. Someone who cares enough about their vision of a game to make an actual effort.If I didn't know any better, HROT could pass as a genuine product of the late 90's. Its custom engine and brown texturework go perfectly along with the setting of the soviet era. It's also heavily inspired by Quake with the general vibe, enemy types (down to the dimming of screen when you're getting hit by flying enemy's projectile), as well as weapons (there's even a thunderbolt analog) - but usually with a weird spin on them. The resulting gameplay is good, feels familiar and offers fair challenge due to the lack of healing supplies, which may be as well a comment on supply scarcity of the portrayed era. Level design is very competent as well.I might not have lived in those times for too long, but I do remember Chernobyl catastrophe as a kid and and I'd say that the author really nailed the overall feeling of those times. In levels there is a myriad of subtle little things and details that someone who had lived in communist block will instantly spot and recognise, with a sort of an amusement and dark familiarity.Overall, I literally have nothing negative to say about this game. I guess it may not be everyone's cup of tea - for someone too young or born outside the cultural ring of central/eastern Europe HROT may feel weird and abstract, but even then, it's a solid retro fps title worth recommending.At the moment when I write this review, 2 of 3 planned episodes with 8-9 levels each are available, plus an endless mode. It's about 5+ hours of gameplay at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Principally, this is a Slavic Quake with a very Soviet flare, but it's much more than that.  The attention to detail and interactivity of each level is impressive as is the atmosphere.  Thankfully, only special enemies are tanky due to the fact that we've long since overcome the technical limitations of Quake's era wherein you could only have so many polygonal enemies on screen without completely tanking memory so the combat loop is a lot more satisfying.  It is difficult, though.  On hard difficulty, you'll be terminally low on health and ammo.  You have to use your movement options and make good use of the terrain to isolate groups of enemies.  The level design is top notch, albeit...it's very brown.  Very dull.  Ugly.  Harsh.  Very bleak and Eastern European which is the tone, I guess.  It fits, but I'm a fan of a wider color palette than mud and diarrhea.  That said, the game is cheap, fun, and it plays well.  If you like movement shooters, there's no reason not to try this one.  Quake still plays alright, but it's showing its age.  Hrot takes up its mantle and expands on its gameplay, atmosphere, and interactivity.  There's also a gas mask horse and gorilla.  Don't ask.  You're better off finding out for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I like Quake. I was expecting some fun Quake-ish movement/shooting but with gas masks and soviet references and, yeah, that's what's here but HROT manages to be genuinely unsettling. There are some mild jump scare-like encounters but there is chiefly a lot of eerie atmosphere and times where you're thinking "oh ♥♥♥♥, what is going to jump me in this next room". There are clever uses of music, foley, lighting, and mechanics to convey mood... a spooky mood. Most of the time the game made me think of a world where S.T.A.L.K.E.R was a boomer shooter, which is high praise coming from a guy who loves both of these kind of games. The game has a very strong sense of atmosphere and a surprisingly large amount of environmental storytelling. You're able to read pretty much all of the text in the game and can interact with many objects (soccer balls, cans, old game & watch style toys). All the little stuff like that helps bring the world together and really convey the fact that the places you're moving through used to be lived in and aren't the carefully constructed videogame levels they really are. HROT is a very immersive experience despite it's aesthetic being that of a 90s shooter, which just goes to show that immersion is not about realism but rather drawing a player into the world you've created and it has certainly drawn me in.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A great old-school shooter that mixes Quake 1 style of gameplay with the Soviet atmosphere of doom and Gloom — set in Czechia, so you still get the gothic cathedrals right between the brutalist appartment buildings. The game is pretty early in development so far, and doesn't have a lot of content, but the first episode has left me wanting for more of this. A game certainly worth of support in its early access form, with hope to see the full version one day!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short. HROT is another game in the wave of recently popular "Boomer shooters". It takes place in Czechoslovakia of 1986, where something has gone terribly wrong. Like almost all shooters in this subgenre, the game doesn't hold the player hand and doesn't do much in terms of storytelling - instead relaying on level design, its enemies and occasional boss fights and jokes with some pieces of lore to carry it.Here some of the game's problems lay, as I don't think most enemies the game has are capable of enforcing different weapon usage and adoptive play style - there is literally one tactic that works on 90% of enemies, which is a shame, as it may make the experience somewhat stale at times. Bosses most of the times are too easy as well, but at least they are not bullet-spungy and each time they have very creative, absurd designs (although they are also most often based on Czech culture, so I don't fully understand them).However, what certainly manages to carry this game, especially in the second half is its settings and loads of absurdities based in Czech culture or further even soviet-block reality of 1986. And while - again - I don't think the gameplay is as good as it should be and the story and lore is so loose and obscure it's pretty much impossible to keep track of it, the gameplay is still solid enough, while the level design and settings successfully manage to carry it till the end. It is an impressive achievement - especially considering custom engine it is using and a game that slavs with interest in boomer shooters should definitely play.

_childDocuments_.review: I love HROT. It's great to just walk around in. I love the mystery and Soviet gloom of the first episode. The software-rendered aesthetic is just so perfect. _childDocuments_.review: This game is browner than quake but an absolute masterpiece in its own right. While it starts with the bleak grey-brown atmosphere of an eastern bloc city you'll come across a variety of other environments throughout the game. The general color scheme will remain, but locations and atmospheres run the spectrum from oppressive to downright bizarre. And of course at the core lies a rock solid shooter of the boomer variety. You shoot the dudes, flip the switches, get the keys and progress through the level picking up weapons and power-ups along the way. 10/10 easy recommend for anyone who likes that sort of thing. For anyone else, it's cheap, try it, it's good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: After the first wave of the "new retro shooters" (Dusk, Amid Evil and Ion Fury), a million such games came out but very few of them I found to be actually enjoyable. HROT is one of the great ones. It's a tightly designed shooter, with incredibly slick level design, solid arsenal and gunplay and a profound sense of identity.Spytihněv crafted a deeply Eastern European game, written in a custom Pascal-based engine, if I understand it correctly. The visual experience is, technically speaking, quite faithful to games such as Quake or Chasm: The Rift, and even artistically HROT adopt much of that often ridiculed "brownness". The fact is, that the almost oppressive quasi-monochromy is claimed as an idiosyncratic identitary element. HROT is, and I quote, "set in a small socialist country neighboring Soviet Union (Czechoslovakia) after an unspecified disaster in 1986. Those times were dark and terrifying and so is the game". This Steam store presentation doesn't lie. The game does whatever it can to immerse you in a bleak and hopeless world, with ominous ambience, oppressive greys and browns, imposing, uncaring Brutalist architecture and more. If often feels suffocating and hopeless. All of this is amplified by the fact that yes, there are monsters roaming around, and supernatural elements, but HROT's world isn't really that much different from the reality that many people lived through in the URSS and neighboring countries during the Cold War. It's a brutal game world, but just one step outside the realm of harsh reality.The atmosphere is so strong that HROT could probably be considered even too oppressive and alienating to actually enjoy. Luckily, there are elements of levity and humour sprinkled throughout the levels, often completely absurd, surreal or otherwise distinct enough that they feed into the identity of the game without breaking its immersion.All the other elements like the shooting or further observations on the levels themselves, while integral in a shooter, almost take a backseat when discussing HROT. Suffice to say that those elements are indeed strong here.I would absolutely recommend the game to anyone that's looking for a competent, even excellent retro shooter, but if you are even remotely interested in this type of setting or you care about playing distinct experiences full of character just buy the game at full price. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Give the demo a shot!Episode 1 out in EA with an endless mode, it's one of the best in the latest retro FPS craze, EP2 & 3 will eventually come out but solo dev with a family life in the middle of a pandemic so be patient and understanding!A ton of personality, charm, atmosphere and individuality despite the clear influences. A solo developer who put in so much effort into little details, both environmentally as well as in gameplay, interactive elements, making combat, movement, music, level design, all feel excellent.If you like Dusk, Half-Life, Quake, Chasm, old Build games, you should absolutely pick this up.I feel like the dreary brown really fits, it's done in a consistent deliberate fashion, with I think just enough shades here and there, which help with making the game easy on the eyes, you always know what you're looking at. Enemies, though also fittingly brownish, still stand out and don't blend in with the environment, making the gameplay feel like everything is easily signposted and critical information stands out at any given time. I was really surprised by how good the moody soundtrack is, just fits and sounds so wonderful, I wonder if even that is composed by the solo dev?Level design feels really satisfying, the way labyrinthine pathways loop back on some more central area where you need a key, the layers, not being just a flat plane, the secrets that are really rewarding to both figure out and what you usually get out of them.The 1986 Soviet controlled Czechoslovakia theme and setting also looks really good, the blocky brutalist buildings, the dirty concrete, the poverty of it all with no baroque extravaganza on display, just functional enough.It can get a bit samey; sewers, underground tunnels, some facilities, factories, streets and stores, but I don't know, somehow I don't mind it that much, maybe my opinion will change if 3 episodes will feel like this, but I'm not sure if I will get sick of it, as long as each episode does shake things up in some way, doesn't have to be environmentally.Weapons include a sickle that hits surprisingly well, even tiny rats! A reliable pistol that you can dual wield and feels great. Your workhorse shotgun that works at decent ranges, has a nice spread of a lot of pellets, feels strong and is strong in how it pushes enemies, knocks them down or straight up gibs them. A submachine gun which also is nifty, though ammo is scarce for that one at the start. An excellent rocket launcher which uses your grenade ammo, which are also handy in a pinch, detonating on impact, or good around corners. A really powerful nice super shotgun that knocks enemies really far. A lightning gun which is neat, could use maybe a bit more flare but gets the job done, and a BFG, a fun lightning ball launching device with a fun detonation effect.Some people complain about the sound effects of weapons, personally I like them, and even if they're muted, I just automatically excuse it subconsciously as fitting the theme of being these cheap knockoff soviet mass produced weapons that mainly get the job done.Still I think they feel really satisfying to use, many elements come together in making the combat feel rewarding, from movement, weapon animations, particle effects and muzzleflashes, ejected smoking shells,, hit feedback in knockback, slight stuns, blood spurts etc.Balance feels surprisingly good, normal feels like normal, still tense and at times challenging, but doable, ammo never at max (so far) but I usually have had enough for every single encounter, big and small, health pickups are just enough to keep me going and strafing will keep you alive for a long time.The game is fond of Doom 3 monster closets, but they haven't felt overly unfair, I expect them, I can see where usually enemies will pour in from, and, if I at all remember that I have them, I can place some land mines in preparation before picking up a key, triggering the enemies to come out.Special note for lovable goofy enemy designs, the game is a perfect balance of being spooky and not taking itself too seriously.Bosses were a bit on the easy side, but still fun, didn't take itself too seriously, silly yet threatening in behaviour, final boss felt like it had a really nice tense buildup to it, well scripted reveal in my opinion.Dev made their own custom Pascal engine from scratch, it runs silky smooth, takes only 100mbs of space on your harddrive, loading saves is instantaneous, looks surprisingly gorgeous despite the old-school feel it goes for; the architecture, enemy design, weapon design, little shaders for windows and metal, rain-fog-dust-particle effects, animated skybox, animated wobbly water texture with neat ripples, a rich audioscape filled with rainsounds, metro sounds, humming machinery etc to bring the world alive, fire that can spread a bit and linger and have dynamic lights, the smoke from fire, lovely grainy gradient to lighting and colors overall, ejected shell casings, the blood decals that can drip from the ceiling, the impact effects, enemies getting knocked back or even down, gore, breakable objects, AI that can zig and zag and not just mindlessly go straight for you, drivable little scooters...You get the idea, it's really feature rich, not much missing and has a lot we either take for granted or only expect in our pseudo-immersive shooters like Dusk, Ion Fury or Half-Life.A good options menu, some odd things like no numerical values for FOV or resolution, but at least those exist as options, alongside vsync, fps cap, fullscreen, brightness, gamma, renderer - Excellent Hud and gameplay settings, toggling all ammo counters, camera animation and strafe tilting, tweaking crosshairs, hud scale, weapon position & scale, message location, setting if switching to new weapon or always on pickup, a bunch of neat QoL stuff to customize, and good bindings as well.I've had no issues, the game feels really polished, haven't encountered bugs, and the game just looks, feels, sounds, is so good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most minimalist games I've ever played. The music is mostly just basslines and drum beats, the animations are simple, the enemy designs are simple, the levels don't make large elaborate background set pieces a lot of the time and you can tell there's just an infinite void outside of the intended walls of the levels you explore, in general this game displays itself in a very very minimalistic manner, but it's not a problem to me. It managed to be fun, interesting, scary, silly, and just intriguing throughout it's entire experience, despite it mostly being brown. Like seriously this is the brownest game I've ever played. It also has no story at all, it's simply a Czech art piece about Czhechoslovak culture in the late 1980s. It's really worth checking out just for the unique strangeness and unseen cultural vision that this game lets you enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t really write reviews for games much, but HROT is fun and unique. _childDocuments_.review: I wasn't impressed back when it was in Early Access, and although little has changed fundamentally, it has managed to win me over years later after hitting 1.0. The game's strength is found primarily in its level design. While a number of "old school" first-person shooters make the mistake of throwing you into arena after arena, HROT has the hallmarks of classic FPS level design that we all know and love. Secrets aplenty, consistent and logical progression through exploration and backtracking, and areas that feel like they attempted to be as realistic as possible with the technology they had at hand back in the day. Its setting and visuals don't gel with me as much as I feel like they should and the graphics are too rudimentary to really provide too much of an atmosphere, but on the gameplay side of things, it's terrific despite its imperfections (namely some off difficulty balancing and weak feeling weapons). It is short, though, so buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a bespoke and fascinating piece of work. It's a fun and interesting shooter with lots of replay value and easter eggs to find. It's also a nostalgia trip that relies not on rote repetition of things you've seen before like so much in "nostalgic" games, but rather a masterful distillation of the qualities of those things and what made them special and interesting at the time. HROT's nostalgia respects your intelligence, in other words. Combined with a poignant and powerful political message at the heart of its latter chapter especially, HROT is a game that truly reaches the standard of what I would call "art" in the videogame space.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it came off a relatively small magazine's CD filled with Quake 1 mods, maps, models. As you extract the mod from the CD, you read the readme file, where the author describes themself going to the science class to create levels for Quake, starting out with just leveling what they knew and then turning it into an art project. An art project to show the grimness of a dystopian presented as an utopia, but only for those who didn't ask questions. A society where the party men are talking about equality, yet showing immense corruption. Asking for complete obedience while looking down on everyone, who they say are their equals. It's a game that portrays everything through it's levels, the presentatation and the bleakness. It's not a graphical restriction, it's a choice that everything looks like it is rusting, like there is no colour in the world. And while the maps are a feat in of themselves, it just doesn't have a lot else going for it. If you loved the entry levels to Quake, where it presents it's monsters, architecture, scope and colour, you will enjoy this. It's atmosphere is insane for such a low fidelity game. If you want something more than that, it just isn't there. It's a feat, though, it's a statement and it is well done and I feel like that merits enough for a recommendation

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through the first two episodes so far (it's still early access, the third isn't out yet), and I have to say I am enjoying myself immensely.  It's Quake, but somehow even more brown, set in soviet-era Czechoslovakia, with a lot of ridiculous enemies and silly notions peppered throughout, and yet it still manages to have it's genuinely scary moments.  There are loads of secrets (I still haven't found nearly all of them) and collectables, a decent variety of weapons, and some interesting levels.  There are even some amusing interactive set pieces (piano, cello, organ, and anacrhonistically, a playable Game & Watch, plus some miscellaneous other things) that keep things interesting throughout.A highly entertaining retro shooter overall with some great humour thrown in.  Just be warned, you're in for a whole lot of brown.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... Weird but fine. You never, ever get a story, but that's somehow ok, the world is brown and grim, and everyone wants to kill you, that's all I know for sure.The gunplay is solid, and you never really run out of every ammo, so you always have enough to take care of enemies, but, there actually somehow seems to be too many weapons instead of too few. Two of them in particular rarely even come up, and their ammo is basically nonexistant, those being the lighting guns. Two of them just fill holes that don't actually exist, those being the crossbow (which you'd assume would be the sniper, but no, it does less damage than the basic shotgun) and the mines (which are hazardous to use when everyone has melee attacks, quake grenades, and shotguns/the equivalent to assault rifles).The levels themselves are varied and well-built, and though they're all key-hunts, they're less-so hunts and moreso just level progress blockers so you do everything in the right order, which is fine considering the clear setup and timing this dev has. Turn a wheel infront of you that doesn't make immediate sense? You either get attacked by a low-damage enemy to get you to face where the key is, or you passed by a gate earlier. This applies to everything except the cursed 4-switch puzzles with their solutions SUPPOSEDLY in the environment, though I only found the pictureframe one, and brute forced all the others because they don't have their answers as obvious as those picture frames, totally killing the pacing the 4 or 5 times they come up.That being said, there's only one level that kinda sags in quality, and it's the penultimate one, where you get 3 arenas that last as long as the ones in Boltgun, and it... Sucks very slightly.Other than that, there's random teleports, tons of small interactible fun things, wacky bosses that make no sense, and it all just leaves me... Confused. Clearly there's something going on, clearly a story just progressed, but you're gonna leave feeling uncertain about what you just experienced. 9/10, cause it's still a very solid and well-made shooter and clearly doesn't necessarily need coherency or a told story to succeed and be good. If anything, the questions and mysteries just make it that much better, since it doesn't really go over the brink aside from the first level of the third chapter, and even that gets explained away without words.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to preface this review by saying that I had previously left a negative review on this game because I was soured by the ending. In some regards I still do find the ending of this game to be too meme-y and short sighted for a game of HROT's quality, but after receiving a humorous reply to my review by the wonderful developer, having some time to think about it, and recently replaying this game and getting all the achievements, I have to admit my first review was far too harsh. This game is legitimately incredible especially considering the game is developed in the developer's own proprietary engine. As a boomer shooter alone HROT is already impressive in terms of its balance, level design, aesthetics, music, and gunplay, but the little interactive elements in each of the levels really show the developer's passion for this project which lifts the game to be something greater. I would absolutely recommend this game to anybody interested in playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm up to the Uranium Mines on Hard, about two-thirds through the campaign, with enough gameplay experience to write this.There's no beating around it, this game's 3D textures, color palettes and sound design were clearly 'inspired' by Q1. Not that that's a bad thing though, this game definitely evokes the same fun atmosphere. There's inspired, and there's copying, and I'm gonna say that HROT lies on the borders of copying, as when I was picking up and scrolling through the weapons it did seem a little too close to Q1's system.The most noticeable divergence here lies in the location, which is somewhere in Communist Yugoslavia it seems(to my foreign eyes). A lot of references to Lenin(whose pictures you can kiss - wth), and the blocky buildings of the era are well-represented by the 90s graphics engine.Bosses have clear life meters, perhaps I'd enjoy more immersion if they had a more visual damage model(eg dropping limbs) instead to indicate failing health.My big gripe here is probably the level secret placements, which seem to use the 'odd textured hidden wall' method a lot of the time. I normally average half to 2/3rd of secrets found per level most FPSes, for this game I'd get only 1 or 2 out of the 9 they sprinkle around. Not that they're necessary to win the game because..Of the quicksave system. Which I abuse on a whim. Baby steps forward, if I feel like it. But hey I guess if you're gonna copy Q1, it's part of the package.All in all, feels like if a couple of Q1 devs decided to do a baby side project after returning to their home country, inspired by their native history. For us on the other side of the screen, something light and easy to pick up for a couple hours.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a boomer shooter inspired by the original Quake and an old FPS called "Chasm" (not to be confused with a Metroidvania of the same name).In HROT you are in Czechoslovakia fighting a roster similar to Quake and DUSK as enemies consist of what appears to be Possessed/Zombie Soldiers, Mutants, and pure abominations as the world appears like it is being pulled into a portal in the sky.You will likely feel this game seems more similar to Quake than DUSK due to the color scheme, enemy roster, and heck... even the grenades look like they're straight outta the original Quake.

_childDocuments_.review: For lack of a better phrase, HROT is a throwback FPS with a soul. That doesn't mean the game is a 10/10 masterpiece; The weapon feedback is a little lackluster, the level design is unpolished, and I can barely remember any of the music. But HROT makes up for those issues with how much it keeps the player on their toes. Enemies can be very lethal, to the point that only taking a few stray bullets will result in dying. That danger pairs really nicely with the level design, where the clearly Slavic urban inspirations get warped by all the key hunting and hidden nooks. The cherry on top is that HROT has an understated sense of humor, which makes the tense encounters and backtracking all the more enticing. This game isn't my go-to pick for anyone who wants a throwback FPS, but I will happily recommend it to anyone looking for something with a bit more flavor.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I am now a proud owner of a pack of prague ratters.Hrot might look like a visually bland game at first, but it is actually a very good quake like or "Boomer shooter" that has really good movement and gunplay. The visual style is dreary and takes place in a soviet era nation which is why every thing looks so bland and depressing, a common theme and artstyle among slavic devs or games inspired by slavic cultures. However despite taking inspiration from that sort of depressing and dreary style, the game is filled with a good amount of humor and silliness. The aesthetic never really gets old or jarring and works decently well, and despite the limited color palette it's easy to tell things apart from one another.The sound design is a bit of a mixed bag though. The music is very good and atmospheric, and the overall ambient noises work quite well. However some of the other sound design, particularly for some of the weapons sounds pretty weak, making them sound like airsoft guns. Enemy noises and grunts do a good job of letting you know when they're around, and mostly sound distinct from one another so just from sound you can tell what enemies are nearby or just spawned.For gameplay the game does a good mix of arena and exploration combat, there are plenty of secrets to be found and enemies to fight along the way. It does do the gameplay loop of having to find keys and usually you'll have new enemies spawn when you get to them to make sure the map isnt just empty while you're going to the proper door, ensuring you are reliably fighting enemies. This doesn't always work well however as there are several points where you'll press a button or get a key and enemies will spawn right next to you, which can feel a little cheap.Overall though for $20 as of this review, this is a very good game that's a lot of fun and feels pretty replayable.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic old school FPS - would strongly recommend. The game plays very much like Return to Castle Wolfenstein but without missions and stealth. The weapons are fun to use. Enemies are interesting to fight against. The artstyle works really will with the soviet theme of the game. There are plenty of amusing secrets and intractable objects to find in all the levels - exploration and trying to activate everything is rewarded.The game is broken in to 3 chapters with a variety of levels. Some levels are narrow corridors where you just go from A to B, some are puzzle-like where you'll loop back round the same area a few times, some are arenas with enemy spawns, and some have unique bosses. Each level you'll be thinking "what next" and the game never fails to deliver throughout the entire journey.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Recently, I saw Civvie 11's YouTube video which was a roundup of retro styled first person shooers in early access and found out about HROT. Watching the footage of the demo, I immediately downloaded it and played the hell out of it until the game was released in early access on Friday and I spent the majority of the weekend playing it. After playing the entire first episode, I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed the time I've spent playing HROT. It definitely nails that mid 90s era, Quake style first person shooter gameplay it strives to recreate. I know I've heard a few complaints about the drab, bleak color choices for the game, but honestly, I think they're fine and really fit that bleak visual style of Cold War era desolation in the Eastern Bloc. My only real complaints are that the ammo is a bit scarce, which could be a stylistic choice, leaning into a survival aspect due to being set in Soviet era Czechoslovakia, but I do feel there are quite a few portions of levels that would benefit from having a bit more ammo available. The only other complaint I have is the sound effects can leave a bit to be desired. The weapon sounds in particular to my ears lack a bit of punch. Some of the enemy sounds and the player death sound also leave a bit to be desired. They just seem a bit too subdued.  These are very minor gripes, however, in what is a very good throwback style First Person Shooter. If you are a fan of Quake, or Chasm:The Rift and want to scratch that itch to play something else like it, look no further than HROT, as I feel you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Never knew a few shades of brown can evoke so much, but the game depicts its communist eastern bloc setting and atmosphere perfectly with so little. I wish modern games AAA would attempt this as well, but fortunately we have boomer shooters to rely on. And this is definitely one heck of a boomer shooter. The movement feels great, though the jump is a bit weak and takes a little to get used to. The guns are nothing new, but they're all fun to use, kicking enemies is fun and exploring and pressing E on every wall in the game to find hidden walls and secrets is great (>.>). The enemies are varied enough and they get more surreal, along with everything else, as you progress. The ambient music is effective at building up the atmosphere and the game is surprisingly spooky at certain points with a few really well done scares (and not just jump scares). Definitely recommended if you like boomer shooters and/or lived in Eastern Europe as a kid.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 The positives :- the atmosphere is good- enemy variety is good- neat niche features- lots of unexpected behavior from the enemiesThe Cons :- Dogs are enemies- only 2 of the weapons are actually useful in combat- the pitiful jump- enemy teleports are nearly silent and hard to hear- enemies hit a bit too hard (I played on normal) - health is scarce and barely heals anything- too many secrets that are hard to find (I know they're called secrets but they're hidden too well in my opinion)- I feel like there was more work put into the niche features (the functioning clock, the game and watch mini-game, the soccer field, etc) rather than the feel of the gameplay- levels feel like labyrinths and are a bit large for this kind of game- armor feels like it does nothing or at the very least barely anythingIn conclusion this isn't really a bad game. I just don't find it to be my cup of tea and wouldn't recommend it outright. Also a lot of the ideas this game has are fine. I personally think they were done better in other games.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: While I fully intend to play the third episode when it comes out, I have to be honest. I have a lot of problems with this game in it's current state.-For one, your character feels simultaneously heavy and floaty. It's hard to explain. The jump is very weak and only seems to go 4 inches off the ground yet you're still able to make the landing or just float up to a slightly elevated platform. I'm not quite sure if it's bad or just strange and awkward . In regards to the shooting, many of the guns feel very soft and not impactful. With the exception of the explosive weapons I feel as though I'm shooting cotton balls at my target instead of hot lead whether it gibs them or not. The smg especially feels underpowered and the sound effects are quite weak.The enemies are cool and fit the setting extremely well (which is good too) they just seem pretty dumb. Sometimes, they'll kind of zig zag up to you for a couple seconds before deciding to shoot at you. Their attacks have little feedback so It does't always make it like I'm actually taking damage. Despite their attacks feeling weak when they connect, enemies just SHRED your armor and since armor is quite rare you'll spend most of the game unprotected. Healing via drinking wine is great, but I just wish there were more health and armor pickups in the levels so i'm not constantly smashed and staggering around. Enemies also have a very frustrating habit of spawning right on top of you during an arena battle, but that's for later. In addition to being dumb, most enemies are easy to kill so you'll only have trouble if you're fighting many at once or if the environment is working against you. -Which brings me to the level design. Hrot has an amazingly grimy and creepy setting, added to by the eerie ambiance. For the most part, the levels are real-world locations repurposed  into competently designed fps environments which feel lived in, but now abandoned. Issues arise when you and your enemies can just clip right through railings and other such obstacles. Enemies can also just shoot you from atop or below a grated floor, and compounded with the fast-paced shooting and (let's be honest) super-brown aesthetic, you're gonna have a hard time locating the target before you get a facefull of bullets and bombs. The game also relies far too much on traps. It feels like just breathing causes walls to lower and for you to get blindsided by some weak monsters that you had no way of seeing coming. This is especially egregious in episode 2 in which nearly every level is jam-pack with traps that just serve to take a chunk of your health off. -Arena combat is also poorly handled. Normally in a shooter with arena battles, the game waits until the player is inside the arena before filling it with monsters. And when new monsters are spawned in, there's clear audio and visual cues to indicate this has happened. Hrot spawns in monsters constantly with no such easily-recognizable cues. This is made worse by the fact that new monsters just spawn in out of nowhere once the first wave has been dispatched, which can cause the player to have monsters spawn right on top of them so that they take unavoidable damage. -There are some really frustrating/annoying design choices as well. I fell like the game uses collapsing floors a bit too often and it starts to loose it's impact and surprise after the fifth in the same episode. The underground levels especially were quite painful. There is an enemy in the bestiary that's literally just a boulder that will, without fail, instantly kill you on contact. Just run away, right? WRONG, bucko. I was running away from a boulder when i dove into a room on my right, thinking the boulder would roll past the doorway so I could proceed. But, much to my horror, the ROCK did a 90 degree turn INTO THE ROOM and UP THE STAIRS to splatter me. It was funny in retrospect, but it also felt like I was unfairly killed for no reason. On my second try I dove into the water below a metal bridge and the boulder was nice enough not to grow gills and swim after me. I can only conclude this was the intended way to do this sequence. Really just a boulder-shaped bruh moment. -Episode two did have one absolutely superb level. Granny's Valley was cool for a plethora of reasons. Giving the player a brief driving segment with other vehicles made the world feel more alive. The level leans heavily into the horror themes of the game by building up the boss with a book and a few notes scattered throughout. The jumpscare in the catacombs took me by surprise, and the way the statue stares at me through the window in the house was extra haunting. It goes to show that this game can take advantage of it's setting and mood to set up a daunting encounter. I just hope in the future the dev doesn't come to rely on jumpscares. one was enough. The final level was also amazing.-If nothing else, Hrot consistently finds new ways to surprise me and keep me guessing, which isn't something many games could do. Not since DUSK have exclaimed "WTF IS THAT". or "WTF IS GOING ON" with genuine interest. I hope this game gets better because there's a ton to like but it's being dragged down by so many issues. I will follow this game with great interest. I paid good money for it, after all.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person that grew up in the boomer shooter era, HROT is a very welcome addition to the family!I played the demo found all the secrets and sunk some hours into endless mod, for me it was an easy choice to buy the full game.Obviously you can choose what ever difficulty you want to play it on, but I played it on hard and it was a pretty good balance of resource management as well as, well difficult, the aray of weapons and enemies really kept me thinking how an encounter could have gone if I just used this gun or went for that enemy 1st.I would highly recommend this game to anyone thats looking for a new game with elements that feel familiar!12/10 can't wait for more episodes!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was...okay.  It wasn't bad, but I don't feel it really excelled at anything.  It has the basic stock-standard old school FPS weapons, level design is acceptable but not memorable in the slightest, monster design is acceptable but there's only a few that are memorable, and the overall flow of the game is fine.  I just don't see myself ever replaying this.The game waffles between serious apocalyptic Soviet locales and just weird/humorous things, so I don't really know what I'm expecting.  A bulldozer that attacks me?  A giant horse?  A creepy statue of a grandma?  Creepy floating heads?  A guy in a wheel chair?  I just don't know what to make of it.  The final boss is just ridiculous (Putin riding a bear and then a pterodactyl) so I assume the overall game is supposed to be funny?  I have no idea anymore.Halfway through the game we battle fish enemies and then wake up in a hospital, escape, then continue with the same style locales and enemies as before.  I still have no idea what that was about.Overall, I just don't know what to make of this game.  I have no idea what the plot was about.  Level design is very forgettable.  Enemies and weapons are fine.  I just didn't really encounter anything in this game that made me feel it offered something new beyond what other retro shooters have offered.  That by itself wouldn't be so bad if it had an interesting story or cool level design, but I didn't see either of those.I'm giving it a thumbs up because I encountered no bugs, it was polished overall in terms of difficulty (health, ammo, enemy count, etc), and at least it wasn't boring like WRATH or Amid Evil.That said, buy it on sale.  It's $20 for ~4 hours of campaign.  I don't think it's worth it at that price.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Cool theme-Great level design -Game play is really smooth-Good balance of tense and ambient music-Very immersive for a simple game-F6 quick save!-The guns you use in a certain situation matter, as does ammo management to a degree making it feel like a FPS /survival horror hybridCons-Some bugs *sometimes when transitioning from an end of a level to beginning of new level i would get teleported back to the last level, was only fixed when game was reloaded *some health items would not pick up, even when I was low hp-very short, needs more content Conclusion This game has a lot of potential. It truly is fun and addicting, and though it is constantly compared to Dusk (a compliment i might add) it really feels like its own thing. I really hope for more content in the future and maybe... a little bit more story breadcrumbs, its really intriguing and i would 100% recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT's not yet quite at the level of the absolute top tier of the ever increasing numbers of retro shooters -- Dusk and Amid Evil, maybe a few others up there with them.  But, man, it's sure close, and it's not done yet.  Fingers crossed the developer actually manages to finish the game, and that he continues upping his game when we eventually get episode 3.  It's already a good, meaty game and well worth playing despite still being in early access.  It took me about 8-9 hours to go through episodes 1 and 2 thoroughly and get all the campaign achievements.  The gritty, grimy Soviet Bloc atmosphere is terrific, the levels are increasingly well designed as the episodes progress, and enough new and varied enemies are introduced gradually to keep things interesting. -

_childDocuments_.review: The only way i can describe HROT in any capacity is imagine an unhinged 3 way mix between You are empty, that short lived period of early 3D games back when the highest possible environmental interactivity was the new big engine based marvel everyone wanted to 1 up each other with, And the kind of authentically crafted homemade experience you could only get from somebody living in the eastern bloc. Good open ended level design with lots of freedom to tackle something with more than 1 strict approach but will have you barely scraping by with regards to resources especially on higher difficulty levels unless you are some pro secret hunter but that's all part of the intended design & nothing is too spongy to come up short ammo wise against in HROT anyway, not even the boss fights

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a game that destroyed my expectations in every capacity.  No screenshots or trailers do this game justice.Firstly, HROT has some of the best game-feel I've seen in any shooter.  There is a really good feeling of player control, and the camera work adds to it a lot.  All of the weapons feel good, and they are also all useful throughout the game.  Level design is solid.  The roster of enemies are all fun, and range into the extremely weird and charming in a bizarre way.This game has a ton of charm that comes from its setting and the attention to detail in the world.  This game clearly takes place after some radioactive disaster, so many of the enemies are geared in hazmat suits and gas masks.  As you explore the world, some areas have remnants of radioactive particles drifting through the air as your Geiger Counter faintly sounds.  This world feels grim and unsettling, and at certain points veers into straight up horror.Definitely recommend this one, even in its current Early Access state, it is well worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: This game not only brings hours of entertainment with vast exploration and hidden goodies around each corner,  but it also brings a sense of nostalgia that we all didn't know we craved so much. The art style is beautiful and vintage. The game play brings me back to the days of early video games like Doom, Wolfenstein, and Duke Nukem. At the end of each area, I look forward to seeing where this adventure takes me next. I would recommend this to anyone who craves that "vintage" video game feel as well as to anyone who wants to involve themselves in a art rich and wonderful setting of a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good modern boomer shooter.This review uses info found in the game's description, so remember to read that first.This game is influenced heavily by  and. See, the visuals and menus are like Quake, but the gameplay is like Chasm. Hell, someone playing the game without reading the game's description might even think it uses one of their engines (more on that later).The age rating seems a little extreme, but it seems to have been chosen by a committee that has no affiliation with the developer. It could also be simply a joke, poking fun at the fact that these throwback games appeal to an older demographic.The engine that the developer made is basic, but it's impressive for a single person. It encapsulates some of the original Quake engine's quirks like vertex warping and the renderer's optional pixelation of visuals.My issues:There's no number representing your FOV in settings, so you would need to make a wild guess if you wanted to set it to a specific number you commonly use.Plus, there's no way that I know of to unbind an action in the menu. I would really like that, as I'm use to that kind of customization.Final thoughts:It's pretty good, if not a little lacking in some spots. I'd recommend it to any 90's shooter fanatic like myself.Also, comments are on. I would love to hear your opinions on this game and my review!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I can vouch for one thing HROT does well, most enemies utilize projectiles over hitscan so you can skillfully avoid their attacks and they have noticeable stun states, so you mechanically get feedback from shooting at them and have some basic utility in interrupting their attacks. These should be the cornerstone mechanics of most FPS.That’s about it for praise.On the other hand, this game takes influence from Quake. Possibly the most 3/5 bland 90s FPS you can play. More notable for being turned into some meme mouse trainer with later sequels and being a hotbed for mods. Whatever aesthetic advantages that Quake had are completely gone here; most of HROT’s levels are brown corridors. The entire game’s color palette is drab dark browns. I’ve played Cruelty Squad and I think this game managed to look even more ugly somehow. It’s hogshit brown everywhere, the enemies, weapons, and levels. The only bit of color that seems to deviate from being brown is some light-colored cans of fish for pickups or whatever. I think you can take random screenshots of the many corridors with crates and industrial garbage strewn about and you can barely tell the levels apart:Quake had SOME color variation, Jesus. Supposedly, it’s intended to make the atmosphere depressing or something. Take notes from Quake here. It only helps when you have other aspects to amplify it. Most of the game’s sound effects are juvenile and lacking in impact. It’s mostly composed of underwhelming gun sounds, wimpy voice effects, and farts. Compare this to the Ranger’s pain screams, Trent Reznor’s OST, or anything in Quake. Try to tell me it’s not a straight downgrade.  When you juxtapose underwhelming, comical sounds with underwhelming, dejected environments. You get literal fecal matter smeared everywhere. I do not get why Eastern Europeans tell me how the West has lost its ‘beEAtY and TrAditiON’ and put out stuff like THIS. It’s repulsive on first contact by using the ugliest color scheme in the world and 98% of the game’s color palette. Even Exhumed has better color variation and it takes place in Egypt, literally a desert.The game’s mechanics are bog standard for these throwbacks. I have given praise where it is due, but I fail to find anything of interest here. Some of the enemies straight copy pastes from Quake. You have some variation of the Ogre from Quake but he makes fart sounds when he struts about, fantastic. There is the teleporting wizard guy from Hexen 2, but now he has an AK or something. The levels consist of brown corridors with brown crates and brown industrial equipment, maybe some brown or gun steel colored buildings here and there. The formula for these levels goes like this, you have the impression it’s nonlinear (it’s not unless you sequence break or something) because it has some slight exploration that leads to locked doors. The progression of these levels boils down to you going around corners, finding a locked door, ‘oh gee I better take the only other path available to find the key’, get the key after killing some enemies, and the alternate path leads back to the locked door/small hub repeat ad nauseum 50 times over. It’s literally the same crap you saw in Quake but it lacks any verticality or Romero-esque design to it. No level gimmicks like Dusk with tornadoes destroying the map or HL cinematic sequences to stop the insufferable blandness. If you're going to make progression completely linear, why not just take inspiration from HL, cut the BS, and just funnel players into the action? Maybe it changes up in later levels or something. I can barely get past the first few as is. The game honestly never feels as open as Build game or System Shock, where it feels like a place, and you can explore/play at your own leisure. Go play Cultic, Hedon, Dusk, Ultra Kill, Ion Fury, or basically anything else. Quake blows, by the way, more liek Half Baked. 40/100 half bakes. It even manages to evoke Quake's tech demo feeling, but arguably way worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game for the atmosphere and visual design. The actual game mechanics are certainly enjoyable, but for me, the shooting is almost a sideshow. I enjoy it mainly for the various Czech national symbols and prominent locations, for the bleak Soviet landscapes and for the various Cold-war-era references. If you're the kind of person who enjoys that kind of stuff (urbex, urban decay, Soviet nostalgia etc.), you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is one of those FPS boomer shooter games that took inspiration of the original Quake game, and with the success of DUSK, the devs of HROT decide that they will add their own slice of having gamers taking control of a person fighting through enemies (sometimes mutated) within some alternate event in Czechoslovakia due to some nuclear disaster in 1986.The visuals has that nice retro aesthetic like Quake, and the music has that ominous droning music (with some intense music at times during a onslaught battle) as if you see a world warped during the events of the Cold War. The gameplay is good even though it can get annoying that enemies may overwhelm you depending on the difficulty. And thankfully, it does support controller to an extent.My only wish is that it also does have a weapon wheel setting to switch which weapon you desire to choose while the gameplay either slows down or pauses instead of going through your weapons left or right.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling HROT "Slavic Quake" honestly doesn't do it justice.It has an understated yet gripping atmosphere, with dark, off-beat humor that will appeal to Czech players first and foremost. With a large roster of monsters and a good selection of weapons, HROT deserves its high rating.Also, this is literally the only game I've ever seen that gives you recipes for beating chapters. Virgin DOOM with its surface-level plot ain't got nothing on Chad HROT and its recipes lemme tell yaMy only wish is that the first episode had a secret level like the other two, but hey the game has 26 levels + 4 survival maps.Buy HROTDrink semi-skimmed milkPraise Gustav

_childDocuments_.review: Wellll...I like the game as it is exactly what you see: a clean, fast-moving, no frills FPS. There are enough enemies to keep it interesting, though more would be appreciated, and level design is decent without being maddening. If you played FPS shooters in the 90's, this is that. And, that's where I have some issue with it. There's not enough content for the price. I got it at a small discount and finished it in about 5 hours. The 7.3 isn't accurate as I left the game on for periods of time to do other tasks. Yes, it is still being built, and more is to come but the price should reflect that maybe only a third of the game is here for you. Steam is stuffed with FPS and ones like HROT and so many of those offer as good or better and experience at a lower price point and with more content. I recommend this only if you're okay with what I've written.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: First I would like to confess that before actually trying HROT I had a very negative impression of the game.The image I had in my mind was of a cheap copy of quake without 1/3 the quality of the original 90's Shooters.But luckily I was very much mistaken!HROT is a game with a fantastic ambience and solid gameplay.When I started playing I realized that it was not possible to use Bunny hops and that this would be a dramatic limitation of the gameplay as a whole, but that was not the case.The fact that we can't use bunny hops just makes the game more unique, the game's movement may not be as frantic as the other Retro FPS like Amid Evil, Dusk, or Prodeus, but it definitely fits the game's proposal.The level design of HROT is very interesting but also very repetitive.So my criticisms about how the game is now, early access, is only 3.Very limited color palette, which consequently affects the ambience in repetitive patterns, and a lack of good background music.I understand that the limited color palette can be an artistic decision to make the game more dark and tense, but I finished Episode 1 and it felt like I had never left the first map. But talking about the format of the maps themselves I admit that it was very interesting.Finally, a good background music is a crucial element for a game to be able to convey the same feeling of the 90's Shooters, I missed the songs during the progression, especially in the intense action parts.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice homage to times when shooters had little story but loads of guns, no reloads and no dumb regen life. A nice homebrewed Quake 1 made in slav-soviet-era styled Chekoslovakian temper and taste. Imagine Quake 1 but if it was released in one of USSR republics. Graphics are nice, enemies are weird and arsenal is just what needed.A nice mixture of humor, slav-specific boomershooter traits and feelings and nice gameplay that remain refined since first 3d shooters. Graphics - modest and nice. gameplay is something that i found very comfy in terms of speed and gunfights. Sound design is like homage to old days. And of course whole bunch of well hidden secrets, references and nice easterblock eggs to found. Hrot is very enjoyable game made of brown concrete of falling soviet stuff, nice taste of granny's kiflis, and good portion of liver dumpings made for dinner. It have no flaws,  i didn't found any. So i recommend this good found masterpiece. Enjoy your canned poultry tovarish! <3
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT feels like a mixture of late build engine games like duke nukem, and quake, with environments that make some sense, relate to reality and have interactions scattered around like duke nukem while still mostly focusing the level design on encounters and movement and gunplay that feels closer to quake 1. HROT is not as good as Dusk but it feels like its trying something entirely different, and while not being as creative, still managing to be enjoyable.Also, I understand that checkpoints are a no no for oldschool games but, can we just get a mixture of checkpoints and manual saves? Please? Its infuriating to be tempted to either save scum or lose a lot of progress upon death.Edit:Also, also, please change/improve the weapon sounds. The weapons are very satisfying in their damage and usage but the sound effects for all guns sound extremely weak. I've heard nerf guns that sound more satisfying. Currently they sound like popcorn machines. This I think is the most important improvement the game needs.
