_childDocuments_.review: I could talk about how the difficulty is as challenging as Blood even on Very Easy difficulty or how the brown art style succeeds where Quake fails or how the hazmat suits make the enemies look more monstrous or the good weapons or well done level design. Unfortunately, there is one massive sticking point that while it doesn't ruin the game, it well color your experience and that's the jarring shifts in tone.I think it mainly comes down a lack of context explain whats going on. Like you exploring these abandoned streets or spooky mines, enemies are puking like a plague hit with all the mutants and monsters around, everything feels oppressive and dire, helped with the games difficulty, and suddenly out of nowhere, you hear music and a clown is doing the macarena or some other dance and destroys the tone we were building up. The final boss is probably the worst offender of this since it's the final thing you fight. I won't spoiler it but it'll be a more fitting final boss for Postal: Brain Damaged.If only the episodes end with some context like DOOM or Duke Nukem to explain what I just did or where I'm going next but instead I'm just given a recipe for a tasty dish. I'm sure the devs thought it was a funny joke but you need to tell me the basics of what the F is going on! You're just breaking my immersion when you do that and I don't really care about immersion.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time playing through Hrot - I will say! i think the first two episodes are much MUCH stronger then the final episode - regardless! It's still a really great _eerie_boomershooter at times. Which is very much and enjoyable - hope this gets a dedicated multiplayer tbh or like community support. Very neat surreal game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I played. Love the PS1 style graphics, gun play is smooth, and I appreciate the very easy mode (it's nice to sometimes feel like a total badass, and I am glad you get that opportunity). One thing I would say is to add more levels, although the ones available are good, the current game (just chapter 1) should be 10$. However with the game being well done and polished so far, I dont mind supporting the dev. I highly recommend you give this a try!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: All the weapons feel weighty and punchy and effective. I do wish the weapon sounds had a more punchy sound design but other than that, no real issues gameplay wise.I'm not sure what other old-school boomer shooters drip with this kind of atmosphere. There's some cool Eastern Bloc eldritch horror thing going on. I've heard/seen people complain about the lack of a thumping soundtrack and I think they're incredibly misguided. The game has an ambient soundtrack that suits the mood and atmosphere, I think asking for a dynamic open string Djent riffage in this game is a mistake and not at all what the game is going for.I had one, pretty major bug. The level that has the end button behind two turrets? I had zero health//zero ammo, so i dodged and weaved passed their projectiles to end the level. However, this is where it would bug to all hell. The next level starts and my character is like stuck, sunk into the raising platform. As soon as i moved or clicked my mouse it would restart me back at my last save in level before, where i had quick saved in the hall way. I had to retry ending the level... 9 times before it finally allowed me to start the next level.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty cool retro shooter. Not the best one (the best one imo is Arcane Dimensions for Quake; yeah, free mod is still better than all the commercial retro releases), but very-very solid & fun. It didn't hook me right away. But it gets better & better with every map. All the fun starts at the 2nd episode: maps are more open & more space for maneuvering, layouts are more intricate & more verticality. Either way this game definetly worth a try if you love retro aesthetics in general
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished and I have to say I absolutely love it. Great dark atmosphere (but there is no shortage of humorous inserts), great level design. Amazing how much you can squeeze out of a limited color palette. Oh, and let's not forget about cute little doggies and a lovely ending ;)Highly recommended if so-called boomer shooters are your thing.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of Quake 1/2 ? Do you miss the simple days of spending a rainy Saturday afternoon playing a game which you could just play a nice game without having to think about a million possible strategies to win? Do you like simple & fun Indie games?Then this is the perfect game for you! :DHROT is that kind of game which you can play, have fun, laugh a bit but still find incredibly smart aspects of the game. By using Q1 game engine, HROT will deliver a well spend afternoon playing a fun game. You will not find high resolution details or Hollywood scripted scenes, but you will laugh, scream and get frustrated about finding all the secret areas and fulfilling all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is much more colorful than the pallet,Reminiscent of old-school shooters HROT has a distinctly survival-esque management of health and resources with ammo and Armour in short supply for many levels, learning how much ammo is needed to take a specific enemy will be vital to your survival.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Outside of the wallhumping for secrets I think this game is wonderfully designed with an engrossing atmosphere. It is absolutely eerie and disconcerting to wander around a good number of the maps. Moment to moment gameplay feels nice with some fun enemies to fight and good guns. The hardest difficulty is frustrating on occasion but not more so than any other boomer shooter. I'm excited to see what gets added.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels great! If you aren't sure about it, try out its free demo!The atmosphere is great, the enemies are varied and have good tells, and overall the gameplay feels pretty rewarding, the difficulties are well balanced, the guns are satisfying to use. Keep in mind though, this game takes maybe 3-4 hours to complete in one sitting on Normal. If you're going for the higher difficulties then it may take a few hours more. As of right now, it's a fairly short game but it's really well done so far for early access.There were a couple of hiccups with enemy AI (they would stand still while aiming a gun at me, but never shoot) maybe twice in the four and a half hours I played it. Aside from that, I encountered no bugs.If the dev keeps working with the great things that are currently in this game, I've got little doubt it'll be great once it's released from early access.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is the Datura-induced lucid fever nightmare you wake up from whilst chained to a derelict basement under an abandoned laundromat somewhere along the steppes of Belarus after answering a deep web ad for volunteer work in developing communities. Creeks bellow out from an unseen stairwell, sending plumes of disintegrated drywall airborne. The clouds of dehydrated plaster glimmer and dance along the numerous beams of light penetrating through the loosely assembled wooden rafters above. The silhouettes of two men peak through the shadows of obscured shelving and cargo pallets. Your heart drops, you feel a rise of bile in your throat as the unimaginable reality of this situation begins to dawn on your now fully conscious mind. The echo of footsteps begin to penetrate through the deafening blare of antiquated air conditioning units, as the two shadows approach you from behind. You're helpless, immobile, confused, and entirely violated. They're getting closer. The shadows grow to absurd heights, easily breaching 6 feet each. They're getting closer. Tears well up in your eyes. They're almost here. You blink away your tears, violently opening and shutting your eyes in a desperate bid to wake up from this all-too realistic nightmare. They're almost here. No, you already woke up, this may be a nightmare, but it's certainly not a creation of nocturnal fiction, this is real, This is happening.They're here. You instinctively close your eyes.That's HROT.This game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ radical, I've never felt more pride to be an an early-adopter and support this cause. Paying 17 bucks for this game in it's infancy felt like sending a check to sponsor disenfranchised Tanzanian youth seeking higher education.I've been following this game since around mid-2019, and I'm so fully funked out to see it in such a fully realized state with an actual functioning Steam page. So often these projects fall into the collective void where all promising Indie-Game-Twitter projects go when their devs grow apathetic or go back to the Arby's register in an effort to keep a roof over their heads without also keeping a ♥♥♥♥ in their mouths. (No disrespect toward sex-workers, you folks are amazing and your profession is valid).Obviously the tone and atmosphere are completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ off the wall and utterly incredible, weaving this horrific web of art design, soundtrack, subtle-lore, and liminal-horror that fully leans into the strength of retro aesthetics in a horror setting and leaves you almost immobilized in many areas. All with this really unique, and largely unexplored within the retro/PSX aesthetic, Eastern European lens.We all got this from the demo and years of peaks through the dev's Twitter. But what seriously took me off guard was just how much the gameplay measured up. The combat opens up in a ton of areas, and the weapon dynamic and enemy balance seem seriously toned and well-tested. Combined with clever arena design, wonderful sense of level progression that carries through from the best of retro FPS, and episode 1 of HROT seriously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crushes that 100% proof Boomer-shooter gooey goodness.There's been murmurs about the weapons, their impact and lack of "GA-GOOSH"ey-ness. But ech, blech, bloacch, bloackh. Don't listen to them Mr. Spythinev, I absolutely love the weapons and their sound design. They feel much lighter compared to the heavy, bassey tones in other contemporary titles of the Retro FPS Renaissance. HROT's weapons feel very utilitarian, and every-man. Fitting the tone of the setting, and the role of the character as just another soldier in the motherland's armies, not a stand-alone death god of boom and shoot. Keepa da noises.Where I feel HROT *might* falter a tad, is simply in its scale and sense of progression? It is only the first episode, and with it being such, there is a sense of same-eyness that starts to occur once you're over an hour in and you're still walking through the same sized narrow halls and eldritch demon-diarrhea soaked train station courtyards. As the game grows, I'd definitely love to see some larger maps alongside utilization of the game's driveable vehicles, perhaps in a Highway-17-esque extended section. Although I am absolutely certain beyond doubt we'll see the game's scale open up as the following episodes progress.To close, HROT is easily worth the $20 asking price, and supporting it's growth is something I feel a genuine sense of pride in doing.Support the arts and the Slavs.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really comment on the theme since it's very "inside jokey." Needless to say you'll get the most out of this game if you're Eastern European or are immersed in that culture. As best as I could ascertain from the information presented, the game is set some time around the cold war and the enemy is communism and/or certain political figures and policies of that era.Combat is fast and fluid although the balance is a little off with some of the enemies. Mid tier mobs are a little too spongy and do a bit too much damage compared to the higher tier, which feel like only a mild threat in comparison. The weapons are functional, but unexciting. Some, like the SMG, feel a bit weak and could do with a small buff in the damage department.Level design is solid enough. There's a few too many sewer levels, but they're about as good as sewer levels can be. You won't remember them once they're done, but they aren't painful to play. Some maps were better than others with lots of secrets, jokes (some easier to understand than others) and achievements to unlock.On the hardest difficulty the challenge is moderate to high. 90% of the time combat revolves around circle straifing with very little room for improvisation. There is some fun stuff like kicking the enemy's grenades back at them, but other than that it's pretty standard run and gun gameplay.Get it if you're a fan of boomer shooters and you're looking for something a little bit different.

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique blend of environmental storytelling via its signs, little trinkets littered about that setup the world without you being directly told much, and a somewhat oppressive, heavy ambient-art-style, which I grew to appreciate. _childDocuments_.review: Its good, someone said its like a mix of kingpin and blood and i have to agree.. i usually think these boomer shooters look awesome (im 31 , so i was like 8 years old when things like duke nukem 3d were popular, i played them but my parents didnt want me to) but never can hold my attention,,i been playing this one for hours and plan on making it the first boomer shooter i complete all the way through..levels are nice and varied with some fun enemy encounters, especially on very hard difficulty. any game that can manage to get me away from tears of the kingdom right now must be doing something right
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a tough game to recommend. I've heard it compared to the Worker and Parasite of Quake's Itchy and Scratchy and it's not too far off base. This is a cold, cruel, depressing Soviet era world of brown and gray skies and gas mask wearing foot soldiers. But like the developer's previous game Legie it doesn't wholly succeed at being a **good** game. Movement is a little stiff, the guns don't have great feedback, and there is no "pain" stun effect on enemies leading to moments where they continue to attack aggressively even as you unload a double barrel in their face. Resources are notoriously scarce with some levels having maybe half a dozen healing items total. And while the level design is pretty top notch throughout, all too often HROT loves literally teleporting enemies into rooms. I can't stress enough how utterly frustrating it is to lose 50 health from a shot to the back by an enemy that silently teleported in behind you. And yet, like Legie, this game is uncompromising in its vision. The design is as cruel as the world you inhabit. You will never have armor for very long forcing you to cherish every secret. Health pickups seem to be front loaded because rarely will you end a level with 50+ health. I deeply value games with a strong vision even if they falter in other areas. What HROT truly is is the Chasm of modern boomer shooters. It's nobody's first choice but dig into the aspic and you'll find a delicious, sour plum. Does that analogy work?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. It has such an eerie and enthralling athmosphere it's truly spectacular. It's really unbelievable, how the developers managed to put so many unique enemies, levels and weapons into this. You can absolutely feel the passion these people put into this game. Not a single Triple-A-game which I played the last years managed to get me this hooked or exited, to see what surprises await in the next levels. I really hope that there will be a sequel to this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dusk, Quake and Soviet-era references, you'll love this. The dev is very clever and creative with levels having horror elements, even laughing right at your face at certain points. If I'd improve one thing it would be the sound design which doesn't have the "oomph" that Dusk's had, but overall the game is exceptionally well-made.If you get this, definitely cap your FPS because my graphics didn't like it if I didn't, very stable and customizable otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a single-player retro FPS set in a small socialist country neighboring Soviet Union (Czechoslovakia) after an unspecified disaster in 1986. Those times were dark and terrifying and so is the game.

name: Iron Harvest
detailed_description: Iron Harvest Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes the Rusviet Revolution and the Operation Eagle Addon, granting access to all new adventures in the alternative reality of 1920+. About the Game Iron Harvest is a real-time strategy game (RTS) set in the alternate reality of 1920+, just after the end of the Great War. The Game lets you control giant dieselpunk mechs, combining epic singleplayer and coop campaigns as well as skirmishes with intense action on the battlefield for multiplayer fans, Iron Harvest is the classic real-time strategy game fans have been waiting for. Tradition clashes with scientific and technological progress, while Europe is still recovering from the brutal battles of the World War. Cities are being rebuilt and in the countryside, the era of the Iron Harvest has begun. Farmers are uncovering the remains of the majestic walking machines that had fought on the battlefields of the Great War. In the midst of this chaos, a new threat appears that will put Europe’s very existence at risk. Secret forces are putting everything they can towards destabilization of entire countries, determined to set the world on fire once again and finally seize control. Lead dozens of different unit types into battle, carefully utilize cover and blast entire buildings to shreds. Take your time to come up with a plan which allows for a wide range of tactics, including a stealth approach. Mechs. We got mechs. Lots of them. Experience an epic overarching story, spanning more than 20 missions over three campaigns. Join nine charismatic heroes and their beastly companions in their adventures across Europe. Team-up with a friend and master all campaigns side-by-side in co-op. Command three diverse factions with over 40 unit types and 9 heroes with unique abilities. Setup skirmish and multiplayer matches any way you want. Configure your personal game interface and choose your favourite input controls. Competitive multiplayer with ladders, ranked matches & leagues. Choose from a vast selection of skirmish maps and challenge maps, available to play in singleplayer and coop. In addition expect regular free updates during the season, including new singleplayer challenges, multiplayer maps and more to look forward to. Conquer resource points, build your base and place fortifications to protect your unit production and research.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is impressive in terms of visual packaging, but the bottom line is that I find it somehow boring: the gameplay is repetitive, the missions are uninteresting. Also there are lots of frustration with obsctacles / sight blockers / covers. Sometimes your units have cover, sometimes they dont. Sometime your troup are blocked by stupid planks and you do not understand why. Bottomline is you do not feel in control, and send all your units in one big blob, which is a pity for an RTS. I do not see how these fundamentals can be improved, so I would not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Like RTS games? Enjoyed Company of Heroes? Also like destruction? Than Iron Harvest is for you! Set in a steampunk World War 1, you play as one of three nations and their array of crazy machines and watch their giant blades pierce into the soft skulls of poor soldiers... Or whatever it ripped apart, hard to tell when they're a red mist and a couple mutilated limbs (Please note, the game is not actually this violent). Moving on, if you've been missing the classic RTS feel in your games but wanting new and improved graphics, than Iron Harvest is your game!

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks complicated at first but when you actually play it it gets really easy with no unique mechanics that would make the gameplay at least less stiff. the campaign is bland and sometimes even boring and anticlimatic. the pvp gameplay offers nothing you get a base at start tha you cant do anything with you can place some building but really only two matter first lets you recruit soldier other machines and the game focuses on capturing resource rigs which is super boring because when you captured 2 or 3 rigs and built 2 building you are at the endgame and it offers nothing more. developers dont really care at the balance of the game so some machines are ♥♥♥♥ others are op. Great concept but very poor execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Good old fashioned RTS. You can't pause and command units during gameplay and I wish there was an option for that. Turn the difficulty down and you'll still have fun without pausing.   I used cheats to disable the unit cap in singleplayer, so I could have enough units to comfortably defend my base and steamroll the enemy (I'm a sore loser). All of the campaign can be Co-op with 3 people controlling the same army. With the RTS skill level of my friends and I, it brings the skill level up to 0.25 of a Korean.  Co-Controling an army with a friend is probably the most fun I had with it. I initially pirated this game but after playing it for a couple hours decided it was well worth purchasing along with both DLC. If a sequel came out I would buy it right off the bat.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest claims to be the rts people want. It's not. It's a stupidly forced faction based pidgeonholed specificity of combat that makes all of them weaker and unfun. There's no room for change in habits, there's no change in how they play. It's just an absurdly dumb and simplistic design that doesn't work well with what systems are in place.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Points:+ Campaign - Well written, long, epic missions, and a ton of fun. It's very clear why this game took so many resources to make. The campaign is a war epic and it shows in every mission.+ Graphics - The game looks great. It runs very stable on my mid range system at high settings. The effects are amazing - buildings explode into pieces, smoke hangs in the air during chaotic firefights, tracers zip back and forth between frontlines, and the battle demolishes the landscape. It's extremely satisfying.+ Setting - The setting is extremely cool. Diesel-punk WW1 era settings are not new, but this is the most fleshed out take on one we've seen so far. The setting is also shared with the tabletop game Scythe which is a bonus if you're into tabletop gaming.+ The Action - If you've ever wondered what CoH would be like if it were more fast paced and action packed, just look at this game. The gameplay flow is extremely fun and gratifying.The bad points:- Balance - At this stage the faction and unit balance is very awkward. It doesn't matter very much for single player and coop play, but in PvP situations it quickly becomes clear that some units are close to useless and others can win you a match just by fielding a ton of them. - Counterplay - The game is very similar to company of heroes, but the counterplay in this game is not nearly as in-depth. Often you'll find yourself trying to balance your army between how many mechs you expect your enemy to have and how much infantry you expect your enemy to have. There are no tech trees at all, or commanders/doctrines like in CoH. So often you end up with similar army comps every match. This is not so terrible since the battles are still thrilling, but it's a point against the game.The Meh Points:~ Lacking Content in Some Areas (For Now) - There are not many multiplayer maps yet. These are going to be added over time, and the existing maps are pretty good. There are also challenge maps that are a ton of fun, and more of those will be added as well. The dev team seems to be fast-moving and updates frequently, so this point will not be an issue within a year. Additionally, there are additional factions in the setting for the dev team to explore. I'm not sure if they will ever add them, but the game is ripe for good old RTS expansions.~ Release Features - Not all features are here as promised on release. For one thing, coop on challenge maps and in campaign missions is missing. They are going to be adding this feature in the coming month, according to the road map. It does not feel good paying full price for a complete game and not getting the complete game. But, I have faith that the dev team will deliver their promises and more.~ The Price - $50 is a steep price to ask of anyone of an RTS game these days. With a years worth of content and an expansion bundled in, $50 would be completely fair. But at this stage the price is a little high. I am an RTS fan and wanted to support the dev team so they could keep making great games, so I paid the price. If you are a casual player, wait for a sale.Conclusion: Iron Harvest is worth your money as a promising RTS. The Singleplayer and Coop fun is here already, and PvP balance is being worked out. It's a good RTS that has potential to be great, and I have faith that the dev team will take it there over the next year.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this game in the brief time that I owned it, and generally speaking, I did not enjoy it very much. I'll preface this review with stating: I am only reviewing the game on categories I felt strongly about. Graphics (other than art design) aren't something I care too much about (unless they're absolutely ♥♥♥♥, which they aren't in Iron Harvest). A few relatively specific categories will also be included, as I felt strongly about them for Iron Harvest. We'll start from the top:--- World Building ---Best part of this game, by far. A universe that throws these super neat looking mechs into a WW1/WW2 setting? Absolutely. And they look great. A lot of the pictures shown at the beginning of the campaign, the ones with the mechs photoshopped into the background of actual WW1 pictures, look awesome. It really sets the tone for the game you are about the be playing and man it gets you hype. Such a neat concept and it really allowed me to ignore the strangely renamed Poland, Germany, Russia and American factions because I was so excited to dive in. Unfortunately, this is basically all Iron Harvest had going for it in my opinion.--- Story ---Jesus. They dropped the ball so hard on the story. Like I said, it starts out super neat with the 'Great War' and the awesome photoshop jobs they did incorporating mechs into the WW1 photos. And then they have the audacity to throw the most cookie-cutter, bland, generic ♥♥♥♥ in your face with absolutely no parallels with the darker introduction of the game. I won't get into details, so you can play it for yourself, but everything about this story was just so fundamentally boring or eye-gougingly terrible that I never finished it. I'm sure there is an argument to be made that 'you shouldn't review the story before you finish the game', which I would typically agree with. However, I played 50% of the campaign, it was awful. If the first half of the campaign is so bad to the point that I cannot continue, it really isn't going to get above the 3/10 mark for me, even if the next half was a literal 10/10 (which I am doubting it is).This brings me to a subsection I want to discuss, which is the voice acting. I really don't comment on voice acting much unless we're talking about Joel from the Last of Us, or some other stand out job (Plenty of examples, won't list them here though, I'm sure you get the jist). Voice acting is something that, if done right, elevates the game, if not, it really doesn't leave an impact. Iron Harvest introduced me to a third perspective however. When the voice acting is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful that I had to slam my head on my desk to get through cut scenes. It only carries over into the actual game play, whenever you select a unit, they spew a brutally awful accent and generic piece of dialogue (that has absolutely no variation, so I hear the same ♥♥♥♥ over and over from the same unit). I mean ♥♥♥♥ this game's voice acting is ♥♥♥♥. It hurts and it makes me angry.--- Gameplay ---After the difficult to bare with story, and the ♥♥♥♥ voice acting, I really was hoping the saving grace for this game would be its gameplay. Company of Heroes with mechs right? What could go wrong? I love Company of Heroes. But... it isn't. It is like a very watered down, janky version of Company of Heroes.Allow me to explain. In CoH, there is a distinct satisfaction to every unit you eliminate. The shots your units fire, be it a Sherman 76 or a standard infantry squad, feels unique and meaningful. I enjoy just... watching the combat between squads in CoH because it feels very much like (what I would imagine, at least) is a real firefight. Units are taken down when your squad loses health, etc.. So as your squad's health lowers, you know that maybe that next Kar98K shot could take out your AT guy, or your sergeant. It distinctly feels like there is a real firefight going on.Iron Harvest does the opposite of this. They took the pretty fun cover-based, squad-based RTS system that CoH has and just sort CTRL+C, CTRL+V'd it without understanding what makes it special. Bullets feel fake. Units will fire a constant stream of automatic bullets into a single unit, where he doesn't even look like he takes damage. Mechs do not feel good when the go up against infantry. They look great in game, sure, but they just entirely miss the marker unlike facing down a Panzer IV in CoH with infantry. I wish I could elaborate more on why this game misses the mark in terms of gameplay, but see for yourself if you still want to buy it. This was really the part I thought would redeem the... disaster of a story but nope. It was just more kindling on the dumpster fire that is Iron Harvest.--- Conclusion ---Kinda ♥♥♥♥ game, buy it ONLY on sale if you want to see for yourself. But if you end up enjoying it, that's cool too.P.S. If anyone tries to tell me that the ♥♥♥♥-awful Boston accent the give all the 'American' soldiers in this game is not "grab a .44 magnum and blow your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brains out" levels of annoying, you're wrong. ♥♥♥♥ I hated hearing that ♥♥♥♥ and I am so happy I returned it. I have a Pavlovian reaction to the point if I hear "YEAH YEAH" in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ accent one more time I will get KING Art and Prime Matter sent to the Hague for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ war crimes. ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr- A nice but flawed return to the RTS, carried by its sound, score, and concept. buy it if it's on sale -  6.5/10Long boiIron Harvest is yet another attempt to revive the RTS genre. In all forms it is a "classic" squad based RTS. Using the simplified base building formula of the genre ala Dawn of war 2 albiet slightly more complex. The game is heavily carried by an impressive theme of WW1 with mechs. Playing with Native languages on is an absolute must, as the performances in polish, russian, and german are stellar. The OST is phenominal going on the shelf of OST's I'm tempted to purchase for listening. The sound design is solid with an impressive ability to immerse you in a chaotic mech filled battlefield. However this game is far from perfect. The mission design leaves a lot to be desired, with maps that feel samey across all 3 base campaigns. The only campaign with a good amount of variety in its mission set is Polania, the rusviet, and saxony campaigns are essentially A move campaign maps with a select few missions being exempt. The AI leaves a lot to be desired, with it following the wave formula for attacking. In fact the AI doesn't even "build" units they just spawn after an indeterminate amount of time.  The factions don't really have any identity from each other. Their rosters use essentially the same units save for their "uber" mechs which at the end of the day are also A move mechs that need different levels of support. The infantry are all functionally the same, though the rusviet infantry just sucks for whatever reason. The multiplayer is dead af,

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply disappointing experience. The game itself is fine at best, but its riddled with strange glitches and features. Your units will decide to not fire back on attacking enemies, or simply ignore issued commands. They will run twenty yards away from their squad-mates to take cover behind a tin can with their backs to the enemies. I'd probably hate this game if I paid full price for it or backed it on kickstarter. Atleast its not Warmachine Tactics.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal RTS. This game heralds from the realm of Company of Heroes, but with outlandish mechs instead of tanks (or mechs styled like tanks!) The gameplay is smooth, the factions all play a little different, enough to make them feel unique, but balanced in the same vein. The visuals are excellent, and extremely well done. The style is a perfect blend of bizarre, yet ordinary. The music is all thematic, whether it's Russian, Polish or Germanic-- you get this bombastic feeling of drama, guts and glory-- exactly what's on the tin. The plot is a little lackluster, but heralds from the realm of Red Alert acting-- a world where it's so bad it's just good, which is exactly where Iron Harvest lands. The AI in skirmishes are a little weak, but play well enough to make a match entertaining, which is exactly what I would call this.If you liked games like Company of Heroes, Dawn of War, or World in Conflict, you will feel right at home here.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to like this game but after playing other RTS games my entire life, and trying multiple recently in order to compare: this sorely misses the mark of an enjoyable play.Frankly, just let us zoom the game interface out further and it would eliminate a multi-faceted headache that this highlights. Moving multiple units to a single firefight is tedious and consistently counter-intuitive, and there is no reason for it to be so difficult to reinforce units and bring them back with full health (unless you pause the game, you will drop a lot of efficiency from focusing on units to reinforce while micro-managing others in a firefight). The problem only exacerbates when the fight moves on to multiple fronts. Next up is the map movement: I cannot express how frustrating it is to be locked into a developer's preference for map movement. I don't like dragging my mouse to the edge of the screen in order to move the map, and my left hand is usually busy pressing macro keys and I don't want to look for the arrow keys and lose efficiency there. The middle mouse scroll ALMOST works, but we are locked into the *reverse* pull. This means pulling left or right will take your camera perspective to the opposite direction pulled. This is like inverted Y-Axis look on a controller, preferable to some but if you make it the unchangeable default in your game (and its not a flight simulator) I will put it down and every second thought it gets will be disgustingly shirked away.I like the aesthetic, its interesting and beautifully produced! I truthfully hope another iteration of this game series comes out, but with more accessibility. I do not recommend buying this game at full price, but picking it up on sale won't hurt. I got enough aesthetic inspiration from this game to make me feel better, but I don't know if I'll be playing it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Story:  Pretty forgettable story with no choices and linear game play.Sound:  Good sound with fun explosions and gunfire.Graphics:  Are decent and unit animation shines.  Overall fidelity is low.Game play:  This is where the game falls down for me and obtains a do not recommend.  It markets itself as an RTS, but it is not.  Base building is super simplistic and nearly every mission features a progress to x point then build defenses that are extremely weak and defend against a counterattack.  It is not fun because you do not have a free flowing map, unit, or base variety.  Resources nodes often cannot be built on top of, forcing you to disperse forces to defend or more often than not run back and forth across the map (FAIL game design).  It makes me miss the days of good node games like Empire at War and Ensemble studios are more recently Relic.  Don't constrain me.  Its not what makes an RTS fun.  Don't make a game difficult by constraining my units.  Just make good AI.  Lastly, that is where the game becomes nonredeemable... the AI is miserable.If you want a 20 unit slug fest then you'll enjoy this game.  Otherwise, stay away.  There are many better choices out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll genuinely save you some money here, rather than buy this game buy Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 or Company of Heroes. If you have both of those, buy Spellforce 3. The game isn't bad, but its so clunky that it just sucks the enjoyment right out. There's frankly barely enough content to justify the price as well. Mech's are either insanely slow and cumbersome, or zippy little glass balls that die too fast to be useful. Infantry are basically carbon copies between factions (with the basic infantry being rock, paper, scissors against each other and the "faction special units" also being rock paper scissors). Heroes are universally op against non-heroic units. But the most damning part is the skirmish and multiplayer mode. There's 6 1v1 maps, 5 2v2 maps, and 3 4v4 maps. And they all are basically chokepoint style maps designed around capture the flag games. Its ok at best. I do not recommend at the price they want though.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is very good, I belief who liked Company of Heros, can also warm up to this game, but it is not quite as complex as COH, there are fewer skills and therefore less micromanagement. Also the cover system is a bit simplified, so a squad can't take cover in a blast crater. Also, a few more upgrade options for units and buildings would have been nice, but that may come with a DLC.  Iron Harvest is a good RTS and a great base to build on.I find the story very well done for an RTS, even without the bombast of a Star Craft, but the film/movie sequences are well done, the atmosphere comes across very well, the speakers do a good job. I especially like the option to have the nations speak their respective languages, I use it during my 2nd playthrough. It should be mentioned that there is the option to play the campaign in co-op as well.The graphics are also quite decent, the mechs are nicely animated, and when a TUR stomps through a building it just looks very satisfying, but why does the thing have to be as slow as a snail on sedatives?Away from the campaigns, I find the AI a bit weak, Medium is really a bit light, and Heavy was funnily enough, more eager to attack than the very difficult AI which was waiting to be wiped out - more or less.I hope that the above points will be improved in the future. The mechanics are very, very heavily borrowed Company of Heroes 1 & 2, but not executed nearly as well or with as much understanding.  For example, your infantry can take cover in this game in a way that looks similar to COH games, but the cover system isn't implemented well and doesn't contribute much to gameplay.    You can control which way your mechs face when they move, like in COH2, but unlike in COH games, this isn't done in a way that offers a good gameplay mechanic.The campaign missions offer more variety than COH or other RTS games, and the visuals and steampunk art style is very enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: I was a backer for this game and was really excited by the concept and art style, but a finished product this is not. Biggest issues are the poor unit pathfinding and unit controls. Controlling the units felt sluggish and clunky and there were many times where my unit would leave cover and rush the unit it was targeting even through the enemy was well within the range circle., so either the range circle needs more detail and tweaking or unit behavior needs to be tweaked. Units stacking in cover occasionally left a person out in the open even if there was a bit of room left in cover. Also, there were graphical issues with some units and the in-engine mini-cutscenes, with clothing clipping on the character models or rendering as blank. If the devs can take a second look at all cutscenes, it'll be pretty evident. Ultimately, the game in its current state is worth half of the asking price, but if the devs add all the missing features other reviews have already spoken at length about AND fix the unit behavior issues, this game can be well worth the full price for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a very interesting setting, aesthetically impressive between sound design and art direction of the mechs, and hosts a decent enough campaign.  because of a myriad of issues however, and a rather pitiful map pool.I'd never heard of 1920s+ before this but this game does an amazing job on selling the setting to you, big stomping mechs of various shapes and sizes with distinct looks, factions that all look very different from one another, a musical score that's surprisingly good... and then the ingame battle chatter and sounds of combat. I wasn't expecting battle chatter of all things to be as good- maybe even the best i've heard in RTS for quite some time? It's varied since there are many unit voices, but also multiple different responses to being embroiled in a firefight. The sounds of gunfire and groaning steel as mechs collapse into fiery heaps is also very satisfying.The campaign while not exactly ground breaking or trying anything new for the genre is enjoyable enough, I had a good time with it. I think what surprised me is how much they  wanted to make it memorable, because the voice acting I had no complaints about and actually enjoyed some characters quite a bit like Gunter von Duisburg of Saxony but more importantly the cinematics; there are many in-engine cinematics throughout the game and even some black and white old war footage that shows the mechs being used in wide scale armed conflict for the first time. So much care and attention went into this.When it comes down to the core gameplay itself, it's fun enough but feels lacking. Before I get too into that, I want to preface what i'm going to say with pointing out that this game is clearly inspired by the Company of Heroes style of RTS which is suppose to be heavily focused on tactics over speed.So what did I find wrong gameplay wise? Well it's easy if I break it down into two areas; Infantry and Base Building. Infantry kind of fall flat in that they're the same across the board with little details like effective range and what kind of exo-suit unit they have being the biggest. The way they designed infantry is that when a squad dies they drop whatever weapon they had in their possession save for exo-suits, and another squad can then equip said weapon and turn into whatever type of unit has that weapon. I.E a rifleman squad becomes a medic unit with pistols if they pick up a medkit. While this is an okay system I suppose, it just leaves infantry across the three factions feeling very samey and also the fact that infantry fall off very hard once the advance mechs start rolling in just makes it feel like infantry were an afterthought. I wish you could have infantry squads that are capable of equipping multiple weapons so they're more effective against various types of threats, and in turn become much more valuable similar to some other games. There's just a lack of identity here that is my real issue. Similar to infantry but much more problematic is that every faction is effectively identical when it comes to buildings. Sure the architecture is different but they call can build three kinds of bunkers, sandbags & barbed wire, a workshop for mechs, a barracks for infantry, and a headquarters for some extra income and two basic units. That's it, there's nothing more to them beyond that. No variation in how they build bases, or what kind of bases they have, no different defensive options, no difference in sandbags/mines/barbed wire, nothing. Again, another thing that feels like an afterthought. While the game has an great array of mechs spread across three factions with their own unique mechs, some of which are titans among iron giants, what is greatly lacking is enough interesting places for them to battle it out. There are a total of six maps as of time of writing, three two player, two four player, and one six player map. That's it. And such a small map pool is almost criminal given the price of the game.Challenges helps alleviate this a little but that's very reaching to say that it makes anything better.Final VerdictIron Harvest feels like a game that released too early and needed more time to come with more to the table to offer for the money it's asking for. While I do not doubt the effort and the passion that went into the game, it's just missing content in areas it shouldn't, and there are some things I wish it borrowed from its inspirations that it didn't. Is it fun? Yes I would say so, but I don't know how often i'll return to this game unfortunately. I need to be absolutely clear that this is  by any means a lost cause, if they take the game's criticisms to heart and administer a healthy dose of post-release content then the game could really live up to the amazing promise it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Comp stomp is my favourite way to play RTS with my friends and I think that's the case for a lot of people, that being so - why is the AI so bad? Easy and medium might as well not exist, hard is brain dead. I'm not interested in the campaign, or any singleplayer or PVP content for that matter.They added a new faction since I played the beta and they don't really seem that viable? This game already had two underwhelming factions, it didn't need a third.Infantry combat is a joke. Severe lack of quality and quantity in this regard. Their implementation is inconsistently bullet spongy, often so slow it's frustrating with no half tracks or similarly useful troop transports. Upgrades aren't as satisfying as  either, in CoH equipping a rifle squad with a BAR for example is cool as hell, and they do veterancy stuff on top of that. MG gameplay is boring and tedious and mortars need a second look too. I think it's fair to say every aspect of infantry combat in this game is flawed in some respect. IH feels like they took all the worst parts of vanilla CoH, tried to simplify them and said "that'll do" at some point way before it was actually finished. Armor isn't even that great beyond the spectacle of moving the big stuff around the map. Using armor is tedious at best. Again, lack of quality and quantity. This game is the epitome of cool concept, terrible execution. Asking for 35 hard earned dollarydoos ON SALE is atrocious. In comparison to Company of Heroes, Iron Harvest plays like crap. In comparison to Company of Heroes: Blitzkrieg, Iron Harvest plays like 15 year old crap covered in mold.An example of an experience that can actually be fun to play with your friends is . It's free if you own Company of Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: "JuSt SpAm BiG mEkS aNd WiN GaMe! Inftry r useless" - every player who clearly never played online.The game has a great campaign compared to the standard for a strategy game these days. The multiplayer is being actively developed and they have made major release with a weekly cadence so far. Two patches alone were dedicated to unit attack responsiveness and cover responsiveness. Each faction is close enough to each other to feel fair, but different enough to feel like distinct factions (Each faction has 1 infantry only they can produce, their basic infantry has different starting weapons, and their vehicles are 100% unique) The beauty of infantry in this game is that they can level up and then equip any looted equipment on the field to change class. For instance, a medic can convert itself to a retreat and repair point, but are difficult to level. Level up some riflemen on unexpecting enemies, then switch into an available medic kit on the floor and boom - instant veteran medics. The same tactics apply to all preferred equipment & heavy weapons lying around.In the campaign it probably does make sense to lean on mechs, however the entire game is balanced differently for single player to enable the campaign to feel the way it should. Realize that campaign and multiplayer are different and the campaign is meant to be time consuming and challenging. I've replayed missions ive beaten for fun and some missions give you huge units caps, encouraging co-op with your friend.To all the fools talking about mech spam wins the game. Play someone online and try to build a mech without making 5+ infantry army first. I dare you to tell me infantry isn't effective. Dawn of war had turrets in your bases, in this game there is nothing to prevent the enemy infantry and reserve 1 from pushing you into your base and destroying you.If you're feeling like the game isn't balanced well or having trouble in MP, check out the online guides for this game. There is a lot of depth to the game that people just aren't exploring for whatever reason. For instance, people assume heavy mech for 700 beats two mechs for 350. If they stood and fought you are right. However this game isn't about direct stand-offs. A Gulyay-Gorod (final rusviet mech) will destroy a smialy (Polania scout mech), however 3 smialy's can run circles around gulyay and stop to shoot him for 10% minimum per volley. They reload in seconds, can run while reloading, and will pick that mega mech apart in 30-40 seconds. Those same smialy's will get evaporated by the newly buffed saxony artillery mech (Erlkonig) who has such range it can fire without being seen. Every faction has very interesting play & counter-play and there is actually A LOT to discover in that regard. A unit that isn't amazing on it's own operates well in packs, some operate well with a complimentary (Small hp, AP mech accompanying a hue HP, slow reload mech). Give it shot and look for resources online if you feel stuck. The community is active on discord and there's a ton of guide material out there.DLA POLANIA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!Thanks,Dawn of War Retiree

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game with an interesting setting, unit voice lines are fitting for their factions, and so forth. But as others voiced it isn't quite worthy of its Triple A price tag, as beyond the unit pathing being very...dumb it also seems to suffer some stability issues. It seems to quite easily glitch, not enough to crash but for the game to act off either due to fire effects making the screen wig out due to glitching flame textures. Or messing with your cosmetics can be...on and off due to the game getting fussy over it.Usually a restart of the game fixes the issues, and it isn't happening ALL the time but still not a good look for it to be so easy to happen when it does.Also the skirmish AI in this game  serious need of a tweak. I can easily beat Insane AI one V one with one tactic with any army vs any army...rush em. If you rush the AI with troops and even more build engineers for cheap then send them out to grab the weapon boxes. The AI simply cannot handle it, more so if you rush building more troops instead of say...a barracks like the AI likes to do. You can have two basic fighting infantry murder their own then push as you pump out more, capturing resources as you push in on the AI.Now I know Rush tactics should work against some, it why people use it. But every...single...time I can just run the AI down and ruin it. And even when I do let them build up it like they never can build up any real steam to be a threat, just a few units at a time going at me and I pick them off. Though that could be due to the extremely slow resource rate in the game, may want to add an option to speed that up for some who want faster games with more units to use.Is it a terrible game...nah, but it still needs work and I hope some updates can come in to fix these issues. Still would recommend to others, BUT I'd give them very clear warnings about the limitations it has right now.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a *bad* game, but it's mostly a scam. When you start the game up for the first time and try to modify your persona, you're presented with an enormous list of in-game purchase content. If I hadn't gotten the game via Humble choice, I would have refunded immediately. As it was, I went ahead and played a bit.There are very, very few units. The maps are an absolute slog. You can't issue commands while paused. You can't seemingly assign a unit both an individual and a group shortcut. The art style is great, but just get a copy of Scythe off eBay. It's the same art. With more variety. Yes, the board game this is a rip from has more unit variety, more faction variety ... and a lot more play variety.Get it for £10 or less and it's worth a few hours. Otherwise, it's just not. The campaign is far too short and truly unbelievably dull. You spend 30-60 minutes participating in an excruciating snowball fight as a 10 year old girl. Depending on how fast you play, that's 15-35% of the campaign. Your units do level-up, but there's no upgrade path. There's no stat screen. Hovering the units doesn't even tell you what their stats are so you can't even determine the relative value of upgraded units. The game simply isn't that good. It looks great, has some fun ideas, but it's really just a collection of purchasable skins. IE, a scam. It's a scam. With this level of in-game purchases, the game should be free.

_childDocuments_.review: In any RTS, it's essential to be able to build a forward base. Not in this game. On the good side, the Polania and Rusviet campaign scenarios are well designed. in contrast, I hate the scenario with Saxony campaign. It's dumb and not fun. It's unfortunate really since the faction has interesting characters. The campaign should show case what the game is capable of doing, not overwhelm the player with scenarios that is too stupid no matter how you look at it. Whoever designed the campaign surely didn't playtest the game. The limit on the number of units I can create is laughable. It seems that they designed the campaign to literally tie one of the players hand, poke one eye, and cripple their leg to make it seem "difficult" -- which says a lot of how poor the scenarios are designed. Also NPCs able to see my units as if no fog of war makes tactical maneuvers impossible. They can snipe my structures across the map without any scouts. Yeah, AIs are bad. I bought this on sale and still feel ripped off.Do I recommend this game? Not at the full price. Wait until it's 60% off since to me that's how much it's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game to release for years. I love the boardgame Scythe which is also based off of Jakub Różalski's artwork. To be completely honest I am not the biggest RTS fan, but I love the franchise and I really wanted to play the game. I bought it and played roughly under three hours of it and am heart broken to say it wasn't very good. The voice acting is sub-par (Playing on non-native mode) and the gameplay is lacking. The cover mechanic really doesn't work and some mechanics just feel useless. I found the computer would be pulling moves all over the map that I just couldn't respond too because I could only focus on one thing at a time. Especially when there is a limit to the units you can have and you are super out-numbered. Over-all I was excited for the game, and it has high potential, but not enough for me to not request a refund for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of strategy games. This game is definitely one of them that I enjoy playing. Been playing it the past few weeks and it's been nothing but fun and entertaining. The soundtrack is so inspiring that you would want to add it to a playlist to replay it on the other missions. Some of the missions are difficult like the stealth ones, but that's what makes the game even more interesting. I've never seen a strategy game have stealth missions like these that are also very interactive, like managing your troops against enemies that are stronger if you have the wrong troops facing them.I like the units, especially the mechanized ones. Their voice lines sound amazing, their movements are fluid, and reloads are  cool. Like the PZM-7 "Smialy" in the Polanian campaign, its reload has to be the coolest in the game in my opinion. It's also got multiplayer sessions where you can face your friends. Some of the maps you can use in those sessions are huge and open where you can have large defensive frontline battles. Overall, its a fantastic game to play and would highly recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Single-Player:The Campaign is a gripping grind where you constantly feel outnumbered, sometimes outmatched as well, but never bored. No, not at all! It's fast paced, and in your face constantly with some new challenge to overcome. The final boss of the campaign had me near chip my teeth, they were so taught! The Characters... Oh, THE CHARACTERS! The development of the characters and their feelings towards The War, The Toll it takes on them, The Zealotism they inspire... it's magnificent.This might contend for my favorite RTS Single-player Campaign of all time. It's f*cking rad!Multiplayer:The Controls are very similar to other big RTS titles like Command&Conquer and Dawn of War, with a very similar play-feel to DoW2. Minimal base building; Tank traps, sandbags, turrets/bunkers, etc. Heavy focus on Mechanized Combat (obviously), kinda wish the infantry didn't kinda lose their purpose after a certain point of the game, but that's honestly my only real gripe.This game is Fantastic.If you're newer to RTS, PLEASE pick it up! The Campaign is very beginner friendly, and the story is breathtakingly robust.If you're a veteran of Red Alert 3 and Dark Crusade, you'll feel right at home!Close to a Perfect 10 as I can think. Its Fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game more than company heroes 1 or 2, dawn of war series, whole shebang, and I'm going to tell you why. It's simple. That's it. You don't need to worry about too many moving parts but the pace of everything will still keep you engaged. I just get into the flow of a match and forget about everything it feels so intuitive. You might lose your first match or two horribly, because it is different. I wanted to use a lot of infantry, but then realized that I absolutely have to focus on mechs and anti-mech guns. You can still use a lot of infantry, but you absolutely do need combined arms. It can be rough though fighting against certain factions depending on what your faction is. Before I knew what I was doing, it was really rough. I love the aesthetic of everything, its all so much fun. I only wish I had gotten the game sooner. Not a lot of people seem to play it anymore, but the campaign is still very fun for me at least.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a while before it came out, then when it released to mixed reviews I decided to hold off. The F2P weekend and the game being on discount was a good chance to try the game, so I downloaded and started the Polania campaign.This is a game with a huge amount of potential in the IP, sadly let down by bad game design. I can't complain to have put a huge amount of time into the game, but you don't need to in order to see the deep, deep problems here.The game performs well when you are controlling a small number of units in the fairly scripted early missions. The enemies will be entrenched in certain locations and you can flank, use cover and abilities to take them down with minimal losses. However, once the game reaches the base-building stage, the missions just turn into a race against time to gather resources to squash the enemy before they amass enough troops to destroy your base. The game lets you know when you're taking too long by sending bigger and bigger waves troops to harass your base and speed you along.This is where the game starts to fall apart. You're forced to play quickly, tactics go out the window and the more units you control at once, the worse the game handles the cover mechanic, with troops getting confused about how to use cover and sitting on the wrong side of a wall in full view of the enemy, while taking fire and not automatically returning fire. The enemy start throwing grenades, then an enemy flamethrower mech shows up and your troops get wrecked.I get that perhaps the devs wanted troops to feel like meat for the grinder and the mechs to feel powerful but it's too imbalanced. Troops will stand in the open and plink away at flame mechs who just demolish them. The enemy AI will just spawn more and more units off-screen and fights just turn into battles of attrition as huge waves of enemies bum-rush your units and you hope you have the durability to survive the flood. Meanwhile, a timer in the background is counting down until the AI does it again. Can you gather enough resources and pump enough units out to beat the clock?This isn't really fun, tactical or clever gameplay. A shame because the setting and the mech designs are cool and the story seemed interesting. A massive wasted opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest : Waste of a great story!Although the dieselpunk style 1920's alternate reality was a great backdrop for a story. The gameplay is quite possibly one of the worst I have ever experienced. Company of Heroes came out in 2006 and you would think the gameplay mechanics of a similar rts game would improve over 14 years but...it actually is worse than CoH. The campaign missions are filled with antiquated battle mechanics. You can command a great army balanced with a combination of soldiers and mechs and still lose interest in completing missions because they are such a drag. Somehow even with enemy right in front of your units (i.e. mechs/squads) they refuse to fire unless commanded. so you can have a force of a 4/5 units but only 1 or two will engage the enemy. Somehow your mechs will always suck at manuvering and will take critical hits almost all the time while not even targeting an enemy in an arms length. The population mechanic also sucks, how does a landmine count as a pop+1? I don't know but it does. You do not have the option to set a default stance for a squad or a mech such as whether they will pursue an enemy or just take damage like idiots. No matter how much resource you control the enemy has unlimited resources even if you control 9 out of 10 mines/oil rigs. The stealth missions have basically no stealth mechanics to work with. Your stealth heroes have no way gauging the enemy's vision. even if the enemy units have their backs against you, somehow they know you're there. Staying in the shadows and destroying spotlights have no mechanics to work with in this game unlike MiMiMi studios games. I love to play RTS games for the story and I am not a hard mode fanatic nor do I participate in LAN parties or competetive online skirmishes. The Normal Mode gameplay is simply hours of frustration over grinding at the objective because your soldiers and mechs suck at killing the enemy or maintaining a formation because there is no option to make a formation while having multiple units selected. A Heavy artillery does not fire at targets far away unless you tell them to. THE MEDICS DONT EVEN HEAL SOLDIER SQUADS UNLESS YOU TELL THEM TO EVERY SINGLE TIME! IMAGINE THE FRUSTRATION THAT THEY DONT HAVE AUTO CASTING AND THEY COST.... WAIT FOR IT..........OIL AND IRON TO USE MEDICINE AND BANDAGES!!? I can understand the oil and iron expense while fixing a mech but seriously if the medics can't auto cast, they are just really bad meat-shields....Basically every unit you control is so bad at simply managing tasks or maintaining stances that if you want to strategise an objective by splitting up your forces, you will tearing your hair out trying to manage both because of how clunky the overall game mechanic is. So I have been playing the campaigns just to see the story end. It feels like a drag and I fell like I have wasted my money. Because again, the purpose of any game is to be fun and not seem like a chore. In that regard Iron Harvest is an absolute waste. I would not even recommend someone even download this game from one of the pirated websites because it feels so outdated in terms of gameplay.TLDR: 1. Good story, cool hero units.2. Horrible gameplay and outdated game mechanics.3. You are better off playing company of heroes all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable campaign. The setting is magnificent, the tone is too. I've been moved, I've scrambled to prepare for assaults with anticipation, I've had rushes as I watch my freedom fighters spring an ambush on enemies, I've laughed at my despised enemies taking the bait right into my waiting jaws. This couldn't happen without a campaign that makes one care. Love how you can capture guns and mechs, good CoH (Company of Heroes) influences there.Love how you can re-spec troops to be other classes in the field, on the fly,  depending on what's on hand. Setting where your troops will run to as they vacate a structure is nice.The cover system is good, but not perfect. Sometimes I found my last man in the unit crouching on the wrong side of the cover. Often I found the Ai running at my well 'dug in' troops instead of trying to flank or respect the kill zone between them and my troops, happily speeding through my hail of rifle fire to engage in melee... This felt a bit off. Having units with individuals like 1 heavy cannoner, 1 HMG guy, would feel more authentic than the entire unit swapping out with cannons or HMGs.  For me it is up there with CoH 2 because I like the Iron Harvest campaign better. I think CoH 2 has an edge with multiplayer, but I also think with a few adjustments the Devs could make this game superior in Multiplayer as well. For me, or probably for any steam or dieselpunk fan, this is an instant favourite.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest brings some enjoyable mechanics to the RTS genre. Walking your mechs through structures is easily one of the most fun features on the battlefield. Most of the maps I played on were varied enough and supplemented my strategies as well as that of the enemy. Coming from a Company of Heroes 1 & 2 background, it is easy to see pretty early on where this game excels and where it falls short. There are a lot of quality of life elements missing that made COH so enjoyable. For example, healing your units is a major inconvenience unless you have a unit who happened to pick up a medics kit in the field. Were you able to build small outposts that could reinforce your forces beyond the home base, that would be very welcomed. I found myself constantly running squads back to the barracks to heal and resupply their missing units. The difficulty of this game is fair. Not overwhelming on normal but not a cake walk either, which is good and this can always be adjusted. The world map mode is right up my alley. Reminds me of galactic conquest from the battlefront days. The story mode is decent but nothing I found myself writing home about. All in all, pick this title up only if you are wanting an interesting aesthetic and the joy of walking large mechanical war machines around on a map. Iron Harvest certainly sells itself on the premise and presentation but the execution of a really great RTS title falls a little short for me personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at reviews online, I was expecting to have an experience that was mediocre, but fun enough to make getting the game on sale worth it. "A love letter to CoH with too small a budget" was the the impression I got from others before playing, but I found myself having a lot more fun than I expected, and I wholly recommend it.They really strove to follow CoH's footsteps in almost every way. Aside from the setting, where Iron Harvest differs from CoH is that it dials back on the micro, and added a little C&C spice with the heroes (a la commandos). It ends up being a more fast paced and arcadey take. The graphics are really good. Most impressive is the building destruction and damage on the battlefield. Mechs will stomp on walls and walk through buildings. An entire city will end up leveled, aftermath of explosions of a long battle coating the landscape. It's a satisfying feeling when you can't even see where the road used to be anymore, and that city block is a field now.I can't speak on the campaign--I haven't played it yet.There's a lot I love about IH, but because much of what I love is what I love about CoH, it'd be redundant to touch on those qualities. That strength is also a bit of a weakness. It practically ends up being another flavour of Coh, and while I do love CoH and how IH tastes, it could stand to deviate and expand on the formula some more. I hope this game is successful enough that they'll make a sequel, because I can really see it coming into its own and being one of the best RTS out there.I'm sure I'll spot new things further down the line when I've a more competent grasp of everything, but so far my complaints are few: Most can be split up by whether they're affective against infantry or armoured units. I guess this is a consequence of aiming for a more arcadey feeling and lack of unit abilities, but I wish there was more decision making and strategy in what you produce.  Each faction has the same two buildings: barracks and workshops. Nothing really there except which you decide to build first. This aspect definitely needs expanding on. There could easily be 2 more buildings as both the barracks and workshops can be upgraded to unlock a whole other set of units for production. Splitting them up would be an immediate improvement and allow for more meaningful choice and strategy.Outside of those two major things, all IH is missing is some polish, and polish goes a long way.They're not bad, but they leave more to be desired and don't leave a strong impression. Except the grunts you hear during melee bouts and deaths; those are kind of bad. Sometimes you have one or two models going a different route than the rest of the squad which can be... interesting. That said, being able to C+click to tell mechs to move in reverse to a destination is a much loved feature. Why CoH doesn't have this baffles me. To explain, you can go in for a melee attack to prevent squads from using their weapons to even the playing field. It's a great idea and can be fun, but it seems like a bit of an afterthought. You can be behind cover, firing on the enemy, but they will frequently just run up and vault them for a good ol' lengthy bout of fisticuffs. If it went faster and there were ways to avoid it, it'd be in a good spot. It needs expansion to add some depth. Perhaps adding an element of risk, increasing damage done to squads charging in, or units with different melee specialties. It's more of a graphical detail than a mechanic currently because it doesn't take them that long to get back up and shooting again. Now, with heroes it works as you would expect since they're a single unit, it's just with squads that it ends up being more visual flare.   A lot of things you'd expect to be able to position behind for cover, you can't. Where models position behind cover is questionable at times as well. Four might go up to the wall of sandbags, but another will be behind a crate 10 feet back.As I said in the beginning, as much as I love it, IH is little more than another flavour of CoH. Why is this? It's not just the shared mechanics, but also part of the delivery. I love Jakub Różalski's art, and the game could stand to embrace it more. Saying it needs to be gritty isn't quite it, but the atmosphere his artwork holds isn't quite there on the maps. It's there in the mechs, and it's there in the UI art, but not so much in the game itself. Let me ask you this, what do you see when you look at Jakub Różalski's art? Almost every work is from the perspective of the common folk, as towering and daunting machines of a wartorn world creep in the distance. IH has those machines, but that is half of what the art and world of Jakub Różalski is. What of the common folk? If you were to ask me how this game could embrace both aspects, it envision it being something like this:Don't just have fuel and ore resources, have food as well. The fields in the art of Jakub Różalski are those of farmers, of people trying to make it by. Imagine if there were farms that you had to capture, to feed your army lest they begin to starve. Not only that, imagine if you had to tread carefully on these farms. Bombing them to kingdom come while fighting the enemy might not be in your best interest, as it would kill the farms and farmers that feed your war. Perhaps you could do just that to farms under the enemy's control if you can't hold them for yourself? Now  would be true victory points. Iron Harvest has the Iron, but not the Harvest. It needs to divorce itself from CoH and really embrace its setting, to come into its own and stand amongst it's peers instead of in their shadow.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun RTS. Never played Company of Heroes, so I have no idea if this is similar to that, but it does seem somewhat similar to Halo Wars, which I played for forever. The campaign is interesting, and the characters are intriguing. As far as gameplay goes, there are multiple campaign missions that are unique and provide a new challenge for the players, which is nice. The skirmish maps are about as interesting as any game's skirmish maps, although I'd appreciate a bit more variety (going back to Halo Wars, it was always fun to have to capture additional base sites from neutral parties, so adding something like that would be interesting, although it may not make sense for the setting). Critiques:Air units are overpowered. I wouldn't really have an issue with this if there was a proper counter to them, like anti-air infantry or mechs, but there isn't really an obvious option, aside from anti air defenses which can only be built by your base. A lot of people complain about the specialized nature of infantry, and while I personally have no problem with this as it makes sense and there are ways to change the infantry specialization, that is a thing that exists in the game. My biggest issue in the game is the way cover works. It doesn't make a whole lot of sense in my opinion, and there are a lot of areas where it seems like there should be cover and there isn't. Men of War: Assault Squad 2 did an outstanding job with cover and I'd love to see something like that in this game. Overall, this is a very fun game and I'd definitely recommend it, especially if the devs decide to fix some of the balance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally recommend this game!I backed this game on Kickstarter (so really, I was lucky and got this game on a discount already) and played a little bit of the closed beta- there has been a ton of refinement in just the past 3-4 months, and though there are a couple items not in the release as of this writing, devs have a roadmap detailing that all features from the store page will be up and running in the next 4 weeks. There is no fraud here.That said, what is in the game already is very worth. The campaign is well written, music is good, great graphics and art- if you like the Scythe-Boardgame world this is based in, it is a must-play.It is very similar to COH2, however it is also different- many of the 'same' mechanics (cover, destructible terrain) are here but they are also slightly different. To say one is better or the other is better, I think it is just better to look at it that this is a different game, period. You can de-crew weapons in this game, something you can't do in COH2. The cover system is a little weird (compared to COH2) but it works, just takes getting used to. And most actions you set your troops to doing will have an interruptible time-counter (sorta like 'channeling' a spell in some games) which is a mechanic you have to get used to- different than COH2. Armies/"army cards" and pop-cap have different rules, so your army is limited in size by a couple adjustable constraints. Retreating is also different- you don't have added resistance to damage and run-away at light speed when you're in retreat mode so if you have poor timing or a bad retreat path you will have your squad get wiped! There are other differences, so playing through the campaign you do learn what they are and how they work (or just trial-& error some skirmish matches and you will get most of it).If you like Starcraft/Warcraft, C&C games, COH and the Dawn of War RTS games, and like that they are all different in their different ways and yet you like them for how they are... you're really going to like this game, because again it is like those games, but different in sufficient ways to be unique. When you smash through some buildings with your biggest 'mech like Godzilla and blow up some stuff, it is just a little bit easy to really like this game.Other nice comforts about it are that there is a good achievements system set-up in the game with like a goals-map to unlock cosmetics, which I think is pretty well done (almost have to have stuff like that nowadays, and this game has a good one).  Full campaign for each faction (there's three), and I already saw some hints in the campaign that possibly some of the other factions from the boardgame might someday be added? Who knows.So if you are an RTS fan (campaigns & light multiplayer) or a Scythe fan, I am sure you would really like this game. If you want to play an extremely-well made new RTS game, I am sure you would enjoy playing this game. There's nothing else like it right now, I doubt there will be another game like it really. Get it!
