_childDocuments_.review: As a starting note to those that ask: "Is this Scythe as an RTS???" and say: "This looks like Jakub Rozalski's art!". You are correct, Iron Harvest is from that universe. Which is quite an exciting universe to build an RTS from with an amazing amount of content and ideas to work with. I also will admit now I can't cover everything but ey, I ain't the only person reviewing this.I participated in the Alpha/Beta stages, and played games here and there since joining in 2018 to see the progress and provide feedback. As much as I would love to rather recommend the game, I cannot as of writing this review. The reason being is that the release felt rushed, I understand they wanted to make this specific date (1/9/20 - Unless you're American with your weird ways) to match 1920. As mentioned in some other reviews the game still needs work and still feels like a pre-release build. And with that I can't confidently recommend this game with a $68.99 CAD price tag to my peers.Positive:The game at its core and the idea of it is well done, even in its current state. The idea for the game is definitely refreshing for an RTS, and the single-player story is amazing. The mechs are wonderfully done and seeing them crash through buildings is amazing. The variety of units, and the ability to change a squad's speciality on the fly by picking up weapons is great. The three factions feel unique and each offer their own play style. I love the concept of the game, it's potential, and the overall graphics and aesthetic are well done for a small team. Negative:However, the game's potential is still somewhat far off. The pathing is clunky, the controls in general feel clunky. As in you think you deselected a unit or selected a different unit or group, but the previous unit was still selected. There are still bugs that need fixing here and there that seem like they wouldn't be in a full release. There are of course balance issues with some units but that's a given with a fresh-release RTS. The elephant in the room is the lack of Skirmish maps, no co-op campaign, and missing features in general. One of the biggest no-nos of putting a game into full release is advertising features on the store page and those features being minimal or non-existent.Finally I'll say that despite the current state of things, I have faith that KING Art games can fulfill their promises and achieve their ambitions for Iron Harvest. They jumped the gun but I know they are competent and have the drive to finish the job. I'm sure as time goes on this game will turn into a masterpiece that will deserve its current price tag. One day we'll have all the features promised, and who knows what more. I understand that KING Art games is a small team so I ask others to go easy on them, what they have accomplished so far is still a MASSIVE undertaking for them.Keep at it K.A. we're rooting for ya.(Also if you read this, I gotta be honest the release trailer music was uh ... undesirable)After note: K.A. has confirmed they are currently working on the promised features.

In conclusion it has a lot of potential but feels like it's in early access and lacks many features.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------About this game, I like the concept, story and visually this game is great.I also like playing games that I get addicted to playing and this one lacks just that. _childDocuments_.review: is a 'sideways thumb' game for me, although it gets the thumbs-up as a tiebreaker just for the sake of the killer aesthetic and extremely ambitious aims (which it mostly fails to match).The high concept pitch is that in an alternate 1920, the advent of the combustion engine leads not to conventional trucks, tanks and planes, but rather to humanoid mechs like a kind of diesel-powered .  In 1920, an alternate Great War breaks out between the nations of "Polania," "Rusviet," and "Saxony," and if you can't determine what real-world nations these are obvious ciphers for just by name alone, then maybe strategy games aren't for you.  This leads to a funky and unique aesthetic for a "historical" war game, where the drably muted, real-world Eastern European countryside typical of a game like  is now studded with bits of alt-history futuretech like gigantic mad-scientist cables and early civilian "cars" with spider legs instead of wheels.That comparison to  is certainly more than aesthetic, however.  Aside from the mechs (which is admittedly a big "aside"),  is a fairly direct descendant of that seminal RTS title, with some balance weirdness compared to its older relative.   is a game that's more about tactical positioning and unit countering than about basebuilding or infrastructure: it has a noticeably low unit cap for the storied RTS genre, and a similarly very low variety of buildings and upgrades.  Instead, the game puts most of its effort into having a snappy, fast-paced battle cadence, with bitter and immediate fights waged over the automated resource points that will determine who snowballs to victory faster.  The game's dense old-world cityscapes, rich with both sturdy and fragile cover objects, make infantry battles bracing and tricky to navigate, and mis-positioning your riflemen so that they get caught out in the middle of a street can often end with them getting mercilessly cut down in seconds.  Losing a unit isn't an immediate loss, but given that the total unit cap is very low and units accrue experience that makes them fight better over time, every unit death is a  setback that can disrupt your snowball.  Because of this, units require a  amount of micromanagement, even for the already micro-heavy RTS genre: you'll need to be carefully and manually repositioning all your units at all times in every fight, with an itchy trigger finger on the 'retreat' button so that you can avoid those punishing unit deaths.Unfortunately, the game's tech progression means that infantry and thus the whole cover positioning metagame becomes rapidly outmoded, and the map design irrelevant: When the player can start building their first mechs, they're an extremely noticeable improvement over every infantry unit, even those infantry units who are specifically supposed to be "mech killers."  The lightest class of mech come in an anti-infantry and anti-armor variety, and even without the anti-infantry mech -- which easily decimates all infantry -- an anti-armor light mech is still about on equal footing against a unit of anti-armor infantry who should theoretically win that rock-paper-scissors matchup.  By the time the player progresses to medium, and then heavy mechs, mechs can sweep any infantry off the board with all the effort of a feather duster clearing a cobweb.  Because mechs can walk clean through buildings, and shoot through them as well (which is very cool to watch), the cover-to-cover tactical positioning gameplay morphs into just snowballing your doomstack of mechs at the opponent's doomstack of mechs in lieu of more sophisticated tactics.  The only reason that infantry remain present in the game at all is that they're the only units who can heal the much more important mechs (if the "engineer" specialization is chosen), and the only units who can capture resource points, which will drip-feed the player the currency to buy more mechs.By the end of most games of , I had two engineers, no other infantry, and had filled the rest of my army up to the unit cap with simply the heaviest mechs I could, because heavier mechs are better and fight harder than smaller mechs.  I consider this fairly linear progression of power to be a bit boring compared to the combined-arms approach that the game's box art promises, with mechs towering over fields of infantry.Although if I were forced to review it on its strategic ruleset alone I might give  a thumbs down, games are more than their mechanics, and not only does the presentation of  go a long way, but so does the campaign.   has a sprawling, fully voiced story campaign that feels like a throwback to  or  in the best way, which both teaches the player the game and throws in cool but janky "classic RTS" novelty missions like the obligatory stealth sequence with only one or two units.  I particularly enjoyed a toggle entitled "Native Mode," which rather than presenting the game in one regional localization, makes the dialogue of each unit and cutscene accurately reflect the language of their own nation for better immersion.  The campaign is killer throughout, with a legitimately interesting storyline and some cool setpiece moments, and is arguably worth the price of admission for  even if the basic tactics battles aren't on their own.In conclusion,  is a "Company of Heroes-alike" that seeks to at once to follow the footsteps of retro squad-RTS titles that have fallen out of favor today, while also adding a bold new flair with the introduction of mech-versus-mech warfare that turns the  game loop on its head.  It doesn't necessarily succeed as a great, competitively-balanced strategy game that people will be playing a decade from now, but it's worth a play for its solid campaign and its cool dieselpunk setting alone.Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to be talking about the bugs as the devs are still working on the game so they will most likely get fixed instead I will be talking about the feel of the game.Iron Harvest is a Dawn of War style RTS. you move around the map looking for points to control that will give you a steady supply of oil or steel, and that is it, you can build a base but with only 3 buildings you will finish that task very quickly, you can build mechs, but you really don't need to, most of the time you will build infantry to capture points and rely on the reserve system to give you all the mech power you need.The game feels at odds with its self. The Dawn of war style was made to create faster gameplay with infantry playing a key role, as for the 40k franchise murdering large numbers of infantry fits, sure they have big mechs but at the end of the day the focus is on the space marine. Iron harvest has the same system at yet it feels so much slower, and I think the reason why is the focus it should be on these massive awe inspiring mechs, but instead it's on the infantry because they do everything: cap points, build, fortify positions, repair, heal and have mechanics for swapping weapons and cover, while all the mechs do is shoot and walk through buildings and for most mechs the way they shoot and do things feels very similar regardless of faction, the only exception is the serp with its melee.This creates a game where the mechs that are supposed to be the stars of the show are so unimportant that you will only build buildings just so you can send in the reserves, that might have some mechs in. This creates a game that should deliver fast paced action, but doesn't because we are in a slog of waiting till we gather enough oil and steel to get the ones we want, but we don't because the of the reserve system means you will most likely go for what gets you the most bang for your buck.There are interesting mechanics and the game can be fun, but the focus on infantry ruins how the mechs should feel.

Also the least they could have done was give each faction a different skin for the airships. But, sadly even before Operation Eagle came out the game still had a major imbalance, Poland sucked. Their infantry was good, but all infantry except the anti-tank gun and the anti-tank gunners become useless 10-20 minutes in.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you the type of person that likes RTS games but does not play in ranked matches and competitive scenarios? Well, that game is for you then.Don't mind the negative comments, most of them were people that were already playing the game, since they had access to the beta (I mean, some reviewers have 500 hours registered, which is pretty strange, since the game was officialy launched today), and, besides having an earlier access to the game, they also are competitive players.I'm pretty sure that most of the public likes RTS, but noT to the point to play ranked matches. So... yeah, Iron Harvest is a great game if you're this type of player.A great single player campaign, awesome graphics, interesting lore, nice units and factions, a deep strategical layer... Yeah, the game may have some "cons": some features that has not been implemented yet (notice the yet here, yet), some bugs and a little bit of a "clunkiness" in the units movement, but that's about it.Iron Harvest is a great game, if you're into RTS games but doesn't care a lot about ranked matches, buy it. If you play RTS only for ranked matches and competitive scenarios... Stay away, for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept and imaginations, these industrial ww1 looking mech units are great and the great war/interwar period theme are very unique, i love the theme of this game, remind me of Valkyria chronicles. A lot of people complained about the "repetitive" gameplay in the campagin which is kinda true but they are not bad, they are actually quite fun with big explosion, yes you will get tired of it after gaming it for like 3 or 4 hours none stop, but take a break and come back and you enjoy it again, the game remind me of command and conquer games's campaign where the fun is in watching lots of explosion and campy dialogue and cut-scenes. The gameplay itself is some what similar to game like company of heroes, i really love the detail on the units with varity of taking cover animations, but there is also a problem with microing the units as they don't exactly respond to your command due to these detailed animations, and the cover mechanic will make the units don't respond in time because you are trying to micro them and the unit ai are juggling between sticking to playing the cover animation and responding to your command so they won't fire their dam weapon lol. also there is very little incentive to build infantry eventually as you just want those mech, which a big problem in company of heroes 2 where tanks just dominate the game.The story of the game is fun, i can see that the devs poured a lot of hearts and soul into make them and for the effort i will give them A great compliment.  but it sometimes take some funny directions with alternative interpretations of history, take example of the Rosviet Revolution campaign, I thought you be playing as the revolutionaries and overthrown the tyrannical Tsar's government, but nah, you are playing as a counter revolutionary, and it's okay to be a reactionary cuz this reactionary leader is a strong independent woman, and the people's anger at the oppression they suffer and the lack of ability for the people to choose their leader is "worng" and "mob like" and should be stopped so "order" and "law" can be restored, I don't think a inbred who born into a postion of monarchy should even be a monarch in the first place, that maybe there shouldn't even be a monarchy in th first place?  The revolutionary people are framed as "misguided" and "mob like" by evil manipulator usurper like "rasputin" to upset the "order and law". but then again this game is made by people who are heavily influence by liberal politics so i am not too surprised by the story plot. But over all excpt for the funny story theme, the game is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game recently put in 42 hours played the campaign on the hardest difficulty and finished it because I paid 55 bucks for this so I was going to get my moneys worth, first almost full priced game I've bought this year. this game made me angry I had to take a break a few times because it kept putting me in a bad mood. Not because the game is bad it has a lot of strong points the story is alright I enjoy the mechs and the different armies in the campaign tho not sure why we didn't get a few missions where we got to play as the fourth army you come in to contact with in the campaign. The computer cheats like a lot which made it so infuriating playing on the hardest difficulty the computer doesn't have to follow the same rules as you do or at least it seemed to me in my play through to be the case one mission I was taking out the computers base and it spawned a giant army around me and wiped out all my mechs. In few missions I cut the computer off from all resources and it was still able to throw out a lot of big mechs in a short period of time. In the first train section mission the computers train gun can snipe you from half way across the map while in the second mission you get the same weapon and the range isn't anywhere near what the computer got I couldn't even attack mobs over a small forest with it so it was a pretty useless weapon that mission. The base building feels tacked on as there is only three unit producing structures one being your hq so meh. You have your defensive structures like bunkers which are kind of useless because they die so fast I didn't bother using them as in the harder difficulty early in the game you are scrounging for materials like yeah they help with infantry (still get melted) but really the computer is throwing a mix of infantry and mechs at you in quite a few of the missions from the get so I stopped using them quite quickly same with the razor wire and sand bags those are just a waste of resources cause they get destroyed so fast. The land mines are useless the enemies mines one shot your mechs but your mines only do like 1/5th the health of a medium enemy mech at 100 iron a mine they are expensive and useless so I didn't use them at all. The stealth missions brings the game to a grinding halt it was not enjoyable. I get company of heroes 2 vibes from this game while that wasn't my favorite game I didn't hate it nor do I hate this game from what I understand this is an indie developer which I thought was cool for what you got tho honestly I don't think this game is worth 69.89 or 55 as I got it on a bit of a discount. I'd say if you can pick it up for 30 it would be a good play through but in the current state I found myself getting angry at the game more than enjoying myself. But hey if you like company of heroes 2 you'll probably like iron harvest. I'd give it 3/5 pretty average game and sort of a product of the times.

_childDocuments_.review: REVOLTING, NOT REVOLUTIONARY!Honestly I was expecting great things with this game, along the lines of Command and Conquer or Battle for Middle-Earth. One of the biggest issues for me is the set build area's they are very small and often undefendable. The unit Cap and Cost do not match that of a strategy game and more of a 5 party adventure game like Dawn of War 2. The unit Cap also makes those experienced strategists who would play on a veteran setting waste so much time as by the time you've enlisted half your forces you've faced twice your unit Cap in waves of enemies resulting in most your forces being KIA and needing to be re-enlisted and this process does not become any less tedious as you continue.  The Concept, I really liked it was Scythe meets C&C and should have been the revolutionary strategy game for the new generation. The narrative in game is sub-par, there are elements there that make you want to continue but again was very drab and lacklustre, its war yet every cut scene has none of the urgency, emotion or grit of an actual battlefield. Like all strategy games there is three basic objectives defence, escort and offence, if balanced correctly the player will feel like the levels are very different and diverse but unfortunately this game has dropped the ball, with most levels being escort work paired with its other short comings makes it very monotonous and repetitive. To surmise this game its not an Real Time Strategy game its a Role Playing Game that neither delivers on story or entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest at its core is an enjoyable mech filled alt-history RTS akin to Company of Heroes (CoH). Whilst there's less of a focus on squad tactics here than in CoH the unique mechs each of the three factions has more than makes up for it. I can't speak for the multiplayer, but the singleplayer was excellent. It has its corny moments, but an interesting overarching story and varied gameplay keeps you engaged. Also, who doesn't love mechs the size of city blocks stomping through buildings whilst decimating everything around them!? Moreover, the developers keep updating the game with new content, features and bug fixes! Overall I would recommend this game to any strategy games enthusiast, especially if it's on sale. Just don't go into this game expecting CoH III, you'll probably be disappointed. I'm hopeful that we'll get an expansion introducing another bunch of unique mechs, maybe even a faction or a sequel set around the time the Second World War occurred!

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, I love this game. I'm not very good at it, but I love it. The infantry may feel similar in the regard of troop types (which some may dislike) but that is purposeful (And there are differences to the weapons the different faction's infantry wield). But where the big difference lies is the Mechs. If you like Diesel punk then this game is most certainly for you, smoke spewing Mechs ripping through buildings, unabashed by such petty mortal things such as the infrastructure of the city they are meant to take, The Polanian Mechs quickly out maneuvering the enemy, Rusviet Mechs aggressively stomping after the terrified foe, and the bulky Saxonian Mechs holding firm against the pathetic waves of inferior engineered mechs (I'm not faction biased I swear).  Its heaven for those that like such Aesthetics. Of course, like most RTS games it requires some learning to get great at. But with patience even I was able to get better at my favourite faction, mighty Saxony. There is a lot of criticism over the game being made better over weekly updates, but what one must remember is that a lot of game developers are doing this now, they adapt their updates to what the player base wants, they also do regular tweaks to the balancing to ensure that everything feels fair. (Take that Rusviet Vanguard). So in conclusion, I would recommend this game for its setting, its awesome models and its game play.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game at it's current state, I may change my rating once they do something with the game to fix a lot of the Glaring issues, below will be the breakdown on the good and BAD sides of this game. I will be as detailed as can be to help those who might be interested in this game but also want to know more about this game. 1. Menu and Interface (start screen and game interface) Good:- looks niceThat's it!BAD:- clunky- too designed for looks rather than function- In game achievements (required for account cosmetics and other bonuses) soooooo messy (not optimized and time consuming) each achievement you have to unlock individually, no claim all button, and each one has to undergo an animation that adds to the time... that's time of your life wasted in none essential "FLUFF" PLEASE ADD A "CLAIM ALL" BUTTON you're needlessly wasting time. -too much loading between interfaces (due to the aesthetic nature of many of it's menu loading between each area moves between 3-5 seconds at least, this may not be big but it adds up Note: my unit is a mid tier gaming rig. compared to other titles this is a bit annoying, not to everyone but I added it here to inform those who may find this annoying)- no choice for static image (not everyone likes or needs animated background more often than not it's a waste of processing power)2. AI (both enemies and your units)Good:- AI CAN be challenging and fun to play with.again... THAT's it!BAD:- AI CHEATS A LOT (the AI seems to be able to produce units faster and cheaper than players) at first I thought it may be similar to other games that the AI teams just share resource unlike player teams BUT after one game where one of our friends disconnected near the end of the game (note: we all had little to no resources left at that point of the game) the AI managed to pull out several units within the span of a few seconds (not cheap units mind you) like MAGIC... - AI pathing is broken (your units) this is not always the case 100% of the time, but your units can sometimes be as DUMB as Bricks, choosing to go a longer path OR running into enemies despite having a clear path of choice nearby (more often than not this happens to infantry units) .- AI Logic is Broken (this may fall more into how the game has become with the expansion rather than a core issue) some units that can clearly hit targets (have line of sight and CAN hit those targets specifically (flying)) still move closer just to fire... this may be the case if the Game did not give is the attack range of the units... BUT it did, you have the option to show range, and more often than not this range means nothing (mostly on mech units and field guns/cannons/machine guns) even units having a clear shot... and have shot said target before (air unit) often needs to re-position often to a point they cannot fire (often the case with bigger mechs) - AI controlled unites seem to be stronger and more accurate than Player units (specially early game)  early game encounters even 1 on 1 will often end up with you being defeated (even without cover mechanics or such, even same unit types) AI seem to be more accurate than your own.3. Game-play and MechanicsGood:- Fresh take on some RTS mechanics.- unit movement is fluid does not feel too roboticBAD:- COVER MECHANIC IS A JOKE, I've played several games where the enemy has "Gone to cover" and i shot them from obvious openings (such as the back or sides of said cover) and they seem to sponge all the bullets off. I've played a lot of RTS that have cover mechanics and none are as BAD as this one, and I'm not talking about garrison cover either, this game can have units lean on the wall for cover BUT getting shot from the open area of said wall STILL provides cover, rather than how cover works in most games (cover reducing damage due to shots hitting the wall or missing) this games feels like it apples a damage reduction to units for just being IN cover even IF YOU"RE SHOOTING THEM IN THE BACK!- Unit models are oddly overlapping. several instances that I click one unit and send it forward only to see I GOT 2 squads from one click (Note: a drag selection just mouse click) 4. Units and Character design and functionalityGood:- Unique Base Units design per faction (base and not DLC units)- Unique Mech design per faction- Unique Base designs per faction- Each mech unit plays differently but close enough that you don't get confused or overwhelmed- limitation of certain infantry unit types per faction - good and varied unit roster (Base Game)BAD- Shared unit types on flyers (Expansion/DLC) only unique flyers are the new faction and even they have the same onld basic flyers added with the ones they have (sloppy work) - a lot of unit features are just aesthetic (guns that don't fire) (armor that does nothing) (does not have a good feel unlike games of the same genre) - Unite rank value Hardly means anything (for infantry it makes them tougher for mechs it's not noticeable) unlike other games where rank either gives improved range, damage, or armor, other than infantry ranks are hardly noticeable on other units (Example: rank 4 mech Hero can't survive a rank 2 anti armor infantry) - Unit value per feature greatly unused (melee units that should be tanky and tough for "MELEE" Are not, and die more often than not heading towards their target) while range units often share the simple weakness of back attacks (which arty units can exploit)

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not delivering some promised features at launch, still best tactical RTS since CoH2.The game is rather about the right tactic and strategy, than fast hitting keyboard.Right now you have:story mode for all 3 factions with 7 missions3 challenge maps, where you have to defend from waves of enemies3 maps for 1vs13 maps for 2vs22 maps for 3vs3PvPAll together you have by each faction not so much to build,just start with HQ and can build barrack and workshop for mechsdefence tower with 2 upgrades and minesthe 1 exo-suit-squad unit, 3 heroes and 6 mechs are very different,but the 3 weapon systems teams"mortat/anti-mech/mg" and 7 soldiers types are very similar,by each faction you can hire only 5 of 7, as some weapon types are exclusive for other factions, but can he harvested from killed enemy squads, like germany has doctors, poland MG and russia flame throwersThe Story is Ok, but mission design does have quite some hiccups, where you move handful of units over the map or enemy is spamming a lot of enemies. And it more takes time and patience to finish them, than making actual strategical decisions. The game is very good balanced for multiplayer, so far each unit has a functional counter unit.While the missions can be very challenging, the AI in skirmish is for skilled RTS player no problem.Gameplay wise it does have some neat impulses, mechs than break though buildings and obstacles, harvesting gear from killed enemies squads or collect resources from enemy killed mechs, with cover system and retreats do give quite good gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing CoH-like rts game (meaning it resembles the mechanics of company of heroes [a superb game series if you haven't played it] closely while also maintaining its own unique identity)This game is fun for both the casual rts player who doesn't play many of these types of games and for experienced rts players.For the casual player, it offers a good campaign with well done cinematic scenes and good voice acting especially when playing in "native languages" mode. As well as a skirmish and scenarios mode that is full of challenges, rewards and unlockables. With plenty of new stuff being added through a season system which is free to participate in and you get all your rewards, no paywalls once the game is yours. Which is a breath of fresh air in today's dev cycle of games.For the vets, it has casual multiplayer, and ranked multiplayer. A good amount of maps(with definitely more coming) and a variety of game modes. Each faction has its own deep tactical/unit pool and almost every match requires different tactics and units depending on your opponents play style. Unlike games like starcraft, if you are down, or lose a few large battles you are most certainly not out! The matches are a bit lengthier and there is a great comeback potential if you re-organize yourself and truly outwit your opponent, the game is balanced and fair overall. I can highly recommend this game for anyone who enjoys rts, or even wants to get started in it. I suggest getting the deluxe edition as it will give you access to future dlc, as well as a current dlc campaign that's been released already. Finally, sadly no match history or theatre mode yet but i'm sure the devs will be adding these things in the future as it's still a very new game from a relatively small studio. They definitely deserve our support :) This game has amazing potential for the future, and is still currently a great game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably more of an early impressions than a review, but I will not be playing it any further and my last mission had such a sudden drop in my enjoyment that I want to give it a down before I leave it to most likely just sit in my library for the time being. So I actually enjoyed the game a lot for the three first missions. They got an interesting world, a decent enough story if kinda over-the-top in dialogue at times, and as a fan of C&C Red Alert I love that in my RTS games. The combat worked well enough to keep me interested, and I liked the massive and slow robots, and thought the protagonist of the Polania campaign was decent and fun. So what happened in the fourth map that absolutely KILLED my enjoyment of the game?Base building was introduced, and with it a beyond ridiculously low army size, which just made the map an absolute chore to get through, because you can't really build anything up. It made everything grind to a halt as I just saw the ressources keep rising and rising without anything to spend it on, and without the ability to make the battle feel big, and I constantly had to send my army back and forth over the open map, which felt like it was made for way for units than I was able to field and it felt so wrong and artificial to not be able to actually field an overwhelming army in an open map when you have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of ressources. Or put up defences for anything I had taken because I didn't have any way to defend that didn't cut into the army size, even putting up mines and a bunker appeared to cut into it and I just... I really thought it was fun before, but I feel so incredibly limited once the army size gets introduced as a factor. It might work perfect in multiplayer, I don't know, but for the campaign it turns what is otherwise set up as a good or even great title into something that drains the fun out of me...

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure everyone. Before I type anything else I feel obligated to tell you, I love mechs. I have ever since I was a kid. Not those skinny fast Gundam things the kids are always talking about. I'm talkin'  stompy abominations that sputter and are cobbled together with duck tape, zip ties and prayers. Guns booming and clattering as they push the enemy line, firing off one last barrage before shuddering under the weight of it all and collasping over onto a line of trenches, crushing the enemy infantry fleeing before it's terrible might.Iron Harvest looks and like what I imagined the army men and action figures I smashed together as a kid did. The effects and animations of all of the mechs and infantry are varied and wonderfully done, I have nothing but praise for KING Art as far as the models and sound design go. Plenty of variation between factions as well, each factions units are instantly identifiable which I love.That being said, this is not a spectacularly deep game and that bears mentioning as I know some people crave a high APM, extremely intense and in depth RTS. I don't think you'll find that here. The combat feels very much like Company of Heroes, insomuch that if you told me this was a mod for the first game I would believe you. The combat (more or less) boils down to take cover and shoot the other guys. Some things kill infantry well, and not mechs and other things the opposite. More or less anyway. I don't consider myself very good at RTS games, and I have been playing the AI at the hardest difficulty without any issue. The Computer isn't very smart, but i'm just here to smash my mechs against theirs anyways!Skirmish plays as you would imagine, and although i've only played the first 6 levels of the campaign I was very pleased with what I encountered. Very much reminds me of, if you'll humor me, the .It does have a little wonkyness, I've experienced a few times where a unit did not take the path I quite expected it to but nothing outside of acceptable parameter in my personal opinion.  There aren't a huge selection of maps out as of today for the skirmish mode, but the ones that are here are designed well and there are more coming down the pipeline according to the dev roadmap.Coop is as of the time of writing this NOT implemented but is slated to be released in the 2nd week after release. This was a huge deal breaker for some people but I am not so horribly offended that it has hampered my enjoyment of the game in any way.It's not perfect, but damn if I don't love mechs.TLDR: If you every wished Company of Heroes had mechs instead of tanks, do us both a favor and go ahead and click Add to Cart. It's worth it.If you are looking for the next Starcraft, a micro heavy or APM intensive game, I don't think you'll find what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive and really simple to play. It reminds me of my childhood playing Command and Conquer Generals, I have only just scratched the surface of this game. The "War Map" is definitely my favorite game-mode. It is like playing an RTS version of Star Wars BF2: Galactic conquest. The story campaign is pretty good, I recommend it being played in the native dialogue with subtitles. It isn't hard to follow and it gives ample time to read what is on screen, it also isn't really distracting from the game-play as most story dialogue is cut-scene based. Overall, I don't play many RTS so this I would say this is a great introductory one. It's not to complicated and can be picked up easily, while still having a learning curve that makes you extremely deadly the faster you position and take map control. It was a little jarring to have to switch gears from the campaign because it doesn't really punish you for being slow. But if you play anything outside the story, the AI will punish you hard for playing defensive early on. I find it the most fun to be aggressive to a certain point in the map and then build a FOB to then launch attacks from, this combined with the random missions given to you during the World War game-mode make it the go to game mode. I will definitely be sticking with this game for hours and look forward to future content if any.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up regarding the story modeThumbs down regarding the skirmish and multiplayerI give it a thumbs up cause I really enjoyed playing the game also the multiplayer especially at the start. But with the time this game gets a bit repetetive especially for the cases thumbs down.Graphics are dope. It's really hardwarehungry but if you have a machine that can handle this title you're rewarded with a beatiful looking rts. The art style especially of the mechs is so brillant. I luv how they look, how they move, how they attack and how they blow up after drawing their last oily gearwheel  breath. Whats missing here is more diversity, and more cool and various skins. You also need all dlcs if you want to be able to play all factions and available skirmish maps.. that sux.. at least the multiplayer or skirmish mode should be unlocked for everyone.. but maybe I'm  spoiled by sc2 (don't get me wrong!! blizzard and activision ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it all up).The gameplayreview is a bit tricky. I like it somehow even if the delay of the unitreactions is annoying.. all in all the pace of the game is to slow especially with the bigger units. The developers worked hard on this title and I think it improved a lot since they launched it but still everything could be more responsive.The problem with this game is the same like in company of heroes. They have basebuilding but not really. They give you tasks to do but it's not like you really have the feeling of working on a mission. In the storymode it's working cause they combine your duties with several missions and things to keep an eye on, I know it's easier to implement stuff like this into the campaign but cause of the lack of diversity in units, actions and the whole factions in general the gameplay gets monotone soon if you play skirmish and online. Thats a big problem in terms of grabbing someones longterm attention in a singlerounded battle rts.The atmosphere is cool. The somehow standard story is alright but they decided to revive a time that already past by 100 years ago, they did well with that but still they could fresh the whole thing up in a less conservative way. It's like they just added some steampunk elements and kept the rest the same.I luv the heroes and the skills they got, even if I have the feeling they're balancing is off.As I played the game a bit longer and found my favorite faction and units I kept doing the same things over and over again (not in a motivating over the time self improving to perfection way - more like a this is just the way it works best most of the times so I'm doin this) and most of the times I pawned noobs and experienced players with that.. _childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this for a while but could never get myself to pull the trigger on it, I've been glad I did this time around on sale. 25 hours in and only about 60% the way through the numerous campaigns(with dlc at least can't speak to base game) It feels like a real mash up between some early 2000's RTS power houses. The Hero units have an almost Warcraft 3 or Dawn of War feel to them in terms of combat effectiveness and being able to turn the tide on an overwhelmed front. The scale of battle and cover mechanics are right out of Company of Hero's or Dawn of War if not slightly toned down. If I have 1 gripe so far it's been how ineffective infantry units are but against what are basically titans on some maps it's kinda makes sense thematically. some of the unit mechanics are ripped right out of other games too. I hopped into a skirmish mode to check out some more of the game modes and units and low and behold the USA themed faction as StarCraft-esk carriers and the Germans a Reaver like unit as well as a towering end game unit that feels akin to a colossi yet over all manage to play like the Imperial guard in DoW 1 and 2 with Death Guard mortars and a giant Steampunk AT-AT as their heavy hero unit... The Russians feel damn near like 40k Orks with heavy jump pack melee units, flame spewing mechs and massive indirect rocket barrages. Like I said this game feels like it took bits and pieces from some of the best RTS games ever made and tried to roll it up into something new that's really been fun so far! The lack of Workshop support is concerning as some of the maps feel like complete reskins of maps I've played for decades in the DoW series and I'd love so see more battle scaling something akin to the Apoc mods for DoW as well as more control over AI setup in skirmish games. There is a lot of inbuilt retooling for missions it looked like. You can change factions and all sorts of stuff in the in the pregame so for the creative there is plenty of replay-ability built into the single player experience. Overall very happy and that's rare for me with games these days. Oh and NO MICRO TRANSACTIONS ANYWHERE!!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this based on the campaign only. I would like to like this game: the concept is very cool and dieselpunk setting is interesting. But there's a bit too many problems to recommend it. The infantry units are basically identical between factions and while the mechs are interesting and different, they are very slow, cumbersome and clunky. This does fit the setting, but it's not very fun trying to maneuver the hulks around. Units overall move very slowly and even most infantry is very sluggish. The mechs are significantly more effective than infantry and basically you end up using them to win fights and infantry becomes almost useless. This narrows down effective strategies significantly in my mind.The story of the campaign is quite corny, but it gets the job done. Some of the missions are okay, others are boring, some irritating. Overall, the game scratches that RTS itch if you have that, but it doesn't do much else.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game.  8 hours into it and I'm just not enjoying the tediousness of the campaign.  I think I'm on mission #5 or so, and while the campaign/story is cute the gameplay itself is sub-par.I like the world of Scythe, of "1920+" and the concept of this alt-reality, but execution is lacking here.  I've decided to sell the game back after this latest (3rd?) crash.  It's rare that a game crashes on me.  This is a six month old computer and very much up to date with a hefty graphics card.There is no "rock/paper/scissors" weapons vs. armor concept here, or at least not that I can visually see.  Defensive buildings do not really work.  There's no balance.  Abilities take ages to recharge (grenades in particular).  Mechs destroy everything, so barricades and cover really do not matter.  Medics and engineers do not know how to auto-heal.  Gun emplacements set up shop in whichever direction they are walking in rather than the player being able to select a field of fire they'd like to cover. All in all I really, really wanted to like this game, but it's been poorly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I love this game. Cool game, cool setting, cool Mechs, good unit animations, good voice acting, cool story, 6.5/10 maps, just okay 5/10 theatrical cutscenes, really bad AI, really bad non-theatrical cutscenes. Not worth $50 as of 12/1/20, But is definitely worth at least 25-40. Grab it on sale.  I have gone very back and forth on Iron harvest; I have been disappointed, it has grown on me, and now I officially can say I like it and recommend it. At first, the combat seemed dull, and it can be bland if you're not playing tactically. If you just want to have your soldiers shoot each other till they die, you can. Still, it won't be as fun as having one of your squads go in and fistfight with the other team while your other soldiers lay down suppressing fire. I also like how each faction does feel like it has a different playstyle. For example, Polania's units are very lightly armored and are suitable for mobile gameplay. Saxony's units are a mix of well-armed and mobile units. The Rusviets units are usually very heavy with a lot of firepower, but they're slow. I think the gameplay can be exciting, and I think it does need some work in the AI department and map design department. I’d wait for a sale, or a few months for general improvements to go through. I'm very happy that I can finally change my recommendation to positive, because this game has heart and I'm really excited to see it blossom.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Flawed, clunky and about 10 years too late to the game.You might immediately notice my low play time but frankly, as an avid RTS fan, an hour is all I needed to come to the conclusion that I am unlikely to play this game more than once or twice for reasons I will soon go into. As an RTS and huge Company of Heroes fan, It makes me sad to thumbs down this game as I can see a lot of work went into making it (especially the campaign) but the reality is that game-play wise, it just doesn't hold up against the almost 10 year-old competition. It's difficult not to compare this game to Company of Heroes as it clearly took a lot from it in the way of game play yet everything it copies is just not done as well which makes it end up playing like an unpolished"rough-around-the-edges" version of it. Graphics wise, its just okay... frankly not pretty enough for such a hyped and well known 2020 video game release, but my biggest critisism comes in the way of the awful mix of terrible AI, pathfinding, flawed cover system and laughably short weapons range. My riflemen won't shoot until they are literally 4 meters away from the enemy which also seems to cause the enemy infantry to constantly storm my cover and start shooting my troops from the other side of the same wall as them which ends up just looking and playing ridiculous.  In reality they would obviously be killed instantly which brings me to my next point ->The game could use a lot more realism. Yes, it might be set in a fictional, alternative history universe but that doesn't mean it cannot be realistic. Would love to have seen better weapons range and weopons damage physics with fully destructable environments worthy of a 2020 RTS. Instead it feels very boring and dated which brings me to my final point ->There is absolutely no innovation what-so-ever. I realise this game is trying to revive an old classic genre but to release a game of what is now obviously also a tired genre, the game needs at least a little bit of game play and/or graphical innovation if they have any hopes of attracting audiences outside of the nostalgic oldschool Millennial and Gen Z RTS lovers. Ultimately, this game has reminded me why the RTS genre died out to begin with - because the games were largely all carbon copies of one-and-other that started to loose fun factor and innovation after Company of Heroes 1. This game had huge potential but in the end, as a self confessed RTS lover, this game was released about 10 years too late and as such, is sadly a disappointment. I hope the developers continue to improve it and maybe one day I will return to it, but for now, this one is shelved for at least a year after only a couple hours playtime. The Good-Interesting alternate history setting-Music is very nice-Story/Some competent voice actingThe Bad-Unpolished and dated gameplay-Flawed and buggy pathfinding/cover system-Boring map design and very limited selection of skirmish maps.-Some dated graphics-Random bugs-Inferior to decade old competition-Infuriatingly short weapons ranges -Bad AIOverall score 6.5 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start by mentioning I was rudely interrupted after finishing a mission by a pop up screen in game telling me "Hey if you liked the game, post a review, we need the free advertising!"Dear developers, be careful what you wish for. Because I'm a mischievous imp, and when you ask me to give my opinion, you can be bloody damn sure I'm going to give it.Like a lot of people have mentioned, Iron Harvest takes a relatively interesting setting which could have made the people engrossed by it, and turned it into a gameplay mess. It tries very very hard to be a company of heroes clone, but it fails to understand a lot of the core ideas and design choices made by Relic for Company of Heroes. RTS have a long history. And over time they evolved into certain directions for very good reasons. If you take recent RTS, or even more ancient ones such as Supreme Commander which keeps a very high place in people's heart, you see something quite important. The first pitfall such games avoid, is the tendency of RTS of old such as command&conquer or even Dune 2, to have the high end units such an upgrade over regular infantry that it's absolutely pointless to produce said infantry past a certain point. This was fixed in Red Alert 2, Starcraft 1 and 2, and Company of Heroes where units either have some particular skills/modes that make them valuable, or the capacity with the right positionning and equipement for infantry to take down armored units. Iron Harvest ignores this evolution and jump with both feet right in the pitfall by having the mechs being infantry wreckers, even when said infantry is supposed to take them down, and even when they are supposed to be anti-mechs themselves. The gun emplacements feel weak againt mechs. The anti tank infantry feels weak against mechs and way too squishy while being shredded by explosions. The game has a system of cover, but it doesn't seem to understand that infantry NEEDS to be able to pack up behind one, otherwise they will never have enough room for cover in a lot of situations. It leads to infantry models being out in the open and exposed when a cover isn't large enough for a whole squad. When you have 3 squads moving together, expect 2 of them to be out in the open because they can't take cover due to lack of room. It leads to further micro as you scramble to put every squad behind a cover. Said micro is further enhanced by a game which has a lot of difficulty grouping units by type, especially when they have skill to use, and kills ergonomy.As such, most of the missions feels like they were designed for units which worked way differently than the way they work in the game. Gun emplacements you need to go through without a possibility to flank them. Said flanking not working well enough. Absolutely idiotic and hard conditions to get the platinum medals which are neither fun nor interesting. For a RTS which has base building and unit production, a lot of missions have only predeployed units and no or little base building, focusing on heroes units... Your flexibility is as such very limited. Said missions rely a lot of foreknowledge to succeed in them. A grand total of 7 missions by campaign. This is very weak when compared to other RTS. Even more so when you consider some of them are quite short, or heroes focused, the long ones being long due to annoying gimmicks instead of fun(Escort missions, defense phases you can't skip with a poor terrain to setup defenses...). I will give the devs credits for making coop a possibility... But said coop is also poorly done, and you just are two people controlling the same units. Expect to have problems when one player give orders to some units, and the other decides he needs one of those units to do something else. A proper way to make coop would have been 2 players with 2 different bases or failing that, sets of units with different roles in the mission. Dawn of War 2 did that relatively well. Red Alert 3 did that even better. Of course that would have meant maybe to have different versions of the same missions for coop... But why not? Either you put effort and energy into your game, or you don't. And it's not a matter of finding excuses like "we are small indie devs" or "we don't have enough budget". The reality is the market. And when you have games which give better things than the one you're making, you need to match or surpass them, or lower your price. Players have no reasons to play mediocre games when good ones exist.Could the game be better? Certainly. A coherent balancing and quality of life additions would go a very long way. But it's not easy, and it takes time. Company of Heroes 2 is still trying to balance itself, and it's still not balanced properly even now. At some point it was even very much unbalanced. And let's not forget in many cases, balance changes made for multiplayer ruined key elements of the campaigns, making some missions quite a hassle to complete. And even this balancing won't save the terrible missions as they are right now. And for me, the campaigns are the main draw, as I don't care for competitive multiplayer. From what I heard, things such as early rushes exist at the moment, which is never a good sign.Don't claim you are the new sensation of RTS when you obviously don't have the skills and know-how to make such a game, because there will always be people waiting for you to eat your words if you brag. Just because you have an hairy arse doesn't mean you're a bear.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: The graphics are spectacularSounds are spot on and provide immersion to the war experienceUnits are unique(ish) The ability to set up ambushes and hide behind cover provides that extra thumbs up for an RTS gameThe Bad and Ugly: You are heavily restricted on how many units you can create. And multiplayer "skirmish" maps are extremely small in size. This is supposed to take place in an alternate history after world war one ... you know... that war where millions of people died? Yet you are capped to having a small number of units at any given time... you can't set up massive fortifications and defensive lines with pillboxes ....  in fact the barbed wire and sandbag fortifications are absolutely useless since you can win 99.9% of all maps by spamming a whole bunch of mechs and steamrolling an enemy.... Because of this the game feels "empty" and unfulfilled ... i was hoping to have several hundred riflemen and machinegunners entrenched in defensive fortifications with pillboxes and artillary / mortars... instead i got like 3 four man squads of riflemen and some mechs to go harass the enemy....Company needs to massively increase the size of unit caps and at LEAST tripple the size of playable maps for this to become a good game... otherwise it is a hollow and empty experience

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Iron Harvest is the best RTS game I've ever played in 4 decades of gaming.I've been a fan of RTS games for decades. Iron Harvest lured me back in with the promise of a fresh take. It has not disappointed! Beyond the original concepts like dieselpunk mechs in an alternative timeline, what sets Iron Harvest apart from others in the genre is the storyline and character development, which is on par with (if not superior to) Blizzard titles. It's about more than building units and defeating the enemy. As early as the tutorial, you care about the characters and their cause. The smooth transitions from one campaign to the next always manage to keep you fighting for the "good guys", maintaining the feeling that the missions are important for the characters and their cause. All of this is complemented with a majestic soundtrack and quality native voice acting creating rich depth of gameplay. And once you complete all of the campaigns, you have World Map mode (turn-based land grab with a board game feel), Skirmish mode, and of course Multiplayer. It's the game that keeps giving!Iron Harvest is one of the most well-done games I've ever played. If you enjoy RTS, this title is a must-own. I also highly recommend the Operation Freedom DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest is a great game. I don't have much experience with RTS games, but found that the game was easy to learn, but way harder to master. The campaign is for the most part very well made, it slowly introduces you to different mechanics in a way that doesn't overwhelm you. For most casual players, the campaign will do just fine, but the multiplayer modes are great fun. It is an expensive game, but it is absolutely worth it, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest my first impressions on this game weren't that great.  The campaign like others have stated, starts out incredibly slow.  Spending like 15 minutes to teach you the basics like how to move a camera, that took me all of about 10 seconds to figure out on my own.  If you've played company of heroes you really dont need the tutorial stages at all.  Not to mention I personally found the main character you play as incredibly annoying, whiny, obnoxious, and preachy.  Even at the beginning where you can tell the story wants you to feel sorry for her, I kept thinking to myself "well no duh you dummy, the boys said they didnt want to play with you but you demanded they let you and then proceded to attack them from behind their backs, of course they are gonna gain up on you and throw snowballs back!"  First she whines and cries about how the boys dont want to play with her, then she whines and cries when they do play with her that the snowballs hurt.  Just annoying as all hell.  Even when she grows up she is pretty annoying.     So why am I rating it positively? because if you can put ear plugs in your ears for the terrible voice acting and obnoxious main character, You will find an incredibly rewarding gameplay loop.  Fully destructible environments, Tons of cool mechs and infantry units to play with, beautiful graphics.   When things speed up it gets fun, the setting of this game is just so unique and badass.  Watching hulking AT AT style mechs march through a clean victorian city demolishing buildings with massive infantry skirmishes on the ground, so freaking cool.  The game definitely needs more content, the amount of skirmish maps that come with the base game is downright criminal for such a fun game.  Would love to see more environments to do battle in.   Open farms, war torn cities, desert locations, mountainous regions, Military bases, forests.  This universe is so ripe with style,  I crave to see more of it and destroy it with giant robots.  Buy on a sale and you are sure to like it, as long as you can get past the 30 minute intro.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest... a game that claims to be made with the spirit of of old RTS games in mind. Nearly every review you'll see will talk about how great it is. Entire articles written on how its a breath of fresh air in the gas chamber of modern strategy games. However, to be blunt, it is none of these things. The game itself sits upon an amazing choice of setting and the aesthetic choices that the development team made has is simply outstanding. The game runs on max settings on a low end PC and has no performance issues as well, all whilst still being an absolutely beautiful experience. That, sadly, is where the list of true positives for the game end.The gameplay itself is akin to that of any proper RTS, showing clear inspiration from titles such as Company of Heroes and Halo Wars, falling directly on its face in execution. Yes, I know. "How the hell does that work?" I hear you ask. Well simply put it lacks any fleshed out base building mechanics. Unlike the aforementioned titles, who boasted quite the ability of variety, there is simply no base building at all. Outside of the campaign, the every match starts with your barracks and workshop prebuilt. The only "base building" there seems to be is clicking on the building, sliding your cursor to the bottom right corner, and clicking the upgrade button. After about 10 whole whopping seconds you are granted the ability to create a handful of meh units whose apparent niche uses are completely undermined by less expensive, far more effective units that you could've built anyway before you wasted your resources. Which is a great segway into the next topic.The mechs. Despite seeming to be what the entire game is based around, they fall short in actual viability. There is not a single thing the mechs do, that a cheaper, faster,(and sometimes more healthy) infantry unit can't do. They are entirely there to look pretty. They move at paces a blind elderly snail would find leisurely and they're damage output doesn't feel at all like it matches the beefiness on display. I'm talking a giant autocannon laying into unprotected infantry for two whole minutes and the infantry just take it because of how the hit point system works(if they're even hit in the first place). And my god, the hit point system. Quite possibly one of the worst things ever introduced to strategy games. Nothing makes combat feel so smooth and impactful as watching two units shoot at eachother for minutes on end until one bursts into flames or has a heart attack and dies. If a bang bang the size of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ truck hits you, I'm sorry, you're dead as ♥♥♥♥. I don't care how much "Veterancy" you have. Anyways, after some light reading, I'm sure they were valuable at some point, but just like all other modern RTS games, the devs had to "balance" things for online play. Thus, leading into my greatest issue.What was so wrong with the pace of Company of Heroes, or Dawn of War, or Command and Conquer. Why in the everloving hell did autists with ADHD and no social life have to steal the RTS genre. Every RTS now, and by extension every multiplayer compatible game, has this air around it. You know what I mean. The air of  competitive gaming. Where everything has to be balanced around it being played in tournaments around the world for billion dollar jackpot prizes. Even though it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ won't. Min maxers, meta gamers, and the like flock to these games because they live for intense competition. Casual gaming is dead. Killed by greed and exploitation. If you want to play a game thats competitive or make one thats competitive then be my guest. But RTS games forged an identity as being a solid choice for avid single players. They had enjoyable campaigns and even better offline skirmish modes where the AI only cheated if you really wanted them to. But now AI cheating is just blatant and hidden behind "difficulty". The only balancing attention games get is for the online base. And good luck trying to play online as a first timer. You'll get your ♥♥♥♥ mixed like they stuck a kitchenaid up there. All in all, my verdict is such: If you enjoy older RTS as a singleplayer experience, this isn't for you. If you're an autistic loner with ADHD who can multitask like a supercomputer, then despite its flaws, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ made for you bro. I truly mean that with the utmost sincerity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great campaign mode! The story is well-written and appropriately over-the-top. This is an RTS game, but most maps in the campaign will have several objective stages to go through before you get to the "kill everything" stage (and sometimes you don't even get a "kill everything" stage). And you can really make mistakes here. If you don't plan carefully, you'll probably have to restart the level.I could see someone criticizing the game for throwing new mechanics at you a little too quickly on certain maps, but I personally enjoyed it. It isn't your typical mindless RTS, where you do the same thing over and over again. The setting is also the same setting used in the board game, Scythe! You get a chance to learn a lot more about the different nations in that game.

_childDocuments_.review: If I was to be succinct, this is Company of Heroes in a world inspired by Scythe and Bioshock.It's fine for what it is. It is not as tuned or enjoyable as CoH2, but when compared to the circus that CoH3 is, the gap suddenly becomes much more narrow. _childDocuments_.review: *EDIT: came back to give it a chance and played some multiplayer. Matchmaking still took too long and I experienced an extremely toxic community. Time to abandon IH.______Dear devs, I really tried to love your game, but...After four whole weeks since realese, I'm still massively disappointed by Iron Harvest.Campaign:- Even tough much advertised, the campaign was quite underwhelming for me- I didn't like this whole 'tesla stuff' at all- Many missions just where boring and/or not fun to play- Rather annoying characters - You won't get rewards for some missions (incl. secondary objectives) so you can't finish the campaign 'on paper' - Predictable story, rather unexciting- The so called 'coop-campaign' is an utter joke. Just the regular singleplayer campaign but you share the units with a friend. Note that you can only control one unit in some missions!Gameplay:- Very poor cover system and questionable pathfinding- The models behaviour is quite dumb and memesy, looks rather bad aswell - Lackluster combat- All modles from a squad look and move exactly the same (it's 2020!) which I think is terrible- The AI seems not to work at all in skirmish, even on insane difficulty it rarely builds something and puts up a fight- Some of the bigger Mechs really do not feel and play as the weapons of mass destruction they are ment to be- Base building is as minimalistic as it can be- Very very few maps! And all of them are mirrowed so they lack diversity in themselves aswell- The factions infrantry and weapon systems are exactly the same for the most part (lack of diversty again)- The gameplay just doesn't feel good and takes most of the setting's immersion General stuff:- Why can't we just invite friends in a lobby to play online against other people with them? Isn't this part of RTS? so frustrating...- You can't 'ping' on the map for your teammates (should be standard)- It doesn't feel like a deadly World War- The heroe's animals make the game feel even more childish and out of place- Partly dumb unit modles, e.g.: every saxonian infantryman wears sunglasses (wtf) and rusviet pioneers seem to be 70+ years old- Poor matchmaking, takes very longI think it's a real pity that the game is the way it is but sadly Iron Harvest makes it more than hard for me to like it. Would refund if I still could

_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. The concept is cool and the skeleton of a good game is there, but it fails on too many points. This game feels very much like company of heroes, but worse in many categories.I think probably my biggest complaint is how slow everything in the game moves. It's boring how long it takes my units to move across the map or retreat. There's a lot of time in this game when all I can do is watch my units walk from point A to point B. That slowness leads to many units feeling unresponsive. Everything moves slowly and this means they react slowly as well. Unit pathing isn't bad but it's not good, so you'll need to reposition and redirect units a lot, but with how slow they move and react, it becomes a tedious and frustrating task. This last thing is more of a gripe than a real complaint, but the story is very bad. Characters are strange knock-offs of real life historical figures of the time, and the actual story is a tired "evil organization pulling all the strings" situation.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mostly RTS in WC2/WC3/SC/SC2 with all expansions.  The key commands are frustrating to get used to as I want to deselect a unit and continue to press the ESC key which brings up the main in-game menu.  Currently on Walker Ace campaign and I am quite annoyed by the allowed pathing.  Literally made my unit go into retreat mode and crossed paths with the AI enemies.  The XP buildup is annoying and keeping things in check is way more cumbersome than to rely on a hero unit alone. Tech is also BS because you need your engineers leveled up to make more static defenses.  I loved the demo but the full game play isn't appeasing and thankfully I only paid for the deal at $15.(50% off)UpdateThere are some bugs in the campaign and I have yet to play the skirmish.When an enemy squad die, there is usually 1 unit in that squad that is still alive but technically bugged out on the field.  Another is in the DLC when the units just froze up and wouldn't accept commands after killing a mech in a tiny pathway.  Game was still working but menus wouldn't respond or show up anymore thus a complete game shutdown.

_childDocuments_.review: To shorten things up in the beginning:The game is absolutely worth a buy (especially during a sale) for any RTS fan out there. A Solid 70/100It even has Tesla Coils, atleast in a mission ;)Pros:- The Game has a very good story/campaigns for a RTS game, like we had back when C&C/SC2 was at it's peak.Tempest Rising will be pretty similar, atleast i hope- Alot of singleplayer content for a fair price, decently long campaign, took me about 20 hours for the main campaign without any DLC on normal and i've been playing RTSs since the late 90s and probably every major and minor titles out there. After the campaign you still have Skirmish matches with alot of maps (after all the updates the game received) and the newly Total War/Dawn of War styled Global Map, which the devs added for free!- Graphics are beautiful, effects are flashy and look great, the destruction of buildings is a nice addition, especially if you walk a giant mech through a building and it collapses piece by piece (it even rivals Company of Heroes 3 Building destruction!), but it has it's flaws (like mechs clipping into the building until it collapses) as does the CoH 3 destruction.- Sound is meaty, music is fitting, nothing outstanding-1920+ setting is just awesome and has so much potential, are there even other games in this universe?All in all a good, HOWEVER, the game has issues.Cons:- Gameplay, this is probably the biggest weakness of the game. Gameplay is very shallow and lacks depth, variation and balance.The factions are too similar, infantry is a bit too weak. Mobile machine guns and AT guns are too sluggish etc.Barely any basebuilding and therefore Lack of defensive/tactical options.Because the gameplay is lacking so much the game doesn't have a big MP community (i myself don't care about MP in RTS games, i enjoy campaigns and skirmish/coop matches against bots)Devs wanted to "copy" Company of Heroes however, a different apporach would have been better for the settings, bigger less micro intensive battles like, Men of War/Dawn of War 1/C&C/Supreme Commander style of gameplay- Performance, oh boy this is another major disadvantage the game has. Yes it looks great but for the graphics and unit count you get, the performance is abysmal. If alot is going on, you get sub 60fp even with a decent PC (5800X + 2070super). The big problem is, the GPU uitilization which never hits 100% yet the FPS are ♥♥♥♥♥. It is Unity after all :(- First Campaign (Polania) starts a bit weak, in terms of story and gameplay, but once you made it through you get the great second campaign (Rusviet) and the excellent third Campaign (Saxony). - Unit responsivenes, even after all the updates, still feels very clumsy and unresponsiveLike i wrote before a solid 70/100 or 7/10 :PI absolutely enjoyed the campaign and will enjoy the game for more hours for sure.Since there is so much unused potential and the 1920+ setting is vast, i desperately hope King Art will get another chance for a Iron Harvest 2 where they can fix the issues of the first game and add new stuff.King Art, PLEASE make a second Iron Harvest game, RTS players need more good games, we were suffering for too long.Next time let us cripple the mechs piece by piece like targeting their feet, to make them immobile.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a dieselpunk WW1 Company of Heroes. Wouldn't mind a bit more variety in units, although I'm not complaining. They've mixed the WW1 atmosphere with dieselpunk style very well. It seems they're not doing very new and innovative things when it comes to gameplay. Having said that, it's polished and I haven't run into any overly frustrating mechanics and bugs yet.You can choose from 4 difficulty settings, which is probably enough, imo. I haven't tried all the difficulty settings yet. Easy is really easy and medium difficulty makes for a very/fairly relaxed game. I'd imagine hard and insane will be challenging enough for experienced players to still have fun. Skirmishes can be too short, so I find myself choosing a high victory point count all the time.Rather than quick games (which can be fun, especially if you don't have much time on your hands, don't get me wrong) I'd like more defensive missions with a bit slower pace and more tactical gameplay. The population limit might prevent overcrowded battlefields, but it feels a bit underwhelming. Mechs are powerful, as they should be, but it would be nice to see more infantry crawling around to make the mechs stand out more. The artwork and clips give a much more epic view of the mechs than what is shown on the battlefield you play on.I only played the tutorial when it comes to the story, but if the rest of the missions have the same creativity, it's really promising. Learning the game mechanics by throwing snowballs and hunting a deer also serves the story, because you don't just play your first mission commanding troops in an all-out war.All in all, Iron Harvest is, in my opinion, a polished and attractive RTS with a moderate learning curve. It feels like a nice game to play now and then, when you've played another game for too long and want a break. Its style (and story) sets it apart from other RTSes, so if you need your daily/weekly dieselpunk WW1 shot, Iron Harvest is a game for you.9/10 mechs are squeaking and creaking in anticipation

_childDocuments_.review: This is an updated review. I have recently picked up the game again and still feel the problems it had last time i played. The air vehicles are imo a little bit of a let down due to lack of flavor but that's fine. However they a lot of times feel like glass. Their expensive and pack a tiny punch but can be kill very fast. Which in a game which prides resource management isn't a good investment. Plus for the air units they are slower then walking units... do i really need to elaborate? It makes that the mechs are slow. Their big and carry heavy weaponry, however air units typically are much faster. Personally the air units in this game feel like they could be destroyed by the wright brother's plane with a pistol taped on. Personally I think the Blimp is well rounded its a big heavy unit that hits hard and it makes sense its close to the ground. But, the other units are supposed to be like planes fast and hard hitting. IMO if the developers are reading this, I recommend possibly reworking air. For example allow for AA cannons to be built outside the base, but allow the air support to be fast and devastating. Air should be like a thing you call into battle time to time; like a bombing run or close air support run. This way we get to keep the engaging gameplay pre-operation eagle and we get a new management idea where we the players would have to invest into AA to prevent such attack. Allow me to paint you a picture: a choke point is completely locked down by the enemy; fortified positions, defensive mechs, lots of troops the whole nine yards if you will. When suddenly, what at first seems to be a suicide run bashes straight into the enemy distracting and buying time for an anti-mech squad to flank the defenses and destroy the AA cannons. The enemy thinks they've survived the attack as the last of the attacking troops are dealt with, when suddenly overhead a couple of Revere's can be heard soaring above. In an instant the enemies once invincible line is crippled and the player is able to an armored spearhead attack and break through the lines. Now in this proposal we continue to have engaging battles, strategic placement, and the ability to underdog (pull out a win at the last moment) Iron harvest dev's if your reading this I would love to hear your opinion, but for right now I am sad to say I cannot recommend your game.
