_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from multiplayer point of view mainly. I don't personally care about campaings in strategy games so I will not say anything about it. However I've played a couple of skirmishes against the computer and all I can say about that is that the ai in this game is extremely easy and simple even on the hardest difficulty.The game could be good and fun but in it's current state I just cannot recommend or play it. The community while being active and somewhat helpful if you ask the right questions, refuses completely to acknowledge any criticism towards the game and it's shortcomings.-Despite what some part of the community says, the game is quite literally a bare bone version of Company of Heroes. It has all the same mechanics, but just WAY less of them. For example there are currently only two different buildings that can be upgraded once and the hq.-There is currently three factions. They are identical to each others in the way how every unit is built, however the "small" differences between the factions units is what makes this game very unbalanced. Polanian (offensive faction) units are the powerful meta while Saxony (defensive faction) is pretty much worthless in the hands of equally skilled players. This leads to very little choice on what and how you should play.-The matches are too short, usually games last from 5 to 15 minutes at most. By the time you can afford to start producing your most expensive units, either your team is already rushing the enemy hq or the other way around and at that point the match is already decided. There is no way to recover if you've lost most of your units and the enemy is destroying your base.-On some maps the game is decided in the first 30 SECONDS, not even exaggerating. The maps feature weapon caches you can give your units and whoever gets their hands to these caches first, wins the game. The worst case being 2vs2 map called Crash Site. After getting the weapon caches you have the upper hand in the early game which allows you to also capture all of the resources, so the other team will get no resources and the already in the lead being one will start snowballing towards victory right away. There are not many maps in the game so you are bound to get the bad maps.-The game has many bugs, some smaller and some bigger. I will not list these since not all of them are game breaking and the developers listen to the community in some capacity on what should be fixed. The biggest annoyance to me however was the reverse command (hold C by default and click where to move unit) on mechs. First of all, the game does not list the command in the command toolbar for whatever reason, which makes most players oblivious that such an important thing even exists. Not only that but the reversing itself is buggy. Sometimes the mechs won't actually reverse despite the game even showing you are issuing said command, but will just turn around and walk normally to the chosen position. This can and will cost you valuable mechs because they turn their weak backs towards the enemy while moving and get destroyed.TL;DR:The game just isn't worth it in it's current state and I don't see it getting much better in the near future due to a small developer team and a backwards ass cult following of the game. I do hope to see the game and meta in a better state sometime and return to this otherwise very interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I want to love this game. I really do. You've got mechs with big dumb guns, you've got a cover system for infantry (it needs polish but it's there), and you've got some downright pretty maps. The game is stifled by a lack of variety, however. Sure, there are differences between the three factions you can play, but at the core of it all, they're the same unit with a different coat of paint. You build just two simple buildings back at HQ, which upgrade into an "advanced" form of itself, a barracks and a vehicle production facility and there is literally zero upgrading to customize your infantry/mechs. Infantry are versatile, able to swap weapons with that of their defeated adversary (for a limited time before the equipment despawns) should the need suit them, but mechs are doomed to be railroaded in their purpose. The flagship scout mech will always shoot that same big rifle and, because of this, the game suffers. I often found myself looking for units with more abilities, as well. Heroes have a couple at their disposal, some active or passive, but basic infantry have a simple "rally" ability and maybe a role-specific "throw the grenade" type ability.When attacked by mechs, I wanted my infantry to throw smokes or something to obscure vision, temporarily disable a mech by hitting it with an EMP, or try to cripple it with a well-placed shot to the backside.. but these options are just unavailable so I often find my infantry retreating once the armor arrives. I will say that AT fire feels super satisfying. Blasting the mechs with anything cannon related is pretty and feels like it HURTS.  Tl;dr - This game is the solid groundwork for something, but it feels unfinished. I like mechs but I also like options. The unit variety needs expanding and units need upgrades/more abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent presentation but jank is just terrible to handle. Takes away from enjoying it too much. Missclicks, double clicks for single action waiting for it to eventually decide to respond, bad pathing, freezing bug. -Edit after completing campaign.I still finished it, but after playing Polonia on hard, last mission took me 4 hours straight with 4 retries. A 4 hour mission, apparently I needed it. After switching to easy I noticed how the game started running better. Because of the jank, you don't need to use your abilities as well and the game runs better. Basically, the issue is complete lack of focus on gameplay. It's just bad, there's potential there, but it's just not there. Minimal effort done on gameplay or balancing. The general idea is that infantry is quick, captures resources and is versatile, mechs are very slow and lumbering and do not fit through certain paths. It's great, I love watching when mech that is larger than a building crashes through it. Beautiful. However, what you need is that those mechs are centerpiece of battle - they're slow, but extremely heavy hitting should focus your effort around them, where mechs push the line, while infantry supports them, fights other infantry, and try to provide edge for your mechs to take down enemy. It's just not that. The mechs are powerful enough only in groups, but they're still squishy and don't have the weight. You just spam certain mechs and rush the enemy, overwhelming their build. Just not satisfying. Crewed weapons are pointless, only usable for base defence, mechs aren't powerful enough and are too cheap, infantry only builds run into hard counters - machine gun and then just get wiped out, meaning you need to have mechs to take out hard counters, and you need alot of them, so you might as well run mech only build, with infantry for capture only. The mission design is infuriating. Way too many no-base missions, which are tedious, because there's no interesting abilities to work with and they recharge at snail pace. Base missions are also bad, because sometimes you think you're fighting an opponent, but no it's just scripted spawns, which make your strategy completely irrelevant, just rush through, to the sometimes vague objectives and push on. Oh and the jank, is just tedious to deal with. There's no place for tactical game. The gameplay, clearly was not a priority. For instance, Usonia brought new type of units - airships, which are just mechs, but slower and can move through terrain. OK, maybe interesting. But the problem is, that every single Usonia mission has anti-air turrets, meaning your new type of unit is utterly useless. It's much more efficient to run infantry and light mech build to rush through. Oh and armor types - you have 4 armors - unarmored, light, medium and heavy. Weapon penetration is corresponding. You can still penetrate medium armor with unarmored weapons, but it's very hard. OK, there's potential here. Problem is, later heroes get medium-heavy weapons, which makes them significantly more efficient than any mech of any size, because armor penetration means that if you do 150 dmg against infantry you do 150 dmg against a mech, making infantry sometimes harder to kill than a mech. It's just unbalanced and poorly thought through gameplay. Clearly art department takes the priority and I think they're convinced their story is good, which it isn't. It starts promising, but very soon becomes standard vague conspiracy filled with cameo cliches. Nikola Tesla is in this, that should tell you level of storytelling. The American campaign is frankly insulting in it's formulaism and banality. Just boring. So much potential, great art, so wasted. Still gonna try world map and some missions before quitting. --after trying world map and a few skirmishing--The same issue with scripted events and forces just ruined fun in world map. It doesn't clearly explain or show what does reinforcing region mean, you get random and bewildering starting options and the army you get when you play, is just random. Sometimes you get partial infantry, reinforcements are whatever, sometimes you get partial mech support. The worst part was when I was assaulting Polish capital. There's a scripted mech unit inside a  camp you had to take out. I did, then pushed forward the line and a mech unit (pretty powerful) spawned right behind me. I had to build 5 bunkers surrounding their spawn point to deal with them because they respawned pretty regularly. This is just insulting design and those scripted spawns take away from enjoying the game, because you can't plan, it's just go all the time, which gets boring. As a comparison to say, Rise of Nations - no contest. Much better map game, much better RTS, still the only ones, that managed to make aircraft feel like aircraft. Tried multiplayer skirmishing, it's fine. I'm sure if I tried long enough I'd find some balancing issues, but at least there's no scripted spawning, so when you get snowballed, it's fair. There's a few creative modes and there's real creativity in this game, just all wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of the day Iron Harvest is a repetitive RTS with an unimaginative story that becomes pretty boring after you're halfway through the campaign. Iron Harvest has a great setting, steampunk post WW1 in Europe and in Arabia. The story is okay at best, mashing up real world events with conspiracy theorist fantasies (the illuminati led by Rasputin and whatnot) and the big steampunk trope which obviously is Nikola Tesla making machines and guns that go ZAAAPPPPPP.And no you cant play with these inventions as there is no Tesla faction in the game nor can you recruit these units at any point. Gameplay wise all missions end up feeling the same, the factions hardly differentiate from each other except for a unit or two and the unique hero.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Definetly not worth the 50 bucks. Especially if you plan to play this game with friends, don't bother, there is not nearly enough content to play with your friends.Pros: -artstyle of the units is pretty nice, same goes for most enviroments-great unit variety.cons: -advertised co-op campaign is not in the game-unit variety does not feel impactfull, it feels like whoever sits in cover wins when it comes to infantry-only 6! pvp/comp stomp maps in total, 3 maps for 2Players, 2 for 4 Players and 1 single map for 6 Players.-Voiceacting is mediocre and the accents are hilariously clichee.-static guns like mortars and mg's don't autoturn to attack enemy troops, which makes mortars especially clonky to use, since both mg's and mortars are slow. and with slow, i mean, so slow that even mechs look fast next to them.-while the steam page claims that this game has controller support, don't try it, the controller support is not there All in all, it feels not even remotely complete for a 1.0 full release, its not worth the 50 bucks, and its steam page includes features that are not in the game yet, and is thus false advertisment
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on discount at 30$.The story seems worth it. The campaign does not play like utter morbid crud.Challenges are not co-op - you should note that, as I was interest in last stand and the such with my friends.The multiplayer is absolutely ungodly terrible. I don't think they could make it worst if they tried. Everything with it is wrong. Everything is too slow or too fast or not deadly enough and it is the most infuriating thing I have dealt with in a multiplayer game in years.Strongly no recommend for anything but story.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. It definitely has elements similar to Starcraft 2 with the Hero focus. I'm not a competitive gamer. I'm glad I bought this and I am likely going to buy some DLC if I can catch them on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: So it is a company of heroes clone without the AAA polish, not something I would hate outright but they have made some wierd design choices. You cannot use a normal control group to bind your structures, coming from any rts whatsoever makes this choice a bit puzzling. Victory points as in Company of heroes 2/ DOW are kinda unescecary, especially considering how fast they tick down. When you win a couple of fights early, that snowballs into the win. The input lag in the game is an entire second, its really annoying. Buildings actually dont help your troops more than regular cover, turning them into death traps for your infantry. IH has a reserve system, essentially a single recruitable batch of units you pick at the start of the game. You get a points quota and it is the only way you can produce a hero, making it more or less a must have for every game. This was a mistake as it is essentially like a production boom in every other game except you dont have to tech as much, thus investing much less. Lets not get into the HORRIBLE and i mean absolutely terrible balancing by the team essentially curbing any build other than what the dev wants the meta to be. The nerfs are so bad that I am surprised that a functional adult could actually approve something like this for a patch.In short, they had something good in spite of its flaws, but they decided to curb stomp it. NO FUN ALLOWED. Strategy is forbidden, you are now forced into a rock paper scissors with horribly slow moving mechs......I regret kickstarting this, It is genuinely sad to see the devs ruining their own product.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say other than WHAT A GAME! These devs clearly stated what they wanted to achieve, how they wanted to do it, and when they wanted to get it done. The fact that these devs not only did all of the above, but also delivered an amazing game and solid addition to the RTS genre is simply AWESOME! This game combines steam punk theme with WWI and I have to say that it delivers in every way possible. Its Company of Heroes meets Steampunk meets WWI and I love it.The game has multiple skirmish modes against both players and AI, multiple factions to choose from with highly diverse units for each, and a campaign! I was a backer and I have enjoyed seeing the progress that this game and its devs have completed.

_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Yay:+ Cool settings and great graphics+ Destructible buildings+ Familiar UI for regular RTS playersNay:- Just Company of Heroes 2 with mechs instead of tanks - nothing new.- The AI will randomly start shooting buildings until they blow up (which takes a while with submachine guns lol)- Enemy just spams mechs after a certain point, and some mechs are not well balanced (in both directions: some have no advantages and are worse than a squad a grenadiers, and others are just ridiculously powerful and have sniper like range.)All-in-all, it doesn't add enough to the RTS world to be worth $50, so I will not be keeping it. _childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Great RTS game with a decent story with some unique RTS traits. I really enjoyed the repair/heal tactic. I normally built a squad of 1 anti infantry mech, 1 long range and 1 anti armor mech with 2 backup engineer squads. This results in a slow grind through the levels but satisfying when all the units are veteran and are dominating with the correct actioning of reverse moves to cause traps. The only problem I have with this game is the units are a more or less the same across all factions which was a little disappointing. Especially the infantry, which are the exact same apart from one forgettable mech infantry unit for two factions. This results in the same tactics across all the factions more or less. Would of also liked a Fenris or Tesla campaign as part of the main play through. Apart from the above this is a great game and would highly recommend. I would love to see this evolving further through the lead up to WW2.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having a few flaws, Iron Harvest is about the closest thing to a quality RTS since C&C Generals - which is saying something. I love the game, personally. Each faction feels mostly balanced without being cookie cutter at all. Of course the game needs more balancing and polish, but if the game is supported for say, another year -- and all signs seem to indicate such -- this title will be a banger. Actually it already is one; it'll just keep getting better. I'm hoping it eventually crosses the threshold from "good" to "one of the all-time greats" and if the game continues on its current trajectory I think it will. Call me a believer. You'll have to see for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game in 2019, so I joined a bit late. The game was rushed, I'd argue the time they needed to finish the game would've been another year, possibly two after the actual release date. I was there for the alpha, beta test, and release date. I've since scrapped my last review as I feel it praised the game too much. The developers seem to be good, hard working people but unfortunately their business practices aren't the sort I'd recommend to people.With that said what was ruined?, Combat in the game is a good start. During the alpha test you could expect to see late game "Super Units" like the Kaiser or Tur mechs if you rushed building a mech factory and saved the resources. A high risk, high reward bit of a game play for the turtle type players like myself. Imagine using only experimental units and using the bare minimum tech 1-3 units in Supreme Commander. They have since the beta ruined that method of game play by forcing you to build both a barracks building, and a mech factory, then you'd upgrade both of them all of which costs resources *building the buildings, then upgrading both require resources* , then you can save up a lot of resources to pay for a single super unit... in other words you most likely will not see super units used in multiplayer games as they're inefficient and impractical to use. I should mention infantry are cheaper, faster, and have far more utility than mechs anyways so it's almost like the point of the game (the mechs) have been invalidated.In short I am displeased with the game, it's very disappointing, and I have not even received my backer rewards (the physical items such as a mech figurine among other trinkets) , which were >promised< to be given the day of the release of the game. I understand that the lunacy revolving around the pandemic is a fine excuse for the delay, but excuses aren't worth much to me or any of the other >very patient might I add< backers who paid forward and have subsequently been left out, I do however know the worth of the items I >paid< for which I do not have on the day they were promised, $120 U.S.D.With all of that in mind, I would recommend you stay away from Iron Harvest unless you see it on sale for under $20 U.S.D. it'd be worth the price at that point, don't bother purchasing the Rusviet Revolution DLC, and certainly only pick up the Usonia DLC if it's under $10 U.S.D. the prices are ridiculous.Oh I should also add I've spent some time on the Discord server, mentioning how I feel a bit disgruntled about how the backers who have spent over twice the price of the current game on products they have yet to receive, ought to receive the DLC for free as a show of good faith and good PR practice, and I've been berated by an insulting moderator, I won't name but let's just say he has used some f"owl" language.To better make my point, Imagine this:You walk into a restaurant. You ask for a hamburger, some french fries and a drink.You're given the drink, and given fries that are not properly cooked. You're waiting for your hamburger, patiently for many minutes, finally you get annoyed and ask "Where is my hamburger?", at the same time, people who have just gotten into line are receiving a hamburger, fries, and an apple pie. You're told all sorts of good excuses, like "one of our employees caught the flu, and isn't feeling well." , which you sympathize with, but then you keep waiting and being told the flu caused delays. You're then told that you >might< get the burger in a little while. You wait a few more minutes, then you ask if it's ready now, they tell you now you might get it if you wait 3 times as long as you already have.You >might< get what you paid for if you wait roughly 10 times the length of time everyone else waited, and they paid for things they're getting for half the price you paid, plus a bonus.Does that seem like good business practice? Does that seem like you care about your fans / playerbase / customers?This is all a metaphor for how I was promised an assortment of physical goods, and have now waited nearly an entire calendar year for the goods I was promised, and the best they can tell me and the other backers is "Ooooh we're getting around to it!, just be patient, don't want more than what you paid for, even though you've waited an entire year for these products we >still< haven't got a shipping date for, pay no attention to the fact we promised we'd ship it all together on September 1st of >last year<".In all seriousness, anger aside, I ask anyone, any person, who reads this. What would your policy be?, People who took a risk, the people who are essentially your investors, whom you made >promises to<, have been more than patient enough, waiting for the products, would you just.. keep them waiting? With no major updates, no compensation for their time?, no attempt to keep a strong relationship with those who helped you get your feet off the ground?Sincerely, to the developer team. I want you all to know I don't hate you. I hate that you don't care about the backers or your more loyal fans.Do. Not. Buy. This. Game.

_childDocuments_.review: This games setting is great. Its refreshing to see an RTS game in 2020; however, I can not recommend this game. Although I've only done the first 3 missions of the first campaign, the game is poorly made code wise. AI pathing is extremely dumb. You can tell a unit to go there and they will literally take a direct straight line route to that spot and get stuck running into a wall. You have to babysit them to get them where you want.The enemy AI is extremely extremely dumb. I put it on the hardest mode and the AI doesn't seem to have a plan whatsoever. They come attack in wave and chase your units rather than capture the objective after defeating you.They also see their units being attacked and let them die and not support them with nearby units. (i don't know if this is campaign only or works in multiplayer but I assume its the same because of how bad the AI is)Again, the concepts of the game are great but they have to work on a lot to make this game amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, has a heap of potential, and I really wanna recommend it, but for the price, no way! $40 would be pushing it.It lacks depth and it feels really bare compared to other RTS games, the multiplayer aspect of this game gets boring really quick with not a lot to do and the lack of units that there are is very disappointing.The game is really cool and has a great concept, and I really really hope the devs bring out more stuff and make this game a bit more fulfilled, to make the $70 worth paying, I'd wait for a sale for this one, unless you're really really keen.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a beautiful game bogged down by bugs and just terrible quality of life management. My background is Starcraft, Warcraft, Command and Conquer, SC2, Total War, etc. and I really tried to give this game a fair shot and downed some hours into it. My hope is that the game is patched into greatness? But I just really haven't heard of that happening very often if ever.  Okay so ill start with negative which burned this game out for me fast. -Basically when you get a lot of the bigger mechs they will frequently not attack when you try to have them attack another mech they will instead move right next to the other mech like its going for a hug while its getting blown away. This along with other issues like this makes the game require much more micro management but you are hindered from your ability to micro manage due to its poor design or due to defects so you just end up in RTS Hell (this is explained in other points in this list below). -Units that specialize in close combat will also have a weak pistol as a secondary which is okay and cool... except for the fact that they will ALWAYS default the pistol and NEVER go into close combat unless you micro manage it and unit selection is near impossible in this game. (which is another issue I address in this list) there is no Total War equivalent to say I WANT you to only use melee or range etc you have to micro manage  it and all troops default range. -the game will randomly freeze during a mission and within the 10 hours I played this happened multiple times. id say 3 or 4 times? Thats not too bad honestly im forgiving but all the other issues plus this is just too much. - closing the game or hitting escape can take between 10 full seconds to a full minute I know that sounds like not a long time but its a damn long time and is annoying. I think there is a issue with their "junk cache system"/ pre allocated memory resources during cut scenes and pausing the game which causes the massive lag that is seen. This happens with every scene and every time you try to exit etc. -unit selection is not intuitive  and when your dealing with mechs that take 10 real time seconds to deploy that have infantry units around it if you try to pull back the infantry (and you will) your going to move that mech too by accident every time and now you have no mech for 30 seconds and you lose everything. - even on easy the game is too hard because of all the issues I cant beat it without tearing out my hair. -units AI is missing in key places it should exist. You can have a unit set to auto heal mechs or other units but the range they do this is like a half a inch. you cant have a full group of units and expect that the medics/engineers will heal everyone in they only heal people directly next to them. Worse yet trying to select a unit to heal another unit is almost impossible. The unit selection hud is terrible. I mean Epic Bad. its impossible to navigate. Trying to hot key squads to get around this issue is useless because of all the other issues you lose people constantly and need to remake them every hmmm id say 20 seconds or so. Also units engaging combat strongly depends on the units range. If their range is long they will end up roaming the map if you dont micro manage them. If its short they will stand by while their buddies a foot in front of them are getting gunned down. -The hot key for retreat and attack in melee is right next to each other and more then once I hit retreat by accident and worse yet once done I have yet to find a way to stop the retreat. (T is attack melee and R is retreat).its just a beautiful game that was made poorly thats all. I love RTS and at the core of the game I love the game but I just hate how I have to navigate the game its just impossible and unplayable for me. It might be one of the best RTS games I've played in ages but I really cant tell because I just cant play it in its current state. The good is just that its a good story, environment, and just how it looks is stunning, I love the units, the world they made everything. My best guess is a lot of the issues i am seeing are patented? so they couldn't legally make the hud and unit selection better? I dont know.. I dont know why it ended up as bad as it did. Maybe get it on sale but im not sure how much time you'll get out of it before the issues frustrate you to the point you give up on the game like I did. I will say this. For better or worse Im past the refund limit because I spent 10 hours giving the game a chance, but I dont regret it I did love giving the game a chance so take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write reviews but this game is something special, if for no other reason than the setting, dieselpunk is not something I see done a lot. While I'm not a huge fan of the COH style RTS it fits this game.Enemy AI seems a bit slow, Unit pathing can be wonky, and some features just aren't there rn, but imo the game makes up for the short comings somewhat with an awesome campaign, unique factions, and excellent visuals/art style. At $50USD I  recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of boring. Not enough units to justify. Maybe if they combined 2 of the factions or made all of the factions into 1 faction it would be worth it but bleh. _childDocuments_.review: Painfully Boring. All factions are the same. Get in during sales.I really tried to finish the campaign and ended the effort three separate occasions. As compared to CoH where the campaigns feels "alive" and varied and having to figure out what unit counters what because of diversity, expect none of that in IH. I really really tried to finish the campaign then when reaching another Saxony mission with objectives almost very similar to another earlier mission, I stopped and decided to write this review. The setting was promising with the idea of WWI but with giant mechs and warring factions based on real-life European counterparts. The lack of unit variety, the strangely janky controls of units who don't stay in cover anyways, and the "eventually everything goes melee anyways" strategies, makes Iron Harvest unfortunately my first not recommended game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: I had a go on the free weekend. This kind of RTS isn't my usual style, but I did enjoy the strong narrative direction where the campaign missions bring fresh scenarios and introduce you to the different units and concepts. Units feel slow yet squishy when countered so bad moves are punished hard. I had a bad cold and it was taking me a long time to learn how to play properly. It's a good game. Gets compared to Company of Heroes a lot and that really is it's closest comparison, but it's doing its own thing as well. These aren't my favourite style of RTS though, so I wouldn't want to jump into this one on multiplayer etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Boring!!!!!!!I'm going to have to edit my one word review because of the message i received after posting.Nethairlinn  [developer] Posted: Jan 17 @ 12:09pmHey Royce,It's of course difficult to elaborate on a feeling like "boring", I can understand that, but could you try anyway, please?Maybe you can determine what exactly you're missing to make Iron Harvest more exciting for you.Is it too easy? Doesn't the theme or story grab you?The devs are constantly working to improve the game and also to bring new content, so detailed feedback helps immensely.Thanks a lot :)I was pleasantly surprised to see a title where devs actually care about their game and improving on it so here goes.Iron Harvest is a very cool concept.  An alternate timeline based around the Great War era with steam punk elements.  The graphics are very good, the game mechanics are adequate, but the feel of the game seems more like whack a mole to me than an actual strategy game.  You spend your time building troops, capturing resources on the map, and attacking/defending until you control the map.  I can think of at least a dozen titles built around the same concept.  There isn't really anything to set Iron Harvest apart from any of those titles beyond the overall concept, and that isn't enough to carry it.I have to admit I only gave a few hours, and that only in campaign mode, but it was enough for me to determine that I didn't want to spend any more time.  The story line is dry, and the wash, rinse, repeat, game play that I saw coming just didn't interest me.If you like that sort of game then this is a title you would probably enjoy.  As it is I may give it another go at some point just to see what the devs have done.  I would give a big thumbs up just for them.  I'll have to stick with the thumbs down for the game though.  This one just didn't do anything for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully fun Diesel punk alternate history!  It has taken me a bit to get the hang of the game play, and some of the unit behavior still annoys me.  But it's beautifully done and a pleasure to watch my little mechs stomping around and destroying the buildings around them.  The more I play the more I see the units are rather well thought out and balanced.  Is it dramatically different from other games like this I have played?  Not really, but it's certainly better looking!  It has been a lot of fun and I plan to keep playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Long-drawn, units shoot the floor, damage against 1 hp retreaters kind of gameplay like in Company of Heroes or Dawn of War II. Not really a strategy game, more of a real time X-Com.If a constant feeling of restraint and frustration is your vibe, you will love controlling units in this game.It is exciting and suspenseful and captures the atmosphere of being stuck in the mud with too much going on to save everyone very well.There is an emphasis on single squads of units, and experience matters.The skill needed for this game is teleporting your camera over the screen and giving lots of commands to many, very very sucidical men, women and bears.If you are fine with that, the game has a lot of interesting and unique content. The atmosphere is nostalgic and yet futuristic.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review was edited from my initial one to actually offer an explanation, rather than providing a one word response to just make Steam's persistent and pestering pop-up requests to review games go away)My review can be considered the opinion of someone with a respectable exposure to the RTS genre, but not someone who engages with any competitive multiplayer scene. I generally like the game in terms of story, aesthetics and  sound design, but gameplay itself has some shortcomings. My negative experience comes from my time in the game's single-player campaign, which I had been playing on the game's normal difficulty. While I had been enjoying the initial missions of the game with Polania, the difficulty of the later Rusviet and  opening Saxony sections have been killing my desire to want to push through. In particular I will highlight the 'No Man's Land' mission, which I felt was borderline impossible, having to juggle a push against a well-entrenched enemy while simultaneously holding off very aggressive assaults, all with a pop-cap that seemed rather low (~56 vs. earlier missions 72). IIn terms of general game design, I must express my frustration with how the mechs themselves control. In short, their complete lack of speed and  turrets (forward facing guns only) makes them feel very unresponsive and difficult to command in attack scenarios. Ironically, they prove to me exactly why tanks exist in the real-world and not big stompy robots.As a small ask I would like a way to add newly created units to existing control groups without having to first select the group you want to add to. (Like Shift+2 to add to group two, like in AoE-3) I don't think there's a keybind for this. In summary, If you are only casually into RTS games and play primarily for story/skirmish modes, I would advise caution if seeking to purchase Iron Harvest. The campaign mission design needs a balance pass as they having been turning into exercises of frustration as the story progresses; I keep find myself dreading the next mission.  Perhaps they could be improved by toning down the aggression of the ai in certain objectives, or improving the tutorial sections to better teach the player the correct way to play. Often a secondary purpose of a story campaign is to do just that, but I'm not really feeling that here.

_childDocuments_.review:
Iron Harvest is a real-time strategy game (RTS) set in the alternate reality of 1920+, just after the end of the Great War. The Game lets you control giant dieselpunk mechs, combining epic singleplayer and coop campaigns as well as skirmishes with intense action on the battlefield for multiplayer fans, Iron Harvest is the classic real-time strategy games fans have been waiting for.

Tradition clashes with scientific and technological progress, while Europe is still recovering from the brutal battles of the World War. Cities are being rebuilt and in the countryside, the era of the Iron Harvest has begun. Farmers are uncovering the remains of the majestic walking machines that had fought on the battlefields of the Great War.

In the midst of this chaos, a new threat appears that will put Europe's very existence at risk. Secret forces are putting everything they can towards destabilization of entire countries, determined to set the world on fire once again and finally seize control.

name: Maid of Sker
detailed_description: NEW CO-OP HORROR SHOOTER SKER RITUAL 🧟🔫 About the Game Brave the nightmares of the Quiet Ones. Do not panic…don’t even breathe! Maid of Sker is a first-person survival horror, set in a remote hotel with a gory and macabre history from Welsh folklore. Armed with only a defensive sound device, you’ll utilise stealth tactics to avoid death amongst a cult of sound-based AI enemies. Set in 1898 and inspired by the haunting Welsh tale of Elisabeth Williams, this is a story of a family empire driven by torture, slavery, piracy and a supernatural mystery that suffocates the grounds of the hotel. Created and developed by Wales Interactive with a plot crafted by the writing talent and designers behind the likes of SOMA, Don’t Knock Twice and Battlefield 1. Features • 3D sound-based AI system as the core survival mechanic. • Realistic visuals featuring 4k uncapped on PC (1080p 60fps minimum). • A chilling story inspired by Welsh folklore fusing psychological, gothic and British horror. • Re-imagining of famous Welsh hymns Calon Lân (A Pure Heart), Suo-Gân (Welsh Lullaby) and Ar Hyd Y Nos (All Through the Night) from the spine-chilling voice of Tia Kalmaru. With the support of the Creative Europe Programme - MEDIA of the European Union

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker delivers an enjoyable survival horror experience, with ideas redolent of the  movies and is inspired by British folklore. Whilst the playtime is quite short-lived, the gameplay is simple, yet effective and features an engaging new mode to try out after completion of the main story.The story is set in 1898, Wales and is inspired by the Welsh tale surrounding the haunting of Elisabeth Williams. This legend centred around the downfall of a family empire with references to supernatural happenings being behind it. Maid of Sker follows suit in this narrative with the protagonist, Thomas, heading to Sker hotel after receiving a letter from his betrothed, Elizabeth, stating that something had gone horribly wrong with the hotel’s grand reopening. Thomas arrives, only to find the place in complete shambles, dilapidated and seemingly abandoned. His quest to aid his love propels him deeper into the sinister depths of the hotel, only to discover that it is not so abandoned after all. With blind, masked men from a cult called the Quiet Ones lurking throughout the establishment, completely devoid of their sanity.The madness seems to all stem from a specific melody (references to famous Welsh hymns) and Thomas has no choice but to try and compose a countermelody to reverse the lunacy that has taken control. To do so, he must search and accumulate musical cylinders that are spread throughout the hotel, in order to piece them together and ultimately free the many minds that are lost to the supernatural influence of the harmonic tune.Maid of Sker is a survival horror that attempts to focus on the application of stealth tactics to avoid the various enemies. In the main story, there are no weapons or even places to hide which surprised me, the only real mechanic is holding your breath. Understandably, for some, this may not seem very appealing nor engaging and I believe that is a fair critique. This is by no means an excellent stealth game and I am cautious whether it should even be labelled as stealth at all, simply due to the enemies simplistic design. I found the few puzzles to be average, neither difficult nor mindlessly simple and each area featured a descriptive map that allowed me to navigate the hotel with ease. Thomas roams around the hotel, searching for the musical cylinders and often comes into contact with the brainless enemies who are influenced by the sinister melody. I call them brainless, as it really is an accurate description of them. Yes, they cannot see me, and their design is supposed to rely solely on sound, similar to the  movie franchise, but they really cannot hear very well either. It was exceptionally easy to just walk right by them, almost rubbing sides with them, brushing against the curtains or stepping on broken glass and they would not hear a thing. This was all possible as long as I was holding M1 to hold my breath, and you can hold it for a substantial amount of time. Although, it does become more complex in later chapters, with the addition of new enemy types that are alerted easier and a large increase in the quantity of enemies overall, I still think the stealth idea is not the titles strongpoint. In complete transparency, I do not enjoy games with a hardcore stealth focus, and I am certainly not one to enjoy the patience they require. Thus, I did not mind the enemies design here, and liked the simplicity. It is clear that this opinion will vary from person to person and depending on your preference, could make or break the game for some players. Although there are no weapons, players do obtain a "phonic modulator" which stuns all enemies for a short period of time, allowing players to sneak past. This is especially helpful in later sections of the game where it is easy to become overrun and backed into a small corner. However, there are limited charges for it and thus the device must be used sparingly, it cannot be relied on to get through the entirety of the game. This was a welcome addition and although I only used it a few times (playing on recommended normal difficulty), I imagine this would be an exceptional help in higher difficulties.Being a long time horror enthusiast, I come to expect to see similarities between the classics such as  (RE) and Silent Hill. I believe drawing inspiration from these titles is not a negative, but there is a fine line between being a cheap RE clone and being able to expand upon the classics and to make something unique. I do not believe Maid of Sker is a cheap clone, but the inspiration is clearly visible. The only character in the game that can see players is basically a version of Mr X from RE. The similarities are unmistakable with his towering height, follows players relentlessly, loud, thudding steps that can be heard through walls, wears a trench coat.... need I say more? Interestingly, I also felt the game resembled some themes of , I suppose due to the phonic modulator gadget, but it is also more than that, something I cannot seem to pinpoint, but that semblance is present.After completing the game, I was delighted to see a new mode to try out. In this mode, it is completely different to the main game and players have access to weapons, including an axe, revolver, shotgun and more. This created an entirely different experience where we actually are involved in combat and need to fight to escape. Players can still choose to be stealthier if they wish, but the addition of several new enemy types make combat the easiest choice. I thought this was an excellent extension alongside the main game and would recommend playing this after completing the story.In the beginning of the game, in the outdoor area, the game is absolutely gorgeous, which I was not expecting. However, majority of the game is evidently inside in the hotel (or outside it, but at night) and I always thought it was just too dark. Even after playing around with the gamma slider, it still came off as a tad grainy. Nevertheless, this was only a minor gripe.Sound design was excellent and built tension well, with sharp chord sounds demonstrating an enemy had heard you, random thuds coming from the walls, objects suddenly falling on the floor and abruptly breaking the painful silence. This sound design helped craft the horror atmosphere, without relying on cheap jumpscares.Maid of Sker is a short survival horror experience developed by  with a stealth focus and a clear inspiration from the classics of the genre. Despite its minimal stealth mechanics, it does feature an excellent, eerie sound design that creates the high tension which horror fans crave. Although I greatly enjoyed my playthrough, due to its short length, I'd recommend this at a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker, set in 1898, is based on a well-known Welsh folklore telling the story of the romance of Elizabeth Williams and Thomas Evans.Elizabeth's father, who is not at all happy about this liaison, locks her up in the Sker house to keep them apart. About 10 years later, Elizabeth died of her broken heart and has been haunting the property as a ghost ever since.  Thomas, who has received a strange letter from his Elizabeth, is asked to compose a melody that harmonizes with a music box.So, with the new tune in his luggage, Thomas travels to the Sker house, which is a hotel by the sea and is surrounded by melancholic sounds.On the way there, however, it quickly becomes clear that things are not right here.We encounter a strange figure of light and the hotel seems to be completely deserted. But we soon realize that we are not alone.The melancholic sounds cast a spell on the staff and they have been wandering through the old hotel as if hypnotized ever since. In addition, everyone is blind because they have a kind of bag over their heads. But they hear extremely well, so from now on Thomas has to move as silently as possible through the old property in search of his missing lover and the missing pieces of music.The concept behind Maid of Sker is simple and the developers themselves describe the gameplay as tactical stealth. In principle you could leave it that way, but for the most part you just dodge the enemy and rarely have to be really tactical. Even if all enemies sneaking around can hear well, they are blind and also quite slow. And even if you were heard, it's not that difficult to tag the opponents. You can also hold your breath to be completely still, but this only works for a moment, and the longer you hold your breath, your field of view will become blurred.There are passages where you are more or less forced to hold your breath, for example in a dusty basement or when walking past a fire. In the later course of the game you get a device in your hand, a kind of sonic weapon that can put the opponent out of action for a short time. Apart from that, we are actually completely defenseless.Apart from these exciting ideas, the rest of the gameplay is rather rudimentary as it is not possible to look around the corner or over the edge of cover. The set level of difficulty also decides on the ability of hearing the opponent. The more difficult it is chosen, the better our adversaries hear. But with enough patience, these are actually not a real problem at any difficulty level, since their paths are relatively easy to see through.Unfortunately, the whole thing is sometimes a bit surprising because noises can alert the blind monsters, but you can walk past them in the immediate vicinity without the footsteps making them sit up and take notice. Some things like squeaky gates alert them, but loud conversations or phones or doors opening and slamming don't. There seems to be a bit of a lack of consistency here.As far as the exploratory aspect of the hotel goes, the Maid of Sker really nailed it. We move through the plausibly built hotel and also through the surrounding outdoor area, which includes a cemetery, a forest and an abandoned mine. In addition, there is something to learn about the exciting background story in the form of documents and records at every location. Optionally, the game offers small music statues as collectibles that you can already hear from a certain distance and at that moment you want to know where you can find the thing.The premises are quite winding, but still pleasant in typical survival horror manner and really invite you to explore. However, as the game progresses, exploring becomes more tedious as more and more blind monsters appear, so that you are forced to take more and more detours or have to accept longer waiting times, for example to get from one end of the floor to the other with the required key. Trial & error or backtracking are therefore unavoidable and can sometimes lead to some frustration.Genre lovers can look forward to the safe concept of discovering secret paths, solving switch puzzles or finding keys. Even if you can move relatively freely in the hotel, the outdoor areas are unfortunately quite linear. A little more would certainly have done the game and the atmosphere here even better.Graphically, the whole thing is more of an emotional roller coaster ride, because the motion blur makes everything look a bit spongy and there are rooms that sometimes have more and sometimes less detail. But despite the mentioned weaknesses in the implementation, the game also has positive things to offer.The atmosphere, while never really scary, is always eerie and well set off by the appropriate soundscape. The enemies can be located quite well by their footsteps and the ambient noises, be it screams or dogs barking from afar and the creaking of the floors sometimes give you goosebumps while the melancholic singing touches you on an emotional level. This is rounded off by the excellent English speakers.Apart from the main game, the game also offers successful FPS challenges that can be accessed via the main menu.The aim of the challenges is to leave the floor or the building without getting killed.Even if these challenges are almost more fun because you can attack your opponents with firearms and melee weapons, it is advisable to only play them after the main game has been completed, otherwise you will not be familiar with the premises and will probably run around even more aimlessly.For the challenges, there are achievements that, apart from two additional ones, consist of mastering the four levels. There are two achievements for each of these levels. Once for mastering the level itself and completing the level with the grade A*, which means reaching a score of at least 100k and staying under a certain time.The other achievements that the game offers can only be obtained if you play through the game several times.Maid of Sker is an unusual game, somewhere between questionable and excellent.The story and the game certainly don't turn the genre upside down and through the stringently told story you can quickly guess in which direction the whole thing is going.Nevertheless, the game manages to take a different path of creepiness. The oppressive atmosphere and the music that runs through the whole game contribute immensely to the atmosphere. Enemy design is original if a little disturbing.The telling of the story, which does not take place with cutscenes but only through the gramophone and found texts, as well as the monotonous gameplay stand in the way of a clear recommendation for me. But if you can turn a blind eye or two, the game is an interesting and original horror story that can keep you busy for four to six hours if the price is right.Review date: November 14, 2022✔ subtle horror✔ Mysterious and exciting story✔ Great designed hotel✔ good art design✔ logically structured areas✔ good use of sounds✔ melancholic soundtrack✔ Focus is on exploration✔ clear maps✔ three levels of difficulty✔ alternate endings✘ too much motion blur✘ Rudimentary stealth mechanics✘ Opponents are easy to see through✘ Sneaking is tiring over time✘ relatively short

_childDocuments_.review: NO STORY SPOILERSTL;DR - Great visuals, great atmosphere, intriguing story but ultimately a tedious experience let down by the actual gameplay.This is a wonderfully looking, exquisitely sounding game that is let down by one major issue - The gameplay loop is repetitive and kinda boring. I honestly think it would be better experienced on ‘Safe Mode’ without enemies just to enjoy the atmosphere and story. But for that I wouldn’t pay the full price.THE GOODYou can tell a lot of work has gone into this. The flavour is a little different, with some Welsh folklore and Greek Myths weaved through. Elements from staple Horror titles, such as Resident Evil and Amnesia have been borrowed and utilised well. This creates a world that feels real and immersive. I loved the environments, the lighting and particularly the sound.If you are new to the Horror genre of games then this may well give you a frightening experience. THE BADWhilst the opening hour or so is great and sets a tense atmosphere and an intriguing story sadly any moderate to veteran Horror player is going to quickly work out that the enemies use pretty basic patterns and aren't threatening. You are often forced into situations where you have to wait for enemies to move slowly through their patrol routes so you can grab an objective. I believe the idea of this was to generate tension and unpredictability but it just becomes kinda tedious. There is very little variety to shake this up. You can see what they were trying to attempt with the Boss fights but in execution they are laughable, particularly the last one.The ‘Hold Breath’ mechanic is a nice idea but it didn’t do much for me. At times it was an irritation as I would use it to allow an enemy to pass me by but many times they would just stop next to me, at which point I can’t move and they won’t move. So the breath eventually runs out and I’m forced to run, but not out of fear, more necessity. Which is another sad note - The enemies, when alerted are not frightening at all. They hiss and give you a few slaps if they can catch you, but once you work out that they can’t enter save rooms the whole thing becomes an exercise in timing and patience.Whilst the world itself is wonderfully atmospheric I found that there is little in the way of extras to find to reward exploration. There are some notes but mostly the story is told through the Homophones found in every save room that are visible on the map. So honestly there isn’t a massive amount of incentive to explore. Yes, there’s the Music Doll collectables but in a game like this those are just padding for a little extra play time. Honestly, I just can't recommend it because I found myself relieved when the whole thing was over. THE UGLYThat dog was definitely finished last thing on a Friday before deadline.

_childDocuments_.review: A competent indie survival-horror. Some people here described it as a walking sim in their reviews, and i sort of understand where they're coming from, but Maid of Sker is actually more akin to Resident Evil and Amnesia.  Big gloomy manor with keys and items to collect, backtracking, secret rooms and secret passages, you know the deal. Unfortunately, it's very basic, there's only a handful of locked rooms and overly simple puzzles to solve. I really wish the progression, levels and puzzles were much more complex, but that's not a deal breaker.What sets MoS apart is its main gimmick when it comes to stealth: enemies are blind and only rely on their ears to find you. Making any sort of noise is ill-advised, so you gotta walk slowly, and hold your breath if something makes you cough. A cool design choice for sure, but just like the rest, it's not perfect. Most of time you avoid your foes just like you would in any other similar game. But sometimes the approach gets more tricky, and that when it gets interesting. But it's still underexploited imo.Engaging story, atmosphere and themes make that so-so game worth your time if you like horror. N.B: do yourself a favour and disable TAA if you play this. It's horrendously implemented and makes everything blurry when you sprint or move.

_childDocuments_.review: With plenty of survival horror games available, creating something new and familiar to the  formula is challenging.  took up the task, improving the overused formula, even if only by a small margin.On the behest of her beloved, Thomas sets out to the famous Sker hotel. But, without any concierge to greet him upon his arrival, his fingers were twitching to leave a poor  review. Just then, a telephone rings, and on the other end, Elizabeth, his beloved. Pleading with him to not leave a negative review as it may damage her family reputation, she instead proposes he composes a counter melody to free the hotel staff from the weird sack head sickness that befell them. The story is nothing grand, and it most certainly didn't have me glued to my chair. It's your typical  trope seen in many horror media before. And you can find the bits and pieces that shed light on the events leading up to everyone rocking a sack on their head throughout the hotel in the form of gramophone recordings and notes. Overall, it was fine, but nothing you'll ponder over as you take a stroll through the busy neon streets of Tokyo.Let's get one thing straight -  The formula can provide some great horror moments, but at this point, seeing the 100th game doing the exact same thing  did without any innovation really grinds my gears. But, while  doesn't deviate from this formula, it does . That item is the , which is obtained early on. Its high-frequency noise will make enemies shriek in pain, giving you a small window to slip past them. But ammo is scarce, so you can't use it carelessly. There are no lockers to hide in, but you can hold your breath. This is seen on the promotional material and used as the main selling point.  (duh, the idiots have sacks on their heads). But, I do think this mechanic could have been expanded upon. More environmental traps that produce noise could have been placed throughout the hotel. You can bump into stuff or cough, which alerts the enemy, but I still feel there are far too few sound hazards for you to worry about.; It has fixed pathfinding, thus is easily exploited. I really think games should do away with this, or at least have more than one path coded into the AI, so it isn't as predictable. But, one enemy - the , does pose a serious problem. He will always find you, perhaps because Thomas wears some distinct cologne or something. You can stun him tho with that phonic modulator thingy, so that is nice. His inclusion does amp up the tension in certain areas, as haste is needed when completing those puzzles, or you risk his delicate hands crushing your skull. And having normal enemies to manoeuvre past while also trying to quickly finish a puzzle can lead to some happy little accidents, which mostly end in you dying.I did like the level design of . Starting off linear, as you slowly learn the mechanics and get accustomed to muting yourself, it opens up on your return to the hotel for the second time, letting you explore more freely. The hotel is separated into smaller open levels, with plenty of shortcuts and plenty of stuff to bump into and alert enemies. But, you know the drill by know -  These keys are found in the form of, well, keys, or as some intricate puzzles that make zero sense why someone would design a door to open that way. I did like that the hallways and majority of rooms are tight, offering little to no options in manoeuvring past enemies, so you can find yourself in a pickle if you are not careful. And the simplicity of the puzzles wasn't an issue for me. This ain’t no puzzle game. They are here to give players something to explore the hotel for and provide a change of pace. All of the information you need to solve them is available in the environment, so you won’t find yourself frustrated by a particular puzzle. Some puzzles do repeat way too often, like press or pull a switch to open a door.A recent update did add some challenges, and we got to use some weapons in them. I personally really liked how they felt, and perhaps in their future game,  will let us use weapons as we fight monsters. The boss battle at the end was ok, but be warned, each challenge is only a slightly different run. The layout is the same, the enemy spawns are the same, the boss is the same. It's just different conditions imposed on you. Still, I had fun trying to speedrun these challenges and compete on its leaderboards.I did think the enemy design was quite poor. They don't really have any variety. Putting a different hat on a sack doesn't make the enemy unique or interesting to look at. They are still using the same model. The hotel itself did look fine, and the rooms didn't have that empty feeling. But the real star of the show is the game’s lighting, the driving force behind creating an amazing horror atmosphere alongside the amazing audio. The ambient sound design compliments the visuals exceptionally well, with the old wooden floors creaking as the uneasy enemy howling and loud footsteps slowly creep up from the shadows. This is where the great directional audio shines, helping you tell what direction a possible threat may come from. Music is also exceptional, contributing to the atmosphere and constant tension you feel, and the songs you hear are simply grand. They are re-imaginings of famous Welsh hymns, and sung by Tia Kalmaru, with the most majestic voice I’ve ever heard. offers an enjoyable survival horror experience without relying on cheap and gimmicky jump scares, letting its amazing atmosphere and sound design do all the work. Even if the AI was a bit challenged, I think I will leave a positive  review for my stay at the Sker hotel.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are beautiful, with detailed, intricate environments that are a pleasure to explore.The audio (which is critical in a game like this) is also quite excellent, featuring lovely background music and tense, realistic sound effects.Without spoiling anything, the story is intriguing. It's compelling enough to drive you to progress forward to find out what's really going on at the hotel and what happened to the family who own it.As far as the gameplay goes, it's a fairly simplistic case of wandering the halls of the hotel, finding items and completing puzzles, attempting to avoid the various enemies along the way. You will need to be as quiet as possible, as the enemies are sensitive to sounds specifically. Crouching around and holding your breath will become a frequent necessity.If I have anything negative to add, it may be that the enemies aren't quite as dangerous as I thought they would be, or as sensitive to the noises. Honestly though, this might be because I'm playing on Normal rather than Hard difficulty, so take that with a pinch of salt.I'm having a lot of fun playing through this, and I hope many others do as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker was, I feel, a very undertalked about game. The atmosphere was absolutely chilling in some portions of the game. The lore kept me so interested, and I loved searching for every collectible. I found that searching for collectibles triggered my inner completionist and had me craving to find every single thing. Maid of Sker was absolutely gorgeous and had me stopping just to admire the beauty of it. During the game, if I were you, I would "save scum" as much as possible. You'll thank me later and save yourself hours of frustration. If you do not like stealthy games, this game will not be for you, to put it bluntly. You will not be using weapons throughout the game, and you will have to rely on being silent and stealthy throughout (you will have to hold your breath as you walk by enemies). This mechanic gets to be annoying sometimes, but you'll get accustomed to this very quickly. This mechanic also keeps you on edge throughout the whole game, as you will have to be constantly attentive to your surroundings to try and pin-point which direction an enemy is coming from. I really enjoyed my playthrough and found myself unlocking both of the endings. Both endings were kind of predictable, in my opinion, but were also very well developed and intriguing.I'd highly recommend to check this game out if you're looking for a spooky game this Spooktober. Rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic horror game - while there is a lot of background gore (environmental so if you're sensitive, it is ignorable), most of it is atmospheric. The story is fascinating, the music gorgeous, the levels interesting and there's a lot of environmental storytelling. The stealth sections can be tedious (most of the game is sneaking around), I never actually got annoyed about it. There's also the option to turn the difficulty down which does make the stealth sections much more tolerable. Yes, you'll still be sneaking everywhere but the detection meters of the enemies are far less frustrating.Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential, but I couldn't finish it.  Its so easy to get stuck with low health and then you are screwed.  The enemies cant see but they might as well have super vision.  There are tons of them in and area and even standing still can get you caught if they wonder close enough.  The spawns of them seem to be right in locations where you can get caught. Once they find you you're dead.  Only escape is to run to a save room and wait forever for them to reset.  You get this little contraption that can stun them, but the uses for this thing are very limited.  I swear certain areas are made for you to get caught. Multiple times I found myself in a hallway with an enemy on each side, I just had to die, no way around them.  You'd think with a stealth horror game you'd have hide mechanics, but nope, best you get are some vents that'll take you to a different room, which the enemy can get to by opening a door.This game isn't scary, its just a stealth game that has bad mechanics.  It sucks because the graphics and music are beautiful and the story was interesting.  I just couldn't deal with getting caught every two seconds because the enemies have enhanced detection skills.  I got hurt, I was one hit away from death, while wondering around looking for a health drink I got caught in a cut scene that sent me to the next part of the game.  So I had to wander around a new area, swarming with enemies and no health.  This game had potential but screwed it up with the actual mechanics.  If you want a good stealth horror game go play the original Outlast or Alien: Isolation.  Those games did it right.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: This is an atmospheric first-person survival horror game set in a remote hotel with a gory and macabre history from British folklore.Set in 1898 and inspired by the haunting Welsh tale of Elisabeth Williams, this is a story of a family empire driven by torture, slavery, piracy and a supernatural mystery that suffocates the grounds of the hotel.In this game you're pretty much defenseless against these blind enemies that lurk in the dark (and at least 75% of the game is in the dark). However, these enemies get attracted to sound and mostly towards the noises that you make (they don't get attracted towards environmental noises as much except in certain scripted areas) and at certain point of the game you get a device with limited charges (to be found in the world) that you can use to temporarily disable their hearing and run away.+ Amazing sound design and atmosphere.+ Good graphics.+ Mostly smooth gameplay and good controls.+ Supports controller.+ Interesting enemy design + I really REALLY loved the music in this game.+ The game is priced just right for the content. - Enemies sometimes are either really smart or really dumb which made the game feel inconsistent as in they can get attracted to your footsteps but not doors opening and closing.- Dying in the game can be really irritating near end game not due to the difficulty of the game but due to the fact that you have to backtrack from your last save  so that you don't attract enemies and get killed again.- I have been getting some random stutters throughout the game for no reason.- The story barley makes sense to me.- The only device you can use to temporarily defend yourself is useless against certain type of enemies  and there is no hint about that whatsoever so you're pretty much left out to find this out by yourself and possibly dying in the process.~ The game can be finished within 4-6 hours only! I personally had no issue with the game being short as it DIDN'T feel short when I played it and I really couldn't see the game going any longer than this without being stretched but for some others, you may feel that the game is on the short side.With an average blind walkthrough I got 6.3 hours into the game..and that's with me trying to find all collectables by myself (no guides) and getting all endings Overall I think this game is worth it if you're a survival horror fan specially for this price. However, If you're still skeptical due to the cons mentioned above, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains no major spoilers, nor any actual minor ones to speak of. (pronounced "", which I didn't know until I first booted it up) is a horror game in the modern style of collecting notes, solving [mostly simple] puzzles, and running from as well as avoiding enemies that you're otherwise unable to dispatch. It's nothing new that you haven't already seen before necessarily, but it does have a couple of things to distinguish itself from its contemporaries. The graphics are quite nice and have a mostly photorealistic aesthetic set in the late 1800s. A lot of the movement and interactions are well animated making the moment-to-moment gameplay pretty believable whilst complimenting the visuals well. The majority of the game takes place inside of a mansion and it looks very convincing as you traverse its many rooms and look upon its interior decor. The non-mansion areas also look equally as realistic within their respective settings. As this is a horror game, expect some detestable visuals.The main "gimmick" of this game is sound. First off, the music's great. The lovely and at times unearthly-like singing that you'll hear throughout the game adds to the audio impact as well. When it comes to gameplay though, sound plays an important part in how you progress because 90% of your adversaries are blind and can only track you via auditory triggers. What you step on, bump into, manually move, or interact with all produce varying levels of audible tones. This is noteworthy because even if there's no enemy within an area or inside a room with you, they can still potentially find you from wherever they were if they've heard you. Unfortunately there are no real opportunities for you to use these mechanics to your advantage against your enemies. You either make noise, or you don't, with only one later exception. Environmental sounds also play a role here, not only since it can distract your adversaries, but within its design to induce tense feelings during quieter sections or further emphasize those uneasy moments.To build upon how important sound is, there's also the ability to cover your mouth and hold your breath, which is useful to keep your breathing inaudible when close to those whom wish you harm. This goes hand-in-hand with the super simple and basic stealth element of pressing the crouch button to move slow. Here's where things get a little, irregular. The AI can use some improvement; sometimes they follow the stealth rules, sometimes they don't. Collision detection and enemy awareness triggers seem to be the core issues there. They are also pretty dumb and can get stuck on walls or objects. At one point an enemy got stuck in a doorway and I couldn't pass through it, leaving me to try and squeeze by with as little contact as possible like being at a packed club and heading to the bar area. Of course that ended up with my presence being detected and his attempt at hitting me with a haymaker...but he missed, 'cause I peace'd outta there. This also speaks to something I've noticed where you can either crouch-walk through most of the game's enemy traffic-heavy areas and go largely undetected, which takes a lot more time, or you can just forgo stealth altogether and book it to wherever you need to get to so long as you have an idea where you're headed. Obviously the latter is much faster. Both are viable options though and I used each for specific goals. There are two endings in the game, a good and a bad one, the former of which requires obtaining all of a specific type of item. Both endings just kind of end, bringing a conclusion to all you've endured but not much more than that. Most of the story or lore you'll have to read through from items you pick up to have a better understanding of the situation and what lead up to it. It took me about 5 maybe 6 hours total to get all 20 achievements, but the game is about 4 maybe 5 hours long. If you're a dollar-per-hour value gamer, you may feel like there's a bit of a discrepancy here.Maid of Sker doesn't break any new ground in the  crowded first person horror genre, especially within this subgenre style, but it brings its own flavor to the endeavor.  Its use of Welsh mythology does help it out in that regard and this is also seen in elements of the narrative. The voice acting is pretty good which adds to the immersion, along with filling in the map when interacting with the environment. It has some enemy AI issues and certain sounds and sections of the score loop far too regularly, sounding repetitious. The price of admission could be considered a little high, so catch it on sale if you're interested in it but aren't ready for it at that MSRP. Recommended Xbox Gamepad

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to give this game a negative review but Maid of Sker is pretty sub-par. I'd love to just give this a positive review and call it a day, mainly because this is from a small Welsh developer and the game is set in Wales and based on Welsh folk lore, being Welsh myself I want to show support for devs from my country but ultimately I'd be lying if I said I liked this game. I won't be delving much into this mostly because there isn't much to say. Maid of Sker is a fps horror game which mainly focuses on atmosphere and stealth, the atmosphere is ok and I enjoyed the ost which used Welsh lyrics, the graphics are alright and the tone is pretty decent, the stealth however... Stealth is super tedious in this game, you spend half the game crouch walking which is slow af, holding your breath which dims your fov and occasionally using a few simple items to stun enemies, it's boring and tedious and enemies are too dumb and uninteresting to be a challenge or even scary. Enemies suck, they look like the bad guys from the strangers so just humans with bags on their heads, super lame and not scary to run away from, they catch you they punch you and you just sit in a corner and hold your breath. Puzzles are almost nonexistent, the most complex it gets is flick a switch and press a button and then repeat. The rest is just walking around finding items to stick in key slots, I almost want to say this game tried to emulate what RE7 did but ultimately I feel it failed. The story is just meh, unforgettable characters and a weak conclusion. It's also really short, I'd normally say this isn't a good thing but for this game despite being 3-4 hours long I couldn't wait for it to be over. So to wrap this up I'm sorry to bash something that came from my home country but I have to be honest, this game was pretty ass.
