short_description: Go on a journey as Kaze in this 90’s classics inspired platformer. When the Crystal Islands get cursed, Kaze needs to save her friend Hogo while facing enraged living vegetables. Find the Wild Masks to unleash the powers of the legendary guardians and master land, sky and sea.

_childDocuments_.review: Watch out! An evil magician dares to give vegetables of Carrotland sentience! Sure enough, those immediately resort to crime, not to mention how uncomfortable eating them must've gotten. Somehow, I never doubted their deep-rooted scorn. Seeing enraged living veggies as enemies reminded me of Commander Keen Dreams. Maybe it isn't an appropriate reference, though, for Keen has little to do with it gameplay-wise. This one's more in line with Donkey Kong where Kaze, a slightly uncanny bunny with a forehead, replaced all the monkeys. Highly successfully, I might add, making me immediately realise I struck gold just by looking at the game.Pristine and colourful like Looney Tunes, it bubbles with good spirits, playing to jolly music with tribal beats that add energetic cheer to its crispy world, every facet of which is meticulously drawn, and all inhabitants boast hilariously expressive animations. The grumpy carrots alone kept me amused throughout and, overall, lively creature designs did most of the heavy lifting. More importantly, appearances aren't merely decorative, you can usually tell how to deal with each enemy at first glance. These guys have a flat head, perfect for stomping, while those bear a set of giant teeth, so no frontal attacks. You get the picture.Kaze doesn't fall into the trap so many over-animated games before it dug for themselves. Your inputs are always prioritised over the game's desire to flaunt its painstaking efforts. Our hero reacts to button presses immediately, and I wanted to stress this aspect first thing! You don't get such perfectly responsive controls every day, it's easy to imagine how poor ones could undo all the candy castles I threw up earlier. Fortunately, Kaze has you covered and then some, providing the luxury of fully remappable keys and D-pad support. We barely perceive the significance of such little amenities until we're robbed of them.Kaze doesn't like to put spokes in your wheel, in general. With no hacking or slashing to stop you dead in your tracks, it emphasizes pure platforming in short bursts where enemies exist to boost your momentum. Not to mention occasional abilities like dashing or flying granted by the titular Wild Masks, the rabbit's default moveset revolves around haste: spin cuts through enemies on the go, increasing horizontal speed, and the same button winds up helicopter ears for course correction when airborne. Stomping lets you lose altitude in an instant, slamming the sentience out of enemies and turning them back into edibles... Wait, are we the baddies?Regardless, some of the stage gimmicks speed things up immensely. However, despite the zoomed-in camera, you always have time to react even during its fastest segments. The difficulty ramps up gradually to ease you into new mechanics, reaching respectable heights without getting frustrating. When all else fails, Kaze normally has one extra hit and, coupled with generous hitboxes, it makes sure you won't have anyone else to blame but yourself. Sparse checkpoints (usually one per level) could've been a problem if the levels weren't so short. No feature outstays its welcome, making it possible to saturate levels with assorted turmoil that wouldn't fly otherwise.Instead of trying to get you stumped, the stages were designed to flow, arranging a great variety of enemies and obstacles in harmonising ways. To boot, their cycles reset with every retry so you can always learn the clear patterns of any obstacle course or a boss and eventually run them over with flying colours. Speaking of patterns, Kaze shakes things up regularly. You'll be hard-pressed to find two similar levels in a row, and by the time an obstacle returns, it changes beyond recognition. From the classic "floor is lava" premise and jelly-bouncing to a slingshot ride or genre-swapping Runner sequences, these are but a few types of variations for your entertainment.Finally, I'm not sure if I'm qualified to talk about collectibles, but I like how going for them makes one take serious risks. I'm sure more skilful people than me would find it thrilling. I only went for bonus challenges since they directly unlocked more game to enjoy, and the game didn't rob me of a good ending, thankfully. Being a bang for your buck as it is, if you're going for every collectible and winning gold medals in local time trials, Kaze would provide you with even more hours of top-notch content. That said, I feel content with the package and, I believe, made all the reasons for my adoration known by this point. Hop in, it's fun.My curator
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Friends of classic platformers have reason to rejoice - this is a top representative of the genre. An ancient curse turns the peaceful vegetables of Carrotland into deadly monsters. You play Kaze, a young rabbit lady who must save her friend Hugo. Hugo has been sucked in by a collar while exploring an ancient temple together with Kaze. Grave robbers live dangerously, Indiana Jones or Lara Croft already had to learn that! And background stories in action games are almost always stupid, so what the hell.Kaze and the Wild Masks is a classic side-scrolling 2D platformer with a modern look. The world is divided into levels, and Kaze basically has to reach the exit in each level to unlock the next one. Levels that have already been completed can be restarted from the overview map at any time to collect missing gems or improve the time in speedrun mode.Kaze attacks enemies by spinning around her own axis like a whirlwind (Hi, Crash!) or simply jumping on their heads like Mario did. With spiky enemies, however, she shouldn't do the "jumping on their heads" thing. Kaze can turn her long rabbit ears like a helicopter and so float through the air, she probably learned that from Rayman. This allows her to hover a bit and thus cover further distances than if she just jumps. This mechanic will soon become second nature to you, otherwise Kaze won't get far.Kaze automatically hangs herself from vines with her ears, she can then jump up or drop down. She grabs ladders completely automatically - just jump on it. Kaze can pick up barrels lying around and throw them at her opponents. Of course, she also masters a smash attack to smash her opponents (or to get gems out of plants).Very soon Kaze finds the first of the namesake Wild Masks. When Kaze wears such a mask on her head, it not only looks cool but she also gains new abilities. For example, she can fly with the eagle mask. The shark mask allows her to move under water. Each mask also has additional functions, for example Kaze can also shoot with the eagle mask, or accelerate with the shark mask to fight against strong currents. Later, Kaze also finds the mask of a tiger and a lizard.The individual levels are designed differently and each offers different challenges. At the beginning, you are slowly introduced to the different game mechanics. For example, there is a cave inhabited by deadly crabs that often stay on tiny platforms. It is impossible to avoid them - however, these crabs are very shy of light. A plant often found in the cave opens briefly when touched and shines a bright light on everything. So you have to touch the plant and then run as fast as possible past the crabs hiding from the light. You don't have much time, however, as the plants quickly close up again...The difficulty level starts very low, even beginners should be able to complete the first few levels easily. Kaze basically can't take much and dies with every hit or when she falls off a platform. However, she can always pick up hearts in the course of the game, which absorb the first hit. A loss of life is not quite so dramatic, however, as Kaze has an infinite number of lives. If she dies, you start the level from the beginning or from the last save point. The first of the superbly staged boss fights is the end of the fun, however, and things really get down to business. Even veterans are challenged here. But what the heck, even those who have never played the tough classics like Mega Man or Metroid (infinite lives? Excuse me?) are used to a challenge these days after hits like Cuphead, Super Meatboy or Celeste. In addition to the normal mode, you can also choose a "casual mode" in which there are more save points and life energy in the levels. The scope of Kaze and the Wild Masks is considerable - over 30 levels with more than 50 bonus levels need to be completed.If you complete a level, you can receive gems for it if you fulfil the necessary requirements. If you find all 4 letters (K, A, Z, E) in a level, you receive a yellow citrine at the end, which unlocks a picture of the background story in the album. If you collect at least 100 (small) purple amethysts in a level, you will receive a large purple amethyst. If you have completed both bonus stages, you will receive a green emerald. If you have collected enough of them (six), you can unlock additional levels.Hidden in each level are two bonus stages. The aim is to complete certain tasks under time pressure. This can be collecting all the gems or defeating a certain number of enemies. The tasks and the level structure are quite different, but you always have to get a crystal half within the time limit to finish. The first bonus stages are still quite simple, but later on they are difficult to find and require a lot of practice to complete. One wrong jump and it's over.Kaze and the Wild Masks also caters to speedrunners. After completing a level for the first time, a speedrun mode is available. If you start the level again, a stopwatch appears right at the beginning, which you can activate. If you do this, all the collectibles (but not the enemies) disappear and a countdown begins. The goal is to reach the end of the level before the countdown expires.The levels Levels full of action and danger make use of the game mechanics of many old classics. You could also say that Kaze and the Wild Masks has cribbed everything that has worked well in 2D platform games in the past. Connoisseurs will always be reminded of Super Mario (or Giana Sisters for all you Amiga fans), Rayman, Earthworm Jim or more recent hits like Owlboy and Song of the Deep. Their whirlwind attack is clearly from Crash Bandicoot. Kaze and The Wild Masks is also a great homage to the unforgettable Nintendo classic Donkey Kong Country by Rare. The dangling from vines or the repeated jumping on the heads of several enemies could have been taken straight from Rare's masterpiece. Oscar Wild was absolutely right when he once said "Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery". In the case of Kaze and the Wild Masks, however, it is by no means pure imitation, but rather the reworking of classic game principles for a modern audience using current technologies.The pixel graphics are inspired by games on the Nintendo SNES or Sega Mega Drive, but are high-resolution and not as pixelated as they were back then. Absolutely gorgeous, I kept stopping to look at the backgrounds or smile at an opponent's animations. 4K resolution (3840×2160) is supported, and scrolling is completely smooth. Simply ingenious. With my ultrawidescreen monitor (3440×1440), however, it doesn't look quite as good - here Kaze and the Wild Masks runs smoothly, but with black bars on both sides.Whether using the Xbox One gamepad, Steam controller, Xbox 360 controller, PlayStation Dualshock 4 (it even shows the PlayStation buttons), a PlayStation 3 pad or my little 8BitDo Zero 2 controller, Kaze and the Wild Masks worked straight away with every wireless gamepad I tested it with. Thanks to three memory slots, up to three players can save their game progress independently of each other.Kaze and the Wild Masks is a great looking, varied retro platformer. It's immense fun to sit down on the living room couch, turn on the big flatscreen and soundbar, and use a wireless gamepad to play a game whose basic design is easily 30 years old. It plays like one of the successful games from the 90s, but technically state-of-the-art and much less frustrating thanks to infinite lives and automatic (cloud) saves. Collectibles and a speedrunner mode (with online leaderboards) entice you to replay previously completed sections. All in all, Kaze and the Wild Masks is one of the most entertaining 2D platform games of recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Almost every element of this game, has been seen before, but this was made flawless!This game is on point! It feels like it was made for speedrunning - Every single element in each level is timed to perfection. I always hated speedrunning, but this game made me love it - Nothing beats the flow in this game.Controls are perfect and the music fits very well. Difficulty level is very low, this wasn't hard at all. There is a slight difficulty spike in the end boss, but nothing too bad. The way this game is set up, you can memorise yourself out of a though spot, its all about recognizing the patterns. There is also a casual mode, which I tried out and this makes the game a breeze - Fit for kids too. My only real "complaint" is the art. I don't like how there are 3 different styles mixed throughout the game. Somehow this was distracting for me.I waited forever on this game and it did not let me down! Devs did an amazing job on this game and its a must-play if you like platforms or speedrunning.Olaf's laugh is reason enough to play this game - Remember to eat your veggies!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Way too many auto-scrolling levels, the whole second half of the game is nothing but auto-scrolling levels. Something is always chasing you (a tornado, a monster, rising acid or lava) or you're stuck on a moving platform, one wrong jump and it's all over. And with only one checkpoint per level, the game rarely feels enjoyable, it's just repeating the same sections over and over until you memorize all the blind jumps and can finally be done.Worse yet are the dragon mask levels where your character is running automatically and you can only double jump and dash downwards, all at rather high speed, leaving you barely any time to react, it's incredibly frustrating. I was expecting a cool retro platformer, not Temple Run. Very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun and challenging platformers out there. Beautiful levels and charming soundtrack. Every level represents you with new things and gives you new masks abilities that allows you reach new grounds plus secrets. Controls feels fluid and well made. You can try beat game fast or try to do everything whats in there. Checkpoints are on point. If you like Donkey Kong or Mario Maker this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a Donkey Kong Country game made by an indie dev, with a lot of similar mechanics. You can spin attack off the ledge and jump in midair, similar to certain ape games. Kaze herself is basically Dixie Kong from DKC2 and onwards, sporting helicopter ears, on the other hand, the health system is more traditional, which means the devs get an opportunity to utilize her abilities without a compromise. The controls are as tight and responsive, and the level design is engaging, with some interesting mechanics and trademark "gimmicks". The titular masks are similar to animal buddies, eagle mask is like Squawks the Parrot, tiger mask allows for forward dash and wall climbing, shark mask enables modern swimming controls similar to new 2D rayman games, and of course, DKC Tropical Freeze, and then there's forgotten mask that acts like a traditional autorunner, though I like to think it's inspired by minecarts, but with additional abilities, like double jump and quick downward dash. The autorunning segments are easily the hardest in the game.And of course, there are also collectibles for completionists. There are no lives, but there are crystals that give you a gem after you collect a certain amount, similar to lums from new 2D rayman games, there are KONG letters, I mean KAZE letters that also award a gem, and lastly there are 2 bonus barrels in each stage, I mean bonus crystals that lead to bonus stages. Thankfully, if you fail, you don't have to go back to where the crystal were or have to replay the stage to retry, you can retry the bonus as much as you want until success. Those are required for 100% completion and good ending, which took me almost 5 and a half hours to complete, but there's still a lot of replayability. You can attempt time attack challenges, or try to beat all stages without taking damage for all achievements.The only small negative I have is that the story is underdeveloped. After beating the first boss, it turns out we're saving critters, that don't contribute, besides the first world's airship that acts as a world select. It isn't immediatly obvious that besides beating the bad guy, we're saving people. I think it should've been shown in the first cinematic to make the player more invested in beating the evil. Otherwise there isn't much to the story, beat the bad guy and save your friend. There is some historical backstory that you unlock by collecting KAZE letters, but otherwise, yeah. Not much to say.While it may seem like the game borrows too much from DKC games, I don't think it automatically makes the game bad. In fact, it's quite the opposite, the game is very fun, as I said the level design is engaging and varied. This game is easily the most fun I've had recently playing a video game, and if you're craving for more DKC-like goodness, and even if you don't, I highly recommend checking this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic love letter to the 2D platformers of the 90s. This game is a splendid mix of the Donkey Kong Country series and Rayman Legends, taking the best parts from each and giving it a fresh coat of polish. Graphics and music are great as well. A slight disclaimer is that the game is fairly short and one could probably finish it in around 3 or 4 hour, but the abundance of things to collect kept me engaged and wanting to complete it. Would love to see where the developers go next, they are definitely on my radar.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Well, since Nintendo is currently starving us DKC fans to death as of recent, it's nice to see some people actually create this concoction a spiritual successor that utilizes the best level designs and features from the older DKC games. You'll find everything here that is reminiscent to your past experiences with Donkey Kong, whether it be the music, quirky enemy and boss designs, or even the hidden bonus levels. Kaze doesn't just take everything from what Rare established however, as the designers here obviously took note that Dixie Kong was the best and pretty much molded Kaze after her, replacing another Kong instead with an extra heart (such as with Rayman Origins/Legends). The masks that allow her to transform into different animals are also efficient at adding level variety similar to the animal buddies from the DKC games such as Squawks and Enguarde. What I love most is how this game takes concepts from the classic SNES trilogy and refines them in a way, as if Rare themselves from the olden days were to make this game now. If that's what the creators were going for, then man, they aced it. My experience with the game was great, and the only complaint that I really have is I wanted , but most can agree that's usually a way of praise as well. PixelHive has definitely landed on my radar for their future products, and hey, I'm convinced that only a Kaze sequel could dethrone the current one as my new favorite indie platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through Donkey Kong Country 1 and 2 dozens of times, so this is absolutely my genre.  I can recommend Kaze and the Wild Masks to anyone who enjoys challenging platformers.  Here are the pros and cons:Pros:Very cute art styleLove letter to DKC and games like itGreat musicQuite impressive for such a small team and worth the asking priceCons:The autorun stages are tuned to be way too difficult. It took me about 5.5 hours to do a non 100 percent playthrough and I'd say about 40 percent of that time was spent on the handful of autorun stages.  I usually enjoy these in games, but the ones on offer here are almost purely memory based instead of skill based, so even a highly skilled player won't be able to get through these without dying several times.I also wish the story was a little more coherent.  I understood the story of DKC. I understood the story of Super Mario World. I do not understand the story or plot of this game. It's not a big deal, but I hope if there's a sequel, there's at least something that explains why you're doing what you're doing.Overall, I would totally recommend this game to fans of the platforming genre. If you enjoy DKC or 2d Mario, you will like this.  I hope a Kaze 2 gets made!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I was simply looking for some retro-inspired platforming game while waiting for major releases. Noticed Kaze and Wild Masks lost and forgotten amidst other games in my library and decided to give it a shot. I struck gold - that was definitely one of the best choices I could have made in pixel-art gaming!!Well, (a big) yes and no. Kaze and The Wild Masks is in fact DK-like. This experience was so close to the trilogy that it has brought tears to my eyes while playing. I really needed to play something as such and was unaware of it.It's undeniable - the game isn't original when it comes to ideas. All of them are taken from the source: level design; moves (such as the helicopter glide thingy or the spinning attack); how to defeat enemies; animal transformations; bonuses; how to beat the bonuses; how to hide bonuses and coins, and so on. Wouldn't be surprised if an eventual Kaze 2 implemented a co-op system between two characters, like Diddy Kong and Dixie Kong. If you lived the SNES era, you will notice some ideas taken from Super Mario World too. Is that bad? Can't tell for sure what you guys would expect, but as of me, not at all. That's a huge pro! at the same time, being a DK-ish isn't exactly downright copy-paste. The Brazilian developers have managed to explore extremely well the possibilities and the resources at hand, creating a totally fluid, engaging game through a gameplay experience that takes you back with absolute competence. That means at the same time you see and feel the inspiration, you get a new experience, tough to be created. It's crystal clear they had a clear insight of what Donkey Kong is like and how to reproduce the ideas. They've surely spent hundreds or thousands of hours of their lives playing the trilogy.I've had a blast with Kaze and The Wild Masks and simply couldn't put it down. That got me regretting the game was too short. Wish it were longer - and deserved that, because I haven't had enough of it. The devs have put a lot of their hearts and dedication into it.Kaze and The Wild Masks is probably the best 2D DK-like platforming game you will find up to this day. Just play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Great platformer! Obvious inspirations/homages aside; the controls, visuals, and sound design are top notch. The level design is also very well done in teaching the player the various movement abilities that are needed to complete the level. Game difficulty rises gradually until you encounter some really mean-spirited platforming sections but not in a frustrating way; solving the puzzle always feels good. Had my eye on this game for a long time during development and it exceeded my expectations. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY similar to old Donkey Kong Country games, really a love letter to those games.This is a great sidescrolling platformer, with tight controls, great visuals and a sweet soundtrack.Gameplay is very fluid and responsive, and the 4 masks add some fun variations to the base gameplay.Worlds and levels have very strong themes, present in the visuals and level design. Every level has tons of collectibles to please completionists, and although it is possible to gather all of them on the first run through a level, most likely you will be revisiting some of them to find stuff you missed.Bosses are neat, especially the last one which is just visually stunning.My only complaints would be that the story is pretty shallow and could be explored some more, and some level sections are very difficult, requiring lots of retries.Overall, very solid game, and fans of DKC will certainly love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game that takes a lot of the good ideas of Donkey Kong Country, Rayman and Crash Bandicoot and mashes them in one very smooth feeling package with great artwork. Kaze is cute and I would die for her.My main sorespot of the game is the bosses, because they are all variants on surviving an autoscroller until you can attack, repeat 3-4 times, with the last boss being an especially unnecessarily long-winded and incredibly boring take on this already not especially inspiring formula and sits like a tumour on an otherwise pretty good video game.Still, I had fun. It's a pretty short videogame clocking in at around the 3 hour mark with the caveat that the last 20-30 minutes is going to be tediously memorising the final boss lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It basically is the Dixie Kong oriented spin-off we never got.It very much is an old-school DKC game, and a great one at that. Anyone who liked the original DKC games will like this one. Definitely one of my favourite 2D platformers, tough enough to be challenging but fair with good controls.Plus there’s not too many female lead mascot platformers which was a nice bonus. Representation in the animal kingdom is such an underrated issue.It always does bug me when people knock a game for being an imitation of another. If a game imitates another at a high enough quality then it’s a good game and one to naturally recommend to those who like the game being imitated. Not to mention that this sort of thing is how we get new genres and subgenres. Given the length you might want to wait for a discount, but anyone who adores platformers will get a really fun experience out of it. Kaze definitely seems to be something diehard fans of DKC made and that’s super neat. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the WIld Masks is a love letter to those who grew playing the golden titles of platforming, it definitely makes you feel at home with its heavily inspired 90's style, more particularly using Donkey Kong as an inspiration. it's as simple as it can be, walk jump attack and make it to the finish, the good and never-failing platformer formula.You play as Kaze and the goal of your adventure is to defeat the evil thingie that locked your friend into a ring and transformed veggies into monsters. You can understand the goal of feeling like an authentic 90's classic that narrate short and simple stories as simple as it possibly can, and in that regard it checks the mark very well, it is truly meant to not be too complex.Controls are extremely fluid, it responds perfectly and they work in perfect harmony with the very carefully made level design, everything is so precise and synchronized, which also means the game will be quite challenging as you progress, don't let the cute looks fool you this game is loyal to its 90's inspirations even in difficulty and challenge.The "Wild Masks" part of the title comes from a very important mechanic in this game. In some levels and boss fights you will be given a mask, and depending on what animal is the mask you will get a set of new abilities to explore and go through new level gimmicks. Similar to how animal buddies work in the DK series, the levels are meticulously planned and designed to go along with the flow of that specific mask and its gimmicks, so don't make much expectations of using these whenever wherever you want, you will use them when the game lets you. With that said all the masks are super dope and adds fun new gimmicks to the stages, each exploring very well their set of abilities.Graphics are charming, colorful and superbly detailed, everything is insanely well animated and the scenery as a whole always feels super alive, the art design people did a damn good job at making everything so smooth. The soundtrack is also pretty good, a tropical-ish energy which reminds you even more of Donkey Kong.No collectible is needed to progress, only beating the levels is necessary, but if you're a completionist you'll find good replay value in this game, there's a handful of different collectibles you can go after in every stage and incentive your exploration. You may want to go after the red gems though, since they unlock the true ending of the game and they're the easiest to collect. The other collectibles are driven towards extra content like some pieces of story and extra stages, so if you're more of a casual player but still wants the true ending you can get the needed gems without much sweat.Play time is short overall and it can vary depending on your goals, you could beat it in around 3-ish hours playing in a normal pace while not caring for full completion, but if you are looking for 100% completion which includes collectible gems, time trials medals and no damage crowns, then it would take about 10-12 hours more or less to do so. There's also an achievement of completing the game in 2 hours, but that's a breeze once you get the hang of the game and its level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a beautiful and well designed game. I never had any performance hiccups and the cut scenes have an excellent cartoon feel.I just hated the level design. There were too many autoscrollers where one mistake would lose you minutes of progress. Many of the levels pushed you to go fast, and then would hit you with a blind obstacle. I was frustrated more than I was having fun. Also, many times you'd get to the end of the level to find you missed something, then you have to slog through the level again to tie up loose ends. I may have had a different opinion if I lowered the difficulty. I played on the recommended difficulty which only has one checkpoint per level.The game is a great platformer, I just didn't like the level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those platformers that is so precise that its awe-inspiring AND brutally unforgiving. I respect the work that went into it; most levels can be beaten without stopping our heroine in her quest for platforming goodness.I liked collecting crystals and finding secrets in every level. I liked that the only way to beat a boss was to do it hitless but where the game truly shined, in my humble opinion, was when trying to do every level flawlessly – then, it became a speedrunners dream.The most important part of creating a good platformer is trust; every platform, every step and jump has to be measured to mere inches to provide an optimal experience. Many times, when playing Kaze I felt the levels has just the right amount difficulty to make it challenging but also rewarding.And as such, I salute the developers… it’s a throw back to the 90’s with exquisite pixelated art and rich platforming variety. The powers of each mask meant you couldn’t play every level the same and added more layers to the gameplay and heck, you can even become a shark!Now let's be honest; who doesn’t get a little excited when you can get 50 jumps in a row, with pinpoint accuracy and without hesitation? It’s platforming crack, I tell you and as such, I give it a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Holy balls I'm impressed.Went in thinking "oh nice, indie game from my country, looks cute, nice animations, it's cheap too. Gonna buy to support local game development."Finally got myself around to try it and ended up getting my old DKC era hardcore back into the game.This game FEELS like Donkey Kong Country but different. I love all the challenges and stuff you can try and do, and nothing feels unfair, every time you mess up, it's something you didn't fully pay attention or just didn't know about.I just finished the first hub almost completely, still need gold medal + crown on the secret stage, but I'm tired for now.Thank you PixelHive for such a great yet simple game. I was needing a breath of fresh air among all the incredibly annoying  AAA titles that try to be over the top and end up just being too exaggerated.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever played Donkey Kong Country 2, this plays like if you controlled only Dixie. Which is a big yes for me.You platform across 4 zones with 6~7 stages per zone, with a boss at the end. Pretty straightforward, with an easy to grasp moveset, complemented by the masks mentioned in the title (which work like the animal barrels in DKC).The pixel art is well done, the OST is nice and fits each stage perfectly, and the whole feel of the game is a mix between soothing and challenging....My only gripes is that there is no real difficulty curve. You can find a stage on zone 1 or 2 that is way harder than one in the last zone, and vice versa. Also, while the cutscene images are nice, sometimes they look a bit... Off. It doesn't ruin the game in any way, but it's weird how the exact same artstyle looks so nice in one scene, and a bit uncanny in another.Still, an overall 8/10, hoping for a sequel. ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommend! Kaze is a fun, engaging and challenging platformer.The occasional difficulty spikes might scare some people off but I enjoyed it because Kaze is one of those rare polished gems.You can feel that the devs made sure every enemy and hazard will behave exactly the same everytime you retry a checkpoint, which makes the game very satisfying to overcome because mastery is viable.You will die and repeat a lot of long segments over and over, but don't let yourself color that in negativity, because that's really what the game is designed around. It's full of things where you're not supposed to know they're coming, and through hindsight via trial and error, you'll hit a lot of awesome zen moments. You will find yourself trivializing segments you used to struggle with. That's what I love about this game.That consistency is something that I think is often taken for granted in games, especially platformers, and I applaud PixelHive Studios for making Kaze the very tightly crafted and charming game that it is.(Side note: )
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this after seeing reviews say that this game feels similar to Donkey Kong Country (which I have no experience with but want to try). Things I likeDislikes (Not Con, just some things I dislike)As for playtime, I took about 10hours on my first playthrough to collect everything except time trials and no damage crowns.Overall, a very decent platformer that anyone can enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Very Donkey Kong Country-esque, except a bit easier compared to say DKC2 or Returns. Controls similarly to DKC 1-3, but a bit less momentum based and you always have access to Dixie's hover. Level design explores some cool mechanic combinations, such as wind in the bird levels and ghost chases underwater. Levels were pretty fun overall, I enjoyed the second half of world 2 to the end much more than world 1 to the first half of world 2.The transformations are essentially DKC animal buddies, but aside from the bird being straight-up Squawks the others have unique aspects. The shark is essentially Tropical Freeze swimming on crack (fast consistent movement & huge burst forward on small cooldown), the lizard is a DKC minecart with a double jump and divekick, and the tiger feels separate from the DKC games, granting a horizontal dash & wall jumps. Overall all the transformations are really fun, including the lizard being an autoscroller.Checkpoint positions and bonus rooms seemed fine to me, but I've played a lot of the old DKC trilogy and a ton of Tropical Freeze so I'm already used to the checkpoint distance and bonus room minigames. None of the bonus room minigames are ever repeated which is actually impressive, and some bonus rooms took me a while to find. There's also a separate difficulty with more checkpoints if you're annoyed by the checkpoint distance being too far.Removing lives and having "bananas" act as a collectible is fantastic, as lives suck in platformers but there's still a banana-like item to help guide the player to specific routes. I wish the "bananas" stayed when doing time attack though, as they really feel like a core part of the level design and would help with creating visual cues.100% recommend if you like DKC, still recommend if you like platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Addictive and satisfying platformer, seasoned with elements of precision and speedrunning, but not taking it to the extreme. Immaculate pixel art, catchy but not annoying soundtrack, thoroughly thought-out mechanics, diverse level design. Recommended if you like to master your jumping skills, and are not afraid to develop a kink for huge ears.Longer description.All reviews compare Kaze to Donkey Kong Country; I'm probably lucky to never have played it, so this type of games feels completely new to me. While Kaze requires some precision, both in 2-D and timing, and has speedrunning modes, or enforces some form of speedrunning on you (requiring or not allowing to stop), it does that with great deal of respect to the player. First of all, the game is forgiving to possibly imperfect actions of the player: you can miss half a second, jump higher or lower, land here and there - and if you generally doing it right, you don't need to be 100% precise to pass. Second, game doesn't require you to score every goal in one run; it allows you to return and complete some challenges later. Third, the learning curve is gentle, and first three episodes look like basically tutorial for a fourth one, where level designers dump every possible sneaky trick on you. Fourth, every level has two challenges that allow you to master some helpful moves. Regarding more difficult levels, yes, series of repetitions-and-failures may make you want to rage-quit, but on next day muscle memory kicks in, and you skim through the obstacles like hot knife through the butter. Another very good upside of Kaze is that while all levels share the same platforming formula, each level brings a different dish to the table, becoming a mini-game on its own (while not forgetting to remind you of the skills you acquired earlier). The only sections that feel like having some room for improvement are boss-fights: they are basically longer version of challenges, requiring you to dodge things for extended period of time (you just need to repeat sequences long enough until you will memorize them). Graphics is very good; most levels have different backgrounds; album that depicts some lore is good addition. Kaze, an angry rabbit with omnipotent ears, is nice protagonist.I very recommend Kaze to all appreciators of platformer genre, and hope that we will eventually see a, sequel or a DLC, or community-created levels. Big thanks to the authors.P.S. Regarding speedrunning: the fact that each level can be completed in time trial mode serves as a hint to how it may be played. In most cases you can get out of every tricky situation just by moving forward almost without stops, and jumping a lot, so you will achieve perfect synchronicity with the enemies or obstacles.  (Also when dying in the middle of some  especially evil level again and again, you will find yourself getting to that place faster and faster with each iteration)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Could not vibe with this game at all. Its visual style is nice and the enemies had fun designs, but this one just got more and more frustrating to play. Levels were uninspiring and the later game focused too much on autoscrollers. They're fine once in a while, but overstay their welcome quickly so when they started to appear one after another I decided that I'd had enough. Plus finding out you missed a collectible and having to play through them again just added to the frustration. You can make a challenging level without having to throw in an autoscroller element.The dragon mask is especially guilty of this. It makes Kaze autorun and forces you to make split-second decisions to obstacles that come at you at high speed, which most of the time meant you had to play through the level multiple times in order to memorize it so you could finally complete it. Which might I add, did not feel satisfying. They let out more of a "thank ♥♥♥♥ they're over" reaction from me. Some of these levels even threw in an enemy that chases you unless you temporarily stop it by touching a blue light.. but if you touch a red light they start going after you quicker instead, making these levels even more stressful. And let me tell you, those red lights are scattered everywhere. ♥♥♥♥ that.My advice to the developers is if you like autoscrollers so much maybe make one of those "run" games instead of needlessly shoving them into a platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's Donkey Kong Country but you don't have to hold down the Y button all game to run.I don't need to say much else. It's just DKC again and really good at it. The game is distilled DKC down to the $15 price range so all the levels are tightly packed, go quickly, and each has a pretty neat gimmick. You can recognize obstacles from various DKCs and even a few Mario games here and there. The swimming is all DKC:TF though but without the incredible weight/momentum of that game. Kaze turns on a dime underwater. All this means the game plays great for speed play and especially speedruns.Only downsides: Every single boss is "Survive until the weakness appears" and they all run a bit long. The minecart levels include a double jump and a dive jump and the dive jump is almost impossible to time perfectly as it behaves differently to any jump you have ever used in platforming before. But you are still asked to do a bunch of complicated jump bounce jump jump dive maneuvers at mine cart speed and it is incredibly aggravating and I cleared the whole game without it ever feeling natural to me. And the music just isn't good enough and you should just pop on the DKC2-3 soundtracks instead.Beyond that, excellent little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is one of my favorites platforms games, and I do recommend.But let's talk about the things I find lame, or lacking.- The music is not spectacular. Some levels are good, still the majority felt not atmospheric enough. - It is true that there is not a difficulty progressions. You can have a hard level (even in the first islands), then the next one is easy.- Some hit boxes are off, which can be frustrating for 0 damage runs.- There was one level I couldn't find the second green fragment without y tutorial.- You will need to memorize some levels to be able to perfect them. So add this time to your schedule. Specially the last Boss.- There is no achievement for killing all enemy's on a level, in fact you can ignore them all, except for the bosses.- There are indeed many auto scroll levels, some may like, some may not. And levels where you can go back are very rare.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the more I like it.  Kaze is very much a throw-back to old-school 2D platformers, particularly the Donkey Kong Country SNES trilogy; if you are going to model your playstyle after something, then emulate arguably the best.  Kaze plays extremely similar to Dixie Kong with the twirl, helicopter slow-descent, and general movement.  The gameplay feels like it is right out of DKC.  The level design is solid and feels like it's in the DKC3 mold of most levels having a specific gimmick.  I know I had many moments of "Oh!  This is just like <x level>! ".  That gimmick change keeps everything fresh from level to level.    There are a decent number of collectibles for each level: the classic 4 letters, 2 bonus stages per level, and a special 100+ gem bonus.  Normally, several of these would be tied to your number of lives.  HOWEVER, there is no life system in this game.  Without going into spoiler territory, every one of these 3 level bonuses does have some sort of purpose.  In addition, every level has a bonus for beating the stage hitless and under par time (in a Crash Bandicoot nod).  These can get downright nasty and doesn't get you an in-game bonus, but it's there for Steam completion.    The 4 mask power-ups are well-implemented when in use, in a DKC2 animal barrel sort of way.    Soundtrack is pretty good.  Buck's Throne is my stand-out for this one.  Having a Casual mode is great for folks that aren't the most familiar with the genre.  A couple of knocks:   1)  The game is relatively short.  Only 4 levels with about 35 levels means that you could blow through this one.  If you don't want to go for the Steam achievements and just want to one-and-done, may not be for you.  2) Most of the levels are fine, but there are some levels that require a lot of patience and trial-and-error (the Lizard levels, for example).  The lack of a life system does mitagate this somewhat though.Overall, this may not be my favorite 2D platofrmer that you can get on Steam, but it is a super solid throw-back, especially if you have a DKC itch to scratch.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a ripoff of Donkey Kong Country.  There is no shame in it's game, either, as it totally embraces DKC gameplay mechanics and doesn't seem to give a damn.  Fortunately, the game is really fun to play, has cool animation, great boss battles, and really hard-to-find secrets. Is it original?  Nope.  Yet, it's so fun to play that I beat it in a day.  Short, breezy, and scratches the DKC itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It is a Donkey Kong clone with nice music and art. It is quite fun to start off with, but right from the start this game had weird decisions and as I continued to play I began to really dislike the game. I like to finish games I start so I am glad this one is over.The game is okay for the most part. The inspiration it has taken from Donkey Kong is a bit too much as I found myself only wanting to play those games as they are better in my opinion. The bonus games are quite the chore here. They worked in DKC2, but here they just slow down the experience. The game gets really obsessed with stuff chasing you at one point which I do not like as it feels like every level is a sort of speed run with a rubber banding tornado or whatever chasing you. Especially as there is a ton of those levels. The levels in which you run automatically are awful. The imagination just dies halfway through and I did not think this game was too hard, but I do consider it to be very annoying to play. Why do you float by pressing the attack button instead of simply holding the jump button? Reminds me of a bad SMW hack. It is definitely not bad, but I do not think I can recommend this considering the feelings I had once I was done with this even though the final boss was awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Not done yet with it but having fun so far but there's a big problem, it's likely to not affect many but there are so many damn flashbangs in this game.Get into the bonus game level -> game flashes bright white.Pick up bonus game collectibles -> game flashes bright white.Get to the end of a stage -> game flashes bright white.Again at the result screen -> game flashes bright white.When the result screen is done tallying it up -> game flashes bright white.Collecting powerups -> game flashes bright white.Changing map screen -> game flashes bright white.Would have really liked a photosensitive mode that turned those into fade to black instead to avoid all the flashes, it makes me nauseous and gives me a headache so i can only play a level at a time before i need to take a break >:(Other than that i works fine but really damn annoying, not enough to give a negative rating (as it's a personal problem, not the game breaking would be unfair if i did).Play time will be heavily inflated as i just leave it on while i recover, can take an hour or more before i bother with it again. the game actually won't take all that long to play so disregard my time if you want to know ~how long it is.Edit: 100% run completed, that last boss was awful, double area denial and rng placement for stuff made it darn annoying to play, the final part of it was hard to see what was part of the foreground and what you were supposed to interact with.And the damn flashbangs was everywhere, every stage transition they decided to just blind their players and there are 4 of them ever few minutes.Why the hell did they decided that anytime you move somewhere else to throw up a pure white screen at max brightness and have bright flashes during gameplay >:(It's still not a bad game but this really soured the experience for me, will be just a one and done type of game, not worth playing through again.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this is obviously a spiritual successor to Donkey Kong Country. The game proudly wears its inspiration on its sleeve. But you'd be wrong to dismiss this as just a simple copy. It readily improves on the original formula, with slick controls devoid of any jank, clean visual design that make spotting traps and obstacles easy, and a host of quality of life improvements that remove all the frustration that was so common in the design of games from the 1990s.Really, it's a great game. It's pretty short, but the quality is there, and even then, I'll never blame a game for having not enough of it: developers need to eat.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Short Disclaimer: I don't think that the game is really bad, but one problem on steams rating system is that that it favors mediocre or slightly okayish games, when they absolutely take no risks in their game design decisions which I don't rewardYou can just say "yes" or "no" while the overall rating doesn't give you much insight about the overall quality of the game. That's why I decided to give a negative review and focus on the points I didn't likeForemost I want to say that Kaze nails the most important aspects of plattformers and probably that's why it's received so overwhelmingly positive. - the controls are very smooth and fluid- the level design is pretty strong and catered to these controlsSo I can't lie, saying that I didn't have fun playing Kaze, for it's runtime it delivers an enjoyable experience that can transport you almost in a Zen-like state once you blast through the levels.But the carefully crafted level designs becomes an double-edged-sword eventually, everything connects, every single obstacle has one definitive and obvious approach to tackle through. You know exactly when to jump, not because of your good observation, but because the game subliminal told you to do it. This can be good for the first batch of levels as some sort of tutorial, but this design philosophy drafts through the entire game on almost every single level.it feels like you play an autorunner where you have fully control over the character, if that makes sense. Everything is laid out to you in the most optimal way, with hitzones that are always in favour to the player by a large margin, there is not much thinking involved, rarely timing is required because the levels are synched in a way that you can run through them from the get go.I know it sounds odd to critisize that, since it has a lot of flow, but in this case I think it got too much flow for its own good. If you are someone like me, who is experienced in plattformers and bend on challenges, the game will have nothing in stock for you.That's one of the major differences between Donkey Kong Country, there are of course a lot of similarities which are undeniable, but I can tell you with 100% accuracy that's not how Rare back then designed their games. DKC involved a lot precision plattforming but it rarely forced you into bottlenecks, where the answer how you pass certain obstacles is layed out by the developer.In Kaze enemies are most of the time nothing more than just an tool to get you across an obstacle or they are the obstacle itself, so they are an intergal part of the level design, if you remove just one of them, the level woud stop "working" at that moment, these are memoreable moments where it's awesome seeing someone playing the game, but it's one of these things that look awesome on the screen but are almost trivial to execute. Everything chains in one fluid movement-combo and I can see why this may seem impressive for others, but at long last like mentioned it bottlenecks you into one obvious dominant strategy, where you don't have to stop moving or change direction even onceIn DKC there is a lot of more freedom, enemies are there to make a passage more difficult on top, so disposing them can be utilized by a lot of different methods and is incentified, the same goes for the pathing of the levels itself. In Kaze everything is streamlined to one critical Path, it's curated and fleshed out in a sense that it gives you a pretty empowering feeling like you're one sort of an pro player. DKC uses verticality and a lot of hidden bonus paths, to create a much more satisfying exploration, which surprises even today after all these times with new findings, even if that allows you to circumvent some obstacles.Kazes exploration is streamlined to an definitive amount of collectibles. Since the game rejects lifes, "gems" are simply there to unlock an an extra ending. So it becomes an compulsion to collect them all, if you want to see everything, if not they are completely meaningless, since they only have an effect if you collect all of them.There are 2 bonus areas in every level, where you collect halfes of an green gemstone that unlock an bonus level of the current world, these are very short and always have one gimmick attached to them, but completing them all just grants you another hidden sequence in the long end, at long last there are "KAZE" letters to unlock a piece of the lore of the game at the end of every level. Any of the collectibles is tracked and add to the total completion of your save file, once you collected all of them, there is no reason getting back.What bores me of that concept is that it simply extends its playtime because of that typical "completionist" attitude so much modern indie plattformers cater to. It's nothing new and special and the pattern throughout the 4 worlds of the games is so easily predictable there is no room for surprises and wonder, it's extremely streamlined and well known by now how to design a run of the mill plattformer, so the game gives you also an collectible for playing through a stage without getting hit, this also sounds pretty difficult at first, but means nothing in a plattformer where everything is layed out in your favor.Not forgetting the bosses, bosses in Kaze are the typical "just dodge and survive for a certain amount of time and then you can hit the boss" there is a pretermined course of events who never change, this make the bosses feel indirect and results in just more plattforming, sry but there is not much difference between an autoscroller and an screen where you dodge stuff for an amount of time, on both you have no control over the pacing. There is one last piece of collectibles which are medals, you get rewarded for completing time trials on every level and before you think "oh but maybe the game challenges you by having to beat the levels pretty fast?" I have to disappoint you, the gold times, for mastering the time trials is overly generous, since the times always end on a power of 5, it's pretty obvious the times were given on guesswork, these time trials are the very opposite of the level design itself, I can imagine one of the devs plays through the level with a time of 1:38 and someone says "ah ok so we know the game pretty well, just make it 1:50 so it's reasonable for the player" if that was how it's done then it's pretty weak, best times for time trials shouldn't be "reasonable" you should think "how the hell am I supposed to beat that!?" getting more and more knowledge after every try, cause in the end the fun of time trials to me is getting the optimum out of my time, games like Crash Bandicoot or Rayman Origins demonstrate this very good. But like I said, since everything is so streamlined, even harsher time trials wouldn't be so much fun, cause you already are able to play the most optimized route from the get to, the only thing you have to consider is not making any mistakes. So basically the time trials just extend time again, by making you play through the levels 2 times, only that you now have no checkpoints.To be fair, the game also features a leaderboard, where you can compare your times with complete strangers on the internet, if that's your thing then more power to you. I never attend to online leaderboards because I'm never sure that people simply use bugs I don't know or straight-out cheat getting on the first placeIn the end unfortunately the game does nothing remarkable it straight out rips almost all the concepts from DKC  and translates them to an typical modern indie plattformer. The Wild Masks are like the animals, none of the leveldesign elements are creative and resemble DKC as well. It's fun for its runtime but it's not challenging and not replayable that much because if you are at least halfway decent in plattformersm you already mastered the game after the first minute, since everything is so "been there, done that before"It's as polished as it is predictable.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This, unfortunately, is as close as you can get to a Donkey Kong game without buying a Nintendo console. A lot is done right with this game. It has good level design, good music, a good level of challenge and a good level of versatility throughout the 5-10 hours (depending on how much you want to do). It does have some weird hit box issues where the corners of things like enemies and walls don't exist. This does lead to frustration at times, but a little perseverance will get you through it. There really aren't enough 2D platformers with this level of old school challenge to them. So, if you love the DK games, you'll definitely enjoy your time with Kaze.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks ReviewGraphics: Crisp visuals but the environments are bland and unimaginative in comparison to something like DKC. Enemy designs such as the carrots and pumpkins are not very interesting and get repetitive to look at fast. Music: The music is fine, nothing special or memorable. The music sounds similar to old school Crash Bandicoot games.Length: About 4-6 hours to collect everything. Double if you decide to do the time trials. Gameplay: The gameplay is similar to DKC, but not nearly as challenging. Solid platforming and movement feels snappy. The masks are fun and help this game standout from other platformers. More focus on the masks, perhaps the ability to collect the masks and swap between them on the fly, would have made this game even more fun. The enemies become stale very fast. However, the bosses are pretty fun. Conclusion: I had fun with it, but it is not the kind of game I would play more than once. More variety in enemy design, more focus on the masks and better music would have elevated this game closer to the level of DKC, but as it stands it is a good foundation.Score: 7.5
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is an amazing retro style platformer. If you enjoyed games like Donkey Kong Country and other similar platformers in the 90s then you should check this game out. I think this is a beautiful love letter to platforming games of the past. The graphics are gorgeous, music is great and the gameplay is SO much fun. The game has a lot of potential for speed runners as well. Also, shark mask is best mask.

_childDocuments_.review: fun classic style platformer. art is beautiful and each level offers something new. generally good difficulty (not too hard or too easy), although some parts get a bit more difficult where you have to memorize patterns, but nothing you cant beat after a couple of goes at it. seems great so far.each level you can find two bonus stages where you have different objectives (usually collecting the coins on screen) classic platformer stuff and real fun.i like the mask mechanic (although it could be used more often) reminds me of kid chameleon a bit.Edit: ok the later levels become too much speed button memorization. makes me feel like i have to play memory, rather than a fun platformer. to those that enjoy autorun platformer levels with precision memorization its still good. i lost interest at that point.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Far from perfect but a fun challenge to 100% the in game stuff.To restate the obvious, Kaze and the Wild Masks takes a lot of inspiration from the Donkey Kong Country series. I felt this reached the point of hampering it in the early goings. It felt like a not-quite-there, easier, wanna-be. But it still controlled tight, looked decent, and played great on Steam Deck. So I started going for the 100% to pad the playtime. Thankfully Kaze quickly blossoms into very much its own thing and the difficulty climbs. It has wholly unique concepts and while the inspiration is always in the backbone, it separates itself in a satisfying way. The 100% never felt out of reach all while still giving a challenge. In cleaning up some levels, it took me more attempts than I'd care to admit. I had fun for the most part.Some of the level designs will bring out the groans. Especially the endless runners. But I felt like they kept things mixed up enough. I never felt like I was being beat down with too many annoying things in a row. I never got close to quitting in any manner, rage or otherwise. I dunno, it all sorta worked just enough. Paid three bucks USD, got ten plus hours of getting everything, ran flawless on Deck out of the box, and I felt satisfied at the end. Sounds good to me!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. Must have if you like Donkey Kong Country or any platform. The style is unique, gameplay is amazing and the music completes the puzzle. I had tons of fun getting 100%. For it's price, I firmly believe that it's more than 10x worth it. I just wish this game was longer or had a sequel. Overall, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: People keep saying it's Donkey Kong Country, but sadly I've never played that one. Instead, it reminded me of both Rayman and Sonic. Gameplay is solid, really liked the power ups and boss fights. Levels themselves were fine, some more frustrating than others but enjoyable overall. The art is pretty and I had fun, which is the most important aspect. I'd have liked a bit more of story and a better game design than just selecting levels on a world map.All in all, solid game. 7.5/10 - Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I've been slowly pecking away at getting all the collectibles in this game as I go forward, but what I've played so far has been an incredible trip down memory lane. This game is incredibly reminiscent of the Donkey Kong Country games that most people have said already. There's kong letters to grab, hidden bonus stages, the blast barrels, everything lol. Even the way you pick up the jars and throw them is like Dixie kong from DKC2 and 3. If you are a fan of those games, this is a must have. It gets old school hard pretty quick, which might be a turn off for some, but I welcome that kind of challenge. And even then, there's an option to turn down the difficulty for those that want an easier time playing this game. The artwork, as well, is super beautiful. The developers definitely poured their hearts into creating all the characters and backdrops in this game, and it shows tremendously. Overall, this game is a lot of fun and feels rewarding when you get the No Damage and/or Time Attack collectibles specifically. I highly recommend anyone that is a fan of old school platformers to pick this game up, especially given that it's only $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with Kaze and the Wild Masks. I never played a Donkey Kong Country game but I think I might get into it sometime soon. If you're a DKC fan and you have $20 in your pocket, then you should try this game out. If someone like me who has no experience with the games that it's emulating, I'm sure Donkey Kong Country fans will like it too.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The game can get quite challenging in places and the platforming feels great, very smooth.Kaze imitates Donkey Kong Country as much as it can.  You're collecting 4 letters in each stage, there are bonus barrels hidden in stages.. Many of the same types of enemies.. A helicopter spin to hover in the air like Dixie Kong..  Many of the same tricks DKC uses to change up the platforming in levels are present here too, like:This list could go on and on.. and it all probably sounds great if you're a fan of that series (I am.  Big fan).  The game doesn't have as much charm all over really.  The animal buddies in Donkey Kong Country were more organic and charming than the masks that fulfil the same role here.  The cutscenes in this game I ended up skipping because they were quite basic and uninteresting.    You can hear a bit of inspiration in this, but without some good melodies it's ultimately resulted in dull background music rather than moody & melodic foreground music.There's some missing features and QoL issues when comparing this to DKC too.  ..Like how you can't change which side of a rope you are holding onto.. Or how you are normally pressing B to hover in the air, but when you're transformed into a particular form it instead does a down smash, which out of habit you will press intending to tailspin.  ..Lots of little things like that which add up to remind you that you're playing something of lower quality.The game is pretty short.  The levels themselves are pretty short too, and none of them ever open up as much as some DKC levels did.If you're unaware of it, check out .  It was made by some of the guys who did Donkey Kong Country and they even got David Wise to compose for it.  I'd say it's a better game, with a really nice hub world to explore between levels.  In fact, that's another little thing that Kaze could do better.  The map and hub screen is less interesting than that of DKC, it doesn't capture my imagination in the same way.  It feels like I'm just on a level select screen, rather than exploring a continent, wondering what that next area on the horizon is.  The Game Boy versions of the Donkey Kong Country games were quite good also, I think Donkey Kong Land 2 might actually be my favourite of the series somehow.While Kaze could be bigger, better and more charming compared to DKC, I admit that it actually gets a lot of it right as well, and to cut it some slack; DKC left some big shoes to fill.  Kaze  worth a look if you loved DKC, but don't expect it to rival the excellence of that franchise.  I hope these devs go on to make another game in a similar vein, but change their composer and try to improve on a lot of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of reviews talking about and comparing this game to Donkey Kong Country, so i decided to write a review from someones perspective who has never played DKC before.Firstly, this product feels like passion project. It is incredibly polished. From animations to sound effects and music, you can feel that a lot of work have gone in to this. So you can be sure when you are buying this, it is a finished product.Game is also bug free too, I have encountered only one issue which forced me to skip some levels. However, after I reported this to the developers, they've been really helpful and fixed it in two days. Big thanks to Spillim!I had a lot fun playing this. Masks provide a variety of different gameplay mechanics. You can try to collect everything or try speedrunning it, which has an in-game leaderboard. Only disappointing fact is that it's getting less attention than it deserves. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty and enjoyable platformer.For some reason, the first though that came to me on the first screen was "Sonic".I really enjoy the looks of the game and the music matches the style.The first level was trivially easy but I had to redo seconds of the second level six times, so I believe the game isn't easy.It has, thankfully, two difficulty settings : original (the one I've used) and casual, with more checkpoints.If you like 2D platformers, this one is a winner.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A great tribute to all classics like Sonic, Mario and DK and many other plataforms, you'll notice some waterfall stage like Green Hill Zone from Sonic, you'll also notice similarities to some rope escalator in the DK series, there will be lava stages, acid rising up stages, bonus stages and jewels to collect to open the bonus stages, it has everything to make the gameplay memorable, the story is very simple but the game is fun, the mask transforms the physics of the game you can become a bird, a tiger that can walk on the walls and jump on air or a lizard that runs only forward and you have to jump in the right time. In the end it all comes to jump in the right time you will master it but it may take some time, the process to achieve perfection that is fun. This game is worth your time. You'll feel like the first time you played DK on the SNES, or like someone who did that.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the beginning but then the game just deteriorated into autoscroller type trial and error / pattern learning and execution stuff which I did not enjoy. You just don't see what's in front of you so you just have to memorize and properly execute. No room for creativity, no room for any errors - it's tedious really. I stopped having fun playing it and then refunded it, that was basically after the final level of the 2nd world. If you do like those Donkey Kong kind of trial and error autoscroller levels, then you'll really like this. I wasn't that into those games back then either though.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The game is clearly going for the same sort of feel as Donkey Kong Country, or more specifically, DKCR/DKCTF. At its best, the game makes it about 80% of the way there. Unfortunately, the game is rarely at its best. Level design is fairly underwhelming, stage gimmicks range from meh to infuriating, bonus stages range from tedious to frustrating, and there's just a constant feeling that everything is a little off with the gameplay.As an example, pots. You can grab pots, like barrels in DKC. In those games, when you're holding a barrel and run into an enemy, you break the barrel and the enemy dies. In Kaze, you take damage and drop the pot. Another example, the bird mask. It comes with a projectile attack, but instead of being a handy straight horizontal shot, or a falling arc like Squawks from DKC, the projectile is a parabola, rising for a short time before falling. I had so many shots that flew right over enemy heads. These are little things, but there's little issues like this all over the place that hinder the flow of the game.The game is at its best and worst in the time trials. In some parts of some levels, things are designed such that if you know the level well and keep up max pace, everything will line up perfectly to weave your way through the stage. A lot of DKCR/DKCTF levels are like this too, and it's the hallmark of the latter day Rayman games (Origins and Legends). When things line up like this, time trials feel absolutely amazing. The problem is that they hardly ever are designed with this in mind, and when things don't like up? The time trials then start to feel pretty awful to run through, with a lot of levels feel like they're designed to resist you going fast instead of facilitate it.There's a lot of potential in this game, and clearly plenty of people are willing to look past the issues, judging by the reviews on here. I can't look past the issues, and I can't recommend the game as it is. I look forward to seeing what the devs do in the future, but this one is a bit of a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. A hidden gem. People usually compare this to donkey kong country, but I can see way more than that: I would dare to say that this is a happy combination of Donkey Kong Country + Sonic + Mickey and Donald Magical Quest (specially the third game).I can't help but feel 7 years old again, playing SNES  or SEGA Genesis as I was literally playing with a big smile on my face. The visuals are nice, the music is awesome, the controls feels good and it is a challenging game, but not a punishing one.I recommend this game with my eyes closed - maybe you will not find it better then the classics I mentioned, but it is clearly not trying to be better. Is a love letter to the classics.

_childDocuments_.review: DKC 2 but you play as an adorable female rabbit that uses her ears as propellers to glide around. In this holy year(of the rabbit), what more could you ask for? _childDocuments_.review: A controversial game. Cons here for somebody can be pros, and in the opposite way. _childDocuments_.review: It's a revival of the  (and therefore easier, for some) by the impecable level design and modern framerate. The levels have an amazing flow you can follow, everything is placed just at the right distance and with timing to keep you going forward. Collectibles are lined up as to teach mechanics and new movement skills. Challenge stages are well hidden and offer great training. . Of course, being like DKC, expect quite a lot of frustration while repeating parts of levels you aren't getting the gist of.The only downsides I see are: the soundtrack, while good, doesn't quite reach the DKC grade; the final chapter, levels and boss fight included, are a bit too brutal for my taste, I felt like the challenge was more about the movement flow being broken, to trick us, rather than like on previous chapters, where the difficulty was matching the skill level the devs demanded; and finally, while it only happened like 5 times in my 14 hours of playing, I swear I've gone through platforms I should've landed on, killing and angering me more than usual.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I do believe I'm in the minority here, but I cannot recommend this game to people other than those who enjoy extremely long sections of trial and error (particularly in Original Mode). I was really excited to try Kaze, but before I even finished the first world I found the game to just be an endurance test. As of writing this I have just finished the third world. This is coming from someone who has played extremely little of the Donkey Kong Country titles, which this does seem reminiscent of, so it is likely just not my type of platformer. As a massive fan of Celeste, I picked this up wanting to experience more precision platformers but I just haven't enjoyed my time with Kaze. There's clearly a lot of care put into the aesthetics and deliberation in the level design, but I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a beautiful platformer game. Graphics, enemy design, main character everything looks fantastic. It really plays like the platformers from the 90's. Controls are fluid and responsive. Controlling Kaze is easy and super responsive. Level design is really good and it offers a lot of variety. Boss fights are cool. The game is not challenging but checkpoint placement can be cruel sometimes. It offers a lot of replay value as well. In order to complete a level %100 you have to collect gems, find 2 bonus levels, find the letters that spell KAZE, finish the level without getting hit and lastly finish it under a certain time to get the gold medal. You can spend a lot of time trying to achieve these in every level. Soundtrack is nice, there are some nice tunes. My only complaint with this game is that enemies don't pose a threat. Most of them just walk back and forth. When you die in this game, it isn't because of enemies, it is because of gravity. I think enemies could have been more aggressive and agile. Other than that it is an amazing game from start to finish. A must play for the platformer game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun little game. Great artwork. Controls are simple but tight. The music is wonderful (I especially loved the ice level theme!). Level design is good and I really enjoyed how it favoured boldness. Hesitating usually meant ending up struggling more than when you are just bold and keep pushing forward; once you tap into that flow, things just gel really nicely. While I personally didn´t care that much for one of the dragon mask levels, all the rest was top notch. Beat it in about 7-8 hours.I also quite enjoyed the added extra challenge of completing the three tokens for each level (I didn't get all of them yet though :D).All in all, a really nice little platformer that harkens back to the days of playing games on the SNES.Well done PIxelHive!
