_childDocuments_.review: This is a very competently designed platforming game with 16bit-era mechanics and difficulty but coated in modern HD graphics. The game seems innocent enough at first but gets progressively more difficult with each level. For the most part it's a fair challenge with plenty of variety in its platforming mechanics, but it's also often pretty rage-inducing (just like games were back in the day!). There are also time-trial challenges, collectibles & such that add some replay value.I have two complaints. First, the auto-scroll levels (there are three, I think) represent a HUGE difficulty spike, as you have to rely on memorization and trial & error a bit too much. You'll probably die more times in these few levels than in the rest of the game combined. Second, while the boss fights are fair, they are of the kind that I don't really like whereby you have to wait for the boss to finish its move routine until you get a chance to hit it once.Anyway, if you're looking for a challenging and ultimately rewarding platformer with pleasant graphics and good mechanics, Kaze should be right up your alley. But you better have nerves of steel and a high tolerance for pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a true homage to the Donkey Kong Country platformer games with a charming graphic style. It stays true to it in every way: enemies, masks that feel like animal companions, challenging bosses, hidden bonus levels in every main level and lots of bananas... uh... crystals to collect!The real surprise for me that Kaze held is that its level design is just as good as in your favorite entry in the DKC series!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! It's mainly inspired by the Donkey Kong Country games, with a bit of Rayman Origins/Legends involved and a . The main feature of Kaze is the masks, which are similar to the animal buddies of the Country games. I personally love 3 of the 4 masks, with the exception of the dragon mask which functions like the minecart levels of DKC, which I didn't adore either. So it's clearly a matter of personal taste, the dragon mask levels are still well designed.Overall it's a really fun platformer that you can nearly 100% in a little over 6 hours (I got everything but the complete speedrunning achievements and the complete no hit achievement). _childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game with tight controls, great level design and satisfying platforming, and I absolutely recommend it to any Donkey Kong Country fan.There are some things it even does better than the modern offerings like Returns and Tropical Freeze; the titular masks with their unique controls and alternate playstyles are filling in wonderfully for the animal buddies from the SNES games, which were sorely missed in the recent DKC games. And in particular, Kaze's bonus rooms, which are all unique and clever challenges with their own goals and mechanics, eat Tropical Freeze's bland and repetitive bonus rooms for lunch.That said, the boss fights are the elephant in the room here. They're all terrible, I won't sugar-coat it. The bosses in DKC often left something to be desired even at their very best, it's true, but every last antagonist in Kaze is cut from the same cloth as Little Horn from Super Meat Boy, or Colonel Pluck from DKC Returns. You just have to survive and dodge their attacks for way too long, get in your one hit when you can, while they're briefly vulnerable, and repeat. It's miserable.But it's not enough to ruin an otherwise excellent game. If you like Donkey Kong Country, or sidescrollers in general, you should check this one out. Just be prepared for its lowest points.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit above Mix. I don't find this game interesting most of the time.Good:(1) Good character development - rabbit glides using ears, grab ropes using ears... devs put in some effort.(2) Starts easy then increasingly goes harder, focus and keep a good rhythm, a lot of the time you need to jump on multiple enemies to proceed, timing is essential.(3) If you fail too many times the game allows you to skip and win, even for a boss level.Things to be improved:(1) Machines remain the same in different islands. A change in the background art is easy to get people bored.(2) Occasionally transform into a tiger, eagle and shark, but still run like a rabbit.(3) Could use more enemies, or more detailed graphics, add some animation or cutscenes. It is not exciting.Honetely for a similar price I'd pick Witcheye, Mighty Goose, Zool Redimensioned etc.

_childDocuments_.review: An hour in and I can easily say that the latest entry in the DKC franchise is really great so far! I love how Dixie is back, though, she looks a little weird honestly... and Diddy's... a floating head, or... something. Anyway, it feels just like the old games, and there's even some visual design reminiscent of another favorite of mine, Super Mario World (I swear, those slopes are the exact same angles).You know, thinking on it more it seems like they changed a LOT of things actually. The bananas look totally different (they're all crystallized or something?), the "KONG" letters (which I was glad to see are still here!) are... I think one or two of the letters might actually be wrong? It's just not like Nintendo to miss something like that... gosh, even the Kremlings, they're all in these weird vegetable costumes!Anyway, if you liked the other games you'll surely enjoy this one! And even if you've never played any of them before... if you enjoy challenging, quick platforming, delightful, fun visuals, and a lovely, energetic soundtrack then... just give it a go anyway; I don't think you'll regret it! 😊

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions had been to say it's a charming game and reminiscent of greats such as Donkey Kong Country on the SNES. Now at roughly 30 hours into this delightful platformer, I can say it brings much more to the table or rather, as much as you'd want a game to bring with the benefit of knowing the 90's greats from hindsight. The soundtrack is top tier--the theme in particular captures an honest, adventurer's spirit that I look forward to experiencing in all kinds of remixes. The narrative is uncomplicated but enriches the game. The bosses are better realized than any of the DK bosses, the masks bring a unique spread of experiences that add a compelling flavor but more than anything else--the level design is deceptively brilliant. First, you'll likely notice that the game has several achievements which favor time trials and speed running--each level is designed to be run smoothly from start to finish and once you've mastered the timing of your jumps and enemy placements, you'll find it satisfyingly silky smooth. Then, however, there is an entirely new version of each map for folks who master the speed running mechanic--the spin jump, where you press b at the edge of a platform to spin forward and propel your jumps further and faster. Once this move is in your arsenal, you will notice there is an entirely deeper level of design brilliance to be appreciated as the levels not only run smooth if you don't employ this, but run with devilish genius once you do. The end result will leave you feeling like you've expertly threaded a storm of needles to arrive at the end of the game (Jelly Dungeon and Scalding Gears are in particular, fantastic). It's like your own skill unlocks an entirely different version of the game. This degree of design finesse speaks to a care and love that went into crafting this game that I have not seen in any recent Triple A titles and reminds me of such hits as Hollow Knight or Celeste. A joy of a game that has something for a casual player and someone who really wants to get great at it. I cannot suggest it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) Beautiful art style.2) Good level designs/music.3) Boss fights/music where my  thing in this game as they had the RIGHT balance of fun/challenging WITHOUT being frustrating to beat (along with hype music),  (see below).1)  The "ground pound" attack should've been given its  (like the "B button" on the XBox one controller) because I had many MANY  when I meant to "hover" instead of ground pounding, particularly in the "Free Fall" level where I wanted to drop down a rope and then immediately hover, but SO MANY times Kaze ended-up doing a "ground pound" instead which resulted in so many unnecessary deaths in this stage and many other stages too (Note to developers: please add a control option to give "ground pound" its own button instead of being the same button as the spin/hover button).2) Bouncing on enemies does NOT allow you to "hover" immediately after jumping on their heads and I really DISLIKED that aspect because that also led to many frustrating deaths (especially with how low Kaze bounces off their heads), not to mention the fact that bouncing really "kills the momentum" when you can't immediately hover after bouncing on the enemies heads. (Being able to "bounce+hover" would've made platforming feel so much smoother/better IMO)3) No dialogue/voice-acting during the story and no other characters that could've breathed more life into this game's universe (like for example 4) The game is very short, even after getting 100% collectibles, especially for its current asking price ($20 on PC and $30 on consoles). I feel the short length of this game and the fact that it doesn't have that much of replayability value, may not be worth that price (especially compared to  which costs $15 and has so much replayability value with 3 different characters and alternative story paths).5)  Unlike the earlier bosses in the game, the final boss in this game was a  To be more specific, my problems with the final boss fight can be summarized as follows:- The backstory of the final boss was told through "photos" you unlock in the gallery section rather than proper cutscenes, which really didn't give any "identity" to the final boss and made the final boss so forgettable and not really feel like a "true final boss" at all. Simply put, I just didn't get any sense of why should I consider this boss as the "final boss" at all without proper backstory-telling first IMO.- The final boss fight SHOULD'VE had their own "intro cutscene" before the final fight, but nope, the final fight immediately began without any context and that was both confusing as well as being very VERY anti-climactic/underwhelming for a "final battle".- Unlike the previous bosses who had awesome/hype boss music, the final boss music was TERRIBLE/BORING.- The final boss battle itself was not well-done at all and didn't utilize the power of masks very well at all (it was more "running/dodging" than actually using those masks to hit the final boss). The whole final fight felt frustrating rather than fun/epic (all previous boss fights were done way better IMO).- Even when the final boss is "dizzy" and is about to die, if you wait or don't proceed to deliver the final blow (and I wasn't even sure what to do at that point), you just "instantly die" for no reason whatsoever and I find that aspect to be quite stupid/punishing, especially after doing everything right all the way to the very end.This game is clearly inspired by the original "Donkey Kong Country" trilogy on the SNES and while this game has done well to follow in the footsteps of the Donkey Kong Country games, it honestly doesn't add or revolutionize those games using modern hardware/technology the same way  did to the "2D Sonic the Hedgehog" games which had voice-acting, great cutscenes, so many unique characters/villains, character abilities and so on. But nonetheless I think "Kaze and the Wild Masks" is a good starting point for this franchise and should this game get a sequel in the future, I hope it avoids all the "Cons" I listed above and that it should learn a few things from  when it comes to revolutionizing old beloved 2D platformers when creating a "spiritual successors" to those games in the modern era.

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks wants to hearken back to the '90s with its very DKC inspired design. From its two-hitpoint, one checkpoint, 2D-side-scrolling design to its moveset (spinning off a ledge gives you so much coyote time just like DK's roll, and you can pick up and throw some jars just like barrels) and masks (some definitely hearken back to the rideable characters in DKC), one might be forgiven for calling this game a "clone."Unfortunately, I can't say this game is nearly as fun as DKC.The big problem with this game is the level design: it quickly devolves into autoscroller after autoscroller where minor mistakes routinely give you no recourse but to simply die or lose your only precious hitpoint. Whether you're chased by a tornado or zipping down a long line of ziplines or climbing up rising ooze or stuck in that godawful autorunning mask (more on that one later), rarely after the game's halfway point do any of the levels give you a chance to simply stand still. And the sections get _so_ long after island two; dying and having to do 2 or 3 whole godforsaken minutes of the same platforming over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over because you keep hitting one in a long sequence of precise buttons a couple frames too late or accidentally got slowed down by a missed jump you think you can recover but nope there's the danger ready to autokill you... it just gets tedious. The fun disappears quick and if you truly want to stick with it, eventually it all feels like a waste of time.It becomes trial-and-error. There are some sections that genuinely require a specific set of inputs at specific times in order to get through - with literally no other way to move forward. Miss one input? You fell into a pit and have to restart the section again. This is especially the case with the autorunning mask. I genuinely don't know what they were thinking with that one; I must have died over 60 times in one of its levels just trying to figure out what it required me to do. And don't get me wrong, I do like the occasional minecart to break up the monotony. But the autoscroller gimmicks in this game are just way too excessive - and precise.I played through to the any% ending on original difficulty (and FYI my hours are messed up because I played it on deck in offline mode for a time), and I considered doing another playthrough on easy to better flesh out my opinion - because who knows, perhaps the increased health points and checkpoints would have made the game much more tolerable. And perhaps if I do end up going through with that, I'll edit my review, but for now I really don't want to touch this game again.Idk, if you really like trial-and-error, perhaps this is the game for you; but I really don't think it's fair to compare this game (or at least to compare it favorably) to DKC.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looked fun and bought it on sale without much expectations. After finishing the game 100% on original mode after 5 hours of playing I can say really enjoyed it (had some frustrating moments too).The art style was already appealing to me, small cinematics were also cool, the controls were quite tight and didn't expect the game would put up a challenge sometimes. The auto-scroller parts were... a bit annoying sometimes and felt I was being bamboozled by certain things.What I also didn't expect is that you can collect the bonuses and can leave the map just fine, so you didn't need to completely need to do the level again.There are 2 game modes, Original and Casual.Original is how it's meant to be played, casual adds more hearts and waypoints, there's nothing wrong using/switching to casual mode if you think it's too difficult :)If you love "difficult" platformers I can say this is a hidden gem...
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was a little disappointed because, at first, it feels like a reskin of Donkey Kong Country 3 and, while that's my favorite DKC game of the series, I wanted this game to have iterated upon the DKC formula and wanted to know what this game had to offer that was new.But boy did they deliver. This game is awesome, it has some new concepts and the challenge is pretty good. Also the final boss is amazing. It brings in everything that you've learned so far, even the powerups play a part in that fight. (It also has a casual mode, though I don't know how different the challenges are in that mode)The concept of the masks themselves are akin to the DKC3 animal barrels and are just as refreshing as those are in DKC3 - They break the monotony of the way you play the game and the levels are designed around them, keeping the challenge fair and fun. My favorite is the Dragon mask. It makes you feel like a badass in a rage without removing the challenge (the challenges with that revolve around platforming and smashing enemies to stay in the air).The music is great, the art is gorgeous. I wish there was more art in the game, but we get enough to get a grasp of the story and when art appears it feels like a treat.There are bonus levels (after completing in-levels bonus challenges) which are a fun extra challenge and definitely worth unlocking.The game is also great for speedrunning. I'm not a speedrunner, but when I tried going as fast as I could. things just seemed to fall into place to make speedrunning work. Also, no RNG from what I could tell. Unlike DKC bonus 'collect green bananas' barrels, green gems always spawn in the same location, so you can plan around that.Advice: Ground pounding gives you a little extra height. If you're going fast, you may just be able to reach things and platforms by adding groundpound to your jump, instead of going a bit further then backtracking and "losing time".
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The comparisons to DKC are accurate for better and worse. The mechanics are almost identical, as are the objectives, enemies and the level design. I liked DKC in the 90s, but it didn't age as well as other platformers, and its pitfalls have been carried into Kaze. It handles well and looks great, although it was unstable for me. It crashed at the end of the first level, then again when I entered a level and returned to the overworld. After it hung again when trying to quit the game, I decided to get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Donkey Kong Country 2 is still one of my favourite platformer ever to this day. I thought I could give Kaze and the Wild Masks a try and I did. This is like a 1:1 copy pasta of DKC with the same level design, but with a mix of good pixel art and wannabe Sonic (and I'm sorry, I hate Sonic Art style). Levels feel bland, the music doesn't sound catchy enough to keep me going. The parts I love about DKC 2 is how it feels surreal but still natural and smooth to play. The musics are on point and the gameplay is really responsive.In Kaze, sadly, not so much. Having the hovering option after a jump, but on the attack button... Really ? _childDocuments_.review: Allow me to cut to the chase this time. Things like graphics, music, collectibles, content etc are what you can expect when compared to other games in the genre. They’re done with care and they’re great. However, I believe that the game’s Steam page is misleading when it’s describing the gameplay and challenge. There is one mention of ‘but challenging platformer’. This is VERY underselling how challenging it is and whether it’s really a traditional platformer. It feels more like an auto-runner. You see, most levels (certainly after world 2) turn into either being A) chased by an enemy that one hit kills you B) same with a whirlwind C) moving camera that forces you to hurry up D) lava or toxic pool chasing you F) no solid ground so you have to jump on enemies to survive etc. Basically what it amounts to is you having to perfect a level, one mistake and it’s over. Levels have only one checkpoint which means you’re going to have to redo most of it regardless. The character also has to morph into one of the 4 different animals with their own moves depending on the level. One animal is a literal auto-runner, you can’t control its movement aside from jumping. Oh, and I hope you’re excited about the last boss having 4 phases with ‘platforming’ in between (aka chased by the enemy with one hit KO) and you can retry all the phases if you die, no checkpoints. It doesn’t make a difference if you do the last boss on casual except for taking one more hit I guess. I did the last 2 levels on casual and I’m not sure this is going to be enough for most people. Original difficulty feels too hardcore and I’m not sure if casual can be considered normal based on what I’ve seen. I don’t recommend Kaze even for lovers of platformers unless you’re looking for high challenge and an extreme form of trial and error. Make research about casual mode if you must. I can confirm that you can change the difficulty at any time (I wish I noticed this sooner). I won’t give Kaze 2 a try if it ever comes out. Seriously, what were they thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an ambitious "Donkey Kong Country" clone that gets most of it right. Specifically, it feels the most like the second one. This game has a nice challenge, great art, and good music, though not something I would buy the soundtrack for. If you are looking for a well made, classic experience that is fairly challenging if you go for everything, I'd get this game.Kaze is a rabbit that is going on a journey to free her friend from a ring due to a mishap. The story is told through getting the equivalent of the "KONG" tokens, and as far as I can tell are optional. There are 4 worlds and you will go from stage to stage until you hit the boss. Much like Donkey Kong Country, there are hidden bonus levels you will need to beat if you want to complete the game. And much like Crash Bandicoot, there are also time trials you can complete as extra content, though I didn't do that.The masks are basically your animal buddies from Donkey Kong Country.If you ever wanted more Donkey Kong country this is more of it. I recommend those games if you like this one, even the gameboy ones are pretty ok.-     The sprites appear to be hand drawn with that "rough" look that makes the edges look pixelated, but not like those garbage games that make the art look, worse. Think "Jazz Jackrabbit 2" with a more detail. It looks good.-     If you are only trying to get to the final boss, the game offers a reasonable challenge on the non-easy difficulty. It's very refreshing, and encourages you to play it that way. You have no lives, so keep trying until you get it.-     Finally a modern game that lets me bind a different key for ground slam. Always make ground slam and dash on different buttons if you have room for them. Excellent use of controller space.    While the controls are not as tight as say, Dead Cells, I felt largely in control at all times, where any failures were mistakes I made. The platforming is also very forgiving. Just note, you will only be able to hover when descending, otherwise the animation won't trigger.-     I wanted more story and got it, and when I wanted to focus on getting 100%, I didn't need to worry about it getting in the way. Brevity is the soul of wit. -     There were a few times were it seemed like my character's speed and angle was set rather than carried over from a previous jump, but inconsistently. You will get over it, and learn when this changes during gameplay, but be careful when bouncing on enemies.-     I don't quite remember Donkey Kong Country bosses taking a literal age to finish, and then having to start over a 4 minute fight if I got hit. The final boss I can understand, but the second boss in the game is a huge slog, and it doesn't help that the flying mask controls were not designed for accuracy. Also the second boss has the Super Mario Bros. II wind physics. Once you get the gimmick of each boss you need to do it again, 2 more times, for every boss except the last one, which has new gimmicks each phase.    Thankfully the bosses are a very small part of the game. The weakest point of the game for sure.-     In order to get the best ending, you need to get 100 gems on every stage. In order to get 100 gems on every stage, you need to unlock the extra levels by completing all the bonus rooms in every stage. So at the bare minimum, you need the bonus rooms and gems. I don't think the KAZE coins are necessary, though I did get all of those.     Finding and doing the bonus rooms is fun, collecting 100 gems is not, except on the very short challenge stages that you unlock. I don't remember DCK requiring a banana total at the end. This seems more like the Crash Bandicoot box gem concept, except I did not enjoy collecting the gems in these stages. Thankfully the collection radius is quite generous, so it's only really frustrating in like 4/30 stages. You don't need to get every single gem as there are more than 100 in each stage, but you can only miss around 4.    If you didn't get all the bonus rooms and gems before you fight the final boss, you will need to beat the final boss again to see the better ending, which I did not enjoy having to do. That boss is long and requires a lot of memorization.    Needless to say my next playthrough will be a casual one.I had fun with this well put-together game. If a sequel is made, the bosses should take a lot, and I do mean A LOT less time to complete. Other than that, I am looking forward to another game from this developer if they want to make something else. If you like "classic" platformers, buy this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a 2D platformer that goes straight to the point: the focus is not on the story, but rather on the gameplay, which is really well done and well complemented by the wonderful level design.The game takes heavy inspiration from the Donkey Kong Country franchise, so if you are a fan of that series, you should definitely check out Kaze and the Wild Masks. The gameplay feels quite similar, but Kaze still manages to be a great experience on its own right, although it is certainly a much shorter game.Kaze has a set of basic actions such as spinning to attack or using her long ears to extend her jumps, but there are also masks you can find in several levels that change up the gameplay, such as one that turns you into a bird that can fly freely, or one that turns you into a tiger, changing your normal spin attack into a lunging attack that clings to walls and lets you climb. The masks give the gameplay a good variety, and the level design itself is also great: the game is always throwing new concepts at you, making sure that things never grow stale. No level ever feels derivative or repetitive.The game also has a fairly nice soundtrack. The highlight is definitely the more ambient music that plays in certain levels and really helps complement the atmosphere. The art direction is also noteworthy; not only do the levels look great, but there is a huge variety of creative enemy designs based on vegetables, and the game keeps surprising you with them constantly up until the end. The animations are also very well done, really bringing to life all those great designs.All in all, Kaze and the Wild Masks is a great action 2D platformer that takes many cues from Donkey Kong Country and does a fantastic job at offering an experience that feels familiar while still staying fresh and doing its own thing. It may be a bit short, but it's still definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of platformers, especially DKC.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun platformer game with lots of potential, however it doesn't feel that long of a game.The game plays very well, feeling like the old Donkey Kong Country games, and even has mechanics close to the game, examples being attacking off a ledge and able to jump mid-air from it, even picking up the urns to throw at enemies.Gameplay is fairly simple to play, and good to master, you have your movement and jumps, you have a "Crash Bandicoot" spin attack, and your rabbit ears are useful for picking and throwing urns and hanging off ropes to cross areas also. Eventually you'll even earn powerups that'll give you some ability, changing how you play, from flight, swimming, wall climbing, and then for some reason, auto run. The game would also be fairy challenging, getting hit once will KO you and you respawn back at the previous checkpoint you found, there is however hearts around the map, grabbing one will give you a one hit shield of sorts, unless you get KO-ed to a one-hit KO situation. There is also a difficulty setting if the game is too tricky and can be changed on the fly mid-game. There are also collectables to find in game, yellow letters that spell out KAZE to earn some backstory, green gem pieces hidden away in challenge rooms, which can unlock a locked stage in each world hub, and lastly the red crystals, grabbing 100 each stage earns a gem which "may" have a effect on something, if you clear a stage without getting hit you'll earn a special medal for that stage, and lastly after clearing a stage for the first, if you play it again, there'll be a clock for a time trial, beat the time set for a medal for that. Again while the game is fairly challenging, its not that long of a game, there is 4 world hubs with their own end-boss and a locked gimmick stage, but even after that, it didn't take me long to beat the game casually and get all the collectables, minus not getting hit each stage and time trials, the speedrun achievement also points that out also since it can be beaten in less than 2 hours, so while its fun to play, the fun only lasts for so long, by the time you get the feeling for another stage, its near the time where your almost finished with the game.Would i recommend this game, yes, it shares alot of gameplay from Donkey Kong Country and has potential to be a great contender for platformers, but the lack of stages, or rather the length of the stages, means it can be completed quickly, but because of how fun it was, i wouldn't mind a sequel on it and hope for some future improvements should they decide to. If you are unsure about getting the game, wait for maybe a sale of 10-20%, since i had a blast playing it, and it deserves the love it can get.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in 7.5 hours on Normal mode.A very fun game reminiscent of Donkey Kong Country. You play a rabbit that inadvertently unleashes an evil doer and your bro gets their spirit trapped inside a jeweled ring. So it's now up to you to save Carrotland.There aren't many mechanics if any. Cept for maybe weighted platforms, which I didn't really care for. Oh, and the on and off light switches.My favorite moment was the level with air currents that blew you up and you can control your height with your hover.All the art is very nice to look at. The animations on Kaze and everything else is great, and gives plenty of silliness.While you go through 4 different lands that have a theme, they don't really. Once you enter the stages, they will vary. So if you enter the snow land, you won't encounter all snow or ice themed levels. You actually encounter lava filled landscapes, and dark ruins filled with brambles. I found it a little odd to be honest. They had the assets to create perhaps 2-3 more lands to actually make every land be it's own theme. I have a feeling they had to cut a lot of bosses, and thus we have this sort of mashup. I also hazard a guess that they also ran out of time or budget. I do miss a map screen to select your levels. Instead, you walk on a flat straight path to select the level with cute dioramas.The music can feel a bit...I don't know, generic? It has it's charm and it is not bad music but I wasn't jamming out to any particular track. The music is fine. I suppose I was spoiled by the legend, David Wise.A simple platformer but still great and plenty of challenge. Definitely pick this one up. I'm sure if the dev team had a bigger budget and more time, they would give you the full adventure with more lands, levels, mechanics, and bosses. Right now, it's a quick polished adventure.I recommend this game because there was a lot of love put into it. The quality of the controls, levels, and style is top notch. I feel calling it a clone is in poor taste because it stands to be the best DKC "clone". Who doesn't want more different flavors of DKC platforming in their life?

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Indie Platformers I have ever played alongside Celeste, Shovel Knight, and A Hat in Time. Above all else, this is a love letter to classic Donkey Kong Country while also taking some inspiration from the new DKC games as well a dash of Rayman and Mega Man for it's heart mechanic and some level gimmicks respectively. While I don't have too much experience with the original DKC Trilogy, I still adored this game. The level themes were unique and interesting, the music was very solid, the controls were responsive, and Kaze's abilities are super fun to use. However, there isn't much content here. I've already gotten all the collectibles and achievements and I've only played for about 10 hours. I'd still highly recommend the purchase even for the full $20, especially for those hardcore DKC fans, but the shorter length may be a turn off for some.

_childDocuments_.review: A must play game for any fans of the DKC series. It's pretty much every Donkey Kong Country game mashed together, with a little dash of Rayman Legends. Although it is an indie game after all, so don't expect the same level of quality or quantity of the games it was inspired by.  As of writing this review, I 100%'d the game, then played it again for a speedrun achievement. - The controls are super tight and responsive, probably the only time in my life I have ever   wished for more water levels because the controls are that good. - Level design is super fun. Mechanics and level gimmicks are well utilized and the difficulty   curve is perfect. The game never gets so frustrating that you want to rage quit, but there are   some parts that gave me a hard time.- Graphics are pleasing with a cute indie pixel aesthetic and great animations to match. - The music doesn't particularly stand out, but it's does a serviceable job. Kaze and the Wild Masks is a wonderful little platformer that more than satisfies my cravings for another DKC style game. I happily recommend this game to any fans of 2d platformers.

Wouldn't be so critic yet just with that, but the game makes you believe you have these awesome power ups as mask: They are not power ups, they are sections of the game forcing you to change playstyles (imo this didn't need the fanfare the masks bring, since when they appear the level is specifically designed for you to use the new moveset, so you don't feel powered up at all). _childDocuments_.review: Gliding in air requires you to hold attack, instead of jump. You have to hold the attack button to hold onto a rock and release attack to throw, instead of just pick it up with attack and then press attack again to throw. Ground pound is down and attack and for some reason feels wrong to me. These feel terrible and there are no options to change them. It seems there was some sort of push to use only two buttons, even though they are copying a game that had 6 buttons main buttons available to it. Other than that, moving around feels good.Some of the levels are terrible. The game has an overworld where you pick what level to play, but it's linear. This means you have to play and beat the bad levels to continue. The game could benefit from a branching overworld where the more controversial levels could be optional paths.The art is great. However, the game feels a bit too much like a copy-paste of Donkey Kong Country, without anything new. The main character is replaced with a Sonic character and the enemies are replaced with fairly forgettable vegetables. It otherwise has extremely similar levels, game mechanics, enemy types/ai, etc. You spin instead of roll, you collect gems instead of bananas, you collect KAZE letters instead of KONG letters, you wear masks instead of ride on top of animals, you shoot around on sling shots instead of barrels, you throw rocks instead of barrels, you ground pound with your butt from the air instead of slapping the ground with your hands, etc. This would be fine if there was something unique about the game or if they just improved every aspect of the game, but the levels aren't better, the music is worse, and the story seems to have been thrown in as an after-thought. The art is really the only thing going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly competent implementation of an uninspired game design.It might be exactly what it's supposed to be and that just happens to not be my cup of tea...After all, the game design seems mostly inspired by the Donkey Kong SNES games, which I find completely joyless. I'd rank this game well above DK, but still not really my thing.More specifically, I don't enjoy the movement mechanics and overall level design. It feels like it's a dozen or so tweaks away from actually feeling good to control.The levels have recurring readibility issues, like low contrast brambles and slippery walls that you can easily miss until it's too late.The whole game feels slow, to a sometimes frustrating degree, but sometimes you hardly have any time to react, such as when you get blindsided by offscreen projectiles whilst in a low-agility mode (swimming, flying). Other than that, I'd probably have chosen to play most of the game at about 125% speed.The main praise I have is for the polished presentation and flawless implementation.Overall, even though it's not bad or anything, I don't really recommend playing this game unless you're positive it's for you.If you don't really enjoy it at the start, you probably won't enjoy the rest either. It doesn't really pull an "it gets good" on you or anything later on.

_childDocuments_.review: // H // O // T // : // R // U // N //// R // E // V // I // E // W // S //Guest Review by GameGerryIt's 1994, you're 12 years old, you awaken, your sheets soaked with sweat, it's 4 AM. You're in your room, but it's not your room - is it? To find some semblance of comfort, you look for your poster for Super Mario 3, only to see a poster for a game called Extraordinary Merino now on the Nitro Enjoyment System. WHAT IS THAT? Oh well, who cares, Donkey Kong Country is coming out soon, you think. You go downstairs to find the VHS tape you got in the mail that was a Donkey Kong Country promo - it's gone. WHERE IS IT? You call your friend Bart, he answers the phone - "BART!" you say - he says "WHO? my name is BRANT!" Okay whatever. You ask Brant if he's still excited for Donkey Kong Country coming out. He says "What in the HELL is that???" You start describing it to him, the barrels, the bonus stages, the banana power ups. Brant quickly interrupts you - "Oh sounds like you are describing KAZE, we watched the promo for that last week when it was delivered to your house on Beta Max tape." WHAT IN THE HELL? You quickly hang up the phone and go to the entertainment center, digging though what you now realize are Beta tapes. You find a brightly colored one with the text "KAZE" emblazoned on the side - you insert the tape. Lo and behold there it is some BS knock-off of Donkey Kong Country with vegetables and some rabbit??, and for some reason the people in the video are really hyped for it. What system does it say it's for???? Sega? SEGA GENESIS? You look under the TV, and there it is - the only system you own, a Sega Genesis. How can this be???? You look for any sign of your NES or SNES - they aren't there, just some brick called Nitro Enjoyment System. What is that? You remember the poster, NO! It can't be. You run to the front door and open it, there is a newspaper on the ground. You look at the headline on the first page "NITRO ENJOYMENT OUT OF BUSINESS" - You scan the article - Nitro Enjoyment never recovered from the Extraodinary Merino flop they released 6 years ago and following the release of their Laserdisc attachment, they folded. Sega has reined supreme, Nintendo doesn't appear to exist. You run back into your room and slam the door, in bed you are upset, but then realize - at least you can still play Sonic! Then you look on the back of your door - a large poster looms with the title SANIC is back in SANIC THE BULLDOG 3 now with music from Vanilla Ice. You close your eyes, hoping to wake from this nightmare, but you never do - this is hell. TL:DR - Kaze Kong Country - do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The description says its 90's inspired game and frankly it belongs into the 90's. In the modern days it's simply boring. You have normal movement (no run, no dash), you have attack button (kinda like a dash but not really) and then you can slowly hover down after a jump. You run around in levels collecting gems for the sake of collecting them, they don't seem to serve any purpose other than "you collected them all great". Enemies are one hit kill, both they die from one attack but so do you. And getting hit by an enemy restarts the level. Nothing else to say because that is the whole game. YAWN!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: "Dad, can we buy Donkey Kong Tropical Freeze?""We have Tropical Freeze at home."This is the Tropical Freeze we have at home.  It's honestly not a bad game, but it's clearly trying to be a non-Nintendo version of that game that the comparisons are impossible to not make.   And this just can't compare to that perfection of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I can see how this can be compared to DKC, but there is a glaring difference. I actually wanted to finished all the games in that series. This game, I couldn't even be bothered to finish the first world. We have this issue in gaming where we don't look at a game for it's own merits. Don't spend your money and just go play DKC like you actually want to instead of looking for a DKC hole filler.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Although not quite innovative per se, it does manage to excel at doing things.To start things off, the game just "feels" great from the get go. The controls feel great (What do you know? The devs already fixed Air Smash input just one day after my review!), the visuals are great, and the audio is great.I love how the levels were designed, it feels like every level has its own "gimmick" and with the Wild Masks, they never feel boring. I also love the devs' decision to remove Lives.The bosses are not that special, they are very "meh", but the final boss is really something, feels like a "final exam" where you need to master most of the games' fundamentals to beat. Although, it does feel like it depends on memorizing the pattern and does contradict the devs' philosophy behind removing Lives (to respect the player's time by not letting them repeat the same things over and over again).Main story is about 3-5 hours long, but it has decent replay-ability value that spans it more through Time Trials, Collectibles and Bonus level. Challenging game, in a good way - there is no "annoyingly" hidden Collectibles and more often than not, failure seems to be in the player's control and never feels frustrating but encourages you to learn and try something else, very addictive!Oh yeah, pretty cool narrative behind the story-telling too. Basically the story is told in pictures that you unlock when collecting a level's K-A-Z-E letters. Love the mystery feeling behind it and how it is open to interpretation.People who come in expecting a "Donkey Kong Country"-ish game will not be disappointed, however, there's much to Kaze and the Wild Masks than that and it certainly does have its unique identity. Definitely worth your time and money - there is no going wrong with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: At this day and age, NO GAME should be pixelated! And for the price! Yeah, got it on sale. But still don't want that!I grew up with pixelated games, don't wanna go back. The game probably is good. But sorry, not going back to that format. They could of done a none pixelated version(Cuphead). Why is pixelated games popular? Don't know , maybe peoples vision going bad and can't tell the difference. By the way, I love sidescrollers( Ori). Just not pixelated. And not above $5 for it being so. Maybe it would sell better for the real asking price not pixelated, I would of paid full price! Again Ori.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: meh. if you like DKC or Rayman, just pick it up, the graphics and music aren't quite as good but it makes up for it with its polish and there are a few original ideas here and there. overall you could do a lot better with other modern platformers like "Celeste" or "The end is Nigh". If you've finished those, why not try something older that you haven't played. I would exhaust everything before recommending this game, because it doesn't really do anything new to even justify its existence. what it is, is competently made. that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great well-rounded platformer that has tight controls for precision moves and unique mechanics to keep the experience interesting the whole way through.  There were some frustrating parts that made me put the controller down for a break, but I was always able to come back and overcome the challenges with persistence.  The level design gets tough, but not soul crushing kaizo hard, and the option to switch out to a more casual mode is a welcome one.  The story, art, and music all show a steady high standard of quality, it all left me very satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Dunno about this one. It strikes me as somewhat overrated. It's certainly fun in parts, but even the "casual mode" becomes annoyingly, grindingly hard after the initial world. (There are only four short worlds, though.) Graphics and music are okay (not amazing); there's no real storyline. And every enemy and mechanic in the game is borrowed (plagiarised) from Donkey Kong Country: it's truly shameless. So even if you like DKC you might find this rather too unoriginal to be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game! It has quickly become one of favorite platformers! :) The controls are really tight, every gamestyle really fun, the music's nice as well as the beautiful artstyle! There are several things you can collect, all of them really fun without ever being too frustrating.I also love the difficulty of the game. It's very challenging but never frustrating (well... two or three levels might be, but that's the smallest problem), absolute every level is fun in fact, and especially with the well-made controls (and I'm playing with the keyboard!)I'd absolutely love to see more from Kaze! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an extremely competent spiritual successor to Donkey Kong Country. The game starts out rather slow and simple, but gets really engaging a little ways in.I'm disappointed that the "Wild Masks" aren't incorporated more strongly. To continue the Donkey Kong Country reference, they're more like the dedicated animal buddy stages than the persistant upgrades I was hoping they would be.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim, thinking for the longest time it was a Klonoa spiritual successor. Surprise to me: It's a Donkey Kong Country type game! It's clear there is a lot of wonderful art, animation, and effort in this game. I love it! The only issue is the game can rely a bit too much on trial and error, and the secret areas can be a bit too hidden at times. Do not feel ashamed if you are a seasoned platformer veteran and need to use casual mode!Bravo to the creators of this game! It is lovely!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth getting on sale. A bit too short for a full cost purchase.Game has great music, lots of style- even though it's clearly DKC inspired (which is a good thing). Some levels can be a bit difficult but that comes with old school style platformers. Most importantly, the levels are fun to play through and the controls are tight enough for those levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you're tired of waiting for Ubisoft to make another Rayman game, Kaze is the answer to your prayers. While distinct enough to be its own property, it takes clear influence from the aforementioned neglected franchise as well as Crash Bandicoot and Donkey Kong Country. Kaze is a beautiful fusion of those series that's approachable to casual players while not being so easy as to bore a more experienced 2D platformer veteran. Completing all of the Time Trials, beating every level Hitless, and getting the achievement for beating the game in under 2 hours were all fair and satisfying challenges. It's also not too long, as a casual playthrough will only take 5 or 6 hours, and getting every achievement shouldn't take much longer than 10 - 15 hours.It's a good game. You should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good challenging platformer with nostalgic elements resembling Donkey Kong and the 2D Sonic The Hedgehog games. I appreciated the sense of completion I got from collecting all the types of gems. It has the retro level of difficulty found in the SNES Donkey Kong games, which can be a positive or a negative depending on how you feel about it. The boss battles are three hit mechanics with three stages of challenging sequences, so I spent considerable time on them, but the repetition was not boring by any means. I also enjoyed the music and how well it fits the movement of the level. A speed run "mode" is built in for those who like that, but I've not tried it myself. I really appreciated the vibrant color choices and the hand drawn art and animation styles.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best 2D platformer available, it brings the good old 16bit feelings. A lot of negative reviews are complaining about the difficulty, but there's nothing wrong with it, the difficulty is on point, a good challenge if you want no-hit + time trials medals. It's a good game to have 100% of achievements.The only annoyance in this game is the huge amount of auto-scroller/auto-runner.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bursting with charm and quality. It plays just like the classic Dkc games and i mean that in the best way possible. The sprite art is detailed and very expressive, and there are some nice tunes. I would say that 25 dollars is a little steep but I think if you are a big fan of challenging 2d platformers this is a must try.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A game inspired by the Donkey Kong Country saga. It is really good and short. It will take a few hours if you want to 100% the game, but not a lot. Some levels are hard, but in general, the difficulty is not very high. The art and music are not to my taste. Overall, it's a great game, and I did not find any technical problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, like everyone said its a lot like Donkey Kong Country. The platforming and jumping is tight, although sometimes you'll go through platforms so the collision detection and hitboxes could be a bit better. Also the game really could use a double jump, and not being able to jump after landing on an enemy is kind of dumb as well. Its pretty fun, and some of the masks are cool, but later levels become stupid runner sections (laziest game design ever) and ziplines, rising lava, tornado chases, etc. Instead of good platforming its just following preset button pressing and its tons of stupid trial and error sections, especially with way too many instant death pits. There only being 1 checkpoint all levels could be better as although the levels aren't long some of the checkpoints and end of levels are far apart, forcing you to replay a decent amount. Only getting 2 hits total could have been better, should have been 3, although they do have casual thankfully so if you have to switch you can. The final boss is terribly designed, breaking the 3 attack rule and having no checkpoints but 5 different multi-part stages, forcing a ton of trial and error and repetition. The game is also pretty short, but it does have a great art and visual design. Collectibles are basically useless and theres almost no story at all. 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun DKC-alike! Quite short and sweet but has the extra collectables and stuff if you want more of a challenge! It's nice that it includes an easier mode for people who don't want to experience torture (like me!)Very nice sprite art and decent music. Quite an easy recommend if you're a fan of platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Not even with rabbit ears you can shut your eyes hard enough to not see the homage this is to the Donkey Kong Country Series. You have a Stop&Go Station, Vulture Culture, Trick Track Trek, Target Terror, Toxic Tower and many many more. Add to this the perfection that is the music and level design and this is indeed modern DKC which lots of people like me loved back in the day. The worlds and levels look pixel sharp, almost all the music (especially boss music) is a instant banger and the namesake wild masks you play as all alter the gameplay significantly, causing each level to be something special. The game also impressively shows what happens to the greens your kids don't eat. Show them the enemy designs of this game if they won't eat their veggies ;-)It's not handholdy though, so you should be prepared to get your ass kicked by some levels. Especially if you want 100% and beat each level no-hit. The game does have some minor minor flaws, so this is some bickering on a very high level:All in all, if you look for a beautiful (for eyes and ears), fun and challenging 2D platformer, look no further.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Fair to say this is an homage to the Donkey Kong Country series that stands on its own. It's a platformer where you complete 8 stages per area while collecting crystals (>= 100), completing 2 challenge rooms or spell out the word KAZE by collecting its letters. There are transformative power ups that give you flight, swimming and wall climbing / dashing abilities that are used on a few stages. Heck, remember Bramble Blast and the barrel sections? Hehehe.... they're here too!I haven't encountered any mine cart sections yet... yet! They're probably here somewhere.It's been a good time so far. The bright visuals, mellow audio tracks and snappy controls make this an easy recommendation for people looking for something similar to DKC. Even if you're new to the DKC style games this one hasn't been demanding on my platforming skills so far so don't worry about it being overly difficult. Maybe it picks up later? I'll update the review once I'm done.Update - Completed the game in 6.4 hours including all collectibles and bonus stages. There were "mine cart" levels in the game! Looking forward to Pixel Hive's future work!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of wish there was more of this game. Played for just over 50 hours and i've gotten all but the speedrun trophy. By that i mean, i had a lot of fun playing it and wanted to do everything there was to do it the game. It's just a charming, if a little basic 2D platformer that really wants to give you the classic 16 bit experience. One criticism i'm willing to give is the hit boxes on the barrels are horrible. Expect to die a lot from phasing through the edges of barrels. All in all, fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If I could leave a "sideways" thumb here I would.One one hand, the overall game play, graphics and level design are enjoyable.On the other hand, most of this is ruined by an overabundant use of "run quickly from left to right through the entire level" mechanics. It got old quick back in the day and it's even more stupid now. One or two levels spread out over the entire game would be acceptable but the use of this game play becomes more frequent as you progress and one of the special "masks" you acquire also uses this mechanic.To the developers: Use this mechnic sparingly, if at all the next game. Let your players take their time and enjoy exploring your beautifully crafted levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun platformer game which nailed a lot, if not all aspects of a great platformer game. Lots of versatility with the masks which keeps the gaming experience fresh.It´s a pretty quick game to beat, even if you collect all the optional stuff. The difficulty is adjusted really nice (I played the harder recommended difficulty) and advancing to the next save point feels rewarding. Some of the hidden secrets we´re a bit annoying to find (I can imagine some people enjoy the finding experience) but most of the time they were positioned really well.Small spoiler: Also I would have enjoyed a hidden true final boss after collecting all the stuff, but that didn´t happen. :/Still, If you like platformers, you just can´t go wrong with this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid platformer but it isn't particularly exceptional. I like the art style and art work but personally I'm not huge on any of the actual designs of the characters or enemies. There's nothing wrong with them it just isn't anything that really appeals to me. The music is nice but not overly memorable. There are four worlds with 6 main stages, a bonus stage and a boss level. To just play through any of these isn't very difficult, but trying to complete them will pose a minor challenge. I think it would be hard to recommend this game at $15 given how little content there really is but on sale for $5 or less it is worth your time if you are interested in platformers at all. I definitely had enough fun with this game that I'm not upset that I played it but there are also a lot of other things you could play that would be better overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a beautiful love letter to Donkey Kong Country and well worth the price tag to platformer enthusiasts.  The music does an excellent job even when comparing it to the soundtracks from the DKC series.  The art is cute, fun, and well done.  It brings all the elements you’d expect with time attack mode, hidden bonus stages, 3 types of collection challenges per level, a challenge per level to take no damage, and challenging boss fights.  Many levels are challenging and give you a fulfilling sense of accomplishment when you overcomes them.  I look forward to going for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice platformer in really beautiful 16bit pixel art. The challenge is correct, the musics are groovy, and I really like the sounds, especially the very funny voices of the evil vegetables!A little too bad the mask transformations are just possible in some levels, levels that are especially designed for these forms, and of course the transformations can't be avoided. So, if you're looking for a Kid Chameleon vibe, it's not here.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: it follows Donkey Kong formula a lot, yet for some reason it s not as fun as Donkey Kong. Difficulty is not arranged properly some stages although late in game a breeze and some unnecessarily "challenging". I have no issues with challenge you can look at my profile and see but this game does not offer a good challenge IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I definitely would recommend this to anyone looking for a cute, challenging platformer.  Sometimes I found some parts tediously difficult to repeat in their entirety, but the level design is great!  This game was so worth it on discount.  It's great to play on Steam Deck too!  Good short fun that doesn't overstay its welcome!  And you can always try to 100% it if you're looking for an even bigger challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good platformer that really wants to be Donkey Kong Country. For the most part it does a really good job. It stumbles with a few things though. It would have been a solid B tier platformer if it came out back in the day.It's very tough, which is a good thing and it requires a lot of skill. Finding collectables takes the gameplay to the next level.Where it stumbles is there is a fair amount of trial and error and having to memorize levels. This isn't just for the collectables either. Sometimes just getting through a level feels more about knowing what to do and when than actually doing something difficult. The check points are also sometimes weirdly placed. You might spend a long time never seeing one, or you might stumble across one almost immediately. There seems to be no rhyme or reason to their placement sometimes.Still my gripes are minor. They're just things Donkey Kong Country did to a much lesser extent. Those games focused more on skill. But that's not to say this game doesn't require skill; it definitely does.Still trial and error gameplay was a big part of the genre back then, particularly B tier platformers and below, so I guess they nailed it if that's what they were going for. But I know some people might be disappointed. Still a good game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best 2D platformers I've played as a seasoned platformer player. The diificulty is just right (played on original difficulty), the level design is stellar and the controls, even if simple, feel really on point.This might be one of the few games where I've not only done but looked forward to doing the two things that I most hate in videogames in EVERY STAGE: time attacks and no-hits. I hope this is enough proof of how good it feels to play Kaze.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very much underrated 2D plat former game. Controls are tight and button input reaction are all immediate and precise. Throughout the game, you will able from time to time put on different mask that changes your entire game play.There are a total of four different masks namely the eagle mask, shark mask, tiger mask and the dragon mask. Each offering a different skill set to master when you don on the mask. A fun and challenging game out there. Definitely deserve much much more love from players out there that enjoys a decent platformer game. My only complaint is the last boss, which is freaking tough as hell. There are a lot of instant death with this boss and it is divided into four parts. One wrong move and you will report to heaven. If you think some of cuphead bosses are are tough, wait till you fight the last boss of this game. Nevertheless this game is still highly recommended...!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it until I got the dragon mask. Now I hate it. started off strong too. well others will feel differently and that's fine. I recommend because if your'e skills are sharper than mine then you will enjoy the fast,unfair and BS dragon auto scroll nonsense. it's a shame too because the game is gorgeous and looks amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The developers clearly played a lot of the 16-bit era Donkey Kong Country games and it shows given how much this game was inspired by them, right down to nailing the feel of the tight precision controls and really good level design that compliment the controls. No two levels feel the same even if some of them do borrow elements from other levels. All that and more makes for some of the best side-scrolling platforming I've experienced in a very long time.Each level has four KAZE letters to grab and two bonus stages for those seeking to fully complete the game, the former unlocking bonus artwork and the latter unlocks extra bonus levels to play. Getting at least 100 small pink crystals in a level also grants a big pink crystal for that level and while not needed to finish the game, getting them all unlocks the true ending. Time trials are also present when replaying levels a second time with bronze, silver and gold times to beat similar to Crash 3.While the game can be quite difficult at times, limited lives are not a thing in this game so you will eventually beat it if you keep trying. If it still becomes too much for you, an optional Casual Mode adds extra checkpoints and allows one extra hit point to make things a little easier. Unlike other games that include a similar feature, the game never asks if you want to turn it on if you're having trouble nor does it completely break the entire game design when enabled.If you don't have a Switch but still want a game that plays and feels like Donkey Kong Country, or you're already a big fan of those games and are looking for other games like it, I'd strongly suggest giving this one a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art, great sound design, fun levels... What's not to love?Personally, I found the difficulty just perfect (played on the original mode). The game offered some challenge, but it never made me feel frustrated. With some practice, all levels and achievements are doable. I guess "hardcore platformer gamers" might find the game too easy, but for a casual gamer like myself, it is well-balanced. Big thumbs-up!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A 2d sidescrolling platformer of the same lineage as Donkey Kong Country that has just as much ingenuity and challenge. Kaze and the Wild Masks delivers a variety of levels and mechanics that do not overstay their welcome. In particular, I loved the auto-run levels that forced you to jump, double jump, and dive bomb through some truly hair-raising obstacles. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy platformers like Sonic and Mario, then you'll enjoy Kaze and the Wild Masks. Some levels are definitely more challenging than others if you consider finding all of the KAZE letters, secret portals, and Gems; I completed each of these tasks for every level. Overall, I wouldn't consider this game a difficult platformer given the target audience, but it is still fun to play. I got this game for my daughter and myself.I'd recommend this game to any platformer fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many games i would deem perfect but Kaze and the Wild Masks is one of them.It is heavily inspired from Donkey Kong and has the same level of polish you would expect from a Nintendo game. While it doesn't hide its inspiration, it manages to be distinct by adding tons of unique mechanics.Every level is memorable and has its own theme going on. Collectibles, rushing through levels that flow like butter, unique boss fights and so on. From its artstyle to its gameplay, it is filled to the brim with charm and you can clearly see how much love and passion was put into making this game.Its criminal how little its known. Everyone should play this game.I will keep an eye on this developer for their future games. I strongly recommend you to play Kaze, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Has a staggering amount in common with Donkey Kong Country, This works both in favor and against it. There are some cool ideas and mechanics explored with powers, the controls are tight and responsive and levels can be fun to playthrough. In a lot of ways it even improves on DK with instantly repeatable challenge stages. Something about it though doesn't feel the same to me and I found myself becoming uninterested in the levels and wondering how many I have left. It just lacks the cool environment changes, soundtrack quality and art design that made DK so good. Still, a solid experience if you want a platformer and it could just be me.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, engaging platformer that takes a clear inspiration from Donkey Kong Country while adding its own twists. Kaze is very fun to control, with a rather familiar helicopter twirling move and a downwards bounce that feels very satisfying to use, along with a forward attack that keeps your momentum which feels incredible to use. The masks also add fun new abilities - think of them like the Animal Barrels from DKC2/3 where you get transformed entirely for the rest of the level. This style works great for the game, it allows the levels to be hand-crafted around the mask's abilities and leads to much more interesting level designs than we would have otherwise.Not quite as unforgiving as some of the more sadistic challenges that the DKC series has to offer, but it's plenty difficult in its own right and should provide a decent but fair challenge for most players. I died plenty of times but generally checkpoints are well-placed and most challenges are able to be conquered after you realize your mistake. The game generally flows extremely well, which is something that matters a lot for a game that takes its influence from one of the greatest game series ever in terms of flow. Overall I'd definitely recommend this game, it's really fun and definitely scratches the DKC itch
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Now that i've completed it, it's time to review it. First off this game is a fast platformer, rarely does it make you wait too long. It's levels just like it's worlds, are short and sweet. Getting 100 gems, the two challenge pieces, not getting hit and the timer are all fun objectives.The only complaints that i have about this game are very small. The unlockable 7/7 levels shouldn't have a timer, they're more focused on being a test of skills, so not getting hit is enough. The timer achievment is weak and the speedrunner achievment is too hard, unless you know it beforehand. Lastly the last boss had good platforming, but the transformations segments were a little too easy(tiger was good tho).Now for the praises, the level variety is good, you don't tire yourself of playing this game. The masks are fun power ups, they change the pace of a level and none felt uneeded. The difficulty is just right, getting gold medals on all levels is very attainable, most levels i had at least 10 secs before gold expired. The dash jump out of platforms and dash comboing off enemies was excellent. The dash is very fluid and stops when you expect it to, the air movement is top notch as well. Backgrounds were pretty and fit the levels. The music was nice and i didn't get tired of it. The minimal story did more than enough. Overall if you like platformers, you'll love this game. It can be short, if you don't try to do everything it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a really good old school styled platformer that not only captures the feel and look of old platformers, it also improves on it. Now what is the story. Two young adventurers Kaze and her friend/brother Hugo go to an old temple in search of a powerful relic, but the moment they find it tragedy happens. Hugo’s body and soul is sealed in the relic and an ancient evil that was trapped in it escapes, now it's up to Kaze to not only save her brother, but also stop the evil Typhoon from conquering the land with his vegetable army.So then the likes, the gameplay is really good it's hard but fair with the game starting off easy, but as you progress it introduces new challenges that makes it hard, the game also varies up the platforming not just with difficulty, but there are also these masks that give you certain powers like the ability to fly or the ability to cling to walls which help diversify the platforming.The pixel graphics are really good not only is it nice to look at and has a great use of color; it also has this nice cartoony feel that makes it feel like this would get a cartoon spin-off if this game was in the 90’s. The levels are really good each one quite diverse with plenty of interesting scenery that not only makes you want to stop and stare, but even explore. The enemy and bosses are really good each one with their own unique design, I also really love the fact that all the enemies are vegetable/ fruit /plant-based as they each one had some unique looks and animation.The story is good while it is your simple stop the bad guy story there's plenty of these little letters that if you get them all it unlocks a story that tells how all this came to be, I found it quite interesting as it had a Kung Fu Panda sort of vibe to it, especially with the main villain Typhoon. The characters are quite adorable looking, even those we don't really know much about them as this is a simple platformer, but there is still a little bit in the story that we get hints of their personality.The music is really good with plenty of great tracks to listen to that just really compliments the game. There is also plenty of challenges you can do which were are quite good, even if they are a little frustrating, it's hard but still fair. Also I like how all the achievements are quite easy to get it just takes time and practice even the hardest achievement the speedrunner can be completed if you played the game enough times.So then the dislikes, the game can be a little short if you're not going after any of the achievements and the price is a bit to high I mean practically $20, again if you're not going to go after all the achievements like I did the game and the price does seem a bit too much. I also would have liked that the game would have a few more bosses to fight instead of the four we have.Now then with all that done Kaze and the Wild Masks is a really good old school styled platformer that not only captures the feel and look of old platformers, it also improves on it, it has really good gameplay, really good graphics and a good story. So I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of old school Platformers this is definitely for you, I only recommend that you wait till it's on sale so you can save a couple of bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and enjoyable 2D side-scroller/platform game that fans of old school games like Sonic the Hedgehog would enjoy. You adventure through a variety of levels that include all kinds of different enemies and obstacles which Kaze navigates by using her two basic abilities - hovering (using her ears) and a spin-attack to defeat foes (many vegetable-type foes, like carrots!) You also get to use Wild Masks at points throughout the game (an eagle, tiger, shark, and some kind of dragon or lizard) all of which give you added and different abilities. The game world consists of 4 'worlds' (Forgotten Grove, Frozen Mountains, Toxic Tide, and Carrotland) each containing between 6-7 levels that are varied, colourful, and accompanied by a decent soundtrack. Within each level, there are a number of collectables for you to get which opens up 'bonus' stages throughout the game. There are two play modes - Casual and Regular. Casual gives you checkpoints and the option to pass a certain section if you are really struggling with it, but even this mode can be quite challenging. (You'll likely die plenty of times!) It has a good replay factor too, as you'll probably want to go back and get all of the items you missed first time around to try and 100% the game. There are also Time Trials available to test your speediness. This is a great game, if on the short side in terms of length, but I would definitely recommend it to anyone who loves a 2D platformer. It's fun to play, challenging but not frustrating, and is visually enjoyable. I give it a solid 7/10.
