_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this as someone who enjoys retro throwbacks and I was a little worried at first about the difficulty but I have been extremely impressed and delighted by the curve. The level design is impeccable, I especially love the Dragon levels. It's already looking like one of my GOTYs. Kaze's design and the aesthetic alone really appeals in a way I can hardly describe but I am obsessed. This game is Sonic the way Sonic should have been done and a great way to experience Sonic as an adult or even if you just missed out. This game keeps me wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like DKC and collectathon type of games you'll love this. It's got the level design and aesthetic/music of DKC and the combat reminds me of Crash with the spin attack. There are a few collectibles in each level to get including a crystal that you get in 2 pieces via Sonic esque bonus stages, letters of the main characters name lifted straight from DKC, collecting 100 gems, and time trials so there's plenty of fun stuff to go back and get after you beat the main game. Which is one of my few problems here, the game is very short, for a $20 indie platformer I usually want around 6-8 worlds and about a 4-6 hour single player and I beat this game in a little under 4 hours, but I still want to go back and 100% it sometime so with than included there should be plenty for the money's worth here I just think it would have been cool if there were a little more than 4 worlds. Great game overall though, controls feel smooth and the level design is good, bosses are fun, and the mask mechanic that alters how you play each stage is unique and great to use. This game is kind of a nice mish mash of other classic games in 1 and I recommend it highly, 8/10 from me
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember when I added this game to my wishlist. It was in 2018 and to be honest, I cannot remember how I learned about it. What drew me in was the art style, how colorful the presentation was and the concept of the masks seemed cool; also for my nostalgia, the copter ears reminded me of Jazz Jackrabbit 2 and it was another plus for that.The gameplay is very fluid, featuring tight and responsive controls. Not once was I feeling cheated when I messed up a jump or platforming section.The masks, as I said, are a cool concept which brings new, fun and engaging ways of playing/finishing the stages. (I have some feedback for this, down below).The stages are cool, fun and colorful. They don't focus on one mechanic, which is great, and thus they bring plenty of challenges to the table - especially in the last world.The characters are very well designed. It's clear that all the sprites (Kaze, enemies, game objects etc.) had a lot of love and care invested in them. Nothing seemed off, weird or of poor quality.The plot fits this kind of game. It's basic and easy to understand, which is told mostly through images and short animations.The SFX are clear, high quality and do their job well bringing the world around you to life.The music is alright. It has the role of being ambiental, rather than action inducing, or blood pumping - with small exceptions here and there.Yes, you will find lots of fun in this game, well worth your money. This is a quality product which delivers a smooth and challenging experience (or casual - the option is there).I encountered only a couple minor bugs during the whole game, like being stuck right besides the banana cannon after being hit, which happened under a very specific situation out of my control, which couldn't be replicated when I tried on my own. Other than that, this is a polished game (yeah, hard to believe in 2021).If anyone from the game's team is reading this, these are my 2 cents of what can be improved or added.1. The masks can be taken to a new level by having stages with multiple paths, which feature a type of mask (or more?) - thus bringing more variety and verticality to the game. Or only 1 path, which can be crossed with all the masks, but with which mask? Up to the player.2. Boss rush mode.3. A "New Game+" mode, if possible. The early stages can be harder, with a different design maybe - more traps, pits, enemies etc.4. This is gimmicky, but an in-game option to toggle between Xbox and PS4 button overlays would be neat.5. A skip intro option.Hope this review sheds some light for newcomers or people that were on the fence buying this title!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone's been pointing out the similarities to DKC, and I have to agree - as a fan of that game, I can tell you in some cases which levels from DKC inspired certain boards in Kaze - but I've been having a great time, the momentum based platforming feels good, and the levels provide a satisfying challenge without overstaying their welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge platformer fan, so this was an obvious fit for me, but I'm enjoying it even more than I thought I would. The controls are great, with sharp response times and simple controls. There isn't as much enemy variety as you might expect, but there are a lot of neat little mechanics that are introduced (including some auto-runner sections that are really great) and the level design ramps up perfectly in difficulty. I'm about 60% done with the game right now, so it'll probably be ten or twelve hours to get a full 100%, which I think is a great length. Overall, really recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game and I'm so glad it exists for people who missed out on the majesty of Donkey Kong Country games and various other 90's platformers like Kid Chameleon. I'm happy to report this game belongs in the top tier of its genre, excelling in level design, art direction, memorable set pieces, tight controls, excellent music, the whole damn experience. Once I picked it up, I just could not put it down and I could immediately tell this is the sort of game that was made for me. It's challenging but fair, the secrets are hidden well enough without being obtuse, the masks are all fun to use in their unique ways. I can't say enough good things about this game. Probably the only issue I had was with the final boss fight being kind of tedious compared to the relatively quick bosses that came before it, but it's supposed to be "epic" and use everything you've learned up to this point, so I'll give it a pass.9.5/10, Just a truly fantastic platformer and I can't wait to see what this team makes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: My very first review here on steam and why? Because I think this game deserves it. Basically this game is Donkey Kong Country. It's not just inspired by it. It basically is Donkey Kong Country but with a rabbit - and a lot of angry vegetables.But in my opinion it's copying it so well, that it doesn't need to hide it, where it is coming from. Maybe it's not just that on point as its idol, but it is still a very, very well done platformer with a lot of fun level setups. It doesn't do anything new. Every gameplay mechanic you will find here was already used in a ton of platformer before that as well but it is doing it in such a thoughtful and fun way, that it is still one of the most enjoyable platformer you will find here on Steam. Especially for speedrunners! I bet this will be one of the best gems at the next GDQs.Kudos to the developer especially if you consider that you are such a small team. Nintendo probably couldn't do it better under these circumstances!The only thing which I did not like is the playtime. In my opinion it's a bit too short and I was hoping for more interesting and challenging bonus stages as a reward for collecting all the stuff in the levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Really good platformer inspired by the Donkey Kong Country series while giving it a lot of it's own personality and mechanics to make it it's own game, had a blast playing through this game, while my expectations weren't particularly high this game blew me away and it's probably one of my favorite games I have ever played, it also features some of the best swiming controls I have ever tried.Definitely recommended if you're a fan of platformers, this is a must play for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Rayman Origins and donkey Kong Country, this is a great game. The controls are smooth and responsive, the levels are creative and both difficult and not frustrating, and the game looks pretty and cute. It's not that long, I 100%ed it in under 9 hours, but i think it is definitely worth its price. Don't go in expecting much of a story, as while it is there, there's no dialog to fully explain everything, and I'd probably say that's my biggest problem... but it's a very small problem that didn't really distract from my enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Style feels Rayman-like with whacky vegetable enemies.Stages are beautiful, varied and extremely detailed, while still staying readable when your character is in fast paced action flow mode.Gameplay is strongly inspired by Donkey Kong Country (minus the barrel mechanics), but has its own charming quirks.Difficulty is demanding, but always fair so far.Obviously a lot of love was put into this game, it is an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to tribute classic 90's platformers and especially Donkey Kong. I loved Donkey Kong as one of my favorite SNES games and also one of my best-of-all-time games.This game does the job, it's really fun to play and you get that nostalgic feeling.Played the Alpha/Beta a few times and bought it on day one and there's really nothing to regret.Get this game, they deserve your money :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome precision platformer! The art is incredibly cozy, and the playstyle is just awesome. You get rewarded for both being curious and exploring the levels, and also for memorizing the map and also for having lightning quick reflexes! An incredible game that's worth the price and the time investment!!Platformer is by far the most clogged genre on steam, with at least a new platformer coming out every single day, but this one is actually awesome! You have very unique biomes, enemies, bosses, and forms!The story is told without any words and it works. The main protagonist, Kaze, is quite memorable, partly because you get to see her name every level.All in all, it's the most satisfying game I've bought in 2021!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: With the original Donkey Kong Country trilogy on the Super Nintendo (specifically DKC2) being my favorite games of all time, I have waited a long time for a game to deliver that same type of game play.  This game is exactly what I have been waiting for.  The atmosphere, level design, and especially the controls were hitting all the right notes for me all the way through. The levels last for just the right amount of time, never overstaying their welcome.  I am so glad to see an indie game studio understand what made the original DKC games great for more than just the graphical fidelity.  I am very happy that the final product did not disappoint and would highly recommend this game to any 2-D platformer enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Old school platformer.  Feels a lot like Donkey Kong Country even down to the levels being designed for speed runs so everything is timed for never letting go of right.  The graphics are really nice although the animated cutscenes make me wish the game used hand animated sprites instead of pixel.I really only have two small complaints:1) The music is a little lacking.  It's not bad, but I'm not in a rush to buy the OST.2) This is purely a personal pet peeve of mine but I can't stand rotating pixels.  If you're going to make a pixel game then you really need to upscale render your textures and use pixel snapping.  Rotating pixels always make me think of Flash animations and look cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: (Note:- I have not completed this game yet so the review will  change at some point.)This game is beautifully handcrafted, and you can see the level of detail that has gone into this game.This is a definite must have for all those whom adore the 2D platformer styled game playWhen i played the demo teaser a while back the first things that sprung to my mind apart from nostalgia overload is how much it reminded me of my childhood favourite game Sparkster for the SNES or Rocket Knight depending where you are from :P and this is not a bad thing at all. It takes Elements and inspiration and owns every aspect of the 2D platform genre and owns the stage in being original and its own thingStory: The story is a simply story line nothing to extravagant which is certainly a nice call back to the games from the 90's and is a nice yet welcomed change of paceGraphics: Gorgeously crafted 2D sprite graphics and brightly colouredSize: This is quite a big game for the amount you are paying 30 levels + 4 Boss fights + 60 Bonus levels and then not to mention the dreaded time trials x_x but really good fun Difficulty: each level varies but this game starts nice and easy to get you used to the controls and then gets difficult very quickly and sometimes frustrating. Some of you may have no troubles from the get go, but from my own personal play through I have died quite a lot (Not for the faint hearted especially if you are not into the rage aspect of games)Pros:-Huge variety of levels and extras to keep you entertained Challenging Controls are snappy and very responsive (played with both keyboard and controller) although will say I my personal preference is playing with controllerCons:- Music will get annoying very quickly especially if you die a lot like I did xD (This is only cons really because of me not the game itself) The music is actually really well done.first two bosses are easy but like all boss battles once you learn their pattern it will be a breeze (Will update when I progress further through the game)For the price that this game is being sold at, I feel that this game is worth every penny and more I would say, and I honestly cannot wait to see where the game Developers go from here :)

name: Dolmen
detailed_description: Dolmen casts players onto a hostile alien world known as Revion Prime. Your job? Bring back samples of a crystal with particularly unique properties; the so-called 'Dolmen'. These crystals are capable of allowing interaction between realities, revolutionising space exploration and changing the known world forever. DYNAMIC COMBAT In Dolmen you will grow stronger with each battle! Experience a rich combat system with various weapons and moves at your disposal. Switch natively between melee and ranged combat to overcome the most challenging enemies Revion Prime has to offer. ENERGY MODE Energy management is key to victory in Dolmen. Energy is not only used for ranged weapons, but also for activating 'Energy Mode'. 'Energy Mode' imbues your melee weapons with elemental status effects, letting you take full advantage of your enemy's weaknesses. DISCOVER A MYSTERIOUS PLANET A devastated, darkly beautiful world is waiting to be explored. Will you find all the secrets that Revion Prime has to offer? Or will this cruel world push you to the brink of death? A CHALLENGE AWAITS Surviving is the last thing this world wants you to do. Will you see your timeline erased or will you overcome the challenge that awaits you? ENCOUNTER GRUESOME BOSSES Revion Prime offers a plethora of gruesome monstrosities that will put your skills to the test.

_childDocuments_.review: Revion Prime was just another anonymous planet under Zoan control (your faction, by the way), until the powerful DOLMEN Crystals were discovered on it. Some scientists got their hands full, started experimenting with trans-dimensional technology, and made a real mess of things - on top of other factions wanting a slice of the cake. Guess who has to clean up the mess?If the classic trope of “someone fiddled with stuff they couldn’t comprehend and screwed up reality” sounds clichè, that’s because it is. Despite locales actually feeling diverse and reasonably well-designed, at no point the narrative premise evolves past “bash everyone in your way to get the damn crystals” or has any memorable character. We have the power-tripped supervillain, the zero-charm protagonist that says probably five lines in the entire game, the generic utilitarian radio operator, and a slew of NPCs with the personality of a rusted wheelbarrow, that have no quests or backstories whatsoever. Not even the optional lore files salvage it, as they never really prove interesting.DOLMEN plays out as a classic souls-like in this part, meaning you’ll be roaming various locales crawling with enemies, look out for the occasional item to collect, and most importantly activate Beacons (bonfires), which allow you to restore HP and Batteries (Estus), but also respawn enemies. Beacons also allow you to fast-travel between each, and teleport to your ship which contains crafting, cosmetic and leveling-up facilities, plus a totally useless NPC that just stands there staring at you menacingly.Don’t expect a complex level layout with exciting secrets and mind-bending verticality or hidden shortcuts: most levels are linear, with just a couple exceptions - most don’t even have any real shortcut or looping design at all. The only reasons to explore are crates with crafting materials, hidden NPCs that grant unique parts and lore files, but that’s all rather easy to find.Bread and butter of the experience, the combat here has some good ideas, admittedly. First of all, healing doesn’t work as you may be accustomed to for this genre. Energy (as in, Mana) acts as your healing medium, and can only be recharged with Batteries, coming in limited amounts and restored at Beacons - Estus Flask with extra steps. Mana also is used for Energy Mode, which is an amped-up status you can trigger at any time, that gives elemental powers to your attacks, other than also for ranged weapons and eventual weapon-specific abilities.The way elemental effects are handled is pretty good, as when enemies with one of the three status effects (Frozen, Burning, Poisoned) are hit with a weapon of that same element, this triggers powerful passive effects that deal significant amounts of damage - debuff first, hit second, that’s the way to go. This is a smart system that could have been built upon, but sadly it wasn’t so.Now onto the issues. The main issue with combat is the jank, with fiddly animations and mechanics that are about as reliable as that used car you bought last month from that shady salesman. What is customary in the genre just isn’t there: backstabs, ripostes, spells, stat-boosting consumables - all of this simply isn’t accounted for, making combat feel shallow not after long. The balance is all over the place really, with ranged easily overpowering everything else, alongside a fast melee as side to exploit elemental effects while energy recharges. Boss design feels average at best, with none of the fights really feeling epic despite their evolving movesets and sometimes considerable difficulty.Enemies and breakable elements drop crafting materials that can be used at the ship’s printer to craft progressively better weapons and armors, each with stat requirements to be used, of course. Each armor and weapon will contribute towards a certain Technology (Zoan, Driller, Revian) with passive abilities to match, think of it as a ‘set bonus’ of sorts. Crafted items can be further enhanced with Epic and Rare materials which give them better stats compared to the “regular” versions. Unless you want to craft boss weapons, which require you to kill each boss three times (respawning them costs crystals with low drop rate), the rest of the materials will come along without particular grinding in general. You can use Nanites (souls) to improve your character stats permanently in the ship pod, and this works like in any other Souls game.You can attempt bosses in jolly cooperation with your fellow DOLMEN players, using a beacon near each arena. The design of this is dement however, as it requires consumable, low-drop resources you can lose on death to be activated, no refunds in case you lose. Whoever thought gating multiplayer behind resource grinding was a good idea, didn’t think straight at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has been long overdue.The reception  got at launch was pretty bad. So bad that it sat at a “Mostly Negative” rating for a while, as quietly as it did in my Library. With that, and with what I’ve heard from a friend who played it, I ended up waiting. Amongst other things, I didn’t want to be the guy to kick it while it’s down. Luck would have it that in the few months it took me to get around to it, a couple of patches rolled out. It was time, finally, to go into the game full of enthusiasm, ready to give it its fair shake.Just think of the possibilities: it would be my review that’d usher in a new wave of appreciation for it! I could take pride in being the one who stayed behind, the one who revisited the game all these months later and say: “Hey everyone! It’s GOOD now!”, and the masses of Steam would flock to me, hoist me on their shoulders, and we’d all sing Kumbaya as we waddle off into the sunset, burdened by carrying my fat ass, newly purchased copies of  clutched firmly in our grasps.But no. This is not the timeline we're in.I gave it my all to like , but for nearly every feature I would have liked to highlight as something it does well, the game fought me.As the story goes, you’re an employee of Zoan, a galactic conglomerate in charge of a research facility on Revion Prime – a planet gone AWOL. You’re the, erm,  of a rescue team, tasked with beaming down to the planet’s surface and not so much finding out what happened, as recovering samples of a crystal called Dolmen that’s been found on the planet in ample supply. You see, the crystal is valuable because it has reality-bending capabilities, allowing for travel between universes and thus being extremely sought out for space travel and exploration.It's a great premise, one that the game doesn’t do anything memorable with. Corporate intrigue? A reality-bending mineral? Several universes, all clashing together in one place and creating a chaotic environment for all these parties that are searching for the crystal to duke it out in? All within a sleek sci-fi setting? Sign me right up, we’ve got GOTY material here! But no.  uses its Dolmen as nothing more than a McGuffin, and any creative way all these elements could’ve impacted the plot is nowhere to be found.It’s a souls-like, so it tries to hide the narrative’s most interesting bits off the main path. From time to time, you’ll come across a terminal or tablet on the ground that’s . These can be interacted with to bring up a text log and deliver some of the driest storytelling I’ve ever had the chance to read. They're lore dispensers, plain and simple, that tie into the world in the most basic way imaginable. Even the protagonist, the aforementioned Commander, while completely voiced and showing glimmers of some kind of noble and heroic personality, succumbs to the uninspiredness of it all, as his VA delivers almost every line in the same way.This blandness crosses over to the art style as well, even if the game looks good on a technical level. I was once told one of the biggest reasons why  architecture and world were so memorable is because everything had this feeling of being designed independently of the player, ie. they first designed these gargantuan castles and then figured out how to have you get around them. It seems that  designers took that literally and only made their environments huge while forgetting to make them interesting and add any semblance of direction. Empty hallways, hangars, and server rooms, none of which stick out, with the way to proceed often placed in some obscure corner. I kid you not, at one point, the only way I could tell I was progressing through an area as opposed to going back to its beginning was because a voice-over played.Now, let's talk about the gameplay. If you didn't find the story intriguing enough, then the combat alone probably won't be able to redeem  in your eyes, even if it's where the best-realized ideas lie. Think  combos, built by rapidly switching between melee and ranged weapons, slowed down to a souls-like tempo and you’re on the right path. Holding CTRL will have you swap to a ranged weapon with infinite ammo, limited by the mana pool you also use to heal. The genius idea here is that your mana pool is split into two parts. Healing will use up its maximum capacity, restored by nomming on an Energy Battery, while shooting your gun only diminishes its current value and allows it to refill once you've let your guns cool off for a bit.New equipment is obtained by crafting, which, while straightforward, is what I’d call a ‘neat addition’. The variety is pretty decent; swords, axes, shield combos, fist weapons, pistols, shotguns, sci-fi black hole guns… Finding secrets and progressing through the game will award you with blueprints to then craft these gizmos from, using the various materials you find, each crafted piece having different stats depending on what materials you imbue it with.Another important aspect of  combat are elemental weaknesses all enemies have, fire, ice, and toxin, with each weapon’s damage corresponding to one. The dance is simple: match the element of your ranged weapon to the one your enemy is weak to, then shoot 'em enough to fully inflict the associated debuff. Then, proceed to swoop in with a melee weapon of the same element for a devastating blow. Light attacks, heavy attacks, dodges… you get the picture; though finer examples like backstabs and parries are missing.Unfortunately, despite having an assortment of ‘okay’ enemies and some memorable bosses to fight,  feels like a third-person shooter in disguise; not only because of how effective ranged weapons are, but because of how ineffective melee is.A lack of animation cancelling and poorly animated enemy attacks is mainly to blame. If I had to list every time I was taken aback by my dodge not registering, we’d be here forever. I’ll give you an example, though: imagine fighting a ranged enemy — if you dodge at any point after the shot has been fired, you’ll get hit, even from a mile away. So, dodge while they’re raising their weapon, even if it goes against common video game logic. Which frame of the windup animation do you have to dodge during? You’ll have to figure it out on your own. I gave up trying to read the animation cues and started relying on counting the seconds from when a symbol signifying an upcoming unblockable attack would appear above the enemies’ heads to when I'd get hit – after getting hit enough times, of course.As a friend who watched me play put it: “It just seemed like every time you went for a melee attack, it wasn’t worth it.”. And he's right. Even if it takes longer compared to melee, it's better to just stay back and blast away at your problems.Believe it or not, I was still considering a positive rating after beating the game last night. I thought of a clever conclusion to my review as well, of how I’ll lambast having Steam’s rigid binary of “Recommended” and “Not Recommended” loaded and pointed against the back of my head, and how I’ll lament not being able to hide behind a “57/100” like a true professional.But no. Typing all this out made me realize that I can’t recommend . I also thought of giving it another playthrough with a different build, but shuddered at the thought of any other jank I might uncover while not levelling up my guns. I accept this defeat, head bowed in shame and boots bloodied.

_childDocuments_.review: Dolmen is a bad game, plain and simple. Nothing really works as intended, stamina/energy management is broken, healing system is a chore. There is litterally nothing to find in the few (3) areas you'll explore and combat is slow, floaty, unresponsive and most of all, unenjoyable. Everything is so bad that i truly believe that nothing has been play tested beforehand. So many core mechanics of the game do not work, it's impossible otherwise. Stay away from this thing, or at least, wait for a big, BIG sale (it will happen very soon).
_childDocuments_.name: Dolmen

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a triple A Dark Souls type experience this one is probably not for you. However, if you can enjoy a lower budget somewhat clunkier experience you will probably have fun with the game. The closest comparison would be "Hellpoint" and if you didn't have any major issues with it you might find yourself at home with Dolmen too.It is the usual souls experience where you go around collecting nanites (souls) and different item drops to upgrade your stats and your equipment. You have your usual assortment of different melee weapons and in addition a decent variety of firearms. Personally I didn't have any technical issues apart from not having the option to rebind movement controls, but you can fix that with "Autohotkey" or similar third party programs. The game has received a lot of bad press on the technical issues so your mileage may vary on the matter. Overall I ended up enjoying the game and had no major problems with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Its really sad to see the reviews for this game. Having recently bought this game and completed it 3 times. One with Guns only, one with dual wield only, one with unga bunga asmongold style club smash only. I can say that I have now the right to give a review for this sadly rather down voted game.As a fan of dark souls games, this game is really good. It has fun bosses, that are arguably sadly rather easy; despite what people say. Looking at you in the comments who says last boss is hard. (literally one of the easiest bosses in the game).  Just like your typical dark souls games; clearing to the bosses is where most of your deaths will come from, especially those dark shadowey ET lookin MF'ers in act 3 of this game, holy god are they annoying :D in a good way.The game looks visually nice, plays well, the bosses are fun, the weapons are fun, the builds are fun.Despite what people say, Stamina is not an issue in the slightest, not even for unga bunga builds. Just play 1-2 hits , dodge chill 2 secs, 1-2 hits chill 2 secs and u will never have any problems.Honestly, can see myself playing this again in the future, its well worth the price. I feel sorry for the devs who likely took the down voting to heart and wont make a second game. I would truly love to see a Dolmen 2 tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: actualy surprisingly competentit's a soulslike / Hellpoint-like like you'd expectlight, heavy attacksranged aswell as melee (although the guns are a pretty viable option from the getgo here, due to how ressources work)you got 3 bars, two of which works as usual: health and stamina. then there's energy. energy supports your ranged attacks, and refills automaticaly (slowish) or when hitting enemies with melee (faster, depening on your perks alot faster).you can also enter a special "mode" on button press (Y on pad) to get into energy mode, which lets you use your melee attacks ignoring stamina (and letting it recharge) but using energy instead, while also applying status effects and elemental damage. your energy bar only gets realy depleted when healing; to recharge spend energy you got energy-estus-flaks (4 to start with, but there are temporary ones in the levels).armor comes in head, chest, arms and legs, weapons can be dual wield, two handed, 1 handed, shields, handguns, sniper(ish), assault guns, shotguns, etc. there's enough here to be fun. you do not find loot, but similiar to Monster Hunter enemies drop materials. the moment you find the neccessary material for an item-recipe you can see the full recipe on board of your ship and having all the mats-> craft it and later upgrade it in the same process. when crafting each item got slots (saw now 1 to 3 slots, but there might be more), where you can also slot materials dropped by enemies, which come in different rarities and offer boni (more damage/defense, more attackspeed, etc.). so the system works less like a From game, more like a grinder (which is a good thing for this game in my book). you earn nanites by killing enemies, which you can spend leveling your char (all the expected stats are here). this + the Monster Hunter ish loot mechanic turn the game more in a Diablo, less in DS. it's actualy quite motivating to hunt for that last mat to get a new piece of gear, especialy since armor and weapons comes with special abilities and stats (and also kinda set-boni, due to the perk system / technologies).you got also the technologies-menue, which offers small and big passive boni (like a damage shield, or health league) depending on who's gear you wear and how many parts (not neccessarly, gear has points attached to it). one tree is for human, the remaining 2 are centered on the alien races.mechanicaly it's rock solid. now the plot doesn't exist, which in parts explains the small download and install size. you get ingame cutscenes, and fully voiced (main characters...aka the ship A.I. ? and your char) and some nonesense-speak-voiced audio. the rest is presented in item-text and terminals, etc. giving text to support lore. but it's as basic as you can get. having everything maxed out and RTX enabled the game doesn't look half bad. the sci-fi-flair is pretty great, it's not Hellpoint, but very colorfull in parts. some Deadspace influences are clearly here aswell. now the player model is okay, some enemy models are downright hideous, low polygon, low quality textures...and humanish models beside your character look god awefull. but the enviroments are neat, and some effects look great (other look like PSX effects...sadly some of the first you see).the levels i played now where pretty good. there's hidden stuff (mats) everywhere, shortcuts and ways to outplay the enemies.the music is very good (when it plays), soundeffects are again very hit'n miss.combat is okay. once you get the hang of it it's pretty fun (better than Lords of the Fallen and co.), but it feels floaty and some enemies are just strange to fight...the camera spazzes out also (rarely).i haven't encountered any major bugs or performance issues however the menu controls with a pad are strange, some effects need a doover (the spider green death poof...Jesus) and the human models...realy?is it worth 40 euros? nah. looks and feels more like a 25-30 ish game, but if you are not strapped for money or like me a fan of sci-fi-soulslikes (Hellpoint) it's a good game...not great by any means, but also not as bad as some make it out to be. funny enough the worst part was the start.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on a soulslike kick since finishing Elden Ring, having played and enjoyed Nioh 2, The Surge 2, and Stranger of Paradise, as well as replaying Dark Souls 3, so when I heard there was another sci-fi soulslike on the scene, my interest was piqued - but to be entirely honest, avoid this one unless you've played every other major soulslike you can get your hands on.  It's far from the worst indie soulslike attempt I've played, but it's... not great.There are four key problems here.1: It's missing elements that are genre staples elsewhere, like backstabbing, and the ability to riposte after a parry.  On its own that might not be so bad, but it feeds into problem two.2: The things it changes or tries to introduce to the formula seem ill-conceived, and it gives you a lot of tools without properly incentivizing you to use them.  Parrying is riskier than blocking, particularly given most enemies poorly telegraph, but doing it doesn't reward you with anything other than a reduction in damage coming through your block because you can't riposte.  You can't backstab, but there is a special attack out of sprint that it seems like the game wants you to use to start fights, but the game punishes you for for sprinting into combat, because stamina drains quickly and recovers slowly, and the dodge is expensive.  And on the front of 'new ideas', the energy system is a mess, letting you heal twice while moving, but then forcing you to stand still for anagonizingly long period of time in order to recover those heal charges.  The only thing this game does differently that I actually liked is 'energy mode', which can be used to give elemental buffs to your melee weapons, but it's poorly explained, and it seems like using it will prevent you from healing until you actually try it.  I also like that you can pick up your souls by touching them instead of having to push a button, it's nice to not have to distract yourself more than necessary to recover your souls during a fight.3: For a soulslike, it's poorly tuned.  Everything feels sluggish and awkward, stamina is too precious forcing you to spend ages backpedalling while it recovers and encouraging you to ration dodges, but then blocking feels unsafe, I've had enemies hit me through it despite the 'you blocked' feedback playing out, the first zone has you fighting next to a lot of cliffs but there's nothing to stop enemy drops from spawning over a pit then falling out of reach, status effects are devastating and apply very quickly, even through block.  These are just the problems I can think of off the top of my head.  It's difficult to convey how bad it feels to play coming off other more tightly tuned soulslikes.4: Perhaps most devastating, I would be willing to look past everything I've already talked about if the game had a strong sense of personality, or if I was interested in the world and story, but I regret to say that it's just incredibly bland.  There's no identity here.  You're some Faceless Space Hero out to Shoot the Generic Aliens and Stop the Dimensional Catastrophe.  You have seen this before, in other games, done better.  I'm willing to give messy games the benefit of the doubt if there's a good sense of aesthetic or an interesting story, (the first Surge game is a good example for that) but Dolmen has neither - and if the story does get good eventually, I can't say, because its hook is terrible.I might be willing to give this one a longer try if I was confident I could return it if it doesn't improve, but as it stands, this is an expensive game, and it left a poor first impression, so I just want to get my money back while I still can.  If you're looking for a sci-fi themed soulslike that brings some interesting and fun new ideas to the table without breaking the underlying formula, The Surge 2 is substantially cheaper and a better time.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I finished the game, I'll confidently say if you can't tolerate budget titles, stay away from Dullmen. It is indeed a dull game riddled with broken systems which barely could worth 20$ at launch. I'll increase my bet further and say sooner than later we'll see this game in Humble Bundle and such and it will only retail for 1€ at key stores similar to Hellpoint's fate.If we had a checklist of 'what makes a cheap/bad souls-like iteration', Dullmen would fill in many boxes. Including the following:Attempting to create interesting lore but does have a bad presentation so you barely care what is happening. The villain doesn't really go beyond 'you are all weak so gotta be killed' and all other bosses are types of atrocious monsters that I couldn't care less how they were created or brought to life.Creating an mp experience yet locking people out of it for no reason. Wow. Why the f? You use fragments (which you also need to respawn bosses) to create an mp session and if you die and can't pick up your fragments back, they'll be gone forever. There are enemies that drop fragments and it is not incredibly rare but I'll say it loud, compared to any souls games or probably Remnant/Nioh etc. the CO-OP IS INACCESSIBLE. If you plan to play with a bud of yours, just don't. You won't get more than a few tries and that's if you can get a hold of your fragments in the first place. Also, if you die the respawned boss disappears. So ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lame. If you want people to use fragments for mp functions and if you want people to grind boss materials for crafting, well, then just make them even more common and make them permanent once you get them as long as you do not spend them (similar to insight in Bloodborne). Devs, what did you try to accomplish there? Don't you want to be more accessible when Elden Ring is getting praised all day for its accessibility? Don't you want your players to have fun instead of going through this completely unnecessary CHORE? (ps: You can try to find mp sessions without a cost, I don't know if you defeat the boss in someone's world is going to impact your world as well. Generally, it does not but I was unable to test it. 200 peak players and no sessions. Duh)A rather steep difficulty curve. After killing a lame spider (just spam some r2 heavy attack you'll be fine) you get to fight 2 super-duper killer soldiers back to back. That is 2nd boss of the game and it has two phases. The boss arena also sucks your whole stamina out if you get caught to some sort of energy-draining ball. So, every souls-like game probably has a boss that is actually a complete litmus test. If you look up to achievements in each game, I bet there would be a boss (early game) that divided people, and many failed. Remember people complaining about Lady Butterfly or most recently Margit/Godrick? Those are tough but they teach you the game and well, Elden Ring is an open-world ARPG so you are free to go wherever and grind. Sekiro is more about precision and utilizing the patterns but even in it, you can upgrade your character a bit. In Mortal Shell, you can just go grab a better shell. In Remnant/The Surge 2 you can skip some locations to find a better farming spot (and well there are glitches lmao). It's important if you allow people to do that (besides the glitches ofc) and all three aforementioned games allow it. If you make a compact linear game you need to a fine adjustment. Although Dolmen is an RPG as well in Dolmen it does not seem to be possible to grind (well, it's speculation but I have a strong feeling about it) cuza) You need to craft gear b) You need to farm materialsSo gear is pretty much left out of the equation. But it's also hard to farm souls(whatever they call that in this game, idk) to level up.In a game in which its first 2 hour is quite linear, 2nd boss is a huge middle finger to players and is only the boss with a 2nd phase (although I just finished the game I don't remember the entirety of the bosses lmao). Sounds good on the paper but does not really teach the game imo. You don't have any good gear or stats at that point and it's not like you can get any better ones or grind, you don't really have anywhere else to go or to do. It might make most people quit for good.Well, speaking of corridors the game introduces much bigger spaces later on. I wish it did not as %90 of the game turns into large areas without anything to do or to collect (except for crafting materials, again) and some do not even contain enemies. You just walk and roll around a huge-ass room, similar to this.Why spend any effort to create a huge ass useless room? It's beyond my understanding. This is not a cinematic experience. In a game that relies on exploration, I often wasted time trying to look at corners etc. to see if I was missing anything but no, areas are large just to be large, devs did not justify it. Level design is often bland. That is a huge problem with many budget souls-like titles. Yet, you still can have a creative mind. There is some sort of small backtrack in the game, there are shortcuts and some parts of the map connect to each other but it's just not a game-changer. Furthermore, there are far more loading screens between areas than I'd anticipated.The placement of checkpoints. They are weird and I feel devs do dirty to players. They sometimes place them very close to boss doors and sometimes they just hide them in a complete another place (like inside a room or a place where you need to take an elevator to access and there is a loading screen every time). This made me go complete wacko mode. Are you dumb? Why don't you put checkpoints CLOSE to BOSSES? You wanted us to respawn bosses, remember? Hell, why even hide them? Only to frustrate people as they are wasting their time? This is already a compact game. Place close checkpoints and let people practice the bosses dammit. Spawn some checkpoints after a boss is defeated, why do you want me to take an elevator every time or run through a room to another where you could have placed it to a huge ass room in the first place?Ranged weapons are also not will be a selling point. Compared to Hellpoint it looks broken and even compared to Unchained, it looks unpolished. There's a class that focuses on the ranged combat but I don't see how it's going to serve the player as most of the bosses are designed for melee combat and ranged absolutely does nothing.Elements and energy management are the marketing focuses of this game. Elemental ranged attacks feel utterly useless and meanwhile, you can also go in energy mode (and deal elemental damage of whichever reactor core you are equipped with) and deal some elemental damage over time it also feels completely useless, especially with the bosses. You don't even get to stagger them when you build the bar up. There is no real strategy for choosing a boss' weak point and applying elemental damage as far as I am concerned. You apply resin to your wep. in Dark Souls and in here you just craft the weapons with elements themselves. Yet, the game definitely does not feel like it is built around this mentality.At last, it's a huge headache trying to manage the energy. You use it for your reactor core and also replenish your health. You have limited batteries (similar to Estus etc.) to replenish your energy and it only replenishes half of your bar. And half of your energy replenishes a small percentage of your health. You can't move at all while using a battery (if you thought using Estus in DS2 left you vulnerable). I mean even if you thought replenishing your bar to full would be op, at least allow us to have some movement or apply it instantly. The use of battery combined with energy management is some serious ♥♥♥♥.By no means it's the worst souls, I believe the crown still belongs to Unchained but save yourself some time&money. It's a janky and an uninspring attempt.4.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well...Just finished the game.I love all kind of Souls-Like like Darksouls, Bloodborne, Lords of the Fallen etc...This game is not as bad as people want to sell you in the reviews, but still I had to downvote, because neutral is not possible...Positive Points: + Game is much prettier than people are talking here in the forums and reviews... Still better than most of the originals From Software Games.+ Armor Design is pretty cool when u are able to craft better armor later on.+ Probably the best approach to ranged combat in all souls-like games I have played yet. Negative Points:- The story is utterly trash. Ancient alien civ disappeared..Bad guys show up, looking for something no idea. The whole story was really nonsense and you did not miss anything by skipping all the notes on the ground. - Massive empty rooms - Yep, you are literally walking for 5 minutes to find out that there is absolutely nothing in alternative routes to disover or loot...- Stat points, there are stat points that make no sense, because other stat points value multiple stats while others are just affecting one stat, with the same impact, so its very confusing. - Balancing is really strange, there are enemies that punish you hard for attacking them in melee and also in range, you have to kite them unncesseraily long around the room to the land some shots...Just playing with your time to prolong the game. - There is no new game + or any reason why you should play the game for a second time.- Lots of stuff will be missing in your inventory which you were not able to craft due to lack of materials. The game wants from you to kill all bosses again for two times on the same difficulty to get the materials. But there is no additional content or challenge to try to weapons on. There is no benefit or motivation for you doing so, except the achievments. - The last boss is having a MASSIVE difficulty spike compared to the other bosses. - The elemental system where you can apply debuffs to enemies can be neglected, you cant add them to bosses anyway due to their fast subside. And adding them to normal enemies doesnt make any sense because they die too fast. - Level Design is unrewarding and not clever like to be expected from a souls-like. The ending of the game is somewhat of spoiling a second part with multiplayer aspects, but literally it felt like a joke watching the outro, because it did fit exactly into the rest of nonsense you have been told. Sorry devs, your approach was good, with nice design aswell, but somehow the spark did not glow long enough to rescue this game anywhere since the community burried this game hard and fast.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the video game with a decent foundation that was ruined the most by making it a Soulslike.And this isn't even really a Soulslike - it's more of a Sekirolike, but also with shooting. (Is it the first Shadowtowersoulsekiro-like?)Dodging doesn't feel consistent. Parrying doesn't feel consistent. The Soulslike mechanics drag this game down hard.With such unpolished Soulslike mechanics, dying in 3-5 hits feels entirely unfair and not worth the time investment.The game would be vastly more enjoyable as a hybrid third-person melee/shooter. Maybe something like , except a slower and more methodical sci-fi dungeon crawler, rather than pure hack'n'slash. The world design and level design are pretty good. Areas can feel pretty large, and there's some clever inter-connectivity among them. The art style is a bit generic sci-fi, but it's done well enough with varied areas and a wider color palette than the standard Soulslike brown-gray. While the Soulslike mechanics make them worse, the bosses are decently varied. The developers tried to do something unique with each boss, and each one felt creative enough. Not every experiment works, but some do.The developers showed they can make a competent video game. Some of their achievements should be acknowledged for that. I don't think I ran into any bugs or performance issues.So I give it a 51% recommend.However, this is a bad Soulslike. It's a Mostly Positive game buried underneath Very Negative Soulslike mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this is an indie game, this game has blown me away with its quality. I've seen some reviews mention bugs, clunky fighting and such but I have not experienced any such things myself so I do suppose a fair heads up is that you may or may not encounter such issues depending on your system specs and with likely upcoming patches, may never experience any at all!It is clear to me having played through three bosses at the point of this review that a lot of thought went into the boss fights and I personally feel like this game has good value to it. Great visuals, cool cutscenes, nice voice acting, solid battle system. I've heard some people say it isn't worth the asking price, but considering we often underpay developers in the industry and expect them to deliver faster than humanly possible which creates very harsh and toxic environments, I personally don't see it as being unreasonably expensive (like We Happy Few was that severely overpriced itself to be able to do "discounts" at 60 bucks) considering how the quality put into it has been. Yes, I got a key for free to try this game out but I still put the saved money to cancer research because I think a gift given should be forwarded when possible. Did I think it was worth that amount? Yes. If you're not picking it up now, I'd gladly recommend picking it up at a discount.I personally hope they get enough sales to possibly polish even further and maybe even make more content as I can easily see this game having some exciting DLC diving even deeper into the lore they've seeded in so far.

_childDocuments_.review: After 15.5 hours to reach 100% completion with build experimenting, I feel confident in this review.Like many, if not most souls-like games. Don't expect to come into this with the expectation it is going to match FromSoftware levels of polish and deliverance (which bear in my mind those games are far from perfect as well). So from my perspective that is an incredibly disingenuous approach which is immediately destined to failure.Dolmen comes from a small studio which I may be wrong, but I believe this is their first game and they overall did a sufficient job. I can say day one it was rough, the game did feel more like an alpha and was incredibly choppy, rendering issues plagued it along with wonky hit detection. After an almost 1gig patch though. The game is in  state it should have released in.The story is nothing to write home about, but I would hope anyone interested in this wasn't coming for the story, the overwhelming consensus is that it's not very good and I am in concurrence with that statement. So to get into it now, it took me 15.5 hours to 100% and I can say that I thoroughly enjoyed Dolmen's offerings, any longer and the content wouldn't have sustained that. I spent a bit of time farming and going back through areas realizing I somehow missed a hidden cave or two that aren't really all that hidden. If you are trying to go for the one play through and be done, you're looking at about a roughly 8-9 hour game, but skill and comfort with souls games will really dictate time commitment.Graphics:-Solid for a small studio, they aren't anywhere near the worst you will encounter, but once you are done with the game you probably won't remember it outside of name.-Environments are decent and vary slightly with the exception of a few areas that stand out more, so it's going to feel a little recycled at times.Gameplay:-Movement can be janky at times and the animations stiff. Hit detection is much better after the big patch.-Melee is arguably the weaker aspect of combat, not all weapons feel balanced well, but again that may be a little more subjective due to preference in play styles and general player skill/adaptability. -I did a hybrid build and found a sword that scaled with "Science" and a Rifle that scaled the same. The shooting feels good to me in this game, I never played immortal unchained so I can't use that reference, but there is a good flow between melee and shooting which I found myself steamrolling the game once I found my build.Design:-Normal enemies are decent. Each area has their one or two new introduced enemies and for myself that was sufficient enough. They vary in a couple different moves and some designs have had a lot more work put into them than others and that becomes blatantly clear very fast.-Map and overall world are fairly straight forward, you'll find the occasional extra path here and there. Effectively this felt like a linear game with a souls format incorporated for character progress.-Bosses are the strongest aspect, this is something I feel strongly that this game shares with Hellpoint, general enemies are okay and you learn their behaviors fairly fast, while the bosses will actually be where you die until you understand their moves and timing. Thumbs up to the team for their boss designs, they felt fun to fight and even more fun to annihilate in end game.At best I would give this game a 7/10 and at worst I would give it a 6/10. For most people this will be a decent buy when it's on sale, or if you want to support the devs more so than pick it up at full price. This game does offer a fairly good souls-like experience at least for one play through and when you find yourself in need of something until the next souls game that will scratch your itch. This game can help fill the void.A couple of final notes;1. I never found a single person ever needing help for a boss, nor did anyone ever join my games. co-op to my understanding is for boss fights ONLY so if you have a friend that is playing to than coordinate it. The player base doesn't really exist from my experience.2. Sound design is good in some areas, only passable in others. You're weapon animation sounds may go out, but after whatever fight they go out in is over they return.3. I'm not sure how people ran into enemies that destroyed them so easily in more negative reviews, I must have always been on the right path to progression, or I'm comfortable enough in souls games to have a good grasp on how to progress, because I never encountered that complaint that seemed like it held validity. If you need another souls-experience and you already played the heavy hitters, you'll find a short and albeit fairly mediocre experience here, but overall enjoyable and somewhat of a passion project.Good Job, Devs. With how the ending played out, I really hope this universe gets expanded on and your next game can truly be fleshed out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you have other soulslikes you wanna play, this one should be far down the list, but if you are starved for these kinds of games, buying this on sale is ok, but expect it to be a little clunky.I really feel like this game is some shorts steps away from being a good game, so I was really on the fence about this, but I will leave it as a negative, reluctantly.In my opinion the game has some nice details and attention paid to setting, somewhat of a story, but what kills it a bit for me is balancing on bosses, weapons, dodging mechanic and so, and I really think if they had spent a bit more time polishing it it would have been SO much better.For the most part I actually liked both enemy and boss designs, but it also comes back to timers on what you can and cannot dodge feeling "off", and also getting hit multiple times even if you are staggered or knocked down means if you get unlucky you can basically be killed by a combo if you got hit by the first hit.That said it is far from impossible to complete the game even with melee build, I played both with 1h and 2h weapons, and mostly ignored guns until I killed the final boss and was gonna farm for 100% achies, and some of those guns are overpowered and makes it a LOT easier.Final note: To get 100% achies you may need to farm a bit but it was not super bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely enjoying this game so far!I can only assume the negative reviews are a combination of three possible things:1 - Memefluencers talking trash, and encouraging their mindless fanbase to review bomb it.2 - A lack of understand core mechanics.3 - Graphics.Now, to address point number one, well, one MarkiPewdiePliarEyes says to hate on something, hundreds of brainwashed fans will do just that.Point number two, a misunderstanding of how to play the game. We will give some leniency here because people see "Soulslike" and just make a bunch of assumptions about the game. I have learned some trenendously important mechanics that aren't explained well... It's a ranged combat game. 50/50 ranged and melee. You use your "battery" which is basically your mana pool to fire your gun, but when you use your battery for this specific function, it actually replenishes! Fire a few shots, switch to melee while it regenerates, and you can still use it to heal. Once you realize this is a shooter too, the entire flow alters, but unfortunately, due to point number one, I'd say 90% of people will never realize this and abandon it. I'd say this game needs a far more comprehensive tutorial, like... "Dumb as a box of rocks" levels of tutorial. Maybe include more videos or something?Point three, the graphics. While I believe graphics do not make a game, many modern gamers will turn their noses up at any game which does not require a military grade computer to run. The most common complaint I've seen in the discussions and reviews is that it "looks like a Playstation 2 game" but you know what? The PS2 was home to some of the best games of all time, so by making this your argument, you're basically self reporting that you only care about the graphics, and even if the game is fantastic, you won't care because all you care about are the graphics.So in the end, I really have to say that I enjoyed this game as much as The Surge, and MORE than Hellpoint. If you're a true gamer, and you have a will of your own, try this game out. It's on sale for like $3 bucks, and as long as you are capable of enjoying a game with less than quadruple A graphics, I think you'd really enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I actually won this game from a giveaway,so thankfully I did not pay for it.TLDR: It's not bad, but it's far from good. Wait for a massive sale like under $5 spend no more than $10. It feels like an Alpha, or best case a Beta release. The game does have promise, but it's going to need some massive updates.The camera is your enemy no ifs ands or buts. The devs and their infinite wisdom decided to put your character in the middle of the screen instead of offsetting to one side or the other. This basically causes your camera to stare at the floor about 9ft. (3m) in front of your character when you lock on to larger enemies. This makes it more difficult to read moves to, you know play the game, it also puts the icon that basically says  this attack is unblockable off your screen entirely. Getting near a wall while fighting is basically a death sentence, the camera will cram into the wall and freak out in an attempt to get your target locked enemy back on the screen. The controls themselves are about as responsive as a coma patient. everything feels sluggish, and inconsistent. Compounded by the stamina regen being slower than two turtles banging in a snow storm. The graphics are that of a playstation 2  vomiting into the unreal engine and it getting upscaled... slightly. Collision needs some attention as there have been several times I was stabbed through a wall. The story seems to of been drafted by a kindergartner high on cocaine. Weapon choice is stupid limited, and the animations for them are pure garbage. If you want souls style weapon hit combos forget it, you're better off WALKING up to what ever enemy hitting the heavy attack, then rolling away. On slower enemies you can get an additional swing or 2 in but it's not likely, nor worth the risk as enemies don't get staggered unless you are hitting for roughly 70%+ of their health bar, keep in mind every hit you take no matter how small can and will interrupt your attack animations. Do not use the jump attack, doing so basically puts you in slow motion leaving you wide open during the animation and increases damage by maybe 5%??? you can easily get 2 basic heavy attacks off in that time or 1.5 light attacks.On the topic of attacks, just heavy attack, the animation is faster, it deals more damage, and uses maybe an additional 10% stamina for 1.5 - 2x the damage. Light attacks are really not worth it, at least in my experience. Don't skip cut scenes for boss introductions, there is a decent chance your character will be rendered invisible making it neigh impossible to tell where you're at to attack / defend properly, assuming your attacks register at all.The dodge happens on button press not release, and is prolly the only responsive part of the game assuming you are not stuck in some animation lock. I refer back to heavy attacking over light attacking as the animation lock is shorter. The environment would actually be pretty cool if it didn't look like it was designed to run on the sega dreamcast. Enemy variation is non existent minus bosses, I played through the first 3rd of the game and saw 5 maybe 6 different enemy types, and at the beginning of the 2nd area it looked like larger versions of enemy types from area 1. The "Cool weapons" come from farming the bosses monster hunter style, after you beat the boss the first time you can spend special crystals to for the boss to respawn for an attempt at killing it again to get the drop. again first 3rd of game it seems you need to kill each boss 3x to get ALL the boss weapons. Combat is slow, and attempting to take on multiple enemies at once is not fun, I don't mean it's difficult, i mean it's not fun. It's basically bait a single target out to kill, or spend  your time walking backwards in circles waiting for their attacks to "clump" so you can swing with out being hit and then basically getting stun locked. Loads of empty rooms with nothing in them, if game continues on like this no replay value, very linear not much to explore.  I know it seems I ripped into the game, especially being I got it for free, but asking $40 for this is asinine.While it is.... entertaining, at least for a short time, I'd not be shocked if the devs were still in college and this was their "Final" I'd say spend no more than $10 on this game and that's being generous as there are loads of better games for $5.If there is / are major updates to improve things I'll check it out again, and update my review at that time, until then I'll just have to live knowing, while know it's not going to happen, that the devs should of payed people to play this so they can get some feedback and of released it in a finished condition... Seriously guys, apply for a job at Ubisoft or something, even their games are more complete.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not terrible, and for a studio's debut game it's actually kind of impressive, but I can only recommend this to people who are so into the soulslike genre that they enjoy even weak games in it.The artwork for this game isn't overly unique or interesting. It's generic scifi glowtech vs. bugmonsters. Not awful, but there is nothing here that makes it stick out or is particularly clever.The general gameplay and the controls don't feel snappy. There is just something about them that feels simultaneously stiff and floaty. It's not unplayable, but when you're coming fresh off Elden Ring where the controls are really sharp you'll feel this. The dodging and blocking in particular are weird. Raising your shield takes a moment, but timing blocks right is extremely powerful in this game, even more than parrying in a from soft game. Dodging is very effective, but many enemies lack good animations and telegraphs, instead they get a UI prompt that they are about to perform an unblockable attack. This kind of leaves it without the satisfaction of narrowly avoiding attacks and outsmarting enemies. The biggest issue I have is that the gameplay ideas just kind of miss for me. There is an elemental damage system, but it doesn't really add to the game it's just a chore to match elements to enemies so they take full damage. They only give you two ranged weapon slots so you can't even equip a weapon of each type and have to change loadouts just to be strapped for whatever level you're in. If your best weapon is the wrong element, tough luck. The energy system is bizarre. You effectively have a mana bar that recharges, but gets shorter when you heal yourself, and then has to be replenished with batteries that require you to stand still for a really long time uninterrupted. I'm having a really hard time seeing a reason why this system works the way it does. Nothing about it rewards clever management or risk taking, your health potions just take this weird detour through your energy bar and take forever to drink.The character system is also just not interesting. The only way to give a character unique passives is by advancing down one of three linear technology trees. How do you do that? By equipping pieces of armor of the corresponding technology type. This isn't even a bad idea in theory, it effectively breaks down character builds into ranged, melee and tank and allows you to hybridize as well by mixing armor. In practice it just isn't a deep enough system to make you feel like you're really building a character though.Ranged weapons have special abilities that simply activate at random. Without the ability to use them deliberately they are just kind of irrelevant, you can't rely on them. The game is also extremely linear. There is a bit of exploration here and there to discover some hidden resources, but for the most part there is a singular path forward. Shotcuts back to previous areas sometimes crop up, but serve no actual purpose, since you can teleport between rest sites and backtracking is never necessary as far as I can tell. So overall, while I am not recommending this title I will say that it comes pretty close to being decent. It's one of those games where it looks good enough and has a price point where you expect AA quality, but you're getting some serious indie jank once you're actually playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely do reviews, good or bad. It's my personal belief that games will survive if they're made well, or sink if they aren't. I have to make a special exception for this one. Maybe I've been spoiled by the resurging Soulsborne hype created by ER, maybe I'm just getting crotchety in my old age, truth be told I couldn't tell you. What I can tell you, is that Dolmen sets out to build upon the idea of Dark Souls, but falls flat on its face in every aspect. The "story" is bad. Really bad. The creature design almost reminds me of Independence Day if they had put more than one type of alien in it. The gameplay is clunky, unoriginal, and entirely artificial in terms of difficulty. Within the first 20 minutes I encountered an enemy that did twice the damage of all the others around it, took half the damage per swing, and had no distinction from the others. I wouldv'e settled for bigger even, but no, it was just a super bug. Don't spend money on this game.

The first area is OK, but the rest is packed with empty rooms and no interaction, very lazy design... for example there is a small room with 3 strong ninjas (very badly) hidden and nothing else to do there, dead end. And worse, some enemies don't react if you take them out from a distance and others walk blindly into the fire and get themselves killed. This area (just before the second boss) is only good to farm XP effortlessly as the enemies are always in the same position and follow the same patterns. You can build up your character easily to take on the bosses but I don't see the point if the regular enemies are so bad and predictable. So only buy it cheap if you really like boss battles.

_childDocuments_.review: A sci-fi Souls-like that does its job. It brings nothing revolutionary to the formula, the graphics are not amazing for a 2022 game, but that's totally fine by me. So if you use up too much blue bar healing you will have nothing for your GUN attack. You are able to refill your blue bar, but the action to do so take a fair amount of time and WILL get you hit or KILLED your timing is not spot on. Also hitting the enemy SLOWLY refills your blue bar as well.2ND :  The graphics are not all that bad I would say they are on par with Hellpoint. Also like in Hellpoint and dark souls farming is a thing. Surprising the framing is not Honorable. You will not spend hours trying to get that one item from killing over an over the same enemy, that said because of how the combat works until you get the hang of it YOU WILL NOT HAVE ANY FUN what so ever. Basicly before melee attacking an enemy you will want to use your gun and effect them with the stat of the gun ( ICE,FIRE,ACID ) otherwise you are hitting a brick wall with a wet noddle. ( your not gonna get very far )Taking that with how you will need to manage your BLUE BAR for healing and gun uses I see a lot of people giving up on this game before really giving it a try.3D  :    I would have to agree with a lot of the negative reviews about how this game screams EARLY ACCESS and it does. Given that fact I am hoping that the DEVS do polish up the game ( since i am stuck with it now LOL ) all in all wait fo a sale as it is the price is WAY WAY WAY WAY to high for what the game is, One review had a play time of 12 hours and made the comment of how there are only 3 areas.  ( really hope that is not the case ) Since I seem to have found myself in a spot where I have no where else to go ( really hoping I am missing something ) because you do have the option to re-spawn the bosses ether one or all that you killed up to the point I am at. I am thinking it is for item drops to make farming bosses easier ( O I REALLY HOPE )    6 out of 10    not to bad played much worse

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real hidden gem ... and hard as f*ck; probably the most stressful souls-like I've played so far.80% of enemies ambush you, 10% of enemies lure you into getting ambushed by those mentioned 80%, and the last 10% are bosses and make you start all over again after one-shotting you.I don't know how I completely missed this game on its release date. I recently saw someone do a walkthrough, watched the first 15 minutes and was intrigued. The many bad reviews made me doubt my purchase (got it for 17€) at first, but after 10 hours of gameplay I can tell you for sure:It's a great game if you get it for less than 20€  because it's very short. Whatever the reviews say, it's a souls-like experience par excellence. In its core it is similar to The Surge, Hellpoint or Mortal Shell. No map, no objective, "bonfires" to teleport to your ship, shortcuts, confusing map layout, several completely optional areas and bosses, and very little help whatsoever. The story is weak but the voice acting and overall presentation are very good. The upgrade and progression systems are elaborate and motivating, and enemies drop a lot of items so it's not really grindy. That being said, the game is extremely hard and very stressful because enemies and hazardous environments give you very little room for mistakes. According to the achievements, not even 15% of players  made it into the third area, less than 10% made into the fourth.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Game is janky, but if you are able to look past that, the underlying systems definitely make up for that!(Not done with the game yet, plan on finishing it soon.)Game starts out a bit slow, with low res environements and slow-ish, janky animations. Story is some kind of superior-alien-invading-and-killing-everything-weird-stargate mashup.But after about an hour in, I really came to enjoy this hidden gem here. Crafting system for new armor and weapons seems like a mix of Monster Hunter, where you kill certain enemies and get parts from them and your normal RPG where you find stuff out in the wilds.Actually pretty engaging - go out - hunt enemies - come back - get new stuff - upgrade said stuff to different levels - upgrade said stuff even more with different modular parts you can slot in. Works with armor and weapons.Fighting system is a stamina based mix of melee and gun fights. A bit slow to start with, but after the first act (3-4hrs), enemies get more agile and aggressive. Also you got 3 different elemental statuses, your weapons get a special on hit effect if the status effect is progged on enemies and you also can activate some kind of berserk mode to give yourself more oomph, depending on what core you slotted. Only fought the first three bosses so far, but they were interesting to fight, not just your typical button mashing and hit and run bosses. Leveling up works on one hand like every other game in that genre, you get some kind of exp (which you loose after dying twice without picking them up) and you invest those in stamina, health, skill, ... But on the other hand, depending on what armor you chose you get points in three different "skill trees" (I use that term pretty loosely here), each with three big bonuses (like a big shield explosion after getting hit)Level design is area based, some shortcuts to unlock, some secrets to unravel here and there. Until now I had fun while exploring.Textures are most of the time somewhat low-res, but do the job. First area actually felt somewhat eery, but maybe that's just me. Bugs: At the moment, I encountered one bug when respawning bosses for farming mats - skipping the cutscene (10-15sec) makes your character invisible.Verdict:Release time shortly after Elden Ring probably got expectations of people through the roof; that's the only explanation for me, why the reviews are THAT bad. But if you go in open minded (and can look past some jankyness) this one is a buy from me. Maybe wait for a sale if you are on a tight budget.
