_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Revion Prime!Dolmen is a Sci-fi souls game, by playing the game is possible to see that it draws inspiration from Dead Space in its design, but the core gameplay is a pure souls game!Right now I can see that Dolmen is in a strange spot, people are complaining about the game not being polished like other big souls games or that the combat is clunky, etc. This is a game made primarily by a small team in Brazil, that had a limited budget to give it a shot and bring this project to life, Brazil it's just starting to set foot in the triple-A industry.So, with that being said, let's start with the good.-Combat is incredibly good, and I am impressed! when the game starts the first section is kinda strange, a big section, with several paths to follow, and a lot of enemies. I've felt lost, and I've died A LOT! But then, I just understood how the reactors and the elemental weapons work, and when you get the grip as I did, the combat becomes really interesting and rewarding, suddenly, you become to be careful about your surroundings and how to move correctly to not become stuck or fall and start to focus on win the battles against several enemies that have interesting combat designs.-The enemy's patterns are interesting. Enemies attack with melee, projectiles, they can descend from walls, they can dash, or run towards you, use abilities at the same time that they are attacking, heck, some enemies do a lot of these things at the same time, and when they do, I just run for my life!!-Designs and art direction are great! I love Sci-fi and here we have a game that is mixing Alien creatures with space beasts and you are a futuristic soldier killing them. Scenarios are dark, lights blinking, you get the point, if you like the Dead Space vibe, you're in for a treat.-The story of the game is rich, and is fantastic, it is possible to discover so much about the races involved, the Dolmen crystals, and what happened in the place that game takes place.-The game is optimized. It runs great, I've played some hours, and the only bugs that I've encountered or killed me or I killed them!-The story kinda holds your hands. This is a negative point for me, but it is a personal one, Dolmen presents its story too raw, and the starting point explains too much. For me, I would like more mystery. This also applies to some cinematics, but don't get me wrong, the story is rich and interesting, it's just that the presentation could be better.-Lack of polishment, but I understand why. Yes, this is an indie game, this is the first shot of a studio that tried their best to bring Dolmen to life. Some sounds, interactions, designs, or stuff that is linked to the atmosphere could be better. But as I said Dolmen was tough to be made, it's here, and I am looking forward to some patches so that this game keeps getting better!!In the end, Dolmen is a nice game that you should give a try, I understand that some people are upset about the game, but I think that is not okay to just land a negative review because of the first 20 minutes. Give the game a try first and see for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: After this and Gungrave I don't think I can trust Prime Matter as a publisher anymore. _childDocuments_.review: Game is an utter trash fire.The Good:+ I have nothing positive to say about the execution. Maybe on a very high level some of the ideas here could be done well. But it is not done well here.+ It's name apparently means big ♥♥♥♥ in Swedish which gave me a chuckle.The Bad:- The game has major control issues. My xbox controller by default wasn't detected this isn't great but not a deal breaker,- But once my controller was detected and working the game seems to drop inputs or outright refuse any input as you stand there with full stamina unable to move as enemies get free hits on you.- The controls even when they are working do not feel at all good. From things as simple as camera panning felling stiff, to your attacks felling stiff and feedback from enemies attacking you being non existent, it feels bad to interact with the game.- Boss design is lacking (want to fight a big version of the same enemies you've already been fighting?) and will make you target small enemies at the same time. This could work but the camera doesn't allow for this to work well. You will be attacked from the boss with attacks you cannot see coming as the camera and small fov get in the way. - Speaking of enemies, the design from what I've seen is very generic which goes for the world also. It very much so comes across as an asset flip. Which I don't believe it is, but the assets don't feel designed with a single vision in mind. Rather they feel like a bunch of assets taking at random from all over.This is perhaps the worst souls-like I have tried and it is embarrassing that a group of people came together and had such flawed and horrid felling mechanics that they tried to build a game around. They really needed to get the basics down and make sure it felt good to control before building everything else. I really struggle to understand what they where thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another really cool Souls-like that needs a little more love from souls fans. It is a little janky here and there but its consistent and predictable so you're able to treat it like its part of the challenge. What I mean by that is for example there is a Sekiro style "danger" symbol that indicates an attack is unblockable, on a few of the bosses if you are merely reacting to seeing the symbol you will not be able to react in time. You'll just have to know it's coming from fighting at enemy enough which can definitely get annoying but whatever. Guns are really fun in this game, I mostly played a skill/science build which was fun because guns can do big damage but they are also excellent for applying status effects to bad guys to deal big damage when you slap them around in melee. The armor sets are cool as is the method of crafting better versions of them, and the environments are good. It is a short game taking me only 14 hours to get through and that's with heavy exploration and getting stuck on the odd boss. Definitely a good play if you enjoyed Hellpoint. Not as fleshed out as that game but still a fun ride! Looking forward to a possible sequel in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 6/10 game; if you can nab it for cheap enough (20$ range) it's worth it.Pros. - 1: Combat is pretty clean and the Conditions + Reactors system feels very intuitive and flows well. They make for pretty great resource management and are engaging! 2: The enemy, environment and sound designs are all cohesive and the music compliments them all well enough. 3: The weapons are very fun and satisfying with some unique modifiers, especially in the Ranged Weapons.Cons. - 1: There's not /enough/ combat and once you've beaten the game, that's it; the grind is unsatisfying and there's little reason to farm anything out other than those last few achievements. Start a new character and go again with different setups because there's no end game or post game whatsoever. 2: Maps are way too big with enemies spread out too thin, especially so in certain areas and what feels about half of the game. There's no way to quickly warp to checkpoints, so you have to physically go /all the way/ to them every time, making Farming Routes incredibly tedious due to how LARGE the maps are with no mobility options other than backstep spamming. 3: The crafting/looting are straight up bad and the UI is counter intuitive which makes navigating the menus clunky. Don't spend valuable rarer mats on Tier 1 and Tier 2 armors because those stats do not transition into their stronger versions, which the game does not indicate whatsoever.Overall, I enjoy the game; it's got some strong points, but said points get overshadowed by poor game design in quite a few areas. Story is pretty basic but the written Lore 'journals' flesh it out just enough to have my approval. Would love to see the good parts of this game expanded on and given a lot more replay value similar to Nioh.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that a game that looked so promising (despite its budget and all) and HAD a good start, ends up being a boring, uninspired experience.Let's start with the pros:+ Graphics, optimization, and surprisingly, audio design are good. I ran the game at ultra 1080p 75fps with no hiccups or whatsoever.+ Cool take on ranged combat in Souls-like games, seriously, if the weapons did more damage, they would be even better to use.+ Good animations, above average when it comes to AA games.+ Solid controls.+ Overall, good level design, much better than Code Vein.And there are the only positive points I could think of, really.Now, let's go with the cons:- Basic and uninspired enemy design.- Null variety of weapons and armor (literally, only 3 types of weapons!).- Uninsteresting combo variety.- The parry works when it wants to, and there isn't even a clear indicator when it'll trigger.- Bosses are a pain the ass and  is by far the worst offender of the bunch, doing an attack that's very hard to dodge and also can instakill you.- Normal enemies are hit sponges, and the worst of it is that they can kill you in 3-4 hits!- Trivial plot and lore.- NPCs suck hard.- Samey environments, limited by the setting. If the game happened in a planet, it'd be so much more interesting, but I guess that's because...- Lack of budget, the game drips it everywhere and it shows. IMO, the studio should have aimed for a much smaller game to test the waters with Souls-like mechanics. Something like Titan Souls or Hyperlight Drifter.I think I already said everything I wanted to. Not much to add, but if you really are into sci-fi stuff, have low standards and get this game in a juicy sale, might be worth it.Final score: 4.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: While perhaps one of the lower budget third-person Souls-likes, Dolmen is still passable. It is on the short side, and due to the reliance on firearms is easiest compared to Immortal: Unchained. In fact, close combat often seems to be a very dangerous choice.Of the Souls-likes I have played, strangely, Dolmen seems the easiest to adapt to a different game type. Perhaps in part due to its story, it seems like it could have been a sci-fi survival akin to Dead Space, or a story shooter in the form of Halo.Dolmen's use of energy is at least somewhat curious. Energy is what the player uses for firearms or elemental melee.  So, as additional damage or stamina. At the same time, maximum energy is used to heal or a few select attacks, and can be replenished with batteries. The healing is immediate, meaning it can be used in the middle of a roll or attack but battery use takes time. This means the player has a little bit of a safety net before they need to expose themselves to more danger by standing still. Using it as a bonus stamina bar is also a nice touch.Still, while not amazing it is still an alright time.

_childDocuments_.review: Dolmen is another game in the ever popular Souls-like genre with inspirations from third person shooters like Dead Space, and it's a game that got critically slammed by almost everyone. But I'm not going to slam it, because I honestly really enjoyed my time with this game quite a bit. Sure it's quite amateurish in places, has some balance issues and moments where I'm scratching my head trying to figure out what on Earth the developers were thinking at certain points of the game - but those high points are extremely high, more than enough to make me recommend Dolmen. As usual I break things down into bullet points:Pros:- Satisfying gameplay that strongly encourage mixing up melee and ranged weapons on the fly- A large variety of one handed and two handed weapons, with a nice selection of unique guns with primary and secondary fire modes- Energy system adds a nice resource dynamic, making you balance your healing, guns and reactor as they can cut into each other- Reactor system that allows players to apply extra damage. status and keep their combo going with the energy meter is great- Pushing the players to use status effects creates some great strategies and encourages mixing up your weapons- Technology system that pushes players into using certain gear can allow for some interesting playstyles- Some really great alien locations- Unique and very alien enemies with drastically different behaviours and attack patterns to overcome- The game makes parry-able and unparry-able attacks well defined with some useful visual feedback when enemies wind up their attacks- Most bosses are very good, with a few notable ones being amazing in my opinion- All boss fights are repeatable as many times as you want, so long as you have Dolmen fragments- A grinder's paradise for wanting to get rare drops, materials and currency for levels ups, though no grinding is required to beat the game- Robust crafting system that is your only way to get gear, but allows you to tune them with upgrade materials- Has some nice fashion- It's short length works in its favour, as it doesn't outstay its welcome- A more straight forward story compared to other Souls-likes, if you prefer thatCons:- Level design is a huge mixed bag; some areas are really well designed and fun to play through, while other areas are far too big with far too much running and nothing else- Enemy placements are also a mixed bag, with some placed very well while others are scattered around places all hodge podge while some massive areas have no enemies at all- Some boss runs are agonizing, thanks to spread out checkpoint placements and zero shortcuts to previous ones- Painfully linear, a straight line from A to B with only a couple of offshoots- No New Game Plus, meaning all you can do after beating the game is grind for achievements or restart a new game- Some enemies are irritating and quite unbalanced in damage output and defense- Certain enemies can have unblockable attacks or poor telegraphing- Certain guns like the shotgun and Driller MG has its spread increased when locked on, locking off and aiming makes them much better- Multiplayer is disappointing, as it's reserved purely for boss fights- Story and lore fails to grasp, with not much going on outside of what you're playing- Voice acting is very amateurish, but the boring kind sadly- The UI in the most of the game menus is horrible and needlessly hard to keep track of things- Full price is asking for way too muchSo yes, the sci-fi theme and the mixing of gunplay really drew me to this game - as a fan of Hellpoint and Immortal Unchained it seemed totally up my alley. However the game falls short compared to both of those in several areas mentioned in the cons, which are some glaring faults for me and it's easy to see why people may not like the game, but the biggest thing holding Dolmen back is easily the price. If the game was £15-£20 at full price then it would be a lot easier to digest, but sadly £38 is asking for far too much for a game as flawed as this. I picked it up at 75% off which was about £9 and I'd say I definitely got my money's worth and really enjoyed my time with the game despite the obvious stumbles.Perhaps the developers can really iron out the issues and polish things up with a DLC or even a full on sequel at some point, but as it stands it's a very flawed but extremely enjoyable game for the part, and I recommend it for Souls-likes fans looking for something a bit different to the usual formula.EDIT: Added a couple pros and cons that I forgot about while writing this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't honestly understand why people hate on this as much as they do, it made me go in sceptical of the experience but in the end I actually enjoyed it from start to finish. As far as souls-like or souls-lite games go, sure it ain't exactly top of the board or anything but it isn't NEARLY as bad as most are making it out to be, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥' way...its FINE bro, it works, its short and its interesting.Put it this way...its like Hellpoints slightly special sibling, you can see the family resemblance but it's still in its infancy and a bit slower upstairs...it needs to grow more to be a rival at all but it shows potential. It was honestly a really good attempt. The price is a bit steep for how much you get and the fact that it isn't really competition for others of its ilk, that is something else I can agree on, this is more a 15-20 pound product...generous? maybe, but probably still better to get it on a good sale too.There isn't really much you can say about these types of games that hasn't been said a million times, they all follow a very similar formula and just repaint it to be fit for purpose. Stats, weapons, armour, bosses, the eerie silence as you wander around wondering whether you might be ambushed at any point or not, dead bodies scatter every corner you look and the hallways are tainted in darkness that tells a foreboding story. There's an interesting--albeit small--selection of enemy types you'll encounter and besides the 3 main bosses, there's 1 or 2 mini bosses in between each of them. The bosses were fairly easy, they telegraph their moves making them easy to predict and dodge, but making the occasional mistake is never fatal as long as you act accordingly with your heals and their TTK (Time To Kill) is reasonable. You have your "bonfires" you can use to teleport around or back to the safety of your ship where you can allocate points into stats, craft new tiers of gear or change the colour of your armour if you fancy a palate change.What I found interesting was the passives you could gain depending on which types of gear you wore. There are 3 lines of technology; Human, Revian and Driller and they all do something a little different to compliment your chosen build. Wearing a mix of each type of armour allows you to net a little something from all 3, or you can just focus on one and change it up as you see fit. Going hybrid didn't really detract from the experience either, it didn't feel like it made it harder, in fact it almost felt like the other way around due to how the different technologies can compliment one another.It's good, I definitely recommend giving it a go, but maybe wait for a sale first!

_childDocuments_.review: so look. this is not as good as elden ring or any of the other from games. Its not the best souls like ive played and ive played a lot of them. It is my new favorite genre since the end of good fps and immersive sims. That being said it isnt that bad. I dont want to give the impression that it will become your favorite game because there are some problems for sure. It is not however as bad as some of the reviews will tell you. It ran really well looked pretty good and was fun to play. It isnt super long which i liked but its still a good 15 to 20 hour game depending on your skill. Everything is kinda basic on a souls like level but the maps are pretty fun to go through. The enemies are distinct and have their own patterns and ways to defeat them. I like the bosses. They were all pretty memorable and required some skill to get through. On the bad side. Its straight forward. There isnt a ton of secrets. Almost no npcs. There is a small delay between some actions and it can feel restricting. But my final verdict will be a 7 out of 10. It all works and i enjoyed my time. If you like souls like games and it is on sale give it a shot if you dont like it refund it. I got it for 10 bucks. I wouldnt pay full price for it but it is always on sale

Cosmic Horror and Sci-Fi are two ways to talk about Dolmen. It is a third person action game with RPG elements but with a lovecraftian plot that calls players to find what's behind the darkest secret of the universe! A forgotten planet called Revion Prime will be the place where the action takes part. And it won't be easy: Adaptation and exploration will be your main weapons as you craft new items and equipments from your enemies' carcasses! Every step can be your last one!

Use your experience points to improve yourself and face what no human has ever faced. After all, quoting David Hume: "The life of man is of no greater importance to the universe than that of an oyster." Maybe he was right Or not.

name: The Talos Principle 2
detailed_description: Born into a new world where biological humanity is extinct but human culture lives on in a city of robots, you find yourself swept up in a mind-bending adventure involving a mysterious megastructure hiding enormous powers. The more you discover, the more you will be confronted with questions about the nature of the cosmos and the purpose of civilization. The broken promise of a better tomorrow, the fear of repeating humankind’s mistakes, faith in reason or renouncing humanity altogether - the choices you make and the sides you take will determine the course of events. A New Generation of Puzzles Solve a wide array of puzzles with varying difficulty levels, including clever metapuzzles and highly challenging Gold puzzles. Finish the game without solving every puzzle, or pursue the rewards of complete mastery. A variety of new abilities, such as gravity manipulation and mind transference, join the established mechanics of the original Talos Principle, creating a fresh but familiar experience. A Philosophical Odyssey Take the next step forward in the story of The Talos Principle in a thought-provoking, character-driven interactive story with multiple endings penned by returning writers Jonas Kyratzes (The Eternal Cylinder, Clash: Artifacts of Chaos) and Tom Jubert (The Swapper, Subnautica), joined by Verena Kyratzes (The Hand of Merlin, Serious Sam 4). Brave New World Explore more than a dozen all-new environments, from a city on the brink of a paradigm shift to the varied landscapes of a mysterious island that holds the keys to the future. Take a break from puzzle-solving to discover long-buried secrets and strands of forgotten history. The Melodies of Creation Immerse yourself in the rich, bittersweet world of The Talos Principle with a stunning soundtrack by master composer Damjan Mravunac (Serious Sam, The Talos Principle), with a guest appearance by Chris Christodoulou (Risk of Rain 1 and 2).

name: Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials
detailed_description: *Crash* ... That was the sound of you landing face first in an abyss filled with monsters, traps, and eldritch secrets. But hey, it's ok barbarian, you are not alone: Pip, your best friend—and mysteriously luminous bat—is with you. And it's only by truly working together that you'll be able to solve the abyss' puzzles, fight off its hungry denizens, discover its true purpose and maybe -just maybe- make it out alive with the secrets of the primordials. Key Features Gain new skills for your barbarian and elemental powers for Pip, the (magic) bat! A narrative-driven metroidvania with dialogue choices and plenty of humor and snark. Big numbers! 400+ rooms, 20+ hours of evolving gameplay, 10+ bosses, 60+ minutes of music and almost 30,000 words of text that a barbarian would never bother to read! Puzzles. A multitude of assists available to tailor the difficulty to your needs, like slow motion, regen, extra loot & stats! RPG elements with a level-up minigame. Contains more fruit throwing than probably any other game. Companions that join you in your quest and help you out in fights. Multiple endings based on your choices and actions. The thrown fruit are NOT wasted, they are eaten by the bat (who is magic). A ton of secrets and hidden loot just about everywhere. The (magic) bat has a whopping FIVE different squeaking sounds! Fewer repetitive jokes than this description has. A controller is recommended for an optimal experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: Main dev is my brother.Fun fact: Main dev started drawing cave dungeon levels full of monsters, traps and fireballs on large sheets of paper at age 7. So he knows his stuff.This game is a great Metroidvania full of hidden secrets. The whole game is drawn by pixel by pixel and a lot of work has been done on the light effects. Musics are beautiful. Dialogues are fun and full of surprises. Batbarian can be quite challenging when it comes to bosses but there is always a way to manage if you learn their patterns and grind a little.If you like Metroidvanias, you'll like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Batbarian is not a bad game, and it has several good things going for it, but ultimately despite me trying very hard to give it the benefit of the doubt it didn't end up winning me over and I found myself not even having the patience to beat it.First, the good: The presentation is excellent. I love the tiny, well-animated sprites, the dialogue is fun and the plot offers enough to keep me interested. Like most Metroidvanias, it is satisfying to get progressively stronger, to gain access to areas I wasn't able to reach before, and to solve clever puzzles.Now, the bad: When the game started, I found myself in a dark cave, the only source of light my bat companion who emanates an aura of radiance. Soon I found an infinite supply of fruit I could throw to get my bat to fly around the room, revealing terrain, enemies and switches. "Cool", I thought, "The gimmick of the first area is limited visibility." But I was wrong. That's the gimmick for the . I found myself constantly having to take baby steps everywhere I went, even in rooms I had already been through. Enemies I couldn't see would catch me off guard, I would fall into holes because I didn't notice them quick enough, and finding switches was a pain because I couldn't even see what they had activated.Now, when you level up you have control over which of three stats gets boosted: Attack, defense, or visibility. In theory, increasing your visibility makes it easier to see more of the room around you. In practice, I found the difference to be so negligible that it felt like a waste not to upgrade my attack power instead. To be fair, the game includes a menu of optional tweaks designed to make the game easier and more accessible (kind of like Celeste). The first of these tweaks was "increased lighting", which dramatically made the game more playable (and didn't prevent me from unlocking achievements). But even with that option active, I often found myself frustrated at my lack of awareness of my surroundings.I don't like playing 2D platformers with an analog stick, which is the way this game is intended to be played. I spent about 15 minutes tinkering with button mapping until I found a layout I was comfortable with, but even that included compromises. I didn't like the throwing mechanic (which is a BIG part of the game), and I hated how the fruit variations could only be carried in extremely limited numbers, making it difficult to experiment with them and punishing me if I missed throws.The map represents each room with a single square, so if I wanted to backtrack to a place I had been I might not realize that I could only access a particular room if I approached from a different room that led to a corridor inaccessible from the room I was in (even though the map showed my room and the next room connected). Backtracking in general is a chore. Jumping never felt natural to me, and there are way too many jumps with blocks placed specifically for you to knock your head against mid-jump. The jumping also made some boss fights feel much more difficult than they should have been.It's worth noting that puzzle-solving is a main mechanic and not just something you'll occasionally find yourself doing. Many, many rooms involve figuring out what combination of bat form and throwable projectile to use, then trying to get a handle of the cumbersome controls in order to pull off some demanding and unforgiving platforming. Trying to find new paths felt cumbersome and often just led to dead ends with no progress made.Despite its issues I did often find myself enjoying Batbarian. But as the game progressed I found myself feeling frustration more than satisfaction, and eventually I decided I just wasn't having enough fun to warrant sticking with it to the end. There are some clever ideas here, and I'm sure there are people who the game will appeal to way more than it did to me, but in the end it's got too many issues to earn my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this game starts pretty nice. The movement feels good, and at least for the earlier level designs, they're moderately challenging and feel satisfying to complete. The design is clever. The writing is nicely tongue-in-cheek, and I generally like the setting and the characters. The art is exceptional at getting across more detail than is technically present - a real testament to how skilled the artist is. The music is great, the sound design is solid, the color palette is vibrant and varied. The game is a blast for the first few areas.This changes. There's a large spike in difficulty when you get to a later area with fire and ice, and that spike in difficulty was abrupt enough to make it difficult to determine which next room was REQUIRED for progression. Finding secrets should be hard, sure. Finding your progression? I don't know if that should suddenly be so difficult that you can't tell which way to go.It gets substantially worse later, however. Eventually you reach a part of the game where you'll be on low health constantly, so when you hit a puzzle room that takes a couple of minutes to set up to even attempt to complete, and then you die immediately and the checkpoint restarts you on low health AGAIN so you have to spend several minutes setting the room up AGAIN to try it one time out of the TEN or so needed to get the timing and jumps right...well, it sucks enough fun out of it that even when you complete the puzzle, it just feels like you overcame an annoyance rather than accomplished something.This is compounded by the throwing. I'm sorry, but using the right stick to throw only really works in games that do not require you to be doing a lot of other complex actions at the same time - and this one DOES. If you're aiming, you either have to give up on jumping and attacking, or you have to put your controller down and claw-hand it - and that means you can't use the triggers, which are NECESSARY at several points in the game. If you didn't have a control scheme in mind for throwing that worked well, you probably shouldn't have made it a central element of your game. Every time I hit a part of the game where combat requiring throwing occurred, I just shut off - all enjoyment gone, interest zero. These fights are not worth half the time they take. (This gets worse when you get more elements for pip, and your controls immediately feel like they've lost their precision)Also leveling up feels worthless. I understand that the levels improve things in a variety of ways, but the step ups are so minuscule at each level that it feels as if the levels are entirely inconsequential. And yes, I know the assist options are a thing. But at what point would anyone use these? Health regen might be useful, but that feels like something you should be EARNING through progression, not just flicking on in the menu. All of that being said...it's still a very well made game, and it's challenging. If you can handle the throwing controls and the occasional infuriatingly placed checkpoint, then this is still a very good game. I have finished the game now, albeit not with enough completion for the true ending. The ending was...well, nothing surprising there, but I can say that at least the opening of the final act included a very nice subversion of the 'it was all a dream' idea. For that alone, I'll change my recommendation of the game to recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials

_childDocuments_.review: (Referred to as just  from now on)  was somewhat of a surprise for me in terms of difficulty, since I’ve played through several Metroidvanias in the pastI knew what to expect on the surface. However, this title in particular  thoroughly put me through my paces in regards to the boss fights which was somewhat unexpected on first glance of this title. Boss fights is definitely where this game shines the most with exploration and finding secrets coming in close behind it.• Fun and challenging platforming throughout• Loads of puzzles and secrets to make your character strong• Compelling and intriguing story• Each boss battle is varied and challenging in different ways• Assist mode which makes the game easier if you’re having too much trouble• 3 different endings that require you to defeat (or not) different bosses and unlock secret passages• Dialogue is humours throughout the entire game• Pips different abilities provide the player with new mechanics to reach new places, make enemies weak and avoid getting hit• Some odd platforming sections that seemed to need prior knowledge to avoid taking damage• Sometimes difficult to tell what’s a platform and what’s part of the background• When there’s loads of enemies on one screen, it really gets cluttered along with the enemies projectiles• Leveling up is done with a weird wheel that I guess is meant to be random but is slow enough for you to easily upgrade the stat you want, which begs the question of why bother with a mechanic like this?Exploration is done like any standard Metroidvania, you’ll progress through a maze like cave with certain areas being restricted, requiring some ability to gain access to it. Getting lost or not really knowing where to go next is somewhat part of the experience, giving off a sense of satisfaction when you finally figure out where to go next (or feeling dumb for not trying to do that sooner). You’ll acquire a handful of different abilities but the more unique one is using your magical bat named Pip. You’ll gain new elements for Pip to change to on the fly, being able to change his aura to fire, ice or neutral. This mechanic isn’t just used to gain access to new places however, you can block enemy projects by using the right element. For example fire can block ice, ice can block fire and neutral can block purple flames, the game utilises this in a number of different ways, most notably with some of the late game bosses that use magic to attack you. Pips’ neutral stat is also used as a light source in the dark areas you explore, you can throw a berry to move Pip ahead to see where you’re going, throw a berry that Pip hates to get him to attack an enemy and throw a stick berry to make Pip stay in one area for longer. These mechanics all work well together and provide extremely valuable against certain bosses.To traverse through the dark abyss you’ll need to platform your way around the place, who knew that caves were so conveniently designed this way! As you progress the difficulty of platforming increases, but a considerable amount in certain places. Sometimes figuring out what to do isn’t quite straight forward or easy, so it's lucky that you can damage boost your way through spikes if the path ahead looks too difficult to get through. It's possible, obviously, to get through the entire game without having to damage boost your way through, but sometimes it seems that you’ll take more damage trying to do it the legitimate way than if you purposely took a few hits to get through.The platforming segments are consistent throughout, and you’ll also be present with a multitude of puzzles to solve to progress. They are mostly self explanatory but sometimes can be slightly confusing if you overlook a pressure plate or switch that gets lost in the background scenery. Puzzles mainly utilise Pips abilities once again, and do require some form of forethought before steaming in and making moves immediately. Though, in some situations where you can mess up a puzzle, you can enter a portal that resets the room allowing you to try again instantly.Challenge is definitely no exception for this title despite the cute pixel art style that this game inherits, it definitely packs a punch with boss battles and might catch some people off guard. Each boss you encounter is vastly different from the last using new mechanics that you used to platform around that area and explore. But this brings up the age old discussion of fairness. A boss battle has to have a sense of difficulty but also being fair, the obvious franchise that this is most commonly brought up in would be . This game by no means shares common ground with DS, the only thing these titles loosely have in common is challenge.  for the most part is fair, you’ll have to learn the boss’s moves and react accordingly, however there is one particular boss that crosses the line.Until you reach near the end of the game the bosses will be challenging, you’ll be killed countless times trying to learn their movesets before you eventually get the hang of it. However, when you put two bosses together and expect the player to defeat them both simultaneously then it crosses the line of being fair. This boss caused me the most trouble and personally was the hardest in the title and for good reason. With one of them throwing projectiles whilst the other using an extremely long lance that can span almost the entire width of the screen, as well as pressure plates that shoot out fire from either side, then you're in for a rough fight. This might’ve been passable if this boss was optional but alas, it wasn’t.I can see a lot of players giving up at that point just because of the unfair nature of the fight. Sure, it's doable (barely defeated them with half a heart of health myself) but it does feel unfair with too much going on to really keep track of at once.As you progress and explore this mysterious abyss inside of a mountain, you’ll come across different areas that are distinctly different from one another both visually and mechanically. No two areas feel the same and they are even coloured differently on the map so you can correlate them to their areas. Some enemies are area specific and manage to blend in with the environments accurately to make it look like they’ve always been there. is a satisfying and challenging Metroidvania that provides hundreds of secrets and a compelling story line that I won’t spoil here. It definitely proves to be a challenge, particularly with its bosses despite the charming pixel art style that it uses. The mechanics used for your bat Pip are fleshed out and utilised in different ways to help you on your journey in more ways than one. Overall, it's a great Metroidvania that I would recommend to anyone who likes this particular genre.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A fun, charming, 12-20hr Metroidvania focused on action and technically-challenging puzzle-platforming, with plenty of secrets to track down, optional challenges, and a fair bit of world-building to satisfy explorers. Multitasking is required through timed precision platforming sections, and toggle-able assists provide a great approach to adaptive difficulty which might feel necessary in the late-game. And Pip is adorable. Can't wait to see what Demonic Pixels conjure up next!An immensely enjoyable Metroidvania romp that wears its inspirations on its sleeve and owns it. It doesn't take itself too seriously, but it is by no means a walk in the park. Assists can be toggled on the fly to make parts of the game easier without sacrificing any achievement runs or save file progress. The game clearly takes elements from greats of the genre such as Symphony of the Night, Super Metroid, and La-Mulana, and implements them to great effect in a much more concise package whilst emphasising action- and puzzle-platforming gameplay.Some sections of the game can feel absolutely brutal, such as when you need to quickly and precisely manoeuvre your acrobatically-challenged barbarian through a timed platforming challenge, dodging spike traps and jumping at the last possible moment, all whilst throwing fruits for your adorable bat companion to gobble up. The upshot of this is that you feel absolutely unstoppable once you've conquered a challenging room, and over the course of the game you learn how to push your barbarian's movement to its limits, granting you a feeling of mastery and immense satisfaction as you breeze through rooms filled with traps and enemies.Then you hit a new room, or an old foe of a platforming section, and those feelings are replaced with ones of determination, frustration, despair, more determination, and the cycle repeats. The aforementioned assists help greatly in this regard, and I certainly made use of them when I felt overwhelmed. There are plenty of optional challenges if you really want to test your mastery of the game mechanics, some of which exist solely for a (well-deserved) sense of accomplishment.Exploration and a sense of wonder are what I look for in a Metroidvania, and Batbarian certainly delivers. There are plenty of collectibles and upgrades hidden around the map, which is itself not enormous, giving the feeling of a world which is just full to bursting with secrets to uncover. Graffiti and old notes line the caverns, providing hints, clues, and backstory to the world which can change how you perceive the threats around you, or nudge you in the right direction and give you an "Aha!" moment for a puzzle you've long-since abandoned.The characters you encounter are charming and have plenty of personality, with myriad dialogue options giving you the opportunity to shape how your barbarian approaches them - will you swear vengeance for the fate you've suffered, or will you simply let every single person you encounter know how much you hate magic and just want to smack them in the face? There isn't a huge amount of character development in the game, but what there is presents a welcome addition to the genre, reinforcing the fact popularised (for many) by Hollow Knight that you don't need to forego all sense of charm in your characters to provide an experience which can still leave players feeling isolated and afraid of the unknown.The soundtrack absolutely slaps. It feels perfectly suited to the detailed environments and emphasises the story beats, with the area's music fading out to an ominous, oppressive. minimalist score as you approach a boss encounter, before hitting you with a bombastic boss battle theme as your barbarian and bat brawl with the behemoth before you.It's not a perfect game, of course. There are times when my barbarian felt clunky and some encounters felt downright unfair, or when I felt cheated by the game because a slight deviation of the stick as you throw a stone or fruit can mean you completely whiff at the end of a timed platforming challenge. The assists help in these situations, giving you boosted battle capabilities or slowing down time as you line up a shot, and being able to switch them on the fly is a brilliant way of implementing adaptive difficulty.I enjoyed my time with Batbarian immensely, and while I haven't seen absolutely everything the game has to throw at you (the optional challenge rooms might be beyond me), I can say with certainty that I am more than satisfied with it. Its unique approach to navigating the world with limited movement capabilities and a single ranged ability (used almost entirely for puzzle solving) is refreshing, and leaves you with a sense of accomplishment once you learn to manoeuvre more effectively and make the most out of every jump, thrown stone, and Pip's abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Breath of fresh air! Batbarian focuses on atmosphere; it captures the feeling of being trapped within a dungeon. Enemies are strong, rests are few and far between, and the darkness is nearly all-encompassing. All this allows the game's relationships to shine--and there's no bond deeper than the one between a barbarian and their bat. It also allows the quirky sense of humor to land, which is probably the game's most stunning accomplishment.I'd recommend playing with the assists, especially for some of the boss combat. Also, please place diligent markers on your map. Don't be like me and leave it mostly blank until you need to go through every room in a mad scramble for those last few gems.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often give my opinion on a game (and I've played a lot...), but I was shocked to see the low number of reviews. This game deserves way more recognition.After the first hour of the game, here's how I would have summed up the game : a more accessible version of La Mulana, with the same kind of humour as The Messenger, but with interesting light-based mechanics.Now, I have finished the game (99,5%, missing one chest that is nowhere to be found) and here's what I have to say :+ : the music is really good, as in "I will listen to it even after I finish the game" good.+ : the art is great but I was hoping we would see more "highly detailed sprites" as we see at some occasions, they look really good.+ : the design of the puzzles is on point, nothing too easy, nothing impossible. + : I like this kind of humour, it's not often a game makes me laugh but this one made me laugh OUT LOUD a few timesAside from that, the movements of the character are not often as precise as we'd expect, it can be hard to jump on a platform above you if it means going to the side then back again for example. I did not feel the need to read the papers and notes scattered around the game, but I did feel compelled to read all the dialog (but it should be noted that following the story is important). The combat system is pretty basic, and a few extra attacks would have been welcome.The power ups gained during level-ups don't seem to have a lot of impact (I couldn't see any difference probably because the enemies' strength would scale up as well).Since our movements and attacks are limited, the fights can often turn out to be quite messy, with enemies everywhere and the character forced to tank damage and hit everything as quickly as possible like... a barbarian. Batbarian isn't perfect, but there aren't many games that make me want to play MORE. And here I wish there were more zones to explore because of how I enjoyed it. Great job really, can't wait to see what you do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Do yourself a favor and pick up the OST. It's rare for a Metroidvania to nail the music so well, but the electric violin kills it.If you want to see my first impressions as they happened, watch my video above. Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials is a straightforward Metroid-style action-platformer with dialogue choices. Control starts off mediocre but feels good the moment you gain the ability to sprint. You have an adorable bat named Pip and get to throw fruit and rocks (and presumably more later). I chose our female protagonist with the claws, eager to slice through everything in my way. And as another diversion from the traditional Metroid formula, you also get companions whose attacks act as a more limited special attack than you would have in a Castlevania.The Steam description doesn't do this game justice. The music is worth the price of admission alone, the dialogue rides the careful line of being witty without being overbearing, and gameplay is more than satisfactory. The darkness of each room lets you feel claustrophobic. But it's the occasional room and boss battle where this game shine. The first non-boss boss room includes three traps that you get to trigger against waves of enemies. It's a fantastic moment and rewards good gameplay. The first boss fight: a simple giant slime, managed to narrowly beat me for my first game over (with a Zelda-esque death sound I wasn't expecting).Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials is a game I wholeheartedly recommend. Buy it now if you can afford it. Wishlist it if you can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Batbarian is an interesting game, very basic but not in a bad way at all, if you're looking for a fun game with some humorous moments and settings that allow you to play in varying ways to suit you then you got a winner on your hands, I will say no new game plus which is a huge minus for various reasons but even so it was a good time I'd be happy to play again dood.Okay the meat of the game! So to start you get the choice of "male barbarian!" Who dons a mighty long sword and then you have "Female barbarian!" of whom has claw gauntlets which are awesome, now I don't now if there's a difference between the two classes but it's nice to have the choice isn't it dood?Gameplay consists of walking, attacking and throwing a lot, that's really it, which ironically isn't as bad as it sounds with the light mechanics and puzzles in the game as well as various ways to take on or even not take on enemies and your trusty bat Pip who travels with you (hence the name batbarian if it wasn't obvious lol) has various mechanics of it's own dood.The difficulty is...interesting, if you decide to do it normally then the game is frankly frustrating at times, beatable but goodness it's gonna test your skills, especially with how bosses have quite frankly annoying puzzle aspects to them and so much happening on screen that you don't know where to look and sometimes you barely have a choice in getting hit even as you need to attack, on top of that one boss was quite frankly RNG to the maximum but I will leave that for one good reason I will explain in the next paragraph dood.So abooout difficulty, you see as hard as the game is, there are a lot of things that will help you, yes you! the player feel like a god among men! Or women...or both I dunno, still there's an assist mode, this has various functions including health regen when your health gets real low, slow motion throws, higher attack and defence, more item drops, more experience, double effects on the items you pick up, better lighting and possibly one or two more I forgot, now granted I did not use any of these until after I beat the game, I have standards but after I did I used it to get the two easier endings because once was enough for me XD still these settings are a great way to vary your gameplay and either just give you a little extra edge or right out have a win mode, which I appreciate for players who need that extra hand or people who want to do a fun run dood.Treasure is a thing, it varies from gold, gems, (which you trade for stuff) permanent stat upgrades (which like the levels themselves I have to admit they weren't all that great but I guess they did enough) and sometimes progression items or the like, the issue though is not all treasure is in a chest, suffice to say there's a way later on to get an effect that tells you if a treasure is around...as long as it's in a chest, frankly for one particular item this made it frustrating and probably accounts for a large chunk of my gameplay believe it or not as I literally marked the whole map and went through each room one by one to no avail only to find the item in a random rock that doesn't even look like you can get to it, hope the devs never do that again dood. (not even worth it honestly which was the saddest part) The story was oddly interesting for a game I expected to be more funny than serious, although you do have the choice between being serious or joking around kinds of dialogue which I appreciate, it actually managed to get me pretty hype at points, I will say though that an aspect of the story is one that people tend to dislike a lot but I felt had a reasonable excuse for it myself dood.Improvements? Let's see, the basic difficulty with no help is a liiittle much, especially for some of the puzzle elements of the bosses, granted if the aim was for roguelike difficulty then it's totally fine, then there's switching aspects of Pip (trying not to spoil) considering how many buttons weren't uses I feel as though having a separate button would have been better, switching was at times a nightmare as you need to be so quick with it that I at least often pressed the wrong bumper and switched to the wrong thing, having a separate bumper for each would be easier to remember than "wait was it left or right? I forgot I'm being killed!?" and finally if you are going to make bosses as hard as you are yet have times of invincibility and even RNG you need to either make it a very short segment or lower the damage for that part because wow did that kill me a loooot and it never felt fun or fair in a lot of cases dood.Okay so yeah, it's a fun game, I wouldn't pay a huge amount for it, especially with no new game plus to speak of which is always a wasted opportunity in these kinds of games but it's definitely a game I'm happy I played, I hope this review helps you decide if you want to buy the game or not and if you do I hope you all have a great time, thank you for reading dood ^-^/

_childDocuments_.review: Other than it's ungoogable name, Batbarian is an excellent Metroidvania that certainly matches the best of the genre has to offer. It's unique selling point is the strange , but effective, mix of platforming puzzle and precise jumping action that coalesce into well-crafted and demanding adventure. Below are noteworthy points:- Unlike most Metroivania, this isn't a character action game, most of the progression comes from your Pip, the glowing bat. Your traversal and combat options remain mostly identical during the whole game.- The puzzles in this game are REAL brainy puzzle that demand a bit of pause before proceeding further.- The game features a slew of optional assists to customise the experience; including one to make the game less dark if it isn't your thing.- The music is awesome :P- The game feature modern checkpoints, usually respawning you close to where you died (instead of a save point you crossed 20 mins ago).In short, this game is excellent, fan of Metroidvanias or not. It was easily worth it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Very funny metroidvania. When I write reviews, I like to give a fair look at both what the game gets right and also the things it could improve on, but honestly, I can't think of anything Batbarian really needs to do better. If you are a fan of these kinds of games, Batbarian is the real deal.  It has a seriously funny story, charming characters, a detailed world, fun chiptunes, beautiful pixel art, and secrets galore! Batbarian is so jam-packed with secrets, I scarcely go even a couple rooms without coming across a hidden area. It really rewards the investigative player... the one that likes to strike every wall and jump into every corner of the world. I also would like to mention one more thing. When I first bought the game, I had some issues getting it to run right. Any gamer who has been around for a while has no doubt come across games that use the Unity Engine and probably has experienced the dreaded Unity stutter. Unfortunately, Batbarian was stuttering quite bad on my computer. Well, I posted about it in the Steam forums. Not even a couple hours later the developer responded to help me out. We went back and forth for a while trying different things out, but to no avail. So I did a bit of research and discovered a fix that seems to work for a lot of Unity games having the same problem: run it in exclusive fullscreen. Unfortunately, the game didn't support this. Guess what? The developer actually coded it into the game that very same day and gave me a beta version to try out. It worked! No more stutter! How many developers do you know that give that kind of individual attention to one little dude having a problem that no one else seemed to suffer from? In an industry where so many publishers and developers simply view us gamers as walking wallets to be exploited, this kind of behavior needs called out and rewarded. So thanks guys. You really made my day.So guys and gals, Batbarian is a great game. Easily the best metroidvania I've played all year (and this year had some serious contenders). If you are a fan of the genre, this is one you definitely don't want to miss this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good.I bought it after testing the demo and I do not regret anything. It is exactly what the demo sells.Good plateformer with secrets, puzzles, secrets in secrets, fights, boss that are not boring till now... all the ingredients are here. Not clunky at all. Checkpoints everywhere. Good exploration. Character skills increase by different ways. Imaginative. And it is stupid fun. Largely inspired from the classics such as Wonder boy and well done.--Edit--Hard at times. Especially if you want to get everything. Some puzzles are really based on reflexes so, even if you understand how to get access to that safe, making it may be another story.For the bosses, if it is too difficult, it is probably because you lack something. So, go back to explore, find what you did previously miss then come back to conclude the fight.Checkpoints are not everywhere. But close to. You may not want to immediately struggle in one place with the risk of dying and have to redo 3 or 4 hard maps. Continue a bit your exploration. Find the next checkpoint and make your life easier. You will probably have unlock shortcuts in between that will permit to access the hard stuff with a save just before.Dungeon is really well done in that manner.Still very good game to me. But I play it by fractions. Never a very long trip. Because the required repetition for some puzzles is exhausting.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure - I know the devs and received a free beta build to test.  That said....This game is a strong buy!!  Not sure if my hours played will show up with this review but I put in over 100 hours and loved every single moment.This world is IMMERSIVE. Wonderful dynamic pixel art that is by turns cute, demonic, and frightening.  Every character's animations show the love and care that the devs put in.  Each area has a distinct feel that is complemented by an out-of-this world soundtrack that will pull you in and sit you right in the middle of this sprawling secret-filled dungeon.  In one part where you actually see some sunlight, you will find yourself breathing a sigh of relief.The fruit and aura mechanics are novel and keep the gameplay fresh, allowing access to a surprising breadth of puzzles should the player desire them.  I went in expecting a run-of-the-mill pixel art metroidvania and was blown away by the depth and cleverness (though always fairness) of the puzzles.  The puzzles are pleasingly simple, friendly, and yet challenging enough to be quite rewarding.  Many of these puzzles hide optional powerups that can help you on your way but aren't necessary, so if you are a completionist and/or a puzzle fiend, there will be plenty for you to enjoy, but if you just want to go on an adventure and and explore and fight and level up, you can do that too without being forced into excessive puzzling.The boss fights are tough but fair and engaging enough in their movements and animations that I didn't mind the times I needed several attempts to get past them.Finally, the characters and dialogue can only be described as thoroughly charming.  Personalities (including those of fallen adventurers who went before you) are well developed, and provided me with a good number of out-loud belly laughs.The game builds to an incredible crescendo as you start to discover what's going on.  I won't say much more other than the gravity of my mission weighed heavily on me as it appeared the story was beginning to come to a close. Overall I played for many times the number of hours that the devs expected, but I just couldn't put it down until I'd discovered every last secret, put every puzzle to bed, and seen all of the endings.12/10 would (and did) fall down into a cave and throw fruit for the world's cutest animated bat again and again and again.  This game felt very special to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials

_childDocuments_.review: Oofta. If I could give a "neutral" instead of a thumbs up or a thumbs down, I would.This game does so much right! The atmosphere is great and cohesive (it isn't just "cave level the game" it's got some bite to it, I attribute a lot of this to fantastic sound design and the lore directly reflecting the enemies), the writing is on point (I was skeptical of the humor in the first couple hours, but even the lame jokes have good payoffs later), and the puzzles were shockingly well made! I don't want to give any spoilers here, which restricts me from talking up a lot of the good points, but this was overall a fun game.The puzzles in particular were worth their weight, thinking on it. I'm always down for a brain-tickler, and trying to navigate between switches, buttons, sliding blocks, and elemental effects could get really complex at times. Plenty "aha!" moments to go around....Three problems though. Excuse me whilst I rant, this comes from a place of love.First: Movement is borked. The acceleration feels off? You move slow, then speed up drastically. I've seen this type of acceleration scheme before, but this one feels particularly rough. Throw in one-tile jumps, disappearing platforms, and timed segments, and I still hadn't fully adjusted by the time I reached the end. Second: This one has a name- Pip. Pip blocks shots of certain elements and alters the environment depending on his element. You can move him around by throwing berries. To throw berries at the correct spot, you have two terrible methods to do so, but that's not even what I'm complaining about. Nonono, see, Pip is needed for platforming. Light a crystal to power a platform, freeze a dude to stand on him, so on and so forth.Pip is a bat and he ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ acts like one. It NEVER felt consistent whether he would actually activate the platform (or negate the shot) even if he was the right element, because he lags behind your character. Great, I get that he is a living breathing creature, but TWO OF THE THREE FINAL BOSSES NEED HIM TO ACTIVATE PLATFORMS AND COULD YOU JUST KEEP THE TIMING THE SAME, PIP? ♥♥♥♥!(Throwing berries should fix the timing issue, but it doesn't, he meanders over to the berry and then zips back to you like greased lightning. It is awful to time.)Three: Leading off of this, what the ♥♥♥♥ are the late game bosses? The game has a sharp upturn in difficulty, but I can wade through the levels no problem before throwing enough batbodies at the bosses to drown them. One of the bosses has more bullets than a Touhou game, while dodging (telegraphed but instant) attacks from the top of the screen, WHILE ALSO dodging a melee combatant. Another has more bullets than a Touhou game, then bum-rushes you with two melee attackers in a trapped arena. Another has more bullets than a Touhou game, but double whatever amount of bullets you're thinking of. So on and so forth, I want to say that every boss after the second is a spike in difficulty all on their own. ALL of these bosses require use of Pip (except one that 'just' requires throwables that can run out mid-fight and must then be gathered from damage-sponge enemies), while optionally flicking his elemental powers back and forth to mitigate some of the bullets because apparently you weren't keeping enough on your mind. I'm sure the developers were trying to make it difficult, and they succeeded... by inducing sensory overload. I can not observe 3-5 oncoming sources of damage while giving two separate responses, and it is not fun to try. Related note, I may be a completionist, but I'm not going to go for the "no death" achievement and God himself couldn't make me.But, uhhh... yeah, the rest of the game was a ball! It's a shame, every boss has its own unique spin on it (I LOVE the ideas behind every boss after... well, plot stuff) but I ended up dreading every time I saw a health bar. But the levels, the puzzles, and the plot? Good stuff. So, yeah, I'd give a neutral if I could, but I don't regret my purchase. Thumbs up from me!

_childDocuments_.review: Once you pass the initial frustration, this game gets very addictive! I can see why some people get too frustrated to keep going.However, as you learn the structure of the dungeon and get the hang of solving the puzzle, this game gets very addictive! I especially got excited when Pip (the bat) acquired the fire aura, which enabled me to access more places. You also start seeing more unique monsters later and it's a lot of fun.The puzzles are well-made, almost seems impossible initially but you'll get satisfying "Ah Ha!" moments. If it's too difficult, you can also turn on some assists to help you to keep going, or leave the place and progress other areas first. _childDocuments_.review: Starts out really good, has that good old-school platformer feeling. Dialogues are funny, the whole setting is great. Action is very simplistic and not hard. After a few hours you start to realize that this game is neither RPG, neither Metroidvania (only very slightly). It's just a pure puzzle platformer with sometimes funny dialogues. Map exploration is fairly linear in a sense, but you will encounter many locked doors or inaccessible passageways in your way and you have 0 clue how to progress furher. Sometimes you accidentally find something and somewhere something happens. It's a game where you constantly feel lost. Strange feeling. I encountered a bug where I destroyed some enemies that fire projectiles and 1 unkillable ice elemental left and ... I had to die. Then I teleported back to the campfire and .... lost quite a lot of progress. There is NO fun in doing the same thing, the same precision puzzles and puzzles overall. This game is filled with small annoying puzzles. puzzles, puzzles, puzzles, puzzles.... It sucks the fun out of this game very rapidly. F that. I hate when games concentrate on making puzzles out of everything. It's a plague in today's gaming. A cheap way to make you spend more time in the game and a cheap way to mask games' lack of variety in content.Good, but dreadful game at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is and should be a simple review.  If you like running, jumping, fighting monsters, unlocking new abilities and areas, finding items, exploring dungeons, finding secrets, going up against wild and creative bosses and laughing at extremely well written dialogue, this game is for you.  On top of all this you will fall in love with the world's cutest animated bat.Everything in this game from the jokes to the character animations to the AMAZING soundtrack has been done with a level of hand-made care that shines through in every moment.Like many games of this type, it takes a few minutes to get up to speed with your abilities and get accustomed to the dungeon environment (though there are many slime and other monster encounters to have fun with right from the get-go).  After that it's on - run jump hack slash, switch all the switches, and use all your tools to survive all the trap rooms.I was struck by how good the balance feels right from the beginning - not a cakewalk, but also fair, all while communicating to you that it's the beginning of the game and you're weak.This game is a fun time made with love.  Romp is the right word.  It's both serious and playful in all the right ways.And if all that isn't enough, THE SPLASH SCREENS WHEN YOU BOOT UP ARE SKIPPABLE - THANK YOU GOOD PEOPLE DEVS YOU THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING!!!!!Edit: OMG THE DEVS ALSO ADDED OPTIONAL ASSISTS FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE MORE INTERESTED IN THE SIGHTS/SOUNDS/STORY AND WOULD LIKE A LITTLE HELP WITH THE ACTION-ORIENTED PARTS OF THE GAME - they truly did think of everything!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, the controls, gameplay and music are all top notch. The storytelling is great and genuinely funny and its a rewarding experience. _childDocuments_.review: Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials is a Metroid-vania-esque dungeon crawler with RPG elements, healthy doses of tongue-in-cheek humor, and a great deal of platforming challenge. The mechanics (from the jump physics to melee attacks) feel solid as any decent platformer would have, but where Batbarian shines is the addition of Pip, the titular characters flying companion, and the methods in which you can use her to both solve puzzles and attack enemies. Unlike some games of its ilk, the backtracking doesn't feel tedious and the story unfolds in an intuitive way. During my time playing the game, I rarely felt lost--at the same time, there is enough challenge that I've had to sit and think about the best way to approach new, more difficult scenarios. That said, for those of us who aren't as adept as platforming, there are options to ease some of the difficulty of the game (although you will not be able to obtain achievements while these options are turned on). The branching dialogue trees offer some replay value for future runs through the dungeon (and many times had me chuckling). I recommend this game! You can really tell that the developers have a deep love for what they've created.

_childDocuments_.review: oh man it's out ^^Charming AF metroidvania with WAY too much to do in it ( 12 hours, and I was slightly past the halfway mark? ) Controls are tight ( on controller, you can't use D-Pad to move your char, but you get over it after you realize why ) Huge, Sprawling metroidvania, very simialr to Hollow Knight in this regard.The writing is very charming, oftentimes chuckle-worthy ( alot of the engagements involve you selecting your repsonse, and they all have unique dialogue back-and-forth as a reuslt of your choice ) you can play as lady barbarian, or guy - they just look different. You make your way through the maps, tossing fruits and rocks to hit switches, or to send your bat Pip, to light a thing. LAter on, you get different skills for Pip whih change her lighting function to somehting liek, fire, or ice - and the pzzles can get pretty tricky when you stack all the skills together.The boss fights are difficult at first, but there's patterns. You get EXP and level up in this game, and when that happens - you get a roulette wheel to choose you perks.You also find powrups in the world, like a drink that increases your STR permanently, or HP , stone carrying amount, etc.There's also a staggering amount of hidden gems you can use to trade into a certain NPC you meet later on to get special items.I had a hard time putting this down throughout it's development, and I'm eager to dive back in - I already spotted tons of QoL improvements when i fired it up before launch. There's a new host of assist mode options, which are sorely needed, as this game can kick your buns at times :)VERY HIGHLY RECOMMENDED ! If you like Hollow Knight, or just well-made Metroidvanias, this is one you won't want to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of thoughts about this game. It's well written, it's funny, the central mechanic of using the right stick to throw things leads to some interesting design and puzzles. But the sparse metroidvania elements clash with the precision platforming in ways that are ultimately too frustrating to recommend. Enemy damage is extremely high and it's easy to become trapped in a fight where your only options are play perfectly (sometimes against enemies that only exist in that room and have unique mechanics you need to figure out for the first time) or reset to the last save. Puzzles require use of resources with extremely limited ammo that isn't restored when resetting the puzzle. Puzzle progress is only saved on checkpoint/save, so if you die after completing a puzzle, you get to do it all over again. The game frequently wants you to move with the left stick and aim with the right stick while jumping and/or attacking with the face buttons. I'm not sure what sort of chernobyl hands the devs have but normal human hands aren't particuarly fond of that. There's good bits here, but overall the game is too messy and unrewarding to recommend to even the sort of person who plays every game tagged "metroidvania" on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: So... I am giving thumbs down rather than thumbs up, because this game did not entertain me one bit, and I gave it a fair time (95 minutes).I like metroidvanias, I like puzzle solving, and I don't mind platforming and combat - but any of these things, in this game, felt fun. There's the typical stuff - you traverse and explore the map, you fight some monsters, collect gold to buy equipment, you platform around, you encounter puzzles you can't solve quite yet because you need new abilities.The unique ability in this game is your illuminated bat, which is basically your main puzzle solving thing, since all puzzles I encountered so far are based on the light. You throw fruit around for bat to pick up, and different fruit will do different things - either make it stay and chew longer, or destroy the tile in anger.There are also NPCs - I've acquired one so far, and they follow you around, and you can use their ability.There's levelling, and you get to upgrade your attack, defense, or ambient light.See... on paper, all this sounds fun, but for me, it just wasn't. I kept playing, waiting for the "real game" to begin, and it never did. You're just stuck in these dark caves, and whatever gameplay you see in the beginning - will continue onwards, at least until my stopping point.Maybe I'm wrong, but I should be having fun within first 10 minutes, with game's core mechanics, in order to keep playing, and I am just about to uninstall this one. I've started playing other similar games with more or less unique mechanics - like Underhero and Blasphemous, and those started entertaining me from the very beginning.I won' refund it even if I could, simply because - its not a bad game, at all. Before you get it, it'd be worthwhile seeing few youtube videos for longer play sessions, just to see what is it about. If it hooks you, great. If not, move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Requires way too much precision for a game that doesn't offer any type of assistive control or snap-to platforming.  A large portion of the jumps in the game are near pixel perfect, both in height and distance, leading to a largely unsatisfactory experience.I have just quit at a point at which it requires a single-frame jump input which I find is impossible to do consistently because of this design.  The room in question has a gate to make it difficult to retry on a failed jump, while also damage you on a failed jump.  It is purpose built to mock the player for their failures, rather than challenge them.EDIT: I'm revising this based on developer discussion and feedback.  This developer is not delusional or malicious and does care to revise their own designs to be better, so there's no reason to dissuade anyone from this game.  The above case existed but it was clearly a case where the developer themselves did see the flaw in it prior to it even being pointed out.  I can only expect that this game will be refined over time.If you're here for a platforming game, it's not a terrible fit, but you might run into some frustrations.Also, the game very much revolves around limited resources in a way that only requires you to farm for them to progress through puzzles, instead of scarcity offering any value to game play, and they are extremely limited resource.  Think Super Metroid but you only get 5 super missiles, ever.  2 Super bombs.  And there is no reliable way to get them back, short of grinding a single units of currency to go buy them from a shop.It is also not a strong Metroidvania candidate.  It has the exploration, but a vast majority of the gameplay is rooms that are puzzles, rather than any meaningful exploration or traversal mechanisms.  You will get one single movement upgrade, the rest are just variations of door keys.  It is an original set of mechanics, but the design doesn't play toward the strengths of exploration, it is more just about doing every room's puzzle to get to the next puzzle.The experience system is tied to a lot mechanic and otherwise leveling up confers no benefits outside of these random stats.  Based on initial stats, you basically gain +3% damage or +1.5% defense off of your initial base value, and you get 3 slot rolls per level up.  This doesn't appear to add anything positive to the game experience and the game would have done better to balance without experience at all.  At time of review, I have not even reached +100% damage in total from levels or pickups, making my total damage modification over the course of the game not feel noteworthy, and the defense gains are nearly impossible to measure.If you're looking for a Metroidvania, I'd look elsewhere.However, puzzles are generally interesting, inventive, or at least rewarding to accomplish, but there is a much, much stronger focus on room to room puzzles over exploration.If you're looking for a platforming puzzle game, might be decent.  The puzzles are fine, but it's somewhat marred by the platforming, and in some cases you're expected to have 3 thumbs to be able to solve a puzzle smoothly, but those appear to be relatively rare.
