_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game Review: A Quacking Good TimeIf you’ve ever dreamed of being a chaotic, feathered menace in a quaint English village, then Untitled Goose Game is your dream come true. This delightful indie gem lets you step into the webbed feet of a goose with an insatiable desire to wreak havoc. Who knew that flapping around and stealing people’s stuff could be so entertaining?From the moment you honk your first honk, you’ll feel a sense of purpose. Your mission? Cause as much mayhem as possible while the poor villagers scowl in confusion. Picture this: a peaceful gardener meticulously tending to his flowers, only for you to swoop in and steal his rake, leaving him to chase you around like a scene from a slapstick comedy. It’s pure gold.The graphics are charmingly simple, almost like a children’s storybook come to life. But don’t be fooled—behind that cute exterior lies a goose that takes joy in stealing glasses, turning on sprinklers, and dropping picnic blankets. You’ll find yourself devising elaborate plans, like a feathery mastermind plotting to trap unsuspecting villagers in your web of chaos.The controls are surprisingly intuitive, allowing you to glide through your villainous tasks with the grace of a ballet dancer and the subtlety of a bull in a china shop. But don't get too comfortable; the villagers will fight back! You’ll quickly learn that nothing ruins your day quite like a determined human wielding a broom.As for the soundtrack? Think of it as a delightful accompaniment to your mischief, with jaunty tunes that make you feel like a devious protagonist in a silent film. Every honk feels like a rallying cry for your fellow geese, urging you on in your quest for chaos.In conclusion, Untitled Goose Game is a whimsical reminder that sometimes, being a jerk is just plain fun. So grab your feathers, channel your inner honker, and prepare for some good old-fashioned goose antics. Just remember, what happens in the village stays in the village—unless you leave behind a trail of chaos and stolen goods. In that case, everyone will know it was you. 🦢

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE untitled goose game. Untitled goose game is set in a small English town. You are a goose who needs to check-off his to-do list. The to-do list will have you doing things like getting the gardener wet, stealing his keys, trap someone in a telephone both, make someone spit out there tea, make a bucket fall on someone's head, breaking the vase, ect. The game is not that big map-wise, but I just love the little town so much! from it's market on the street corner, to the outdoor pub, to it's well. I just love how the game feels so open. On top of that you have the amazing instrumental piano music that gives the game that much more personality! Untitled goose game is also 2-player local co-op, so you and your friend can wreak havoc together! The controls are pretty simple. The only thing I found the slightest hard/frustrating is a couple of the tasks, but every time you complete that one hard one it feels so good! And the few that I did find hard were not impossible nor easy, it gave me just the right amount of challenge. The game itself is not that hard, but if your looking for something too have fun with and goof around, it is PERFECT for that. The controls are simple, but they aren't the best with keyboard and mouse. I suggest using a controller, or getting it on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, or Xbox 1. Also when you "finish" the game you have a couple "to-do also" lists that add some replay ability. Overall I would say that this game is suitable for all ages, and I give this game a 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Untitled Goose Game

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is a charming and entertaining experience, perfect for anyone looking for a bit of whimsical fun. The premise is simple: you play as a mischievous goose causing all sorts of playful chaos in a quaint village.While the game is on the shorter side, it makes every moment count with clever puzzles and delightful interactions. The art style and soundtrack add to its quirky charm, making it a memorable experience despite its brief length.If you’re looking for a light-hearted game to brighten your day, Untitled Goose Game is definitely worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Untitled Goose Game

_childDocuments_.review: In Untitled Goose Game, you'll explore and use your goose's environment to complete silly tasks all while being a great nuisance to the denizens of a charming, little town.Overall, I loved that the game encourages players to explore and experiment with its sandbox's numerous objects and to study the routines of the townsfolk in order to figure out how to complete tasks and progress forward through the game.Also of note, I played this using an Xbox Controller and I can say that the controls worked perfectly fine and were easy to grasp upon starting the game.So go on and pick up this wonderful treat of a game! And you too can go honk and waddle your way to being the most mischievous goose in town.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is an absolute gem that delivers pure joy from start to finish. Every moment spent as the mischievous goose is a delightful experience filled with laughter and satisfaction. The game’s charming, minimalist art style perfectly complements its whimsical nature, making it a visual treat.The game-play is brilliantly simple yet incredibly engaging. The tasks you undertake as the goose are hilariously creative, from  to . Each objective is a new opportunity for fun and chaos, and the freedom to approach them in various ways (for a better time) adds a layer of replayability.What truly sets this game apart is its humor. The goose’s antics are endlessly amusing, and the reactions of the villagers are priceless. _childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the untitled goose game! Here you can be goose, goose around and don’t give a goose about the goosing problems of everygoose life!  No, you’re not a duck. You’re a goose. And that’s great! This “game” – though more so a simulation of the typical British small-town living circumstances – certainly will bring a smile to your heart and force a “HONK” from your lips. Being the silly bird you are, war is your option over piece by any length and trouble your choice of action when completing your quests. Lock people up, steal their keys, break their glasses and perform for an audience – do whatever a goose has to do!Short answer: No. Long answer: No, it isn’t.Unlike other “be an animal” games, like Goat Simulator, I am Fish or Deer Simulator, this game goes for a more literal understanding of being a goose. It is way less skewed towards the crazy and hyperbolic use of physics, action or extreme control-scheme challenges and much more aimed at a relaxing, but still sometimes intricate gameplay.Untitled Goose Game is a game about completing silly tasks in a fun, friendly setting and finding your way through unique and fun puzzles that are spelled out to you simply through a cutesy To-Do-List style quest-log. But don´t worry, you’re not grinding for useless cosmetic loot, hunting for the next achievement or fiddling with weird RNG to complete a quest. Sometimes you will have to show patience, sometimes it´s more about your motorskills of being a goose and some other times yet again it’s about using your brain to understand what is asked of you. But every task is light-hearted, fun and nicely integrated into the small, but cozy world around you. You’re a goose, you create harmless chaos and terrorize the neighbourhood just enough already. No need to also do backflips, hunt after a timer or raise your wanted level.The game runs very smooth, though the controls take a bit to get used to. While the controls overall are fine, easy to understand and easy to learn, they do feel a bit “unresponsive”, mainly due to the limited turning radius of your goose. But this all works in favour of the game, as you can shorten the turning radius by simply walking instead of running and other issues with the controls are also alleviated by simply playing. One frustrating thing this game sadly doesn’t really address is the way you’re pushed around by aggravated NPCs. While the interactions are wanted and needed for the gameplay to work, there can be instances where they push you into weird corner or where the hitboxes feel odd. There’s also moments where any and all control goes out of the window when your goose enters a brief “escape mode” from being pushed around. It’s generally fine, but can be a bit frustrating to play around with. You can get used to it and trick the NPCs AI into acting in your favour by manipulating their actions and pathing through your position or taking away another object from them, but the less of control never really starts feeling good.Overall though, the controls are good and the game does run even on weak hardware without hickups.This game is not for people who don’t like questing. BUT, there’s also secret tasks to complete, a speed-run mode, extra challenges for those wanting more and a superb local (and Steam-connect online) two-player mode that I can highly recommend.I see this game therefore as a game for couples, those who like to play silly little games, people who simply like to play something calm and on-the-side and those, who simply want to be a goose.It certainly comes highly recommended not just because of the setting, idea and execution, but also the very nice sound design, world design and especially recommended for those, who are into game design as a whole, as I can see this game doing a lot of small things very very good that other games struggle with a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the immense pleasure of diving into the quirky world of the "Untitled Goose Game," and let me tell you, it's an absolute gem that will leave you grinning from ear to ear. The game's charming visuals, coupled with its playful soundtrack of different piano notes, set the stage for an adventure that's as heartwarming as it is hilarious. The attention to detail in the game world is astounding; every nook and cranny is filled with opportunities for mischief, and you'll find yourself cackling with glee as you terrorize the unsuspecting villagers.What truly sets the Untitled Goose Game apart is its intuitive gameplay mechanics. Controlling the goose feels natural, and the puzzles are cleverly designed, encouraging you to think outside the box to achieve your feathered objectives. The joy of honking at just the right moment or stealing a villager's hat without them noticing is unparalleled.But beyond its gameplay brilliance, the game's real charm lies in its ability to evoke a genuine sense of happiness and amusement. _childDocuments_.review: one imagines the untitled goose game to be simple in nature, yet it is far from. as one continues throughout the adventure of this mischievous mallard, they gain a sort of appreciation for its complexities. coming from someone recently engrossing themselves in this journey, i can wholeheartedly back up this claim. whether its your first time through, just completing the core objectives and exploring the four diverse regions, or finding the secret tasks, ones much harder, its clear that untitled goose game is great.typical to many indie games, this treasure was clearly well polished and carefully designed. the way that they designed the game in a way that is obviously 3D, but cleverly put in a perspective of 2D style gameplay was a breath of fresh air from the usual one or the other. untitled goose game as a whole is lovely; the art style: magnificent, the soft piano music: beautiful, the interactions made with the npcs: hilarious at times.my only gripe with the final product is the achievements, more specifically, the "___, quickly" set. to complete these achievements and 100% the game, each area has to have its tasks done in less than seven minutes. for this to happen, you must find a route that allows for quick task-doing, while avoiding the finicky movement of npcs and grab mechanics. even then, it could be imperfect, and the tasks might be done right after the bell strikes. when this happens, its time to restart and try again. this, without a doubt, was the worst experience, especially the back gardens.in summary, the untitled goose simulator is not perfect, it can be at times one of the most frustrating things available on steam, and at others you feel like you are on top of the world. my time playing this was a mix of these things, and i overall had a wonderful time. house house made a masterpiece, but one not everyone can understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixing stealth with hilarity with the deep, often ignored, dark human lust for chaos and bullying small children. This game has a surprisingly beautiful ending and tells a charming tale while leaving much up to the players interpretation. It manages to have replayability while still having a good storyline that is satisfying every time. It also has a fun interactive soundtrack that gives cues and clues in game. The game is puzzling enough to be difficult but not impossible. The instructions are clear enough that you know exactly what you need to do, but vague enough you aren't sure how to do it. Each level has at least one difficult problem that you have to think outside the box for, and always you must look around for what to do. The bonus content (extra lists) at the end of the game offer even more replayability, during which I guarantee you will find easter eggs and little things you didn't notice before. The lists often have one clear way to do things, but you can always do it another way, so I strongly recommend looking outside the box for strange ways to do things when replaying, it almost always pays off. The NPC interactions are also something worth hunting for, so 100%ing this game still doesn't get you through all the content. All in all, a true masterpiece of gaming with a fun concept that they pulled of amazingly well. I strongly recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is the quirky indie game that AAA studios just can't make anymore. In this game you play as the titular goose running, honking, and flapping your wings through a suburban English village. The game sees you navigate through four scenarios, a garden, a street, two interconnected backyard gardens, and a pub. These four settings are seamlessly connected as you complete a "to-do list" of puzzles and tasks involving collecting or placing props in the interactive environment and having human NPCs react with them in fun and unique ways. One thing that should be noted is this is an extremely short game, about four hours in length, including the hidden "to-do list" and speed-run challenges, but even so I believe it's worth the $20 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you played a goose wreaking havoc on a small village. It is effectively a puzzle game, where you are given a level of items and humans and specific tasks such as "steal the gardener's hat". Controls are deliberately a little difficult but you get used to them quickly and they add just enough of a challenge to make the game engaging.The game is quaint, charming, cute, and a million other adjectives like that. Everything goes towards building the aesthetic the game is going for. The art style is simple, with an almost picture book quality to it, that works well. The gameplay is also simple and easily understood, but has enough variety and obstacles to keep you engaged. But what really took it over the top for me is the music. As you do things these little piano snippets play that feel like they narrate what you do! A nice flourish to almost every action.The game is fairly short, your initial play through will only take about 3 to 4 hours, at which point it will give you a few more tasks that take maybe another hour or two to complete (ignore my play time, I left the game running at one point). The game does not overstay its welcome, so its shortness is probably a good thing, but I know I would have enjoyed a bit more goosey hijinks. But the final sequence of the game that leads you through all previous sections on a chase, is such a perfect ribbon on the experience, I can't be mad. This is a game that almost anyone can enjoy. It is simple enough for kids and non-gamers, but does everything so well that even gamers can enjoy it. And some of the achievements are hard enough to even provide a challenge should you need that. A+ all around.

_childDocuments_.review: I always thought of myself as a kind, gentle, considerate, and most of all , honest, individual. Or at least I always tried to be.  Then...I became the Horrible Goose, and my hidden "dark side" was revealed. In addition to meet the set goals in the game, the AI is intuitive and open-ended enough that you can make your own game of just creating as much havoc and misery in the village as possible. Annoy, steal, vandalize, and even terrorize the villagers with impunity. All backed up with a musical score based on Debussy's "Preludes", and somehow reminiscent of MisterRogers Neighborhood if MisterRogers Neighborhood took place in an alternate universe where the "beautiful day in the neighborhood" is constantly ruined by sociopathic poultry.There is some mild violence in some of the tasks, such as making the gameskeeper hit his thumb, and I discovered on my own, you can actually lead the little boy into the lake and make him repeatedly dunk his head underwater.  However, no one dies, and there is no blood. Parents of younger children might need to look at some sample game plays online and see if it is suitable for their kids. As it is, MY kid (who is a millennial adult) introduced me to this game on her Switch. A friend's daughter of a similar age also had a Switch but not many games, so I gave the Untitled Goose Game to her last Christmas.  I only recently got the game for myself once I discovered that it was available for PC, and was on sale.  The game can be relaxing as well because it is so open ended. There are many items in the game that the Goose can interact with, but are not part of the task list.  So far, I haven't tried to "beat the clock" by going through an entire list under 6 minutes, but my only complaint is that there should be a few more suggested tasks. There are some parts of the village you never actually see, such as the actual bell tower (the bell is heard ringing in the game, and the Goose steals the bell from the model village). Despite my joking that the game brought out the worst in me, it really is a cute, relaxing game that would be good as a starter game for people who aren't ready for, or don't want, any complex games.

_childDocuments_.review: Everybody knows the goose. You honk, you terrorize a small English village, you honk again, and you solve puzzles. And then you honk again. "Untilted Goose Game" is a quaint little puzzle game. The graphics are simple, the audio works, and the puzzles are not very challenging. The game can be beaten in 3 hours. The achievements come fast, and some of them are novel enough to be worth attempting, if only for the zany antics you'll get into. I like the game, and I'd recommend it.... just not on PC. I use a standard Xbox 360 controller on a Windows 10 machine. The controls in the game are awful at times. Some of the puzzles require very precise movement or timing, and a control scheme akin to infamous ice world levels from NES platformers is not meant to be a compliment. Do the positives outweigh the negatives, especially at a Steam Sale price point? Yes. Would I play the game again? Probably. _childDocuments_.review: This is a quaint and funny little puzzle game that is such a nice time to spend a few hours with. Its minimalist aesthetic and ambient sound design are a perfect match for the small English village in which it’s set. The somewhat isometric viewpoint is also a good match for this environment, highlighting its quaintness, even if the camera can be frustrating to wrangle in some situations. But even with all this quiet charm the game manages not to get stale, thanks to the energy thrust upon it by your antics. Upon starting it up, the game only gives you a list of tasks to complete but in order to cross most of the items off the list you’ll need to get into some mischief. The kind that’ll usually release a burst of frenetic action upon the world, causing people to yell and/or run, items to fall and/or break, and a string of musical notes to fly into your ears. Suffice to say it is immensely satisfying because, after all, how could you not enjoy crossing things off a list AND upsetting stuffy British people at the same time? The tasks themselves range in complexity but there’s never too much frustration in figuring out how to pull them off and so the whole experience strikes the perfect mix between relaxing, intriguing and funny. And to top it all off, the conclusion is pretty much perfect.And while there’s not much more to say than that, you can also extend your playtime if you’d like by taking on the bonus To Do List that appears after the credits roll. The tasks on it are a very nice inclusion as they’re grander in scope and so require you to move back and forth between every section (which are now completely open to each other) giving you a chance to appreciate the scope and detail of this nice little environment even more. This game is all-in-all a wholly satisfying experience, if you’ve got the patience and temperament for it.

_childDocuments_.review: So usually, I like to play a game a bit more before I recommend it, but I knew as soon as I saw the page on the steam shop that I had to own it and after an hour or so of playing it with my brother (and both of us in pain from laughter) I knew it was a keeper!The tone and visual style of the game is similar to Donut Country or Katamari Damacy: you are essentially ruining people’s lives in a fun and droll way, immersed in a quirky and somewhat minimalist environment; the play style of the game is more like a brain-teaser: like those old point-and-click games, if you can figure out the fractured logic of the game, with a little practice, you have a lot of fun!  The objectives range from the simple to the mind-boggling complex and there are plenty of secret achievements that reward you for experimentation and thinking outside the box.Of course the game is not perfect and my only real complaint so far is about the controls.  The goose handles like a bowling ball covered in molasses and the initial controller bindings of ‘A’ being for running and ‘B’ for item manipulation is pretty much the opposite of what I got used to playing Final Fantasy games for 20 years.  Fortunately, the button assignment can be changed and, again with some practice, the directional movements can be acclimated to without too much detriment to the overall game.Anyway, I am always on the lookout for innovative games with unique styles and I definitely love a good laugh... and this game has those things in spades (pun intended--check out the groundskeeper in the first area).  Therefore, especially if you want a humorous break from the usual “kill all the enemies” kind of game, this game comes highly recommended!  Hail the “horrible goose” (which I think should have been the name of the game, but whatever)!  Would honk again!

_childDocuments_.review: Some might say this is not much play time for the price, but I see why this game has become a Thing, a meme, a phenomenon.  The art work is charming, and it's rather amusing to realise suddenly that what we're playing here is no more or less than HITMAN without the violence and flashy 3D modelling!  This is a stealth game involving theft and combat.  But no one really gets hurt and it's all in good fun.The eponymous Goose wanders around a delightful little village, causing mischief and mayhem;  the devs set you a challenge in the form of a To-Do list which assigns tasks like "shut the boy in the phone booth," or "drop a tankard in the river".  You have to figure out how to hide, run, and finagle your way around the irritable townspeople to achieve your goals.  The difficulty level ramps nicely, until the end game does feel like an achievement.I found the mouse/kbrd controls rather difficult for this one, and switched to a gamepad.  Fortunately you can map your gamepad buttons (though not the ToDo List key apparently which is Tab -- I wish the devs would let me map that one to a gamepad button as well, so I could be freed from the keyboard).  The perspective is 3rd person aerial with a bit of zoom, but no other camera control (a bit frustrating at times).  What makes the game though, is the animation.  The goose's body language (and the humans' too) is naturalistic and comical.  Just watching my goose waddle around brought a smile to my face, before I'd even managed any mischief.I'd recommend this one for anyone who likes a relaxing, humorous puzzle game.  If you found HITMAN too stressful and violent but enjoyed the stealth aspects, try the Goose!  Extra nice touches are:  human interactions in the Pub scene, the model village which replicates the full size village, and of course the jingling bell in the endgame!  Suitable for anyone from about eight to eighty -- and eminently replayable as the action is so much fun to watch.

_childDocuments_.review: Im a 27 years old male, I have been living alone since i was 19, when i moved away from my parents and I settled down on a little apartment. Since i was a child, I used to play on the park with my neighbors. We enjoyed one particular game, maybe you have heard of it, it was called "Hide And Seek". The game had 2 roles, the seeker, who has to count to 10, without looking at his enviroment, before starting his duty, and the people who hide as good as they can. The seeker must find all the players hiding, so he can win. I don't know if this is a common practice, but when a person was found by the seeker, both of them would run as fast as they could to the counting point, if the person who was hiding got there first, he would be safe, and would win against the seeker. Many of my friends played the game normally, hiding, and then running towards the tree where the seeker was counting, sometimes winning, sometimes losing, they had lots of fun doing so, but I didn't. For some reason, playing games as a children was always so boring to me, they never "clicked" for me. But there was something, just one little thing, on that one particular game, one feature that fulfilled my profound desires and yearnings, that was the moment when the seeker founds you. Instead of just running towards the counting point, i would pick the most odd, darkest places for the seeker to go, i went under cars and grabbed the leg of the seeker when he was nearby, up in some trees hiding on the leaves i would jump into them, behind corners, inside bushes... My goal was never to win the game, my goal was to scare the seeker, frighten, terrify, shock this person.The enjoyment i had on those golden days of my life was taken away from me, because the parents of the kids threatened me, they said their kids were scared of playing with me. Once a child, who got scared of me, ran away and fell down, he got a huge wound on his head, which he still has in the form of a scar. The only thing that fulfilled me, that made me feel alive, probably the only moment of my life where i could be myself, was gone.The years passed, i got through my life normally. I graduated from middle school, highschool and college. I made normal relationships with everyone, never had a problem at all. But something was missing, this desire, this feeling, this painful need to annoy people, to make then scared, see them cry in fear. This eventually lead me to live my life in a profound emptiness, everyday was just, dull, boring, flat, tasteless. I thought my life was doomed to be like this forever, condemned to the boredom. But when i saw this game on the steam store, i saw hope, i saw light. It's not the same than scaring people in real life, but this game provides me joy, it's comforting, it's a dildo that gives pleasure, that satisfy the needs of one of the most deep parts of my soul. I recommend this game, than rather than giving me entertainament, gave me life once again. Thank you, Untitled Goose Game.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game at its core is a casual puzzle game, but not like any I've played before. The aesthetic is simple but artistic, with prominent music and sound effects.  The graphics and animal-oriented gameplay remind me of Ape Out, but contrary to the brutal battles in that game, here you're just a goose on the loose, causing chaos with no real consequence for mistakes. I can't think of another game where exploration is more rewarding.  It's funny but challenging, logical but silly, just a lot of fun to play. You are, however, rewarded for being methodical and organized, which adds a strategy element.  It's an unconventional game that should appeal to players of a lot of different genres.

_childDocuments_.review: 🦆 Untitled Goose Game: A Quacking Good Time (Despite the Neck Envy) 🦆Well, well, well, what have we here? It's me, your friendly neighborhood duck, ready to spill the beans on the feathered phenomenon known as Untitled Goose Game. Now, don't let my webbed feet fool you – I might be writing this review with a touch of neck envy, but even I can't deny the hilarious havoc that these mischievous geese are causing.Let's get one thing straight: geese might have those long, elegant necks that make them look all regal and fancy, but us ducks? We're the true masters of waddling finesse. Anyway, enough about my neck woes – let's dive into the chaos!Untitled Goose Game is a whirlwind of feathers, flaps, and fowl play. As a duck, I appreciate a good prank when I see one, and watching those cheeky geese honk their way through a quiet village is nothing short of quacking genius. From stealing hats to terrorizing the local gardener, it's like a symphony of honks that would make even the most stoic duck crack a smile.The game's physics? Absolutely egg-cellent. I may not have a long neck, but I know good gameplay when I see it. Tugging on items, dragging objects, and causing pandemonium – it's like a duck's dream come true. And the best part? The humans' reactions! I can practically hear their screams of frustration and see their flailing arms as they try to outwit those pesky geese. Ah, the satisfaction!But let's not forget about the checklist of mayhem. As someone who appreciates a well-organized pond (seriously, is it so hard to keep a pond clean?), I understand the joy of ticking off tasks one by one. Whether it's making a picnic go awry or getting a poor soul all wet, each accomplished task is a victory for birds everywhere.So, to all you aspiring avian agents of chaos out there, if you're ready to spread your wings and wreak havoc with the best of them, then Untitled Goose Game is your golden egg. It's a reminder that even us ducks can appreciate the art of a well-executed prank, even if we're a tad bit envious of those luxurious necks. So flap your wings, unleash your inner goose, and let the mayhem begin! 🎮🦆🕊️

_childDocuments_.review: Geese are found worldwide. They can adapt equally well to hot climates (as long as shade is provided) as to cold climates - as seen in their ability to withstand northern winters out of doors with the minimum of shelter. In spite of this broad adaptability, commercial goose production is only important in relatively few countries in Asia and Europe.Domestic geese come in a wide range of colours, sizes and shapes. In general, domestic breeds are much larger than their wild ancestors although they have in many cases retained their ability to fly.There are two main types of domestic geese. The first are thought to have their origins in Europe, descendants of the wild Greylag goose (Anser anser) and the second are thought to have their origins in Asia, descendants of the wild Swan goose (Anser cygnoides). Crosses between the domestic breeds which have originated from these two species of wild geese are fertile and in fact have resulted in a number of recognised breeds.Over the centuries many countries, and even regions within countries, have developed their own breeds and types of geese. But although there is a large pool of genetic material available for the genetic improvement of the domestic goose, it appears to have been relatively under-utilised. In addition, there are also species of wild geese which could be domesticated or could at least contribute to the commercial goose germplasm. For example, from temperate climates, there is the Canada goose (Branta canadansis) of North America and the American Swan goose (Coscoroba coscoroba) of southern South America. From the tropics, there is the Egyptian goose (Alopochen aegyptiacus) from Africa, the Nene goose (Branta sandvicensis) from the Hawaiian Islands, the Bar-headed goose (Anser Indicus) from India and central Asia, the Northern Spur-winged goose (Plectropectus gambensis) from Africa and the Semipalmated (magpie) goose (Anseranas semipalmata) from Australia and New Guinea.This book will deal only with domestic geese that descended from either the Greylag goose (Anser anser) or the Swan goose (Anser cygnoides).From the research for this book and a search of its Animal Genetic Resources Data-base, The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) have identified 96 breeds or genetic groups of geese, although there are probably more. Many of these breeds, although important world germplasm resources, are of little direct economic importance today because of their relatively low performance level and/or their low numbers and limited geographic distribution. In addition to these breeds, both old and new, there are a number of commercial cross-breeds made available by companies specialising in goose breeding.The white Chinese geese have orange shanks, beaks and knobs while the brown variety has orange shanks but its beaks and knobs are black or very dark green. One feature of the knob is that it can be used for sexing at 6-8 weeks of age, if not before. The knob of the male is larger and more pronounced than that of the female. The Chinese goose is relatively small in body size with mature males averaging 5.0 kg and females 4.0 kg. However, the breed is known for its high egg production and there are reports of Chinese geese laying up to 100 eggs in a breeding season of approximately five months (February to the end of June) although 50-60 eggs is the average. Egg weight, at 120 g, is lighter than for most other breeds.Because the body conformation and meat yield of the Chinese goose is not as good as that of other breeds, it has not been widely used for meat production, either as a pure breed or in breeding programmes as a female line to produce a crossbred commercial goose. However, a number of breeds of geese have been developed by combining Anser anser type with Anser cygnoides type, using the Chinese goose as described here.The Chinese goose is reported to be very effective as a guard animal. In addition it has strong legs and when required, can range over large distances to forage. This may explain in part why the distribution of this bird extends beyond the borders of China and why they are commonly found in countries like Siberia and India.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Beautiful aesthetics. Minimal, cartoonish graphics with nice chromatic palette. It looks so clean, but also has some cool details here and there.- Awesome, fluid animations. Goose's movements, how it walks, how it grabs things or pulls bigger ones with more effort, everything looks realistic and eye pleasant.- It has some pretty cool tasks that look like small puzzles. They're pretty simplistic, but they have fun and offer some interesting and refreshing gameplay mechanics. Most of them get solved in multiple ways. There are some extra, a little bit harder, tasks even after finishing the main game.- Smooth, responsive controls. Being a goose was never so immersive.- Great physics and collisions. Each object behaves differently depending on its weight and center of balance. Friction when pulling or pushing things looks good. Things dropping and knocking each other is realistic enough. - Much interactivity. You can grab and move almost everything that is close to goose's size. This makes its world feel more alive and immersive.- Nice minimal music that fits perfectly to visual aesthetics and enhances the overall humorous vibes.- It's hilarious. The concept of being an evil goose that makes a mess wherever it goes is funny, but it gets even better by the NPC's reactions, their frustration and goose's honks. The bad- There is no main story or a profound reason of doing things. I know you're just a goose, but it has to give you a purpose. Now, you do random tasks just because an list of objectives tell you so. After a while messing with everything aimlessly may feel monotonous and a bit silly.- NPCs' AI is mediocre. They have short repetitive routines, slow reactions and you can easily trick them. They are allowed to move inside certain boundaries so you can get away pretty easily. Yeah, it isn't a stealth assassin simulation game, but its gameplay is based on how you deceive people so AI should be better.- Cameras are occasionally problematic and things can get hidden behind others. It would be nice if you could rotate the camera freely and zoom out more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic and extremely creative (despite it's name and in spite of the developer's name, which makes it looks like they saved all brain power for the game): you are a piece of s##t goose that's out there to ruin everyone's day. And it's hilarious. It works more like a sandbox sim game, where you have lots of small tasks to do, that finally open up new zones (i.e. exhausting the groundskeeper will make him fall and open the door). I feel bad specially for the artsy lady, as exposing her bra to the neighborhood mustn't be nice, and the kid, as you scare the beegezus outta him, and then make him look like a muppet with funny sunglasses.Artwork is great. Both it and the music suits the atmosphere exquisitely.My only complaint is the duration of the game. Sure, you unlock new tasks on your second run, that require the combination of objects and/or people from different zones, but it keeps being the same. Hope there are talks to make a second game with a bigger town, and more reactions from people.Couldn't try the coop option, but it's great there is one.Recommendable for a rainy sunday afternoon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a little while since I played Untitled Goose Game on the Switch, but playing it over on PC did not at all disappoint. Being able to create feathery, honking mayhem with a friend really adds a whole new dimension to the proceedings. While one goose runs distraction, the other gets the goods -- there is still some sneaking necessary, but with a P2 things get much more chaotic and direct. Very much in keeping with the eponymous goose's vibe. Untitled Goose Game is very much worth every penny you'll spend on it. It's clear that a lot of love went into this game's creation, and everything about it is highly expressive and finely-tuned. The devs have crafted a world brimming with life and color. No words are needed to convey each villager's feelings towards the intrusive goose -- each one feels unique in their presentation and challenge.  I'm not sure if it's simply the difference between Switch and PC (or if I'm talking out my a**) but the controls felt more responsive. 10/10 would HONK again

Randomly generated levels, bonus levels, or something more than this painfully short story mode. Fun for a very short bit. I generally try not get get games that I'll spend less than one hour for every dollar spent.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a goose and do what a goose would do: be the biggest ♥♥♥♥ in existence for your own personal gain.This game is seriously just dumb and that's where it gets its charm. It's a game about being the wild animal iconic for being an ass to humans... like, how do you get gameplay out of that?? But somehow these "House House" folk have done it. It has a simplistic artstyle, some great humor, interesting puzzles, and plenty of people to piss off. Though this game is really only good for one go as the story remains linear for every playthrough, there are still a bunch of tasks to complete after you beat the game giving you something further to do. Furthermore, if you like speedrunning there's even an entire to-do list for completing each and every stage before the church bell rings (in one consecutive run and there's no fast travel feature; no way to skip a stage and complete the next stage at the beginning of the church bell timer). There's a decent amount of content here though it's still pretty small. The playtime recorded for this review is how long it took for me to beat the game (everything I say here is fresh in my head) so don't expect something expansive beyond about 5 stages. There is of course the recently added coop mode where you can play it with a friend and a good dozen or so achievements to unlock in addition to completing the final to-do lists, so if you're willing to squeeze as much out of this game as possible then that $20 is definitely worth it. Otherwise I'd say either wait for a good sale or just avoid it all together if you don't want to pay that much for a 2-hour long experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, but a short game. Even if you  poke around a bunch, it will only require a couple hours to play through. So at full price there are games with far more longevity if that matters to you.If duration doesn't matter to you, you're in for a treat. I didn't purchase until after the cooperative update and I'm glad I waited. Similar to watching comedy, I feel that the laughs hit harder when enjoying it with another person. The visuals are spot on, the controls are slick, all of the sound effects and music are delightful. Finally, once done the "main" game, the bonus objectives are creative enough to make us go back and take on the challenge. Pick it up!

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not fun. Pro:- mostly good aesthetics- nice conceptCon: -  - very short duration, and practically no replay value- glitches which make you or the NPCs unable to move- not much depth, fluidity, or spontaneity, so it's like you're just going through the motions- causing havoc as a goose should be funny, but for some reason there's not much genuinely good humour (probably due to both the frustrating controls and plot)- the setting (an English village) feels dead due to the lack of activity and detail - not being able to control the viewing perspective was kind of irritating/suffocating- getting stuck on a task is really annoying, and the game doesn't give you enough options on how to complete the objectives... you'll probably end up giving in and searching for a walkthrough at some point, and since the gameplay itself isn't hard enough to give any satisfaction, your enjoyment is inevitably ruined - the aboriginal "land acknowledgement" thing in the end creditsI bought the game for 50% off (£7.74), and I still wouldn't recommend it at that price.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty short and fun game. You get to be a horrible goose and annoy humans. However, the controls are a bit clumsy. There are times when double-clicking doesn't register, or when you run towards a location but end up getting stuck on edges or small objects which then causes the goose to stop. It's not a big issue during regular play, but it becomes frustrating when attempting the speedrun achievements. Nevertheless, it remains a positive experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I've heard reviews and heard the hype, and this game definitely lives up to that. Tons of fun and relatively relaxing. I also love that the main game is feasible for pretty much anyone, but there are additional challenges along the way for people who want them (i.e. doing each task list quickly). Well balanced, perfectly quirky, and a blast to play. HONK.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm sure that $20 worth of effort went into the game, there's not $20 of content. I bought it for $10.59 on sale, but if I were to set my own price I probably would have paid $5. I'm not going to try and return it because I can afford to overpay for entertainment, but I was genuinely surprised that the game ended where it did. For a twenty dollar game, I was expecting content along the lines of Kerbal, Factorio, or Subnautica. In hindsight I realize now that I got those games in early access, that those games in particular may be exceptional in terms of content and quality, and that $20 just isn't what it used to be. The "overwhelmingly positive" reviews don't really reflect the lack of content either, and I get the feeling a lot of it is from meme reviews leaving a positive review to say: "goose game funny." And, no offense people, but I get the feeling that a lot of you got it for the memes and never completed the puzzles. So in all seriousness, and from someone who completed the main game: find a different puzzle game for $20. 3.7 hours, even 3.7 good hours, just doesn't cut it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this, as I had seen something about this game on Twitch.The visuals are not these high resolution images as some might want, but the art style is amazing and very fitting for this game. I personally love the art style, even if it is not very detailed (faces from the humans), but perhaps from the point of view of geese it is very fitting. The game is very colourful, even though I have only played the first two levels (Gardner and High Street).The sounds amd music are nice, might get annoying when playing with a child, on the otherhand it is very nice to play this game with the kids. They'll have loads of fun.I played the first level (Gardener) in multi-player co-op (there is *no* splitscreen, and this can cause issues from time to time, when making up strategies to annoy the person(s) in the level). I also played the first two levels (Gardner and High Street) in single player.I can only recommend this title, even though I am not sure how certain levels can be finished before the bell rings.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a charming little game, clearly crafted with love and attention. The art style and animations were terrific, the soundtrack was thoroughly enjoyable, and the mechanics were simple yet a lot of fun to play with. It even made me laugh out loud a number of times.You can get through the game, from start to finish, in just a few hours, but I find the game so lovable that I've already played through it several times. And there are challenges/achievements that will take probably 10-20 hours to complete.I bought the game at full price when it launched on Steam, and I don't regret it. If you want to wait for a sale, by all means be a smart shopper, but the game is worth the full asking price, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the surprises of the year for me. It's a very casual-friendly game but don't let that fool you — despite being simple it's very well-planned. Some of the trickier pranks require good understanding of gameplay mechanics and perfect execution, especially when playing solo.The game is not very long — I've played for 3 hours and already cleared all basic tasks as well as figured out some advanced ones. I'll probably clear it in 3 more. But it was a ton of fun with my brother and I actually picked it up on the Switch again to play with friends.Overall — a definite recommend. If there's a DLC in the future, I'm picking it up on day 1.

_childDocuments_.review: UGG was fun enough but not necessarily challenging or replay-able, more times than not I immediately suspected how to solve a challenge and it was only a matter of time and frustration to achieve the goal. It the controls were easier and the game ran 1.5x speed it would be trivially challenging. While I liked the idea and premise (it had its funny parts and looks clean) I don't feel that $15 was a good value. There are emptier parts of some maps, many more things could have been interact-able, longer challenges for each sub-map, and better controls--it felt like a made-for-phone application and not a PC game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game genre of being chaotic animals messing with humans has got to be one of my favorite trends in recent years There is something about being a menace to people which is so charming and fun! _childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game left me disappointed. I had high expectations since I'd heard a lot about it and was excited to play, but I waited for a discount of over 50%, knowing it was a pretty short game.And yes — it is short. I managed to complete every task in each location. Some took several tries, but overall, four hours was enough to finish the game.Some tasks require more complex problem-solving than others, so keep that in mind if you get stuck. If you're wondering whether you can interact with something, you probably can. If the particular location has the 'no goose' sign displayed eventually, you're doing things right. CAUSE HAVOC AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE.All in all, I have mixed feelings about the game. It's visually appealing and fun to play, but it's just too short. I recommend waiting for a discount — it's not worth the full price.PS. Actually you can use a keyboard and mouse to play, but I found it more comfortable with a pad.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s fun and charming playing as an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ duck.You’re a duck that’s an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Go around, honk, make a mess, cause neighbors to forever hate each other, and cause a farmer to have to buy back his own stolen tools. It’s great. The game is basically you going to an area, finding a list of tasks to complete and moving on. The pacing is nice as each area is small and most of the quests make sense. Each one is basically a miniature adventure puzzle where you go around manipulating objects. It’s not very difficult but the instructions can be a bit vague sometimes. This kinda has an upside where it feels gratifying to figure out the mini puzzle. The piano background music grows in intensity as you get chased or sneak around and it’s cute.The game does have issues with the AI being stupid sometimes and the collision not being great. It’s also short and considering the price, it’s not worth it at full price. The ending, however, is fantastic and made me genuinely laugh out loud. Overall, it’s a one and done decent puzzler and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game leaves much to be desired. The game quickly devolves from a charming brain teaser to a cluster of chores, many of which are entirely or partially out of your control. The beauty of the game becomes lost in unnecessarily tedious tasks and vague goals that leave you scratching your head. Gameplay is punishing to the point where the rewarding feeling for mentally solving a task becomes lost quickly after realizing how mechanically difficult and frustrating it can be to actually solve it in the game. Consistency between levels suffers. Certain mechanics are taught to the player then the mechanic changes in the next level. The tutorial is maze like and took longer than needed to teach the few controls of the Goose. Multiplayer is not online, it's local, just as an FYI for players hoping to play with their friends online. The advertising for that feature was misleading.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who owns geese, I can verify that geese are intelligent, cunning, mischievous and occasionally ill-tempered...but they're also highly social animals. So perhaps instead of judging this goose for its mischief, we should see its actions as desperate cries for attention from a lonely creature longing for affection. How dare we judge this poor bird?!

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is one of those games that is purely cathartic, and it's one I keep coming back to when I want to cause goose-powered chaos. It reminds me a bit of Portal, in that the game is mechanically tight, but doesn't overcomplicate itself any more then it has to. It's a good time all around, and certainly worth the asking price.My one argument against the game is that it's short enough to leave you wanting more of it, even through the additional tasks it gives you once you've completed the main story. In this way, it falls just short of the length of games like Portal, where the game is long enough to feel fullfilling, but also just short enough to not overstay its welcome.An additional map, or even a small handful of new areas would likely suffice to push the game into that sweet spot. The addition of coop indicates that House House is still willing to put effort into the game, so maybe? Maybe not?Either way, you'll still have a fun few hours playing the game as is, and I still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: In concept and in viewing, it's quite funny. However, playing the game yourself? Not so much. The controls... are a lot left to be desired. Turning is abysmal whether you're running or not, running feels very clunky (Not to mention you have a hard time actually getting away from the people if they're chasing you, and it have a lower turn control definitely doesn't help), and picking up some objects is more trouble than it's worth. Don't forget, you can softlock yourself by putting the bell in the garage and closing the garage, only to find out you can't open it. So what ends up looking like a good spot while you're surveying the market area ends up screwing you over and that late into the final task. And while it's funny at first (the game, I mean), it really does just devolve into headache-inducing puzzles that you need a guide for because some are just that convoluted, like making the burly guy get a bucket on his head or stealing the gardener's hat. Coupled with the game's controls make for what looks like a meme game turned into an infuriating experience. Unfortunate, too, because conceptually, it's a great idea. It's just the execution has a lot to be desired for.

However, for a puzzle to be solvable it has to be intuitive and logical - which many of the task in the Untitled Goose game are not. I want to love it, I really do, however the difficulty in just figuring what the game wants from you is wasting more time and bringing less joy that I would expect such a fun concept game to have.

At first, there comes a screen rolling problem, like the Contra's 2P mode, when Goose1 and Goose2 stays at the left/right edge respectively, Goose1 can NOT go left while Goose2 remains still, vise versa. _childDocuments_.review: Stupid honk memes aside, this game is an exercise in frustration.Want to put items in a shopping basket for a quest? Too bad, the shopkeeper sees it from MILES away and undoes your progress.Accidentally fell into the river while trying to drop a glass in it and forgot to open a shortcut door, which only opens from one side? Too bad! Have fun slooowly going through the whole map to get back to this location.Finally got to the last quest? Have fun carrying an item that immediately attracts attention to anyone, and more so if you sprint! And you have to wrestle it back everytime you drop it. Oh, and did I mention that all the shortcuts you could use to speed this up are magically patched up just for this quest?Maybe it wouldn't be so bad if the controls were good. The default KB/M controls are complete trash, even when I switched from mouse to arrow keys, it didn't help. Controller is a bit better, but still not good. If the walk/sprint was not wonky, if you didn't have to move to a specific position to take an item off of people's hands, the game would be so much better. Instead, you have to wrestle both the controls and the NPCs. It's only funny when your progress gets undone maybe a couple of times, but it happens constantly.Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was young my family ran a small animal farm.  We had chickens, ducks, rabbits, and of course, geese.  At first we just had two geese.  Hope and Joy.  They were pretty chill.  Mostly just honkin' around and being geese.  Then we got two more geese.  Georgia and Ruby.  Though we quickly found out Georgia was not Georgia and was instead Jeremy.  Jerry --as we called him-- was very very very mean.  He would run at you from across the property just to bite your knees.  He was what we in the industry call; a bastard.  It got so bad that the FedEx driver would not get out of his truck and would instead sit there honking the horn until one of us came and grabbed the package from him.  Jerry terrorized me and my siblings.  Jerry eventually died doing what he loved.  Domestic terror.  He got hit by a car cause he was chasing them in the road.  To this day I HATE geese with a burning passion.  It's an inside joke with my friends and family. They think it's funny how much i say I hate them but I really truly hate them.Moral of the story.  If you want to be a bastard and honk at children, play this game.

You can play however you'd like, and progressing is done by having fun. Definitely a worthwhile time for anyone interested. Everyone in my inner circle must be notified of the glory this game contains. To many more wonderful games such as this to grace my steam library is truly the end goal in life.

_childDocuments_.review: A game so based it doesn't even need a title. Untitled Goose Game places you in control of one goose freedom fighter on a quest to rid the world of its scourge of peace, quiet and common decency. Combining stealth elements and puzzle solving, you'll swindle, gaslight and otherwise terrorize some perfectly nice people that are just minding their own business. You monster.Being a goose isn't always easy, regardless. Advanced goose physics mean that you'll have to occasionally fight with your clumsy goose feet as you move, not to mention that the A.I. of the townspeople is unreliable and erratic, no doubt on account of your damage to their mental health. You may sometimes find your schemes thwarted by these circumstances, but don't despair! Rise above your station, and begin a new reign of chaos, at least for three hours or so. You're bound to feel better about something by the end of it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely morning in the village and you are a horrible goose. Untitled Goose Game is a slapstick-stealth-sandbox, where you are a goose let loose on an unsuspecting village. Make your way around town, from peoples' back gardens to the high street shops to the village green, setting up pranks, stealing hats, honking a lot, and generally ruining everyone’s day.

name: HyperParasite
detailed_description: Invading a grime encrusted dystopia straight out the eighties, you're the monster the authorities warned about. Dragging your bloody tentacles on the greasy asphalt, you snatch body after body . You are the HyperParasite ; an evil alien with a bone to pick with humanity…just because it’s fun . Infesting the sickest corners of the most ass-kicking decade, you must fight your way to the top of the pop-cultural food chain, in order to push the Big Red Button and bring about the mushroom cloud of finality. Be the baddest, navigating the dangerous procedurally generated streets of a hopeless past, in this tough twin-stick roguelite brawling S.O.B. 'Long live the new flesh' Look at all those juicy meat-sacks going to waste on those grotty humans! As the HyperParasite you can make better use of them, snatching hosts with your tentacles, absorbing them and their different abilities . Once they die you can discard their skin, but keep on snatching, since one shot as the parasite and it's permadeath . That is, unless you found some nice upgrades , so keep your eyes open…or your feelers high...or whatever a parasite does. 'Hosting makes me feel good' Feed the parasite with over 60 different characters , as you collect and control hosts , each with their own unique attack and smack-down . Hunt down the host class boss, rip their brain off (they didn´t use it anyway), and take it back to Wito's, our ever-greedy shopkeeper . Using some very weird machinery to store the brain , you can then unlock the character with your hard stolen cash. There's even a storage unit for your already collected hosts to come back to in later games. 'Yeah, Downtown must be the friendliest place on Earth...' Since the game is procedurally generated , nobody knows what's waiting around the next dark corner. Can you survive the 5 Acts of this grungy-looking synthwave-filled world? Maybe yes, if you remember that what lies in the shadows is essential, as there are secrets within secrets to explore within its roguelite mapping system. And if you keep a tentacle out for the bosses , as they pack one mean punch! Pump up the volume! Original beats served by Van Reeves and Joe Kataldo, delivering a thumping score with a pulsating synthwave bassline, punctuating every snatch and kill. A friend in need... Trouble loves company, as you can bring a mate to deliver twice the carnage in two-player local co-op mode.

short_description: A rogue-lite twin-stick shooter/brawler that never plays the same twice. Collect and control 60 different characters as the body-snatching alien Parasite with a grudge against humanity. Fight to the top of the food chain: possess the President, push the Big Red Button and one-up the human race.

_childDocuments_.review: An isometric Roguelite that masters the mechanics of a twin stick shooter and its interesting premise, but uses them in frustrating ways. There is also not enough content to make it enjoyable and replayable, there aren’t any interesting combos that can cause the game to go crazy and change, and there isn’t any real customization to speak of in terms of skills or upgrades.👍  👍Unique premise👎  👎Repetitive gameplayDisappointing upgradesFrustrating difficulty curveBeing an alien parasite that can take over human minds to enslave them to its will isn’t easy. For one, an alien parasite’s body is made of gelatinous goo that explodes with the slightest poke, let alone a baseball bat strike or a bullet, but that is why the fleshy meat sacks are so important. Hyper Parasite puts the player in such a situation where they must pilot this odd creature in an isometric twin-stick shooter which has strong and interesting mechanics but fails at my three Cs of a good Roguelite. I include in this review what must be included for it to be set alongside the hall of fame greats. As previously mentioned, the parasite itself is very weak, which is why the main mechanic focuses on taking over bodies which each have their own individual health-pools, normal attack, and special ability. Starting out, the player is only able to possess a few enemies but when killing the ones yet unlocked, there is a chance their brain can be obtained and stored in a lab adjacent to the shop. Money can then be invested in unlocking their DNA so that they can be possessed, opening up new possibilities in terms of abilities. This implementation does cause some issues when moving on to the next level, of which there are five, when it turns out that all of the bodies for the next level are locked behind the brains that have only a chance of dropping. This causes an intense difficulty spike which ends up being extremely frustrating. The reason for this is that by the time the player is able to reliably get to the next level, they will have unlocked almost all of the characters from the previous level, making the latter extremely easy because every time the player’s host body dies, the game spawns another one which ends up making it nearly impossible to fail. To then be hit by everything to be locked again feels like an unwelcome surprise.Another disappointment arrives in the form of upgrades. They can be bought at the shop or rarely  dropped by killed enemies. These upgrades come in three different categories such as single use items like a sentry turret, damage over time, or a stat up. The single use items are rather costly and not especially helpful as they take away from the main currency of unlocking bodies which makes them feel useless and ultimately, in most cases where the player buys them, detrimental. Damage over time upgrades can be helpful, especially when there aren’t a lot of stat ups in a run, but as, upgrades they ultimately leave a lot to be desired since they are only useful in the early game. Finally, the most important upgrade to talk about would be the stat ups. They come in three flavors: extra life, more damage, and more defense. The only one I found to be useful would be the damage up as by the time the player has started to master a level, the game is throwing so many enemies – also known as free lives – at the player that they don’t have to care about anything defensive at all. It certainly won’t help a player going to a new level, as it will only end up prolonging the inevitable death. Damage is also the most important stat to have, as if the player doesn’t take attack constantly, most bodies that aren’t heavy hitters start to deal menial amounts of damage that will end up requiring the player to sit around circling a normal enemy for a whole minute, which is neither satisfying nor rewarding.I now get to the three  of a good Roguelite, and as someone who has found that rougelites are their favorite genre of game I can say that I think these three things are what establish a masterful and top tier roguelite game, whether that be through a mix or mastery of a single . The first  is content, the it is the backbone of most roguelites as they are procedurally generated. Hyper Parasite is quite lacking in this department and I did get tired of constantly seeing the same bodies and the same rooms which made it feel repetitive. I got tired of playing the same level to unlock things to get to the next, as every run felt almost entirely the same. This is contrasted by a rougelite master of content “Enter the Gungeon” which has so many guns that there is always something new to look forward to in the next run.Combos are important and can often change the game around in new and exciting ways. Currently there aren’t any real combos in the game so everything feels very static. The bodies inhabited never change, and neither do their stats or abilities. One way I would have loved to see the game enhance to main mechanic of taking over bodies would have been if they could be fused in the lab to get a new body. One such example could be the gang guy who throws a chain and the hobo who performs a light melee attack. Fuse them together and you have the gang hobo who pushes their cart forward with chains attached to it and then it comes back to them and the distance is based upon how long the player charged the attack. Sadly, once the player sees a particular body, they know exactly what to expect which adds to the repetitive nature of the game. A rougelite great for this would be the Binding of Isaac, also a personal favorite of mine.This focuses on skill trees and making a run unique. It would have been fun to potentially unlock characters to take over every time but make them much cheaper and have skill trees that allowed some enemy bodies to do better than others. This might alleviate the issue of any body being good every run. The king of this style would be Tales of Maj’Eyal or ADOM.The story is simple and only really explains why the events of the game is occurring, which is normal for a rougelite.The sound design is all right but once again repetitive. The one aspect of the sound design I did enjoy however is the announcer. His boisterous and excited pronouncements at the amount of slaughter and carnage on the screen help to make it feel more interesting and provides a sense of power in the player’s actions.The graphics are good, as every unique body is pretty easily distinguishable which helps to know what their power is from the start.The game controls best on a controller.: No real bugs to speak of.

_childDocuments_.review: I was completely unaware of HyperParasite's (HP) existence, until the developer sent a message saying this would be perfect for, “Someone who eats Enter the Gungeon and Binding of Isaac for breakfast.” Intrigued, I checked out the store page, saw that it had a respectable review score, and decided I'd throw down on that sort of challenge, especially since I've not played those two games that had been referenced. I'm skipping breakfast, and taking this game to lunch. HP is a twin stick shooter, rogue lite, and you control a weak parasite. It can kill enemies, but being hit by anything takes away a life, and you start each run with only one. At the earliest possibility, you'll want to inhabit a suitable host, since if the host dies, it doesn't harm the parasite. Plus, their attack power is significantly stronger. In spite of being able to find upgrades and skills during runs, there are no permanent stat increases, as each run has you start in a random body. For this review, I'll only address how HP plays in 80's Mode, as that's the default mode to play in.So, how do you get stronger? By being a good parasite, of course. At first, you're surrounded by enemies that are useless to you, because they have a padlock icon over them, indicating you can't infect them. Ironically, what you'll want to find are red-ringed enemies, which you can never possess. However, if it's an enemy you haven't unlocked yet, killing it produces a brain, which you take to the shop and unlock with money. From then on, you can possess that enemy as often as you want. Unlocked bodies only pertain to each individual zone, of which there are five, with each new location forcing you to start from scratch.It's possible to play this game with the keyboard, but I found it worked quite well with a controller. There's some interesting features to this title, primarily because of how you're a distinct entity from the host bodies you invade. Due to this, it's possible to make use of the host's special abilities, or discard them in favor of a better alternative.At the start of HP, an opening cutscene plays out, with the President of the USA (PS) warning the nation about an alien parasite infecting bodies. Your goal is to take possession of the PS, and launch the nuclear arsenal to wipe out all human life. With intelligence agencies determining your goal, but not your location, everyone has been ordered to eliminate you, though I don't know how they recognize you while inside a host. Plus, whenever someone would determine where you are, why not call in a nuclear strike on that area? Because there wouldn't be a game, of course! The game's visuals don't scream 80's to me the way others say. Although the bodies you can possess references media from that time, the visuals otherwise make me think of games made in the 2010's. HP isn't a pixelated game, and there are details present in each environment, such as the litter, trash fires, and neon signs in the Downtown area. However, I don't care much for the visuals, as it has a washed out look. What I mean by this is that the edges don't look crisp, but somewhat blurred, and the backgrounds seem random with their colors.I find the title theme unpleasant, as it has a strange pitch to it. Otherwise, I think the music is reasonably good. When you're exploring stages without enemies around, the game plays a calmer track. However, when you're locked in combat, it speeds up, and plays a more aggressive song. The music does change for each zone, but I don't recall there being a variety of songs in each area. HP would benefit from more versatility in the music selection, especially with how much you replay the same spots.🌟 I like the variety of enemies in the game, including some of the creative weaponry. For instance, the basketball player who throws basketballs, or the ex-FBI agent who shoots a paperclip gun.🌟 There are currently two game modes available, with plans to release other modes in future updates. Plus, the game has local coop.❌ Some details aren't explained very well in HP. For instance, what luck has an effect on, which order you need to navigate alternative routes in, how you're supposed to get past barriers like the garbage dumpster or the void, etc.❌ Since all money is lost when you fail a run, and buying host bodies is the only way to cause a permanent effect, it's easy to make a decent run, but make no progress whatsoever from it.❌ RNG plays a big role in your runs: whether you'll have access to the shop at a convenient time, the quality of skills available, and how much money you get, since its luck-dependent.🔍 Though you will be outgunned and in tough situations, enemies are easy to manipulate. If you get out of their line of sight by taking cover, they'll pause before rushing toward you, which is a great opportunity to turn the corner and blast them.🔍 Putting bodies into storage allows you to access them from any other Wito shop within the same run. So, if you've not unlocked a host body in the 3rd area, you can have spare bodies waiting for you once you get there.🔍 There are consistent items in each main area: Wito's shop, at least three upgrades, one secret item, one mini-boss, and one elite enemy. At first, when I saw less hosts in upcoming zones, I was somewhat disappointed. However, as I put more than a dozen hours into HP, I was exasperated by how many remained. The unique gameplay of HP in turn creates a unique downside. Since the trade-off you make for not having permanent stat upgrades is access to an endless pool of spare bodies to inhabit, the start of each run starts playing the same way each time, as a boring routine. Although the overwhelming advantage shifting to your favor is fun at first, when you have to kill every enemy to clear rooms and get to the next zone, it gets old quick. Especially since you have to make each run count by finding all the upgrades and skills that you can, because you need them to make progress in the later areas where you don't have several hosts already unlocked. This is what made me give up on going further with HP. Not because it was too hard, but because investing so much time just to put a few drops in the bucket in later areas was so unrewarding and frustrating. By the time I quit, I was able to consistently clear the first three bosses, and had taken down the 4th boss on my first attempt fighting it. Without a way to shave off some of this needless repetition, I've no interest in playing this further, and don't recommend it in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: At start it seemed to me like an ordinary boring roguelike, first 40 minutes was monotonous and grindy. I noted music (track of the first location actually) and good visual style. The game revealed itself after i beat first boss (which is actually not so spectacular from point of experience and gameplay) but then you got access to new areas with a new style and challenges. Suddenly the game gains its true colors and shine - fun, variable and challenging, as a good roguelike should be.I find that on these levels game prepared brand new host bodies (playable characters) as well as enemies.And even on first locations it can surprise you with new interesting events, just give it a shot.As for core mechanics - all good, moving, shooting and using skills feels just right and well designed.Ye, there are weaknesses, as confusing tutorial, very small icons and fonts, unclear power-ups. But all these trivia.Technical part is good, i didnt faced any bug or glitch.All in all it is a good game and most importantly it is fun and aesthetically attractive

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often buy Early Access game, but I had a chance to try HyperParasite in London at Rezzed the last weekend, and yes, i had to buy it.First of all, the game is thousand times more polished that what i do usually expect from EA games. I died like 20 times before the tutorial was over, but that is only pushing me to play more.The devs at the booth were awesome and friendly, it's refreshing to meet people that funnel such a passion in their work. I am gonna play a lot more before adding more technicalities to this review, but already know, in less than 2 hours, the amount of 80s refs to stuff I grew up with gave me glorious goosebumps. At some point I will also stop dying this much, i guess.Really cool game, very glad i bought it, and freaking glad I am playing it.[Edit - 1st of September] Since the review I doubled my playing time, the game grew with weekly updates that kept it alive and show the devs real dedication, i died countless times, and i finally managed to beat the hell out of Rocco Marcellino. Ah, and I met the devs again in Gamescom and they are still cool. Bigger thumps up than before. This is what an early access should be.PS still love this game

_childDocuments_.review: good concept but definitely not enough content and the playtime is made up by ridiculous grinding. Most times you get to the shop it feels like the special item is the same amount of gold as all the money on the map after youve gone through and destroyed everything. Everytime you get to a new area you just die cause you can't unlock the characters on the map, and it takes about 10 games to be able to do anything in the levelGame crashes like nobodys business, i'm done with this game until it gets some content and fixes the ridiculous crashes
