_childDocuments_.review: I waited SO LONG for this one.I tried. I really really tried to love this.But this is just NOT GOOD.In short: This takes everything Startopia did and does it worse.1. Research is tiresome. I liked the fact you can unlock the first level with Prestige, but what happened to Tech Crates?! What about Idle Research to randomly improve tech?2. Manufacturing is slow and troublesome. It's also buggy as hell - you constantly need to cancel and re issue  commands. It's tiresome. Also, why do I need to fabricate a Mk2 drone as preq to Mk3 drone!? Doesn't make any sense. We are in 2021, how come there's no auto-fabrication orders?3. Which brings me to Cargo holds. They SUCK. They are far worse than the original game. I mean, shared inventory someone? WE HAD IT! Why did we *loose* features?4. Trade. There's no trade till about half-way through progress. NO TRADE AT ALL. What happened to rip-off trader to bootstrap you?5. Again, tech crates. Why do I have to fabricate the same room 5 times just to improve it, especially when fabrication is so so tiresome. I mean, the Factory knows to create a fabrication chain of Minerals->Plastic->Holo Crystal-> Drone. Why can't the lab just *order* the fabrication as a chain?These are just the *major* problems of gameplay. It's SO annoying that things we *had* in the original disappeared.But the worse part is - it's a cheap fake and you feel it. Aliens are basically a clone of the original (the entertainer, the scientist, the police, etc. Right down to factory and recycler having the same alien), but they're all cartoonish and "colorful".The jokes of VAL are a lame attempt to recreate the gritty/dark feel of the original, which makes no sense given that everything else is super cartoonish and disco-lights.Also, security. Security drones SUCK. The Mechs are unwieldy unless you waste tons of space. And the worst part? THERE ARE NO WARRIORS. NONE. Your aliens simply run, and only drones and mechs fight. So if it happens that your Mech got a bit stuck on the biodeck, that's it. You're done for.This game is to the original like a cheap obvious fake.Spare your coin. Play the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write these,  but Startopia... this is not.So I have just completed the first few missions as well as the tutorials and to say I'm disappointed is an understatement.It's as if the developers have gone, "here is a title that was popular back in the day lets try and clone it. However lets remove all the things which made it fun and replace it with a higher res mess."Ok maybe its not quite that bad but lets talk about why this is a disappointment. For the record I played the original to death and loved it. It  wasn't without its flaws but it was a fun game that had a good difficulty curve and presented hours of laughs.- The Narration: In the original game we had real voice actors providing witty comments, engaging dialogue helping you progress through the story. Most of all they made you laugh! Where as in this version you have a choice of 3 different narrators which all feel like they are a cheap text to speech cop-out which to be quite frank is grating me. Yes I know you can change the voices but its between annoying voice, 1, 2 or 3 but seriously take a moment and listen to the original and you will get what I mean.- The Tutorials: For new players to the series these are an important gateway to get you in to the game. However I'm not sure the developers have actually played them through. They miss key pieces of info, send you all over the place and have little to no consistency. They have text falling out of menu's for gods sake! To say its rough on release is an understatement. - The UI: How did they chuff this up? The UI is much harder to use, additional clicks all over the place that don't need to be there, short cuts removed etc. Its clunky as heck to use, menu's are hidden and its all round counter intuitive. - Game Design: I'm not sure they have thought about the logic of what and why they have made certain decisions. The Berth being a prime example. They have moved food in to it.. not sure why but ok, but then they don't allow bins in it as a room item which is mental, so berths just become a garbage dump.- Its Dark: By this I mean the original was light, seeing the differences between rooms, aliens etc etc was clean and understandable. Now its this mash of organisms, but distinguishing between them isn't obvious. And the bin graphic is an outside star twinkle texture... why?- Security: This is not a reason to buy the game but .. wtf, Security was previously run by the "Gor" which was basically a walking meat tank with muscles and spikes on its shoulders. Now we have the "Leviathan" which sounds scary for sure... its a fat smiling dolphin.. I mean.. come on >.<I came in to this game with such high hopes, I bought it regardless of the cost without a second thought. However its like a poor clone that has had no love put in to it. I can guarantee of this was done by a lone dev as a project of love it would have been so much better.  Buy maybe with some patches they can resolve it so I will hold on with hope :).But for now.. It pains me to say it but I'd say play the original and have some laughs, but avoid this.Sorry for ranting all!
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews and I was torn for a few days on whether or not to purchase. There isn't a whole lot of YouTube content on this game, especially since the last round of bug fixes. I thought to myself, are the bugs THAT bad? Is it really not playable? I ended up pulling the trigger and I am glad that I did! This is, in my opinion, an improvement over the original game. I have about 200 hours into the original, from when it was first released many years ago and more recent play thrus. For this game, I completed the campaign in about 10 hours and I really didn't min-max, was just completing the objectives. In regards to the bugs, are there some? Sure are! The game crashed once on my randomly during the last mission and once I lost sound for a few minutes. I went to save and reload, but after saving, the sound was back on! I had no real bugs besides that but like I said, I was just progressing through the missions. If you enjoyed the original, I think you will enjoy this one just as much. There are a few differences in game play, but I think it is an improvement overall. The BioDeck is much less micro managing but serves a far larger importance than the original. Trading is still here, but I didn't make a ton of energy like I did in the original. I found the key to this game was using the factory and BioDeck. I like the unlocking of tech/items feature and the research feels good. Combat is better than the first, but still not the point of the game imo, so I was fine with it. I kind of fell in love with the FunDeck's music as well. Overall, I would recommend this game to others. It has potential for addons in the future and with 10 hours in the books, only one crash. I had fun playing and look forward to sinking some more time into the game, isn't that what its all about?! Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original to death and have completed the game on Admiral difficulty, so I've been through the worst of it. And I'm looking at that "Mixed" rating, and I've got something to say on the matter.So if you're looking for the opinion of someone who played the original, played the new one and wants to give a contrary opinion to that rating, then read on. Truth be told I find the negative reception to this game understandable, but . A number of blemishes mar the sheen of an otherwise quite passable and unique creature management simulator. But those negative points need to be worked through first before getting to it.Not only are there quite a few things to find unpalatable straight off the bat, there's a few things that come out during the real meat of the game that are more than likely responsible for turning the early unfavourable impressions into dissatisfied reviews. But the standout in both of those sordid camps is the character of VAL.VAL can be compared to GlaDOS only if you're willing to commit grievous verbal heresy. She goes from being a dutiful service droid to passive-aggressive indifference to contemptuous sarcasm over the course of the campaign, which would normally be interesting if it was the development arc of an actual . VAL, however, is not something I can really call a "character". VAL is done entirely in text-to-speech, which is honestly impressive, but it means the script for VAL is essentially reading itself and there's no human being involved with its delivery. What you end up with is Microsoft Sally droning on and on in a way that just isn't interesting, and is - painful as it is to type - only occasionally funny, if you forgive the fact that most of the time the humour is a variation on "meatsacks are dumb." Not to say that there aren't some solid bits that play more to general robot humour that hit their mark, but it's not enough to redeem the "character."Monotone AI voices have been done before - they can work perfectly fine, if the AI itself is some sort of character you come to care about in some way, but VAL's indifference-to-hostility arc means we have nothing to get attached to. Put simply, VAL is one of the chief reasons this game failed to connect with its target audience. I can tell that the promise of a text-to-speech companion would have cut costs considerably for voice acting and localisation. But if you load up the original Startopia, you'll hear the original VAL on the very first mission; on the second, you'll hear him talking about the aliens dying in your hospital and the possibility of failing the mission. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the difference is  between original VAL and modern VAL. Original VAL , for starters, and was voice acted by some truly legendary British dude who so perfectly nailed the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy humour it's a wonder he wasn't genetically designed for the role. VAL in Spacebase Startopia, by contrast, is almost better being turned off completely.I've had to work past a few quirks in this game, and there's a few. You know how, in complex simulation games, you get into some weird situations where units don't quite path-find correctly because of a rare situation they're in? Truthfully that doesn't happen very often at all in this game - a fact that you'll probably be surprised at - but it can happen when creatures are spawning due to illness or piracy keeps happening in the same place.I could never honestly figure out why my aliens had such problems raising their Fun need at the Disco as consistently as I would have liked. I think it was something to do with possibly (A) the Disco's actually being overloaded at 80% workload instead of 100% or something, or more likely (B) not placing enough Food/Drink/Sleep/Hygiene fillers on the Fun Deck so they had to go too far away to satisfy those needs; I figured this out rather late in the game and didn't experiment quite as much.What else. Oh, yes. The music and sound bugs. Strangely these I had less trouble with, since there are easy fixes - one of which involves . Annoying to deal with, yes, but not a dealbreaker.There are other small bugs too; a few times my Mechs didn't quite correctly respond to my commands, which was frustrating beyond measure. Things of that ilk. There are definitely little things that made me have to look into exactly why things were happening the way they were happening on my station, but with some observation the answers weren't ever too far away, eventually.With all this negativity put on the table, it's past time to start singing a few select praises of Spacebase Startopia, because despite popular opinion, there are many things that are worthy of at least an honourable mention.Spacebase Startopia is a relatively complex creature simulation game. Every creature has a plethora of Needs, a multitude of effects being applied to it from buildings, its immediate environment, research effects, its own particular stat points and the like. The economy of the game - not just in terms of Energy, but in terms of the Resource hard assets and the ecosystem by which you gain them, store them and use them - is accessible, but detailed without becoming overly complex. When you take a step back and consider that all of this runs at a scale of around ~600 aliens on your part of the station, it should be said that effectively clobbing all this together is no mean feat. The original Startopia definitely provided a workable blueprint, but the actual implementation of it in Unity is quite an impressive feat at the scale Spacebase Startopia can go to. I encountered few pathfinding issues that weren't caused by aliens running from enemies that continued to plague them. It creaks and strains under load when filtering for alien selections, but the fact that it runs nicely when simulating the actual game has to be given some credit; it works, and works fairly well. While it's nice that the engine runs and all that, the real draw is the actual game itself and damn if this didn't really get its pincers into me. Things were coming to life before my eyes mission by mission, and slowly the core of the game came out and before I knew it I was well and truly hooked, There really is something satisfying about playing this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Dare I say it, when you get past all of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ above, I had some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ . The visuals, which I originally thought to be bland compared to the original, started to really come to life with the later buildings and in the detailed interactions the aliens have with the various objects in the rooms. And I can't deny that I've been humming the music while outside, the Fun Deck beats having burrowed deep into my ears at this point. Or the Sub Deck. Their tracks both rock.I  why this game failed to get higher ratings. The "out there right in front of you" parts suck. VAL sucks. But when I was done with the missions I immediately went into Free Play and started a new space station simply because I wasn't finished.It turned out some of VAL's better jokes are in the Free Play mode, so that worked out pretty well in the end too.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading the reviews, I put off purchasing this game for a year and finally bought it on sale. I'm really glad I gave it a try. I was a big fan of the original. After playing most of the campaign, I really am confused about what a lot of the negative reviews are talking about. The game has many of the same mechanics, processes, buildings, and alien functions as the original: a race for medicine, one for recycling, one for communication, another for security, as well as entertainment, farming, religion, etc. It has terrorist bombs like the original and spacestation sections, even the layout of the station is identical to the original with three layers: biodeck, entertainment deck, and subdeck for industry, cargo, and basic alien needs. The game must have undergone some updates in the last year since the original reviews because the annoying voice of the original AI is now optional: you have the choice of 3 different AI voices. I listened to the original voice and it was atrocious, so I can completely understand why people hated it a year ago. Anyway, its a good space station building game really. No bugs, no problems really. I'm glad I gave it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice remake of the old Startopia from 2001, but still a lot of bugs. Definitely not worth 50€.The idea is ok, Gameplay did not much change in 20 years. The graphics are nicer, sound as well, but the engine seems to have massive problems. Without slowing down the game speed it is nearly impossible to get thru the later missions with more than one opponent. There is just too much micro management going on while fighting. You need to harvest any plant/tree manually on the bio deck to have sufficient resources at the beginning. Money is usually not a problem in this game, with every innovation you get a lot of money to build the new building and hire employes. But the bugs really made me dislike the game. It is in early access at best. Not a game that you can charge the full price for.The bugs that really annoyed me:-  Research and Factory. Even if you have researched an Item, the factory will not let you build it and say it is not researched yet. Even worse, if you have many factories. Some will let you build the new item, some others not. If you save the game, go back to the main menu and load it again it fixes it. Until you research something new or move the factories to a different place. Then you have to do it over again.-  Aliens at the wrong place. I noticed some Aliens laying around somewhere on the ground. Then I clicked on them to see what is wrong the screen changed to a different level and they where sleeping in a hotel actually. Sometimes hats are stuck somewhere, just the hats, not with aliens.And some more stuff, not sure if they are actually bugs or just a bad engine:-  Aliens are angry and complain about disco, but the large disco is not even utilized to 10%.- Aliens are angry about thirst or sleep, but again the buildings that provide drinks/slurps or the stasis chamber/hotels are empty.- resources are rotten on the bio deck while my fuzzy are lines up on the wall doing nothing.Navigating thru the station is a pain. The camera has to be a the right angle/height to move from one sector to another and you get stuck at every gate.I think a fair price would ne 19,99€ once the bugs are fixed. After Port Royal 4 this is the 2nd bad game from Kalypso.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the original Startopia and must have spent hundreds of hours playing it as a kid, I even go back to it every few years to play a little bit still, so I was super surprised to see that they made another one!Unfortunately trying this out I was left feeling incredibly disappointed, the short summary of my experience is that it feels completely "souless", it fails to capture pretty much anything about the feel and look of the old game, the aestethics, sounds, music, etc all feel worse (which is honestly kinda baffling considering how dated old Startopia is today), the gameplay feels underwhelming and really strange compared to the old, its full of weird decisions and changes that deviate a lot from what this is based on. Ultimately this gives off the impression of being some kind of chinese bootleg knock off game made by a team who has seemingly never played the original, or failed to understand what made the original good.Here are some gripes I had in no particular order:- The camera controls are somehow worse than the original, if press and hold your mousewheel and use the movement keys, you zoom in, you also use the same prompt to rotate the camera (because no sane person is going to use Q and E to rotate the view). The incredibly cramped space of the decks (compared to the more spacious and open old decks) also mean you don't get as clean of a view of everything as before. You switch decks using F1-F3, but can no longer switch decks on the fly with TAB. There are few keybinds to tweak this, if any.- Instead of Aarona Dal, the one trader that will show up at any time, selling you basic neccesities and sometimes random goods at ludicrious prices you instead get some generic menu on a timer that shuffles 4 random items, a lot of which are these awful worthless bloated temporary use items. When Aarona showed up, you got a distinct icon for him, you'd check to see what he had and exit out, in this game you often straight up forget to check the trading menu at all.I could be completely wrong also, but I swear you could sell your junk to him too, but that might just be me going senile.- The new VAL (and lack of Aarona, and any "voiceovers" for any of the alien requests) is terrible, the new voices are these humorless patronizing annoying pricks devoid of charm. They often don't alert you at all when something is happening, and will instead most of the time only appear to sprout of some repetetive quip or insult. The alien designs also lack charm. I really really miss the old aliens, the new ones look so bad. Instead of the chad kaskagovorian race we now have fat loser bears who can't even fight. Oh yeah, aliens now all apparently communicate through twitter to express their thoughts. #crime #criminalseverywhere #sad #trash #shutupthismethodofwritingandconveyingthingsisntfunnyorcuteyoudidareallybadjobhere.- Events are strange too. You can't even tell when a starquake happens, you just get a box that says it happened. You for some reason randomly get alerted about random visitor groups showing up, but they don't mean anything. For some reason the game ASKS you if you want hostiles to board your station and attack you, and they will pay you to do this (???), and the majority of requests you get are just "hey we are going to spawn garbage piles or pollute the air in exhange for money".I just don't get it, how did you manage to make the events and alien requests somehow less impactful and varied than a game where it boiled down to "ooga booga the screen shakes and a building takes damage", "help we are sick let us board your station and get healed", "we are in a pilgrimage :)" and "a spy has planted a bomb and will blow up 4 buildings"?- You can no longer change the cost of buildings and services. What?In fact you can't even tell how much energy anything does or costs, how much am I paying for my staff? How much am I making per patient cured? What am I charging for people to board my station? Etc, the game literally does not tell you this. It felt like I was making most of my money from recycling garbage and thats just weird man.It used to be in the past that if you had too many visitors on the station you'd upcharge the Ports so that people stopped showing up as often, but now you can't do that and visitors show up forever beyond capacity.- There is an unlock system for some reason? You passively earn "prestige points" which you use to unlock things, but you have to unlock them in a certain order because the requirements tend to require you to have a previous unlock built. So to even have the ability to build a starport and actually trade with people I needed to have a bunch of random entertainment deck buildings.I never did reach the point where I got a research lab going, but I guess you just unlock everything, and then use the lab to IMPROVE the things instead? Also you get PAID for unlocking things? Why? What was wrong with the old system of having to unlock things through a research three with the analyzer, and being incentivized to use the factory to produce the things you unlocked for cheaper than outright building them? - Combat is really not good. For some reason, none of the alien staff are armed anymore. So if you get a chest burster or a pirate or anything hostile, you literally cannot fight back unless you have a staffed security station with drones. Drones are also pretty limited in quantity. You can also build "mechs" which are these giant slow robots that just suck so bad and require all this space to even move around, I don't like it. I prefered the system of clicking on hostiles to designate termination and any available hands running to gun them down. Security scuzzers are gone too, only drones and mechs can fight.- Quality of life changes were good but weirdly random. Hold and click to hoover up trash n such, and to quickly dump it all. Good. Press the number keys to select which slot in your bar you want instead of having to dump things in order, but don't select anything by default (weird, but neat I guess?). Hold the mouse button on the promotion button to promote everyone... of the specific race you are looking at. Also remove the ability to promote people whenever you want. Uhhh... Select singular plants and click a harvest button in a menu to harvest the one plant, instead of just clicking on a plant to harvest instantly or display a time to harvest circle. Uhhhhhhh.... Click outside of the menu to exit the menu but require the ESC key to exit some, uhhhh...We now have garbage bots, which automatically collect garbage, but also there are no more trash bins and aliens must now just drop garbage directly on the floor. Uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh....- Alien AI is wonky? A lot of the time workplaces were understaffed, despite 4 times the number of aliens required being available and free. Sometimes people would just die too because they didn't seek medical care until they were literally about to drop dead. Also I had a really hysterical sound bug where all the sound would just mute. The fix for this was pausing the game, going into the options menu, and then unpausing. This would happen every 5-15 minutes or so.Anyway there is more I could gripe about, but the point is that this is just Startopia but worse. It is not an improvement.It is MUCH EASIER though, so if you couldn't figure out how to play the original at all, or have never played the original and have nothing to compare the experience to, then this is probably for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who put 100+ hours into the old one: this game was designed by someone who played the original and copied it and didn't understand what they were doing. I preordered this a year ago, and I'm disappointed.- Berths used to be for sleep only. Now they also contain food AND hygiene, which...fine in theory, right? A one-stop show for aliens to chow, clean up and sleep. Except that these things generate garbage, and you CANNOT put garbage cans into the berth, so it just accumulates garbage everywhere. Also, you get extra long queues into the building as everyone tries to wedge into there first.- The humor. It tries to be as wacky as the original but goes overboard into cringe territory. I hate to say it, but - the opening cutscene was forced and unfunny. The narrator doesn't stop, and even as the Glados voice filter it was a nonstop insult parade.- The new "worker" class aliens. They used to be cute little salt hogs who were all about working and never stopping. Now it's garbage aliens who live for garbage. Fine. But they all wear boxer shorts with little hearts on them, and that's just juvenile.- Hashtags! There shouldn't be hashtags, those went out of fashion years ago and take me out of the game in an unpleasant way.- Unclear visual design. I didn't realize I had waiting crates - they're hidden on a shelf in your energy collector. That shouldn't be happening!And so on and so forth. It's a... decent Startopia clone and I'll play more, but all of these irritations build up into something really unpleasant, and I'm extremely tempted to uninstall it and play the original instead. That at least won't insult me NONSTOP as I do the basic tutorial missions! (and yes, I'm aware the old VAL gave you withering disdain and how you were barely competent, but he was voiced by the most perfect person and the writing was funny, not...cruel.)

_childDocuments_.review: I should clarify that I have not played the original Startopia, and thus won’t be making any comparisons here. That said, I am a fan of such simulation, management, and base building games, so I was quite excited to give Spacebase Startopia a look.First up was the tutorial, which wasn’t really the greatest. It guides you along the steps to setting up a base, but it doesn’t really explain what each building, resource, and such does. You’re just kinda placing stuff to check off each objective. It wasn’t until I got into the campaign that I really started to understand things, but even then, it was mostly a trial and error affair while I figured it all out. And despite the cutesy graphics, there is a LOT to this game, especially once you start working on the fun deck and have like 20 different buildings to place down there.There’s a good amount of variety with regards to buildings, units, resources, and the like and the management aspects are fairly polished. There’s this entire employment system, worker management, trading, and even sabotage for when you’re playing with AI or other players. It’s a fleshed-out experience for sure and the gameplay depth is pretty good for the most part.However, that’s before you consider all the smaller problems on top of that, which unfortunately start piling up quickly. For one, the gameplay has a serious problem with pacing. At the start, it is simply too slow, but once you get things rolling, it is too fast. I would go from just sitting there waiting for energy and prestige points to accumulate to eventually having a screen full of issues I have to fix. There are no time controls, so no pausing, no speeding things up, and I feel this is a game that could desperately use them.I was also not a fan of how “clicky” the game became as it went on. From random bombs spawning in the middle of your base that can only be removed by hand to having to shuffle around contraband goods whenever the galactic inspector arrived, there’s some really annoying micromanaging tasks thrown in there for seemingly no reason other than to add something else for you to worry about.Then there’s the combat, which has its own pacing issue. That being that it is far too slow and clunky, regardless of what stage of the game you’re at. You simply build your units and mechs and send them towards the enemy. Yes, there is a research tree and you can upgrade your damage, attack speed, and all that, but even that is not enough to save the combat from feeling like anything other than tacked-on and boring.Yes, there is a sandbox mode with a bunch of victory conditions you can setup. You can play against AI or even other players in multiplayer mode – although I was unable to test the multiplayer prior to release. The sandbox is where I ended up spending most of my time, either just messing around setting up the most optimal base or duking out with the AI. There is also a campaign, but it is only ten missions long and I managed to clear the first five within just four hours. I would have finished it, but unfortunately I got softlocked right at the end of mission five. An enemy that was supposed to spawn did not and no amount of reloading would fix that.And no, that was not the only bug I encountered. The bugs I found included:And those are just the ones I remember. It really made the game hard to play at times, especially when one of those stuck buildings was something like the elevator and you have this massive backlog of angry visitors forming in front of it until the game is reloaded.I wouldn’t say the performance is outright bad, but it definitely follows that base building trend of getting progressively less stable as it goes on. I started each run at around 80-90 fps or so and by the time I had built up my decks and had a bunch of aliens roaming everywhere, it would dunk to like 30-40 fps. Not entirely unexpected, but worth noting anyways.I was also annoyed by the complete omission of any sort of control rebinding. In fact, you can’t even view what the controls are supposed to be. There are no tooltips with hotkey indicators, no control layout in the settings menu, nothing. It’s a 100% trial and error affair outside of the few basic controls taught during the tutorial. And no, the UI is not helping there either. It can oftentimes be difficult to navigate and requires a bit of wrestling at times when managing your inventory and placing objects.I cannot recommend Spacebase Startopia – at least, not in its current state. The underlying gameplay is actually pretty good and I won’t deny I had a bit of fun with it, it’s just the mountain of smaller issues on top of that that really make it a hard sell. Whether that be the gameplay issues like lack of time controls and clunky combat or the far more numerous technical issues, I simply cannot in good faith recommend a game with such issues. Perhaps this will be something I can change in the future, but not as it stands.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I will go on record saying that the original Startopia is one of my favorite games ever and that I was very excited about this game. I knew there would be changes. I knew that I needed to reign in my expectations and to take this game at face value and to judge it fairly for what it was and what it was trying to be. I usually go into movies and games expecting mediocrity and I am usually right. I try not to get too hyped because I have been disappointed too many times. As the old saying goes, "Don't expect much, and you'll never be disappointed." Words to live by, indeed. However, I found this reboot a less than satisfactory management game, even when divorcing myself from my beloved original Startopia.First: The humor is gone. The original Startopia had a very dry, British wit about a huge, messed-up universe that was very, well, alien. The closest thing you see to a Human being, originally, is the sirens, but they are lofty and strange. The adorable Mamau can infect your passengers with horrible parasites that kill them and grow into massive scrashers. Everything is run-down and cobbled together. There's a thing called an Oroflex that swallows peaople spins around and vomits them out and people love it so much that they will pay you for it. One of the most valuable resources is Turdite, which is literally pooped out by horribly, corrupt and rich slug people who have no jobs on the station but to spend money. While VALwas a joyless bastard, he was also hilarious and occasionally praised you, which rounded him out. He also had a silky, British accent. In his place is a text-to-voice Siri parody that is just annoying and too confrontational. I got a chuckle every once in a while, but the world just didn't feel as alive, weird and varied. Instead we have social media references and everything just being too clean. And, no, I don't think that the game not being rated "M" doomed it to be not funny.Second: Most of what gave Startopia its identity is gone. The only thing to make it over to my knowledge are the grays being doctors, a new VAL program (granted a very inferior one), the station being a donut and skuzzers (though they look nothing alike how they used to and are now called Fuzzies). Most of the races have been removed or replaced by much blander counterparts. Instead of rough, blue-collar salt hogs, we have dumb aardvarks in boxers. Instead of the staunch and "miserable" Grekka Targ we have "Bugs" (why was it so necessary to give them such an awful, generic name. Many of the aliens are also never introduced so it feels like it doesn't matter what shows up when. In the original, there were missions for every alien race, so you understood what they wanted and how they acted. I like the moth girls and the dryads, but I don't get many of the other changes.Third: Everything just sort of happens. There is a constant flow of hundreds of aliens coming and going. Everyone makes an exact ant-line everywhere and it constantly feels like none of it matters. I couldn't even analyze if my station was doing well because there is always such a constant, endless stream of nonsense. Also, in a baffling development, you can't shut down your port or add new ones. I really don't understand this at all. In the first one, you needed lots of ports, but you could also make them exit only in case you needed to bleed out visitors. One time, in the original, I made all of my ports exit only because I had a really bad case of space plague on board and I needed to get it under control. This made it so that new people wouldn't clog the hospitals. I was losing many visitors and residents to space plague, but I also offset this by raising the cost of healthcare a lot so that someone who couldn't afford it would just leave. If they didn't die on my station, it wasn't my problem. It's unethical, but it's how I saved that playthrough. There's none of that here and in a management game you need to be able to, you know, make decisions about how your station works.Lastly: The game is very quiet. There's just not much going on. All of the rooms look the same. It's very strange that they combined the resting, eating and hygiene area into one building. This would have been fine if they had added other buildings, but they really didn't. It was hard to feel like the aliens had much identity either and it's pretty hard to care for something called "Bug". There's just a constant stream of guys that you can't stop or really influence in any manner.In Conclusion: It's nice to be able to pick up things with the pattern buffer by holding down the click to pick up a whole bunch. It's nice to see something get some attention after such a long time. However, this seems to indicate that the game will stay buried in obscurity for basically forever. It's a very samey, boring experience, with missions that are too short to really get a feel for a station before you have to move on. While some stuff looks nice, the personality has been scrubbed away almost entirely. It doesn't even matter if there were all new races if there were new jokes to be told. The bugs are cute, but I know nothing about them except that they work at the telecommunications station. The moth girls are adorable and have good energy, but they only work at disco clubs. The grays are no longer tourists that also conduct medical experiments on less-advanced species. You can no longer pet the Maumau because it doesn't exist anymore.Still, at least it's not as bad as Warcraft III: Reforged, which needlessly destroyed the original game forever, so we can thank Zedem that we can still visit a Love Nest, decorate with nice stuff and kill Space Vermin in a galaxy far, far, far away and I can drink some mucus wine to that...Also, why is there no Arona Daal?
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Devs are cashing and milking on nostalgia feeling by impersonating games like Dungeon Keeper and now they copy-cating Startopia without understanding of what made those games legends.So what do we have this time... a management game without a pause buttons, where you constantly have to click everything till you have a carpal tunnel syndrome. Lazy cashgrabbers do not grasp what a "fun" aspects of a management game are.Pros:(o) Graphics are niceCons:(o) Cookie clicker has dropped a ball comparing to this game. It is normal to make 100-150 clicks in one minute, like collecting 50 garbage, 50 times to click on plants, 50 times to pick those crate, 50 times to put all into storage or 50 times into recycling.(o) No Pause(o) Notifications are coming like a spam, you don't read and react because you don't have time to.(o) Research is locked behind totally unnecessary "achievements" like "build two pots and manually plant 2 plants into pots"(o) everything basically revolts around immense clicking
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: "...And One large Coke.""Is diet Pepsi okay?""Sure."And then you receive some unholy sewer brand version of Sprite.Startopia, originally, had a weird kind of magic, mostly stemming from the humour of the AI assistant, and the other bits and bops.This is gone.The AI is just mean now.Also, you're constantly bombarded with stuff to do that isn't fun to do.1/7, waste of money. Just play the original, it works surprisingly well on most systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Think of this as Startopia the sequel and suddenly this seems a lot less like a remake - its not.  This is a reimagining of a game and it has a lot more content than the original ever did.It doesnt quite catch the humor of the original game, though it does try to.  What it lacks in humor though it more than makes up for in scope - there is a lot to this game - many constructions on the first two decks, easy customization of the top deck and each mission as you progress takes some time.It does grow a little tedious and repetitive if you play a marathon session, but if you take it in chunks each mission brings a little extra to the game.  There ARE some bugs in this still but I found saving and reloading was enough to clear them.In summary this is a great game, but DO NOT buy at full price.  It is far too expensive.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Startopia. The jokes are not as bad as the negative reviews say. The company did a good job recreating the humor of the original Startopia, which many negative reviewers may not be familiar with. But what's bad is this: The game is really dumbed down. It's not the startopia we knew and loved. It's virtually a smartphone app level of the real thing. You build the necessary things, little skill is required, you wait, you win. Some of the things you need to click on, like garbage and vermin, are just insulting to your intelligence... This just doesn't feel like a game at all. There is zero skill involved. Zero fun in watching the aliens interact. Zero immersion.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the beta I figured maybe by the time release rolled around they'd improve some things, fix the bugs, flesh out the game a bit more. Nope. It's the EXACT SAME as the Beta. Nothing changed, nothing improved, nothing was added. For starters: the voice of the computer. Why is it a direct ripoff of Glados? Also, what's with the constant insults?!? VAL from the original would needle you once in a while, but he wouldn't constantly belittle you to the point where you scratch your head and wonder what you're doing playing this thing. Other issues: the garbage system is flat out broken, pathfinding is non-existent (I can't count how many times I had to move/remove items simply because my mech couldn't navigate somewhere), the music and sound effects often cut out for no apparent reason, and don't even get me started on the new version of the berth (why the heck they added food AND cleaning to that room is beyond me).Save your money or go buy the original, this just isn't worth your investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Just not worth it. I unfortunately pre-purchased so I could play the Beta and help provide feedback during development. A lot of the beta testers' feedback went unanswered or not incorporated in the final game due to lack of resources, time, or apathy.For a space station building simulation it lacks a lot. Even basic things like trading with traveling traders is barely in the game and not worth the effort in game.If you saw this trailer and got excited, just go buy Startopia. This is not a sequel or remake of the original muckyfoot startopia. It is a dumbed down version with better graphics.Edit after playing through half the missions so far: Still the same review. Numerous bugs and incomplete features. Very little is intuitive. Every mission basically plays the same. Missions where you need to find certain aliens or criminals is impossible without just clicking each individual alien and looking at their info screens which is cumbersome and not fun at all. If this gives you a feel for it, I started putting all of the bug and feedback into the game forum, but i am only partway through the list and can't post any more because I've made too many posts.Edit 2: more details of current issues, responses to current bugs in forum are limited and unsure if there is any progress towards fixing any of them.Research lab queuing is bugged (researching via research screen works only if you have a crate in cargo hold but doesn't tell you which ones you have, there is literally a hidden queue of research that you can't see or change, placing crates directly into research lab is buggy and sometimes doesn't work)Factory production queueing is bugged and unintuitive (not proceeding to next item, lack of player feedback with UI, can't repeat an item that is in production you have to queue up a second one and then make that one repeat)Alien behaviors are bugged (not fulfilling needs even when angry, walking through walls)Robot Worker behaviors bugged (not performing jobs next to them, idle with work to do, etc)Dryads working on bio-deck don't plant in open areas, plant in areas that are not on the approved list
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's like if you took the original Startopia, constructed of real Legos, and then tried to recreate it using those giant childproof ones so 3-year-olds don't choke.It's overly simplified, it's not as charming, and there's nothing good about it. It takes forever to make any progress and has a bunch of useless plate spinning added in to give you "something to do" that amounts to little more than frustrating busywork.If you already own the original and loved it and you're hoping for a spiritual successor, this is not what you're wanting, stay  away from this. If you haven't played the original and you're looking for a quaint little management game, you should go ahead and purchase the original as it's an infinitely better experience than what you'll find here.I would not recommend this game even on a heavy discount. $5 is too much for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Full of bugs and idiotic design decisions. Sound cuts out frequently, tool-tips don't update consistently in menus, blueprints don't save between missions, crates glitch into the floor. VAL9000 is so distracting that 99% of people just mute it. The game could be salvageable and worthwhile to play if Kalypso had any interest in fixing the issues, but they don't. They got their nostalgia cash-grab and now they've moved on.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Resounding Meh.The oiginal Startopia, where I wasted hundreds of hours from a young age into adulthood, had a gritty, absurdist and nihilistic intelligence to it, slapstick animations ahead of its time and kinky sous-entendres of a sci-fi consumerist hedonistic society of aliens, drinking and gambling and dying.The new one has none of that, unfortunately. Banal creatures and rote animations in pastel colors, visiting Cat cafés and walking out once their money is depleted, like an android app with more budget.The narrator had some funny voice clips, but yeah, it's just going to hurt your nostalgia.It has enough elements to remind you of your Startopia days, but that's just to ride the marketing train. It will disappoint you. It's not ''it''.I restarted freeplays several time here and there, and simply never got to the upper tiers, I get terribly bored.I'm sorry!
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: The original Startopia is a game I like to replay again every few years, I would recommend purchasing the original over this.The new writing for VAL is terrible. The voice that is supposed to tell you when things are happening does not, choosing spends its time trying to make the most awful drawn out jokes. This contributes a budget-knock-off feel of this game when compared to the original.The UI is worse that the original in many ways, a few examples;An example opening a crate places the unpack icon to the left of the screen, this makes opening things a nuisance, especially on an ultra-wide screen. The original placed the unpack icon where you right clicked. Combat now has a (redundant) separate UI, it's clunky and annoyingly stops all non combat functions. In the original you right clicked on things you wanted dead, more clicks = more dead priority. This new interface adds nothing.Your employees are no longer flagged. Trying to find the aliens who sure aren't manning their stations? Now you have to click though them on a list! The original just had icons above their heads.The original was by no means a perfect game, but this has none of the charm. The few things that are improvements are countered by baffling changes that make the overall experience worse. I really wanted to like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original startopia and spent 80+ hours just chilling in freeplay. I can't do that in this one because it's so poorly optimized I get performance issues before I even finish completely building up the smallest map. Frequent frame drops from interacting with the UI, beaming things up, and moving the camera. I literally have zero trust in Kalypso releasing a finished product at this point. It's sad because it really does a good job of replicating the old game. My specs are a GTX 1080, i5-8600K, and 16GB RAM.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend avoiding this game. It is not Startopia we fell in love with back in the day. Interface is clunky, with some puzzling decisions, like you can't switch decks by clicking on minimap, only by clicking exact deck button, which was super advanced technology original Startopia could do. Not to mention anything with longer list, like alien list being super unresponsive to clicks, like it has database system that is equally old as original game, except that was far more responsive. Then their attempt at allowing you to click what you will teleport out with nothing really smart about it, because often I would click on create to pick it up, but instead drop what I had in my teleporter instead, because game literally isn't smart enough to thing about it for a moment. I am pointing at create, I don't want to drop trash all over the place. It is very simple logic, unless you are Starbase Startopia, then it is thing from 2030. It requires ton more micromanagement, with it spamming ton of stuff at you at once. Narrator is straight up trying to be Glados, but with zero personality to it, it isn't offensive, neither it is fun, just boring. Also combat is super ridiculous, not using aliens you hired, but you get 4 almost useless bots in your security center, that I have yet to see survive anything they can't overwhelm with huge numbers. Or you can build mechs, for which you need grand canyon sized hole through your base, in order for them to be able to get anywhere. Making it super easy to fail first combat mission. Oh and just to make things perfect they also made them require some materials that aren't easy to get or produce, which you will in mentioned mission need on short notice. And whole system is designed with zero creativity, only thinking about how to artificially limit things to force player in challenge developer wanted. Also game does absolutely terrible job explaining anything. Sure original didn't have great combat tutorial either, but it generally did great job at teaching you the rest. And don't even get me started on mess that is biodeck, at least with original you got some create scheme, but in 2021, making some reasonable in game help to determine what you need or which plants to harvest to get something, or maybe even AI that would help you with, oh, we are producing something that requires X, lets prioritize harvesting X. Nope, lets just throw player in the water and let them figure out swiming like it is 90s or something. So all I will say is, just buy original Staropia and take more relaxing experience. I just can't say I had much fun with this game. Yes, I only clocked in 8h, but I saw enough to know that issues won't change and neither it looks like game will get any updates fixing them.P.S. Also game is still buggy too. When switching decks, audio will randomly cut off and after 5-10min of playing also randomly decide to return. And this is the only game where I got this issue and regardless, I did make sure drivers are up to date, checked all the settings to ensure it was set properly to my headphones, even tried disabling audio over HDMI, just in case, so it wouldn't get multiple choices to somehow confuse.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, even if it's on sale, I would say don't get this game unless they put in a fast forward option. There's nothing entertaining about staring at my phone for ten minutes while I wait for an objective to finish. Also, the aliens walk slowly, so it's a case of hurry up and wait. If they add in that feature, I'll change my review to passable. This is very much a game that you can play while doing something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't Startopia. The Devs tried, they did. But you're just playing Bin Man Simulator with a heavy hint of verbally abusive AI.Unlike VAL of the original, the VAL in this game lacks any humour, it is simply a constant stream of snide remarks that don't come across as humorous but more condescending and tactless. The Voice Actors should of studied the original VAL, as should the writers.Gameplay wise it gets super repetitive after a while. Even more than the original Startopia. Buildings deteriorate at a shocking pace, and the need to build energy transmitters on the Fun Deck makes planning it out a chore.Fuzzies (This games silly name for Scuzzers) aren't very intelligent. You cant set their priorities like you could in the old game so what they do is up to them and they don't always prioritise things in a logical manner. Leading to a lot of spoiled goods, broken buildings and uncollected waste.Visitors and Staff don't use the bins either, and trash accumulates at an unusually high rate, meaning you'll be frequently doing a clean up of your station every 5-10 minuets. Which gets worse as you take over more sectors.Staff AI isn't very Intelligent either. They won't get treated for their sickness until the very last moment, at which point the station is in its own pandemic, everyones angry and you start wishing you could open the airlocks and blow them all out into space. There isn't any proper way to manage work shifts either, so buildings are staffed whenever staff remember they have a job. Meaning you'll often hire more staff than you need to be sure you'll have something working.The Devs really did try, I can't fault them there. But their understanding on what made the original game so unique and beloved is clearly lacking. The Dark humour, the sarcasm etc that was so heavily influenced by Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy, Red Dwarf etc is non-existent here and that gives this game very little soul.Giving your races quirky information is not the same, here it comes across as shallow and silly for the sake of being silly, and only works to belittle the game this one seeks to reimagine, remake and give new life to. And also only serves to make this game less enjoyable.Edit:I should also note that this game is still quite buggy and really should still be considered early access.Quite often you'll get the sense this game is unfinished, features feel unpolished, the build menu feels a little empty.Over all I'd say give this a miss for now, and come back in 6 months. But don't hold your breath. The Devs have a lot of work ahead of themselves to give this game some life back. That includes giving it that Red Dwarf or Hitchhikers feel. Some Sirens. Love Nests and Shops, Decor etc. Especially since the Fun Deck and Sub Deck just feel a little bland. The Fun Deck feels like a cheap amusement park and the Sub Deck a little meh.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I Played the original when it first came out, thought it was too short.Negative reviews are exaggerated . I waited  20 years for this sequel and its really not bad at all.The gameplay is true to the original, with a few gameplay mechanics added.The graphics are perfectly fitting for this style of game.Some of the main complaints seem to be about how the game doesnt add much over the original. That may be true, but the original promised me a sequel and 20 years later this is what we got. I'm just hoping that the slew of negative reviews doesn't send a message to the developer, encouraging them NOT to continue adding to this new incarnation of startopia.I really would like to see what kind of new content they would be able to add to this formula, and nobody is going to be improving the original, so lets give them a chance to release some more content for this version. It was tragic that we had to wait this long for more startopia, lets not try to make that forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the original I have to say this is a downgrade, which is a real shame.the main AI voice companion is little better than a text to speech bot in 3 different flavour, each of which is equally annoying.the campaign is actually somewhat challenging but none of the missions last long enough to really let you feel the length and depth of the full game and unlock all the tiers of building (but there is Skirmish for that being fair)the alien AI annoys me the most how ever, especially the need for sickbays, aliens will complain endlessly about being ill, but won't go to the sickbay even if there's plenty of spaces available in it and can end up dying, and worse still can make other aliens ill, which yeah, cool, realism, but it is an annoying gameplay feature as it makes natural bottlenecks like the lifts between levels hotspots, the same sort of thing can be said for most of the needs minus the epidemic.it's also quite telling how successfull this game isn't because when trying to google things like how rooms work or if doing X thing to room helps with Y need there's next to no info online, very little discussion and so on.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's really well-made and faithful successor of Startopia... Until mid-late game.The Campaign is short and shallow, although funny enough to be entertaining.No problem, just play sandbox mode! Sandbox mode was awesome in Startopia!Plus the modern UI and QoL makes it so much easier to do what you want to without excessive amounts of clicking!(One of the biggest advantages of a remake IMO)But then you start running into bugs, can't take over enemy AI sectors because your Giant mech gets stuck between buildings, and when you tell your aliens to attack the sector they don't move there. Things basically don't work like they should so you get soft-locked.If you want an awesome experience just replay the beginning of a sandbox over and over and everything will be perfect 😂It has a lot of potential but the devs have basically made a hollow, modernised remake of a cult classic and haven't bothered to fix age old bugs or issues the community has.Another nostalgia-bait game which would be AMAZING if it actually got the support it deserves.Stick with the original to avoid having your heart broken.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Feels Soulless.I loved the original Startopia, it really hit the vibe of a different type of Dungeon Keeper or Theme Hospital style game. It had a lot of heart, goofy british humor, and really fun scenarios.Space Base: Startopia checks all the boxes but misses the heart of it. The tutorial basically takes you through all the scenarios of the original, but doesn't really teach you the game. The sound design is lacking which I think is what breaks the immersion. The original Startopia had sound effects for almost anything going on, the larger your station got, the more hectic it sounded. The background ambient of a station droned on and it really sucked me in. Going to the terraforming deck was a peaceful experience that felt different from the other decks. Not so much with this version. It just feels like it drags on and I'm watching numbers tick up, there doesn't seem to have the same personality and charm, the camera feels worse than the original, and while checking all the boxes to have the same features, it's 2021, a lot has changed in these games and could have been done so much better. The art direction is adequate and the graphics are okay, but even the lighting lacks any character. It's an adequate game to bring what was around in 2001 to 2021, but honestly I'd probably just enjoy going back to the original more.

_childDocuments_.review: played way too much of the dungeons series, owning every story dlc, and thought "wow they remade one of their old games that people loved". i am very dissapointed and here is why:tutorials are thrash, the asisstent is making ONLY insulting remarks - constantly(wich gets more annoying than it is boring in a longer gaming session), the camera can get stuck in a building if it is big enough so you have to "wiggle" around, ESC opens the main menue instead of making your selection go away, you have to right click something to select it.....RIGHT click, usefullness of the description is rather left wanting and the mission themselfs are boring because it always involves picking up a bomb before it explodes.half of these can be patched, but the missions need a remake to be enjoyable and the AI remarks need new recordings. i haven´t played all of the missions but 4 out of 10 is nearly half.wait for a sale
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this but I really, really, can't.Startopia, the first one, wasn't anything but a barely above average game. It had a few good ideas : 3 decks which all have an unique function, some combat, some trading... Somehow, the devs here managed to copy this part, but make everything else work badly.There is no pause.There is no balance.There is little to no pathfinding.The tutorial is amazingly bad.There isn't an easy way to know if you're gaining (or losing) energy (money).Campaign is the "same" as the bad campaign of the first game, a collection of freeplay that ends before the endgame where your goal is to reach the highest level of research available... which raises at each map.Writing is... bad. Like. Really awful. Basically the only thing you "interact" with during the whole campaign basically just insults you all game long. For no reason.Every action you need to make requires 3-10 clicks. For no reasons. Research requires you to build 3 to 5 times the same building, remember what you did, and then click on research. Why ? I don't know.There is no easy way to know if your fuzzies (workers) are overworked.Combat... sigh. It was bad in the first game. Still is. Most outrageous things I saw is that when attacking a sector, moving back to the sector you're attacking from makes you immune to enemy attacks. However you can still attack them. The "last" sector to conquer is the enemy core. Enemy workers can repair the enemy core back to full in a dozen seconds. Basically you need to watch out for them else it's impossible to end the game.Pathfinding is bad. Mechs in particular keep getting stuck.I don't know what to say.Making a good game, one that'll last forever, is indeed complicated. Making an average one that cashes on nostalgia ?... that isn't complicated. That's all that was needed there. Somehow they failed.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, despite the reviews. I just couldn't.Nostalgia goggles aside, everything about this game screams "half-baked". The UI looks like a 30-minute Photoshop job. The AI assistant you'll be talking to uses a generic text-to-speech voice that gets annoying within the first five minutes. Everything's so fast-paced that the game ends up playing like a soulless click-clickity-click-fest. There are some interesting details, but there's no time to enjoy them or just... chill for a bit.tl;dr: This game has no business calling itself Startopia. It has none of the things that made the original great. The price tag is just insult to injury.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Save your money.This is not a fun game, Marked as full release this feels very much like early access.With missing features such as statistics panels, Basic time controls, And having a decent amount of bugs and a campaign that failed to keep me entertained after the 5th mission as it feels like it is just an extended tutorial.Audio glitches and complete lack of audio after reloading a save at times.Horrible very repetitive dialog, I started a free play game and within 10 minutes heard the same line repeated 3 times.. Very annoying.Laggy menus and lacking an option to adjust scroll speed in the menu.When ever i open the visitor menu and switch between tabs there is always a momentary lag spike, And using the mouse wheal to scroll down the list is so slow, Then there is the duplication glitch on auto save, Where if you have the factory open and the game saves, All the icons get duplicated, Very annoying.Then there is what i consider one of if not the most annoying part to the game.. The vermin.If i didnt have to manual exterminate these pests it wouldn't be so annoying, But if you leave a deck unattended for a while garbage will start to pile up, Doesn't matter how many garbage cans you have, Then the vermin come and you can have a massive infestation on your hands.You will have to site there and click on them one by one to get rid of them.There is a item you can craft to make it a bit easier, But it has a VERY small AOE and the game doesnt even tell you about this item.NPC's from what i can tell dont bother using the garbage cans you provide no matter how close there are, They will just leave it on the ground insuring you always have a garbage and pest problem, Then there is the bio deck, You cant even place garbage bin on that deck, I opened up 9 out of 20 section on the bio deck, Cane back an hour later to hundreds of vermin and trash everywhere.This game is not well thought out and a real disappointment, Not at all worth 57 bucks, And the devs should be ashamed of themselves for making this pile of garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Review: while the art direction is solid and it faithfully recreates the bones of what made Startopia great, it just doesn't do anything new or innovative with the concept, and like all Realmforge titles, the pacing is extremely slow without giving you enough to do to keep things interesting.Pros:-Fun, colorful, art and animations-Really really wants to do Startopia justice.Cons:-Sluggish UI-Terrible pacing-Audio fades in and out at random.-Combat is clunky and boring-Realmforge's humor is still tired and flat.I was pretty excited for this release, as someone who spend an embarrassing amount of time on the original Startopia. I don't typically play in betas so I went into this fresh. I enjoyed Realmforge's Dungeons titles, with some criticisms, and I was hoping that they'd learned some lessons to apply to Spacebase Startopia.It's obvious that the developers have a lot of love for the original. The art design is great, the aliens are colorful and expressive, and the fact that aliens of the same species come in different colors and outfits does a whole lot to make the station feel alive. The kitsch-y neon sci-fi aesthetic of the station and the buildings work well, and everything is immediately recognizable for what it is (with the possible exception of the recycler and factory).The good design doesn't extend to the UI, however. It's sluggish, and frequently obtuse. I can't tell you the number of times I've been building a room and accidentally cancelled it because I didn't press 'confirm' when clicking a popup. There is no energy-flow screen, so it's impossible to find out just where your energy is coming from or going, and often your energy will drop suddenly due to an inspector or other event, and you won't even know why until you click on the notification minutes later. On the Bio Deck, certain biomes might be grayed out, with no explanation as to why.Picking up items is easy enough, but dropping them is wonky as well. Instead of right-clicking to drop, you have to select an item from the buffer to drop, but once you finish dropping items of a given type, it moves to the next item, frequently leading you to drop items accidentally. You also cannot open crates directly from the buffer or the cargo bay. It's not terrible, but over time it makes doing things feel just a tad to laborious. Terraforming on the Biodeck is also finicky, with water being invisible if it touches a bulkhead at all.One problem Realmforge has always had with its games is the pacing. This was a gripe in Dungeons for me, and it's a gripe here, too. I am not opposed to leisurely pacing in games. The original Startopia did it as well. However, if gathering energy to build new rooms and progression through the tech tree is going to be so slow there needs to be enough to do to keep the player interested, and there just isn't.  The trading port is unlocked late, so manufacturing goods is pointless, and plants grow so slowly that it's a chore anyway. I cannot for the life of me fathom why they would give you the factory before giving you a way to profit off of it. In every scenario I played with a Factory available, it spend 90% of the game idle. Not to mention that building new Fuzzers and advanced goods costs precious energy that you need to save for rooms anyway. Micromanaging room settings and prices is also gone. At the same time, alien needs and population expand very quickly, leading to long queue times as you wait for the energy to expand your facilities. The bottleneck at the elevators between decks always looks like a violent mob with the rage indicators overhead as aliens wait to get to the Disco. Opening new sections on the Fun Deck is cost-prohibitive early on, so at best one can add a single extra elevator next to the first. So far, of my 5 hours playing this game (and finishing half the campaign plus some free play), half of that time has been spent picking up trash while waiting for the funds to build the next thing required to advance my research (the ridiculously expensive security station). The one new thing they've added from the old, the mechs, haven't come into play at all, and I honestly am not sure why they would choose that to add to a station management sim. WIth this pacing, the game could really have done with some customizability and optimization tools for us to fiddle, or ways to interact with the station visitors and residents while waiting for the various subsystems like trade and research to come into play. Let us schedule shifts for our employees, increase or decrease prices for services, cap the visitor count to prevent overcrowding, build rooms that aren't squares jam-packed with as many stations as possible.Or else just speed the pace up a bit.Aside from all that, the only other complaint I have is the persistent audio issues. The music fades in and out at random, as well as VAL's voice. In one case, the sound stopped entirely for several minutes, only to return all at once, with several of VALs lines playing simultaneously. I can't even adequately critique the sound track because of it. I also ran into one UI but where after looking at an alien's detail menu, the keyboard controls and camera button on the mouse locked up entirely, requiring me to close the game and restart it. As far as release bugs go, not egregious by the standards of the day, but annoying nonetheless.In the end, I'm not sure I can recommend this game based on my experience. The terrific art design can't make up for the fact that RF hasn't quite learned what makes for engaging management sim gameplay. Or how not to run a mediocre joke into the ground.  If, through patches, they shuffle the tech progression, pacing, give the player more granular control over the station, and add more interactivity, they'll possibly end up with a worthy successor to Startopia. As it is now, it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not finished. Kalypso may think it is, but that is because they didn't QA test it at all. There are so many issues, such as scuzzers not being able to fight, and your employees seem to also be against it. But guess what is something you need to do! Kill enemies! This means you have to get your tech tree really high and research security stations and wait for them to give you police bots, and guess what. They're not very good! You also need a damn transporter to move them about floors, what?!As with the original, you can hire a single, yes SINGLE, species to help with the biodeck. They get annoyed over the smallest thing, so you're constantly losing them unless your starbase is the cleanest smoothest working thing ever, even at the start. Garbage also builds up stupidly often, and its now impossible(ish) to entirely get rid of it. They added far more micromanagement stuff without thought over the original. Your air? Can now get bad and you need to freshen it with lots of bought O2 boxes or produced on the biodeck. You also can promote your staff which does... things? It's not immediately obvious and i noticed no difference, it seems to cheer them up if they're feeling sad, which is often, but RIP energy/money.They tried to give the commentator and VAL the same level of humor as the original. However I can only assume they fed the old lines into a bad AI and it generated other 'fun' or 'comedy' things, badly.Pathfinding is bad, aliens often find their way around with only minor messups, but your scuzzers and big fighting mechs seem to think they can walk through walls and get stuck all the time.tldr: Bad game that is just nostalgia bait, go to Steam Shop or even GOG and buy the original. It's way more fun, actually works, and more importantly the developers cared, this is just a pump & dump game by Kalypso, which they're getting very good at doing from their previous games too. I hope in time we get a proper spiritual successor rather than this ridiculous expensive game that feels like a beta that got released as gold.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR if you are looking for your nostalgia fix this aint the game for you chief. But it is a good game especially if you haven't played the original.Being a reboot(?) of the original Startopia i will be making comparisons to that game. let me say that if i had to choose recommend that game over this one simply because the original has more character. That being said effort has been put in here and its not just a blatant cash grab so it has that going for it.Gameplay wise it plays much the same as the original game you start with one segment on each of the three decks on the station Maintenance, Entertainment and bio each deck has different things you can build (or teraform in the case of the bio deck) that allow you to keep your visitors and employees happy. Each race has a job they can perform for you as an employee, one race specialises in Medical stuff, another does the Garbage recycling etc. so you want to have a number of different races on hire to keep everything running smoothly. these aliens-when on staff-can level up and perform better as a result. each campaign mission has you do something different. From recycling a certain amount of energy, to healing a certain number of sick aliens to rehabilitating a certain number of criminals...The issue i have is these missions are carbon copies of the original game. The campaign does feel a bit lazy so far as a result and in the (at the time of this writing) 2 hours ive played i haven't seen any variation and its been almost identical level to level (with the ability to buy more segments in this game than the original)the main gameplay difference ive found so far is research, in the original, you would build a laboratory you would hire some Turrakens to work in it and you would drop crates of resources, buildings or droids in and they would research the next thing down the tech tree based on what item you put in the lab and then if you put an already researched item in the lab they would improve that item. In this game you have a menu, in this menu you have a number of options for research that you have to complete a prerequisite task, so for cargo holds you have to produce 5 resources, for a factory you have to store 5 things in a cargo bay, to unlock the tourism stuff you have to own one cafe etc. I Feel the old way was more interesting but this new one does have its merits as you can see what you want to unlock and how to unlock itA Definite downgrade from the original game is the Character the original had. Your AI assistant in the original would spout amusing anecdotes from time to time which so far appear to be missing. and Arona Dhall would ocasionally pop in to sell you some of his "Quality goods" that "Fell off the back of a trolley" neither makes a return. In this and for your AI assistant in this one you can choose from 3 voices one sounds like EVA from command and conquer, one sounds like GLADOS from portal or the other sounds like "we needed a male voice to balance things out lets just make Generic Male AI no 1". I picked "GLADOS" and the sass is entertaing but after a while it does feel a bit out of place due to the Cutesy art style which leads me to a gripe of mine. In the original Game i could picture all but one of the races doing the jobs they did (seriously the insects only do Comms work? they just didn't look very suited to the job to me) in this one i would say only one seems to make sense in their job (Dryad farmers) the worst offender is the security aliens...they are chubby,fluffy,almost always smiling and not very intimidating at all, one cutscene even shows them dancing in waterfalls on their home planet like some sort of cat thats enjoying a massage. the original had 8 foot tall, muscle born aliens with Red carapace for skin and stern expressions now THEY were who i would want for my security. there is one change i did appreciate though and that was the addition of uniforms, it used to be that your employees would have your faction symbol over them now they wear uniform clothing, which is a subtle but more immersive approach and one that i actually prefer over the original game (although having the option to have the faction icon might be nice, but i didn't go looking for it)I am also pleased that the soundtrack does seem to have taken a few cues from the original. The only track that seems to be missing a spiritual successor is the entertainment deck, but i think i know why they didnt put that in considering the cutesy art style, it might also might be the reason for the absence of the Siren race from the original. but all in all not a huge loss
