_childDocuments_.review: It has some issues but it's not nearly as bad as some people are making it out to be. tl:dr at the endHalf of the issues people seem to have seems to me that they did not understand or are aware of game mechanics that are already there. This seems to be confirmed by the little total gametime of the reviewers. One might argue that if so many people didn't understand the mechanics then there is still an issue with the game, and that might be true, but one thing I don't think people get is that the 'tutorial' just teaches you the very basics, but the campaign itself is basically a tutorial too to prepare you for sandbox mode. Each chapter goes into detail on one feature, teaching you how that works, and then moving to a new one. I will make some examples of issues people highlighted in the reviews which make little sense to me:- Inhabitants complain that rooms aren't there when they are. They don't. If they do, it's because the room is closed as there are no workers in it. When you go check the workers might be there, but that's because they got back in the meanwhile. This is frustrating at the start, but I think it's actually the result of good simulation: Your workers only go back to work when they satisfied their needs, if the rooms they go to to do that are far away, or have massive queues, or also don't have workers it takes them longer to do so and get back to work. It's a cascade effect, where if one room doesn't work properly it can slow down everything else as a result. You can either hire more workers (and no, double the workers for number of shifts isn't enough: are you expecting these things to work 12 hours a day, you slavedriver?)- You can't buy more workers / other things whenever you want but have to wait for the rng shop. Yeah, you can't. Thing is, you aren't meant to use the shop as the primary way to obtain things. You are meant to build them in the factory. You can build anything you need in it as long as you have the resources (aka, a lot of dryads employees harvesting them for you and fuzzies going to pick them up and putting them in storage or you can periodically make a sweep and pick them up and deposit them yourself)- There's trash everywhere even though I put trashcans everywhere! You still need fuzzies to pick up the trash and drop it in the trashcan (so if they are busy doing other things they won't, you can assign some fuzzies to trash duty only too, but mine kept reverting back to automatic, probably a bug they'll hopefully resolve). Also, have you ever seen any place with a lot of people in it that hasn't trash everywhere? I like that when put into the role of an administrator I also have to deal with people (or aliens in this case) being dirty animals. Now moving to the actual issues (the other half):- The AI assistant is extremely annoying. People complained about the voice sounding about text to speech and about it trying to be some sort of GLADos rudeness but failing to be funny. I don't mind the text to speech, it's an AI, makes all the sense it'd sound like a robot. But it is just not funny. It keeps blabbing on and on about what bad job you are doing which, fair enough I guess, but then makes absolutely moronic examples and comparisons. 'I'd remove all the organics from the base, it'd give more energy and organics are so inefficient' oh, so you would remove organics from the project specifically designed to make the organics meet and reach agreements? That's literally the opposite of your job, and I'm the one doing it badly?- The menus being clunky and hard to navigate, and the UI being pretty bad in general. This is the biggest issue the game has, and probably the one from which misunderstanding about the game mechanics comes from. Too many clunky menus, a separate UI for the combat (why? there's three commands for the combat units in total), having some key information straight missing (like the energy breakdown. As far as I found there's no way to see what your ins and outs of energy are. You might have some massive wasters you can't address because you are unaware of them).- Lack of pause. I think this is an intended gameplay choice, I wouldn't mind it much if it didn't make it almost impossible to design rooms without the base going bonkers while you are busy doing that. I think designing rooms in single player should pause the game.- Combat is bad. Besides the nonsensical separate UI for combat, mentioned above, the combat is just lame. You get the unit, click on the enemy, that's it. Another thing people complained about was the Mechs needing two empty tiles to move around the base. I don't actually mind that one, it makes me design bases with wide avenues in the middle with decorations  and plants on the side which give the base a more organic look than a bunch of rooms all cramped together.- Camera lags sometimestl:dr The game is more like a rough gem than awful, like some people are putting it. Half the issues you see in the review aren't actually there, but some key ones are, which are: Bad UI and menus, annoying AI assistant, lame combat. If those three are a deal-breaker don't play it, otherwise give it a chance and play the tutorials and the campaign (basically an extra long tutorial) to learn the game before going into sandbox.

_childDocuments_.review: Until the last level, I would have considered this a "meh," but then the last level is such a deliberately terrible experience that it changed my mind to bad.  I loved the original Startopia.  I played it for hundreds of hours.  This is so much blander and worse.  The aliens are totally mute.  No cute little noises and voicelines like before.  Aliens all feel so samey.  I couldn't tell you a single thing one alien race prefers over another, if anything.  There's no charm.  The Eu'reka and the Bugs have cool designs, but everyone else is just boring.  Even now, I can tell you what the Sirens' or the Karmaramas' personality was.  Here?  I just played 32 hours of this game and I couldn't tell you what the Bugs like.  Researching new buildings is annoying.  You need so many visitors to be happy to unlock anything, and then you spend those points.  It can take forever just to get to security centers and jails.  So then what does your research center do?  It improves things, using buildings in crates.  Which means buildings have to be cheap to allow for you to research them five or six times, so producing buildings in your factory is ludicrously cheap, so buying and selling them to traders is also cheap, so trade is no longer useful or interesting, since the buildings you buy get researched instead of sold.  It also adds so many extra "utilities."  Bad air's now a thing, because buildings designed to be used on an enclosed space station just exhaust right into the air, so you need buildings to clear the air.  The fun deck isn't actually wired for electricity, so you need generators to power new sections.  The elevators are no longer instant, so you need lots of those to avoid long lines.  It's like they saw playtesters having too much room, money, and fun and decided they had to put a stop to that.I literally don't even know what the aliens are doing half the time.  You can hire 6 aliens and have no one working.  But then my fun deck is also mostly unused.  Casinos, sushi restaurants, cat cafes, arcades, they're all going unused.  So why is no one working?  I ended up hiring a dozen aliens just to ensure someone was working at all times.Combat's slow and terrible.  Do you have more mechs than the enemy?  You win.  Do you have fewer?  You lose.  That's it.  Not once did a battle turn out any other way.  No more employees fighting or contributing in any way.  No more taking over sections with Scuzzers.  You just blow up buildings until you win, or, to take over their main section, you spend 10 minutes shooting their energy core, even when they have nothing that can stop you.  Plus, you have to constantly send drones back, because whereas Memaus planting chestbursters was rare and avoidable in the original, here, everyone just gets facehugged, so you have constant people dying to chest parasites.  I could go on, but this is already a screed.There are some QoL improvements.  It's easier to hire, fire, and promote aliens.  It's easier to teleport goods.  Some of the new buildings are cute.  I like that it has premade templates, which apparently the AI doesn't use, so if you take over sections, it's still full of terribly designed monstrosities, just like in the original.  That's it.  It feels like someone described the original Startopia to someone who then tried to recreate it with better graphics.  So much is blatantly copied that they obviously were aware of the original, but so many things are worse that it doesn't feel like they played it, or if they did, they didn't enjoy it.TLDR;  It's bland, boring, and full of terrible design decisions.  It could just be blandly inoffensive, but the final level make it actively offensive.  Try it if you get it for free or in a bundle with better games.  Otherwise, avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially looking forward to this game when it was announced in 2019, a spiritual successor to the legendary sci-fi management game by MuckyFoot in 2001.It skipped my mind when it released in 2021 due to other things going on in my life and now I decided to try and play it despite the mixed reviews and let's just say I should've thought something was up and it's readily apparent now. This game has terrible optimization issues where the whole game chugs trying to access your employee menu. The AI pathing is exceptionally bad and nobody seems to seek out the Sick Bay when needed. VAL is especially annoying as they're nothing like the snarky but by-your-side inorganic of the original with a grating text-to-speech voice.And good LORD the ending is such a copout whereas the original you were actually helping to make the galaxy better in the wake of intergalactic warfare and VAL even offers to toast with a bottle of champagne, I couldn't stand getting that far because while I could work through the slow process of building up my army in the penultimate mission, I couldn't stand the massive amount of chugging caused by navigating the menus.I don't like the additions of more needs for the aliens which means more things the game needs to keep track of and leads to an even greater strain when you're dealing with hundreds of visitors and Unity is *not* the kind of engine for agent-based sim gameplay as we've seen with both Cities: Skylines games. (For an example of a well-optimized game, see the first two RollerCoaster Tycoon games which are programmed in x86 Assembler with a bit of C++ to run on Windows, those games will run decent even on an old ThinkPad)Oxygen management is just another hassle. Having to build the lifts between floors rather than two coming with each segment.Energy distributors on the Fun Deck which replaces the more subtle Power Rating that limits your spending ability.Worse still is the complete lack of planning for any mod support at all which would've helped by, say, bringing back the feel of the original or even a total conversion mod of the original but nothing of that sort was planned or even considered.What are some of the things I *do* like about this game? Well some of the neat shortcuts for performing functions such as the item vacuum and the ability to instantly unpack with Shift+R.Research improves the performance of facilities rather than just simply making them cheaper to produce.A lot of actions can be performed more directly rather than the original's play-by-feel with the lack of numbers.Dryads can passively harvest from plants on the Bio-Deck without destroying them but you can harvest them directly if you need resources urgently.I'm not angry at this game, I'm just plain disappointed at the wasted potential of a sequel or successor to one of the defining games of my childhood

_childDocuments_.review: I am quite disappointed about this game... considering the cost of it and technically being a remake I would have expected a bit more to begin with (or a cheaper product).If you're an old Startopia player...  the controls will absolutely confuse you. Simple stuff like "everything's done with right-click" - why?! It makes no sense. Clicking on an alien should be at least done with left-click, building stuff with right-click. Simple controls, why is everything on right-click. The left mouse button has no immediate use... makes no sense to me.Flying with the camera makes no sense, when using WASD the camera stays in the same height/position and moves around. As soon as you click the middle mouse button to see where you are going, the height baiscally changes and you fly to the point (down to the floor) that you are looking at. That again makes no sense to me. If I wanna fly and look around, I basically have to decide... either I look around and move the camera knowing i fly on the ground, have to look up again to fly up to then continue looking around. Or... I move with WASD only but then can't look around the station. Who the heck came up with that?One of the most "delightful" parts of the old game was the AI talking in the background, coming up with random facts and stories and sometimes being a bit smart-pantsy... the new AI is just a condescending annoying [enter word here]. I have no idea, why someone would think that AI is in any way funny whilst through the whole game play (and I haven't even played that much yet) it's just talking you down, how is that supposed to keep you entertained?Some of the essential game mechanics are also completely changed. Why does the berth have food AND cleaning in the same building? The berth was originally just sleeping quarters and you could move the foods elsewhere, forcing your aliens to discover the station. Now everything is just inside the berth. What'S the point? Apart from the fact that the berth is now constantly overrun because EVERYONE tries to get into it, whilst before the lavatory and the food station were elsewhere and the sleeping quarters too... so 3x as many aliens now try to get into the berth with an endless queue unless you build a huge amount of berths.The graphics are cute, I find some parts are just too interactive - don'T get me wrong, i don't mind the atmosphere cleanser to move and wiggle and blow clouds, but not EVERYTHING in that station has to move and wiggle and blink... even the doors of the lift keep wiggling... a bit much?!The factory is a bit confusing, but that might just be me being too used to other systems. I just find the interface a bit illogical, though the original's Startopia factory interface wasn't much better to be fair.I like the fact that "hired" aliens now where the stations uniform. That's a small little feature I quite enjoy. As silly as it may sound.I will update this review over time, but so far, I am not impressed. In German there is a word "verschlimmbessern" which roughly translates into worse-bettern... meaning... someone tried to improve the game play but actually broke it or made it worse. The new aliens are cute, but why did they have to change, what was wrong with the old ones? Focus should have been elsewhere...
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't exactly scratch the same itches as the original Startopia. It just kinda scratches around the sweet spots.VAL is now voiced by Text-to-speech, is a little more demeaning, and is basically a weird mix of GLaDOS and the Original Startopia VAL.Building rooms and stuff kinda feel empty and lacking. Not much better gear put into 'em. You'll probably be using the blueprints a lot(Which is a neat feature).Combat System has changed though. You now use Drones and Mechas for battle. A pretty neat upgrade to the original's Employee VS Employee shootouts IMO.Overall, it's a different flavored Startopia that has it's charms. Not a sequel, but a side grade with different content and modernized graphics.Have fun, Command-Rs. ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This game has big shoes to fill. And it does that moderately well. Gameplay does feel like Startopia. Graphics is good. And all in all it's not a bad game.But there are issues. Many people mention the bad voice acting. Well it's not really voice acting, since it feels like an AI reading stuff. But that's not necessarily bad since the only voice you hear is supposed to be a cold hearted AI. I don't even mind the fun making an insulting jokes made about carbon-based life form's inefficiency. What a I would complain about is the humor and general writing of the voice acting. It's fine when the voice throws in an insult about non-artificial lifeforms now and again. But there is almost nothing else. Almost always the same punchline to everything. And that gets old and boring real quick. It's like someone keeps making the same your-mom-jokes every second sentence. Not very creative. On this topic the old Startopia is lightyears ahead of this one with Arona and the old VAL.Gameplaywise it's solid Startopia. I'd like some more chart and statistics. It feels like there wasn't much effort put in to make notable improvements though. It's pretty much a refurbished Startopia with a different combat system (although I personally don't care much about combat in Startopia) and worse voice acting/humor.So if you want a refurbished Startopia with better graphics and similar gameplay and don't care that much about the humor and voice acting aspect. Go ahead and buy it.I personally hope that they keep working on this game, listen to suggestions and improve it. It is in no way bad as many reviewers make it out to be. It just has lots of room for improvement.Right now I would only pick it up if it was like half price or so on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original and enjoyed it. While I didn't spend hundreds of hours on the original, but I did spend more than 30. However, something about this remake just feels... off. It is definitely missing some "je ne sais quoi".Maybe it's the "trying to be GlaDOS snark, but is actually just boringly mean" dialog. Maybe it's how the campaign feels "slow" or "too hand-holdie" after suggesting the tutorial that was, also, slow. Maybe it's the fact that all the aliens aren't as visually unique or striking as they were in the original. But something is "off" about this one and just isn't worth my time -- even when I got the game as part of a humble bundle for $15 with a ton of other content to sweeten the value.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I ticked "yes" because the game works... But note that its not a perfect game. If you bought the original game, congrats, you bought this game. The aliens are more or less the same but their appearances and name was changed, there was no reason to do that. Strange is that one of the dialogues actually mentions the "Grey" aliens from the original. It felt like they intended to add some or all of the original aliens, but either because of licensing issues, a bright idea or just a cheap way of adding more races, they didn't. Anyway, since it plays the same as the original it acts as a modern version, but its still got some issues from the original. So it feels a bit... Lazy? _childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I have hundreds of hours in the original "Startopia" from when I was a kid and my dad bought me the original game from a charity shop. So I'm a big fan of the original game and was hoping this would largely be a re-texturing of the original game.I spent all of 8 minutes in a sandbox level and decided that I had seen enough. My major gripes:* The camera controls are utterly terrible.* It feels like the game needs a way higher FOV.* Some of the alien races have been completely changed (security race, the angel race, the religious race).* All of the races have been somewhat renamed.* Various core buildings have been removed.* Scuzzers are replaced with fuzzies (I can't overstate my disgust).* The fuzzies have 0 character, unlike the scuzzers who had such original movement and animations.* The bio deck looks really weird, I can't describe it.I have requested a refund, and will likely just buy the original (and clearly best) version of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia is a playful attempt as a spiritual successor to Startopia. I did purchase the game the moment it was available on Steam and was able to see the 'pre-alpha' (or whatever it is called). There are several similar elements to its predecessor, but this game lacks many fundamental game elements that really made the older game 'sing'. Cons: - it's far too easy to lose, with the removal of Arona Daal. Without a fresh supply of trade, the game gets very difficult. - Research is completely restructured and now is not as critical of a process - No Security Scuzzers without a Security Station which takes up a LOT of room. This means if you don't land grab quickly, you can 'die on the vine' without having a military. That and Mechs need a LOT of room to move. - The UI is very dodgy. I either have to click multiple times to get an order issued, or I have to close out of the menu I'm in completely for it to register. - Research is very buggy. I have to 'deconstruct' and 'reconstruct my Research Station every few researches as it seems to get stuck. - The game has no soul. Startopia had custom 'voices' and personalities for each alien type. Here, I just can't give a care who has what problems.Maybe I'll revisit this game some other time, but this feels very unpolished. TBH, it makes me want to load up Startopia instead of playing this version anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike most, I didn't play the original Startopia when I was younger, so I'm not bringing that to the table here. From a purely objective view as a fan of management-type games, I'm not at all satisfied with playing this game.Firstly, I agree with a lot of others when it comes to the notifications. There are way too many. I should never be yelling at a bunch of lines of code to shut up, but there wasn't a consecutive 3-minute span of time where I didn't literally get mad at this game's inability to shut up.I didn't complete the campaign. It was alright for some time, but the mission "Thunderdome" if I remember right, has you amass a 400,000 credits as its initial goal. Okay! No problem and I soundly beat the computer opponent to it...but wait! Now I need to defend my sectors and take over one of his...alright let me just build up and WHOA!? Here come not one, not two but four, FOUR, (4) mechs, plus a butt-ton of security drones. Meanwhile, I can barely build new ones because I can't get the medicine needed to make holo crystals to make more mechs. No plants in my Bio deck are dropping meds and no traders are selling them. Great game!I tried free play but without opponents there's really no challenge. I put on opponents and turned on the setting so that, instead of mech combat to take sectors you have a bidding war with your opponent, but it was taking stupid amounts of money to expand since the bids only go up in 10000 credit increments. Regardless, I got pissed off anyway because, for some reason, my security drones were refusing to fight the pirates that the game decided to not tell me were assaulting me. Or the multiple chest-bursters that were spawning every thirty seconds. Literally, they just wouldn't follow my commands. Great game!In brief, I just was not having fun, to such a degree, in fact, that I just don't believe someone could have possibly played this and said "Yeah! This a product we should release." Go somewhere else for your entertainment. This was painfully frustrating at worst and merely "okay" at even the best moments. Don't fart away your money on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: You only launch once. Players only remember the release, not the fixes that came later.Starbase Startopia could have waited a bit.This game is an execution in failure; not by design nor concept, but by numerous bugs and balance issues. It is clear Realmforge Studios rushed a project they barely tested and might not have ever played. This is particularly evident as all the base game features work; but the AI routines and balance have significant issues. AI will sometimes bumble around lost, stuck, unable to reach their destination or perform a task. Buildings decay at such a fast rate, that it exhausts the workers and player in futile attempts to maintain them. These are issues that could have been caught with playing for more than 15 - 20 minutes at time. It is clear Realmforge Studios lacked the commitment to even play their finished product nor examine quality control.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to leave a good review, i really do. The game looks good and has that Startopia-vibe to it I've experienced for the last 20 years. _childDocuments_.review: It's fun and frustrating. I can't recommend it at this price.Combat is so broken and frustrating. Controlling the mechs and drones is a nightmare, they rarely do what you expect them to do. Making room for mech paths across the base means you'll waste precious space that could have been used for buildings.Trading is weird, even if you have the right stuff, sometimes the button to sell or buy them just doesn't work (and it isn't because of lack of energy).Variable building templates don't move between saves, making them pointless, specifically in the campaign where you would usually build 1-2 buildings of the same type.I didn't finish the campaign, as I reached the level that has 3 other computer players that I need to defeat, and it relies on the frustrating combat, keeps damaging your buildings and energy core every now and then (for fun, I guess?), and randomly gives some bonus to a random player (no idea what that bonus is).I'll probably jump in again for free play later, but this just looks unfinished to me, and for that price, and an original game to live up to, I expected more.UPDATE AFTER FREE PLAYSo, I jumped into Free Play, with no other players so I never bother with mechs and their paths, and no VAL bonuses. It starts off a bit better but later the whole thing collapses. Employees keep quitting for lack of nature in fun and sub decks (The game says placing plants in pots would help, which I already did, but there's no way to see whether it's working or not, there's no nature overlay or any feedback when employees go next to plants).Then visitors started dying, apparently only 1 or 2 medics bother with their job out of the 14 hired ones.The last research tiers are also disappointing, they unlock fancier buildings fulfilling the same needs, with much less visitor capacity and gigantic buildings that make viewing the base more annoying.I'll set the game aside for a while, maybe updates will improve things a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sad game. _childDocuments_.review: So I don't do reviews, but I feel like I have to make one about this game because I am a huge fan of the first game and have even played what I would consider a fair amount (enough to test all the features and hit endgame a few times). So Startopia is one of my favourite strategy games I played as a child. It was humorous, strange and Sci-Fi all muddled into one. I loved it. I only wish I could say the same about this game. Lets start off with the base game play. This game is truly beautiful. From the overall graphics to the unique designs of the buildings, each designed uniquely for its purpose. That is unfortunately where the good points stop. This game had so much potential, but I had no idea that they'd remove so many themes from the first game. One of the issues they plagued this game with, was a heavy amount of micro management for the sake of micro management. You can only build so much before you are over-cumbered with soaring the floors with an eagle eye to call out every shot and pick up litter. Yes, you apparently are a part time bin man. This doesn't just affect litter though, you also have to micro manage every single building for when they need repairs because now in this game, they just lose durability over time (at a rather fast pace) leaving you flustered with so many tasks to do and you haven't even unlocked your third room for all your floors yet. This takes away the ability to be able to look at what you've crafted becoming slowly self sufficient. Now lets move on to other players (AI mainly). Not only do they advance and unlock rooms at an incredibly fast rate (leaving you feeling like you need to rush to expand your total space) but they also cause a lot of issues when you want to expand. The AI of the visitors/workers is actually broken, where any unique colour textures they have get instantly removed when you hire them because they only designed the uniform for that particular species with the one skin. Not only that, but they also have the tendency to leave their disease until it's gotten out of hand before getting treated, meaning that they are infecting more and more of the population. Now this will cause you a lot of issues, but because you're still trying to keep up with all the micro managing you do, you start to find it difficult to keep up. You cannot force them to get treated either, they have to go by their own choice. This often will leave you getting annoyed when people get mad when they're hungry etc, even though you have plenty of facilities to satisfy them, it's just the AI is ridiculously bad. Also P.s no matter how many workers you hire, the rooms they need to fill will never be full at once, so yeah, that's not annoying at all.Now on to war. One of the most fun attributes to the first game was being able to get an army of workers to fight the enemy to take their rooms and expand. This has been replaced with something that actually made me rage quit when I first discovered how the takeover process works. The workers do not arm themselves, not even the brutes. Nope, the brutes are just some fat Sci-Fi build-a-bear looking species that only operate machines via the station. So drones, sounds fun, right? Nope. The drones are actually awful. They will occasionally arrest criminals, but they aren't something you can just build on command, so you will find you are heavily limited. Not only that, but they added this war command table for you to control that is essentially completely useless and could be literally replaced with a right click. It is so awful to use that even when I was forcing myself to use it, it was just god awful. So verdict. As a whole, this game is just an unbelievable disappointment. Lacking in many areas it's first instalment thrived, removing the subtle humour and replacing it with a really cringe bot voice. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone. In fact, I'd honestly get my money back if I could. I honestly suggest the original Startopia as its far superior and while the graphics are certainly out of date, the game play is spot on and everything I wanted this game to be. Honestly devastated. Honestly, you could pay double the amount of this games value for the first instalment and you'd get more value out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed is exactly right, that is the experience I got from this game. _childDocuments_.review: Dear god! Who tested this game? Apparently no-one!1. Main menu doesn't even work correctly. Highlighted option remain highlighted. Going into other options shows them over the top of the previous options so you can even read them!2. Tried different resolutions but instead of offering the usual 1920x1080 or other 16:9 resolutions I can only choose 100%, 90%, 80% etc resolution of my 32:9 5120x1440 screen. Bonkers!3. _childDocuments_.review: Badly broken, unplayable past midgame, and abandoned, unfortunately.The game is feature-complete but riddled with game-breaking bugs.UI stops working after a while -- clicking on things becomes only sporadically effective, often just stopping working for 10-60 seconds at a time.  The keyboard will sometimes stop working, and alt-F4 is the only solution to that.  Sound frequently just dies -- sometimes dropping to the main menu fixes it, other times it needs a restart (which particularly sucks because it's got a good soundtrack and that's a significant part of the appeal of the game).  UI elements disappear or stop working.  Sometimes going to menu will fix it, other times not.  It's a mess.The game doesn't quite work internally.  One of the biggest problem is that staffing is broken -- for each position, you're supposed to assign 3 aliens to fill all 3 day shifts, but for some reason they often just won't attend, and no amount of overstaffing can fix it.For example, on the mission where you have to keep the station free of criminals, you need to keep three security stations (4 positions per station) staffed -- that should be 36 aliens to cover all shifts, 48 if you're being careful.  I ended up assigning 85 aliens (!) to staff them, but they were always between 0 and 3 working at each station.  What are the other 70-something doing that whole time?  Makes it kind of hard to accomplish mission objectives.  The game does model needs (eating, restroom, etc.), but it's well beyond that.  Pretty frustrating.Another problem is everyone being mad at my station for boredom because there's no disco.  There's a big disco almost always at 0% usage.  Yeah, staffing problem for sure (in this case 24 staff to run 2 slots in the disco, so constantly not staffed), but even when they decide to work, no one uses it.  Nothing you can do except watch them fume.I see discussions on these and other bugs in reddit, etc., from a year ago, and none of it has been fixed.There's a fun game somewhere underneath the bugs, but this game is definitely not worth buying until it's fixed, and Kalypso has a reputation for not letting their developers bring their games up to solid prime-time playability.  It just never got finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game for about 10 minutes before requesting a refund. I encountered issues with the camera skipping, which seemed like it might be due to a bug. I'm a big fan of the original game, so I'll be happy to consider purchasing this title again in the future if the developers address these concerns. I apologize for the negative feedback; I’m just hoping for improvements to make it as great as the original.RIP

_childDocuments_.review: It's Okay. Original Startopia is a GEM and have alway's wished for a Startopia 2. Starbase Startopia is a good alternative as long as you don't compare it to the original. An option to pause the game would be good but you can slow game speed. The price though is way too expensive,  £45 when it first came out and now £35 or £40 with the sound track. _childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews before buying the game. Actually, I was a bit confused as I had never played this kind of game before. I wanted to give the game a chance, as I thought I could refund it anyway. Overall I liked the game. It has a different atmosphere and gameplay. I like it.Our aliens are a little unhappy. It is up to us to make them happy. I felt like I was manage an interstellar hotel. The game is a bit like a space hotel business game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: The original Startopia is a gem. A flawed gem, perhaps - many of the campaign missions are ridiculously hard until you know the correct, quick, painless, gamey way to brush through them. But a gem, nonetheless. Gorgeous, aged very well indeed. The new Startopia is... wrong. Sure, it looks flashy. Sure, it borrowed heavily from the original. But what was a huge, sprawling, empty canvas is now a tiny station. The deliciously sarcastic computer is now a choice of three bloody annoying soulless voices. Micromanagement is back with a vengeance. The graphics make my eyes hurt. I was looking forward to this for months. And the painful fact is still that the ancient (2001!!!) original looks, plays and feels so much better than this. Asked for refund. Will reconsider if, at some point in the future, VAL returns. Possibly. Meanwhile, my old starbase awaits.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game in its current form. The comedy of the station AI falls rather flat, navigating around the station is tricky, the game seems to subtly push you towards making your station mech-unfriendly, and the sound will occasionally just die for no apparent reason. If you enjoyed Startopia, play Startopia, a great game that still stands up well today.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; Buy this game on sale, this game does have enjoyable moments. _childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing Startopia since the original and have always came back to it throughout the years.  This game is that game and more!  I’m very excited to spend hours in this game for sure as it has everything I loved about the original with a ton more content thrown on top of it. If you love sandbox and colony builders, then you’ll love this game!  They added a lot more customization to building blueprints too, which is a huge plus.  You can now make your Spacebase exactly how you want it with more fine detail.  The only thing that could be added to make it even more customization friendly is changing panel textures and flooring, but other then that customization is still very well done in this game, basically enough to let your imagination go wild.The thing I most loved about this game is taking care of your new tourist aliens almost as if your Spacebase is a theme-park.  You have to give them entertainment, give them places to sleep, hygiene fixes and more!  You also can craft and trade in this game with other space ships!  Not only that, there are also baddies that will come in and try to destroy your Spacebase, so you’ll need a good security as well.After putting a few hours into the released version of the game, I still haven't found the reason for so much hate on this game.  I still think it could use a bit of polishing with some things, but overall I still think it's a pretty solid game and am having a blast.  Most of my time spent in this game was in beta while making this review earlier.  Now having played the game in its release state, I haven't encountered anything that makes me want to change my thoughts on this game.  I do hope that the devs do take some notes on some of these reviews as I do agree with some of the things noted, but I still don't see why It's very close to mostly negative.  Could just be me, maybe I am good at finding the diamond in the rough, heh. I know words are just words… and aren’t the full picture, so I have some content for you to watch that will give you a better picture on how the game will play out.  You can check that out from the link below.  I can say that it was definitely worth my money.I’ll be doing more content on this game soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like there's a potentially very solid game at its core - and I've definitely had a few genuine laugh-out-loud chuckles in the first three missions, but the game has a glaring issue that makes it impossible for me to enjoy the way I want to enjoy builders/colony management sims for any length of time.There is no pause button. It certainly looks like there's a built-in pause functionality as the engine keeps running but the simulation pauses when you pull up the Steam overlay, but I can't for the life of me figure out how to actually pause the game so I can tweak my rooms and builds without feeling rushed.I play this type of game to relax, and the lack of a transparent pausing functionality currently makes me unable to do that because any time spent tweaking rooms is time that my station might fall into shambles.Can't be hard to implement, but I will be waiting until that feature is added.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, it's not the OG Startopia, but it didn't need to be. In some ways it's better with more dynamic rooms. In some way's it's not... I still miss the sarcasm of your OG AI assistant and also Arona. The Presitige unlock system is interesting, and make sense. I like the updated Sabotage capabilities. It's a very different game, but still in the same vein as the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: With Spacebase, the devs have essentially done three things:1. Copy-pasted Startopia2. Re-skinned everything3. Turned the maturity level down from teen-adult to child-teen in hopes of attracting a younger demographic, which unfortunately grinds the gears of the mature demographicFans of Startopia will find only a few changes in Spacebase, and most of them make the game worse. People new to Startopia are paying fifty bucks for something that they can pay  for.The ten levels of the flaunted voiced campaign is nothing more than tutorial levels with voice-overs, unlocking one step higher tech per level. And the voice-overs is  most annoying pile of garbage you most likely ever have come across in a video game. Ten years from now people will be using Spacebase as a meme for horrible A.I. voice-overs.Outside of the campaign the game has very little replayability as you're building the same buildings in the same build-order every game and have very limited character control.If you can find this game for free, try it. Until then, get the original.

_childDocuments_.review: *Updated* For nostalgia sake I really wanted to finish this game and be able to recommend it, but I absolutely can not.I battled through the campaign, I have no sense of achievement at having completed it, I'm actually just more annoyed at the anticlimactic ending to what was a level designed without much apparent thought.Overall, as a game this isn't fun to play, the difficulty spike and micromanagement are dreadful (especially since there's no pause to enable making the micro management less overwhelming when things get complex), it's riddled with bugs, a whole bunch of shockingly bad game design choices, mechanics, UX and UI abominations. This is a bag of flaming garbage that I regret having purchased even on sale that does a disservice to the fans of the original by downgrading the game play.It's bad enough for me to say this is probably the last game I ever buy from either Realmforge Studios and Kalypso Media as I don't trust they have a clue what they are doing and certainly don't think play testing is important (if they did, how could they possibly get this so horribly wrong)

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia is a remake to the ancient game Startopia.I played the previous game an awful lot back in the day and was happy to see that this game is remade.Spacebase Startopia is a juggling simulator just like Startopia was where you have to make your citizens happy and give them proper things to keep them busy like a SCI-FI Disneyland.It unfortunately has a lot of content removed such as the Memau, Skrasher, Grekka Targ, Kasvagorian, Turraken, Zedem Monk, and Polvakian Gem Slugs. But the Dryads in game look exactly like the Karmarama did.Also the Greys are the same, and the Groulien Salt Hogs are the exact same as the version in this game.I personally liked the original names for most of them and species wish they included them as variants in this game or at least skins.For example: The new replacer for the Gem Slugs is definitely much cooler than it was, but I'd still like the Jabba The Hutt style slugs to be in the game for more variety.The siren replacer being giant fuzzy moths in hipster clothing is a welcome change though, I absolutely love their design.One of the main issues with the game is the obsession with the garbage script, if you don't take care of garbage at the beginning of each match it's already over due to the 30 Vermin spawning out of every single coke can. I get the mechanic but it's very annoying and takes away from the game's overall feel to it.The next issue is by far removing the Memaus, they were incredibly immersive and to have them completely taken away and the jumpscare of a giant Skrasher bursting out of an infected person who got bit by one that was sick is sad, because that added incredible urgency to curing sick people.Another thing like the original is the enemy CPU advancing way too fast and instant research glitch by them being able to research more than 4 things from a single science station, but that was in the original so that's true to the content.Also the lack of diversity in the races of the game which the original game also had is very jarring. I get the set amount of races but I wish there were at least 20-30 different races. That may be asking too much as mechanics change that, but it would make the game really warrant its 40$ Price Tag.As it stands it's got decent gameplay, very good for livestreamers and I wish that more people would pick it up.25$-20$ is a good price for it watch it when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: If you expect this game to have any of the charm of the original Startopia, you will be disappointed. The original Startopia was not a perfect game but was still a masterpiece in terms of sound effects, narration, animation and atmosphere. Spacebase is not a masterpiece. It's basically a pig wearing lipstick.Back when Staropia was released it was a solid 9/10 for me, with a point deducted only for rather atrocious rival AI, it's still at least a 7/10 despite the dated graphics which honestly still work pretty well considering that "polygon" games are still popular.For Spacebase a 4/10 is more than generous, even without comparing it with the much superior original game, it's just not a well designed or implemented game. It's unfortunate because I thoroughly enjoyed Dungeons 3 by Realmsforge.So my verdict is, if you haven't played the original Staropia, do! And whether or not you've played the original don't bother with Spacebase unless you're a really big fan of colony builder type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's really not as bad as the reviews make it seem. I played the original shortly before getting this and really I don't think there's really a ton of difference between the two. Certainly not enough that I'd say one is obviously superior.Nothing here is breaking the mold at all but it is pretty and enjoyable and slightly funny.My only recommendation is to turn the robot voice off. Even though she's actually kind of helpful in notifying you of bad things you have to pay attention to, it's really not worth it. The robot is just constantly berating you and not in a way that is entertaining or funny (unlike the Dungeons game which was actually funny). This is just a constant stream of negativity and not in the self-depricating way they were hoping for. Plus the voice actors are just REALLY bad. I get they're supposed to be robots, but damn. If you INSIST on having the robot voice on, use the highly distorted version as it masks the garbage performance somewhat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fine successor of the old startopia, yes the game is a little different from the original one, less humor, some rooms work different, but it is very enjoyable for the fans of Startopia.People are crying because of the narrator, or some nonsense they can find, i honestly don't get it, this is a very faithful version of startopia, with great graphics and playability.We do need some quality of life upgrades, better path finding, smarter robots, zoom needs to go farther away. But honestly this game is very well made, and i plan to play it for a long time, i absolutely recommend it.Just ignore comments with less than 1-2 hours, seriously, this game is great, specially if you enjoyed old Startopia.

_childDocuments_.review: preliminary review 2 days after launch: after playing 4 hours in closed beta, 13 hours since release and over the years easily 200+ hours of the real  i can say with confidence: no.just no.i'll try to keep it fair here. at first i was not amused, by now i'm straight p#ssed off.at some point this game could end up being really good but that time feels months away. there are so many things in need of more polish, more refinement or plain fixing that it sucks the fun out of everything.the AI keeps talking without end in a cringy and unfunny way and often interrupts itself because its 20  seconds long pointless yada yada yada doesn't  end before the next pointless monologue starts. this way you easily miss the 20% of actually important notifications. you are busy manually removing bombs from your station every 75 seconds (i actually used my phone to stop the time) or dealing with any other "urgent disaster" forced on you  that playing the actual game and building & managing a space station gets basically impossible. you get Interrupted before you even remember what you were doing before you got Interrupted last time. it's actually insane. 30+ aliens waiting at the elevator getting hungry, tired, dirty, bored, ill and angry because the elevators only carry 1 person every 5 seconds. and your space inside the station is limited and expensive if not impossible to expand depending on the mission.GUI, usability and quality of life features are a straight F grade. you have messages and menus flooding the screen, menus hidden inside of menus, notifications that get overlooked or plain lost by the game since you get overwhelmed with all sorts of notifications all the time (remember the bombs every 75 seconds?). every action requires more clicks than it should and on top of that mouse clicks often don't register for some reason. you have lists of aliens and rooms but as soon as you click on one of them for details the list closes and all filters reset. it's utterly pointless to even try using.the flying trader arona daal is no more. back then he ripped you off but he had some useful things at the start of a mission. instead you get the VAL shop and it's completely useless. only single use items (!) or like  10x overpriced stuff. you learn to ignore it quickly. and even if you do need something specific it's usually not available thanks to the item rotation. horrific!the new research system is a hybrid of actual research and prestige points for making visitors happy. all that is neither easy nor fun to use. at one point i just stopped caring about the bonuses and just clicked all the buttons i could afford to click. worked just fine and didn't waste idle time you simply don't have during playing.after  playing for about 1 hour and owning a third of the station performance starts getting really bad. even with a 8c/16t cpu, 32gb ram, gtx 1080 and all my steam games on ssd.actually last game i was down to 20 fps after 3 hours of playing. that's amazingly terrible performance. i just played one of the later missions involving combat and getting rid of competing station administrators. let's just say the combat system is so clunky it's out of this world. beating that mission took me 4 hours. one time i had 15 minutes of combat straight. i needed to monitor every second of it and after that my station was totally f#cked up because i couldn't react to the constant messages & events and i was unable to adjust to changing demands and increased station size. i won the war but fixing up my station after that took me a full hour.oh and let's not forget: the single player missions are just an extended tutorial just like with the original startopia. sandbox and multiplayer are the real deal. if you don't care about that it's game over after 10 missions and about  20 hours. the amount of micro managing is off the charts. in fact building a nice station, making your visitors happy and rolling a profit turns to a side note when being bombarded with urgent emergencies all the time and the need to do absolutely everything yourself. want some potted plants to touch up your station, a pond on the bio deck for swimmers or just a single minute of peace and quiet? NOPE! you don't have time for any of that.did i mention? this game has no pause. brilliant!every mission i find myself thinking "i need to do this and build that" and 30 minutes later it's still not done! because bombs here, alien attack there, cringy AI speech in my ears and my attention getting trapped by bad interface or another random bug i just managed to find. i think i will stop here. with both complaining and actually playing. i think i made my points very clear.also it's massively overpriced. this game is not an original concept. it's 20 years old. they copied like 90% of it, made some changes and usually for the worse actually.with the clever use of discounts i paid 38€ for the extended edition and still i feel like i got tricked into paying  double what it's actually worth.if you want to start a starbase right now get the old startopia. it's 1/10th of the price but 10x better a  game.this game needs a lot more work to be enjoyable or even to hope to come close to the old one.don't tell me you tested this game 8 hours a day at the office when playing 30 minutes is enough to make me wanna smash my keyboard, torture the voice actors or just alt-f4 and forget i own this sad imitation.almost 9 months and a few updates later i finally managed to get the last achievement that was bugged before.and within the next second i quit and uninstalled.they fixed some stuff and added some quality of life features that should have been in the game from the start. but the game's performance is still terrible even on potent hardware and the problem of aliens being too stupid to fulfill their own needs is still there.to think that i paid 38€ on day 1 for this abomination makes me wanna hurl. worst deal of 2021 apart from corona.let's never talk about this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start...I played the beta and could see it was no where near complete then. So i waited until the final release of the game to see if any of the problems i had before were fixed... Then that is where it went wrong.There are more bugs now than there were in the Beta such as:.All sounds except for the music, just... disappear for no reason!.Crappy AI (Aliens and bots get stuck... way to easily..All AI Voices still sounds off in places (not a comment on it not being the original one... That's another problem entirely).Some things are not explained well (Clicking the Pop Up Buffs to activate, i was under the impression that it just kind of worked on its own).The Humour is Bad... Really bad....Graphical glitches every once in a while.Item Hit boxes are Janky at best (cant collect litter sometimes, Minimap in the top left is near impossible to click to change decks with no clear reason why hovering over the bottom deck will sometimes  highlights the Top Deck. _childDocuments_.review: When I first found out that StarTopia was getting a modern remake/sequel, I was absolutely thrilled. I spent hundreds of hours playing the original as a kid. Oddly enough, despite its overall interesting gameplay and design, along with stellar writing and humour, the original game never really took off. I was sure it was going to die in obscurity.Spacebase Startopia lacks all of the above. The graphics have been bumped up, but simultaneously lost all their charm. The biggest offender is VAL. In StarTopia, VAL was a snarky AI with stellar voice acting and dry British humour. In Spacebase, you can choose three voices, or a fourth "no voice" option, and they're all bland. You might as well have just put a speech synthesizer in.I'm sure the developers poured a lot of love into this project, but it just feels like a soulless sequel to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Review update: Can no longer recommend. The developer stopped updating the game three months after release. With the mentioned bugs in place, it disappoints.Original review, with hope removed:Not that bad in gameplay (I think the improvements in gameplay outweigh the downsides when compared to the original). But really bad in humor. Dull, repetitive - really embarassing. Still, not bad in gameplay!Not a highly optimized, sophisticated, large-scale RTS, but a fun playfield. I say it's enjoyable (ignoring the insulting jokes) and the later missions are a sufficient challenge.Some bad stuff:* Has performance issues. Building a large base, even with my 5900X, it blocks rendering half a second whenever a crate is put into storage.* Trading is obviously unbalanced and bugged.* Big bases are less attractive since aliens won't be super smart when it comes to route planning.* Hired aliens quit for lack of promotion (payment) when they already are fully promoted. Compared to the original, where you could just keep clicking the promotion button to fill them up with energy (money).Some good stuff:* Templates for rooms, yay!* Mechs. I was sceptic at first, but a new game mechanic should always be welcome.* The Biodeck is more important and easier to terraform (compared to original).It's hard to recommend at full price. But when on sale for half price, I'd say give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Ninety-five percent of carbon-based lifeforms enjoy their time on Spacebase Startopia. Only five percent experience an unfortunate and surely accidental death.If you want to see gameplay and watch some of my second impressions as they happened, click on the video above. Spacebase Startopia is a delightful management sim where you run Space Disneyland. VAL, your sarcastic and dry humored AI is here to help... or maybe to watch you suffer. VAL always gets those two things mixed up. Prove yourself worthy as a spacebase manager by earning more energy than you spend. And don't worry: if you fail, you're easily replaced.The learning curve is steep, and despite the tutorial you're likely to miss a few things your first time. And maybe your second time too. (I certainly did.) But that's okay, because VAL is here with its three voice options to question your decisions even when you think you're doing the right thing. There's a bevy of aliens, structures, and even a splash of combat. You can min-max to optimize your building choices or take the more beginner-friendly pre-made structures as you're learning the game. The devs certainly tried to make things accessible even if at times you're left scratching your head about what to do. Or do the completely wrong thing despite your best efforts.But for those who can get past its learning curve, Spacebase Startopia shows its charm in the many aliens leaving reviews on your spacebase, just like other reviewers and I are doing on this game. #ConfusingButFun sums up my review, and maybe Kalypso will decide to hire me just like I hired my customers in-game. The tutorial isn't mandatory, but you'll need to play it to understand this game, and early missions continue to expand on your knowledge. But Startopia doesn't hold your hand either. In the second mission I mistakenly thought I needed to convert my food into better food via my factory instead of simply storing the food. And that was after I hired all of the dryads I possibly could while trying to figure out how to produce more food.If you can laugh off your mistakes and confusion along the way, there's a deep and sprawling game here to enjoy. Watching hapless aliens live their lives makes you feel like you're making a real difference as you extort their money for your corporate overlords. Did I say you were running Space Disneyland? Space Walmart might have been a better comparison.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to focus on mech production this time. Got one when the AI attacked me with 3. I was also forced to either make mys security drones blow themselves up or have 50% HP. That's on easy difficulty. Must be fun on higher difficulty levels.RTS wise: it's like Starcraft 2 with only 1 playable race with only 1 combat unit - the Thor. When you fight an enemy, whoever has more mechs will win. Security droids do nothing against mechs so it's just: you have 2, enemy has 3 = you lose. You have 3, enemy has 2 = you win. You have an aqual amount of mechs: usually you win because AI sucks at controling them. If you just pull out low hp mechs and repair them you should be fine. Remember how you could defend in the orginal startopia by hiring 20 workers provided you had enough cash? In this game your regular employees just do nothing and die. It's all down to mechs and nothing else. Only 3 types, melee, mid range, long range. Slow, sluggish, poorly animated. Just uninteresting overall.Sim wise: remember how dungeon 3 FPS dips hard when you pick up 20 creatures and drop them on the dungeon exit? This might be the same engine but as soon as you build up to 3 sectors, there's constantly more than 20 createures on screen. Ryzen 5 3600 + GTX 1060 6GB should not choke on this game yet I've heard even much stronger specs like 1080 Ti are also struggling here. Other than that it's just Startopia so if you really loved the original game, you should give this one a spin. Running a free play scenario with no oponnents is always an option. Though as soon as your base gets large performance will make it almost unplayable. Pathing also sucks. When I've got a full ring base employees kept quiting because they went for a drink to the other end of the station and while walking they got so thirsty that they quit. Room sizes make it impossible to have everything near everything so as your base grows, people will start quitting.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit to note: things are being patched - mostly Quality of Life things for now - but I will write a more comprehensive update when enough has changed to prompt another playthrough. Just highlighting that for now the below still applies, other than some of the pointless clicking has been eliminated through reduction in some activities and options to auto-resolve events and suppress notifications.Original review:There are some minor improvements over Startopia with multi-pickup, factory queues, and modern graphics.With some things your mileage might vary, like the different approach to research (doesn't work for me), resources and needs (it's messy and doesn't land as far as I'm concerned) and the bio deck terraforming (why is this just a dumbed down version of Startopia's system? Worse as far as I'm concerned).There are also serious problems with writing, pace, combat, glitches, and lack of understanding of what was good about the mechanics being cloned, or failing that a clear vision about the direction they were going to take with them this time. It's like Baby's First RTS, plus a bunch of pointless clicking and busywork that get in the way of what could be a solid builder/manager.Played 200 hours in beta, gave feedback about all these things and there was either no will or insufficient resources to make meaningful changes. No amount of UI and graphical polish can make up for it just not being much fun. Go play the original for £5 and have an actually good time - even with the old graphics.But the thing that tipped me into a firm negative is the unatmospheric, lazy, inept, nonsensical failure of a campaign. There isn't even boss fight music, and you have to click 'main menu' to get the entirely non sequitur ending "cinematic" that was animated in an afternoon by the work experience kid.The idea that this was allowed to be released without a total rewrite to at least make it make basic sense is absurd and insulting - all of these things could be fixed by someone with some basic skill and interest in the genre.For £50, it's obscene.Strong avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the old Startopia, this game doesn't feel the same. Maybe it's just nostalgia talking but here's my main insights about the game:Pros:- Cutesy artstyle, cartoony and quality animations for just about everything.-Lots of avaible building.-Can decorate things in details.Cons:- Way, way, way too much busywork. The Biodeck barely harvest anything on its own because the Fuzzers only pick up one crate at a time most of the time. Cleaning up after garbage gets old quick.- Long wait time. Especially in early and even mid-game in Freeplay, you're going to WAIT. Wait until you have enough prestige to buy new buildings. Wait until you have enough money to buy anything. Wait until you get the event to clean up garbage or destroy your O2 to get money.- Alien AI is meant to have a lot of differents tastes and wants, but they move very slowly. You have to build multiple elevators for them to move around easily to the fun deck, but even then... After like 3 hours of freeplay in building and unlocking everything the aliens just swarms the discos and disregards almost every single other buildings. So I have just discos upon discos that works half the time because the employees take breaks very often to go eat and tend to their own needs.All in all. It may be more cute than the old Startopia, but it's swamped in busywork and tedious gameplay. You can't design the berth and bars the same way you could with old startopia, and the design of some aliens feels more "safe" and not as imaginative as the old Startopia.All in all, this is buyer's regrets at its peak.Also, VAL is insufferable. Funny quips and condescending comments gets old very, very, very quickly. About the moment you hear the same insulting jab about your thinking process or your slow gameplay twice.Get the old Startopia on GoG.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, but it - funnily enough, needs some more programming.- Trash is out of control. You'll spend the most of your time picking it up and squishing the vermin it attracts by clicking on them, even though I'm not sure if it really does any good. Building a crazy number of garbage cans help.- The worker fuzzies aren't programmed well and frequently stop working without any explanation. One way to help them work a little better is to build extra charging stations, but that isn't a fix all. It seems like they start to glitch when their batteries are low.- The tutorial is SEVERELY lacking. For example, I didn't know that repairs take crates from a factory, so when retrying a level, an hour in I failed the mission because I hadn't built a factory or produced any crates - ran out of energy due to most of my facilities failing at once, and not being able to repair them due to having no crates.- The pop-up events come in two versions - timed ones that pop up on the main screen, and smaller events that come through the message window. The problem is that the message window is really easy to miss.- Mission five glitched out so that after an hour of work, the boss didn't load in, even after reloading a save, making it impossible to win.- Having only ten campaign missions in a game this price isn't acceptable.This game could be great if given some more work. It obviously was released too soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: NEWEST REVIEW:Update 1.2 introduced some small but important gameplay and UI tweaks that does enough to turn playing the game from a negative experience to a positive one: You can have fun with this game now as no single aspect of managing the station will now try and dominate your time.The game isn't perfect and it's not the Startopia of old. It completely lacks the wit and humour of the original. But from a gameplay and machcanics standpoint it's now playable and engaging.This is speaking from the perspective of if you enjoy playing long-form "Free Play" sessions where it takes 4-6 hours of play to complete the mission objectives. The single player campaign is fine up to the last final missions where it falls apart.If you want the gameplay experience of a Startopia reimagining then you'll get it. The artistic choices in terms of VO and Audio work is still quite bad though. I suggest you turn "VAL" off and put some of your own music on while you play.OLDER REVIEW:I've played through most of the campaign and played through a long free play game.For many like myself this game is to be compared to the original made back in the early 2000s.It has all the elements in place to be just as good as the original, but some heavy rebalancing of elements would be needed to make this game as enjoyable as the prior iteration in terms of game feel.I stress that if this game interests you. Keep an eye on it over the next upcoming months and let's see if the devs plan to address the balancing issues.It suffers from the following that is unlikely to be fixed:- A lack of wit and humour. The original leaned heavily towards Douglas Adams Hitchhikers guide to the galaxy. There's none of that here and it's replaced by a badly written GlaDOS style humour. Take my advise and turn the sound off for VAL. You're not missing anything.What can be fixed in later updates:The balancing of this game is well out of whack. Some elements are far too hard to control in the games later stage which leads to too much of your time focused on doing things you shouldn't need to. Namely:- Garbage management. In the original the concept was simple: Put bins around your base and garbage is managed. This game tries to over complicate it with bins that walk to recyclers’, bots that pick up trash and even employees that pick up trash. And all of this extra complexity is thrown away because the game can't manage garbage in the late game and can't communicate to you how you can fix it. Creating a very un-fun late stage where you spend 50% of your time collecting trash manually. Horrible. To the devs: You overthought this one. Scale it back and make it manageable. this system at it stands would need to clearly tell the player what they need to do to fix the problem, which it doesn't.Trading: Items you buy are not automatically put into the cargo hold. Why? Why add this extra step of needing fuzzers to carry it? Scale this complexity back.It's kept some things from the orignal game that didn't need to be there. Manually promoting your staff isn't a meaningful choice. You either remember to do it or they quit. That isn't any fun in the orignal game and it didn't need to be here either.Building more fuzzers is too complex for its own good. The game will almost effectively complete before you get the chance to craft what you need to upgrade your fuzzers to the amount and the tech level where they can manage the station well.The UI for this game is needlessly complicated. Combat has its own UI and it's not merited. Building rooms is a chore. Which is a shame because you can save blueprints of building designs which is smart and interesting.Overall:I can't recommend the game at this point due to its flaws with balancing. I really hope the devs care enough about this game to spend the time to rebalance the experience, dial back things that are not fun like waste management and focus on the aspects of the game that is fun like room design, layout optimisation and exploiting trade and manufacturing.My fingers are crossed for a rebalancing. This game can be fun with what it has in systems and assets. It just needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Many people wanted a perfect Clone of Startopia, this game is not that. It has many resemblences to Startopia, while still having enough differences to feel different and that is ok.It is a decent game that deserves a chance. Best is tough that you watch a letsplay from someone you trust to decide if you want it.The Good.-C.R.A.T.E.S still exist and have been expanded. Some can even be used to grant buffs, such as faster workers, recharging bots etc. Otherwise its the same Food, Med, building crates like in Startopia.-The Stations are round and you got the 3 decks. (Inner, Entertainment and the Garden)-The early levels are pretty similiar to the 1st few Startopia levels. (level 1 collect Garbage and so forth)- You open a Door and the rooms are filled with Garbage, Vermin and Monsters.-Specific Aliens work in specific Buildings.-The 3rd Deck Gardening can be edited. You get more biomes now then in the Original Startopia.-Controls are almost the same with the exception of Hotkeys.-The Buildings are similiar to Startopia but got different names.-Diseases are dangerous unlike in startopia. If someone gets sick adn they decide they rather go to the Disco then the Doctor expect the Med bays to be overcrowded soon, tough it is a great money maker.-You can build Giant Mechs, they need space to navigate tough.-More research options, great for people like me who like games with research.The Bad and the Ugly-The Voice AI that assists you somehow does not feel like it belongs in the game. Could just be me tough.-The jokes early one are bad, they get kind of better later, but never reach Startopia levels of humour.-In Startopia Aliens in the Disco had awesome Dance moves, now we got Greys who twerk.-Startopia Disco music is great, here the Music is also Good it is more of techno style, still good tough.-The art style. _childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I found it more annoying than entertaining.The phrase "We were on the verge of greatness. We were this close." comes to mind. You can tell it's obviously made by people who loved or at least understood the old Startopia, which is more than I can say about other companies' attempts to replicate something, and it obviously did a lot of things right too... but...1. The UI seems to have this annoying habit of ignoring clicks. Like, it might literally take more than one click to get it to acknowledge that, yes, ffs, I really do want to switch from placing doors to placing beds, when I'm designing a berth. I don't know if it's my frame rate being too low to register brief clicks (I only have a RTX 2080 TI, after all;)) or I'm possibly dragging a bit when I click or what, but it's the only game doing that and it's annoying.2. Conversely, the UI lets you click right through dialogs. Like, let's say I'm designing a berth, I have a bed selected, and one of those timed events shows up where I must choose one bonus or another. Clicks to open it up and pick a choice will literally also place a bed, if it's within the berth blueprint. Or let's say the AI assistant started ranting at you again, and you want to click the little arrow to shut it up. Yep, same thing happens. Processing the click didn't stop when it hit the dialog, but basically continued straight through.At times, I find it easier to just cancel whatever room I'm designing or decorations I'm placing, and deal with those dialogs, then restart.3. Which, combined with the fact that I can't pause the game while designing someting, to avoid such interruptions, is really annoying AF.4. The fact that something as basic as being able to buy more worker robots is basically up to whether it was randomly available in the "VAL shop" at the moment. I might have to literally click that one every 2 minutes, and still get none. Imagine if you were playing Warcraft (the RTS, not "world of") and it was random if you can buy a peon right now or not. In some missions where you might need to do them in a fixed time for an achievement, so basically it's up to some dice rolls if that achievement's physically possible to do or not. Yeah, that's the experience here.5. The chatty robot assistant. Look, a snarky AI assistant who seems to exist just to insult you may even be funny the first time around. Now imagine playing the same mission half a dozen times because you want to get an achievement. Yeah, the experience is like being at a party and some drunk guy follows you around to tell you the same dad jokes half a dozen times. Better yet, if they weren't even as much jokes as some 'funny' way to insult you. And they're not even witty retorts or comments on the current situation, but lines that he memorized from somewhere else and is regurgitating verbatim, whether they fit or not, over and over and over again.I swear to the elder gods, a couple of times I actually found myself shouting "SHUT UP! JUST <bleep>ING SHUT UP ALREADY!" at the screen.6. But it's actually worse, because the game ranting and raving for minutes in a row is drowning actually useful information. I've watched even youtubers who play games as their day job, still miss important information, like that some crate is available, because it was buried in a 2-minute long lame attempt at the game doing a stand-up comedy audience take-down routine.Look, devs... the purpose of a UI -- whether it includes basically a glorified text-to-speech option or not -- is to make it EASIER to get the important information, not to drown it in a 2-minute long rant about how obviously you're too stupid to understand that you need to place the berth first.7. The pointless distractions like clicking space cockroaches (kind of like shooting the mice in Hospital Tycoon) to get rid of them before they infect everyone. I can understand why someone thought it would be a great gameplay addition to have something more for the player to do, but that is negated by its being repetitive and pointless. Those cockroaches will respawn in seconds, for example. It's literally easier and saner to just let them be, and just live with everyone taking trips to the doctor often.8. The camera... oh dear. Now I kind of understand why you can't scroll out too far without going through a ceiling or bulkhead, when you're inside a space station, so I'll give this the lowest priority. But... really, it's the only city builder kind of game in recent history, where I have to wrestle the camera (and I really mean wrestle) just to place some building.9. ... and at times moving the camera gives me a slight case of nausea. Which I don't remember getting in any other game. Not sure if it's the curved space or some blur they do or what, but yeah.10. Remember that talk about how I get interrupted while I'm trying to design a berth? Yeah, that's also because I get to design the same one over and over and over again every time. The game basically does let you "save" a design, but it's pretty much just a way to duplicate a room. (Which, granted, is already more than other games often.) You can only have one custom design per room type, and it isn't "saved" in any meaningful sense of the word. In the next mission, or even if you restart the current one, it's gone. So I have to recreate the same design I found to work well, every single mission. While wrestling the camera again, and being interrupted all over again.
