_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin with people who negatively review this game forget it's currently early access and only released 2 months ago (at the time of this review)Honestly I usually find these games kind of boring, but the simple and absurd nature presented just appealed to me. It's still quite clearly an unfinished product, with ultimately somewhat limited things to do other then base building and minor management elements. Ive also crashed a few times and when you get to a large base with lots of rooms and maxed out cultists, some get stuck in place during breakfast time, making their moods drop purely because of imperfect coding.Although the initial cult customisation is cool with a surprising amount of options, it's all ultimately meaningless. I wanted to make a cookie themed cult (obviously) but in the end was forced to  It's a little underwhelming that there is an end goal that changes nothing once you complete it, and to even do so is just more of what you've been doing the whole time. Researching stuff, sending people on missions and buying stuff. However it seems the "Darkness" route is one of 4, with the other 3 not being released yet and presented as locked, so there's potential.Customising cultists themselves comes down to purely RNG when it comes to traits. What profession you want them to do and how you level up their skills are mostly also dictated by said traits. Assigning them to specific tasks is also interestingly presented and although its intuitive to let members work where they are needed, having to manually set where I want people to work while I cross reference it with their mismatched traits is annoying at best. Id rather when the game spawns a cultist they have a recommended place of work (Reception, Therapy Rooms, Module Rooms, Etc), and their traits that boost skills revolve around whats useful there, rather then having a mixture of traits boosting skills that don't compliment eachother due to only 2 specific skills ever mattering for each job.Or you know, each skill could have more depth in side bonuses so I don't feel forced to max out specifically 2 skills for specifically one job, or have jack of all trades type cultists who arent excelling at any job since skill investment is limited. Its not like missions make it worthwhile to have mixed skills either maxing out a single skill is more helpful because like I said, theres only limited skill investment.This is a late game nitpic however, as early on you really just take who you can get.The gameplay loop itself addictive as all hell too, but all that stops the moment you beat the game as there is little to no replay value currently. I don't get anything special for completing the finale, and there is only so much I can build up my base until I run out of room. The potential for depth is there however, and my issues with the game come from it purely being an unfinished product, rather then it being a not thought out product. There's room to grow is what I'm saying.The only thing I don't like right now is the pricepoint at $29.95 in my local currency, which seems a little high for whats on offer here currently. Quoting the developers:  This implies that the full release will go up in price, and I'm not sure if that is justified. I personally think if the content I'm expecting to see comes to fruition, then sure, full price at $30 is fine and inline with other similar games published by Team 17. But $40+ seems a little ambitious for the type of content being provided. I don't mean to discredit the hard work and clear love put into this game, but besides games made by well known developers I cant really think of any games in this genre that push into low priced Triple A game territory.Due to its early access nature I can't give it a fair score out of 10 (if this was a full release it would be a 4-5 tbh) but I can definitely recommend a purchase as it is quite  enjoyable to see people worshipping "The Cookie Godess" or whoever you decide.Overall for a newly released early access game, it's actually quite impressive what it already has to offer. It truly does feel like early access rather then an unfinished product. But the fact it's open access is why I can easily recommend this game as although its limited, buying into early access is basically paying to play an unfinished product, isn't it?I don't see this game ending up in Early Access hell either, with Team 17 funding it, you will get your moneys worth one day.Just have a little faith :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually really pleased with this gem of a game. At first, I thought HIJaC would just be a goofy little colony simulator that would die a slow death in Steam's mass grave of unfinished pre-alpha cash grabs, but the amount of fun I ended up having surpassed my unreasonably high expectations. The colony management is satisfying, the engine is robust, and the customisation is unusually vast. The jokes are dry but land well in context. Me being a mindless psychopath, I created The Order from the Silent Hill games. My cultists worship Alessa with fear and pride, and we have daily conversions in the Church of The Rebirth. Sadly there is no flesh peeling from the walls at dusk, no fire sirens, and I cannot flay followers who leave in anger and throw the bloody refuse at the church doors. I hope Konami doesn't read this review. They'll flag it for IP infringement. Going forward, I have two ideas. First of all, I'd love to see some mod workshop integration. Community contributions would compliment the style of HIJaC well, and I believe modding is the last step into really involving the community (that doesn't really exist yet) in the final stages of development. Second, what cult is complete without some innocent murder? Give us the framework to harbour dark secrets and the high stakes risk/reward elements of HIJaC will be much more satisfying. Thank you for your time,Ynsin.

_childDocuments_.review: After a few starts, ups, downs, and a multitude of craziness. A finale has been reached.  This game runs with the same feel of management builders on a grid base.  The game has a whitty story and a sudden finish as the ending mechanic upon reaching all prerequisites will be a instant finish when activated, you are given a one more day option to continue your group.Pros:Full Customization of your cult.Mechanics are simple for the new, but allows more advanced plays.Skill tree allows for choices to move forward at the sacrifice of progress towards another direction.Multiple currency types for use with different aspects.Cons:Leveling system punishes the unaware as this choice will determine if there will be a happiness issue that could make or break your cult.Lack of End Game Options - The game allows for multiple forms of building a cult, but the end game is a single finish at this time.  This will most likely change as other directions are in the works which will allow for more options in the end.Overall if you are a fan of games like Prison Architect, Academia, and other management builders on a grid map, you will have a place in this cult.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game being a bit of a cult nerd; I know a lot about them and at one point, an ex and I had talked about making a cult simulator game because of my weird passion. So, I was STOKED to see there was a game coming out similar to what I'd envisioned and it's okay. Like, it has room to grow. A lot of room. But it's a good foundation.Some feedback:Cult lore: Often power and control are major themes behind the origins of cults, and that's something that isn't really explored in the game. It's more so a financial theme. What if I want my cult of Herbologists to be off the grid farmers who recruit people by selling their vegetables in a mini market that can be upgraded over time? Rules: Many cult leaders run a tight ship to control their flock and have many asinine rules for their followers to adhere to. We should be able to create our own asinine rules/10 Commandments for our followers to follow. That way I know who's following the rules, who gets a good bed and who's sleeping on a dirty mattress.Hierarchy: There's usually some sort of hierarchy in place that lets the followers know who's who, and who you have to get through to become someone worthy. Let's get an inner sanctum going, y'know, or let us segregate cleaning/menial tasks to our newbies, and work their way up to doing cooler stuff. Maybe grouping of jobs/roles within a pyramid (hehe) on the Cult members job page.Better quests: Not sure if you've seen what stuff cults get up to, but it's rarely talking to the media. I've noticed you can unlock other quests after a while, and they seem like the type of quests that are better for the beginning of the game (especially because there isn't a campaign, storyline or active quests within the cult or quotas to unlock levels that provide you with more content). It would also be cool if my cult members, who have their own info/job history/needs had their own side quests.Overall, the game has potential but it doesn't play like an actual cult game. Which is sad, as it's the only game of its type on the market. I'll continue to play for a few hours here and there, and look forward to more content coming out in the future. If you're looking for a game that has room to grow, I'd recommend it. If you're looking for a game about cults, I wouldn't really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I joined a Cult is a city-building game with a cultist theme.Pros:-Fun theme with a variety of cult designs to run with.Cons:-While you can dress your characters up differently, ultimately all cults have to choose 1 of 3 three routes to go down in terms of themed buildings.-Game is slow. Even at the fastest speed research and accumulating resources can take forever.-intro feels somewhat janky and low effort. Tutorial is very hand-holdy and makes it hard to get into the game intially.Overall, despite the cool premise, gameplay wise this is the same as any generic city-building sim game. The pacing actually even drops it further and makes you question if its worthwhile to slog through. After 3 hours I thought maybe it would pick up, after 6 hours I was ready to move on with my life. Not the worst game, but there's definitely many other city-sim games that can scratch that itch better.Rating: 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I agree with almost everything Nayu says in their review . With regards to the protests, I think that they missed a mechanic (which, to be fair, is never spelt out and you might miss it) where if you mouse over the protester that's banging on your fence, the relevant skill will highlight over all your cultists at once making it pretty easy to pick out the relevant cultists. Other than that, I agree with pretty much everything.Additionally, the endgame SUCKS... With regards to the cult-specific ending, all of that research can be done ***only*** by the head of your cult (this is the Divine Inspiration tree). Even with maxxed out items (that you get from the regular research tree), this research takes a significantly long time. At this point in the game, I have completed the regular research tree, maxxed out every building, and had every single follower at 'good' or better. There's a couple of very short research spots, but they are to place a cult-specific mission on the mission map, which are thirty (30) hours in f'ing duration. While these missions are underway, the head of your cult cannot do any Divine Inspiration research. For no good reason, at all.In addition to this there are 4 buildings that can be operated *only* by the head of your cult, 2 of which affect followers (non-cultists) and 2 affect cultists. Followers, of course, only appear during the day which overlaps with the default schedule of your leader, which means that if you want to use those buildings you have to stop doing the Divine Inspiration research. (the other two rooms can be used during 'rest' time)So my last several hours of gameplay were just... waiting out the clock on either research or missions, and then spending hundreds of thousands of $$$ to build the Finale Room. And. The game ends. With a big picture. Just an image.Extremely anti-climactic.While there are multiple endings (3 cult specialities and, I assume, 2 endings for each), why the f*ck would I sit through ALL of that again for, essentially, a low-effort 'congratulations' screen?For the most part, I found the game to be astonishingly easy (and I am NOT good at colony sims), just unnecessarily long.If you want to kill 3-4 hours? Sure, this is a good buy on a deal. Playing it all the way through was a complete waste of my time, and I regret doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's fine. It's not going to blow your socks off, but it's an fun time-waster that's difficult to lose.It's a base builder about running your own cult in the 70's!  The music and theming all add to the 70's vibe in a funky way, but once the novelty wears off, it feels more like running an amusement park than a cult. It's easy to pick up if you've never played a base builder before. Even on challenging difficulty, I had no problems managing my resources and typically read a book while the game ran on full speed. The biggest downside to the game is that it's just... boring. There's a lot of waiting for things to happen, either building resources, waiting for research or waiting for missions to complete. Bad events are either entirely avoidable (if you don't forget to click something), or unavoidable and relatively harmless. They don't add any challenge or pressure to the game, and for the most part I was annoyed clicking the "accept" button three times a day because my cultists forgot to wash their hands and now their tummy hurt. The variety of decorations and rooms add some spice to the gameplay, and I'll admit that part of why I played as long as I did was to make a couple of pretty, themed compounds. Towards the endgame, you tend to have more money than anything else, and I enjoyed spending all of it to make extravagant bathrooms. The system for improving decor is more complex than just adding a bunch of rugs and pictures, and I personally enjoyed trying to max out scores while keeping with my theme. The writing is light and witty, and there are numerous events that quiz you on your everyday knowledge. Being able to successfully jump a car, for example, can give one of your cultists a permanent +6 to their skills. Sometimes, it feels out of place, especially when running an evil cult. I'm liquidizing followers for their purple goo, but the music is cheerful and cultists are joking about The Minkler. It never really felt like I was running a cult trying to take over the world, but rather a fun, afternoon retreat for everyone I hadn't eaten yet.Overall, it's a fine game. It doesn't have the addictive quality I usually find in base builders, but it's easy gameplay and groovy vibe might appeal to those new to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't have that many hours in the game I was hoping on at least a little bit realistic version of a cult game. In this game you run a religion where your members reach out into the community and prosthelytize to people as well as share your religious propaganda and occasionally commit robbery and such to steal artifacts (kind of like in evil genius). You need to keep your followers happy and satisfied with food, bathrooms, cleanliness and entertainment.While there is cult-ish elements in the game, it takes an approach of tricking people out of their money rather than the real issue of lust of control over others at any expense.In short, this game feels like rimworld meets evil genius rather than anything really cult-like. The lack of the devs ever (last i checked what they said on the matter) having a plan to add mods also makes the game pretty stale with little point in re-playing the game. (and I will explain why)The cult designer (at the start of the game) has no relevance to gameplay in any way shape or form. The design of the cult is ONLY art style and has no impact of what your 'cult' does or how others react to it. There also is no real way to have your people outreach to people or force them into the 'cult'. Rather, you have a few rooms that have the ability to let people come in off the street and talk to your people (without prompting, pamphlets or anything else other than them just walking by). If you are expecting to customize your cult to be like Aum Shinrikyo and appeal to the anime crowd, Peoples Temple Agricultural Project (jonestown) and appeal to christianity x communism x Socialism or Heavens Gate and appeal to christianity x UFO's, then you can save your time and wait for another game. Every playthrough in this game will have the same flavor as there just isn't another way to build the 'cult' other than the generic way they have you play through the game.Other than all of that, the game is just ok. The one part that does truely shine in this game is the people you can recruit to be your 'workers' as you can recruit 5 different ranks (as far as i can tell) and each come with traits that are a bonus and a curse. They gain xp and level up as they work and go on missions. They have the standard way of keeping your people happy with nothing really new other than the rooms can become crowded and you get a debuff on the room where they are too full of objects or have a broken object in the room.On broken objects and logistics, you can assign a worker to a repair room, however, they randomly wander through your buildings and look in them to clean and fix items. The issue is that they occasionally miss entire rooms of broken objects that can leave you with a room that is non-functional for days at a time unless you manually direct them to fix the object. The food in the game is basically 4 tiers of food with 'snack machine' being the least and 'meat and vegetables' being the best. While this is ok to start with they do not have a way of auto-ordering new ingredients for your people to cook with for the 3 higher tiers of food. This means if you forget to top the food off by purchasing more for 2-3 days then your people will revert to eating vending machine food and suffering large debuffs to their moods. I would expect the devs to change this in the future as it makes for a annoying and frustrating way of playing the game.workers will randomly man rooms as they feel like they want or do not want to. I don't know if this is intended or not but it becomes increasingly frustrating to get your workers to work at rooms as your amount of workers grow from the researches you do to increase them. There is a way to forbid them performing other jobs and this is what you end of having to do for every single worker for them to even work and man the open rooms as they tend to just wander around the starting area and sometimes get stuck. (them getting stuck i would lay at the feet of a game bug and not intentional design)In summery, I personally would call the game ok. It has a few interesting elements and only really 1 new idea to bring to the table. Without mod support the game will very likely fade into obscurity unless there are some pretty drastic improvements to make the game more interesting and replayable.

_childDocuments_.review: My review is neutral, but more on the no than yes side for now. For clarification, my example game I use as the base line when evaluating management style games is Oxygen Not Included.The reason why I've decided to not recommend the game is the following:- The UI is not intuitive- The management side is made hard by not having clean overviews. I want to have an overview that is easy to use + provides at a quick glance what you need to invest in to make your cult + cultists thrive.- The misson tab is overwhelming with whats on the screen, but its very unclear what certain missions provide- The mission tab, when assigning a cultists does not show what impact certain cultists have over others. Only the success % changes when I click around on a few of them.- The skills are confusing and it's unclear what to focus on (prioritize)- It's not easy to assign cultists to certain roles because again, the interface + skills are not intuitive- The way the research tree has been set up is not logical to me. Stuff like better toilets + bedrooms should be moved to earlier in the tree, to ensure cultists stay happy/healthy (no heat early on). Perhaps adding another branch to the tree which solely focusses on the cultists needs might help?- There is a lot of text, but all this text does not make things any clearer- Cultist management tab is not helpful at all. I'm resorted to having to click on each cultists separately, which is not great- Cannot save your custimized cult settings (appearance). So I have to keep recreating it when I want to restart . Would be great to save a custom template.- When you demolish/delete something, you do not get your money back- There is no undo button- The toilet mechanic makes no sense to me. It feels like you have to build a toilet next to every room to ensure your cultists don't pee their pants

_childDocuments_.review: It's lacking a lot of qol that would make it fun. Premise? fun. Style? fun. Story elements? mostly fun.Research balance is very wack; there are major qol features that simply aren't in the game; there's only really one way of building your cult due to the debuffs you receive late game. There's no storage for items you collect, you simply have to sell them and repurchase them (I say repurchase because when you unlock new items in missions where you're told "you found this item :)" you still have to purchase the item. You find 1 copy of that item which you can then buy. It's ♥♥♥♥. lol.) if you don't want to individually take items from one side of your cult to the other; there's no way to get rid of the AWFUL and horrendously un-fun debuffs you get at the end of the game that require you to do certain things to provide for your followers... including some that are contradictory (like needing multiple bathrooms AND requiring that all rooms be above a certain prestige level)... and the debuffs are the same every run. Quirks are only negative - who thought of that ♥♥♥♥ idea? why not instead of "acolyte gets a bad mood if near X" you could get a quirk that was "acolyte gets good mood if not near X"? That would be effectively the same mechanic, but it wouldn't feel like the game was punishing me for literally everything that I do. Which, now that I'm phrasing it that way, is pretty much what the entire game feels like it's doing. There is very, very few things that feel like bonus that are just nice to have - all of the things that are supposed to be bonuses feel like they're a requirement for not having to struggle 70% of the game, or they just feel like ♥♥♥♥. If you're reading this and decide that it still sounds like you might have fun: A - lol and good luck, but more importantly B - just play on the easier settings. I've done 3 play throughs for the 3 different finale achievements, and the harder difficulties are actually harder, sure, but because they game forces you to play the same way regardless, I'd say the difference is mostly equivalent to a boss fight where the only change between easy and hard is that the boss has 3x the health. Don't play it. If the devs make a miraculous return, rebalance much of the game, remove the debuffs and/or otherwise fix them, fix a LOT of qol moments, and allow more options in gameplay (as it is, there's exactly one way you can play this game, with 3 different flavours and technically "6" endings (2 per flavour).)Also the achievement for earning 100k influence is bugged. idk what it's measuring, but it's telling me I've only earned 51k, when I have, in fact beaten the game 3 times, and earned several hundred thousand influence at this point. When I was first looking at the achievements on my first play through and comparing them, I have something like 60K influence 70% of the way through that run.  I'm counting this as 100%'d. I'm uninstalling it and then going to pretend I've never heard of this game before.Also it's late, sorry about the walls of text. This game isn't even worth me trying to make it more readable.TD;DR: don't. If you do, play on "easy" (see explanation in the wall somewhere). But more seriously, don't do this to yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun resource management game that sucks you in and will have you playing for hours without feeling like time has passed. The game became more difficult as it went on in terms of gaining influence and maintaining it. I started playing right as this game was released in early access so it's still rough around the edges and has room to improve but it was a good first impression that had me obsessively playing away for days! Hope this becomes a cult favorite, pun intended! If you like resource management games, you'll probably like this one. It takes a dark subject and takes a wacky spin on it that still depicts the dark aspects of an unfortunate reality.Pros:- fun resource management- wacky style and music- light-hearted satire- fast start - easy to make money in gameCons:- research and maintaining influence in later game becomes grueling- missing 1 or 2 sermons in game can cause you to fall into negative faith and makes it difficult to recover from- not enough negative consequences for your actions, even police raids feel more like a minor nuisance than an actual threat to your livelihood- follower cap feels nonsensical to me, why would a cult based on making more money restrict its number of followers? If the goal is to make more money, shouldn't they want as many followers as they can get?- Cult leader feels practically useless outside of sermons and divine inspirations. As for the cult aspects of the game, I like that the game overall portrays the cult you run as a money making scam. True real life cults are best categorized using the BITE model (behavioral control, information control, thought control, and emotion control), and I would like more controlling aspects of this to appear in the game in the future. The game approaches the darker aspects with a wacky pizzazz - you're taking financial advantage of your followers, your recruits are isolated and alienated from their families, you recruit and discard your cultists as assets instead of as people, your followers will steal and vandalize in their missions for the good of the cult, you can even sacrifice your followers later in the game. Those are real things that can happen in cults, yes, but I would like to see More cult aspects in the future involving the followers. Things that I would like to see in the future with this game to make the cult more cult-like (these aren't requirements for me to enjoy the game, these are just suggestions to give more cult aspects that reflect the real life counterparts): -Having a reward and punishment system for recruits and followers to maintain control would make sense, as well as the possible ability for recruits to start families while within the cult and have a cult-ran school to have children grow up indoctrinated by the cult. -Have the option to ban or encourage specific kinds of clothing and entertainment for your followers and recruits. -Add missions involving slandering ex-followers, as well as add more consequences for dismissing longtime recruits and followers. -Add undercover agents that infiltrate the cult to try and destabilize it and rescue people from the cult. -Add missions involving cultists committing violent acts for the leader. -Add the ability to give titles and hierarchical roles to the recruits so that they can be managed better. -Add one or more initiation ceremonies such as baptisms or confirmations. -Add the option to re-invite ex-members back into the cult if they still hold faith aka allow some ex-members to still be brainwashed and want back in. -Add missions to spread cult propaganda or establish auxiliary churches in other locations that follow your cult. Basically add missions involving door-knocking and evangelism.Hope to see this game improve and expand as the developers update it! Hope this review is helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: Mindnumbing. The cult theme is just a half-baked skin on top of this simple Prison Architect clone. There's very little here that even feels cult-y besides being able to dress your people and customize the name of your cult/idol/deity. That's something that happens in the start screen, and after that, the theme mostly drops in place of a very basic retail management game. Progress is slowly doled out exclusively through adherence to the tired "research" trope, and research is essentially the only currency in the game that matters. The game is so poorly paced that every night consists of 12 in-game hours of watching your characters sleep or maybe you'll get to send them on off-screen missions like it's a Facebook game from 2008. Because such missions are nearly worthless in favor of research, up to the mid-game where you need them to 'reduce heat', you'll spend half of every in-game day just staring at the screen waiting for night to end.The game markets itself on being scandalous in theme, but nothing provocative happens in the game besides the appearance of a facility designed to mock spiritualism. The tutorial opens and closes with a 'hilarious' squid costume cult getting arrested for 'being brainwashed.' Compare that to the jaw-dropping opening of Prison Architect's double-homicide scene, and you realize this game is a cheap cash-in appealing to Streamers and Youtubers. 'Huhu, I made a cult and named it after myself. My community is a cult! It's a joke I came up with!'The one thing going for this game is it's pretty chill. If you just want to watch numbers tick up on three-speed for the illusion of progress, this is great. Otherwise, it's certainly not worth the retail or even the sale price. If my child made this I'd be very impressed, but a team of grown adults should be able to do something better than carbon copying an already popular formula and then dumbing-it-down close to oblivion.

_childDocuments_.review: So coming to this after playing very briefly immediately after its early access launch and being burnt out on early access games in general I was excited to see the full 1.0 product release. A cult-themed "colony builder" like Rimworld/Dwarf Fortress/etc. sounded fantastic and I was hopeful to play a great one of those with some direction to the gameplay. Unfortunately, what I played was a boring plate spinner management game without much substance that drags itself out.The first and primary issue is largely my fault, I came into this anticipating it to be a sort of colony game like Rimworld or similar, and this game is actually only like that on the surface. Instead, it's more akin to a management builder like Rollercoaster Tycoon or any of those where the building is in service to and very limited by the actual overall progression of the game. To that end, most of the cultists and followers you get are disposable by design and that's fine, that's actually in the spirit of a cult. But it lends itself to making a substantial part of the game just checking boxes and raising numbers on someone you actually don't care about and undermines the personal aspect of the title.Beyond that, the management itself is dull, shallow, and also drawn out to a massive degree. The numbers go up slowly, the requirements to unlock things keep needing larger numbers which take forever to achieve, and there's little to actually worry about. There's the notion of running out of any of the resources you need or possibly accruing too much negative attention in the form of 'heat,' but I never actually had any of these matter in the course of the game. Instead, even playing on the fastest speed for the overwhelming majority of the game it still claimed twelve to thirteen hours of my time and I would have left satisfied and happy if it was half of that.The cult aspect is also pretty undeveloped. The brief tutorial intro shows a neat compound and shows followers and cultists and also hints at possible different types or evolutions by joking about one of them mid-transformation into a fish person. However, it ends up that there's very little to the actual cult beyond what you see at first glance with nothing beneath. There are some silly rooms and you can dress your cult up in various different ways but beyond the thematic aspect of running a cult there's almost nothing to it.Honey, I Joined a Cult is, on the surface, a fantastic concept and a great themed game. But in execution it comes up woefully short and lacking, leaving you spinning plates you've already mastered for several hours after you've seen and experienced all there is to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the game for the last few days, and put in about 10ish hours or so. If you're looking for a full game, I'd recommend against buying right now. But there's not only great potential here, but the developers (a two man team, it sounds like) have done a good job at adding whimsy and humor to the game. The mechanics have been thought out pretty well, and as content gets added, I'd wager that this will be a pretty great game. I ran into a few minor bugs. When I was trying to put the foundation down for a new building, I'd extended it out and was about to let it build when the "worship" window popped up from the nightly worship thing. When I closed the window out, the foundation wasn't there, but the money it would have cost was gone. That's a hard bug to catch, so I wouldn't be surprised if that got through a QA shop for a larger team. Also, the maintenance system seems wonky on occasion. Sometimes a member won't automatically go fix a thing, ever, and you have to manually have someone do it. It can become a pain to manually direct that over and over again. I very much look forward to more content as this goes along, and would encourage folks out there to consider buying it to support the developer. And if it's not in the roadmap already, I'd encourage the developers to add a mod system so that we can add content on our own volition as well. Great job to the dev team, and keep up the good work.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting building and management game.In short, it's something similar to Prison Architect, however you manage a cult in the 1970s rather than a prison in the 1980s. You have a lot of customization options and a decently large area for your compound. You make money from your followers via therapy rooms, and your cultists act as staff members. You need to keep track of your cultists' needs, as if they get too low their mood goes down. If hunger gets too low they can even start taking damage. If a cultist's mood gets too low they can suffer a Mood Break, which basically means they go a bit looney and have to vent in the middle of the road for a few in-game hours. They can even leave entirely.There are also things to research and missions to go on. You do have to be mindful with the missions though: cultists can be arrested if things go poorly. The game does tell you the chance of success when you select someone to send though so you can easily avoid mission failure. Doing most missions generates heat however, with the only exception being the missions that remove heat. Heat does go down over time, too. Heat generally represents the amount of negative attention your cult is getting. If it gets too high, people will start protesting and you'll get police investigations. It has a cap of 1000 though, so I'm pretty sure you can afford to be a little risky.Also, construction. One of the main bits of the game. The mechanics are pretty much what you'd expect: you can build walls, foundations, doors, assign rooms, and put objects down. Things are built immediately too, no need to wait. One tip though: don't mess up. Removing objects doesn't give you a refund and demolishing walls and foundations costs money. It kinda makes sense realistically but its not what you'd expect in a video game. Also, there's no planning tool.Overall though, I would very much recommend this game if you're a fan of games like the previously mentioned Prison Architect. Even if it does somethings differently.Also, for my fellow Linux users: this game works great under Proton!

It starts with a disgraced cult leader escaping getting plastic surgery, and thus forming a new cult, which you run. _childDocuments_.review: At it's core, Honey, I Joined a Cult seems to be a business management sim.  Collect employees, level them up, and put them in places where their talents will be most useful.  I appreciated that it's going for some more complexity here, and it seems to want to focus on a more manageable group of individuals but ... well, the whole cult thing is pretty much just the framing device.  Yeah, you are running a cult.  Whether or not the game is going to hold your attention I think depends on whether or not that joke is enough to carry it for you.  It reminded me more of Academia: School Simulator than Prison Architect, ie: more emphasis on a business simulation than intertwined systems interacting.My play time here was pretty short and it is in early access, but I don't know that I can blame all my concerns on it simply being unfinished.  I think they have their core loop pretty well finished: build rooms, research new ones. That's the problem: the reason I can't recommend is because a game about building a cult doesn't make me want to build a cult.  Your involvement outside of research and new buildings felt pretty minimal, and I guess I just didn't see what the payoff was expected to be.  I appreciated that it seemed to have an actual progression curve (many games seem to skip this), but disliked the slow pace, hands-off building, and arbitrary feeling it has.  Make rooms you need, wait for money to come in.Again, the joke is in the title.  I assume they'll tighten things up during early access but there is no guarantee that is the case, in which case I have to judge it on what it is and right now I think it's problems are deeper than missing content.  If anything, I applaud it for having it's entire game loop on display.  Still, that shows me it's not what I enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent if flawed management game. It certainly gets some things right. The customisation of the cult is fun. There are an array of traits and quirks to help your cultists stand out. Information is readily accessible, and though the tables can get a bit busy, the tooltips help to clarify details. What really holds it back is a lack of polish and balance. As to the former, typos are rife and I experienced the occasional crash. The latter is more fundamental. It's strangely easy once you get your cult going. I had a single mood break, zero deaths, zero cultists choosing to leave and a handful of protests in my 18-hour game. However, there is a long mid-game grind as your leader slowly tries to gather points to unlock the finale. With my resources at max and no other real issues to deal with, I wound up spending hours with the game mostly running in the background.  The game does try to impart some artificial difficulty by adding random debuffs every once in a while. These were largely ignorable, but could be frustrating when a couple of them combined to be unavoidable - case in point penalties to mood both if a toilet was not private and if a room was of low prestige, the only solution to which is to build a bunch of lavish rooms consisting of a single toilet and a lot of decorative items, or cop a regular penalty.It is good enough for a ten or so hour run, but overstays its welcome through the grind. Worth joining for a while, but not worth drinking the Kool-Aid for.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw some of the reviews that complained about it being boring, but I assumed they just didn't like games in this genre.I never got to the point of figuring out if they were correct, because right when I started to reach a point where it could get interesting, I was hit with an "event" called Shifting Realities. Here's what it does: it rolls a die randomly and injures one of your cultists, and it keeps doing this for something like 72 hours. By the time I was a third of the way through the event, about 75% of my cult was sidelined--some with multiple injuries. I was STILL in the tutorial phase of the game when this crap hit me.There's no counter play, the event is exceptionally long, it's unpredictable, and it does tremendous damage to your progress because the injuries last SO long.So I can't even tell you if the game gets repetitive/boring, because this kind of game design meets a level of disrespect I don't think players should have to deal with. That's not fun--not even the sort of !!!FUN!!! you experience in games like Dwarf Fortress.Take a pass on this game. It will only frustrate you. I was so pissed I went and put the entire developer and publisher on ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of the game, the humor is silly and the game has solved some typical management game issues in good ways (your cult members will get up in the night and get a snack if they're hungry, pretty smart little fellows). I firmly believe this is going to be a great game with some more work.But I have to say, right now it almost feels kind of empty. Don't get me wrong, there's quite a few rooms to research and build. But there's no fun objectives. The unspoken objective is to grow rich, which seems a bit too easy, and to grow your cult, which seems a bit pointless (since everything runs smoothly with just a few members and followers). Not even the slightest 'if you want to unlock this you need x amount of members/followers'. It even starts really nicely with an introduction story, but the story is abruptly cut off and the game basically says 'do whatever you want now'.There's a few things that still need to be ironed out and that's completely understandable for an early access game. There's a warning if a cult member is starving but if their health is declining for other reasons the game won't tell you. To change the sermon type you need an altar, yet the altar can neither be purchased nor researched. Moving, deleting and upgrading objects still feels a bit clunky. All completely fixable things.In short, the game is on a good way, it's just not there yet for me.

_childDocuments_.review: In Honey, I Joined a Cult, you play a Prison Architect-esque management-tycoon game where you're in charge of running a cult, managing its gradual expansion while trying to keep under the radar of both the general public and law enforcement. It largely plays the same as Prison Architect, but focuses more mood management; in that sense it plays more akin to Rimworld.I do not want to dissuade people or the devs too much as I enjoyed the game for what it is, but as it stands at the moment, there is a solid base for gameplay however there are some glaring concerns that affect my otherwise glowing review of the game.The first is that it seems a bit  sandboxy, in the sense that after you play for a bit, it ends up feeling samey. It's open-endedness with being able to "create your own cult" does not lend to its uniqueness from playthrough to playthrough. Perhaps having a campaign of some sort with unique scenarios will help in improving this aspect, as playing the standard sandbox mode ends up feeling repetitive with, to be fair, some changes depending on which "path" you take for divine inspirations (which could be thought of as overarching themes for your cult). Additionally, having more events or more dynamic pawns akin to Rimworld would make it more unique per playthrough, but perhaps that may be asking too much at the moment given the current state. Hopefully this will be improved in the future.The second is that the AI seems... absentminded? For example, the AI will wander around while working doing nothing as there is work to be done, then decide "Oh, this needs to be fixed" then walk over to it, and repeat. It was beginning to get annoying to see two of my maintenance Watchers idle around while there were 6-8 broken items that needed to be fixed, sometimes requiring manual intervention on my end to get them to fix something. I hope that this will be improved in future patches.My final complaint is how hygiene works. My understanding is that washing a pawn's hands after using the toilet only grants a  at cleaning the pawn. Which severely increases the likelihood of a Watcher getting injured from poor hygiene, especially in early game. It's really frustrating to see injuries created from eating without washing hands, akin to Rimworld's "ate without table" debuff. This should certainly be switched to a bar like Mood or Health, with the differing tiers of sinks offering faster filling of the hygiene, a higher maximum of the hygiene bar, or something similar. At least in this way, it puts some control back into the player's hands about how they should handle hygiene, rather than making it pure RNG about whether or not someone will get an illness from poor hygiene.Now, the final verdict. Is it worth ~20 USD/23 CAD off-sale? At this point, I would say yes. There's enough content to last a dedicated player about 12-15 hours per playthrough. Despite my grievances about the game, I did enjoy it for what it was and I am excited to see what they'll be able to do in the future, with my main hope being the implementation of a campaign mode. Unfortunately, I have not played Rimworld Ideology yet so I do not have a frame of reference to compare the two.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty fun when I started but the further you progress there are a lot of annoying bugs.I've read other reviews and although I didn't experience any bugs that may hinge my progression, it was still annoying to deal with.1.) Every once and a while when trying to complete missions the menu for your characters would bug out and would not open up. Or what I usually like to do is send one on a mission then preselect characters for another mission I cannot open the window again even if i select the little pencil indicating to edit the characters chosen. The only viewable windows are the mission screen and the map. This will happen pretty frequently which is annoying because I can't get missions done for that day. I would try to save and quit and come back but it would only seem to reset when the next missions would load up for the next day.2.) If you have characters who have multiple jobs set to high priority your characters will bug out and run in circles bc they don't know where to go. Even trying to manually select the character and clicking on a job or action to override would not work. They would continue to cycle on a circle until the "calendar shift" you set for them would change. For example one of my characters was suppose to assign themselves a job. However, they were running around in circles as if they didn't know what job to do. Tried to select a job to override but it would not change anything. They finally stopped running around in circles once his "work time" on the calendar was changed to "free time" then they went to go do things like use the toilet and go to the rec room. Now this could hinge possibly hinge your gaming experience like causing a mood break for a character because I had this happen on a separate occasion. One of my characters was on break but then was circling around not knowing what to do first eat or toilet. I tried to select one and same thing happened -- could not override they finally shifted schedules on calendar by that time they had a mood break.3.) This just recently happened but all characters in my game are now bald. Which doesn't bother me or effects the game play experience in any way. However, being a visual learner I remember who my characters are and what skill sets they have based on their appearance first then I check the name (because some can look the same) But now that their physical differences are all bugged out and they all look like clones its difficult for me to differentiate who is who to, to send to a job that needs to be done so I would have to pull up the menu with the characters are go through the skill tree and figure it out that way.This isn't a bug but something for the developers to think about.1.) It's really annoying that selling objects and deleting walls does not give us a gain back in money. You basically just lose out on that money and it's really annoying when you're a beginner and starting off early. As you progress a little further money won't be an issue but before for the people playing the game for the first time I would wait to start building complex rooms too early on where you might have to modify later. Because if you decide you don't like the design or want to redo it deleting walls or redoing outdoor flooring will start tacking up if you don't know how to make money at first. Example: I started off building the bedroom and making little "cubicles" for all of my characters which I kept having to redesign because I didn't place the room in a good spot to begin with.All in all, this game is a pretty fun time waster but with especially the bugs that I've come across and the inconvenience of a few aspects of the game that you keep learning about as you go (obviously not talking about game challenges, but the user functions provided for you on the game) just makes it a little more less appealing to play the more progress I make.

_childDocuments_.review: As a management sim, the game is ok - it's fairly basic: you manage the well being of cultists and followers, working hours and jobs based on your cultists' skill points and quirks. You manage the overall fame and infamy of the cult. In time, you unlock research and rooms to progress down a major cult theme. For the first 1/2 of the game, it's quite fun learning the mechanics, unlocking new rooms.. but then the game grinds to a slow crawl to death as you realise there's not much more to the game. Once you have all the rooms unlocked, you realise the game just throws a bunch of the same things at you to gate your progress to slightly improve each room while you work towards finishing your cult. Firstly, the game really needs a x5, x10, x30 speed mode. Secondly, what's the reason for limiting the number of research rooms I can build? Thirdly, there needs more variety to earn unique cult points (sending 4 cultists on a 30 hour job to earn +5 Darkness is ridiculously slow progression).Unfortunately, despite the 3 cults having slightly different mechanics to each other - the difference and core feedback loop doesn't encourage me to continue to play this game. As you can see from Global Achievement Stats only 0.8% of players have completed the game on each of the major cults. It means that most players won't be bothered 100% achievement hunt this - it's a boring slog. Would be much better if they implemented higher fast-forwards.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Joined a Cult is a fun game in which you build a cult in the hopes of gaining faith, enlightenment, and of course copious amounts of money from your followers. The game has a minimalist artistic design in which characters are moving across a grid and not being directly controlled. Think of Rimworld or Prison Architect. The gameplay is engaging and the theme of cults makes it that much more fun to play with and watch play out before you.  The game intrigued me because it resembled Rimworld, one of my favorite games. The game has many similarities but is not as big of a sandbox in comparison. You have rooms that you can build and items that are associated with them directly. You can edit the schedules of each cultist, which is helpful, some missions come in the night. If you like Rimworld you will find a warm familiar feeling playing this.  I like the organization of the pop up screens and how things like missions and the building menu, as well as character details frame the screen when you need to look at them while still focusing on the center of the screen. This was great for building and trying to look at multiple people, moving around, etc. The UI in general is attractive and pleasing to the eyes. The filter menu really helps navigate and build rooms without having to scroll through pages of items. Very nice quality of life inclusion. The settings menu does not offer much control other than standard basic controls, but does have a night time performance mode in the graphics settings if that happens to be valuable to you. The game is quite funny and brilliant in design and scratches that itch of wanting more games in a similar vein of Rimworld. Building is simple and everything is well organized and the tutorial does a good job of setting you on the right path towards acquiring more followers to your cult. I enjoy that I can play this casually while listening to a podcast or music, being able to multitask adds value in management games for me. I absolutely love this game and I look forward to seeing it evolve with the roadmap the devs have planned. Dang good!

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I'm in love. The way you manage your members' needs is similar to that of the Sims, and the pixel art brings back memories of Stardew. I also adore the concept of trying to create a successful(?) cult in a humorous, self aware way.I will say, there's a few bugs I've noticed so far, and while they aren't game breaking, they're definitely a bit irritating when you have limited funds.1. When I tried to turn paths back into grass with a line, it spends the money but doesn't change. I had to do each individual square in order for it to work.2. At one point I attempted to create a new foundation that was rather large (around $300). Once again, it spent my money but there was no foundation to be seen. This was especially frustrating because it was about an hour and a half into gameplay, so I didn't have a whole lot of money to work with.3. Sometimes, when trying to change a follower's job, they'll just continue to do their current job and ignore the reassignment. I will say, however, it could have been my fault for accidentally assigning them to something I told them to ignore, but it's happened with three different followers from what I can recall.Like I said, these bugs aren't game breaking, and I'm only bringing them up for the benefit of the devs! I know you all are a small team, so I wanted to make you both aware in case you weren't. I look forward to future updates and many more hours of gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: The game developer hates you. I don't know how else to explain some of the atrocious design decisions they've made here. It's essentially a simplified version of Rimworld, but somehow the devs have made the interface harder to use even though they have less systems. Rooms are a pain in the ass to manage because room specific furniture can't be placed anywhere except in that room, so if you want to do something like say switch the locations of two rooms, it's an absolute pain in the ass. First, you have to re-designate both rooms, and then, since each room is already filled to the brim with random crap, you're doing tetris to slowly switch the furniture of the two rooms when there's huge amounts of free space outside these rooms that you could use as a holding area but the game won't let you!Heat management is awful, there's only one real way to reduce heat which is heat reduction missions. The Ministry of Propaganda is counter-intuitive, you'd think that it reduces heat and increases PR, but no, it increases heat instead! This is so confusing that I've seen game guides claim you can use the Ministry of Propaganda to reduce heat.The game also doesn't autosave when you exit, and the sometimes prompts you to save first but if you say you want to save it doesn't create the save automatically, it just sends you back to the menu and you have to save manually and then try exiting the game again?? Have the devs played an actual video game before?It's clear the devs don't actually know what made Rimworld fun, they just re-skinned it while making the game more restrictive and removed all complexity from the game. Well, the more complex stuff was what made Rimworld good, without it the devs are struggling to come up with interesting game mechanics to keep the players interested in playing. Protests which are supposed to be this game's version of combat(?) I guess, are horrible and require way too much micro-management. Not to mention you don't even get rewarded after it! The heat reduction is minimal, you don't gain any influence from it, nor any items. It's just an annoying mechanic you're forced to interact with or be punished. At least Rimworld combat was both punishing and rewarding. A big raid also means lots of loot. Plus you could build your base to better manage raids, which places interesting design constraints in base building. In this game, which strips out the combat and only has base-building, you can't even design your base to better handle the negative events the game throws at you, heat management is literally a matter of not interacting with the game because all interesting game-play elements generate heat and the only way to reduce heat is one mission type that you only get one of a day, which for big cults is barely enough to manage the passive heat your cult generates.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, the reason I picked up this game is because I loved Cult of the Lamb and I wanted to try some other management games like it. I was drawn to HIJAC because of the groovy artstyle and the base building aspect, as well as the more "realistic" modern-day depiction of the Cult that would be a neat contrast to CoTL's fantasy cult. I was surprised that I was not, in fact, playing as the leader of the cult, which in hindsight was foreshadowing how little control I would have over the game. There is so much ♥♥♥♥ to manage that it's humanely impossible to keep track of it all. You need to keep track of every single minute detail, down to the schedules of each individual cultist. Speaking of, every single NPC in the game has their own set of stats that you need to keep track of and level up, which happens at a snails pace and makes them effectively useless for anything. The UI is clunky and ugly as sin, and each menu acts like a pop-up add that you have to manually close when you're done using, and each one takes up at least a third of the screen, making the game feel claustrophobic.The customization of the game is severely limited too. You don't even get to choose the theme of your cult until you've researched at least a dozen prerequisites beforehand, and in that time you're stuck with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ options for cult quality of life, the upgrades for which are locked behind grating waits for the research tree. This game is so unnecessarily complicated, with so many useless mechanics and micromanagement that it feels bloated and claustrophobic, with very little actually being accomplished, with incredibly long waits between stuff actually happening, even with in-game time being sped up. All in all, it's actually fitting that you don't get to play as the cult leader, because you're not the leader. You're not even the god. You're a grunt doing all the game's work for it, and seeing little to no returns for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game in its current early access state.  But like all early access titles, it suffers from balancing & technology progression issues (in terms of unlocking reasearch) as well as the lack of endgame content. For a few examples of lacking content: I can't see a use for the prison/cell doors than cosmetics, no upgrades for the canteen, people constantly getting sick from eating with "dirty hands", the cult being unable to grow their own food on the compound (become fully independent of society lol) or expand the compound to have more access to land to build on, etc...I hope it will mean something more in the future.  Fortunately, the clean aesthetically-pleasing UI and the core gameplay is so relaxing to play through and easy to get immersed in, it's given me all sorts of ideas and hopes for future updates.  Right now, I'm really keen on more missions/endgame content updates.  At the moment, the endgame is essentially a Doomsday cult but I hope to see some variance soon.  It would be pretty interesting for example, to build a cult before destroying the world and then continuing that cult in the post-apocalyptic wasteland.  Sigh...one can dream.

_childDocuments_.review: First 5 hours or so I had fun, maybe a bit longer than that then the boredom happened. I think it was around in game day 30 because I was around there when I went online to see how long this game was to decide if I was going to stick with it. The fast forwards isn't fast enough so I started watching something and playing this a bit in the background. I got to the point where I felt like I was progressing faster and it would make the game harder with little warning by adding new rules like walking into a room with less than a prestige level of 7 will give the characters negative stats... so I get to clutter up my Cult with a bunch of decorations to make it look stupid to improve the room levels. Some of the room levels refused to go up, do they count towards this? no idea, it's not explained. This is about the point where I slowly realized I do not like this game anymore. So later they impose negative modifier for my bedroom being below a comfy level. Well the bedroom is maxed at 50 prestige and no one likes it so I take it I should have unknowingly focused on the bedroom when researching stat upgrades long ago to improve the beds. Now it would be different if things progressively got harder or gradually these rule sets were put in and explained. Instead they were not, you are having an okay time then out of nowhere here is a permanent negative modifier to inconvenience you. So all my members started to leave the cult after that modifier. Played this game for 12 hours with no one leaving or issues, they throw in a random new rule with no warning and barely explained and I went from never having a cult member leave to all of them leaving over 3 days. Made it to day 85 before I closed the game. Was there something I could do different? That's why I give this a negative review, I didn't care enough to Google it to find out because I had just been going through the motions for an additional 5 hours and things never really got better after I started getting bored. It's not that old so maybe they will patch it to make me enjoy it more later. I didn't down right hate it but I would not recommend it as it is now.2 crashes, it has auto save. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, this is the second time I changed this review and Steam really needs a "Mixed" button - I didn't hate this game and can see other people having fun with it, it just started to bore me after a few hours. However the end-game is plain bad so I went with "Thumbs Down" in the end.So I really liked the idea of the game - creating a cult in the 70s - and a lot of the basics are done well. The design is cool, cult creation is a lot of fun and watching the money roll in while your cultists treat followers with pseudo-scientific procedures is pretty great. That fact that the creators added a few mini games is cool too since it breaks up the monotony thats an issue for titles like this sometimes.And this is were things start to get less fun. It's an idle game and a lot of the tasks you have to repeat aren't challenging or interesting. Repairing toilets, assigning cultists to missions, picking underwhelming research options etc. Best case scenario: Your cult runs like a well oiled machine and you dont have to do anything. I tried the game on a harder difficulty too but that didn't make it more challenging, just more annoying. The game is also not as complex as similar titles which isn't a huge deal but adds to the monotony.Speaking of monotony: The music is pretty underwhelming. As far as I can tell there are only two rather similar songs included. I only played for a few hours and can't bear those tunes any longer. Thats kinda frustrating since the setting and various cult options scream for more variety here. (What's weird is that there are 5 songs on the DLC soundtrack - maybe it's a bug, maybe they play later in the game, I dont know...)My biggest issue is that story and main objective weren't enough to motivate me. Unlike in other games you are not fighting for survival so the things you do often feel pointless. I didn't really care for my individual cultists either, even though I am usually a sucker for that kind of thing. They have very little backstory and I've never seen them interact with one another. Thats kinda sad and a feature like that would have gone a long way.However, I was curious about the path my cult would take and that motivated me to keep playing. And while that wasn't ideal to begin with - I didnt keep playing because it was huge fun or I cared about my cult - the ending was just horrible. The game starts to throw annoying stuff at you and adds pointless tasks to prolong the finale. Whats even more annoying is that it doesn't play out on screen, there isnt even a cutscene. You just press a button and the game ends - what a letdown!In short: If you really dig the setting and enjoy idle games in general chances are you'll have some fun with this one too. (If you'll get your moneys worth depends on your personal budget I guess...) But there are games with better mechanics and more variety out there so I wouldnt recommend it if its not right down your alley to begin with. Also the end game is pretty horrific and you just feel like you've wasted a lot of time in the end...

Save before you choose a theme Yes, the 100k influence is quite a grind No No No No No, you can play on the easiest difficulty NoHoney, I Joined a Cult is an awesome tycoon kinda game in which you run a cult and try to keep your inner circle believing in what you say, but also get more followers to get more money and influence. And if that isn't enough, you try to keep the heat as low as possible otherwise people will start to demonstrate before your building and that will not do any good for the mood of the people in your inner circle. I love this kind of unique theme. I enjoy building theme parks/ hospitals and things like that, but those more unusual ones just feel refreshing. It is nice to explore this kind of themes and what to do different. Here it made sense to send your people on missions to reduce the heat or get more pr so higher quality people want to join your cult. And having to hold ceremonies every 24h to keep your people believe in you made sense as well. It took me a bit to get used to the game, not everything was clear at once. The game does a good job of trying to explain everything but quite a lot is happening, so I didn't memorize everything from the tutorial at the beginning. I would recommend doing the tutorial at the beginning, as that also is an easy way to get the achievement for holding a 5-star Sermon. What I also liked was that the game told me how to get influence when it recognized that I struggled with that a bit.  A few things I would love to see in the game are a few more Quality of Life features. For example, you have to order ingredients for your cook to make food. I would love to see a button to just order everything to max capacity at the top o the screen, or the highest quality food at the top, now those are on the bottom, which means you have to scroll down every time you have to order food. Kinda the same thing with the followers, later on, you get options to see the quality of the followers, but those where you can see the information from in the followers menu are at the bottom, so again you have to scroll down. A way to be able to send away multiple people from your inner circle (aka Watchers) or followers without having to open their menu and send them away and then open the main menu again for the next one would also be a welcome addition. These are all small things but would make the game a lot more friendly in my opinion. The achievements are mostly what you expect in a management/tycoon kind of game like this. Get an X amount of all the different resources. Get good quality people, place decor items, and more things like that. There is an achievement for losing the game, this is easily done by turning off the vending food and don't make your Watchers any food. There are achievements for the ending with each theme and there are 3 themes in total. For those achievements I would highly recommend waiting with selecting a theme very late in the game so you have unlocked all the other stuff and have a nice cult, then make a save which you only use to restart and choose the other themes when done with one theme. The game only has a few save slots, so be very careful to not save over that one save slot you used for this.

_childDocuments_.review: So when I first heard about this game back in 2018 I was thinking it sounds like a right laugh, I was anticipating this release and couldn't wait. The dissapointment to see that even after 3 years of development that it comes to steam in "Early Access". After playing about an hour of this game I can see why it is in Early Access... what have the developers been doing those 3 years? I will not accept the pandemic being an excuse as this game was a year in development before that hit. With a publisher like Team17 behind them I would have thought they would have had a better time getting this out faster with some extra support? Obviously not.About the game itself...You build a base to house your cult, you keep the needs and wants up to make sure that all is well and you don't get caught by the police, you build rooms to provide services to get money and eventually recruit new members to your cult. Yeah.. pretty basic formula really.You can rename a lot of the bits and bobs, like the cult name, who they worship ect.. but thats really about it, its the same no matter which way you look at it. So "insert cult name here" is pretty much the only customisation you can do, the way you build the areas really doesn't seem to vary much, there seems to be only 1 way to play it. Build room A, bring in some money, research room B, build it, bring in some money, research room C... ect..ect...ectThis game needs more customisation, There needs to be an inbuilt editor to allow people to design their own idols, and/or at least Steam Workshop to allow modding. I don't know just doesn't seem as good as other games I have played that are like this before. Maybe I hyped it up in my mind too much thinking this was going to be the best "base builder management" game I have ever played, The fact it was cults gave it that comedic effect but it seems to have fallen short of actually being funny.Maybe wait for it to be discounted, I am sure it will feature on a Humble Bundle or Choice at some point - as a lot of these games seem to do - I got my copy through Humble with the 20% discount, and even then I still feel I have paid too much for this game.The plus side though from what I have seen of the game so far it seems well made, there doesn't seem to be many bugs or any real issues I have come across personally (not saying there isn't any just I havent seen them)I may give this another go when it is further in development, or when it comes out of Early Access, but if its taken 3 years to get here then I estimate I will see you all in another 3 years to update this review? But for now if you are after a game like this Prison Architect seems to have a lot more going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is kinda cool, but there are two things that really bug me about it.1. I dislike how foundations, walls, etc, just "magically appear" once you pay money to have them built, and it's all instant.  This game is similar closer to Prison Architect and RimWorld in the top-down art and genre, but even both those games required stuff to actually be built.  I'd really like to see them handle this better, but this in itself is not enough of a reason to not buy the game (it's early access, after all), but I guess I expected something better despite that).  Maybe they could hire workers who they pay with $$ until they can recruit enough workers who run on faith instead?  Who knows... but I don't like how it is right now.2. The influence mechanic makes no sense to me.  You use influence to research stuff (huh?).  And what can you research?  Well, more followers and members, sure... that part makes sense.  But that's less than 10% of the research tree.  I need influence just so I have the right to buy a toilet//bed/kitchen/whatever and until then, I have to sleep in a bag or poop in a bucket?  Really?  It's like the devs said "We need a tech tree cause all good games have tech trees" and yet couldn't figure out how to fit it in with a cult concept properly.  Considering this is such a significant part of the game, this is the main reason I can't recommend the game.Other than that, it's an okay game and you're getting what you think you're getting.Edit: So some dev said "hey... we've made some changes on our beta build..." so I went reading thru the patch notes, and see nothing related.  While some devs seem to really read reviews and take them to heart, I'm not sure these guys are one.  Maybe their discord community is better?

_childDocuments_.review: Really winds me up people leave a negative review on an early access game that has been out for literal days. Do you people not understand early access? One negative review starts with "Still needs a lot of work" - well done Sherlock. ITS EARLY ACCESS.Actual review - Really solid base to build off. Excited to see where this goes. Graphically it is a similar style to Prison Architect, a bit less similar to Rim World but in the same style as these games. Personally i'm quite a fan of this style. I would say so far it is most similar to Prison Architect in terms of gameplay. You build rooms, recruit followers & staff, and try to make money while keeping heat down. Buildings automatically appear when placed instead of any construction time. There are some great lines the followers speak when moving around. And they each have their own stats and traits too.Looking forward to seeing what is added. Depth is required across the gameplay loops. I agree with those who say they would like more "cult" related things. Very much a base simulator with a cult theme rather than being cult focused at the moment.I do like the missions and the "world" map, looking forward to more interaction and maybe more freedom to pick places on the map to send recruits with different outcomes, rather than being told the location?Some gameplay notes for the developers, should they read this:A softlock in the tutorial while placing down the 3 decor items in which I couldnt place the third one, but reloaded and worked fine after that. Sure that will be fixed in no time.Early game was good, lots to unlock and discover and was fun watching the followers use the rooms. Didnt find it too dificult though, just had to be patient for money. I would say that certain things break down far, far too quickly (bathroom objects) and the mechanics behind the janitors doesnt really make sense. They should be prioritising broken things. Because they go room to room cleaning, some days they dont have time to make it across the compound before running out of time and the broken items are not fixed and compound. Manually controlling the staff can fix this, but can be a pain.I would also say that there is balancing required around the number of followers you start with (less) and staff (more) to make the game a bit harder. I found I had not enough staff to operate all the therapies and modules, but i had over 100k in the bank come the mid game. Also, heat should be increased as i found it easy to hover around the 100 mark.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.
