_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin... The game itself is fun, it's... fine. There are a lot of issues I see with it though after doing a first play through. First of all if furniture is near a door when you're placing it it'll delete that furniture item without warning, and that open space that it's registering the door to interfere with is MUCH larger than reasonable. I had flowers lined along a wall and it deleted all the decor items when I placed an entrance. It does the same thing if you delete walls near items and that can really bite when you've got a several thousand dollar item against a wall you need to expand. Continuing on, a way to skip the tutorial at least after your first play-through would be nice. Taking nearly 2.5 hours just to get through that part up to the leaders sanctum again is really annoying. The end of sermon screen does not need to be that intrusive and it could wait at least until I've set down my items or the building to pop up instead of messing up the task I was working on. One area where I feel like I could have used a little more instruction and reminder of mechanics would have been the first protest in my game, reminding how to get the characters to interact with things instead of leaving me confused as it said to interact but with everything else so automatized I never really had to encourage my cult members to do anything that wasn't the protests and forgot the command until hovering over it. Font size increase would be a big step in the right direction for the lacking accessibility options, a lot of the buttons are really small and I'm not sure if it was a glitch or not sometimes when I'd have to change tabs to be able to select something but that mixed with small buttons made it really annoying sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this title I was imagining some kind of "play house" but in a cult setting, maybe building some sort of bonds between the different NPCs, but really this is more about optimizing the little working ants in your cult. By deciding which kind of perks and buffs you prefer in your little sea of workers you can kick people out and convince other to join as you go through out the game.With four currencies you slowly build your cultist following from scratch and try to gain as little heat as bossible, heat being something of the bad reputation your following aquire through time - but ofcourse there are ways to reduce this increasing heat by PR-campagins and pilgrimage.About 4-5 hours into the game I got the gist of it and started to really enjoy what was going on, continuesly through the coming game sessions I got a deeper understanding of this strategy game and I would rather call it an optimizing resource management than a simulator. _childDocuments_.review: As I sunk over 40 hours into this game I have to admit it's entertaining enough.tl;drBasically it should be in early-access. I really enjoyed the game but it has plenty of problems and even if it had any replayability (which it has not) I wouldn't put myself through it again unless there was a mayor QoL overhaul.**Review**It leaves almost no replayability after you did a run, besides "seeing" the different endings which is basically a matter of choosing button A or button B at one point.The game is clearly inspired by Prison Architect and Rimworld, and really does a great job mixing them.A severe lack of QoL components and the above mentioned issue of replayability make me believe this was barely tested and I constantly find myself fighting against the game trying to do what I would assume is natural tasks in this game.Your cultists have traits, and with these traits comes proficiency to work certain rooms. It's a nightmare trying to keep track of what cultist is set to work what room, what traits they need and sifting through possible followers to recruit as cultists that would complement which cultists I already have. All this information is available to you just not at the same time so there's a barrage of menu-swapping, hoovering for tool-tips and comparing in order to make any kind of decisions.Cultists are also very needy and want their rooms to have a certain standard. The way to do that is by decorating the rooms with items that you mostly find when out on missions. Here's one of the biggest QoL issues, there's a ton of categories of decoration, that makes sense from an actual decorators point of view ('rugs', 'lights', 'paintings' and the more confusing 'decor' and 'ornament'). But there's no easy way to find the "best" items without scrolling through each menu and there's hundreds of items.The game is not hard and I don't think you can actually loose without actively trying, there's some values to keep track of like "faith" that replenishes to a point each day but depletes during the course of the day depending on how good your cultists are. This is actually a neat mechanic to make sure the player is playing "the right way", I can't explain it better but it's a good  thing.Other values are there only to slow down the player and to rack up hours (as in my situation) namely "heat" that's something that adds up each time you do missions (which are needed to improve your cult in various ways) along with more sinister activites and you don't need much of it for things to go south so the heat have to be kept under control (there's ways to reduce it) but this limits what you can do each day greatly and most of it will be spent just fast forwarding and waiting.There's plenty of minor irks I have with this game all across the board but then this would turn into a bug report/feature request more than a review.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Joined a Cult is a delightful simulation game that stands out with its high replayability and charming graphics. It's a game where you take on the quirky and engaging task of running your own cult, complete with all the whimsical and bizarre elements you could imagine.The game's art style is immediately captivating, featuring cute and colorful graphics that bring a light-hearted and humorous tone to the otherwise eccentric concept of cult management. The visuals are not just pleasing to the eye but also add to the overall enjoyment of the game, making each interaction and development more engaging.What truly makes 'Honey I Joined a Cult' shine is its replayability. Each playthrough offers a new experience, as you can experiment with different cult doctrines, base layouts, and follower management strategies. This variety keeps the game fresh and exciting, inviting you to explore new ways to expand and maintain your cult.However, it's worth noting that the game can become a bit grindy towards the end. As your cult grows, the management aspects can become more demanding, requiring a bit more patience and time to progress. While this might be a slight drawback for some players, the game's charm and the satisfaction of seeing your cult flourish often outweigh the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, me and my bestie started a cult. We had a bible, a doctrine, an origin story - the whole schtick. This game lets me pretend I have the charisma to actually follow through on my dreams and see the ninja pixies THRIVING, Honey, I Joined a Cult a resource management game in which you establish and grow a cult. There are loads of flavour decisions you can make along the way to really make it feel like your new home from home. I ran through a 'darkness' playthrough, but will almost certainly be back to try out one of the others - one must never simply settle for the first cult one comes across. Said flavour decisions also had me literally laughing out loud multiple times, the sense of humour really balances the bleakness of cults with the surrealness of the real world. I also really enjoyed the aesthetics as the cuteness is also a brilliant example of the kind of humour i've poorly described above. there are still some teeny tiny bugs/choices that are questionable (e.g. my cult leader thinks outside is a very poor room so they're never happy enough for a 5* sermon) but nothing game breaking, or even anything that took away from my absolute enjoyment of the game. I c an't wait to see what the devs do next because this was just so much fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I Joined a Cult is a unique and engaging game that offers a complex and intriguing experience for those willing to dive into its intricacies. While it may not be for everyone due to its steep learning curve, it delivers on several fronts that truly shine and make it a must-try for those who appreciate deep, immersive gameplay.The user interface (UI) of Honey, I Joined a Cult is undoubtedly complex, but that complexity is part of what makes it so captivating. It may take some time to grasp all the mechanics, but once you get the hang of it, it's a rewarding experience. The depth of the UI allows for in-depth control over your cult's activities, and this level of control is essential for the game's success.The storytelling in this game is nothing short of captivating. As you learn to create and manage your cult, you'll be drawn into a narrative filled with twists and turns. Deception, manipulation, and the pursuit of faith and wealth form the core of the storyline, making it an enticing journey that keeps you engaged from start to finish.The cartoon graphics in Honey, I Joined a Cult are visually appealing, with a unique and vibrant style that adds a lot to the overall atmosphere. The funky music accompanying the game adds charm and immersion, making it an enjoyable sensory experience.The game dynamics, while admittedly challenging, are part of what makes it stand out. It requires significant time and effort to understand and truly master, but the payoff is worth it. The need for careful management of your cultists, resources, and schedules adds a layer of strategy that will keep you coming back for more. The priority-based task assignment system is a clever addition, allowing you to make crucial decisions and see their impact on your cult's growth and success.In conclusion, Honey, I Joined a Cult is a game that may not be for the faint of heart, but for those who enjoy in-depth management and storytelling, it's a hidden gem waiting to be discovered. _childDocuments_.review: Title: Honey, I Joined a Cult: A Hilariously Entertaining Misadventure!Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)Attention all thrill-seekers and potential cult enthusiasts, get ready for a wild ride with "Honey, I Joined a Cult"! In this zany simulation game, you'll dive headfirst into the quirky world of cults, hilariously embracing your inner follower while trying not to lose your mind (or your sense of humor) in the process.The game starts with a bang as you accidentally find yourself caught up in the alluring and enigmatic world of cults. The graphics are charmingly retro, perfectly capturing the absurdity of the cult's rituals and activities. You'll find yourself laughing out loud as you witness fellow cult members wearing the quirkiest robes you've ever seen or performing the most outrageous dances to please the enigmatic leader.The gameplay mechanics are engaging, as you navigate the delicate balance between appeasing the charismatic cult leader and maintaining your sanity. It's a rollercoaster of emotions as you try to impress the leader with strange tasks, which sometimes involve odd chores like convincing trees to grow faster or chasing butterflies for their "spiritual energy."However, as fun as "Honey, I Joined a Cult" can be, it falls short in terms of depth and longevity. The novelty wears off after a while, and the repetitive nature of the tasks can leave you yearning for more substance. Although the game introduces different cult factions and leader personalities, the core gameplay loop remains relatively unchanged.And here's where the shadow of "Cult of the Lamb" looms large. Despite being released much later, "Cult of the Lamb" offers a refreshingly immersive experience, with its deep narrative, complex character development, and challenging gameplay mechanics. It takes the cult simulation genre to a whole new level, leaving "Honey, I Joined a Cult" feeling like a humorous but ultimately limited precursor.In conclusion, "Honey, I Joined a Cult" is an enjoyable mid-tier game that will undoubtedly tickle your funny bone. The hilarious scenarios and quirky cult antics provide a decent dose of entertainment. However, if you're in the market for a more robust and captivating cult simulation experience, "Cult of the Lamb" is the superior option to delve into the captivating world of charismatic leaders, devoted followers, and plenty of dark humor. So grab your sacrificial butter knife and embark on the journey of a lifetime – just remember to keep your wits about you!

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, this game is a very scaled down version of rimworld with a funny motive on top. I struggled with the recommendation because for me it sits exactly in the middleground....but if i have to chose it dibs slightly towards the negative.I did like the game overall, situations that i hated were few but when they came, they came in force, so here are my top-2-stinkers:1) Adding a strong requirement to have individual bathrooms in a game where you have ~20 pawns that all need to poop at the same time every day sucks. It just sucks. It would be fine if some other game mechanikcs spread the poop-times out more, so you would get along with ~1 room per 5 pawns....but since such mechanics are missing the game really asks you to build upwards of 10 exactly identical bathrooms and does not offer a function to just copy an existing room.2) Demonstrations. Man....what were they thinking with this? I like the basic idea....but this game lacks a quick bar for you pawns like rimworld has and during a demonstration you need to quickly assign individual pawns to individual protestors. This means you need to pause the game, bring up the pawn overview (which covers the entire screen!!), chose a pawn, close the window, assign the pawn to the protestor, unpause the game, wait for the next protestor, repeat. I fail to put in words how unfun this is. It is so disgustingly bad that every single time a day started with a demonstration i had to fight the urge to simply quit the game in frustration. This event/mechanic is less playable and fun than any other part of the game. Annoyingly, the "Tier 2" event of this type (Police raid) is FAR more playable than this....but most of the time you will get this Tier 1 version. It is with no doubt in my mind the single worst thing about this game. It just sucks. I would have enjoyed the game noticeably more if this event would not exist.---There were other, much more minor things that i found not that great...like room decorations that are available in unlimited quantities being too weak in the second half of the game and the ones available in limited quantities being too much of a hassle for still too little prestige. For example, if you sacrifice a very-good recruit (which is the best quality and they are not that common) ou get an object of prestige 7. Placing 12 such items in a room makes this room 6*7 + 6*3.5 = 63 prestige....but you need 75 to reach the highest rating. This is for EACH INDIVIDUAL ROOM. Maybe that explaines why i hate the requirement to have 10-15 bathrooms so much. Sure, you don't have to decorate each room - but this is pretty much the core idea of this game: Building rooms and putting objects in them.I also did not like the way the game-room works. I would have MUCH preferred if you could have just upgraded the items in each category when you get them....but since each individual item will start to bore your pawns and put them on cooldown you will have to keep all of them...so by the end of the game you need a giant game-room plastered with 3 tiers of entertainment in each category. Minor complaint, really, but did not like it.---Overall the game is good....but none of its good parts were as strong as its weakest parts (looking at you, demonstrations!) were frustrating.The part i enjoyed the most was optimising my pawns, eliminating their quirks and negative traits, trying to get the best positive traits. This is what this game does well, in my opinion. In some rooms you can actually see and "feel" an impact from adding a worker with really good traits for the job. But then you realise that in order to do that you simply have to sit out days, watching you screen as you do absolutely nothing because it costs so much influence to do and the only way to get influence is to watch the game play itself....that's why i diped towards not recommended in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems like it wants to be a somewhat sandboxy game that lets your cult and compound/temple become whatever you envision and still be playable. However, there are feedback loops in the game balancing that makes it very easy to have your cult go into a negative spiral of self implosion if you don't play the game "right". I'm not just saying the game is too difficult, because it is quite possible to understand the rules of the game and then to try to play optimally to win. But that's a whole different game experience than what seems to be advertised. If the game really is aiming to be a challenging min/max-fest, then a lot of elements seem out of place. If the game instead is aiming for the whimsical sandboxy style, then it should be better at adapting the difficulty so that the player feels the challenge but generally overcomes it even when venturing outside of the mechanically optimal.

I more or less brute forced my way through the whole game and spent the majority of it in fast forward mode waiting for research to finish. You can basically ignore follower level it won't matter much. You can't make multiple of several rooms which dramatically slows the game down. Money is a joke very early on and serves little purpose. Followers are heavily restricted to slow the game down, research is heavily restricted to slow the game down...I am sure you get the point. All such games are basically just a glorified excel and drills down to numbers crunching. Many negative reviews points out 'flaws' which doesn't exist, perhaps the reviewer didn't spend enough time or didn't look carefully. Examples like 'lack of job priorities', 'lack of overview' or 'too much heat' are simply wrong, maybe in the time those were written those functions didn't exist yet?All in all - solid position, worth trying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has tons of potential. At the same time, there are flaws that still linger.Pros:- Customization in almost everything. The Cult? You can change the appearance, name, and even titles of your cult's leadership at any time. Compound? Well, with enough cash, anything is possible. Difficulty? Grindfest or quick and dirty, we got you. Location? Well...- The midgame is slightly varied. The paths the cult can go in do have a unique feel to them. After playing through all 3 (as of writing this) paths, I can say that the difference isn't as big as some might like, but it is noticeable.- The End Game scene is satisfying, as you get to see your grand plan for the cult come true.Cons:- Heat is hardly a threat even on the highest multipliers if you save money and research propaganda center. Unless you're trying to speedrun, you most likely aren't going to get a protest or a police raid if you take your time. Heck, you may not even get a police raid despite wanting to see what is like (like myself).- The End Game, while satisfying to reach, is very grindy. It takes a lot of research and cash to actually finish the final task. Adjusting modifiers can help with that, but it still takes a lot of time to finish final research.- You will always start in the same location, get the same events, and have the same grass covered compound. The events themselves are varied, don't get me wrong. However, you will get repeats if you are trying to accomplish all 3 pathways. I wasn't bothered by this, but I'm sure someone will be.Overall, I give it a 8.5/10.It does scratch the spot where you actually run a cult where the cultists actually know how to take care of themselves, but at the same time it can get bland and can screech to a grindfest if difficulty is adjusted poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is highly addictive if you enjoy other simulation games such as Prison Architect, or to a lesser degree Rimworld. You build a cult form the ground up starting with 3 cultists and a cult leader. It is your job to provided for their needs while recruiting Followers which can eventually become Cultists after they have hung out and been bled dry of their money for a bit.Cultists can take on tasks such as running the various cult rooms or researching, cleaning, cooking etc.Followers exist to be recruited as cultists/resource generation primarily and other options are made available later in the game.After a bit of research you get to decide the direction of your cult and currently there are 3 Paths to choose from. (Darkness, Futurology, Peace&Love)Each path opens up new rooms, cult goals,costume pieces, and even some special cultists to recruit.After Choosing your path and researching its tree with your leader further you are given even more choices in regards to the direction you want to take your cult in.The game does not currently have a true sandbox mode but allows you to continue playing after reaching an ending. With that said to reach the end of the game you have to actively accomplish goals and finally press a button that triggers the ending where you can see your stats, and choose if you would like to call it quits or go back and continue on your cult building way. Currently, according to the devs in the discussion section, there are no plans to implement a stand-alone sandbox mode or mod support. However, they are open to it if enough people express an interest in it!Updates are made regularly and so far have added in a lot of great content and ways to play.Get this game if you enjoy games like Prison Architect and are looking for something new to play!May your followers be many, and your cultist dreams realized!

_childDocuments_.review: Several among us are likely to have that one friend or relative, or we at least know someone who’s a teensy bit too much into alternative medicine or guided meditation. You can tell they’re not deepening a practice or applying the result of some research to a new topic, but rather they’re coasting on a rush of feel-good vibes that they only maintain in chasing the Next Great Thing. Sometimes, the Next Great Thing is a stand-up desk, or maybe a keto diet. At other times, it’s a cult.Honey, I Joined a Cult takes a subject matter that’s usually mired in uncomfortable bits of Pop Culture tidbits, like knowing about Marshall Applewhite’s desire to ride the tail of the Hale-Bopp comet to some perceived astral plane, or Japan’s Aum Shinrikyo and its infamous sarin gas attacks carried out in Tokyo’s subway system – and skirts right past all that grue to effectively poke at the simple truth behind most cultists; which is that these people are lost, in need of guidance – and sometimes given to a bit of the old word salad. That, at least, can make them funny. So you’re a quack and a scam artist – or a guru, naturally – and you’ve just hatched you next get-rich-reasonably-quick scheme; which is to start a cult. The basics are straightforward, seeing as a brainwashing routine couldn’t survive a constant immersion in the outside world. Your job is to see to every single need of your cultists and to arrange for the gradual expansion and eventual prominence of your ad-hoc bit of faux spirituality. It starts with the basics (food, rest, hygiene and a place to pray) and quickly expands with the need to not only draw in other faithful, but also maintain what you’ve built for yourself. You need to see to your followers’ crumbling mental health and also diversify your message, eventually figuring out if you’re more of the type to be coasting on the works of New Age ASMRtists or if awakening a few Great Old Ones is more your jam. Either way, you’ll need a media presence, influence in the wider world – and money. Lots of it. Mechanically, it’s all very close to Introversion Software’s Prison Architect – the one difference is you’re screaming about aliens and God giving you superpowers to keep your “inmates” happy. There’s a few recognizable quirks in the mechanics, from a Management screen that interfaces with each cultist’s individual quirks and foibles to a schedule that can be set on a per-hour basis. A lot like Planet Coaster or Planet Zoo, this is a game where a lot of the fun is in making minute adjustments over several hours. If you’re more the SimCity type and enjoy seeing how moving a decimal point can futz with your slime mold of an ecosystem, you’ll probably want to stay away. HIJaC is a game for the motherers and terminal optimizers but works on a scale that feels more like the later half of Netflix’s “Keep Sweet” documentary than, say, Scientology’s bafflingly meteoric rise.Of course, it’s all still in Early Access, and could use a little more variety. You’ll first love the very “Hippie Meets Shaft” vibes of the soundtrack, and then maybe start to think about muting it on occasion. The main loop is hard to break, and most events that alter everyday life on the compound are simple, from a toilet breaking down and needing a visit from the maintenance man to someone you’d sent on a mission ending up in the pokey for a few days. Fail to keep your followers’ mental stats in check, and you could find yourself with your elected Chosen One foaming at the mouth out by the complex’s main gates, screaming insult-filled gibberish at random passerbys. Early on, generating stable growth and keeping everyone debatably sane is a bit of an ordeal, so balancing issues can still pop up. As it stands, however, Honey I Joined a Cult is a fun and deeply satirical little ditty that isn’t likely to wow any Management Sim fan’s socks off, but that gets some laughs out of anyone with a bit of a history on what happens when a relative suddenly goes nuts about Celtic mythology and massive chunks of pyrite yanked out of old concrete slabs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good.  It feels like there's a lack of depth, like there could be more things added in.  The faith is slow to accumulate at the beginning, which slows your cult development.  Money is the issue, which relates to faith, which relates to prestige....  it's vicious circle that can really hamper your beginnings, making it feel kind of grindy.  These things could have been alleviated if there had been rich personalities added to the cult members, perhaps interpersonal relationship issues.  Or if there had been random issues that could occur, causing problems for the player to over come, therefore making them feel more vested in the cult.  But there are no real random events, and it is very easy to avoid the legal issues that you see in the trailer.The game is win-able.  It's a satisfying feeling to actually finish it, but at some point I wanted to finish it just for the accomplishment rather than because it was still fun to play.  There is probably some replay value if you want to try a different themed cult and perhaps try a speed run, but I can't imagine more than two play throughs.  All in all, a fun game if not too deep.  But worthy of playing if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the game is officially out, I want to say I am SO GLAD I put time into this game. It's clear the developers are passionate about what they do, know what they're doing, and listen to feedback. Any issues I had when the game was in beta got worked out. The skills/rooms tell you what coordinate, so you aren't developing skills blindly. The addition to doing things at night and just all around changes have all been positive in my opinion. Well worth it!!This game has a LOT of potential. And considering it's just two people, I am thoroughly impressed. However. there are quality of life fixes and just some things that need improved on before I can really sink hours into this. I'm finding that when I am building walls, when you place a new room where it shares a wall with an existing one, it's deleting the walls that already exist, along with forcing weird room shapes sometimes. The wall issues need fixed because while I don't have OCD, it bothers me when one room is sitting lower than the others, or that all of a sudden my walls are being deleted and it won't even let me replace them. You made a 'delete wall' button. DO NOT make adding walls also delete walls at the same time. counterproductive. The skills I feel could use better explanation as well. Since this is a micromanagement kind of game, I don't want to sink 20 hours in and realize I set up all my cultists wrong because I wasn't sure what the skills do.Other than those, the game seems really cool. I do enjoy the sandbox aspect of it. I definitely plan on keeping an eye on this game. I bought it knowing that once they finish it and it leaves early access, it's going to be a great game. Already on the way there.

_childDocuments_.review: When first thrown into what I expected to be another average base building/management simulator for another group of people that just happened to be worshiping a long forgotten worm god, I wasn't expecting the level of control and complexity for a fresh off the shelf game that's still being heavily developed. There are a few things that I would add that could hopefully make the ride to being sent to another planet as a race of robots a little smoother, but overall the game has been developed nicely and it offers enough gameplay and intriguing interactions to keep the casual player interested and discovering new things throughout. From enjoying your basic group of friends who just happen to be helping you turn your favorite followers into food, to making sure your scheduling and futureproofing happen correctly, the game is definitely a 9/10 for games of it's genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and engaging, with a surprising level of micro-management options. Has a quaint retro feel and that quirky Team17 sense of humour. A must-have if you grew up in the 90's on Theme Park and the like. I forgot this game was early access because it's so smooth and stable. The team seems committed to adding more content and the game has a bright future as a cult classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Really like the idea of this game from the get go!!  The design feels very similar to prison architect which made it simple to pick up but there are additional elements to it I definitely need to dive more into.  Only negative would be the follower number restrictions, seemed to be set really low and really hard to unlock more... would prefer higher numbers so more chaos ensues.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hesitant to review this one because I'm still on the fence about it, but it's undeniably charming. It feels like it goes *juuuust* on the side of overcomplicated though. Like it goes really into the weeds on stuff. And while that is a negative for me, I can definitely see where many others would enjoy so many options, hence the thumbs up. Maybe get it on sale like I did if you're unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and addictive. Build a compound, manage & upgrade cultists, followers, and resources (money, faith, influence...). If you like building/management sims with a lot clicking around and observing AND have an interests in cults - this is for you. Achieved world domination in the early access version and will definitely return to play god as the developers add more content. Hint: focus heavily on heat reduction missions and utilize the covert-ops to move forward and get to the end!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: If this was a full release, I'd be a little disappointed. I haven't gotten THAT far in the game yet, though. What I will say is that this is great for an early access title and I can't wait to see what the future holds. If you like games in this genre, buy this when it's on sale, or wait for the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting game. Definitely a fun and new take on the same style that Prison Architect uses. I'm a big fan so far and really love the direction the developers are going with the game so far. Updates have provided increased technology to research and new items to use in the game, which means the game will be fresh and new periodically throughout the early access development. Big thumbs up, cant wait to see what else comes to this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Very well designed, a lot of humour lifted from Father Ted and Black Books with lovely cute graphics.  I don't find it particularly shallow, but the research tree is a bit harsh, although I guess not feeding them very well or giving them comfortable pews is intended to make the early game a bit of a grind.Could use some more flexibility about direction of the cult itself, as in you don't necessarily want to live a life of darkness until  a later sage and the ideas about alternative health are a bit questionable - some complimentary therapies are not actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy in reality.Might consider adding a bit of food growing and more grim menial labour for the less useful followers, and maybe some sort of study facility for their time off rather than constant board games and puggies.I think this is an extremely competent and fun start and I look forward to the point at which it will be getting DLC additions.  Is it value for money? It has certainly had a lot of thought and work put into it and it is very stylish, but I do think it is quite early.For most less serious game players it is more than good enough, on the other hand for your Project Zomboid or Banished players it is a good start and very nice to play. Not at all sorry I bought it.edit after 40 hours - there is a lot of hidden flexibility if you mess with the timeline, however I am seeing some coding issues in the later stages when it is a long game.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed Prison Architect, I don't mind the familiar "feel" - actually the opposite. I found it easy to pick up and enjoyable. I think the game finds a good way to add some humor to a normally not-so-funny subject without being crass. I can't wait to see what else they will add as the game progresses through it's build
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I'm hooked! Love at first sight! I knew this game was for me just by the title and the psychedelic 70's cover!! I'm really into this type of Sim game, but I was getting bored with the same kinda stuff over and over so this is a nice change. I love how you can be creative with your cult name and outfits especially the HATS!! :) I am really glad I bought this game and looking forward to future updates and more content!!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: "Honey, I joined a cult." Is a cult.  I couldn't believe this is Early Access. It's well worth it and they update pretty regularly too! So many customization options, so many things you can do and play with. Amazing resource management and satire game. Okay yes, it's a bit upsetting that I put 40+ hours into a game and then an update came out that didn't get to load the new stuff to my old save. Eh, whatever. Cults come and go right? I've started to treat the restarts like my cult got "busted" in the last game and damn it... Okay lets take 3 folks! I love the narrative concept and the game is funny enough with enough content to keep you sated for hours. More so with all the amazing updates they add!Being a player of this game is being part of the Cult. Join us. We have punch and pie.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun at first and it's novelty is neat but once you get a good handle on the balance of resources and some patience it loses any fun for it and has no repayable value. It's fun to make your own cult, discover more outfit options and to start out build your own compound with neat rooms to focus on. Then when you eventually and inevitably spiral down a resource shortage and start failing, doing it again loses it's spark. It's very easy to cheese. Making a room prestigious is as simple as buying more stuff. More money is best done by getting more followers doing more stuff. It's hard at first but the further you go in the easier it is. Usually luck has a lot to do with how well you can do in a game like this. Sometimes you can't account for everything in a management game or have to choose the lesser of two options. Not really so in this game. It's simply increase output with no real sacrifice. After beating the game I found myself not really interested in doing it again. I summoned the great old one with half a million cash, all my cult members good quality or higher and 3 special characters. I maxed out on faith every night and didn't even bother researching any more because of the influence cost. Heat wasn't an issue, money wasn't an issue, nothing stood in my way except the time it took to discover and receive all the pieces to summon the great old one. By the time I did I was sick of the game. I would not want to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a thumbs up, for potential. It still has a long ways to go.I've heard comparisons to "prison architect", but outside of the graphics, that's where it stops. Prison architect is heavily focused on compound optimization, risk, etc, which is not a focus of HIJAC. I feel it's more similar to Roller Coaster Tycoon, or Two Point Hospital.A lot of the challenges in this game can be overcome just by waiting. It's very much an idle game, waiting for your cultists to accumulate enough resources for the next step, without any real risk involved. There's nothing wrong with an "idle" game style (if that's your thing), but there are hindrance. For example, every night your sermon will freeze the game with a popup. Additionally, certain rooms require micromanagement, and really don't produce what they cost.The early game can be a tricky balancing act. Getting your "faith" generation above the "faith" cost of your cultists can be a real issue. But once you're up and running, it's no problem. You can also easily lower your heat, so police will never be an issue (unless you want them to be). Additionally, the "therapy" rooms are almost functionally identical. The only incentive to have a variety, is because your followers will get "bored". What this game needs is not just "more content", but a rework of certain systems. Also, a campaign would be nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Never been really into the idea of management games like Prison Architect and the like, but I think game has converted me into the Cult of Management.The funky and fitting music now plays in my head continually and I like it. The only issue I currently have is one I'm sure will be added in in the near future, and that's just to have more than one module room, or at least more than one hypnosis station and maybe a way to assign specific followers to use those module rooms since they are a one time deal.Overall, yes, love it, more please.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This really has the trappings of a great game, however there are too many aspects to fix before I can recommend the game.+ Very nice artstyle+ No gamebreaking bugs that I've discovered+ Great Music+ A great format- A decently large amount of QL improvements need to be made- It is a very slow game, this combined with the lack of customisation in a run makes the game feel like it's not going anywhere- A lack of challenge, as soon as you know the mechanics you'll never have another issue for the rest of the game- Faith has no payable uses other than cult upkeep which is a non-issue, essentially a useless resource- There is a research tree but it is entirely linear, no choices cut off other options- Alongside the linear research tree there is no mechanical reason to have different styles of cults, I don't get benefits and disadvantages from different gods. This means once you beat the game, there is nothing else to do.- A minor thing is that the symbols for very poor and poor cultists need to be reversed. It should go copper, silver, gold not silver, copper, gold.- A lot of minor bugs, for example changing hairstyles while people are asleep will cause them to go bald until they wake up.All in all, I can see this becoming an amazing game it really has the potential, but at the current price with the current content I'd hold off buying. I'll change this review if we get to that stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good start. But it needs more.Games like this do GREAT with customization and random events. In particular I would like for the cult to have more interactions and feel a bit more alive. This game simply needs more to do and during down time (when you aren't building or doing missions) and it needs more simulation. Before it sounds like I am being too critical, I do want to point out this is early access. Do I like it? yes. Does it need work? yes.  Should you get it?If you are into rimworld or prison architect you will find this charming but a bit simple in it's current state. I would say yes but temper your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is FUN! If you ever wanted to be a cult leader, this is the game for you. And even if you didn't, this is still the game for you. Yes, it is currently in early access and you can see that in the game play as in late game, it becomes a little repetitive but you will still have a great time playing this game. Right now, the variety of items you can use to decorate is a little lacking. My biggest wish for this game, is that we can join the avatars to the missions into town to retrieve objects, increase PR or any of the nefarious missions you can send your avatar on.Hopefully the developers are going to continue working on this as this is a promising game you can sink hours and hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game has received a couple of negative reviews which I can partially understand. The game is fun, there is no doubt about that and the potential is there for a future interesting setting. However at the current state the game is in, there is a lack of depth/content in the game. There are missions, there is a tech three and still I do get the feeling something is missing. I will however give the game a positive review since I am enjoying the game and I do believe something nice can come from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so far out there. I legitimately thought this was going to be a softcore idle game where you gather resources to do research. NOPE. You get to build rooms that can infuse your cultists with Demonic Energy (possibly turning them into a demon, though personally I haven't had that happen), you can yeet followers into a pit and offering a "sacrifice" to whatever Diving Being you decided to make fun on, Contract Rooms to make deals with demons, and least we not forget a room that has the capability of summon Eldritch horrors to take over the world.Play this game enough, do enough, and you get pleasantly greeted by a picture of some guy, chilling on a lawn chair with a drink, watching the world around him literely burn around him as you hear screams and, what I can only assume is ASMR that would have made H.P. Lovecraft swoon.It's a fantastic game that never, for a second, takes itself seriously, and it makes for rediculous antics, and some times very interesting situations. 10/10, would recommend to any one who can run anything on potato settings, can read, and wants to laugh themselves to the bathroom before any leakage happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: There's enough interesting and funny stuff going on in this early-access release to make me think there might be a really fun game here eventually, but at the moment, there's just too much waiting and not enough doing.Other than not enough to build/do, my biggest specific problem is with the "Heat" game mechanic, which is basically a measure of how closely the cops are watching your cult. It only goes down  on its own, and the missions that let you actively reduce it seem to stop being offered after a while. Since every other mission seems to increase Heat, there's a strong disincentive against doing anything interesting for much of the game, since you don't want to provoke a raid.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the trailer, I got hooked. It looked like a fun strategy game, the art style is cute. Started playing it since yesterday. It takes a while to get a hang of what's actually happening and what needs to be done. Sometimes it gets a bit monotonous and frustrating but at the same time it's addicting! Been playing for hours :)
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, this game is in "Early Access"; that said, for being an "Early Access" game, there's a whole lot of good going on!:- Fun to play for hours at a time- Runs really well even on the most potato computer- Lots of customization options to personalize your cult- The "preferred" skills for specific roles is SO INCREDIBLY HELPFUL when trying to figure out how to assign cultists or where to put their skill points when leveling them up (and to be fair, most of my bads are QoL fixes rather than actual issues):- Decor is so prohibitively expensive, especially early on, but a room lacking prestige from decor dents the quality/output of that room that you're pretty much going to need to spend all your money on decor instead of building facilities, which hampers your ability to generate more income- It would be nice to be able to "upgrade" room features, like beds or toilets, when a new tier is unlocked; as it stands now, you have to purchase the new item, then delete the old item- The Kitchen mechanic is a little annoying; it would be nice to set a recurring purchase order for food ingredients when it gets below a certain threshold or something similar.Overall I give it a 9/10. Great game if you like Two Point Hospital or Prison Architect!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this with some appreciation for the idea, but ultimately, I just don't find this very good.* It's too grind-heavy to really feel enjoyable. Build room to meet $need or extort money from your followers. Watch them inevitably get dissatisfied with the room's equipment or purpose. Build more stuff. Continue.* The room choices are also fairly bland and feel very much same-same. This is especially disappointing given the wide range of possibilities that the theme allows for.* There's too much pointless micromanagement. Having to order ingredients for the kitchen or research hamburgers to make in there is pretty much just silly, for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I love the fact this game was done by two people and they had to learn how to make it prior, so expect a little longer in the updates. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I really like it. Firstly - they get the basics absolutely spot on. Day length? Perfect. Speed of movement? Perfect. Priorities? Perfect. Pathing? Perfect. Whilst this might not seem like much, a base builder with all the good ideas in the world won't work without them. I'll even go as far as to say the basics here feel better than Prison Architect (PA), the next generation of basics, if you will.Cult stuff is funny and there's good humour throughout the game. The theme in general is a lot of fun, this feels more like a successor to Evil Genius than the actual crappy mobile-esque sequel. Research tree is huge and will keep you engaged for a while, there's also a secondary research resource as well which can lead to absolutely crazy upgrades (like a pit of doom)! Seeing as this secondary research is one of their key items on the road map I can see a lot of replayability in the future.So, here's some recommendations game devs:- Two new rooms;  - PR office - when manned, stops PR from ticking down;  - Attorney's office - when manned, slowly vents heat;- Room restrictions;  - Attorney's office and infirmary - average or higher quality only (this will drive people to replace cultists);  - others that you might think of;- Upgrades;  - Lobby or Recruitment office - let me filter out followers, after a certain point I no longer want very poor/poor;  - Give some skill boosts other than retail to the bartenders;- Research; - Increased PR limit - even better cultists/followers;- Followers;  - I would like to see a slightly upgraded system to the one the game has now. I'd like followers to be assigned a cult level and traverse my compound based on that level (all set by me). For example, a follower coming in at level one might be allowed to do the Meditation Chamber, level two they can then do the Energy Spa, level three it's time for the Hypno module. As a follower increases in level, you could also increase their base monetary and influence gains. You do see this in real life cults, pay £200 to move up to level two!!!! etc. The end of this circuit could then be aforementioned pit, or signing a contract and going back round.My last point is a big one, but important. The biggest thing the game lacks at the moment is complexity, especially around base design. As it stands now, your followers simply complete every exercise before getting bored, leaving and cursing your name. I don't like the open endedness of that, especially when everything else in the game is so polished.  So, to finish - brilliant game, unlimited potential - grab it now for a good 20/30 hours of fun with potentially hundreds of hours of it on the road map.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but to be honest it needs way more content and a serious UI polish pass. A little looking around at the better job priority systems out there (Oxygen Not Included or Going Medieval, for instance) would be a good way to research changes needed.I finished the game in about 14.5 hours. You get 10 premade cults but as far as I can tell, they're mostly the same and offer no real replayability. Once you unlock and finish your choice of doomsday room, the game is over.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

I understand its early access and I do hope it gets better but at this point its just bleh

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very excited to see the expansion of this game! What the developers have done here is very cute in its art style, nostalgic and funny in all the little references and quotes the characters' speech bubbles have, and the premise of the game I find really interesting and refreshing. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: First, the only simulation game I have played is Sims 4. That is my knowledge base. Clocking in at almost 7hrs, I have already destroyed my cult. You might wonder how could you ruin the cult***....but that's for the end of this review. Pros:+Good templates for your Cult, if you just want to dive into the game instead of agonizing over every detail. +A good laugh from the dialogue.+ Good mix between designing your camp and carrying out missions. Lots of decor and ways to earn more.+ Missions, divine inspirations, and research provide a good pace setting as your cult is building. I always found a balance between completing a mission, designing, and overall management. +Different jobs the cult members are assigned to. Have to keep them busy! Leveling them up and a template system is very nice!+An infuriating amount of undesirable cult members. I have to roll up my sleeves and whip them into shape. Yeah it's a positive because it mimics real life. I mean you would be a lazy cult member too, wouldn't you?Cons:+ The navigational interface is not intuitive for a player new to simulation games. My main sticking point is that in order to move an object or delete it, I have to click in multiple menus. For example, want to move a bed? You can't just click on the bed. Steps are Click on Room -> 2 menus pop up -> Click on "See Room Specific Objects" -> Click on "Move Object" -> Move the object. My question is why so many steps?+Typical bugs such as the maintenance worker not fixing the equipment, cult members standing idle, not feeding themselves.+Can be overwhelming for a new player. I do not see an easy to access "guide" or "journal" feature that compiles all the information as you go through developing your cult. For example, still figuring out once the kitchen ability is unlocked does the person assigned actually boost the kitchen stats and benefit every member? or is it individualized?  Another example is the covert operations. I unlocked that and built the room, but nothing seems to happen when selecting the Covert button. +The cult member traits are varied and randomized, but as updates go on would like to see some more higher quality followers at an earlier point in the game. +You will probably need to do a second play through (if you are dumb like me). There are some features such as giving pep talks to your members that I did not realize were available. It is a bit confusing. Overall, I would recommend and especially if the Cons of my review are addressed/implemented. **You would think after upgrading literal **** buckets to fine clean thrones and feeding the members hamburgers instead of candy bars from the vending machine they would be grateful, but nooooooooooooo...my star member who I built a separate bedroom for decided to up and croak. She was the true leader and it all went downhill from there...
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game. I bought it because I thought they had added some neat new features to help characterize your cult. That was not the case. This is basically a re-skin of prison architect. There is nothing new added. The tutorial is clunky and does not set the player up for success. The intro is incredibly long and you aren't able to skip it.Basically had no motivation to continue playing after realizing a prison architect clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is delightful and so much fun. I love simulation games and this is one of the most unique ones that I've played. If you like games like Two Point Hospital and Prison Architect then you will really enjoy this game. There is less of a money management and more of people management which I really enjoy. I do really hope that more content gets added like cult traits and some quality of life improvements. It's in early access though so I'm sure there is plenty more fun things to come. So far I'm loving this game and am completely sucked in! Just worked on my cult for 6 hours straight lmao.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Played through a whole cult within 21 hours, enjoyed all of it! Will play various different cults throughout for sure. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and immediately played it for 6 hours straight. It's pretty simple, create your own cult, get followers, make sure they are happy. The idea is great. _childDocuments_.review: Really fun time killer, i cant wait to see what else gets added. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a really cool game, but I am stuck in the tutorial. So many times I get stuck on something. So I destroyed it, and that also destroyed the floor under it where I clicked. Then, you can't replace that floor. I did the lectern part, but could not get the first part. Anyway, the game is in early access. It's really frustrating to play right now, but I will be back at full release and will update my review then. If the devs happen to see this, I'm pretty excited for your game, best of luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I waited too long, i wanted to like it. And even with the support of team 17, all that was delivered was the bare bones of prison architect.It looks like they took more time redesigning sprites than working on giving this game an actual objective, because the current gameplay feels like either forced tutorials or just sandbox.And the animations, oh god those beating heads will haunt me for life
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game the first week of early access release. Honestly, I was expecting more from the full version. It's a competent simulator in that it runs well and the numbers can be balanced. It's cute. The concept is great. But it's about as deep as a puddle. If you're new to colony sims you will probably enjoy it. If you're a veteran, you'll likely be disappointed which is why I can't recommend it for the price. Without workshop support, which would mean fans could actually turn this into a worthy addition to the genre, there's just no reason to ever play it more than once. It's a $12 USD game at best and that may be a bit generous. It's like a well optimized Prison Architect with about 10% of the content of vanilla PA. With all of the competition in the base building/ colony sim market, I can name at least six games still in early access, at the same price or less, that have more content and more replay value than Honey, I Joined A Cult.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I Joined a Cult is a game developed by Sole Survivor Games and published by Team17The game offers some nice graphics, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameHoney, I Joined a Cult overall, however, is an okay game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is an okay-ish to meh simulation game and to play in short bursts

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying this game and for early access there is still quite a bit to it. Playing as one of the rebuilt cults to Santa Claus worship, praise the Jolly Red Man! It can get a bit redundant after a point waiting for enough influence to start research on the next unlock. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: love the game but it needs a lot of tweaks! missions in general get to difficult to quickly and rapidly become impossible  but because of low pr rating cant get better followers to recruit i stuck with poor or very poor, also pool of revelations only one or two followers ever use it . so still you have to get rid of most of your followers every time you want to recruit! its taking ages and ages to get a decent team together. other things like scrolling research screen and why does the research not pop up complete and then allow the researcher to carry on with out you having to go to research screen and scroll to where the item you research is on the tech tree? it doesn't make sense why be able to stack research if it wont start after the last one? i suggest a way of picking up followers or sending them to specific rooms eg pool of rev so you can make use of this facility more. maybe costing influence to do it? a more intuitive interface in general would be good improvement i found myself having to do things a bit awkwardly in daily stuff. moving rooms and changing stuff is a pain and awkward. also placing object direct to rooms from menu you cant see the prestige gain, please make it so you can! there's  lots more like that i look forward to seeing this grow!  i do love this game a few tweaks will make it a legend!

_childDocuments_.review: I was shocked to learn this was a two-person studio. So yes, I 100% recommend supporting this effort.There isn't a whole lot of content. 8 hours in and I feel as though I've stabilized the cult and am making so much money (with no real pressing need to spend any) that I could just sort of hang out and be fine basically forever. So the progression curve needs a little smoothing out. More themes, some sort of "take over the city" mechanic, or random "emergencies" (vandals breaking into the compound, a bunch of cultists going vegan and rendering your burgers powerless, etc.) which would disrupt the gameplay loop would liven it up as well.But again, this two-person effort is more than worth supporting, in my mind. Of course, I knew that the second I heard the intro music. They have the foundation of a great game here, and I'm excited to see how it turns out.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Something I like the most about this game is the ability to control individual cult members. In Prison Architect the characters were categorized where in this game a cult member can have more options. These characters can be leveled up so there's a strategy here that I'm still learning. I'm excited to see how this game grows. It's far easier to learn than Another Brick in the Mall which is too confusing to me. Great addition to the genre.11/10 will play for too long.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: With the understanding of this game still being early access it has a lot going for it already. If you have not played a game of this type before, I recommend taking some time to understand the game mechanics, and then beginning a new game after you feel comfortable with everything. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game that I'm looking forward to seeing how it develops. As at Alpha release the game is fairly bare based on the developer's roadmap but it still gave me an enjoyable 20 hours to play through to the finale. The intro is very well threshed out with a decent cut scene but the finale is currently lacking with a single screen acknowledging you've completed the finale task (I suspect they will match the finale quality/cut scene to the intro in due course). I recommend purchasing if you want to support the developers and have an enjoyable, relaxing base building experience pending completion of game. Until more development is done there is limited replay value as many features that will provide variety aren't available yet.Largely bug free with some text missing which simply appears to be coded wrong/missing code e.g. dialogue box will have "%xxxxx%" where it might refer to an object. The only other bug is that some unique items will provide 2 in your inventory but can only be placed once. Neither of these affected my play through in a significant way. The developers seem really good at taking on feedback and I have had them come back to me through steam bug reporting when I've raised an issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game only 4 hours in and I feel like there is a ton more to learn and do. The tech tree is pretty big and the game is very in depth for just coming out into EA.There are some annoying things like being not being able replace foundations if you delete them on accident  in the middle of the room or not being able to re-sell/recycle old objects that you put down. Some of the scheduleing and priority can feel clunky and hard to figure out and use but it gets the job done.Overall its is very much for the price of $20 if not more
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game needs a bit more work, there are spots where the AI is buggy and there are a few missing textures, but I honestly don't mind it. The game is still in development and it's 100% playable. It's an addicting, fun, and cute game.I was a bit confused on how the kitchen worked but figured it out on my own after a few minutes, but I'd recommend adding a place where you can read through tutorials for unlocked rooms.Another thing I might recommend is raising the cap for members or followers, but this honestly isn't an issue until late game.Overall, a really fun game that stays engaging for hours and isn't too repetitive!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I've officially joined a cult! This game has been really great so far! You're building your cult from the ground up so expect it to take a little bit of time. The biggest issues I'm having with the game is that it seems a little clunky when it comes to the menus and what not, they are like overly big and a little slow to navigate, its not very smooth transitions between menus and building. I also felt that the intro was overly slow with no fast forward button that I could figure out. There's also not a lot in customization for your cult right now so I hope to see that in future updates. But overall I am having a great time expanding my cult and can't wait to see whats next!!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a recommend because it's pretty good, even though what this game is about seems very unimportant to the game. I figured this game was about the cult that you design and run, sadly the cult you design is not important. Just to be sure i restarted a few times, with a few different cults, and sure enough, the Amazing cult of Bob Ross played exactly like the naked porn stars of Ron Jeremy. Not a single difference gameplay wise. Sure things looked a little different, different pictures, names of things and such, but the game was exactly the same, thankfully again the game was good although missing a lot of QOL stuff like making/saving blueprints, saving schedules, clear description of what items do (like drains, i haven't seen any water in the game so i'm guessing it's just decoration but...). And looking at the roadmap of things to come for the game, none of it seemed like it would actually change the gameplay between cults, but maybe it will (fingers crossed). So for now it gets a thumbs up from pappy, but just marginally as the game should be about your cult specifically not just some generic thing, atleast i hoped it was anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great ideas and is fun at the start but it rapidly get repetitive. You just have to be patient and after a certain point, when you have enough different therapy rooms, you make enough money to max out everything.The evolution/size of your cult depends on research so it makes the game fairly easy. You can't really outgrown your cult. You are caps on the number of follower and cult members (both are quiet low) and the first upgrade for both doesn't add a lot so you end up having a lot of people leaving because the cult is full (which make the lobby job useless in some ways).At this point, the waiting game begins. You wait for your research to complete while piling cash and then, depending on the research, you build a room or unlock some other more or less relevant upgrade.Then the cycle continue... Wait-->Cash/Influence-->Research-->Room/Bonus-->Wait-->Cash/Influence....Doing mission can generate heat (which is not good, you want to avoid having too much) and at one point, I was kind of locked out of doing missions because people started leaving my cults for being bored at doing the same therapy rooms over and over and when people leave, it generate heat. To decrease heat, you have to passively wait (again) or unlock the mission to lower heat. And since you get caped out fast on cultist, you have to think about it before sending them on missions.Also, characters have different quality. You start with one moderate and all the others that you recruits for a while are very bad quality (at least for me). Even with the recruitment room and one moderate character maxed out on recruitment skills (speech and retail I think, I'm not sure for the skills names exactly), I wasn't able to recruit better ones. And from what I've seen, there is no way to know which followers are what quality unless you recruit them (unless I'm missing something). So from my understanding, if you want better cult members, you have to "cycle" through the followers that are ready to be recruited by recruiting them and then kicking them out if they are low quality? So that make them angry because they are kicked out and you loose one follower (which mean cash and influence income).Maybe that's one way to prevent people from leaving by themselves but I find it kind of weird and they end up leaving anyway.Starting Customization for your cult are fairly limited as well. If you want to "role-play" your cult and give them a certain flavor, it might be impossible for now. I know you unlock new item in game and you can customize your cult at any time but still, it be nice to have more options when you create your cult and then unlock more epic skins one in game instead of simply unlocking a new hat skin. It would be nice to have... I don't know... special cult member skins? Like a glowing skin or coloured auras.... flaming hairs (just random ideas on top of my head) but my point is that it would had some nice incentive to go fetch items in game and still make it possible to have more customization when creating your cult.Anyway, the game isn't bad and I haven't seen any bugs so far. The only thing I saw was the characters going through objects. Objects are kind of sprites with "standing points" for npcs, they can pass through with no problems and sometimes, it break the immersion of placing stuff in a room since it doesn't affect anything.I would wait a few updates and see where the game goes before buying it. There is a lot of research in the tree but really little incentive to go far in it or to keep playing.Longer review than expected but I hope it can give feedback to both players and devs. I'm open to comments if I've been missing out on stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: A game that has a *.docx file that explains how to use Borlderless Windows API straight into the installation folder. Perhaps a memo for devs.I hadn't yet gived a try to an IL disassembler of choice, not even to know if it's feasible. And maybe I don't really want to disasm at all - given the preface, I think that the rest of the book is a theological mess to put it gently.Anyway.The game promise a management sim with weirdo faith theme.It delivers it.Gets boring fast - for me, I ALT+F4 the game without reaching half an hour of playtime.I recommend it because it has an original religion-related setting that can be very funny and engaging for the casual player.But also, I have to say that 18€ on sale is a bit too much.I'm pretty sure that I won't bought this if only I had a Demo to play with.Because my lamentations have nothing to do with Early Access - the path where the game is heading is clear, and the roadmap is useful, but it will add things, not revolutionize the existing mechanics, as far I can tell.The art (graphics + music) is pretty nice.The UX (mostly UI accessibility and ease of use) is overall good.So, buy this if you loved Prison Architect or similar games.I suggest to take it on sale only, tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game has good bones, just a few issues:There is no way to tell a follower (member) to take care of their issues, ie) need sleep or food, they just die if it is not the scheduled time. This is especially bad if they die from sleep deprivation after being in the hospital because they were there overnight.The follower cap, not the members, starts too small. At only 15.Decor cost is too high for some objects and you'd have to fill up the room with decor to have a decent pristiege Goodwill missions should be a thing, to drop the heat score. Charity, etc.It has promise, but playing it right now is all about grinding. Getting enough points in whatever you need to level up is difficult. Money generation is ok, but maybe have an option for members to go out and work to bring in money.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good demo but not a good game. It absolutely has potential. I'm looking forward to some additional features as well as quality of life improvements. I'm glad that I have been watching for release and I'm glad that they did decide to make it possible to worship our lord and master Cthulhu. At this current state I would call this a magnificent chocolate cake that just doesn't pass the toothpick test yet. I do not regret buying it because I'm glad I could support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of genuine potential, however there are a LOT of kinks to work out that they need to address to make it really good. There's a lot of spelling errors in the dialogue which I find quite irritating - it isn't very clear how to fix things when they break (it says to right click, but the assigned worker usually never goes there), you can't see the quality of workers until after you recruit them which is annoying (because apparently dismissing too many people at once will affect your reputation), there aren't many missions, and there's a dialogue box that keeps saying to upgrade and you can't even do that. It really has a great concept though - the music is fitting, the animation is funny, the objects are hilarious etc. This game, again, has a LOT of potential, but if you leave it like this, I would think you invested a lot of time and effort for nothing on developing, and wasted the time of users.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun enough so far, but there are some issues that need to be fixed. namely; if you tell a character to do something, they prioritise basically everything else over that thing, it gets incredibly annoying... That and when a character needs to do a thing like eat when they're scheduled to sleep and they're not supposed to they go to that thing, but also try to sleep at the same time, which causes them to go into a break...TLDR; Game is fun, but there are bugs that need to be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I really do. But as of now it just isn't all there. I know it is early access and I'm sure a lot of my issues with it may be fixed. At its current state I just can't recommend it.The first half hour was fun and I genuinely enjoyed it. But as I progressed a bit and did a bit of looking around (in game and online) on what sort of stuff I can do in it, I felt underwhelmed. The layout of the research tree wasn't to my liking. It felt like I had to follow a fairly linear path instead of just doing my own thing. Creating different rooms was also just missing a lot. I didn't feel like there were a ton of options for the objects to put into rooms and there was definitely a very limited selection of decor. I felt like the missions were all kind of the same.Don't get me wrong; it has great potential. But the key word is potential. Maybe if I had played it a little longer I would have stumbled across something that made it significantly more enjoyable but I didn't see that coming. It really feels like a lesser version of Rimworld and a lesser version of Prison Architect were put together and then they took even more features out. Realistically, the DLC in Rimworld that adds the Ideologies makes a better cult game in my mind. There feels like there are way more options in Rimworld with that DLC. I'm not saying I want this game to be a Rimworld clone. But I am saying that a game that wasn't really intended to be a cult focused game can be played more like a cult focused game than this one at this moment.I love the aesthetics. I love the theme. I love the setting. But I can't say that I love the game. Yet. My biggest hope is that they really revamp this game while it is in early access.3.5/10
