name: Vertigo 2
detailed_description: Vertigo 2 is a single-player adventure built from the ground up for VR. Deep underground in the reaches of Quantum Reactor VII, you awake to finish your journey home. You’ll have to face bizarre alien flora and fauna leaking from other universes - and deadly android security forces whose job is to purge the reactor of all life. Try to determine who to trust as sinister agents lurk just out of sight. Key features include: Huge, bespoke world design – an incredible range of environments makes Vertigo 2 much more of an adventure than Vertigo 1. Enemy variety – dozens of creatures and robots are waiting to be discovered. Hybrid locomotion – both smooth locomotion and teleportation are viable. State of the art VR weapons – carry an arsenal of 14 weapons, all with unique reload mechanics. Fully voiced characters – a diverse cast brings the many characters of Vertigo 2 to life. Original soundtrack – hours of original songs and scoring. Intense boss fights – Vertigo is notorious for its ambitious boss encounters, and Vertigo 2 brings 10 brand new bosses. Substantial campaign – 18 chapters long, Vertigo 2’s story has many times as much content as Vertigo 1.
about_the_game: Vertigo 2 is a single-player adventure built from the ground up for VR. Deep underground in the reaches of Quantum Reactor VII, you awake to finish your journey home. You’ll have to face bizarre alien flora and fauna leaking from other universes - and deadly android security forces whose job is to purge the reactor of all life. Try to determine who to trust as sinister agents lurk just out of sight. Key features include: Huge, bespoke world design – an incredible range of environments makes Vertigo 2 much more of an adventure than Vertigo 1. Enemy variety – dozens of creatures and robots are waiting to be discovered. Hybrid locomotion – both smooth locomotion and teleportation are viable. State of the art VR weapons – carry an arsenal of 14 weapons, all with unique reload mechanics. Fully voiced characters – a diverse cast brings the many characters of Vertigo 2 to life. Original soundtrack – hours of original songs and scoring. Intense boss fights – Vertigo is notorious for its ambitious boss encounters, and Vertigo 2 brings 10 brand new bosses. Substantial campaign – 18 chapters long, Vertigo 2’s story has many times as much content as Vertigo 1.
short_description: Vertigo 2 is a single-player VR adventure. Explore the depths of the vast Quantum Reactor as you descend to finish your journey home.

_childDocuments_.review: The human mind may never comprehend how one person made this.Pros:The gun play is very smooth and fun. Reloads feel great.I did not play the first game, but the story still held my interest, especially near the end.The save system is flawless. Plenty of checkpoints and exactly where you would expect them to be.A crazy amount of endless enemy types will keep you on your toes.Weapon upgrades gave you something to search for.Cons:Minor bugs. Teleporting in the water launches you up into the air. Some minor NPC movement bugs. Overall, nothing game breaking.Bosses were a little boring. Just unload your weapons into them and move on.Collectables and secrets were few and far between, besides the weapon upgrade machines.Invisible walls block you from exploring certain places where I felt there should have been secrets or something.Overall, extremely well polished. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a must buy and a fun first person VR adventure.As a game made by just one person, Vertigo 2 is quite impressive. The game flow smoothly along with various cruxes and bosses along the way. The plot was basically un-decipherable to me and I lost all interest in what was actually happening. I lament the "multi-verse" trend in games and movies as it gives too much latitude to give writers the chance to do anything and everything at any turn. I liked: - The weapons are all unique and fun. Leveling up weapons is interesting. And the secret weapons are a bonus. - The music is fair. Not annoying. Not spectacular. - The movement is very good, using a split between smooth locomotion and teleport which makes sense. - The art isn't AAA, but it's good enough and the creativity of level design and enemies is enjoyable.- The play time is long. I play kind of slow and I spent a whopping 23 hours to complete it. The not as good:- The plot is too convoluted and confusing. - The voice acting was "ok" but not great. I understand that's a limitation of being a solo developer and budget.- The difficulty, on "normal" was at times a little frustrating. I re-played one boss 20 times before beating it. I did enjoy the challenge, but it was just a couple boss fights that seemed too much. I only turned the difficulty down once, for Cyber-Joseph at the end.All in all it's at the top of the pile currently for indie VR action adventure games. While the VR industry continues to grow, this is what we have until AAA studios find it profitable to make VR specific games. And I salute the indie devs that put so much hard work in to these games so we have things to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing VR for about 6 years (PSVR in 2017), and I've always sort of had that idea of what a VR game could be. A perfect VR game that pulls off everything it tries. A VR game that can pull off even the most ambitious ideas.This is it.This game took me about 8 hours to complete, and that was without doing all the secret side stuff. This game is hard, even on the easy difficulty. You actually have to think when you fight, and when you finally beat a boss after trying super hard, it feels super good. The guns feel very solid and polished. I will admit that when I first started, the guns felt a bit hard to control, but they felt good after like 20 minutes.The game runs really well, especially for how AMAZING it looks. And if it doesn't run well for you, then there's lots of settings for you to tweak.The dev is super chill. It's just one guy (other than the acting work), and he is super good and interacts with the community a lot.In other words,buy it buy it buy it buy it buy it buy it buy it buy it buy it

_childDocuments_.review: The developer clearly LOVES the Half Life series and Portal.Vertigo is excellently weird, in a lot of novel ways.  It acts as a linear corridor shooter in the same way as Alyx, but in a charming low-budget way.  It reminded me very strongly of Half Life 1 in a lot of places. Vertigo's story is its strong suit.  Things are strange, but the story stays within its established bounds and lets you learn the space.  The story branches in a couple places, and I haven't seen that executed well in VR before.The game is not perfect, notably in its gun selection.  A lot of guns feel a little bit awkward to use, and only a couple of them are truly exciting.  Some of them were simply outclassed by later ones.  The secret weapons feel like a punishment; when you pick one up, you're locked into a difficult encounter which you can only use the inferior secret weapon in.  Unlocking the bow in particular took like half an hour to escape from.  The map design is also sometimes a little awkward, especially in dark areas.Overall, one of the best shooters available on VR as a platform.  It doesn't exceed Alyx, but that makes sense because it's a small operation up against Valve.  Vertigo is a pretty great second, and far ahead of Boneworks.  I'm going to go hit up NG+ and see if I can't find more secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best VR game out there in my opinion. I have a bit of a VR addiction, and I do my best to buy or at least demo EVERY single VR game/experience that I possibly can. With that said - nothing else that I have found is as perfectly crafted for VR as Vertigo 2 is and I was extremely impressed from start to finish. This game was clearly crafted by someone that loves VR as much as I do and it shows at all times.  Every good virtual reality game mechanic that I have ever experienced can be found in this game, and on top of that, they even invented new ones that I had never ran into before. The story is fun, and at times hilarious but never anything less than interesting. It is the first VR game that I truly felt sad when I realized I was at the end of the game and I just wished it could keep going forever. Thankfully though  after you beat it you realize it kind of does go on forever thanks to all the cool replay-ability features the game has. There is a new game+ feature, different characters you can play through the game with all packing their own unique abilities/weaknesses and even a level creator feature Mario Maker style. The biggest highlight for me though is the graphics. This game is STUNNING and all of this is even more impressive when you learn it was pretty much all done by one guy. Just buy it, I can not wrap my head around a scenario where someone that truly loves VR would not absolutely LOVE this game from top to bottom. I wish every VR game could even be half as perfect as this one was in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many VR games and I can say with confidence this is the best VR game ever made, I would even consider it to be in the top 5 best games EVER. It does right what so many VR games have got wrong.CLIMBING:It has the best climbing I've ever seen in a VR game, no instant snapping like Alyx, no shaky "realistic physics" system like in Boneworks, it just lerps to your hands creating a bit of drag and it feels weighty and works perfectly. A while ago Zach made a video called "I solved VR ladders maybe", he definitely did.WEAPONS:Guns are great too, there are SIXTEEN! (I think) They all have fantastic reloads, and all feel impactful, with the exception of the trident SMG which seems to do very little damage compared to the others.The gun upgrade system is great too, with many to find and very interesting upgrades that often change up the weapon's gameplay in meaningful ways.STORY:The story and lore are great, I'm yet to get the second ending, so I can't comment on that (at the very tail end of my NG+ run). The writing is really funny, but what kept me interested in the story is the fleshed out lore, it feels like you are in a fully thought-out universe,  All in all I loved the feeling of being in this world.COMBAT:Combat feels really good, super satisfying, when bullets connect you know. It can be pretty tough towards the end of the campaign, even on normal, but it forced me to really plan out how I was going to beat a certain encounter, which I liked. There's an enormous variety of enemies, and with your huge arsenal of weapons combat never gets old. The cubehead guys are my favourite, they're funny :)PHYSICS:Physics interactions are pretty important in VR games, and Vertigo 2 does better than most, the physics on held items and guns feel great. fantastically weighty. Something I noticed loosely related to physics is the fact there's no hand poses on bigger items, when you grab a big cube for example your hands just close, without looking like you're grabbing it. I'm sure this was probably done due to glitches with it, I know the annoyance of working with hand poses, but it takes me out a bit. Chairs are also pretty glitchy they tend to fling you around if you attempt to grab them. Don't try to hold a weapon in a moving vehicle, if it touches anything inside the vehicle it will do some cyberpunk 2077 style stuff with your arm flinging it around everywhere and sometimes making your arms fly off into the distance. It looks like an issue with unity physics, but since you don't ever need to use your weapons in vehicles, maybe disabling them once you enter could fix it.Unfortunately another physics issue is doors, if you push through them in the wrong way you do tend to get your arms stuck in them for a few seconds which happens really often on 90HZ, I turned my headset up to 120HZ and the issue was a lot less pronounced. Most people will likely be running the game on 90HZ though. This issue isn't brought up very much so maybe it isn't an issue for most people.I also want to note that the IK on the arms is fantastic, honestly the best I've ever seen, it's not really physics related but there's nowhere better to put it.GRAPHICS: Graphics are really good, enemy models look great, The environments are sprawling and look beautiful. The particle effects are really nice, I love some good particle effects, also loved them in Vertigo Remastered. Weapon models are masterfully done. One issue I do have though is the human animation, honestly, it's not great, Brian looks pretty goofy, both his animations and his character model, but the entire game is made by one person so it's unfair to be annoyed over what is a small aspect of an incredible game, plus the animations of other creatures look good.CAMPAIGN: To me, the campaign is the most impressive part of Vertigo 2, the entire thing made just by Zach, It is absolutely jawdropping, the best campaign I have ever seen in a VR game, maybe besides Alyx (which suffers from boring combat, unlike Vertigo 2). There's tons of variety here, there's even a level that has 2 separate paths and bossfights, I'm not gonna spoil anything, you should go play it. It took me what I would guess is 12 hours, and I didn't even look for the weapon mods or secret weapons on my first go, there is tons to do in this game, and with the coming level editor and workshop support, the content here will be near limitless.SOUND:The music is really good, like really really good, I've already put a few tracks from the game into my playlists, I'm still in shock after hearing that Zach also produced all the music. The sound effects are also very good, and react to your environment.PERFORMANCE:I was so happy with the performance here, I have a PC on the older side and have pretty bad performance issues with most VR games, areas of Boneworks drop down to <30FPS for me,  Alyx is really stuttery and I can't play Blade and Sorcery in anything other than 1v1 mode without my FPS dropping below 90. In Vertigo 2 on the other hand I can run the game at 120HZ 95% of the time!! I have NEVER been able to do that with any other VR game before, I can barely run the home menu at that lmao. There was clearly a lot of work put into optimisation and my PC (and me) are very grateful. FINAL NOTES:If I'm missing anything I'll update the review, there's a lot here to talk about here so sorry if the review seems a bit rambly. If you plan on taking in the story I recommend playing Vertigo Remastered first, the combat isn't as good, but it's very entertaining and still a fantastic game. My final verdict is if you own a VR headset, I can't stress enough that this is the first game you should be playing, you'll 100% enjoy it.Also side note, Zach, if you're somehow reading this, I wanted to say you're a huge inspiration to me. I've almost finished highschool now, and have been making games for years, and am just now trying to learn VR development. The fact you've made this incredible VR game, starting in HS, mainly on your own is just mind blowing. I'm sure I'll never be able to undertake a project as ambitious as this, but your work really inspires me :)10/10 Game

_childDocuments_.review: The storytelling of Portal… The physical interactions of Boneworks… The weirdness of Willy Wonka… Wrap ‘em all together and you get Vertigo. A series made by… Wait, ONE PERSON?!That’s right, other than voice acting and some characters/world creation, the entirety of the playable games, [INCLUDING THE ENTIRE SOUNDTRACK], were made by Zach Tsiakalis-Brown. The immersion of this series is astounding. There are boss battles, massive landscapes, eldritch horrors beyond human comprehension…The game really is an impressive feat in game development. _childDocuments_.review: Like its predecessor, it's one of the best games in VR. For everyone who says, "There are no good VR games, everything is a tech demo," here you go. It is an actual, real game, made exclusively for VR, with competent, satisfying VR interactions, It took me 10 hours to complete, which, by VR standards, makes it an epic. Plus you get to save a robot society from commie robots! Or help them plunge robot society into a genocidal totalitarian nightmare if you want to be evil.And unlike most VR games that I finish once and am done with forever, I'm eager to do it all again in New Game+, so I can have all the guns from the beginning and get them fully upgraded. It's basically a Half-Life-style shooter with a cartoony Rick and Morty vibe. Lots of cool, bizarre alien environments to explore. Unbelievable that it was made by one guy. You're amazing! Please keep making VR games for us!Only complaints: Not much interaction with the environment. The character is painfully slow and there is no way to sprint/run. (Although I realize after I beat it that you can actually ready your teleport while moving by pressing down the stick.) Come on, stop coddling us. People will get used to VR. Once you get your VR legs, fast direct motion is fine .Been playing the HL2 mods, sprinting and strafing all over the place; it's fine.There were a few difficulty spikes that almost made me go "F this", especially where the checkpoints were too far apart, or where it saves 2 seconds from you getting killed. Had no shame in turning the difficulty down to Easy a few times, because even if I could get through it, it would have been more tedious than fun. And there weren't really any puzzles that I can think of...weren't there in the first one?So it's a great follow-up to the original, a completely new game, unlike some formerly great VR games where the sequel is a buggy unplayable mess consisting nothing but recycled content, cough cough WD:SaS:R cough cough, this is an all-new game, as good as the first. If you liked the original, absolutely play this. And if you haven't, get Vertigo Remastered right now.PS: WTF, upgrade stations don't reset on NG+? So I can never get any more than I already have unless I find any that I missed? What's the point of NG+ then? And there isn't even a console command to give all mods? >:-( PPS: Ok, there isn't a command, but if you use the command to enable to developer menu, there's a switch in the dev menu to give you all mods. Nice. Still, having all the mod benches reset while letting you keep the ones you have, so you collect them all again on NG+ until you have them all would have enhanced my enthusiasm and motivation for a second playthrough. Not doing that seems like a really weird choice that I don't understand the point of.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, it's one of the most anticipated VR games of this year.The problem is, it is just not fun and it making VR look really bad. The main problem is the gunplay, all guns are clunky and uncomfortable, handles are at different angles just to piss you off, for reloading you have to grab ammo from a floating point like 30 cm from your body which is hard to do while walking around in gunfights.  All enemies are tanks, every fight is a real slogfest where you mostly have to reload at least once for every enemy, they also all have 100% pinpoint accuracy. To win you basically have to figure out how many seconds it takes for an enemy to go pew and you just hide around a corner and pop out between shots. To beat enemies that charge at you you just teleport onto something so it will just run into the object you are standing on, like they did in games 20 years back.You walk extremely slowly so to dodge you have to use the teleport all the time, also just traversing the map you will mostly use teleport to stave off boredom. If you cannot use stick locomotion this game is probably unplayable for you.Still I forced myself to keep going hoping for some kind of stockholm syndrome to kick in until a few hours in I noticed it is way easier to just run/teleport past enemies so you don't have to fight. This made me realize I was not having fun at all.From what I heard this game is done by a single person and it really shows.I seriously DO NOT understand why ratings for this game are so high. If this really is one of the best VR games of this year it does not bode well for VR in general.It's exactly what we don't need in VR games, it feels like a huge step back. If I tried this game before I bought my first headset I would probably never have rolled into VR gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to write long-winded reviews but felled compelled to do so for this game for some reason.Story: Let me start of by saying that I have not played Vertigo 1 so I didn't necessarily understand everything the game had to offer, though it did a decent job catching me up to speed. Regardless, the story didn't really interest me too much. It was interesting enough to tie together the events of the game but I wasn't too invested in it. So don't expect too much from the story, though the gameplay makes up for that. I also wasn't really all that invested in any of the characters, most of them are quite one dimensional and uninteresting. Sometimes one would come through with a funny line or gag but most of them weren't anything to write home about.Gameplay: I'd have to say that the gameplay is one of Vertigo 2's biggest strengths. The movement is relatively responsive and customizable allowing for players to play any way they like. The guns the game has to offer are each quite unique especially when you take all of their upgrades into consideration which make them feel even more distinct. The guns are also really responsive and fun to use, I especially like their different reload functions. Speaking of the reload functions I quite liked how Vertigo 2 handles it's ammo system. You don't gather ammo like in most shooters, instead your ammo is manufactured at your waist and takes a certain amount of time to recharge. This means that you never have to stop using a gun for an extended period of time due to a lack of ammo, but you do have to switch weapons often during extended encounters keeping them feeling fresh. These encounters can sometimes be a bit too extended, going on for a bit too long in my opinion but I only felt that way about 3 or 4 times. Sometimes it does also feel like the gameplay falls into a bit of a loop just throwing encounter after encounter at the player but then shakes it up with the introduction of a new and unique enemy. Some chapters of the game also dragged on a bit too long for my liking whilst others were really short. Lastly I'll also mention the enemy variety which is quite impressive. There's quite a few different enemies which you'll want to tackle differently though some can definitely be too easy whilst some are unnecessarily tough. Ps. There's a reason Valve elected not to put runner zombies into Halve Life Alyx, you could have done the same and saved me a lot of trauma.The look: The game visually looks okay. The graphics aren't bad and most models look at least decent though some definitely look a bit less polished than others. It's something I can personally look past especially considering the relatively small team behind the models. One thing that did bother me a bit was how empty some of the environments looked. In a few sections the player is exposed to the outside world which looks very empty and bland except for the areas which are explorable which felt a bit odd. Maybe obstructing large open areas with mountains or buildings would have been better but who am I. Asides that the game also features a few scripted events/cutscenes in which the player is able to also move about. In these scenes npcs bounce right into each other and push one another around which definitely looks a bit goofy which can be a good or bad thing depending on the kind of person you are (I personally found it to be hilarious).Overall I had a good time with the game spending about 10 hours beating the entire story without getting every upgrade or secret weapon (which there's six of). The game seems to offer decent replayability with a chapter select and new game+ which I presume allows the player to experience the story again but with all their weapons available from the start.I would recommend this game to anyone who is in the mood for a fun VR shooter that you can just dip in and out of at ease. I'd give this game a 7.5~8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: One of the best and most polished VR games I've ever played. Must own.As far as sequels go, this game improves upon the first in so many ways. New and interesting characters to get invested in, unique branching story paths with multiple endings, expanded world building and higher stakes, all while maintaining its sense of identity from the first game. The arsenal of weaponry has been expanded and gunplay improved significantly - but with the caveat that none of the first game's tools and weaponry exist in the same form (except for one secret unlockable). Gone is dual-wielding, as now your off-hand is permanently assigned to the new teleporter. The new teleporter no longer acts as a portal that you can peek through before teleporting, which was a cool feature before but one that I didn't really miss once I got into the game. There is already more replayability out of the box, with an entire codex to fill out and complete, and an arsenal of weapons with unique upgrades hidden throughout all the levels - not to mention a 'New Game Plus' built right into the base game. The story overall was longer and well paced and kept me on my toes the whole time, introducing many new characters to interact with (as well as bringing back and fleshing out some of the originals), all with their own motivations and personalities. Level design is amazing all throughout, with so many unique locations and biomes to visit, and tons of new enemy variations lurking around each corner to test your reaction and put your new arsenal of weapons through their paces. Each of the weapons have unique reload mechanisms, and unlike the first game, ammo is now a thing - but its been implemented really well. Your ammo stores replenish over time, so if one gun runs dry you can just switch to another and let its magazines restore in the background. This forces you to rely on your entire arsenal, rather than just sticking to your favourite or best gun, which I found beneficial as it forces you become practiced with all of them. And you will need all of them by the end of the game. The bosses you must face are all very fun and unique, and often force you to use not just your arsenal of weapons, but also your surroundings to win against, forcing you to think quick in the moment. Overall I have very few complaints about this game, it is definitely one of the best singleplayer VR games to exist so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This, right 'ere is one of the best VR games ever made, if not the best one so far. For how much this game manages to cover in it's well paced gameplay, I'd kill for a third game. This game hits a mid point between some of the best vr games, and to me feels like a blend between something like Budget Cuts, experimental, and something like Half-Life: Alyx. Oh, and don't even get me started on the Rick and Morty-esc humor this game pulls at EVERY chance. The references don't stick out like a sore thumb, and really put a smile on the "all-around" gamers such as myself. This game feels like a VR game built by someone who loves the platform. Everything from the music, characters, environments, and gun-play make this game a killer experience, and should really be up there with the main titles people should recommend to new and veteran VR enthusiasts. The game has very little bugs, and it's largest down points are all thrown out the window with the game's charm. My only nit-picks are the middle to late game being a little draggy, and the animation. Even with that being said, I do believe this game is definitely my new favorite story-vr game. It's no boneworks, but it really doesn't need to be. This game manages to shine in ways most people may miss on their first playthrough, but it's little nods and secrets will really make you think and have a little laugh.In the great words of FUNKe, "Play it, then play it again, then play it again, and notice how hilariously overpowered you get compared to when you started."My point is, you've just wasted a bunch of time reading this, and should really just play the damn game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not to be that guy, but this is one of those neutral but tending to negative reviews.The game itself would be fine, if it wasnt for some factors, which mainly are:Story/dialogues - This is more a personal thing, but I really am not a fan of the humor. I know its supposed to be very cliche with lots of inside jokes, but its just not for me. Most of the dialogues i really wish i could just skip to continue the game. Maybe its because I didnt play the first game, which is why im not going to weight it that much into my opinion.Difficulty - Most of the time im doing very okay with little to no health loss. Suddenly you are thrown into a combat sequence where 5 enemies surround you, and you have to take multiple hits in a short amount of time. Suddenly there is a raptor killing you in 3 attacks. Trying to dodge the attacks? Sometimes it works, sometimes the enemy has an aimbot like accuracy. If it mostly werent for the sudden "you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥" fights, i wouldnt complain, but especially around the gate segment early on i had to reload so many times because you just get mowed down in a second. It feels like you have little to no control over the flow of the fight.secrets (?) - I probably missed half of the secrets because the game is very bad at telling you which way is the one to progress, and which way lets you explore a bit more. So you go down a path, realize that might be the correct way, you turn around, follow a different path and now you are locked out of the actual side path. Idk, some indicator that tells you "this is a no return way, you sure?" would be great.The gunplay, the sound effects are great, the interactivity and the weapon system are also very spot on. Enemy variety is the same as the game difficulty. You have absolute useless bullet sponges that hit like a wet towel, you have enemies just taking 2 shots to kill you. Its very much all over the space.I will probably finish this game and then see if i actually put in a thumbs down, i got it on a big discount so it is okay for that price, but if i would have gotten it for full price, i would be probably very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most ambitious and creative VR games out there. It does not hold back and excels on it's thrilling gameplay, gunplay and combat, beautiful environments to explore, it's witty writing of humor, incredibly fun boss fights to encounter, it's pretty underrated game soundtrack, engaging story line, and just an overall fantastic labor of love of what makes people enjoy VR. The insane developer who put this whole game together, Zach Tsiakalis-Brown, creates a  Sci-Fi action FPS VR game with quantity, polish, and loads of content to provide an amazing VR experience.  10-14 hour long campaign's pacing is well timed and brings out new ideas for you to play to make it way more unique then most singleplayer VR games. I have the utmost most respect for Zach's work and hope that it gets the recognition it deserves. When people list of essential VR games (games like   etc,) for people to see what VR's full potential is,  is without a doubt up there! Try the demo and see if you like it, It shows a good amount of what this game has to offer!!Note that while it can be intense for some players due to multiple vehicle rides, screen shake, and a plethora of effects in the campaign to lead to motion sickness, there are complimentary comfort options to make your experience smooth as possible for your liking!

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is one of the best and on my opinion the hardest story game I've played so far.The game is very polished and the gun play is really good feeling the voice acting and the replayability of the game is really good and worth the the $32 and definitely recommend if you want a story shooter game and want a challenge i definitely recommend it(Read this before you play!!!)There are levels that contain submerged monsters and big fish in water if you have submechaniphobia a fear of submerged things than try to skip some parts or don't play it! _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who's played Half Life: Alyx twice over, beaten the campaigns of both Walking Dead: Saints and Sinners and Bonelab. Someone who's put hundreds upon hundreds of hours into Boneworks, Beat Saber, Blade and Sorcery, VRChat, and Pavlov... I think Vertigo 2  just be the best VR game I've ever played.You should get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must have - in my top 3 vr games of all time.PROS: Extremely satisfying reloading (for the most part, more on that later)Very interesting storyActual funny momentsRuns perfectly on my end with no bugs encountered throughout my entire gameplay Beautiful varying settings on many different levelsInsane musicI have no mouth, and i must screamCONS:Sometimes its hard to grab the ammo from your side in the middle of a fight, its too offset to the side and it can take multiple tries to actually grab it.The game is pretty hard. I played on normal mode for 4/5 of the game but when the game started throwing in hordes of enemies it became too hard (some people may like it but i think it would be better to have 4 or 5 difficulties instead of 3).Despite me just talking about how hard the game is, some bosses are just too easy. E.g the last boss was one of the easiest ones, it would be harder to fight 15 robots than the boss.Things i would like to change:I really liked the AK-47 but i didnt like the fact that there was no indicator of how many bullets are left in the mag - i dont want a bullet counter however that would make it worse but i think you should be able to rack the slide slightly to see if there is a bullet inside or have it like halo where the shooting sound changes when the ammo is running out.I also think the bosses couldve been a lot better. A lot of them werent really unique in how youre supposed to kill them; just walk in circles and shoot. I wish that instead of the normal weak spots on a boss, there should be environmental ways to kill them. For example, the first boss couldve been different where its shield comes on straight away instead of after a certain amount of damage dealt to it. To get rid of the shield you do the same thing with the extinguisher grenades but instead of shooting it again, there couldve been large fire extinguishers/ CO2 tanks/ water tanks around the room that you shoot to slow down the boss so that you can then go for the killing blow in the end.Manual saves instead of relying on checkpointsIn conclusion, this is at least 10x better than bonelab, thats all i have to say.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences one could have.Vertigo Remastered was already a great game, although was lacking in variety and really leaning into the potential that VR gives. Vertigo 2 however does all of that, and then much much more.Weapons don't only have great designs, reloading them is both infinitely satisfying and greatly intuitive. There are plenty of puzzles that make full use of VR, even in small ways that help make doing them fun even when the concept is simple. But what surprised me most of all was all the hidden content.While vertigo remastered didn't have much in the way of extra content, Vertigo 2 has so much unique content to find, not just in terms of upgrades, which themselves are all unique and even upgrades with simple premises (i.e. faster fire rate) add more detail onto your weapons. Secrets could contain secret bosses, weapons, or even just jokes that were well worth the search.What really had me was that it felt that so much love was put into the game, into the reloading, the jokes, the overall atmosphere felt like there was fun had making it. On the main story, its generally simple and it makes one of the last choices you have in the game so much more impactful. Its fleshed out way more in 2 then 1, but still keeps you shooting your way through robots, aliens, and what not to get home.Its a very, very easy buy. even at full price, its unreasonable the price for this game with the level of content and fun which is present.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Look, Half Life: Alyx's cinematic moments, attention to detail and graphics are very very cool, I agree, I've played it four times. However, I just played this game for the first time, and holy hell it's amazing. First of all, the gunplay is amazing. There are 8 main weapons (The shotgun is just mwah) and idk how many 'hidden weapons' which I only managed to get two of, but will achieve all of them before I stop playing this game. The enemy variety in this game is brilliant, and the bosses were my first proper VR bosses, and for whatever reason reminded me of when I first played Splatoon 2's offline 'story' mode on my switch, this massive boss in an arena with tons of mobility, it was just perfect. I have crippling thalassophobia (fear of oceans) and there was a few points where I nearly through my very expensive headset into my very expensive PC. This game is a must buy and is genuinely my favourite VR game, knocking Alyx down to second place, and I'm considering buying Vertigo Remastered once I'm 100% finished - I might even go full achievement hunting for this game.PS:- I love the cameos in this game the portal references were absolutely beautiful.Edit: Just a couple things I missed/forgot to talk about - There are some choice making elements in this game that are pretty seamless and can result in you getting different guns and fighting different bosses on your travels, and as far as I'm aware, and I could be wrong, some choices can open up different endings.. maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: 45 minutes in. I am very, very impressed. Cartoony? Absolutely. Physics? Beautiful. Surprises? Everywhere. Artistic consideration? Yes. Combat? Super fun. _childDocuments_.review: Finished Vertigo 2 last night and I must say, **WOW**! The game is stunning and unique from start to finish. The journey took a total of over 19 hours, which is looong considering the attention to detail and top notch gameplay. Each chapter is noticeably different than the previous and the level design is incredible. The brilliant design and drastically different levels offer a truly unique game with nothing else like it in all of VR. Each chapter also has hidden areas of the maps that keep you peaking in every corner (maybe even through what seems to be a closed door…).There are a huge variety of enemies, that have multiple different attacks and even enemies who fight other enemies. There are over 10 extremely fun and unique weapons, with 5 or 6 hidden weapons that you *really* need to be looking for the entire game to find. There are numerous upgrades to each weapon that adds something great. Upgrades can change the strategy for that weapon or it can make it go from maybe your least favorite to all of a sudden your go to.There is a solid story, beautiful visuals, tons of adjustable settings, top notch soundtrack and audio (one characters voice is the only thing that seemed off about the game), bHaptic support (thanks to @Florian Fahrenberger who not only did the bHaptics for the game but is also recognized in the credits! Twice!), smooth controls, lots of achievements, different paths you can take that changes the journey (and weapons) and a well polished VR experience that we are fortunate to play & will have you playing again & again.Vertigo 2, while not perfect, is as good as VR gets in 2023. I caught myself stunned on numerous occasions where I’d just stop and look around the environment. There was a psychedelic experience that was mind melting and a part of a level that legit felt like I was in another realm of life or fever dream.If you have a PC & VR, **buy Vertigo 2**. It’s games like this that make all the ups & downs of VR, well worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the full version of this game because I enjoyed the demo. It started off pretty well and then several issues became apparent. First of all, teleportation is pretty bad. With the Index controllers, you must push the left stick in to teleport. Then streaks of light flash at you every move you make. There are also several sections where you must enter water. You can't teleport through water so you must go into the options and change the setting to full locomotion to make it through the water then go back into the options to re-enable teleportation. The constant reloading is also a pain to deal with in my opinion. Each gun only fires a few shots and I was constantly getting overwhelmed by sections of numerous enemies while trying to reload. There is also no trainer or cheat code with a true no reload feature. The graphics in this game are also outdated and at times the animations are janky. There are also some pretty harsh frame rate drops every time the game auto-saves. I also did not enjoy the forced sections where you must fly in a helicopter and ride in a mine car, as experiences like that tend to cause me some nausea. Overall, I lost interest in playing so I cannot recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Writing is obnoxiously corny at times, but aside from that a phenomenally well made and fun VR game. Highly, highly recommended. One downside, and one that you'll commonly see people mention, is the difficulty. This can be solved twofold; one, try and hit headshots, they reward you with ~3x damage per hit, which massively helps in fights. Aside from that, know your enemy. Running headfirst with a shotgun every time will get you killed.But if youre still finding the game too hard, just turn it down. I played through the game on Normal mode, but some bosses were still just a bit too much, and I turned it to Easy temporarily during the fight, then set it back. It's a minor annoyance, but makes the game much more enjoyable. Don't torment yourself, put it on Easy or Story if you need to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything a sequel should be. Took what the first game did brilliantly well and made it better in almost every way. It took me around 10 hours to beat the game on my first run through, but I'll definitely play it again on New Game Plus.If you have a VR, do yourself a favour and pick this one up. Seriously, its good.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is so long. It just kept going and going, and just when I think it ends, it keeps going even more. I had been at it for well over 12 hours in order to complete it, and the journey throughout was outstanding.Games nowadays often tend to have a few-hour-long campaign, especially with live service games that focus more on multiplayer. VR games are often even shorter than that. The fact this one went on for as long as it did, especially considering it was primarily developed by one guy, is hella impressive.I've never felt more stunned in a VR campaign since 's first debut. It was visually impressive throughout as well.The guns themselves, they all feel great. They all have some nice weight to them, they each have their own unique designs and traits. The reloads feel extra smooth as well, something that a lot of VR shooters don't focus on too terribly much, especially for games with more original, sci-fi designs, versus realistic guns like you see in  or . A personal favorite of mine is the Trident SMG, the way the magazine slots in feels so satisfying, not to mention the way it ejects slightly when pressing the eject button, and then you can either pull it out manually by hand or knock it out fully with a fresh mag.The ammo is virtually infinite, because while reloads are physical and you can reload endlessly, you can only have so many magazine slots per gun at a time, so every time you take a fresh magazine, a cool-down appears to regenerate an empty ammo slot. Empty slots regenerate one at a time until you're at max capacity again. If you use up all your ammo too quickly, you have to wait for at least one slot to finish regenerating a mag before you can reload. There's also a setting to have guns reload automatically in your inventory when not in use, so it's full when you pull it back out again.One of my favorite VR games of all time is , also known as  (come on, Early Access, over a hundred updates, an update every Friday for 7 years, made by one guy, what's not to like?), so as soon as I heard Anton Hand's voice (as well as spotted some sosigs later on), I squealed like a girl.Some sections reminded me visually of Black Mesa's Xen reimagining. It all looked pretty, the lighting and atmosphere helped set the tone.Something the game does that's interesting too, is frequently change the setting/location. Most games that do it often lead to mass confusion, and it's not very appealing. But  seems to pull it off successfully. Granted, it  get just a little confusing sometimes, but I enjoyed it all the same. Each location had its own style and theme to it. Its own colors and details. It was practically eye candy in most cases.As long as the campaign is, I will admit there was a level or two that I felt overstayed their welcome, and were a little too long for comfort. But the rest was right as rain, so 1 bad thing out of 100 other good things is impressive regardless.Can't wait to see the Sandbox update.  has significantly more in store compared to , so I bet plenty of people will have even more tools and toys to play with.I would also love to see some mutators like in the first game. Such as removing the cool-down for ammo regeneration, so you can reload as many times as you want without having to wait for a slot to finish after you've reloaded so many times in a short time span. Or a hit-scan option like in the original.Thanks for an amazing experience, regardless. Almost makes me wish Anton could port some of the guns to . I bet that Annihilator Shotgun would feel right-at-home in 's arsenal.

_childDocuments_.review: Jaw on the floow. That's how I would describe this game.Some people might dislike the humor and quirkiness (try the demo and you will know). And some people might only ever want to play multiplayer games. For everybody else, this is a no-brainer purchase recommendation. The game has been, and will probably be in the future, often compared to Half-Life Alyx, and I get it. While the graphics might not be quite up there, the interactions and polish are. And the creativity and environments might actually surpass it. In every single one of the 18 chapters, you are bombarded with a plethora of new creatures, weapons, and breathtaking worlds.Jaw on the floor. That about sums it up.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game and it's absolutely insane that this was largely made by one person, but there's definitely some jank and rough edges in here. The worst was physics bugs during some sequences that made me die repeatedly. I also found the combat to be a slog at times. I'd attribute this to balancing issues and the enemy AI being pretty basic, but hey maybe that's a skill issue. Where the game shines is with the visuals and level design, it's often jaw-droppingly beautiful and it does a brilliant job of using the sense of scale you get in VR to it's fullest

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for a couple years now and I'm glad to say it did not disappoint!  It's got rock-solid gunplay, a large variety of enemies, large and detailed environments, an engaging story, and interesting characters.  The best part though is the boss fights, some of the best I've seen in VR!  The only complaint I really have is some weird pacing issues.  Specifically, some parts feel like they overstay their welcome a bit.  Nothing nearly as bad as the centipod fight from the first game though lol.  Vertigo 1 was sorely underappreciated and I really hope Vertigo 2 gains more traction.  Zach deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is one of the most impressive games I have ever played. _childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a good game and it's fun with pretty visuals, but I don't know what people are smoking to compare this to Alyx and Boneworks/labs. _childDocuments_.review: Already very good. High quality game from graphics to physics interactions to story to gameplay. Lots of little gimmick toys to play with in the first level alone. Makes nice use of VR with interesting enemies and locations. Already had a lot of fun with this one and can tell I'm going to enjoy the rest. This is an actual full-fledged VR GAME, not a tech demo or the thousandth 'interact with guns in excruciatingly detailed and ultimately boring and janky ways' game. An original, fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: My setup: Valve Index, RTX 3090, i9 10900K, 32GB, and Win10. It's not easy communicating the greatness of the game. Maybe better with an example. I had this issue of having about 20 soldiers to battle and one big alien monster. I ended up hiding under a desk, while the monster killed all the soldiers, lol. The monster did get badly hurt, and when meeting it I killed it with a single shot.This illustrates the way you have to think in Vertigo 2. There's no way you easily could take out that many soldiers or such a powerful alien monster. Well, you could shoot them all, but that would be difficult and time-consuming.In another place, I met a similar monster, and I fled - but found a platform and could shoot it from a long distance.The crazy content means you're constantly on the edge of your seat in Vertigo 2. There are aliens who only attack you, if you attack them - so do not shoot at them first. I'm doing a lot more thinking in this game than I anticipated, especially for the harder battles.AI is pretty good, had an alien friend following me, and it did so nicely. Then again, this is a first person shooter, you're not going to meet anything defeating you in chess ;-)Graphics are getting better later in the game, some of the first levels may suffer from being designed many years ago, while later levels look more fresh. There are several low-poly models looking like PS4 assets, and many low-res textures. But you also got high-res textures for guns, and textures look great when they are 10 feet away or more. You can find great dynamic shadows too, all in all graphics are great, animations too. Sound is excellent with the Index speakers.There are several combat situations which don't need to bow to Alyx, but generally Vertigo 2 is below the quality of Alyx, then again everything is. Vertigo 2 shines with its crazy universe, dark humor and semi-insane story - there's no other VR game just remotely close to it. Vertigo 2 is a surreal experience, and a perfect example of a virtual/alternate reality.My rating of the game would be 9.5/10. Alyx transcends the ordinary scale with 15/10.Btw, seems that Vertigo 2 only supports native SteamVR drivers, thus no OpenXR and no native Meta driver support. Of course no issue for Index users. Vertigo 2 supports Index finger tracking too.For left-handed users: note that currently left-handed controls are not working optimally - teleport has been assigned to left thumbstick, and I often teleport into enemies. Making custom controller bindings, I can't get teleport to work on the right Index controller - also you may need teleport to defeat the first boss and to jump correctly. Dev has promised to fix this March 31, but nothing has happened yet.Also not all parts of the game perform optimally, around the first boss some stutter is unavoidable, even reducing res to 20% (twenty!) the stutter was there, so it had nothing to do with needing a more powerful gpu - but no big deal, it was gone in the following level.With the Index res 280%, 4xMSAA and all other graphics settings maxed I get solid 90 fps - only dipping below near the first boss.PS. I did not like the playable demo - if you're considering buying this game try the full version instead, you can test it for up to 2 hours and refund if you don't like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: No clue how a single person (yes, one singular person made just about this whole game) manages to make a better VR game than most AAA can. In a lot of regards, if you ask me it passes even Boneworks and Half Life Alyx! The gun play is great, the enemies are interesting and varied, the bosses are (very) difficult challenges, the jokes are funny, and somehow? There are very few bugs. Possibly the best VR game on the market right now, and I'd recommend anyone with a headset (and to be honest, a fair amount of skill) play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is excellent and is deserving of every bit of praise. The game was very engaging throughout, with only a few parts of the game feeling truly frustrating. Unfortunately, these parts are all within the latter half of the game, leaving a great impression, but a bit of a frustrating near-end experience.I cannot see very well in VR, so I especially struggled with the stealth enemies. The fact that you had to face 6-8 of them and they only became fully visible when they were right in your face dogpiling you, it was really quite frustrating, and i ended up having to cheese the last confined room with all the stealth bots (not fun).I also struggle with being overwhelmed in VR and most players can. The sheer amount of enemies this game can throw at you, especially sniper enemies which make it impossible to move around some sparse environments, makes it a case of trial and error sometimes.Apart from these main issues (which ended up being quite a big two issues, but whatever) I absolutely loved Vertigo 2, and highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: You need to play this game, seriously, you need to play it. From the weapons to the enemy's you fight, everything feels really smooth. Just the fact that the game never really gets repetitive makes it better than most VR shooters nowadays. The amount content is insane, I've played for about 15 hours now and I haven't even done everything there is to do. Bottom line is, the game is fun and long.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun in the sense of level design and story telling, but the combat kind of struggles. The enemies (unlike in Alyx) will always aim directly at your head with laser accuracy. Which IMHO makes for a bad combat experience. You cant really take cover and shoot from behind it, they will rush you and get right in your face, and if you peak out of cover you will die pretty fast since they all instant lock to your head. The enemies with slow projectiles are manageable, but ones with normal weapons kill ya fast (even on Normal). There are tons of secrets, easter-eggs and unlock-ables so it does have its replay value. This game definitely takes a lot of inspiration from Source games like Half life. Over all a fun experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, like on par with Half Life: Alyx levels of greatness. The level design is just really fantastic and varied. You'll find 0 repeated puzzles in here. The art style is just cartoon-ish enough where you'll be immersed in all of the landscapes but every texture doesn't need to be incredibly detailed to be convincing. The enemies and boss fights are all unique from each other and all have their own quirks. And the gunplay, y'all the gunplay is easily the best I've had in a VR game. Each weapon, and there's like over a dozen weapons, is unique yet has it's own strengths, weakness, and skill curves. And they are all fun to use, even the crappy starter pistol has cool animations and textures and all that. Then there's a few dozen upgrades, that are of course all unique, but they all somehow feel useful. Like each of the up-gradable weapons has up to 5 upgrades, and despite all the weapons being different, and all the upgrades also being different, they each feel unique and useful in some cases. Then there's the story and the lore, which are surprisingly developed for like a 10 hour linear story line game developed by one dude. No spoilers, but when picking which ending I really felt like my decision made a difference in the realms. Also there's this level of humor that's infused though out the whole game that I really appreciate and makes me smile, especially with the loading screen tips. Just easy 11/10, you should buy it at full price and play the whole thing. Honestly this game is so good, I beat the story, then immediately turned on New Game + to beat it again and find all the secrets I missed, which I NEVER do.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 added a hole lot of new and exciting developments to the game play and story. The game play is more based around half life alyx, but the system came from vertigo 1 and still holds strong, I never found myself looking at my holster to find my gun taking me away from battle it's just one button and hand moment. _childDocuments_.review: A superb VR adventure that feels charmingly handmade and that's jam-packed with creativity. While it's occasionally rough around the edges, you can still tell just how much effort has been packed into the experience.The game has a great sense of humor with strange and memorable characters (some of which have questionable voice acting). There's so much variety in the scenarios that recounting every cool moment to friends would make you sound completely mad. By the end of it all, Vertigo 2 becomes a grand journey in which you cross a vast distance and conquer countless unpredictable obstacles. Every chapter and set piece has something new and exciting to offer. You're constantly looking forward to what the game has planned next.There's also some pretty deep lore to a story that mostly involves gunning your way through each dimensional anomaly. While all the jabbering felt out of place at first, eventually the amount of background stuff going on does make you feel like you’re an essential part of a greater conflict.Gameplay is just as strong as the presentation with just as much escalating variety. Your arsenal is stylish and weird with sound effects, reloads, and impacts never ceasing to satisfy. Your robot and unusual alien foes offer an amusingly diverse range of targets to point and shoot at. The bosses always make for great climatic moments for their respective chapters.A few other notes about things that bothered me here and there. Controlling the two-handed weapons comes into conflict with the game's emphasis on physics in gameplay, which makes them difficult to operate precisely. Also, enemies are pretty tanky on normal difficulty. The number of shots it can take to down a single enemy can really prolong densely-packed combat sequences. Switching to easy halfway through made for a lot more manageable (but not trivial), conveniently paced, and believable gunplay experience.As for VR comfort, you kinda have to be immune to motion sickness to get through a few parts. Anyone with thalassophobia should be prepared for a number of sudden and unwelcome underwater segments. Additionally, there’s a lot of time spent in dark, cramped, horror-like conditions that aren’t too overwhelming but can be seriously uncomfortable.In the end, Vertigo 2 was a fantastic excuse to pick up VR again for the first time in a while. It’s awesome to finally have another deeply immersive, well-polished, and masterfully creative linear single-player adventure in VR’s recently-stagnant repertoire. I'm more than ready to recommend it to anyone looking for another reason to play VR. Especially if you're into Valve games. Some of the references to the game's obvious inspirations here are pretty shameless.

_childDocuments_.review: Really awesome game. It's awe inspiring how you're expected to multitask in this game and especially with the harder fights how there can be multiple mechanics being utilized while you're reloading, throwing grenades, teleporting around etc. You will have to use the teleport in this as there's no increased walking speed and though its not super comfortable having to move the left stick and hold it to teleport around, it does kinda feel like doom vfr. Playing this can be alot of work but it's more engaging than any VR game i've ever owned. You'll do a lot of shooting and a lot of walking and a few decent puzzles on the way to the core. If you struggle with VR controls this is going to be really challenging for your average player. I've never died as many times in VR as I have on here though I think it's reasonable overall.My only compaint is that instructions could be clearer... for example youre given a sword for a boss but no clarification or warm-up for it as if you'd just know immediately what to do and that youll pull the trigger when boss is in weakened state. There are situations like that throughout so enjoy the journey and prepare to get lost occasionally

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; One of the best VR games I've ever played. The gameplay/fun factor is AAA level quality, but the graphics and voice acting are not.PROS:- Shooting feels great. There are multiple weapons that are unique and have their own reload mechanics. - The VR mechanics are very polished- The levels are unique and interesting. - Enemies are varied with different attacks, speed, health, etc. which makes each combat encounter feel fresh.- There are secrets to be found, exploration pays off- Bosses that are unique and not just bullet sponges. You need to learn their attacks to figure out how to defeat them.CONS (I had a tough time coming up with this list, meaning these cons that I listed are very minor in my opinion):- The voice acting is hit or miss. This game was mostly made by 1 person with help from a few others so this con gets a pass from me.- Some of the textures can be bland. - The dialogue is mostly funny but there were also lines that made me cringe.THIS GAME MAY NOT BE FOR YOU IF:- You're someone who needs realistic graphics. As you've probably already noticed the art style is more cartoony. For me this isn't much of a con as the art style fits the mood of the game. And I'm having so much fun that I'm immersed by the gameplay and well polished VR mechanics without needing realism.- You're looking for an easy game to just breeze through. The game can be very difficult in some spots, specifically bosses. It's not Elden Ring by any means but there are a few areas that I have died many times. You can easily access the dev console to cheat your way through if it's too much for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the greatest VR games... no.. VIDEO GAMES I have ever played. This game wasn't just made with passion, it was made with LOVE and a seemingly infinite amount of creativity. With references to portal, half life, H3VR, and so many more, there is so much in this game that comes together to genuinely make it one of the best VR games I have ever played. Fair warning though: It throws basically every phobia you could possibly have at you. Thalassophobia (fear of the ocean), Nyctophobia (fear of the dark), Automatonophobia (fear of mannequins), Entomophobia (fear of bugs), Aracnophobia (fear of spiders. To a lesser degree here. There are some eight legged enemies in this game but they aren't exactly spiders, more robotic... things with 8 legs), and so many more that I've lost track of but those are the major ones. All terrifying yes, but it's genuinely all worth it for this incredible experience of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: IMO this may be the best FPS VR game. Amazing how many different worlds and enemy types you encounter, the level of creativity is impressive. I also think they have the best implementation of the dash/teleport I've seen for VR first person games — works smoothly for fast-paced shootouts, boss fights, and exploring terrain, even some mild "platforming" segments. The "selfie" mechanic is super clever and should be in every VR game.A couple minor quality of life and polish issues, but that can easily be forgiven considering how small the dev team is. Overall a totally unique and wonderful game. One of the best in VR!

_childDocuments_.review: Never even heard of Vertigo 1 which was apparently criminally underrated, and this right is AT LEAST the second best VR game ever made, possibly the very best depending on your taste. Because this is a very Half Life inspired game it's easy to compare to the other "best VR game ever": Half Life Alyx.  Cool setpieces and a focus on environments work very well for VR, as does shooting with interesting reload mechanics. This is the main element for Boneworks and Alyx as well. I think the enemies are appropriately paced and they are very varied, with hilarious designs. Game is not very serious and actually funny a lot of the time. Every second of this game introduces something new to keep it fresh all the way through.  The game has all the physics of other titles like Boneworks and Alyx, making the world feel very present. Breaking glass, having the spent magazine eject and become a physical item you can pick up, being able to throw and move most things in the world, having your gun collide with objects and walls. It all seems quite simple but it's a must for VR games, and here it's extremely well done. Unlike Alyx this game goes much further with VR, never shying from things that can cause extreme motion sickness (dude the boat), but that also makes it much more dynamic and interesting. Still criminally underrated buy now this is Alyx tier ong no cap

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true exhibition of what VR is capable of. Smart, diverse, large-scale, 2d games quality level VR game with good plot, interesting characters, good gunplay, a vast world to explore. If you need a short description, this game feels a lot like crossover between Men In Black 1, Half-Life and Rick and Morty. At times, I would even say that I see some inspiration taken from Cowboy Bebop. And this mix works so well. Goods are delivered and they are good.And all this achieved by one person. Honestly, it blows my mind. You can expect game of such high quality from a huge team of gamedev experts, but behind Vertigo 2 stands just one guy. A true labor of love. P.S. If you never played Vertigo 1 - Vertigo 2 offers story recap, but please, do yourself a favor and play the first game too - it's also one of the best games made for VR so far, though Vertigo 2 still is a major improvement,

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Guns are fun to shoot, reload and use. Enemies are fun, challenging and varied. Environments are visually impressive and fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Wow.  I just finished the game after 20 hours, and it was enjoyable all the way through.I ran it on an RTX 2060 and I didn't think the graphics were lacking.  My HMD is a Quest 2 and I played it entirely over AirLink with no issues noted stemming from using WiFi instead of a cord.I wouldn't say the game is perfect with some jank here and there, which I would expect from a VR game.  Considering I'm not actually holding anything other than a controller, pretending I'm grabbing and eating a healing fungus isn't going to be perfect.I love the exploratory aspects of going through an abandoned facility, and this had that while also providing a reasonable amount of difficulty with mobs and bosses.I would definitely recommend this to other VR players (and I have), and I am looking forward to playing through the NG+ (which I didn't realize there would be) and also playing through Vertigo Remastered.

_childDocuments_.review: You want a single player VR game with a full-length 10+ hour campaign in the vein of a Half-Life game? This is the game you want! Gunplay is really good, and it has this unique system where you don’t pick up ammo in the world, but instead, new magazines gradually re-spawn in your pocket. This means you don’t need to hunt around for ammo, but you still need to be conservative and alternate what guns you’re using. The balance can be a bit off for some of them. The AK shreds enemies, but the SMG feels like you need to dump an entire magazine into even basic enemies to kill them. Likewise, the shotgun also feels very under-powered, which is a blasphemy for a video game shotgun, especially for one named "Annihilator". The reloading is really satisfying, with many guns having a weird gimmick that make them unlike any other VR guns. It can be a bit finnicky sometimes. You can do a magazine reload with the AK, but the game is very fussy about how quickly or slowly you need to hit the magazine to knock it out. It seems like it only works half the time. There’s a big variety of enemies and worlds, there’s just a lot of content in general! It’s a very impressive effort for a one-man dev team.My biggest gripe with this game is the difficulty of the bosses. Overall, the game is challenging, but the bosses (save for 2 of them) cause the difficulty curve to take a sudden spike. A lot of their attacks do heavy damage and are very difficult to avoid. Which really isn’t helped by how damned slow your character is and how long you need to stand around waiting for the teleporter to reach maximum teleport distance. It’s honestly only really useful for dodging short-range attacks. One of them even commits the cardinal sin of having a swarm of quiet, tiny enemies who you can’t see unless you’re looking down. So while you’re fighting the boss, these little bastards have snuck up on you and are chipping away at your health. For pretty much all the bosses, I had to turn the difficulty down to easy, since I was sick of wasting my time. Thankfully, you can change the difficulty setting at any time.Overall, Vertigo 2 is an excellent fully-featured single player VR game that needs to be in the library of any Half-Life fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Well, that was amazing. I saw some footage beforehand (thanks habie247) and after a lot of drift issues, anxiety, fear, and almost refunding the game since it got so bad... I am so glad I didn't. The game is so well done and one of the most visually captivating VR games I've ever played. Gunplay is perfect, Story is a blast, Humor is great, but expect some freaky/fearful moments. No jumpscares necessarily but times you are in the dark fighting creepy aliens. My experience was mostly smooth, some crashes after loading a level and left controller drift (which didn't appear to be on my end oddly) overall this game has reached my top 10 favorite of all time. Only fitting I give it 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: While at work I watched a review from Habie147 on this game, since I was fishing around for new VR games at the time. I watched the review and was very impressed by what I saw, then bought and installed the game the very same night - boy am I glad I didI don't know what it is, but I  the 'infiltrate a top secret/high-tech facility' setting to bits.The story meanders away from that here and there, but does so in a way that makes sense and doesn't take you out of it.The gunplay is a little dated on some weapons: they have the movement sensitivity toned down to feel 'heavy', no two-handed weapons have a virtual stock (not a massive dealbreaker in this game), some weapons feel quite weak without damage upgradesOn the flip side, the movement feels good, all the weapons have the right amount of physics interactions to them without any jank. The game looks and sounds fantastic plus the soundtrack is pretty damn good. Oh and to top it all off there's an AKM in the game and it's probably one of the best guns in the entire game.Some of the boss fights were a little annoying to do, namely the Saplord and Cyber Joseph. Died LOTS during those fights. The pair of Centaurs was also quite annoying since they do massive damage and take a lot of it. I didn't like how some parts of the game NEEDED the teleport function since it felt kind of cheap.All in all, great game with a couple of relatively minor snags along the way. Definitely worth it though

_childDocuments_.review: There are adventures and new places quite literally around every corner. It offers a perfect blend of discovery, story, combat and puzzles - being the closest thing you'll get to actually  a fun, sci-fi action movie. The diversity in both scenery and gameplay in this game is seriously impressive. The gameplay is very smooth, and much love is put into detail.The fact that basically every second review of this game here compares the title to Half Life: Alyx should tell you everything you need to know. It might not have HL:Alyx' level of polish, graphics or finesse, but it has a whole lot of character to more than make up for that. It shines  it can take itself less seriously and simply provide a fun, wild ride.When I found this game (and the first one) I couldn't believe that I never heard of it before.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the end of chapter 10, I'm convinced this is one of the best VR games that has been made so far.The environments and music are genuinely amazing. The primary weapons are satisfying and fun to use and upgrade. The gunplay is challenging yet rewarding.Be warned, though; some of the bosses are very tough. I appreciate a good challenge and have played many VR games, but I ended up using god mode for the chapter 10 boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this was (mostly) created by one developer is truly incredible. It took me about 9 hours to complete the campaign, and now with New Game +, differing endings, a chapter with a branching story path, there is enough reasons for me to start all over.It is filled with ideas and rarely does one sequence outstay its welcome. Maybe a couple too many boss fights for my liking, but they are mostly well executed. Despite lower production values due to the nature of the size of the production, there are some very awe inspiring scenes in the game that use VR's sense of scale incredibly well.If one man can do all of this, then I can scarcely imagine what he could accomplish with a whole team behind him. I'd say Valve should hire him, but we are all probably better off where he is right now, making these kinds of VR games.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the best VR game of our time. The gameplay is simply phenomenal, the enemies don't stand around waiting to be killed. And there are several strategies for taking out each enemy, some I have yet to even discover. And each weapon actually has strengths and weaknesses, instead of just real life weapons ported into vr. What i'm trying to say is, the combat in this game is the most realized of any vr game I have played so far, there are consequences for not thinking, you need to dodge and position yourself properly otherwise you will die. My only gripe is that the AK47 is a little overpowered for dealing with robots, the trident actually has travel time and recoil you have to account for and the ak has basically none... That said it did carry me through the really difficult sections. And i also didn't get the recoil or sight mods for the trident because i thought it would be too easy. I was wrong, this game is HARD.Oh yeah and the story is bonkers crazy, it feels like anything could happen at any moment and its so awesome that I'm not going to even hint at it for risk of spoiling it for you. This is a MUST HAVE vr game. Don't think, just buy it now.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wanted to like this game. All the trappings are there - solid graphics, phenomenal optimization (runs great!) and art design that I can get behind. There's some tiny rough edges that aren't really worth discussing. Overall the presentation is great!But the guns... the guns :(First hour was fun, but something seemed a little *off*. I figured I'd get over it, but rounding the corner on hour two, I had to face it -  the guns in this game just don't feel good to me. The designs and everything are really imaginative. I'm not about to say the game should have mil-sim guns or anything like that. I don't mind that they aren't hitscan (I *love* Compound's guns).But they deal so little damage that combat - y'know, the main part of the game - starts to feel like a slog.Sidenote: The exception here is the revolver, that gun feels great. Unfortunately the ammo system doesn't really allow you to use a single gun for too long.Since the player has such little damage output, gunfight encounters all play out the same: Hide around a corner while robots walk towards you in a straight line and take them out 1-by-1 with revolver headshots. Its a shame, because the areas that you're clearly meant to fight in are, again, imaginative and well-crafted.Encounters with other creatures are at least interesting, but again marred by all the enemies feeling like damage sponges.Final straw for me was a sort of turret section - I'm riding on a platform moving along an orange lava river. Orange lava monsters that throw orange projectiles start spawning rapidly. They're too far away for the shotgun to be effective, and the revolver shoots too slowly to be viable here (you need to shoot down projectiles that are lobbed at you; the revolver has a very slow rate of fire) - and the weapon system is too slow for quick-swapping to be an option. But the pistol, the most best option here, takes about 1-1.5 mags to kill one enemy, and there's something like 8 on screen. Trying to aim at the tough-to-see damage sponges while dodging tough-to-see projectiles was just... boring. This section was then immediately followed up by another corner-camping gunfire battle. And that's where I quit out.I dunno, maybe the problem is me - it seems like other VR players are loving this game, and honestly that's a net positive for them *and* the dev. (Which, also, holy crap, this is a solo dev project, which is mind-blowing!) You love to see it! But its nuts to me that people are putting it in the same league as HL: Alyx, etc.That said, I won't refund it -- I feel like my core complaints are mostly addressable by tweaking weapons stats & damage values, maybe they'll do that. Or maybe they'll use the money to make the next game an absolute banger, which they're clearly capable of.PS - to all VR devs out there (I'm looking at you too, Boneworks/labs) - please hire voice actors if you're going to have extensive dialogue in your game, OR just don't write you game to have 2+ minute sections that's just being talked at by someone.
