_childDocuments_.review: Its not very often that you come across a game that uses every single part of its medium to give you a great experience, especially nowadays. Vertigo 2 is so far above its peers that it actually assimilates them into its design. I counted no less than five games I had played before in VR that Vertigo had simply used as set pieces. Riding boats, shooting aliens and robots, taking a turret to enemy helicopters, what other games call their whole experience, Vertigo 2 calls a twenty minute stretch. And it goes on for over ten hours. The writing is hilarious. Every character is likable and I felt very sad when some of then were gone. The music was also fantastic. The wow moments keep coming one after the other like a machine gun and I promise it's like nothing you ever experienced in VR before. You'll be eaten by a fish, and then rocketed through its bloodstreams. You'll be hopping over lava waves while plugging a giant worm in the face with your shotgun. I don't want to ruin the best moments, but those were some of my favorites. Every single time I tried to guess what this game would do next, I was proven wrong with the biggest smile on my face. This is an extremely special experience that I am really thankful I was able to have and I can't wait to keep playing it over and over, though nothing will be as magical as the first. Now for what's not so great: The bosses are extremely tough. This is fun of course but one in particular, the church leader with the turban, is just too stressful for what you've got going on there. Even the brain boss, with a room you could barely stretch your arms in, was more manageable. They just stuffed too many enemies into the room at once, which all disappear when you defeat the boss anyway, so it was pretty unnecessary. Also I will echo other peoples sentiments that the SMG is a waste of a slot. It does hardly any damage and is the biggest and clunkiest gun, the worst part is that the spot to rip out your mag and the spot to lay your hand for stability are right next to each other and I don't need to tell you why that was problematic. I also wish the secret bow and arrow had better tracking with the pulling hand, so I felt better using it in more stressful and up close situations.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet because my controllers are dead and its late but like... THIS GAME IS SO GOOD. It is a linear story game which is heavily inspired by Half-Life 1, Alyx, and BONEWORKS (maybe a little bit of DOOM too). THIS IS A VR GAME DONE RIGHT.Although I haven't really been following the story, I feel like the storytelling is very much reminiscent of Half-Life storytelling as characters interact and talk to you and seamlessly flow from talking to gameplay. The story doesn't drag down this game at all, it clearly isn't taking itself too seriously and the humor has made me snicker a couple times.I absolutely love the gameplay, it doesn't feel like its in VR just to be in VR; that is an issue I have with a lot of other VR titles. If you have played Alyx before, the gunplay, healing system, and weapon upgrading system are all very very familiar. The enemies do offer a challenge and require you to be precise and take cover. There are a lot of really engaging boss fights in this game which all vary from each other in unique ways.Also just like, wow, its clear a lot of effort was poured into making the assets in this game. Every single model appears to be made for this game, not store bought (although there isn't anything wrong with store bought assets). It brings a lot of life to the environment when the assets look purpose built and made with lots of care and passion.There are plenty of other things which I can praise about this game too. There are so many moments which are nowhere short of the word EPIC. I am also surprised at how well vehicles are done in this game, they don't feel clunky and make for really intense moments. I wont spoil what you will be doing with vehicles but just know, its much better than BONELAB's vehicles.PLEASE PLEASE buy this game. Give the people who made this game money, this is clearly a labor of love for VR and gaming which deserves endless praise. I am probably over-hyping this, but if you are someone like me who has been a PCVR enthusiast for nearly a decade now, this is one of those games which scratches the right itches in all the right places.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice environments and atmosphere, some of them reminded me of parts of WoW.   Ive struggled with a few of the boss fights and decided just knock down the difficulty when it starts getting too frustrating (but giving it a decent go first). _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible world, designs, story, humor. Feels good to play. Also the most challenging VR game I've ever played for sure. Absolutely AAA feeling work for a single dev. Worth the price I promise. One of the best VR campaigns out there. ...but I am not short on complaints.The controls are just really very bad, but I really feel like this is all very easily fixable. I'm curious why the guns/hands feel super floaty in comparison to any other VR games. It's not a dealbreaker, but if it's a stylistic thing... it doesn't feel good. I would like to be able to dual wield and that would make a lot of sequences feel better, even if I had to put something away to reload. The game could just be ambidextrous rather than having to set handedness in the menu. It also sucks that my storage has to be on the opposite arm from my shooting hand. It feels very old school in a very bad way that I have to put my gun away to use a grenade or heal. Seeing as I'm left handed, the mirror'd controls are a pain. I want to be able to shoot with my left hand, and still control all motion with that hand too because that's how every game works with a regular controller where my left thumb controls motion. The mirroring sort of works but I mostly prefer teleportation which is stuck on the right. Also if I do try to throw a grenade with my right hand, I hit B (Quest 2 controller) to pop the pin... and it pauses the game. Also, in left handed mode every weapon in the game is held by my left hand while auxiliary actions (mainly reloading) is done by my right hand... until you pick up the aether bow. Then it switches for some reason. I just cannot imagine why this behaves this way. Maybe it's only programmed for right-handed mode or something, I didn't actually try switching the commands because...I didn't get the chance to use the aether bow. After I finished the challenge (which was frustrating for the controls and other reason that I'll get to), nothing happened. I lost access to the bow. It was no longer in the chest but it also wasn't in my inventory. Based on the backward feeling controls, I wonder if this is a bug with the handedness.I also feel like the game wasn't really tested for users who would prefer to teleport most of the time. Smooth motion makes me a little sick after not too long so I was really happy to see that the game supports dash teleportation which is my favorite alternative! Buuuuuuut, any range enemy seems to pin on you perfectly when you are only teleporting. This was really frustrating to figure out for how to fight the aetherbacks. It took me way too long to realize that they only really miss if you're strafing when they fire. With teleportation you would have to perfectly let go of the button after their arrow is in the air. This really sucks because it makes it so that not only am I forced to use smooth motion but I'm also wobbling back and forth the whole time which makes me extra ill./rAgain, I want to be clear that this game is not just great for something built by one person, but it just is a great game that's worth your time and money. But there are a handful of times where where the fact that it really was built by one person starts to show, especially in lack of testing. I really think making the game truly ambidextrous by attaching guns to the player body would be the way to go. I realize that this is an "arsenal shooter" (e.g. like Doom or Metal Gear Solid) and that may be tough so I'd say do something like what Resident Evil 4 VR does and just allow the player to assign weapons to body locations in a menu (live action menu or not). This allows the VR experience to flourish, feel less limiting, and keep the action moving. I realize my smooth motion complains are far more fundamental in the gameplay and tougher to make an easy for.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Vertigo 1. loving Vertigo 2 more.Pros:Lovely visual style. (stylized, cartoony etc etc but lovely)Good performanceEngaging and satisfying mechanics. Weapons are fun to shoot and reload. Teleporting, climbing, moving around feels good. Inventory is good.Environments, levels and puzzles are interesting and fun. Entering a new area and just taking in the strangeness is super enjoyable.Progression feels natural and engaging.Music is greatTremor-mitigation (weight/physics/friction to weapon movement) I have a tremor and this game makes it easier for me to aim well. Even "AAA" games like the tedious half life alyx don't have anything of the sort.Cons:Voice acting is serviceable. Not bad, not great. Mostly serviceable. Sometimes not so good. It's fine, but clearly not very professional. Lip smacking sounds in dialogue, attempts at characterized voices (which don't quite pan out) etcSound mixing is a bit sloppy at times. Sort of entwined with the voice acting quibbleBoss fights can be tedious and not quite clear in terms of player impact.No control configuration (I'd like to be able to change jump to forward on the right trackpad. Since clicking the right trackpad usually causes a snap turn as well)Game is a bit too hard - even on easy. Boss fights can be frustrating due to this. On easy (in my option) a good player shouldn't die several times before managing to defeat the boss. Just a feeling of wasted time. Easy mode (in my opinion) should be about moving through the game and enjoying it. Not "having a challenge" before needing to go to work. I have limited time. I just want to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game through on hard mode only dropping to normal for the last boss. It was a good game, but because of the cons mentioned above I would give it a C+. Many levels had poor balance. There were way too many wave shooter levels. Some guns were completely useless. Some bosses got way more attention than others. Some bosses were just repeated from previous sections of the game. Difficulty scaling simply impacted damage and didn't change enemy types, wave numbers, or enemy quantity. While some of these issues were nit-picks many should have been caught in play testing. Very impressive this was essentially made by one person. Imagine what he could do with a team and more quality control.

_childDocuments_.review: I put off playing this for a long time because I honestly didn't expect much from the cartoony graphics and somewhat amateurish sounding voice acting, but WOW this is a fantastic game and perfect for anyone who is a fan of classic level-based first person shooters. First off, this game builds on everything the first game did well. It has a great arsenal of weapons, there is a wide variety of interesting enemies and areas to explore. I never got bored and the game moves along at a great pace, introducing new mechanics and scenarios. I also want to give a special call out to the bosses in this game as they are all really well done and creative. They also can put up quite a fight and some of them are HARD, but they keep you on your toes and aren't just artificially hard due to massive health pools like some of the bosses in the first game.Now, with all the praise, I do have some complaints. There are quite a few bugs and some of them are potentially progress halting such as your hands wigging out in the 2 flying sections of the game, making it near impossible to grab/aim the gatling gun. The story and writing/voice acting is also eh and didn't make a whole lot of sense to me, but there's enough charm there that I didn't care.Overall though, definitely worth a buy!

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is a must buy for VR. If you loved Vertigo Remastered, then I'm sure you'll love this game as well. Fair warning though: this game is a lot more challenging than Vertigo Remastered with tough boss fights. However, you can turn down the difficulty as well as enable cheats from the console commands. So this game is accessible for all.I beat the game in about 14 hours on normal difficulty. I had a lot of fun along the way. However, the game is not perfect and with only one developer, I don't think you can expect perfection. However, it's simply boggles the mind that one developer can make one of the best games in VR and a game that should be a strong contender for VR GOTY 2023. Zach Tsiakalis-Brown deserves all the kudos, not just for bringing this great game for PCVR, but also for the more than reasonable price tag (if anything, it is on the low side).Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 fps for the most part. I did experience some bugs, but the biggest one (Steam VR crashing) is one that I can't exactly say for sure is the game's fault so I'll just mention it, but without assigning blame. I do think the gun angle was too high by default for the Meta Quest 2 touch controllers. Lastly, there is some jank overall to some of the VR interactions. All the graphical, sound, & gameplay settings that you would expect are here. You can play comfortably seated.However, I will add that teleport is a necessary gameplay element in some of the boss fights. So if you don't like teleport, unfortunately, unless you cheat & use console commands, it is something you will have to do. I would have preferred a sprinting option. The gameplay, story, graphics, sounds, all come together to make for a great VR adventure. It's a can't miss VR experience. Honestly, you should stop reading this review and just buy the game. It's not perfect, but it's a great game that deserves a VR nomination for GOTY 2023 at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo Set the bar to beat for early VR single player games.Vertigo Remastered Brought out the absolute best and showed what Zach could do.Vertigo 2 builds on what has come before.  It's bigger, better, and packed with lots more content and variety than the first game/s. From environments, story-telling, enemies, weapons and some fantastic boss fights.Vertigo 2 really shows off what can be done by a solo independent dev, providing a better experience than many games with a large studio behind them.It's one of those games that everyone who plays PCVR should own.Disclaimer - I have been a beta tester for this game, and received it for free.           - Blame me if you find any game breaking bugs I missed, I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game I have ever played. I like it even more than Half-Life: Alyx, which is also incredible (obviously). The writing is entertaining and doesn't take itself seriously, and the gameplay is very tight with the need to swap weapons often on the hard difficulty very engaging. The guy who made this is seriously a savant, doing most of the work on his own. I've only completed the game once, but I'm excited to go back in and find the rest of the secret weapons and try out the other characters. 10/10 issa masterpiece.Edit: This game does to Half-Life: Alyx, what High On Life did to Doom Eternal
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy game, with dated graphics, cringe voice acting, bad jokes and cliche mechanics. Gameplay is frustrating and boring, with multiple glitches preventing progress. Gun handling is even worse. The fact that this game is getting positive reviews despite being so mediocre and poorly executed truly makes me concerned for the future of VR gaming.Comparing this game to Half-Life: Alyx is like adding a spoiler to a Prius and calling it a Formula 1 car. Sure it has a motor and four wheels, but it's definitely not anywhere close to being a race car.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This experience was amazing. A wacky, fun, and stunning game. The weapons feel amazing and are a massive step up from vertigo 1. The story is easier to understand than vertigo 1 and its a step up from vertigo 1. I was amazed on how good vertigo 1 was for a single guy but this game makes it feel like a AAA studio made it. Every chapter has a new game play element just for it. He made 14 weapons all of them made from scratch. The endings feel perfect. Everything about this game is perfect. Its as good or better than bonelab and boneworks. I am praying we get some sort of story continuation even though this game wrapped it up perfect. I highly recommend this amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: It was short. Memorable. And worth keeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeepiiiiiinnnnnnnn.......That was me falling through the world. Three times. Only going a little off the beaten track.The game was not without its bugs when I played through. Some save points were deadly. Grenades felt like they were coated in grease. _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put into words how much I enjoy this game. I mean, I figured it would be fun, but I didn't think it would become one of my favorites. The best way I can describe this work of art is: the Half Life and Rick and Morty universes had an illegitimate child, but that child went on to be a beacon of hope for VR indie devs.The gun-play is fantastic. Weapons feel weighty when they need to, but not overly cumbersome. The story is actually quite entertaining and original, and the soundtrack bops between a Sci-Fi/Space opera and whimsical storybook adventure.While it is a bit more challenging than expected, it is still one of the most well-made, and enjoyable experiences on the VR market today.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the one, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.Oh my god IDK where to begin.I'll list the stuff that impressed me and the stuff that didn'tpros:Music is a vibeThere are many different locations and a lot a very uniqueThere is swimming and it feels really goodThere are vehicle rides and you can even use mounted weapons, oooOOoH mah gawdNPC's that are both friendly, provide lore, speak to you and follow you through locations sort of like Cpt. Price :D and ohh I wanted that so bad, companions in VR are really coolEnemy variety: Forget about soldiers and zombies, we've god DINOSAURS, big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robots, crabs, lil goblins, fire golems, cubes from minecraft, cacodemons and I'm sure a bunch more, haven't gotten there yet.Secret weapons♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GORGEOUS CUTSCENES, not only did the devs figure out to make cutscenes work in VR, but they also look so good, with beautiful "camera" angles and establishing shots. Shots of the Earth in space literally made my jaw drop.Splash texts are full of ROFLSIf I find more cool stuff as I play further, I'll list them aboveNow for the meh parts.cons:The weapons are really floaty, the reloading feels solid and good, but in order to simulate weight, they used a similar mechanic to Saints and Sinners, where the gun just kinda wobbles around when it really shouldn't. Makes it a bit hard to perform skillshots fast.Boss fights aren't always clear on what to do and lack health indication for the boss itself, which is a bit of an issue (1 boss at least, again, I'm pretty early on)There are a couple of soft locking bugs, the ones I experience were the black robot soldier guy can ram into you and send you flyin out of bounds if IT is behind the door and YOU are on the other side of it. And at Chapter 5 there's an "elevator" with a valve in a magma filled room that on my playthrough looses collision towards the end of the ride and sends me flying into death, thankfully you can use nearby pipes to teleport to the nexr location.Other than that, Holy ♥♥♥♥. Best game, at least for me personally. Step aside, Boneworks and Alyx.Finally, a game purchased in 2023 that doesn't leave me disappointed.Also sorry if my spelling sucks, English isn't my mothertongue.

_childDocuments_.review: When the first game came out, I enjoyed it immensely. Naturally as soon as the second game came out I bought it immediately. I was expecting it to just wrap up the first game in about 4-5 hours. Boy was I wrong, not only is it 3 to 4 times longer than the first game, it adds more of what made the first game great. I'm talking sci-fi weapons, freaky looking alien creatures, in depth lore, large areas each with different themes and areas to explore, many boss fights, puzzles, fun characters, and so, so much more. This game is what Boneworks wishes it could be. What really impressed me though, was finding out that most of this game was made by one developer. It runs like it was made by a team. This game is worth your time and money, so if you have $30 to spare check it out, you will not be disappointed.Keep up the incredible work Zach! 10/10  Would buy one of Nani's boats again

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game ive ever played, ♥♥♥♥ it, this is the best game i've ever played. Every VR game i've played feels like a tech demo compared to this. The worldbuilding just makes it feel real, ever corner of every beautiful environment feels lived in, from the NPC's to the intricate layouts of every map, to the diverse and original enemies and bosses.The only thing i can compare this game to is when I first played Mario galaxy 2 as a kid. Every 30 minutes it feels like i’m a completely new world just as beautiful as the last and yet it all transitions together smoothly. _childDocuments_.review: So - just finished the game.  I am leaving my original review below to show my state of mind after one of the bosses.This game is hard to describe.  I both loved and hated the game.  If I could go back in time I would show myself this review.  You will see amazing things that will leave you in awe.  You will laugh in delight and humour.  You will get this quirky little organic gun that is insanely fun to use.  So why did I also hate it?Imagine you are watching "The Godfather" for the first time.  Marvel at the loving detail the creator invested in this art.  You are captivated by the story, and immensely enjoying yourself.  Suddenly - for some reason, the creator splices in a sequence of someone running their nails down a chalkboard.  How long is this going to go on?  You don't know.  Eventually you suffer through it, and get back to loving the movie when suddenly it happens again ... and later again ... and again.These are the boss fights, and the combats with ridiculous difficulty spikes.  The bosses are all interesting and quite lethal.  They also frequently take place in a very small room with little to no cover.  I guess you are just supposed ... to be perfect?  I am playing a game, not training for the olympics!  One of the boss fights was literally "Oh, you know that boss that was giving you trouble before?  Well, here are two and now do it in a room with hardly any cover.  Have Fun!".  The game of course has a checkpoint system, and for the most part it is pretty good.  It was only one mega fight near the end where you would die, and you would restart right in the middle of your foes and die again in 4 seconds.  Wheeeeee!  It is absolutely INFURIATING because the rest of the game is SO GOOD!  WHY ARE YOU SABOTAGING THIS MASTERPIECE?Mercifully the game has difficulty levels that you can change on the fly (otherwise I wouldn't have progressed past 20% of the game).  Once it became clear that some of the difficulty cliffs were just stupidly difficult and unfair, I would just sigh, roll my eyes and lower the difficulty down to story to get past this chore.  I mean ... you will still die, just not as often.  Once the boss or insane combat was over and I was having fun again - I would put it back to normal, and I had to do this over and over again because the game was so wildly uneven.The weapons.  The weapons are various and you can get upgrades for them.  Many of them are so inaccurate that you couldn't hit a lake if you were standing at the bottom.  Once they are partially upgraded, you might be able to hit the broadside of a barn.  Seriously, the weapons seem to prefer to shoot around an enemy rather than at it.  None of this applies to the organic gun which is just pure fun.Now you know what is super not fun?  Being trapped in a small room with a lethal boss, fumbling with your weapons to reload.  Reloading of course takes two hands, which is kind of hard to do when you are running/teleporting constantly to avoid the bosses attacks.  However the game offers some advice.  It is easier to switch to another weapon which will be loaded, so do this a few times and then go back to your favourite weapon - and this works ... sometimes.  See - for some reason - even though you can see on the selection dial that there are mags available for that weapon - when you switch back to it - it remains empty.  I don't know why - but there you are - pointing an empty gun at a pissed off boss.  It is wall punchingly frustrating.So - yeah - you can get past the drudgery by changing the difficulty level.  However, there is one section that this WON'T help with.  It is in this lab with a bunch of puzzles (ugh) - one of which is a non-sequitur.  You can just look up the solution, right?  Yeah ... but not with one of them because everyone loves a JUMPING puzzle with clunky physics right?  Especially if there are a chained sequence of tasks and if you fail you get to do it all over again.  But wait ... there is more ... how about a really unforgiving TIME LIMIT, and if time runs out ... well, do it over again, and again, and again.  WHY?  WHY ARE YOU MAKING ME DO THIS?????????????So ... overall I am going to change my original review and give this a thumbs up ... but just BARELY.  I figure the good parts will linger in my memory more than the terrible boss design and clunky weapon loading.  Oh ... did I mention that there were like 11 or so bosses?  Yeah ... this is not a case of just suffering through one or two.  Anyway - if you don't mind difficulty cliffs and doing the same fight over and over and over again - then yeah, this game is great.  Except for that timed puzzle - that is just game cancer.------------------  Original Review ------------------------------------------------------I know it says I only played for 5 minutes.  Its because when I play PCVR I need to play disconnected from the internet.  I actually have about 3 hours in it and haven't finished the game yet.I was a huge fan of Vertio - but I am actually pretty disappointed with this.  Why?  Its the bloody bosses.  I thought the bosses in Vertigo were interesting and fun.  Someone somewhere must have complained because the bosses (while still interesting ) are wall punchingly frustrating.  Even on Story mode you will die again, and again and again *SapLord* - with no way to get past them.  And let me say - fighting a boss in a tiny arena in VR while fumbling with weapons and teleports is NOT fun. _childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an amazing VR experience. The fact that it was created by one individual makes it even more remarkable. However, there is one fatal flaw. More on that in a minute.I'm not sure what the average time is for a complete play-through. It took me 73 hours to complete the game. A lot of that time was spent in frustration because I could not progress through the game, thanks to several overly difficult boss battles.While some creatures you have to battle with seem overly simplistic in their design, you quickly get over that feeling when they start hurling objects at you. There are very few sequences where you get to explore an environment without first dispatching a number of attackers. While the game is heavily focused on gunplay and less on puzzle-solving, I did enjoy the times when I had to solve a puzzle to progress through the game.One feature that impressed me was the number of different environments. When I wasn't looking over my shoulder to see who was shooting at me, I enjoyed walking around in immersive worlds, most of which involved a perspective of height, thus the name Vertigo.Another impressive feature is the sound. It was never intrusive and almost always clued you into something that was or was not about to happen. This game also has a well-defined goal: to reach the core.This is not a game you can play without the assistance of a guide, or watching a walkthrough. In my case, I could not have made it through most of the boss battles without resorting to outside help. The whole idea of the boss battle was new to me. Apparently, it's a feature in a lot of 2D graphic games. My problem is that each time I had to confront a boss in an arena, gameplay came to a screeching halt. Even though I had the game set on easy, I found several of the boss battles to be nearly impossible. Some would argue that my problems with boss battles only point to my weakness as a player. I would argue that I am not alone in my complaint of overly difficult battles. This is born out by the fact that only a quarter of players who start the game actually finish it.Rather than appeal to the small number of players who appreciate a difficult challenge, the game would have been so much better had the boss battles been a little easier. Despite this one complaint, this is a game that should be on your list. Congratulations to the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:-It'll take you about 10 hours to get through the story. -There are 6 secret weapons and lots of lore to collect, encouraging exploration.-Bosses are some of the best I've seen in a VR game.-I think there's multiple endings? I haven't replayed the final levels so I'm not 100% sure yet.-After you beat it, you unlock New Game Plus, allowing you to replay levels and upgrade your guns again (since upgrade stations can only be used once).Here's my review video if you'd prefer REVIEW:Changing my review. Originally it was a thumbs down for me due to poor balancing, and while I still think some areas need a nerf, the worst offender was the boat level, which the developer did nerf.. wish I knew a nerf was coming before I suffered through that level, but either way it shows the dev is listening, so let's talk about what this game does right.THE GOOD:Let me start by saying that the fact this game is made by a single developer is actually insane. There's just so much content, so many unique ideas all crammed into this game, it's truly a treat to play. Even the more annoying parts make up for it with every level delivering a unique experience.The best example I could give is that Vertigo 2 feels like the original Half-Life, but in VR. Not a VR port, but it's own game with idea after idea thrown at the player, with each area being something fresh just as you start getting bored of the last.The final levels in the game are really evocative of the original Half-Life, with you traveling through different dimensions at a breakneck speed, flying across jump pads while sniping enemies and being bombarded with all sorts of enemies.The highlight for me is the boss fights. These manage to actually be intense and difficult, which is something you don't see in VR. They've all got their own mechanics, their own special one-shot-kill move you need to dodge, and the last few fights end up being a true endurance test with you juggling all your weapons, desperately trying to reload them all while avoiding attacks. They're difficult, but very rarely did I feel cheated when I died, only frustrated.Guns feel intentionally sloppy. A few hours into the game and I was starting to get annoyed at how much the guns flop about, but I got used to it, and this is a good time to mention that you can upgrade all your weapons at weapon stations hidden throughout the game.The moment it all clicked for me was when I purchased stability, which is usually a useless upgrade on weapons, right? Not in Vertigo 2! Stability made the guns actually have a lot more control, so I think it was all intentionally annoying so the upgrades would feel meaningful.Another thing about the guns is there's unlimited ammo that's on a cooldown for each weapon, which is fine. I never felt like I had too much ammo to feel overpowered, but there are definitely some guns that shine more than others.THE BAD:There's not many things this game does wrong, but what it does do wrong almost made me quit playing.Around the middle of the game, you're thrown into a massive warzone map. The concept of it is great, but the execution is a bit frustrating. You have allies, but they're stupid and just get in the way, and enemies seem to always target me. Fighting your way through the streets is all well and good, but eventually you get to the enemy stronghold and are just barraged with wave after wave of enemies.. seriously, the fight takes like 10 minutes and if you die, you have to start again.I'm all for an epic battle, but it was more of a battle on my patience than difficult.One main complaint with this game is there's a couple areas like this that just have wayyy too many enemies, and it trivializes fights, forcing you to take cover, peak your head out to shoot, then hide until your ammo recharges.Worst of all, a handful of these battles barely have any cover at all, so if you have 1 hit when you get to these spots, good luck.Another issue I had was enemy variety.. okay let me start by saying there's a good amount of enemy types in this game ranging from all sorts of weirdo aliens, but overall there's a bit too many of the same copy-pasted robot enemies.There's even this one big robot that acts as a sort of mini boss. He's pretty difficult to beat, but near the end of the game he's a normal enemy.Personally I'd like to see some of these areas tweaked. I know Vertigo 2 is trying to be a difficult game, but less is more in this case. I'm pretty good at VR games, and even I was struggling with some areas.. mostly the boat area I mentioned above, which was thankfully nerfed.CONCLUSION:Vertigo 2 is one of those rare games that would be great even without being in VR. A lot of VR games are pretty mediocre if you take away the VR gimmick (like Saints and Sinners and even Boneworks). They're great games in VR, but without? Ehhh.I know this isn't a very good argument, but I'm just trying to say that even if Vertigo 2 wasn't in VR, it would still be a great game, but being in VR brings it to a whole other level that I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a run and gun shooter with a few pretty good jokes thrown in here and there. When you finally overcome one obstacle, you're greeted with a harder one immediately after. There is no getting stronger. There is no exploration. There is no such thing as outsmarting the enemy. The only way to progress is by trying over and over again. You might blame it on the clunky UI or the snails pace locomotion, but it's how the game is made and it's how it was meant to be.The only praise I can say is that it's incredible satisfying when you do finally progress, and if that's your thing then by all means get the game. _childDocuments_.review: I have to be completely honest, I mainly selected no just so this wouldn't get buried under all the other positive reviews that praise this game as the new leading standard for VR games and, keyword, experiences. For what it's worth, I think Vertigo 2 was a pretty fun VR game that, if you're a consistent VR user looking for something new or completely new to the genre itself than it'll likely scratch the itch, but I think there's a massive push to really herald this game as something it isn't; revolutionary.I'll start with what Vertigo 2 does right; being a game. I think it does a much better job out the gate actually interesting the player than Vertigo 1/Remastered did. I played and ultimately refunded Remastered because I felt it was far too arcade-y, sluggish, and failed to captivate me within the two hour refund window, which was disappointing after so many reviews for that game put it on par with Alyx, Boneworks, and TWD. Vertigo 2, as evidenced by my play hours, does a much better job out the gate getting the player involved. The weapons all, for the most part, feel unique to use and reload, but you'll find yourself really just quick cycling through your weapon wheel in the later stages of the game to maximize time shooting over time reloading, which I felt really trivialized the combat in the end game. I wouldn't even consider myself getting better or more in-tune with the game, I just found my entire arsenal of weaponry to literally overpower the waves of mobs you shoot. Whether or not you think that's a negative is up to you, I'm not entirely sure if this was conscious decision on the devs part to emulate DOOM or Half-Life, but it doesn't feel like the enemy design held up to the weapon power creep.On that note, the enemies are visually varied and visually unique, unfortunately the AI is on par with that of Bethesda enemies and, apart from a few exceptions, all just have some form of range attack to throw or shoot at you. I think the enemies work great as they're introduced throughout the story, as each time you find yourself fighting a new one you have to learn what's unique about it, but that starts to get predictable once you figure out their entire behavior model boils down to; Do they run at you or stand still, do they use cover or ignore it, and are their ranged attacks instant or projectiles? And even then, when there's just a massive group of them on screen, you just find yourself prioritizing which ones are closest since they don't meaningfully interact with each other apart from whether or not they hold position or charge at you.The environments are definitely varied and some setpieces are downright gorgeous, but I found exploring some areas to be confusing since it wasn't always clear which path was the way forward and which path was optional. I wouldn't say it really hampered my experience since I found all the secret weapons and most of the weapon upgrades and codex entries, but I did find it a little tedious to have to scour wide open areas on the off chance there was something hidden. On that note, I'm not sure if this was just an issue on my end or if it is intentional, but for some reason using smooth locomotion to go forward is slower than going sideways or backwards. Yes, you can teleport, but it bothered me that through my entire play through that my character moved slowest in the direction that you'd be able to move the quickest.The music is great, the voice acting is pretty good, and the animations are a little hit or miss. I think that about covers the game aspect, now for (in my opinion the most important part) the VR experience part of it.I do not know what identity Vertigo 2 has.I had a feeling once it was described by the creator as "Half-Like" that it would be overly influenced by Valve, and it definitely is, so much to the point that I think it was so focused on trying to be some Valve-esque game that it neither hits that mark or creates a unique VR experience. The most involved parts of the game are a helicopter turret section, which I found myself fighting the turret as much as I was fighting enemies with it, a boat section that all you really need to do is go full throttle and then turn every once in a while, and the reloading, which you do a lot. Apart from that, you don't interact with the environment like you can in Alyx, you don't have a reason to interact with it like you would Into the Radius or TWD, and it doesn't let you find creative ways to traverse it like you would in Boneworks. It's first and foremost a VR Shooter, which is fine, but apart from light exploration and upgrading that's all it really is. Despite how big the stages are you don't feel immersed in them apart from purely visuals, and that's if you don't mind some of the strange enemy designs.I don't understand what it does as a VR experience to earn some of the recognition that it's superior to Alyx; it has more guns and enemies and biomes but, at the end of the day, thats just more things to shoot at, with more things to shoot with, in more areas to shoot in.TWD has crafting progression and exploration. Into the Radius has exploration and gear progression. Boneworks has it's entire physics-focused playstyle and playgrounds. The one thing Vertigo 2 offers over those is boss fights, and those are so hit or miss that I honestly couldn't remember half of them off the top of my head.Look, I'm being overly critical because as much as I enjoyed it as a VR shooter, I didn't walk away from it thinking it brought something new to the VR table to advance it. If you want to make the argument that it presents the idea that VR levels can be big, enemies can be varied, and bosses can be incorporated you can, but Alyx presented that 3 years ago. Vertigo 2 could've, theoretically, been that advancement, but it's an indie game with I think just 1 dev. To expect that would be just asinine.I applaud what was done as a solo passion project for years, I think what's presented is a fun VR shooter with enough variety for things to feel fresh as you play through it's 8-12 hour campaign. But unless it's your first VR game do not go into it expecting something groundbreaking or the "new bar" for VR to hit. It's a fun game, but it's not a new VR experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So, i had 4 major issues with the original (despite the original also being fantastic btw)1. length of the game2. replay value3. cliffhanger ending4. lack of boss fightsand i can say that all 4 were addressed here, the main story easily took me 11 hours to beat (hard difficulty, but still very long game regardless)the game has hidden encyclopedia entries, hidden weapon upgrade cases, 2 endings, and even a split path near the middle that decides what weapons you get throughout the rest of the run with their own unique story and boss fights, and even secret (missable) weapons you can findthe game has a proper, beginning, middle and end story, that doesnt just suddenly end.and there are SO many bosses here, i think there are like like 14 easily of the top of my headand you get a newgame+ mode when you beat it, in case you were concerned about missing things.overall, extremely happy about how the game ended up, a must have for any vr owners and a very easy recommendation from me, highy suggest you .also buy Vertigo Remastered along side it if you dont already have the first game.I did have some minor nitpicks, but they are just that, nitpicks:1.when in seated mode, you can use the [right stick] up+down to go between crouched and standing, but its not done gradually, its either full standing or fully crouched, i wish it was done like boneworks where you can adjust your height with the right stick instead of it being a binary choice, there are many occasions (mostly elevator buttons/switches) where i was either too tall, or too low to use them.2. you can only teleport with the left touchpad with no way to rebind it (i played in smooth locomotion mode, right handed, seated) this was an issue throughout the entire game because most other games put the teleport feature on your dominant hand for quicker access, this left me with very bad reaction times when trying to dodge boss attacks (you cannot dodge some attacks without it). Might be because of the lack of buttons available to put it on, but i do hope there is a way to put it on the dominant hand somehow. (perhaps clicking in the stick, as its unused in the game)And thats it really, i had no other issues in the gameI do hope we get post launch support with this product as i simply want to play it even more. The original got a dlc for custom levels, and i do hope it returns along side some sort of endless wave based mode (some levels in the game are just begging to be arenas)

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Vertigo 1, to the point of speedrunning it a few times. So when I heard that Vertigo 2 was coming out, I knew I would buy it, expecting it to be very similar, though perhaps a bit polished. Especially as it's made by a sole dev. And hoooooly balls was I wrong! Vertigo 2 makes Vertigo 1, a good enough game in its own right, feel like a mere tech demo. The animations, game play, story, setting, landscapes, soundtrack, weapon optimization and variety, enemies, and levels all scream "AAA game". I'm about 10 hours in, and every level introduces new, well-thought-out, and (most importantly) fun mechanics, enemies, weapons, and concepts. This is an absolute must-buy, though make sure you play Vertigo 1 first, as the story is a continuation of that.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a trend with VR games where they either don't take advantage of VR and feel like regular games that surround you, or they do take advantage of VR in some cool ways but don't full commit to certain aspects that would make them feel more complete. Half-Life Alyx is a bunch of pretty shooting galleries, Boneworks/Bonelab are cool physics sandboxes in simplistic environments, etc.Vertigo 2 is a whole video game.It fully uses VR in the way you would expect from an "experimental" game, but it also has all the staples of regular flat screen gaming that VR developers just haven't been able to get right yet. It doesn't feel like a tech demo, or a hardware showcase, or a port of a game you've already played. It feels like an actual, straight up, video game. And a pretty damn good one at that.The story lures you in with a joke-y tone that it never fully drops, but further inspection of the world around you and the encyclopedia reveals the rabbit hole goes a lot deeper than a Half-Life parody, with some well voice acted characters to boot. The environments are varied, from laboratory corridors to breathtakingly huge alien forests, and none of them bored me. The arsenal you amass is not only well balanced to utilize all the guns throughout the whole playthrough, but also contain some curve balls to make them more than just a regular game inventory (the long range "sniper" weapon is a revolver that only has iron sights until you pump multiple upgrades into it. It is rad). The music seriously goes hard, and much like all the other aspects of the game, only gets better as you go along. It's got some crazy secrets for immense replay value, along with a New Game + for the truly dedicated. And, to top it all off, you don't even have to play the (admittedly dated) Vertigo Remastered in order to understand this game thanks to a handy recap.A must have for any VR library.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 shows a better understanding of what a sequel should be than Bonelab. Compared to Vertigo, it has better guns, better environments, and bigger - much bigger - aliens and enemies, all of which I would say Bonelab failed to deliver from Boneworks. But this game deserves more than just a comparison to SLZ's games. Where Vertigo established the SCP-like nature of its world, this game drives home the concept with fully fleshed out lore for its denizens, including how each manage to survive and coexist in this facility. My only nitpick would be that there might be a bit too much information at first, and it can be hard to first get into the thick data entries, which you somewhat need to if you really want to learn about the world. But after the first chapter or so, you start to gather them at a much more reasonable pace, making it much easier to keep track. Overall, I came for the guns and stayed for the LORE.

_childDocuments_.review: I cry, knowing it will be years yet until I play a game of its caliber again. TLDR: buy, play, savor, regret you ran out, weep.I would advise you play the remaster of Vertigo 1 first, I played the first chapter and got annoyed at all the self referential humor going on, so I went back and played my copy of the first game. Correct decision. Several visual gags rely on the foreknowledge of the last game.Speaking of gags, the game has... a sense of humor? As the visual style and palette of voice actors may have clued you in, this game goes in for a cartoon-y art style (bright color, saturated, lots of good stuff like that) And honestly? It's feels good to look at. At times, especially in the wider open areas, the lack o small details are apparent, but fortunately in those areas you are usually distracted by the ass-wagon of enemies trying to murder youWhich brings me to combat. The combat is IMO the weakest part of this game. And that is not a criticism. I like the weapon designs they went with. They're wacky, variable, and give you capabilities you otherwise wouldn't have in the ways you least expected them. I love their enemy variety, it is wonderful and needs to be seen to be believed. Some of the weapons are pea-shooters, especially by endgame, but this is always compensated for by the ammo regen system. My railgun can 1 hit kill most enemies, but it has woeful regen times, so unless you hate that crab, you use the starter pistol. Certain enemies are also predisposed to weakness to certain weapon types, which rewards you for weapon switching. The combat style, with the teleporter bunnyhopping, is suited for fast pace combat with large groups of enemies in open areas with cover, slow methhodical corner hallway clearing ala Halflife, or big bosses with attack patterns. And the game has all three: well done. The shotgun is also OP as ♥♥♥♥ and I followed a friends advice to never upgrade to keep fair. Still used it time to time. It's a really nice shotgun tooMy only criticisms are thus 1. The cartoonishness of the of the weapons makes them feel mediocre (Looking at you Hammer and Sickle). 2. Not all weapons get the attention that they deserve because some of the situations they're good for are too... situational. You will be mainlining the one gun that is good versus android, because that's a majority of the enemies. 3. The difficulty scaling is brutal and somewhat random. Between group battles, hallway battles, and boss battles, the first is by far the most difficult, and turning a corner to be met by hells whole Xenos and robot buggery squadron is a bit jarring when 10 minutes ago I was doing healing drugs to RP being a heroine addict. The Bosses are at least always fair. As in slack off and die (they can and will 2-hit combo murder you), pay attention and use your brain and you can avoid most damage with easeYes this review was disproportionately about the combat, it's the central gameplay loop! GitsThe exploration parts are divine BTW. The open areas, vehicle sections (word to the wise, play this game AFTER acquiring VR legs) and scale they employ many, many times feels like I'm playing in a museum to other realities. It's great. The lore is great. The plot is great. If you are the kind of person who cares about science fiction and thematic elements, you're smart enough that I needn't opine about the quality: you will enjoy it. Off with you!In short: Weep. Because this game feels like what the world would be like if VR had AAA devs. I suppose they do. Good job Zach

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 10/10Vertigo 2 isn't just a game; it's an unparalleled virtual reality experience that sets an unprecedented standard for immersive gameplay. From the moment you step into its virtual world, you're transported to a realm where innovation and creativity collide, resulting in a gaming masterpiece that earns a perfect 10.One of the most striking aspects of Vertigo 2 is its breathtaking visuals. The graphics are nothing short of stunning, with an attention to detail that makes every environment feel alive and dynamic. From futuristic cityscapes to alien landscapes, the game's artistry is a testament to the developers' commitment to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in virtual reality.The gameplay mechanics are a revelation, seamlessly blending traditional first-person shooter elements with mind-bending puzzles and gravity-defying challenges. The level design is a triumph, offering a perfect balance of exploration and action. Each stage feels like a carefully crafted work of art, encouraging players to think critically and adapt to ever-changing circumstances.The narrative is equally compelling, weaving an intricate and engaging story that keeps you hooked from start to finish. The character development is top-notch, and the voice acting is impeccable, adding layers of emotion and depth to the overall experience. As you progress through the game, you'll find yourself invested in the fate of the characters and the unfolding mysteries of the plot.Vertigo 2 truly shines in the realm of virtual reality. The level of immersion it achieves is unparalleled, making you forget the real world as you navigate through its rich environments. The attention to detail in the VR interactions, from gripping weapons to solving puzzles, is a testament to the developers' commitment to delivering a true VR masterpiece.Moreover, the soundtrack deserves special mention. It has 17 long chapters and I really struggled on the big bosses where you die a lot. After dying a lot of the fire boss, I tried dropping back to easy difficulty and found that there is absolutely no difference. It was just as hard as normal with no noticeable reduction in difficulty at all. I hope this can be fixed, because the idea of an easy difficulty should not be a taxing, die a lot experience. _childDocuments_.review: ********* VOTE VERTIGO 2 FOR VR GAME OF THE YEAR!!! *********Don't pass this up!     Once again I'm blown away. Vertigo 2 is just as well designed and fun to play as the first but better in every way imaginable! Like the first game this one does an AMAZING job at being a VR shooter! Not just a shooter where you can move your hands around.  You can tell time was taken to really think about all the many ways you can interact with your hands and with the world around you.      Each weapon is unique to the others in terms of how and what it shoots (if it shoots) and how you operate it. So much more here than just reloading different magazines. In the game world(s) there are so many different mechanics and interactions. Levers, switches, knobs and dials, buttons, swipes, grabs, climbs and all sorts of things.     The levels and worlds are well designed and all different and interesting in their own ways just like the weapons. And the enemies are no different. Each enemy has its own strengths and weaknesses and the game does a great job of mixing things up. Just as you get used to an enemy type and its mechanics, BOOM, new enemies you've never seen before or even one of the many fun boss fights against all sorts of crazy bad guys!     But levels and enemies mean nothing without a good story, right? Well this game has it. I was always so excited to hop in and see how far i can get into it with each time i played. The whole story from the first is still going on. (don't worry though you don't NEED to play it before enjoying the second, however it will give you tons of insight into whats going on, who's who, and some of the references to the older game in this one) It picks up right were the first left off. however there's now a little twist in that some new factions are forming and [[[SPOILER ALERT]]] you may have to choose some sides.     I really could talk about these games and how much I like them and how well they are put together for hours, but to make a long review short I'll just say this:  If you've played the first Vertigo game you know everything I'm talking about. You can tell this game was made with love in every line of code. the characters, the story, the guns, its all so good! This is that x10! So many new locations and levels, way more weapons than the first, so many more new enemies (and friends), all the great mechanics and interactions, and tons of references to other great games (VR and not). Its hands down my FAVORITE VR game series and I can't wait to see what else this developer can cook up!

_childDocuments_.review: A truly expansive, native VR experience that took me over 12 hours to complete!  The environments were beautiful, the music and voice acting were excellent, and the story was humorous, nicely vague, and kept you guessing and engaged throughout.  The variety of weapons along with some of the missions to specifically use the secret weapons were fun, and I ultimately found that almost every weapon had a good use in the game.  In many cases, learning how to defeat certain classes of enemy by learning their timings and attacks was engaging and rewarding.  However, I do have quite a few strong criticisms for the game (EDIT:  many of these have been resolved but I'm leaving my original comments in followed by edits...this is definitely my second favorite VR game to date after HLA).  Taken as a whole, I'd have to say that I enjoyed the overall experience of Vertigo Remastered over this.  Although the minigun finale of that game was a bit lackluster, and it ended a bit too suddenly, I felt it was a tighter experience where you felt satisfied from beginning to end.  For Vertigo 2, the creator was far more ambitious but missed the mark in some areas.  I will list my criticisms in order of importance to me:1.  You cannot win the boss battles (at least on Hard difficulty) without using teleport and there is no sprint option - I have a rule in HLA and VR in general where I only use teleport to speed things along or do necessary platforming moves, but never during combat and as sparingly as possible to maintain immersion.  That's not possible in V2 where every boss battle require teleporting to survive, and this was a massive disappointment to me.  IMO, there should be a sprint option and you should be able to sprint/jump away from any dangers with the same results as teleporting.  EDIT:  I actually can beat a couple of the bosses without teleporting now that I understand their timings better, but I would still like to see a sprint option added to keep the tension high in boss battles and in general.  Not a fan of teleporting in general.2.  Several levels have significant stuttering, likely as a result of them being so huge - The lava and forest levels are where I noticed this the most, and lowering graphics settings didn't seem to help much at all.  In some areas, restarting the game seemed to clear it up but YMMV.  EDIT:  Recent updates seems to have fixed the forest level lag but I am still seeing it in the lava level to some extent.  Still, it seems much improved.3.  The combat can get tedious at times plus enemies respawn when loading an autosave - I especially noticed the tedious combat in the forest level, especially with so many saplings to kill who quickly become easy to figure out and dispatch.  In another forest section, I had killed all of the flies in a certain part, then died a bit later but when I loaded the autosave I was being swarmed by the flies who were already dead.  I don't think enemies should load back in after loading a save.4.  There was nothing overly creative or skilled as it pertains to how to defeat the bosses - In most cases, you just pummeled them with everything you had, evaded one of several of their scripted attacks, and then rinse and repeat until an obvious weakness would appear for you to exploit.  Some overt or environmental storytelling hinting to the player that certain areas might be the vulnerable ones to focus on would have made for more interesting combat moments.  EDIT:  Upon further review, the bosses do have some weak points to exploit, but in most cases the methods to defeat them don't require much creative thinking.I still enjoyed the game quite a bit, but the aforementioned criticisms will likely keep me from wanting to play it much in the future aside from my obligatory achievement grabbing that I'll be doing now.  However, if sprinting is added and some of the larger levels are better optimized, I would definitely give it another go after letting it breathe for a bit.  EDIT:  Well I ate my own words and have been playing the custom levels as well as replaying the game attempting to challenge myself in assorted ways, and with the new playable characters.  New content continues to fly in and this will be a heavily played game for me going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly the a next level paradigm shift for gaming. I've just come back to this game after playing Remnant 2 for a while. Within 10 minute of playing it all clicked again. The freedom of expression and of play style choice cannot be matched. Just Imagine for a second, replacing grindy repetitive task with genuinely challenging complex encounters with sly round about solutions. I haven't beat the game yet but coming back mid-game I cannot help but be floored by the ease of interaction and weapon swapping. I feel so "animation locked" in 2D games. A lot of games feel so formulaic and are overtly numbers, and RNG driven. This results in gaming most often feeling like a part time job. Vertigo 2 is just fun, visually stunning, poetic and an all around really good time. I cannot believe gaming has made it this far. I feel lucky to be able to experience this game, and am really excited to recommend it to anyone who may be interested in trying out VR gaming. I originally got into VR with the intentions of Sim Racing, but I'm glad I was able to take a nice detour into a more creative side.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is a very good and very polished VR game. The gameplay is smooth, and has numerous interesting mechanics. I really enjoyed using the weapons, the feel and mechanics of the different weapons all felt unique. The art style is also unique and enjoyable to admire. The story and voice acting are decent and help me really understand the world I'm in, and I really do enjoy the touch of humor that the game has. I will say tho that the game is fast paced, and will likely be difficult for people that are new to VR. But if you've developed your "VR legs" or are already acquainted with VR, then definitely give Vertigo 2 a shot. Vertigo 2 is up there as some of the best VR games of all time. It's just plain fun and worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Figured I should finally review this game since it's clear at this point that the game annoyed me enough that I'm never going to play it again.The 2 handed weapons are a cool idea, but they just don't work. It's almost impossible to aim with them since they seem to only work well and not glitch out if you keep your hands the same distance apart as the actual grips on the gun, but of course you can't actually see where your hands are from in VR. Occasionally the shotgun will just glitch out and move itself several feet away because it got confused about how to turn my hand positions into the gun pose. Very annoying when it would frequently happen during fights.The one-handed weapons aren't much better, the barrel angle doesn't match the controllers at all, it makes aiming very uncomfortable. There's a setting for adjusting this but there's no obvious way to tune it.The enemy and level design is a mess. Every enemy is a bullet sponge, which makes every encounter really grind-y and unfun, and the game has no issues throwing piles of enemies at you in poorly designed levels that make it very easy to just softlock yourself doing an impossible encounter over and over again until you get lucky. And it does this at the start of the game. I got stuck on one particular room early in the game for nearly an hour, which contained a lot of puzzle-esque things to interact with, all of which would immediately get you killed if you go near them. The level design is really strange.Eventually I gave up because the game devolved into sending rows of bullet sponges at me over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid Half-Like. You probably don't need to play the first game to fully appreciate this one, it improves on it in every way and there is a story recap cutscene.Creative and punchy weapons, upgraded shotgun especially, albeit with a lacklustre SMG. It bears mentioning how satisfying and tactile some of the reloads can be, once your ammo stocks have regenerated. Hunting down upgrade points and secret weapons provides some entertaining exploration, and you can toggle off any upgrades you want to disable.It has a very unique and stylised world and enemy design, with a mysterious story that shines in its exciting set-pieces, which can provide a decent challenge at times. An underrated element that serves to construct the universe-hopping setting is the colourful database that fills out with each creature, character and location you come across.It has its fair share of replay value too, given the number of ways to try another playthrough thanks to the update, plus some player-made levels to fiddle around in. I was compelled to go back through the game at least once more to find the stuff I missed.This sets the standard for single player action in VR. It's a rare case where it felt like playing a whole-ass game, rather than another experimental sandbox tech demo or the next 'Call of Duty but VR'.P.S. Completionists are going to want to keep that square key in their pocket for half the game. And

_childDocuments_.review: This game is FUN.It lives at a beautiful intersection between balls to the walls creativity and fast paced easy to learn fun to master gameplay.Its 10-14 hours full of many explosive set pieces, scary moments... and the pacing... *chefkiss*. It is only when you play a game with truly amazing level design that you realise how important level design is.I don't want my review to be too long and a lot of people have already talked about enemy variety, world building ecc.. but I want to speak briefly about the gameplay because it's not been talked enough IMO. The gunplay seems simple and I was slightly disappointed at first you could not dual wield like in Vertigo 1 however, when the difficulty started to ramp up, I realised how smart it was to introduce a manual recharge. Every gun has a different recharge mechanics and the more you use them the better you get with that particular gun.When you start to get the hang of it and understand that often the smart move is not to recharge but cycle to a different gun to create some space between you and the enemies... maybe teletransport behind cover, you take a breath, recharge a gun you were using before, you nail the recharge, shot in face the enemy that was almost getting to you ecc.. you start to feel like a real badass and the gameplay really clicks. Some of the encounters and bosses in which I had to cycle through almost all the guns and teletransport all around were true peak gaming moments for me. I already praised the pacing and level design in general terms but what really works about them, and for my money makes it a masterpiece, is that it strikes a very rare balance between making you feel scared and making feel a badass action hero. I would not characterize this as a horror game but there are plenty scary monsters, dark spaces, unknown dangers and thalassophobia inducing sections. What distinguishes it from a horror game in my opinion is that for every horror element there is an awe inducing one (sometimes at the same moment). This really an experience made for VR and VR elevates it to more of the sum of its parts and to the realm of Masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: How about that, a VR shooter with an engaging and lengthy story. Awesome and sprawling levels, high enemy variety, with great gameplay. Vertigo remastered was already one of the best VR games out there, and this just expands on it. Props to you zach, you made a better VR game than most studios could even dream of. And yes, a far better buy than bonelab.edit: Just finished the game, oh boi was it amazing. The sheer scope of it absolutely blew my mind. Just to list a few things, its got flipping incredible environments, insane enemy encounters, and handful of bosses. Yeah, bosses! We dont see nearly enough of them in VR games now days, and the ones in Vertigo 2 were all unique, and super fun to take on. I played through on hard, and it took me around 10 hours. Given the higher difficulty I actually struggled quite a bit on some enemy encounters and bosses, but I had fun trying to get past them (which I eventually did). Also, gosh damn, does it have plenty of incredible set pieces. I wont spoil any, but you never know what epic sequence is about to play out. I could really keep on rambling, it has tons of awesome NPCs to meet and interact with, lots of option content (I missed all of the 6 secret weapons which im gonna go back and collect), the narrative is suprisingly great, with lots of twists and stuff, and theres just so much moreAbsolutely blow away. My new favourite VR game, and I think im gonna jump back in for another playthrough hahaoooh also, one more thing if you missed it: you can play with a friend if you click the eye at the top right and select drone. They can only really move and shoot, but its a great feature if there anyone you want to go through the game with :D

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game, and I can't recommend it strongly enough!The art style is simple, but beautiful, and makes great use of scale.  There are some stunning sights in this game. The character models can be a bit clunky at times, and the animation is sometimes lacking, but the personality of each character comes through.  I appreciated that every level is populated with various creatures or robots, not all of which are hostile.  Some are just there, going about their day.The writing is very silly and doesn't take itself too seriously, but never in a lazy way.  The characters are interesting and varied, the world is well thought out, with a coherent lore and a deep backstory. Despite the general zaniness, the levels felt like places, not levels, which, to my mind, is the best thing you can say about a video game level.  I really enjoyed the in-game encyclopedia entries that unlocked during gameplay, and would always start each session by reading all the ones I had unlocked during the last one. There are are also some great Half-Life-style set pieces, which keep the narrative moving along, and are often quite funnyWhere the game really shines, though, is in the interactions.  The game has some physics, so your hands interact with the environment in a believable way, but doesn't go to extremes like Boneworks, where it feels like you're playing QWOP VR.  The haptic feedback for various interactions is really fine-tuned to perfection, and makes everything feel natural.  The guns (and there are a lot of guns) are varied, and all feel unique, each with it's own reloading method.  Speaking of reloading, the game's ammo system is a nice compromise between infinite ammo and ammo boxes.  Each gun takes magazines of some kind which have to be replaced when they run out, but the magazines regen over time. This means you have to think about ammo, but don't have to hoard it, or spend all your time searching for hidden ammo boxes.  The health system, likewise, is an interesting compromise.  You have regenerating health, but only up to 50%.  To get to 100%,  you have to consume health items or use first aid stations (which both feel great, by the way).  This made it so you had to worry about getting hit, but not so much that it wasn't fun.There's more to talk about, like the variety of enemies and bosses, or all the secrets, Easter eggs, and cameos, but the bottom line is that this is a great game and you should buy it.

Upgrade stations feel strange, sometimes you get alot of them throughout the same level and then you go without them for a long time. There are also weapons you dont get to keep which is weird. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to find a VR game that makes me not want to put my controllers down, but this game managed to keep me enagaged with it to the point where I managed to complete it in 3 days.This game is a masterpiece with a great story, great gunplay, heart-throbing gameplay in general, detailed levels, some of the best music I've ever heard, a large number of secrets, metal gear level amount of world-building, multiple endings and great difficulty balancing with most fights feeling hard but mostly fair, it also features puzzles which aren't that great, in my opinion, but they are few and far between, so they don't break the pacing, one thing you shouldn't expect is Half Life:Alyx levels of interractivity, you won't be finding newspapars to read and you can't crush soda cans here, but you can break glass and some objects, you can also wear hats and take selfies which save as screenshots.A video game is supposed to be fun and should want to keep the player interested in what it has to offer and this game managed to do that spectacularly.10/10.

In Vertigo 2 the jank is a lot of fun most of the time (not vehicle sections). - Best loading screens in any game ever- Doesn't take itself too seriously but still takes itself seriously enough to be an immersive experience.- Story and worldbuilding is magnificent.- Best bossfights I've seen in VR games.- Indie game (I love indie games)- Hands down the third best OST in a VR game (1st and second are BW and BL)- H3VR reference in the game- Nani says trans rights (canon)- Insane ratio with performance and graphics, like this game is insanely beautiful and I ran it at a solid 90fps (besides the first boss which is currently broken CPU-usage-wise)- Only one real gun and yet getting it is an insane moment if you didn't know it was coming. - IN GAME LEVEL EDITOR WITH CUSTOM ASSET IMPLEMENTATIONS- Should've been GOTY 2023

_childDocuments_.review: Umm...holy crap was this so much better than I expected. At first it seemed like an Alyx kind of game, and while it has that Valve irreverence sorta baked into its writing, the farther in I went, the more I realized that I was traversing a, in a lot of ways literal, melting pot of several game/genre ideas. For some titles, this doesn't work, but in Vertigo 2, it's so deeply embedded in the plot that all the wild and wacky stuff you'll witness on your journey just fits together flawlessly. You'll go between many different environments and set pieces, each feeling quite different from the last, with nothing outstaying its welcome. The weapons, each serving fairly specific, but not required, purposes, all feel pretty good to shoot and reload, with some upgrades that I liked and some I feel I didn't really need.Overall, Vertigo 2 may very well be the best single player VR title I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. Mr. Solo Dev, do me a favor, do ALL of us a favor.....make another game plz!
