_childDocuments_.review: the game is good and i genuinely do recommend getting it, possibly one of the best singleplayer VR experiences out there, if you look past the janky bits that is.the weapons are pretty eh until you upgrade them. I seriously cannot stress this enough, look for those upgrade stations. You can see if you missed any in the chapter select screen. the ones you cannot upgrade that you get from chapter 10 are pretty neat. with one having an overpowered weapon and underpowered melee, and the other having exactly the opposite.The levels are quite simply amazing, they're usually on an incredibly large scale and every environment is unique and usually quite good looking for a VR game. sadly though if you have to go through them a second time because something broke or perhaps you missed something, well there isn't a sprint button. you can however teleport to move slightly faster. so the levels with the size that they are can be annoying if you have to go through them a second time. thankfully that usually doesn't happen and they do flow fairly well. just keep in mind checkpoints can be kinda funky sometimes so make sure you are where you think you are in terms of level progression after getting shot in the head or restarting the game.The enemies are a big step up from remastered, going from moronic bot with a laser pew pew to basically being on-par with the half life 2 combine and beyond. The game gets hard, believe me. The progression of this difficulty however is fairly well-paced imo and the weapons you get are spaced apart just right to keep combat fresh as your arsenal and options in combat expand. I do wish the enemies moved a bit slower though or that there were less of them in certain situations (chapter 10, church side is practically unbeatable from the amount of hitscan enemies and how crappy your guns are in a fight like this), it can be quite easy to get overwhelmed since the combat and arenas seem like they were built for a flatscreen movement shooter and not a VR game. this does however slowly correct itself as you acquire more weapon upgrades and start dealing more damage. Most enemies are well designed and fun to fight with one hard to see exception called a stealth bot. you'll know what i mean when you get your ass handed to you by them.The polish is fairly well executed, i didn't really notice many issues throughout the game, just a few nitpicks but none of them are of note.the movement is quite standard and plays a lot like half life 2 but in vr. air strafe B-hops included! one thing i did notice though is that conveyors are slightly janky and tend to completely ♥♥♥♥ your movement up if they aren't going perfectly straight (like going up at a 45° angle or bending 90°). Your teleport however always works so you can rely on it if you manage to get yourself stuck like I have several times.The music is absolutely wonderful and its available on most streaming services, including some of the more obscure ones like TiDAL which I can always appreciate. Not everyone uses spotify (like the entire hi-fi community) and most companies dont seem to realize this when publishing their OST's.all in all i'd say its definitely worth the money and this will 100% keep me entertained for the next 20-30 hours or so as i strive to 100% this ♥♥♥♥♥.Played on Index w/ ASUS 3060 OC, Ryzen 7 3700x @~4.2ghz, 32gb ram, on maximum graphics. No real fps drops ever noticed, smooth all the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: What if I told you that this game is one of the best VR games? It really is! The gunplay is extremely fun, the game looks great with a stylish cartoony look with some of the most beautiful scenery in a VR game! Vertigo 2 improves on everything from the first game and is quite challenging and the campaign is pretty lengthy (took me Approx. 10 hours to complete). Plus, there is an upcoming update that gives access to a really neat in-VR level editor which is (as of now) is currently in beta! I have not yet seen something like this in VR! You seriously get a bang for your buck with this game!Okay, now keep all of that in mind. What if I also told you that this game was made by a solo developer? And yet, I do not lie. This game was seriously made by one individual. ONE PERSON made this and yet we have AAA studios struggling to even make a VR game that is even close to how polished this game is. This really gives a WTF?! moment lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have played everything that VR currently has to offer, and I mean, EVERYTHING. The itch.io games, the praydog and luke ross mods, the FLAT2VR ported games, the dolphin VR emulated games, every steamVR game, every PSVR2 game, nearly each and every quest game, and nothing, i mean NOTHING comes close to what I experienced playing this game. It takes everything else by the balls and goes "this is how its done". It has numerous endings, decisions that change the outcome of the game and how it plays out, easter eggs, spectacles, weapons, characters, the list goes on and on. New game + doesn't hurt either. I can not put into words how much I recommend experiencing this game blind, along with playing Vertigo Remastered prior if you get the chance. 11/10 You knocked it out the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an action Sci-FI FPS mixed with minimal puzzles, exploration and a lot of hilarious humor.The game resumes the story after the already amazing VERTIGO (Remastered version strongly recommended).You are trapped in a different dimension an trying to go back home escaping from some Sci-Fi captors, there are some other interdimensional characters searching for you and some arcane artifacts. This gives you the premise for a great Half-LIke Action FPS in Virtual Reality that will blow your mind, several times, get ready !!Vertigo 2 is an absolute GEM for VR gaming and should be played entirely, and probably replay it with the added features and mutators.Also I have to say this game should be, and has my vote for being the VR GAME of the YEAR. I freaking love it hehehIt plays great, has great humor, great action parts, several smart and hilarious plot twists, great bosses and it looks incredible in VR. Specially on some specific crazy parts that I was absolutely "wooooow!!" for a millionth time in VR :)Here is some basic gameplay with a lot of pew pew : 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed using the Index headset and VIVE pro (2.0) wands.Love the references to Halflife and other references in the game.  The action is nice.  Pistols are varied, most weapons are upgradeable with very rare printers for modification parts.  Ammo is "automatically produced" so you don't have to find and pick up ammo throughout the game.The cons:The later levels start getting punishing for no reason at all and harder to navigate rather than the streamlined and linear approach the game takes in the beginning.Some weapons require "both hands" to be attached in order to aim which is a ridiculous concept in VR that I really wish no game had ever started doing.  If I needed both hands to aim, I would do it in real life, not in the game where now I can't actually steady my aim because I can't touch my hands together and I'm not putting my plastic "gun" sleeve on just for the times I use a shotgun or need to snipe.Trying to grab the machine gun in the ATOL is almost impossible while it's movingThere seems to be no way to speed up ammo production and the better the weapon, the more you want to use it, the slower the regeneration is for the ammo so the more you CANNOT use it.Boats and other methods of automated transit are seriously flawed, like to bounce around when they hit loading areas, etc.Turning locomotion off (which is specifically using blink) is required in some areas, but it is also fundamentally flawed since more than once I found myself being "reset" into a wall or on top of nothing in the sky.  Don't try swimming without locomotion, that's even worse.The aiming angle of the shotgun is far different than the rest of the guns and really "off" in terms of the angle.I only made it about halfway (ish) through the game before I started seeing cut and paste areas like with the centaur camps.Overall:  I loved the game at first, but the longer you play it the more you're kinda ready for it to be over.  It's a great game that over plays its uniqueness and makes you end up  getting frustrated with some of its quirks like the voice acting that sounds like a couple kids from drama class in high school and the cutscenes that you can't understand at all.I'm clicking recommend, but if there was a neutral button I'd pick that.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is VR's Half Life, a fun shooter/puzzler with great humor and plot. The weapons are satisfying and fun to use, the secrets are well hidden but not impossible to find without a guide, and it's fun enough to justify replay after replay. This game was made by one guy and its better than whole studios in some cases. It's a love letter to people who's been in VR since 2016 and a great welcome to those new. If you haven't gotten this game and you have a headset what are you waiting for??? I promise you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo was an amazing experience from the opening moments to the last moments. Weapons feel good to use, enemy variety expands over every chapter. Levels never feel boring. Levels feel huge and super fun to traverse through. One moment in the game you get to battle in this on going war, and at the beginning you get to choose which side you want to be on.  Anyways yeah, so which ever side you pick will depict which weapons you get and which characters you fight. This game is something that you will keep wanting more from after the end credits role. And I think it deserves to be in everyone's steam library.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: You see streams of this on youtube. You see screenshots. And you think.. "Looks like just another VR game". But it's not. I know there's a lot of hyperbole out there about this game. And I wouldn't go so far as to call this 'the savior of VR'. First of all I don't think it needs a savior in terms of software, it's the hardware that is still challenging for people, both the price and the use, depending on the person and their circumstances.But this is a very good VR game.. period.The story keeps you going and the graphics looks crispier than Vertigo Remastered. The gun and gameplay is fun and expanded upon compared to the first title. There's more choice and there's more fun to be had there. Pros- Beautiful environments to explore (if not a bit empty now and then, but much less so than the first one)- Fun guns and gunplay- Some basic story choices giving players more agency in the story and adding replay value- Lots of fun characters- Adventure!!!- New Game+- Lots of interactive environments- Fun puzzles, nothing too challenging- A very special friend from the first game is back and it made me tear up- It runs great while streaming it to Discord on my 2080 super. (unlike some other VR titles)- The game is much longer than Vertigo Remastered and I'm all in for it! (About halfway into it now I think?)Cons- The first (main) pistol feels like it's tilted upwards too much, forcing me to rotate my wrist downwards too much in order to 'get the shot'. I find myself switching to other weapons often because of that which is a shame. All the other guns seem fine on my Valve Index Controllers.- Like any other VR title there is some 'jank' but nothing too weird, and not more so than other benchmark titles like Boneworks and Alyx. Don't push your hands against the window while inside a train, just a thought.- The game endsPlayed on HTC Vive Pro with Index Controllers.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best games you can play in vr by farpros:the game has tons of weapons including secret weapons (that require doing a puzzle or a minigame)amazing voice acting and bonus points for (gianni matragrano)outstanding ost's beautiful environmentnanicons:repetitive enemies (the game has lots of enemies to begin with, and mostly are reskins with diffrent weapons)some enemies are unbalancedthe game could be hardware demanding (due to the very big levels and the visual effects)----------------------------------if you are thinking of buying the game then i absolutely recommend this banger of a game
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 so far has been been bigger and better than Vertigo Remastered, which is high praise.  Every VR game should strive to be as good as Vertigo 2.  Its a smooth experience and the weapons feel great.  I won't go as far to say it feels AAA but its a blast to play.  Looking forward to playing the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: A seriously impressive amount of imagination, variety and content packed into this VR shooter. I think the closest comparison is Half-Life 2 due how to this game throws so many different/new things at you in basically every chapter. The first 2-3 hours start off a little slow and are about on par with the previous game (Vertigo Remastered), but from there the game just ramps up in set pieces and craziness. Then, you throw in the post-game content like different playable characters, workshop level editor, NG+, etc. Definitely one of the greatest VR games to date and an incredible/monumental achievement by a mostly solo indie developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty amazing story and narrative for VR, really sucked me in and got me hooked at first. My only complaint was the combat is really off in some ways, like everything is made out of rubber including your hands, but if that frustrates you like it did me there is the option to turn down the combat difficulty so it's whatever. Seems like a lot of replay ability too, with NG+, new characters to play as, and alternate endings.Oh I also hated that you are forced to use the teleport function in order to get past certain areas in the game. It's fine but why not just have a bigger jump so you don't have to use it? I also hated how one of the main actors seemed to have a bad microphone but also very minor and I got used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Must-buy.This is what I wanted Half-Life Alyx to feel like. This has so much charm and good gameplay.The world is cool and I love all the interesting character designs.Also love a game that has super satisfying reloads for guns. Every time I popped a canister into my shotgun I felt the happy chemicals in muh brain.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is amazing, BUTThe designer that balanced and named the "Normal" difficulty like that should be fired immediatelly. How about boss that shoots at you constantly and there's only 2 rocks on the edge of arena? How about on top of that flying enemy appears half way through and shoots explosives at you while circling around arena? You think boss would stop attacking at that moment? You'd be wrong!And how about fight on boats? When your boat bounces on waves, enemy boats bounce on waves, laser revolver which is hitscan still doesn't hit enemies when you aim directly at them. Oh and how about 4 enemy boats at same time all have gunners, and a sprinkle of mines that you need to shoot before you crash into them. THAT IS ANYTHING BUT NORMAL. And those gunners hit you all the time, they dont seem to be bothered by waves. All fights in this game have some way to deal with them, but those two - just plain stupid.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing it has so much passion a polish put into it with well hidden weapon upgrade stations, lots of unique enemy types, memorable locations, a good story, secret weapons, the graphics are good in my opinion, good characters, challenging bosses and the puzzles can be a bit difficult but that's what puzzles a for.I also love the references to half, portal, some other vr games and vertigo remastered.10/10 go in blind and don't spoil the game
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: like a 7.5-8.5/10The game mechanics themself are really fun: the guns are all really cool, the enemies all have cool designs, the story is (so far) pretty good, and it can be really funny at times. However, there are some problems: the story is intriguing at the start, but once you get to the tree chapter, it kinda gets boring. I’m in the water monster chapter right now so hopefully it gets better again. The bosses are so bad. Their attacks are so annoying to dodge, and deal way to much damage. It makes you ask ‘how did that hit me?’ Instead of ‘why did I get hit by that?’ Also sometimes you suddenly meet a flood of enemies at once and can barely do anything. I’d say you should get it, but like, wait for it to go on sale. Then you’ll get your money’s worth. Still, one of the best story based tv games I’ve played.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 has got to be my favourite vr game. Its unique game play and story had me captivated from the moment i started the game. The Easter eggs are hilarious, creepy and cool, they make you feel rewarded for exploring. One thing i give top props for is the way they make the secret weapons not feel like some random thing you found in a bin, but rather a whole optional area that has its own content that would more often than not be skipped over. The weapons are fun to use and not unbalanced, i still used the starting pistol all the way through to the final boss. The game offers a strong challenge for the veteran vr players, yet an inviting story to peek the interests of most gamers. I without hesitation give this game a 10/10, as there is nothing wrong with this game, cant wait for a 3rd instalment/ a new game from these developers. Love your work, keep it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Does it dethrone Alyx as the best VR game ever made? Maybe, if it doesn't it comes VERY close. Playing the first one and second side-by-side is like a demonstration in what VR game developers have learned in 6 years. Everything is taken into account when it comes to mechanics and worldbuilding. There are still some technical issues. Had a few glitches that were annoying but resolved quickly. Seems to be some issues with controller rebindings. One part (the boat) that tanked my performance no matter what I did. Things that will hopefully be fixed with updates.I was already planning my second playthrough before I beat it. Then when I did it unlocked New Game+.Vertigo 2 should be a household name in VR as long as VR exists. Anyone making AAA (or any) VR games, take note. This is how you make a good VR game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of the games of all times. 10/10more finished/polished than most AAA VR games on launch, gameplay never gets boring, very good voice acting and some of the best gameplay/gunplay mechanics. very refreshing from the norm, and always keeps you on your toes. only vr story game that properly rewards you for exploring off the set path for the story, and the combat is fun, challenging, but not too hard. very few bugs, mostly visual but nothing game breaking.if you are dwelling on buying this game, just do yourself a favor and buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly believe the first Vertigo is one of the greatest VR games ever created. This game, however, is terrible. They tried to do far too much. I couldn't even keep playing it after the first 30 minutes. I couldn't figure out how to kill the creatures attacking me. If I have to put that much thought into a game it's not fun and definitely not worth playing. I wanted to love this game but I can't because It's awful. I may give it another shot, but for now, there are way better games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an amazing game in it's own. The closest you get to a Half-Life style one, without actually ripping it off. There is so much creativity in here... Like, that it uses your steam profile image in some areas. :D Comedy is gold too and then... there is the recent update which adds new player characters. And those essentially feel like a new game. And a map editor inside VR? What is going on? And most of it is done by a single person?One of the greatest achievements I've seen so far and worth every penny if not more!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is 100% am must have VR title, I had little to no issues while playing except for that the game freezes while auto saving sometimes making me feel sick but beyond that is an amazing story with a variety of weapons to collect with upgrades and multiple kinds of alien/robot enemies for you to discover.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of BONEWORKS and was very sad after finishing the game. Got this recommended if I liked BONEWORKS and damm it did not disappoint. Finished the game and enjoyed every second of it. Beautiful Visuals even on older Hardware and majestic Sound-Design. Haven't had this much fun at a game in a hot while. Worth every Cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the hell out of this game so far!Apart from some out of border stuff, this is game works quite well.Gameplay is entertaining: lots of shooting with some platforming.Mechanics are also what they should be.The narrative is somewhat confusing, but that doesn't mind me. It's clear what you have to do to complete each chapter. You're part of mini stories within the game, which is cool enough for me to keep me going.There is a lot to explore in the many worlds that are presented.Character design and the cartoonish graphics are awesome, love it!All that for 28 euros, you can't go wrong on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I’m honestly speechless.For starters this shouldn’t be someone's first VR experience. But it definitely should be experienced eventually. Half-Life: Alyx spoiled me as my first real VR experience because most VR games that were “Acclaimed and considered the standard for VR” were ultimately destroyed when HL Alyx’s insane polish hit the scene and raised the bar even higher.This game . It may even exceed it in some areas. The first game proved more non-valve half-like games in VR can work. This game takes everything good about the first and cranks it up to 100. I’m not exaggeratingThis game is constantly throwing new, fun and exciting things at you. Every chapter and set piece feels unique and memorable. There’s tons of weapons to play with and tons of secrets scattered throughout the game. They really know when to balance comedy and horror appropriately. It’s just so, so good. I can gush on and on about everything I liked about this game but I think it’s best you just go in blind and have as much fun as I have.For a game on this big of a scale designed entirely by one person is absolutely insane. You deserve the highest praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, did I expect to get such an adventure, when I first saw this funky colourful comic? Nope. But I enjoyed it a lot. Such a vivid voice acting too. I love all of the characters. It's remarkable, how crazy and chaotic the game seems, but piece for piece you understand how well the universe is thought through
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, it's surprising it had made just by one developer ( i´ll buy every game from this guy). It offers much more than the predecesor, but personally i prefer the one (it had incredible locations, a shrink part and a weapon with great zoom scope).PROS: Hands don't go through objects and walls + Varied game and many worlds to explore + Different and multiple cool weapons (bow and organic bomb were my favorites) + Everything works fine + Funny to play + Different ways to go and things to discover + EtcCONS: I missed 2 bosses because you have to choose + I'd would like a weapon with more scope (the revolver has one but it's too near)
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: YOU NEED TO BE PLAYING THIS!!!We got some very good games this year with Hubris, Red Matter 2 and a few others, but the King so far has got to be Vertigo 2! Been waiting a looooong time and am not disappointed. Today's developers are the premier artists of our time. These guys and gals encompass all the arts into a modern medium that can thrill the senses like no other art before. Play the game, if you haven't played Vertigo remastered yet, go play it first. Two thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. Brilliant. Unique. The world is so alive, the guns feel great, wonderful enemy variety, outstanding bosses, this game has everything you could want for an indie VR Half-Like. It does not disappoint, it does not falter, it took a small team like four years to make since it was first revealed, and it shows. Just wonderful. I wish nothing but the best for this dev’s future career, they’re so talented.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is absolutely going on my list of Must Play VR games. I haven't beaten it yet (trying to savor it a bit since amazing PCVR games don't come out every day. Or month... or even year for that matter) so this is just my thoughts after my first 4 hours with the game.Zach is once again flexing their understanding of what makes a great VR experience. Weapons feel good and have a nice weightiness to them without being overly wobbly. Enemy variety keeps things interesting. Physics objects and interatcions galore. The gore system is over the top, but oh so satisfying. Boss fights are engaging and require more than just spamming em with a wall of bullets. The narrative is interesting, writing is genuinely funny at times, and as a whole it's just a cohesive package. The fact that ONE person developed this just boggles my mind.Visually speaking it's a marvel at times, but some of the more enclosed areas can be a little muted feeling. Thankfully the environments never feel repetitive. Each portion of the game has been given it's own vibe so you're not just looking at the same color palettes or assets all the time. Lighting is fantastic. Texture detail on the things that matter most are crisp, and somehow it runs like an absolute dream on my old GTX 1080. Even while using the built in Spectator camera.Now it's not a flawless game. I did encounter some very minor bugs. Nothing game breaking, but for example there was a moment when one of the characters (Bryan) told me to follow them somewhere and they just got stuck in place. I went to the location without them, and the game teleported them to me and fixed itself. Other than that nothing to write home about so far. One non bug related gripe I do have is that Bryan has the worst animations in the game despite being a main character. I'm assuming it's because they used a pretty basic mo-cap solution, but it is something to note. Not a deal breaker by any means though.Overall I'm really happy I decided to pick Vertigo 2 up! It does a fantastic job building upon all the things that made the first game awesome while also pushing the bar higher for VR games in general. 100% give the demo a try if you're on the fence about it, and know that it's only a small taste of what the full enchilada has to offer. I don't usually give number scores because I feel they're a bit meaningless in the grand scheme of things, but if I had to slap a number on it, this would easily be a 9.7-9.8 out of 10. Small deductions for minor bugs and a little bit wonky looking mo-cap. Highly Recommend it to anyone who's starving for good PCVR games. This is GOOD food. I promise you that it's worth the cost of entry.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This acid trip is if Half life and Rick and morty got a child.Its so weird, goofy and the game doesnt even take itself seriously, but at the same time, its unironically such a damn good VR game! A VR Shooter that plays very similar to half life, in which you fight aliens and robots, while a lot of weird ♥♥♥♥ is happening. Same goes for the Creature design. Some aer just... the hell? (in a good way) The story seems to be great too, even tho i didnt understood most of it. Probablly because im just one who doesnt pay that much attention to the story, but rather to details and gameplay. And my god, in these points, this games scores!If you have a decent VR headset, buy this game. Its a experience you will never forget
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: (NO STORY SPECIFICS REVIEW)(this review doesn't mention the bottomless update - which added an entire level editor, modifiers and different characters to chose from)This is a MUST play PCVR title that's oozing with style.# storyThe story is great and follows on from Vertigo Remastered. It also features two branching paths that you can chose from, and you're free to load from an earlier save once you're done to check them both out.# visualsThis game's environments are beautiful and unique - you find yourself somewhere completely new before you get comfortable with your surroundings.# weaponsThis game's weapons feel *designed* for VR. A lot of games have you use real-world guns that are 'ported' over from reality - Vertigo's guns feel designed around your controllers. Love the designs and feel.Swinging melee weapons around felt a little sluggish at first. Took some getting used to, but you'll be shooting for 97% of the game anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The pinnacle of VR gaming. Unironically one of the greatest VR games made.Guns could use a bit more solid aiming, but in terms of music, gameplay, maps, voice acting, it's all so wonderful, and for 9 hours of content, content you can replay for 2 endings and 2 choices and different gameplay, I'll sing the praises all day and night.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: First Playthrough:This has instantly become my favourite game. Just finished my first playthrough and I cant help myself but want to jump straight back in. From a gameplay perspective everything just feels *right*. Weapons are all solid, fun to use and look incredible, enemies each have incredible design and killing them feels so satisfying. Boss fights are all unique and have heart racing moments. The story is so good, it's rare I play a game with a story and actually feel like i'm making actual world-altering decisions but everything in this game feels connected and the story had me hooked from the opening cutscene. Some moments in this game are actually jaw dropping-ly beautiful, I found myself taking moments just too look around at where I was and take it in. Sometimes I find it hard to truly imagine what a level *is* when playing games, in some games levels are just a web of interconnected hallways that make no sense but this game has a real sense of reality that really helps keep the player grounded and the sense of scale amplifies that. Going into my second playthrough soon, hope to find the rest of the secret weapons I missed!A game hasn't made me feel genuine excitement and happiness for a while but this really captured that and the fact it was developed by Zulubo alone has genuinely inspired me too. 10/10 will play many times in the future.36 Hours:This game still holds up as easily my favourite VR game. Everything I said above still holds true and the more I play the more I seem to enjoy it. As of the time of writing this there has been some major updates to the game, one that adds 3 whole new ways to play the main campaign, one turning it into essentially a VR boomer shooter! The love and care that is put into this game is immense and it really shines through. The beta sandbox mode is intuitive and fun and the community already has made some incredible stuff to keep me playing and I've loved my albeit quite little time messing with the sandbox tools. With the introduction of the sequel feature in sandbox there is also mini campaigns being build by the community which is just unheard of in the VR space right now and im really excited to see where it goes especially with the features this game provides. With PSVR 2 release on the horizon I'd imagine more people will be checking out the reviews of Steam before purchasing and if you're someone looking into this game at all I'd take the plunge. The Vertigo Universe feels lively and fun, the gameplay is fluid and intuitive and the design is nothing short of beautiful. Play Vertigo 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the greatest VR games out there, it's still remarkable that a single developer was able to make such an incredible game (along with the amazing soundtrack), with such high quality and variety that rivals and even beats triple-A attempts at VR games. You can really tell this was made with passion and care. The latest update just added even more content with a VR level editor and great options to make replaying even more unique.This game can be rather challenging sometimes, even on normal, especially in comparison to HL:A and more accessible VR games, it really encourages you to make full use of your toolkit, although you can always lower the difficulty, but I encourage sticking to it and learning enemies attacks and behaviour, and what's most effective for you. Taking a break if you're struggling or getting frustrated can often help more than you'd think too :)If you're into the Half-Life series, or just want a fun, high quality singleplayer VR campaign that's up there with games like Half-Life Alyx and Boneworks, with it's own unique and fun identity, this is absolutely worth buying and playing. It deserves all the praise and support it's getting, and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Better gameplay than Half-Life Alyx. A proper, uncompromising VR FPS. Lots of unique weapons that are satisfying to reload. Engaging story and impressive level design.Valve should take inspiration from this game for HL3 in VR, as it pushes the medium forwards more than any other FPS so far. A must buy for VR fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is without a question my favorite VR game ever, and will likely remain that way for a long time. The guns feel great, the voice acting is wonderful, the story is insanely well put together, and the soundtrack is incredible. If you like good story games, good mechanics, and just want an overall fun time, this is a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: FRIGGIN AWESOME VR GAME. This game is PACKED with hours worth of story . The game references franchises like Half-Life and Portal in certain sections of the story which is really neat. The music is great and weapons have improved greatly since the previous game. ALL of this was made by one guy which makes this game even more amazing. 11/10 would recommend this game after playing through the previous one.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blatant ripoff of ULTRAKILL. You run around underground killing robots and monsters with wacky weapons, just to end up in a final boss battle where Gianni Matragrano yells at you. It even stole one of the bosses from ULTRAKILL but the dev decided to put it in a secret room so that less people would notice and call out this knock-off.The game threatened to send Nani to my house to beat me up if I leave a negative review though, so I give this game a 13/8, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best VR experiences that I have ever had!!! _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I really thought it was going to be another mediocre fps type game.  Game play is smooth and keeps you interested. Very little bugs ( I can't remember any that stood out as problems).Boss's are challenging. Area's are all different and unique. Does not get repetitive.  It's not exactly difficult, although I still want a play through on hard difficulty now. The game is not short either. I expected to finish in 3-4 hours as your typical vr game. Nope. There's hidden "stuff" around and different paths in the story line you can take. What I still cannot believe, is one person created this game. Amazing work! I have only played a few VR games that have blown me away, this one and half life alyx so far have been the only 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, it's decent to playthrough but I think it's a lot harder than the last game. Boss fights are completely frustrating, you are given no hints as to what you need to do to the boss, given no cover and you get absolutely pummelled. It consists of dying repeatedly a dozen times and then quitting the game and searching for a tutorial, for every boss. This is even the case with a lot of scenarios in the game, where it's just not clear what exactly you are supposed to do in order to successfully proceed, you just end up dying repeatedly. I found the story to be too silly to really get into and I struggled to even follow what was going on in the actual story, some of the characters I can't even understand what they are saying, like Nani. The environments in some of the later sections of the game are very nice and interesting though. Guns are well enough but I found the larger weapons to be too finicky and ended up mainly using the revolver. I'd say it's worth playing just because of the lack of proper full campaign style games on VR, and most of the scenes in this game are pretty nice in VR too.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Paid £30 for this game and feel like I stole it. Easily one of, if not the best VR game out there (yes, even better than Alyx). Great story, characters, gameplay and levels.9.999 / 10(would have given a 10/10 but there is some slight jank with the controls such as not being able to rebind teleport to your off hand. hopefully this will get patched.)Reviewed at launch on quest 2 via air-link. Performance was great. Played on 9700K with 2070S, 32GB ram
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is VR Game of the Year thus far in 2023. I've played nearly 200 games and few can match the depth this game has. _childDocuments_.review: So much has been said about this game - but not by me! Yet. I can't believe I never bothered to start up this game after buying it. The guns are really fun and the loop of constantly switching weapons while healing is awesome. In the videos I didn't care too much for the cartoony visuals, but they look really great in VR. There's lots of detail on the guns and there are some breathtaking environmental compositions. Don't sleep on this one!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games available.  As others have mentioned, it's basically the only other game that's even close to HL: Alyx in terms of gameplay and overall quality.  Feels like a legit triple-a title.  The fact that one dude made it is mind blowing (though that's probably not true, he likely had help on the music / art assets but who knows(???)).  Either way, Fn amazing game, really well balanced difficulty, the movement options are top notch, and even full locamoton doesn't cause the typical headache/vomit-y feelings (not sure how he pulled that one off!).  Also really loved the underwater 'swimming' quite clever... and some of the vehicle sections are pretty cool too.  Overall, this game gives me hope for the future of VR because honeslty, it's a bit sad how long we have to go between truly great releases that are worth the price of admission.  Let's face it, VR is not likely to be mainstream anytime soon, but just maybe we'll get a few more masterpieces like this along the way.  My highest recommendation, go buy this right now.

_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent example of a game created by a single developer. The campaign is huge and has different levels. Game gives similar emotions to the HL Alyx, game design mechanics are simple and fun with the ability to change the difficulty for your play style. A lot of weapons and different enemies funny jokes and a great atmosphere. For VR it's must must-play collection like Bonewroks, and HL Alyx.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not a AAA VR game, but damn is it close.At its core, it's another FPS with sci-fi background story, multiverse shenanigans and so on. But it's so well executed that it feels fresh again.It's a love letter to Portal and Half-Life,  with several influences mixed in including High on Life, Outer Wilds, Boneworks. The theme of the game varies wildly during gameplay, like Super Mario Galaxy would, going from gory zombie-escape thing to Banjo-Kazooie child friendly battles.It's varied, it's fun, it has a teensy tiny bit of jank left, but come on.In 2023, it's an absolute must-get if you want to get some really fun use of your VR headset again.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: First game was great! Second game has so many things that are annoying. Can't dual wield weapons anymore. Weapon accuracy is garbage. Constant crouching while trying to turn around... more than half of the range of my right thumbstick makes me crouch... this, coupled with the manual reloading change means that combat isn't difficult, it's just frustrating. I have looked up the comments and seen that others have had the crouching issue... which is unique to Seated Mode players.  It makes boss fights impossibly difficult; and I have the game set to Story difficulty! There are other game design elements that feel out of place. It makes me sad, as I really enjoyed the first game very much, but find that I am getting so frustrated by the gameplay flaws that I cannot finish the story of this sequel. This game needs more than just a remastering... it took everything that was great about the first game and threw it out the window.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece and the best vr game of all time. _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well put-together game. Aside from fairly minor glitches, nothing caused me any problems. The enemies have good variety so encounters do not feel static as you progress. The weapons feel VERY solid. (I'm a big fan of the revolver) The fact that you can gib enemies or cause visible damage to their extremities adds a lot of flavour to how powerful each weapon in your arsenal feels. I have not yet had a chance to experiment with the secret weapons aside from one (and I was horrible at aiming it) but it still added variety and fun to my playthrough. I'm definitely going to be giving ng+ a shot. If you like vr games (and don't get too motion sick) I would absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games I've played. Really good weapon handling, beautiful art design, funny characters and writing, a good story, and it's super well polished (only major bug I encountered was an issue interacting with buttons, but that can be solved by making the window fullscreen, so do that)A little short (my playthrough came in at a little under 9 hours) but there is a new game+ with some reasons to replay such as differing story choices and finding secrets (there's apparently 6 secret weapons and I found 2, so can replay to find more)Overall I definitely recommend to all VR gamers, and if you loved the first game you will not be dissapointed. Overall just a massive improvement compared to the (already great) orignal.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Everything a Shooter - VR or not - can do right, Vertigo 2 does right.Interesting and satisfying gunplay with a variety of weapons to choose from? Check.Singleplayer Campaign that does not feel short but also does not overstay its welcome? Check.Constantly changing up the gameplay with new settings, new enemies, slower moments as well as hectic fights? Check!Its also a very good example of what a VR shooter can be, if it wants its selling point to be more than "If you point your hand in real life, you also point your gun in game!". This game does its best to be fair, but combat speed is practically on par with Flatscreen shooters - compare to Alyx, which for all its perfection has a much slower combat pace compared to HL2. Did i mention it has a New Game + mode and unlockable secret weapons and characters (the latter of which change up the gameplay entirely)?If you have a VR headset and even a passing interest in FPS games, there is very little that should stop you from playing this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I loved it. Not perfect, but FULL of good moments and fun ideas. Zany and whimsical. Some of the best setpiece encounters and vistas that I've seen in VR. Spiritual successor to linear narrative FPS games like HL1/2 that don't really get made anymore.Downsides: The beginning is weak. I didn't find the VA with the most lines in the game convincing (he also smacks his lips constantly). And there are too many offices/warehouses/corridors to shoot through, although the game's more vivid locations make up for that.Buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing (Quest 2 - wireless with Virtual Desktop) with a full battery and only stopped when the battery was empty. I haven't encountered a single hiccup, bug or crash. The weapons and shooting mechanics are great, the physics are good, and the writing made me laugh (in a good way). The environments are imaginative and full of surprises and scratch any exploring itch you may have. The in-game interfaces are cleverly designed and I love the fact that you can switch the position of the ammo from the typical (and height adjustable) belt, to your back(pack) so the game can be played perfectly while you're seated - something that most developers don't think about. And, of course, the graphics are very good, showing many and interesting details and I often caught myself just looking around, instead of continuing with the game and the story. Also excellent voice acting and alien sounds. A must have, if you're into VR, and especially if you think there are not enough quality, story-based, single-player campaigns in your library. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and I did for the most part, but the decision to force you to use teleportation instead of having a free move sprinting option makes the boss fights atrociously annoying/frustrating. And yes, I've played through most of the game, but I'm at the last boss (I think), and even on easy I will probably never be able to finish the game due to this extremely odd design decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this is the best VR game I've ever played....even better than HL:Alyx. Vertigo 2 is what I would call a true AAA VR game because it feels like there is just more going on in the game than any other VR title. The world feels alive, responsive and eventful with much to look at, the story lore is easy to get into and understand and there is actually quite a bit of enemies and weapons to be found. I've played Vertigo Remastered and this is a huge improvement, making it one of the few sequels I've ever experienced that actually lives up to the hype and delivers. Weapon handling is straightforward and works well and the A.I. actually can put up a good fight and make for some epic battles. I haven't had any performance or bug issues with the game, so that's a huge plus. The chapters are long enough and provide quite a bit of game play compared to other games while the voice acting is good and dialogue/events in the game can be very funny. Vertigo 2 is the VR game that you want to get if you're looking for something that has more content like tradition pancake games and it's actually a shame that it took this long for something of this caliber to be released in VR. It proves that VR  games can have bigger scope and more content and hopefully will inspire developers to create similar experiences in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun. Kind of Half Life with a Rick & Morty vibe. Cool weapons, creative art, and a nice variety of environments, with some laughs along the way. It ran pretty well on my system (Quest 2, RTX 3060ti, 8 core Ryzen, Win 11), with a few little goofs (like head popping through a wall) and one crash.When it comes to combat, I admit I'm not much of a soldier. Easy mode was plenty challenging for me. The boss battles I could mostly handle, except the lava monster, which was frustrating.  More competent players will have no problem.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure where the praise for this game is coming from. The top review saying this is equivalent to Half Life: Alyx or Boneworks is a perfect embodiment of pure delusion. This games gun handling sucks. Everywhere I aim, my character acts like the guns are 100 pounds and there is what can only be described as an "input delay" in VR as my character swings his arms 2 seconds later to ACTUALLY match where I am aiming. The gun models and reloading are pretty cool, I'll give it that. The game is very very easy, and the combat is not engaging at all. I know it was made by one guy and by no means am I attempting to down talk his work here, but the blind praise in these reviews is extremely misleading. If you think this is ANYTHING like Boneworks or Half Life: Alyx you are probably referring to the extremely obvious HL:A inspired healing stations, or the extremely slow lackluster movement. Boneworks because.... guns? Not sure. For VR veterans, I would not recommend this game to you. If you're new to VR, maybe. Just know, there are so many better games to play, and especially for 30$?? _childDocuments_.review: Works on Reverb G2.Vertigo 2 is much bigger and better than the original. It stands out among other story-driven VR shooters thanks to intense pacing, creative designs and huge variety of everything.The game never gets old during it's 10+ hours campaign by constantly switching locations and adding new weapons and enemies, including a lot of bosses. Core gameplay gravitates towards old-school shooter, but it has a place for surprisingly well made turret section, simple machinery usage and many exploration/story bits. Sadly, there is also some pretty boring corridor shooting here and there, but it never lasts for too long.Gunplay is physical and responsive, weapons are creative and fun to use. Most enemies have satisfying damage indications and death animations. AI of humanoids is decent: they are a bit blind to nearby missed shots and friendly deaths, but at least they can take cover and never get stuck in the terrain.Visuals look really sharp and distinct, while performing reasonably well. There is some infrequent screen stuttering, but it seems that was introduced in one of the latest patches and is not linked to overall performance.Physics is also quite good, with only minor item interaction jank.Overall, Vertigo 2 is one of the best story-driven VR shooters and a breath of fresh air in terms of quality and polish after disappointing Saints & Sinners 2 and Hubris
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: An impressive one-man indie production. Vertigo 2 is a great VR experience and is a must-play FPS. _childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is legit super good. The original Vertigo was pretty good by itself, but this sequel does most things bigger and better. You actually have branching paths in the story, and the gunplay is decent in this game. its still not perfect, since shooting in VR really doesnt work very well if you dont have a larger space, and since you are unable to feel any real feedback for two handed weapons to really work well, but for what it is, its decently solid.One major complaint I have is unfortunately, the sponginess of the enemies. It often takes an inordinate amount of bullets to kill them, making all of your guns feel anemic. This was pretty bad in the original Vertigo as well. Weapon balancing is also not all that great either, as an example, the revolver feels a lot better to use than your starter pistol, but the ammo takes an age to regenerate, and it becomes relatively worthless in the mid game onwards due to how low your overall DPS is with it due to the very slow fire rate. Also, using the sights on some of the guns is not intuitive. The models are sometimes far too large/tall, so its awkward to use the sights. As examples, the starter pistol is VERY tall, the iron sights are barely useable, if you stick a reflex sight on it, it becomes impossible to aim, as its so high up compared to your hand, that it doesnt naturally come to your eyes when pointing it. the optic glass for the reflex sight is also a tiny little thing, so catching the dot in the sight is a pain. Every time I pull up the pistol to aim, I have to wave it around to find the dot. it was so bad that I unequipped the reflex sight shortly after getting it. The SMG iron sights are pure trash as well, I know it was to make it "unique feeling" by putting the middle blade back near your face, and the side blades in the front near the muzzle, but it doesnt work. It feels immensely awkward to try and use the iron sights on the SMG. If you have any training with actual firarms, you understand that you aim with irons by focusing on the middle blade, having it up close shortens the effective distance of your sights, making aiming accurately more difficult, as it is like getting normal sights and pulling them all the way near your face. the first thing you want to get for the SMG is the reflex sight, the glass on that is actually decently large, so you can catch the dot and use it to aim without much trouble. Its better to just hipfire the SMG for close range use till you get optics for it. With that said, I do have to point to the shotgun having good irons. I actually like the iron sights for the shotgun. Its a ghost ring sight, but with the full sight image being an aiming cross. Its natural and easy to use, which is what makes good iron sights.One final nitpick: The loading tips are really insulting. It feels like most of them are mean-spirited, unless its supposed to be a joke. If they are supposed to be a joke, it's a very bad joke.The overall package as a game is very very good though, for sure, this is one of the best VR games out there right now IMO. It really does feel like its near the same level as Half Life: Alyx.If you are new to VR, you will want to get this game (along with the original Vertigo Remastered), but dont play it as one of your first games, it will ruin most other experiences because your bar will be set far too high. Most of the other popular VR titles out there are usually much more limited in scope, or are very early generation VR games, where they are still figuring out good ways to do things. Play around with some other smaller popular titles to get a feeling for VR and get used to your setup and play space, then you can give games like the Vertigo series and HL:A a play to see the true potential of VR.Just a heads up: there is a short event in the game that might trigger thalassophobia if you have it. I noped through that in about a minute thankfully.

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredible that a game developed solely by one person is better than many action-adventures created by full teams, VR or otherwise. The amount of variety on display with regards to characters, weapons, enemies, environments, and level scenarios is simply remarkable. Not to be hyperbolic, but at times this game felt like I was playing something old school--in the sense that it delivers a true adventure through pure gameplay. There is conventional storytelling, however, and it's actually solid; a lot of the characters have nice voice acting, too. Being the ambitious, impressive work of a solo dev, I think there's inherent leeway to overlook some flaws. This game is quite polished, all things considered. Occasionally the enemies can feel too spongy, and encounters wavy, but much of that drag is mitigated by knowing your arsenal. Playing on Index, I never got the hang of keeping my thumb off the trackpad, which led to sweaty situations where instead of continuing to fire my weapon, I accidentally put away my weapon. Also, the vignette effect when at low health made certain parts very hard to see. But that's probably the definition of a skill issue. Now to wait 5-7 years for the next game.

As many say its its half life meets Rick and Morty. I've put in 15 hours and still not completed it.Its almost unbelievable this was made by one guy. _childDocuments_.review: This is the best single-player VR game I've ever played.The game utilizes VR almost to its fullest, especially on the Index.I have never played a game that uses the click on the Index controllers as a hair trigger before, which lets you use the trigger's pull for abilities on your guns.I love the quirky character design, the enemies are so gross and funny.The movement uses both teleporting and locomotion to create really interesting fights with enemies and bosses, where you have to dodge by teleporting away from some attacks or to retrieve to cover.Small details like being able to crush cans in your hands and certain NPCs reacting to your hands are very nice touches and make it fun to mess around to see what happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really understand the hype for this game, and a part of me feels that it's a combination of a desperation people have for "content", and anything that remotely resembles half-life nostalgia. If there was a neutral rating I'd give it that, but I'm leaning more towards negative simply because I'm not finding it that fun but it's enough to hold my attention in short bursts between chapters.It's just very bland and very drawn out. Yes, it's a lengthy game, but only because it repeats the same fights, draws out combat sequences of repeated spawned enemies of the same model, and slogs through so much walking. It's just a basic shooting game with not much else to it. The environments are not that high quality; they're conceptually weird and unique, most of the time, but texture qualities are low and techniques like pop-in are very obvious even when maxed out. The gun models are higher quality, but then you look down at your character model in contrast which is noticeably lower.The gun play is okay although some weapons have more physics tied to them than others and sometimes glitch out (like the enlightened gun). The AI is rough at times, especially when NPCs are supposed to be on your side, chapter 10 was frustrating having a group of AI follow you in a circle but constantly bump into you, get in your way, knock your physics influenced gun to the side while you're aiming, etc.Movement is somewhat annoying as the environments are sometimes very large requiring you to walk a long distance across open landscapes, but the movement speed is slow with no sprint button and no way to increase it. That means most of the time I'm clicking in the left analogue stick to teleport walk forward but waiting for the teleport's cooldown just as it's quicker, but I'm always left wanting to move faster while my hand feels strained constantly clicking.I'd describe this game as a very large meal but one that isn't very tasty, there's little substance to this game unless you're a massive fan of the humour which dips in and out, but the story is incoherent and seems to just be an excuse to move the player forward. The boss fights are somewhat frustrating often requiring trial and error attempts with checkpoints sometimes well thought out and sometimes resetting entire fights, exposing you to the awful loading tip one-liners that are a mix between edgy and cringe-inducing.Again, if I could I would rate this neutrally, and overall I would temper your expectations unless you're for something to really pass the time, or you're looking for something a little weirder with less polish. This game tries to be many things, a story-driven game, a shooter, has upgrades, light-hearted humour, horror, but in trying to do so much it ends up being a jack of all trades with a lot of content but none of it particularly strong.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is one of the most fantastic, engaging, and fun games I've ever played. Period. It being VR is a major plus of course. The game's story is super fun and quirky, the weapons are all pretty unique and great to mess around with and master. The newly added Sandbox Mode is freaking amazing. So much potential for custom levels. The dev is a really hard working and kind person who put a bunch of heart and soul into this game. I highly highly recommend it to any VR owners.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is easily 2023's VR Game of The Year. The fact that it didn't win that award isn't surprising but it is disappointing.The fact that 1 man can make a better VR game than 95% of large VR studios is crazy. Then again this guy did contract work at Valve, he knows his stuff.If you're looking for a fantastic mostly linear, story driven singleplayer game, a half-like, or just another good VR game to play, do yourself a favor and play this game.Tons of weapons, branching story paths for slightly different playthroughs, lots of enemy types, tons of bosses, and lots of level diversity. New mechanics, weapons, set pieces, and other cool "things" you get to do (I don't want to spoil these moments for you) happen quite often and the game doesn't let you play for too long without introducing something new.But everything is just super polished. I ended up playing with the metal door on the healing station for like 10 minutes just because it was so satisfying to open and close. I don't know why it was, but it was.game good buy it

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i highly suggest playing vertigo remastered before 2.aside from alyx, i have never seen a (relatively) cohesive story told in this way in a vr game before, and from about a quarter of the way through, i realized this game is my favorite single-player campaign ever.THE STORY/CAMPAIGNSure, boneworks has a great campaign, and a good story (albeit hidden deeply) However, vertigo takes the idea of a vr story, and expands upon it greatly, characters, factions with different motives, and non enemy npcs that give the game life.THE ENVIRONMENTSthis game looks stunning. where half-life Alyx put you into a beautiful yet dystopian city 17, it looked FANTASTIC, however only about when the game ends, is where we start to see a change in enviroment.Vertigo 2  starts in the halls of Planck industries' own QR-7 but after the first hour, you are suddenly shooting down airships, fighting your way through cave systems, fighting in a battlefield towards a castle, and so much more i don't want to spoil.  THE WEAPONSMany other vr games have tactical weaponry, and that is far from a bad thing.however, vertigo 2, while still functionally similar to your standard rifles and handguns, they look and feel so greatfully different. and there are also secret weapons that you can find hidden through the game. if you have a keen eye, you may also find weapon upgrade cases that function similar to the drones in doom 2016-eternal.i have never liked a vr game to THIS extent since boneworks, if you believe that anything i mentioned sounds interesting, GET THE DAMN GAME. you are in for one hell of a journey.EDIT:After the update this game went from amazing to straight up the BEST VR GAME. Not only did the gigantic campaign receive a few changes, but now you have 3 more unique characters to play as, each having their own fun spin on the way the game is played, as well as a bucket-load of mutators that make the game harder, easier or stranger depending on which ones you choose. as well as a fully fleshed out level editor with most of vertigo 2's props where you can make any level that you can think of. i think it is an absolute crime that this game is fairly unknown as of now, but hopefully many more people get to play this masterpiece when it comes out for PSVR 2 in the future, as Zach put so much effort and care into this game. in conclusion...BUY THE DAMN GAME NOW.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game perfectly balances out comedy and goofiness with serious, good gun fights. The physics feel absolutely amazing, and the guns are creative and very fun to use. Its obvious that this game took some inspiration from half life, portal, high on light, and a  few others. The result is one of the top 5 best vr games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not stress this enough.This game felt better then my first time ever playing Boneworks, a game I looked forward to playing for almost 4 years.This game felt better then Half-Life: Alyx.This game makes Bonelab feel like a tech demo.This game is well optimized.This game has a lot of content.This game has several weapons, endings, interesting character, and TONS of lore for you nerds that are into that.If you wanted a Sci-Fi story game that feels heavily Half-Life inspired, play this game.If you like VR at all even, just.. play this game.Took me 8.8 hours to complete.Suffered SteamVR errors a couple times, or the game itself crashing, but it was very minimal and did not take away from the game by any means.I never once had an FPS drop the entire time I played, it was a constant 120 FPS, no problems at all.Just.. please.Try it, maybe even just the demo.VR Game Of The Year, 2023.The 4 year wait was worth it.Love you Zulubo.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game. The story is good and funny. At least we have a full campaign in a VR game !!!! Good game with a full campaign are so rare in VR, I could pay double the price for it !The game start slow and I wasn't impressed with the graphics nor the enemies animation. But the more I played,  the better I found this game.While the textures aren't great, the universe is pretty cool with lots of varieties. As for the enemies, their's lot's of varieties too.And it's not just reskins, they really do feel completely different.I also love the fact that some species are neutral and some are enemies with one another.The music is good too with great passage on specials occasions.Theirs also several weapons (got 6 as of now) wich do play differently and are upgradable. _childDocuments_.review: This game and the previous game (Vertigo Remastered) are the only VR games I've played that come anywhere close to the quality of Half-Life: Alyx, which I consider to be the best VR game ever made. It combines the masterful level design of Half-Life with extra freedoms that HLA lacks, without going overboard and becoming a janky mess like Boneworks. _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a downright comedy game, but you never have time to laugh because the action is always frantic. The environments, characters, dialogue, weapons, story, enemy types, NPCs, never cease to entertain. There are dramatic moments but those are mostly in service to the humorous ridiculousness of this world.A game where I didn't mind dying over and over again to the bosses because they were so awesome I wanted to replay them anyway. Great soundtrack as well.The thing that bothered me though is the motion sickness. I wish the game's teleport worked the same as in Half Life Alyx, where the screen fades to black for a split second as you teleport from one spot to another, masking the movement between the two spots. In this game, the teleport moves you very quickly between the two spots, which very slowly made me more and more dizzy. Also the part of the game where you drive the excavator really took me out, after that I dumped the headset and layed in bed for the rest of the day. Though, when replaying the game for achievements I found I was getting more and more used to it so perhaps it's just a matter of me getting my VR-legs.I may very well nominate this game for best VR Steam Award at the end of the year!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best recent VR games, but not without flaws. It is a zany, campy, sci-fi adventure that doesn't take itself seriously. It continues right after the first Vertigo game and actually fills in the gaps and explains many of the holes left by the first game's (mostly nonexistent) plot.Overall, I would rate this game in the same category as say Half-Life Alyx or Boneworks. It is a 10+ hour long narrative-driven shooter with some added features to give replay value. That sort of thing is unfortunately still rare in VR, and that alone makes it worth buying. In more detail:The Good:Gameplay - Vertigo 2 is *fun*. It is fast-paced (much more-so than Alyx) and features a variety of enemies with different abilities. The game gives the player a decent range of weapons, with upgrade trees for each. You can customize your loadout to fit different playstyles. There are also several somewhat hidden secret weapons you can obtain.Environments - Vertigo 2 takes the player through an assortment of bizarre and breathtaking environments. There was one moment where I was walking through a giant underground cave with large dinosaur-like creatures walking around. The music set the stage perfectly and all I could think to myself was "this is why I got a VR headset." There are some peak VR experiences in this game.The Mixed:Tone - As I said, this game REALLY doesn't take itself seriously, maybe to a fault. There are lots of overt references to other video games. There are lots of call-backs and cameos from previous parts of the game and the first game. There are lots of places where the internal logic of the game world bends to fit a particular gag or plot point. The loading screens are full of snarky jokes from the developer. Taken all together it's all a bit too ... self-indulgent? It kind of gives the vibe that the developer thinks they're really funny and wants us all to acknowledge it. Personally, I think the game overall is good enough to justify some self-indulgence, but it's cutting it really close. Also, the dev's political opinions do filter through pretty clearly in some parts. It's not a bad thing necessarily - calling video games art means that people should be allowed to express political opinions through them. But when combined with the above, I don't think it comes off too well. Through all of this, though, the game kept me entertained!Story - As would be expected from the above, the story is a constant stream of characters popping in and out of the story at random times. Sometimes they are friends. Sometimes they are enemies. Sometimes both! Sometimes they die. Sometimes they Deus Ex Machina the player out of a contrived situation. It works well as a device to keep the player moving through the many different environments and set-pieces. It's very fun in the moment, but upon reflecting back over the whole game, there isn't much stitching it all together. The plot is just a constant stream of "And then this thing happened!" without too much rhyme or reason.The Bad: Onboarding - The only really bad word I have to say about the game is about the first 10 minutes or so. Frankly, they suck. The opening cutscene has two characters that I couldn't understand without subtitles. (I had to skip it and restart the game with subtitles just to understand) Also, the first character you see is one of the worst modeled and voice-acted in my opinion. So I could see someone picking up this game and not being able to get past the first part.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Among the many players deeply immersed in this game, I find that I genuinely don't have enough words to describe how amazing my experience is. This game not only exceeds but truly changes my initial expectations. Each level has its own unique style, and every 'enemy' reveals special weaknesses that you have to discover on your own. Is the game worth the full price? Absolutely! Are you still eager to keep playing but wonder if you're still in the real world? Absolutely. The only downside is that you can only play this game with VR. But it's genuinely an extraordinary VR gaming experience, unparalleled in its kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 starts out interesting, but slowly devolves into genuinely frustrating, infuriating, and just outright awful gameplay as it progresses. The sheer number of times I got save-locked into nearly unwinable fights is just unforgiveable. The difficulty wildly and violently flails between "I have full healing and no reason to use it" to "I have no healing and must survive on only the natural 50% regen for the entirety of a 4 part boss fight."The game is utterly saturated with combat cheap shots. See a healing item? Sure there will be melee units who can each half-health damage you instantly spawning the moment you try to get it. Everything feels remarkably cheap, and almost everything devours your health, leaving you no choice but to be either full health, or living on a prayer hoping they miss long enough for you to deal damage. Combat is nothing short of either boring, or infuriatingly painful having to eat cheap shot after cheap shot or being just outright swarmed by suicidal enemies who just face tank you.Level design is often nonsensical, leading to a lot of painful back tracking and skyrim-esc self-looping rooms. Its not always apparent where you need to go, and the pacing drags on painfully long for some levels.The Lore is the only redeeming quality of the game, and the only reason I completed it. Which is strange to say that a game that is borderline "Rick and Morty non-serious" actually has a decent sub-plot when its not being perpetually self referential or just cheesy. And yea, I do not encourage you to play Vertigo 1. I made the mistake of playing it, and it is honestly this but shorter and even more riddled with the same problems.Worse is the game has some real potential, its just buried underneath agonizingly bad combat and level design. Absolutely reeks of "we ran out of ideas, so lets just, uh, THROW EVERYTHING AT THE SAME TIME! THAT'S ENGAGING RIGHT?" Only combat utterly falls apart when you have next to no cover and no means of defending yourself outside of healing item spam. Atleast Vertigo 1 had a laser sword you could cheekily use to defend yourself from projectiles, Vertigo 2 has nothing and expects you to "Doom 2016" the game only you don't have the health, speed, or mobility to do that. So you get stuck in a corner and relying exclusively on the one most broken gun in the game, the shotgun. (It's so broken they actually have to take it away from you at the very end.)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to join the choir of good reviews prising this game as one of the best VR experiences I've ever had.The gameplay and the sense of adventure are absolute gold. Graphics are cartoon-ish yet epic and immersive. Sound design and music are incredible and everything is very well directed, drowning you deeper and deeper the more you play, into the Vertigo world.I love that every step forward puts you in a new situation with different types of challenges to discover, new enemies and new, unique locations always so interesting to explore.The use of VR is outstanding, giving you so much freedom in setting up strategies to get out of trouble: brawling, sniping, running, hiding, trapping.. 100% pure fun.I also want to remark the fact that the game doesn't force you into repetitive, uninteresting activities (unlike many other games), such as grinding or search for ammunition or health potions. No, at all times, all you do, it's something exciting, interesting, fun. Congrats!

_childDocuments_.review: This is in my top 3 of VR games, probably number 1, I purchased vertigo remastered when I heard about this game, I beat that game and immediately knew I had to purchase this. if you're looking for a fun story driven, very interactive, multitude of weapons half life inspired game than this is it.
