_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an incredibly fun and engaging experience that touches on so many capabilities of current gen VR. The art style is beautiful 3D eye candy that doesn’t rely heavily on high res textures. Because it doesn’t need to! In turn, this gives back on performance for a smooth ride. V2 is truly enjoyable has been a wild ride. The challenge has definitely been ramped up since the first game so be prepared to use your noggin, your eyes, and your evasive maneuvers.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Such a well made game. Seeing the credits roll and reading that the music, the art and the dev was the same person really put my jaw on the floor. This is the future of VR this game if phenomenal, I have never played anything like this before. There were moments where I stopped playing and just looked at the world around me because it was so immersive. The environments felt so alive, it didn't feel like a piece of code someone had created that I was walking through, it actually felt like i was in a foreign universe, the AI interact with one another, there are fights that don't require you, there are dinosaurs versus aliens vs robots and you're just in the middle of all of it. The use of scale is so good as well. I always wondered why not more VR devs use the power of scale to their advantage. Everything works so well in VR the bosses feel fresh and not like bullet sponges unlike other VR games. Boneworks, Alyx and vertigo are the big three of VR and i think vertigo 2 is the best one. Usually when games have things like secret bosses or secret weapons I don't usually bother to replay levels and search for secrets, but this game is just such a joy to play that I have started hunting for secrets. So satisfying. The game feels so tactile, the sound design even the healing pods are such a joy to use. Even though the ar gun you get is kinda ass the reload is just so nice...So I used it as many times as I could. The guns are creative, the enemies feel fair. It all feels like a nice challenge, I didn't really get frustrated, except the boat level...that one took me a couple of tries. The story is so well delivered and really does immerse you. One of the coolest bit of this game is the ability of choice, the whole story is centred on autonomy, the robots becoming sentient the overarching theme of faith, its simply a well written story let alone a VR story, and you really do feel like you're in control. This is a linear game but there are multiple endings you can get. Finding how to get the other ending was so fun. If you've bothered to read any reviews you're already interested. This game is an easy recommendation to ANYONE. I'm just so impressed by this game, it was so fun to play. I could go on about the whole game for days, but I do not want to spoil anything. YOU NEED to play this game. You will forget how much money you spent on it. You can always make that money back. Experiences like this are rare. This game is an absolute gem. 10/10 truly an epic journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Literally the best VR game I've played.An absolute joy from start to finish, and so full of creativity it makes every other game look empty in comparison, seriously it feels like every inch of this game had so much passion and creative ideas put into it. The characters and level designs are off the wall and i was constantly being left stunned by the kinds of locations and creatures around every corner. It's like the game gets better and better the deeper you get into it, the levels get more wild and the gameplay gets more chaotic. The final boss had me grinning from ear to ear.The VR mechanics and controls are the best ive seen in any VR game to date, everything feels excellent. The gunplay is spot on and the movement/interaction is so smooth and clean. Performance is excellent too, which is normally such a let down for most other VR games. This game looks VERY pretty, and a lot of care and attention was obviously put in to keeping the environments clean and deliberate, not full of clutter and turning it into a laggy mess. I really can't believe how polished and well put together everything in here is for an indie game, especially one made by essentially one person (Zach you're a master of your craft).People call this the "indie half life" and that's a pretty spot-on description. Though Vertigo 2 utterly surpassed it in creativity, soul, and pure spectacle.Buy this game, play the whole thing. It's one of (if not the) best VR experience on offer right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This took me about 14 hours to beat compared to about 4 for Vertigo Remastered. They're both great games, and the original 2016 Vertigo was a very good game. Like the original Vertigo, Vertigo 2 has some major difficulty spikes. There are some bosses you're going to struggle beating, so be prepared to die over and over again. You might even feel like giving up. What makes it even harder is that you're not sure if you're even hurting some of the bosses. That might be my main gripe with the game. Some other gripes: your walk speed is too slow, teleport is too slow, teleport is required too often to progress or beat a boss, the controls require that you remap the steam vr bindings to avoid some annoyances, there are windowed cut scenes, your arms are too thin, and some of the levels are uninteresting or bland to look at. Other than that, it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the main story today, and I have to say, this is some of the most fun I've had in VR in a long time. The environments are unique and fun to explore, the weapons are absolutely amazing (especially when upgraded), and the boss fights, as weird as this sounds, remind me of Hollow Knight due to how challenging, yet fair they are. The characters are memorable, which seems to be quite rare in games nowadays, and the cut scenes are both well placed and entertaining. I'd also like to mention that this is without a doubt, the funniest game I've ever played. TLDR: 10/10 game, up there with Half-Life: Alyx and BONELAB / BONEWORKS, and the only reason I'm not playing it right now is because my VR headset is recharging.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply Magnificent. A new game from one of the, if not the best game vr developer out thereA roughly 12 hour experience by 1 developer is mind blowing. After playing Vertigo Remasterd at its release i was already stunned. But Vertigo 2 offers so much more. Tons of dialogue scenes, which you can walk away from. It is full of references to the previous game, and other games. The characters are fun, interesting, mysterious and sometimes even scary. The game is full of secrets, so exploring is key. After 12 hours i bet i still missed whole areas, weapons and siderooms. The soundtrack bangs, especially the one during the Autonica chapter. My god this game even has storyline braches. You can liturally alter the storyline based on your choises and paths you take. Which is something i did not come to expect from this game. And lastly, this game runs smooth. It can be nauseating for newcommers. But it is super smooth for me. The mechanics are super fluent. The gun animations are more then satisfying and reloading is just absolutely amazing.This game made me feel like a child, it was a real adventure that kept going, took you to all kinds of places. I never knew what happened next. The game is full of random events, places etc. I was still discovering new enemy types in the last hour of the game. The variaty is just immense.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to say it now, this game is 100 the best purchase I've made in months.but the main reason im posting this is because everyones goes "waahhh gun clunky :(((" with a bad review.so, from my research, the game is made in the Unity editor, i use the same.assuming that they are using Configurable joints (basically joints that can act as springs, hinges, etc. kind of like the constrainer from Bonelab.) i can say simply, on moving objects, they are horrible to work with.that "snappy movement" from guns when moving quickly is literally 99% unfixable. (from my research and use of unity / config joints for almost 2 years now.)they basically all types of joints, from configurable joints to spring joints (config joints are basically every single type in one component, but you can also have individual ones.) to hinge joints and so on, all require a rigidbody.rigidbodies are what basically give gravity, mass, and physics.the way i think the recoil in the game works, is it chooses two random values between two other values (how much should the recoil go up, and how much left or right should it go)-before adding forces to the tip of your current weapon upwards and either to the left or the right (depending on the other values.)so in the most simplistic way possible, there quite literally is ZERO fix without COMPLETELY scrapping the physics-based gun handling system, and replacing them with ones which will either just phase through walls making cheating easier, or contacting unity to get better with colliders. (im sure there are a few other ways but these are the main ones i found.)me personally as a developer, have ZERO issue with the clunky gun physics because i understand how displeased they must have been finding out that they cant give you a better experience, and that it would just feel less polished.they tried their best. that's all i can say.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo1 and Vertigo 2 are interesting games.Vertigo 1 I left on the backburner until I basically ran out of FPS VR games to play and so I just really got into it recently and the big thing I noticed was that although it was one of the first VR games I got 5 years later it was still one of the most solid vr games to play and it felt good to play and felt like quality.Vertigo 2 is the same thing again but with more experience and story elements. Again it all feels like quality.It doesn't have the freedom of Boneworks, but as a simple FPS shooter it is fantastic and fun.When badguys spit ink or fireballs at you feel free to smack the projectiles with your guns as well as dodging. A shotgun makes a pretty good baseball bat for that (the projectiles break apart on impact).UPDATE: I have been working through the campaign and it is really good. The story and characters pull you into the world and make you care about what you are doing and the best part is the bosses are creative, have personality, they are challenging, the game is challenging, but the game is difficult in a way that makes you want more and let's you learn how to be good at it. It's like an old Nintendo game where you have to learn the timing and the patterns, but it isn't so brutal that you feel like it is unfair (on normal difficulty anyway).It uses teleport but this game is a rare example of teleporting making the game more fun and not less fun.UPDATE 2: THis has been a great few months for VR first person shooters. Bonelabs was a bit of a let down, but then  we got a whole bunch of other FPS games that came out after. Some were Quest ports and some were from smaller developers, but most of them were actually really good and others at least had the right spirit. BUT VERTIGO 2 IS NOW KING OF THEM ALL.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best single player VR game out right now, period. Half life alyx's campaign doesn't hold a candle in terms of scope or mechanics due to it being shackled down from trying to appeal to a new player base, and boneworks and bonelab's physics are impressive but underutilized in their laughable campaigns. Vertigo 2 has more unique weapons, enemies, and levels than either, and lasts longer with a first playthrough being ten hours long, plus including new game plus, multiple endings, future sandbox level creator, tons of secrets, etc etc. You also don't need to play vertigo remastered to know whats going on here, that game has a pretty minimal story and vertigo 2 includes a recap at the beginning anyway, so if you're hesitant to buy this because you think you need to play vertigo 1 first, don't be, while that game is still very good, (and you should play it eventually) this is miles ahead in every regard and is only five dollars more, so if you're strapped on cash get Vertigo 2 first.TL;DR: BUY THE GAME

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTE MINDBLOWING!A couple years ago I played the first Vertigo and thought to myself that the game was just a short demo that someone half-assed put out for money. Then as I dove deeper into the story I fell in love. It gave me the same nostalgia as playing Half Life 2 for the first time. I beat the game pretty fast and enjoyed all the quirkyness of the original style and put the ol' Oculus down for good until I heard a rumor. A wisp through the grapevine that hinted at the development of Vertigo 2. This was the perfect time for me to try it out and see if it could live up to my expectations that I set for a single developer. When I say that my mind was blown, I mean it. The art style and optimization made it feel seamless and the arcade style of weapons felt great! Every corner I rounded had me thinking that the game was going to end as the gameplay felt too good to be true. Oh! I can't forget the great voice acting either! Each and every single one of the voice actors in the game made me either chuckle from their comedic jokes or sink my heart with the seriousness in their voice. I'm glad I got to experience this and hope others can as well. This game hands down better win ALL the awards coming towards it and I wish Mr. Brown the best of luck on the next one!

If this is the kind of action that you're looking for, then by all means buy the game. You won't be disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me - I had an absolute blast playing this - much better than many VR games costing the same or more.Firstly the game is huge - really good value for money. The story is quirky and fun - but the main star is the levels - I had some truly unique experiences (not just in VR - but from any shooter) and marvelled at some of the worlds this throws you into. The weapons are varied and mostly satisfying, and have lots of upgrade options. The ammo system is excellent, encouraging you to hide out from time to time while your ammo replenishes. You'll also meet some very bizarre enemies - many of which I guarantee you have never seen in a game before.There's really only a few minor grumbles - some of the early levels are a bit flat and grey, making you think you've bought an average indy game, but persevere  and you will be greatly rewarded. The teleportation is just a bit too slow for my liking (the target spot arcs away from you at a limited pace, so quick movements are tricky - but then perhaps that would have made it too easy to avoid enemies). But honestly these are minor complaints in an otherwise fantastic game.I can't recommend this enough - just brilliant.

name: Evergate
detailed_description: 'Welcome back to the Afterlife, Ki. Let's get you to the Evergate, and back to Earth' When a lost soul named 'Ki' awakens in the afterlife, her path back to earth is blocked by the ‘Evergate’. To return home, Ki must decipher her mysterious connection to kindred spirit as she navigates through memories of a time once past. Navigate through each new memory via 85 challenging stages. Harness the ‘Soulflame’ mechanic, unlock new abilities and find your own creative ways to reach each end gate. This ancient power of the Afterlife allows Ki to slow down time, take aim and fire a beam of energy at white surfaces known as 'The Source'. Use your Soulflame to smash through the mysterious crystals scattered throughout each memory. Unleash their power to soar to new heights, reach the unreachable and safely navigate perilous environments. Hit multiple crystals at once to combined their energies and find new creative ways to reach the end gate. Rise to the challenge and collect 'Essences' by reaching all the areas within each memory. Use them to unlock ancient artefacts and boost Ki's attributes. Move faster, jump higher and harness even greater powers! Gorgeous hand-drawn visuals and an elegantly orchestrated soundtrack - recorded by a live orchestra - immerse players in the Afterlife and bring dreams, nightmares and spirits alive in stunning detail. Stone Lantern Games is a Boston-based studio comprised of 4 MIT graduates. Like a gamer choosing a character class, each engineer on the team specializes in one of four proficiencies: Visual Effects, Art, Music, or Narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate is sadly going to be a game that is going to be overlooked by a majority of people. It gives off the impression that it's similar to Ori and the Blind Forest from a visual standpoint, and it's a small indie platformer that may not have that extra oompf that forces you to look at it. Yet, if you actually dig into a game, you'll find a fresh take on the platforming puzzle genre that forces you to keep on thinking creatively, while still forcing you to have a semi-precision in order to execute your puzzle plan. Needless to say, there's not a lot wrong here on the surface, and my entire first two hours with the game was basically me having fun on stream while really appreciating the eye for game design.Dividing levels into three objectives that don't run concurrently all the time was smart, to force replayability but to allow for experimentation with the actual path that you're going to travel, and there's enough leeway in most of these elements in order to scoot by even when a plan falls apart at first attempts. I really enjoyed the subtle layers of teaching: forcing you to think about new obstacles in a different way, and not just use each tool like you had used before hand. The artifacts is a nice touch to help out the game too for those who may have difficulty, although I do believe at times it can be a little bit too forgiving with those aritfacts (ice one in particular).The presentation, while feeling similar, is definitely its own thing: and I was really surprised with the level of detail in the environments in particular. Storytelling is left to be there for people to enjoy if they want, and let's you fill in the holes with your own interpretation without feeling hopelessly lost. Honestly, I'm actually somewhat sad, because I know this game is going to get overlooked in the big picture, but it's a real enjoyable romp that you should take a look at.  list]

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful looking game with an art style reminiscent of Ori and a great soundtrack, but wildly different gameplay.  Here you’ll find a precision trial and error puzzle platformer.  The game is split into different worlds each made of a collection of levels.  The main goal is to get to the end using the special jumping mechanic wherein you slow down time and jump off of some part of the level onto another.  The game requires extreme precision.  Most of the platforming will require a restart of the entire level if you fail one piece of it.  This part deterred me from continuing.  The levels don’t allow for much creativity as it’s clear there is one correct path and it must be done with extreme precision.  The levels quickly become very complicated and tedious to complete.  I would’ve preferred more dynamism in the level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: It looks as if Ori and Dandara had a love child, but with its own unique twists. This is a wonderful puzzle platformer. It's tough, but incredibly satisfying when everything lines up correctly. I actually think it feels a lot like Celeste in its gameplay, in that it has very intuitive abilities, and you'll die again and again, but that makes victory feel all the sweeter. It's smooth, intuitive, and getting all the extra rewards for every level is utterly mindbending from the start.Don't listen to anyone saying it's an Ori clone. Those people have no idea what this game is, or possibly no idea what Ori is. Evergate is not a Metroidvania, it is a tough but satisfying puzzle platformer that's a ton of fun.It puzzles me that using a similar visual style leads to so much criticism. These games are beloved for their art styles as well as gameplay/story. If another dev adopts a similar style and makes a good game, what’s the problem? This is how anything artistic works: something that has a distinct style inspires other creators. It’s the same with game mechanics, and the piece they draw on is always only a tiny part of what makes or breaks the game.So if you feel on the fence about getting it because you're worried it's just a rip off, know that it isn't. Evergate is a fun little game with a lot of heart and its own identity.   It's got 5-8 hours of content, and it is absolutely worth it. I really hope more people get to enjoy this gem of a game.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Evergate is a well polished Platformer-Puzzle game with speedrunning elements.Longer:Evergate is a traditional side-scrolling platformer in the way of games like DCK2, where instead of a team-up mechanic you have the ability to fire your "soul-flame" through a crystal and gain its effects. There are 10 total chapters + epilogue, and bonus levels. The story is well-woven into the game, as is the music, atmosphere and worldbuilding.Every book builds on the main premise of the game, leading to a few antagonist encounters.  As you progress by gaining essence through completion goals or speedrunning, you'll be able to equip artifacts which are both speedrunning tactics for the advanced platformer and a way to help out someone who's struggling with different areas of the game. The puzzle element comes from the crystals. The first 3 books are exciting but not too tantalizing. After book there there starts to be ramp up in puzzles which take some time, thinking, and experimentation to figure out. This culminates in significant puzzles in the last 4 books of the game.Disclosure: I kickstarted & played the game through the whole life cycle
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. Ive been following it sense the days of the kickstarter, its been lots of fun seeing the game grow and develop into what It is today.GameplayThe game play is quite simple to understand, you shoot your soulflame at a crystal in order to use the crystals ability to solve puzzles. The puzzles have good diffucuty scaling with the early levels being more like a tutorial. Once you figure out one of the later levels or puzzles it just feels so satisfying to do it and maybe even try and do it a few more times to collect essence.ControlsThe controls feel very smooth. I played the game on kb&m so I cant say much about the controller but I have heard alot of people say good things about controller as well. _childDocuments_.review: Evergate. This game is a puzzle platformer developed by Stone Lantern Games and published by PQube. Introduced at the Nintendo Indie Game Showcase, it was enough to grab the attention of the crowd. Perhaps for users who did not know Evergate until now, it may be a hidden gem-like game. Really? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ) After playing the game, it is even better than expected. It's one of the best examples of its genre. You guide the child-like soul, Ki that is probably inspired by the mana (soul) concept in the East, on her journey through the Afterlife. As wielding the soulflame to boost to new heights, you will have an adventure with her. As the game progresses, you encounter Ki's past memories across lifetimes. The story itself is mediocre, but the essence of this game lies in the puzzle platformer mechanics and how is it presented to the player.It's a soulflame mechanic. Basically you can slow down time, take aim, and unleash the mysterious power. What really makes Evergate great is the way that it adds new ideas and gameplay mechanics constantly to provide a fresh sense to the player. With 10 worlds where they have beautiful hand-drawn artwork and admiring soundtrack, each offer clever and various levels that you play through. There is a collecting element added here, which can affect puzzle solving. It means that you can enjoy amazing open-ended puzzles that the dev team really put a lot of effort into it.Evergate. It's a well-made puzzle-platformer with gorgeous design and an astonishing soundtrack. With the various gameplay mechanics, every new world you meet adds the cleverly designed levels gradually. If you are looking for a good puzzle platformer where you can experience indie spirit, definitely Evergate is for you. Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like platformers? Buy Evergate. It is as simple as that. You can't find a better platformer at any price by any developer. The level design is ingenious, the controls are tight, the music is lovely, and more than anything, it's really fun to play! I can't remember the last time a game gripped me like this. I just couldn't put it down. Every new chapter in the game (there are 10) adds new mechanics and totally changes the way you navigate the levels. The final bits of the game are a beautiful culmination of everything you have learned. You can play this game casually and get through every level in a few minutes, or you can try to beat insanely fast speedrun times and learn perfect precision to get every collectible. Play this game any way you want to...but do yourself a favor, and PLAY THIS GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviewers have noted, Evergate is a beautiful, finely-tuned platformer with deep and unique mechanics. But I want to call out a particular aspect of the game that I find especially impressive: more than almost any other game I've played, it makes room for players of a wide range of skill levels.The levels in Evergate can be completed just by getting to the exit, which ranges from fairly easy to moderately difficult, depending on the level. Each level also has three optional goals, some of which are very difficult (or at least they were for me). Completing the the optional goals unlocks powerups; collecting and playing around with them provides replay value for completionists, while players having trouble can go back to gather powerups from earlier worlds to help them through the later ones. Even beyond the game's explicit goals and rewards, it's extremely satisfying to get "in the groove" and blaze through a level with precision jumps, and I get the feeling Evergate would be a lot of fun to speedrun.I played through a beta version of Evergate on PC and then 100%-ed the final version on Switch, and I felt nicely challenged but not frustrated throughout the entirety of both playthroughs. That's impressive, and it makes me think that a broad range of other players would enjoy it just as much as I did. If you have any interest in platformers, give Evergate a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't have many reviews, so I thought I'd leave one. Evergate is a lite puzzle platformer (the puzzles are far from mind-bending) with some Ori vibes. However, the similarities to Ori are mostly in the graphical style and presentation, which are both great. The soundtrack is pleasing to listen to as well. It is definitely a fun game, and you're looking at at least 10hrs of quality fun if you decide to go for some of the challenges offered by the achievement set. The achievements in this game are a nice mix of challenges, exploring different ideas like beating x levels without jumping, and just general misc stuff. They were quite fun even to just figure them out.There is quite a bit of replayability if you're a speedrunner, as there are a variety of strategies for going faster due to the artifact system. There are 30 artifacts in the game, each giving you a modifier such as burning things whenever you fire, or an increased jump height or speed, all the way to creating a vortex when you fire your first shot for a level. If you're not a speedrunner though, you're looking at a solid 10hr experience here.One thing I quite enjoyed about Evergate is its progression. There are 10 worlds which are divided into books and chapters (4 books each with 2-3 chapters), and each book introduces a new use for the soulflame and focuses on this new use for the remainder of the world. This keeps the gameplay fresh throughout the game without ever feeling like you've seen a certain mechanic too much.Overall a nice lightly challenging game with a nice atmosphere, music, and unique gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful and amazing 2D Puzzle-Platformer that I highly recommend and will now explain why I think that way.The Music in this game is gorgeous, it just hits you emotionally at all the right moments throughout the game and its sweet story. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Evergate is a puzzle platformer with a polished gameplay, unique artstyle, an amazing soundtrack and a cute story. It follow Ki and her journey through the afterlife as trouble stirs. If you enjoy speedrunning you'll love this game. If you don't, there still is plenty to enjoy.Length: My first playthrough of the game took about 6 hours. Each level has 3 challenges to it. First is using all of the available tools. Second is reaching 3 specific areas on each level. This is finishing the level under a time limit. My first playthrough consisted of doing the first two challenges through each level. Speedrunning through each level afterwards took me about two hours. Level Design: It's very cleverly design. You can go through each level multiple ways, especially once you get more abilities. I found the puzzles to be a bit challenging, but not frustrating. Story: It's nice and cute. It's a little confusing at first, but I believe that's intended as your character is learning as you do about the afterlife. Artsyle: Very unique, beautiful, enhances gameplay and never interferes with it. Soundtrack: Great soundtrack. I found myself humming the songs outside of the game. I'd put it just below the tier of ori and hollow knight. Replay Value: It has decent replay value. Because of the different ways you can do each level, it doesn't get too repetitive. Saying this, there isn't necesarily anything too unique through each playthrough. If you enjoy speedrunning, it has a lot of replay value though. Performance: I had no performance issues and only one minor bug throughout the whole game.Cons: I found once I got all the skills and abilities, the only way to truly utilize them was to just speed up your time in previous levels. I would've enjoyed something like B side on Celeste where it's similar map, but you really gotta platform and think differently. Wishlist: I have no idea if there are any plans, but workshop support for community made maps would be really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate is a gorgeous puzzle platformer with some of the most unique and interesting mechanics I've seen in years. The puzzles offer a balanced challenge in terms of both problem-solving and mechanical execution, and mastering the controls to fly through the levels feels incredibly satisfying. The fantastic level design also gives the player a lot of freedom to come up with unique and creative solutions to the puzzles, rewarding players who enjoy thinking outside the box.The settings menu includes the basic necessities (volume control and key rebindings) as well as a lot of other quality-of-life improvements, such as a speedrun mode that adds a timer for each stage.The next section might be going outside the scope of what you'd be looking for from a review, but this game means a lot to me. I've been following its journey to completion ever since the first public demo releases, and the developers are genuinely some of the most lovely people I've ever met in my entire life. So seriously, if any of this looks or sounds interesting to you, give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: While the aesthetics are surely inspired by Ori, the gameplay is pretty different. You make your way through levels by activating "crystals" placed around the map, and to do that you fire a beam at them — which only works if there's a white surface at the end of the beam. As a result, every level is a sort of puzzle. You also have artifacts which give you powerful upgrades and can break many levels (for example +30% jump height lets you reach many platforms you otherwise couldn't), however you can only equip one at a time, and this type of level-breaking is kinda part of the appeal. Changing your equipped artifact restarts the level.The crystals themselves grow in variety over the course of the game, so at first you're only working with one type in each "room", but at the end it's many more, significantly increasing complexity. Some of the later levels can be a b*tch to navigate the intended way, but the game never demands use of artifacts, and so you can usually, if not always, find a way to break them, should you need it.Movement is pretty fast, especially falling, but aiming your beam slows down time, and you can also hold Q to freeze it completely whenever and for as long as you want. So I wouldn't say the game requires much mechanical skill, it's all about figuring out how to get through.There's also a neat story and good BGM.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. This game is so polished, you'd never believe it was made by such a small team! The visuals are some of the most gorgeous I've seen - as well as being adorable - and the music is FANTASTIC. I'm so glad I decided to buy the soundtrack with it! The gameplay is really sharp and tight, which is crucial in a precision platformer, and the pacing is perfect - the new abilities are introduced gradually enough that they never feel overwhelming, yet none of the mechanics outstay their welcome.When it comes to difficulty, Evergate is definitely not an easy game. There's an achievement for dying/resetting 100 times, which I got after about 2 hours. I really appreciated the option to simplify ability activation because I was having some coordination issues with my controller, and there's other options to change things or make them easier too! There are two elements to each level, figuring out what to do and then executing it, and most of the time, the former was a lot trickier. Some levels, I bummed around, totally lost, for 15-20 minutes, but usually it was quicker than that and there were only a few levels that I found truly frustrating (and only one where I had to cheat, because I somehow managed to miss ). When you throw artifacts into the mix, which convey various extra abilities suited to different playstyles, you open up some different ways to complete levels. In feel, it reminds me of games like Blue Fire, Unbound: Worlds Apart, Nihilumbra (the void part), and the White Palace section of Hollow Knight, but never as difficult or downright unfair as those games got at their worst (unlike Evergate, the White Palace's execution is WAY harder than figuring it out; it's an exercise in "You want me to do what now?"). There are also a couple of levels reminiscent of the escape sequences in Ori and the Blind Forest, which I've always enjoyed in a sort of masochistic way. In terms of replay value, the time trials and tons of tricky achievements will let you keep going if you want!Finally, I adore the story! It's so rare to see a game that focuses on platonic relationships, let alone a sibling one. I really enjoyed the lack of cliche in the story beats, and how it covered grounds from innocent joy to jaded heartbreak to redemption. It truly touched my heart, and I'm SO glad this isn't one of those games (*coughGuacameleecough*) that forces you collect a bunch of super difficult extras for the privilege of a non-tragic ending.If you enjoy precision platformers at all, I HIGHLY recommend picking this one up, and throw the soundtrack in as well! Though occasionally frustrating, Evergate is a beautiful and thoroughly enjoyable experience that will leave you with a smile. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, as everyone mentioned, similar to Celeste, so if you like Celeste you 99% would enjoy it.Few myth busted from negative reviews:- It's shorter that Celeste. Right, but you still need about 10 hours to complete. It's like getting through A-sides without berries, same, I think.- Need to be very precise on controls. Wrong. No room takes more than 30 seconds, average 10-15 seconds, restarts are instant (no animation delay/fade), I could not imagine less punishment for death.- Puzzles are repetitive - also wrong, you never applying same two tricks in a row, if you repeat something - only in the middle of combination of new mechanics, so it's always fresh. Only first world, maybe, as you only get access to 1 puzzle element, but even then I did not felt bored.- Missing tutorial. Dunno maybe who wrote that was blind. There is a tutorial. And you need to repeat basic game actions several times. Game literally have 4 controls - left, right, jump, and activate (with aim). WTH you need more tutorial for? It's just - aim the crystal with mouse and click, that's all the controls! _childDocuments_.review: Evergate is a relaxing puzzle platformer that is mostly about strategy. Execution is typically not difficult due to time slowdown/stop but flying through the air chaining multiple crystals can be very satisfying.The puzzles stay interesting by introducing new mechanics in every world and gradually ramping the complexity. Additionally, each level has three optional objectives which are the main source of difficulty in the game. Completing these objectives will unlock power-ups that will help make levels easier or allow new strategies for speedrunning.The story is not interesting but that does not matter in such a gameplay-focused title.Overall, if you enjoy platformers and puzzles, pick this up!

_childDocuments_.review: Genre:  -Puzzle Platformer Fit for me:-Not in my top 10 fav genre, so bad fit.  However, I love all other types of platformers, so maybe this one can win me over.Pros:-Gorgeous artistic style.  They clearly took inspiration from Ori, as this game has a similar aesthetic and the main character resembles Ori.  They are creative enough to make it their own unique experience while paying tribute to one of the most beautiful games ever made.-Perfect tranquil soundtrack w/ spot on sound effects.  Everything sounds really good and fits well w/i the Evergate world.-Extremely responsive and fluid controls.  They nailed the most basic part of this game.  This entire game centers around chaining multiple mechanics while in mid-air, so the controls need to feel silky smooth, and they do.-Fun movement, jumping, and the main juggling/slow down time mechanic.  Another clear inspiration from Ori but they expanded upon it big time.  They created an entire game centering around this one mechanic but added 10 different environmental mechanics that interact w/ this chaining/slow down time mechanic.  It's executed perfectly, and is fun, engaging, and intuitive to use.-This is a true puzzle platformer that really combines some of the best elements of puzzle games and the best elements of precision platformers.  I would play a lot more puzzle platformers if they all had this type of gameplay.-Adorable, heart warming story that works really well w/ the gameplay experienceCons:-Some of the mechanics at the end are bit complicated and it would have been nice to have some form of tutorial on how to use them.  I eventually figured them out, but they sometimes took a good amount of trial and error.-There are a ton of upgrades that you can unlock, but I found myself mostly using the 30% jump increase and 20% boost increase.  A lot of the other upgrades seemed fun, but felt very situational, mostly meant to be used in the world that you gained access to those upgrades.  It would have been nice if all of the upgrades were a bit more applicable.-No level editor.  I think a level editor would be a really cool idea, so maybe it's a possibility in a sequel.Thoughts:-Evergate is my new favorite puzzle platformer.  If all puzzle platformers had a similar focus on fluid, precise platforming sections; I'd play a lot more of them.  This is a great option for ppl that like precision platformers but would prefer a slower, more methodical approach.  I really enjoyed my experience w/ this one and will be on the lookout for any future games by these devs.Consensus:-Excellent Game (Tier 2 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This is hands down my new favorite puzzle platformer.  It knows exactly what it is, and doesn't try to do too much.  With a gorgeous aesthetic, excellent fundamental mechanics, and a heart warming story, Evergate is a great game and one of my bigger surprises of 2020.  I love when I play a game that gets me excited to try other similar games in that genre.  Here's hoping that I can find some more puzzle platformer hidden gems!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into puzzle-platformers, buy this. Just do it. Evergate is a fun game with smooth gameplay. The puzzle elements really come into play if you go for 100% the game, because essence collection, makes explore the level differently, especially if you wanna get more than one at the same time. Some achievements also do that. Evergate has 60+ level with gorgeous art, outstanding soundtrack. The puzzles are super fun, the story is average but cute and wholesome. There are a wide variety of artifacts that are unlocked upon completing essence%, that can be fun to experiment with or give a level more than one way to approach. I feel like certain aspects of this game can be improved, however for what it does, it does really well and it's really fun and engaging and that's what truly matters. Bonus: the devs are really cool. Overall I give this very fun game 8.5/10.

I'm awful at jumping puzzles, but they make it so easy to restart the levels repeatedly and instantly, and if you are a speed runner this is going to be your jam!! _childDocuments_.review: There's something about ethereal gameplay and orchestral music that gets me every time.If you want to see some Evergate gameplay for yourself, watch my first impressions gameplay above. Evergate is a puzzle platformer that's kind to newbies and rewards good players with a satisfying gameplay experience. Each stage is fairly straightforward, but if you're going for 100% there's enough uncertainty and enough precision required to take a few goes. Plus, when you're just starting out, it's going to take a hot minute to get used to it. You jump, you shoot Soulflame, and as long as your Soulflame passed through a crystal you'll get a boost on your jump. Pass it through multiple crystals and you'll get an even bigger boost.If that all sounds a bit pedestrian, it's because Evergate has to be seen or experienced. The art style is beautiful. The orchestral music is so good that I'm disappointed it's not available to buy separately. And once you start playing, you understand how much fun this game would look if it was done as a speedrun. Failure is frequent but doesn't feel punishing because you just respawn instantly with the level reset. The lack of downtime is huge. There's also a bit of a mystery at work, told beautifully through images and sound effects that leaves so much to the imagination. This team knew what they were doing, and they executed it well.Either buy Evergate now or add it to your wishlist. It's a fantastic game that isn't receiving near the attention it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Curator Page: Evergate a 2d puzzle game set in a wonderful hand drawn vision of the afterlife, where you play as Ki who wakes up and is greeted by the grounds keeper,  who helps you wield and use your soulflame (your main mechanic in the game) and tells KI, if she is to  return to earth she must go through the Evergate, But it seems the gate has more in store for her when it presents a memory book to her, uncommon for the gate to do, going through these memory books you find out that the memories are not Ki’s and it's up to you to progress the levels to learn the reason. Evergate Is a wonderful 2d platform that will bring speed runner flocking to it just because of its technical way that people could finish each level quickly and the game encourage it. With 3 different objectives during each stage that unlock ancient artifacts to boos Ki’s attributes like move faster, jump higher, and many more to help you along the way. The 3 objectives are  1. Collect all essence in the stage which are like small collectibles scattered on each stage. 2. Destroy every special crystal in the stage (I’ll go over them more in a second) 3. Beating the stage within a set amount of time. Each giving you one point to help you unlock the 3 unlocks in each memory book. Now the Special crystals I talked about. These crystals are the ones that help you traverse the stages. Activated by your soulflame only while you are aligned with a white section on the ground. Thats the best I can explain it but you should be able to see what I mean in the gameplay. Each memory book adds a new crystal to list. First being a simple launch crystal that sends you in the opposite direction you aim your soulflame. Others being platforms, flames, item swap and many more. Making later levels complex with multiple ways to complete. Other obstacles will dot your adventure as well, many death traps on each stage like thorns, a strange osculating star fall or whatever it is, and then my distain. The crows that will aim for you after each special crystal you destroy. They are used in some stages to help you reach the summit but are a real pain in the ass.  Now of course the graphics and sound design. The wonderful hand drawn elements in this game give the wonderful personality it has. I love how a good bit of games are going in this direction and gives the individuality to each title I play. Sound design is not too bad in this game the music I am in love with. The score that they gave this game works perfectly and is very uplifting and floaty. But, the sound effects at time that can be bothersome. The gem destroying gets repetitive and back again to the crows their howl is not my most favorite especial when you are speed running through the level and may need to retry the level because you made a mistake. But other than that, Evergate is a fun and beautiful game with a wonderful story. That I think most people will enjoy with its level design. I would recommend this game if you think it looks good and you think the game looks fun because, it is and you won't be disappointed. With 85 stages for 19.99 it well worth its price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many of you I collect stand-out indie games despite an eternal backlog. The art and puzzle-platforming of Evergate caught my eye a couple years back, and now finally playing it, it's everything I hoped for. The art's lovely and blends into responsive, thoughtful gameplay, as the other reviews say. It has several chapters and several levels per chapter, plus bonus challenge levels, each with three tiers of challenge -- clearing, getting bonus coins, and then meeting a speed-run goal. Just clearing is sufficient to progress, the coins achievable just by trying things out, the speed runs requiring precision and practice but not to the point of frustration (so far!).As for music, it hasn't gotten tedious to listen to on the tougher levels yet, if anything it's a bit catchy as I swing back through the parts of the level I've solved. The levels being designed with speed-run in mind, it's not slow or exhausting to get back to where I was after resetting to try another solution. Admittedly haven't played long, but no complaints after 100%'ing the first chapter for sure. Go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate was recommended to me as the newest indie platformer for people who enjoy games like Celeste and Hollow Knight. :-)I really liked it and can definitely recommend it. The goal of the game is basically to connect a number of level "items" in the correct order and way to reach the goal. The "items" you activate with your beam will give your character varying abilities (e.g. they launch you up or give you a double jump) and the underlying mechanics are all interesting and feel satisfying to use. It is not only about solving the puzzles, but you also have to time and execute your solution in the right way. This is where the game becomes a platformer. I would say the platforming feels pretty well overall: it is relatively slow paced and allows you to even slow down time which fits the puzzle character of the game. This makes the gameplay feel pretty chill. You can chain moves pretty fast once you get good at the game, but it never feels like you're in a rush. Both puzzle and platforming gameplay wise, the game provides a challenge, but is not super hard either.For each level you have three extra goals: reach the goal under a certain time limit, collect collectibles that are spread throughout the level and use all the "items" in the level. Especially the last one is a breath of fresh air that feels weird at first, but will grow into something you enjoy. You are probably used to the convention that basically the more things you skip in a level (let's say a health pickup), the better you play. This is how you should play to reach the time goal, but if you're going for the "use all items" goal, you have to play the levels in a different way. You could say you have to dance with the level. :-) Sometimes it's also much harder to include all the items in your combination of moves than ignoring some. The three goals that you don't have to complete all at the same time provide an opportunity to play each level in multiple different ways and see it in a different light each time.I found most of the levels pretty good and satisfying to figure out. Some levels were very intuitive and I could improvise the solution while flying through the air while others took a while to think about different options. A few levels go a little overboard in my opinion with putting a huge number of items in the level where you only really need a fraction of them. Some people like having a lot of different options, but I prefer levels that have a more specific solution. Other levels are exactly like that though and you need to use all items in a clever way to be able to reach the goal. So in general, the level design is really nice and probably has something for everyone.The game comes with nice graphics, a relaxing soundtrack and a cute little story for setting the mood. I found the mechanics very polished and I didn't really find any glitches even though I played it at launch. It seems like a miracle that the game even runs on my laptop at all which can run Celeste and Super Meat Boy, but not Hollow Knight. Evergate - like Hollow Knight - has lots of particle and lighting effects, but it always ran fluently for me.

_childDocuments_.review: been following this game since 2019 when i saw it at PAX East, drawn in by the elegant visuals. i'm not the biggest fan of platformers, but this game had a certain magnetism about it that i couldn't ignore.now that the game is released, i was very pleased with my experience. fortunately, Evergate is not just a "pretty face" - it's a damn good puzzle platformer too. it's clever and well paced - just as soon as you get the hang of one mechanic, they introduce a new one, and it feels rewarding to learn how to combine the new mechanics with the old ones.i appreciate that its "campaign" doesn't overstay its welcome, however if you really enjoy these types of games, there are lots of challenges to go back and complete, as well as several bonus levels. i beat the game in ~6hrs, but i bet there's another 3-4hrs of content there if you want it.the storytelling does a lot with a little, which makes it a great accessory to the gameplay - it's easy to follow, it delivers a nice message without ever distracting from the gameplay.in my opinion this game was well worth the 1.5yr wait, especially if you're a fan of these types of games. please buy the game if you think you'd be interested, as this is one of those studios that we should support!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I'm a kickstarter backer, beta tester, and contributorEvergate is a tight and tricky 2D puzzle platformer that combines the otherworldly art style of Ori and Child of Light with the tough-but-fair, die-til-you-get-it, stage-based platforming of Celeste and Super Meat Boy. On top of this foundation is a unique puzzle mechanic in the form of memory crystals that the protagonist Ki must shoot with her soulflame to unleash their powers. Crystals must be used with wit and precision to reach the gate at the end of each level, and to unlock playstyle-boosting artifacts via optional achievements.A charming and affecting story about second chances enhanced by a magnificent fully orchestral soundtrack round out this impressive first release from four-person indie outfit Stone Lantern Games.Fully supports both controller and KBM play, and is a bast for both heady, deliberate play and speed-running.
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent puzzle platformer, rewarding both careful planning and skillful play. The puzzles and mechanics are really well designed, with the different crystals offering a really solid variety of challenges for the different worlds/levels. The straightforward path is often discovered after a bit of experimentation or thinking, but often levels with have surprising shortcuts or tricks to the layout you can abuse to blaze through an otherwise tough room.Besides the gameplay, the art and the music (especially the music!) is excellent! The vibe is really beautiful and dream-like, with the jump in settings translating over to the aesthetics in a fun way. Definitely can recommend if you're into either puzzle platformers or more skill-based ones like Celeste.
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: A nice gem of a game with great level design, music, visuals and an interesting story. The Artifacts were also a great incentive to replay levels and complete objectives/gain the essence required to unlock them. Some of the artifacts did feel a bit cheap but you can play the whole game without using any of them. I'm glad most of them are fun to use since it actually felt worth unlocking them and spiced up the way in which you completed a level.The objectives are completely optional so you can finish the whole game quite easily if you were to play it that way. For the best experience, I recommend trying to complete the "collect the petals" and "destroy the crystals" objectives at the same time. It makes completing a level much trickier and provides a very enjoyable challenge.For a puzzle platformer with no combat, the game had a good amount of story which I personally found interesting and felt that it enhanced the experience. Though it was mostly told through a few seconds of visuals and a bit of dialogue whenever your reached a new area/level, it was still enough to make it feel like you'd been through a meaningful journey once you reached the end of the game.The visuals were quite charming and the music blended quite well with them. It great soundtrack that set the mood perfectly for each level, especially during the final area. Overall it's a fun, charming game with a good amount of replayability and an interesting story that has a nice message. It's definitely worth checking out, especially if you're into puzzle platformers or indie games in general.

The game can be played casually, as a completionist or as a speed runner. All three are a great time. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: No further updates or communications from Eko since my last message. The game is left in an awkward state. The rucks are too easy to win and the AI is tactically awful and will happily kick the ball out of the full, kick the ball when there's space ahead, or try and play from behind their goal line. I can still recommend the game because of the hours I've put into it but it's still not worth it at full price, especially with no further updates coming.EDIT: Eko are listening to feedback and have already added some much needed improvements to the game! I would keep an eye on the game because if they keep this up, I could eventually be recommending it at full price.I'm in an awkward position where I can't truly say whether I recommend this game or not. This is the first rugby game since Rugby 08 that has intrigued me enough not only to pick it up, but to pick it upon release.The main takeaway is that firstly, it's a rugby game and secondly, I've actually had fun playing it! I wouldn't say at this point it's worth it at full price but it's a really step in the right direction and if Eko Software and Bigben keep moving in that same direction, we can expect a good rugby game by the next world cup.- The game is actually fun. I've enjoyed my time playing it.- There's a nice amount of tactical fidelity and room to play around with it. Each tactic feels different enough to another.- A decent number of licensed teams and players. Probably the best we can get until the game is big and popular enough to include the lower divisions and full licensing from around the world.- The controls (that I've figured out) feel like they work. I've not been left scratching my head asking why a player has done X when I asked him to do Y.- A proper build-a-team career mode called "Solo mode". I really like the FIFA-style cards!- The menu interface is visually good and easy to use.- Substitution suggestions works really well.- Mechanically, as a game, a lot of it works. It doesn't quite have the fun and polish of FIFA and it doesn't feel like it quite represents a real rugby match yet but it's closing in on both.- The cost of the game for what you get. It's not worth full price.- Breakdowns against the AI are too easy. As long as you have one or two players nearby, you'll win it with ease.- The pacing of the game could be improved. Tackling feels fast and responsive but everything else feels slow and clunky. It makes any tactics outside of ridiculous offloads and constantly passing it wide to the winger very difficult. EDIT: Pacing has been improved and is on the right track!- Sprints down the wing are difficult as the typical winger has enough stamina to take them around 10 metres before they slow down to toddler-pace. Same with grubbering it past - it seems defenders always have an advantage. EDIT: This isn't as bad as it was before with the newer patch! Much improved!- Stamina in general is quite confusing. Being hit by a tackle takes away half of a player's stamina?- Player and team ratings don't match up or are misleading. Looking at my build-a-team with mostly players from Leicester Tigers for example: England star Manu Tuilagi 68, single capped Noel Reid 78. England international George Ford has a rating of 71, Jarrod Evans has 77. I assume this takes into account team performance as well as individual (struggling Leicester).- 40 metre offloads from props are still a thing. I understand this is a fun vs realism thing but it's laughable at times.- The AI commits way too many fouls and there aren't red cards. I've seen a match with 7 yellow cards, 2 of which were the same player (no red). EDIT: This has been patched out and is no longer a problem.- EDIT: A fair amount of bugs. Crashing right at the end of matches and the AI refusing to use the ball after a maul are the two gamebreaking ones.- EDIT: The game is a bit too easy now, even on Pro. The AI has some real blunder moments like kicking the ball out on the full.- Player representations on the pitch aren't great. This is purely a visual/graphical thing and hasn't impacted my enjoyment of the game.- Commentary team audio sync doesn't match the game. "Taking forever to take this restart!" after 10 minutes of open-play. "The referee has called an advantage after a foul" after a simple knock-on.- The tutorials leave a lot to be desired and I felt like I didn't gain anything from using them. Is there even a page to show me which button does what? What do the flashing buttons mean during the lineout?- It's clunky and cumbersome to organise your squad on the team management screen. The option to filter by position (sort isn't that great) or a "best-in-slot" quick selection option would help a lot.- Broken field play is still too organised. I want turnovers to feel as manic and disorganised as they do in a real match and make opportunist tries from them more of an option.- The attacking line is usually so flat, even at its deepest, that kicking is quite difficult. I can get off 1 in 10 drop goals or crossfield kicks without being tackled first.- EDIT: A few laws are inconsistent, e.g. Knock-ons are given for a chargedown and sometimes I get the line-out throw-in for a ball I kicked out.- A career/manager mode with full seasons, progression and proper transfers. I'd even be happy with a random player generator to add some bulk around the licensed players.- Southern Hemisphere rugby, lower division teams.- Missing tournaments like the Six Nations.- No real graphics options.- No build-a-player option.- If there's a way to name my custom team, I have no idea how to. I've been playing as "My Team 1" for the past 2/3 seasons.- No option to select your kicker.- EDIT: The option to make custom leagues. There's no licensing for an English Premiership league but we could get around that by making it ourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: BIGBEN are a Promoter I admire because they deliver games that I Actually Want to See & they have been behind some of the Greatest Game releases in the last few years too; o Dacar Rally, o AO Tennis 2 (with all its faults),o WRC 8 (an absolute Masterpiece).BUT, they have also been involved in some of the worst games ever released, I'm of course talking about RUGBY 18.THANKFULLY RUGBY 20 is huge leaps ahead of RUGBY 18 and a totally new approach, control system and mechanics lead RUGBY 20 into an unassailable lead over its predecessor.Certainly RUBGY 20 does not appear to offer the perfect rugby experience, but I would argue that this is the direction the gaming community were PLEADING for & it certainly does do a great job of delivering a relatively Realistic RUGBY experience and sets a decent foundation where improvement WILL be needed and hopefully will come.I have already changed this review from Not Recommended To Recommended and back again TWICE!  So I really am on the fence here.o NEW Mechanics – many of which I adore. Lineouts – Scrum – Tactics - Goal Kicking!o Graphics are acceptable; Not much of an improvement over RUGBY 18 TBH, but lots of nice cut-scenes and animations.o Tackling is pretty good in all honesty, I like it a lot (Area for enhancement but AOK as is).o LEAGUE option is OK, I like how you can set a favourite and it auto defaults to it (NICE TOUCH).o Some licensed players are really well recreated.o Some BIG NASTY & Illegal Tackles + resulting Injuries (thank goodness!).o MY TEAM (Almost Career) - Similar to FIFA's UT, but without the micro-transaction BS.o Gameplay I have had a game that was REALLY fun to play!  So sometimes it all works (which is why I say it has the potential).o Commentary - limited & stuttery but OK.o I think I counted 10 stadiums, they're OK.o Tutorials are ESSENTIAL in this game and what's there is good (some missing see below).o League Mode - start from French Div 3 get promoted through the divisions.o Challenges are NOT what they sound like (They are in-game weekly challenges) I was kind of expecting scenarios.o Passing is SLOW & Laborious. Passes happen Really late.o Slow gameplay, tackling seems a fast paced affair, but running, kicking and passing all seems too slow.o Licensing - if there is Modding then OK this can be bypassed, but without it, it is a problem. o No Single player career.o Online MP just doesn't seem to work.  I find a player, then sit waiting for that player endlessly...to do what? You already said player found?o Audio - Just quite poor and audio is SO Important to immersion.o Missing Tutorials.  Tackling (when the circle around your feet appears) Kick-off.Look this is a £30 game & for that sort of money I expect to be able to play happily for a long time & I am not sure this game is ready to deliver that.  Jonah Lomu Rugby was a game I played with my brothers over and over and over again, and if we had the chance we would probably play it today too, but this is NOT that game, it is nothing like that game.I am glad that the game has received WAY MORE Depth & revised motion capture animations do make the game feel more authentic.  Where this game REALLY delivers is on the Tactics & Set-Plays, `some` of the Mechanics (Tackling, Goal Kicking, lineouts etc..). Sadly it lacks in the most important areas (Passing, Player Movements, Responsiveness, AI Intelligence), it evens says in the trailer you can pass before or after tackle contact (but not during & this IS another problem).The issues in this game are not issues that cannot be resolved, a few tweaks to the arrangement of the algorithm & passes will be enacted when the player calls for them (not a second or two later) and the AI is something that will always be under constant scrutiny and tweaking.It's probably the BEST Rugby UNION game available, ATM, but I wouldn't say it was the best Rugby game available ATM.For me...Right now I do JUST about recommend this game...No I don't...Honestly I am RIGHT ON The FENCE!With a FEW Tweaks and IMPROVEMENTS I do recommend this game...but it needs tweaking.In all honesty I should NOT recommend the game, until these improvements have arrived, but I am so close to giving this a thumbs up!The issues will annoy me too much, BUT I think (hope) they will be improved??? This has the potential to be a great RUGBY game & I really hope they will improve the game.  I will keep my eye on this one, and see what Patches updates and improvements they offer up in the next few months.
_childDocuments_.name: RUGBY 20

_childDocuments_.review: Huge strides forward from Rugby 18, and more tactical gameplay on the field than Rugby Challenge 3, but suffers from clunky player movement, suspect AI, and the lack of an in-depth franchise mode (one of my favorite aspects of sports games). Look, it's not FIFA, but it's fun enough to play and worth $30 or so if you're a rugby fan. The My Squad mode gives you something fun to work towards.I'd recommend giving it a shot. It's meant to be played realistically, so be sparing with the sprint button, earn the right to go wide with crash-ball forward play, and my god, do more than just pass left, left, left, get tackled, then pass right, right, right. Use all the new tactical options at your disposal--it's the biggest selling point of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Before i start know that i have lived and breathed rugby for 30 years, i know more than enough to give a verdict on this game so here goes...GRAPHICS  6/10Not great, could and prob should be a lot better than they are in 2020 for a £31 gameANIMATIONS 5/10just watch a replay of a player sprinting down the wing, the movements are laughable and poorly implementedDIFFICULTY  3/10This is where the game falls flat on its face, you have 3 levels...amateur, semi pro and pro.  With amateur and semi pro you can easily win every ruck and force turn over after turn over, with pro you will struggle to make one turnover per match, not that this makes the game hard..it doesn't.  The game is easy even at pro level, i have yet to lose a single game in my first 3 seasons and i'm no games wizard.A.I,  4/10The A.I. will constantly trunk the ball up thru the middle of the park and only rarely throw it wide, this just makes it easy to knock em back time and time again.  On the rare occasion they do throw it wide it feels a lot better but like i said its a rare occasion, 90% of the time they are as dumb as rocks.FEATURES 6/10The modes of play are not too bad, you have various leagues and nations, i did not expect a full license so im ok with certain teams and players missing.  What im not ok with is the solo mode where you create a team with card style players and run them thru a season.  Whats the first thing you do when you create your own team?  That's right you give them a cool name, but wait!  in this game your team name is called "myteam1"  and you have no control to rename it .... ARE THEY ♥♥♥ SERIOUS!   Why in gods name would they think that this is ok!  how detached from reality are the developers to think that a simple omission like this is acceptable, it may not appear to be a massive deal but it is, i'm lost for words at the total stupidity on display here...just wow!BOTTOM LINEAfter 17 hrs i am totally bored of this game, it presents zero challenge to keep me engaged and playing, i have gone thru 3 seasons unbeaten with "myteam1"  sigh!  who are rated 68, along the way i have easily beaten teams rated up to 82 all on pro difficulty, the AI are predictable and clueless and rarely pose a threat.   For a game that costs £31 this is not even close to being value for money, its fun for 10 mins the you start seeing all the cracks, The devs do not respond to comments and suggestions, gone are the days when developers had pride in their products, this has been dumped on steam and left to rot.  Do yourself a favour, keep your money and kick this into touch.Update:  Devs dropped an update out of the blue, poor communication still,  this update does go some way to making this game better BUT STILL NO WAY TO NAME YOUR TEAM, so annoying.   The AI will now offload more which makes them more dangerous and therefore more interesting, the game though is still too easy at pro level, only the very best teams will give you a good game...i'm still yet to lose a game, this gets boring!Getting better but still some way to go imo.  I really want to recommend this but i have to be honest, for the price its not quite where it should be, really hope they keep improving it.Update 2My final match on this poor game saw me run out 117-0 winners.  The A.I. are possibly the worst of any game i have ever played, oh and forget multiplayer because no one plays the game, if you do have a mate to play with you will experience chronic rubber banding issues that just sour the whole experience, as if its not bad enough already!  Zero updates forth coming and covid -19 is no excuse because plenty of devs are still working on games.  Rugby 20 is a con of a game that should be removed from steam...DO NOT BUY!

_childDocuments_.review: So, after about 16 hours in Rugby 18 and a few in this one, I think I can review this pretty objectively as I know what my expectations were. If you're not, it's a high red flagged NO.I want to start by saying that the only reason someone would buy or recommend this game is that they're a huge fan of the sport and, driven by melancholy, they still miss the good old Rugby 08 days and search for modern alternatives and rosters as updated as possible. As we all know, this rugby games market is not that great overall and we have a very specific and narrow list of games to chose from. Some better than others. This is clearly better than others, so this is why I'll recommend it. I really want to believe that at some point the Rugby games by Eko would be the new 'gold standard' of Rugby games, as there is a lot of potential. However, at this point, while there is are some great improvements compared to Rugby 18 (and also some downgrades, which we'll discuss at the cons), it's still hard to recommend this game (especially at the price tag it's got). This is, unfortunately, where the pros kind of stop...This would be a dream if it was more mod friendly. I, personally, could've gotten over the clunkiness of the game, over the AI and all that, as I know what the expectations should be for a rugby game, if it would at least let you do your own stuff. I'd highly recommend for future releases that at least a edit national squads option to be implemented, so you can select which people you'd want in your national squad, as a workaround for licensing. _childDocuments_.review: Bit buggy at launch, but with the new updates being released in the public development beta earlier this week, this is becoming a brilliant rugby game! I feel that this game gets an unfair amount of criticism. Some of the reviews I've read don't appear to have explored the game fully, complaining about features not being there which are present or comparisons to the likes of FIFA football games. A series that have DECADES of development behind them and 1000x the budget. Played mostly on "semi pro" difficultyPositives - Large selection of licensed teams to choose from - play through top leagues with your favourite team- "My team" lets you create your own team from the players you have collected from booster packs. You can then play and manage your created team to success in Solo mode- Kicking system is brilliant- Lineout system is great- Scrum system is good, intuitive enough not to just be mashing buttons and not so labourious it slows the game down too much - Tutorials are good, but without the beta they lacked a control list (this has been added in the beta, thank you!)Notable Features improved in the beta - rucks which were previously too easy are now much more competitive, more difficult to turn over the opposite team allowing the AI to string more phases in attack- AI are much smarter in attack, making for some interesting moments defending cross field kicks, pick and go's and set plays - yellow cards are reduced, game flows alot better. - Control list in pause menu! (I'd previously been scoring trys by purposefully getting tackled over the line!)All the beta updates are detailed in the patch notes but I thought I'd note down the main ones Multiplayer- haven't tried it yet, may update when I do Minor issues - licences for some international teams and SH competitions are not available. This is understandable, licenses are very expensive - player models are a mixed bag, I suspect this is linked to licenses(player likeness) and/or development cost- Team/Player Rating system is off, the DEVS HAVE ADDRESSED THIS and are looking into it. This is due to their suppliers' system. Rugby fans who know of a certain supplier's database will probably agree that it's not accurate at all. - occasional odd bug where the controls will lock up after a scrum, player will make a tackle from 20 meters away, minor things that can be patched All in all, until the beta release I was on the fence about recommending this game. But with the fixes they're bringing through, this game is brilliant to play now and shows that the Devs are dedicated to bringing the game up to the standard fans are asking for. I'd probably say this is the best rugby game.you can buy right now

_childDocuments_.review: General consensus is that if you want to play a half decent rugby game prior to the release of Rugby 20, you needed to play games that are ten years old or so. No. Licences are missing with no ability to edit your own teams (which would inevitably let you add people in). Half of the mechanics in the game are not intuitive and the tutorial does a poor job of letting you know exactly how they work. On Semi-Pro difficulty, your entire team are turnover kings, easily winning rucks from the opposition. That all being said, it does have more licences than PES ever had when it was first released, and some of the mechanics are really good. I've played this for two hours so far, a couple of times as my preferred teams and a couple of times as "MyTeam" which I'm sure I'd enjoy more if I actually understood how it all worked.Fifa 2020 is about £45, and this game is £30. It needs improvements for sure, but I think really for £30 if you're a rugby fan you should get this game. If you have no idea about how to play rugby and have just been interested, or you like sports team management sims, do not buy this game. It will either not explain literally anything to you including the rules of the game, or will not include the depth you want to see.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best rugby game available, with the worst tutorial ;) They just didn't explain how to attack.  You can adjust tactics in the menu though, and here's a quick primer:Start with "Classic" mode.  This is old school rugby where the skillful backs attack, and the big forwards stay out of the way.  If you played some schools rugby, or just played a while back (like me), this is what you're used to!  Tapping RS will do a side step and a long press a hand off.Then try a 2-4-2.  This means the big forwards do most of the early ball carrying.  2 are on one wing, 2 on the other with 4 in the middle.  Focus on using the group of four in the middle to get the ball moving upfield for a few phases, before spreading it wide.  For set plays, try giving your line more depth so you have more time to execute.1-3-3-1.  This is the hardest and unfortunately the default for a lot of teams.  Now you have 2 groups of 3 forwards to use in the middle of the field.  You can play the ball much faster b/c there is always a second pod available.  Once you've played a few phases, look for smaller backs hanging out behind the forwards.  Try passing the ball straight backwards to them by hitting both pass buttons before spreading the ball wide.  Pass chain 1-3-3-1, type B with diamond pod shapes works well.With the recent patches the game plays really well.  Still a few rough edges for sure and you'll want to turn the commentary off.Bottom line if you love rugby or want to learn the game, pick this up.
