_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'll start this review by saying it is FAAAAAR from perfect. The commentary is just awful, not necessarily in terms of what they're saying, but the TONE in which they say it really is not convincing. Not only that but the timing is terrible, they'll call players by the wrong names, get the teams mixed up, get the amount of penalties in a game wrong...for example earlier the commentators said it was my "51st attempt at goal"...I don't think there's been a rugby match in existence that has had even half that amount. The commentators will say something when the entirely opposite thing is occurring, like "they've kicked the ball for possession behind the enemy line" when in reality I've booted the ball a mile out of the stadium because I want to end the half. Or, "he's definitely going to score here!" when I'm about 10 meters out with 3 players on top of the guy with the ball. Or, when missing a sideline conversion because it bounces off of the posts, the commentators say "he really should be getting those, that's a really basic kick"....uhhh is it? It just really ruins the ambience of the entire thing. However, you'd think it's something that would be relatively easy to sort out...right? So why haven't they done it yet? At least it's not like Rugby Challenge where I feel like they've gotten the entire mechanics for the players wrong. The mechanics....I'm not sure if I'm even using this word correctly, but the mechanics for this game are in my opinion....quite good. If you compare (which I am going to quite a lot) to the Rugby Challenge 'series' (said sarcastically because they're all basically the same game) the movement of the players and the way in which they pass the ball is somewhat satisfying and fluent, sure, it's not perfect, but it's way better than anything I've witnessed in the past 10 years of rugby games. The ONE THING that REALLY BUGS ME however, which is something that truly annoyed me in Rugby Challenge and I don't know why they seem to have done the same here, is the motion/way that they score tries. It's like...you've pressed 'A' to score, and then they take about 3 seconds to actually put it down, meanwhile they're doing some stupid Ashton-esque dive into the air (BTW DEVELOPERS LIKE 10% OF RUGBY PLAYERS WILL ACTUALLY ATTEMPT A SWAN DIVE OVER THE TRY LINE). It's not needed, just put the damn ball down, take a note out of Rugby 08, look at the ways in which they score, look how fluent it is, it's SATISFYING to score tries in Rugby 08 because they just put the ball down straight away and players behind them in motion don't catch up with the try scorer (which just looks utterly stupid) before he's actually put the ball down. However, this game above all its flaws, is fun. The lineouts are done really well, the scrummaging is good enough, the set piece and rucks are good in general I think. Something key for me, which Rugby Challenge failed to do, was giving the player the ability to build phases and not just whip it wide every time, because in this game it won't work. You genuinely have to build phases to suck the defence in, and it feels great when you've been knocking on the opposition try line phase after phase for you to finally sneak your winger in at the corner, it's satisfying. Another thing done really well for me is the kicking, both the restarts and kicking at goal feel relatively realistic, when you nail a touch line conversion, you feel as though you've earned those 2 points, whereas in other games (YEAH MAINLY RUGBY CHALLENGE), you could just bop over a touch line conversion as easily as you could in front of the posts. I've written enough and to summarise, I would recommend this game, mainly because I got it on ♥♥♥ for £16, mixed with the fact that it is a lot of fun AND MAINLY (I CANNOT STRESS THIS ENOUGH) THE DEVS ARE STILL BRINGING OUT UPDATES AND TAKING IN FEEDBACK AND CONTINUOUSLY BRINGING OUT PATCHES TO IMPROVE THE GAME.6/10 no where near perfect BUT....it has the potential to be the best rugby game in the past 10 years.

I win against the throw more often than not on the hardest difficulty.It's also really easy to win scrums against the head on proKicking a ball that's already on the ground works like 10% of the times, mashing the button, pressing it right when the prompt comes up, doesn't matter, it almost never works.Crashes a decent amountNo rolling mauls, just button mashing games that almost always result in the same yardage gainIf you play aerial ping pong, eventually the opp team fullback or wing or whoever received your kick will just kick it out on the full even if they're not behind the 22, or otherwise kick a big lateral kick to a teammate that you can just wait on and get a turnover in the ruck.Rucks are pretty good though. name: Subnautica: Below Zero
detailed_description: Below Zero is an underwater adventure game set on an alien ocean world. It is the next chapter in the Subnautica universe and is developed by Unknown Worlds. Return to planet 4546B Submerge yourself in an all-new, sub-zero expedition in an arctic region of Planet 4546B. Arriving with little more than your wits and some survival equipment, you set out to investigate what happened to your sister... Uncover the truth Alterra left in a hurry after a mysterious incident. Abandoned research stations dot the region. What happened to the scientists who lived and worked here? Logs, items, and databanks scattered among the debris paint a new picture of the incident. With limited resources, you must improvise to survive on your own. Discover uncharted biomes Swim beneath the blue-lit, arching expanses of Twisty Bridges. Become mesmerized by the glittering, mammoth crystals of the Crystal Caverns. Clamber up snow covered peaks and venture into the icy caves of Glacial Basin. Maneuver between erupting Thermal Vents to discover ancient alien artifacts. Below Zero presents entirely new environments for you to survive, study, and explore. Construct habitats and vehicles Survive the harsh climate by constructing extensive habitats, scavenging for resources, and crafting equipment. Blast across the snowy tundra on a Snowfox hoverbike. Cruise through enchanting and perilous biomes in your modular Seatruck. Research alien lifeforms Something undiscovered lurks around every corner. Swim through the giant Titan Holefish, encounter the haunting Shadow Leviathan, and visit the adorable Pengwings. Keep your wits about you. Not all creatures in this strange world are friendly. Survive the chilly temperatures Jump in, the water’s warm. The below zero temperatures of this arctic region pose a new threat. New weather conditions blanket above-ground habitats. Craft a toasty cold suit, sip on piping hot coffee, and warm up next to Thermal Lilies to stave off the chill. An ocean of intrigue What really happened to your sister? Who were the aliens who came here before? Why were they on this planet? Can we find solace from grief in truth? Below Zero extends the story of the Subnautica universe, diving deep into the mystery introduced in the original game. About the development team Below Zero is created by Unknown Worlds, a small studio that traces its roots back to the 2002 Half-Life mod Natural Selection. It is the same studio that created the original Subnautica. The team is scattered around the globe, from the United States to the United Kingdom, France, Russia, Austria, Australia, Canada, and many more places. Warning This game contains flashing lights that may make it unsuitable for people with photosensitive epilepsy or other photosensitive conditions. Player discretion is advised.

_childDocuments_.review: Below Zero is a good follow up to the original subnautica and it has more emphasis on story than surviving, with the huge allocation of resources to PDA logs and voice acting which is done very well. The biomes are great and fit the aesthetic of 4546B nicely and really immerses you in the world. Many improvements and quality of life changes have been added since the prequel, but there are some bugs that are annoying and can break the immersion at times. My main gripe is that compared to the original the map is much smaller and it makes the game way shorter, with a play time of 28 hours to finish the game compared to the 45 hours i needed to do so at a casual speed. And despite the biomes being pretty well made, they start feeling quite small after a few visits. The danger in the game is significantly reduced as you're more likely to die from thirst or drowning rather than being attacked by sea monsters. Leviathans are much weaker compared to the first game, dealing little damage to your seatruck while playing a flashy animation of your vehicle getting chewed up. The prawnsuit has been nerfed and is significantly less tanky which is a good thing. Your ability to quickly repair your vehicles further trivialises these sea monsters as after a while you realise they're not a huge threat. And after you acquire the defense perimeter upgrade you will pretty much never be in danger. TLDR; below zero is a decent expansion instead of a full fledged game. Not enough danger in general, could be a bit denser content wise. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to cry.I loved the first Subnautica.  It was the ocean exploration game I'd always dreamed of.  The creatures were beautiful in sound and in design.  The story unfolded through your exploration.  The world felt so big and alive.  It was an immersive (lol) experience near perfection, especially for an aquatic science nerd like me.Then they decided to make Below Zero.  And somehow - either through incompetence or spite, because there's no way this was done through ignorance - they took everything that people loved and replaced it with the parts that people hated.Namely, the biggest change: instead of exploration driving the story, story drives the exploration.  This sounds great on paper, but is terrible in execution.  Mainly because the game utilizes Forspoken-style dialogue long before Forspoken made it noticeable.  You know the reveal in Subnautica when ?  How the player is given that much information and then gives them time to realize the situation?  If it were this game's writers,   That's the game.   don't get to decide how you feel about the situation you are in.  The game will tell you what you need to feel.  It will tell you where to go next.  And it will rip you out of your immersion every time.  Creature design is a step down.  They don't look or act like beings adapted to their environment, as the critters in the first game did.  They look and act like beings adapted to be in a videogame.  The predators have looks and sounds that demand the audience be scared of them.  Its the same effect as a man in costume chasing you in a haunted house screaming "OOGA BOOGA BOOGA."  The Leviathans don't deliver the same awe or terror as the ones in the first game; again, the designs try to hard to be spooky.  Honestly, the only design I encountered that I liked were the sea monkeys.  And even then, they're overanimated to the point of parody.  The only thing this game did better than the first was base building options.  You can build a huge underwater house with rooms, rather than a bunch of circular modules.  These options lead to a much more homier base that looks more refined.  But they added a lot of that back to Subnautica, so there is really absolutely no reason to get this game.If I sound unusually harsh, its because this is a franchise I care about.  I bought this game day one of Early Access.  I remember when Robin was a researcher sending samples to her sister Sam up on a satellite , and when  was a prick who warmed up to life .  It was cozy and a great base line for an unfolding story set in a growing frozen world.  It was all about research and exploration, just like what I wanted.  And they THREW IT ALL OUT THE WINDOW BECAUSE I DONT KNOW.  I genuinely do NOT know what they were going for.  And the final result is such an obnoxious, hand-holdy, unimmersive experience.Here's hoping the true Subnautica 2 will be a return to form.  I shudder to think of the result if they decide to do the whole "throw out the parts people liked and buckle down on what they didnt" cycle again.

_childDocuments_.review: "Not being as good as the first doesn't make it NOT one of the best survival games out there."--STORY--4/5 - Great!-Doesn't overstay it's welcome, relatively well-written and robin as a protagonist is really easy to like and has a lot of personality even if we can't see her face. Doesn't interfere with the game-play at all and builds a lot on-top of subnautica's pre-existing world building. Isn't especially grand or spectacular or emotionally moving or anything like that but it doesn't need to be.--Gameplay--4/5 - StellarFirst, the bad. Sometimes the Environment is a bit buggy and the leviathan AI aren't nearly as intimidating as the first game, minus the Shadow Leviathans which sorta haunt me, however, this gameplay overall feels much more refined than the first, despite losing a lot of the fear factor that made the original a living nightmare. Satisfying gameplay loop, feels excellent to scan everything and discover new locations, and it's honestly peak survival game, there's not one element or system i can nitpick, besides the tedious land segments which admittedly are cool but need more fleshing out, still, wonderful time all around.-- Sound and Music --5/5 - PerfectHits the same highs that the original hits, in every way too. Every sound is memorable, and the voice cast here especially is excellent, in my opinion it's a huge step up from most of the life-pod voicelines, which by themselves were also just as good. The ambience of this game rivals but some of the kings of ambience in horror games, and really keeps you on your feet, the music as rare as it can be is very memorable and fits the vibe especially, and honestly it's just perfect. Everything sounds like it wants to kill me and i LOVE it.I could go on for a bit more, but honestly, just play the game for yourself. If you want more underwater nightmares, just play the first, but if you love that game and ocean survival as a genre, it doesn't get much better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler freeAn amazing "Wtf was that noise" simulator. Just like the first game.First and foremost, if you are reading this and you loved Subnautica, then you will love Subnautica Below Zero. I've seen some negativity saying this game "stripped the spirit" of the original Subnautica by adding/removing the features listed below (Like traversing land or having a smaller world). This is false. The spirit of the first game is not only intact, but it's even stronger due to some of the changes made. Differences listed below:Differences:+ Much bigger focus on the narrative, with actual characters to learn about and cooperate with. This doesn't change the core of the game, which is basically swim around discovering things at your own leisure in whatever direction or fashion you decide to do it in, just like the first game. You slowly uncover what happened/is happening as you progress. Each new area presents new dangers which you will have to find ways to equip yourself for.+ The new characters are great, especially Robin, our Protagonist. She is witty and isn't afraid to ask hard questions even if her life is in direct danger. + Solid voice acting all around. Their personalities are brought to life as you learn about them and maybe even what happened to them.+ The soundtrack is still great.+ New Items+ New Enemies+ There are landmasses to traverse in this one and specific items utilized for these landmasses+ This game is longer than the first (First being ~20 hours. This one being ~25-30 hours depending on your playstyle).+/- I honestly don't remember if the world itself is smaller than the first game, but it doesn't even matter. There is still a big rich and deep world out there with more content than the first game, and you will love it all the same. Quality > Quantity in this instance.+/- The Cyclops is gone. If that is the game breaker for you, as I see in so many reviews on here (and wow), then yeah, you can dodge this game. It's been replaced with the Seatruck which has overall better utilization since you can attach/detach the components you want or need.The rest is mostly identical. Solid gameplay with smooth optimization and plenty of (new) fish to run away from.If you are still reading by this point, then do yourself a favor and PLAY SUBNAUTICA FIRST, then come play this game. Both are absolutely fantastic experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: Game version: 49371Total game duration: 15hPercentage of game completed: 100%Subnautica: Original laid the foundations, Subnautica: Below Zero confirms the know-how !Up until now, I'd never managed to get 100% into the game, due to a lack of interest. But after finishing the first opus, I decided to start a new game. I was expecting a lot from this second opus after a more than successful Subnautica: Original, so I was expecting an improved game with some nice new features. In my opinion, this game is a success, despite a few imperfections. So here's my review of Subnautica: Below Zero.Graphically, the game has taken a huge step up from its predecessor. The game's detail is truly impressive. In the first opus, the different biomes had identities that could appear empty or even redundant, apart from a few magnificent biomes (the deep biomes). In this opus, the biomes are unique and give off a different, powerful energy. I really enjoyed discovering some beautifully crafted visuals. It's one of the game's strong points, not to mention the soundtrack, which puts the icing on the cake! It was a real pleasure to wander around, both visually and audibly.The second strong point of this game is the story behind this second opus. Here too, the game has reached a new level. The main character is accompanied for 95% of the adventure, adding interaction and a more human side to the story. Half the story revolves around the main character, bringing us back to the world of the architects we met in the first game. You'll be led to discover architects' sites distributed across the game's map. The second part of the story revolves around a member of the main character's family, and takes you to Alterra's various bases around the planet. The story is much more complete and interesting to follow in this game. I really enjoyed following the different tracks and discovering this universe.The open-world aspect of the game is also a success, with resources that are much easier to find and identify, each rock can be used to obtain a mineral if you're lucky. It's easy enough to get the right elements to be able to go deeper into the ocean of subnautica, but also to go further into the land/glacier of the game. The terrestrial part is much more present than in the previous game, and is a real plus. The only weak point I'm going to highlight here is the transport section. In the first game there were 3 vehicles, the first very maneuverable and fast, the second huge but very slow and the third with legs and very interesting for progression. In this opus, there are 3 vehicles : the first is modular, rather slow despite the improvements, and not very maneuverable; the second has legs and is of no interest in my savegame and the third is only for the land section. We've gone from 3 different vehicles with impacts on evolution in the game to 3 vehicles, 1 of which has no impact on evolution and 1 that can be avoided. Admittedly, the map is smaller in area and the biomes are narrower, making them less accessible for larger vehicles, but I do miss the cyclops and the freedom to build within it.This game remains a success, and congratulations to the studio for this second opus. The third is already in the pipeline and will be released in UE5, so we can't wait to discover a world that's even more visually appealing and more advanced in terms of story scripting!

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me say if you have not played the first one, stop reading, go play it now, thank me later.   Really go do it now, even at full price.  It's a masterpiece! Go now!I really, really wish i could say the same for the 2nd one. It just doesn't capture the magic from the first game.  The "water surface to sea floor" areas are much smaller and less variety.   Everything feels the same no matter where you're at.  The first game had very distinct sections which made for cool exploration and helpful navigation.    The "below the seafloor" area is terrible.  Hands down, terrible.  Cramped, confusing, mazes.  The first one had beautiful tunnels and caves to explore.  I can only remember twice in this game where i came upon something underground and just went "wow"!  The first game i felt like i was doing that around every corner i turned down there.The land areas were also terrible. You've developed a game about underwater game play and for some reason put a large land area in it.   It was not fun AT ALL.  Moving around the land always felt like a chore.  The bike vehicle was clunky and hard to maneuver.  Also the penguin bots felt like a bad mini game.   I hate to have to look something up about a game, but there was nothing intuitive about using the penguin bot to collect a very needed material nor did it make any sense.Base design/options were on par with the first one.  Have to say i really enjoyed the hand held scanner and would have liked to have seen some upgrades for it to improve it.    Vehicles though, you let me down.  Sea truck was a cool idea but only one of the compartments was actually needed.  Overall, again buy the first one even at full price.  Buy the second one on sale and you have nothing else to play.  Unknown worlds i really, really, REALLY hope that you do better if you make a 3rd one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first Subnautica, you're probably going to enjoy this sequel. But keep in mind that it is different. It has a voiced protagonist, a distinct story-line, and a smaller map. For me, none of that took away from the experience, but I understand how that might impact other players. I've been playing in Early Access for months and ran through the game from start to finish since yesterday's official release. I'm happy that I bought and played the game, and I think it was worth my money. Lots of quality of life improvements, better base building, interesting and beautiful biomes, new creatures to make scary noises from a distance. More "deep" biomes which I really like. Diving and finding there's a whole separate biome below you is really cool. The only issue with the game isn't an issue with the /game/. Don't go into the Steam forums unless you want to read a bunch of whiny pissbabies talking about how having a black woman as the protagonist ruins their immersion, or if you think the mention of gay people means the devs have "sold out to the woke sjws" or whatever the hell is today's conspiracy.  I can't believe the gaming community is still at the point where so much as mentioning minorities gets people in a fricken tizzy. That's my review: Buy the game and try it out if you loved Subnautica.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica: Below Zero is a good game. While in early access, improved controls, game-play mechanics and vehicles help turn the experience of exploring 4546B into a smooth and enjoyable one. It's story is linear when compared to Subnautica's and doesn't tie all of its sub-plots together nearly as well. The map is smaller, both horizontally and vertically, with about 1/2 being unexplorable due to ice and the max depth stopped at 1100 meters. Why did I recommend the game then when I have so many critiques? Because Subnautica is a beloved game. It was unique and incredible! Lots of people look forward to the game's official release and they should know what they're getting into. That being said, if you go into this game with the right expectations you'll have a blast. Rather than the mysterious horror which permeated the first installment in the series, Below Zero is meant to be more light-hearted, adventurous and funny while still remaining bits of mystery and suspense. Simply put, don't go into this as seriously as the first game! The biomes are beautiful, many more so than the first game! Bases are way more customizable and efficient and there's a wide cast of characters. It will be fun, just love it for what it is!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is disappointing. Not because of what it is, but because of what it could have been.What this game is, is the original Subnautica with a couple of slight tweaks and a completely superfluous land-based portion bolted on.This land-based portion was an incredible missed opportunity: In theory it should have added another fun aspect to the game, one that builds on and compliments the existing excellent gameplay loop of exploring deeper underwater to gain better equipment to explore even deeper. One could have ventured out onto the surface to gather resources to craft gear to venture further afield. Yet, instead, exploring the surface world is unchallenging and tedious. Unlike the underwater portions of this game and its predecessor, with their lush, interesting environments populated by varied flora and fauna, we instead explore a small, blank, boring wilderness in which there is virtually nothing to do. The only exception to this monotony is the Glacial Forest and Excavation Site, which were both pretty cool.Nevertheless, the two new game mechanics introduced for surface exploration, Spy Penglings and the Snowfox, are incredibly underdeveloped; the former merely provides a cumbersome method for accessing resources, all but one of which can be far more easily acquired elsewhere (and the exception merely provides a slight and unnecessary boost to surface exploration), and the later had the potential to be a really fun mode of transport, but ended up merely a clunky way of expanding surface range.There were some great ideas here, but it feels like they weren't properly implemented, most probably due to budgetary constraints. The surface portions of the game needed to be far bigger, far prettier and far more challenging. There needed to be unique resources only accessible via Spy Pengling, jumps to make the Snowfox fun and abandoned surface bases that can be restored using surface-only resources to recharge the Snowfox and thus expand the surface exploration range. The constant warnings of extreme weather needed dire consequences if ignored.Finally, whilst the original Subnautica had a couple of excusable rough edges towards the end, Below Zero should have learned from this. Instead, one of the final moments of the game is spent blindly bumping around an incredibly confusing cave, trying to find a tiny hidden entrance whilst being constantly harassed by leviathans. Not fun!So when I say this game is 'disappointing', it's because it doesn't live up to its potential. It could have been so much more! And yet... I still recommend it. The parts that are copy-pasted from the original, the parts where you're all alone in the darkness, way out of your depth, you're exploring some enchanting new biome and the music swells... that's when it all comes together.To put it another way; when this game is good, it's copying Subnautica's homework. If you're new to the series, play the original first. If, like me, you already know and love the original, then at its best Below Zero is more of that, just with some less fun bits tacked on that have to endured.The story and soundtrack are both excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: A good, but perhaps not great, continuation of the Subnautica game. Once more the aquatic map offers variety in biomes and new enemies, although this time I just didn't feel as enchanted as with the original. This could be down to the simple fact I had high expectations and the novelty isn't there a second time around, but I did feel the 'route' of the story wasn't as flexible as with the original game. I ended up doing a lot of things in the 'wrong' order, and the narrative didn't adapt as well until I found myself on the 'right path'. The time between resulted in a lot of wandering and backtracking, without it necessarily being the enjoyable exploration I felt in the previous instalment. I'm not sure the map is precisely the same area, but the world felt smaller, or at least, less interesting to explore. The overland ice areas in particular, did not fill me with wonder like the Grand Reef or Blood Kelp biomes had before. If I had one actual complaint it would be the damn vehicle for traversing the ice, it was useless with horrible controls. A smaller issue is again, the PRAWN suit is just superior in every way to other modes of transport, it really needed a downside to balance it out.However, this is more Subnautica at its core, one of the best video games out, and that itself will give you your money's worth. _childDocuments_.review: Ah, Subnautica. The best survival game I have ever played and definitely one of the best games I've ever played. Playing through that game was an absolute joy, heavily bolstered by its open-endedness, sheer terror, and the oddly compelling, dangerous curiousity to swim even deeper, and deeper, and deeper into the abyss than ever before. The brightest moment of that game for me was, ironically, exploring the deepest, darkest parts of the map, expertly crafted by Unknown Worlds, all by myself. The isolation was the cornerstone of Subnautica. It's part of what makes it so freaking good. I struggled to go even deeper than even 50m for the first 10 hours because of the sheer terror I felt exploring, but I forced myself to do it anyways because it's just so much fun.I have nothing but fond memories from the original Subnautica. I still play it to this day. Very few games have the honor to be replayed by me regularly. And even fewer games have mastered the feeling that the fear of the oceans gives you, the fear of the unknown.So, you would think that the sequel to such a well-beloved game would be just as good, if not better, right?Well, you thought wrong. Subnautica: Below Zero is nowhere as bright as the shining star that was the original Subnautica.What's the quote again? "Wide as an ocean, but deep as a puddle"?The world is about 1/5th the size of the original's world. So, with that in mind, you would expect for Below Zero's world to go even deeper than the original, and be the exact opposite of that quote?Small as a puddle, but deep as an ocean. Ha, you would think, right?Below Zero's world is as wide as a puddle and shallow as one. The world doesn't get very deep at all compared to the original Subnautica. and there's not anywhere near as many places to dive in. There's not very much underwater biome variety as well. In fact, about a 1/3 of the world is covered up with walkable terrain. And guess what? The walking is awful. Everywhere you walk, even in your bases above and below the sea, being stuck on a random object isn't an uncommon ocurrence. A massive shame such a large portion of an underwater survival game is spent exploring above the sea level, and you can't even have a bug-free time doing so, eh?Speaking of going underwater, Below Zero is nowhere near as scary as the original. The devs just brightened everything, took away all the cool leviathans from the first game and replaced them with gimmicky creatures and plants designed to piss you off (cough cough Sea Monkey) or make the game boring as crap (oxygen bubble plants. the inclusion of these actually takes away all incentive to use vehicles.).All that brilliantly paced tension: Gone. A major tool for Subnautica's succes: Gone.Below Zero has a prewritten, voiced protagonist, a woman named Robin, as well, but the story is very poorly written, illogical, and very handholdy to the point where it makes Mass Effect Andromeda's story look enticing, taking away one of the best aspects of the original: The freedom to do whatever you want, to go wherever you want, whenever you want as whoever you wish to be. The original Subnautica also had a prewritten protagonist as well (a man named Riley, I believe), but that protagonist was silent, so it makes the game even more impressionable as you become more and more immersed in the world. You start playing as Riley, but by the end of the game, you are playing as yourself. A quick explanation of what I mean:The original Subnautica was about your personal journey. Your adventures. Every action you take is your own. Below Zero is about Robin's journey, not yours. It can't even tell Robin's story well, unfortunately. Robin's story is entirely made from her and her sister's negligence, how the hell is that compelling, Unknown Worlds?And now, the soundtrack. The soundtrack of Subnautica has morphed, from tense, but futuristic electronic music, absolutely dripping with atmosphere with every sound, every note. A perfect blend between technologically mystifying ocean exploration and bone chilling horror.Simon Chylinski knew what he was doing, man. (I'll post links for both Subnautica and Below Zero for comparison.) ..to generic underwater exploration music that sounds like something from Spore. The new composer, Ben Prunty thought a national geographic album would be more appropiate.A travesty, really. So, because of these shortcomings (and more I haven't mentioned), Below Zero absolutely destroys every aspect that made the original game so compelling:To see what's beyond the murky, pitch black depths.To go where no man has gone before.To recognize and overcome the primal terror of looking directly at the abyss and having it staring back at you with malicious intent.To explore an alien world as if you personally inhabited it yourself, as if you were the protagonist.That was what the original Subnautica stood for. That was what made it so successful in the first place.So, why the sudden change in direction for the series after such a massive success?Look at Unknown Worlds, what do the devs have to say about this?UW actually fired the OG Subnautica's composer and sound director, Simon Chylinski, (which explains why the sound design is this game is so bland) over making a mild joke about an Attack Helicopter (shortly before Subnautica's release, I believe.)I've also noticed that during the early access period for Below Zero, the story was remade about 6-8 times. The game was fundementally changed several times throughout the early access period. The original voice actor for Robin was changed as well.I've never, ever seen any early access game pull changes that drastically in my 15+ years of gaming, so that leaves me a few questions:Did Unknown Worlds have any sort of solid plan for Below Zero? Was there any sort of infighting going on between the dev team at Unknown Worlds?Why were they having such a hard time deciding on one idea and sticking with it?I sense  (gestures directly towards Unknown Worlds) is having a Bioware moment and throwing away all sorts of talent foolishly and trying to recapture lightning in a bottle without the capabilities to do so.Because of these actions that the devs have been doing a lot as of recently, and because of the bad product they've shipped out as Subnautica: Below Zero, I really can't recommend this game in any good faith.In fact, dare I say, I don't have any faith that Unknown Worlds' next project is going to turn out well. I expect Subnautica 3 to be a disaster.Subnautica: Below Zero, for me, is a 4/10. Below Zero is a major dissappointment for me personally, which really depresses me since I was a massive fan of the original Subnautica. That game changed me, made reconsider what kinds of games I should play.If you want to venture into the wondrous, aquatic alien world of Planet 4546B, I highly recommend playing the original Subnautica and completely ignore Below Zero entirely so you don't soil the memories you get from playing the original.TL;DR: Subpar: Below Average isn't worth your time.Man, this game made me sad. :(

_childDocuments_.review: I simply couldn't stick with Below Zero. After about 12 hours of trying, I gave up and watched a story summary on YouTube to see if I was missing out on anything special (and apparently I wasn't).The OG Subnautica has my wholehearted recommendation, but something about the map and "additions" of this game just didn't do it for me this time around. There's some interesting ideas here, and I would like to say I'd recommend this to anyone who hasn't played the first one... But sadly, some of the gameplay that was introduced (and is required to progress) isn't as solid. There's a lot of time spent out of the water in this one, and those sections are frustrating and tedious as opposed to the more invigorating ocean exploration. On top of this, the narrative (especially the characters) isn't as interesting as the first time around, and a large part of me wishes they had relied on the exquisite environmental storytelling and minimal dialogue of the first game. There's a lot of uninteresting people talking a lot, especially towards the end.I'd love to see the devs try again with this series, but there needs to be some serious additions that focus on fun, a bigger and more interesting map, and a story that doesn't make me roll my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: So is subnautica: below zero a good game? Yes, it is!Would I recommend people to play it? Yes!If I played subnautica before will I still enjoy this? ProbablyIs it better then the original subnautica? NoSo I am just going to line up a few improvements and a few downsides to subnautica: below zero and try to bring accross why I would recommend buying the first game over this one. improvements: Smaller world - I actually didn't like that I had to sit in my seamoth for 7 minutes to get to a different biome in the original game and the smaller world fixes that issue. Even tough the seatruck is a lot slower then the seamoth (we will get to you) the world is easy to travel around in and the smaller scope feels like a vast improvement and reduces time wasted on traveling. The only thing is that it probably caused some of my dissappointments as well. (I am looking at you seatruck and leviathans.)More creatures- the original subnautica always felt a bit empty to me due to an underpopulated world. The new one has a lot of life in area's and some of its creatures are really cool to admire for a bit. They added cool new creatures with new behavior and traits. They also designed a lot of creatures that filled the same exact same role as older creatures which confused me a bit... why not just carry over the old creatures? But I appriciate the effort they went trough and it made the enviroment feel a lot more aliveMore options in basebuilding- you can be more creative with your base, I didn't use it much since I am not playing subnautica for basebuilding but its there for those that do like it.Didn't encounter any glitches- Wierd one to include but the original subnautica felt buggy in places, I clipped trough the world once and I had things opperate in wierd ways. This one didn't have that once.Better resource management- IDK if it was just me being efficient or the game being designed better, but where in the old subnautica I frequently had to go out of my way to find resources that I frequently needed I had basicly no issues in this game. So I am going to give it a  thumbs up for that.The rest is just subnautica being what subnautica is good at: cool setting, underwater movement feels good, creature design is cool.The cons:The seatruck- oh this thing... this is the "seamoth" equivelant in this game... and the cyclops as well. The idea is that you attach modules to expand its uses and gradually make it a great moving base. What this means is that you start with a discount seamoth that just isnt as fast as the original speedster and end up with a discount cyclops that doesn't have the cool looks or storage options as the original and somehow feels slower too. It also robs the game of that good feeling when you finally craft the mighty cyclops or the rocket: this truck is your "best" vehicle and you are stuck with it for the rest of the game unless you move around using the prawn suit. I ended up using one storage module and the prawnsuit carrier, since anything added to it would slow it to a crawl. Definite downgrade to the OG vehicles.The land section- This games main selling point is that there is more land in it. The two trailers on the main page have two land sections take up half the video and I just wonder why... The land sections were never a strong point of subnautica and it hasn't improved much. For starters the land is the only place where you can get effected by the most annoying weather: blizzards. This heavily decreases your sight and is just there to annoy you. And of course you lose the third dimension of exploration which is compensated by making the all the area's look the same and making it one big maze, so you will walk around in circles thinking you are making progress when you actually aren't. On top of that the area only has 3 creatures: a penguen, the bear & the leviathan worm.Area design- The area design in this game is notably worse then in the first game. In the first game there were a lot of area's that felt different with vastly different ecosystems. And not only did they copy paste some. (The kelp zone and giant jelly fish are back) the new ones just aren't as vibrant and intresting looking. 2 area's in the game share the same "caves with plant vines trough them" theme and the deepest area in the game is a crystal cave and for the surface they just went "lol snow and rocks".Leviathans - Honestly this one is just kind of expectations related because it let me down. The original reaper is #1 and wont be beaten for sure. But we saw other giants and suprisingly the reaper was the smallest leviathan in the game. We were even teased with the idea of massive giants living outside the game area surpassing the size of the emperor seadragon. So what was the next logical step for below zero? To scale these massive creatures down...The smallest leviathan class creature is half the size of the reaper and the largest (moving) leviathan is half the size of the the emperor seadragon. And I assume this has to do with the scaling down of the enviroments, but the original game teased this so well and we are just left with these tiny chrimps of leviathans. And on top of this the big baddies aren't that scary. For some reason the deepest leviathan doesn't make a lot of noise when attacking you so he always caught me by suprise. Sure he does lots of damage but that has never been a problem in subnautica. Also for some reason they always drop you off at the exact same place & rotation that you were picked up from instead of draging you around like the reaper did, so gettting grabbed now has even less consequences to it.And the worm is such a hilarious non-factor that it is almost embarassing. The game promotes these "Thumpers" that are supposed to distract him, but I never used them because you can just run past all his attacks and he will never hit you. He will knock you off your snowglide and do some damage to it, but you just get back on and run away. All in all I did enjoy my time with Subnautica: Below zero and I think it is worth the price. It is worth the money I spend on it and thus I can recommend it. The land section is the only thing that really irked me about the game since land shouldn't be the selling point and there are other games that do it better. I would still recommend the original due to its better focus on sea exploration and the looks.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game in itself, but intensely disappointing compared to the first. Some of it was inevitable, of course: we've already done this once, so it's harder to surprise us. But really, the game seems to promise much that it doesn't deliver on. There are some fascinating biomes, but mostly the world is repetitive and boring. There's almost no reason to visit most locations more than once. Without the intelligent threat posed by some of the creatures in the first game (and these new creatures are also AI stupid)  and the time limit implied by the plot, there's very little tension here. Once the mystery of what happened to your sister is resolved, and it's not much of a mystery, you're left wondering why there's still any game to wade through. The Architect part of the plot blows. The above-water segments are treated exactly the same as underwater segments through the use of heat-loss rather than oxygen-loss time limits, but it's still very little threat and they're a complete chore to hoof through. You are drowning in resources. You have a massive collection of vehicles and vehicle parts, most of which are little use and the rest of which remove any tension or need for movement planning, so I was vastly overprepared for all the situations I encountered. Subnautica caused terror, confusion, and sadness through judicious use of atmosphere, environment and set-pieces, but this game doesn't have many equivalent moments. Subnautica used the crushing drive for survival as plot, and office politics for brief moments of levity; Below Zero has office politics for plot and occasionally remembers being 600m underwater in an alien ocean might also be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Below Zero, but with a few moans and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 7.5/10For myself, the original Subnautica set the bar extremely high! Mostly because it was a fresh new twist on survival and crafting, but also because of its more focused story and exploration... and, , the underwater setting.Subnautica is easily among my top 3 favourite games of all time, next to titles like SOMA and Jagged Alliance 2. Yes, I'm "old"! I've been playing PC games since the mid 90's. The fact Subnautica ends up so high in my favourite all-time games, next to incredible titles like Baldur's Gate, Fallout, X-Com, Half-Life, Myst, etc... says a whole lot about how Subnautica mesmerized me.75% of it, is mainly due to the underwater & horror themes. It plays with my natural, but not too extreme, thalassophobia. This game is among the first games that played with one of my natural fears. It kept the crafting aspect relatively basic and simple. I liked this, because I can't say I care too much about crafting games.Now, back to Below Zero. I enjoyed it, because it's a little more of Subnautica. Unfortunately, I found some of it little weaker. Discovery fell a little flat this time. That was mainly due to re-using many assets. I did not feel on a different planet or place. It felt like I was simply starting over in a much smaller and less intense Subnautica.My favourite aspect of Subnautica, felt slightly diluted by the amount of land you explore. Don't get me wrong,  everything is high quality, just like original Subnautica. But, the underwater world felt much smaller. They packed a good amount of content in it though. But, somehow, I felt less anticipation, or stress, as I was exploring. Sometimes size and scale plays an important role in the immersive aspect. Horror, especially with thalassophobia, can be impacted way more with size and scale.This, plus the very regular audio logs and way stronger story, meant I didn't feel as "alone" or lost in an alien world. I miss that feeling, because part of the fear of always going deeper, and exploring that dark crevice, also comes from a certain amount of loneliness and feeling alone.I thought the modular Seatruck was a move in the right direction, considering the map was smaller. But, the snowfox, I did not care for it very much. Maybe if all land was connected, I would have enjoyed it more?Voice actors all played their roles perfectly. The main voice actress, Kimberly Brooks, and Matthew Marsh (for AL-AN), were spot on! Very enjoyable when they had lines.I did enjoy the extra focus on the architects (especially the end of the game).As much as I enjoyed my time in Below Zero, I felt a longing to play original Subnautica instead. Below Zero felt more like Subnautica 1.5. That's okay though, Subnautica 2 was recently teased. All is good!Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: It´s not a bad game, not at all BUT it is just a downgraded Subnautica and smaller/less in quite every aspect. So, taking into account that the "original" huge Subnautica has the identical price tag (2022) than this "dlc-sized" game, I simply cannot give a thumb up.With "smaller/less" not (only) referring to the map which is much smaller (in area and depth) with less biomes - but also almost all other aspects of the game. Some examples:- While in Subnautica you could build a submarine (with sonar and stuff), place things inside - here you have just a "seatruck" with prebuild modules, lacking most of the features, noise-mechanics completely missing, no speed-steps, no sensors, no customization, nothing. - While in Subnautica I was really horrified by the Reapers, the Chelicerates are somehow much less terrifying, as other said, they are looking like huge shrimps. Overall the game feels much less frigthening and dramatic. The world is shallower, brighter, no huge endless caves (can be positive or negative).- While in Subnautice one felt really alone and desperate, stranded on an alien planet, trying to survive completely alone - here you fly to the planet on purpose, have allies to talk with, human bases everywhere. Overall, much less "dramatic".- Subnautica had two stories which where intertwined (the alien thing and the escape thing), while the alien-thing was not expected from the beginning but discovered - here, one story is just the centuries-old "search for your sister/brother/mother/child"-thing and the other one some sci-fi stuff without any connection to the first story.- While in Subnautica you were alone in the wide ocean (only two tiny islands), seeing over hours nothing but water - now about 1/3 of the (in comparison tiny) map is above sealevel, dry land (not sub nautica). That takes a lot of the desperation-feeling as you can just leave the ocean and take a walk whenever you want.Overall, its just a heavily downgraded and smaller version of Subnautica with less features. Would be a perfect DLC (maybe with option to travel between the "main"-word and the "arctic"-world), but in this form, its a major step backwards. _childDocuments_.review: I have been following this game since early beta. Hell, I've followed the original Subnautica since it was just half-way through Early Access. The original was a big hit, and now it's runner-upper is here. Does it stand up to the titan that is Subnautica? Well, Below Zero has, without a doubt, seen a bit of criticism. Not much, mind you, but it's noticeable. It seems that the reviews are either very positive, or very negative.That being said, Subnautica: Below Zero was a great experience over all. Sure, there are a few things here and there I'd change, but the game itself is great if you really just let yourself enjoy it. A lot of people seem to rush the game, or read too much into the bigger picture instead of taking in the smaller details. This game is not for them. This game is all about taking things slow and smooth. Every game can suck if you do the bare minimum required of you to beat the game.Main criticism I'd give is Robin. After looking back, she's a bit of a strange personality. I saw almost no sadness in her when finding out how her sister had died, and it was just a bit dry in my opinion. Don't get me wrong, an overly enthusiastic and cheery character works great, especially when put next to such a serious and seemingly emotionless character such as Al-An, but a bit of variety would have been better. The Alterra storyline could also have been touched on a bit more. Something to really get the player going, ensuring negative feelings toward the supposedly corrupt company. If you get enough PDA entries and really read into it, you see why and what they are to blame for, but it's not quite enough still.The creatures in the game are all great, how ever, I find them a bit strange in one particular region. The way they attack is unlike the original game, and almost ruins them entirely. A part of the thrill of being chased is not knowing how far, or close you are to the creature. That's quite easy to decipher when they make a loud chomping sound all the time while attacking you. Now, this is done very well with the Shadow Leviathan, the way you hear him pushing water out of it's way as it charges you with it's spade-head is horrifying and really got me out of my chair, but hearing a constant ear-tearing sound from the Squidshark, a considerably smaller creature, isn't as great.Lastly, the land part of the map feels quite barren. In the sea you have all kinds of things, small to big, it feels like a genuine ecosystem. But on land, there are 3 creatures, ranging from small, big, and leviathan. I would have killed to see a bit more liveliness in the Glacial Basin, some sort of food chain at least, but at the same time, the lack of life makes it feel more deserted, lonely, and scary, and that is a big part of this game, maybe not as big as the original, but they still rewrote the storyline to make you feel more alone, so this issue is a double edged sword.Other than that though, the game is fantastic. The base building was improved well, the environment feels lively as ever, except for the land part, which I am still unsure on, is it a good thing or a bad thing? Nevertheless, the game gave me a good experience. The story was great, the cinematography was beautiful, the characters were fun and interesting, albeit a small cast.One of the main reasons that people find this game underwhelming is due to the fact that it's predecessor was already a very hard goal to beat. But, if you just let yourself sink into the game for a bit, focus on what you want to do with it, it will feel like just as fun as the original. I had a hell of a time making bases with the new large rooms, outposts on land, messing around with the music system, and all the great features this game brings. Subnautica: Below Zero, and it's predecessor, will always have a spot in my library for them. Nothing is quite like them, and that's the magic of it in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: While yes, Subnautica below zero was originally meant to be a DLC to Subnautica, It still works well as a game. It has the feel of Subnautica; the mix of alien and natural, however leans more into alien in this game. While the map is much smaller, It still gave me the normal Subnautica length. The biomes are quite diverse, and in my opinion, some look better with the added bioluminescence.  Some biomes just feel desolate, even when they have heaps of life. An instance would be the biome that delta station sits on, with no real purpose but diamonds, which you can get elsewhere. The biome reminds me of the crag field from the original Subnautica, a desolate landscape. A lesser example would be the purple geyser biome that lies next to it, But the biome has a use and contains important story elements. However below zero cancels that out with the good biome, which for me are the purple and red crystal caverns, both have good atmosphere and contain story elements, with a fun amount of danger in them. However getting to these places are hard, as the game is really unclear. you don't get any reason to explore, and beacons and notifications only appear after exploring. My least favourite is either getting to the greenhouse or the red crystal caverns, both being unnecessarily hard to find. Alan also takes forever to give locations, so I found random ones before he gave coordinates to them. They also replaced the Seamoth and Cyclops with the Seatruck, which I kind of like. It doesn't have the nostalgia as the other, but is much more customisable. However with 4 segments, the Seatruck feels slower than the cyclops without any speed upgrades. I also dislike the fact that you need to scan the fragments for the speed upgrade, instead of having a data box. I couldn't find enough fragments to complete the recipe. This lead to me just dumping my sSatruck segments in the end just for speed. The game also feels a bit empty, with not many dangerous enemies in the important and useful biomes. The land feels more populated, but only really after the bridge when the worm shows up. Also the salad removes the entire effect of heat, and also being a better source of food than the nutrient block. Even with all of that, It still is a good game, it still has the subnautica feel but could be improved with some tweaks. I would recommend, getting the feeling of subnautica all over again is very nice, and it doesn't fail as a game. I do wish it could have been made a bit more clear, but still a fun game. 7-8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Joined the Franchise during the Beta Testing for Subnautica Below Zero and completely fell in love with it. The graphics and storylines were amazing and you didn't wanna stop playing and building on your base. When the storyline completely changed during Beta Testing. I stopped playing since I didn't wanna end up even more confused since there was dialog from both storylines available already. So now that the game was finally out. I used this longer weekend to play through the whole game. The storyline is rather touching, but it doesn't really give you a great suspence about what turns the story could take. There are a lot of points that are left away (or I just didn't end up finding the PDAs). Like when and how did the others workers leave the planet and how will the storyline of Marguerits end. The ending is left open a lot. Which makes me hope that there will be a 3rd Subnautica that connects to ending of this one. But then that also leaves the question of if it then could/would even be an underwater game. Since we didn't see any water in the cinematic. All in all there was a lot of Equipment that was unneeded in my opinion. I played the whole game through without even having to create or use a Prawn Suit once. It was nice for the storyline and presentation since you had a mine. But all in all you didn't really need it to play the game. The Seatruck is so designed that you could only use it to get through the whole game, without even an additional base. There were also a lot of equipment and plants that I was confused we weren't able to scan. The tiered plant circle display would have been an amazing addition to any greenhouse and I was really hoping that we might end up getting it also. But when I wasn't able to gather or scan the Bulbo Tree in Marguerits base that really confused me, since that one was available already in the original Subnautica. And for me it was a vital part of it, so of course I wanted to add it to my greenhouse. There was a lot less flora to play around with in and outside the base. While the land part of the game is designed really well and an interesting addition to the underwater world. I have to confess that I disliked it a lot. There was a lot of variation between the different biomes and locations, which made it interesting to see how they're different in fauna und flora. The interaction and little games that we were able to do with the Spy Pengling were really neat. And they were also needed to find important tools for the storyline. But I really disliked that areas where the Leviathans were. In the water you can move your way around them but on land it was nearly impossible. All in all it's really interesting game and I love that you guys still made it available for iOS users. (me included xD)There is a huge difference between the first one and this ones graphics and animation with I can only applaud the developers and designers for. I personally really enjoyed the verbalized interactions between Robin and Al-An and loved that we had another character in the game that were were able to interact with. That made a huge difference since the first one was kinda lonely sometimes. And while I may have finished it rather quickly in under 15 hrs... I will just restart it again and enjoy it a bit more while building a great base. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: First Play through reviewSo after getting as far as possible (since ending isn't out yet) I wanted to kinda voice my opinion as someone that subnautica was my first survival type game.Good Points1. I love the story and the voice touches too it it brings you in makes you even more curious as to what happened and how2. I like the changes to the prawn suit and for the most part the idea of the truck3. The biomes are beautiful and as always I love the attention to detail4. I found it relatively similar in ease as the first one regarding knowing what you need to make what you want...finding it was different story...but the layout of the pda as always was great5. I love that you acknowledge the aurora from the first story!!! To many games don't acknowledge their beginnings.Some improvements1. I wish there was a little better direction to the story there are many points where things go silent for a while and for some you have to be on top of an item to be alerted to it. It would be nice if for example you found one you were then given another shortly afterward.(Trying to say that without spoilers)For example in the first one one of the scans in the alien area gave you the locations to a couple of the others.2. The biomes are very very cluttered in some cases making it very very hard to navigate or even know where you have been or need to go...I wish the pathfinder tool was back in this one..that would be a biiiiig help. On that same note it also makes it almost impossible in some cases to get the truck even with just the prawn suit attachment where you need to go.3. There seem to be a lot of unanswered questions in the story...I don't know if the ending will answer everything but so far...it doesn't feel like it to be honest I think a lot will be answered but I feel like a major part won't be. (I could be totally wrong on that one to be clear)4. Locating fragment was incredibly difficult this time around again partly because the biomes clutter so you ended up going in circles for a while but also in some of the areas it was soo hard to tell if there was or wasn't an item there (nests)All in all I have no doubt I will replay this one quite a few times until I get as comfortable with it as I am the first one. I think the premise is good and if you have been like I was hesitant to try survival type games I think both subnautica's are an amazing introduction to them and good for a new player just wanting to try the genre. I would definitely say this game was worth the purchase and I would recommend to others but I would also recommend giving feeback as the the developers from what I have seen so far have a lot of love for this game and I think want to make it the best if can be...I hope they make more!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS....Right let’s start by insisting that Subnautica is one of, if not THE greatest game ever made. It’s gaming perfection and I have hundreds of hours in it so below zero was following in some very big footsteps. With 60 hours of this game behind me, try as hard as I might, I cannot help but feel hugely deflated by this second title. There are some fabulous ideas make no mistake but they are all poorly implemented. I don’t care about the character at all. Not one bit. The game gives me no reason to. There is no story to her at all, no background, She is a nod to Ripley without a doubt but she just seems to laugh and joke her way through the game with an alien in her head. There is no character development at all. But I can live with that, it’s the game I really care about. Here ladies and gentlemen is my largest gripe and unbelievable as it is, you could easily work through this entire game with the first scuba tank, a rebreather and the sea glide. I kid you not. You just don’t NEED ANYTHING, The base building has some fabulous new additions and irons out what annoying oversights there were in the first game, but does NOTHING to aid you at all. Subnautica was so big and so deep multiple bases were a prerequisite without dozens of batteries or power cells and hours of travel. The cyclops was a proper mobile base that was awesome and inspiring to pilot. It felt intimidating the first time you saw how dam big it was and the computer voice was awesome. The sea truck has a bizarre modular system that just doesn’t work. It’s far too small and by the time you turn it into a mile long vessel to be of any use it’s so long and cumbersome it’s best just leaving the darn thing at home. The prawn suit is useless. You just don’t need it for anything at all. It mines stuff that’s it. Getting it onto land is a nightmare and when you do it’s a total lottery as to which caves you fit in and which you don’t, totally wasted, resource hungry to build and utterly worthless. Then there are the islands. Oh god the islands. Here the game fails. Monumentally in my opinion. The western basin is simply too large and ultimately becomes a giant labyrinth with no real purpose. You’ll spend hours wandering around aimlessly looking for the one little cave that leads you to the ultimate goal. It’s not hard, it’s just pointlessly tedious and I found myself swearing at the monitor for just how boring it was. They need to be FAR smaller and play much less of a roll in an underwater game. Margareet is a character you want to be more involved with but again, she just exists. She’s built an entire world for herself but can’t make a simple electronic device work to disable the satellite tracking. It’s embarrassing story writing, so off we go the hero, and in minutes do just that and.,,, boom. Nothing, it’s disabled and nothing. It’s just another story thread to nowhere. Ultimately Margareet herself just sits feet up on a table wanting nothing more to do with you. It’s just such a waste of a character, The game is still not finished so I’m definitely not saying this is it. But Subnautica this is not. It’s lost that magical survival feeling. That awesome sense of achievement when the last piece of the cyclops is found. The first game had a mission. A clear and unavoidable goal of needing to get off the planet and then entangles it with a brilliant and totally feasible alien plot with perfect pacing and real intrigue. Below zero spoon feeds you a bunch of sites to scan that again ultimately do nothing at all other than lead to the next one. The graphics are superb, sound as good as ever, but alas the developers have steered too far from the game that led to it, I honestly think is could be as good as Subnautica, they have several of the voice actors from the series “Archer” to my ears, but the story needs some major major work to make this a more cohesive experience. 4/10 for me. So far.........

As she dove headfirst into this virtual universe, I couldn't help but feel a pang of isolation, longing for a way to connect with her in a world dominated by screens and algorithms.Determined to bridge the gap between us, I mustered the courage to explore this foreign terrain by creating my own gaming profile and immersing myself in the game that had captured my daughter's imagination. As I navigated the virtual landscapes, I felt like a fish out of water, struggling to grasp the mechanics and intricacies of the game.Turning to my daughter for guidance, she eagerly offered to be my mentor, patiently teaching me the ropes and sharing her expertise. With her guidance, I slowly but surely began to find my footing in this digital realm, discovering a newfound sense of camaraderie and understanding with my daughter.Our roles reversed as she became the teacher and I, the student. Through shared victories and defeats, we forged a bond that transcended generational barriers, finding common ground in the unlikeliest of places.This game became our shared sanctuary, a place where words were unnecessary, and actions spoke volumes. It opened the door to conversations we had never thought to have, fostering a sense of closeness and mutual respect that had eluded us in the fast-paced world we inhabited.As we ventured through virtual quests and conquered digital foes together, I realized that the true treasure lay not in the pixels on the screen but in the moments of connection and understanding we shared. This game became a bridge that spanned the divide between us, reminding me that in the vast expanse of the digital landscape, the most valuable treasures are the bonds we forge with those we love.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, which is March 7, 2021. The game is still one month away from official launch. This review is based on the pre-launch condition of the game, and I'll try and update it when the game officially launches.For the most part, what you're getting with Below Zero is exactly what you got in the original Subnautica. The time spent under the ocean, exploring the biomes and uncovering secrets is effectively unchanged mechanically from the first game. This is great, and I loved the first game. So why the negative review?The time spent on LAND is big change from the original subnautica and is, for the most part frustrating, or wholly negative. Because the game is set in the Arctic, land areas are mostly white ice broken up by caves and the like between cliffs and glaciers. Visually its distinct and looks good. For navigation in a game that specifically eschews a traditional video game map with a "you are here" marker, its awful. The devs even seem to have noticed this and there are 2 static maps available of specific areas. Both don't help much, because the areas are both convoluted and lack good, non-repeating landmarks. Underwater navigation, comparatively, is the same as the first game, with lots of useful landmarks to use to orient yourself. Beacons help with both, and can be used on land, but are distinctly less useful on land, due to the convoluted cave systems that connect areas.The other big issue on Land is the Ice Worm, a new enemy that only appears in a certain area of land. These act like you would expect, popping out of the ice to attack you as you traverse. Unfortunately they are, at the moment, very poorly  implemented. They don't do a great deal of damage to the player personally, and the vehicle you're given to navigate the Land sections takes damage but will never die in one shot. The worms will knock you off your vehicle, apparently regardless of distance as they breach the ice. So traversal of the area becomes, rather than tense, just tedious. As you're knocked off your bike every 30 seconds or so, repair it, then continue on your way. There are items to convince the worms to stay away from you for a time, but they, if anything add the tedium of setting them up. The animations involving the worms are also need a lot of work, as they can appear in odd places, based on their size, and leave nothing behind. The whole creature is just not very well done at this time. I'm hoping they do a lot of improvements with them.Bugs:-The most common bug I've experienced, and it can be frustrating, is to do with the main vehicle in the game. Very frequently you'll find yourself "swimming" in the air of the vehicle, either on entry or getting out of the driver's seat. Sometimes this is fixed by opening the PDA or pausing, often not. The only way to fix it if the above doesn't work is somehow getting out of the vehicle. Another issue to do with the Seatruck is that, unlike the Cyclops, you can "park" it in such a way it isn't level. Leaving all your modules inaccessible.-I've had multiple sound bugs, where sounds will overlap each other in odd ways, including cutting off dialog.If you absolutely loved the first game you can probably overlook the above and end up enjoying it anyway. The Land sections are relatively limited and once you're done with them you never have to go back as far as I know. If the Ice Worms and the issues to do with the Seatruck are fixed on release I can definitely recommend this game to anyone. But as it stands, I can only recommend it to someone who wants more Subnautica and has some patience to deal with jank. Most of the new additions to the game are great, especially the new base pieces and the new biomes are stunning as always. Really hoping I can amend this review come May.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not recommending this game for three main reasons.A: It's super unfinished at the momentB: The protagonist is voiced and has an unbearable personality.C. Storyline is inferior in what has been developed so farSo the first part is pretty basic. Huge portions of the map are literally not made, features are buggy, the story isn't even done yet. The game simply isn't finished and I don't mean not fleshed out I mean you're literally buying half a game. If you want to spend money to support the devs and test what they have at the moment that's great, but don't buy the game under the prerogative that you are buying a full game it's not even close.The second part is what really motivated me to not recommend the game. So in the first subnautica your protagonist is unvoiced and generally devoid of personality ext. Voiced protagonists rarely bother me (i.g. fallout 4's voicing didn't bother me), however the way it was executed ruined the game for me and it's not really fixable. You play a female, which I'm fine with, but she is so ARROGANT. In subnautica I was always checking over my shoulder suspicious of any fish in the ocean because half of them could kill you. It really felt like I was fighting to survive and I felt my character experienced the same fear I did. However this protagonist's dialogue and voice convey that she is utterly unafraid of the terrors of the deep, and the mysterious alien race you re-encounter, and it frankly just comes off as both fake and annoying. Furthermore she comes off as some super eco warrior type, which I'm not really into. It probably would have been fine if the other bits of her personality weren't so toxic, but this really just killed any empathy I might have had for the character. This resulted in me almost enjoying below zero, but every time my character opened her mouth it completely broke immersion and I just wanted to play something else, anything else.Finally I found the story mediocre. Let me preface that the is story is not *bad*, but despite the voice acting added to it, it simply falls short of the first, at least with what is in it. For starters you are not alone you have constant radio communication with your sister who is in orbit, which greatly removes the fear and unknown from the story. In the first one you you were frantically searching for the other survivors, while trying to find out what happened and what is going on. It was full of twists and turns and I never knew what was going to happen next. However, in this the story comes off more of a grocery list of instructions. Part of this can once again be accredited to the deplorable protagonist, but even without that the mystique of the first story just seems absent.Ultimately the game will eventually be fleshed out solving the first problem and that might lead to the story getting more interesting as the game is finished. However, there's no way to get around a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ protagonist and that same protagonist will remove any joy I might get from the story or gameplay so it with a heavy heart I can't recommend this game despite how much I enjoyed the first one.
