_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: In its own respect, Subnautica: Below Zero is a fairly enjoyable experience with plenty to keep the player invested and entertained. However, when compared to the original Subnautica, it is a noticeably underwhelming experience that has been significantly limited from its predecessor.Full Review: I should start this review by mentioning that I have over 200 hours logged in the original Subnautica and only around 73 hours in Below Zero. That being said, If I were to boot Subnautica back up and jump right back into it, I feel like I would be able to do so much more exploring and uncover way more than I did originally. However, I do not have that same feeling with Below Zero. Even though I enjoyed my playthrough of Below Zero, I have no urge to jump back into it after having beaten it as I feel like I have seen everything that there is to see and have done everything that there is to do. And I think a lot of this has to do with how much easier Below Zero is than its predecessor.There are some areas in which BZ has improved over Subnautica. These areas include the story, which seems to be much more on-rails than before, and general mechanics that effect progression such as blueprint acquirement and resource gathering. The story is now delivered in a much more fluid and streamlined way that makes it easier for the player to uncover new story threads and progress throughout the general narrative of BZ. It is more enjoyable as a whole, but it ultimately removes a lot of the difficulty and intrigue that could be found in the original's narrative design that hooked the player and drove them to do much more exploring in an effort to uncover more of the story. The aforementioned progression mechanics have once again been streamlined in a way that makes it easier to progress throughout the game while offering a more limited, on-rails experience for the player. Minerals that would have typically been considered rare in the original game are now much more abundant in many more biomes. The average player will still likely end up accumulating an overabundance of titanium earlier on, but resources such as copper, lead, gold, silver, lithium, ruby, cave sulfur, diamond and even nickel ore are way easier to find and gather in the less hostile beginner biomes. On top of that, item fragments are also now super abundant and easy to find. I am willing to bet that the average player will likely be able to craft everything in the game within 15-20 hours of playing. These improvements to story and progression make the game more enjoyable to a certain degree, but they greatly hinder the incentive for exploration.The most significant criticism that I can make of BZ when compared to Subnautica is that it just feels a lot less scary. There is still a decent amount of hostile fauna that poses a threat to the player, But these creatures are just not as scary as the ones from the original Subnautica for several reasons. One of these reason is the design of these creatures. I am fully aware that I am not the first person to make this comparison, but the Chelicerate "Leviathan" looks like a giant shrimp. I feel like this was supposed to be BZ's equivalent to the Reaper Leviathan in Subnautica due to it mostly inhabiting early biomes and lacking any form of bioluminescence. As someone who used to be downright terrified of the Reapers and actually experienced a handful of lucid nightmares involving them, this is an absolutely insulting change made to BZ and it spits in the face of horror. While I still do not think it would've lived up to the precedent set by the Reaper, I think the Cryptosuchus would've been a much better fit for the Chelicerate if it were made larger and did more damage. Despite being a lower-level threat, the Cryptosuchus offers way more in regards to being terrifying than any other aquatic creature in the game. It features a more intimidating design and produces a louder and more terrifying roar than the Chelicerate's underwhelming squeal.That being said, all of the other dangerous leviathans in the game (Shadow, and Ice Worm) are scary looking/sounding enough, but they still aren't exactly scary for one big reason. They are too easy to deal with. When I say "deal with" I do not mean killing or, in some cases, even harming these creatures. They are just too easy to deter. For starters, the moment that the player unlocks the Seatruck Perimeter Defense Upgrade, they are basically impervious to any and all hostile aquatic fauna. The moment that a Chelicerate or Shadow Leviathan grabs your Seatruck, you are able to activate the SPDU and completely interrupt their attack. This causes them to swim away from the player's Seatruck without having dealt any damage if the upgrade is deployed early enough. This worked similarly to if the Reaper would grab the players Seamoth in Subnautica. However, the Ghost Leviathan literally gave zero f*cks about the player's fancy SPDU and would often ram the player head on regardless as to whether or not they deployed the upgrade. Furthermore, once the player acquires the Prawn Suit and Thumper, they have absolutely nothing to worry about on land. Temperature is unaffected within the Prawn Suit, and Ice Worm Leviathans will be completely distracted by Thumper and do minimal damage to the Prawn Suit. The Prawn Suit is honestly so overpowered that you would think the developers would implement something in BZ to prevent the player from bringing it onto land, but they don't. That being said, if you already have a Prawn Suit, you shouldn't even bother wasting your time crafting the Snowfox. It is far less useful than the Prawn Suit and honestly feels a bit like a desperate attempt by Unknown Worlds to add more redundant content to the game.(While on the topic of redundant content, I often felt no need to take advantage of the new base customization features added to this game. Since I never really felt the need to use this mechanic, I will not be commenting on it. Use it at your own risk.)I know that I've mostly been crapping on this game, but I do think it is still an enjoyable experience as long as players don't go into it expecting a major evolution on the original Subnautica. The world is still incredibly stunning (despite being considerably smaller than the original). The creatures are well-designed and cool-looking. Even the Chelicerate looks pretty cool, I just don't think it has any business as a leviathan-class creature. The biomes are diverse and plentiful. While I am not a huge fan of the inclusion of land-based terrain, land biomes look absolutely immaculate when compared to the land biomes in Subnautica. I also think that a lot of the new gear featured in-game is very cool and useful, even though some of it may be considered redundant when compared to other gear. The story in BZ is also far more engaging and unique than that of its predecessor. Also, the option to pin certain craftable items to your HUD is a new mechanic that I found extremely useful. I do feel like this mechanic could've been developed a bit more, but it still serves a huge purpose. And while this game isn't quite able to evoke the same crap-your-pants terror that the original was capable of, I was still thoroughly creeped out in a lot of sections and even flinched a few times early in game (This feeling did wear off after about 5-10 hours of playing). The game is still plenty engaging and kept me coming back whenever I would log off for the day. I DO NOT THINK THIS IS A BAD GAME!If you have invested many hours into the original Subnautica and find yourself wanting more of the same, tried-and-true formula with minor tweaks to make it more enjoyable, I think you will have a lot of fun in Subnautica: Below Zero. If you are someone who has never played Subnautica, I think you will enjoy BZ. If you are expecting a complete evolution of Subnautica, you will not find it in this game, and you will be dissapointed in many ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Most reviews here have covered basics to death. It's Subnautica again, but not quite as good. Technical stability is probably better, and gameplay is generally the same.What threw me for a loop was the story.SPOILERS FOR SUBNAUTICA AND BELOW ZERO AHEAD:The story lacks any sort of sense of mystery or suspense that the first game had. Subnautica dropped you into a hostile, alien environment with no explanation except knowing your ship went down, explosively. You collected logs to piece together the sad stories of the other survivors, and overtime figure out why your ship was shot down. Then you realize you need to go deeper and explore this alien remnants to figure out how to save yourself from this disease. Each step of the plot progresses to the next smoothly, with incredible moments of emotion and suspense mixed in.All of this with no voiced protagonist.Now I'm not saying that having a voiced protagonist and more "plot-based" story in Below Zero was a bad idea, but the writing consistently misses the connections and intrigue that drove the first game. You go to this planet to figure out what happened to your sister.Great concept, really. But the execution is baffling. We immediately fail to draw much interest because the game tells you that your sister is dead. Within about 30 minutes of gameplay, it is very easy to find logs that explain to anyone with even slight inference abilities why and how your sister died. You can find more details as you go, but none of the characters draw much interest since the situation is so mundane. Not to mention that our character reacts to news of her beloved sisters death with the emotion of a wet blanket. Plot points, plot holes and inconsistencies are abound, but mostly I just didn't really care about any of these people, and neither does Robin it seems.The second aspect of the story, the "alien stuff". Is better. Not great, but fine. But notice how I said "second aspect". These two stories have zero connection to each other, at all. It can only be described as two separate stories that happen in the same place, on top of each other. Our alien companion might comment about your sister, but you *don't even have to have him* at any point that far, so his dialogue is purely fluff.In the end, it feels like the game had two teams of writers, which had entirely different ideas for a story for this game, and then were told to just smash them together in a bowl. It gets very messy.All of that said, I still recommend Below Zero. It's a very good survival and exploration game with solid and fun mechanics, and one can totally ignore the story aspects and just enjoy the game if you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Some odd design decisions, exploration that feels deliberately confusing, and weak use of characters keep Below Zero from being excellent, even if its gameplay and presentation have been improved upon. This feels like a hastily made expansion to the original Subnautica versus a fully fledged sequel.My biggest issue with the game are its exhausting land sections, where they try to capture the underwater feel with temperature replacing oxygen and the snowfox replacing your seatruck. The game has these long stretches with nothing but suffering through identical frozen hallways, with intermittent snowstorms completely ruining your sense of direction. I don't know why the developers thought, in a game called Subnautica, that players would want to spend more time out of the water. If I wanted to wander around frozen wastes in a snow storm I would play The Long Dark. The world itself felt like a huge step back from the original Subnautica in several ways and I'm torn on what I found more disappointing; the complete lack of player impact on the world (the first had the Aurora explode and powering an alien cannon), and the god awful sense of exploration. It felt like because the developers had a smaller map with fewer biomes they made them harder to navigate and landmark. In the first game I rarely felt the need for beacons because I could reliably find previously visited locations, in Below Zero I was printing beacons out constantly from frustration.Even if you were an adoring fan of the first Subnautica I encourage you to wait for a sale. Still a strong game but it fails to live up to the expectations of the first.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews have made comments about how they think the story of this game as well as other aspects are a downgrade from Subnautica 1. The environment, base building, creatures, terror, etc. were recaptured very well in Subnautica 2. The story is not all that bad in my opinion and I liked the interaction between Robin and Al-An. I was expecting throughout for Al-An to turn on Robin and become evil but I was pleasantly surprised in a subversion of expectations way when Al-An never did and he and Robin finally made it to his home world in search of his people. I think for most people, if they enjoyed Subnautica 1 they will enjoy 2 as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The old recipe to which i've felt in love, I haven't explored the abyssal depths of the game yet so i'm probably missing a lot as i'm writting this. The core is the same as Subnautica but it feels more challenging than the previous game : enemies, more necessary out of sub cave network exploration (despite you can still go for the "make it fit" approach), tech discovery, raw material less accessible, etc...The map editing seems less "area" composed. I might be only me but i'm have more a hard time knowing where I am looking at the ground or the species around me than in subnautica. Which gives it a more natural feeling.The fauna which, at first felt too recycled, is extremely riched and imaginative. The flora is also breathtaking and I urge to see those luminescent plants in the abyss. Anyway, I'm having a blast discovering the environnement while scanning everything and reading what there is to say in the PDA. Yes, i'm not lying. If you're a developper at Unknown world entertainement or the coffee/boring stuff intern, please know that you didn't type all those descriptions for nothing ;). I haven't done much of the ground exploration nor faced the cold weather mechanic for a long period of time  but it's clever. I mean, in subnautica, you'd feel more confortable outside the water knowing what can lurk in and finding plenty of fruits and vegetables. In this one, keeping your head below the water is the only option, i think it makes you want to blend with this world even more...despite that you'll hear shivering underwater screams quite frequently. One great addition, is the versatile "Sea Truck". Clearly despite the satisfaction of having a giant sub with the Cyclops, it was more a burden than anything else and not pratical at depths that it should have. From the blueprints i've found that Sea Truck, equivalent to the Sea Moth, can be upgrade with modules allowing you to have a small mobile base, more manoeuvrable than that giant one eye coffin.I enjoy the fact that in this one, at least there are some direct interaction with npc and a voice for the character. Despite what you may think, this doesn't sabotage the solitary feeling you have. I'm also glad they've kept that cynical tone concerning Alterra, or more likely our "world vision" about how we consider existence, lifeform, human interaction, propriety, working. Just to add that little extra perception of :" I'm trapped on a planet where i'm definitely not an apex predator and not even in my element, struggling every day but ♥♥♥♥ yeah, this is THE LIFE !".Anyway, I'm probably spoiling way too much and lost your attention 200 paragraphs ago.To sum up everything, I'm not a big spender. I could have waited for the game price to go down especially because there isn't much necessity for a rush. In fact, I bought and finished the first one a few months ago ! I almost never spend 30€ on a game (besides that PUBG joke) and all I can say is that i'm glad I've shown my support to great studios who have brought me back nostalgia of scuba diving and shallow diving in exotic water or more common ones. On top of that who also have given me the interest of creatures in our own oceans, quite hard to reach and which aren't much more different from the alien lifeform that I'm wishing so much we'll discover soon enough ! Once more I thank you so much everyone who has been involved in this serie !

_childDocuments_.review: Having played through this game and it's predecessor multiple times - If you have not played the first Subnautica game, go do that instead of this. I do not recommend this game.I never want to see this games starting zone (Ice Island where PHI Robotics dock is) again in my life. It's so frustrating, I want to wrap the section up as fast as I can to move on, but there is no way of knowing when you are done the zone or what you even have to do there. I have spent hours there and my only goal is to move on so I never have to go back but there's so much garbage to roll through there. I very much want to play this game through again but I can't justify HOURS OF FRUSTRATION of trying to get past this zone again. The lack of polish on a game that has been Early Access this long and is the second iteration of, is rough. I tried to swim out of a ships wreckage and saw the ocean surface, only to swim into another layer of the ship and suddenly have a roof over my head with no way to get out. Sometimes my character falls literally a foot off a ledge (some folks would consider it a step) and I take damage for it - I can jump higher than I fell. It would be better if you had multiple voice packs to select from for the PDA warning system. I liked the old voice and don't like the new one. I want to turn it off but need the sound for the warning. This might seem silly but when I hear it, I stop thinking about the game play and start thinking it's the most thick accent I have ever heard like you're making fun of that accent. There are not a lot of lines coming from the PDA, wouldn't have been tough to do. The game is called Subnautica. Having to ride a bike on an island for hours before I can get back to the water is not what I signed up for. I want to play the part of the game I like without having to waste such a large amount of time. I fully understand working towards something and getting the cooler stuff later but the sheer amount of time you have to waste before getting to the enjoyable content is mind blowing.They left the cool vehicles in the first game with the exception of the prawn suit which was the least cool vehicle in the first game.  Just go play the first one and you're never going to be as upset as I am about the second one. I want to play this game but I am going to have to find a step-by-step guide to get me through ice-maze island so I spend the least amount of time possible there but at the same time I don't want to spend hours doing something I hate in hopes that I'll enjoy it later.

_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR: save your money until about 4 more updates. Or more.On the one hand, I really do like the game and want to see it through. I'm having a blast with it. When it works.But on the other hand, all the bugs make it unplayable at this time. Again. Still. Every time I have an issue, I look up possible solutions. Same problems I have, but going back to 2016 with issue still not resolved. I had high hopes that the official final release would have solved most/some of the issues. Nope.Like I started with, the game is good. From the flora and fauna to the story line to the lore. I really want to continue playing to see how it all comes together. I find the game to be enjoyable. When it works.When it doesn't work, game play becomes a constant "why bother". For example, there is the terrain graphics failing to load. All I have are geometric shapes that don't fill in. I've sat around and waited for it to load. It doesn't. Swimming through iceberg geometry is cool up to a point. Then there's the "perpetual loop of saving". It never finishes the save. I read that it just sometimes takes a while and gets hung up. Okay. I just waited 45 minutes and then it froze. Lost 1.5hrs of game time. And that's the third time today, Umpteenth time this week. And that's just the top two of the problems I have with this game.Nearly all games have bugs. I get that. But this is a game that was in beta for how long? Years? And these bugs still exist?So yes, great game - when it works. I'll set this one aside (again) for a while and come back to see if it ever gets fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea how Subnautica: Below Zero can be so similar to the original yet is so much worse. The Devs took the worst parts of the original and made a game around it. It's the weakest part of the game because the whole area is nearly featureless yet is so massive you need to backtrack a dozen times to finish exploring (and you need to explore the whole thing to finish the game).  There's also the map and level design. Almost anything important is contained in small, hard-to-find caves inside another bigger cave. Since they took out echolocation and there's no real way to explore other than to stumble around in the dark.There's also the story which despite being more extensive is somehow worse. Both the alien and Robin's story is terrible and makes no sense within the context of the previous game. They also resurrected another character from the original game despite it being impossible according to the lore. She doesn't even play a big part in the story and could have been replaced with a PDA and it would be narratively better.

_childDocuments_.review: Played both the original, and then Below Zero in experimental mode and now the full release. I absolutely love these games. Below Zero is a creative continuation of the first game that always keeps the player on their toes. Unlike the first game, Below Zero has much more character development, a welcome addition! Furthermore, get ready for more story, fun creatures, and exploration of new world elements... and also a cat named Potato. If you loved the original Subnautica, you'll likely appreciate the new mechanics, like the added temperature gauge, the ability to pin recipes, the jukebox, and many more creatures to interact with (baby Stalkers are my personal favorite). Overall, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: So here's my take:Pros: Plenty of exploration, open world adventure, structures to find. The map is well developed in the areas of interest. The island itself is well made. You will love the gameplay there is no question about it.Cons: The map is incomplete in certain areas, go too far around the main island and you encounter a "void" In addition, this game has a fair share of bugs, most commonly with the Sea Prawn. First of all, it is impossible to get the MK1 depth module, and MK2 requires that it be manually imported by command into the game. The reason why this sucks is because the SeaTruck only goes down to 900M, while the sea prawn with MK2 can reach 1000.  Biggest pro: The game has amazing graphics, and exploration/adventure.Biggest con: There is no story.... Developers are reworking it at the time of this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite up to first Subnautica level. Land exploration part is interesting but there is almost nothing new to explore with high-tier depth upgrades. Story is... well, bland. There is some new stuff to buid but now you can't pick up and install any lab equipment like in the first game (why? they were just decorations anyway). Seatruck is a disasterously ugly crossbred between Cyclops and Seamoth. It cannot be your mobile base and has no storage space without bulky attached modules of varying uselessness. Thank god Prawn Suit was not mutilated and land hoverbike is kinda fun. There is no stun-gun so top-leve leviathan extermination now requires a Prawn Suit drill, not just a knife. Overal the game looks like a weird mix between a genuine attempt to make a good game and half-baked quick money-grab on a popular title.TLDR: Expect Subnautica-lite. With hoverbike.

_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the first game it pains me to not really recommend Below Zero. Whilst most of the core gameplay is preserved, the game does itself a major disservice with both the plot and the land sections.Your original motivation for the story is quite literally sidelined for another, creating a fairly jarring experience in knowing what you are trying to achieve and where to explore. Subnautica's original plot worked because the player had the primary goal of escaping the planet, and an understanding of what they needed to do - everything else is world building and set dressing. In this we're told to care about one thing, and then another, complete with sections where you circle the room waiting for a character to stop talking.The land sections sway between disorientating and dull, with exploration throwing you more resources than you can really carry, and leviathan encounters which are mostly just annoying to deal with when on the hoverbike. Subnautica's first title breaks up the excellent sea-based play with the odd island sections, whilst Below Zero demands you dedicate your time for one section. I think the developers were far too wed to their original vision of these areas.On top of other faults like exploration just not quite being as intricate and interesting, and less polish than I'd expect for the same engine and general gameplay, I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game and loved this one too. It's a bit different but it's still Subnautica at the core. Everything feels more polished too. Exploring is fun, building is fun, the story is cool, and some of the biomes are INCREDIBLE. You also have a lot flexibility in how you approach things and in what order. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica Below Zero is a fantastic game. It would be a perfect masterpiece, if it's predecessor didn't exist.But first off, Below Zero is nonetheless a great addition to the lore of Planet 4546B. It shows a completely different region and shows just how beautifully crafted this world is. New Creatures, related to some Fish of the tropics, Plant life you think you know, but still differs ever so slightly. The map design is beautiful, each and every biome is a sight for sore eye. (This will come back to bite tho.) The game has an amazing soundtrack which definitely exceeds the one from the first game but this is also a bit of a critique as I personally feel the tracks are a bit too persistent. For example in a biome of crystal caves the soundtrack is blasting your ears nonstop which really hurts the atmosphere. If you compare it to the Lost River of Subnautica for example, the soundtrack for that biome plays every now and then but mostly, the ambience is what fills you with immersion. Absolute Perfection. This game sadly did suffer a bit because of it's otherwise amazing soundtrack.The story of this game is neat. It's a good main storyline with some really forgettable sideplots. I don't remember anything about the Sister's subplot but the main storyline is really cool and gets a lot deeper into the cosmic aspect of Subnautica's general story which I really like. The characters are sympathetic and interesting, especially the main two. Their dynamic is really fun.This game is a lot more story driven than Subnautica which yes, is a rather negative point in comparison of the two games but honestly, it's just cool. I don't really mind it. Now we get into the territory of the negative.The map is sadly way too small. It is really beautiful and I admire the effort put into designing all of it. But it's really small and you'll get the feeling of having seen everything very quickly basically. The beautifully designed biomes are beautiful yes but that is not what the ocean is as a whole. It has it's beautiful sceneries, but it also has dunes of nothing. Subnautica excelled at that. Below Zero not so much. And another sad part about it, most of the really wonderful and interesting places just feel very... "unnecessary". This game was very enthusiastic about featuring a lot more land than the first one. But you honestly only go there for the story a few times and you have no reason to go there otherwise really. A lot of materials and ressources just feel like they have no purpose. Kyanite which was essential for survival in the endgame of Subnautica was basically just there to be there. The jellyfish biome was really cool. But you only go there for one ressource and just go back not exploring it any further. Because you have no reason to. There is nothing there except marvelous design.This game is 100% a downgrade from the first. Is it still worth checking out?Absolutely. It's a wonderful addition to the lore of Subnautica and I loved my time playing it.If you loved Subnautica, you'll like Below Zero.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, if you liked the original then you'll like this. They really outdid themselves in world design this time around, and have a more fleshed out story. _childDocuments_.review: It's more Subnautica!If you've played Subnautica 1 (which I recommend as this game's plot heavily references the events of the original) you'll feel right at home.Overall though I think I still like the original Subnautica more. BZ is more of the same, with improvements all around. There's more base pieces to build, more customization, more fishes and monsters. Although it feels like there is less to explore here. I think there's the same amount of content, there may even be more than the original (I have 60 hours played vs 49 but I put an extra effort into making my base look pretty rather than functional), but a good portion of it is exploring on-land. A lot more than the original.Now you can traverse land with a buildable hoverbike which, honestly, doesn't feel amazing to control. There is almost a deadzone; a delay between turning left and right, making it feel kind of sluggish.The open snow plains feel pretty boring to explore. There's little to look at and everything looks the same, which leads to getting lost for a long time, and when that's in a place you're not enjoying it only adds salt to the wound. Later on there is a gimmick to the open snow planes that feels REALLY buggy and is more irritating than terrifying. Not to mention a module you can build, which is supposed to help, just straight up doesn't work.Subnautica should stick to what it does best, underwater exploring... Speaking of, the new biomes range from absolutely radical to meh. Maybe the first game made me jaded, but I never felt that absolute fear and dread while exploring that the first game did so well.It also feels like it gives you less direction too. And while I'm all about exploring and finding things for myself, some absolutely vital story-progression items are hidden away hundreds of meters down in a cave that has 100 branching paths and it's in one of them. The game doesn't even mark it for you. I went by a crucial artifact nearly 10 times and only managed to find it by looking it up online.As for good things? The codex entries are fascinating. I've read every single one. The only other game I've done that with is Prey 2017 and the OG Subnautica. The voice acting is superb too and even though they are just disembodied voices, I'd grown attached to every one of them (except Emmanuel, ♥♥♥♥ you, bootlicker).The Sea Truck is a really fun change. I still think it should be called the Sea Bus, but that doesn't sound as cool. The Sea Truck has several modules you can attach to the back trailer-style, and each one makes the thing longer (and slower). Do you choose to be a speedy, narrow vehicle gliding through the water and narrow passageways? Or bring your entire base with you with storage, fabricator and prawn dock modules, complete with its own aquarium?I've already mentioned it, but it's worth repeating. The base building is twice as good. There is so much more room for customization and the large rooms and glass domes add SO much to making your base feel cozy. Also that jukebox stayed on since the moment I built it and learned you could import your own custom music!My OG Subnautica base felt like a place to craft and get work done, but my base in BZ felt like home. Even as I write this I'm thinking of opening the game and just relaxing in the lounge I made and listening to some tunes while I sip coffee in game.The crafting also feels a lot less of a chore. I was excited to build a huge base, and put lots of little meaningless things inside it because the requirements felt so accessible, without devolving into everything feeling like a freebie.Conclusion:Gripes aside, it's still a fantastic game. Even though I think the original is still the better game overall, the game's plot is just as good, if not even better (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that ending is A+). If you just want more Subnautica buy this game even at full price, it's absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a worthy entry to the franchise and is enjoyable to play (once), but obviously can't help but be compared to Subnautica itself and in that comparison it does fall short in places.   It's clear that the intent in Below Zero was to create something tighter, more streamlined and more narrative-driven than Subnautica, but in doing so they managed to strip away a lot of the features that made the original so compelling.   With a smaller map, more linear paths between locations and fewer overall options (in crafting, vehicle choices and even base locations) the game loses some of the sense of open exploration in favor of being guided along to the conclusion of a pair of storylines (discovering the truth behind your sister's death, and discovering the story behind the planet's previous alien inhabitants).   Chasing after the truth of what happened to your sister is the main reason Robin finds herself on the planet in the first place, but the conclusion of that storyline feels hollow and unsatisfying.   In my playthrough I just happened to stumble into the final set piece of that story, clicked a couple of buttons and then was treated to dialog that made it sound like the game was over.    The alien storyline has a more fleshed out conclusion but is also bogged down in the middle by relying on you just stumbling onto a number of locations to move that story along.Many of the biomes and sub-biomes are hidden away down single entry points, narrow tunnels or other easily-overlooked entrances.   More than once I had felt like I'd seen the deepest or most central area of a biome only to wander around for a few hours and eventually find that there was some other path tucked away where the storyline was allowed to continue.    Certain resources (particularly nickel ore) are also annoyingly hidden away in singular small caves and alcoves, easily missed and essential for moving to deeper depths.  I don't enjoy having to rely on wikis to figure out the next step in a game but more than once in Below Zero I found myself faced with a choice of retracing my steps and wasting hours looking in every corner of the map for something I might have missed, or checking on the wiki where I can find a certain resource.  To that end, the map, while relatively small and linear, isn't crafted in a way that naturally leads the player from one area to the next.  Simply following the contours of the terrain and exploring often brings you into dead-ends or the limits of the map itself.   Where Subnautica featured multiple entry points which would eventually converge on key locations deeper down, the map in Below Zero is more segregated with a single way in to most areas that can sometimes be difficult to chance across.The vehicles are a bit more limited as well.  While the trusty Seamoth and Cyclops are replaced by the SeaTruck, which can be customized to an extent with various modules that extend its length and add functionality and fill the overall roles of both vehicles, the penalties for doing so get severe.     While the design of the SeaTruck seems to allow it to be segmented and articulated like an eel, able to weave and flex through the many, many narrow gaps and tight tunnels in the game, it's instead locked in as a rigid pole that gets harder and more frustrating to maneuver through the map as you add modules.    There's a convenient lever to detach the train and use only the more nimble cab for exploring, but at that point it's easier to just climb out and do it in the Prawn exosuit or as a free dive.  The Seatruck then fails to really shine as either a mobile base or an exploration craft, and instead ends up as an unsatisfying compromise between the two.The large number of vehicle upgrades from Subnautica have also been trimmed down in Below Zero, to the point where you never have more upgrade options than available slots in your vehicles.  In fact the Prawn has 4 upgrade slots but I only ever found 3 upgrades to put in it.  The only exception to this is the Prawn's interchangeable tool arms, all of which carried over but just like in the original, I managed the game fine with only a drill arm and the default manipulator hand for the entire playthrough.Lastly, base building is again an essential part of the game where your survival and continued success rely on an ever-expanding list of habitation modules and devices to provide energy, water, grow food and fabricate tools.   However, the small size of the map and the very tight spaces in most of the biomes really mean that you never have to branch out from wherever your first base gets built.    Subnautica really encouraged the player to set up multiple bases around the map and down in the deeps, drawing on a number of various power sources that were available, but Below Zero let me get away with a single base in the shallows that was never more than 1km away from any point on the map I found myself.  I never bothered building a thermal reactor or bioreactor, and indeed a bit of light exploration found me gifted with more premade nuclear fuel rods than I would ever need for the nuclear reactor I did end up making to supplement the solar panels.   The scanner room which I also relied heavily on in Subnautica took a place of significantly less importance in Below Zero, in part because of the vastly reduced resource requirements for crafting and in part because of the lack of anything interesting to scan for.I can recommend this game objectively as being fun and entertaining on its own merits - certainly it's better than 80% of the games on Steam - but with the caveat that if you're only going to buy one game in the Subnautica franchise you'll most likely have a better time with the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Something has happened to this studio since the release of NS2 and Subnautica.In retrospect it is more than a tad ironic that Jonas Botel was just last year gushing about the benefits of early access, player feedback, and incremental testing when the studio can't seem to even finish an obviously half-assed (and full-priced) expansion within the modest time span of several years. There is not nearly enough content. They haven't listened to player feedback with regard to the poor script or the terrible design decisions for player vehicles.As of the time of this writing their last announcement is of a price hike for both this and the original Subnautica, which doesn't seem to tell the same story as Mr. Botel.Having bought this game in EA because of their previously stellar record, it pains me to say that your money is best kept firmly in your wallet.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a snoozefest. The first game was way better. - Voiced protagonist ruins a lot of the tension and dread of feeling alone and isolated. NPCs look terrible (as expected) and don't really add anything to the game. -Story is really boring and feels identical to the first installment. - Subtle hints of leftist propaganda in the voice logs scattered around the game. Doesn't make the game any better, but most people probably won't care. Avoid if that's not your jam. - Biomes are decent at best, but most of the time I found myself really venturing out and exploring yet never finding anything of interest. - Still too many inconsistencies with base building. Although fun, more often than not, base compartments and segments are too large to fit anywhere you try to build them. Sometimes when you try to fabricate a room or compartment and KNOW that there's nothing in the way, the habitat builder tool still marks the blueprint in red - as in: blocked by other environmental objects or mass. This was also an issue in the first game. You'd think they'd have fixed this by now.- For having a voiced protagonist that completely ruins the tension and atmosphere that the first game captured flawlessly and still not offer native multiplayer is a damn shame. How long have we, the community, asked for this feature? Only two really good things about this game are the parts they ported from the first one and the soundtrack. I prefer Simon Chylinski's work, but that doesn't mean BZ's soundtrack isn't good. Ben Prunty does a fine job with what he's handed.Edit: I will add that the trailer was fairly well made, but it certainly does go out of its way to belittle the old, chubby white man. Not that I expected anything less from modern games these days. Double standards are the leftists' specialty after all.

Original has predators that will not only take you out but your vehicles out really quick if you make to many mistakes. This game has ZERO predators that caused me to be like oh crap I am gonna be dead meat (well the first time seeing some it was like that but after you learn they are weak and cant do anything your good...) now and have to restart (which for me adds to the thrill). Took me three deaths in the original before I started be super cautious.  4: Alot of people complained about the Sea Truck speed, I concur. Even with the horse power upgrade it sucks. I think I COULD approve of this game if they somehow were able to add the new items to the original game... like new buildings and ships and stuff. Then I could play the original again with the new stuff haha.

All of them are applied differently, which makes this a new exploration and worthwile, especially if you played the first version.Love the game.That said, I will not spend as much time with this game as with the first Subnautica. _childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I have a hard time recommending Below Zero to anyone except the most hardcore Subnautica fans. The whole game has so many downright strange design decisions, and compared to it's incredible predecessor I can't help but feel like it's a bit of a disappointment.-In the original game, you were alone. Everyone on your ship is dead, and your one chance of escape was detonated in front of you. The only voice you're allowed to hear outside of the data logs of your dead friends is a cold, unfeeling AI (at least up until the very end). In Below Zero, a few hours in you'll always have AL-AN chilling in your subconscious. The main character talks too, and she's... just incredibly unlikable. After awhile, her dialogue lines really started to grate on me. The weirdest part is this wasn't a problem in early builds! She used to actually talk like a human being with emotions, and bounced off AL-AN and her sister pretty well. A shame they butchered her character in the full release.-The ocean was vast and terrifying in Subnautica. Everything felt unknown and scary. In Below Zero, the map is tiny, and it's very rare I actually got unnerved by anything. Now, I wouldn't have a problem with the smaller map if they put that development time into making the sea much more densely packed and interesting, but instead, they focused on the Arctic, which ended up releasing as a broken, unfinished mess of an aboveground area. I have no idea how they did it, but they somehow managed to make a HOVERBIKE not fun to use. It's almost impressive.-Speaking of vehicles and not being fun, that applies to all of them. The zippy Seamoth has been replaced with the slow, bulky Seatruck, which while a cool concept just isn't fun to actually pilot. They also completely ruined the Prawn Suit Grappling Hook, as for some reason they decided chaining grapple boosts to zip across the landscape at (reasonably) fast speeds was just *too fun*, and patched that out. Despite the world being so much smaller it takes an artificially long time to travel from point A to point B due to these changes. In Subnautica it wasn't often I had to face one direction and hold down the W key for longer than a minute, but in Below Zero it happened *frequently*.-Also, despite being much smaller, the world manages to be much more confusing somehow. Incredibly useful blueprints are stuck in very obscure positions, important areas can be easily missed if you're not poking into every crack in the terrain, and fragments can get incredibly annoying to find (there were several occasions where I'd spend upwards of an hour searching for one or two fragments despite already being in the biomes they spawned inside).-I'm not going to get into the story, but... I really don't understand what they were thinking.It really sucks that this game turned out like this, as there's still glimmers of Subnautica in there, deep down. The environments are beautiful, and areas like the Tree Spires and Twisty Bridges really have that mysterious, beautiful charm of the first game. Unfortunately, that charm never lasted long, as instead of focusing on those areas the game spends far too much forcing you into the terrible Arctic sections and prodding you towards the next goal of the complete mess of a story it has.If you really, really, REALLY loved Subnautica, and are willing to look past this game's flaws just to get something close to it, then sure, I'd recommend Below Zero. I genuinely do think it has some good aspects, but they are greatly overshadowed by the flaws. Otherwise, just play (or replay!) the first game, it's leagues better.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun enough. It feels anemic compared to the first game. We got some cool new stuff like the arctic areas, but for the most part it just has less story, less things to unlock and build, less to explore, less leviathans, less to keep me interested. The first game is fantastic and I 110% recommend it, but this one is more like a 70%. It's good enough but it feels more like a DLC than a full sequel; it feels like this is going backwards. Had this game released first, followed by the original, I would've been impressed by the improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 game feels uninspired compared to the first "subnautica". Art design is still very pretty, but the story has been jumbled around a lot and some SJW stuff got mixed in. There is an extensive LAND area in this ocean based game that you have to slog through per the plot. Its all white, not very interesting to look at  with frequent white-out snowstorms that make it impossible to see. Don't bother with this, this game should have been a DLC to Subnautica, not marketed as a new game. Its not different enough from the original to be interesting and the stuff they did change changed it for the worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great DLC, feels almost like a game. It is amazingly beautiful and calm. Like with the original game, sometimes i just swim around and stare at everything. Alan is adorable, Robin is funny, Margery is so badass. One bad thing is that the enemies are annoying, not scary. All of them have a crashfish vibe.Spoilers ahead! I love how this game is so colorful, but the story is nuts. A mega corporation planned to harvest a space rabies to use it to get more money (even though they own ♥♥♥♥♥ solar systems). Your sister worked for them and then, all of a sudden, decided that she dislikes what she is doing, committed some crimes and died (talking all her colleges with her). Your job is to investigate her death (by committing some crimes yourself) with 0 equipment or skills. You go to this weird planet, almost crush, almost get eaten a couple of times. Then you find a giant talking green cube with an alien dude inside it. This dude "misunderstands" you, gets into your head LITERALLY, tells you how he probably took out his whole species, but the only option of winning the game is to go with him to some unknown planet on his small ship with no door. Great. Ahh, by the way, you can leave even without investigating your sister's death or healing a giant half unfrozen infectious corpse that can take down the whole planet;s eco-system.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to echo what some of the top reviews said: this game is excellent until the mid game. Once you are really starting to get into it the story dies off and you realize that you've basically already explored most of the biomes. The above-ground exploration was surprisingly boring, so much so that I basically looked up how to finish the 2 parts of the quest that were there. I has just unlocked the "best food in the game", yet I literally didn't need it cause the story was wrapping up so quick. The snowy terrain just wasn't that interesting to explore. As far as crafting and base-building goes, there are a lot of options. You can design your base to be all pretty and sustainable but there is really not practical motivation to. If you're the kind of person that likes to design an underwater sea base alone on an alien planet, go for it. Me? I'd rather play The Sims for that. This game mainly left me thinking: couldn't they have done more? More biomes, more quest? I still had a great time, but by the end I pretty much couldn't wait to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is the game is worse than the original, especially the environments and the vehicles. I'd say it's still worth it, but it is disappointing. When I finished, I didn't have the desire to go back and build and explore, which is a major let-down.Subnautica is one of my favorite games of all time, and I would go back and start a new story anytime. Below zero is an experience I'm somewhat glad I had, but it does not hold a candle to the original. If you plan to buy this game, do not set your expectations too high and you'll be satisfied enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Altogether, it is a downgraded version of the original. I enjoyed all the new quality-of-life equipment, like the Mineral Detector and the new base modules, like the Control Room. The new underwater biomes are great to explore and visually look distinguished. However, the land potions of the game are terrible. All the new vehicles feel awful to operate (especially the Snow Fox) and have less specialized purposes than the originals. The story is not engaging and uninteresting. There is an entertaining game here, but everything enjoyable was accomplished better in the original. I only recommend the game to people who love the original and can look past the many flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Subnautica: Below Zero, as it is pretty nice game. Especially for new players that haven't played the first Subnautica yet (and aren't biased by it like I am). I can't deny that the first game is far more superior though. Below Zero is a fun game if you like exploration, survival and building games. However for a bigger challenge and a more immersive world, I recommend Subnautica instead.Subnautica: Below Zero starts in a similar way as its predecessor. You crash on planet 4546B and try to survive. The difference is, this time you have a more story-driven gameplay. Where in the previous Subnautica, you had to pretty much explore and listen to your radio to progress. In below zero you will be constantly guided where you have to go next.Could contain some spoiler about the gameplay itself, but not the story.+ There is an interesting story and the game is pretty immersive.+ Lots of different creatures to scan and PDA entries to discover.+ Beautiful area to explore.+ New buildings and also some familiar ones (if you played the first one).+ New and fun vehicles, such as the seatruck and snowfox.+ I love how you can expand the seatruck to be like a mobile base.- I was carrying around the prawn suit, but I hardly ever had to use it. Could have used it, but I didn't and didn't have to. Which makes it feel like an unnecessary vehicle.- While still immersive I felt like something was missing. You encounter the same creatures almost everywhere and I hardly got the feeling that there was a lot of diversity in the different areas. For example, you encounter the squidshark almost everywhere in the sea. And on land you encounter the snow stalker everywhere. This is probably due to the map being quite small.- I did have a few minor bugs, that were a little annoying while playing. But nothing game   breaking.- Much shorter than the previous one. Was able to finish in 35 hours. Probably could have   been even shorter if I didn't mess around as much as I did. The map is also pretty small,   especially compared to the first game.- I felt like the seatruck was a replacement for the cyclops and seamoth in one vehicle. Seeing   as how small the map is this wasn't too bad. But there is no hit detection anywhere on the   seatruck. Which makes you bump into everything, if an area becomes too narrow.- The leviathans are underwhelming. Where I would seriously feel terror, when I heard a   reapers or ghost leviathans cry. The leviathans in this game feel very underwhelming and   almost docile. Sure they would attack you, but it just wasn't that impressive. Also the fact   that there are very few of them and that they have smaller sizes really takes away the terror   that reapers instilled.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: After only 3 hours it is clear to me, that this game lost everything that made the first part great: The underwater world is way to constructed and artifically colourful to unfold any kind of lasting atmosphere. The constant droning of way to frequent, annoyingly long and quite frankly uninteresting audiologs contributes to the same factor as well as making sure you never feel alone, while the feeling of being alone was to me one of the factors that really drove said lasting atmosphere of the first game home. The first game was a masterclass in how reduced design makes a world feel natural & believable - after all reality isn't constructed to be visually entertaining either - just to be all the more intense when you break that scheme at the end to slowly lead the player into very otherwordly setpieces. This game on the other hand is a perfect negative example of how turning up everything to eleven constantly nets you a sum of enjoyability below zero.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: - There are some nice QoL changes and the game expects you to have played Subnautica;- It is set in a smaller (but denser) map. It also adds significant land content, which a lot of players are more ambivalent about (I personally prefer the aquatic sections - We are playing these games for that content - but did overall enjoy it and did not find it to overstay its welcome);- Warmth mechanic on land that, to be fair, lacks weight;- The game is gorgeous;- I found it much easier and less scary than its predecessor: Easier access to consumables and recipes from the beginning, and less open waters populated with large predators (that are not as dangerous, despite BZ not having a stasis rifle), aka less thassalophobia;- The main vehicle of this game is the sea truck. Its highlight is that it is a mix between the Seamoth and the Cyclops in the way that you can attach modular compartments that fill various roles.Overall a pleasant and more dense experience. I try to take the game for what it is and not compare it too much to Subnautica (even though I did that a lot here). I enjoyed my adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: First thing i would recomend if you havent already is to play Subnautica 1. In my oponion one of the most unique games ever created,i loved every minute of it...Now mooving on to Below zero i have mixed feelings,the game is still beautifull but in my opinion feels a lot smaller than subnautica 1,it just doesnt feel like theres that much to explore and ended up rushing to end the story because i felt like id explored the map one two many times.i think the devs should have worked on making more/deeper biomes than reworking the story,all in all i rate Below zero 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to Subnautica, although you might also think of it as stand-alone DLC.It's certainly large enough to be thought of as a sequel, clocking in at around 20-30 hours depending on how lost you get and how much exploration you want to do, but I certainly think I got my monies worth. The area of planet 4546B you explore is a bit smaller than the first game, but there's still tons to explore and find.The Buildings are mostly the same as before, but with a few new additions. The Cyclops submarine and Seamoth are both gone, replaced by the modular Seatruck instead. It's a nifty idea that works well enough for the region you're in. I miss the Cyclops a bit but it really wouldn't fit through all the small passages here anyway, so it's not a big loss.Speaking of... prepare to go free-swimming through loads of tight caves this time around, the 3D-map of the Seaglide is actually useful now. While navigating without it is doable, you're bound to miss stuff if you always keep it off. Fortunately, oxygen during these free-diving jaunts is much less of an issue than in the original with the addition of oxygen producing flora conveniently scattered around the caves.There is a bigger focus on story this time around as well, with the protagonist speaking both to herself and others. While you're heavily incentivized to do your own exploring to push the story forward, you also rather quickly find a map you help you navigate. While it's only a PDA entry and not an automap feature, you'll still find yourself referencing it repeatedly.As many have said, it's not quite as good as the original, but that's more a testament to that game's greatness than anything else. Below Zero is still very good, and if you enjoyed the first one then you'll probably enjoy this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Small Subnautica 1 spoilers in this review.I don't know if its impressive or not, that almost everything I liked about the first Subnautica has been stripped out. All the mystery, discovering things for yourself, the eventual base building to getting the Cyclops which essentially became your customisable mobile base, are just not as well implemented or as profound as the first game.I must mention first how jarring it was to hear the protagonist speak - vs Sub1 where you were Gordon Freeman style silent, you talk out loud, a lot. I mean the voice actress is an incredible talent (Kimberly Brooks, AKA Ashley Williams in the Mass Effect series) but it didn't fit with the style of game for me at all.What makes Sub1 so good is the feeling of isolation, loneliness and the quiet peaceful sea and what lurked beneath. No one to talk to, listening to audio logs. It was like it was yourself making sense of the world. Whereas here, we have a voice who pretty much tells you what to think or how to react... I mean I get it, probably a bigger budget than the first game, get a talented voice actor to do some lines... a more 'fleshed out' storyline and characters... but as I said, I personally didn't like it.Mystery - When Sub1 starts you know nothing of the world. Who Alterra are, who you are, what you're doing. This is trickle fed to you as the game progresses with plot and non-plot important 'log files' that you find from other survivors - a kind of story telling I've loved since System Shock. Then there is the whole alien aspect and the lore behind why the planet is the way it is which was interesting. Below Zero removes most of this - I accept, we're gonna know who Alterra are at the start of the second game, of course, and yes there are log files but it's all very overt and obvious. You don't need to connect any dots as its all done for you. This on top of the protagonist talking and reacting to stuff spoilt the experience I had in Sub1.Discovering things for yourself - I think within an hour of the game I had roughly 10 waypoints the story had driven me towards. In Sub1 the story didn't progress until you answered the radio, where you'd receive a waypoint to another potential survivor - and even then you may have struggled to 'get' to that location. In Below Zero it feels much more rail-roaded that you're gonna get all these waypoints and you need to go to them all at some point but it doesn't really matter when. I think this could be better... let the player discover some areas through exploration, or other means like a clue that leads you from one thing to another then another. Pulling a thread. Sub1 was not perfect in this aspect, but it felt more natural - for example one of the life pods happened to be near a cave system that was initially difficult to access... piquing your interest, do you risk going down or not early or wait and prepare properly? None of this in Below Zero at all - the way points are the story points. This is poor game-story-pacing, imo.Base Building - Yes, actually this is largely the same. There are some new additions like the Control Room which is quite cool though.Cyclops - It's gone! And I'm upset. I can see why they removed it given Below Zero is 'smaller' and more vertical in size... the size of the Cyclops would have been too big. But gone is the customisable home with the quirky 'wElCoMe aBoArD CaPtAiN' voice.... So what do we get instead - the Sea Truck. Quite possibly the dullest vehicle imaginable. No honky horn. Can't turn the engines on and off, or the interior lights like my 'ol beloved Cyclops. What we can do is attach modular 'trailers' to it, like a storage trailer, a sleep trailer, a fish tank trailer - making your Sea Truck into this long, difficult to maneuver stick in the icy depths. It's really disappointing if I'm honest.World - There is much more land, and even a land vehicle called the Snowfox, which is really unpleasant to ride. Janky and breaks really easily. Exploring land was quite fun though. There is a new survival mechanic to manage: 'heat' which, like food and water, is fairly trivial and not exactly difficult - but I imagine in a perma-death play through you might have to pack a few warm salads for.Underwater the world is much more vertical, as mentioned - but its also more 'alien' - perhaps too much to begin with. In Sub1 you started in the 'shallows' - fairly Earth-relatable coral area, pretty and safe. In Below Zero we start in a safe place but its very cosmic right off the bat. This makes the later areas less impactful because you've 'kinda seen sh1t' already. Just another example of poor game-pacing to be honest.On a final note; The addition of 'air' plants was not a great idea... it made early exploration a little too easy. Once you get a larger tank it pretty much means infinite air underway which in my mind is against the whole idea.I probably sound quite harsh, but I am recommending this. It's still Subnautica game loop. It's still pretty well made. It's still about deep water and taking risks at times. Large enemies that are much more aggressive... in fact everything is more aggressive than Sub1... so yeah its still alright but I'm also really kinda gutted they went this way with the series as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I've enjoyed the game. It's a little more challenging than the first Subnautica, because the locations of crafting materials are at different depths, and one has to relearn locations for previously common items. This is not a complaint in the slightest sense, it's just an example of one of the things to be expected from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Another incredible entry into the rich universe being created for Subnautica. Some huge improvements already in the alpha from Subnautica are far more fluid, smooth movements of creatures and entities in the Eco system, the incredible addition of the large landmass, and the actual personality given to the main character supported by her communication with other entities and people. I definitively feel more immersed in Below Zero than I did in Subnatuica. The exciting exploration aspect is there with the suspenseful discoveries and dangers is back and better than ever. I can't wait to see how the end product improves the already thriving gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game, from the looks to the feel is absolutely great. I haven't been able to take my hands off in the past few days!The map is smaller, but much more interactive and fleshed out, than Subnautica's. It is beautiful, with much more to do, see, and explore vertically. Not to mention, the land sections have been overhauled compared to the jankiness of Subnautica!The story is amazing. I don't want to spoil any of it, but it's not spoonfed and it's also not Dark Souls level of "Find it out yourself." It's a nice inbetween!Base building is even better than before. I never built a super elaborate base in the first Subnautica, but I couldn't help myself this time when I could practically make myself a palace.This game is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Based on what I've seen so far (trying not to see too much) I'm excited for this game to reach final release. I am doing what I did with the first game - I play a little bit when it's in it's early iterations, and then I don't touch it until it's finished. But I still check the developer updates to see where things are going.The one thing I would REALLY like to see is some cross over between the two games for new/updated content. If we cannot have Robyn or the new buildings/vehicles in the original Subnautica, then maybe give us access to the old map (without story content) in Below Zero so that we can update some old base builds with the new fun stuff.Excited to see where this goes!
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the resource gathering, base building, survival aspect of the original Subnautica then you'll probably enjoy this game. However, if you're main reason for liking Subnautica was the diverse biomes and how vibrant the game feels sometimes then you may not want to play this game. The biomes are often bleak and uninteresting, and the only biome really comparable to the original is the tree spires, which the game never requires you to go to
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Too much differed beyond what made Subnautica great. Lots of gameplay bugs still, lot of cut content (things like the backup camera for the janky Seatruck, or the stasis rifle), story is pretty weak (probably from completely overhauling the story 3/4ths of the way through development which only made it marginally better) and the voiced protagonist detracts rather than adds to the overall game quality.Fauna AI seems to have lost a lot of aggressiveness in the bigbois, never once did I feel threatened besides the Ghost Leviathans in the Crystal caverns. And then those were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ due to constant locking on to you if they see you from 200 meters away, not moving, no lights, nothing to draw attention to you.The playable area without including the boring, buggy, and annoying gigantic land section, is really bland and small. Solid 1/3rd to 1/2 is just boring sparse generic arctic areas. Sea Monkeys tend to be all over the place too, due to the small underwater play area, greatly increasing their annoying presence.The overland section is entirely too large for how uninteresting it is. There just isn't really much of a reason to explore there, while constantly fighting either the Ice Worm, the terrain in a prawn, or the cold on foot. Requiring a special full suit just to not have to worry about the cold is also quite annoying. The Snowfox was pretty useless all things considered. Still deal with cold, but the terrain becomes even harder to deal with. The only real use for it would be dealing with the Ice Worm, but tbh the prawn does well enough with some buggy grapple-jumping at worst.I could go on for a bunch more but its honestly just not worth the effort. Just like this game isn't worth buying anywhere near full price. Might be worth 10, maybe could recommend it as just something to continue the subnautica feel a bit at 5.But overall, I'd say don't bother.Oh, and ♥♥♥♥ whoever decided to make the PDA voice so annoying and heavily accented. The original was great, no reason to change it.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, good balance of survival, crafting/base building, and story-driven exploration. One cannot describe how uncomfortable you feel in the deep, dark ocean when you can hear a large leviathan somewhere off in the distance ready to devour you but it's night time so you can't see 3 feet in front of you.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: If you want more Subnautica, here it is. Most of the same mechanics are present along with some new stuff. Also, performance is better - no pop-in or stutter - though overall it might be a little more demanding (though I think that stuff might have finally been fixed in the original game). Also, texture quality is significantly improved and crisp. Also, being able to pin recipes to the HUD is a major quality of life improvement that they need to back-port to the original game. The Apocalyptic Log trope is still used extensively but it's a bit more compelling since you're actually trying to figure out what happened and it's not all just filler.Potential things you'll see people complain about:1) The on-land parts. Personally, I think adding more land areas was a mistake. But it's worth suffering through them to play the rest of the game. You can kinda cheese most of it using the tank-like Prawn anyway.2) I wasn't sure at first about shifting from a silent, Gordon Freeman style protagonist to a specific, voiced character. But it works and I've enjoyed the story. And honestly the whole silent protagonist trope is pretty worn out. People saying they "can't relate" to a voiced character apparently don't play any other videogames since that's like... most of them. 3) The Sea Truck. A lot of people prefer the Seamoth/Cyclops combo (Prawn is still available). While I wish the Seamoth was still an *option*, the Sea Truck is a practical vehicle for this game and there are places the Cyclops just wouldn't work due to depth being too shallow or spaces being too tight.I think Below Zero was originally intended as a sort of "stand alone expansion" but it feels as big as the original game to me. While the world is a bit smaller, there's more to do in it, and a lot more story to enjoy. If you have played neither game I do suggest playing the original first. I'd still rate it slightly higher, and Below Zero by design has spoilers for the original game since it partly continues that backstory.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica was one of the best games i have ever played, and when they announced subnautica BZ I was probably the most hyped i have ever been for a game! but... when it came out and i played it through I felt it was missing a certain mystical feeling that the first subnautica reveled in! as I've played it more I realized that the biggest thing bringing it down is that it has too much STORY. hear me out, in the first subnautica  BUT the new subnautica intro immediately introduces you two 3 voiced characters, and it also establishes that we already know the name and history of the planet we're landing on.  I really wish they handled the story as carefully as they did in the first game.I don't hate this game and i truly wish that it could improve :/ 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure it's no surprise, but if you liked the original Subnautica you'll like this one too. It's basically more of the same, which for a game like this isn't a bad thing in the slightest. However, I will say that it feels like a bit of a step down - like the Borderlands Pre-Sequel to 2, where it probably would've felt better as DLC instead of its own standalone thing.Part of it's just the chosen biome spread, but Below Zero's world feels a lot smaller and less rich and "alive" than the original Subnautica. There's not as many crazy, creepy ocean things to explore, not as much variety in what's going on, and even though the new and different leviathan designs are all fantastic and I love seeing them, they don't have as much staying power as the ones from the original - although the Chelicerate, in my opinion, may take the cake from the Reapers for being the scariest. Oops!Below Zero is good, but it's definitely not -as- good as the original Subnautica. If you're looking for an entry point and don't know whether to choose this one or the other, then I can tell you, definitely go for the original first.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, not as great as the first but still enjoyable!the story is alright, nothing too greatthe gameplay is like the first game, but its still a chore having to find out where to go, even more so in this part 2.also i have to mention some things are really not needed, like upgrading your seatruck to have about 5 compartmentsor a big energyreactor, placing 2 tiny things on your roof is often enough power.it would have been cool if there were more places on land to explore and not constantly freeze to death,also the snowfox could have been more useful, like i said a lot of items were really not neededi also barely had to use the propulsion cannonthe story is around 30 hours long which is fine.all in all, you get what you are looking for which is a sequel to the first and on that the game delivers.however it feels more like a DLC more than anything.i would rate the game 7/10enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I've started several times in this game; it's always enjoyable. My style is slow motion, taking my time to explore and sight-see, as the story unfolds and discoveries increase the ability to build things in the game or find more clues to unfold more of the story. I'm really glad the game has the option to play Survival mode but without the food/water challenges. When I played pure Survival, I got annoyed very quickly with how often one had to stop and deal with gathering food/water. Not so bad later in the game after you discover technologies that help with that, but early on, it's a pain. Highly recommend this game...it's a visual delight and fun gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Much worse than the original. Looks like the developers have deliberately threw out everything that was cool to add new stuff. The thing is, new things are lame. Cyclops and Seamoth are unavailable. Instead, we have the Seatrack, which is tragically slow and generally uninteresting. Prawn is available but not needed. I have not used it once. You find the ingredients needed for it to be useful at the end of the game, when you don't need it anymore, and besides, there are no places where the seatruck cannot reach easier. We spend a large part of the game on the surface. And that's the worst part of the game. Most of the time you can't see anything because it's either raining, snowing, hail or fog, and the creatures living there are irritating and uninteresting. It feels like the surface part is there to make the game unnaturally stretched and therefore the story is boring. I've waited so long for this game and I'm definitely disappointed.
