_childDocuments_.review: Smaller in size than its predecessor, some of the most enjoyable transit mechanics of the previous game had to be slowed down for this one.  No fast and manoeuvrable seamoth, slower seaglide and no need for a large mobile base like a Cyclops in a map that trades real estate for close biome density.  Instead you get a vehicle option that, of necessity, is a poor amalgam of the Seamoth and Cyclops without the standout virtues of either.  If your Prawn suit could swing across large sections of the map like it could with the cable attachment in the previous game you'd quickly see how little real estate your're working with here.  The chilling surface biome is an interesting addition but unfortunately it's climate and wildlife hazards are completely trivialised by the existence of the Prawn suit. Combine that with a disjointed, unconnected two-plot narrative and some fully animated and voiced characters that don't seem to serve a meaningful purpose and I found the overall experience to be less enjoyable than the first outing.  That said, it's probably still a decent game if you haven't played the first one and the overall aesthetics are still top notch.

_childDocuments_.review: SBZ is a solid effort at taking Subnautica and giving the fans a reason to return to 4546B and learn more about the original aliens in a round-a-bout way using another story of a woman trying to find out about the fate of her sister. The underwater locations, fauna and flora are again top-notch with a wide variety but with some familiar ones returning. In my opinion, gripes about the PDA voice are unwarranted. First off, you only hear it when you're in trouble, and in the beginning, with a small tank, you're always getting warnings, so while I can understand this gets annoying, I feel that people are annoyed because they can't find the larger tanks or the blueprint for the seatruck. Because once you attain those, the PDA voice is largely gone.I really liked the story and all the side stories you find on PDA's that fill in what living with a small cadre of people must have felt like. The larger story and ultimate arc is with the alien though, and this was done very nicely. I felt that it extended the experience from the original Subnautica, making this a true "part 2" of the story and it greatly satisfied many of the questions I had from the original Subnautica. Kudo's to the story & writers on this. Note: I do have a small nitpick that I somehow missed what became of everyone and it would have been nice to find the cave where Sam met her end. The new seatruck is fine and the ability to add-on modules, while interesting, didn't give me a lot of reason to use many of them. The storage and docking module are must-haves and serve a more nimble purpose in SBZ because it has to be. And this is where my gripes start coming into play. I felt that the game relies too much on mazes and very complicated tunnels and tight spaces, in what I can only characterize as really trying to disorient the player. So whereas the original Subnautica had larger areas that were distinct, SBZ is far more complicated with tight constrained areas, with many paths that are very confusing, and when you get into these tunnel areas, the term house of mirrors comes to mind as I felt continually lost. Nothing/everything seemed familiar to the point where I just gave up. The land based activities were too long, too large and in my opinion, far more complicated than the underwater environment because you frequently have so little visibility and when you do, every chunk of ice looks the same. Without a map, this is very difficult to navigate and I was constantly disoriented. I  came to loathe any forays onto land it was a POI on land that I finally resorted to a youtube to find a location because I grew so frustrated with this portion of the game. I would estimate that this comprises a solid 6-8 hours of the 25 hours it took me to complete the game and therefore sullies my overall impression of the game. When I finished the original Subnautica, I immediately started a replay and I have hundreds of hours and over 10 replays. Right now, the only reason I would replay this would be to explore a bit more and to rush the land portions and to be honest, it's not on my top-10 list of things to do in the gaming moment right now. So, I think SBZ was a worthy effort, I enjoyed my time with it, but there is no way it compares to the original Subnautica. Does that make it a bad game? No, I believe this is a good game, but just because it doesn't reach quite as far or quite as good as the original, I would still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: My original review was negative, as many others were as well. HOWEVER... seeing the resounding hard work the team has put in to addressing all the backlash from its beloved players once again rockets Unknown Worlds to the top of my favorite devs list once again. Not only have almost all the gripes about the cringe-worthy early preview builds been fixed, but they said, "Oh wow, they're really not happy," and ripped out and revamped the story all together.1. Similar (not same) feel to the original with a more structured story. Sure, best I can tell, you're not totally in the dark (if that's what you prefer) like in the original, but as opposed to the early days of this game, it no longer holds your hand and can be very unforgiving. I can only surmise that this will get worse (in the BEST way for us as players!)2. Weather adds a profoundly interesting and different experience... Surely if they intend to roll out this mechanic they're keeping it secret, but, tides/currents would be super awesome.3. The annoying conversation between sisters has been removed and at least one of the voice actresses was replaced, which is great because the new one sounds more appropriate and less bubbly. _childDocuments_.review: Have you played Subnautica 1 before? If not, go play that now. It is a better game all-around.Below Zero is okay, on the whole. If you liked the first one, you'll probably like Below Zero and will get a good 20-30 hours out of it easily. But the thing that made Subnautica 1 great was that you truly felt alone, stuck on a world full of water, with nowhere to go but deeper below. The sense of isolation was remarkable.With Below Zero, we now have characters that directly talk with our own character and so that feeling of isolation - probably the best thing about Subnautica - is simply removed entirely. Then tack on the questionable idea of an above water area that is far too large and difficult to navigate and it just falls a bit flat. I have been playing this from very early in the beta and it is unfortunate because the feedback on the above water area was all there from the start. The story I am more forgiving on as they did change writers mid-way through the game. But one wonders what game we could have had if they had spent more time building out the underwater parts of the map (the map is fairly small) instead of re-doing voice acting work multiple times and designing a large above ground area that is nothing but aggravating for the player to be in.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica was a very awe-striking. Below Zero? Its about 76% of what Subnautica was.TL;DR: The game is good but you shouldn't compare it to Subanutica 1.For the record, I played the game as much as possible to get the entire experience. Ranging from scanning anything possible, to the story, and to visiting the new biomes the game introduces. I managed to finish the game in 36 hours. Almost half the time as the first Subnautica 1(64 hours).Conclusion? Don't go into the game expecting to get the same experience as Subnautica 1.Lets start with the con:-The game has a so-and-so story. -The game has way too much content cut. Various events and an entire biome have been abandoned or removed.-Even though there is a story, I had no idea how much I was progressing.-Exploring the land segments of the game felt underwhelming. Again, contents were cut.The above does not mean the game is completely bad,Now that the bad parts are done-Lets start with the pros:-Right off the bat-and I mean LITERALLY- the game is so colorful and has vibrant biomes. I am not even playing on the highest settings and was still blown away. Existing in that environment are brand new fauna and flora. The design of the animals in this game is quite intriguing and vibrant.-At some point in the game there is a partner you get to meet and they join you for a rest of the game. Said partner brings more life to the story. To meet this partner you have to  I recommend letting this partner join you as soon as possible.-The game's fear focus still exists but it is completely driven away by the beauty of the environment.  After all the above. It is essential that you realize you shouldn't completely compare Below Zero to Subnautica 1.Below Zero as a game is amazing, but as a predecessor, its meh.I was heavily absorbed in the colorfulness of the ecosystem to judge anything else.Map is kind of small and the design of the leviathans is not as scary due to the fear factor of the game being heavily reduced by the developers. The game has its own charming experience.(By the way. I remember seeing reviews before hand stating that the temperature system of the game is bad. I never died of hypothermia in the game. There are various things available that balance this.)Conclusion: Don't go into Below Zero expecting the same experience as Subnautica 1. HOWEVER, give the game the benefit of the doubt because I believe the pros make it worth the buy.Just buy it at like 30% off if you are really not sure its worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Original Subnautica is much better, but this game is still solid. Slight spoilers for original Subnautica and some in game mechanics ahead.I didn't really like how the character you play as talks, and there's a bit too much dialogue for a new Subnautica. I thought that it was amazing how the original Subnautica didn't have to rely on dialogue exposure, how it told its story more subtly. Subnautica had a lot of story even though there were barely any voice lines other than the PDA. Everything was more mysterious and I preferred it that way. In Below Zero, it kinda ruins the charm of the original game when it just flat out tells you everything that's going on and where you need to go. That's also something you don't get with Below Zero, the true sense of being lost and in fear. All the hostile leviathans in Subnautica were terrifying but in Below Zero, they're such pushovers, I barely feel like my life is on the line when I encounter one.The main gameplay is basically the same, however they added a temperature mechanic which is neat. It makes you manage your time more on land. The biggest issue with this mechanic I have is that there are way too many ways to get your temperature bar up to full, I have only died one time of hypothermia and that was because I wasn't paying attention, it's very easily avoided.Subnautica Below Zero lost a lot of the charm the original had, but I'd still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I should have known better from this developer. Warning: if you plan on using a controller for this game, your buttons/on-screen prompts will be bugged. Specifically, the game will instruct you to press LT when it's actually RT, and vise versa. Remapping any of the controller buttons seems to either revert instantly or break other functions. I'm willing to bet my left nut that it'll never get fixed, either.Now, considering the unique niche this game sits in, I might be bothered to tinker with settings/mods/tweaks until I found a solution. But then I remembered my experience with Subnautica 1, IT HAD THE SAME ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ISSUES!!!! This is a problem that plagued the first game and the developers either couldn't give a ♥♥♥♥ to fix it OR they loved trolling controller users so much that they happily carried the bug over to their sequel. I'm baffled.Then I remembered how I dumped 40+ hours into Subnautica 1 (even suffering through controller bugs) but couldn't finish due to a different game-breaking glitch. _childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I didn't like Below Zero at first.  It lacks for me some of that *drive* that makes Subnautica so different from most survival crafting games: You have a goal, and the clues and resources that further that goal feed into one another, right up until the end.  And the end rules.  When has that ever happened for a survival sim?Below Zero is doing something different, in tone and narrative.  I'm not sure all of it works, but the bones of the game are still here, with new and interesting problems to solve, and QoL improvements to the crafting and construction compared to the original.  Exploration is still rewarding, it's just less elegant than Subnautica in pointing where to go next.  Because of that, I can't recommend it OVER the original, but as a Standalone DLC for people who have already mastered Subnautica, it still has a lot to offer.  There are enough original and interesting scenarios to scratch that novel exploration itch.  Honestly, they could just make new maps and new framing stories in this vein several more times and I'd be eager to play more.  Not as tightly constructed or harrowing as the original, but worth a go if you want more Subnautica.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not that this game is bad: it's that it's everything that the original Subnautica is, but just less all around. Less well balanced, worse writing, etc., as well as having all the weaknesses of the original (e.g., how the wonderful thalassophobic sense of peril at the beginning of the game isn't replaced by anything else as you become comfortable in the sea in the late game). So why play this game when you could just play the original?The one major new thing is, of course, the ability to go above ground. This is a great concept: you have the same basic mechanic of only being able to be away from your safe home for a little while (hypothermia replaces drowning), but now you have to navigate a 2-D environment instead of a 3-D one, which should open up new dangers and opportunities. Unfortunately, this part of the game was just not thought through that well: for example, I couldn't read the ice worms' signals, so they weren't scary so much as confusing; or again, my hoverbike thing got damaged randomly and without feedback, which again turned what should have been a sense of peril into something just annoying and confusing.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a strange one to review as I've come straight from finally playing deep into Subnautica.This is probably the starting point which makes more sense for new players. It is more story driven than the original and feels more restricted, in room to explore, in spite of also having some areas on dry land to visit. Where this falls a little is that the story handholds til it doesn't and you're left going back to aimlessly exploring (or googling locations if that suits better) to find the item which triggers further progression. The original's event driven narrative worked better for me in providing the loose framework for the exploration.It's perfectly ok as a game, some exceptionally minor texture issues are the only issues I've had so far, but I can understand those who were hoping for the original's breadth being a little disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Following on from the hundreds of hours I sunk into Subnautica, the idea of a sequel terrified me as much as it excited me. If you came to the reviews to see if Below Zero was like the first Subnautica, I'll make it quick: Below Zero's narrative shifts tightens its focus on Robin, your avatar in this frozen hellscape. Unlike Ryley, Robin has thoughts and feelings and desires. She exhibits fear and responds to the world, often without your input. The more I played, the more I found that it didn't diminish the experience at all. It was just different to what I was expecting after the first Subnautica. Let it get its hooks in you and there's a personal story within Below Zero. In Subnautica, I always wondered about the lives and exploits of the voices we hear over the many PDAs we find. The lifepod survivors and the Degasi crew. In Below Zero, I felt like I was living one of those smaller stories.Can you still slack off and built amazing bases? Absolutely! The base building feels even more satisfying in Below Zero; with so many more options for customising your base to your liking. Even the above ground bases are worthwhile in many areas!My return to 4546b was incredible. I felt like I was coming home, but someone had redecorated while I was gone.

_childDocuments_.review: Below Zero is very, very different from Subnautica 1 and feels like more like DLC rather than a sequel, that is not a criticism. Below Zero provides more story elements which takes away from the isolation from the first game, All leviathans (except the smallest, most common one)  are less scary than the first game even if you have no clue what the creatures are or where they are found during your first play-through, you're reaction will be similar to "what is that" then after encourtering it again that reaction becomes "oh it's you again", from a biological perspective (i'm a biology student who is studying marine biology at the moment) the land based portions of the game makes no sense as there is little food for the carnivores to survive on unless they can swim (which they might but most likely not") or if they were closer to the water and able to catch prey from near icy shores.Criticisms aside, this game looks 3x better than the first, the introduction of weather mechanics feels very natural and enhances the atmosphere of the game, although there are less creatures, each creature feels 1.5x to 2x more detailed than those in the previous title (except for the Reapers, obviously), each biome feels very unique and beautiful whilst also being unnerving, and that's the perfect word to describe the terror aspect of Below Zero; unnerving.  While Subnautica was an almost constantly terrifying, beautiful and unique, unintentional horror survival game with a bread crumb story, Below Zero is an often unnerving, gorgeous, mesmerising story driven survival game. does that make it better/worse? from a horror aspect yes, from a story aspect maybe, as it depends if you enjoyed the story telling of the first. from a technical aspect no as Below Zero has a lot more personalisation than Subnautica ever did.To make it simple, if you are a fan of the first game, you'll like this one, however it will never be as scary as the first one, it can still leave you anxious with the endless abyss of icy cold oceans and weird sea monsters, but the absolute, ♥♥♥♥-your-pants terror you faced in Subnautica will never return.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica Below Zero is kind of an ambivalent game. The loop of exploring, finding new blueprints, buidling new equipment and using it to explore further works great and is as addicitive as in the first Subnautica game. Unfortunately, Below Zero had some points that really hampered the experience for me. The biggest issue are the land areas. They are simply too big and confusing. I kept circling around the same spots all the time because I was totally. As much as I liked the parts under water, the land parts of Below Zero are an immense pain in the ass. These parts really ruined the game for me. What I also found to be very annoying is that the game doesn't give you proper clues as to where you should go next. That made the story feel like a guessing game. The game world itself is much smaller than in the first game. But it is as colorful and interesting as one would expect. But the constant sense of horror isn't nearly as present as in the first game. For some reason, I found the encounters with Leviathans rather annoying, whereas in the first game they really scared me. The new story is rather interesting, albeit it takes away the constant feeling of loneliness you had in the first Subnautica. To sum it up: Subnautica Below Zero is a decent game, but in my opinion can't hold up with its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there are aspects of this game I like similar to Subnautica, overall I am not able to recommend it.My main issue is that the map and environments in general is very cramped compared to the first game.  The cave systems in particular were frustrating as you'd enter one thinking you were getting close to finding an objective, only to realize that the point 100 meters away was actually in a completely different cave system.  In the first game, if you were stealthy enough, you could avoid confrontations with the leviathans.  In this game, a late game biome is so cramped you are guaranteed to be attacked multiple times as you attempt to explore it.The other main issue I had with the game is that key resources and blue prints proved way too difficult to find.  I eventually had to resort to guides to find these items, and the difficulty in accessing them was such that not even a written guide proved sufficient.  I had to watch YouTube videos showing exactly, step-by-step how to find these spots/resources.  The first game did a much better job of creating a flow in which you naturally came across locations, blueprints and resources organically.The story was fine, but I appreciated that the first game had a silent protagonist and more focused story as it let you feel you were in their shoes and were discovering things on your own vs. being pushed along by external forces.Graphics, voice acting, and moment-to-moment game play are all good and similar to the first game.I think Subnautica is one of the best games ever made, and I don't regret supporting the developer by purchasing this game.  I hope in their next game they gravitate back more to what made the first one great.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Subnatica and was very excited for Subnautica Below Zero. There are several similarities between the two games that give you a good throwback feeling but a lot of new things that make it really exciting. I am hoping and praying that we can get more in the future! I want to know what happens next! Anyhow back to the game! This is a fun resource gathering, mystery solving game with giant deadly fish. Explore everywhere, utilize the Scanners to find fragments to make your life easier and have fun. This game is not for people who dislike deep water and oceans or those who get easily frustrated if you get lost a few times.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The game's really gorgeous and a worthy sequel to the first one. Once again it was so cool to swim trough the new areas and discover all the new there was offered. The story was great and having a talking character was a new take on the game, but at least she's well written and likeable character. The conversations she has are really interesting to hear and lay really nice thoughts on individuality and autonomy. It was very interesting to see the ties between the first game and this one, and the architecture body was amazing. Loved the design on it. The new creatures were fun to investigate and the penguins stole my heart. The new base building is really cool and the new upgrades really feel worth it!Sadly it had some cons;It didn't manage to create the same feeling as the first one, something was missing. The safe zone was beautiful but it never felt the same. The game felt like the depths weren't as intimidating and it almost felt like there was less to discover and the depths were only spooky for a moment before you got used to it. Sure it was new to be on land and explore that further too, but somehow it just didn't stick with me. The first game had me going around and wanting to build a new habitat in each corner to just view the fauna swimming around and just mind their own business, in this game though it felt off. I could never find the right spot for it, it just never felt the same. The upgraded PDA felt bit meh, since it was trying too hard to be something new, but still the same so it would be familiar to the player. The old one was new and fresh and cracked jokes, this one was basically the same with a different voice and logo on it. It jsut feels like something two competing companies wouldn't do. Then last, the predators. They just didn't do it for me. They were there and scared me only for the first time until i got a better look at them. The first game handled the introduction of predators well and never kept them too active to be a menace instead of threat. The predators were mostly annoying and just in the way. Especially since there was only one way to fight back, zapping them with your seatruck. In the old game you could fight back with your prawn suit and so on, in this one no matter what you did the bigger predators could just grab you and have a nom. It was mostly annoying and not scary. And the shadow leviathans were jsut annoying and i hated the crystal caves. Prawn suit felt so unnecessary in the game, in the old one you needed it to advance, in this one it was just for material gathering, it had no other use at all. All in all, a wonderful game and if they ever decide to make another one i know it's going to be beautiful and i'll jump on that one too!
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game, i thoroughly enjoyed it.Im not sure if i am the only one to think it but this map is no where near as good as the first subnautica but below Zero's story was by far superior.i also felt that this game was a lot shorter than the first... None the less, this was a very good game and i would still recommend playing it
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This review is more neutral than pure negative, probably a 45/100 for me.It is very easy to finish this game and accidentally miss a lot of its coolest areas and parts of the "story". None of the stories which are started are actually resolved at the end (ESPECIALLY if you miss some spots that the game NEVER directs you to), so it all just feels deflated. I finished the game and even went back and found all the areas I missed and it STILL doesn't resolve the intrigue of the major storylines. Some stories/mysteries that are initiated are just completely abandoned with no opportunity to explore them. This could be worth playing if you really, really just want more Subnautica gameplay and the story doesn't matter to you. Frankly it really is not flushed out enough to be considered a good standalone game.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Its a shame, had I not have played the first game I would definitely thumbs up this one. As a successor to such an amazing game though.. Below Zero was a disappointment. If you haven't played either game, and you can only buy one.. buy the first game. If you can afford both.. play this one first.I'll be honest I haven't even finished this one. Most of my 44 hours were during it's early access phase. I'll attempt to finish it someday.. but it's never gonna be a "I gotta play this again!", like the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Smaller and more optimized then the first, Below Zero manages to fix almost everything wrong with its predecessor, and even add some QoL features that make the gameplay less frustrating and allows for extended base customization options. The only issue; the game will not help you find your way forward. You just have to poke around the map to figure out whats going on, but luckily the condensed map and the less plentiful enemies makes it much easier. And surprisingly, the scariest creature in this game might be the one found only on land
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: First of all i both own the orinal subnatica and below zero and played them both. (haven't finished any of them tho... lol and i totally haven't played in my world for more than 20 hours) And if i would be a 100% sure i think i like below zero most! I'm not saying the orinal game is bad, NO!I just think that there's a little bit more things in this game. I mean Subnatica is a very big game and below zero is a small game it's just that there's more to do, If you ask me.BUT i would still recommend playing subnatica first and then play below zero. With that being said they are still both underwater games where you have to survive.When i first played subnatica in like 2019, (mabye 2018, cant remember) i really like'd it even tho i don't really like horror games.If you want to know if it is a horror game i would say... in a way, i mean yeah, the enemies are pretty scary. (in both games) But when you have played it a lot of time there not really THAT scary. There's is a few bugs in the game, but they will hopefully get fixed.If you really just want to play this or just miss the good all days, then i would say you should buy it. _childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and continues the story of the original Subnautica, can't wait to see what Subnautica 2 brings.  I like the exclusion of the stasis gun to prevent easy cheese killing of big predators.Overall it doesn't feel as large and expansive as the original and sometimes I had issues figuring out where to go next.  As a whole though, I enjoyed the first Subnautica and if you did,  you should give this one a try as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Gave me a lot of hours of fun. The change in direction of story felt good, and it delivers a good ending, as it's predecessor, although it does not fill totally the shoes of the first game. If you are stuck between playing this or the predecessor, I'd recomend, go with the Subnautica first.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played and loved Subnautica, like me, you'll love Below Zero.If you didn't play Subnautica but are interested in a Underwater-survival-story game, play Subnautica and then come back to Below Zero.If you played Subnautica and liked it because it was underwater and spooky, Keep in mind that Below Zero is more above-ground.It still has it's spooky moments deep under the sealevel, but it's more above ground than the first one with it's two islands.All in all though, they really nailed it, cannot wait for Subnautica 2 (which is 3, idk why they named it 2)
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: OH. MY. GOD. I rarely, if EVER leave reviews. I just hate taking the time to type things, you know? I played the original Subnautica, from early access to release, over about the 1-1.5 year period. Loved it. Fantastic, horror, survival, exploration. The whole caboodle. So of course, when I saw another one coming out, I instantly bought it. Let me tell you something, if Unknown Worlds makes a 3rd, 4th or 5th Subnautica, I will and will have purchased them. This game, while no different than  the first Subnautica gameplay wise, has a fantastic story. I am so glad I didn't spoil the ending for myself, because seeing it first hand was so much more worth it. Its tough to describe the joy I felt at the ending and the satisfaction I felt with completing it. All I can say Unknown Worlds, is out-bloody-standing job, and where is game 3? GIMME! Until next time! Alex
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Below Zero is more of what you love from the first game, with some tweaks. If that's all you wanted, I recommend the game. The base building is much better in this one as well, so I had a lot of fun with the new features. Critically I do have a small handful of complaints. I think the map would have been a lot better without any focus on the glacier parts of the map. Land movement up there feels janky and isn't really that interesting at all. The game has more of a story focus on it this time, which, while admirable, doesn't really enhance the experience a lot. The story was also rewritten more than halfway through the project which may explain why. The result is something that just kinda gets in the way of the experience, not in any dramatic way mind you, but enough to just kinda squint and go "eh," before you carry on with whatever your previous task was. I will say in regards to the story that it does have great voice acting, something I appreciated a lot from the first game and was glad to see carry over.Below Zero gets the job done, and sometimes that's enough. 3/5
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica and Below Zero are both incredibly beautiful games.They can both manage to be very peaceful and pulse pounding unnerving.The fear of the unknown and the reward of curiosity are what makes these games so good.Below Zero is much more narrative driven but the overall hook of the games are the same.The below ocean survival sim makes these unique over games such as Raft or Rust, but if you like those types of games, definitely give this one a shot.Happy to see the progress of the game studio and cannot wait to see what they come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours in, I'm in love with this game. I waited for the full release and it's been worth it. There's a bunch more story to this one and it drives your desire to explore so much more. And it feels polished this time. No glaring bugs to report so far. The old immersion breaking texture pop from the original Subnautica is almost entirely eradicated. If I had to list one annoyance, it would be the surface mapping and occasionally getting stuck when exploring dry ground. More reason to get back in the water!The balance of exploration against aggressive fauna feels just right; enough to keep you checking over your shoulder every few seconds, but not so much that it becomes annoying, and it can be usually be dealt with by a swift dodge/getaway.I was worried it might feel too samey, returning to a planet I've spent many hours exploring in the previous title. I needn't have worried, there's so much new stuff here it's frankly incredible how much work they've put in. The new biomes feel such much more real and alive than the original. The lily-pad zone blew my mind with the scale and the thought behind it. Then I realised you could hitch a lift on a whale! Genuinely, I gasped.From a lover of single player survival games, this is a breath of fresh air in a sea of unpolished flotsam. Pun totally intended. 10/10. Please don't change what you're doing Unknown Worlds, these games of yours are magical.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The first Subnautica never had much of a negative effect on me, but 5 hours in this one and it already gave me nightmares about getting lost in labyrinthine underwater caves full of stuff trying to grab me and bite me while I struggled to find small pockets of air that would keep me going for a few seconds more, as the batteries on my tools slowly and relentlessly dropped to zero.I hate it, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into a freezing underwater adventure on an alien planet. Set one year after the original Subnautica, Below Zero challenges you to survive a disaster at an alien research station on Planet 4546B. Craft tools, scavenge for supplies, and unravel the next chapter in the Subnautica story.
